shloka_text: तौ राजपुत्रौ कार्त्स्न्येन धर्म्यमाख्यानमुत्तमम्। वाचोविधेयं तत्सर्वं कृत्वा काव्यमनिन्दितौ।।1.4.12।। ऋषीणां च द्विजातीनां साधूनां च समागमे। यथोपदेशं तत्त्वज्ञौ जगतुस्सुसमाहितौ।।1.4.13।।
transliteration: tau rājaputrau kārtsnyena dharmyamākhyānamuttamam| vācovidheyaṃ tatsarvaṃ kṛtvā kāvyamaninditau ṛṣīṇāṃ ca dvijātīnāṃ sādhūnāṃ ca samāgame| yathopadeśaṃ tattvajñau jagatussusamāhitau
translation: तौ राजपुत्रौ these two princes, धर्म्यम् based on dharma, उत्तमम् greatest, तत् सर्वम् आख्यानम् the entire epic, कात्स्नर्येन completely, वाचोविधेयम् committed to memory, कृत्वा having made, अनिन्दितौ blameless, तत्त्वज्ञौ well versed, सुसमाहितौ disciplined, यथोपदेशम् as instructed (by sage Valmiki), ऋषीणाम् of the ascetics, द्विजातीनाम् of the learned brahmins, साधूनां च of  saints also, समागमे in the meetings, जगतु: chanted.
explanation: These two princes blameless, disciplined and wellversed, committed to memory the whole epic and chanted as instructed in the assembly of rishis, brahmins and saints.

shloka_text: तौ राजपुत्रौ कार्त्स्न्येन धर्म्यमाख्यानमुत्तमम्। वाचोविधेयं तत्सर्वं कृत्वा काव्यमनिन्दितौ।।1.4.12।। ऋषीणां च द्विजातीनां साधूनां च समागमे। यथोपदेशं तत्त्वज्ञौ जगतुस्सुसमाहितौ।।1.4.13।।
transliteration: tau rājaputrau kārtsnyena dharmyamākhyānamuttamam| vācovidheyaṃ tatsarvaṃ kṛtvā kāvyamaninditau ṛṣīṇāṃ ca dvijātīnāṃ sādhūnāṃ ca samāgame| yathopadeśaṃ tattvajñau jagatussusamāhitau
translation: तौ राजपुत्रौ these two princes, धर्म्यम् based on dharma, उत्तमम् greatest, तत् सर्वम् आख्यानम् the entire epic, कात्स्नर्येन completely, वाचोविधेयम् committed to memory, कृत्वा having made, अनिन्दितौ blameless, तत्त्वज्ञौ well versed, सुसमाहितौ disciplined, यथोपदेशम् as instructed (by sage Valmiki), ऋषीणाम् of the ascetics, द्विजातीनाम् of the learned brahmins, साधूनां च of  saints also, समागमे in the meetings, जगतु: chanted.
explanation: These two princes blameless, disciplined and wellversed, committed to memory the whole epic and chanted as instructed in the assembly of rishis, brahmins and saints.

shloka_text: महात्मानौ महाभागौ सर्वलक्षणलक्षितौ। तौ कदाचित्समेतानामृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्। आसीनानां समीपस्थाविदं काव्यमगायताम्।।1.4.14।।
transliteration: mahātmānau mahābhāgau sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitau| tau kadācitsametānāmṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām| āsīnānāṃ samīpasthāvidaṃ kāvyamagāyatām
translation: महात्मानौ great persons, महाभागौ dignified ones, सर्वलक्षणलक्षितौ endowed with all good features, तौ both of them, कदाचित् on a particular occasion, समेतानाम् assembled at one place, भावितात्मनाम् of honoured ones, आसीनानाम् of those who were seated, ऋषीणाम् ascetics', समीपस्थौ standing in their presence, इदम् this, काव्यम् great epic, अगायताम् chanted.
explanation: On a particular occasion both the great princes who were dignified and endowed with good features, chanted this great epic in the presence of honoured ascetics who assembled at one place.

shloka_text: ﻿तच्छ्रुत्वा मुनयस्सर्वे बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणा:। साधुसाध्विति तावूचु: परं विस्मयमागता:।।1.4.15।।
transliteration: ﻿tacchrutvā munayassarve bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇā:| sādhusādhviti tāvūcu: paraṃ vismayamāgatā:
translation: ﻿ सर्वे all, मुनय: sages, तत् श्रुत्वा having heard that, परम् great, विस्मयम् wonder, आगता: having experienced, बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणा: been overcome with tears of joy in their eyes, साधु साधु इति excellent, excellent, तौ about Kusa and Lava, ऊचु: exclaimed.
explanation: ﻿ All the sages having heard the chanting (of that glorious kavya), experienced great astonishment. Overcome with tears of joy in their eyes, they praised them, exclaiming "Excellent, Excellent".

shloka_text: ते प्रीतमनसस्सर्वे मुनयो धर्मवत्सला:। प्रशशंसु: प्रशस्तव्यौ गायमानौ कुशीलवौ।।1.4.16।।
transliteration: te prītamanasassarve munayo dharmavatsalā:| praśaśaṃsu: praśastavyau gāyamānau kuśīlavau
translation: धर्मवत्सला: ते सर्वे all those who love dharma, मुनय: sages, प्रीतमनस: pleased, प्रशस्तव्यौ praiseworthy, गायमानौ while both of them were chanting, कुशीलवौ singers (Kusa and Lava), प्रशशंसु: praised.
explanation: All the sages steeped in dharma, pleased with them, praised the admirable Kusa and Lava as they sang.

shloka_text: अहो गीतस्य माधुर्यं श्लोकानां च विशेषत:। चिरनिर्वृत्तमप्येतत्प्रत्यक्षमिव दर्शितम्।।1.4.17।।
transliteration: aho gītasya mādhuryaṃ ślokānāṃ ca viśeṣata:| ciranirvṛttamapyetatpratyakṣamiva darśitam
translation: गीतस्य of the song, माधुर्यम् melody, अहो how surprising, विशेषत: especially, श्लोकानामथ of verses, एतत् this history, चिरनिर्वृत्तमपि though happened long ago, प्रत्यक्षमिव as if  happening at the present moment, दर्शितम् is shown.
explanation: How melodious is this chanting, especially the verses Though it (the events) had happened long ago, it is described as if it is happening at the present moment, exclaimed the audience.

shloka_text: ﻿प्रविश्य तावुभौ सुष्ठु भावं सम्यगगायताम्। सहितौ मधुरं रक्तं सम्पन्नं स्वरसम्पदा।।1.4.18।।
transliteration: ﻿praviśya tāvubhau suṣṭhu bhāvaṃ samyagagāyatām| sahitau madhuraṃ raktaṃ sampannaṃ svarasampadā
translation: ﻿ तौ उभौ both of them, सहितौ in unison, भावम् in theme, सुष्ठु excellently, प्रविश्य having entered, मधुरम् melodiusly, रक्तम् entrancing, स्वरसम्पदा sadja and other notes, सम्पन्नम् endowed with, सम्यक् very well, अगायताम् chanted.
explanation: ﻿ They both chanted in perfect unison in theme and passion, with their charming melodious voice endowed with the rich notes of music (sadja and other).

shloka_text: एवं प्रशस्यमानौ तौ तपश्श्लाघ्यैर्महात्मभि:। संरक्ततरमत्यर्थं मधुरं तावगायताम्।।1.4.19।।
transliteration: evaṃ praśasyamānau tau tapaśślāghyairmahātmabhi:| saṃraktataramatyarthaṃ madhuraṃ tāvagāyatām
translation: तप: श्लाघ्यै: by ascetics who were commendable for their austerities, महात्मभि: by great sages, एवम् in this manner, प्रशस्यमानौ being praised, तौ both of them, संरक्ततरम् highly entrancing, अत्यर्थम् even with greater desire, मधुरम् sweetly, अगायताम् chanted.
explanation: Praised in this manner by the great sages commendable for their austerities, they chanted even with greater charm and sweetness.

shloka_text: प्रीत: कश्चिन्मुनिस्ताभ्यां संस्थित: कलशं ददौ। प्रसन्नो वल्कलं कश्चिद्ददौ ताभ्यां महायशा:।।1.4.20।।
transliteration: prīta: kaścinmunistābhyāṃ saṃsthita: kalaśaṃ dadau| prasanno valkalaṃ kaściddadau tābhyāṃ mahāyaśā:
translation: कश्चित् some one from the assembly of, मुनि: sage, प्रीत: pleased, संस्थित: seated there, ताभ्याम् for both of them, कलशम् waterpitcher, ददौ gave, महायशा: renowned, कश्चित्  another one, प्रसन्न: delighted, वल्कलम् bark garment, ददौ gave.
explanation: Pleased with the singing, one of the sages seated in the assembly presented them a pitcher. Another sage of renown got so delighted that he gave them garments.

shloka_text: आश्चर्यमिदमाख्यानं मुनिना सम्प्रकीर्तितम्। परं कवीनामाधारं समाप्तं च यथाक्रमम्।।1.4.21।।
transliteration: āścaryamidamākhyānaṃ muninā samprakīrtitam| paraṃ kavīnāmādhāraṃ samāptaṃ ca yathākramam
translation: मुनिना by sage Valmiki, सम्प्रकीर्तितम् has been told, इदम् this, आख्यानम् legendary poem, आश्चर्यम् is causing surprise, कवीनाम् for the poets, परम् supreme, आधारम् foundation, यथाक्रमम् according to specific rules  and order, समाप्तं च is  also completed.
explanation: This wonderful epic chronologically composed and completed by the sage (Valmiki),  is the supreme source for poetry.

shloka_text: अभिगीतमिदं गीतं सर्वगीतेषु कोविदौ। आयुष्यं पुष्टिजनकं सर्वश्रुतिमनोहरम्।।1.4.22।। प्रशस्यमानौ सर्वत्र कदाचित्तत्र गायकौ । रथ्यासु राजमार्गेषु ददर्श भरताग्रज:।।1.4.23।।
transliteration: abhigītamidaṃ gītaṃ sarvagīteṣu kovidau| āyuṣyaṃ puṣṭijanakaṃ sarvaśrutimanoharam praśasyamānau sarvatra kadācittatra gāyakau | rathyāsu rājamārgeṣu dadarśa bharatāgraja:
translation: आयुष्यम् bestowing longevity, पुष्टिजनकम् causing nourishment (prosperity), सर्वश्रुतिमनोहरम् to all pleasing to hear, अभिगीतम् having sung well, इदम् this, गीतम् poem, प्रशस्यमानौ being admired, रथ्यासु in the streets, राजमार्गेषु in principal roads, सर्वत्र everywhere, गायकौ singers Kusa and Lava, सर्वगीतेषु among all kinds of songs, कोविदौ proficient, कदाचित् on one occasion, भरताग्रज: Sri Rama, ददर्श saw them.
explanation: The two singers, proficient in all kinds of notes recited the epic in the streets and on the principal roads. It was pleasing to hear for all. It gave long life and prosperity to the listeners. People admired them. Once Rama happened to see them.

shloka_text: अभिगीतमिदं गीतं सर्वगीतेषु कोविदौ। आयुष्यं पुष्टिजनकं सर्वश्रुतिमनोहरम्।।1.4.22।। प्रशस्यमानौ सर्वत्र कदाचित्तत्र गायकौ । रथ्यासु राजमार्गेषु ददर्श भरताग्रज:।।1.4.23।।
transliteration: abhigītamidaṃ gītaṃ sarvagīteṣu kovidau| āyuṣyaṃ puṣṭijanakaṃ sarvaśrutimanoharam praśasyamānau sarvatra kadācittatra gāyakau | rathyāsu rājamārgeṣu dadarśa bharatāgraja:
translation: आयुष्यम् bestowing longevity, पुष्टिजनकम् causing nourishment (prosperity), सर्वश्रुतिमनोहरम् to all pleasing to hear, अभिगीतम् having sung well, इदम् this, गीतम् poem, प्रशस्यमानौ being admired, रथ्यासु in the streets, राजमार्गेषु in principal roads, सर्वत्र everywhere, गायकौ singers Kusa and Lava, सर्वगीतेषु among all kinds of songs, कोविदौ proficient, कदाचित् on one occasion, भरताग्रज: Sri Rama, ददर्श saw them.
explanation: The two singers, proficient in all kinds of notes recited the epic in the streets and on the principal roads. It was pleasing to hear for all. It gave long life and prosperity to the listeners. People admired them. Once Rama happened to see them.

shloka_text: स्ववेश्म चानीय तदा भ्रातरौ स कुशीलवौ। पूजयामास पूजार्हौ रामश्शत्रुनिबर्हण:।।1.4.24।।
transliteration: svaveśma cānīya tadā bhrātarau sa kuśīlavau| pūjayāmāsa pūjārhau rāmaśśatrunibarhaṇa:
translation: तदा thereafter, शत्रुनिबर्हण: destroyer of enemies, स: राम: Rama, पूजार्हौ the twins deserving honour, भ्रातरौ brothers, कुशीलवौ Kusa and Lava, स्ववेश्म to his royal palace, आनीय having brought, पूजयामास extended respectful hospitality.
explanation: Thereafter, Rama, the destroyer of enemies, having invited the two brothers Kusa and Lava who deserved honour. He brought them to his royal palace and extended respectful hospitality.

shloka_text: आसीन: काञ्चने दिव्ये स च सिंहासने प्रभु:। उपोपविष्टस्सचिवैर्भ्रातृभिश्च परन्तप:।।1.4.25।।
transliteration: āsīna: kāñcane divye sa ca siṃhāsane prabhu:| upopaviṣṭassacivairbhrātṛbhiśca parantapa:
translation: परन्तप: tormentor of enemies, स: प्रभु: that Rama, सचिवै: by ministers, भ्रातृभिश्च by brothers, उपोपविष्ट: surrounded by, दिव्ये in a splendid, काञ्चने golden, सिंहासने throne, आसीन: was seated.
explanation: Rama, the tormentor of enemies, surrounded by his ministers and brothers occupied the splendid golden throne.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा तु रूपसम्पन्नौ तावुभौ नियतस्तथा। उवाच लक्ष्मणं रामश्शत्रुघ्नं भरतं तदा।।1.4.26।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā tu rūpasampannau tāvubhau niyatastathā| uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmaśśatrughnaṃ bharataṃ tadā
translation: नियत: selfpossessed, राम: Rama, तदा then, रूपसम्पन्नौ very handsome, तौ those, उभौ both of them, दृष्ट्वा having seen, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, शत्रुघ्नम् Satrughna, तथा and, भरतम् Bharata, उवाच said.
explanation: Then selfpossessed Rama, having seen those very handsome brothers (Kusa and Lava), addressed Lakshmana, Satrughna and Bharata, saying:

shloka_text: श्रूयतामिदमाख्यानमनयोर्देववर्चसो:। विचित्रार्थपदं सम्यग्गायकौ तावचोदयत्।।1.4.27।।
transliteration: śrūyatāmidamākhyānamanayordevavarcaso:| vicitrārthapadaṃ samyaggāyakau tāvacodayat
translation: देववर्चसो: of both possessing lustre of devatas, अनयो: of both of them, विचित्रार्थपदम्  portraying excellent sense and words, इदम् this, आख्यानम् poem, सम्यक् completely, श्रूयताम् let it be heard, तौ गायकौ those singers, अचोदयत् urged.
explanation: "Listen to this story sung by both of them, portraying excellent sense and words". Having said this, Rama urged the singers with the lustre of devatas to commence.

shloka_text: तौ चापि मधुरं रक्तं स्वञ्चितायतनिस्वनम् । तन्त्रीलयवदत्यर्थं विश्रुतार्थमगायताम् ।।1.4.28।।
transliteration: tau cāpi madhuraṃ raktaṃ svañcitāyatanisvanam | tantrīlayavadatyarthaṃ viśrutārthamagāyatām
translation: तौ च both of them, मधुरम् melodiously, रक्तम् engaging, स्वञ्चितायतनिस्वनम् good and ample voice, तन्त्रीलयवत् tuning their stringed instruments, अत्यर्थम् greatly, विश्रुतार्थम् distinctly meaningful, अगायताम् chanted.
explanation: Both of them, with good and ample voice, chanted the kavya in a distinctly meaningful way. Tuning their stringed instruments, they sang melodiously and engagingly.

shloka_text: ह्लादयत्सर्वगात्राणि मनांसि हृदयानि च। श्रोत्राश्रयसुखं गेयं तद्बभौ जनसंसदि।।1.4.29।।
transliteration: hlādayatsarvagātrāṇi manāṃsi hṛdayāni ca| śrotrāśrayasukhaṃ geyaṃ tadbabhau janasaṃsadi
translation: श्रोत्राश्रयसुखम् comfortable to the sense of hearing, तत् that, गेयम् poem, जनसंसदि in the assembly of men, सर्वगात्राणि all the sense organs, मनांसि minds, हृदयानि च hearts also, ह्लादयत् rejoicing, बभौ shone.
explanation: The chanting of the kavya in the assembly of men comforted the sense of hearing. The listeners rejoiced in their mind, heart and the whole being.

shloka_text: इमौ मुनी पार्थिवलक्षणान्वितौ कुशीलवौ चैव महातपस्विनौ। ममापि तद्भूतिकरं प्रवक्ष्यते महानुभावं चरितं निबोधत।।1.4.30।।
transliteration: imau munī pārthivalakṣaṇānvitau kuśīlavau caiva mahātapasvinau| mamāpi tadbhūtikaraṃ pravakṣyate mahānubhāvaṃ caritaṃ nibodhata
translation: इमौ both these, मुनी sages, पार्थिवलक्षणान्वितौ endowed with attributes of royalty, कुशीलवौ चैव singers Kusa and Lava, महातपस्विनौ great ascetics, ममापि even for me, भूतिकरम् conducive to my welfare, महानुभावम् having great purport, तत् चरितम् that history, प्रवक्ष्यते  will be narrated, निबोधत listen with concentration of mind.
explanation: Addressing the assembly of men Rama said "Both Kusa and Lava, even though ascetics, are endowed with the attributes of royalty. Eventhough they are singers, they are ascetics. This is even conducive to my wellbeing. Listen to the meaningful story with concentration".

shloka_text: ततस्तु तौ रामवच:प्रचोदितावगायतां मार्गविधानसम्पदा। स चापि राम: परिषद्गतः शनैर्बुभूषयासक्तमना बभूव।।1.4.31।।
transliteration: tatastu tau rāmavaca:pracoditāvagāyatāṃ mārgavidhānasampadā| sa cāpi rāma: pariṣadgataḥ śanairbubhūṣayāsaktamanā babhūva
translation: तत: thereafter, तौ the two brothers, रामवच:प्रचोदितौ encouraged by words of Rama, मार्गविधानसम्पदा according to 'Marga' mode of singing, अगायताम् chanted, परिषद्गत: who was in the assembly, स: राम: अपि even Rama, शनै: बुभूषया desirous of having a peaceful mind, आसक्तमना: बभूव fixed their mind on chanting.
explanation: Encouraged by the words of Rama, the two brothers chanted according to marga mode of singing (classical style). Even Rama who was in the assembly desirous of peace, concentrated his mind on that chanting. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे चतुर्थस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the fourth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana in synopsis of the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: . सर्वा पूर्वमियं येषामासीत्कृत्स्ना वसुन्धरा । प्रजापतिमुपादाय नृपाणां जयशालिनाम् ।।1.5.1।।
transliteration: . sarvā pūrvamiyaṃ yeṣāmāsītkṛtsnā vasundharā | prajāpatimupādāya nṛpāṇāṃ jayaśālinām
translation: सर्वाः all (bounded by all islands), कृत्स्ना entirely, इयं वसुन्धरा this earth, प्रजापतिम् उपादाय commencing from Prajapati (Manu) and his descendents, जयशालिनाम् of victorious, येषां  नृपाणाम् relating to those kings, पूर्वम् in the olden periods, आसीत् belonged.
explanation: Formerly, this entire earth belonged to  those victorious kings starting from Prajapati (Manu).
comments: Dasaratha's kingdom and greatness of Ayodhya

shloka_text: येषां स सगरो नाम सागरो येन खानित: । षष्टि: पुत्रसहस्राणि यं यान्तं पर्यवारयन् ।।1.5.2।।
transliteration: yeṣāṃ sa sagaro nāma sāgaro yena khānita: | ṣaṣṭi: putrasahasrāṇi yaṃ yāntaṃ paryavārayan
translation: येन by whom, सागर: ocean, खानित: was made to be dug, यान्तम् while he was marching (to the battle), यम् whom, षष्टि: पुत्रसहस्राणि sixty thousand sons, पर्यवारयन् surrounded by, स: that, सगरो नाम king named Sagara, येषाम् amongst those.
explanation: Among them a king named Sagara got the ocean dug and his sixty thousand sons surrounded him whenever he went (to battle).

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकूणामिदं तेषां राज्ञां वंशे महात्मनाम् । महदुत्पन्नमाख्यानं रामायणमिति श्रुतम् ।।1.5.3।।
transliteration: ikṣvākūṇāmidaṃ teṣāṃ rājñāṃ vaṃśe mahātmanām | mahadutpannamākhyānaṃ rāmāyaṇamiti śrutam
translation: तेषाम् their, महात्मनाम् mighty monarchs, इक्ष्वाकूणाम् of the Ikshvakus, राज्ञाम् of kings, वंशे in that race, रामायणमिति known as 'Ramayanam', श्रुतम् celebrated, महत् great, इदम् this, आख्यानम् epic, उत्पन्नम् arose.
explanation: It was from the family of mighty monarchs with Ikshvaku as its founder and the kings born in that race, the celebrated epic known as the 'Ramayanam' arose.

shloka_text: तदिदं वर्तयिष्यामि सर्वं निखिलमादित: । धर्मकामार्थसहितं श्रोतव्यमनसूयया ।।1.5.4।।
transliteration: tadidaṃ vartayiṣyāmi sarvaṃ nikhilamādita: | dharmakāmārthasahitaṃ śrotavyamanasūyayā
translation: तत् thence, इदम् this (Ramayanam), सर्वम् completely, वर्तयिष्यामि I shall propagate in this world, निखिलम् the entire Ramayanam, धर्मकामार्थसहितम् incorporating the merits of dharma, artha and kama, आदित: from the beginning, अनसूयया without prejudice, श्रोतव्यम् should be heard .
explanation: I shall propagate this Ramayanam, incorporating the merits of dharma, artha and kama, and complete in all respects. It deserves to be heard right from the start without prejudice.

shloka_text: कोसलो नाम मुदितस्स्फीतो जनपदो महान् । निविष्टस्सरयूतीरे प्रभूतधनधान्यवान् ।।1.5.5।।
transliteration: kosalo nāma muditassphīto janapado mahān | niviṣṭassarayūtīre prabhūtadhanadhānyavān
translation: प्रभूतधनधान्यवान् abundant in foodgrains and wealth, मुदित: rejoiced, स्फीत: prosperous, कोसलो नाम named Kosala, महान् great, जनपद: country, सरयूतीरे on the banks of river Sarayu, निविष्ट: was situated.
explanation: On the banks of river Sarayu, a great and prosperous country named Kosala, abundant in foodgrains and wealth and inhabited by contended people, was situated.

shloka_text: अयोध्या नाम नगरी तत्रासील्लोकविश्रुता । मनुना मानवेन्द्रेण या पुरी निर्मिता स्वयम् ।।1.5.6।।
transliteration: ayodhyā nāma nagarī tatrāsīllokaviśrutā | manunā mānavendreṇa yā purī nirmitā svayam
translation: तत्र in that Kosala country, या पुरी that city, मानवेन्द्रेण by lord of men, मनुना by Manu, स्वयम् personally, निर्मिता built, अयोध्या नाम named Ayodhya, लोकविश्रुता famous, नगरी city, आसीत् existed.
explanation: In the country called Kosala was the famous capital city of Ayodhya built by the lord of men, Manu .

shloka_text: आयता दश च द्वे च योजनानि महापुरी । श्रीमती त्रीणि विस्तीर्णा सुविभक्तमहापथा ।।1.5.7।।
transliteration: āyatā daśa ca dve ca yojanāni mahāpurī | śrīmatī trīṇi vistīrṇā suvibhaktamahāpathā
translation: श्रीमती beautiful and pleasing, सुविभक्तमहापथा welllaid out thoroughfares, महापुरी that great city of Ayodhya, दश च द्वे च twelve, योजनानि yojanas (fortyeight krosas or ninetysix miles), आयता in length, त्रीणि three yojanas (twelve krosas or twenty four miles), विस्तीर्णा in breadth.
explanation: With welllaid out thoroughfares, the beautiful and prosperous city of Ayodhya extended for twelve yojanas in length and three yojanas in breadth.

shloka_text: राजमार्गेण महता सुविभक्तेन शोभिता । मुक्तपुष्पावकीर्णेन जलसिक्तेन नित्यश: ।।1.5.8।।
transliteration: rājamārgeṇa mahatā suvibhaktena śobhitā | muktapuṣpāvakīrṇena jalasiktena nityaśa:
translation: सुविभक्तेन with welllaid out, मुक्तपुष्पावकीर्णेन strewn with fully blown blossoms, नित्यश: regularly, जलसिक्तेन sprinkled with water, महता by great, राजमार्गेण by principal highway, शोभिता looked splendid.
explanation: It looked splendid with its welllaid out and broad highway strewn with flowers and regularly sprinkled with water.

shloka_text: तां तु राजा दशरथो महाराष्ट्रविवर्धन: । पुरीमावासयामास दिवं देवपतिर्यथा ।।1.5.9।।
transliteration: tāṃ tu rājā daśaratho mahārāṣṭravivardhana: | purīmāvāsayāmāsa divaṃ devapatiryathā
translation: महाराष्ट्रविवर्धन: developing the prosperity of that great kingdom, राजा दशरथ: king Dasaratha, देवपति: Indra, दिवं यथा like heaven, तां पुरीम् that city, आवासयामास lived.
explanation: King Dasartha, augmenting the prosperity of the great kingdom, lived in the city of Ayodhya like Indra in heaven.

shloka_text: कवाटतोरणवतीं सुविभक्तान्तरापणाम् । सर्वयन्त्रायुधवतीमुपेतां सर्वशिल्पिभि: ।।1.5.10।।
transliteration: kavāṭatoraṇavatīṃ suvibhaktāntarāpaṇām | sarvayantrāyudhavatīmupetāṃ sarvaśilpibhi:
translation: कवाटतोरणवतीम् having arched outer gateways ornamented with panel doors, सुविभक्तान्तरापणाम् numerous welllaid local markets, सर्वयन्त्रायुधवतीम् having all kinds of  instruments and weapons, सर्वशिल्पिभि: all kinds of artificers, उपेताम् possessed of.
explanation: The city where all kinds of artificers lived had arched outer gateways, wellarranged local markets and all kinds of instruments and weapons.

shloka_text: सूतमागधसम्बाधां श्रीमतीमतुलप्रभाम् । उच्चाट्टालध्वजवतीं शतघ्नीशतसङ्कुलाम् ।।1.5.11।।
transliteration: sūtamāgadhasambādhāṃ śrīmatīmatulaprabhām | uccāṭṭāladhvajavatīṃ śataghnīśatasaṅkulām
translation: सूतमागधसम्बाधाम् abounded in euologists and genealogists praising the kings, श्रीमतीम् prosperous, अतुलप्रभाम् having matchless splendour, उच्चाट्टालध्वजवतीम् with stately edifices decorated with flags, शतघ्नीशतसङ्कुलाम् possessed of hundreds of sataghnis (missiles).
explanation: With matchless splendour, it abounded in eulogists and genealogists. It contained stately edifices decorated with flags and hundreds of sataghnis (missiles).

shloka_text: वधूनाटकसङ्घैश्च संयुक्तां सर्वत: पुरीम् । उद्यानाम्रवणोपेतां महतीं सालमेखलाम् ।।1.5.12।।
transliteration: vadhūnāṭakasaṅghaiśca saṃyuktāṃ sarvata: purīm | udyānāmravaṇopetāṃ mahatīṃ sālamekhalām
translation: वधूनाटकसङ्घैश्च by hosts of female dancers and actors, संयुक्ताम् furnished with, सर्वत: पुरीम् on all sides of the city (surrounded by suburban towns), उद्यानाम्रवणोपेताम् filled with  gardens and mangogroves, महतीम् extensive, सालमेखलाम् rampart of sal trees as a girdle.
explanation: The city with suburban towns on all sides had several female dancers and actors.It was filled with gardens and mangogroves. And girdled by sal trees.

shloka_text: दुर्गगम्भीरपरिघां दुर्गामन्यैर्दुरासदाम् । वाजिवारणसम्पूर्णां गोभिरुष्ट्रै: खरैस्तथा ।।1.5.13।।
transliteration: durgagambhīraparighāṃ durgāmanyairdurāsadām | vājivāraṇasampūrṇāṃ gobhiruṣṭrai: kharaistathā
translation: दुर्गगम्भीरपरिघाम् having strong fortifications and deep moat, दुर्गाम् difficult to access, अन्यै: by others, दुरासदाम् incapable of being approached, वाजिवारणसम्पूर्णां abounded with horses and elephants, तथा and, गोभि: by cattle, उष्ट्रै: by camels, खरै: by mules.
explanation: It was enclosed by strong fortifications and a deep moat. No enemy can ever enter and occupy that city. It abounded with several elephants and horses, cattle, camels and mules.

shloka_text: सामन्तराजसङ्घैश्च बलिकर्मभिरावृताम् । नानादेशनिवासैश्च वणिग्भिरुपशोभिताम् ।।1.5.14।।
transliteration: sāmantarājasaṅghaiśca balikarmabhirāvṛtām | nānādeśanivāsaiśca vaṇigbhirupaśobhitām
translation: बलिकर्मभि: by kings who make payment of tribute, सामन्तराजसङ्घैश्च by a host of tributary kings from neighbouring kingdoms, आवृताम् thronged, नानादेशनिवासै: by people from different countries, वणिग्भि: च with merchants also, उपशोभिताम् embellished.
explanation: It was embellished with a host of tributary kings who used to pay tributes and with  merchants from different countries.

shloka_text: प्रासादै रत्नविकृतै: पर्वतैरुपशोभिताम् । कूटागारैश्च सम्पूर्णामिन्द्रस्येवामरावतीम् ।।1.5.15।।
transliteration: prāsādai ratnavikṛtai: parvatairupaśobhitām | kūṭāgāraiśca sampūrṇāmindrasyevāmarāvatīm
translation: रत्नविकृतै: modified with precious gems(and decorated), प्रासादै: by palaces, पर्वतै: by mountains, उपशोभिताम् resplendent, कूटागारै: च by mansions, सम्पूर्णाम् complete, इन्द्रस्य अमरावतीमिव like Indra's Amaravati.
explanation: Like Indra's Amaravati, it was adorned by mountains and mansions with precious stones.

shloka_text: चित्रामष्टापदाकारां नरनारीगणैर्युताम् । सर्वरत्नसमाकीर्णां विमानगृहशोभिताम् ।।1.5.16।।
transliteration: citrāmaṣṭāpadākārāṃ naranārīgaṇairyutām | sarvaratnasamākīrṇāṃ vimānagṛhaśobhitām
translation: चित्राम् wonderful to behold, अष्टापदाकाराम् like the shape of a board used to play the game of Ashtapada, the game of chance, नरनारीगणै: by groups of men and women, युताम् endowed with, सर्वरत्नसमाकीर्णाम् rich in all kinds of gems, विमानगृहशोभिताम् adorned with sevenstoried palaces.
explanation: With groups of men and women and adorned with sevenstoried palaces, it looked wonderful like a board where the game of ashtapada, is played. It was rich in all kinds of gems.

shloka_text: गृहगाढामविच्छिद्रां समभूमौ निवेशिताम् । शालितण्डुलसम्पूर्णामिक्षुकाण्डरसोदकाम् ।।1.5.17।।
transliteration: gṛhagāḍhāmavicchidrāṃ samabhūmau niveśitām | śālitaṇḍulasampūrṇāmikṣukāṇḍarasodakām
translation: गृहगाढाम् dense with dwellings, अविच्छिद्राम् no place left unutilised, समभूमौ on a levelled land, निवेशिताम् constructed, शालितण्डुलसम्पूर्णाम् stocked fully with fine-grained rice, इक्षुकाण्डरसोदकाम् water tasting like sugarcane juice.
explanation: Its dwellings were constructed on levelled ground with no space left unutilised. It was abundantly stocked with fine-grained rice and water which tasted sweet like sugarcane juice.

shloka_text: दुन्दुभीभिर्मृदङ्गैश्च वीणाभि: पणवैस्तथा । नादितां भृशमत्यर्थं पृथिव्यां तामनुत्तमाम् ।।1.5.18।।
transliteration: dundubhībhirmṛdaṅgaiśca vīṇābhi: paṇavaistathā | nāditāṃ bhṛśamatyarthaṃ pṛthivyāṃ tāmanuttamām
translation: दुन्दुभीभि: by trumpets, मृदङ्गैश्च by mrudangas, वीणाभि: by vinas, तथा and, पणवै: by panavas, भृशम् excessively, नादितां resounded, पृथिव्याम् on earth, अत्यर्थम् exceedingly, अनुत्तमाम् unsurpassed, ताम् that city.
explanation: The city echoed with the sounds of trumpets, mrudangas, vinas and panavas. There was no city on earth superior to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: विमानमिव सिद्धानां तपसाधिगतं दिवि । सुनिवेशितवेश्मान्तां नरोत्तमसमावृताम् ।।1.5.19।।
transliteration: vimānamiva siddhānāṃ tapasādhigataṃ divi | suniveśitaveśmāntāṃ narottamasamāvṛtām
translation: दिवि in heaven, तपसा through austerities, अधिगतम् acquired, सिद्धानाम् by siddhas, विमानमिव like an aerialcar, सुनिवेशितवेश्मान्ताम् of perfectly constructed palaces, नरोत्तमसमावृताम् inhabited by noblest of men.
explanation: Like an aerial car acquired by the siddhas in heaven through their austerities, the palaces were perfectly constructed in rows and inhabited by the noblest of men.

shloka_text: ﻿ये च बाणैर्न विध्यन्ति विविक्तमपरापरम् । शब्दवेध्यं च विततं लघुहस्ता विशारदा: ।।1.5.20।। सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणां मत्तानां नर्दतां वने । हन्तारो निशितैश्शस्त्रैर्बलाद्बाहुबलैरपि ।।1.5.21।। तादृशानां सहस्रैस्तामभिपूर्णां महारथै: । पुरीमावासयामास राजा दशरथस्तदा ।।1.5.22।।
transliteration: ﻿ye ca bāṇairna vidhyanti viviktamaparāparam | śabdavedhyaṃ ca vitataṃ laghuhastā viśāradā:  siṃhavyāghravarāhāṇāṃ mattānāṃ nardatāṃ vane | hantāro niśitaiśśastrairbalādbāhubalairapi  tādṛśānāṃ sahasraistāmabhipūrṇāṃ mahārathai: | purīmāvāsayāmāsa rājā daśarathastadā
translation: ﻿ लघुहस्ता: sharphanded, विशारदा: skilled(in fight), ये who, विविक्तम् solitary person, अपरापरम् one who has no father or son, शब्दवेध्यम् following the sound, विततं च spreading over (the fleeing foe), बाणै: with arrows, न विध्यन्ति would not pierce, वने in the forest, नर्दताम् roaring, मत्तानाम् inebriated, सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणाम् lions, tigers and boars, निशितै: with sharp, शस्त्रै: weapons, बलात् with the strength (of instruments), बाहुबलैरपि with the strength of arms as well, हन्तार: slayers, तादृशानाम् relating to those, महारथै: by maharathas, सहस्रै: in thousands, अभिपूर्णां filled, ताम् that, पुरीम् city of Ayodhya, तदा then, राजा दशरथ: king Dasaratha, आवासयामास inhabited.
explanation: ﻿ The city was inhabited by thousands of warriors known as maharathas. They were skilled archers and sharphanded. They would not pierce with arrows, solitary persons, persons without defence, fleeing foes who could be tracked down through hints from sound. With sharp arrows or with the strength of their arms, they would kill roaring and inebriated lions, tigers, boars etc. in the forest. It was in that city (of Ayodhya) that king Dasaratha lived.

shloka_text: ﻿ये च बाणैर्न विध्यन्ति विविक्तमपरापरम् । शब्दवेध्यं च विततं लघुहस्ता विशारदा: ।।1.5.20।। सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणां मत्तानां नर्दतां वने । हन्तारो निशितैश्शस्त्रैर्बलाद्बाहुबलैरपि ।।1.5.21।। तादृशानां सहस्रैस्तामभिपूर्णां महारथै: । पुरीमावासयामास राजा दशरथस्तदा ।।1.5.22।।

translation: ﻿ लघुहस्ता: sharphanded, विशारदा: skilled(in fight), ये who, विविक्तम् solitary person, अपरापरम् one who has no father or son, शब्दवेध्यम् following the sound, विततं च spreading over (the fleeing foe), बाणै: with arrows, न विध्यन्ति would not pierce, वने in the forest, नर्दताम् roaring, मत्तानाम् inebriated, सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणाम् lions, tigers and boars, निशितै: with sharp, शस्त्रै: weapons, बलात् with the strength (of instruments), बाहुबलैरपि with the strength of arms as well, हन्तार: slayers, तादृशानाम् relating to those, महारथै: by maharathas, सहस्रै: in thousands, अभिपूर्णां filled, ताम् that, पुरीम् city of Ayodhya, तदा then, राजा दशरथ: king Dasaratha, आवासयामास inhabited.
explanation: ﻿ The city was inhabited by thousands of warriors known as maharathas. They were skilled archers and sharphanded. They would not pierce with arrows, solitary persons, persons without defence, fleeing foes who could be tracked down through hints from sound. With sharp arrows or with the strength of their arms, they would kill roaring and inebriated lions, tigers, boars etc. in the forest. It was in that city (of Ayodhya) that king Dasaratha lived.

shloka_text: ये च बाणैर्न विध्यन्ति विविक्तमपरापरम् । शब्दवेध्यं च विततं लघुहस्ता विशारदा: ।।1.5.20।। सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणां मत्तानां नर्दतां वने । हन्तारो निशितैश्शस्त्रैर्बलाद्बाहुबलैरपि ।।1.5.21।। तादृशानां सहस्रैस्तामभिपूर्णां महारथै: । पुरीमावासयामास राजा दशरथस्तदा ।।1.5.22।।
transliteration: ye ca bāṇairna vidhyanti viviktamaparāparam | śabdavedhyaṃ ca vitataṃ laghuhastā viśāradā:  siṃhavyāghravarāhāṇāṃ mattānāṃ nardatāṃ vane | hantāro niśitaiśśastrairbalādbāhubalairapi  tādṛśānāṃ sahasraistāmabhipūrṇāṃ mahārathai: | purīmāvāsayāmāsa rājā daśarathastadā
translation: लघुहस्ता: sharphanded, विशारदा: skilled(in fight), ये who, विविक्तम् solitary person, अपरापरम् one who has no father or son, शब्दवेध्यम् following the sound, विततं च spreading over (the fleeing foe), बाणै: with arrows, न विध्यन्ति would not pierce, वने in the forest, नर्दताम् roaring, मत्तानाम् inebriated, सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणाम् lions, tigers and boars, निशितै: with sharp, शस्त्रै: weapons, बलात् with the strength (of instruments), बाहुबलैरपि with the strength of arms as well, हन्तार: slayers, तादृशानाम् relating to those, महारथै: by maharathas, सहस्रै: in thousands, अभिपूर्णां filled, ताम् that, पुरीम् city of Ayodhya, तदा then, राजा दशरथ: king Dasaratha, आवासयामास inhabited.
explanation: The city was inhabited by thousands of warriors known as maharathas. They were skilled archers and sharphanded. They would not pierce with arrows, solitary persons, persons without defence, fleeing foes who could be tracked down through hints from sound. With sharp arrows or with the strength of their arms, they would kill roaring and inebriated lions, tigers, boars etc. in the forest. It was in that city (of Ayodhya) that king Dasaratha lived.

shloka_text: तामग्निमद्भिर्गुणवद्भिरावृतां द्विजोत्तमैर्वेदषडङ्गपारगै: । सहस्रदैस्सत्यरतैर्महात्मभि र्महर्षिकल्पै ऋषिभिश्च केवलै: ।।1.5.23।।
transliteration: tāmagnimadbhirguṇavadbhirāvṛtāṃ dvijottamairvedaṣaḍaṅgapāragai: | sahasradaissatyaratairmahātmabhi rmaharṣikalpai ṛṣibhiśca kevalai:
translation: अग्निमद्भि: by brahmins worshipping the  sacrificial fire, गुणवद्भि: endowed with virtues, वेदषडङ्गपारगै: versed in four vedas and six vedangas (branches of learning at the end of vedas), सहस्रदै: offering charity in thousands, सत्यरतै: devoted to truth, महात्मभि: by exceedingly wise, महर्षिकल्पै: resembling divine sages, केवलै: ऋषिभि: च by unique sages, द्विजोत्तमै: by excellent dwijas (brahmana, kshatriya and vaisyas), आवृताम् filled with, ताम् that Ayodhya.
explanation: That city (of Ayodhya) was filled with excellent dwijas (brahmana, kshatriya and vaisyas) performing rituals of sacrificial fire, virtuous and wellversed in the Vedas and Vedangas. They were generous, truthful and dignified. They were almost equal to rishis and maharshis. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे पञ्चमस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the fifth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: . तस्यां पुर्यामयोध्यायां वेदवित्सर्वसङ्ग्रह: । दीर्घदर्शी महातेजा: पौरजानपदप्रिय: ।।1.6.1।। इक्ष्वाकूणामतिरथो यज्वा धर्मरतो वशी । महर्षिकल्पो राजर्षिस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुत: ।।1.6.2।। बलवान्निहतामित्रो मित्रवान्विजितेन्द्रिय: । धनैश्च सङ्ग्रहैश्चान्यैश्शक्रवैश्रवणोपम: ।।1.6.3।। यथा मनुर्महातेजा लोकस्य परिरक्षिता । तथा दशरथो राजा वसञ्जगदपालयत् ।। 1.6.4।।

translation: वेदवित् wellversed in vedas, सर्वसङ्ग्रह: commanding all resources, दीर्घदर्शी far sighted, महातेजा: possessing great splendour, पौरजानपदप्रिय: dear to the inhabitants in towns and villages, इक्ष्वाकूणाम् among Ikshvaku kings, अतिरथ: a great charioteer capable of fighting with many maharathas singlehandedly, यज्वा performer of sacrifices, धर्मरत: devoted to the practice of dharma, वशी in full control over his subjects, महर्षिकल्प: equal to a great sage, राजर्षि: royal saint, त्रिषु लोकेषु in the three worlds (Bhooloka, Bhuvarloka, Suvarloka), विश्रुत: renowned, बलवान् possessed of strength, निहतामित्र: destroyer of enemies, मित्रवान् having friends, विजितेन्द्रिय: having perfect control over his senses, धनैश्च with wealth, अन्यै: other riches, सङ्ग्रहैश्च accumulated possessions, शक्रवैश्रवणोपम: comparable to Indra and Kubera, राजा दशरथ: king Dasaratha, तस्याम् in that, (अयोद्यया) पुर्याम् city of Ayodhya, वसन् living, लोकस्य for the entire world, परिरक्षिता protector, महातेजा: highly powerful, मनु: Manu, यथा as, तथा in that manner, जगत् world, अपालयत् ruled.
explanation: From that city of Ayodhya, king Dasaratha ruled the entire world, following the tradition of Manu who was a highly powerful protector of the people. Dasaratha was well versed in the Vedas. He commanded all resources. Farsighted, he possessed great prowess. He was dear to the inhabitants of towns and villages. Among Ikshvaku kings, he was a great charioteer capable of fighting with many maharathas singlehanded. He performed many sacrifices and was devoted to the practice of dharma. He was in full control over his subjects. He was a great sage, a royal saint and renowned in the three worlds (Bhooloka, Bhuvarloka and Suvarloka). He was mighty. He was a destroyer of enemies. He had scores of good friends. He had perfect control over his senses. In riches, he was comparable to Indra and Kubera.
comments: Description of riches, comforts, etc of the subjects of the kingdom during Dasaratha's reign

shloka_text: तेन सत्याभिसन्धेन त्रिवर्गमनुतिष्ठता । पालिता सा पुरी श्रेष्ठा इन्द्रेणेवामरावती ।।1.6.5।।
transliteration: tena satyābhisandhena trivargamanutiṣṭhatā | pālitā sā purī śreṣṭhā indreṇevāmarāvatī
translation: सत्याभिसन्धेन bound by his promise, त्रिवर्गम् dharma, artha and kama (righteousness, attainment of riches or worldly prosperity and pleasure considered as three of the four ends of life, the fourth one being moksha), अनुतिष्ठता by the strict followerm, तेन by the king Dasaratha, श्रेष्ठा best of cities, सा पुरी that city of Ayodhya, इन्द्रेण by Indra, अमरावती  Amaravati, इव like, पालिता ruled.
explanation: King Dasaratha, who always kept his word and followed dharma, attained prosperity and pleasure in equal measure by righteous means ruled that best of the cities as Indra ruled Amaravati.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्पुरवरे हृष्टा धर्मात्मानो बहुश्रुता: । नरास्तुष्टा धनैस्स्वैस्स्वैरलुब्धास्सत्यवादिन: ।।1.6.6।।
transliteration: tasminpuravare hṛṣṭā dharmātmāno bahuśrutā: | narāstuṣṭā dhanaissvaissvairalubdhāssatyavādina:
translation: तस्मिन् In that, पुरवरे excellent city, नरा: people, हृष्टा: happy, धर्मात्मान: virtuous, बहुश्रुता: widely learned, स्वै:स्वै: of their own, धनै: riches and possessions, तुष्टा: contended, अलुब्धा: without greed, सत्यवादिन: were speaking truth.
explanation: The people living in that excellent city were happy, virtuous, wellread (in the Vedas and the sastras) and content with the possessions of their own. They were free from avarice. And always spoke the truth.

shloka_text: नाल्पसन्निचय: कश्चिदासीत्तस्मिन् पुरोत्तमे । कुटुम्बी यो ह्यसिद्धार्थोऽगवाश्वधनधान्यवान् ।।1.6.7।।
transliteration: nālpasannicaya: kaścidāsīttasmin purottame | kuṭumbī yo hyasiddhārtho'gavāśvadhanadhānyavān
translation: तस्मिन् In that, पुरोत्तमे best of cities, य: who, अल्पसन्निचय: one who accumulated the  riches in smaller quantities, असिद्धार्थ: had not fulfilled (dharma, artha and kama), अगवाश्वधनधान्यवान् prosperous in wealth of foodgrains, cattle and horses, कुटुम्बी householder, कश्चित् even one, नासीत् did not exist.
explanation: In that best of cities, there was not even a single householder who had not adequate wealth or who had not achieved dharma, artha and kama or who did not possess the wealth of foodgrains, cattle and horses.

shloka_text: कामी वा न कदर्यो वा नृशंस: पुरुष: क्वचित् । द्रष्टुं शक्यमयोध्यायान्नाविद्वान्न च नास्तिक: ।।1.6.8।।
transliteration: kāmī vā na kadaryo vā nṛśaṃsa: puruṣa: kvacit | draṣṭuṃ śakyamayodhyāyānnāvidvānna ca nāstika:
translation: कामी lustful person, न कदर्यो वा miser (who tortures parents, wife, sons and sisters), नृशंस: cruel, पुरुष: man, अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, क्वचित् anywhere, द्रष्टुम् to be seen, न शक्यम् not possible, अविद्वान् न not scholarly, नास्तिक: atheist, न not.
explanation: The lustful, the miserly, the unscholarly and atheists were not to be seen anywhere in the city of Ayodhya.

shloka_text: सर्वे नराश्च नार्यश्च धर्मशीलास्सुसंयता: । उदिताश्शीलवृत्ताभ्यां महर्षय इवामला: ।।1.6.9।।
transliteration: sarve narāśca nāryaśca dharmaśīlāssusaṃyatā: | uditāśśīlavṛttābhyāṃ maharṣaya ivāmalā:
translation: सर्वे all, नराश्च men, नार्यश्च women, धर्मशीला: righteous in conduct, सुसंयता: fully selfcontrolled, शीलवृत्ताभ्याम् with good conduct and behaviour, उदिता: prospering,  महर्षय: इव like maharshis, अमला: pure.
explanation: All men and women (in the city) were of righteous conduct, fully selfcontrolled and prosperous with good conduct and behaviour. They were pure like maharshis.

shloka_text: नाकुण्डली नामकुटी नास्रग्वी नाल्पभोगवान् । नामृष्टो नानुलिप्ताङ्गो नासुगन्धश्च विद्यते ।।1.6.10।।
transliteration: nākuṇḍalī nāmakuṭī nāsragvī nālpabhogavān | nāmṛṣṭo nānuliptāṅgo nāsugandhaśca vidyate
translation: अकुण्डली without earornaments, न विद्यते there was none, अमकुटी without coronet, न  none, अस्रग्वी without wearing garlands, न none, अल्पभोगवान् deficient in worldly enjoyments, न none, अमृष्ट: unclean (cleansed without applying oil before bath), न none, नानुलिप्ताङ्ग: without having his limbs anointed, असुगन्धश्च without applying fragrant substances on his body, न none.
explanation: In the city, there was none without earornaments, without coronet, without wearing garlands and none unclean. And none without the anointment of fragrants on the body.

shloka_text: नामृष्टभोजी नादाता नाप्यनङ्गदनिष्कधृक् । नाहस्ताभरणो वाऽपि दृश्यते नाप्यनात्मवान् ।।1.6.11।।
transliteration: nāmṛṣṭabhojī nādātā nāpyanaṅgadaniṣkadhṛk | nāhastābharaṇo vā'pi dṛśyate nāpyanātmavān
translation: अमृष्टभोजी eating the food without full satisfaction, न दृश्यते cannot be seen, अदाता  person without charitable nature, न none, अनङ्गदनिष्कधृक् अपि also without wearing bracelets on the upper arms and ornament around the neck, न none, अहस्ताभरणो वाऽपि without wearing handornaments, न none, अनात्मवानपि one who had not restrained his self, न none.
explanation: (In the city of Ayodhya) there was no one who did not eat food to full satisfaction and was not charitable. None was found without wearing ornaments on the hands and bracelets on the upper arms and around the neck. Also no one could be seen who had not restrained his passions and emotions.

shloka_text: नानाहिताग्निर्नायज्वा न क्षुद्रो वा न तस्कर: । कश्चिदासीदयोध्यायान्न च निर्वृत्तसङ्कर: ।।1.6.12।।
transliteration: nānāhitāgnirnāyajvā na kṣudro vā na taskara: | kaścidāsīdayodhyāyānna ca nirvṛttasaṅkara:
translation: अयोध्यायाम् In the city of Ayodhya, अनाहिताग्नि: person who did not kindle sacrificial fire, न  आसीत् did not exist, अयज्वा not performing sacrifices, न none, क्षुद्र: meanminded, न none, तस्कर: thief, न none, निर्वृत्तसङ्कर: improper descent of mixed castes, कश्चित्    even one, न none.
explanation: In the city of Ayodhya there was none who did not kindle the sacrificial fire. There was none who did not perform a sacrifice. There were no thieves or meanminded persons or persons of improper descent of mixed castes.

shloka_text: स्वकर्मनिरता नित्यं ब्राह्मणा विजितेन्द्रिया: । दानाध्ययनशीलाश्च संयताश्च परिग्रहे ।।1.6.13।।
transliteration: svakarmaniratā nityaṃ brāhmaṇā vijitendriyā: | dānādhyayanaśīlāśca saṃyatāśca parigrahe
translation: ब्राह्मणा: The brahmins, नित्यम् always, स्वकर्मनिरता: interested in the performance of their duties, विजितेन्द्रिया: having control over senses, दानाध्ययनशीला:च having the nature of charity and selfstudy, संयताश्च selfcontrolled with regard to, परिग्रहे accepting charity,  संयताश्च the marital relations were  confined, परिग्रहे to their wives.
explanation: The brahmins were always interested in the performance of their duties. They had control over their senses. They were charitable and studious. They were selfcontrolled  while accepting charity and maintaining marital relations.

shloka_text: न नास्तिको नानृतको न कश्चिदबहुश्रुत: । नासूयको न चाऽशक्तो नाविद्वान्विद्यते तदा ।।1.6.14।।
transliteration: na nāstiko nānṛtako na kaścidabahuśruta: | nāsūyako na cā'śakto nāvidvānvidyate tadā
translation: तदा during that period, कश्चित् even one, नास्तिक: atheist, न none, अनृतक: speaking  untruthful statements, न none, अबहुश्रुत: not very learned in sastras, न none, असूयक: a detractor who finds faults in others (a jealous man), न none, अशक्त: incompetent, न  none, अविद्वान् not scholarly, न none.
explanation: That time there was no atheist, no liar and none ignorant of the sastras. There was no one who was jealous, incompetent or illiterate.

shloka_text: नाषडङ्गविदत्रासीन्नाव्रतो नासहस्रद: । न दीन: क्षिप्तचित्तो वा व्यथितो वाऽपि कश्चन ।।1.6.15।।
transliteration: nāṣaḍaṅgavidatrāsīnnāvrato nāsahasrada: | na dīna: kṣiptacitto vā vyathito vā'pi kaścana
translation: अत्र in that city of Ayodhya, अषडङ्गवित् not wellversed in the six vedangas (Siksha, Vyakarana, Chhandas, Nirukta, Jyotisha and Kalpa), नासीत् did not exist, अव्रत: who did not perform religious vows, न none, असहस्रद: who would not donate in thousands, न none, दीन: distressed or miserable, क्षिप्तचित्तो वा agitated mind, न none, व्यथित: vexed, कश्चन not even one.
explanation: There was no brahmin who was not well versed in the Vedangas or who did not perform religious vows. There was not even one  who would not donate in thousands. There was no one distracted or depressed.

shloka_text: कश्चिन्नरो वा नारी वा नाश्रीमान्नाप्यरूपवान् । द्रष्टुं शक्यमयोध्यायां नापि राजन्यभक्तिमान् ।।1.6.16।।
transliteration: kaścinnaro vā nārī vā nāśrīmānnāpyarūpavān | draṣṭuṃ śakyamayodhyāyāṃ nāpi rājanyabhaktimān
translation: अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, नरो वा man, नारी वा or woman, कश्चित् even one, अश्रीमान् not endowed with wealth, अरूपवान् अपि without beauty, द्रष्टुम् to see , न शक्यम् not possible, राजनि in the king, अभक्तिमान् not devoted, न none.
explanation: In Ayodhya, there was no man or woman who was not endowed with wealth or beauty. It was not possible to see any one who had no devotion for the king.

shloka_text: वर्णेष्वग्र्यचतुर्थेषु देवतातिथिपूजका:। कृतज्ञाश्च वदान्याश्च शूरा विक्रमसंयुता: ।।1.6.17।। दीर्घायुषो नरास्सर्वे धर्मं सत्यं च संश्रिता: । सहिता: पुत्रपौत्रैश्च नित्यं स्त्रीभि: पुरोत्तमे ।।1.6.18।।
transliteration: varṇeṣvagryacaturtheṣu devatātithipūjakā:| kṛtajñāśca vadānyāśca śūrā vikramasaṃyutā:  dīrghāyuṣo narāssarve dharmaṃ satyaṃ ca saṃśritā: | sahitā: putrapautraiśca nityaṃ strībhi: purottame
translation: पुरोत्तमे in that best of cities, अग्र्यचतुर्थेषु in the first of the four orders, वर्णेषु in  castes, सर्वे all, नरा: men, देवतातिथिपूजका: worshipped the gods and guests, कृतज्ञाश्च endowed with gratitude, वदान्याश्च munificient, शूरा: heroic, विक्रमसंयुता: possessing prowess, दीर्घायुष: longlived, नित्यम् always, पुत्रपौत्रै: with sons and grandsons, स्त्रीभि: wives, च सहिता: surrounded by, धर्मम् righteousness, सत्यम् च truth, संश्रिता: resorted  to.
explanation: There in Ayodhya the best of cities, the first of the four castes (brahmins) used to worship gods and guests. They had the sense of gratitude. They were munificient, heroic and possessed prowess. They lived long. They were righteous and truthful. And they lived together with their sons, grandsons and wives.

shloka_text: वर्णेष्वग्र्यचतुर्थेषु देवतातिथिपूजका:। कृतज्ञाश्च वदान्याश्च शूरा विक्रमसंयुता: ।।1.6.17।। दीर्घायुषो नरास्सर्वे धर्मं सत्यं च संश्रिता: । सहिता: पुत्रपौत्रैश्च नित्यं स्त्रीभि: पुरोत्तमे ।।1.6.18।।
transliteration: varṇeṣvagryacaturtheṣu devatātithipūjakā:| kṛtajñāśca vadānyāśca śūrā vikramasaṃyutā:  dīrghāyuṣo narāssarve dharmaṃ satyaṃ ca saṃśritā: | sahitā: putrapautraiśca nityaṃ strībhi: purottame
translation: पुरोत्तमे in that best of cities, अग्र्यचतुर्थेषु in the first of the four orders, वर्णेषु in  castes, सर्वे all, नरा: men, देवतातिथिपूजका: worshipped the gods and guests, कृतज्ञाश्च endowed with gratitude, वदान्याश्च munificient, शूरा: heroic, विक्रमसंयुता: possessing prowess, दीर्घायुष: longlived, नित्यम् always, पुत्रपौत्रै: with sons and grandsons, स्त्रीभि: wives, च सहिता: surrounded by, धर्मम् righteousness, सत्यम् च truth, संश्रिता: resorted  to.
explanation: There in Ayodhya the best of cities, the first of the four castes (brahmins) used to worship gods and guests. They had the sense of gratitude. They were munificient, heroic and possessed prowess. They lived long. They were righteous and truthful. And they lived together with their sons, grandsons and wives.

shloka_text: क्षत्रं ब्रह्ममुखं चासीद्वैश्या: क्षत्रमनुव्रता: । शूद्रास्स्वधर्मनिरतास्त्रीन्वर्णानुपचारिण: ।।1.6.19।।
transliteration: kṣatraṃ brahmamukhaṃ cāsīdvaiśyā: kṣatramanuvratā: | śūdrāssvadharmaniratāstrīnvarṇānupacāriṇa:
translation: क्षत्रम् the kshatriya (warrior) caste, ब्रह्ममुखम् आसीत् was obedient to brahmins, वैश्या: merchants, क्षत्रम् warriors, अनुव्रता: followed, शूद्रा: sudras, त्रीन् three, वर्णान् castes, उपचारिण: assisted, स्वधर्मनिरता: fully occupied in their respective professions.
explanation: The kshatriyas were obedient to brahmins and vaisyas followed kshatriyas. Sudras assisted the three castes and all were fully occupied in their respective professions.

shloka_text: सा तेनेक्ष्वाकुनाथेन पुरी सुपरिरक्षिता । यथा पुरस्तान्मनुना मानवेन्द्रेण धीमता ।।1.6.20।।
transliteration: sā tenekṣvākunāthena purī suparirakṣitā | yathā purastānmanunā mānavendreṇa dhīmatā
translation: सा पुरी that city, पुरस्तात् previously, मानवेन्द्रेण foremost among men, धीमता by the supreme person in wisdom, मनुना by Manu, यथा in the manner administered as, तेन by that, इक्ष्वाकुनाथेन protector of Ikshvaku race emperor Dasaratha, सुपरिरक्षिता was ably governed.
explanation: That city was ably governed by Dasaratha, scion of the Ikshvakus, in the same way as it was  previously administered by (Manu), the foremost among men and and the most intelligent.

shloka_text: योधानामग्निकल्पानां पेशलानाममर्षिणाम् । सम्पूर्णा कृतविद्यानां गुहा केसरिणामिव ।।1.6.21।।
transliteration: yodhānāmagnikalpānāṃ peśalānāmamarṣiṇām | sampūrṇā kṛtavidyānāṃ guhā kesariṇāmiva
translation: अग्निकल्पानाम् of men comparable to a flaming fire, पेशलानाम् of experts, अमर्षिणाम्  determined, कृतविद्यानाम् accomplished in the learning of science of arms, योधानाम् warrior, केसरिणाम् resembling lions, गुहा इव like mountain caves, सम्पूर्णा filled with.
explanation: It abounded with warriors, like a cave with lions. They were almost like flaming fire, the most determined among experts and accomplished in learning (the science of arms).

shloka_text: काम्भोजविषये जातैर्बाह्लीकैश्च हयोत्तमै: । वनायुजैर्नदीजैश्च पूर्णा हरिहयोत्तमै:।।1.6.22।।
transliteration: kāmbhojaviṣaye jātairbāhlīkaiśca hayottamai: | vanāyujairnadījaiśca pūrṇā harihayottamai:
translation: काम्भोजविषये in the region of Kambhoja, जातैः born, बाह्लीकै: in the region of Bahlika, वनायुजै: in the region of Vanayu, नदीजैश्च in the region of Sindhu, हरिहयोत्तमै: by excellent horses like the Indra's horse called Ucchaisrava, हयोत्तमै: by excellent horses, पूर्णा full of.
explanation: The city was full of excellent horses born in the regions of Kambhoja, Bahlika, Vanayu and Sindhu, similar to that of Indra's horse (called Ucchaisrava).

shloka_text: विन्ध्यपर्वतजैर्मत्तै: पूर्णा हैमवतैरपि । मदान्वितैरतिबलैर्मातङ्गै: पर्वतोपमै: ।।1.6.23।। ऐरावतकुलीनैश्च महापद्मकुलैस्तथा । अञ्जनादपि निष्पन्नैर्वामनादपि च द्विपैः ।।1.6.24।।
transliteration: vindhyaparvatajairmattai: pūrṇā haimavatairapi | madānvitairatibalairmātaṅgai: parvatopamai:  airāvatakulīnaiśca mahāpadmakulaistathā | añjanādapi niṣpannairvāmanādapi ca dvipaiḥ
translation: मत्तै: by intoxicated, विन्ध्यपर्वतजै: born in Vindhya mountains, मातङ्गै: elephants, मदान्वितै: associated with rut flowing from the temples, अतिबलै: by enormously strong, पर्वतोपमै: like unto mountains, हैमवतैरपि born in Himavat mountains, ऐरावतकुलीनैश्च born from  good breed of Airavata, द्विपै: च with elephants, तथा and, महापद्मकुलै: by those born in Mahapadma breed, अञ्जनात् from Anjana (one of the Diggajas guarding a quarter), निष्पन्नै: breed, वामनादपि from Vamana also (name of the elephant that presides over south), पूर्णा full of.
explanation: It was full of intoxicated elephants born in Vindhya mountains, elephants of enormous strength looking like mountains and born in the Himalayas. Elephants of good breed hailing from the family of  Airavata (Indra's vehicle), Mahapadma, Anjana and Vamana.

shloka_text: विन्ध्यपर्वतजैर्मत्तै: पूर्णा हैमवतैरपि । मदान्वितैरतिबलैर्मातङ्गै: पर्वतोपमै: ।।1.6.23।। ऐरावतकुलीनैश्च महापद्मकुलैस्तथा । अञ्जनादपि निष्पन्नैर्वामनादपि च द्विपैः ।।1.6.24।।
transliteration: vindhyaparvatajairmattai: pūrṇā haimavatairapi | madānvitairatibalairmātaṅgai: parvatopamai:  airāvatakulīnaiśca mahāpadmakulaistathā | añjanādapi niṣpannairvāmanādapi ca dvipaiḥ
translation: मत्तै: by intoxicated, विन्ध्यपर्वतजै: born in Vindhya mountains, मातङ्गै: elephants, मदान्वितै: associated with rut flowing from the temples, अतिबलै: by enormously strong, पर्वतोपमै: like unto mountains, हैमवतैरपि born in Himavat mountains, ऐरावतकुलीनैश्च born from  good breed of Airavata, द्विपै: च with elephants, तथा and, महापद्मकुलै: by those born in Mahapadma breed, अञ्जनात् from Anjana (one of the Diggajas guarding a quarter), निष्पन्नै: breed, वामनादपि from Vamana also (name of the elephant that presides over south), पूर्णा full of.
explanation: It was full of intoxicated elephants born in Vindhya mountains, elephants of enormous strength looking like mountains and born in the Himalayas. Elephants of good breed hailing from the family of  Airavata (Indra's vehicle), Mahapadma, Anjana and Vamana.

shloka_text: भद्रैर्मन्द्रैर्मृगैश्चैव भद्रमन्द्रमृगैस्तथा। भद्रमन्द्रैर्भद्रमृगैर्मृगमन्द्रैश्च सा पुरी। नित्यमत्तैस्सदा पूर्णा नागैरचलसन्निभै:।।1.6.25।।
transliteration: bhadrairmandrairmṛgaiścaiva bhadramandramṛgaistathā| bhadramandrairbhadramṛgairmṛgamandraiśca sā purī| nityamattaissadā pūrṇā nāgairacalasannibhai:
translation: सा पुरी that city, भद्रै: Bhadra, मन्द्रै: Mandra, मृगैश्चैव Mriga races, भद्रमन्द्रमृगै: interbreed of these three races, भद्रमन्द्रै: interbred of Bhadra and Mandra, भद्रमृगै: Bhadra and Mriga, मृगमन्द्रैश्च Mriga and Mandra, नित्यमत्तै: always intoxicated, अचलसन्निभै: like  mountains, नागै: elephants, सदा always, पूर्णा full.
explanation: The city (of Ayodhya) was always full of intoxicated elephants resembling mountains belonging to the races of Bhadra, Mandra, Mriga and interbreed of these three races, interbreed of races of Bhadra and Mandra, Bhadra and Mriga, Mriga and Mandra.

shloka_text: सा योजने च द्वे भूय: सत्यनामा प्रकाशते । यस्यां दशरथो राजा वसन् जगदपालयत् ।।1.6.26।।
transliteration: sā yojane ca dve bhūya: satyanāmā prakāśate | yasyāṃ daśaratho rājā vasan jagadapālayat
translation: दशरथ: राजा king Dasaratha, यस्याम् in which city, वसन् living, राज्यम् kingdom, अपालयत् ruled, सा that Ayodhya, भूय: outside, द्वे योजने distance of two yojanas, सत्यनामा worthy of its name, प्रकाशते was shining.
explanation: The city where king Dasaratha lived and ruled, spread over a distance of sixteen miles. And it was worthy of its name.

shloka_text: तां पुरीं स महातेजा राजा दशरथो महान् । शशास शमितामित्रो नक्षत्राणीव चन्द्रमा: ।।1.6.27।।
transliteration: tāṃ purīṃ sa mahātejā rājā daśaratho mahān | śaśāsa śamitāmitro nakṣatrāṇīva candramā:
translation: महातेजा: possessing great splendour, महान् revered, राजा दशरथ: king Dasaratha, शमितामित्र: by soothing  his foes, ताम् that, पुरीम् city of Ayodhya, चन्द्रमा: Moon, नक्षत्राणीव like stars, शशास ruled.
explanation: Mighty king Dasaratha, of great brilliance vanquished his foes and ruled the city like the Moon over the  stars.

shloka_text: तां सत्यनामां दृढतोरणार्गलां गृहैर्विचित्रैरुपशोभितां शिवाम् । पुरीमयोध्यां नृसहस्रसङ्कुलां शशास वै शक्रसमो महीपति: ।।1.6.28।।
transliteration: tāṃ satyanāmāṃ dṛḍhatoraṇārgalāṃ gṛhairvicitrairupaśobhitāṃ śivām | purīmayodhyāṃ nṛsahasrasaṅkulāṃ śaśāsa vai śakrasamo mahīpati:
translation: दृढतोरणार्गलाम् having strong gates and solid locks, विचित्रै: by excellent, गृहै: edifices, उपशोभिताम् adorned, शिवाम् auspicious, नृसहस्रसङ्कुलाम् teeming with thousands of men, सत्यनामाम् true to its name, अयोध्यां invincible, पुरीम् city of Ayodhya, शक्रसम: equal to Indra, महीपति: king Dasaratha, शशास वै ruled.
explanation: The king who equalled Indra (in splendour) ruled the invincible city of Ayodhya true to its name with its strong gates and solid locks. It was adorned with wonderful edifices teeming with thousands of men. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे षष्ठस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the sixth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana  the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: . तस्यामात्या गुणैरासन्निक्ष्वाकोस्तु महात्मन: । मन्त्रज्ञाश्चेङ्गितज्ञाश्च नित्यं प्रियहिते रता: ।।1.7.1।।
transliteration: . tasyāmātyā guṇairāsannikṣvākostu mahātmana: | mantrajñāśceṅgitajñāśca nityaṃ priyahite ratā:
translation: महात्मन: of the magnanimous, तस्य his, इक्ष्वाको: of the descendent of Ikshvaku, गुणै:  with virtues, मन्त्रज्ञाश्च competent counsellors, इङ्गितज्ञाश्च skilled in judging motives from the features of the face, नित्यम् always, प्रियहिते doing all that was dear and could bring welfare to the king, रता: intent on, अमात्या: ministers, आसन् existed.
explanation: The ministers of the great descendent of the Ikshvakus were endowed with all virtues. They were competent counsellors, skilled in judging motives from facial features and were always intent on doing good and all that was dear and helpful to the king.
comments: King Dasaratha's court and description of the virtues of ministers

shloka_text: अष्टौ बभूवुर्वीरस्य तस्यामात्या यशस्विन: । शुचयश्चानुरक्ताश्च राजकृत्येषु नित्यश: ।।1.7.2।।
transliteration: aṣṭau babhūvurvīrasya tasyāmātyā yaśasvina: | śucayaścānuraktāśca rājakṛtyeṣu nityaśa:
translation: वीरस्य of the mighty, यशस्विन: glorious, तस्य for that king Dasaratha, शुचय: free from blemish in dealings, नित्यशः ever, राजकृत्येषु in royal duties, अनुरक्ताश्च loyally devoted, अष्टौ eight, अमात्या: ministers, बभूवु: had been employed.
explanation: The mighty and glorious (king Dasaratha) had eight ministers who were free from blemish in their dealings and ever devoted to royal duties.

shloka_text: धृष्टिर्जयन्तो विजयस्सिद्धार्थो ह्यर्थसाधक: । अशोको मन्त्रपालश्च सुमन्त्रश्चाष्टमोऽभवत् ।।1.7.3।।
transliteration: dhṛṣṭirjayanto vijayassiddhārtho hyarthasādhaka: | aśoko mantrapālaśca sumantraścāṣṭamo'bhavat
translation: धृष्टि: Dhrishti, जयन्त: Jayanta, विजय: Vijaya, सिद्धार्थ: Siddhartha, अर्थसाधक: Arthasadhaka, अशोक: Ashoka, मन्त्रपालश्च Mantrapala, सुमन्त्रः Sumantra, अष्टम: eigth, अभवत् were present.
explanation: The eight ministers were Dhrishti, Jayanta,Vijaya, Siddhartha, Arthasadhaka, Ashoka, Mantrapala and Sumantra.

shloka_text: ऋत्विजौ द्वावभिमतौ तस्याऽऽस्तामृषिसत्तमौ । वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च मन्त्रिणश्च तथापरे ।।1.7.4।।
transliteration: ṛtvijau dvāvabhimatau tasyā''stāmṛṣisattamau | vasiṣṭho vāmadevaśca mantriṇaśca tathāpare
translation: तस्य for him, वसिष्ठ: Vasihta, वामदेव: च and Vamadeva, द्वौ two, ऋषिसत्तमौ excellent rishis, अभिमतौ highly desired, ऋत्विजौ family priests, आस्ताम् existed, तथा and, अपरे some other, मन्त्रिणश्च counsellors also.
explanation: He had two wellchosen excellent rishis, Vasishta and Vamadeva, as family priests besides some other counsellors.

shloka_text: विद्याविनीता ह्रीमन्त: कुशला नियतेन्द्रिया: । श्रीमन्तश्च महात्मानश्शास्त्रज्ञा दृढविक्रमा: ।।1.7.5।। कीर्तिमन्त: प्रणिहिता: यथावचनकारिण: । तेज: क्षमायश:प्राप्ता स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिण: ।।1.7.6।।
transliteration: vidyāvinītā hrīmanta: kuśalā niyatendriyā: | śrīmantaśca mahātmānaśśāstrajñā dṛḍhavikramā:  kīrtimanta: praṇihitā: yathāvacanakāriṇa: | teja: kṣamāyaśa:prāptā smitapūrvābhibhāṣiṇa:
translation: विद्याविनीता: well educated in all branches of knowledge, ह्रीमन्त: those who feel ashamed to do unjust acts, कुशला: proficient, नियतेन्द्रिया: those having restrained senses, श्रीमन्तश्च wealthy, महात्मान: illustrious, शास्त्रज्ञा: versed in shastras, दृढविक्रमा: steadfast in  prowess, कीर्तिमन्त: renowned, प्रणिहिता: fixing their attention on their thoughts, यथावचनकारिण: doing in accordance with word, तेज:क्षमायश:प्राप्ता: possessing splendour forgiveness and fame, स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिण: speaking with a smile.
explanation: They were welleducated in all branches of knowledge and deemed unjust acts shameful. They were renowned, proficient, versed in sastras, wealthy and magnanimous. They had their senses restrained and their deeds were in accordance with their words. They acted with determination. They were brilliant, forgiving and reputed. And always spoke with a smile.

shloka_text: विद्याविनीता ह्रीमन्त: कुशला नियतेन्द्रिया: । श्रीमन्तश्च महात्मानश्शास्त्रज्ञा दृढविक्रमा: ।।1.7.5।। कीर्तिमन्त: प्रणिहिता: यथावचनकारिण: । तेज: क्षमायश:प्राप्ता स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिण: ।।1.7.6।।
transliteration: vidyāvinītā hrīmanta: kuśalā niyatendriyā: | śrīmantaśca mahātmānaśśāstrajñā dṛḍhavikramā:  kīrtimanta: praṇihitā: yathāvacanakāriṇa: | teja: kṣamāyaśa:prāptā smitapūrvābhibhāṣiṇa:
translation: विद्याविनीता: well educated in all branches of knowledge, ह्रीमन्त: those who feel ashamed to do unjust acts, कुशला: proficient, नियतेन्द्रिया: those having restrained senses, श्रीमन्तश्च wealthy, महात्मान: illustrious, शास्त्रज्ञा: versed in shastras, दृढविक्रमा: steadfast in  prowess, कीर्तिमन्त: renowned, प्रणिहिता: fixing their attention on their thoughts, यथावचनकारिण: doing in accordance with word, तेज:क्षमायश:प्राप्ता: possessing splendour forgiveness and fame, स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिण: speaking with a smile.
explanation: They were welleducated in all branches of knowledge and deemed unjust acts shameful. They were renowned, proficient, versed in sastras, wealthy and magnanimous. They had their senses restrained and their deeds were in accordance with their words. They acted with determination. They were brilliant, forgiving and reputed. And always spoke with a smile.

shloka_text: क्रोधात्कामार्थहेतोर्वा न ब्रूयुरनृतं वच: । तेषामविदितं किञ्चित्स्वेषु नास्ति परेषु वा । क्रियमाणं कृतं वापि चारेणापि चिकीर्षितम् ।।1.7.7।।
transliteration: krodhātkāmārthahetorvā na brūyuranṛtaṃ vaca: | teṣāmaviditaṃ kiñcitsveṣu nāsti pareṣu vā | kriyamāṇaṃ kṛtaṃ vāpi cāreṇāpi cikīrṣitam
translation: क्रोधात् either in anger, कामार्थहेतोर्वा or for the reason of pecuniary gains or for desire, अनृतम् untruth or unjust, वच: word, न ब्रूयु: do not utter, स्वेषु in the midst of their own, परेषु वा or among their enemies, क्रियमाणम् what was being done, कृतं वापि or what had been done, चिकीर्षितम् or intended to be done, तेषाम् for them, चारेण through spies, अविदितम्  unknown, किञ्चित् even little, नास्ति was not there.
explanation: Either in anger or for pecuniary gains or for fulfilment of desire, they never uttered an untrue or unjust word. In the midst of their own people or among their enemies, they knew, through spies everything being done or had been done or intended to be done in future.

shloka_text: कुशला व्यवहारेषु सौहृदेषु परीक्षिता: । प्राप्तकालं तु ते दण्डं धारयेयुस्सुतेष्वपि ।।1.7.8।।
transliteration: kuśalā vyavahāreṣu sauhṛdeṣu parīkṣitā: | prāptakālaṃ tu te daṇḍaṃ dhārayeyussuteṣvapi
translation: ते those ministers, व्यवहारेषु in their dealings, कुशला: competent, सौहृदेषु in friendship, परीक्षिता: tested, सुतेष्वपि even in the matter of sons, प्राप्तकालम् appropriately, दण्डम्   punishment, धारयेयु: used to impose.
explanation: They knew how to deal (with people). They were true to their friends. They used to impose appropriate punishment even on their own sons.

shloka_text: कोशसङ्ग्रहणे युक्ता बलस्य च परिग्रहे । अहितं चापि पुरुषं न विहिंस्युरदूषकम् ।।1.7.9।।
transliteration: kośasaṅgrahaṇe yuktā balasya ca parigrahe | ahitaṃ cāpi puruṣaṃ na vihiṃsyuradūṣakam
translation: कोशसङ्ग्रहणे in replenishing the exchequer, बलस्य army's, परिग्रहे च also holding, युक्ता:  experts, अदूषकम् who did not commit any offence, अहितं पुरुषमपि those who were not wellwishers, न विहिंस्यु: never inflicted with punishment.
explanation: They were experts in replenishing the exchequer and in collecting the army. They never inflicted any punishment even on those who were not their wellwishers, if they did not commit any offence.

shloka_text: वीराश्च नियतोत्साहा राजशास्त्रमनुष्ठिता: । शुचीनां रक्षितारश्च नित्यं विषयवासिनाम् ।।1.7.10।।
transliteration: vīrāśca niyatotsāhā rājaśāstramanuṣṭhitā: | śucīnāṃ rakṣitāraśca nityaṃ viṣayavāsinām
translation: वीराश्च mighty and powerful, नियतोत्साहा: possessing steady perseverance, राजशास्त्रम् state policy, अनुष्ठिता: followed, विषयवासिनाम् living in the state, शुचीनाम् of virtuous people, नित्यम् always, रक्षितारश्च protectors.
explanation: They were heroic. They possessed steady perseverance. They followed the state policy and always protected the virtuous people living in the state.

shloka_text: ब्रह्म क्षत्रमहिंसन्तस्ते कोशं समपूरयन् । सुतीक्ष्णदण्डास्संप्रेक्ष्य पुरुषस्य बलाबलम् ।।1.7.11।।
transliteration: brahma kṣatramahiṃsantaste kośaṃ samapūrayan | sutīkṣṇadaṇḍāssaṃprekṣya puruṣasya balābalam
translation: ब्रह्म brahmanas, क्षत्रम् kshatriyas, अहिंसन्त: did not cause pain (in thought, word and deed), ते they, कोशम् treasury, समपूरयन् filled, पुरुषस्य for a person, बलाबलम् strength and weakness, सम्प्रेक्ष्य investigating, सुतीक्ष्णदण्डा: inflicted  stringent punishments.
explanation: While ensuring that they did not cause pain to brahmanas and kshatriyas (in thought, word and deed), they filled the treasury. They inflicted stringent punishments on a man after examining his strength and weakness.

shloka_text: शुचीनामेकबुद्धीनां सर्वेषां सम्प्रजानताम् । नासीत्पुरे वा राष्ट्रे वा मृषावादी नर: क्वचित् ।।1.7.12।।
transliteration: śucīnāmekabuddhīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ samprajānatām | nāsītpure vā rāṣṭre vā mṛṣāvādī nara: kvacit
translation: शुचीनाम् of the chaste in conduct, एकबुद्धीनाम् unanimous in decisionmaking, सर्वेषाम् of all men, सम्प्रजानताम् administrating the kingdom, पुरे वा either in the city, राष्ट्रे वा or in the kingdom, क्वचित् anywhere, मृषावादी was a liar, नर: man, नासीत् did not exist.
explanation: While the ministers of chaste conduct administered the kingdom with unanimous decisions, there was no one who was a liar, either in the city or in the kingdom.

shloka_text: कश्चिन्न दुष्टस्तत्रासीत्परदाररतो नर: । प्रशान्तं सर्वमेवासीद्राष्ट्रं पुरवरं च तत् ।।1.7.13।।
transliteration: kaścinna duṣṭastatrāsītparadārarato nara: | praśāntaṃ sarvamevāsīdrāṣṭraṃ puravaraṃ ca tat
translation: तत्र in that kingdom, दुष्ट: wicked, परदाररत: enamoured of others' wives, नर: men, कश्चित् even one, नासीत् did not exist, सर्वम् entire, राष्ट्रम् empire, तत् that, पुरवरं च best of cities, प्रशान्तम् आसीत् serenity prevailed.
explanation: In that kingdom no one was wicked or enamoured of others' wives. Serenity prevailed over the entire kingdom including the city of excellence.

shloka_text: सुवाससस्सुवेषाश्च ते च सर्वे सुशीलिन: । हितार्थं च नरेन्द्रस्य जाग्रतो नयचक्षुषा ।।1.7.14।।
transliteration: suvāsasassuveṣāśca te ca sarve suśīlina: | hitārthaṃ ca narendrasya jāgrato nayacakṣuṣā
translation: ते सर्वे all the ministers, सुवासस: wore excellent clothes, सुवेषाश्च well adorned, सुशीलिन: good character, नरेन्द्रस्य king's, हितार्थम् for the welfare of, नयचक्षुषा with politics as their eyes, जाग्रत: vigilant.
explanation: They all were welldressed in fine clothes. They possessed good character with an eye on justice and vigilant about the king's welfare.

shloka_text: गुरोर्गुणगृहीताश्च प्रख्याताश्च पराक्रमे । विदेशेष्वपि विज्ञातास्सर्वतो बुद्धिनिश्चयात् ।।1.7.15।।
transliteration: gurorguṇagṛhītāśca prakhyātāśca parākrame | videśeṣvapi vijñātāssarvato buddhiniścayāt
translation: गुरोः from elderly venerable persons like father, mother etc, गुणगृहीता: receiving inspiration through their virtues, पराक्रमे in the matter of prowess, प्रख्याता: renowned, सर्वत: in all affairs, बुद्धिनिश्चयात् guided by their intellect, विदेशेष्वपि in other countries as well, विज्ञाता: were famous.
explanation: They imbibed virtues from the elderlies. They were renowned in prowess. They were guided by their intellect in all affairs. They were wellknown everywhere.

shloka_text: सन्धिविग्रहतत्त्वज्ञा: प्रकृत्या सम्पदान्विता: ।।1.7.16।। मन्त्रसंवरणे शक्ताश्श्लक्ष्णास्सूक्ष्मासु बुद्धिषु । नीतिशास्त्रविशेषज्ञास्सततं प्रियवादिन: ।।1.7.17।।
transliteration: sandhivigrahatattvajñā: prakṛtyā sampadānvitā:  mantrasaṃvaraṇe śaktāśślakṣṇāssūkṣmāsu buddhiṣu | nītiśāstraviśeṣajñāssatataṃ priyavādina:
translation: सन्धिविग्रहतत्त्वज्ञा: well aware of the real nature of peace or war, प्रकृत्या inherently, सम्पदा by affluent, अन्विता: possessed, मन्त्रसंवरणे in keeping the plans secretly, शक्ता: capable, सूक्ष्मासु in sharp, बुद्धिषु in comprehension, श्लक्ष्णा: gracious, नीतिशास्त्रविशेषज्ञा: distinguished in the science of ethics and morality, सततम् always, प्रियवादिन: spoke pleasing words.
explanation: The ministers were inherently well aware of the real nature of peace or war. They were affluent, adept in keeping secrecy and sharp in comprehending the points (before making any decision). They were experts in the science of ethics and morality. They always spoke  pleasing words.

shloka_text: सन्धिविग्रहतत्त्वज्ञा: प्रकृत्या सम्पदान्विता: ।।1.7.16।। मन्त्रसंवरणे शक्ताश्श्लक्ष्णास्सूक्ष्मासु बुद्धिषु । नीतिशास्त्रविशेषज्ञास्सततं प्रियवादिन: ।।1.7.17।।

translation: सन्धिविग्रहतत्त्वज्ञा: well aware of the real nature of peace or war, प्रकृत्या inherently, सम्पदा by affluent, अन्विता: possessed, मन्त्रसंवरणे in keeping the plans secretly, शक्ता: capable, सूक्ष्मासु in sharp, बुद्धिषु in comprehension, श्लक्ष्णा: gracious, नीतिशास्त्रविशेषज्ञा: distinguished in the science of ethics and morality, सततम् always, प्रियवादिन: spoke pleasing words.
explanation: The ministers were inherently well aware of the real nature of peace or war. They were affluent, adept in keeping secrecy and sharp in comprehending the points (before making any decision). They were experts in the science of ethics and morality. They always spoke  pleasing words.

shloka_text: ईदृशैस्तैरमात्यैस्तु राजा दशरथोऽनघ: । उपपन्नो गुणोपेतैरन्वशासद्वसुन्धराम् ।।1.7.18।।
transliteration: īdṛśaistairamātyaistu rājā daśaratho'nagha: | upapanno guṇopetairanvaśāsadvasundharām
translation: अनघ: free from sin, दशरथ: राजा king Dasaratha, गुणोपेतै: by those endowed with virtues, ईदृशै: with such, अमात्यै: ministers, उपपन्न: surrounded, वसुन्धराम् earth, अन्वशासत् ruled.
explanation: The faultless king Dasaratha, with the assistance of such ministers endowed with virtues, ruled the earth.

shloka_text: अवेक्षमाणश्चारेण प्रजा धर्मेण रञ्जयन् । प्रजानां पालनं कुर्वन्नधर्मान्परिवर्जयन् ।।1.7.19।। विश्रुतस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वदान्यस्सत्यसङ्गर: । स तत्र पुरुषव्याघ्रश्शशास पृथिवीमिमाम् ।।1.7.20।।
transliteration: avekṣamāṇaścāreṇa prajā dharmeṇa rañjayan | prajānāṃ pālanaṃ kurvannadharmānparivarjayan  viśrutastriṣu lokeṣu vadānyassatyasaṅgara: | sa tatra puruṣavyāghraśśaśāsa pṛthivīmimām
translation: पुरुषव्याघ्र: tiger among men, स: king Dasaratha, चारेण with spies, अवेक्षमाण: guarding, प्रजा: the poeple, रञ्जयन् pleasing, प्रजानाम् of people, पालनं कुर्वन् protecting, अधर्मान्  unrighteous ones, परिवर्जयन् deserting, वदान्य: munificient, सत्यसङ्गर: undertaking to uphold truth, त्रिषु लोकेषु in the three worlds, विश्रुत: wellknown, इमाम् this, पृथिवीम् earth, धर्मेण with righteousness, शशास reigned.
explanation: In the three worlds he (Dasaratha) was acclaimed in the three words as munificient and upholder of truth, a tiger among men, who ruled protecting and guarding the people through spies. He. ruled the kingdom with righteousness by deserting irreligious and keeping the subjects happy.

shloka_text: अवेक्षमाणश्चारेण प्रजा धर्मेण रञ्जयन् । प्रजानां पालनं कुर्वन्नधर्मान्परिवर्जयन् ।।1.7.19।। विश्रुतस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वदान्यस्सत्यसङ्गर: । स तत्र पुरुषव्याघ्रश्शशास पृथिवीमिमाम् ।।1.7.20।।

translation: पुरुषव्याघ्र: tiger among men, स: king Dasaratha, चारेण with spies, अवेक्षमाण: guarding, प्रजा: the poeple, रञ्जयन् pleasing, प्रजानाम् of people, पालनं कुर्वन् protecting, अधर्मान्  unrighteous ones, परिवर्जयन् deserting, वदान्य: munificient, सत्यसङ्गर: undertaking to uphold truth, त्रिषु लोकेषु in the three worlds, विश्रुत: wellknown, इमाम् this, पृथिवीम् earth, धर्मेण with righteousness, शशास reigned.
explanation: In the three worlds he (Dasaratha) was acclaimed in the three words as munificient and upholder of truth, a tiger among men, who ruled protecting and guarding the people through spies. He. ruled the kingdom with righteousness by deserting irreligious and keeping the subjects happy.

shloka_text: नाध्यगच्छद्विशिष्टं वा तुल्यं वा शत्रुमात्मन: । मित्रवान्नतसामन्त: प्रतापहतकण्टक: ।।1.7.21।। स शशास जगद्राजा दिवं देवपतिर्यथा ।
transliteration: nādhyagacchadviśiṣṭaṃ vā tulyaṃ vā śatrumātmana: | mitravānnatasāmanta: pratāpahatakaṇṭaka:  sa śaśāsa jagadrājā divaṃ devapatiryathā |
translation: मित्रवान् having many friends, नतसामन्त: humbled tributary kings, प्रतापहतकण्टक: slayed the  thorny enemies with might, आत्मन: for himself, विशिष्टं वा superior, तुल्यं वा or equal, शत्रुम् foe, नाध्यगच्छत् did not meet, स: राजा that king, देवपति: Indra, यथा like, जगत् world, शशास ruled.
explanation: The king (Dasaratha) had many friends. All the tributary kings were obedient to him. He killed his enemies with his might. There was no foe who was either superior to or equal to him. He ruled the world as Indra ruled the heaven.

shloka_text: तैर्मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रहिते नियुक्तै र्वृतोऽनुरक्तै: कुशलैस्समर्थै: । स पार्थिवो दीप्तिमवाप युक्त स्तेजोमयैर्गोभिरिवोदितोऽर्क: ।।1.7.22।।
transliteration: tairmantribhirmantrahite niyuktai rvṛto'nuraktai: kuśalaissamarthai: | sa pārthivo dīptimavāpa yukta stejomayairgobhirivodito'rka:
translation: मन्त्रहिते in counselling for  his welfare, नियुक्तै: appointed, अनुरक्तै: by the affectionate ones, कुशलै: skilful ones, समर्थै: by the capable, तै: मन्त्रिभि: with those ministers, वृत:  surrounded by, स: पार्थिव: the king, तेजोमयै: luminous, गोभि: by rays, युक्त: filled with, उदित: rising, अर्क: इव like the Sun, दीप्तिम् brightness, अवाप obtained.
explanation: Accompanied by the ministers who were devoted to his welfare, adept in counselling, skilful, capable and loyal towards him, the king acquired glory like the rising Sun with luminous rays. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे सप्तमस्सर्ग: ।। Thus ends the seventh sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तस्य त्वेवं प्रभावस्य धर्मज्ञस्य महात्मन:। सुतार्थं तप्यमानस्य नासीद्वंशकरस्सुत:।।1.8.1।।
transliteration: tasya tvevaṃ prabhāvasya dharmajñasya mahātmana:| sutārthaṃ tapyamānasya nāsīdvaṃśakarassuta:
translation: एवंप्रभावस्य of such majestic one,  धर्मज्ञस्य of the knower of righteousness, महात्मन: of the greatful soul,  सुतार्थम् for begetting sons, तप्यमानस्य performing rigourous austerities, तस्य for king Dasaratha, वंशकर: perpetuating the race,  सुत: son, नासीत् did not beget.
explanation: Such a majestic, righteous, and magnaninous king had no son to perpetuate the race even though he performed austerities for one.
comments: Dasaratha had no sons to continue the Ikshvaku race --sorrow grew  with advancing age-- intends to perform aswamedha for a successor-- summons all ministers and counsellors--sages and family priests to approve his proposal.

shloka_text: चिन्तयानस्य तस्यैवं बुद्धिरासीन्महात्मन: । सुतार्थं हयमेधेन किमर्थं न यजाम्यहम्।।1.8.2।।
transliteration: cintayānasya tasyaivaṃ buddhirāsīnmahātmana: | sutārthaṃ hayamedhena kimarthaṃ na yajāmyaham
translation: चिन्तयानस्य for him while reflectig over the matter, तस्य for him, महात्मन: of that  magnanimous king, एवम् in this way, बुद्धि:आसीत् had a thought, सुतार्थम् to obtain sons, हयमेधेन with Horsesacrifice, न किमर्थम् why not, यजामि(अहम्) I shall perform sacrifice.
explanation: While reflecting over the matter, a thought struck the magnanimous king: 'Why not invoke gods by performing a horsesacrifice for a son'.

shloka_text: स निश्चितां मतिं कृत्वा यष्टव्यमिति बुद्धिमान्। मन्त्रिभिस्सह धर्मात्मा सर्वैरेव कृतात्मभि:।।1.8.3।। ततोऽब्रवीदिदं राजा सुमन्त्रं मन्त्रिसत्तमम्। शीघ्रमानय मे सर्वान्गुरूंस्तान् सपुरोहितान्।।1.8.4।।
transliteration: sa niścitāṃ matiṃ kṛtvā yaṣṭavyamiti buddhimān| mantribhissaha dharmātmā sarvaireva kṛtātmabhi: tato'bravīdidaṃ rājā sumantraṃ mantrisattamam| śīghramānaya me sarvāngurūṃstān sapurohitān
translation: बुद्धिमान् sagacious, धर्मात्मा pious, स: राजा that king, कृतात्मभि: having control over themselves, सर्वैरेव all, मन्त्रिभि: by ministers, यष्टव्यमिति sacrifice should be performed, निश्चिताम् firmly, मतिं कृत्वा after making up his mind, तत: thereafter, मन्त्रिसत्तमम् best of ministers, सुमन्त्रम् Sumantra, इदम् following command, अब्रवीत् spoke, सपुरोहितान् along with family priests, तान् सर्वान् all those, मे गुरून् my spiritual preceptors, आनय bring.
explanation: Having made up his mind to perform the sacrifice, that sagacious and pious king, in consultation with his wise ministers, issued the following command to Sumantra, the best of ministers "Bring all my spritual preceptors along with family priests."

shloka_text: स निश्चितां मतिं कृत्वा यष्टव्यमिति बुद्धिमान्। मन्त्रिभिस्सह धर्मात्मा सर्वैरेव कृतात्मभि:।।1.8.3।। ततोऽब्रवीदिदं राजा सुमन्त्रं मन्त्रिसत्तमम्। शीघ्रमानय मे सर्वान्गुरूंस्तान् सपुरोहितान्।।1.8.4।।

explanation: Having made up his mind to perform the sacrifice, that sagacious and pious king, in consultation with his wise ministers, issued the following command to Sumantra, the best of ministers "Bring all my spritual preceptors along with family priests."

shloka_text: ततस्सुमन्त्रस्त्वरितं गत्वा त्वरितविक्रम:। समानयत्स तान् सर्वान् समस्तान्वेदपारगान् ।।1.8.5।। सुयज्ञं वामदेवं च जाबालिमथ काश्यपम् । परोहितं वसिष्ठं च ये चान्ये व्दिजसत्तमा: ।। 1.8.6 ।।
transliteration: tatassumantrastvaritaṃ gatvā tvaritavikrama:| samānayatsa tān sarvān samastānvedapāragān  suyajñaṃ vāmadevaṃ ca jābālimatha kāśyapam | parohitaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca ye cānye vdijasattamā:
translation: तत: thereupon, त्वरितविक्रम: a man with swift movements, स: सुमन्त्र: that Sumantra, त्वरितम् immediately,गत्वा having gone, सुयज्ञम् Suyajna, वामदेवं च Vamadeva, अथ and जाबालिम् Jabali, काश्यपम् Kasyapa, पुरोहितम् priest, वसिष्ठं च Vasistha, अन्ये other, ये व्दिजसत्तमा: excellent brahmins, वेदपारगान् who had command of trhe Vedas, समस्तान् gathering together, तान् सर्वान् all of them, समानयत् brought.
explanation: Thereupon Sumantra of swift movement immediateiy brought together Suyajna, Vamadeva,Jabali, Kasyapa and priest Vasistha along with other brahmins who had mastery over the Vedas.

shloka_text: ततस्सुमन्त्रस्त्वरितं गत्वा त्वरितविक्रम:। समानयत्स तान् सर्वान् समस्तान्वेदपारगान् ।।1.8.5।। सुयज्ञं वामदेवं च जाबालिमथ काश्यपम् । परोहितं वसिष्ठं च ये चान्ये व्दिजसत्तमा: ।। 1.8.6 ।।
transliteration: tatassumantrastvaritaṃ gatvā tvaritavikrama:| samānayatsa tān sarvān samastānvedapāragān  suyajñaṃ vāmadevaṃ ca jābālimatha kāśyapam | parohitaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca ye cānye vdijasattamā:
translation: तत: thereupon, त्वरितविक्रम: a man with swift movements, स: सुमन्त्र: that Sumantra, त्वरितम् immediately,गत्वा having gone, सुयज्ञम् Suyajna, वामदेवं च Vamadeva, अथ and जाबालिम् Jabali, काश्यपम् Kasyapa, पुरोहितम् priest, वसिष्ठं च Vasistha, अन्ये other, ये व्दिजसत्तमा: excellent brahmins, वेदपारगान् who had command of trhe Vedas, समस्तान् gathering together, तान् सर्वान् all of them, समानयत् brought.
explanation: Thereupon Sumantra of swift movement immediateiy brought together Suyajna, Vamadeva,Jabali, Kasyapa and priest Vasistha along with other brahmins who had mastery over the Vedas.

shloka_text: तान्पूजयित्वा धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथस्तदा। इदं धर्मार्थसहितं श्लक्ष्णंवचनमब्रवीत्।।1.8.7।।
transliteration: tānpūjayitvā dharmātmā rājā daśarathastadā| idaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ ślakṣṇaṃvacanamabravīt
translation: धर्मात्मा virtuous, दशरथ: राजा king Dasaratha, तदा then, तान् them, पूजयित्वा after paying homage, धर्मार्थसहितम् righteous and meaningful, श्लक्ष्णम् gracious, इदं वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् uttered.
explanation: Virtuous king Dasaratha paid homage to them (the ministers) and uttered these gracious, righteous and meaningful words.

shloka_text: मम लालप्यमानस्य पुत्रार्थन्नास्ति वै सुखम्। तदर्थं हयमेधेन यक्ष्यामीति मतिर्मम।।1.8.8।।
transliteration: mama lālapyamānasya putrārthannāsti vai sukham| tadarthaṃ hayamedhena yakṣyāmīti matirmama
translation: पुत्रार्थम् to have sons, लालप्यमानस्य suffering from intense sorrow, मम for me, सुखम्  happiness, नास्ति वै not there, तदर्थं for that reason, (अहम् I), हयमेधेन यक्ष्यामि I shall perform Horsesacrifice, इति thus, मम my, मति: intention.
explanation: There is no happiness for one who has no son. This is the cause of my intense suffering. Therefore, I have made up my mind to perform a horsesacrifice.

shloka_text: तदहं यष्टुमिच्छामि शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा। कथं प्राप्स्याम्यहं कामं बुद्धिरत्रविचार्यताम्।।1.8.9।।
transliteration: tadahaṃ yaṣṭumicchāmi śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā| kathaṃ prāpsyāmyahaṃ kāmaṃ buddhiratravicāryatām
translation: तत् therefore, अहम् I, शास्त्रदृष्टेन according to Scriptures, कर्मणा by spiritual act, यष्टुम् to perform sacrifice, इच्छामि I am desirous, कामम् my desire, कथम् how, अहम् I, प्रप्स्यामि can fulfill, अत्र in this matter,  बुद्धि: solution, विचार्यताम् may be deliberated.
explanation: Therefore, I intend to perform a horsesacrifice in accordance with the scriptures. How  can I fulfil my desire in this regard? You may deliberate and find a solution".

shloka_text: ततस्साध्विति तद्वाक्यं ब्राह्मणा: प्रत्यपूजयन्। वसिष्ठप्रमुखास्सर्वे पार्थिवस्य मुखाच्च्युतम्।।1.8.10।।
transliteration: tatassādhviti tadvākyaṃ brāhmaṇā: pratyapūjayan| vasiṣṭhapramukhāssarve pārthivasya mukhāccyutam
translation: तत: then, वसिष्ठप्रमुखा: vasishta etc, ब्राह्मणा: brahmins, सर्वे all, पार्थिवस्य king's, मुखात् from the mouth, च्युतम् delivered, तत् वाक्यम् those words, साधु इति well said, प्रत्यपूजयन् extolled.
explanation: The brahmins along with Vasishta in the forefront extolled the king's decision, exclaiming, 'Well, Well'.

shloka_text: ऊचुश्च परमप्रीतास्सर्वे दशरथं वच:। सम्भारास्सम्भ्रियन्तां ते तुरगश्च विमुच्यताम्।।1.8.11।।
