translation: त्रिदशपुङ्गव: foremost of gods, सर्वलोकनमस्कृत: bowed by all in the worlds, देवेश: lord of devatas, celestial beings, विष्णु: Visnu, एवम् in this manner, उक्त: addressed, समेतान् assembled, धर्मसंहितान् guided by law of righteousness, पितामहपुरोगान् led by the grand  sire, तान् those, सर्वान् all, त्रिदशान् gods, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Visnu, the lord of the celestials, foremost among the gods and bowed by all in the worlds addressed the assembled devatas who were guided by the law of righteousness and were led by the grand sire, Brahma.

shloka_text: भयं त्यजत भद्रं वो हितार्थं युधि रावणम्। सपुत्रपौत्रं सामात्यं समित्रज्ञातिबान्धवम्।।1.15.27।। हत्वा क्रूरं दुरात्मानं देवर्षीणां भयावहम्। दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च। वत्स्यामि मानुषे लोके पालयन्पृथिवीमिमाम्।।1.15.28।।
transliteration: bhayaṃ tyajata bhadraṃ vo hitārthaṃ yudhi rāvaṇam| saputrapautraṃ sāmātyaṃ samitrajñātibāndhavam hatvā krūraṃ durātmānaṃ devarṣīṇāṃ bhayāvaham| daśavarṣasahasrāṇi daśavarṣaśatāni ca| vatsyāmi mānuṣe loke pālayanpṛthivīmimām
translation: भयम् fear, त्यजत abandon, भद्रम् blessings (to you), व: for your, हितार्थम् welfare, सपुत्रपौत्रम् along with his sons and grandsons, सामात्यम् along with his ministesrs, समित्रज्ञाति बान्धवम् along with friends, relations and allies, क्रूरम् cruel, दुरात्मानम् wicked minded, देवर्षीणाम् for gods and rishis, भयावहम् dreadful, रावणम् Ravana, युधि in the battle, हत्वा after killing, इमाम् पृथिवीम् this earth, पालयन् while ruling, दशवर्षसहस्राणि ten thousand years, दशवर्षशतानि ten hundred years, मानुषे लोके in the world of men, वत्स्यामि I will dwell.
explanation: Abandon your fear and may you be blessed; for your welfare I shall slay in battle the cruel, wicked Ravana, dreadful to gods and sages, together with his sons, grandsons, ministers, friends, kinsmen and allies, and then dwell in the world of men, ruling this earth for eleven thousand years.

shloka_text: भयं त्यजत भद्रं वो हितार्थं युधि रावणम्। सपुत्रपौत्रं सामात्यं समित्रज्ञातिबान्धवम्।।1.15.27।। हत्वा क्रूरं दुरात्मानं देवर्षीणां भयावहम्। दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च। वत्स्यामि मानुषे लोके पालयन्पृथिवीमिमाम्।।1.15.28।।
transliteration: bhayaṃ tyajata bhadraṃ vo hitārthaṃ yudhi rāvaṇam| saputrapautraṃ sāmātyaṃ samitrajñātibāndhavam hatvā krūraṃ durātmānaṃ devarṣīṇāṃ bhayāvaham| daśavarṣasahasrāṇi daśavarṣaśatāni ca| vatsyāmi mānuṣe loke pālayanpṛthivīmimām
translation: भयम् fear, त्यजत abandon, भद्रम् blessings (to you), व: for your, हितार्थम् welfare, सपुत्रपौत्रम् along with his sons and grandsons, सामात्यम् along with his ministesrs, समित्रज्ञाति बान्धवम् along with friends, relations and allies, क्रूरम् cruel, दुरात्मानम् wicked minded, देवर्षीणाम् for gods and rishis, भयावहम् dreadful, रावणम् Ravana, युधि in the battle, हत्वा after killing, इमाम् पृथिवीम् this earth, पालयन् while ruling, दशवर्षसहस्राणि ten thousand years, दशवर्षशतानि ten hundred years, मानुषे लोके in the world of men, वत्स्यामि I will dwell.
explanation: Abandon your fear and may you be blessed; for your welfare I shall slay in battle the cruel, wicked Ravana, dreadful to gods and sages, together with his sons, grandsons, ministers, friends, kinsmen and allies, and then dwell in the world of men, ruling this earth for eleven thousand years.

shloka_text: एवं दत्वा वरं देवो देवानां विष्णुरात्मवान्। मानुषे चिन्तयामास जन्मभूमिमथात्मन:।।1.15.29।।
transliteration: evaṃ datvā varaṃ devo devānāṃ viṣṇurātmavān| mānuṣe cintayāmāsa janmabhūmimathātmana:
translation: आत्मवान् the highest soul, विष्णु: देव: lord Visnu, देवानाम् for devatas, एवम् in this manner, वरम् boon, दत्वा having given, अथ there after, आत्मन: for himself, मानुषे in the world of men, जन्मभूमिम् place of birth, चिन्तयामास reflected.
explanation: Lord Visnu, supreme soul having given boon to devatas in this manner, reflected as to the place where he should take birth as a man in this world of men.

shloka_text: तत: पद्मपलाशाक्ष: कृत्वाऽऽत्मानं चतुर्विधम्। पितरं रोचयामास तथा दशरथन्नृपम्।।1.15.30।।
transliteration: tata: padmapalāśākṣa: kṛtvā''tmānaṃ caturvidham| pitaraṃ rocayāmāsa tathā daśarathannṛpam
translation: तत: thereafter, पद्मपलाशाक्ष: lord having eyes resembling lotus petals, तदा then, आत्मानम् himself, चतुर्विधम् in four ways, कृत्वा having made, दशरथम् नृपम् king Dasaratha, तथा पितरम् as father, रोचयामास liked.
explanation: Thereafter, the Lord with eyes like the lotus petal was pleased to transform himself into four forms and to choose king Dasaratha as his father.

shloka_text: तदा देवर्षि गन्धर्वास्सरुद्रास्साप्सरोगणा:। स्तुतिभिर्दिव्यरूपाभिस्तुष्टुवुर्मधुसूदनम्।।1.15.31।।
transliteration: tadā devarṣi gandharvāssarudrāssāpsarogaṇā:| stutibhirdivyarūpābhistuṣṭuvurmadhusūdanam
translation: तदा then, सरुद्रा: along with rudras, साप्सरोगणा: along with groups of apsaras, देवर्षिगन्धर्वा: devatas, rishis and gandharvas, दिव्यरूपाभि: celestial beauty, स्तुतिभि: hymns, मधुसूदनम् slayer of Madhu, तुष्टुवु: praised.
explanation: Then along with gandharvas, groups of apsaras, rishis, rudras and devatas sang in praise of the 'Lord Slayer of Madhu', with hymns of celestial beauty.

shloka_text: तमुद्धतं रावणमुग्रतेजसं प्रवृद्धदर्पं त्रिदशेश्वरद्विषम्। विरावणं साधुतपस्विकण्टकं तपस्विनामुद्धर तं भयावहम्।।1.15.32।।
transliteration: tamuddhataṃ rāvaṇamugratejasaṃ pravṛddhadarpaṃ tridaśeśvaradviṣam| virāvaṇaṃ sādhutapasvikaṇṭakaṃ tapasvināmuddhara taṃ bhayāvaham
translation: उद्धतम् inflamed, उग्रतेजसम् one with frightful prowess, प्रवृद्धदर्पम् having fully grown insolence, त्रिदशेश्वरद्विषम् the enemy of the lord of gods (Indra ), तपस्विकण्टकम् source of vexation to ascetics, तपस्विनाम् for maharshis, भयावहम् dreadful, तम् him, तम् रावणम् that Ravana, विरावणम् he who causes grerat agony in the three worlds making people cry loudly, साधु rightly, उद्धर uproot him.
explanation: "Therefore, uproot that mighty Ravana possessing frightful prowess, inflamed pride, limitless insolence causing agony to the three worlds, a source of vexation to ascetics and  a dreadful enemy of Indra.

shloka_text: तमेव हत्वा सबलं सबान्धवं विरावणं रावणमग्य्रपौरुषम्। स्वर्लोकमागच्छ गतज्वरश्चिरं सुरेन्द्रगुप्तं गतदोषकल्मषम्।।1.15.33।।
transliteration: tameva hatvā sabalaṃ sabāndhavaṃ virāvaṇaṃ rāvaṇamagyrapauruṣam| svarlokamāgaccha gatajvaraściraṃ surendraguptaṃ gatadoṣakalmaṣam
translation: सबलम् along with his forces, सबान्धवम् with his relations, विरावणम् causing distress in  the worlds, अग्य्रपौरुषम् having foremost manliness, तम् एव him only, रावणम् Ravana, हत्वा having slain, चिरम् in long time, गतज्वर: purged of distress, सुरेन्द्रगुप्तम् protected by Indra, गतदोषकल्मषम् freed from faults and sins, स्वर्लोकम् celestial region, आगच्छ return.
explanation: Kill Ravana, the cause of distress in the worlds, kill his forces and relatives. Them return to heaven  protected by Indra after freeing from distress, faults and sins". इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे पञ्चदशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the fifteenth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततो नारायणो देवो नियुक्तस्सुरसत्तमै:। जानन्नपि सुरानेवं श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रवीत्।।1.16.1।।
transliteration: tato nārāyaṇo devo niyuktassurasattamai:| jānannapi surānevaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: तत: then, सुरसत्तमै: by best of devatas, नियुक्त: having been employed, नारायण:देव: lord Narayana, जानन्नपि although cognizant of, सुरान् addressing devatas, एवम् in this manner, श्लक्ष्णम् softly, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Although Omniscient lord Narayana knew the means to be employed, when he was requested by the best of devatas he spoke to them softly:
comments: Devatas urge Visnu to incarnate in human form to destroy Ravana--A celestial being from Prajapatya emerges from the sacrificial fire--gives a vessel containing payasam--his wives partake the payasam and become pregnant.

shloka_text: उपाय: को वधे तस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मन:। यमहं तं समास्थाय निहन्यामृषिकण्टकम्।।1.16.2।।
transliteration: upāya: ko vadhe tasya rāvaṇasya durātmana:| yamahaṃ taṃ samāsthāya nihanyāmṛṣikaṇṭakam
translation: दुरात्मन: of the evil minded, तस्य रावणस्य that Ravana's, वधे in the matter of destruction, उपाय: strategies, क: what?, यम् by which ever strategies, आस्थाय after adopting, ऋषिकण्टकम् thorn by the side of sages(causing sufferings to sages), तम् him, अहम् I, निहन्याम् I shall kill.
explanation: "What strategies should be adopted in the matter of destruction of that evilminded Ravana who is a thorn to the sages?".

shloka_text: एवमुक्तास्सुरास्सर्वे प्रत्यूचुर्विष्णुमव्ययम्। मानुषीं तनुमास्थाय रावणं जहि संयुगे।।1.16.3।।
transliteration: evamuktāssurāssarve pratyūcurviṣṇumavyayam| mānuṣīṃ tanumāsthāya rāvaṇaṃ jahi saṃyuge
translation: एवम् उक्ता: in this manner addressed, सुरा: the devatas, सर्वे all, अव्ययम् Imperishable, विष्णुम् Vishnu, प्रत्यूचु: replied back, मानुषीम् relaing to human being, तनुम् body, आस्थाय assuming, संयुगे in the battle, रावणम् जहि kill Ravana.
explanation: When the devatas were thus addressed by the imperishable Visnu, they replied him saying, "You may assume the form of a human being and slay Ravana in the battle".

shloka_text: स हि तेपे तपस्तीव्रं दीर्घकालमरिन्दम  । येन तुष्टोऽभवद्ब्रह्मा लोककृल्लोकपूर्वज:।।1.16.4।।
transliteration: sa hi tepe tapastīvraṃ dīrghakālamarindama  | yena tuṣṭo'bhavadbrahmā lokakṛllokapūrvaja:
translation: अरिन्दम ODestroyer of foes, स: Ravana, दीर्घकालम् for long time, तीव्रम् severe, तप: penance, तेपे performed, येन by which, लोककृत् creator of the world, लोकपूर्वज: born prior to the creation of the worlds, ब्रह्मा Brahma, तुष्ट:अभवत् was very pleased.
explanation: "O destroyer of foes Lord Brahma was very pleased with Ravana's intense penance over a long time৷৷

shloka_text: सन्तुष्ट: प्रददौ तस्मै राक्षसाय वरं प्रभु:। 04 नानाविधेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो भयं नान्यत्र मानुषात्।।1.16.5।। अवज्ञाता: पुरा तेन वरदाने हि मानवा:। 105
transliteration: santuṣṭa: pradadau tasmai rākṣasāya varaṃ prabhu:| 04 nānāvidhebhyo bhūtebhyo bhayaṃ nānyatra mānuṣāt avajñātā: purā tena varadāne hi mānavā:| 105
translation: सन्तुष्ट: very pleased, प्रभु: all powerful Brahma, तस्मै राक्षसाय for that rakshasa, मानुषात् अन्यत्र except from men, नानाविधेभ्य: from several others, भूतेभ्य: from living beings, भयम्  fear, न none, वरम् boon, प्रददौ granted, पुरा earlier, वरदाने at the time of granting boon, तेन by him, मानवा: men, अवज्ञाता: were disregarded.
explanation: Pleased, with the rakshasa Brahma granted a boon to the effect that except from men, there was, for him, no fear of death from any other living beings. Ravana ignored men while seeking the boon.

shloka_text: एवं पितामहात्तस्माद्वरं प्राप्य स दर्पित:।।1.16.6।। उत्सादयति लोकान्त्रीन् स्त्रियश्चाप्यपकर्षति । तस्मात्तस्य वधो दृष्टो मानुषेभ्य: परन्तप।।1.16.7।।
transliteration: evaṃ pitāmahāttasmādvaraṃ prāpya sa darpita: utsādayati lokāntrīn striyaścāpyapakarṣati | tasmāttasya vadho dṛṣṭo mānuṣebhya: parantapa
translation: एवम् in this manner, तस्मात् पितामहात् from that Brahma, वरम् boon, प्राप्य having obtained,  स: Ravana, दर्पित: became arrogant, त्रीन् three, लोकान् worlds, उत्सादयति destroyed,  स्त्रिय: women, अपकर्षति च carries away by violence, तस्मात् for that reason, परन्तप O Destroyer of foes, तस्य वध: killing him, मानुषेभ्य: from(by) men, दृष्ट: has been seen.
explanation: Having obtained the boon from Brahma, Ravana, greed and arrogant went on bringing  destruction to the three worlds. He carried away women by violence. O destroyer of foes his death is possible by men only."

shloka_text: एवं पितामहात्तस्माद्वरं प्राप्य स दर्पित:।।1.16.6।। उत्सादयति लोकान्त्रीन् स्त्रियश्चाप्यपकर्षति । तस्मात्तस्य वधो दृष्टो मानुषेभ्य: परन्तप।।1.16.7।।
transliteration: evaṃ pitāmahāttasmādvaraṃ prāpya sa darpita: utsādayati lokāntrīn striyaścāpyapakarṣati | tasmāttasya vadho dṛṣṭo mānuṣebhya: parantapa
translation: एवम् in this manner, तस्मात् पितामहात् from that Brahma, वरम् boon, प्राप्य having obtained,  स: Ravana, दर्पित: became arrogant, त्रीन् three, लोकान् worlds, उत्सादयति destroyed,  स्त्रिय: women, अपकर्षति च carries away by violence, तस्मात् for that reason, परन्तप O Destroyer of foes, तस्य वध: killing him, मानुषेभ्य: from(by) men, दृष्ट: has been seen.
explanation: Having obtained the boon from Brahma, Ravana, greed and arrogant went on bringing  destruction to the three worlds. He carried away women by violence. O destroyer of foes his death is possible by men only."

shloka_text: इत्येतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सुराणां विष्णुरात्मवान्। पितरं रोचयामास तदा दशरथं नृपम्।।1.16.8।।
transliteration: ityetadvacanaṃ śrutvā surāṇāṃ viṣṇurātmavān| pitaraṃ rocayāmāsa tadā daśarathaṃ nṛpam
translation: इति in this manner, सुराणाम् devatas, एतत् वचनम् these words, श्रुत्वा having heard, आत्मवान् intellectual, विष्णु: Visnu, तदा then, दशरथं नृपम्  king Dasaratha, पितरम् as father, रोचयामास liked (chosen).
explanation: Having heard the words of devatas, selfpossessed Visnu chose king Dasaratha as his father.

shloka_text: स चाप्यपुत्रो नृपतिस्तस्मिन्काले महाद्युति:। अयजत्पुत्रियामिष्टिं पुत्रेप्सुररिसूदन:।।1.16.9।।
transliteration: sa cāpyaputro nṛpatistasminkāle mahādyuti:| ayajatputriyāmiṣṭiṃ putrepsurarisūdana:
translation: तस्मिन् काले at that time, महाद्युति: effulgent, अरिसूदन: destroyer of enemies, स:नृपति: that king, अपुत्र: without sons, पुत्रेप्सु: wishing to beget sons, पुत्रियाम् इष्टिम् a sacrifice to obtain sons, अयजत् performed.
explanation: At that time, the brilliant king (Dasaratha), destroyer of enemies, who had no sons was performing a sacrifice for sons.

shloka_text: स कृत्वा निश्चयं विष्णुरामन्त्र्य च पितामहम्। अन्तर्धानं गतो देवै: पूज्यमानो महर्षिभि:।।1.16.10।।
transliteration: sa kṛtvā niścayaṃ viṣṇurāmantrya ca pitāmaham| antardhānaṃ gato devai: pūjyamāno maharṣibhi:
translation: स: विष्णु: Vishnu, निश्चयं कृत्वा having decided, पितामहम् Grandsire, Brahma, आमन्त्र्य bidding farewell, देवै: by devatas, महर्षिभि: by maharshis, पूज्यमान: worshipped by, अन्तर्धानं गत: disappeared.
explanation: After Visnu had decided (to incarnate) and he was worshipped by devatas and maharshis he disappeared bidding farewell to Brahma.

shloka_text: तो वै यजमानस्य पावकादतुलप्रभम्। प्रादुर्भूतं महद्भूतं महावीर्यं महाबलम्।।1.16.11।। कृष्णं रक्ताम्बरधरं रक्तास्यं दुन्दुभिस्वनम्। स्निग्धहर्यक्षतनुजश्मश्रुप्रवरमूर्धजम्।।1.16.12।। शुभलक्षणसम्पन्नं दिव्याभरणभूषितम्। शैलशृङ्गसमुत्सेथं दृप्तशार्दूलविक्रमम्।।1.16.13।। दिवाकरसमाकारं दीप्तानलशिखोपमम्। तप्तजाम्बूनदमयीं राजतान्तपरिच्छदाम्।।1.16.14।। दिव्यपायससम्पूर्णां पात्रीं पत्नीमिव प्रियाम्। प्रगृह्य विपुलां दोर्भ्यां स्वयं मायामयीमिव।।1.16.15।।
transliteration: to vai yajamānasya pāvakādatulaprabham| prādurbhūtaṃ mahadbhūtaṃ mahāvīryaṃ mahābalam kṛṣṇaṃ raktāmbaradharaṃ raktāsyaṃ dundubhisvanam| snigdhaharyakṣatanujaśmaśrupravaramūrdhajam śubhalakṣaṇasampannaṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitam| śailaśṛṅgasamutsethaṃ dṛptaśārdūlavikramam divākarasamākāraṃ dīptānalaśikhopamam| taptajāmbūnadamayīṃ rājatāntaparicchadām divyapāyasasampūrṇāṃ pātrīṃ patnīmiva priyām| pragṛhya vipulāṃ dorbhyāṃ svayaṃ māyāmayīmiva
translation: तत: then, यजमानस्य  while Dasaratha was performing the sacrifice, पावकात् from the sacrificial fire, अतुलप्रभम् of unmatched splendour, महावीर्यम् of great prowess, महाबलम् great strength, कृष्णं रक्ताम्बरधरम् clad in black and crimpson garment, रक्तास्यम् redfaced, दुन्दुभिस्वनम् having a voice similar to the sounds of drum, स्निग्धहर्यक्षतनुजश्मश्रुप्रवरमूर्धजम्  with whiskers of soft and shining  tawny hair resembling mane of lion and excellent hair, शुभलक्षणसम्पन्नम् endowed with auspicious signs, दिव्याभरणभूषितम् adorned with splendid divine ornaments, शैलश्रुङ्गसमुत्सेथम् resembling the height of a peak of a mountain, दृप्तशार्दूलविक्रमम् having the strides of an arrogant tiger, दिवाकरसमाकारम्  similar to the Sun in radiance, दीप्तानलशिखोपमम् looking like the crest of blazing fire, महत् great, भूतम् being, तप्तजाम्बूनदमयीम् made of gold purified in fire, राजतान्तपरिच्छदाम् made of silver, दिव्यपायससम्पूर्णाम् filled with divine (excellent) Payasam(a preparation of rice in milk and sugar), मायामयीमिव as if made out of illusion, विपुलाम् large, पात्रीम् vessel, प्रियां पत्नीमिव like a beloved wife, स्वयम् on his own, दोर्भ्याम् with both the hands, प्रगृह्य holding, प्रादुर्भूतम् emerged.
explanation: During the sacrifice, there emerged from the sacrificial fire a mighty being with unmatched splendour, his prowess and strength. He wore a black and crimson garment. He had a red face. His voice was similar to the sounds of a drum. He had whiskers of soft and shining tawny hair resembling the mane of a lion He had fine hair on his head. He was endowed with auspicious signs and adorned with splendid divine ornaments. His height resembled a mountain peak. He walked with the strides of a ferocious tiger. Similar to the Sun in radiance, he looked like the crest of a blazing fire. This divine being held like his beloved wife both hands, a large vessel made of gold purified, in fire, covered with a silver lid and filled with payasam (a preparation of rice in milk and sugar). It looked as though it was created  by magic.

shloka_text: तो वै यजमानस्य पावकादतुलप्रभम्। प्रादुर्भूतं महद्भूतं महावीर्यं महाबलम्।।1.16.11।। कृष्णं रक्ताम्बरधरं रक्तास्यं दुन्दुभिस्वनम्। स्निग्धहर्यक्षतनुजश्मश्रुप्रवरमूर्धजम्।।1.16.12।। शुभलक्षणसम्पन्नं दिव्याभरणभूषितम्। शैलशृङ्गसमुत्सेथं दृप्तशार्दूलविक्रमम्।।1.16.13।। दिवाकरसमाकारं दीप्तानलशिखोपमम्। तप्तजाम्बूनदमयीं राजतान्तपरिच्छदाम्।।1.16.14।। दिव्यपायससम्पूर्णां पात्रीं पत्नीमिव प्रियाम्। प्रगृह्य विपुलां दोर्भ्यां स्वयं मायामयीमिव।।1.16.15।।
transliteration: to vai yajamānasya pāvakādatulaprabham| prādurbhūtaṃ mahadbhūtaṃ mahāvīryaṃ mahābalam kṛṣṇaṃ raktāmbaradharaṃ raktāsyaṃ dundubhisvanam| snigdhaharyakṣatanujaśmaśrupravaramūrdhajam śubhalakṣaṇasampannaṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitam| śailaśṛṅgasamutsethaṃ dṛptaśārdūlavikramam divākarasamākāraṃ dīptānalaśikhopamam| taptajāmbūnadamayīṃ rājatāntaparicchadām divyapāyasasampūrṇāṃ pātrīṃ patnīmiva priyām| pragṛhya vipulāṃ dorbhyāṃ svayaṃ māyāmayīmiva
translation: तत: then, यजमानस्य  while Dasaratha was performing the sacrifice, पावकात् from the sacrificial fire, अतुलप्रभम् of unmatched splendour, महावीर्यम् of great prowess, महाबलम् great strength, कृष्णं रक्ताम्बरधरम् clad in black and crimpson garment, रक्तास्यम् redfaced, दुन्दुभिस्वनम् having a voice similar to the sounds of drum, स्निग्धहर्यक्षतनुजश्मश्रुप्रवरमूर्धजम्  with whiskers of soft and shining  tawny hair resembling mane of lion and excellent hair, शुभलक्षणसम्पन्नम् endowed with auspicious signs, दिव्याभरणभूषितम् adorned with splendid divine ornaments, शैलश्रुङ्गसमुत्सेथम् resembling the height of a peak of a mountain, दृप्तशार्दूलविक्रमम् having the strides of an arrogant tiger, दिवाकरसमाकारम्  similar to the Sun in radiance, दीप्तानलशिखोपमम् looking like the crest of blazing fire, महत् great, भूतम् being, तप्तजाम्बूनदमयीम् made of gold purified in fire, राजतान्तपरिच्छदाम् made of silver, दिव्यपायससम्पूर्णाम् filled with divine (excellent) Payasam(a preparation of rice in milk and sugar), मायामयीमिव as if made out of illusion, विपुलाम् large, पात्रीम् vessel, प्रियां पत्नीमिव like a beloved wife, स्वयम् on his own, दोर्भ्याम् with both the hands, प्रगृह्य holding, प्रादुर्भूतम् emerged.
explanation: During the sacrifice, there emerged from the sacrificial fire a mighty being with unmatched splendour, his prowess and strength. He wore a black and crimson garment. He had a red face. His voice was similar to the sounds of a drum. He had whiskers of soft and shining tawny hair resembling the mane of a lion He had fine hair on his head. He was endowed with auspicious signs and adorned with splendid divine ornaments. His height resembled a mountain peak. He walked with the strides of a ferocious tiger. Similar to the Sun in radiance, he looked like the crest of a blazing fire. This divine being held like his beloved wife both hands, a large vessel made of gold purified, in fire, covered with a silver lid and filled with payasam (a preparation of rice in milk and sugar). It looked as though it was created  by magic.

translation: तत: then, यजमानस्य  while Dasaratha was performing the sacrifice, पावकात् from the sacrificial fire, अतुलप्रभम् of unmatched splendour, महावीर्यम् of great prowess, महाबलम् great strength, कृष्णं रक्ताम्बरधरम् clad in black and crimpson garment, रक्तास्यम् redfaced, दुन्दुभिस्वनम् having a voice similar to the sounds of drum, स्निग्धहर्यक्षतनुजश्मश्रुप्रवरमूर्धजम्  with whiskers of soft and shining  tawny hair resembling mane of lion and excellent hair, शुभलक्षणसम्पन्नम् endowed with auspicious signs, दिव्याभरणभूषितम् adorned with splendid divine ornaments, शैलश्रुङ्गसमुत्सेथम् resembling the height of a peak of a mountain, दृप्तशार्दूलविक्रमम् having the strides of an arrogant tiger, दिवाकरसमाकारम्  similar to the Sun in radiance, दीप्तानलशिखोपमम् looking like the crest of blazing fire, महत् great, भूतम् being, तप्तजाम्बूनदमयीम् made of gold purified in fire, राजतान्तपरिच्छदाम् made of silver, दिव्यपायससम्पूर्णाम् filled with divine (excellent) Payasam(a preparation of rice in milk and sugar), मायामयीमिव as if made out of illusion, विपुलाम् large, पात्रीम् vessel, प्रियां पत्नीमिव like a beloved wife, स्वयम् on his own, दोर्भ्याम् with both the hands, प्रगृह्य holding, प्रादुर्भूतम् emerged.

His voice was similar to the sounds of a drum. He had whiskers of soft and shining tawny hair resembling the mane of a lion He had fine hair on his head. He was endowed with auspicious signs and adorned with splendid divine ornaments. His height resembled a mountain peak. He walked with the strides of a ferocious tiger. Similar to the Sun in radiance, he looked like the crest of a blazing fire. This divine being held like his beloved wife both hands, a large vessel made of gold purified, in fire, covered with a silver lid and filled with payasam (a preparation of rice in milk and sugar). It looked as though it was created  by magic.

shloka_text: समवेक्ष्याब्रवीद्वाक्यमिदं दशरथं नृपम्। प्राजापत्यं नरं विद्धि मामिहाभ्यागतं नृप।।1.16.16।।
transliteration: samavekṣyābravīdvākyamidaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam| prājāpatyaṃ naraṃ viddhi māmihābhyāgataṃ nṛpa
translation: दशरथं नृपम् king Dasaratha, समवेक्ष्य seeing him, इदम् वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् had spoken, नृप Oking, इह अभ्यागतम् have come here, प्राजापत्यम् from Prajapati (Brahma), नरम् person, विद्धि you know.
explanation: Having seen king Dasaratha, he said, "O King you know I have been sent by Prjapati (Brahma), and I am here".

shloka_text: तत: परं तदा राजा प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलि:। भगवन् स्वागतं तेऽस्तु किमहं करवाणि ते।।1.16.17।।
transliteration: tata: paraṃ tadā rājā pratyuvāca kṛtāñjali:| bhagavan svāgataṃ te'stu kimahaṃ karavāṇi te
translation: तत:परम् thereafter, तदा then, राजा king, कृताञ्जलि: with folded palms, प्रत्युवाच replied, भगवन् O Revered lord, ते स्वागतम् अस्तु welcome to you, अहम् I, ते to you, किम् what, करवाणि can do.
explanation: With folded palms the king replied, "O revered lord. Welcome to you. What can I do for you?".

shloka_text: अथो पुनरिदं वाक्यं प्राजापत्यो नरोऽब्रवीत्। राजन्नर्चयता देवानद्य प्राप्तमिदं त्वया।।1.16.18।।
transliteration: atho punaridaṃ vākyaṃ prājāpatyo naro'bravīt| rājannarcayatā devānadya prāptamidaṃ tvayā
translation: अथो thereafter, प्राजापत्य: the being sent by Prajapati, नर: that person, पुन: again, इदं वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke, राजन् O king, देवान्  devatas, अर्चयता while  worshipping, त्वया by you, अद्य today, इदं this, प्राप्तम् obtained.
explanation: Thereafter the one who came from Prajapati answered, "O King you have obtained this payasam today in return for the worship offered to the devatas".

shloka_text: इदं तु नृपशार्दूल पायसं देवनिर्मितम्। प्रजाकरं गृहाण त्वं धन्यमारोग्यवर्धनम्।।1.16.19।।
transliteration: idaṃ tu nṛpaśārdūla pāyasaṃ devanirmitam| prajākaraṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ dhanyamārogyavardhanam
translation: नृपशार्दूल O Best among kings, देवनिर्मितम् prepared by gods, प्रजाकरम् conferring progeny, धन्यम् bestowing affluence, आरोग्यवर्धनम् helps in improving health, इदम् पायसम् this Payasam, त्वम् you, गृहाण receive.
explanation: "O Lion among kings, receive this payasam prepared by gods, conferring progeny, bestowing affluence and improving health.

shloka_text: भार्याणामनुरूपाणामश्नीतेति प्रयच्छ वै। तासु त्वं प्राप्स्यसे पुत्रान्यदर्थं यजसे नृप।।1.16.20।।
transliteration: bhāryāṇāmanurūpāṇāmaśnīteti prayaccha vai| tāsu tvaṃ prāpsyase putrānyadarthaṃ yajase nṛpa
translation: नृप O King, अश्नीत इति "consume it", अनुरूपाणाम् worthy, भार्याणाम् consorts, प्रयच्छ वै give it to them, यदर्थम् for whose sake, यजसे  you are performing  this sacrifice, पुत्रान् such sons, तासु inthem, त्वम् you, प्राप्स्यसे will obtain.
explanation: O King you are performing this sacrifice for the sake of sons. Give this to your  worthy consorts to consume it. They will bear you sons".

shloka_text: तथेति नृपति: प्रीतश्शिरसा प्रतिगृह्यताम्। पात्रीं देवान्नसम्पूर्णां देवदत्तां हिरण्मयीम्।।1.16.21।।
transliteration: tatheti nṛpati: prītaśśirasā pratigṛhyatām| pātrīṃ devānnasampūrṇāṃ devadattāṃ hiraṇmayīm
translation: नृपति: king, तथेति so be it, तां देवान्नसम्पूर्णाम् all that food prepared by deities, देवदत्ताम् bestowed by devatas, हिरण्मयीम् golden, पात्रीम् vessel, शिरसा by lowering his head respectfully, प्रतिगृह्य having received, प्रीत: pleased.
explanation: Dasaratha was pleased to receive respectfully the golden vessel filled with the payasam  prepared and bestowed by devatas.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्य च तद्भूतमद्भुतं प्रियदर्शनम्। मुदा परमया युक्तश्चकाराभिप्रदक्षिणम्।।1.16.22।।
transliteration: abhivādya ca tadbhūtamadbhutaṃ priyadarśanam| mudā paramayā yuktaścakārābhipradakṣiṇam
translation: परमया by utmost, मुदा युक्त: endowed with joy, अद्भुतम् wonderful, प्रियदर्शनम् having pleasant countenance, तत् भूतम् that being, अभिवाद्य having saluated, प्रदक्षिणम् चकार  circumambulated.
explanation: Overwhelmed with great joy, he, walked around that wonderful being of pleasant  countenance again and again and saluated him respectfully.

shloka_text: ततो दशरथ: प्राप्य पायसं देवनिर्मितम्। बभूव परमप्रीत: प्राप्य वित्तमिवाधन:।।1.16.23।।
transliteration: tato daśaratha: prāpya pāyasaṃ devanirmitam| babhūva paramaprīta: prāpya vittamivādhana:
translation: तत: afterthat, दशरथ: Dasaratha, देवनिर्मितम् prepared by devatas, पायसम् Payasam, प्राप्य having obtained, वित्तम् wealth, प्राप्य having got, अधन:इव like a person having no wealth, परमप्रीत:बभूव was highly pleased.
explanation: Dasaratha who received the payasam prepared by devatas was highly pleased like a poor man who received wealth.

shloka_text: ततस्तदद्भुतप्रख्यं भूतं परमभास्वरम्। संवर्तयित्वा तत्कर्म तत्रैवान्तरधीयत।।1.16.24।।
transliteration: tatastadadbhutaprakhyaṃ bhūtaṃ paramabhāsvaram| saṃvartayitvā tatkarma tatraivāntaradhīyata
translation: तत: then, अद्भुतप्रख्यम् having a wonderful form, परमभास्वरम् highly effulgent, तद्भूतम् that being, तत्कर्म that task, संवर्तयित्वा having performed, तत्रैव from there, अन्तरधीयत disappeared.
explanation: Then that effulgent figure of wonderful form having given the bowl of payasam vanished from there.

shloka_text: हर्षरश्मिभिरुद्योतं तस्यान्त:पुरमाबभौ। शारदस्याभिरामस्य चन्द्रस्येव नभोंऽशुभि:।।1.16.25।।
transliteration: harṣaraśmibhirudyotaṃ tasyānta:puramābabhau| śāradasyābhirāmasya candrasyeva nabhoṃ'śubhi:
translation: हर्षरश्मिभि: with rays of happiness, उद्द्योतम् got brightened, तस्य his, अन्त:पुरम् inner apartment, अभिरामस्य delightful, शारदस्य autumnal, चन्द्रस्य moon's, अंशुभि: beams, नभ:इव like sky, आबभौ shone.
explanation: The inner apartment, brightened with rays of happiness, shone like the autumnal sky in the glow of the moon.

shloka_text: सोऽन्त:पुरं प्रविश्यैव कौसल्यामिदमब्रवीत्। पायसं प्रतिगृह्णीष्व पुत्रीयं त्विदमात्मन:।।1.16.26।।
transliteration: so'nta:puraṃ praviśyaiva kausalyāmidamabravīt| pāyasaṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva putrīyaṃ tvidamātmana:
translation: स: he, अन्त:पुरम् inner apartment, प्रविश्यैव after entering, कौसल्याम् addressing queen Kausalya, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke, आत्मन: for you, पुत्रीयम् bestowing sons, इदम् this, पायसम् Payasam, प्रतिगृह्णीष्व receive it.
explanation: He entered the inner apartment and addressing queen Kausalya said, "Receive this payasam which has the power to give you sons".

shloka_text: कौसल्यायै नरपति: पायसार्धं ददौ तदा। अर्धादर्धं ददौ चापि सुमित्रायै नराधिप:।।1.16.27।। कैकेय्यै चावशिष्टार्धं ददौ पुत्रार्थकारणात्। प्रददौ चावशिष्टार्धं पायसस्यामृतोपमम्।।1.16.28।। अनुचिन्त्य सुमित्रायै पुनरेव महीपति:। एवं तासां ददौ राजा भार्याणां पायसं पृथक् ।।1.16.29।।
transliteration: kausalyāyai narapati: pāyasārdhaṃ dadau tadā| ardhādardhaṃ dadau cāpi sumitrāyai narādhipa: kaikeyyai cāvaśiṣṭārdhaṃ dadau putrārthakāraṇāt| pradadau cāvaśiṣṭārdhaṃ pāyasasyāmṛtopamam anucintya sumitrāyai punareva mahīpati:| evaṃ tāsāṃ dadau rājā bhāryāṇāṃ pāyasaṃ pṛthak
translation: तदा then, नरपति: king Dasaratha, कौसल्यायै for Kausalya, पायसार्धम् half of Payasa, ददौ gave, नराधिप: king, अर्धात् from the half portion, अर्धम् half of it, सुमित्रायै अपि for Sumitra also, ददौ gave, अवशिष्टार्धम् the remaining half, पुत्रार्थकारणात् for the sake of son, कैकेय्यै for Kaikeyi, ददौ gave, महीपति: king, अनुचिन्त्य having thought over, पायसस्य Payasam, अमृतोपमम् resembling ambrosia, अवसिष्टार्धम् the remaining half, पुनरेव again, सुमित्रायै for Sumitra, प्रददौ gave, एवम् in this manner, राजा king, तासां भार्याणाम् for his wives, पृथक् separately, पायसम् Payasam, ददौ gave.
explanation: Then Dasaratha gave half the portion of payasam to Kausalya, half of the remaining half to Sumitra, half of the remaining portion (oneeighth of original) to Kaikeyi for the sake of a son. On further thinking, he gave the remaining oneeighth portion to Sumitra. In this manner the king divided and distributed the payasam among his wives separately.

shloka_text: कौसल्यायै नरपति: पायसार्धं ददौ तदा। अर्धादर्धं ददौ चापि सुमित्रायै नराधिप:।।1.16.27।। कैकेय्यै चावशिष्टार्धं ददौ पुत्रार्थकारणात्। प्रददौ चावशिष्टार्धं पायसस्यामृतोपमम्।।1.16.28।। अनुचिन्त्य सुमित्रायै पुनरेव महीपति:। एवं तासां ददौ राजा भार्याणां पायसं पृथक् ।।1.16.29।।
transliteration: kausalyāyai narapati: pāyasārdhaṃ dadau tadā| ardhādardhaṃ dadau cāpi sumitrāyai narādhipa: kaikeyyai cāvaśiṣṭārdhaṃ dadau putrārthakāraṇāt| pradadau cāvaśiṣṭārdhaṃ pāyasasyāmṛtopamam anucintya sumitrāyai punareva mahīpati:| evaṃ tāsāṃ dadau rājā bhāryāṇāṃ pāyasaṃ pṛthak
translation: तदा then, नरपति: king Dasaratha, कौसल्यायै for Kausalya, पायसार्धम् half of Payasa, ददौ gave, नराधिप: king, अर्धात् from the half portion, अर्धम् half of it, सुमित्रायै अपि for Sumitra also, ददौ gave, अवशिष्टार्धम् the remaining half, पुत्रार्थकारणात् for the sake of son, कैकेय्यै for Kaikeyi, ददौ gave, महीपति: king, अनुचिन्त्य having thought over, पायसस्य Payasam, अमृतोपमम् resembling ambrosia, अवसिष्टार्धम् the remaining half, पुनरेव again, सुमित्रायै for Sumitra, प्रददौ gave, एवम् in this manner, राजा king, तासां भार्याणाम् for his wives, पृथक् separately, पायसम् Payasam, ददौ gave.
explanation: Then Dasaratha gave half the portion of payasam to Kausalya, half of the remaining half to Sumitra, half of the remaining portion (oneeighth of original) to Kaikeyi for the sake of a son. On further thinking, he gave the remaining oneeighth portion to Sumitra. In this manner the king divided and distributed the payasam among his wives separately.

shloka_text: तास्त्वेतत्पायसं प्राप्य नरेन्द्रस्योत्तमास्स्त्रय:। सम्मानं मेनिरे सर्वां: प्रहर्षोदितचेतस:।।1.16.30।।
transliteration: tāstvetatpāyasaṃ prāpya narendrasyottamāsstraya:| sammānaṃ menire sarvāṃ: praharṣoditacetasa:
translation: नरेन्द्रस्य king's, उत्तमा: excellent, ता:स्त्रिय: those women, सर्वा: all, एतत् this, पायसम् Payasam, प्राप्य having received, प्रहर्षोदितचेतस: minds filled with delight, सम्मानम्  honour  मेनिरे considered.
explanation: The virtuous wives of the king were exceedingly delighted and felt honoured after receiving the payasam .

shloka_text: ततस्तु ता: प्राश्य तदुत्तमास्त्रियो महीपतेरुत्तमपायसं पृथक्। हुताशनादित्यसमानतेजसो ऽचिरेण गर्भान्प्रतिपेदिरे तदा।।1.16.31।।
transliteration: tatastu tā: prāśya taduttamāstriyo mahīpateruttamapāyasaṃ pṛthak| hutāśanādityasamānatejaso 'cireṇa garbhānpratipedire tadā
translation: ततः then, महीपते: king's, ता:उत्तमास्त्रिय: excellent consorts, तत् उत्तमपायसम् that choicest Payasam, पृथक् separately, प्राश्य having consumed, हुताशनादित्यसमानतेजस: resembling glowing fire and Sun in lustre, अचिरेण after short gap of time, तदा then, गर्भान् प्रतिपेदिरे became pregnant.
explanation: Then the excellent consorts of the king who glowed like fire and the Sun, having consumed the choicest payasam, became pregnant in a short time.

shloka_text: ततस्तु राजा प्रसमीक्ष्य ता: स्त्रिय: प्ररूढगर्भा: प्रतिलब्धमानस:। बभूव हृष्टस्त्रिदिवे यथा हरि: सुरेन्द्रसिद्धर्षिगणाभिपूजित:।।1.16.32।।
transliteration: tatastu rājā prasamīkṣya tā: striya: prarūḍhagarbhā: pratilabdhamānasa:| babhūva hṛṣṭastridive yathā hari: surendrasiddharṣigaṇābhipūjita:
translation: तत: then, राजा king, प्ररूढगर्भा: pregnant women, ता: स्त्रिय: those wives, प्रसमीक्ष्य having seen, प्रतिलब्धमानस: having regained composure of mind, त्रिदिवे in the heavens, सुरेन्द्रसिद्धर्षिगणाभिपूजित: worshipped by Indra, hosts of siddhas and rishis, यथा हरि: like Visnu, हृष्ट:बभूव became delighted.
explanation: The king now regained his composure of mind on seeing his pregnant wives. He looked delighted like Visnu worshipped by Indra, and hosts of siddhas and rishis. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे षोडशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the sixteenth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: पुत्रत्वं तु गते विष्णौ राज्ञस्तस्य सुमहात्मन:। उवाच देवतास्सर्वास्स्वयम्भूर्भगवानिदम्।।1.17.1।।
transliteration: putratvaṃ tu gate viṣṇau rājñastasya sumahātmana:| uvāca devatāssarvāssvayambhūrbhagavānidam
translation: विष्णौ when Vishnu, सुमहात्मन: of the high minded, राज्ञ: king's, पुत्रत्वम् filialrelationship, गते(सति) having become, भगवान् स्वयम्भू: selfborn lord, Brahma, सर्वा: addressing all, देवता: devatas, इदम् these words, उवाच spoke.
explanation: When Visnu had decided to be born as the son of that great king (Dasaratha), the selfborn Lord (Brahma), addressed all devatas :
comments: At the instance of Brahma, devas procreate different forms of monkey chiefs and bears.

shloka_text: सत्यसन्धस्य वीरस्य सर्वेषान्नो हितैषिण:। विष्णोस्सहायान्बलिनस्सृजध्वं कामरूपिण:।।1.17.2।।
transliteration: satyasandhasya vīrasya sarveṣānno hitaiṣiṇa:| viṣṇossahāyānbalinassṛjadhvaṃ kāmarūpiṇa:
translation: सत्यसन्धस्य truthful to promise, वीरस्य of the heroic, सर्वेषाम् नः for all of us, हितैषिण: wishing  the welfare, विष्णो: of Vishnu, सहायान् helpers(as companions), बलिन: strong, powerful and valiant, कामरूपिण: capable of changing forms at their free will, सृजध्वम् create.
explanation: Create strong and powerful beings capable of assuming forms at free will to extend support to Visnu who is  true to his word, heroic and benevolent.

shloka_text: मायाविदश्च शूरांश्च वायुवेगसमाञ्जवे। नयज्ञान्बुद्धिसम्पन्नान्विष्णुतुल्यपराक्रमान्।।1.17.3।। असंहार्यानुपायज्ञान् दिव्यसंहननान्वितान्। सर्वास्त्रगुणसम्पन्नानमृतप्राशनानिव।।1.17.4।। अप्सरस्सु च मुख्यासु गन्धर्वाणां तनूषु च । सृजध्वं हरिरूपेण पुत्रांस्तुल्यपराक्रमान्।।1.17.5।।
transliteration: māyāvidaśca śūrāṃśca vāyuvegasamāñjave| nayajñānbuddhisampannānviṣṇutulyaparākramān asaṃhāryānupāyajñān divyasaṃhananānvitān| sarvāstraguṇasampannānamṛtaprāśanāniva apsarassu ca mukhyāsu gandharvāṇāṃ tanūṣu ca | sṛjadhvaṃ harirūpeṇa putrāṃstulyaparākramān
translation: मायाविद: knowers of all kinds of illusions and deceitful tricks, शूरान् च brave, जवे in speed, वायुवेगसमान् equal to the speed of wind, नयज्ञान् knowers of statecraft, बुद्धिसम्पन्नान्  endowed with intellect, विष्णुतुल्यपराक्रमान् equal to Visnu in prowess, असंहार्यान् cannot be withdrawn from their endeavour, उपायज्ञान् knowledgeable in various means and ways of achieving victory namely Sama, Dana, Bheda and Danda, दिव्यसंहननान्वितान् having supernatural bodies, सर्वास्त्रगुणसम्पन्नान् possessed of capabilities in employing  and resisting weapons, अमृतप्राशनानिव resembling those who subsist on Amrita(immortals), (विष्णु)तुल्यपराक्रमान् in prowess equal to Visnu, पुत्रान् sons, मुख्यासु among the chief, अप्सरस्सु च apsarasas, गन्धर्वीणाम् gandharva women, तनूषु च from their bodies, हरिरूपेण in the form of monkeys, सृजध्वम् you may create.
explanation: Incarnate as monkeys in the womb of  chiefs of apsarasas and gandharvas. Create sons who have the knowledge of deceitful tricks, who are brave, who match wind in speed, who are endowed with intellect and statecraft, who are determined, who are  knowledgeable in various means of achieving victory, who are supernatural  bodies, who possess capability of employing and resisting weapons, who resemble those who subsist on amrita (immortals) and are equal (to Visnu) in prowess.

shloka_text: पूर्वमेव मया सृष्टो जाम्बवानृक्षपुङ्गव:। जृम्भमाणस्य सहसा मम वक्त्रादजायत।।1.17.6।।
transliteration: pūrvameva mayā sṛṣṭo jāmbavānṛkṣapuṅgava:| jṛmbhamāṇasya sahasā mama vaktrādajāyata
translation: जाम्बवान् by name Jambavan, ऋक्षपुङ्गव: foremost of bears, पूर्वमेव previously, मया by me, सृष्ट: was created, जृम्भमाणस्य मम when I was yawning, वक्त्रात् from my face, सहसा suddenly, अजायत was created.
explanation: Earlier Jambavan, the foremost among bears was suddenly emerged out of my face while I was yawning.

shloka_text: ते तथोक्ता भगवता तत्प्रतिश्रुत्य शासनम्। जनयामासुरेवं ते पुत्रान्वानररूपिण:।।1.17.7।।
transliteration: te tathoktā bhagavatā tatpratiśrutya śāsanam| janayāmāsurevaṃ te putrānvānararūpiṇa:
translation: भगवता by that Brahma, तथा in that manner, उक्ता: having been instructed, ते all of them, तत् प्रतिश्रुत्य having agreed, एवम् in this manner, वानररूपिण: those assuming the form of monkeys, पुत्रान् sons, जनयामासु: gave birth.
explanation: Instructed by Brahma in that manner, all of them gave birth to sons in the form of monkeys.

shloka_text: ऋषयश्च महात्मानस्सिद्धविद्याधरोरगा:। चारणाश्च सुतान्वीरान्ससृजुर्वनचारिण:।।1.17.8।।
transliteration: ṛṣayaśca mahātmānassiddhavidyādharoragā:| cāraṇāśca sutānvīrānsasṛjurvanacāriṇa:
translation: महात्मान: the distinguished, ऋषयश्च rishis, सिद्धविद्याधरोरगा siddhas, vidhyadharas and uragas, चारणा: charanas, वीरान् heroic, वनचारिण: dwellers in the woods, सुतान् sons, ससृजु: procreated.
explanation: Distinguished rishis, siddhas, vidhyadharas, uragas, charanas procreated (in the form of monkeys) heroic sons who became forestdwellers.

shloka_text: वानरेन्द्रं महेन्द्राभमिन्द्रो वालिनमूर्जितम्। सुग्रीवं जनयामास तपनस्तपतां वर:।।1.17.9।।
transliteration: vānarendraṃ mahendrābhamindro vālinamūrjitam| sugrīvaṃ janayāmāsa tapanastapatāṃ vara:
translation: इन्द्र: Indra, महेन्द्राभम् resembling Mahendra mountain, ऊर्जितम् having  body of mighty strength, वालिनम् by name Vali, वानरेन्द्रम् chief of monkeys, जनयामास gave birth to, तपताम् among those causing heat, वर: great, तपन: Sun, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva (begot).
explanation: Indra gave birth to Vali, chief of monkeys resembling Mahendra mountain and having a mighty body. Sun, great among those producing heat, begot Sugriva.

shloka_text: बृहस्पतिस्त्वजनयत्तारं नाम महाहरिम्। सर्ववानरमुख्यानां बुद्धिमन्तमनुत्तमम्।।1.17.10।।
transliteration: bṛhaspatistvajanayattāraṃ nāma mahāharim| sarvavānaramukhyānāṃ buddhimantamanuttamam
translation: बृहस्पतिस्तु Brihaspati, सर्ववानरमुख्यानाम्  among all monkey chiefs, अनुत्तमम् with none to surpass, बुद्धिमन्तम् highly intelligent, तारम् नाम by name Tara, महाहरिम् great monkey,	अजनयत् gave birth.
explanation: Brihaspati begot the intelligent monkey Tara who  had none to surpass him among the monkey chiefs.

shloka_text: धनदस्य सुतश्श्रीमान् वानरो गन्धमादन:। विश्वकर्मात्वजनयन्नलं नाम महाहरिम्।।1.17.11।।
transliteration: dhanadasya sutaśśrīmān vānaro gandhamādana:| viśvakarmātvajanayannalaṃ nāma mahāharim
translation: श्रीमान् glorious, गन्धमादन: by name Gandhamadana, वानर: monkey, धनदस्य Kubera's, सुत: son, विश्वकर्मा Viswakarma, नलं नाम by name Nala, महाहरिम् great monkey, अजनयत् begot.
explanation: Kubera begot glorious Gandhamadana and Viswakarma begot a great monkey Nala.

shloka_text: पावकस्य सुतश्श्रीमान् नीलोऽग्निसदृशप्रभ:। तेजसा यशसा वीर्यादत्यरिच्यत वानरान्।।1.17.12।।
transliteration: pāvakasya sutaśśrīmān nīlo'gnisadṛśaprabha:| tejasā yaśasā vīryādatyaricyata vānarān
translation: पावकस्य Agni's (the fire god), सुत: son, श्रीमान् prosperous , अग्निसदृशप्रभ: equal to Agni in brightness, नील: Neela, तेजसा by energy, यशसा by fame, वीर्यात् due to prowess, वानरान् other monkeys, अत्यरिच्यत surpassed.
explanation: Neela, the prosperous son of Agni the firegod who equalled him in glow surpassed other monkeys in energy, renown and prowess.

shloka_text: रूपद्रविणसम्पन्नावश्विनौ रूपसम्मतौ। मैन्दं च द्विविदं चैव जनयामासतुस्स्वयम्।।1.17.13।।
transliteration: rūpadraviṇasampannāvaśvinau rūpasammatau| maindaṃ ca dvividaṃ caiva janayāmāsatussvayam
translation: रूपद्रविणसम्पन्नौ endowed with wealth of beauty, अश्विनौ Aswini devatas, स्वयं रूपसम्मतौ esteemed because of their beauty, मैन्दं च Mainda, द्विविदं चैव Dvivida, जनयामासतु: procreated.
explanation: Aswini devatas, endowed with wealth and beauty, procreated Mainda and Dwivida who were highly esteemed for their beauty.

shloka_text: वरुणो जनयामास सुषेणं वानरर्षभम्। शरभं जनयामास पर्जन्यस्तु महाबलम्।।1.17.14।।
transliteration: varuṇo janayāmāsa suṣeṇaṃ vānararṣabham| śarabhaṃ janayāmāsa parjanyastu mahābalam
translation: वरुण: Varuna, सुषेणं by name Sushena, वानरर्षभम् monkey warrior, जनयामास created, पर्जन्यस्तु Parjanya, महाबलम् possessed of great strength, शरभम् Sarabha, जनयामास begot.
explanation: Varuna begot the monkey warrior Sushena and Parjanya, Sarabha of great strength.

shloka_text: मारुतस्यात्मजश्श्रीमान्हनुमान्नाम वीर्यवान् । वज्रसंहननोपेतो वैनतेयसमो जवे।।1.17.15।।
transliteration: mārutasyātmajaśśrīmānhanumānnāma vīryavān | vajrasaṃhananopeto vainateyasamo jave
translation: श्रीमान् dignified and graceful, वीर्यवान् endowed with prowess(wisdom andcourage), वज्रसंहननोपेत: with his body as hard as diamond, जवे in speed, वैनतेयसम: equalling Garuda, हनुमान् नाम named Hanuman, मारुतस्य आत्मज: son of Vayu, Windgod, Vayu.
explanation: Vayu, the windgod, begot a son named Hanuman, mighty and graceful, having a body as hard as a diamond and speed equal to Garuda's.

shloka_text: ते सृष्टा बहुसाहस्रा दशग्रीववधे रता:। अप्रमेयबला वीरा विक्रान्ता: कामरूपिण:।।1.17.16।।
transliteration: te sṛṣṭā bahusāhasrā daśagrīvavadhe ratā:| aprameyabalā vīrā vikrāntā: kāmarūpiṇa:
translation: दशग्रीववधे in the matter of slaying Ravana, रता: desirous, अप्रमेयबला: men of immeasurable strength, विक्रान्ता: courageous, कामरूपिण: capable of assuming different forms at will, बहुसाहस्रा: in many thousands, ते वीरा: those warriors, सृष्टा: were created.
explanation: Thousands of warriors possessing immeasurable strength and courage and capable of assuming any form at will were created to kill Ravana.

shloka_text: मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशा वपुष्मन्तो महाबला:। ऋक्षवानरगोपुच्छा: क्षिप्रमेवाभिजज्ञिरे।।1.17.17।।
transliteration: merumandarasaṅkāśā vapuṣmanto mahābalā:| ṛkṣavānaragopucchā: kṣipramevābhijajñire
translation: मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशा: similar to Meru and Mandara mountains, वपुष्मन्त: endowed with bodies, महाबला: great warriors, ऋक्षवानरगोपुच्छा: bears,monkeys, monkeys with cowtails, क्षिप्रमेव quickly, अभिजज्ञिरे came into being.
explanation: Endowed with bodies similar to the Meru and Mandara mountains and having  great strength, bears, monkeys, monkeys with cowtails quickly came into being.

shloka_text: यस्य देवस्य यद्रूपं वेषो यश्च पराक्रम:। अजायत समस्तेन तस्य तस्य सुत: पृथक्।।1.17.18।।
transliteration: yasya devasya yadrūpaṃ veṣo yaśca parākrama:| ajāyata samastena tasya tasya suta: pṛthak
translation: यस्य देवस्य for whichever god, यत् रूपम् whatever form, वेष: form of dress, पराक्रम:च prowess also, य: तस्य तस्य  for that respective God, सुत: sons, पृथक् separately, तेनसमः      similar to his procreator, अजायत was born.
explanation: The sons of devatas retained characteristics like beauty, form and prowess of their procreator (gods).

shloka_text: गोलाङ्गूलीषु चोत्पन्ना: केचित्सम्मतविक्रमा:। ऋक्षीषु च तथा जाता वानरा: किन्नरीषु च।।1.17.19।।
transliteration: golāṅgūlīṣu cotpannā: kecitsammatavikramā:| ṛkṣīṣu ca tathā jātā vānarā: kinnarīṣu ca
translation: सम्मतविक्रमा: men of highlyhonoured valour, केचित् वानरा: some Monkeys, गोलाङ्गूलीषु च from female monkeys with tails, उत्पन्ना: were born, तथा similarly, ऋक्षीषु from female bears, किन्नरीषु च female kinnaras, जाता: were created.
explanation: Some monkeys with acknowledged, valour were born to female monkeys with tails         Similarly some other monkeys were born to female bears and female kinnaras.

shloka_text: देवा महर्षिगन्धर्वास्तार्क्ष्या यक्षा यशस्विन:। नागा: किम्पुरुषाश्चैव सिद्धविद्याधरोरगा:।।1.17.20।। बहवो जनयामासुर्हृष्टास्तत्र सहस्रश:। वानरान्सुमहाकायान्सर्वान्वै वनचारिण:।।1.17.21।। अप्सरस्सु च मुख्यासु तथा विद्याधरीषु च। नागकन्यासु च तथा गन्धर्वीणां तनूषु च ।।1.17.22।।
transliteration: devā maharṣigandharvāstārkṣyā yakṣā yaśasvina:| nāgā: kimpuruṣāścaiva siddhavidyādharoragā: bahavo janayāmāsurhṛṣṭāstatra sahasraśa:| vānarānsumahākāyānsarvānvai vanacāriṇa: apsarassu ca mukhyāsu tathā vidyādharīṣu ca| nāgakanyāsu ca tathā gandharvīṇāṃ tanūṣu ca
translation: देवा: devatas, महर्षिगन्धर्वा: great rishis, gandharvas, तार्क्ष्या: garudas,यक्षा: yakshas, यशस्विन: renowned, नागा: serpants, किम्पुरूषाश्चैव kimpurushas,सिद्धविद्याधरोरगा: siddhas, vidyadharas, uragas, बहव: many, हृष्टा: pleased, तत्र there, मुख्यासु among the principal, अप्सरस्सु apsarasas, तथा and, विद्याधरीषु च among female vidhyadaris, नागकन्यासु in daughters of nagas, तथा and, गन्धर्वीणाम् of female gandhrvas, तनूषु च in bodies सुमहाकायान् of gigantic physique, वनचारिण: forest wanderers, सर्वान् all, वानरान् monkeys, सहस्रश: in thousands, जनयामासु: gave birth.
explanation: The devatas, rishis, gandharvas, garudas, yakshas, kimpurushas, siddhas, vidyadharas, uragas and many others were immensely pleased. Thousands of gigantic monkeys wandering in forests were procreated from principal apsarasas  vidhyadaris, nagas, and  gandharvas.

shloka_text: देवा महर्षिगन्धर्वास्तार्क्ष्या यक्षा यशस्विन:। नागा: किम्पुरुषाश्चैव सिद्धविद्याधरोरगा:।।1.17.20।। बहवो जनयामासुर्हृष्टास्तत्र सहस्रश:। वानरान्सुमहाकायान्सर्वान्वै वनचारिण:।।1.17.21।। अप्सरस्सु च मुख्यासु तथा विद्याधरीषु च। नागकन्यासु च तथा गन्धर्वीणां तनूषु च ।।1.17.22।।
transliteration: devā maharṣigandharvāstārkṣyā yakṣā yaśasvina:| nāgā: kimpuruṣāścaiva siddhavidyādharoragā: bahavo janayāmāsurhṛṣṭāstatra sahasraśa:| vānarānsumahākāyānsarvānvai vanacāriṇa: apsarassu ca mukhyāsu tathā vidyādharīṣu ca| nāgakanyāsu ca tathā gandharvīṇāṃ tanūṣu ca
translation: देवा: devatas, महर्षिगन्धर्वा: great rishis, gandharvas, तार्क्ष्या: garudas,यक्षा: yakshas, यशस्विन: renowned, नागा: serpants, किम्पुरूषाश्चैव kimpurushas,सिद्धविद्याधरोरगा: siddhas, vidyadharas, uragas, बहव: many, हृष्टा: pleased, तत्र there, मुख्यासु among the principal, अप्सरस्सु apsarasas, तथा and, विद्याधरीषु च among female vidhyadaris, नागकन्यासु in daughters of nagas, तथा and, गन्धर्वीणाम् of female gandhrvas, तनूषु च in bodies सुमहाकायान् of gigantic physique, वनचारिण: forest wanderers, सर्वान् all, वानरान् monkeys, सहस्रश: in thousands, जनयामासु: gave birth.
explanation: The devatas, rishis, gandharvas, garudas, yakshas, kimpurushas, siddhas, vidyadharas, uragas and many others were immensely pleased. Thousands of gigantic monkeys wandering in forests were procreated from principal apsarasas  vidhyadaris, nagas, and  gandharvas.

shloka_text: देवा महर्षिगन्धर्वास्तार्क्ष्या यक्षा यशस्विन:। नागा: किम्पुरुषाश्चैव सिद्धविद्याधरोरगा:।।1.17.20।। बहवो जनयामासुर्हृष्टास्तत्र सहस्रश:। वानरान्सुमहाकायान्सर्वान्वै वनचारिण:।।1.17.21।। अप्सरस्सु च मुख्यासु तथा विद्याधरीषु च। नागकन्यासु च तथा गन्धर्वीणां तनूषु च ।।1.17.22।।
transliteration: devā maharṣigandharvāstārkṣyā yakṣā yaśasvina:| nāgā: kimpuruṣāścaiva siddhavidyādharoragā: bahavo janayāmāsurhṛṣṭāstatra sahasraśa:| vānarānsumahākāyānsarvānvai vanacāriṇa: apsarassu ca mukhyāsu tathā vidyādharīṣu ca| nāgakanyāsu ca tathā gandharvīṇāṃ tanūṣu ca
translation: देवा: devatas, महर्षिगन्धर्वा: great rishis, gandharvas, तार्क्ष्या: garudas,यक्षा: yakshas, यशस्विन: renowned, नागा: serpants, किम्पुरूषाश्चैव kimpurushas,सिद्धविद्याधरोरगा: siddhas, vidyadharas, uragas, बहव: many, हृष्टा: pleased, तत्र there, मुख्यासु among the principal, अप्सरस्सु apsarasas, तथा and, विद्याधरीषु च among female vidhyadaris, नागकन्यासु in daughters of nagas, तथा and, गन्धर्वीणाम् of female gandhrvas, तनूषु च in bodies सुमहाकायान् of gigantic physique, वनचारिण: forest wanderers, सर्वान् all, वानरान् monkeys, सहस्रश: in thousands, जनयामासु: gave birth.
explanation: The devatas, rishis, gandharvas, garudas, yakshas, kimpurushas, siddhas, vidyadharas, uragas and many others were immensely pleased. Thousands of gigantic monkeys wandering in forests were procreated from principal apsarasas  vidhyadaris, nagas, and  gandharvas.

shloka_text: कामरूपबलोपेता यथाकामं विचारिण:। सिंहशार्दूलसदृशा दर्पेण च बलेन च।।1.17.23।।
transliteration: kāmarūpabalopetā yathākāmaṃ vicāriṇa:| siṃhaśārdūlasadṛśā darpeṇa ca balena ca
translation: कामरूपबलोपेता: (all these monkeys were endowed )with the powers to assume any form at free will and possessed strength, यथाकामम् freely, विचारिण: wanderers, दर्पेण च in arrogance, बलेन च by prowess, सिंहशार्दूलसदृशा: like unto lions and tigers.
explanation: They were endowed with the powers to assume any form at will. They possessed enormous strength and power to freely wander in forests. They were like lions and tigers in pride and prowess.

shloka_text: शिलाप्रहरणास्सर्वे सर्वे पादपयोधिन:।।1.17.24।। नखदंष्ट्रायुधास्सर्वे सर्वे सर्वास्त्रकोविदा:।
transliteration: śilāpraharaṇāssarve sarve pādapayodhina: nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhāssarve sarve sarvāstrakovidā:|
translation: सर्वे all, शिलाप्रहरणा: could strike with rocks as weapons, सर्वे all, पादपयोधिन: they could fight with trees, सर्वे all, नखदंष्ट्रायुधा: used nails and teeth as weapon, सर्वे all, सर्वास्त्रकोविदा: skilled in the use of all weapons.
explanation: They all could strike with rocks, use nails and teeth and trees as weapons. They were skilled in the use of all kinds of weapons.

shloka_text: विचालयेयुश्शैलेन्द्रान्भेदयेयुस्स्थिरान्द्रुमान्। क्षोभयेयुश्च वेगेन समुद्रं सरितां पतिम्।।1.17.25।।
transliteration: vicālayeyuśśailendrānbhedayeyussthirāndrumān| kṣobhayeyuśca vegena samudraṃ saritāṃ patim
translation: शैलेन्द्रान् mountains, विचालयेयु: could move, स्थिरान् द्रुमान् deeprooted trees, भेदयेयु: could break, वेगेन with speed, सरितां पतिम् the lord of the rivers, समुद्रम् Samudra, क्षोभयेयु: could cause disturbance.
explanation: They could shake mountains and uproot deeprooted trees. With their speed they could cause disturbance to Samudra, the lord of the rivers.

shloka_text: दारयेयु: क्षितिं पद्भ्यामाप्लवेयुर्महार्णवम्। नभ:स्थलम् विशेयुश्च गृह्णीयुरपि तोयदान्।।1.17.26।।
transliteration: dārayeyu: kṣitiṃ padbhyāmāplaveyurmahārṇavam| nabha:sthalam viśeyuśca gṛhṇīyurapi toyadān
translation: पद्भ्याम् with their feet, क्षितिम् this earth, दारयेयु: forcibly cause cleavage, महार्णवम् mighty ocean, आप्लवेयुः jump with one leap and cross, नभ:स्थलम् the sky, विशेयुश्च could enter, तोयदान् अपि clouds also, गृह्णीयु: could seize.
explanation: They could cause cleavage to this earth with their feet, cross the mighty ocean with one leap and enter the sky and even seize the clouds.

shloka_text: गृह्णीयुरपि मातङ्गान्मत्तान्प्रव्रजतो वने। नर्दमानाश्च नादेन पातयेयुर्विहङ्गमान्।।1.17.27।।
transliteration: gṛhṇīyurapi mātaṅgānmattānpravrajato vane| nardamānāśca nādena pātayeyurvihaṅgamān
translation: वने in the forest, प्रव्रजत: sojourning, मत्तान्  arrogant,मातङ्गान् अपि elephants also, गृह्णीयु: could capture, नर्दमाना: while roaring, नादेन with their sounds, विहङ्गमान् birds in flight, पातयेयुः could be made to fall down.
explanation: They could capture wild elephants sojourning in the forest and make the flying birds drop down screaming.

shloka_text: ईदृशानां प्रसूतानि हरीणां कामरूपिणाम्। शतं शतसहस्राणि यूथपानां महात्मनाम्।।1.17.28।।
transliteration: īdṛśānāṃ prasūtāni harīṇāṃ kāmarūpiṇām| śataṃ śatasahasrāṇi yūthapānāṃ mahātmanām
translation: कामरूपिणाम् of those who were capable of assuming any form at will, यूथपानाम् commanders of monkey forces, महात्मनाम् eminent, ईदृशानाम्  of such, हरीणाम् monkeys, शतम् hundred, शतसहस्राणि hundred thousands, प्रसूतानि were born.
explanation: A crore of monkeys capable of assuming any form at will, great monkeys and commanders of monkey forces were created.

shloka_text: ते प्रधानेषु यूथेषु हरीणां हरियूथपा:। बभूवुर्यूथपश्रेष्ठा वीरांश्चाजनयन् हरीन्।।1.17.29।।
transliteration: te pradhāneṣu yūtheṣu harīṇāṃ hariyūthapā:| babhūvuryūthapaśreṣṭhā vīrāṃścājanayan harīn
translation: ते हरियूथपा: those commanders of monkey forces, हरीणाम् monkeys, प्रधानेषु  among important ones, यूथेषु monkey forces, यूथपश्रेष्ठा: बभूवु: important monkeys were born, वीरान् herioc, हरीन् monkeys, अजनयन् created.
explanation: Those monkey commanders created heroic monkeys among the chief monkey clans who later proved the best among clanleaders.

shloka_text: अन्ये ऋक्षवत: प्रस्थानवतस्थु स्सहस्रश:। अन्ये नानाविधान्शैलान्भेजिरे काननानि च।।1.17.30।।
transliteration: anye ṛkṣavata: prasthānavatasthu ssahasraśa:| anye nānāvidhānśailānbhejire kānanāni ca
translation: अन्ये some monkeys, सहस्रश: in thousands, ऋक्षवत: abounding in bears, प्रस्थान् plateaus on the top of mountains, अवतस्थु: dwelt, अन्ये some others, नानाविधान् various, शैलान् mountains, काननानि च forests also, भेजिरे inhabited.
explanation: Thousands of monkeys dwelt on the plateaus on the top of mountains abounding in bears. Some others inhabited various hills and forests.

shloka_text: सूर्यपुत्रं च सुग्रीवं शक्रपुत्रं च वालिनम्। भ्रातरावुपतस्थुस्ते सर्व एव हरीश्वरा:।।1.17.31।। नलं नीलं हनूमन्तमन्यांश्च हरियूथपान्। 3
transliteration: sūryaputraṃ ca sugrīvaṃ śakraputraṃ ca vālinam| bhrātarāvupatasthuste sarva eva harīśvarā: nalaṃ nīlaṃ hanūmantamanyāṃśca hariyūthapān| 3
translation: ते हरीश्वरा: these leaders of monkey forces, सर्वे all, भ्रातरौ two  brothers, सूर्यपुत्रम् son of Sungod, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, शक्रपुत्रम् Indra's son, वालिनं च Vali also, नलम् Nala,नीलम् Neela, हनूमन्तम् Hanuman, अन्यान् other, हरियूथपान् leaders of monkey forces, उपतस्थु: dwelt near them.
explanation: All those leaders, Nala, Neela, Hanuman and others dwelt near those two brothers Sugriva, the offspring of Surya and Vali, the son of Indra.

shloka_text: ते तार्क्ष्यबलसम्पन्नास्सर्वे युद्धविशारदा:। विचरन्तोऽर्दयन्दर्पात्सिंहव्याघ्रमहोरगान्।।1.17.32।।
transliteration: te tārkṣyabalasampannāssarve yuddhaviśāradā:| vicaranto'rdayandarpātsiṃhavyāghramahoragān
translation: तार्क्ष्यबलसम्पन्ना: those endowed with the might of Garuda, युद्धविशारदा: wellversed in the art of warfare, ते सर्वे all of them, विचरन्त: moving around, दर्पात् due to arrogance, सिंहव्याघ्रमहोरगान् lions, tigers, mighty serpents, अर्दयन् tormented.
explanation: Endowed with the might of Garuda and wellversed in warfare, all of them  moving around tormented ferouious lions, tigers and mighty serpents .

shloka_text: तांश्च सर्वान्महाबाहुर्वाली विपुलविक्रम:। जुगोप भुजवीर्येण ऋक्षगोपुच्छवानरान्।।1.17.33।।
transliteration: tāṃśca sarvānmahābāhurvālī vipulavikrama:| jugopa bhujavīryeṇa ṛkṣagopucchavānarān
translation: महाबाहु: mighty armed, विपुलविक्रम: one with immense prowess, वाली Vali, तान् सर्वान् all of those, ऋक्षगोपुच्छवानरान् bears, Gopuchhas, monkeys, भुजवीर्येण with the strength of his arms, जुगोप protected.
explanation: Mighty armed leader Vali endowed  with immense prowess  protected, with his strong arms all those bears, gopuchhas(cowtailed) and monkeys.

shloka_text: तैरियं पृथिवी शूरैस्सपर्वतवनार्णवा। कीर्णा विविधसंस्थानैर्नानाव्यञ्जनलक्षणै:।।1.17.34।।
transliteration: tairiyaṃ pṛthivī śūraissaparvatavanārṇavā| kīrṇā vividhasaṃsthānairnānāvyañjanalakṣaṇai:
translation: शूरै: by the valiant, विविधसंस्थानै: having many forms, नानाव्यञ्जनलक्षणै: with various characteristic signs relating to the body and tribes, तै: by them, सपर्वतवनार्णवा with its mountains, forests, seas, इयं पृथिवी this earth, कीर्णा was pervaded.
explanation: Born in many forms  wih various characteristics (relating to the body and tribe), they pervaded this earth with its mountains, forests and seas.

shloka_text: तैर्मेघबृन्दाचलकूटकल्पै: महाबलैर्वानरयूथपालै:। बभूव भूर्भीमशरीररूपै स्समावृता रामसहायहेतो:।।1.17.35।।
transliteration: tairmeghabṛndācalakūṭakalpai: mahābalairvānarayūthapālai:| babhūva bhūrbhīmaśarīrarūpai ssamāvṛtā rāmasahāyaheto:
translation: मेघबृन्दाचलकूटकल्पै: resembling masses of clouds and mountain peaks,महाबलै: by those endowed with immense strength, भीमशरीररूपै: by those having fearful forms and countenances, तै: वानरयूथपालै: by commanders of  the monkey forces, भू: earth, रामसहायहेतो: in order to assist Rama, समावृता बभूव became covered.
explanation: In order to assist Rama, this earth was filled with commanders of those who led the monkey forces resembling masses of clouds and mountains. They loan endowed with immense strength and fearful forms and countenances. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे सप्तदशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the seventeenth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: निर्वृत्ते तु क्रतौ तस्मिन्हयमेधे महात्मन:। प्रतिगृह्य सुरा भागान्प्रतिजग्मुर्यथागतम्।।1.18.1।।
transliteration: nirvṛtte tu kratau tasminhayamedhe mahātmana:| pratigṛhya surā bhāgānpratijagmuryathāgatam
translation: महात्मन: magnanimous king Dasaratha's, तस्मिन् हयमेधे  when Aswamedha, क्रतौ sacrifice, निर्वृत्ते सति had been completed, सुरा: devatas, भागान् their share of Havis, प्रतिगृह्य having received, यथागतम् from wherever they came, प्रतिजग्मु: returned.
explanation: Completed by the magnanimous king (Dasaratha). The aswamedha and putreshti sacrifices, the devatas received their share of havis and returned to their respective  abodes.
comments: Dasaratha sends Rsyasringa and the kings and to their respective places -- returns to Ayodhya with his wives--birth of Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata and Satrughna -- purificatory and naming rites -- description of their virtues and characteritics --  Viswamitra comes to meet Dasaratha

shloka_text: समाप्तदीक्षानियम: पत्नीगणसमन्वित:। प्रविवेश पुरीं राजा सभृत्यबलवाहन:।।1.18.2।।
transliteration: samāptadīkṣāniyama: patnīgaṇasamanvita:| praviveśa purīṃ rājā sabhṛtyabalavāhana:
translation: पत्नीगणसमन्वित: together with his queens, राजा king Dasaratha, समाप्तदीक्षानियम: having observed the rules of initiation, सभृत्यबलवाहन: along with his servants, army chariots, पुरीम् city of Ayodhya, प्रविवेश entered.
explanation: Having completed the prescribed vows (in respect of aswamedha), king Dasaratha together with his queens returned to the city of Ayodhya accompanied by his attendants, army and chariots.

shloka_text: यथार्हं पूजितास्तेन राज्ञा वै पृथिवीश्वरा:। मुदिता: प्रययुर्देशान्प्रणम्य मुनिपुङ्गवम्।।1.18.3।।
transliteration: yathārhaṃ pūjitāstena rājñā vai pṛthivīśvarā:| muditā: prayayurdeśānpraṇamya munipuṅgavam
translation: पृथिवीश्वरा: lords of the earth, kings,तेन राज्ञा by that king (Dasaratha), यथार्हम् in a fitting manner, पूजिता: having been honoured, मुदिता: pleased, मुनिपुङ्गवम् best of sages, Vasistha, प्रणम्य having made obeisance, देशान् to their own countries, प्रययु: returned.
explanation: Having been honoured by the king (Dasaratha) in a be fitting manner, the highly pleased lords of the earth (kings) made obeisance to the best of sages (Vasishta) and returned to their own countries.

shloka_text: श्रीमतां गच्छतां तेषां स्वपुराणि पुरात्तत:। बलानि राज्ञां शुभ्राणि प्रहृष्टानि चकाशिरे।।1.18.4।।
transliteration: śrīmatāṃ gacchatāṃ teṣāṃ svapurāṇi purāttata:| balāni rājñāṃ śubhrāṇi prahṛṣṭāni cakāśire
translation: तत: पुरात्  from that town, स्वपुराणि to their own town, गच्छताम्  set out  for, श्रीमताम् dignified, तेषाम् राज्ञाम् those kings', शुभ्राणि bright, प्रहृष्टानि delighted, बलानि forces, चकाशिरे      shone.
explanation: When the army of the kings left the city (Ayodhya) for their own, the armed forces shone bright and cheerfl.

shloka_text: गतेषु पृथिवीशेषु राजा दशरथस्तदा। प्रविवेश पुरीं श्रीमान् पुरस्कृत्य द्विजोत्तमान्।।1.18.5।।
transliteration: gateṣu pṛthivīśeṣu rājā daśarathastadā| praviveśa purīṃ śrīmān puraskṛtya dvijottamān
translation: पृथिवीशेषु when kings, गतेषु (सत्सु) departed, तदा then, श्रीमान् the exalted, राजा दशरथ: king Dasaratha, द्विजोत्तमान् foremost of brahmins, पुरस्कृत्य preceded by them, पुरीम् प्रविवेश entered the capital city.
explanation: After the departure of the rulers, the exalted king Dasaratha preceded by the foremost of brahmins entered the city (of Ayodhya).

shloka_text: शान्तया प्रययौ सार्धमृश्यशृङ्गस्सुपूजित:। अन्वीयमानो राज्ञाऽथ सानुयात्रेण धीमता।।1.18.6।।
transliteration: śāntayā prayayau sārdhamṛśyaśṛṅgassupūjita:| anvīyamāno rājñā'tha sānuyātreṇa dhīmatā
translation: अथ after that, ऋश्यशृङ्ग: sage Rsyasringa, सुपूजित: having been duly honoured, सानुयात्रेण along his followers, धीमता by the intellectual, राज्ञा king Romapada, अन्वीयमान: was being accompanied, शान्तया सार्धम् with Santa, प्रययौ set out.
explanation: Having been duly honoured by king Dasaratha, sage Rsyasringa with his wife Santa  accompanied by the wise king Romapada and his followers set out for his country.

shloka_text: एवं विसृज्य तान्सर्वान्राजा सम्पूर्णमानस:। उवास सुखितस्तत्र पुत्रोत्पत्तिं विचिन्तयन्।।1.18.7।।
transliteration: evaṃ visṛjya tānsarvānrājā sampūrṇamānasa:| uvāsa sukhitastatra putrotpattiṃ vicintayan
translation: राजा king Dasaratha, एवम् in this manner, तान् सर्वान्  all of them, विसृज्य having sent them, सम्पूर्णमानस: with composed mind, पुत्रोत्पत्तिम् about begetting sons, विचिन्तयन् thinking, तत्र there, सुखित: उवास lived happily.
explanation: When they (guests) all departed in this manner, Dasaratha with his desire fulfilled, his thought centred on begetting sons lived happily.

shloka_text: ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु ऋतूनां षट्समत्ययु:। ततश्च द्वादशे मासे चैत्रे नावमिके तिथौ।।1.18.8।। नक्षत्रेऽदितिदैवत्ये स्वोच्चसंस्थेषु  पञ्चसु। ग्रहेषु कर्कटे लग्ने वाक्पताविन्दुना सह।।1.18.9।। प्रोद्यमाने जगन्नाथं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम्। कौसल्याऽजनयद्रामं सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम्।।1.18.10।। विष्णोरर्धं महाभागं पुत्रमैक्ष्वाकुवर्धनम्।
transliteration: tato yajñe samāpte tu ṛtūnāṃ ṣaṭsamatyayu:| tataśca dvādaśe māse caitre nāvamike tithau nakṣatre'ditidaivatye svoccasaṃstheṣu  pañcasu| graheṣu karkaṭe lagne vākpatāvindunā saha prodyamāne jagannāthaṃ sarvalokanamaskṛtam| kausalyā'janayadrāmaṃ sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutam viṣṇorardhaṃ mahābhāgaṃ putramaikṣvākuvardhanam|
translation: तत: then, यज्ञे when sacrifice, समाप्ते was completed, ऋतूनाम् of seasons, षट् six, समत्ययु: were spent, तत: then, द्वादशे मासे in twelfth month, चैत्रे in Chaitra month, नावमिके तिथौ on the nineth day of the rising Moon, अदितिदैवत्ये presided by Aditi as devata, नक्षत्रे when the star (Punarvasu)was in ascendent, पञ्चसु ग्रहेषु and the five planets (Sun, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter and Venus), स्वोच्चसंस्थेषु in their own exalted houses,  कर्कटे लग्ने in Karkata Lagna, वाक्पतौ when Brihaspati, इन्दुना सह  along with Moon, प्रोद्यमाने was rising, कौसल्या Kausalya, जगन्नाथम् lord of the entire universe, सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् bowed to by all the worlds, सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम् adorned with all the characteristics, विष्णो: Vishnu's, अर्धम् facet, महाभागम् highly fortunate, ऐक्ष्वाकुवर्धनम्  perpetuating the Ikshvaku race, रामम् Rama, पुत्रम् as his son, अजनयत् gave birth .
explanation: Six seasons (one year) passed after the completion of the sacrifice. In the twelfth month of Chaitra on the ninth day (of the bright fortnight), with Aditi as presiding deity when the star Punarvasu was in the ascendent and the five planets Sun, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter and Venus, were exalted in their own house in karkata lagna, when Brihaspati was in conjunction with the Moon, Kausalya gave birth to a son: a facet of Visnu, Lord of the entire universe who received obeisance from all the worlds and was adorned with all auspicious signs, the venerable one  to perpetuate the Ikshvaku race.

shloka_text: ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु ऋतूनां षट्समत्ययु:। ततश्च द्वादशे मासे चैत्रे नावमिके तिथौ।।1.18.8।। नक्षत्रेऽदितिदैवत्ये स्वोच्चसंस्थेषु  पञ्चसु। ग्रहेषु कर्कटे लग्ने वाक्पताविन्दुना सह।।1.18.9।। प्रोद्यमाने जगन्नाथं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम्। कौसल्याऽजनयद्रामं सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम्।।1.18.10।। विष्णोरर्धं महाभागं पुत्रमैक्ष्वाकुवर्धनम्।
transliteration: tato yajñe samāpte tu ṛtūnāṃ ṣaṭsamatyayu:| tataśca dvādaśe māse caitre nāvamike tithau nakṣatre'ditidaivatye svoccasaṃstheṣu  pañcasu| graheṣu karkaṭe lagne vākpatāvindunā saha prodyamāne jagannāthaṃ sarvalokanamaskṛtam| kausalyā'janayadrāmaṃ sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutam viṣṇorardhaṃ mahābhāgaṃ putramaikṣvākuvardhanam|
translation: तत: then, यज्ञे when sacrifice, समाप्ते was completed, ऋतूनाम् of seasons, षट् six, समत्ययु: were spent, तत: then, द्वादशे मासे in twelfth month, चैत्रे in Chaitra month, नावमिके तिथौ on the nineth day of the rising Moon, अदितिदैवत्ये presided by Aditi as devata, नक्षत्रे when the star (Punarvasu)was in ascendent, पञ्चसु ग्रहेषु and the five planets (Sun, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter and Venus), स्वोच्चसंस्थेषु in their own exalted houses,  कर्कटे लग्ने in Karkata Lagna, वाक्पतौ when Brihaspati, इन्दुना सह  along with Moon, प्रोद्यमाने was rising, कौसल्या Kausalya, जगन्नाथम् lord of the entire universe, सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् bowed to by all the worlds, सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम् adorned with all the characteristics, विष्णो: Vishnu's, अर्धम् facet, महाभागम् highly fortunate, ऐक्ष्वाकुवर्धनम्  perpetuating the Ikshvaku race, रामम् Rama, पुत्रम् as his son, अजनयत् gave birth .
explanation: Six seasons (one year) passed after the completion of the sacrifice. In the twelfth month of Chaitra on the ninth day (of the bright fortnight), with Aditi as presiding deity when the star Punarvasu was in the ascendent and the five planets Sun, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter and Venus, were exalted in their own house in karkata lagna, when Brihaspati was in conjunction with the Moon, Kausalya gave birth to a son: a facet of Visnu, Lord of the entire universe who received obeisance from all the worlds and was adorned with all auspicious signs, the venerable one  to perpetuate the Ikshvaku race.

shloka_text: कौसल्या शुशुभे तेन पुत्रेणामिततेजसा।।1.18.11।। यथा वरेण देवानामदितिर्वज्रपाणिना।
transliteration: kausalyā śuśubhe tena putreṇāmitatejasā yathā vareṇa devānāmaditirvajrapāṇinā|
translation: कौसल्या Kausalya, अमिततेजसा by one with immeasurable lustre, तेन पुत्रेण by that son, देवानाम् among devatas, by the foremost,वज्रपाणिना by the wielder of Thunderbolt, Indra, अदिति: यथा like Aditi, शुशुभे looked resplendent.
explanation: Kausalya glowed with the undiminished lustre of her son, just as Aditi with  her son Indra, the foremost among the gods and  the wielder of thunder.

shloka_text: भरतो नाम कैकेय्यां जज्ञे सत्यपराक्रम:।।1.18.12।। साक्षाद्विष्णोश्चतुर्भागस्सर्वैस्समुदितो गुणै:।
transliteration: bharato nāma kaikeyyāṃ jajñe satyaparākrama: sākṣādviṣṇoścaturbhāgassarvaissamudito guṇai:|
translation: सत्यपराक्रम: having truthful prowess, साक्षात् manifestly, विष्णो: Visnu's, चतुर्भाग: fourth part, सर्वै: गुणै: with every kind of virtue, समुदित: united with, भरतो नाम named Bharata, कैकेय्याम् of Kaikeyi, जज्ञे was born.
explanation: As an incarnation of the  fourth part of Visnu, imbued with all virtues, and armed with truth Bharata was born to Kaikeyi.

shloka_text: अथ लक्ष्मणशत्रुघ्नौ सुमित्राऽजनयत्सुतौ।।1.18.13।। वीरौ सर्वास्त्रकुशलौ विष्णोरर्धसमन्वितौ।
transliteration: atha lakṣmaṇaśatrughnau sumitrā'janayatsutau vīrau sarvāstrakuśalau viṣṇorardhasamanvitau|
translation: अथ then, सुमित्रा Sumitra, वीरौ heroic, सर्वास्त्रकुशलौ skilled in the use of all weapons, विष्णो: Visnu's, अर्धसमन्वितौ having facets of Visnu, लक्ष्मणशत्रुघ्नौ Lakshmana and Satrughna, सुतौ sons, अजनयत् gave birth.
explanation: Sumitra gave birth to Lakshmana and Satrughna who were heroic, skilled in the use of all weapons and endowed with the facets of Visnu.

shloka_text: पुष्ये जातस्तु भरतो मीनलग्ने प्रसन्नधी:।।1.18.14।। सार्पे जातौ च सौमित्री कुलीरेऽभ्युदिते रवौ।
transliteration: puṣye jātastu bharato mīnalagne prasannadhī: sārpe jātau ca saumitrī kulīre'bhyudite ravau|
translation: प्रसन्नधी: of pure intellect, भरत: Bharata, पुष्ये when the Pushya star was in ascendant, मीनलग्ने in Meena lagna, जात: was born, सौमित्री sons of Sumitra, सार्पे in Aslesha star, कुलीरे in the Karkata lagna, रवौ when Sun, अभ्युदिते is rising, जातौ were born.
explanation: Bharata endowed with pure intellect was born in meena lagna when pushya was in the ascendant. Lakshmana and Satrughna were born in karkata lagna with the star aslesha .

shloka_text: राज्ञ: पुत्रा महात्मानश्चत्वारो जज्ञिरे पृथक्।।1.18.15।। गुणवन्तोऽनुरूपाश्च रुच्या प्रोष्ठपदोपमा:।
transliteration: rājña: putrā mahātmānaścatvāro jajñire pṛthak guṇavanto'nurūpāśca rucyā proṣṭhapadopamā:|
translation: गुणवन्त: endowed with every good quality, अनुरूपा: worthy, रुच्या in brightness,   प्रोष्ठपदोपमा: resembling Purva Bhaadra, Uttara Bhaadra stars, महात्मान: highly noble, राज्ञ: King's, चत्वार: four, पुत्रा: sons, पृथक् successively, जज्ञिरे were born In this manner.
explanation: Four worthy sons were successively born to the noble king (Dasaratha), endowed with all virtuous, resembling purvabhadra and uttarabhadra  stars in brightness.

shloka_text: जगु: कलं च गन्धर्वा ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणा:।।1.18.16।। देवदुन्दुभयो नेदु: पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता। उत्सवश्च महानासीदयोध्यायां जनाकुल:।।1.18.17।।
transliteration: jagu: kalaṃ ca gandharvā nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇā: devadundubhayo nedu: puṣpavṛṣṭiśca khāccyutā| utsavaśca mahānāsīdayodhyāyāṃ janākula:
translation: गन्धर्वा: gandharvas, कलम् melodiously, जगुः sang, अप्सरोगणा: groups of apsaras, ननृतु: danced, देवदुन्दुभय: celestial kettle drums, नेदु: sounded, खात् from the sky, पुष्पवृष्टिश्च showers of flowers, च्युता was released, अयोध्यायाम् in the city of Ayodhya, जनाकुल: tumult of men, महान्  great, उत्सवश्च आसीत् festivities took place.
explanation: The gandharvas sang melodiously. Groups of apsaras danced. Celestial kettledrums were sounded. Flowers were showered from the sky. Men througed to Ayodhya to witness the festivities.

shloka_text: जगु: कलं च गन्धर्वा ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणा:।।1.18.16।। देवदुन्दुभयो नेदु: पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता। उत्सवश्च महानासीदयोध्यायां जनाकुल:।।1.18.17।।
transliteration: jagu: kalaṃ ca gandharvā nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇā: devadundubhayo nedu: puṣpavṛṣṭiśca khāccyutā| utsavaśca mahānāsīdayodhyāyāṃ janākula:
translation: गन्धर्वा: gandharvas, कलम् melodiously, जगुः sang, अप्सरोगणा: groups of apsaras, ननृतु: danced, देवदुन्दुभय: celestial kettle drums, नेदु: sounded, खात् from the sky, पुष्पवृष्टिश्च showers of flowers, च्युता was released, अयोध्यायाम् in the city of Ayodhya, जनाकुल: tumult of men, महान्  great, उत्सवश्च आसीत् festivities took place.
explanation: The gandharvas sang melodiously. Groups of apsaras danced. Celestial kettledrums were sounded. Flowers were showered from the sky. Men througed to Ayodhya to witness the festivities.

shloka_text: रथ्याश्च जनसम्बाधा नटनर्तकसङ्कुला: । गायनैश्च विराविण्यो वादनैश्च तथाऽपरै:।।1.18.18।।
transliteration: rathyāśca janasambādhā naṭanartakasaṅkulā: | gāyanaiśca virāviṇyo vādanaiśca tathā'parai:
translation: रथ्या: highways, जनसम्बाधा: thickly populated by men, नटनर्तकसङ्कुला: thronged by actors and dancers, गायनैश्च by  singers, वादनै: by performers on different instruments, तथा and,  अपरै: by other euologists and genealogists, विराविण्य: were resounding with noise.
explanation: The highways were crowded with men, thronged by actors and dancers. The voices of singers, performers on different instruments, eulogists and genealogists reverberated.

shloka_text: प्रदेयांश्च ददौ राजा सूतमागधवन्दिनाम्। ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ वित्तं गोधनानि सहस्रश:।।1.18.19।।
transliteration: pradeyāṃśca dadau rājā sūtamāgadhavandinām| brāhmaṇebhyo dadau vittaṃ godhanāni sahasraśa:
translation: राजा king, सूतमागधवन्दिनाम् for bards, euologists and genealogists, प्रदेयान् च gifts fit to be bestowed, ददौ gave, ब्राह्मणेभ्य: for brahmins, वित्तम् wealth, सहस्रश: in thousands, गोधनानि kine, ददौ gave.
explanation: The king distributed deserving gifts to priests, euologists and genealogists. He gave brahmins in charity thousands of cows and other valuables.

shloka_text: अतीत्यैकादशाहं तु नामकर्म तथाऽकरोत्। ज्येष्ठं रामं महात्मानं भरतं कैकयीसुतम्।।1.18.20।। सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणमिति शत्रुघ्नमपरं तथा। वसिष्ठ: परमप्रीतो नामानि कृतवान् तदा ।।1.18.21।।
transliteration: atītyaikādaśāhaṃ tu nāmakarma tathā'karot| jyeṣṭhaṃ rāmaṃ mahātmānaṃ bharataṃ kaikayīsutam saumitriṃ lakṣmaṇamiti śatrughnamaparaṃ tathā| vasiṣṭha: paramaprīto nāmāni kṛtavān tadā
translation: तथा and, एकादशाहम् eleven days, अतीत्य having completed, नामकर्म naming ceremony, अकरोत् he (Vasishta) performed, महात्मानम् illustrious one, ज्येष्ठम् eldest son, रामम् as Rama, कैकयीसुतम् the son of Kaikeyi, भरतम् as Bharata, सौमित्रिम् a son of Sumitra, लक्ष्मणमिति as Lakshmana, अपरम् the other son, शत्रुघ्नम् as Satrughna, परमप्रीत: highly delighted, वसिष्ठ: Vasishta, तदा then, नामानि कृतवान् gave names.
explanation: After a lapse of eleven days, the naming ceremony was performed. Highly delighted preceptor Vasishta named Kausalya's son Rama, Kaikeyi's son Bharata, one son of Sumitra, Lakshmana and the other Satrughna.

shloka_text: अतीत्यैकादशाहं तु नामकर्म तथाऽकरोत्। ज्येष्ठं रामं महात्मानं भरतं कैकयीसुतम्।।1.18.20।। सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणमिति शत्रुघ्नमपरं तथा। वसिष्ठ: परमप्रीतो नामानि कृतवान् तदा ।।1.18.21।।
transliteration: atītyaikādaśāhaṃ tu nāmakarma tathā'karot| jyeṣṭhaṃ rāmaṃ mahātmānaṃ bharataṃ kaikayīsutam saumitriṃ lakṣmaṇamiti śatrughnamaparaṃ tathā| vasiṣṭha: paramaprīto nāmāni kṛtavān tadā
translation: तथा and, एकादशाहम् eleven days, अतीत्य having completed, नामकर्म naming ceremony, अकरोत् he (Vasishta) performed, महात्मानम् illustrious one, ज्येष्ठम् eldest son, रामम् as Rama, कैकयीसुतम् the son of Kaikeyi, भरतम् as Bharata, सौमित्रिम् a son of Sumitra, लक्ष्मणमिति as Lakshmana, अपरम् the other son, शत्रुघ्नम् as Satrughna, परमप्रीत: highly delighted, वसिष्ठ: Vasishta, तदा then, नामानि कृतवान् gave names.
explanation: After a lapse of eleven days, the naming ceremony was performed. Highly delighted preceptor Vasishta named Kausalya's son Rama, Kaikeyi's son Bharata, one son of Sumitra, Lakshmana and the other Satrughna.

shloka_text: ब्राह्मणान्भोजयामास पौराञ्जानपदानपि। अददाद्ब्रह्मणानां च रत्नौघममितं बहु।।1.18.22।। तेषां जन्मक्रियादीनि सर्वकर्माण्यकारयत्।
transliteration: brāhmaṇānbhojayāmāsa paurāñjānapadānapi| adadādbrahmaṇānāṃ ca ratnaughamamitaṃ bahu teṣāṃ janmakriyādīni sarvakarmāṇyakārayat|
translation: ब्राह्मणान् brahmins, पौरान् inhabitants of the city, जानपदानपि also rural folk, भोजयामास were offered, ब्राह्मणानाम् for Brahmins, अमितम् unlimited, बहु abundant, रत्नौघम् heaps of jewels, अददात् bestowed, तेषाम् for them, जन्मक्रियादीनि rites to be performed at the time of birth, सर्वकर्माणि and all other rites, अकारयत् were made to be performed.
explanation: Brahmins as well as inhabitants of the city and rural areas were feasted. (Dasaratha) bestowed on brahmins unlimited and abundant jewels in charity. The rites at the time of birth and all other rites (associated with the newborn) were duly performed.

shloka_text: तेषां केतुरिव ज्येष्ठो रामो रतिकर: पितु:।।1.18.23।। बभूव भूयो भूतानां स्वयम्भूरिव सम्मत:।
transliteration: teṣāṃ keturiva jyeṣṭho rāmo ratikara: pitu: babhūva bhūyo bhūtānāṃ svayambhūriva sammata:|
translation: तेषाम् amongst all of them, ज्येष्ठ: eldest, राम: Rama, केतुरिव like flag, पितु: for his father भूय: exceedingly, रतिकर: causing pleasure, स्वयम्भूरिव like Brahma, भूतानाम्  for all living beings, सम्मत:बभूव became highly respectable .
explanation: Among them, Rama like the exalted flag, became dear to his father like Brahma he was highly respected by all living beings.

shloka_text: सर्वे वेदविदश्शूरास्सर्वे लोकहिते रता:।।1.18.24।। सर्वे ज्ञानोपसम्पन्नास्सर्वे समुदिता गुणै:।
transliteration: sarve vedavidaśśūrāssarve lokahite ratā: sarve jñānopasampannāssarve samuditā guṇai:|
translation: सर्वे all of them, वेदविद: wellversed in vedas, शूरा: were heroic, सर्वे all, लोकहिते in the welfare of people, रता: devoted, सर्वे all, ज्ञानोपसम्पन्ना: endowed with knowledge, सर्वे all, गुणै: with virtues, समुदिता: were furnished with.
explanation: All the sons (of Dasaratha) became wellversed in the Vedas. They were heroic, endowed with knowledge  and virtues and were devoted to the welfare of the people.

shloka_text: तेषामपि महातेजा रामस्सत्यपराक्रम:।।1.18.25।। इष्टस्सर्वस्य लोकस्य शशाङ्क इव निर्मल:।
transliteration: teṣāmapi mahātejā rāmassatyaparākrama: iṣṭassarvasya lokasya śaśāṅka iva nirmala:|
translation: तेषामपि among all of them also, महातेजा: highly lustrous,  सत्यपराक्रम: truly mighty, राम: Rama, निर्मल: free from moral taints, शशाङ्क:इव like moon, सर्वस्य लोकस्य इष्ट: was dear to the entire world.
explanation: Among them  the highly lustrous and truly mighty Rama was stainless (in character). He was auspicious to the entire world like the Moon.

shloka_text: गजस्कन्धेऽश्वपृष्ठे च रथचर्यासु सम्मत:।।1.18.26।। धनुर्वेदे च निरत: पितृशुश्रूषणे रत:।
transliteration: gajaskandhe'śvapṛṣṭhe ca rathacaryāsu sammata: dhanurvede ca nirata: pitṛśuśrūṣaṇe rata:|
translation: गजस्कन्धे on mounting elephants, अश्वपृष्ठे च while  riding on the back of horse, रथचर्यासु going about in chariots, सम्मत: has been accepted as skilled, धनुर्वेदे च in archery also, निरत: always engaged, पितृश्शुश्रूषणे in service of his parents, रत: was devoted.
explanation: Accepted as skilled in mounting elephants, riding horses, driving chariots and also in archery, he was always emgaged in the service of his parents.

shloka_text: बाल्यात्प्रभृति सुस्निग्धो लक्ष्मणो लक्ष्मिवर्धन:।।1.18.27।। रामस्य लोकरामस्य भ्रातुर्ज्येष्ठस्य नित्यश:।
transliteration: bālyātprabhṛti susnigdho lakṣmaṇo lakṣmivardhana: rāmasya lokarāmasya bhrāturjyeṣṭhasya nityaśa:|
translation: लक्ष्मिवर्धन: causing prosperity to grow, लक्ष्मण: Lakshmana, बाल्यात् प्रभृति from his childhood, लोकरामस्य for a man of delight of the world, ज्येष्ठस्य of the eldest, भ्रातु: of the brother, रामस्य in the matter of Rama, नित्यश: always, सुस्निग्ध: remained very friendly .
explanation: Right from his very childhood Lakshmana, an enhancer of fortune, always remained very  attached to his eldest brother Rama, the delight of the world.

shloka_text: सर्वप्रियकरस्तस्य रामस्यापि शरीरत:।।1.18.28।। लक्ष्मणो लक्ष्मिसम्पन्नो बहि:प्राण इवापर:।
transliteration: sarvapriyakarastasya rāmasyāpi śarīrata: lakṣmaṇo lakṣmisampanno bahi:prāṇa ivāpara:|
translation: लक्ष्मिसम्पन्न: possessed of auspiciousness, लक्ष्मण: Lakshmana, शरीरत: अपि even by offering his body, सर्वप्रियकर: doing every thing dear to him, तस्य रामस्य for that Rama, अपर: another, बहि: प्राण इव like life moving outside (his body).
explanation: Lakshmana,  possessed of fortune, was the dearest to his brother than his own body. As though he was his life without.

shloka_text: न च तेन विना निद्रां लभते पुरुषोत्तम:।।1.18.29।। मृष्टमन्नमुपानीतमश्नाति न हि तं विना।
transliteration: na ca tena vinā nidrāṃ labhate puruṣottama: mṛṣṭamannamupānītamaśnāti na hi taṃ vinā|
translation: पुरुषोत्तमः greatest among men( Rama), तेन विना without Lakshmana, निद्राम् sleep, न लभते did not obtain, उपानीतम् having been presented, मृष्टम्  best cooked, अन्नं च food, तं विना without him, न हि अश्नाति would not partake the same.
explanation: Rama, the greatest among men would not sleep without Lakshmana's company. He would not partake even the choicest food minus to him.

shloka_text: यदा हि हयमारूढो मृगयां याति राघव:।।1.18.30।। तदैनं पृष्ठतोऽन्वेति सधनु: परिपालयन्।
transliteration: yadā hi hayamārūḍho mṛgayāṃ yāti rāghava: tadainaṃ pṛṣṭhato'nveti sadhanu: paripālayan|
