translation: राघव: Raghava, हयम् horse back, आरूढ: mounting on, यदा whenever, मृगयाम् for hunting, याति goes, तदा then, स: Lakshmana, धनु: परिपालयन् holding bow in his hand, एनम् him    (Rama), पृष्ठत: behind, अन्वेति followed.
explanation: Whenever Raghava (Rama) went hunting into the forest, riding the horse, Lakshmana used to follow him holding bow and arrows (in his hand).

shloka_text: भरतस्यापि शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मणावरजो हि स:।।1.18.31।। प्राणै: प्रियतरो नित्यं तस्य चासीत्तथा प्रिय:।
transliteration: bharatasyāpi śatrughno lakṣmaṇāvarajo hi sa: prāṇai: priyataro nityaṃ tasya cāsīttathā priya:|
translation: लक्ष्मणावरज: younger brother of Lakshmana, स: शत्रुघ्न: that Satrughna, भरतस्यापि for Bharata also, नित्यम् always, प्राणै: (more than his) life, प्रियतर: was  dearer, तस्य च आसीत्  for Satrughna also, तथा in that manner, प्रिय: became dear( to Bharata).
explanation: In a similar manner Satrughna, younger brother of Lakshmana, became dearer than his own life to Bharata. Similarly, Bharata also was dear to Satrughna.

shloka_text: स चतुर्भिर्महाभागै:पुत्रैर्दशरथ: प्रियै:।।1.18.32।। बभूव परमप्रीतो देवैरिव पितामह:।
transliteration: sa caturbhirmahābhāgai:putrairdaśaratha: priyai: babhūva paramaprīto devairiva pitāmaha:|
translation: स: दशरथ: Dasaratha, महाभागै: by the very fortunate ones, चतुर्भि: four, पुत्रै: by sons, पितामह: Brahma, देवै: इव like devatas, परमप्रीत: बभूव was highly pleased.
explanation: With his very fortunate sons, Dasaratha was highly pleased like Brahma was with the gods.

shloka_text: ते यदा ज्ञानसम्पन्नास्सर्वैस्समुदिता गुणै:।।1.18.33।। ह्रीमन्त: कीर्तिमन्तश्च सर्वज्ञा दीर्घदर्शिन:। तेषामेवं प्रभावानां सर्वेषां दीप्ततेजसाम्।।1.18.34।। पिता दशरथो हृष्टो ब्रह्मा लोकाधिपो यथा।
transliteration: te yadā jñānasampannāssarvaissamuditā guṇai: hrīmanta: kīrtimantaśca sarvajñā dīrghadarśina:| teṣāmevaṃ prabhāvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dīptatejasām pitā daśaratho hṛṣṭo brahmā lokādhipo yathā|
translation: ते they, यदा when, ज्ञानसम्पन्ना: were enriched with knowledge, सर्वैः गुणै: by all virtues, समुदिता: united, ह्रीमन्त: modest, कीर्तिमन्तश्च renowned, सर्वज्ञा: knower of all things, दीर्घदर्शिन: farsighted, एवं in this manner, प्रभावानाम्  having such faculties, दीप्ततेजसाम् of the men of shining glory, तेषां सर्वेषाम् in their matter, पिता दशरथ: father Dasaratha, लोकाधिप: lord of the worlds, ब्रह्मा यथा like Brahma, हृष्ट: rejoiced.
explanation: All his sons were enriched  with knowledge and endowed  with all virtues. They were modest, renowned, omniscient and farsighted. Dasaratha rejoiced at the sight of those glorious sons with such faculties and looked like Brahma, Lord of the worlds.

shloka_text: ते यदा ज्ञानसम्पन्नास्सर्वैस्समुदिता गुणै:।।1.18.33।। ह्रीमन्त: कीर्तिमन्तश्च सर्वज्ञा दीर्घदर्शिन:। तेषामेवं प्रभावानां सर्वेषां दीप्ततेजसाम्।।1.18.34।। पिता दशरथो हृष्टो ब्रह्मा लोकाधिपो यथा।
transliteration: te yadā jñānasampannāssarvaissamuditā guṇai: hrīmanta: kīrtimantaśca sarvajñā dīrghadarśina:| teṣāmevaṃ prabhāvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dīptatejasām pitā daśaratho hṛṣṭo brahmā lokādhipo yathā|
translation: ते they, यदा when, ज्ञानसम्पन्ना: were enriched with knowledge, सर्वैः गुणै: by all virtues, समुदिता: united, ह्रीमन्त: modest, कीर्तिमन्तश्च renowned, सर्वज्ञा: knower of all things, दीर्घदर्शिन: farsighted, एवं in this manner, प्रभावानाम्  having such faculties, दीप्ततेजसाम् of the men of shining glory, तेषां सर्वेषाम् in their matter, पिता दशरथ: father Dasaratha, लोकाधिप: lord of the worlds, ब्रह्मा यथा like Brahma, हृष्ट: rejoiced.
explanation: All his sons were enriched  with knowledge and endowed  with all virtues. They were modest, renowned, omniscient and farsighted. Dasaratha rejoiced at the sight of those glorious sons with such faculties and looked like Brahma, Lord of the worlds.

shloka_text: ते चापि मनुजव्याघ्रा वैदिकाध्ययने रता:।।1.18.35।। पितृशुश्रूषणरता धनुर्वेदे च निष्ठिता:।
transliteration: te cāpi manujavyāghrā vaidikādhyayane ratā: pitṛśuśrūṣaṇaratā dhanurvede ca niṣṭhitā:|
translation: ते they, मनुजव्याघ्रा अपि also tigers among men, वैदिकाध्ययने in the study of vedas, रता: were engaged, पितृशुश्रूषणरता: intent on doing service to their parents, धनुर्वेदे in the archery also, निष्ठिता: were proficient.
explanation: They (like) tigers among men, were fond of the study of the Vedas  and were always engaged in the service of their parents. They were also proficient in the science of archery.

shloka_text: अथ राजा दशरथस्तेषां दारक्रियां प्रति।।1.18.36।। चिन्तयामास धर्मात्मा सोपाध्यायस्सबान्धव:।
transliteration: atha rājā daśarathasteṣāṃ dārakriyāṃ prati cintayāmāsa dharmātmā sopādhyāyassabāndhava:|
translation: अथ thereafter, धर्मात्मा the virtuous, राजा दशरथ: king Dasaratha, सोपाध्याय: along with priests, सबान्धव: along with relatives, तेषाम् their, दारक्रियां प्रति marriage, चिन्तयामास was engaged in the thought .
explanation: Then the virtuous king Dasaratha deliberated with his priests and kinsmen about the marriage of his sons.

shloka_text: तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य मन्त्रिमध्ये महात्मन:।।1.18.37।। अभ्यगच्छन्महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनि:।
transliteration: tasya cintayamānasya mantrimadhye mahātmana: abhyagacchanmahātejā viśvāmitro mahāmuni:|
translation: महात्मन: of the noble minded, तस्य king Dasaratha, मन्त्रिमध्ये in the midst of counsellors, चिन्तयमानस्य while he was thinking, महातेजा: highly illustrious king, विश्वामित्र: महामुनि: ascetic Viswamitra, अभ्यगच्छत् arrived.
explanation: While the nobleminded king was thus deliberating in the midst of his counsellors,  there arrived the effulgent ascetic Viswamitra.

shloka_text: स राज्ञो दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी द्वाराध्यक्षानुवाच ह।।1.18.38।। शीघ्रमाख्यात मां प्राप्तं कौशिकं गाधिनस्सुतम्।
transliteration: sa rājño darśanākāṅkṣī dvārādhyakṣānuvāca ha śīghramākhyāta māṃ prāptaṃ kauśikaṃ gādhinassutam|
translation: स: he, राज्ञ: king's, दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी desirous of seeing, द्वाराध्यक्षान् door keepers, उवाच ह addressed saying, "गाधिन: Gadhi's, सुतम् son, कौशिकम् born in the line of Kusika, माम् me, प्राप्तम् having arrived, शीघ्रम् speedily, आख्यात declare".
explanation: Desirous of seeing the king (Dasaratha) he accosted the doorkeepers, saying "Inform the king quickly about the arrival of Viswamitra, the son of Gadhi born in the line of Kusika".

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं त्रासाद्राज्ञो वेश्म प्रदुद्रुवु:।।1.18.39।। सम्भ्रान्तमनसस्सर्वे तेन वाक्येन चोदिता:।
transliteration: tacchrutvā vacanaṃ trāsādrājño veśma pradudruvu: sambhrāntamanasassarve tena vākyena coditā:|
translation: तत् वचनम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, सर्वे all of them, सम्भ्रान्तमनस: with excited minds, तेन वाक्येन by that statement, चोदिता: prompted, राज्ञ: king's, वेश्म apartment, त्रासात् due to fear, प्रदुद्रुवुः hastened.
explanation: On hearing those words (of Viswamitra) all of them prompted by fear because of left for the royal apartment with excited minds and hurried steps.

shloka_text: ते गत्वा राजभवनं विश्वामित्रमृषिं तदा।।1.18.40।। प्राप्तमावेदयामासुर्नृपायैक्ष्वाकवे तदा।
transliteration: te gatvā rājabhavanaṃ viśvāmitramṛṣiṃ tadā prāptamāvedayāmāsurnṛpāyaikṣvākave tadā|
translation: तदा then, ते they, राजभवनम् towards royal palace, गत्वा having gone, तदा then, विश्वामित्रम् ऋषिम् maharshi Viswamitra, प्राप्तम् having come, ऐक्ष्वाकवे to the king belonging to Ikshvaku race, नृपाय to king Dasaratha, आवेदयामासु: communicated.
explanation: Having reached the royal hall, they reported to the king (Dasaratha), descendant of the Ikshvakus about the arrival of sage Viswamitra.

shloka_text: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सपुरोधास्समाहित:।।1.18.41।। प्रत्युज्जगाम तं हृष्टो ब्रह्माणमिव वासव:।
transliteration: teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sapurodhāssamāhita: pratyujjagāma taṃ hṛṣṭo brahmāṇamiva vāsava:|
translation: तेषाम् theirs, तत् वचनम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, हृष्ट: immensely pleased, सपुरोधा: together with his preceptors, समाहित: with absorbed mind, तम् him, वासव: Indra, ब्रह्माणमिव like Brahma, प्रत्युज्जगाम went forth to receive him.
explanation: Having heard their words, Dasaratha in great joy went forth together with his preceptors to receive him like Indra receiving Brahma.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा ज्वलितं दीप्त्या तापसं संशितव्रतम्।।1.18.42।। प्रहृष्टवदनो राजा ततोऽर्घ्यमुपहारयत्।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā jvalitaṃ dīptyā tāpasaṃ saṃśitavratam prahṛṣṭavadano rājā tato'rghyamupahārayat|
translation: तत: then, राजा king, ज्वलितम् shining, दीप्त्या with radiance, तापसं ascetic, संशितव्रतम् who had fulfilled his vows, तम् him, दृष्ट्वा having seen, प्रहृष्टवदन: with cheerful countenance,        अर्घ्यम् respectable offerings, उपहारयत् offered.
explanation: Seeing Viswamitra, shining with the power of his penance fulfilled the king with a cheerful countenance made offerings with due respect.

shloka_text: स राज्ञ: प्रतिगृह्यार्घ्यं शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा।।1.18.43।। कुशलं चाव्ययं चैव पर्यपृच्छन्नराधिपम्।2
transliteration: sa rājña: pratigṛhyārghyaṃ śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā kuśalaṃ cāvyayaṃ caiva paryapṛcchannarādhipam|2
translation: स: he, शास्त्रदृष्टेन as shown in the scriptures, कर्मणा by religious rites, राज्ञ: of the king, अर्घ्यम् offerings, प्रतिगृह्य having received, नराधिपम् king, कुशलं च welfare of the kingdom, अव्ययं prosperity, पर्यपृच्छत् enquired.
explanation: Viswamitra received the offerings as ordained in the scriptures and enquired from the king about the welfare and prosperity of his kingdom.

shloka_text: पुरे कोशे जनपदे बान्धवेषु सुहृत्सु च ।।1.18.44।। कुशलं कौशिको राज्ञ: पर्यपृच्छत्सुधार्मिक:।
transliteration: pure kośe janapade bāndhaveṣu suhṛtsu ca  kuśalaṃ kauśiko rājña: paryapṛcchatsudhārmika:|
translation: सुधार्मिक: exceedingly virtuous, कौशिक: Viswamitra, राज्ञ: King's, पुरे in the cities, कोशे in treasury, जनपदे in the villages, बान्धवेषु among relatives, सुहृत्सु च among friends, कुशलम् welfare, पर्यपृच्छत् enquired.
explanation: The exceedingly virtuous sage Viswamitra enquired from the king about the treasury welfare of his subjects living in cities and villages, and the well being of his friends and relatives.

shloka_text: अपि ते सन्नतास्सर्वे सामन्ता रिपवो जिता:।।1.18.45।। दैवं च मानुषं चापि कर्म ते साध्वनुष्ठितम्।
transliteration: api te sannatāssarve sāmantā ripavo jitā: daivaṃ ca mānuṣaṃ cāpi karma te sādhvanuṣṭhitam|
translation: सामन्ता: tributary kings, सर्वे all, ते to you, अपि सन्नता: are they submissive, रिपव: enemies, जिता: are conquered, ते to you, दैवतं कर्म rites for propitiating gods, मानुषं चापि service to humanity, साधु rightly, अनुष्ठितम् performed.
explanation: Are the tributary kings submissive to you? Have you conquered your enemies? Are the rites for propitiating gods and the services to humanity  performed rightly?

shloka_text: वसिष्ठं च समागम्य कुशलं मुनिपुङ्गव:।।1.18.46।। ऋषींश्च तान्यथान्यायं महाभागानुवाच ह।
transliteration: vasiṣṭhaṃ ca samāgamya kuśalaṃ munipuṅgava: ṛṣīṃśca tānyathānyāyaṃ mahābhāgānuvāca ha|
translation: मुनिपुङ्गव: the foremost of ascetis,Viswamitra, वसिष्ठं च  Vasistha also, तान् महाभागान् all those distinguished men, ऋषींश्च sages also, यथान्यायम् according to customary protocol, समागम्य having approached, कुशलम् welfare, उवाच spoke (enquired).
explanation: The foremost of ascetis, Viswamitra approached Vasishta and all other distinguised sages following the protocal and enquired about their welfare.

shloka_text: ते सर्वे हृष्टमनसस्तस्य राज्ञो निवेशनम्।।1.18.47।। विविशु: पूजितास्तत्र निषेदुश्च यथार्हत:।
transliteration: te sarve hṛṣṭamanasastasya rājño niveśanam viviśu: pūjitāstatra niṣeduśca yathārhata:|
translation: सर्वे all of them, हृष्टमनस: with gladdened hearts, तस्य राज्ञ: that king's, निवेशनम् royal palace, विविशु: entered, तत्र there, यथार्हत: according to their statusmerit, पूजिता: having been honoured, निषेदुश्च sat down.
explanation: All of them with gladdened hearts entered the royal palace and sat down, in accordance with their position after having been duly honoured by the king.

shloka_text: अथ हृष्टमना राजा विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम्।।1.18.48।। उवाच परमोदारो हृष्टस्तमभिपूजयन्।
transliteration: atha hṛṣṭamanā rājā viśvāmitraṃ mahāmunim uvāca paramodāro hṛṣṭastamabhipūjayan|
translation: अथ thereafter, परमोदार: highly generous, राजा king Dasaratha, हृष्टमना: wellpleased, तम् महामुनिम् that great sage, विश्वामित्रम् Visvamitra, अभिपूजयन् while  worshipping, हृष्ट: with joy, उवाच spoke৷৷
explanation: Then the munificent king, very much (at Viswamitra's arrival) pleased offered him a happy hospitality and spoke:

shloka_text: यथाऽमृतस्य सम्प्राप्तिर्यथावर्षमनूदके। यथा सदृशदारेषु पुत्रजन्माऽप्रजस्य च ।।1.18.49।। प्रणष्टस्य यथालाभो यथा हर्षो महोदये। तथैवागमनं मन्ये स्वागतं ते महामुने।।1.18.50।।
transliteration: yathā'mṛtasya samprāptiryathāvarṣamanūdake| yathā sadṛśadāreṣu putrajanmā'prajasya ca  praṇaṣṭasya yathālābho yathā harṣo mahodaye| tathaivāgamanaṃ manye svāgataṃ te mahāmune
translation: महामुने O Great sage, अमृतस्य nectar's, सम्प्राप्ति: obtaining, यथा like, अनूदके in a parched land वर्षम् rain, यथा like, अप्रजस्य for a man without progeny, सदृशदारेषु through his worthy wife, पुत्रजन्म birth of sons, यथा like, प्रणष्टस्य for one who lost wealth, लाभः recoveryof, यथा like, महोदये in a great achievement, हर्ष: joy, यथा like, ते आगमनम् your arrival, तथा एव similar to that, मन्ये I am considering, स्वागतम् welcome to you,
explanation: "O great sage, welcome to you Your arrival, to me, is like nectar (to a human being), rains to the parched land, birth of a son to the childless through his worthy wife, recovery of lost properity and festive joy in a great achievemnt.

shloka_text: यथाऽमृतस्य सम्प्राप्तिर्यथावर्षमनूदके। यथा सदृशदारेषु पुत्रजन्माऽप्रजस्य च ।।1.18.49।। प्रणष्टस्य यथालाभो यथा हर्षो महोदये। तथैवागमनं मन्ये स्वागतं ते महामुने।।1.18.50।।
transliteration: yathā'mṛtasya samprāptiryathāvarṣamanūdake| yathā sadṛśadāreṣu putrajanmā'prajasya ca  praṇaṣṭasya yathālābho yathā harṣo mahodaye| tathaivāgamanaṃ manye svāgataṃ te mahāmune
translation: महामुने O Great sage, अमृतस्य nectar's, सम्प्राप्ति: obtaining, यथा like, अनूदके in a parched land वर्षम् rain, यथा like, अप्रजस्य for a man without progeny, सदृशदारेषु through his worthy wife, पुत्रजन्म birth of sons, यथा like, प्रणष्टस्य for one who lost wealth, लाभः recoveryof, यथा like, महोदये in a great achievement, हर्ष: joy, यथा like, ते आगमनम् your arrival, तथा एव similar to that, मन्ये I am considering, स्वागतम् welcome to you,
explanation: "O great sage, welcome to you Your arrival, to me, is like nectar (to a human being), rains to the parched land, birth of a son to the childless through his worthy wife, recovery of lost properity and festive joy in a great achievemnt.

shloka_text: कं च ते परमं कामं करोमि किमु हर्षित: ।।1.18.51।। पात्रभूतोऽसि मे ब्रह्मन्दिष्टया प्राप्ताऽसि कौशिक । अद्य मे सफलं जन्म जीवितं च सुजीवितम्।।1.18.52।।
transliteration: kaṃ ca te paramaṃ kāmaṃ karomi kimu harṣita:  pātrabhūto'si me brahmandiṣṭayā prāptā'si kauśika | adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ ca sujīvitam
translation: ब्रह्मन् O Brahman, हर्षित: satisfied, ते to you, परमम् great, कं कामम् which wish, किमु in what manner, करोमि shall I do, मे for me, पात्रभूत: असि (you) are role model for righteousness,कौशिक O Viswamitra!, दिष्टचा luckily, प्राप्त: असि (you) have come, अद्य now, मे my, जन्म birth, सफलम् fruitful, जीवितं च life also, सुजीवितम् has accomplished its objective.
explanation: "O Brahman! what is your desire and in what manner shall I fulfill it to your satisfaction? You are a role model for righteousness. How fortunate I am you have come! My birth is rendered fruitful. My life has accomplished its objective.

shloka_text: कं च ते परमं कामं करोमि किमु हर्षित: ।।1.18.51।। पात्रभूतोऽसि मे ब्रह्मन्दिष्टया प्राप्ताऽसि कौशिक । अद्य मे सफलं जन्म जीवितं च सुजीवितम्।।1.18.52।।
transliteration: kaṃ ca te paramaṃ kāmaṃ karomi kimu harṣita:  pātrabhūto'si me brahmandiṣṭayā prāptā'si kauśika | adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ ca sujīvitam
translation: ब्रह्मन् O Brahman, हर्षित: satisfied, ते to you, परमम् great, कं कामम् which wish, किमु in what manner, करोमि shall I do, मे for me, पात्रभूत: असि (you) are role model for righteousness,कौशिक O Viswamitra!, दिष्टचा luckily, प्राप्त: असि (you) have come, अद्य now, मे my, जन्म birth, सफलम् fruitful, जीवितं च life also, सुजीवितम् has accomplished its objective.
explanation: "O Brahman! what is your desire and in what manner shall I fulfill it to your satisfaction? You are a role model for righteousness. How fortunate I am you have come! My birth is rendered fruitful. My life has accomplished its objective.

shloka_text: पूर्वं राजर्षिशब्देन तपसा द्योतितप्रभः। ब्रह्मर्षित्वमनुप्राप्त: पूज्योऽसि बहुधा मया।।1.18.53।।
transliteration: pūrvaṃ rājarṣiśabdena tapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ| brahmarṣitvamanuprāpta: pūjyo'si bahudhā mayā
translation: पूर्वम् formerly, राजर्षिशब्देन by the word of 'Rajarshi', द्योतितप्रभ: indicating your shining (power), अनु thereafter, तपसा by austerities, ब्रह्मर्षित्वम् status of Brahmarshi, प्राप्त: (you have) obtained, मया by me, बहुधा in several ways, पूज्य:असि you are worthy of worship.
explanation: Earlier you were rajarshi, a warrior sage. By your austerities you have obtained the brilliance that lends radiance even to the Sun and the Moon you have gained the status of a brahmrshi. In several ways you are worthy of my worship.

shloka_text: तदद्भुतमिदं ब्रह्मन्पवित्रं परमं मम। शुभक्षेत्रगतश्चाहं तव सन्दर्शनात्प्रभो।।1.18.54।।
transliteration: tadadbhutamidaṃ brahmanpavitraṃ paramaṃ mama| śubhakṣetragataścāhaṃ tava sandarśanātprabho
translation: ब्रह्मन् O Brahman, तत् therefore  इदम् this l, अद्भुतम् wonderful, मम to me, परमम् great, पवित्रम् pure, प्रभो O Lord, तव your, सन्दर्शनात् by the presence, अहम् I, शुभक्षेत्रगतश्च have acquired merits of pilgrimage .
explanation: O Brahman your arrival has caused surprise to me. It has conferred great purity on me. O Lord by your very presence here, I feel I haved acquired the merits of a          pilgrimage.

shloka_text: ब्रूहि यत्प्रार्थितं तुभ्यं कार्यमागमनं प्रति। इच्छाम्यनुगृहीतोऽहं त्वदर्थपरिवृद्धये।।1.18.55।।
transliteration: brūhi yatprārthitaṃ tubhyaṃ kāryamāgamanaṃ prati| icchāmyanugṛhīto'haṃ tvadarthaparivṛddhaye
translation: आगमनं प्रति in coming here, तुभ्यम् to you, प्रार्थितम् desired, यत् कार्यम् the purpose, ब्रूहि tell me, अहम् I, अनुगृहीत: am favoured, त्वदर्थपरिवृद्धये to achieve your object, इच्छामि I am desirous.
explanation: Be pleased to tell me the purpose of your visit. I desire to be given the privilege of doing service to achieve your object.

shloka_text: कार्यस्य न विमर्शं च गन्तुमर्हसि कौशिक। कर्ता चाहमशेषेण दैवतं हि भवान्मम।।1.18.56।।
transliteration: kāryasya na vimarśaṃ ca gantumarhasi kauśika| kartā cāhamaśeṣeṇa daivataṃ hi bhavānmama
translation: कौशिक O Visvamitra, कार्यस्य of the work, विमर्शम् hesitation, गन्तुम् न अर्हसि you ought not get, अहम् I, विशेषेण specially, कर्ता च I shall accomplish that act, भवान् you, मम for me, दैवतं हि are a god.
explanation: O Viswamitra you need not hesitatate to tell me what ought to be performed. I shall accomplish that act in every possible special way. You are a god to me.

shloka_text: मम चायमनुप्राप्तो महानभ्युदयो द्विज। तवागमनज: कृत्स्नो धर्मश्चानुत्तमो मम।।1.18.57।।
transliteration: mama cāyamanuprāpto mahānabhyudayo dvija| tavāgamanaja: kṛtsno dharmaścānuttamo mama
translation: द्विज O Brahmin, मम for me, अयम् this, महान् great, अभ्युदय: prosperity, अनुप्राप्त: has come, मम for me, तव आगमनज: in consequence of your coming here, कृत्स्न: entire, धर्म: excellent merit, अनुत्तम: great.
explanation: O Brahmin I have attained this high foutune today. My great merit has been realised as a result of your arrival".

shloka_text: इति हृदयसुखं निशम्य वाक्यं श्रुतिसुखमात्मवता विनीतमुक्तम्। प्रथितगुणयशा गुणैर्विशिष्ट: परमऋषि: परमं जगाम हर्षम्।।1.18.58।।
transliteration: iti hṛdayasukhaṃ niśamya vākyaṃ śrutisukhamātmavatā vinītamuktam| prathitaguṇayaśā guṇairviśiṣṭa: paramaṛṣi: paramaṃ jagāma harṣam
translation: आत्मवता by the  wise and prudent, Dasaratha, इति in this manner, विनीतम् in a  humble way, उक्तम् spoken, हृदयसुखम् comfortable to the mind, श्रुतिसुखम् pleasant to the ears, वाक्यम् words, निशम्य having heard, प्रथितगुणयशा: with celebrated qualities and fame, गुणै: by  virtues, र्विशिष्ट: distinguished, परमऋषि: excellent rishi, परमम् great, हर्षम् जगाम experinced delight.
explanation: On hearing the words spoken in such an humble manner by the prudent king words pleasing  to the mind and to the ears, the great rishi of  celebrated virtues and fame, of sterling qualities experienced deep delight. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे अष्टादशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the eighteenth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा राजसिंहस्य वाक्यमद्भुतविस्तरम्। हृष्टरोमा महातेजा विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत।।1.19.1।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā rājasiṃhasya vākyamadbhutavistaram| hṛṣṭaromā mahātejā viśvāmitro'bhyabhāṣata
translation: राजसिंहस्य of the lion among kings, Dasaratha, तत् अद्भुतविस्तरम् that astonishing detail, वाक्यम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, महातेजा: highly vigorous, विश्वामित्र: Viswamitra, हृष्टरोमा: having hair on the body bristling with joy, अभ्यभाषत said.
explanation: Having heard these wonderful words of Dasaratha, the lion among kings, the brilliant Viswamitra with hair on end replied:
comments: Viswamitra requests king Dasaratha to send Rama to protect the sacrifice contemplated by him -- grief of Dasaratha.

shloka_text: सदृशं राजशार्दूल तवैतद्भुवि नान्यथा। महावंशप्रसूतस्य वसिष्ठव्यपदेशिन:।।1.19.2।।
transliteration: sadṛśaṃ rājaśārdūla tavaitadbhuvi nānyathā| mahāvaṃśaprasūtasya vasiṣṭhavyapadeśina:
translation: राजशार्दूल O Tiger among kings, भुवि in this earth, महाकुलप्रसूतस्य having born in an illustrious line, वसिष्ठव्यपदेशिन: having been initiated by Vasishta, तव for you, एतत् this, सदृशम् befitting, न अन्यथा not in any other way.
explanation: "O Tiger among kings having been born on earth in an illustrious lineage and initiated by Vasishta, this way (of speaking) befits you. It cannot be any other way.

shloka_text: यत्तु मे हृद्गतं वाक्यं तस्य कार्यस्य निश्चयम्। कुरूष्व राजशार्दूल भव सत्यप्रतिश्रव:।।1.19.3।।
transliteration: yattu me hṛdgataṃ vākyaṃ tasya kāryasya niścayam| kurūṣva rājaśārdūla bhava satyapratiśrava:
translation: राजशार्दूल O Great king, मे my, हृद्गतम् conceived in my mind, यत् whichever, वाक्यम् word, तस्य कार्यस्य for such purpose, निश्चयम् decision, कुरुष्व take, सत्यप्रतिश्रव: भव become truthful to your promise.
explanation: O Tiger among kings I shall unfold the purpose conceived in my mind. Take a decision and be truthful to your promise.

shloka_text: अहंनियममातिष्ठे सिध्यर्थं पुरुषर्षभ। तस्य विघ्नकरौ द्वौ तु राक्षसौ कामरूपिणौ।।1.19.4।।
transliteration: ahaṃniyamamātiṣṭhe sidhyarthaṃ puruṣarṣabha| tasya vighnakarau dvau tu rākṣasau kāmarūpiṇau
translation: पुरुषर्षभ O Best among men, अहम् I, सिध्यर्थम् for succesful accomplishment(of a sacrifice), नियमम् religious discipline, आतिष्ठे I shall abide, तु but, कामरूपिणौ those assuming forms at free will, द्वौ two, राक्षसौ rakshasas, तस्य for that sacrifice, विघ्नकरौ are creating impediments.
explanation: O best among men for the successful completion of a sacrifice I took up a selfimposed  religious observance. Two rakshasas, capable of assuming forms at will, are creating impediments to that sacrifice.

shloka_text: व्रते मे बहुशश्चीर्णे समाप्त्यां राक्षसाविमौ। मारीचश्च सुबाहुश्च वीर्यवन्तौ सुशिक्षितौ।।1.19.5।। समांसरुधिरौघेण वेदिं तामभ्यवर्षताम्।
transliteration: vrate me bahuśaścīrṇe samāptyāṃ rākṣasāvimau| mārīcaśca subāhuśca vīryavantau suśikṣitau samāṃsarudhiraugheṇa vediṃ tāmabhyavarṣatām|
translation: बहुश: In many ways, चीर्णे performed, मे my, व्रते sacrifice, समाप्त्याम् nearing completion, वीर्यवन्तौ powerful, सुशिक्षितौ two welltrained beings, मारीचश्च Maricha, सुबाहुश्च and also Subahu, समांसरुधिरौघेण by the stream of blood along with flesh, तां वेदिम् that altar, अभ्यवर्षताम् rained.
explanation: When my sacrifice generally speaking, is nearing completion the powerful and welltrained Maricha and Subahu who are raining streams of blood and flesh upon the altar.

shloka_text: अवधूते तथाभूते तस्मिन्नियमनिश्चये।।1.19.6।। कृतश्रमो निरुत्साहस्तस्माद्देशादपाक्रमे।
transliteration: avadhūte tathābhūte tasminniyamaniścaye kṛtaśramo nirutsāhastasmāddeśādapākrame|
translation: तस्मिन् नियमनिश्चये when the solemn vow for observance of that religious rite, अवधूते was pushed aside, तथा भूते when it happened so, कृतश्रम: an exerted man, निरुत्साहः discouraged, तस्मात् देशात् from that country, अपाक्रमे I left.
explanation: The (solemn) vow for observance of religious rites being thus interrupted, I left that country as an exerted and discouraged man.

shloka_text: न च मे क्रोधमुत्स्रष्टुं बुद्धिर्भवति पार्थिव।।1.19.7।। तथा भूता हि सा चर्या न शापस्तत्र मुच्यते।
transliteration: na ca me krodhamutsraṣṭuṃ buddhirbhavati pārthiva tathā bhūtā hi sā caryā na śāpastatra mucyate|
translation: पार्थिव O King, क्रोधम् wrath, उत्स्रष्टुम् to vent out, मे बुद्धि: न भवति my mind does not permit, सा चर्या that sacrificial perfomnce of sacrifice, तथा भूता हि  is such that, तत्र at that time, शाप: curse, न मुच्यते will not be released.
explanation: O King my mind does not permit me to vent my wrath. The nature of sacrifice is such that I refrain from cursing them.

shloka_text: स्वपुत्रं राजशार्दूल रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्।।1.19.8।। काकपक्षधरं शूरं ज्येष्ठं मे दातुमर्हसि।
transliteration: svaputraṃ rājaśārdūla rāmaṃ satyaparākramam kākapakṣadharaṃ śūraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ me dātumarhasi|
translation: राजशार्दूल O Great king, सत्यपराक्रमम् truthful to his prowess, काकपक्षधरम् sidelocks of  hair, शूरम् valiant, स्वपुत्रम् your son, ज्येष्ठम् eldest one, रामम् Rama, मे to me, दातुम् to entrust, अर्हसि it is befitting of you.
explanation: O tiger among kings it is befitting of you to entrust your eldest son Rama to me who is valiant, young (having sidelocks of hair) and true to his prowess.

shloka_text: शक्तो ह्येष मया गुप्तो दिव्येन स्वेन तेजसा।।1.19.9।। राक्षसा ये विकर्तारस्तेषामपि विनाशने।
transliteration: śakto hyeṣa mayā gupto divyena svena tejasā rākṣasā ye vikartārasteṣāmapi vināśane|
translation: मया by me, गुप्त: protected, एष: he, दिव्येन by the divine, स्वेन his own, तेजसा by power, ये विकर्तार: those causing impediments, राक्षसा: rakshasas, तेषामपि even to them, विनाशने in destroying, शक्त: हि is capable.
explanation: Protected by me and by his own divine power, Rama is capable of destroying even those demons causing impediments to the sacrifice.

shloka_text: श्रेयश्चास्मै प्रदास्यामि बहुरूपं न संशय:।।1.19.10।। त्रयाणामपि लोकानां येन ख्यातिं गमिष्यति।
transliteration: śreyaścāsmai pradāsyāmi bahurūpaṃ na saṃśaya: trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ yena khyātiṃ gamiṣyati|
translation: अस्मै for him, बहुरूपम्  several forms of, श्रेयश्च blessings for his wellbeing, प्रदास्यामि I will confer, संशय:न no doubt, येन by which, त्रयाणाम् of the  three, लोकानामपि worlds also, ख्यातिम् fame, गमिष्यति he will attain.
explanation: I will confer upon him, without doubt, a lot of blessings for his wellbeing by which he will attain fame in all the three worlds.

shloka_text: न च तौ राममासाद्य शक्तौ स्थातुं कथञ्चन।।1.19.11।। न च तौ राघवादन्यो हन्तुमुत्सहते पुमान्।
transliteration: na ca tau rāmamāsādya śaktau sthātuṃ kathañcana na ca tau rāghavādanyo hantumutsahate pumān|
translation: तौ Maricha and Subahu, रामम् Rama, आसाद्य having reached, कथञ्चन in any way,  स्थातुम् stand, न शक्तौ not be able, राघवात्  except Rama, अन्य: any other, पुमान् man, तौ both of them, हन्तुम् to slay, न उत्सहते will not be  capable.
explanation: Both of them (Maricha and Subahu) will not be able to withstand Rama in any way. Rama, and Rama alone, is capable of destroying them.

shloka_text: वीर्योत्सिक्तौ हि तौ पापौ कालपाशवशं गतौ।।1.19.12।। रामस्य राजशार्दूल न पर्याप्तौ महात्मन:।
transliteration: vīryotsiktau hi tau pāpau kālapāśavaśaṃ gatau rāmasya rājaśārdūla na paryāptau mahātmana:|
translation: वीर्योत्सिक्तौ proud of their strength, तौ पापौ those two wicked demons, कालपाशवशम् noosed by  of Yama, the god of death, गतौ (have) become, राजशार्दूल O Great king, महात्मन: of the magnanimous, रामस्य for Rama, न पर्याप्तौ no match.
explanation: Proud of their strength, the two wicked demons have been noosed by Yama, the god of death. O tiger among kings they are no match for the magnanimous Rama.

shloka_text: न च पुत्रकृतस्नेहं कर्तुमर्हसि पार्थिव।।1.19.13।। अहं ते प्रतिजानामि हतौ तौ विद्धि राक्षसौ।
transliteration: na ca putrakṛtasnehaṃ kartumarhasi pārthiva ahaṃ te pratijānāmi hatau tau viddhi rākṣasau|
translation: पार्थिव O King, पुत्रकृतम् developed towards your son, स्नेहम् paternal affection, कर्तुम् to do,  न अर्हसि it is not proper for you, तौ राक्षसौ both those rakshasas, हतौ (will) perish, विद्धि know it well, अहम् I, ते to you, प्रतिजानामि I assure you.
explanation: "O king it is not proper for you to hesitate because of your paternal affection. You need to know that both the rakshasas will perish. This, I assure you.

shloka_text: अहं वेद्मि महात्मानं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्।।1.19.14।। वसिष्ठोऽपि महातेजा ये चेमे तपसि स्थिता:।
transliteration: ahaṃ vedmi mahātmānaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākramam vasiṣṭho'pi mahātejā ye ceme tapasi sthitā:|
translation: महात्मानम् nobleminded, सत्यपराक्रमम् truthful to his prowess, रामम् Rama, अहम् I, वेद्मि I know, महातेजा: highly lustrous, वसिष्ठोऽपि Vasishta also, ये तपसि स्थिता: those who are steadfast in asceticism, इमे sages.
explanation: I know Rama who is a great soul, true to his prowess and also Vasishta of great lustre and these other sages who have been steadfast in asceticism also know.

shloka_text: यदि ते धर्मलाभं च यशश्च परमं भुवि।।1.19.15।। स्थितमिच्छसि राजेन्द्र रामं मे दातुमर्हसि।
transliteration: yadi te dharmalābhaṃ ca yaśaśca paramaṃ bhuvi sthitamicchasi rājendra rāmaṃ me dātumarhasi|
translation: राजेन्द्र O Great king, ते to you, धर्मलाभम् benefits of righteousness, इच्छसि यदि if you are  seeking, परमम् great, यशश्च fame, भुवि in this world, स्थितम् everlasting, रामम् Rama, मे to me, दातुम् to give me, अर्हसि it is proper and fit.
explanation: O king of kings, if you are seeking the benefits of righteousness, great everlasting fame in this world, it is fit and proper to give Rama to me.

shloka_text: यदिह्यनुज्ञां काकुत्स्थ ददते तव मन्त्रिण:।।1.19.16।। वसिष्ठप्रमुखा: सर्वे ततो रामं विसर्जय।
transliteration: yadihyanujñāṃ kākutstha dadate tava mantriṇa: vasiṣṭhapramukhā: sarve tato rāmaṃ visarjaya|
translation: काकुत्स्थ O Kakustha, तव your, मन्त्रिण: counsellors, वसिष्ठप्रमुखा: Vasistha, being the foremost among them, सर्वे all, अनुज्ञाम् consent, ददते यदि if they give, तत: then, रामम् Rama, विसर्जय you may relieve him.
explanation: O Kakustha if your counsellors and all other sages headed by Vasishta give their consent, then only you may relieve Rama.

shloka_text: अभिप्रेतमसंसक्तमात्मजं दातुमर्हसि।।1.19.17।। दशरात्रं हि यज्ञस्य रामं राजीवलोचनम्।
transliteration: abhipretamasaṃsaktamātmajaṃ dātumarhasi daśarātraṃ hi yajñasya rāmaṃ rājīvalocanam|
translation: अभिप्रेतम् dear to you, आत्मजम् son, राजीवलोचनम् lotuseyed, रामम् Rama, असंसक्तम् impartial and detached, यज्ञस्य of the sacrifice, दशरात्रम् ten days, दातुम् अर्हसि you deserve to  give.
explanation: You should spare your dear son, the lotuseyed Rama, impartial and detached, for ten nights.

shloka_text: नात्येति कालो यज्ञस्य यथाऽयं मम राघव।।1.19.18।। तथा कुरुष्व भद्रं ते मा च शोके मन: कृथा:।
transliteration: nātyeti kālo yajñasya yathā'yaṃ mama rāghava tathā kuruṣva bhadraṃ te mā ca śoke mana: kṛthā:|
translation: राघव O Descendent of Raghu, Dasaratha, मम my, यज्ञस्य this  sacrifice, अयं काल: the time, यथा in whichever manner, नात्येति does not get delayed, तथा in that manner, कुरुष्व act, शोके in grief, मन: mind, मा कृथा: do not indulge, भद्रं prosperity, ते to you.
explanation: O (Dasaratha), descendant of Raghu act in such a manner that the time for my sacrifice is not delayed. Do not indulge in grief. Prosperity to you"

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्त्वा धर्मात्मा धर्मार्थसहितं वच:।।1.19.19।। विरराम महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनि:।
transliteration: ityevamuktvā dharmātmā dharmārthasahitaṃ vaca: virarāma mahātejā viśvāmitro mahāmuni:|
translation: धर्मात्मा virtuous, महातेजा: resplendent, महामुनि: great sage, विश्वामित्र: Visvamitra, इत्येवम् in this manner, धर्मार्थसहितम् meaing containing religious merit, वच: words, उक्त्वा having spoken, विरराम became silent.
explanation: After speaking these words charged with dharma and artha the great sage resplendent Viswamitra fell silent.

shloka_text: स तन्निशम्य राजेन्द्रो विश्वामित्रवचश्शुभम्।।1.19.20।। शोकमभ्यगमत्तीव्रं व्यषीदत भयान्वित:।
transliteration: sa tanniśamya rājendro viśvāmitravacaśśubham śokamabhyagamattīvraṃ vyaṣīdata bhayānvita:|
translation: स:राजेन्द्र: that Indra of kings, king Dasaratha, शुभम् auspicious, तत् विश्वामित्रवच: those words of Visvamitra, निशम्य having listened, तीव्रम् intense, शोकम् grief, अभ्यगमत् obtained, भयान्वित: over powered by fear, व्यषीदत became despondent.
explanation: Having listened to those auspicious words of Viswamitra, the king among kings, (Dasaratha) experienced intense grief out of fear. He became despondent.

shloka_text: इति हृदयमनोविदारणं मुनिवचनं तदतीव शुश्रुवान्। नरपतिरभवन्महांस्तदा व्यथितमना: प्रचचाल चासनात्।।1.19.21।।
transliteration: iti hṛdayamanovidāraṇaṃ munivacanaṃ tadatīva śuśruvān| narapatirabhavanmahāṃstadā vyathitamanā: pracacāla cāsanāt
translation: इति in this manner, हृदयमनोविदारणम्  breaking the heart and mind, तत् मुनिवचनम् those words of sage Visvamitra, शश्रुवान् listened, महान् revered, नरपति: king, तदा then, अतीव व्यथितमना: अभवत् was exstreemly mentally agitated, आसनात् from his throne, चचाल च was shaken.
explanation: The great king felt shaken off his throne after listening to the words of the sage (Viswamitra) which broke his heart and terribly upset his mind. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये  बालकाण्डे एकोनविंशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the nineteenth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा राजशार्दूलो विश्वामित्रस्य भाषितम्। मुहूर्तमिव निस्संज्ञस्संज्ञावानिदमब्रवीत्।।1.20.1।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā rājaśārdūlo viśvāmitrasya bhāṣitam| muhūrtamiva nissaṃjñassaṃjñāvānidamabravīt
translation: राजशार्दूल: great king, विश्वामित्रस्य Visvamitra's, तत् भाषितम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, मुहूर्तमिव for a moment, निस्संज्ञ: lost his senses, संज्ञावान् regained his consciousness, इदम् अब्रवीत् thus spoke.
explanation: On hearing Viswamitra, words the tiger among kings (Dasaratha) lost his senses for a moment  and  on regaining his consciousness spoke this way.
comments: On king Dasaratha's refusal to accede to his request, Viswamitra gets enraged.

shloka_text: ऊनषोडशवर्षो मे रामो राजीवलोचन:। न युद्धयोग्यतामस्य पश्यामि सह राक्षसै:।।1.20.2।।
transliteration: ūnaṣoḍaśavarṣo me rāmo rājīvalocana:| na yuddhayogyatāmasya paśyāmi saha rākṣasai:
translation: राजीवलोचन: lotuseyed, मे राम: my Rama, ऊनषोडशवर्ष: in lessthan sixteen years of age, अस्य for him, राक्षसै:सह with the rakshasas, युद्धयोग्यताम् abilities to fight in a battle, न पश्यामि I do not see.
explanation: "My lotuseyed son Rama is less than sixteen. I do not think  he has ability to fight with the rakshasas in a battle.

shloka_text: इयमक्षौहिणी पूर्णा यस्याहं पतिरीश्वर:। अनया संवृतो गत्वा योद्धाऽहं तैर्निशाचरै:।।1.20.3।।
transliteration: iyamakṣauhiṇī pūrṇā yasyāhaṃ patirīśvara:| anayā saṃvṛto gatvā yoddhā'haṃ tairniśācarai:
translation: पूर्णा completely, इयम् अक्षौहिणी this Akshauhini, यस्या: for which, अहं I, पति: am the lord, ईश्वर: sustainer, अनया with this Akshauhini, संवृत: accompanied  by, गत्वा having gone, अहं I, तै:निशाचरै: with those night rangers, rakshasas, योद्धा will engage in the battle.
explanation: Here is the whole akshauhini (army) of which I am the lord and sustainer. Accompanied  by the  akshauhini I shall engage those rakshsasas in the battle.

shloka_text: इमे शूराश्च विक्रान्ता भृत्या मेऽस्त्रविशारदा:। योग्या रक्षोगणैर्योद्धुं न रामं नेतुमर्हसि।।1.20.4।।
transliteration: ime śūrāśca vikrāntā bhṛtyā me'straviśāradā:| yogyā rakṣogaṇairyoddhuṃ na rāmaṃ netumarhasi
translation: मे भृत्या: my servants, इमे these warriors, शूराश्च also valiant, विक्रान्ता: powerful, अस्त्रविशारदा: those skilled in use of weapons, रक्षोगणै: multitude of rakshasas, योद्धुम् to engage in battle, योग्या: are fit, रामम् Rama, नेतुम् नार्हसि not proper on your part to take him.
explanation: These servants of mine are warriors, valiant, powerful and courageous, skilled in the use of weapons and fit to engage multitude of rakshasas in battle. It is not proper to take Rama with you.

shloka_text: अहमेव धनुष्पाणिर्गोप्ता समरमूर्धनि। यावत्प्राणान्धरिष्यामि तावद्योत्स्ये निशाचरै:।।1.20.5।।
transliteration: ahameva dhanuṣpāṇirgoptā samaramūrdhani| yāvatprāṇāndhariṣyāmi tāvadyotsye niśācarai:
translation: अहमेव I myself, धनुष्पाणि: with a bow in hand, गोप्ता will protect, यावत् as long as, प्राणान् my life, धरिष्यामि I sustain, तावत् till such time, समरमूर्धनि on the battlefield, निशाचरै: with rakshasas, योत्स्ये will engage in the battle.
explanation: Wielding bow in hand I will protect the sacrifice. As long as my life sustains, I will engage the rakshasas in the battle.

shloka_text: निर्विघ्ना व्रतचर्या सा भविष्यति सुरक्षिता। अहं तत्रागमिष्यामि न रामं नेतुमर्हसि।।1.20.6।।
transliteration: nirvighnā vratacaryā sā bhaviṣyati surakṣitā| ahaṃ tatrāgamiṣyāmi na rāmaṃ netumarhasi
translation: अहम् I, तत्र there, आगमिष्यामि shall come, सा व्रतचर्या that observance of vows,सुरक्षिता will be well protected, निर्विघ्ना without obstacles, भविष्यति will continue, रामम् Rama, नेतुम् to take, नार्हसि it is not proper on your part.
explanation: . I shall go there, protect the sacrifice and see that it is conducted without obstacles. It is not proper to take Rama with you.

shloka_text: बालो ह्यकृतविद्यश्च न च वेत्ति बलाबलम्। न चास्त्रबलसंयुक्तो न च युद्धविशारद:।।1.20.7।। न चासौ रक्षसां योग्य: कूटयुद्धा हि ते ध्रुवम् ।
transliteration: bālo hyakṛtavidyaśca na ca vetti balābalam| na cāstrabalasaṃyukto na ca yuddhaviśārada: na cāsau rakṣasāṃ yogya: kūṭayuddhā hi te dhruvam |
translation: हि indeed, बाल: a child, अकृतविद्यश्च is not learned in the science of warfare, बलाबलम् strengths and weaknesses, न वेत्ति does not know, अस्त्रबलसंयुक्त:च न  has not acquired the strength of weapons, युद्धविशारद: च न not proficient in warfare, असौ he, रक्षसाम् of  rakshasas, योग्य:न is not qualified, ते those rakshasas, ध्रुवम् certainly, कूटयुद्धा: हि are  deceitful in battle.
explanation: Rama is still a child, he is not learned in the science of warfare,he does not know the  strength and weakness of enemies. He has not acquired  as yet the strength of using  weapons and is not proficient in warfare. You know certainly those rakshasas are deceitful in battle. And hence he is not qualified to oppose them in the battle succesfully.

shloka_text: विप्रयुक्तो हि रामेण मुहूर्तमपि नोत्सहे।।1.20.8।। जीवितुं मुनिशार्दूल न रामं नेतुमर्हसि।
transliteration: viprayukto hi rāmeṇa muhūrtamapi notsahe jīvituṃ muniśārdūla na rāmaṃ netumarhasi|
translation: रामेण from Rama, विप्रयुक्त: separated, मुहूर्तमपि even for a moment, जीवितुम् to live, नोत्सहे I do not like, मुनिशार्दूल O Best of ascetics, रामम् Rama, नेतुम् to take, नार्हसि it is not proper on your part (You should not take).
explanation: Separated from Rama, I do not like to live even for a moment. O tiger among ascetics, it is not proper to take Rama with you.

shloka_text: यदि वा राघवं ब्रह्मन्नेतुमिच्छसि सुव्रत।।1.20.9।। चतुरङ्गसमायुक्तं मया च सहितं नय।
transliteration: yadi vā rāghavaṃ brahmannetumicchasi suvrata caturaṅgasamāyuktaṃ mayā ca sahitaṃ naya|
translation: सुव्रत O Sage of excellent vows, ब्रह्मन् O Brahman, वा or, राघवम् Rama, नेतुम् to take him, इच्छसि you are intending, चतुरङ्गसमायुक्तम् my army consiting of elephants, chariots, cavalry and infantry, मया च सहितम् along with me, नय you may take.
explanation: O sage of great vows, O brahman if at all you intend to take Rama with you, take me  also along with my army.

shloka_text: षष्टिर्वर्षसहस्राणि जातस्य मम कौशिक।।1.20.10।। दु:खेनोत्पादितश्चायं न रामं नेतुमर्हसि।
transliteration: ṣaṣṭirvarṣasahasrāṇi jātasya mama kauśika du:khenotpāditaścāyaṃ na rāmaṃ netumarhasi|
translation: कौशिक O Scion of Kusika family, जातस्य having born, मम for me, षष्टि: sixty, वर्षसहस्राणि thousand years passed, अयम् this Rama, दु:खेन with great efforts, उत्पादित: is obtained,  रामम् Rama, नेतुम् to take him, नार्हसि it is not proper for you.
explanation: O scion of of Kusika family, sixty thousand years have passed since I was born.  Rama was born to me after a great deal of suffering. It is not proper to take him with you.

shloka_text: चतुर्णामात्मजानां हि प्रीति:परमिका मम।।1.20.11।। ज्येष्ठं धर्मप्रधानं च न रामं नेतुमर्हसि।
transliteration: caturṇāmātmajānāṃ hi prīti:paramikā mama jyeṣṭhaṃ dharmapradhānaṃ ca na rāmaṃ netumarhasi|
translation: चतुर्णाम् among the four, आत्मजानाम् sons, मम for me, परमिका great, प्रीति: हि affection           indeed, ज्येष्ठम् eldest, धर्मप्रधानम् च with virtue as prime qualification, रामम् Rama, नेतुम् to take, नार्हसि it is not proper.
explanation: My love for Rama among all my four sons is supreme.It is not proper for you to take Rama, the eldest son whose prime qualification  is his virtue.

shloka_text: किंवीर्या राक्षसास्ते च कस्य पुत्राश्च ते च के।।1.20.12।। कथं प्रमाणा: के चैतान्रक्षन्ति मुनिपुङ्गव।
transliteration: kiṃvīryā rākṣasāste ca kasya putrāśca te ca ke kathaṃ pramāṇā: ke caitānrakṣanti munipuṅgava|
translation: मुनिपुङ्गव O Best of sages, ते राक्षसा: those rakshsas, किंवीर्या how powerful?, कस्य whose, पुत्रा: sons?, ते they, के who?, कथंप्रमाणा: how much is the size of their body, एतान् them, के who, रक्षन्ति are protecting.
explanation: O best of sages, how powerful are those rakshsas? Whose  sons are they? Who are they and how huge is their body? Who are protecting them?

shloka_text: कथं च प्रतिकर्तव्यं तेषां रामेण रक्षसाम्।।1.20.13।। मामकैर्वा बलैर्ब्रह्मन्मया वा कूटयोधिनाम्।3
transliteration: kathaṃ ca pratikartavyaṃ teṣāṃ rāmeṇa rakṣasām māmakairvā balairbrahmanmayā vā kūṭayodhinām|3
translation: ब्रह्मन् O Brahman, कूटयोधिनाम् of those treacherous and deceitful warriors, तेषाम् रक्षसाम् in the matter of those rakshasas, रामेण by Rama, मामकै: my, बलै: वा with forces, मया वा by me, कथम् how, प्रतिकर्तव्यम् to retaliate.
explanation: O brahman, how to rebuff those deceitful warriors either through Rama or through my army or through me?

shloka_text: सर्वं मे शंस भगवन्कथं तेषां मया रणे।।1.20.14।। स्थातव्यं दुष्टभावानां वीर्योत्सिक्ता हि राक्षसा:।4 तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत।।1.20.15।।
transliteration: sarvaṃ me śaṃsa bhagavankathaṃ teṣāṃ mayā raṇe sthātavyaṃ duṣṭabhāvānāṃ vīryotsiktā hi rākṣasā:|4 tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā viśvāmitro'bhyabhāṣata
translation: भगवन् O Venerable one, दुष्टभावानाम् of the wicked natured, तेषाम् of them, मया by me, रणे in the battle, कथम् how, स्थातव्यम् to stay, सर्वम् all this matter, मे to me, शंस tell, राक्षसा: rakshasas, वीर्योत्सिक्ता: proud of their prowess, तस्य his, तत् वचनम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, विश्वामित्र: Viswamitra, अभ्यभाषत spoke.
explanation: O venerable one, how to fight those wickednatured ones in the battle and stay aginst them? For rakshasas are proud of their prowess". Having heard the words of Dasaratha, Viswamitra said:

shloka_text: सर्वं मे शंस भगवन्कथं तेषां मया रणे।।1.20.14।। स्थातव्यं दुष्टभावानां वीर्योत्सिक्ता हि राक्षसा:।4 तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत।।1.20.15।।
transliteration: sarvaṃ me śaṃsa bhagavankathaṃ teṣāṃ mayā raṇe sthātavyaṃ duṣṭabhāvānāṃ vīryotsiktā hi rākṣasā:|4 tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā viśvāmitro'bhyabhāṣata
translation: भगवन् O Venerable one, दुष्टभावानाम् of the wicked natured, तेषाम् of them, मया by me, रणे in the battle, कथम् how, स्थातव्यम् to stay, सर्वम् all this matter, मे to me, शंस tell, राक्षसा: rakshasas, वीर्योत्सिक्ता: proud of their prowess, तस्य his, तत् वचनम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, विश्वामित्र: Viswamitra, अभ्यभाषत spoke.
explanation: O venerable one, how to fight those wickednatured ones in the battle and stay aginst them? For rakshasas are proud of their prowess". Having heard the words of Dasaratha, Viswamitra said:

shloka_text: पौलस्त्यवंशप्रभवो रावणो नाम राक्षस:। स ब्रह्मणा दत्तवरस्त्रैलोक्यं बाधते भृशम्।।1.20.16।। महाबलो महावीर्यो राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृत:।
transliteration: paulastyavaṃśaprabhavo rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasa:| sa brahmaṇā dattavarastrailokyaṃ bādhate bhṛśam mahābalo mahāvīryo rākṣasairbahubhirvṛta:|
translation: पौलस्त्यवंशप्रभव: born in the illustrious race of Pulastya, रावणो नाम by name Ravana, राक्षस: rakshasa, महाबल: of great strength, महावीर्य: of great prowess, स: he, ब्रह्मणा by Brahma, दत्तवर: by boon granted, बहुभि: by several, राक्षसै: by rakshasas, वृत: accompanied, त्रैलोक्यम् three worlds, भृशम् excessively, बाधते is tormenting.
explanation: A rakshasa named Ravana, born in the illustrious race of Pulastya, of great strength and prowess and granted a boon by Brahma, accompanied by many rakshasas, is grievously tormenting the three worlds.

shloka_text: श्रूयते हि महावीर्यो रावणो राक्षसाधिप:।।1.20.17।। साक्षाद्वैश्रवणभ्राता पुत्रो विश्रवसो मुने:।
transliteration: śrūyate hi mahāvīryo rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipa: sākṣādvaiśravaṇabhrātā putro viśravaso mune:|
translation: साक्षात् evidently, वैश्रवणभ्राता brother of Kubera, विश्रवस:मुने: ascetic Visrava's, पुत्र: son, राक्षसाधिप: king of rakshasas, रावण: Ravana, महावीर्य: of great prowess, श्रूयते it is heard.
explanation: Ravana, king of rakshasas, is the brother of Kubera and son of ascetic Visravana. He is said to possess great prowess.

shloka_text: यदा स्वयं न यज्ञस्य विघ्नकर्ता महाबल:।।1.20.18।। तेन सञ्चोदितौ द्वौ तु राक्षसौ वै महाबलौ। मारीचश्च सुबाहुश्च यज्ञविघ्नं करिष्यत:।।1.20.19।।
transliteration: yadā svayaṃ na yajñasya vighnakartā mahābala: tena sañcoditau dvau tu rākṣasau vai mahābalau| mārīcaśca subāhuśca yajñavighnaṃ kariṣyata:
translation: महाबल: he, possessing great strength, यदा when, स्वयम् on his own, यज्ञस्य for sacrifice, विघ्नकर्ता न does not create impediments, तेन by, सञ्चोदितौ prompted, मारीचश्च Maricha, सुबाहुश्च Subahu, द्वौ राक्षसौ two rakshasas, यज्ञविघ्नम् obsctacles of sacrifice, करिष्यत: cause.
explanation: Although endowed with great strength, Ravana, by himself, never created impediments to the sacrifice. But two rakshasas by name Maricha and Subahu are incited by him to cause obstacles".

shloka_text: यदा स्वयं न यज्ञस्य विघ्नकर्ता महाबल:।।1.20.18।। तेन सञ्चोदितौ द्वौ तु राक्षसौ वै महाबलौ। मारीचश्च सुबाहुश्च यज्ञविघ्नं करिष्यत:।।1.20.19।।
transliteration: yadā svayaṃ na yajñasya vighnakartā mahābala: tena sañcoditau dvau tu rākṣasau vai mahābalau| mārīcaśca subāhuśca yajñavighnaṃ kariṣyata:
translation: महाबल: he, possessing great strength, यदा when, स्वयम् on his own, यज्ञस्य for sacrifice, विघ्नकर्ता न does not create impediments, तेन by, सञ्चोदितौ prompted, मारीचश्च Maricha, सुबाहुश्च Subahu, द्वौ राक्षसौ two rakshasas, यज्ञविघ्नम् obsctacles of sacrifice, करिष्यत: cause.
explanation: Although endowed with great strength, Ravana, by himself, never created impediments to the sacrifice. But two rakshasas by name Maricha and Subahu are incited by him to cause obstacles".

shloka_text: इत्युक्तो मुनिना तेन राजोवाच मुनिं तदा। न हि शक्तोऽस्मि सङ्ग्रामे स्थातुं तस्य दुरात्मन:।।1.20.20।।
transliteration: ityukto muninā tena rājovāca muniṃ tadā| na hi śakto'smi saṅgrāme sthātuṃ tasya durātmana:
translation: इति in this manner, तेन मुनिना by that sage, उक्त: spoken, राजा king Dasaratha, तदा then, मुनिम् addressing the sage, उवाच said, सङ्ग्रामे in the battle, तस्य दुरात्मन: of that evil minded one, स्थातुम् to stand, शक्त: न अस्मि I am not capable.
explanation: Informed in this manner by sage Viswamitra, king Dasaratha addressed the sage,  saying, "I am not competent enough to stand before those evilminded rakshasas in the batlle".

shloka_text: स त्वं प्रसादं धर्मज्ञ कुरुष्व मम पुत्रके। मम चैवाल्पभाग्यस्य दैवतं हि भवान्गुरु:।।1.20.21।।
transliteration: sa tvaṃ prasādaṃ dharmajña kuruṣva mama putrake| mama caivālpabhāgyasya daivataṃ hi bhavānguru:
translation: धर्मज्ञ O Knower of truth, स:त्वम् such of you, मम to me, पुत्रके in the little son, अल्पभाग्यस्य of the unfortunate, मम च in my matter, प्रसादम् favour,  कुरुष्व extend, गुरु: spiritual preceptor, भवान् you, दैवतं हि verily god.
explanation: "You are the knower of righteousness. Extend your favour to my little son and also to me for I am so who is unfortunate. You are verily my spiritual preceptor and god.

shloka_text: देवदानवगन्धर्वा यक्षा:पतगपन्नगा:। न शक्ता रावणं सोढुं किं पुनर्मानवा युधि।।1.20.22।।
transliteration: devadānavagandharvā yakṣā:patagapannagā:| na śaktā rāvaṇaṃ soḍhuṃ kiṃ punarmānavā yudhi
translation: देवदानवगन्धर्वा: gods, danavas and gandharvas, यक्षा: yakshas, पतगपन्नगा: birds and great serpents, युधि in the battle, रावणम् Ravana, सोढुम् to endure him, न शक्ता: are not capable, मानवा: men, किं पुन: again to say.
explanation: Gods, danavas, gandharvas, yakshas, birds and great serpents cannot withstand Ravana in battle. What are men to him? (They are no match to him).

shloka_text: स हि वीर्यवतां वीर्यमादत्ते युधि राक्षस:। तेन चाहं न शक्तोऽस्मि संयोद्धुं तस्य वा बलै:।।1.20.23।। सबलो वा मुनिश्रेष्ठ सहितो वा ममात्मजै:।
transliteration: sa hi vīryavatāṃ vīryamādatte yudhi rākṣasa:| tena cāhaṃ na śakto'smi saṃyoddhuṃ tasya vā balai: sabalo vā muniśreṣṭha sahito vā mamātmajai:|
translation: स: राक्षस: that rakshasa, युधि in the battle, वीर्यवताम् of the warriors, वीर्यम् prowess, आदत्ते हि takes, मुनिश्रेष्ठ O Foremost of ascetics, सबलो वा either with forces, मम आत्मजै:सहितो वा or together with my sons, अहम् I, तेन with him, तस्य बलै:वा  or with his forces, संयोद्धुम् to engage in battle, न शक्तोऽस्मि I am not competant.
explanation: That rakshasa pulls out warriors' prowess in the battle. O foremost of ascetics Either with forces or with my sons it is not possible for me to engage him or his forces in battle.

shloka_text: कथमप्यमरप्रख्यं सङ्ग्रामाणामकोविदम्। बालं मे तनयं ब्रह्मन् नैव दास्यामि पुत्रकम्।।1.20.24।।
transliteration: kathamapyamaraprakhyaṃ saṅgrāmāṇāmakovidam| bālaṃ me tanayaṃ brahman naiva dāsyāmi putrakam
translation: ब्रह्मन् O Brahman, अमरप्रख्यम् resembling celestial deities, सङ्ग्रामाणाम् in the warfare, अकोविदम् not experienced, बालं पुत्रकम् dear young child, मे my, तनयम् son, कथमपि how so ever, नैव दास्यामि I never, never give him.
explanation: O brahman although my son resembles the celestials he is not experienced in warfare. On no account shall I spare him.

shloka_text: अथ कालोपमौ युध्दे सुतौ सुन्दोपसुन्दयो:।।1.20.25।। यज्ञविघ्नकरौ तौ ते नैव दास्यामि पुत्रकम्।
transliteration: atha kālopamau yudhde sutau sundopasundayo: yajñavighnakarau tau te naiva dāsyāmi putrakam|
translation: अथ and, ते you, यज्ञविघ्नकरौ those causing obstacles to sacrifice, सुन्दोपसुन्दयो: of Sunda and Upasunda, सुतौ तौ sons, युध्दे in the battle, कालोपमौ resemble god of death, Yama, पुत्रकम् my son, नैव दास्यामि I shall never part with him.
explanation: Further the sons of Sunda and Upasunda by name Maricha and Subahu are causing obstacles to your sacrifice. They resemble the god of death, Yama. I shall never part with my son.

shloka_text: मारीचश्च सुबाहुश्च वीर्यवन्तौ सुशिक्षितौ। तयोरन्यतरेणाहं योध्दा स्यां ससुहृद्गण:।।1.20.26।।
transliteration: mārīcaśca subāhuśca vīryavantau suśikṣitau| tayoranyatareṇāhaṃ yodhdā syāṃ sasuhṛdgaṇa:
translation: मारीचश्च Maricha, सुबाहुश्च Subahu, वीर्यवन्तौ possessed of prowess, सुशिक्षितौ experienced  in warfare, अहम् I, ससुहृद्गण: with my best friends, तयो: in them, अन्यतरेण with one of them, योध्दा स्याम् can combat.
explanation: Maricha and Subahu not only possess prowess but also are experienced in warfare. Together with my group of friends I can combat with one of the two".

shloka_text: इति नरपतिजल्पनाद्द्विजेन्द्रं कुशिकसुतं सुमहान्विवेश मन्यु:। सुहुत इव मखेऽग्निराज्यसिक्त स्समभवदुज्ज्वलितो महर्षिवह्नि:।।1.20.27।।
transliteration: iti narapatijalpanāddvijendraṃ kuśikasutaṃ sumahānviveśa manyu:| suhuta iva makhe'gnirājyasikta ssamabhavadujjvalito maharṣivahni:
translation: इति in this manner, नरपतिजल्पनात् with the statements of king Dasaratha, द्विजेन्द्रम् Indra among ascetics, कुशिकसुतम् son of Kusika, सुमहान् great, मन्यु: rage, विवेश entered, महर्षिवह्नि: fire in the form of maharshi, मखे in the sacrifice, सुहुत: with good offerings of  oblation, आज्यसिक्त: sprinkled with clarified butter, अग्नि:इव like  sacrificial fire, उज्वलित: समभवत् blazed.
explanation: Having heard the statements of the king the son of Kusika, Viswamitra who was like Indra among the ascetics was seized by great anger. As though fire in the form of  maharshi blazed like the sacrificial fire into which oblations of clarified butter have been poured. ।। iऋफफछफौ चफळउफp८फउफफऋफhफॊ खफफऔउफळE१ळऋफ फबn८E१फखऋफॊ अफफऔफE१फhbॊ६ भखफघफजजफMफऩ ityढऍ डrंmadraचऍ vmंkंya ikyऍ bakङऍ viनडassargaध৷৷ Thus ends the twentieth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य स्नेहपर्याकुलाक्षरम्। समन्यु: कौशिको वाक्यं प्रत्युवाच महीपतिम्।।1.21.1।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya snehaparyākulākṣaram| samanyu: kauśiko vākyaṃ pratyuvāca mahīpatim
translation: तस्य king Dasaratha's, स्नेहपर्याकुलाक्षरम् affectionfilled confused letters, तत् वचनम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, कौशिक: Visvamitra, समन्यु: with anger, महीपतिम् addressing  the king, वाक्यम् words, प्रत्युवाच replied.
explanation: Out of affection towards his son, his (king Dasaratha's) plea to Viswamitra was full of contradiction. And on hearing the king, enraged Viswamitra replied:
comments: On king Dasaratha's refusal to accede to his request, Viswamitra gets enraged.

shloka_text: पूर्वमर्थं प्रतिश्रुत्य प्रतिज्ञां हातुमिच्छसि। राघवाणामयुक्तोऽयं कुलस्यास्य विपर्यय:।।1.21.2।।
transliteration: pūrvamarthaṃ pratiśrutya pratijñāṃ hātumicchasi| rāghavāṇāmayukto'yaṃ kulasyāsya viparyaya:
translation: पूर्वम् formerly, अर्थम् object or thing, प्रतिश्रुत्य having promised, प्रतिज्ञाम् that promise, हातुम् to break, इच्छसि your are desirous, अयं विपर्यय: in contrariety (breach of vow), राघवाणाम्  Raghu's, अस्य कुलस्य in the race of, अयुक्त: improper.
explanation: Having formerly promised the thing, you now wish to break your pledge; such a breach of vow is improper and unbecoming in the race of Raghu.

shloka_text: यदीदं ते क्षमं राजन् गमिष्यामि यथाऽगतम्। मिथ्याप्रतिज्ञ: काकुत्स्थ सुखीभव सबान्धव:।।1.21.3।।
transliteration: yadīdaṃ te kṣamaṃ rājan gamiṣyāmi yathā'gatam| mithyāpratijña: kākutstha sukhībhava sabāndhava:
translation: राजन् O King, इदम् this act of yours, ते to you, क्षमं यदि if appropriate, यथाऽगतम् from where I have come, गमिष्यामि I shall go, काकुत्स्थ OScion of the race of Kakutstha, मिथ्याप्रतिज्ञ: proving false to your promise, सबान्धव: along with your relatives, सुखीभव be happy.
explanation: O king, if this act of yours is appropriate to you, I will go back (to the places) where from I came. O scion of the race of kakutstha, you have proved false to your promise. Live happily with your relatives".

shloka_text: तस्य रोषपरीतस्य विश्वामित्रस्य धीमत:। चचाल वसुधा कृत्स्ना विवेश च भयं सुरान्।।1.21.4।।
transliteration: tasya roṣaparītasya viśvāmitrasya dhīmata:| cacāla vasudhā kṛtsnā viveśa ca bhayaṃ surān
translation: धीमत: of the wise, तस्य विश्वामित्रस्य that Visvamitra's, रोषपरीतस्य seized of wrath, कृत्स्ना entire, वसुधा earth, चचाल had shaken, सुरान् devatas, भयम् fear,  विवेश gripped.
explanation: At the sight of the wise sage Viswamitra seized of wrath, the entire earth shook and  devatas were gripped in fear.

shloka_text: त्रस्तरूपं तु विज्ञाय जगत्सर्वं महानृषि:। नृपतिं सुव्रतो धीरो वसिष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।1.21.5।।
transliteration: trastarūpaṃ tu vijñāya jagatsarvaṃ mahānṛṣi:| nṛpatiṃ suvrato dhīro vasiṣṭho vākyamabravīt
translation: सुव्रत: adherent of ascetic practices, धीर: steadfast in his duty, महान् ऋषि: great Rishi, वसिष्ठ: Vasishta, सर्वम् जगत् entire world, त्रस्तरूपम् freightened form, विज्ञाय knowing, नृपतिम् addressing the king, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said:
explanation: Great Vasishta, an adherent of ascetic practices and steadfast (to duty), seeing that the entire world frightened addressed the king, saying:

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातस्साक्षाद्धर्म इवापर:। धृतिमान् सुव्रत: श्रीमान्नधर्मं हातुमर्हसि।।1.21.6।।
transliteration: ikṣvākūṇāṃ kule jātassākṣāddharma ivāpara:| dhṛtimān suvrata: śrīmānnadharmaṃ hātumarhasi
translation: इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले in the line of  Ikshvaku, जात: born, साक्षात् truely, अपर: another, धर्म: इव god of righteousness (personified), धृतिमान् firm, सुव्रत: observing excellent vows, श्रीमान् auspicious one, धर्मम् virtuousness, हातुम् to abandon, न अर्हसि you are not fit.
explanation: "Born in the line of Ikshvaku, you are a veritable the second god of righteousness, firm adherent of vows auspicious and virtuous. It is not right on your part to abandon your promise.

shloka_text: त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातो धर्मात्मा इति राघव। स्वधर्मं प्रतिपद्यस्व नाधर्मं वोढुमर्हसि।।1.21.7।।
transliteration: triṣu lokeṣu vikhyāto dharmātmā iti rāghava| svadharmaṃ pratipadyasva nādharmaṃ voḍhumarhasi
translation: राघव O Dasaratha, धर्मात्मा इति as righteousminded, त्रिषु लोकेषु in three worlds, विख्यात:, reputed, स्वधर्मम् your own duty, प्रतिपद्यस्व observe, अधर्मम् unjust act, वोढुम् to endure, न अर्हसि not worthy of you.
explanation: O Dasaratha you are reputed in the three worlds as righteousminded. Do your own duty. Do not follow an unjust act which is unworthy of respect.

shloka_text: संश्रुत्यैवं करिष्यामीत्यकुर्वाणस्य राघव। इष्टापूर्तवधो भूयात्तस्माद्रामं विसर्जय।।1.21.8।।
transliteration: saṃśrutyaivaṃ kariṣyāmītyakurvāṇasya rāghava| iṣṭāpūrtavadho bhūyāttasmādrāmaṃ visarjaya
translation: राघव O Dasaratha, एवं करिष्यामि इति I shall do so, संश्रुत्य having promised, अकुर्वाणस्य for one who does not fulfill, इष्टापूर्तवध: भूयात् destruction of merits earned through pious acts of sacrifice and other charitable acts, तस्मात् for that reason, रामम् Rama, विसर्जय send him.
explanation: O Dasaratha, a promise made and not kept amounts to destruction of merits earned through previous pieties. Therefore send Rama (with him).

shloka_text: कृतास्त्रमकृतास्त्रं वा नैनं शक्ष्यन्ति राक्षसा:। गुप्तं कुशिकपुत्रेण ज्वलनेनामृतं यथा।।1.21.9।।
transliteration: kṛtāstramakṛtāstraṃ vā nainaṃ śakṣyanti rākṣasā:| guptaṃ kuśikaputreṇa jvalanenāmṛtaṃ yathā
translation: कृतास्त्रम् trained in the use of arms, अकृतास्त्रं वा or untrained,  कुशिकपुत्रेण by Viswamitra, गुप्तम् protected, एनम् this Rama, ज्वलनेन by flaming fire, अमृतं यथा like divine nectar, राक्षसा: rakshasas, न शक्ष्यन्ति will not be able to compete.
explanation: Trained or not in the use of arms, as long as Rama is protected by Viswamitra, just as nectar is protected by the flaming firegod rakshasas will not be able to compete with him.

shloka_text: एष विग्रहवान् धर्म एष वीर्यवतां वर:। एष बुध्याऽधिको लोके तपसश्च परायणम्।।1.21.10।।
transliteration: eṣa vigrahavān dharma eṣa vīryavatāṃ vara:| eṣa budhyā'dhiko loke tapasaśca parāyaṇam
translation: एष: Visvamitra, विग्रहवान् embodiment, धर्म: righteousness, एष: Visvamitra, वीर्यवताम् of those possessing prowess, वर: excellent, एष: Visvamitra, बुध्या in intellect, लोके in this world, अधिक: surpasses, तपस: in asceticism, परायणम् last resort (supreme refuge).
explanation: This (Viswamitra) is an embodiment of righteousness and unsurpassed among the powerful. None can excel him in intellect in this world. He is the supreme refuge in austerity.

shloka_text: एषोऽस्त्रान् विविधान्वेत्ति त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे। नैनमन्य: पुमान्वेत्ति न च वेत्स्यन्ति केचन।।1.21.11।।
transliteration: eṣo'strān vividhānvetti trailokye sacarācare| nainamanya: pumānvetti na ca vetsyanti kecana
translation: एष: this one, विविधान् various kinds of, अस्त्रान् weapons, वेत्ति knows, सचराचरे among all animate and inanimate beings, त्रैलोक्ये in three words, अन्य: पुमान् no other man, एनं न वेत्ति does not know him, केचन none, न वेत्स्यन्ति are not going to know about him in future.
explanation: This Viswamitra knows the use of various kinds of weapons which no one knows among the animate and the inanimate in the three worlds. Nor will any one even know in future.

shloka_text: न देवा नर्षय: केचिन्नासुरा न च राक्षसा:। गन्धर्वयक्षप्रवरास्सकिन्नरमहोरगा:।।1.21.12।।
transliteration: na devā narṣaya: kecinnāsurā na ca rākṣasā:| gandharvayakṣapravarāssakinnaramahoragā:
translation: देवा: devatas, न(वेत्स्यन्ति) will not be able to know how to use weapons, ऋषय: rishis, केचित् न none knows, असुरा: nor asuras, राक्षसा: न nor rakshasas, सकिन्नरमहोरगा: along with kinnaras or mighty serpants, गन्धर्वयक्षप्रवरा: nor gandharvas nor best of yakshas.
explanation: No gods nor sages nor asuras in rakshasas nor kinnaras nor mighty serpents nor gandharvas nor the best of yakshas (will be able to know)

shloka_text: सर्वास्त्राणि भृशाश्वस्य पुत्रा: परमधार्मिका:। कौशिकाय पुरा दत्ता यदा राज्यं प्रशासति।।1.21.13।।
transliteration: sarvāstrāṇi bhṛśāśvasya putrā: paramadhārmikā:| kauśikāya purā dattā yadā rājyaṃ praśāsati
translation: भृशाश्वस्य Bhrisasva's, परमधार्मिका: highly virtuous, पुत्रा: sons, सर्वास्त्राणि they also, यदा when, पुरा formerly, राज्यम् kingdom, प्रशासति ruling, कौशिकाय for Viswamitra, दत्ता: were given.
explanation: All these weapons were given to Viswamitra by Bhrisasva's highly virtuous sons while he was ruling the kingdom.

shloka_text: तेऽपि पुत्रा भृशाश्वस्य प्रजापतिसुतासुता:। नैकरूपा महावीर्या दीप्तिमन्तो जयावहा:।।1.21.14।।
transliteration: te'pi putrā bhṛśāśvasya prajāpatisutāsutā:| naikarūpā mahāvīryā dīptimanto jayāvahā:
translation: प्रजापतिसुतासुता: grand sons of Prajapati, भृशाश्वस्य Bhrisasva's, पुत्रा: sons, तेऽपि as the weapons, नैकरूपा: of diverse forms, महावीर्या: highly energetic, दीप्तिमन्त: full of glory, जयावहा: bring victory.
explanation: Grandsons (daughter's sons) of Prajapati, they (these weapons) are in diverse forms, highly energetic and full of glory they bring victory.

shloka_text: जया च सुप्रभा चैव दक्षकन्ये सुमध्यमे। ते सुवातेऽस्त्रशस्त्राणि शतं परमभास्वरम्।।1.21.15।।
transliteration: jayā ca suprabhā caiva dakṣakanye sumadhyame| te suvāte'straśastrāṇi śataṃ paramabhāsvaram
translation: जया च Jaya, सुप्रभा च and Suprabha, सुमध्यमे of slender waists, दक्षकन्ये the two daughters of Daksha, ते they, अस्त्रशस्त्राणाम् of Astras and Shastras(weapons for striking and throwing arms and missiles), परमभास्वरम् effulgent, शतम् one hundred, सुवाते gave birth to sons (named as Samharas).
explanation: Jaya and Suprabha of slender waists are the two daughters of Daksha. They gave  birth to one hundred effulgent sons known as astras and shastras.

shloka_text: पञ्चाशतं सुतान् लेभे जया नाम परान् पुरा। वधायासुरसैन्यानाममेयान् कामरूपिण:।।1.21.16।।
transliteration: pañcāśataṃ sutān lebhe jayā nāma parān purā| vadhāyāsurasainyānāmameyān kāmarūpiṇa:
translation: पुरा formerly, जया नाम named Jaya, असुरसैन्यानाम् for asura army, वधाय for the destruction, अमेयान् immeasurable prowess, कामरूपिण: possessing power of changing forms at free will, वरान् boon, पञ्चाशतम् fifty, सुतान् sons, लेभे obtained.
explanation: Formerly Jaya, for the destruction of the army of asuras gave birth to fifty sons by virtue of a boon. They  possess immeasurable power of changing forms at will.

shloka_text: सुप्रभाऽजनयच्चापि पुत्रान्पञ्चाशतं पुन:। संहारान्नामदुर्धर्षान् दुराक्रामान् बलीयस:।।1.21.17।।
transliteration: suprabhā'janayaccāpi putrānpañcāśataṃ puna:| saṃhārānnāmadurdharṣān durākrāmān balīyasa:
translation: सुप्रभापि Suprabha also, दुर्धर्षान् unassailable, दुराक्रमान् invincible, बलीयस: morepowerful, संहारान् नाम Samhara by name पुन: still, पञ्चाशतम् fifty, पुत्रान् sons, अजनयत्  gave birth.
explanation: Suprabha gave birth to another fifty sons named Samharas who are unassailable,  invincible and more powerful.

shloka_text: तानि चास्त्राणि वेत्त्येष यथावत्कुशिकात्मज:। अपूर्वाणां च जनने शक्तो भूयस्स धर्मवित्।।1.21.18।।
transliteration: tāni cāstrāṇi vettyeṣa yathāvatkuśikātmaja:| apūrvāṇāṃ ca janane śakto bhūyassa dharmavit
translation: एष: कुशिकात्मज: this Visvamitra, तानि अस्त्राणि these weapons, यथावत् very well, वेत्ति knows, धर्मवित् virtuous, स: भूय: he also, अपूर्वाणाम् of new weapons, जनने च in creation, शक्त: capable.
explanation: Viswamitra is well conversant with these weapons. Being virtuous, he is capable of creating new weapons also.

shloka_text: एवं वीर्यो महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महायशाः। न रामगमने राजन् संशयं कर्तुमर्हसि।।1.21.19।।
transliteration: evaṃ vīryo mahātejā viśvāmitro mahāyaśāḥ| na rāmagamane rājan saṃśayaṃ kartumarhasi
translation: महातेजा: highly effulgent, महायशा: highly renowned, विश्वामित्र: Visvamitra, एवं वीर्य: has  such prowess, राजन् O King, रामगमने to send Rama, संशयम् doubt, कर्तुम् to entertain, नार्हसि it is not proper for you.
explanation: Such is the prowess of Viswamitra who is a highly effulgent and highly renowned  sage. O King in sending Rama, you need not entertain any doubt.

shloka_text: तेषां निग्रहणे शक्तस्स्वयं च कुशिकात्मज:। तव पुत्रहितार्थाय त्वामुपेत्याभियाचते।।1.21.20।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ nigrahaṇe śaktassvayaṃ ca kuśikātmaja:| tava putrahitārthāya tvāmupetyābhiyācate
translation: कुशिकात्मज: son of Kusika, स्वयं च by himself, तेषाम् of those rakhsasas, निग्रहणे in  repressing, शक्त: capable, तव your, पुत्रहितार्थाय welfare of your son, त्वाम् you, उपेत्य having reached, अभि याचते begs.
explanation: Son of Kusika, even though capable of repressing those rakhsasas by himself, it is for the welfare of your son that he is here requesting you to spare him".

shloka_text: इति मुनिवचनात्प्रसन्नचित्तो रघुवृषभस्तु मुमोद भास्वराङ्ग:। गमनमभिरुरोच राघवस्य प्रथितयशा: कुशिकात्मजाय बुध्या।।1.21.21।।
transliteration: iti munivacanātprasannacitto raghuvṛṣabhastu mumoda bhāsvarāṅga:| gamanamabhiruroca rāghavasya prathitayaśā: kuśikātmajāya budhyā
translation: रघुवृषभ: the foremost of Raghus, इति in this manner, मुनिवचनात् by the words of sage Vasishta, प्रसन्नचित्त: with composed mind, भास्वराङ्ग: has a shining body, मुमोद well pleased, प्रथितयशा: one with manifested fame, कुशिकात्मजाय for Visvamitra, राघवस्य गमनम् for taking Rama, बुध्या with his mind, अभिरुरोच consented.
explanation: Satisfied in his mind at the words of the sage (Vasishta), the full one among the Raghus' (Dasaratha) one with wide reputation, his frame shining gave his cheerful consent to the son of Kusika for Rama's departure. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे एकविंशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the twentyfirst sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तथा वसिष्ठे ब्रुवति राजा दशरथस्सुतम प्रहृष्टवदनो राममाजुहाव सलक्ष्मणम्।।1.22.1।।
transliteration: tathā vasiṣṭhe bruvati rājā daśarathassutama prahṛṣṭavadano rāmamājuhāva salakṣmaṇam
translation: वसिष्ठे when Vasistha, तथा in that manner, ब्रुवति having said, राजा the king, दशरथ: Dasaratha, प्रहृष्टवदन: with cheerful countenance, स्वयम् himself, सलक्ष्मणम् along with Lakshmana, रामम् Rama, आजुहाव summoned.
explanation: Vasishta having said thus, king Dasaratha, with cheerful countenance summoned Rama and Lakshmana.
comments: Dasaratha sends Rama and Lakshmana with Viswamitra--Viswamitra confers knowledge of bala and atibala to Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: कृतस्वस्त्ययनं मात्रा पित्रा दशरथेन च। पुरोधसा वसिष्ठेन मङ्गलैरभिमन्त्रितम्।।1.22.2।। स पुत्रं मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय राजा दशरथ: प्रियम्। ददौ कुशिकपुत्राय सुप्रीतेनान्तरात्मना।।1.22.3।।
transliteration: kṛtasvastyayanaṃ mātrā pitrā daśarathena ca| purodhasā vasiṣṭhena maṅgalairabhimantritam sa putraṃ mūrdhnyupāghrāya rājā daśaratha: priyam| dadau kuśikaputrāya suprītenāntarātmanā
translation: स: दशरथ: राजा that king Dasaratha, मात्रा by mother, पित्रा दशरथेन च by father Dasaratha (by himself), कृतस्वस्त्ययनम् giving farewell by recitation of mantras for securing prosperity and averting evils, पुरोधसा वसिष्ठेन by priest Vasishta, मङ्गलै: by auspicious, अभिमन्त्रितम् making sacred by recitation of special mantras, प्रियम् पुत्रम् affectionate son, मूर्ध्नि on the forehead, उपाघ्राय having kissed, सुप्रीतेन with a pleased, अन्तरात्मना heart, कुशिकपुत्राय for kusika's son, ददौ delivered Rama (to the care of Viswamitra).
explanation: Rama was given farewell by his parents with recitation of mantras (for securing prosperity and averting evils). Priest Vasishta sanctified him with mantras Dasaratha kissed his son on the forehead and delivered him to the care of Viswamitra, with a heart full of cheer.

shloka_text: कृतस्वस्त्ययनं मात्रा पित्रा दशरथेन च। पुरोधसा वसिष्ठेन मङ्गलैरभिमन्त्रितम्।।1.22.2।। स पुत्रं मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय राजा दशरथ: प्रियम्। ददौ कुशिकपुत्राय सुप्रीतेनान्तरात्मना।।1.22.3।।
transliteration: kṛtasvastyayanaṃ mātrā pitrā daśarathena ca| purodhasā vasiṣṭhena maṅgalairabhimantritam sa putraṃ mūrdhnyupāghrāya rājā daśaratha: priyam| dadau kuśikaputrāya suprītenāntarātmanā
translation: स: दशरथ: राजा that king Dasaratha, मात्रा by mother, पित्रा दशरथेन च by father Dasaratha (by himself), कृतस्वस्त्ययनम् giving farewell by recitation of mantras for securing prosperity and averting evils, पुरोधसा वसिष्ठेन by priest Vasishta, मङ्गलै: by auspicious, अभिमन्त्रितम् making sacred by recitation of special mantras, प्रियम् पुत्रम् affectionate son, मूर्ध्नि on the forehead, उपाघ्राय having kissed, सुप्रीतेन with a pleased, अन्तरात्मना heart, कुशिकपुत्राय for kusika's son, ददौ delivered Rama (to the care of Viswamitra).
explanation: Rama was given farewell by his parents with recitation of mantras (for securing prosperity and averting evils). Priest Vasishta sanctified him with mantras Dasaratha kissed his son on the forehead and delivered him to the care of Viswamitra, with a heart full of cheer.

shloka_text: ततो वायुस्सुखस्पर्शो नीरजस्को ववौ तदा। विश्वामित्रगतं दृष्ट्वा रामं राजीवलोचनम्।।1.22.4।।
transliteration: tato vāyussukhasparśo nīrajasko vavau tadā| viśvāmitragataṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ rājīvalocanam
translation: तत: then, राजीवलोचनम् lotuseyed, रामम् Rama, विश्वामित्रगतम् going with Visvamitra, दृष्ट्वा havingseen, तदा then, वायु: wind, सुखस्पर्श: with agreeable touch, नीरजस्क: without pollen, ववौ breezed.
explanation: At the sight of the lotuseyed Rama accompanying Viswamitra, the wind blew pollenfree with a gentle touch.

shloka_text: पुष्पवृष्टिर्महत्यासीद्देवदुन्दुभिनिस्वनै:। शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोष: प्रयाते तु महात्मनि।।1.22.5।।
transliteration: puṣpavṛṣṭirmahatyāsīddevadundubhinisvanai:| śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣa: prayāte tu mahātmani
translation: महात्मनि glorious Visvamitra, प्रयाते तु when he had departed, महती incessant, पुष्पवृष्टि: showers of flowers, देवदुन्दुभिनिस्वनै: with the sounds of celestial drums, शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोष: आसीत् sounds of blowing conches and beating drums arose.
explanation: The departure of glorious Viswamitra was greeted with incessant showers of flowers, the beating of celestial drums and the blowing of conches.

shloka_text: विश्वामित्रो ययावग्रे ततो रामो धनुर्धर:। काकपक्षधरो धन्वी तं च सौमित्रिरन्वगात्।।1.22.6।।
transliteration: viśvāmitro yayāvagre tato rāmo dhanurdhara:| kākapakṣadharo dhanvī taṃ ca saumitriranvagāt
translation: विश्वामित्र: Viswamitra, अग्रे in the forefront, ययौ walked, तत: behind him, धनुर्धर: with bow in his hand, राम: Rama (followed), काकपक्षधर: having side locks of hair, धन्वी an archer, सौमित्रि: Sumitra's son Lakshmana, तम् अन्वगात् followed him.
explanation: Viswamitra walked in the forefront. Behind him was Rama, bow in hand, while in the archer, Sumitra's son (Lakshmana) with side locks of hair followed.

shloka_text: कलापिनौ धनुष्पाणी शोभमानौ दिशो दश । विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं त्रिशीर्षाविव पन्नगौ।।1.22.7।। अनुजग्मतुरक्षुद्रौ पितामहमिवाश्विनौ।
transliteration: kalāpinau dhanuṣpāṇī śobhamānau diśo daśa | viśvāmitraṃ mahātmānaṃ triśīrṣāviva pannagau anujagmaturakṣudrau pitāmahamivāśvinau|
translation: कलापिनौ equipped with quivers, धनुष्पाणी the twain with bows in their hands, दश दिश: in ten cardinal points, शोभमानौ illuminating, अक्षुद्रौ warriors of not a little prowess and splendour, त्रिशीर्षौ three hooded, पन्नगौ इव resembling two serpents, महात्मानम् magnanimous, विश्वामित्रम् Visvamitra, अश्विनौ twin Aswini devatas, पितामहमिव like Brahma, अनुजग्मतु: followed.
explanation: Rama and Lakshmana equipped with bows and quivers resembled three hooded serpents. Warriors of no less prowess, they illuminated the ten quarters and followed the high souled Viswamitra like twin Aswanikumaras  following the grandsire, Brahma.

shloka_text: तदा कुशिकपुत्रं तु धनुष्पाणी स्वलङ्कृतौ।।1.22.8।। बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणौ खड्गवन्तौ महाद्युती । कुमारौ चारुवपुषौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ   ।।1.22.9।। अनुयातौ श्रिया दीप्तौ शोभयेतामनिन्दितौ। स्थाणुं देवमिवाचिन्त्यं कुमाराविव पावकी ।।1.22.10।।
transliteration: tadā kuśikaputraṃ tu dhanuṣpāṇī svalaṅkṛtau baddhagodhāṅgulitrāṇau khaḍgavantau mahādyutī | kumārau cāruvapuṣau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau    anuyātau śriyā dīptau śobhayetāmaninditau| sthāṇuṃ devamivācintyaṃ kumārāviva pāvakī
translation: तदा then, धनुष्पाणी bows in their hands, स्वलङ्कृतौ wellattired, बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणौ their left arms covered by leather to protect from bowstring and fingers encased in Gauna skin, खड्गवन्तौ armed with scimitars, महाद्युती resplendent, कुमारौ youthful beings, चारुवपुषौ having elegent physique, श्रिया with lustre, दीप्तौ radiating, अनिन्दितौ faultless, भ्रातरौ brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, अनुयातौ following the sage, पावकी born to firegod, कुमारौ sons Skanda and Visakhu, अचिन्त्यम् incomprehensible, देवम् god, स्थाणुम् इव like Iswara, कुशिकपुत्रम् son of Kausika, शोभयेताम् cast their radiance.
explanation: Then bows in hand, wellattired, their fingers encased in mongrel skin, for protection (against the bowstring) armed with scimitars, resplendent, young, handsome the two brothers, Rama and Lakshmana shone unblemished. As they followed sage Viswamitra spreading radiance, they looked like sons of the god of fire, (Skanda and Visakhu) following the  incomprehensible Siva.

shloka_text: तदा कुशिकपुत्रं तु धनुष्पाणी स्वलङ्कृतौ।।1.22.8।। बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणौ खड्गवन्तौ महाद्युती । कुमारौ चारुवपुषौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ   ।।1.22.9।। अनुयातौ श्रिया दीप्तौ शोभयेतामनिन्दितौ। स्थाणुं देवमिवाचिन्त्यं कुमाराविव पावकी ।।1.22.10।।
transliteration: tadā kuśikaputraṃ tu dhanuṣpāṇī svalaṅkṛtau baddhagodhāṅgulitrāṇau khaḍgavantau mahādyutī | kumārau cāruvapuṣau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau    anuyātau śriyā dīptau śobhayetāmaninditau| sthāṇuṃ devamivācintyaṃ kumārāviva pāvakī
translation: तदा then, धनुष्पाणी bows in their hands, स्वलङ्कृतौ wellattired, बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणौ their left arms covered by leather to protect from bowstring and fingers encased in Gauna skin, खड्गवन्तौ armed with scimitars, महाद्युती resplendent, कुमारौ youthful beings, चारुवपुषौ having elegent physique, श्रिया with lustre, दीप्तौ radiating, अनिन्दितौ faultless, भ्रातरौ brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, अनुयातौ following the sage, पावकी born to firegod, कुमारौ sons Skanda and Visakhu, अचिन्त्यम् incomprehensible, देवम् god, स्थाणुम् इव like Iswara, कुशिकपुत्रम् son of Kausika, शोभयेताम् cast their radiance.
explanation: Then bows in hand, wellattired, their fingers encased in mongrel skin, for protection (against the bowstring) armed with scimitars, resplendent, young, handsome the two brothers, Rama and Lakshmana shone unblemished. As they followed sage Viswamitra spreading radiance, they looked like sons of the god of fire, (Skanda and Visakhu) following the  incomprehensible Siva.

shloka_text: तदा कुशिकपुत्रं तु धनुष्पाणी स्वलङ्कृतौ।।1.22.8।। बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणौ खड्गवन्तौ महाद्युती । कुमारौ चारुवपुषौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ   ।।1.22.9।। अनुयातौ श्रिया दीप्तौ शोभयेतामनिन्दितौ। स्थाणुं देवमिवाचिन्त्यं कुमाराविव पावकी ।।1.22.10।।
transliteration: tadā kuśikaputraṃ tu dhanuṣpāṇī svalaṅkṛtau baddhagodhāṅgulitrāṇau khaḍgavantau mahādyutī | kumārau cāruvapuṣau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau    anuyātau śriyā dīptau śobhayetāmaninditau| sthāṇuṃ devamivācintyaṃ kumārāviva pāvakī
translation: तदा then, धनुष्पाणी bows in their hands, स्वलङ्कृतौ wellattired, बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणौ their left arms covered by leather to protect from bowstring and fingers encased in Gauna skin, खड्गवन्तौ armed with scimitars, महाद्युती resplendent, कुमारौ youthful beings, चारुवपुषौ having elegent physique, श्रिया with lustre, दीप्तौ radiating, अनिन्दितौ faultless, भ्रातरौ brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, अनुयातौ following the sage, पावकी born to firegod, कुमारौ sons Skanda and Visakhu, अचिन्त्यम् incomprehensible, देवम् god, स्थाणुम् इव like Iswara, कुशिकपुत्रम् son of Kausika, शोभयेताम् cast their radiance.
explanation: Then bows in hand, wellattired, their fingers encased in mongrel skin, for protection (against the bowstring) armed with scimitars, resplendent, young, handsome the two brothers, Rama and Lakshmana shone unblemished. As they followed sage Viswamitra spreading radiance, they looked like sons of the god of fire, (Skanda and Visakhu) following the  incomprehensible Siva.

shloka_text: अध्यर्धयोजनं गत्वा सरय्वा दक्षिणे तटे। रामेति मधुरां वाणीं विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत।।1.22.11।।
transliteration: adhyardhayojanaṃ gatvā sarayvā dakṣiṇe taṭe| rāmeti madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ viśvāmitro'bhyabhāṣata
translation: अध्यर्धयोजनम् more than a half Yojana, गत्वा having travelled, सरय्वा: river Sarayu, दक्षिणे तटे on southern bank, वश्वामित्र: Viswamitra, राम इति addressing him as "O Rama", मधुराम् sweet, वाणीम् words, अभ्यभाषत spoke.
explanation: After crossing a distance of over half a yojana on the southern bank of Sarayu, Viswamitra addressed Rama sweet in a gentle voice.

shloka_text: गृहाण वत्स सलिलं मा भूत्कालस्य पर्यय:। मन्त्रग्रामं गृहाण त्वं बलामतिबलां तथा।।1.22.12।।
transliteration: gṛhāṇa vatsa salilaṃ mā bhūtkālasya paryaya:| mantragrāmaṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ balāmatibalāṃ tathā
translation: वत्स O Child, सलिलम् water, गृहाण take into your hands, कालस्य पर्यय:माभूत् let  no delay occur, त्वम् you, मन्त्रग्रामम् collection of mantras, तथा and, बलाम् Bala, अतिबलां Atibala, गृहाण receive.
explanation: "O child, take this water (in your hands), let there be no delay. You will receive from me a collection of mantras and also bala and atibala.

shloka_text: न श्रमो न ज्वरो वा ते न रूपस्य विपर्यय:। न च सुप्तं प्रमत्तं वा धर्षयिष्यन्ति नैऱृता:।।1.22.13।।
transliteration: na śramo na jvaro vā te na rūpasya viparyaya:| na ca suptaṃ pramattaṃ vā dharṣayiṣyanti naiṟṛtā:
translation: ते to you, श्रम:न neither fatigue, ज्वरो वा nor fever, रूपस्य विपर्यय: न nor change in appearance, सुप्तम् whether in sleep, प्रमत्तं वा or inattentive condition, नैरृता: rakshasas, न धर्षयिष्यन्ति cannot trouble you.
explanation: "(If you receive these mantras), you will experience neither fatigue, nor fever nor will there be a change in your appearance. Whether you are asleep or agitated, rakshasas cannot harm you.

shloka_text: न बाह्वोस्सदृशो वीर्ये पृथिव्यामस्ति कश्चन। त्रिषु लोकेषु वै राम न भवेत्सदृशस्तव ।।1.22.14।।
transliteration: na bāhvossadṛśo vīrye pṛthivyāmasti kaścana| triṣu lokeṣu vai rāma na bhavetsadṛśastava
translation: राम O Rama, बाह्वो: of your hands, वीर्ये in might, सदृश: parallel man, कश्चन anyone, पृथिव्याम् in this earth, नास्ति does not exist, त्रिषु in the three, लोकेषु worlds, तव सदृश: equal to you, न भवेत् does not exist.
explanation: O Rama, there is none in this world equal to the might of your hands nor does such a person exist in the three worlds.

shloka_text: न सौभाग्ये न दाक्षिण्ये न ज्ञाने बुद्धिनिश्चये। नोत्तरे प्रतिवक्तव्ये समो लोके तवाऽनघ।।1.22.15।।
transliteration: na saubhāgye na dākṣiṇye na jñāne buddhiniścaye| nottare prativaktavye samo loke tavā'nagha
translation: अनघ O Sinless one, सौभाग्ये in auspiciouness, तव सम: equal to  you, लोके in this world, न none, दाक्षिण्ये in kindness, न none, ज्ञाने in wisdom, बुद्धिनिश्चये in decisionmaking, न  none, उत्तरे when a reply, प्रतिवक्तव्ये has to be given, न none.
