explanation: O sinless one, there is none in this world equal to you in good fortune, kindness, wisdom, in taking a decsion or giving a reply.

shloka_text: एतद्विद्याद्वये लब्धे भविता नास्ति ते सम:। बलात्वतिबला चैव सर्वज्ञानस्य मातरौ।।1.22.16।।
transliteration: etadvidyādvaye labdhe bhavitā nāsti te sama:| balātvatibalā caiva sarvajñānasya mātarau
translation: एतद्विद्याद्वये when these two kinds of knowledge, लब्धे सति have been secured, ते सम: equal to you, नास्ति there will not be, न भविता nor going to be in future, बला Bala, अतिबला चैव Atibala also, सर्वज्ञानस्य for all kinds of knowledge, मातरौ mothers.
explanation: With these two kinds of knowledge secured, there will be none equal to you, at present or in fututre. Bala and atibala are  mother to all kinds of knowledge .

shloka_text: क्षुत्पिपासे न ते राम भविष्येते नरोत्तम । बलामतिबलां चैव पठत: पथि राघव।।1.22.17।।
transliteration: kṣutpipāse na te rāma bhaviṣyete narottama | balāmatibalāṃ caiva paṭhata: pathi rāghava
translation: नरोत्तम O Best among men, राघव Oborn in the line of Raghu, राम ORama,पथि on the way, बलाम् Bala, अतिबलां चैव Atibala, पठत: if recited, ते to you, क्षुत्पिपासे hunger or thirst, न भविष्येते will not get.
explanation: O Rama, best among men, scion in the line of Raghu, on your way you will not feel hunger or thirst if you recite bala and atibala.

shloka_text: विद्याद्वयमधीयाने यशश्चाप्यतुलं त्वयि। पितामहसुते ह्येते विद्ये तेजस्समन्विते।।1.22.18।। प्रदातुं तव काकुत्स्थ सदृशस्त्वं हि धार्मिक।
transliteration: vidyādvayamadhīyāne yaśaścāpyatulaṃ tvayi| pitāmahasute hyete vidye tejassamanvite pradātuṃ tava kākutstha sadṛśastvaṃ hi dhārmika|
translation: विद्याद्वयम् these two sciences, अधीयाने when pursued, त्वयि by you, अतुलम् unequalled, यशश्च fame, ककुत्स्थ ORama, born in the line Kakutstha, धार्मिक one who conforms to justice, तेजस्समन्विते both possessed of virtues, पितामहसुते two daughters of grand sire, Brahma, एते विद्ये these sciences, तव to you, प्रदातुम् conferring, त्वम् you, सदृश: fit person.
explanation: O Rama, born in the line Kakutstha and one who is righteous, these two radiant sciences are daughters of the grandsire Brahma. If you pursue these two sciences, you will get unequalled fame. You are a fit person to confer these two sciences.

shloka_text: कामं बहुगुणास्सर्वे त्वय्येते नात्र संशय:। तपसा सम्भृते चैते बहुरूपे भविष्यत:।।1.22.19।।
transliteration: kāmaṃ bahuguṇāssarve tvayyete nātra saṃśaya:| tapasā sambhṛte caite bahurūpe bhaviṣyata:
translation: एते बहुगुणा: these many qualities, सर्वे all, कामम् very-well, त्वयि in you, अत्र in this matter, संशय: न no doubt, तपसा with asceticism, सम्भृते nourished, एते these two sciences, बहुरूपे multiple forms, भविष्यत: will assume.
explanation: You possess all these qualities in great measure. There is no doubt that If these two sciences (mantras) are nourished with austerities they will assume multiple forms (and benefit you)".

shloka_text: ततो रामो जलं स्पृष्ट्वा प्रहृष्टवदनश्शुचि:। प्रतिजग्राह ते विद्ये महर्षेर्भावितात्मन:।।1.22.20।।
transliteration: tato rāmo jalaṃ spṛṣṭvā prahṛṣṭavadanaśśuci:| pratijagrāha te vidye maharṣerbhāvitātmana:
translation: तत: thereafter, राम: Rama, जलम् water, स्पृष्ट्वा having touched, शुचि: got purified, प्रहृष्टवदन: with happy coutenance, भावितात्मन: one who has perceived the supreme soul, महर्षे: from maharshi, ते विद्ये those two sciences, प्रतिजग्राह received.
explanation: Thereafter Rama, touched the water and was sanctified. With a cheerful face he received those two sciences from the maharshi who had perceived the supreme soul.

shloka_text: विद्यासमुदितो रामश्शुशुभे भूरिविक्रम:। सहस्ररश्मिर्भगवान् शरदीव दिवाकर:।।1.22.21।। गुरुकार्याणि सर्वाणि नियुज्य कुशिकात्मजे। ऊषुस्तां रजनीं तत्र सरय्वां सुसुखं त्रय:।।1.22.22।।
transliteration: vidyāsamudito rāmaśśuśubhe bhūrivikrama:| sahasraraśmirbhagavān śaradīva divākara: gurukāryāṇi sarvāṇi niyujya kuśikātmaje| ūṣustāṃ rajanīṃ tatra sarayvāṃ susukhaṃ traya:
translation: भूरिविक्रम: a highly valiant hero, राम: Rama, विद्यासमुदित: possessed of the knowledge of the two sciences, कुशिकात्मजे in the matter of Visvamitra, सर्वाणि all, गुरुकार्याणि services  to be rendered in relation to a preceptor, नियुज्य having performed, शरदि like in autumnal season, सहस्ररश्मि: (Sun) emitting thousand rays, भगवान् दिवाकर:इव  resembling Sungod, शुशुभे appeared resplendent, त्रय: the three men, तत्र there, सरय्वाम् on the bank of river Sarayu, ससुखम् with great comfort, तां रजनीम् that night, ऊषु: dwelt.
explanation: . Rama, the highly heroic  after acquiring knowledge (of the two sciences) and having rendered all services to preceptor Viswamitra, appeared resplendent like the Sungod in autumn. There the three of them spent the night comfortably on the bank of Sarayu.

shloka_text: विद्यासमुदितो रामश्शुशुभे भूरिविक्रम:। सहस्ररश्मिर्भगवान् शरदीव दिवाकर:।।1.22.21।। गुरुकार्याणि सर्वाणि नियुज्य कुशिकात्मजे। ऊषुस्तां रजनीं तत्र सरय्वां सुसुखं त्रय:।।1.22.22।।
transliteration: vidyāsamudito rāmaśśuśubhe bhūrivikrama:| sahasraraśmirbhagavān śaradīva divākara: gurukāryāṇi sarvāṇi niyujya kuśikātmaje| ūṣustāṃ rajanīṃ tatra sarayvāṃ susukhaṃ traya:
translation: भूरिविक्रम: a highly valiant hero, राम: Rama, विद्यासमुदित: possessed of the knowledge of the two sciences, कुशिकात्मजे in the matter of Visvamitra, सर्वाणि all, गुरुकार्याणि services  to be rendered in relation to a preceptor, नियुज्य having performed, शरदि like in autumnal season, सहस्ररश्मि: (Sun) emitting thousand rays, भगवान् दिवाकर:इव  resembling Sungod, शुशुभे appeared resplendent, त्रय: the three men, तत्र there, सरय्वाम् on the bank of river Sarayu, ससुखम् with great comfort, तां रजनीम् that night, ऊषु: dwelt.
explanation: . Rama, the highly heroic  after acquiring knowledge (of the two sciences) and having rendered all services to preceptor Viswamitra, appeared resplendent like the Sungod in autumn. There the three of them spent the night comfortably on the bank of Sarayu.

shloka_text: दशरथनृपसूनुसत्तमाभ्यां तृणशयनेऽनुचिते सहोषिताभ्याम्। कुशिकसुतवचोऽनुलालिताभ्यां सुखमिव सा विबभौ विभावरी च।।1.22.23।।
transliteration: daśarathanṛpasūnusattamābhyāṃ tṛṇaśayane'nucite sahoṣitābhyām| kuśikasutavaco'nulālitābhyāṃ sukhamiva sā vibabhau vibhāvarī ca
translation: अनुचिते unaccustomed, तृणशयने on the bed of grass, सहोषिताभ्याम् by those two who slept together, कुशिकसुतवचोऽनुलालिताभ्याम् who were put in good humour by the gentle words of Visvamitra, दशरथनृपसूनुसत्तमाभ्याम् by the two eminent sons of Dasaratha (Rama and Lakshmana), सा विभावरी च that night also, सुखमिव as if with comfort, विबभौ occured to their mind.
explanation: The night was spent as though with comfort by the two eminent sons of Dasaratha, who shared the unaccustomed bed of grass. They were kept in good humour by the words of Kusika's son. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे द्वाविंशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the twenty second sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां विश्वामित्रो महामुनि:। अभ्यभाषत काकुत्स्थौ शयानौ पर्णसंस्तरे।।1.23.1।।
transliteration: prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ viśvāmitro mahāmuni:| abhyabhāṣata kākutsthau śayānau parṇasaṃstare
translation: शर्वर्याम् when the night, प्रभातायाम् turned into day break, महामुनि: eminent ascetic, विश्वामित्र: Visvamitra, पर्णसंस्तरे in the bed of leaves, शयानौ lying down, काकुत्स्थौ Rama and Lakshmana, अभ्यभाषत spoke.
explanation: When the night turned into daybreak, the eminent ascetic Viswamitra, addressing the descendants of Kakutstha (Rama and Lakshmana) who were lying on a bed of leaves said:
comments: Accompanied by Rama and Lakshmana, Viswamitra reaches the hermitage of Kama at the confluence of Sarayu and Ganga.

shloka_text: कौसल्या सुप्रजा राम पूर्वा सन्ध्या प्रवर्तते। उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल कर्तव्यं दैवमाह्निकम्।।1.23.2।।
transliteration: kausalyā suprajā rāma pūrvā sandhyā pravartate| uttiṣṭha naraśārdūla kartavyaṃ daivamāhnikam
translation: कैसल्या सुप्रजा: OBeloved son of Kausalya, (a son by whom Kausalya became a blessed mother), राम ORama, पूर्वा सन्ध्या the daybreak, प्रवर्तते is commencing ,नरशार्दूल OBest among men, उत्तिष्ठ awake (fromsleep), दैवम् oblations to gods, आह्निकम् religious rite  to be performed every day at a fixed hour, कर्तव्यम् are required to be done.
explanation: "O beloved son of Kausalya, O Rama the day dawns. O best among men, awake, oblations to gods and other sacred rites are required to be performed".

shloka_text: तस्यर्षे: परमोदारं वचश्श्रुत्वा नृपात्मजौ । स्नात्वा कृतोदकौ वीरौ जेपतु: परमं जपम्।।1.23.3।।
transliteration: tasyarṣe: paramodāraṃ vacaśśrutvā nṛpātmajau | snātvā kṛtodakau vīrau jepatu: paramaṃ japam
translation: वीरौ endowed with heroism, नृपात्मजौ the two princes, तस्य ऋषे: that rishi's, परमोदारम् highly generous, वच: words, श्रुत्वा having heard, स्नात्वा having bathed, कृतोदकौ offered  oblations of waters(to Sungod standing in the water), परमम् holy, जपम् tapa, जेपतु: recited.
explanation: On hearing the very affectionate call of Viswamitra both the brave princes had their bath and offered oblations to Sungod (standing in the water) and recited the holy name of the Lord.

shloka_text: कृताह्निकौ महावीर्यौ विश्वामित्रं तपोधनम्। अभिवाद्याभिसंहृष्टौ गमनायाभितस्थतु:।।1.23.4।।
transliteration: kṛtāhnikau mahāvīryau viśvāmitraṃ tapodhanam| abhivādyābhisaṃhṛṣṭau gamanāyābhitasthatu:
translation: महावीर्यौ both(brothers)exceedingly powerful, कृताह्निकौ having performed daily rites, अभिसंहृष्टौ highly energetic, तपोधनम् a sage with asceticism as wealth, विश्वामित्रम् Visvamitra, अभिवाद्य having prostrated before him with reverence, गमनाय for their onward journey, अभितस्थतु: both of them stood ready before him.
explanation: On performing the morning rites, the two highly powerful and and energetic princes stood before Viswamitra who was richly endowed with asceticism. They prostrated before him. And stood ready for their onward journey.

shloka_text: तौ प्रयातौ महावीर्यौ दिव्यां त्रिपथगां नदीम्। ददृशाते ततस्तत्र सरय्वास्सङ्गमे शुभे।।1.23.5।।
transliteration: tau prayātau mahāvīryau divyāṃ tripathagāṃ nadīm| dadṛśāte tatastatra sarayvāssaṅgame śubhe
translation: तत: thereafter, महावीर्यौ तौ those two endowed with great prowess, प्रयातौ (they)having gone a little further, तत्र there, शुभे by the holy, सरय्वा: river Sarayu, सङ्गमे in the confluence (with river Ganga), दिव्यां divine, त्रिपथगां flowing in three branches, नदीम् river, ददृशाते saw.
explanation: Thereafter, having gone a little further both the heroic brothers looked at the confluence of holy  Sarayu with  divine Ganga divided into three branches.

shloka_text: तत्राश्रमपदं पुण्यमृषीणामग्य्रतेजसाम् । बहुवर्षसहस्राणि तप्यतां परमं तप:।।1.23.6।।
transliteration: tatrāśramapadaṃ puṇyamṛṣīṇāmagyratejasām | bahuvarṣasahasrāṇi tapyatāṃ paramaṃ tapa:
translation: तत्र there, बहुवर्षसहस्राणि for many thousands of years, परमम् utmost, तप: austerities, तप्यताम् while performing austerities, अग्य्रतेजसाम् sages of topmost vital power, ऋषीणाम् of the  anchorites, पुण्यम् sacred, आश्रमपदम् hermitage.
explanation: There they saw a sacred hermitage of anchorites of great vitality performing severe austerities for thousands of years.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीतौ राघवौ पुण्यमाश्रमम्। ऊचतुस्तं महात्मानं विश्वामित्रमिदं वच:।।1.23.7।।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaprītau rāghavau puṇyamāśramam| ūcatustaṃ mahātmānaṃ viśvāmitramidaṃ vaca:
translation: तम् that, पुण्यम् sacred, आश्रमम् hermitage, दृष्ट्वा having seen, परमप्रीतौ exceedingly delighted, राघवौ the two princes of Raghu race, महात्मानम् illustrious sage, तं विश्वामित्रम् addressing Visvamitra, इदम् वच: these words, ऊचतु: said.
explanation: Exceedingly delighted to see the sacred hermitage, the two princes enquired from the illustrious sage Viswamitra:

shloka_text: कस्यायमाश्रम: पुण्य: कोन्वस्मिन्वसते पुमान्। भगवन् श्रोतुमिच्छाव: परं कौतूहलं हि नौ।।1.23.8।।
transliteration: kasyāyamāśrama: puṇya: konvasminvasate pumān| bhagavan śrotumicchāva: paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi nau
translation: भगवन् O Worshipful one, अयम् this, पुण्य:आश्रम: sacred hermitage, कस्य whose, अस्मिन् in this, क: नु who indeed, पुमान् man, वसते lives, श्रोतुम् to hear, इच्छाव: we both are desirous, नौ for both of us, परम् keenly, कौतूहलं हि curiosity.
explanation: "O worshipful one, whose sacred hermitage is this? Who lives here? Indeed, we are curious to know".

shloka_text: तयोस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य मुनिपुङ्गव:। अब्रवीच्छ्रूयतां राम यस्यायं पूर्व आश्रम:।।1.23.9 ।।
transliteration: tayostadvacanaṃ śrutvā prahasya munipuṅgava:| abravīcchrūyatāṃ rāma yasyāyaṃ pūrva āśrama:
translation: मुनिपुङ्गव: the foremost of sages, तयो: theirs, तत् वचनम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, प्रहस्य after gently smiling, अब्रवीत् said, पूर्व: in the days past, अयम् आश्रम: this heritage, यस्य whose, श्रूयताम् let it be heard.
explanation: On having heard their words, the foremost of sages gently smiled and said, "O Rama listen, who this hermitage belonged to in the past".

shloka_text: कन्दर्पो मूर्तिमानासीत्काम इत्युच्यते बुधै:। तपस्यन्तमिह स्थाणुं नियमेन समाहितम्।।1.23.10।। कृतोद्वाहं तु देवेशं गच्छन्तं समरुद्गगणम्। धर्षयामास दुर्मेधा हुङ्कृतश्च महात्मना।।1.23.11।।
transliteration: kandarpo mūrtimānāsītkāma ityucyate budhai:| tapasyantamiha sthāṇuṃ niyamena samāhitam kṛtodvāhaṃ tu deveśaṃ gacchantaṃ samarudgagaṇam| dharṣayāmāsa durmedhā huṅkṛtaśca mahātmanā
translation: कन्दर्प: Kandarpa also known as Manmatha, मूर्तिमान् incarnated in human form, आसीत् lived, बुधै: by the learned, काम: इति उच्यते is called Kama, दुर्मेधा: foolish minded, इह here, तपस्यन्तम् while doing penance, नियमेन in accordance with rules, समाहितम् absorbed in meditation, कृतोद्वाहम् with his newly wedded wife, समरुद्गगणम् accompanied by maruts, गच्छन्तम् wending his way, देवेशम् lord of deities, स्थाणुम् Siva, धर्षयामास opposed him, महात्मना by Lord Siva, हुङ्कृतश्च roared in menacing sound.
explanation: "Kandarpa (the god of love) once lived here in human form. He is called Kama by the learned. The wicked Kama on his way with the maruts (god of wind) insulted Siva, the god of gods, while he was absorbed in austere meditation along with his newly wedded consort. On seeing Kama Lord Siva roared at him (menacingly).

shloka_text: कन्दर्पो मूर्तिमानासीत्काम इत्युच्यते बुधै:। तपस्यन्तमिह स्थाणुं नियमेन समाहितम्।।1.23.10।। कृतोद्वाहं तु देवेशं गच्छन्तं समरुद्गगणम्। धर्षयामास दुर्मेधा हुङ्कृतश्च महात्मना।।1.23.11।।
transliteration: kandarpo mūrtimānāsītkāma ityucyate budhai:| tapasyantamiha sthāṇuṃ niyamena samāhitam kṛtodvāhaṃ tu deveśaṃ gacchantaṃ samarudgagaṇam| dharṣayāmāsa durmedhā huṅkṛtaśca mahātmanā
translation: कन्दर्प: Kandarpa also known as Manmatha, मूर्तिमान् incarnated in human form, आसीत् lived, बुधै: by the learned, काम: इति उच्यते is called Kama, दुर्मेधा: foolish minded, इह here, तपस्यन्तम् while doing penance, नियमेन in accordance with rules, समाहितम् absorbed in meditation, कृतोद्वाहम् with his newly wedded wife, समरुद्गगणम् accompanied by maruts, गच्छन्तम् wending his way, देवेशम् lord of deities, स्थाणुम् Siva, धर्षयामास opposed him, महात्मना by Lord Siva, हुङ्कृतश्च roared in menacing sound.
explanation: "Kandarpa (the god of love) once lived here in human form. He is called Kama by the learned. The wicked Kama on his way with the maruts (god of wind) insulted Siva, the god of gods, while he was absorbed in austere meditation along with his newly wedded consort. On seeing Kama Lord Siva roared at him (menacingly).

shloka_text: अवदग्धस्य रौद्रेण चक्षुषा रघुनन्दन। व्यशीर्यन्त शरीरात्स्वात्सर्वगात्राणि दुर्मते:।।1.23.12।।
transliteration: avadagdhasya raudreṇa cakṣuṣā raghunandana| vyaśīryanta śarīrātsvātsarvagātrāṇi durmate:
translation: रघुनन्दन O Descendent of Raghu, रौद्रेण with fierce, चक्षुषा (third)eye, अवदग्धस्य he was  burnt down, दुर्मते: of the evil intentioned Kama, स्वात् from his own, शरीरात् body, सर्वगात्राणि all the limbs, व्यशीर्यन्त were consumed.
explanation: "O descendant of Raghu, burnt down by his fierce (third) eye, all the limbs of the body of that evilminded Kama were consumed.

shloka_text: तस्य गात्रं हतं तत्र निर्दग्थस्य महात्मना। अशरीर: कृत: काम: क्रोधाद्देवेश्वरेण हि।।1.23.13।।
transliteration: tasya gātraṃ hataṃ tatra nirdagthasya mahātmanā| aśarīra: kṛta: kāma: krodhāddeveśvareṇa hi
translation: महात्मना by that lord Siva, निर्दग्थस्य having burnt down totally, तस्य his, गात्रम् body, तत्र there, हतम् disappeared, देवेश्वरेण by the lord of devatas, क्रोधात् because of wrath, काम: Kama, अशरीर: disembodied, कृत: had been made.
explanation: Having been completely burnt down by Lord Siva, Kama's body was destroyed. Mighty angry, Siva, reduced Kama to a 'disembodied being.

shloka_text: अनङ्ग इति विख्यातस्तदाप्रभृति राघव। स चाङ्गविषयश्श्रीमान्यत्राङ्गं प्रमुमोच ह।।1.23.14।।
transliteration: anaṅga iti vikhyātastadāprabhṛti rāghava| sa cāṅgaviṣayaśśrīmānyatrāṅgaṃ pramumoca ha
translation: राघव O Rama, तदाप्रभृति from that time onwards, अनङ्ग इति as Ananga, विख्यात: had become wellknown, यत्र where, अङ्गम् body, प्रमुमोच ह he gave up, स:च that place, श्रीमान् beautiful, अङ्गविषय: Ananga desa, विख्यात: famed.
explanation: O descendant of the Raghus, from that time onwards, he was known as 'Ananga' (one without form). The  beautiful place where he gave up his body is known as Angadesa.

shloka_text: तस्यायमाश्रम: पुण्यस्तस्येमे मुनय: पुरा। शिष्या धर्मपरा नित्यं तेषां पापं न विद्यते।।1.23.15।।
transliteration: tasyāyamāśrama: puṇyastasyeme munaya: purā| śiṣyā dharmaparā nityaṃ teṣāṃ pāpaṃ na vidyate
translation: अयम् this, तस्य his, पुण्य: holy, आश्रम: hermitage, पुरा formerly, तस्य his, शिष्या: disciples, इमे मुनय: these ascetics, नित्यम् always, धर्मपरा: righteous, तेषाम् for them, पापम् sin, न विद्यते does not accrue.
explanation: This holy hermitage belongs to Kama. These ascetics are his disciples. They are  always righteous and are free from sin.

shloka_text: इहाद्य रजनीं राम वसेम शुभदर्शन। पुण्ययोस्सरितोर्मध्ये श्वस्तरिष्यामहे वयम्।।1.23.16।।
transliteration: ihādya rajanīṃ rāma vasema śubhadarśana| puṇyayossaritormadhye śvastariṣyāmahe vayam
translation: शुभदर्शन OAuspicious looking one, राम Rama, वयम् we, अद्य today, रजनीम् this night, इह here, पुण्ययो: of both the sacred, सरितो: rivers, मध्ये in the midst, वसेम shall stay, श्व: tomorrow, तरिष्यामहे cross over.
explanation: O auspiciouslooking Rama, we will stay here tonight at the confluence of both these sacred rivers (Sarayu and Ganga) and cross over Ganga tomorrow.

shloka_text: अभिगच्छामहे सर्वे शुचय: पुण्यमाश्रमम्। स्नाताश्च कृतजप्याश्च हुतहव्या नरोत्तम।।1.23.17।।
transliteration: abhigacchāmahe sarve śucaya: puṇyamāśramam| snātāśca kṛtajapyāśca hutahavyā narottama
translation: नरोत्तम O Chief of men, सर्वे all of us, स्नाताश्च have taken bath, कृतजप्याश्च have  performed Japa (muttering god's sacred name severally), हुतहव्या: offered oblations in fire, शुचय: pure, पुण्यम् pious, आश्रमम् hermitage, अभिगच्छामहे  we will enter.
explanation: O best of men, after morning ablutions offering oblations to the sacred fire, all of us sanctified will enter this pious hermitage".

shloka_text: तेषां संवदतां तत्र तपोदीर्घेण चक्षुषा। विज्ञाय परमप्रीता मुनयो हर्षमागमन्।।1.23.18।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ saṃvadatāṃ tatra tapodīrgheṇa cakṣuṣā| vijñāya paramaprītā munayo harṣamāgaman
translation: तत्र there, तेषाम् they, संवदताम् were conversing, मुनय: ascetics, तपोदीर्घेण with their far reaching austerities, चक्षुषा vision, विज्ञाय having recognised them, परमप्रीता: immensely pleased, हर्षम् delight, आगमन् obtained.
explanation: As they were conversing thus, the ascetics, with their far reaching spiritual vision (beyond the veil of time) recognised them and were immensely pleased.

shloka_text: अर्घ्यं पाद्यं तथाऽतिथ्यं निवेद्य कुशिकात्मजे। रामलक्ष्मणयो: पश्चादकुर्वन्नतिथिक्रियाम्।।1.23.19।।
transliteration: arghyaṃ pādyaṃ tathā'tithyaṃ nivedya kuśikātmaje| rāmalakṣmaṇayo: paścādakurvannatithikriyām
translation: अर्घ्यम् respectable offerings, पाद्यम् water for washing feet, तथा and, आतिथ्यम् hospitality, कुशिकात्मजे to Visvamitra, निवेद्य having offered, पश्चात् thereafter, रामलक्ष्मणयो: for Rama and Lakshmana, अतिथिक्रियाम् acts of hospitality, अकुर्वन् performed.
explanation: After extending hospitality to the son of Kusika (Viswamitra) with respectful offerings, and water for washing feet they played the host to Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: सत्कारं समनुप्राप्य कथाभिरभिरञ्जयन्। यथार्हमजपन् सन्ध्यामृषयस्ते समाहिता:।।1.23.20।।
transliteration: satkāraṃ samanuprāpya kathābhirabhirañjayan| yathārhamajapan sandhyāmṛṣayaste samāhitā:
translation: सत्कारम् hospitality, समनुप्राप्य having received, कथाभि: with their conversation, अभिरञ्जयन् delighted, ते ऋषय: those rishis, समाहिता: with composed minds, यथार्हम् in accordance with tradition, सन्ध्याम् evening prayers, अजपन् recited.
explanation: Having received due hospitality, they delighted them (ascetics) with their talk. The rishis with composed minds recited their evening prayer as usual.

shloka_text: तत्र वासिभिरानीता मुनिभिस्सुव्रतै: सह। न्यवसन् सुसुखं तत्र कामाश्रमपदे तदा।।1.23.21।।
transliteration: tatra vāsibhirānītā munibhissuvratai: saha| nyavasan susukhaṃ tatra kāmāśramapade tadā
translation: तत्र there, वासिभि: by the residents, सुव्रतै: by those faithful to their vows, मुनिभि: ascetics, सह along with them, आनीता: having been brought, तदा then, तत्र there, कामाश्रमपदे in Kama's hermitage, सुसुखम् happily, न्यवसन् dwelt .
explanation: The ascetics who resided there, faithful to their vows, took them in. There they staed happily  in Kama's hermitage.

shloka_text: कथाभिरभिरामाभिरभिरामौ नृपात्मजौ। रमयामास धर्मात्मा कौशिको मुनिपुङ्गव:।।1.23.22।।
transliteration: kathābhirabhirāmābhirabhirāmau nṛpātmajau| ramayāmāsa dharmātmā kauśiko munipuṅgava:
translation: धर्मात्मा the magnanimous, मुनिपुङ्गव: foremost of ascetics, कौशिक: son of Kusika, अभिरामौ charming, नृपात्मजौ princes, अभिरामाभि: by enchanting, कथाभि: tales, रमयामास delighted them.
explanation: Foremost among the ascetics the son of Kusika (Viswamitra) delighted the charming  princes with enchanting tales. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे त्रयोविंशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the twentythird sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तत: प्रभाते विमले कृताह्निकमरिन्दमौ। विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य नद्यास्तीरमुपागतौ।।1.24.1।।
transliteration: tata: prabhāte vimale kṛtāhnikamarindamau| viśvāmitraṃ puraskṛtya nadyāstīramupāgatau
translation: तत: thereafter, अरिन्दमौ two destroyers of enemies, विमले on a pure, प्रभाते daybreak, कृताह्निकम् by observing daily oblations, विश्वामित्रम् Viswamitra, पुरस्कृत्य ahead of them नद्या: river's, तीरम्  bank, उपागतौ arrived.
explanation: Thereafter the destroyers of foes, Rama and Lakshmana offering their morning oblations on that bright dawn arrived at the bank of the river (Ganga) with Viswamitra ahead of them.
comments: While crossing the river Rama asks "What is this tumultuous sound gushing from the Ganga?"--Viswamitra gives the reply--The trio enter the forest -- Viswamitra narrates the story of Tataka.

shloka_text: ते च सर्वे महात्मानो मुनयस्संश्रितव्रता:। उपस्थाप्य शुभां नावं विश्वामित्रमथाब्रुवन्।।1.24.2।।
transliteration: te ca sarve mahātmāno munayassaṃśritavratā:| upasthāpya śubhāṃ nāvaṃ viśvāmitramathābruvan
translation: महात्मान: highminded, संश्रितव्रता: strict observers of vows, ते सर्वे all those, मुनय: ascetics, शुभाम् auspicious, नावम् boat, उपस्थाप्य kept ready, अथ there after, विश्वामित्रम् addressed Visvamitra, अब्रुवन् saying.
explanation: All the highminded ascetics and strict followers of vows secured an auspicious boat for them and addressed Viswamitra, saying:

shloka_text: आरोहतु भवान्नावं राजपुत्रपुरस्कृत:। अरिष्टं गच्छ पन्थानं मा भूत्कालविपर्यय:।।1.24.3।।
transliteration: ārohatu bhavānnāvaṃ rājaputrapuraskṛta:| ariṣṭaṃ gaccha panthānaṃ mā bhūtkālaviparyaya:
translation: भवान् O Great rishi, राजपुत्रपुरस्कृत: with the princes ahead of you, नावम् boat, आरोहतु you may board it, अरिष्टम् devoid of evils, पन्थानम् path, गच्छ go, कालविपर्यय: loss of time,  माभूत् let not take place.
explanation: With the princes ahead of you, board the boat. Tread the safe path. Let there be no loss of time.

shloka_text: विश्वामित्रस्तथेत्युक्तवा तानृषीनभिपूज्य च। ततार सहितस्ताभ्यां सरितं सागरङ्गमाम्।।1.24.4।।
transliteration: viśvāmitrastathetyuktavā tānṛṣīnabhipūjya ca| tatāra sahitastābhyāṃ saritaṃ sāgaraṅgamām
translation: विश्वामित्र: Visvamitra, तथेति 'so be it', उक्त्वा having said, तान् ऋषीन् all those sages, अभिपूज्य having worshipped, ताभ्याम् by Rama and Lakshmana, सहित: accompanied by, सागरङ्गमाम् flowing towards the sea, सरितम् river Ganga, ततार crossed.
explanation: "Be it so", said Viswamitra and paid respect to all those sages. And accompanied by them (Rama and Lakshmana), crossed the river flowing towards the sea.

shloka_text: ततश्शुश्राव वै शब्दमतिसंरम्भवर्धितम्। मध्यमागम्य तोयस्य सह राम:कनीयसा।।1.24.5।।
transliteration: tataśśuśrāva vai śabdamatisaṃrambhavardhitam| madhyamāgamya toyasya saha rāma:kanīyasā
translation: तत: then, राम: Rama, तोयस्य of  the water, मध्यम् midst, आगम्य having come,      अतिसंरम्भवर्धितम् greatly augmented by the speed, शब्दम् thunderous noise, कनीयसा सह with his younger brother, शुश्राव heard.
explanation: As they reached the midstream, Rama and his younger brother heard a sound greatly  augmented by the speed (of the river).

shloka_text: अथ रामस्सरिन्मध्ये पप्रच्छ मुनिपुङ्गवम्। वारिणो भिद्यमानस्य किमयं तुमुलो ध्वनि:।।1.24.6।।
transliteration: atha rāmassarinmadhye papraccha munipuṅgavam| vāriṇo bhidyamānasya kimayaṃ tumulo dhvani:
translation: अथ thereafter, राम: Rama, सरिन्मध्ये in the midst of river, मुनिपुङ्गवम् best of the sages, प्रपच्छ enquired of, भिद्यमानस्य bursting, वारिण: waters, तुमुल: tumultuous, अयं ध्वनि: this sound, किम् what?
explanation: Rama enquired of Viswamitra, the best of sages, "What is this tumultuous sound  bursting out of the waters?"

shloka_text: राघवस्य वचश्श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमन्वित:। कथयामास धर्मात्मा तस्य शब्दस्य निश्चयम्।।1.24.7।।
transliteration: rāghavasya vacaśśrutvā kautūhalasamanvita:| kathayāmāsa dharmātmā tasya śabdasya niścayam
translation: कौतूहलसमन्वितः filled with curiosity, राघवस्य वच: Rama's words, श्रुत्वा having heard, धर्मात्मा righteous minded one, तस्य of  that,  शब्दस्य relating to that sound, निश्चयम् nature, कथयामास narrated.
explanation: At the words of Rama filled with curiosity, the righteous (Viswamitra) narrated the true nature of that sound.

shloka_text: कैलासपर्वते राम मनसा निर्मितं सर:। ब्रह्मणा नरशार्दूल तेनेदं मानसं सर:।।1.24.8।।
transliteration: kailāsaparvate rāma manasā nirmitaṃ sara:| brahmaṇā naraśārdūla tenedaṃ mānasaṃ sara:
translation: नरशार्दूल O Best among men, राम Rama, कैलासपर्वते on the mount Kailasa, ब्रह्मणा by Brahma, सर: lake, मनसा by his thought, निर्मितम् created, तेन for that reason, इदं सर: this lake, मानसम् is called Manasa.
explanation: "O tiger among men, Rama. Brahma created out of his mind a lake on mount Kailas and so that lake is called Manasa (Sarovara).

shloka_text: तस्मात्सुस्राव सरसस्सायोध्यामुपगूहते । सर प्रवृत्ता सरयू: पुण्या ब्रह्मसरश्च्युता।।1.24.9।।
transliteration: tasmātsusrāva sarasassāyodhyāmupagūhate | sara pravṛttā sarayū: puṇyā brahmasaraścyutā
translation: तस्मात् सरस: from that Manasa lake, सुस्राव flowed, सा that river, अयोध्याम् Ayodhya, उपगूहते surrounds, सर प्रवृत्ता because it flows from that lake, सरयू: is known as Sarayu, ब्रह्मसरश्च्युता released from the lake of Brahma, पुण्या sacred.
explanation: This river which flows from Manasa Sarovara is, therefore, known as 'Sarayu'. It surrounds  Ayodhya. This sacred river flows from that lake of Brahma.

shloka_text: तस्यायमतुलश्शब्दो जाह्नवीमभिवर्तते। वारिसङ्क्षोभजो राम प्रणामं नियत:कुरु।।1.24.10।।
transliteration: tasyāyamatulaśśabdo jāhnavīmabhivartate| vārisaṅkṣobhajo rāma praṇāmaṃ niyata:kuru
translation: जाह्नवीम् river Ganga, अभिवर्तते approaches, अयम् this, अतुल: great, शब्द: sound, तस्या: that river's, वारिसङ्क्षोभज: produced when the waters are clashed at their confluence, राम Rama, नियत: with a concentrated mind, प्रणामम् respectful salutations, कुरु do.
explanation: When Ganga approaches this river (Sarayu), there is a clash of waters and this great noise is produced. Rama, offer respectful salutations here, with a calm mind".

shloka_text: ताभ्यां तु तावुभौ कृत्वा प्रणाममतिधार्मिकौ। तीरं दक्षिणमासाद्य जग्मतुर्लघुविक्रमौ।।1.24.11।।
transliteration: tābhyāṃ tu tāvubhau kṛtvā praṇāmamatidhārmikau| tīraṃ dakṣiṇamāsādya jagmaturlaghuvikramau
translation: अतिधार्मिकौ both who were exceedingly righteous, तौ उभौ both of them, ताभ्याम् to the two rivers, प्रणामम् obeisance, कृत्वा having made, दक्षिणं तीरम् southern bank, आसाद्य having reached, लघुविक्रमौ with quick steps, जग्मतु: proceeded.
explanation: Deeply religious (in nature) they both made obeisance to the two rivers and reached the southern bank and advanced with quick steps.

shloka_text: स वनं घोरसङ्काशं दृष्ट्वा नृपवरात्मज:। अविप्रहतमैक्ष्वाक: पप्रच्छ मुनिपुङ्गवम्।।1.24.12।।
transliteration: sa vanaṃ ghorasaṅkāśaṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpavarātmaja:| aviprahatamaikṣvāka: papraccha munipuṅgavam
translation: ऐक्ष्वाक: descendent of Ikshvaku, नृपवरात्मज: son of best of kings, स: he, घोरसङ्काशम् dreadful, अविप्रहतम् untrodden, वनम् forest, दृष्ट्वा having seen, मुनिपुङ्गवम् foremost of ascetics, पप्रच्छ asked.
explanation: He who was a descendent of Ikshvaku and son of the best of kings, (Dasaratha) having seen that untrodden and dreadful forest asked the foremost of the ascetics:

shloka_text: अहो वनमिदं दुर्गं झिल्लिकागणनादितम्। भैरवैश्शपदै: पूर्णं शकुन्तैर्दारुणारुतै:।।1.24.13।।
transliteration: aho vanamidaṃ durgaṃ jhillikāgaṇanāditam| bhairavaiśśapadai: pūrṇaṃ śakuntairdāruṇārutai:
translation: झिल्लिकागणनादितम् having ceaseless sounds of crickets, भैरवै: by the frightful, श्वापदै: ferocious beasts, दारुणारुतै: creating fearful cries, शकुन्तै: by birds, पूर्णम् filled, इदम् this, वनम् forest, दुर्गम् inaccessible, अहो what a wonder.
explanation: "What a wonder This inaccessible forest echoes with the (shrill) chirpings of crickets It is filled with ferocious beasts and birds producing fearful sounds.

shloka_text: नानाप्रकारैश्शकुनै र्वाश्यद्भिर्भैरवस्वनै:। सिंहव्याघ्रवराहैश्च वारणैश्चोपशोभितम्।।1.24.14।।
transliteration: nānāprakāraiśśakunai rvāśyadbhirbhairavasvanai:| siṃhavyāghravarāhaiśca vāraṇaiścopaśobhitam
translation: वाश्यद्भि: shrieking, भैरवस्वनै: frightful sounds, नानाप्रकारै: by  various kinds of, शकुनै: birds, सिंहव्याघ्रवराहै: च lions, tigers, boars, वारणै: च by elephants, उपशोभितम् shining.
explanation: "It resounds with the frightful shricks of various kinds of birds. Lions, tigers, boars and elephants prowl about.

shloka_text: धवाश्वकर्णककुभैर्बिल्वतिन्दुकपाटलै:। सङ्कीर्णं बदरीभिश्च किन्न्वेतद्दारुणं वनम्।।1.24.15।।
transliteration: dhavāśvakarṇakakubhairbilvatindukapāṭalai:| saṅkīrṇaṃ badarībhiśca kinnvetaddāruṇaṃ vanam
translation: धवाश्वकर्णककुभै: with Dhava, Ashvakarna, Kakubha, बिल्वतिन्दुकपाटलै: with Bilva,Tinduka, Patala, बदरीभिश्च with Badaris, सङ्कीर्णम् thronged, एतत् दारुणम् this frightening, वनम् forest, किं नु what indeed could this be?
explanation: This forest jampacked with dhava, ashvakarna, kakubha, bilva, tinduka, patala and badari trees, how frightening this forest could be"

shloka_text: तमुवाच महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनि:। श्रूयतां वत्स काकुत्स्थ यस्यैतद्दारुणं वनम्।।1.24.16।।
transliteration: tamuvāca mahātejā viśvāmitro mahāmuni:| śrūyatāṃ vatsa kākutstha yasyaitaddāruṇaṃ vanam
translation: महातेजा: highly powerful, महामुनि: great sage, विश्वामित्र: Viswamitra, तम् addressing him, उवाच spoke, वत्स O Child, काकुत्स्थ Kakusthsa, एतत् दारुणं वनम् this dreadful forest, यस्य whose, श्रूयताम् let it be heard.
explanation: Viswamitra, the great sage radiating energy addressing Rama said, "O child of kakusthsa dynasty I shall tell you whose dreadful forest this is. Listen"

shloka_text: एतौ जनपदौ स्फीतौ पूर्वमास्तां नरोत्तम। मलदाश्च करूशाश्च देवनिर्माणनिर्मितौ।।1.24.17।।
transliteration: etau janapadau sphītau pūrvamāstāṃ narottama| maladāśca karūśāśca devanirmāṇanirmitau
translation: नरोत्तम O Best among men, पूर्वम् formerly, देवनिर्माणनिर्मितौ built by celestial architects, मलदाश्च Malada, करूशा: च and also Karusha, स्फीतौ large and prosperous, एतौ जनपदौ these two cities, आस्ताम् existed.
explanation: O best among men, formerly these two large and prosperous cities called Malada and Karusha built by celestial architects existed.

shloka_text: पुरा वृत्रवधे राम मलेन समभिप्लुतम्। क्षुधा चैव सहस्राक्षं ब्रह्महत्या समाविशत्।।1.24.18।।
transliteration: purā vṛtravadhe rāma malena samabhiplutam| kṣudhā caiva sahasrākṣaṃ brahmahatyā samāviśat
translation: राम O Rama, पुरा in ancient times, वृत्रवधे at the time of destruction of Vritrasura, मलेन by impurity, क्षुधा चैव by hunger also, समभिप्लुतम् overpowered, सहस्राक्षम् Indra, ब्रह्महत्या sin arising out of slaying Brahmin, समाविशत्  attacked.
explanation: O Rama, in ancient times after killing Vritrasura, Indra was overpowered by the sin of slaying a brahmin and was affected by impurity and hunger.

shloka_text: तमिन्द्रं स्नापयन् देवा ऋषयश्च तपोधना:। कलशैस्स्नापयामासुर्मलं चास्य प्रमोचयन्।।1.24.19।।
transliteration: tamindraṃ snāpayan devā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanā:| kalaśaissnāpayāmāsurmalaṃ cāsya pramocayan
translation: तम् इन्द्रम् Indra, देवा: devatas, स्नापयन् while bathing him, तपोधना: sages possessing asceticism as wealth, ऋषयश्च rishis, कलशै: with waterpitchers, स्नापयामासु: bathed him, अस्य मलम् his impurities, प्रमोचयन् liberated.
explanation: Devas and rishis endowed with the wealth of asceticism bathed Indra with the (consecrated) waters (brought from all rivers) from the pitchers and got him cleansed of impurities.

shloka_text: इह भूम्यां मलं दत्वा दत्वा कारूशमेव च। शरीरजं महेन्द्रस्य ततो हर्षं प्रपेदिरे।।1.24.20।।
transliteration: iha bhūmyāṃ malaṃ datvā datvā kārūśameva ca| śarīrajaṃ mahendrasya tato harṣaṃ prapedire
translation: महेन्द्रस्य Mahendra's, शरीरजम् born from the body, मलम् taint and impurity, इह here, भूम्याम् at this place, दत्त्वा having left, कारूशमेव च hunger also, दत्त्वा having left, तत: there after, हर्षम् joy, प्रपेदिरे obtained.
explanation: With the hunger and the taint and impurity from the body of Mahendra removed at this place, the devas rejoiced.

shloka_text: निर्मलो निष्करूशश्च शुचिरिंन्द्रो यदाभवत्। ददौ देशस्य सुप्रीतो वरं प्रभुरनुत्तमम्।।1.24.21।।
transliteration: nirmalo niṣkarūśaśca śuciriṃndro yadābhavat| dadau deśasya suprīto varaṃ prabhuranuttamam
translation: इन्द्र: Indra, यदा when, निर्मल: removed of his impurities, निष्करूशश्च unaffected by hunger, शुचि: अभवत् became pure, प्रभु: all powerful lord, सुप्रीत: highly pleased, देशस्य for that region, अनुत्तमम् excellent, वरम् boon, ददौ gave.
explanation: Cleansed of his impurities and his hunger gone, Indra once again became pure. Allpowerful Indra highly pleased gave an excellent boon to that region.

shloka_text: इमौ जनपदौ स्फीतौ ख्यातिं लोके गमिष्यत:। मलदाश्च करूशाश्च ममाङ्गमलधारिणौ।।1.24.22।।
transliteration: imau janapadau sphītau khyātiṃ loke gamiṣyata:| maladāśca karūśāśca mamāṅgamaladhāriṇau
translation: मम my, अङ्गमलधारिणौ bearing impurities of my body, इमौ these, जनपदौ places, स्फीतौ becoming prosperous, मलदाश्च Malada, करूशाश्च and Karusha, लोके in this world, ख्यातिम् fame, गमिष्यत: will attain.
explanation: Indra blessed the place saying, 'Having absorbed impurities of my body, let these places be extremely fertile and prosperous and let this be renowned throughout this world as Malada and Karusha'.

shloka_text: साधु साध्विति तं देवा: पाकशासनमब्रुवन्। देशस्य पूजां तां दृष्ट्वा कृतां शक्रेण धीमता।।1.24.23।।
transliteration: sādhu sādhviti taṃ devā: pākaśāsanamabruvan| deśasya pūjāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtāṃ śakreṇa dhīmatā
translation: धीमता by the wise, शक्रेण by Indra, कृताम् performed, ताम् देशस्य of  that land, पूजाम् honour, दृट्वा having seen, देवा: gods, साधु साधु इति 'Well, Well', तं पाकशासनम् adddressing Indra, अब्रुवन् said.
explanation: Having seen the honour bestowed on that land by the wise Indra, the gods said to him, 'Well done, Well done'.

shloka_text: एतौ जनपदौ स्फीतौ दीर्घकालमरिन्दम। मलदाश्च करूशाश्च मुदितौ धनधान्यत:।।1.24.24।।
transliteration: etau janapadau sphītau dīrghakālamarindama| maladāśca karūśāśca muditau dhanadhānyata:
translation: अरिन्दम O Destroyer of enemies, मलदाश्च Malada, करूशाश्च and Karusha, स्फीतौ prosperous, एतौ these, जनपदौ townships, दीर्घकालम् for a long time, धनधान्यत: with the harvest of corn and wealth, मुदितौ rejoiced.
explanation: O Destroyers of enemies these prosperous townships, Malada and Karusha looked cheerful with (bumper) crops and wealth for a long time.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य यक्षी वै कामरूपिणी। बलं नागसहस्रस्य धारयन्ती तदा ह्यभूत्।।1.24.25।। ताटका नाम भद्रं ते भार्या सुन्दस्य धीमत:। 2 मारीचो राक्षस: पुत्रो यस्याश्शक्रपराक्रम:।।1.24.26।।
transliteration: kasyacittvatha kālasya yakṣī vai kāmarūpiṇī| balaṃ nāgasahasrasya dhārayantī tadā hyabhūt tāṭakā nāma bhadraṃ te bhāryā sundasya dhīmata:| 2 mārīco rākṣasa: putro yasyāśśakraparākrama:
translation: अथ thereafter, कस्यचित्कालस्य after a lapse of some time, कामरूपिणी capable of assuming forms at will, नागसहस्रस्य of a thousand elephants, बलम् strength of, धारयन्ती possessing, ताटका नाम यक्षी yakshi known as Tataka, धीमत: of the  intelligent, सुन्दस्य Sunda's, भार्या wife, शक्रपराक्रम: possessed of the power of Indra, मारीच: rakshasa known as Maricha, यस्या: whose, पुत्र: son, अभूत् became known, भद्रं ते May prosperity greet you.
explanation: Then, after a lapse of several years, O gentle one a terrible yakshini by name Tataka, wife of intelligent Sunda, capable of assuming different forms at will, possessed of the strength of a thousand elephants and mother of a rakshasa known as Maricha armed with the power of Indra took possession of this place.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य यक्षी वै कामरूपिणी। बलं नागसहस्रस्य धारयन्ती तदा ह्यभूत्।।1.24.25।। ताटका नाम भद्रं ते भार्या सुन्दस्य धीमत:। 2 मारीचो राक्षस: पुत्रो यस्याश्शक्रपराक्रम:।।1.24.26।।
transliteration: kasyacittvatha kālasya yakṣī vai kāmarūpiṇī| balaṃ nāgasahasrasya dhārayantī tadā hyabhūt tāṭakā nāma bhadraṃ te bhāryā sundasya dhīmata:| 2 mārīco rākṣasa: putro yasyāśśakraparākrama:
translation: अथ thereafter, कस्यचित्कालस्य after a lapse of some time, कामरूपिणी capable of assuming forms at will, नागसहस्रस्य of a thousand elephants, बलम् strength of, धारयन्ती possessing, ताटका नाम यक्षी yakshi known as Tataka, धीमत: of the  intelligent, सुन्दस्य Sunda's, भार्या wife, शक्रपराक्रम: possessed of the power of Indra, मारीच: rakshasa known as Maricha, यस्या: whose, पुत्र: son, अभूत् became known, भद्रं ते May prosperity greet you.
explanation: Then, after a lapse of several years, O gentle one a terrible yakshini by name Tataka, wife of intelligent Sunda, capable of assuming different forms at will, possessed of the strength of a thousand elephants and mother of a rakshasa known as Maricha armed with the power of Indra took possession of this place.

shloka_text: वृत्तबाहुर्महावीर्यो विपुलास्य तनुर्महान्। राक्षसो भैरवाकारो नित्यं त्रासयते प्रजा:।।1.24.27।।
transliteration: vṛttabāhurmahāvīryo vipulāsya tanurmahān| rākṣaso bhairavākāro nityaṃ trāsayate prajā:
translation: वृत्तबाहु: one who has round arms, महावीर्य: a highly energetic, विपुलास्यतनु: having large face and huge body, महान् gigantic, भैरवाकार: having dreadful form, राक्षस: rakshasa, नित्यम् always, प्रजा: inhabitants, त्रासयते frightens.
explanation: The arms (of Maricha) are round and strong. He is highly energetic. He has a large face and a huge body. In appearance, he is gigantic and possesses a dreadful form. That rakshasa always threatened the inhabitants.

shloka_text: इमौ जनपदौ नित्यं विनाशयति राघव। मलदांश्च करूशांश्च ताटका दुष्टचारिणी।।1.24.28।।
transliteration: imau janapadau nityaṃ vināśayati rāghava| maladāṃśca karūśāṃśca tāṭakā duṣṭacāriṇī
translation: राघव O Rama, दुष्टचारिणी a woman with wicked deeds, ताटका Tataka, मलदांश्च Malada, करूशांश्च Karusha, इमौ जनपदौ these two townships, नित्यम् always, विनाशयति destroys .
explanation: "O Rama that wicked than Tataka carried on her depredations at regular intervals in these locations, Malada and Karusha.

shloka_text: सेयं पन्थानमावृत्य वसत्यध्यर्धयोजने। अत एव न गन्तव्यं ताटकाया वनं यत:।।1.24.29।।
transliteration: seyaṃ panthānamāvṛtya vasatyadhyardhayojane| ata eva na gantavyaṃ tāṭakāyā vanaṃ yata:
translation: सा such, इयम् thisTataka, पन्थानम् the path, आवृत्य obstructing, अध्यर्धयोजने at one and half yojanas distance, वसति living, यत: for which reason, ताटकाया: Tataka, वनम् forest, अत एव for that reason, न गन्तव्यम् one should not traverse.
explanation: Tataka lives at a distance of one and a half yojanas from here obstructing the path. Since Tataka dwells in this forest, no one comes here (because of fears).

shloka_text: स्वबाहुबलमाश्रित्य जहीमां दुष्टचारिणीम्। मन्नियोगादिमं देशं कुरु निष्कण्टकं पुन:।।1.24.30।।
transliteration: svabāhubalamāśritya jahīmāṃ duṣṭacāriṇīm| manniyogādimaṃ deśaṃ kuru niṣkaṇṭakaṃ puna:
translation: स्वबाहुबलम् strength of your own arms, आश्रित्य employing, दुष्टचारिणीम् this one of wicked deeds, इमाम् her, जहि slay,मन्नियोगात् by my order, इमं देशम् this country, पुन: again, निष्कण्टकम् devoid of that thorn, कुरु do it (make it habitable).
explanation: "By  the strength of your arms slay this one of wicked deeds. Comply with my orders and make this country safe (and habitable).

shloka_text: न हि कश्चिदिमं देशं शक्नोत्यागन्तुमीदृशम्। यक्षिण्या घोरया राम उत्सादितमसह्यया।।1.24.31।।
transliteration: na hi kaścidimaṃ deśaṃ śaknotyāgantumīdṛśam| yakṣiṇyā ghorayā rāma utsāditamasahyayā
translation: राम O Rama, घोरया by the dreadful, असह्यया by the intolerable, यक्षिण्या yakshini, उत्सादितम् destroyed, ईदृशम् such, इमम् देशम् this country, आगन्तुम् to approach, कश्चित् any one, न शक्नोति is not capable.
explanation: O Rama none dare approach this country ravaged by such dreadful, intolerable yakshini.

shloka_text: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथैतद्दारुणं वनम्। यक्ष्या चोत्सादितं सर्वमद्यापि न निवर्तते।।1.24.32।।
transliteration: etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yathaitaddāruṇaṃ vanam| yakṣyā cotsāditaṃ sarvamadyāpi na nivartate
translation: एतत् वनम् this forest, सर्वम् entirely, दारुणम् cruel, यक्ष्या by the yakshi,  यथा in such a  manner, उत्सादितम् ruined, अद्यापि even now, यथा in a manner, न निवर्तते does not go  back, एतत् सर्वम् all this, ते to you, आख्यातम् has been told.
explanation: You have been told the manner in which this fierce forest is entirely ruined by that cruel yakshini. Tell now she has not left this place". इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे चतुर्विंशतिस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the twentyfourth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ तस्याप्रमेयस्य मुनेर्वचनमुत्तमम्। श्रुत्वा पुरुषशार्दूल: प्रत्युवाच शुभां गिरम्।।1.25.1।।
transliteration: atha tasyāprameyasya munervacanamuttamam| śrutvā puruṣaśārdūla: pratyuvāca śubhāṃ giram
translation: अप्रमेयस्य having super human faculty beyond comprehension, तस्य मुने: that sage's, उत्तमम् excellent, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, पुरुषशार्दूल: greatest among men, शुभाम् auspicious, गिरम् speech, प्रत्युवाच replied.
explanation: On hearing the excellent words of Viswamitra, a sage with unimaginable faculty. Rama, the tiger among men (Rama) replied in a, gentle voice:
comments: Rama, further enquires Viswamitra narrates the birth of Tataka, her marriage, curse, etc., and convinces Rama to slay her.

shloka_text: अल्पवीर्या यदा यक्षा श्श्रूयन्ते मुनिपुङ्गव। कथन्नागसहस्रस्य धारयत्यबला बलम्।।1.25.2।।
transliteration: alpavīryā yadā yakṣā śśrūyante munipuṅgava| kathannāgasahasrasya dhārayatyabalā balam
translation: मुनिपुङ्गव O Best of ascetics, यक्षा: yakshas, अल्पवीर्या: possess little prowess, यदा श्रूयन्ते since it is being heard, अबला a woman, नागसहस्रस्य thousand elephants', बलम् strength, कथम् how, धारयति possesses.
explanation: "O best of ascetics, I have heard the yakshas possess little prowess. How can a woman who is by gender weak possess the strength of a thousand elephants?

shloka_text: विश्वामित्रोऽब्रवीद्वाक्यं शृण येन बलोत्तरा। वरदानकृतं वीर्यं धारयत्यबला बलम्।।1.25.3।।
transliteration: viśvāmitro'bravīdvākyaṃ śṛṇa yena balottarā| varadānakṛtaṃ vīryaṃ dhārayatyabalā balam
translation: विश्वामित्र: Visvamitra, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke, अबला a woman, येन for which ever  reason, बलोत्तरा acquired great strength, शृणु you may listen, वरदानकृतम् by virtue of a boon, वीर्यम् prowess, बलम् strength, धारयति possesses.
explanation: Viswamitra said, "Listen, how she acquired the prowess and strength by virtue of a boon she received.

shloka_text: पूर्वमासीन्महायक्षस्सुकेतुर्नाम वीर्यवान्। अनपत्यश्शुभाचारस्स च तेपे महत्तप:।।1.25.4।।
transliteration: pūrvamāsīnmahāyakṣassuketurnāma vīryavān| anapatyaśśubhācārassa ca tepe mahattapa:
translation: पूर्वम् in the days past, सुकेतुर्नाम named Suketu, वीर्यवान् powerful, महायक्ष: great yaksha, आसीत् existed, अनपत्य: he was without children, स: he, शुभाचार: one with pure practices,  महत्  great, तप: penance, तेपे performed.
explanation: "In the past there was a powerful and great yaksha by name Suketu. He had no  children. So he performed an intense penance following virtuous practices.

shloka_text: पितामहस्तु सुप्रीतस्तस्य यक्षपते स्तदा। कन्यारत्नं ददौ राम ताटकां नाम नामत:।।1.25.5।।
transliteration: pitāmahastu suprītastasya yakṣapate stadā| kanyāratnaṃ dadau rāma tāṭakāṃ nāma nāmata:
translation: राम O Rama, तदा then, पितामह: Brahma, सुप्रीत: highly gratified, तस्य यक्षपते: towards  that king of yakshas, नामत: by name, नाम wellknown as, ताटकां Tataka, कन्यारत्नम् gem of a daughter, ददौ granted.
explanation: Rama the grandsire Brahma was highly gratified and granted to the king of yakshas, the gem of a daughter by name known asTataka.

shloka_text: ददौ नागसहस्रस्य बलं चास्या: पितामह:। नत्वेव पुत्रं यक्षाय ददौ ब्रह्मा महायशा:।।1.25.6।।
transliteration: dadau nāgasahasrasya balaṃ cāsyā: pitāmaha:| natveva putraṃ yakṣāya dadau brahmā mahāyaśā:
translation: पितामह: lord Brahma, अस्या: for her, नागसहस्रस्य thousand elephants, बलम् strength, ददौ  granted, महायशा: that illustrious, ब्रह्मा lord Brahma, यक्षाय for that yaksha, पुत्रं तु son, न ददौ did not bestow.
explanation: The illustrious grandsire Brahma granted her the strength of a thousand elephants, but did not bestow a son on the yaksha.

shloka_text: तां तु जातां विवर्धन्तीं रूपयौवनशालिनीम्। झर्झपुत्राय सुन्दाय ददौ भार्यां यशस्विनीम्।।1.25.7।।
transliteration: tāṃ tu jātāṃ vivardhantīṃ rūpayauvanaśālinīm| jharjhaputrāya sundāya dadau bhāryāṃ yaśasvinīm
translation: जाताम् born, विवर्धन्तीम् as she was growing, रूपयौवनशालिनीम् shining with youthful charm and beauty, यशस्विनीम् glorious, ताम् her, झर्झपुत्राय son of Jharjha, सुन्दाय for Sunda, भार्याम् as wife, ददौ gave.
explanation: As she grew up, glowing with youth and beauty she was given in marriage to Sunda, son of Jharjha.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य यक्षी पुत्रमजायत। मारीचं नाम दुर्धर्षं यश्शापाद्राक्षसोऽभवत्।।1.25.8।।
transliteration: kasyacittvatha kālasya yakṣī putramajāyata| mārīcaṃ nāma durdharṣaṃ yaśśāpādrākṣaso'bhavat
translation: अथ thereafter, कस्यचित् कालस्य after some time, यक्षी the female yakshi,Tataka, मारीचं नाम by name Maricha, दुर्धर्षम् unassailable, पुत्रम् son, अजायत gave birth, य: he, शापात् because of the curse, राक्षस: अभवत् became rakshasa.
explanation: After some time that yakshini gave birth to an unassailable son by name Maricha. Because of a curse, he became a rakshasa (though born of yaksha parentage).

shloka_text: सुन्दे तु निहते राम सागस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम्। ताटका सह पुत्रेण प्रधर्षयितुमिच्छति।।1.25.9।।
transliteration: sunde tu nihate rāma sāgastyamṛṣisattamam| tāṭakā saha putreṇa pradharṣayitumicchati
translation: राम: O Rama, सुन्दे when Sunda, निहते was killed, सा ताटका that Tataka, पुत्रेण सह along with her son, ऋषिसत्तमम् excellent of sages, अगस्त्यम् Agastya, प्रधर्षयितुम् to attack him, इच्छति desires(ed).
explanation: O Rama when Sunda died Tataka along with her son wanted to attack Agastya, the best of sages.

shloka_text: भक्षार्थं जातसंरम्भा गर्जन्ती साभ्यधावत।0 आपतन्तीं तु तां दृष्ट्वा अगस्त्यो भगवानृषि:।।1.25.10।। राक्षसत्वं भजस्वेति मारीचं व्याजहार स:। 1
transliteration: bhakṣārthaṃ jātasaṃrambhā garjantī sābhyadhāvata|0 āpatantīṃ tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā agastyo bhagavānṛṣi: rākṣasatvaṃ bhajasveti mārīcaṃ vyājahāra sa:| 1
translation: सा she, गर्जन्ती roaring, जातसंरम्भा with haste and excitement, भक्षार्धम् to devour, अभ्यधावत rushed towards him, भगवान् venerable, स: अगस्त्य: ऋषि: that Agastya rishi, आपतन्तीम् approaching, ताम् her, दृष्ट्वा having seen, राक्षसत्वम् demons' nature, भजस्व इति partake, मरीचम् Maricha, व्याजहार spoke(cursed).
explanation: Roaring, she rushed with excitement to devour him. The venerable  rishi Agastya saw her approaching him and cursed Maricha to assume form of a demoness.

shloka_text: अगस्त्य: परमक्रुद्धस्ताटकामपि शप्तवान्।।1.25.11।। पुरुषादी महायक्षी विरूपा विकृतानना। इदं रूपं विहायाथ दारुणं रूपमस्तु ते।।1.25.12।।
transliteration: agastya: paramakruddhastāṭakāmapi śaptavān puruṣādī mahāyakṣī virūpā vikṛtānanā| idaṃ rūpaṃ vihāyātha dāruṇaṃ rūpamastu te
translation: परमक्रुद्ध: exceedingly wrathful, अगस्त्य: Agastya, ताटकामपि Tataka also, शप्तवान् cursed, इदं रूपम् this form, विहाय abandoning, अथ thereafter, विरूपा disfigured shape, विकृतानना hideous countenance, पुरुषादी becoming a cannibal, महायक्षी great yakshi, ते to you, दारुणं रूपम् अस्तु let it be a terrible form.
explanation: Mighty angry, Agastya cursed Tataka saying, 'Abandon this form of a great yakshini and assume the terrible figure of a rakshasi, a cannibal with distorted appearance and a hideous countenance'.

shloka_text: अगस्त्य: परमक्रुद्धस्ताटकामपि शप्तवान्।।1.25.11।। पुरुषादी महायक्षी विरूपा विकृतानना। इदं रूपं विहायाथ दारुणं रूपमस्तु ते।।1.25.12।।
transliteration: agastya: paramakruddhastāṭakāmapi śaptavān puruṣādī mahāyakṣī virūpā vikṛtānanā| idaṃ rūpaṃ vihāyātha dāruṇaṃ rūpamastu te
translation: परमक्रुद्ध: exceedingly wrathful, अगस्त्य: Agastya, ताटकामपि Tataka also, शप्तवान् cursed, इदं रूपम् this form, विहाय abandoning, अथ thereafter, विरूपा disfigured shape, विकृतानना hideous countenance, पुरुषादी becoming a cannibal, महायक्षी great yakshi, ते to you, दारुणं रूपम् अस्तु let it be a terrible form.
explanation: Mighty angry, Agastya cursed Tataka saying, 'Abandon this form of a great yakshini and assume the terrible figure of a rakshasi, a cannibal with distorted appearance and a hideous countenance'.

shloka_text: सैषा शापकृतामर्षा ताटका क्रोधमूर्छिता। देशमुत्सादयत्येनमगस्त्यचरितं शुभम्।।1.25.13।।
transliteration: saiṣā śāpakṛtāmarṣā tāṭakā krodhamūrchitā| deśamutsādayatyenamagastyacaritaṃ śubham
translation: शापकृतामर्षा enraged at the curse, सा एषा ताटका this same Tataka, क्रोधमूर्छिता has become senseless with anger, अगस्त्यचरितम् place tread over by Agstya, शुभम् sacred, एनं देशम् this land, उत्सादयति is destroying.
explanation: Enraged at the curse, senseless, Tataka with anger, has been ravaging this sacred land when Agastya walked.

shloka_text: एनां राघव दुर्वृत्तां यक्षीं परमदारुणाम्। गोब्राह्मणहितार्थाय जहि दुष्टपराक्रमाम्।।1.25.14।।
transliteration: enāṃ rāghava durvṛttāṃ yakṣīṃ paramadāruṇām| gobrāhmaṇahitārthāya jahi duṣṭaparākramām
translation: राघव (राम) O Rama, दुर्वृत्ताम् wicked, परमदारुणाम् highly cruel, दुष्टपराक्रमाम् having vile prowess, एनां यक्षीम् this yakshi, गोब्राह्मणहितार्थाय for the welfare of brahmins and the cows, जहि you may slay her.
explanation: O Rama for the welfare of cows and brahmins, slay this yakshini who is wicked, extremely cruel and possessing vile prowess.

shloka_text: न ह्येनां शापसम्स्पृष्टां कश्चिदुत्सहते पुमान्। निहन्तुं त्रिषु लोकेषु त्वामृते रघुनन्दन।।1.25.15।।
transliteration: na hyenāṃ śāpasamspṛṣṭāṃ kaścidutsahate pumān| nihantuṃ triṣu lokeṣu tvāmṛte raghunandana
translation: रघुनन्दन O Rama, शापसम्स्पृष्टाम् maligned by the curse, एनाम् this yakshini, निहन्तुम् to slay, त्वां ऋते except you, कश्चित् पुमान् a single man, त्रिषु लोकेषु in three worlds, न उत्सहते हि not inclined.
explanation: O son of Raghu's dynasty she is maligned by the curse, and so not a single man in the three worlds except you, is  competent to slay this yakshini.

shloka_text: न हि ते स्त्रीवधकृते घृणा कार्या नरोत्तम। चातुर्वण्यहितार्थाय कर्तव्यं राजसूनुना।।1.25.16।।
transliteration: na hi te strīvadhakṛte ghṛṇā kāryā narottama| cāturvaṇyahitārthāya kartavyaṃ rājasūnunā
translation: नरोत्तम O Best among men, स्त्रीवधकृते by the act of slaying a woman, ते to you, घृणा pity न कार्या need not be shown, राजसूनुना by a prince, चातुर्वर्ण्यहितार्थाय in the interests four orders of the society, कर्तव्यम् should be done.
explanation: O best among men you need not hate killing a woman. You are a prince. You should serve the interest of the four orders of the society.

shloka_text: नृशंसमनृशंसं वा प्रजारक्षणकारणात्। पातकं वा सदोषं वा कर्तव्यं रक्षता सता।।1.25.17।।
transliteration: nṛśaṃsamanṛśaṃsaṃ vā prajārakṣaṇakāraṇāt| pātakaṃ vā sadoṣaṃ vā kartavyaṃ rakṣatā satā
translation: रक्षता while protecting, सता by a virtuous man, प्रजारक्षणकारणात् for the welfare of the subjects, नृशंसं वा either cruel, अनृशंसं वा or not cruel ,पातकं वा or a sin, सदोषं वा or involving a mistake, कर्तव्यम् should be done.
explanation: Whether cruel or kind, sinful or wrong whatever contributes to the protection of the subjects, should be done by the righteous (king).

shloka_text: राज्यभारनियुक्तानामेष धर्मस्सनातन:। अधर्म्यां जहि काकुत्स्थ धर्मोह्यस्या न विद्यते।।1.25.18।।
transliteration: rājyabhāraniyuktānāmeṣa dharmassanātana:| adharmyāṃ jahi kākutstha dharmohyasyā na vidyate
translation: राज्यभारनियुक्तानाम् for those who enjoined by the burden of royalty, एष: this one, सनातन: eternal, धर्म: law, काकुत्स्थ O Kakusthsa, अधर्म्याम् unjust (Tataka ), जहि kill her, अस्या: for this Tataka, धर्म: righteousness, न विद्यते हि knows not.
explanation: This is the eternal law binding those who are appointed to bear the burden of a kingdom. O Kakutstha kill her. She knows no dharma.

shloka_text: श्रूयते हि पुरा शक्रो विरोचनसुतां नृप। पृथिवीं हन्तुमिच्छन्तीं मन्थरामभ्यसूदयत्।।1.25.19।।
transliteration: śrūyate hi purā śakro virocanasutāṃ nṛpa| pṛthivīṃ hantumicchantīṃ mantharāmabhyasūdayat
translation: नृप O Prince, पुरा in the days of the past, पृथिवीम् this earth, हन्तुम् to destroy, इच्छन्तीम् intending, विरोचनसुताम् daughter of Virochana, मन्थराम् Manthara, शक्र: Indra, अभ्यसूदयत् slew, श्रूयते हि it is heard.
explanation: O Prince It is heard that in the past Indra slew Manthara, Virochana's daughter who intended to destroy the earth.

shloka_text: विष्णुनापि पुरा राम भृगुपत्नी दृढव्रता। अनिन्द्रं लोकमिच्छन्ती काव्यमाता निषूदिता।।1.25.20।।
transliteration: viṣṇunāpi purā rāma bhṛgupatnī dṛḍhavratā| anindraṃ lokamicchantī kāvyamātā niṣūditā
translation: राम O Rama, पुरा in the olden days, लोकम् this world, अनिन्द्रम् devoid of Indra, इच्छन्ती desirous, दृढव्रता determined to vow, काव्यमाता mother of Sukracharya, भृगुपत्नी अपि wife of sage Bhrigu, विष्णुनाऽपि by Visnu also, निषूदिता destroyed.
explanation: 'O Rama! In olden times, Kavya, the mother of Sukracharya, the wife of sage Bhrigu, was destroyed by Vishnu determined to destroy Indra.'

shloka_text: एतैश्चान्यैश्च बहुभी राजपुत्र महात्मभि:। अधर्मसहिता नार्यो हता: पुरुषसत्तमै:।।1.25.21।।
transliteration: etaiścānyaiśca bahubhī rājaputra mahātmabhi:| adharmasahitā nāryo hatā: puruṣasattamai:
translation: राजपुत्र O Prince, महात्मभि: magnanimous, एतैश्च by them, अन्यै:च by others, पुरुषसत्तमै: by the best among men, बहुभिः by several, अधर्मसहिता: unrighteous ones, नार्य: women, हता: were killed.
explanation: O Prince by these magnanimous persons and by great men several unrighteous women were killed for the common good". इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे पञ्चविंशस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the twentyfifth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: मुनेर्वचनमक्लीबं श्रुत्वा नरवरात्मज:। राघव: प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा प्रत्युवाच दृढव्रत:।।1.26.1।।
transliteration: munervacanamaklībaṃ śrutvā naravarātmaja:| rāghava: prāñjalirbhūtvā pratyuvāca dṛḍhavrata:
translation: दृढव्रत: a man firm in his vows, नरवरात्मज: the son of the foremost of men, राघव: Rama, अक्लीबम् determined, manly and bold, मुने: ascetic's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having listened, प्राञ्जलि:भूत्वा with folded palms, प्रत्युवाच replied.
explanation: After listening to the manly command of ascetic Viswamitra, Rama, of the lineage of Raghu, the son of the foremost of men and firm in determination, replied with folded palms:
comments: Sri Rama kills Tataka

shloka_text: पितुर्वचननिर्देशात्पितुर्वचनगौरवात्। वचनं कौशिकस्येति कर्तव्यमविशङ्कया।।1.26.2।।
transliteration: piturvacananirdeśātpiturvacanagauravāt| vacanaṃ kauśikasyeti kartavyamaviśaṅkayā
translation: पितु: of my father, वचननिर्देशात् to fulfil the words of command, पितु: of my sire's, वचनगौरवात् to honour his words, कौशिकस्य Kausika's, वचनम् इति the words as such, अविशङ्कया without hesitation, कर्तव्यम् fit to be done.
explanation: "As I have to fulfill the command of my father and honour his words and the instruction of Kausika (Viswamitra), I shall execute it (kill Tataka) without hesitation.

shloka_text: अनुशिष्टोऽस्म्ययोध्यायां गुरुमध्ये महात्मना। पित्रा दशरथेनाहं नावज्ञेयं हि तद्वच:।।1.26.3।।
transliteration: anuśiṣṭo'smyayodhyāyāṃ gurumadhye mahātmanā| pitrā daśarathenāhaṃ nāvajñeyaṃ hi tadvaca:
translation: अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, गुरुमध्ये in the presence of elders, महात्मना by the magnanimous, पित्रा father, दशरथेन by Dasaratha, अहम् I, अनुशिष्ट: अस्मि have been ordered, तद्वच: his words, नावज्ञेयं हि cannot be disobeyed(turned down).
explanation: In Ayodhya in the presence of elders and spiritual masters (of Dasaratha's court), I have been ordered by my magnanimous father to act according to your instructions  and his words cannot be disobeyed.

shloka_text: सोऽहं पितुर्वचश्श्रुत्वा शासनाद्ब्रह्मवादिन:। करिष्यामि न सन्देहस्ताटकावधमुत्तमम्।।1.26.4।।
transliteration: so'haṃ piturvacaśśrutvā śāsanādbrahmavādina:| kariṣyāmi na sandehastāṭakāvadhamuttamam
translation: स: अहम्  such as I am, पितु: father's, वच: words, श्रुत्वा having heard, ब्रह्मवादिन: of the man  endowed with the knowledge of vedas, शासनात् in accordance with the command, उत्तमम् the welcoming act, ताटकावधम् slaying of Tataka, करिष्यामि I shall perform, सन्देह: न no doubt.
explanation: As per the words of my father and the command of Viswamitra, who has the knowledge of the Brahman,  I shall execute the welcome act of killing Tataka.

shloka_text: गोब्राह्मणहितार्थाय देशस्यास्य सुखाय च। तव चैवाप्रमेयस्य वचनं कर्तुमुद्यत:।।1.26.5।।
transliteration: gobrāhmaṇahitārthāya deśasyāsya sukhāya ca| tava caivāprameyasya vacanaṃ kartumudyata:
translation: गोब्राह्मणहितार्थाय for the welfare of cows and brahmins, अस्य देशस्य this country's, सुखाय च  for the happiness, अप्रमेयस्य of the man possessing boundless energy, तव your, वचनम् words, कर्तुम् to perform, उद्यत: I am prepared.
explanation: For the welfare of cows and brahmins and also for the good of this country, I am ready to perform such acts as commanded by you of  boundless energy".

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा धनुर्मध्ये बध्वा मुष्टिमरिन्दम:। ज्याशब्दमकरोत्तीव्रं दिशश्शब्देन नादयन्।।1.26.6।।
transliteration: evamuktvā dhanurmadhye badhvā muṣṭimarindama:| jyāśabdamakarottīvraṃ diśaśśabdena nādayan
translation: अरिन्दम: destroyer of enemies, एवम् उक्त्वा having spoken thus, धनुर्मध्ये in the middle of the bow, मुष्टिम् the fist, बद्वा clinching, शब्देन with sounds, दिश: ten cardinal directions,   नादयन् sounding, तीव्रम् severe, ज्याशब्दम् with twanging sounds of the bowstring, अकरोत्  performed.
explanation: Rama, the destroyer of enemies having said so clinched the middle of the bow with his fist and filled the ten quarters with the resounding twanging of the bowstring.

shloka_text: तेन शब्देन वित्रस्तास्ताटकावनवासिन:। ताटका च सुसंक्रुद्धा तेन शब्देन मोहिता।।1.26.7।।
transliteration: tena śabdena vitrastāstāṭakāvanavāsina:| tāṭakā ca susaṃkruddhā tena śabdena mohitā
translation: ताटकावनवासिन: all the beings living in that Tataka forest, तेन शब्देन with that sound, वित्रस्ता: were terrified, ताटका च Tataka also, तेन शब्देन by that sound, सुसंक्रुद्धा was furious with anger, मोहिता amazed.
explanation: The dwellers of the Tataka forest were terrified by the sound (of the bow). Tataka, was might angry and amazed.

shloka_text: तं शब्दमभिनिध्याय राक्षसी क्रोधमूर्छिता। श्रुत्वा चाभ्यद्रवद्वेगाद्यतश्शब्दो विनिस्सृत:।।1.26.8।।
transliteration: taṃ śabdamabhinidhyāya rākṣasī krodhamūrchitā| śrutvā cābhyadravadvegādyataśśabdo vinissṛta:
translation: राक्षसी rakshasi, तं शब्दम् that sound, श्रत्वा having heard, क्रोधमूर्छिता infatuated with anger, अभिनिध्याय thought for a while, यत: from which direction, शब्द: sound, विनिस्सृत: originated(in that direction), वेगात् speedily, अभ्यद्रवत् rushed.
explanation: Hearing that sound, the demoness thought for a while and senseless with anger  rushed in the direction where the sound had come from.

shloka_text: तां दृष्ट्वा राघव: क्रुद्धां विकृतां विकृताननाम्। प्रमाणेनातिवृद्धां च लक्ष्मणं सोऽभ्यभाषत।।1.26.9।।
transliteration: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghava: kruddhāṃ vikṛtāṃ vikṛtānanām| pramāṇenātivṛddhāṃ ca lakṣmaṇaṃ so'bhyabhāṣata
translation: स:राघव: Rama, क्रुद्धाम् full of wrath, विकृताम् disfigured, विकृताननाम् with distorted face, प्रमाणेन in size, अतिवृद्धां च gigantic, तां दृष्ट्वा having seen her, लक्ष्मणम् addressing Lakshmana, अभ्यभाषत spoke.
explanation: Filled with wrath Rama saw Tataka, disfigured with a distorted face and gigantic in size. Turning to Lakshmana he said :

shloka_text: पश्य लक्ष्मण यक्षिण्या भैरवं दारुणं वपु:। भिद्येरन् दर्शनादस्या भीरूणां हृदयानि च।।1.26.10।।
transliteration: paśya lakṣmaṇa yakṣiṇyā bhairavaṃ dāruṇaṃ vapu:| bhidyeran darśanādasyā bhīrūṇāṃ hṛdayāni ca
translation: लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, यक्षिण्या: yakshini's, भैरवम् dreadful, दारुणम् hideous, वपु: body,पश्य behold, अस्या: her, दर्शनात् from the appearance, भीरूणाम् of the timid, हृदयानि hearts, भिद्येरन् will break.
explanation: "O Lakshmana, behold, the sight of the dreadful hideous body of this yakshini will break timid hearts.

shloka_text: एनां पश्य दुराधर्षां मायाबलसमन्विताम्। विनिवृत्तां करोम्यद्य हृतकर्णाग्रनासिकाम्।।1.26.11।।
transliteration: enāṃ paśya durādharṣāṃ māyābalasamanvitām| vinivṛttāṃ karomyadya hṛtakarṇāgranāsikām
translation: दुराधर्षाम् unassailable, मायाबलसमन्विताम endowed with strength gained through black magic, एनाम् her, हृतकर्णाग्रनासिकाम् deprive her of ears and tip of nose, विनिवृत्ताम् turned away, अद्य now, करोमि I shall do, पश्य see.
explanation: See, she is unassailable because of the strength gained through black magic. I shall cut off her ears and the tip of her nose and make her turn away.

shloka_text: न ह्येनामुत्सहे हन्तुं स्त्रीस्वभावेन रक्षिताम्। वीर्यं चास्यां गतिं चापि हनिष्यामीति मे मति:।।1.26.12।।
transliteration: na hyenāmutsahe hantuṃ strīsvabhāvena rakṣitām| vīryaṃ cāsyāṃ gatiṃ cāpi haniṣyāmīti me mati:
translation: स्त्रीस्वभावेन by virtue of being a woman, रक्षिताम् is protected, एनां हन्तुम् to slay her, न उत्सहे I am not inclined, अस्याम् in her, वीर्यम् prowess, गतिं चापि power of motion, हनिष्यामीति I will destroy, thus, मे मति: this is my opinion.
explanation: By virtue of being a woman, she is protected. I am not inclined to slay her but take away her prowess and power of motion".

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवाणे रामे तु ताटका क्रोधमूर्छिता। उद्यम्य बाहू गर्जन्ती राममेवाभ्यधावत।।1.26.13।।
transliteration: evaṃ bruvāṇe rāme tu tāṭakā krodhamūrchitā| udyamya bāhū garjantī rāmamevābhyadhāvata
translation: रामे when Rama, एवम् in this manner, ब्रुवाणे was speaking thus, ताटका Tataka, क्रोधमूर्छिता infatuated with anger, बाहू both her arms, उद्यम्य uplifting, राममेव towards Rama, गर्जन्ती roaring, अभ्यधावत rushed.
explanation: While Rama was still speaking, Tataka, incensed with fury rushed with her uplifted arms towards him roaring.

shloka_text: विश्वामित्रस्तु ब्रह्मर्षिर्हुङ्कारेणाभिभर्त्स्यताम्। स्वस्ति राघवयोरस्तु जयं चैवाभ्यभाषत।।1.26.14।।
transliteration: viśvāmitrastu brahmarṣirhuṅkāreṇābhibhartsyatām| svasti rāghavayorastu jayaṃ caivābhyabhāṣata
translation: ब्रह्मर्षि: Brahmarshi, विश्वामित्रस्तु Visvamitra, ताम् her, हुङ्कारेण with a Hunkara (menacing sound), अभिभर्त्स्य threatened, राघवयो: for Rama and Lakshmana, स्वस्ति अस्तु May there be aupicousness, जयंचैव victory also, अभ्यभाषत spoke.
explanation: Brahmarshi Viswamitra threatened her with hunkara (menacing sound), uttering, "Auspices to the Raghavas (Rama and Lakshmana) be aupicousness and success" victorious.

shloka_text: उद्धून्वाना रजो घोरं ताटका राघवावुभौ। रजोमोहेन महता मुहूर्तं सा व्यमोहयत्।।1.26.15।।
transliteration: uddhūnvānā rajo ghoraṃ tāṭakā rāghavāvubhau| rajomohena mahatā muhūrtaṃ sā vyamohayat
translation: सा ताटका that Tataka, घोरम् fearful, रज: dust, उद्धून्वाना throwing up, राघवौ उभौ both Rama and Lakshmana, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, महता with a great, रजोमोहेन with dust employed to confound them, व्यमोहयत् bewildered.
explanation: Tataka raising a cloud of frightening dust left the descendants of Raghu bewildered quite for a moment.

shloka_text: ततो मायां समास्थाय शिलावर्षेण राघवौ। अवाकिरत्सुमहता ततश्चुक्रोध राघव:।।1.26.16।।
transliteration: tato māyāṃ samāsthāya śilāvarṣeṇa rāghavau| avākiratsumahatā tataścukrodha rāghava:
translation: तत: then, मायाम् the power of magic, समास्थाय assuming, सुमहता with an extensive  शिलावर्षेण with rain of boulders, राघवौ on both Rama and Lakshmana, अवाकिरत् showered, तत: then, राघव: Rama, चुक्रोध was filled with wrath.
explanation: Then invoking the power of magic, she showered extensive rain of boulders on both the descendants of Raghu. Rama was enraged at this.

shloka_text: शिलावर्षं महत्तस्याश्शरवर्षेण राघव:। प्रतिहत्योपधावन्त्या: करौ चिच्छेद पत्रिभि: ।।1.26.17।।
transliteration: śilāvarṣaṃ mahattasyāśśaravarṣeṇa rāghava:| pratihatyopadhāvantyā: karau ciccheda patribhi:
translation: राघव: Rama, तस्या: her, महत् mighty, शिलावर्षम् rain of rocks, शरवर्षेण with volleys of arrows, प्रतिहत्य retaliating, उपधावन्त्या: while she was running towards him, करौ both her hands, पत्रिभि: with arrows, चिच्छेद cut off.
explanation: Rama retaliated that mighty rain of rocks with a volley of arrows. While she was advancing towards him, he cut off her hands.

shloka_text: ततश्छिन्नभुजां श्रान्तामभ्याशे परिगर्जतीम्। सौमित्रिरकरोत्क्रोधाद्धृतकर्णाग्रनासिकाम्।।1.26.18।।
transliteration: tataśchinnabhujāṃ śrāntāmabhyāśe parigarjatīm| saumitrirakarotkrodhāddhṛtakarṇāgranāsikām
translation: तत: then, छिन्नभुजाम् with her hands chopped, श्रान्ताम् tired, अभ्याशे in the nearby place, परिगर्जतीम् roaring, सौमित्रि: Lakshmana, क्रोधात् with indignation, हृतकर्णाग्रनासिकाम् अकरोत् cut off her ears and nose.
explanation: When she was tired and roaring in a nearby place with her hands chopped off, Lakshmana cut off her ears and the tip of her nose in indignation.

shloka_text: कामरूपधरा सद्य: कृत्वा रूपाण्यनेकश: । अन्तर्धानं गता यक्षी मोहयन्तीव मायया ।।1.26.19।। अश्मवर्षं विमुञ्चन्ती भैरवं विचचार ह ।
transliteration: kāmarūpadharā sadya: kṛtvā rūpāṇyanekaśa: | antardhānaṃ gatā yakṣī mohayantīva māyayā  aśmavarṣaṃ vimuñcantī bhairavaṃ vicacāra ha |
translation: अन्तर्धानं गता vanishing from the sight, यक्षी that yakshi, मोहयन्तीव as if deluding, मायया  with the power of magic, कामरूपधरा capable of assuming forms at will , सद्य: immediately, अनेकश: in various ways, रूपाणि forms , कृत्वा having assumed, अश्मवर्षम् rain of heavy rocks, विमुञ्चन्ती releasing, भैरवम् frightfully, विचचार ह moving about.
explanation: Capable of assuming forms at will, that yakshini intending to delude the princes through her power of magic, vanished from the sight. She then assumed various forms and released a rain of rocks. And started moving about frightfully.

shloka_text: ततस्तावश्मवर्षेण कीर्यमाणौ समन्तत:।।1.26.20।। दृष्ट्वा गाधिसुतश्श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
transliteration: tatastāvaśmavarṣeṇa kīryamāṇau samantata: dṛṣṭvā gādhisutaśśrīmānidaṃ vacanamabravīt|
translation: तत: then, समन्तत:on all sides, अश्मवर्षेण with rain of stones, कीर्यमाणौ being thrown out, तौ Rama and Lakshmana, दृष्ट्वा having seen, श्रीमान् auspicious, गाधिसुत: son of Gadhi, इदं वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: On seeing them hit and thrown about by a rain of stones from all sides, the  auspicious son of Gadhi, (Viswamitra) spoke these words:

shloka_text: अलं ते घृणया राम पापैषा दुष्टचारिणी।।1.26.21।। यज्ञविघ्नकरी यक्षी पुरावर्धति मायया।
transliteration: alaṃ te ghṛṇayā rāma pāpaiṣā duṣṭacāriṇī yajñavighnakarī yakṣī purāvardhati māyayā|
translation: राम Rama, ते to you, घृणया out of compassion, अलम् enough, पापा sinful, दुष्टचारिणी wicked woman, यज्ञविघ्नकरी obstructor of sacrifice, एषा यक्षी this yakshi, मायया by magic power, पुरावर्धति will regain with strength.
explanation: "O Rama she does not deserve any more compassion. This yakshini who is sinful, wicked and obstructor of sacrifice will regain her strength by her magical powers ".

shloka_text: वध्यतां तावदेवैषा पुरा सन्ध्या प्रवर्तते।।1.26.22।। रक्षांसि सन्ध्याकालेषु दुर्धर्षाणि भवन्ति वै।
transliteration: vadhyatāṃ tāvadevaiṣā purā sandhyā pravartate rakṣāṃsi sandhyākāleṣu durdharṣāṇi bhavanti vai|
translation: सन्ध्या Dusk, पुरा प्रवर्तते is approaching, तावदेव before that time, एषा वध्यताम् she may be killed, सन्ध्याकालेषु during evening time, रक्षांसि rakshasas, दुर्धर्षाणि भवन्ति वै  become unassailable.
explanation: Kill her, for dusk is fast approaching. During evening the strength of rakshasas tends to increase and they become unassailable".

shloka_text: इत्युक्तस्तु तदा यक्षी अश्मवृष्ट्याभिवर्षतीम्।।1.26.23।। दर्शयन् शब्दवेधित्वं तां रुरोध स सायकै:।
transliteration: ityuktastu tadā yakṣī aśmavṛṣṭyābhivarṣatīm darśayan śabdavedhitvaṃ tāṃ rurodha sa sāyakai:|
translation: इति in this manner, उक्त: addressed, स: Rama, तदा then, शब्दवेधित्वम् skill in targetting the object by the sound, दर्शयन् exhibiting, अश्मवृष्ट्या with rain of stones, अभिवर्षतीम् showering, ताम् यक्षीम् that yakshi, सायकै: with arrows, रुरोध prevented.
explanation: Addressed thus (by Viswamitra), Rama attacked her exhibiting his skill in targetting her by the sound and prevented with arrows the yakshini from showering  stones.

shloka_text: सा रुद्धा शरजालेन मायाबलसमन्विता।।1.26.24।। अभिदुद्राव काकुत्स्थं लक्ष्मणं च विनेदुषी।
transliteration: sā ruddhā śarajālena māyābalasamanvitā abhidudrāva kākutsthaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca vineduṣī|
translation: शरजालेन with multitude of arrows, रुद्धा prevented, मायाबलसमन्विता possessed of magical  powers, सा that female demon, विनेदुषी roaring, काकुत्स्थम् Rama, लक्ष्मणं च also Lakshmana, अभिदुद्राव advanced.
explanation: . Prevented by a multitude of arrows, she with her magical powers, advanced towards Rama and Lakshmanaroaring.

shloka_text: तामापतन्तीं वेगेन विक्रान्तामशनीमिव।।1.26.25।। शरेणोरसि विव्याथ सा पपात ममार च।
transliteration: tāmāpatantīṃ vegena vikrāntāmaśanīmiva śareṇorasi vivyātha sā papāta mamāra ca|
translation: विक्रान्ताम् advancing powerully, अशनीमिव like to a thunderbolt, वेगेन with speed, आपतन्तीम्  approaching, ताम् her, शरेण with arrow, उरसि in the chest, विव्याथ pierced,  सा पपात she fell down, ममार च also died.
explanation: Her chest pierced with an arrow, she rushing menacingly towards them like a thunderbolt fell down dead.

shloka_text: तां हतां भीमसङ्काशां दृष्ट्वा सुरपतिस्तदा।।1.26.26।। साधु साध्विति काकुत्स्थं सुराश्च समपूजयन्।
transliteration: tāṃ hatāṃ bhīmasaṅkāśāṃ dṛṣṭvā surapatistadā sādhu sādhviti kākutsthaṃ surāśca samapūjayan|
translation: तदा then, सुरपति: Indra, सुराश्च other celestial beings, हताम् slain, भीमसङ्काशाम् of terrible appearance, तां दृष्ट्वा having seen her, साधु साधु इति" well done, well done" saying so, काकुत्स्थम् Rama, समपूजयन् worshipped.
explanation: Having seen the slain yakshini of terrible appearance, Indra and other celestials worshipped Rama, exclaiming "well done, well done ".

shloka_text: उवाच परमप्रीत स्सहस्राक्ष: पुरन्दर:।।1.26.27।। सुराश्च सर्वे संहृष्टा विश्वामित्रमथाब्रुवन्।
transliteration: uvāca paramaprīta ssahasrākṣa: purandara: surāśca sarve saṃhṛṣṭā viśvāmitramathābruvan|
translation: अथ then, सहस्राक्ष: the thousandeyed, पुरन्दर: Devendra, परमप्रीत: was exceedingly pleased, उवाच said, सर्वे all, सुराश्च celestial beings, संहृष्टा: were delighted, विश्वामित्रम् addressing Viswamitra, अब्रुवन् spoke.
explanation: Then exceedingly pleased the thousandeyed Indra and all other delighted celestials  said to Viswamitra:

shloka_text: मुने कौशिक भद्रं ते सेन्द्रास्सर्वे मरुद्गणा:।।1.26.28।। तोषिता: कर्मणाऽनेन स्नेहं दर्शय राघवे।
transliteration: mune kauśika bhadraṃ te sendrāssarve marudgaṇā: toṣitā: karmaṇā'nena snehaṃ darśaya rāghave|
translation: कौशिकमुने O Ascetic Kausika, ते to you, भद्रम् may prosperity be to you, सेन्द्रा: together   with Indra, सर्वे all, मरुद्गणा: devatas, अनेन कर्मणा by this act of Rama, तोषिता: have been gratified, राघवे towards Rama, स्नेहम् friendship, दर्शय show.
explanation: "O ascetic Kausika, may prosperity be to you All devatas have been gratified by this act (of Rama) and have expressed their love for Rama.

shloka_text: प्रजापतेर्भृशाश्वस्य पुत्रान् सत्यपराक्रमान्।।1.26.29।। तपोबलभृतो ब्रह्मन् राघवाय निवेदय।
transliteration: prajāpaterbhṛśāśvasya putrān satyaparākramān tapobalabhṛto brahman rāghavāya nivedaya|
translation: ब्रह्मन् O Brahmarshi, प्रजापते: Prajapati's, भृशाश्वस्य Brishaswas', पुत्रान् sons, सत्यपराक्रमान् men of truthful prowess, तपोबलभृत़ः men endowed with ascetic energy, राघवाय for Rama, निवेदय offer.
explanation: "O Brahmarshi, you may offer to Rama, the sons of  Prajapati Brishasva who are the weapons bestowed with the power that comes from truth and ascetic energy".

shloka_text: पात्रभूतश्च ते ब्रह्मंस्तवानुगमने धृत:।।1.26.30।। कर्तव्यं च महत्कर्म सुराणां राजसूनुना।
transliteration: pātrabhūtaśca te brahmaṃstavānugamane dhṛta: kartavyaṃ ca mahatkarma surāṇāṃ rājasūnunā|
translation: ब्रह्मन् O Brahmarshi, तव अनुगमने in following you, धृत: firm, ते to you, पात्रभूत:च worthy to receive, राजसूनुना by this prince, सुराणाम् for the benefit of celestial beings, महत् many, कर्म task, कर्तव्यं च have to be accomplished.
explanation: "O Brahmarshi following you with firmness of mind, Rama is worthy to receive the weapons. He who is a prince has to accomplish many such great tasks for the benefit of the celestials".

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा सुरास्सर्वे हृष्टा जग्मुर्यथागतम्।।1.26.31।। विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य ततस्सन्ध्या प्रवर्तते।
transliteration: evamuktvā surāssarve hṛṣṭā jagmuryathāgatam viśvāmitraṃ puraskṛtya tatassandhyā pravartate|
translation: एवम् in this manner, उक्त्वा having said these words, सुरा: celestial beings, सर्वे all, हृष्टा: were pleased, विश्वामित्रम् Visvamitra, पुरस्कृत्य having honoured him, यथागतम् from where they had come from, जग्मु: returned, तत: then, सन्ध्या dusk, प्रवर्तते commences(ed).
explanation: Having said these words, the celestials were pleased. They honoured Viswamitra and returned to their abodes from where they had come. And then dusk set in.

shloka_text: ततो मुनिवर: प्रीतस्ताटकावधतोषित:।।1.26.32।। मूर्ध्नि राममुपाघ्राय इदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
transliteration: tato munivara: prītastāṭakāvadhatoṣita: mūrdhni rāmamupāghrāya idaṃ vacanamabravīt|
translation: तत: then, मुनिवर: best of ascetics, प्रीत: rejoiced, ताटकावधतोषित: pleased with slaying of Tataka , रामम् Rama, मूर्ध्नि on the head,  उपाघ्राय having smelt fondly , इदं वचनम् this  word, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Then, the best of ascetics Viswamitra rejoiced over the death of Tataka, kissed the forehead of Rama (fondly) and spoke these words:

shloka_text: इहाद्य रजनीं राम वसेम शुभदर्शन।।1.26.33।। श्व: प्रभाते गमिष्यामस्तदाश्रमपदं मम।
transliteration: ihādya rajanīṃ rāma vasema śubhadarśana śva: prabhāte gamiṣyāmastadāśramapadaṃ mama|
translation: शुभदर्शन O Auspicious looking one, राम Rama, अद्य today, रजनीम् this night, इह here, वसेम we will live, श्व: tomorrow, प्रभाते in the morning, मम my, तत् आश्रमपदम् that  hermitage, गमिष्याम: we shall proceed.
explanation: "O auspiciouslooking Rama tonight we shall stay here. Tomorrow morning we proceed to my hermitage".

shloka_text: विश्वामित्रवच: श्रुत्वा हृष्टो दशरथात्मज:।।1.26.34।। उवास रजनीं तत्र ताटकाया वने सुखम्।
transliteration: viśvāmitravaca: śrutvā hṛṣṭo daśarathātmaja: uvāsa rajanīṃ tatra tāṭakāyā vane sukham|
translation: विश्वामित्रवच: words of Visvamitra, श्रुत्वा having heard, दशरथात्मज: son of Dasaratha, हृष्ट: rejoiced, तत्र there, ताटकाया: Tataka's, वने in the forest, सुखम् happily, रजनीम् night, उवास lived.
explanation: Having heard the words of Viswamitra, Rama rejoiced and rested happily that night in the Tataka forest .

shloka_text: मुक्तशापं वनं तच्च तस्मिन्नेव तदाहनि।।1.26.35।। रमणीयं विबभ्राज यथा चैत्ररथं वनम्।
transliteration: muktaśāpaṃ vanaṃ tacca tasminneva tadāhani ramaṇīyaṃ vibabhrāja yathā caitrarathaṃ vanam|
translation: तदा then, तस्मिन् अहनि एव on that day itself, तत् वनं च that forest also, मुक्तशापम् freed  from the curse, चैत्ररथम् known as Chitraratha, वनम् forest, यथा the samemanner, रमणीयम् charming, विबभ्राज shone.
explanation: Freed from the curse from that day that forest looked charming and shone like Chitraratha Kubera's (garden).

shloka_text: निहत्य तां यक्षसुतां स राम: प्रशस्यमानस्सुरसिद्धसङ्घै:। उवास तस्मिन्मुनिना सहैव प्रभातवेलां प्रतिबोध्यमान:।।1.26.36।।
transliteration: nihatya tāṃ yakṣasutāṃ sa rāma: praśasyamānassurasiddhasaṅghai:| uvāsa tasminmuninā sahaiva prabhātavelāṃ pratibodhyamāna:
translation: स: राम: that Rama, तां यक्षसुताम् that daughter of that yaksha, निहत्य having slain, सुरसिद्धसङ्घै: by the  multitude of devatas and siddhas, प्रशस्यमान: having been praised, मुनिना सह along with sage, Visvamitra, तस्मिन्नेव in the same forest, प्रभातवेलाम् at the first glimpse of dawn, प्रतिबोध्यमान: having been awakened, उवास lived.
explanation: Rama having killed the daughter of yaksha was praised by multitudes of devatas and siddhas. He stayed in the same forest with the sage. At the first glimpse of dawn, he was awakened by the sage (Viswamitra). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे षड्विंशस्सर्ग:।।7 Thus ends the twentysixth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ तां रजनीमुष्य विश्वामित्रो महायशाः। प्रहस्य राघवं वाक्यमुवाच मधुराक्षरम्।।1.27.1।।
transliteration: atha tāṃ rajanīmuṣya viśvāmitro mahāyaśāḥ| prahasya rāghavaṃ vākyamuvāca madhurākṣaram
translation: अथ thereafter, महायशाः illustrious, विश्वामित्रः Visvamitra, तां रजनीम् that night, उष्य having  stayed, प्रहस्य smiling, राघवम् addresseing, मधुराक्षरम् with sweet accents, वाक्यम् these words, उवाच spoke.
explanation: The night over, illustrious Viswamitra called Rama with a sweet smile.
comments: Viswamitra confers celestial weapons on Rama

shloka_text: परितुष्टोऽस्मि भद्रं ते राजपुत्र महायशः। प्रीत्या परमया युक्तो ददाम्यस्त्राणि सर्वशः।।1.27.2।।
transliteration: parituṣṭo'smi bhadraṃ te rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ| prītyā paramayā yukto dadāmyastrāṇi sarvaśaḥ
translation: महायशः of great renown, राजपुत्र O Prince, परितुष्टः अस्मि  I am extremely pleased, ते भद्रम् May you prosper, परमया प्रीत्या with great love and affection, युक्तः filled with, अस्त्राणि weapons, सर्वशः from all over, ददामि I shall give.
explanation: "O prince of great renown, I am extremely pleased. May you prosper Out of great love and affection for you I shall make over all the weapons.

shloka_text: देवासुरगणान्वापि सगन्धर्वोरगानपि। यैरमित्रान् प्रसह्याजौ वशीकृत्य जयिष्यसि।।1.27.3।। तानि दिव्यानि भद्रं ते ददाम्यस्त्राणि सर्वशः ।
transliteration: devāsuragaṇānvāpi sagandharvoragānapi| yairamitrān prasahyājau vaśīkṛtya jayiṣyasi tāni divyāni bhadraṃ te dadāmyastrāṇi sarvaśaḥ |
