translation: भगवान् venerable, महतपा: renowned ascetic, वसिष्ठ: ऋषि: rishi Vasishta, जनकम् addressing king Janaka, तथा इति "Be it so", उक्त्वा having said, विश्वामित्रम् to Visvamitra, धार्मिकम् virtuous, शतानन्दं च Satananda, पुरस्कृत्य in the forefront, प्रपामध्ये in the center of the marriage pavillion, विधिवत् in accordance with scriptures, वेदिम् altar, कृत्वा having constructed, गन्धपुष्पै: with fragrant flowers, सुवर्णपालिकाभिश्च with golden hollow plates, साङ्कुरै: with sprouts, छिद्रकुम्भैश्च water pots containing holes, अङ्कुराढ्यै: filled with sprouts, शरावैश्च earthenware vessels, सधूपकै: by burning frgrant insenses, धूपपात्रै: holders of frgrant insenses, शङ्खपात्रै: conch shaped vessels, सृवै: sacrificial ladles, सृग्भि: bowls, अर्घ्याभिपूरितै: filled with with water for Arghya and other purposes, पात्रै: with vessels, लाजपूर्णै: roasted paddy, पात्रीभि: with vessels, अभिसंस्कृतै: sanctified, अक्षतै: rice grains, ताम् that, वेदिम् altar, समन्तत on all sides, अलञ्चकार adorned.
explanation: Venerable and renowned ascetic Vasishta said "Be it so".And with Viswamitra and virtuous Satananda in the forefront, an altar was duly improvised in the centre of the sacrificial pavilion. He adorned the altar on all sides  with fragrant flowers, golden ladles, waterpots with holes filled with sprouts, earthen vessels with sprouts, holders of burning fragrant incense conchshaped vessels, sacrificial ladles, bowls filled with with water for arghya and other purposes, vessels with roasted paddy and grains of rice.

shloka_text: दर्भैस्समैस्समास्तीर्य विधिवन्मन्त्रपूर्वकम्। अग्निमादाय वेद्यां तु विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम्।।1.73.24।। जुहावाग्नौ महातेजा वसिष्ठो भगवानृषि:।
transliteration: darbhaissamaissamāstīrya vidhivanmantrapūrvakam| agnimādāya vedyāṃ tu vidhimantrapuraskṛtam juhāvāgnau mahātejā vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣi:|
translation: महातेजा: highly lustrous, भगवान् worshipful, वसिष्ठ: ऋषि: rishi Vasistha, समै: of equal proportions, दर्भै: Darbha grass, विधिवत् according to tradition, मन्त्रपुरस्कृतम् reciting mantra, समास्तीर्य having strewn, विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम् reciting mantras according to scriptures, वेद्याम् on the altar, अग्निम् fire, आदाय having placed, अग्नौ in the fire, जुहाव  offered oblations.
explanation: Brilliant and worshipful rishi Vasishta chanted, mantras according to tradition, put the darbha grass of equal proportions around the altar, placed the fire on the altar, recited the mantras from the scriptures and offered oblations into the flame.

shloka_text: ततस्सीतां समानीय सर्वाभरणभूषिताम्।।1.73.25।। समक्षमग्ने स्संस्थाप्य राघवाभिमुखे तदा। अब्रवीज्जनको राजा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनम्।।1.73.26।।
transliteration: tatassītāṃ samānīya sarvābharaṇabhūṣitām samakṣamagne ssaṃsthāpya rāghavābhimukhe tadā| abravījjanako rājā kausalyānandavardhanam
translation: तत thereafter, राजा king, जनक: Janaka, सर्वाभरणभूषिताम् adorned with various ornaments, सीताम् Sita, समानीय having brought, अग्ने: समक्षम् in the presence of Agni, राघवाभिमुखे facing Rama, संस्थाप्य placing, तदा then, कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनम् enhancing the joy of Kausalya,  अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Thereafter king Janaka brought Sita adorned with various ornaments and placed her in the presence of Agni in front of Rama, the enhancer of the joy of Kausalya. And said:

shloka_text: ततस्सीतां समानीय सर्वाभरणभूषिताम्।।1.73.25।। समक्षमग्ने स्संस्थाप्य राघवाभिमुखे तदा। अब्रवीज्जनको राजा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनम्।।1.73.26।।
transliteration: tatassītāṃ samānīya sarvābharaṇabhūṣitām samakṣamagne ssaṃsthāpya rāghavābhimukhe tadā| abravījjanako rājā kausalyānandavardhanam
translation: तत thereafter, राजा king, जनक: Janaka, सर्वाभरणभूषिताम् adorned with various ornaments, सीताम् Sita, समानीय having brought, अग्ने: समक्षम् in the presence of Agni, राघवाभिमुखे facing Rama, संस्थाप्य placing, तदा then, कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनम् enhancing the joy of Kausalya,  अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Thereafter king Janaka brought Sita adorned with various ornaments and placed her in the presence of Agni in front of Rama, the enhancer of the joy of Kausalya. And said:

shloka_text: इयं सीता मम सुता सहधर्मचरी तव। प्रतीच्छ चैनां भद्रं ते पाणिं गृह्णीष्व पाणिना।।1.73.27।।
transliteration: iyaṃ sītā mama sutā sahadharmacarī tava| pratīccha caināṃ bhadraṃ te pāṇiṃ gṛhṇīṣva pāṇinā
translation: मम my, सुता daughter, तव your, सहधर्मचरी with you observing righteous deeds, सीता Sita, इयम् this girl, एनाम् her, प्रतीच्छ च accept, ते भद्रम् prosperity to you, पाणिम् her hand, पाणिना with your hand, गृह्णीष्व hold.
explanation: "This my daughter Sita will be your partner in performing her rightful duty. Accept her. Farewell. Take her hand into your own.

shloka_text: पतिव्रता महाभागा छायेवानुगता सदा। इत्युक्त्वा प्राक्षिपद्राजा मन्त्रपूतं जलं तदा।।1.73.28।।
transliteration: pativratā mahābhāgā chāyevānugatā sadā| ityuktvā prākṣipadrājā mantrapūtaṃ jalaṃ tadā
translation: महाभागा highly fortunate, पतिव्रता devoted, faithful and loyal wife, सदा always, छाया इव like shadow, अनुगता follows, इति thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, राजा king, तदा then,मन्त्रपूतम् sanctified with mantra, जलम् water, प्राक्षिपत् released.
explanation: By being a devoted wife this highly fortunate Sita would always follow you like a shadow". Thus spoken, he sprinkled the water sanctified with mantras (on them).

shloka_text: साधु साध्विति देवाना मृषीणां वदतां तदा	। देवदुन्दुभिर्निर्घोष: पुष्पवर्षो महानभूत्।।1.73.29।।
transliteration: sādhu sādhviti devānā mṛṣīṇāṃ vadatāṃ tadā	| devadundubhirnirghoṣa: puṣpavarṣo mahānabhūt
translation: तदा then, साधु साधु इति "Well, Well" saying so, वदताम् exclaiming, ऋषीणाम् sages, देवानाम् devatas, देवदुन्दुभिनिर्घोष: sounded the celestial kettledrums, महान् great, पुष्पवर्ष: rain of flowers, अभूत् fell.
explanation: Then gods and sages exclaimed: 'well, well'. Celestial kettledrums were sounded and there was a steady rain of flowers.

shloka_text: एवं दत्त्वा तदा सीतां मन्त्रोदकपुरस्कृताम्	। अब्रवीज्जनको राजा हर्षेणाभिपरिप्लुत:।।1.73.30।।
transliteration: evaṃ dattvā tadā sītāṃ mantrodakapuraskṛtām	| abravījjanako rājā harṣeṇābhiparipluta:
translation: तदा then, जनक: राजा king Janaka, मन्त्रोदकपुरस्कृताम् with waters sanctified by mantras, सीताम् Sita, दत्वा having given, हर्षेण with delight, अभिपरिप्लुत: eyes suffused with tears, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Then king Janaka sprinkled on Sita waters sanctified by mantras, and immersed in delight said:

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणागच्छ भद्रं ते ऊर्मिलामुद्यतां मया। प्रतीच्छ पाणिं गृह्णीष्व माभूत्कालस्य पर्यय:।।1.73.31।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇāgaccha bhadraṃ te ūrmilāmudyatāṃ mayā| pratīccha pāṇiṃ gṛhṇīṣva mābhūtkālasya paryaya:
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, आगच्छ come, मया by me, उद्यताम् ready to be bestowed upon, ऊर्मिलाम् Urmila, प्रतीच्छ accept, पाणिम् her hand, (पाणिना with your hand), गृह्णीष्व hold, कालस्य time, पर्यय: delay, माभूत् let not happen.
explanation: "Lakshmana come and accept my daughter. Urmila ready to be bestowed upon you by me. Take her hand. Let there be no delay".

shloka_text: तमेवमुक्त्वा जनको भरतं चाभ्यभाषत। गृहाण पाणिं माण्डव्या: पाणिना रघुनन्दन	।।1.73.32।।
transliteration: tamevamuktvā janako bharataṃ cābhyabhāṣata| gṛhāṇa pāṇiṃ māṇḍavyā: pāṇinā raghunandana
translation: जनक: Janaka, तम् to Lakshmana, एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, भरतं च addressing  Bharata, अभ्यभाषत had spoken, रघुनन्दन O Descendent of Raghu, पाणिना with your hand, माण्डव्या: Mandavi's, पाणिम् hand, गृहाण hold.
explanation: Janaka, having spoken thus to Lakshmana addressed Bharata: "O Descendant of the Raghus hold Mandavi's hand in your own".

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नं चापि धर्मात्मा अब्रवीज्जनकेश्वर:। श्रुतकीर्त्या महाबाहो पाणिं गृह्णीष्व पाणिना।।1.73.33।।
transliteration: śatrughnaṃ cāpi dharmātmā abravījjanakeśvara:| śrutakīrtyā mahābāho pāṇiṃ gṛhṇīṣva pāṇinā
translation: धर्मात्मा Virtuous, जनकेश्वर: monarch Janaka, शत्रुघ्नं चापि addressing Satrghna also, अब्रवीत् spoke, महाबाहो O Mighty armed one, पाणिना with your hand, श्रुतकीर्त्या: Srutakirti's, पाणिम् hand, गृह्णीष्व hold.
explanation: The righteous king Janaka, said again: "O Mightyarmed Satrughna take the hands of Srutakirti".

shloka_text: सर्वे भवन्तस्सौम्याश्च सर्वे सुचरितव्रता:। पत्नीभिस्सन्तु काकुत्स्था माभूत्कालस्य पर्यय:।।1.73.34।।
transliteration: sarve bhavantassaumyāśca sarve sucaritavratā:| patnībhissantu kākutsthā mābhūtkālasya paryaya:
translation: काकुत्स्था: O Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata and Satrughna, भवन्त: all of you, सर्वे all, सौम्या: च gentle also, सुचरितव्रता: possess good conduct and faithful vows, पत्नीभि: with your wives, सन्तु become, कालस्य of time, पर्यय: delay, माभूत् let not happen.
explanation: O Descendants of Kakustha (Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata and Satrughna) you all are gentle. You possess sound character. You are true to your vows. Live with your wives. Let there be no delay".

shloka_text: जनकस्य वच श्शृत्वा पाणीन् पाणिभिरास्पृशन्। चत्वारस्ते चतसृ़णां वसिष्ठस्य मते स्थिता:।।1.73.35।।
transliteration: janakasya vaca śśṛtvā pāṇīn pāṇibhirāspṛśan| catvāraste catasṛ़ṇāṃ vasiṣṭhasya mate sthitā:
translation: ते those, चत्वार: four, जनकस्य Janaka's, वच: words, श्रुत्वा having heard, वसिष्ठस्य Vasishta's, मते consent, स्थिता: staying, पाणिभि: hands, चतसृ़णां those four sisters, पाणीन् hands, अस्पृशन् touched.
explanation: At the words of Janaka the four princes took the hands of the four sisters with their own with the consent of Vasishta .

shloka_text: अग्निं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य वेदिं राजानमेव च। ऋषींश्चैव महात्मानस्सभार्या रघुसत्तमा:।।1.73.36।। यथोक्तेन तदा चक्रुर्विवाहं विधिपूर्वकम्।
transliteration: agniṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vediṃ rājānameva ca| ṛṣīṃścaiva mahātmānassabhāryā raghusattamā: yathoktena tadā cakrurvivāhaṃ vidhipūrvakam|
translation: महात्मान: magnanimous, रघुसत्तमा: greatest in the race of Raghu, सभार्या accompanied by their wives, अग्निं sacred fire, वेदिम् altar, राजानमेव च king Janaka, ऋषींश्चैव sages also, प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य having circumabulted, यथोक्तेन in obedience to the directions, विधिपूर्वकम् in accordance with the scriptures, विवाहम् marriage, चक्रु: made.
explanation: The great, noble princes of the race of Raghu, accompanied by their wives circumambulated the altar of the sacred fire. King Janaka and the sages in obedience to the directions of Vasishta and in accordance with the sastras conducted the matrimonial.

shloka_text: काकुत्स्थैश्च गृहीतेषु ललितेषु च पाणिषु।।1.73.37।। पुष्पवृष्टिर्महत्यासीदन्तरिक्षात्सुभास्वरा।
transliteration: kākutsthaiśca gṛhīteṣu laliteṣu ca pāṇiṣu puṣpavṛṣṭirmahatyāsīdantarikṣātsubhāsvarā|
translation: काकुत्स्थै: Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata and Satrughna, ललितेषु elegant, पाणिषु hands, गृहीतेषु while accepting, अन्तरिक्षात् from the sky, सुभास्वरा with immense splendour, महती great, पुष्पवृष्टि: rain of flowers, आसीत् was showered.
explanation: While the descendants of Kakustha (Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata and Satrughna) held the elegant hands (of Sita, Urmila, Mandavi, and Srutakirti) there was a heavy rain of bright flowers from the sky.

shloka_text: अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः। आपृष्ट्वा तौ च राजानौ जगामोत्तरपर्वतम्	।।1.74.1।। आशीर्भि: पूरयित्वा च कुमारांश्च सराघवान्।
transliteration: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ| āpṛṣṭvā tau ca rājānau jagāmottaraparvatam	 āśīrbhi: pūrayitvā ca kumārāṃśca sarāghavān|
translation: अथ afterwards, रात्र्याम् when the night, व्यतीतायाम् had passed away, स: that, महामुनि: great ascetic, विश्वामित्र: Visvamitra, राघवान् born in the race of Raghu, कुमारान् च princes, आशीर्भि: with blessing, पूरयित्वा having filled, तौ those two, राजानै kings, आपृष्ट्वा having taken leave of them, उत्तरपर्वतम् northern mountains, जगाम went.
explanation: Night over, the great ascetic Viswamitra, profusely blessed the princes born in the race of Raghu, took leave of the two kings and set out towards the northern (Himalayas) mountains.
comments: Viswamitra leaves for the Himavat mountain--king Janaka offers gifts to his daughters--King Dasaratha departs for his kingdomencounter with Parasurama.

shloka_text: विश्वामित्रे गते राजा वैदेहं मिथिलाधिपम्	। आपृष्ट्वाऽथ जगामाशु राजा दशरथ: पुरीम्।।1.74.2।।
transliteration: viśvāmitre gate rājā vaidehaṃ mithilādhipam	| āpṛṣṭvā'tha jagāmāśu rājā daśaratha: purīm
translation: विश्वामित्रे when Visvamitra, गते had departed, अथ thereafter, राजा one who causes joy to his people, दशरथ: राजा king Dasaratha, मिथिलाधिपम् lord of Mithila, वैदेहम् king Janaka, आपृष्ट्वा taking leave of him, आशु speedily, पुरीम् to city of Ayodhya, जगाम went.
explanation: With the departure of Viswamitra, king Dasaratha who was the source of happiness to his subjects took leave of Janaka, king of Mithila and speedily set out for the city of Ayodhya.

shloka_text: गच्छन्तं तं तु राजानमन्वगच्छन्नराधिप:।।1.74.3।। अथ राजा विदेहानां ददौ कन्याधनं बहु।
transliteration: gacchantaṃ taṃ tu rājānamanvagacchannarādhipa: atha rājā videhānāṃ dadau kanyādhanaṃ bahu|
translation: नराधिप: king Janaka, गच्छन्तम् while going, तम् that, राजानम् king Dasaratha, अन्वगच्छत् followed, अथ thereafter, विदेहानाम् lord of Videhas, राजा king Janaka, बहु plenty of, कन्याधनम् gifts to his daughters, ददौ gave.
explanation: King Janaka, lord of the Videhas, gave plenty of gifts to his daughters and followed king Dasaratha for some distance on his journey to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: गवां शतसहस्राणि बहूनि मिथिलेश्वर:। कम्बलानां च मुख्यानां क्षौमकोट्यंबराणि च।।1.74.4।। हस्त्यश्वरथपादातं दिव्यरूपं स्वलङ्कृतम्	। ददौ कन्यापिता तासां दासीदासमनुत्तमम्	।।1.74.5।।
transliteration: gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi bahūni mithileśvara:| kambalānāṃ ca mukhyānāṃ kṣaumakoṭyaṃbarāṇi ca hastyaśvarathapādātaṃ divyarūpaṃ svalaṅkṛtam	| dadau kanyāpitā tāsāṃ dāsīdāsamanuttamam
translation: कन्यापिता father of brides, मिथिलेश्वर: lord of Mithila, गवाम् of cows, बहूनि several, शतसहस्राणि hundred thousands, मुख्यानाम् of excellent, कम्बलानाम् carpets, क्षौमकोट्यम्बराणि च crores of silk garments, हस्त्यश्वरथपादातम् elephants, horses, chariots and infantry, 	दिव्यरूपम् of celestial beauty, स्वलङ्कृतम् welldecorated, अनुत्तमम् excellent, दासीदासम् male and female servants, तासाम् for them, ददौ gave.
explanation: The king of Mithila and father of the brides gave a hundred thousand cows, excellent woollen carpets, crores of silk garments, four divisions of elephants, horses, chariots and infantry and welldecorated, excellent male and  maidservants shining in celestial beauty.

shloka_text: गवां शतसहस्राणि बहूनि मिथिलेश्वर:। कम्बलानां च मुख्यानां क्षौमकोट्यंबराणि च।।1.74.4।। हस्त्यश्वरथपादातं दिव्यरूपं स्वलङ्कृतम्	। ददौ कन्यापिता तासां दासीदासमनुत्तमम्	।।1.74.5।।
transliteration: gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi bahūni mithileśvara:| kambalānāṃ ca mukhyānāṃ kṣaumakoṭyaṃbarāṇi ca hastyaśvarathapādātaṃ divyarūpaṃ svalaṅkṛtam	| dadau kanyāpitā tāsāṃ dāsīdāsamanuttamam
translation: कन्यापिता father of brides, मिथिलेश्वर: lord of Mithila, गवाम् of cows, बहूनि several, शतसहस्राणि hundred thousands, मुख्यानाम् of excellent, कम्बलानाम् carpets, क्षौमकोट्यम्बराणि च crores of silk garments, हस्त्यश्वरथपादातम् elephants, horses, chariots and infantry, 	दिव्यरूपम् of celestial beauty, स्वलङ्कृतम् welldecorated, अनुत्तमम् excellent, दासीदासम् male and female servants, तासाम् for them, ददौ gave.
explanation: The king of Mithila and father of the brides gave a hundred thousand cows, excellent woollen carpets, crores of silk garments, four divisions of elephants, horses, chariots and infantry and welldecorated, excellent male and  maidservants shining in celestial beauty.

shloka_text: हिरण्यस्य सुवर्णस्य मुक्तानां विद्रुमस्य च।।1.74.6।। ददौ परमसंहृष्ट: कन्याधनमनुत्तमम्।
transliteration: hiraṇyasya suvarṇasya muktānāṃ vidrumasya ca dadau paramasaṃhṛṣṭa: kanyādhanamanuttamam|
translation: परमसंहृष्ट: immensely pleased, हिरण्यस्य golden, सुवर्णस्य of fine glow, मुक्तानाम् pearls', विद्रुमस्य corals, अनुत्तमम् excellent, कन्याधनम् ornaments to his daughters, ददौ gave.
explanation: Immensely delighted, he gave his excellent daughters gold, pearls and corals.

shloka_text: दत्त्वा बहु धनं राजा समनुज्ञाप्य पार्थिवम्।।1.74.7।। प्रविवेश स्वनिलयं मिथिलां मिथिलेश्वर:।
transliteration: dattvā bahu dhanaṃ rājā samanujñāpya pārthivam praviveśa svanilayaṃ mithilāṃ mithileśvara:|
translation: मिथिलेश्वर: lord of Mithila, राजा king Janaka, बहु धनं plenty of wealth, दत्त्वा having given, पार्थिवम् king Dasaratha, समनुज्ञाप्य after making him give consent to Janaka to go back, स्वनिलयम् own residence, मिथिलाम् Mithila, प्रविवेश entered.
explanation: The Lord of Mithila bestowed a lot of wealth on his daughters and with the consent of the king (Dasaratha) reentered his residence in Mithila.

shloka_text: राजाऽप्ययोध्याधिपतिस्सह पुत्रैर्महात्मभि:। ऋषीन् सर्वान् पुरस्कृत्य जगाम सबलानुग:।।1.74.8।।
transliteration: rājā'pyayodhyādhipatissaha putrairmahātmabhi:| ṛṣīn sarvān puraskṛtya jagāma sabalānuga:
translation: अयोध्याधिपति: lord of Ayodhya, राजापि king Dasaratha also, महात्मभि: with illustrious, पुत्रै: सह along with his sons, सर्वान् all, ऋषीन् sages, पुरस्कृत्य placing him in the forefront, सबलानुग: followed by his army and followers, जगाम went.
explanation: King Dasaratha of Ayodhya also left along with his great sons preceded by the sages and followed by the army.

shloka_text: गच्छन्तं तं नरव्याघ्रं सर्षिसङ्घं सराघवम्।।1.74.9।। घोरा: स्म पक्षिणो वाचो व्याहरन्ति ततस्तत:।
transliteration: gacchantaṃ taṃ naravyāghraṃ sarṣisaṅghaṃ sarāghavam ghorā: sma pakṣiṇo vāco vyāharanti tatastata:|
translation: सर्षिसङ्घम् with hosts of sages, सराघवम् with Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata and Satrughna, नरव्याघ्रम् tiger among men, तम् that, Dasaratha, ततस्तत: here and there, घोरा: frightening, पक्षिण: birds, वाच: disagreeable sounds, व्याहरन्ति स्म uttered.
explanation: While this tiger among men Dasaratha, was returning with the hosts of sages and his sons, he observed here and there frightening birds making disagreeable sounds.

shloka_text: भौमाश्चैव मृगा स्सर्वे गच्छन्ति स्म प्रदक्षिणम्।।1.74.10।। तान् दृष्ट्वा राजशार्दूलो वसिष्ठं पर्यपृच्छत।
transliteration: bhaumāścaiva mṛgā ssarve gacchanti sma pradakṣiṇam tān dṛṣṭvā rājaśārdūlo vasiṣṭhaṃ paryapṛcchata|
translation: भौमा: those relating to earth, सर्वे all, मृगा: beasts, प्रदक्षिणम् moving to the right, गच्छन्ति  went away, तान् them, दृष्ट्वा having seen, राजशार्दूल: best among men, Dasaratha, वसिष्ठम् Vasishta, पर्यपृच्छत enquired.
explanation: Seeing the beasts on the way rushing to the right the tiger among men, enquired of Vasishta:

shloka_text: असौम्या: पक्षिणो घोरा मृगाश्चापि प्रदक्षिणा:।।1.74.11।। किमिदं हृदयोत्कम्पि मनो मम विषीदति।
transliteration: asaumyā: pakṣiṇo ghorā mṛgāścāpi pradakṣiṇā: kimidaṃ hṛdayotkampi mano mama viṣīdati|
translation: घोरा: freightening, पक्षिण: birds, असौम्या: are disagreeable, मृगाश्चापि deers also, प्रदक्षिणा: on to their right, हृदयोत्कम्पि trembling my heart, इदम् this, किम् what, मम my, मन: mind, विषीदति depressed of spirits.
explanation: "While the frightening birds are inauspicious, the deer on the right are favourables Why is this? My heart beats. My mind is depressed.

shloka_text: राज्ञो दशरथस्यैतच्छ्रुत्वा वाक्यं महानृषि:।।1.74.12।। उवाच मधुरां वाणीं श्रूयतामस्य यत्फलम्।
transliteration: rājño daśarathasyaitacchrutvā vākyaṃ mahānṛṣi: uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ śrūyatāmasya yatphalam|
translation: महानृषि: that great rishi Vasishta, राज्ञ: दशरथस्य king Dasarath's, एतत् these, वाक्यम् words, श्रुत्वा having listened, मधुराम् in gentle accents, वाणीम् words, उवाच spoke, अस्य for this, यत् which, फलम् consequence, श्रूयताम् may be heard.
explanation: To these words of king Dasaratha the great ascetic Vasishta replied in a gentle voice, "I shall tell you the consequences Listen".

shloka_text: उपस्थितं भयं घोरं दिव्यं पक्षिमुखाच्च्युतम्।।1.74.13।। मृगा: प्रशमयन्त्येते सन्तापस्त्यज्यतामयम्।
transliteration: upasthitaṃ bhayaṃ ghoraṃ divyaṃ pakṣimukhāccyutam mṛgā: praśamayantyete santāpastyajyatāmayam|
translation: पक्षिमुखात् from the mouth of these birds, च्युतम् released (foretells), दिव्यम् of celestial nature, उपस्थितम् befallen, घोरम् dreadful, भयम् fear, एते these, मृगा: beasts, प्रशमयन्ति restoring peace, अयम् this, सन्ताप: grief, त्यज्यताम् may be abandoned.
explanation: The dreadful cries from the mouths of birds foretell an event of celestial nature likely to befall but the movements other of deer indicate restoration of peace. Therefore do not grieve.

shloka_text: तेषां संवदतां तत्र वायु: प्रादुर्बभूव ह।।1.74.14।। कम्पयन् पृथिवीं सर्वां पातयंश्च द्रुमांच्छुभान्।
transliteration: teṣāṃ saṃvadatāṃ tatra vāyu: prādurbabhūva ha kampayan pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ pātayaṃśca drumāṃcchubhān|
translation: तेषां when they, संवदताम् were conversing, तत्र there, पृथिवीम् the earth, कम्पयन् shaking, शुभान् beautiful, द्रुमान् trees, पातयन् felling, वायु: wind, प्रादुर्बभूव ह arose.
explanation: While they were conversing, a storm blew, shaking the earth and felling down beautiful trees.

shloka_text: तमसा संवृतस्सूर्य स्सर्वा न प्रबभुर्दिश।।1.74.15।। भस्मना चावृतं सर्वं संमूढमिव तद्बलम्।
transliteration: tamasā saṃvṛtassūrya ssarvā na prababhurdiśa bhasmanā cāvṛtaṃ sarvaṃ saṃmūḍhamiva tadbalam|
translation: सूर्य: Sun, तमसा with darkness, संवृत: covered, सर्वा: all, दिश: cardinal quarters, न प्रबभु: did not shine, तत् that, सर्वम् all, बलम् army, भस्मना with ashes, आवृतं covered with, संमूढमिव as if fainted.
explanation: The Sun was wrapped in dark. The quarters were devoid of brightness. The entire army was covered with ashes, as if they fainted.

shloka_text: वसिष्ठश्चर्षयश्चान्ये राजा च ससुतस्तदा	।।1.74.16।। संसज्ञा इव तत्रासन् सर्वमन्यद्विचेतनम्।
transliteration: vasiṣṭhaścarṣayaścānye rājā ca sasutastadā	 saṃsajñā iva tatrāsan sarvamanyadvicetanam|
translation: तदा then, वसिष्ठश्च Vasishta, अन्ये other, ऋषयश्च saints, ससुत: with his sons, राजा king Dasaratha, ससंज्ञा: इव as if having consciousness, (तत्र)आसन् remained, अन्यत् others, सर्वम् entire, विचेतनम् lost their consciousness.
explanation: At that time Vasishta and other saints, the king and his sons held their senses under control. All others lost their consciousness.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तमसि घोरे तु भस्मच्छन्नेव सा चमू:।।1.74.17।। ददर्श भीमसङ्काशं जटामण्डलधारिणम्। भार्गवं जामदग्न्यं तं राजराजविमर्दिनम्।।1.74.18।। कैलासमिव दुर्धर्षं कालाग्निमिव दुस्सहम्। ज्वलंतमिव तेजोभिर्दुर्निरीक्ष्यं पृथग्जनै:।।1.74.19।। स्कन्धे चासज्य परशुं धनुर्विद्युद्गणोपमम्	। प्रगृह्य शरमुख्यं च त्रिपुरघ्नं यथा शिवम्।।1.74.20।।
transliteration: tasmiṃstamasi ghore tu bhasmacchanneva sā camū: dadarśa bhīmasaṅkāśaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam| bhārgavaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ taṃ rājarājavimardinam kailāsamiva durdharṣaṃ kālāgnimiva dussaham| jvalaṃtamiva tejobhirdurnirīkṣyaṃ pṛthagjanai: skandhe cāsajya paraśuṃ dhanurvidyudgaṇopamam	| pragṛhya śaramukhyaṃ ca tripuraghnaṃ yathā śivam
translation: तस्मिन् In that, घोरे fearful, तमसि darkness, भस्मच्छन्नेव looking as if covered with ashes, सा चमू: that army, भीमसङ्काशम् looking dreadful, जटामण्डलधारिणम् wearing a crown of  matted hair, राजराजविमर्दिनम् decimated the king of kings, कैलासमिव like Kailasa Mountain, दुर्धर्षम् inaccessible, कालाग्निमिव like the fire at the time of dissolution, दुस्सहम् difficult to endure, तेजोभि: with energy, ज्वलन्तमिव as if blazing, पृथग्जनै: by ordinary people, दुर्निरीक्षम् incapable of being gazed upon, परशुम् axe, स्कन्धे on his shoulder, आसज्य hanging, विद्युद्गणोपमम् resembling group of lightenings, धनु: bow, शरमुख्यम्  principal arrow, प्रगृह्य grasping, त्रिपुरघ्नम् slayer of Tripura, शिवं यथा like Siva, तम् that, भार्गवम् descendent of Bhrugu, जामदग्नयम् son of Jamadagni, ददर्श beheld.
explanation: In that dreadful darkness while the army looked as if covered with ashes, king Dasaratha encountered the repressor of kings, descendant of Bhrugu and son of Jamadagni with a terrible crown of matted hair, inaccessible like Kailasa mountain and unendurable like the fire at the time of dissolution. The laymen gazing at his blazing energy,hanging an axe on his shoulder and holding a bow in his hand which flashed like lighning and the principal arrow he looked like Siva at the time of slaying of Tripura.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तमसि घोरे तु भस्मच्छन्नेव सा चमू:।।1.74.17।। ददर्श भीमसङ्काशं जटामण्डलधारिणम्। भार्गवं जामदग्न्यं तं राजराजविमर्दिनम्।।1.74.18।। कैलासमिव दुर्धर्षं कालाग्निमिव दुस्सहम्। ज्वलंतमिव तेजोभिर्दुर्निरीक्ष्यं पृथग्जनै:।।1.74.19।। स्कन्धे चासज्य परशुं धनुर्विद्युद्गणोपमम्	। प्रगृह्य शरमुख्यं च त्रिपुरघ्नं यथा शिवम्।।1.74.20।।
transliteration: tasmiṃstamasi ghore tu bhasmacchanneva sā camū: dadarśa bhīmasaṅkāśaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam| bhārgavaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ taṃ rājarājavimardinam kailāsamiva durdharṣaṃ kālāgnimiva dussaham| jvalaṃtamiva tejobhirdurnirīkṣyaṃ pṛthagjanai: skandhe cāsajya paraśuṃ dhanurvidyudgaṇopamam	| pragṛhya śaramukhyaṃ ca tripuraghnaṃ yathā śivam
translation: तस्मिन् In that, घोरे fearful, तमसि darkness, भस्मच्छन्नेव looking as if covered with ashes, सा चमू: that army, भीमसङ्काशम् looking dreadful, जटामण्डलधारिणम् wearing a crown of  matted hair, राजराजविमर्दिनम् decimated the king of kings, कैलासमिव like Kailasa Mountain, दुर्धर्षम् inaccessible, कालाग्निमिव like the fire at the time of dissolution, दुस्सहम् difficult to endure, तेजोभि: with energy, ज्वलन्तमिव as if blazing, पृथग्जनै: by ordinary people, दुर्निरीक्षम् incapable of being gazed upon, परशुम् axe, स्कन्धे on his shoulder, आसज्य hanging, विद्युद्गणोपमम् resembling group of lightenings, धनु: bow, शरमुख्यम्  principal arrow, प्रगृह्य grasping, त्रिपुरघ्नम् slayer of Tripura, शिवं यथा like Siva, तम् that, भार्गवम् descendent of Bhrugu, जामदग्नयम् son of Jamadagni, ददर्श beheld.
explanation: In that dreadful darkness while the army looked as if covered with ashes, king Dasaratha encountered the repressor of kings, descendant of Bhrugu and son of Jamadagni with a terrible crown of matted hair, inaccessible like Kailasa mountain and unendurable like the fire at the time of dissolution. The laymen gazing at his blazing energy,hanging an axe on his shoulder and holding a bow in his hand which flashed like lighning and the principal arrow he looked like Siva at the time of slaying of Tripura.

transliteration: tasmiṃstamasi ghore tu bhasmacchanneva sā camū: dadarśa bhīmasaṅkāśaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam| bhārgavaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ taṃ rājarājavimardinam kailāsamiva durdharṣaṃ kālāgnimiva dussaham| jvalaṃtamiva tejobhirdurnirīkṣyaṃ pṛthagjanai: skandhe cāsajya paraśuṃ dhanurvidyudgaṇopamam	| pragṛhya śaramukhyaṃ ca tripuraghnaṃ yathā śivam

explanation: In that dreadful darkness while the army looked as if covered with ashes, king Dasaratha encountered the repressor of kings, descendant of Bhrugu and son of Jamadagni with a terrible crown of matted hair, inaccessible like Kailasa mountain and unendurable like the fire at the time of dissolution. The laymen gazing at his blazing energy,hanging an axe on his shoulder and holding a bow in his hand which flashed like lighning and the principal arrow he looked like Siva at the time of slaying of Tripura.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तमसि घोरे तु भस्मच्छन्नेव सा चमू:।।1.74.17।। ददर्श भीमसङ्काशं जटामण्डलधारिणम्। भार्गवं जामदग्न्यं तं राजराजविमर्दिनम्।।1.74.18।। कैलासमिव दुर्धर्षं कालाग्निमिव दुस्सहम्। ज्वलंतमिव तेजोभिर्दुर्निरीक्ष्यं पृथग्जनै:।।1.74.19।। स्कन्धे चासज्य परशुं धनुर्विद्युद्गणोपमम्	। प्रगृह्य शरमुख्यं च त्रिपुरघ्नं यथा शिवम्।।1.74.20।।
transliteration: tasmiṃstamasi ghore tu bhasmacchanneva sā camū: dadarśa bhīmasaṅkāśaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam| bhārgavaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ taṃ rājarājavimardinam kailāsamiva durdharṣaṃ kālāgnimiva dussaham| jvalaṃtamiva tejobhirdurnirīkṣyaṃ pṛthagjanai: skandhe cāsajya paraśuṃ dhanurvidyudgaṇopamam	| pragṛhya śaramukhyaṃ ca tripuraghnaṃ yathā śivam
translation: तस्मिन् In that, घोरे fearful, तमसि darkness, भस्मच्छन्नेव looking as if covered with ashes, सा चमू: that army, भीमसङ्काशम् looking dreadful, जटामण्डलधारिणम् wearing a crown of  matted hair, राजराजविमर्दिनम् decimated the king of kings, कैलासमिव like Kailasa Mountain, दुर्धर्षम् inaccessible, कालाग्निमिव like the fire at the time of dissolution, दुस्सहम् difficult to endure, तेजोभि: with energy, ज्वलन्तमिव as if blazing, पृथग्जनै: by ordinary people, दुर्निरीक्षम् incapable of being gazed upon, परशुम् axe, स्कन्धे on his shoulder, आसज्य hanging, विद्युद्गणोपमम् resembling group of lightenings, धनु: bow, शरमुख्यम्  principal arrow, प्रगृह्य grasping, त्रिपुरघ्नम् slayer of Tripura, शिवं यथा like Siva, तम् that, भार्गवम् descendent of Bhrugu, जामदग्नयम् son of Jamadagni, ददर्श beheld.
explanation: In that dreadful darkness while the army looked as if covered with ashes, king Dasaratha encountered the repressor of kings, descendant of Bhrugu and son of Jamadagni with a terrible crown of matted hair, inaccessible like Kailasa mountain and unendurable like the fire at the time of dissolution. The laymen gazing at his blazing energy,hanging an axe on his shoulder and holding a bow in his hand which flashed like lighning and the principal arrow he looked like Siva at the time of slaying of Tripura.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा भीमसङ्काशं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्। वसिष्ठप्रमुखा विप्रा जपहोमपरायणा:।।1.74.21।। सङ्गता मुनयस्सर्वे सञ्जजल्पुरथो मिथ:।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasaṅkāśaṃ jvalantamiva pāvakam| vasiṣṭhapramukhā viprā japahomaparāyaṇā: saṅgatā munayassarve sañjajalpuratho mitha:|
translation: भीमसङ्काशम् fearful appearance, ज्वलन्तम् like flaming, पावकम् इव like fire, तम् him, दृष्ट्वा having seen, जपहोमपरायणा: engaged in reciting mantras and oblations to the fire, विप्रा: brahmanas, वसिष्ठप्रमुखा: Vasishta and others, सर्वे मुनय: all saints, सङ्गता: having assembled, अथो afterwards, मिथ: mutually, सञ्जजल्पु: whispered.
explanation: At the sight of the fearful appearance of Parasurama looking like flaming fire, Vasishta and all other saints who were in the habit of chanting mantras and offering oblations to the fire whispered among themselves:

shloka_text: कच्चित्पितृवधामर्षी क्षत्रं नोत्सादयिष्यति।।1.74.22।। पूर्वं क्षत्रवधं कृत्वा गतमन्युर्गतज्वर:। क्षत्रस्योत्सादनं भूयो न खल्वस्य चिकीर्षितम्।।1.74.23।।
transliteration: kaccitpitṛvadhāmarṣī kṣatraṃ notsādayiṣyati pūrvaṃ kṣatravadhaṃ kṛtvā gatamanyurgatajvara:| kṣatrasyotsādanaṃ bhūyo na khalvasya cikīrṣitam
translation: पितृवधामर्षी enraged at the slaughter of his father, क्षत्रम् kshatriya race, नोत्सादयिष्यतिकच्चित् is he not intent upon exterminating, पूर्वम् formerly, क्षत्रवधम् slaughter of kshatriyas, कृत्वा having made, गतमन्यु: freed from anger, गतज्वर: freed from grief, भूय: again, क्षत्रस्य of kshatriya race, उत्सादनम् annihilation, अस्य for him, न चिकीर्षितं खलु is not desirous of doing it indeed.
explanation: Enraged at the slaughter of his father (by Kartaveeryarjuna), is he intent upon  exterminating the kshatriya race? Having slaughtered the kshatriyas, in the past he was freed from anger and grief. Is he again desirous of annihilating the kshatriyas?

shloka_text: कच्चित्पितृवधामर्षी क्षत्रं नोत्सादयिष्यति।।1.74.22।। पूर्वं क्षत्रवधं कृत्वा गतमन्युर्गतज्वर:। क्षत्रस्योत्सादनं भूयो न खल्वस्य चिकीर्षितम्।।1.74.23।।
transliteration: kaccitpitṛvadhāmarṣī kṣatraṃ notsādayiṣyati pūrvaṃ kṣatravadhaṃ kṛtvā gatamanyurgatajvara:| kṣatrasyotsādanaṃ bhūyo na khalvasya cikīrṣitam
translation: पितृवधामर्षी enraged at the slaughter of his father, क्षत्रम् kshatriya race, नोत्सादयिष्यतिकच्चित् is he not intent upon exterminating, पूर्वम् formerly, क्षत्रवधम् slaughter of kshatriyas, कृत्वा having made, गतमन्यु: freed from anger, गतज्वर: freed from grief, भूय: again, क्षत्रस्य of kshatriya race, उत्सादनम् annihilation, अस्य for him, न चिकीर्षितं खलु is not desirous of doing it indeed.
explanation: Enraged at the slaughter of his father (by Kartaveeryarjuna), is he intent upon  exterminating the kshatriya race? Having slaughtered the kshatriyas, in the past he was freed from anger and grief. Is he again desirous of annihilating the kshatriyas?

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वाऽर्घ्यमादाय भार्गवं भीमदर्शनम्। ऋषयो राम रामेति वचो मधुरमब्रुवन्।।1.74.24।।
transliteration: evamuktvā'rghyamādāya bhārgavaṃ bhīmadarśanam| ṛṣayo rāma rāmeti vaco madhuramabruvan
translation: ऋषय: saints, एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having talked amongst themselves, अर्घ्यम् the arghya, आदाय taking, भीमदर्शनम् dreadful appearance, भार्गवम् son of Bhargava, राम राम इति "Rama, Rama" saying so, मधुरम् वच: soothing words, अब्रुवन् spoke.
explanation: The saints having thus talked amongst themselves, offered arghya to the son of Bhargava, of dreadful appearance and addressed him in soothing words: "O Rama O Rama".

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य तु तां पूजामृषिदत्तां प्रतापवान्। रामं दाशरथिं रामो जामदग्न्योऽभ्यभाषत।।1.74.25।।
transliteration: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjāmṛṣidattāṃ pratāpavān| rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ rāmo jāmadagnyo'bhyabhāṣata
translation: प्रतापवान् valiant, जामदग्न्य: son of Jamadagni, राम: Parasurama, ऋषिदत्ताम् offered by saints, ताम् पूजाम् that homage, प्रतिगृह्य having accpted, दाशरथिं रामम् Rama, son of Dasaratha, अभ्यभाषत spoke.
explanation: Valiant Parasurama, son of Jamadagni, having accepted the homage offered by the saints addressed Rama, son of Dasaratha and said: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे चतुस्सप्ततितमस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the seventyfourth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: राम दाशरथे राम वीर्यं ते श्रूयतेऽद्भुतम्। धनुषो भेदनं चैव निखिलेन मया श्रुतम्।।1.75.1।।
transliteration: rāma dāśarathe rāma vīryaṃ te śrūyate'dbhutam| dhanuṣo bhedanaṃ caiva nikhilena mayā śrutam
translation: दाशरथे son of Dasaratha, राम O Rama, राम O Rama, ते your, वीर्यम् prowess, अद्भुतम् marvellous, श्रूयते is being heard, धनुष: bow's, भेदनं चैव breaking also, निखिलेन completely, मया by me, श्रुतम् heard.
explanation: "O Rama, Rama, son of Dasaratha I have heard in full of your marvellous prowess and your feat in breaking the bow of Siva.
comments: Ignoring Dasaratha, Parasurama tells Rama to string the bow of Visnu.

shloka_text: तदद्भुतमचिन्त्यं च भेदनं धनुषस्त्वया। तच्छ्रुत्वाऽहमनुप्राप्तो धनुर्गृह्यापरं शुभम्।।1.75.2।।
transliteration: tadadbhutamacintyaṃ ca bhedanaṃ dhanuṣastvayā| tacchrutvā'hamanuprāpto dhanurgṛhyāparaṃ śubham
translation: त्वया by you, धनुष: bow's, तत् भेदनम् that breaking, अद्भुतम् astonishing, अचिन्त्यम् च unimaginable, तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, अहम् I, अपरम् another, शुभम् auspicious, धनु: bow, गृह्य bringing, अनुप्राप्त: have come here.
explanation: The fact that you have broken Siva's bow is an astonishing act. It is beyond imagination. Having heard it I have come here with another auspicious bow.

shloka_text: तदिदं घोरसङ्काशं जामदग्न्यं महद्धनु:। पूरयस्व शरेणैव स्वबलं दर्शयस्व च।।1.75.3।।
transliteration: tadidaṃ ghorasaṅkāśaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ mahaddhanu:| pūrayasva śareṇaiva svabalaṃ darśayasva ca
translation: घोरसङ्काशं appearing dreadful, जामदग्न्यम् obtained through Jamadagni, तत् that, इदम् this, महत् mighty, धनु: bow, शरेणैव with arrow, पूरयस्व fill it, स्वबलम् your own prowess, दर्शयस्व show.
explanation: This mighty, dreadful bow was obtained through Jamadagni. You may display your prowess by fixing on it an arrow.

shloka_text: तदहं ते बलं दृष्ट्वा धनुषोऽस्य प्रपूरणे। द्वन्द्वयुद्धं प्रदास्यामि वीर्यश्लाघ्यस्य राघव।।1.75.4।।
transliteration: tadahaṃ te balaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhanuṣo'sya prapūraṇe| dvandvayuddhaṃ pradāsyāmi vīryaślāghyasya rāghava
translation: राघव O Rama, तत् that, अहम् I, अस्य this, धनुष: bow's, प्रपूरणे in stretching it, ते your, बलम् strength, दृष्ट्वा having seen, वीर्यश्लाघ्यस्य to you acclaimed in prowess, द्वन्द्वयुद्धं a duel combat, प्रदास्यामि shall give.
explanation: O Rama after witnessing your strength in stretching and stringing this bow, I shall engage you in a duel acclaiming your prowess".

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा दशरथस्तदा। विषण्णवदनो दीन: प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।1.75.5।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rājā daśarathastadā| viṣaṇṇavadano dīna: prāñjalirvākyamabravīt
translation: तदा then, राजा king, दशरथ Dasaratha, तस्य his, तत् that, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard,  विषण्णवदन: with dejected face, दीन: full of sorrow, प्राञ्जलि: with joined hands, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: When king Dasaratha heard these words, his face fell. He humbly pleaded with him his hands folded:

shloka_text: क्षत्ररोषात्प्रशान्तस्त्वं ब्राह्मणश्च महायशा:। बालानां मम पुत्राणामभयं दातुमर्हसि।।1.75.6।।
transliteration: kṣatraroṣātpraśāntastvaṃ brāhmaṇaśca mahāyaśā:| bālānāṃ mama putrāṇāmabhayaṃ dātumarhasi
translation: क्षत्ररोषात् from anger against kshatriyas, प्रशान्त: quietened,  ब्राह्मण: brahmana, महायशा: highly renowned, बालानाम् of young boys, मम my, पुत्राणाम् sons, अभयम् assurance of security, दातुम् to give, अर्हसि behoves of you.
explanation: "You are a brahmana, highly renowned and withdrawn from anger against kshatriyas. It behoves of you to give assurance of security to my sons who are young.

shloka_text: भार्गवाणां कुले जात: स्वाध्यायव्रतशालिनाम्। सहास्राक्षे प्रतिज्ञाय शस्त्रं निक्षिप्तवानसि।।1.75.7।।
transliteration: bhārgavāṇāṃ kule jāta: svādhyāyavrataśālinām| sahāsrākṣe pratijñāya śastraṃ nikṣiptavānasi
translation: स्वाध्यायव्रतशालिनाम् resplendent with the study of vedas and observance of vows, भार्गवाणाम् relating to Bhargavas, कुले in the race of, जात: was born, सहास्राक्षे in the name of Indra, प्रतिज्ञाय having vowed, शस्त्रं arms, निक्षिप्तवान् असि have renounced.
explanation: Born in the family of (saint) Bhrigu versed in the study of the Vedas and  observance of vows. You have promised in the name of  the thousandeyed Indra to renounce the arms.

shloka_text: स त्वं धर्मपरो भूत्वा काश्यपाय वसुन्धराम्	। दत्त्वा वनमुपागम्य महेन्द्रकृतकेतन:।।1.75.8।।
transliteration: sa tvaṃ dharmaparo bhūtvā kāśyapāya vasundharām	| dattvā vanamupāgamya mahendrakṛtaketana:
translation: स: such, त्वम् you, धर्मपर: one intent on righteousness, भूत्वा by being, काश्यपाय for Kasyapa, वसुन्धराम् this earth, दत्त्वा having given, वनम् forest, उपागम्य having reached, महेन्द्रकृतकेतन: made a residence on the Mahendra mountain.
explanation: By adhering to righteousness in life and having conferred the earth upon Kasyapa, you retired to the forest and made your residence on the Mahendra mountain.

shloka_text: मम सर्वविनाशाय सम्प्राप्तस्त्वं महामुने। न चैकस्मिन् हते रामे सर्वे जीवामहे वयम्	।।1.75.9।।
transliteration: mama sarvavināśāya samprāptastvaṃ mahāmune| na caikasmin hate rāme sarve jīvāmahe vayam
translation: महामुने O Great ascetic, त्वम् you, मम my, सर्वविनाशाय for total destruction, सम्प्राप्त: arrived,  एकस्मिन् one, रामे Rama, हते if killed, वयम् us, सर्वे all, न जीवामहे will not survive.
explanation: O Great ascetic today you have arrived evidently for the total destruction of our family. If Rama is killed none of us will survive".

shloka_text: ब्रुवत्येवं दशरथे जामदग्न्य: प्रतापवान्। अनादृत्यैव तद्वाक्यं राममेवाभ्यभाषत।।1.75.10।।
transliteration: bruvatyevaṃ daśarathe jāmadagnya: pratāpavān| anādṛtyaiva tadvākyaṃ rāmamevābhyabhāṣata
translation: दशरथे when Dasaratha, एवम् in this way, ब्रुवति while saying, प्रतापवान् valiant, जामदग्न्य: son of Jamadagni, तद्वाक्यम् those words, अनादृत्यैव disregarding, राममेव Rama only, अभ्यभाषत addressed.
explanation: Disregarding these words of Dasaratha, the valiant son of Jamadagni said to Rama.

shloka_text: इमे द्वे धनुषी श्रेष्ठे दिव्ये लोकाभिविश्रुते। दृढे बलवती मुख्ये सुकृते विश्वकर्मणा।।1.75.11।।
transliteration: ime dve dhanuṣī śreṣṭhe divye lokābhiviśrute| dṛḍhe balavatī mukhye sukṛte viśvakarmaṇā
translation: इमे these, द्वे two, धनुषी bows, श्रेष्ठे excellent, दिव्ये celestial, लोकाभिविश्रुते wellknown in the  worlds, दृढे stout, बलवती powerful, मुख्ये best of all, विश्वकर्मणा by Visvakarma, सुकृते are  well made.
explanation: "These two excellent celestial bows are wellknown throughout the worlds. They are stout and strong. They are the best of all, wellmade by Visvakarma.

shloka_text: अतिसृष्टं सुरैरेकं त्र्यम्बकाय युयुत्सवे। त्रिपुरघ्नं नरश्रेष्ठ भग्नं काकुत्स्थ यत्त्वया।।1.75.12।।
transliteration: atisṛṣṭaṃ surairekaṃ tryambakāya yuyutsave| tripuraghnaṃ naraśreṣṭha bhagnaṃ kākutstha yattvayā
translation: नरश्रेष्ठ O Best among men, काकुत्स्थ Rama, यत् which, त्त्वया by you, भग्नं was broken, युयुत्सवे wishing to fight, त्र्यम्बकाय for threeeyed Siva, सुरै: by devatas, अतिसृष्टं was given,  त्रिपुरघ्नम् destroyer of Tripuras, एकम् one (of the two).
explanation: O Best among men O Descendant of Kakustha one of these broken by you, was given by the gods to the threeeyed Siva, who, wishing to fight the demon Tripura with this bow, destroyed him.

shloka_text: इदं द्वितीयं दुर्धर्षं विष्णोर्दत्तं सुरोत्तमै:। तदिदं वैष्णवं राम धनु: परमभास्वरम्। समानसारं काकुत्स्थ रौद्रेण धनुषा त्विदम्।।1.75.13।।
transliteration: idaṃ dvitīyaṃ durdharṣaṃ viṣṇordattaṃ surottamai:| tadidaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ rāma dhanu: paramabhāsvaram| samānasāraṃ kākutstha raudreṇa dhanuṣā tvidam
translation: दुर्धर्षम् unassailable, इदम् this, द्वितीयम् second bow, सुरोत्तमै: chiefs of celestials, विष्णो: for Visnu, दत्तम् given, काकुत्स्थ born in the race of Kakutsthsa, राम Rama, परमभास्वरम् highly radiant, तत् that, इदम् this, वैष्णवम् pertaining to Visnu, धनु: bow, रौद्रेण धनुषा with the bow of Rudra, समानसारम् equal to its energy.
explanation: This second bow which is unassailable was given by chief of the celestials to Visnu. O Rama born in the race of Kakutstha this highly radiant bow of Visnu is as strong as the bow of Siva.

shloka_text: तदा तु देवतास्सर्वा: पृच्छन्ति स्म पितामहम्। शितिकण्ठस्य विष्णोश्च बलाबलनिरीक्षया।।1.75.14।।
transliteration: tadā tu devatāssarvā: pṛcchanti sma pitāmaham| śitikaṇṭhasya viṣṇośca balābalanirīkṣayā
translation: तदा then, सर्वा: all, देवता: devatas, शितिकण्ठस्य bluethroated, Siva's, विष्णो: Visnu's, बलाबलनिरीक्षया to ascertain the strengths and weaknesses, पितामहम् grandsire, Brahma, पृच्छन्ति स्म enquired.
explanation: Then all the gods in order to ascertain the strength and weakness of Siva and Visnu enquired of the Grandsire, Brahma:

shloka_text: अभिप्रायं तु विज्ञाय देवतानां पितामह:। विरोधं जनयामास तयो स्सत्यवतां वर:।।1.75.15।।
transliteration: abhiprāyaṃ tu vijñāya devatānāṃ pitāmaha:| virodhaṃ janayāmāsa tayo ssatyavatāṃ vara:
translation: सत्यवताम् among truth speaking ones, वर: foremost, पितामह: grandsire, Brahma, देवतानाम् devatas', अभिप्रायम् intention, विज्ञाय having come to know, तयो: for both of them, विरोधम् quarrel, जनयामास instigated.
explanation: Foremost among the truthful, Grandsire Brahma come to know the intention of the gods and triggered a conflict between the gods.

shloka_text: विरोधे च महद्युद्धमभवद्रोमहर्षणम्	। शितिकण्ठस्य विष्णोश्च परस्परजिगीषुणो:।।1.75.16।।
transliteration: virodhe ca mahadyuddhamabhavadromaharṣaṇam	| śitikaṇṭhasya viṣṇośca parasparajigīṣuṇo:
translation: विरोधे in that fight, परस्परजिगीषिणो: each desirous of victory over the other, शितिकण्ठस्य Siva's, विष्णोश्च Visnu's, रोमहर्षणम् causing one's hair to stand on its end, महत् great, युद्धम् battle, अभवत् took place.
explanation: In that thrilling fight between Siva and Visnu, each desirous of victory over the other, a ferocious battle took place causing one's hair to stand on end.

shloka_text: तदा तु जृम्भितं शैवं धनुर्भीमपराक्रमम्। हुङ्कारेण महादेव स्तम्भितोऽथ त्रिलोचन:।।1.75.17।।
transliteration: tadā tu jṛmbhitaṃ śaivaṃ dhanurbhīmaparākramam| huṅkāreṇa mahādeva stambhito'tha trilocana:
translation: तदा then, हुङ्कारेण with 'Humkara' by Visnu, भीमपराक्रमम् dreadful prowess, शैवं धनु: Siva's bow, जृम्भितं yawned (stretched), अथ thereafter, त्रिलोचन: threeeyed, महादेव: Mahadeva, स्तम्भित: was made motionless.
explanation: Then, with the 'Humkara' produced by Visnu, Siva's bow of dreadful prowess was stretched, which struck the threeeyed Mahadeva motionless.

shloka_text: देवैस्तदा समागम्य सर्षिसघै स्सचारणै:। याचितौ प्रशमं तत्र जग्मतुस्तौ सुरोत्तमौ।।1.75.18।।
transliteration: devaistadā samāgamya sarṣisaghai ssacāraṇai:| yācitau praśamaṃ tatra jagmatustau surottamau
translation: तदा then, सर्षिसंघै: hosts of sages, सचारणै: with charanas, देवै: devatas, तत्र there, समागम्य having assembled, याचितौ beseeched, तौ those two, सुरोत्तमौ foremost of devatas, प्रशमम् peace, जग्मतु: obtained.
explanation: Then hosts of sages, charanas and the gods assembled there and beseeched both of them, the preeminent among the gods to keep peace.

shloka_text: जृम्भितं तद्धनुर्द्रृष्ट्वा शैवं विष्णुपराक्रमै:। अधिकं मेनिरे विष्णुं देवा स्सर्षिगणास्तदा	।।1.75.19।।
transliteration: jṛmbhitaṃ taddhanurdrṛṣṭvā śaivaṃ viṣṇuparākramai:| adhikaṃ menire viṣṇuṃ devā ssarṣigaṇāstadā
translation: विष्णुपराक्रमै: with the prowess of Visnu, जृम्भितम् made inert, तत् that, शैवम् relating to Siva, धनु: bow, दृष्ट्वा haivng seen, तदा then, सर्षिगणा: hosts of sages, देवा: devatas, विष्णुम् Visnu, अधिकम् as superior, मेनिरे thought over.
explanation: Now that the bow of Siva was made inert by Visnu's prowess, hosts of sages and  gods acknowlged Visnu as superior.

shloka_text: धनू रुद्रस्तु सङ्कृद्धो विदेहेषु महायशा:। देवरातस्य राजर्षेर्ददौ हस्ते ससायकम्।।1.75.20।।
transliteration: dhanū rudrastu saṅkṛddho videheṣu mahāyaśā:| devarātasya rājarṣerdadau haste sasāyakam
translation: सङ्कृद्ध: enraged, महायशा: renowned, रुद्रस्तु Siva, विदेहेषु in the country of Videha, ससायकम् together with arrow, धनु: bow, राजर्षे: to the royal saint, देवरातस्य devarata's, हस्ते hands, ददौ gave.
explanation: Glorious Siva, enraged at this, placed the bow together with the arrow in the hands of Rajarshi Devarata in the country of Videha.

shloka_text: इदं च वैष्णवं राम धनु: परपुरञ्जयम्। ऋचीके भार्गवे प्रादाद्विष्णु: स न्यासमुत्तमम्।।1.75.21।।
transliteration: idaṃ ca vaiṣṇavaṃ rāma dhanu: parapurañjayam| ṛcīke bhārgave prādādviṣṇu: sa nyāsamuttamam
translation: राम O Rama, स: that, विष्णु: Visnu, परपुरञ्जयम् capable of conquering hostile cities, इदम् this, वैष्णवं धनु: bow of Visnu, भार्गवे belonging to Bhrigu race, ऋचीके named Richika,   उत्तमम् the best, न्यासम् in trust, प्रादात् gave.
explanation: This bow of Visnu, O Rama capable of conquering hostile cities, was given in trust to Richika belonging to the race of Bhrigu.

shloka_text: ऋचीकस्तु महातेजा: पुत्रस्याप्रतिकर्मण:। पितुर्मम ददौ दिव्यं जमदग्नेर्महात्मन:।।1.75.22।।
transliteration: ṛcīkastu mahātejā: putrasyāpratikarmaṇa:| piturmama dadau divyaṃ jamadagnermahātmana:
translation: महातेजा: exceedingly lustrous, ऋचीकस्तु Ruchika, पुत्रस्य to his son, अप्रतिकर्मण: of unrivalled valour, महात्मन: of the maganimous one, मम my, पितु: father, जमदग्ने: to Jamadagni, ददौ gave.
explanation: Brilliant Ruchika gave this bow to his son, the great Jamadagni, my father, a man of unrivalled valour.

shloka_text: न्यस्तशस्त्रे पितरि मे तपोबलसमन्विते। अर्जुनो विदधे मृत्युं प्राकृतां बुद्धिमास्थित:।।1.75.23।।
transliteration: nyastaśastre pitari me tapobalasamanvite| arjuno vidadhe mṛtyuṃ prākṛtāṃ buddhimāsthita:
translation: तपोबलसमन्विते endowed with ascetic energy, मे my, पितरि when my father, न्यस्तशस्त्रे renounced the weapons, अर्जुन: Karta Virya Arjuna, प्राकृताम् in a vulgar manner, मृत्युम् death, बुद्धिम् mind,  आस्थितः resorting to, विदधे made.
explanation: My father equipped with ascetic energy renounced the weapon and was killed by Kartaveeryarjuna in a vulgar manner.

shloka_text: वधमप्रतिरूपं तु पितु श्शृत्वा सुदारुणम्। क्षत्रमुत्सादयन्रोषाज्जातं जातमनेकश:।।1.75.24।। पृथिवीं चाखिलां प्राप्य काश्यपाय महात्मने	। यज्ञस्यान्ते तदा राम दक्षिणां पुण्यकर्मणे	। दत्त्वा महेन्द्रनिलयस्तपोबलसमन्वित:।।1.75.25।।
transliteration: vadhamapratirūpaṃ tu pitu śśṛtvā sudāruṇam| kṣatramutsādayanroṣājjātaṃ jātamanekaśa: pṛthivīṃ cākhilāṃ prāpya kāśyapāya mahātmane	| yajñasyānte tadā rāma dakṣiṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇe	| dattvā mahendranilayastapobalasamanvita:
translation: राम O Rama, अप्रतिरूपम् incomparable, सुदारुणम् extremely ruthless, पितु: father's, वधम् slaying, श्रुत्वा having heard, रोषात् out of fury, जातं जातम् born again and again, क्षत्रम् kshatriya race, उत्सादयन् decimating, अखिलाम् entire, पृथिवीम् earth, प्राप्य having won, यज्ञस्य sacrifice's, अन्ते at the end of, महात्मने to the magnanimous, पुण्यकर्मणे doer of meritorious acts, काश्यपाय for Kasyapa, दत्त्वा having given, तपोबलसमन्वित: endowed with ascetic energy, महेन्द्रनिलय: living on Mahendra mountain as my abode.
explanation: O Rama Having heard the slaying of my father incomparable in extreme ruthlessness, I decimated the Kshatriya race again and again out of fury as they were born and reborn. I conquered the entire earth. At the conclusion of the sacrifice I conferred it on the great soul Kasyapa of meritorious acts. Gifted with ascetic energy I have (now) made the Mahendra mountain my abode.

shloka_text: वधमप्रतिरूपं तु पितु श्शृत्वा सुदारुणम्। क्षत्रमुत्सादयन्रोषाज्जातं जातमनेकश:।।1.75.24।। पृथिवीं चाखिलां प्राप्य काश्यपाय महात्मने	। यज्ञस्यान्ते तदा राम दक्षिणां पुण्यकर्मणे	। दत्त्वा महेन्द्रनिलयस्तपोबलसमन्वित:।।1.75.25।।
transliteration: vadhamapratirūpaṃ tu pitu śśṛtvā sudāruṇam| kṣatramutsādayanroṣājjātaṃ jātamanekaśa: pṛthivīṃ cākhilāṃ prāpya kāśyapāya mahātmane	| yajñasyānte tadā rāma dakṣiṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇe	| dattvā mahendranilayastapobalasamanvita:
translation: राम O Rama, अप्रतिरूपम् incomparable, सुदारुणम् extremely ruthless, पितु: father's, वधम् slaying, श्रुत्वा having heard, रोषात् out of fury, जातं जातम् born again and again, क्षत्रम् kshatriya race, उत्सादयन् decimating, अखिलाम् entire, पृथिवीम् earth, प्राप्य having won, यज्ञस्य sacrifice's, अन्ते at the end of, महात्मने to the magnanimous, पुण्यकर्मणे doer of meritorious acts, काश्यपाय for Kasyapa, दत्त्वा having given, तपोबलसमन्वित: endowed with ascetic energy, महेन्द्रनिलय: living on Mahendra mountain as my abode.
explanation: O Rama Having heard the slaying of my father incomparable in extreme ruthlessness, I decimated the Kshatriya race again and again out of fury as they were born and reborn. I conquered the entire earth. At the conclusion of the sacrifice I conferred it on the great soul Kasyapa of meritorious acts. Gifted with ascetic energy I have (now) made the Mahendra mountain my abode.

shloka_text: अद्यतूत्तमवीर्येण त्वया राम महाबल। श्रुतवान् धनुषो भेदं ततोऽहं द्रुतमागत:।।1.75.26।।
transliteration: adyatūttamavīryeṇa tvayā rāma mahābala| śrutavān dhanuṣo bhedaṃ tato'haṃ drutamāgata:
translation: महाबल O Highly energetic, राम O Rama, अद्य now, उत्तमवीर्येण with excellent prowess, त्वया by you, धनुष: भेदम् breaking of the bow, श्रुतवान् having listened, अहम् I, तत: for that reason, द्रुतम् speedily, आगत: have come.
explanation: O Mighty Rama when I heard that you have broken the bow with your extraordinary prowess, I have come here quickly.

shloka_text: तदिदं वैष्णवं राम पितृपैतामहं महत्। क्षत्रधर्मं पुरस्कृत्य गृह्णीष्व धनुरुत्तमम्।।1.75.27।।
transliteration: tadidaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ rāma pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat| kṣatradharmaṃ puraskṛtya gṛhṇīṣva dhanuruttamam
translation: राम O Rama, क्षत्रधर्मम् duties of kshatriya, पुरस्कृत्य treating with respect, तत् that, इदम् this, पितृपैतामहम् being inherited from my father and forefathers, महत् eminent, उत्तमम् excellent, वैष्णवम् related to Visnu, धनु: bow, गृह्णीष्व take hold of.
explanation: Respect the duties of a kshatriya, O Rama Take hold of this great, uncommon bow of Visnu inherited by me from my father and forefathers.

shloka_text: योजयस्व धनुश्श्रेष्ठे शरं परपुरञ्जयम्। यदि शक्नोषि काकुत्स्थ द्वन्द्वं दास्यामि ते तत:।।1.75.28।।
transliteration: yojayasva dhanuśśreṣṭhe śaraṃ parapurañjayam| yadi śaknoṣi kākutstha dvandvaṃ dāsyāmi te tata:
translation: काकुत्स्थ O Descendant of Kakutstha, धनु: श्रेष्ठे in this excellent bow, परपुरञ्जयम् capable of conquering cities of enemies, शरम् arrow, योजयस्व unite it, शक्नोषि यदि if it is possible for you to do so, तत: then, ते to you, द्वन्दम् duel combat, दास्यामि shall offer.
explanation: O Descendant of Kakustha this best bow is capable of conquering enemy cities. Fix an arrow. If it is possible for you to do so, then I shall engage you in a duel". इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे पञ्चसप्ततितमस्सर्ग: ।। Thus ends the seventyfifth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तज्जामदग्न्यस्य वाक्यं दाशरथिस्तदा। गौरवाद्यंन्त्रितकथ: पितू राममथाब्रवीत्।।1.76.1।।
transliteration: śrutvā tajjāmadagnyasya vākyaṃ dāśarathistadā| gauravādyaṃntritakatha: pitū rāmamathābravīt
translation: तदा then, दाशरथि: Rama, जमदग्न्यस्य Parasurama's, (तत्) वाक्यम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, पितु: father's, गौरवात् out of respect, यन्त्रितकथ: avoiding furthur conversation, अथ thereafter, रामम् addressing Parasurama, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Hearing the words of the son of Jamadagni (Parasurama), Rama, the son of Dasaratha, avoiding further conversation out of respect for his father intercepted Parasurama saying:
comments: Rama bends the bow of Visnu--Parasurama returns to Mahendra mountain.

shloka_text: श्रुतवानस्मि यत्कर्म कृतवानसि भार्गव। अनुरुंध्यामहे ब्रह्मन् पितुरानृण्यमास्थितम्।।1.76.2।।
transliteration: śrutavānasmi yatkarma kṛtavānasi bhārgava| anuruṃdhyāmahe brahman piturānṛṇyamāsthitam
translation: भार्गव O Bhrigu's son, Parasurama, यत् which, कर्म acts, कृतवानसि you have done, श्रुतवान्  अस्मि I have listened, ब्रह्मन् O Brahman, पितुः to your father, आनृण्यम् repaying the debt, आस्थितम् obtained, अनुरुन्ध्यामहे we will commend.
explanation: "O Descendant of Bhrigu I have listened to the (marvellous) acts you have performed. O Brahman I commend you for discharging your duty in repaying the debt to your father.

shloka_text: वीर्यहीनमिवाशक्तं क्षत्रधर्मेण भार्गव। अवजानासि मे तेज: पश्य मेऽद्य पराक्रमम्।।1.76.3।।
transliteration: vīryahīnamivāśaktaṃ kṣatradharmeṇa bhārgava| avajānāsi me teja: paśya me'dya parākramam
translation: भार्गव O Descendant of Bhrugu, वीर्यहीनमिव as if I am without valour, क्षत्रधर्मेण by duties of Kshatriya, अशक्तमिव as though incompetant, अवजानासि you are insulting me, अद्य today, मे my, तेज: energy, पराक्रमम् valour, पश्य you may witness.
explanation: You underrate me O Bhargava as though I am devoid of valour and incompetent to perform the duties of a Kshatriya. Now witness my energy and valour.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा राघव: क्रुद्धो भार्गवस्य शरासनम्। शरं च प्रतिजग्राह हस्ताल्लघुपराक्रम:।।1.76.4।।
transliteration: ityuktvā rāghava: kruddho bhārgavasya śarāsanam| śaraṃ ca pratijagrāha hastāllaghuparākrama:
translation: लघुपराक्रम: with quick vigour, राघव: Rama, क्रुद्ध: enraged, इति उक्त्वा having thus spoken, भार्गवस्य from Parasurama's, हस्तात् hand, शरासनम् bow, शरं च also an arrow, प्रतिजग्राह grasped (pulled).
explanation: Having spoken thus, the enraged Rama, gifted with quick vigour, seized the bow and arrow from Parasurama's hands.

shloka_text: आरोप्य स धनू राम श्शरं सज्यं चकार ह। जामदग्न्यं ततो रामं राम: क्रुद्धोऽब्रवीद्वच:।।1.76.5।।
transliteration: āropya sa dhanū rāma śśaraṃ sajyaṃ cakāra ha| jāmadagnyaṃ tato rāmaṃ rāma: kruddho'bravīdvaca:
translation: स: that, राम: Rama, धनु: bow, आरोप्य bending it, शरम् arrow, सज्यम् stretching the string, चकार performed, राम: Rama, तत: thereafter, क्रुद्ध: enraged, जामदग्न्यं son of Jamadagni, रामम् Parasurama, वच: words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Infuriated Rama bent the bow stretched it, fixed the arrow and addressed Parasurama, the son of Jamadagni:

shloka_text: ब्राह्मणोऽसीति पूज्यो मे विश्वामित्रकृतेन च। तस्माच्छक्तो न ते राम मोक्तुं प्राणहरं शरम्।।1.76.6।।
transliteration: brāhmaṇo'sīti pūjyo me viśvāmitrakṛtena ca| tasmācchakto na te rāma moktuṃ prāṇaharaṃ śaram
translation: राम O Parasurama, ब्राह्मण: असि you are a brahmin, इति for this reason, विश्वामित्रकृतेन through Visvamitra, मे for me, पूज्य: worthy of homage, तस्मात् for that reason, ते your, प्राणहरणम् life taking, शरम् arrow, मोक्तुम् to release,न शक्त: I am not competent.
explanation: "You are a brahmin, O Parasurama. You are also related to Viswamitra. Hence you are worthy of homage. I cannot, therefore, release this against you to take your life.

shloka_text: इमां पादगतिं राम तपोबलसमार्जिताम्। लोकानप्रतिमान्वा ते हनिष्यामि यदिच्छसि	।।1.76.7।।
transliteration: imāṃ pādagatiṃ rāma tapobalasamārjitām| lokānapratimānvā te haniṣyāmi yadicchasi
translation: राम O Parasurama, ते your, इमाम् this, पादगतिम् movement of your feet, तपोबलसमार्जिताम्  earned through asceteic energy, अप्रतिमान् incomparable, लोकान् वा worlds, हनिष्यामि I shall destroy, यत् whichever, इच्छसि you are desiring, tell me.
explanation: I shall destroy your mobility, O Parasurama or the higher worlds earned through your matchless asceteic energy. Tell me which one you choose.

shloka_text: न ह्ययं वैष्णवो दिव्य श्शर: परपुरञ्जय:। मोघ: पतति वीर्येण बलदर्पविनाशनः।।1.76.8।।
transliteration: na hyayaṃ vaiṣṇavo divya śśara: parapurañjaya:| mogha: patati vīryeṇa baladarpavināśanaḥ
translation: परपुरञ्जय: conquering hostile cities, वीर्येण by prowess, बलदर्पविनाशन: destroyer of the pride and strength, दिव्य: celestial, अयम् this, वैष्णव: शर: arrow of Vishnu, मोघ: vain, न पतति हि shall not fall.
explanation: On conquering the hostile cities and destroying the pride and strength of the enemy by its prowess, this celestial arrow of Visnu shall not go in vain".

shloka_text: वरायुधधरं रामं द्रष्टुं सर्षिगणा स्सुरा:। पितामहं पुरस्कृत्य समेतास्तत्र सङ्घश:।।1.76.9।। गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव सिद्धचारणकिन्नरा:। यक्षराक्षसनागाश्च तद्द्रष्टुं महदद्भुतम्।।1.76.10।।
transliteration: varāyudhadharaṃ rāmaṃ draṣṭuṃ sarṣigaṇā ssurā:| pitāmahaṃ puraskṛtya sametāstatra saṅghaśa: gandharvāpsarasaścaiva siddhacāraṇakinnarā:| yakṣarākṣasanāgāśca taddraṣṭuṃ mahadadbhutam
translation: वरायुधधरम् holding that mighty weapon, रामम् Rama, द्रष्टुम् to behold, सर्षिगणा: accompanied by sages, सुरा: devatas, पितामहम् grandsire, पुरस्कृत्य keeping in forefront, तत्र there, सङ्घश: in groups, समेता: assembled, गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव gandharvas and apsaras,  सिद्धचारणकिन्नरा: siddhas, charanas, kinnaras, यक्षराक्षसनागाश्च yakshas, rakshsas, nagas, तत् that, महत् great, अद्भुतम् wonder, द्रष्टुम् to see (came).
explanation: The gods with the Grandsire, Brahma in the forefront, accompanied by sages in groups assembled there to see Rama holding that mighty bow. Gandharvas, apsaras, siddhas, charanas, kinnaras, yakshas, rakshsas and nagas also came there to witness that great wonder.

shloka_text: वरायुधधरं रामं द्रष्टुं सर्षिगणा स्सुरा:। पितामहं पुरस्कृत्य समेतास्तत्र सङ्घश:।।1.76.9।। गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव सिद्धचारणकिन्नरा:। यक्षराक्षसनागाश्च तद्द्रष्टुं महदद्भुतम्।।1.76.10।।
transliteration: varāyudhadharaṃ rāmaṃ draṣṭuṃ sarṣigaṇā ssurā:| pitāmahaṃ puraskṛtya sametāstatra saṅghaśa: gandharvāpsarasaścaiva siddhacāraṇakinnarā:| yakṣarākṣasanāgāśca taddraṣṭuṃ mahadadbhutam
translation: वरायुधधरम् holding that mighty weapon, रामम् Rama, द्रष्टुम् to behold, सर्षिगणा: accompanied by sages, सुरा: devatas, पितामहम् grandsire, पुरस्कृत्य keeping in forefront, तत्र there, सङ्घश: in groups, समेता: assembled, गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव gandharvas and apsaras,  सिद्धचारणकिन्नरा: siddhas, charanas, kinnaras, यक्षराक्षसनागाश्च yakshas, rakshsas, nagas, तत् that, महत् great, अद्भुतम् wonder, द्रष्टुम् to see (came).
explanation: The gods with the Grandsire, Brahma in the forefront, accompanied by sages in groups assembled there to see Rama holding that mighty bow. Gandharvas, apsaras, siddhas, charanas, kinnaras, yakshas, rakshsas and nagas also came there to witness that great wonder.

shloka_text: जडीकृते तदाऽलोके रामे वरधनुर्धरे। निर्वीर्यो जामदग्न्योऽसौ रामो राममुदैक्षत।।।1.76.11।।
transliteration: jaḍīkṛte tadā'loke rāme varadhanurdhare| nirvīryo jāmadagnyo'sau rāmo rāmamudaikṣata|
translation: तदा then, रामे when Rama, वरधनुर्धरे was bearing that excellent bow, लोके world, जडीकृते having been made motionless, असौ this, जामदग्नय: son of Jamadagni, राम: Parasurama, निर्वीर्य: bereft of prowess, रामम् Rama, उदैक्षत gazed at him.
explanation: Then when Rama stretched the great bow, the world became motionless. The son of Jamadagni, Parasurama, bereft of prowess gazed at him with astonishment.

shloka_text: तेजोभिहतवीर्यत्वाज्जामदग्न्यो जडीकृत:। रामं कमलपत्राक्षं मन्दं मन्दमुवाच ह।।1.76.12।।
transliteration: tejobhihatavīryatvājjāmadagnyo jaḍīkṛta:| rāmaṃ kamalapatrākṣaṃ mandaṃ mandamuvāca ha
translation: तेजोभि: हतवीर्यत्वात् having been subdued of his energy by the prowess of Rama, जडीकृत: having been made motionless, जामदग्न्य: son of Jamadagni, कमलपत्राक्षम् him whose eyes resembling lotus petals, रामम् Rama, मन्दं मन्दम् slowly, slowly, उवाच ह spoke.
explanation: His energy subdued by Rama's prowess, the paralysed, Parasurama, son of Jamadagni spoke in gentle words to him whose eyes resembled the lotus petals:

shloka_text: काश्यपाय मया दत्ता यदा पूर्वं वसुन्धरा। विषये मे न वस्तव्यमिति मां काश्यपोऽब्रवीत्।।1.76.13।।
transliteration: kāśyapāya mayā dattā yadā pūrvaṃ vasundharā| viṣaye me na vastavyamiti māṃ kāśyapo'bravīt
translation: पूर्वम् formerly, वसुन्धरा earth, यदा when, मया by me, काश्यपाय for Kasyapa, दत्ता was  given, मे my, विषये in my country, न वस्तव्यम् इति shall not live, माम् me, काश्यप: Kasyapa, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: "When I gave this entire earth to Kasyapa, he said to me, 'you shall not live in my country'.

shloka_text: सोऽहं गुरुवच: कुर्वन् पृथिव्यां न वसे निशाम्। कृता प्रतिज्ञा काकुत्स्थ कृता भू: काश्यपस्य हि।।1.76.14।।
transliteration: so'haṃ guruvaca: kurvan pṛthivyāṃ na vase niśām| kṛtā pratijñā kākutstha kṛtā bhū: kāśyapasya hi
translation: सः अहम् such I, गुरुवच: words of my spiritual guide, कुर्वन् following, पृथिव्याम् on this earth, निशाम् during night, न वसे I will not live, काकुस्त्थ O Rama, प्रतिज्ञा vow, कृता has been made, भू: earth, काश्यपस्य for Kasyapa, कृता हि has been given.
explanation: O Descendant of Kakustha having gifted this earth to Kasyapa, I promised him that I would not live here, during night time. For the earth belongs to him.

shloka_text: तदिमां त्वं गतिं वीर हन्तुं नार्हसि राघव। मनोजवं गमिष्यामि महेन्द्रं पर्वतोत्तमम्।।1.76.15।।
transliteration: tadimāṃ tvaṃ gatiṃ vīra hantuṃ nārhasi rāghava| manojavaṃ gamiṣyāmi mahendraṃ parvatottamam
translation: वीर O Valourous one, राघव Rama, तत् for that reason, त्वम् you, इमाम् this, गतिम् power of motion, हन्तुम् to destroy, नार्हसि is not fit, मनोजवम् with the speed of mind, महेंद्रम् Mahendra mountain, पर्वतोत्तमम् best of hills, गमिष्यामि I shall go.
explanation: For this, you should not destroy my mobility, O valiant son of the Raghus. I shall go to Mahendra, the best of mountains, with the speed of mind.

shloka_text: लोकास्त्वप्रतिमा राम निर्जितास्तपसा मया	। जहि तान् शरमुख्येन मा भूत्कालस्य पर्यय:।।1.76.16।।
transliteration: lokāstvapratimā rāma nirjitāstapasā mayā	| jahi tān śaramukhyena mā bhūtkālasya paryaya:
translation: राम O Rama, मया by me, अप्रतिमा: unrivalled, लोका: worlds, तपसा by asceticism, निर्जिता: have been conquered, तान् them, शरमुख्येन with this chief of arrows, जहि strike, कालस्य time, पर्यय: delay, माभूत् let not happen.
explanation: Strike with the, principal arrow the unrivalled worlds conquered by my asceticism. Do not delay, O Rama

shloka_text: अक्षय्यं मधुहन्तारं जानामि त्वां सुरेश्वरम्। धनुषोऽस्य परामर्शात् स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु परंतप।।1.76.17।।
transliteration: akṣayyaṃ madhuhantāraṃ jānāmi tvāṃ sureśvaram| dhanuṣo'sya parāmarśāt svasti te'stu paraṃtapa
translation: अस्य this, धनुष: bow's, परामर्शात् from stretching, त्वाम् you, अक्षय्यम् imperishable one, सुरेश्वरम् lord of devatas, मधुहन्तारम् Visnu, the slayer of Madhu, जानामि I know, परंतप tormentor of enemies, ते स्वस्ति अस्तु safety to you.
explanation: By the fact that you have stretched this bow, I have come to know that you are Visnu, Lord of the gods, slayer of Madhu, O Imperishable one O Tormentor of enemies Fare well.

shloka_text: एते सुरगणास्सर्वे निरीक्षन्ते समागता:। त्वामप्रतिमकर्माणमप्रतिद्वन्द्वमाहवे।।1.76.18।।
transliteration: ete suragaṇāssarve nirīkṣante samāgatā:| tvāmapratimakarmāṇamapratidvandvamāhave
translation: समागता: assembled, एते these, सर्वे all, सुरगणा: hosts of devatas, अप्रतिमकर्माणम् of  incomparable deeds, आहवे in the combat, अप्रतिद्वन्द्वम् unassailable, त्वाम् you, निरीक्षन्ते are looking at.
explanation: All your deeds are incomparable. You are unassailable in combat. All these hosts of gods have assembled here and are looking at you.

shloka_text: न चेयं मम काकुत्स्थ व्रीडा भवितुमर्हति। त्वया त्रैलोक्यनाथेन यदहं विमुखीकृत:।।1.76.19।।
transliteration: na ceyaṃ mama kākutstha vrīḍā bhavitumarhati| tvayā trailokyanāthena yadahaṃ vimukhīkṛta:
translation: काकुत्स्थ O Rama, त्रैलोक्यनाथेन by the lord of three worlds, त्वया by you, अहम् I, यत् that    (I am), विमुखीकृत: have been defeated, इयम् this one, मे to me, व्रीडा shame, भवितुम् to become, न अर्हति does not behove.
explanation: I have been defeated by you, O Descendant of Kakustha lord of the three worlds. Therefore, it is not right for me to feel ashamed.

shloka_text: शरमप्रतिमं राम मोक्तुमर्हसि सुव्रत। शरमोक्षे गमिष्यामि महेन्द्रं पर्वतोत्तमम्।।1.76.20।।
transliteration: śaramapratimaṃ rāma moktumarhasi suvrata| śaramokṣe gamiṣyāmi mahendraṃ parvatottamam
translation: सुव्रत one faithful to vows, राम Rama, अप्रतिमम् incomparable, शरम् arrow, मोक्तुम् to release, अर्हसि behoves of you, शरमोक्षे after release of the arrow, पर्वतोत्तमम् excellent of mountains, महेन्द्रम् Mahendra, गमिष्यामि I shall go.
explanation: You are faithful to vows O Rama This arrow has no equal in prowess. It behoves of you to release it against me. After its release I shall go to the excellent Mahendra  mountain".

shloka_text: तथा ब्रुवति रामे तु जामदग्नये प्रतापवान्। रामो दाशरथि श्श्रीमान् चिक्षेप शरमुत्तमम्।।1.76.21।।
transliteration: tathā bruvati rāme tu jāmadagnaye pratāpavān| rāmo dāśarathi śśrīmān cikṣepa śaramuttamam
translation: जामदग्नये when the son of Jamadagni, रामे Parasurama, तथा in that way, ब्रुवति was saying, प्रतापवान् valiant, दाशरथि: son of Dasaratha, राम: Rama, उत्तमम् excellent, शरम् arrow, चिक्षेप employed.
explanation: Thus spoke  Parasurama, son of Jamadagni to Rama, the valiant son of Dasaratha who (then) discharged the principal arrow.

shloka_text: स हतान् दृश्य रामेण स्वांल्लोकांस्तपसार्जितान्। जामदग्न्यो जगामाशु महेन्द्रं पर्वतोत्तमम्।।1.76.22।।
transliteration: sa hatān dṛśya rāmeṇa svāṃllokāṃstapasārjitān| jāmadagnyo jagāmāśu mahendraṃ parvatottamam
translation: स: that, जामदग्न्य: Parasurama, तपसा by asceticism, अर्जितान् earned, स्वान् his own, लोकान् worlds, रामेण by Rama, हतान् struck, दृश्य having seen, आशु speedily, पर्वतोत्तमम् excellent among mountains, महेन्द्रम् Mahendra, जगाम went.
explanation: Having witnessed the destruction of those regions earned by him through asceticism, the son of Jamadagni left for the best of mountains Mahendra.

shloka_text: ततो वितिमिरास्सर्वा दिशश्चोपदिशस्तथा। सुरा स्सर्षिगणा रामं प्रशशंसुरुदायुधम्।।1.76.23।।
transliteration: tato vitimirāssarvā diśaścopadiśastathā| surā ssarṣigaṇā rāmaṃ praśaśaṃsurudāyudham
translation: तत: thereafter, सर्वा all, दिश: quarters, तथा also, उपदिश: intermediate quarters, वितिमिरा:  were cleared of darkness, सर्षिगणा: hosts of sages, सुरा: devatas, उदायुधम् wielding that bow, रामम् Rama, प्रशशंसु: extolled.
explanation: Thereafter all the quarters including the intermediaries were cleared of darkness. Hosts of sages and gods extolled Rama when he wielded the bow.

shloka_text: रामं दाशरथिं रामो जामदग्न्य: प्रशस्य च। तत: प्रदक्षिणी कृत्य जगामात्मगतिं प्रभु:।।1.76.24।।
transliteration: rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ rāmo jāmadagnya: praśasya ca| tata: pradakṣiṇī kṛtya jagāmātmagatiṃ prabhu:
translation: प्रभु: competent, जामदग्न्य: son of Jamadagni, राम: Parasurama, दाशरथिम् son of Dasaratha, रामम् Rama, प्रशस्य च having praised, तत: then, प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य having circumambulated him, आत्मगतिम् to his own abode, जगाम went.
explanation: Parasurama, the competent son of Jamadagni, having praised Rama, the son of Dasaratha circumbulated him and left for his abode. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे षट्सप्ततितमस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the seventysixth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: गते रामे प्रशान्तात्मा रामो दाशरथिर्धनु:। वरुणायाप्रमेयाय ददौ हस्ते ससायकम्।।1.77.1।।
transliteration: gate rāme praśāntātmā rāmo dāśarathirdhanu:| varuṇāyāprameyāya dadau haste sasāyakam
translation: रामे when Rama, गते had departed, प्रशान्तात्मा with serene mind, दाशरथि: son of Dasaratha, राम: Rama, ससायकम् together with arrow, धनु: bow, अप्रमेयाय immeasurable, strength, वरुणाय to Varuna, हस्ते in his hand, ददौ gave.
explanation: When Parasurama departed, Rama, son of Dasaratha with a serene mind gave the bow along with the arrow to Varuna of immeasurable strength.
comments: Dasaratha enters the city of Ayodhya with his sons and their wives--Bharata and Satrughna depart with their maternal uncle--Rama's virtues described.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्य ततो रामो वसिष्ठप्रमुखानृषीन्। पितरं विह्वलं दृष्ट्वा प्रोवाच रघुनन्दन:।।1.77.2।।
transliteration: abhivādya tato rāmo vasiṣṭhapramukhānṛṣīn| pitaraṃ vihvalaṃ dṛṣṭvā provāca raghunandana:
translation: तत: thereafter, रघुनन्दन: descendant of Raghu, राम: Rama, वसिष्ठप्रमुखान् Vasishta and other, ऋषीन् rishis, अभिवाद्य having paid obeisance, विह्वलम् agitated, पितरम् father, दृष्ट्वा  having seen, प्रोवाच said.
explanation: Thereafter Rama the descendant of the Raghus, paid obeisance to Vasishta and other rishis, and looked at his father who appeared agitated said:

shloka_text: जामदग्न्यो गतो राम: प्रयातु चतुरङ्गिणी। अयोध्याभिमुखी सेना त्वया नाथेन पालिता।।1.77.3।।
transliteration: jāmadagnyo gato rāma: prayātu caturaṅgiṇī| ayodhyābhimukhī senā tvayā nāthena pālitā
translation: जामदग्न्य: son of Jamadagni, राम: Rama, गत: had gone, नाथेन by being a lord, त्वया by you, पालिता ruled, चतुरङ्गिणी सेना four divisions of army, अयोध्याभिमुखी towards Ayodhya, प्रयातु let it advance.
explanation: "Parasurama, son of Jamadagni, has gone. Let the four divisions of the army of  which you are the commander proceed towards Ayodhya.

shloka_text: सन्दिशस्व महाराज सेनां त्वच्छासने स्थिताम्। शासनं काङ्क्षते सेना चातकालिर्जलं यथा।।1.77.4।।
transliteration: sandiśasva mahārāja senāṃ tvacchāsane sthitām| śāsanaṃ kāṅkṣate senā cātakālirjalaṃ yathā
translation: महाराज O King, त्वच्छासने in your command, स्थिताम् remaining, सेनाम् army, सन्दिशस्व direct it, चातकालि: rows of Chataka birds, जलं यथा like water, सेना army, शासनं command, काङ्क्षते is seeking.
explanation: The army which is under your command O King is awaiting your orders like the chatakas awaiting water. Direct them (to proceed).

shloka_text: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा दशरथ स्सुतम्। बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य मूर्ध्नि चाघ्राय राघवम्।।1.77.5।। गतो राम इति श्रुत्वा हृष्ट: प्रमुदितो नृप:। पुनर्जातं तदा मेने पुत्रमात्मानमेव च।।1.77.6।।
transliteration: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā daśaratha ssutam| bāhubhyāṃ sampariṣvajya mūrdhni cāghrāya rāghavam gato rāma iti śrutvā hṛṣṭa: pramudito nṛpa:| punarjātaṃ tadā mene putramātmānameva ca
translation: राजा king, दशरथ: Dasaratha, रामस्य Rama's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, सुतम् son, राघवम् Rama, बाहुभ्याम् with hands, सम्परिष्वज्य having embraced, मूर्ध्नि on the forehead, आघ्राय च having smelt (kissed in delight), राम: Parasurama, गत: इति had departed, श्रुत्वा having listened, हृष्ट: filled with joy, प्रमुदित: exceedingly delighted, नृप: king, पुत्रम् son, तदा then, आत्मानमेव himself as well, पुन: again, जातम् having been born, मेने considered.
explanation: On hearing the words 'Parasurama has departed' from Rama, king Dasaratha embraced him and kissed his forehead. The king, immensely happy, felt he and his son were reborn.

shloka_text: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा दशरथ स्सुतम्। बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य मूर्ध्नि चाघ्राय राघवम्।।1.77.5।। गतो राम इति श्रुत्वा हृष्ट: प्रमुदितो नृप:। पुनर्जातं तदा मेने पुत्रमात्मानमेव च।।1.77.6।।
transliteration: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā daśaratha ssutam| bāhubhyāṃ sampariṣvajya mūrdhni cāghrāya rāghavam gato rāma iti śrutvā hṛṣṭa: pramudito nṛpa:| punarjātaṃ tadā mene putramātmānameva ca
translation: राजा king, दशरथ: Dasaratha, रामस्य Rama's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, सुतम् son, राघवम् Rama, बाहुभ्याम् with hands, सम्परिष्वज्य having embraced, मूर्ध्नि on the forehead, आघ्राय च having smelt (kissed in delight), राम: Parasurama, गत: इति had departed, श्रुत्वा having listened, हृष्ट: filled with joy, प्रमुदित: exceedingly delighted, नृप: king, पुत्रम् son, तदा then, आत्मानमेव himself as well, पुन: again, जातम् having been born, मेने considered.
explanation: On hearing the words 'Parasurama has departed' from Rama, king Dasaratha embraced him and kissed his forehead. The king, immensely happy, felt he and his son were reborn.

shloka_text: चोदयामास तां सेनां जगामाशु तत: पुरीम्। पताकाध्वजिनीं रम्यां तूर्योद्घुष्टनिनादिताम्।।1.77.7।। सिक्तराज पथां रम्यां प्रकीर्णकुसुमोत्कराम्	। राजप्रवेशसुमुखै: पौरैर्मङ्गलवादिभि:।।1.77.8।। सम्पूर्णां प्राविशद्राजा जनौघैस्समलङ्कृताम्।
transliteration: codayāmāsa tāṃ senāṃ jagāmāśu tata: purīm| patākādhvajinīṃ ramyāṃ tūryodghuṣṭanināditām siktarāja pathāṃ ramyāṃ prakīrṇakusumotkarām	| rājapraveśasumukhai: paurairmaṅgalavādibhi: sampūrṇāṃ prāviśadrājā janaughaissamalaṅkṛtām|
translation: राजा king Dasaratha, ताम् that, सेनाम् army, चोदयामास directed, पताकाध्वजिनीम् adorned with flags and banners, रम्याम् beautiful, तूर्योद्घुष्टनिनादिताम् resounding with the sounds of trumpets, सिक्तराजपथाम् royal highways sprinkled with water, प्रकीर्णकुसुमोत्करामम् with flowers strewn, राजप्रवेशसुमुखै: delighted with the king's entry, मङ्गलवादिभि: making auspicious sounds with instruments, पौरै: by citizens, सम्पूर्णाम् filled with, जनौघै: by  groups of people, समलङ्कृताम् well decorated, पुरीम् city, आशु speedily, जगाम went.
explanation: Thereafter, king Dasaratha directed his army to proceed speedily in advance. When he    reached the city of Ayodhya it looked welldecorated with flags and banners. It  resounded with trumpets. The royal highways were sprinkiled with water and strewn with flowers. It was filled with groups of people. Awaiting with delight the arrival of  the king the citizens produced merry sounds with musical instruments.

shloka_text: चोदयामास तां सेनां जगामाशु तत: पुरीम्। पताकाध्वजिनीं रम्यां तूर्योद्घुष्टनिनादिताम्।।1.77.7।। सिक्तराज पथां रम्यां प्रकीर्णकुसुमोत्कराम्	। राजप्रवेशसुमुखै: पौरैर्मङ्गलवादिभि:।।1.77.8।। सम्पूर्णां प्राविशद्राजा जनौघैस्समलङ्कृताम्।
transliteration: codayāmāsa tāṃ senāṃ jagāmāśu tata: purīm| patākādhvajinīṃ ramyāṃ tūryodghuṣṭanināditām siktarāja pathāṃ ramyāṃ prakīrṇakusumotkarām	| rājapraveśasumukhai: paurairmaṅgalavādibhi: sampūrṇāṃ prāviśadrājā janaughaissamalaṅkṛtām|
translation: राजा king Dasaratha, ताम् that, सेनाम् army, चोदयामास directed, पताकाध्वजिनीम् adorned with flags and banners, रम्याम् beautiful, तूर्योद्घुष्टनिनादिताम् resounding with the sounds of trumpets, सिक्तराजपथाम् royal highways sprinkled with water, प्रकीर्णकुसुमोत्करामम् with flowers strewn, राजप्रवेशसुमुखै: delighted with the king's entry, मङ्गलवादिभि: making auspicious sounds with instruments, पौरै: by citizens, सम्पूर्णाम् filled with, जनौघै: by  groups of people, समलङ्कृताम् well decorated, पुरीम् city, आशु speedily, जगाम went.
explanation: Thereafter, king Dasaratha directed his army to proceed speedily in advance. When he    reached the city of Ayodhya it looked welldecorated with flags and banners. It  resounded with trumpets. The royal highways were sprinkiled with water and strewn with flowers. It was filled with groups of people. Awaiting with delight the arrival of  the king the citizens produced merry sounds with musical instruments.

shloka_text: पौरै: प्रत्युद्गतो दूरं द्विजैश्च पुरवासिभि:। पुत्रैरनुगत श्श्रीमान् श्रीमद्भिश्च महायशा: ।।1.77.9।। प्रविवेश गृहं राजा हिमवत्सदृशं पुनः।
transliteration: paurai: pratyudgato dūraṃ dvijaiśca puravāsibhi:| putrairanugata śśrīmān śrīmadbhiśca mahāyaśā:  praviveśa gṛhaṃ rājā himavatsadṛśaṃ punaḥ|
translation: पौरै: by the citizens, पुरवासिभि: living in the city, द्विजै: च by brahmins also, दूरम् from a long distance, प्रत्युद्गत: welcomed by walking towards him, श्रीमद्भि: by the graceful, पुत्रै: sons, अनुगत: followed by, श्रीमान् elegant, महायशा: possessing high fame, राजा king, पुन: again, हिमवत्सदृशम् resembling Himavat, गृहम् residence, प्रविवेश entered.
explanation: Prosperous king Dasaratha of great fame followed by his elegant sons entered the city of Ayodhya while the citizens and brahmins came forward from a long distance to welcome him who reentered his palace looking like the Himalayan mountain.

shloka_text: ननन्द सजनो राजा गृहे कामै स्सुपूजित:।।1.77.10।। कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च कैकेयी च सुमध्यमा। वधूप्रतिग्रहे युक्ता याश्चान्या राजयोषित:।।1.77.11।।
transliteration: nananda sajano rājā gṛhe kāmai ssupūjita: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca kaikeyī ca sumadhyamā| vadhūpratigrahe yuktā yāścānyā rājayoṣita:
translation: राजा king, गृहे in the residence, कामै: with objects of enjoyment, सुपूजितः well honoured, सजन: with his relations and family members, ननन्द rejoiced, कौसल्या च Kausalya, सुमित्रा च Sumitra, सुमध्यमा slender waisted, कैकेयी च Kaikeyi, या: ह्यन्या: others, राजयोषितः women of royal family, वधूप्रतिग्रहे in receiving the new brides, युक्ता: engaged.
explanation: The king and his kith and kin were received with honour in a pleasing manner. Kausalya, Sumitra and Kaikeyi of slender waist and other women attending on the king were busy in receiving the new brides.

shloka_text: ननन्द सजनो राजा गृहे कामै स्सुपूजित:।।1.77.10।। कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च कैकेयी च सुमध्यमा। वधूप्रतिग्रहे युक्ता याश्चान्या राजयोषित:।।1.77.11।।
transliteration: nananda sajano rājā gṛhe kāmai ssupūjita: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca kaikeyī ca sumadhyamā| vadhūpratigrahe yuktā yāścānyā rājayoṣita:
translation: राजा king, गृहे in the residence, कामै: with objects of enjoyment, सुपूजितः well honoured, सजन: with his relations and family members, ननन्द rejoiced, कौसल्या च Kausalya, सुमित्रा च Sumitra, सुमध्यमा slender waisted, कैकेयी च Kaikeyi, या: ह्यन्या: others, राजयोषितः women of royal family, वधूप्रतिग्रहे in receiving the new brides, युक्ता: engaged.
explanation: The king and his kith and kin were received with honour in a pleasing manner. Kausalya, Sumitra and Kaikeyi of slender waist and other women attending on the king were busy in receiving the new brides.

shloka_text: ततस्सीतां महाभागामूर्मिलां च यशस्विनीम्। कुशध्वजसुते चोभे जगृहुर्नृपपत्नय:।।1.77.12।।
transliteration: tatassītāṃ mahābhāgāmūrmilāṃ ca yaśasvinīm| kuśadhvajasute cobhe jagṛhurnṛpapatnaya:
translation: तत: thereafter, नृपपत्नय: king's wives, महाभागाम् highly fortunate, सीताम् Sita, यशस्विनीम्  having fame, ऊर्मिलां च Urmila, उभे both, कुशध्वजसुते daughters of Kusadhwaja, जगृहु: received.
explanation: Thereafter the queens received the highly fortunate Sita, Urmila of high fame and both the daughters of Kusadhwaja, Mandavi and Srutakirti.

shloka_text: मङ्गलालम्भनैश्चापि शोभिता: क्षौमवासस:। देवतायतनान्याशु सर्वास्ता: प्रत्यपूजयन्।।1.77.13।।
transliteration: maṅgalālambhanaiścāpi śobhitā: kṣaumavāsasa:| devatāyatanānyāśu sarvāstā: pratyapūjayan
translation: ता: सर्वा: all of them, मङ्गलालम्भनैश्चापि holding auspicious substances, शोभिता: shining, क्षौमवासस: attired in silken apparels, आशु immediately, देवतायतनानि temples, प्रत्यपूजयन् worshipped.
explanation: With auspicious aricles in their hands, all the new brides who shone in silken apparels immediately went to temples and worshipped the family deities.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्याभिवाद्यांश्च सर्वा राजसुतास्तदा। स्वं स्वं गृहमथासाद्य कुबेरभवनोपमम्।।1.77.14।। गोभिर्धनैश्च धान्यैश्च तर्पयित्वा द्विजोत्तमान्। रेमिरे मुदिता: सर्वा भर्तृभि: सहिता रह:।।1.77.15।।
transliteration: abhivādyābhivādyāṃśca sarvā rājasutāstadā| svaṃ svaṃ gṛhamathāsādya kuberabhavanopamam gobhirdhanaiśca dhānyaiśca tarpayitvā dvijottamān| remire muditā: sarvā bhartṛbhi: sahitā raha:
translation: तदा then, सर्वा: all of them, राजसुता: princesses, अभिवाद्यान् worthy of homage, अभिवाद्य having paid obeisance, अथ thereafter, कुबेरभवनोपमम् resembling the palace of Kubera, स्वं स्वम् their own, गृहम् residence, आसाद्य having reached, गोभि: with cows, धनैश्च with riches, धान्यैश्च with corn, द्विजोत्तमान् brahmins, तर्पयित्वा (अर्चयित्वा) having worshipped, रह: in private, भर्तृभि: with husbands, सहिता: united with, मुदिता: well pleased, रेमिरे enjoyed.
