explanation: Then all the princesses paid obeisance to those worthy of worship and entered their residence that resembled the palace of Kubera.Thereafter pleased with gifting  cows, riches and corn to brahmins and satisfying them they joined their husbands and enjoyed themselves in privacy

shloka_text: अभिवाद्याभिवाद्यांश्च सर्वा राजसुतास्तदा। स्वं स्वं गृहमथासाद्य कुबेरभवनोपमम्।।1.77.14।। गोभिर्धनैश्च धान्यैश्च तर्पयित्वा द्विजोत्तमान्। रेमिरे मुदिता: सर्वा भर्तृभि: सहिता रह:।।1.77.15।।
transliteration: abhivādyābhivādyāṃśca sarvā rājasutāstadā| svaṃ svaṃ gṛhamathāsādya kuberabhavanopamam gobhirdhanaiśca dhānyaiśca tarpayitvā dvijottamān| remire muditā: sarvā bhartṛbhi: sahitā raha:
translation: तदा then, सर्वा: all of them, राजसुता: princesses, अभिवाद्यान् worthy of homage, अभिवाद्य having paid obeisance, अथ thereafter, कुबेरभवनोपमम् resembling the palace of Kubera, स्वं स्वम् their own, गृहम् residence, आसाद्य having reached, गोभि: with cows, धनैश्च with riches, धान्यैश्च with corn, द्विजोत्तमान् brahmins, तर्पयित्वा (अर्चयित्वा) having worshipped, रह: in private, भर्तृभि: with husbands, सहिता: united with, मुदिता: well pleased, रेमिरे enjoyed.
explanation: Then all the princesses paid obeisance to those worthy of worship and entered their residence that resembled the palace of Kubera.Thereafter pleased with gifting  cows, riches and corn to brahmins and satisfying them they joined their husbands and enjoyed themselves in privacy

shloka_text: कुमाराश्च महात्मानो वीर्येणाप्रतिमा भुवि । कृतदारा: कृतास्त्राश्च सधना: ससुहृज्जना:।।1.77.16।। शुश्रूषमाणा: पितरं वर्तयन्ति नरर्षभा:।
transliteration: kumārāśca mahātmāno vīryeṇāpratimā bhuvi | kṛtadārā: kṛtāstrāśca sadhanā: sasuhṛjjanā: śuśrūṣamāṇā: pitaraṃ vartayanti nararṣabhā:|
translation: महात्मान: magnanimous, वीर्येण in prowess, भुवि on this earth, अप्रतिमा: incomparable, कृतदारा: having got married, कृतास्त्राश्च competent in the use of weapons, सधना: endowed with wealth, ससुहृज्जना: together with friends, नरर्षभा: excellent among men, कुमारा: sons, पितरम् father, शुश्रूषमाणा: serving, वर्तयन्ति were moving on their way.
explanation: All the princes who were best of men, great souls, incomparable in prowess on earth, capable of the use of weapons and endowed with wealth moved about with friends, serving their father and following his commands.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य राजा दशरथ: सुतम्।1.77.17।। भरतं कैकयीपुत्र मब्रवीद्रघुनन्दन:।
transliteration: kasyacittvatha kālasya rājā daśaratha: sutam|1.77.17|| bharataṃ kaikayīputra mabravīdraghunandana:|
translation: अथ thereafter, कस्यचित्कालस्य after some time, रघुनन्दनः delight of Raghu race, राजा दशरथ: king Dasaratha, कैकयीपुत्रम् son of Kaikeyi, सुतम् son, भरतम् addressing Bharata, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: After some time king Dasaratha the delight of the Raghu race addressed his son Bharata:

shloka_text: अयं केकयराजस्य पुत्रो वसति पुत्रक।।1.77.18।। त्वां नेतुमागतो वीर युधाजिन्मातुलस्तव।
transliteration: ayaṃ kekayarājasya putro vasati putraka tvāṃ netumāgato vīra yudhājinmātulastava|
translation: पुत्रक O Child, त्वाम् you, नेतुम् to take, आगत: has come, केकयराजस्य Kekaya king's, पुत्र: son, वीर: heroic one, तव your, मातुल: metarnal uncle, अयम् this, युधाजित् Yudhajit, वसति is here.
explanation: "The heroic Yudhajit son of the king of Kekaya, your maternal uncle, has come here and wishes to take you with him, O Child

shloka_text: प्रार्थितस्तेन धर्मज्ञ मिधिलायामहं तथा।।1.77.19।। ऋषिमध्ये तु तस्य त्वं प्रीतिं कर्तुमिहार्हसि।
transliteration: prārthitastena dharmajña midhilāyāmahaṃ tathā ṛṣimadhye tu tasya tvaṃ prītiṃ kartumihārhasi|
translation: धर्मज्ञ O Knower of duties, अहम् I, तेन by him, मिधिलायाम् in Mithila, ऋषिमध्ये in the midst of sages, तथा in that way, प्रार्थित: have been requested, त्वम् you, तस्य for him, प्रीतिम् delight, कर्तुम् to cause, अर्हसि behoves of you.
explanation: O Knower of dharma this was his request to me in Mithila in the midst of sages. You should bring him delight (by obliging him).

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा दशरथस्यैतद्भरत: कैकयीसुत:।।1.77.20।। अभिवाद्य गुरुं रामं परिष्वज्य च लक्ष्मणम्। गमनायाभिचक्राम शत्रुघ्नसहितस्तदा।।1.77.21।।
transliteration: śrutvā daśarathasyaitadbharata: kaikayīsuta: abhivādya guruṃ rāmaṃ pariṣvajya ca lakṣmaṇam| gamanāyābhicakrāma śatrughnasahitastadā
translation: कैकयीसुत: son of Kaikeyi, भरत: Bharata, दशरथस्य Dasaratha's, एतत् this, श्रुत्वा having heard, गुरुम् father, रामम् Rama, अभिवाद्य having paid obeisance, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, परिष्वज्य embracing, तदा then, शत्रुघ्नसहित: together with Satrughna, गमनाय to depart, अभिचक्राम started.
explanation: Having heard the words of Dasaratha, Bharata, son of Kaikeyi paid obeisance to his father and Rama, embraced Lakshmana and prepared for the journey with Satrughna.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा दशरथस्यैतद्भरत: कैकयीसुत:।।1.77.20।। अभिवाद्य गुरुं रामं परिष्वज्य च लक्ष्मणम्। गमनायाभिचक्राम शत्रुघ्नसहितस्तदा।।1.77.21।।
transliteration: śrutvā daśarathasyaitadbharata: kaikayīsuta: abhivādya guruṃ rāmaṃ pariṣvajya ca lakṣmaṇam| gamanāyābhicakrāma śatrughnasahitastadā
translation: कैकयीसुत: son of Kaikeyi, भरत: Bharata, दशरथस्य Dasaratha's, एतत् this, श्रुत्वा having heard, गुरुम् father, रामम् Rama, अभिवाद्य having paid obeisance, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, परिष्वज्य embracing, तदा then, शत्रुघ्नसहित: together with Satrughna, गमनाय to depart, अभिचक्राम started.
explanation: Having heard the words of Dasaratha, Bharata, son of Kaikeyi paid obeisance to his father and Rama, embraced Lakshmana and prepared for the journey with Satrughna.

shloka_text: आपृच्छ्य पितरं शूरो रामं चाक्लिष्टकारिणम्। मातृश्चापि नरश्रेष्ठ श्शत्रुघ्नसहितो ययौ।।1.77.22।।
transliteration: āpṛcchya pitaraṃ śūro rāmaṃ cākliṣṭakāriṇam| mātṛścāpi naraśreṣṭha śśatrughnasahito yayau
translation: शूर: valiant, नरश्रेष्ठ: excellent among men, Bharata, पितरम् father, अक्लिष्टकारिणम् doer of acts without fatigue, रामम् Rama, मातृश्चापि mothers also, आपृच्छ्य having asked (their leave), शत्रुघ्नसहित: together with Satrughna, ययौ departed.
explanation: Valiant Bharata, the best of men took leave of his father Dasaratha, a tireless brother Rama and mothers and departed with Satrughna.

shloka_text: गते तु भरते रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबल:। पितरं देवसंङ्काशं पूजयामासतुस्तदा।।1.77.23।।
transliteration: gate tu bharate rāmo lakṣmaṇaśca mahābala:| pitaraṃ devasaṃṅkāśaṃ pūjayāmāsatustadā
translation: तदा then, भरते when Bharata, गते had departed, राम: Rama, महाबल: mighty one,  लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana also, देवसंङ्काशम् resembling god, पितरम् father, पूजयामासतु: both of them served.
explanation: After the departure of Bharata, mighty Rama  and Lakshmana continued to serve their godlike father.

shloka_text: पितुराज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य पौरकार्याणि सर्वश:। चकार रामो धर्मात्मा प्रियाणि च हितानि च।।1.77.24।।
transliteration: piturājñāṃ puraskṛtya paurakāryāṇi sarvaśa:| cakāra rāmo dharmātmā priyāṇi ca hitāni ca
translation: धर्मात्मा Illustrious, राम: Rama, पितु: father's, आज्ञाम् command, पुरस्कृत्य treating with respect, प्रियाणि pleasing, हितानि च of wellbeing welfare, पौरकार्याणि the duties towards citizens, सर्वश: all ones, चकार made.
explanation: Righteous Rama discharged his duties towards the citizens for their allround comfort and welfare giving top priority to (the execution of) the command of his father.

shloka_text: मातृभ्यो मातृकार्याणि कृत्वा परमयन्त्रित:। गुरूणां गुरुकार्याणि काले कालेऽन्ववैक्षत।।1.77.25।।
transliteration: mātṛbhyo mātṛkāryāṇi kṛtvā paramayantrita:| gurūṇāṃ gurukāryāṇi kāle kāle'nvavaikṣata
translation: परमयन्त्रित: highly cotrolled and disciplined to his duties, मातृभ्य: for his mothers, मातृकार्याणि duties towards his mothers, कृत्वा having done, गुरूणाम् for adorable ones, गुरुकार्याणि duties towards Spiritual preceptors, काले काले at approprtiate times, अन्ववैक्षत supervised.
explanation: With unfailing regularity Rama carried out his duties towards his mothers, and his elders, looking into them from time to time.

shloka_text: एवं दशरथ: प्रीतो ब्राह्मणा नैगमास्तथा। रामस्य शीलवृत्तेन सर्वे विषयवासिन:।।1.77.26।।
transliteration: evaṃ daśaratha: prīto brāhmaṇā naigamāstathā| rāmasya śīlavṛttena sarve viṣayavāsina:
translation: एवम् in this way, रामस्य Rama's, शीलवृत्तेन with good conduct and character, दशरथ: Dasaratha, प्रीत: pleased, ब्राह्मणा: brahmanas, तथा also, नैगमा: inhabitants of the city, सर्वे all, विषयवासिन: the people of the country.
explanation: Dasaratha was pleased with the good conduct and character of Rama. Brahmanas as also the inhabitants of the city and the people of the country at large were happy with him.

shloka_text: तेषामतियशा लोके राम स्सत्यपराक्रमः। स्वयम्भूरिव भूतानां बभूव गुणवत्तर:।।1.77.27।।
transliteration: teṣāmatiyaśā loke rāma ssatyaparākramaḥ| svayambhūriva bhūtānāṃ babhūva guṇavattara:
translation: लोके in this world, अतियशा: possessing great fame, सत्यपराक्रम: truthful and full of prowess, गुणवत्तर: possessing many greater virtues, राम: Rama, तेषाम् for the people of that kingdom, भूतानाम् for beings, स्वयम्भू: इव like Brahma, बभूव became.
explanation: In world the glorious and virtuous Rama armed with the power of truthfulness became the protector of the people like Brahma (to living beings).

shloka_text: रामस्तु सीतया सार्धं विजहार बहूनृतून् । मनस्स्वी तद्गतस्तस्याः नित्यं हृदि समर्पित:।।1.77.28।।
transliteration: rāmastu sītayā sārdhaṃ vijahāra bahūnṛtūn | manassvī tadgatastasyāḥ nityaṃ hṛdi samarpita:
translation: मनस्वी the sensitive one, रामस्तु Rama, तद्गत: fixing his mind on Sita, तस्या: her, हृदि heart, नित्यम् always, समर्पित: dedicating, सीतया सार्धम् with Sita, बहून् many, ऋतून् seasons, विजहार went.
explanation: With his heart fixed on Sita to whom he was always devoted, Rama, the wise went about enjoying with her (the beauty of) all the seasons.

shloka_text: प्रिया तु सीता रामस्य दारा: पितृकृता इति। गुणाद्रूपगुणाच्चापि प्रीतिर्भूयोऽभ्यवर्धत।।1.77.29।।
transliteration: priyā tu sītā rāmasya dārā: pitṛkṛtā iti| guṇādrūpaguṇāccāpi prītirbhūyo'bhyavardhata
translation: सीता Sita, पितृकृता by his father, दारा इति as wife, रामस्य Rama's, प्रिया became beloved, गुणात् because of virtues, रूपगुणाच्चापि by virtue of beauty as well, प्रीति: affection, भूय: again, अभ्यवर्धत developed.
explanation: Chosen by his father Sita became Rama's beloved wife with her virtue and beauty his affection for her grew further.

shloka_text: तस्याश्च भर्ता द्विगुणं हृदये परिवर्तते। अन्तर्जातमपि व्यक्तमाख्याति हृदयं हृदा।।1.77.30।।
transliteration: tasyāśca bhartā dviguṇaṃ hṛdaye parivartate| antarjātamapi vyaktamākhyāti hṛdayaṃ hṛdā
translation: भर्ता her husband Rama, तस्या: her, हृदये heart, द्विगुणम् twice, परिवर्तते revolving, हृदयम् in heart, अन्तर्जातम् अपि every thought born inside also, हृदा with heart, व्यक्तम् clearly, आख्याति he will communicate.
explanation: For sita her husband was doubly dear. They were clearly communicating through each other's heart every thought generated in the mind.

shloka_text: गच्छता मातुलकुलं भरतेन तदाऽनघ। शत्रुघ्नो नित्यशत्रुघ्नो नीतः प्रीतिपुरस्कृतः।।2.1.1।।
transliteration: gacchatā mātulakulaṃ bharatena tadā'nagha| śatrughno nityaśatrughno nītaḥ prītipuraskṛtaḥ
translation: मातुलकुलम्  maternal uncle's house, गच्छता  set out, भरतेन by Bharata, तदा then, अनघ: sinless one, नित्यशत्रुघ्न: one who is always successful in destroying foes, शत्रुघ्न: Satrughna, प्रीतिपुरस्कृत:  endowed with affection, नीत: taken.
explanation: Bharata set out for his maternal uncle's house. He took with him the sinless Satrughna who is always successful in destroying foes and on whom he had bestowed his love and affection.
comments: Description of Rama's virtues Dasaratha contemplates to install Rama as heirapparent Invites kings and elders from towns and villages to seek their opinion.

shloka_text: तत्र न्यवसद्भ्रात्रा सह सत्कारसत्कृतः। मातुलेनाश्वपतिना पुत्रस्नेहेन लालितः।।2.1.2।।
transliteration: tatra nyavasadbhrātrā saha satkārasatkṛtaḥ| mātulenāśvapatinā putrasnehena lālitaḥ
translation: स: he (Bharata), अश्वपतिना by the lord of horses (here, by Aswapati), मातुलेन by his maternal uncle, सत्कारसत्कृत: treated with warm hospitality, पुत्रस्नेहेन with filial affection, लालित: was treated, भ्रात्रा सह along with his brother, तत्र there, न्यवसत् stayed on.
explanation: Treated with warm hospitality and fatherly affection by his maternal uncle Aswapati, Bharata stayed on there along with his brother.

shloka_text: तत्रापि निवसन्तौ तौ तर्प्यमाणौ च कामतः। भ्रातरौ स्मरतां वीरौ वृद्धं दशरथं नृपम्।।2.1.3।।
transliteration: tatrāpi nivasantau tau tarpyamāṇau ca kāmataḥ| bhrātarau smaratāṃ vīrau vṛddhaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam
translation: वीरौ heroes, भ्रातरौ both brothers, तत्र there, निवसन्तौ while living, कामत: of their own accord, तर्प्यमाणौ चापि even though satisfied, वृद्धम् aged, दशरथं नृपम् king Dasaratha, स्मरताम् (constanly) remembered.
explanation: Though both the heroic brothers stayed there satisfied on their own they constantly remembered their aged father.

shloka_text: राजाऽपि तौ महातेजा स्सस्मार प्रोषितौ सुतौ। उभौ भरतशत्रुघ्नौ महेन्द्रवरुणोपमौ।।2.1.4।।
transliteration: rājā'pi tau mahātejā ssasmāra proṣitau sutau| ubhau bharataśatrughnau mahendravaruṇopamau
translation: महातेजा: brilliant, राजापि the king also, महेन्द्रवरुणोपमौ  equal to great Indra and Varuna, प्रोषितौ who were away from home, सुतौ sons, भरतशत्रुघ्नौ उभौ both Bharata and Satrughna, सस्मार remembered.
explanation: The glorious king Dasaratha also remembered his sons, Bharata and Satrughna, who  were like the great Indra and Varuna, (now) away from home.

shloka_text: सर्व एव तु तस्येष्टा श्चत्वारः पुरुषर्षभाः। स्वशरीराद्विनिर्वृत्ताश्चत्वार इव बाहवः।।2.1.5।।
transliteration: sarva eva tu tasyeṣṭā ścatvāraḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ| svaśarīrādvinirvṛttāścatvāra iva bāhavaḥ
translation: चत्वार: four, पुरुषर्षभा: bull among men, सर्वे एव तु all of them, तस्य his, स्वशरीरात् from his body, निर्वृत्ता: originated, चत्वार: four, बाहव: इव just as arms, इष्टा: dear
explanation: Dasaratha, a bull among men, loved all his four sons equally just as the  arms of his own body.

shloka_text: तेषामपि महातेजा रामो रतिकरःपितुः। स्वयम्भूरिव भूतानां बभूव गुणवत्तरः।।2.1.6।।
transliteration: teṣāmapi mahātejā rāmo ratikaraḥpituḥ| svayambhūriva bhūtānāṃ babhūva guṇavattaraḥ
translation: भूतानाम् to all living beings, स्वयम्भूरिव like the Selfborn (Brahma), तेषामपि among them also, गुणवत्तरः  virtuous, महातेजा: effulgent, राम: Rama, पितु: to the father, रतिकर: was a source of delight, बभूव became.
explanation: Even among them the brilliant Rama was a source of delight to his father like the Selfborn (Brahma) to all living beings.

shloka_text: स हि देवैरुदीर्णस्य रावणस्य वधार्थिभिः। अर्थितो मानुषे लोके जज्ञे विष्णुस्सनातनः।।2.1.7।।
transliteration: sa hi devairudīrṇasya rāvaṇasya vadhārthibhiḥ| arthito mānuṣe loke jajñe viṣṇussanātanaḥ
translation: सनातन: the eternal, विष्णु: Visnu, उदीर्णस्य रावणस्य arrogant Ravana's, वधार्थिभि: by those desirous of slaying, देवै: by devatas, अर्थित: entreated, मानुषे लोके in the mortal world, स:  he (Rama), जज्ञे हि was born indeed.
explanation: Entreated by the devatas desirous of slaying arrogant Ravana, the eternal Visnu was indeed born in the mortal world as Rama.

shloka_text: कौशल्या शुशुभे तेन पुत्रेणामिततेजसा। यथा वरेण देवानामदितिर्वज्रपाणिना।।2.1.8।।
transliteration: kauśalyā śuśubhe tena putreṇāmitatejasā| yathā vareṇa devānāmaditirvajrapāṇinā
translation: अमिततेजसा of boundless energy, पुत्रेण with son, तेन by him, कौशल्या Kausalya, देवानां वरेण with the excellent among the devatas, वज्रपाणिना with the wielder of the thunderbolt (Indra), अदितिर्यथा like Aditi, शुशुभे looked splendid.
explanation: Kausalya looked splendid with her son, Rama of boundless energy, as did Aditi with the chief of the gods Indra, wielder of thunder.

shloka_text: स हि रूपोपपन्नश्च वीर्यवाननसूयकः। भूमौवनुपमस्सूनुर्गुणैर्दशरथोपमः।।2.1.9।।
transliteration: sa hi rūpopapannaśca vīryavānanasūyakaḥ| bhūmauvanupamassūnurguṇairdaśarathopamaḥ
translation: स: he (Rama), रूपोपपन्न: च handsome too, वीर्यवान् energetic, अनसूयक: free from envy, गुणै: by virtues, दशरथोपम: equal to Dasaratha, भूमौ on this earth, अनुपम: incomparable, सूनु: हि son he was.
explanation: Endowed with beauty and strengh, free from envy, and in virtues equal to Dasaratha, Rama was verily an incomparable son on earth.

shloka_text: स तु नित्यं प्रशान्तात्मा मृदुपूर्वं च भाषते। उच्यमानोऽपि परुषं नोत्तरं प्रतिपद्यते।।2.1.10।।
transliteration: sa tu nityaṃ praśāntātmā mṛdupūrvaṃ ca bhāṣate| ucyamāno'pi paruṣaṃ nottaraṃ pratipadyate
translation: नित्यम् always, प्रशान्तात्मा one with a calm and serene mind, स: he (Rama), मृदुपूर्वम् gently, भाषते speaks, परुषम् harsh words, उच्यमान: अपि though addressed, उत्तरम् reply, न प्रतिपद्यते does not speak.
explanation: With an unfailing serenity of mind, Rama never paid back harshness with harshness.

shloka_text: कथञ्चिदुपकारेण कृतेनैकेन तुष्यति। न स्मरत्यपकाराणां शतमप्यात्मवत्तया।।2.1.11।।
transliteration: kathañcidupakāreṇa kṛtenaikena tuṣyati| na smaratyapakārāṇāṃ śatamapyātmavattayā
translation: आत्मवत्तया with selfrestraint, स: he (Rama), कथञ्चित् somehow, कृतेन done (by some one), एकेन single, उपकारेण benefit rendered, तुष्यति is pleased, अपकाराणाम् offences, शतमपि even a hundred, न स्मरति does not remember.
explanation: Gifted with selfrestraint, Rama was pleased even with a single benefit done somehow to him, yet did not remember even a hundred offences  committed by others.

shloka_text: शीलवृद्धैर्ज्ञानवृद्धैर्वयोवृद्धैश्च सज्जनैः। कथयन्नास्त वै नित्यमस्त्रयोग्यान्तरेष्वपि।।2.1.12।।
transliteration: śīlavṛddhairjñānavṛddhairvayovṛddhaiśca sajjanaiḥ| kathayannāsta vai nityamastrayogyāntareṣvapi
translation: अस्त्रयोग्यान्तरेष्वपि even at intervals during  the practice of weapons, शीलवृद्धै: rich in virtues, ज्ञानवृद्धै: mature in wisdom, वयोवृद्धैश्च aged, सज्जनै: saintly persons, नित्यम् always, कथयन् आस्ते interacts.
explanation: Even during intervals of  his practice of weapons he never failed to interact with saintly persons and with people advanced in age, virtue and wisdom.

shloka_text: बुद्धिमान्मधुराभाषी पूर्वभाषी प्रियंवदः। वीर्यवान्न च वीर्येण महता स्वेन विस्मितः।।2.1.13।।
transliteration: buddhimānmadhurābhāṣī pūrvabhāṣī priyaṃvadaḥ| vīryavānna ca vīryeṇa mahatā svena vismitaḥ
translation: बुद्धिमान् wise, मधुराभाषी softspoken, पूर्वभाषी first to address, प्रियंवद: speaks pleasing words, वीर्यवान् valiant, महता overwhelming, स्वेन relating to his own, वीर्येण at his strength, न च विस्मित: surprised (here, proud).
explanation: Wise and softspoken, he was the first to speak to others words pleasing to hear. Though mighty, he was never proud of his overwhelming strength.

shloka_text: नचानृतकथो विद्वान् वृद्धानां प्रतिपूजकः। अनुरक्तः प्रजाभिश्च प्रजाश्चाप्यनुरञ्जते।।2.1.14।।
transliteration: nacānṛtakatho vidvān vṛddhānāṃ pratipūjakaḥ| anuraktaḥ prajābhiśca prajāścāpyanurañjate
translation: अनृतकथ: न च never indulged in falsehood, विद्वान् learned, वृद्धानाम् of elders, प्रतिपूजक: honours them by going forward, प्रजाभि: by his subjects, अनुरक्त: was loved, प्रजाश्चापि also his subjects, अनुरञ्जते loves.
explanation: Rama never told lies. He was a learned man. He honoured elders by going forward to them. He loved his subjects as much as his subjects loved him.

shloka_text: सानुक्रोशो जितक्रोधो ब्राह्मणप्रतिपूजकः। दीनानुकम्पी धर्मज्ञो नित्यं प्रग्रहवांश्चुचिः।।2.1.15।।
transliteration: sānukrośo jitakrodho brāhmaṇapratipūjakaḥ| dīnānukampī dharmajño nityaṃ pragrahavāṃścuciḥ
translation: सानुक्रोश: compassionate जितक्रोध: one who has conquered anger, ब्राह्मणप्रतिपूजक: worshipper of  brahmins, दीनानुकम्पी compassionate to the distressed, धर्मज्ञ: one who knows (follows) righteousness, नित्यम् always, प्रग्रहवान् selfrestrained, शुचि: pure in spirit.
explanation: He was kindhearted and compassionate to the distressed, coolheaded and righteous. A worshipper of brahmins he was always selfrestrained and pure in spirit.

shloka_text: कुलोचितमतिः क्षात्रं धर्मं स्वं बहुमन्यते। मन्यते परया कीर्त्या महत्स्वर्गफलं ततः।।2.1.16।।
transliteration: kulocitamatiḥ kṣātraṃ dharmaṃ svaṃ bahumanyate| manyate parayā kīrtyā mahatsvargaphalaṃ tataḥ
translation: कुलोचितमतिः having thoughts befitting his dynasty, स्वम् his own, क्षात्रं धर्मम् code of conduct relating to kshatriyas, बहुमन्यते honours, ततः from that,  कीर्त्या with glory, महत् great, स्वर्गफलम् fruits of heaven, मन्यते considers.
explanation: He entertained thoughts befitting his (great) dynasty and honoured the code of conduct of a kshatriya. He believed one could attain heavenly abode through his great achievements.

shloka_text: नाऽऽश्रेयसि रतो विद्वान्नविरुद्धकथारुचिः। उत्तरोत्तरयुक्तौ च वक्ता वाचस्पतिर्यथा।।2.1.17।।
transliteration: nā''śreyasi rato vidvānnaviruddhakathāruciḥ| uttarottarayuktau ca vaktā vācaspatiryathā
translation: अश्रेयसि pursuits not conducive to one's welfare, रतः न not interested, विद्वान् learned, विरुद्धकथारुचिः न not interested in speaking against others, उत्तरोत्तरयुक्तौ in debates, वाचस्पति: यथा like Brihaspati, वक्ता an orator
explanation: A learned man, he evinced no interest in pursuits that did not contribute to one's welfare or had he any liking for speaking against others. But in debates his oratorical flourish was comparable to Brihaspati's.

shloka_text: ﻿अरोगस्तरुणो वाग्मी वपुष्मान्देशकालवित्। लोके पुरुषसारज्ञ स्साधुरेको विनिर्मितः।।2.1.18।।
transliteration: ﻿arogastaruṇo vāgmī vapuṣmāndeśakālavit| loke puruṣasārajña ssādhureko vinirmitaḥ
translation: ﻿ अरोगः free from disease, तरुणः young, वाग्मी eloquent, वपुष्मान् healthy, देशकालवित् aware of time and place, पुरुषसारज्ञः a judge of men's worth, लोके in this world, विनिर्मितः created, एकः one, साधुः a sage.
explanation: ﻿ He was young, eloquent, healthy and free from disease. He was conscious of (right) time and place (for his pursuits). He was capable of ascertaining the potentiality of men. He was born a sage in this world.

shloka_text: स तु श्रेष्ठैर्गुणैर्युक्तः प्रजानां पार्थिवात्मजः। बहिश्चर इव प्राणो बभूव गुणतः प्रियः।।2.1.19।।
transliteration: sa tu śreṣṭhairguṇairyuktaḥ prajānāṃ pārthivātmajaḥ| bahiścara iva prāṇo babhūva guṇataḥ priyaḥ
translation: श्रेष्ठै: excellent, गुणैः with qualities, युक्तः bestowed with, सः he, पार्थिवात्मजः king's son, प्रजानाम् for his subjects, गुणतः by his virtues, प्रियः favourite one, बहिश्चरः exterior, प्राणः इव  like vital life, बभूव became.
explanation: Bestowed with such excellent qualities, the prince (Rama) became a favourite of his subjects.  He was like their vital life outside their bodies.

shloka_text: सम्यग्विद्याव्रतस्नातो यथावत्साङ्गवेदवित्। इष्वस्त्रे च पितु श्श्रेष्ठो बभूव भरताग्रजः।।2.1.20।।
transliteration: samyagvidyāvratasnāto yathāvatsāṅgavedavit| iṣvastre ca pitu śśreṣṭho babhūva bharatāgrajaḥ
translation: सम्यक् thoroughly, विद्याव्रतस्नातः had the sacred ablution marking the completion of the vow relating to the respective branches of learning, यथावत् in accordance with tradition, साङ्गवेदवित् knew Vedas along with its auxiliary sciences, भरताग्रजः elder brother of Bharata, इष्वस्त्रे in the science of archery, पितुः for father, श्रेष्ठ: best, बभूव became.
explanation: With the appropriate sacred ablution marking the completion of the vow relating to the respective branches of learning in accordance with tradition, this elder brother of Bharata achieved proficiency in the Vedas and its auxiliary sciences. He surpassed his father in archery.

shloka_text: कल्याणाभिजन स्साधुरदीन स्सत्यवागृजुः। वृद्धैरभिविनीतश्च द्विजैर्धर्मार्थदर्शिभिः।।2.1.21।।
transliteration: kalyāṇābhijana ssādhuradīna ssatyavāgṛjuḥ| vṛddhairabhivinītaśca dvijairdharmārthadarśibhiḥ
translation: कल्याणाभिजनः born in a family of noble descent, साधुः saintly person, अदीनः one without meanness, सत्यवाक् one truthful in his words, ऋजुः man of rectitude, धर्मार्थदर्शिभिः by those who are conversant in dharma and artha, वृद्धैः by the aged, द्विजैः by brahmins, अभिविनीतः welldisciplined.
explanation: Born in a family of noble descent, he was saintly. A man without meanness.He was truthful and a man of rectitude. The training he received under aged brahmins conversant with dharma and artha made him welldisciplined.

shloka_text: धर्मकामार्थतत्त्वज्ञः स्मृतिमान्प्रतिभानवान्। लौकिके समयाचारे कृतकल्पो विशारदः।।2.1.22।।
transliteration: dharmakāmārthatattvajñaḥ smṛtimānpratibhānavān| laukike samayācāre kṛtakalpo viśāradaḥ
translation: धर्मकामार्थतत्त्वज्ञः knower of true nature of dharma, artha and kama, स्मृतिमान् of (sharp) memory, प्रतिभानवान् of great genius, लौकिके समयाचारे in social practices and customs, कृतकल्पः accomplished in Kalpa (vedic rituals), विशारदः highly skilled.
explanation: He knew the true nature of dharma, artha and kama. With a sharp memory,  he was a genius. He was highly skilled in accomplishing tasks related to social practices and customs.

shloka_text: निभृत स्संवृताकारो गुप्तमन्त्र स्सहायवान्। अमोघक्रोधहर्षश्च त्यागसंयमकालवित्।।2.1.23।।
transliteration: nibhṛta ssaṃvṛtākāro guptamantra ssahāyavān| amoghakrodhaharṣaśca tyāgasaṃyamakālavit
translation: निभृतः modest, संवृताकारः one who concealed his feelings without any outward manifestation, गुप्तमन्त्र: one who counselled in secrecy, सहायवान् having good friends, अमोघक्रोधहर्षश्च his anger or pleasure did not go vain, त्यागसंयमकालवित् knows the occasion  when to sacrifice and when to excercise restraint.
explanation: He (Rama) was modest and did not reveal his inner feelings. He counselled in secrecy and had good friends. Never was his anger or pleasure in vain. He knew the occasion  when to sacrifce and when to exercise restraint.

shloka_text: ﻿दृढभक्ति स्स्थिरप्रज्ञो नासद्ग्राही न दुर्वचाः। निस्तन्द्रिरप्रमत्तश्च स्वदोषपरदोषवित्।।2.1.24।।
transliteration: ﻿dṛḍhabhakti ssthiraprajño nāsadgrāhī na durvacāḥ| nistandrirapramattaśca svadoṣaparadoṣavit
translation: ﻿ दृढभक्तिः was firm in his devotion, स्थिरप्रज्ञः possessed a steady intellect, असद्ग्राही न not one to accept anything ignoble, दुर्वचाः न no bad words, निस्तन्द्रि: devoid of idleness, अप्रमत्तः not swayed by emotions, स्वदोषपरदोषवित् knew his faults as well as of others.
explanation: ﻿ He was firm in his devotion and steady in intellect. He accepted nothing ignoble nor used bad words. He was not swayed by emotions or prone to idleness. He knew his faults as well as of others.

shloka_text: शास्त्रज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च पुरुषान्तरकोविदः। यः प्रग्रहानुग्रहयोर्यथान्यायं विचक्षणः।।2.1.25।।
transliteration: śāstrajñaśca kṛtajñaśca puruṣāntarakovidaḥ| yaḥ pragrahānugrahayoryathānyāyaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ
translation: यः who (he), शास्त्रज्ञः च wellversed in scriptures, कृतज्ञः च was grateful, पुरुषान्तरकोविद: skilled in differentiating the comparative merits of men, यथान्यायम् in accordance with  justice, प्रग्रहानुग्रहयोः in reprimanding and favouring, विचक्षणः was a skilled one.
explanation: He was versed in scriptures. He was grateful (to those who did him some good) and skilled in differentiating the comparative merits of men. Fair in his judgement he dispensed justice in accordance with law by reprimanding (the delinquent) and favouring (the honest).

shloka_text: सत्सङ्ग्रहप्रग्रहणे स्थानविन्निग्रहस्य च। आयकर्मण्युपायज्ञ स्सन्दृष्टव्ययकर्मवित्।।2.1.26।।
transliteration: satsaṅgrahapragrahaṇe sthānavinnigrahasya ca| āyakarmaṇyupāyajña ssandṛṣṭavyayakarmavit
translation: सत्सङ्ग्रहप्रग्रहणे in receiving and encouraging the righteous, निग्रहस्य च in  restraining also, स्थानवित् knower of right means, आयकर्मणि in acts of raising revenue, उपायज्ञः knower of means, सन् by being so, दृष्टव्ययकर्मवित् expending money in the prescribed manner.
explanation: He was skilled in  receiving and encouraging the righteous and in punishing (the wicked). He knew  whom to punish. He knew the right means of raising revenue and also expending money in the prescribed manner.

shloka_text: श्रैष्ठ्यं शास्त्रसमूहेषु प्राप्तो व्यामिश्रकेषु च। अर्थधमौ च सङ्गृह्य सुखतन्त्रो न चालसः।।2.1.27।।
transliteration: śraiṣṭhyaṃ śāstrasamūheṣu prāpto vyāmiśrakeṣu ca| arthadhamau ca saṅgṛhya sukhatantro na cālasaḥ
translation: शास्त्रसमूहेषु in scriptures, व्यामिश्रकेषु च also in the mutually interconnected (and which are mutually contradictory) branches of learning, श्रैष्ठ्यम् proficiency, प्राप्तः obtained, अर्थधर्मौ in artha and dharma, सङ्गृह्य having grasped,  सुखतन्त्रः sought pleasure, अलसः न not indolent.
explanation: He obtained proficiency in scriptures and interconnected (mutually contradictory) branches of learning. Only after having grasped the (philosophy of) artha (statecraft) and dharma (righteousness), he sought pleasure. He was never indolent.

shloka_text: वैहारिकाणां शिल्पानां विज्ञाताऽऽर्थविभागवित्। आरोहे विनये चैव युक्तो वारणवाजिनाम्।।2.1.28।।
transliteration: vaihārikāṇāṃ śilpānāṃ vijñātā''rthavibhāgavit| ārohe vinaye caiva yukto vāraṇavājinām
translation: वैहारिकाणाम् meant for entertainment, शिल्पानाम् of art and craft, विज्ञाता one who understood, अर्थविभागवित् one who knows how to dispense wealth, वारणवाजिनाम् on elephants and horses, आरोहे in mounting, विनये चैव in humbling, युक्तः was experienced.
explanation: He had understanding of art and craft useful for entertainment. He knew proper  ways of dispensing wealth. He was experienced in riding elephants and horses and in humbling them.

shloka_text: धनुर्वेदविदां श्रेष्ठो लोकेऽतिरथसम्मतः। अभियाता प्रहर्ता च सेनानयविशारदः।।2.1.29।।
transliteration: dhanurvedavidāṃ śreṣṭho loke'tirathasammataḥ| abhiyātā prahartā ca senānayaviśāradaḥ
translation: लोके in this world, धनुर्वेदविदाम् among those skilled in archery, श्रेष्ठः excellent,  अतिरथसम्मत: reckoned as a great wielder of warchariots by his equals, अभियाता advanced towards his enemies, प्रहर्ता च striking at them, सेनानयविशारदः expert in commanding troops.
explanation: He was the best among those skilled in archery in this world. He was reckoned as a great wielder of warchariots and one who strikes at the enemies by advancing towards them. He was an expert in commanding troops. (Atiratha is an excellent warrior who can manage his chariot, horses and the charioteer.)

shloka_text: अप्रधृष्यश्च सङ्ग्रामे क्रुध्दैरपि सुरासुरैः। अनसूयो जितक्रोधो न दृप्तो न च मत्सरी। न चावमन्ता भूतानां न च कालवशानुगः।।।2.1.30।।
transliteration: apradhṛṣyaśca saṅgrāme krudhdairapi surāsuraiḥ| anasūyo jitakrodho na dṛpto na ca matsarī| na cāvamantā bhūtānāṃ na ca kālavaśānugaḥ|
translation: क्रुद्धैः by the enraged, सुरासुरैरपि even by devatas or rakshasas, सङ्ग्रामे in the battle, अप्रधृष्यः was incapable of being repressed, अनसूयः free from envy, जितक्रोधः subdued his anger, न दृप्तः was not proud of, मत्सरी च न was not malicious, भूतानाम् among living beings, नच अवमन्ता never slighted, कालवशानुगः च न did not bow to the pressure of time
explanation: He was incapable of being repressed even by the enraged devatas or rakshasas in the battle. He was free from envy and had subdued his anger and pride. He was never malicious and he never slighted any living being nor did he bow to the pressure of time.

shloka_text: एवं श्रेष्ठगुणैर्युक्तः प्रजानां पार्थिवात्मजः। सम्मतस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वसुधायाः क्षमागुणैः।।2.1.31।। बुद्ध्या बृहस्पतेस्तुल्यो वीर्येणापि शचीपतेः।
transliteration: evaṃ śreṣṭhaguṇairyuktaḥ prajānāṃ pārthivātmajaḥ| sammatastriṣu lokeṣu vasudhāyāḥ kṣamāguṇaiḥ buddhyā bṛhaspatestulyo vīryeṇāpi śacīpateḥ|
translation: एवम् in this way, श्रेष्ठगुणैः with excellent qualities, युक्तः endowed, पार्थिवात्मजः son of the king, प्रजानाम् for his subjects, त्रिषु लोकेषु in the three worlds, सम्मतः was held in high esteem, क्षमागुणैः by the quality of forbearance, वसुधायाः by earth, बुद्ध्या by his  intelligence, बृहस्पतेः with Brihaspati's, वीर्येण by prowess, शचीपतेः consort of Sachi (Indra), तुल्यः equal.
explanation: Thus endowed with such excellent qualities, the subjects in the three worlds held him in high esteem. In forbearance he was like the earth, in wisdom like Brihaspati and in prowess like the consort of Sachi (Indra).

shloka_text: तथा सर्वप्रजाकान्तैः प्रीतिसंजननैः पितुः।।2.1.32।। गुणैर्विरुरुचे रामो दीप्तस्सूर्य इवांशुभिः।
transliteration: tathā sarvaprajākāntaiḥ prītisaṃjananaiḥ pituḥ guṇairviruruce rāmo dīptassūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ|
translation: तथा thus, सर्वप्रजाकान्तै: cherished by all his subjects, पितुः for his father, प्रीतिसंजननैः a source of delight, गुणैः by virtues, रामः Rama, अंशुभिः with rays, दीप्तः resplendent, सूर्यः इव like the Sun, विरुरुचे shone.
explanation: Rama whose virtues were cherished by all his subjects was a source of delight to his father and he shone like the rays of the resplendent Sun.

shloka_text: तमेवं व्रतसम्पन्नमप्रधृष्यपराक्रमम्।।2.1.33।। लोक पालोपमं नाथमकामयत मेदिनी।
transliteration: tamevaṃ vratasampannamapradhṛṣyaparākramam loka pālopamaṃ nāthamakāmayata medinī|
translation: एवं व्रतसम्पन्नम् enriched with such avowed virtues, अप्रधृष्यपराक्रमम् a man with indomitable prowess, लोकपालोपमम् equal to guardians of the quarters, तम् him, मेदिनी the earth, नाथम् as lord, अकामयत desired.
explanation: The earth desired him as her lord, for he was bestowed with such avowed virtues and with indomitable prowess equal to all the guardians of the quarters.

shloka_text: एतैस्तु बहुभिर्युक्तं गुणैरनुपमैस्सुतम्।।2.1.34।। दृष्ट्वा दशरथो राजा चक्रे चिन्तां परन्तपः।
transliteration: etaistu bahubhiryuktaṃ guṇairanupamaissutam dṛṣṭvā daśaratho rājā cakre cintāṃ parantapaḥ|
translation: परन्तपः subduer of enemies, दशरथः राजा king Dasaratha, अनुपमैः with incomparable, बहुभिः innumerable, एतैः these, गुणैः qualities, युक्तम् endowed with, सुतम् his son, दृष्ट्वा having seen, चिन्ताम् चक्रे contemplated.
explanation: Observing his son endowed with such innumerable and incomparable virtues, king Dasaratha, subduer of enemies started thinking.

shloka_text: अथ राज्ञो बभूवैवं वृद्धस्य चिरजीविनः।।2.1.35।। प्रीतिरेषा कथं रामो राजा स्यान्मयि जीवति।
transliteration: atha rājño babhūvaivaṃ vṛddhasya cirajīvinaḥ prītireṣā kathaṃ rāmo rājā syānmayi jīvati|
translation: अथ thereafter, चिरजीविनः a man of long life, वृद्धस्य of the aged, राज्ञः king, मयि me, जीवति while living, रामः Rama, राजा king, कथं स्यात् how will he become?, एषा प्रीतिः this pleasure, एवम् in this way, बभूव a (thought) flashed
explanation: Thereafter, flashed in the mind of that aged king who had (already) lived long this pleasant thought as to how Rama will become king while he was alive.

shloka_text: एषा ह्यस्य परा प्रीतिर्हृदि संपरिवर्तते।।2.1.36।। कदा नाम सुतं द्रक्ष्याम्यभिषिक्तमहं प्रियम्।
transliteration: eṣā hyasya parā prītirhṛdi saṃparivartate kadā nāma sutaṃ drakṣyāmyabhiṣiktamahaṃ priyam|
translation: अहम् I, अभिषिक्तम् coronate, प्रियं सुतम् dear son, कदा नाम oh when, द्रक्ष्यामि can I see, एषा this, परा great, प्रीतिः pleasure, अस्य his, हृदि in heart, संपरिवर्तते हि repeatedly surfaced.
explanation: The thought of seeing his dear son coronated repeatedly surfaced his mind so great was his affection (for Rama).

shloka_text: वृद्धिकामो हि लोकस्य सर्वभूतानुकम्पनः।।2.1.37।। मत्तः प्रियतरो लोके पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्।
transliteration: vṛddhikāmo hi lokasya sarvabhūtānukampanaḥ mattaḥ priyataro loke parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān|
translation: लोकस्य for this world, वृद्धिकामः desires to promote prosperity, सर्वभूतानुकम्पन: that (Rama) one who showed kindness to all living beings, वृष्टिमान् possessing rain, पर्जन्य: इव like Parjanya, the raingod, लोके in this world, मत्तः than me, प्रियतरः हि is dearer to  all people.
explanation: (He said to himself) 'his (Rama's) only desire is to promote the prosperity of this world. He is one who shows compassion to all beings and is like the raingod dearer than me to the people of the world'.

shloka_text: यमशक्रसमो वीर्ये बृहस्पतिसमो मतौ।।2.1.38।। महीधरसमो धृत्यां मत्तश्च गुणवत्तरः।
transliteration: yamaśakrasamo vīrye bṛhaspatisamo matau mahīdharasamo dhṛtyāṃ mattaśca guṇavattaraḥ|
translation: वीर्ये in prowess, यमशक्रसमः equal to Yama and Indra, मतौ in wisdom, बृहस्पति समः equal to Brihaspati, धृत्याम् in firmness, महीधरसमः equal to a mountain, मत्तः च than me also, गुणवत्तरः  a man of greater virtues.
explanation: 'In prowess he is equal to Yama and Indra,in wisdom to Brihaspati and in firmness to a mountain and in virtues greater than me'.

shloka_text: महीमहमिमां कृत्स्नामधितिष्ठन्तमात्मजम्।।2.1.39।। अनेन वयसा दृष्ट्वा यथास्वर्गमवाप्नुयाम्।
transliteration: mahīmahamimāṃ kṛtsnāmadhitiṣṭhantamātmajam anena vayasā dṛṣṭvā yathāsvargamavāpnuyām|
translation: कृत्स्नाम् entire dominion, इमाम् this, महीम् earth, अधितिष्ठन्तम् established, आत्मजम् son, अनेन in this, वयसा age, दृष्ट्वा having seen, अहम् I, यथा as if, स्वर्गम् heaven, अवाप्नुयाम् will attain.
explanation: 'Seeing my son ruling this entire dominion of the earth, I will experience the bliss of attaining heaven at this age.'

shloka_text: इत्येतैर्विविधैस्तैस्तैरन्यपार्थिवदुर्लभैः।।2.1.40।। शिष्टैरपरिमेयैश्च लोके लोकोत्तरैर्गुणैः। तं समीक्ष्य महाराजो युक्तं समुदितैश्शुभैः।।2.1.41।। निश्चित्य सचिवैस्सार्धं युवराजममन्यत।
transliteration: ityetairvividhaistaistairanyapārthivadurlabhaiḥ śiṣṭairaparimeyaiśca loke lokottarairguṇaiḥ| taṃ samīkṣya mahārājo yuktaṃ samuditaiśśubhaiḥ niścitya sacivaissārdhaṃ yuvarājamamanyata|
translation: इति in this manner, विविधैः various, अन्यपार्थिवदुर्लभैः not found in other kings, तै: तै: by respective, एतैः with these virtues, लोके in this world, अपरिमेयैः immeasurable, लोकोत्तरैः distinguished in this world, समुदितैः all converged at one place, शुभैः auspicious, शिष्टैः  praiseworthy, गुणैः virtues, युक्तम् endowed with, तम् him, समीक्ष्य having observed, महाराजः king (Dasaratha), सचिवैः सार्धम् with his ministers, निश्चित्य having decided, युवराजम् as princeregent, अमन्यत thought.
explanation: King Dasaratha in consultation with his ministers observed that Rama is endowed  with various virtues not found in other kings, immeasurable virtues which are praiseworthy, and exemplary. He is distinguished in this world as all qualities seem to have merged in him. The king then made up his mind to make him princeregent.

shloka_text: इत्येतैर्विविधैस्तैस्तैरन्यपार्थिवदुर्लभैः।।2.1.40।। शिष्टैरपरिमेयैश्च लोके लोकोत्तरैर्गुणैः। तं समीक्ष्य महाराजो युक्तं समुदितैश्शुभैः।।2.1.41।। निश्चित्य सचिवैस्सार्धं युवराजममन्यत।
transliteration: ityetairvividhaistaistairanyapārthivadurlabhaiḥ śiṣṭairaparimeyaiśca loke lokottarairguṇaiḥ| taṃ samīkṣya mahārājo yuktaṃ samuditaiśśubhaiḥ niścitya sacivaissārdhaṃ yuvarājamamanyata|
translation: इति in this manner, विविधैः various, अन्यपार्थिवदुर्लभैः not found in other kings, तै: तै: by respective, एतैः with these virtues, लोके in this world, अपरिमेयैः immeasurable, लोकोत्तरैः distinguished in this world, समुदितैः all converged at one place, शुभैः auspicious, शिष्टैः  praiseworthy, गुणैः virtues, युक्तम् endowed with, तम् him, समीक्ष्य having observed, महाराजः king (Dasaratha), सचिवैः सार्धम् with his ministers, निश्चित्य having decided, युवराजम् as princeregent, अमन्यत thought.
explanation: King Dasaratha in consultation with his ministers observed that Rama is endowed  with various virtues not found in other kings, immeasurable virtues which are praiseworthy, and exemplary. He is distinguished in this world as all qualities seem to have merged in him. The king then made up his mind to make him princeregent.

shloka_text: दिव्यन्तरिक्षे भूमौ च घोरमुत्पातजं भयम्।।2.1.42।। स़ञ्चचक्षेऽथ मेधावी शरीरे चात्मनो जराम्।
transliteration: divyantarikṣe bhūmau ca ghoramutpātajaṃ bhayam sa़ñcacakṣe'tha medhāvī śarīre cātmano jarām|
translation: अथ thereafter, मेधावी sagacious (Dasaratha), दिवि in heaven, अन्तरिक्षे in the sky, भूमौ च on earth, उत्पातजम् portentous omens, घोरम् dreadful, भयम् fear, आत्मनः his, शरीरे in the body, जरां च old age also, सञ्चचक्षे perceived.
explanation: The sagacious king, too perceived his body ageing and the portentous omens in the heaven, in the sky and on the earth causing dreadful concern.

shloka_text: पूर्णचन्द्राननस्याथ शोकापनुदमात्मनः।।2.1.43।। लोके रामस्य बुबुधे सम्प्रियत्वं महात्मनः।
transliteration: pūrṇacandrānanasyātha śokāpanudamātmanaḥ loke rāmasya bubudhe sampriyatvaṃ mahātmanaḥ|
translation: अथ afterwards, पूर्णचन्द्राननस्य having countenance resembling the full Moon, महात्मनः of the noble, रामस्य Rama's, आत्मनः his, शोकापनुदम् dispeller of grief, लोके सम्प्रियत्वम् he being a favourite of the people, बुबुधे realised.
explanation: The king realised afterwards that his grief would be dispelled if noble Rama whose countenance resembled the full moon and who was a favourite of the people is crowned.

shloka_text: आत्मनश्च प्रजानां च श्रेयसे च प्रियेण च।।2.1.44।। प्राप्तकालेन धर्मात्मा भक्त्या त्वरितवान् नृपः।
transliteration: ātmanaśca prajānāṃ ca śreyase ca priyeṇa ca prāptakālena dharmātmā bhaktyā tvaritavān nṛpaḥ|
translation: धर्मात्मा righteous नृपः king, आत्मनश्च of his own, प्रजानां च of his subjects, श्रेयसे च for the welfare, प्रियेण च with much love, प्राप्तकालेन proper time having come, भक्त्या with longing, त्वरितवान् hastened.
explanation: Longing for it, the noble king realized that the time was ripe for the acceleration of the process of safeguarding his own and his subjects' welfare.

shloka_text: नानानगरवास्तव्यान्पृथग्जानपदानपि।।2.1.45।। समानिनाय मेदिन्याः प्रधानान्पृथिवीपतीन्।
transliteration: nānānagaravāstavyānpṛthagjānapadānapi samānināya medinyāḥ pradhānānpṛthivīpatīn|
translation: नानानगरवास्तव्यान् residents of various cities, जानपदानपि villagers also, मेदिन्याः of this earth, प्रधानान् important persons exercising authority, पृथिवीपतीन् kings, पृथक् separately, समानिनाय summoned.
explanation: He summoned individually kings and all important citizens residing in various cities and villages of this earth.

shloka_text: न तु केकयराजानं जनकं वा नराधिपः।।2.1.46।। त्वरया चानयामास पश्चात्तौ श्रोष्यतः प्रियम्।
transliteration: na tu kekayarājānaṃ janakaṃ vā narādhipaḥ tvarayā cānayāmāsa paścāttau śroṣyataḥ priyam|
translation: नराधिपः the king (Dasaratha), त्वरया in  haste, केकयराजानम् king of Kekaya country, जनकं वा or Janaka, तौ both of them, प्रियम् glad news, पश्चात् afterwards, श्रोष्यतः would hear, न आनयामास did not summon.
explanation: The king did not invite both the kings of Kekaya and Janaka  in  haste with an  intention that they would hear the glad news at a later date.

shloka_text: तान्वेश्मनानाभरणैर्यथाऽर्हं प्रतिपूजितान्।।2.1.47।। ददर्शालङ्कृतो राजा प्रजापतिरिव प्रजाः।
transliteration: tānveśmanānābharaṇairyathā'rhaṃ pratipūjitān dadarśālaṅkṛto rājā prajāpatiriva prajāḥ|
translation: वेश्मनानाभरणैः  houses and ornaments, यथार्हम् in a befitting manner, प्रतिपूजितान् having been received respectfully, तान् all of them, राजा king (Dasaratha), अलङ्कृतः adorned, प्रजापतिः lord Brahma, प्रजाः इव like people, ददर्श beheld.
explanation: The king who received them in a befitting manner and provided them with residence and ornaments looked like lord Brahma adorned by the people.

shloka_text: अथोपविष्टे नृपतौ तस्मिन्परबलार्दने।।2.1.48।। ततः प्रविविशु श्शेषा राजानो लोकसम्मताः।
transliteration: athopaviṣṭe nṛpatau tasminparabalārdane tataḥ praviviśu śśeṣā rājāno lokasammatāḥ|
translation: अथ then, परबलार्दने tormenter of the enemy forces, तस्मिन् that, नृपतौ king, उपविष्टे when he was seated, ततः thereafter, लोकसम्मताः beloved of their subjects, शेषाः remaining, राजानः kings, प्रविविशुः entered.
explanation: After the king (Dasaratha) who was a tormenter of enemy forces was seated, the rest of the kings beloved of their subjects entered (the assembly hall).

shloka_text: अथ राजवितीर्णेषु विविधेष्वासनेषु च।।2.1.49।। राजानमेवाभिमुखाः निषेदुर्नियता नृपाः।
transliteration: atha rājavitīrṇeṣu vividheṣvāsaneṣu ca rājānamevābhimukhāḥ niṣedurniyatā nṛpāḥ|
translation: अथ then, नृपाः (those) kings, राजवितीर्णेषु given by king, विविधेषु different, आसनेषु in the seats, राजानमेव the king alone, अभिमुखाः facing, नियताः following the royal tradition, निषेदु: were seated.
explanation: Then  the kings (who entered the assembly) took the seats assigned to them facing the king (Dasaratha), following the royal tradition.

shloka_text: सलब्धमानैर्विनयान्वितैर्नृपैः पुरालयैर्जानपदैश्च मानदैः। उपोपविष्टैर्नृपतिर्वृतो बभौ सहस्रचक्षुर्भगवानिवामरैः।।2.1.50।।
transliteration: salabdhamānairvinayānvitairnṛpaiḥ purālayairjānapadaiśca mānadaiḥ| upopaviṣṭairnṛpatirvṛto babhau sahasracakṣurbhagavānivāmaraiḥ
translation: लब्धमानैः by those who received honour, विनयान्वितैः by those endowed with modesty, उपोपविष्टैः by those seated nearby, नृपैः by the kings, पुरालयैः by those residing in towns, जानपदैः च also in villages, मानदै: by the respectful,  वृतः surrounded by, सः नृपतिः that king, अमरैः by devatas, भगवान् lord, सहस्रचक्षुरिव like the thousandeyed (Indra), बभौ shone.
explanation: Surrounded by those feudatory kings endowed with modesty, and received with due honour and by the respectful residents of cities and villages, the king (Dasaratha), resembled lord Indra, the thousand eyed encircled by the gods. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे प्रथमस्सर्गः। Thus ends the first sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततः परिषदं सर्वामामन्त्र्य वसुधाधिपः। हितमुद्धर्षणं चैवमुवाच प्रथितं वचः।।2.2.1।।
transliteration: tataḥ pariṣadaṃ sarvāmāmantrya vasudhādhipaḥ| hitamuddharṣaṇaṃ caivamuvāca prathitaṃ vacaḥ
translation: तत: thereafter, वसुधाधिप: lord of the earth (king Dasaratha), सर्वाम् entire, परिषदम् assembly, आमन्त्र्य having invited, हितम् aimed at their welfare, उर्द्धर्षणम् thrilling, प्रथितम् pleasing, वच: words, एवं in this manner, उवाच spoke.
explanation: Thereafter, the lord of the earth (king Dasaratha) addressed the entire assembly of  invitees. He spoke these pleasing words aimed at their welfare which thrilled and delighted the hearts (of the assembled kings):
comments: Dasaratha commends to the assembly of elders and counsellors for installation of Rama as Prince Regent-- Assembly approves the proposal of Dasaratha with delight describing the virtues of Rama in support of their approval.

shloka_text: ﻿दुन्दुभिस्वनकल्पेन गम्भीरेणानुनादिना। स्वरेण महता राजा जीमूत इव नादयन्।।2.2.2।। राजलक्षणयुक्तेन कान्तेनानुपमेन च। उवाच रसयुक्तेन स्वरेण नृपतिर्नृपान्।।2.2.3।।
transliteration: ﻿dundubhisvanakalpena gambhīreṇānunādinā| svareṇa mahatā rājā jīmūta iva nādayan rājalakṣaṇayuktena kāntenānupamena ca| uvāca rasayuktena svareṇa nṛpatirnṛpān
translation: ﻿ नृपति: lord of men, राजा king (Dasaratha), दुन्दुभिस्वनकल्पेन resonant as the sound of a kettledrum, गम्भीरेण with a deep (voice), अनुनादिना echoing, महता great, स्वरेण with voice, जीमूत: इव like the cloud, नादयन् thundering, राजलक्षणयुक्तेन having traits of royalty, कान्तेन with an attractive voice, अनुपमेन च and with an incomparable, रसयुक्तेन delightful, स्वरेण with voice, नृपान् addressing kings, उवाच said.
explanation: ﻿ Lord of men (king Dasaratha) addressed the feudatory kings with words deep, resonant, loud like the kettledrum or the rumbling cloud, in a delightful, incomparable and attractive voice that carried all the dignity of royalty:

shloka_text: ﻿दुन्दुभिस्वनकल्पेन गम्भीरेणानुनादिना। स्वरेण महता राजा जीमूत इव नादयन्।।2.2.2।। राजलक्षणयुक्तेन कान्तेनानुपमेन च। उवाच रसयुक्तेन स्वरेण नृपतिर्नृपान्।।2.2.3।।
transliteration: ﻿dundubhisvanakalpena gambhīreṇānunādinā| svareṇa mahatā rājā jīmūta iva nādayan rājalakṣaṇayuktena kāntenānupamena ca| uvāca rasayuktena svareṇa nṛpatirnṛpān
translation: ﻿ नृपति: lord of men, राजा king (Dasaratha), दुन्दुभिस्वनकल्पेन resonant as the sound of a kettledrum, गम्भीरेण with a deep (voice), अनुनादिना echoing, महता great, स्वरेण with voice, जीमूत: इव like the cloud, नादयन् thundering, राजलक्षणयुक्तेन having traits of royalty, कान्तेन with an attractive voice, अनुपमेन च and with an incomparable, रसयुक्तेन delightful, स्वरेण with voice, नृपान् addressing kings, उवाच said.
explanation: ﻿ Lord of men (king Dasaratha) addressed the feudatory kings with words deep, resonant, loud like the kettledrum or the rumbling cloud, in a delightful, incomparable and attractive voice that carried all the dignity of royalty:

shloka_text: विदितं भवतामेतद्यथा मे राज्यमुत्तमम्। पूर्वकैर्मम राजेन्द्रैस्सुतवत्परिपालितम्।।2.2.4।।
transliteration: viditaṃ bhavatāmetadyathā me rājyamuttamam| pūrvakairmama rājendraissutavatparipālitam
translation: मे my, उत्तमम् greatest, राज्यम् kingdom, मम my, पूर्वकै: by the predecessors, राजेन्द्रै: by great kings, सुतवत् like children, यथा like, परिपालितम् were ruled, एतत् all this, भवताम् to you, विदितम् is wellknown.
explanation: It is wellknown to all of you that people of this greatest kingdom were ruled by my predecessors who were great kings, who looked after the subjects as though they were their own children.

shloka_text: सोऽहमिक्ष्वाकुभि स्सर्वैर्नरेन्द्रैः परिपालितम्। श्रेयसा योक्तुकामोऽस्मि सुखार्हमखिलं जगत्।।2.2.5।।
transliteration: so'hamikṣvākubhi ssarvairnarendraiḥ paripālitam| śreyasā yoktukāmo'smi sukhārhamakhilaṃ jagat
translation: स: such, अहम् I, इक्ष्वाकुभि: belonging to the Ikshvaku race, सर्वै: by all, नरेन्द्रै: by kings, परिपालितम् ruled, सुखार्हम् worthy of happiness, अखिलम् entire, जगत् world, श्रेयसा with welfare, योक्तुकाम: अस्मि desire to  accomplish.
explanation: I desire to  accomplish the welfare of this entire world which deserves the happiness brought about by the rule of all the Ikshvaku kings.

shloka_text: ﻿मयाप्याचरितं पूर्वैः पन्थानमनुगच्छता। प्रजा नित्यमनिद्रेण यथाशक्त्यभिरक्षिताः।।2.2.6।।
transliteration: ﻿mayāpyācaritaṃ pūrvaiḥ panthānamanugacchatā| prajā nityamanidreṇa yathāśaktyabhirakṣitāḥ
translation: ﻿ पूर्वै: by my predecessors, आचरितम् trodden, पन्थानम् path, अनुगच्छता while following, नित्यम् always, अनिद्रेण vigilant, मयापि by me also, प्रजा: people, यथाशक्ति to the best of my ability, अभिरक्षिता: were protected.
explanation: ﻿ Following the path of my forefathers I protected the people to the best of my ability by being ever vigilant.

shloka_text: इदं शरीरं कृत्स्नस्य लोकस्य चरता हितम्। पाण्डुरस्याऽतपत्रस्यच्छायायां जरितं मया।।2.2.7।।
transliteration: idaṃ śarīraṃ kṛtsnasya lokasya caratā hitam| pāṇḍurasyā'tapatrasyacchāyāyāṃ jaritaṃ mayā
translation: कृत्स्नस्य of the entire, लोकस्य world's, हितम् welfare, चरता observing, मया by me, इदम् this, शरीरम् body, पाण्डुरस्य white, आतपत्रस्य royal parasol's, छायायाम् under the shadow, जरितम् attained old age.
explanation: My body has attained old age after ruling the entire world ensuring the welfare of the people under the shade of royal white parasol.

shloka_text: प्राप्य वर्षसहस्राणि बहून्यायूंषि जीवतः। जीर्णस्यास्य शरीरस्य विश्रान्तिमभिरोचये।।2.2.8।।
transliteration: prāpya varṣasahasrāṇi bahūnyāyūṃṣi jīvataḥ| jīrṇasyāsya śarīrasya viśrāntimabhirocaye
translation: बहूनि several, वर्षसहस्राणि thousands of years, आयूंषि lifespan, प्राप्य having reached,    जीवत: while living, जीर्णस्य of the decayed, अस्य शरीरस्य for this body, विश्रान्तिम् rest, अभिरोचये I desired.
explanation: Having lived for thousands of years this body is now worn out  due to old age and therefore I want rest.

shloka_text: राजप्रभावजुष्टां हि दुर्वहामजितेन्द्रियैः। परिश्रान्तोऽस्मि लोकस्य गुर्वीं धर्मधुरं वहन्।।2.2.9।।
transliteration: rājaprabhāvajuṣṭāṃ hi durvahāmajitendriyaiḥ| pariśrānto'smi lokasya gurvīṃ dharmadhuraṃ vahan
translation: राजप्रभावजुष्टां with royal qualities (might, courage etc.,), अजितेन्द्रियै: by those who have not controlled their senses, दुर्वहाम् difficult to sustain, गुर्वीम् heavy, लोकस्य world's, धर्मधुरम् burden of duty, वहन् carrying, परिश्रान्त: अस्मि I have become weary.
explanation: I am weary of carrying on the heavy burden of duty and find it difficult to sustain the rule of dharma. It can be shouldered by those who have royal qualities (of might, courage etc) and not by those who have not controlled their senses.

shloka_text: सोऽहं विश्रममिच्छामि पुत्रं कृत्वा प्रजाहिते। सन्निकृष्टानिमान्सर्वाननुमान्य द्विजर्षभान्।।2.2.10।।
transliteration: so'haṃ viśramamicchāmi putraṃ kṛtvā prajāhite| sannikṛṣṭānimānsarvānanumānya dvijarṣabhān
translation: स: अहम् such as I am, सन्निकृष्टान् assembled, इमान् these, द्विजर्षभान् the best among (learned) brahmins, सर्वान् all, अनुमान्य after convincing them, पुत्रम् my son, प्रजाहिते for the welfare of the people, कृत्वा having consecrated, विश्रमम् rest, इच्छामि am desiring.
explanation: Therefore, after convincing all of you, the best of (learned) brahmins present here, I intend to take rest by installing my son to look after the welfare of the people.

shloka_text: अनुजातो हि मां सर्वैर्गुणैर्ज्येष्ठो ममात्मजः। पुरन्दरसमो वीर्ये रामः परपुरञ्जयः।।2.2.11।।
transliteration: anujāto hi māṃ sarvairguṇairjyeṣṭho mamātmajaḥ| purandarasamo vīrye rāmaḥ parapurañjayaḥ
translation: वीर्ये in prowess, पुरन्दरसम: equal to Indra, परपुरञ्जय: conqueror of enemy cities, मम my , ज्येष्ठ: आत्मज: eldest son, राम: Rama, सर्वै: by all, गुणै: virtues, माम् me, अनुजात: हि inherited indeed.
explanation: My eldest son Rama, inheriting every virtue of mine, is a conqueror of enemy cities  and is equal to Indra in prowess.

shloka_text: तं चन्द्रमिव पुष्येण युक्तं धर्मभृतां वरम्। यौवराज्ये नियोक्ताऽस्मि प्रीतः पुरुषपुङ्गवम्।।2.2.12।।
transliteration: taṃ candramiva puṣyeṇa yuktaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam| yauvarājye niyoktā'smi prītaḥ puruṣapuṅgavam
translation: पुष्येण by the Pushya star, युक्तम् in conjunction, चन्द्रमिव resembling moon, धर्मभृताम् among upholders of righteousness, वरम् best, पुरुषपुङ्गवम् foremost among men, तम् him (Rama), प्रीत: pleased, यौवराज्ये as heirapparent, नियोक्ताऽस्मि propose to install.
explanation: I propose to install him (Rama), foremost among upholders of righteousness and the best of men who resembles the Moon in brightness when in conjunction with Pushya star, as heirapparent to the throne.

shloka_text: अनुरूपस्स वै नाथो लक्ष्मीवान् लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। त्रैलोक्यमपि नाथेन येन स्यान्नाथवत्तरम्।।2.2.13।।
transliteration: anurūpassa vai nātho lakṣmīvān lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ| trailokyamapi nāthena yena syānnāthavattaram
translation: नाथेन as lord, येन by whom, त्रैलोक्यमपि even the three worlds, नाथवत्तरम् स्यात् will have  better protector, स: he, लक्ष्मीवान् a man possessing signs of greatness, लक्ष्मणाग्रज: elder  brother of Lakshmana, अनुरूप: befitting, नाथ: वै is the lord.
explanation: With him (Rama) as ruler, all the three worlds will also have a better protector.That elder brother of Lakshmana with signs of greatness is certainly the most befitting to rule this kingdom.

shloka_text: अनेन श्रेयसा सद्यस्संयोज्यैवमिमां महीम्। गतक्लेशो भविष्यामि सुते तस्मिन्निवेश्य वै।।2.2.14।।
transliteration: anena śreyasā sadyassaṃyojyaivamimāṃ mahīm| gatakleśo bhaviṣyāmi sute tasminniveśya vai
translation: तस्मिन् when such, सुते son (Rama), इमाम् this, महीम् earth, निवेश्य entrusting, अनेन श्रेयसा  to ensure the welfare of the world, एवम् thus, सद्य: without any delay, संयोज्य having united, गतक्लेश: relieved of my anxieties, भविष्यामि shall become.
explanation: I shall be relieved of my anxiety  by entrusting the land (ruled by me) to my son (Rama) without any more delay and thus ensure the continued welfare of this world.

shloka_text: यदिदं मेऽनुरूपार्थं मया साधु सुमन्त्रितम्। भवन्तो मेऽनुमन्यन्तां कथं वा करवाण्यहम्।।2.2.15।।
transliteration: yadidaṃ me'nurūpārthaṃ mayā sādhu sumantritam| bhavanto me'numanyantāṃ kathaṃ vā karavāṇyaham
translation: मया by me, सुमन्त्रितम् well thoughtover, इदम् this word, साधु proper, मे my, अनुरूपार्थं यदि if  worthy of me, भवन्त: you, मे to me, अनुमन्यन्ताम् your consent shall be given, अहम् I, कथं वा how else, करवाणि I shall do?
explanation: Although it (this decision) is personally favourable to me and I have decided after seeking good counsel, you should also give me your consent and tell me what I should do.

shloka_text: यद्यप्येषा मम प्रीतिर्हितमन्यद्विचिन्त्यताम्। अन्या मध्यस्थचिन्ता हि विमर्दाभ्यधिकोदया।।2.2.16।।
transliteration: yadyapyeṣā mama prītirhitamanyadvicintyatām| anyā madhyasthacintā hi vimardābhyadhikodayā
translation: एषा this, मम my, प्रीति: यद्यपि even though I like, अन्यत् any alternative, हितम् means of welfare, विचिन्त्यताम् let it be thought over, मध्यस्थचिन्ता opinion of those without partiality, अन्या alternative, विमर्दाभ्यधिकोदया deliberations may bring good.
explanation: Although this is what I would like to do, please suggest alternative ways of achieving the welfare (of this kingdom). Deliberations by the unbiased (on this issue) may bring good.

shloka_text: इति ब्रुवन्तं मुदिताः प्रत्यनन्दन्नृपा नृपम्। वृष्टिमन्तं महामेघं नर्दन्त इव बर्हिणः।।2.2.17।।
transliteration: iti bruvantaṃ muditāḥ pratyanandannṛpā nṛpam| vṛṣṭimantaṃ mahāmeghaṃ nardanta iva barhiṇaḥ
translation: इति thus, ब्रुवन्तम् speaking, नृपम् king Dasaratha, नृपा: kings, मुदिता: delighted, वृष्टिमन्तम् raining, महामेघम् thick cloud, नर्दन्त: making sounds, बर्हिण: इव like peacocks, प्रत्यनन्दन् acclaimed.
explanation: Having thus heard king Dasaratha speak, the kings acclaimed him with delight, like peacocks crying (in joy) to see thick clouds.

shloka_text: स्निग्धोऽनुनादी संजज्ञे तत्र हर्षसमीरितः। जनौघोद्घुष्टसन्नादो विमानं कम्पयन्निव।।2.2.18।।
transliteration: snigdho'nunādī saṃjajñe tatra harṣasamīritaḥ| janaughodghuṣṭasannādo vimānaṃ kampayanniva
translation: तत्र there, स्निग्ध: affectionate, अनुनादी echoing, हर्षसमीरित: filled with pleasure, जनौघोद्घुष्टसन्नाद: sounds of rapturous cries of multitude of people, विमानम् that palace, कम्पयन्निव seemed as if shaking, संजज्ञे emanated.
explanation: There emanated cries of love and joy from the multitude of people (conveying their approval) whose reverberation seemed to shake the palace.

shloka_text: तस्य धर्मार्थविदुषो भावमाज्ञाय सर्वशः। ब्राह्मणा जनमुख्याश्च पौरजानपदै स्सह।।2.2.19।। समेत्य मन्त्रयित्वा तु समतागतबुद्धयः। ऊचुश्च मनसा ज्ञात्वा वृद्धं दशरथं नृपम्।।2.2.20।।
transliteration: tasya dharmārthaviduṣo bhāvamājñāya sarvaśaḥ| brāhmaṇā janamukhyāśca paurajānapadai ssaha sametya mantrayitvā tu samatāgatabuddhayaḥ| ūcuśca manasā jñātvā vṛddhaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam
translation: ब्राह्मणा: brahmins, पौरजानपदै: सह along with the inhabitants of towns and villages, जनमुख्या: च prominent men also, धर्मार्थविदुष: conversant with dharma (righteousness) and artha (state craft), तस्य his (Dasaratha's), भावम् views, सर्वश: entirely, आज्ञाय having known, समेत्य having joined together, मन्त्रयित्वा having deliberated, मनसा with mind, ज्ञात्वा having ascertained, समतागतबुद्धय: unanimous in their thinking, वृद्धम् addressing the aged man (Dasaratha), ऊचु: spoke.
explanation: Brahmins, kings and other prominent men, inhabitants of towns and villages  having  fully known the views of Dasaratha who was conversant with artha and dharma  joined together and deliberated. They thought out well and having arrived at unanimity in their thinking thus addressed the aged king Dasaratha.

shloka_text: तस्य धर्मार्थविदुषो भावमाज्ञाय सर्वशः। ब्राह्मणा जनमुख्याश्च पौरजानपदै स्सह।।2.2.19।। समेत्य मन्त्रयित्वा तु समतागतबुद्धयः। ऊचुश्च मनसा ज्ञात्वा वृद्धं दशरथं नृपम्।।2.2.20।।
transliteration: tasya dharmārthaviduṣo bhāvamājñāya sarvaśaḥ| brāhmaṇā janamukhyāśca paurajānapadai ssaha sametya mantrayitvā tu samatāgatabuddhayaḥ| ūcuśca manasā jñātvā vṛddhaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam
translation: ब्राह्मणा: brahmins, पौरजानपदै: सह along with the inhabitants of towns and villages, जनमुख्या: च prominent men also, धर्मार्थविदुष: conversant with dharma (righteousness) and artha (state craft), तस्य his (Dasaratha's), भावम् views, सर्वश: entirely, आज्ञाय having known, समेत्य having joined together, मन्त्रयित्वा having deliberated, मनसा with mind, ज्ञात्वा having ascertained, समतागतबुद्धय: unanimous in their thinking, वृद्धम् addressing the aged man (Dasaratha), ऊचु: spoke.
explanation: Brahmins, kings and other prominent men, inhabitants of towns and villages  having  fully known the views of Dasaratha who was conversant with artha and dharma  joined together and deliberated. They thought out well and having arrived at unanimity in their thinking thus addressed the aged king Dasaratha.

shloka_text: अनेकवर्षसाहस्रो वृद्धस्त्वमसि पार्थिव। स रामं युवराजानमभिषिञ्चिस्व पार्थिवम्।।2.2.21।।
transliteration: anekavarṣasāhasro vṛddhastvamasi pārthiva| sa rāmaṃ yuvarājānamabhiṣiñcisva pārthivam
translation: पार्थिव O mighty king त्वम् you, अनेकवर्षसाहस्र: many thousands of years old, वृद्ध: असि have become old, स: such as you are, रामम् Rama, पार्थिवम् as ruler of the earth, युवराजानम् as prince regent, अभिषिञ्चिस्व coronate him.
explanation: O mighty king, you have grown many thousands of years old. Therefore, you should coronate Rama as prince regent of this kingdom.

shloka_text: इच्छामो हि महाबाहुं रघुवीरं महाबलम्। गजेन महताऽयान्तं रामं छत्रावृताननम्।।2.2.22।।
transliteration: icchāmo hi mahābāhuṃ raghuvīraṃ mahābalam| gajena mahatā'yāntaṃ rāmaṃ chatrāvṛtānanam
translation: महाबाहुम् mightyarmed, रघुवीरम् hero among the Raghus, महाबलम् mighty, रामम् Rama, छत्रावृताननम् his countenance shadowed by the royal parasol, महता great, गजेन on an elephant, यान्तम् riding, इच्छाम: हि are desiring.
explanation: We cherish to see the mightyarmed hero among the Raghus, Rama, riding on a majestic elephant, his countenance shadowed by the royal parasol.

shloka_text: इति तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा तेषां मनःप्रियं। अजानन्निव जिज्ञासुरिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.2.23।।
transliteration: iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rājā teṣāṃ manaḥpriyaṃ| ajānanniva jijñāsuridaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: इति in this way, तद्वचनम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, राजा the king, तेषाम् their, मन: प्रियम् pleasing to their mind, अजानन्निव as if he did not know earlier, जिज्ञासु: with a wish to ascertain, इदम् these, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having heard them king Dasaratha, pretending as though he was not aware of their heart's desire but was now wishing to ascertain it, spoke these words:

shloka_text: श्रुत्वैव वचनं यन्मे राघवं पतिमिच्छथ। राजान स्संशयोऽयं मे किमिदं ब्रूत तत्त्वतः।।2.2.24।।
transliteration: śrutvaiva vacanaṃ yanme rāghavaṃ patimicchatha| rājāna ssaṃśayo'yaṃ me kimidaṃ brūta tattvataḥ
translation: राजान: O kings, मे my, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वैव soon after listening, यत् since, राघवम् son of the Raghus (Rama), पतिम् as king, इच्छथ wish, मे to me, अयम् this,  संशय: doubt, तत् इदम् this, तत्त्वत: truly, ब्रूत you may tell.
explanation: O kings, soon after listening to my words, all of you wish Rama to be king. (But) I doubt (in my mind) whether you have said it from your heart৷৷

shloka_text: कथं नु मयि धर्मेण पृथिवीमनुशासति। भवन्तो द्रष्टुमिच्छन्ति युवराजं ममात्मजम्।।2.2.25।।
transliteration: kathaṃ nu mayi dharmeṇa pṛthivīmanuśāsati| bhavanto draṣṭumicchanti yuvarājaṃ mamātmajam
translation: मयि by me, धर्मेण righteously, पृथिवीम् this earth, अनुशासति while governing, भवन्त: you, मम my, आत्मजम् son, युवराजम् as princeregent, द्रष्टुम् to see, कथं नु why indeed, इच्छन्ति wish
explanation: When the earth is being ruled righteously by me why indeed you intend to see my son as prince regent?

shloka_text: ते तमूचुर्महात्मानं पौरजानपदैस्सह। बहवो नृप कल्याणा गुणाः पुत्रस्य सन्ति ते।।2.2.26।।
transliteration: te tamūcurmahātmānaṃ paurajānapadaissaha| bahavo nṛpa kalyāṇā guṇāḥ putrasya santi te
translation: पौरजानपदै: सह along with inhabitants of towns and villages, ते those (kings), महात्मानम् that magnanimous, तम् addressing him, ऊचु: said, नृप O king, ते your, पुत्रस्य son's, बहव: many, कल्याणा: auspicious, गुणा: सन्ति are virtues indeed.
explanation: Those kings along with the inhabitants of towns and villages answered the  magnanimous king: O king your son, indeed has many auspicious and admirable  virtues.

shloka_text: गुणान् गुणवतो देव देवकल्पस्य धीमतः। प्रियानानन्दनान्कृत्स्नान्प्रवक्ष्यामोऽद्य तान् शृणु।।2.2.27।।
transliteration: guṇān guṇavato deva devakalpasya dhīmataḥ| priyānānandanānkṛtsnānpravakṣyāmo'dya tān śṛṇu
translation: देव O king, गुणवत: of the man endowed with virtues, देवकल्पस्य resembling devatas, धीमत: sagcious Rama's, प्रियान् dear, आनन्दनान् causing delight, कृत्स्नान् all, तान् गुणान् his virtues, अद्य now, वक्ष्याम: we shall speak, शृणु listen.
explanation: O king, we shall now speak about those great virtues of the sagacious (Rama). Comparable to those of the gods, they are dear and a source of delight for every one. Please listen.

shloka_text: दिव्यैर्गुणैश्शक्रसमो रामस्सत्यपराक्रमः। इक्ष्वाकुभ्योऽपि सर्वेभ्यो ह्यतिरिक्तो विशांपते।।2.2.28।।
transliteration: divyairguṇaiśśakrasamo rāmassatyaparākramaḥ| ikṣvākubhyo'pi sarvebhyo hyatirikto viśāṃpate
translation: विशांपते O lord of the people (Dasaratha), राम: Rama, दिव्यै: by the divine, गुणै: by virtues, शक्रसम: equal to Indra, सत्यपराक्रम: one with proven valour, सर्वेऽभ्योपि among all also, इक्ष्वाकुभ्य: among the descendents of Iksvaku, अतिरिक्त: distinguished.
explanation: Lord of the people Rama with his divine virtues is equal to Indra. He with his  proven valour is exceptional among all the descendents of the Iksvakus.

shloka_text: राम स्सत्पुरुषो लोके सत्यधर्मपरायणः। साक्षाद्रामाद्विनिर्वृत्तो धर्मश्चापि श्रिया सह।।2.2.29।।
transliteration: rāma ssatpuruṣo loke satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ| sākṣādrāmādvinirvṛtto dharmaścāpi śriyā saha
translation: लोके in this world, राम: Rama, सत्पुरुष: a venerable man, सत्यधर्मपरायण: devoted to truth and righteousness, रामात् from Rama, धर्म: च अपि righteousness also, श्रिया सह along with prosperity, साक्षात् directly, विनिर्वृत्त: flows.
explanation: Devoted to truth and righteousness Rama is the most venerable among men in this world. Even righteousness along with prosperity flows directly from Rama.

shloka_text: प्रजासुखत्त्वे चन्द्रस्य वसुधायाः क्षमागुणैः। बुद्ध्या बृहस्पतेस्तुल्यो वीर्ये साक्षाच्छचीपतेः।।2.2.30।।
transliteration: prajāsukhattve candrasya vasudhāyāḥ kṣamāguṇaiḥ| buddhyā bṛhaspatestulyo vīrye sākṣācchacīpateḥ
translation: प्रजासुखत्त्वे in causing happiness to the people, चन्द्रस्य of the Moon, क्षमागुणै: in the virtue of forbearance, वसुधाया: of the earth, बुद्ध्या by wisdom, बृहस्पते: of Brihaspati, वीर्ये in prowess, शचीपते: of  Indra, साक्षात् directly, तुल्य: equal.
explanation: He is equal to the Moon in causing happiness to the people, to the earth in forbearance, to Brihaspati in wisdom and to Indra in prowess.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿धर्मज्ञः सत्यसन्धश्च शीलवाननसूयकः। क्षान्तः सान्त्वयिता श्लक्ष्णः कृतज्ञो विजितेन्द्रियः।।2.2.31।।
transliteration: ﻿﻿dharmajñaḥ satyasandhaśca śīlavānanasūyakaḥ| kṣāntaḥ sāntvayitā ślakṣṇaḥ kṛtajño vijitendriyaḥ
translation: ﻿﻿ धर्मज्ञ: knower of righteousness, सत्यसन्ध: true to his vows, शीलवान् one with good character, अनसूयक: free from envy, क्षान्त: one with forbearance, सान्त्वयिता one who consoles others, श्लक्ष्ण: gentle, कृतज्ञ: grateful, विजितेन्द्रिय: one who has conquered the senses.
explanation: ﻿﻿ Rama knows the ways of righteousness. He is true to his word and free from envy. He possesses a sound character with forbearance, gentleness and a sense of gratitude. With his senses under control, he is a source of consolation (in stressful times).

shloka_text: मृदुश्च स्थिरचित्तश्च सदा भव्योऽनसूयकः। प्रियवादी च भूतानां सत्यवादी च राघवः।।2.2.32।। बहुश्रुतानां वृद्धानां ब्राह्मणानामुपासिता। तेनास्येहाऽतुला कीर्तिर्यशस्तेजश्च वर्धते।।2.2.33।।
transliteration: mṛduśca sthiracittaśca sadā bhavyo'nasūyakaḥ| priyavādī ca bhūtānāṃ satyavādī ca rāghavaḥ bahuśrutānāṃ vṛddhānāṃ brāhmaṇānāmupāsitā| tenāsyehā'tulā kīrtiryaśastejaśca vardhate
translation: राघव: son of the Raghus (Rama), मृदु: च softspoken, स्थिरचित्त: च steadfast, सदा always, भव्य: serene, अनसूयक: free from envy, भूतानाम् for living beings, प्रियवादी pleasing  सत्यवादी च one who always speaks the truth, बहुश्रुतानाम् of those learned in a number of  shastras, वृद्धानाम् of elderly persons, ब्राह्मणानाम् of brahmins, उपासिता serves, तेन with these, अस्य his, अतुला incomparable, कीर्ति: glory, यश: fame, तेजश्च splendour, इह in this world, वर्धते growing.
explanation: This son of the Raghus (Rama) is softspoken, steadfast, always serene, truthful and  free from envy. He is pleasing to all beings. He serves those elderly brahmins versed in many lores. With these virtues his incomparable glory, fame and splendour have steadily grown.

shloka_text: मृदुश्च स्थिरचित्तश्च सदा भव्योऽनसूयकः। प्रियवादी च भूतानां सत्यवादी च राघवः।।2.2.32।। बहुश्रुतानां वृद्धानां ब्राह्मणानामुपासिता। तेनास्येहाऽतुला कीर्तिर्यशस्तेजश्च वर्धते।।2.2.33।।
transliteration: mṛduśca sthiracittaśca sadā bhavyo'nasūyakaḥ| priyavādī ca bhūtānāṃ satyavādī ca rāghavaḥ bahuśrutānāṃ vṛddhānāṃ brāhmaṇānāmupāsitā| tenāsyehā'tulā kīrtiryaśastejaśca vardhate
translation: राघव: son of the Raghus (Rama), मृदु: च softspoken, स्थिरचित्त: च steadfast, सदा always, भव्य: serene, अनसूयक: free from envy, भूतानाम् for living beings, प्रियवादी pleasing  सत्यवादी च one who always speaks the truth, बहुश्रुतानाम् of those learned in a number of  shastras, वृद्धानाम् of elderly persons, ब्राह्मणानाम् of brahmins, उपासिता serves, तेन with these, अस्य his, अतुला incomparable, कीर्ति: glory, यश: fame, तेजश्च splendour, इह in this world, वर्धते growing.
explanation: This son of the Raghus (Rama) is softspoken, steadfast, always serene, truthful and  free from envy. He is pleasing to all beings. He serves those elderly brahmins versed in many lores. With these virtues his incomparable glory, fame and splendour have steadily grown.

shloka_text: देवासुरमनुष्याणां सर्वास्त्रेषु विशारदः। सम्यग्विद्याव्रतस्नातो यथावत्साङ्गवेदवित्।।2.2.34।।
transliteration: devāsuramanuṣyāṇāṃ sarvāstreṣu viśāradaḥ| samyagvidyāvratasnāto yathāvatsāṅgavedavit
translation: देवासुरमनुष्याणाम् among devatas, asuras and men, सर्वास्त्रेषु in wielding all kinds of weapons, विशारद: expert, सम्यक् properly, विद्याव्रतस्नात: completed the vow of acquiring various branches of learning, यथावत् duly, साङ्गवेदवित् has learnt the Vedas and their supplementary sciences.
explanation: He is an expert in wielding all kinds of weapons available to devas, asuras and  men. He has achieved mastery over all sciences and has appropriately acquired knowledge of the Vedas and its ancillary sciences.

shloka_text: गान्धर्वे च भुवि श्रेष्ठो बभूव भरताग्रजः। कल्याणाभिजन स्साधुरदीनात्मा महामतिः।।2.2.35।।
transliteration: gāndharve ca bhuvi śreṣṭho babhūva bharatāgrajaḥ| kalyāṇābhijana ssādhuradīnātmā mahāmatiḥ
translation: भरताग्रज: the elder brother of Bharata (Rama), गान्धर्वे in music, भुवि on this earth, श्रेष्ठ:  बभूव became greatest, कल्याणाभिजन: having a noble descent, साधु: a pious man, अदीनात्मा with his mind free from meanness, महामति: possessing great intellect.
explanation: This elder brother of Bharata is the greatest exponent in music on earth. Pious, sagacious, free from meanness, he is of noble descent.

shloka_text: द्विजैरभिविनीतश्च श्रेष्ठैर्धर्मार्थनैपुणैः। यदा व्रजति सङ्ग्रामं ग्रामार्थे नगरस्य वा।।2.2.36।। गत्वा सौमित्रिसहितो नाऽविजित्य निवर्तते।
transliteration: dvijairabhivinītaśca śreṣṭhairdharmārthanaipuṇaiḥ| yadā vrajati saṅgrāmaṃ grāmārthe nagarasya vā gatvā saumitrisahito nā'vijitya nivartate|
translation: धर्मार्थनैपुणै: distinguished in the twin aspects of dharma and artha श्रेष्ठै: by the best, द्विजै: by brahmins, अभिविनीत: wellinstructed in all the matters, ग्रामार्थे for the sake of a village, नगरस्य वा or a town, यदा when, सङ्ग्रामम् the battle, व्रजति proceeds, सौमित्रिसहित: along with Lakshmana, गत्वा having gone, अविजित्य without conquering, न निवर्तते does not return.
explanation: Whenever he, wellinstructed in all matters by the best of brahmins wellversed in dharma and artha proceeds along with Lakshmana to wage a war for the sake of a village or a town, he never returns without conquering the enemy.

shloka_text: सङ्ग्रामात्पुनरागम्य कुञ्जरेण रथेन वा।2.2.37।। पौरान् स्वजनवन्नित्यं कुशलं परिपृच्छति।। पुत्रेष्वग्निषु दारेषु प्रेष्यशिष्यगणेषु च।2.2.38।। निखिलेनानुपूर्व्याच्च पितापुत्रानिवौरसान्।।
transliteration: saṅgrāmātpunarāgamya kuñjareṇa rathena vā|2.2.37|| paurān svajanavannityaṃ kuśalaṃ paripṛcchati|| putreṣvagniṣu dāreṣu preṣyaśiṣyagaṇeṣu ca|2.2.38|| nikhilenānupūrvyācca pitāputrānivaurasān||
translation: सङ्ग्रामात् from the battlefield, कुञ्जरेण mounting on elephant, रथेन वा or on a chariot, पुन: आगम्य having returned, पौरान् citizens, स्वजनवत् like his own kith and kin, पिता father, औरसान् पुत्रानिव like sons of his own blood, पुत्रेषु with respect to their children, अग्निषु sacred fires, दारेषु wives, प्रेष्यशिष्यगणेषु च multitudes of their servants and disciples, निखिलेन in detail, आनुपूर्व्याच्च by following the proper order (protocol), नित्यम् always, कुशलम् welfare, परिपृच्छति enquires.
explanation: While returning from the battlefield, either on a chariot or an elephant Rama stops and  enquires in detail and in order, the welfare of the citizens as he would do for his kith and kin. He enquires about the welfare of their children, sacred  rituals, wives, their servants and disciples as a father would enquire of his sons.

shloka_text: सङ्ग्रामात्पुनरागम्य कुञ्जरेण रथेन वा।2.2.37।। पौरान् स्वजनवन्नित्यं कुशलं परिपृच्छति।। पुत्रेष्वग्निषु दारेषु प्रेष्यशिष्यगणेषु च।2.2.38।। निखिलेनानुपूर्व्याच्च पितापुत्रानिवौरसान्।।
transliteration: saṅgrāmātpunarāgamya kuñjareṇa rathena vā|2.2.37|| paurān svajanavannityaṃ kuśalaṃ paripṛcchati|| putreṣvagniṣu dāreṣu preṣyaśiṣyagaṇeṣu ca|2.2.38|| nikhilenānupūrvyācca pitāputrānivaurasān||
translation: सङ्ग्रामात् from the battlefield, कुञ्जरेण mounting on elephant, रथेन वा or on a chariot, पुन: आगम्य having returned, पौरान् citizens, स्वजनवत् like his own kith and kin, पिता father, औरसान् पुत्रानिव like sons of his own blood, पुत्रेषु with respect to their children, अग्निषु sacred fires, दारेषु wives, प्रेष्यशिष्यगणेषु च multitudes of their servants and disciples, निखिलेन in detail, आनुपूर्व्याच्च by following the proper order (protocol), नित्यम् always, कुशलम् welfare, परिपृच्छति enquires.
explanation: While returning from the battlefield, either on a chariot or an elephant Rama stops and  enquires in detail and in order, the welfare of the citizens as he would do for his kith and kin. He enquires about the welfare of their children, sacred  rituals, wives, their servants and disciples as a father would enquire of his sons.

shloka_text: शुश्रूषन्ते च व श्शिष्याः कच्चित्कर्मसु दंशिताः।।2.2.39।। इति नः पुरुषव्याघ्र स्सदा रामोऽभिभाषते।
transliteration: śuśrūṣante ca va śśiṣyāḥ kaccitkarmasu daṃśitāḥ iti naḥ puruṣavyāghra ssadā rāmo'bhibhāṣate|
translation: व: your, शिष्या: disciples, कर्मसु in their tasks, दंशिता: perform, शुश्रूषन्ते are serving, इति like this, पुरुषव्याघ्र: a tiger among men, राम: Rama, सदा always, न: us, अभिभाषते enquires.
explanation: Rama, a tiger among men, always enquires whether our disciples discharge their duties.

shloka_text: व्यसनेषु मनुष्याणां भृशं भवति दुःखितः।।2.2.40।। उत्सवेषु च सर्वेषु पितेव परितुष्यति।
transliteration: vyasaneṣu manuṣyāṇāṃ bhṛśaṃ bhavati duḥkhitaḥ utsaveṣu ca sarveṣu piteva parituṣyati|
translation: मनुष्याणाम् of people, व्यसनेषु in misfortunes, भृशम् profoundly, दु:खित: भवति is grieved, सर्वेषु among all, उत्सवेषु on festive occasions, पितेव like father, परितुष्यति rejoices.
explanation: He grieves profoundly whenever people are afflicted by misfortunes (and) rejoices like a father on festive occasions.

shloka_text: सत्यवादी महेष्वासो वृद्धसेवी जितेन्द्रियः।।2.2.41।। स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषी च धर्मं सर्वात्मना श्रितः।
transliteration: satyavādī maheṣvāso vṛddhasevī jitendriyaḥ smitapūrvābhibhāṣī ca dharmaṃ sarvātmanā śritaḥ|
translation: सत्यवादी one who speaks the truth, महेष्वास: one who is a great archer, वृद्धसेवी one who serves the aged, जितेद्रिय: one who has conquered his senses,  स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषी च   speaks with a smiling face, सर्वात्मना wholeheartedly, धर्मं श्रित: takes refuge in dharma.
explanation: . He is one who speaks the truth. He is a great archer, one who has conquered his senses and serves the aged. He speaks with a  smile and protects dharma with all his heart.

shloka_text: सम्यग्योक्ता श्रेयसां च न विगृह्य कथारुचिः।।2.2.42।। उत्तरोत्तरयुक्तौ च वक्ता वाचस्पतिर्यथा।
transliteration: samyagyoktā śreyasāṃ ca na vigṛhya kathāruciḥ uttarottarayuktau ca vaktā vācaspatiryathā|
translation: सम्यक् rightly, श्रेयसां योक्ता does good, विगृह्य creating dissention, कथारुचि: न not interested in conversation, उत्तरोत्तरयुक्तौ in debates, वाचस्पतिर्यथा like Brihastpati, वक्ता orator.
explanation: He helps those who take refuge in him. He is not  interested in conversation leading to  dissentions. But during debates he is eloquent like Brihaspati (establing the truth on the basis of reasoning).

shloka_text: ﻿सुभ्रूः आयतताम्राक्षः साक्षाद्विष्णुरिव स्वयम्।।2.2.43।। रामो लोकाभिरामोऽयं शौर्यवीर्यपराक्रमैः।
transliteration: ﻿subhrūḥ āyatatāmrākṣaḥ sākṣādviṣṇuriva svayam rāmo lokābhirāmo'yaṃ śauryavīryaparākramaiḥ|
translation: ﻿ लोकाभिराम: one who is the delight of the worlds, अयम् he, राम: Rama, सुभ्रू: having charming eyebrows, आयतताम्राक्ष: having large coppercoloured eyes, शौर्यवीर्यपराक्रमै: with heroism, bravery and valour, साक्षात् manifesting, स्वयम् personally, विष्णु: इव like Visnu.
explanation: ﻿ Rama, who is the source of delight to the world, has charming eyebrows and large coppercoloured eyes. He is endowed with heroism, bravery and valour like Visnu manifested.

shloka_text: प्रजापालनतत्त्वज्ञो न रागोपहतेन्द्रियः।।2.2.44।। शक्तस्त्रैलोक्यमप्येको भोक्तुं किन्नु महीमिमाम्।
transliteration: prajāpālanatattvajño na rāgopahatendriyaḥ śaktastrailokyamapyeko bhoktuṃ kinnu mahīmimām|
translation: प्रजापालनतत्वज्ञ: proficient in the ways and means of ruling the people, रागोपहतेन्द्रिय: senses not overpowered by passion,  न not, एक: alone, त्रैलोक्यमपि three worlds, भोक्तुम् to enjoy, शक्त: capable, इमाम् this, महीम् earth, किन्नु why to say?
explanation: He is proficient in the ways and means of ruling the people. His senses are not overpowered by passion. He alone is capable of ruling the three worlds, what to speak the earth

shloka_text: नास्य क्रोधः प्रसादश्च निरर्थोऽस्ति कदाचन।।2.2.45।। हन्त्येव नियमाद्वध्यानवध्ये न च कुप्यति।
transliteration: nāsya krodhaḥ prasādaśca nirartho'sti kadācana hantyeva niyamādvadhyānavadhye na ca kupyati|
translation: अस्य his, कोप: anger, प्रसादश्च favour also, कदाचन ever, निरर्थ(क): in vain, नास्ति is not, नियमात् in accordance with justice, वध्यान् those who deserve to be killed, हन्ति एव is punishable, अवध्ये those who should not be killed, न कुप्यति does not get angry.
explanation: His anger or favour never goes in vain. He kills those who rightly deserve to be killed  and flares not at those whose life is to be spared.

shloka_text: युनक्त्यर्थैः प्रहृष्टश्च तमसौ यत्र तुष्यति।।2.2.46।। शान्तै स्सर्वप्रजाकान्तैः प्रीतिसञ्जननैर्नृणाम्। गुणैर्विरुरुचे रामो दीप्त स्सूर्य इवांशुभिः।।2.2.47।।
transliteration: yunaktyarthaiḥ prahṛṣṭaśca tamasau yatra tuṣyati śāntai ssarvaprajākāntaiḥ prītisañjananairnṛṇām| guṇairviruruce rāmo dīpta ssūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ
translation: असौ he (this Rama), यत्र wherever, तुष्यति is pleased, तम् him, प्रहृष्ट: pleased, अर्थै: with wealth, युनक्ति bestows, शान्तै: with tranquil, सर्वप्रजाकान्तै: charming to all men, नृणाम् for men, प्रीतिसञ्जननै: causing delight to the good, गुणै: with virtues, राम: Rama, अंशुभि: with rays, दीप्त: shining, सूर्य: इव like Sun, विरुरुचे shines.
explanation: When pleased, Rama bestows wealth. Like the Sun shining with his rays, He shines  with his qualities of tranquil, charming and loving nature.

shloka_text: युनक्त्यर्थैः प्रहृष्टश्च तमसौ यत्र तुष्यति।।2.2.46।। शान्तै स्सर्वप्रजाकान्तैः प्रीतिसञ्जननैर्नृणाम्। गुणैर्विरुरुचे रामो दीप्त स्सूर्य इवांशुभिः।।2.2.47।।
transliteration: yunaktyarthaiḥ prahṛṣṭaśca tamasau yatra tuṣyati śāntai ssarvaprajākāntaiḥ prītisañjananairnṛṇām| guṇairviruruce rāmo dīpta ssūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ
translation: असौ he (this Rama), यत्र wherever, तुष्यति is pleased, तम् him, प्रहृष्ट: pleased, अर्थै: with wealth, युनक्ति bestows, शान्तै: with tranquil, सर्वप्रजाकान्तै: charming to all men, नृणाम् for men, प्रीतिसञ्जननै: causing delight to the good, गुणै: with virtues, राम: Rama, अंशुभि: with rays, दीप्त: shining, सूर्य: इव like Sun, विरुरुचे shines.
explanation: When pleased, Rama bestows wealth. Like the Sun shining with his rays, He shines  with his qualities of tranquil, charming and loving nature.
