explanation: Having perceived that Rama was determined to carry out his father's command, Kausalya with her throat choked with tears said these words of piety:
comments: Kausalya insists on Rama to take her along with him to the forest --Rama tells her that service to one's husband is the supreme virtue--Kauslaya allows Rama to proceed.

shloka_text: अदृष्टदुःखो धर्मात्मा सर्वभूतप्रियंवदः। मयि जातो दशरथात्कथमुञ्छेन वर्तयेत्।।2.24.2।।
transliteration: adṛṣṭaduḥkho dharmātmā sarvabhūtapriyaṃvadaḥ| mayi jāto daśarathātkathamuñchena vartayet
translation: अदृष्टदुःखः one who had never experienced sorrow, धर्मात्मा righteous, सर्वभूतप्रियंवदः one who speaks pleasantly to all, दशरथात् of Dasaratha, मयि to me, जातः born, उञ्छेन by collecting the grains fallen on the ground, कथम् how, वर्तयेत् will maintain.
explanation: How will this righteous Rama, born to me through Dasaratha, who speaks pleasantly to all, and who has not experienced any sorrow before live on the grains gleaned?

shloka_text: यस्य भृत्याश्च दासाश्च मृष्टान्यन्नानि भुञ्जते। कथं स भोक्ष्यतेऽनाथो वने मूलफलान्ययम्।।2.24.3।।
transliteration: yasya bhṛtyāśca dāsāśca mṛṣṭānyannāni bhuñjate| kathaṃ sa bhokṣyate'nātho vane mūlaphalānyayam
translation: यस्य whose, भृत्याश्च servants,दासाश्च attendants, मृष्टानि delicious, अन्नानि cooked rice, भुञ्जते enjoy, अथः hereafter, सः अयम् such Rama, वने in the forest, मूलफलानि roots and fruits, कथम् how, भोक्ष्यते will eat?
explanation: How will Rama live on roots and fruits in the forest hereafter when his servants and attendants enjoy delicious food (here)?

shloka_text: कः एतच्छ्रद्दधेच्छ्रुत्वा कस्य वा न भवेद्भयम्। गुणवान्दयितो राज्ञा राघवो यद्विवास्यते।।2.24.4।।
transliteration: kaḥ etacchraddadhecchrutvā kasya vā na bhavedbhayam| guṇavāndayito rājñā rāghavo yadvivāsyate
translation: गुणवान् virtuous, दयितः affectionate, राघवः Rama, राज्ञा by the king, विवास्यते इति यत् will be exiled in this way, एतत् all this, श्रुत्वा having heard,  कः who, श्रद्धधेत् will believe,  कस्य वा to whom, भयम् fear, न भवेत् will not cause.
explanation: Who will believe that the virtuous and affectionate scion of the Raghus is exiled this way by the king? Who will not tremble in fear to hear this?

shloka_text: नूनं तु बलवान् लोके कृतान्तस्सर्वमादिशन्। लोके रामाभिरामस्त्वं वनं यत्र गमिष्यसि।।2.24.5।।
transliteration: nūnaṃ tu balavān loke kṛtāntassarvamādiśan| loke rāmābhirāmastvaṃ vanaṃ yatra gamiṣyasi
translation: राम O Rama, लोके अभिरामः delight of this world, त्वम् you, वनम् to the forest, यत्र गमिष्यसि  if ordered to go, लोके in the world, सर्वम् everything,  आदिशन् while ordering, कृतान्तः destiny, नूनम् certainly, बलवान् allpowerful.
explanation: O Rama if you, being the delight of the world, are (ordered) to go to the forest, it has to be said certainly that destiny which rules everything is allpowerful.

shloka_text: अयं तु मामात्मभव स्तवादर्शनमारुतः। विलापदुःखसमिधो रुदिताश्रुहुताहुतिः।।2.24.6।। चिन्ताबाष्पमहाधूमस्तवागमनचित्तजः। कर्शयित्वा भृशं पुत्र निश्वासायाससम्भवः।।2.24.7।। त्वया विहीनामिह मां शोकाग्निरतुलो महान्। प्रधक्ष्यति यथा कक्षं चित्रभानुर्हिमात्यये।।2.24.8।।
transliteration: ayaṃ tu māmātmabhava stavādarśanamārutaḥ| vilāpaduḥkhasamidho ruditāśruhutāhutiḥ cintābāṣpamahādhūmastavāgamanacittajaḥ| karśayitvā bhṛśaṃ putra niśvāsāyāsasambhavaḥ tvayā vihīnāmiha māṃ śokāgniratulo mahān| pradhakṣyati yathā kakṣaṃ citrabhānurhimātyaye
translation: पुत्र O son, आत्मभवः born from the body, तव अदर्शन मारुतः (my) sighs that will suggest your absence, विलापदुःखसमिधः with fuels of lamentation and affliction, रुदिताश्रुहुताहुतिः invoking with the offering of oblations of (my) wailing tears, चिन्ताबाष्पमहाधूमः with great  smoke of vapour arising from anxious thoughts, तव your, आगमन चित्तजः born from the thought of your return, निश्वासायाससम्भवः produced from sighs of exhaustion, अतुलः incomparable, महान् great, अयं शोकाग्नि: this fire of grief,  इह now, त्वया by you, विहीनाम्  deprived, माम् me, भृशम् very much, कर्शयित्वा having emaciated, हिमात्यये in summer, चित्रभानुः fire, कक्षं यथा like or a bunch of dry grass, प्रधक्ष्यति will burn.
explanation: After your departure, O son, an incomparably huge fire of grief with sighs of exhaustion will burst from my body, fanned by the wind of your absence and fuelled by lamentation and affliction. My wailing tears will be the oblations. My anxiety will be the great smoke rising vapour. This fire of grief will leave me very much emaciated and burn me like fire burns a forest of dead trees or a bunch of dry grass in summer.

shloka_text: अयं तु मामात्मभव स्तवादर्शनमारुतः। विलापदुःखसमिधो रुदिताश्रुहुताहुतिः।।2.24.6।। चिन्ताबाष्पमहाधूमस्तवागमनचित्तजः। कर्शयित्वा भृशं पुत्र निश्वासायाससम्भवः।।2.24.7।। त्वया विहीनामिह मां शोकाग्निरतुलो महान्। प्रधक्ष्यति यथा कक्षं चित्रभानुर्हिमात्यये।।2.24.8।।
transliteration: ayaṃ tu māmātmabhava stavādarśanamārutaḥ| vilāpaduḥkhasamidho ruditāśruhutāhutiḥ cintābāṣpamahādhūmastavāgamanacittajaḥ| karśayitvā bhṛśaṃ putra niśvāsāyāsasambhavaḥ tvayā vihīnāmiha māṃ śokāgniratulo mahān| pradhakṣyati yathā kakṣaṃ citrabhānurhimātyaye
translation: पुत्र O son, आत्मभवः born from the body, तव अदर्शन मारुतः (my) sighs that will suggest your absence, विलापदुःखसमिधः with fuels of lamentation and affliction, रुदिताश्रुहुताहुतिः invoking with the offering of oblations of (my) wailing tears, चिन्ताबाष्पमहाधूमः with great  smoke of vapour arising from anxious thoughts, तव your, आगमन चित्तजः born from the thought of your return, निश्वासायाससम्भवः produced from sighs of exhaustion, अतुलः incomparable, महान् great, अयं शोकाग्नि: this fire of grief,  इह now, त्वया by you, विहीनाम्  deprived, माम् me, भृशम् very much, कर्शयित्वा having emaciated, हिमात्यये in summer, चित्रभानुः fire, कक्षं यथा like or a bunch of dry grass, प्रधक्ष्यति will burn.
explanation: After your departure, O son, an incomparably huge fire of grief with sighs of exhaustion will burst from my body, fanned by the wind of your absence and fuelled by lamentation and affliction. My wailing tears will be the oblations. My anxiety will be the great smoke rising vapour. This fire of grief will leave me very much emaciated and burn me like fire burns a forest of dead trees or a bunch of dry grass in summer.

shloka_text: अयं तु मामात्मभव स्तवादर्शनमारुतः। विलापदुःखसमिधो रुदिताश्रुहुताहुतिः।।2.24.6।। चिन्ताबाष्पमहाधूमस्तवागमनचित्तजः। कर्शयित्वा भृशं पुत्र निश्वासायाससम्भवः।।2.24.7।। त्वया विहीनामिह मां शोकाग्निरतुलो महान्। प्रधक्ष्यति यथा कक्षं चित्रभानुर्हिमात्यये।।2.24.8।।
transliteration: ayaṃ tu māmātmabhava stavādarśanamārutaḥ| vilāpaduḥkhasamidho ruditāśruhutāhutiḥ cintābāṣpamahādhūmastavāgamanacittajaḥ| karśayitvā bhṛśaṃ putra niśvāsāyāsasambhavaḥ tvayā vihīnāmiha māṃ śokāgniratulo mahān| pradhakṣyati yathā kakṣaṃ citrabhānurhimātyaye
translation: पुत्र O son, आत्मभवः born from the body, तव अदर्शन मारुतः (my) sighs that will suggest your absence, विलापदुःखसमिधः with fuels of lamentation and affliction, रुदिताश्रुहुताहुतिः invoking with the offering of oblations of (my) wailing tears, चिन्ताबाष्पमहाधूमः with great  smoke of vapour arising from anxious thoughts, तव your, आगमन चित्तजः born from the thought of your return, निश्वासायाससम्भवः produced from sighs of exhaustion, अतुलः incomparable, महान् great, अयं शोकाग्नि: this fire of grief,  इह now, त्वया by you, विहीनाम्  deprived, माम् me, भृशम् very much, कर्शयित्वा having emaciated, हिमात्यये in summer, चित्रभानुः fire, कक्षं यथा like or a bunch of dry grass, प्रधक्ष्यति will burn.
explanation: After your departure, O son, an incomparably huge fire of grief with sighs of exhaustion will burst from my body, fanned by the wind of your absence and fuelled by lamentation and affliction. My wailing tears will be the oblations. My anxiety will be the great smoke rising vapour. This fire of grief will leave me very much emaciated and burn me like fire burns a forest of dead trees or a bunch of dry grass in summer.

shloka_text: कथं हि धेनु स्स्वं वत्सं गच्छन्तं नानुगच्छति। अहं त्वाऽनुगमिष्यामि यत्र पुत्र गमिष्यसि।।2.24.9.।।
transliteration: kathaṃ hi dhenu ssvaṃ vatsaṃ gacchantaṃ nānugacchati| ahaṃ tvā'nugamiṣyāmi yatra putra gamiṣyasi||2.24.9.||
translation: धेनुः cow, गच्छन्तम् wandering, स्वं वत्सम् its calf, कथं हि how, नानुगच्छति will not follow, पुत्र son, यत्र whereever, गमिष्यसि you will go, अहम् I, त्वा you, अनुगमिष्यामि will follow.
explanation: I shall follow you wherever you go, my son, like a cow following its calf. How is it possible for a cow not to follow its wandering calf?

shloka_text: तथा निगदितं मात्रा तद्वाक्यं पुरुषर्षभः। श्रुत्वा रामोऽब्रवीद्वाक्यं मातरं भृशदुःखिताम्।।2.24.10।।
transliteration: tathā nigaditaṃ mātrā tadvākyaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ| śrutvā rāmo'bravīdvākyaṃ mātaraṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitām
translation: पुरुषर्षभः best among men, रामः Rama, मात्रा by mother, तथा that way, निगदितम् spoken, तद्वाक्यम् those words, श्रुत्वा on hearing, भृशदुःखिताम् deeply afflicted, मातरम् addressing his mother, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: At these words of his mother who was deeply afflicted Rama, best among men replied:

shloka_text: कैकेय्या वञ्चितो राजा मयि चारण्यमाश्रिते। भवत्या च परित्यक्तो न नूनं वर्तयिष्यति।।2.24.11।।
transliteration: kaikeyyā vañcito rājā mayi cāraṇyamāśrite| bhavatyā ca parityakto na nūnaṃ vartayiṣyati
translation: कैकेय्या by Kaikeyi, वञ्चितः was deceived, राजा king, मयि when I, अरण्यम् forest, आश्रिते will be resorting to, भवत्या च by you also, परित्यक्तः deserted, न वर्तयिष्यति he will not live, नूनम् this is certain.
explanation: The king was deceived by Kaikeyi. If you also desert him after I have gone to the forest, surely he will not live.

shloka_text: भर्तुः किल परित्यागो नृशंसः केवलं स्त्रियाः। स भवत्या न कर्तव्यो मनसाऽपि विगर्हितः।।2.24.12।।
transliteration: bhartuḥ kila parityāgo nṛśaṃsaḥ kevalaṃ striyāḥ| sa bhavatyā na kartavyo manasā'pi vigarhitaḥ
translation: स्त्रियाः for a woman, भर्तुः husband's, परित्यागः desertion, केवलम् only, नृशंसः किल is a cruel  act indeed, विगर्हितः is abominable, सः that, भवत्या by you, मनसापि even in mind, न कर्तव्यः  must not be done.
explanation: For a woman, to desert her husband is a cruel act. You must not do that which is  contemptible even to think.

shloka_text: यावज्जीवति काकुत्स्थः पिता मे जगतीपतिः। शुश्रूषा क्रियतां तावत्सहि धर्मस्सनातनः।।2.24.13।।
transliteration: yāvajjīvati kākutsthaḥ pitā me jagatīpatiḥ| śuśrūṣā kriyatāṃ tāvatsahi dharmassanātanaḥ
translation: मे पिता my father, जगतीपतिः lord of the earth, काकुत्स्थः  the descendant of Kakutstha, यावत् as long as, जीवति lives, तावत् till then, शुश्रूषा service, क्रियताम् be done, सः that one, धर्मः हि सनातनः it is eternal virtue.
explanation: As long as the king, my father, the lord of the earth, a descendant of Kakutshta lives, you shall serve him. This is eternal virtue (in a woman).

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु रामेण कौशल्या शुभदर्शना। तथेत्युवाच सुप्रीता राममक्लिष्टकारिणम्।।2.24.14।।
transliteration: evamuktā tu rāmeṇa kauśalyā śubhadarśanā| tathetyuvāca suprītā rāmamakliṣṭakāriṇam
translation: रामेण by Rama, एवम् thus, उक्ता having been said, शुभदर्शना auspiciouslooking lady, कौशल्या Kausalya, सुप्रीता exceedingly pleased, अक्लिष्टकारिणम् unshakable in actions, रामम् to Rama, तथेति 'Be it so', उवाच said.
explanation: At these words of Rama, unshakable in action, auspiciouslooking Kausalya, exceedingly pleased said 'Be it so'.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु वचनं रामो धर्मभृतां वरः। भूयस्तामब्रवीद्वाक्यं मातरं भृशदुःखिताम्।।2.24.15।।
transliteration: evamuktastu vacanaṃ rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ| bhūyastāmabravīdvākyaṃ mātaraṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitām
translation: धर्मभृतां among upholders of rightcouness, वरः foremost, रामः Rama, एवम् in this way, वचनम् words, उक्तः having been spoken to, भृश दुःखिताम् in deep grief, ताम् her, मातरम् to mother, भूय: again, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Thus addressed, Rama, the foremost among upholders of righteousness, said to his mother who was in deep grief:

shloka_text: मया चैव भवत्या च कर्तव्यं वचनं पितुः। राजा भर्ता गुरु श्श्रेष्ठस्सर्वेषामीश्वरः प्रभुः।।2.24.16।।
transliteration: mayā caiva bhavatyā ca kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ pituḥ| rājā bhartā guru śśreṣṭhassarveṣāmīśvaraḥ prabhuḥ
translation: मया चैव by me as well, भवत्या च by you also, पितुः father's, वचनम् words, कर्तव्यम् fit to be carried out, राजा king, भर्ता supporter husband, गुरुः guru, श्रेष्ठः best, सर्वेषाम् for all, ईश्वरः is the lord, प्रभुः master.
explanation: You and I should obey father's words. He is the king, supporter, preceptor, the best (among men) and  lord and master of all of us.

shloka_text: इमानि तु महारण्ये विहृत्य नव पञ्च च। वर्षाणि परमप्रीतः स्थास्यामि वचने तव।।2.24.17।।
transliteration: imāni tu mahāraṇye vihṛtya nava pañca ca| varṣāṇi paramaprītaḥ sthāsyāmi vacane tava
translation: इमानि these, नव पञ्च च nine plus five (fourteen), वर्षाणि years, महारण्ये in the wild forest, विहृत्य having roamed, परमप्रीतः with supreme pleasure, तव your, वचने words (obeying your word), स्थास्यामि shall abide by.
explanation: Roaming the wild forest for fourteen years I shall abide by your words with supreme pleasure.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता प्रियं पुत्रं बाष्पपूर्णानना तदा। उवाच परमार्ता तु कौशल्या पुत्रवत्सला।।2.24.18।।
transliteration: evamuktā priyaṃ putraṃ bāṣpapūrṇānanā tadā| uvāca paramārtā tu kauśalyā putravatsalā
translation: तदा then, एवम् thus, उक्ता addressed, पुत्रवत्सला affectionate towards (her) son, कौशल्या Kausalya, परमार्ता a greatly distressed, बाष्पपूर्णानना with her face (eyes) filled with tears, प्रियम् beloved, पुत्रम् son, उवाच said.
explanation: Thus addressed by Rama, the affectionate Kausalya, deeply distressed, her eyes filled with tears, said to her beloved son:

shloka_text: आसां राम सपत्नीनां वस्तुं मध्ये न मे क्षमम्। नय मामपि काकुत्स्थ वनं वन्यां मृगीं यथा।।2.24.19।। यदि ते गमने बुद्धिः कृता पितुरपेक्षया।
transliteration: āsāṃ rāma sapatnīnāṃ vastuṃ madhye na me kṣamam| naya māmapi kākutstha vanaṃ vanyāṃ mṛgīṃ yathā yadi te gamane buddhiḥ kṛtā piturapekṣayā|
translation: राम O Rama, मे for me, आसाम् of these, सपत्नीनाम् of cowives, मध्ये in the midst of, वस्तुम्  to live, न क्षमम् not able, काकुत्स्थ scion of the Kakutstha race (Rama), पितुः with regard to your father, अपेक्षया with wish, गमने in going away, ते to you, बुद्धि: decision, कृता यदि if it is made, मामपि also me, वन्याम् relating to the forest (wild), मृगीं यथा like a female deer, वनम् to the forest, नय take me.
explanation: O Rama, I am not able to live in the midst of these cowives. O descendant of Kakutstha, if you have resolved to go to the forest as per the wishes of your father take mea wild deeralong with you into the forest.

shloka_text: तां तथा रुदतीं रामो रुदन्वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.24.20।। जीवन्त्या हि स्त्रिया भर्ता दैवतं प्रभुरेव च
transliteration: tāṃ tathā rudatīṃ rāmo rudanvacanamabravīt jīvantyā hi striyā bhartā daivataṃ prabhureva ca
translation: रामः Rama, तथा that way, रुदतीम् wailing, ताम् to her, रुदन् while (himself) sobbing, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् said, जीवन्त्या for a living lady, स्त्रियाः for a woman, भर्ता husband alone, दैवतम् is god, प्रभुरेव च is also lord (master).
explanation: Adding his tears to his mother's who was wailing Rama said As long as a woman lives, her husband is her god and also her lord (master).

shloka_text: भवत्या मम चैवाद्य राजा प्रभवति प्रभुः। न ह्यनाथा वयं राज्ञा लोकनाथेन धीमता।।2.24.21।।
transliteration: bhavatyā mama caivādya rājā prabhavati prabhuḥ| na hyanāthā vayaṃ rājñā lokanāthena dhīmatā
translation: प्रभुः powerful one, राजा king, अद्य now, भवत्याः for you, मम च for me also, प्रभवति has the authority to command, लोकनाथेन by lord of the entire world, धीमता by sagacious one, राज्ञा by king, वयम् we, अनाथाः without master, न हि are not.
explanation: The powerful king has authority over you as well as over me. As long as he is the sagacious lord of the entire world, how can we be without a master?

shloka_text: भरतश्चापि धर्मात्मा सर्वभूतप्रियंवदः। भवतीमनुवर्तेत स हि धर्मरतस्सदा।।2.24.22।।
transliteration: bharataścāpi dharmātmā sarvabhūtapriyaṃvadaḥ| bhavatīmanuvarteta sa hi dharmaratassadā
translation: धर्मात्मा virtuous, सर्वभूतप्रियंवदः who speaks pleasantly to all beings, भरतश्चापि Bharata also, भवतीम् you, अनुवर्तेत will follow, सः he, सदा always, धर्मरतः हि is attached to righteousness.
explanation: Bharata, who is virtuous and speaks pleasantly to all beings and who is always attached to righteousness will surely remain obedient to you.

shloka_text: यथा मयि तु निष्क्रान्ते पुत्रशोकेन पार्थिवः। श्रमं नावाप्नुयात्किञ्चिदप्रमत्ता तथा कुरु।।2.24.23।।
transliteration: yathā mayi tu niṣkrānte putraśokena pārthivaḥ| śramaṃ nāvāpnuyātkiñcidapramattā tathā kuru
translation: मयि me, निष्क्रान्ते having departed to the forest, पार्थिवः king, पुत्रशोकेन with grief for his son, यथा how, किञ्चित् even a little, श्रमम् effort, न अवाप्नुयात् will not obtain, तथा in that way, अप्रमत्ता with attention, कुरु do.
explanation: After my departure, you must see that the king is not  overpowered by grief for his son and struggles as little as possible.

shloka_text: दारुणश्चाप्ययं शोको यथैनं न विनाशयेत्। राज्ञो वृद्धस्य सततं हितं चर समाहिता।।2.24.24।।
transliteration: dāruṇaścāpyayaṃ śoko yathainaṃ na vināśayet| rājño vṛddhasya satataṃ hitaṃ cara samāhitā
translation: दारुणः terrible, अयं शोकः this  grief, एनम् him, यथा in a manner, न विनाशयेत् will not ruin (his health), समाहिता with composed mind, वृद्धस्य of the old, राज्ञः of the king, सततम् always, हितम् good, चर act.
explanation: See that the old king does not succumb to this terrible grief. Serve him with a composed mind.

shloka_text: व्रतोपवासनिरता या नारी परमोत्तमा। भर्तारं नानुवर्तेत सा तु पापगतिर्भवेत्।।2.24.25।।
transliteration: vratopavāsaniratā yā nārī paramottamā| bhartāraṃ nānuvarteta sā tu pāpagatirbhavet
translation: या नारी whichever woman, व्रतोपवासनिरता engaged in vows and fastings, परमोत्तमा highly pious, भर्तारम् husband, नानुवर्तेत does not follow, सा she, पापगतिः hell a, भवेत् will get.
explanation: A woman may be highly pious engaged in vows and fastings, but if she does not follow her husband, she will be condemned to hell.

shloka_text: भर्तु श्शुश्रूषया नारी लभते स्वर्गमुत्तमम्। अपि या निर्नमस्कारा निवृत्ता देवपूजनात्।।2.24.26।।
transliteration: bhartu śśuśrūṣayā nārī labhate svargamuttamam| api yā nirnamaskārā nivṛttā devapūjanāt
translation: या who, निर्नमस्कारा pays no respect, देवपूजनात् from worshipping gods, निवृत्ता has abstained, नारी अपि woman also, भर्तुः husband's, शुश्रूषया with service, उत्तमम् highest, स्वर्गम् heaven, लभते will attain.
explanation: A woman who serves her husband will attain the highest heaven even if she pays no homage to gods and abstains from worshipping them.

shloka_text: शुश्रूषामेव कुर्वीत भर्तुः प्रियहिते रता। एष धर्मः पुरा दृष्टो लोके वेदे श्रुतः स्मृतः।।2.24.27।।
transliteration: śuśrūṣāmeva kurvīta bhartuḥ priyahite ratā| eṣa dharmaḥ purā dṛṣṭo loke vede śrutaḥ smṛtaḥ
translation: भर्तुः husband's, प्रियहिते wellbeing, रता engaged, शुश्रूषामेव service alone, कुर्वीत shall do, एषः this, पुरा in ancient times, लोके in this world, दृष्टः is seen, वेदे in the Vedas, श्रुतः is heard, स्मृतः declared in Smritis, धर्मः is truth.
explanation: A wife who serves her husband and who is engaged in doing good to him is righteous. This dharma exists in this world since ancient times, declared in the Vedas and the smritis.

shloka_text: अग्निकार्येषु च सदा सुमनोभिश्च देवताः। पूज्यास्ते मत्कृते देवि बाह्मणाश्चैव सुव्रताः।।2.24.28।।
transliteration: agnikāryeṣu ca sadā sumanobhiśca devatāḥ| pūjyāste matkṛte devi bāhmaṇāścaiva suvratāḥ
translation: देवि O devi, मत्कृते for my sake, सदा always, देवताः the gods, अग्निकार्येषु in offering oblations to the firegod, सुमनोभिश्च with flowers, ते to you, पूज्याः worthy of worship, सुव्रताः true to their religious vows, ब्राह्मणाश्चैव brahmins also.
explanation: For my sake, O devi worship the firegod with offerings of oblations and flowers, and brahmins who are true to religious vows.

shloka_text: एवं कालं प्रतीक्षस्व ममागमनकाङ्क्षिणी। नियता नियताहारा भर्तृशुश्रूषणे रता।।2.24.29।।
transliteration: evaṃ kālaṃ pratīkṣasva mamāgamanakāṅkṣiṇī| niyatā niyatāhārā bhartṛśuśrūṣaṇe ratā
translation: एवम् in this maner, मम my, आगमनकाङ्क्षिणी looking forward to my return, नियता selfpossessed lady, नियताहारा observing discipine in food, भर्तृ शुश्रूषणे in the service of your husband, रता devoted, कालम् time, प्रतीक्षस्व wait for.
explanation: Looking forward to my return, spend your time this way with moderate intake, a mind under control and a life devoted to the service of your husband.

shloka_text: प्राप्स्यसे परमं कामं मयि प्रत्यागते सति। यदि धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठो धारयिष्यति जीवितम्।।2.24.30।।
transliteration: prāpsyase paramaṃ kāmaṃ mayi pratyāgate sati| yadi dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭho dhārayiṣyati jīvitam
translation: मयि when I, प्रत्यागते सति having returned, धर्मभृताम् of protcetor of dharma, श्रेष्ठः best, जीवितम् life, धारयिष्यति यदि if  he contains, परमम् highest, कामम् desire, प्राप्स्यसे will obtain.
explanation: If my father, who is the best among the upholders of righteousness, survives till I come back, you will have your highest desires fulfilled.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु रामेण बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणा। कौशल्या पुत्रशोकार्ता रामं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.24.31।।
transliteration: evamuktā tu rāmeṇa bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇā| kauśalyā putraśokārtā rāmaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: रामेण by Rama, एवम् in this manner, उक्ता having been said, कौशल्या Kausalya, पुत्रशोकार्ता distressed with grief for her son, बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणा with her eyes filled with tears, रामम् to Rama, वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: To these words of Rama, Kausalya, distressed with grief for her son, replied with her eyes filled with tears:

shloka_text: गमने सुकृतां बुद्धिं न ते शक्नोमि पुत्रक। विनिवर्तयितुं वीर नूनं कालो दुरत्ययः।।2.24.32।।
transliteration: gamane sukṛtāṃ buddhiṃ na te śaknomi putraka| vinivartayituṃ vīra nūnaṃ kālo duratyayaḥ
translation: वीर O valiant one, पुत्रक my child, गमने to go to the forest, सुकृताम् firmly resolved, ते बुध्दिम् your mind, विनिवर्तयितुम् to revert, न शक्नोमि I am not able, नूनम् certainly, कालः time, दुरत्ययः difficult to overcome (pass).
explanation: I am unable to dissuade you, O my brave son, from your firm resolve to go to the forest. It is surely difficult (for me) to bide time.

shloka_text: गच्छ पुत्र त्वमेकाग्रो भद्रं तेऽस्तु सदा विभुः। पुनस्त्वयि निवृत्ते तु भविष्यामि गतव्यथा।।2.24.33।।
transliteration: gaccha putra tvamekāgro bhadraṃ te'stu sadā vibhuḥ| punastvayi nivṛtte tu bhaviṣyāmi gatavyathā
translation: पुत्र O Son त्वम् you, एकाग्रः with resolute mind, गच्छ go, विभुः god, ते to you, सदा always, भद्रम् safety, अस्तु be it, त्वयि when you, पुनः again, निवृत्ते तु on your coming back,  गतव्यथा relieved of suffering, भविष्यामि I shall become.
explanation: Go with a steadfast mind, O my son May god be gracious. Only with your return, I shall be relieved of my suffering.

shloka_text: प्रत्यागते महाभागे कृतार्थे चरितव्रते। पितुरानृण्यतां प्राप्ते त्वयि लप्स्ये परं सुखम्।।2.24.34।।
transliteration: pratyāgate mahābhāge kṛtārthe caritavrate| piturānṛṇyatāṃ prāpte tvayi lapsye paraṃ sukham
translation: महाभागे when the reverend one, त्वयि you, कृतार्थे with your purpose accomplished, चरितव्रते when your vow is fulfilled, पितुः father's, आनृण्यताम् acquittal of debt, प्राप्ते obtained, प्रत्यागते on coming back, परम् supreme, सुखम् happiness, लप्स्ये I will attain.
explanation: O reverend one, when you come back after having accomplished your purpose, performed your vows and acquitted yourself of the debt you owe your father, I shall attain supreme happiness.

shloka_text: कृतान्तस्य गतिः पुत्र दुर्विभाव्या सदा भुवि। यस्त्वां सञ्चोदयति मे वच आच्छिद्य राघव।।2.24.35।।
transliteration: kṛtāntasya gatiḥ putra durvibhāvyā sadā bhuvi| yastvāṃ sañcodayati me vaca ācchidya rāghava
translation: पुत्र O son, राघव O Rama, यः whichever (destiny), मे my, वचः words, आच्छिद्य  cutting asunder (disregarding), त्वा you, सञ्चोदयति is prompting, कृतान्तस्य destiny's, गतिः course, सदा always, भुवि in this world, दुर्विभाव्या is inconceivable.
explanation: O Rama inconceivable is the course of destiny which is inciting you to go to the forest disregarding my words.

shloka_text: गच्छेदानीं महाबाहो क्षेमेण पुनरागतः। नन्दयिष्यसि मां पुत्र साम्ना वाक्येन चारुणा।।2.24.36।।
transliteration: gacchedānīṃ mahābāho kṣemeṇa punarāgataḥ| nandayiṣyasi māṃ putra sāmnā vākyena cāruṇā
translation: महाबाहो O mighty armed one, इदानीम् now, गच्छ go, पुत्र O son, क्षेमेण safely, पुनः आगतः again on your return, साम्ना in a gentle voice, चारुणा by sweet, वाक्येन  utterances, माम् me, नन्दयिष्यसि please.
explanation: Go now, O my mightyarmed son and come back safe. And on your return, delight me with your sweet, gentle utterances.

shloka_text: अपीदानीं स कालस्स्याद्वनात्प्रत्यागतं पुनः। यत्त्वां पुत्रक पश्येयं जटावल्कलधारिणम्।।2.24.37।।
transliteration: apīdānīṃ sa kālassyādvanātpratyāgataṃ punaḥ| yattvāṃ putraka paśyeyaṃ jaṭāvalkaladhāriṇam
translation: पुत्रक O my dear child, वनात् from the forest, पुनः again, प्रत्यागतम् have returned, जटावल्कल  धारिणम् wearing matted hair and bark, त्वाम् you, यत् since, पश्येयम् will see, सः कालः that time, इदानीम् now itself, अपि स्यात् can it be now itself?
explanation: O my dear child, how pleasing would it be, if today were to be the day of your return from the forest when I can see you wearing matted hair and robes of bark

shloka_text: तथा हि रामं वनवासनिश्चितं समीक्ष्य देवी परमेण चेतसा। उवाच रामं शुभलक्षणं वचो बभूव च स्वस्त्ययनाभिकाङ्क्षिणी।।2.24.38।।
transliteration: tathā hi rāmaṃ vanavāsaniścitaṃ samīkṣya devī parameṇa cetasā| uvāca rāmaṃ śubhalakṣaṇaṃ vaco babhūva ca svastyayanābhikāṅkṣiṇī
translation: देवी Devi (Kausalya), रामम् Rama, तथा like that, वनवासनिश्चितम् determined to go to the forest, समीक्ष्य (ददर्श) seeing, परमेण चेतसा with supreme consciousness, शुभलक्षणम् with auspicious qualities (virtues), रामम् to Rama, वचः words, उवाच said, स्वस्त्ययनाभिकाङ्क्षिणी wishing to perform ceremonies for (his) wellbeing, बभूव became.
explanation: Seeing Rama full of auspicious qualities resolved to go to the forest and having spoken to him with the fullness of her heart, Devi Kausalya now braced herself up to perform ceremonies in the interest of  Rama's wellbeing. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुर्विंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the twentyfourth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of  the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: साऽवनीय तमायासमुपस्पृश्य जलं शुचिः। चकार माता रामस्य मङ्गलानि मनस्विनी।।2.25.1।।
transliteration: sā'vanīya tamāyāsamupaspṛśya jalaṃ śuciḥ| cakāra mātā rāmasya maṅgalāni manasvinī
translation: मनस्विनी highminded lady, माता mother, सा she, तम् आयासम् such anguish, अवनीय restraining, जलम् water, उपस्पृश्य having performed the sipping (achamana), शुचिः rite sure, रामस्य of Rama, मङ्गलानि auspicious ceremonies, चकार performed.
explanation: Highminded mother Kausalya, her anguish subdued, performed the sipping rite (achamana) and her self rendered pure, performed auspicious ceremonies for Rama.
comments: Kausalya performs benedictory rites for Rama and offers prayers to all gods to protect him Rama departs for the palace of Sita.

shloka_text: न शक्यसे वारयितुं गच्छेदानीं रघूत्तम। शीघ्रं च विनिवर्तस्व वर्तस्व च सतां क्रमे।।2.25.2।।
transliteration: na śakyase vārayituṃ gacchedānīṃ raghūttama| śīghraṃ ca vinivartasva vartasva ca satāṃ krame
translation: रघूत्तम O the best among descendants of Raghu, वारयितुम् to dissuade, न शक्यसे not able,  इदानीम् now, गच्छ go, शीघ्रम् soon, विनिवर्तस्व return, सताम् of good men, क्रमे in footsteps, वर्तस्व follow.
explanation: I am unable to dissuade you, O the best among the descendants of Raghus, from going into the forest. Go now and return soon. Follow in the footsteps of the virtuous.

shloka_text: यं पालयसि धर्मं त्वं धृत्या च नियमेन च। स वै राघवशार्दूल धर्मस्त्वामभिरक्षतु।।2.25.3।।
transliteration: yaṃ pālayasi dharmaṃ tvaṃ dhṛtyā ca niyamena ca| sa vai rāghavaśārdūla dharmastvāmabhirakṣatu
translation: राघवशार्दूल O tiger among the descendants of Raghu त्वम् you, धृत्या with courage, नियमेन च with selfdiscipline, यं धर्मम् which duty, पालयसि you are carrying out, सः धर्मः वै that duty alone, त्वाम् you, अभिरक्षतु let it protect.
explanation: The duty which you are carrying out with courage and selfdiscipline, O tiger among the descendants of Raghu will alone protect you.

shloka_text: येभ्यः प्रणमसे पुत्र चैत्येष्वायतनेषु च। ते च त्वामभिरक्षन्तु वने सह महर्षिभिः।।2.25.4।।
transliteration: yebhyaḥ praṇamase putra caityeṣvāyataneṣu ca| te ca tvāmabhirakṣantu vane saha maharṣibhiḥ
translation: पुत्र son, चैत्येषु in sacred places, आयतनेषु च in temples, येभ्यः to whom, प्रणमसे you are saluting, ते they, महर्षिभिः सह together with maharshis, त्वाम् you, वने in the forest,  अभिरक्षन्तु protect you.
explanation: O my son may the gods in the temples and in other sacred places and the maharshis you bow to protect you in the forest

shloka_text: यानि दत्तानि तेऽस्त्राणि विश्वामित्रेण धीमता। तानि त्वामभिरक्षन्तु गुणैस्समुदितं सदा।।2.25.5।।
transliteration: yāni dattāni te'strāṇi viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā| tāni tvāmabhirakṣantu guṇaissamuditaṃ sadā
translation: धीमता by the sagacious, विश्वामित्रेण by Viswamitra, ते to you, यानि अस्त्राणि those weapons, दत्तानि were bestowed, तानि they, गुणैः with (mantric) qualities, समुदितम् endowed, त्वाम् you, सदा always, अभिरक्षन्तु may protect.
explanation: May the weapons endowed with mantric qualities, which were bestowed on you by sagacious Viswamitra always protect you

shloka_text: पितृशुश्रूषया पुत्र मातृशुश्रूषया तथा। सत्येन च महाबाहो चिरं जीवाभिरक्षितः।।2.25.6।।
transliteration: pitṛśuśrūṣayā putra mātṛśuśrūṣayā tathā| satyena ca mahābāho ciraṃ jīvābhirakṣitaḥ
translation: महाबाहो O mighty armed, पुत्र son, पितृशुश्रूषया in the service of your father, तथा also,  मातृशुश्रूषया in the service of your mother, सत्येन with truth, अभिरक्षितः you have been  protected, चिरं जीव live long.
explanation: O my mighty armed son protected by the service to your father, mother and to truth, live long

shloka_text: समित्कुश पवित्राणि वेद्यश्चायतनानि च। स्थण्डिलानि विचित्राणि शैला वृक्षाः क्षुपा ह्रदाः।।2.25.7।। पतङ्गाः पन्नगास्सिंहास्त्वां रक्षन्तु नरोत्तम।
transliteration: samitkuśa pavitrāṇi vedyaścāyatanāni ca| sthaṇḍilāni vicitrāṇi śailā vṛkṣāḥ kṣupā hradāḥ pataṅgāḥ pannagāssiṃhāstvāṃ rakṣantu narottama|
translation: नरोत्तम best among men, समित्कुश पवित्राणि sacrificial fuel, kusha grass and sacred finger rings made of kusa grass, वेद्यश्च sacrificial altars, आयतनानि च temples also, विचित्राणि various one, स्थण्डिलानि levelled sacrificial grounds, शैलाः mountains, वृक्षाः trees, क्षुपा: plants, ह्रदाः lakes, पतङ्गा: birds, पन्नगाः serpents, सिंहाः lions, त्वाम् you, रक्षन्तु may protect.
explanation: O best of men may sacrificial fuel, kusa grass and sacred rings made of kusha grass, sacrificial altars, temples, various levelled sacrificial grounds, mountains, trees, plants, lakes, birds, serpents and lions protect you

shloka_text: स्वस्तिसाध्याश्च विश्वे च मरुतश्च महर्षयः। स्वस्ति धाता विधाता च स्वस्ति पूषा भगोऽर्यमा।।2.25.8।। लोकपालाश्च ते सर्वे वासवप्रमुखास्तथा।
transliteration: svastisādhyāśca viśve ca marutaśca maharṣayaḥ| svasti dhātā vidhātā ca svasti pūṣā bhago'ryamā lokapālāśca te sarve vāsavapramukhāstathā|
translation: साध्याश्च devatas known as 'Sadhyas', विश्वे च viswe devatas, मरुतश्च maruts (windgod), महर्षयः the great ascetics, स्वस्ति expiatory mantras, धाता sustainer (Virat Purusha), विधाता च the preserver of creation (lord Brahma), स्वस्ति bestow blessings to you, पूषा Sun, भगः the Sun known as Bhaga, अर्यमा the Sun known as Aryama, तथा also, वासवप्रमुखाः others headed by Indra, सर्वे all, ते लोकपालाश्च guardians of the world.
explanation: May all gods known as Sadhyas, Visvedevatas, Maruts, great ascetics, the sustainer (Virat Purusha), the preserver of creation (lord Brahma), Sun, Bhaga, Aryama, and all other important guardians of the world headed by Indra bestow their blessings on you

shloka_text: ऋतवश्चैव पक्षाश्च मासा स्संवत्सराः क्षपाः।।2.25.9।। दिनानि च मुहूर्ताश्च स्वस्ति कुर्वन्तु ते सदा।
transliteration: ṛtavaścaiva pakṣāśca māsā ssaṃvatsarāḥ kṣapāḥ dināni ca muhūrtāśca svasti kurvantu te sadā|
translation: ऋतवश्चैव six seasons also, पक्षाश्च two fort nights, मासाः months, संवत्सराः years, क्षपा: nights, दिनानि च days also, मुहूर्ताश्च moments (each 48 minutes), ते to you, सदा always,  स्वस्ति कुर्वन्तु may bring propitiousness to you.
explanation: May the six seasons, years, months, fortnights, nights, days and moments bring good to you

shloka_text: स्मृतिर्धृतिश्च धर्मश्च पातु त्वां पुत्र सर्वतः।।2.25.10।। स्कन्दश्च भगवान्देव स्सोमश्च स बृहस्पतिः। सप्तर्षयो नारदश्च ते त्वां रक्षन्तु सर्वतः।।2.25.11।।
transliteration: smṛtirdhṛtiśca dharmaśca pātu tvāṃ putra sarvataḥ skandaśca bhagavāndeva ssomaśca sa bṛhaspatiḥ| saptarṣayo nāradaśca te tvāṃ rakṣantu sarvataḥ
translation: पुत्र O my son, स्मृतिः memory, धृतिश्च resolution(Dhriti), धर्मश्च Dharma, त्वाम् you, सर्वतः always, पातु may guard, भगवान् of divine personages, देवः god, स्कन्दश्च Skanda, सोमश्च Soma, सः that, बृहस्पतिः Brihaspati (preceptor of gods), ते to you, सप्तर्षयः seven rishis,  नारदश्च Narada, त्वाम् you, सर्वतः everywhere, रक्षन्तु protect you.
explanation: O my son may Smriti, Dhriti and Dharma always guard you. May divine personages and gods, Skanda, Soma, Brihaspati, the seven rishis and Narada protect you at all times

shloka_text: स्मृतिर्धृतिश्च धर्मश्च पातु त्वां पुत्र सर्वतः।।2.25.10।। स्कन्दश्च भगवान्देव स्सोमश्च स बृहस्पतिः। सप्तर्षयो नारदश्च ते त्वां रक्षन्तु सर्वतः।।2.25.11।।
transliteration: smṛtirdhṛtiśca dharmaśca pātu tvāṃ putra sarvataḥ skandaśca bhagavāndeva ssomaśca sa bṛhaspatiḥ| saptarṣayo nāradaśca te tvāṃ rakṣantu sarvataḥ
translation: पुत्र O my son, स्मृतिः memory, धृतिश्च resolution(Dhriti), धर्मश्च Dharma, त्वाम् you, सर्वतः always, पातु may guard, भगवान् of divine personages, देवः god, स्कन्दश्च Skanda, सोमश्च Soma, सः that, बृहस्पतिः Brihaspati (preceptor of gods), ते to you, सप्तर्षयः seven rishis,  नारदश्च Narada, त्वाम् you, सर्वतः everywhere, रक्षन्तु protect you.
explanation: O my son may Smriti, Dhriti and Dharma always guard you. May divine personages and gods, Skanda, Soma, Brihaspati, the seven rishis and Narada protect you at all times

shloka_text: याश्चापि सर्वतस्सिध्दा दिशश्च सदिगीश्वराः। स्तुता मया वने तस्मिन्पान्तु त्वां पुत्र नित्यशः।।2.25.12।।
transliteration: yāścāpi sarvatassidhdā diśaśca sadigīśvarāḥ| stutā mayā vane tasminpāntu tvāṃ putra nityaśaḥ
translation: पुत्र O my son, सिद्धाः Siddhas, सदिगीश्वरा: along with the guardians of the quarters, याः दिशश्च those quarters, मया by me, स्तुताः are invoked, तस्मिन् वने in that forest, त्वाम् you, सर्वतः from all sides, नित्यशः at all times, पान्तु protect.
explanation: May Siddhas, guardians of the quarters invoked by me protect you from all  directions in that forest at all times, O my son

shloka_text: शैलास्सर्वे समुद्राश्च राजा वरुण एव च। द्यौरन्तरिक्षं पृथिवी नद्यस्सर्वास्तथैव च।।2.25.13।। नक्षत्राणि च सर्वाणि ग्रहाश्च सहदेवताः। अहोरात्रे तथा सन्ध्ये पान्तु त्वां वनमाश्रितम्।।2.25.14।।
transliteration: śailāssarve samudrāśca rājā varuṇa eva ca| dyaurantarikṣaṃ pṛthivī nadyassarvāstathaiva ca nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvāṇi grahāśca sahadevatāḥ| ahorātre tathā sandhye pāntu tvāṃ vanamāśritam
translation: सर्वे all, शैलाः mountains, समुद्राश्च also seas, राजा lord, वरुण एव च Varuna, द्यौः the heaven, अन्तरिक्षम् the space, पृथिवी च the earth as well, तथैव च also, सर्वाः all,  नद्यः rivers, सर्वाणि all, नक्षत्राणि च the stars, सहदेवताः together with their presiding deities,  ग्रहाश्च planets, अहोरात्रे day and night, तथा and, सन्ध्ये dawn and dusk, आश्रितम् having taken refuge, त्वाम् you, पान्तु may protect.
explanation: When you dwell in the forest may all the mountains, seas, lord Varuna, heaven, space, and earth and also all rivers, all stars and planets with their presiding deities, day, night, dawn and dusk protect you

shloka_text: शैलास्सर्वे समुद्राश्च राजा वरुण एव च। द्यौरन्तरिक्षं पृथिवी नद्यस्सर्वास्तथैव च।।2.25.13।। नक्षत्राणि च सर्वाणि ग्रहाश्च सहदेवताः। अहोरात्रे तथा सन्ध्ये पान्तु त्वां वनमाश्रितम्।।2.25.14।।
transliteration: śailāssarve samudrāśca rājā varuṇa eva ca| dyaurantarikṣaṃ pṛthivī nadyassarvāstathaiva ca nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvāṇi grahāśca sahadevatāḥ| ahorātre tathā sandhye pāntu tvāṃ vanamāśritam
translation: सर्वे all, शैलाः mountains, समुद्राश्च also seas, राजा lord, वरुण एव च Varuna, द्यौः the heaven, अन्तरिक्षम् the space, पृथिवी च the earth as well, तथैव च also, सर्वाः all,  नद्यः rivers, सर्वाणि all, नक्षत्राणि च the stars, सहदेवताः together with their presiding deities,  ग्रहाश्च planets, अहोरात्रे day and night, तथा and, सन्ध्ये dawn and dusk, आश्रितम् having taken refuge, त्वाम् you, पान्तु may protect.
explanation: When you dwell in the forest may all the mountains, seas, lord Varuna, heaven, space, and earth and also all rivers, all stars and planets with their presiding deities, day, night, dawn and dusk protect you

shloka_text: ऋतवश्चैव षट्पुण्या मासास्संवत्सरास्तथा। कलाश्च काष्ठाश्च तथा तव शर्म दिशन्तु ते।।2.25.15।।
transliteration: ṛtavaścaiva ṣaṭpuṇyā māsāssaṃvatsarāstathā| kalāśca kāṣṭhāśca tathā tava śarma diśantu te
translation: पुण्याः pious, षट् six, ऋतवश्चैव seasons, ते to you, मासाः months, तथा also, संवत्सराः years,  कलाश्च kala, काष्ठाश्च kashta (kala and kashta are the names for the minute divisions of time), तव your, शर्म welfare, दिशन्तु you may offer.
explanation: May all the six pious seasons, months, years, kala and kashta contribute to your wellbeing

shloka_text: महावने विचरतो मुनिवेषस्य धीमतः। तवादित्याश्च दैत्याश्च भवन्तु सुखदास्सदा।।2.25.16।।
transliteration: mahāvane vicarato muniveṣasya dhīmataḥ| tavādityāśca daityāśca bhavantu sukhadāssadā
translation: मुनिवेषस्य clad in ascetic garb, महावने in the wild forest, विचरतः wandering, धीमतः sagacious, तव your, आदित्याश्च sons of Aditi, devatas, दैत्याश्च sons of Diti, daityas, सदा always, सुखदाः bestowers of happiness, भवन्तु be.
explanation: May gods and demons always give you happiness when you wander in that great forest clad in ascetic garb

shloka_text: राक्षसानां पिशाचानां रौद्राणां क्रूरकर्मणाम्। क्रव्यादानां च सर्वेषां मा भूत्पुत्रक ते भयम्।।2.25.17।।
transliteration: rākṣasānāṃ piśācānāṃ raudrāṇāṃ krūrakarmaṇām| kravyādānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ mā bhūtputraka te bhayam
translation: पुत्रक O my child, ते to you, रौद्राणाम् of the fearful, क्रूरकर्मणाम् of those committing cruel acts, राक्षसानाम् of rakshasas, पिशाचानाम् of pisachas, 'सर्वेषाम् of all, क्रव्यादानां च of flesheating animals, भयम् fear, माभूत may not be.
explanation: Let there be no fear from rakshasas who are fearful to look at and commit cruel acts, from pisachas (evil spirits) and from flesheating animals, O my child

shloka_text: प्लवगा वृश्चिका दंशामशकाश्चैव कानने। सरीसृपाश्च कीटाश्च मा भूवन्गहने तव।।2.25.18।।
transliteration: plavagā vṛścikā daṃśāmaśakāścaiva kānane| sarīsṛpāśca kīṭāśca mā bhūvangahane tava
translation: गहने in an inaccessible, कानने in the forest, तव to you, प्लवगाः monkeys,  वृश्चिकाः scorpions, दंशाः wild gnats, मशकाश्च mosquitoes also, सरीसृपाश्च reptiles also, कीटाश्च insects too, मा भूवन् may not be there.
explanation: May monkeys, scorpions, wild gnats, mosquitoes, reptiles and insects in that inaccessible forest not trouble you

shloka_text: महाद्विपाश्च सिंहाश्च व्याघ्रा ऋक्षाश्च दंष्ट्रिणः। महिषा श्शृङ्गिणो रौद्रा न ते द्रुह्यन्तु पुत्रक।।2.25.19।।
transliteration: mahādvipāśca siṃhāśca vyāghrā ṛkṣāśca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ| mahiṣā śśṛṅgiṇo raudrā na te druhyantu putraka
translation: पुत्रक my dear son, महाद्विपाश्च mighty elephants also, दंष्ट्रिणः with pointed incisors, सिंहाश्च lions, व्याघ्राः tigers, ऋक्षाश्च bears and, शृङ्गिणः with horns, रौद्राः fierce ones, महिषाः wild buffaloes, ते to you, न द्रुह्यन्तु may not harm.
explanation: May the mighty elephants, lions with pointed incisors, tigers, bears and fierce, wild, horned buffaloes, do you no harm, O my dear son

shloka_text: नृमांसभोजना रौद्रा ये चान्ये सत्वजातयः। मा च त्वां हिंसिषुः पुत्र मया संपूजितास्त्विह।।2.25.20।।
transliteration: nṛmāṃsabhojanā raudrā ye cānye satvajātayaḥ| mā ca tvāṃ hiṃsiṣuḥ putra mayā saṃpūjitāstviha
translation: पुत्र O my child, नृमांसभोजिनः cannibals, रौद्राः frightening ones, ये अन्ये all others, सत्वजातयः ferocious breeds of animals, इह here, मया by me, संपूजिताः have been worshipped, त्वाम् you, मा च हिंसिषुः may not harm.
explanation: May the ferocious breed of cernivores I worship not harm you, O my child

shloka_text: आगमास्ते शिवास्सन्तु सिध्यन्तु च पराक्रमाः। सर्वसम्पत्तये राम स्वस्तिमान्गच्छ पुत्रक।।2.25.21।।
transliteration: āgamāste śivāssantu sidhyantu ca parākramāḥ| sarvasampattaye rāma svastimāngaccha putraka
translation: पुत्रक O my child, राम Rama, ते your, आगमाः paths, शिवाः safe (auspecious), सन्तु be, पराक्रमाश्च valour also, सिध्यन्तु be accomplished, स्वस्तिमान् safe man, सर्वसंपत्तये achieve success in everything, गच्छ go.
explanation: O Rama may your path be auspecious May your valour be fruitful Go safel and achieve success in everything

shloka_text: स्वस्ति ते ऽस्त्वन्तरिक्षेभ्यः पार्थिवेभ्यः पुनः पुनः। सर्वेभ्यश्चैव देवेभ्यो ये च वै परिपन्थिनः।।2.25.22।।
transliteration: svasti te 'stvantarikṣebhyaḥ pārthivebhyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ| sarvebhyaścaiva devebhyo ye ca vai paripanthinaḥ
translation: अन्तरिक्षेभ्यः from the sky, पुनः again, पार्थिवेभ्यः from earthly gods (kings), पुनः again, सर्वेभ्यः from all, देवेभ्यश्चैव from devatas also, ये ते परिपन्थिन from all those who obstruct your path, ते to you, स्वस्ति अस्तु safety be yours.
explanation: May gods from the sky, the earth and all other gods protect you and let there be no harm to you from your foes.

shloka_text: गुरुस्सोमश्च सूर्यश्च धनदोऽथ यमस्तथा। पान्तु त्वामर्चिता राम दण्डकारण्यवासिनम्।।2.25.23।।
transliteration: gurussomaśca sūryaśca dhanado'tha yamastathā| pāntu tvāmarcitā rāma daṇḍakāraṇyavāsinam
translation: राम Rama, गुरुः Guru or Brihaspati, सोमश्च Moon also, सूर्यश्च Sun too, अथ also, धनदः Kubera, तथा also, यमः Yama, अर्चिताः having been worshipped, दण्डकारण्यवासिनम् living in Dandaka forest, त्वाम् you, पान्तु may protect you.
explanation: Propitiated by my worship, O Rama may Brihaspati, Moon, Sun, Kubera and Yama protect you when you are in Dandaka forest

shloka_text: अग्निर्वायुस्तथा धूमो मन्त्राश्चर्षिमुखाच्च्युताः। उपस्पर्शनकाले तु पान्तु त्वां रघुनन्दन।।2.25.24।।
transliteration: agnirvāyustathā dhūmo mantrāścarṣimukhāccyutāḥ| upasparśanakāle tu pāntu tvāṃ raghunandana
translation: रघुनन्दन O Joy of the Raghus O Son of the Raghu race, उपस्पर्शनकाले at the time of taking bath, त्वाम् you, अग्नि: fire,  वायुः wind, तथा also, धूमः smoke, ऋषिमुखात् from the mouths of rishis, च्युताः released,  मन्त्राश्च mantras, पान्तु protect you.
explanation: May Fire, Wind, Smoke and Mantras emanated from the mouths of rishis protect you when you take your ablutions, O Son of the Raghu race O Joy of the Raghus

shloka_text: सर्वलोकप्रभुर्ब्रह्मा भूतभर्ता तथर्षयः। ये च शेषास्सुरास्ते त्वां रक्षन्तु वनवासिनम्।।2.25.25।।
transliteration: sarvalokaprabhurbrahmā bhūtabhartā tatharṣayaḥ| ye ca śeṣāssurāste tvāṃ rakṣantu vanavāsinam
translation: सर्वलोकप्रभुः lord of all the worlds, Siva, ब्रह्मा Brahma, भूतभर्ता supporter of beings, Visnu, तथा also, ऋषयः rishis, शेषाः the remaining, ये सुराः those gods, ते to you,  वनवासिनम् dwelling in the forest, त्वाम् you, रक्षन्तु protect.
explanation: May Siva, lord of all the worlds, Visnu, supporter of living beings, Brahma, rishis and all the rest of the gods protect you while you dwell in the forest

shloka_text: इति माल्यैस्सुरगणान्गन्धैश्चापि यशस्विनी। स्तुतिभिश्चानुरूपाभिरानर्चाऽयतलोचना।।2.25.26।।
transliteration: iti mālyaissuragaṇāngandhaiścāpi yaśasvinī| stutibhiścānurūpābhirānarcā'yatalocanā
translation: यशस्विनी illustrious lady, आयतलोचना largeeyed (Kausalya), इति thus, माल्यैः with garlands, गन्धैश्चापि with fragrant susbtances, अनुरूपाभिः by appropriate articles, स्तुतिभिश्च with prayers, सुरगणान् hosts of gods, आनर्च worshipped.
explanation: Thus illustrious, largeeyed Kausalya worshipped hosts of gods by offering them garlands and fragrant substances with appropriate prayers.

shloka_text: ज्वलनं समुपादाय ब्राह्मणेन महात्मना। हावयामास विधिना राममङ्गलकारणात्।।2.25.27।।
transliteration: jvalanaṃ samupādāya brāhmaṇena mahātmanā| hāvayāmāsa vidhinā rāmamaṅgalakāraṇāt
translation: ज्वलनम् the sacred fire, समुपादाय having arranged, राममङ्गल कारणात् for the welfare of Rama, महात्मना great, ब्राह्मणेन by the brahmin (priest), विधिना duly, हावयामास offered oblations.
explanation: After collecting the sacred fire through great brahmins she duly offered oblations to the gods for the welfare of Rama.

shloka_text: घृतं श्वेतानि माल्यानि समिधश्श्वेतसर्षपान्। उपसम्पादयामास कौशल्या परमाङ्गना।।2.25.28।।
transliteration: ghṛtaṃ śvetāni mālyāni samidhaśśvetasarṣapān| upasampādayāmāsa kauśalyā paramāṅganā
translation: परमाङ्गना noble lady, कौशल्या Kausalya, घृतम् clarified butter, श्वेतानि white,  माल्यानि garlands of flowers, समिधः sacred fuel, श्वेत सर्षपान् white grains of mustard seed,  उपसंपादयामास obtained.
explanation: Noble Kausalya procured clarified butter, garlands of white flowers, sacred fuel, and grains of white mustard seed (for oblations to the gods).

shloka_text: उपाध्याय स्सविधिना हुत्वा शान्तिमनामयम्। हुतहव्यावशेषेण बाह्यं बलिमकल्पयत्।।2.25.29।।
transliteration: upādhyāya ssavidhinā hutvā śāntimanāmayam| hutahavyāvaśeṣeṇa bāhyaṃ balimakalpayat
translation: सः उपाध्यायः that officiating priest, विधिना duly, अनामयम् sound health, शान्तिं हुत्वा having performed sacrificial offerings for peace, हुतहव्यावशेषेण with the remainder of the offerings, बाह्यम् external, बलिम् ceremonies, अकल्पयत् performed.
explanation: The officiating priest performed the ritual of sacrificial offerings strictly in accordance   with rules for peace and happiness of Rama. With the remainder of the offerings, he performed whatever ceremonies were to be done externally.

shloka_text: मधु दध्यक्षतघृतैः स्वस्तिवाच्यद्विजांस्ततः। वाचयामास रामस्य वनेस्वस्त्ययनक्रियाः।।2.25.30।।
transliteration: madhu dadhyakṣataghṛtaiḥ svastivācyadvijāṃstataḥ| vācayāmāsa rāmasya vanesvastyayanakriyāḥ
translation: मधु दध्यक्षतघृतैः with honey, curds, rice and clarified butter, द्विजान् brahmins, स्वस्तिवाच्य  who pronounced benedictory prayers, ततः thereafter, वने in the forest, रामस्य of Rama, स्वस्त्ययनक्रियाः reciting mantras preparatory for averting evil, वाचयामास got recited.
explanation: Thereafter she made the brahmins pronounce benedictory prayers, offering honey, curd, rice and clarified butter.Then she got mantras (expiatory rites) recited for averting evil to Rama while in the forest.

shloka_text: ततस्तस्मै द्विजेन्द्राय राममाता यशस्विनी। दक्षिणां प्रददौ काम्यां राघवं चेदमब्रवीत्।।2.25.31।।
transliteration: tatastasmai dvijendrāya rāmamātā yaśasvinī| dakṣiṇāṃ pradadau kāmyāṃ rāghavaṃ cedamabravīt
translation: यशस्विनी illustrious, राममाता Rama's mother, ततः thereafter, तस्मै that, द्विजेन्द्राय best among brahmins, काम्याम् as desired, दक्षिणाम् appropriate gifts, प्रददौ gave, राघवम् to Rama, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् च also spoke.
explanation: The illustrious Kausalya, mother of Rama gave abundant gifts to the best of the brahmins and thereafter said to him:

shloka_text: यन्मङ्गलं सहस्राक्षे सर्वदेवनमस्कृते। वृत्रनाशे समभवत्तत्ते भवतु मङ्गलम्।।2.25.32।।
transliteration: yanmaṅgalaṃ sahasrākṣe sarvadevanamaskṛte| vṛtranāśe samabhavattatte bhavatu maṅgalam
translation: वृत्रनाशे at the time of slaying of Vritra, सर्वदेवनमस्कृते salutations bestowed by all gods,  सहस्राक्षे on god of a thousand eyes (Indra), यत् whichever, मङ्गलम् blessings, समभवत् was bestowed, तत् मङ्गलम् that auspiciousness, ते भवतु may happen to you.
explanation: May the same blessings bestowed by all the gods on the thousandeyed Indra at the time of killing Vritra be with you

shloka_text: यन्मङ्गलं सुपर्णस्य विनताऽकल्पयत्पुरा। अमृतं प्रार्थयानस्य तत्ते भवतु मङ्गलम्।।2.25.33।।
transliteration: yanmaṅgalaṃ suparṇasya vinatā'kalpayatpurā| amṛtaṃ prārthayānasya tatte bhavatu maṅgalam
translation: पुरा formely, अमृतम् nectar, प्रार्थयानस्य while seeking, सुपर्णस्य for Garuda,  विनता Vinata, यत् मङ्गलम् which blessings, अकल्पयत् created, तत् मङ्गलम् that auspiciousness, ते भवतु happen to you.
explanation: May you be conferred with the same blessings which Vinata bestowed on Garuda at the time of bringing nectar

shloka_text: अमृतोत्पादने दैत्यान् घ्नतो वज्रधरस्य यत्। अदितिर्मङ्गलं प्रादात्तत्ते भवतु मङ्गलम्।।2.25.34।।
transliteration: amṛtotpādane daityān ghnato vajradharasya yat| aditirmaṅgalaṃ prādāttatte bhavatu maṅgalam
translation: अदितिः Aditi, अमृतोत्पादने at the time of churning out nectar, दैत्यान् the daityas, घ्नतः slew, वज्रधरस्य of the wielder of thunder (Indras's), तत् मङ्गलम् blessings, प्रादात् gave, तत् मङ्गलम् blessings, ते भवतु may be yours.
explanation: May you be bestowed with the same blessings conferred by Aditi on Indra, the wielder of thunder for the killing of daityas at the time nectar was generated

shloka_text: त्रीन्विक्रमान्प्रक्रमतो विष्णोरमिततेजसः। यदासीन्मङ्गलं राम तत्ते भवतु मङ्गलम्।।2.25.35।।
transliteration: trīnvikramānprakramato viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ| yadāsīnmaṅgalaṃ rāma tatte bhavatu maṅgalam
translation: राम O Rama, त्रीन् three, विक्रमान् strides, प्रक्रमतः of him who was occupying, अमिततेजसः highly lustrous, विष्णोः Visnu's, यत् मङ्गलम् whichever auspiciousness, आसीत् was to be, तत् मङ्गलानि that auspiciousness, ते भवतु may be yours.
explanation: O Rama by occupying three footsteps of space, highly lustrous Visnu owned the three worlds and obtained glory. May you obtain similar auspiciousness

shloka_text: ऋतवस्सागरा द्वीपा वेदा लोका दिशश्च ते। मङ्गलानि महाबाहो दिशन्तु शुभमङ्गलाः।।2.25.36।।
transliteration: ṛtavassāgarā dvīpā vedā lokā diśaśca te| maṅgalāni mahābāho diśantu śubhamaṅgalāḥ
translation: महाबाहो O mightyarmed one, शुभमङ्गलाः auspicious happenings, ऋतवः seasons, सागराः seas, द्वीपाः islands, वेदाः the Vedas, लोकाः worlds, दिशश्च the quarters, ते to you,  मङ्गलानि blessings, दिशन्तु let them bestow.
explanation: O mightyarmed Rama may the auspicious and prosperous seasons, seas, islands. the Vedas, the worlds and the quarters bless you

shloka_text: इति पुत्रस्य शेषांश्च कृत्वा शिरसि भामिनी। गन्धैश्चापि समालभ्य राममायतलोचना।।2.25.37।। ओषधीं चापि सिद्धार्थां विशल्यकरणीं शुभाम्। चकार रक्षां कौशल्या मन्त्रैरभिजजाप च।।2.25.38।।
transliteration: iti putrasya śeṣāṃśca kṛtvā śirasi bhāminī| gandhaiścāpi samālabhya rāmamāyatalocanā oṣadhīṃ cāpi siddhārthāṃ viśalyakaraṇīṃ śubhām| cakāra rakṣāṃ kauśalyā mantrairabhijajāpa ca
translation: आयतलोचना largeeyed lady, भामिनी beautiful lady, कौशल्या Kausalya, इति in this way uttering, पुत्रस्य son's, शिरसि on the head, शेषाश्च the remains (of offerings), कृत्वा having offered, रामम् Rama, गन्धैश्चापि with sandalpaste also, समालभ्य having applied, सिद्धार्थां  for fruitful attainment, शुभाम् auspicious, विशल्यकरणीम् Vishalyakarani, (capable of removing extraneous substances causing great pain in the body), ओषधीम् medicinal herb, रक्षाम् armlet, चकार made, मन्त्रै: with sacred prayers, अभिजजाप च muttered repeatedly in a low tone.
explanation: The largeeyed Kausalya placed the remains of the offerings on his (Rama's) head and  applied sandal cream to his body. She tied an auspicious medicinal herb known as Vishalyakarani to his arm for attainment of his objectives, repeatedly muttering prayers.

shloka_text: इति पुत्रस्य शेषांश्च कृत्वा शिरसि भामिनी। गन्धैश्चापि समालभ्य राममायतलोचना।।2.25.37।। ओषधीं चापि सिद्धार्थां विशल्यकरणीं शुभाम्। चकार रक्षां कौशल्या मन्त्रैरभिजजाप च।।2.25.38।।
transliteration: iti putrasya śeṣāṃśca kṛtvā śirasi bhāminī| gandhaiścāpi samālabhya rāmamāyatalocanā oṣadhīṃ cāpi siddhārthāṃ viśalyakaraṇīṃ śubhām| cakāra rakṣāṃ kauśalyā mantrairabhijajāpa ca
translation: आयतलोचना largeeyed lady, भामिनी beautiful lady, कौशल्या Kausalya, इति in this way uttering, पुत्रस्य son's, शिरसि on the head, शेषाश्च the remains (of offerings), कृत्वा having offered, रामम् Rama, गन्धैश्चापि with sandalpaste also, समालभ्य having applied, सिद्धार्थां  for fruitful attainment, शुभाम् auspicious, विशल्यकरणीम् Vishalyakarani, (capable of removing extraneous substances causing great pain in the body), ओषधीम् medicinal herb, रक्षाम् armlet, चकार made, मन्त्रै: with sacred prayers, अभिजजाप च muttered repeatedly in a low tone.
explanation: The largeeyed Kausalya placed the remains of the offerings on his (Rama's) head and  applied sandal cream to his body. She tied an auspicious medicinal herb known as Vishalyakarani to his arm for attainment of his objectives, repeatedly muttering prayers.

shloka_text: उवाचातिप्रहृष्टेव सा दुःखवशवर्तिनी। वाङ्ग्मात्रेण न भावेन वाचाऽसंसज्जमानया।।2.25.39।।
transliteration: uvācātiprahṛṣṭeva sā duḥkhavaśavartinī| vāṅgmātreṇa na bhāvena vācā'saṃsajjamānayā
translation: दुःखवशवर्तिनी filled with distress, सा she, अतिप्रहृष्टेव as if she was exceedingly happy,  संसज्जमानया with confused, वाचा with a tone, वाङ्मात्रेण in mere words, उवाच said, भावेन न not with mind.
explanation: Even though Kausalya was filled with distress, she appeared as if she was very much happy. She uttered  mere words in a confusing tone without applying her mind.

shloka_text: आनम्य मूर्ध्नि चाघ्राय परिष्वज्य यशस्विनी। अवदत्पुत्र सिद्धार्थो गच्छ राम यथासुखम्।।2.25.40।।
transliteration: ānamya mūrdhni cāghrāya pariṣvajya yaśasvinī| avadatputra siddhārtho gaccha rāma yathāsukham
translation: यशस्विनी illustrious lady, आनम्य bending him down, मूर्ध्नि on his forehead, आघ्राय having smelt, परिष्वज्य having embraced, अवदत् spoke, पुत्र O son, राम Rama, सिद्धार्थः having fulfilled your objective, यथा सुखम् in peace and happiness, गच्छ go.
explanation: Illustrious Kausalya embraced Rama, bending his head down and smelt his forehead. And then said O Rama go in peace and come back after accomplishing the objective.

shloka_text: अरोगं सर्वसिद्धार्थमयोध्यां पुनरागतम्। पश्यामि त्वां सुखं वत्स सुस्थितं राजवर्त्मनि।।2.25.41।।
transliteration: arogaṃ sarvasiddhārthamayodhyāṃ punarāgatam| paśyāmi tvāṃ sukhaṃ vatsa susthitaṃ rājavartmani
translation: वत्स O my son, अरोगम् without illness, सर्वसिद्धार्थम् accomplishing all objectives, सुखम्  happily (in good health), पुनः again, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, आगतम् having reached,  राजवर्त्मनि on the royal path (as king), सुस्थितम् firmly standing, त्वाम् you, पश्यामि I shall behold.
explanation: O my son I shall be happy to behold you back in Ayodhya in sound health successful in your objectives and firmly established in the kingdom.

shloka_text: प्रणष्टदुःखसङ्कल्पा हर्षविद्योतितानना। द्रक्ष्यामि त्वां वनात्प्राप्तं पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्।।2.25.42।।
transliteration: praṇaṣṭaduḥkhasaṅkalpā harṣavidyotitānanā| drakṣyāmi tvāṃ vanātprāptaṃ pūrṇacandramivoditam
translation: वनात् from the forest, प्राप्तम् having received, त्वाम् you, उदितम् rising, पूर्णचन्द्रमिव like full moon, प्रणष्टदुःखसंकल्पा having removed my sorrowful thoughts, हर्षविद्योतितानना my face sparkling with joy, द्रक्ष्यामि shall behold.
explanation: When you return from the forest like the full Moon rising, I shall behold you with my anxieties gone and my face sparkling with joy.

shloka_text: भद्रासनगतं राम वनवासादिहागतम्। द्रक्ष्यामि च पुनस्त्वां तु तीर्णवन्तं पितुर्वचः।।2.25.43।।
transliteration: bhadrāsanagataṃ rāma vanavāsādihāgatam| drakṣyāmi ca punastvāṃ tu tīrṇavantaṃ piturvacaḥ
translation: राम O Rama, पितुः वचः father's words, तीर्णवन्तम् having crossed (fuliflled), वनवासात् from your exile, इह here, पुनः again, आगतम् having arrived, त्वाम् you, भद्रासनगतम् sitting on the throne,  द्रक्ष्यामि I shall see.
explanation: After you have fulfilled your father's words and returned from your exile I shall behold you seated on the throne, O Rama

shloka_text: मङ्गलैरुपसपन्नो वनवासादिहागतः। वध्वा मम च नित्यं त्वं कामान्संवर्ध याहि भोः।।2.25.44।।
transliteration: maṅgalairupasapanno vanavāsādihāgataḥ| vadhvā mama ca nityaṃ tvaṃ kāmānsaṃvardha yāhi bhoḥ
translation: भोः O Rama, वनवासात् from the forest, इह here, आगतः having returned, मङ्गलै: with auspicious events, उपसम्पन्नः endowed with, त्वम् you, वध्वाः of my daughterinlaw (Sita's), मम च for me also, कामान् desires, नित्यम् always, संवर्ध enhance, याहि go.
explanation: O Rama, credited with auspicious events on return from the forest, fulfil my desires and those of my daughterinlaw (Sita).

shloka_text: मयाऽर्चिता देवगणाश्शिवादयो महर्षयो भूतमहासुरोरगाः। अभिप्रयातस्य वनं चिराय ते हितानि काङ्क्षन्तु दिशश्च राघव।।2.25.45।।
transliteration: mayā'rcitā devagaṇāśśivādayo maharṣayo bhūtamahāsuroragāḥ| abhiprayātasya vanaṃ cirāya te hitāni kāṅkṣantu diśaśca rāghava
translation: राघव O son of the Raghu race मया by me, अर्चिताः worshipped, शिवादयः Siva and others, देवगणाः gods, महर्षयः the great rishis, भूतमहासुरोरगाः bhutas, great asuras, serpents, दिशश्च four quarters, वनम् to the forest, अभिप्रयातस्य having exiled, ते your, हितानि welfare,  चिराय for a long time, काङ्क्षन्तु may wish for.
explanation: O son of the Raghu race Lord Siva and other gods, the great rishis, bhutas, great asuras and serpents and four quarters worshipped by me will always promote your welfare when you dwell in the forest.

shloka_text: इतीव साऽश्रुप्रतिपूर्णलोचना समाप्य च स्वस्त्ययनं यथाविधि। प्रदक्षिणं चैव चकार राघवं पुनः पुनश्चापि निपीड्य सस्वजे।।2.25.46।।
transliteration: itīva sā'śrupratipūrṇalocanā samāpya ca svastyayanaṃ yathāvidhi| pradakṣiṇaṃ caiva cakāra rāghavaṃ punaḥ punaścāpi nipīḍya sasvaje
translation: इतीव speaking thus, सा she, अश्रुप्रतिपूर्णलोचना eyes filled with tears, यथाविधि duly, स्वस्त्ययनम् benedictory rites, समाप्य च having completed, राघवम् to the descendant of the Raghu dynasty, प्रदक्षिणं चकार circumambulate, पुनः पुनः च अपि repeatedly, निपीड्य holding him tight, सस्वजे embraced.
explanation: Thus with her eyes brimming with tears, she duly completed the benedictory rites and  circumambulated the scion of the Raghus and embraced him again and again holding him tight.

shloka_text: तथा तु देव्या स कृतप्रदक्षिणो निपीड्य मातुश्चरणौ पुनः पुनः। जगाम सीतानिलयं महायशा स्स राघवः प्रज्वलित स्स्वया श्रिया।।2.25.47।।
transliteration: tathā tu devyā sa kṛtapradakṣiṇo nipīḍya mātuścaraṇau punaḥ punaḥ| jagāma sītānilayaṃ mahāyaśā ssa rāghavaḥ prajvalita ssvayā śriyā
translation: देव्या by Devi Kausalya, तथा that way, कृतप्रदक्षिणः having circumambulated, सः Rama,  मातुः his mothers, चरणौ feet, पुनः पुनः again and again, निपीड्य holding fast, महायशाः illustrious, सः राघवः that son of the Raghu race, स्वया by his own, श्रिया with glory, प्रज्वलितः glowing, सीतानिलयम् to the palace of Sita, जगाम went.
explanation: Circumambulated by mother Kausalya, the illustrious scion of the Raghu race clasped his mother's feet again and again. And shining in his glory, proceeded to the palace of Sita. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चविंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the twentyfifth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of  the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्य च कौसल्यां राम स्संप्रस्थितो वनम्। कृतस्वस्त्ययनो मात्रा धर्मिष्ठे वर्त्मनि स्थितः।।2.26.1।। विराजयन्राजसुतो राजमार्गं नरैर्वृतम्। हृदयान्याममन्थेव जनस्य गुणवत्तया।।2.26.2।।
transliteration: abhivādya ca kausalyāṃ rāma ssaṃprasthito vanam| kṛtasvastyayano mātrā dharmiṣṭhe vartmani sthitaḥ virājayanrājasuto rājamārgaṃ narairvṛtam| hṛdayānyāmamantheva janasya guṇavattayā
translation: राजसुतः prince, रामः Rama, मात्रा by mother, कृतस्वस्त्ययन: having been greeted with benedictory rites, कौशल्याम् to Kausalya, अभिवाद्य च after paying obeisance, धर्मिष्ठे in the righteous, वर्त्मनि on the path, स्थितः fixed, वनम् to the forest, सम्प्रस्थितः set out, नरैः (जनैः) by the people, वृतम् surrounded with, राजमार्गम् highway, विराजयन् illuminating (with his lustre), गुणवत्तया by excellent virtues, जनस्य people's, हृदयानि hearts, अममन्थेव मपहीला् (stirred).
explanation: After the benedictory rites were performed by his mother Kausalya, Rama paid obeisance to her and staying on the righteous path decided to depart to the forest. He entered the highway thronged with people and illumining it with his lustre and stirred their hearts with (remembrances of) his excellent virtues.
comments: Sita enquires why Rama is distressedRama informs her about his impending banishment and instructs her to stay back in Ayodhya.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्य च कौसल्यां राम स्संप्रस्थितो वनम्। कृतस्वस्त्ययनो मात्रा धर्मिष्ठे वर्त्मनि स्थितः।।2.26.1।। विराजयन्राजसुतो राजमार्गं नरैर्वृतम्। हृदयान्याममन्थेव जनस्य गुणवत्तया।।2.26.2।।
transliteration: abhivādya ca kausalyāṃ rāma ssaṃprasthito vanam| kṛtasvastyayano mātrā dharmiṣṭhe vartmani sthitaḥ virājayanrājasuto rājamārgaṃ narairvṛtam| hṛdayānyāmamantheva janasya guṇavattayā
translation: राजसुतः prince, रामः Rama, मात्रा by mother, कृतस्वस्त्ययन: having been greeted with benedictory rites, कौशल्याम् to Kausalya, अभिवाद्य च after paying obeisance, धर्मिष्ठे in the righteous, वर्त्मनि on the path, स्थितः fixed, वनम् to the forest, सम्प्रस्थितः set out, नरैः (जनैः) by the people, वृतम् surrounded with, राजमार्गम् highway, विराजयन् illuminating (with his lustre), गुणवत्तया by excellent virtues, जनस्य people's, हृदयानि hearts, अममन्थेव मपहीला् (stirred).
explanation: After the benedictory rites were performed by his mother Kausalya, Rama paid obeisance to her and staying on the righteous path decided to depart to the forest. He entered the highway thronged with people and illumining it with his lustre and stirred their hearts with (remembrances of) his excellent virtues.

shloka_text: वैदेही चापि तत्सर्वं न शुश्राव तपस्विनी। तदेव हृदि तस्याश्च यौवराज्याभिषेचनम्।।2.26.3।।
transliteration: vaidehī cāpi tatsarvaṃ na śuśrāva tapasvinī| tadeva hṛdi tasyāśca yauvarājyābhiṣecanam
translation: तपस्विनी engaged in religious austerities (for consecration), वैदेही चापि Sita also, तत्सर्वम् all that, न शुश्राव did not hear, तस्याः her, हृदि in heart, तत् that, अभिषेचनम् एव  only consecration (was reflecting).
explanation: Sita, her mind preoccupied with thoughts about consecration, was engaged in religious austerities and hence could not hear of all this (development).

shloka_text: देवकार्यं स्वयं कृत्वा कृतज्ञा हृष्टचेतना। अभिज्ञा राजधर्माणां राजपुत्रं प्रतीक्षते।।2.26.4।।
transliteration: devakāryaṃ svayaṃ kṛtvā kṛtajñā hṛṣṭacetanā| abhijñā rājadharmāṇāṃ rājaputraṃ pratīkṣate
translation: कृतज्ञा grateful (to god), राजधर्माणाम् duties of a king (palace rituals), अभिज्ञा experienced in, हृष्टचेतना with pleased mind, स्वयम् herself, देवकार्यम् worship of gods, कृत्वा having made,  राजपुत्रम् prince, प्रतीक्षते was awaiting.
explanation: Experienced in palace rituals, Sita, grateful (to God) after performing worship of the deities was awaiting in a happy mood the arrival of the prince.

shloka_text: प्रविवेशाथ रामस्तु स्वं वेश्म सुविभूषितम्। प्रहृष्टजनसम्पूर्णं ह्रिया किञ्चिदवाङ्मुखः।।2.26.5।।
transliteration: praviveśātha rāmastu svaṃ veśma suvibhūṣitam| prahṛṣṭajanasampūrṇaṃ hriyā kiñcidavāṅmukhaḥ
translation: अथ thereafter, रामस्तु Rama, ह्रिया with embarrassment, किञ्चित् a little, अवाङ्मुखः with his head bent down, प्रहृष्टजनसम्पूर्णम् thronged with excited people, सुविभूषितम् welldecorated, स्वं वेश्म his own residence, प्रविवेश entered.
explanation: His head bent down in embarrassment, Rama entered his welldecorated residence thronged with excited people.

shloka_text: अथ सीता समुत्पत्य वेपमाना च तं पतिम्। अपश्यच्छोकसन्तप्तं चिन्ताव्याकुलितेन्द्रियम्।।2.26.6।।
transliteration: atha sītā samutpatya vepamānā ca taṃ patim| apaśyacchokasantaptaṃ cintāvyākulitendriyam
translation: अथ thereafter, सीता Sita, समुत्पत्य entering suddenly, वेपमाना च a trembling, शोकसन्तप्तम् distressed with grief, चिन्ताव्याकुलितेन्द्रियम् senses agitated due to anxiety, तं पतिम् her husband, अपश्यत् beheld.
explanation: Sita got up suddenly, (her limbs) trembling to see her husband distressed with grief and agitated with anxiety.

shloka_text: तां दृष्ट्वा स हि धर्मात्मा न शशाक मनोगतम्। तं शोकं राघवः सोढुं ततो विवृततां गतः।।2.26.7।।
transliteration: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sa hi dharmātmā na śaśāka manogatam| taṃ śokaṃ rāghavaḥ soḍhuṃ tato vivṛtatāṃ gataḥ
translation: धर्मात्मा virtuous, सः that, राघवः son of the Raghus (Rama), ताम् her, दृष्ट्वा having seen, मनोगतम् in mind, तं शोकम् that sorrow, सोढुम् to endure (control), न शशाक was not able, ततः for that reason, विवृतताम् गतः manifested.
explanation: On seeing her, virtuous Rama could not contain the sorrow in his mind which  manifested (through his external appearance).

shloka_text: विवर्णवदनं दृष्ट्वा तं प्रस्विन्नममर्षणम्। आह दुःखाभिसन्तप्ता किमिदानीमिदं प्रभो।।2.26.8।।
transliteration: vivarṇavadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ prasvinnamamarṣaṇam| āha duḥkhābhisantaptā kimidānīmidaṃ prabho
translation: विवर्णवदनम् pale face, प्रस्विन्नम् heavily perspiring, अमर्षणम् indignant, तम् him, दृष्ट्वा having seen, दुःखाभिसन्तप्ता  consumed with grief, आह uttered, प्रभो O Lord, इदानीम् now, इदम् this, किम् what?
explanation: On seeing Rama with a pale face. indignant and heavily perspiring, Sita, consumed  with grief said, My Lord, why are you now like this?

shloka_text: अद्य बार्हस्पत श्श्रीमान्युक्तः पुष्योऽनु राघव। प्रोच्यते ब्राह्मणैः प्राज्ञैः केन त्वमसि दुर्मनाः।।2.26.9।।
transliteration: adya bārhaspata śśrīmānyuktaḥ puṣyo'nu rāghava| procyate brāhmaṇaiḥ prājñaiḥ kena tvamasi durmanāḥ
translation: राघव O scion of the Raghu race, अद्य today, श्रीमान् auspicious one, बार्हस्पतः with Brihaspati presiding over, पुष्यः Pushya star, युक्तः as suitable, प्राज्ञैः by learned ones, ब्राह्मणैः by brahmins, प्रोच्यते is declared, त्वम् you, केन for what reason, दुर्मनाः असि are dejected?
explanation: O scion of the Raghu race, today has been declared by learned brahmins a suitable and auspicious day for consecration under Pushya star with Brihaspati as presiding deity. Then why are you dejected?

shloka_text: न ते शतशलाकेन जलफेननिभेन च। आवृतं वदनं वल्गु छत्रेणापि विराजते।।2.26.10।।
transliteration: na te śataśalākena jalaphenanibhena ca| āvṛtaṃ vadanaṃ valgu chatreṇāpi virājate
translation: वल्गु charming, ते your, वदनम् face, शत शलाकेन with a hundred ribs, जलफेननिभेन (white) like foam in water, छत्रेण by umbrella, आवृतम् having been covered, न विराजते does not shine.
explanation: How is it that your charming face shines not today under a hundredribbed umbrella (white) like foam in water?

shloka_text: व्यजनाभ्यां च मुख्याभ्यां शतपत्रनिभेक्षणम्। चन्द्रहंसप्रकाशाभ्यां वीज्यते न तवाननम्।।2.26.11।।
transliteration: vyajanābhyāṃ ca mukhyābhyāṃ śatapatranibhekṣaṇam| candrahaṃsaprakāśābhyāṃ vījyate na tavānanam
translation: शतपत्रनिभेक्षणम् eyes resembling lotus, तव आननम् your face, चन्द्रहंस प्रकाशाभ्याम् with the glow of the moon or swan, मुख्याभ्याम् by the excellent, व्यजनाभ्याम् with fans, न वीज्यते is not being fanned.
explanation: (How is it that) your face, with its lotuslike eyes is not being fanned by excellent fans of the colour of the Moon or the swan.

shloka_text: वाग्मिनो वन्दिनश्चापि प्रहृष्टास्त्वां नरर्षभ। स्तुवन्तो नात्र दृश्यन्ते मङ्गलैः स्सूतमागधाः।।2.26.12।।
transliteration: vāgmino vandinaścāpi prahṛṣṭāstvāṃ nararṣabha| stuvanto nātra dṛśyante maṅgalaiḥ ssūtamāgadhāḥ
translation: नरर्षभ O best among men वाग्मिन: eloquent men, वन्दिनश्चापि panegyrists, सूतमागधाः charioteers and bards, प्रहृष्टाः delighted, त्वाम् you, मङ्गलैः with auspicious words, स्तुवन्तः praising, अत्र here, न दृश्यन्ते are not seen.
explanation: (How is it that) O best among men eloquent panegyrists, charioteers, bards are not seen singing your praise with auspicious words?

shloka_text: न ते क्षौद्रं च दधि च ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः। मूर्ध्नि मूर्धाभिषिक्तस्य ददति स्म विधानतः।।2.26.13।।
transliteration: na te kṣaudraṃ ca dadhi ca brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ| mūrdhni mūrdhābhiṣiktasya dadati sma vidhānataḥ
translation: वेदपारगाः versed in the Vedas, ब्राह्मणाः brahmins, मूर्धाभिषिक्तस्य having been consecrated,   ते your, मूर्ध्नि on head, विधानतः conforming to rites, क्षौद्रं च honey also, दधि च curds, न ददति स्म did not sprinkle.
explanation: How is it that brahmins versed in the Vedas have not duly sprinkled the mixture of honey and curd on your head (prior to your consecration)?

shloka_text: न त्वां प्रकृतय स्सर्वा श्श्रेणीमुख्याश्च भूषिताः। अनुव्रजितुमिच्छन्ति पौरजानपदास्तथा।।2.26.14।।
transliteration: na tvāṃ prakṛtaya ssarvā śśreṇīmukhyāśca bhūṣitāḥ| anuvrajitumicchanti paurajānapadāstathā
translation: सर्वाः all, प्रकृतयः ministers, श्रेणीमुख्याश्च also the heads of guilds, तथा also, पौरजानपदाः citizens of towns and villages, भूषिताः adorned, त्वाम् you, अनुव्रजितुम् to follow, न इच्छन्ति do not seek.
explanation: How is it that welladorned ministers, citizens from towns and villages, heads of guilds and others do not follow you?

shloka_text: चतुर्भिर्वेगसम्पन्नैर्हयैः काञ्चनभूषितैः। मुख्यः पुष्यरथो युक्तः किं न गच्छति तेऽग्रतः।।2.26.15।।
transliteration: caturbhirvegasampannairhayaiḥ kāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ| mukhyaḥ puṣyaratho yuktaḥ kiṃ na gacchati te'grataḥ
translation: वेगसम्पन्नैः running swiftly, काञ्चनभूषितैः decorated with gold, चतुर्भिः four, हयैः horses, युक्तः harnessed, मुख्यः important, पुष्यरथः ceremonial chariot, किम् why, ते अग्रतः preceding you, न गच्छति is not going.
explanation: How is it that the chief ceremonial chariot, decorated with gold and harnessed by four galloping horses is not preceding you?

shloka_text: हस्ती चाग्रत श्श्रीमां स्तव लक्षणपूजितः। प्रयाणे लक्ष्यते वीर कृष्णमेघगिरि प्रभः।।2.26.16।।
transliteration: hastī cāgrata śśrīmāṃ stava lakṣaṇapūjitaḥ| prayāṇe lakṣyate vīra kṛṣṇameghagiri prabhaḥ
translation: वीर O valiant one, तव your, प्रयाणे in your journey, अग्रतः in front, लक्षणपूजितः endowed with good features and revered, कृष्णमेघगिरिप्रभः with the lustre of a dark cloud or a  mountain, श्रीमान् auspicious one, हस्ती an elephant, न लक्ष्यते is not seen.
explanation: How is it that the elephant, whose lustre resembles that of a mountain or a dark cloud and endowed with auspicious features is not seen leading your procession, O valiant one

shloka_text: न च काञ्चनचित्रं ते पश्यामि प्रियदर्शन। भद्रासनं पुरस्कृत्य यान्तं वीर पुरस्कृतम्।।2.26.17।।
transliteration: na ca kāñcanacitraṃ te paśyāmi priyadarśana| bhadrāsanaṃ puraskṛtya yāntaṃ vīra puraskṛtam
translation: वीर O heroic one, प्रियदर्शन O one with a pleasant countenance, काञ्चनचित्रम् carved in gold, ते to you, भद्रासनम् throne, पुरस्कृत्य keeping in front of, यान्तम् proceeding, पुरस्कृतम् keeping in front, न च पश्यामि I do not see.
explanation: O heroic one O handsome one how is it that I do not see your attendants proceeding in front with the throne carved in gold?

shloka_text: अभिषेको यथा सज्जः किमिदानीमिदं तव। अपूर्वो मुखवर्णश्च न प्रहर्षश्च लक्ष्यते।।2.26.18।।
transliteration: abhiṣeko yathā sajjaḥ kimidānīmidaṃ tava| apūrvo mukhavarṇaśca na praharṣaśca lakṣyate
translation: अभिषेकः consecration, यथा as, सज्जः arranged, तव your, मुखवर्णः complexion of your face, अपूर्वः unusual, प्रहर्षश्च delightful, न लक्ष्यते not seen, इदानीम् now, इदम् this, किम् why?
explanation: How is it that when arrangements are under way now for your consecration, the complexion of your countenance does not look like what it was before? There is no joy on your face.

shloka_text: इतीव विलपन्तीं तां प्रोवाच रघुनन्दनः। सीते तत्र भवांस्तातः प्रव्राजयति मां वनम्।।2.26.19।।
transliteration: itīva vilapantīṃ tāṃ provāca raghunandanaḥ| sīte tatra bhavāṃstātaḥ pravrājayati māṃ vanam
translation: इतीव in this way, विलपन्तीम् lamenting, ताम् to her, रघुनन्दनः Rama, प्रोवाच said , सीते O Sita, तत्रभवान् venerable, तातः father, माम् me, वनम् to the forest, प्रव्राजयति  banishing.
explanation: O Sita my venerable father is banishing me to the forest, said Rama, the scion of the Raghus, the joy of the Raghu race, seeing her thus lamenting.

shloka_text: कुले महति सम्भूते धर्मज्ञे धर्मचारिणि। शृणु जानकि येनेदं क्रमेणाभ्यागतं मम।।2.26.20।।
transliteration: kule mahati sambhūte dharmajñe dharmacāriṇi| śṛṇu jānaki yenedaṃ krameṇābhyāgataṃ mama
translation: महति in a noble, कुले family, सम्भूते born in, धर्मज्ञे knower of righteousness, धर्मचारिणि for an observer of righteousness, जानकि Sita, येन क्रमेण in such course, इदम् this, अभ्यागतम् has befallen, शृण listen.
explanation: You were born in a noble family. You know and practise dharma. I shall tell you how this banishment has come about. Do listen.

shloka_text: राज्ञा सत्यप्रतिज्ञेन पित्रा दशरथेन च। कैकेय्यै मम मात्रे तु पुरा दत्तौ महावरौ।।2.26.21।।
transliteration: rājñā satyapratijñena pitrā daśarathena ca| kaikeyyai mama mātre tu purā dattau mahāvarau
translation: राज्ञा by the king, सत्यप्रतिज्ञेन true to his promise, पित्रा my father, दशरथेन by Dasaratha, पुरा earlier, मम मात्रे to my mother, कैकेय्यै to Kaikeyi, महावरौ two great boons, दत्तौ were given.
explanation: My father, king Dasaratha, true to his promise, had earlier granted two great boons to my mother Kaikeyi.

shloka_text: तयाऽद्य मम सज्जेऽस्मिन्नभिषेके नृपोद्यते। प्रचोदित स्स समयो धर्मेण प्रतिनिर्जितः।।2.26.22।।
transliteration: tayā'dya mama sajje'sminnabhiṣeke nṛpodyate| pracodita ssa samayo dharmeṇa pratinirjitaḥ
translation: अद्य now, नृपोद्यते the king was getting ready, मम my, अस्मिन् अभिषेके for this consecration, सज्जे in the preparation, तया by her, सः that, समयः promise, प्रचोदितः was urged, धर्मेण in the name of righteousness, प्रतिनिर्जितः has been conquered.
explanation: When the king was preparing for my consecration, she reminded him of the promise and in the name of righteousness he has been cornered.

shloka_text: चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि वस्तव्यं दण्डके मया। पित्रा मे भरतश्चापि यौवराज्ये नियोजितः।।2.26.23।।
transliteration: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi vastavyaṃ daṇḍake mayā| pitrā me bharataścāpi yauvarājye niyojitaḥ
translation: मया by me, चतुर्दश वर्षाणि fourteen years, दण्डके in Dandaka forest, वस्तव्यम् am to dwell, मे पित्रा by my father, भरतश्चापि Bharata also, यौवराज्ये as heirapparent,  नियोजितः has been appointed.
explanation: I am to dwell in the Dandaka forest for fourteen years while father has appointed  Bharata princeregent.

shloka_text: सोऽहं त्वामागतो द्रष्टुं प्रस्थितो विजनं वनम्। भरतस्य समीपे तु नाहं कथ्यः कदाचन।।2.26.24।। बुद्धियुक्ता हि पुरुषा न सहन्ते परस्तवम्। तस्मान्नते गुणाः कथ्या भरतस्याग्रतो मम।।2.26.25।।
transliteration: so'haṃ tvāmāgato draṣṭuṃ prasthito vijanaṃ vanam| bharatasya samīpe tu nāhaṃ kathyaḥ kadācana buddhiyuktā hi puruṣā na sahante parastavam| tasmānnate guṇāḥ kathyā bharatasyāgrato mama
translation: विजनम् desolate, वनम् forest, प्रस्थितः set to depart, सः अहम् such me, त्वाम् you, द्रष्टुम् to see, आगतः I have come, भरतस्य Bharata's, समीपे in the presence of, कदाचन at any time, अहम् I, न कथ्यः not to be told , बुद्धियुक्ताः intellectuals, पुरुषाः men, परस्तवम् praising others , न सहन्ते हि cannot endure, तस्मात् for that reason, भरतस्य Bharata's, अग्रतः infront of, ते those, मम गुणाः my virtues, न कथ्याः should not be mentioned.
explanation: I have come to see you before departing for the desolate Dandaka forest. You should never praise me in the presence of Bharata because intellectuals cannot tolerate others being praised before them. You should never extol my virtues before him.

shloka_text: सोऽहं त्वामागतो द्रष्टुं प्रस्थितो विजनं वनम्। भरतस्य समीपे तु नाहं कथ्यः कदाचन।।2.26.24।। बुद्धियुक्ता हि पुरुषा न सहन्ते परस्तवम्। तस्मान्नते गुणाः कथ्या भरतस्याग्रतो मम।।2.26.25।।
transliteration: so'haṃ tvāmāgato draṣṭuṃ prasthito vijanaṃ vanam| bharatasya samīpe tu nāhaṃ kathyaḥ kadācana buddhiyuktā hi puruṣā na sahante parastavam| tasmānnate guṇāḥ kathyā bharatasyāgrato mama
translation: विजनम् desolate, वनम् forest, प्रस्थितः set to depart, सः अहम् such me, त्वाम् you, द्रष्टुम् to see, आगतः I have come, भरतस्य Bharata's, समीपे in the presence of, कदाचन at any time, अहम् I, न कथ्यः not to be told , बुद्धियुक्ताः intellectuals, पुरुषाः men, परस्तवम् praising others , न सहन्ते हि cannot endure, तस्मात् for that reason, भरतस्य Bharata's, अग्रतः infront of, ते those, मम गुणाः my virtues, न कथ्याः should not be mentioned.
explanation: I have come to see you before departing for the desolate Dandaka forest. You should never praise me in the presence of Bharata because intellectuals cannot tolerate others being praised before them. You should never extol my virtues before him.

shloka_text: नापि त्वं तेन भर्तव्या विशेषेण कदाचन। अनुकूलतया शक्यं समीपे त्वस्य वर्तितुम्।।2.26.26।।
transliteration: nāpi tvaṃ tena bhartavyā viśeṣeṇa kadācana| anukūlatayā śakyaṃ samīpe tvasya vartitum
translation: त्वम् you, तेन by him, कदाचन at any time, विशेषेण with a special treatment, न भर्तव्या  should not be supported, अनुकूलतया तु by being favourable only, अस्य his, समीपे in his vicinity, वर्तितुम् to remain, शक्यम् is possible.
explanation: Never expect special treatment from Bharata. You can (continue to) stay with him (here) by conducting yourself in a favourable manner.

shloka_text: तस्मै दत्तं नृपतिना यौवराज्यं सनातनम्। स प्रसाद्यस्त्वया सीते नृपतिश्च विशेषतः।।2.26.27।।
transliteration: tasmai dattaṃ nṛpatinā yauvarājyaṃ sanātanam| sa prasādyastvayā sīte nṛpatiśca viśeṣataḥ
translation: नृपतिना by the king, तस्मै for him, सनातनम् perpetual, यौवराज्यम् regency, दत्तम् given, सीते O Sita, सः he, त्वया by you, प्रसाद्यः has to be pleased, नृपतिश्च king also, विशेषतः especially.
explanation: O Sita the king has conferred the hereditary regency on him. Therefore, O Sita, you must make efforts to win his favour, especially a king's.

shloka_text: अहं चापि प्रतिज्ञां तां गुरोस्समनुपालयन्। वनमद्यैव यास्यामि स्थिरा भव मनस्विनी।।2.26.28।।
transliteration: ahaṃ cāpi pratijñāṃ tāṃ gurossamanupālayan| vanamadyaiva yāsyāmi sthirā bhava manasvinī
translation: अहं चापि I also, गुरोः father's, तां प्रतिज्ञाम् that promise, समनुपालयन् while fulfilling, अद्यैव now itself, वनम् to the forest, यास्यामि shall go, मनस्विनि highminded, Sita, त्वम् you, स्थिरा भव keep steady.
explanation: I am leaving for the forest right away for fulfilling my father's pledge. O highminded Sita be steady.

shloka_text: याते च मयि कल्याणि वनं मुनिनिषेवितम्। व्रतोपवासपरया भवितव्यं त्वयाऽनघे।।2.26.29।।
transliteration: yāte ca mayi kalyāṇi vanaṃ muniniṣevitam| vratopavāsaparayā bhavitavyaṃ tvayā'naghe
translation: अनघे O sinless one, कल्याणि O auspicious one, मयि me, मुनिनिषेवितम् inhabited by ascetics, वनम् to the forest, याते when I am gone, त्वया by you, व्रतोपवास परया engaged in vratas and fasting, भवितव्यम् should be done.
explanation: O sinless, auspicious one engage yourself in vratas and fasting after my departure to the forest inhabited by ascetics.

shloka_text: काल्यमुत्थाय देवानां कृत्वा पूजां यथाविधि। वन्दितव्यो दशरथः पिता मम नरेश्वरः।।2.26.30।।
transliteration: kālyamutthāya devānāṃ kṛtvā pūjāṃ yathāvidhi| vanditavyo daśarathaḥ pitā mama nareśvaraḥ
translation: काल्यम् fimely, उत्थाय rising, यथाविधि according to the prescribed rituals, देवानाम् of the gods, पूजाम् कृत्वा having worshipped, मम पिता my father, नरेश्वरः lord of the people, दशरथः to Dasaratha, वन्दितव्यः is worthy of homage (by you).
explanation: You must rise in time and with the (household) gods duly worshipped, pay obeisance to my father, king Dasaratha.

shloka_text: माता च मम कौशल्या वृद्धा सन्तापकर्शिता। धर्ममेवाग्रतः कृत्वा त्वत्त स्सम्मानमर्हति।।2.27.31।।
transliteration: mātā ca mama kauśalyā vṛddhā santāpakarśitā| dharmamevāgrataḥ kṛtvā tvatta ssammānamarhati
translation: सन्तापकर्शिता emaciated due to grief, वृद्धा aged, मम माता च my mother, कौशल्या Kausalya, धर्ममेव duty only, अग्रतः कृत्वा placing ahead, त्वत्तः by you, सम्मानम् respect, अर्हति  deserves.
explanation: You should give importance to duty(dharma) and show respect to my aged mother who is emaciated due to grief.

shloka_text: वन्दितव्याश्च ते नित्यं या श्शेषा मम मातरः। स्नेह प्रणयसम्भोगै स्समा हि मम मातरः।।2.26.32।।
transliteration: vanditavyāśca te nityaṃ yā śśeṣā mama mātaraḥ| sneha praṇayasambhogai ssamā hi mama mātaraḥ
