translation: दुर्मतिः wickedminded, असमञ्जः तु as for Asamanjasa, पथि on the street, क्रीडतः playing, बालकान् children, गृहीत्वा seizing, सरय्वा: Sarayu's, अप्सु in waters, प्रक्षिपन् while hurling, तेन with that, रमते amused.
explanation: That wickedminded Asamanjasa used to seize the children playing on the street and amuse himself by hurling them in the waters of river Sarayu.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा नागरा स्सर्वे कृद्धा राजानमब्रुवन्। असमञ्जं वृणीष्वैकमस्मान्वा राष्ट्रवर्धन।।2.36.20।।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nāgarā ssarve kṛddhā rājānamabruvan| asamañjaṃ vṛṇīṣvaikamasmānvā rāṣṭravardhana
translation: तम् them, दृष्ट्वा on watching, सर्वे all, नागराः people of the city, कृद्धाः enraged, राजानम् to the king, अब्रुवन् spoke, राष्ट्रवर्धन O enhancer of (prosperity of) the kingdom, एकम् one, असमञ्जम् Asamanjasa, अस्मान् वा or us, वृणीष्व choose.
explanation: Watching it, all the enraged citizens said to the king, 'O enhancer of the prosperity of the kingdom, either you choose Asamanjasa or us'.

shloka_text: तानुवाच ततो राजा किन्निमित्तमिदं भयम्। ताश्चापि राज्ञा सम्पृष्टा वाक्यं प्रकृतयोऽब्रुवन्।।2.36.21।।
transliteration: tānuvāca tato rājā kinnimittamidaṃ bhayam| tāścāpi rājñā sampṛṣṭā vākyaṃ prakṛtayo'bruvan
translation: ततः then, राजा king, तान् to them, उवाच said, इदं भयम् this fear, किन्निमित्तम्  why?, राज्ञा by the king, सम्पृष्टाः having been asked, ताः those, प्रकृतयश्चापि subjects also, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रुवन् said.
explanation: The king  then asked them, 'Why this fear?'. And the citizens responded:

shloka_text: डक्रीडतस्त्वेष नः पुत्रान् बालानुद्भ्रान्तचेतनः। सरय्वां प्रक्षिपन्मौर्ख्यादतुलां प्रीतिमश्नुते।।2.36.22।।
transliteration: ḍakrīḍatastveṣa naḥ putrān bālānudbhrāntacetanaḥ| sarayvāṃ prakṣipanmaurkhyādatulāṃ prītimaśnute
translation: उद्भ्रान्तचेतनः with an insane mind, एषः this one, क्रीडतः while playing, बालान् young ones, नः our, पुत्रान् sons, सरय्वाम् in Sarayu river, प्रक्षिपन् while throwing, मौर्ख्यात् in his insanity, अतुलाम्  incomparable, प्रीतिम् pleasure, अश्नुते deriving.
explanation: That insane (Asamanjasa) while throwing our children who were playing around into Sarayu river in his insanity derived incomparable pleasure'.

shloka_text: स तासां वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रकृतीनां नराधिपः। तं तत्याजाहितं पुत्रं तेषां प्रियचिकीर्षया।।2.36.23।।
transliteration: sa tāsāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā prakṛtīnāṃ narādhipaḥ| taṃ tatyājāhitaṃ putraṃ teṣāṃ priyacikīrṣayā
translation: सः नराधिपः that  king, तेषां प्रकृतीनाम् of those subjects, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard,  तासाम् to all of them, प्रियचिकीर्षया with the intention of pleasing them, अहितम् malevolent, तं पुत्रम् that son, तत्याज banished.
explanation: That king (Sagara) heard the words of the citizens and with the intention of doing good to them, banished that malevolent son.

shloka_text: तं यानं शीघ्रमारोप्य सभार्यं सपरिच्छदम्। यावज्जीवं विवास्योऽयमिति स्वानन्वशात्पिता।।2.36.24।।
transliteration: taṃ yānaṃ śīghramāropya sabhāryaṃ saparicchadam| yāvajjīvaṃ vivāsyo'yamiti svānanvaśātpitā
translation: पिता father, Sagara, भार्यम् to (his sons's) wife, सपरिच्छदम् with the clothes on them (then their, तम् him, शीघ्रम् without delay, यानम् in a carriage, आरोप्य got him placed, अयम् this one, यावज्जीवम् for life, विवास्यः इति shall be banished, स्वान् his servants, अन्वशात् ordered.
explanation: Then the father made him and his wife climb a carriage with the clothes they had at the time on them and at once ordered his servants to banish him for life.

shloka_text: स फालपिटकं गृह्य गिरिदुर्गाण्यलोडयत्। दिश स्सर्वास्त्वनुचरन् स यथा पापकर्मकृत्।।2.36.25।।
transliteration: sa phālapiṭakaṃ gṛhya giridurgāṇyaloḍayat| diśa ssarvāstvanucaran sa yathā pāpakarmakṛt
translation: स: he, पापकर्मकृत् यथा like an evildoer, सर्वाः all, दिशः directions, अनुचरन् wandering about, सः he, फालपिटकम् a spade and a basket, गृह्य holding, गिरिदुर्गाणि impenetrable mountains, अलोडयत् spent digging.
explanation: Like an evildoer wandering about in different directions, holding a spade and a basket in his hand, he went about digging the impenetrable mountains.

shloka_text: इत्येनमत्यजद्राजा सगरो वै सुधार्मिकः। रामः किमकरोत्पापं येनैवमुपरुध्यते।।2.36.26।।
transliteration: ityenamatyajadrājā sagaro vai sudhārmikaḥ| rāmaḥ kimakarotpāpaṃ yenaivamuparudhyate
translation: सुधार्मिकः highly righteous, सगरः राजा king Sagara, इति thus, एनम् him, अत्यजत् abandoned, रामः Rama, किं पापम् what sin, अकरोत् has committed, येन by which, एवम् this way,  उपरुध्यते should be banished.
explanation: Highly righteous king Sagara thus banished his son. What sin has Rama committed to secure a similar banishment?

shloka_text: न हि कञ्चन पश्यामो राघवस्यागुणं वयम्। दुर्लभो ह्यस्य निरय श्शशाङ्कस्येव कल्मषम्।।2.36.27।।
transliteration: na hi kañcana paśyāmo rāghavasyāguṇaṃ vayam| durlabho hyasya niraya śśaśāṅkasyeva kalmaṣam
translation: वयम् we, राघवस्य Rama's, अवगुणम् fault, कञ्चन even a little, न पश्यामः हि we do not see, शशाङ्कस्य moon's, कल्मषम् इव like stain, अस्य for this Rama, निरयः hell (blemish), दुर्लभः is difficult to find
explanation: We see no fault in Rama. Unlike the stain in the Moon it is difficult to find any  blemish in him.

shloka_text: अथवा देवि दोषं त्वं कञ्चित्पश्यसि राघवे। तमद्य ब्रूहि तत्वेन तदा रामो विवास्यताम्।।2.36.28।।
transliteration: athavā devi doṣaṃ tvaṃ kañcitpaśyasi rāghave| tamadya brūhi tatvena tadā rāmo vivāsyatām
translation: अथवा nevertheless, देवि Devi (Kaikeyi), त्वम् you, राघवे in the scion of the Raghu race (Rama), कञ्चित् the little, दोषम् fault, पश्यसि see, तम् about him, अद्य now, तत्त्वेन truly, ब्रूहि speak, तदा then, रामः Rama, विवास्यताम् will be exiled.
explanation: O Kaikeyi speak truly if you find any fault in this scion of the Raghu race (Rama). Then he will be exiled.

shloka_text: अदुष्टस्य हि संत्यागः सत्पथे निरतस्य च। निर्दहेदपि शक्रस्य द्युतिं धर्मनिरोधनात्।2.36.29।।
transliteration: aduṣṭasya hi saṃtyāgaḥ satpathe niratasya ca| nirdahedapi śakrasya dyutiṃ dharmanirodhanāt|2.36.29||
translation: अदुष्टस्य of an innocent, सत्पथे on the righteous path, निरतस्य च engaged in, संत्यागः  banishment, धर्मनिरोधनात् by restraining righteousness, शक्रस्य अपि even Indra's, द्युतिम्  brilliance, निर्दहेत् will be destroyed.
explanation: The act of banishment of an innocent one walking the righteous path is like destroying the brilliance of Indra by restraining his righteousness.

shloka_text: तदलं देवि रामस्य श्रिया विहतया त्वया। लोकतोऽपि हि ते रक्ष्यः परिवादः शुभानने।।2.36.30।।
transliteration: tadalaṃ devi rāmasya śriyā vihatayā tvayā| lokato'pi hi te rakṣyaḥ parivādaḥ śubhānane
translation: देवि Devi, तत् for that reason, त्वया by you, रामस्य Rama's, श्रिया with prosperity, विहतया has been ruined, अलम् enough, शुभानने O one of auspicious countenance, ते to you, लोकतः in the world, परिवादः अपि censure also, रक्ष्यः हि is to be saved.
explanation: O Devi, there is no use obstructing Rama's prosperity. O one with an auspicious countenance, save yourself from the censure of the world.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु सिद्धार्थवचो राजा श्रान्ततरस्वनः। शोकोपहतया वाचा कैकेयीमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.36.31।।
transliteration: śrutvā tu siddhārthavaco rājā śrāntatarasvanaḥ| śokopahatayā vācā kaikeyīmidamabravīt
translation: सिद्धार्थवचः Siddhartha's words, श्रुत्वा having heard, राजा king, श्रान्ततरस्वनः in progressively failing voice, शोकोपहतया griefstricken, वाचा words, कैकेयीम् to Kaikeyi, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having heard Siddhartha, the king, stricken with grief, said to Kaikeyi in a gradually feeble voice.

shloka_text: एतद्वचो नेच्छसि पापवृत्ते हितं न जानासि ममात्मनो वा। आस्थाय मार्गं कृपणं कुचेष्टा चेष्टा हि ते साधुपथादपेता।।2.36.32।।
transliteration: etadvaco necchasi pāpavṛtte hitaṃ na jānāsi mamātmano vā| āsthāya mārgaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ kuceṣṭā ceṣṭā hi te sādhupathādapetā
translation: पापवृत्ते O one of vicious behaviour, एतत् वचः all these words, नेच्छसि do not please you, कुचेष्टा  of wicked attempts, कृपणम् vile, मार्गम् path, आस्थाय having adopted, मम to me, आत्मनो वा or to  you also, हितम् good, न जानासि you do not know, ते to you, चेष्टा actions, साधुपथात् from the right path, अपेता devoid
explanation: O Kaikeyi of vicious behaviour, you do not aceept even the words of Siddhartha. You woman of wicked acts, having adopted vile ways, and abjured the right path cannot know what is good either for you or for me.

shloka_text: अनुव्रजिष्याम्यहमद्य रामं राज्यं परित्यज्य सुखं धनं च। सहैव राज्ञा भरतेन च त्वं यथासुखं भुङ्क्ष्व चिराय राज्यम्।।2.36.33।।
transliteration: anuvrajiṣyāmyahamadya rāmaṃ rājyaṃ parityajya sukhaṃ dhanaṃ ca| sahaiva rājñā bharatena ca tvaṃ yathāsukhaṃ bhuṅkṣva cirāya rājyam
translation: अहम् I, राज्यम् kingdom, सुखम् comfort, धनं च wealth, परित्यज्य forsaking, अद्य today, रामम् Rama, अनुव्रजिष्यामि shall follow, त्वम् you, राज्ञा with the king, भरतेन सहैव along with Bharata, यथासुखम् happily, चिराय for a long time, राज्यम् kingdom, भुङ्क्ष्व enjoy.
explanation: Abandoning this kingdom, these comforts and this wealth, I shall follow Rama. Enjoy the kingdom for a long time happily along with king Bharata. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षट्त्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends  the thirtysixth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: महामात्रवचः श्रुत्वा रामो दशरथं तदा। अभ्यभाषत वाक्यं तु विनयज्ञो विनीतवत्।।2.37.1।।
transliteration: mahāmātravacaḥ śrutvā rāmo daśarathaṃ tadā| abhyabhāṣata vākyaṃ tu vinayajño vinītavat
translation: विनयज्ञः knower of politeness, रामः Rama, महामात्रवचः minister's words, श्रुत्वा having heard, तदा then, दशरथम् Dasaratha, विनीतवत् humbly, वाक्यम् words, अभ्यभाषत spoke.
explanation: On hearing the minister, Rama who knew how to be polite spoke these words  to Dasaratha humbly:
comments: Rama puts on bark--Vasistha blames Kaikeyi--says Sita was not ordained to wear bark.

shloka_text: त्यक्तभोगस्य मे राजन् वने वन्येन जीवतः। किं कार्यमनुयात्रेण त्यक्तसङ्गस्य सर्वतः।।2.37.2।।
transliteration: tyaktabhogasya me rājan vane vanyena jīvataḥ| kiṃ kāryamanuyātreṇa tyaktasaṅgasya sarvataḥ
translation: राजन् O king, त्यक्तभोगस्य of forsaker of pleasures, सर्वतः  entirely, त्यक्तसङ्गस्य of one who has given up attachments, वने in the forest, वन्येन available in the forest, जीवतः subsisting, मे for me, अनुयात्रेण followers, किं कार्यम् what is the use?
explanation: O king giving up pleasures and attachments altogether I am going to live on whatever is available in the forest. What is the use of followers?

shloka_text: यो हि दत्त्वा द्विपश्रेष्ठं कक्ष्यायां कुरुते मनः। रज्जुस्नेहेन किं तस्य त्यजतः कुञ्जरोत्तमम्।।2.37.3।।
transliteration: yo hi dattvā dvipaśreṣṭhaṃ kakṣyāyāṃ kurute manaḥ| rajjusnehena kiṃ tasya tyajataḥ kuñjarottamam
translation: यः such a man, द्विपश्रेष्ठम् best of elephants, दत्त्वा having given away, कक्ष्यायाम् rope tied to its girth, मनः mind, कुरुते will do, कुञ्जरोत्तमम् best elephant, त्यजतः of a man while  giving up, तस्य his, रज्जुस्नेहेन for attachment for the rope, किम् why?
explanation: Having given away the best of elephants, will any one be interested in the rope tied to its girth? Why should one have any attachment for the rope after he has given up the elephant?

shloka_text: तथा मम सतां श्रेष्ठ किं ध्वजिन्या जगत्पते। सर्वाण्येवानुजानामि चीराण्येवाऽनयन्तु मे।।2.37.4।।
transliteration: tathā mama satāṃ śreṣṭha kiṃ dhvajinyā jagatpate| sarvāṇyevānujānāmi cīrāṇyevā'nayantu me
translation: सताम् among the virtuous, श्रेष्ठ best, जगत्पते lord of the universe, तथा in that way, मम to me, ध्वजिन्या with the army, किम् what use?, सर्वाण्येव all things, अनुजानामि am giving away, मे to me, चीराण्येव tattered clothes only, आनयन्तु bring.
explanation: O best among the virtuous O lord of the world, I do not have any use for this army. I am giving away everything (to Bharata). Bring the bark only.

shloka_text: खनित्रपिटके चोभे समानयत गच्छतः। चतुर्दश वने वासं वर्षाणि वसतो मम।।2.37.5।।
transliteration: khanitrapiṭake cobhe samānayata gacchataḥ| caturdaśa vane vāsaṃ varṣāṇi vasato mama
translation: गच्छतः going away, चतुर्दश fourteen, वर्षाणि years, वने in the forest, वासम् dwelling, वसतः residing , मम to me, उभे two things, खनित्रपिटके a basket and a crowbar, समानयत bring.
explanation: I am going to the forest to live there for fourteen years. Bring me two things: a basket and a crowbar.

shloka_text: अथ चीराणि कैकेयी स्वयमाहृत्य राघवम्। उवाच परिधत्स्वेति जनौघे निरपत्रपा।।2.37.6।।
transliteration: atha cīrāṇi kaikeyī svayamāhṛtya rāghavam| uvāca paridhatsveti janaughe nirapatrapā
translation: अथ thereupon, कैकेयी Kaikeyi, जनौघे in the presence of the assembly of people, निरपत्रपा without any sense of shame, स्वयम् herself, चीराणि bark robes, अहृत्य having brought, परिथत्स्व  'wear', इति saying so, राघवम् to Rama, उवाच said.
explanation: Thereupon in the assembly of people, without any sense of shame Kaikeyi herself brought the bark robes and said to the son of the Raghus (Rama), Wear it.

shloka_text: स चीरे पुरुषव्याघ्रः कैकेय्या प्रतिगृह्य ते। सूक्ष्मवस्त्रमवक्षिप्य मुनिवस्त्राण्यवस्त ह।।2.37.7।।
transliteration: sa cīre puruṣavyāghraḥ kaikeyyā pratigṛhya te| sūkṣmavastramavakṣipya munivastrāṇyavasta ha
translation: पुरुषव्याघ्रः tiger (best) among men, सः he, कैकेय्याः from Kaikeyi, ते those, चीरे bark robes, प्रतिगृह्य having received, सूक्ष्मवस्त्रम् fine apparel, अपक्षिप्य after removing,  मुनिवस्त्राणि ascetic robes, अवस्त ह put on
explanation: The tiger among men (Rama) received the bark robes from Kaikeyi and putting off the fine apparel wore the robes of an ascetic.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणश्चापि तत्रैव विहाय वसने शुभे। तापसाच्छादने चैव जग्राह पितुरग्रतः।।2.37.8।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaścāpi tatraiva vihāya vasane śubhe| tāpasācchādane caiva jagrāha pituragrataḥ
translation: लक्ष्मणश्चापि Lakshmana also, तत्रैव there only, पितुः father's, अग्रतः in front (presence), शुभे auspicious, वसने raiment, विहाय having discarded, तपसाच्छादने चैव the clothing of an ascetic, जग्राह accepted.
explanation: Lakshmana also  removed his auspicious raiment in front (presence) of his father and accepted (put on) the robes of an ascetic.

shloka_text: अथाऽत्मपरिधानार्थं सीता कौशेयवासिनी। समीक्ष्य चीरं सन्त्रस्ता पृषती वागुरामिव।।2.37.9।।
transliteration: athā'tmaparidhānārthaṃ sītā kauśeyavāsinī| samīkṣya cīraṃ santrastā pṛṣatī vāgurāmiva
translation: अथ then, कौशेयवासिनी wearing silk clothes, सीता Sita, आत्मपरिधानार्थम् meant for her to wear, चीरम् bark robes, समीक्ष्य having seen, पृषती doe, वागुरामिव like a (fowler's) snare, सन्त्रस्ता was frightened.
explanation: Then Sita in silk clothes glanced at the bark robes meant for her to wear and was frightened like a doe seeing a (fowler's) snare.

shloka_text: सा व्यपत्रपमाणेव प्रगृह्य च सुदुर्मनाः। कैकेयी कुशचीरे ते जानकी शुभलक्षणा।।2.37.10।। अश्रुसम्पूर्ण नेत्रा च धर्मज्ञा धर्मदर्शिनी। गन्धर्वराजप्रतिमं भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.37.11।।
transliteration: sā vyapatrapamāṇeva pragṛhya ca sudurmanāḥ| kaikeyī kuśacīre te jānakī śubhalakṣaṇā aśrusampūrṇa netrā ca dharmajñā dharmadarśinī| gandharvarājapratimaṃ bhartāramidamabravīt
translation: सुदुर्मनाः with a deeply distressed mind, शुभलक्षणा of auspicious nature, धर्मज्ञा knows her duties, धर्मदर्शिनी perceives righteousness, सा जानकी that Sita, व्यपत्रपमाणेव as though feeling ashamed, कैकेयी from Kaikeyi, ते those, कुशचीरे garments made of kusa grass, प्रगृह्य having received, अशृसम्पूर्णनेत्रा with her eyes suffused with tears, गन्धर्वराजप्रतिमम् the very image of king of gandharvas, भर्तारम् to her husband, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Sita of auspicious nature who knew her duties and understood righteousness, took the garments made of kusa grass from Kaikeyi. With a sense of abashment her eyes suffused with tears, she said to her husband who was the very image of  the king of gandharvas.

shloka_text: सा व्यपत्रपमाणेव प्रगृह्य च सुदुर्मनाः। कैकेयी कुशचीरे ते जानकी शुभलक्षणा।।2.37.10।। अश्रुसम्पूर्ण नेत्रा च धर्मज्ञा धर्मदर्शिनी। गन्धर्वराजप्रतिमं भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.37.11।।
transliteration: sā vyapatrapamāṇeva pragṛhya ca sudurmanāḥ| kaikeyī kuśacīre te jānakī śubhalakṣaṇā aśrusampūrṇa netrā ca dharmajñā dharmadarśinī| gandharvarājapratimaṃ bhartāramidamabravīt
translation: सुदुर्मनाः with a deeply distressed mind, शुभलक्षणा of auspicious nature, धर्मज्ञा knows her duties, धर्मदर्शिनी perceives righteousness, सा जानकी that Sita, व्यपत्रपमाणेव as though feeling ashamed, कैकेयी from Kaikeyi, ते those, कुशचीरे garments made of kusa grass, प्रगृह्य having received, अशृसम्पूर्णनेत्रा with her eyes suffused with tears, गन्धर्वराजप्रतिमम् the very image of king of gandharvas, भर्तारम् to her husband, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Sita of auspicious nature who knew her duties and understood righteousness, took the garments made of kusa grass from Kaikeyi. With a sense of abashment her eyes suffused with tears, she said to her husband who was the very image of  the king of gandharvas.

shloka_text: कथं नु चीरं बध्नन्ति मुनयो वनवासिनः। इति ह्यकुशला सीता सा मुमोह मुहुर्मुहुः।।2.37.12।।
transliteration: kathaṃ nu cīraṃ badhnanti munayo vanavāsinaḥ| iti hyakuśalā sītā sā mumoha muhurmuhuḥ
translation: वनवासिनः forestdwellers, मुनयः sages, चीरम् (bark) tattered clothe, कथम् how, बध्नन्ति नु  wear them, इति thus, सा सीता that Sita, अकुशला unskilled (unhabituate), मुहुर्मुहुः again and again, मुमोह was perplexed.
explanation: Sita, unacquainted with wearing bark robes, asked Rama, perplexed 'How do the sages who live in the forest wear bark garment?'.

shloka_text: कृत्वा कण्ठे च सा चीरमेकमादाय पाणिना। तस्थौ ह्यकुशला तत्र व्रीडिता जनकात्मजा।।2.37.13।।
transliteration: kṛtvā kaṇṭhe ca sā cīramekamādāya pāṇinā| tasthau hyakuśalā tatra vrīḍitā janakātmajā
translation: सा जनकात्मजा that daughter of Janaka, (Sita), एकम् one end, चीरम् of garment, कण्ठे on the neck, कृत्वा having placed, पाणिना with hand, आदाय held, तत्र thereafter, अकुशला unskilled (unhabituated), व्रीडिता  feeling ashamed, तस्थौ stood.
explanation: The daughter of Janaka, placed one end of the garment round her neck and held the other in her hand, and stood ashamed as she did not know what to do next.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तत्क्षिप्रमागम्य रामो धर्मभृतां वरः। चीरं बबन्ध सीतायाः कौशेयस्योपरि स्वयम्।।2.37.14।।
transliteration: tasyāstatkṣipramāgamya rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ| cīraṃ babandha sītāyāḥ kauśeyasyopari svayam
translation: धर्मभृताम् among protectors of righteousness, वरः foremost, रामः Rama, क्षिप्रम् quickly, आगम्य having come forward, तत् चीरम् that bark garment, तस्याः सीतायाः Sita's, कौशेयस्य silk garment's, उपरि upon, स्वयम् himself, बबन्ध fastened.
explanation: Rama, foremost among protectors of righteousness, came forward quickly and fastened the bark himself over her silk garment.

shloka_text: रामं प्रेक्ष्य तु सीताया बध्नन्तं चीरमुत्तमम्। अन्तःपुरगता नार्यो मुमुचुर्वारि नेत्रजम्।।2.37.15।।
transliteration: rāmaṃ prekṣya tu sītāyā badhnantaṃ cīramuttamam| antaḥpuragatā nāryo mumucurvāri netrajam
translation: सीतायाः of Sita, चीरम् garment, बध्नन्तम् when he was fastening, उत्तमम् excellent, रामम्  Rama, प्रेक्ष्य having seen, अन्तःपुरगताः of the inner apartment, नार्यः women, नेत्रजम्  born of the eyes, वारि tears, मुमुचुः released.
explanation: Beholding Rama fastening the bark garment on Sita, the women of the inner apartment shed tears from their eyes.

shloka_text: ऊचुश्च परमायस्ता रामं ज्वलिततेजसम्। वत्स नैवं नियुक्तेयं वनवासे मनस्विनी।।2.37.16।।
transliteration: ūcuśca paramāyastā rāmaṃ jvalitatejasam| vatsa naivaṃ niyukteyaṃ vanavāse manasvinī
translation: परमायस्ताः profoundly distressed, ज्वलिततेजसम् with burning lustre, रामम् to Rama, ऊचुश्च also said, वत्स dear child, मनस्विनी highminded, इयम् this Sita, एवम् thus, वनवासे to dwell in the forest, न नियुक्ता was not ordered.
explanation: Profoundly distressed, they said to Rama glowing with burning lustre O dear, no one has ordered this highminded Sita to dwell in the forest.

shloka_text: पितुर्वाक्यानुरोधेन गतस्य विजनं वनम्। तावद्दर्शनमस्या नः सफलं भवतु प्रभो।।2.37.17।।
transliteration: piturvākyānurodhena gatasya vijanaṃ vanam| tāvaddarśanamasyā naḥ saphalaṃ bhavatu prabho
translation: प्रभो  O lord, पितुः father's, वाक्यानुरोधेन in obedience to the words, विजनम् desolate, वनम् to the forest, गतस्य after you have left, तावत् till such time, नः for us, सफलम् fruitful, अस्याः her, दर्शनम् भवतु audience be available.
explanation: In obedience to the words of your father, O lord you are going to the forest. Till you return, please allow us to have her (Sita's) audience.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेन सहायेन वनं गच्छस्व पुत्रक। नेयमर्हति कल्याणी वस्तुं तापसवद्वने।।2.37.18।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇena sahāyena vanaṃ gacchasva putraka| neyamarhati kalyāṇī vastuṃ tāpasavadvane
translation: पुत्रक O son, सहायेन as companion, लक्ष्मणेन with Lakshmana, वनम् to the forest, गच्छस्व you may go, कल्याणी auspicious lady, इयम् she, तापसवत् like a hermit, वने in the forest, वस्तुम् to live, नार्हति is not worthy of.
explanation: Go, O son to the forest with Lakshmana as your companion. (But) this auspicious Sita, will not be able to live in the jungle like a hermit.

shloka_text: कुरु नो याचनां पुत्र सीता तिष्ठतु भामिनी। धर्मनित्यस्स्वयं स्थातुं न हीदानीं त्वमिच्छसि।।2.37.19।।
transliteration: kuru no yācanāṃ putra sītā tiṣṭhatu bhāminī| dharmanityassvayaṃ sthātuṃ na hīdānīṃ tvamicchasi
translation: पुत्र O son, न: our, याचनाम् prayer, कुरु you may accede, भामिनी lovely, सीता Sita, तिष्ठतु  remain here, धर्मनित्यः faithful to your duty, त्वम् you, स्वयम् on your own, स्थातुम् to remain, इदानीम् now, न इच्छसि हि do not desire.
explanation: Do accede to our prayer. Let lovely Sita stay with us as you, O son faithful to your duty, will not like to remain here.

shloka_text: तासामेवंविधा वाच शृण्वन् दशरथात्मजः। बबन्धैव तदा चीरं सीतया तुल्यशीलया।।2.37.20।।
transliteration: tāsāmevaṃvidhā vāca śṛṇvan daśarathātmajaḥ| babandhaiva tadā cīraṃ sītayā tulyaśīlayā
translation: दशरथात्मज: son of Dasaratha (Rama), तासाम् their, एवंविधाः such ways, वाचः words, शृण्वन् listening, तदा then, तुल्यशीलया similar in nature, सीतया by Sita, चीरम् bark robes, बबन्धैव got them fastened.
explanation: While Rama was listening to such words uttered by them, he got the bark robes fastened round Sita who was of similar nature.

shloka_text: चीरे गृहीते तु तया समीक्ष्य नृपतेर्गुरुः। निवार्य सीतां कैकेयीं वसिष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.37.21।।
transliteration: cīre gṛhīte tu tayā samīkṣya nṛpaterguruḥ| nivārya sītāṃ kaikeyīṃ vasiṣṭho vākyamabravīt
translation: तया by her, चीरे bark garment, गृहीते was worn, नृपतेः king's, गुरुः preceptor, वसिष्ठः Vasistha, समीक्ष्य having seen, सीताम् of Sita, निवार्य having restrained, कैकेयीम् to Kaikeyi, (वाक्यम्) अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: When Sita wore the bark garments, Vasistha, the king's preceptor who was watching this restrained her (Sita) and said to Kaikeyi:

shloka_text: अतिप्रवृत्ते दुर्मेधे कैकेयि कुलपांसनि। वञ्चयित्वा च राजानं न प्रमाणेऽवतिष्ठसे।।2.37.22।।
transliteration: atipravṛtte durmedhe kaikeyi kulapāṃsani| vañcayitvā ca rājānaṃ na pramāṇe'vatiṣṭhase
translation: अतिप्रवृत्ते exceeding all limits of decency, दुर्मेधे a woman of evil mind, कुलपांसनि disgrace to the race, कैकेयि Kaikeyi, राजानम् to king, वञ्चयित्वा च having deceived, प्रमाणे conforming to the standards (of righteousness ), न अवतिष्ठसे are you not abiding
explanation: . You are exceeding all limits of decency O Kaikeyi your motive is evil. You are a disgrace to the race You have deceived the king and your behaviour does not conform to the standards (of righteousness).

shloka_text: न गन्तव्यं वनं देव्या सीतया शीलवर्जिते। अनुष्ठास्यति रामस्य सीता प्रकृतमासनम्।।2.37.23।।
transliteration: na gantavyaṃ vanaṃ devyā sītayā śīlavarjite| anuṣṭhāsyati rāmasya sītā prakṛtamāsanam
translation: शीलवर्जिते  devoid of good conduct, देव्या by the divine, सीतया Sita, वनम् to the forest, न गन्तव्यम् need not go, सीता Sita, रामस्य Rama's, प्रकृतम् present, आसनम् royal throne, अनुष्ठास्यति she will occupy.
explanation: You are devoid of good conduct, O Kaikeyi Divine Sita need not go to the forest. Remaining here she should occupy the royal throne of Rama.

shloka_text: आत्मा हि दारास्सर्वेषां दारसङ्ग्रहवर्तिनाम्। आत्मेयमिति रामस्य पालयिष्यति मेदिनीम्।।2.37.24।।
transliteration: ātmā hi dārāssarveṣāṃ dārasaṅgrahavartinām| ātmeyamiti rāmasya pālayiṣyati medinīm
translation: दारसङ्ग्रहवर्तिनाम् of men who guard their wives, सर्वेषाम् for all, दाराः wife, आत्मा हि is the very soul, इयम् this Sita, रामस्य Rama's, आत्मा इति soul,  मेदिनीम् this earth, पालयिष्यति will rule.
explanation: For every householder, his wife is the soul. Since Sita is the soul of Rama, she can rule this earth.

shloka_text: अथ यास्यति वैदेही वनं रामेण सङ्गता। वयमप्यनुयास्यामः पुरं चेदं गमिष्यति।।2.37.25।।
transliteration: atha yāsyati vaidehī vanaṃ rāmeṇa saṅgatā| vayamapyanuyāsyāmaḥ puraṃ cedaṃ gamiṣyati
translation: अथ otherwise, वैदेही Sita, रामेण with Rama, सङ्गता united, वनम् to the forest, यास्यति if goes, वयमपि all of us also, अनुयास्यामः will follow, इदम् this, पुरं च city also, गमिष्यति will go.
explanation: Otherwise, if Sita goes with Rama to the forest, all of us along with the entire city will follow.

shloka_text: अन्तपालाश्च यास्यन्ति सदारो यत्र राघवः। सहोपजीव्यं राष्ट्रं च पुरं च सपरिच्छदम्।।2.37.26।।
transliteration: antapālāśca yāsyanti sadāro yatra rāghavaḥ| sahopajīvyaṃ rāṣṭraṃ ca puraṃ ca saparicchadam
translation: सदारः with his wife, राघवः descendant of the Raghus, यत्र where (lives), अन्तपालाश्च guardians of the harem, सहोपजीव्यम् living together with the patron, राष्ट्रं च the kingdom, सपरिच्छदम् along with the retinue, पुरं च the city, यास्यन्ति will go.
explanation: The guardians of the harem, its patron king Dasaratha with his retinue and, the people of this city will go wherever Rama lives with his wife.

shloka_text: भरतश्च सशत्रुघ्नश्चीरवासा वनेचरः। वने वसन्तं काकुत्स्थ मनुवत्स्यति पूर्वजम्।।2.37.27।।
transliteration: bharataśca saśatrughnaścīravāsā vanecaraḥ| vane vasantaṃ kākutstha manuvatsyati pūrvajam
translation: सशत्रुघ्नः Satrughna, भरतश्च also Bharata, चीरवासाः wearing bark robes, वनेचरः wandering in the forest, वने in the forest, वसन्तं living there, पूर्वजम् elder brother, काकुत्स्थम् Son of the Kakutstha (Rama), अनुवत्स्यति follow.
explanation: Wandering in the forest and wearing bark, Satrughna and Bharata will live in the company of their elder brother (Rama) in the jungle.

shloka_text: तत श्शून्यां गतजनां वसुधां पादपै स्सह। त्वमेका शाधि दुर्वृत्ता प्रजानामहिते स्थिता।।2.37.28।।
transliteration: tata śśūnyāṃ gatajanāṃ vasudhāṃ pādapai ssaha| tvamekā śādhi durvṛttā prajānāmahite sthitā
translation: प्रजानाम् people's, अहिते in doing harm, स्थिता intent upon, दुर्वृत्ता with vile behaviour, त्वम् एका you alone, ततः after that, गतजनाम् deserted by men, शून्याम् empty, वसुधाम् earth, पादपैः सह  along with trees, शाधि rule.
explanation: Intent upon doing harm to the people with your vile behaviour, you alone rule this kingdom full of trees and deserted by men.

shloka_text: न हि तद्भविता राष्ट्रं यत्र रामो न भूपतिः। तद्वनं भविता राष्ट्रं यत्र रामो निवत्स्यति।।2.37.29।।
transliteration: na hi tadbhavitā rāṣṭraṃ yatra rāmo na bhūpatiḥ| tadvanaṃ bhavitā rāṣṭraṃ yatra rāmo nivatsyati
translation: यत्र where, रामः Rama, भूपतिः king, न not, तत् there, राष्ट्रम् kingdom, न भविता हि is not indeed there, यत्र where, रामः Rama, निवत्स्यति he dwells, तत् वनम् that forest also, राष्ट्रम् kingdom, भविता will become.
explanation: That is not a kingdom where Rama does not rule. If Rama lives in the forest, that shall be  the kingdom.

shloka_text: न ह्यदत्तां महीं पित्रा भरतः शास्तुमर्हति। त्वयि वा पुत्रवद्वस्तुं यदि जातो महीपतेः।।2.37.30।।
transliteration: na hyadattāṃ mahīṃ pitrā bharataḥ śāstumarhati| tvayi vā putravadvastuṃ yadi jāto mahīpateḥ
translation: भरतः Bharata, महीपतेः of the king (Dasaratha), जात: यदि if born, पित्रा by father, अदत्ताम् not given, महीम् earth, शास्तुम् to rule, त्वयि in you, पुत्रवत् like a son, वस्तुं वा to live, न अर्हति is not fit.
explanation: If Bharata is truly born to the king, he will not rule the kingdom which has not been bestowed on him (wholeheartedly) by his father. Nor will he live like a son to you.

shloka_text: यद्यपि त्वं क्षितितलाद्गगनं चोत्पतिष्यसि। पितृर्वंशचरित्रज्ञः सोऽन्यथा न करिष्यति।।2.37.31।।
transliteration: yadyapi tvaṃ kṣititalādgaganaṃ cotpatiṣyasi| pitṛrvaṃśacaritrajñaḥ so'nyathā na kariṣyati
translation: त्वम् you, क्षितितलात् from the earth, गगनम् to the sky, उत्पतिष्यसि यद्यपि even if you can fly, पितुर्वंशचरित्रज्ञः knower of traditions of his father's dynasty, सः Bharata, अन्यथा otherwise, न करिष्यति will not act.
explanation: Even if you were to fly from earth to sky, Bharata who knows the traditions of his  father's dynasty, will not act otherwise.

shloka_text: तत्त्वया पुत्रगर्धिन्या पुत्रस्य कृतमप्रियम्। लोके हि स न विद्येत यो न राममनुव्रतः।।2.37.32।।
transliteration: tattvayā putragardhinyā putrasya kṛtamapriyam| loke hi sa na vidyeta yo na rāmamanuvrataḥ
translation: तत् therefore, पुत्रगर्धिन्या by a woman greedily guarding her son's interest, त्वया by you, पुत्रस्य of your son, अप्रियम् harm, कृतम् is done, लोके in this world, यः who, रामम् to Rama, अनुव्रतः follows, न not, सः he, न विद्येत हि will not be there.
explanation: Therefore, by greedily guarding your son's interest you are doing him harm. There is  none in this world who will not follow Rama.

shloka_text: द्रक्ष्यस्यद्यैव कैकेयी पशुव्यालमृगद्विजान्। गच्छतस्सह रामेण पादपांश्च तदुन्मुखान्।।2.37.33।।
transliteration: drakṣyasyadyaiva kaikeyī paśuvyālamṛgadvijān| gacchatassaha rāmeṇa pādapāṃśca tadunmukhān
translation: कैकेयी Kaikeyi, रामेण सह along with Rama, गच्छतः leaving, पशुव्यालमृगद्विजान् flocks of cattle, elephants, deer and birds, तदुन्मुखान् bending towards him, पादपांश्च trees also, अद्यैव today, द्रक्ष्यसि you will see.
explanation: Today  you shall see, O Kaikeyi, flocks of cattle, elephants, deer and birds following Rama, even the trees bending towards him.

shloka_text: अथोत्तमान्याभरणानि देवि देहि स्नुषायै व्यपनीय चीरम्। न चीरमस्याः प्रविधीयतेति न्यवारयत्तद्वसनं वसिष्टः।।2.37.34।।
transliteration: athottamānyābharaṇāni devi dehi snuṣāyai vyapanīya cīram| na cīramasyāḥ pravidhīyateti nyavārayattadvasanaṃ vasiṣṭaḥ
translation: अथ then, देवि Devi (Kaikeyi), चीरम् bark robes, व्यपनीय having removed, स्नुषायै your daughterinlaw, उत्तमानि precious, आभरणानि ornaments, देहि give, अस्याः her, चीरम् bark robes, न प्रविधीयत was not decided, इति thus, वसिष्ठः Vasistha, तत् that, वसनम् garment, न्यवारयत् prevented.
explanation: O Kaikeyi remove those bark robes and bestow on your daughterinlaw precious ornaments. She was not ordained to wear the bark. Vaisishta, saying so, prevented Sita from wearing that garment.

shloka_text: एकस्य रामस्य वने निवास स्त्वया वृतःकेकयराजपुत्री। विभूषितेयं प्रतिकर्मनित्या वसत्वरण्ये सह राघवेण।।2.37.35।।
transliteration: ekasya rāmasya vane nivāsa stvayā vṛtaḥkekayarājaputrī| vibhūṣiteyaṃ pratikarmanityā vasatvaraṇye saha rāghaveṇa
translation: केकयराजपुत्री O daughter of the king of Kekaya, त्वया by you, एकस्य रामस्य only for Rama, वने in the forest, निवासः dwell, वृतः is sought for, इयम् this Sita,  विभूषिता welladorned,  प्रतिकर्मनित्या engaged daily in decorating, राघवेण सह along with Rama, अरण्ये in the forest, वसतु shall live.
explanation: O Kaikeyi, you asked that Rama only should dwell in the forest (wearing bark robes). Therefore let Sita, adorn her body daily, while she  lives in the forest with Rama.

shloka_text: यानैश्च मुख्यैः परिचारकैश्च सुसंवृता गच्छतु राजपुत्री। वस्त्रैश्च सर्वैस्सहितैर्विधानै र्नेयं वृता ते वरसम्प्रदाने।।2.37.36।।
transliteration: yānaiśca mukhyaiḥ paricārakaiśca susaṃvṛtā gacchatu rājaputrī| vastraiśca sarvaissahitairvidhānai rneyaṃ vṛtā te varasampradāne
translation: राजपुत्री princess Sita, मुख्यैः with excellent, यानैश्च with chariots, परिचारकैश्च with attendants, सुसंवृता surrounded by, वस्त्रैश्च with garments, सर्वैः with everything, सहितैः together, विधानैः necessities, गच्छतु let go, ते your, वरसम्प्रदाने while seeking boons, इयम् this Sita, न वृता is not included.
explanation: Equipped with excellent chariots, attendants, garments, and all other needs let the princess (Sita) go. While seeking boons, you did not include Sita.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तथा जल्पति विप्रमुख्ये गुरौ नृपस्याप्रतिमप्रभावे। नैव स्म सीता विनिवृत्तभावा प्रियस्य भर्तुः प्रतिकारकामा।।2.37.37।।
transliteration: tasmiṃstathā jalpati vipramukhye gurau nṛpasyāpratimaprabhāve| naiva sma sītā vinivṛttabhāvā priyasya bhartuḥ pratikārakāmā
translation: नृपस्य king's, गुरौ preceptor, अप्रतिमप्रभावे possessing incomparable  power, विप्रमुख्ये foremost of brahmins, तस्मिन् that Vasistha, तथा in that way, जल्पति  speaking, सीता Sita, प्रियस्य beloved, भर्तुः husband, प्रतिकारकामा to serve him, विनिवृत्तभावा to swerve from her resolve, नैव स्म did not agree.
explanation: (Though) Vasistha, endowed with matchless power, the preceptor of the king and foremost among the brahmins thus expressed himself, Sita was not willing to swerve from her resolve in order to serve her beloved husband. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तत्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyseventh sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तस्यां चीरं वसानायां नाथवत्यामनाथवत्। प्रचुक्रोश जनस्सर्वो धिक्त्वां दशरथं त्विति।।2.38.1।।
transliteration: tasyāṃ cīraṃ vasānāyāṃ nāthavatyāmanāthavat| pracukrośa janassarvo dhiktvāṃ daśarathaṃ tviti
translation: नाथवत्याम् having her husband, तस्याम् that Sita, अनाथवत् like one without a support, चीरम् tattered (bark) garment, वसानायाम् while wearing, सर्वः जनः all the people, त्वाम् about you, धिक् इति 'fie on you', दशरथम् to Dasaratha, प्रचुक्रोश shouted.
explanation: Beholding Sita who was wearing a bark garment, like one without a support, though having a husband, all the people cried bitterly exclaiming O Dasaratha, fie on you.
comments: Rama prays his father to look after his mother with compassion and regard.

shloka_text: तेन तत्र प्रणादेन दुःखितस्स महीपतिः। चिच्छेद जीविते श्रद्धां धर्मे यशसि चात्मनः।।2.38.2।।
transliteration: tena tatra praṇādena duḥkhitassa mahīpatiḥ| ciccheda jīvite śraddhāṃ dharme yaśasi cātmanaḥ
translation: महीपतिः that Lord of the earth (king), तत्र there, तेन प्रणादेन by that shout, दुःखितः distressed, आत्मनः his own, जीविते in life, धर्मे in righteousness, श्रद्धाम् faith, चिच्छेद broke.
explanation: Hearing that tumult the distressed Dasaratha lost faith in his own life and in his righteousness.

shloka_text: स निःश्वस्योष्णमैक्ष्वाक स्तां भार्यामिदमब्रवीत्। कैकेयि कुशचीरेण न सीता गन्तुमर्हति।।2.38.3।।
transliteration: sa niḥśvasyoṣṇamaikṣvāka stāṃ bhāryāmidamabravīt| kaikeyi kuśacīreṇa na sītā gantumarhati
translation: सः ऐक्ष्वाकः that descendant of the Ikshvakus (Dasaratha), उष्णम् निःश्वस्य heaving hot sighs, भार्याम् to his wife (Kaikeyi), इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् he spoke, कैकेयी O Kaikeyi, सीता Sita, कुशचीरेण with kusa garment, गन्तुम् to go, नार्हति is not worthy of.
explanation: The descendant of the Ikshvakus (Dasaratha), heaving hot sighs, said to his wife O Kaikeyi, Sita does not deserve to go (to the forest) in garment of kusa grass.

shloka_text: सुकुमारी च बाला च सततं च सुखोचिता। नेयं वनस्य योग्येति सत्यमाह गुरुर्मम।।2.38.4।।
transliteration: sukumārī ca bālā ca satataṃ ca sukhocitā| neyaṃ vanasya yogyeti satyamāha gururmama
translation: सुकुमारी च delicate, बाला च young, सततम् always, सुखोचिता accustomed to comfort, इयम् she, वनस्य to dwell in the forest, न योग्या is not fit, इति thus, मम गुरुः my preceptor, सत्यम् truly, अह said.
explanation: Sita a delicate, young princess accustomed to comforts is not fit to dwell in the forest. This is what my preceptor has truly spoken.

shloka_text: इयं हि कस्यापकरोति किञ्चि त्तपस्विनी राजवरस्य कन्या। या चीरमासाद्य जनस्य मध्ये स्थिता विसंज्ञाश्रमणीव काचित्।।2.38.5।।
transliteration: iyaṃ hi kasyāpakaroti kiñci ttapasvinī rājavarasya kanyā| yā cīramāsādya janasya madhye sthitā visaṃjñāśramaṇīva kācit
translation: या (सा) Sita, चीरम् bark garment, आसाद्य having received, काचित् obscure one, श्रमणीव like a female ascetic, विसंज्ञा lost senses, जनस्य मध्ये amidst people, स्थिता standing, इयम् this,  राजवरस्य कन्या daughter of the greatest of kings (Janaka), तपस्विनी ascetic, कस्य to whom, किञ्चित् even little, अपकरोति has done harm?
explanation: Sita, daughter of Janaka, the greatest among kings, stands amidst people wearing bark garment like an ascetic with her senses switched off. To whom and what harm has she done?

shloka_text: चीराण्यपास्याज्जनकस्य कन्या नेयं प्रतिज्ञा मम दत्तपूर्वा। यथासुखं गच्छतु राजपुत्री वनं समग्रा सह सर्वरत्नैः।।2.38.6।।
transliteration: cīrāṇyapāsyājjanakasya kanyā neyaṃ pratijñā mama dattapūrvā| yathāsukhaṃ gacchatu rājaputrī vanaṃ samagrā saha sarvaratnaiḥ
translation: जनकस्य Janaka's, कन्या daughter, चीराणि bark garments, अपास्य taking off, आत् afterwards, इयम् this,  प्रतिज्ञा promise, मम to me, दत्तपूर्वा न not given earlier, राजपुत्री princess, सर्वरत्नैः सह together with jewels, समग्रा with all needs, वनम् to the forest, यथासुखम् happily, गच्छतु go.
explanation: Let the daughter of Janaka take off her bark garments. This is not the promise I had made to you earlier. Let the princess happily go to the forest adorned with all jewels and with all other necessities.

shloka_text: अजीवनार्हेण मया नृशंसा कृता प्रतिज्ञा नियमेन तावत्। तवया हि बाल्यात् प्रतिपन्नमेतत् तन्मां दहेद्वेणुमिवात्मपुष्पम्।।2.38.7।।
transliteration: ajīvanārheṇa mayā nṛśaṃsā kṛtā pratijñā niyamena tāvat| tavayā hi bālyāt pratipannametat tanmāṃ dahedveṇumivātmapuṣpam
translation: अजीवनार्हेण unfit to live, मया by me, नियमेन with a vow, नृशंसा cruel, प्रतिज्ञा promise, कृता तावत् has been made, बाल्यात् out of childishness (foolishness), त्वया by you, एतत् this, प्रतिपन्नं हि  was taken, तत् that one, वेणुम् bamboo, आत्मपुष्पम् इव like its own flowers, माम् me, दहेत् should burn.
explanation: By giving this cruel promise through importunity, I have rendered myself unfit to live. This promise was made as a child's play and it (now) destroys me like a bamboo destroyed by its own flowers.

shloka_text: रामेण यदि ते पापे किञ्चित्कृतमशोभनम्। अपकारः क इह ते वैदेह्या दर्शितोऽधमे।।2.38.8।।
transliteration: rāmeṇa yadi te pāpe kiñcitkṛtamaśobhanam| apakāraḥ ka iha te vaidehyā darśito'dhame
translation: पापे O sinful woman, अधमे O wretch, रामेण by Rama, ते to you, किञ्चित् even a little,  अशोभनम् unbecoming, कृतं यदि has been done, वैदेह्या Sita, इह here, ते to you, कः what, अपकारः offence, दर्शितः has been shown.
explanation: O sinful woman O wretch Rama might have done something unbecoming to you, but what offence has Sita committed?

shloka_text: मृगीवोत्फुल्लनयना मृदुशीला तपस्वीनी। अपकारं कमिह ते करोति जनकात्मजा।।2.38.9।।
transliteration: mṛgīvotphullanayanā mṛduśīlā tapasvīnī| apakāraṃ kamiha te karoti janakātmajā
translation: मृगीव like a doe, उत्फुल्लनयना largeeyed, मृदुशीला of gentle ways, तपस्विनी worthy of compassion, जनकात्मजा daughter of Janaka, इह here, ते to you, कम् अपकारम्  what offence done, करोति is doing?
explanation: What wrong has the daughter of Janaka largeeyed like a doe, so gentle and worthy of compassion done to you?

shloka_text: ननु पर्याप्त मेतत्ते पापे रामविवासनम्। किमेभिः कृपणैर्भूय: पातकैरपि ते कृतैः।।2.38.10।।
transliteration: nanu paryāpta metatte pāpe rāmavivāsanam| kimebhiḥ kṛpaṇairbhūya: pātakairapi te kṛtaiḥ
translation: पापे O wicked woman, एतत् this, रामविवासनम् the exile of Rama, ते to you, पर्याप्तं ननु is not enough, भूयः still, कृतैः by those committed, कृपणैः by the wretched, एभिः by these, पातकैरपि sins also, ते to you, किम् why?
explanation: Rama's exile, O wicked woman, is enough for you. What are you committing further heinous crimes for?

shloka_text: प्रतिज्ञातं मया तावत् त्वयोक्तं देवि शृण्वता। रामं यदभिषेकाय त्वमिहागतमब्रवीः।।2.38.11।।
transliteration: pratijñātaṃ mayā tāvat tvayoktaṃ devi śṛṇvatā| rāmaṃ yadabhiṣekāya tvamihāgatamabravīḥ
translation: देवि O Devi, अभिषेकाय for installation, इह here, आगतम् came, रामम् to Rama, त्वम् you,  अब्रवीः had spoken, त्वया by you, उक्तम् what has been said, शृण्वता being heard, मया by me, तावत् to that extent, प्रतिज्ञातम् has been promised.
explanation: I have heard you, O Devi speaking to Rama when he came here in connection with the coronation. I promised you to that extent only.

shloka_text: तत्त्वेतत्समतिक्रम्य निरयं गन्तुमिच्छसि। मैथिलीमपि या हि त्वमीक्षसे चीरवासिनीम्।।2.38.12।।
transliteration: tattvetatsamatikramya nirayaṃ gantumicchasi| maithilīmapi yā hi tvamīkṣase cīravāsinīm
translation: या त्वं such you, तत् एतत् all that, अतिक्रम्य having exceeded, मैथिलीं अपि even the princess of Mithila (Sita) also, चीरवासिनीं one wearing bark garment, ईक्षसे want to see, निरयं hell, गन्तुं to go, इच्छसि wish.
explanation: Having exceeded all that, you want to behold Sita in bark garment and thereby, wish for hell.

shloka_text: इतीव राजा विलपन्महात्मा शोकस्य नान्तं स ददर्श किञ्चित्। भृशातुरत्वाच्च पपात भूमौ तेनैव पुत्रव्यसनेन मग्नः।।2.38.13।।
transliteration: itīva rājā vilapanmahātmā śokasya nāntaṃ sa dadarśa kiñcit| bhṛśāturatvācca papāta bhūmau tenaiva putravyasanena magnaḥ
translation: महात्मा noble soul, सः राजा that king, इतीव thus, विलपन् while lamenting, शोकस्य grief's, किञ्चित् even a little, अन्तम् end, न ददर्श could not see, भृशातुरत्वाच्च deeply tormented, तेन  that, पुत्रव्यसनेन एव by separation from son only, मग्नः immersed, भूमौ on the ground,  पपात fell.
explanation: The king could not see any end to his lamentation. Immersed in the grief of separation from his son and deeply tormented, he fell down on the ground.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवन्तं पितरं रामस्सम्प्रस्थितो वनम्। अवाक्छिरसमासीनमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.38.14।।
transliteration: evaṃ bruvantaṃ pitaraṃ rāmassamprasthito vanam| avākchirasamāsīnamidaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: वनम् to the forest, सम्प्रस्थितः set out to forest, रामः Rama, एवम् in this way, ब्रुवन्तम्  speaking, अवाक्छिरसमम् with bowed head, आसीनम् sitting, पितरम् addressing his father, इदं वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Rama who was about to leave for the forest addressed his father who sat with his head bent once again:

shloka_text: यं धार्मिक कौशल्या मम माता यशस्विनी। वृद्धा चाक्षुद्रशीला च न च त्वां देव गर्हते।।2.38.15।।
transliteration: yaṃ dhārmika kauśalyā mama mātā yaśasvinī| vṛddhā cākṣudraśīlā ca na ca tvāṃ deva garhate
translation: धार्मिक O righteous one, देव O lord, यशस्विनी illustrious, मम माता my mother, इयम् कौशल्या Kausalya, वृद्धा aged, अक्षुद्रशीला च does not possess meanness of character, त्वाम् you, न च गर्हते does not reproach.
explanation: O righteous father O king my aged and illustrious mother, Kausalya possesses neither a mean character nor does she blame you.

shloka_text: मया विहीनां वरद प्रपन्नां शोकसागरम्। अदृष्टपूर्वव्यसनां भूयस्सम्मन्तुमर्हसि।।2.38.16।।
transliteration: mayā vihīnāṃ varada prapannāṃ śokasāgaram| adṛṣṭapūrvavyasanāṃ bhūyassammantumarhasi
translation: वरद O bestower of boons, मया with me, विहीनाम् separated, शोकसागरम् ocean of sorrow,  प्रपन्नाम् enter into, अदृष्टपूर्वव्यसनाम् experiencing such unforeseen suffering, भूयः in a greater measure, सम्मन्तुम् to care for her, अर्हसि should.
explanation: O bestower of boons,  separated from me and unaccustomed to suffering, she will be plunged into an unforeseen ocean of sorrow. You should pay her greater attention.

shloka_text: पुत्रशोकं यथा नर्च्छेत्त्वया पूज्येन पूजिता। मां हि सञ्चिन्तयन्ती सा त्वयि जीवेत्तपस्विनी।।2.38.17।।
transliteration: putraśokaṃ yathā narcchettvayā pūjyena pūjitā| māṃ hi sañcintayantī sā tvayi jīvettapasvinī
translation: तपस्विनी one who deserves compassion, सा she, माम् about me, सञ्चिन्तयन्ती while constantly thinking, पुत्रशोकम् grief on account of her son, यथा as, न इच्छेत् does not obtain, पूज्येन venerable, त्वया by you, पूजिता honoured, त्वयि in you, जीवेत् shall live.
explanation: Let her not grieve on account of her son. O venerable father, if she, who deserves compassion is honoured by you, she will live.

shloka_text: इमां महेंन्द्रोपम जातगर्धिनीं तथा विधातुं जननीं ममार्हसि। यथा वनस्थे मयि शोककर्शिता न जीवितं न्यस्य यमक्षयं व्रजेत्।।2.38.18।।
transliteration: imāṃ maheṃndropama jātagardhinīṃ tathā vidhātuṃ jananīṃ mamārhasi| yathā vanasthe mayi śokakarśitā na jīvitaṃ nyasya yamakṣayaṃ vrajet
translation: महेन्द्रोपम equal to Indra, मयि me, वनस्थे staying in the forest, शोककर्शिता emaciated by sorrow, जीवितम् life, न्यस्य having yielded, यथा how, यमक्षयम् abode of Yama, न व्रजेत् will not go, तथा in that way, जातगर्धिनीम् a woman with a possesive feeling,   इमाम् this, मम जननीम् my mother, विधातुम् अर्हसि should do.
explanation: You are powerful like Indra.You should act accordingly so that my mother who has a possesive feeling towards her son should not, due to emaciation go to the abode of Yama after my departure for the forest. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टत्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyeighth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: रामस्य तु वचः शृत्वा मुनिवेशधरं च तम्। समीक्ष्य सह भार्याभी राजा विगतचेतनः।।2.39.1।। नैनं दुःखेन सन्तप्तः प्रत्यवैक्षत राघवम्। न चैनमभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य प्रत्यभाषत दुर्मनाः।।2.39.2।।
transliteration: rāmasya tu vacaḥ śṛtvā muniveśadharaṃ ca tam| samīkṣya saha bhāryābhī rājā vigatacetanaḥ nainaṃ duḥkhena santaptaḥ pratyavaikṣata rāghavam| na cainamabhisamprekṣya pratyabhāṣata durmanāḥ
translation: भार्याभिः सह with his wives, राजा king, रामस्य Rama's, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, मुनिवेशधरम् dressed like an ascetic, तम् him, समीक्ष्य च beholding, विगतचेतन unconscious, दुःखेन with grief, सन्तप्तः tormented, एनम् this, राघवम् Rama, न प्रत्यवैक्षत could not look at, दुर्मनाः dejected mind, एनम् him, अभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य having looked at,  न प्रत्यभाषत च did not reply.
explanation: After hearing  Rama and beholding him in the robes of  an ascetic, Dasaratha and his wives fell unconscious. With his body and mind afflicted with grief, Dasaratha could not look Rama in the face nor could he make a reply.
comments: Lamentations of Dasaratha--Sumantra fetches the chariot at the command of the king treasury officer gives valuable ornaments and garments to Sita--Kausalya instructs Sita on the obligations of a wife towards her husband-- Rama seeks leave of his other mothers.

shloka_text: रामस्य तु वचः शृत्वा मुनिवेशधरं च तम्। समीक्ष्य सह भार्याभी राजा विगतचेतनः।।2.39.1।। नैनं दुःखेन सन्तप्तः प्रत्यवैक्षत राघवम्। न चैनमभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य प्रत्यभाषत दुर्मनाः।।2.39.2।।
transliteration: rāmasya tu vacaḥ śṛtvā muniveśadharaṃ ca tam| samīkṣya saha bhāryābhī rājā vigatacetanaḥ nainaṃ duḥkhena santaptaḥ pratyavaikṣata rāghavam| na cainamabhisamprekṣya pratyabhāṣata durmanāḥ
translation: भार्याभिः सह with his wives, राजा king, रामस्य Rama's, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, मुनिवेशधरम् dressed like an ascetic, तम् him, समीक्ष्य च beholding, विगतचेतन unconscious, दुःखेन with grief, सन्तप्तः tormented, एनम् this, राघवम् Rama, न प्रत्यवैक्षत could not look at, दुर्मनाः dejected mind, एनम् him, अभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य having looked at,  न प्रत्यभाषत च did not reply.
explanation: After hearing  Rama and beholding him in the robes of  an ascetic, Dasaratha and his wives fell unconscious. With his body and mind afflicted with grief, Dasaratha could not look Rama in the face nor could he make a reply.

shloka_text: स मुहूर्तमिवासंज्ञो दुःखितश्च महीपतिः। विललाप महाबाहू राममेवानुचिन्तयन्।।2.39.3।।
transliteration: sa muhūrtamivāsaṃjño duḥkhitaśca mahīpatiḥ| vilalāpa mahābāhū rāmamevānucintayan
translation: महाबाहुः mightyarmed, सः महीपतिः that Lord of the world (king), मुहूर्तम् for a moment, असंज्ञः इव almost unconscious, दुःखितश्च grieved, रामम् एव Rama alone, अनुचिन्तयन् while  brooding, विललाप lamented.
explanation: The mightyarmed king lost consciousness for a moment and in grief lamented, brooding only over Rama.

shloka_text: मन्ये खलु मया पूर्वं विवत्सा बहवःकृताः। प्राणिनो हिंसिता वापि तस्मादिदमुपस्थितम्।।2.39.4।।
transliteration: manye khalu mayā pūrvaṃ vivatsā bahavaḥkṛtāḥ| prāṇino hiṃsitā vāpi tasmādidamupasthitam
translation: मया by me, पूर्वम् in the past, बहवः many, विवत्साः deprived of children, कृताः have been reduced, वापि or, प्राणिनः living beings, हिंसिताः are harmed, तस्मात् therefore, इदम् this, उपस्थितम् has befallen, मन्ये खलु I deem.
explanation: 'In the past I must have separated many from their children or harmed many living beings. That is why I think this calamity has befallen me.

shloka_text: न त्वेवानागते काले देहाच्च्यवति जीवितम्। कैकेय्या क्लिश्यमानस्य मृत्युर्मम न विद्यते।।2.39.5।। योऽहं पावकसङ्काशं पश्यामि पुरतः स्थितम्। विहाय वसने सूक्ष्मे तापसाच्छादमात्मजम्।।2.39.6।।
transliteration: na tvevānāgate kāle dehāccyavati jīvitam| kaikeyyā kliśyamānasya mṛtyurmama na vidyate yo'haṃ pāvakasaṅkāśaṃ paśyāmi purataḥ sthitam| vihāya vasane sūkṣme tāpasācchādamātmajam
translation: काले when the time, अनागते has not come yet, देहात् from body, जीवितम् life, न च्यवति  does not leave, यः अहम् such as I am, सूक्ष्मे fine, वसने clothes, विहाय having removed, तापसाच्छादम् wearing the robes of an ascetic, पावकसङ्काशम् like fire, आत्मजम् son, पुरतः स्थितम् standing before me, पश्यामि I, कैकेय्या by Kaikeyi, क्लिश्यमानस्य while being tormented, मम to me, मृत्युः death, न विद्यते does not come.
explanation: Unless the destined hour arrives, life does not leave the body. Therefore, even though I am tormented by Kaikeyi and even after seeing my son, standing before me, (bright) like fire, taking off his fine clothes and wearing the robes of an ascetic my end does not come.

shloka_text: न त्वेवानागते काले देहाच्च्यवति जीवितम्। कैकेय्या क्लिश्यमानस्य मृत्युर्मम न विद्यते।।2.39.5।। योऽहं पावकसङ्काशं पश्यामि पुरतः स्थितम्। विहाय वसने सूक्ष्मे तापसाच्छादमात्मजम्।।2.39.6।।
transliteration: na tvevānāgate kāle dehāccyavati jīvitam| kaikeyyā kliśyamānasya mṛtyurmama na vidyate yo'haṃ pāvakasaṅkāśaṃ paśyāmi purataḥ sthitam| vihāya vasane sūkṣme tāpasācchādamātmajam
translation: काले when the time, अनागते has not come yet, देहात् from body, जीवितम् life, न च्यवति  does not leave, यः अहम् such as I am, सूक्ष्मे fine, वसने clothes, विहाय having removed, तापसाच्छादम् wearing the robes of an ascetic, पावकसङ्काशम् like fire, आत्मजम् son, पुरतः स्थितम् standing before me, पश्यामि I, कैकेय्या by Kaikeyi, क्लिश्यमानस्य while being tormented, मम to me, मृत्युः death, न विद्यते does not come.
explanation: Unless the destined hour arrives, life does not leave the body. Therefore, even though I am tormented by Kaikeyi and even after seeing my son, standing before me, (bright) like fire, taking off his fine clothes and wearing the robes of an ascetic my end does not come.

shloka_text: एकस्याः खलु कैकेय्याः कृतेऽयं क्लिश्यते जनः। स्वार्थे प्रयतमानायाः संश्रित्य निकृतिं त्विमाम्।।2.39.7।।
transliteration: ekasyāḥ khalu kaikeyyāḥ kṛte'yaṃ kliśyate janaḥ| svārthe prayatamānāyāḥ saṃśritya nikṛtiṃ tvimām
translation: इमाम् this, निकृतिम् deception, संश्रित्य resorting to, स्वार्थे for selfish ends, प्रयतमानायाः in pursuit of, एकस्याः only one, कैकेय्याः कृतेः for Kaikeyi, अयं जनः these people, क्लिश्यते are suffering.
explanation: Only because of Kaikeyi  who resorted to this deception in pursuit of selfish ends so many people are made to suffer.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु वचनं बाष्पेण पिहितेन्द्रियः। रामेति सकृदेवोक्त्वा व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह।।2.39.8।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu vacanaṃ bāṣpeṇa pihitendriyaḥ| rāmeti sakṛdevoktvā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha
translation: एवम् in this manner, वचनम् words, उक्त्वा having uttered, बाष्पेण with tears, पिहितेन्द्रियः with  blurred vision, रामेति saying 'O Rama', सकृदेव only once, उक्त्वा having said, व्याहर्तुम् to speak, न शशाक ह was not able.
explanation: Having uttered these words and muttering, 'O Rama' only once, his vision blurred by tears, he could speak no more.

shloka_text: संज्ञां तु प्रतिलभ्यैव मुहूर्तात्स महीपतिः। नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां सुमन्त्रमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.39.9।।
transliteration: saṃjñāṃ tu pratilabhyaiva muhūrtātsa mahīpatiḥ| netrābhyāmaśrupūrṇābhyāṃ sumantramidamabravīt
translation: सः महीपतिः that Lord of the world (king), मुहूर्तात् after a moment, संज्ञाम् senses, प्रतिलभ्यैव having regained, अश्रुपूर्णाभ्याम् filled with tears, नेत्राभ्याम् with eyes, सुमन्त्रम् to Sumanatra, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Regaining his senses in a moment, the king, with eyes filled with tears, said to Sumantra:

shloka_text: औपवाह्यं रथं युक्त्वा त्वमायाहि हयोत्तमैः। प्रापयैनं महाभागमितो जनपदात्परम्।।2.39.10।।
transliteration: aupavāhyaṃ rathaṃ yuktvā tvamāyāhi hayottamaiḥ| prāpayainaṃ mahābhāgamito janapadātparam
translation: त्वम् you, औपवाह्यम् suitable for the journey, रथम् chariot, हयोत्तमैः with finest horses, युक्त्वा having harnessed, आयाहि you shall come, एनम् this, महाभागम् magnanimous, इतः from here, जनपदात् this city, परम् place situated outside, प्रापय reach.
explanation: Harness the finest horses to the chariot suitable for the journey, drive this magnanimous Rama to a place outside the city, and come back.

shloka_text: एवं मन्ये गुणवतां गुणानां फलमुच्यते। पित्रा मात्रा च यत्साधुर्वीरो निर्वास्यते वनम्।।2.39.11।।
transliteration: evaṃ manye guṇavatāṃ guṇānāṃ phalamucyate| pitrā mātrā ca yatsādhurvīro nirvāsyate vanam
translation: गुणवताम् of virtuous men, गुणानाम् of virtues, फलम् reward, एवम् this only, उच्यते is said, मन्ये I think, यत् since, साधुः pious man, वीरः heroic, पित्रा by father, मात्रा च by mother, वनम् to the forest, निर्वास्यते is being banished.
explanation: That the pious and heroic son is banished by his parents to the forest is, I think, the reward to the virtuous for his virtues.

shloka_text: राज्ञो वचनमाज्ञाय सुमन्त्रः शीघ्रविक्रमः। योजयित्वाऽययौ तत्र रथमश्वैरलङ्कृतम्।।2.39.12।।
transliteration: rājño vacanamājñāya sumantraḥ śīghravikramaḥ| yojayitvā'yayau tatra rathamaśvairalaṅkṛtam
translation: राज्ञः the king's, वचनम् words, आज्ञाय having known, सुमन्त्रः Sumantra, शीघ्रविक्रमः of swift steps, अलङ्कृतम् decorated, रथम् chariot, अश्वैः with horses, योजयित्वा yoked, तत्र there, आययौ came.
explanation: In obedience to the words of the king, Sumantra promptly harnessed the horses to a welldecorated chariot and brought it there.

shloka_text: तं रथं राजपुत्राय सूत: कनकभूषितम्। आचचक्षेऽञ्जलिं कृत्वा युक्तं परमवाजिभिः।।2.39.13।।
transliteration: taṃ rathaṃ rājaputrāya sūta: kanakabhūṣitam| ācacakṣe'ñjaliṃ kṛtvā yuktaṃ paramavājibhiḥ
translation: सूतः the charioteer (Sumantra), अञ्जलिं कृत्वा with folded palms, राजपुत्राय the king's son, कनकभूषितम् decked in gold, परमवाजिभिः with excellent horses, युक्तम् harnessed, तं रथम् that chariot, आचचक्षे informed.
explanation: With folded palms Sumantra informed the prince that a chariot, decked in gold and harnessed with excellent horses, is ready.

shloka_text: राजा सत्वरमाहूय व्यापृतं वित्तसंञ्चये। उवाच देशकालज्ञो निश्चितं सर्वत श्शुचिम्।।2.39.14।।
transliteration: rājā satvaramāhūya vyāpṛtaṃ vittasaṃñcaye| uvāca deśakālajño niścitaṃ sarvata śśucim
translation: राजा the king, देशकालज्ञो aware of (the right) place and time, निश्चितम् firm, सर्वतः in every way, शुचिम् honest, वित्तसञ्चये in the treasury, व्यापृतम् working as officer, सत्वरम् hurriedly, आहूय having summoned, उवाच said.
explanation: The king who was aware of the right place and time summoned hurriedly the treaury officer, who was firm and honest and said to him:

shloka_text: वासांसि च महार्हाणि भूषणानि वराणि च। वर्षाण्येतानि सङ्ख्याय वैदेह्याः क्षिप्रमानय।।2.39.15।।
transliteration: vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi ca| varṣāṇyetāni saṅkhyāya vaidehyāḥ kṣipramānaya
translation: एतानि these, वर्षाणि years, सङ्ख्याय calculating, वैदेह्याः for the princess of Videha (Sita), महार्हाणि highly valuable, वासांसि च garments, वराणि excellent, भूषणानि च ornaments, क्षिप्रम् quickly, आनय fetch.
explanation: Assess the (needs for) number of years the princess of Videha (Sita) is going to be in the forest, and fetch her quickly highly valuable garments and excellent ornaments.

shloka_text: नरेन्द्रेणैवमुक्तस्तु गत्वा कोशगृहं ततः। प्रायच्छत्सर्वमाहृत्य सीतायै सममेव तत्।।2.39.16।।
transliteration: narendreṇaivamuktastu gatvā kośagṛhaṃ tataḥ| prāyacchatsarvamāhṛtya sītāyai samameva tat
translation: नरेन्द्रेण by the king, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken to, ततः then, कोशगृहम् to the treasury, गत्वा having gone, सर्वम् all those things, आहृत्य having brought, तत् that, सममेव wholly, सीतायै for Sita, प्रायच्छत् gave.
explanation: Ordered thus by the king, the officer went to the treasury, collected all the things and presented them to Sita.

shloka_text: सा सुजाता सुजातानि वैदेही प्रस्थिता वनम्। भूषयामास गात्राणि तैर्विचित्रैर्विभूषणैः।।2.39.17।।
transliteration: sā sujātā sujātāni vaidehī prasthitā vanam| bhūṣayāmāsa gātrāṇi tairvicitrairvibhūṣaṇaiḥ
translation: वनम् to the forest, प्रस्थिता ready to depart, सुजाता of noble birth, सा वैदेहि that princess from Videha (Sita), सुजातानि beautiful, गात्राणि limbs, विचित्रैः sparkling, तैः विभूषणैः those ornaments, भूषयामास adorned.
explanation: That princess of noble birth from Videha adorned her beautiful limbs with the sparkling ornaments and got ready to depart for the forest.

shloka_text: व्यराजयत वैदेही वेश्म तत्सुविभूषिता। उद्यतोंऽशुमतः काले खं प्रभेव विवस्वतः।।2.39.18।।
transliteration: vyarājayata vaidehī veśma tatsuvibhūṣitā| udyatoṃ'śumataḥ kāle khaṃ prabheva vivasvataḥ
translation: सुविभूषिता well adorned, वैदेही Sita, तत् वेश्म that palace, काले at dawn, उद्यतः rising, विवस्वतः Sun's, प्रभा light, खमिव like sky, व्यराजयत got illumined.
explanation: Welladorned Sita illumined the palace like the rising Sun lighting up the sky at dawn.

shloka_text: तां भुजाभ्यां परिष्वज्य श्वश्रूर्वचनमब्रवीत्। अनाचरन्ती कृपणं मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय मैथिलीम्।।2.39.19।।
transliteration: tāṃ bhujābhyāṃ pariṣvajya śvaśrūrvacanamabravīt| anācarantī kṛpaṇaṃ mūrdhnyupāghrāya maithilīm
translation: श्वश्रूः motherinlaw ( Kausalya), कृपणम् compassionately, अनाचरन्तीम् not acting, तां मैथिलीम् that princess from Mithila (Sita), भुजाभ्याम् with arms, परिष्वज्य having embraced, मूर्ध्नि on the forehead, उपाघ्राय after kissing, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Kausalya, Sita's motherinlaw, took her in her arms, embraced her, kissed her on the forehead, and said to her who conducted herself without evoking any pity.

shloka_text: असत्य स्सर्वलोकेऽस्मिन्सततं सत्कृताः प्रियैः। भर्तारं नानुमन्यन्ते विनिपातगतं स्त्रियः।।2.39.20।।
transliteration: asatya ssarvaloke'sminsatataṃ satkṛtāḥ priyaiḥ| bhartāraṃ nānumanyante vinipātagataṃ striyaḥ
translation: अस्मिन् in this, सर्वलोके in all the worlds, असत्यः untrue, स्त्रियः women, प्रियैः by husbands, सततम् at all times, सत्कृताः though honoured, विनिपातगतम् fallen into misfortunes, भर्तारम् husband, नानुमन्यन्ते do not agree (follow).
explanation: Those women who, although always gratified, do not follow their husband when they fall into misfortune, are regarded as unfaithful.

shloka_text: एष स्वभावो नारीणामनुभूय पुरा सुखम्। अल्पामप्यापदं प्राप्य दुष्यन्ति प्रजहत्यपि।।2.39.21।।
transliteration: eṣa svabhāvo nārīṇāmanubhūya purā sukham| alpāmapyāpadaṃ prāpya duṣyanti prajahatyapi
translation: पुरा earlier, सुखम् pleasures, अनुभूय having enjoyed, अल्पामपि though in small measure, आपदम् trouble, प्राप्य having obtained, दुष्यन्ति censure them, प्रजहत्यपि or even abandon them, एषः this, नारीणाम् women's, स्वभावः nature.
explanation: Though they have enjoyed all pleasures (with their husbands) earlier, they censure them in the wake of the slightest trouble or even abandon them. This is the nature of women.

shloka_text: असत्यशीला विकृता दुर्ग्राह्यहृदयास्सदा। युवत्यः पापसंङ्कल्पाः क्षणमात्राद्विरागिणः।।2.39.22।।
transliteration: asatyaśīlā vikṛtā durgrāhyahṛdayāssadā| yuvatyaḥ pāpasaṃṅkalpāḥ kṣaṇamātrādvirāgiṇaḥ
translation: पापसङ्कल्पाः evilminded, युवत्यः young ladies, असत्यशीलाः infidel, विकृताः perverted ones, तथा also, दुर्ग्राह्यहृदयाः hard to read their hearts, क्षणमात्रात् in an instant, विरागिणः are devoid of affection.
explanation: Evilminded young ladies are infidels. They are of perverted nature. They are inscrutable. In an instant they lose their love (for their husbands).

shloka_text: न कुलं न कृतं विद्या न दत्तं नापि सङ्ग्रहः। स्त्रीणां गृह्णाति हृदयमनित्यहृदया हि ताः।।2.39.23।।
transliteration: na kulaṃ na kṛtaṃ vidyā na dattaṃ nāpi saṅgrahaḥ| strīṇāṃ gṛhṇāti hṛdayamanityahṛdayā hi tāḥ
translation: स्त्रीणाम् women's, हृदयम् heart, कुलम् family tradition, न गृह्णाति does not attract, कृतम् benefit received, न not, विद्या education, दत्तम् gifts, न not, सङ्ग्रहः अपि not even accumulated wealth, न not, ताः those, अनित्यहृदयाः हि unstable minds indeed.
explanation: Neither family traditions nor benefits received, nor education nor affection nor gifts nor even accumulated wealth attract women's hearts. Their minds are unstable indeed.

shloka_text: साध्वीनां हि स्थितानां तु शीले सत्ये श्रुते शमे। स्त्रीणां पवित्रं परमं पतिरेको विशिष्यते।।2.39.24।।
transliteration: sādhvīnāṃ hi sthitānāṃ tu śīle satye śrute śame| strīṇāṃ pavitraṃ paramaṃ patireko viśiṣyate
translation: तु but, शीले in chastity, सत्ये in truth, श्रुते in scriptures, शमे in stability, स्थितानाम्  remaining fixed, साध्वीनाम् of virtuous ones, स्त्रीणाम् women, एकः only, पतिः husband, परमम् supreme, पवित्रम् as holy, विशिष्यते is distinguished.
explanation: But for those virtuous women whose minds are fixed in chastity, truth, scriptures and stability, the husband occupies a distinguished place and is considered supremely holy.

shloka_text: स त्वया नावमन्तव्यः पुत्रः प्रव्राजितो मम। तव दैवतमस्त्वेष निर्धनः सधनोऽपि वा।।2.39.25।।
transliteration: sa tvayā nāvamantavyaḥ putraḥ pravrājito mama| tava daivatamastveṣa nirdhanaḥ sadhano'pi vā
translation: प्रव्राजितः exiled, मम my, सः पुत्रः son, त्वया by you, नावमन्तव्यः is not to be underestimated, निर्धनः without wealth, सधनोऽपि वा or with wealth, एषः he, तव your, दैवम् अस्तु be your god.
explanation: You must not underestimate my son in his exile. You must treat him as your god whether he is wealthy or not.

shloka_text: विज्ञाय वचनं सीता तस्या धर्मार्थसंहितम्। कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेदं श्वश्रूमभिमुखे स्थिताम्।।2.39.26।।
transliteration: vijñāya vacanaṃ sītā tasyā dharmārthasaṃhitam| kṛtāñjaliruvācedaṃ śvaśrūmabhimukhe sthitām
translation: सीता Sita, तस्याः her, धर्मार्थसंहितम् in conformity with dharma and artha, वचनम् words, विज्ञाय having understood, कृताञ्जलिः with folded palms, अभिमुखे facing her, स्थिताम् standing, श्वश्रूम् to her motherinlaw, इदम् this word, उवाच said.
explanation: Sita who understood the import of these words which were in conformity with dharma and artha, repiled to her motherinlaw facing her with folded palms:

shloka_text: करिष्ये सर्वमेवाहमार्या यदनुशास्ति माम्। अभिज्ञास्मि यथा भर्तुर्वर्तितव्यं श्रुतं च मे।।2.39.27।।
transliteration: kariṣye sarvamevāhamāryā yadanuśāsti mām| abhijñāsmi yathā bharturvartitavyaṃ śrutaṃ ca me
translation: आर्या venerable one, यथा as, माम् me, अनुशास्ति instructing, सर्वमेव all that, अहम् I, करिष्ये shall do, भर्तुः in relation to my husband, यथा how, वर्तितव्यम् should conduct myself, अभिज्ञा अस्मि I am aware, मे श्रुतं च I have heard it earlier.
explanation: I shall do exactly all that the venerable motherinlaw instructs me. I have heard it earlier and have fully understood as to how I should conduct myself towards my husband.

shloka_text: न मामसज्जनेनार्या समानयितुमर्हति। धर्माद्विचलितुं नाहमलं चन्द्रादिव प्रभा।।2.39.28।।
transliteration: na māmasajjanenāryā samānayitumarhati| dharmādvicalituṃ nāhamalaṃ candrādiva prabhā
translation: आर्या the worshipful lady, माम् me, असज्जनेन with wicked people, समानयितुम् to equate, न अर्हति not fit for, अहम् I, प्रभा radiance, चन्द्रादिव like from the Moon, धर्मात् from virtue, विचलितुम् to swerve, नालम् I cannot.
explanation: My worshipful motherinlaw should not equate me with wicked people (women). I cannot swerve from the path of virtue like radiance which never leaves the Moon.

shloka_text: नातन्त्री वाद्यते वीणा नाचक्रो वर्तते रथः। नापतिस्सुखमेधेत या स्यादपि शतात्मजा।।2.39.29।।
transliteration: nātantrī vādyate vīṇā nācakro vartate rathaḥ| nāpatissukhamedheta yā syādapi śatātmajā
translation: अतन्त्री without strings, वीणा veena (lute), न वाद्यते cannot be played, अचक्रः without wheels, रथ: a chariot, न वर्तते does not move, अपतिः without husband, शतात्मजा a hundred sons, स्यादपि even if she has, सुखम् happiness, न एधेत one does not flourish.
explanation: A veena (lute) sans strings cannot be played. A chariot without wheels cannot move. Similarly, a woman without her husband finds no  happiness even though she has one hundred sons.

shloka_text: मितं ददाति हि पिता मितं माता मितं सुतः। अमितस्य हि दातारं भर्तारं का न पूजयेत्।।2.39.30।।
transliteration: mitaṃ dadāti hi pitā mitaṃ mātā mitaṃ sutaḥ| amitasya hi dātāraṃ bhartāraṃ kā na pūjayet
translation: पिता father, मितम् to a limited extent, ददाति हि gives, माता mother, सुतः son, अमितस्य unlimited extent, दातारम् giver, भर्तारम् husband, न पूजयेत् who will not worship?
explanation: While the happiness that the father, mother and son give is limited, a husband gives unlimited happiness. Which wife will not worship such a husband?

shloka_text: साहमेवं गता श्रेष्ठा श्रुतधर्मपरावरा। आर्ये किमवमन्येऽहं स्त्रीणां भर्ता हि दैवतम्।।2.39.31।।
transliteration: sāhamevaṃ gatā śreṣṭhā śrutadharmaparāvarā| ārye kimavamanye'haṃ strīṇāṃ bhartā hi daivatam
translation: आर्ये O exalted lady, एवं गता one with these (ideals), श्रेष्ठा an eminent woman, श्रुतधर्मपरावरा having been instructed in ordinary and special obligations, सा अहम् I, किम् why, अवमन्येयम् understimate him, स्त्रीणाम् for women, भर्ता husband, दैवतं हि is god indeed.
explanation: Instructed about my obligations by an eminent lady (her mother?), imbued with these ideals, how can I, O exalted one, underestimate him (my husband)? For a woman the husband is a god indeed

shloka_text: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा कौशल्या हृदयङ्गमम्। शुद्धसत्त्वा मुमोचाश्रु सहसा दुःखहर्षजम्।।2.39.32।।
transliteration: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā kauśalyā hṛdayaṅgamam| śuddhasattvā mumocāśru sahasā duḥkhaharṣajam
translation: कौशल्या Kausalya, हृदयङ्गमम् heartstirring, सीतायाः Sita's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, शुद्धसत्त्वा with purified mind, सहसा instantaneously, दुःखहर्षजम् produced out of joy and grief, अश्रु tears, मुमोच shed.
explanation: Listening to the heartstirring words of Sita, Kausalya with her heart so pure burst instantaneously into tears of joy and grief.

shloka_text: तां प्राञ्जलिरभिक्रम्य मातृमध्येऽतिसत्कृताम्। रामः परमधर्मात्मा मातरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.39.33।।
transliteration: tāṃ prāñjalirabhikramya mātṛmadhye'tisatkṛtām| rāmaḥ paramadharmātmā mātaraṃ vākyamabravīt
translation: परमधर्मात्मा extremely virtuous, रामः Rama, मातृमध्ये in the midst of his mothers, अतिसत्कृताम् highly revered lady, ताम् that, मातरम् to mother (Kausalya), प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, अभिक्रम्य having approached, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Most virtuous Rama approached his mother, that highly revered lady among all his mothers, and with folded hands said:

shloka_text: अम्ब मा दुःखिता भूस्त्वं पश्य त्वं पितरं मम।। क्षयो हि वनवासस्य क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति।।2.39.34।।
transliteration: amba mā duḥkhitā bhūstvaṃ paśya tvaṃ pitaraṃ mama|| kṣayo hi vanavāsasya kṣiprameva bhaviṣyati
translation: अम्ब O mother, त्वम् you, दुःखिता मा भूः do not grieve, त्वम् you, मम पितरम् my father, पश्य look after, वनवासस्य of my exile in the forest, क्षयः end, क्षिप्रमेव quickly, भविष्यति will come.
explanation: O mother, do not grieve. Look after my father. My stay in the forest will soon come to an end.

shloka_text: सुप्तायास्ते गमिष्यन्ति नव वर्षाणि पञ्च च। सा समग्रमिह प्राप्तं मां द्रक्ष्यसि सुहृद्वृतम्।।2.39.35।।
transliteration: suptāyāste gamiṣyanti nava varṣāṇi pañca ca| sā samagramiha prāptaṃ māṃ drakṣyasi suhṛdvṛtam
translation: ते you, सुप्तायाः while asleep, नव पञ्च च nine plus five (fourteen), वर्षाणि years, गमिष्यन्ति will pass off, सा you, इह here, (सम्) प्राप्तम् have arrived, सुहृद्वृतम् surrounded by my friends, समग्रम्  completely, माम् me, द्रक्ष्यसि will see.
explanation: Fourteen years will pass off like a night's sleep. You will see me come home safe and sound, surrounded by my friends.

shloka_text: एतावदभिनीतार्थमुक्त्वा स जननीं वचः। त्रयश्शतशतार्धाश्च ददर्शा वेक्ष्य मातरः।।2.39.36।।
transliteration: etāvadabhinītārthamuktvā sa jananīṃ vacaḥ| trayaśśataśatārdhāśca dadarśā vekṣya mātaraḥ
translation: सः he, अभिनीतार्थम् with highly polished meaning, एतावत् up to this extent, वचः words, उक्त्वा  having spoken, आवेक्ष्य after looking at them, त्रयः three, त्रयश्शतशतार्धा: three hundred and fifty, मातरः च mothers, ददर्श he saw.
explanation: Speaking thus to his mother with highly polished words, he then turned his gaze at his other three hundred and fifty mothers.

shloka_text: ता श्चापि स तथैवार्ता मातृ़र्दशरथात्मजः। धर्मयुक्तमिदं वाक्यं निजगाद कृताञ्जलिः।।2.39.37।।
transliteration: tā ścāpi sa tathaivārtā mātṛ़rdaśarathātmajaḥ| dharmayuktamidaṃ vākyaṃ nijagāda kṛtāñjaliḥ
translation: सः that, दशरथात्मजः Son of Dasaratha (Rama), तथैव similarly, आर्ताः distressed, ताः those, मातृरपि mothers also, कृताञ्जलिः with folded palms, धर्मयुक्तम् steeped in virtue, इदं वाक्यम् these words, निजगाद uttered.
explanation: To all the mothers who stood deeply distressed with grief the son of Dasaratha spoke with folded hands these words suffused with virtue:

shloka_text: संवासात्परुषं किञ्चिदज्ञानाद्वापि यत्कृतम्। तन्मे समनुजानीत सर्वाश्चामन्त्रयामि वः।।2.39.38।।
transliteration: saṃvāsātparuṣaṃ kiñcidajñānādvāpi yatkṛtam| tanme samanujānīta sarvāścāmantrayāmi vaḥ
translation: संवासात् by virtue of our living together, अज्ञानाद्वा or through ignorance, किञ्चित् even a little, यत् any, परुषम् harsh gesture, कृतम् has been done, मे to me, तत् that, समनुजानीत forgive, वः you, सर्वाः all, आमन्त्रयामि I am seeking leave of you.
explanation: If I have been harsh towards you, on account of our living together or through ignorance may you forgive me. I (now) seek leave of you all.

shloka_text: वचनं राघवस्यैतध्दर्मयुक्तं समाहितम्। शुश्रुवुस्ताः स्त्रियंस्सर्वा श्शोकोपहतचेतसः।।2.39.39।।
transliteration: vacanaṃ rāghavasyaitadhdarmayuktaṃ samāhitam| śuśruvustāḥ striyaṃssarvā śśokopahatacetasaḥ
translation: ताः those, सर्वाः all, स्त्रियः women, राघवस्य of the descendant of the Raghus (Rama's), धर्मयुक्तम् endowed with virtue, समाहितम्  well balanced, एतत् this, वचनम् words, शोकोपहतचेतसः senses afflicted by grief, शुश्रुवुः heard.
explanation: All the women with their senses afflicted by grief heard the virtuous and wellbalanced words of the scion of the Raghu race:

shloka_text: जज्ञेऽथ तासां सन्नादः क्रौञ्चीनामिव निस्वनः। मानवेन्द्रस्य भार्याणामेवं वदति राघवे।।2.39.40।।
transliteration: jajñe'tha tāsāṃ sannādaḥ krauñcīnāmiva nisvanaḥ| mānavendrasya bhāryāṇāmevaṃ vadati rāghave
translation: राघवे when Rama, एवम् in this way, वदति while he was saying, अथ thereafter, तासाम् of  those women, भार्याणाम् of wives, सन्नादः cry, क्रौञ्चीनाम् of female geese (or herons), निस्वन: इव like sound, जज्ञे arose.
explanation: While Rama said so, there arose a loud cry of the wives of the king like the cry of the female herons.

shloka_text: मुरजपणवमेघघोषवत् दशरथवेश्म बभूव यत्पुरा। विलपितपरिदेवनाकुलं व्यसनगतं तदभूत्सुदुःखितम्।।2.39.41।।
transliteration: murajapaṇavameghaghoṣavat daśarathaveśma babhūva yatpurā| vilapitaparidevanākulaṃ vyasanagataṃ tadabhūtsuduḥkhitam
translation: यत् दशरथवेश्म Dasaratha's palace, पुरा earlier, मुरजपणवमेघघोषवत् reechoed with the sounds of drums and other musical instruments like rumbling of the cloud, तत् that one, विलपितपरिदेवनाकुलम् filled with wailings and lamentations, व्यसनगतम् trapped in calamity, सुदुःखितम् अभूत् was filled with sorrow.
explanation: Dasaratha's palace which reverberated, like the rumblings of the cloud, with the sounds of drums and other musical instruments earlier, now immensely griefsticken and trapped in calamity, is filled with wailings and lamentations. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyninth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of  the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ रामश्च सीता च लक्ष्मणश्च कृताञ्जलिः। उपसङ्गृह्य राजानं चक्रुर्दीना: प्रदक्षिणम्।।2.40.1।।
transliteration: atha rāmaśca sītā ca lakṣmaṇaśca kṛtāñjaliḥ| upasaṅgṛhya rājānaṃ cakrurdīnā: pradakṣiṇam
translation: अथ thereafter, कृताज्ञलिः folded hands, रामश्च Rama also, सीता च  Sita also, लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana also, राजानम् king, उपसङ्गृह्य holding, दीनाः forlom, प्रदक्षिणं चक्रुः circumambulated him.
explanation: Thereafter, Sita, Rama and Lakshmana with folded palms in a forlom state touched (the feet of) the king and circumambulated him.
comments: Rama, Lakshmana and Sita set out for the forest--wailing of citizens, queens and the king.

shloka_text: तं चापि समनुज्ञाप्य धर्मज्ञस्सीतया सह। राघव श्शोकसम्मूढो जननीमभ्यवादयत्।।2.40.2।।
transliteration: taṃ cāpi samanujñāpya dharmajñassītayā saha| rāghava śśokasammūḍho jananīmabhyavādayat
translation: धर्मज्ञः knower of duty, राघवः Rama, सीतया सह along with Sita, तम् (to him), समनुज्ञाप्य after taking leave of, शोकसम्मूढः griefstricken, जननीम् to mother, अभ्यवादयत् paid obeisance.
explanation: Taking leave of Dasaratha, the righteous descendant of the Raghus (Rama) along with Sita paid obeisance to his mother Kausalya who was afflicted with deep grief.

shloka_text: अअन्वक्षं लक्ष्मणो भ्रातुः कौशल्यामभ्यवादयत्। अथ मातु स्सुमित्राया जग्राह चरणौ पुनः।।2.40.3।।
transliteration: aanvakṣaṃ lakṣmaṇo bhrātuḥ kauśalyāmabhyavādayat| atha mātu ssumitrāyā jagrāha caraṇau punaḥ
translation: लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, भ्रातुः to his brother, अन्वक्षम् following immediately, कौशल्याम् of Kausalya, अभ्यवादयत् paid obeisance, अथ thereafter, मातुः of his mother, सुमित्रायाः Sumitra's, चरणौ feet, पुनः again, जग्राह held.
explanation: Immediately following Rama, his brother, Lakshmana also paid obeisance to Kausalya and, thereafter, held the feet of his own mother Sumitra.

shloka_text: तं वन्दमानं रुदती माता सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्। हितकामा महाबाहुं मूध्नर्युपाघ्राय लक्ष्मणम्।।2.40.4।।
transliteration: taṃ vandamānaṃ rudatī mātā saumitrimabravīt| hitakāmā mahābāhuṃ mūdhnaryupāghrāya lakṣmaṇam
translation: माता mother, वन्दमानम् who was paying homage, सौमित्रिम् her son, महाबाहुम्   mightyarmed, लक्ष्मणम् of Lakshmana, मूर्ध्नि on his forehead, उपाघ्राय having smelt, रुदती  wailing, हितकामा wellwisher, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: While the mightyarmed Lakshmana paid her homage, Sumitra wailed, kissed him on his forehead, wished him well and said:

shloka_text: सृष्टस्त्वं वनवासाय स्वनुरक्तस्सुहृज्जने। रामे प्रमादं मा कार्षीः पुत्र भ्रातरि गच्छति।।2.40.5।।
transliteration: sṛṣṭastvaṃ vanavāsāya svanuraktassuhṛjjane| rāme pramādaṃ mā kārṣīḥ putra bhrātari gacchati
translation: पुत्र O son, सुहृज्जने in beloved ones, स्वनुरक्तः deeply attached, वनवासाय to dwell in the forest,  सृष्टः born , गच्छति leaving for the forest, भ्रातरि with regard to your brother, रामे of Rama, प्रमादम् inattention, मा कार्षीः never do.
explanation: Although deeply attached to your beloved ones, O Son, you are born to dwell in the forest. Never be inattentive towards your brother Rama who is on his way (to the forest).

shloka_text: व्यसनी वा समृद्धो वा गतिरेष तवानघ। एष लोके सतां धर्मो यज्ज्येष्ठवशगो भवेत्।।2.40.6।।
transliteration: vyasanī vā samṛddho vā gatireṣa tavānagha| eṣa loke satāṃ dharmo yajjyeṣṭhavaśago bhavet
translation: अनघ O sinless one, व्यसनी वा in adversity, समृद्धो वा or in prosperity, एषः this one,  तव your, गतिः is refuge, ज्येष्ठवशगः following the eldest brother, भवेत् इति यत् if it happens,  एषः this, लोके in this world, सताम् of virtuous men, धर्मः is the duty.
explanation: Rama is your refuge in times of adversity or prosperity, O sinless one To be obedient to the eldest (brother) is the duty of virtuous men in this world.

shloka_text: इदं हि वृत्तमुचितं कुलस्यास्य सनातनम्। दानं दीक्षा च यज्ञेषु तनुत्यागो मृधेषु च।।2.40.7।।
transliteration: idaṃ hi vṛttamucitaṃ kulasyāsya sanātanam| dānaṃ dīkṣā ca yajñeṣu tanutyāgo mṛdheṣu ca
translation: दानम् charity, यज्ञेषु in sacrifices, दीक्षा च initiation, मृधेषु in battles, तनुत्यागः च giving one's  body, इदम् this one, अस्य कुलस्य of this race, उचितम् befitting, सनातनम् ancient, वृत्तं हि is the tradition.
explanation: Charity, initiation at sacrifices and yielding life in battles are the befitting ancient traditions prevailing in your race.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणं त्वेवमुक्त्वा सा संसिद्धं प्रियराघवम्। सुमित्रा गच्छ गच्छेति पुनः पुनरुवाच तम्।।2.40.8।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaṃ tvevamuktvā sā saṃsiddhaṃ priyarāghavam| sumitrā gaccha gaccheti punaḥ punaruvāca tam
translation: सा सुमित्रा that Sumitra, प्रियराघवम् to beloved Rama, संसिद्धम् fully prepared, लक्ष्मणम्  Lakshmana, एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having said, गच्छ गच्छ इति exclaiming 'go, go', तम् to him, पुनः पुनः again and again, उवाच said.
explanation: Having said this to Lakshmana Sumitra again and again said to her beloved Rama, who was fully prepared, 'Go, go'.

shloka_text: रामं दशरथं विद्धि मां विद्धि जनकात्मजाम्। अयोध्यामटवीं विध्दि गच्छ तात यथासुखम्।।2.40.9।।
transliteration: rāmaṃ daśarathaṃ viddhi māṃ viddhi janakātmajām| ayodhyāmaṭavīṃ vidhdi gaccha tāta yathāsukham
translation: रामम् to Rama, दशरथम् as Dasaratha, विद्धि know, जनकात्मजाम् Sita, माम् as me, विद्धि know, अटवीम् forest, अयोध्याम् as Ayodhya, विद्धि know, तात child, यथासुखम् in peace, गच्छ go.
explanation: (To Lakshmana she said) Regard Rama as Dasaratha, Sita as me and the forest as Ayodhya. My child, go in peace.

shloka_text: ततः सुमन्त्रः काकुत्स्थं प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्। विनीतो विनयज्ञश्च मातलिर्वासवं यथा।।2.40.10।।
transliteration: tataḥ sumantraḥ kākutsthaṃ prāñjalirvākyamabravīt| vinīto vinayajñaśca mātalirvāsavaṃ yathā
translation: ततः then, विनीतः humble, विनयज्ञश्च knower of politeness, सुमन्त्रः Sumantra, प्राञ्जलिः with folded palms, मातलिः Matali, वासवं यथा as Indra, काकुत्स्थम् to the scion of the Kakutstha race, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Then Sumantra who knows the ways of politeness and humility spoke to Rama, with folded hands as Matali did to Indra.

shloka_text: ररथमारोह भद्रं ते राजपुत्र महायशः। क्षिप्रं त्वां प्रापयिष्यामि यत्र मां राम वक्ष्यसि।।2.40.11।।
transliteration: rarathamāroha bhadraṃ te rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ| kṣipraṃ tvāṃ prāpayiṣyāmi yatra māṃ rāma vakṣyasi
translation: राजपुत्र O Prince, महायशः O illustrious one, रथं chariot, आरोह mount, ते to you, भद्रम् wish you well, यत्र whereever, वक्ष्यसि you guide (one), त्वाम् you, क्षिप्रम् speedily, प्रापयिष्यामि I will take.
explanation: O Illustrious prince, wish you well Mount the chariot. I shall convey you speedily whereever you want.

shloka_text: चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि वस्तव्यानि वने त्वया। तान्युपक्रमितव्यानि यानि देव्यासि चोदितः।।2.40.12।।
transliteration: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi vastavyāni vane tvayā| tānyupakramitavyāni yāni devyāsi coditaḥ
translation: चतुर्दश fourteen, वर्षाणि years, त्वया by you, वने in the forest,  वस्तव्यानिव you will dwell, यानि those, देव्या by queen Kaikeyi, चोदितः असि you have been directed, तानि those,  उपक्रमितव्यानि should be commenced.
explanation: You have been directed by Kaikeyi to live in the forest for fourteen years. Accordingly you must now commence counting those years as directed.

shloka_text: तं रथं सूर्यसङ्काशं सीता हृष्टेन चेतसा। आरुरोह वरारोहा कृत्वालङ्कारमात्मनः।।2.40.13।।
transliteration: taṃ rathaṃ sūryasaṅkāśaṃ sītā hṛṣṭena cetasā| āruroha varārohā kṛtvālaṅkāramātmanaḥ
translation: वरारोहा lovely limbs, सीता Sita, आत्मनः her person, अलङ्कारम् decoration, कृत्वा having made, हृष्टेन with pleased, चेतसा mind, सूर्यसङ्काशम् resembling the Sun, तं रथम् that chariot,  आरुरोह boarded.
explanation: Sita of lovely limbs decorated herself and with a cheerful mind boarded the chariot which was shining like the Sun.

shloka_text: अथो ज्वलनसङ्काशं चामीकरविभूषितम्। तमारुरुहतुस्तूर्णं भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।।2.40.14।।
