transliteration: atho jvalanasaṅkāśaṃ cāmīkaravibhūṣitam| tamāruruhatustūrṇaṃ bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
translation: अथ thereafter, भ्रातरौ both the brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, उज्वलनसङ्काशम्  appearing like blazing fire, चामीकरविभूषितम् decorated with gold, तम् the chariot, तूर्णम्  immediately, आरुरुहतुः both ascended.
explanation: Thereafter, Rama and Lakshmana also boarded that chariot decorated with gold and  shining like blazing fire.

shloka_text: वनवासं हि संख्याय वासांस्याभरणानि च। भर्तारमनुगच्छन्त्यै सीतायै श्वशुरो ददौ।।2.40.15।।
transliteration: vanavāsaṃ hi saṃkhyāya vāsāṃsyābharaṇāni ca| bhartāramanugacchantyai sītāyai śvaśuro dadau
translation: श्वशुरः fatherinlaw (Dasaratha), भर्तारम् to the husband, अनुगच्छन्त्यै following, सीतायै to Sita, वनवासम् going to dwell in the forest, संख्याय having counted, वासांसि clothes, आभरणानि च ornamets, ददौ gave.
explanation: Fatherinlaw (Dasaratha) gave clothes and ornaments on the assessment of the number of years Sita was going to spend in the forest with her husband.

shloka_text: तथैवायुधजालानि भ्रातृभ्यां कवचानि च। रथोपस्थे प्रतिन्यस्य सचर्म कठिनं च तत्।।2.40.16।। सीतातृतीयानारूढान् दृष्ट्वा दृष्टमचोदयत्। सुमन्त्रस्सम्मतानश्वान् वायुवेगसमान्जवे।।2.40.17।।
transliteration: tathaivāyudhajālāni bhrātṛbhyāṃ kavacāni ca| rathopasthe pratinyasya sacarma kaṭhinaṃ ca tat sītātṛtīyānārūḍhān dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭamacodayat| sumantrassammatānaśvān vāyuvegasamānjave
translation: तथैव similarly, भ्रातृभ्याम् for brothers, आयुधजालानि multitude of weapons, कवचानि armours, सचर्म along with shield, तत् कठिनं च protective leather covering the hand,  रथोपस्थे in the centre of the chariot,  प्रतिन्यस्य placing, सुमन्त्रः Sumantra, सीतातृतीयान् Rama and Lakshmana with Sita as third person, आरूढान् ascended, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सम्मतान् honoured, जवे in speed, वायुवेग समान् like the speed of the wind, अश्वान् horses, धृष्टम् briskly, अचोदयत् drove them.
explanation: So also Dasaratha secured a multitude of weapons, shields and protective leathercoverings for hands and placed them at the centre of the chariot, for use by the brothers. When Sumantra ensured that Sita, Rama and Lakshmana boarded the chariot,  he briskly hastened the horses which were as speedy as the wind.

shloka_text: तथैवायुधजालानि भ्रातृभ्यां कवचानि च। रथोपस्थे प्रतिन्यस्य सचर्म कठिनं च तत्।।2.40.16।। सीतातृतीयानारूढान् दृष्ट्वा दृष्टमचोदयत्। सुमन्त्रस्सम्मतानश्वान् वायुवेगसमान्जवे।।2.40.17।।
transliteration: tathaivāyudhajālāni bhrātṛbhyāṃ kavacāni ca| rathopasthe pratinyasya sacarma kaṭhinaṃ ca tat sītātṛtīyānārūḍhān dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭamacodayat| sumantrassammatānaśvān vāyuvegasamānjave
translation: तथैव similarly, भ्रातृभ्याम् for brothers, आयुधजालानि multitude of weapons, कवचानि armours, सचर्म along with shield, तत् कठिनं च protective leather covering the hand,  रथोपस्थे in the centre of the chariot,  प्रतिन्यस्य placing, सुमन्त्रः Sumantra, सीतातृतीयान् Rama and Lakshmana with Sita as third person, आरूढान् ascended, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सम्मतान् honoured, जवे in speed, वायुवेग समान् like the speed of the wind, अश्वान् horses, धृष्टम् briskly, अचोदयत् drove them.
explanation: So also Dasaratha secured a multitude of weapons, shields and protective leathercoverings for hands and placed them at the centre of the chariot, for use by the brothers. When Sumantra ensured that Sita, Rama and Lakshmana boarded the chariot,  he briskly hastened the horses which were as speedy as the wind.

shloka_text: प्रतियाते महारण्यं चिररात्राय राघवे। बभूव नगरे मूर्छा बलमूर्छा जनस्य च।।2.40.18।।
transliteration: pratiyāte mahāraṇyaṃ cirarātrāya rāghave| babhūva nagare mūrchā balamūrchā janasya ca
translation: राघवे Rama, चिररात्राय for a long period, महारण्यम् to the great forest, प्रतियाते having set out, नगरे  in the city, मूर्छा बभूव was deprived of  senses, जनस्य for men, बलमूर्छा च were deprived of their strength.
explanation: Having seen Rama set out  for the great forest for a long period, the city was stilled and men were enervated.

shloka_text: तत्समाकुलसम्भ्रान्तं मत्तसङ्कुपितद्विपम्। हयशिञ्जितनिर्घोषं पुरमासीन्महास्वनम्।।2.40.19।।
transliteration: tatsamākulasambhrāntaṃ mattasaṅkupitadvipam| hayaśiñjitanirghoṣaṃ puramāsīnmahāsvanam
translation: तत् पुरम् that city, मत्तसङ्कुपितद्विपम् with elephants intoxicated and provoked (by sounds), हयशिञ्जितनिर्घोषम्  the tinkling of bells and the neighing of the horses, महास्वनम् mighty roar, आकुलसम्भ्रान्तम् आसीत् became flurried and distressed.
explanation: The city was distressed and flurried by the intoxicated elephants, provoked by the mighty sound of the tinkling of bells and the neighing of the horses.

shloka_text: तत स्सबालवृद्धा सा पुरी परमपीडिता। राममेवाभिदुद्राव घर्मार्ता सलिलं यथा।।2.40.20।।
transliteration: tata ssabālavṛddhā sā purī paramapīḍitā| rāmamevābhidudrāva gharmārtā salilaṃ yathā
translation: ततः thereafter, बालवृद्धा including young and old, सा पुरी that city, परमपीडिता extremely afflicted, घर्मार्तः oppressed with heat, सलिलं यथा like water, रामम् एव towards Rama only,  अभिदुद्राव ran.
explanation: Thereafter the extremely afflicted people of the city, including young and old alike, ran towards Rama like men oppressed with heat running for water.

shloka_text: पार्श्वतः पृष्ठतश्चापि लम्बमानास्तदुन्मुखाः। बाष्पपूर्णमुखास्सर्वे तमूचुर्भृशनिस्वनाः।।2.40.21।।
transliteration: pārśvataḥ pṛṣṭhataścāpi lambamānāstadunmukhāḥ| bāṣpapūrṇamukhāssarve tamūcurbhṛśanisvanāḥ
translation: सर्वे all, पार्श्वतः by his side, पृष्ठतश्चैव behind, लम्बमानाः hanging upon, तदुन्मुखाः facing him, बाष्पपूर्णमुखाः faces covered with tears, भृशनिस्वनाः heaving deeply, तम् addressing that Sumantra, ऊचुः said.
explanation: All the people hanging from the chariot from behind and by the sides, heaving deeply, their faces covered with tears, thus addressed to Sumantra:

shloka_text: संयच्छ वाजिनां रश्मीन् सूत याहि शनैश्शनैः। मुखं द्रक्ष्याम रामस्य दुर्दर्शं नो भविष्यति।।2.40.22।।
transliteration: saṃyaccha vājināṃ raśmīn sūta yāhi śanaiśśanaiḥ| mukhaṃ drakṣyāma rāmasya durdarśaṃ no bhaviṣyati
translation: सूत O charioteer, वाजिनाम् horses, रश्मीन् reins, संयच्छ control, शनैः शनैः slowly, slowly,  याहि go, रामस्य Rama's, मुखम् face, द्रक्ष्यामः we will see,  नः for us, दुर्दर्शम् difficult to see,  भविष्यति will become.
explanation: O charioteer, control the reins of the horses and go slow so that we may look at the face of Rama, for soon we will not be able to see him.

shloka_text: आयसं हृदयं नूनं राममातुरसंशयम्। यद्देवगर्भप्रतिमे वनं याति न भिद्यते।।2.40.23।।
transliteration: āyasaṃ hṛdayaṃ nūnaṃ rāmamāturasaṃśayam| yaddevagarbhapratime vanaṃ yāti na bhidyate
translation: देवगर्भप्रतिमे resembling the offspring of gods, वनम् to the forest, याति while going, यत् for what reason, न भिद्यते does not break, नूनम् certainly, राममातुः of the mother of Rama (Kausalya's),  हृदयम् heart, आयसम् is made of iron, असंशयम् no doubt.
explanation: Alas, the heart of Kausalya whose son, Rama, resembles the offspring of the gods, does not break even though he is going to the forest Undoubtedly it must be made of iron.

shloka_text: कृतकृत्या हि वैदेही छायेवानुगता पतिम्। न जहाति रता धर्मे मेरुमर्कप्रभा यथा।।2.40.24।।
transliteration: kṛtakṛtyā hi vaidehī chāyevānugatā patim| na jahāti ratā dharme merumarkaprabhā yathā
translation: धर्मे in duty, रता attached, छायेव like shadow, अनुगता following, वैदेहि Sita, अर्कप्रभा sunlight, मेरुम् यथा like mount Meru, पतिम् her husband, न जहाति does not leave,   कृतकृत्या हि accomplished her purpose.
explanation: Sita, deeply attached to her duty, and with her desire fulfilled is following her husband like a shadow just as the sunlight which never leaves mount Meru.

shloka_text: अहो लक्ष्मण सिद्धार्थ स्सततं प्रियवादिनम्। भ्रातरं देवसङ्काशं यस्त्वं परिचरिष्यसि।।2.40.25।।
transliteration: aho lakṣmaṇa siddhārtha ssatataṃ priyavādinam| bhrātaraṃ devasaṅkāśaṃ yastvaṃ paricariṣyasi
translation: लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, यः त्वम् such as you, प्रियवादिनम् who speaks pleasant words, देवसङ्काशम् godlike, भ्रातरम् to brother, सततम् always, परिचरिष्यसि attend, सिद्धार्थः fulfilled the purpose, अहो oh.
explanation: With your desires fulfilled, O Lakshmana, you will attend to your godlike brother who always speaks pleasant words.

shloka_text: महत्येषा हि ते सिध्दिरेष चाभ्युदयो महान्। एष स्वर्गस्य मार्गश्च यदेनमनुगच्छसि।।2.40.26।।
transliteration: mahatyeṣā hi te sidhdireṣa cābhyudayo mahān| eṣa svargasya mārgaśca yadenamanugacchasi
translation: एनम् this Rama, अनुगच्छसि (इति) यत् the fact that you are following him,  एषा that one, ते for you, महती great, सिध्दि: achievement, एषः this, महान् great, अभ्युदयः prosperity, एषः this one, स्वर्गस्य to heaven, मार्गश्च way.
explanation: The very fact that you are  following Rama is a great achievement and a great fortune for you. This, in fact, is the way to heaven.

shloka_text: एवं वदन्तस्ते सोढुं न शेकुर्बाष्पमागतम्। नरास्तमनुगच्छन्तः प्रियमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम्।।2.40.27।।
transliteration: evaṃ vadantaste soḍhuṃ na śekurbāṣpamāgatam| narāstamanugacchantaḥ priyamikṣvākunandanam
translation: एवम् thus, वदन्तः speaking, इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम् delight of Ikshawaku dynasty, प्रियम् beloved, तम् that Rama, अनुगच्छन्तः following, ते नराः those people, आगतम् having arrived, बाष्पम् tears, सोढुम् to bear, न शेकुः were not able.
explanation: Speaking thus, the people following their beloved Rama, the delight of the Ikshvaku dynasty, were not able to bear (restrain) the tears flowing from their eyes.

shloka_text: अथ राजा वृत स्त्रीभिर्दीनाभिर्दीनचेतनः। निर्जगाम प्रियं पुत्रं द्रक्ष्यामीति ब्रुवन् गृहात्।।2.40.28।।
transliteration: atha rājā vṛta strībhirdīnābhirdīnacetanaḥ| nirjagāma priyaṃ putraṃ drakṣyāmīti bruvan gṛhāt
translation: अथ then, दीनचेतनः in desolation, राजा king, प्रियम् beloved, पुत्रम् son, द्रक्ष्यामीति I wish to see him, ब्रुवन् saying, दीनाभिः distressed, स्त्रीभिः by ladies, वृतः surrounded, गृहात् from the palace, निर्जगाम emerged.
explanation: I wish to see my beloved son said the king with a sense of desolation and emerged, surrounded by forlorn women, from the palace.

shloka_text: शुश्रुवे चाग्रतः स्त्रीणां रुदन्तीनां महास्वनः। यथा नादः करेणूनां बद्धे महति कुञ्जरे।।2.40.29।।
transliteration: śuśruve cāgrataḥ strīṇāṃ rudantīnāṃ mahāsvanaḥ| yathā nādaḥ kareṇūnāṃ baddhe mahati kuñjare
translation: अग्रतः in front of, रुदन्तीनाम् crying, स्त्रीणाम् of women, महास्वनः loud sound, महति when great,  कुञ्जरे elephant, बद्धे when fastened, करेणूनाम् of female elephants, नादः यथा like a sound,  शुश्रुवे heard.
explanation: He heard the women crying loudly in front like wailings of cowelephants when their bull elephant is captured.

shloka_text: पिता हि राजा काकुत्स्थः श्रीमान् सन्नस्तदाऽभवत्। परिपूर्णः शशी काले ग्रहेणोपप्लुतो यथा।।2.40.30।।
transliteration: pitā hi rājā kākutsthaḥ śrīmān sannastadā'bhavat| paripūrṇaḥ śaśī kāle graheṇopapluto yathā
translation: श्रीमान् one of great prosperity, काकुत्स्थ: born in the race of Kakutstha (Dasaratha), पिता father, राजा king, तदा then, काले at that time, ग्रहेण by Rahu, उपप्लुतः eclipsed, पूर्णशशी यथा like the full Moon, सन्नः अभवत् was shrunk.
explanation: The king born in the race of Kakutstha, though bright, looked dull then like the full Moon eclipsed (by Rahu).

shloka_text: स च श्रीमानचिन्त्यात्मा रामो दशरथात्मजः। सूतं सञ्चोदयामास त्वरितं वाह्यतामिति।।2.40.31।।
transliteration: sa ca śrīmānacintyātmā rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ| sūtaṃ sañcodayāmāsa tvaritaṃ vāhyatāmiti
translation: श्रीमान् glorious one, अचिन्त्यात्मा unimaginable form, सः दशरथात्मजः that son of Dasaratha, रामः Rama, त्वरितम् fast, वाह्यताम् इति drive, सूतम् charioteer,  सञ्चोदयामास exhorted.
explanation: The son of Dasaratha, glorious Rama of inconceivable courage, exhorted the charioteer to drive the chariot fast.

shloka_text: रामो याहीति सूतं तं तिष्ठेति स जनस्तदा। उभयं नाशकत्सूतः कर्तुमध्वनि चोदितः।।2.40.32।।
transliteration: rāmo yāhīti sūtaṃ taṃ tiṣṭheti sa janastadā| ubhayaṃ nāśakatsūtaḥ kartumadhvani coditaḥ
translation: तदा then, रामः Rama, याहि इति saying 'drive on', जनः citizens, तिष्ठेति 'stay, stay', तं सूतम् to the charioteer, चोदितः urged, सूतः that charioteer, अध्वनि on the way, उभयम् both the acts, कर्तुम् to do, नाशकत् was unable.
explanation: Urged by Rama to drive fast on the one hand and by the citizens to stay, on the other, the charioteer could do neither on the way.

shloka_text: निर्गच्छति महाबाहौ रामे पौरजनाश्रुभिः। पतितैरभ्यवहितं प्रशशाम महीरजः।।2.40.33।।
transliteration: nirgacchati mahābāhau rāme paurajanāśrubhiḥ| patitairabhyavahitaṃ praśaśāma mahīrajaḥ
translation: महाबाहौ mightyarmed, रामे Rama, निर्गच्छति going away, अभ्यवहितम् raised, महीरजः dust of the earth, पतितैः by the fallen, पौरजनाश्रुभिः with the tears of the citizens, प्रशशाम subsided.
explanation: As the mightyarmed Rama was going away, the dust raised from the earth subsided with the tears falling from the citizens' (eyes).

shloka_text: रुदिताश्रुपरिद्यूनं हाहाकृतमचेतनम्। प्रयाणे राघवस्यासीत्पुरं परमपीडितम्।।2.40.34।।
transliteration: ruditāśruparidyūnaṃ hāhākṛtamacetanam| prayāṇe rāghavasyāsītpuraṃ paramapīḍitam
translation: राघवस्य Rama's, प्रयाणे at the time of departure, पुरम् the city, रुदिताश्रुपरिद्यूनम् drenched  with tears from weeping, हाहाकृतम् 'Alas, Alas', अचेतनम् insensate, परम पीडितम् आसीत् became tormented.
explanation: At the time of Rama's departure, the insensate city was drenched with tears of the deeply afflicted people crying, 'Alas, Alas'.

shloka_text: सुस्राव नयनैः स्त्रीणामस्रमायाससम्भवम्। मीनसङ्क्षोभचलितै स्सलिलं पङ्कजैरिव।।2.40.35।।
transliteration: susrāva nayanaiḥ strīṇāmasramāyāsasambhavam| mīnasaṅkṣobhacalitai ssalilaṃ paṅkajairiva
translation: स्त्रीणाम् women's, नयनैः with (from) eyes, आयाससम्भवम् born of anguish, अस्रम् tears, मीनसङ्क्षोभ चलितैः shaken by the movements of fish, पङ्कजैः by lotuses, सलिलमिव like waterdrops, सुस्राव fell.
explanation: Tears born of anguish fell from the eyes of women just as waterdrops fall from lotuses shaken by the movements of fishes.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा तु नृपति श्श्रीमानेकचित्तगतं पुरम्। निपपातैव दुःखेन हतमूल इव द्रुमः।।2.40.36।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā tu nṛpati śśrīmānekacittagataṃ puram| nipapātaiva duḥkhena hatamūla iva drumaḥ
translation: श्रीमान् prosperous, नृपतिः king, एकचित्तगतम् absorbed in the same thought, पुरम् the city,  दृष्ट्वा having seen, दुःखेन with grief, हतमूलः with roots severed, द्रुमः इव like tree, निपपातैव  fell down.
explanation: Having seen the city (people) absorbed in one single thought, the prosperous king, griefstricken, fell down on the ground like a tree severed at its root.

shloka_text: ततो हलहलाशब्दो जज्ञे रामस्य पृष्ठतः। नराणां प्रेक्ष्य राजानं सीदन्तं भृशदुःखितम्।।2.40.37।।
transliteration: tato halahalāśabdo jajñe rāmasya pṛṣṭhataḥ| narāṇāṃ prekṣya rājānaṃ sīdantaṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitam
translation: ततः then, भृश दुःखितम् intensely grieved, सीदन्तम् enfeebled, राजानम् king, प्रेक्ष्य having seen, नराणाम् men's, हलहलाशब्दः a tumultous roar, रामस्य Rama's, पृष्ठतः behind, जज्ञे emanated.
explanation: When the people saw the king enfeebled by deep grief, they raised an uproar behind Rama's (chariot).

shloka_text: हा रामेति जनाः केचिद्राममातेति चापरे। अन्तःपुरं समृद्धं च क्रोशन्तः पर्यदेवयन्।।2.40.38।।
transliteration: hā rāmeti janāḥ kecidrāmamāteti cāpare| antaḥpuraṃ samṛddhaṃ ca krośantaḥ paryadevayan
translation: केचित् some, जनाः people, हा रामेति O Rama, अपरे some others, राममातेति O mother of Rama, क्रोशन्तः while crying, समृद्धम् loudly, अन्तःपुरं च inner apartment, पर्यदेवयन् made them weep.
explanation: Some among them wailed 'Oh Rama', while some others cried 'Oh mother of Rama' By crying loudly, they made the women in the inner apartment cry too.

shloka_text: अन्वीक्षमाणो रामस्तु विषण्णं भ्रान्तचेतसम्। राजानं मातरं चैव ददर्शानुगतौ पथि।।2.40.39।।
transliteration: anvīkṣamāṇo rāmastu viṣaṇṇaṃ bhrāntacetasam| rājānaṃ mātaraṃ caiva dadarśānugatau pathi
translation: रामस्तु Rama, अन्वीक्षमाणः glanced back, विषण्णम् dejected, भ्रान्तचेतसम् with a disturbed mind, राजानम् king, मातरं चैव mother also, पथि on the highway, अनुगतौ following, ददर्श  beheld.
explanation: When Rama glanced back, he saw his mother and father trailing behind him on the highway, with an agitated and dejected mind.

shloka_text: स बद्ध इव पाशेन किशोरो मातरं यथा। धर्मपाशेन सङ्क्षिप्तः प्रकाशं नाभ्युदैक्षत।।2.40.40।।
transliteration: sa baddha iva pāśena kiśoro mātaraṃ yathā| dharmapāśena saṅkṣiptaḥ prakāśaṃ nābhyudaikṣata
translation: पाशेन बद्धः fastened by cord, किशोरः इव like a foal, सः Rama, धर्मपाशेन by bonds of duty,  सङ्क्षिप्तः restrained, मातरं यथा like mother, प्रकाशम् clearly, नाभ्युदैक्षत did not see.
explanation: Like a fastened foal cannot see its mother, Rama restrained by bonds of duty could not see his parents clearly.

shloka_text: पदातिनौ च यानार्हावदुःखार्हौ सुखोचितौ। दृष्ट्वा सञ्चोदयामास शीघ्रं याहीति सारथिम्।।2.40.41।।
transliteration: padātinau ca yānārhāvaduḥkhārhau sukhocitau| dṛṣṭvā sañcodayāmāsa śīghraṃ yāhīti sārathim
translation: यानार्हौ worthy of going on chariot, पदातिनौ (now) going on foot, सुखोचितौ accustomed to comforts, अदु:खार्हौ unworthy of experiencing sorrow, दृष्ट्वा having seen, शीघ्रम् swiftly,  याहि इति 'go' thus, सारथिम् of charioteer, सञ्चोदयामास urged.
explanation: Seeing his parents, who were worthy of riding a chariot now going on foot, who were accustomed to comforts and did not deserve any suffering, Rama urged his charioteer to drive fast.

shloka_text: न हि तत्पुरुषव्याघ्रो दुःखदं दर्शनं पितुः। मातुश्च सहितुं शक्तस्तोत्रार्दित इव द्विपः।।2.40.42।।
transliteration: na hi tatpuruṣavyāghro duḥkhadaṃ darśanaṃ pituḥ| mātuśca sahituṃ śaktastotrārdita iva dvipaḥ
translation: पुरुषव्याघ्रः tiger (best) among men, तोत्रार्दितः tormented by the goads, द्विपः इव like an elephant, दुःखदम् causing agony, पितुः father's, मातुश्च mother's, तत् दर्शनम् that sight, सहितुम् to endure, न शक्तः हि was not able.
explanation: Rama the best among men, could not, like an elephant tormented by the goad, endure that pitiful sight of his father and mother.

shloka_text: प्रत्यगारमिवायान्ती वत्सला वत्सकारणात्। बद्धवत्सा यथा धेनू राममाताभ्यधावत।।2.40.43।।
transliteration: pratyagāramivāyāntī vatsalā vatsakāraṇāt| baddhavatsā yathā dhenū rāmamātābhyadhāvata
translation: बद्धवत्सा fastened calf, वत्सला affectionate, अगारं प्रति towards the shed, आयन्ती coming, धेनुः इव like cow, वत्सकारणात् यथा for its calf, राममाता Rama's mother, अभ्यधावत ran behind.
explanation: Rama's mother ran after the chariot, like an affectionate cow running towards the shed to join its fastened calf.

shloka_text: तथा रुदन्तीं कौसल्यां रथं तमनुधावतीम्। क्रोशन्तीं राम रामेति हा सीते लक्ष्मणेति च।।2.40.44।। रामलक्ष्मणसीतार्थं स्रवन्तीं वारि नेत्रजम्। असकृत्प्रैक्षत तदा नृत्यन्तीमिव मातरम्।।2.40.45।।
transliteration: tathā rudantīṃ kausalyāṃ rathaṃ tamanudhāvatīm| krośantīṃ rāma rāmeti hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca rāmalakṣmaṇasītārthaṃ sravantīṃ vāri netrajam| asakṛtpraikṣata tadā nṛtyantīmiva mātaram
translation: (सः Rama), तथा thus, रुदन्तीम् weeping, राम रामेति O Rama, O Rama, हा सीते O Sita, लक्ष्मणेति च O Lakshmana, क्रोशन्तीम् crying, रामलक्ष्मणसीतार्थम् for Rama, Lakshmana and Sita, नेत्रजम् born of eyes, वारि tears, स्रवन्तीम् shedding, नृत्यन्तीम् इव like a dancer, मातरम् mother, तां कौशल्याम् that Kausalya, असकृत् repeatedly, प्रैक्षत saw.
explanation: While Kausalya was weeping and running after the chariot, crying O 'Rama, O Sita, O Lakshmana, shedding tears for them, Rama repeatedly glanced at her who was twisting and bending as if in a dancing pose.

shloka_text: तथा रुदन्तीं कौसल्यां रथं तमनुधावतीम्। क्रोशन्तीं राम रामेति हा सीते लक्ष्मणेति च।।2.40.44।। रामलक्ष्मणसीतार्थं स्रवन्तीं वारि नेत्रजम्। असकृत्प्रैक्षत तदा नृत्यन्तीमिव मातरम्।।2.40.45।।
transliteration: tathā rudantīṃ kausalyāṃ rathaṃ tamanudhāvatīm| krośantīṃ rāma rāmeti hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca rāmalakṣmaṇasītārthaṃ sravantīṃ vāri netrajam| asakṛtpraikṣata tadā nṛtyantīmiva mātaram
translation: (सः Rama), तथा thus, रुदन्तीम् weeping, राम रामेति O Rama, O Rama, हा सीते O Sita, लक्ष्मणेति च O Lakshmana, क्रोशन्तीम् crying, रामलक्ष्मणसीतार्थम् for Rama, Lakshmana and Sita, नेत्रजम् born of eyes, वारि tears, स्रवन्तीम् shedding, नृत्यन्तीम् इव like a dancer, मातरम् mother, तां कौशल्याम् that Kausalya, असकृत् repeatedly, प्रैक्षत saw.
explanation: While Kausalya was weeping and running after the chariot, crying O 'Rama, O Sita, O Lakshmana, shedding tears for them, Rama repeatedly glanced at her who was twisting and bending as if in a dancing pose.

shloka_text: तिष्ठेति राजा चुक्रोश याहि याहीति राघवः। सुमन्त्रस्य बभूवात्मा चक्रयोरिव चान्तरा।।2.40.46।।
transliteration: tiṣṭheti rājā cukrośa yāhi yāhīti rāghavaḥ| sumantrasya babhūvātmā cakrayoriva cāntarā
translation: राजा king, तिष्ठेति 'stay, stay', चुक्रोश cried, राघवः Rama, याहि इति 'go, go', सुमन्त्रस्य Sumantra's, आत्मा mind, चक्रयो: two wheels, अन्तरा इव like in between, बभूव became.
explanation: The king cried, 'Stay, Stay', while Rama said 'Go on, Go on'. Sumantra's mind was caught as if in between two wheels.

shloka_text: नाश्रौषमिति राजानमुपालब्धोऽपि वक्ष्यसि। चिरं दुःखस्य पापिष्ठमिति रामस्तमब्रवीत्।।2.40.47।।
transliteration: nāśrauṣamiti rājānamupālabdho'pi vakṣyasi| ciraṃ duḥkhasya pāpiṣṭhamiti rāmastamabravīt
translation: उपालब्धोऽपि even when reproached, नाश्रौषमिति 'I did not hear', राजानम् to the king, वक्ष्यसि you will tell, दुःखस्य agony, चिरम् for long time, पापिष्ठम् cannot be endured, इति thus, रामः  Rama, तम् to him, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: When the king reproaches you for not stopping the chariot, you can say 'I could not hear'.Prolonging agony is sinful, said Rama to Sumantra.

shloka_text: रामस्य स वचः कुर्वन्ननुज्ञाप्य च तं जनम्। व्रजतोऽपि हयान् शीघ्रं चोदयामास सारथिः।।2.40.48।।
transliteration: rāmasya sa vacaḥ kurvannanujñāpya ca taṃ janam| vrajato'pi hayān śīghraṃ codayāmāsa sārathiḥ
translation: स सारथिः charioteer, रामस्य Rama's, वचः words, कुर्वन् obeying, तम् जनम् that multitude of people, अनुज्ञाप्य having given permision (taking leave), व्रजतोऽपि even though moving, हयान् horses, शीघ्रम् with greater speed, चोदयामास hastened.
explanation: Obeying the command of Rama and after taking leave of the people, Sumantra hastened the horses although they were galloping.

shloka_text: न्यवर्तत जनो राज्ञो रामं कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम्। मनसाप्यश्रुवेगैश्च न न्यवर्तत मानुषम्।।2.40.49।।
transliteration: nyavartata jano rājño rāmaṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam| manasāpyaśruvegaiśca na nyavartata mānuṣam
translation: राज्ञः king's, जनः people, रामम् of Rama, प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा circumanbulating him in imaginataion, न्यवर्तत returned, मानुषम् people, मनसा अपि even mentally, अश्रुवेगैश्च flow of their tears, न न्यवर्तत did not stop.
explanation: The king's men returned, with Rama circumambulated (on the plane of their minds). But from their minds they could not hold back their tears (grief).

shloka_text: यमिच्छेत्पुनरायान्तं नैनं दूरमनुव्रजेत्। इत्यमात्या महाराजमूचुर्दशरथं वचः।।2.40.50।।
transliteration: yamicchetpunarāyāntaṃ nainaṃ dūramanuvrajet| ityamātyā mahārājamūcurdaśarathaṃ vacaḥ
translation: यम् whom, पुनः again, आयान्तम् returning, इच्छेत् desires, एनम् him, दूरम् for a long distance,  न अनुव्रजेत् should not follow, इति thus, अमात्याः ministers, महाराजम् king, दशरथम्  to Dasaratha, वचः words, ऊचुः said.
explanation: We should not follow over a long distance those we wish to return, said the ministers to king Dasaratha.

shloka_text: तेषां वचः सर्वगुणोपपन्नं प्रस्विन्नगात्रः प्रविषण्णरूपः। निशम्य राजा कृपणः सभार्यो व्यवस्थितस्तं सुतमीक्षमाणः।।2.40.51।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ vacaḥ sarvaguṇopapannaṃ prasvinnagātraḥ praviṣaṇṇarūpaḥ| niśamya rājā kṛpaṇaḥ sabhāryo vyavasthitastaṃ sutamīkṣamāṇaḥ
translation: प्रस्विन्नगात्रः with a perspiring body, प्रविषण्णरूपः with a melancholic appearance, कृपणः overcome with grief, सभार्यः along with his wives, राजा the king, तेषाम् their,  सर्वगुणोपपन्नम् endowed with every virtue, वचः words, निशम्य having heard, तं सुतम् that son, ईक्षमाणः while looking at, व्यवस्थितः stood there.
explanation: Dasaratha and his wives, overcome with grief, heard their words steeped in virtue (wisdom). The king stood there with his perspiring body and melancholic appearance, fixing his gaze on his son. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे चत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortieth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic  composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्स्तु पुरुषव्याघ्रे विनिर्याति कृताञ्जलौ। आर्तशब्दोऽहि सञ्जज्ञे स्त्रीणामन्त:पुरे महान्।।2.41.1।।
transliteration: tasminstu puruṣavyāghre viniryāti kṛtāñjalau| ārtaśabdo'hi sañjajñe strīṇāmanta:pure mahān
translation: पुरुषव्याघ्रे tiger (foremost) among men, तस्मिन् that Rama, कृताञ्जलौ with folded palms, विनिर्याति having departed, अन्तःपुरे in the inner apartment (of the palace), स्त्रीणाम् of women, आर्तशब्दः cries of distress, संजज्ञे arose.
explanation: When Rama, the foremost men, was departing with folded palms there arose a huge cry of distress from the inner apartment of ladies.
comments: On the departure of Rama to the forest, citizens of Ayodhya and women from the inner apartment lament

shloka_text: अनाथस्य जनस्यास्य दुर्बलस्य तपस्विनः। यो गतिश्शरणं चासीत्स नाथः क्व नु गच्छति।।2.41.2।।
transliteration: anāthasya janasyāsya durbalasya tapasvinaḥ| yo gatiśśaraṇaṃ cāsītsa nāthaḥ kva nu gacchati
translation: अनाथस्य of the orphan, दुर्बलस्य of the weak, तपस्विनः of the miserable, अस्य जनस्य of these people, यः who, गतिः refuge, शरणं च also the protector, आसीत्  was, सः नाथः such protector, क्व नु गच्छति where is he now going?
explanation: Rama was a refuge and a protector to all the people who were defenceless, weak and miserable. Where is such a protector going now? (said the people).

shloka_text: न क्रुध्यत्यभिशप्तोऽपि क्रोधनीयानि वर्जयन्। क्रुद्धान्प्रसादयन्सर्वान् समदुःखः क्व गज्छति।।2.41.3।।
transliteration: na krudhyatyabhiśapto'pi krodhanīyāni varjayan| kruddhānprasādayansarvān samaduḥkhaḥ kva gajchati
translation: अभिशप्तोऽपि even when denounced, न क्रुध्यति will not be angry, क्रोधनीयानि acts provoking wrath, वर्जयन् while  abandoning, क्रुद्धान् those who were enraged, सर्वान् all of them, प्रसादयन् pacifies, समदुःखः sharing their sorrow, क्व where, गच्छति is going?
explanation: Where is he who, even if reviled, never gets angry, never does acts that provoke anger, pacifies those who are enraged and shares the sorrows of others going now?

shloka_text: कौशल्यायां महातेजा यथा मातरि वर्तते। तथा यो वर्ततेऽस्मासु महात्मा क्व नु गच्छति।।2.41.4।।
transliteration: kauśalyāyāṃ mahātejā yathā mātari vartate| tathā yo vartate'smāsu mahātmā kva nu gacchati
translation: महातेजाः effulgent, यः Rama, मातरि with regard to his mother, कौशल्यायाम् Kausalya, यथा as, वर्तते treats, तथा in that way, अस्मासु in us, वर्तते treats, महात्मा a magnanimous  one, क्व नु where, गच्छति is he going?
explanation: Where is he, that effulgent, magnanimous one who treated us (with the same respect) as he treated his mother Kausalya, going now?

shloka_text: कैकेय्या क्लिश्यमानेन राज्ञा सञ्चोदितो वनम्। परित्राता जनस्यास्य जगतः क्व नु गच्छति।।2.41.5।।
transliteration: kaikeyyā kliśyamānena rājñā sañcodito vanam| paritrātā janasyāsya jagataḥ kva nu gacchati
translation: कैकेय्या by Kaikeyi, क्लिश्यमानेन by being tormented, राज्ञा by the king, वनम् to the forest, सञ्चोदितः one ordered, अस्य जनस्य of these people, जगतः of the whole world, परित्राता protector, Rama, क्व नु where, गच्छति is he going?
explanation: Tormented by Kaikeyi, the king ordered him to go to the forest. Where is he, who happened to be the protector of the people of this world, going now?

shloka_text: अहो निश्चेतनो राजा जीवलोकस्य सम्प्रियम्। धर्म्यं सत्यव्रतं रामं वनवासे प्रवत्स्यति।।2.41.6।।
transliteration: aho niścetano rājā jīvalokasya sampriyam| dharmyaṃ satyavrataṃ rāmaṃ vanavāse pravatsyati
translation: राजा king, निश्चेतनः nonsense, अहो alas, जीवलोकस्य of the world of living beings, सम्प्रियम् is dear, धर्म्यम् is righteous, सत्यव्रतम् faithful to truth, रामम् Rama, वनवासे to dwell in the forest, प्रवत्स्यति is sending away.
explanation: Alas, the king must be devoid of any sense as he is sending away Rama, who is dear to the world, is righteous and truthful, to dwell in the forest.

shloka_text: इति सर्वा महिष्यस्ता विवत्सा इव धेनवः। रुरुदुश्चैव दुःखार्ताः सस्वरं च विचुक्रुशुः।।2.41.7।।
transliteration: iti sarvā mahiṣyastā vivatsā iva dhenavaḥ| ruruduścaiva duḥkhārtāḥ sasvaraṃ ca vicukruśuḥ
translation: इति thus, सर्वाः all, ताः महिष्यः all the wives, विवत्साः deprived of their calfs, धेनवः इव like cows, दुःखार्ताः tormented with sorrow, रुरुदुश्चैव wept, सस्वरम् loudly, विचुक्रुशुः cried.
explanation: So wept aloud the anguished wives of the king like cows separated from their calves.

shloka_text: स तमन्तः पुरे घोरमार्तशब्दं महीपतिः। पुत्रशोकाभिसन्तप्तः श्रुत्वा चासीत्सुदुःखितः।।2.41.8।।
transliteration: sa tamantaḥ pure ghoramārtaśabdaṃ mahīpatiḥ| putraśokābhisantaptaḥ śrutvā cāsītsuduḥkhitaḥ
translation: पुत्रशोकाभिसन्तप्तः oppressed with sorrow caused by the departure of his son, सः महीपतिः that king, अन्तःपुरे in the inner apartment (of the palace), घोरम् horible, तम् that, आर्त शब्दम्  wailings, श्रुत्वा having heard, सुदुःखितः आसीत् became increasingly distressed.
explanation: Upon hearing the dreadful wailing from the inner apartments of the palace, the king already devasted at the separation from his son, grew even more distressed.

shloka_text: नाग्निहोत्राण्यहूयन्त नापचन् गृहमेधिनः अकुर्वन्न प्रजाः कार्यं सूर्यश्चान्तरधीयत।।2.41.9।।
transliteration: nāgnihotrāṇyahūyanta nāpacan gṛhamedhinaḥ akurvanna prajāḥ kāryaṃ sūryaścāntaradhīyata
translation: अग्निहोत्राणि (Fire) in agnihotra sacrifice, नाहूयन्त was not invoked, गृहमेधिनः householders, नापचन् did not cook, प्रजाः people, कार्यम् daily chores, न अकुर्वन् did not do, सूर्यश्च even the Sun, अन्तरधीयत also obscured.
explanation: The sacred fire in agnihotra sacrifices was not invoked householders did not cook their food the people did not attend to their daily chores. And the Sun set.

shloka_text: व्यसृजन् कबलान्नागा गावो वत्सान्न पाययन्। पुत्रं प्रथमजं लब्ध्वा जननी नाभ्यनन्दत।।2.41.10।।
transliteration: vyasṛjan kabalānnāgā gāvo vatsānna pāyayan| putraṃ prathamajaṃ labdhvā jananī nābhyanandata
translation: नागाः elephants, कबलान् mouthful of food, व्यसृजन् shed, गावः cows, वत्सान् calves, न पाययन् did not suckle, जननी mothers, प्रथमजम् to the firstborn, पुत्रम् son, लब्धवा having begotten, नाभ्यनन्दत were not pleased.
explanation: Elephants dropped their morsel of food. Cows did not suckle their calves. Even the mothers were not pleased with their firstborn sons.

shloka_text: त्रिशङ्कुर्लोहिताङ्गश्च बृहस्पतिबुधावपि। दारुणा स्सोममभ्येत्य ग्रहास्सर्वे व्यवस्थिताः।।2.41.11।।
transliteration: triśaṅkurlohitāṅgaśca bṛhaspatibudhāvapi| dāruṇā ssomamabhyetya grahāssarve vyavasthitāḥ
translation: त्रिशङ्कु: Trishanku, लोहिताङ्गश्च Mars, बृहस्पतिबुधावपि Jupiter as also Mercury, दारुणाः fierce aspect, सर्वे all, ग्रहाः planets, सोमम् Moon, अभ्येत्य approaching, व्यवस्थिताः remained.
explanation: The constellation Trishanku, the planets Mars, Jupiter, Mercury and other fierce planets took their position near the Moon.

shloka_text: नक्षत्राणि गतार्चींषि ग्रहाश्च गततेजसः। विशाखास्तु सधूमाश्च नभसि प्रचकाशिरे।।2.41.12।।
transliteration: nakṣatrāṇi gatārcīṃṣi grahāśca gatatejasaḥ| viśākhāstu sadhūmāśca nabhasi pracakāśire
translation: नक्षत्राणि the constellation of stars, गतार्चींषि shorn of their radiance, ग्रहाश्च planets also, गततेजसः diminished  their brilliance, विशाखास्तु as for Visakha stars, सधूमाः with smoke, नभसि in the sky, प्रचकाशिरे were shining.
explanation: The stars were shorn of their radiance. The brilliance of the planets diminished. Shrouded in smoke the Visakha constellation appeared in the sky.

shloka_text: कालिकानिलवेगेन महोदधिरिवोत्थितः। रामे वनं प्रव्रजिते नगरं प्रचचाल तत्।।2.41.13।।
transliteration: kālikānilavegena mahodadhirivotthitaḥ| rāme vanaṃ pravrajite nagaraṃ pracacāla tat
translation: महोदधिः great ocean, कालिकानिलवेगेन इव like windblown dark clouds, उत्थितः aroused, रामे Rama, वनम् to the forest, प्रव्रजिते having been exiled, तत् नगरम् that city (of Ayodhya), प्रचचाल was shaken.
explanation: After Rama left for the forest, dark clouds appeared (in the sky) like the (waves of) the great ocean uplifted by the speed of the wind which shook the city.

shloka_text: दिशः पर्याकुलास्सर्वा स्तिमिरेणेव संवृताः। न ग्रहो नापि नक्षत्रं प्रचकाशे नकिञ्चन।।2.41.14।।
transliteration: diśaḥ paryākulāssarvā stimireṇeva saṃvṛtāḥ| na graho nāpi nakṣatraṃ pracakāśe nakiñcana
translation: सर्वाः all, दिशः cardinal points, पर्याकुलाः agitated, तिमिरेण with darkness, संवृताः इव covered, ग्रहः planet, न प्रचकाशे did not shine, नक्षत्रमपि even stars, किञ्चन anything, न not shining.
explanation: As if covered with darkness, all the cardinal points became agitated. No planet, no star nor was anything (any heavenly body) shining (in the sky).

shloka_text: अकस्मान्नागरस्सर्वो जनो दैन्यमुपागमत्। आहारे वा विहारे वा न कश्चिदकरोन्मनः।।2.41.15।।
transliteration: akasmānnāgarassarvo jano dainyamupāgamat| āhāre vā vihāre vā na kaścidakaronmanaḥ
translation: सर्वः all, नागरः relating to the city, जनः people, अकस्मात् suddenly, दैन्यम् helplessness, उपागमत् obtained, आहारे वा either in nourishment, विहारे वा or in recreation, कश्चित् none, मनः their mind, न अकरात् not done.
explanation: All of a sudden the people of the city became miserable. No one was interested in eating and enjoying (life).

shloka_text: शोकपर्यायसन्तप्त स्सततं दीर्घमुच्छवसन्। अयोध्यायां जनस्सर्व श्शुशोच जगतीपतिम्।।2.41.16।।
transliteration: śokaparyāyasantapta ssatataṃ dīrghamucchavasan| ayodhyāyāṃ janassarva śśuśoca jagatīpatim
translation: अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, सर्वः all, जनः people, शोकपर्यायसन्तप्तः afflicted with a series of grief, सततम् always, दीर्घम् deeply, उच्छवसन् heaving, जगतीपतिम् the lord of the world, शुशोच bewailed.
explanation: All the citizens of Ayodhya, afflicted with a series of grief and heaving deep sighs  ceaselessly bewailed at the sight of the lord of the world (Dasaratha).

shloka_text: बाष्पपर्याकुलमुखो राजमार्गगतो जनः। न हृष्टो लक्ष्यते कश्चित्सर्व श्शोकपरायणः।।2.41.17।।
transliteration: bāṣpaparyākulamukho rājamārgagato janaḥ| na hṛṣṭo lakṣyate kaścitsarva śśokaparāyaṇaḥ
translation: राजमार्गगतः in the royal highway, जनः people, बाष्पपर्याकुलमुखः faces full of tears, कश्चित् any body, हृष्टः happy, न लक्ष्ययते could not be seen, सर्वः all, शोकपरायणः was plunged in sorrow.
explanation: The faces of the people on the highway were turbid with tears. None looked happy. All were plunged in sorrow.

shloka_text: न वाति पवन श्शीतो न शशी सौम्यदर्शनः। न सूर्यस्तपते लोकं सर्वं पर्याकुलं जगत्।।2.41.18।।
transliteration: na vāti pavana śśīto na śaśī saumyadarśanaḥ| na sūryastapate lokaṃ sarvaṃ paryākulaṃ jagat
translation: पवनः wind, शीतः cool, न वाति does not blow, शशी Moon, सौम्यदर्शनः with pleasant appearance, न not, सूर्यः Sun, लोकम् the world, न तपते did not warm, सर्वम्  entire, जगत् world, पर्याकुलम् was agitated.
explanation: The breeze did not blow cool. No more did the Moon look pleasant. The Sun did not give warmth to the world. All the world was agitated.

shloka_text: अनर्थिनस्सुताः स्त्रीणां भर्तारो भ्रातरस्तथा। सर्वे सर्वं परित्यज्य राममेवान्वचिन्तयन्।।2.41.19।।
transliteration: anarthinassutāḥ strīṇāṃ bhartāro bhrātarastathā| sarve sarvaṃ parityajya rāmamevānvacintayan
translation: सुताः sons, भर्तारः husbands, स्त्रीणाम् towards women, अनर्थिनः had no concern, तथा similarly, भ्रातरः brothers, अनर्थिनः had no mutual interest, सर्वे all, सर्वम् everything, परित्यज्य having deserted, राममेव about Rama only, अन्वचिन्तयन् they thought.
explanation: Mothers stopped thinking of their sons and husbands of their wives. Brothers were no longer interested in each other. Every one deserted every one and thought only of Rama.

shloka_text: ये तु रामस्य सुहृद स्सर्वे ते मूढचेतसः। शोकभारेण चाक्रान्ता श्शयनं न जहुस्तदा।।2.41.20।।
transliteration: ye tu rāmasya suhṛda ssarve te mūḍhacetasaḥ| śokabhāreṇa cākrāntā śśayanaṃ na jahustadā
translation: तदा then, रामस्य Rama's, ये सुहृदः those friends, ते सर्वे all of them, मूढचेतसः bewildered, शोकभारेण with burden of sorrow, आक्रान्ताः afflicted, शयनम् couches, न जहुः did not leave.
explanation: All the friends of Rama were stupefied. Afflicted with the burden of sorrow they did not leave their bed.

shloka_text: ततस्त्वयोध्या रहिता महात्मना पुरन्दरेणेव मही सपर्वता। चचाल घोरं भयशोकपीडिता सनागयोधाश्वगणा ननाद च।।2.41.21।।
transliteration: tatastvayodhyā rahitā mahātmanā purandareṇeva mahī saparvatā| cacāla ghoraṃ bhayaśokapīḍitā sanāgayodhāśvagaṇā nanāda ca
translation: ततः thereafter, पुरन्दरेण by Indra, रहिता without, सपर्वता with mountains, महीव like earth, महात्मना magnanimous Rama, रहिता without, अयोध्या Ayodhya, भयशोकपीडिता agitated by fear and sorrow, घोरम् dreadfully, चचाल had shaken, सनागयोधाश्वगणा filled with hosts of  warriors, elephants and horses, ननाद च made sounds.
explanation: Without magnanimous Rama, Ayodhya thereafter looked like the earth along with its mountains bereft of Indra. Afflicted with fear and sorrow it started shaking dreadfully with the sounds of horses, elephants and warriors. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyfirst sarga of Ayodhyakanda of  the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: यावत्तु निर्यतस्तस्य रजोरूपमदृश्यत। नैवेक्ष्वाकुवरस्तावत्सञ्जहारात्मचक्षुषी।।2.42.1।।
transliteration: yāvattu niryatastasya rajorūpamadṛśyata| naivekṣvākuvarastāvatsañjahārātmacakṣuṣī
translation: तस्य that Rama, निर्यतः as he was going, रजोरूपम् the form of dust, यावत् as long as, अदृश्यत was visible, तावत् so long, इक्ष्वाकुवरः the best of Ikshvaku dynasty, king Dasaratha, आत्मचक्षुषी his eyes, नैव सञ्जहार did not withdraw.
explanation: As long as the dust raised by the wheels of the chariot of Rama (who was departing to the forest) was visible, Dasaratha, the best of the Ikshvakus, could not withdraw his eyes (from  Rama).
comments: Grief stricken Dasaratha falls down-- denounces Kaikeyi--reaches the chamber of Kausalya.

shloka_text: यावद्राजा प्रियं पुत्रं पश्यत्यत्यन्तधार्मिकम्। तावद्व्यवर्धते वास्य धरण्यां पुत्रदर्शने।।2.42.2।।
transliteration: yāvadrājā priyaṃ putraṃ paśyatyatyantadhārmikam| tāvadvyavardhate vāsya dharaṇyāṃ putradarśane
translation: राजा king, प्रियम् beloved, अत्यन्तधार्मिकम् exceedingly virtuous, पुत्रम् son, यावत् as long as, पश्यति was able to see, तावत् so long, अस्य his, पुत्रदर्शने for the sight of the son, धरण्याम् the dust on the earth, व्यवर्धतेव appeared growing.
explanation: So long as king Dasaratha was able to see his exceedingly virtuous and beloved  son (Rama), it appeared that his body kept rising from the earth to have a sight of his son.

shloka_text: न पश्यति रजोऽप्यस्य यदा रामस्य भूमिपः। तदाऽऽर्तश्च विषण्णश्च पपात धरणीतले।।2.42.3।।
transliteration: na paśyati rajo'pyasya yadā rāmasya bhūmipaḥ| tadā''rtaśca viṣaṇṇaśca papāta dharaṇītale
translation: भूमिपः the king, यदा when, अस्य रामस्य that Rama's, रजोऽपि even the dust, न पश्यति could not see, तदा then, आर्तः च stricken with grief, विषण्णः च with despondency, धरणीतले on the earth, पपात fell down.
explanation: When the king could no longer see even the dust, he fell on the ground, despondent and grief stricken.

shloka_text: तस्य दक्षिणमन्वागात्कौसल्या बाहुमङ्गना। वामं चास्यान्वगात्पार्श्वं कैकेयी भरतप्रिया।।2.42.4।।
transliteration: tasya dakṣiṇamanvāgātkausalyā bāhumaṅganā| vāmaṃ cāsyānvagātpārśvaṃ kaikeyī bharatapriyā
translation: अङ्गना wife, कौशल्या Kausalya, तस्य his, दक्षिणं बाहुम् right hand, अन्वगात् reached,  ,भरतप्रिया beloved (mother) of Bharata, कैकेयी च Kaikeyi, वामम् left, पार्श्वम् side, अन्वगात् reached.
explanation: Kausalya reached for the right hand of Dasaratha (to raise him up) and Kaikeyi the beloved (mother) of Bharata reached for his left.

shloka_text: तां नयेन च सम्पन्नो धर्मेण विनयेन च। उवाच राजा कैकेयीं समीक्ष्य व्यथितेन्द्रियः।।2.42.5।।
transliteration: tāṃ nayena ca sampanno dharmeṇa vinayena ca| uvāca rājā kaikeyīṃ samīkṣya vyathitendriyaḥ
translation: नयेन with rectitude, धर्मेण with virtue, विनयेन च also with humility, सम्पन्नः endowed with, राजा king, तां कैकेयीम् to that Kaikeyi, समीक्ष्य having seen, व्यथितेन्द्रियः one with painful senses reeling, उवाच said.
explanation: The king, endowed with rectitude, virtue and also humility, stared at  and said to Kaikeyi with pain.

shloka_text: कैकेयि मा ममाङ्गानि स्प्राक्षीस्त्वं दुष्टचारिणी। न हि त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छामि न भार्या न च बान्धवी।।2.42.6।।
transliteration: kaikeyi mā mamāṅgāni sprākṣīstvaṃ duṣṭacāriṇī| na hi tvāṃ draṣṭumicchāmi na bhāryā na ca bāndhavī
translation: कैकेयि O Kaikeyi, दुष्टचारिणी a woman of evil conduct, त्वम् you, मम my, अङ्गानि limbs, मा स्प्राक्षीः do not touch, त्वाम् you, द्रष्टुम् to look at, न हि इच्छामि do not wish, भार्या wife, न not, बान्धवी relation, न not.
explanation: O Kaikeyi you are a woman of evil conduct. Do not touch my body. I do not wish to see you. You are not my wife or my relation.

shloka_text: ये च त्वामनुजीवन्ति नाहं तेषां न ते मम। केवलार्थपरां हि त्वां त्यक्तधर्मां त्यजाम्यहम्।।2.42.7।।
transliteration: ye ca tvāmanujīvanti nāhaṃ teṣāṃ na te mama| kevalārthaparāṃ hi tvāṃ tyaktadharmāṃ tyajāmyaham
translation: ये च who, त्वाम् you, अनुजीवन्ति depend upon you for subsistence, तेषाम् their, अहम् I, न not, ते they, मम to me, न not, केवलार्थपराम् seeking your selfish interests alone, त्यक्तधर्माम्  deserting righteousness, त्वाम् you, अहम् I, त्यजामि abandon.
explanation: Your dependents have nothing to do with me nor I with them. I denounce you since you are a selfseeker without any sense off righteousness.

shloka_text: अगृह्णां यच्च ते पाणिमग्निं पर्यणयं च यत्। अनुजानामि तत्सर्वमस्मिन् लोके परत्र च।।2.42.8।।
transliteration: agṛhṇāṃ yacca te pāṇimagniṃ paryaṇayaṃ ca yat| anujānāmi tatsarvamasmin loke paratra ca
translation: ते your, पाणिम् hand, अगृह्णां (इति) यत् the fact of holding, अग्निम् of (to) fire, पर्यणयं च (इति) यत् the fact of having circumambulated, तत्सर्वम् all that, अस्मिन् in this, लोके world, परत्र च  in the next orld also, अनुजानामि renouncing.
explanation: I renounce the relationship established with you through marriage by taking your hand and circumambulating the fire, both in this world and in the next.

shloka_text: भरतश्चेत्प्रतीतः स्याद्राज्यं प्राप्येदमव्ययम्। यन्मे स दद्यात्पित्रर्थं मामां तद्दत्तमागमत्।।2.42.9।।
transliteration: bharataścetpratītaḥ syādrājyaṃ prāpyedamavyayam| yanme sa dadyātpitrarthaṃ māmāṃ taddattamāgamat
translation: अव्ययम् imperishable, (इदं) राज्यम् this kingdom, प्राप्य having secured, भरतः Bharata, प्रतीतः स्यात् चेत् if he is pleased, सः he, पित्रर्थम् in the form of funeral offerings, मे to me, यत् which, दद्यात् gives, तद्दत्तम् given by him, माम्  me, मागमत् may it not reach.
explanation: If Bharata feels pleased to secure this imperishable kingdom, then may his obsequial offerings at my funeral not reach me

shloka_text: अथ रेणुसमुध्वस्तं समुत्थाप्य नराधिपम्। न्यवर्तत तदा देवी कौशल्या शोककर्शिता।।2.42.10।।
transliteration: atha reṇusamudhvastaṃ samutthāpya narādhipam| nyavartata tadā devī kauśalyā śokakarśitā
translation: अथ then, रेणुसमुध्वस्तम् coated with dust, तं नराधिपम् to that king, समुत्थाप्य having lifted, देवी queen, कौशल्या Kausalya, शोककर्शिता emaciated due to sorrow, तदा then, न्यवर्तत  returned to her palace.
explanation: Then Kausalya, emaciated due to sorrow, lifted the king who was thoroughly coated with dust and returned to the palace.

shloka_text: हत्वेव ब्राह्मणं कामात् स्पृष्ट्वाग्निमिव पाणिना। अन्वतप्यत धर्मात्मा पुत्रं सञ्चिन्त्य तापसम् ।।2.42.11।।
transliteration: hatveva brāhmaṇaṃ kāmāt spṛṣṭvāgnimiva pāṇinā| anvatapyata dharmātmā putraṃ sañcintya tāpasam
translation: धर्मात्मा virtuous one, तापसम् wearing the robes of an ascetic, पुत्रम् son, सञ्चिन्त्य remembering, कामात् intentionally, ब्राह्मणम् to a brahmin, हत्वेव as if slew, पाणिना with hand, अग्निम् to fire, स्पृष्ट्वा इव as if touched, अन्वतप्यत plunged in grief.
explanation: That virtuous Dasaratha, recalling (the sight of) his son with the robes of an ascetic, burned with remorse as if he had intentionally slain a brahmin or placed his hand in fire.

shloka_text: निवृत्त्यैव निवृत्त्यैव सीदतो रथवर्त्मसु। राज्ञो नातिबभौ रूपं ग्रस्तस्यांशुमतो यथा।।2.42.12।।
transliteration: nivṛttyaiva nivṛttyaiva sīdato rathavartmasu| rājño nātibabhau rūpaṃ grastasyāṃśumato yathā
translation: रथवर्त्मसु trail of the chariot, निवृत्त्यैव निवृत्त्यैव turning again and again, सीदतः grieving, राज्ञः  the king's, रूपम् countenance, ग्रस्तस्य as if swallowed by Rahu, अंशुमत: यथा like Sun,  नातिबभौ did not shine.
explanation: Turning back again and again at the trail of (Rama's) chariot, the grieving king appeared lustreless like the Sun in eclipse.

shloka_text: विललाप च दुःखार्तः प्रियं पुत्रमनुस्मरन्। नगरान्तमनुप्राप्तं बुध्वा पुत्रमथाब्रवीत्।।2.42.13।।
transliteration: vilalāpa ca duḥkhārtaḥ priyaṃ putramanusmaran| nagarāntamanuprāptaṃ budhvā putramathābravīt
translation: प्रियम् beloved, पुत्रम् son, अनुस्मरन् reflecting, दुःखार्तः tortured with sorrow, विललाप च  lamented, अथ then, पुत्रम् son, नगरान्तम् end of the city, अनुप्राप्तम् havng reached, बुध्वा having realised, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: The griefstricken king began to lament thinking of his beloved son, and (suddenly) realizing that his son had crossed the limits of the city, said:

shloka_text: वाहननां च मुख्यानां वहतां तं ममात्मजम्। पदानि पथि दृश्यन्ते स महात्मा न दृश्यते।।2.42.14।।
transliteration: vāhananāṃ ca mukhyānāṃ vahatāṃ taṃ mamātmajam| padāni pathi dṛśyante sa mahātmā na dṛśyate
translation: मम my, आत्मजम् son, तम् that Rama, वहताम् carrying, मुख्यानाम् preeminent, वाहनानाम्  horses', पदानि hoofprints, पथि in the path, दृश्यन्ते are seen, महात्मा magnanimous, सः Rama, न दृश्यत is not to be seen.
explanation: I can see the marks of the hooves of the splendid horses carrying my son on the highway but not that magnanimous Rama.

shloka_text: यः सुखेषूपधानेषु शेते चन्दनरूषितः। वीज्यमानो महार्हाभिः स्त्रीभिर्मम सुतोत्तमः।।2.42.15।। स नूनं क्वचिदेवाद्य वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः। काष्ठं वा यदि वाश्मानमुपधाय शयिष्यते।।2.42.16।।
transliteration: yaḥ sukheṣūpadhāneṣu śete candanarūṣitaḥ| vījyamāno mahārhābhiḥ strībhirmama sutottamaḥ sa nūnaṃ kvacidevādya vṛkṣamūlamupāśritaḥ| kāṣṭhaṃ vā yadi vāśmānamupadhāya śayiṣyate
translation: यः मम सुतोत्तमः best among my  sons, चन्दनरूषितः daubed with sandal cream, महार्हाभिः graceful, स्त्रीभिः by women, वीज्यमानः being fanned, सुखेषु luxurious, उपधानेषु on cushions, शेते was sleeping, सः such Rama, अद्य today, नूनम् surely, क्वचिदेव some where, वृक्षमूलम् at the foot of a tree, उपाश्रितः taking refuge, काष्ठं a log, यदि वा or, आश्मानम् a stone, उपधाय using as pillow, शयिष्यते he will sleep.
explanation: Rama, the best of all my sons who, smeared with sandalpaste and fanned by graceful women used to sleep (with his head) on comfortable cushions will surely, from now on, lie down somewhere at the foot of a tree, (his head) pillowed upon a piece of wood or stone.

shloka_text: यः सुखेषूपधानेषु शेते चन्दनरूषितः। वीज्यमानो महार्हाभिः स्त्रीभिर्मम सुतोत्तमः।।2.42.15।। स नूनं क्वचिदेवाद्य वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः। काष्ठं वा यदि वाश्मानमुपधाय शयिष्यते।।2.42.16।।
transliteration: yaḥ sukheṣūpadhāneṣu śete candanarūṣitaḥ| vījyamāno mahārhābhiḥ strībhirmama sutottamaḥ sa nūnaṃ kvacidevādya vṛkṣamūlamupāśritaḥ| kāṣṭhaṃ vā yadi vāśmānamupadhāya śayiṣyate
translation: यः मम सुतोत्तमः best among my  sons, चन्दनरूषितः daubed with sandal cream, महार्हाभिः graceful, स्त्रीभिः by women, वीज्यमानः being fanned, सुखेषु luxurious, उपधानेषु on cushions, शेते was sleeping, सः such Rama, अद्य today, नूनम् surely, क्वचिदेव some where, वृक्षमूलम् at the foot of a tree, उपाश्रितः taking refuge, काष्ठं a log, यदि वा or, आश्मानम् a stone, उपधाय using as pillow, शयिष्यते he will sleep.
explanation: Rama, the best of all my sons who, smeared with sandalpaste and fanned by graceful women used to sleep (with his head) on comfortable cushions will surely, from now on, lie down somewhere at the foot of a tree, (his head) pillowed upon a piece of wood or stone.

shloka_text: उत्थास्यति च मेदिन्याः कृपणः पांसुकुण्ठितः। विनिश्श्वसन् प्रस्रवणात्करेणूनामिवर्षभः।।2.42.17।।
transliteration: utthāsyati ca medinyāḥ kṛpaṇaḥ pāṃsukuṇṭhitaḥ| viniśśvasan prasravaṇātkareṇūnāmivarṣabhaḥ
translation: करेणूनाम् of female elephants, ऋषभः lord, bull elephant, प्रस्रवणात् इव like from Prasravana mountain, विनिश्वसन् heaving sighs, पांसुकुण्ठितः crusted with dust, कृपणः unfortunate     Rama, मेदिन्याः from the ground, उत्थास्यति च will rise up.
explanation: That unfortunate Rama, having been covered with dust, will get up from the ground sighing like a bull elephant rising from mount Prasravana.

shloka_text: द्रक्ष्यन्ति नूनं पुरुषा दीर्घबाहुं वनेचराः। राममुत्थाय गच्छन्तं लोकनाथमनाथवत्।।2.42.18।।
transliteration: drakṣyanti nūnaṃ puruṣā dīrghabāhuṃ vanecarāḥ| rāmamutthāya gacchantaṃ lokanāthamanāthavat
translation: दीर्घबाहुम् longarmed, लोकनाथं lord of the world, अनाथवत् like without a protector, उत्थाय  rising (from the ground), गच्छन्तम् walking, रामम् Rama, नूनम् surely, वनेचराः forestdwellers, पुरुषाः men, द्रक्ष्यन्ति they will see.
explanation: Surely the forestrovers will be gazing upon the longarmed Rama, protector of the world, as he rises (from the ground) and wanders in the jungle unprotected.

shloka_text: सा नूनं जनकस्येष्टा सुता सुखसदोचिता। कण्टकाक्रमणाक्लान्ता वनमद्य गमिष्यति।।2.42.19।।
transliteration: sā nūnaṃ janakasyeṣṭā sutā sukhasadocitā| kaṇṭakākramaṇāklāntā vanamadya gamiṣyati
translation: सुखसदोचिता accustomed to comforts, जनकस्य Janaka's, इष्टा beloved, सुता daughter, सा Janaki, कण्टकाक्रमणक्लान्ता troubled due to piercing of thorns, अद्य now, वनम् to the forest, गमिष्यति will go.
explanation: Sita, beloved daughter of Janaka, who is accustomed to comforts, will now wander in the forest troubled by piercing thorns.

shloka_text: अनभिज्ञा वनानां सा नूनं भयमुपैष्यति। श्वापदानर्दितं श्रुत्वा गम्भीरं रोमहर्षणम्।।2.42.20।।
transliteration: anabhijñā vanānāṃ sā nūnaṃ bhayamupaiṣyati| śvāpadānarditaṃ śrutvā gambhīraṃ romaharṣaṇam
translation: वनानाम् of the forests, अनभिज्ञा un acquainted, सा Sita, नूनम् surely, गम्भीरम् deep and fearful, रोमहर्षणम् causing horripilation, श्वापदानर्दितम् roaring of wild animals, श्रुत्वा having heard, भयम् fear, उपैष्यति will obtain.
explanation: Sita who knows not the forest will now live in terror, listening to the hairraising, horrible roars of wild animals.

shloka_text: सकामा भव कैकेयि विधवा राज्यमावस। न हि तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं विना जीवितुमुत्सहे।।2.42.21।।
transliteration: sakāmā bhava kaikeyi vidhavā rājyamāvasa| na hi taṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ vinā jīvitumutsahe
translation: कैकेयि Kaikeyi, सकामा भव desire be fulfilled, विधवा as widow, राज्यम् kingdom, आवस inhabit, पुरुषव्याघ्रम् tiger among men, तं विना without him, जीवितुम् to live, न उत्सहे हि do not desire.
explanation: O Kaikeyi, your desire is fulfilled.  Rule the kingdom as a widow. Without Rama, the best of men, I don't desire to live.

shloka_text: इत्येवं विलपन् राजा जनौघेनाभिसंवृतः। अपस्नात इवारिष्टं प्रविवेश पुरोत्तमम्।।2.42.22।।
transliteration: ityevaṃ vilapan rājā janaughenābhisaṃvṛtaḥ| apasnāta ivāriṣṭaṃ praviveśa purottamam
translation: इत्येवम् in this manner, विलपन् lamenting, राजा king, जनौघेन by the multitude of people, अभिसंवृतः surrounded, अपस्नातः one who has taken inauspicious (funeral) bath, अरिष्टं इव like an ominous, पुरोत्तमम् best of cities (Ayodhya), प्रविवेश entered.
explanation: Thus the king, who looked like one after the inauspicious (funeral) bath, surrounded by streams of people entered the most beautiful city (Ayodhya) which portended misfortune.

shloka_text: शून्यचत्वरवेश्मान्तां संवृतापणदेवताम्। क्लान्तदुर्बलदुःखार्तां नात्याकीर्णमहापथाम्।।2.42.23।। तामवेक्ष्य पुरीं सर्वां राममेवानुचिन्तयन्। विलपन् प्राविशद्राजा गृहं सूर्य इवाम्बुदम्।।2.42.24।।
transliteration: śūnyacatvaraveśmāntāṃ saṃvṛtāpaṇadevatām| klāntadurbaladuḥkhārtāṃ nātyākīrṇamahāpathām tāmavekṣya purīṃ sarvāṃ rāmamevānucintayan| vilapan prāviśadrājā gṛhaṃ sūrya ivāmbudam
translation: शून्यचत्वरवेश्मान्ताम् where the courtyards or the mansions were deserted, संवृतापणदेवताम् where temples and marketplaces were closed, क्लान्तदुर्बलदुःखार्ताम् weak and exhausted with with grief, नात्याकीर्णमहापथाम् the highways no longer crowded, ताम् that, सर्वाम् entire, पुरीम् to city of Ayodhya, आवेक्ष्य having seen, राजा king, राममेव about Rama only, अनुचिन्तयन् thinking, विलपन् lamenting, सूर्यः sun, अम्बुदम् इव like clouds, प्राविशत् entered.
explanation: There the mansions and squares on the highways were all deserted. The temples and marketplaces were closed. The people were weak, fatigued and tormented with grief. The highways were not much crowded. Having seen such a sight of the city on all sides, lamenting and brooding over Rama, Dasaratha entered his palace like the Sun plunging into a cloud.

shloka_text: शून्यचत्वरवेश्मान्तां संवृतापणदेवताम्। क्लान्तदुर्बलदुःखार्तां नात्याकीर्णमहापथाम्।।2.42.23।। तामवेक्ष्य पुरीं सर्वां राममेवानुचिन्तयन्। विलपन् प्राविशद्राजा गृहं सूर्य इवाम्बुदम्।।2.42.24।।
transliteration: śūnyacatvaraveśmāntāṃ saṃvṛtāpaṇadevatām| klāntadurbaladuḥkhārtāṃ nātyākīrṇamahāpathām tāmavekṣya purīṃ sarvāṃ rāmamevānucintayan| vilapan prāviśadrājā gṛhaṃ sūrya ivāmbudam
translation: शून्यचत्वरवेश्मान्ताम् where the courtyards or the mansions were deserted, संवृतापणदेवताम् where temples and marketplaces were closed, क्लान्तदुर्बलदुःखार्ताम् weak and exhausted with with grief, नात्याकीर्णमहापथाम् the highways no longer crowded, ताम् that, सर्वाम् entire, पुरीम् to city of Ayodhya, आवेक्ष्य having seen, राजा king, राममेव about Rama only, अनुचिन्तयन् thinking, विलपन् lamenting, सूर्यः sun, अम्बुदम् इव like clouds, प्राविशत् entered.
explanation: There the mansions and squares on the highways were all deserted. The temples and marketplaces were closed. The people were weak, fatigued and tormented with grief. The highways were not much crowded. Having seen such a sight of the city on all sides, lamenting and brooding over Rama, Dasaratha entered his palace like the Sun plunging into a cloud.

shloka_text: महाह्रदमिवाक्षोभ्यं सुपर्णेन हृतोरगम्। रामेण रहितं वेश्म वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च।।2.42.25।।
transliteration: mahāhradamivākṣobhyaṃ suparṇena hṛtoragam| rāmeṇa rahitaṃ veśma vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca
translation: रामेण with Rama, वैदेह्या with Sita, लक्ष्मणेन च also with Lakshmana, रहितम् absent, वेश्म palace, सुपर्णेन by Suparna, हृतोरगम् a serpent snatched away, अक्षोभ्यम् an unperturbed, महाह्रदम् इव like a great tank
explanation: The palace without Rama, Lakshmana and Sita, stood like a vast, unperturbed lake with serpents snatched away by Suparna (Garuda).

shloka_text: अथ गद्गदशब्दस्तु विलपन्मनुजाधिपः। उवाच मृदुमन्दार्थं वचनं दीनमस्वरम्।।2.42.26।।
transliteration: atha gadgadaśabdastu vilapanmanujādhipaḥ| uvāca mṛdumandārthaṃ vacanaṃ dīnamasvaram
translation: अथ thereupon, मनुजा (वसुधा) धिपः lord of men, गद्गदशब्दः with choked throat, विलपन्  lamenting, मृदु gently, मन्दार्थम् in low voice, अस्वरम् feeble, दीनं वचनम् in melancholic tones, उवाच said.
explanation: Thereupon Dasaratha lamenting with his throat choked addressed (his attendants) in a low, feeble, melancholic, gentle voice:

shloka_text: कौशल्यायां गृहं शीघ्रं राममातुर्नयन्तु माम्। न ह्यन्यत्र ममाश्वासो हृदयस्य भविष्यति।।2.42.27।।
transliteration: kauśalyāyāṃ gṛhaṃ śīghraṃ rāmamāturnayantu mām| na hyanyatra mamāśvāso hṛdayasya bhaviṣyati
translation: राममातुः Rama's mother, कौशल्यायाः Kausalya's, गृहम् apartment, माम् me, शीघ्रम् quickly, नयन्तु be taken, मम हृदयस्य for my heart, अन्यत्र in any other place, आश्वासः solace, न भविष्यति हि not possible.
explanation: Take me quickly to the apartment of Rama's mother, Kausalya. There is no other place where my heart can find solace.

shloka_text: इति ब्रुवन्तं राजानमनयन् द्वारदर्शिनः। कौशल्याया गृहं तत्र न्यवेश्यत विनीतवत्।।2.42.28।।
transliteration: iti bruvantaṃ rājānamanayan dvāradarśinaḥ| kauśalyāyā gṛhaṃ tatra nyaveśyata vinītavat
translation: इति in this way,  ब्रुवन्तम् while saying, राजानम् king Dasaratha, द्वारदर्शिनः  doorkeepers, कौशल्यायाः Kausalya's, गृहम् apartment, अनयन् brought him, तत्र there, विनीतवत् respectfully, न्यवेश्यत he was made to rest.
explanation: Having heard the king, the doorkeepers took  him to the apartment of Kausalya and  there respectfully made him rest.

shloka_text: ततस्तस्य प्रविष्टस्य कौशल्याया निवेशनम्। अधिरुह्यापि शयनं बभूव लुलितं मनः।।2.42.29।।
transliteration: tatastasya praviṣṭasya kauśalyāyā niveśanam| adhiruhyāpi śayanaṃ babhūva lulitaṃ manaḥ
translation: ततः then, कौशल्यायाः Kausalya's, निवेशनम् residence, प्रविष्टस्य having entered, तस्य his, मनः mind, शयनम् couch, अधिरुह्यापि though having climbed, लुलितम् बभूव was tossed about.
explanation: His mind tossed restlessly although he entered Kausalya's palace and climbed into the couch.

shloka_text: पुत्रद्वयविहीनं च स्नुषयापि विवर्जितम्। अपश्यद्भवनं राजा नष्टचन्द्रमिवाम्बरम्।।2.42.30।।
transliteration: putradvayavihīnaṃ ca snuṣayāpi vivarjitam| apaśyadbhavanaṃ rājā naṣṭacandramivāmbaram
translation: राजा king, पुत्रद्वयविहीनम् without his two sons, स्नुषयापि also by daughterinlaw, विवर्जितम् deserted, भवनम् palace, नष्टचन्द्रम् devoid of the Moon, अम्बरम् इव like the sky, अपश्यत् he saw.
explanation: To the king, the palace deserted by his two sons and his daughterinlaw, seemed like the sky without the Moon.

shloka_text: तच्च दृष्ट्वा महाराजो भुजमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्। उच्चैस्स्वरेण चुक्रोश हा राघव जहासि माम्।।2.42.31।।
transliteration: tacca dṛṣṭvā mahārājo bhujamudyamya vīryavān| uccaissvareṇa cukrośa hā rāghava jahāsi mām
translation: वीर्यवान् valiant, महाराजः the great king, तत् that palace, दृष्ट्वा having seen, भुजम् his hands, उद्यम्य  having lifted up, हा राघव Oh Rama, माम् me, जहासि are forsaking, उच्चौः स्वरेण in loud voice, चुक्रोश screamed.
explanation: The valiant maharaja looked around that palace, lifted up his arms and shouted in a loud voice, Oh scion of the Raghus (Rama) you have forsaken me.

shloka_text: सुखिता बत तं कालं जीविष्यन्ति नरोत्तमाः। परिष्वजन्तो ये रामं द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुनरागतम्।।2.42.32।।
transliteration: sukhitā bata taṃ kālaṃ jīviṣyanti narottamāḥ| pariṣvajanto ye rāmaṃ drakṣyanti punarāgatam
translation: ये नरोत्तमाः those fortunate people, तं कालम् till that tme, जीविष्यन्ति will live, पुनः again, आगतम् return, रामम् Rama, परिष्वजन्तः while embracing, सुखिताः happily, द्रक्ष्यन्ति will see, बत what a pity?
explanation: Oh how fortunate are those best of men who will live until that time to see Rama return and embrace him.

shloka_text: अथ रात्र्यां प्रपन्नायां कालरात्र्यामिवात्मनः। अर्धरात्रे दशरथः कौशल्यामिदमब्रवीत्।।2.42.33।।
transliteration: atha rātryāṃ prapannāyāṃ kālarātryāmivātmanaḥ| ardharātre daśarathaḥ kauśalyāmidamabravīt
translation: अथ then, दशरथः Dasaratha, आत्मनः for himself, कालरात्र्यामिव like the night of death, रात्र्याम् night, प्रपन्नायाम् had set in, अर्धरात्रे in the middle of the night, कौशल्याम् addressing Kausalya, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: In the middle of the night which, for him, felt like the night of death Dasaratha said to Kausalya thus:

shloka_text: रामं मेऽनुगता दृष्टिरद्यापि न निवर्तते। न त्वा पश्यामि कौसल्ये साधु मां पाणिना स्पृश।।2.42.34।।
transliteration: rāmaṃ me'nugatā dṛṣṭiradyāpi na nivartate| na tvā paśyāmi kausalye sādhu māṃ pāṇinā spṛśa
translation: कौशल्ये O Kausalya, रामम् Rama, अनुगता having followed, मे दृष्टिः my sight, अद्यापि even now, न निवर्तते has not returned, त्वा you, साधु clearly, न पश्यामि unable to see, माम् me, पाणिना with your hand, स्पृश touch.
explanation: O Kausalya, my sight that had followed Rama has not yet returned. I cannot see you clearly. Please touch me with your hand.

shloka_text: तं राममेवानुविचिन्तयन्तं समीक्ष्य देवी शयने नरेन्द्रम्। उपोपविश्याधिकमार्तरूपा विनिश्वसन्ती विललाप कृच्छ्रम्।।2.42.35।।
transliteration: taṃ rāmamevānuvicintayantaṃ samīkṣya devī śayane narendram| upopaviśyādhikamārtarūpā viniśvasantī vilalāpa kṛcchram
translation: देवी Kausalya, शयने in bed, रामम् एव Rama alone, अनुविचिन्तयन्तम् one who was continuously brooding, तं नरेन्द्रम् that king, समीक्ष्य having seen, उपोपविश्य sitting by his side, अधिकम् extremely, आर्तरूपा distressed, विनिश्वसन्ती sighing deeply, कृच्छ्रम् being in painful situation, विललाप lamented.
explanation: Having seen the king in bed brooding over Rama, the queen, (Kausalya), sitting by his side, sighed and lamented, deeply anguished. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortysecond sarga of Ayodhyakanda of  the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततः समीक्ष्य शयने सन्नं शोकेन पार्थिवम्। कौशल्या पुत्रशोकार्ता तमुवाच महीपतिम्।।2.43.1।।
transliteration: tataḥ samīkṣya śayane sannaṃ śokena pārthivam| kauśalyā putraśokārtā tamuvāca mahīpatim
translation: ततः then, पुत्रशोकार्ता struck by grief on account of her son's departure, कौशल्या  Kausalya, शयने on the couch, शोकेन due to grief, सन्नम् exhausted, पार्थिवम् king, समीक्ष्य having gazed, तं महीपतिम् to that lord of the world, Dasaratha, उवाच said.
explanation: Struck by the grief of her son's departure, Kausalya looked at the king who lay on the couch completely exhausted and said to him.
comments: Lamentations of Kausalya.

shloka_text: राघवे नरशार्दूले विषमुप्त्वाहिजिह्मगा। विचरिष्यति कैकेयी निर्मुक्तेव हि पन्नगी।।2.43.2।।
transliteration: rāghave naraśārdūle viṣamuptvāhijihmagā| vicariṣyati kaikeyī nirmukteva hi pannagī
translation: अहिजह्मगा moving obliquely like a serpent, कैकेयी Kaikeyi, नरशार्दूले tiger (best) among men, राघवे in Rama, विषम् venom, उप्त्वा having sown out, निर्मुक्ता casting off the slough, पन्नगी इव like a sheserpent, विचरिष्यति will wander about.
explanation: Moving crookedly like a snake, Kaikeyi has released her venom on Rama, the best among men. Now she will move about freely like a sheserpent that has cast off its slough.

shloka_text: विवास्य रामं सुभगा लब्धकामा समाहिता। त्रासयिष्यति मां भूयो दुष्टाहिरिव वेश्मनि।।2.43.3।।
transliteration: vivāsya rāmaṃ subhagā labdhakāmā samāhitā| trāsayiṣyati māṃ bhūyo duṣṭāhiriva veśmani
translation: सुभगा happly, (Kaikeyi), रामम् Rama, विवास्य having banished, लब्दकामा having satisfied her desires, भूयः again, वेश्मनि in the house, दुष्टाहिरिव like a vicious serpent, माम् me, समाहिता accomplished, त्रासयिष्यति will torture me.
explanation: Having banished Rama, she is now happy with her desires fulfilled. And like a vicious serpent living in the house she will again frighten me.

shloka_text: अथ स्म नगरे रामश्चरन् भैक्षं गृहे वसेत्। कामकारो वरं दातुमपि दासं ममात्मजम्।।2.43.4।।
transliteration: atha sma nagare rāmaścaran bhaikṣaṃ gṛhe vaset| kāmakāro varaṃ dātumapi dāsaṃ mamātmajam
translation: मम my, आत्मजम् son, दासम् as slave, दातुम् अपि even to give, वरम् is better, अथ  thereafter, रामः Rama, कामकारः discharging the duties, नगरे in the city (Ayodhya), भैक्षम् food obtained by begging, चरन् moving about, गृहे in the house, वसेत् would have lived.
explanation: It would have been better had I offered her my son as a slave. He would have lived on in the house by doing his duties and begging his food in the city.

shloka_text: पातयित्वा तु कैकेय्या रामं स्थानाद्यथेष्टतः। प्रदिष्टो रक्षसां भागः पर्वणीवाहिताग्निना।।2.43.5।।
transliteration: pātayitvā tu kaikeyyā rāmaṃ sthānādyatheṣṭataḥ| pradiṣṭo rakṣasāṃ bhāgaḥ parvaṇīvāhitāgninā
translation: कैकेय्या of Kaikeyi, यथेष्टतः according to her whim, रामम् to Rama, स्थानात् from his place, पातयित्वा having thrown down, अहिताग्निना by the sacrificers, पर्वणि on the new moon days, रक्षसाम् to rakshasas, भागः इव like the share, प्रदिष्टः is given.
explanation: You have thrown away Rama from his place as per the whim of Kaikeyi, like the share of offering meant for gods given away to rakshasas by the sacrificers on the new Moon days.

shloka_text: गजराजगतिर्वीरो महाबाहुर्धनुर्धरः। वनमाविशते नूनं सभार्य स्सह लक्ष्मणः।।2.43.6।।
transliteration: gajarājagatirvīro mahābāhurdhanurdharaḥ| vanamāviśate nūnaṃ sabhārya ssaha lakṣmaṇaḥ
translation: गजराजगतिः having the gait of the king of the elephants, वीरः hero, महाबाहुः mightyarmed,  धनुर्धरः archer Rama, सभार्यः with wife, सहलक्ष्मणः with Lakshmana, नूनम् surely, वनम् forest, आविशते is entering.
explanation: My mightyarmed son, a great archer and a hero, Rama whose gait is like that of the king of elephants, must be entering the forest along with his consort Sita and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: वने त्वदृष्टदुःखानां केकय्यानुमते त्वया। त्यक्तानां वनवासाय कान्ववस्था भविष्यति।।2.43.7।।
transliteration: vane tvadṛṣṭaduḥkhānāṃ kekayyānumate tvayā| tyaktānāṃ vanavāsāya kānvavasthā bhaviṣyati
translation: अदृष्टदुःखानाम् who have never seen suffering, कैकेय्याः Kaikeyi's, अनुमते her desire, त्वया by you, वनवासाय to dwell in the forest, त्यक्तानाम् have been abandoned, वने in the  forest, का नु what, अवस्था भविष्यति will be their state.
explanation: You have banished them as per the desire of Kaikeyi. What will be their plight in the forest, for they have never experienced any hardship earlier

shloka_text: ते रत्नहीनास्तरुणाः फलकाले विवासिताः। कथं वत्स्यन्ति कृपणाः फलमूलैः कृताशनाः।।2.43.8।।
transliteration: te ratnahīnāstaruṇāḥ phalakāle vivāsitāḥ| kathaṃ vatsyanti kṛpaṇāḥ phalamūlaiḥ kṛtāśanāḥ
translation: रत्नहीनाः deprived of best of things, फलकाले at the time of fruition (enjoyment), विवासिताः having been exiled, तरुणाः young people, ते they, कृपणाः living in misery, फलमूलैः fruits and roots, कृताशनाः for food, कथम् how, वत्स्यन्ति will they live?
explanation: Deprived of all costly things they have been banished at the tender age of youth, a time for enjoying their lives. How will they lead a miserable life subsisting on fruits and roots?

shloka_text: अपीदानीं स कालस्स्यान्मम शोकक्षय श्शिवः। सभार्यं यत्सह भ्रात्रा पश्येयमिह राघवम्।।2.43.9।।
transliteration: apīdānīṃ sa kālassyānmama śokakṣaya śśivaḥ| sabhāryaṃ yatsaha bhrātrā paśyeyamiha rāghavam
translation: यत् when, सभार्यम् with wife, राघवम् Rama, सह भ्रात्रा with Lakshmana, इह here, पश्येयम् I shall see, शोकक्षयः annhilation of sorrow, शिवः auspcious, सः कालः that time, इदानीम्  now, मम to me, अपि स्यात् will it come?
explanation: Will there ever be that auspicious moment to end my sorrow? When I can see  Rama here along with his wife and brother?

shloka_text: श्रृत्वैवोपस्थितौ वीरौ कदायोध्या भविष्यति। यशस्विनी हृष्टजना सूच्छ्रितध्वजमालिनी।।2.43.10।।
transliteration: śrṛtvaivopasthitau vīrau kadāyodhyā bhaviṣyati| yaśasvinī hṛṣṭajanā sūcchritadhvajamālinī
translation: वीरौ the two heroes, उपस्थितौ having returned, श्रुत्वैव hearing, यशस्विनी famous, अयोध्या Ayodhya, हृष्टजना with cheerful people, सूच्छ्रितध्वजमालिनी uplifted flags, कदा when?, भविष्यति will it be?
explanation: When will the city of Ayodhya attain that glory when having heard that both the brave brothers have come back the people will rejoice and fill it with uplifted banners?

shloka_text: कदा प्रेक्ष्य नरव्याघ्रावरण्यात्पुनरागतौ। नन्दिष्यति पुरी हृष्टा समुद्र इव पर्वणि।।2.43.11।।
transliteration: kadā prekṣya naravyāghrāvaraṇyātpunarāgatau| nandiṣyati purī hṛṣṭā samudra iva parvaṇi
translation: अरण्यात् from the forest, पुनः again, आगतौ having come back, नरव्याघ्रौ tigers (best) among men, Rama and Lakshmana, प्रेक्ष्य having seen, पुरी the city of Ayodhya, पर्वणि on a fullmoon day, समुद्र इव like the sea, हृष्टा overflow (overjoyed), कदा when, नन्दिष्यति will it rejoice?
explanation: When will, like the swelling sea on a full Moon day, the city hail the return of Rama and Lakshmana, the best among men?

shloka_text: कदाऽयोध्यां महाबाहुः पुरीं वीरः प्रवेक्ष्यति। पुरस्कृत्य रथे सीतां वृषभो गोवधूमिव।।2.43.12।।
transliteration: kadā'yodhyāṃ mahābāhuḥ purīṃ vīraḥ pravekṣyati| puraskṛtya rathe sītāṃ vṛṣabho govadhūmiva
translation: महाबाहुः mightyarmed, वीरः hero, वृषभः bull, गोवधूमिव like cow, सीताम् Sita, रथे on the chariot, पुरस्कृत्य placing in front, अयोध्यां पुरीम् to the city of Ayodhya, कदा when, प्रवेक्ष्यति will enter?
explanation: When will the mightyarmed hero (Rama) enter the city of Ayodhya with Sita in front in the chariot, like a bull following the cow?

shloka_text: कदा प्राणिसहस्राणि राजमार्गे ममात्मजौ। लाजैरवकिरिष्यन्ति प्रविशन्तावरिन्दमौ।।2.43.13।।
transliteration: kadā prāṇisahasrāṇi rājamārge mamātmajau| lājairavakiriṣyanti praviśantāvarindamau
translation: प्रविशन्तौ when they enter, अरिन्दमौ subduers of enemies, मम my, आत्मजौ sons, राजमार्गे on the highway, प्राणिसहस्राणि thousands of people, लाजैः with parched grain, कदा when, अवकिरिष्यन्ति shower.
explanation: When will the people in their thousands shower the parched grain on the highway when my sons (Rama and Lakshmana), subduers of enemies, enter the city?

shloka_text: प्रविशन्तौ कदाऽयोध्यां द्रक्ष्यामि शुभकुण्डलौ। उदग्रायुधनिस्त्रिंशौ सश्रृङ्गाविव पर्वतौ।।2.43.14।।
transliteration: praviśantau kadā'yodhyāṃ drakṣyāmi śubhakuṇḍalau| udagrāyudhanistriṃśau saśrṛṅgāviva parvatau
translation: अयोध्याम् of Ayodhya, प्रविशन्तौ when they enter, शुभकुण्डलौ wearing auspicious earrings, उदग्रायुधनिस्त्रिंशौ with powerful weapons and swords raised high, सश्रृङ्गौ with peaks, पर्वताविव like mountains, कदा when, द्रक्ष्यामि shall I see?
explanation: When shall I see both of them wearing auspicious earrings and holding poweful weapons (bows) and swords high, like two mountain peaks?

shloka_text: कदासुमनसः कन्याद्विजातीनां फलानि च। प्रदिशन्तः पुरीं हृष्टाः करिष्यन्ति प्रदक्षिणम्।।2.43.15।।
transliteration: kadāsumanasaḥ kanyādvijātīnāṃ phalāni ca| pradiśantaḥ purīṃ hṛṣṭāḥ kariṣyanti pradakṣiṇam
translation: हृष्टाः delighted, कन्याद्विजातीनाम् to young girls and to brahmins, सुमनसः flowers, फलानि च fruits also, प्रदिशन्तः while offering, कदा when, पुरीम् the city, प्रदक्षिणम् circling, करिष्यन्ति will do?
explanation: When will I see them delightfully moving round the city with young brahmin girls offering them flowers and fruits.

shloka_text: कदा परिणतो बुद्ध्या वयसा चामरप्रभः। अभ्युपैष्यति धर्मज्ञस्त्रिवर्ष इव मां ललन्।।2.43.16।।
transliteration: kadā pariṇato buddhyā vayasā cāmaraprabhaḥ| abhyupaiṣyati dharmajñastrivarṣa iva māṃ lalan
translation: अमरप्रभः possessing the lustre of gods, धर्मज्ञः knower of righteousness (Rama), बुद्ध्या in wisdom, वयसा च in age, परिणतः fully mature, त्रिवर्षः इव like a three year old boy, ललन् playfully, माम् me, कदा when, अभ्युपैष्यति will he reach?
explanation: When will Rama, the knower of righteousness, possessing the lustre of gods, and fully mature in age and wisdom come back to me playfully like a threeyearold boy?

shloka_text: निस्संशयं मया मन्ये पुरा वीर कदर्यया। पातुकामेषु वत्सेषु मातृ़णां शातितास्स्तनाः।।2.43.17।।
transliteration: nissaṃśayaṃ mayā manye purā vīra kadaryayā| pātukāmeṣu vatseṣu mātṛ़ṇāṃ śātitāsstanāḥ
translation: वीर O valiant one, कदर्यया out of avarice, मया by myself, निस्संशयम् undoubtedly, पुरा formerly, वत्सेषु calves, पातुकामेषु thirsting for milk, मातृ़णाम् of mothers, स्तनाः udders, शातिताः hacked by me.
explanation: O valiant one, in my previous birth I must have undoubtedly hacked off the udders of cows when the calves were thirsting for milk from their mothers.

shloka_text: साहं गौरिव सिंहेन विवत्सा वत्सला कृता। कैकेय्या पुरुषव्याघ्र बालवत्सेव गौर्बलात्।।2.43.18।।
transliteration: sāhaṃ gauriva siṃhena vivatsā vatsalā kṛtā| kaikeyyā puruṣavyāghra bālavatseva gaurbalāt
translation: पुरुषव्य्राघ्र O tiger among men, बालवत्सा young calf, गौरिव like cow, वत्सला having affection in the calf, सा अहम् I, कैकेय्या by Kaikeyi, सिंहेन by lion, गौरिव like cow, बलात् forcibly, विवत्सा separated from the calf, कृता is rendered.
explanation: O best of men I have been forcibly separated from my affectionate son by Kaikeyi just like a cow from its calf by a lion.

shloka_text: न हि तावद्गुणैर्जुष्टं सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम्। एकपुत्रा विना पुत्रमहं जीवितुमुत्सहे।।2.43.19।।
transliteration: na hi tāvadguṇairjuṣṭaṃ sarvaśāstraviśāradam| ekaputrā vinā putramahaṃ jīvitumutsahe
translation: एकपुत्रा having only one son, अहम् I, तावद्गुणैः with such virtue, जुष्टम् endowed with, सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम् adept in all shastras, पुत्रं विना without my son, जीवितुम् to live, न उत्सहे हि I do not desire.
explanation: I cannot live without my only son who is adept in all scriptures and endowed with all virtues.

shloka_text: न हि मे जीविते किञ्चित्सामर्थ्यमिह कल्प्यते। अपश्यन्त्याः प्रियं पुत्रं महाबाहुं महाबलम्।।2.43.20।।
transliteration: na hi me jīvite kiñcitsāmarthyamiha kalpyate| apaśyantyāḥ priyaṃ putraṃ mahābāhuṃ mahābalam
translation: महाबाहुम् mightyarmed, महाबलम् immensely strong, प्रियं पुत्रम् beloved son, अपश्यन्त्या: without seeing him, मे for me, इह in this world, जीविते in this life,  किञ्चित् little, सामर्थ्यम् ability, न कल्प्यते हि is not provided.
explanation: Without seeing my beloved son, longarmed and mighty, I have but little strength to live in this world.

shloka_text: अयं हि मां दीपयते समुत्थितः तनूजशोकप्रभवो हुताशनः। महीमिमां रश्मिभिरुद्धतप्रभः यथा निदाघे भगवान् दिवाकरः।।2.43.21।।
transliteration: ayaṃ hi māṃ dīpayate samutthitaḥ tanūjaśokaprabhavo hutāśanaḥ| mahīmimāṃ raśmibhiruddhataprabhaḥ yathā nidāghe bhagavān divākaraḥ
translation: तनूजशोकप्रभवः born out of the grief of separation from my son, अयम् this, हुताशनः fire, समुत्थितः having arisen, निदाघे in summer, उद्धतप्रभः immense heat, भगवान्  divine, दिवाकरः Sun, रश्मिभिः with his rays, इमाम् this, महीं यथा like earth, माम् me, दीपयते is burning.
explanation: I am consumed by this blazing fire of grief caused by separation from my son like the earth scorched in summer by the Sungod with his oppressive rays इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortythird sarga of Ayodhyakanda of  the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: विलपन्ती तथा तां तु कौसल्यां प्रमदोत्तमाम्। इदं धर्मे स्थिता धर्म्यं सुमित्रा वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.44.1।।
transliteration: vilapantī tathā tāṃ tu kausalyāṃ pramadottamām| idaṃ dharme sthitā dharmyaṃ sumitrā vākyamabravīt
translation: धर्मे in virtues, स्थिता abiding, सुमित्रा Sumitra, तथा then, विलपन्तीम् lamenting, प्रमदोत्तमाम् best among women, तां कौशल्याम् to that Kausalya, धर्म्यम् conforming to righteousness, इदं वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: While Kausalya, the best of women was thus lamenting, virtuous Sumitra spoke to her these righteous words:
comments: Sumitra consoles Kausalya.

shloka_text: तवार्ये सद्गुणैर्युक्तः पुत्र स्स पुरुषोत्तमः। किं ते विलपितेनैवं कृपणं रुदितेन वा।।2.44.2।।
transliteration: tavārye sadguṇairyuktaḥ putra ssa puruṣottamaḥ| kiṃ te vilapitenaivaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ ruditena vā
translation: आर्ये O venerable one, सद्गुणैः with every good quality, युक्तः endowed with, तव your, सः पुत्रः such a son, पुरुषोत्तमः the greatest among men, एवम् in this way, ते you, विलपितेन with lamentation, कृपणम् bitterly, रुदितेन वा or by weeping, किम् what is the use?
explanation: My venerable lady, your son Rama is the greatest among men and is endowed with every virtue. Why do you lament in this way? Why do you weep bitterly?

shloka_text: यस्तवार्ये गतः पुत्रस्त्यक्त्वा राज्यं महाबलः। साधु कुर्वन् महात्मानं पितरं सत्यवादिनम्।।2.44.3।। शिष्टैराचरिते सम्यक्छश्वत्प्रेत्यफलोदये। रामो धर्मे स्थित श्रेष्ठो न स शोच्यः कदाचन।।2.44.4।।
transliteration: yastavārye gataḥ putrastyaktvā rājyaṃ mahābalaḥ| sādhu kurvan mahātmānaṃ pitaraṃ satyavādinam śiṣṭairācarite samyakchaśvatpretyaphalodaye| rāmo dharme sthita śreṣṭho na sa śocyaḥ kadācana
translation: आर्ये O noble lady, महाबलः mighty, यः Rama, तव पुत्रः your son, महात्मानम्   magnanimous, पितरम् father, साधु worthy of, सत्यवादिनम् as truthful one, कुर्वन् to do, राज्यम् kingdom, त्यक्त्वा renouncing, शिष्टैः by virtuous men, सम्यक् fully, शश्वत्  everlasting, आचरिते followed, प्रेत्य in the next world, फलोदये at the time of fruition, धर्मे in virtues, स्थितः stuck, श्रेष्ठः best, सः that, रामः Rama, कदाचन at any point, शोच्यः न  not to be grieved over.
explanation: In order to vindicate the words of his great and truthful father, O noble lady,your mighty son has renounced the kingdom and has gone (to the forest). He has stuck to the path so scrupulously followed by the wise, the everlasting results of which can be fully realised in the world to come. Such a peerless son is never to be grieved over.

shloka_text: यस्तवार्ये गतः पुत्रस्त्यक्त्वा राज्यं महाबलः। साधु कुर्वन् महात्मानं पितरं सत्यवादिनम्।।2.44.3।। शिष्टैराचरिते सम्यक्छश्वत्प्रेत्यफलोदये। रामो धर्मे स्थित श्रेष्ठो न स शोच्यः कदाचन।।2.44.4।।
transliteration: yastavārye gataḥ putrastyaktvā rājyaṃ mahābalaḥ| sādhu kurvan mahātmānaṃ pitaraṃ satyavādinam śiṣṭairācarite samyakchaśvatpretyaphalodaye| rāmo dharme sthita śreṣṭho na sa śocyaḥ kadācana
translation: आर्ये O noble lady, महाबलः mighty, यः Rama, तव पुत्रः your son, महात्मानम्   magnanimous, पितरम् father, साधु worthy of, सत्यवादिनम् as truthful one, कुर्वन् to do, राज्यम् kingdom, त्यक्त्वा renouncing, शिष्टैः by virtuous men, सम्यक् fully, शश्वत्  everlasting, आचरिते followed, प्रेत्य in the next world, फलोदये at the time of fruition, धर्मे in virtues, स्थितः stuck, श्रेष्ठः best, सः that, रामः Rama, कदाचन at any point, शोच्यः न  not to be grieved over.
explanation: In order to vindicate the words of his great and truthful father, O noble lady,your mighty son has renounced the kingdom and has gone (to the forest). He has stuck to the path so scrupulously followed by the wise, the everlasting results of which can be fully realised in the world to come. Such a peerless son is never to be grieved over.

shloka_text: वर्तते चोत्तमां वृत्तिं लक्ष्मणोऽस्मिन् सदानघः। दयावान् सर्वभूतेषु लाभस्तस्य महात्मनः।।2.44.5।।
transliteration: vartate cottamāṃ vṛttiṃ lakṣmaṇo'smin sadānaghaḥ| dayāvān sarvabhūteṣu lābhastasya mahātmanaḥ
translation: अनघः blameless one, सर्वभूतेषु in all creatures, दयावान् compassionate, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, अस्मिन् in the matter (of Rama), सदा always, उत्तमाम् highest, वृत्तिम् conduct, वर्तते doing(showing), महात्मनः great soul, तस्य to him, लाभः is benefit.
explanation: Blameless Lakshmana, compassionate to all beings, has acted most nobly in this matter for the benefit of his great soul.

shloka_text: अरण्यवासे यद्दुःखं जानती वै सुखोचिता। अनुगच्छति वैदेही धर्मात्मानं तवात्मजम्।।2.44.6।।
transliteration: araṇyavāse yadduḥkhaṃ jānatī vai sukhocitā| anugacchati vaidehī dharmātmānaṃ tavātmajam
translation: सुखोचिता used to comforts, वैदेही Sita, अरण्यवासे living in the forest, यत् दुःखम् those hardships, जानती वै knowingly, धर्मात्मानम् virtuous, तव your, आत्मजम् son, अनुगच्छति is following.
explanation: The daughter of Videha (Sita) who was used to comforts has knowingly followed your virtuous son into the hardships of forest life.

shloka_text: कीर्तिभूतां पताकां यो लोके भ्रमयति प्रभुः। धर्मसत्यव्रतधनः किं न प्राप्तस्तवात्मजः।।2.44.7।।
transliteration: kīrtibhūtāṃ patākāṃ yo loke bhramayati prabhuḥ| dharmasatyavratadhanaḥ kiṃ na prāptastavātmajaḥ
translation: प्रभुः competent, यः who, कीर्तिभूताम् renowned, पताकाम् the banner, लोके in this world, भ्रमयति waving, धर्मसत्यव्रतधनः one who considers righteousness and truth as wealth, तव आत्मजः your son, किम् what, न प्राप्तः did not gain.
explanation: Your allcompetent son who considers righteousness and truth as wealth, is waving  the flag of fame in this world. What is that which your son did not gain ?

shloka_text: व्यक्तं रामस्य विज्ञाय शौचं माहात्म्यमुत्तमम्। न गात्रमंशुभि स्सूर्य स्सन्तापयितुमर्हति।।2.44.8।।
transliteration: vyaktaṃ rāmasya vijñāya śaucaṃ māhātmyamuttamam| na gātramaṃśubhi ssūrya ssantāpayitumarhati
translation: रामस्य Rama's, शौचम् purity, उत्तमम् excellent, माहात्म्यम् greatness, विज्ञाय having known, सूर्यः sun, अंशुभिः with rays, गात्रम् body, सन्तापयितुम् to torment, न अर्हति will not be inclined,  व्यक्तम् this is evident.
explanation: Knowing Rama's sterling purity and greatness the Sun evidently dare not scorch his body with its rays.
