transliteration: mayā hi cirapuṣṭena dukhasaṃvardhitena ca| viprayujyata kauśalyā phalakāle dhigastu mām
translation: चिरपुष्टेन nurtured for a long time, दुःखसंवर्धितेन reared with great dificulty, मया me, कौशल्या Kausalya, फलकाले at the moment of fuition, विप्रायुज्यत has been separated, माम् me, धिक् अस्तु shame on me.
explanation: Kausalya nurtured me for a long time and reared me with great difficulty. When she was going to enjoy the fruits of her labour, I have been separated from her. Fie upon me

shloka_text: मा स्म सीमन्तिनी काचिज्जनयेत्पुत्रमीदृशम्। सौमित्रे योऽहमम्बाया दद्मि शोकमनन्तकम्।।2.53.21।।
transliteration: mā sma sīmantinī kācijjanayetputramīdṛśam| saumitre yo'hamambāyā dadmi śokamanantakam
translation: सौमित्रे Lakshmana, यः अहम् am I, अम्बायाः to my mother, अनन्तकम् infinite, शोकम् pain, दद्मि am giving, ईदृशम् such, पुत्रम् a son, काचित् सीमन्तिनी (जननी) any mother, मा स्म जनयेत् may not give birth.
explanation: O Lakshmana, I am causing endless sorrow to my mother. May no mother give birth to a son like me

shloka_text: मन्ये प्रीतिविशिष्टा सा मत्तो लक्ष्मण शारिका। यस्यास्तच्छ्रूयते वाक्यं शुक पादमरेर्दश।।2.53.22।।
transliteration: manye prītiviśiṣṭā sā matto lakṣmaṇa śārikā| yasyāstacchrūyate vākyaṃ śuka pādamarerdaśa
translation: लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, यस्याः myna's, शुक parrot, अरेः enemy's, पादम् foot, दश bite, तत् वाक्यम् such statement, श्रूयते heard, सा शारिका that myna, मत्तः more than I, प्रीतिविशिष्टा more pleased, मन्ये I think.
explanation: (On hearing my banishment) her myna would say to her parrot, 'O parrot, bite the foot of the enemy (Kaikeyi)'. I think  that bird is  a greater source of joy to my mother than I, O Lakshmana

shloka_text: शोचन्त्या अल्पभाग्याया न किञ्चिदुपकुर्वता। पुत्रेण किमपुत्राया मया कार्यमरिन्दम।।2.53.23।।
transliteration: śocantyā alpabhāgyāyā na kiñcidupakurvatā| putreṇa kimaputrāyā mayā kāryamarindama
translation: अरिन्दम conquerer of enemies, शोचन्त्याः experiencing great sorrow, अल्पभाग्यायाः less fortunate, अपुत्रायाः without a son, किञ्चित् little, नोपकुर्वता could not be helped, पुत्रेण by the son, मया by me, किम् what, कार्यम् can be done?
explanation: My mother has less fortune and more grief like a woman without a son, O Lakshmana, subduer of enemies For her, what is the use of a son like me who cannot render any service to her?

shloka_text: अल्पभाग्या हि मे माता कौशल्या रहिता मया। शेते परमदुःखार्ता पतिता शोकसागरे।।2.53.24।।
transliteration: alpabhāgyā hi me mātā kauśalyā rahitā mayā| śete paramaduḥkhārtā patitā śokasāgare
translation: अल्पभाग्या less fortunate, मे माता my mother, कौशल्या Kausalya, मया with me, रहिता bereft of, परमदुःखार्ता extremely distressed, शोकसागरे ocean of sorrow, पतिता fallen into, शेते  must be lying.
explanation: My mother is unlucky as she has been separated from me. Extremely distressed, she must have plunged into an ocean of grief.

shloka_text: एको ह्यहमयोध्यां च पृथिवीं चापि लक्ष्मण। तरेयमिषुभिः क्रुद्धो ननु वीर्यमकारणम्।।2.53.25।।
transliteration: eko hyahamayodhyāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ cāpi lakṣmaṇa| tareyamiṣubhiḥ kruddho nanu vīryamakāraṇam
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, अहम् I, क्रुद्धः am enraged, एकः alone, अयोध्यां च Ayodhya, पृथिवीं चापि and also the whole earth, इषुभिः with arrows, तरेयम् will cross, वीर्यम् prowess, अकारणं ननु without reason.
explanation: Once enraged, O Lakshmana I can overpower Ayodhya, even the whole world all by myself with my arrows. But exhibition of prowess without any reason is not desirable.

shloka_text: अधर्मभयभीतश्च परलोकस्य चानघ। तेन लक्ष्मण नाद्याह मात्मानमभिषेचये।।2.53.26।।
transliteration: adharmabhayabhītaśca paralokasya cānagha| tena lakṣmaṇa nādyāha mātmānamabhiṣecaye
translation: अनघ O sinless one, अहम् I, अधर्मभयभीतश्च with the fear of unrighteous conduct, परलोकस्य च for the other world also, लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, तेन therefore, अद्य at this time, आत्मानम् myself, नाभिषेचये did not get crowned.
explanation: O sinless one, I did not get myself coronated owing to fear of unrighteous conduct and fear of the other world.

shloka_text: एतदन्यश्च करुणं विलप्य विजने वने। अश्रुपूर्णमुखो रामो निशि तूष्णीमुपाविशत्।।2.53.27।।
transliteration: etadanyaśca karuṇaṃ vilapya vijane vane| aśrupūrṇamukho rāmo niśi tūṣṇīmupāviśat
translation: रामः Rama, निशि in the night, विजने in the desolate, वने in the  forest, एतत् all these, अन्यच्च and other, करुणम् pitiful, विलप्य lamenting, अश्रुपूर्णमुखः face filled with tears, तूष्णीम् silently, उपाविशत् sat.
explanation: Like this and in many other ways Rama lamented pitifully in that desolate forest. When his face was filled with tears, he sat silently in the night.

shloka_text: विलप्योपरतं रामं गतार्चिषमिवानलम्। समुद्रमिव निर्वेगमाश्वासयत लक्ष्मणः।।2.53.28।।
transliteration: vilapyoparataṃ rāmaṃ gatārciṣamivānalam| samudramiva nirvegamāśvāsayata lakṣmaṇaḥ
translation: विलप्य having lamented, उपरतम् ceased, गतार्चिषम् with extinguished flames, अनलम् इव  like fire, निर्वेगम् without moving, समुद्रमिव like the sea, रामम् Rama, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, आश्वासयत consoled.
explanation: Lakshmana consoled Rama who ceased to lament like fire with extinguished flames or like a motionless sea:

shloka_text: ध्रुवमद्य पुरी राजन्नयोध्यायुधिनां वर। निष्प्रभा त्वयि निष्क्रान्ते गतचन्द्रेव शर्वरी।।2.53.29।।
transliteration: dhruvamadya purī rājannayodhyāyudhināṃ vara| niṣprabhā tvayi niṣkrānte gatacandreva śarvarī
translation: आयुधिनाम् among wielder of weapons, वर foremost, राजन् O king, अद्य now, अयोध्यापुरी city of Ayodhya, त्वयि when you, निष्क्रान्ते had departed, गतचन्द्र without moon, शर्वरीव like night, निष्प्रभा without lustre, ध्रुवम् certain.
explanation: O Rama, foremost of warriors, it is certain that since your departure, the city of Ayodhya must be lustreless like night without the Moon.

shloka_text: नैतदौपयिकं राम यदिदं परितप्यते। विषादयसि सीतां च मां चैव पुरुषर्षभ।।2.53.30।।
transliteration: naitadaupayikaṃ rāma yadidaṃ paritapyate| viṣādayasi sītāṃ ca māṃ caiva puruṣarṣabha
translation: राम O Rama, इदम् in this manner, यत् परितप्यते that you are lamenting, एतत् all this, औपयिकम् proper, न not, पुरुषर्षभ foremost of men, सीतां च Sita, मां चैव me also, विषादयसि disheartening.
explanation: This is not the way you should lament, O Rama. O foremost of men, by doing so you are disheartening me and Sita as well.

shloka_text: न च सीता त्वया हीना न चाहमपि राघव। मुहूर्तमपि जीवावो जलान्मत्स्याविनोद्धृतौ।।2.53.31।।
transliteration: na ca sītā tvayā hīnā na cāhamapi rāghava| muhūrtamapi jīvāvo jalānmatsyāvinoddhṛtau
translation: राघव O Rama, त्वया by you, हीना without, सीता Sita, न not,  अहमपि I also, न not, जलात्  from water, उद्धृतौ removed, मत्स्याविव like fish, मुहूर्तमपि even for a moment, न जीवावः will not survive.
explanation: Without you Sita or I will not survive even for a moment like a fish taken out of water, O Rama

shloka_text: नहि तातं न शत्रुघ्नं न सुमित्रां परन्तप। द्रष्टुमिच्छेयमद्याहं स्वर्गं चापि त्वया विना।।2.53.32।।
transliteration: nahi tātaṃ na śatrughnaṃ na sumitrāṃ parantapa| draṣṭumiccheyamadyāhaṃ svargaṃ cāpi tvayā vinā
translation: परन्तप O tomentor of enemies, Rama, अहम् I, अद्य now, त्वया विना without you, तातम्  father, द्रष्टुम् see, न हि इच्छेयम् shall not desire, शत्रुघ्नम् Satrughna, न not, सुमित्राम्  Sumitra, स्वर्गं चापि even heaven.
explanation: Without you, O Rama, tormentor of enemies, I wish to see neither father nor Satrughna nor Sumitra nor even heaven itself

shloka_text: ततस्तत्र सुखासीनौ नातिदूरे निरीक्ष्य ताम्। न्यग्रोधे सुकृतां शय्यां भेजाते धर्मवत्सलौ।।2.53.33।।
transliteration: tatastatra sukhāsīnau nātidūre nirīkṣya tām| nyagrodhe sukṛtāṃ śayyāṃ bhejāte dharmavatsalau
translation: ततः thereafter, तत्र there, सुखासीनौ seated comfortably, धर्मवत्सलौ attached to righteousness, नातिदूरे not far (from there), न्यग्रोधे under a banyan tree, सुकृताम् wellmade,  तां शय्याम् that bed, निरीक्ष्य having seen, भेजाते lay down.
explanation: Thereafter Rama and Sita, the duo, nurturers of righteousness, from their comfortable  seats moved to the bed wellmade under the banyan tree not far (from there where they were sitting) and lay down (to sleep).

shloka_text: स लक्ष्मणस्योत्तमपुष्कलं वचो निशम्य चैवं वनवासमादरात्। समाः समस्ता विदधे परन्तपः प्रपद्य धर्मं सुचिराय राघवः।।2.53.34।।
transliteration: sa lakṣmaṇasyottamapuṣkalaṃ vaco niśamya caivaṃ vanavāsamādarāt| samāḥ samastā vidadhe parantapaḥ prapadya dharmaṃ sucirāya rāghavaḥ
translation: परन्तपः tormentor of enemies, सः राघवः that Rama, एवम् thus, लक्ष्मणस्य Lakshmana's, उत्तमपुष्कलम् excellent and copious, वचः utterances, आदरात् out of love, निशम्य having heard, सुचिराय for a long period, धर्मम् that code of conduct of forest life, प्रपद्य having obtained, समस्ता: all, समाः the years, वनवासम् life in the forest, विदधे resorted to.
explanation: Rama, the tormentor of enemies, listened, out of love, to the excellent and copious words of Lakshmana and permitted him to live in the forest for the entire period of fourteen years by observing the prescribed code of conduct as enjoined on  life in the forest.

shloka_text: ततस्तु तस्मिन् विजने वने तदा महाबलौ राघववंशवर्धनौ। न तौ भयं सम्भ्रममभ्युपेयतु र्यथैव सिंहौ गिरिसानुगोचरौ।।2.53.35।।
transliteration: tatastu tasmin vijane vane tadā mahābalau rāghavavaṃśavardhanau| na tau bhayaṃ sambhramamabhyupeyatu ryathaiva siṃhau girisānugocarau
translation: ततः thereafter, तदा then, विजने in desolation, तस्मिन् that, वने in the  forest, महाबलौ very strong, तौ the two, राघववंशवर्धनौ perpetuators of the Raghu race, (Rama and Lakshmana), गिरिसानु गोचरौ dwelling on the slopes of mountains, सिंहौ यथैव  like two lions, भयम् fear, सम्भ्रमम् hesitation, न अभ्युपेयतुः did not feel.
explanation: Then the two mighty perpetuators of the Raghu race, who were like two lions dwelling on the slopes of mountains, lived in that lonely forest  without fear or hesitation. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे त्रिपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftythird sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ते तु तस्मिन्महावृक्षे उषित्वा रजनीं शिवाम्। विमलेऽभ्युदिते सूर्ये तस्माद्देशात्प्रतस्थिरे।।2.54.1।।
transliteration: te tu tasminmahāvṛkṣe uṣitvā rajanīṃ śivām| vimale'bhyudite sūrye tasmāddeśātpratasthire
translation: ते they (Rama, Sita and Lakshmana), शिवाम् auspicious, रजनीम् night, तस्मिन् that, महावृक्षे big tree, उषित्वा having remained, विमले when the bright, सूर्ये Sun, अभ्युदिते had risen, तस्मात् देशात् from that region, प्रतस्थिरे set out.
explanation: They (Rama, Sita and Lakshmana) spent that auspicious night under that great tree and set out from there after the bright sun rose.
comments: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana depart for Dandaka forest -- reach the hermitage of sage Bharadwaja -- seek advice for a dwelling -- place -- Bharadwaja suggests Chitrakuta at the confluence of rivers Ganga and Yamuna -- they set out after a night's stay.

shloka_text: यत्र भागीरथीं गङ्गां यमुनाभिप्रवर्तते। जग्मुस्तं देशमुद्दिश्य विगाह्य सुमहद्वनम्।।2.54.2।। ते भूमिभागान्विविधान् देशांश्चापि मनोरमान्। अदृष्टपूर्वान् पश्यन्तस्तत्र तत्र यशश्विनः।।2.54.3।।
transliteration: yatra bhāgīrathīṃ gaṅgāṃ yamunābhipravartate| jagmustaṃ deśamuddiśya vigāhya sumahadvanam te bhūmibhāgānvividhān deśāṃścāpi manoramān| adṛṣṭapūrvān paśyantastatra tatra yaśaśvinaḥ
translation: यशश्विनः illustrious, ते they, सुमहत् very great, वनम् forest, विगाह्य having entered, विविधान् different, भूमिभागान् regions of the land, अदृष्टपूर्वान् hithertounseen, मनोरमान् enchanting, देशांश्चापि regions also, तत्र तत्र here and there, पश्यन्तः viewing, यमुना Yamuna, यत्र where, भागीरथीम् Bhagirathi, गङ्गाम् Ganga's, अभिप्रवर्तते flows into, तं देशम् that place, उद्दिश्य intending (to reach), जग्मुः went.
explanation: Illustrious Rama, Sita and Lakshmana entered the deep forest and saw the different regions of the land and other enchanting places which they had never seen before and proceeded towards the region where the river Yamuna merged with Bhagirathi Ganga.

shloka_text: यत्र भागीरथीं गङ्गां यमुनाभिप्रवर्तते। जग्मुस्तं देशमुद्दिश्य विगाह्य सुमहद्वनम्।।2.54.2।। ते भूमिभागान्विविधान् देशांश्चापि मनोरमान्। अदृष्टपूर्वान् पश्यन्तस्तत्र तत्र यशश्विनः।।2.54.3।।
transliteration: yatra bhāgīrathīṃ gaṅgāṃ yamunābhipravartate| jagmustaṃ deśamuddiśya vigāhya sumahadvanam te bhūmibhāgānvividhān deśāṃścāpi manoramān| adṛṣṭapūrvān paśyantastatra tatra yaśaśvinaḥ
translation: यशश्विनः illustrious, ते they, सुमहत् very great, वनम् forest, विगाह्य having entered, विविधान् different, भूमिभागान् regions of the land, अदृष्टपूर्वान् hithertounseen, मनोरमान् enchanting, देशांश्चापि regions also, तत्र तत्र here and there, पश्यन्तः viewing, यमुना Yamuna, यत्र where, भागीरथीम् Bhagirathi, गङ्गाम् Ganga's, अभिप्रवर्तते flows into, तं देशम् that place, उद्दिश्य intending (to reach), जग्मुः went.
explanation: Illustrious Rama, Sita and Lakshmana entered the deep forest and saw the different regions of the land and other enchanting places which they had never seen before and proceeded towards the region where the river Yamuna merged with Bhagirathi Ganga.

shloka_text: यथा क्षेमेण गच्छन् स पश्यंश्च विविधान् द्रुमान्। निवृत्तमात्रे दिवसे रामः सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्।।2.54.4।।
transliteration: yathā kṣemeṇa gacchan sa paśyaṃśca vividhān drumān| nivṛttamātre divase rāmaḥ saumitrimabravīt
translation: सः रामः that Rama, यथा क्षेमेण on a safe way, गच्छन् going, विविधान् various, द्रुमान् trees, पश्यंश्च looking at, दिवसे day, निवृत्तमात्रे when ended, सौमित्रिम् to Lakshmana, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Walking on the safe path and observing various kinds of trees Rama said to Lakshmana at the end of the day:

shloka_text: प्रयागमभितः पश्य सौमित्रे धूममुन्नतम्। अग्नेर्भगवतः केतुं मन्ये सन्निहितो मुनिः।।2.54.5।।
transliteration: prayāgamabhitaḥ paśya saumitre dhūmamunnatam| agnerbhagavataḥ ketuṃ manye sannihito muniḥ
translation: सौमित्रे O son of Sumitra, Lakshmana, प्रयागम् अभितः near Prayaga, उन्नतम् rising high, भगवतः of the venerable, अग्नेः fire's, केतुम् the banner, धूमम् smoke, पश्य look, मुनिः the sage, सन्निहितः close by, मन्ये I think.
explanation: O son of Sumitra, look at the column of smoke rising like the banner of the venerable firegod near Prayaga. I think an ascetic dwells nearby.

shloka_text: नूनं प्राप्ताः स्म सम्भेदं गङ्गायमुनयोर्वयम्। तथा हि श्रूयते शब्दो वारिणो वारिघट्टितः।।2.54.6।।
transliteration: nūnaṃ prāptāḥ sma sambhedaṃ gaṅgāyamunayorvayam| tathā hi śrūyate śabdo vāriṇo vārighaṭṭitaḥ
translation: वयम् we, गङ्गायमुनयोः Ganga and Yamuna, सम्भेदम् confluence, प्राप्ताः स्म have reached,  नूनम् it is certain, तथा हि as for, वारिघट्टितः dashed by waters, वारिणः waters, शब्दः sound, श्रूयते is heard.
explanation: We have surely reached the confluence of Ganga and Yamuna which can be ascertained from the sounds of clashing water.

shloka_text: दारूणि परिभिन्नानि वनजैरुपजीविभिः। भरद्वाजाश्रमे चैते दृश्यन्ते विविधा द्रुमाः।।2.54.7।।
transliteration: dārūṇi paribhinnāni vanajairupajīvibhiḥ| bharadvājāśrame caite dṛśyante vividhā drumāḥ
translation: वनजैः by the foresters, उपजीविभिः those people subsisting on them, परिभिन्नानि are broken,  दारूणि logs of wood, भरद्वाजाश्रमे in the hermitage of Bharadwaja, एते all these, विविधाः different, द्रुमाश्च trees also, दृश्यन्ते are seen.
explanation: Here are logs of wood cut into pieces by forestdwellers, living on forest products. You can see various trees near the hermitage of sage Bharadwaja.

shloka_text: धन्विनौ तौ सुखं गत्वा लम्बमाने दिवाकरे। गङ्गायमुनयोस्सन्धौ प्रापतुर्निलयं मुनेः।।2.54.8।।
transliteration: dhanvinau tau sukhaṃ gatvā lambamāne divākare| gaṅgāyamunayossandhau prāpaturnilayaṃ muneḥ
translation: धन्विनौ the two archers, तौ those two, सुखम् comfortably, गत्वा having gone,  दिवाकरे Sun, लम्बमाने was hanging, गङ्गायमुनयोः of Ganga and yamuna, सन्धौ at the confluence, मुनेः of sage Bharadwaja, निलयम् hermitage, प्रापतुः arrived.
explanation: The two archers (Rama and Lakshmana) reached comfortably (walking at an easy pace) by evening the hermitage of sage Bharadwaja near the confluence of Ganga and Yamuna.

shloka_text: रामस्त्वाश्रममासाद्य त्रासयन्मृगपक्षिणः। गत्वा मुहूर्तमध्वानं भरद्वाजमुपागमत्।।2.54.9।।
transliteration: rāmastvāśramamāsādya trāsayanmṛgapakṣiṇaḥ| gatvā muhūrtamadhvānaṃ bharadvājamupāgamat
translation: रामः Rama, अश्रमम् hermitage, आसाद्य having approached, मृगपक्षिणः animals and birds, त्रासयन् frightening, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, अध्वानम् on the path, गत्वा proceeding, भरद्वाजम् Bharadhwaja, उपागमत् reached.
explanation: Seeing Rama approaching the hermitage the deer and the birds were frightened. Proceeding on the path, for a while Rama reached (the place of) Bharadwaja.

shloka_text: ततस्त्वाश्रमासाद्य मुनेर्दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणौ। सीतयानुगतौ वीरौ दूरादेवावतस्थतुः।।2.54.10।।
transliteration: tatastvāśramāsādya munerdarśanakāṅkṣiṇau| sītayānugatau vīrau dūrādevāvatasthatuḥ
translation: ततः then, सीतया by Sita, अनुगतौ followed, वीरौ those two heroes, आश्रमम् hermitage, आसाद्य having reached, मुनेः ascetic's, दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणौ wishing to see, दूरादेव at a distance, अवतस्थतुः stood.
explanation: Thereafter the two heroes followed by Sita arrived at the hermitage and, wishing to see the sage, waited at a distance.

shloka_text: स प्रविश्य महात्मानमृषिं शिष्यगणैर्वृतम्। संशितव्रतमेकाग्रं तपसा लब्धचक्षुषम्।।2.54.11।। हुताग्निहोत्रं दृष्ट्वैव महाभागं कृताञ्जलिः। रामः सौमित्रिणा सार्धं सीतया चाभ्यवादयत्।।2.54.12।।
transliteration: sa praviśya mahātmānamṛṣiṃ śiṣyagaṇairvṛtam| saṃśitavratamekāgraṃ tapasā labdhacakṣuṣam hutāgnihotraṃ dṛṣṭvaiva mahābhāgaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ| rāmaḥ saumitriṇā sārdhaṃ sītayā cābhyavādayat
translation: सः रामः Rama, प्रविश्य having entered, संशितव्रतम् one practising rigorous austerities, एकाग्रम् with concentration of mind, तपसा with asceticism, लब्दचक्षुषम् one who has obtained spiritual insight, हुताग्निहोत्रम् one who has kindled fire in sacrificial rituals, महाभागम् distinguished, शिष्यगणैः with disciples, वृतम् surrounded by, महात्मानम् highsouled, ऋषिम् sage, दृष्ट्वैव having seen, सौमित्रिणा Lakshmana, सार्धम् along with, सीतया च Sita too, अभ्यवादयत् paid obeisance.
explanation: Rama entered the hermitage and saw that highsouled Bharadwaja surrounded by his disciples. He was a distinguished sage who (himself) kindled sacrficial fires and acquired spiritual insight by practising rigid austerities with concentration of mind and ascetic powers. Rama, Lakshmana and Sita paid their obeisance to that great sage.

shloka_text: स प्रविश्य महात्मानमृषिं शिष्यगणैर्वृतम्। संशितव्रतमेकाग्रं तपसा लब्धचक्षुषम्।।2.54.11।। हुताग्निहोत्रं दृष्ट्वैव महाभागं कृताञ्जलिः। रामः सौमित्रिणा सार्धं सीतया चाभ्यवादयत्।।2.54.12।।
transliteration: sa praviśya mahātmānamṛṣiṃ śiṣyagaṇairvṛtam| saṃśitavratamekāgraṃ tapasā labdhacakṣuṣam hutāgnihotraṃ dṛṣṭvaiva mahābhāgaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ| rāmaḥ saumitriṇā sārdhaṃ sītayā cābhyavādayat
translation: सः रामः Rama, प्रविश्य having entered, संशितव्रतम् one practising rigorous austerities, एकाग्रम् with concentration of mind, तपसा with asceticism, लब्दचक्षुषम् one who has obtained spiritual insight, हुताग्निहोत्रम् one who has kindled fire in sacrificial rituals, महाभागम् distinguished, शिष्यगणैः with disciples, वृतम् surrounded by, महात्मानम् highsouled, ऋषिम् sage, दृष्ट्वैव having seen, सौमित्रिणा Lakshmana, सार्धम् along with, सीतया च Sita too, अभ्यवादयत् paid obeisance.
explanation: Rama entered the hermitage and saw that highsouled Bharadwaja surrounded by his disciples. He was a distinguished sage who (himself) kindled sacrficial fires and acquired spiritual insight by practising rigid austerities with concentration of mind and ascetic powers. Rama, Lakshmana and Sita paid their obeisance to that great sage.

shloka_text: न्यवेदयत चात्मानं तस्मै लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः। पुत्रौ दशरथस्यावां भगवन् रामलक्ष्मणौ।।2.54.13।।
transliteration: nyavedayata cātmānaṃ tasmai lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ| putrau daśarathasyāvāṃ bhagavan rāmalakṣmaṇau
translation: लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः Lakshmana's elder brother (Rama), तस्मै to that sage, आत्मानम् himself, न्यवेदयत introduced, भगवन् O venerable one, अवाम् both of us, दशरथस्य Dasaratha's, पुत्रौ sons, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana.
explanation: Lakshmana's elder brother (Rama) introduced himself (to Bharadwaja), O venerable one, we are both sons of Dasaratha, Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: भार्या ममेयं वैदेही कल्याणी जनकात्मजा। मां चानुयाता विजनं तपोवनमनिन्दिता।।2.54.14।।
transliteration: bhāryā mameyaṃ vaidehī kalyāṇī janakātmajā| māṃ cānuyātā vijanaṃ tapovanamaninditā
translation: इयम् this, कल्याणी auspicious one, मम my, भार्या consort, जनकात्मजा daughter of Janaka, वैदेही Vaidehi (Sita), अनिन्दिता irreproachable, माम् me, विजनम् desolate, तपोवनम् penacegrove, अनुयाता has followed.
explanation: This blessed one is my consort, Sita, daughter of Janaka. Irreproachable she has followed me to the desolate grove of penance (hermitage).

shloka_text: पित्रा प्रव्राज्यमानं मां सौमित्रिरनुज प्रियः। अयमन्वगमद्भ्राता वनमेव दृढव्रतः।।2.54.15।।
transliteration: pitrā pravrājyamānaṃ māṃ saumitriranuja priyaḥ| ayamanvagamadbhrātā vanameva dṛḍhavrataḥ
translation: दृढव्रतः of firm resolve, भ्राता brother, अनुजः younger, प्रियः dear, अयं सौमित्रिः this son of Sumitra, पित्रा by father, प्रव्राज्यमानम् being sent on exile, माम् me, वनमेव to the forest, अन्वगमत् followed.
explanation: This is the son of Sumitra, my beloved younger brother, a man of firm resolve. He has accompanied me when I was sent on exile to the forest by my father.

shloka_text: पित्रा नियुक्ता भगवन् प्रवेक्ष्यामस्तपोवनम्। धर्ममेव चरिष्याम स्तत्र मूलफलाशनाः।।2.54.16।।
transliteration: pitrā niyuktā bhagavan pravekṣyāmastapovanam| dharmameva cariṣyāma statra mūlaphalāśanāḥ
translation: भगवन् O venerable one, पित्रा by father, नियुक्ताः ordered by, तपोवनम् penancegrove प्रवेक्ष्यामः we will enter, तत्र there, मूलफलाशनाः subsisting on roots and fruits, धर्ममेव following righteous ways, चरिष्यामः will practise.
explanation: O venerable one on my father's command we entered the desolate forest of penance. Subsisting on roots and fruits, I shall practise the righteous way of life.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजपुत्रस्य धीमतः। उपानयत धर्मात्मा गामर्घ्यमुदकं ततः।।2.54.17।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rājaputrasya dhīmataḥ| upānayata dharmātmā gāmarghyamudakaṃ tataḥ
translation: धर्मात्मा sage Bharadwaja, धीमतः of the sagacious, तस्य that, राजपुत्रस्य prince's,  तत् वचनम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, ततः then, गाम् bull, अर्घ्यम् for arghya, उदकम् water, उपानयत brought.
explanation: Sage Bharadwaja heard the words of sagacious Rama and offered a bull, water (for washing feet) and arghya (offering to a guest).

shloka_text: नानाविधानन्नरसान् वन्यमूलफलाश्रयान्। तेभ्यो ददौ तप्ततपा वासं चैवाभ्यकल्पयत्।।2.54.18।।
transliteration: nānāvidhānannarasān vanyamūlaphalāśrayān| tebhyo dadau taptatapā vāsaṃ caivābhyakalpayat
translation: तप्ततपाः one who practised severe penance, नानाविधान् different kinds of, वन्यमूलफलाश्रयान् made from the fruits and roots, अन्नरसान् food and drink, तेभ्यः for them, ददौ gave, वासं चैव restingplace also, अकल्पयत् arranged.
explanation: The ascetic who practised severe penance offered them different kinds of food and drink made from roots and fruits available in the forest. He also provided them a place to rest in.

shloka_text: मृगपक्षिभिरासीनो मुनिभिश्च समन्ततः। राममागतमभ्यर्च्य स्वागतेनाहतं मुनिः।।2.54.19।।
transliteration: mṛgapakṣibhirāsīno munibhiśca samantataḥ| rāmamāgatamabhyarcya svāgatenāhataṃ muniḥ
translation: मृगपक्षिभिः by animals and birds, मुनिभिश्च by hermits also, समन्ततः surrounded, आसीनः seated, मुनिः sage (Bharadwaja), आगतम् arrived, तं रामम् to that Rama, स्वागतेन with  welcome, अभ्यर्च्य having paid homage, आह uttered.
explanation: There the sage sat, surrounded by hermits, animals and birds after having welcomed Rama with due honour.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य च तामर्चामुपविष्टं स राघवम्। भरद्वाजोऽब्रवीद्वाक्यं धर्मयुक्तमिदं तदा।।2.54.20।।
transliteration: pratigṛhya ca tāmarcāmupaviṣṭaṃ sa rāghavam| bharadvājo'bravīdvākyaṃ dharmayuktamidaṃ tadā
translation: सः भरद्वाजः that Bharadwaja, तदा then, ताम् that, अर्चाम् hospitality, प्रतिगृह्य having  received, उपविष्टम् seated in front, राघवम् to Rama, धर्मयुक्तम् in conformity with  righteousness, इदं वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Rama accepted the hospitality of Bharadwaja and took a seat in front of the sage, who spoke to him these words in conformity with righteousness:

shloka_text: चिरस्य खलु काकुत्स्थ पश्यामि त्वामिहागतम्। श्रुतं तव मया चेदं विवासनमकारणम्।।2.54.21।।
transliteration: cirasya khalu kākutstha paśyāmi tvāmihāgatam| śrutaṃ tava mayā cedaṃ vivāsanamakāraṇam
translation: काकुत्स्थ O descendant of the Kakutstha dynasty, चिरस्य after a long time, इह here, आगतम् arrived here, त्वाम् you, पश्यामि खलु I see indeed, अकारणम् without any reason, तव your, इदम् this, विवासनम् banishment, मया by me, श्रुतं च is heard too.
explanation: O descendant of the Kakutstha dynasty, I am able to see you on your arrival here after a long time. I have also heard about your unwarranted banishment.

shloka_text: अवकाशो विविक्तोऽयं महानद्योस्समागमे। पुण्यश्च रमणीयश्च वसत्विह भवान् सुखम्।।2.54.22।।
transliteration: avakāśo vivikto'yaṃ mahānadyossamāgame| puṇyaśca ramaṇīyaśca vasatviha bhavān sukham
translation: महानद्योः of two great rivers, समागमे at the confluence, अयम् this, अवकाशः region, विविक्तः solitary, पुण्यश्च is also sacred, रमणीयश्च pleasant, भवान् you, इह here, सुखम् comfortably, वसतु can dwell.
explanation: This sacred and solitary region near the confluence of two great rivers (Ganga and Yamuna) is a pleasant place. You may stay here comfortably.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु वचनं भरद्वाजेन राघवः। प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं रामः सर्वहिते रतः।।2.54.23।।
transliteration: evamuktastu vacanaṃ bharadvājena rāghavaḥ| pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ rāmaḥ sarvahite rataḥ
translation: सर्वहिते for the wellbeing of all, रतः devoted, राघवः born in the dynasty of Raghu, रामः Rama, भरद्वाजेन by Bharadwaja, एवम् in this way, वचनम् these words, उक्तः having been addressed, शुभम् auspicious, वाक्यम् words, प्रत्युवाच spoke in reply.
explanation: Rama, ever devoted to the wellbeing of every one, heard Bharadwaja and replied to him with these auspicious words:

shloka_text: भगवन्नित आसन्नः पौरजानपदो जनः। सुदर्शमिह मां प्रेक्ष्य मन्येऽहमिममाश्रमम्।।2.54.24।। आगमिष्यति वैदेहीं मां चापि प्रेक्षको जनः। अनेन कारणेनाहमिह वासं न रोचये।।2.54.25।।
transliteration: bhagavannita āsannaḥ paurajānapado janaḥ| sudarśamiha māṃ prekṣya manye'hamimamāśramam āgamiṣyati vaidehīṃ māṃ cāpi prekṣako janaḥ| anena kāraṇenāhamiha vāsaṃ na rocaye
translation: भगवन् O venerable one, इतः from here, पौरजानपदः inhabiting towns and villages, जनः subjects, आसन्नः living closely, इह here, माम् me, सुदर्शम् easily to be seen, प्रेक्ष्य having seen, जनः people, वैदेहीम् Sita, मां चापि me too, प्रेक्षकः in order to see, इमम् आश्रमम् to this hermitage, आगमिष्यति will frequent, अहम् I, मन्ये think so, अनेन कारणेन for this reason, अहम् I, इह here, वासम् to reside, न रोचये do not desire.
explanation: O venerable sage, I feel the people living in nearby villages and towns, perceiving that we can be easily seen here, will frequent this ashram. This is the reason I don't wish to stay here.

shloka_text: भगवन्नित आसन्नः पौरजानपदो जनः। सुदर्शमिह मां प्रेक्ष्य मन्येऽहमिममाश्रमम्।।2.54.24।। आगमिष्यति वैदेहीं मां चापि प्रेक्षको जनः। अनेन कारणेनाहमिह वासं न रोचये।।2.54.25।।
transliteration: bhagavannita āsannaḥ paurajānapado janaḥ| sudarśamiha māṃ prekṣya manye'hamimamāśramam āgamiṣyati vaidehīṃ māṃ cāpi prekṣako janaḥ| anena kāraṇenāhamiha vāsaṃ na rocaye
translation: भगवन् O venerable one, इतः from here, पौरजानपदः inhabiting towns and villages, जनः subjects, आसन्नः living closely, इह here, माम् me, सुदर्शम् easily to be seen, प्रेक्ष्य having seen, जनः people, वैदेहीम् Sita, मां चापि me too, प्रेक्षकः in order to see, इमम् आश्रमम् to this hermitage, आगमिष्यति will frequent, अहम् I, मन्ये think so, अनेन कारणेन for this reason, अहम् I, इह here, वासम् to reside, न रोचये do not desire.
explanation: O venerable sage, I feel the people living in nearby villages and towns, perceiving that we can be easily seen here, will frequent this ashram. This is the reason I don't wish to stay here.

shloka_text: एकान्ते पश्य भगवन्नाश्रमस्थानमुत्तमम्। रमेत यत्र वैदेही सुखार्हा जनकात्मजा।।2.54.26।।
transliteration: ekānte paśya bhagavannāśramasthānamuttamam| rameta yatra vaidehī sukhārhā janakātmajā
translation: भगवन् revered one, सुखार्हा deserves comfort, जनकात्मजा Janaka's daughter, वैदेही Vaidehi, यत्र where, रमेत may enjoy, एकान्ते in a solitary, उत्तमम् agreeable, आश्रमस्थानम् hermitage, पश्य see.
explanation: O revered one, Janaka's daughter (Sita) deserves comfort. Suggest a solitary and agreeable place for our hermitage where she can enjoy herself.

shloka_text: एतछ्रुत्वा शुभं वाक्यं भरद्वाजो महामुनिः। राघवस्य ततो वाक्यमर्थग्राहकमब्रवीत्।।2.54.27।।
transliteration: etachrutvā śubhaṃ vākyaṃ bharadvājo mahāmuniḥ| rāghavasya tato vākyamarthagrāhakamabravīt
translation: महामुनिः great sage, भरद्वाजः Bharadwaja, राघवस्य Rama's, एतत् these, शुभम् auspicious, वाक्यम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, ततः after that, अर्थग्राहकम् conveying the meaning, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: On hearing the auspicious words of Rama conveying his intention, the great sage Bharadwaja replied to him thus:

shloka_text: दशक्रोश इतस्तात गिरिर्यत्रनिवत्स्यसि। महर्षिसेवितः पुण्यः सर्वतः सुखदर्शनः।।2.54.28।। गोलाङ्गूलानुचरितो वानरर्क्षनिषेवितः। चित्रकूट इति ख्यातो गन्धमादनसन्निभः।।2.54.29।।
transliteration: daśakrośa itastāta giriryatranivatsyasi| maharṣisevitaḥ puṇyaḥ sarvataḥ sukhadarśanaḥ golāṅgūlānucarito vānararkṣaniṣevitaḥ| citrakūṭa iti khyāto gandhamādanasannibhaḥ
translation: तात O dear, महर्षिसेवितः inhabited by sages, पुण्यः sacred, सर्वतः from all sides, सुखदर्शनः whose sight causes delight, गोलाङ्गूलानुचरितः full of wandering apes, वानरर्क्षनिषेवितः inhabited by monkeys and bears, चित्रकूटः इति by name Chitrakuta, ख्यातः wellknown, गन्धमादनसन्निभः like 'Gandhamadana' mountain, गिरिः mountain, इतः from here, दशक्रोशे at a distance of ten krosas, यत्र there, निवत्स्यसि you can live.
explanation: O my son ten krosas (about twenty miles) from here is a mountain wellknown as  Chitrakuta, resembling 'Gandhamadana'. That mountain frequented by maharshis is sacred. It looks pleasant from all sides. Monkeys, apes and bears wander there and it is an appropriate place for you to live in.

shloka_text: दशक्रोश इतस्तात गिरिर्यत्रनिवत्स्यसि। महर्षिसेवितः पुण्यः सर्वतः सुखदर्शनः।।2.54.28।। गोलाङ्गूलानुचरितो वानरर्क्षनिषेवितः। चित्रकूट इति ख्यातो गन्धमादनसन्निभः।।2.54.29।।
transliteration: daśakrośa itastāta giriryatranivatsyasi| maharṣisevitaḥ puṇyaḥ sarvataḥ sukhadarśanaḥ golāṅgūlānucarito vānararkṣaniṣevitaḥ| citrakūṭa iti khyāto gandhamādanasannibhaḥ
translation: तात O dear, महर्षिसेवितः inhabited by sages, पुण्यः sacred, सर्वतः from all sides, सुखदर्शनः whose sight causes delight, गोलाङ्गूलानुचरितः full of wandering apes, वानरर्क्षनिषेवितः inhabited by monkeys and bears, चित्रकूटः इति by name Chitrakuta, ख्यातः wellknown, गन्धमादनसन्निभः like 'Gandhamadana' mountain, गिरिः mountain, इतः from here, दशक्रोशे at a distance of ten krosas, यत्र there, निवत्स्यसि you can live.
explanation: O my son ten krosas (about twenty miles) from here is a mountain wellknown as  Chitrakuta, resembling 'Gandhamadana'. That mountain frequented by maharshis is sacred. It looks pleasant from all sides. Monkeys, apes and bears wander there and it is an appropriate place for you to live in.

shloka_text: यावता चित्रकूटस्य नरशृङ्गान्यवेक्षते। कल्याणानि समाधत्ते न पापे कुरुते मनः।।2.54.30।।
transliteration: yāvatā citrakūṭasya naraśṛṅgānyavekṣate| kalyāṇāni samādhatte na pāpe kurute manaḥ
translation: नरः a man, यावता as long as, चित्रकूटस्य Chitrakuta mountain's, शृङ्गानि peaks, आवेक्षते beholds, कल्याणानि auspicious deeds, समाधत्ते will perform, पापे in sinful thoughts, मनः the mind, न कुरुते will not employ.
explanation: As long as one beholds the peaks of mount Chitrakuta, he will be inspired to do good deeds and will not employ his mind in sinful thoughts.

shloka_text: ऋषयस्तत्र बहवो विहृत्य शरदां शतम्। तपसा दिवमारूढाः कपालशिरसा सह।।2.54.31।।
transliteration: ṛṣayastatra bahavo vihṛtya śaradāṃ śatam| tapasā divamārūḍhāḥ kapālaśirasā saha
translation: तत्र there, बहवः many, ऋषयः ascetics, शरदां शतम् for hundreds of years, तपसा with austerities, विहृत्य having roamed about, कपालशिरसा सह with the skulls on their heads, दिवम् heaven, आरूढाः have ascended.
explanation: On the Chitrakuta mountain many ascetics wandered about (lived) for hundreds of years carrying on penance. In the process they became so much emaciated that they looked as if they were left (only) with the skulls on their heads. (In the end) they ascended heaven.

shloka_text: प्रविविक्तमहं मन्ये तं वासं भवतस्सुखम्। इह वा वनवासाय वस राम मया सह।।2.54.32।।
transliteration: praviviktamahaṃ manye taṃ vāsaṃ bhavatassukham| iha vā vanavāsāya vasa rāma mayā saha
translation: राम Rama, प्रविविक्तम् solitary, तं वासम् that abode, भवतः for your, सुखम् happiness, अहम् I,  मन्ये think, मया सह with me, इह वा or here, वनवासाय for the period of banishment, वस you may live.
explanation: O Rama, I think you will enjoy your stay there in a solitary place. Or else, you may live with me here during the period of banishment.

shloka_text: स रामं सर्वकामैस्तं भरद्वाजः प्रियातिथिम्। सभार्यं सह च भ्रात्रा प्रतिजग्राह धर्मवित्।।2.54.33।।
transliteration: sa rāmaṃ sarvakāmaistaṃ bharadvājaḥ priyātithim| sabhāryaṃ saha ca bhrātrā pratijagrāha dharmavit
translation: धर्मवित् one who knows his duty, सः भरद्वाजः that Bharadwaja, सभार्यम् with his consort, भ्रात्रा सह with brother, च and, प्रियातिथिम् beloved guest, तं रामम् that Rama, सर्वकामैः with all desires, प्रतिजग्राह honoured.
explanation: Bharadwaja, who knows his duty honoured Rama, his beloved guest with his consort and brother by extending all kinds of hospitality.

shloka_text: तस्य प्रयागे रामस्य तं महर्षिमुपेयुषः। प्रपन्ना रजनी पुण्याः चित्राः कथयतः कथाः।।2.54.34।।
transliteration: tasya prayāge rāmasya taṃ maharṣimupeyuṣaḥ| prapannā rajanī puṇyāḥ citrāḥ kathayataḥ kathāḥ
translation: प्रयागे at Prayaga, तं महर्षिम् that great sage, उपेयुषः sitting near, रामस्य of Rama, चित्राः interesting, कथाः tales, कथयतः while conversing, पुण्या that holy, रजनी night, प्रपन्ना had set in.
explanation: At Prayaga, while the great sage Bharadwaja was narrating to Rama sitting near him several interesting anecdotes, the holy night set in.

shloka_text: सीतातृतीयः काकुत्स्थः परिश्रान्तः सुखोचितः। भरद्वाजाश्रमे रम्ये तां रात्रिमवसत्सुखम्।।2.54.35।।
transliteration: sītātṛtīyaḥ kākutsthaḥ pariśrāntaḥ sukhocitaḥ| bharadvājāśrame ramye tāṃ rātrimavasatsukham
translation: सुखोचितः used to comforts, परिश्रान्तः exhausted, सीतांतृतीयः Sita counted as the third, काकुत्स्थ: Rama, रम्ये in the lovely, भरद्वाजाश्रमे hermitage of Bharadwaja, तां रात्रिम् that night, सुखम् happily, अवसत् stayed.
explanation: The exhausted scion of the Kakutsthas, used to comforts, stayed in the lovely hermitage of Bharadwaja for the night with Sita, as the third member (of the group).

shloka_text: प्रभातायां रजन्यां तु भरद्वाजमुपागमत्। उवाच नरशार्दूलो मुनिं ज्वलिततेजसम्।।2.54.36।।
transliteration: prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ tu bharadvājamupāgamat| uvāca naraśārdūlo muniṃ jvalitatejasam
translation: नरशार्दूलः tiger (best) among men, रजन्याम् after the night, प्रभातायाम् at dawn, भरद्वाजम् to Bharadwaja, उपागमत् approached, ज्वलिततेजसम् with blazing lustre, मुनिम् the sage, उवाच said.
explanation: When the night passed into dawn, Rama the best of men approached the resplendent Bharadwaja and said.

shloka_text: शर्वरीं भगवन्नद्य सत्यशील तवाश्रमे। उषिताः स्मेह वसतिमनुजानातु नो भवान्।।2.54.37।।
transliteration: śarvarīṃ bhagavannadya satyaśīla tavāśrame| uṣitāḥ smeha vasatimanujānātu no bhavān
translation: सत्यशील O truthful, भगवन् O venerable, इह here, तव आश्रमे in your hermitage, शर्वरीम् the night, उषिता स्म we have spent, अद्य to day, नः us, भवान् you, वसतिम् dwellingplace, अनुजानातु permit.
explanation: O venerable sage devoted to truth, we have spent the night in your hermitage. Please permit us to depart for the dwellingplace (suggested by you).

shloka_text: रात्र्यां तु तस्यां व्युष्टायां भरद्वाजोऽब्रवीदिदम्। मधुमूलफलोपेतं चित्रकूटं व्रजेति ह।।2.54.38।।
transliteration: rātryāṃ tu tasyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ bharadvājo'bravīdidam| madhumūlaphalopetaṃ citrakūṭaṃ vrajeti ha
translation: तस्याम् रात्र्याम् when that night, व्युष्टायाम् had come to a close, भरद्वाजः Bharadwaja, मधुमूलफलोपेतम् abounding in honey, roots, and fruits, चित्रकूटम् to Chitrakuta, व्रज go, इति thus, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: When the night came to a close, Bharadwaja said (to Rama): You may proceed to Chitrakuta which abounds in roots, fruits and honey.

shloka_text: वासमौपयिकं मन्ये तव राम महाबल नानानगगणोपेतः किन्नरोरगसेवितः। मयूरनादाभिरुतो गजराजनिषेवितः।।2.54.39।। गम्यतां भवता शैल श्चित्रकूटः स विश्रुतः। पुण्यश्च रमणीयश्च बहुमूलफलायुतः।।2.54.40।।
transliteration: vāsamaupayikaṃ manye tava rāma mahābala nānānagagaṇopetaḥ kinnaroragasevitaḥ| mayūranādābhiruto gajarājaniṣevitaḥ gamyatāṃ bhavatā śaila ścitrakūṭaḥ sa viśrutaḥ| puṇyaśca ramaṇīyaśca bahumūlaphalāyutaḥ
translation: महाबल O mighty one, राम Rama, तव your, औपयिकम् right, वासम् place for your stay, मन्ये I think, नानानगगणोपेतः full of various types of trees, किन्नरोरगसेवितः inhabited by kinneras, serpents, मयूरनादाभिरुतः echoing with cries of peacocks, गजराजनिषेवितः frequented by mighty tuskers, पुण्यश्च sacred, रमणीयश्च delightful, बहुमूलफलायुतः abounding in many roots and fruits, विश्रुतः wellknown, सः that, चित्रकूटः Chitrakuta, शैलः mountain, भवता by you, गम्यताम् go.
explanation: O mighty Rama, I think mount Chitrakuta is the right place for you to stay. Go there. That mountain is full of trees of every kind, is inhabited by kinneras and uragas (serpents). It echoes with the cries of peacocks, is frequented by mighty tuskers. Filled with fruits and roots, it is sacred and pleasant.

shloka_text: वासमौपयिकं मन्ये तव राम महाबल नानानगगणोपेतः किन्नरोरगसेवितः। मयूरनादाभिरुतो गजराजनिषेवितः।।2.54.39।। गम्यतां भवता शैल श्चित्रकूटः स विश्रुतः। पुण्यश्च रमणीयश्च बहुमूलफलायुतः।।2.54.40।।
transliteration: vāsamaupayikaṃ manye tava rāma mahābala nānānagagaṇopetaḥ kinnaroragasevitaḥ| mayūranādābhiruto gajarājaniṣevitaḥ gamyatāṃ bhavatā śaila ścitrakūṭaḥ sa viśrutaḥ| puṇyaśca ramaṇīyaśca bahumūlaphalāyutaḥ
translation: महाबल O mighty one, राम Rama, तव your, औपयिकम् right, वासम् place for your stay, मन्ये I think, नानानगगणोपेतः full of various types of trees, किन्नरोरगसेवितः inhabited by kinneras, serpents, मयूरनादाभिरुतः echoing with cries of peacocks, गजराजनिषेवितः frequented by mighty tuskers, पुण्यश्च sacred, रमणीयश्च delightful, बहुमूलफलायुतः abounding in many roots and fruits, विश्रुतः wellknown, सः that, चित्रकूटः Chitrakuta, शैलः mountain, भवता by you, गम्यताम् go.
explanation: O mighty Rama, I think mount Chitrakuta is the right place for you to stay. Go there. That mountain is full of trees of every kind, is inhabited by kinneras and uragas (serpents). It echoes with the cries of peacocks, is frequented by mighty tuskers. Filled with fruits and roots, it is sacred and pleasant.

shloka_text: तत्र कुञ्जरयूथानि मृगयूथानि चाभितः। विचरन्ति वनान्तेस्मिन् तानि द्रक्ष्यसि राघव।।2.54.41।।
transliteration: tatra kuñjarayūthāni mṛgayūthāni cābhitaḥ| vicaranti vanāntesmin tāni drakṣyasi rāghava
translation: राघव Rama, तत्र there, अस्मिन् वनान्ते in the middle of the forest, अभितः throughout, कुञ्जरयूथानि herds of elephants, मृगयूथानि च and herds of deer, विचरन्ति range about, तानि all that, द्रक्षयसि you will see.
explanation: You will see, O Rama, herds of elephants and deer ranging in the forest.

shloka_text: सरित्प्रस्रवणप्रस्थान् दरीकन्दरनिर्झरान्। चरतः सीतया सार्धं नन्दिष्यति मनस्तव।।2.54.42।।
transliteration: saritprasravaṇaprasthān darīkandaranirjharān| carataḥ sītayā sārdhaṃ nandiṣyati manastava
translation: सीतया सार्धम् along with Sita, सरित्प्रस्रवणप्रस्थान् rivers, waterfalls, plateaus, दरीकन्दरनिर्झरान्  caverns and mountaintorrents, चरतः while wandering, तव your, मनः mind, नन्दिष्यति will be joyful.
explanation: Your heart will be filled with joy while you wander with Sita beholding rivers, waterfalls, plateaus, caverns and mountaintorrents.

shloka_text: प्रहृष्टकोयष्टिककोकिलस्वनैर्विनादितं तं वसुधाधरं शिवम्। मृगैश्च मत्तैर्बहुभिश्च कुञ्जरैः सुरम्यमासाद्य समावसाश्रमम्।।2.54.43।।
transliteration: prahṛṣṭakoyaṣṭikakokilasvanairvināditaṃ taṃ vasudhādharaṃ śivam| mṛgaiśca mattairbahubhiśca kuñjaraiḥ suramyamāsādya samāvasāśramam
translation: प्रहृष्टकोयष्टिककोकिलस्वनैः with the notes of cheerful lapwings and cuckoos, विनादितम् echoed, बहुभिः by many, मृगैश्च deer (animals), मत्तै: intoxicated, कुञ्जरैश्च by elephants, सुरम्यम् exceedingly charming, तं वसुधाधरम् that mount Chitrakuta, आसाद्य having reached, आश्रमम् hermitage, समावस dwell there.
explanation: The auspicious mountain (Chaitrakuta) resounds with the note of cheerful lapwings and cuckoos. Intoxicated elephants and deer move about in the enchanting mountain. There you may settle down in a hermitage. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाश स्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyfourth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: उषित्वा रजनीं तत्र राजपुत्रावरिन्दमौ। महर्षिमभिवाद्याथ जग्मतुस्तं गिरिं प्रति।।2.55.1।।
transliteration: uṣitvā rajanīṃ tatra rājaputrāvarindamau| maharṣimabhivādyātha jagmatustaṃ giriṃ prati
translation: अरिन्दमौ destroyers of enemies, राजपुत्राः the (two) princes, तत्र there, रजनी night, उषित्वा having spent, अथ thereafter, महर्षिम् great sage (Bharadwaja), अभिवाद्य having offered obeisance, तं गिरिं प्रति in the direction of that mountain, जग्मतुः went.
explanation: After spending the night, the princes, destroyers of enemies, offered obeisance to that great sage (Bharadhwaja) and went towards that mount Chitrkuta.
comments: The trio cross Yamuna -- decide to reside on the river bank -- Sita rejoices getting her favourite flowers and fruits.

shloka_text: तेषां चैव स्वस्त्ययनं महर्षि स्स चकार ह। प्रस्थितांश्चैव तान्प्रेक्ष्य पिता पुत्रानिवान्वगात्।।2.55.2।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ caiva svastyayanaṃ maharṣi ssa cakāra ha| prasthitāṃścaiva tānprekṣya pitā putrānivānvagāt
translation: सः महर्षिः that great sage, तेषाम् to them, स्वस्त्ययनम् blessings for their safe journey, चकार ह made, प्रस्थितान् set forth, तान् them, प्रेक्ष्य having seen, पिता father, पुत्रानिव like his own children, अन्वगात् च followed also.
explanation: Seeing them setting forth, the great sage blessed them for a safe journey and followed them like a father following his children.

shloka_text: ततः प्रचक्रमे वक्तुं वचनं स महामुनिः। भरद्वाजो महातेजा रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्।।2.55.3।।
transliteration: tataḥ pracakrame vaktuṃ vacanaṃ sa mahāmuniḥ| bharadvājo mahātejā rāmaṃ satyaparākramam
translation: ततः then, महातेजाः effulgent, महामुनिः great sage, सः भरद्वाजः that Bharadwaja, सत्यपराक्रमम् to one whose strength is truth, रामम् to Rama, वचनम् words, वक्तुम् to tell, प्रचक्रमे began.
explanation: Then that great effulgent sage Bharadwaja began to speak to Rama whose strength was truth.

shloka_text: गङ्गायमुनयो स्सन्धिमासाद्य मनुजर्षभौ। कालिन्दीमनुगच्छेतां नदीं पश्चान्मुखाश्रिताम्।।2.55.4।।
transliteration: gaṅgāyamunayo ssandhimāsādya manujarṣabhau| kālindīmanugacchetāṃ nadīṃ paścānmukhāśritām
translation: मनुजर्षभौ two (best) among men, गङ्गायमुनयोः सन्धिम् the confluence of Ganga and Yamuna, गत्वा having reached, पश्चान्मुखाश्रिताम् flowing westward, कालिन्दी नदीम् river Kalindi (Yamuna), अनुगच्छेताम् proceed along.
explanation: Reaching the confluence of rivers Ganga and Yamuna, O Rama and Lakshmana best among men proceed along the Kalindi (Yamuna) river flowing westward.

shloka_text: अथाऽसाद्य तु कालिन्दी शीघ्रस्रोतसमापगाम्। तस्यास्तीर्थं प्रचलितं पुराणं प्रेक्ष्य राघवौ।।2.55.5।। तत्र यूयं प्लवं कृत्वा तरतांशुमतीं नदीम्।
transliteration: athā'sādya tu kālindī śīghrasrotasamāpagām| tasyāstīrthaṃ pracalitaṃ purāṇaṃ prekṣya rāghavau tatra yūyaṃ plavaṃ kṛtvā taratāṃśumatīṃ nadīm|
translation: राघवौ the scions of the Raghus (Rama and Lakshmana), अथ then, शीघ्रस्रोतसम् rapidiy flowing आपगाम् river, कालिन्दीम् Kalindi (Yamuna), आसाद्य having reached, प्रचलितम् served by many, पुराणम् ancient, तस्याः तीर्थम् spot on the river bank, प्रेक्ष्य finding, तत्र there, यूयम् you, प्लवम् a raft, कृत्वा having made, अंशुमतीम् that daughter of the Sun (Yamuna), नदीम् river, तरत cross over.
explanation: On reaching that swiftflowing river Yamuna, O Rama and Lakshmana O scions of the Raghu race, you will find an ancient spot (on the river bank). There make a raft and cross Kalindi, daughter of the Sun.

shloka_text: ततो न्यग्रोधमासाद्य महान्तं हरितच्छदम्।।2.55.6।। विवृद्धं बहुभिर्वृक्षै श्श्यामं सिद्धोपसेवितम्। तस्मै सीताञ्जलिं कृत्वा प्रयुञ्जीताशिषश्शिवाः।।2.55.7।।
transliteration: tato nyagrodhamāsādya mahāntaṃ haritacchadam vivṛddhaṃ bahubhirvṛkṣai śśyāmaṃ siddhopasevitam| tasmai sītāñjaliṃ kṛtvā prayuñjītāśiṣaśśivāḥ
translation: ततः हरितच्छदम् with lush green leaves, महान्तम् large, बहुभि: by many, वृक्षै: trees, विवृध्दम्  densely grown, सिध्दोपसेवितम् inhabited by siddhas (sages who have attained perfection), श्यामम् dark (shady), न्यग्रोधम् banyan tree, आसाद्य having approached, सीता Sita, तस्मै to it, अञ्जलिम् folded palms, कृत्वा having made, शिवाः auspicious, आशिष: invocations, प्रयुञ्जीत offer.
explanation: There you will find a large, banyan tree with its lush green leaves, looking dark with its densely grown trees. It is inhabited by siddhas. Sita should offer with folded palms invocations for her wellbeing.

shloka_text: ततो न्यग्रोधमासाद्य महान्तं हरितच्छदम्।।2.55.6।। विवृद्धं बहुभिर्वृक्षै श्श्यामं सिद्धोपसेवितम्। तस्मै सीताञ्जलिं कृत्वा प्रयुञ्जीताशिषश्शिवाः।।2.55.7।।
transliteration: tato nyagrodhamāsādya mahāntaṃ haritacchadam vivṛddhaṃ bahubhirvṛkṣai śśyāmaṃ siddhopasevitam| tasmai sītāñjaliṃ kṛtvā prayuñjītāśiṣaśśivāḥ
translation: ततः हरितच्छदम् with lush green leaves, महान्तम् large, बहुभि: by many, वृक्षै: trees, विवृध्दम्  densely grown, सिध्दोपसेवितम् inhabited by siddhas (sages who have attained perfection), श्यामम् dark (shady), न्यग्रोधम् banyan tree, आसाद्य having approached, सीता Sita, तस्मै to it, अञ्जलिम् folded palms, कृत्वा having made, शिवाः auspicious, आशिष: invocations, प्रयुञ्जीत offer.
explanation: There you will find a large, banyan tree with its lush green leaves, looking dark with its densely grown trees. It is inhabited by siddhas. Sita should offer with folded palms invocations for her wellbeing.

shloka_text: समासाद्य तु तं वृक्षं वसेद्वातिक्रमेत वा। क्रोशमात्रं ततो गत्वा नीलं द्रक्ष्यथ काननम्।।2.55.8।। पलाशबदरीमिश्रं रम्यं वंशैश्च यामुनैः।
transliteration: samāsādya tu taṃ vṛkṣaṃ vasedvātikrameta vā| krośamātraṃ tato gatvā nīlaṃ drakṣyatha kānanam palāśabadarīmiśraṃ ramyaṃ vaṃśaiśca yāmunaiḥ|
translation: तम् वृक्षम् that tree, समासाद्य having reached, वसेद्वा one may tarry or, अतिक्रमेत वा or can go past, तत: from there, क्रोशमात्रम् at a distance of a krosa, गत्वा having gone, नीलम् dark, पलाशबदरीमिश्रम् mixed with Palasa and Badari trees, यामुनै: on Yamuna, वंशै: च with bamboos also, रम्यम् beautiful, काननम् forest, द्रक्ष्यथ you will see.
explanation: Reaching that tree, you may tarry or proceed further. A krosa from there, you will see a beautiful forest filled with dark trees mixed with Palasas and badaris and bamboos on the Yamuna.

shloka_text: स पन्थाश्चित्रकूटस्य गत स्सुबहुशो मया।।2.55.9।। रम्यो मार्दवयुक्तश्च वनदावैर्विवर्जितः।
transliteration: sa panthāścitrakūṭasya gata ssubahuśo mayā ramyo mārdavayuktaśca vanadāvairvivarjitaḥ|
translation: स: that one, चित्रकूटस्य of Chitrakuta, पन्था: path, मया by me, बहुश: several times, गत: gone, रम्य beautiful, मार्दवयुक्तश्च marked with smoothness, वनदावै: forest fires, विवर्जित: is without.
explanation: That path leads to Chitrakuta. I had travelled through it several times. It is beautiful, smooth and safe from forest fires.

shloka_text: इति पन्थानमावेद्य महर्षिस्सन्यवर्तत।।2.55.10।। अभिवाद्य तथेत्युक्त्वा रामेण विनिवर्तितः।
transliteration: iti panthānamāvedya maharṣissanyavartata abhivādya tathetyuktvā rāmeṇa vinivartitaḥ|
translation: स: महर्षि: that great sage, इति thus, पन्थानम् path, आवेद्य after directing, रामेण by Rama, तथेति 'so be it', उक्त्वा having said, अभिवाद्य paying obeisance, विनिवर्तित: having been requested to return, न्यवर्तत turned back.
explanation: The great sage returned after instructing Rama about the path. So be it, said Rama and offering obeisance requested Bharadhwaja to go back.

shloka_text: उपावृत्ते मुनौ तस्मिन्रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।।2.55.11।। कृतपुण्याः स्म सौमित्रे मुनिर्यन्नोऽनुकम्पते।
transliteration: upāvṛtte munau tasminrāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt kṛtapuṇyāḥ sma saumitre muniryanno'nukampate|
translation: तस्मिन् मुनौ the sage (Bharadhwaja), उपावृत्ते having turned back, राम Rama, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, अब्रवीत् said, सौमित्रे son of Sumitra, Lakshmana, कृतपुण्या: स्म we are fortunate indeed, यत् since, मुनिः the sage, न: on us, अनुकम्पते is showing compassion.
explanation: With the sage gone, Rama said, O Saumitri (son of Sumitra) we are lucky, for the sage has been so kind.

shloka_text: इति तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ मन्त्रयित्वा मनस्विनौ। सीतामेवाग्रतः कृत्वा कालिन्दीं जग्मतुर्नदीम्।।2.55.12।।
transliteration: iti tau puruṣavyāghrau mantrayitvā manasvinau| sītāmevāgrataḥ kṛtvā kālindīṃ jagmaturnadīm
translation: मनस्विनौ nobleminded, तौ those two, पुरुषव्याघ्रौ tigers (best) among men, इति thus, मन्त्रयित्वा conversing, सीताम् to Sita, अग्रत: इव ahead of them, कृत्वा keeping, कालिन्दीं नदीम्     towards river Kalindi (Yamuna), जग्मतु: proceeded.
explanation: Thus talking with one another, the two nobleminded tigers (best) among men advanced towards river Kalindi (Yamuna) with Sita walking in front.

shloka_text: अथाऽसाद्य तु कालिन्दीं शीघ्रस्रोतोवहां नदीम्। चिन्तामापेदिरे सर्वे नदीजलतितीर्षवः।।2.55.13।।
transliteration: athā'sādya tu kālindīṃ śīghrasrotovahāṃ nadīm| cintāmāpedire sarve nadījalatitīrṣavaḥ
translation: अथ thereafter, सर्वे all of them, शीघ्रस्रोतोवहाम् rapidly flowing, कालिन्दीं नदीम् river Kalindi, आसाद्य having reached, नदीजलतितीर्षव: wishing to cross the river, चिन्ताम् अपेदिरे pondered.
explanation: Thereafter, they all reached the rapidly flowing river Kalindi and began pondering how to cross it.

shloka_text: तौ काष्ठसङ्घातमथो चक्रतु स्सुमहाप्लवम्। शुष्कैर्वंशै स्समास्तीर्णमुशीरैश्च समावृतम्।।2.55.14।।
transliteration: tau kāṣṭhasaṅghātamatho cakratu ssumahāplavam| śuṣkairvaṃśai ssamāstīrṇamuśīraiśca samāvṛtam
translation: अथ then, तौ both of them, शुष्कै: with dry, वंशै: bamboos, समास्तीर्णम् wellspread, उशीरै: fragrant roots of Ushira bush, समावृतम् covered with, काष्टसङ्घातम् with logs of wood joined together, महाप्लवम् big float, चक्रतु: made.
explanation: Then they both made a big wooden float by joining logs of wood, spreading bamboos on it and covering it with the (fragrant roots of) Ushira bushes.

shloka_text: ततो वेतसशाखाश्च जम्बूशाखाश्च वीर्यवान्। चकार लक्ष्मणश्छित्वा सीताया स्सुखमासनम्।।2.55.15।।
transliteration: tato vetasaśākhāśca jambūśākhāśca vīryavān| cakāra lakṣmaṇaśchitvā sītāyā ssukhamāsanam
translation: तत: then, वीर्यवान् valiant, लक्ष्मण: Lakshmana, वेतसशाखाश्च stems of reeds, जम्बूशाखाश्च   branches from Jambu tree, छित्वा after cutting, सीताया: for Sita, सुखम् comfortable, आसनम् seat, चकार made.
explanation: The valiant Lakshmana cut the stems of reeds and branches of the Jambu tree to prepare a comfortable seat for Sita (on that float).

shloka_text: तत्र श्रियमिवाचिन्त्यां रामो दाशरथिः प्रियाम्। ईषत्संलज्जमानां तामध्यारोपयतप्लवम्।।2.55.16।।
transliteration: tatra śriyamivācintyāṃ rāmo dāśarathiḥ priyām| īṣatsaṃlajjamānāṃ tāmadhyāropayataplavam
translation: दाशरथि: Dasaratha's son, रामः Rama, तत्र there, श्रियमिव looking like Lakshmi (goddess of wealth), अचिन्त्याम् inconceivable (majesty), ईषत् a little, संलज्जमानाम् feeling shy, ताम् प्रियाम् that beloved Sita, प्लवम् float, अध्यारोपयत ascended.
explanation: Rama, son of Dasaratha helped his beloved (Sita), who was looking inconceivably like Lakshmi (goddess of wealth) and was feeling a little bashful while stepping on to the float.

shloka_text: पार्श्वे च तत्र वैदेह्या वसने भूषणानि च। प्लवे कठिनकाजं च रामश्चक्रे सहायुधैः।।2.55.17।।
transliteration: pārśve ca tatra vaidehyā vasane bhūṣaṇāni ca| plave kaṭhinakājaṃ ca rāmaścakre sahāyudhaiḥ
translation: राम: Rama, तत्र there, प्लवे on the float, वैदेह्याः Sita's, पार्श्वे on the side of, वसने clothes, भूषणानि च ornaments, कठिनकाजं a crowbar and a basket, आयुधै: weapons, चक्रे placed.
explanation: Rama placed robes and ornaments on the float by the side of Sita and a spade and a basket along with weapons.

shloka_text: आरोप्य प्रथमं सीतां सङ्घाटं परिगृह्य तौ। तत प्रतेरतुर्यत्तौ वीरौ दशरथात्मजौ।।2.55.18।।
transliteration: āropya prathamaṃ sītāṃ saṅghāṭaṃ parigṛhya tau| tata prateraturyattau vīrau daśarathātmajau
translation: वीरौ heroes, तौ those two, दशरथात्मजौ Dasratha's sons, सङ्घाटम् that float, प्रतिगृह्य  tightly holding, प्रथमम् at first, सीताम् Sita, आरोप्य making her board, ततः then, यत्तौ carefully, प्रतेरतुः crossed.
explanation: Those valiant sons of Dasaratha held the float (firmly) to help Sita step on to it. Then they crossed the river carefully.

shloka_text: कालिन्दीमध्यमायाता सीता त्वेनामवन्दत। स्वस्ति देवि तरामि त्वां पारये न्मे पतिर्व्रतम्।।2.55.19।। यक्ष्ये त्वां गोसहस्रेण सुराघटशतेन च। स्वस्ति प्रत्यागते रामे पुरी मिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्।।2.56.20।।
transliteration: kālindīmadhyamāyātā sītā tvenāmavandata| svasti devi tarāmi tvāṃ pāraye nme patirvratam yakṣye tvāṃ gosahasreṇa surāghaṭaśatena ca| svasti pratyāgate rāme purī mikṣvākupālitām
translation: कालिन्दीमध्यम् the middle of the river Kalindi (Yamuna), आयाता on reaching, सीता Sita, एनाम् to this river, अवन्दत made reverential salutation, देवी O goddess, त्वाम् you, तरामि crossing,  स्वस्ति let safety be ours, मे my, पति: husband, व्रतम् vow, पारयेत् may fulfil, रामे Rama, स्वस्ति safely, इक्ष्वाकुपालिताम् ruled by Ikshvaku kings, पुरीम् city of Ayodhya, प्रत्यागते on his return, त्वाम् you, गोसहस्रेण with the offer of a thousand cows, सुराघटशतेन च with a hundred pots of wine, यक्षे will worship.
explanation: On reaching the middle of the river Yamuna, Sita made reverential salutations to her saying O goddess, I am crossing you, may safety be ours and may my husband fulfil his vow After Rama's (safe) return to the city (of Ayodhya) ruled by the Ikshvaku kings, I shall worship you with a thousand cows and a hundred pots of wine.

shloka_text: कालिन्दीमध्यमायाता सीता त्वेनामवन्दत। स्वस्ति देवि तरामि त्वां पारये न्मे पतिर्व्रतम्।।2.55.19।। यक्ष्ये त्वां गोसहस्रेण सुराघटशतेन च। स्वस्ति प्रत्यागते रामे पुरी मिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्।।2.56.20।।
transliteration: kālindīmadhyamāyātā sītā tvenāmavandata| svasti devi tarāmi tvāṃ pāraye nme patirvratam yakṣye tvāṃ gosahasreṇa surāghaṭaśatena ca| svasti pratyāgate rāme purī mikṣvākupālitām
translation: कालिन्दीमध्यम् the middle of the river Kalindi (Yamuna), आयाता on reaching, सीता Sita, एनाम् to this river, अवन्दत made reverential salutation, देवी O goddess, त्वाम् you, तरामि crossing,  स्वस्ति let safety be ours, मे my, पति: husband, व्रतम् vow, पारयेत् may fulfil, रामे Rama, स्वस्ति safely, इक्ष्वाकुपालिताम् ruled by Ikshvaku kings, पुरीम् city of Ayodhya, प्रत्यागते on his return, त्वाम् you, गोसहस्रेण with the offer of a thousand cows, सुराघटशतेन च with a hundred pots of wine, यक्षे will worship.
explanation: On reaching the middle of the river Yamuna, Sita made reverential salutations to her saying O goddess, I am crossing you, may safety be ours and may my husband fulfil his vow After Rama's (safe) return to the city (of Ayodhya) ruled by the Ikshvaku kings, I shall worship you with a thousand cows and a hundred pots of wine.

shloka_text: कालिन्दी मथ सीता तु याचमाना कृताञ्जलिः। तीरमेवाभिसम्प्राप्ता दक्षिणं वरवर्णिनी।।2.55.21।।
transliteration: kālindī matha sītā tu yācamānā kṛtāñjaliḥ| tīramevābhisamprāptā dakṣiṇaṃ varavarṇinī
translation: वरवर्णिनी lady of fair complexion, सीता Sita, कालिन्दीम् Yamuna, कृताञ्जलि: folding her  hands, याचमाना in supplication, अथ thereafter, दक्षिणं तीरमेव southern bank, अभिसम्प्राप्ता reached.
explanation: While Sita with her fair complexion was thus invoking river Yamuna with folded hands they reached the southern bank.

shloka_text: तत प्लवेनांशुमतीं शीघ्रगामूर्मिमालिनीम्। तीरजै र्बहुभिर्वृक्षै स्सन्तेरुर्यमुनां नदीम्।।2.55.22।।
transliteration: tata plavenāṃśumatīṃ śīghragāmūrmimālinīm| tīrajai rbahubhirvṛkṣai ssanteruryamunāṃ nadīm
translation: तत: then, शीघ्रगाम् swiftflowing, ऊर्मिमालिनीम् full of waves, तीरजै: growing on the banks, बहुभि: many, वृक्षै: trees, अंशुमतीम् daughter of the Sungod, यमुनां नदीम् river Yamuna, सन्तेरु: crossed.
explanation: They crossed the swiftflowing river Yamuna, daughter of the Sungod, full of waves and with trees growing thick on her banks.

shloka_text: ते तीर्णाः प्लवमुत्सृज्य प्रस्थाय यमुनावनात्। श्यामं न्यग्रोध मासेदु श्शीतलं हरितच्छदम्।।2.55.23।।
transliteration: te tīrṇāḥ plavamutsṛjya prasthāya yamunāvanāt| śyāmaṃ nyagrodha māsedu śśītalaṃ haritacchadam
translation: तीर्णा: having crossed, ते they, प्लवम् raft, उत्सृज्य after leaving, यमुनावनात् from the forest adjoining Yamuna river, प्रस्थाय after starting, हरितच्छदम् a place full of greenery, शीतलम्  cool, श्यामम् dark, न्यग्रोधम् banyan tree, असेदु: reached.
explanation: Having crossed the river, they left the float and proceeded from the adjoining forest of Yamuna and reached the dark, cool banyan tree covered with lush green leaves.

shloka_text: न्यग्रोधं तमुपागम्य वैदेही वाक्यमब्रवीत्। नमस्तेऽस्तु महावृक्ष पारयेन्मे पतिर्व्रतम्।।2.55.24।। कौशल्यां चैव पश्येयं सुमित्रां च यशश्विनीम्। इति सीताऽञ्जलिं कृत्वा पर्यगच्छद्वनस्पतिम्।।2.55.25।।
transliteration: nyagrodhaṃ tamupāgamya vaidehī vākyamabravīt| namaste'stu mahāvṛkṣa pārayenme patirvratam kauśalyāṃ caiva paśyeyaṃ sumitrāṃ ca yaśaśvinīm| iti sītā'ñjaliṃ kṛtvā paryagacchadvanaspatim
translation: वैदेही Sita, तं न्यग्रोधम् that banyan tree, उपागम्य having reached, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said, महावृक्ष O great tree, ते to you, नम:अस्तु my salutations, मे पतिः my husband, व्रतम् vow, पारयेत् may fulfil, कौशल्यां च and Kausalya, यशश्विनीम् illustrious, सुमित्रां च also Sumitra, पश्येयम् may I behold, सीता Sita, इति in this way, अञ्जलिं कृत्वा offering reverential salutations with folded hands, वनस्पतिम् to the tree, पर्यगच्छत् went round.
explanation: Having reached the banyan tree, Sita invoked it, saying, 'O great tree I offer you my salutations. May my husband fulfil his vow May I behold Kausalya and the illustrious Sumitra on my return. Saying so, she went round the tree offering reverential salutations with folded hands.

shloka_text: न्यग्रोधं तमुपागम्य वैदेही वाक्यमब्रवीत्। नमस्तेऽस्तु महावृक्ष पारयेन्मे पतिर्व्रतम्।।2.55.24।। कौशल्यां चैव पश्येयं सुमित्रां च यशश्विनीम्। इति सीताऽञ्जलिं कृत्वा पर्यगच्छद्वनस्पतिम्।।2.55.25।।
transliteration: nyagrodhaṃ tamupāgamya vaidehī vākyamabravīt| namaste'stu mahāvṛkṣa pārayenme patirvratam kauśalyāṃ caiva paśyeyaṃ sumitrāṃ ca yaśaśvinīm| iti sītā'ñjaliṃ kṛtvā paryagacchadvanaspatim
translation: वैदेही Sita, तं न्यग्रोधम् that banyan tree, उपागम्य having reached, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said, महावृक्ष O great tree, ते to you, नम:अस्तु my salutations, मे पतिः my husband, व्रतम् vow, पारयेत् may fulfil, कौशल्यां च and Kausalya, यशश्विनीम् illustrious, सुमित्रां च also Sumitra, पश्येयम् may I behold, सीता Sita, इति in this way, अञ्जलिं कृत्वा offering reverential salutations with folded hands, वनस्पतिम् to the tree, पर्यगच्छत् went round.
explanation: Having reached the banyan tree, Sita invoked it, saying, 'O great tree I offer you my salutations. May my husband fulfil his vow May I behold Kausalya and the illustrious Sumitra on my return. Saying so, she went round the tree offering reverential salutations with folded hands.

shloka_text: अवलोक्य तत स्सीतामायाचन्तीमनिन्दिताम्। दयितां च विधेयां च रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।।2.55.26।।
transliteration: avalokya tata ssītāmāyācantīmaninditām| dayitāṃ ca vidheyāṃ ca rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt
translation: तत: then, रामः Rama, अयाचन्तीम् who was seeking blessings, अनिन्दिताम् blemishless, दयिताम् beloved, विधेयां च and obedient, सीताम् Sita, अवलोक्य having seen, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Beholding the obedient, blemishless, beloved Sita invoking blessings, Rama said to Lakhsmana:

shloka_text: सीतामादाय गच्छत्वमग्रतो भरतानुज। पृष्ठतोऽहं गमिष्यामि सायुधो द्विपदां वर।।2.55.27।।
transliteration: sītāmādāya gacchatvamagrato bharatānuja| pṛṣṭhato'haṃ gamiṣyāmi sāyudho dvipadāṃ vara
translation: द्विपदां वर best among bipeds (men), भरतानुज brother of Bharata (Lakshmana), त्वम् you, सीताम् Sita, आदाय taking with you, अग्रत: ahead, गच्छ go, अहम् I, सायुध: armed with weapons, पृष्ठत: from behind, गमिष्यामि will follow.
explanation: O Lakshmana, best among bipeds (men) and brother of Bharata walk ahead with Sita and I shall follow with weapons.

shloka_text: यद्यत्फलं प्रार्थयते पुष्पं वा जनकात्मजा। तत्तत्प्रदद्या वैदेह्या यत्राऽस्या रमते मनः।।2.55.28।।
transliteration: yadyatphalaṃ prārthayate puṣpaṃ vā janakātmajā| tattatpradadyā vaidehyā yatrā'syā ramate manaḥ
translation: जनकात्मजा daughter of Janaka, यद्यत्फलम् whichever fruit, पुष्पं वा or flower, प्रार्थयते requests for, तत्तत् that one, अस्या: वैदेह्या: for this Sita, मन: mind, यत्र where, रमते takes pleasure, प्रदद्य give.
explanation: Whatever fruit or flower the daughter of Janaka asks for, get it. Whatever pleases her mind give it.

shloka_text: गच्छतोऽस्तु तयोर्मध्ये बभूव जनकात्मजा। मातङ्गयोर्मध्यगता शुभा नागवधूरिव।।2.55.29।।
transliteration: gacchato'stu tayormadhye babhūva janakātmajā| mātaṅgayormadhyagatā śubhā nāgavadhūriva
translation: गच्छतोः going like that, तयोः of both, मध्यगता moving in the middle, जनकात्मजा daughter of Janaka, मातङ्गयोः of two male elephants, मध्यगता in between, शुभा auspicious, नागवधूरिव like a female elephant, बभूव remained.
explanation: The daughter of Janaka walked between them like a sheelephant between two males.

shloka_text: एकैकं पादपं गुल्मं लतां वा पुष्पशालिनीम्। अदृष्टपूर्वां पश्यन्ती रामं पप्रच्छ साऽबला।।2.55.30।।
transliteration: ekaikaṃ pādapaṃ gulmaṃ latāṃ vā puṣpaśālinīm| adṛṣṭapūrvāṃ paśyantī rāmaṃ papraccha sā'balā
translation: सा अबला that gentle lady, एकैकम् one by one, पादपम् tree, गुल्मम् shrub, अदृष्टपूर्वाम् never seen before, पुष्पशालिनीम् flowering, लतां वा or a creeper, पश्यन्ती seeing, रामम् to Rama, पप्रच्छ asked.
explanation: That gentle lady enquired of Rama about a tree or a shrub or a creeper in full bloom which she did not see before.

shloka_text: रमणीयान्बहुविधान्पादपान्कुसुमोत्कटान्। सीतावचनसंरब्ध आनयामास लक्ष्मणः।।2.55.31।।
transliteration: ramaṇīyānbahuvidhānpādapānkusumotkaṭān| sītāvacanasaṃrabdha ānayāmāsa lakṣmaṇaḥ
translation: लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, सीतावचनसंरब्धः cheered by the indent of Sita, कुसुमोत्कटान् laden with flowers, रमणीयान् beautiful, बहुविधान् various, पादपान् trees, आनयामास brought.
explanation: Cheered by Sita's indents, Lakshmana brought her various beautiful plants and stocks of flowers.

shloka_text: विचित्रवालुकजलां हंससारसनादिताम्। रेमे जनकराजस्य सुता प्रेक्ष्य तदा नदीम्।।2.55.32।।
transliteration: vicitravālukajalāṃ haṃsasārasanāditām| reme janakarājasya sutā prekṣya tadā nadīm
translation: तदा then, जनकराजस्य सुता daughter of king Janaka (Sita), विचित्रवालुकजलाम् wonderful water and sand, हंससारसनादिताम् echoing with the sounds of swans and cranes, नदीम् river Yamuna, प्रेक्ष्य beholding, रेमे exceedingly delighted.
explanation: Beholding the river Yamuna with its wonderful water and sand echoing with the cackle of swans and cranes, Sita went ecstatic.

shloka_text: क्रोशमात्रं ततो गत्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। बहून्मेध्यान्मृगान्हत्वा चेरतुर्यमुनावने।।2.55.33।।
transliteration: krośamātraṃ tato gatvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau| bahūnmedhyānmṛgānhatvā ceraturyamunāvane
translation: तत: then, भ्रातरौ the two brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, क्रोशमात्रम् a krosa, गत्वा having gone, मेध्यान् suitable for sacrifice (pure), बहून् many, मृगान् deer, हत्वा having slain, यमुनावने in the forest on the bank of Yamuna, चेरतु: ate.
explanation: After walking a krosa into the forest on the bank of Yamuna, the two brothers killed many deer suitable for sacrifice and ate them.

shloka_text: विहृत्य ते बर्हिणपूगनादिते शुभे वने वानरवारणायुते। समं नदीवप्रमुपेत्य सम्मतं निवास माजग्मु रदीनदर्शनाः।।2.55.34।।
transliteration: vihṛtya te barhiṇapūganādite śubhe vane vānaravāraṇāyute| samaṃ nadīvapramupetya sammataṃ nivāsa mājagmu radīnadarśanāḥ
translation: अदीनदर्शना: appearing in high spirits, ते they, बर्हिणपूगनादिते resounding with the melody of peacocks, वानरवारणायुते inhabited by monkeys and elephants, शुभे वने in that lovely forest, विहृत्य roaming about, समम् levelled, सम्मतम् convenient, नदीवप्रम् bank of the river, उपेत्य having reached, निवासम् dwelling, आजग्मतु: made.
explanation: They reached the tableland on the bank of that river and moved in high spirit in the lovely forest resounding with cries of flocks of peacocks and teeming with monkeys and elephants. Finally they selected  a spot for their stay. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyfifth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामवसुप्तमनन्तरम्। प्रबोधयामास शनैर्लक्ष्मणं रघुनन्दनः।।2.56.1।।
transliteration: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāmavasuptamanantaram| prabodhayāmāsa śanairlakṣmaṇaṃ raghunandanaḥ
translation: अथ thereafter, रघुनन्दन: Delight of the Raghus (Rama), रात्र्याम् night, अतीतायाम् had passed, अनन्तरम् then, अवसुप्तम् sleeping, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, शनै: gently, प्रबोधयामास awakened.
explanation: When the night was over, Rama, Delight of the Raghus, gently awakened Lakshmana who was asleep.
comments: Chitrakuta described -- Rama meets sage Valmiki -- Lakshmana builds a leafthatched cottage -- Rama enters the cottage at an auspicious time after due worship of respective deities.

shloka_text: सौमित्रे श्रुणु वन्यानां वल्गु व्याहरतां स्वनम्। सम्प्रतिष्ठामहे काल प्रस्थानस्य परन्तप।।2.56.2।।
transliteration: saumitre śruṇu vanyānāṃ valgu vyāharatāṃ svanam| sampratiṣṭhāmahe kāla prasthānasya parantapa
translation: सौमित्रे  Saumitri (son of Sumitra), वल्गु sweet, व्याहरताम् singing, वन्यानाम् of the sylvan birds, स्वनम् voices, श्रुणु you may listen, परन्तप O tormentor of enemies, प्रस्थानस्य  to set out, काल: time, सम्प्रतिष्ठामहे we shall set out.
explanation: Listen to the songs of the forest birds, O son of Sumitra O tormentor of foes it is time we set out.

shloka_text: स सुप्तस्समये भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणः प्रतिबोधितः। जहौ निद्रां च तन्द्रीं च प्रसक्तं च पथि श्रमम्।।2.56.3।।
transliteration: sa suptassamaye bhrātrā lakṣmaṇaḥ pratibodhitaḥ| jahau nidrāṃ ca tandrīṃ ca prasaktaṃ ca pathi śramam
translation: सुप्त: one asleep, स: लक्ष्मण: that Lakshmana, समये in time, भ्रात्रा by his brother, प्रतिबोधित: awakened, निद्रां च sleep, तन्द्रीं च and drowsiness, पथि during journey, प्रसक्तम् associated with, श्रमं च fatigue, जहौ cast off.
explanation: Awakened by his brother in time, Lakshmana shook off his sleep, his drowsiness and his fatigue due to journey.

shloka_text: तत उत्थाय ते सर्वे स्पृष्ट्वा नद्या श्शिवं जलम्। पन्थानमृषिणाऽदिष्टं चित्रकूटस्य तं ययुः।।2.56.4।।
transliteration: tata utthāya te sarve spṛṣṭvā nadyā śśivaṃ jalam| panthānamṛṣiṇā'diṣṭaṃ citrakūṭasya taṃ yayuḥ
translation: तत: then, ते सर्वे they all, उत्थाय rising, नद्या: river's, शिवम् auspicious, जलम् water, स्पृष्ट्वा having touched, ऋषिणा by the sage (Bharadwaja), आदिष्टम् directed, तम् that, चित्रकूटस्य of Chitrakuta, पन्थानम् path, ययु: went.
explanation: Then they all rose, touched the river's auspicious waters and went the way the sage had directed -- towards mount Chitrakuta.

shloka_text: ततस्सम्प्रस्थितः काले रामस्सौमित्रिणा सह। सीतां कमलपत्राक्षीमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.56.5।।
transliteration: tatassamprasthitaḥ kāle rāmassaumitriṇā saha| sītāṃ kamalapatrākṣīmidaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: तत: then, काले at the proper time, सौमित्रिणा सह along with Lakshmana, सम्प्रस्थित:  setting out, राम: Rama, कमलपत्राक्षीम् eyes like lotus petals, सीताम् addressing Sita, इदं वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Early in the morning Rama set out with Lakshmana and said this to Sita with eyes like lotus petals:

shloka_text: आदिप्तानिव वैदेहि सर्वतः पुष्पितान्नगान्। स्वैः पुष्पैः किंशुकान् पश्य मालिनशिशिरात्यये।।2.56.6।।
transliteration: ādiptāniva vaidehi sarvataḥ puṣpitānnagān| svaiḥ puṣpaiḥ kiṃśukān paśya mālinaśiśirātyaye
translation: वैदेहि O daughter of Videha (Sita), शिशिरात्यये at the end of winter, सर्वत: all over, पुष्पितान् in full bloom, आदीप्तानिव as if illuminated, स्त्वै: by their own, पुष्पै: flowers, मालिन: garland, किंशुकान् नगान् Kimsuka trees, पश्य see.
explanation: O daughter of Videha behold these kimsuka trees in full bloom everywhere. With the passing of winter, they appear bright as though they are garlanded by their own flowers.

shloka_text: पश्य भल्लातकान् फुल्लान्नरै रनुपसेवितान्। फलपत्रैरवनता न्नूनं शक्ष्याम जीवितुम्।।2.56.7।।
transliteration: paśya bhallātakān phullānnarai ranupasevitān| phalapatrairavanatā nnūnaṃ śakṣyāma jīvitum
translation: फुल्लान् in full bloom, फलपत्रै: with fruits and leaves, अवनतान् bent low, नरै: by people, अनुपसेवितान् not enjoyed, भल्लातकान् bhallataka trees, पश्य see, नूनम् surely, जीवितुम् to reside, शक्ष्याम able.
explanation: Behold these bhallataka trees in full bloom though there are none to enjoy them. They are bent with fruits and leaves. Surely, we can live here. (This place is fit for our habitation).

shloka_text: पश्य द्रोणप्रमाणानि लम्बमानानि लक्ष्मण। मधूनि मधुकारीभि स्सम्भृतानि नगे नगे।।2.56.8।।
transliteration: paśya droṇapramāṇāni lambamānāni lakṣmaṇa| madhūni madhukārībhi ssambhṛtāni nage nage
translation: लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, नगे नगे in every tree, मधुकारीभि: by bees, सम्भृतानि assembled, द्रोणप्रमाणानि of the size of wooden vessels, लम्बमानानि hanging down, मधूनि honey, पश्य see.
explanation: O Lakshmana see the honeycombs of the size of wooden vessels crowded by the honeybees hanging down from every tree.

shloka_text: एष क्रोशति नत्यूहस्तं शिखी प्रतिकूजति। रमणीये वनोद्देशे पुष्पसंस्तरसङ्कटे।।2.56.9।।
transliteration: eṣa krośati natyūhastaṃ śikhī pratikūjati| ramaṇīye vanoddeśe puṣpasaṃstarasaṅkaṭe
translation: पुष्पसंस्तरसङ्कटे on the ground strewn with fallen flowers, रमणीये in a delightful, वनोद्धेशे in the forest region, एष: this, नत्यूह: natyuha (a type of cuckoo), क्रोशति is screaming, तम् that bird, शिखी peacock, प्रतिकूजति responding with its screaming.
explanation: In this delightful forest region strewn with fallen flowers the peacock is responding to the screaming of natyuha bird.

shloka_text: मातङ्गयूथानुसृतं पक्षिसंङ्घानुनादितम्। चित्रकूटमिमं पश्य प्रवृद्धशिखरं गिरिम्।।2.56.10।।
transliteration: mātaṅgayūthānusṛtaṃ pakṣisaṃṅghānunāditam| citrakūṭamimaṃ paśya pravṛddhaśikharaṃ girim
translation: मातङ्गयूथानुसृतं followed by the herds of elephants, पक्षिसंङ्घानुनादितम् with flocks of singing birds, प्रवृद्धशिखरम् with very towering peaks, इदम् this, गिरिम् mountain, पश्य see.
explanation: See these flocks of singing birds followed by herds of elephants. See this mount Chitrakuta with its towering peaks.

shloka_text: समभूमितले रम्ये द्रुमैर्बहुभिरावृते। पुण्ये रंस्यामहे तात चित्रकूटस्य कानने।।2.56.11।।
transliteration: samabhūmitale ramye drumairbahubhirāvṛte| puṇye raṃsyāmahe tāta citrakūṭasya kānane
translation: तात O dear, समभूमितले on the even ground, बहुभि: by several, द्रुमैः by trees, आवृते covered with, पुण्ये sacred, चित्रकूटस्य Chitrakuta's, कानने in the forest, रंस्यामहे we will enjoy.
explanation: O dear this sacred forest of Chitrakuta standing on a level land is full of various trees. Let us enjoy it.

shloka_text: ततस्तौ पादचारेण गच्छन्तौ सह सीतया। रम्यमासेदतुश्शैलं चित्रकूटं मनोरमम्।।2.56.12।।
transliteration: tatastau pādacāreṇa gacchantau saha sītayā| ramyamāsedatuśśailaṃ citrakūṭaṃ manoramam
translation: तत: then, सीतयासह with Sita, पादचारेण walking on foot, गच्छन्तौ going, तौ both (Rama and Lakshmana), रम्यम् beautiful, मनोरमम् delightful, चित्रकूटं शैलम् Chitrakuta mountain, आसेदतुः reached.
explanation: Then they both along with Sita walked to that lovely, delightful Chitrakuta mountain.

shloka_text: तन्तु पर्वतमासाद्य नानापक्षिगणायुतम्। बहुमूलफलं रम्यं सम्पन्नं सरसोदकम्।।2.56.13।।
transliteration: tantu parvatamāsādya nānāpakṣigaṇāyutam| bahumūlaphalaṃ ramyaṃ sampannaṃ sarasodakam
translation: नानापक्षिगणायुतम् filled with various kinds of birds, बहुमूलफलम् with varieties of roots and fruits, रम्यम् enchanting, सम्पन्नम् rich, सरसोदकम् of tasty water, तं पर्वतम् that mountain, आसाद्य having reached, (Rama said).
explanation: Rama arrived at that enchanting mountain full of various kinds of birds, fruits and roots, and sweet water. (And said to Lakshmana:)

shloka_text: मनोज्ञोऽयं गिरिस्सौम्य नानाद्रुमलतायुतः। बहुमूलफलो रम्य स्स्वाजीवः प्रतिभाति मे।।2.56.14।।
transliteration: manojño'yaṃ girissaumya nānādrumalatāyutaḥ| bahumūlaphalo ramya ssvājīvaḥ pratibhāti me
translation: सौम्य O gentle one, मनोज्ञ: pleasing to the heart, नानादृमलतायुत: with various kinds of trees and creepers, बहुमूलफल: with many roots and fruits, रम्य: beautiful, अयं गिरि: this mountain, स्वाजीव: a happy place to live in, मे to me, प्रतिभाति appears.
explanation: O gentle one this enchanting mountain with different kinds of trees and creepers and many roots and fruits appears to be a happy place to live in.

shloka_text: मुनयश्च महात्मानो वसन्त्यस्मि शिलोच्चये। अयं वासो भवेत्तावदत्र सौम्य रमेमहि।।2.56.15।।
transliteration: munayaśca mahātmāno vasantyasmi śiloccaye| ayaṃ vāso bhavettāvadatra saumya ramemahi
translation: सौम्य O handsome one, अस्मिन् in this, शिलोच्चये on the mountain, महात्मन: great, मुनयश्च sages, वसन्ति reside, अयम् this, वास: habitation, भवेत्तावत् let it be, अत्र here, रमेमहि will enjoy.
explanation: Great sages reside on this high mountain. Let it be our habitation and let us enjoy our life here, O handsome one

shloka_text: इति सीता च रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च कृताञ्जलिः। अभिगम्याऽश्रमं सर्वे वाल्मीकि मभिवादयन्।।2.56.16।।
transliteration: iti sītā ca rāmaśca lakṣmaṇaśca kṛtāñjaliḥ| abhigamyā'śramaṃ sarve vālmīki mabhivādayan
translation: इति thus, सीता च Sita, रामश्च Rama, कृताञ्जलि: with folded palms, लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana also, सर्वे all, आश्रमम् hermitage, अभिगम्य having approached, वाल्मीकिम् to sage Valmiki, अभिवादयन् paid obeisance.
explanation: Thus Rama, Sita and Lakshmana approached the hermitage of sage Valmiki and paid obeisance to him with folded hands.

shloka_text: तान्महर्षि प्रमुदितः पूजयामास धर्मवित्। अस्यतामिति चोवाच स्वागन्तु निवेद्य च।।2.56.17।।
transliteration: tānmaharṣi pramuditaḥ pūjayāmāsa dharmavit| asyatāmiti covāca svāgantu nivedya ca
translation: धर्मवित् conversant with righteousness, महर्षि: the great sage (Valmiki), प्रमुदित: full of delight, तान् them, पूजयामास honoured, स्वागतम् welcome, निवेद्य having offered, अस्यताम् इति be seated, उवाच च and said.
explanation: The great sage Valmiki conversant with righteousness was delighted. He honoured them by extending welcome and said 'Be seated'.

shloka_text: ततोऽब्रवीन्महाबाहुर्लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। सन्निवेद्य यथान्याय मात्मानमृषये प्रभुः।।2.56.18।।
transliteration: tato'bravīnmahābāhurlakṣmaṇaṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ| sannivedya yathānyāya mātmānamṛṣaye prabhuḥ
translation: तत: then, महाबाहु: mightyarmed, प्रभु: master, लक्ष्माणाग्रज: the elder brother of Lakshmana, आत्मानम् himself, यथान्यायम् duly, ऋषये to the ascetic, सन्निवेद्य having introduced, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: The mightyarmed elder brother of Lakshmana revealed his identity to the sage by duly introducing himself. And said then to Lakshmana:

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणाऽऽनय दारूणि दृढानि च वराणि च। कुरुष्वाऽवसथं सौम्य वासे मेऽभिरतं मनः।।2.56.19।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇā''naya dārūṇi dṛḍhāni ca varāṇi ca| kuruṣvā'vasathaṃ saumya vāse me'bhirataṃ manaḥ
translation: सौम्य लक्ष्मण O handsome Lakshmana, दृढानि strong, वराणि च good, दारूणि logs of wood, आनय fetch, अवसथम् a dwelling, कुरुष्व build, मे मन: my mind, वासे in staying, अभिरतम् is eager.
explanation: O handsome Lakshmana, make a hut with strong, sound logs of wood. My mind impels me to stay here.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सौमित्रिर्विविधान् द्रुमान्। आजहार तत श्चक्रे पर्णशालामरिन्दमः।।2.56.20।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā saumitrirvividhān drumān| ājahāra tata ścakre parṇaśālāmarindamaḥ
translation: सौमित्रि: son of Sumitra (Lakshmana), तस्य Rama's, तत् वचनम् those words, श्रुत्वा on hearing, विविधान् different kinds of, दृमान् logs of wood, आजहार fetched, अरिन्दम: subduer of enemies, तत: then, पर्णशालाम् cottage thatched with leaves, चक्रे built.
explanation: Having heard Rama, Saumitri, the subduer of enemies fetched different kinds of logs of wood, and with them made a hut and thatched it with leaves.

shloka_text: तां निष्ठितां बद्धकटां दृष्ट्वा रामस्सुदर्शनाम्। शुश्रूषमाणमेकाग्रमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.56.21।।
transliteration: tāṃ niṣṭhitāṃ baddhakaṭāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmassudarśanām| śuśrūṣamāṇamekāgramidaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: राम: Rama, निष्ठितान् firmly fixed, बद्दकटाम् with mats tied around as walls, सुदर्शनाम् goodlooking, ताम् दृष्ट्वा having seen it, शुश्रूषमाणम् on listening (to further command), एकाग्रम् with attention, इदं वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Rama saw the goodlooking leafhut with mats tied around as walls, and said to Lakshmana who was awaiting further command with rapt attention:

shloka_text: ऐणेयं मांसमाहृत्य शालां यक्ष्यामहे वयम्। कर्तव्यं वास्तुशमनं सौमित्रे चिरजीविभिः।।2.56.22।।
transliteration: aiṇeyaṃ māṃsamāhṛtya śālāṃ yakṣyāmahe vayam| kartavyaṃ vāstuśamanaṃ saumitre cirajīvibhiḥ
translation: सौमित्रे O Lakshmana, ऐणेयं मांसम् venison of black antelope, आहृत्य having brought, वयम् we, शालाम् this hut, यक्ष्यामहे will worship, चिरजीविभि: those who intend to live longer, वास्तुशमनम् pacification of household deity, कर्तव्यम् should be done.
explanation: O Lakshmana those who intend to live for long (in this hut), should pacify the deity presiding over here. Therefore, we shall bring the venison of a black antelope and make necessary offerings.

shloka_text: मृगं हत्वाऽऽनय क्षिप्रं लक्ष्मणेह शुभेक्षण। कर्तव्य श्शास्त्रदृष्टो हि विधिर्धर्ममनुस्मर।।2.56.23।।
transliteration: mṛgaṃ hatvā''naya kṣipraṃ lakṣmaṇeha śubhekṣaṇa| kartavya śśāstradṛṣṭo hi vidhirdharmamanusmara
translation: शुभेक्षण one who has auspicious looks, लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, मृगम् an antelope, हत्वा  having killed, क्षिप्रम् quickly, इह here, आनय bring, शास्त्रदृष्ट: as prescribed by the  scriptures, विधि: rites, कर्तव्यः हि will have to be carried out, धर्मम् the tradition, अनुस्मर recollect.
explanation: Slay an antelope and bring it here quickly. O Lakshmana The rites as prescribed by the scriptures will have to be carried out. You may recollect that tradition.

shloka_text: भ्रातुर्वचनमाज्ञाय लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा। चकार स यथोक्तं च तं राम पुनरब्रवीत्।।2.56.24।।
transliteration: bhrāturvacanamājñāya lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā| cakāra sa yathoktaṃ ca taṃ rāma punarabravīt
translation: परवीरहा slayer of heroes of the enemy's side, स लक्ष्मण: that Lakshmana, भ्रातु: brother' s, वचनम् words, आज्ञाय having understood, यथोक्तम् as told, चकार carried out, राम: Rama, तम् him, पुन: again, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Lakshmana, slayer of heroes on the enemy's side, understood and implemented what he was told. Rama again said to him:

shloka_text: ऐणेयं श्रपयस्वैतच्छालां यक्ष्यामहे वयम्। त्वर सौम्य मुहूर्तोऽयं ध्रुवश्च दिवसोऽप्ययम्।।2.56.25।।
transliteration: aiṇeyaṃ śrapayasvaitacchālāṃ yakṣyāmahe vayam| tvara saumya muhūrto'yaṃ dhruvaśca divaso'pyayam
