shloka_text: विजनेऽपि वने सीता वासं प्राप्य गृहेष्विव। विस्रम्भं लभतेऽभीता रामे सन्न्यस्तमानसा।।2.60.7।।
transliteration: vijane'pi vane sītā vāsaṃ prāpya gṛheṣviva| visrambhaṃ labhate'bhītā rāme sannyastamānasā
translation: सीता Sita, विजने in the desolate, वनेपि in the forest also, गृहेष्विव like at home, वासम् living, प्राप्य having obtained, रामे in Rama, सन्न्यस्तमानसा with her mind fixed, अभीता without fear, विस्रम्भम् confidence, लभते  is getting.
explanation: Sita with her mind fixed on Rama is living confidently in that desolate forest without any fear as if it were her home.

shloka_text: नास्या दैन्यं कृतं किञ्चित्सुसूक्ष्ममपि लक्ष्यते। उचितेव प्रवासानां वैदेही प्रतिभाति मा।।2.60.8।।
transliteration: nāsyā dainyaṃ kṛtaṃ kiñcitsusūkṣmamapi lakṣyate| uciteva pravāsānāṃ vaidehī pratibhāti mā
translation: अस्याः of her, सुसूक्ष्ममपि even the slightest, दैन्यम् dejection, किञ्चित् not even a little, कृतम् done, न लक्ष्यते not to be seen, वैदेही Sita, प्रवासानाम् for staying away from home, उचितेव as if accustomed, मा to me, प्रतिभाति appears.
explanation: I could not see even the slightest depression in Sita as if she was accustomed to staying away from home.

shloka_text: नगरोपवनं गत्वा यथा स्मरमते पुरा। तथैव रमते सीता निर्जनेषु वनेष्वपि।।2.60.9।।
transliteration: nagaropavanaṃ gatvā yathā smaramate purā| tathaiva ramate sītā nirjaneṣu vaneṣvapi
translation: सीता Sita, पुरा earlier, नगरोपवनम् to the pleasuregardens of the city, गत्वा having gone, यथा as, रमतेस्म was enjoying, निर्जनेषु in desolate, वनेष्वपि even in the forest, तथैव in the same way, रमते enjoying.
explanation: Earlier, just as Sita used to revel in the gardens of the city, so does she now in those desolate forests.

shloka_text: बालेव रमते सीताऽबालचन्द्रनिभानना। रामा रामे ह्यधीनात्मा विजनेऽपि वने सती।।2.60.10।।
transliteration: bāleva ramate sītā'bālacandranibhānanā| rāmā rāme hyadhīnātmā vijane'pi vane satī
translation: रामा charming lady, रामे in Rama, अधीनात्मा one with absorbed mind, अबालचन्द्रनिभानना countenance resembling the full Moon, सीता Sita, विजने desolate, वने in the forest also, सती अपि staying, बालेव like a child, रमते is enjoying.
explanation: Charming Sita whose face resembles the full Moon, with her mind fixed on Rama, is enjoying even the desolate forest like a child.

shloka_text: तद्गतं हृदयं ह्यस्यास्तदधीनं च जीवितम्। अयोध्यापि भवेऽत्तस्या रामहीना तदा वनम्।।2.60.11।।
transliteration: tadgataṃ hṛdayaṃ hyasyāstadadhīnaṃ ca jīvitam| ayodhyāpi bhave'ttasyā rāmahīnā tadā vanam
translation: अस्याः her, हृदयम् heart, तद्गतम् united with Rama, जीवितं च life also, तदधीनम् under his control, अयोध्यापि even Ayodhya too, रामहीना without Rama, तदा then, तस्याः to her, वनम् forest, भवेत् would have become.
explanation: Her heart is ever united with Rama, and her life is under his control. Without Rama, even Ayodhya would become a forest for her.

shloka_text: परिपृच्छति वैदेही ग्रामांश्च नगराणि च। गतिं दृष्ट्वा नदीनां च पादपान्विविधानपि।।2.60.12।। रामं हि लक्ष्मणं वापि पृष्ट्वा जानाति जानकी। अयोध्या क्रोशमात्रे तु विहारमिव संश्रिता।।2.60.13।।
transliteration: paripṛcchati vaidehī grāmāṃśca nagarāṇi ca| gatiṃ dṛṣṭvā nadīnāṃ ca pādapānvividhānapi rāmaṃ hi lakṣmaṇaṃ vāpi pṛṣṭvā jānāti jānakī| ayodhyā krośamātre tu vihāramiva saṃśritā
translation: अयोध्या क्रोशमात्रे at the distance of a krosa from Ayodhya, विहारम् pleasuregarden, संश्रिता इव as if sporting, वैदेही Sita, ग्रामांश्च villages, नगराणि च cities,नदीनाम् rivers', गतिं च   courses, विविधान् different kinds of, पादपानपि trees also, दृष्ट्वा seeing, रामम् to Rama, परिपृच्छति enquiring, लक्ष्मणं वापि or Lakshmana, पृष्ट्वा asking, जानाति knowing.
explanation: Seeing villages, cities, trees of different kinds and courses of rivers, Sita is enquiring from Rama or Lakshmana about them. She feels as though she is sporting in the pleasuregarden just a krosa from Ayodhya.

shloka_text: परिपृच्छति वैदेही ग्रामांश्च नगराणि च। गतिं दृष्ट्वा नदीनां च पादपान्विविधानपि।।2.60.12।। रामं हि लक्ष्मणं वापि पृष्ट्वा जानाति जानकी। अयोध्या क्रोशमात्रे तु विहारमिव संश्रिता।।2.60.13।।
transliteration: paripṛcchati vaidehī grāmāṃśca nagarāṇi ca| gatiṃ dṛṣṭvā nadīnāṃ ca pādapānvividhānapi rāmaṃ hi lakṣmaṇaṃ vāpi pṛṣṭvā jānāti jānakī| ayodhyā krośamātre tu vihāramiva saṃśritā
translation: अयोध्या क्रोशमात्रे at the distance of a krosa from Ayodhya, विहारम् pleasuregarden, संश्रिता इव as if sporting, वैदेही Sita, ग्रामांश्च villages, नगराणि च cities,नदीनाम् rivers', गतिं च   courses, विविधान् different kinds of, पादपानपि trees also, दृष्ट्वा seeing, रामम् to Rama, परिपृच्छति enquiring, लक्ष्मणं वापि or Lakshmana, पृष्ट्वा asking, जानाति knowing.
explanation: Seeing villages, cities, trees of different kinds and courses of rivers, Sita is enquiring from Rama or Lakshmana about them. She feels as though she is sporting in the pleasuregarden just a krosa from Ayodhya.

shloka_text: इदमेव स्मराम्यस्यास्सहसैवोपजल्पितम्। कैकेयी संश्रितं वाक्यं नेदानीं प्रतिभाति मा।।2.60.14।।
transliteration: idameva smarāmyasyāssahasaivopajalpitam| kaikeyī saṃśritaṃ vākyaṃ nedānīṃ pratibhāti mā
translation: अस्याः her, इदमेव this much, स्मरामि I remember, सहसैव suddenly, उपजल्पितम् utterance, कैकेयी संश्रितम् about Kaikeyi, वाक्यम् words, इदानीम् now, मा to me, न प्रतिभाति does not come to my mind.
explanation: Sita did say something about Kaikeyi, but now I do not remember what.

shloka_text: ध्वंसयित्वा तु तद्वाक्यं प्रमादात्पर्युपत्स्थितम्। ह्लादनं वचनं सूतो देव्या मधुरमब्रवीत्।।2.60.15।।
transliteration: dhvaṃsayitvā tu tadvākyaṃ pramādātparyupatsthitam| hlādanaṃ vacanaṃ sūto devyā madhuramabravīt
translation: सूतः charioteer, प्रमादात् inadvertently, पर्युपत्स्थितम् uttered by all means, तद्वाक्यम् those words relating to Kaikeyi, ध्वंसयित्वा holding back, देव्याः to Kausalya, ह्लादनम् causing delight, मधुरम् pleasing, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Diverting the context of what he uttered inadvertently relating to Kaikeyi, the charioteer said pleasing words of consolation to Kausalya.

shloka_text: अध्वना वातवेगेन सम्भ्रमेणाऽऽतपेन च। न विगच्छति वैदेह्याश्चन्द्रांशु सदृशी प्रभा।।2.60.16।।
transliteration: adhvanā vātavegena sambhrameṇā''tapena ca| na vigacchati vaidehyāścandrāṃśu sadṛśī prabhā
translation: वैदेह्याः Sita's, चन्द्रांशु सदृशी resembling the beams of the Moon, प्रभा lustre, अध्वना on the way, वातवेगेन or by the speed of the wind, सम्भ्रमेण or due to haste, आतपेन च or due to scorching heat also, न विगच्छति does not fade.
explanation: Just like the beams of the Moon, Sita's glow is not affected by the fatigue of the journey or by the speed of the wind or by the scorching heat.

shloka_text: सदृशं शतपत्रस्य पूर्णचन्द्रोपमप्रभम्। वदनं तद्वदान्याया वैदेह्या न विकम्पते।।2.60.17।।
transliteration: sadṛśaṃ śatapatrasya pūrṇacandropamaprabham| vadanaṃ tadvadānyāyā vaidehyā na vikampate
translation: वदान्यायाः of that munificent, वैदेह्याः Sita, शतपत्रस्य a hundredpetalled lotus, सदृशम् similar to, पूर्णचन्द्रोपमप्रभम् like the splendour of the full Moon, तत् वदनम् that countenance, न विकम्पते does not change at all.
explanation: The countenance of Sita with her gentle eloquence resembles a hundredpetalled lotus. She has the luminance of the full Moon that has not wilted.

shloka_text: अलक्तरसरक्ताभावलक्तरसवर्जितौ। अद्यापि चरणौ तस्याः पद्मकोशसमप्रभौ।।2.60.18।।
transliteration: alaktarasaraktābhāvalaktarasavarjitau| adyāpi caraṇau tasyāḥ padmakośasamaprabhau
translation: अलक्तरसक्ताभौ shining red like the liquid lac, अलक्तरसवर्जितौ no longer tinted with such liquid, तस्याः her, चरणौ feet, अद्यापि even now, पद्मकोशसमप्रभौ are shining like the lotus buds.
explanation: Her feet, now devoid of lacdye, still look red like lac and shine like the lotus bud.

shloka_text: नूपुरोद्घुष्टहेलेव खेलं गच्छति भामिनी। इदानीमपि वैदेही तद्रागान्नयस्त भूषणा।।2.60.19।।
transliteration: nūpurodghuṣṭaheleva khelaṃ gacchati bhāminī| idānīmapi vaidehī tadrāgānnayasta bhūṣaṇā
translation: भामिनी damsel (Sita), नूपुरोद्घुष्ट हेलेव tinkling anklets proclaiming dalliance, खेलम् (as if) playing, गच्छति going, वैदेही Sita, इदानीमपि even now, तद्रागात् due to affection for Rama, नयस्तभूषणा cast off the ornaments.
explanation: Casting off her ornaments, the damsel (Sita) is gracefully walking as if dalliant with her tinkling anklets for her love for him (Rama).

shloka_text: गजं वा वीक्ष्य सिंहं वा व्याघ्रं वा वनमाश्रिता। नाऽहारयति सन्त्रासं बाहू रामस्य संश्रिता।।2.60.20।।
transliteration: gajaṃ vā vīkṣya siṃhaṃ vā vyāghraṃ vā vanamāśritā| nā'hārayati santrāsaṃ bāhū rāmasya saṃśritā
translation: वनम् forest, आश्रिता resorted, रामस्य Rama's, बाहू arms, संश्रिता having taken refuge, गजं वा elephant, सिंहं वा or lion, व्याघ्रं वा or tiger, वीक्ष्य having seen, सन्त्रासं fear, नाऽहारयति does not get.
explanation: Though in the forest, Sita, under the protection of Rama's arms, is afraid of neither elephants nor lions nor tigers.

shloka_text: न शोच्यास्ते न चात्मनश्शोच्यो नापि जनाधिपः। इदं हि चरितं लोके प्रतिष्ठास्यति शाश्वतम्।।2.60.21।।
transliteration: na śocyāste na cātmanaśśocyo nāpi janādhipaḥ| idaṃ hi caritaṃ loke pratiṣṭhāsyati śāśvatam
translation: ते they, न शोच्याः need not be pitied, आत्मनः च yourself, न not, जनाधिप अपि king also, इदम् this, चरितम् history, लोके in the world, शाश्वतम् permanently, प्रतिष्ठास्यति will endure.
explanation: You need not lament for them or for yourself or for the king. This story of Rama will endure permanently in the world.

shloka_text: विधूय शोकं परिहृष्टमानसा महर्षियाते पथि सुव्यवत्स्थिताः। वनेरता वन्यफलाशनाः पितुश्शुभां प्रतिज्ञां परिपालयन्ति ते।।2.60.22।।
transliteration: vidhūya śokaṃ parihṛṣṭamānasā maharṣiyāte pathi suvyavatsthitāḥ| vaneratā vanyaphalāśanāḥ pituśśubhāṃ pratijñāṃ paripālayanti te
translation: ते they, शोकम् grief, विधूय shaking off, परिहृष्टमानसाः with cheerful hearts, महर्षियाते  established by maharshis, पथि in the path, सुव्यवत्स्थिताः firmly fixed, वने in the forest, रताः  are enjoying, वन्यफलाशनाः subsisting on forest fruits, पितुः father's, शुभाम् auspicious, प्रतिज्ञाम् promise, परिपालयन्ति are upholding.
explanation: They are upholding the sacred promise of their father with cheerful hearts, grief given the goby, steadfastly pursuing the path established by maharsis, subsisting on forest fruits and enjoying the forest life.

shloka_text: तथापि सूतेन सुयुक्तवादिना निवार्यमाणा सुतशोककर्शिता। न चैव देवी विरराम कूजितात्प्रियेति पुत्रेति च राघवेति च।।2.60.23।।
transliteration: tathāpi sūtena suyuktavādinā nivāryamāṇā sutaśokakarśitā| na caiva devī virarāma kūjitātpriyeti putreti ca rāghaveti ca
translation: सुयुक्तवादिना by one who was speaking befittingly, सूतेना by Sumantra, तथा like that, निवार्यमाणापि though prevented, देवी queen Kausalya, सुतशोककर्शिता enfeebled with weeping over her son, प्रियेति 'O My beloved', पुत्रेति 'O my son', राघवेति च 'O Rama', कूजितात् from crying, नचैव विरराम did not stop.
explanation: Though Sumantra was speaking with befitting words to prevent Kausalya from weeping over her son which had enfeebled her, she did not stop crying, 'O my beloved', 'O my son', 'O Rama'. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtieth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: वनं गते धर्मपरे रामे रमयतां वरे। कौसल्या रुदती स्वार्ता भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.61.1।।
transliteration: vanaṃ gate dharmapare rāme ramayatāṃ vare| kausalyā rudatī svārtā bhartāramidamabravīt
translation: धर्मपरे dutiful, रमयताम् pleasing others, वरे greatest, रामे Rama, वनम् forest, गते had gone, कौशल्या Kausalya, स्वार्ता in bitter anguish, रुदती sobbing, भर्तारम् to her husband, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: When Rama, the greatest among those who please the people, he who was conscious of his duty left for the forest. Kausalya, sobbing in bitter anguish, said to her husband:
comments: Kausalya condemns Dasaratha's action -- Dasaratha loses his senses out of intense grief.

shloka_text: यद्यपि त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रथितं ते महद्यशः। सानुक्रोशो वदान्यश्च प्रियवादी च राघवः।।2.61.2।।
transliteration: yadyapi triṣu lokeṣu prathitaṃ te mahadyaśaḥ| sānukrośo vadānyaśca priyavādī ca rāghavaḥ
translation: राघवः Dasaratha, scion of the Raghu dynasty, सानुक्रोशः compassionate, वदान्यश्च generous, प्रियवादी च sweettongued, ते your, महत् great, यशः fame, त्रिषु three, लोकेषु in worlds, प्रथितं यद्यपि even though very popular.
explanation: Your great fame has spread all over the three worlds. People know you as compassionate, generous and sweetspeaking scion of the Raghus.

shloka_text: कथं नरवरश्रेष्ठ पुत्रौ तौ सह सीतया। दुःखितौ सुखसंवृद्धौ वने दुःखं सहिष्यतः।।2.61.3।।
transliteration: kathaṃ naravaraśreṣṭha putrau tau saha sītayā| duḥkhitau sukhasaṃvṛddhau vane duḥkhaṃ sahiṣyataḥ
translation: नरवरश्रेष्ठ best among kings (Dasaratha), सुखसंवृद्धौ brought up with comfort, तौ पुत्रौ your two sons, सीतया सह with Sita, दुःखितौ stricken with grief, वने in the forest, दुःखम्  suffering, कथम् how?, सहिष्यतः endure?
explanation: O Dasaratha, the best among kings, how will your two sons and Sita brought up in great comfort now tolerate the hardships of forest life?

shloka_text: सा नूनं तरुणी श्यामा सुकुमारी सुखोचिता। कथमुष्णं च शीतं च मैथिली प्रसहिष्यते।।2.61.4।।
transliteration: sā nūnaṃ taruṇī śyāmā sukumārī sukhocitā| kathamuṣṇaṃ ca śītaṃ ca maithilī prasahiṣyate
translation: तरुणी young, श्यामा in the prime of life, सुकुमारी delicate, सुखोचिता accustomed to comfort, सा मैथिली that Sita, उष्णं च heat, शीतं च cold, नूनम् surely, कथम् how?, प्रसहिष्यते will bear.
explanation: How can the daughter of Mithila (Sita) who in the prime of her life, accustomed to comforts, endure  heat and cold indeed?

shloka_text: भुक्त्वाऽशनं विशालाक्षी सूपदं शान्वितं शुभम्। वन्यं नैवारमाहारं कथं सीतोपभोक्ष्यते।।2.61.5।।
transliteration: bhuktvā'śanaṃ viśālākṣī sūpadaṃ śānvitaṃ śubham| vanyaṃ naivāramāhāraṃ kathaṃ sītopabhokṣyate
translation: विशालाक्षी largeeyed, सीता Sita, सूपदं शान्वितम् with condiments and soup, शुभम् wellprepared, अशनम् food, भुक्त्वा having partaken, वन्यम् in the forest, नैवारम् made with wild rice, आहारम् food, कथं उपभोक्ष्यते how will she eat?
explanation: How can the largeeyed Sita having enjoyed delicious food mixed with condiments and soup now partake the food prepared with wild grains?

shloka_text: गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा शुभमनिन्दिता। कथं क्रव्यादसिंहानां शब्दं श्रोष्यत्यशोभनम्।।2.61.6।।
transliteration: gītavāditranirghoṣaṃ śrutvā śubhamaninditā| kathaṃ kravyādasiṃhānāṃ śabdaṃ śroṣyatyaśobhanam
translation: अनिन्दिता blameless, शुभम् auspicious, गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषम् sounds of songs and musical instruments, श्रुत्वा having heard, अशोभनम् inauspicious, क्रव्यादसिंहानाम् carnivorous animals' and lions', शब्दम् sound, कथम् how?, श्रोष्यति can hear.
explanation: How can the blameless Sita, used to the soft sound of songs and musical instruments hear the frightful roars of lions and other carnivorous animals?

shloka_text: महेन्द्रध्वजसङ्काशः क्व नु शेते महाभुजः। भुजं परिघसङ्काशमुपधाय महाबलः।।2.61.7।।
transliteration: mahendradhvajasaṅkāśaḥ kva nu śete mahābhujaḥ| bhujaṃ parighasaṅkāśamupadhāya mahābalaḥ
translation: महेन्द्रध्वजसङ्काशः resembling mighty Indra's banner, महाभुजः longarmed one, महाबलः mighty, परिघसङ्काशम् like a sword, भुजम् arm, उपधाय using as a pillow, क्व where, शेते नु is he sleeping?
explanation: Where will that mightyarmed and powerful Rama, as lofty as Indra's banner, sleep using his ironbarlike arm as pillow?.

shloka_text: पद्मवर्णं सुकेशान्तं पद्मनिश्श्वासमुत्तमम्। कदा द्रक्ष्यामि रामस्य वदनं पुष्करेक्षणम्।।2.61.8।।
transliteration: padmavarṇaṃ sukeśāntaṃ padmaniśśvāsamuttamam| kadā drakṣyāmi rāmasya vadanaṃ puṣkarekṣaṇam
translation: पद्मवर्णम् lotuslike complexion, सुकेशान्तम् having beautiful hairends, पद्मनिश्श्वासम् breath of lotus fragrance, पुष्करेक्षणम् eyes like blue lotus, उत्तमम् excellent, रामस्य वदनम् Rama's countenance, कदा when, द्रक्ष्यामि shall I behold?.
explanation: When shall I see Rama with his lotushued face, his beautiful locks of hair, breath of lotus fragrance and eyes like blue lotus?

shloka_text: वज्रसारमयं नूनं हृदयं मे न संशयः। अपश्यन्त्या न तं यद्वै फलतीदं सहस्रधा।।2.61.9।।
transliteration: vajrasāramayaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ me na saṃśayaḥ| apaśyantyā na taṃ yadvai phalatīdaṃ sahasradhā
translation: मे हृदयम् my heart, वज्रसारमयम् is made of thunderbolt, नूनम् surely, संशयः doubt, न not, यत् since, तम् Rama, अपश्यन्त्याः without seeing, इदम् this heart, सहस्रधा thousand pieces, न फलति वै does not shatter.
explanation: No doubt my heart must be made of thunderbolt, since unable to see Rama it does not split into a thousand pieces.

shloka_text: यत्त्वयाऽकरुणं कर्म व्यपोह्य मम बान्धवाः। निरस्ताः परिधावन्ति सुखार्हाः कृपणा वने।।2.61.10।।
transliteration: yattvayā'karuṇaṃ karma vyapohya mama bāndhavāḥ| nirastāḥ paridhāvanti sukhārhāḥ kṛpaṇā vane
translation: त्वया by you, करुणम् heartless, कर्म act, व्यपोह्य cast away, सुखार्हाः deserve pleasures, मम बान्धवाः my relations, निरस्ताः are banished, कृपणाः the miserable ones, वने in the forest, यत् since, परिधावन्ति are running around.
explanation: (O king) It is because of your heartless action, my Rama and my relatives who deserve to enjoy pleasures at this age have been banished and are miserably wandering in wilderness.

shloka_text: यदि पञ्चदशे वर्षे राघवः पुनरेष्यति। जह्याद्राज्यं च कोषं च भरतो नोपलक्षयते।।2.61.11।।
transliteration: yadi pañcadaśe varṣe rāghavaḥ punareṣyati| jahyādrājyaṃ ca koṣaṃ ca bharato nopalakṣayate
translation: राघवः Rama, पञ्चदशे वर्षे in the fifteenth year, पुनः एष्यति यदि if returns, भरतः Bharata, राज्यं च kingdom, कोषं च treasury too, जह्यात् will give up, नोपलक्ष्यते it does not appear.
explanation: Even if Rama returns in the fifteenth year, it is unlikely that Bharata will give up the kingdom and royal treasury (in favour of Rama).

shloka_text: भोजयन्ति किल श्राद्धे केचित्स्वानेव बान्धवान्। ततः पश्चात्समीक्षन्ते कृतकार्या द्विजर्षभान्।।2.61.12।।
transliteration: bhojayanti kila śrāddhe kecitsvāneva bāndhavān| tataḥ paścātsamīkṣante kṛtakāryā dvijarṣabhān
translation: केचित् some people, श्राद्धे in the shraddha ceremony, स्वान् own, बान्धवानेव relatives only, भोजयन्ति किल feed them, कृतकार्याः having completed this ceremony, ततः पश्चात्  thereafter, द्विजर्षभान् bulls (best) among brahmins, समीक्षन्ते will look for.
explanation: Some first feed their own relatives in shraddha ceremony and thereafter look for the best of brahmins to feed.

shloka_text: तत्र ये गुणवन्तश्च विद्वांसश्च द्विजातयः। न पश्चात्तेऽभिमन्यन्ते सुधामपि सुरोपमाः।।2.61.13।।
transliteration: tatra ye guṇavantaśca vidvāṃsaśca dvijātayaḥ| na paścātte'bhimanyante sudhāmapi suropamāḥ
translation: तत्र there, ये those, गुणवन्तश्च virtuous, विद्वांसश्च learned, सुरोपमाः similar to devatas, द्विजातयः ते those brahmins, पश्चात् after others, सुधामपि even ambrosia, न अभिमन्यन्ते will not accept.
explanation: The godlike brahmins who are virtuous and learned will not accept the food after others have partaken even if it is ambrosia.

shloka_text: ब्राह्मणेष्वपि तृप्तेषु पश्चाद्भोक्तुं द्विजर्षभाः। नाभ्युपैतुमलं प्राज्ञा श्शृङ्गच्छेदमिवर्षभाः।।2.61.14।।
transliteration: brāhmaṇeṣvapi tṛpteṣu paścādbhoktuṃ dvijarṣabhāḥ| nābhyupaitumalaṃ prājñā śśṛṅgacchedamivarṣabhāḥ
translation: तृप्तेषु contented, ब्राह्मणेष्वपि even if they are brahmins, प्राज्ञाः the wise, द्विजर्षभाः bulls (best) among brahmins, ऋषभाः like bulls, श्रुङ्गच्छेदमिव shorn of their horns, पश्चात् afterwards, भोक्तुम्  to partake, अभ्युपैतुम् to accept, नालम् should not.
explanation: The bulls (best) among the wise brahmins would not like to accept the food after it is tasted by other brahmins, just as bulls dislike their horns being shorn.

shloka_text: एवं कनीयसा भ्रात्रा भुक्तं राज्यं विशाम्पते। भ्राता ज्येष्ठो वरिष्ठश्च किमर्थं नावमंस्यते।।2.61.15।।
transliteration: evaṃ kanīyasā bhrātrā bhuktaṃ rājyaṃ viśāmpate| bhrātā jyeṣṭho variṣṭhaśca kimarthaṃ nāvamaṃsyate
translation: विशाम्पते O Lord of the world (Dasaratha), एवम् likewise, ज्येष्ठः eldest, वरिष्ठश्च most distinguished one, भ्राता brother, कनीयसा by the younger, भ्रात्रा brother, भुक्तम् enjoyed, राज्यम् kingdom, किमर्थम् why, नावमंस्यते will not disdain.
explanation: O Lord of the world why not the eldest and the most distinguished among the brothers likewise disdain the kingdom enjoyed by the younger brother?

shloka_text: न परेणाऽहृतं भक्ष्यं व्याघ्रः खादितुमिच्छति। एवमेतन्नरव्याघ्रः परलीढं न मन्यते।।2.61.16।।
transliteration: na pareṇā'hṛtaṃ bhakṣyaṃ vyāghraḥ khāditumicchati| evametannaravyāghraḥ paralīḍhaṃ na manyate
translation: व्याघ्रः tiger, परेण by some other animal, आहृतम् procured, भक्ष्यम् food, खादितुम् to eat,        न  इच्छति does not like, एवं in the same way, नरव्याघ्रः the (best) among men (Rama), एतत् परलीढम् enjoyed by others, न मन्यते will not accept.
explanation: Just as a tiger will not eat the food acquired by another beast, Rama, the tiger (best) among men will not accept the kingdom enjoyed by others.

shloka_text: हविराज्यं पुरोडाशाः कुशा यूपाश्च खादिराः। नैतानि यातयामानि कुर्वन्ति पुनरध्वरे।।2.61.17।।
transliteration: havirājyaṃ puroḍāśāḥ kuśā yūpāśca khādirāḥ| naitāni yātayāmāni kurvanti punaradhvare
translation: हविः offering to the Firegod, आज्यम् ghee, पुरोडाशाः sacrificial cakes, कुशाः kusha grass, खादिराः khadira wood, यूपाश्च sacrificial posts, यातयामानि after the lapse of one Yama (three hours), एतानि all these, अध्वरे in the sacrifice, पुनः again, न कुर्वन्ति will not be used.
explanation: Havis, sacrificial offerings like ghee, cakes, kusha grass, and sacrificial posts made from khadira wood, once used in the sacrifice cannot be used again.

shloka_text: तथा ह्यात्तमिदं राज्यं हृतसारां सुरामिव। नाभिमन्तुमलं रामो नष्टसोममिवाध्वरम्।।2.61.18।।
transliteration: tathā hyāttamidaṃ rājyaṃ hṛtasārāṃ surāmiva| nābhimantumalaṃ rāmo naṣṭasomamivādhvaram
translation: तथा in the same way, रामः Rama, आत्तम् enjoyed by others, इदं राज्यम् this kingdom, हृतसाराम् its essence taken away, सुरामिव like liquour, नष्टसोमम् like the run out soma juice, अध्वरमिव like a sacrifice, अभिमन्तुम् to accept, नालम् should not.
explanation: In the same way Rama will not accept this kingdom enjoyed by others like liquour or soma juice drained of its essence.

shloka_text: न चेमां धर्षणां राम सङ्गच्छेदत्यमर्षणः। दारयेन्मन्दरमपि स हि क्रुद्धश्शितैश्शरैः।।2.61.19।।
transliteration: na cemāṃ dharṣaṇāṃ rāma saṅgacchedatyamarṣaṇaḥ| dārayenmandaramapi sa hi kruddhaśśitaiśśaraiḥ
translation: अत्यमर्षण: highly determined, रामः Rama, इमाम् this, धर्षणाम् indignity, न सङ्गच्छेत् will not suffer, क्रुद्ध: if angered, सः he, शितैः with sharp, सरैः with arrows, मन्दरमपि even mount Mandara, दारयेत् हि will split open.
explanation: Rama, highly determined will not suffer this indignity. If enraged, he can split open even mount Mandara with his sharp arrows.

shloka_text: त्वां तु नोत्सहते हन्तुं महात्मा पितृगौरवात्। ससोमार्कग्रहगणं नभस्ताराविचित्रितम्।।2.61.20।। पातयेद्योदिवं क्रुद्धस्सत्वां न व्यतिवर्तते। प्रक्षोभयेद्वारये द्वा महीं शैलशताचिताम्।।2.61.21।।
transliteration: tvāṃ tu notsahate hantuṃ mahātmā pitṛgauravāt| sasomārkagrahagaṇaṃ nabhastārāvicitritam pātayedyodivaṃ kruddhassatvāṃ na vyativartate| prakṣobhayedvāraye dvā mahīṃ śailaśatācitām
translation: तु but, महात्मा great, पितृगौरवात् out of respect for a father, त्वाम् you, हन्तुम् to kill,  नोत्सहते is not showing interest, क्रुद्ध: inflamed, यः who, ससोमार्कग्रहगणम् with Sun, Moon and planets, ताराविचित्रितम् looking wonderful with stars, नभः sky, दिवम् heaven, पातयेत् may pull down, नः he, त्वाम् you, न व्यतिवर्तते is not disobeying,  शैलशत चिताम् surrounded by hundreds of mountains, महीम् earth, प्रक्षोभयेद्वा will shake, दारयेद्वा or may break.
explanation: Out of respect for his father magnanimous Rama is not inclined to kill you. He has not defied the anger, the Sun, the Moon and the sky looking wonderful with stars can be pulled down. He will not even shake or break the earth surrounded by hundreds of mountains.

shloka_text: त्वां तु नोत्सहते हन्तुं महात्मा पितृगौरवात्। ससोमार्कग्रहगणं नभस्ताराविचित्रितम्।।2.61.20।। पातयेद्योदिवं क्रुद्धस्सत्वां न व्यतिवर्तते। प्रक्षोभयेद्वारये द्वा महीं शैलशताचिताम्।।2.61.21।।
transliteration: tvāṃ tu notsahate hantuṃ mahātmā pitṛgauravāt| sasomārkagrahagaṇaṃ nabhastārāvicitritam pātayedyodivaṃ kruddhassatvāṃ na vyativartate| prakṣobhayedvāraye dvā mahīṃ śailaśatācitām
translation: तु but, महात्मा great, पितृगौरवात् out of respect for a father, त्वाम् you, हन्तुम् to kill,  नोत्सहते is not showing interest, क्रुद्ध: inflamed, यः who, ससोमार्कग्रहगणम् with Sun, Moon and planets, ताराविचित्रितम् looking wonderful with stars, नभः sky, दिवम् heaven, पातयेत् may pull down, नः he, त्वाम् you, न व्यतिवर्तते is not disobeying,  शैलशत चिताम् surrounded by hundreds of mountains, महीम् earth, प्रक्षोभयेद्वा will shake, दारयेद्वा or may break.
explanation: Out of respect for his father magnanimous Rama is not inclined to kill you. He has not defied the anger, the Sun, the Moon and the sky looking wonderful with stars can be pulled down. He will not even shake or break the earth surrounded by hundreds of mountains.

shloka_text: नैवं विधमसत्कारं राघवो मर्षयिष्यति। बलवानिव शार्दूलो वालधेरभिमर्शनम्।।2.61.22।।
transliteration: naivaṃ vidhamasatkāraṃ rāghavo marṣayiṣyati| balavāniva śārdūlo vāladherabhimarśanam
translation: बलवान् strong, शार्दूलः tiger, वालधेः of its tail, अभिमर्शनम् इव like twisting, राघवः Rama, एवं विधम् such, असत्कारम् insult, न मर्षयिष्यति will not tolerate.
explanation: A powerful tiger will not allow its tail to be twisted. In the same way Rama also will not tolerate an insult of this sort.

shloka_text: नैतस्य सहिता लोका भयं कुर्युर्महामृथे। अधर्मंत्विह धर्मात्मा लोकं धर्मेण योजयेत्।।2.61.23।।
transliteration: naitasya sahitā lokā bhayaṃ kuryurmahāmṛthe| adharmaṃtviha dharmātmā lokaṃ dharmeṇa yojayet
translation: महामृथे in the great war, लोकाः worlds, सहिताः united, एतस्य for him, भयम् fear, न कुर्युः will not create, धर्मात्मा virtuous, अधर्मम् unrighteous, लोकम् world, धर्मेण with righteousness, योजयेत् will confer.
explanation: Even if all the worlds were to unite and fight against him, he will not fear. This righteous Rama will reestablish justice in this unrighteous world.

shloka_text: नन्वसौ काञ्चनैर्बाणैर्महावीर्यो महाभुजः। युगान्त इव भूतानि सागरानपि निर्दहेत्।।2.61.24।।
transliteration: nanvasau kāñcanairbāṇairmahāvīryo mahābhujaḥ| yugānta iva bhūtāni sāgarānapi nirdahet
translation: महावीर्यः mighty, महाभुजः longarmed, असौ this Rama, काञ्चनैः golden, बाणैः with shafts, युगान्तः इव like at the time of deluge, भूतानि all beings, सागरानपि all the oceans, निर्दहेत् will be consumed in fire.
explanation: Valiant and mightyarmed Rama, with his golden shafts can annihilate all living beings and oceans like at the time of  deluge everything is consumed in fire.

shloka_text: स तादृशस्सिंहबलो वृषभाक्षो नरर्षभः। स्वयमेव हतः पित्रा जलजेनात्मजो यथा।।2.61.25।।
transliteration: sa tādṛśassiṃhabalo vṛṣabhākṣo nararṣabhaḥ| svayameva hataḥ pitrā jalajenātmajo yathā
translation: तादृशः such, सिंहबलः powerful as lion, वृषभाक्षः his eyes resembling a bull's, सः नरर्षभः that one, a bull among men, जलजेन by fish, आत्मजो यथा its own offspring, पित्रैव by his father himself, स्वयम् by himself, हतः killed.
explanation: Such Rama, the best among men, powerful like a lion, with eyes fierce like that of a bull has been destroyed by his own father just as the big fish destroys its own offsprings.

shloka_text: द्विजातिचरितो धर्मश्शास्त्रदृष्टस्सनातनः। यदि ते धर्मनिरते त्वया पुत्रे विवासिते।।2.61.26।।
transliteration: dvijāticarito dharmaśśāstradṛṣṭassanātanaḥ| yadi te dharmanirate tvayā putre vivāsite
translation: धर्मनिरते devoted to righteousness, पुत्रे son, त्वया by you, विवासिते has been banished, ते  to you, शास्त्रदृष्टः seen in the scriptures, सनातनः eternal, द्विजातिचरितः followed by the twiceborn, धर्मः यदि is it righteous act?
explanation: You have banished your son who is devoted to righteousness. Is it in accordance with the scriptures and the eternal tradition followed by the twiceborn?

shloka_text: गतिरेका पतिर्नार्या द्वितीया गतिरात्मजः। तृतीया ज्ञातयो राजंश्चतुर्थी नेह विद्यते।।2.61.27।।
transliteration: gatirekā patirnāryā dvitīyā gatirātmajaḥ| tṛtīyā jñātayo rājaṃścaturthī neha vidyate
translation: राजन् O king, नार्याः for a woman,पतिः husband, एका one, गतिः refuge, आत्मजः son, द्वितीया गतिः second refuge, ज्ञातयः relatives, तृतीया third, चतुर्थी fourth, इह in this world, न विद्यते does not exist.
explanation: O king for a woman the first refuge is the husband, the second her son, the third her relatives and there is no fourth alternative in this world.

shloka_text: एवं तु क्रुद्धया राजा राममात्रा सशोकया। श्रावितः परुषं वाक्यं चिन्तयामास दुःखितः।।2.62.1।।
transliteration: evaṃ tu kruddhayā rājā rāmamātrā saśokayā| śrāvitaḥ paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ cintayāmāsa duḥkhitaḥ
translation: क्रुद्धया in anger, सशोकया afflicted with sorrow, राममात्रा by Rama's mother, एवम् in that way, परुषम् harsh, वाक्यम् words, श्रावितः was forced to hear, राजा king, दुःखितः distressed, चिन्तयामास sadly reflected.
explanation: Forced to hear the harsh words of angry Kausalya, the king, deeply distressed, was absorbed in sad thought.
comments: Sudden flash of a thought in the mind of Dasaratha about an evil act done by him in the past -- Dasaratha attributes present misfortune to the past action -- seeks forgiveness of Kausalya.

shloka_text: चिन्तयित्वा स च नृपो मुमोह व्याकुलेन्द्रियः। अथ दीर्घीण कालेन संज्ञामाप परन्तपः।।2.62.2।।
transliteration: cintayitvā sa ca nṛpo mumoha vyākulendriyaḥ| atha dīrghīṇa kālena saṃjñāmāpa parantapaḥ
translation: सः that, नृपः king, चिन्तयित्वा having thought over, व्याकुलेन्द्रियः with bewildered senses, मुमोह lost consciousness, अथ thereafter, परन्तपः tormentor of enemies, दीर्घेण कालेन  after a long while, संज्ञाम् the senses, आप regained.
explanation: The king (Dasaratha) tormentor of enemies, for a while, lost his consciousness, his senses bewildered. After a long time he regained his senses.

shloka_text: स संज्ञामुपलभ्यैव दीर्घमुष्णं च निश्श्वसन्। कौसल्यां पार्श्वतो दृष्ट्वा पुन श्चिन्तामुपागमत्।।2.62.3।।
transliteration: sa saṃjñāmupalabhyaiva dīrghamuṣṇaṃ ca niśśvasan| kausalyāṃ pārśvato dṛṣṭvā puna ścintāmupāgamat
translation: सः he, संज्ञाम् senses, उपलभ्यैव after getting back, दीर्घम् deep, उष्णं च hot, निश्श्वसन् sighing, पार्श्वतः by the side, कौसल्याम् Kausalya, दृष्ट्वा having seen, पुनः again, चिन्ताम् anxieties, उपागमत् got into.
explanation: When he regained his senses, the king heaved deep, hot sighs. Seeing Kausalya by his side he relapsed into a state of anxiety.

shloka_text: तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य प्रत्याभात्कर्म दुष्कृतम्। यदनेन कृतं पूर्वमज्ञानाच्छब्दवेधिना।।2.62.4।।
transliteration: tasya cintayamānasya pratyābhātkarma duṣkṛtam| yadanena kṛtaṃ pūrvamajñānācchabdavedhinā
translation: चिन्तयमानस्य as he was thinking, तस्य his, पूर्वम् formerly, अनेन by such, शब्दवेधिना Capable of hitting the target by following the sound, अज्ञानात् without knowledge, यत् which, कृतम् has been committed, दुष्कृतम् sinful, कर्म act, प्रत्यभात् flashed back.
explanation: While he was thus reflecting on a sinful act he had inadvertently comitted long ago, the act of discharging an arrow that could hit its target following the sound, flashed in his mind.

shloka_text: अमनास्तेन शोकेन रामशोकेन च प्रभुः। द्वाभ्यामपि महाराज श्शोकाभ्यामन्वतप्यत।।2.62.5।।
transliteration: amanāstena śokena rāmaśokena ca prabhuḥ| dvābhyāmapi mahārāja śśokābhyāmanvatapyata
translation: तेन शोकेन with that grief, रामशोकेन with the grief of Rama's separation, अमनाः with a broken heart, प्रभुः lord, महाराजः maharaja, द्वाभ्याम् by both, शोकाभ्याम् अपि the sorrows also, अन्वतप्यत started regretting.
explanation: The great king, the lord with a broken heart started regretting deeply about both the grievous acts he had committed previously (one is shooting at the son of a sage and the other, banishing Rama).

shloka_text: दह्यामान स्सशोकाभ्यां कौसल्यामाह भूपतिः। वेपमानोऽञ्जलिं कृत्वा प्रसादार्थमवाङ्मुखः।।2.62.6।।
transliteration: dahyāmāna ssaśokābhyāṃ kausalyāmāha bhūpatiḥ| vepamāno'ñjaliṃ kṛtvā prasādārthamavāṅmukhaḥ
translation: शोकाभ्याम् with those two sad incidents, दह्यमानः being afflicted, सः भूपतिः that king (Dasaratha), वेपमानः trembling, आवाङ्मुखः with his head bending downwards, प्रसादार्थम् to appease, अञ्जलिम् with folded palms, कृत्वा having made, कौशल्याम् to Kausalya, आह said.
explanation: Consumed by the double sorrow, the king trembling, with head down and folding his hands said to Kausalya in order to appease her:

shloka_text: प्रसादये त्वां कौसल्ये रचितोऽयं मयाऽञ्जलिः। वत्सला चानृशंसा च त्वं हि नित्यं परेष्वपि।।2.62.7।।
transliteration: prasādaye tvāṃ kausalye racito'yaṃ mayā'ñjaliḥ| vatsalā cānṛśaṃsā ca tvaṃ hi nityaṃ pareṣvapi
translation: कौशल्ये O Kausalya, त्वाम् you, प्रसादये be merciful, मया by me, अयम् this, अञ्जलिः folded  palms, रचितः set, त्वम् you, परेष्वपि even towards enemies, नित्यम् always, वत्सला is affectionate, अनृशंसा च हि not cruel.
explanation: O Kausalya I entreat you with folded palms. Be merciful. Forever affectionate, you are not cruel even towards your enemies.

shloka_text: भर्ता तु खलु नारीणां गुणवान्निर्गुणोऽपि वा। धर्मं विमृशमानानां प्रत्यक्षं देवि दैवतम्।।2.62.8।।
transliteration: bhartā tu khalu nārīṇāṃ guṇavānnirguṇo'pi vā| dharmaṃ vimṛśamānānāṃ pratyakṣaṃ devi daivatam
translation: देवि O Devi, धर्मम् righteousness, विमृशमानानाम् pondering over, नारीणाम् for women, गुणवान् virtuous, निर्गुणोपि वा or not virtuous, भर्ता husband, प्रत्यक्षम् visible, दैवतं खलु indeed god to them.
explanation: O Devi for women who have regard for righteousness, a husband, whether virtuous or not, is a god incarnate.

shloka_text: सा त्वं धर्मपरा नित्यं दृष्टलोक परावरा। नार्हसे विप्रियं वक्तुं दुखिःताऽपि सुदुःखितम्।।2.62.9।।
transliteration: sā tvaṃ dharmaparā nityaṃ dṛṣṭaloka parāvarā| nārhase vipriyaṃ vaktuṃ dukhiḥtā'pi suduḥkhitam
translation: नित्यम् always, धर्मपरा righteousminded one, दृष्टलोकवरावरा knower of both the extremities, सा त्वम् such as you, दुःखितापि although grieved, सुदुःखितम् one who is weighed down with grief, विप्रियम् unpleasant words, वक्तुम् to speak, नार्हसि does not behove you.
explanation: You always adhere to righteousness. You have seen both the extremes (good and bad) of this world. Athough you yourself are in grief it does not behove you to speak unpleasant words to one who is suffering from a greater grief.

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यं करुणं राज्ञः श्रुत्वा दीनस्य भाषितम्। कौसल्या व्यसृजद्बाष्पं प्रणालीव नवोदकम्।।2.62.10।।
transliteration: tadvākyaṃ karuṇaṃ rājñaḥ śrutvā dīnasya bhāṣitam| kausalyā vyasṛjadbāṣpaṃ praṇālīva navodakam
translation: कौशल्या Kausalya, दीनस्य of the wretched, राज्ञः king's, करुणम् pitiable, भाषितम् utterances, तत् वाक्यम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, प्रणाली water conduit, नवोदकमिव like discharging fresh rainwater, बाष्पम् tears, व्यसृजत् shed.
explanation: Kausalya heard the pitiable words uttered by the king who was in a wretched condition. She shed tears like a water channel discharging fresh rainwater.

shloka_text: सा मूर्ध्निबध्वा रुदती राज्ञः पद्ममिवाञ्जलिम्। सम्भ्रमादब्रवीत् त्रस्ता त्वरमाणाक्षरं वचः।।2.62.11।।
transliteration: sā mūrdhnibadhvā rudatī rājñaḥ padmamivāñjalim| sambhramādabravīt trastā tvaramāṇākṣaraṃ vacaḥ
translation: सा that Kausalya, रुदती crying, पद्ममिव like lotus, राज्ञः king's, अञ्जलिम् folded palms,  मूर्ध्नि on her head, बध्वा setting, त्रस्ता frightened, सम्भ्रमात् out of emotion, त्वरमाणाक्षरम्   stumbling syllables, वचः words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Frightened Kausalya, weeping and raising her palms folded like lotus on to her head,  and charged with emotions said with stumbling syllables:

shloka_text: प्रसीद शिरसा याचे भूमौ निपतितास्मि ते। याचितास्मि हता देव क्षन्तव्याऽहं न हि त्वया।।2.62.12।।
transliteration: prasīda śirasā yāce bhūmau nipatitāsmi te| yācitāsmi hatā deva kṣantavyā'haṃ na hi tvayā
translation: देव O lord, प्रसोद be pleased, भूमौ on the earth, निपतिता अस्मि I have fallen down, शिरसा bowing down my head, याचे I beg of you, ते your (by you), याचिता besought, हता अस्मि I have been hit, अहम्  I, त्वया by you, न क्षन्तव्या हि unfit to be pardoned.
explanation: O lord, by falling on the ground at your feet, bowing my head I beg of you to be pleased. By your act of beseeching me, I have been badly hurt. I do deserve to be pardoned.

shloka_text: नैषा हि सा स्त्री भवति श्लाघनीयेन धीमता। उभयोर्लोकयोर्वीर पत्या या सम्साद्यते।।2.62.13।।
transliteration: naiṣā hi sā strī bhavati ślāghanīyena dhīmatā| ubhayorlokayorvīra patyā yā samsādyate
translation: वीर O heroic one, या whoever, श्लाघनीयेन by the praiseworthy, धीमता sagacious one, पत्या by the husband, सम्प्रसाद्यते is appeased, सा एषा such this, स्त्री woman, उभयोः both, लोकयोः worlds, न भवति हि does not belong.
explanation: O heroic one a woman, who is entreated by her sagacious and praiseworthy husband, loses both the worlds.

shloka_text: जानामि धर्मं धर्मज्ञ त्वां जाने सत्यवादिनम्। पुत्रशोकार्तया तत्तु मया किमपि भाषितम्।।2.62.14।।
transliteration: jānāmi dharmaṃ dharmajña tvāṃ jāne satyavādinam| putraśokārtayā tattu mayā kimapi bhāṣitam
translation: धर्मज्ञ O righteous one, धर्मम् righteousness, जानामि I know, त्वाम् you, सत्यवादिनम् truthful, जाने know, तु but, पुत्रशोकार्तया by one afflicted with grief over a son, मया by me, तत् that, किमपि somewhat improper, भाषितम् spoken.
explanation: O righteous one I know the path of dharma. I also know that you are a truthful. Afflicted with grief on account of my son, I spoke somewhat harshly.

shloka_text: शोको नाशयते धैर्यं शोको नाशयते श्रुतम्। शोको नाशयते सर्वं नास्ति शोकसमो रिपुः।।2.62.15।।
transliteration: śoko nāśayate dhairyaṃ śoko nāśayate śrutam| śoko nāśayate sarvaṃ nāsti śokasamo ripuḥ
translation: शोकः grief, धैर्यम् patience, नाशयते destroys, शोकः grief, श्रुतम् knowledge of the scriptures, नाशयते destroys, शोकः grief, सर्वम् everything, नाशयते destroys, शोकसमः equal to grief, रिपुः enemy, नास्ति not there.
explanation: Grief destroys fortitude. Grief destroys knowledge of the scriptures, grief destroys  everything. There is no enemy equal to grief.

shloka_text: शक्य आपतित स्सोढुं प्रहारो रिपुहस्ततः। सोढुंमापतितश्शोकस्सुसूक्ष्मोऽपि न शक्यते।।2.62.16।।
transliteration: śakya āpatita ssoḍhuṃ prahāro ripuhastataḥ| soḍhuṃmāpatitaśśokassusūkṣmo'pi na śakyate
translation: रिपुहस्तः from the enemy's hand, आपतितः suddenly fallen, प्रहारः blow, सोढुम् to endure, शक्यः possible, शोकः grief, सुसूक्ष्मोऽपि however slight, सोढुम् to endure, न शक्यते not possible.
explanation: One can endure an unexpected blow from the enemy's hand but to endure unexpected  grief, however slight it may be, is impossible.

shloka_text: धर्मज्ञा श्श्रुतिमन्तोऽपि छिन्नधर्मार्थसंशयाः। यतयो वीर मुह्यन्ति शोकसम्मूढचेतसः।।2.62.17।।
transliteration: dharmajñā śśrutimanto'pi chinnadharmārthasaṃśayāḥ| yatayo vīra muhyanti śokasammūḍhacetasaḥ
translation: वीर O heroic one, धर्मज्ञाः men wellversed in ethics, श्रुतिमन्तः learned men, छिन्नधर्मार्थसंशयाः  those free from doubts about dharma and artha, यतयः अपि even ascetics,  शोकसम्मूढचेतसः with their senses overwhelmed with grief, मुह्यन्ति are deluded.
explanation: O heroic one even learned ascetics who are well versed in ethics and scriptures and who are free from doubts with regard to dharma and artha, are deluded by grief.

shloka_text: वनवासाय रामस्य पञ्चरात्रोऽद्य गण्यते। य श्शोकहतहर्षायाः पञ्चवर्षोपमो मम।।2.62.18।।
transliteration: vanavāsāya rāmasya pañcarātro'dya gaṇyate| ya śśokahataharṣāyāḥ pañcavarṣopamo mama
translation: वनवासाय for exile in the forest, रामस्य Rama's, पञ्चरात्रः five nights, अद्य today, गण्यते has been counted, यः such a period, शोकहतहर्षायाः whose joy has been destroyed by sorrow, मम to me, पञ्चवर्षोपमः equal to five years.
explanation: This is the fifth night of Rama's exile, but it is like five years to me whose joy has been destroyed by sorrow.

shloka_text: तं हि चिन्तयमानाया श्शोकोऽयं हृदि वर्धते। नदीनामिव वेगेन समुद्रसलिलं महत्।।2.62.19।।
transliteration: taṃ hi cintayamānāyā śśoko'yaṃ hṛdi vardhate| nadīnāmiva vegena samudrasalilaṃ mahat
translation: तम् Rama, चिन्तयमानायाः while thinking of, हृदि in my heart, अयम् this, शोकः sadness, नदीनाम् by river waters, वेगेन by speed, महत् great, समुद्रसलिलमिव like seawaters, वर्धते is increasing.
explanation: As I think of Rama, my heart swells with sorrow just as the ocean rises with rushing rivers.

shloka_text: एवं हि कथयन्त्यास्तु कौसल्यायाश्शुभं वचः। मन्दरश्मिरभूत्सूर्यो रजनी चाभ्यवर्तत।।2.62.20।।
transliteration: evaṃ hi kathayantyāstu kausalyāyāśśubhaṃ vacaḥ| mandaraśmirabhūtsūryo rajanī cābhyavartata
translation: कौशल्यायाः of Kausalya, एवम् in that manner, शुभम् auspicious, वचः words, कथयन्त्याः speaking, सूर्यः the Sun, मन्दरश्मिः आभूत् faded rays, रजनी च night, अभ्यवर्तत had set in.
explanation: While Kausalya was speaking these hearttouching words, the rays of the Sun began to fade and the night fell.

shloka_text: प्रतिबुद्धो मुहूर्तेन शोकोपहतचेतनः। अथ राजा दशरथस्सचिन्तामभ्यपद्यत।।2.63.1।।
transliteration: pratibuddho muhūrtena śokopahatacetanaḥ| atha rājā daśarathassacintāmabhyapadyata
translation: अथ thereafter, सः राजा that king, मूहूर्तेन in a moment, प्रतिबुद्धः was awakened, शोकोपहतचेतनः with his spirit gripped by sorrow, चिन्ताम् worry, अभ्यपद्यत obtained.
explanation: Waking up in a moment tormented with grief, the king began to ponder once again.
comments: Dasaratha recalls the past he had shot an arrow at a hermit boy while he was filling a pot with water, mistaking the sound to be that of an elephant -- Dasaratha realizes the unintentional mistake in killing the boy.

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चैव विवासा द्वासवोपमम्। आविवेशोपसर्गस्तं तम स्सूर्यमिवासुरम्।।2.63.2।।
transliteration: rāmalakṣmaṇayoścaiva vivāsā dvāsavopamam| āviveśopasargastaṃ tama ssūryamivāsuram
translation: रामलक्ष्मणयोः Rama and Lakshmana, विवासात् due to banishment, वासवोपमम् like Indra, तम् him, असुरम् relating to that asura, तमः darkness, सूर्यमिव like the Sun, उपसर्गः great calamity, आविवेश took possesion of.
explanation: Indralike Dasaratha due to banishment of Rama and Lakshmana, was besieged by a great calamity like the Sun enveloped by demonic dark at the time of eclipse.

shloka_text: सभार्ये निर्गते रामे कौसल्यां कोशलेश्वरः। विवक्षुरसितापाङ्गां स्मृत्वा दुष्कृतमात्मनः।।2.63.3।।
transliteration: sabhārye nirgate rāme kausalyāṃ kośaleśvaraḥ| vivakṣurasitāpāṅgāṃ smṛtvā duṣkṛtamātmanaḥ
translation: सभार्ये with his wife, रामे when Rama, निर्गते सति had departed, कोशलेश्वरः king of Kosala (Dasaratha), आत्मनः his own, दुष्कृतम् evil deed, स्मृत्वा remembering, असितापाङ्गाम् with black eye ball, कौशल्याम् to Kausalya, विवक्षुः wished to speak.
explanation: After Rama had left along with his wife the king of Kosala (Dasaratha) recollected his former evil deed and wanted to narrate it to the darkeyed Kausalya.

shloka_text: स राजा रजनीं षष्ठीं रामे प्रव्राजिते वनम्। अर्धरात्रे दशरथ स्संस्मरन् दुष्कृतं कृतम्।।2.63.4।।
transliteration: sa rājā rajanīṃ ṣaṣṭhīṃ rāme pravrājite vanam| ardharātre daśaratha ssaṃsmaran duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam
translation: रामे Rama, वनम् to forest, प्रव्राजिते was banished, राजा king, सः दशरथः Dasaratha, षष्ठीम् sixth, रजनीम् night, अर्धरात्रे in the middle of the night, कृतम् done in the past, दुष्कृतम् evil deeds, संस्मरन् recalled.
explanation: After the banishment of Rama the king spent the sixth night, recalling the evil deed done by him in the past.

shloka_text: स राजा पुत्रशोकार्तः स्मृत्वा दुष्कृतमात्मनः। कौसल्यां पुत्रशोकार्तामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.63.5।।
transliteration: sa rājā putraśokārtaḥ smṛtvā duṣkṛtamātmanaḥ| kausalyāṃ putraśokārtāmidaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: पुत्रशोकार्तः griefstricken because of (separation from) the son, सः राजा the king, आत्मनः his own, दुष्कृतम् misdeed, स्मृत्वा having remembered, पुत्रशोकार्ताम् grieving helplessly due to the separation from his son, कौशल्याम् to Kausalya, इदम् these, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् said
explanation: King Dasaratha distressed by the separation from his son, pondered over his past misdeed, and said to helpless Kausalya, who was equally grieving over the separation from Rama:

shloka_text: यदाचरति कल्याणि शुभं वा यदि वाऽशुभम्। तदेव लभते भद्रे कर्ता कर्मजमात्मनः।।2.63.6।।
transliteration: yadācarati kalyāṇi śubhaṃ vā yadi vā'śubham| tadeva labhate bhadre kartā karmajamātmanaḥ
translation: कल्याणि O auspicious lady, भद्रे o gentle lady, कर्ता the agent of an act, शुभं वा good or, यदि वा or if, अशुभम् evil, यत् whichever, आचरति (कुरुते) performs, आत्मनः his, कर्मजम् result of action, तदेव the same only, लभते will attain.
explanation: O gentle auspicious lady a man has to reap the fruit of his action, good or evil.

shloka_text: गुरुलाघवमर्थानामारम्भे कर्मणां फलम्। दोषं वा यो न जानाति न बाल इति होच्यते।।2.63.7।।
transliteration: gurulāghavamarthānāmārambhe karmaṇāṃ phalam| doṣaṃ vā yo na jānāti na bāla iti hocyate
translation: यः whoever, कर्मणाम् actions, आरम्भे at the beginning, अर्थानाम् the benefits, गुरुलाघवम् relative value, फलम् fruit, दोषं वा or blemish, न जानाति does not know, सः that one, बालः इति as a boy, उच्यते ह is considered.
explanation: He who, at the commencement of any action, does not foresee the good or evil consequences of his action in considered a child.

shloka_text: कश्चिदाम्रवणं छित्त्वा पलाशां श्च निषिञ्चति। पुष्पं दृष्ट्वा फले गृध्नु स्स शोचति फलागमे।।2.63.8।।
transliteration: kaścidāmravaṇaṃ chittvā palāśāṃ śca niṣiñcati| puṣpaṃ dṛṣṭvā phale gṛdhnu ssa śocati phalāgame
translation: कश्चित् some one, पुष्पम् flowers, दृष्ट्वा having seen, फले fruit (of that tree), गृध्नुः greed, आम्रवणम् mango trees, छित्वा having cut, पलाशाम् palasa tree, निषिञ्चति waters, सः he, फलागमे when the fruits are borne, शोचति will repent.
explanation: If some one cuts down mango trees and plants palasa trees and waters them will repent when he sees only flowers while he expects fruit.

shloka_text: अविज्ञाय फलं यो हि कर्म त्वेवानुधावति। स शोचेत्फलवेलायां यथा किंशुकसेचकः।।2.63.9।।
transliteration: avijñāya phalaṃ yo hi karma tvevānudhāvati| sa śocetphalavelāyāṃ yathā kiṃśukasecakaḥ
translation: यः whoever, फलम् fruit, आविज्ञाय not knowing, कर्म तु एव action only, अनुधावति runs after, सः he, किंशुकसेचकः इव like the one who waters kimsuka tree (palasa), फलवेलायाम् at the time of reaping the fruits of action, शोचेत् will regret.
explanation: Without foreseeing the fruits of his action, he who runs after action only will regret at the time of fruition like the one who waters the palasa tree.

shloka_text: सोऽहमाम्रवणं छित्वा पलाशांश्च न्यषेचयम्। रामं फलागमे त्यक्त्वा पश्चाच्छोचामि दुर्मतिः।।2.63.10।।
transliteration: so'hamāmravaṇaṃ chitvā palāśāṃśca nyaṣecayam| rāmaṃ phalāgame tyaktvā paścācchocāmi durmatiḥ
translation: सः अहम् such me, आम्रवणम् mango trees, छित्वा cutting, पलाशान् च palasa trees, न्यषेचयम् have watered, दुर्मतिः unwise, फलागमे at the time of bearing fruit, रामम् Rama, त्यक्त्वा leaving, पश्चात् repenting, शोचामि I am grieving.
explanation: So I have cut the mango trees and watered palasa trees. In utter foolishness, I have banished Rama at the time of fruition and  regretting later.

shloka_text: लब्धशब्देन कौसल्ये कुमारेण धनुष्मता। कुमारश्शब्दवेधीति मया पापमिदं कृतम्।।2.63.11।।
transliteration: labdhaśabdena kausalye kumāreṇa dhanuṣmatā| kumāraśśabdavedhīti mayā pāpamidaṃ kṛtam
translation: कौशल्ये O Kausalya, शब्दवेधी one who can shoot arrows aiming at the target by sound, कुमारः इति in chidhood itself, लब्धशब्देन attaining knowledge of sound, कुमारेण in my youth, धनुष्मता as an archer, मया by me, इदम् this, पापम् sin, कृतम् was done.
explanation: O Kausalya in my youth I was a great archer who could hit the target by its sound. As such I committed this sin.

shloka_text: तदिदं मेऽनुसंम्प्राप्तं देवि दुःखं स्वयं कृतम्। सम्मोहादिह बालेन यथा स्याद्भक्षितं विषम्।।2.63.12।।
transliteration: tadidaṃ me'nusaṃmprāptaṃ devi duḥkhaṃ svayaṃ kṛtam| sammohādiha bālena yathā syādbhakṣitaṃ viṣam
translation: देवि Kausalya, इह in this world, सम्मोहात् out of delusion, बालेन like a boy, भक्षितम् eats, विषम् poison, यथा as, स्यात् may be, स्वयम् one's own self, कृतम् has been done, तत् इदम्  that this, दुःखम् calamity, मे to me, अनुसंप्राप्तम् has befallen.
explanation: Just as a boy consumes poison out of delusion, O Devi, this sorrow has befallen me as a result of my own action.

shloka_text: यथान्यः पुरुषः कश्चित्पलाशैर्मोहितो भवेत्। एवं ममाऽप्यविज्ञातं शब्दवेध्यमयं फलम्।।2.63.13।।
transliteration: yathānyaḥ puruṣaḥ kaścitpalāśairmohito bhavet| evaṃ mamā'pyavijñātaṃ śabdavedhyamayaṃ phalam
translation: अन्यः other, कश्चित् some one, पुरुषः man, पलाशैः by palasa trees, यथा as, मोहितः deluded, भवेत् becomes, एवम् like that, ममापि to me, शब्दवेध्यमयम् the act of shooting the target on hearing the sound, फलम् the consequences, अविज्ञातम् was not premeditated.
explanation: Like some one who is deluded by palasa trees I too did not realise the consequences of shooting the target following the direction of the sound.

shloka_text: देव्यनूढा त्वमभवो युवराजो भवाम्यहम्। ततः प्रावृडनुप्राप्ता मदकामविवर्धिनी।।2.63.14।।
transliteration: devyanūḍhā tvamabhavo yuvarājo bhavāmyaham| tataḥ prāvṛḍanuprāptā madakāmavivardhinī
translation: देवि O Kausalya, त्वम् you, अनूढा not married, अभवः you were, युवराज: भवामि I was prince regent, ततः at that time, मदकामविवर्धिनी inflaming passion and pride, प्रावृट् rainy season, अनुप्राप्ता had set in.
explanation: O Kausalya, you were not married then. I was prince regent. The rainy season that inflames passion and pride had just set in.

shloka_text: उपास्य च रसान्भौमां स्तप्त्वा च जगदंशुभिः। परेताचरितां भीमां रविराविशते दिशम्।।2.63.15।।
transliteration: upāsya ca rasānbhaumāṃ staptvā ca jagadaṃśubhiḥ| paretācaritāṃ bhīmāṃ ravirāviśate diśam
translation: रविः Sun, भौमान् relating to the earth, रसान् juices, उपास्य sucking, जगत् world, अंशुभिः by the rays, तप्त्वा च scorching, परेता चरिताम् ranged by departed souls, भीमाम् fearful, दिशम् quarter, आविशते enter sattained.
explanation: Having sucked the waters of the earth and scorching the world with its rays, the Sun had entered the frightful southern quarter ranged by departed souls.

shloka_text: उष्णमन्तर्दधे सद्य स्स्निग्धा ददृशिरे घनाः। ततो जहृषिरे सर्वे भेकसारङ्गबर्हिणः।।2.63.16।।
transliteration: uṣṇamantardadhe sadya ssnigdhā dadṛśire ghanāḥ| tato jahṛṣire sarve bhekasāraṅgabarhiṇaḥ
translation: सद्यः instantaneously, उष्णम् heat, अन्तर्दधे vanished, स्निग्धा: glistening, घनाः clouds, ददृशिरे were seen, ततः thereafter, सर्वे all, भेकसारङ्गबर्हिणः frogs, geese and peacocks, जहृषिरे rejoiced.
explanation: At that time the heat subsided, glistening clouds appeared. The frogs, geese and peacocks began to rejoice.

shloka_text: क्लिन्न पक्षोत्तरास्स्नाताः कृच्छ्रादिव पतत्रिणः। वृष्टिवातावधूताग्रान्पादपानभिपेदिरे।।2.63.17।।
transliteration: klinna pakṣottarāssnātāḥ kṛcchrādiva patatriṇaḥ| vṛṣṭivātāvadhūtāgrānpādapānabhipedire
translation: क्लिन्न पक्षोत्तराः with the plummage moistened, पतत्रिणः birds, स्नाताः bathed, वृष्टिवातावधूताग्रान् the tops shaken by wind and rain, पादपान् trees, कृच्छ्रात् इव as if with great difficulty, अभिपेदिरे reached.
explanation: The birds with their plummage moistened  as if they had dipped in water reached with great difficulty the tops of the trees which were shaken by the wind and rain.

shloka_text: पतितेनाम्भसाच्छन्नः पतमानेन चासकृत्। आबभौ मत्तसारङ्गस्तोयराशिरिवाचलः।।2.63.18।।
transliteration: patitenāmbhasācchannaḥ patamānena cāsakṛt| ābabhau mattasāraṅgastoyarāśirivācalaḥ
translation: पतितेन dropped, असकृत् ceaselessly, पतमानेन dropping, अम्भसा with rain water, छन्नः covered, मत्तसारङ्गः intoxicated antelopes, अचलः mountain, तोयराशिरिव like a mass of water, अबभौ looked like.
explanation: Engulfed by torrents of rain that continued to fall ceaselessly, the mountain visited by intoxicated antelopes looked like a mass of water.

shloka_text: पाण्डुरारुणवर्णानि स्रोतांसि विमलान्यपि। सुस्रुवुर्गिरिधातुभ्यस्सभस्मानि भुजङ्गवत्।।2.63.19।।
transliteration: pāṇḍurāruṇavarṇāni srotāṃsi vimalānyapi| susruvurgiridhātubhyassabhasmāni bhujaṅgavat
translation: विमलान्यपि as though the waters were pure, स्रोतांसि the rapid flow, गिरिधातुभ्यः of mineral ores, सभस्मानि mixed with ashes, पाण्डुरारुणवर्णानि white and red in colour, भुजङ्गवत् like a serpent, सुस्रुवुः flowed.
explanation: Although pure, the rapidly flowing water from the mountains mixed with the minerals in the soil turned white and red in colour and flowed like a serpent.

shloka_text: आकुलारुण तोयानि स्रोतांसि विमलान्यपि। उन्मार्गजलवाहिनी बभूवुर्जलदागमे।।2.63.20।।
transliteration: ākulāruṇa toyāni srotāṃsi vimalānyapi| unmārgajalavāhinī babhūvurjaladāgame
translation: जलदागमे at the advent of the rainy season, स्रोतांसि streams, विमलान्यपि although pure, आकुलारुण तोयानि mixed up with marshy red soil, उन्मार्गजलवाहिनी by flowing in different directions, बभूवुः became.
explanation: The streams that were pure, mixed with red soil flowed red, deviating from their natural course.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्नतिसुखे काले धनुष्मानिषुमान्रथी। व्यायामकृतसङ्कल्पस्सरयूमन्वगां नदीम्।।2.63.21।।
transliteration: tasminnatisukhe kāle dhanuṣmāniṣumānrathī| vyāyāmakṛtasaṅkalpassarayūmanvagāṃ nadīm
translation: अतिसुखे highly delightful, तस्मिन् काले in that season, व्यायामकृतसङ्कल्पः determined to go hunting, धनुष्मान् holding bow, इषुमान् holding arrows, रथी a charioteer, सरयूनदीम् river Sarayu, अन्वगाम् went.
explanation: In that highly delightful season, wishing to go hunting I, armed with bow and arrows, rode my chariot towards  river Sarayu.

shloka_text: निपाने महिषं रात्रौ गजं वाऽभ्यागतं नदीम्। अन्यं वा श्वापदं कञ्चिज्जिघांसु रजितेन्द्रियः। तस्मिं स्तत्राहमेकान्ते रात्रौ विवृतकार्मुकः।।2.63.22।।
transliteration: nipāne mahiṣaṃ rātrau gajaṃ vā'bhyāgataṃ nadīm| anyaṃ vā śvāpadaṃ kañcijjighāṃsu rajitendriyaḥ| tasmiṃ statrāhamekānte rātrau vivṛtakārmukaḥ
translation: अहम् I, अजितेन्द्रियः without any control over my senses, तस्मिन् there, निपाने in a spot for drinking water, नदीम् river, रात्रौ in the night, अभ्यागतम् having arrived, महिषम् buffalo, गजं वा or elephant, अन्यम् any other, श्वापदं वा any wild animal, जिघांसुः desirous of killing, तत्र there, रात्रौ in the night, एकान्ते in a lonely place, विवृतकार्मुकः with bow strung.
explanation: And there, with no control over my senses, I hid  in a lonely place with my bow in readiness intending to shoot a buffalo or an elephant or any other wild animal that might come to the spot for drinking water in the night.

shloka_text: तत्राहं संवृतं वन्यं हतवांस्तीरमागतम्। अन्यं चापि मृगं हिंस्रं शब्दं श्रुत्वाऽभ्युपागतम्।।2.63.23।।
transliteration: tatrāhaṃ saṃvṛtaṃ vanyaṃ hatavāṃstīramāgatam| anyaṃ cāpi mṛgaṃ hiṃsraṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā'bhyupāgatam
translation: तत्र there, अहम् I, तीरम् आगतम् reached the bank of the river, वन्यम् forest, अभ्युपागतम् arrived, अन्यम् some other, ह्रिंस्रम् cruel, मृगं च also animal, शब्दम् sound, श्रुत्वा having heard, संव़ृतम् secretly, हतवान् killed.
explanation: Hiding and waiting there, following the sounds of animals I killed two animals that had reached the bank of the river.

shloka_text: अथान्धकारे त्वश्रौषं जले कुम्भस्य पूर्यतः। अचक्षुर्विषये घोषं वारणस्येव नर्दतः।।2.63.24।।
transliteration: athāndhakāre tvaśrauṣaṃ jale kumbhasya pūryataḥ| acakṣurviṣaye ghoṣaṃ vāraṇasyeva nardataḥ
translation: अथ thereafter, अन्धकारे in the darkness, अचक्षुर्विषये not within the range of sight, नर्दतः making sounds, वारणस्येव like the sound of an elephant, जले in water, पूर्यतः being filled, कुम्भस्य a pitcher, घोषम् sound, अश्रौषम् heard.
explanation: Then at a place that was out of the range of my sight in darkness I heard the sound of a pitcher being filled with water which resembled the sound of an elephant.

shloka_text: ततोऽहं शरमुधृत्य दीप्तमाशीविषोपमम्। शब्दं प्रति गजप्रेप्सुरभिलक्ष्य त्वपातयम्।।2.63.25।।
transliteration: tato'haṃ śaramudhṛtya dīptamāśīviṣopamam| śabdaṃ prati gajaprepsurabhilakṣya tvapātayam
translation: ततः then, अहम् I, गजप्रेप्सुः wishing to get the elephant, दीप्तम् bright, आशीविषोपमम् like a venomous serpent, शरम् shaft, उधृत्य शब्दं प्रति in the direction of the sound, अभिलक्ष्य aiming at, अपातयम् released.
explanation: Wishing to kill the elephant, I seized my arrow glowing like a venomous snake and aimed it towards the sound.

shloka_text: अमुञ्चं निशितं बाणमहमाशीविषोपमम्। तत्र वागुषसि व्यक्ता प्रादुरासीद्वनौकसः।।2.63.26।। हाहेति पततस्तोये बाणाभिहतमर्मणः।।2.63.27।।
transliteration: amuñcaṃ niśitaṃ bāṇamahamāśīviṣopamam| tatra vāguṣasi vyaktā prādurāsīdvanaukasaḥ hāheti patatastoye bāṇābhihatamarmaṇaḥ
translation: अहम् I, आशीविषोपमम् like a venomous serpent, निशितम् sharp, बाणम् shaft, अमुञ्चम् dischrged, तत्र there, उषसि in the morning twilight, बाणाभिहतमर्मणः with the vital organ hit by the shaft, तोये in water, पततः falling, वनौकसः forestdweller, हा हा इति saying 'Alas', व्यक्ता screaming aloud, वाक् words, प्रादुरासीत् arose.
explanation: Then I discharged a sharp shaft like a venomous serpent. In the morning twilight I saw that the shaft had hit the vital part of the body of a forest dweller and his cry of 'Alas', was clearly heard as he fell in the water.

shloka_text: अमुञ्चं निशितं बाणमहमाशीविषोपमम्। तत्र वागुषसि व्यक्ता प्रादुरासीद्वनौकसः।।2.63.26।। हाहेति पततस्तोये बाणाभिहतमर्मणः।।2.63.27।।
transliteration: amuñcaṃ niśitaṃ bāṇamahamāśīviṣopamam| tatra vāguṣasi vyaktā prādurāsīdvanaukasaḥ hāheti patatastoye bāṇābhihatamarmaṇaḥ
translation: अहम् I, आशीविषोपमम् like a venomous serpent, निशितम् sharp, बाणम् shaft, अमुञ्चम् dischrged, तत्र there, उषसि in the morning twilight, बाणाभिहतमर्मणः with the vital organ hit by the shaft, तोये in water, पततः falling, वनौकसः forestdweller, हा हा इति saying 'Alas', व्यक्ता screaming aloud, वाक् words, प्रादुरासीत् arose.
explanation: Then I discharged a sharp shaft like a venomous serpent. In the morning twilight I saw that the shaft had hit the vital part of the body of a forest dweller and his cry of 'Alas', was clearly heard as he fell in the water.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्निपतिते बाणे वागभूत्तत्र मानुषी। कथमस्मद्विधे शस्त्रं निपतेत्तु तपस्विनि।।2.63.28।।
transliteration: tasminnipatite bāṇe vāgabhūttatra mānuṣī| kathamasmadvidhe śastraṃ nipatettu tapasvini
translation: तस्मिन् when that, बाणे arrow, निपतिते fell, तत्र there, मानुषी man's, वाक् voice, अभूत् came, अस्मद्विधे with people like me, तपस्विनि at a sage, शस्त्रम् arrow, कथम् how, निपतेत्तु can be discharged?
explanation: When the arrow hit him, a man's voice was heard saying, 'How can an arrow be discharged at a person like me who is an ascetic?'

shloka_text: प्रविविक्तां नदीं रात्रावुदाहाऽरोहमागतः। इषुणाऽभिहतः केन कस्य वा किं कृतं मया।।2.63.29।।
transliteration: praviviktāṃ nadīṃ rātrāvudāhā'rohamāgataḥ| iṣuṇā'bhihataḥ kena kasya vā kiṃ kṛtaṃ mayā
translation: अहम् I, उदाहारः in order to take water, रात्रौ at night, प्रविविक्ताम् lonely, नदीम् river, आगतः have come, इषुणा by an arrow, केन by whom, अभिहतः hit, मया by me, कस्य to any, किम् what offence, कृतम् done.
explanation: 'I have come to this lonely spot of the river to take water. Who has hit me with this arrow? What (harm) have I done to any one?'

shloka_text: ऋषेर्हिन्यस्तदण्डस्य वने वन्येन जीवतः। कथं नु शस्रेण वधो मद्विधस्य विधीयते।।2.63.30।।
transliteration: ṛṣerhinyastadaṇḍasya vane vanyena jīvataḥ| kathaṃ nu śasreṇa vadho madvidhasya vidhīyate
translation: न्यस्तदण्डस्य renouncing violence, वने in  the forest, वन्येन forest produce जीवतःsubsisting, मद्विधस्य men like me, ऋषेः for an ascetic, शस्त्रेण with weapon, वधः killing, कथं नु in what way?, विधीयते is perpetrated.
explanation: 'Renouncing violence I live the life of an ascetic on forest produce. Why should any one kill me with a weapon?

shloka_text: जटाभारधरस्यैव वल्कलाजिनवाससः। को वधेन ममर्थी स्यात्किंवाऽस्यापकृतं मया।।2.63.31।।
transliteration: jaṭābhāradharasyaiva valkalājinavāsasaḥ| ko vadhena mamarthī syātkiṃvā'syāpakṛtaṃ mayā
translation: जटाभारधरस्यैव with matted hair, वल्कलाजिनवाससः wearing bark and skin of an antelope, मम my, वधेन by killing, अर्थी interested, कः who?, स्यात् मया could be?, अस्य to him, किं वा what, अपकृतम् harm?
explanation: 'Who wants to kill me who lives like an ascetic with matted hair and wearing bark or the skin of an antelope? What harm have I done to him?

shloka_text: एवं निष्फलमारब्धं केवलानर्थसंहितम्। न कश्चित्साधु मन्येत यथैव गुरुतल्पगम्।।2.63.32।।
transliteration: evaṃ niṣphalamārabdhaṃ kevalānarthasaṃhitam| na kaścitsādhu manyeta yathaiva gurutalpagam
translation: एवम् in this way, केवलानर्थसंहितम् only for mischief, निष्फलम् fruitless, आरब्धम् effort, कश्चित् some one, गुरुतल्पगं यथैव like one who occupies the teacher's bed, साधु मन्येत will consider this proper.
explanation: 'Whoever it is, he has committed only a mischievous and senseless act. This sin like a disciple sleeping on the bed of his preceptor none will approve of.

shloka_text: नाहं तथाऽनु शोचामि जीवितक्षयमात्मनः। मातरं पितरं चोभावनुशोचामि मद्वधे।।2.63.33।।
transliteration: nāhaṃ tathā'nu śocāmi jīvitakṣayamātmanaḥ| mātaraṃ pitaraṃ cobhāvanuśocāmi madvadhe
translation: अहम् I, आत्मनः my own, जीवितक्षयम् loss of life, तथा not so much, नानुशोचामि do not regret, मद्वधे after my killing, मातरम् mother, पितरं च and father, उभौ both, अनुशोचामि I am grieving.
explanation: 'I do not regret so much about the loss of my own life as  about my mother and father after I am dead.

shloka_text: तदेतन्मिथुनं वृद्धं चिरकालभृतं मया। मयि पञ्चत्वमापन्ने कां वृत्तिं वर्तयिष्यति।।2.63.34।।
transliteration: tadetanmithunaṃ vṛddhaṃ cirakālabhṛtaṃ mayā| mayi pañcatvamāpanne kāṃ vṛttiṃ vartayiṣyati
translation: मयि when I, पञ्चत्वम् with five elements, आपन्ने reduced to, मया by me, चिरकालभृतम् supported for a long time, वृद्धम् in old age, एतत् this, मिथुनम् couple, काम् what, वृत्तिम् life, वर्तयिष्यति will live in future.
explanation: 'So long I have been supporting this aged couple. After I am dead, how will they live?

shloka_text: वृद्धै च मतापितरावहं चैकेषुणा हता। केन स्मनिहता स्सर्वे सुबालेनाकृतात्मना।।2.63.35।।
transliteration: vṛddhai ca matāpitarāvahaṃ caikeṣuṇā hatā| kena smanihatā ssarve subālenākṛtātmanā
translation: वृद्धौ aged, मातापितरौ my parents, अहं च me also, एकेषुणा with one single arrow, हताः killed, अकृतात्मना one with malicious intention, सुबालेन by a good boy, केन by whom, सर्वे निहताः स्म all of us are killed.
explanation: 'My aged parents along with me are killed by a single arrow. Who is that malicious knave  who has slain us?

shloka_text: तां गिरं करुणां श्रुत्वा मम धर्मानुकाङ्क्षिणः। कराभ्यां सशरं चापं व्यथितस्यापतद्भुवि।।2.63.36।।
transliteration: tāṃ giraṃ karuṇāṃ śrutvā mama dharmānukāṅkṣiṇaḥ| karābhyāṃ saśaraṃ cāpaṃ vyathitasyāpatadbhuvi
translation: करुणाम् piteous, तां गिरम् words, श्रुत्वा on hearing, धर्मानुकाङ्क्षिणं keen on following the righteous path (fearing that an unrighteous act has been performed), व्यथितस्य worrying, मम my, कराभ्याम् from my hands, सशरम् along with the arrow, चापम् bow भुवि on the land, अपतत् fell down.
explanation: On hearing the piteous voice the bow and arrow dropped from my (trembling) hands since I was keen on following the righteous path.

shloka_text: तस्याहं करुणं श्रुत्वा निशि लालवतो बहु। सम्भ्रान्त श्शोकवेगेन भृशमासं विचेतनः।।2.63.37।।
transliteration: tasyāhaṃ karuṇaṃ śrutvā niśi lālavato bahu| sambhrānta śśokavegena bhṛśamāsaṃ vicetanaḥ
translation: अहम् I, निशि at night, बहु highly, लालवतः lamenting, तस्य his, करुणम् pathetic words, श्रुत्वा having heard, शोकवेगेन through excess of grief, सम्भ्रान्तः frightened, भृशम् extremely, विचेतनः unable to think, आसम् I remained.
explanation: Having heard his pathetic lamentations at night, I was extremely frightened by the force of grief and stood bewildered.

shloka_text: तं देशमहमागम्य दीनसत्त्वस्सुदुर्मनाः। अपश्यमिषुणा तीरे सरय्वास्तापसं हतम्।।2.63.38।। अवकीर्ण जटाभारं प्रविद्धकलशोदकम्। पांसुशोणितदिग्धाङ्गं शयानं शल्यपीडितम्।।2.63.39।।
transliteration: taṃ deśamahamāgamya dīnasattvassudurmanāḥ| apaśyamiṣuṇā tīre sarayvāstāpasaṃ hatam avakīrṇa jaṭābhāraṃ praviddhakalaśodakam| pāṃsuśoṇitadigdhāṅgaṃ śayānaṃ śalyapīḍitam
translation: अहम् I, दीनसत्त्वः in a dissipated state, सुदुर्मनाः with troubled mind, तं देशम् that place, आगम्य having reached, सरय्वाः Sarayu, तीरे on the bank, इषुणा by the arrow, हतम् struck, अवकीर्णजटाभारम् with scattered locks of hair, प्रविद्धकलशोदकम् with water pitcher thrown away, पांसुशोणितदिग्धाङ्गम् body smeared with blood and dust, शयानम् lying, शल्यपीडितम् pierced by the arrow, तापसम् the sage, अपश्यम् I saw.
explanation: With dissipated energy and intensely troubled mind, I reached the bank of river Sarayu and there I saw the ascetic lying struck by the arrow and with scattered locks of hair. The water pitcher was thrown away and his body smeared with blood and dust as he lay on the ground.

shloka_text: तं देशमहमागम्य दीनसत्त्वस्सुदुर्मनाः। अपश्यमिषुणा तीरे सरय्वास्तापसं हतम्।।2.63.38।। अवकीर्ण जटाभारं प्रविद्धकलशोदकम्। पांसुशोणितदिग्धाङ्गं शयानं शल्यपीडितम्।।2.63.39।।
transliteration: taṃ deśamahamāgamya dīnasattvassudurmanāḥ| apaśyamiṣuṇā tīre sarayvāstāpasaṃ hatam avakīrṇa jaṭābhāraṃ praviddhakalaśodakam| pāṃsuśoṇitadigdhāṅgaṃ śayānaṃ śalyapīḍitam
translation: अहम् I, दीनसत्त्वः in a dissipated state, सुदुर्मनाः with troubled mind, तं देशम् that place, आगम्य having reached, सरय्वाः Sarayu, तीरे on the bank, इषुणा by the arrow, हतम् struck, अवकीर्णजटाभारम् with scattered locks of hair, प्रविद्धकलशोदकम् with water pitcher thrown away, पांसुशोणितदिग्धाङ्गम् body smeared with blood and dust, शयानम् lying, शल्यपीडितम् pierced by the arrow, तापसम् the sage, अपश्यम् I saw.
explanation: With dissipated energy and intensely troubled mind, I reached the bank of river Sarayu and there I saw the ascetic lying struck by the arrow and with scattered locks of hair. The water pitcher was thrown away and his body smeared with blood and dust as he lay on the ground.

shloka_text: स मामुद्वीक्ष्य नेत्राभ्यां त्रस्तमस्वस्थचेतसम्। इत्युवाच ततः क्रूरं दिधक्षन्निव तेजसा।।2.63.40।।
transliteration: sa māmudvīkṣya netrābhyāṃ trastamasvasthacetasam| ityuvāca tataḥ krūraṃ didhakṣanniva tejasā
translation: सः he, त्रस्तम् frightened, अस्वस्थचेतसम् shaken up mentally, माम् me, तेजसा with his energy, दिधक्षन्निव as if burning, नेत्राभ्याम् with both eyes, उवदीक्ष्य looked up, ततः then, क्रूरम् cruel, इति thus, उवाच said.
explanation: I was mentally stricken and frightened. He looked up as if buring me with the energy of his eyes. Then he uttered the words 'A cruel act'

shloka_text: किं तवापकृतं राजन्वने निवसता मया। जिहीर्षुरम्भो गुर्वुर्थं यदहं ताडितस्त्वया।।2.63.41।।
transliteration: kiṃ tavāpakṛtaṃ rājanvane nivasatā mayā| jihīrṣurambho gurvurthaṃ yadahaṃ tāḍitastvayā
translation: राजन् O king, गुर्वर्थम् for the sake of my parents, अम्भ: water, जिहीर्षुः wishing to take, अहम् I, त्वया you, ताडितः have been struck, वने in the forest, निवसता residing, मया by me, तव your, किम् what, अपकृतम् harm.
explanation: 'O king you have struck me when I was trying to carry water to my parents. I am a forestdweller. What harm have I done to you?

shloka_text: एकेन खलु बाणेन मर्मण्यभिहते मयि। द्वावन्धौ निहतौ वृद्धौ माता जनयिता च मे।।2.63.42।।
transliteration: ekena khalu bāṇena marmaṇyabhihate mayi| dvāvandhau nihatau vṛddhau mātā janayitā ca me
translation: एकेन by one, बाणेन arrow, मयि at me, मर्मणि vital part, अभिहते when struck, मे my, माता mother, जनयिता च father, अन्धौ blind, द्वौ both, वृद्धौ old ones, निहतौ खलु are killed indeed.
explanation: 'By striking at the vital part of my body with one arrow, you have killed both my aged and blind mother and father too.

shloka_text: तौ कथं दुर्बलावन्धौ मत्प्रतीक्षौ पिपासितौ। चिरमाशाकृतां तृष्णां कष्टां सन्धारयिष्यतः।।2.63.43।।
transliteration: tau kathaṃ durbalāvandhau matpratīkṣau pipāsitau| ciramāśākṛtāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ kaṣṭāṃ sandhārayiṣyataḥ
translation: दुर्बलौ weak ones, अन्धौ blind, पिपासितौ thirsty, तौ both of them, कष्टाम् difficult, आशाकृताम् due to expectation, तृष्णाम् thirst, चिरम् for a long time, कथम् how, सन्धारयिष्यतः will control.
explanation: 'How will the two who are frail, thirsty and blind wait for me for long controlling their thirst with great difficulty with the expectation (that I would fetch them water)?

shloka_text: न नूनं तपसो वास्ति फलयोगश्श्रुतस्य वा। पिता यन्मां न जानाति शयानं पतितं भुवि।।2.63.44।।
transliteration: na nūnaṃ tapaso vāsti phalayogaśśrutasya vā| pitā yanmāṃ na jānāti śayānaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi
translation: नूनम् surely, तपसो वा either for asceticism, श्रुतस्य वा or for scriptural knowledge, फलयोगः attainment of fruit, नास्ति not there, यत् since, पिता my father, भुवि on this earth, पतितम् fallen, शयानम् lying, माम् me, न जानाति not know.
explanation: 'My father does not know that I am lying on the ground. It is true that there is no reward either for asceticism or for scriptural knowledge.

shloka_text: जानन्नपि च किं कुर्यादशक्तिरपरिक्रमः। भिद्यमानमिवाशक्त स्त्रतुमन्यो नगो नगम्।।2.63.45।।
transliteration: jānannapi ca kiṃ kuryādaśaktiraparikramaḥ| bhidyamānamivāśakta stratumanyo nago nagam
translation: अशक्ति: without energy, अपरिक्रमः who cannot walk, भिद्यमानम् being severed, नगम् tree, त्रातुम् to protect, अशक्तः is incapable, अन्यः other, नगः tree, इव like, जानन्नपि knowing also, किम् what, कुर्यात् can it do?
explanation: 'What can my weak father who has no strength to walk do, even if he knows about it? Like a tree which cannot protect another which is being severed, he is helpless.

shloka_text: पितुस्त्वमेव मे गत्वा शीघ्रमाचक्ष्य राघव। न त्वामनुदहेत्क्रुद्धो वनं वह्निरिवैधितः।।2.63.46।।
transliteration: pitustvameva me gatvā śīghramācakṣya rāghava| na tvāmanudahetkruddho vanaṃ vahnirivaidhitaḥ
translation: राघव O scion of the Raghus (Dasaratha), त्वमेव you yourself, शीघ्रम् quickly, गत्वा having gone, मे पितुः to my father, आचक्ष्व inform, क्रुद्ध in wrath, एधितः ignited, वह्निः fire, वनमिव like a forest, त्वाम् you, नानुदहेत् will not be burnt.
explanation: O scion of the Raghus (Dasaratha) Go at once and inform my father, lest in anger he should burn you like ignited fire consuming the forest.

shloka_text: इयमेकपदी राजन्यतो मे पितुराश्रमः। तं प्रसादय गत्वा त्वं न त्वां स कुपितश्शपेत्।।2.63.47।।
transliteration: iyamekapadī rājanyato me piturāśramaḥ| taṃ prasādaya gatvā tvaṃ na tvāṃ sa kupitaśśapet
translation: राजन् O king, यतः from whichever side, मे पितुः my father's, आश्रमः hermitage, इयम् this, एकपदी footpath, त्वम् you, गत्वा having  gone, तम् him, प्रसादय beg his forgiveness, सः he, कुपितः in wrath, त्वाम् you, न शपेत् may not curse.
explanation: 'O king, this footpath leads to my father's hermitage. Go and beg his forgiveness so that he may not curse you out of anger.

shloka_text: विशल्यं कुरु मां राजन्मर्म मे निशितश्शरः। रुणद्धि मृदुसोत्सेधं तीरमम्बुरयो यथा।।2.63.48।।
transliteration: viśalyaṃ kuru māṃ rājanmarma me niśitaśśaraḥ| ruṇaddhi mṛdusotsedhaṃ tīramamburayo yathā
translation: राजन् O king, माम् me, विशल्यम् with weapon taken out, कुरु make, निशितः sharp, शरः arrow, मे मर्म my vital part of the body, मृदु gently, सोत्सेधम् elevated, तीरम् bank, अम्बुरयः like the flow of water, यथा in the same manner, रुणद्धि is preventing.
explanation: 'Gently remove the arrow from my body, O king the sharp arrow is piercing deep into my vital just like the current of the river hits its elevated bank'.

shloka_text: सशल्यः क्लिश्यते प्राणैर्विशल्यो विनशिष्यति। इति मामविशच्चिन्ता तस्य शल्यापकर्षणे।।2.63.49।।
transliteration: saśalyaḥ kliśyate prāṇairviśalyo vinaśiṣyati| iti māmaviśaccintā tasya śalyāpakarṣaṇe
translation: सशल्यः one with a weapon piercing the body, प्राणैः life, क्लिश्यते is pained, विशल्यः if the arrow is removed, विनशिष्यति he will die, इति चिन्ता with this thought, तस्य his, शपकर्षणे in removing the arrow, माम् me, अविशत् has entered.
explanation: The thought of removing the arrow kept me pondering. If not removed, it will be painful, and if removed, he will die.

shloka_text: दुःखितस्य च दीनस्य मम शोकातुरस्य च। लक्षयामास हृदये चिन्तां मुनिसुतस्तदा।।2.63.50।।
transliteration: duḥkhitasya ca dīnasya mama śokāturasya ca| lakṣayāmāsa hṛdaye cintāṃ munisutastadā
translation: तदा then, मुनिसुतः son of the ascetic, दुःखितस्य of a distressed man, दीनस्य wretched, शोकातुरस्य च full of grief, मम my, हृदये in the heart, चिन्ताम् anguish, लक्षयामास perceived.
explanation: The son of the ascetic noticed my anguish and seeing me thus distressed, wretched and afflicted with sorrow, said:

shloka_text: ताम्यमानस्स मां कृच्छ्रादुवाच परमार्तवत्। सीदमानो विवृत्ताङ्गो वेष्टमानो गतः क्षयम्।।2.63.51।।
transliteration: tāmyamānassa māṃ kṛcchrāduvāca paramārtavat| sīdamāno vivṛttāṅgo veṣṭamāno gataḥ kṣayam
translation: ताम्यमानः tormented, सीदमानः plunging into death, विवृत्ताङ्गः with twisted limbs, वेष्टमानः writhing, क्षयम् destruction, गतः having reached, सः he, परमार्तवत् intensely grieved, कृच्छ्रात् with difficulty, माम् me, उवाच said.
explanation: Suffering from excruciating pain, sinking with his limbs twisting and writhing and plunging into death and destruction, with intense agony he uttered the following words with great difficulty:

shloka_text: संस्तभ्य शोकं धैर्येण स्थिरचित्तो भवाम्यहम्। ब्रह्महत्याकृतं पापं हृदयादपनीयताम्।।2.63.52।।
transliteration: saṃstabhya śokaṃ dhairyeṇa sthiracitto bhavāmyaham| brahmahatyākṛtaṃ pāpaṃ hṛdayādapanīyatām
translation: अहम् I, धैर्येण patiently, शोकम् sorrow, संस्तभ्य restraining, स्थिरचित्तः with a firm mind, भवामि I am, ब्रह्महत्याकृतम् killed a brahmin, पापम् sin, हृदयात् from your mind, अपनीयताम् may be removed.
explanation: 'I am now calm. I bear my pain with patience. Remove the fear from your mind that you have committed a sin by slaying a brahmin.

shloka_text: न द्विजातिरहं राजन्मा भूत्ते मनसो व्यथा। शूद्रायामस्मि वैश्येन जातो जनपदाधिप।।2.63.53।।
transliteration: na dvijātirahaṃ rājanmā bhūtte manaso vyathā| śūdrāyāmasmi vaiśyena jāto janapadādhipa
translation: जनपदाधिप O Lord of the land (Dasaratha), राजन् king, न not, अहम् I am, द्विजातिः a brahmin, न not, ते your, मनसः to mind, व्यथा fear, माभूत् may not happen, वैश्येन by a vaisya, शूद्रायाम् to a sudra woman, जातः born, अस्मि I am.
explanation: 'O king Dasaratha, lord of the land, I am not a brahmin. Feel no sense of guilt in your mind. I was born of a sudra mother and a vaisya father.

shloka_text: वधमप्रतिरूपं तु महर्षेस्तस्य राघवः। विलपन्नेव धर्मात्मा कौसल्यां पुनरब्रवीत्।।2.64.1।।
transliteration: vadhamapratirūpaṃ tu maharṣestasya rāghavaḥ| vilapanneva dharmātmā kausalyāṃ punarabravīt
translation: धर्मात्मा the righteous one, राघवः descendant of the Raghu's (Dasaratha), तस्य महर्षेः that maharsi's, अप्रतिरूपम् unique, वधम् killing, विलपन्नेव while lamenting, पुनः again, कौशल्याम् to Kausalya, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Grieving for having unfairly killed the great sage the rightenous descendant of the Raghus (Dasaratha) coutinued to tell Kausalya about it:
comments: Dasaratha relates to Kausalya  the event of the noble ascetic's curse on him -- death of Dasaratha

shloka_text: तदज्ञानान्महत्पापं कृत्वाहं सङ्कुलेन्द्रियः। एकस्त्वचिन्तयं बुध्या कथं नु सुकृतं भवेत्।।2.64.2।।
transliteration: tadajñānānmahatpāpaṃ kṛtvāhaṃ saṅkulendriyaḥ| ekastvacintayaṃ budhyā kathaṃ nu sukṛtaṃ bhavet
translation: अहम् I, अज्ञानात् in ignorance, तत् that, महत् great, पापम् sin, कृत्वा having done, सङ्कुलेन्द्रियः with agitated senses, एकस्तु myself alone, कथं नु how, सुकृतम् well done, भवेत् shall be, बुध्या in my mind, अचिन्तयम् reflected.
explanation: Having committed the sin unwittingly, I was greatly agitated. I reflected in my mind as to how to atone for this great sin.

shloka_text: ततस्तं घटमादाय पूर्णं परमवारिणा। आश्रमं तमहं प्राप्य यथाऽख्यातपथं गतः।।2.64.3।।
transliteration: tatastaṃ ghaṭamādāya pūrṇaṃ paramavāriṇā| āśramaṃ tamahaṃ prāpya yathā'khyātapathaṃ gataḥ
translation: ततः then, परमवारिणा with clean water, पूर्णम् filled, तम् that, घटम् pot आदाय taking hold of, यथाऽख्यातपथम् the path as directed, प्राप्य having reached, अहम् I, अश्रमम् hermitage, गतः entered.
explanation: Holding the pot filled with clean water I reached the hermitage following the path as directed.

shloka_text: तत्राहं दुर्बलावन्धौ वृद्धावपरिणायकौ। अपश्यं तस्य पितरौ लूनपक्षाविव द्विजौ।।2.64.4।। तन्निमित्ताभिरासीनौ कथाभिरपरिश्रमौ। तामाशां मत्कृते हीनावुदासीनावनाथवत्।।2.64.5।।
transliteration: tatrāhaṃ durbalāvandhau vṛddhāvapariṇāyakau| apaśyaṃ tasya pitarau lūnapakṣāviva dvijau tannimittābhirāsīnau kathābhirapariśramau| tāmāśāṃ matkṛte hīnāvudāsīnāvanāthavat
translation: तत्र there, अहम् I, दुर्बलौ frail, अन्धौ blind, वृद्धौ old, अपरिणायकौ without any supporter, लूनपक्षौ with wings severed, द्विजौ इव like birds, तन्निमित्ताभिः on account of their son, कथाभिः with stories, आसीनौ seated, अपरिश्रमौ without any work, मत्कृते  done by me, ताम् आशाम् their hope, हीनौ deprived of, अनाथवत् like orphans, उदासीनौ passive, तस्य his, पितरौ parents, अपश्यम् I saw.
explanation: There I found his weak, blind, old parents. With no supporter, they looked like birds with clipped wings. They sat there helplessly like orphans and passively talking about their son, their only hope that I have deprived them of.

shloka_text: तत्राहं दुर्बलावन्धौ वृद्धावपरिणायकौ। अपश्यं तस्य पितरौ लूनपक्षाविव द्विजौ।।2.64.4।। तन्निमित्ताभिरासीनौ कथाभिरपरिश्रमौ। तामाशां मत्कृते हीनावुदासीनावनाथवत्।।2.64.5।।
transliteration: tatrāhaṃ durbalāvandhau vṛddhāvapariṇāyakau| apaśyaṃ tasya pitarau lūnapakṣāviva dvijau tannimittābhirāsīnau kathābhirapariśramau| tāmāśāṃ matkṛte hīnāvudāsīnāvanāthavat
translation: तत्र there, अहम् I, दुर्बलौ frail, अन्धौ blind, वृद्धौ old, अपरिणायकौ without any supporter, लूनपक्षौ with wings severed, द्विजौ इव like birds, तन्निमित्ताभिः on account of their son, कथाभिः with stories, आसीनौ seated, अपरिश्रमौ without any work, मत्कृते  done by me, ताम् आशाम् their hope, हीनौ deprived of, अनाथवत् like orphans, उदासीनौ passive, तस्य his, पितरौ parents, अपश्यम् I saw.
explanation: There I found his weak, blind, old parents. With no supporter, they looked like birds with clipped wings. They sat there helplessly like orphans and passively talking about their son, their only hope that I have deprived them of.

shloka_text: शोकोपहतचित्तश्च भयसन्त्रस्तचेतनः। तच्चाऽश्रमपदं गत्वा भूयश्शोकमहं गतः।।2.64.6।।
transliteration: śokopahatacittaśca bhayasantrastacetanaḥ| taccā'śramapadaṃ gatvā bhūyaśśokamahaṃ gataḥ
translation: शोकोपहत चित्तः च with mind smitten with grief, भयसन्त्रस्तचेतनः mind charged with apprehension, अहम् I, तत् that, आश्रमपदम् hermitage, गत्वा having reached, भूयः once again, शोकम् sorrow, गतः obtained.
explanation: Smitten with grief and my heart throbbing with fear I reached the hermitage and my sorrow became manifold.

shloka_text: पदशब्दं तु मे श्रुत्वा मुनिर्वाक्यमभाषत। किं चिरायसि मे पुत्र पानीयं क्षिप्रमानय।।2.64.7।।
transliteration: padaśabdaṃ tu me śrutvā munirvākyamabhāṣata| kiṃ cirāyasi me putra pānīyaṃ kṣipramānaya
translation: मे my, पदशब्दम् sound of footsteps, श्रुत्वा having heard, मुनिः sage, वाक्यम् words, अभाषत spoke this, पुत्र son, किम् why, चिरायसि are you delaying, क्षिप्रम् quickly, मे to me, पानीयम् water, आनय bring.
explanation: Hearing the sound of my footsteps, the sage said 'O son why have you delayed? Bring me some water quickly'.

shloka_text: यन्निमित्तमिदं तात सलिले क्रीडितं त्वया। उत्कण्ठिता ते मातेयं प्रविश क्षिप्रमाश्रमम्।।2.64.8।।
transliteration: yannimittamidaṃ tāta salile krīḍitaṃ tvayā| utkaṇṭhitā te māteyaṃ praviśa kṣipramāśramam
translation: तात O Dear child, त्वया by you, यन्निमित्तम् for whatever reason, सलिले in the water, इदम् this, क्रीडितम् sported, इयम् this, ते माता your mother, उत्कण्ठिता with anxicty, क्षिप्रम् quickly, आश्रमम् hermitage, प्रविश enter.
explanation: 'O Dear child, whatever be the reason, you have been sporting in the water so long, come at once to the hermitage. Your mother is anxious.

shloka_text: यद्व्यलीकं कृतं पुत्र मात्रा ते यदि वा मया। न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यं त्वया तात तपस्विना।।2.64.9।।
transliteration: yadvyalīkaṃ kṛtaṃ putra mātrā te yadi vā mayā| na tanmanasi kartavyaṃ tvayā tāta tapasvinā
