translation: पुत्र son, ते your, मात्रा mother, यदिवा or, मया by myself, यत् any, व्यलीकम् displeasing act, कृतम् has been done, तात O Child, तपस्विना by being ascetic, त्वया by you, तत् that one, मनसि in the mind, न कर्तव्यम् should not be taken seriously.
explanation: 'O Child, O Son if your mother or I have done anything disagreeable, do not take it to heart, for you are an ascetic.

shloka_text: त्वं गतिस्त्वगतीनां चक्षुस्त्वं हीनचक्षुषाम्। समासक्तास्त्वयि प्राणाः किं त्वं नो नाभिभाषसे।।2.64.10।।
transliteration: tvaṃ gatistvagatīnāṃ cakṣustvaṃ hīnacakṣuṣām| samāsaktāstvayi prāṇāḥ kiṃ tvaṃ no nābhibhāṣase
translation: अगतीनाम् for us with no support, त्वम् you, गतिः are support, अचक्षुषाम् for us who have no eyes, त्वम् you, चक्षुः हि are our eyes, प्राणाः our vital life, त्वयि in you, समासक्ताः are attached, त्वम् you, नः to us, किम् why, नाभिभाषसे are not talking?
explanation: 'You are a support to the supportless, eyes to the blind, you are our very vital life. Why don't you speak to us'?

shloka_text: मुनिमव्यक्तया वाचा तमहं सज्जमानया। हीनव्यञ्जनया प्रेक्ष्य भीतचित्त इवाब्रुवम्।।2.64.11।।
transliteration: munimavyaktayā vācā tamahaṃ sajjamānayā| hīnavyañjanayā prekṣya bhītacitta ivābruvam
translation: अहम् I, तं मुनिम् that sage, प्रेक्ष्य having seen, भीतचित्त इव with a frightened mind, अव्यक्तया indistinctly, सज्जमानया stammering, हीनव्यञ्जनया with slurring syllables, वाचा with words, अब्रुवम् I uttered.
explanation: As I saw him, my heart was filled with terror and I stammered as I spoke in garbled sentences.

shloka_text: मनसः कर्म चेष्टाभिरभिसंस्तभ्य वाग्बलम्। आचचक्षे त्वहं तस्मै पुत्रव्यसनजं भयम्।।2.64.12।।
transliteration: manasaḥ karma ceṣṭābhirabhisaṃstabhya vāgbalam| ācacakṣe tvahaṃ tasmai putravyasanajaṃ bhayam
translation: अहम् I, चेष्टाभिः with efforts, मनसः mind's, कर्म thoughts, वाग्बलम् power of speech, अभिसंस्तभ्य  holding up firmly, तस्मै him, पुत्रव्यसनजम् the calamity arising due to the death of his son, भयम् fear, आचचक्षे related to him.
explanation: After a lot of effort, with great fear controlling my thoughts and the power of speech, I related to him the calamity that had befallen his son.

shloka_text: क्षत्रियोऽहं दशरथो नाहं पुत्रो महात्मनः। सज्जनावमतं दुःखमिदं प्राप्तं स्वकर्मजम्।।2.64.13।।
transliteration: kṣatriyo'haṃ daśaratho nāhaṃ putro mahātmanaḥ| sajjanāvamataṃ duḥkhamidaṃ prāptaṃ svakarmajam
translation: अहम् I, दशरथः Dasaratha, क्षत्रियः kshatriya, अहम् I, महात्मनः of the great, पुत्रः son, न not, सज्जनावमतम् condemnable by the virtuous, इदम् this, स्वकर्मजम् caused out of my own action, दुःखम् sorrowful, प्राप्तम् has befallen.
explanation: O magnanimous sage I am a kshatriya known as Dasaratha. I am not your son. A pathetic incident has been caused by my own action, condemnable by the virtuous.

shloka_text: भगवंश्चापहस्तोऽहं सरयूतीरमागतः। जिघांसुश्श्वापदं कञ्चिन्निपाने चाऽगतं गजम्।।2.64.14।।
transliteration: bhagavaṃścāpahasto'haṃ sarayūtīramāgataḥ| jighāṃsuśśvāpadaṃ kañcinnipāne cā'gataṃ gajam
translation: भगवन् O revered one, अहम् I, चापहस्तः bow in hand, कञ्चित् a certain, श्वापदम् wild animal, निपाने drinking at the water hole, आगतम् which has come, गजं च an elephant, जिघांसुः wishing to kill, सरयूतीरम् to the bank of river Sarayu, आगतः arrived.
explanation: Wishing to hunt a wild elephant coming down to the water hole for drinking, I went  to the bank of Sarayu, bow in hand, O revered sage

shloka_text: ततश्श्रुतो मया शब्दो जले कुम्भस्य पूर्यतः। द्विपोऽयमिति मत्वाऽयं बाणेनाभिहतो मया।।2.64.15।।
transliteration: tataśśruto mayā śabdo jale kumbhasya pūryataḥ| dvipo'yamiti matvā'yaṃ bāṇenābhihato mayā
translation: ततः thereafter, मया by me, जले in the water, पूर्यतः being filled, कुम्भस्य pot's, शब्दः sound, श्रुतः was heard, अयम् this one, द्विपः इति taking for an elephant, मत्वा having thought, अयम् he, मया by me, बाणेन with arrow, अभिहतः was killed.
explanation: There I heard the sound of a pot being filled with water and mistaking it to be an elephant's, shot an arrow.

shloka_text: गत्वा नद्यास्तत स्तीरमपश्यमिषुणा हृदि। विनिर्भिन्नं गतप्राणं शयानं भुवि तापसम्।।2.64.16।।
transliteration: gatvā nadyāstata stīramapaśyamiṣuṇā hṛdi| vinirbhinnaṃ gataprāṇaṃ śayānaṃ bhuvi tāpasam
translation: ततः then, नद्याः river's, तीरम् bank, गत्वा having gone, इषुणा with an arrow, हृदि in the chest, विनिर्भिन्नम् pierced it, गतप्राणम् with ebbing life, भुवि on the ground, शयानम् lying, तापसम् an ascetic, अपश्यम् I beheld.
explanation: Thereafter I reached the river bank  and beheld an ascetic with an arrow pierced in his chest. He was lying on the ground, his life ebbing away.

shloka_text: भगवच्छशब्दमालक्ष्य मया गजजिघांसुना। विसृप्टोऽम्भसि नाराचस्तेन ते निहतस्सुतः।।2.64.17।।
transliteration: bhagavacchaśabdamālakṣya mayā gajajighāṃsunā| visṛpṭo'mbhasi nārācastena te nihatassutaḥ
translation: भगवन् O venerable one, शब्दम् sound, आलक्ष्य aiming at, गजजिघांसुना intending to kill an elephant, मया by me, अम्भसि in the water, नाराचः with an arrow, विसृष्टः has been released, तेन by that, ते your, सुतः son, निहतः was struck.
explanation: O venerable one I released an arrow towards the water aiming at the sound intending to kill an elephant but it hit your son.

shloka_text: ततस्तस्यैव वचनादुपेत्य परितप्यतः। स मया सहसा बाण उधृतो मर्मतस्तदा।।2.64.18।।
transliteration: tatastasyaiva vacanādupetya paritapyataḥ| sa mayā sahasā bāṇa udhṛto marmatastadā
translation: ततः then, परितप्यतः tormented, तस्यैव by his own, वचनात् words, मया by me, तदा then, उपेत्य reaching him, सहसा at once, सः बाणः that arrow, मर्मतः from his vital part, उधृतः removed.
explanation: Then I approached him. He was suffering from excruciating pain. I pulled out at his word the arrow from his chest.

shloka_text: स चोधृतेन बाणेन तत्रैव स्वर्गमास्थितः। भवन्तौ पितरौ शोचन्नन्धाविति विलप्य च।।2.64.19।।
transliteration: sa codhṛtena bāṇena tatraiva svargamāsthitaḥ| bhavantau pitarau śocannandhāviti vilapya ca
translation: सः च he also, पितरौ parents, भवन्तौ about both of you, शोचन् while grieving, अन्धौ इति   saying you are blind, विलप्य च wailing, उधृतेन extracted, तेन बाणेन by that arrow, तत्रैव there itself, स्वर्गम् heaven, आस्थितः attained.
explanation: Grieving for both of you and crying you are blind he died as soon as the arrow was pulled out.

shloka_text: अज्ञानाद्भवतः पुत्र स्सहसाऽभिहतो मया। शेषमेवं गते यत्स्यात्तत्प्रसीदतु मे मुनिः।।2.64.20।।
transliteration: ajñānādbhavataḥ putra ssahasā'bhihato mayā| śeṣamevaṃ gate yatsyāttatprasīdatu me muniḥ
translation: अज्ञानात् by my ignorance, सहसा suddenly, भवतः पुत्रः your son, मया by me, निहतः was slain, एवं गते when this has happened, यत् whatever, शेषं स्यात् remains to be done, तत् that, मुनिः ascetic, प्रसीदतु be pleased.
explanation: Your son has been killed by me due to my ignorance. Since this has happened, may  the ascetic be pleased to command me on the next course of action.

shloka_text: स तच्च्रुत्वा वचः क्रूरं मयोक्तमघशंसिना। नाशकत्तीव्रमायासमकर्तुं भगवानृषिः।।2.64.21।।
transliteration: sa taccrutvā vacaḥ krūraṃ mayoktamaghaśaṃsinā| nāśakattīvramāyāsamakartuṃ bhagavānṛṣiḥ
translation: भगवान् venerable, सः ऋषिः that sage, अघशंसिना conveying my sinful act, मया by me, उक्तम्  uttered, क्रूरम् cruel, तत् those, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, तीव्रम् intense, आयासम्  anguish, अकर्तुम् not to do, नाशकत् was not able.
explanation: The venerable sage heard my cruel words about the sinful act and was not able to seriously react. (He was stunned).

shloka_text: स बाष्पपूर्णवदनो निश्श्वसन्शोककर्शितः। मामुवाच महातेजाः कृताञ्जलिमुपस्थितम्।।2.64.22।।
transliteration: sa bāṣpapūrṇavadano niśśvasanśokakarśitaḥ| māmuvāca mahātejāḥ kṛtāñjalimupasthitam
translation: महातेजाः brilliant, सः that ascetic, बाष्पपूर्णवदनः face filled with tears, निश्श्वसन् heaving sighs, शोककर्शितः broken with grief, कृताञ्जलिम् with folded palms, उपस्थितम् standing nearby, माम् me, उवाच said.
explanation: The griefstricken, glorious ascetic with his face filled with tears, heaving deep sighs  broke down with grief and spoke to me as I was standing with folded palms.

shloka_text: यद्येतदशुभं कर्म न त्वं मे कथयेस्स्वयम्। फलेन्मूर्धा स्म ते राजन् सद्य श्शतसहस्रधा।।2.64.23।।
transliteration: yadyetadaśubhaṃ karma na tvaṃ me kathayessvayam| phalenmūrdhā sma te rājan sadya śśatasahasradhā
translation: राजन् O king, अशुभम् inauspicious, एतत् this, कर्म act, त्वम् you, मे to me, स्वयम् yourself, न कथयेः यदि not spoke, सद्य: right now, ते your, मूर्धा your head, शतसहस्रधा a hundred thousand pieces, फलेत् स्म would have been split.
explanation: 'O king, hadn't you yourself broken this inauspicious news, your head would have split into a hundred thousand pieces right now.

shloka_text: क्षत्रियेण वधो राजन् वानप्रस्थे विशेषतः। ज्ञानपूर्वं कृत स्स्थानाच्च्यावयेदपि वज्रिणम्।।2.64.24।।
transliteration: kṣatriyeṇa vadho rājan vānaprasthe viśeṣataḥ| jñānapūrvaṃ kṛta ssthānāccyāvayedapi vajriṇam
translation: राजन् king, क्षत्रियेण by a kshatriya, ज्ञानपूर्वम् with prior knowledge, कृतः done, वधः the act of killing, विशेषतः especially, वानप्रस्थे of a forestdweller, वज्रिणम् अपि even if he is wielder of thunderbolt (Indra), स्थानात् from his position, च्वावयेत् would overthrow.
explanation: 'If a kshatriya kills any one knowingly, particularly when in vanaprastha (third stage) this sin can displace even Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt from his position, O king.

shloka_text: सप्तधा तु फलेन्मूर्धा मुनौ तपसि तिष्ठति। ज्ञानाद्विसृजतश्शस्त्रं तादृशे ब्रह्मावादिनि।।2.64.25।।
transliteration: saptadhā tu phalenmūrdhā munau tapasi tiṣṭhati| jñānādvisṛjataśśastraṃ tādṛśe brahmāvādini
translation: तपसि  observing austerities, तिष्ठति staying, मुनौ at the ascetic, तादृशे similar, ब्रह्मवादिनि at one who propagates selfknowledge, ज्ञानात् knowingly, शस्त्रम् weapon, विसृजतः discharges, मूर्धा head, सप्तधा into seven pieces, फलेत् will break.
explanation: 'If any one deliberately discharges a weapon upon an ascetic observing austerities or on him who expounds the Vedas, his head will split into seven pieces.

shloka_text: अज्ञानाद्धिकृतं यस्मादिदं तेनैव जवसि। अपि ह्यद्य कुलं न स्यादिक्ष्वाकूणां कुतो भवान्।।2.64.26।।
transliteration: ajñānāddhikṛtaṃ yasmādidaṃ tenaiva javasi| api hyadya kulaṃ na syādikṣvākūṇāṃ kuto bhavān
translation: इदम् this, यस्मात् for which reason, आज्ञानात् out of ignorance, कृतं हि has been done, तेनैव that is why, जीवसि you will live, इक्ष्वाकूणाम् Ikshvakus', कुलमपि race itself, अद्य now, न स्यात् हि would not have been there, भवान् you also, कुतः where are you
explanation: 'Since you have done this unwittingly you are still alive. If it had been otherwise, your Ikshvaku race itself would have been exterminated, what to speak of you

shloka_text: नय नौ नृप तं देशमिति मां चाभ्यभाषत। अद्य तं द्रष्टुमिच्छावः पुत्रं पश्चिमदर्शनम्।।2.64.27।। रुधिरेणावसिक्ताङ्गं प्रकीर्णाजिनवाससम्। शयानं भुवि निस्संज्ञं धर्म राजवशं गतम्।।2.64.28।।
transliteration: naya nau nṛpa taṃ deśamiti māṃ cābhyabhāṣata| adya taṃ draṣṭumicchāvaḥ putraṃ paścimadarśanam rudhireṇāvasiktāṅgaṃ prakīrṇājinavāsasam| śayānaṃ bhuvi nissaṃjñaṃ dharma rājavaśaṃ gatam
translation: नृप king, अद्य now, पश्चिमदर्शनम् for the last time to see, रुधिरेण in blood, अवसिक्ताङ्गम्   his body spattered, प्रकीर्णाजिनवाससम् with antelope skin in disarray, भुवि on the ground, शयानम् lying, निस्संज्ञम् without senses, धर्मराजवशम् under the sway of the Lord of death, गतम् gone, पुत्रम् son, द्रष्टुम् to see, इच्छावः intend, तं देशम् to that place, नौ us, नय take us, इति thus, माम् me, अभ्यभाषत च spoke.
explanation: 'O king take us to that place. We wish to  have the last look at him, at his garment of antelope skin in disarray, his body spattered with blood, lying on the ground unconscious under the sway of the lord of death'. Thus the sage said to me.

shloka_text: नय नौ नृप तं देशमिति मां चाभ्यभाषत। अद्य तं द्रष्टुमिच्छावः पुत्रं पश्चिमदर्शनम्।।2.64.27।। रुधिरेणावसिक्ताङ्गं प्रकीर्णाजिनवाससम्। शयानं भुवि निस्संज्ञं धर्म राजवशं गतम्।।2.64.28।।
transliteration: naya nau nṛpa taṃ deśamiti māṃ cābhyabhāṣata| adya taṃ draṣṭumicchāvaḥ putraṃ paścimadarśanam rudhireṇāvasiktāṅgaṃ prakīrṇājinavāsasam| śayānaṃ bhuvi nissaṃjñaṃ dharma rājavaśaṃ gatam
translation: नृप king, अद्य now, पश्चिमदर्शनम् for the last time to see, रुधिरेण in blood, अवसिक्ताङ्गम्   his body spattered, प्रकीर्णाजिनवाससम् with antelope skin in disarray, भुवि on the ground, शयानम् lying, निस्संज्ञम् without senses, धर्मराजवशम् under the sway of the Lord of death, गतम् gone, पुत्रम् son, द्रष्टुम् to see, इच्छावः intend, तं देशम् to that place, नौ us, नय take us, इति thus, माम् me, अभ्यभाषत च spoke.
explanation: 'O king take us to that place. We wish to  have the last look at him, at his garment of antelope skin in disarray, his body spattered with blood, lying on the ground unconscious under the sway of the lord of death'. Thus the sage said to me.

shloka_text: अथाहमेकस्तं देशं नीत्वा तौ भृशदुःखितौ। अस्पर्शयमहं पुत्रं तं मुनिं सह भार्यया।।2.64.29।।
transliteration: athāhamekastaṃ deśaṃ nītvā tau bhṛśaduḥkhitau| asparśayamahaṃ putraṃ taṃ muniṃ saha bhāryayā
translation: अथ thereupon, एकः alone, अहम् I, भृशदुःखितौ deeply grieved, तौ both of them, तं देशम् to that place, नीत्वा having taken, भार्यया सह along with his wife, तं मुनिम् to that asetic, तं पुत्रम् their son, अस्पर्शयम् made them touch.
explanation: Thereupon, I took both of them all by myself to that spot and made the grieving ascetics touch the body of their son.

shloka_text: तौ पुत्रमात्मन स्स्पृष्ट्वा तमासाद्य तपस्विनौ। निपेततुश्शरीरेऽस्य पिता चास्येदमब्रवीत्।।62.64.30।।
transliteration: tau putramātmana sspṛṣṭvā tamāsādya tapasvinau| nipetatuśśarīre'sya pitā cāsyedamabravīt
translation: तपस्विनौ both the ascetics, तौ both, तम् their, आत्मनः own, पुत्रम् son, आसाद्य having approached, स्पृष्टवा having touched, अस्य his, शरीरे on body, निपेततुः fell, अस्य his, पिता च father, इदम् this way, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Both the ascetics stroking their son's body and collapsed upon it. And the father said:

shloka_text: नाभिवादयसे माद्य न च माऽमभिभाषसे। किं नु शेषे तु भूमौ त्वं वत्स किं कुपितो ह्यसि।।2.64.31।।
transliteration: nābhivādayase mādya na ca mā'mabhibhāṣase| kiṃ nu śeṣe tu bhūmau tvaṃ vatsa kiṃ kupito hyasi
translation: वत्स child, अद्य today, मा me, नाभिवादयसे you are not greeting us, माम् me, न च अभिभाषसे not also speaking to us, त्वम् you, भूमौ on this ground, किं नु शेषे why are you lying, कुपितः angry, किम् असि why have you become?.
explanation: 'O child why are you not greeting us today nor speaking? Why are you lying on the ground? Are you angry with us?

shloka_text: न त्वहं ते प्रियं पुत्र मातरं पश्य धार्मिक। किं नु नालिङ्गसे पुत्र सुकुमार वचो वद।।2.64.32।।
transliteration: na tvahaṃ te priyaṃ putra mātaraṃ paśya dhārmika| kiṃ nu nāliṅgase putra sukumāra vaco vada
translation: धार्मिक O righteous, पुत्र son, अहम् I, ते to you, प्रियम् dear, न तु if not so, मातरम् mother, पश्य look at, पुत्र O son, किं नु why, नालिङ्गसे are not embracing, सुकुमार O tender child, वचः words, वद tell.
explanation: 'O righteous son if I am no longer dear to you, (at least) look at your mother. O tender child, why are you not embracing me? Speak.

shloka_text: कस्य वाऽपररात्रेऽहं श्रोष्यामि हृदयङ्गमम्। अधीयानस्य मधुरं शास्त्रं वान्यद्विशेषतः।।2.64.33।।
transliteration: kasya vā'pararātre'haṃ śroṣyāmi hṛdayaṅgamam| adhīyānasya madhuraṃ śāstraṃ vānyadviśeṣataḥ
translation: अपररात्रे in the last watch of the night, शास्त्रम् scriptures, विशेषत: especially, अन्वद्वा any other, अधीयानस्य while reciting, कस्य वा or whose, हृदयङ्गमम् delightful to the heart, मधुरम् sweet sound, अहम् I, श्रोष्यामि shall listen?
explanation: 'From whom shall I hear the sweet recitation of scriptures or other texts, delightful to my heart in the last watch of the night?

shloka_text: को मां सन्द्यामुपास्यैव स्नात्वा हुतहुताशनः। श्लाघयिष्यत्युपासीनः पुत्र शोकभयार्दितम्।।2.64.34।।
transliteration: ko māṃ sandyāmupāsyaiva snātvā hutahutāśanaḥ| ślāghayiṣyatyupāsīnaḥ putra śokabhayārditam
translation: पुत्र O son, कः who, स्नात्वा after the ablution, सन्द्याम् morning Sandhya, उपास्यैव having worshipped, हुतहुताशनः having offered oblations to the sacrificial fire, उपासीनः seated near, शोकभयार्दितम् tormented with sorrow and fear, माम् to me, श्लाघयिष्यति serve?
explanation: 'O son I am tortured with sorrow and fear. Who will serve me from now on after the ablution and the morning worship of Sandhya, followed by oblations to the sacrificial fire?

shloka_text: कन्दमूलफलं हृत्वा को मां प्रियमिवातिथिम्। भोजयिष्यत्यकर्मण्यमप्रग्रहमनायकम्।।2.64.35।।
transliteration: kandamūlaphalaṃ hṛtvā ko māṃ priyamivātithim| bhojayiṣyatyakarmaṇyamapragrahamanāyakam
translation: कन्दमूलफलम् tubers and fruits, हृत्वा having brought, कः who, अकर्मण्यम् incapable of  doing any work, अप्रग्रहम् incapable of procuring anything, अनायकम् one who has no guide, माम् me, प्रियम् dear, अतिथिमिव like a guest, भोजयिष्यति will feed?
explanation: 'I am incapable of doing any work, I am unable to procure anything (to meet my needs. now). I have no guide (to help me walk my way). Who will feed me like a welcome guest with tubers and fruits?

shloka_text: इमामन्धां च वृद्धां च मातरं ते तपस्विनीम्। कथं वत्स भरिष्यामि कृपणां पुत्रगर्धिनीम्।।2.64.36।।
transliteration: imāmandhāṃ ca vṛddhāṃ ca mātaraṃ te tapasvinīm| kathaṃ vatsa bhariṣyāmi kṛpaṇāṃ putragardhinīm
translation: वत्स O son, अन्धाम् blind, वृद्धाम् old, तपस्विनीम् miserable, कृपणाम् wretched, पुत्रगर्धिनीम्   yearning for her son, इमाम् this, ते your, मातरम् mother, कथम् how, भरिष्यामि support her?
explanation: 'O son how can I support your wretched and pitiable mother, who is blind, old and yearning for her son?

shloka_text: तिष्ठ मां मागमः पुत्र यमस्य सदनं प्रति। श्वो मया सह गन्तासि जनन्या च समेधितः।।2.64.37।।
transliteration: tiṣṭha māṃ māgamaḥ putra yamasya sadanaṃ prati| śvo mayā saha gantāsi jananyā ca samedhitaḥ
translation: पुत्र son, मां तिष्ठ stay with me, यमस्य of the lord of death, सदनं प्रति to the abode, मागमः do not go, मया with me, जनन्या सह च along with your mother also, समेधितः accompanied by, श्वः tomorrow, गन्तासि may go.
explanation: 'My dear son, stay with me, do not go (now) to the abode of Yama, (lord of death). Tomorrow accompanied by me and your mother you may

shloka_text: उभावपि च शोकार्तावनाथौ कृपणौ वने। क्षिप्रमेव गमिष्यावस्त्वया हीनौ यमक्षयम्।।2.4.38।।
transliteration: ubhāvapi ca śokārtāvanāthau kṛpaṇau vane| kṣiprameva gamiṣyāvastvayā hīnau yamakṣayam
translation: त्वया by you, हीनौ having been deserted, शोकार्तौ afflicted with grief, वने in the forest, अनाथौ without support, कृपणौ wretched ones, उभावपि च both of us also, क्षिप्रमेव quickly, यमक्षयम् to the abode of Yama, गमिष्यावः will go.
explanation: 'Deserted by you and without any support in the forest, afflicted with grief and feeling miserable, both of us also will assuredly go to Yama's abode, quickly.

shloka_text: ततो वैवस्वतं दृष्ट्वा तं प्रवक्ष्यामि भारतीम्। क्षमतां धर्मराजो मे बिभृयात्पितरावयम्।।2.64.39।।
transliteration: tato vaivasvataṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ pravakṣyāmi bhāratīm| kṣamatāṃ dharmarājo me bibhṛyātpitarāvayam
translation: ततः then, वैवस्वतम् lord of death, Yama, दृष्ट्वा having seen, तम् him, भारतीम् in speech, प्रवक्ष्यामि I shall say, धर्मराजः the lord of justice, मे me, क्षमताम् forgive, अयम् this man, पितरौ parents, बिभृयात् continue to maintain.
explanation: 'There seeing Yama, (lord of death), I shall say O Lord of Justice forgive me. Let this boy continue to maintain his parents.

shloka_text: दातुमर्हति धर्मात्मा लोकपालो महायशाः। ईदृशस्य ममाक्षय्या मेकामभयदक्षिणाम्।।2.64.40।।
transliteration: dātumarhati dharmātmā lokapālo mahāyaśāḥ| īdṛśasya mamākṣayyā mekāmabhayadakṣiṇām
translation: महायशाः of high renown, धर्मात्मा righteous, लोकपालः guardian of the worlds, ईदृशस्य of such, मम to me, अक्षय्याम् unfailing, एकाम् one, अभय दक्षिणाम् protection from fear, दातुम् to give, अर्हति behoves him.
explanation: 'That lord of justice, who is highly renowned, righteous and the guardian of the worlds will grant me one unfailing boon of protection from fear.

shloka_text: अपापोऽसि यदा पुत्र निहतः पापकर्मणा। तेन सत्येन गच्छाऽऽशु ये लोकाश्शस्त्रयोधिनाम्।।2.64.41।।
transliteration: apāpo'si yadā putra nihataḥ pāpakarmaṇā| tena satyena gacchā''śu ye lokāśśastrayodhinām
translation: पुत्र O son, पापकर्मणा by a person of sinful deeds, निहतः killed, यथा just as, अपापः असि you are sinless, तेन that, सत्येन with truth, शस्त्रयोधिनाम् those who fight with weapons, ये whichever, लोका: worlds, आशु quickly, गच्छ go.
explanation: 'O sinless son, you are killed by a person of sinful deeds. On this truth, quickly go to those worlds which are attained by those valiant heroes.

shloka_text: यान्ति शूरा गतिं यां च सङ्ग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनः। हतास्त्वभिमुखाः पुत्र गतिं तां परमां व्रज।।2.64.42।।
transliteration: yānti śūrā gatiṃ yāṃ ca saṅgrāmeṣvanivartinaḥ| hatāstvabhimukhāḥ putra gatiṃ tāṃ paramāṃ vraja
translation: पुत्र son, सङ्ग्रामेषु in wars, अनिवर्तिनः the men who do not retreat, शूराः warriors, अभिमुखाः याम् facing the enemy, गतिम् ultimate state, यान्ति will attain, ताम् that one, परमाम् supreme, गतिम् state, व्रज attain.
explanation: O son, attain that supreme goal which brave warriors, who never retreat but fall facing the foe in battle, attain.

shloka_text: यां गतिं सगरश्शैब्यो दिलीपो जनमेजयः। नहुषो दुन्दुमारश्च प्राप्तास्तां गच्छ पुत्रक।।2.64.43।।
transliteration: yāṃ gatiṃ sagaraśśaibyo dilīpo janamejayaḥ| nahuṣo dundumāraśca prāptāstāṃ gaccha putraka
translation: पुत्रक O son, सगरः Sagara, शैब्यः Saibya, दिलीपः Dilipa, जनमेजयः Janamejaya, नहुषः Nahusha, दुन्दुमारश्च Dundumara also, याम् which, गतिम् state, प्राप्ताः have attained, ताम् the same, गच्छ attain.
explanation: 'You will attain, my son, the same supreme state achieved by Sagara, Saibya, Dilipa, Janamejaya, Nahusha and Dundumara.

shloka_text: या गति स्सर्वसाधूनां स्वाध्यायात्तपसाच या। या भूमिदस्याहिऽताग्नेरेकपत्नी व्रतस्य च।।2.64.44।। गोसहस्रप्रदातृ़णां या या गुरुभृतामपि। देहन्यासकृतां या च तां गतिं गच्छ पुत्रक।।2.64.45।।
transliteration: yā gati ssarvasādhūnāṃ svādhyāyāttapasāca yā| yā bhūmidasyāhi'tāgnerekapatnī vratasya ca gosahasrapradātṛ़ṇāṃ yā yā gurubhṛtāmapi| dehanyāsakṛtāṃ yā ca tāṃ gatiṃ gaccha putraka
translation: पुत्रक O son, सर्वसाधूनाम् of all virtuous people, या which, गतिः state, स्वाध्यायात् with the study of Vedas, तपसा च by asceticism, भूमिदस्य  bestowers of land as charity, आहिताग्नेः  who kindle the sacred fires, एकपत्नीव्रतस्य च of the monogamist too, गोसहस्रप्रदातृ़णाम्  who offer a thousand cows in charity, या which, गुरुभृतामपि who nurture the venerable ones, देहन्यासकताम् for those who lay down their bodies voluntarily, या च and those, तां गतिम् the same state, गच्छ you will attain.
explanation: 'You, my son, shall attain that supreme state obtained by those who are virtuous, who study the Vedas and practise asceticism.You shall attain the state merited by those bestowers of land as charity, who kindle the sacred fires, who are monoganists, who offer a thousand cows in charity, who nurture the venerable and who willingly lay down their bodies.

shloka_text: या गति स्सर्वसाधूनां स्वाध्यायात्तपसाच या। या भूमिदस्याहिऽताग्नेरेकपत्नी व्रतस्य च।।2.64.44।। गोसहस्रप्रदातृ़णां या या गुरुभृतामपि। देहन्यासकृतां या च तां गतिं गच्छ पुत्रक।।2.64.45।।
transliteration: yā gati ssarvasādhūnāṃ svādhyāyāttapasāca yā| yā bhūmidasyāhi'tāgnerekapatnī vratasya ca gosahasrapradātṛ़ṇāṃ yā yā gurubhṛtāmapi| dehanyāsakṛtāṃ yā ca tāṃ gatiṃ gaccha putraka
translation: पुत्रक O son, सर्वसाधूनाम् of all virtuous people, या which, गतिः state, स्वाध्यायात् with the study of Vedas, तपसा च by asceticism, भूमिदस्य  bestowers of land as charity, आहिताग्नेः  who kindle the sacred fires, एकपत्नीव्रतस्य च of the monogamist too, गोसहस्रप्रदातृ़णाम्  who offer a thousand cows in charity, या which, गुरुभृतामपि who nurture the venerable ones, देहन्यासकताम् for those who lay down their bodies voluntarily, या च and those, तां गतिम् the same state, गच्छ you will attain.
explanation: 'You, my son, shall attain that supreme state obtained by those who are virtuous, who study the Vedas and practise asceticism.You shall attain the state merited by those bestowers of land as charity, who kindle the sacred fires, who are monoganists, who offer a thousand cows in charity, who nurture the venerable and who willingly lay down their bodies.

shloka_text: न हि त्वस्मिन्कुले जातो गच्छत्यकुशलां गतिम्। स तु यास्यति येन त्वं निहतो मम बान्धवः।।2.64.46।।
transliteration: na hi tvasminkule jāto gacchatyakuśalāṃ gatim| sa tu yāsyati yena tvaṃ nihato mama bāndhavaḥ
translation: अस्मिन् in this, कुले family, जातः born, अकुशलाम् undesirable, गतिम् state, न गच्छति हि will never go, तु but, मम my, बान्धवः relation, त्वम् you, येन by whom, निहतः killed, सः he, यास्यति will attain.
explanation: 'He who has killed you will alone attain that undesirable state, a member of our family will not.'

shloka_text: एवं स कृपणं तत्र पर्यदेवयतासकृत्। ततोऽस्मै कर्तुमुदकं प्रवृत्तस्सहभार्यया।।2.64.47।।
transliteration: evaṃ sa kṛpaṇaṃ tatra paryadevayatāsakṛt| tato'smai kartumudakaṃ pravṛttassahabhāryayā
translation: सः he, एवम् in this way, तत्र there, असकृत् again and again, कृपणम् piteously, पर्यदेवयत  bewailed, ततः then, अस्मै to him, भार्यया सह along with his wife, उदकं कर्तुम् to perform funeral obsequies, प्रवृत्तः commenced.
explanation: In this way the ascetic piteously wailed again and again. Thereafter, he with his wife set about to perform the funeral obsequies of their son.

shloka_text: स तु दिव्येन रूपेण मुनिपुत्रस्स्वकर्मभिः। स्वर्गमध्यारुहत्क्षिप्रं शक्रेण सह धर्मवित्।।2.64.48।।
transliteration: sa tu divyena rūpeṇa muniputrassvakarmabhiḥ| svargamadhyāruhatkṣipraṃ śakreṇa saha dharmavit
translation: धर्मवित् one conversant with righteousness, सः that, मुनिपुत्रः son of the sage, स्वकर्मभिः by the merit of his own deeds, शक्रेण सह with Indra, दिव्येन in a celestial, रूपेण form, क्षिप्रम् quickly, स्वर्गम् heaven, अध्यारुहत् ascended.
explanation: The virtuous son of that ascetic assumed a celestial form through the merit of his good deeds and ascended heaven at once with Indra.

shloka_text: आबभाषे च वृद्धौ तौ सह शक्रेण तापसः। आश्वास्यच मुहूर्तं तु पितरौ वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.64.49।।
transliteration: ābabhāṣe ca vṛddhau tau saha śakreṇa tāpasaḥ| āśvāsyaca muhūrtaṃ tu pitarau vākyamabravīt
translation: सह शक्रेण with Indra, (सः) तापसः that ascetic, तौ both, वृद्धौ to the aged ones, अबाभाषे च  spoke, पितरौ parents, मुहूर्तम् for a brief  moment, आश्वास्य consoling, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: The ascetic in the company of Indra consoling the aged couple for a brief moment said:

shloka_text: स्थानमस्मि महत्प्राप्तो भवतोः परिचारणात्। भवन्तावपि च क्षिप्रं मम मूलमुपैष्यतः।।2.64.50।।
transliteration: sthānamasmi mahatprāpto bhavatoḥ paricāraṇāt| bhavantāvapi ca kṣipraṃ mama mūlamupaiṣyataḥ
translation: भवतोः your, परिचारणात् by (your) service, महत् supreme, स्थानम् state, प्राप्तः अस्मि I have  attained, भवन्तौ अपि च you also, क्षिप्रम् quickly, मम my, मूलम् presence, उपैष्यतः will obtain.
explanation: 'I have attained this supreme state by virtue of the service rendered to you. You will also attain my state soon.'

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु दिव्येन विमानेन वपुष्मता। आरुरोह दिवं क्षिप्रं मुनिपुत्रो जितेन्द्रियः।।2.64.51।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu divyena vimānena vapuṣmatā| āruroha divaṃ kṣipraṃ muniputro jitendriyaḥ
translation: जितेन्द्रियः one with his senses conquered, मुनिपुत्रः sage's son, एवम् in this way, उक्त्वा having said, वपुष्मता beautiful, दिव्येन celestial, विमानेन aerial chariot, क्षिप्रम् quickly, दिवम् heaven, आरुरोह ascended.
explanation: The sage's son with his senses under control said this while ascending heaven on a beautiful, celestial, aerial chariot.

shloka_text: स कृत्वा तूदकं तूर्णं तापस स्सह भार्यया। मामुवाच महातेजाः कृताञ्जलिमुपस्थितम्।।2.64.52।।
transliteration: sa kṛtvā tūdakaṃ tūrṇaṃ tāpasa ssaha bhāryayā| māmuvāca mahātejāḥ kṛtāñjalimupasthitam
translation: महातेजाः brilliant, सः तापसः that ascetic, भार्यया सह with his wife, तूर्णम् immediately, उदकं कृत्वा offering funeral libations, कृताञ्जलिम् with folded palms, उपस्थितम् standing nearby, माम् me, उवाच addressed.
explanation: The radiant ascetic along with his wife hurriedly completed the funeral libations and said to me standing with folded palms:

shloka_text: अद्यैव जहिं मां राजन्मरणे नास्ति मे व्यथा। यच्छरेणैकपुत्रं मां त्वमकर्षीरपुत्रकम्।।2.64.53।।
transliteration: adyaiva jahiṃ māṃ rājanmaraṇe nāsti me vyathā| yacchareṇaikaputraṃ māṃ tvamakarṣīraputrakam
translation: राजन् king, त्वम् you, यत् since, ऐक पुत्रम् having only one son, माम् me, शरेण with the arrow, अपुत्रकम् childless, अकार्षीः rendered, अद्यैव right now, माम् me, जहि slay, मे to me, मरणे in death, व्यथा pain, नास्ति not.
explanation: 'Kill me, O king with the same arrow by which you rendered me childless. Death holds no pain for me.

shloka_text: त्वया तु यदविज्ञानान्निहतो मे सुतश्शुचिः। तेन त्वामभिशप्स्यामि सुदुःखमतिदारुणम्।।2.64.54।।
transliteration: tvayā tu yadavijñānānnihato me sutaśśuciḥ| tena tvāmabhiśapsyāmi suduḥkhamatidāruṇam
translation: त्वया by you, अविज्ञानात् in ignorance, मे my, शुचिः purehearted, सुतः son, यत् since, निहतः was killed, तेन therefore, त्वाम् you, सुदुःखम् deeply sorrowful, अतिदारुणम् extremely dreadful, अभिशप्स्यामि I will curse.
explanation: 'Though you have killed my purehearted son unintentionally, I will pronounce a disastrous and dreadful curse on you.

shloka_text: पुत्रव्यसनजं दुःखं यदेतन्मम साम्प्रतम्। एवं त्वं पुत्रशोकेन राजन्कालं करिष्यसि।।2.64.55।।
transliteration: putravyasanajaṃ duḥkhaṃ yadetanmama sāmpratam| evaṃ tvaṃ putraśokena rājankālaṃ kariṣyasi
translation: साम्प्रतम् now, यत् एतत् just as this, पुत्रव्यसनजम् caused by my son's death, दुःखम् grief, एवम् the same way, राजन् O king, त्वम् you, पुत्रशोकेन by the sorrow over your son, कालं करिष्यसि will die.
explanation: 'Just as I am now suffering from grief caused by my son's death, you, O king, shall die from the sorrow on account of (separation from) your son.

shloka_text: अज्ञानात्तु हतो यस्मात्क्षत्रियेण त्वया मुनिः। तस्मात्त्वां नाविशत्याशु ब्रह्महत्या नराधिप।।2.64.56।।
transliteration: ajñānāttu hato yasmātkṣatriyeṇa tvayā muniḥ| tasmāttvāṃ nāviśatyāśu brahmahatyā narādhipa
translation: नराधिप O lord of men, क्षत्रियेण by being a kshatriya, त्वया by you, यस्मात् since, मुनिः sage, अज्ञानात् ignorantly, हतः killed, तस्मात् for that reason, आशु immediately, ब्रह्महत्या sin of slaying a brahmana, त्वाम् you, न आविशति will not apply.
explanation: 'Since you, O lord of men, you have killed an ascetic unaware, as kshatriya the sin of slaying a brahmin will not accrue to you immediately.

shloka_text: त्वामप्येतादृशो भावः क्षिप्रमेव गमिष्यति। जीवितान्तकरो घोरो दातारमिव दक्षिणा।।2.64.57।।
transliteration: tvāmapyetādṛśo bhāvaḥ kṣiprameva gamiṣyati| jīvitāntakaro ghoro dātāramiva dakṣiṇā
translation: जीवितान्तकरः causing the end of your life, घोरः dreadful, एतादृशः such, भावः mortal condition, दक्षिणा alms, दातारम् इव like a giver, क्षिप्रमेव soon, त्वामपि you also, गमिष्यति will reach.
explanation: 'Just like the merits of alms come to the giver, you are going to face very soon a dreadful situation causing the end of your life.'

shloka_text: एवं शापं मयि न्यस्य विलप्य करुणं बहु। चितामारोप्य देहं तन्मिथुनं स्वर्गमभ्ययात्।।2.64.58।।
transliteration: evaṃ śāpaṃ mayi nyasya vilapya karuṇaṃ bahu| citāmāropya dehaṃ tanmithunaṃ svargamabhyayāt
translation: तत् that, मिथुनम् couple, एवम् in this way, मयि in me, शापम् curse, न्यस्य giving, करुणम् piteously, बहुविलप्य lamenting long, देहम् body, चिताम् funeral pyre, आरोप्य ascending, स्वर्गम् to heaven, अभ्ययात् went.
explanation: Having thus cursed me, the couple piteously lamenting for a long time, laid themselves down on the funeral pyre  and went to heaven.

shloka_text: तदेतच्छिन्तयानेन स्मृतं पापं मया स्वयम्। तदा बाल्यात्कृतं देवि शब्दवेध्यनुशिक्षिणा।।2.64.59।।
transliteration: tadetacchintayānena smṛtaṃ pāpaṃ mayā svayam| tadā bālyātkṛtaṃ devi śabdavedhyanuśikṣiṇā
translation: देवि O Devi (Kausalya), तदा then, शब्दवेध्यनुशिक्षिणा trained in discharging the arrow in the direction of sound, मया by me, बाल्यात् out of ignorance, स्वयम् myself, कृतम् committed, तत् such, एतत् this, पापम् sin, चिन्तयानेन reflecting, स्मृतम् recollected.
explanation: While reflecting about it now, O Devi (Kausalya) I recollect this sin committed by me unintentionally, with childish pranks while practising the art of hitting a target by its sound.

shloka_text: तस्यायं कर्मणो देवि विपाकस्समुपस्थितः। अपथ्यैस्सहम्भुक्ते व्याधिरन्नरसे यथा।।2.64.60।।
transliteration: tasyāyaṃ karmaṇo devi vipākassamupasthitaḥ| apathyaissahambhukte vyādhirannarase yathā
translation: देवि O Devi, तस्य कर्मणः that act's, अयं विपाकः this consequence, अन्नरसे food and drink, अपथ्यैः सह with unhealthy food, सम्भुक्ते सति when partaking, व्याधिः यथा causing illness, समुपस्थितः has befallen.
explanation: Just as a man eating forbidden food and drink falls sick, so have I fallen prey to grief, because of my sin, O Devi

shloka_text: तस्मान्मामागतं भद्रे तस्योदारस्य तद्वचः। यदहं पुत्रशोकेन सन्त्यक्ष्याम्यद्य जीवितम्।।2.64.61।।
transliteration: tasmānmāmāgataṃ bhadre tasyodārasya tadvacaḥ| yadahaṃ putraśokena santyakṣyāmyadya jīvitam
translation: भद्रे O gentle lady, तस्मात् hence, अहम् I, पुत्रशोकेन due to sorrow over my son, जीवितम् life, यत् सन्त्यक्ष्यामि since I am giving up, उदारस्य of the noble, तस्य that ascetic's, तत् वचः those words, मम for me, अद्य today, आगतम् have come true.
explanation: O gentle lady, the words of that noble ascetic have come true today. Hence I am now going to give up my life.

shloka_text: चक्षुभ्यां त्वां न पश्यामि कौसल्ये साधु मां स्फृश। इत्युक्त्वा स रुदंस्त्रस्तो भार्यामाह च भूमिपः।।2.64.62।।
transliteration: cakṣubhyāṃ tvāṃ na paśyāmi kausalye sādhu māṃ sphṛśa| ityuktvā sa rudaṃstrasto bhāryāmāha ca bhūmipaḥ
translation: कौशल्ये O Kausalya, चक्षुर्भ्याम् with eyes, त्वाम् you, न पश्यामि I am unable to see, मां me, साधु  properly, स्फृश touch, भूमिपः lord of the earth, इति उक्त्वा having said so, त्रस्तो frightened, रुदन् weeping, भार्याम् to his wife, आह च said also.
explanation: O Kausalya, I cannot see you with my eyes. Touch me gently, said the frightened Dasaratha, Lord of the earth, to his wife weeping.

shloka_text: एतन्मे सदृशं देवि यन्मया राघवे कृतम्। सदृशं तत्तु तस्यैव यदनेन कृतं मयि।।2.64.63।।
transliteration: etanme sadṛśaṃ devi yanmayā rāghave kṛtam| sadṛśaṃ tattu tasyaiva yadanena kṛtaṃ mayi
translation: देवि O Devi, मया by me, यत् whatever, राघवे to Rama, कृतम् done, एतत् all that, मे to me, सदृशम् befitting, अनेन by him (this Rama), मयि relating to me, यत् whatever, कृतम् done, तत्तु that one, तस्यैव his, सदृशम् is worthy of.
explanation: Whatever I have done to the scion of the Raghu family (Rama) is befitting me, O Devi. And whatever he has done in respect of me is also worthy of him.

shloka_text: दुर्वृत्तमपि कः पुत्रं त्यजेद्भुवि विचक्षणः। कश्च प्रव्राज्यमानो वा नासूयेत्पितरं सुतः।।2.64.64।।
transliteration: durvṛttamapi kaḥ putraṃ tyajedbhuvi vicakṣaṇaḥ| kaśca pravrājyamāno vā nāsūyetpitaraṃ sutaḥ
translation: भुवि in this world, विचक्षणः clearrighted, कः who, दुर्वृत्तमपि even if illbehaved, पुत्रम् son, त्यजेत् will he abandon?, प्रव्राज्यमानो अपि even while he is being banished, कः who, सुतः son, पितरम् at his father, ना सूयेत् will not become angry?
explanation: Which clearsighted man in this world, will abandon his son even if he is of evil conduct? Which son will not get angry with his father when he is banished?

shloka_text: यदि मां संस्पृशेद्रामस्सकृदद्य लभेत वा। यमक्षयमनुप्राप्ता द्रक्ष्यन्ति न हि मानवाः।।2.64.65।।
transliteration: yadi māṃ saṃspṛśedrāmassakṛdadya labheta vā| yamakṣayamanuprāptā drakṣyanti na hi mānavāḥ
translation: रामः Rama, अद्य now, सकृत् once, माम् me, सम्स्पृशेत् will touch?, लभेत वा will he come to my side, यमक्षयम् world of Yama, अनुप्राप्ताः attained, मानवाः men, न द्रक्ष्यन्ति हि cannot see any more indeed
explanation: Before I die, will Rama touch me once or will he come to me? After reaching the abode of Yama men cannot see their relations.

shloka_text: चक्षुषा त्वां न पश्यामि स्मृतिर्मम विलुप्यते। दूता वैवस्वतस्यैते कौसल्ये त्वरयन्ति माम्।।2.64.66।।
transliteration: cakṣuṣā tvāṃ na paśyāmi smṛtirmama vilupyate| dūtā vaivasvatasyaite kausalye tvarayanti mām
translation: कौसल्ये O Kausalya, चक्षुषा with my eyes, त्वाम् you, न पश्यामि cannot see, मम my, स्मृतिः memory, विलुप्यते is failing, वैवस्वतस्य Yama's, एते दूताः these messengers, माम् me, त्वरयन्ति are hastening up.
explanation: O Kausalya, I am unable to see you. My memory is failing and the messengers of Yama are hastening me.

shloka_text: अतस्तु किं दुःखतरं यदहं जीवितक्षये। न हि पश्यामि धर्मज्ञं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्।।2.64.67।।
transliteration: atastu kiṃ duḥkhataraṃ yadahaṃ jīvitakṣaye| na hi paśyāmi dharmajñaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākramam
translation: अहम् I, जीवितक्षये at the last moment of my life, धर्मज्ञम् to the knower of righteousness, सत्यपराक्रमम्  to one possessing the strength of truth, रामम् Rama, न पश्यामि हि इति यत् the fact that I am unable to see,  अतः more than this, दुःखतरम् more sorrowful, किं नु what is there?
explanation: Can there be a greater sorrow than that at the last moment of my life I am unable to see my righteous and truthful son, Rama?

shloka_text: तस्यादर्शनजश्शोकस्सुतस्याप्रतिकर्मणः। उच्छोषयति मे प्राणान्वारिस्तोकमिवातपः।।2.64.68।।
transliteration: tasyādarśanajaśśokassutasyāpratikarmaṇaḥ| ucchoṣayati me prāṇānvāristokamivātapaḥ
translation: अप्रतिकर्मणः of unparalleled deeds, तस्य सुतस्य that son's, अदर्शनजः born out of nonappearance, शोकः grief, स्तोकम् small quantity, वारि water, आतपः इव like heat, मे my, प्राणान् life, उच्छोषयति is drying up.
explanation: My grief in the absence of Rama of peerless deeds is drying up my life as heat dries up small pools of water.

shloka_text: न ते मनुष्या देवास्ते ये चारुशुभकुण्डलम्। मुखं द्रक्ष्यन्ति रामस्य वर्षे पञ्चदशे पुनः।।2.64.69।।
transliteration: na te manuṣyā devāste ye cāruśubhakuṇḍalam| mukhaṃ drakṣyanti rāmasya varṣe pañcadaśe punaḥ
translation: पञ्चदशे वर्षे in the fifteenth year, ये whoever, चारु elegant, शुभकुण्डलम् with auspicious ear rings, रामस्य Rama's, मुखम् countenance, पुनः again, द्रक्ष्यन्ति will behold, ते those, देवाः gods, मनुष्याः men, न not.
explanation: Those who will behold Rama's countenance adorned with auspicious earrings on his return in the fifteenth year are gods not men.

shloka_text: पद्मपत्रेक्षणं सुभ्रु सुदंष्ट्रं चारुनासिकम्। धन्या द्रक्ष्यन्ति रामस्य ताराधिपनिभं मुखम्।।2.64.70।।
transliteration: padmapatrekṣaṇaṃ subhru sudaṃṣṭraṃ cārunāsikam| dhanyā drakṣyanti rāmasya tārādhipanibhaṃ mukham
translation: पद्मपत्रेक्षणम् eyes like lotus petals, सुभ्रु graceful eyebrows, सुदंष्ट्रम् even teeth, चारुनासिकम् of shapely nose, ताराधिपनिभम् resembling the lord of the stars (the Moon), रामस्य Rama's, मुखम् countenance, धन्याः blessed, द्रक्ष्यन्ति will behold.
explanation: Blessed are they who will behold Rama's countenance resembling the Moon, lord of the stars with eyes like lotus petals graceful eyebrows, even teeth and a nose.

shloka_text: सदृशं शारदस्येन्दोः पुल्लस्य कमलस्य च। सुगन्धि मम नाथस्य धन्या द्रक्ष्यन्ति तन्मुखम्।।2.64.71।।
transliteration: sadṛśaṃ śāradasyendoḥ pullasya kamalasya ca| sugandhi mama nāthasya dhanyā drakṣyanti tanmukham
translation: शारदस्य autumnal, इन्दोः Moon, सदृशम् similar, पुल्लस्य fullblown, कमलस्य च similar to lotus, सुगन्धि fragrant, मम नाथस्य my son's, तत् that, मुखम् countenance, धन्याः blessed, द्रक्ष्यन्ति will behold.
explanation: Fortunate indeed are the men who will behold my son's fragrant countenance camparable to the autmnal Moon and the fullblown lotus.

shloka_text: निवृत्तवनवासं तमयोध्यां पुनरागतम्। द्रक्ष्यन्ति सुखिनो रामं शुक्रं मार्गगतं यथा।।2.64.72।।
transliteration: nivṛttavanavāsaṃ tamayodhyāṃ punarāgatam| drakṣyanti sukhino rāmaṃ śukraṃ mārgagataṃ yathā
translation: निवृत्तवनवासम् after completing the period of exile, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, पुनः again, आगतम् returning, रामम् Rama, मार्गगतम् moving on the highway, शुक्रं यथा like the planet Venus, सुखिनः happy persons, द्रक्ष्यन्ति will behold.
explanation: Lucky men will behold Rama return to Ayodhya after the completion of his exile, like the planet Venus moving forward on its orbit.

shloka_text: कौसल्ये चित्तमोहेन हृदयं सीदतीव मे। वेदये न च संयुक्तान् शब्दस्पर्शरसानहम्।।2.64.73।।
transliteration: kausalye cittamohena hṛdayaṃ sīdatīva me| vedaye na ca saṃyuktān śabdasparśarasānaham
translation: कौसल्ये O Kausalya, चित्तमोहेन on account of delusion, मे हृदयम् my heart, सीदतीव as if sinking, अहम् I, संयुक्तान् united, शब्दस्पर्शरसान् the sense of sound, touch and taste, न च वेदये I am not able to know.
explanation: O Kausalya, my heart, it appears is sinking and on account of delusion I am not able to feel the sense objects like sound touch and taste together.

shloka_text: चित्तनाशाद्विपद्यन्ते सर्वाण्येन्द्रियाणि मे। क्षीणस्नेहस्य दीपस्य संसक्ता रश्मयो यथा।।2.64.74।।
transliteration: cittanāśādvipadyante sarvāṇyendriyāṇi me| kṣīṇasnehasya dīpasya saṃsaktā raśmayo yathā
translation: चित्तनाशात् on account of the loss of the mental faculty, मे my, सर्वाण्येव all, इन्द्रियाणि sense organs, क्षीणस्नेहस्य with oil exhausted, दीपस्य like the lamp, संसक्ताः together, रश्मयः यथा like rays, विपद्यन्ते are giving way.
explanation: With the loss of my mental faculty, all the sense organs are giving way, like the rays of the lamp giving way together when the oil is exhausted.

shloka_text: अयमात्मभवश्शोको मामनाथमचेतनम्। संसादयति वेगेन यथा कूलं नदीरयः।।2.64.75।।
transliteration: ayamātmabhavaśśoko māmanāthamacetanam| saṃsādayati vegena yathā kūlaṃ nadīrayaḥ
translation: आत्मभवः selfcreated on account of my son, अयम् this, शोकः sorrow, अनाथम् helpless, अचेतनम् insensible, माम् me, नदीरयः current of the river, कूलं यथा like the bank, वेगेन rapidly, संसादयति eroding.
explanation: This selfcreated grief is rapidly destroying me like the bank of a river eroded by its swift current, leaving me helpless and insensible.

shloka_text: हा राघव महाबाहो हा ममाऽयासनाशन। हा पितृप्रिय मे नाथ हाऽद्य क्वासि गतस्सुत।।2.64.76।।
transliteration: hā rāghava mahābāho hā mamā'yāsanāśana| hā pitṛpriya me nātha hā'dya kvāsi gatassuta
translation: महाबाहो O mightyarmed one, हा राघव Ah Rama, मम my, आयासनाशन destroyer of my agony, हा Ah , हा पितृप्रिय Ah delight of your father, मे नाथ my protector, हा Ah सुत son, क्व where, गतः असि have you gone?.
explanation: Ah, mightyarmed Rama, destroyer of my agonies, Ah, the delight of your father, Ah, my protector, Ah, my son, where have you gone?.

shloka_text: हा कौसल्ये नशिष्यामि हा सुमित्रे तपस्विनि। हा नृशंसे ममामित्रे कैकेयि कुलपांसनि।।2.64.77।।
transliteration: hā kausalye naśiṣyāmi hā sumitre tapasvini| hā nṛśaṃse mamāmitre kaikeyi kulapāṃsani
translation: हा कौशल्ये Ah Kausalya, तपस्विनि pitiable one, हा सुमित्रे Ah Sumitra, हा Ah, नृशंसे cruel one, मम अमित्रे my enemy, कुलपांसनि defiler of my race, कैकेयि Kaikeyi, नशिष्यामि am destroyed.
explanation: Ah, Kausalya, Ah, pitiable Sumitra, Ah, cruel Kaikeyi, my enemy and defiler of my race, I am going to die.

shloka_text: इति रामस्य मातुश्च सुमित्रायाश्च सन्निधौ। राजा दशरथ श्शोचञ्जीवितान्तमुपागमत्।।2.64.78।।
transliteration: iti rāmasya mātuśca sumitrāyāśca sannidhau| rājā daśaratha śśocañjīvitāntamupāgamat
translation: राजा king, दशरधः Dasaratha, इति thus, रामस्य मातुश्च Rama's mother, सुमित्रायाश्च  Sumitra's, सन्निधौ in the presence, इति thus, शोचन् crying in distress, जीवितान्तं end of his life, उपागमत् reached.
explanation: King Dasaratha, thus crying in distress in the presence of Rama's mother and  Sumitra reached the end of his life.

shloka_text: यदा तु दीनं कथयन्नराधिपः प्रियस्य पुत्त्रस्य विवासनातुरः। गतेऽर्धरात्रे भृशदुःखपीडितस्तदा जहौ प्राणमुदारदर्शनः।।2.64.79।।
transliteration: yadā tu dīnaṃ kathayannarādhipaḥ priyasya puttrasya vivāsanāturaḥ| gate'rdharātre bhṛśaduḥkhapīḍitastadā jahau prāṇamudāradarśanaḥ
translation: उदारदर्शनः a man of noble vision, नराधिपः king, दीनम् pitiably, कथयन् while speaking,  पुत्रस्य son's, विवासनातुरः distraught on account of his exile, अर्धरात्रे at midnight, गते having passed away, यदा when, भृशदुःखपीडितः tormented with intense sorrow, तदा then, प्राणम् life, जहौ gave up.
explanation: King Dasaratha, a man of noble vision and lord of men, anguished by the exile of his son, kept pitiably muttering till past midnight  until tormented by an intense agony he breathed his last. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुष्षष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyfourth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां प्रातरेवापरेऽहनि। वन्दिनः पर्युपातिष्ठंस्तत्पार्थिव निवेशनम्।।2.65.1।। सूताः परमसंस्कारा मङ्गलाश्चोत्तमश्रुताः। गायका: स्तुतिशीलाश्च निगदन्तः पृथक् पृथक्।।2.65.2।।
transliteration: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ prātarevāpare'hani| vandinaḥ paryupātiṣṭhaṃstatpārthiva niveśanam sūtāḥ paramasaṃskārā maṅgalāścottamaśrutāḥ| gāyakā: stutiśīlāśca nigadantaḥ pṛthak pṛthak
translation: अथ thereafter, रात्र्याम्  that night, व्यतीतायाम् had passed, अपरे on the following, अहनि day, प्रातः एव in the morning, परमसंस्काराः highly accomplished men, उत्तमश्रुताः proficient in learning, मङ्गलाश्च auspicious men, सूताः genealogists, स्तुतिशीलाः those versed in praising, गायकाः singers, वन्दिनः panegyrists, पृथक् पृथक् separately one by one, निगदन्तः reciting audibly, तत् that, पार्थिवनिवेशनम् palace of the king, पर्युपातिष्ठन् reached.
explanation: Then on the following day (unaware of Dasaratha's death) panegyrists uttering benedictions, highly accomplished bards and genealogists proficient in reciting auspicious words, singers versed in musical science reached the palace one after another eulogising the king's glory.
comments: Dasaratha's death -- heartbroken Kausalya and Sumitra -- palace echoes with the lamentations of Dasaratha's wives.

shloka_text: अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां प्रातरेवापरेऽहनि। वन्दिनः पर्युपातिष्ठंस्तत्पार्थिव निवेशनम्।।2.65.1।। सूताः परमसंस्कारा मङ्गलाश्चोत्तमश्रुताः। गायका: स्तुतिशीलाश्च निगदन्तः पृथक् पृथक्।।2.65.2।।
transliteration: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ prātarevāpare'hani| vandinaḥ paryupātiṣṭhaṃstatpārthiva niveśanam sūtāḥ paramasaṃskārā maṅgalāścottamaśrutāḥ| gāyakā: stutiśīlāśca nigadantaḥ pṛthak pṛthak
translation: अथ thereafter, रात्र्याम्  that night, व्यतीतायाम् had passed, अपरे on the following, अहनि day, प्रातः एव in the morning, परमसंस्काराः highly accomplished men, उत्तमश्रुताः proficient in learning, मङ्गलाश्च auspicious men, सूताः genealogists, स्तुतिशीलाः those versed in praising, गायकाः singers, वन्दिनः panegyrists, पृथक् पृथक् separately one by one, निगदन्तः reciting audibly, तत् that, पार्थिवनिवेशनम् palace of the king, पर्युपातिष्ठन् reached.
explanation: Then on the following day (unaware of Dasaratha's death) panegyrists uttering benedictions, highly accomplished bards and genealogists proficient in reciting auspicious words, singers versed in musical science reached the palace one after another eulogising the king's glory.

shloka_text: राजानं स्तुवतां तेषामुदात्ताभिहिताशिषाम्। प्रासादाऽभोगविस्तीर्णः स्तुतिशब्दोह्यवर्तत।।2.65.3।।
transliteration: rājānaṃ stuvatāṃ teṣāmudāttābhihitāśiṣām| prāsādā'bhogavistīrṇaḥ stutiśabdohyavartata
translation: उदात्ताभिहिताशिषाम् uttering benedictions at high pitch, राजानम् the king, स्तुवताम् those who were praising, तेषाम् their, स्तुतिशब्दः song of praise, प्रासादाऽभोगविस्तीर्णः spread over the entire palace, अवर्तत हि pervaded.
explanation: The songs of those who were eulogising the king and uttering benedictions at high pitch pervaded the entire palace.

shloka_text: ततस्तु स्तुवतां तेषां सूतानां पाणिवादकाः। अपदानान्युदाहृत्य पाणिवादा नवादयन्।।2.65.4।।
transliteration: tatastu stuvatāṃ teṣāṃ sūtānāṃ pāṇivādakāḥ| apadānānyudāhṛtya pāṇivādā navādayan
translation: ततः then, तेषां सूतानाम् स्तुवताम् while the bards were singing the praise of the king, पाणिवादकाः those who praise clapping their palms, अवदानानि his wonderful deeds,  उदाहृत्य citing, पाणिवादान् claps, अवादयन् clapped.
explanation: While the bards sang the praise of the king, those who praise clapping their palms  clapped, citing the wonderful deeds of Dasaratha.

shloka_text: तेन शब्देन विहगाः प्रतिबुद्धा विसस्वनुः। शाखास्थाः पञ्जरस्थाश्च ये राजकुलगोचराः।।2.65.5।।
transliteration: tena śabdena vihagāḥ pratibuddhā visasvanuḥ| śākhāsthāḥ pañjarasthāśca ye rājakulagocarāḥ
translation: तेन by that, शब्देन sound, शाखास्थाः some perched on the branches, पञ्जरस्थाः च and some in cages, ये राजकुलगोचराः found all over the palace, विहागाः birds, प्रतिबुद्धा: awoke, विसस्वनुः began to twitter.
explanation: The birds perched on the branches and some in cages awoke and began to twitter all over the palace.

shloka_text: व्याहृताः पुण्यशब्दाश्च वीणानां चापि निस्स्वनाः। आशीर्गेयं च गाथानां पूरयामास वेश्म तत्।।2.65.6।।
transliteration: vyāhṛtāḥ puṇyaśabdāśca vīṇānāṃ cāpi nissvanāḥ| āśīrgeyaṃ ca gāthānāṃ pūrayāmāsa veśma tat
translation: व्याहृताः uttered, पुण्यशब्दाश्च sacred sounds, वीणानाम् of veena, निस्स्वनाः च notes also, गाथानाम् of hymns composed to metre, आशीर्गेयं च benedictory verses, तत् that, वेश्म house, पूरमायास filled.
explanation: The sacred songs of bards and panegyrists, notes of veena, chantings of metrical hymns and benedictory verses filled the palace.

shloka_text: तत श्शुचिसमाचाराः पर्युपस्थानकोविदाः। स्त्रीवर्ष धरभूयिष्ठा उपतस्थुर्यथापुरम्।।2.65.7।।
transliteration: tata śśucisamācārāḥ paryupasthānakovidāḥ| strīvarṣa dharabhūyiṣṭhā upatasthuryathāpuram
translation: ततः then, शुचिसमाचाराः observing purificatory practices, स्त्रीवर्ष धरभूयिष्ठाः many women  and eunuchs, पर्युपस्थानकोविदा: skilled to serve, यथापुरम् as usual, उपतस्थुः assembled.
explanation: Thereafter, as usual, men observing purificatory practices and skilled in royal service  assembled along with women and eunuchs.

shloka_text: हरिचन्दनसम्पृक्तमुदकं काञ्चनैर्घटैः। आनिन्युस्स्नानशिक्षाज्ञा यथाकालं यथाविधि।।2.65.8।।
transliteration: haricandanasampṛktamudakaṃ kāñcanairghaṭaiḥ| āninyussnānaśikṣājñā yathākālaṃ yathāvidhi
translation: स्नानशिक्षाज्ञाः those acquainted with bathing ceremonies, हरिचन्दन सम्पृक्तम् mixed with yellow sandal paste, उदकम् water, काञ्चनैः in golden, घटैः vessels, यथाकालम् at appropriate times, यथाविधि according to tradition, आनिन्युः brought.
explanation: The bathattendants brought water mixed with yellow sandal paste in golden vessels at appropriate times in accordance with tradition.

shloka_text: मङ्गलालम्भनीयानि प्राशनीयान्युपस्करान्। उपनिन्युस्तथाप्यन्याः कुमारीबहुलाः स्त्रियः।।2.65.9।।
transliteration: maṅgalālambhanīyāni prāśanīyānyupaskarān| upaninyustathāpyanyāḥ kumārībahulāḥ striyaḥ
translation: तथा also, अन्याः some other, कुमारीबहुलाः with young maidens in large numbers, स्त्रियः women, मङ्गलालम्भनीयानि auspicious unguents, प्राशनीयाः articles gratifying to the senses, उपस्करान् articles necessary for completion of bathing ritual, उपनिन्युः brought.
explanation: Also, a group of women mostly young maidens brought auspicious unguents, articles gratifying the senses and those necessary accessories for completion of bathing process.

shloka_text: सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नं सर्वं विधिवदर्चितम्। सर्वं सुगुणलक्ष्मीवत्तद्बभूवाभिहारिकम्।।2.65.10।।
transliteration: sarvalakṣaṇasampannaṃ sarvaṃ vidhivadarcitam| sarvaṃ suguṇalakṣmīvattadbabhūvābhihārikam
translation: तत् then, आभिहारिकम्  articles for the king, सर्वम् all, सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नम् were of good quality, विधिवत् as per tradition, अर्चितम् बभूव (आभूत्) was adorable, सर्वम् everything, सुगुणलक्ष्मीवत्  excellent and auspicious
explanation: All the articles brought for the king (for his bath) were presentable and as per tradition. In quality they were excellent and auspicious.

shloka_text: तत स्सूर्योदयं यावत्सर्वं परिसमुत्सुकम्। तस्थावनुपसम्प्राप्तं किंस्विदित्युपशङ्कितम्।।2.65.11।।
transliteration: tata ssūryodayaṃ yāvatsarvaṃ parisamutsukam| tasthāvanupasamprāptaṃ kiṃsvidityupaśaṅkitam
translation: ततः then, सर्वम् all (attendants with necessary preparations), परिसमुत्सुकम् highly  enthusiastic, अनुपसम्प्राप्तम् without reaching the king, किंस्वित् इति as to what had happened, उपशङ्कितम् doubting, सूर्योदयं यावत् until the sunrise, तस्थौ waited.
explanation: All the highly enthusiastic attendants waited for the king till sunrise. Unable to see the king  they doubted about what had happened

shloka_text: अथ याः कोसलेन्द्रस्य शयनं प्रत्यनन्तराः। ताः स्त्रियस्तु समागम्य भर्तारं प्रत्यबोधयन्।।2.65.12।।
transliteration: atha yāḥ kosalendrasya śayanaṃ pratyanantarāḥ| tāḥ striyastu samāgamya bhartāraṃ pratyabodhayan
translation: अथ thereafter, याः स्त्रियः those women, कोशलेन्द्रस्य of the king of Kosala (Dasaratha's), शयनं प्रति attending on the bed, अनन्तराः with unrestricted movement, ताः तु those women, समागम्य on coming near, भर्तारम् that lord, प्रत्यबोधयन् and began waking him up.
explanation: The women who usually attend to the bed (maids who do the bed in the morning) of Dasaratha (king of Kosala) without any restrictions, approached the king and began waking him up.

shloka_text: तथाप्युचितवृत्ता स्ता विनयेन नयेन च। नह्यस्य शयनं स्पृष्ट्वा किञ्चिदप्युपलेभिरे।।2.65.13।।
transliteration: tathāpyucitavṛttā stā vinayena nayena ca| nahyasya śayanaṃ spṛṣṭvā kiñcidapyupalebhire
translation: तथापि even then, विनयेन with restraint, नयेन obediently, उचित वृत्ताः with agreeable  conduct, ताः those women, अस्य Dasratha's, शयनम् bed, स्पृष्ट्वा having touched, किञ्चित् अपि even a little, न उपलेभिरे did not perceive.
explanation: Conducting themselves agreeably with restraint and obedience,  the women touched the bed of Dasaratha but did not perceive any sign of life.

shloka_text: ताः स्त्रियस्स्वप्नशीलज्ञाश्चेष्टासञ्चलनादिषु ता वेपथुपरीताश्च राज्ञः प्राणेषु शङ्किताः। प्रतिस्रोतस्तृणाग्राणां सदृशं सञ्चकाशिरे।।2.65.14।।
transliteration: tāḥ striyassvapnaśīlajñāśceṣṭāsañcalanādiṣu tā vepathuparītāśca rājñaḥ prāṇeṣu śaṅkitāḥ| pratisrotastṛṇāgrāṇāṃ sadṛśaṃ sañcakāśire
translation: ताः स्त्रीयः those women, चेष्टासञ्चलनादिषु in actions, movements, etc, स्वप्नशीलज्ञाः who know the nature of sleeping men, ताः those women, राज्ञः king's, प्राणेषु regarding king's life, शङ्किताः apprehensive of, वेपथुपरीताः च trembling severely, प्रतिस्रोतस्त्रृणाग्राणाम् the tips of reeds standing against the current, सदृशम् like, सञ्चकाशिरे remained.
explanation: Those women knowledgeable in ascertaining the nature of sleep based on the actions, movements, etc. were apprehensive whether the king was  alive or not. Trembling severely  they seemed like the tips of reeds that  stand against the current.

shloka_text: अथ सन्देहमानानां स्त्रीणां दृष्ट्वा च पार्थिवम्। यत्तदाशङ्कितं पापं तस्य जज्ञे विनिश्चयः।।2.65.15।।
transliteration: atha sandehamānānāṃ strīṇāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca pārthivam| yattadāśaṅkitaṃ pāpaṃ tasya jajñe viniścayaḥ
translation: अथ thereafter, पार्थिवम् king, दृष्ट्वा च having seen, सन्देहमानानाम् suspicious, स्त्रीणाम्  women, यत् that, तत् this, पापम् evil, आशङ्कितम् apprehensive, तस्य its, विनिश्चय: certain, जज्ञे became.
explanation: Having seen the king more closely, those women who were apprehensive till then, became certain of the inevitable.

shloka_text: कौसल्या च सुमत्रच पुत्रशोकपराजिते। प्रसुप्ते न प्रबुध्येते यथा कालसमन्विते।।2.65.16।।
transliteration: kausalyā ca sumatraca putraśokaparājite| prasupte na prabudhyete yathā kālasamanvite
translation: पुत्रशोकपराजिते overpowered by grief on account of separation from the son, प्रसुप्ते fast asleep, कौशल्या च Kausalya, सुमित्रा च and Sumitra, कालसमन्विते यथा as if possessed by death, न प्रबुध्येते did not wake up.
explanation: Overpowered by grief on account of separation from their sons, Sumitra and Kausalya were fast asleep and did not wake up as if they were possessed by death.

shloka_text: निष्प्रभा च विवर्णा च सन्ना शोकेन सन्नता। न व्यराजत कौसल्या तारेव तिमिरावृता।।2.65.17।।
transliteration: niṣprabhā ca vivarṇā ca sannā śokena sannatā| na vyarājata kausalyā tāreva timirāvṛtā
translation: निष्प्रभा च dull, विवर्णा pallid, शोकेन due to sorrow, सन्ना sunk down, सन्नता with limbs shrunk, कौशल्या Kausalya, तिमिरावृता enveloped by darkness, तारेव like stars, न व्यराजत did not shine.
explanation: Kausalya, with her face dull and pallid, sank down, her limbs contracted. She looked lustreless like stars enveloped in darkness.

shloka_text: कौसल्याऽनन्तरं राज्ञस्सुमित्रा तदन्तनरम्। न स्म विभ्राजते देवी शोकाश्रुलुलितानना।।2.65.18।।
transliteration: kausalyā'nantaraṃ rājñassumitrā tadantanaram| na sma vibhrājate devī śokāśrululitānanā
translation: राज्ञः of the king , अनन्तरम् by the side, देवी queen, कौशल्या Kausalya, तदन्तरम् next to her immediately, सुमित्रा Sumitra, शोकाश्रुलुलितानना with her face drooping (on account of shedding tears in sorrow), न स्म विभ्राजते devoid of lustre
explanation: There lay Sumitra next to Kausalya by the side of the king. Queen Kausalya's face was dull, drooping  down on account of shedding tears of sorrow.

shloka_text: ते च दृष्ट्वा तथा सुप्ते शुभे देव्यौ च तं नृपम्। सुप्तमेवोद्गतप्राणमन्तःपुरमदृश्यत।।2.65.19।।
transliteration: te ca dṛṣṭvā tathā supte śubhe devyau ca taṃ nṛpam| suptamevodgataprāṇamantaḥpuramadṛśyata
translation: अन्तःपुरम् women in the inner apartment, तथा in that way, सुप्ते asleep, शुभे auspicious, ते देव्यौ the two queens, तम् that, नृपम् king, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सुप्तमेव as if asleep, उद्गत प्राणम् with lifebreath moving upward and leaving him dead, अमन्यत considered.
explanation: Having seen the two auspicious queens asleep, the women in the inner apartment thought the king died in his sleep.

shloka_text: ततः प्रचुक्रुशुर्दीना स्सस्वरं ता वराङ्गनाः। करेणव इवारण्ये स्थानप्रच्युतयूथपाः।।2.65.20।।
transliteration: tataḥ pracukruśurdīnā ssasvaraṃ tā varāṅganāḥ| kareṇava ivāraṇye sthānapracyutayūthapāḥ
translation: ततः then, ताः वराङ्गनाः those women, अरण्ये in the forest, स्थानप्रच्युतयूथपाः the leader of the herd dislodged, करेणवः इव like the female elephants, दीनाः in distress, सस्वरम् loudly, प्रचुक्रुशुः wailed bitterly.
explanation: Then those women bewailed bitterly and loudly in distress like female elephants in the forest when their leader has fallen out of the herd.

shloka_text: तासामाक्रन्दशब्देन सहसोद्धतचेतने। कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च त्यक्त निद्रे बभूवतुः।।2.65.21।।
transliteration: tāsāmākrandaśabdena sahasoddhatacetane| kausalyā ca sumitrā ca tyakta nidre babhūvatuḥ
translation: कौशल्या च Kausalya, सुमित्रा च Sumitra too, तासाम् their, आक्रन्दशब्देन by the sound of  their cries, सहसा suddenly, उद्धतचेतने recovering senses, त्यक्तनिद्रे बभूवतुः deserted their sleep.
explanation: Hearing the lamentations of the women suddenly Kausalya and Sumitra woke up from sleep, their senses recovered.

shloka_text: कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च दृष्ट्वा स्प़ृष्ट्वा च पार्थिवम्। हा नाथेति परिक्रुश्य पेततुर्धरणीतले।।2.65.22।।
transliteration: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca dṛṣṭvā spa़ṛṣṭvā ca pārthivam| hā nātheti parikruśya petaturdharaṇītale
translation: कौशल्याच Kausalya, सुमित्रा च and Sumitra, पार्थिवम् the king,  दृष्ट्वाच having seen,स्पृष्ट्वा च having touched, हा नाथ इति Ah, lord, saying so, परिक्रुश्य crying loudly, धरणीतले on the floor, पेततुः fell down.
explanation: Kausalya and Sumitra looked at the king, touched his body, cried aloud, 'Ah, lord' and collapsed on the floor.

shloka_text: सा कोसलेन्द्रदुहिता वेष्टमाना महीतले। न बभ्राज रजोध्वस्ता तारेव गगनाच्च्युता।।2.65.23।।
transliteration: sā kosalendraduhitā veṣṭamānā mahītale| na babhrāja rajodhvastā tāreva gaganāccyutā
translation: सा that, कोशलेन्द्रदुहिता daughter of the lord of Kosala, Kausalya, महीतले on the ground, वेष्टमाना rolling, रजोध्वस्ता coated with dust, गगनात् from the sky, च्युता fallen down, तारेव like a star, न बभ्राज did not shine.
explanation: Kausalya, daughter of the lord of Kosala, lay on the ground writhing in pain, coated  with dust, and devoid of brightness like a star without radiance fallen from the sky.

shloka_text: नृपे शान्तगुणे जाते कौसल्यां पतितां भुवि। अपश्यंस्ताः स्त्रियः सर्वा हतां नागवधूमिव।।2.65.24।।
transliteration: nṛpe śāntaguṇe jāte kausalyāṃ patitāṃ bhuvi| apaśyaṃstāḥ striyaḥ sarvā hatāṃ nāgavadhūmiva
translation: नृपे when the king, शान्तगुणे जाते with his body lying still, सर्वाः all, ताः स्त्रीयः those women, भुवि on the earth, पतिताम् fallen, कौशल्याम्  at Kausalya, हताम् slain, नागवधूमिव like a female elephant, अपश्यन् beheld.
explanation: Dasaratha with his body lying still, all the women looked at Kausalya fallen down on the floor like a slain female elephant.

shloka_text: ततस्सर्वा नरेन्द्रस्य कैकेयीप्रमुखाः स्त्रियः। रुदन्त्य श्शोकसन्तप्ता निपेतुर्गतचेतनाः।।2.65.25।।
transliteration: tatassarvā narendrasya kaikeyīpramukhāḥ striyaḥ| rudantya śśokasantaptā nipeturgatacetanāḥ
translation: ततः then, कैकेयीप्रमुखाः led by Kaikeyi, नरेन्द्रस्य king's, स्त्रियः other wives, रुदन्त्यः weeping, शोकसन्तप्ताः burning with grief, गतचेतनाः having lost senses, निपेतुः fell down.
explanation: Then all the wives of the king led by Kaikeyi,  burning with grief and weeping, lost their senses and fell down.

shloka_text: ताभिस्स बलवान्नादः क्रोशन्तीभिरनुद्रुतः। येन स्फीतीकृतं भूयस्तद्गृहं समनादयत् ।। 2.65.26 ।।
transliteration: tābhissa balavānnādaḥ krośantībhiranudrutaḥ| yena sphītīkṛtaṃ bhūyastadgṛhaṃ samanādayat
translation: क्रोशन्तीभिः by the wailing ones, ताभिः by those women, अनुद्रुतः followed, बलवान् strong, loud, सः नादः that sound, येन by which, (भूयः) स्फीतीकृतम् made louder, तत् that, गृहम् house (palaces), समनादयत् reverberated.
explanation: The wailings of the women grew louder and louder until the whole palace reverberated with their lamentations.

shloka_text: तत् परित्रस्तन्त्रसम्भ्रान्त पर्युत्सुकजनाकुलम्। सर्वतस्तुमुलाक्रन्दं परितापार्तबान्धवम्।।2.65.27।। सद्यो निपतितानन्दं दीनविक्लबदर्शनम्। बभूव नरदेवस्य सद्म दिष्टान्तमीयुषः।।2.65.28।।
transliteration: tat paritrastantrasambhrānta paryutsukajanākulam| sarvatastumulākrandaṃ paritāpārtabāndhavam sadyo nipatitānandaṃ dīnaviklabadarśanam| babhūva naradevasya sadma diṣṭāntamīyuṣaḥ
translation: दिष्टान्तम् demise, ईयुषः of him who reached, नरदेवस्य king's, तत् सद्म that palace, परित्रस्तन्त्रसम्भ्रान्त पर्युत्सुकजनाकुलम् thronged with anxious people who were exceedingly bewildered and frightened, सर्वतः all over, तुमुलाक्रन्दम् tumultuous with cries of agony, परितापार्तबान्धवम् with relatives anguished with distress, सद्यः at an instant, निपतितानन्दम् joy  vanished, दीनविक्लबदर्शनम् looked miserable with grief, बभूव became.
explanation: On the demise of Dasaratha, joy instantly vanished. The palace was thronged with anxious people who were exceedingly bewildered and frightened. The royal family was anguished with distress. The palace was filled all over with the tumult of cries of agony. And it looked miserable with grief.

shloka_text: तत् परित्रस्तन्त्रसम्भ्रान्त पर्युत्सुकजनाकुलम्। सर्वतस्तुमुलाक्रन्दं परितापार्तबान्धवम्।।2.65.27।। सद्यो निपतितानन्दं दीनविक्लबदर्शनम्। बभूव नरदेवस्य सद्म दिष्टान्तमीयुषः।।2.65.28।।
transliteration: tat paritrastantrasambhrānta paryutsukajanākulam| sarvatastumulākrandaṃ paritāpārtabāndhavam sadyo nipatitānandaṃ dīnaviklabadarśanam| babhūva naradevasya sadma diṣṭāntamīyuṣaḥ
translation: दिष्टान्तम् demise, ईयुषः of him who reached, नरदेवस्य king's, तत् सद्म that palace, परित्रस्तन्त्रसम्भ्रान्त पर्युत्सुकजनाकुलम् thronged with anxious people who were exceedingly bewildered and frightened, सर्वतः all over, तुमुलाक्रन्दम् tumultuous with cries of agony, परितापार्तबान्धवम् with relatives anguished with distress, सद्यः at an instant, निपतितानन्दम् joy  vanished, दीनविक्लबदर्शनम् looked miserable with grief, बभूव became.
explanation: On the demise of Dasaratha, joy instantly vanished. The palace was thronged with anxious people who were exceedingly bewildered and frightened. The royal family was anguished with distress. The palace was filled all over with the tumult of cries of agony. And it looked miserable with grief.

shloka_text: अतीतमाज्ञाय तु पार्थिवर्षभं यशस्विनं सम्परिवार्य पत्नयः। भृशं रुदन्त्यः करुणं सुदुःखिताः प्रगृह्य बाहू व्यलपन्ननाथवत्।।2.65.29।।
transliteration: atītamājñāya tu pārthivarṣabhaṃ yaśasvinaṃ samparivārya patnayaḥ| bhṛśaṃ rudantyaḥ karuṇaṃ suduḥkhitāḥ pragṛhya bāhū vyalapannanāthavat
translation: पत्नयः wives of the king, यशस्विनम् the illustrious, पार्थिवर्षभम् best of kings, अतीतम् him who has passed away, आज्ञाय realising, सम्परिवार्य surrounding him, सुदुःखिताः with intense sorrow, करुणम् piteously, भृशम् bitterly, रुदन्त्यः weeping, बाहू both their arms, प्रगृह्य holding, अनाथवत् like orphans, व्यलपन् bewailed.
explanation: Realising that the great and illustrious king, Dasaratha, had passed away, his wives gathered around him, weeping piteously and bitterly and holding one another's hands  bewailed like orphans. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyfifth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तमग्निमिव संशान्तमम्बुहीनमिवार्णवम्। हतप्रभमिवाऽऽदित्यं स्वर्गस्थं प्रेक्ष्य पार्थिवम्।।2.66.1।। कौसल्या बाष्पपूर्णाक्षी विविधां शोककर्शिता। उपगृह्य शिरो राज्ञः कैकेयीं प्रत्यभाषत।।2.66.2।।
transliteration: tamagnimiva saṃśāntamambuhīnamivārṇavam| hataprabhamivā''dityaṃ svargasthaṃ prekṣya pārthivam kausalyā bāṣpapūrṇākṣī vividhāṃ śokakarśitā| upagṛhya śiro rājñaḥ kaikeyīṃ pratyabhāṣata
translation: संशान्तम् pacified, अग्निमिव like blazing fire, अम्बुहीनम् without water, अर्णवमिव like the ocean, हतप्रभम् bereft of brightness, आदित्यमिव like the Sun, स्वर्गस्थम् ascended heaven, तं पार्थिवम् that king, प्रेक्ष्य on seeing, कौशल्या Kausalya, बाष्पपूर्णाक्षी with her eyes filled with tears, विविधाम् in several ways, शोककर्शिता emaciated with sorrow, राज्ञः king's, शिरः head, उपगृह्य having grasped, कैकेयीं प्रति looking at Kaikeyi, अभाषत uttered.
explanation: On seeing the king who ascended the heaven just as a blazing fire suddenly extinguishes, or like the ocean emptied of water or the Sun bereft of splendour Kausalya raised the head of the king on to her lap, her eyes filled with tears and body shrunk in sorrow, looked at Kaikeyi and said:
comments: Preservation of the king's body awaiting funeral rites -- Ayodhya plunges into darkness with the demise of the king.

shloka_text: तमग्निमिव संशान्तमम्बुहीनमिवार्णवम्। हतप्रभमिवाऽऽदित्यं स्वर्गस्थं प्रेक्ष्य पार्थिवम्।।2.66.1।। कौसल्या बाष्पपूर्णाक्षी विविधां शोककर्शिता। उपगृह्य शिरो राज्ञः कैकेयीं प्रत्यभाषत।।2.66.2।।
transliteration: tamagnimiva saṃśāntamambuhīnamivārṇavam| hataprabhamivā''dityaṃ svargasthaṃ prekṣya pārthivam kausalyā bāṣpapūrṇākṣī vividhāṃ śokakarśitā| upagṛhya śiro rājñaḥ kaikeyīṃ pratyabhāṣata
translation: संशान्तम् pacified, अग्निमिव like blazing fire, अम्बुहीनम् without water, अर्णवमिव like the ocean, हतप्रभम् bereft of brightness, आदित्यमिव like the Sun, स्वर्गस्थम् ascended heaven, तं पार्थिवम् that king, प्रेक्ष्य on seeing, कौशल्या Kausalya, बाष्पपूर्णाक्षी with her eyes filled with tears, विविधाम् in several ways, शोककर्शिता emaciated with sorrow, राज्ञः king's, शिरः head, उपगृह्य having grasped, कैकेयीं प्रति looking at Kaikeyi, अभाषत uttered.
explanation: On seeing the king who ascended the heaven just as a blazing fire suddenly extinguishes, or like the ocean emptied of water or the Sun bereft of splendour Kausalya raised the head of the king on to her lap, her eyes filled with tears and body shrunk in sorrow, looked at Kaikeyi and said:

shloka_text: सकामा भव कैकेयि भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यमकण्टकम्। त्यक्त्वा राजानमेकाग्रा नृशंसे दुष्टचारिणि।।2.66.3।।
transliteration: sakāmā bhava kaikeyi bhuṅkṣva rājyamakaṇṭakam| tyaktvā rājānamekāgrā nṛśaṃse duṣṭacāriṇi
translation: नृशंसे O cruel one, दुष्टचारिणि O perverse wretch, कैकेयि O Kaikeyi, सकामा भव remain with your wishes fulfilled, राजानम् king, त्यक्त्वा forsaking, एकाग्रा with one objective, अकण्टकम् without any obstacle, राज्यम् kingdom, भुङ्क्ष्व enjoy.
explanation: O cruel one O perverse wretch, O Kaikeyi, your wishes have been fulfilled. You have forsaken the king, that was your only objective. (Now) enjoy the kingdom alone without any obstacles on your way.

shloka_text: विहाय मां गतो रामः भर्ता च स्वर्गतो मम। विपथे सार्थहीनेव नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे।।2.66.4।।
transliteration: vihāya māṃ gato rāmaḥ bhartā ca svargato mama| vipathe sārthahīneva nāhaṃ jīvitumutsahe
translation: रामः Rama, माम् me, विहाय having left, गतः has gone, मम my, भर्ता च lord also, स्वर्गतः has  ascended heaven, विपथे on a wrong path, सार्थहीनेव without wellwishers अहम् I, जीवितुम् to live, न उत्सहे do not desire.
explanation: Rama has gone away leaving me. My lord has ascended the heaven, traversing the wrong road. With my wellwishers gone, I do not want to live.

shloka_text: भर्तारं तं परित्यज्य का स्त्री दैवतमात्मनः। इच्छेज्जीवितुमन्यत्र कैकेय्यास्त्यक्तधर्मणः।।2.66.5।।
transliteration: bhartāraṃ taṃ parityajya kā strī daivatamātmanaḥ| icchejjīvitumanyatra kaikeyyāstyaktadharmaṇaḥ
translation: त्यक्तधर्मणः one who has abandoned righteousness, कैकेय्याः अन्यत्र other than Kaikeyi, का स्त्री which woman, आत्मनः her own, दैवतम् god, तं भर्तारम् her husband, परित्यज्य having abandoned, जीवितुम् to live, इच्छेत् desires.
explanation: Which woman wishes to live, leaving her godlike husband, except Kaikeyi who has given up her sense of duty?

shloka_text: न लुब्धो बुध्यते दोषान् किम्पाकमिव भक्षयन्। कुब्जानिमित्तं कैकेय्या राघवाणां कुलं हतम्।।2.66.6।।
transliteration: na lubdho budhyate doṣān kimpākamiva bhakṣayan| kubjānimittaṃ kaikeyyā rāghavāṇāṃ kulaṃ hatam
translation: लुब्ध: a greedy man, किम्पाकम् a poisonous fruit of bad taste, भक्षयन्निव as if one has eaten, दोषान् faults, न बुध्यते does not know, कुब्जानिमित्तम् on account of the hunchback, कैकेय्या by Kaikeyi, राघवाणाम् of Raghus, कुलम् race, हतम् is destroyed.
explanation: Like a greedy man who eats the (poisonous) kimpaka fruit without realising the defects of the fruit, Kaikeyi has destroyed the Raghu race on account of the hunchback (Manthara).

shloka_text: अनियोगे नियुक्तेन राज्ञा रामं विवासितम्। सभार्यं जनकश्श्रुत्वा परितप्स्यत्यहं यथा।।2.66.7।।
transliteration: aniyoge niyuktena rājñā rāmaṃ vivāsitam| sabhāryaṃ janakaśśrutvā paritapsyatyahaṃ yathā
translation: सभार्यम् with wife, रामम् Rama, अनियोगे is an unworthy act, नियुक्तेन ordered, राज्ञा by the king, विवासितम् has been banished, श्रुत्वा having heard, जनकः Janaka, अहं यथा like me, परितप्स्यति will suffer.
explanation: Hearing the unrighteous action ordered by the king in banishing Rama and his wife  king Janaka will suffer great agony like me.

shloka_text: स मामनाथां विधवां नाद्य जानाति धार्मिकः। रामः कमलपत्राक्षः जीवन्नाशमितो गतः।।2.66.8।।
transliteration: sa māmanāthāṃ vidhavāṃ nādya jānāti dhārmikaḥ| rāmaḥ kamalapatrākṣaḥ jīvannāśamito gataḥ
translation: धार्मिकः virtuous, कमलपत्राक्षः who has lotuspetal like eyes, जीवन् even though alive, इतः from here, नाशम् destruction, गतः obtained, सः रामः that Rama, अद्य now, माम् me, अनाथाम्  without protector, विधवाम् without husband, न जानाति does not know.
explanation: That virtuous Rama of lotuspetaleyes has left this place for good, and does not know that I am without a protector, being a widow now.

shloka_text: विदेहराजस्य सुता तथा सीता तपस्विनी। दुःखस्यानुचिता दुःखं वने पर्युद्विजिष्यति।।2.66.9।।
transliteration: videharājasya sutā tathā sītā tapasvinī| duḥkhasyānucitā duḥkhaṃ vane paryudvijiṣyati
translation: तथा also, तपस्विनी a miserable woman, दुःखस्य of hardships, अनुचिता unworthy, विदेहराजस्य king Videha's, सुता daughter, सीता Sita, वने in the forest, दुःखम् great sorrow, पर्युद्विजिष्यति will be agitated in her mind.
explanation: In the same way Sita, daughter of the king of Videha, who does not deserve hardships will be in deep agony.

shloka_text: नदतां भीमघोषाणां निशासु मृगपक्षिणाम्। निशम्य नूनं सन्त्रस्ता राघवं संश्रयिष्यति।।2.66.10।।
transliteration: nadatāṃ bhīmaghoṣāṇāṃ niśāsu mṛgapakṣiṇām| niśamya nūnaṃ santrastā rāghavaṃ saṃśrayiṣyati
translation: निशाम् at night, भीमघोषाणाम् ghastly sounds, मृगपक्षिणाम् of animals and birds, नदताम् by those making sounds, निशम्य having heard, सन्त्रस्ता frightened, नूनम्  surely, राघवम् Rama, संश्रयिष्यति will take shelter.
explanation: Hearing the ghastly sounds of animals and birds, Sita will surely get frightened and take shelter in Rama.

shloka_text: वृद्धश्चैवाल्पपुत्रश्च वैदेहीमनुचिन्तयन्। सोऽपि शोकसमाविष्टो ननु त्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्।।2.66.11।।
transliteration: vṛddhaścaivālpaputraśca vaidehīmanucintayan| so'pi śokasamāviṣṭo nanu tyakṣyati jīvitam
translation: वृद्धश्चैव aged, अल्पपुत्रश्च not having sons, सोऽपि that Janaka too, शोकसमाविष्टः  overpowered by grief, वैदेहीम् Sita, अनुचिन्तयन् constantly thinking, जीवितम् life, त्यक्ष्यति ननु will give up indeed.
explanation: Old and sonless Janaka, constantly thinking of Sita and overpowered with grief will surely give up his life.

shloka_text: साऽहमद्यैव दिष्टान्तं गमिष्यामि पतिव्रता। इदं शरीर मालिङ्ग्य प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम्।।2.66.12।।
transliteration: sā'hamadyaiva diṣṭāntaṃ gamiṣyāmi pativratā| idaṃ śarīra māliṅgya pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam
translation: पतिव्रता of faithful wife, सा अहम् such as myself, अद्यैव now itself, दिष्टान्तम् death, गमिष्यामि will go to, इदम् this, शरीरम् body, आलिङ्ग्य clasping, हुताशनम् in the fire, प्रवेक्ष्यामि I shall enter.
explanation: As his faithful wife, I shall enter the fire by clasping this (Dasaratha's) body and go to  death today itself

shloka_text: तां ततस्सम्परिष्वज्य विलपन्तीं तपस्विनीम्। व्यपनीय सुदुःखार्तां कौसल्यां व्यावहारिकाः।।2.66.13।।
transliteration: tāṃ tatassampariṣvajya vilapantīṃ tapasvinīm| vyapanīya suduḥkhārtāṃ kausalyāṃ vyāvahārikāḥ
translation: व्यावहारिकाः maidservants (those who customarily attend on the queens), सम्परिष्वज्य  having embraced, विलपन्तीम् lamenting, तपस्विनीम् unfortunate, सुदुःखार्ताम् deeply distressed, तां कौशल्याम् to that Kausaya, ततः from there, व्यपनीय removed.
explanation: The servants led away that unfortunate Kausalya who was lamenting in great anguish  embracing the body of Dasaratha.

shloka_text: तैलद्रोण्यामथामात्या सम्वेश्य जगतीपतिम्। राज्ञस्सर्वाण्यथादिष्टाश्चक्रुः कर्माण्यनन्तरम्।।2.66.14।।
transliteration: tailadroṇyāmathāmātyā samveśya jagatīpatim| rājñassarvāṇyathādiṣṭāścakruḥ karmāṇyanantaram
translation: अथ thereafter, आदिष्टाः having been instructed, अमात्याः counsellors, जगतीपतिम् the (corpse) of the lord of the world (Dasartha), तैलद्रोण्याम् in an oil tub, संवेश्य keeping, अनन्तरम् thereafter, कर्माणि ceremonies, सर्वाणि all, चक्रुः performed.
explanation: The counsellors, instructed (by Vasistha and others), placed the king's body in an oil tub with the understanding that the funeral rites were to be performed hereafter.

shloka_text: न तु सङ्कलनं राज्ञो विना पुत्रेण मन्त्रिणः। सर्वज्ञाः कर्तुमीषुस्ते ततो रक्षन्ति भूमिपम्।।2.66.15।।
transliteration: na tu saṅkalanaṃ rājño vinā putreṇa mantriṇaḥ| sarvajñāḥ kartumīṣuste tato rakṣanti bhūmipam
translation: सर्वज्ञाः conversant with all such matters (relating to the obsequies), मन्त्रिणः counsellors, विना पुत्रेण without sons, राज्ञः king's, सङ्कलनम् funeral obsequies, कर्तुम् to do, न ईषुः did not desire, ततः then, भूमिपम् king's body, रक्षन्ति they are protecting.
explanation: The counsellors who were acquainted with all such matters (relating to the king's funeral) were unwilling to perform the obsequies in the absence of any of the king's sons. Meanwhile, they kept watch over the deadbody of the king.

shloka_text: तैलद्रोण्यां तु सचिवैश्शायितं तं नराधिपम्। हा मृतोऽयमिति ज्ञात्वा स्त्रियस्ताः पर्यदेवयन्।।2.66.16।।
transliteration: tailadroṇyāṃ tu sacivaiśśāyitaṃ taṃ narādhipam| hā mṛto'yamiti jñātvā striyastāḥ paryadevayan
translation: सचिवैः by counsellors, तैलद्रोण्याम् in the oil vat, शायितम् made to lay down, तं नराधिपम् that king, ज्ञात्वा on knowing (having seen), हा alas, अयम् this, मृतः is dead, इति in this way, ताः those, स्त्रियः women, पर्यदेवयन् cried.
explanation: On seeing the king's body laid in the oil vat by the counsellors, the women cried  Alas, the king is dead.

shloka_text: बाहूनुद्यम्य कृपणाः नेत्रप्रस्रवणैर्मुखैः। रुदन्त्य श्शोकसन्तप्ताः कृपणं पर्यदेवयन्।।2.66.17।।
transliteration: bāhūnudyamya kṛpaṇāḥ netraprasravaṇairmukhaiḥ| rudantya śśokasantaptāḥ kṛpaṇaṃ paryadevayan
translation: नेत्रप्रस्रवणैः tears flowing from their eyes, मुखैः with faces, कृपणाः piteously, बाहून् hands, उद्यम्य raising, रुदन्त्यः groaning, शोकसन्तप्ताः burning in grief, कृपणम् helplessly, पर्यदेवयन् lamented.
explanation: With tears flowing down their faces, piteously raising their arms, groaning in their burning grief, the women lamented helplessly.

shloka_text: हा महाराज रामेण सततं प्रियवादिना। विहीनास्सत्यसन्धेन किमर्थं विजहासि नः।।2.66.18।।
transliteration: hā mahārāja rāmeṇa satataṃ priyavādinā| vihīnāssatyasandhena kimarthaṃ vijahāsi naḥ
translation: हा महाराज Alas, the great king, सततम् always, प्रियवादिना by a man speaking pleasing words, सत्यसन्धेन by one firm in promise, रामेण by Rama, विहीनाः deprived of, नः us, किमर्थम् why, विजहासि are you leaving us?
explanation: When we were already deprived of Rama who was always pleasing and truthful, alas, o great king, why did you leave us?

shloka_text: कैकेय्या दुष्टभावायाः राघवेण वियोजिताः। कथं पतिघ्नया वत्स्याम स्समीपे विधवा वयम्।।2.66.19।।
transliteration: kaikeyyā duṣṭabhāvāyāḥ rāghaveṇa viyojitāḥ| kathaṃ patighnayā vatsyāma ssamīpe vidhavā vayam
translation: राघवेण by Rama, वियोजिताः separated, वयम् we, विधवाः widows, दुष्टभावायाः one of evil intentions, पतिघ्नयाः slayer of husband, कैकेय्याः Kaikeyi, समीपे near, कथम् how?, वत्स्याघ्नयाम can we stay?
explanation: A woman of evil intentions, Kaikeyi, at first separated us from Rama. Now she deprived us of our husband. How can we live with one who is a slayer of her husband?

shloka_text: स हि नाथस्सदास्माकं तव च प्रभुरात्मवान्। वनं रामो गतश्श्रीमान्विहाय नृपतिश्रियम्।।2.66.20।।
transliteration: sa hi nāthassadāsmākaṃ tava ca prabhurātmavān| vanaṃ rāmo gataśśrīmānvihāya nṛpatiśriyam
translation: अस्माकम् for us, तव च to you also, सदा always, नाथः protector, प्रभुः master, आत्मवान्  selfpossessed, श्रीमान् prosperous, सः that, रामः Rama, नृपतिश्रियम् royal wealth, विहाय leaving, वनम् to the forest, गतः हि has gone indeed.
explanation: Rama, who was always our and your selfpossessed master and protector has gone to the forest, indeed, abandoning royal wealth.

shloka_text: त्वया तेन च वीरेण विना व्यसनमोहिताः। कथं वयं निवत्स्यामः कैकेय्या च विदूषिताः।।2.66.21।।
transliteration: tvayā tena ca vīreṇa vinā vyasanamohitāḥ| kathaṃ vayaṃ nivatsyāmaḥ kaikeyyā ca vidūṣitāḥ
translation: त्वया विना without you, तेन वीरेण विना without that hero, व्यसनमोहिताः overwhelmed with grief, वयम् we, कैकेय्या by Kaikeyi, विदूषिताः च having being abused, कथम् how, निवत्स्यामः can we live?
explanation: Without you and without the heroic Rama, how can we live overwhelmed with grief and enduring the abuses of Kaikeyi?

shloka_text: यया तु राजा रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः। सीतया सह सन्त्यक्ता स्साकमन्यं न हास्यति।।2.66.22।।
transliteration: yayā tu rājā rāmaśca lakṣmaṇaśca mahābalaḥ| sītayā saha santyaktā ssākamanyaṃ na hāsyati
translation: यया by such a person (Kaikeyi), राजा the king, रामश्च Rama, महाबलः valiant, लक्ष्मणश्च  also Lakshmana, सीतया सह along with Sita, सन्त्यक्ताः have been abandoned, सा that Kaikeyi, अन्यम् other, कम् whom, न हास्यति will not cast aside?
explanation: Why will not Kaikeyi who has abandoned the king, valiant Rama and Lakshmana along with Sita cast aside others?

shloka_text: ता बाष्पेण च संवीताश्शोकेन विपुलेन च। व्यवेष्टन्त निरानन्दा राघवस्य वरस्त्रियः।।2.66.23।।
transliteration: tā bāṣpeṇa ca saṃvītāśśokena vipulena ca| vyaveṣṭanta nirānandā rāghavasya varastriyaḥ
translation: राघवस्य Dasaratha's, ताः वरस्त्रियः those excellent wives, बाष्पेण shedding tears, विपुलेन  with profound, शोकेन च grief, संवीताः overwhelmed, निरानन्दाः cheerlessly, व्यवेष्टन्त are lying unconscious on the  floor.
explanation: The excellent wives of Dasaratha, overwhelmed with profound grief and tears, are  lying unconcious on the floor.
