shloka_text: निशा चन्द्रविहीनेव स्त्रीव भर्तृविवर्जिता। पुरी नाराजतायोध्या हीना राज्ञा महात्मना।।2.66.24।।
transliteration: niśā candravihīneva strīva bhartṛvivarjitā| purī nārājatāyodhyā hīnā rājñā mahātmanā
translation: महात्मना by the great, राज्ञा king, हीना deprived, अयोध्यापुरी city of Ayodhya, चन्द्रविहीना devoid of moon, निशेव night, भर्तृविवर्जिता forsaken by husband, स्त्रीव like woman, नाराजत  did not shine.
explanation: Like night without the Moon, like a woman forsaken by her husband, this city of Ayodhya without that magnanimous king has lost its earlier splendour.

shloka_text: बाष्पपर्याकुलजना हाहाभूतकुलाङ्गना। शून्यचत्वरवेश्मान्ता न बभ्राज यथापुरम्।।2.66.25।।
transliteration: bāṣpaparyākulajanā hāhābhūtakulāṅganā| śūnyacatvaraveśmāntā na babhrāja yathāpuram
translation: बाष्पपर्याकुलजना filled with people shedding tears, हाहाभूतकुलाङ्गना with the cries of anguish of housewives, शून्यचत्वरवेश्मान्ता infront of their houses and the public squares in between the houses, यथा पुरम् city with its earlier brilliance, न बभ्राज does not shine.
explanation: With the people of Ayodhya shedding tears, the housewives crying, in anguish, 'alas alas' the courtyards houses and squares of the roads deserted, the city has lost its earlier brilliance.

shloka_text: गते तु शोकात् त्रिदिवं नराधिपे महीतलस्थासु नृपाङ्गनासु च। निवृत्तचारस्सहसा गतो रविः प्रवृत्तचारा रजनी ह्युपस्थिता।।2.66.26।।
transliteration: gate tu śokāt tridivaṃ narādhipe mahītalasthāsu nṛpāṅganāsu ca| nivṛttacārassahasā gato raviḥ pravṛttacārā rajanī hyupasthitā
translation: नराधिपे when the king, शोकात् due to grief, त्रिदिवम् towards heaven, गते तु having gone, नृपाङ्गनासु wives of the king, महीतलस्थासु च lying on the ground, रविः the Sun, सहसा instantly, निवृत्तचारः ceased his journey, गतः gone, प्रवृत्तचाराः favourable to nightrangers, रजनी night, उपस्थिता set in.
explanation: When king Dasaratha ascended to heaven due to grief over his son and when his wives were lying on the ground, the Sun ceased his journey and the night favourable to creatures of darkness suddenly set in.

shloka_text: ऋते तु पुत्राद्धहनं महीपतेर्नरोचयन्ते सुहृदस्समागताः। इतीव तस्मिन् शयने न्यवेशयन् वनिचिन्त्य राजानमचिन्त्य दर्शनम्।।2.66.27।।
transliteration: ṛte tu putrāddhahanaṃ mahīpaternarocayante suhṛdassamāgatāḥ| itīva tasmin śayane nyaveśayan vanicintya rājānamacintya darśanam
translation: समागताः people who assembled there, सुहृदः friends, पुत्रात् ऋते in the absence of a son, महीपतेः king's, दहनम् for igniting funeral pyre, न रोचयन्ते do not agree, इतीव thus, विचिन्त्य  having thought, अचिन्त्य दर्शनम् in an unexpected form, राजानम् king, तस्मिन् शयने on that bed (in that oil trough), न्यवेशयन् laid.
explanation: The wellwishers who asembled, unwilling to ignite the funeral pyre of the king in the absence of any one of his sons laid the king's deadbody in that oil trough in an unexpected manner.

shloka_text: गतप्रभा द्यौरिव भास्करं विना व्यपेतनक्षत्रगणेव शर्वरी। पुरी बभासे रहिता महात्मना न चास्रकण्ठाऽकुलमार्गचत्वरा।।2.66.28।।
transliteration: gataprabhā dyauriva bhāskaraṃ vinā vyapetanakṣatragaṇeva śarvarī| purī babhāse rahitā mahātmanā na cāsrakaṇṭhā'kulamārgacatvarā
translation: महात्मना by the great Dasaratha, रहिता bereft of, अस्रकण्ठाकुलमार्गचत्वरा courtyards in front of their houses and the squares on the roads filled with people sobbing, पुरी Ayodhya, भास्करं विना without the Sun, द्यौरिव like the sky, व्यपेतनक्षत्रगणाः with crowds of stars, शर्वरीव like night, गतप्रभा having lost the brightness, न बभासे did not shine.
explanation: The city, bereft of illustrious Dasaratha was filled with people sobbing in the courtyards in front of their houses and in the squares in between. That city of Ayodhya bereft of brightness, appeared like the day without the Sun and the night without constellations of stars.

shloka_text: नराश्च नार्यश्च समेत्य सङ्घशः विगर्हमाणा भरतस्य मातरम्। तदा नगर्यां नरदेवसङ्क्षये बभूवुरार्ता न च शर्म लेभिरे।।2.66.29।।
transliteration: narāśca nāryaśca sametya saṅghaśaḥ vigarhamāṇā bharatasya mātaram| tadā nagaryāṃ naradevasaṅkṣaye babhūvurārtā na ca śarma lebhire
translation: तदा then, नरदेवसङ्क्षये after the demise of the king, नगर्याम् in the city, नराश्च men, नार्यश्च women, सङ्घशः in groups, समेत्य assembled, भरतस्य Bharata's, मातरम् mother, विगर्हमाणाः denounced, आर्ताः बभूवुः became extremely distressed, शर्म peace, न च लेभिरे did not have
explanation: After the demise of the king, men and women in the city assembled in groups and denounced the mother of Bharata. Extremely distressed, they had no peace of mind. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtysixth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: आक्रन्दितनिरानन्दा सास्रकण्ठजनाकुला। अयोध्यायामवतता सा व्यतीयाय शर्वरी।।2.67.1।।
transliteration: ākranditanirānandā sāsrakaṇṭhajanākulā| ayodhyāyāmavatatā sā vyatīyāya śarvarī
translation: अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, आक्रन्दितनिरानन्दा rendered cheerless by the lamentations, सास्रकण्ठजनाकुला filled with sobbing people, अवतताः stretched interminably, सा शर्वरी that night, व्यतीयाय passed away.
explanation: The night stretched interminably in Ayodhya, which was filled with sobbing people  rendered cheerless by their lamentations.
comments: Ministers and brahmins speak about the miserable state of a kingdom without king -- urge Vasistha to name the heir apparent for Ayodhya.

shloka_text: व्यतीतायां तु शर्वर्यामादित्यस्योदये ततः। समेत्य राजकर्तारः सभामीयुर्द्विजातयः।।2.67.2।।
transliteration: vyatītāyāṃ tu śarvaryāmādityasyodaye tataḥ| sametya rājakartāraḥ sabhāmīyurdvijātayaḥ
translation: ततः then, शर्वर्याम् when the night, व्यतीतायां तु passed, आदित्यस्य उदये at sunrise, राजकर्तारः those who perform royal investiture, द्विजातयः brahmins, समेत्य having been called, सभाम् assembly hall, ईयुः reached.
explanation: When the night finally ended and after the sunrise next day, the brahmins who perform royal investiture having been called and reached the assembly hall.

shloka_text: मार्कण्डेयोऽथ मौद्गल्यो वामदेवश्च काश्यपः। कात्यायनो गौतमश्च जाबालिश्च महायशाः।।2.67.3।। एते द्विजा स्सहामात्यैः पृथग्वा च मुदीरयन्। वसिष्ठमेवाभिमुखाः श्रेष्ठं राजपुरोहितम्।।2.67.4।।
transliteration: mārkaṇḍeyo'tha maudgalyo vāmadevaśca kāśyapaḥ| kātyāyano gautamaśca jābāliśca mahāyaśāḥ ete dvijā ssahāmātyaiḥ pṛthagvā ca mudīrayan| vasiṣṭhamevābhimukhāḥ śreṣṭhaṃ rājapurohitam
translation: मार्कण्डेयः Markandeya, अथ and, मौद्गल्यः Maudgalya, अथ also, काश्यपः Kasyapa, कात्यायनः Katyayana, गौतमश्च Gautama also, महायशाः of great renown, जाबालिश्च Jabali too, एते  these, द्विजाः brahmins, अमात्यैः सह with ministers, श्रेष्ठम् the chief, राजपुरोहितम् king's priest, वसिष्ठमेव Vasistha himself, अभिमुखाः approached, पृथक् different, वाचम् opinions  उदीरयन् expressed.
explanation: Markandeya, Maudgalya, Kasyapa, Katyayana, Gautama, Jabali of great renown   accompanied by ministers and brahmins approached Vasistha, the chief  priest of the king and expressed different opinions (on the investiture).

shloka_text: मार्कण्डेयोऽथ मौद्गल्यो वामदेवश्च काश्यपः। कात्यायनो गौतमश्च जाबालिश्च महायशाः।।2.67.3।। एते द्विजा स्सहामात्यैः पृथग्वा च मुदीरयन्। वसिष्ठमेवाभिमुखाः श्रेष्ठं राजपुरोहितम्।।2.67.4।।
transliteration: mārkaṇḍeyo'tha maudgalyo vāmadevaśca kāśyapaḥ| kātyāyano gautamaśca jābāliśca mahāyaśāḥ ete dvijā ssahāmātyaiḥ pṛthagvā ca mudīrayan| vasiṣṭhamevābhimukhāḥ śreṣṭhaṃ rājapurohitam
translation: मार्कण्डेयः Markandeya, अथ and, मौद्गल्यः Maudgalya, अथ also, काश्यपः Kasyapa, कात्यायनः Katyayana, गौतमश्च Gautama also, महायशाः of great renown, जाबालिश्च Jabali too, एते  these, द्विजाः brahmins, अमात्यैः सह with ministers, श्रेष्ठम् the chief, राजपुरोहितम् king's priest, वसिष्ठमेव Vasistha himself, अभिमुखाः approached, पृथक् different, वाचम् opinions  उदीरयन् expressed.
explanation: Markandeya, Maudgalya, Kasyapa, Katyayana, Gautama, Jabali of great renown   accompanied by ministers and brahmins approached Vasistha, the chief  priest of the king and expressed different opinions (on the investiture).

shloka_text: अतीता शर्वरी दुःखं या नो वर्षशतोपमा। अस्मिन्पञ्चत्वमापन्ने पुत्रशोकेन पार्थिवे।।2.67.5।।
transliteration: atītā śarvarī duḥkhaṃ yā no varṣaśatopamā| asminpañcatvamāpanne putraśokena pārthive
translation: अस्मिन् पार्थिवे this king, पुत्रशोकेन out of grief over (seperation from) his son, पञ्चत्वम् dissolution into the five elements (death), आपन्ने having attained, या that night, नः for us, वर्षशतोपमा like a hundred years, शर्वरी such night, दुःखम्  sorrowful, अतीता passed.
explanation: While king Dasaratha died on account of grief over (separation from) his son and rejoined the five elements, the sorrowful night seemed like a hundred years for us. (commented the assembly of ministers).

shloka_text: स्वर्गतश्च महाराजो रामश्चारण्यमाश्रितः। लक्ष्मणश्चापि तेजस्वी रामेणैव गतस्सह।।2.67.6।।
transliteration: svargataśca mahārājo rāmaścāraṇyamāśritaḥ| lakṣmaṇaścāpi tejasvī rāmeṇaiva gatassaha
translation: महाराजः the great king, स्वर्गतश्च had attained heaven, रामश्च Rama also, अरण्यम् in the forest, आश्रितः taken refuge, तेजस्वी lustrous, लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana, रामेणैव सह with Rama, गतः went.
explanation: The great king has attained heaven, Rama has taken refuge in the forest and brilliant Lakshmana has also gone with Rama.

shloka_text: उभौ भरतशत्रुघ्नौ केकयेषु परन्तपौ। पुरे राजगृहे रम्ये मातामहनिवेशने।।2.67.7।।
transliteration: ubhau bharataśatrughnau kekayeṣu parantapau| pure rājagṛhe ramye mātāmahaniveśane
translation: परन्तपौ destroyers of enemies, भरतशत्रुघ्नौ Bharata and Satrughna, उभौ both, केकयेषु in the Kekaya kingdom, राजगृहे at Rajagriha, पुरे city, रम्ये beautiful, मातामहनिवेशने are in maternal grandfather's palace.
explanation: Bharata and Satrughna, destroyers of enemies, are at the beautiful city of Rajagriha in the Kekaya kingdom, the palace of their maternal grandfather's palace.

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकूणामिहाद्यैव कश्चिद्राजा विधीयताम्। अराजकं हि नो राष्ट्रं विनाशं समवाप्नुयात्।।2.67.8।।
transliteration: ikṣvākūṇāmihādyaiva kaścidrājā vidhīyatām| arājakaṃ hi no rāṣṭraṃ vināśaṃ samavāpnuyāt
translation: इक्ष्वाकूणाम् in the race of Ikshvakus, कश्चित् anyone, इह here, अद्यैव right now, राजा as king, विधीयताम् should be made, अराजकम् without a king, नः our, राष्ट्रम् country, विनाशम्  destruction, (सम् अव) आप्नुयात् will attain.
explanation: Therefore, let someone from the race of Ikshvakus be appointed king right now.  since without a king, the country will be destroyed.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे विद्युन्माली महास्वनः। अभिवर्षति पर्जन्यो महीं दिव्येन वारिणा।।2.67.9।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade vidyunmālī mahāsvanaḥ| abhivarṣati parjanyo mahīṃ divyena vāriṇā
translation: अराजके where there is no king, जनपदे in a country, विद्युन्माली garlanded with a row of lightning, महास्वनः thunderous, पर्जन्यः raingod, महीम् the earth, दिव्येन with celestial, वारिणा with rain, नाभिवर्षति does not shower.
explanation: In a country without a king, thunderous clouds garlanded by lightning would no longer water the earth with celestial showers.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे बीजमुष्टिः प्रकीर्यते। नाराजके पितुः पुत्रो भार्या वा वर्तते वशे।।2.67.10।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade bījamuṣṭiḥ prakīryate| nārājake pituḥ putro bhāryā vā vartate vaśe
translation: अराजके where there is no king, जनपदे in a country, बीजमुष्टिः handfuls of seeds, न प्रकीर्यते will not be sown (sprout), अराजके where there no king, पुत्र: son, भार्या वा or wife, पितुः father's, वशे control, न वर्तते do not remain.
explanation: Where there is no king, even a handful of seeds will not be sown (will not sprout). In a kingless kingdom, a son or a wife will not obey the father (head of the family).

shloka_text: नाराजके धनं चास्ति नास्ति भार्या प्यराजके। इद मत्याहितं चान्यत्कुतस्सत्य मराजके।।2.67.11।।
transliteration: nārājake dhanaṃ cāsti nāsti bhāryā pyarājake| ida matyāhitaṃ cānyatkutassatya marājake
translation: अराजके when there is no king, धनम् wealth, नास्ति not, अराजके without a king, भार्यापि even wife, नास्ति is not, अत्याहितम् cause of great peril, अन्यत् another, इदं च this one also exists, अराजके where there no king, सत्यम् truth, कुतः where?
explanation: In a kingdom without a king wealth cannot be preserved, no wife would like to stay (with her husband). There is one more cause for a great peril, that is, there is no place for truth in a country (where there is no king).

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे कारयन्ति सभां नराः। उद्यानानि च रम्याणि हृष्टाः पुण्यगृहाणि च।।2.67.12।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade kārayanti sabhāṃ narāḥ| udyānāni ca ramyāṇi hṛṣṭāḥ puṇyagṛhāṇi ca
translation: अराजके where there is no king, जनपदे in a country, नराः people, हृष्टाः rejoiced, सभाम्  assembly, रम्याणि delightful, उद्यानानि gardens, पुण्यगृहाणि sacred edifices (like temples), न कारयन्ति are not built.
explanation: In a country where there is no king, no assemblies are convened by pleasure seeking people, nor do they build delightful gardens or sacred edifices.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे यज्ञशीला द्विजातयः। सत्राण्यन्वासते दान्ता ब्राह्मणा स्संशितव्रताः।।2.67.13।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade yajñaśīlā dvijātayaḥ| satrāṇyanvāsate dāntā brāhmaṇā ssaṃśitavratāḥ
translation: अराजके without a king, जनपदे in a country, यज्ञशीलाः where sacrificial ceremonies are conducted, दान्ताः selfcontrolled, ब्राह्मणाः versed in the study of Vedas, संशितव्रताः of rigorous austerity, द्विजातयः brahmins, सत्राणि sacrifices, न अन्वासते do not practise.
explanation: In a country without a king, selfcontrolled brahmins in charge of sacrificial ceremonies, wellversed in the study of Vedas and strict followers of  austerity will not function.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे महायज्ञेषु यज्वनः। ब्राह्मणा वसुसम्पन्ना विसृजन्त्याप्तदक्षिणाः।।2.67.14।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade mahāyajñeṣu yajvanaḥ| brāhmaṇā vasusampannā visṛjantyāptadakṣiṇāḥ
translation: अराजके without a king, जनपदे in a country, महायज्ञेषु in great sacrifices, यज्वनः the officiating priests, वसुसम्पन्नाः wealthy, ब्राह्मणाः brahmins, आप्तदक्षिणाः abundant gifts, न विसृजन्ति do not offer.
explanation: In a country without a king wealthy brahmins, who have performed great sacrifices, do not offer abundance of gifts to the officiating priests.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे प्रभूतनटनर्तकाः। उत्सवाश्च समाजाश्च वर्धन्ते राष्ट्रवर्धनाः।।2.67.15।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade prabhūtanaṭanartakāḥ| utsavāśca samājāśca vardhante rāṣṭravardhanāḥ
translation: अराजके where there is no king, जनपदे in a country, प्रभूतनटनर्तकाः actors and dancers in large numbers, राष्ट्रवर्धनाः promoting the welfare of the country, उत्सवाश्च celebrations, समाजाश्च assemblies, न वर्धन्ते do not prosper.
explanation: In a country without a king, celebrations of associations promoting the welfare of the country, actors and dancers in large numbers do not prosper.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे सिद्धार्था व्यवहारिणः। कथाभिरनुरज्यन्ते कथाशीलाः कथाप्रियैः।।2.67.16।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade siddhārthā vyavahāriṇaḥ| kathābhiranurajyante kathāśīlāḥ kathāpriyaiḥ
translation: अराजके where there is no king, जनपदे in a country, व्यवहारिणः those engaged in lawsuits, सिद्धार्थाः succeed, न not, कथाशीलाः those who are accustomed to storytelling, कथाप्रियैः with those who love to listen to stories, कथाभिः with stories, न अनुरज्यन्ते are not entertained.
explanation: Where there is no king, those engaged in lawsuits will not succeed and those who are accustomed to storytelling will not entertain those who love to listen to stories.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे उद्यानानि समागताः। सायाह्ने क्रीडितुं यान्ति कुमार्यो हेमभूषिताः।।2.67.17।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade udyānāni samāgatāḥ| sāyāhne krīḍituṃ yānti kumāryo hemabhūṣitāḥ
translation: अराजके without a king, जनपदे in a country, हेमभूषिताः adorned with golden ornaments, कुमार्यः maidens, समागताः having met together, सायाह्ने in the evening, क्रीडितुम् for sporting, उद्यानानि in the pleasure gardens, नयान्ति will not go.
explanation: In a country without a king, young ladies adorned with golden ornaments no longer meet in the evening at the pleasure garden for sporting.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे वाहनै शशीघ्रगामिभिः। नरा निर्यान्त्यरण्यानि नारीभिस्सह कामिनः।।2.67.18।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade vāhanai śaśīghragāmibhiḥ| narā niryāntyaraṇyāni nārībhissaha kāminaḥ
translation: अराजके without a king, जनपदे in a country, कामिनः pleasureseeking men, नराः men, नारीभिः with women too, शीघ्रगामिभिः by swift moving, वाहनैः chariots, अरण्यानि in the woods (for recreation), न निर्यान्ति will not go.
explanation: In a country without a king, pleasureseeking men will not drive in the woods on swiftmoving chariots with women.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे धनवन्तस्सुरक्षिताः। शेरते विवृतद्वाराः कृषिगोरक्षजीविनः।।2.67.19।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade dhanavantassurakṣitāḥ| śerate vivṛtadvārāḥ kṛṣigorakṣajīvinaḥ
translation: अराजके without a king, जनपदे in a country, कृषिगोरक्षजीविनः living by farming and  protecting cattle, धनवन्तः wealthy people, सुरक्षिताः wellprotected, विवृतद्वाराः with the doors wide open, न शेरते do not sleep.
explanation: In a country without a king, wealthy people who live on farming and raising cattle cannot sleep safely in their homes with doors wide open.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे बद्धघण्टाविषाणिनः। अटन्ति राजमार्गेषु कुञ्जरा षष्टिहायनाः।।2.67.20।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade baddhaghaṇṭāviṣāṇinaḥ| aṭanti rājamārgeṣu kuñjarā ṣaṣṭihāyanāḥ
translation: अराजके without a king, जनपदे in a country, षष्टिहायनाः sixty years of age, कुञ्जराः elephants, बद्धघण्टाविषाणिनः of tusks adorned with bells, राजमार्गेषु on the highways, न अटन्ति will not wander about.
explanation: In a country without a king, young elephants of sixty years of age, their tusks adorned with bells no longer wander about on the highways.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे शरान्सन्ततमस्यताम्। श्रूयते तलनिर्घोष इष्वस्त्राणामुपासने।।2.67.21।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade śarānsantatamasyatām| śrūyate talanirghoṣa iṣvastrāṇāmupāsane
translation: अराजके without a king, जनपदे in a country, इष्वस्त्राणाम् arrows and weapons, उपासने practising (the discharge of), सन्ततम् ceaselessly, शरान् arrows, अस्यताम् shooters  throwing, तलनिर्घोषः clappings of the cord on the skin shield (Tala means a protective covering made of hard skin worn on the left hand to prevent injury), न श्रूयते are not heard.
explanation: In a country without a king, the sounds of the ceaseless discharge of arrows and practice of weapons, the clappings of the cord on the skin shield of shooters throwing the arrows are no longer heard.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे वणिजो दूरगामिनः। गच्छन्ति क्षेममध्वानं बहुपण्यसमाचिताः।।2.67.22।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade vaṇijo dūragāminaḥ| gacchanti kṣemamadhvānaṃ bahupaṇyasamācitāḥ
translation: अराजके without a king, जनपदे in a country, दूरगामिनः travelling long distances, वणिजः merchants, बहुपण्यसमाचिताः with several kinds of marketable goods, क्षेमम् safely, अध्वानम् on the way, न गच्छन्ति do not go.
explanation: In a country without a king merchants travelling long distances with several kinds of saleable goods cannot go safely on their way.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे चरत्येकचरो वशी। भावयन्नात्मनाऽत्मानं यत्र सायंगृहो मुनिः।।2.67.23।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade caratyekacaro vaśī| bhāvayannātmanā'tmānaṃ yatra sāyaṃgṛho muniḥ
translation: अराजके where there is no king, जनपदे in a country, एकचरः moving alone, वशी selfcontrolled, आत्मना in mind, आत्मानाम् on the higher self, भावयन् contemplating, यत्रसायं गृहः inn, मुनिः ascetic, न चरति does not wander.
explanation: In a country where there is no king, an ascetic who (normally) moves alone, selfcontrolled and contemplating on the higher self no longer wanders or rests in the inn.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे योगक्षेमं प्रवर्तते। नचाप्यराजके सेना शत्रून्विषहते युधि।।2.67.24।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade yogakṣemaṃ pravartate| nacāpyarājake senā śatrūnviṣahate yudhi
translation: नाराजके without a king, जनपदे in a country, योगक्षेमम् security of possession, न प्रवर्तते does not exist, अराजके without a king, सेना army, युधि in a battle, शत्रून् enemies, न विषहते not be able to oppose.
explanation: In a country without a king, there is no security of possessions and the army cannot withstand the  enemy in a battle.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे हृष्टैः परमवाजिभिः। नरास्संयान्ति सहसा रथैश्च परिमण्डिताः।।2.67.25।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade hṛṣṭaiḥ paramavājibhiḥ| narāssaṃyānti sahasā rathaiśca parimaṇḍitāḥ
translation: अराजके without a king, जनपदे in the country, नराः men, परिमण्डिताः welldressed, हृष्टैः enthusiastically, परमवाजिभिः of excellent horses, रथैश्च chariots, सहसा at once, न संयान्ति will not go.
explanation: In a country without a king, welldressed men are no longer enthusiastic to drive on excellent horses and on chariots.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे नराश्शास्त्रविशारदाः। संवदन्तोऽवतिष्ठन्ते वनेषूपवनेषु च।।2.67.26।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade narāśśāstraviśāradāḥ| saṃvadanto'vatiṣṭhante vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca
translation: अराजके with no king, जनपदे in the country, शास्त्रविशारदाः those wellversed in scriptures, नराः people, वनेषु in the forests, उपवनेषु च in the (recreational) gardens, संवदन्तः conversing, न अवतिष्ठन्ते do not stay.
explanation: In a country with no king people proficient in scriptures do not withdraw to the forests and (recreational) gardens for debates (on scriptures).

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे माल्यमोदकदक्षिणाः। देवताभ्यर्चनार्थाय कल्प्यन्ते नियतैर्जनैः।।2.67.27।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade mālyamodakadakṣiṇāḥ| devatābhyarcanārthāya kalpyante niyatairjanaiḥ
translation: अराजके where there is no king, जनपदे in the country, नियतैः by disciplined ones in spiritual practices, जनैः people, देवताभ्यर्चनार्थाय for worshipping the gods, माल्यमोदकदक्षिणाः garlands of flowers, sweetmeats and alms, न कल्प्यन्ते  do not arrange.
explanation: In a country where there is no king, people who are disciplined in spiritual practices do not offer garlands of flowers, sweetmeats and alms while worshipping gods.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे चन्दनागरुरूषिताः। राजपुत्रा विराजन्ते वसन्त इव शाखिनः।।2.67.28।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade candanāgarurūṣitāḥ| rājaputrā virājante vasanta iva śākhinaḥ
translation: अराजके where there is no king, जनपदे in the country, राजपुत्रा: princes, चन्दनागरुरूषिताः  anointed with sandal paste and agaru, वसन्ते in spring time, शाखिनः इव like trees, न राजन्ते do not look graceful.
explanation: In a country where there is no king, the princes, anointed with sandal paste and agaru, no longer look graceful like blosoming trees in spring time.

shloka_text: यथा ह्यनुदका नद्यः यथा वाऽप्यतृणं वनम्। अगोपाला यथा गावस्तथा राष्ट्रमराजकम्।।2.67.29।।
transliteration: yathā hyanudakā nadyaḥ yathā vā'pyatṛṇaṃ vanam| agopālā yathā gāvastathā rāṣṭramarājakam
translation: अनुदकाः without water, नद्यः rivers, यथा as, आतृणम् without vegetation, वनम् forest, यथा वा or as, आगोपालाः without cowherds, गावः cows, यथा as, अराजकम् without a king, राष्ट्रम्  country, तथा is like that.
explanation: (The kingdom without a king) is like rivers without water, forests without vegetation and  cows without cowherds.

shloka_text: ध्वजो रथस्य प्रज्ञानं धूमो ज्ञानं विभावसोः। तेषां यो नो ध्वजो राजा स देवत्वमितो गतः।।2.66.30।।
transliteration: dhvajo rathasya prajñānaṃ dhūmo jñānaṃ vibhāvasoḥ| teṣāṃ yo no dhvajo rājā sa devatvamito gataḥ
translation: रथस्य of the chariot, ध्वजः the pennant, प्रज्ञानम् a mark of identification, विभावसोः for fire, धूमः smoke, ज्ञानम् is a mark of identification, तेषाम् for such, नः for us, यः that, ध्वजः  pennant  (with his magnanimity we are recognised), सः राजा that king, इतः from here, देवत्वम् to heaven, गतः has gone.
explanation: The pennant is an identification for one's chariot. Smoke is a mark of identifying fire. All of us are recognised by the pennant (magnanimity) of the king and such a king has gone to heaven.

shloka_text: नाराजके जनपदे स्वकं भवति कस्यचित्। मत्स्या इव नरा नित्यं भक्षयन्ति परस्परम्।।2.67.31।।
transliteration: nārājake janapade svakaṃ bhavati kasyacit| matsyā iva narā nityaṃ bhakṣayanti parasparam
translation: अराजके where there is no king, जनपदे in the country, कस्य चित् for any one, स्वकम् as his own, न भवति does not exist, नराः men, मत्स्याः इव like fish, नित्यम् ceaselessly, परस्परम्  one another, भक्षयन्ति devour.
explanation: In a country where there is no king, no one can own anything and, like fish, people devour one another ceaselessly.

shloka_text: ये हि सम्भिन्नमर्यादा नास्तिकाश्छिन्नसंशयाः। तेऽपि भावाय कल्पन्ते राजदण्डनिपीडिताः।।2.67.32।।
transliteration: ye hi sambhinnamaryādā nāstikāśchinnasaṃśayāḥ| te'pi bhāvāya kalpante rājadaṇḍanipīḍitāḥ
translation: सम्भिन्नमर्यादाः those disregarding the bounds of morality, छिन्नसंशयाः dispelling doubts, ये हि those, नास्तिकाः atheists, तेऽपि they also, राजदण्डनिपीडिताः when subjected to royal  punishment, भावाय for virtuous path, कल्पन्ते adopt.
explanation: Atheists, who disregard the bounds of morality and live freely dispelling doubts will tend to follow virtuous path out of fear when subjected to royal punishment.

shloka_text: यथा दृष्टि श्शरीरस्य नित्यमेव प्रवर्तते। तथा नरेन्द्रो राष्ट्रस्य प्रभवस्सत्यधर्मयोः।।2.67.33।।
transliteration: yathā dṛṣṭi śśarīrasya nityameva pravartate| tathā narendro rāṣṭrasya prabhavassatyadharmayoḥ
translation: दृष्टिः eye, नित्यमेव perpetually, यथा as, शरीरस्य of the body (for its protection), प्रवर्तते is engaged, तथा similarly, नरेन्द्रः king, राष्ट्रस्य for the country's, सत्यधर्मयोः for truth and ethics, प्रभवः is the source.
explanation: The king is the source for protecting the truth and morality of a country like the eye which perpetually watches the welfare of the body.

shloka_text: राजा सत्यं च धर्मश्च राजा कुलवतां कुलम्। राजा माता पिता चैव राजा हितकरो नृणाम्।।2.67.34।।
transliteration: rājā satyaṃ ca dharmaśca rājā kulavatāṃ kulam| rājā mātā pitā caiva rājā hitakaro nṛṇām
translation: राजा king, सत्यं च truth, धर्मश्च righteousness, राजा king, कुलवताम् for men of good families, कुलम् family, राजा king alone, माता mother, पिताचैव father also, राजा king, नृणाम् for people, हितकरः one who renders welfare.
explanation: The king is the protector of truth and righteousness, of men of good families. He is father, and mother. He alone renders welfare of the people.

shloka_text: यमो वैश्रवण श्शक्रः वरुणश्च महाबलः। विशेष्यन्ते नरेन्द्रेण वृत्तेन महता ततः।।2.67.35।।
transliteration: yamo vaiśravaṇa śśakraḥ varuṇaśca mahābalaḥ| viśeṣyante narendreṇa vṛttena mahatā tataḥ
translation: ततः for that reason, यमः lord of death, Yama, वैश्रवणः Vaisravana, शक्रः Indra, महाबलः  mighty, वरुणश्च Varuna, नरेन्द्रेण by the king, महता excellent, वृत्तेन with conduct विशेष्यन्ते are surpassed.
explanation: Hence, the king with his excellent conduct surpasses mighty Yama, Vaisravana, Indra and Varuna.

shloka_text: अहो तम इवेदं स्यान्नप्रज्ञायेत किञ्चन। राजा चे न्न भवे ल्लोके विभज साध्वसाधुनी।।2.67.36।।
transliteration: aho tama ivedaṃ syānnaprajñāyeta kiñcana| rājā ce nna bhave lloke vibhaja sādhvasādhunī
translation: अहो how great, राजा a king, साध्वसाधुनी good and evil actions, विभजन् showing the distinction, लोके in the world, न भवेद्यदि if it were not to happen, इदम् this, तमः स्यात्  would be darkness, किञ्चन even a little, न प्रज्ञायेत could not have been known.
explanation: If the king did not show the distinction between the good and evil actions, this world would have been enveloped by darkness. Nothing could have been seen. How great (is the king)?

shloka_text: जीवत्यपि महाराजे तवैव वचनं वयम्। नातिक्रमामहे सर्वे वेलां प्राप्येव सागरः।।2.67.37।।
transliteration: jīvatyapi mahārāje tavaiva vacanaṃ vayam| nātikramāmahe sarve velāṃ prāpyeva sāgaraḥ
translation: महाराजे when the great king, जीवत्यपि was alive also, वयम् we, सर्वे all, सागरः sea, वेलाम्  shore, प्राप्येव after reaching, तव your, वचनमेव words, नातिक्रमामहे never overstepped.
explanation: Even while the great king was alive, we never defied your word like the ocean which does not overstep its shore.

shloka_text: स न स्समीक्ष्य द्विजवर्य वृत्तं नृपं विना राज्यमरण्यभूतम्। कुमारमिक्ष्वाकुसुतं वदान्यं त्वमेव राजानमिहाभिषिञ्च।।2.67.38।।
transliteration: sa na ssamīkṣya dvijavarya vṛttaṃ nṛpaṃ vinā rājyamaraṇyabhūtam| kumāramikṣvākusutaṃ vadānyaṃ tvameva rājānamihābhiṣiñca
translation: द्विजवर्य O best of brahmins, सः you, वृत्तम् all that has happened, समीक्ष्य having considered, नृपं विना without a king, राज्यम् kingdom, अरण्यभूतम् like a forest, त्वमेव yourself, इह here, वदान्यम् generous, इक्ष्वाकु सुतम् born in the Ikshvaku race, कुमारम् son, नः for us, राजानम् as king, अभिषिञ्च consecrate him.
explanation: O Vasistha, the best of brahmins, considering all that has happened and knowing that a kingdom without a king is like a forest, you may consecrate a generous son from  the Ikshvaku race as our king. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyseventh sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तेषां हि वचनं श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठः प्रत्युवाच ह। मित्रामात्यगणान्सर्वान्ब्राह्मणांस्तानिदं वचः।।2.68.1।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ hi vacanaṃ śrutvā vasiṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca ha| mitrāmātyagaṇānsarvānbrāhmaṇāṃstānidaṃ vacaḥ
translation: तेषाम् their, वचनं words, श्रुत्वा having listened, वसिष्टः Vasistha, तान् those, मित्रामात्यगणान्  host of friends and counsellors (of the king), सर्वान् all, ब्राह्मणान् brahmins, इदं वचः these words, प्रत्युवाचह said in reply.
explanation: Having listened to their (the counsellors') words, Vasistha replied to the host of friends and counsellors of the king  and to all the brahmins:
comments: Messengers are sent to get Bharata and Satrughna -- Messengers reach Rajagrha the maternal home of Bharata

shloka_text: यदसौ मातुलकुले दत्तराज्यं परं सुखी। भरतो वसति भ्रात्रा शत्रुघ्नेन समन्वितः।।2.68.2।। तच्छीघ्रं जवना दूता गच्छन्तु त्वरितैर्हयैः। आनेतुं भ्रातरौ वीरौ किं समीक्षामहे वयम्।।2.68.3।।
transliteration: yadasau mātulakule dattarājyaṃ paraṃ sukhī| bharato vasati bhrātrā śatrughnena samanvitaḥ tacchīghraṃ javanā dūtā gacchantu tvaritairhayaiḥ| ānetuṃ bhrātarau vīrau kiṃ samīkṣāmahe vayam
translation: दत्तराज्यम् on whom the kingdom  has been conferred, असौ भरतः that Bharata, भ्रात्रा with his brother, शत्रुघ्नेन with Satrughna, समन्वितः accompanied by, यत् since, मातुलकुले in maternal uncle's house, परम् extremely, सुखी happy, वसति is living, तत् for that reason, वीरौ two valiant, भ्रातरौ brothers, आनेतुम् to bring, जवनाः swift ones, दूताः messengers, त्वरितैः by high speed, हयैः on horses, शीघ्रम् quickly, गच्छन्तु let them go, वयम् we, किम् what, समीक्षामहे shall we deliberate.
explanation: Bharata on whom the kingdom has been conferred is living comfortably in his maternal uncle's house. Let swift messengers go quickly  on speeding horses and bring back the valiant brothers, Bharata and Satrughna. What is there to deliberate for us in this matter?

shloka_text: यदसौ मातुलकुले दत्तराज्यं परं सुखी। भरतो वसति भ्रात्रा शत्रुघ्नेन समन्वितः।।2.68.2।। तच्छीघ्रं जवना दूता गच्छन्तु त्वरितैर्हयैः। आनेतुं भ्रातरौ वीरौ किं समीक्षामहे वयम्।।2.68.3।।
transliteration: yadasau mātulakule dattarājyaṃ paraṃ sukhī| bharato vasati bhrātrā śatrughnena samanvitaḥ tacchīghraṃ javanā dūtā gacchantu tvaritairhayaiḥ| ānetuṃ bhrātarau vīrau kiṃ samīkṣāmahe vayam
translation: दत्तराज्यम् on whom the kingdom  has been conferred, असौ भरतः that Bharata, भ्रात्रा with his brother, शत्रुघ्नेन with Satrughna, समन्वितः accompanied by, यत् since, मातुलकुले in maternal uncle's house, परम् extremely, सुखी happy, वसति is living, तत् for that reason, वीरौ two valiant, भ्रातरौ brothers, आनेतुम् to bring, जवनाः swift ones, दूताः messengers, त्वरितैः by high speed, हयैः on horses, शीघ्रम् quickly, गच्छन्तु let them go, वयम् we, किम् what, समीक्षामहे shall we deliberate.
explanation: Bharata on whom the kingdom has been conferred is living comfortably in his maternal uncle's house. Let swift messengers go quickly  on speeding horses and bring back the valiant brothers, Bharata and Satrughna. What is there to deliberate for us in this matter?

shloka_text: गच्छन्त्विति तत स्सर्वे वसिष्ठं वाक्यमब्रुवन्। तेषां तद्वचनं श्रूत्वा वसिष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.68.4।।
transliteration: gacchantviti tata ssarve vasiṣṭhaṃ vākyamabruvan| teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrūtvā vasiṣṭho vākyamabravīt
translation: ततः after that, गच्छन्तु let them go, इति thus, सर्वे all, वसिष्ठम् addressing Vasistha, वाक्यम् words, अब्रुवन् uttered, तेषाम् their, तत् those, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा on hearing, वसिष्ठः Vasistha, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Let the messengers go, said all of them to Vasistha. On hearing this, Vasistha  replied again.

shloka_text: एहि सिद्धार्थ विजय जयन्ताशोक नन्दन। श्रूयतामिति कर्तव्यं सर्वानेव ब्रवीमि वः।।2.68.5।।
transliteration: ehi siddhārtha vijaya jayantāśoka nandana| śrūyatāmiti kartavyaṃ sarvāneva bravīmi vaḥ
translation: सिद्धार्थ O Siddhartha, विजय O Vijaya, जयन्त O Jayanta, अशोक O Asoka, नन्दन O Nandana, एहि come, वः us, सर्वानेव addressing all of you, (अहम् I), ब्रवीमि am telling, इतिकर्तव्यम् what is required to be done, श्रूयाताम् hear.
explanation: Calling Siddhartha, Vijaya, Jayanta, Asoka and Nandana, Vasistha said, All of you  listen to what is required to be done (by you).

shloka_text: पुरं राजगृहं गत्वा शीघ्रं शीघ्रजवै र्हयैः। त्यक्तशोकैरिदं वाच्य श्शासनाद्भरतो मम।।2.68.6।।
transliteration: puraṃ rājagṛhaṃ gatvā śīghraṃ śīghrajavai rhayaiḥ| tyaktaśokairidaṃ vācya śśāsanādbharato mama
translation: (इतः from here), शीघ्रजवैः go swiftly, हयैः on horses, राजगृहम् to Rajagrha, पुरम् city, गत्वा  having gone, त्यक्त शोकैः concealing signs of grief, भरतः Bharata, मम my, शासनात् by command, इदम् these words, वाच्यः should be told.
explanation: Go at once from here on swift horses to the city of Rajagrha and concealing signs of grief, convey these words to Bharata as my command:

shloka_text: पुरोहित स्त्वां कुशलं प्राह सर्वे च मन्त्रिणः। त्वरमाणश्च निर्याहि कृत्यमात्ययिकं त्वया।।2.68.7।।
transliteration: purohita stvāṃ kuśalaṃ prāha sarve ca mantriṇaḥ| tvaramāṇaśca niryāhi kṛtyamātyayikaṃ tvayā
translation: पुरोहितः the family priest, त्वाम् your, कुशलम् welfare, प्राह has wished, सर्वे all, मन्त्रिणश्च counsellors too, त्वरमाणः च in all haste, निर्याहि return, त्वया by you, आत्ययिकम् urgent, कृत्यम् task exists.
explanation: The family priest and all the counsellors  wish your welfare. You must return in haste. There is an urgent task required to be done by you.

shloka_text: मा चास्मै प्रोषितं रामं मा चास्मै पितरं मृतम्। भवन्त श्शंसिषुर्गत्वा राघवाणामिमं क्षयम्।।2.68.8।।
transliteration: mā cāsmai proṣitaṃ rāmaṃ mā cāsmai pitaraṃ mṛtam| bhavanta śśaṃsiṣurgatvā rāghavāṇāmimaṃ kṣayam
translation: भवन्तः all of you, गत्वा having gone, आस्मै to him, रामम् Rama, प्रोषितम् been exiled to the forest, मा शंसिषुः shall not be communicated, पितरम् father's, मृतम् demise, राघवाणाम् of Raghus, इमम् this, क्षयम् decline, मा शंसिषुः shall not communicate.
explanation: All of you go there and do not communicate (to Bharata) about the exile of Rama or the demise of his father and the disaster that has befallen the Raghus.

shloka_text: कौशेयानि च वस्त्राणि भूषणानि वराणि च। क्षिप्रमादय राज्ञश्च भरतस्य च गच्छत।।2.68.9।।
transliteration: kauśeyāni ca vastrāṇi bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi ca| kṣipramādaya rājñaśca bharatasya ca gacchata
translation: राज्ञश्च the kings, भरतस्य च to Bharata, कौशेयानि वस्त्राणि silk garments, वराणि precious, भूषणानि च ornaments, आदाय taking with you, क्षिप्रम् गच्छत immediately go.
explanation: Take with you silk garments and precious ornaments for the king of Kekaya and Bharata and depart at once.

shloka_text: दत्तपथ्यशना दूता जग्मुस्स्वं स्वं निवेशनम्। केकयां स्ते गमिष्यन्तो हयानारुह्य संमतान्।।2.68.10।।
transliteration: dattapathyaśanā dūtā jagmussvaṃ svaṃ niveśanam| kekayāṃ ste gamiṣyanto hayānāruhya saṃmatān
translation: केकयान् to Kekaya kingdom, गमिष्यन्तः departing, ते दूताः those mesengers, दत्तपथ्यशनाः  necessaries for the journey, सम्मतान् excellent, हयान् horses, आरुह्य having mounted, स्वं स्वम् their respective, निवेशनम् house, जग्मुः went.
explanation: The messengers set to depart to Kekaya kingdom, carrying with them the necessaries for their journey went to their respective homes mounted on  excellent horses.

shloka_text: ततः प्रास्थानिकं कृत्वा कार्यशेषमनन्तरम्। वसिष्ठेनाभ्यनुज्ञाता दूता स्संत्वरिता ययुः।।2.68.11।।
transliteration: tataḥ prāsthānikaṃ kṛtvā kāryaśeṣamanantaram| vasiṣṭhenābhyanujñātā dūtā ssaṃtvaritā yayuḥ
translation: ततः then, दूताः messengers, प्रास्थानिकम् for the journey, अनन्तरम् required to be done, कार्यशेषम् rest of the arrangements, कृत्वा having done, वसिष्ठेन by Vasistha, अभ्यनुज्ञाताः  permitted, संत्वरिताः in haste, ययुः went out.
explanation: Having completed the rest of the arrangements for the journey and permitted by  Vasistha, the messengers left.

shloka_text: न्यन्तेनापरतालस्य प्रलम्बस्योत्तरं प्रति। निषेवमाणा स्ते जग्मुर्नदीं मध्येन मालिनीम्।।2.68.12।।
transliteration: nyantenāparatālasya pralambasyottaraṃ prati| niṣevamāṇā ste jagmurnadīṃ madhyena mālinīm
translation: ते those messengers, अपरतालस्य Aparatala mountain, न्यन्तेन to the west of it, प्रलम्बस्य Pralamba mountain, उत्तरं प्रति to the north of, मध्येन in between, मालिनीं नदीम् river Malini, निषेवमाणाः serving, जग्मुः went.
explanation: The messengers proceeded in westerly direction for some distance and then crossed the southern end of the Aparatala mountain. Thereafter, they travelled northward along the bank of Malini that flows in between Aparatala and Pralamba mountains.

shloka_text: ते हस्तिनापुरे गङ्गां तीर्त्वा प्रत्यङ्मुखा ययुः। पाञ्चालदेशमासाद्य मध्येन कुरुजाङ्गलम्।।2.68.13।। सरांसि च सुपूर्णानि नदीश्च विमलोदकाः। निरीक्षमाणा स्ते जग्मुर्दूताः कार्यवशाद्द्रुतम्।।2.68.14।।
transliteration: te hastināpure gaṅgāṃ tīrtvā pratyaṅmukhā yayuḥ| pāñcāladeśamāsādya madhyena kurujāṅgalam sarāṃsi ca supūrṇāni nadīśca vimalodakāḥ| nirīkṣamāṇā ste jagmurdūtāḥ kāryavaśāddrutam
translation: ते दूताः those messengers, हस्तिनापुरे at Hastinapura, गङ्गाम् Ganga, तीर्त्वा having crossed, प्रत्यङ्मुखाः in the westerly direction, ययुः went, मध्येन कुरुजाङ्गलम् through the middle of Kurujangala, पाञ्चालदेशम् Panchala country, आसाद्य having reached, सुपूर्णानि filled with water, सरांसि च lakes, विमलोदकाः of pellucid waters, नदीश्च rivers, निरीक्षमाणाः  beholding, कार्यवशात् with a view to fulfil their mission, द्रुतम्  fast, जग्मुः went.
explanation: The messengers crossed Ganga at Hastinapura, and went in the westerly direction through the middle of Kurujangala and reached the country of Panchala. Beholding lakes full of water and rivers of pellucid waters there, they travelled fast with a view to fulfilling their mission.

shloka_text: ते हस्तिनापुरे गङ्गां तीर्त्वा प्रत्यङ्मुखा ययुः। पाञ्चालदेशमासाद्य मध्येन कुरुजाङ्गलम्।।2.68.13।। सरांसि च सुपूर्णानि नदीश्च विमलोदकाः। निरीक्षमाणा स्ते जग्मुर्दूताः कार्यवशाद्द्रुतम्।।2.68.14।।
transliteration: te hastināpure gaṅgāṃ tīrtvā pratyaṅmukhā yayuḥ| pāñcāladeśamāsādya madhyena kurujāṅgalam sarāṃsi ca supūrṇāni nadīśca vimalodakāḥ| nirīkṣamāṇā ste jagmurdūtāḥ kāryavaśāddrutam
translation: ते दूताः those messengers, हस्तिनापुरे at Hastinapura, गङ्गाम् Ganga, तीर्त्वा having crossed, प्रत्यङ्मुखाः in the westerly direction, ययुः went, मध्येन कुरुजाङ्गलम् through the middle of Kurujangala, पाञ्चालदेशम् Panchala country, आसाद्य having reached, सुपूर्णानि filled with water, सरांसि च lakes, विमलोदकाः of pellucid waters, नदीश्च rivers, निरीक्षमाणाः  beholding, कार्यवशात् with a view to fulfil their mission, द्रुतम्  fast, जग्मुः went.
explanation: The messengers crossed Ganga at Hastinapura, and went in the westerly direction through the middle of Kurujangala and reached the country of Panchala. Beholding lakes full of water and rivers of pellucid waters there, they travelled fast with a view to fulfilling their mission.

shloka_text: ते प्रसन्नोदकां दिव्यां नानाविहगसेविताम्। उपातिजग्मुर्वेगेन शरदण्डां जनाकुलाम्।।2.68.15।।
transliteration: te prasannodakāṃ divyāṃ nānāvihagasevitām| upātijagmurvegena śaradaṇḍāṃ janākulām
translation: ते those messengers, प्रसन्नोदकाम् of calm waters, दिव्याम् divine, नानाविहगसेविताम्    frequented by fowls of various species, जनाकुलाम् thronged with people, शरदण्डाम् Saradanda river, उपातिजग्मुः crossed and went.
explanation: The messengers crossed the divine Saradanda of calm waters frequented by fowls of various speices and thronged with people. And proceeded speedily.

shloka_text: निकूलवृक्षमासाद्य दिव्यं सत्योपयाचनम्। अभिगम्याभिवाद्यं तं कुलिङ्गां प्राविशन्पुरीम्।।2.68.16।।
transliteration: nikūlavṛkṣamāsādya divyaṃ satyopayācanam| abhigamyābhivādyaṃ taṃ kuliṅgāṃ prāviśanpurīm
translation: दिव्यम् divine, सत्योपयाचनम् Satyopayachana (a tree granting the wishes of those who pray for), निकूलवृक्षम् a tree on the bank, आसाद्य having reached, अभिवाद्यम् paying homage, तम् that one, अभिगम्य having reached, कुलिङ्गांपुरीम् Kulinga city, प्राविशन् entered.
explanation: They reached a divine tree (of great powers) known as Satyopayachana tree and having gone round and paid homage they entered the Kulinga city.

shloka_text: आभिकालं ततः प्राप्य ते बोधिभवनाच्च्युताम्। पितृपैतामहीं पुण्यां तेरुरिक्षुमतीं नदीम्।।2.68.17।।
transliteration: ābhikālaṃ tataḥ prāpya te bodhibhavanāccyutām| pitṛpaitāmahīṃ puṇyāṃ terurikṣumatīṃ nadīm
translation: ततः from there, ते they, अभिकालम् a village known as Abhikala, प्राप्य having reached, बोधिभवनात् from Bodhibhavana mountain, च्युताम् flowing, पितृपैतामहीम् enjoyed by fathers and forefathers, पुण्याम् sacred, इक्षुमतीम् Ikshumati river, तेरुः crossed.
explanation: From there they reached a village known as Abhikala and crossed the sacred Ikshumati flowing from Bodhibhavana mountain. This region was enjoyed by fathers and forefathers of Dasaratha.

shloka_text: अवेक्ष्याञ्जलिपानांश्च ब्राह्मणान्वेदपारगान्। ययुर्मध्येन बाह्लीकान् सुदामानं च पर्वतम्।।2.68.18।।
transliteration: avekṣyāñjalipānāṃśca brāhmaṇānvedapāragān| yayurmadhyena bāhlīkān sudāmānaṃ ca parvatam
translation: अञ्जलिपानान् drinking water with cupped palms, वेदपारगान् versed in the Vedas, ब्राह्मणान् brahmins, अवेक्षय having seen, बाह्लीकान् मध्येन in the middle of Bahlika country, सुदामानम्  known as Sudama, पर्यतं च mountain, ययुः went.
explanation: There they saw the brahmins versed in the Vedas and drank water with cupped  palms. Then they continued their journey through the middle of Bahlika country, and  reached Sudama mountain.

shloka_text: विष्णोः पदं प्रेक्षमाणा विपाशांचापि शाल्मलीम्। नदीर्वापी स्तटाकानि पल्वलानि सरांसि च।।2.68.19।। पश्यन्तो विविधांश्चापि सिंहाव्याघ्रमृग द्विपान्। ययुः पथाऽतिमहता शासनं भर्तुरीप्सवः।।2.68.20।।
transliteration: viṣṇoḥ padaṃ prekṣamāṇā vipāśāṃcāpi śālmalīm| nadīrvāpī staṭākāni palvalāni sarāṃsi ca paśyanto vividhāṃścāpi siṃhāvyāghramṛga dvipān| yayuḥ pathā'timahatā śāsanaṃ bharturīpsavaḥ
translation: विष्णोः Visnu's, पदम् footprints, प्रेक्षमाणाः beholding, विपाशांचापि Vipasa river, शाल्मलीलं चापि Salmali also, नदीः rivers, वापीः deep wells with steps to reach, तटाकानि tanks, पल्वलानि pools, सरांसि च large tanks, विविधान् different, सिंहव्याघ्रमृग द्विपान् lions, tigers and elephants, पश्यन्तः seeing, भर्तुः master's, शासनम् command, ईप्सवः wishing to fulfil,  अतिमहता very long, पथा journey, ययुः went.
explanation: Beholding the footprints of Visnu (on Sudama mountain), and seeing Vipasa, and Salmali rivers, trees, streams, deep wells, ponds, pools, large tanks, different kinds of lions, tigers and elephants, they travelled a long distance with the intention of fulfilling the command of their master.

shloka_text: विष्णोः पदं प्रेक्षमाणा विपाशांचापि शाल्मलीम्। नदीर्वापी स्तटाकानि पल्वलानि सरांसि च।।2.68.19।। पश्यन्तो विविधांश्चापि सिंहाव्याघ्रमृग द्विपान्। ययुः पथाऽतिमहता शासनं भर्तुरीप्सवः।।2.68.20।।
transliteration: viṣṇoḥ padaṃ prekṣamāṇā vipāśāṃcāpi śālmalīm| nadīrvāpī staṭākāni palvalāni sarāṃsi ca paśyanto vividhāṃścāpi siṃhāvyāghramṛga dvipān| yayuḥ pathā'timahatā śāsanaṃ bharturīpsavaḥ
translation: विष्णोः Visnu's, पदम् footprints, प्रेक्षमाणाः beholding, विपाशांचापि Vipasa river, शाल्मलीलं चापि Salmali also, नदीः rivers, वापीः deep wells with steps to reach, तटाकानि tanks, पल्वलानि pools, सरांसि च large tanks, विविधान् different, सिंहव्याघ्रमृग द्विपान् lions, tigers and elephants, पश्यन्तः seeing, भर्तुः master's, शासनम् command, ईप्सवः wishing to fulfil,  अतिमहता very long, पथा journey, ययुः went.
explanation: Beholding the footprints of Visnu (on Sudama mountain), and seeing Vipasa, and Salmali rivers, trees, streams, deep wells, ponds, pools, large tanks, different kinds of lions, tigers and elephants, they travelled a long distance with the intention of fulfilling the command of their master.

shloka_text: ते श्रान्तवाहना दूता विकृष्णेन पथा ततः। गिरिव्रजं पुरवरं शीघ्रमासेदुरञ्जसा।।2.68.21।।
transliteration: te śrāntavāhanā dūtā vikṛṣṇena pathā tataḥ| girivrajaṃ puravaraṃ śīghramāsedurañjasā
translation: विकृष्णेन by  prolonged, पथा journey, श्रान्त वाहनाः tired horses, ते दूताः those mesengers, ततः then, शीघ्रम् swiftly, अञ्जसा straight on, पुरवरम् best of cities, गिरिव्रजम् Girivrajam, आसेदुः reached.
explanation: After a prolonged journey the messengers with their tired horses soon reached Girivraja, the (capital city of Kekaya kingdom) best of cities.

shloka_text: भर्तुः प्रियार्थं कुलरक्षणार्थं भर्तुश्च वंशस्य परिग्रहार्थम्। अहेडमाना स्त्वरया स्म दूता रात्र्यान्तु ते तत्पुरमेव याताः।।2.68.22।।
transliteration: bhartuḥ priyārthaṃ kularakṣaṇārthaṃ bhartuśca vaṃśasya parigrahārtham| aheḍamānā stvarayā sma dūtā rātryāntu te tatpurameva yātāḥ
translation: ते दूताः those messengers, भर्तुः lord's, प्रियार्थम् to please, कुलरक्षणार्थम् to preserve the royal dynasty, भर्तुः of the king's, वंशस्य the house of the Ikshvakus, परिग्रहार्थम् for the protection of (royal honour), त्वरया quickly, अहेडमानाः without negligence, रात्य्राम् in the night, तत् that, पुरमेव that city, याताः reached.
explanation: To please their master (sage Vasistha)  and to preserve the royal dynasty and also to protect the honour of the (race and people), the messengers soon reached their destination by night without any negligence of their duty. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends  the sixtyeighth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: यामेव रात्रिं ते दूताः प्रविशन्ति स्म तां पुरीम्। भरतेनापि तां रात्रिं स्वप्नो दृष्टोऽयमप्रियः।।2.69.1।।
transliteration: yāmeva rātriṃ te dūtāḥ praviśanti sma tāṃ purīm| bharatenāpi tāṃ rātriṃ svapno dṛṣṭo'yamapriyaḥ
translation: ते दूताः those messengers, यामेव on whichever, रात्रिम् night, तां पुरीम् that city, प्रविशन्ति स्म were entering, तां रात्रिम् that night, भरतेनापि by Bharata also, अयम् this, आप्रियः distressing, स्वप्नः dream, दृष्टः has been seen.
explanation: On the very night the messengers were entering the city, Bharata had a distressing dream.
comments: Bharata experiences unhappiness over a distressing and frightening dream.

shloka_text: व्युष्टामेव तु तां रात्रिं दृष्ट्वा तं स्वप्नमप्रियम्। पुत्रो राजाधिराजस्य सुभृशं पर्यतप्यत।।2.69.2।।
transliteration: vyuṣṭāmeva tu tāṃ rātriṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ svapnamapriyam| putro rājādhirājasya subhṛśaṃ paryatapyata
translation: राजाधिराजस्य (the son) of the king of kings, पुत्रः son, तां रात्रिम् that night, व्युष्टाम् एव when dawn appeared, तम् that, अप्रियम् unpleasant, स्वप्नम् dream, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सुभृशम् extremely, पर्यतप्यत felt troubled.
explanation: The son of the king of kings (Bharata) felt extremely troubled hen he had an  unpleasant dream at dawn.

shloka_text: तप्यमानं समाज्ञाय वयस्याः प्रियवादिनः। आयासं हि विनेष्यन्त स्सभायां चक्रिरे कथाः।।2.69.3।।
transliteration: tapyamānaṃ samājñāya vayasyāḥ priyavādinaḥ| āyāsaṃ hi vineṣyanta ssabhāyāṃ cakrire kathāḥ
translation: प्रियवादिनः speaking pleasing words, वयस्याः peers, तप्यमानम् griefstricken, समाज्ञाय having observed, आयासम् despair, विनेष्यन्तः with a view to remove, सभायाम् in the assembly, कथाः stories, चक्रिरे made.
explanation: Observing him griefstricken his peers who always spoke pleasant words, engaged him in a variety of ways in the assembly in order to divert him.

shloka_text: वादयन्ति तथा शान्तिं लास यन्त्यपि चापरे। नाटकान्यपरे प्राहुर्हास्यानि विविधानि च।।2.69.4।।
transliteration: vādayanti tathā śāntiṃ lāsa yantyapi cāpare| nāṭakānyapare prāhurhāsyāni vividhāni ca
translation: शान्तिम् to provide mental peace, वादयन्ति played stringed instruments, तथा similarly, अपरे some, नाटकानि dramatic scenes, लासयन्त्यपि danced, अपरे some, विविधानि various kinds of, हास्यानि jokes, प्राहुः told.
explanation: In order to provide mental peace to Bharata, some played stringed instruments while some enacted dramatic scenes, some danced and cracked various kinds of jokes.

shloka_text: स तैर्महात्मा भरतस्सखिभिः प्रियवादिभिः। गोष्ठीहास्यानि कुर्वद्भिर्न प्राहृष्यत राघवः।।2.69.5।।
transliteration: sa tairmahātmā bharatassakhibhiḥ priyavādibhiḥ| goṣṭhīhāsyāni kurvadbhirna prāhṛṣyata rāghavaḥ
translation: राघवः one born in the Raghu race, महात्मा the magnanimous, सः भरतः that Bharata, गोष्ठीहास्यानि conversations and jokes, कुर्वद्भि: while performing, प्रियवादिभिः were soothing words, सखिभिः by friends also, न प्राहृष्यत could not be delighted.
explanation: The magnanimous Bharata born in the race of Raghus, was not delighted by the conversations and jokes and soothing words of his friends.

shloka_text: तमब्रवीत्प्रियसखो भरतं सखिभिर्वृतम्। सुहृद्भिः पर्युपासीनः किं सखे नानुमोदसे।।2.69.6।।
transliteration: tamabravītpriyasakho bharataṃ sakhibhirvṛtam| suhṛdbhiḥ paryupāsīnaḥ kiṃ sakhe nānumodase
translation: प्रियसखः one dear friend, सखिभिः with friends, वृतम् surrounded, भरतं addressing that Bharata, अब्रवीत् said, सखे O friend, सुहृद्भिः with friends, पर्युपासीनः accompanied by, किम् why, न अनुमोदसे you are not pleased.
explanation: Addressing Bharata amidst his companions some one close among them said O friend why are you dejected in spite of being in the company of friends.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवाणं सुहृदं भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह। श्रुणु त्वं यन्निमित्तं मे दैन्यमेतदुपागतम्।।2.69.7।।
transliteration: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ suhṛdaṃ bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha| śruṇu tvaṃ yannimittaṃ me dainyametadupāgatam
translation: भरतः Bharata, एवम् in this manner, ब्रुवाणम् saying, सुहृदम् his companion, प्रत्युवाच ह replied, मे my, यन्निमित्तम् for what reason, एतत् this, दैन्यम् desolation, उपागतम् that has overtaken me, त्वम् you, श्रुणु listen.
explanation: Addressing his companion who was speaking thus, Bharata replied, saying Listen to the reason this desolation has overtaken me:

shloka_text: स्वप्ने पितरमद्राक्षं मलिनं मुक्त मूर्धजम्। पतन्तमद्रिशिखरात्कलुषे गोमयह्रदे।।2.69.8।।
transliteration: svapne pitaramadrākṣaṃ malinaṃ mukta mūrdhajam| patantamadriśikharātkaluṣe gomayahrade
translation: स्वप्ने in a dream, मलिनम् pale, मुक्तमूर्धजम् with dishevelled hair, अद्रिशिखरात् from the peak of a mountain, कलुषे dirty, गोमयह्रदे pool filled with cow dung, पतन्तम् falling down, पितरम् father, अद्राक्षम् saw.
explanation: In my dream I saw my father looking pale, with dishevelled hair, his body filled with filth falling from the peak of a mountain into a pool of cow  dung.

shloka_text: प्लवमानश्च मे दृष्टस्स तस्मिन्गोमयह्रदे। पिबन्नञ्जलिना तैलं हसन्नपि मुहुर्मुहुः।।2.69.9।।
transliteration: plavamānaśca me dṛṣṭassa tasmingomayahrade| pibannañjalinā tailaṃ hasannapi muhurmuhuḥ
translation: सः he, तस्मिन् that, गोमयह्रदे in the pool filled with cow dung, प्लवमानः floating, अञ्जलिना with both palms cupped, तैलम् oil, पिबन् drinking मुहुर्मुहुः again and again, हसन् laughing, मे by me, दृष्टः was seen.
explanation: I saw my father floating in that pool of cow  dung, drinking oil with cupped palms and  bursting into laughter again and again.

shloka_text: ततस्तिलौदनं भुक्त्वा पुनः पुनरधश्शिराः। तैलेनाभ्यक्तसर्वाङ्गः तैलमेवान्वगाहत।।2.69.10।।
transliteration: tatastilaudanaṃ bhuktvā punaḥ punaradhaśśirāḥ| tailenābhyaktasarvāṅgaḥ tailamevānvagāhata
translation: ततः thereafter, तिलौदनम् rice cooked with sesame seeds, भुक्त्वा eating, पुनः पुनः again and again, अधःशिराः plunging his head downwards, तैलेन with oil, अभ्यक्तसर्वाङ्ग: his body besmeared with oil, तैलमेव into the oil alone, अन्वगाहत entered.
explanation: Thereafter I beheld him eating rice cooked with sesame seeds, his body besmeared with oil plunging again and again into it (the pool).

shloka_text: स्वप्नेऽपि सागरं शुष्कं चन्द्रं च पतितं भवि। उपरुद्धां च जगतीं तमसेव समावृताम्।।2.69.11।। औपवाह्यस्य नागस्य विषाणं शकलीकृतम्। सहसाचापि संशान्तं ज्वलितं जातवेदसम्।।2.69.12।। अवतीर्णां च पृथिवीं शुष्कां श्च विविधान् द्रुमान्। अहं पश्यामि विध्वस्तान् सधूमांश्चापि पर्वतान्।।2.69.13।।
transliteration: svapne'pi sāgaraṃ śuṣkaṃ candraṃ ca patitaṃ bhavi| uparuddhāṃ ca jagatīṃ tamaseva samāvṛtām aupavāhyasya nāgasya viṣāṇaṃ śakalīkṛtam| sahasācāpi saṃśāntaṃ jvalitaṃ jātavedasam avatīrṇāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ śuṣkāṃ śca vividhān drumān| ahaṃ paśyāmi vidhvastān sadhūmāṃścāpi parvatān
translation: अहम् I, स्वप्ने in the dream, सागरम् sea, शुष्कम् having dried up, चन्द्रम् Moon, भुवि on the ground, पतितम् having fallen down, जगतीम् the earth, तमस समावृताम् इव as if enveloped in  darkness, उपरुद्धाम् obscured, औपवाह्यस्य worthy of a ride, नागस्य elephant's, विषाणम् tusk,  शकलीकृतम् broken into pieces, ज्वलितम् blazing, जातवेदनम् fire, सहसा suddenly, संशान्तम् extinguished, पृथिवीम् earth, अवतीर्णां च split open, विविधान् various, द्रुमान् trees, शुष्कांश्च dried up, पर्वतान् mountains, विध्वस्तान् having been destroyed, सधूमान् with smoke, पश्यामि I see.
explanation: In that dream I beheld the sea being dried up and the Moon fallen onto the ground. I saw the earth as though enveloped by darkness and obscured, the tusk of an  elephant worthy of a ride by the monarch broken into pieces, a blazing fire  extinguished suddenly, the earth split open, various trees dried up and mountains crumbled and covered with smoke.

shloka_text: स्वप्नेऽपि सागरं शुष्कं चन्द्रं च पतितं भवि। उपरुद्धां च जगतीं तमसेव समावृताम्।।2.69.11।। औपवाह्यस्य नागस्य विषाणं शकलीकृतम्। सहसाचापि संशान्तं ज्वलितं जातवेदसम्।।2.69.12।। अवतीर्णां च पृथिवीं शुष्कां श्च विविधान् द्रुमान्। अहं पश्यामि विध्वस्तान् सधूमांश्चापि पर्वतान्।।2.69.13।।
transliteration: svapne'pi sāgaraṃ śuṣkaṃ candraṃ ca patitaṃ bhavi| uparuddhāṃ ca jagatīṃ tamaseva samāvṛtām aupavāhyasya nāgasya viṣāṇaṃ śakalīkṛtam| sahasācāpi saṃśāntaṃ jvalitaṃ jātavedasam avatīrṇāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ śuṣkāṃ śca vividhān drumān| ahaṃ paśyāmi vidhvastān sadhūmāṃścāpi parvatān
translation: अहम् I, स्वप्ने in the dream, सागरम् sea, शुष्कम् having dried up, चन्द्रम् Moon, भुवि on the ground, पतितम् having fallen down, जगतीम् the earth, तमस समावृताम् इव as if enveloped in  darkness, उपरुद्धाम् obscured, औपवाह्यस्य worthy of a ride, नागस्य elephant's, विषाणम् tusk,  शकलीकृतम् broken into pieces, ज्वलितम् blazing, जातवेदनम् fire, सहसा suddenly, संशान्तम् extinguished, पृथिवीम् earth, अवतीर्णां च split open, विविधान् various, द्रुमान् trees, शुष्कांश्च dried up, पर्वतान् mountains, विध्वस्तान् having been destroyed, सधूमान् with smoke, पश्यामि I see.
explanation: In that dream I beheld the sea being dried up and the Moon fallen onto the ground. I saw the earth as though enveloped by darkness and obscured, the tusk of an  elephant worthy of a ride by the monarch broken into pieces, a blazing fire  extinguished suddenly, the earth split open, various trees dried up and mountains crumbled and covered with smoke.

translation: अहम् I, स्वप्ने in the dream, सागरम् sea, शुष्कम् having dried up, चन्द्रम् Moon, भुवि on the ground, पतितम् having fallen down, जगतीम् the earth, तमस समावृताम् इव as if enveloped in  darkness, उपरुद्धाम् obscured, औपवाह्यस्य worthy of a ride, नागस्य elephant's, विषाणम् tusk,  शकलीकृतम् broken into pieces, ज्वलितम् blazing, जातवेदनम् fire, सहसा suddenly, संशान्तम् extinguished, पृथिवीम् earth, अवतीर्णां च split open, विविधान् various, द्रुमान् trees, शुष्कांश्च dried up, पर्वतान् mountains, विध्वस्तान् having been destroyed, सधूमान् with smoke, पश्यामि I see.
explanation: In that dream I beheld the sea being dried up and the Moon fallen onto the ground. I saw the earth as though enveloped by darkness and obscured, the tusk of an  elephant worthy of a ride by the monarch broken into pieces, a blazing fire  extinguished suddenly, the earth split open, various trees dried up and mountains crumbled and covered with smoke.

shloka_text: पीठे कार्ष्णायसे चैनं निषण्णं कृष्णवाससम्। प्रहसन्ति स्म राजानं प्रमदाः कृष्णपिङ्गलाः।।2.69.14।।
transliteration: pīṭhe kārṣṇāyase cainaṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ kṛṣṇavāsasam| prahasanti sma rājānaṃ pramadāḥ kṛṣṇapiṅgalāḥ
translation: कार्ष्णायसे on an iron, पीठे seat, निषण्णम् resting, कृष्णवाससम्  clad in black clothes, एनं राजानं this king, कृष्णपिङ्गलाः having dark and brownish complexion, प्रमादाः women, प्रहसन्ति were laughing.
explanation: In the dream, I beheld my father clad in black clothes and resting on a seat made of iron and the women in dark and brownish complexion laughing at him.

shloka_text: त्वरमाणश्च धर्मात्मा रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनः। रथेन खरयुक्तेन प्रयातो दक्षिणामुखः।।2.69.15।।
transliteration: tvaramāṇaśca dharmātmā raktamālyānulepanaḥ| rathena kharayuktena prayāto dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ
translation: धर्मात्मा virtuous one, रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनः wearing garlands of red flowers and with his body  bedaubed with red sandal, त्वरमाणश्च hurrying off, खरयुक्तेन yoked with asses, रथेन on chariot, दक्षिणामुखः southward, प्रयातः went.
explanation: Thereafter, I beheld that virtuous monarch bedecked with garlands made of red flowers and his body bedaubed with red sandalpaste, hurrying off southward on a chariot yoked with asses.

shloka_text: प्रहसन्तीव राजानं प्रमदा रक्तवासिनी। प्रकर्षन्ती मया दृष्टा राक्षसी विकृतानना।।2.69.16।।
transliteration: prahasantīva rājānaṃ pramadā raktavāsinī| prakarṣantī mayā dṛṣṭā rākṣasī vikṛtānanā
translation: रक्तवासिनी clad in red coloured clothes, विकृतानना with an ugly appearance, राक्षसी प्रमदा a  demoness, प्रहसन्तीव as if mocking at him, राजानम् the king, प्रकर्षन्ती dragging, मया by me, दृष्टा was beheld.
explanation: Finally I beheld a demoness attired in red clothes with an ugly appearance, dragging the king away as if mocking at him.

shloka_text: एवमेतन्मया दृष्टमिमां रात्रिं भयावहम्। अहं रामोऽथवा राजा लक्ष्मणो वा मरिष्यति।।2.69.17।।
transliteration: evametanmayā dṛṣṭamimāṃ rātriṃ bhayāvaham| ahaṃ rāmo'thavā rājā lakṣmaṇo vā mariṣyati
translation: एवम् in this manner, इमां रात्रिम् last night, भयावहम् frightening, एतत् this one, (मया)                           दृष्टम् was beheld (by me), अहम् either me, अथवा or, राजा the king, लक्ष्मणो वा or Lakshmana, मरिष्यति might die.
explanation: I had such a frightful dream last night. Either I, Rama, the king or Lakshmana might  die.

shloka_text: नरो यानेन य स्स्वप्ने स्वरयुक्तेन याति हि। अचिरात्तस्य धूमाग्रं चितायां सम्प्रदृश्यते।।2.69.18।।
transliteration: naro yānena ya ssvapne svarayuktena yāti hi| acirāttasya dhūmāgraṃ citāyāṃ sampradṛśyate
translation: स्वप्ने in the dream, यः any one, नरः human, रस्वयुक्तेन yoked to asses, यानेन by carriage, याति sets out, अचिरात् in a short time, चितायाम् on the funeral pyre, तस्य his, धूमाग्रम् wreath of smoke of his deadbody ascending, सम्प्रदृश्यते will be seen.
explanation: If one beholds in a dream a person setting out on a carriage yoked to asses, the wreath of smoke ascending from his funeral pyre will be seen soon.

shloka_text: एतन्निमित्तं दीनोऽहं तन्नवः प्रतिपूजये। शुष्यतीव च मे कण्ठः न स्वस्थमिव मे मनः।।2.69.19।।
transliteration: etannimittaṃ dīno'haṃ tannavaḥ pratipūjaye| śuṣyatīva ca me kaṇṭhaḥ na svasthamiva me manaḥ
translation: अहम् I, एतन्निमित्तम् for this reason, दीनः am desolate, तत् therefore, वः all of you, न प्रतिपूजये not responded well, मे my, कण्ठः throat, शुष्यतीव च is as though getting parched up, मे my, मनः mind, न स्वस्थम् इव is as though uneasy.
explanation: So it is for this reason that I am desolate and cannot respond well to your conversation. It appears as if my throat is getting parched up and my mind is illdisposed.

shloka_text: न पश्यामि भयस्थानं भयं चैवोपधारये भ्रष्टश्च स्वरयोगो मे छाया चोपहता मम। जुगुप्सन्निव चाऽत्मानं न पश्यमि च कारणम्।।2.69.20।।
transliteration: na paśyāmi bhayasthānaṃ bhayaṃ caivopadhāraye bhraṣṭaśca svarayogo me chāyā copahatā mama| jugupsanniva cā'tmānaṃ na paśyami ca kāraṇam
translation: भयस्थानम् any reason for apprehension, नपश्यामि I do not see, भयं चैव fear alone, उपधारये am experiencing, मे my, स्वरयोगः voice, भ्रष्टः degenerated, मम my, छाया च appearance, उपहता haggard, आत्मानम् of my self, जुगुप्सन्निव as if I detest, कारणम् च reason, न पश्यामि cannot see.
explanation: I do not see any reason for apprehension but I experience only fear. My voice has degenerated. My appearance looks haggard. Without any reason whatsoever I detest myself.

shloka_text: इमां च दुस्स्वप्नगतिं निशाम्यतामनेकरूपामवितर्कितां पुरा। भयं महत्तद्धृदयान्नयाति मे विचिन्त्य राजानमचिन्तदर्शनम्।।2.69.21।।
transliteration: imāṃ ca dussvapnagatiṃ niśāmyatāmanekarūpāmavitarkitāṃ purā| bhayaṃ mahattaddhṛdayānnayāti me vicintya rājānamacintadarśanam
translation: अनेकरूपाम् of several images, पुरा formerly, अतर्किताम् unthought of, ताम् such, इमाम् this, दुःस्वप्नगतिम् the course of this nightmare, निशाम्य having perceived, राजानम् the king, अचिन्त्यदर्शनम् as incomprehensible view, विचिन्त्य having thought of, महत् great, तत् that, भयम् fear, मे हृदयात् from my heart, न याति does not go.
explanation: On observing the course of this nightmare, with all those images formerly unconceived and having thought of the king's incomprehensible presence, a great fear that has gripped my heart does not leave me. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनसप्ततितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyninth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki

shloka_text: भरते ब्रुवति स्वप्नं दूतास्ते क्लान्तवाहनाः। प्रविश्यासह्यपरिखं रम्यं राजगृहं पुरम्।।2.70.1।। समागम्य तु राज्ञा च राजपुत्रेण चार्चिताः राज्ञः पादौ गृहीत्वा तु तमूचुर्भरतं वचः।।2.70.2।।
transliteration: bharate bruvati svapnaṃ dūtāste klāntavāhanāḥ| praviśyāsahyaparikhaṃ ramyaṃ rājagṛhaṃ puram samāgamya tu rājñā ca rājaputreṇa cārcitāḥ rājñaḥ pādau gṛhītvā tu tamūcurbharataṃ vacaḥ
translation: भरते Bharata, स्वप्नं about the dream, ब्रुवति while relating, क्लान्तवाहना: men with their vehicles (horses) weary, दूताः messengers, असह्यपरिखम् impassable moat, रम्यम् lovely, राजगृहम् Rajagriha, पुरम् city, प्रविश्य having entered, राज्ञा च with Kekaya king, राजपुत्रेण with king's son, Yuddhajit, समागम्य having met, अर्चिताः were honoured, राज्ञः king's,पादौ feet, गृहीत्वा having touched with reverence, तं भरतम् addressing that Bharata, वचः words, ऊचुः.told.
explanation: While Bharata was relating his dream, the mounted messengers (from Ayodhya) with their weary horses entered the lovely city of Rajagriha  surrounded by an impassable moat. There they met the king of Kekaya country and his son, Yuddhajit and were received with honour. Touching the feet of the king with reverence, they  said to Bharata:
comments: Messengers from Ayodhya arrive as Bharata was describing his nightmare to his friends -- the message of Vasistha is conveyed to Bharata to hurry back to Ayodhya -- departure of Bharata and Satrughna to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: भरते ब्रुवति स्वप्नं दूतास्ते क्लान्तवाहनाः। प्रविश्यासह्यपरिखं रम्यं राजगृहं पुरम्।।2.70.1।। समागम्य तु राज्ञा च राजपुत्रेण चार्चिताः राज्ञः पादौ गृहीत्वा तु तमूचुर्भरतं वचः।।2.70.2।।
transliteration: bharate bruvati svapnaṃ dūtāste klāntavāhanāḥ| praviśyāsahyaparikhaṃ ramyaṃ rājagṛhaṃ puram samāgamya tu rājñā ca rājaputreṇa cārcitāḥ rājñaḥ pādau gṛhītvā tu tamūcurbharataṃ vacaḥ
translation: भरते Bharata, स्वप्नं about the dream, ब्रुवति while relating, क्लान्तवाहना: men with their vehicles (horses) weary, दूताः messengers, असह्यपरिखम् impassable moat, रम्यम् lovely, राजगृहम् Rajagriha, पुरम् city, प्रविश्य having entered, राज्ञा च with Kekaya king, राजपुत्रेण with king's son, Yuddhajit, समागम्य having met, अर्चिताः were honoured, राज्ञः king's,पादौ feet, गृहीत्वा having touched with reverence, तं भरतम् addressing that Bharata, वचः words, ऊचुः.told.
explanation: While Bharata was relating his dream, the mounted messengers (from Ayodhya) with their weary horses entered the lovely city of Rajagriha  surrounded by an impassable moat. There they met the king of Kekaya country and his son, Yuddhajit and were received with honour. Touching the feet of the king with reverence, they  said to Bharata:

shloka_text: पुरोहितस्त्वां कुशलं प्राह सर्वे च मन्त्रिणः। त्वरमाणश्च निर्याहि कृत्यमात्ययिकं त्वया।।2.70.3।।
transliteration: purohitastvāṃ kuśalaṃ prāha sarve ca mantriṇaḥ| tvaramāṇaśca niryāhi kṛtyamātyayikaṃ tvayā
translation: पुरोहितः the family priest (Vasistha), त्वाम् about your, कुशलम् welfare, प्राह enquired, सर्वे  all, मन्त्रिणश्च counsellors also, त्वरमाणः च immediately, निर्याहि you may return, त्वया by you,  आत्ययिकम् urgent matter, कृत्यम्  to be attended.
explanation: The family priest (Vasistha) and all the counsellors have enquired about your welfare. You must return immediately. There is an urgent matter to be attended by you.

shloka_text: इमानि च महार्हाणि वस्त्राण्याभरणानि च। प्रतिगृह्य विशालक्ष मातुलस्य च दापय।।2.70.4।।
transliteration: imāni ca mahārhāṇi vastrāṇyābharaṇāni ca| pratigṛhya viśālakṣa mātulasya ca dāpaya
translation: विशालाक्ष largeeyed one, (Bharata), इमानि these, महार्हाणि precious, वस्त्राणि raiments, आभरणानि च ornaments, प्रतिगृह्य having accepted, मातुलस्य to your maternal uncle, दापय give, विशालाक्ष O largeeyed one (Bharata)
explanation: Oh largeeyed one (Bharata) you are asked to take these excellent raiments and precious ornaments and bestow them on your maternal uncle (said the messengers).

shloka_text: अत्र विशंतिकोट्यस्तु नृपतेर्मातुलस्य ते। दशकोट्यस्तु सम्पूर्णास्तथैव च नृपात्मज।।2.70.5।।
transliteration: atra viśaṃtikoṭyastu nṛpatermātulasya te| daśakoṭyastu sampūrṇāstathaiva ca nṛpātmaja
translation: नृपात्मज O prince Bharata, अत्र among this, विंशतिकोट्यः twenty crore, नृपतेः for the king, तथैव च similarly, सम्पूर्णाः complete, दशकोट्यस्तु ten crores, ते to your, मातुलस्य to be given to your maternal uncle.
explanation: O prince these gifts worth twenty crore are intended for the king and the rest of the gifts worth ten crore for your maternal uncle.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य तु तत्सर्वं स्वनुरक्त स्सुहृज्जने। दूतानुवाच भरतः कामैस्सम्प्रतिपूज्य तान्।।2.70.6।।
transliteration: pratigṛhya tu tatsarvaṃ svanurakta ssuhṛjjane| dūtānuvāca bharataḥ kāmaissampratipūjya tān
translation: सुहृज्जने the relatives and friends, स्वनुरक्तः who is very affectionate, भरतः Bharata, तत् that, सर्वम् all, प्रतिगृह्य having received, तान् दूतान् those messengers, कामैः what they liked, सम्प्रतिपूज्य in return honouring them, उवाच said.
explanation: Affectionate towards his relatives and friends, Bharata received all those gifts and in return honoured those messengers with things they liked, asking them:

shloka_text: कच्चित्सुकुशली राजा पिता दशरथो मम। कच्चिच्चारोगता रामे लक्ष्मणे च महात्मनि।।2.70.7।।
transliteration: kaccitsukuśalī rājā pitā daśaratho mama| kacciccārogatā rāme lakṣmaṇe ca mahātmani
translation: मम पिता my father, राजा दशरथः king Dasaratha, कच्चित् I hope, सकुशली doing well, रामे Rama, महात्मनि great, लक्ष्मणे च in Lakshmana also, अरोगता good health, कच्चित् I hope.
explanation: I hope my father, Dasaratha is doing well and revered Rama and Lakshmana are in good health

shloka_text: आर्या च धर्मनिरता धर्मज्ञा धर्मदर्शिनी। अरोगा चापि कौसल्या माता रामस्य धीमतः।।2.70.8।।
transliteration: āryā ca dharmaniratā dharmajñā dharmadarśinī| arogā cāpi kausalyā mātā rāmasya dhīmataḥ
translation: आर्या च venerable lady indeed, धर्मनिरता devoted to righteousness, धर्मज्ञा adept in  righteousness, धर्मदर्शिनी observes the prescribed code of conduct, धीमतः sagacious, रामस्य Rama's, माता mother, कौशल्या Kausalya, अपि अरोगा is she keeping good health.
explanation: (I hope) Kausalya mother of the sagacious Rama the venerable lady devoted to righteousness one who knows the ways of righteousness and observes the prescribed code of conduct, is keeping sound  health.

shloka_text: कच्चित्सुमित्रा धर्मज्ञा जननी लक्ष्मणस्य या। शत्रुघ्नस्य च वीरस्य साऽरोगा चापि मध्यमा।।2.70.9।।
transliteration: kaccitsumitrā dharmajñā jananī lakṣmaṇasya yā| śatrughnasya ca vīrasya sā'rogā cāpi madhyamā
translation: या that, धर्मज्ञा knowledgeable in the ways of righteousness, लक्ष्मणस्य Lakshmana's, वीरस्य one who is full of valour, शत्रुघ्नस्य च Satrughna's, जननी mother, मध्यमा middle mother, सा सुमित्रापि that Sumitra, कच्चित् I hope, अरोगा is free from illness.
explanation: I hope my mother Sumitra (the middle one) who is familiar with the ways of righteousness, the mother of valiant Lakshmana and Satrughna, is enjoying good health.

shloka_text: आत्मकामा सदा चण्डी क्रोधना प्राज्ञमानिनी। अरोगा चापि मे माता कैकेयी किमुवाच ह।।2.70.10।।
transliteration: ātmakāmā sadā caṇḍī krodhanā prājñamāninī| arogā cāpi me mātā kaikeyī kimuvāca ha
translation: आत्मकामा ever intent on her welfare, सदा always, चण्डी irascible, क्रोधना wrathful, प्राज्ञमानिनी who is proud of her intelligence, मे माता my mother, कैकेयी Kaikeyi, अपि अरोगा is she free from illness, किम् what, उवाच ह did she say?
explanation: And what about my mother Kaikeyi, ever intent on her own wellbeing, wrathful, irascible and proud of her intelligence? Is she maintaining sound health?

shloka_text: एवमुक्तास्तु ते दूताः भरतेन महात्मना। ऊचुस्सप्रश्रयं वाक्यमिदं तं भरतं तदा।।2.70.11।।
transliteration: evamuktāstu te dūtāḥ bharatena mahātmanā| ūcussapraśrayaṃ vākyamidaṃ taṃ bharataṃ tadā
translation: महात्मना magnanimous, भरतेन by Bharata, एवम् in this way, उक्ताः uttered, ते दूताः those messengers, तदा then, तं भरतम् addressing that Bharata, सप्रश्रयम् respectfully, इदं these  वाक्यम् (वचः) words, ऊचुः spoke.
explanation: Having listened to the words of that magnanimous Bharata, those messengers addressed him  gracefully with these words.

shloka_text: कुशलास्ते नरव्याघ्र येषां कुशलमिच्छसि। श्रीश्च त्वां वृणुते पद्मा युज्यतां चापि ते रथः।।2.70.12।।
transliteration: kuśalāste naravyāghra yeṣāṃ kuśalamicchasi| śrīśca tvāṃ vṛṇute padmā yujyatāṃ cāpi te rathaḥ
translation: नरव्याघ्र tiger among men (Bharata), येषाम् whose, कुशलम् welfare, इच्छसि you are  enquiring, ते they, कुशलाः are doing well, श्रीः prosperity, पद्मा goddess of wealth, त्वाम्  you, वृणुते chosen you, ते to you, रथः chariot, युज्यतां चापि may be yoked.
explanation: O tiger among men (Bharata) those of whose welfare you are enquiring are all doing well. May the goddess of wealth and prosperity await you and let your chariot be yoked.

shloka_text: भरतश्चापि तान् दूतानेवमुक्तोऽभ्यभाषत। आपृच्चेऽहं महाराजं दूतास्सन्त्वरयन्ति माम्।।2.70.13।।
transliteration: bharataścāpi tān dūtānevamukto'bhyabhāṣata| āpṛcce'haṃ mahārājaṃ dūtāssantvarayanti mām
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः uttered, भरतश्चापि Bharata, तान् दूतान् to those messengers, अभ्यभाषत said, माम् me, दूताः messengers, सन्त्वरयन्ति are hastening me up, अहम् I, महाराजम् great king (of Kekaya), आपृच्छे shall seek permission to leave.
explanation: Having thus been addressed, Bharata said to the messengers. Let me seek the permission of the great king of Kekaya to leave and say goodbye, informing him that the messengers are hastening me up.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु तान् दूतान्भरतः पार्थिवात्मजः। दूतै स्सञ्चोदितो वाक्यं मातामहमुवाच ह।।2.70.14।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu tān dūtānbharataḥ pārthivātmajaḥ| dūtai ssañcodito vākyaṃ mātāmahamuvāca ha
translation: दूतैः messengers, सञ्चोदितः having been pressed, पार्थिवात्मजः king's son, भरतः Bharata,  तान् दूतान् to those messengers, एवम् in the aforesaid manner, उक्त्वा having said, मातामहम् addressing maternal grandfather, वाक्यम् these words, उवाच ह said.
explanation: Having addressed the messengers who were pressing him to leave (for Ayodhya) Bharata said to his maternal grandfather:

shloka_text: राजन् पितुर्गमिष्यामि सकाशं दूतचोदितः। पुनरप्यहमेष्यामि यदा मे त्वं स्मरिष्यसि।।2.70.15।।
transliteration: rājan piturgamiṣyāmi sakāśaṃ dūtacoditaḥ| punarapyahameṣyāmi yadā me tvaṃ smariṣyasi
translation: राजन् O king, दूतचोदितः urged by the messengers, पितुः father's, सकाशम् for, गमिष्यामि I shall go, त्वम् you, मे for me, यदा whenever, स्मरिष्यसि remember, पुनरपि again, अहं एष्यामि I shall come.
explanation: O king, urged by these messengers I wish to go to my father. I shall come back again (from Ayodhya) whenever you  remember me.

shloka_text: भरतेनैवमुक्तस्तु नृपो मातामहस्तदा। तमुवाच शुभं वाक्यं शिरस्याघ्राय राघवम्।।2.70.16।।
transliteration: bharatenaivamuktastu nṛpo mātāmahastadā| tamuvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ śirasyāghrāya rāghavam
translation: तदा then, भरतेन by Bharata, एवम् thus, उक्तः urged, मातामहः the maternal grandfather, नृपः king (of Kekaya), तम् that, राघवम् to one of Raghu dynasty (Bharata), शिरसि on his head, आघ्राय having smelt, शुभम् auspicious, वाक्यम् words, उवाच spoke.
explanation: Then the  king of Kekaya, the maternal grandfather of Bharata, having heard the words of the scion of the Raghu dynasty (Bharata), kissed him on his forehead and spoke these auspicious words:

shloka_text: गच्छ तातानुजाने त्वां कैकेयीसुप्रजास्त्वया। मातरं कुशलं ब्रूयाः पितरं च परन्तप।।2.70.17।।
transliteration: gaccha tātānujāne tvāṃ kaikeyīsuprajāstvayā| mātaraṃ kuśalaṃ brūyāḥ pitaraṃ ca parantapa
translation: तात O child, गच्छ you may go, त्वाम् you, अनुजाने I permit, त्वया by you, कैकेयी Kaikeyi, सुप्रजाः has a worthy son, परन्तप O slayer of enemies, मातरम् your mother, पितरं च and father, कुशलम् welfare, ब्रूयाः convey.
explanation: You may go, my child I permit you to leave. Kaikeyi has a worthy son in you. O slayer of enemies convey my best wishes to your mother and father.

shloka_text: पुरोहितं च कुशलं ये चान्ये द्विजसत्तमाः। तौ च तात महेष्वासौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।।2.70.18।।
transliteration: purohitaṃ ca kuśalaṃ ye cānye dvijasattamāḥ| tau ca tāta maheṣvāsau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
translation: तात O child, पुरोहितम् to the family priest (Vasistha), अन्ये and others, ये द्विजसत्तमाः those illustrious brahmins, महेष्वासौ great bowmen (Rama and Lakshmana), कुशलम् best wishes, (ब्रूहि convey).
explanation: My child, convey my best wishes, too, to your family priest Vasistha and other illustrious brahmins and also to those two great bowmen (Rama and Lakshmana).

shloka_text: तस्मै हस्त्युत्तमांश्चित्रान्कम्बलानजिनानि च। अभिसत्कृत्य कैकेयो भरताय धनं ददौ।।2.70.19।।
transliteration: tasmai hastyuttamāṃścitrānkambalānajināni ca| abhisatkṛtya kaikeyo bharatāya dhanaṃ dadau
translation: कैकेयः king of Kekaya, तस्मै भरताय to that Bharata, हस्त्युत्तमान् wellbred elephants, चित्रान्  of manycoloured, कम्बलान् blankets, अजिनानि च antelope skins, धनम् riches, अभिसत्कृत्य  having felicitated, ददौ bestowed.
explanation: The king of Kekaya felicitated Bharata, out of affection and bestowed on him wellbred elephants, manycoloured blankets, antelope skins and riches.

shloka_text: रुक्मनिष्कसहस्रे द्वे षोडशाश्वशतानि च। सत्कृत्य कैकयीपुत्रं केकयो धनमादिशत्।।2.70.20।।
transliteration: rukmaniṣkasahasre dve ṣoḍaśāśvaśatāni ca| satkṛtya kaikayīputraṃ kekayo dhanamādiśat
translation: केकयः king of Kekaya, कैकयीपुत्रं son of Kaikeyi, सत्कृत्य having honoured, द्वे two, रुक्मनिष्कसहस्रे two thousand gold coins, षोडश अश्वशतानि च sixteen hundred  horses also, धनम् as wealth, आदिशत् bestowed.
explanation: King of Kekaya generously gave to the son of Kaikeyi (Bharata) in his honour two thousand gold coins and  sixteen hundred horses.

shloka_text: तथाऽमात्यानभिप्रेतान्विश्वास्यांश्च गुणान्वितान्। ददावश्वपतिः क्षिप्रं भरतायानुयायिनः।।2.70.21।।
transliteration: tathā'mātyānabhipretānviśvāsyāṃśca guṇānvitān| dadāvaśvapatiḥ kṣipraṃ bharatāyānuyāyinaḥ
translation: तथा in the same way, अश्वपतिः Ashwapati, भरताय for Bharata, अभिप्रेतान् eamenable, विश्वास्यान् trustworthy men, गुणान्वितान् virtuous men, अमात्यान् counsellors, अनुयायिनः as companions, ददौ gave.
explanation: Similarly his maternal uncle Ashwapati quickly presented him amenable, trustworthy and virtuous counsellors as companions on his return journey.

shloka_text: ऐरावतानैन्द्रशिरान्नागान्वै प्रियदर्शनान्। खरान् श्रीघ्रान्सुसंयुक्तान्मातुलोऽस्मै धनं ददौ।।2.70.22।।
transliteration: airāvatānaindraśirānnāgānvai priyadarśanān| kharān śrīghrānsusaṃyuktānmātulo'smai dhanaṃ dadau
translation: मातुलः maternal uncle, अस्मै for him (Bharata), ऐरावतान् born in Iravata mountain, ऐन्द्रशिरान्  born in Indrasira mountain, प्रियदर्शनान् beautiful to behold, नागान् elephants, शीघ्रान् swift moving, सुसंयुक्तान् welltrained, खरान् asses, धनम् riches, ददौ gave.
explanation: His maternal uncle gave him the wealth of goodlooking elephants born in Iravata and Indrasira mountains and swiftmoving and welltrained asses which can be yoked easily. He gave riches too.

shloka_text: अन्तःपुरेऽति संवृद्धान् व्याघ्रवीर्यबलान्वितान्। दंष्ट्राऽऽयुधान्महाकायान् शुनश्चोपायनं ददौ।।2.70.23।।
transliteration: antaḥpure'ti saṃvṛddhān vyāghravīryabalānvitān| daṃṣṭrā''yudhānmahākāyān śunaścopāyanaṃ dadau
translation: अन्तःपुरे in the inner apartment, अति संवृद्धान् wellraised, व्याघ्रवीर्यबलान्वितान् having the  strength and courage of tigers, दंष्ट्राऽऽयुधान् whose fangs are their weapons spears, महाकायान् of huge body, शुनश्च dogs also, उपायनम् as gift, ददौ gave.
explanation: He also gave him a gift of wellraised dogs of the inner apartment hugebodied with the strength and courage of tigers who used their fangs as weapons.

shloka_text: स दत्तं केकयेन्द्रेण धनं तन्नाभ्यनन्दत। भरतः कैकयीपुत्रो गमनत्वरया तदा।।2.70.24।।
transliteration: sa dattaṃ kekayendreṇa dhanaṃ tannābhyanandata| bharataḥ kaikayīputro gamanatvarayā tadā
translation: तदा then, गमनत्वरया in a hurry to depart, सः that, कैकयीपुत्रः son of Kaikeyi, भरतः Bharata, केकयेन्द्रेण by the king of Kekaya, दत्तम् given, धनम् wealth, नाभ्यनन्दत did not delight him.
explanation: All the wealth given by the king of Kekaya did not delight Bharata, son of Kaikeyi who was in a hurry to depart for Ayodhya.

shloka_text: बभूव ह्यस्य हृदये चिन्ता सुमहती तदा। त्वरया चापि दूतानां स्वप्नस्यापि च दर्शनात्।।2.70.25।।
transliteration: babhūva hyasya hṛdaye cintā sumahatī tadā| tvarayā cāpi dūtānāṃ svapnasyāpi ca darśanāt
translation: दूतानाम् messengers', त्वरया चापि with the haste to depart, स्वप्नस्य dream's, दर्शनाच्चापि also due to beholding, तदा then, अस्य his, हृदये in the heart, सुमहती intense, चिन्ता anxiety, बभूव हि filled with.
explanation: Then his heart was filled with extreme anxiety due to the haste of the messengers to depart and also due to the dream he had.

shloka_text: स स्ववेश्माभ्यतिक्रम्य नरनागाश्वसंवृतम्। प्रपेदे सुमहच्छ्रीमान्राजमार्गमनुत्तमम्।।2.70.26।।
transliteration: sa svaveśmābhyatikramya naranāgāśvasaṃvṛtam| prapede sumahacchrīmānrājamārgamanuttamam
translation: श्रीमान् prosperous, सः he (Bharata), नरनागाश्वसंवृतम् thronged with men, elephants and horses, सुमहत् great, स्ववेश्म his residence, अभ्यतिक्रम्य having passed by, अनुत्तमम् incomparable, राजमार्गम् royal highway, प्रपेदे obtained.
explanation: Prosperous Bharata on leaving his residence, passed through incomparable royal highway thronged with men, elephants and horses.

shloka_text: अभ्यतीत्य ततोऽपश्यदन्तःपुरमुदारधीः। ततस्तद्भरतश्श्रीमानाविवेशानिवारितः।।2.70.27।।
transliteration: abhyatītya tato'paśyadantaḥpuramudāradhīḥ| tatastadbharataśśrīmānāviveśānivāritaḥ
translation: उदारधीः nobleminded, अभ्यतीत्य having crossed, ततः thereafter, अन्तःपुरम् inner apartment, अपश्यत् saw, ततः then, श्रीमान् prosperous, भरतः Bharata, अनिवारितः without any restriction, तत् in that apartment, आविवेश entered.
explanation: Then the nobleminded, prosperous Bharata, on leaving the  highway, saw  the inner apartment of the king which he entered unhindered.
