shloka_text: स मातामहमापृच्छ्य मातुलं च युधाजितम्। रथमारुह्य भरतश्शत्रुघ्नसहितो ययौ।।2.70.28।।
transliteration: sa mātāmahamāpṛcchya mātulaṃ ca yudhājitam| rathamāruhya bharataśśatrughnasahito yayau
translation: सः भरतः that Bharata, मतामहम् maternal grandfather, मातुलम् uncle, युधाजितम् Yaddhajit, आपृच्छ्य taking leave, शत्रुघ्नसहितः along with Satrughna, रथम् chariot, आरुह्य having ascended, ययौ went.
explanation: Thus having taken leave of his maternal grandfather and uncle Yuddhajit, Bharata accompanied by Satrughna boarded the chariot and went along.

shloka_text: रथान्मण्डल चक्रांश्च योजयित्वा परश्शतम्। उष्ट्र गोऽश्वबलैर्भृत्या भरतं यान्तमन्वयुः।।2.70.29।।
transliteration: rathānmaṇḍala cakrāṃśca yojayitvā paraśśatam| uṣṭra go'śvabalairbhṛtyā bharataṃ yāntamanvayuḥ
translation: भृत्याः servants, मण्डलचक्रांश्च of wellrounded wheels, परश्शतान् more than a hundred, रथान् chariots, योजयित्वा harnessing, उष्ट्रगोश्वबलैः with camels, oxen, and horses, यान्तम् going on, भरतम् Bharata, अन्ययुः followed.
explanation: And the servants harnessing more than a hundred chariots of wellrounded wheels and also camels, oxen and horses followed Bharata who started off.

shloka_text: बलेन गुप्तो भरतो महात्मा सहार्यकस्याऽत्मसमैरमात्यैः। आदाय शत्रुघ्नमपेतशत्रुर्गृहाद्ययौ सिद्ध इवेन्द्रलोकात्।।2.70.30।।
transliteration: balena gupto bharato mahātmā sahāryakasyā'tmasamairamātyaiḥ| ādāya śatrughnamapetaśatrurgṛhādyayau siddha ivendralokāt
translation: बलेन with army, गुप्तः under the protection of, महात्मा illustrious, अपेतशत्रुः devoid of enemies, भरतः Bharata, आत्मसमैः like himself, अमात्यैस्सह accompanied by ministers, शत्रुघ्नम् Satrughna, आदाय having taken, आर्यकस्य venerable grandfather's, गृहात् from house, सिद्ध: like siddha, इन्द्रलोकादिव from the regions of Indra, ययौ went.
explanation: Under the protection of the army, the illustrious Bharata who was devoid of enemies, accompanied by ministers who were comparable to him and Satrughna, departed from his venerable grandfather's house like a siddha leaving the regions of Indra. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्ततितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventieth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿﻿﻿[Crossing many rivers, forests and territories Bharata reaches Ayodhya -- witnesses scenes of dull desolation charged with an atmosphere of apprehensions -- enters the palace dejected] स प्राङ्मुखो राजगृहादभिनिर्याय राघवः। ततस्सुदामां द्युतिमान् सन्तीर्यावेक्ष्य तां नदीम्।।2.71.1।। ह्लादिनीं दूरपारां च प्रत्यक्स्रोतस्तरङ्गिणीम्। शतद्रूमतरच्छ्रीमान्नदीमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः।।2.71.2।।
transliteration: ﻿﻿﻿﻿[Crossing many rivers, forests and territories Bharata reaches Ayodhya -- witnesses scenes of dull desolation charged with an atmosphere of apprehensions -- enters the palace dejected] sa prāṅmukho rājagṛhādabhiniryāya rāghavaḥ| tatassudāmāṃ dyutimān santīryāvekṣya tāṃ nadīm hlādinīṃ dūrapārāṃ ca pratyaksrotastaraṅgiṇīm| śatadrūmataracchrīmānnadīmikṣvākunandanaḥ
translation: ﻿﻿﻿﻿ द्युतिमान् the glorious, श्रीमान् the auspicious, इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः the delight of the Ikshvaku race, सः राघवः that (Bharata) of Raghu dynasty, राजगृहात् from Rajagriha, प्राङ्मुखः eastwards, अभिनिर्याय set out, ततः then, ताम् that, सुदामाम् Sudama, नदीम् river, आवेक्ष्य seen, सन्तीर्य having crossed, ह्लादिनीम् river Hladini, दूरपाराम् very wide, प्रत्यक्स्रोतस्तरङ्गिणीम् flowing westwards crested with waves, शतद्रूम् नदीम् river Satadru (Satlej), अतरत् crossed.
explanation: ﻿﻿﻿﻿ Glorious and prosperous prince Bharata, the delight of the Ikshvaku race, set out from Rajagriha, took the eastern direction, and observing the course of the river Sudama crossed Hladini and Satadru rivers which were very wide and flowing westwards crested with waves.
comments: Bharata's homeward journey from Rajagriha to Ayodhya -- the many rivers, forests and regions he crosses on the way -- after seven nights he beholds Ayodhya bereft of its former joy and splendour -- alarmed by the lifeless and ominous sights in the city he dreads some calamity -- he enters the royal palace with a grieving and apprehensive heart.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿स प्राङ्मुखो राजगृहादभिनिर्याय राघवः। ततस्सुदामां द्युतिमान् सन्तीर्यावेक्ष्य तां नदीम्।।2.71.1।। ह्लादिनीं दूरपारां च प्रत्यक्स्रोतस्तरङ्गिणीम्। शतद्रूमतरच्छ्रीमान्नदीमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः।।2.71.2।।
transliteration: ﻿﻿sa prāṅmukho rājagṛhādabhiniryāya rāghavaḥ| tatassudāmāṃ dyutimān santīryāvekṣya tāṃ nadīm hlādinīṃ dūrapārāṃ ca pratyaksrotastaraṅgiṇīm| śatadrūmataracchrīmānnadīmikṣvākunandanaḥ
translation: ﻿﻿ द्युतिमान् the glorious, श्रीमान् the auspicious, इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः the delight of the Ikshvaku race, सः राघवः that (Bharata) of Raghu dynasty, राजगृहात् from Rajagriha, प्राङ्मुखः eastwards, अभिनिर्याय set out, ततः then, ताम् that, सुदामाम् Sudama, नदीम् river, आवेक्ष्य seen, सन्तीर्य having crossed, ह्लादिनीम् river Hladini, दूरपाराम् very wide, प्रत्यक्स्रोतस्तरङ्गिणीम् flowing westwards crested with waves, शतद्रूम् नदीम् river Satadru (Satlej), अतरत् crossed.
explanation: ﻿﻿ Glorious and prosperous prince Bharata, the delight of the Ikshvaku race, set out from Rajagriha, took the eastern direction, and observing the course of the river Sudama crossed Hladini and Satadru rivers which were very wide and flowing westwards crested with waves.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿ऐलाधाने नदीं तीर्त्वा प्राप्य चापरपर्पटान्। शिलामकुर्वतीं तीर्त्वा आग्नेयं शल्यकर्षणम्।।2.71.3।। सत्यसन्धश्शुचिश्श्रीमान्प्रेक्षमाण श्शिलावहाम्। अत्ययात्स महाशैलान्वनं चैत्ररथं प्रति।।2.71.4।।
transliteration: ﻿﻿ailādhāne nadīṃ tīrtvā prāpya cāparaparpaṭān| śilāmakurvatīṃ tīrtvā āgneyaṃ śalyakarṣaṇam satyasandhaśśuciśśrīmānprekṣamāṇa śśilāvahām| atyayātsa mahāśailānvanaṃ caitrarathaṃ prati
translation: ﻿﻿ सत्यसन्ध: one who is always true to his word, शुचिः purehearted, श्रीमान् handsome, सः he (Bharata), ऐलाधाने in Eladhana, नदीम् river, तीर्त्वा crossed, अपरपर्पटान् Aparaparpata region, प्राप्य च having reached, शिलाम् hill, अकुर्वतीम् originating, तीर्त्वा having crossed, आग्नेयम् towards northeast, शल्यकर्षणम् Salyakarsna, शिलावहाम् Silavaha, प्रेक्षमाणः observing, चैत्ररथं वनं प्रति towards a forest called Chaitraratha, महाशैलान् great mountains, अत्ययात् went beyond.
explanation: ﻿﻿ Bharata, ever true to his word, handsome and purehearted, reached Aparaparpata region and crossed river Satadru at Eladhana, the mountain in which river Silavaha originates. Then he traversed Salyakarsna regions in the northeast, observing the course of the Silavaha and went beyond the great mountains in the direction of the forest called Chaitraratha.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿ऐलाधाने नदीं तीर्त्वा प्राप्य चापरपर्पटान्। शिलामकुर्वतीं तीर्त्वा आग्नेयं शल्यकर्षणम्।।2.71.3।। सत्यसन्धश्शुचिश्श्रीमान्प्रेक्षमाण श्शिलावहाम्। अत्ययात्स महाशैलान्वनं चैत्ररथं प्रति।।2.71.4।।
transliteration: ﻿﻿ailādhāne nadīṃ tīrtvā prāpya cāparaparpaṭān| śilāmakurvatīṃ tīrtvā āgneyaṃ śalyakarṣaṇam satyasandhaśśuciśśrīmānprekṣamāṇa śśilāvahām| atyayātsa mahāśailānvanaṃ caitrarathaṃ prati
translation: ﻿﻿ सत्यसन्ध: one who is always true to his word, शुचिः purehearted, श्रीमान् handsome, सः he (Bharata), ऐलाधाने in Eladhana, नदीम् river, तीर्त्वा crossed, अपरपर्पटान् Aparaparpata region, प्राप्य च having reached, शिलाम् hill, अकुर्वतीम् originating, तीर्त्वा having crossed, आग्नेयम् towards northeast, शल्यकर्षणम् Salyakarsna, शिलावहाम् Silavaha, प्रेक्षमाणः observing, चैत्ररथं वनं प्रति towards a forest called Chaitraratha, महाशैलान् great mountains, अत्ययात् went beyond.
explanation: ﻿﻿ Bharata, ever true to his word, handsome and purehearted, reached Aparaparpata region and crossed river Satadru at Eladhana, the mountain in which river Silavaha originates. Then he traversed Salyakarsna regions in the northeast, observing the course of the Silavaha and went beyond the great mountains in the direction of the forest called Chaitraratha.

shloka_text: ﻿सरस्वतीं च गङ्गां च युग्मेन प्रतिपद्यच। उत्तरान्वीरमत्स्यानां भारुण्डं प्राविशद्वनम्।।2.71.5।।
transliteration: ﻿sarasvatīṃ ca gaṅgāṃ ca yugmena pratipadyaca| uttarānvīramatsyānāṃ bhāruṇḍaṃ prāviśadvanam
translation: ﻿ सरस्वतीं च Saraswati, गङ्गां च Ganga, युग्मेन at the confluence, प्रतिपद्य having arrived, वीरमत्स्यानाम् of Veeramatsya region, उत्तराम् to the north, भारुण्डं वनम् forest Bharunda, प्राविशत् entered.
explanation: ﻿ Arriving at the confluence of Saraswati and Ganga and traversing the north of Veeramatsya region, he entered the Bharunda forest.

shloka_text: ﻿वेगिनीं च कुलिङ्गाख्यां ह्लादिनीं पर्वताऽऽवृताम्। यमुनां प्राप्य सन्तीर्णः बलमाश्वासयत्तदा।।2.71.6।।
transliteration: ﻿veginīṃ ca kuliṅgākhyāṃ hlādinīṃ parvatā''vṛtām| yamunāṃ prāpya santīrṇaḥ balamāśvāsayattadā
translation: ﻿ वेगिनीम् rapidlyflowing, पर्वतावृताम् hillbound, ह्लादिनीम् pleasing to the mind, कुलिङ्गाख्याम् known as Kulinga, यमुनाम् Yamuna, प्राप्य having arrived, सन्तीर्णः he crossed, तदा then, बलम् army, आश्वासयत् made them rest.
explanation: ﻿ He crossed the swiftflowing river known as Kulinga surrounded by hills and pleasing to the mind. Thereafter on crossing Yamuna he made his army rest on the otherside.

shloka_text: ﻿सशीतीकृत्य तु गात्राणि क्लान्तानाश्वास्य वाजिनः। तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च प्रायादादाय चोदकम्।।2.71.7।।
transliteration: ﻿saśītīkṛtya tu gātrāṇi klāntānāśvāsya vājinaḥ| tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca prāyādādāya codakam
translation: ﻿ गात्राणि their limbs, शीतीकृत्य having cooled, क्लान्तान् weary, वाजिनः horses, आश्वास्य having refreshed, तत्र there, स्नात्वा having bathed, पीत्वा च and drinking, उदकम् water, आदाय took, प्रायात् set out.
explanation: ﻿ The weary horses rested and cooled their bodies. And they bathed and drank. They set out again refreshed taking with them a store of water.

shloka_text: ﻿राजपुत्रो महारण्यमनभीक्ष्णोपसेवितम्। भद्रो भद्रेण यानेन मारुतः खमिवात्ययात्।।2.71.8।।
transliteration: ﻿rājaputro mahāraṇyamanabhīkṣṇopasevitam| bhadro bhadreṇa yānena mārutaḥ khamivātyayāt
translation: ﻿ भद्रः the blessed one, राजपुत्रः prince (Bharata), अनभीक्ष्णोपसेवितम् uninhabited, महारण्यम् vast forest, भद्रेण by an excellent, यानेन on chariot, मारुतः windgod, खमिव like sky, अत्ययात् passed through.
explanation: ﻿ Then with the blessed prince (Bharata) on an excellent chariot, it (the army) moved through the vast and uninhabited forest like the god of wind passing through the sky.

shloka_text: ﻿भागीरथीं दुष्प्रतरामंशुधाने महानदीम्। उपायाद्राघवस्तूर्णं प्राग्वटे विश्रुते पुरे।।2.71.9।।
transliteration: ﻿bhāgīrathīṃ duṣpratarāmaṃśudhāne mahānadīm| upāyādrāghavastūrṇaṃ prāgvaṭe viśrute pure
translation: ﻿ राघवः the descendant of Raghu (Bharata), विश्रुते in the famous, प्राग्वटे Pragvata, पुरे city, अंशुधाने at a place known as Anshudhana, दुष्प्रतराम् difficult to cross, महानदीम् mighty river, भागीरथीम् Bhagirathi, तूर्णम् quickly, उपायात् reached.
explanation: ﻿ Bharata, the descendant of Raghu, knowing that the mighty river Bhagirathi was difficult to cross at a place known as Anshudhana, quickly reached the famous city of Pragvata.

shloka_text: ﻿स गङ्गां प्राग्वटे तीर्त्वा समायात्कुटिकोष्ठिकाम्। सबल स्तां स तीर्त्वाऽथ समायाद्धर्मवर्धनम्।।2.71.10।।
transliteration: ﻿sa gaṅgāṃ prāgvaṭe tīrtvā samāyātkuṭikoṣṭhikām| sabala stāṃ sa tīrtvā'tha samāyāddharmavardhanam
translation: ﻿ सः he, प्राग्वटे at Pragvata city, गङ्गाम् river Ganga, तीर्त्वा having crossed, कुटिकोष्ठिकाम् Kutikoshti river, समायात् reached, सः Bharata, सबलः with his army, ताम् that river, तीर्त्वा having crossed, अथ thereafter, धर्मवर्धनम् Dharmavardhana village, समायात् reached.
explanation: ﻿ With Ganga at Pragvata city and river Kutikoshtika crossed along with his army, he reached Dharmavardhana village.

shloka_text: ﻿तोरणं दक्षिणार्धेन जम्भूप्रस्थमुपागमत्। वरूथं च ययौ रम्यं ग्रामं दशरथात्मजः।।2.71.11।।
transliteration: ﻿toraṇaṃ dakṣiṇārdhena jambhūprasthamupāgamat| varūthaṃ ca yayau ramyaṃ grāmaṃ daśarathātmajaḥ
translation: ﻿ दशरथात्मजः son of Dasaratha, (Bharata), तोरणम् Torana region, दक्षिणार्थेन southern direction of, जम्बूप्रस्थम् Jambuprastha village, उपागमत् arrived, वरूथम् Varutha village, रम्यं pleasant, ग्रामं च village, ययौ obtained.
explanation: ﻿ Having traversed the southern end of Torana, the son of Dasaratha (Bharata) reached the beautiful Varutha village via Jambuprastha.

shloka_text: ﻿तत्र रम्ये वने वासं कृत्वाऽसौ प्राङ्मुखो ययौ। उद्यानमुज्जिहानायाः प्रियका यत्र पादपाः।।2.71.12।।
transliteration: ﻿tatra ramye vane vāsaṃ kṛtvā'sau prāṅmukho yayau| udyānamujjihānāyāḥ priyakā yatra pādapāḥ
translation: ﻿ असौ he (Bharata), अत्र there, रम्ये charming, वने forest, वासम् stay, कृत्वा having made, प्राङ्मुखः eastwards, यत्र where, प्रियकाः known as priyaka, पादपाः trees, उज्जिहानायाः Ujjihana, उद्यानम् garden, ययौ reached.
explanation: ﻿ He (Bharata) halted in that charming forest for a while, proceeded eastwards till he reached a place known as Ujjihana garden abounding in spriyaka trees.

shloka_text: ﻿सालांस्तु प्रियकान्प्राप्य शीघ्रानास्थाय वाजिनः। अनुज्ञाप्याथ भरतः वाहिनीं त्वरितो ययौ।।2.71.13।।
transliteration: ﻿sālāṃstu priyakānprāpya śīghrānāsthāya vājinaḥ| anujñāpyātha bharataḥ vāhinīṃ tvarito yayau
translation: ﻿ भरतः Bharata, सालान् sala trees, प्रियकान् priyaka trees, प्राप्य having reached, शीघ्रान् swiftrunning, वाजिनः horses, आस्थाय having harnessed, अथ thereafter, वाहिनीम् forces, अनुज्ञाप्य having commanded, त्वरितः quickly, ययौ set out.
explanation: ﻿ After reaching the groves of sala and priyaka trees, Bharata harnessed the swiftrunning horses to the chariot and ordered his forces to proceed fast.

shloka_text: ﻿वासं कृत्वा सर्वतीर्थे तीर्त्वा चोत्तानिकां नदीम्। अन्या नदीश्च विविधाः पार्वतीयैस्तुरङ्गमैः।।2.71.14।। हस्तिपृष्ठकमासाद्य कुटिकामत्यवर्तत। ततार च नरव्याघ्रो लौहित्ये स कपीवतीम्।।2.71.15।।
transliteration: ﻿vāsaṃ kṛtvā sarvatīrthe tīrtvā cottānikāṃ nadīm| anyā nadīśca vividhāḥ pārvatīyaisturaṅgamaiḥ hastipṛṣṭhakamāsādya kuṭikāmatyavartata| tatāra ca naravyāghro lauhitye sa kapīvatīm
translation: ﻿ सर्वतीर्थे in a place known as Sarvatirtha, वासम् halt, कृत्वा having made, उत्तानिकां नदीम् Uttanika river, विविधाः various, अन्याः others, नदीश्च rivers, पार्वतीयैः born in the mountains, तुरङ्गमैः on horses, तीर्त्वा having crossed, हस्तिपृष्ठकम् on an elephant, आसाद्य ascending, कुटिकाम् Kutika river, अत्यवर्तत crossed over, सः नरव्याघ्रः the tiger among men, लौहित्ये near Lauhitya, कपीवतीम् river Kapivati, ततार crossed.
explanation: ﻿ That tiger among men, Bharata halted at a place known as Sarvatirtha and crossed the Uttanika and various other rivers with the help of hillborn horses. He crossed the Kutika river on an elephant the river Kapivati at a place known as Lauhitya.

shloka_text: ﻿वासं कृत्वा सर्वतीर्थे तीर्त्वा चोत्तानिकां नदीम्। अन्या नदीश्च विविधाः पार्वतीयैस्तुरङ्गमैः।।2.71.14।। हस्तिपृष्ठकमासाद्य कुटिकामत्यवर्तत। ततार च नरव्याघ्रो लौहित्ये स कपीवतीम्।।2.71.15।।
transliteration: ﻿vāsaṃ kṛtvā sarvatīrthe tīrtvā cottānikāṃ nadīm| anyā nadīśca vividhāḥ pārvatīyaisturaṅgamaiḥ hastipṛṣṭhakamāsādya kuṭikāmatyavartata| tatāra ca naravyāghro lauhitye sa kapīvatīm
translation: ﻿ सर्वतीर्थे in a place known as Sarvatirtha, वासम् halt, कृत्वा having made, उत्तानिकां नदीम् Uttanika river, विविधाः various, अन्याः others, नदीश्च rivers, पार्वतीयैः born in the mountains, तुरङ्गमैः on horses, तीर्त्वा having crossed, हस्तिपृष्ठकम् on an elephant, आसाद्य ascending, कुटिकाम् Kutika river, अत्यवर्तत crossed over, सः नरव्याघ्रः the tiger among men, लौहित्ये near Lauhitya, कपीवतीम् river Kapivati, ततार crossed.
explanation: ﻿ That tiger among men, Bharata halted at a place known as Sarvatirtha and crossed the Uttanika and various other rivers with the help of hillborn horses. He crossed the Kutika river on an elephant the river Kapivati at a place known as Lauhitya.

shloka_text: ﻿एकसाले स्थाणुमतीं विनते गोमतीं नदीम्। कलिङ्गनगरे चापि प्राप्य सालवनं तदा।।2.71.16।। भरतः क्षिप्रमागच्छत्सुपरिश्रान्तवाहनः।
transliteration: ﻿ekasāle sthāṇumatīṃ vinate gomatīṃ nadīm| kaliṅganagare cāpi prāpya sālavanaṃ tadā bharataḥ kṣipramāgacchatsupariśrāntavāhanaḥ|
translation: ﻿ भरतः Bharata, एकसाले at Ekasala village, स्थाणुमतीम् Sthanumati river, विनते at Vinata village, गोमतीं नदीम् Gomati river, सुपरिश्रान्तवाहनः with extremely fatigued horses, तदा then, कलिङ्गनगरे चापि at Kalinganagara, सालवनम् sala forest, प्राप्य having reached, क्षिप्रम् quickly, आगच्छत् came.
explanation: ﻿ Bharata crossed the rivers Sthanumati at Ekasala and Gomati at Vinata villages. Thereafter as his horses were extremely tired he rested for a while in the sala forest in Kalinganagara before he speedily set out (again).

shloka_text: ﻿वनं च समतीत्याशुशर्वर्यामरुणोदये।।2.71.17।। अयोध्यां मनुना राज्ञा निर्मितां सन्ददर्श ह।
transliteration: ﻿vanaṃ ca samatītyāśuśarvaryāmaruṇodaye ayodhyāṃ manunā rājñā nirmitāṃ sandadarśa ha|
translation: ﻿ आशु quickly, शर्वर्याम् in the night, वनं च forest also, समतीत्य having passed through, अरुणोदये at sunrise, मनुना राज्ञा by king Manu, निर्मिताम् built, अयोध्याम् Ayodhya, सन्ददर्श ह saw.
explanation: ﻿ He passed quickly through the forest at night and at sunrise beheld the city of Ayodhya built by king Manu.

shloka_text: ﻿तां पुरीं पुरुषव्याघ्रस्सप्तरात्रोषितः पथि।।2.71.18।। अयोध्यामग्रतो दृष्ट्वा सारथिं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
transliteration: ﻿tāṃ purīṃ puruṣavyāghrassaptarātroṣitaḥ pathi ayodhyāmagrato dṛṣṭvā sārathiṃ vākyamabravīt|
translation: ﻿ पथि on the way, सप्तरात्रोषितः spent seven nights, पुरुषव्याघ्रः tiger among men, अग्रतः before him, ताम् अयोध्यां पुरीम् that Ayodhya city, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सारथिम् to the charioteer, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: ﻿ Having spent seven nights on his way, that tiger among men (Bharata) saw Ayodhaya before him. He said to the charioteer:

shloka_text: ﻿एषा नातिप्रतीता मे पुण्योद्याना यशस्विनी।।2.71.19।। अयोध्या दृश्यते दूरात्सारथे पाण्डुमृत्तिका। यज्वभिर्गुणसम्पन्नैर्ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः।।2.71.20।। भूयिष्ठमृद्धैराकीर्णा राजर्षिपरिपालिता।
transliteration: ﻿eṣā nātipratītā me puṇyodyānā yaśasvinī ayodhyā dṛśyate dūrātsārathe pāṇḍumṛttikā| yajvabhirguṇasampannairbrāhmaṇairvedapāragaiḥ bhūyiṣṭhamṛddhairākīrṇā rājarṣiparipālitā|
translation: ﻿ सारथे O charioteer, पुण्योद्याना a city of sacred gardens, यशस्विनी of great renown, पाण्डुमृत्तिका with white clay, यज्वभिः those who perform sacrifices, गुणसम्पन्नैः by the virtuous, वेदपारगैः by those well versed in the vedas, भूयिष्ठम् in abundance , ऋद्धैः by the wealthy, ब्राह्मणैः by brahmins, आकीर्णा filled with, राजर्षिपरिपालिता ruled by rajarsis, एषा अयोध्या such Ayodhya, मे to me, नातिप्रतीता not so clearly, दूरात् from a distance, दृश्यते is seen.
explanation: ﻿ O charioteer I am able to see Ayodhya of great renown from a distance but not so clearly that whiteclaycity of Ayodhya, with its sacred gardens ruled by several rajarsis, inhabited by numerous wealthy people, by virtuous brahmins and priests who perform sacrifices and who are wellversed in the Vedas.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿﻿एषा नातिप्रतीता मे पुण्योद्याना यशस्विनी।।2.71.19।। अयोध्या दृश्यते दूरात्सारथे पाण्डुमृत्तिका। यज्वभिर्गुणसम्पन्नैर्ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः।।2.71.20।। भूयिष्ठमृद्धैराकीर्णा राजर्षिपरिपालिता।
transliteration: ﻿﻿﻿eṣā nātipratītā me puṇyodyānā yaśasvinī ayodhyā dṛśyate dūrātsārathe pāṇḍumṛttikā| yajvabhirguṇasampannairbrāhmaṇairvedapāragaiḥ bhūyiṣṭhamṛddhairākīrṇā rājarṣiparipālitā|
translation: ﻿﻿﻿ सारथे O charioteer, पुण्योद्याना a city of sacred gardens, यशस्विनी of great renown, पाण्डुमृत्तिका with white clay, यज्वभिः those who perform sacrifices, गुणसम्पन्नैः by the virtuous, वेदपारगैः by those well versed in the vedas, भूयिष्ठम् in abundance , ऋद्धैः by the wealthy, ब्राह्मणैः by brahmins, आकीर्णा filled with, राजर्षिपरिपालिता ruled by rajarsis, एषा अयोध्या such Ayodhya, मे to me, नातिप्रतीता not so clearly, दूरात् from a distance, दृश्यते is seen.
explanation: ﻿﻿﻿ O charioteer I am able to see Ayodhya of great renown from a distance but not so clearly that whiteclaycity of Ayodhya, with its sacred gardens ruled by several rajarsis, inhabited by numerous wealthy people, by virtuous brahmins and priests who perform sacrifices and who are wellversed in the Vedas.

shloka_text: ﻿अयोध्यायां पुरा शब्दश्श्रूयते तुमुलो महान्।।2.71.21।। समन्तान्नरनारीणां तमद्य न श्रुणोम्यहम्।
transliteration: ﻿ayodhyāyāṃ purā śabdaśśrūyate tumulo mahān samantānnaranārīṇāṃ tamadya na śruṇomyaham|
translation: ﻿ पुरा earlier, अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, नरनारीणाम् men and women, महान् great, तुमुलः tumultous, शब्दः sound, समन्तात् all over, श्रूयते would hear, अद्य now, तम् that sound, अहम् I, न श्रुणोमि not hear.
explanation: ﻿ I do not hear now, in Ayodhya the tumultous noise of men and women I used to hear earlier all over.

shloka_text: ﻿उद्यानानि हि सायाह्ने क्रीडित्वोपरतैर्नरैः।।2.71.22।। समन्तात्परिधावद्भिः प्रकाशन्ते ममान्यथा।
transliteration: ﻿udyānāni hi sāyāhne krīḍitvoparatairnaraiḥ samantātparidhāvadbhiḥ prakāśante mamānyathā|
translation: ﻿ सायाह्ने early in the morning, क्रीडित्वा sporting, उपरतैः free from desire, समन्तात् all over, परिधावद्भिः strolling, नरैः people, उद्यानानि parks, मम I, अन्यथा no one, प्रकाशन्ते हि looking bright.
explanation: ﻿ I do not see people who with passion used to stroll in the parks early in the morning. I see no cheerfulness in any one.

shloka_text: ﻿तान्यद्यानुरुदन्तीव परित्यक्तानि कामिभिः।।2.71.23।। अरण्यभूतेव पुरी सारथे प्रतिभाति मे।
transliteration: ﻿tānyadyānurudantīva parityaktāni kāmibhiḥ araṇyabhūteva purī sārathe pratibhāti me|
translation: ﻿ कामिभिः people full of passion, परित्यक्तानि abandoned, तानि that, अद्य now, अनुरुदन्तीव as if weeping, सारथे O charioteer, पुरी city, अरण्यभूतेव like a forest, मे to me, प्रतिभाति it appears.
explanation: ﻿ O charioteer, people full of passion have abandoned the gardens. To me, the city looks like a forest as if weeping.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿न ह्यत्र यानैर्दृश्यन्ते न गजैर्न च वाजिभिः।।2.71.24।। निर्यान्तो वाऽभियान्तो वा नरमुख्या यथापुरम्।
transliteration: ﻿﻿na hyatra yānairdṛśyante na gajairna ca vājibhiḥ niryānto vā'bhiyānto vā naramukhyā yathāpuram|
translation: ﻿﻿ अत्र here, नरमुख्याः important people, यथापुरम् as in the past, यानैः riding, निर्यान्तो वा people going (out of city), अभियान्तो वा or coming in, न दृश्यन्ते हि not seen, गजैः elephants, न not, वाजिभिः च horses also, न not.
explanation: ﻿﻿ Important people mounted on elephants or horses are not seen going out of the city or coming in.

shloka_text: ﻿उद्यानानि पुरा भान्ति मत्तप्रमुदितानि च।।2.71.25।। जनानां रतिसंयोगेष्वत्यन्तगुणवन्ति च।
transliteration: ﻿udyānāni purā bhānti mattapramuditāni ca janānāṃ ratisaṃyogeṣvatyantaguṇavanti ca|
translation: ﻿ पुरा earlier, उद्यानानि gardens, मत्तप्रमुदितानि च very melodiously singing, जनानाम् for people, रतिसंयोगेषु lovers for their pleasures, अत्यन्तगुणवन्ति च very appropriate, भान्ति would be.
explanation: ﻿ Earlier the gardens used to reverberate with passionate songs of birds--places appropriate for lovers seeking pleasures.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿तान्येतान्यद्य पश्यामि निरानन्दानि सर्वशः।।2.71.26।। स्रस्तपर्णैरनुपथं विक्रोशद्भिरिव द्रुमैः।
transliteration: ﻿﻿tānyetānyadya paśyāmi nirānandāni sarvaśaḥ srastaparṇairanupathaṃ vikrośadbhiriva drumaiḥ|
translation: ﻿﻿ अद्य now, अनुपथम् footpath, स्रस्तपर्णैः dry leaves, विक्रोशद्भिरिव as if crying, द्रुमैः trees, तान्येतानि such (gardens), सर्वशः all over, निरानन्दानि cheerless, पश्यामि see.
explanation: ﻿﻿ Now the trees appear cheerless, the paths are full of dry leaves fallen all over. It appears as if the trees are crying.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿नाद्यापि श्रूयते शब्दः मत्तानां मृगपक्षिणाम्।।2.71.27।। संरक्तां मधुरां वाणीं कलं व्याहरतां बहु।
transliteration: ﻿﻿nādyāpi śrūyate śabdaḥ mattānāṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām saṃraktāṃ madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ kalaṃ vyāharatāṃ bahu|
translation: ﻿﻿ संरक्ताम् in the red tincture (of the rising Sun), मधुराम् melodious, वाणीम् voices, बहु many, कलम् sweet sound, व्याहरताम् freely singing and moving, मत्तानाम् proud, मृगपक्षिणाम् animals and birds, शब्दः sound, अद्यापि now, न श्रूयते not hearing.
explanation: ﻿﻿ I do not hear in the red tincture of the rising Sun the melodious voices of the freely moving animals and birds.

shloka_text: ﻿चन्दनागरुसम्पृक्तो धूपसम्मूर्छितोऽतुलः।।2.71.28।। प्रवाति पवन श्श्रीमान्किन्नुनाद्य यथापुरम्।
transliteration: ﻿candanāgarusampṛkto dhūpasammūrchito'tulaḥ pravāti pavana śśrīmānkinnunādya yathāpuram|
translation: ﻿ चन्दनागरुसम्पृक्तः fragrance of sandal and incense, धूपसम्मूर्छितः smell wafting through the smoke, अतुलः incomparable, श्रीमान् prosperous, पवनः wind, अद्य now, यथापुरम् in the city always, किं नु why is it not, न प्रवाति not blowing?
explanation: ﻿ Why is it that the incomparable fragrance of sandal and incense that used to fill the nostrils, not blowing now in the prosperous city of Ayodhya?

shloka_text: ﻿﻿भेरीमृदङ्गवीणानां कोणसङ्घट्टितः पुनः।।2.71.29।। किमद्य शब्दो विरतस्सदा दीनगतिः पुरा।
transliteration: ﻿﻿bherīmṛdaṅgavīṇānāṃ koṇasaṅghaṭṭitaḥ punaḥ kimadya śabdo viratassadā dīnagatiḥ purā|
translation: ﻿﻿ पुरा earlier, दीनगतिः melancholy, पुनः again, कोणसङ्घट्टितः sounds of musical instruments, भेरीमृदङ्गवीणानाम् of the trumpets, mrudangas and veena, शब्दः sound, अद्य now, किम् why, विरतः not heard.
explanation: ﻿﻿ Why is it that the sounds of musical instruments like mrudangas and veenas are not heard now? Why is the city filled with melancholy?

shloka_text: ﻿अनिष्टानि च पापानि पश्यामि विविधानि च।।2.71.30।। निमित्तान्यमनोज्ञानितेन सीदति मे मनः।
transliteration: ﻿aniṣṭāni ca pāpāni paśyāmi vividhāni ca nimittānyamanojñānitena sīdati me manaḥ|
translation: ﻿ अनिष्टानि inauspicious symptoms, च also, पापानि sinful sights, पश्यामि see, विविधानि various निमित्तानि passing, अमनोज्ञानि ugly, तेन hence, सीदति filled with grief, मे my मनः mind.
explanation: ﻿ Since I see many passing, inauspicious, sinful, ugly sights, my mind shrinks.

shloka_text: ﻿सर्वथा कुशलं सूत दुर्लभं मम बन्दुषु।।2.71.31।। तथाह्यसति सम्मोहे हृदयं सीदतीव मे।
transliteration: ﻿sarvathā kuśalaṃ sūta durlabhaṃ mama banduṣu tathāhyasati sammohe hṛdayaṃ sīdatīva me|
translation: ﻿ सूत charioteer, सर्वथा all over, मम to me, बन्धुषु relations, कुशलम् welfare, दुर्लभम् not seem to be true, तथाहि therefore, सम्मोहे deluded, असति it is, मे my, हृदयम् heart, सीदतीव filled with grief.
explanation: ﻿ I do not see anywhere, O charioteer the wellbeing, of my kinsmen. Hence I feel deluded and my heart is filled with grief.

shloka_text: ﻿विषण्ण श्श्रान्तहृदयस्त्रस्त स्सुलुलितेन्द्रियः।।2.71.32।। भरतः प्रविवेशाशु पुरीमिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्।
transliteration: ﻿viṣaṇṇa śśrāntahṛdayastrasta ssululitendriyaḥ bharataḥ praviveśāśu purīmikṣvākupālitām|
translation: ﻿ विषण्णः dejected, श्रान्तहृदयः with depressed heart, त्रस्तः fearful man, सुलुलितेन्द्रियः losing control over his senses, भरतः Bharata, आशु quickly, इक्ष्वाकुपालिताम् ruled by the Ikshvakus, पुरीम् city of Ayodhya, प्रविवेश entered.
explanation: ﻿ Dejected and depressed at heart, with no control over his senses and his mind full of apprehension, Bharata swiftly entered the city of Ayodhya ruled by the Ikshvakus.

shloka_text: ﻿द्वारेण वैजयन्तेन प्राविशच्छ्रान्तवाहनः।।2.71.33।। द्वास्स्थैरुत्थाय विजयं पृष्टस्तै स्सहितो ययौ।
transliteration: ﻿dvāreṇa vaijayantena prāviśacchrāntavāhanaḥ dvāssthairutthāya vijayaṃ pṛṣṭastai ssahito yayau|
translation: ﻿ श्रान्तवाहनः with his horses exhausted, वैजयन्तेन known as Vaijayanta, द्वारेण through gate of, प्राविशत् entered, द्वाःस्थैः by gate keepers, उत्थाय having stood up, विजयम् victory, पृष्टः having been uttered, तैः सहितः along with them, ययौ went.
explanation: ﻿ He entered the city through the gate known as Vaijayanta with his horses exhausted. The doorkeepers stood up and amidst cries of victory followed him in.

shloka_text: ﻿स त्वनेकाग्रहृदयो द्वास्स्थं प्रत्यर्च्य तं जनम्।।2.71.34।। सूतमश्वपतेः क्लान्तमब्रवीत्तत्र राघवः।
transliteration: ﻿sa tvanekāgrahṛdayo dvāssthaṃ pratyarcya taṃ janam sūtamaśvapateḥ klāntamabravīttatra rāghavaḥ|
translation: ﻿ सः राघवः तु as for the descendant of Raghus, अनेकाग्रहृदयः with a bewildered mind, द्वास्स्थम् to the gatekeepers, तम् those, जनम् people, प्रत्यर्च्य greeting in turn तत्र there, अश्वपतेः to Ashwapati, क्लान्तम् exhausted, सूतम् to the charioteer, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: ﻿ Bewildered, that descendant of Raghu (Bharata), reciprocated the greetings of the gatekeepers and then addressed the exhausted charioteer, Ashwapati:

shloka_text: ﻿किमहं त्वरयाऽनीतः कारणेन विनानघ।।2.71.35।। अशुभाशङ्कि हृदयं शीलं च पततीव मे।
transliteration: ﻿kimahaṃ tvarayā'nītaḥ kāraṇena vinānagha aśubhāśaṅki hṛdayaṃ śīlaṃ ca patatīva me|
translation: ﻿ अनघ O irreproachable one, अहम् I am, कारणेन विना without any reason, त्वरया in haste, किम् why, आनीतः was brought, हृदयम् my heart, अशुभाशङ्कि apprehends something inauspcious, मे my, शीलं च disposition, पततीव is lost.
explanation: ﻿ O irreproachable one, why was I brought here in haste without any reason? My mind apprehends something inauspicious. I feel indisposed.

shloka_text: ﻿श्रुता नो यादृशाः पूर्वं नृपतीनां विनाशने।।2.71.36।। आकारांस्तानहं सर्वानिहपश्यामि सारथे।
transliteration: ﻿śrutā no yādṛśāḥ pūrvaṃ nṛpatīnāṃ vināśane ākārāṃstānahaṃ sarvānihapaśyāmi sārathe|
translation: ﻿ सारथे O charioteer, नृपतीनाम् kings', विनाशने in destruction, यादृशाः such kind of, पूर्वम् in times past, नः us, श्रुताः have been heard, तान् सर्वान् all those, आकारान् signs, अहम् I, इह पश्यामि I am seeing now.
explanation: ﻿ O charioteer I now see the very for ebodings I had heard in the past in connection with the death of kings.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿सम्मार्जनविहीनानि परुषाण्युपलक्षये।।2.71.37।। असंयत कवाटानि श्रीविहीनानि सर्वशः। बलिकर्मविहीनानि धूपसम्मोदनेन च।।2.71.38।। अनाशितकुटुम्बानि प्रभाहीनजनानि च। अलक्ष्मीकानि पश्यामि कुटुम्बिभवनान्यहम्।।2.71.39।।
transliteration: ﻿﻿sammārjanavihīnāni paruṣāṇyupalakṣaye asaṃyata kavāṭāni śrīvihīnāni sarvaśaḥ| balikarmavihīnāni dhūpasammodanena ca anāśitakuṭumbāni prabhāhīnajanāni ca| alakṣmīkāni paśyāmi kuṭumbibhavanānyaham
translation: ﻿﻿ अहम् I, सम्मार्जनविहीनानि unswept, कुटुंम्बिभवनानि houses of families, परुषाणि dirty, उपलक्षये discern, असंयत कवाटानि doors not closed, सर्वशः on every side, श्रीविहीनानि bereft of beauty, बलिकर्मविहीनानि devoid of offering oblations, धूपसम्मोदनेन च with fragrance of burnt incense, अनाशितकुटुम्बानि familes without food, प्रभाहीनजनानि च men devoid of brightness, अलक्ष्मीकानि inauspicious, पश्यामि I see
explanation: ﻿﻿ I see the unswept homes of householders standing dirty with doors not closed. There is no beauty anywhere. No one offers oblations (at the time of worship). There is no fragrance of burning incense. The families have no food to eat. The people look cheerless. I see inauspiciousness everywhere.

shloka_text: ﻿सम्मार्जनविहीनानि परुषाण्युपलक्षये।।2.71.37।। असंयत कवाटानि श्रीविहीनानि सर्वशः। बलिकर्मविहीनानि धूपसम्मोदनेन च।।2.71.38।। अनाशितकुटुम्बानि प्रभाहीनजनानि च। अलक्ष्मीकानि पश्यामि कुटुम्बिभवनान्यहम्।।2.71.39।।
transliteration: ﻿sammārjanavihīnāni paruṣāṇyupalakṣaye asaṃyata kavāṭāni śrīvihīnāni sarvaśaḥ| balikarmavihīnāni dhūpasammodanena ca anāśitakuṭumbāni prabhāhīnajanāni ca| alakṣmīkāni paśyāmi kuṭumbibhavanānyaham
translation: ﻿ अहम् I, सम्मार्जनविहीनानि unswept, कुटुंम्बिभवनानि houses of families, परुषाणि dirty, उपलक्षये discern, असंयत कवाटानि doors not closed, सर्वशः on every side, श्रीविहीनानि bereft of beauty, बलिकर्मविहीनानि devoid of offering oblations, धूपसम्मोदनेन च with fragrance of burnt incense, अनाशितकुटुम्बानि familes without food, प्रभाहीनजनानि च men devoid of brightness, अलक्ष्मीकानि inauspicious, पश्यामि I see
explanation: ﻿ I see the unswept homes of householders standing dirty with doors not closed. There is no beauty anywhere. No one offers oblations (at the time of worship). There is no fragrance of burning incense. The families have no food to eat. The people look cheerless. I see inauspiciousness everywhere.

shloka_text: ﻿सम्मार्जनविहीनानि परुषाण्युपलक्षये।।2.71.37।। असंयत कवाटानि श्रीविहीनानि सर्वशः। बलिकर्मविहीनानि धूपसम्मोदनेन च।।2.71.38।। अनाशितकुटुम्बानि प्रभाहीनजनानि च। अलक्ष्मीकानि पश्यामि कुटुम्बिभवनान्यहम्।।2.71.39।।
transliteration: ﻿sammārjanavihīnāni paruṣāṇyupalakṣaye asaṃyata kavāṭāni śrīvihīnāni sarvaśaḥ| balikarmavihīnāni dhūpasammodanena ca anāśitakuṭumbāni prabhāhīnajanāni ca| alakṣmīkāni paśyāmi kuṭumbibhavanānyaham
translation: ﻿ अहम् I, सम्मार्जनविहीनानि unswept, कुटुंम्बिभवनानि houses of families, परुषाणि dirty, उपलक्षये discern, असंयत कवाटानि doors not closed, सर्वशः on every side, श्रीविहीनानि bereft of beauty, बलिकर्मविहीनानि devoid of offering oblations, धूपसम्मोदनेन च with fragrance of burnt incense, अनाशितकुटुम्बानि familes without food, प्रभाहीनजनानि च men devoid of brightness, अलक्ष्मीकानि inauspicious, पश्यामि I see
explanation: ﻿ I see the unswept homes of householders standing dirty with doors not closed. There is no beauty anywhere. No one offers oblations (at the time of worship). There is no fragrance of burning incense. The families have no food to eat. The people look cheerless. I see inauspiciousness everywhere.

shloka_text: ﻿अपेतमाल्यशोभानि ह्यसम्मृष्टाजिराणि च। देवागाराणि शून्यानि न चाभान्ति यथापुरम्।।2.71.40।।
transliteration: ﻿apetamālyaśobhāni hyasammṛṣṭājirāṇi ca| devāgārāṇi śūnyāni na cābhānti yathāpuram
translation: ﻿ अपेतमाल्यशोभानि deprived of the splendour of garlands, असम्मृष्टाजिराणि च floors of the front yards unsmeared, देवागाराः temples, शून्यानि empty, यथापुरम् as before, नाभान्ति च not shining.
explanation: ﻿ The temples stand devoid of the beauty of floral offerings. The floors of front yards are left unswept and unsmeared. They look deserted, devoid of brightness of the past.

shloka_text: ﻿देवतार्चाः प्रविद्धाश्च यज्ञगोष्ठ्यस्तथाविधाः। माल्यापणेषु राजन्ते नाद्य पण्यानि वा तथा।।2.71.41।।
transliteration: ﻿devatārcāḥ praviddhāśca yajñagoṣṭhyastathāvidhāḥ| mālyāpaṇeṣu rājante nādya paṇyāni vā tathā
translation: ﻿ देवतार्चाः offerings to deities, प्रविद्धा: च have been dispensed with, यज्ञगोष्ठ्यः groups of people performing holy sacrifices, तथाविधाः as before, तथा usual, माल्यापणेषु in the markets where garlands are sold, अद्य now, पण्यानि items (garlands) for sale, न राजन्ते are not there.
explanation: ﻿ The offerings to deities have been dispensed with. There are no groups of people performing the usual holy sacrifices. The markets where garlands were sold now stand without them.

shloka_text: ﻿दृश्यन्ते वणिजोऽप्यद्य न यथापूर्वमत्रवै। ध्यानसंविग्नहृदयाः नष्टव्यापारयन्त्रिताः।।2.71.42।।
transliteration: ﻿dṛśyante vaṇijo'pyadya na yathāpūrvamatravai| dhyānasaṃvignahṛdayāḥ naṣṭavyāpārayantritāḥ
translation: ﻿ नष्टव्यापारयन्त्रिताः restrained by the loss of business, ध्यानसंविग्नहृदयाः with distracted attention, वणिजोऽपि even traders, अद्य now, अत्र there, यथापूर्वम् as before, न दृश्यन्ते are not seen.
explanation: ﻿ Even traders seem restrained by the loss of business. They are not seen as before concentrating on their trade.

shloka_text: ﻿देवायतनचैत्येषु दीनाः पक्षिगणास्तथा।।2.71.43।। मलिनं चाश्रुपूर्णाक्षं दीनं ध्यानपरं कृशम्। सस्त्रीपुंसं च पश्यामि जनमुत्कण्ठितं पुरे।।2.71.44।।
transliteration: ﻿devāyatanacaityeṣu dīnāḥ pakṣigaṇāstathā malinaṃ cāśrupūrṇākṣaṃ dīnaṃ dhyānaparaṃ kṛśam| sastrīpuṃsaṃ ca paśyāmi janamutkaṇṭhitaṃ pure
translation: ﻿ तथा as before, देवायतनचैत्येषु in temples and in sanctuaries, पक्षिगणाः multitude of birds, दीनाः dispirited, पुरे in the city, सस्त्रीपुंसम् with women and men, जनम् people, उत्कण्ठितम् with choked throats, मलिनम् dull, अश्रुपूर्णाक्षम् eyes filled with tears, दीनम् piteous, ध्यानपरम् absorbed in distressing thoughts, कृशम् emaciated, पश्यामि I see.
explanation: ﻿ I see groups of birds frequenting the temples. The sanctuaries appear dispirited. The people in the city, both men and women look dull, emaciated, pitiable with throats choked. Their eyes are filled with tears and minds absorbed in distressing thoughts.

shloka_text: ﻿देवायतनचैत्येषु दीनाः पक्षिगणास्तथा।।2.71.43।। मलिनं चाश्रुपूर्णाक्षं दीनं ध्यानपरं कृशम्। सस्त्रीपुंसं च पश्यामि जनमुत्कण्ठितं पुरे।।2.71.44।।
transliteration: ﻿devāyatanacaityeṣu dīnāḥ pakṣigaṇāstathā malinaṃ cāśrupūrṇākṣaṃ dīnaṃ dhyānaparaṃ kṛśam| sastrīpuṃsaṃ ca paśyāmi janamutkaṇṭhitaṃ pure
translation: ﻿ तथा as before, देवायतनचैत्येषु in temples and in sanctuaries, पक्षिगणाः multitude of birds, दीनाः dispirited, पुरे in the city, सस्त्रीपुंसम् with women and men, जनम् people, उत्कण्ठितम् with choked throats, मलिनम् dull, अश्रुपूर्णाक्षम् eyes filled with tears, दीनम् piteous, ध्यानपरम् absorbed in distressing thoughts, कृशम् emaciated, पश्यामि I see.
explanation: ﻿ I see groups of birds frequenting the temples. The sanctuaries appear dispirited. The people in the city, both men and women look dull, emaciated, pitiable with throats choked. Their eyes are filled with tears and minds absorbed in distressing thoughts.

shloka_text: ﻿इत्येवमुक्त्वा भरतस्सूतं तं दीनमानसः। तान्यनिष्टान्ययोध्यायां प्रेक्ष्य राजगृहं ययौ।।2.71.45।।
transliteration: ﻿ityevamuktvā bharatassūtaṃ taṃ dīnamānasaḥ| tānyaniṣṭānyayodhyāyāṃ prekṣya rājagṛhaṃ yayau
translation: ﻿ भरतः Bharata, अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, तानि these, अनिष्टानि ominous sights, प्रेक्ष्य having seen, दीनमानसः with depressed heart, तं सूतम् that charioteer, इत्येवम् in this way, उक्त्वा having said, राजगृहम् king's palace, ययौ proceeded.
explanation: ﻿ With these words said to the charioteer, Bharata, having seen such ominous sights in Ayodhya, proceeded to the king's palace with a depressed heart.

shloka_text: ﻿तां शून्यशृङ्गाटकवेश्मरथ्यां रजोऽरुणद्वारकवाटयन्त्राम्। दृष्ट्वा पुरीमिन्द्रपुरप्रकाशां दुःखेन सम्पूर्णतरो बभूव।।2.71.46।।
transliteration: ﻿tāṃ śūnyaśṛṅgāṭakaveśmarathyāṃ rajo'ruṇadvārakavāṭayantrām| dṛṣṭvā purīmindrapuraprakāśāṃ duḥkhena sampūrṇataro babhūva
translation: ﻿ शून्यशृङ्गाटकवेश्मरथ्याम् a place with crossroads, houses, and highways deserted, रजोऽरुणद्वारकवाटयन्त्राम् the fittings (nuts and bolts) on the doors red with dust, इन्द्रपुरप्रकाशाम् once having the lustre of the city of Indra, तां पुरीम् that city, दृष्ट्वा having seen, दुःखेन with grief, सम्पूर्णतरः overwhelmed, बभूव became.
explanation: ﻿ As he (Bharata) beheld the city of Ayodhya that once had the lustre of the city of Indra, now with its crossroads, houses and highways all deserted, the fittings (nuts and bolts) on the doors red with dust, he was overwhelmed with grief.

shloka_text: अपश्यंस्तु ततस्तत्र पितरं पितुरालये। जगाम भरतो द्रष्टुं मातरं मातुरालये।।2.72.1।।
transliteration: apaśyaṃstu tatastatra pitaraṃ piturālaye| jagāma bharato draṣṭuṃ mātaraṃ māturālaye
translation: ततः thereafter, भरतः Bharata, तत्र there, पितुः father's, आलये abode, पितरम् father, अपश्यन् not seen, मातुः mother's, आलये in the abode, मातरम् mother, द्रष्टुम् to see,  जगाम went.
explanation: Not finding his father in his abode, Bharata went to see his mother in her apartment.
comments: Bharata meets Kaikeyi -- hears from Kaikeyi about the demise of king Dasaratha and Rama's exile -- Vasistha calls upon Bharata to perform obsequies and get consecrated

shloka_text: अनुप्राप्तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा कैकेयी प्रोषितं सुतम्। उत्पपात तदा हृष्टा त्यक्त्वा सौवर्णमासनम्।।2.72.2।।
transliteration: anuprāptaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā kaikeyī proṣitaṃ sutam| utpapāta tadā hṛṣṭā tyaktvā sauvarṇamāsanam
translation: कैकेयी Kaikeyi, प्रोषितम् sent, तं सुतम् that son, अनुप्राप्तम् who had arrived, दृष्ट्वा having seen, तदा then, हृष्टा delighted, सौवर्णम् golden, आसनम् seat, त्वक्त्वा leaving, उत्पपात sprang up.
explanation: On seeing her son, who was sent away, presently arriving, the delighted Kaikeyi sprang up from her golden seat.

shloka_text: स प्रविश्यैव धर्मात्मा स्वगृहं श्रीविवर्जितम्। भरतः प्रतिजग्राह जनन्याश्चरणौ शुभौ।।2.72.3।।
transliteration: sa praviśyaiva dharmātmā svagṛhaṃ śrīvivarjitam| bharataḥ pratijagrāha jananyāścaraṇau śubhau
translation: धर्मात्मा a man of righteous conduct, सः भरतः that Bharata, श्रीविवर्जितम् devoid of cheer, स्वगृहम् his home, प्रविश्यैव on entering, जनन्याः mother's, शुभौ auspicious, चरणौ feet, प्रतिजग्राह clasped.
explanation: On entering home the righteous Bharata found it devoid of cheer and touched the auspicious feet of his mother (with reverence).

shloka_text: सा तं मूर्धन्युपाघ्राय परिष्वज्य यशस्विनम्। अङ्के भरतमारोप्य प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे।।2.72.4।।
transliteration: sā taṃ mūrdhanyupāghrāya pariṣvajya yaśasvinam| aṅke bharatamāropya praṣṭuṃ samupacakrame
translation: सा she, यशस्विनम् illustrious, तं भरतम् to Bharata, मूर्धनि on his forehead, उपाघ्राय having smelt, परिष्वज्य having hugged, अङ्के on her lap, आरोप्य made him rest, प्रष्टुम् to  question, उपचक्रमे began.
explanation: Kaikeyi, gave her illustrious son Bharata a hug, kissed him on his forehead, made him rest on her lap and began her query.

shloka_text: अद्य ते कतिचिद्रात्र्य श्च्युतस्याऽर्यकवेश्मनः। अपि नाध्वश्रमशशीघ्रं रथेनापततस्तव।।2.72.5।।
transliteration: adya te katicidrātrya ścyutasyā'ryakaveśmanaḥ| api nādhvaśramaśaśīghraṃ rathenāpatatastava
translation: आर्यकवेश्मनः from your noble grandfather's residence, च्युतस्य having left, ते to you, अद्य by now, कतिचित् how many, रात्र्य: nights, शीघ्रम् swiftly, रथेन on chariot, आपततः while moving, तव to you, अध्वश्रमः weary of journey, अपि न is not there?
explanation: How many nights have you spent (on the way) since you left your noble grandfather's residence? Hasn't the hurried journey (over such a long distance) on the chariot left you exhausted?

shloka_text: ﻿आर्यकस्ते सुकुशली युधाजिन्मातुलस्तव। प्रवासाच्च सुखं पुत्र सर्वं मे वक्तुमर्हसि।।2.72.6।।
transliteration: ﻿āryakaste sukuśalī yudhājinmātulastava| pravāsācca sukhaṃ putra sarvaṃ me vaktumarhasi
translation: ﻿ पुत्र son, ते your, आर्यकः revered grandfather, सुकुशली is he doing well?, तव your, मातुलः maternal uncle, युधाजित् Yudhajit, प्रवासात् the sojourn, सुखम् is it pleasant?, मे to me, सर्वम् everything, वक्तुम् to tell, अर्हसि behoves you.
explanation: ﻿ My son are your revered grandfather and your maternal uncle Yudhajit doing well? Did you have a pleasant time during the sojourn? You should tell me all this.

shloka_text: एवं पृष्टस्तु कैकेय्या प्रियं पार्थिवनन्दनः। आचष्ट भरत स्सर्वं मात्रे राजीवलोचनः।।2.72.7।।
transliteration: evaṃ pṛṣṭastu kaikeyyā priyaṃ pārthivanandanaḥ| ācaṣṭa bharata ssarvaṃ mātre rājīvalocanaḥ
translation: राजीवलोचनः lotuseyed, पार्थिवनन्दनः king's delight, भरतः Bharata, कैकेय्या by Kaikeyi, एवम् in this manner, प्रियम् lovingly, पृष्ट: having been asked, मात्रे to his mother, सर्वम् every thing, आचष्टे narrated.
explanation: Thus asked lovingly by his mother Kaikeyi, the lotuseyed Bharata, the king's delight  narrated everything to her.

shloka_text: अद्य मे सप्तमी रात्रिश्च्युतस्याऽर्यकवेश्मनः। अम्बायाः कुशली तात युधाजिन्मातुलश्च मे।।2.72.8।।
transliteration: adya me saptamī rātriścyutasyā'ryakaveśmanaḥ| ambāyāḥ kuśalī tāta yudhājinmātulaśca me
translation: आर्यकवेश्मनः from noble grandsire's residence, च्युतस्य having left, मे to me, अद्य now, सप्तमी seventh, रात्रिः night, अम्बायाः mother's, तातः father, मे my, मातुलश्च maternal uncle, युधाजित् Yudhajit, कुशली is keeping well.
explanation: This is the seventh night since I left my noble grandsire's residence. My mother's father, king of Kekaya and my maternal uncle Yudhajit are doing well.

shloka_text: यन्मे धनं च रत्नं च ददौ राजा परन्तपः। परिश्रान्तं पथ्यभवत्ततोऽहं पूर्वमागतः।।2.72.9।।
transliteration: yanme dhanaṃ ca ratnaṃ ca dadau rājā parantapaḥ| pariśrāntaṃ pathyabhavattato'haṃ pūrvamāgataḥ
translation: परन्तपः subduer of enemies, राजा king of Kekaya, मे to me, यत् which, धनं च wealth, रत्नं च gems, ददौ had given, that one, पथि on the way, परिश्रान्तम् अभवत् were exhausted, ततः therefore, अहम् I, पूर्वम् in advance, आगतः I came.
explanation: The (horses carrying) the wealth including the gems which the king (of Kekaya), the subduer of enemies had bestowed on me were exhausted on the way. Therefore I have come in advance.

shloka_text: राजवाक्यहरैर्दूतैस्त्वर्यमाणोऽहमागतः। यदहं प्रष्टुमिच्छामि तदम्बा वक्तुमर्हति।।2.72.10।।
transliteration: rājavākyaharairdūtaistvaryamāṇo'hamāgataḥ| yadahaṃ praṣṭumicchāmi tadambā vaktumarhati
translation: अहम् I, राजवाक्यहरैः by those carrying out royal orders, दूतैः messengers, त्वर्यमाणः have  hastened, आगतः came, अहम् I, यत् which one, प्रष्टुम् to ask, इच्छामि wish,  तत् all that, अम्बा mother, वक्तुम् to tell, अर्हति behoves you.
explanation: Urged upon by the messengers carrying out the orders of the king, I have come. You, O mother, should answer the questions. I wish to ask you.

shloka_text: शून्योऽयं शयनीयस्ते पर्यङ्को हेमभूषितः। न चायमिक्ष्वाकुजनः प्रहृष्टः प्रतिभाति मा।।2.72.11।।
transliteration: śūnyo'yaṃ śayanīyaste paryaṅko hemabhūṣitaḥ| na cāyamikṣvākujanaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ pratibhāti mā
translation: शयनीयः a place worthy of resting, हेमभूषितः decorated with gold, अयम् this, ते your, पर्यङ्क: couch, शून्यः is empty, अयम् च and this, इक्ष्वाकुजनः  attendants of Ikshavaku, प्रहृष्टः with delight, मा to me, न प्रतिभाति does not appear.
explanation: Your goldbedecked couch, worthy of resting lies empty. None of the attendants of the Ikshvakus look cheerful.

shloka_text: ﻿राजा भवति भूयिष्ठमिहाम्बाया निवेशने। तमहं नाद्य पश्यामि द्रष्टुमिच्छन्निहाऽगतः।।2.72.12।।
transliteration: ﻿rājā bhavati bhūyiṣṭhamihāmbāyā niveśane| tamahaṃ nādya paśyāmi draṣṭumicchannihā'gataḥ
translation: ﻿ राजा king, भूयिष्ठम् mostly, इह here, अम्बायाः mother's, निवेशने residence, भवति stays, अद्य today, तम him, अहम् I, न पश्यामि do not see, द्रष्टुम् to see, इच्छन् with a wish, इह here, आगतः came.
explanation: ﻿ I had come here with the hope to see king Dasaratha who spends most of his time in my mother's residence. But today I do not see him .

shloka_text: पितुर्ग्रहीष्ये चरणौ तं ममाऽख्याहि पृच्छतः। आहोस्विदम्ब ज्येष्ठायाः कौसल्याया निवेशने।।2.72.13।।
transliteration: piturgrahīṣye caraṇau taṃ mamā'khyāhi pṛcchataḥ| āhosvidamba jyeṣṭhāyāḥ kausalyāyā niveśane
translation: अम्ब O mother, पितुः father's, चरणौ both the feet, ग्रहीष्ये I shall hold, पृच्छतः thus asking, मम to me, तम् about him, आख्याहि you may tell, आहोस्वित् perchance, ज्येष्ठायाः the eldest mother's, कौशल्यायाः Kausalya's, निवेशने at her residence.
explanation: I would like to pay obeisance at my father's feet. Will you answer my question, O mother, and tell me regarding his whereabouts? Or perchance could he be at the residence of my eldest mother Kausalya?

shloka_text: तं प्रत्युवाच कैकेयी प्रियवद्घोरमप्रियम्। अजानन्तं प्रजानन्ती राज्यलोभेन मोहिता।।2.72.14।।
transliteration: taṃ pratyuvāca kaikeyī priyavadghoramapriyam| ajānantaṃ prajānantī rājyalobhena mohitā
translation: प्रजानन्ती In spite of knowing, राज्यलोभेन due to greed for kingdom, मोहिता infatuated, कैकेयी Kaikeyi, घोरम् dreadful, अप्रियम् unpleasant news, प्रियवत् as if it was pleasing, अजानन्तम् ignorant of what had transpired, तम्  him (Bharata), प्रत्युवाच conveyed to him.
explanation: In spite of knowing everything, Kaikeyi actuated by greed for the kingdom, broke the unpleasant and dreadful news as if it were pleasing to Bharata, who was ignorant of what had transpired.

shloka_text: ﻿या गतिस्सर्वभूतानां तां गतिं ते पिता गतः। राजा महत्मा तेजस्वी यायजूकस्सतां गतिः।।2.72.15।।
transliteration: ﻿yā gatissarvabhūtānāṃ tāṃ gatiṃ te pitā gataḥ| rājā mahatmā tejasvī yāyajūkassatāṃ gatiḥ
translation: ﻿ राजा king, महात्मा highsouled one, तेजस्वी brilliant one, यायजूकः ever engaged in performing sacrifices, सताम् for virtuous people, गतिः refuge, ते पिता your father, सर्वभूतानाम् for all living beings, या which, गतिः ultimate course, तां गतिम् that course, गतः attained.
explanation: ﻿ Your highsouled, brilliant father ever engaged in performing sacrifices and a refuge for the virtuous people, went the inevitable way every living being must follow (attained heaven).

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतो वाक्यं धर्माभिजनवाञ्चुचिः। पपात सहसा भूमौ पितृशोकबलार्दितः।।2.72.16।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā bharato vākyaṃ dharmābhijanavāñcuciḥ| papāta sahasā bhūmau pitṛśokabalārditaḥ
translation: धर्माभिजनवान् born of the righteous race, शुचिः a man of pure nature, भरतः Bharata, तत् at that, वाक्यम् words, श्रुत्वा on hearing, पितृशोकबलार्दितः shattered by the force of grief due to his father's demise, सहसा at once, भूमौ on the ground, पपात collapsed.
explanation: On hearing these words, he (Bharata), born of a righteous race and endowed with purity of character was shattered by the immense grief of his father's demise and dropped down instantaneously on the floor.

shloka_text: हा हतोऽस्मीति कृपणां दीनां वाचमुदीरयन्। निपपात महाबाहुर्बाहू विक्षिप्य वीर्यवान्।।2.72.17।।
transliteration: hā hato'smīti kṛpaṇāṃ dīnāṃ vācamudīrayan| nipapāta mahābāhurbāhū vikṣipya vīryavān
translation: महबाहुः mightyarmed one, वीर्यवान् valiant, हा हतः अस्मि Alas I am finished, इति thus, कृपणाम् evoking compassion, दीनाम् pitiable, वाचम् words, उदीरयन् uttering, बाहू arms, विक्षिप्य having lifted, निपपात fell down.
explanation: The mightyarmed, valiant Bharata, uttering pitiable words, evoking compassion. Alas, I am finished fell down at once throwing up his arms.

shloka_text: ततश्शोकेन संवीतः पितुर्मरणदुःखितः। विललाप महातेजा भ्रान्ताकुलितचेतनः।।2.72.18।।
transliteration: tataśśokena saṃvītaḥ piturmaraṇaduḥkhitaḥ| vilalāpa mahātejā bhrāntākulitacetanaḥ
translation: ततः after that, महातेजाः radiant Bharata, शोकेन by grief, संवीतः overwhelmed, पितुः father's, मरण दुःखितः sorrowing over death, भ्रान्ताकुलितचेतनः his mind afflicted with delusion, विललाप lamented.
explanation: Overwhelmed with grief, radiant Bharata reeling with delusion due to sorrow, lamented over the death of his father.

shloka_text: एतत्सुरुचिरं भाति पितुर्मे शयनं पुरा। शशिनेवामलं रात्रौ गगनं तोयदात्यये।।2.72.19।।
transliteration: etatsuruciraṃ bhāti piturme śayanaṃ purā| śaśinevāmalaṃ rātrau gaganaṃ toyadātyaye
translation: मे पितुः my father's, एतत् this, सुरुचिरम् lovely, शयनम् couch, पुरा formerly, तोयदात्यये at the end of the rainy season, रात्रौ in the night, अमलम् spotless, गगनम् sky, शशिनेव as though by the Moon, भाति स्म used to radiate.
explanation: This couch of my father once used to shine like the spotless night sky irradiated by the autumnal Moon.

shloka_text: तदिदं न विभात्यद्य विहीनं तेन धीमता। व्योमेव शशिना हीनमप्च्छुष्क इव सागरः।।2.72.20।।
transliteration: tadidaṃ na vibhātyadya vihīnaṃ tena dhīmatā| vyomeva śaśinā hīnamapcchuṣka iva sāgaraḥ
translation: धीमता sagacious, तेन by him, विहीनम् deprived of, तत् इदम् that this couch, अद्य today, शशिना by the Moon, हीनम् devoid of, व्योमेव like sky, अप्च्छुष्कः dried up by evaporation of water, सागरः इव like the sea, न विभाति is not shining.
explanation: But today this couch without my sagacious father no longer shines like the sky without the Moon or like the sea evaporated.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿बाष्पमुत्सृज्य् कण्ठेन स्वात्मना परमपीडितः। आच्छाद्य वदनं श्रीमद्वस्त्रेण जयतां वरः।।2.72.21।।
transliteration: ﻿﻿bāṣpamutsṛjy kaṇṭhena svātmanā paramapīḍitaḥ| ācchādya vadanaṃ śrīmadvastreṇa jayatāṃ varaḥ
translation: ﻿﻿ जयताम् among the victorious, वरः the foremost, कण्ठेन with throat, बाष्पम् tears, उत्सृज्य having released, वस्त्रेण with raiment, श्रीमत् auspicious, वदनम् countenance, आच्छाद्य having covered, स्वात्मना at his heart, परमपीडितः was profoundly distressed.
explanation: ﻿﻿ Bharata, the foremost among the victorious, clearing his tearchoked throat and covering his auspicious countenance with raiment, wept in profound distress with tears overflowing.

shloka_text: तमार्तं देवसङ्काशं समीक्ष्य पतितं भुवि। निकृत्तमिव सालस्य स्कन्धं परशुना वने।।2.72.22।। मत्तमातङ्गसङ्काशं चन्द्रार्कसदृशं भुवः। उत्थापयित्वा शोकार्तं वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्।।2.72.23।।
transliteration: tamārtaṃ devasaṅkāśaṃ samīkṣya patitaṃ bhuvi| nikṛttamiva sālasya skandhaṃ paraśunā vane mattamātaṅgasaṅkāśaṃ candrārkasadṛśaṃ bhuvaḥ| utthāpayitvā śokārtaṃ vacanaṃ cedamabravīt
translation: आर्तम् anguished, देवसङ्काशम् resembling gods, वने in the forest, परशुना by an axe, निकृत्तम् severed, सालस्य sala tree's, स्कन्धमिव like a trunk, सुतम् son, भुवि पतितम् fallen on the ground, मत्तमातङ्गसङ्काशम् like a mighty elephant, चन्द्रार्कसदृशम् similar to the Sun and the Moon, शोकार्तम् tormented by grief, तम् to him (Bharata), भुवः from the ground, उत्थापयित्वा having lifted him up, इदम् these, वचनं च words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Anguished and griefstricken, he who resembled the gods, fell down on the ground like a trunk of the sala tree in the forest severed by an axe. Seeing her son who was like a mighty elephant or like the Sun or the Moon, Kaikeyi lifted him up from the ground and spoke these words:

shloka_text: तमार्तं देवसङ्काशं समीक्ष्य पतितं भुवि। निकृत्तमिव सालस्य स्कन्धं परशुना वने।।2.72.22।। मत्तमातङ्गसङ्काशं चन्द्रार्कसदृशं भुवः। उत्थापयित्वा शोकार्तं वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्।।2.72.23।।
transliteration: tamārtaṃ devasaṅkāśaṃ samīkṣya patitaṃ bhuvi| nikṛttamiva sālasya skandhaṃ paraśunā vane mattamātaṅgasaṅkāśaṃ candrārkasadṛśaṃ bhuvaḥ| utthāpayitvā śokārtaṃ vacanaṃ cedamabravīt
translation: आर्तम् anguished, देवसङ्काशम् resembling gods, वने in the forest, परशुना by an axe, निकृत्तम् severed, सालस्य sala tree's, स्कन्धमिव like a trunk, सुतम् son, भुवि पतितम् fallen on the ground, मत्तमातङ्गसङ्काशम् like a mighty elephant, चन्द्रार्कसदृशम् similar to the Sun and the Moon, शोकार्तम् tormented by grief, तम् to him (Bharata), भुवः from the ground, उत्थापयित्वा having lifted him up, इदम् these, वचनं च words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Anguished and griefstricken, he who resembled the gods, fell down on the ground like a trunk of the sala tree in the forest severed by an axe. Seeing her son who was like a mighty elephant or like the Sun or the Moon, Kaikeyi lifted him up from the ground and spoke these words:

shloka_text: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ किं शेषे राजपुत्र महायशः। त्वद्विधा नहि शोचन्ति सन्त स्सदसि सम्मताः।।2.72.24।।
transliteration: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha kiṃ śeṣe rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ| tvadvidhā nahi śocanti santa ssadasi sammatāḥ
translation: महायशः illustrious one, राजपुत्र prince, उत्तिष्ठ उत्तिष्ठ arise, arise, किं शेषे why are you lying down, सदसि in the assembly, सम्मताः worthy of honour, त्वद्विधाः like you, सन्तः learned people, न शोचन्ति हि ought not to grieve.
explanation: O illustrious prince arise, arise. Why are you lying down on the floor? Learned people like you, who are worthy of honour in the assembly ought not to grieve like this.

shloka_text: ﻿दानयज्ञाधिकारा हि शीलश्रुतिवचोऽनुगा। बुद्धिस्ते बुद्धिसम्पन्न प्रभेवार्कस्य मन्दिरे।।2.72.25।।
transliteration: ﻿dānayajñādhikārā hi śīlaśrutivaco'nugā| buddhiste buddhisampanna prabhevārkasya mandire
translation: ﻿ बुद्धिसम्पन्न intelligent, ते your, बुद्धिः wisdom, शीलश्रुतिवचोनुगा ever following virtuous conduct and scriptures, दानयज्ञाधिकारा entitled to dispense charity and perform sacrifices, अर्कस्य Sun's, मन्दिरे in the house, प्रभेव like light, (will always shine).
explanation: ﻿ O highly intelligent one, by your wisdom, virtuous conduct and scriptural knowledge you are entitled to dispense charity and perform sacrifices. You will always shine incessantly like light of the Sun.

shloka_text: स रुदित्वा चिरं कालं भूमौ विपरिवृत्य च। जननीं प्रत्युवाचेदं शोकैर्बहुभिरावृतः।।2.72.26।।
transliteration: sa ruditvā ciraṃ kālaṃ bhūmau viparivṛtya ca| jananīṃ pratyuvācedaṃ śokairbahubhirāvṛtaḥ
translation: सः he (Bharata), बहुभिः in many ways, शोकैः with sorrow, आवृतः engulfed by, चिरं कालम् for a long time, रुदित्वा having wept, भूमौ on the ground, विपरिवृत्य च and rolled, जननीम्  to his mother, इदम् these words, प्रत्युवाच replied.
explanation: Bharata engulfed in profuse sorrow wept for a long time rolling on the ground and then said these words in reply to his mother:

shloka_text: अभिषेक्ष्यति रामं नु राजा यज्ञं नु यक्ष्यते। इत्यहं कृतसङ्कल्पो हृष्टो यात्रामयासिषम्।।2.72.27।।
transliteration: abhiṣekṣyati rāmaṃ nu rājā yajñaṃ nu yakṣyate| ityahaṃ kṛtasaṅkalpo hṛṣṭo yātrāmayāsiṣam
translation: राजा king, रामम् Rama, अभिषेक्ष्यति नु  about to consecrate, यज्ञम् sacrifice, यक्ष्यते नु or will perform indeed, इति thinking, अहम् I, कृतसङ्कल्पः with these thoughts, हृष्टः delighted, यात्राम् journey, अयासिषम् had undertaken.
explanation: Thinking that the king is about to consecrate Rama or perform some sacrifice, I undertook the journey in great delight.

shloka_text: तदिदं ह्यन्यथा भूतं व्यवदीर्णं मनो मम। पितरं यो न पश्यामि नित्यं प्रियहिते रतम्।।2.72.28।।
transliteration: tadidaṃ hyanyathā bhūtaṃ vyavadīrṇaṃ mano mama| pitaraṃ yo na paśyāmi nityaṃ priyahite ratam
translation: तत् इदम् all this, अन्यथा differently, भूतम् has happened, यः such me, नित्यम् always, प्रियहिते  my welfare and happiness, रतम् intent on, पितरम् father, न पश्यामि I do not behold, मम my, मनः mind, व्यवदीर्णम् is shattered.
explanation: Now everything has turned out to be different. My mind is shattered.I no longer behold my father who is ever intent on my welfare and happiness.

shloka_text: अम्ब केनात्यगाद्राजा व्याघिना मय्यनागते। धन्या रामादयस्सर्वे यैः पिता संस्कृत स्स्वयम्।।2.72.29।।
transliteration: amba kenātyagādrājā vyāghinā mayyanāgate| dhanyā rāmādayassarve yaiḥ pitā saṃskṛta ssvayam
translation: अम्ब O mother, राजा king, मयि my, अनागते even before I could return, केन व्याधिना by what ailment, अत्यगात् passed away, यैः by Rama and others, पिता father, स्वयम् personally, संस्कृतः has been offered last rites, such, रामादयः Rama and others, धन्याः are fortunate.
explanation: O mother what ailment caused the king's death before I could return? How fortunate are Rama and others by whom the last rites of my father were performed

shloka_text: ﻿न नूनं मां महाराजः प्राप्तं जानाति कीर्तिमान्। उपजिघ्रेद्धि मूर्ध्नि तात स्सन्नम्य सत्वरम्।।2.72.30।।
transliteration: ﻿na nūnaṃ māṃ mahārājaḥ prāptaṃ jānāti kīrtimān| upajighreddhi mūrdhni tāta ssannamya satvaram
translation: ﻿ कीर्तिमान् illustrious, महाराजः great king, माम् me, प्राप्तम् reaching this place, न जानाति does not know, नूनम् surely, तातः father, सत्वरम् quickly, माम् me, सन्नम्य bending, मूर्ध्नि on the fore head, उपजिघ्रेत् हि would have smelt indeed( kissed).
explanation: ﻿ Surely the illustrious maharaja is not aware of my arrival. Otherwise he would have quickly bent my head and kissed me on my forehead.

shloka_text: ﻿क्व स पाणिस्सुखस्पर्शस्तातस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। येन मां रजसा ध्वस्तमभीक्ष्णं परिमार्जति।।2.72.31।।
transliteration: ﻿kva sa pāṇissukhasparśastātasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ| yena māṃ rajasā dhvastamabhīkṣṇaṃ parimārjati
translation: ﻿ रजसा with dust, ध्वस्तम् covered, माम् me, येन by which (hand), अभीक्ष्णम् repeatedly, परिमार्जति used to wipe away, अक्लिष्टकर्मणः of tireless actions, तातस्य father's, सुखस्पर्शः having pleasant touch, सः पाणिः that hand, क्व where is it?
explanation: ﻿ Where is that hand of my father of unwearied actions, the hand that would wipe away the dust from my person with a pleasant touch?

shloka_text: यो मे भ्राता पिता बन्धुर्यस्य दासोऽस्मि धीमतः। तस्य मां शीघ्रमाख्याहि रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः।।2.72.32।।
transliteration: yo me bhrātā pitā bandhuryasya dāso'smi dhīmataḥ| tasya māṃ śīghramākhyāhi rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
translation: यः who, मे to me, भ्राता brother, पिता father, बन्धुः relative, धीमतः wise, यस्य whose, दासः अस्मि I am a slave (of that wise man), तस्य such, अक्लिष्टकर्मणः of a man of unwearied actions, रामस्य to Rama, माम् about me, शीघ्रम् at once, आख्याहि announce.
explanation: Announce at once my arrival to the wise Rama, the man of unwearied actions, my brother, father and friend whose slave I am.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿पिता हि भवति ज्येष्ठो धर्ममार्यस्य जानतः। तस्य पादौ ग्रहीष्यामि स हीदानीं गतिर्मम।।2.72.33।।
transliteration: ﻿﻿pitā hi bhavati jyeṣṭho dharmamāryasya jānataḥ| tasya pādau grahīṣyāmi sa hīdānīṃ gatirmama
translation: ﻿﻿ धर्मम् the ways of righteousness, जानतः one who knows, आर्यस्य of the noble person, ज्येष्ठः eldest brother, पिता भवति हि becomes father, तस्य his, पादौ feet, ग्रहीष्यामि shall hold, स: he, इदानीम् now, मम my, गतिः हि is a refuge indeed.
explanation: ﻿﻿ To one who knows the ways of righteousness the elder brother is (like) the father. Indeed, he (Rama) is my refuge and I shall hold his feet now.

shloka_text: ﻿﻿﻿धर्मविद्धर्मनित्यश्च सत्यसन्धो दृढव्रतः। आर्यः किमब्रवीद्राजा पिता मे सत्यविक्रमः।।2.72.34।।
transliteration: ﻿﻿﻿dharmaviddharmanityaśca satyasandho dṛḍhavrataḥ| āryaḥ kimabravīdrājā pitā me satyavikramaḥ
translation: ﻿﻿﻿ धर्मवित् conversant with virtuous conduct, धर्मनित्यश्च one who always conducts himself in a righteous manner, सत्यसन्ध: fixed upon truth, दृढव्रतः firm in vows, सत्यविक्रमः one whose strength is truth, आर्यः venerable one, राजा king, मे पिता my father, किम् what, अब्रवीत् did he say (at the time of his death)?
explanation: ﻿﻿﻿ What did my father, the noble king, conversant with righteous conduct, true, to his vows, one who always conducted himself in a righteous manner, whose truth was his prowess (at the time of his death)?

shloka_text: पश्चिमं साधु सन्देशमिच्छामि श्रोतुमात्मनः। इति पृष्टा यथातत्त्वं कैकेयी वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.72.35।।
transliteration: paścimaṃ sādhu sandeśamicchāmi śrotumātmanaḥ| iti pṛṣṭā yathātattvaṃ kaikeyī vākyamabravīt
translation: आत्मनः relating to me, पश्चिमम् last, सन्देशम् message, साधु exactly, श्रोतुम् to listen, इच्छामि wish, इति thus, पृष्टा questioned, कैकेयी Kaikeyi, यथा तत्त्वम् as actually happened, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: I want to hear the exact words of my father's last message to me. Thus questioned (by Bharata), Kaikeyi related the exact facts:

shloka_text: रामेति राजा विलपन् हा सीते लक्ष्मणेति च। स महात्मा परं लोकं गतो गतिमतां वरः।।2.72.36।।
transliteration: rāmeti rājā vilapan hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca| sa mahātmā paraṃ lokaṃ gato gatimatāṃ varaḥ
translation: गतिमताम् among those who attained the excellent state, वरः the foremost, महात्मा magnanimous, सः that, राजा king, रामेति O Rama, हा सीते O Sita, लक्ष्मणेति च O Lakshmana also, विलपन् lamenting, परं लोकम् to the other world, गतः went.
explanation: The magnanimous king, the foremost of those who attained the excellent state after, death, went to the other world, lamenting 'O Rama, O Sita, O Lakshamana'.

shloka_text: इमां तु पश्चिमां वाचं व्याजहार पिता तव। कालधर्मपरिक्षिप्तः पाशैरिव महागजः।।2.72.37।।
transliteration: imāṃ tu paścimāṃ vācaṃ vyājahāra pitā tava| kāladharmaparikṣiptaḥ pāśairiva mahāgajaḥ
translation: तव your, पिता father, महागजः like a great elephant, पाशैरिव as though by cords,               कालधर्मपरिक्षिप्तः caught by the noose of fate and time, पश्चिमाम् last, इमाम् this, वाचम् words, व्याजहार uttered.
explanation: Your father, caught by the noose of death, like a great elephant bound by cords, uttered these last words:

shloka_text: सिद्धार्थास्ते नरा राममागतं सह सीतया। लक्ष्मणं च महाबाहुं द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुनरागतम्।।2.72.38।।
transliteration: siddhārthāste narā rāmamāgataṃ saha sītayā| lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābāhuṃ drakṣyanti punarāgatam
translation: सीतया सह along with Sita, आगतम् returned, रामम् Rama, पुनः again, आगतम् arrived, महाबाहुम् mightyarmed, लक्ष्मणं च with Lakshmana, द्रक्ष्यन्ति see, ते नराः those men, सिद्धार्थाः will have their desires fulfilled.
explanation: 'Those men who will see Rama returning home along with Sita and mightyarmed Lakshmana, will have their desires fulfilled.'

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा विषसादैव द्वितीयाप्रियशंसनात्। विषण्णवदनो भूत्वा भूयः पप्रच्छ मातरम्।।2.72.39।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā viṣasādaiva dvitīyāpriyaśaṃsanāt| viṣaṇṇavadano bhūtvā bhūyaḥ papraccha mātaram
translation: तत् that one, श्रूत्वा on hearing, द्वितीयाप्रियशंसनात् the account of second unpleasant tidings, विषसादैव more distressed, विषण्णवदनः भूत्वा with downcast countenance, भूयः again, मातरम् mother, पप्रच्छ enquired.
explanation: Bharata was more distraught on hearing the words that conveyed the second unpleasant tidings. With downcast countenance, he again enquired of his mother thus:

shloka_text: ﻿क्व चेदानीं स धर्मात्मा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया च समं गतः।।2.72.40।।
transliteration: ﻿kva cedānīṃ sa dharmātmā kausalyānandavardhanaḥ| lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā ca samaṃ gataḥ
translation: ﻿ धर्मात्मा righteous one, सः he, कौशल्यानन्दवर्धनः one who enhances the delight of Kausalya, भ्रात्रा with his brother, लक्ष्मणेन सह with Lakshmana too, सीतया च समम् with Sita, इदानीम् at this time, क्व where, गतः has gone?
explanation: ﻿ Where has righteous Rama who enhances the delight of Kausalya along with his brother Lakshmana and Sita gone now?

shloka_text: तथा पृष्टा यथातत्त्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे। मातास्य सुमहद्वाक्यं विप्रियं प्रियशङ्कया।।2.72.41।।
transliteration: tathā pṛṣṭā yathātattvamākhyātumupacakrame| mātāsya sumahadvākyaṃ vipriyaṃ priyaśaṅkayā
translation: तथा thus, पृष्टा  questioned, अस्य माता his mother, सुमहत् great, विप्रियम् grievous, वाक्यम् words, प्रियशङ्कया presuming it to be pleasant, यथातत्त्वम् exact fact, आख्यातुम् to relate, उपचक्रमे commenced.
explanation: Thus questioned, his mother started relating the exact events, presuming them to be pleasant tidings (for Bharata).

shloka_text: स हि राजसुतः पुत्र चीरवासा महावनम्। दण्डकान्सह वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणानुचरो गतः।।2.72.42।।
transliteration: sa hi rājasutaḥ putra cīravāsā mahāvanam| daṇḍakānsaha vaidehyā lakṣmaṇānucaro gataḥ
translation: पुत्र O son, राजसुतः king's son (prince), सः that Rama, चीरवासाः attired in garments of bark, लक्ष्मणानुचरः followed by Lakshmana, वैदेह्या सह with Sita, महावनम् great forest, दण्डकान् to Dandaka, गतः हि left.
explanation: O my son, prince Rama attired in garments of bark along with Sita and followed by Lakshmana left for the great Dandaka forest.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतस्त्रस्तो भ्रातुश्चारित्रशङ्कया। स्वस्य वंशस्य महात्म्यात्प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे।।2.72.43।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā bharatastrasto bhrātuścāritraśaṅkayā| svasya vaṃśasya mahātmyātpraṣṭuṃ samupacakrame
translation: भरतः Bharata, तत् that word, श्रुत्वा having heard, स्वस्य वंशस्य his dynasty's, महात्म्यात् due to greatness, भ्रातुः his brother's, चरित्रशङ्कया doubting about unrighteous conduct, प्रष्टुम्  to ascertain, समुपचक्रमे again started.
explanation: Conscious of the glory of his race, Bharata continued to enquire if there was any unrighteous conduct on the part of his brother.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्न ब्राह्मणधनं हृतं रामेण कस्यचित्। कच्चिन्नाढ्यो दरिद्रो वा तेनापापो विहिंसितः।।2.72.44।।
transliteration: kaccinna brāhmaṇadhanaṃ hṛtaṃ rāmeṇa kasyacit| kaccinnāḍhyo daridro vā tenāpāpo vihiṃsitaḥ
translation: रामेण by Rama, कस्यचित् of some one or the other, ब्राह्मण धनम् wealth of brahmin, न हृतं  did not seize, कच्चित् I hope not, तेन by him, आढ्यः a rich man, दरिद्रो वा or a poor one, अपापः innocent, न विहिंसितः was not tortured, कच्चित् I hope.
explanation: I hope Rama did not seize the wealth of any brahmin nor did any harm to an innocent person, whether rich or poor.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्न परदारान्वा राजपुत्रोऽभिमन्यते। कस्मात्स दण्डकारण्ये भ्रूणहेव विवासितः।।2.72.45।।
transliteration: kaccinna paradārānvā rājaputro'bhimanyate| kasmātsa daṇḍakāraṇye bhrūṇaheva vivāsitaḥ
translation: राजपुत्रः the prince, परदारान् another man's wife, नाभिमन्यते वा कच्चित् did not covet, I hope, स: he, Rama, भ्रूणहा like a sinner who had slain a child in embryo, दण्डकारण्ये to Dandaka forest, कस्मात् why, विवासितः has been banished.
explanation: I hope he did not covet another man's wife. Like a sinner who had slain a child in embryo why has he been banished to Dandaka forest?

shloka_text: ﻿अथास्य चपला माता तत्स्वकर्म यथातथम्। तेनैव स्त्रीस्वभावेन व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे।।2.72.46।।
transliteration: ﻿athāsya capalā mātā tatsvakarma yathātatham| tenaiva strīsvabhāvena vyāhartumupacakrame
translation: ﻿ अथ thereafter, चपला the capricious one, अस्य माता his mother, तेन by the same, स्त्री स्वभावेन with her earlier feminine disposition, तत् that, स्वकर्म her own deeds, यथातथम् faithfully, व्याहर्तुम् to tell, उपचक्रमे commenced.
explanation: ﻿ Then the capricious mother, with the same feminine disposition which she had displayed earlier, started giving a faithful account of all her deeds.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु कैकेयी भरतेन महात्मना। उवाच वचनं हृष्टा मूढा पण्डितमानिनी।।2.72.47।।
transliteration: evamuktā tu kaikeyī bharatena mahātmanā| uvāca vacanaṃ hṛṣṭā mūḍhā paṇḍitamāninī
translation: महात्मना great, भरतेन by Bharata, एवम् thus, उक्ता spoken, मूढा the foolish lady, पण्डितमानिनी thinking herself to be wise, कैकेयी Kaikeyi, हृष्टा delightfully, वचनम् these words, उवाच spoke.
explanation: On hearing the words of great Bharata, that foolish woman Kaikeyi thinking herself to be wise, cheerfully said:

shloka_text: न ब्राह्मणधनं किञ्चिद्धृतं रामेण कस्यचित् कश्चिन्नाढ्यो दरिद्रो तेनापापो विहिंसितः। न रामः परदारांश्च चक्षुर्भ्यामपि पश्यति।।2.72.48।।
transliteration: na brāhmaṇadhanaṃ kiñciddhṛtaṃ rāmeṇa kasyacit kaścinnāḍhyo daridro tenāpāpo vihiṃsitaḥ| na rāmaḥ paradārāṃśca cakṣurbhyāmapi paśyati
translation: रामेण by Rama, कस्यचित् some one's, ब्राह्मण धनम् wealth of brahmin, किञ्चित् even a little, न हृतम् was not seized, तेन by him, आढ्यः whether rich, दरिद्रो वा or poor अपापः innocent, कश्चित् even a little, न विहिंसितः was not harmed, रामः Rama, परदारान् wife of other man, चक्षुर्भ्याम् with the eyes, न पश्यति did not see.
explanation: Rama did not rob any brahmin of even a little wealth nor did he harm any innocent man, whether rich or poor. He never casts his eyes on another's wife.

shloka_text: मया तु पुत्र श्रुत्वैव रामस्यैवाभिषेचनम्। याचितस्ते पिता राज्यं रामस्य च विवासनम्।।2.72.49।।
transliteration: mayā tu putra śrutvaiva rāmasyaivābhiṣecanam| yācitaste pitā rājyaṃ rāmasya ca vivāsanam
translation: पुत्र O my son, मया तु by me, रामस्यैव Rama's, अभिषेचनम् consecration, श्रुत्वैव on hearing itself, पिता your father, ते for you, राज्यम् kingdom, रामस्य Rama's, विवासनं च  banishment, याचितः has been asked.
explanation: My son, I on hearing of Rama's consecration asked your father to confer the kingdom on you and banish Rama.

shloka_text: स स्ववृत्तिं समास्थाय पिता ते तत्तऽथाकरोत्। रामश्च सह सौमित्रिः प्रेषितस्सह सीतया।।2.72.50।।
transliteration: sa svavṛttiṃ samāsthāya pitā te tatta'thākarot| rāmaśca saha saumitriḥ preṣitassaha sītayā
translation: ते पिता your father, सः he, स्ववृत्तिम् kept up his own promise, समास्थाय having followed, तत् that one, तथा exactly, अकरोत् performed, सहसौमित्रि along with Lakshmana, रामश्च Rama also, सीतया सह along with Sita, प्रेषितः were sent.
explanation: Your father, faithful to his word, banished Rama along with Lakshmana and Sita.

shloka_text: तमपश्यन्प्रियंपुत्रं महीपालो महायशाः। पुत्रशोकपरिद्यूनः पञ्चत्वमुपपेदिवान्।।2.72.51।।
transliteration: tamapaśyanpriyaṃputraṃ mahīpālo mahāyaśāḥ| putraśokaparidyūnaḥ pañcatvamupapedivān
translation: महायशाः renowned, महीपालः ruler of this earth, तम् that, प्रियं पुत्रम् beloved son, अपश्यन् not being able to behold, पुत्रशोक परिद्यूनः stricken by filial grief, पञ्चत्वम् the state of merger in the five elements, उपपेदिवान् obtained.
explanation: The renowned ruler of the earth (king Dasaratha), unable to behold (the sorry state of) his beloved son and stricken by filial grief, merged into the five elements (died).

shloka_text: त्वयात्विदानीं धर्मज्ञ राजत्वमवलम्ब्यताम्। त्वत्कृते हि मया सर्वमिदमेवं विधं कृतम्।।2.72.52।।
transliteration: tvayātvidānīṃ dharmajña rājatvamavalambyatām| tvatkṛte hi mayā sarvamidamevaṃ vidhaṃ kṛtam
translation: धर्मज्ञ O knower of dharma, इदानीम् now, त्वया by you, राजत्वम् kingship, अवलम्ब्यताम् take possession of, मया by me, त्वत्कृते for your sake only, एवं विधम् in this manner, इदं सर्वम् all this, कृतं हि has been done.
explanation: O knower of dharma, assume kingship now. It is only for your sake that all this has been done by me.

shloka_text: ﻿मा शोकं मा च सन्तापं धैर्यमाश्रय पुत्रक। त्वदधीना हि नगरी राज्यं चैतदनामयम्।।2.72.53।।
transliteration: ﻿mā śokaṃ mā ca santāpaṃ dhairyamāśraya putraka| tvadadhīnā hi nagarī rājyaṃ caitadanāmayam
translation: ﻿ पुत्रक my son, शोकम् sorrow, मा आश्रय do not take recourse, सन्तापं च to remorse, मा do not take recourse, धैर्यम् courage, आश्रय take recourse, नगरी this city, त्वदधीना is under your control, अनामयम् free from obstacles, एतत् this, राज्यं च kingdom also.
explanation: ﻿ My son, give up sorrow and agony and take recourse to courage. This city as well as the kingdom, free from all obstacles, is under your control.

shloka_text: सश्रूत्वा तु पितरं वृत्तं भ्रातरौ च विवासितौ। भरतो दुःखसन्तप्त इदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.73.1।।
transliteration: saśrūtvā tu pitaraṃ vṛttaṃ bhrātarau ca vivāsitau| bharato duḥkhasantapta idaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: भरतः Bharata, पितरम् father, वृत्तम् had passed away, भ्रातरौ the two brothers, विवासितौ  were in exile, श्रुत्वा तु having heard, दुःखसन्तप्तः afflicted with sorrow, इदम् these, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: On hearing about the demise of the father and his two brothers sent in exile, Bharata  overtaken by sorrow spoke thus:
comments: Bharata grieves over his misfortune -- accuses Kaikeyi in so many words -- reveals his decision to bring back Rama to Ayodhya and serve him.

shloka_text: किं नु कार्यं हतस्येह मम राज्येन शोचतः। विहीनस्याथ पित्रा च भ्रात्रा पितृसमेन च।।2.73.2।।
transliteration: kiṃ nu kāryaṃ hatasyeha mama rājyena śocataḥ| vihīnasyātha pitrā ca bhrātrā pitṛsamena ca
translation: पित्रा च with father, अथ and, पितृसमेन like to a father to me, भ्रात्राच with brother, विहीनस्य bereft, शोचतः of a grieving one, हतस्य fallen into misfortunes, मम to me, इह now, राज्येन with the kingdom, किं नु कार्यम् of what avail?
explanation: Bereft of my father and my brother who was like a father to me, of what avail is this kingdom to me when I am grieving and fallen into misfortunes?

shloka_text: दुःखे मे दुःखमकरोर्व्रणे क्षारमिवादधाः। राजानं प्रेतभावस्थं कृत्वा रामं च तापसम्।।2.73.3।।
transliteration: duḥkhe me duḥkhamakarorvraṇe kṣāramivādadhāḥ| rājānaṃ pretabhāvasthaṃ kṛtvā rāmaṃ ca tāpasam
translation: राजानम् king, प्रेतभावस्थम् reducing to a corpse, रामं च also Rama, तापसम् as an ascetic, कृत्वा having made, मे to me, दुःखे in one sorrow, दुःखं another sorrow, (मे) अकरोः you have caused, व्रणे in the wound, क्षारम् salt, आदधाः इव like putting.
explanation: You have caused the death of the king and reduced Rama to an ascetic. You have piled one sorrow over sorrow on me like rubbing salt to the wound

shloka_text: कुलस्य त्वमभावाय कालरात्रिरिवाऽगता। अङ्गारमुपगूह्य स्म पिता मे नावबुद्धवान्।।2.73.4।।
transliteration: kulasya tvamabhāvāya kālarātririvā'gatā| aṅgāramupagūhya sma pitā me nāvabuddhavān
translation: त्वम् you, कुलस्य family's, अभावाय for destruction, कालरात्रिरिव like a fatal night, आगता  have arrived, मे पिता my father, अङ्गारम् a live charcoal, उपगूह्य having embraced, नावबुद्धवान् did not realize.
explanation: You have come here for the destruction of this race, like a fatal night. My father did not realize that he was embracing a live charcoal.

shloka_text: मृत्युमापादितो पिता त्वया मे पापदर्शिनि। सुखं परिहृतं मोहात्कुलेऽस्मिन्कुलपांसनि।।2.73.5।।
transliteration: mṛtyumāpādito pitā tvayā me pāpadarśini| sukhaṃ parihṛtaṃ mohātkule'sminkulapāṃsani
translation: पापदर्शिनि O woman of sinful thoughts, त्वया by you, मे पिता my father, मृत्युम् death, आपादितः was led to, कुलपांसनि O obloquy of the race, मोहात् out of folly, अस्मिन्  कुले in this family, सुखम् happiness, परिहृतम् has been taken away.
explanation: O woman of sinful thoughts, you have brought about the death of my father. O obloquy of the race, by your folly you have deprived this family of its happiness.

shloka_text: त्वां प्राप्य हि पिता मेऽद्य सत्यसन्धो महायशाः। तीव्रदुःखाभिसन्तप्तो वृत्तो दशरथो नृपः।।2.73.6।।
transliteration: tvāṃ prāpya hi pitā me'dya satyasandho mahāyaśāḥ| tīvraduḥkhābhisantapto vṛtto daśaratho nṛpaḥ
translation: मे my, पिता father, सत्यसन्धः adhering to truth, महायशाः renowned, नृपः king, दशरथः Dasaratha, अद्य now, त्वाम् you, प्राप्य having come under your influence, तीव्र दुःखाभिसन्तप्तः tormented by intense grief, वृत्तः has departed from this world.
explanation: My father king Dasaratha who is bound to truth and highly renowned, having come under your influence and tormented by intense grief has departed from this world.

shloka_text: विनाशितो महाराजः पिता मे धर्मवत्सलः। कस्मात्प्रव्राजितो रामः कस्मादेव वनं गतः।।2.73.7।।
transliteration: vināśito mahārājaḥ pitā me dharmavatsalaḥ| kasmātpravrājito rāmaḥ kasmādeva vanaṃ gataḥ
translation: धर्मवत्सलः righteous, महाराजः great king, मे पिता my father, कस्मात् for what reason, विनाशितः has been destroyed, रामः Rama, कस्मात् for what reason, प्रव्राजितः has been exiled, वनम् to the forest, गतः has gone.
explanation: Why was my father the righteous maharaja killed? Why was Rama exiled into the forest?

shloka_text: कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च पुत्रशोकाभिपीडिते। दुष्करं यदि जीवेतां प्राप्य त्वां जननीं मम।।2.73.8।।
transliteration: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca putraśokābhipīḍite| duṣkaraṃ yadi jīvetāṃ prāpya tvāṃ jananīṃ mama
translation: पुत्रशोकाभिपीडिते tormented by the grief on account of separation from their sons, कौशल्या च Kausalya and, सुमित्रा च Sumitra too, मम जननीम् my own mother, त्वाम् you, प्राप्य having obtained, जीवेतां यदि will survive, दुष्करम् difficult.
explanation: Tormented by the grief of separation from their sons, it is difficult for Kausalya and Sumitra to survive under you, O my mother.

shloka_text: ननुत्वार्योऽपि धर्मात्मा त्वयि वृतिमनुत्तमाम्। वर्तते गुरुवृत्तिज्ञो यथा मातरि वर्तते।।2.73.9।।
transliteration: nanutvāryo'pi dharmātmā tvayi vṛtimanuttamām| vartate guruvṛttijño yathā mātari vartate
translation: धर्मत्मा righteous, गुरुवृत्तिज्ञः well aware of his duties towards elders, आर्योऽपि noble, too  मातरि towards his mother, यथा as, वर्तते conducted himself, त्वयि towards you, अनुत्तमाम् very great, वृत्तिम् conduct, वर्तते ननु is abiding indeed.
explanation: My noble and righteous brother (Rama), who is well aware of his duties to the elders conducted himself before you as he would before his own mother.

shloka_text: तथा ज्येष्ठा हि मे माता कौसल्या दीर्घदर्शिनी। त्वयि धर्मं समास्थाय भगिन्यामिव वर्तते।।2.74.10।।
transliteration: tathā jyeṣṭhā hi me mātā kausalyā dīrghadarśinī| tvayi dharmaṃ samāsthāya bhaginyāmiva vartate
translation: तथा in the same way, मे my, ज्येष्टा eldest, माता mother, दीर्घदर्शिनी a lady with farsight, कौशल्या Kausalya, धर्मम् righteousness, समास्थाय having adhered, त्वयि towards you, भगिन्यामिव as if a sister, वर्तते हि conducted
explanation: In the same way my eldest mother the farsighted Kausalya, too adhered to righteousness and conducted herself towards you like a sister.

shloka_text: तस्याः पुत्रं कृताऽत्मानं चीरवल्कलवाससम्। प्रस्थाप्य वनवासाय कथं पापे न शोचसि।।2.73.11।।
transliteration: tasyāḥ putraṃ kṛtā'tmānaṃ cīravalkalavāsasam| prasthāpya vanavāsāya kathaṃ pāpe na śocasi
translation: पापे O perverse wretch, कृतात्मानम् a man pure in mind, तस्याः Kauslaya's, पुत्रम् son, चीरवल्कलवाससम् made to adorn garments made of bark, वनवासाय to dwell in the forest, प्रस्थाप्य having sent, कथम् how, न शोचसि you do not feel remorseful?
explanation: You have forced Kausalya's son, so pure in mind, to wear garments made of bark and dwell in the forest. Do you not feel remorse for it, O perverse wretch?

shloka_text: अपापदर्शनं शूरं कृतात्मानं यशस्विनम्। प्रव्राज्य चीरवसनं किन्नु पश्यसि कारणम्।।2.73.12।।
transliteration: apāpadarśanaṃ śūraṃ kṛtātmānaṃ yaśasvinam| pravrājya cīravasanaṃ kinnu paśyasi kāraṇam
translation: अपापदर्शनम् one who never contemplated evil, शूरम् valiant, कृतात्मानम् having control over his mind, यशस्विनम् the glorious, चीरवसनम् clad in bark clothes, प्रव्राज्य after being exiled, किन्नु what possible, कारणम् reason, पश्यसि do you see?
explanation: The glorious, valiant, selfpossessed (Rama) had never contemplated evil. What possible reason do you have for sending him, clothed in bark, into exile?

shloka_text: ﻿लुब्धाया विदितो मन्ये न तेऽहं राघवं प्रति। तथाह्यनर्धो राज्यार्थं त्वयाऽनीतो महानयम्।।2.73.13।।
transliteration: ﻿lubdhāyā vidito manye na te'haṃ rāghavaṃ prati| tathāhyanardho rājyārthaṃ tvayā'nīto mahānayam
translation: ﻿ लुब्धायाः of avaricious, ते to you, अहम् I, राघवं प्रति to Rama, न विदितः were unaware of, मन्ये I deem, तथाहि that is proper, त्वया by you, राज्यार्थम् for the sake of kingdom, अयम् this, महान् great, अनर्थः calamity, आनीतः has been brought about.
