explanation: After travelling a long distance on chariots, carriages, horses and elephants, they reached the river Ganga close to Srngiberapura, a country ruled vigilantly by Rama's friend, the valiant Guha who lived there along with his relatives.

shloka_text: उपेत्य तीरं गङ्गायाश्चक्रवाकैरलङ्कृतम्। व्यवातिष्ठत सा सेना भरतस्यानुयायिनी।।2.83.21।।
transliteration: upetya tīraṃ gaṅgāyāścakravākairalaṅkṛtam| vyavātiṣṭhata sā senā bharatasyānuyāyinī
translation: भरतस्य अनुयायिनी following Bharata, सा सेना that army, चक्रवाकैः with chakravakas (the ruddy geese), अलङ्कृतम् graced, गङ्गायाः river Ganga's, तीरम् bank, उपेत्य having reached, व्यवातिष्ठत halted there.
explanation: The army following Bharata reached the bank of the river Ganga, graced by chakravakas (ruddy geese) and halted there.

shloka_text: निरीक्ष्यानुगतां सेनां तां च गङ्गां शिवोदकाम्। भरतस्सचिवान्सर्वानब्रवीद्वाक्यकोविदः।।2.83.22।।
transliteration: nirīkṣyānugatāṃ senāṃ tāṃ ca gaṅgāṃ śivodakām| bharatassacivānsarvānabravīdvākyakovidaḥ
translation: अनुगताम् following, सेनाम् army, शिवोदकाम् having sacred waters, तां गङ्गां च that river Ganga, निरीक्षय having gazed at, वाक्यकोविदः proficient in speech, भरतः Bharata, सर्वान् all, सचिवान् to ministers, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: As he beheld the army following him and the river Ganga of sacred waters in front of him, Bharata who was proficient in speech said to his ministers:

shloka_text: निवेशयत मे सैन्यमभिप्रायेण सर्वतः। विश्रान्ताः प्रतरिष्यामश्श्व इदानीमिमां नदीम्।।2.83.23।।
transliteration: niveśayata me sainyamabhiprāyeṇa sarvataḥ| viśrāntāḥ pratariṣyāmaśśva idānīmimāṃ nadīm
translation: मे सैन्यम् my army, अभिप्रायेण according to their desires, सर्वतः all over, निवेशयत you may halt, इदानीम् now, विश्रान्ताः having taken rest, नदीम् river, श्वः tomorrow, प्रतरिष्यामः will cross.
explanation: You may, according to your convenience, halt the army anywhere here and, after taking rest (for the night), we shall cross the river Ganga tomorrow.

shloka_text: दातुं च तावदिच्छामि स्वर्गतस्य महीपतेः। और्ध्वदेहनिमित्तार्थमवतीर्योदकं नदीम्।।2.83.24।।
transliteration: dātuṃ ca tāvadicchāmi svargatasya mahīpateḥ| aurdhvadehanimittārthamavatīryodakaṃ nadīm
translation: नदीम् river, अवतीर्य descending, स्वर्गतस्य to the departed, महीपतेः king's, और्ध्वदेहनिमित्तार्थम् for the good of his life in the other world, उदकम् libations with water, दातुम् च to offer, इच्छामि तावत् I wish.
explanation: Meanwhile, I shall get into this river and offer libations with water to the departed king for the good of his life in the other world.

shloka_text: तस्यैवं ब्रुवतोऽमात्यास्तथेत्युक्त्वा समाहिताः। न्यवेशयंस्तां छन्देन स्वेन स्वेन पृथक्पृथक्।।2.83.25।।
transliteration: tasyaivaṃ bruvato'mātyāstathetyuktvā samāhitāḥ| nyaveśayaṃstāṃ chandena svena svena pṛthakpṛthak
translation: तस्य his (Bharata's), एवम् in this way, ब्रुवतः while saying, अमात्याः ministers, तथेति 'be it so', उक्त्वा  saying, समाहिताः with composed minds, ताम् they, स्वेन स्वेन each of their, छन्देन with pleasure, पृथक् पृथक् separately न्यवेशयन् rested.
explanation: While he (Bharata's) was speaking this way, all the ministers assented by saying 'Be it so' and made arrangement for their troops to rest separately according to their pleasure.

shloka_text: निवेश्य गङ्गामनु तां महानदीं चमूं विधानैः परिबर्हशोभिनीम्। उवास रामस्य तदा महात्मनो विचिन्तयानो भरतो निवर्तनम्।।2.83.26।।
transliteration: niveśya gaṅgāmanu tāṃ mahānadīṃ camūṃ vidhānaiḥ paribarhaśobhinīm| uvāsa rāmasya tadā mahātmano vicintayāno bharato nivartanam
translation: भरतः Bharata, परिबर्हशोभिनीम् looking splendid with their royal insignia, चमूम् army, ताम् that, महानदीम् mighty river, गङ्गाम् अनु following Ganga, विधानैः with adequate arrangements, निवेश्य encamping, तदा then, महात्मनः magnanimous, रामस्य Rama's, निवर्तनम् to bring back, विचिन्तयानः pondering, उवास stayed.
explanation: The army encamped by Bharata looked splendid with royal insigaia. After making necessary arrangements for the army on the bank of the mighty river Ganga and pondering over the means of bringing back the magnanimous Rama, Bharata stayed. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे त्र्यशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightythird sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततो निविष्टां ध्वजिनीं गङ्गामन्वाश्रितां नदीम्। निषादराजो दृष्ट्वैव ज्ञातीन्सन्त्वरितोऽऽब्रवीत्।।2.84.1।।
transliteration: tato niviṣṭāṃ dhvajinīṃ gaṅgāmanvāśritāṃ nadīm| niṣādarājo dṛṣṭvaiva jñātīnsantvarito''bravīt
translation: ततः then, निषादराजः king of the nishadas (Guha), गङ्गां नदीम् river Ganga, अन्वाश्रिताम् all along the bank, निविष्टाम् encamped, ध्वजिनीम् the bannered army, दृष्ट्वैव on seeing, सन्त्वरितः hurriedly, ज्ञातीन् to relatives, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Guha, king of the nishadas, observed the bannered army encamped all along the bank of the river Ganga, hurried off and said to his kinsmen:
comments: Guha spots from a distance Bharata's army approaching -- wants to know the intentions of Bharata -- convinced of Bharata's loyalty, he extends warn hospitality.

shloka_text: महतीयमितस्सेना सागराभा प्रदृश्यते। नास्यान्तमधिगच्छामि मनसापि विचिन्तयन्।।2.84.2।।
transliteration: mahatīyamitassenā sāgarābhā pradṛśyate| nāsyāntamadhigacchāmi manasāpi vicintayan
translation: इतः this side, सागराभा looking like an ocean, इयम् this, महती vast, सेना army, प्रदृश्यते appearing, मनसा in my mind, विचिन्तयन्नपि even by thinking, अस्याः this army's, अन्तम्  end, नाधिगच्छामि I am not able to reach.
explanation: Here is an army as vast as the ocean, and I am unable to comprehend its magnitude even mentally.

shloka_text: यथा तु खलु दुर्बुद्धिर्भरत स्स्वयमागतः। स एष हि महाकायः कोविदारध्वजो रथे।।2.84.3।।
transliteration: yathā tu khalu durbuddhirbharata ssvayamāgataḥ| sa eṣa hi mahākāyaḥ kovidāradhvajo rathe
translation: दुर्बुद्धि: evilminded, भरतः Bharata, स्वयम् himself, यथा तु आगतः खलु has come it appears,  सः that, महाकायः of huge size, कोविदारध्वजः having the emblem of kovidara                          (promegranate) tree, एषः this one, रथे हि on the chariot.
explanation: It appears that the evilminded Bharata himself has come here. The emblem of a huge kovidara (pomegranate) tree is seen on his chariot.

shloka_text: बन्धयिष्यति वा दाशानथवाऽस्मान्वधिष्यति। अथ दाशरथिं रामं पित्रा राज्याद्विवासितम्।।2.84.4।। सम्पन्नां श्रियमन्विच्छन्स्तस्य राज्ञ स्सुदुर्लभाम्। भरतः कैकयीपुत्रो हन्तुं समधिगच्छति।।2.84.5।।
transliteration: bandhayiṣyati vā dāśānathavā'smānvadhiṣyati| atha dāśarathiṃ rāmaṃ pitrā rājyādvivāsitam sampannāṃ śriyamanvicchanstasya rājña ssudurlabhām| bharataḥ kaikayīputro hantuṃ samadhigacchati
translation: कैकयीपुत्रः Kaikeyi's son, भरतः Bharata, दाशान् fishermen, बन्धयिष्यति is going to bind us  with cords?, अथवा or, अस्मान् us, वधिष्यति will slay?, अथ or, तस्य राज्ञः that king's, सम्पन्नाम्  prosperous, सुदुर्लभाम् not easily obtainable, श्रियम् wealth, अन्विच्छन् wishing, पित्रा by father, राज्यात् from kingdom, विवासितम् banished, दाशरथिम् son of Dasaratha, रामम् to Rama, हन्तुम् to slay, समधिगच्छति is he marching forward?
explanation: Could it be that Bharata, son of Kaikeyi, has come here to bind us with the cords or to slay us? Or is he marching forward with the intention of taking possession of a prosperous, rare kingdom by slaying Rama who has been banished by his father:

shloka_text: बन्धयिष्यति वा दाशानथवाऽस्मान्वधिष्यति। अथ दाशरथिं रामं पित्रा राज्याद्विवासितम्।।2.84.4।। सम्पन्नां श्रियमन्विच्छन्स्तस्य राज्ञ स्सुदुर्लभाम्। भरतः कैकयीपुत्रो हन्तुं समधिगच्छति।।2.84.5।।
transliteration: bandhayiṣyati vā dāśānathavā'smānvadhiṣyati| atha dāśarathiṃ rāmaṃ pitrā rājyādvivāsitam sampannāṃ śriyamanvicchanstasya rājña ssudurlabhām| bharataḥ kaikayīputro hantuṃ samadhigacchati
translation: कैकयीपुत्रः Kaikeyi's son, भरतः Bharata, दाशान् fishermen, बन्धयिष्यति is going to bind us  with cords?, अथवा or, अस्मान् us, वधिष्यति will slay?, अथ or, तस्य राज्ञः that king's, सम्पन्नाम्  prosperous, सुदुर्लभाम् not easily obtainable, श्रियम् wealth, अन्विच्छन् wishing, पित्रा by father, राज्यात् from kingdom, विवासितम् banished, दाशरथिम् son of Dasaratha, रामम् to Rama, हन्तुम् to slay, समधिगच्छति is he marching forward?
explanation: Could it be that Bharata, son of Kaikeyi, has come here to bind us with the cords or to slay us? Or is he marching forward with the intention of taking possession of a prosperous, rare kingdom by slaying Rama who has been banished by his father:

shloka_text: भर्ताचैव सखाचैव रामो दाशरथिर्मम। तस्यार्थकामास्सन्नद्धा गङ्गाऽनूपे प्रतिष्ठत।।2.84.6।।
transliteration: bhartācaiva sakhācaiva rāmo dāśarathirmama| tasyārthakāmāssannaddhā gaṅgā'nūpe pratiṣṭhata
translation: दाशरथिः son of Dasaratha, रामः Rama, मम to me, भर्ता चैव is my master, सखाचैव friend too, तस्य his, अर्थकामाः wealth and desires, गङ्गाऽनूपे on the bank of river Ganga, प्रतिष्ठत   remain stationed.
explanation: Rama, son of Dasaratha, is not only my master but also my friend. Therefore, to safeguard his interests remain stationed here on the bank of the river Ganga.

shloka_text: तिष्ठन्तु सर्वे दाशाश्च गङ्गामन्वाश्रिता नदीम्। बलयुक्ता नदीरक्षा मांसमूलफलाशनाः।।2.84.7।।
transliteration: tiṣṭhantu sarve dāśāśca gaṅgāmanvāśritā nadīm| balayuktā nadīrakṣā māṃsamūlaphalāśanāḥ
translation: मांसमूलफलाशनाः living on meat, roots and fruits, नदीरक्षाः protectors of the river, सर्वे all, दाशाश्च fishermen, बलयुक्ताः with your troops, गङ्गां नदीम् river Ganga, अन्वाश्रिताः following  and taking up your positions, तिष्ठन्तु stay here.
explanation: Let all the fishermen, who live on meat, roots and fruits and protect the river, stay here with the troops by taking up positions along the banks of the river Ganga.

shloka_text: नावां शतानां पञ्चानां कैवर्तानां शतं शतम्। सन्नद्धानां तथा यूनां तिष्ठन्त्वित्यभ्यचोदयत्।।2.84.8।।
transliteration: nāvāṃ śatānāṃ pañcānāṃ kaivartānāṃ śataṃ śatam| sannaddhānāṃ tathā yūnāṃ tiṣṭhantvityabhyacodayat
translation: पञ्चानाम् five, शतानाम् hundred, नावाम् boats, सन्नद्धानाम् fully equipped, तथा also, यूनाम् youths, कैवर्तानाम् fishermen, शतं शतम् one hundred in each, तिष्ठन्तु stand, इति like that, अभ्यचोदयत् exhorted.
explanation: Let five hundred boats, each manned by a hundred young fishermen fully equipped, be in readiness he exhorted them.

shloka_text: यदाऽऽदुष्टस्तु भरतो रामस्येह भविष्यति। सेयं स्वस्तिमती सेना गङ्गामद्य तरिष्यति।।2.84.9।।
transliteration: yadā''duṣṭastu bharato rāmasyeha bhaviṣyati| seyaṃ svastimatī senā gaṅgāmadya tariṣyati
translation: भरतः Bharata, इह here, रामस्य toward Rama, अदुष्टः not illdisposed, यदा तु भविष्यति  when it be proved, सा इयम् that this, सेना army, अद्य today, स्वस्तिमती in safety, गङ्गाम् Ganga, तरिष्यति will cross over.
explanation: Should it happen that Bharata is not illdisposed toward Rama, the army will safe cross the river Ganga today itself.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वोपायनं गृह्य मत्स्यमांसमधूनि च। अभिचक्राम भरतं निषादाधिपतिर्गुहः।।2.84.10।।
transliteration: ityuktvopāyanaṃ gṛhya matsyamāṃsamadhūni ca| abhicakrāma bharataṃ niṣādādhipatirguhaḥ
translation: निषादाधिपतिः गुहः overlord of the nishadas, Guha, इति thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, मत्स्यमांसमधूनि fish, meat and wine, उपायनम् as gifts, गृह्य holding, भरतम् to Bharata, अभिचक्राम approached.
explanation: Having spoken thus, Guha, lord of the nishadas, approached Bharata, taking with him fish, meat and wine as offerings.

shloka_text: तमायान्तं तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। भरतायाऽचचक्षेऽथ विनयज्ञो विनीतवत्।।2.84.11।।
transliteration: tamāyāntaṃ tu samprekṣya sūtaputraḥ pratāpavān| bharatāyā'cacakṣe'tha vinayajño vinītavat
translation: अथ thereafter, प्रतापवान् valiant, विनयज्ञः conversant with modesty, सूतपुत्रः son of charioteer, Sumantra, आयान्तम् approaching, तम् him, सम्प्रेक्ष्य having seen, विनीतवत्   humbly, भरताय to Bharata, आचचक्षे informed.
explanation: The valiant Sumantra, conversant with ways of modesty, observed Guha approaching them and humbly informed Bharata.

shloka_text: एष ज्ञातिसहस्रेण स्थपतिः परिवारितः। कुशलो दण्डकारण्ये वृद्धो भ्रातुश्च ते सखा।।2.84.12।।
transliteration: eṣa jñātisahasreṇa sthapatiḥ parivāritaḥ| kuśalo daṇḍakāraṇye vṛddho bhrātuśca te sakhā
translation: ज्ञातिसहस्रेण with thousands of relations, परिवारितः surrounded by, एषः स्थपतिः this lord,  दण्डकारण्ये in the Dandaka forest, कुशलः skilled, वृद्धः aged one, ते your, भ्रातुः brother's, सखा च friend also.
explanation: Guha who has come here surrounded by too many thousands of his relations is fully acquainted with the Dandaka forest. He is an aged man and a friend of your brother said Sumatra.

shloka_text: तस्मात्पश्यतु काकुत्स्थ त्वां निषादाधिपो गुहः। असंशयं विजानीते यत्र तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।।2.84.13।।
transliteration: tasmātpaśyatu kākutstha tvāṃ niṣādādhipo guhaḥ| asaṃśayaṃ vijānīte yatra tau rāmalakṣmaṇau
translation: काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, तस्मात् therefore, निषादाधिपः overlord of Nishadas, गुहः Guha, त्वाम् you, पश्यतु let him see, तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ both Rama and Lakshmana, यत्र where, असंशयम्   undoubtedly, विजानीते he will know.
explanation: O scion of the Kakusthas (Bharata) therefore, give audience to the overlord of the nishadas, Guha, who undoubtedly knows the whereabouts of Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: एतत्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा सुमन्त्राद्भरत श्शुभम्। उवाच वचनं शीघ्रं गुहः पश्यतु मामिति।।2.84.14।।
transliteration: etattu vacanaṃ śrutvā sumantrādbharata śśubham| uvāca vacanaṃ śīghraṃ guhaḥ paśyatu māmiti
translation: भरतः Bharata, सुमन्त्रात् from Sumantra, एतत् शुभम् these auspicious, वचनम् word, श्रुत्वा having heard, गुहः Guha, शीघ्रम् at once, माम् me, पश्यतु let him see, इति these, वचनम् word, उवाच said.
explanation: On hearing these auspicious words of Sumantra, Bharata said Let Guha see me at once.

shloka_text: लब्ध्वाऽभ्यनुज्ञां संहृष्टो ज्ञातिभिः परिवारितः। आगम्य भरतं प्रह्वो गुहो वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.84.15।।
transliteration: labdhvā'bhyanujñāṃ saṃhṛṣṭo jñātibhiḥ parivāritaḥ| āgamya bharataṃ prahvo guho vacanamabravīt
translation: गुहः Guha, अभ्यनुज्ञाम् permission, लब्ध्वा having obtained, संहृष्टः delighted, ज्ञातिभिः relatives, परिवारितः escorted by, आगम्य having approached, प्रह्वः bowing humbly, भरतम् to Bharata, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Having obtaind the permission, a delighted Guha, escorted by his relatives,  approached Bharata and humbly said:

shloka_text: निष्कुटश्चैव देशोऽयं वञ्चिताश्चापि ते वयम्। निवेदयामस्ते सर्वे स्वके दासकुले वस।।2.84.16।।
transliteration: niṣkuṭaścaiva deśo'yaṃ vañcitāścāpi te vayam| nivedayāmaste sarve svake dāsakule vasa
translation: अयम् this, देशः country, ते your, निष्कुटः is like a pleasuregarden behind your house, वयम् we, वञ्चिताश्चापि are subordinate, ते सर्वे all of us, निवेदयामः soliciting, दासकुले in the house of this servant, वस stay.
explanation: This country is like a pleasuregarden at the backyard of your palace. All of us are  subordinate to you and we solicit you to stay in the house of  this servant of yours.

shloka_text: अस्ति मूलं फलञ्चैव निषादैस्समुपाहृतम्। आर्द्रं च मांसं शुष्कं च वन्यं चोच्चावचं महत्।।2.84.17।।
transliteration: asti mūlaṃ phalañcaiva niṣādaissamupāhṛtam| ārdraṃ ca māṃsaṃ śuṣkaṃ ca vanyaṃ coccāvacaṃ mahat
translation: निषादैः by nishadas, समुपाहृतम् have been brought, मूलम् root, फलं चैव fruits also, वन्यम्  the forest produce, आर्द्रम् fresh, शुष्कं च dried, उच्चावचम् of great variety, महत् best, मांसं च  अस्ति meat are here.
explanation: Here are roots, fruits and a great variety of forest produce, fresh and dried meat brought by the nishadas.

shloka_text: आशंसे स्वाशिता सेना वत्स्यतीमां विभावरीम्। अर्चितो विविधैः कामै श्श्व स्ससैन्यो गमिष्यसि।।2.84.18।।
transliteration: āśaṃse svāśitā senā vatsyatīmāṃ vibhāvarīm| arcito vividhaiḥ kāmai śśva ssasainyo gamiṣyasi
translation: सेना army, स्वाशिता refreshed, इमाम् विभावरीम् this night, वत्स्यति will spend, आशंसे I hope, विविधैः by various, कामैः by our hospitality, अर्चितः treated, श्वः tomorrow, ससैन्यः with army, गमिष्यसि will go.
explanation: We hope your army having  refreshed themselves will spend the night here. With our hospitality extended, you can proceed tomorrow. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुरशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightyfourth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु भरतो निषादाधिपतिं गुहम्। प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो वाक्यं हेत्वर्थसंहितम्।।2.85.1।।
transliteration: evamuktastu bharato niṣādādhipatiṃ guham| pratyuvāca mahāprājño vākyaṃ hetvarthasaṃhitam
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः having spoken, महाप्राज्ञः  great intellectual, भरतः Bharata, निषादाधिपतिम् the overlord of the nishadas, गुहम् Guha, हेत्वर्थसंहितम् in well thought out and significant, वाक्यम् words, प्रत्युवाच replied.
explanation: When thus spoken to, Bharata, a great intellectual, replied to Guha with these well thought out and meaningful words.
comments: Bharata expresses his desire to bring back Rama -- enquires the way to Bharadwaja's hermitage.

shloka_text: ऊर्जितः खलु ते कामः कृतो मम गुरोस्सखे। यो मे त्वमीदृशीं सेनामेकोऽभ्यर्चितुमिच्छसि।।2.85.2।।
transliteration: ūrjitaḥ khalu te kāmaḥ kṛto mama gurossakhe| yo me tvamīdṛśīṃ senāmeko'bhyarcitumicchasi
translation: मम my, गुरोः elder brother's, सखे friend, यः त्वम् you, एकः alone, ईदृशीम् this large, सेनाम् army, अभ्यर्चितुम् to extend hospitality, इच्छसि want, ते your, कृतः done, कामः desire, ऊर्जितः खलु is indeed great.
explanation: O dear friend of my elder brother, your desire to extend hospitality to this large army all alone is indeed noble.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा तु महातेजा गुहं वचनमुत्तमम्। अब्रवीद्भरत श्श्रीमाननिषादाधिपतिं पुनः।।2.85.3।।
transliteration: ityuktvā tu mahātejā guhaṃ vacanamuttamam| abravīdbharata śśrīmānaniṣādādhipatiṃ punaḥ
translation: महातेजाः of great radiance, श्रीमान् the majestic one, भरतः Bharata, गुहम् to Guha, उत्तमम् courteous, वचनम् word, उक्त्वा तु having said, पुनः again, निषादाधिपतिम्  addressing king of the nishadas, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Having spoken to Guha courteously, the majestic, radiant Bharata continued:

shloka_text: कतरेण गमिष्यामि भरद्वाजाश्रमं गुह। गहनोऽयं भृशं देशो गङ्गाऽनूपो दुरत्ययः।।2.85.4।।
transliteration: katareṇa gamiṣyāmi bharadvājāśramaṃ guha| gahano'yaṃ bhṛśaṃ deśo gaṅgā'nūpo duratyayaḥ
translation: गुह Guha, कतरेण by which path, भरद्वाजाश्रमम् to the hermitage of Bharadwaja, गमिष्यामि can I go, गङ्गनूपः marshy banks of Ganga, अयम् this, देशः region, भृशम् highly, गहनः is dense, दुरत्ययः very difficult to traverse.
explanation: O Guha this region of Ganga with its dense forest is very difficult to cross. How can I reach the hermitage of Bharadwaja?

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजपुत्रस्य धीमतः। अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं गुहो गहनगोचरः।।2.85.5।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rājaputrasya dhīmataḥ| abravītprāñjalirvākyaṃ guho gahanagocaraḥ
translation: धीमतः of the sagacious, तस्य राजपुत्रस्य of that king's son, तत् वचनम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, गहनगोचरः one who ranges in the dense forest, गुहः Guha, प्राञ्जलिः with folded palms (in reverence), वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: When he heard those words of the sagacious Bharata, Guha the forest ranger answered him reverentially with folded palms.

shloka_text: दाशास्त्वाऽनुऽगमिष्यन्ति धन्विनस्सुसमाहिताः। अहं त्वानुगमिष्यामि राजपुत्र महायशः।।2.85.6।।
transliteration: dāśāstvā'nu'gamiṣyanti dhanvinassusamāhitāḥ| ahaṃ tvānugamiṣyāmi rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
translation: महायशः a man of great renown, राजपुत्रः king's son, धन्विनः armed with bows, दाशाः fishermen, सुसमाहिताः wellprepared, त्वा you, अनुगमिष्यन्ति shall follow, अहम् I, त्वा you, अनुगमिष्यामि shall follow.
explanation: O prince of great renown I shall follow you, wellprepared with these fishermen, armed with bows.

shloka_text: कच्छिन्नदुष्टो व्रजसि रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। इयं ते महती सेना शङ्कां जनयतीव मे।।2.85.7।।
transliteration: kacchinnaduṣṭo vrajasi rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ| iyaṃ te mahatī senā śaṅkāṃ janayatīva me
translation: अक्लिष्टकर्मणः of unwearied actions, रामस्य towards Rama, दुष्टः bearing illwill, न व्रजसि कच्छित् are you not going to that place?, महती large, ते your, इयं सेना this army, मे to me, शङ्काम् doubt, जनयतीव as though arouses.
explanation: Are you not going to that place with the evil intention of causing harm to Rama of unwearied actions? This large army of yours arouses doubts in me.

shloka_text: तमेवमभिभाषन्तमाकाश इव निर्मलः। भरतश्श्लक्ष्णया वाचा गुहं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.85.8।।
transliteration: tamevamabhibhāṣantamākāśa iva nirmalaḥ| bharataśślakṣṇayā vācā guhaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: आकाशः इव like the sky, निर्मलः tranquil, भरतः Bharata, एवम् thus, अभिभाषन्तम् talking, तं गुहम् addressing Guha, श्लक्ष्णया in gentle, वाचा voice, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: When he heard Guha thus speaking, Bharata who was as tranquil as the sky, said to him in a gentle voice.

shloka_text: माभूत्स कालो यत्कष्टं न मां शङ्कितुमर्हसि। राघव स्सहि मे भ्राता ज्येष्ठः पितुसमो मतः।।2.85.9।।
transliteration: mābhūtsa kālo yatkaṣṭaṃ na māṃ śaṅkitumarhasi| rāghava ssahi me bhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ pitusamo mataḥ
translation: यत् which, कष्टम् calamity, सः कालः that time, मा भूत् shall not come, माम् to me, शङ्कितुम् to suspect, नार्हसि you should not, मे my, ज्येष्ठः eldest, भ्राता brother, सः राघवः that Rama, पितृसमः is equal to my father, मतः हि he has been held in high esteem.
explanation: That calmitous time will never come (again). You should not suspect me. I look upon Rama, my eldest brother, as my father.

shloka_text: तं निवर्तयितुं यामि काकुत्स्थं वनवासिनम्। बुद्धिरन्या न ते कार्या गुह सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते।।2.85.10।।
transliteration: taṃ nivartayituṃ yāmi kākutsthaṃ vanavāsinam| buddhiranyā na te kāryā guha satyaṃ bravīmi te
translation: वनवासिनम् residing in the forest, तम् काकुत्स्थम् to that scion of the Kakutsthas, निवर्तयितुम् to bring back, यामि I am going, गुह O Guha, ते to you, अन्या other, बुद्धि: thought, न कार्या not to be entertained, ते to you, सत्यम् truth, ब्रवीमि I am telling.
explanation: I am going to bring back that scion of the kakutsthas (Rama) who resides in the forest. O Guha, do not entertain any other thought. I am tellng you the truth.

shloka_text: स तु संहृष्टवदन श्श्रुत्वा भरतभाषितम्। पुनरेवाब्रवीद्वाक्यं भरतं प्रति हर्षितः।।2.85.11।।
transliteration: sa tu saṃhṛṣṭavadana śśrutvā bharatabhāṣitam| punarevābravīdvākyaṃ bharataṃ prati harṣitaḥ
translation: भरतभाषितम् Bharata's words, श्रुत्वा on hearing, संहृष्टवदनः one whose is face beaming with joy, सः तु that Guha, हर्षितः delighted, भरतं प्रति looking at Bharata, पुनरेव once  again, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: When he heard those words of Bharata, Guha was delighted and his face beamed with joy as he said to Bharata:

shloka_text: धन्यस्त्वं न त्वया तुल्यं पश्यामि जगतीतले। अयत्नादागतं राज्यं यस्त्वं त्यक्तुमिहेच्छसि।।2.85.12।।
transliteration: dhanyastvaṃ na tvayā tulyaṃ paśyāmi jagatītale| ayatnādāgataṃ rājyaṃ yastvaṃ tyaktumihecchasi
translation: यः त्वम् such a man as you are, इह now, अयत्नात् effortlessly, आगतम् arrived, राज्यम् kingdom, त्यक्तुम् to renounce, इच्छसि wish, त्वम् you, धन्यः are blessed, त्वया your, तुल्यम् equal, जगतीतले on this earth, न पश्यामि I do not see.
explanation: Blessed indeed you are as you desire to renounce the kingdom that has come to you effortlessly. I see none equal to you on this earth.

shloka_text: शाश्वती खलु ते कीर्तिर्लोकाननुचरिष्यति। यस्त्वं कृच्छ्रगतं रामं प्रत्यानयितुमिच्छसि।।2.85.13।।
transliteration: śāśvatī khalu te kīrtirlokānanucariṣyati| yastvaṃ kṛcchragataṃ rāmaṃ pratyānayitumicchasi
translation: यः त्वम् you, कृच्छ्रगतम् who is in great difficulty, रामम् Rama, प्रत्यानयितुम् to bring back, इच्छसि desire, ते your, शाश्वती everlasting, कीर्तिः fame, लोकान् in this world, अनुचरिष्यति will spread.
explanation: You desire to bring back Rama who is in great difficulty. This everlasting fame of yours will spread all over the world.

shloka_text: एवं सम्भाषमाणस्य गुहस्य भरतं तदा। बभौ नष्टप्रभस्सूर्यो रजनी चाभ्यवर्तत।।2.85.14।।
transliteration: evaṃ sambhāṣamāṇasya guhasya bharataṃ tadā| babhau naṣṭaprabhassūryo rajanī cābhyavartata
translation: तदा then, गुहस्य Guha's, एवं thus, भरतं to Bharata, सम्भाषमाणस्य while conversing, सूर्यः sun, नष्टप्रभः diminished light, बभौ shone, रजनी च night, अभ्यवर्तत set in.
explanation: As Guha was thus conversing with Bharata, the rays of the Sun diminished and the night set in.

shloka_text: सन्निवेश्य स तां सेनां गुहेन परितोषितः। शत्रुघ्नेन सह श्रीमाञ्छयनं समुपागमत्।।2.85.15।।
transliteration: sanniveśya sa tāṃ senāṃ guhena paritoṣitaḥ| śatrughnena saha śrīmāñchayanaṃ samupāgamat
translation: श्रीमान् fortunate Bharata, सः he, तां सेनां that army, सन्निवेश्य having encamped, गुहेन with Guha, परितोषितः gratified, शत्रुघ्नेन सह along with Satrughna, शयनं sleep, समुपागमत्  obtained.
explanation: Fortunate Bharata gratified by Guha encamped his army and retired to bed along with Satrughna.

shloka_text: रामचिन्तामय श्शोको भरतस्य महात्मनः। उपस्थितो ह्यनर्हस्य धर्मप्रेक्षस्य तादृशः।।2.85.16।।
transliteration: rāmacintāmaya śśoko bharatasya mahātmanaḥ| upasthito hyanarhasya dharmaprekṣasya tādṛśaḥ
translation: महात्मनः of the magnanimous, धर्मप्रेक्षस्य of a man of righteous outlook, अनर्हस्य of him who  does not deserve (grief), भरतस्य Bharata's, तादृशः such, रामचिन्तामयः filled with the thought of Rama, शोकः grief, उपस्थितः हि had befallen.
explanation: But the thought of Rama caused grief to the magnanimous Bharata, a man of righteous outlook who did not deserve such grief.

shloka_text: अन्तर्दाहेन दहनस्सन्तापयति राघवम्। वनदाहाभिसन्तप्तं गूढोऽग्निरिव पादपम्।।2.85.17।।
transliteration: antardāhena dahanassantāpayati rāghavam| vanadāhābhisantaptaṃ gūḍho'gniriva pādapam
translation: वनदाहाभिसन्तप्तं dried by forest fire, पादपं tree, गूढः hidden, अग्निरिव like a fire, राघवम्  Bharata, दहनः grief, अन्तर्दाहेन burning within himself, सन्तापयति scorching.
explanation: Just like a concealed forestfire scorching the dried up forest, the fire of sorrow kindled in his mind scorched Bharata.

shloka_text: प्रसृतस्सर्वगात्रेभ्यस्स्वेदं शोकाग्निसम्भवम्। यथा सूर्यांशुसन्तप्तो हिमवान् प्रसृतोहिमम्।।2.85.18।।
transliteration: prasṛtassarvagātrebhyassvedaṃ śokāgnisambhavam| yathā sūryāṃśusantapto himavān prasṛtohimam
translation: सूर्यांशुसन्तप्तः heated by the Sun's rays, हिमवान् Himalayas, यथा just as, हिमं ice, प्रसृतः melted, सर्वगात्रेभ्यः from all limbs, शोकाग्निसम्भवम् caused by the fire of grief, स्वेदम् sweat, प्रसृतः poured out.
explanation: Like the ice melted by the heat of the Sun's rays flows down the Himalayas, sweat poured from all parts of his body caused by the fire of grief.

shloka_text: ध्याननिर्धरशैलेन विनिश्श्वसितधातुना। दैन्यपादपसंघेन शोकायासाधिशृङ्गिणा।।2.85.19।। प्रमोहानन्तसत्त्वेन सन्तापौषधिवेणुना। आक्रान्तो दुःखशैलेन महता कैकयीसुतः।।2.85.20।।
transliteration: dhyānanirdharaśailena viniśśvasitadhātunā| dainyapādapasaṃghena śokāyāsādhiśṛṅgiṇā pramohānantasattvena santāpauṣadhiveṇunā| ākrānto duḥkhaśailena mahatā kaikayīsutaḥ
translation: कैकयीसुतः Kaikeyi's son, ध्याननिर्धरशैलेन by the cavityless rocks of that mountain of contemplation, विनिःश्वसितधातुना by the minerals of heaving sighs, दैन्यपादपसंघेन by the multitude of trees in the form of dejection, शोकायासाधिशृङ्गिणा by the peaks of  sorrow fatigue and mental distress, प्रमोहानन्तसत्त्वेन by the countless creatures of stupor, सन्तापौषधिवेणुना by the bamboo tree of sorrow, महता great, दुःखशैलेन by the mountains of grief, आक्रान्तः was invaded.
explanation: Bharata, son of Kaikeyi was stricken by a lofty mountain of grief. The cavityless rocks of that mountain were his contemplation, the minerals were his sighs, the multitude of trees were his desolation, peaks were his fatigue and mental distress, the unlimited number of animals were his stupor, the bamboo tree was his sorrow.

shloka_text: ध्याननिर्धरशैलेन विनिश्श्वसितधातुना। दैन्यपादपसंघेन शोकायासाधिशृङ्गिणा।।2.85.19।। प्रमोहानन्तसत्त्वेन सन्तापौषधिवेणुना। आक्रान्तो दुःखशैलेन महता कैकयीसुतः।।2.85.20।।
transliteration: dhyānanirdharaśailena viniśśvasitadhātunā| dainyapādapasaṃghena śokāyāsādhiśṛṅgiṇā pramohānantasattvena santāpauṣadhiveṇunā| ākrānto duḥkhaśailena mahatā kaikayīsutaḥ
translation: कैकयीसुतः Kaikeyi's son, ध्याननिर्धरशैलेन by the cavityless rocks of that mountain of contemplation, विनिःश्वसितधातुना by the minerals of heaving sighs, दैन्यपादपसंघेन by the multitude of trees in the form of dejection, शोकायासाधिशृङ्गिणा by the peaks of  sorrow fatigue and mental distress, प्रमोहानन्तसत्त्वेन by the countless creatures of stupor, सन्तापौषधिवेणुना by the bamboo tree of sorrow, महता great, दुःखशैलेन by the mountains of grief, आक्रान्तः was invaded.
explanation: Bharata, son of Kaikeyi was stricken by a lofty mountain of grief. The cavityless rocks of that mountain were his contemplation, the minerals were his sighs, the multitude of trees were his desolation, peaks were his fatigue and mental distress, the unlimited number of animals were his stupor, the bamboo tree was his sorrow.

shloka_text: विनिश्श्वसन्वै भृशदुर्मनास्ततः प्रमूढसंज्ञः परमापदं गतः। शमं न लेभे हृदयज्वरार्दितो नरर्षभो यूथहतो यथर्षभः।।2.85.21।।
transliteration: viniśśvasanvai bhṛśadurmanāstataḥ pramūḍhasaṃjñaḥ paramāpadaṃ gataḥ| śamaṃ na lebhe hṛdayajvarārdito nararṣabho yūthahato yatharṣabhaḥ
translation: ततः then, नरर्षभः best among men (Bharata), विनिश्श्वसन् heaving sighs, भृशदुर्मनाः with greatly distraught mind, प्रमूढसंज्ञः with bewildered senses, परमापदं a great calamity, गतः caught, हृदयज्वरार्दितः oppressed by the fever raging his heart, यूथहतः separated from the herd, ऋषभः यथा like a bull, शमं peace of mind, न लेभे  did not get.
explanation: Then best of men, Bharata, with highly distraught mind and heaving sighs, with senses bewildered and oppressed by the fever raging in his heart and caught in a great calamity, like a bull separated from the herd enjoyed no peace of mind.

shloka_text: गुहेन सार्धं भरतस्समागतो महानुभावस्सजनस्समाहितः। सुदुर्मनास्तं भरतं तदा पुनर्गुह स्समाश्वासयदग्रजं प्रति।।2.85.22।।
transliteration: guhena sārdhaṃ bharatassamāgato mahānubhāvassajanassamāhitaḥ| sudurmanāstaṃ bharataṃ tadā punarguha ssamāśvāsayadagrajaṃ prati
translation: महानुभावः magnanimous, सजनः along with his people, भरतः Bharata, समाहितः with a composed mind, गुहेन सार्धं with Guha, समागतः joined, तदा then, सुदुर्मनाः with greatly distraught mind, गुहः Guha, तं भरतम् that Bharata, पुनः again, अग्रजं प्रति about elder brother Rama, आश्वासयत् consoled.
explanation: Bharata, a man of great magnanimity, joined Guha together with his people with composed mind. Then Guha, greatly distraught, again consoled  Bharata  regarding his elder brother Rama. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चाशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightyfifth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: आचचक्षेऽथ सद्भावं लक्ष्मणस्य महात्मनः। भरतायाप्रमेयाय गुहो गहनगोचरः।।2.86.1।।
transliteration: ācacakṣe'tha sadbhāvaṃ lakṣmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ| bharatāyāprameyāya guho gahanagocaraḥ
translation: अथ then, गहनगोचरः forest ranger, गुहः Guha, अप्रमेयाय to a man of immeasurable (virtues), भरताय to Bharata, महात्मनः of the magnanimous, लक्ष्मणस्य Lakshmana's, सद्भावम् good nature, आचचक्षे explained.
explanation: Then Guha, the forest ranger, described to Bharata the countless qualities of the goodnatured, magnanimous Lakshmana:
comments: Guha's reminiseesces.

shloka_text: तं जाग्रतं गुणैर्युक्तं शरचापासिधारिणम्। भ्रातृगुप्त्यर्थमत्यन्तमहं लक्ष्मणमबृवम्।।2.86.2।।
transliteration: taṃ jāgrataṃ guṇairyuktaṃ śaracāpāsidhāriṇam| bhrātṛguptyarthamatyantamahaṃ lakṣmaṇamabṛvam
translation: अहम् I, भ्रातृगुप्त्यर्थम् for the sake of protecting his brother, अत्यन्तम् completely, जाग्रतम् keeping awake, शरचापासिधारिणम् holding arrows, bow and sword, गुणैः with virtues, युक्तम् endowed with, तं लक्ष्मणम् that Lakshmana, अबृवम् I said.
explanation: I spoke to the virtuous Lakshmana, who was holding arrows, bow and sword in his hand and keeping awake completely for the protection of his brother.

shloka_text: इयं तात सुखा शय्या त्वदर्थमुपकल्पिता। प्रत्याश्वसिहि शेष्वास्यां सुखं राघवनन्दन।।2.86.3।।
transliteration: iyaṃ tāta sukhā śayyā tvadarthamupakalpitā| pratyāśvasihi śeṣvāsyāṃ sukhaṃ rāghavanandana
translation: राघवनन्दन delight of the race of Raghu, तात my friend, (लक्ष्मण Lakshmana), सुखा comfortable, इयम् this, शय्या couch, त्वदर्थम् for your sake, उपकल्पिता has been arranged, प्रत्याश्वसिहि be assured, अस्याम् upon it, सुखम् peacefully, शेष्व lie down.
explanation: My friend, Lakshmana, the delight of the Raghavas this comfortable couch has been arranged for you. Lie down peacefully without any anxiety.

shloka_text: उचितोऽयं जनस्सर्वो दुःखानां त्वं सुखोचितः। धर्मात्मंस्तस्य गुप्त्यर्थं जागरिष्यामहे वयम्।।2.86.4।।
transliteration: ucito'yaṃ janassarvo duḥkhānāṃ tvaṃ sukhocitaḥ| dharmātmaṃstasya guptyarthaṃ jāgariṣyāmahe vayam
translation: धर्मात्मन् O righteous one, अयम् this, सर्वः all, जनः people, दुःखानाम् for hardships, उचितः  are accustomed, त्वम् you, सुखोचितः are used to comfort, तस्य for Rama's, गुप्त्यर्थम् for the sake of protection, वयम् we, जागरिष्यामहे will stay awake.
explanation: O righteous one you are used to conforts where as all of our people are accustomed to hardships. So we will stay awake and protect Rama.

shloka_text: नहि रामात्प्रियतरो ममास्ति भुवि कश्चन। मोत्सुकोऽभूर्ब्रवीम्येतदप्यसत्यं तवाग्रतः।।2.86.5।।
transliteration: nahi rāmātpriyataro mamāsti bhuvi kaścana| motsuko'bhūrbravīmyetadapyasatyaṃ tavāgrataḥ
translation: मम for me, भुवि on earth, रामात् more than Rama, प्रियतरः dearer, कश्चन none, नास्ति हि does not exist, अथ and, उत्सुकः anxious, मा भूः do not have, तव your, अग्रतः in presence, एतत् this, सत्यम् truthful, वाक्यम् words, ब्रवीमि I am telling.
explanation: To me, there is none on earth dearer than Rama. Do not have any anxiety. I am telling you the truth.

shloka_text: अस्य प्रसादादाशंसे लोकेऽस्मिन् सुमहद्यशः। धर्मावाप्तिं च विपुलामर्थकामौ च केवलम्।।2.86.6।।
transliteration: asya prasādādāśaṃse loke'smin sumahadyaśaḥ| dharmāvāptiṃ ca vipulāmarthakāmau ca kevalam
translation: अस्य this Rama's, प्रसादात् grace, अस्मिन् in this लोके world, सुमहत् great, यशः renown, विपुलाम् abundance of, धर्मावाप्तिं च advantage of righteousness, केवलम् solely, अर्थकामौ च  artha (prosperity) and kama (pleasure), आशंसे I desire.
explanation: By the grace of Rama, I want to acquire in this world great renown, abundance of righteousness, absolute artha (prosperity) and kama (pleasure).

shloka_text: सोऽहं प्रियसखं रामं शयानं सह सीतया। रक्षिष्यामि धनुष्पाणि स्सर्वै स्स्वैर्ज्ञातिभिस्सह।।2.86.7।।
transliteration: so'haṃ priyasakhaṃ rāmaṃ śayānaṃ saha sītayā| rakṣiṣyāmi dhanuṣpāṇi ssarvai ssvairjñātibhissaha
translation: सः अहं as for me, सर्वैः with all, स्वैः own, ज्ञातिभिः सह with relatives, सीतया सह along with Sita, शयानम् asleep, प्रियसखम् dear friend, रामम् to Rama, धनुष्पाणिः bow in hand, रक्षिष्यामि I will protect.
explanation: As for me, bow in hand and all my kinsmen with me, I shall protect my dear friend Rama who is resting with Sita.

shloka_text: न हि मेऽविदितं किञ्चिद्वनेऽस्मिंश्चरत स्सदा। चतुरङ्गं ह्यपि बलं प्रसहेम वयं युधि।।2.86.8।।
transliteration: na hi me'viditaṃ kiñcidvane'smiṃścarata ssadā| caturaṅgaṃ hyapi balaṃ prasahema vayaṃ yudhi
translation: अस्मिन् वने in this forest, सदा always, चरतः ranging, मे to me, अविदितम् unknown, किञ्चित् nothing, न हि not, वयम् we, युधि in the battle, चतुरङ्गं बलम् अपि four divisions of the army also, प्रसहेम हि will withstand.
explanation: Nothing is unknown to me in this forest in which I range about continually. We can withstand an army of four divisions in a battle.

shloka_text: एवमस्माभिरुक्तेन लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना। अनुनीता वयं सर्वे धर्ममेवानुपश्यता।। 2.86.9।।
transliteration: evamasmābhiruktena lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā| anunītā vayaṃ sarve dharmamevānupaśyatā
translation: एवं thus, अस्माभिः by us, उक्तेन having been uttered, महात्मना by the  magnanimous, धर्ममेव virtuousness alone, अनुपश्यता seeing, लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, वयम् we, सर्वे all, अनुनीताः  have been entreated.
explanation: The magnanimous Lakshmana, established in dharma, replied:

shloka_text: कथं दाशरथौ भूमौ शयाने सह सीतया। शक्या निद्रा मया लब्धुं जीवितं वा सुखानि वा।।2.86.10।।
transliteration: kathaṃ dāśarathau bhūmau śayāne saha sītayā| śakyā nidrā mayā labdhuṃ jīvitaṃ vā sukhāni vā
translation: दाशरथौ Rama, सीतया सह with Sita, भूमौ on the ground, शयाने while sleeping, मया by me,  निद्रा sleep, लब्धुम् to obtain, कथम् how, शक्या is it possible, जीवितं वा either life, सुखानि वा  or comforts.
explanation: While Rama sleep on the ground with Sita, how can I find sleep or joy or comfort?

shloka_text: यो न देवासुरैस्सर्वैश्शक्यः प्रसहितुं युधि। तं पश्य गुह संविष्टं तृणेषु सह सीतया।।2.86.11।।
transliteration: yo na devāsuraissarvaiśśakyaḥ prasahituṃ yudhi| taṃ paśya guha saṃviṣṭaṃ tṛṇeṣu saha sītayā
translation: गुह O Guha, यः that Rama, सर्वैः by all, देवासुरैः by gods and demons, युधि in battle, प्रसहितुं  to withstand, न शक्यः not possible, तम् him, सीतया सह with Sita, तृणेषु on the grass, संविष्टम् lying down, पश्य behold.
explanation: O Guha behold Rama, whom gods and demons combined cannot withstand in a battle now lying on a bed of grass with Sita.

shloka_text: महता तपसा लब्धो विविधैश्च परिश्रमैः। एको दशरथस्यैष पुत्रस्सदृशलक्षणः।।2.86.12।।
transliteration: mahatā tapasā labdho vividhaiśca pariśramaiḥ| eko daśarathasyaiṣa putrassadṛśalakṣaṇaḥ
translation: एषः this Rama, महता by great, तपसा with austerities, विविधैः by various, परिश्रमैश्च with   efforts as well, लब्धः was obtained, दशरथस्य Dasaratha's, एकः one, सदृशलक्षणः one with very similar virtues, पुत्रः is the son.
explanation: Rama is the only one among the sons who resembles his father in various virtues. Dasaratha obtained him after a great deal of austerities and efforts as well.

shloka_text: अस्मिन्प्रव्राजिते राजा न चिरं वर्तयिष्यति। विधवा मेदिनी नूनं क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति।।2.86.13।।
transliteration: asminpravrājite rājā na ciraṃ vartayiṣyati| vidhavā medinī nūnaṃ kṣiprameva bhaviṣyati
translation: अस्मिन् when he, प्रव्राजिते is exiled, राजा king Dasaratha, चिरम् for a long time, न वर्तयिष्यति will not survive, नूनम् surely, मेदिनी earth, क्षिप्रमेव soon, विधवा widow, भविष्यति will become.
explanation: After Rama is exiled, king Dasaratha will not survive for long and surely the earth will soon be widowed.

shloka_text: विनद्य सुमहानादं श्रमेणोपरताः स्त्रियः। निर्घोषो विरतो नूनमध्य राजनिवेशने।।2.86.14।।
transliteration: vinadya sumahānādaṃ śrameṇoparatāḥ striyaḥ| nirghoṣo virato nūnamadhya rājaniveśane
translation: स्त्रियः women, सुमहानादम् loud sounds, विनद्य having cried, श्रमेण with exhaustion, उपरताः  have ceased, अद्य now, राजनिवेशने in the king's palace, निर्घोषः clamour, नूनम् surely, विरतः   has subsided.
explanation: The women of the inner apartment who lamented loudly, must have stopped weeping out of weariness. By now, the clamour in the king's palace would have surely subsided.

shloka_text: कौसल्या चैव राजा च तथैव जननी मम। नाशंसे यदि जीवेयुस्सर्वे ते शर्वरीमिमाम्।।2.86.15।।
transliteration: kausalyā caiva rājā ca tathaiva jananī mama| nāśaṃse yadi jīveyussarve te śarvarīmimām
translation: कौसल्या चैव even Kausalya, राजा च king also, तथैव in the same way, मम जननी my mother, ते सर्वे all of them, इमाम् this, रजनीम् night, यदि जीवेयुः if they are alive, नाशंसे I do not think.
explanation: I doubt whether the king, Kausalya and my mother Sumitra and the rest of them will outlive this night.

shloka_text: जीवेदपि च मे माता शत्रुघ्नस्यान्ववेक्षया। दुःखिता या तु कौसल्या वीरसूर्विनशिष्यति।।2.86.16।।
transliteration: jīvedapi ca me mātā śatrughnasyānvavekṣayā| duḥkhitā yā tu kausalyā vīrasūrvinaśiṣyati
translation: मे माता my mother, शत्रुघ्नस्य Satrughna's, अन्ववेक्षया looking at, जीवेदपि च might be alive, वीरसूः mother of a warrior, या कौसल्या that Kausalya, सा तु as for her, दुःखिता with extreme grief, विनशिष्यति will die.
explanation: My mother might live, looking at Satrughna. But Kausalya, who is the mother of a hero, will die from extreme grief.

shloka_text: अतिक्रान्तमतिक्रान्तमनवाप्य मनोरथम्। राज्ये राममनिक्षिप्य पिता मे विनशिष्यति।।2.86.17।।
transliteration: atikrāntamatikrāntamanavāpya manoratham| rājye rāmamanikṣipya pitā me vinaśiṣyati
translation: मे पिता my father, अतिक्रान्तम् अतिक्रान्तम् gone by one after another, मनोरथम् cherished desire, अनवाप्य without fulfilling, राज्ये in the kingdom, रामम् Rama, अनिक्षिप्य without placing, विनशिष्यति will pass away.
explanation: My father, king Dasaratha, failing to fulfil his cherished desires one after another and unable to place Rama on the throne, will pass away.

shloka_text: सिद्धार्थाः पितरं वृत्तं तस्मिन्काले ह्युपस्थिते। प्रेतकार्येषु सर्वेषु संस्करिष्यन्ति भूमिपम्।।2.86.18।।
transliteration: siddhārthāḥ pitaraṃ vṛttaṃ tasminkāle hyupasthite| pretakāryeṣu sarveṣu saṃskariṣyanti bhūmipam
translation: तस्मिन्काले when that moment, उपस्थिते had arrived, वृत्तम् being in that state, पितरम् my father, भूमिपम् for the lord of the earth, सर्वेषु all, प्रेतकार्येषु in funeral rites, संस्करिष्यन्ति will perform, सिद्धार्थाः men who attained their purpose.
explanation: When the moment of death arrives for my father, those who perform the funeral rites for him would have fulfilled their desire.

shloka_text: रम्यचत्वरसंस्थानां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्। हर्म्यप्रासादम्पन्नां सर्वरत्नविभूषिताम्।।2.86.19।। गजाश्वरथसंबाधां तूर्यनादविनादिताम्। सर्वकल्याणसंपूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलाम्।।2.86.20।। आरामोद्यानसंपूर्णां समाजोत्सवशालिनीम्। सुखिता विचरिष्यन्ति राजधानीं पितुर्मम।।2.86.21।।
transliteration: ramyacatvarasaṃsthānāṃ suvibhaktamahāpathām| harmyaprāsādampannāṃ sarvaratnavibhūṣitām gajāśvarathasaṃbādhāṃ tūryanādavināditām| sarvakalyāṇasaṃpūrṇāṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākulām ārāmodyānasaṃpūrṇāṃ samājotsavaśālinīm| sukhitā vicariṣyanti rājadhānīṃ piturmama
translation: रम्यचत्वरसस्थानाम् with lovely crossroads and squares, सुविभक्तमहापथाम् welllaid  highways, हर्म्यप्रासादसंपन्नाम् full of mansions and palaces, सर्वरत्नविभूषिताम् encrusted with every kind of precious stone, गजाश्वरथसंबाधाम् full of elephants, horses and chariots, तूर्यनादविनादिताम् resounding with trumpets, सर्वकल्याणसंपूर्णाम् with universal wellbeing, हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलाम् crowded with healthy people, आरामोद्यानसंपूर्णाम् with plenty of pleasuregardens and parks, समाजोत्सवशालिनीम् shining with community festivities, मम पितुः my father's, राजधानीम् capital (Ayodhya), सुखिताः with all comforts, विचरिष्यन्ति will move  about.
explanation: There in the capital of my father with its lovely crossroads and squares, welllaid  highways, full of mansions and palaces encrusted with all kinds of precious stones, teeming with elephants, horses and chariots, resounding with trumpets, and with wellbeing everywhere, and plenty of pleasuregardens, and parks and community festivals, people sound in health would be moving about in great comfort.

shloka_text: अपिसत्यप्रतिज्ञेन सार्धं कुशलिना वयं। निवृत्ते समये ह्यस्मिन् सुखिताः प्रविशेमहि।।2.86.22।।
transliteration: apisatyapratijñena sārdhaṃ kuśalinā vayaṃ| nivṛtte samaye hyasmin sukhitāḥ praviśemahi
translation: वयं we, आस्मिन् in this, समये the time, निवृत्ते returning, सत्यप्रतिज्ञेन who fulfilled his vow, कुशलिना सार्धं along with him in safe condition, सुखिताः with happiness, अपि प्रविशेमहि will we enter Ayodhya?
explanation: Can we ever reenter Ayodhya happily after safely fulfilling the vow and completing the term of exile?

shloka_text: परिदेवयमानस्य तस्यैवं सुमहात्मनः। तिष्ठतो राजपुत्रस्य शर्वरी साऽत्यवर्तत।।2.86.23।।
transliteration: paridevayamānasya tasyaivaṃ sumahātmanaḥ| tiṣṭhato rājaputrasya śarvarī sā'tyavartata
translation: सुमहात्मनः of the highminded, एवं in this way, परिदेवयमानस्य lamenting so, तस्य राजपुत्रस्य that prince, तिष्ठतः while waiting, सा शर्वरी that night, अत्यवर्तत elapsed.
explanation: While the highminded prince was lamenting this way and was waiting, the night passed off.

shloka_text: प्रभाते विमले सूर्ये कारयित्वा जटा उभौ। अस्मिन् भागीरथीतीरे सुखं सन्तारितौ मया।।2.86.24।।
transliteration: prabhāte vimale sūrye kārayitvā jaṭā ubhau| asmin bhāgīrathītīre sukhaṃ santāritau mayā
translation: विमले when bright, सूर्ये Sun, प्रभाते at dawn, उभौ both, आस्मिन् in this, भागीरथीतीरे on the bank of Bhagirathi, जटाः matting their hair, कारयित्वा made, मया by me, सुखम् comfortably, सन्तारितौ were ferried.
explanation: The next morning when the Sun shone bright, both of them matted their hair on the bank of the river Bhagirathi (Ganga) and I ferried them across comfortably.

shloka_text: जटाधरौ तौ द्रुमचीरवाससौ महाबलौ कुञ्जरयूथपोपमौ। वरेषुचापासिधरौ परन्तपौ व्यपेक्षमाणौ सह सीतया गतौ।।2.86.25।।
transliteration: jaṭādharau tau drumacīravāsasau mahābalau kuñjarayūthapopamau| vareṣucāpāsidharau parantapau vyapekṣamāṇau saha sītayā gatau
translation: जटाधरौ wearing matted hair, द्रुमचीरवाससौ those two dressed in bark robes, महाबलौ of great strength, कुञ्जरयूथपोपमौ comparable to elephants, वरेषुचापासिधरौ armed with excellent bows, arrows and swords, तौ both, परन्तपौ slayers of enemies, व्यपेक्षमाणौ looking back alertly, सीतया सह along with Sita, गतौ went.
explanation: Rama and Lakshmana, slayers of enemies, who are as strong as bull elephants, with their hair matted, wearing robes made of bark, armed with excellent bows, arrows and swords went along with Sita looking around (vigilantly). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षडशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightysixth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: गुहस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरतो भृशमप्रियम्। ध्यानं जगाम तत्रैव यत्र तच्छ्रुतमप्रियम्।।2.87.1।।
transliteration: guhasya vacanaṃ śrutvā bharato bhṛśamapriyam| dhyānaṃ jagāma tatraiva yatra tacchrutamapriyam
translation: भरतः Bharata, भृशम् highly, अप्रियम् unpleasant, गुहस्य from Guha, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, तत् अप्रियम् that unpleasant, यत्र wherever, श्रुतम् was heard, तत्रैव there only, ध्यानम्  thought, जगाम obtained.
explanation: Extremely unhappy over what he heard from Guha, Bharata was immersed in thought then and there.
comments: Bharata enquires about Rama, Sita and Lakshmana -- Guha narrates to Kausalya how Rama, Sita and Lakshmana spent their time, matted their hair and slept on grass.

shloka_text: सुकुमारो महासत्त्वस्सिंहस्कन्धो महाभुजः। पुण्डरीकविशालाक्ष स्तरुणः प्रियदर्शनः।।2.87.2।। प्रत्याश्वस्य मुहूर्तं तु कालं परमदुर्मनाः। पपात सहसा तोत्रैर्ह्यतिविद्ध इव द्विपः।।2.87.3।।
transliteration: sukumāro mahāsattvassiṃhaskandho mahābhujaḥ| puṇḍarīkaviśālākṣa staruṇaḥ priyadarśanaḥ pratyāśvasya muhūrtaṃ tu kālaṃ paramadurmanāḥ| papāta sahasā totrairhyatividdha iva dvipaḥ
translation: सुकुमारः delicate, महासत्त्वः highly energetic, सिंहस्कन्धः with shoulders like that of a lion, महाभुजः mightyarmed, पुण्डरीकविशालाक्षः wideeyed like lotus petals, तरुणः youthful, प्रियदर्शनः of graceful appearance, मुहूर्तं कालं तु for a moment, प्रत्याश्वस्य having revived, परमदुर्मनाः with deeply distressed mind, तोत्रैः by whips, अतिविद्धः smitten, द्विपः इव like an elephant, सहसा at once, पपात fell down.
explanation: The delicate, youthful, highly energetic and mightyarmed Bharata of graceful appearance, with shoulders like that of a lion and wideeyed like lotus petals, recovered for a moment and with a mind deeply distressed fell down at once like an elephant smitten by a goad.

shloka_text: सुकुमारो महासत्त्वस्सिंहस्कन्धो महाभुजः। पुण्डरीकविशालाक्ष स्तरुणः प्रियदर्शनः।।2.87.2।। प्रत्याश्वस्य मुहूर्तं तु कालं परमदुर्मनाः। पपात सहसा तोत्रैर्ह्यतिविद्ध इव द्विपः।।2.87.3।।
transliteration: sukumāro mahāsattvassiṃhaskandho mahābhujaḥ| puṇḍarīkaviśālākṣa staruṇaḥ priyadarśanaḥ pratyāśvasya muhūrtaṃ tu kālaṃ paramadurmanāḥ| papāta sahasā totrairhyatividdha iva dvipaḥ
translation: सुकुमारः delicate, महासत्त्वः highly energetic, सिंहस्कन्धः with shoulders like that of a lion, महाभुजः mightyarmed, पुण्डरीकविशालाक्षः wideeyed like lotus petals, तरुणः youthful, प्रियदर्शनः of graceful appearance, मुहूर्तं कालं तु for a moment, प्रत्याश्वस्य having revived, परमदुर्मनाः with deeply distressed mind, तोत्रैः by whips, अतिविद्धः smitten, द्विपः इव like an elephant, सहसा at once, पपात fell down.
explanation: The delicate, youthful, highly energetic and mightyarmed Bharata of graceful appearance, with shoulders like that of a lion and wideeyed like lotus petals, recovered for a moment and with a mind deeply distressed fell down at once like an elephant smitten by a goad.

shloka_text: तदवस्थं तु भरतं शत्रुघ्नोऽनन्तरस्थितः। परिष्वज्य रुरोदोच्चैर्विसंज्ञश्शोककर्शितः।।2.87.4।।
transliteration: tadavasthaṃ tu bharataṃ śatrughno'nantarasthitaḥ| pariṣvajya rurodoccairvisaṃjñaśśokakarśitaḥ
translation: अनन्तरस्थितः standing close by, शत्रुघ्नः Satrughna, तदवस्थम् in this state, भरतम् Bharata, परिष्यज्य having embraced, शोककर्शितः smitten with grief, विसंज्ञः having lost his senses,  उच्चैः loudly, रुरोद cried.
explanation: Seeing Bharata in that state, Satrughna who was standing close by, smitten with grief clasped him, cried loudly and fell senseless.

shloka_text: ततस्सर्वास्समापेतुर्मातरो भरतस्य ताः। उपवासकृशा दीना भर्तृव्यसनकर्शिताः।।2.87.5।।
transliteration: tatassarvāssamāpeturmātaro bharatasya tāḥ| upavāsakṛśā dīnā bhartṛvyasanakarśitāḥ
translation: ततः thereafter, उपवासकृशाः emaciated due to fasting, दीनाः desolate, भर्तृव्यसनकर्शिताः afflicted by the calamity of their husband's death, सर्वाः all, भरतस्य Bharata's, ताः मातरः  mothers, समापेतुः rushed towards him.
explanation: Then Bharata's mothers, who were emaciated due to fasting and afflicted by the calamity of the death of their husband were desolate, rushed towards him.

shloka_text: ताश्च तं पतितं भूमौ रुदन्त्यः पर्यवारयन्। कौसल्या त्वनुसृत्यैनं दुर्मनाः परिषस्वजे।।2.87.6।।
transliteration: tāśca taṃ patitaṃ bhūmau rudantyaḥ paryavārayan| kausalyā tvanusṛtyainaṃ durmanāḥ pariṣasvaje
translation: ताश्च all of them, रुदन्त्य: sobbing, भूमौ on the ground, पतितम् fallen, तम् him, पर्यवारयन् surrounded, कौसल्या तु as for Kausalya, दुर्मनाः in a depressed mind, अनुसृत्य approaching, एनम् that Bharata, परिषस्वजे took him into her arms.
explanation: Sobbing, they gathered around Bharata who had fallen on the ground, while Kausalya approached him in a depressed state and took him into her arms.

shloka_text: वत्सला स्वं यथा वत्समुपगूह्य तपस्विनी। परिपप्रच्छ भरतं रुदन्ती शोकलालसा।।2.87.7।।
transliteration: vatsalā svaṃ yathā vatsamupagūhya tapasvinī| paripapraccha bharataṃ rudantī śokalālasā
translation: शोकलालसा distressed in grief, तपस्विनी desolate, वत्सला with filial love, रुदन्ती weeping, स्वम् her own, वत्सं यथा like child, उपगूह्य clasping, भरतम् Bharata, परिपप्रच्छ enquired.
explanation: Desolate Kausalya, in deep distress, clasped Bharata out of filial love as if he were her own child, wept and enquired of him:

shloka_text: पुत्र व्याधिर्न ते कच्चिच्छरीरं परिबाधते। अद्य राजकुलस्यास्य त्वदधीनं हि जीवितम्।।2.87.8।।
transliteration: putra vyādhirna te kacciccharīraṃ paribādhate| adya rājakulasyāsya tvadadhīnaṃ hi jīvitam
translation: पुत्र O son, व्याधिः illness, ते शरीरम् your body, कच्चित् न परिबाधते is not troubling, I hope, अद्य now, अस्य राजकुलस्य of this royal house, जीवितम् life, त्वदधीनं हि is dependent on you.
explanation: O son I hope you are not affected by illness. Now the existence of this royal house devolves on you.

shloka_text: त्वां दृष्ट्वा पुत्र जीवामि रामे सभ्रातृकेगते। वृत्ते दशरथे राज्ञि नाथ एकस्त्वमद्य नः।।2.87.9।।
transliteration: tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā putra jīvāmi rāme sabhrātṛkegate| vṛtte daśarathe rājñi nātha ekastvamadya naḥ
translation: पुत्र O son, सभ्रातृके along with your brother, Lakshmana, रामे Rama, गते having  gone, राज्ञि king, दशरथे Dasaratha, वृत्ते had departed, त्वाम् you, दृष्ट्वा seeing, जीवामि I am living, अद्य now, त्वम् you, एकः alone, नः for us, नाथः are protector.
explanation: O my son, with Rama gone to the forest along with your brother Lakshmana and with king Dasaratha departed from this world, I continue to live seeing you. From now on you alone are our sole protector.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्न लक्ष्मणे पुत्र श्रुतं ते किंचदप्रियम्। पुत्रे वाऽप्येकपुत्राया स्सहभार्ये वनं गते।।2.87.10।।
transliteration: kaccinna lakṣmaṇe putra śrutaṃ te kiṃcadapriyam| putre vā'pyekaputrāyā ssahabhārye vanaṃ gate
translation: पुत्र O son, लक्ष्मणे relating to Lakshmana, सहभार्ये with his wife, वनम् to the forest, गते had gone, एकपुत्रायाः of me having only one son, पुत्रे वा or relating to Rama, किंचित् even  little, अप्रियम् unpleasant news, ते to you, कच्चित् न श्रुतम् is not heard, I hope not.
explanation: O my son, I hope you have not heard any unpleasant news about Lakshmana or about my only son Rama who has gone to the forest along with his wife.

shloka_text: स मुहूर्तं समाश्वस्य रुदन्नेव महायशाः। कौसल्यां परिसान्त्वेद्यं गुहं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.87.11।।
transliteration: sa muhūrtaṃ samāśvasya rudanneva mahāyaśāḥ| kausalyāṃ parisāntvedyaṃ guhaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: महायशाः of great renown, सः that Bharata, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, समाश्वस्य composing himself, कौसल्याम् Kausalya, परिसान्त्वेद्यं reassuring, रुदन्नेव still weeping, गुहम् to Guha, वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Highly renowned Bharata, composing himself for a moment and still weeping, reassured Kauslaya, and then said this to Guha:

shloka_text: भ्राता मे क्वावसद्रात्रौ क्व सीता क्व च लक्ष्मणः। अस्वपच्छयने कस्मिन् किं भुक्त्वा गुह शंस मे।।2.87.12।।
transliteration: bhrātā me kvāvasadrātrau kva sītā kva ca lakṣmaṇaḥ| asvapacchayane kasmin kiṃ bhuktvā guha śaṃsa me
translation: गुह O Guha, मे भ्राता my brother, रात्रौ in the night, क्व where, अवसत् did he dwell, सीता Sita, क्व where did she stay, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, क्व where did he stay, किम् what, भुक्त्वा  having eaten, कस्मिन् in which, शयने couch, अस्वपत् did he sleep, मे to me, शंस tell me.
explanation: O Guha where did my brother Rama, Sita and Lakshmana spend that night? What did they eat? On what couch did they sleep? Tell me all that.

shloka_text: सोऽब्रवीद्भरतं हृष्टो निषादाधिपतिर्गुहः। यद्विधं प्रतिपेदे च रामे प्रियहितेऽतिथौ।।2.87.13।।
transliteration: so'bravīdbharataṃ hṛṣṭo niṣādādhipatirguhaḥ| yadvidhaṃ pratipede ca rāme priyahite'tithau
translation: निषादाधिपतिः overlord of the nishadas, सः गुहः that Guha, हृष्टः delighted, प्रियहिते beloved friend, अतिथौ guest, रामे relating to Rama, यद्विधम् in whatever way, प्रतिपेदे all that he had  provided, भरतम् to Bharata, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Thereupon delighted Guha, overlord of the nishadas, told Bharata all that he had provided to Rama, his beloved friend and guest:

shloka_text: अन्नमुच्चावचं भक्षाः फलानि विविधानि च। रामायाभ्यवहारार्थं बहुचोपहृतं मया।।2.87.14।।
transliteration: annamuccāvacaṃ bhakṣāḥ phalāni vividhāni ca| rāmāyābhyavahārārthaṃ bahucopahṛtaṃ mayā
translation: मया by me, रामाय to Rama, अभ्यवहारार्थम् for the purpose of meal, उच्चावचम् of various kinds, अन्नम् rice, भक्षाः eatables, विविधानि of several kinds, फलानि च fruits also, बहु in great quantity, उपहृतम् was brought.
explanation: I offered Rama rice including a variety of eatables like fruits in great quantity for his food.

shloka_text: तत्सर्वं प्रत्यनुज्ञासीद्राम स्सत्यपराक्रमः। न तु तत्प्रत्यगृह्णात्स क्षत्रधर्ममनुस्मरन्।।2.87.15।।
transliteration: tatsarvaṃ pratyanujñāsīdrāma ssatyaparākramaḥ| na tu tatpratyagṛhṇātsa kṣatradharmamanusmaran
translation: सत्यपराक्रमः a man with truth as prowess, रामः Rama, तत्सर्वम् all that, प्रत्यनुज्ञासीत् acknowledged ordered, सः he, क्षत्रधर्मम् the duty of a kshatriya, अनुस्मरन् remembering, तत् all that, न तु प्रत्यगृह्णात् did not accept it.
explanation: Rama whose prowess is his truth, acknowledged all that but remembering the duty enjoined on a kshatriya did not accept them.

shloka_text: न ह्यस्माभिः प्रतिग्राह्यं सखे देयं तु सर्वदा। इति तेन वयं राजन्ननुनीता महात्मना।।2.87.16।।
transliteration: na hyasmābhiḥ pratigrāhyaṃ sakhe deyaṃ tu sarvadā| iti tena vayaṃ rājannanunītā mahātmanā
translation: राजन् O king, सखे O friend, आस्माभिः by us, न प्रतिग्राह्यम् should not be received, सर्वदा always, देयम् should be given, इति thus, महात्मना by the great, तेन by him, वयम् we, अनुनीताः were entreated.
explanation: O king that great Rama entreated us in a friendly manner by saying 'O friend we should always give to others but should never accept anything from others'.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेन समानीतं पीत्वा वारि महायशाः। औपवास्यं तदाऽकार्षीद्राघवस्सह सीतया।।2.87.17।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇena samānītaṃ pītvā vāri mahāyaśāḥ| aupavāsyaṃ tadā'kārṣīdrāghavassaha sītayā
translation: महायशाः the illustrious one, राघवः Rama, तदा then, लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, समानीतम् brought by, वारि water, सीतया सह with Sita, पीत्वा after drinking, औपवास्यम् fasting, अकार्षीत्  undertook.
explanation: Illustrious Rama along with Sita only drank the water brought by Lakshamana and  undertook fasting.

shloka_text: ततस्तु जलशेषेण लक्ष्मणोऽप्यकरोत्तदा। वाग्यतास्ते त्रय स्सन्ध्यां समुपासत संहिताः।।2.87.18।।
transliteration: tatastu jalaśeṣeṇa lakṣmaṇo'pyakarottadā| vāgyatāste traya ssandhyāṃ samupāsata saṃhitāḥ
translation: ततः तु thereafter, तदा then, लक्ष्मणोऽपि Lakshmana also, जलशेषेण with the remainder of the water, अकरोत् satisfied his hunger, ते त्रयः those three, वाग्यताः observing silence, संहिताः intently, सन्ध्याम् evening worship, समुपासत performed.
explanation: Thereafter Lakshmana also drank the remainder of water. Then all the three observing silence intently performed the evening worship.

shloka_text: सौमित्रिस्तु ततः पश्चादकरोत्स्वास्तरं शुभम्। स्वयमानीय बर्हींषि क्षिप्रं राघवकारणात्।।2.87.19।।
transliteration: saumitristu tataḥ paścādakarotsvāstaraṃ śubham| svayamānīya barhīṃṣi kṣipraṃ rāghavakāraṇāt
translation: ततः पश्चात् thereafter, सौमित्रिस्तु son of Sumitra on his part, स्वयम् himself, बर्हींषि darbha grass, आनीय having brought, राघवकारणात् for the sake of Rama, क्षिप्रम् quickly, शुभम् auspicious, स्वास्तरम् comfortable bed, अकरोत् prepared.
explanation: Therafter, the son of Sumitra (Lakshmana) himself fetched darbha grass and quickly prepared an auspicious and comfortable bed for Rama.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्समाविशद्राम स्स्वास्तरे सह सीतया। प्रक्षाल्य च तयोः पादावपचक्राम लक्ष्मणः।।2.87.20।।
transliteration: tasminsamāviśadrāma ssvāstare saha sītayā| prakṣālya ca tayoḥ pādāvapacakrāma lakṣmaṇaḥ
translation: रामः Rama, तस्मिन् on that, स्वास्तरे bed, सीतया सह with Sita, समाविशत् lay down, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana,  तयोः their, पादौ feet, प्रक्षाल्य having washed, अपचक्राम left for a distant place.
explanation: Rama lay down upon the bed along with Sita. Thereafter Lakshmana, having washed their feet, moved to a distant place.

shloka_text: एतत्तदिङ्गुदीमूलमिदमेव च तत्तृणम्। यस्मिन्रामश्च सीता च रात्रिं तां शयितावुभौ।।2.87.21।।
transliteration: etattadiṅgudīmūlamidameva ca tattṛṇam| yasminrāmaśca sītā ca rātriṃ tāṃ śayitāvubhau
translation: रामश्च Rama as well as, सीता Sita, उभौ both, तां रात्रिम् that night, यस्मिन् where, शयितौ slept, तत् that, इंगुदीमूलम् foot of the ingudi tree, एतत् this only, तत् that, तृणं च grass bed, इदमेव this one only.
explanation: Here at the foot of the ingudi tree and upon that bed of grass both Rama and Sita rested that night.

shloka_text: नियम्य पृष्ठे तु तलाङ्गुलित्रवान् शरैस्सुपूर्णाविषुधी परन्तपः। महाद्धनु स्सज्यमुपोह्य लक्ष्मणो निशामतिष्ठत्परितोऽस्य केवलम्।।2.87.22।।
transliteration: niyamya pṛṣṭhe tu talāṅgulitravān śaraissupūrṇāviṣudhī parantapaḥ| mahāddhanu ssajyamupohya lakṣmaṇo niśāmatiṣṭhatparito'sya kevalam
translation: परन्तपः scorcher of enemies, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, तलाङ्गुलित्रवान् wearing protective covering for his palms and fingers (made of gohaskin), शरैः arrows, सुपूर्णौ filled with,  इषुधी two quivers, पृष्ठे on his back, नियम्य strapping, सज्यम् furnished with string, महत् great, धनुः bow, उपोह्य holding, निशाम् during that night, अस्य Rama's, परितः  surrounding, अतिष्ठत् केवलम् stood throughout.
explanation: Lakshmana, the scorcher of enemies, wearing protective covering for his palms and fingers (made of gohaskin), strapping on his back two quivers filled with arrows, holding a great bow, strung ready, stood sentinel throughout the night guarding the surrounding.

shloka_text: तत स्त्वहंचोत्तमबाणचापधृत् स्थितोऽभवं तत्र स यत्र लक्ष्मणः। अतन्द्रितैर्ज्ञातिभिरात्तकार्मुकैर्महेन्द्रकल्पं परिपालयंस्तदा।।2.87.23।।
transliteration: tata stvahaṃcottamabāṇacāpadhṛt sthito'bhavaṃ tatra sa yatra lakṣmaṇaḥ| atandritairjñātibhirāttakārmukairmahendrakalpaṃ paripālayaṃstadā
translation: ततः thereafter, अहं तु as for me, तदा then, उत्तमबाणचापधृत् holding the best of arrows and bow, अतन्द्रितैः with the indefatigable, आत्तकार्मुकैः armed with bows, ज्ञातिभिः with my kinsmen, महेन्द्रकल्पम् comparable to Indra, परिपालयन् while protecting, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, यत्र wherever, तत्र there, स्थितः अभवम् remained standing.
explanation: Then, holding the best of arrows and bow along with my indefatigable kinsmen similarly armed with bows, I stood by the side of Lakshmana guarding Rama who is comparable to Indra. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्ताशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightyseventh sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा निपुणं सर्वं भरत स्सह मन्त्रिभिः। इङ्गुदीमूलमागम्य रामशय्यामवेक्ष्य ताम्।।2.88.1।। अब्रवीज्जननी स्सर्वा इह तेन महात्मना। शर्वरी शयिता भूमाविदमस्य विमर्दितम्।।2.88.2।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā nipuṇaṃ sarvaṃ bharata ssaha mantribhiḥ| iṅgudīmūlamāgamya rāmaśayyāmavekṣya tām abravījjananī ssarvā iha tena mahātmanā| śarvarī śayitā bhūmāvidamasya vimarditam
translation: भरतः Bharata, तत् सर्वम् all that, निपुणम् attentively, श्रुत्वा having listened, मन्त्रिभिस्सह along with ministers, इङ्गुदीमूलम् to the foot of the ingudi tree, आगम्य having reached, ताम्  रामशय्याम् that Rama's bed, अवेक्ष gazing, सर्वाः all, जननीः mothers, अब्रवीत् said, तेन महात्मना by that magnanimous, Rama, इह here, भूमौ on the ground, शर्वरी night, शयिता has been slept, अस्य his, विमर्दितम् crushed bed, इदम् this one.
explanation: After listening to all that Guha had said, Bharatha reached the foot of the ingudi tree accompanied by his ministers and gazing at Rama's bed, said to all his mothers the magnanimous Rama rested that night here on this ground in that crushed bed.
comments: Guha relates to Bharata about Rama's life in the forest contrary to the life in Ayodhya.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा निपुणं सर्वं भरत स्सह मन्त्रिभिः। इङ्गुदीमूलमागम्य रामशय्यामवेक्ष्य ताम्।।2.88.1।। अब्रवीज्जननी स्सर्वा इह तेन महात्मना। शर्वरी शयिता भूमाविदमस्य विमर्दितम्।।2.88.2।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā nipuṇaṃ sarvaṃ bharata ssaha mantribhiḥ| iṅgudīmūlamāgamya rāmaśayyāmavekṣya tām abravījjananī ssarvā iha tena mahātmanā| śarvarī śayitā bhūmāvidamasya vimarditam
translation: भरतः Bharata, तत् सर्वम् all that, निपुणम् attentively, श्रुत्वा having listened, मन्त्रिभिस्सह along with ministers, इङ्गुदीमूलम् to the foot of the ingudi tree, आगम्य having reached, ताम्  रामशय्याम् that Rama's bed, अवेक्ष gazing, सर्वाः all, जननीः mothers, अब्रवीत् said, तेन महात्मना by that magnanimous, Rama, इह here, भूमौ on the ground, शर्वरी night, शयिता has been slept, अस्य his, विमर्दितम् crushed bed, इदम् this one.
explanation: After listening to all that Guha had said, Bharatha reached the foot of the ingudi tree accompanied by his ministers and gazing at Rama's bed, said to all his mothers the magnanimous Rama rested that night here on this ground in that crushed bed.

shloka_text: महाभागकुलीनेन महाभागेन धीमता। जातो दशरथेनोर्व्यां न रामस्स्वप्तु मर्हति।।2.88.3।।
transliteration: mahābhāgakulīnena mahābhāgena dhīmatā| jāto daśarathenorvyāṃ na rāmassvaptu marhati
translation: महाभागकुलीनेन by the highborn, महाभागेन by a highly fortunate man, धीमता by the sagacious, दशरथेन by Dasaratha, जातः born, रामः Rama, उर्व्याम् on the naked earth, स्वप्तुम् to sleep, न अर्हति does not deserve.
explanation: Rama, son of highly fortunate and sagacious Dasaratha, born of a noble lineage does not deserve to rest on this naked earth.

shloka_text: अजिनोत्तरसंस्तीर्णे वरास्तरणसंचये। शयित्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रः कथं शेते महीतले।।2.88.4।।
transliteration: ajinottarasaṃstīrṇe varāstaraṇasaṃcaye| śayitvā puruṣavyāghraḥ kathaṃ śete mahītale
translation: पुरुषव्याघ्रः best among men, Rama, अजिनोत्तरसंस्तीर्णे on over spreads of deer skin,          वरास्तरणसंचये on bed made of a pile of excellent spreads, शयित्वा used to sleep, महीतले on the ground, कथम् how, शेते can sleep?
explanation: How could Rama, the best among men used to a bed made of a pile of excellent spreads and overspread with deer skin, sleep on the bare ground?

shloka_text: प्रासादाग्रविमानेषु वलभीषु च सर्वदा। हैमराजतभौमेषु वरास्तरणशालिषु।।2.88.5।। पुष्पसञ्चयचित्रेषु चन्दनागरुगन्धिषु। पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाशेषु शुकसङ्घरूतेषुच।।2.88.6।। प्रासादवरवर्येषु शीतवत्सु सुगन्धिषु। उषित्वामेरुकल्पेषु कृतकाञ्चन भित्तिषु।।2.88.7।। गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषैर्वराभरणनिस्स्वनैः। मृदङ्गवरशब्दैश्च सततं प्रतिबोधितः।।2.88.8।। वन्दिभिर्वन्दितः काले बहुभि स्सूतमागधैः। गाथाभिरनुरूपाभि स्स्तुतिभिश्च परन्तपः।।2.88.9।।
transliteration: prāsādāgravimāneṣu valabhīṣu ca sarvadā| haimarājatabhaumeṣu varāstaraṇaśāliṣu puṣpasañcayacitreṣu candanāgarugandhiṣu| pāṇḍurābhraprakāśeṣu śukasaṅgharūteṣuca prāsādavaravaryeṣu śītavatsu sugandhiṣu| uṣitvāmerukalpeṣu kṛtakāñcana bhittiṣu gītavāditranirghoṣairvarābharaṇanissvanaiḥ| mṛdaṅgavaraśabdaiśca satataṃ pratibodhitaḥ vandibhirvanditaḥ kāle bahubhi ssūtamāgadhaiḥ| gāthābhiranurūpābhi sstutibhiśca parantapaḥ
translation: परन्तपः scorcher of enemies, (सः that Rama), सर्वदा always, प्रासादाग्रविमानेषु वलभीषु च in the attic of the sevenstoreyed mansion, हैमराजतभौमेषु the floors paved with gold and silver, वरास्तरणशालिषु spread with excellent carpets, पुष्पसंचयचित्रेषु decked with bouquets of flowers, चन्दनागरुगन्धिषु perfumed with sandal and agaru, पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाशेषु brightness like white clouds, शुकसङ्घरुतेषु च echoed with cries of flocks of parrots, शीतवत्सु cool, सुगन्धिषु in places fragrant with perfumes, कृतकाञ्चनभित्तिषु surrounded by goldplated walls, मेरुकल्पेषु like mount Meru, प्रासादवरवर्येषु in the best of mansions, उषित्वा having dwelt, गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषैः with the sounds of songs and musical instruments, वराभरणनिस्वनैः with the tinkling of ornaments, मृदङ्गवरशब्दैश्च and with excellent sounds of drums, (तत्र there), प्रतिबोधितः awakened, बहुभिः by many, सूतमागधैः bards and genealogists, वन्दिभिः by the panegyrists  गाथाभिः with ballads, अनुरूपाभिः by worthy, स्तुतिभिश्च by songs of praise, काले at appointed time, वन्दितः saluted in reverence.
explanation: Rama, scorcher of enemies, one who was accostomed to dwell in the attic of sevenstoreyed mansions with floors paved with gold, and silver, spread with excellent carpets, decked with bouquets of flowers and perfumed with sandal and agaru. The peaks of those palaces were bright like towering white clouds and echoed with cries of  parrots. They were cool and fragrant with perfumes. The marvellous palaces made of golden walls are comparable to mount Meru. He used to wake up to the sounds of songs and musical instruments, the tinkling of finest ornaments and the splendid sounds of the drums. Many bards, genealogists and panegyrists singing befitting ballads and extolling his virtues at appropriate time used to salute him in reverence (Bharata lamented).
