shloka_text: अश्रद्धेयमिदं लोके न सत्यं प्रतिभाति मा। मुह्यते खलु मे भाव स्स्वप्नोऽयमिति मे मतिः।।2.88.10।।
transliteration: aśraddheyamidaṃ loke na satyaṃ pratibhāti mā| muhyate khalu me bhāva ssvapno'yamiti me matiḥ
translation: लोके in the world, इदम् this, अश्रद्धेयम् can not be believed, सत्यम् truly, मा to me, न प्रतिभाति does not appear, मे my, भावः thought (mind), मुह्यते खलु is bewildered, अयम् this, स्वप्नः इति like a dream, मे my, मतिः thinking.
explanation: It is unbelievable that such a thing has happened to Rama in this world. It does not seem real to me and looks appears like a dream and my mind is bewildered.

shloka_text: न नूनं दैवतं किंचित्कालेन बलवत्तरम्। यत्र दाशरथी रामो भूमावेव शयीत सः।।2.88.11।।
transliteration: na nūnaṃ daivataṃ kiṃcitkālena balavattaram| yatra dāśarathī rāmo bhūmāveva śayīta saḥ
translation: दैवतम् divine power, कालेन in course of time, किंचित् even a little, बलवत्तरम् more strong, न not, नूनम् surely, यत्र where, सः दाशरथि: that Dasaratha's son, रामः Rama, भूमावेव on the ground itself, शयीत had to sleep.
explanation: Dasaratha's son, Rama had to rest on the ground would admittedly mean that no divine power is mightier than Time (Destiny).

shloka_text: विदेहराजस्य सुता सीता च प्रियदर्शना। दयिता शयिता भूमौ स्नुषा दशरथस्य च।।2.88.12।।
transliteration: videharājasya sutā sītā ca priyadarśanā| dayitā śayitā bhūmau snuṣā daśarathasya ca
translation: विदेहराजस्य king of Videha, सुता daughter, प्रियदर्शना one who causes delight to the beholder, दशरथस्य Dasaratha's, दयिता beloved, स्नुषा च daughterinlaw also, सीता च Sita too, भूमौ on the ground, शयिता rested.
explanation: Sita, daughter of Janaka, king of Videha, and beloved daughterinlaw of Dasaratha who caused delight to the beholder, too had to rest on the bare ground.

shloka_text: इयं शय्या मम भ्रातुरिदं हि परिवर्तितम्। स्थण्डिले कठिने सर्वं गात्रै र्विमृदितं तृणम्।।2.88.13।।
transliteration: iyaṃ śayyā mama bhrāturidaṃ hi parivartitam| sthaṇḍile kaṭhine sarvaṃ gātrai rvimṛditaṃ tṛṇam
translation: इयम् this, मम भ्रातुः my brother's, शय्या couch, इदम् here, परिवर्तितं हि tossed about, कठिने on a hard, स्थण्डिले earth, सर्वम् entire, तृणम् grass, गात्रैः by his limbs, विमृदितम् is crushed.
explanation: This is my brother's couch and it is here where he had tossed about. The grass spread on this hard surface is crushed by his limbs.

shloka_text: मन्ये साभरणा सुप्ता सीताऽस्मिञ्छयनोत्तमे। तत्र तत्र हि दृश्यन्ते सक्ताः कनकबिन्दवः।।2.88.14।।
transliteration: manye sābharaṇā suptā sītā'smiñchayanottame| tatra tatra hi dṛśyante saktāḥ kanakabindavaḥ
translation: सीता Sita, अस्मिन् this, शयनोत्तमे on excellent bed, साभरणा with her jewellery, सुप्ता must have slept, मन्ये I think, तत्र तत्र here and there, सक्ताः stuck to, कनकबिन्दवः particles of gold dust, दृश्यन्ते are seen.
explanation: Some particles of gold dust are seen stuck to this bed here and there. I think Sita might have rested on this excellent bed with all her jewellery.

shloka_text: उत्तरीयमिहाऽसक्तं सुव्यक्तं सीतया तदा। तथा ह्येते प्रकाशन्ते सक्ताः कौशेयतन्तवः।।2.88.15।।
transliteration: uttarīyamihā'saktaṃ suvyaktaṃ sītayā tadā| tathā hyete prakāśante saktāḥ kauśeyatantavaḥ
translation: तदा then, सीतया by Sita, उत्तरीयम् upper garment, इह here, आसक्तम् had been, सुव्यक्तम् is  is well evident, तथाहि as for instance, सक्ताः stuck, एते कौशेयतन्तवः these silken threads, प्रकाशन्ते are shining.
explanation: That the upper garment of Sita might have been caught here is well evident from the shining silken threads stuck.

shloka_text: मन्ये भर्तु स्सुखा शय्या येन बाला तपस्विनी। सुकुमारी सती दुःखं न हि विजानाति मैथिली।।2.88.16।।
transliteration: manye bhartu ssukhā śayyā yena bālā tapasvinī| sukumārī satī duḥkhaṃ na hi vijānāti maithilī
translation: येन for what reason, बाला the young lady, तपस्विनी unfortunate, सुकुमारी delicate lady, सती chaste lady, मैथिली Sita, दुःखम् suffering, न हि (वि)जानाति does not know, for that reason, भर्तुः husband's, शय्या bed, सुखा comfortable, मन्ये I think.
explanation: Hapless Sita is young and delicate. Being a chaste lady, she, even in these (adverse) circumstances, does not feel the brunt. Hence, maybe she thinks her husbands' (hard) bed comfortable to her.

shloka_text: हा हन्ताऽस्मि नृशंसोऽहं यत्सभार्यः कृते मम। ईदृशीं राघवश्शय्यामधिशेते ह्यनाथवत्।।2.88.17।।
transliteration: hā hantā'smi nṛśaṃso'haṃ yatsabhāryaḥ kṛte mama| īdṛśīṃ rāghavaśśayyāmadhiśete hyanāthavat
translation: हा हन्त Alas, what a difficulty, अहम् I, नृशंसः अस्मि I have been cruel, यत् since, मम कृते  because of me, राघवः Rama, सभार्यः with his spouse, अनाथवत् like an orphan, ईदृशीम् such, शय्याम् bed, अधिशेते is reclining upon.
explanation: Alas, what suffering Because of a cruel man like me Rama along with his spouse was condemned to recline upon such bed like an orphan.

shloka_text: सार्वभौमकुले जात स्सर्वलोकस्य सम्मतः। सर्वलोकप्रियस्त्यक्त्वा राज्यं सुखमनुत्तम्।।2.88.18।। कथमिन्दीवरश्यामो रक्ताक्षः प्रियदर्शनः। सुखभागी न दुःखार्ह श्शयितो भुवि राघवः।।2.88.19।।
transliteration: sārvabhaumakule jāta ssarvalokasya sammataḥ| sarvalokapriyastyaktvā rājyaṃ sukhamanuttam kathamindīvaraśyāmo raktākṣaḥ priyadarśanaḥ| sukhabhāgī na duḥkhārha śśayito bhuvi rāghavaḥ
translation: सार्वभौमकुले in the house of emperors, जातः was born, सर्वलोकस्य of the entire world, सम्मतः worthy of reverence, सर्वलोकप्रियः beloved of all the worlds, इन्दीवरश्यामः with the complexion of a blue lotus, रक्ताक्षः of reddened eyes, प्रियदर्शनः pleasing to look, सुखभागी worthy of happiness, न दुःखार्हः does not deserve suffering, राघवः Rama, राज्यम् kingdom, अनुत्तमम् excellent, सुखम् comforts, त्यक्त्वा having given up, भुवि on this ground, कथम् how, शयितः did he sleep?
explanation: How could such Rama sleep on the ground? He was born in the house of emperors, worthy of reverence by the entire world and beloved of all the worlds, with the complexion of a blue lotus, with red eyes, and pleasing looks, one who deserves to be happy and not to suffer by renouncing the kingdom and excellent comforts.

shloka_text: सार्वभौमकुले जात स्सर्वलोकस्य सम्मतः। सर्वलोकप्रियस्त्यक्त्वा राज्यं सुखमनुत्तम्।।2.88.18।। कथमिन्दीवरश्यामो रक्ताक्षः प्रियदर्शनः। सुखभागी न दुःखार्ह श्शयितो भुवि राघवः।।2.88.19।।
transliteration: sārvabhaumakule jāta ssarvalokasya sammataḥ| sarvalokapriyastyaktvā rājyaṃ sukhamanuttam kathamindīvaraśyāmo raktākṣaḥ priyadarśanaḥ| sukhabhāgī na duḥkhārha śśayito bhuvi rāghavaḥ
translation: सार्वभौमकुले in the house of emperors, जातः was born, सर्वलोकस्य of the entire world, सम्मतः worthy of reverence, सर्वलोकप्रियः beloved of all the worlds, इन्दीवरश्यामः with the complexion of a blue lotus, रक्ताक्षः of reddened eyes, प्रियदर्शनः pleasing to look, सुखभागी worthy of happiness, न दुःखार्हः does not deserve suffering, राघवः Rama, राज्यम् kingdom, अनुत्तमम् excellent, सुखम् comforts, त्यक्त्वा having given up, भुवि on this ground, कथम् how, शयितः did he sleep?
explanation: How could such Rama sleep on the ground? He was born in the house of emperors, worthy of reverence by the entire world and beloved of all the worlds, with the complexion of a blue lotus, with red eyes, and pleasing looks, one who deserves to be happy and not to suffer by renouncing the kingdom and excellent comforts.

shloka_text: धन्यः खलु महाभागो लक्ष्मण श्शुभलक्षणः। भ्रातरं विषमे काले यो राममनुवर्तते।।2.88.20।।
transliteration: dhanyaḥ khalu mahābhāgo lakṣmaṇa śśubhalakṣaṇaḥ| bhrātaraṃ viṣame kāle yo rāmamanuvartate
translation: यः that, विषमे in adverse, काले times, भ्रातरम् brother, रामम् Rama, अनुवर्तते is accompanying, शुभलक्षणः a man of auspicious virtues, महाभागः a great man, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, धन्यः खलु is indeed fortunate.
explanation: Surely Lakshmana of great merit and auspicious virtues is fortunate since he is accompanying his brother Rama in times of adversity.

shloka_text: सिद्धार्था खलु वैदेही पतिं याऽनुगता वनम्। वयं संशयिता स्सर्वे हीनास्तेन महात्मना।।2.88.21।।
transliteration: siddhārthā khalu vaidehī patiṃ yā'nugatā vanam| vayaṃ saṃśayitā ssarve hīnāstena mahātmanā
translation: या that Sita, वनम् to the forest, पतिम् husband, अनुगता had followed, वैदेही Sita, सिद्धार्था खलु has surely acomplished her object, महात्मना by the magnanimous, तेन by that Rama, हीनाः bereft of, वयम् we, सर्वे all, संशयिताः are full of doubts.
explanation: Sita has, indeed, accomplished her object by accompanying her husband (to the forest). Bereft of that magnanimous Rama, all of us are in doubt (if he will accept our services).

shloka_text: आकर्णधारा पृथिवी नौः इव प्रतिभाति मा। गते दशरथे स्वर्गं रामे चारण्यमाश्रिते।।2.88.22।।
transliteration: ākarṇadhārā pṛthivī nauḥ iva pratibhāti mā| gate daśarathe svargaṃ rāme cāraṇyamāśrite
translation: दशरथे Dasaratha, स्वर्गम् to heaven, गते having ascended, रामे च when Rama too, अरण्यम् forest, आश्रिते having taken shelter, पृथिवी earth, आकर्णधारा without helmsman, नौः इव like a ship, मा to me, प्रतिभाति appears.
explanation: King Dasaratha having ascended to heaven and Rama taken shelter in the forest, this kingdom appears to me like a ship without a helmsman.

shloka_text: न च प्रार्थयते कच्चिन्मनसापि वसुन्धराम्। वनेऽपि वसतस्तस्य बाहुवीर्याभिरक्षिताम्।।2.88.23।।
transliteration: na ca prārthayate kaccinmanasāpi vasundharām| vane'pi vasatastasya bāhuvīryābhirakṣitām
translation: वने in the forest, वसतः अपि though residing, तस्य his, बाहुवीर्याभिरक्षिताम् protected by the might of his arms, वसुन्धराम् this earth, कश्चित् none, मनसापि even in thought, न च प्रार्थयते does not desire.
explanation: No one, even in thought, would ever desire this kingdom, protected by the strength of his arms even while residing in the forest.

shloka_text: शून्यसंवरणारक्षामयन्त्रितहयद्विपाम्। अपावृतपुरद्वारां राजधानीमरक्षिताम्।।2.88.24।। अप्रहृष्टबलां शून्यां विषमस्थामनावृताम्। शत्रवो नाभिमन्यन्ते भक्षान्विषकृतानिव।।2.88.25।।
transliteration: śūnyasaṃvaraṇārakṣāmayantritahayadvipām| apāvṛtapuradvārāṃ rājadhānīmarakṣitām aprahṛṣṭabalāṃ śūnyāṃ viṣamasthāmanāvṛtām| śatravo nābhimanyante bhakṣānviṣakṛtāniva
translation: शून्यसंवरणारक्षां without guards to keep vigil over the ramparts, अयन्त्रितहयद्विपाम् with horses and elephants are not in control, अपावृतपुरद्वाराम् with the city gates kept wide open, अरक्षिताम् unprotected, अप्रहृष्टबलाम् unhappy army, शून्याम् empty (demoralised), विषमस्थाम् in dire difficulties, अनावृताम् wide open, राजधानीम् the capital city (Ayodhya), शत्रवः enemies, विषकृतान् mixed with poison, भक्षानिव like food, नाभिमन्यन्ते will not think of.
explanation: Now the gates of our capital city (Ayodhya) are wide open. The city is unprotected and endangered. There are no guards to keep vigil over the ramparts. The horses and elephants are not in control (hence unprepared for battle). The army is unhappy and demoralised. At this state even the enemies will not like to seize the city, they will shun it like food mixed with poison.

shloka_text: शून्यसंवरणारक्षामयन्त्रितहयद्विपाम्। अपावृतपुरद्वारां राजधानीमरक्षिताम्।।2.88.24।। अप्रहृष्टबलां शून्यां विषमस्थामनावृताम्। शत्रवो नाभिमन्यन्ते भक्षान्विषकृतानिव।।2.88.25।।
transliteration: śūnyasaṃvaraṇārakṣāmayantritahayadvipām| apāvṛtapuradvārāṃ rājadhānīmarakṣitām aprahṛṣṭabalāṃ śūnyāṃ viṣamasthāmanāvṛtām| śatravo nābhimanyante bhakṣānviṣakṛtāniva
translation: शून्यसंवरणारक्षां without guards to keep vigil over the ramparts, अयन्त्रितहयद्विपाम् with horses and elephants are not in control, अपावृतपुरद्वाराम् with the city gates kept wide open, अरक्षिताम् unprotected, अप्रहृष्टबलाम् unhappy army, शून्याम् empty (demoralised), विषमस्थाम् in dire difficulties, अनावृताम् wide open, राजधानीम् the capital city (Ayodhya), शत्रवः enemies, विषकृतान् mixed with poison, भक्षानिव like food, नाभिमन्यन्ते will not think of.
explanation: Now the gates of our capital city (Ayodhya) are wide open. The city is unprotected and endangered. There are no guards to keep vigil over the ramparts. The horses and elephants are not in control (hence unprepared for battle). The army is unhappy and demoralised. At this state even the enemies will not like to seize the city, they will shun it like food mixed with poison.

shloka_text: अद्यप्रभृति भूमौ तु शयिष्येऽहं तृणेषु वा। फलमूलाशनो नित्यं जटाचीराणि धारयन्।।2.88.26।।
transliteration: adyaprabhṛti bhūmau tu śayiṣye'haṃ tṛṇeṣu vā| phalamūlāśano nityaṃ jaṭācīrāṇi dhārayan
translation: अद्य प्रभृति from today, अहम् I, जटाचीराणि matted hair and robes made of bark, धारयन् wearing, नित्यम् always, फलमूलाशनः eating fruits and roots, भूमौ तु on the ground itself, तृणेषु वा or on the grass, शयिष्ये I will sleep.
explanation: From today onwards, wearing matted hair and clad in robes made of bark and living on fruits and roots, I too shall sleep on the naked ground or on grass.

shloka_text: तस्यार्थमुत्तरं कालं निवत्स्यामि सुखं वने। तं प्रतिश्रवमामुच्य नास्य मिथ्या भविष्यति।।2.88.27।।
transliteration: tasyārthamuttaraṃ kālaṃ nivatsyāmi sukhaṃ vane| taṃ pratiśravamāmucya nāsya mithyā bhaviṣyati
translation: तम् Rama's, प्रतिश्रवम् vow, आमुच्य casting on me, उत्तरं कालम् the rest of his term (of exile), तस्य अर्थम् on account of him, वने in the forest, सुखम् cheerfully, निवत्स्यामि shall dwell, अस्य his vow, मिथ्या untrue, न भविष्यति shall not become.
explanation: Taking upon myself the vow of Rama, I too shall live in the forest cheerfully for the rest of the term on behalf of him so that his vow shall not prove untrue.

shloka_text: वसन्तं भ्रातुरर्थाय शत्रुघ्नो माऽनुवत्स्यति। लक्ष्मणेन सहत्वार्यो ह्ययोध्यां पालयिष्यति।।2.88.28।।
transliteration: vasantaṃ bhrāturarthāya śatrughno mā'nuvatsyati| lakṣmaṇena sahatvāryo hyayodhyāṃ pālayiṣyati
translation: शत्रुघ्नः Satrughna, भ्रातुः अर्थाय on behalf of my  brother Rama, वसन्तम् living (in the forest), मा me, अनुवत्स्यति will live by following me, आर्यः esteemed brother, लक्ष्मणेन सह along with Lakshmana, अयोध्याम् Ayodhya, पालयिष्यति हि will rule.
explanation: As I live in the forest on behalf of my brother Rama, Satrughna will live with me. My esteemed brother Rama will rule Ayodhya along with Lakshmana.

shloka_text: अभिषेक्ष्यन्ति काकुत्स्थमयोध्यायां द्विजातयः। अपि मे देवताः कुर्युरिमं सत्यं मनोरथम्।।2.88.29।।
transliteration: abhiṣekṣyanti kākutsthamayodhyāyāṃ dvijātayaḥ| api me devatāḥ kuryurimaṃ satyaṃ manoratham
translation: द्विजातयः brahmins, काकुत्स्थम् to Rama, अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, अभिषेक्ष्यन्ति will crown him, देवताः gods, इमम् this, मे my, मनोरथम् desire, सत्यम् as true, अपि कुर्युः will they make it?
explanation: In Ayodhya the brahmins shall coronate Rama. Will the gods make this desire of mine true?

shloka_text: प्रसाद्यमान श्शिरसा मया स्वयं बहुप्रकारं यदि नाभिपत्स्यते। ततोऽनुवत्स्यामि चिराय राघवम् वनेचरन्नार्हति मामुपेक्षितुम्।।2.88.30।।
transliteration: prasādyamāna śśirasā mayā svayaṃ bahuprakāraṃ yadi nābhipatsyate| tato'nuvatsyāmi cirāya rāghavam vanecarannārhati māmupekṣitum
translation: मया by me, स्वयम् personally, बहुप्रकारम् in many ways, शिरसा bowing down my head, प्रसाद्यमानः seeking his grace, न प्रपत्स्यते यदि if it is not granted, ततः then, वने चरन् living in the forest, राघवम् Rama, चिराय for a long time, अनुवत्स्यामि will live along him, माम् me, उपेक्षितुम् to ignore, नार्हति he cannot.
explanation: I will seek his grace in many ways by bowing down my head. Even then if Rama does not grant my wish, I shall also live with him as long as it takes. He will not be able to ignore a forester like me. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टाशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightyeigth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: उष्य रात्रिं तु तत्रैव गङ्गाकूले स राघवः। भरतः काल्यमुत्थाय शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.89.1।।
transliteration: uṣya rātriṃ tu tatraiva gaṅgākūle sa rāghavaḥ| bharataḥ kālyamutthāya śatrughnamidamabravīt
translation: राघवः born in the race of Raghu, सः भरतः that Bharata, तत्र there, गङ्गाकूले एव on the bank of the river Ganga only, रात्रिम् night, उष्य having stayed, काल्यम् at daybreak, उत्थाय rising, शत्रुघ्नम् Satrughna, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Bharata got up at daybreak after spending the night on the bank of the Ganga at that very place where Rama, the descendent of Raghu, had stayed. And said these words to Satrughna:
comments: Guha ferries Bharata, Satrughna and all others across Ganga -- Bharata sets out to meet sage Bharadwaja.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नोत्तिष्ठ किं शेषे निषादाधिपतिं गुहम्। शीघ्रमानय भद्रं ते तारयिष्यति वाहिनीम्।।2.89.2।।
transliteration: śatrughnottiṣṭha kiṃ śeṣe niṣādādhipatiṃ guham| śīghramānaya bhadraṃ te tārayiṣyati vāhinīm
translation: शत्रुघ्न Satrughna, उत्तिष्ठ arise, किम् why, शेषे are you asleep, ते for you, भद्रम् blessings to you, निषादाधिपतिम् overlord of Nishada, गुहम् Guha, शीघ्रम् quickly, आनय fetch, वाहिनीम् the army, तारयिष्यति he will help us in ferrying across.
explanation: O Satrughna, blessings to you Why are you still alseep? Arise fetch Guha the king of the nishadas quickly. He will ferry the army across the river.

shloka_text: जागर्मि नाहं स्वपिमि तमेवाऽर्यं विचिन्तयन्। इत्येवमब्रवीद्भ्रात्ता शत्रुघ्नोऽपि प्रचोदितः।।2.89.3।।
transliteration: jāgarmi nāhaṃ svapimi tamevā'ryaṃ vicintayan| ityevamabravīdbhrāttā śatrughno'pi pracoditaḥ
translation: भ्राता the brother, शत्रुघ्नोऽपि Satrughna also, प्रचोदितः having been urged upon, अहम् I, तम् that, आर्यम् एव about esteemed brother Rama only, विचिन्तयन् thinking about, जागर्मि I am awake, न स्वपिमि not sleeping, इत्येवम् in this way, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Urged by his brother Bharata, Satrughna replied 'I am not asleep. I am awake. I am deeply thinking of our esteemed brother, Rama'

shloka_text: इति संवदतोरेवमन्योन्यं नरसिंहयोः। आगम्य प्राञ्जलिः काले गुहो भरतमब्रवीत्।।2.89.4।।
transliteration: iti saṃvadatorevamanyonyaṃ narasiṃhayoḥ| āgamya prāñjaliḥ kāle guho bharatamabravīt
translation: नरसिंहयोः lions among men, Bharata and Satrughna, इत्येवम् in this way, अन्योन्यम् with one another, संवदतोः while both of them were conversing, गुहः Guha, काले at appropriate time, आगम्य having arrived, प्राञ्जलिः with folded palms, भरतम् to Bharata, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: While the two lions among men, Bharata and Satrughna were thus conversing with each other, Guha came in the appropriate time and said to Bharata with folded palms:

shloka_text: कच्चित्सुखं नदीतीरेऽवात्सीः काकुत्स्थ शर्वरीम्। कच्चित्ते सह सैन्यस्य तावत्सर्वमनामयम्।।2.89.5।।
transliteration: kaccitsukhaṃ nadītīre'vātsīḥ kākutstha śarvarīm| kaccitte saha sainyasya tāvatsarvamanāmayam
translation: काकुत्थ्स O scion of the Kakutstha race (Bharata), शर्वरीम् night, नदीतीरे on the bank of the river, सुखम् comfortably, कच्चित् वात्सीः you had passed, I hope, सह सैन्यस्य along with the army, ते to you, सर्वम् all, अनामयं तावत् कच्चित् there was no inconvenience, I trust.
explanation: O scion of the Kakutstha race (Bharata) I trust, you and your army passed the night on the river bank comfortably without any inconvenience.

shloka_text: गुहस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा तत्तु स्नेहादुदीरितम्। रामस्यानुवशो वाक्यं भरतोऽपीदमब्रवीत्।।2.89.6।।
transliteration: guhasya vacanaṃ śrutvā tattu snehādudīritam| rāmasyānuvaśo vākyaṃ bharato'pīdamabravīt
translation: रामस्य of Rama, अनुवशः obedient, भरतोऽपि Bharata too, स्नेहात् out of affection, उदीरितम् uttered, तत् that, गुहस्य Guha's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा on hearing, इदं वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: On hearing Guha's affectionate words Bharata, ever obedient to Rama, replied:

shloka_text: सुखा न श्शर्वरी राजन् पूजिताश्चापि ते वयम्। गङ्गां तु नौभिर्बह्वीभिर्दाशास्सन्तारयन्तु नः।।2.89.7।।
transliteration: sukhā na śśarvarī rājan pūjitāścāpi te vayam| gaṅgāṃ tu naubhirbahvībhirdāśāssantārayantu naḥ
translation: राजन् O king, नः for us, शर्वरी the night, सुखा comfortable, वयम् we, ते to (by) you, पूजिताश्चापि have been honoured, दाशाः fishermen, बह्वीभिः by many, नौभिः boats, नः us, गङ्गाम् the river Ganga, सन्तारयन्तु please, ferry us across.
explanation: O king (Guha) the night passed comfortably for us. We have been honoured by you in many ways. Let your fishermen be ordered to ferry us across the Ganga in their boats.

shloka_text: ततो गुह स्सन्त्वरितं श्रुत्वा भरतशासनम्। प्रति प्रविश्य नगरं तं ज्ञातिजनमब्रवीत्।।2.89.8।।
transliteration: tato guha ssantvaritaṃ śrutvā bharataśāsanam| prati praviśya nagaraṃ taṃ jñātijanamabravīt
translation: ततः then, गुहः Guha, सन्त्वरितम् quickly, भरतशासनम् at Bharata's command, श्रुत्वा having heard, नगरम् his establishment, प्रति प्रविश्य having entered, तम् that, ज्ञातिजनम् to his relations, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Then at Bharata's command Guha returned to his habitation quickly and said to his relations:

shloka_text: उत्तिष्ठत प्रबुध्यध्वं भद्रमस्तु च वस्सदा। नाव स्समनुकर्षध्वं तारयिष्याम वाहिनीम्।।2.89.9।।
transliteration: uttiṣṭhata prabudhyadhvaṃ bhadramastu ca vassadā| nāva ssamanukarṣadhvaṃ tārayiṣyāma vāhinīm
translation: उत्तिष्ठत arise, प्रबुध्यध्वम् awake, सदा always, वः भद्रम् अस्तु be blessed, नावः the boats, समनुकर्षध्वम् haul down, वाहिनीम् the army, तारयिष्याम we shall ferry them across.
explanation: Arise and awake. May you be ever blessed. Haul down the boats into the river. We have to ferry the army (across the river).

shloka_text: ते तथोक्ता स्समुत्थाय त्वरिता राजशासनात्। पञ्चनावां शतान्याशु समानिन्युस्समन्ततः।।2.89.10।।
transliteration: te tathoktā ssamutthāya tvaritā rājaśāsanāt| pañcanāvāṃ śatānyāśu samāninyussamantataḥ
translation: तथा thus, उक्ताः addressed, ते they, राजशासनात् by the king's command, त्वरिताः in haste, आशु immediately, समन्ततः from every direction, नावाम् of the boats, पञ्चशतानि five hundreds, समानिन्युः brought.
explanation: On hearing these words, they arose in haste and immediately brought five hundred boats from every direction in accordance with the command of their king (Guha).

shloka_text: अन्या स्स्वस्तिकविज्ञेया महाघंटाधरा वराः। शोभमानाः पताकाभिर्युक्तवातास्सुसंहताः।।2.89.11।।
transliteration: anyā ssvastikavijñeyā mahāghaṃṭādharā varāḥ| śobhamānāḥ patākābhiryuktavātāssusaṃhatāḥ
translation: महाघंटाधराः fitted with large bells, वराः excellent, पताकाभिः with flags, शोभमानाः looking  magnificent, युक्तवाताः filled with sails, सुसंहताः built solidly, स्वस्तिकविज्ञेयाः known as Swastika, अन्याः also some other boats (brought).
explanation: They brought excellent boats known as Swastika, solidly built, they lookd magnificent, filled with large bells, sails and flags.

shloka_text: तत स्स्वस्तिकविज्ञेयां पाण्डुकम्बलसंवृताम्। सनन्दिघोषां कल्याणीं गुहो नावमुपाहरत्।।2.89.12।।
transliteration: tata ssvastikavijñeyāṃ pāṇḍukambalasaṃvṛtām| sanandighoṣāṃ kalyāṇīṃ guho nāvamupāharat
translation: ततः then, गुहः Guha, पाण्डुकम्बलसंवृताम् covered with white canvas, सनन्दिघोषाम् generating aptivating sounds, कल्याणीं auspicious, स्वस्तिकविज्ञेयाम् known as Swastika, नावम् boat, उपाहरत् brought.
explanation: Then Guha personally brought an auspicious boat known as Swastika covered with white canvas and generating captivating sounds.

shloka_text: तामारुरोह भरतश्शत्रुघ्नश्च महाबलः। कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च याश्चान्या राजयोषितः।।2.89.13।। पुरोहितश्च तत्पूर्वं गुरवो ब्राह्मणाश्च ये। अनन्तरं राजदारास्तदैव शकटापणाः।।2.89.14।।
transliteration: tāmāruroha bharataśśatrughnaśca mahābalaḥ| kausalyā ca sumitrā ca yāścānyā rājayoṣitaḥ purohitaśca tatpūrvaṃ guravo brāhmaṇāśca ye| anantaraṃ rājadārāstadaiva śakaṭāpaṇāḥ
translation: भरतः Bharata, ताम् आरुरोह boarded it, महाबलः of great strength, शत्रुघ्नश्च Satrughna also, कौसल्या च Kausalya, सुमित्रा च Sumitra, अन्याः other, याः राजयोषितः other royal women, तत्पूर्वम् before them, पुरोहितश्च family priest (Vasistha), गुरवः preceptors, ये ब्राह्मणाश्च such  brahmins, अनन्तरम् thereafter, राजदाराः king's wives, तथैव also, शकटापणाः wagons and supplies.
explanation: The family priest (Vasistha) and other brahmins were the first to board. Next mighty Bharata and Satrughna, Kausalya, Sumitra, women of the palace including the other wives of the king and wagons and supplies followed.

shloka_text: तामारुरोह भरतश्शत्रुघ्नश्च महाबलः। कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च याश्चान्या राजयोषितः।।2.89.13।। पुरोहितश्च तत्पूर्वं गुरवो ब्राह्मणाश्च ये। अनन्तरं राजदारास्तदैव शकटापणाः।।2.89.14।।
transliteration: tāmāruroha bharataśśatrughnaśca mahābalaḥ| kausalyā ca sumitrā ca yāścānyā rājayoṣitaḥ purohitaśca tatpūrvaṃ guravo brāhmaṇāśca ye| anantaraṃ rājadārāstadaiva śakaṭāpaṇāḥ
translation: भरतः Bharata, ताम् आरुरोह boarded it, महाबलः of great strength, शत्रुघ्नश्च Satrughna also, कौसल्या च Kausalya, सुमित्रा च Sumitra, अन्याः other, याः राजयोषितः other royal women, तत्पूर्वम् before them, पुरोहितश्च family priest (Vasistha), गुरवः preceptors, ये ब्राह्मणाश्च such  brahmins, अनन्तरम् thereafter, राजदाराः king's wives, तथैव also, शकटापणाः wagons and supplies.
explanation: The family priest (Vasistha) and other brahmins were the first to board. Next mighty Bharata and Satrughna, Kausalya, Sumitra, women of the palace including the other wives of the king and wagons and supplies followed.

shloka_text: आवासमादीपयतां तीर्थं चाप्यवगाहताम्। भाण्डानि चाददानानां घोषस्त्रिदिवमस्पृशत्।।2.89.15।।
transliteration: āvāsamādīpayatāṃ tīrthaṃ cāpyavagāhatām| bhāṇḍāni cādadānānāṃ ghoṣastridivamaspṛśat
translation: आवासम् the shelters in that camp, आदीपयताम् those who are burning, तीर्थं चापि through the descent of the river, अवगाहताम् those who are going down, भाण्डानि supplies, आददानानाम् of transporting, घोषः clamour, त्रिदिवम् the heaven, अस्पृशत् not touching.
explanation: The clamour of the people setting fire to the temporary shelters in that camp, descending down the river and transporting the supplies into the boats reached the heaven.

shloka_text: पताकिन्यस्तु ता नावस्स्वयं दाशैरधिष्ठिताः। वहन्त्यो जनमारूढं तदा सम्पेतुराशुगाः।।2.89.16।।
transliteration: patākinyastu tā nāvassvayaṃ dāśairadhiṣṭhitāḥ| vahantyo janamārūḍhaṃ tadā sampeturāśugāḥ
translation: पताकिन्यः (adorned) with flags, दाशैः by the fishermen, स्वयम् themselves, अधिष्ठिताः  occupied, ताः नावः those boats, तदा then, आरूढम् boarded, जनम् men, वह्नत्यः carrying, आशुगाः swiftly rowing men, सम्पेतुः moved.
explanation: Those boats adorned with flags were propelled by the fishermen occupying them. They sailed with men rowing on board fast.

shloka_text: नारीणामभिपूर्णा स्तु काश्चित् काश्चिच्च वाजिनाम्। काश्चिदत्र वहन्ति स्म यानयुग्यं महाधनम्।।2.89.17।।
transliteration: nārīṇāmabhipūrṇā stu kāścit kāścicca vājinām| kāścidatra vahanti sma yānayugyaṃ mahādhanam
translation: अत्र there, काश्चित् some boats, नारीणाम् with women, अभिपूर्णाः were filled with, काश्चित् some others, वाजिनाम् with horses, काश्चित् while still others, यानयुग्यम् the draught animals for drawing carriages, महाधनम् great treasures, वहन्ति स्म were transporting.
explanation: Some boats were filled with women, some others with horses. while still others transported draught animals for drawing carriages and the great treasures.

shloka_text: ता स्स्म गत्वा परं तीरमवरोप्य च तं जनम्। निवृत्ताः काण्डचित्राणि क्रियन्ते दाशबन्धुभिः।।2.89.18।।
transliteration: tā ssma gatvā paraṃ tīramavaropya ca taṃ janam| nivṛttāḥ kāṇḍacitrāṇi kriyante dāśabandhubhiḥ
translation: ताः those, परं तीरम् the other bank, गत्वा having reached, तं जनम् the men, अवरोप्य disembarked, निवृत्ताः स्म returned, दाशबन्धुभिः the fisherfolk, काण्डचित्राणि lovely formations with their craft, क्रियन्ते स्म exhibited.
explanation: Having reached the other bank, the men disembarked. While returning, the fisherfolk exhibited their craft of lovely formations.

shloka_text: सवैजयन्तास्तु गजा गजारोहप्रचोदिताः। तरन्त स्स्म प्रकाशन्ते सध्वजा इव पर्वताः।।2.89.19।।
transliteration: savaijayantāstu gajā gajārohapracoditāḥ| taranta ssma prakāśante sadhvajā iva parvatāḥ
translation: सवैजयन्ताः embellished with banners, गजारोहप्रचोदिताः goaded by their mahouts, गजाः the elephants, तरन्तः while crossing the water, सध्वजाः with flags, पर्वताः इव like mountains, प्रकाशन्ते स्म were shining.
explanation: The elephants, embellished with banners and goaded by their mahouts looked splendid like mountains with banners while crossing in the water.

shloka_text: नावस्त्वारुरुहुश्चान्ये प्लवैस्तेरु स्तथापरे। अन्ये कुम्भघटैस्तेरुरन्येतेरुश्च बाहुभिः।।2.89.20।।
transliteration: nāvastvāruruhuścānye plavaisteru stathāpare| anye kumbhaghaṭaisteruranyeteruśca bāhubhiḥ
translation: अन्ये other, नावः boats, आरुरुहुश्च boarded, अपरे others, तथा like that, प्लवैः on rafts, तेरुः crossed, अन्ये others, कुम्भघटैः with large pots, तेरुः crossed, अन्ये others, बाहुभिः with their arms, तेरुः च crossed.
explanation: Only some of the people were able to board the boats. Some others crossed on rafts and on large pots. Still others swam with their arms.

shloka_text: सा पुण्या ध्वजिनी गङ्गां दाशैस्सन्तारिता स्वयम्। मैत्रे मुहूर्ते प्रययौ प्रयागवनमुत्तमम्।।2.89.21।।
transliteration: sā puṇyā dhvajinī gaṅgāṃ dāśaissantāritā svayam| maitre muhūrte prayayau prayāgavanamuttamam
translation: दाशैः by the fishermen, स्वयम् themselves, गङ्गाम् the river Ganga, सन्तारिता ferried over, पुण्या auspicious, सा ध्वजिनी army, मैत्रे मुहूर्ते at the auspicious hour of Maitra, उत्तमम् great, प्रयागवनम् forest of Prayaga, प्रययौ reached.
explanation: The auspicious army, ferried across the river Ganga by the fishermen, reached the great forest of Prayaga at the auspicious hour of Maitra.

shloka_text: आश्वासयित्वा च चमूं महात्मा निवेशयित्वा च यथोपजोषम्। द्रष्टुं भरद्वाजमृषिप्रवर्य मृत्विग्वृतस्सन्भरतः प्रतस्थे।।2.89.22।।
transliteration: āśvāsayitvā ca camūṃ mahātmā niveśayitvā ca yathopajoṣam| draṣṭuṃ bharadvājamṛṣipravarya mṛtvigvṛtassanbharataḥ pratasthe
translation: महात्मा the noble one, भरतः Bharata, चमूम् the army, आश्वासयित्वा having rested, यथोपजोषम्  according to their pleasure, निवेशयित्वा having encamped, ऋषिप्रवर्यम् the distinguished rishi, भरद्वाजम् Bharadwaja, द्रष्टुम् to see, ऋत्विग्वृतस्सन् surrounded by his priests, प्रतस्थे  set out.
explanation: The noble Bharata, got his army encamped according to their pleasure and set out, accompanied by his priests, to see the distinguished sage Bharadwaja.

shloka_text: भरद्वाजाश्रमं दृष्ट्वा क्रोशादेव नरर्षभः। बलं सर्वमवस्थाप्य जगाम सह मन्त्रिभिः।।2.90.1।। पद्भ्यामेव हि धर्मज्ञो न्यस्तशस्त्रपरिच्छदः। वसानो वाससी क्षौमे पुरोधाय पुरोधसम्।।2.90.2।।
transliteration: bharadvājāśramaṃ dṛṣṭvā krośādeva nararṣabhaḥ| balaṃ sarvamavasthāpya jagāma saha mantribhiḥ padbhyāmeva hi dharmajño nyastaśastraparicchadaḥ| vasāno vāsasī kṣaume purodhāya purodhasam
translation: धर्मज्ञः knower of righteous ways, नरर्षभः the best among men, क्रोशादेव from a distance of one krosa, भरद्वाजाश्रमम् Bharadwaja's hermitage, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सर्वम् entire, बलम् army, अवस्थाप्य  brought to a halt, न्यस्तशस्त्रपरिच्छदः lay aside the royal robes and weapons, क्षौमे वाससी silk garments, वसानः wearing, पुरोधसम् with family priest, Vasistha, पुरोधाय placing ahead of him, मन्त्रिभिस्सह along with ministers, पद्भ्याम् एव on foot, जगाम went.
explanation: Bharata, the knower of righteous ways and the best among men, saw the hermitage of Bharadwaja from a distance of one krosa and brought his entire army to a halt. He laid aside all his royal robes and weapons. Clad in silk garments, he went on foot along with his ministers, with the family priest Vasistha ahead of him.
comments: Bharadwaja welcomes Bharata and Vasistha -- Bharata discloses his intention to get back Rama.

shloka_text: भरद्वाजाश्रमं दृष्ट्वा क्रोशादेव नरर्षभः। बलं सर्वमवस्थाप्य जगाम सह मन्त्रिभिः।।2.90.1।। पद्भ्यामेव हि धर्मज्ञो न्यस्तशस्त्रपरिच्छदः। वसानो वाससी क्षौमे पुरोधाय पुरोधसम्।।2.90.2।।
transliteration: bharadvājāśramaṃ dṛṣṭvā krośādeva nararṣabhaḥ| balaṃ sarvamavasthāpya jagāma saha mantribhiḥ padbhyāmeva hi dharmajño nyastaśastraparicchadaḥ| vasāno vāsasī kṣaume purodhāya purodhasam
translation: धर्मज्ञः knower of righteous ways, नरर्षभः the best among men, क्रोशादेव from a distance of one krosa, भरद्वाजाश्रमम् Bharadwaja's hermitage, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सर्वम् entire, बलम् army, अवस्थाप्य  brought to a halt, न्यस्तशस्त्रपरिच्छदः lay aside the royal robes and weapons, क्षौमे वाससी silk garments, वसानः wearing, पुरोधसम् with family priest, Vasistha, पुरोधाय placing ahead of him, मन्त्रिभिस्सह along with ministers, पद्भ्याम् एव on foot, जगाम went.
explanation: Bharata, the knower of righteous ways and the best among men, saw the hermitage of Bharadwaja from a distance of one krosa and brought his entire army to a halt. He laid aside all his royal robes and weapons. Clad in silk garments, he went on foot along with his ministers, with the family priest Vasistha ahead of him.

shloka_text: तत स्सन्दर्शने तस्य भरद्वाजस्य राघवः। मन्त्रिणस्तानवस्थाप्य जगामानुपुरोहितम्।।2.90.3।।
transliteration: tata ssandarśane tasya bharadvājasya rāghavaḥ| mantriṇastānavasthāpya jagāmānupurohitam
translation: ततः then, राघवः scion of the Raghu race (Bharata), तान् मन्त्रिणः those ministers, तस्य भरद्वाजस्य that Bharadwaja's, संदर्शने within sight, अवस्थाप्य halted, अनुपुरोहितम् following his priest जगाम went.
explanation: Then the scion of the Raghu race (Bharata) halted his ministers within sight of Bharadwaja's (hermitage) and went along following his priest Vasistha.

shloka_text: वसिष्ठमथ दृष्ट्वैव भरद्वाजो महातपाः। सञ्चचाऽलासनात्तूर्णं शिष्यानर्घ्यमिति ब्रुवन्।।2.90.4।।
transliteration: vasiṣṭhamatha dṛṣṭvaiva bharadvājo mahātapāḥ| sañcacā'lāsanāttūrṇaṃ śiṣyānarghyamiti bruvan
translation: अथ thereafter, महातपाः the great ascetic, भरद्वाजः Bharadwaja, वसिष्ठम् Vasistha, दृष्ट्वैव on seeing, अर्घ्यम् इति bring offerings of water, शिष्यान् to disciples, ब्रुवन् saying, तूर्णम् soon, आसनात् from seat, सञ्चचाल moved.
explanation: On seeing Vasistha, the great ascetic Bharadwaja immediately left his seat and said to his disciples, Bring offerings of water.

shloka_text: समागम्य वसिष्ठेन भरतेनाभिवादितः। अबुद्ध्यत महातेजास्सुतं दशरथस्य तम्।।2.90.5।।
transliteration: samāgamya vasiṣṭhena bharatenābhivāditaḥ| abuddhyata mahātejāssutaṃ daśarathasya tam
translation: महातेजाः radiant Bharadwaja, वसिष्ठेन with Vasistha, समागम्य having met, भरतेन by Bharata, अभिवादितः greeted, तम् him, दशरथस्य Dasaratha's, सुतम् as son,  अबुद्ध्यत knew of.
explanation: After meeting Vasistha and greeted by Bharata, the radiant Bharadwaja could recognize he was the son of Dasaratha.

shloka_text: ताभ्यामर्घ्यं च पाद्यं च दत्वा पश्चात्फलानि च। आनुपूर्व्याच्छ धर्मज्ञः पप्रच्छ कुशलं कुले।।2.90.6।।
transliteration: tābhyāmarghyaṃ ca pādyaṃ ca datvā paścātphalāni ca| ānupūrvyāccha dharmajñaḥ papraccha kuśalaṃ kule
translation: धर्मज्ञः knower of righteous ways (Bharadwaja), आनुपूर्व्यात् in order, ताभ्याम् to both of them, अर्घ्यं च welcomeoffering, पाद्यं च water for washing feet, पश्चात् thereafter, फलानि च fruits, दत्वा having given, कुले in the family, कुशलम् welfare, पप्रच्छ enquired.
explanation: Offering them both in order arghya (welcomeoffering), water to wash their feet and fruits in accordance with the practice, he enquired Bharata about the welfare of the family.

shloka_text: अयोध्यायां बले कोशे मित्रेष्वपि च मन्त्रिषु। जानन् दशरथं वृत्तं न राजानमुदाहरत्।।2.90.7।।
transliteration: ayodhyāyāṃ bale kośe mitreṣvapi ca mantriṣu| jānan daśarathaṃ vṛttaṃ na rājānamudāharat
translation: अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, बले in the army, कोशे in the treasury, मित्रेष्वपि च of the friends also, मन्त्रिषु of the ministers, वृत्तम् wellbeing, जानन् knowingly, राजानम् king, दशरथम् Dasaratha, नोदाहरत् did not mention.
explanation: He enquired about the welfare of Ayodhya, of the army, treasury, friends and the ministers. But knowingly did not mention about Dasaratha's wellbeing (the knew Dasaratha was dead).

shloka_text: वसिष्ठो भरतश्चैनं पप्रच्छतुरनामयम्। शरीरेऽग्निषु वृक्षेषु शिष्येषु मृगपक्षिषु।।2.90.8।।
transliteration: vasiṣṭho bharataścainaṃ papracchaturanāmayam| śarīre'gniṣu vṛkṣeṣu śiṣyeṣu mṛgapakṣiṣu
translation: वसिष्ठः Vasistha, भरतश्च also Bharata, एनम् him, शरीरे about his health, अग्निषु his sacred fires, वृक्षेषु his trees, शिष्येषु his disciples, मृगपक्षिषु about animals and birds, अनामयम् well being, पप्रच्छतुः enquired.
explanation: Vasistha and Bharata also enquired about his health and welfare of his sacred fires, his disciples, animals and birds and trees of the hermitage.

shloka_text: तथेति तत्प्रतिज्ञाय भरद्वाजो महातपाः। भरतं प्रत्युवाचेदं राघवस्नेहबन्धनात्।।2.90.9।।
transliteration: tatheti tatpratijñāya bharadvājo mahātapāḥ| bharataṃ pratyuvācedaṃ rāghavasnehabandhanāt
translation: महातपाः the great ascetic, भरद्वाजः Bharadwaja, तथेति saying so, so, तत् that welfare, प्रतिज्ञाय informing, राघवस्नेहबन्धनात् out of affection for Rama, भरतं प्रति addressing Bharata, इदम् these words, उवाच said.
explanation: Saying, all is well, the great ascetic Bharadwaja, out of his affection for Rama, said to Bharata:

shloka_text: किमिहाऽगमने कार्यं तव राज्यं प्रशासतः। एतदाचक्ष्व मे सर्वं न हि मे शुद्ध्यते मनः।।2.90.10।।
transliteration: kimihā'gamane kāryaṃ tava rājyaṃ praśāsataḥ| etadācakṣva me sarvaṃ na hi me śuddhyate manaḥ
translation: राज्यम् kingdom, प्रशासतः while ruling over, तव for you, इह here, आगमने in the arrival, कार्यम् reason, किम् what, एतत् all this, सर्वम् completely, मे to me, आचक्ष्व tell, मे to me, मनः my mind, न हि शुद्ध्यते is not clear about it.
explanation: Why have you come here when you ought to be ruling the kingdom? Tell me everything about this. My mind is not clear in this matter.

shloka_text: सुषुवे यममित्रघ्नं कौसल्यानऽन्दवर्धनम्। भ्रात्रा सह सभार्यो यश्चिरं प्रव्राजितो वनम्।।2.90.11।। नियुक्तः स्त्रीनियुक्तेन पित्रा योऽसौ महायशाः। वनवासी भवेतीह समाः किल चतुर्दश।।2.90.12।। कच्छिन्न तस्यापापस्य पापं कर्तुमिहेच्छसि। अकण्टकं भोक्तुमना राज्यं तस्यानुजस्य च।।2.90.13।।
transliteration: suṣuve yamamitraghnaṃ kausalyāna'ndavardhanam| bhrātrā saha sabhāryo yaściraṃ pravrājito vanam niyuktaḥ strīniyuktena pitrā yo'sau mahāyaśāḥ| vanavāsī bhavetīha samāḥ kila caturdaśa kacchinna tasyāpāpasya pāpaṃ kartumihecchasi| akaṇṭakaṃ bhoktumanā rājyaṃ tasyānujasya ca
translation: अमित्रघ्नम् destroyer of enemies, आनन्दवर्धनम् enhances the delight of, यं that Rama, कौसल्या Kausalya, सुषुवे gave birth, यः that, सभार्यः with his wife, भ्रात्रा सह along with his brother, चिरम् for a long time, वनम् to the forest, प्रव्राजितः has been banished, महायशाः  illustrious, यः असौ that Rama, स्त्री नियुक्तेन urged by a woman, पित्रा by his father, चतुर्दश fourteen, समाः years, वनवासी living in the forest, भव shall become, इति thus, इह here, नियुक्तः has been ordered, तस्य his, अपापस्य sinless, तस्य his, अनुजस्य च brother, पापम्  harm, कर्तुम् to do, अकण्टकम् without obstacles, राज्यम् kingdom, भोक्तुमनाः to enjoy, इह here, न इच्छसि not intending to do so?
explanation: Rama, destroyer of enemies and enhancer of the delight of his mother Kausalya, has been banished to the forest for a long time along with his wife and brother. That illustrious one has been ordered by his father to live in the forest for fourteen years through the pursuasion of a woman. To enjoy the kingdom without obstacles do you intend to cause any harm to that irreproachable Rama and his brother?

shloka_text: सुषुवे यममित्रघ्नं कौसल्यानऽन्दवर्धनम्। भ्रात्रा सह सभार्यो यश्चिरं प्रव्राजितो वनम्।।2.90.11।। नियुक्तः स्त्रीनियुक्तेन पित्रा योऽसौ महायशाः। वनवासी भवेतीह समाः किल चतुर्दश।।2.90.12।। कच्छिन्न तस्यापापस्य पापं कर्तुमिहेच्छसि। अकण्टकं भोक्तुमना राज्यं तस्यानुजस्य च।।2.90.13।।

translation: अमित्रघ्नम् destroyer of enemies, आनन्दवर्धनम् enhances the delight of, यं that Rama, कौसल्या Kausalya, सुषुवे gave birth, यः that, सभार्यः with his wife, भ्रात्रा सह along with his brother, चिरम् for a long time, वनम् to the forest, प्रव्राजितः has been banished, महायशाः  illustrious, यः असौ that Rama, स्त्री नियुक्तेन urged by a woman, पित्रा by his father, चतुर्दश fourteen, समाः years, वनवासी living in the forest, भव shall become, इति thus, इह here, नियुक्तः has been ordered, तस्य his, अपापस्य sinless, तस्य his, अनुजस्य च brother, पापम्  harm, कर्तुम् to do, अकण्टकम् without obstacles, राज्यम् kingdom, भोक्तुमनाः to enjoy, इह here, न इच्छसि not intending to do so?
explanation: Rama, destroyer of enemies and enhancer of the delight of his mother Kausalya, has been banished to the forest for a long time along with his wife and brother. That illustrious one has been ordered by his father to live in the forest for fourteen years through the pursuasion of a woman. To enjoy the kingdom without obstacles do you intend to cause any harm to that irreproachable Rama and his brother?

shloka_text: सुषुवे यममित्रघ्नं कौसल्यानऽन्दवर्धनम्। भ्रात्रा सह सभार्यो यश्चिरं प्रव्राजितो वनम्।।2.90.11।। नियुक्तः स्त्रीनियुक्तेन पित्रा योऽसौ महायशाः। वनवासी भवेतीह समाः किल चतुर्दश।।2.90.12।। कच्छिन्न तस्यापापस्य पापं कर्तुमिहेच्छसि। अकण्टकं भोक्तुमना राज्यं तस्यानुजस्य च।।2.90.13।।
