translation: लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, धर्मम् righteousness, अर्थं च prosperity (wealth) also, कामं च desire, पृथिवीं चापि earth (kingdom) also, भवताम् अर्थे for your sake, इच्छामि I want, एतत् all this, ते to you, प्रतिशृणोमि I swear.
explanation: O Lakshmana, on the oath of righteousness, I wish wealth and pleasure as well as this kingdom for the sake of you all.

shloka_text: भ्रात्रूणां संग्रहार्थं च सुखार्थं चापि लक्ष्मण। राज्यमप्यहमिच्छामि सत्येनाऽयुधमालभे।।2.97.6।।
transliteration: bhrātrūṇāṃ saṃgrahārthaṃ ca sukhārthaṃ cāpi lakṣmaṇa| rājyamapyahamicchāmi satyenā'yudhamālabhe
translation: लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, भ्रात्रूणाम् brothers', संग्रहार्थम् remain united, सुखार्थं चापि and also for happiness, अहम् I, राज्यमपि even kingdom, इच्छामि I desire, सत्येन truly, आयुधम् weapons, अलभे I hold.
explanation: O Lakshmana, I desire this kingdom only for the unity and happiness of my brothers. I swear on the weapon I hold.

shloka_text: नेयं मम मही सौम्य दुर्लभा सागराम्बरा। न हीच्छेयमधर्मेण शक्रत्वमपि लक्ष्मण।।2.97.7।।
transliteration: neyaṃ mama mahī saumya durlabhā sāgarāmbarā| na hīccheyamadharmeṇa śakratvamapi lakṣmaṇa
translation: सौम्य O gentle, लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, सागराम्बरा with the sea as garment, इयम् this, मही earth, मम to me, दुर्लभा difficult, न not, अधर्मेण unrighteously, शक्रत्वमपि even Indrahood, न इच्छेयं हि I do not desire.
explanation: O gentle Lakshmana, lordship of this earth with the sea as its garment is not difficult to obtain (for me). But I do not desire even Indrahood by unrighteous means.

shloka_text: यद्विना भरतं त्वां च शत्रुघ्नं चापि मानद। भवेन्मम सुखं किञ्चिद्भस्म तत्कुरुतां शिखी।।2.97.8।।
transliteration: yadvinā bharataṃ tvāṃ ca śatrughnaṃ cāpi mānada| bhavenmama sukhaṃ kiñcidbhasma tatkurutāṃ śikhī
translation: मानद O bestower of honour (Lakshmana), यत् any happiness, भरतम् Bharata, त्वां च you also, शतृघ्नं चापि Satrughna too, विना without leaving, मम to me, भवेत् happens, तत् that, किञ्चित् सुखम् some happines, शिखी fire, भस्म as ashes, कुरुताम् let it be reduced.
explanation: O protector of honour even if there were to be some happiness which I could enjoy without you, Bharata, and Satrughna, let it be reduced to ashes by fire.

shloka_text: मन्येऽहमागतोऽयोध्यां भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। मम प्राणात्प्रियतरः कुलधर्ममनुस्मरन्।।2.97.9।। श्रुत्वा प्रव्राजितं मां हि जटावल्कलधारिणम्। जानक्यासहितं वीर त्वया च पुरुषर्षभ।।2.97.10।। स्नेहेनाऽक्रान्तहृदय श्शोकेनाकुलितेन्द्रियः। द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो ह्येष भरतो नान्यथाऽगतः।।2.97.11।।
transliteration: manye'hamāgato'yodhyāṃ bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ| mama prāṇātpriyataraḥ kuladharmamanusmaran śrutvā pravrājitaṃ māṃ hi jaṭāvalkaladhāriṇam| jānakyāsahitaṃ vīra tvayā ca puruṣarṣabha snehenā'krāntahṛdaya śśokenākulitendriyaḥ| draṣṭumabhyāgato hyeṣa bharato nānyathā'gataḥ
translation: वीर O valiant one, पुरुषर्षभ best among men, भ्रातृवत्सलः affectionate towards brothers, मम to me, प्राणात् more than life, प्रियतरः dearer, भरतः Bharata, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, आगतः  had returned, माम् me, जानक्या with Janaki, त्वया च with you, सहितम् in the company of, जटावल्कलधारिणम् wearing barks and matted locks, प्रव्राजितम् having been exiled, श्रुत्वा hearing, कुलधर्मम् duties of race, अनुस्मरन् remembering, स्नेहेन with devotion, आक्रान्तहृदय: mind possessed by, शोकेन with distress, आकुलितेन्द्रियः with agitated senses, द्रष्टुम् to see, अभ्यागतः has arrived, अहम् I, मन्ये consider, एषः भरतः this Bharata, अन्यथा for  any other reason, न आगतः has not come.
explanation: O best among men, O valiant one I think Bharata who is affectionate towards his brothers and who is dearer to me than my life, must have returned to Ayodhya and has heard that I had been exiled along with you and Janaki, wearing barks and matted locks. Remembering the duties of the race with an afflicted mind and with agitated senses he has come here to see me. He has not come with any other intention.

shloka_text: मन्येऽहमागतोऽयोध्यां भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। मम प्राणात्प्रियतरः कुलधर्ममनुस्मरन्।।2.97.9।। श्रुत्वा प्रव्राजितं मां हि जटावल्कलधारिणम्। जानक्यासहितं वीर त्वया च पुरुषर्षभ।।2.97.10।। स्नेहेनाऽक्रान्तहृदय श्शोकेनाकुलितेन्द्रियः। द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो ह्येष भरतो नान्यथाऽगतः।।2.97.11।।
transliteration: manye'hamāgato'yodhyāṃ bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ| mama prāṇātpriyataraḥ kuladharmamanusmaran śrutvā pravrājitaṃ māṃ hi jaṭāvalkaladhāriṇam| jānakyāsahitaṃ vīra tvayā ca puruṣarṣabha snehenā'krāntahṛdaya śśokenākulitendriyaḥ| draṣṭumabhyāgato hyeṣa bharato nānyathā'gataḥ
translation: वीर O valiant one, पुरुषर्षभ best among men, भ्रातृवत्सलः affectionate towards brothers, मम to me, प्राणात् more than life, प्रियतरः dearer, भरतः Bharata, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, आगतः  had returned, माम् me, जानक्या with Janaki, त्वया च with you, सहितम् in the company of, जटावल्कलधारिणम् wearing barks and matted locks, प्रव्राजितम् having been exiled, श्रुत्वा hearing, कुलधर्मम् duties of race, अनुस्मरन् remembering, स्नेहेन with devotion, आक्रान्तहृदय: mind possessed by, शोकेन with distress, आकुलितेन्द्रियः with agitated senses, द्रष्टुम् to see, अभ्यागतः has arrived, अहम् I, मन्ये consider, एषः भरतः this Bharata, अन्यथा for  any other reason, न आगतः has not come.
explanation: O best among men, O valiant one I think Bharata who is affectionate towards his brothers and who is dearer to me than my life, must have returned to Ayodhya and has heard that I had been exiled along with you and Janaki, wearing barks and matted locks. Remembering the duties of the race with an afflicted mind and with agitated senses he has come here to see me. He has not come with any other intention.

shloka_text: मन्येऽहमागतोऽयोध्यां भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। मम प्राणात्प्रियतरः कुलधर्ममनुस्मरन्।।2.97.9।। श्रुत्वा प्रव्राजितं मां हि जटावल्कलधारिणम्। जानक्यासहितं वीर त्वया च पुरुषर्षभ।।2.97.10।। स्नेहेनाऽक्रान्तहृदय श्शोकेनाकुलितेन्द्रियः। द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो ह्येष भरतो नान्यथाऽगतः।।2.97.11।।
transliteration: manye'hamāgato'yodhyāṃ bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ| mama prāṇātpriyataraḥ kuladharmamanusmaran śrutvā pravrājitaṃ māṃ hi jaṭāvalkaladhāriṇam| jānakyāsahitaṃ vīra tvayā ca puruṣarṣabha snehenā'krāntahṛdaya śśokenākulitendriyaḥ| draṣṭumabhyāgato hyeṣa bharato nānyathā'gataḥ
translation: वीर O valiant one, पुरुषर्षभ best among men, भ्रातृवत्सलः affectionate towards brothers, मम to me, प्राणात् more than life, प्रियतरः dearer, भरतः Bharata, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, आगतः  had returned, माम् me, जानक्या with Janaki, त्वया च with you, सहितम् in the company of, जटावल्कलधारिणम् wearing barks and matted locks, प्रव्राजितम् having been exiled, श्रुत्वा hearing, कुलधर्मम् duties of race, अनुस्मरन् remembering, स्नेहेन with devotion, आक्रान्तहृदय: mind possessed by, शोकेन with distress, आकुलितेन्द्रियः with agitated senses, द्रष्टुम् to see, अभ्यागतः has arrived, अहम् I, मन्ये consider, एषः भरतः this Bharata, अन्यथा for  any other reason, न आगतः has not come.
explanation: O best among men, O valiant one I think Bharata who is affectionate towards his brothers and who is dearer to me than my life, must have returned to Ayodhya and has heard that I had been exiled along with you and Janaki, wearing barks and matted locks. Remembering the duties of the race with an afflicted mind and with agitated senses he has come here to see me. He has not come with any other intention.

shloka_text: अम्बां च कैकयीं रुष्य परुषं चाप्रियं वदन्। प्रसाद्य पितरं श्रीमार्नाज्यं मे दातुमागतः।।2.97.12।।
transliteration: ambāṃ ca kaikayīṃ ruṣya paruṣaṃ cāpriyaṃ vadan| prasādya pitaraṃ śrīmārnājyaṃ me dātumāgataḥ
translation: श्रीमान् auspicious Bharata, अम्बाम् mother, कैकयीम् at Kaikeyi, रुष्य angered, परुषम् harshly, अप्रियं च bitterly, वदन् speaking, पितरम् father, प्रसाद्य having propitiated, मे to me, राज्यम् kingdom, दातुम् to offer, आगतः has come.
explanation: Auspicious Bharata, angry with Kaikeyi and having spoken to her unpleasant, bitter words and having propitiated our father, has come here to offer me the kingdom.

shloka_text: प्राप्तकालं यदेषोऽस्मान्भरतो द्रष्टुमिच्छति। अस्मासु मनसाऽप्येष नाप्रियं किञ्चिदाचरेत्।।2.97.13।।
transliteration: prāptakālaṃ yadeṣo'smānbharato draṣṭumicchati| asmāsu manasā'pyeṣa nāpriyaṃ kiñcidācaret
translation: एषः भरतः this Bharata, अस्मान् us, यत् द्रष्टुम् इच्छति should he desire to see, प्राप्तकालम् this is appropriate time, एषः he, अस्मासु in us, मनसा अपि even by thought, किंचित् even a little, अप्रियम् harm, नाचरेत् will not do.
explanation: Finding the time appropriate, Bharata has come to see us. Even in his mind he would have never thought of causing any harm to us in any way.

shloka_text: विप्रियं कृतपूर्वं ते भरतेन कदा नु किम्। ईदृशं वा भयं तेऽद्य भरतं योऽत्र शङ्कसे।।2.97.14।।
transliteration: vipriyaṃ kṛtapūrvaṃ te bharatena kadā nu kim| īdṛśaṃ vā bhayaṃ te'dya bharataṃ yo'tra śaṅkase
translation: अत्र here, यः such you, अद्य now, भरतम् about Bharata, शङ्कसे you suspect, ते to you, भरतेन by Bharata, कदा नु at any time anything, किम् विप्रियम् anything disagreeable, ईदृशम् such, भयं वा or fear, कृतपूर्वम् has been done in the past.
explanation: Why are you suspicious of Bharata? Has he done anything disagreeable to you any time in the past?

shloka_text: न हि ते निष्ठुरं वाच्यो भरतो नाप्रियं वचः। अहं ह्यप्रियमुक्त स्स्यां भरतस्याप्रिये कृते।।2.97.15।।
transliteration: na hi te niṣṭhuraṃ vācyo bharato nāpriyaṃ vacaḥ| ahaṃ hyapriyamukta ssyāṃ bharatasyāpriye kṛte
translation: भरतः Bharata, ते to you, निष्ठुरम् harsh word, न वाच्यः must not speak, अप्रियम् harsh, वचः words, न not, भरतस्य to Bharata, अप्रिये unpleasant act, कृते if it has been done, अहम् I, अप्रियम् harsh words, उक्तः स्यां हि has been told.
explanation: You must not speak any harsh or unpleasant words against Bharata. If you do, they will be deemed to be directed against me.

shloka_text: कथं नु पुत्राः पितरं हन्युः कस्यां चिदापदि। भ्राता वा भ्रातरं हन्यात्सौमित्रे प्राणमात्मनः।।2.97.16।।
transliteration: kathaṃ nu putrāḥ pitaraṃ hanyuḥ kasyāṃ cidāpadi| bhrātā vā bhrātaraṃ hanyātsaumitre prāṇamātmanaḥ
translation: सौमित्रे O Lakshmana, कस्यां चित् आपदि in whatever calamity, पुत्र: son, पितरम् father, कथं नु how, हन्युः can slay, भ्राता वा or a brother, आत्मनः as his own, प्राणम् life, भ्रातरम् his own brother, हन्यात् will kill?
explanation: Whatever be the calamity, O Lakshmana, how will sons slay their father, or a brother kill his own brother who is as dear to him as his own life?

shloka_text: यदि राज्यस्य हेतोस्त्वमिमां वाचं प्रभाषसे। वक्ष्यामि भरतं दृष्ट्वा राज्यमस्मै प्रदीयताम्।।2.97.17।।
transliteration: yadi rājyasya hetostvamimāṃ vācaṃ prabhāṣase| vakṣyāmi bharataṃ dṛṣṭvā rājyamasmai pradīyatām
translation: राज्यस्य हेतोः for the sake of a  kingdom, त्वम् you, इमां वाचम् these words, प्रभाषसे यदि if you are saying  भरतम् Bharata, दृष्टवा seeing, अस्मै for him, राज्यम् kingdom, प्रदीयताम् be given, वक्ष्यामि I shall tell.
explanation: If you are saying all these words only for the sake of the kingdom, then I shall ask Bharata when I see him to offer this kingdom to you.

shloka_text: उच्यमानोऽपि भरतो मया लक्ष्मण तद्वचः। राज्यमस्मै प्रयच्छेति बाढमित्येव वक्ष्यति।।2.97.18।।
transliteration: ucyamāno'pi bharato mayā lakṣmaṇa tadvacaḥ| rājyamasmai prayaccheti bāḍhamityeva vakṣyati
translation: लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, भरतोऽपि Bharata also, अस्मै to him, राज्यम् kingdom, प्रयच्छ give, इति  thus, उच्यमानः having been told, तद्वच: that word, बाढम् इत्येव certainly so, वक्ष्यति will say.
explanation: O Lakshmana if I earnestly exhort Bharata to offer this kingdom to you, then on hearing those words, he would say, 'Certainly so'.

shloka_text: तथोक्तो धर्मशीलेन भ्रात्रा तस्य हिते रतः। लक्ष्मणः प्रविवेशेव स्वानि गात्राणि लज्जया।।2.97.19।।
transliteration: tathokto dharmaśīlena bhrātrā tasya hite rataḥ| lakṣmaṇaḥ praviveśeva svāni gātrāṇi lajjayā
translation: धर्मशीलेन by a man of virtuous disposition, भ्रात्रा by brother, तथा thus, उक्तः uttered, तस्य  his brother's, हिते in welfare, रतः devoted, लक्ष्मणः Lakshamana, लज्जया with a sense of shame, स्वानि his own, गात्राणि limbs, प्रविवेशेव entered.
explanation: Having heard the words uttered by his brother, Rama of virtuous disposition, Lakshmana who was devoted to his brother's welfare, shrank.

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यं लक्ष्मण श्श्रुत्वा व्रीलितः प्रत्युवाच ह। त्वां मन्ये द्रष्टुमायातः पिता दशरथ स्स्वयम्।।2.97.20।।
transliteration: tadvākyaṃ lakṣmaṇa śśrutvā vrīlitaḥ pratyuvāca ha| tvāṃ manye draṣṭumāyātaḥ pitā daśaratha ssvayam
translation: लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, तद्वाक्यम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, व्रीलितः abashed, प्रत्युवाच ह replied, पिता father, दशरथः Dasaratha, त्वां you, द्रष्टुम् to see, स्वयम् personally, आयातः has come, मन्ये I think.
explanation: Hearing the words of Rama, Lakshmana was abashed and said I think it is our father, king Dasaratha who has come here personally to see you.

shloka_text: व्रीलितं लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा राघवः प्रत्युवाच ह। एष मन्ये महाबाहुरिहास्मान्द्रष्टुमागतः।।2.97.21।।
transliteration: vrīlitaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ pratyuvāca ha| eṣa manye mahābāhurihāsmāndraṣṭumāgataḥ
translation: व्रीलितम् ashamed, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, दृष्ट्वा seeing, राघवः Rama, प्रत्युवाच ह replied, महाबाहुः mightyarmed, एषः this king Dasaratha, अस्मान् us, द्रष्टुम् to see, इह here, आगतः has come, मन्ये I think.
explanation: Observing Lakshmana's abashment, Rama said I think the mightyarmed king Dasaratha has come to see all of us here.

shloka_text: अथवा नौ ध्रुवं मन्ये मन्यमान स्सुखोचितौ। वनवासमनुध्याय गृहाय प्रतिनेष्यति।।2.97.22।।
transliteration: athavā nau dhruvaṃ manye manyamāna ssukhocitau| vanavāsamanudhyāya gṛhāya pratineṣyati
translation: अथवा or rather, नौ both of us, सुखोचितौ accustomed to comforts, मन्यमानः treating, वनवासम् dwelling in the forest, अनुध्याय having thought of, गृहाय to home, प्रतिनेष्यति take back, ध्रुवम् this is certain, मन्ये I think.
explanation: Or rather having thought of the adversities of dwelling in a forest and also by realising  that both of us are accustomed to comforts, I think he has certainly come to take us back home.

shloka_text: इमां वाप्येष वैदेहीमत्यन्तसुखसेविनीम्। पिता मे राघव श्श्रीमान्वनादादाय यास्यति।।2.97.23।।
transliteration: imāṃ vāpyeṣa vaidehīmatyantasukhasevinīm| pitā me rāghava śśrīmānvanādādāya yāsyati
translation: मे पिता my father, श्रीमान् prosperous, एषः राघवः this Raghava, अत्यन्त सुखसेविनीम् brought up in every luxury, इमाम् this lady, वैदेहीम् वा or princess Vaidehi, वनात् from the forest, आदाय यास्यति will take her back.
explanation: Our father, the prosperous Dasaratha, after withdrawing this princess Vaidehi who is brought up in luxury from the forest (to Ayodhya), will return.

shloka_text: एतौ तौ सम्प्रकाशेते गोत्रवन्तौ मनोरमौ। वायुवेगसमौ वीर जवनौ तुरगोत्तमौ।।2.97.24।।
transliteration: etau tau samprakāśete gotravantau manoramau| vāyuvegasamau vīra javanau turagottamau
translation: वीर O valiant one, गोत्रवन्तौ both of them of high pedigree, मनोरमौ charming, वायुवेगसमो windswift, जवनौ both swift, तौ those, एतौ these two, तुरगोत्तमौ splendid horses, सम्प्रकाशेते are shining.
explanation: O valiant warrior, you can see those two splendid horses of high pedigree, charming, swift and equal to wind in speed are shining (in the army).

shloka_text: स एष सुमहाकायः कम्पते वाहिनीमुखे। नागश्शत्रुञ्जयो नाम वृद्धस्तातस्य धीमतः।।2.97.25।।
transliteration: sa eṣa sumahākāyaḥ kampate vāhinīmukhe| nāgaśśatruñjayo nāma vṛddhastātasya dhīmataḥ
translation: सुमहाकायः huge, शत्रुञ्जयः named Satrunjaya, धीमतः of the sagacious, तातस्य father's, सः that, वृद्धः aged, नागः elephant, एषः here it is, वाहिनीमुखे at the head of the army, कम्पते moving about.
explanation: There is that huge and aged elephant named Satrunjaya which belogns to our sagacious father proceeding at the head of the army.

shloka_text: न तु पश्यामि तच्छत्रं पाण्डुरं लोकसत्कृतम् | पितुर्दिव्यं महाबाहो संशयो भवतीह मे।।2.97.26।।
transliteration: na tu paśyāmi tacchatraṃ pāṇḍuraṃ lokasatkṛtam | piturdivyaṃ mahābāho saṃśayo bhavatīha me
translation: महाबाहो O long-armed one, पाण्डुरम् white in colour, लोकसत्कृतम् well-respected by men, दिव्यम् splendid, पितुः father's, तत् then, छत्रं तु canopy, न पश्यामि I do not see, इह in this matter, मे to me, संशयः doubt, भवति is arising.
explanation: I do not see, O long-armed one! that splendid white canopy of my father, well-respected by men. And this gives rise to doubts in my mind.

shloka_text: वृक्षाग्रादवरोह त्वं कुरु लक्ष्मण मद्वचः। इतीव रामो धर्मात्मा सौमित्रिं तमुवाच ह।।2.97.27।।
transliteration: vṛkṣāgrādavaroha tvaṃ kuru lakṣmaṇa madvacaḥ| itīva rāmo dharmātmā saumitriṃ tamuvāca ha
translation: लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, त्वम् you, वृक्षाग्रात् from the tree top, अवरोह climb down, मद्वचः my words, कुरु follow, इतीव thus, धर्मात्मा the righteous one, रामः Rama, तं सौमित्रम् to that Lakshmana, उवाच ह said.
explanation: Get off the treetop, O Lakshmana, and do what I say said the righteous Rama.

shloka_text: अवतीर्य तु सालाग्रात्तस्मात्स समितिञ्जयः। लक्ष्मणः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा तस्थौ रामस्य पार्श्वतः।।2.97.28।।
transliteration: avatīrya tu sālāgrāttasmātsa samitiñjayaḥ| lakṣmaṇaḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā tasthau rāmasya pārśvataḥ
translation: समितिञ्जयः conqueror of the enemy, सः लक्ष्मणः that Lakshmana, तस्मात् सालाग्रात् from the top of that sala tree, अवतीर्य having descended, प्राञ्जलिः भूत्वा with folded palms, रामस्य Rama's, पार्श्वतः by the side of, तस्थौ stood.
explanation: Lakshmana, the conqueror of foes, descended from the top of the sala tree and stood by the side of Rama with folded palms.

shloka_text: भरतेनापि सन्दिष्टा सम्मर्दो न भवेदिति। समन्तात्तस्य शैलस्य सेना वासमकल्पयत्।।2.97.29।।
transliteration: bharatenāpi sandiṣṭā sammardo na bhavediti| samantāttasya śailasya senā vāsamakalpayat
translation: सम्मर्दः crowding, न भवेत् let it not happen, इति thus, भरतेनापि by Bharata also, सन्दिष्टा instructed, सेना army, तस्य शैलस्य that mountain's, समन्तात् around, आवासम् encampment, अकल्पयत् made.
explanation: Let not the hermitage be crowded commanded Bharata, and the army encamped  around the mountain.

shloka_text: अध्यर्धमिक्ष्वाकुचमूर्योजनं पर्वतस्य सा। पार्श्वे न्यविशदावृत्य गजवाजिरथाकुला।।2.97.30।।
transliteration: adhyardhamikṣvākucamūryojanaṃ parvatasya sā| pārśve nyaviśadāvṛtya gajavājirathākulā
translation: गजवाजिरथाकुला with throngs of horses, elephants and chariots, सा that, इक्ष्वाकुचमूः the army of the descendant of Ikshvaku, अध्यर्धयोजनम् a distance more than one and a half yojanas, पर्वतस्य mountain's, पार्श्वे by the side of, आवृत्य having surrounded, न्यविशत् encamped.
explanation: Bharata's army full of horses, elephants and chariots covering a distance of more than one and a half yojanas encamped by the side of the mountain.

shloka_text: सा चित्रकूटे भरतेन सेना धर्मं पुरस्कृत्य विधूय दर्पम्। प्रसादनार्थं रघुनन्दनस्य विराजते नीतिमता प्रणीता।।2.97.31।।
transliteration: sā citrakūṭe bharatena senā dharmaṃ puraskṛtya vidhūya darpam| prasādanārthaṃ raghunandanasya virājate nītimatā praṇītā
translation: धर्मम् righteousness, पुरस्कृत्य adopting, दर्पम् pride, विधूय casting aside, रघुनन्दनस्य Rama's, प्रसादनार्थम् to propitiate, नीतिमता by a moralist, भरतेन by Bharata, प्रणीता having been brought, सा that, सेना army, चित्रकूटे on Chitrakuta, विराजते was shining.
explanation: The army brought by Bharata, the great moralist, was shining around Chitrakuta mountain following dharma, and casting off all pride, in order to please Rama. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तनवतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetyseventh sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: निवेश्य सेनां तु विभुः पद्भ्यां पादवतां वरः। अभिगन्तुं स काकुत्थ्समियेष गुरुवर्तकम्।।2.98.1।।
transliteration: niveśya senāṃ tu vibhuḥ padbhyāṃ pādavatāṃ varaḥ| abhigantuṃ sa kākutthsamiyeṣa guruvartakam
translation: विभुः the lord, पादवताम् among the bipeds, वरः best, सः that Bharata, सेनाम् army, निवेश्य after encamping, गुरुवर्तकम् devoted the preceptor (father), काकुत्थ्सम् Rama, पद्भ्याम् on foot, अभिगन्तुम् to approach, इयेष wished.
explanation: On encamping the army, lord Bharata, the best among men, wished to approach on foot Rama who was devoted to his father.
comments: Bharata's joy on locating the hermitage of Sri Rama.

shloka_text: निविष्टमात्रे सैन्ये तु यथोद्देशं विनीतवत्। भरतो भ्रातरं वाक्यं शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.98.2।।
transliteration: niviṣṭamātre sainye tu yathoddeśaṃ vinītavat| bharato bhrātaraṃ vākyaṃ śatrughnamidamabravīt
translation: सैन्ये army, यथोद्देशम् in assigned places, निविष्टमात्रे after encamping, भरतः Bharata, भ्रातरम् brother, शत्रुघ्नम् to Satrughna, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: After the army encamped in the assigned places, Bharata said to his brother Satrughna thus:

shloka_text: क्षिप्रं वनमिदं सौम्य नरसङ्घै स्समन्ततः। लुब्धैश्च सहितैरेभि स्त्वमन्वेषितुमर्हसि।।2.98.3।।
transliteration: kṣipraṃ vanamidaṃ saumya narasaṅghai ssamantataḥ| lubdhaiśca sahitairebhi stvamanveṣitumarhasi
translation: सौम्य O dear Satrughna, नरसङ्घै: with groups of people, सहितैः accompanied by, लुब्धैश्च  in the company of hunters as well, त्वम् you, क्षिप्रम् quickly, इदं वनम् this forest, समन्ततः all over, अन्वेषितुम् to explore, अर्हसि should.
explanation: O dear Satrughna, you should explore this forest quickly along with groups of our people and  hunters as well.

shloka_text: गुहो ज्ञातिसहस्रेण शरचापासिधारिणा। समन्वेषतु काकुत्स्थमस्मिन् परिवृतस्स्वयम्।।2.98.4।।
transliteration: guho jñātisahasreṇa śaracāpāsidhāriṇā| samanveṣatu kākutsthamasmin parivṛtassvayam
translation: गुहः Guha, शरचापासिधारिणा armed with bows, arrows and swords, ज्ञातिसहस्रेण with a thousand kinsmen, परिवृतः surrounded by, स्वयम् himself, अस्मिन् in this forest, काकुत्स्थम् Rama, समन्वेषतु explore.
explanation: Let Guha, surrounded by a thousand kinsmen and armed with bows, arrows and swords look for Rama.

shloka_text: अमात्यै स्सह पौरैश्च गुरुभिश्च द्विजातिभिः। वनं सर्वं चरिष्यामि पद्भ्यां परिवृत स्स्वयम्।।2.98.5।।
transliteration: amātyai ssaha pauraiśca gurubhiśca dvijātibhiḥ| vanaṃ sarvaṃ cariṣyāmi padbhyāṃ parivṛta ssvayam
translation: स्वयम् I myself, अमात्यैः सह with counsellors, पौरैश्च with citizens, गुरुभिश्च with preceptors, द्विजातिभिः with brahmins, परिवृतः surrounded by, सर्वम् entire, वनम् forest, पद्भ्याम् on foot, चरिष्यामि I shall move about.
explanation: 'I myself shall go on foot surrounded by ministers, citizens, preceptors and brahmins and search the entire forest.

shloka_text: यावन्न रामं द्रक्ष्यामि लक्ष्मणं वा महाबलम्। वैदेहीं च महाभागां न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति।।2.98.6।।
transliteration: yāvanna rāmaṃ drakṣyāmi lakṣmaṇaṃ vā mahābalam| vaidehīṃ ca mahābhāgāṃ na me śāntirbhaviṣyati
translation: रामम् Rama, महाबलम् powerful, लक्ष्मणं वा Lakshmana, महाभागां illustrious, वैदेहीं च Sita, यावत्  till such time, न द्रक्ष्यामि I do not see, मे to me, शान्ति peace, न भविष्यति shall not come.
explanation: 'I shall not rest in peace until I see Rama, powerful Lakshmana and illustrious princess of Videha (Sita).

shloka_text: यावन्न चन्द्रसङ्काशं द्रक्ष्यामि शुभमाननम्। भ्रातुः पद्मपलाशाक्षं न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति।।2.98.7।।
transliteration: yāvanna candrasaṅkāśaṃ drakṣyāmi śubhamānanam| bhrātuḥ padmapalāśākṣaṃ na me śāntirbhaviṣyati
translation: चन्द्रसङ्काशम् radiant as the Moon, पद्मपलाशाक्षम् eyes resembling lotuspetals, भ्रातुः brother Rama, शुभम् auspicious, आननम् face, यावत् till such time, न द्रक्ष्यामि I do not see, मे to me, शान्तिः peace, न भविष्यति shall not come.
explanation: I shall not attain peace until I see my brother, Rama whose auspicious countenance looks radiant as the Moon and whose eyes as lotuspetals.

shloka_text: यावन्न चरणौ भ्रातुः पार्थिवव्यञ्जनान्वितौ। शिरसा धारयिष्यामि न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति।।2.98.8।।
transliteration: yāvanna caraṇau bhrātuḥ pārthivavyañjanānvitau| śirasā dhārayiṣyāmi na me śāntirbhaviṣyati
translation: भ्रातुः brother's, पार्थिवव्यञ्जनान्वितौ bearing the signs of royalty, चरणौ feet, यावत् till such time, शिरसा with the head, न धारयिष्यामि I will not carry, मे to me, शान्ति: peace, न भविष्यति  shall not come.
explanation: Peace shall not come to me until I hold on my head the feet of my brother, the insignia of royalty.

shloka_text: यावन्न राज्ये राज्यार्हः पितृपैतामहे स्थितः। अभिषेकजलक्लिन्नो न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति।।2.98.9।।
transliteration: yāvanna rājye rājyārhaḥ pitṛpaitāmahe sthitaḥ| abhiṣekajalaklinno na me śāntirbhaviṣyati
translation: राज्यार्हः one who is worthy of this kingdom, अभिषेकजलक्लिन्नः wet with the holy waters of consecration, पितृपैतामहे pertaining to our father and forefathers, राज्ये in the kingdom, यावत् till such time, न स्थितः is not established, मे my, शान्तिः peace, न भविष्यति shall not attain.
explanation: I shall not attain peace until Rama, who is worthy of this kingdom, is sprinkled with the holy water of coronation and assumes the ancestral kingdom.

shloka_text: सिद्धार्थः खलु सौमित्रिर्यश्चन्द्रविमलोपमम्। मुखं पश्यति रामस्य राजीवाक्षं महाद्युति।।2.98.10।।
transliteration: siddhārthaḥ khalu saumitriryaścandravimalopamam| mukhaṃ paśyati rāmasya rājīvākṣaṃ mahādyuti
translation: यः who, चन्द्रविमलोपमम् like the spotless Moon, राजीवाक्षम् whose eyes resemble red lotuses, महाद्युति of great effulgence, रामस्य Rama's, मुखम् countenance, पश्यति beholds, सौमित्रिः Lakshmana, सिद्दार्थः खलु blessed indeed.
explanation: Lakshmana, one who beholds the highly effulgent countenance of Rama, resembling the spotless Moon and whose eyes resemble red lotuses, is blessed indeed

shloka_text: कृतकृत्या महाभागा वैदेही जनकात्मजा। भर्तारं सागरान्तायाः पृथिव्या यानुगच्छति।।2.98.11।।
transliteration: kṛtakṛtyā mahābhāgā vaidehī janakātmajā| bhartāraṃ sāgarāntāyāḥ pṛthivyā yānugacchati
translation: या that Sita, सागरान्तायाः bounded by the ocean, पृथिव्याः of the earth, भर्तारम् Rama as lord, अनुगच्छति who is following, महाभागा illustrious lady, जनकात्मजा daughter of Janaka, वैदेही princess of Videha (Sita), कृतकृत्या has accomplished her purpose.
explanation: Sita, the illustrious daughter of Janaka and princess of Videha, has accomplished her purpose by following Rama, the lord of this earth bounded by the ocean.

shloka_text: सुभगश्चित्रकूटोऽसौ गिरिराजोपमो गिरिः। यस्मिन्वसति काकुत्स्थः कुबेर इव नन्दने।।2.98.12।।
transliteration: subhagaścitrakūṭo'sau girirājopamo giriḥ| yasminvasati kākutsthaḥ kubera iva nandane
translation: काकुत्स्थ: Rama, यस्मिन् on which, कुबेरः Kubera, the lord of wealth, नन्दने इव like in the Nandana garden, वसति staying, असौ such, गिरिराजोपमः comparable to the king of the mountains, Himavan, चित्रकूटः गिरिः Chitrakuta mountain, सुभगः is fortunate.
explanation: Like Kubera in the Nandana garden, Rama lives here on mount Chitrakuta which is indeed blessed like the Himalaya, king of the mountains.

shloka_text: कृतकार्यमिदं दुर्गं वनं व्यालनिषेवितम्। यदध्यास्ते महातेजा राम श्शस्त्रभृतां वरः।।2.98.13।।
transliteration: kṛtakāryamidaṃ durgaṃ vanaṃ vyālaniṣevitam| yadadhyāste mahātejā rāma śśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
translation: शस्त्रभृताम् among those who wield weapons, वरः the foremost, महातेजाः most radiant, रामः Rama, यत् that, अध्यास्ते is dwelling, व्यालनिषेवितम् inhabited by wild animals, दुर्गम् inaccessible, इदं वनम् this forest, कृतकार्यम् accomplished its task.
explanation: Fortunate is this inaccessible forest which is inhabited by wild animals to have become the dwelling place of the most radiant Rama, the foremost among the wielders of weapons.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा भरतः पुरषर्षभः। पद्भ्यामेव महाबाहुः प्रविवेश महाद्वनम्।।2.98.14।।
transliteration: evamuktvā mahātejā bharataḥ puraṣarṣabhaḥ| padbhyāmeva mahābāhuḥ praviveśa mahādvanam
translation: महातेजा: a man of great radiance, पुरुषर्षभः best of men, महाबाहुः mightyarmed, भरतः Bharata, एवम् in this way, उक्त्वा having said, महत् great, वनम् forest, पद्भ्यामेव on foot alone, प्रविवेश entered.
explanation: Having said thus, the best of men, mightyarmed and highly energetic Bharata entered the great forest on foot.

shloka_text: स तानि द्रुमजालानि जातानि गिरिसानुषु। पुष्पिताग्राणि मध्येन जगाम वदतां वरः।।2.98.15।।
transliteration: sa tāni drumajālāni jātāni girisānuṣu| puṣpitāgrāṇi madhyena jagāma vadatāṃ varaḥ
translation: वदताम् among the eloquent, वर: best, सः that, गिरिसानुषु on mountain slopes, जातानि growing, पुष्पिताग्राणि tops of trees in bloom, तानि those, द्रुमजालानि मध्येन through the midst of multitude of trees, जगाम went.
explanation: Bharata, the best among the eloquent, made his way amidst multitude of trees grown on mountain slopes with their tops in full bloom.

shloka_text: स गिरेश्चित्रकूटस्य सालमासाद्य पुष्पितम्। रामाश्रमगतस्याग्नेर्ददर्श ध्वजमुच्छ्रितम्।।2.98.16।।
transliteration: sa gireścitrakūṭasya sālamāsādya puṣpitam| rāmāśramagatasyāgnerdadarśa dhvajamucchritam
translation: सः that, चित्रकूटस्य गिरेः atop Chitrakuta mountain, पुष्पितम् flowering, सालम् sala trees, असाद्य having reached, रामाश्रमगतस्य in Rama's hermitage, अग्नेः of the burning fire, उच्छ्रितं lofty, ध्वजम् banner of smoke, ददर्श beheld.
explanation: Having reached a flowering sala tree atop Chitrakuta mountain, he beheld a lofty banner of smoke rising from the fire burning in Rama's hermitage.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा भरत श्रीमान्मुमोद सह बान्धवः। अत्र राम इति ज्ञात्वा गतः पारमिवाम्भसः।।2.98.17।।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bharata śrīmānmumoda saha bāndhavaḥ| atra rāma iti jñātvā gataḥ pāramivāmbhasaḥ
translation: श्रीमान् the majestic, सह बान्धवः with relatives, भरतः Bharata, तम् that smoke, दृष्ट्वा having seen, रामः Rama, अत्र इति here he is, ज्ञात्वा having known, अम्भसः of waters, पारम् the other bank, गतः इव having reached, मुमोद rejoiced.
explanation: On seeing the smoke, majestic Bharata in the company of relatives concluded that Rama was staying there and rejoiced like a man who had reached the other bank of the river.

shloka_text: स चित्रकूटे तु गिरौ निशम्यव रामाश्रमं पुण्यजनोपपन्नम्। गुहेन सार्धं त्वरितो जगाम पुनर्निवेश्यैव चमूं महात्मा।।2.98.18।।
transliteration: sa citrakūṭe tu girau niśamyava rāmāśramaṃ puṇyajanopapannam| guhena sārdhaṃ tvarito jagāma punarniveśyaiva camūṃ mahātmā
translation: महात्मा the magnanimous one, सः that Bharata, चित्रकूटे गिरौ on Chitrakuta mountain, पुण्यजनोपपन्नम् inhabited by pious men, रामाश्रमम् Rama's hermitage, निशम्य having heard about, चमूम् the army, निवेश्यैव having camped at a distance, पुनः again, गुहेन सार्धम् with Guha, त्वरितः quickly, जगाम went.
explanation: Having heard of Rama's hermitage on the Chitrakuta mountain inhabited by pious men, magnanimous Bharata, commanded his army to stay at a distance, and quickly proceeded with Guha. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टनवतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetyeighth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: निविष्टायां तु सेनायामुत्सुको भरतस्तदा। जगाम भ्रातरं द्रष्टुं शत्रुघ्नमनुदर्शयन्।।2.99.1।।
transliteration: niviṣṭāyāṃ tu senāyāmutsuko bharatastadā| jagāma bhrātaraṃ draṣṭuṃ śatrughnamanudarśayan
translation: तदा then, सेनायाम् when the army, निविष्टायाम्  encamped, भरतः Bharata, उत्सुकः with eagerness, शत्रुघ्नम् Satrughna, अनुदर्शयन् showing, भ्रातरम् brother, द्रष्टुम् to see, जगाम went.
explanation: Eager to see his brother, Bharata encamped the army and set out showing the hermitage to Satrughna.
comments: Bharata sees Rama seated in the hermitage with matted hair and bark robes with Sita nearby -- Bharata's lamentation.

shloka_text: ऋषिं वसिष्ठं सन्दिश्य मातृ़र्मे शीघ्रमानय। इति त्वरितमग्रे स जगाम गुरुवत्सलः।।2.99.2।।
transliteration: ṛṣiṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ sandiśya mātṛ़rme śīghramānaya| iti tvaritamagre sa jagāma guruvatsalaḥ
translation: गुरुवत्सलः devoted towards elders, सः Bharata, मे my, मातृ़ः mothers, शीघ्रम् quickly, आनय bring, इति thus, ऋषिम् rishi, वसिष्ठम् Vasistha, सन्दिश्य having conveyed, त्वरितम् quickly, अग्रे ahead, जगाम proceeded.
explanation: Bharata, deeply devoted towards elders, indicated to sage Vasistha to bring along the mothers, and  proceeded ahead quickly.

shloka_text: सुमन्त्रस्त्वपि शत्रुघ्नमदूरादन्वपद्यत। रामदर्शनजस्तर्षो भरतस्येव तस्य च।।2.99.3।।
transliteration: sumantrastvapi śatrughnamadūrādanvapadyata| rāmadarśanajastarṣo bharatasyeva tasya ca
translation: सुमन्त्रस्त्वपि Sumantra on his part, शत्रुघ्नम् to Satrughna, अदूरात् not far from, अन्वपद्यत  followed, रामदर्शनजः arising from seeing Rama, तर्षः overeager, तस्य च for him also, भरतस्येव is like that of Bharata.
explanation: Sumantra, who was overeager, like Bharata, to see Rama, followed Satrughna who was not far from him.

shloka_text: गच्छन्नेवाथ भरतस्तापसालय संस्थिताम्। भ्रातुः पर्णकुटीं श्रीमानुटजं च ददर्श ह।। 2.99.4।।
transliteration: gacchannevātha bharatastāpasālaya saṃsthitām| bhrātuḥ parṇakuṭīṃ śrīmānuṭajaṃ ca dadarśa ha
translation: अथ thereafter, श्रीमान् the majestic one, भरतः Bharata, गच्छन्नेव while walking, तापसालयसंस्थिताम् situated like huts of hermits, भ्रातुः brother's, पर्णकुटीम् hut made of leaves, उटजं च thatched cottage, ददर्श ह beheld.
explanation: While walking, Bharata beheld a hut made of leaves looking like a hermit's cottage.

shloka_text: शालायास्त्वग्रत स्तस्या ददर्श भरत स्तदा। काष्ठानि चावभग्नानि पुष्पाण्युपचितानि च।।2.99.5।।
transliteration: śālāyāstvagrata stasyā dadarśa bharata stadā| kāṣṭhāni cāvabhagnāni puṣpāṇyupacitāni ca
translation: तदा then, भरतः Bharata, तस्याः शालायाः that leafy hut's, अग्रतः in front of, अवभग्नानि shattered, काष्ठानि logs of wood, उपचितानि plucked, पुष्पाणि च also flowers, ददर्श beheld.
explanation: In front of that hut Bharata beheld shattered logs of wood and also flowers plucked.

shloka_text: स लक्ष्मणस्य रामस्य ददर्शाऽश्रममीयुषः। कृतं वृक्षेष्वभिज्ञानं कुशचीरैः क्वचित्क्वचित्।।2.99.6।।
transliteration: sa lakṣmaṇasya rāmasya dadarśā'śramamīyuṣaḥ| kṛtaṃ vṛkṣeṣvabhijñānaṃ kuśacīraiḥ kvacitkvacit
translation: सः he, आश्रमम् hermitage, ईयुषः of a man proceeding towards, लक्ष्मणस्य Lakshmana's, रामस्य Rama's, क्वचित् क्वचित् here and there, वृक्षेषु on trees, कुशचीरैः with kusa grass and strips of bark, कृतम् rendered, अभिज्ञानम् as a sign to ascertain, ददर्श beheld.
explanation: Bharata beheld here and there knots of kusa grass and strips of bark tied on trees as signs to ascertain the way to the hermitage of Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: ददर्श वने तस्मिन्महत स्सञ्चयान्कृतान्। मृगाणां महिषाणां च करीषै शशीतकारणात्।।2.99.7।।
transliteration: dadarśa vane tasminmahata ssañcayānkṛtān| mṛgāṇāṃ mahiṣāṇāṃ ca karīṣai śaśītakāraṇāt
translation: सः that Bharata, तस्मिन् वने in that forest, शीतकारणात् due to cold, मृगाणाम् deer's, महिषाणां च also of buffaloes, करीषैः dried cakes of dung, कृतान् prepared, महतः large, सञ्चयान् heaps, ददर्श beheld.
explanation: He also beheld large heaps of dried cakes of dung of buffaloes and deer for use against cold in the forest.

shloka_text: गच्छन्नेव महाबाहुर्द्युतिमान्भरत स्तदा। शत्रुघ्नं चाब्रवीद्धृष्टस्तानमात्यांश्च सर्वशः।।2.99.8।।
transliteration: gacchanneva mahābāhurdyutimānbharata stadā| śatrughnaṃ cābravīddhṛṣṭastānamātyāṃśca sarvaśaḥ
translation: महाबाहुः longarmed, द्युतिमान् effulgent, भरतः Bharata, तदा then, गच्छन्नेव while going, हृष्टः rejoiced, शत्रुघ्नं च to Satrughna, सर्वशः all around, तान् those, अमात्यांश्च to the ministers, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Walking on, the longarmed, effulgent and delighted Bharata said to Satrughna and the ministers surrounding him:

shloka_text: मन्ये प्राप्ताः स्म तं देशं भरद्वाजो यमब्रवीत्। नातिदूरे हि मन्येऽहं नदीं मन्दाकिनीमितः।।2.99.9।।
transliteration: manye prāptāḥ sma taṃ deśaṃ bharadvājo yamabravīt| nātidūre hi manye'haṃ nadīṃ mandākinīmitaḥ
translation: यम् about which, भरद्वाजः Bharadwaja, अब्रवीत् had spoken, तं देशम् that region, प्राप्ताः स्म  we must have reached, मन्ये I think, मन्दाकिनीं नदीं Mandakini river, इतः from here, नातिदूरे not far, अहम् I, मन्ये think.
explanation: We must have reached the region about which Bharadwaja had spoken. I think river Mandakini is not far from here.

shloka_text: उच्चैर्बद्धानि चीराणि लक्ष्मणेन भवेदयम्। अभिज्ञानकृतः पन्था अकाले गन्तुमिच्छता।।2.99.10।।
transliteration: uccairbaddhāni cīrāṇi lakṣmaṇena bhavedayam| abhijñānakṛtaḥ panthā akāle gantumicchatā
translation: चीराणि long bark garments, उच्चैः on lofty places (trees), बद्धानि have been fastened, अयम् this, अकाले at odd times, गन्तुम् to move out, इच्छता wishing, लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, अभिज्ञानकृतः marks of identification, पन्थाः भवेत् it must have been the path.
explanation: Here are long bark garments fastened on lofty places as marks of identification left by Lakshmana, to locate the path at odd times which may be needed while going out.

shloka_text: इदं चोदात्तदन्तानां कुञ्जराणां तरस्विनाम्। शैलपार्श्वे परिक्रान्तमन्योन्यमभिगर्जताम्।।2.99.11।।
transliteration: idaṃ codāttadantānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tarasvinām| śailapārśve parikrāntamanyonyamabhigarjatām
translation: शैलपार्श्वे on the hillside, इदम् this, उदात्तदन्तानाम् of the largetusked, तरस्विनाम् swift अन्योन्यम् charging at one another, अभिगर्जताम् trumpeting, कुञ्जराणाम् elephants', परिक्रान्तम् place.
explanation: This must be the place on the hillside on which mighty tuskers wander about trumpeting and charging at one another.

shloka_text: यमेवाधातुमिच्छन्ति तापसा स्सततं वने। तस्यासौ दृश्यते धूम स्सङ्कुलः कृष्णवर्त्मनः।।2.99.12।।
transliteration: yamevādhātumicchanti tāpasā ssatataṃ vane| tasyāsau dṛśyate dhūma ssaṅkulaḥ kṛṣṇavartmanaḥ
translation: वने in the forest, तापसाः ascetics, सततम् always, यमेव only whom, आधातुम् to maintain, इच्छन्ति wishing, तस्य that, कृष्णवर्त्मनः of blacktrailed fires, असौ this, सङ्कुलः thick, धूमः smoke, दृश्यते is seen.
explanation: Here is the thick smoke emanating from the blacktrailed fire maintained perpetually by the ascetics living in the forest.

shloka_text: अत्राहं पुरुषव्याघ्रं गुरुसत्कारकारिणम्। आर्यं द्रक्ष्यामि संहृष्टो महर्षिमिव राघवम्।।2.99.13।।
transliteration: atrāhaṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ gurusatkārakāriṇam| āryaṃ drakṣyāmi saṃhṛṣṭo maharṣimiva rāghavam
translation: अहम् I, पुरुषव्याघ्रम् the best of men, Rama, गुरुसत्कारकारिणम् rendering great hospitality, आर्यम् venerable, महर्षिमिव like a great sage, राघवम् to Rama, संहृष्टः with a delighted heart, अत्र here, द्रक्ष्यामि I shall see.
explanation: I shall see here with a delighted heart the venerable Rama, the best of men, who renders great hospitality (to elders) and who resembles a maharshi.

shloka_text: अथ गत्वा मुहूर्तन्तु चित्रकूटं स राघवः। मन्दाकिनीमनुप्राप्तस्तं जनं चेदमब्रवीत्।।2.99.14।।
transliteration: atha gatvā muhūrtantu citrakūṭaṃ sa rāghavaḥ| mandākinīmanuprāptastaṃ janaṃ cedamabravīt
translation: अथ thereafter, सः राघवः that Bharata, चित्रकूटम् towards Chitrakuta (mountain), मुहूर्तम् for a moment, गत्वा having gone, मन्दाकिनीम् river Mandakini, अनुप्राप्तः having reached, तं जनम्  to those people, इदम् those words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Bharata walked for a short distance towards mount Chitrkuta when he reached river Mandakini. And then said to his ministers:

shloka_text: जगत्यां पुरषव्याघ्र आस्ते वीरासने रतः। जनेन्द्रो निर्जनं प्राप्य धिङ्मे जन्म सजीवितम्।।2.99.15।।
transliteration: jagatyāṃ puraṣavyāghra āste vīrāsane rataḥ| janendro nirjanaṃ prāpya dhiṅme janma sajīvitam
translation: जनेन्द्रः the lord of men, पुरषव्याघ्रः a tiger among men, निर्जनम् a place devoid of people, प्राप्य having reached, वीरासने in 'heroic' posture, रतः remaining, जगत्याम् on the ground, आस्ते is sitting, मे my, सजीवितम् life, जन्म birth, धिक् fie upon.
explanation: Rama, the lord of men, a tiger among men, is sitting on the ground in a 'heroic' (yogic) posture in this secluded forest. O fie upon my birth and my life

shloka_text: मत्कृते व्यसनं प्राप्तो लोकनाथो महाद्युतिः। सर्वान्कामान्परित्यज्य वने वसति राघवः।।2.99.16।।
transliteration: matkṛte vyasanaṃ prāpto lokanātho mahādyutiḥ| sarvānkāmānparityajya vane vasati rāghavaḥ
translation: लोकनाथः lord of the world, महाद्युतिः effulgent, राघवः Rama, मत्कृते on my account, व्यसनम्  calamity, प्राप्त: has faced, सर्वान् all, कामान् desires, परित्यज्य renouncing, वने in the forest, वसति is living.
explanation: Effulgent Rama, the lord of the world, had to renounce all desires and undergo this calamity of living in the forest on my account.

shloka_text: इति लोकसमाक्रुष्टः पादेष्वद्य प्रसादयन्। रामस्य निपतिष्यामि सीताया लक्ष्मणस्य च।।2.99.17।।
transliteration: iti lokasamākruṣṭaḥ pādeṣvadya prasādayan| rāmasya nipatiṣyāmi sītāyā lakṣmaṇasya ca
translation: इति thus, लोकसमाक्रुष्टः reviled by the world, अद्य now, प्रसादयन् seeking the grace, रामस्य Rama's, सीतायाः Sita's, लक्ष्मणस्य च and Lakshmana's, पादेषु at the feet, निपतिष्यामि shall fall down.
explanation: Reviled by the world, I shall now fall at the feet of Sita, Rama and Lakshmana seeking their grace.

shloka_text: एवं संविलपं स्तस्मिन्वने दशरथात्मजः। ददर्श महतीं पुण्यां पर्णशालां मनोरमाम्।।2.99.18।। सालतालाश्वकर्णानां पर्णैर्बहुभिरावृताम्। विशालां मृदुभिस्तीर्णां कुशैर्वेदिमिवाध्वरे।।2.99.19।। शक्रायुधनिकाशैश्च कार्मुकैर्भारसाधनैः। रुक्मपृष्ठैर्महासारै श्शोभितां शत्रुबाधकैः।।2.99.20।। अर्क रश्मि प्रतीकाशैर्घोरैस्तूणीगतैश्शरैः। शोभितां दीप्तवदनै स्सर्पैर्भोगवतीमिव।।2.99.21।। महारजतवासोभ्यामसिभ्यां च विराजिताम्। रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्यां चर्मभ्यां चापि शोभिताम्।।2.99.22।। गोधाङ्गुळित्रैरासक्तैश्चित्रैः काञ्चनभूषितैः। अरिसंघैरनाधृष्यां मृगै स्सिंहगुहा मिव।।2.99.23।।
transliteration: evaṃ saṃvilapaṃ stasminvane daśarathātmajaḥ| dadarśa mahatīṃ puṇyāṃ parṇaśālāṃ manoramām sālatālāśvakarṇānāṃ parṇairbahubhirāvṛtām| viśālāṃ mṛdubhistīrṇāṃ kuśairvedimivādhvare śakrāyudhanikāśaiśca kārmukairbhārasādhanaiḥ| rukmapṛṣṭhairmahāsārai śśobhitāṃ śatrubādhakaiḥ arka raśmi pratīkāśairghoraistūṇīgataiśśaraiḥ| śobhitāṃ dīptavadanai ssarpairbhogavatīmiva mahārajatavāsobhyāmasibhyāṃ ca virājitām| rukmabinduvicitrābhyāṃ carmabhyāṃ cāpi śobhitām godhāṅguḻitrairāsaktaiścitraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ| arisaṃghairanādhṛṣyāṃ mṛgai ssiṃhaguhā miva
translation: एवम् in that way, संविलपन् lamenting, दशरथात्मजः son of Dasaratha (Bharata), तस्मिन् वने in that forest, महतीम् great, पुण्याम् sacred, मनोरमाम् enchanting, सालतालाश्वकर्णानाम् of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees, बहुभिः by abundance of, मृदुभिः by soft, पर्णैः with leaves, आवृताम् covered, अध्वरे in the sacrifice, कुशैः with kusa grass, तीर्णाम् spread over, विशालाम् spacious, वेदिमिव like altar, शक्रायुधनिकाशैः resembling the thunderbolt of Indra, भारसाधनैः capable of achieving targets, रुक्मपृष्ठैः goldplated, महासारै: by powerful, शत्रुबाधकैः oppressing the enemies, कार्मुकैः with bows, शोभिताम् glittering, सर्पैः with serpents, भोगवतीम् इव like Bhogavati, अर्करश्मिप्रतीकाशैः like the rays of the Sun, घोरैः by dreadful, दीप्तवदनैः with tips blazing, तूणीगतैः stored in quivers, शरैः with arrows, शोभिताम् adorned with, महारजतवासोभ्याम् scabbards made of silver, असिभ्याम् with a pair of swords, विराजिताम् was shining, रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्याम् of different colours with golden spots, चर्मभ्याम् with shields, ताम् all of them, काञ्चनभूषितैः decorated with gold, चित्रैः different kinds, आसक्तै: hung, गोधाङ्गुलित्रैः fingerguards made of skin of iguana, मृगैः with the deer, सिंहगुहामिव like the cave of a lion, अरिसङ्घै: with hordes of enemies, अनाधृष्याम् impregnable, पर्णशालाम् hut made of leave, तस्मिन् वने in that forest, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.

shloka_text: एवं संविलपं स्तस्मिन्वने दशरथात्मजः। ददर्श महातीं पुण्यां पर्णशालां मनोरमाम्।।2.99.18।। सालतालाश्वकर्णानां पर्णैर्बहुभिरावृताम्। विशालां मृदुभिस्तीर्णां कुशैर्वेदिमिवाध्वरे।।2.99.19।। शक्रायुधनिकाशैश्च कार्मुकैर्भारसाधनैः। रुक्मपृष्ठैर्महासारै श्शोभितां शत्रुबाधकैः।।2.99.20।। अर्क रश्मि प्रतीकाशैर्घोरैस्तूणीगतैश्शरैः। शोभितां दीप्तवदनै स्सर्पैर्भोगवतीमिव।।2.99.21।। महारजतवासोभ्यामसिभ्यां च विराजिताम्। रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्यां चर्मभ्यां चापि शोभिताम्।।2.99.22।। गोधाङ्गुळित्रैरासक्तैश्चित्रैः काञ्चनभूषितैः। अरिसंघैरनाधृष्यां मृगै स्सिंहगुहा मिव।।2.99.23।।
transliteration: evaṃ saṃvilapaṃ stasminvane daśarathātmajaḥ| dadarśa mahātīṃ puṇyāṃ parṇaśālāṃ manoramām sālatālāśvakarṇānāṃ parṇairbahubhirāvṛtām| viśālāṃ mṛdubhistīrṇāṃ kuśairvedimivādhvare śakrāyudhanikāśaiśca kārmukairbhārasādhanaiḥ| rukmapṛṣṭhairmahāsārai śśobhitāṃ śatrubādhakaiḥ arka raśmi pratīkāśairghoraistūṇīgataiśśaraiḥ| śobhitāṃ dīptavadanai ssarpairbhogavatīmiva mahārajatavāsobhyāmasibhyāṃ ca virājitām| rukmabinduvicitrābhyāṃ carmabhyāṃ cāpi śobhitām godhāṅguḻitrairāsaktaiścitraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ| arisaṃghairanādhṛṣyāṃ mṛgai ssiṃhaguhā miva
translation: एवम् in that way, संविलपन् lamenting, दशरथात्मजः son of Dasaratha (Bharata), तस्मिन् वने in that forest, महतीम् great, पुण्याम् sacred, मनोरमाम् enchanting, सालतालाश्वकर्णानाम् of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees, बहुभिः by abundance of, मृदुभिः by soft, पर्णैः with leaves, आवृताम् covered, अध्वरे in the sacrifice, कुशैः with kusa grass, तीर्णाम् spread over, विशालाम् spacious, वेदिमिव like altar, शक्रायुधनिकाशैः resembling the thunderbolt of Indra, भारसाधनैः capable of achieving targets, रुक्मपृष्ठैः goldplated, महासारै: by powerful, शत्रुबाधकैः oppressing the enemies, कार्मुकैः with bows, शोभिताम् glittering, सर्पैः with serpents, भोगवतीम् इव like Bhogavati, अर्करश्मिप्रतीकाशैः like the rays of the Sun, घोरैः by dreadful, दीप्तवदनैः with tips blazing, तूणीगतैः stored in quivers, शरैः with arrows, शोभिताम् adorned with, महारजतवासोभ्याम् scabbards made of silver, असिभ्याम् with a pair of swords, विराजिताम् was shining, रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्याम् of different colours with golden spots, चर्मभ्याम् with shields, ताम् all of them, काञ्चनभूषितैः decorated with gold, चित्रैः different kinds, आसक्तै: hung, गोधाङ्गुलित्रैः fingerguards made of skin of iguana, मृगैः with the deer, सिंहगुहामिव like the cave of a lion, अरिसङ्घै: with hordes of enemies, अनाधृष्याम् impregnable, पर्णशालाम् hut made of leave, तस्मिन् वने in that forest, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.
