shloka_text: एवं संविलपं स्तस्मिन्वने दशरथात्मजः। ददर्श महातीं पुण्यां पर्णशालां मनोरमाम्।।2.99.18।। सालतालाश्वकर्णानां पर्णैर्बहुभिरावृताम्। विशालां मृदुभिस्तीर्णां कुशैर्वेदिमिवाध्वरे।।2.99.19।। शक्रायुधनिकाशैश्च कार्मुकैर्भारसाधनैः। रुक्मपृष्ठैर्महासारै श्शोभितां शत्रुबाधकैः।।2.99.20।। अर्क रश्मि प्रतीकाशैर्घोरैस्तूणीगतैश्शरैः। शोभितां दीप्तवदनै स्सर्पैर्भोगवतीमिव।।2.99.21।। महारजतवासोभ्यामसिभ्यां च विराजिताम्। रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्यां चर्मभ्यां चापि शोभिताम्।।2.99.22।। गोधाङ्गुळित्रैरासक्तैश्चित्रैः काञ्चनभूषितैः। अरिसंघैरनाधृष्यां मृगै स्सिंहगुहा मिव।।2.99.23।।
transliteration: evaṃ saṃvilapaṃ stasminvane daśarathātmajaḥ| dadarśa mahātīṃ puṇyāṃ parṇaśālāṃ manoramām sālatālāśvakarṇānāṃ parṇairbahubhirāvṛtām| viśālāṃ mṛdubhistīrṇāṃ kuśairvedimivādhvare śakrāyudhanikāśaiśca kārmukairbhārasādhanaiḥ| rukmapṛṣṭhairmahāsārai śśobhitāṃ śatrubādhakaiḥ arka raśmi pratīkāśairghoraistūṇīgataiśśaraiḥ| śobhitāṃ dīptavadanai ssarpairbhogavatīmiva mahārajatavāsobhyāmasibhyāṃ ca virājitām| rukmabinduvicitrābhyāṃ carmabhyāṃ cāpi śobhitām godhāṅguḻitrairāsaktaiścitraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ| arisaṃghairanādhṛṣyāṃ mṛgai ssiṃhaguhā miva
translation: एवम् in that way, संविलपन् lamenting, दशरथात्मजः son of Dasaratha (Bharata), तस्मिन् वने in that forest, महतीम् great, पुण्याम् sacred, मनोरमाम् enchanting, सालतालाश्वकर्णानाम् of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees, बहुभिः by abundance of, मृदुभिः by soft, पर्णैः with leaves, आवृताम् covered, अध्वरे in the sacrifice, कुशैः with kusa grass, तीर्णाम् spread over, विशालाम् spacious, वेदिमिव like altar, शक्रायुधनिकाशैः resembling the thunderbolt of Indra, भारसाधनैः capable of achieving targets, रुक्मपृष्ठैः goldplated, महासारै: by powerful, शत्रुबाधकैः oppressing the enemies, कार्मुकैः with bows, शोभिताम् glittering, सर्पैः with serpents, भोगवतीम् इव like Bhogavati, अर्करश्मिप्रतीकाशैः like the rays of the Sun, घोरैः by dreadful, दीप्तवदनैः with tips blazing, तूणीगतैः stored in quivers, शरैः with arrows, शोभिताम् adorned with, महारजतवासोभ्याम् scabbards made of silver, असिभ्याम् with a pair of swords, विराजिताम् was shining, रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्याम् of different colours with golden spots, चर्मभ्याम् with shields, ताम् all of them, काञ्चनभूषितैः decorated with gold, चित्रैः different kinds, आसक्तै: hung, गोधाङ्गुलित्रैः fingerguards made of skin of iguana, मृगैः with the deer, सिंहगुहामिव like the cave of a lion, अरिसङ्घै: with hordes of enemies, अनाधृष्याम् impregnable, पर्णशालाम् hut made of leave, तस्मिन् वने in that forest, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.

shloka_text: प्रागुदक्प्रवणां वेदिं विशालां दीप्तपावकाम्। ददर्श भरतस्तत्र पुण्यां रामनिवेशने।।2.99.24।।
transliteration: prāgudakpravaṇāṃ vediṃ viśālāṃ dīptapāvakām| dadarśa bharatastatra puṇyāṃ rāmaniveśane
translation: भरतः Bharata, तत्र there, रामनिवेशने at Rama's residence, प्रागुदक्प्रवणाम् sloping to the northeast, विशालाम् spacious, दीप्तपावकाम् having flaming fire, पुण्याम् sacred, वेदिम् altar, ददर्श beheld.
explanation: Bharata beheld at Rama's residence a sacred and spacious altar sloping to the northeast, with a burning fire upon it.

shloka_text: निरीक्ष्य स मुहूर्तं तु ददर्श भरतो गुरुम्। उटजे राममासीनं जटामण्डलधारिणम्।।2.99.25।।
transliteration: nirīkṣya sa muhūrtaṃ tu dadarśa bharato gurum| uṭaje rāmamāsīnaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam
translation: सः भरतः that Bharata, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, निरीक्ष्य looking around, उटजे in the cottage, आसीनम् seated, जटामण्डलधारिणम् wearing matted locks of hair, गुरुम् esteemed brother, रामम् Rama, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Bharata looked around for a moment and saw his esteemed brother Rama seated in that thatched cottage wearing matted locks of hair.

shloka_text: तं तु कृष्णाजिनधरं चीरवल्कलवाससम्। ददर्श राममासीनमभितः पावकोपमम्।।2.99.26।। सिंहस्कन्धं महाबाहुं पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम्। पृथिव्यास्सागरान्तायाः भर्तारं धर्मचारिणम्।।2.99.27।। उपविष्टं महाबाहुं ब्रह्माणमिव शाश्वतम्। स्थण्डिले दर्भसंस्तीर्णे सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च।।2.99.28।।
transliteration: taṃ tu kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ cīravalkalavāsasam| dadarśa rāmamāsīnamabhitaḥ pāvakopamam siṃhaskandhaṃ mahābāhuṃ puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇam| pṛthivyāssāgarāntāyāḥ bhartāraṃ dharmacāriṇam upaviṣṭaṃ mahābāhuṃ brahmāṇamiva śāśvatam| sthaṇḍile darbhasaṃstīrṇe sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca
translation: कृष्णाजिनधरम् clad in antelope skin, चीरवल्कलवासम् dressed in garments made of bark, अभितः near him, पावकोपमम् resembling blazing fire, आसीनम् seated, सिंहस्कन्दम् with his  shoulders like that of a lion, महाबाहुम् longarmed, पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम् with eyes like white lotus, सागरान्तायाः bounded by the ocean, पृथिव्याः of the earth, भर्तारम् the lord, धर्मचारिणम् follower of righteouness, तं रामम् that Rama, ददर्श saw, महाबाहुम् of longarmed one, शाश्वतम् eternal, ब्रह्माणमिव like the creator Brahma, सीतया with Sita, लक्ष्मणेन along with Lakshmana, दर्भसंस्तीर्णे on the ground strewn with darbha grass, स्थण्डिले on the bare ground, उपविष्टम् seated.
explanation: He saw Rama, lord of the oceanbound earth, seated like blazing fire, clad in antelope skin and garment of bark, with long arms and shoulders like a lion and eyes like white lotuses. The mightyarmed warrior seemed like Brahma, the creator and the eternal, protector of righteousness. Accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana Rama sat on the bare ground strewn with darbha grass.

shloka_text: तं तु कृष्णाजिनधरं चीरवल्कलवाससम्। ददर्श राममासीनमभितः पावकोपमम्।।2.99.26।। सिंहस्कन्धं महाबाहुं पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम्। पृथिव्यास्सागरान्तायाः भर्तारं धर्मचारिणम्।।2.99.27।। उपविष्टं महाबाहुं ब्रह्माणमिव शाश्वतम्। स्थण्डिले दर्भसंस्तीर्णे सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च।।2.99.28।।
transliteration: taṃ tu kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ cīravalkalavāsasam| dadarśa rāmamāsīnamabhitaḥ pāvakopamam siṃhaskandhaṃ mahābāhuṃ puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇam| pṛthivyāssāgarāntāyāḥ bhartāraṃ dharmacāriṇam upaviṣṭaṃ mahābāhuṃ brahmāṇamiva śāśvatam| sthaṇḍile darbhasaṃstīrṇe sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca
translation: कृष्णाजिनधरम् clad in antelope skin, चीरवल्कलवासम् dressed in garments made of bark, अभितः near him, पावकोपमम् resembling blazing fire, आसीनम् seated, सिंहस्कन्दम् with his  shoulders like that of a lion, महाबाहुम् longarmed, पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम् with eyes like white lotus, सागरान्तायाः bounded by the ocean, पृथिव्याः of the earth, भर्तारम् the lord, धर्मचारिणम् follower of righteouness, तं रामम् that Rama, ददर्श saw, महाबाहुम् of longarmed one, शाश्वतम् eternal, ब्रह्माणमिव like the creator Brahma, सीतया with Sita, लक्ष्मणेन along with Lakshmana, दर्भसंस्तीर्णे on the ground strewn with darbha grass, स्थण्डिले on the bare ground, उपविष्टम् seated.
explanation: He saw Rama, lord of the oceanbound earth, seated like blazing fire, clad in antelope skin and garment of bark, with long arms and shoulders like a lion and eyes like white lotuses. The mightyarmed warrior seemed like Brahma, the creator and the eternal, protector of righteousness. Accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana Rama sat on the bare ground strewn with darbha grass.

shloka_text: तं तु कृष्णाजिनधरं चीरवल्कलवाससम्। ददर्श राममासीनमभितः पावकोपमम्।।2.99.26।। सिंहस्कन्धं महाबाहुं पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम्। पृथिव्यास्सागरान्तायाः भर्तारं धर्मचारिणम्।।2.99.27।। उपविष्टं महाबाहुं ब्रह्माणमिव शाश्वतम्। स्थण्डिले दर्भसंस्तीर्णे सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च।।2.99.28।।
transliteration: taṃ tu kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ cīravalkalavāsasam| dadarśa rāmamāsīnamabhitaḥ pāvakopamam siṃhaskandhaṃ mahābāhuṃ puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇam| pṛthivyāssāgarāntāyāḥ bhartāraṃ dharmacāriṇam upaviṣṭaṃ mahābāhuṃ brahmāṇamiva śāśvatam| sthaṇḍile darbhasaṃstīrṇe sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca
translation: कृष्णाजिनधरम् clad in antelope skin, चीरवल्कलवासम् dressed in garments made of bark, अभितः near him, पावकोपमम् resembling blazing fire, आसीनम् seated, सिंहस्कन्दम् with his  shoulders like that of a lion, महाबाहुम् longarmed, पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम् with eyes like white lotus, सागरान्तायाः bounded by the ocean, पृथिव्याः of the earth, भर्तारम् the lord, धर्मचारिणम् follower of righteouness, तं रामम् that Rama, ददर्श saw, महाबाहुम् of longarmed one, शाश्वतम् eternal, ब्रह्माणमिव like the creator Brahma, सीतया with Sita, लक्ष्मणेन along with Lakshmana, दर्भसंस्तीर्णे on the ground strewn with darbha grass, स्थण्डिले on the bare ground, उपविष्टम् seated.
explanation: He saw Rama, lord of the oceanbound earth, seated like blazing fire, clad in antelope skin and garment of bark, with long arms and shoulders like a lion and eyes like white lotuses. The mightyarmed warrior seemed like Brahma, the creator and the eternal, protector of righteousness. Accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana Rama sat on the bare ground strewn with darbha grass.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा भरत श्श्रीमान् दुःखशोकपरिप्लुतः। अभ्यधावत धर्मात्मा भरतः कैकेयी सुतः।।2.99.29।।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bharata śśrīmān duḥkhaśokapariplutaḥ| abhyadhāvata dharmātmā bharataḥ kaikeyī sutaḥ
translation: श्रीमान् majestic, भरतः Bharata, तम् that Rama, दृष्ट्वा having seen, दुःखशोकपरिप्लुतः overwhelmed with grief and distress, धर्मात्मा righteous, कैकयीसुतः son of Kaikeyi, भरतः Bharata, अभ्यधावत ran towards him.
explanation: Beholding Rama, Bharata the majestic and righteous son of Kaikeyi overwhelmed with grief and distress rushed towards him.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वैव विललापाऽर्तो बाष्पसन्दिग्धया गिरा। अशक्नुवन् धारयितुं धैर्याद्वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.99.30।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvaiva vilalāpā'rto bāṣpasandigdhayā girā| aśaknuvan dhārayituṃ dhairyādvacanamabravīt
translation: दृष्ट्वैव as soon as he saw, आर्तः anguished, बाष्पसन्दिग्धया choked with tears, गिरा with words, विललाप lamented, धैर्यात् with courage, धारयितुम् to restrain, अशक्नुवन् being unable, वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: On seeing Rama, Bharata could not control his grief with patience and lamented in great anguish and with words choked with tears said:

shloka_text: य स्संसदि प्रकृतिभिर्भवेद्युक्त उपासितुम्। वन्यैर्मृगैरुपासीन स्सोऽयमास्ते ममाग्रजः।।2.99.31।।
transliteration: ya ssaṃsadi prakṛtibhirbhavedyukta upāsitum| vanyairmṛgairupāsīna sso'yamāste mamāgrajaḥ
translation: यः he who, संसदि in the royal assembly, प्रकृतिभिः by ministers and other subjects, उपासितुम् to be attended upon, युक्तः one who deserves, भवेत् becomes, सः he, अयम् this, man, मम my, अग्रजः elder brother, वन्यैः wild, मृगैः by the beasts, उपासीनः आस्ते is being attended.
explanation: My elder brother who deserves to be attended by ministers and other subjects in the royal assembly sits here today in the forest surrounded by wild beasts.

shloka_text: वासोभिर्बहुसाहस्रैर्यो महात्मा पुरोचितः। मृगाजिने सोऽयमिह प्रवस्ते धर्ममाचरन्।।2.99.32।।
transliteration: vāsobhirbahusāhasrairyo mahātmā purocitaḥ| mṛgājine so'yamiha pravaste dharmamācaran
translation: यः महात्मा that magnanimous (Rama), पुरा formerly, बहुसाहस्रैः with many thousands, वासोभिः with clothes, उचितः was accustomed, सः such, अयम् now, धर्मम् righteousness, आचरन् practising, मृगाजिने two deer kins, प्रवस्ते is wearing.
explanation: Such magnanimous Rama, a follower of dharma, accustomed to be attired in  thousands of dresses in the past now clad in two deer skins, is practising righteousness.

shloka_text: अधारयद्यो विविधाश्चित्रास्सुमनसस्तदा। सोऽयं जटाभारमिमं वहते राघवः कथम्।।2.99.33।।
transliteration: adhārayadyo vividhāścitrāssumanasastadā| so'yaṃ jaṭābhāramimaṃ vahate rāghavaḥ katham
translation: यः that Rama, तदा then, विविधाः various, चित्राः colours, सुमनसः flowers, आधारयत् wore, सः such a man, अयं राघवः this Rama, इमं जटाभारम् the weight of matted hair, कथम् how, वहते is able to bear?
explanation: How is it that Rama who used to wear variegated flowers formerly, now bears these heavy matted locks?

shloka_text: यस्य यज्ञैर्यथादिष्टैर्युक्तो धर्मस्य सञ्चयः। शरीरक्लेशसम्भूतं स धर्मं परिमार्गते।।2.99.34।।
transliteration: yasya yajñairyathādiṣṭairyukto dharmasya sañcayaḥ| śarīrakleśasambhūtaṃ sa dharmaṃ parimārgate
translation: यथोद्विष्टैः in accordance with desire, यज्ञैः with sacrifices, यस्य to whom, धर्मस्य righteousness, सञ्चयः accumulation, युक्तः was quite possible, सः such Rama, शरीरक्लेशसंभूतम् rising due to mortification of body, धर्मम् righteouness, परिमार्गते is seeking.
explanation: That Rama, who in accordance with tradition deserves accredition of religious merit through sacrifices now seeks it through mortification of body.

shloka_text: चन्दनेन महार्हेण यस्याङ्गमुपसेवितम्। मलेन तस्याङ्गमिदं कथमार्यस्य सेव्यते।।2.99.35।।
transliteration: candanena mahārheṇa yasyāṅgamupasevitam| malena tasyāṅgamidaṃ kathamāryasya sevyate
translation: यस्य whose, अङ्गम् body, महार्हेण by highly valuable, चन्दनेन with sandal paste, उपसेवितम्  smeared, तस्य his, आर्यस्य esteemed brother's, इदम् अङ्गम् this body, मलेन with dirt, कथम् how, सेव्यते is being served?
explanation: How is it that the body of my venerable brother which was once smeared with expensive, fragrant sandal paste is now covered with dust?

shloka_text: मन्निमित्तमिदं दुःखं प्राप्तो रामः सुखोचितः। धिग्जीवितं नृशंसस्य मम लोकविगर्हितम्।।2.99.36।।
transliteration: mannimittamidaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpto rāmaḥ sukhocitaḥ| dhigjīvitaṃ nṛśaṃsasya mama lokavigarhitam
translation: सुखोचितः accustomed to comforts, रामः Rama, मन्निमित्तम् on my account, इदं दुःखम् this misfortune, प्राप्तः has obtained, नृशंसस्य of a cruel one, मम my, लोकविगर्हितम् condemned by the world, जीवितम् धिक् fie on my life.
explanation: It is on my account that Rama who was accustomed to all comforts has fallen into this misfortune. Fie on my life of cruelty which is condemned by the world.

shloka_text: इत्येवं विलपन्दीनः प्रस्विन्नमुखपङ्कजः। पादावप्राप्य रामस्य पपात भरतो रुदन्।।2.99.37।।
transliteration: ityevaṃ vilapandīnaḥ prasvinnamukhapaṅkajaḥ| pādāvaprāpya rāmasya papāta bharato rudan
translation: भरतः Bharata, दीनः miserable, प्रस्विन्नमुखपङ्कजः lotuslike countenance full of sweat, इत्येवम् thus, विलपन् lamenting, रामस्य Rama's, पादौ feet, अप्राप्य before reaching, रुदन् crying in distress, पपात fell down.
explanation: Thus Bharata lamented in misery and with his lotuslike countenanace sweating  before reaching Rama's feet fell down, crying in distress.

shloka_text: दुःखाभितप्तो भरतो राजपुत्रो महाबलः। उक्त्वाऽर्येति सकृद्दीनं पुनर्नोवाच किञ्चन।।2.99.38।।
transliteration: duḥkhābhitapto bharato rājaputro mahābalaḥ| uktvā'ryeti sakṛddīnaṃ punarnovāca kiñcana
translation: महाबलः mighty, राजपुत्रः prince, भरतः Bharata, दुःखाभितप्तः oppressed with grief, आर्य इति saying o Arya (venerable one), सकृत् once, दीनम् in distress, उक्त्वा having said, पुनः again, किञ्चन anything, नोवाच could not speak.
explanation: Mighty prince Bharata, oppressed with grief, could only say, O Arya (venerable one) And in distress could not speak any more.

shloka_text: बाष्पाभिहतकण्ठश्च प्रेक्ष्य रामं यशस्विनम्। आर्येत्येवाभिसङ्क्रुश्य व्याहर्तुं नाशकत्तदा।।2.99.39।।
transliteration: bāṣpābhihatakaṇṭhaśca prekṣya rāmaṃ yaśasvinam| āryetyevābhisaṅkruśya vyāhartuṃ nāśakattadā
translation: यशस्विनम् glorious, रामम् Rama, प्रेक्ष्य on seeing, बाष्पाभिहतकण्ठश्च with choked throat, अथ then, आर्येत्येव O Arya, सङ्क्रुश्य crying out, तदा thereafter, व्याहर्तुम् to talk further, नाशकत् was not able.
explanation: As he beheld the glorious Rama, with his throat choken with tears, he cried out, O Arya (venerable one) and thereafter, was unable to speak any more.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नश्चापि रामस्य ववन्दे चरणौ रुदन्। तावुभौ स समालिङ्ग्य रामश्चाश्रूण्यवर्तयत्।।2.99.40।।
transliteration: śatrughnaścāpi rāmasya vavande caraṇau rudan| tāvubhau sa samāliṅgya rāmaścāśrūṇyavartayat
translation: शत्रुघ्नश्चापि Satrughna too, रुदन् weeping, रामस्य Rama's, चरणौ feet, ववन्दे prostrated, सः रामश्च that Rama also, तौ उभौ the two of them, समालिङ्ग्य having embraced, अश्रूणि  tears, अवर्तयत् shed.
explanation: Satrughna also prostrated himself at the feet of tearful Rama who embraced both of them.

shloka_text: ततस्सुमन्त्रेण गुहेन चैव समीयतु राजसुतावरण्ये। दिवाकरश्चैव निशाकरश्च यथाऽम्बरे शुक्रबृहस्पतिभ्याम्।।2.99.41।।
transliteration: tatassumantreṇa guhena caiva samīyatu rājasutāvaraṇye| divākaraścaiva niśākaraśca yathā'mbare śukrabṛhaspatibhyām
translation: ततः therafter, अरण्ये in the forest, राजसुतौ the princes (Rama and Lakshmana), अम्बरे in the sky, दिवाकरश्चैव Sun, निशाकरश्च Moon, शुक्रबृहस्पतिभ्याम् with Sukra and Brihaspathi, यथा similarly, सुमन्त्रेण with Sumantra, गुहेन चैव with Guha, समीयतुः met.
explanation: Thereafter, princes Rama and Lakshmana joined Sumantra and Guha in the forest like the Sun and the Moon meeting the planets Sukra and Brihaspati in the sky.

shloka_text: तान्पार्थिवान्वारणयूथपाभान्समागतां स्तत्र महत्यरण्ये। वनौकसस्तेऽपि समीक्ष्य सर्वेऽप्यश्रूण्यमुञ्चन्प्रविहाय हर्षम्।।2.99.42।।
transliteration: tānpārthivānvāraṇayūthapābhānsamāgatāṃ statra mahatyaraṇye| vanaukasaste'pi samīkṣya sarve'pyaśrūṇyamuñcanpravihāya harṣam
translation: ते सर्वे they all, वनौकसः inhabitants of the forest, तत्र there, महति in great, अरण्ये in the forest, समागतान् united, वारणयूथपाभान् with the effulgence of mighty leaders of elephant herds, तान् पार्थिवान् those kings, समीक्ष्य on seeing, हर्षम् delight, प्रविहाय having forsaken, अश्रूणि tears, अमुञ्चन् shed.
explanation: On seeing the princes now assembled in the great forest like mighty leaders of elephant herds, inhabitants of the forest had nothing but tears of grief, not joy, to shed. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetyninth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: जटिलं चीरवसनं प्राञ्जलिं पतितं भुवि। ददर्श रामो दुर्दर्शं युगान्ते भास्करंयथा।।2.100.1।।
transliteration: jaṭilaṃ cīravasanaṃ prāñjaliṃ patitaṃ bhuvi| dadarśa rāmo durdarśaṃ yugānte bhāskaraṃyathā
translation: रामः Rama, जटिलम् wearing matted locks, चीरवसनम् wearing bark robes, प्राञ्जलिम् with folded palms, भुवि on the ground, पतितम् fallen, युगान्ते at the time of dissolution of the world, भास्करं यथा like sun, दुर्दर्शम् difficult to look at, ददर्श beheld.
explanation: Rama beheld Bharata with matted locks and robes of bark fallen down on the ground with folded hands like the Sun at the time of dissolution of the world. It was really difficult to look at him.
comments: Meeting of Bharata and Rama -- Rama enquires about his father and others -- about Bharata's rule at Ayodhya.

shloka_text: कथंचिदभिविज्ञाय विवर्णवदनं कृशम्। भ्रातरं भरतं रामः परिजग्राह बाहुना।।2.100.2।।
transliteration: kathaṃcidabhivijñāya vivarṇavadanaṃ kṛśam| bhrātaraṃ bharataṃ rāmaḥ parijagrāha bāhunā
translation: रामः Rama, विवर्णवदनम् of pallid countenance, कृशम् emaciated, भ्रातरम् brother, भरतम् Bharata, कथंचित् with great difficulty, अभिविज्ञाय having recognised, बाहूना with his arm,  परिजग्राह caught hold of.
explanation: Rama found it extremely difficult to recognise Bharata with his emaciated body and pallid face. He held him in his arms and lifted him.

shloka_text: आघ्राय रामस्तं मूर्ध्नि परिष्वज्य च राघवः। अङ्के भरतमारोप्य पर्यपृच्छत्समाहितः।।2.100.3।।
transliteration: āghrāya rāmastaṃ mūrdhni pariṣvajya ca rāghavaḥ| aṅke bharatamāropya paryapṛcchatsamāhitaḥ
translation: राघवः born in the race of Raghu, रामः Rama, तं भरतम् to that Bharata, मूर्ध्नि on the forehead, आघ्राय having kissed, परिष्वज्य च and also embracing, अङ्के on his lap, आरोप्य making him sit, समाहितः with composed mind, पर्यपृच्छत् enquired.
explanation: Born in the race of Raghu, Rama embraced Bharata and kissed him on his forehead. Placing him on his lap, he enquired thus with a composed mind:

shloka_text: क्व नु तेऽभूत्पिता तात यदरण्यं त्वमागतः। न हि त्वं जीवतस्तस्य वनमागन्तुमर्हसि।।2.100.4।।
transliteration: kva nu te'bhūtpitā tāta yadaraṇyaṃ tvamāgataḥ| na hi tvaṃ jīvatastasya vanamāgantumarhasi
translation: तात O dear, त्वम् you, आरण्यम् to the forest, यत् आगतः now that you have come, ते पिता our father, क्व नु where, अभूत् was he, तस्य he, जीवतः while living, त्वम् you, वनम् to the forest, आगन्तुम् to come, न अर्हसि हि does not behove you.
explanation: O dear, now that you have come to the forest, where is our father king Dasaratha? You ought not come to the forest while he is living.

shloka_text: चिरस्य बत पश्यामि दूराद्भरतमागतम्। दुष्प्रतीकमरण्येऽस्मिन् किं तात वनमागतः।।2.100.5।।
transliteration: cirasya bata paśyāmi dūrādbharatamāgatam| duṣpratīkamaraṇye'smin kiṃ tāta vanamāgataḥ
translation: अस्मिन् अरण्ये to this forest, दूरात् from a distance, आगतम् have come, दुष्प्रतीकं of emaciated limbs, भरतम् Bharata, चिरस्य after a long time, पश्यामि I see, बत it is a pity, तात dear brother, वनम् to the forest, किम् why, आगतः did you come?
explanation: You have come a long distance (from Ayodhya) to this forest, O Bharata It is a pity,  dear brother, to see you after a long time, so emaciated. What brings you to the forest?

shloka_text: कच्चिद्धारयते तात राजा यत्त्वमिहाऽगतः। कच्चिन्न दीन स्सहसा राजा लोकान्तरं गतः।।2.100.6।।
transliteration: kacciddhārayate tāta rājā yattvamihā'gataḥ| kaccinna dīna ssahasā rājā lokāntaraṃ gataḥ
translation: तात dear child, त्वम् you, इह now, यत् आगतः that you have come here, राजा king Dasaratha, कच्चिद्दारयते Is he surviving, I trust so?, राजा king Dasaratha, दीनः dejected, सहसा immediately, लोकान्तरम् to the other world, न गतः कच्चित् I hope he did not depart.
explanation: My dear (brother), now that you have come here, I trust, king Dasaratha is keeping good health and hope, he has not departed prematurely in despondency for the other world.

shloka_text: कच्चित्सौम्य न ते राज्यं भ्रष्टं बालस्य शाश्वतम्। कच्चिच्छुश्रूषसे तात पितरं सत्यविक्रमम्।।2.100.7।।
transliteration: kaccitsaumya na te rājyaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ bālasya śāśvatam| kaccicchuśrūṣase tāta pitaraṃ satyavikramam
translation: सौम्य O gentle one, बालस्य young ones, ते your, शाश्वतम् permanent, राज्यम् kingdom, न भ्रष्टं कच्चित् I trust it has not been forfeited, तात dear child, सत्यविक्रमम् a man whose prowess is truthfulness, पितरम् father, शुश्रूषसे कच्चित् I trust you are looking after.
explanation: O gentle one, being young and inexperienced, I trust, you have not forfeited the kingdom for ever. Dear child, I trust, you are looking after father whose prowess is his truthfulness.

shloka_text: कच्चिद्धशरथो राजा कुशली सत्यसंङ्गरः। राजसूयाश्वमेधानामाहर्ता धर्मनिश्चयः।।2.100.8।।
transliteration: kacciddhaśaratho rājā kuśalī satyasaṃṅgaraḥ| rājasūyāśvamedhānāmāhartā dharmaniścayaḥ
translation: सत्यसंङ्गरः who is true to his promise, राजसूयाश्वमेधानाम् Rajasuya and Ashwamedha sacrifices, आहर्ता performer, धर्मनिश्चयः firm adherent of righteousness, राजा दशरथः king Dasaratha, कच्चित् कुशली I trust he is in good health.
explanation: I trust king Dasaratha, who is true to his promise, a performer of Rajasuya and Ashwamedha sacrifices and a firm adherent of righteousness is in good health.

shloka_text: स कच्चिद्ब्राह्मणो विद्वान् धर्मनित्यो महाद्युतिः। इक्ष्वाकूणामुपाध्यायो यथावत्तात पूज्यते।।2.100.9।।
transliteration: sa kaccidbrāhmaṇo vidvān dharmanityo mahādyutiḥ| ikṣvākūṇāmupādhyāyo yathāvattāta pūjyate
translation: तात dear child, ब्राह्मणः brahmin (versed in the Vedas), विद्वान् learned, धर्मनित्यः ever fixed in virtues, महाद्युतिः effulgent, सः that, इक्ष्वाकूणाम् Ikshvaku's, उपाध्यायः preceptor, यथावत् as usual, पूज्यते कच्चित् I trust he is being honoured.
explanation: O dear child I trust, the family preceptor of the Ikshvakus, Vasistha, the brahmin (versed in the Vedas), who is learned, ever fixed in virtues and effulgent is being honoured as usual.

shloka_text: सा तात कच्चित्कौसल्या सुमित्रा च प्रजावती। सुखिनी कच्चिदार्या च देवी नन्दति कैकयी।।2.100.10।।
transliteration: sā tāta kaccitkausalyā sumitrā ca prajāvatī| sukhinī kaccidāryā ca devī nandati kaikayī
translation: तात dear child, सा कौसल्या that Kausalya, सुखिनी कच्चित् trust she is happy, प्रजावती mother of excellent progeny, सुमित्रा च Sumitra too, आर्या noble, देवी queen, कैकयी Kaikeyi, नन्दति कच्चित् I trust she is delightful.
explanation: Dear child I trust, Kausalya and Sumitra, mothers of an excellent progeny are happy. I trust, the noble queen Kaikeyi is happy too.

shloka_text: कच्चिद्विनयसम्पन्नः कुलपुत्रो बहुश्रुतः। अनसूयुरनुद्रष्टा सत्कृतस्ते पुरोहितः।।2.100.11।।
transliteration: kaccidvinayasampannaḥ kulaputro bahuśrutaḥ| anasūyuranudraṣṭā satkṛtaste purohitaḥ
translation: विनयसम्पन्नः one who is endowed with modesty, कुलपुत्रः born of high family, बहुश्रुतः conversant in scriptures, अनसूयुः free from envy, अनुद्रष्टा one who can give directions, पुरोहितः priest, ते to (by) you, सत्कृतः कच्चित् I trust, you honour.
explanation: I trust, you continue to honour the family priest (Suyajna, son of Vasistha) who is endowed with modesty, born of high family, conversant in scriptures, free from envy and who can give you directions with regard to your duties.

shloka_text: कच्चिदग्निषु ते युक्तो विधिज्ञो मतिमानृजुः। हुतं च होष्यमाणं च काले वेदयते सदा।।2.100.12।।
transliteration: kaccidagniṣu te yukto vidhijño matimānṛjuḥ| hutaṃ ca hoṣyamāṇaṃ ca kāle vedayate sadā
translation: ते your, अग्निषु sacred fires, युक्तः employed, विधिज्ञः knower of ritual precepts, मतिमान्  sagacious, ऋजुः upright, सदा always, हुतं च what was offered as oblation, होष्यमाणं च what is going to be offered as oblation, काले at an appropriate time, वेदयते कच्चित् I trust he informs.
explanation: I trust, the sagacious priest who knows ritual precepts, who is upright and is employed to take care of your sacred fires, informs you always regarding what was offered and what is to be offered as oblation at appropriate time.

shloka_text: कच्चिद्देवान्पित्रून् मातृ़र्गुरून्पितृसमानपि। वृद्धांश्च तात वैद्यांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चाभिमन्यसे।।2.100.13।।
transliteration: kacciddevānpitrūn mātṛ़rgurūnpitṛsamānapi| vṛddhāṃśca tāta vaidyāṃśca brāhmaṇāṃścābhimanyase
translation: तात dear, देवान् gods, पित्रून् fathers, मात़ृ़: mothers, गुरून् teachers, पितृसमानपि relations equal to your father, वृद्धांश्च aged people, वैद्यांश्च physicians, ब्राह्मणांश्च brahmins, अभिमन्यसे कच्चित् I trust you are paying homage.
explanation: Dear brother, I trust you continue to pay homage to gods, father, mothers, teachers, relations equal to your father, aged people, physicians and brahmins.

shloka_text: इष्वस्त्रवरसम्पन्नमर्थशास्त्र विशारदम्। सुधन्वानमुपाध्यायं कच्चित्त्वं तात मन्यसे।।2.100.14।।
transliteration: iṣvastravarasampannamarthaśāstra viśāradam| sudhanvānamupādhyāyaṃ kaccittvaṃ tāta manyase
translation: तात dear child, इष्वस्त्रवरसम्पन्नम् he who is furnished with excellent arrows and other weapons, अर्थशास्त्रविशारदम् master in state craft, उपाध्यायम् teacher, सुधन्वानम् Sudhanva, त्वम् you, मन्यसे कच्चित् I hope you pay respect.
explanation: I hope you treat with respect Sudhanva who is equipped with the most formidable arrows and other weapons propelled by mantras and a master in the science of statecraft.

shloka_text: कच्चिदात्मसमा श्शूरा श्श्रुतवन्तो जितेन्द्रियाः। कुलीनाश्चेङ्गितज्ञाश्च कृतास्ते तात मन्त्रिणः।।2.100.15।।
transliteration: kaccidātmasamā śśūrā śśrutavanto jitendriyāḥ| kulīnāśceṅgitajñāśca kṛtāste tāta mantriṇaḥ
translation: तात O dear, आत्मसमाः men equal to you, शूराः brave men, श्रुतवन्तः learned men, जितेन्द्रियाः men with selfcontrol, कुलीनाश्च men of noble birth, इङ्गितज्ञाश्च men skilled in guessing from hints, ते to you, मन्त्रिणः as ministers, कृताः कच्चित् I hope you have appointed.
explanation: I hope, dear brother, you have appointed men who are brave, learned, selfcontrolled, of noble birth and skilled in guessing from hints.

shloka_text: मन्त्रो विजयमूलं हि राज्ञां भवति राघव। सुसंवृतो मन्त्रधरैरमात्यै श्शास्त्रकोविदैः।।2.100.16।।
transliteration: mantro vijayamūlaṃ hi rājñāṃ bhavati rāghava| susaṃvṛto mantradharairamātyai śśāstrakovidaiḥ
translation: राघव O Bharata, शास्त्रकोविदैः by men learned in scriptures, मन्त्रधरैः by those who can withhold proper counselling, अमात्यैः by ministers, सुसंवृतः wellguarded, मन्त्रः advice, राज्ञाम् to the king, विजयमूलम् root of victory, भवति हि will become.
explanation: O Bharata the wellguarded advice of ministers, learned in scriptures and capable of proper counselling, is the root of victory for kings, specially when the advice is kept in confidence.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्निद्रावशं नैषीः कच्चित् कालेऽवबुध्यसे। कच्चिच्चापररात्रेषु चिन्तियस्यर्थनैपुणम्।।2.100.17।।
transliteration: kaccinnidrāvaśaṃ naiṣīḥ kaccit kāle'vabudhyase| kacciccāpararātreṣu cintiyasyarthanaipuṇam
translation: निद्रावशम् controlled by sleep, नैषीः कच्चित् are you not, I trust, काले at appropriate time, प्रबुध्यसे कच्चित् are awake, I hope, अपररात्रेषु in the early hours, अर्थनैपुणम् about judicious statecraft, चिन्तयसि कच्चित् are you thinking, I trust.
explanation: I trust you are not under the grip of sleep but wake up at appropriate times, I hope you always think of the means of judicious statecraft during the last part of the night.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैकः कच्चिन्न बहुभिस्सह। कच्चित्ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति।।2.100.18।।
transliteration: kaccinmantrayase naikaḥ kaccinna bahubhissaha| kaccitte mantrito mantro rāṣṭraṃ na paridhāvati
translation: एकः alone, न मन्त्रयसे कच्चित् you are not planning, I hope, बहुभिस्सह with many, न कच्चित्  hope you are not discussing, मन्त्रितः when decided, ते मन्त्रः that decision, राष्ट्रम् about the kingdom, न परिधावति कच्चित् does not run through, I trust.
explanation: I hope you neither decide alone nor discuss with many. I trust a decision once made by you is not leaked in the kingdom.

shloka_text: कच्चिदर्थं विनिश्चित्य लघुमूलं महोदयम्। क्षिप्रमारभसे कर्तुं न दीर्घयसि राघव।।2.100.19।।
transliteration: kaccidarthaṃ viniścitya laghumūlaṃ mahodayam| kṣipramārabhase kartuṃ na dīrghayasi rāghava
translation: राघव O Bharata, लघुमूलम् with a little effort, महोदयम् yielding great result, अर्थम् an endeavour, विनिश्चित्य having determined, क्षिप्रम् quickly, कर्तुम् to execute, आरभसे कच्चित्  are commencing, न दीर्घयसि are not postponing unduly.
explanation: O Bharata, having determined on an endeavour involving a little effort and yielding great results, I trust you commence to execute it quickly without procrastination?

shloka_text: कच्चित्तु सुकृतान्येव कृतरूपाणि वा पुनः। विदुस्ते सर्वकार्याणि न कर्तव्यानि पार्थिवाः।।2.100.20।।
transliteration: kaccittu sukṛtānyeva kṛtarūpāṇi vā punaḥ| viduste sarvakāryāṇi na kartavyāni pārthivāḥ
translation: पार्थिवाः other kings, सुकृतान्येव wellaccomplished acts only, पुनः again, कृतरूपाणि वा or almost accomplished, ते your, सर्वकार्याणि all those endeavours, विदुः कच्चित् are informed,  कर्तव्यानि endeavours intended to be performed in future, न are not revealed.
explanation: I trust, other kings come to know of your endeavours only when your endeavours suceed or about to succeed. I hope, efforts intended to be made in future are not revealed to them beforehand.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्नतर्कैर्युक्त्या वा ये चाप्यपरिकीर्तिताः। त्वया वा तवामात्यैर्बुध्यते तात मन्त्रितम्।।2.100.21।।
transliteration: kaccinnatarkairyuktyā vā ye cāpyaparikīrtitāḥ| tvayā vā tavāmātyairbudhyate tāta mantritam
translation: तातः dear, त्वया वा by you, तव your, अमात्यैर्वा or by ministers, मन्त्रितम् determination, तर्कैः  by conjecture, युक्त्या वा or by inference, ये चापि other means, अपरिकीर्तिताः so far not  been revealed, (with those means or by others), कच्चिन्न बुध्यते I hope are not known.
explanation: Dear brother, I hope others are not able to understand your determination or those of your ministers, either by conjecture or by inference or through other means without being revealed either by you or by your ministers.

shloka_text: कच्चित्सहस्रान्मूर्खाणामेकमिच्छसि पण्डितम्। पण्डितो ह्यर्थकृच्छ्रेषु कुर्यान्निश्रेयसं महत्।।2.100.22।।
transliteration: kaccitsahasrānmūrkhāṇāmekamicchasi paṇḍitam| paṇḍito hyarthakṛcchreṣu kuryānniśreyasaṃ mahat
translation: मूर्खाणाम् among fools, सहस्रात् in preferance to a thousand, एकम् single, पण्डितम् wise man, इच्चसि कच्चित् I hope are preferring, अर्थकृच्छेषु in difficult situations, पण्डितः a wise man, महत् immense, निश्रेयसम् help, कुर्यात् will render.
explanation: I hope by setting aside a thousand fools, you prefer a single wise man. A wise man will be of immense help in difficult situations.

shloka_text: सहस्राण्यपि मूर्खाणां युद्युपास्ते महीपतिः। अथवाप्ययुतान्येव नास्ति तेषु सहायता।।2.100.23।।
transliteration: sahasrāṇyapi mūrkhāṇāṃ yudyupāste mahīpatiḥ| athavāpyayutānyeva nāsti teṣu sahāyatā
translation: महीपतिः king, मूर्खाणाम् fools, सहस्राणि in thousands, अथवा or else, अयुतान्येव or tens of thousands, उपास्ते यद्यपि even if he seeks assistance, तेषु among them, सहायता help, नास्ति not there.
explanation: Even if the king seeks the assistance from thousands or tens of thousands of fools, they cannot render any help to him.

shloka_text: एकोऽप्यमात्यो मेधावी शूरो दक्षो विचक्षणः। राजानं राजपुत्रं वा प्रापयेन्महतीं श्रियम्।।2.100.24।।
transliteration: eko'pyamātyo medhāvī śūro dakṣo vicakṣaṇaḥ| rājānaṃ rājaputraṃ vā prāpayenmahatīṃ śriyam
translation: मेधावी prudent, शूरः brave, दक्षः skilful, विचक्षणः clearsighted man, एकः a single one, अमात्यः अपि even minister, राजानम् the king, राजपुत्रं वा or a prince, श्रियम् prosperity, प्रापयेत् can bring.
explanation: A single clearsighted minister who is prudent, brave and skilful can bring about great prosperity to a king or a prince.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्मुख्या महात्स्वेव मध्यमेषु च मध्यमाः। जघन्याश्च जघन्येषु भृत्याः कर्मसु योजिताः।।2.100.25।।
transliteration: kaccinmukhyā mahātsveva madhyameṣu ca madhyamāḥ| jaghanyāśca jaghanyeṣu bhṛtyāḥ karmasu yojitāḥ
translation: मुख्याः important, भृत्याः servants, महत्सु in important, कर्मसु एव in tasks, योजिताः कच्चित् have been employed, I hope, मध्यमाः mediocre men, मध्यमेषु to the mediocre tasks, जघन्याः तु low people, जघन्येषु in the lower tasks, योजिता कच्चित् are employed, I hope.
explanation: I hope you have employed highly competent servants for important tasks, mediocre servants in mediocre tasks and low people in inferior tasks.

shloka_text: अमात्यानुपधातीतान्पितृपैतामहाञ्छुचीन्। श्रेष्ठांछ्रेष्ठेषुकच्चित्वं नियोजयसि कर्मसु।।2.100.26।।
transliteration: amātyānupadhātītānpitṛpaitāmahāñchucīn| śreṣṭhāṃchreṣṭheṣukaccitvaṃ niyojayasi karmasu
translation: उपधातीतान् unyielding to bribery and other temptations, पितृपैतामहान् men who hold hereditary positions, शुचीन् full of integrity, श्रेष्ठान् eminent, अमात्यान् ministers, त्वम् you, श्रेष्ठेषु for superior, कर्मसु for tasks, नियोजयसि कच्चित् I hope you are assigning.
explanation: I hope you are assigning ministers, who are unyielding to bribery and other temptations, holding positions hereditarily and who are full of integrity and eminence, with superior tasks.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्नोग्रेण दण्डेन भृशमुद्वेजितप्रजम्। राष्ट्रं तवानुजानन्ति मन्त्रिणः कैकयीसुत।।2.100.27।।
transliteration: kaccinnogreṇa daṇḍena bhṛśamudvejitaprajam| rāṣṭraṃ tavānujānanti mantriṇaḥ kaikayīsuta
translation: कैकयीसुत O Bharata, उग्रेण by severe, दण्डेन with punishment, भृशम् excessively, तव राष्ट्रम् your kingdom, उद्वेजितप्रजम् citizens being agitated, मन्त्रिणः ministers, नानुजानन्ति कच्चित्  I suppose will not permit so.
explanation: Are not the citizens of your kingdom agitated at severe punishment meted out to them reproaching your ministers?

shloka_text: कच्चित्त्वां नावजानन्ति याजकाः पतितं यथा। उग्रप्रतिग्रहीतारं कामयानमिव स्त्रियः।।2.100.28।।
transliteration: kaccittvāṃ nāvajānanti yājakāḥ patitaṃ yathā| ugrapratigrahītāraṃ kāmayānamiva striyaḥ
translation: याजकाः performers of sacrifice, उग्रप्रतिग्रहीतारम् accepting unmerited charity, पतितं यथा like an outcaste, स्त्रियः women, कामयानम् इव to a lustful one, त्वाम् you, नावजानन्ति कच्चित् hope they are not insulting you.
explanation: Just like a performer of sacrifice scorns at an outcaste or a woman scorns at a lustful lover, do the subjects not scorn you for collecting taxes more than what is due?

shloka_text: उपायकुशलं वैद्यं भृत्यसंदूषणे रतम्। शूरमैश्वर्यकामं च यो न हन्ति स हन्यते।।2.100.29।।
transliteration: upāyakuśalaṃ vaidyaṃ bhṛtyasaṃdūṣaṇe ratam| śūramaiśvaryakāmaṃ ca yo na hanti sa hanyate
translation: उपायकुशलम् skilled in contrivances, वैद्यम् learned person, शूरम् warrior, ऐश्वर्यकामं च passionate for wealth, भृत्यसंदूषणे in corrupting the minds of servants and making them revolt against their master, रतम् one who is engaged, यः such man, न हन्ति will not kill, सः that man, हन्यते will be killed.
explanation: A learned person but skilled in contrivances, a warrior with passion for wealth and a man ever engaged in corrupting the minds of servants must be slain. A king who does not kill them is himself killed in due course.

shloka_text: कच्चिद्धृष्टश्च शूरश्च मतिमान् धृतिमान् शुचिः। कुलीनश्चानुरक्तश्च दक्षस्सेनापतिः कृतः।।2.100.30।।
transliteration: kacciddhṛṣṭaśca śūraśca matimān dhṛtimān śuciḥ| kulīnaścānuraktaśca dakṣassenāpatiḥ kṛtaḥ
translation: हृष्टश्च cheerful, शूरश्च brave, मतिमान् sagacious,  धृतिमान् steadfast, शुचिः honest, कुलीनश्च born of good family, अनुरक्तश्च also loyal, दक्षः efficient, सेनापतिः chief of army,  कृतः कच्चित् I hope has been appointed.
explanation: I trust you have appointed a man who is cheerful, brave, sagacious, steadfast, honest, of a good family, loyal and efficient as the army chief.

shloka_text: बलवन्तश्च कच्चित्ते मुख्या युध्दविशारदाः। दृष्टापदाना विक्रान्तास्त्वया सत्कृत्यमानिताः।।2.100.31।।
transliteration: balavantaśca kaccitte mukhyā yudhdaviśāradāḥ| dṛṣṭāpadānā vikrāntāstvayā satkṛtyamānitāḥ
translation: बलवन्तः powerful, युध्दविशारदाः skilled in war, दृष्टापदानाः men with proven  herioc exploits, विक्रान्ताः courageous men, ते मुख्याः those prominent soldiers, त्वया by you, सत्कृत्य having honoured, मानिताः कच्चित् I hope they are respected.
explanation: I trust you honour and respect those prominent soldiers who are courageous, powerful, skilled in war and who have proven heroic exploits.

shloka_text: कच्चिद्बलस्य भक्तं च वेतनं च यथोचितम्। सम्प्राप्तकालं दातव्यं ददासि न विलम्बसे।।2.100.32।।
transliteration: kaccidbalasya bhaktaṃ ca vetanaṃ ca yathocitam| samprāptakālaṃ dātavyaṃ dadāsi na vilambase
translation: बलस्य of the army, दातव्यम् to be given, भक्तं च food (rations), यथोचितम् suitable, वेतनं च wages, सम्प्राप्तकालम् in due time, ददासि कच्चित् I trust you are paying, न विलम्बसे not delaying.
explanation: I trust you distribute rations and wages to your army in due time without making delay.

shloka_text: कालातिक्रमणाच्चैव भक्तवेतनयोर्भृताः। भर्तुः कुप्यन्ति दुष्यन्ति सोऽनर्थ स्सुमहान् स्मृतः।।2.100.33।।
transliteration: kālātikramaṇāccaiva bhaktavetanayorbhṛtāḥ| bhartuḥ kupyanti duṣyanti so'nartha ssumahān smṛtaḥ
translation: भृताः (dependent) attendants, भक्तवेतनयोः regarding food materials and wages, कालातिक्रमणात् beyond stipulated time, भर्तुः about the masters, कुप्यन्ति will be incensed, दुष्यन्ति will become corrupted, सः that one, सुमहान् very great, अनर्थः calamity, स्मृतः has been stated in the scriptures.
explanation: It has been mentioned in the scriptures that if provisions and wages are not paid in stipulated time, the dependent attendants will be incensed with their masters and will turn hostile and become corrupt, leading to great calamity.

shloka_text: कच्चित्सर्वेऽनुरक्तास्त्वां कुलपुत्राः प्रधानतः। कच्चित्प्राणां स्तवार्थेषु सन्त्यजन्ति समाहिताः।।2.100.34।।
transliteration: kaccitsarve'nuraktāstvāṃ kulaputrāḥ pradhānataḥ| kaccitprāṇāṃ stavārtheṣu santyajanti samāhitāḥ
translation: सर्वे all men, प्रधानतः especially, कुलपुत्राः men of our family, त्वाम् to you, अनुरक्ताः कच्चित् I hope they are loyal, समाहिताः men with steady mind, तव अर्थेषु for your cause, प्राणान् life, कच्चित् सन्त्यजन्ति I hope are ready to sacrifice.
explanation: I hope all men of a good family, especially those who belong to our race, are loyal to you and are ready to sacrifice their lives for your cause.

shloka_text: कच्चिज्जानपदो विद्वान्दक्षिणः प्रतिभानवान्। यथोक्तवादी दूतस्ते कृतो भरत पण्डितः।।2.100.35।।
transliteration: kaccijjānapado vidvāndakṣiṇaḥ pratibhānavān| yathoktavādī dūtaste kṛto bharata paṇḍitaḥ
translation: भरत O Bharata, जानपदः one who is born in your country, विद्वान् wellinformed, दक्षिणः favourable, प्रतिभानवान् one with quick understanding, यथोक्तवादी one who repeats, पण्डितः expert man, ते to (by) you, दूत: as envoy, कृतः कच्चित् I hope has been chosen.
explanation: O Bharata, I hope you have chosen as your envoy an expert born in your own country, wellinformed, skilful and quick to understand one who repeats and reports (exactly) what has been told.

shloka_text: कच्चिदष्टादशान्येषु स्वपक्षे दश पञ्च च। त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरविज्ञातैर्वेत्सि तीर्थानि चारकैः।।2.100.36।।
transliteration: kaccidaṣṭādaśānyeṣu svapakṣe daśa pañca ca| tribhistribhiravijñātairvetsi tīrthāni cārakaiḥ
translation: अन्येषु on enemy's side, अष्टादश eighteen, तीर्थानि officials by close watch, स्वपक्षे on your side, दश पञ्च च ten plus five (fifteen), अविज्ञातैः by those unrecognisable by others, त्रिभिः त्रिभिः three for each official, चारकैः spies, वेत्सि कच्चित् I hope you acquire information.
explanation: I hope you collect information (of their secret efforts) intelligently through unrecognisable spies with three of them closely watching each of the eighteen officials (there are eighteen categories of officials in a kingdom) of the enemy's side and fifteen (officials) on your side.

shloka_text: कच्चिद्व्यपास्तानहितान्प्रतियातांश्च सर्वदा। दुर्बलाननवज्ञाय वर्तसे रिपुसूदन।।2.100.37।।
transliteration: kaccidvyapāstānahitānpratiyātāṃśca sarvadā| durbalānanavajñāya vartase ripusūdana
translation: रिपुसूदन O slayer of foes, व्यपास्तान् defeated, प्रतियातांश्च having gone back, दुर्बलान् weak, अहितान् foes, सर्वदा at all times, अनवज्ञाय without neglecting, वर्तसे कच्चित् I hope you remain alert.
explanation: O slayer of foes, I hope you are always alert about your foes who were defeated by you and have come back. You should not ignore your enemies thinking they are weak.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्न लौकायतिकान्ब्राह्मणांस्तात सेवसे।। अनर्थकुशला ह्येते बालाः पण्डितमानिनः।।2.100.38।।
transliteration: kaccinna laukāyatikānbrāhmaṇāṃstāta sevase|| anarthakuśalā hyete bālāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ
translation: तात O dear child, लौकायतिकान् thinking of this world only, those atheists, ब्राह्मणान्  brahmins, न सेवसे कच्चित् I hope you are not keeping company, पण्डितमानिनः fancying         them as learned, बालाः foolish, एते these people, अनर्थकुशलाः हि adept in bringing disaster indeed.
explanation: Dear brother, I hope you do not serve those brahmins who are atheists, who foolishly think of this world alone and fancy themselves as learned. They only bring disasters.

shloka_text: धर्मशास्त्रेषु मुख्येषु विद्यमानेषु दुर्बुधाः। बुद्धिमान्वीक्षिकीं प्राप्य निरर्थं प्रवदन्ति ते।।2.100.39।।
transliteration: dharmaśāstreṣu mukhyeṣu vidyamāneṣu durbudhāḥ| buddhimānvīkṣikīṃ prāpya nirarthaṃ pravadanti te
translation: दुर्बुधाः these superficial fellows, मुख्येषु among the principal, धर्मशास्त्रेषु in scriptures, विद्यमानेषु while existing, आन्वीक्षिकीम् relating to the science of logic, बुद्धिम् intelligence, प्राप्य having obtained, निरर्थम् futile, प्रवदन्ति argue.
explanation: While principal scriptures do exist, these superficial fellows take resort to the science of logic based on abstract reasoning, and indulge in futile talks.

shloka_text: वीरैरध्युषितां पूर्वमस्माकं तात पूर्वकैः। सत्यनामां दृढ द्वारां हस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलाम्।।2.100.40।। ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यै स्स्वकर्मनिरतैस्सदा। जितेन्द्रियैर्महोत्साहैर्वृतामार्यै स्सहस्रशः।।2.100.41।। प्रासादैर्विविधाकारैर्वृतां वैद्यजनाकुलाम्। कच्चित्सुमुदितां स्फीतामयोध्यां परिरक्षसि।।2.100.42।।
transliteration: vīrairadhyuṣitāṃ pūrvamasmākaṃ tāta pūrvakaiḥ| satyanāmāṃ dṛḍha dvārāṃ hastyaśvarathasaṅkulām brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairvaiśyai ssvakarmanirataissadā| jitendriyairmahotsāhairvṛtāmāryai ssahasraśaḥ prāsādairvividhākārairvṛtāṃ vaidyajanākulām| kaccitsumuditāṃ sphītāmayodhyāṃ parirakṣasi
translation: ताता O dear child, वीरैः by the heroic, अस्माकम् our, पूर्वकैः by ancestors, पूर्वम् formerly, अध्युषिताम् inhabited, सत्यनामाम् true to its name, दृढद्वाराम् with sturdy gates, हस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलाम् full of elephants, horses and chariots, सदा always, स्वकर्मनिरतैः engaged in their respective professions, जितेन्द्रियैः by selfcontrolled men, महोत्साहैः by  highly energetic men, आर्यैः by venerable men, सहस्रशः in their thousands, ब्राह्मणैः by brahmins, क्षत्रियैः by kshatriyas (warriors), वैश्यैः by vaisyas (merchants), वृतम् surrounded, विविधाकारैः of various kinds, प्रासादैः with palaces, वृताम् filled with, वैद्यजनाकुलाम् full of learned people, सुमुदिताम् with everything available, स्फीताम् prosperous, अयोध्याम् Ayodhya, परिरक्षसि कच्चित् I trust you are protecting.
explanation: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

shloka_text: कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्ट स्सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः। देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.43।। प्रहृष्टनरनारीकस्समाजोत्सवशोभितः। सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान्हिंसाभिः परिवर्जितः।।2.100.44।। अदेवमातृको रम्य श्श्वापदैः परिवर्जितः। परित्यक्तो भयैस्सर्वैः खनिभिश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.45।। विवर्जितो नरैः पापैर्मम पूर्वै स्सुरक्षितः। कच्चिज्जनपदस्स्फीतः सुखं वसति राघव।।2.100.46।।
transliteration: kacciccaityaśatairjuṣṭa ssuniviṣṭajanākulaḥ| devasthānaiḥ prapābhiśca taṭākaiścopaśobhitaḥ prahṛṣṭanaranārīkassamājotsavaśobhitaḥ| sukṛṣṭasīmā paśumānhiṃsābhiḥ parivarjitaḥ adevamātṛko ramya śśvāpadaiḥ parivarjitaḥ| parityakto bhayaissarvaiḥ khanibhiścopaśobhitaḥ vivarjito naraiḥ pāpairmama pūrvai ssurakṣitaḥ| kaccijjanapadassphītaḥ sukhaṃ vasati rāghava
translation: राघव O Bharata, चैत्यशतैः by hundreds of sanctuaries near villages, जुष्ट: furnished,  सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः filled with people where life is made comfortable, देवस्थानैः with shrines, प्रपाभिश्च with centres for providing water, तटाकैश्च with tanks, उपशोभितः graced with, सुकृष्टसीमा wellploughed land, पशुमान् with excellent cattle, हिंसाभिः with violence, परिवर्जितः abandoned, अदेवमातृकः not dependant on rain, रम्यः enchanting, श्वापदैः with wild animals, परिवर्जितः devoid of, सर्वैः by all kinds, भयैः of fears, परित्यक्तः expelled, खनिभिश्च with mines, उपशोभितः adorned with, पापैः by sinful, नरैः with people, विवर्जितः deserted,  मम my, पूर्वैः by ancestors, सुरक्षितः wellprotected, जनपद: country, स्फीतः कच्चित् I trust is prosperous, सुखम् comfortably, वसति कच्चित् I hope they are living.
explanation: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

shloka_text: कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्ट स्सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः। देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.43।। प्रहृष्टनरनारीकस्समाजोत्सवशोभितः। सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान्हिंसाभिः परिवर्जितः।।2.100.44।। अदेवमातृको रम्य श्श्वापदैः परिवर्जितः। परित्यक्तो भयैस्सर्वैः खनिभिश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.45।। विवर्जितो नरैः पापैर्मम पूर्वै स्सुरक्षितः। कच्चिज्जनपदस्स्फीतः सुखं वसति राघव।।2.100.46।।
transliteration: kacciccaityaśatairjuṣṭa ssuniviṣṭajanākulaḥ| devasthānaiḥ prapābhiśca taṭākaiścopaśobhitaḥ prahṛṣṭanaranārīkassamājotsavaśobhitaḥ| sukṛṣṭasīmā paśumānhiṃsābhiḥ parivarjitaḥ adevamātṛko ramya śśvāpadaiḥ parivarjitaḥ| parityakto bhayaissarvaiḥ khanibhiścopaśobhitaḥ vivarjito naraiḥ pāpairmama pūrvai ssurakṣitaḥ| kaccijjanapadassphītaḥ sukhaṃ vasati rāghava
translation: राघव O Bharata, चैत्यशतैः by hundreds of sanctuaries near villages, जुष्ट: furnished,  सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः filled with people where life is made comfortable, देवस्थानैः with shrines, प्रपाभिश्च with centres for providing water, तटाकैश्च with tanks, उपशोभितः graced with, सुकृष्टसीमा wellploughed land, पशुमान् with excellent cattle, हिंसाभिः with violence, परिवर्जितः abandoned, अदेवमातृकः not dependant on rain, रम्यः enchanting, श्वापदैः with wild animals, परिवर्जितः devoid of, सर्वैः by all kinds, भयैः of fears, परित्यक्तः expelled, खनिभिश्च with mines, उपशोभितः adorned with, पापैः by sinful, नरैः with people, विवर्जितः deserted,  मम my, पूर्वैः by ancestors, सुरक्षितः wellprotected, जनपद: country, स्फीतः कच्चित् I trust is prosperous, सुखम् comfortably, वसति कच्चित् I hope they are living.
explanation: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

shloka_text: कच्चित्ते दयितास्सर्वे कृषिगोरक्षजीविनः। वार्तायां संश्रितस्तात लोको हि सुखमेधते।।2.100.47।।
transliteration: kaccitte dayitāssarve kṛṣigorakṣajīvinaḥ| vārtāyāṃ saṃśritastāta loko hi sukhamedhate
translation: तात dear child, सर्वे all men, कृषिगोरक्षजीविनः those who live on agriculture and cattlerearing, ते to you, दयिता कच्चित् I trust are favourable, वार्तायाम् in profession (of cattle raising), संश्रितः depending on, लोकः world, सुखम् happily, एधते हि grows.
explanation: I trust all those men who live on agriculture and cattlerearing are favourable to you. The world's prosperity, dear brother, grows on the profession of cattle rearing.

shloka_text: तेषां गुप्तिपरीहारैः कच्चित्ते भरणं कृतम्। रक्ष्या हि राज्ञा धर्मेण सर्वे विषयवासिनः।।2.100.48।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ guptiparīhāraiḥ kaccitte bharaṇaṃ kṛtam| rakṣyā hi rājñā dharmeṇa sarve viṣayavāsinaḥ
translation: गुप्तिपरीहारैः by affording protection and through prevention of adversities, तेषाम् their, भरणम् maintenance, ते to you (by you), कृतं कच्चित् has been done, I hope, राज्ञा by the king, विषयवासिनः those living in the country, सर्वे all, धर्मेण with righteousness, रक्ष्याः हि are  required to be protected.
explanation: I trust you nourish them and also afford portection and prevent adversities. A king must protect all those people living in his country in accordanc with righteousness.

shloka_text: कच्चिस्त्रिय स्सान्त्वयसि कच्चित्ताश्च सुरक्षिताः। कच्चिन्न श्रद्धास्यासां कच्चिद्गुह्यं न भाषसे।।2.100.49।।
transliteration: kaccistriya ssāntvayasi kaccittāśca surakṣitāḥ| kaccinna śraddhāsyāsāṃ kaccidguhyaṃ na bhāṣase
translation: स्त्रियः women, सान्त्वयसि कच्चित् I hope you are pacifying, ताः they, ते to (by) you, सुरक्षिताः कच्चित् I trust they are  guarded well, आसाम् words of the women, न श्रद्धास्यासां कच्चित् I trust you believe not, गुह्यम् secret, न भाषसे कच्चित् I trust you do not divulge.
explanation: I trust, you keep the women pacified and wellprotected, you do not believe their words and do not divulge any secrets to them.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्नागवनं गुप्तं कच्चित्ते सन्ति धेनुकाः। कच्चिन्न गणिकाश्वानां कुञ्जराणां च तृप्यसि।।2.100.50।।
transliteration: kaccinnāgavanaṃ guptaṃ kaccitte santi dhenukāḥ| kaccinna gaṇikāśvānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca tṛpyasi
translation: नागवनम् habitat of elephants, गुप्तं कच्चित् I trust is protected, ते to you, धेनुकाः milch cows, सन्ति कच्चित् I trust you have, गणिकाश्वानाम् mares, कुञ्जराणांच elephants, न तृप्यसि कच्चित् I trust you are not contented.
explanation: I trust, you protect the habitat of elephants and you have a large number of milch cows. I trust you are not contented with the existing number of female and male elephants and horses.

shloka_text: कच्चिद्दर्शयसे नित्यं मनुष्याणां विभूषितम्। उत्थायोत्थाय पूर्वाह्णे राजपुत्र महापथे।।2.100.51।।
transliteration: kacciddarśayase nityaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vibhūṣitam| utthāyotthāya pūrvāhṇe rājaputra mahāpathe
translation: राजपुत्र O prince नित्यम् daily, पूर्वाह्णे early in the morning, उत्थायोत्थाय rising early, महापथे on the thoroughfare, मानुष्याणाम् to the people, विभूषितम् welladorned, दर्शयसे कच्चित् I trust you are presenting yourself.
explanation: O prince, I trust, you rise early daily and present yourself welladomed to the people on the thoroughfare.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्न सर्वे कर्मान्ताः प्रत्यक्षास्तेऽविशङ्कया। सर्वे वा पुनरुत्सृष्टा मध्यमेवात्र कारणम्।।2.100.52।।
transliteration: kaccinna sarve karmāntāḥ pratyakṣāste'viśaṅkayā| sarve vā punarutsṛṣṭā madhyamevātra kāraṇam
translation: सर्वे all, कर्मान्ताः servants, ते to you, अविशङ्कया without fear, न प्रत्यक्षाः कच्चित् I trust do not present themselves, सर्वे all, उत्सृष्टाः वा पुनः or again (I trust) are not kept in a distance, अत्र here, मध्यमेव middle course, कारणम् reason for welfare of all the workers.
explanation: All the servants, I trust, do not present themselves to you directly. At the same time they do not remain out of sight with fear at a distance. The middle course is the best way for the welfare of every one.

shloka_text: कच्चित्सर्वाणि दुर्गाणि धनधान्यायुधोदकैः। यन्त्रैश्च परिपूर्णानि तथा शिल्पिधनुर्धरैः।।2.100.53।।
transliteration: kaccitsarvāṇi durgāṇi dhanadhānyāyudhodakaiḥ| yantraiśca paripūrṇāni tathā śilpidhanurdharaiḥ
translation: सर्वाणि all, दुर्गाणि the forts, धनधान्यायुधोदकैः with wealth, grains, weapons and water, यन्त्रैश्च with ammunitions or machines of war, तथा similarly, शिल्पिधनुर्धरैः with craftsmen and archers, परिपूर्णानि कच्चित् are adequately provided, I trust.
explanation: Hope all the forts are adequately provided with wealth, foodgrains, weapons and water, with machines of war and craftsmen and archers.

shloka_text: आयस्ते विपुलः कच्चित्कच्चिदल्पतरो व्ययः। अपात्रेषु न ते कच्चित्कोशो गच्छति राघव।।2.100.54।।
transliteration: āyaste vipulaḥ kaccitkaccidalpataro vyayaḥ| apātreṣu na te kaccitkośo gacchati rāghava
translation: राघव O Bharata, ते your, आयः revenues, विपुलः कच्चित् are abundant, I trust, व्ययः expenditure, अल्पतरः कच्चित् is much less, I hope, ते your, कोशः treasury, अपात्रेषु to  undeserving people, न गच्छति कच्चित् does not pass, I trust.
explanation: O Bharata, I trust, your revenues are abundant and expenditure much less. I trust you do not give away your treasure to undeserving persons.

shloka_text: देवतार्थे च पित्रर्थेब्राह्मणाभ्यागतेषु च। योधेषु मित्रवर्गेषु कच्चिद्गच्छति ते व्ययः।।2.100.55।।
transliteration: devatārthe ca pitrarthebrāhmaṇābhyāgateṣu ca| yodheṣu mitravargeṣu kaccidgacchati te vyayaḥ
translation: ते your, व्ययः expenditure, देवतार्थे च for the sake of the gods, पित्रर्थे for the sake of ancestors, ब्राह्मणाभ्यागतेषु for brahmins and guests, योधेषु on warriors, मित्रवर्गेषु on hordes of friends, गच्छति कच्चित् is being spent I hope.
explanation: I trust, you are spending only on gods, ancestors, brahmins, guests, warriors and hosts of friends.

shloka_text: कच्चिदार्यो विशुद्धात्मा क्षारित श्चापरकर्मणा। अपृष्ट श्शास्त्रकुशलैर्न लोभाद्वध्यते शुचिः।।2.100.56।।
transliteration: kaccidāryo viśuddhātmā kṣārita ścāparakarmaṇā| apṛṣṭa śśāstrakuśalairna lobhādvadhyate śuciḥ
translation: विशुद्धात्मा of purehearted man, आर्यः venerable one, शुचिः honest, अपकर्मणा with  unworthy act, क्षारितः falsely accused of adultery, शास्त्रकुशलैः by those wellversed in scriptures, अपृष्टः without consulting, लोभात् out of avarice, न वध्यते कच्चित् I trust is not slain.
explanation: I trust a man who is honest, purehearted and venerable, falsely accused of adultery is not slain out of avarice without consulting experts in scriptures.

shloka_text: गृहीतश्चैव पृष्टश्च काले दृष्टस्सकारणः। कच्चिन्न मुच्यते चोरो धनलोभान्नरर्षभ।।2.100.57।।
transliteration: gṛhītaścaiva pṛṣṭaśca kāle dṛṣṭassakāraṇaḥ| kaccinna mucyate coro dhanalobhānnararṣabha
translation: नरर्षभ O best among men, काले at the time of committing theft, दृष्टः who has been caught redhanded, गृहीतश्चैव one who is arrested, पृष्टश्च one who has been interrogated, सकारणः one who has sufficient evidence, चोरः thief, धनलोभात् out of greed for money, न मुच्यते  कच्चित् I hope is not set free.
explanation: O best among men I trust that a thief, caught redhanded and interrogated and has sufficient proof is not set free, out of greed for money.

shloka_text: व्यसने कच्चिदाढ्यस्य दुर्गतस्य च राघव। अर्थं विरागाः पश्यन्ति तवामात्या बहुश्रुताः।।2.100.58।।
transliteration: vyasane kaccidāḍhyasya durgatasya ca rāghava| arthaṃ virāgāḥ paśyanti tavāmātyā bahuśrutāḥ
translation: राघव O Bharata, बहुश्रुताः wellinformed, तव अमात्याः your ministers, आढ्यस्य of a rich man, दुर्गतस्य च to a poorman, व्यसने in times of hardship, अर्थम् any matter, विरागाः impartially, पश्यन्ति कच्चित् I trust they look at impartially.
explanation: O Bharata, I trust that your ministers are wellinformed and look into all matters in times of hardship pertaining to whether a man is rich or poor without any bias to either.

shloka_text: यानि मिथ्याभिशस्तानां पतन्त्यश्रूणि राघव। तानि पुत्रान्पशून्घ्नन्ति प्रीत्यर्थमनुशासतः।।2.100.59।।
transliteration: yāni mithyābhiśastānāṃ patantyaśrūṇi rāghava| tāni putrānpaśūnghnanti prītyarthamanuśāsataḥ
translation: राघव Bharata, मिथ्याभिशस्तानाम् of those who are falsely accused, यानि अश्रूणि those tears, पतन्ति fall, तानि they, प्रीत्यर्थम् for the sake of pleasure, अनुशासतः one who commands,  पुत्रान्पशून् his sons and cattle, घ्नन्ति they will destroy.
explanation: O Bharata, the tears falling from the eyes of persons, who are falsely accused and punished for the pleasure of the king will destroy his progeny and cattle as well.

shloka_text: कच्चिद्वृद्धांश्च बालांश्च वैद्यामुख्यांश्च राघव। दानेन मनसा वाचा त्रिभिरेतैर्बुभूषसे।।2.100.60।।
transliteration: kaccidvṛddhāṃśca bālāṃśca vaidyāmukhyāṃśca rāghava| dānena manasā vācā tribhiretairbubhūṣase
translation: राघव Bharata, वृद्धांश्च the old, बालांश्च the children, वैद्यमुख्यांश्च foremost of learned people, दानेन with gifts, मनसा with affection, वाचा with kind words, एतैः these, त्रिभिः with  three,  बुभूषसे कच्चित् I trust you thrive.
explanation: O Bharata, I trust you wish to thrive by treating the old, children and foremost of learned people with the three expedients namely gifts, affection and kind words.

shloka_text: कच्चिद्गुरूंश्च वृद्धांश्च तापसान् देवतातिथीन्। चैत्यांश्च सर्वान्सिध्दार्थान्ब्राह्मणांश्च नमस्यसि।।2.100.61।।
transliteration: kaccidgurūṃśca vṛddhāṃśca tāpasān devatātithīn| caityāṃśca sarvānsidhdārthānbrāhmaṇāṃśca namasyasi
translation: गुरूंश्च prceptors, वृद्धांश्च the old, तापसान् the ascetics, देवतातिथीन् gods and guests, चैत्यांश्च shrines, सिध्दार्थान् acomplished men, ब्राह्मणांश्च brahmins, सर्वान् all, नमस्यसि कच्चित् I trust you are paying homage.
explanation: I trust you pay homage to the preceptors, the aged ones, ascetics, gods and guests, to shrines and to accomplished brahmins.

shloka_text: कच्चिदर्थेन वा धर्ममर्थं धर्मेण वा पुनः। उभौ वा प्रीतिलोभेन कामेन च न बाधसे।।2.100.62।।
transliteration: kaccidarthena vā dharmamarthaṃ dharmeṇa vā punaḥ| ubhau vā prītilobhena kāmena ca na bādhase
translation: अर्थेन with prosperity, धर्मं वा or righteousness, धर्मेण with righteousness, अर्थं वा prosperity, पुनः again, प्रीतिलोभेन longing for pleasure, कामेन with desire for sensual enjoyment, उभौ both, न बाधसे कच्चित् I trust you are not thwarting.
explanation: I trust, righteousness for the sake of prosperity or prosperity for the sake of righteousness or both for the sake of sensual pleasure are not thwarted by you.

shloka_text: कच्चिदर्थं च धर्मं च कामं च जयतां वर। विभज्य काले कालज्ञ सर्वान्वरद सेवसे।।2.100.63।।
transliteration: kaccidarthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca jayatāṃ vara| vibhajya kāle kālajña sarvānvarada sevase
translation: जयताम् among the victorious, वर best, कालज्ञ one having the knowledge of time, वरद granter of boons (best of men), धर्मंच righteousness, कामंच legitimate pleasure, सर्वान् all of them, काले proper time, विभज्य dividing time for each, सेवसे कच्चित् I trust you are attending.
explanation: O Bharata, the best among the victorious, conversant with timely actions and a bestower of boons you are the best of men. I trust, you allocate adequate time for attending to all the three expedients of life like dharma, artha and kama.

shloka_text: कच्चित्ते ब्राह्मणा श्शर्म सर्वशास्त्रार्थकोविदाः। आशंसन्ते महाप्राज्ञ पौरजानपदैस्सह।।2.100.64।।
transliteration: kaccitte brāhmaṇā śśarma sarvaśāstrārthakovidāḥ| āśaṃsante mahāprājña paurajānapadaissaha
translation: महाप्राज्ञ O highly sagacious one, सर्वशास्त्रार्थ कोविदाः those who can comprehend the meaning of all scriptures, ब्राह्मणाः brahmins, पौरजानपदैस्सह along with the inhabitants of the city and country too, ते your, शर्म happiness, आशंसन्ते कच्चित् I trust they are seeking.
explanation: O highly sagacious Bharata, those brahmins who can comprehend the meaning of all scriptures along with the inhabitants of the city and country, I trust, are seeking your happiness.

shloka_text: नास्तिक्यमनृतं क्रोधं प्रमादं दीर्घसूत्रताम्। अदर्शनं ज्ञानवतामालस्यं पञ्चवृत्तिताम्।।2.100.65।। एकचिन्तनमर्थानामनर्थज्ञैश्च मन्त्रणम्। निश्चितानामनारम्भं मन्त्रस्यापरिरक्षणम्।।2.100.66।। मङ्गलाद्यप्रयोगं च प्रत्युत्थानं च सर्वतः। कच्चित्वं वर्जयस्येतान्राजदोषांश्चतुर्दश।।2.100.67।।
transliteration: nāstikyamanṛtaṃ krodhaṃ pramādaṃ dīrghasūtratām| adarśanaṃ jñānavatāmālasyaṃ pañcavṛttitām ekacintanamarthānāmanarthajñaiśca mantraṇam| niścitānāmanārambhaṃ mantrasyāparirakṣaṇam maṅgalādyaprayogaṃ ca pratyutthānaṃ ca sarvataḥ| kaccitvaṃ varjayasyetānrājadoṣāṃścaturdaśa
translation: नास्तिक्यम् atheism, अनृतम् falsehood, क्रोधम् anger, प्रमादम् inattention, दीर्घसूत्रताम्   procrastination, ज्ञानवताम् wise people's, अदर्शनम् evasion, आलस्यम् indolence, पञ्चवृत्तिताम् gratification of all five senses, अर्थानाम् relating to the affairs (of the kingdom), एकचिन्तनम् thinking alone, अनर्थज्ञैः by those proficient in worthless acts, मन्त्रणम् consultation, निश्चितानाम् of acts decided upon, अनारम्भम् not to implement, मन्त्रस्य counsel, अपरिरक्षणम् not protecting, मङ्लादि beginning of an auspicious note and the like, अप्रयोगं च not to practise, सर्वतः on all sides, प्रत्युत्थानं च attacking all the enemies at a time, एतान् all these, चतुर्दश fourteen, राजदोषान् defects of the king, त्वम् you, वर्जयसि कच्चित् I trust you eschew.
explanation: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

shloka_text: दशपञ्चचतुर्वर्गान्सप्तवर्गं च तत्त्वतः। अष्टवर्गं त्रिवर्गं च विद्यास्तिस्रश्च राघव।।2.100.68।। इन्द्रियाणां जयं बुद्ध्या षाड्गुण्यं दैवमानुषम्। कृत्यं विंशतिवर्गं च तथा प्रकृतिमण्डलम्।।2.100.69।। यात्रादण्डविधानं च द्वियोनी सन्धिविग्रहौ। कच्चिदेतान्महाप्राज्ञ यथावदनुमन्यसे।।2.100.70।।
transliteration: daśapañcacaturvargānsaptavargaṃ ca tattvataḥ| aṣṭavargaṃ trivargaṃ ca vidyāstisraśca rāghava indriyāṇāṃ jayaṃ buddhyā ṣāḍguṇyaṃ daivamānuṣam| kṛtyaṃ viṃśativargaṃ ca tathā prakṛtimaṇḍalam yātrādaṇḍavidhānaṃ ca dviyonī sandhivigrahau| kaccidetānmahāprājña yathāvadanumanyase
translation: महाप्राज्ञः O highly sagacious, राघवः Bharata, दशपञ्चचतुर्वर्गान् the fifteen of the fourfold  divisions, सप्तवर्गं च the seven divisions, अष्टवर्गम् the eight divisions, त्रिवर्गं च the three  divisions, तिस्र: three, विद्याः च kinds of knowledge, इन्द्रियाणाम् of the senses, जयम् victory over, षाडगुण्यम् six qualities, दैवमानुषम् evils arising from destiny and human agency, कृत्यम् kritya, विंशतिवर्गं च division of twenty, तथा similarly, प्रकृतिमण्डलम् Prakriti and Mandalas, यात्रादण्डविधानं च practices of yatra and chastisement, द्वियोनिः two sources of, सन्धि विग्रहौ peace and war, तत्त्वतः the true nature, बुध्द्या by intellect, एतान् alone, यथावत् appropriately, अनुमन्यसे कच्चित् I trust you follow.
explanation: O highly sagacious Bharata, I trust, having understood their true nature you are appropriately following the ten, five and four divisions, the seven divisions, the eight divisions, the three divisions, three kinds of knowledge, victory over the senses, the six qualities, evils arising from destiny and human agency, kritya, division of twenty, similarly Prakriti and Mandalas and two sources of Yatra and chastisement and of peace and war.

shloka_text: मन्त्रिभिस्त्वं यथोद्दिष्टैश्चतुर्भिस्त्रिभिरेव वा। कच्चित्समस्तैर्व्यस्तैश्च मन्त्रं मन्त्रयसे मिथः।।2.100.71।।
transliteration: mantribhistvaṃ yathoddiṣṭaiścaturbhistribhireva vā| kaccitsamastairvyastaiśca mantraṃ mantrayase mithaḥ
translation: त्वम् you, यथोद्दिष्टैः as adumbrated in sacred texts, चतुर्भिः by four, त्रिभिरेव वा or three, मन्त्रिभिः with counsellors, समस्तै: together, व्यस्तैश्च separately with each one, मिथ: in secrecy, मन्त्रम्  counsel, मन्त्रयसे कच्चित् I trust you deliberate.
explanation: I trust you deliberate in secrecy on your counsel with three or four counsellors, together and separately with each one, as laid down in sacred texts.

shloka_text: कच्चित्ते सफला वेदाः कच्चित्ते सफलाः क्रियाः। कच्चित्ते सफला दाराः कच्चित्ते सफलं श्रुतम्।।2.100.72।।
transliteration: kaccitte saphalā vedāḥ kaccitte saphalāḥ kriyāḥ| kaccitte saphalā dārāḥ kaccitte saphalaṃ śrutam
translation: ते your knowledge of, वेदाः Vedas, सफलाः कच्चित् I trust is fruitful, ते क्रियाः your acts,  सफला कच्चित् I trust are productive, ते दाराः your wife, सफलाः कच्चित् I trust is useful, ते श्रुतम् the scriptures you have heard, सफलं कच्चित् I trust, is useful.
explanation: I trust, the Vedas you have studied are fruitful, the acts which you commenced are productive, your wife is fruitful (blessed with a son) and the scriptures you studied are useful.

shloka_text: कच्चिदेषैव ते बुद्धिर्यथोक्ता मम राघव। आयुष्या च यशस्या च धर्मकामार्थ संहिता।।2.100.73।।
transliteration: kaccideṣaiva te buddhiryathoktā mama rāghava| āyuṣyā ca yaśasyā ca dharmakāmārtha saṃhitā
translation: राघव O Bharata, ते बुद्धि: your intellect, आयुष्या is enhancing your life span, यशस्या च augmenting your fame, धर्मकामार्थ संहिता in accordance with righteousness, (legitimate) pleasure and prosperity, मम to (by) me, यथा as, उक्ता said, एषैव कच्चित् I trust it is in conformity with that.
explanation: O Bharata, I trust your intellect is in conformity with what I said conducive to long life, and fame in accordance with righteousness, (legitimate) pleasure and prosperity.

shloka_text: यां वृत्तिं वर्तते तातो यां च नः प्रपितामहाः। तां वृत्तिं वर्तसे कच्चिद्याच सत्पथगा शुभा।।2.100.74।।
transliteration: yāṃ vṛttiṃ vartate tāto yāṃ ca naḥ prapitāmahāḥ| tāṃ vṛttiṃ vartase kaccidyāca satpathagā śubhā
translation: तातः our father, याम् वृत्तिम् whichever course, वर्तते is following, याम् which course, नः our, प्रपितामहाः followed by ancestors, या च सत्पथगा which one walks the path of truth, शुभा auspicious, ताम् that, वृत्तिम् course, वर्तसे कच्चित् I trust, you follow.
explanation: I trust, you walk the auspicious path of truth (virtue) followed by our father and forefathers.

shloka_text: कच्चित्स्वादु कृतं भोज्यमेको नाश्नासि राघव। कच्चिदाशंसमानेभ्यो मित्रेभ्य स्सम्प्रयच्छसि।।2.100.75।।
transliteration: kaccitsvādu kṛtaṃ bhojyameko nāśnāsi rāghava| kaccidāśaṃsamānebhyo mitrebhya ssamprayacchasi
translation: राघव Bharata, स्वादुकृतम् prepared deliciously, भोज्यम् food, एकः alone, नाश्नासि कच्चित् I  trust you are not partaking, अशंसमानेभ्यः to those who desire them, मित्रेभ्यः to friends, सम्प्रयच्छसि कच्चित् I trust you are giving it.
explanation: O Bharata, I trust you do not partake delicious food all by yourself, and you share it with your friends when they want it.

shloka_text: राजा तु धर्मेण हि पालयित्वा महामतिर्दण्डधरः प्रजानाम्। अवाप्य कृत्स्नां वसुधां यथावदितश्च्युत स्स्वर्गमुपैति विद्वान्।।2.100.76।।
transliteration: rājā tu dharmeṇa hi pālayitvā mahāmatirdaṇḍadharaḥ prajānām| avāpya kṛtsnāṃ vasudhāṃ yathāvaditaścyuta ssvargamupaiti vidvān
translation: महामति: one who has great wisdom, विद्वान् learned man, राजा तु as for the king, कृत्स्नां entire, वसुधाम् earth, अवाप्य having acquired, प्रजानाम् for people, दण्डधरः holding Danda in hand, यथावत् in accordance with tradition, धर्मेण righteously, पालयित्वा having ruled, इतः  from here, च्युतः having been released, स्वर्गम् heaven, उपैति हि will ascend.
explanation: The highly sagacious and learned king, having acquired the entire earth and punishing the people in accordance with tradition and righteously ruling the kingdom, will ascend the his release (from this world). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे शततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह। किं मे धर्माद्विहीनस्य राजधर्मः करिष्यति।।2.101.1।।
transliteration: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha| kiṃ me dharmādvihīnasya rājadharmaḥ kariṣyati
translation: रामस्य Rama's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा on listening, भरतः Bharata, प्रत्युवाच ह replied, धर्मात् from righteousness, विहीनस्य devoid of, मे to me, राजधर्मः royal duties, किं करिष्यति of what use  to me.
explanation: On listening to Rama, Bharata replied Of what use shall be these royal duties to me, when I have fallen from righteousness?
comments: Bharata pleads with Rama to return -- informs passing away of king Dasaratha.

shloka_text: शाश्वतोऽयं सदा धर्मः स्थितोऽस्मासु नरर्षभ। ज्येष्ठेे पुत्रे स्थिते राजा न कनीयान् भवेन्नृपः।।2.101.2।।
transliteration: śāśvato'yaṃ sadā dharmaḥ sthito'smāsu nararṣabha| jyeṣṭhee putre sthite rājā na kanīyān bhavennṛpaḥ
translation: नरर्षभ best of men, अयम् this one, शाश्वतः ancient, धर्मः righteousness, अस्मासु in our race, सदा always, स्थितः exists, राजन् O king, ज्येष्ठपुत्रे the eldest son, स्थिते is there, कनीयान् younger one, नृपः king, न भवेत् can never become.
explanation: O best of men there is an ancient tradition in our race that the younger son cannot become king when the eldest is there.

shloka_text: स समृद्धां मया सार्धमयोध्यां गच्छ राघव। अभिषेचयचात्मानं कुलस्यास्य भवाय नः।।2.101.3।।
transliteration: sa samṛddhāṃ mayā sārdhamayodhyāṃ gaccha rāghava| abhiṣecayacātmānaṃ kulasyāsya bhavāya naḥ
translation: राघव Rama, सः he, मया सार्धम् with me, समृद्धाम् prosperous, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, गच्छ return, नः for us, अस्य कुलस्य for this race, भवाय for the good of, आत्मानम् yourself, अभिषेचय  coronated.
explanation: Therefore, O scion of the Raghu race, return along with me to prosperous Ayodhya and for the good of our race get your self coronated.

shloka_text: राजानं मानुषं प्राहु र्देवत्वे सम्मतो मम। यस्य धर्मार्थसहितं वृत्तमाहुरमानुषम्।।2.101.4।।
transliteration: rājānaṃ mānuṣaṃ prāhu rdevatve sammato mama| yasya dharmārthasahitaṃ vṛttamāhuramānuṣam
translation: राजानम् king, मानुषम् to be a man, प्राहुः is said (by the wise), यस्य whose, धर्मार्धसहितम् in conformity with righteousness and state craft, वृत्तम् conduct, अमानुषम् beyond human capacity, आहुः they say, मम my, देवत्वे godly, सम्मतः has been claimed.
explanation: Other think the king to be a human, but to me, he is divine since his conduct and the statecraft are superhuman as they are in conformity with righteousness.

shloka_text: केकयस्थे च मयि तु त्वयि चारण्य माश्रिते। दिवमार्यो गतो राजा यायजूक: सतां मतः।।2.101.5।।
transliteration: kekayasthe ca mayi tu tvayi cāraṇya māśrite| divamāryo gato rājā yāyajūka: satāṃ mataḥ
translation: मयि me, केकयस्थे while I was in Kekaya, त्वयि च when you, अरण्यम् to the forest, आश्रिते having taken refuge, आर्यः revered, यायजूकः ever performing sacrifices, सताम् by the virtuous, मतः esteemed, राजा king, दिवम् to heaven, गतः went.
explanation: While I was in Kekaya and you took refuge in the forest, venerable king (Dasaratha), who was always engaged in sacrifices and was held in high esteem by the virtuous, ascended to heaven.

shloka_text: निष्क्रान्तमात्रे भवति ससीते सहलक्ष्मणे। दुःखशोकाभिभूतस्तु राजा त्रिदिवमभ्यगात्।।2.101.6।।
transliteration: niṣkrāntamātre bhavati sasīte sahalakṣmaṇe| duḥkhaśokābhibhūtastu rājā tridivamabhyagāt
translation: ससीते along with Sita, सहलक्ष्मणे with Lakshmana, भवति when you, निष्क्रान्तमात्रे had just set out, राजा king, दुःखशोकाभिभूतः griefstricken, त्रिदिवम् to heaven, अभ्यगात् went.
explanation: As soon as you set out for the forest along with Sita and Lakshmana, the king, overwhelmed with grief, attained heaven.

shloka_text: उत्तिष्ठ पुरुषव्याघ्र क्रियतामुदकं पितुः। अहं चायं च शत्रुघ्नः पूर्वमेव कृतोदकौ।।2.101.7।।
transliteration: uttiṣṭha puruṣavyāghra kriyatāmudakaṃ pituḥ| ahaṃ cāyaṃ ca śatrughnaḥ pūrvameva kṛtodakau
translation: पुरुषव्याघ्रः O best of men, उत्तिष्ठ arise, पितुः to father, उदकम् traditional libation of water, क्रियताम् offer, अहं च I also, अयम् this, शत्रुघ्नश्च Satrughna also, पूर्वमेव already, कृतोदकौ  offered libations of water.
explanation: Arise, O best of men and offer libations to our father. I and Satrughna have already done so.

shloka_text: प्रियेण किल दत्तं हि पितृलोकेषु राघव। अक्षय्यं भवतीत्याहुर्भवांश्चैव पितुः प्रियः।।2.101.8।।
transliteration: priyeṇa kila dattaṃ hi pitṛlokeṣu rāghava| akṣayyaṃ bhavatītyāhurbhavāṃścaiva pituḥ priyaḥ
translation: राघव O Rama, प्रियेण by a dear one, दत्तम् offered, पितृलोकेषु in the world of manes, अक्षय्यम् भवति becomes eternal, इति thus, आहुः खलु people say indeed, भवांश्चैव you alone, पितुः to father, प्रियः is beloved.
explanation: O son of Raghu's race, it is said that whatever is offered by a dear son becomes eternal in the world of manes. You alone are the beloved son of our father.

shloka_text: त्वामेव शोचंस्तव दर्शनेप्सुस्त्वय्येव सक्तामनिवर्त्य बुद्धिम्। त्वया विहीन स्तव शोकमग्नस्त्वां संस्मरन्नस्तमितः पिता ते।।2.101.9।।
transliteration: tvāmeva śocaṃstava darśanepsustvayyeva saktāmanivartya buddhim| tvayā vihīna stava śokamagnastvāṃ saṃsmarannastamitaḥ pitā te
translation: ते your, पिता father, त्वया by you, विहीनः separated, त्वामेव about you, शोचन् grieving, तव your, दर्शनेप्सुः wishing to see, त्वय्येव in you alone, सक्ताम् fixing, बुद्धिम् mind, अनिवर्त्य without diverting, तव your, शोकमग्नः immersed in sorrow, त्वाम् you, संस्मरन् remembering, अस्तमितः departed.
explanation: Your father, deprived of you, brooding over you, wishing to behold you, unable to divert his mind fixed on you, remembering you alone and immersed in sorrow departed (from this world). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोत्तर शततम स्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredone sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तां श्रुत्वा करुणां वाचं पितुर्मरणसंहिताम्। राघवो भरते नोक्तां बभूव गतचेतनः।।2.102.1।।
transliteration: tāṃ śrutvā karuṇāṃ vācaṃ piturmaraṇasaṃhitām| rāghavo bharate noktāṃ babhūva gatacetanaḥ
translation: राघवः one born in the race of the Raghus (Rama), भरतेन by Bharata, उक्ताम् uttered, पितुः father's, मरणसंहिताम्  union with death, करुणाम् pitiable, तां those, वाचम् words, श्रुत्वा on hearing, गत चेतनः unconscious, बभूव became.
explanation: Having heard the words of Bharata regarding the death of his father, Rama became unconscious.
comments: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana's grief over king Dasaratha's death -- Rama and Lakshmana offer libations of water in Mandakini river

shloka_text: तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा वाग्वज्रंभरते नोक्त ममनोज्ञं परन्तपः।।2.102.2।। प्रगृह्य रामो बाहू वैपुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुमः। वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह।।2.102.3।।
transliteration: taṃ tu vajramivotsṛṣṭamāhave dānavāriṇā vāgvajraṃbharate nokta mamanojñaṃ parantapaḥ pragṛhya rāmo bāhū vaipuṣpitāgro yathā drumaḥ| vane paraśunā kṛttastathā bhuvi papāta ha
translation: परन्तपः destroyer of enemies, रामः Rama, आहवे in the battle, दानवारिणा by the enemy of demons (Indra), उत्सृष्टम् hurled, वज्रमिव like thunderbolt, अमनोज्ञम् unpleasant, भरतेन by Bharata, उक्तम् spoken, तम् that, वाग्वज्रम् thunderlike words, बाहू both arms, प्रगृह्य stretching forth, वने in the forest, परशुना by an axe, कृत्तः severed, पुष्पिताग्रः with flowering tops, द्रुमः tree, यथा as, तथा like that, भुवि on the ground, पपात ह fell down.
explanation: On hearing the thunderlike words spoken by Bharata afflicting the mind, like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra (enemy of demons) in a battle, Rama, the scorcher of enemies, stretching forth both his arms, fell down on the ground like a tree with flowering tops severed by an axe in the forest.

shloka_text: तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा वाग्वज्रंभरते नोक्त ममनोज्ञं परन्तपः।।2.102.2।। प्रगृह्य रामो बाहू वैपुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुमः। वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह।।2.102.3।।
transliteration: taṃ tu vajramivotsṛṣṭamāhave dānavāriṇā vāgvajraṃbharate nokta mamanojñaṃ parantapaḥ pragṛhya rāmo bāhū vaipuṣpitāgro yathā drumaḥ| vane paraśunā kṛttastathā bhuvi papāta ha
translation: परन्तपः destroyer of enemies, रामः Rama, आहवे in the battle, दानवारिणा by the enemy of demons (Indra), उत्सृष्टम् hurled, वज्रमिव like thunderbolt, अमनोज्ञम् unpleasant, भरतेन by Bharata, उक्तम् spoken, तम् that, वाग्वज्रम् thunderlike words, बाहू both arms, प्रगृह्य stretching forth, वने in the forest, परशुना by an axe, कृत्तः severed, पुष्पिताग्रः with flowering tops, द्रुमः tree, यथा as, तथा like that, भुवि on the ground, पपात ह fell down.
explanation: On hearing the thunderlike words spoken by Bharata afflicting the mind, like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra (enemy of demons) in a battle, Rama, the scorcher of enemies, stretching forth both his arms, fell down on the ground like a tree with flowering tops severed by an axe in the forest.

shloka_text: तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा वाग्वज्रंभरते नोक्त ममनोज्ञं परन्तपः।।2.102.2।। प्रगृह्य रामो बाहू वैपुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुमः। वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह।।2.102.3।।
transliteration: taṃ tu vajramivotsṛṣṭamāhave dānavāriṇā vāgvajraṃbharate nokta mamanojñaṃ parantapaḥ pragṛhya rāmo bāhū vaipuṣpitāgro yathā drumaḥ| vane paraśunā kṛttastathā bhuvi papāta ha
translation: परन्तपः destroyer of enemies, रामः Rama, आहवे in the battle, दानवारिणा by the enemy of demons (Indra), उत्सृष्टम् hurled, वज्रमिव like thunderbolt, अमनोज्ञम् unpleasant, भरतेन by Bharata, उक्तम् spoken, तम् that, वाग्वज्रम् thunderlike words, बाहू both arms, प्रगृह्य stretching forth, वने in the forest, परशुना by an axe, कृत्तः severed, पुष्पिताग्रः with flowering tops, द्रुमः tree, यथा as, तथा like that, भुवि on the ground, पपात ह fell down.
explanation: On hearing the thunderlike words spoken by Bharata afflicting the mind, like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra (enemy of demons) in a battle, Rama, the scorcher of enemies, stretching forth both his arms, fell down on the ground like a tree with flowering tops severed by an axe in the forest.

shloka_text: तथा हि पतितं रामं जगत्यां जगतीपतिम्। कूलघातपरिश्रान्तं प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्।।2.102. 4।। भ्रातरस्ते महेष्वासं सर्वतश्शोककर्शितम्। रुदन्तस्सह वैदेह्या सिषिचुस्सलिलेन वै।।2.102.5।।
transliteration: tathā hi patitaṃ rāmaṃ jagatyāṃ jagatīpatim| kūlaghātapariśrāntaṃ prasuptamiva kuñjaram||2.102. 4|| bhrātaraste maheṣvāsaṃ sarvataśśokakarśitam| rudantassaha vaidehyā siṣicussalilena vai
