translation: कृतात्मा man of firm determination, आत्मवान् selfpossessed, रामः Rama, एवम् in this way, विलपन्तम् lamenting, यशस्विनम् illustrious, दुःखितम् depressed, तं भरतम् that Bharata, प्रेक्ष्य seeing, समाश्वासयत् consoled him.
explanation: Having seen the illustrious Bharata lamenting that way, Rama, a man of firm determination and selfpossession, consoled him thus:

shloka_text: नाऽत्मनः कामकारोऽस्ति पुरुषोऽयमनीश्वरः। इतश्चेतरतश्चैनं कृतान्तः परिकर्षति।।2.105.15।।
transliteration: nā'tmanaḥ kāmakāro'sti puruṣo'yamanīśvaraḥ| itaścetarataścainaṃ kṛtāntaḥ parikarṣati
translation: आत्मनः by oneself, कामकारः to do at free will, नास्ति is not there, अयम् this, पुरुषः man, अनीश्वरः is not independent, कृतान्तः fate, एनम् him, इतश्च from this way, इतरतश्च or the  other way, परिकर्षति is pulled.
explanation: A man is neither independent nor competent to do any act on his free will. Fate pulls him this way or the other.

shloka_text: सर्वे क्षयान्ताः निचयाः पतनान्ता समुच्छ्रयाः। संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्।।2.105.16।।
transliteration: sarve kṣayāntāḥ nicayāḥ patanāntā samucchrayāḥ| saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ ca jīvitam
translation: सर्वे all, निचयाः accumulations of wealth, क्षयान्ताः deplete at the end, समुच्छ्रयाः elevated positions, पतनान्ताः degrade at the end, संयोगाः union, विप्रयोगान्ताः end in separation, जीवितम् life, मरणान्तम् has death at the end.
explanation: All accumulations of wealth deplete at the end. Every man who attains elevated positions falls at the end. Every union culminates in separation. Every life ends in death.

shloka_text: यथा फलानां पक्वानां नान्यत्र पतनाद्भयम्। एवं नरस्य जातस्य नान्यत्र मरणाद्भयम्।।2.105.17।।
transliteration: yathā phalānāṃ pakvānāṃ nānyatra patanādbhayam| evaṃ narasya jātasya nānyatra maraṇādbhayam
translation: पक्वानाम् ripened, फलानाम् fruits, पतनात् from falling down, अन्यत्र no other, भयम् fear, यथा as how, न not, एवम् in the same way, जातस्य of one who is born, नरस्य for a man, मरणात्  more than death, अन्यत्र from any other source, भयम् fear, न not.
explanation: The only fear of a ripened fruit is the fear of falling down (from the tree). In the same way every man who is born has no other fear except the fear of death.

shloka_text: यथाऽगारं दृढस्थूणं जीर्णं भूत्वाऽवसीदति। तथैव सीदन्ति नरा जरामृत्युवशं गताः।।2.105.18।।
transliteration: yathā'gāraṃ dṛḍhasthūṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ bhūtvā'vasīdati| tathaiva sīdanti narā jarāmṛtyuvaśaṃ gatāḥ
translation: दृढस्थूणम् with sturdy pillars, आगारम् house, यथा as, जीर्णं भूत्वा after getting dilapidated, अवसीदति decays, तथैव in the same way, नराः people, जरामृत्युवशंगताः under the sway of  old age and death, सीदन्ति are destroyed.
explanation: Even a house constructed with sturdy pillars gets dilapidated and ultimately decays. In the same way people under the sway of old age and death are destroyed (at last).

shloka_text: अत्येति रजनी या तु सा न प्रतिनिवर्तते। यात्येव यमुना पूर्णा समुद्रमुदकाकुलम्।।2.105.19।।
transliteration: atyeti rajanī yā tu sā na pratinivartate| yātyeva yamunā pūrṇā samudramudakākulam
translation: या such, रजनी night, अत्येति passes off, सा that one, न प्रतिनिवर्तते does not return, पूर्णा filled with waters, यमुना river Yamuna, उदकाकुलम् waterfilled, समुद्रम् to the ocean, यात्येव flows forever.
explanation: A night that once passe off does not return like the waters of river Yamuna that flow into the ocean filled with water (the water do not flow back into Yamuna).

shloka_text: अहोरात्राणि गच्छन्ति सर्वेषां प्राणिनामिह। अायूंषि क्षपयन्त्याशु ग्रीष्मे जलमिवांशवः।।2.105.20।।
transliteration: ahorātrāṇi gacchanti sarveṣāṃ prāṇināmiha| aāyūṃṣi kṣapayantyāśu grīṣme jalamivāṃśavaḥ
translation: इह in this world, गच्छन्ति are passing, अहोरात्राणि days and nights, ग्रीष्मे in summer, अंशवः rays of the sun, जलमिव like the water, सर्वेषाम् all, प्राणिनाम् living things', आयूंषि life span, आशु are quickly, क्षपयन्ति are decaying.
explanation: The passing days and nights quickly decrease the life span of all living beings in this world, like sunrays drying up the water in summer.

shloka_text: आत्मानमनुशोच त्वं किमन्यमनुशोचसि। आयुस्ते हीयते यस्य स्थितस्य च गतस्य च।।2.105.21।।
transliteration: ātmānamanuśoca tvaṃ kimanyamanuśocasi| āyuste hīyate yasya sthitasya ca gatasya ca
translation: स्थितस्य च whether you stand, गतस्य च or moving, यस्य whosoever, आयुः life span, हीयते decreases, आत्मानम् about you, त्वम् you, अनुशोच grieve, अन्यम् about others, किम् why, अनुशोचसि are you grieving?
explanation: Whether you are static or moving, your lifespan decreases. Therefore, you should only grieve about yourself and not for any one else.

shloka_text: सहैव मृत्युर्व्रजति सह मृत्युर्निषीदति। गत्वासुदीर्घमध्वानं सहमृत्युर्निवर्तते।।2.105.22।।
transliteration: sahaiva mṛtyurvrajati saha mṛtyurniṣīdati| gatvāsudīrghamadhvānaṃ sahamṛtyurnivartate
translation: मृत्युः death, सहैव along with you, व्रजति is moving, सह मृत्युः along with death, निषीदति a man sits, सुदीर्घम् very long, अध्वानम् way, गत्वा having gone, सहमृत्युः with death, निवर्तते is returning.
explanation: Death follows a man wherever he goes. When he sits, death sits with him. Even after travelling a very long distance, the man returns along with death.

shloka_text: गात्रेषु वलयः प्राप्ता श्श्वेताश्चैव शिरोरुहाः। जरया पुरुषो जीर्णः किं हि कृत्वा प्रभावयेत्।।2.105.23।।
transliteration: gātreṣu valayaḥ prāptā śśvetāścaiva śiroruhāḥ| jarayā puruṣo jīrṇaḥ kiṃ hi kṛtvā prabhāvayet
translation: गात्रेषु in man's limbs, वलय: wrinkles, प्राप्ताः are formed, शिरोरुहाश्चैव hair also, श्वेताः becomes grey, जरया with old age, जीर्णः one decays, पुरुषः a man, किं हि what, कृत्वा having done, प्रभावयेत् can influence.
explanation: Wrinkels form on the body and hair turns grey in old age. In this way, decayed with age, what can a man do to have control over death.

shloka_text: नन्दन्त्युदित आदित्ये नन्दन्त्यस्तमितेऽहनि। आत्मनो नावबुध्यन्ते मनुष्या जीवितक्षयम्।।2.105.24।।
transliteration: nandantyudita āditye nandantyastamite'hani| ātmano nāvabudhyante manuṣyā jīvitakṣayam
translation: मनुष्याः people, आदित्ये the Sun, उदिते rises, नन्दन्ति rejoice, रवौ when the Sun, आस्तमिते sets, नन्दन्ति rejoice, आत्मनः their own, जीवितक्षयम् decline of life span, नावबुद्ध्यन्ते are not aware of.
explanation: People rejoice when the Sun rises and rejoice when the Sun sets. But they are unaware of the decline of the life span of their own.

shloka_text: हृष्यन्त्यृतुमुखं दृष्ट्वा नवं नवमिहागतम्। ऋतूनां परिवर्तेन प्राणिनां प्राणसङ्क्षयः।।2.105.25।।
transliteration: hṛṣyantyṛtumukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā navaṃ navamihāgatam| ṛtūnāṃ parivartena prāṇināṃ prāṇasaṅkṣayaḥ
translation: ऋतुमुखम् setting of a season, दृष्ट्वा having seen, इह now, नवं नवम् something new             (flowers and fruits), आगतम् have arrived, हृष्यन्ति feel delighted, ऋतूनाम् of seasons, परिवर्तेन by changes, प्राणिनाम् of living beings', प्राणसङ्क्षयः life span decreases.
explanation: At the advent of each new season men feel delighted to see the newly blossomed flowers and fruits. But with the change of the scasons the life span also diminishes.

shloka_text: यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे। समेत्य च व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कञ्चन।।2.105.26।। एवं भार्याश्चपुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च धनानि च। समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः।।2.105.27।।
transliteration: yathā kāṣṭhaṃ ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca sameyātāṃ mahārṇave| sametya ca vyapeyātāṃ kālamāsādya kañcana evaṃ bhāryāścaputrāśca jñātayaśca dhanāni ca| sametya vyavadhāvanti dhruvo hyeṣāṃ vinābhavaḥ
translation: यथा as, महार्णवे in a mighty ocean, काष्ठं च a piece of wood, काष्ठं च another piece of wood, समेयाताम् might meet, समेत्य having met, कञ्चन कालम् for a short span, आसाद्य remaining together, व्यपेयातां च get separated, एवम् in the same way, भार्याश्च wives, पुत्राश्च sons, ज्ञातयश्च relatives, धनानि च riches, समेत्य after coming together, व्यवधावन्ति get separated, एषाम् their, विनाभवः separation, ध्रुवो हि is certain.
explanation: In a mighty ocean, two pieces of logs meet one another, float together and in due course get separated. In the same way wives, sons, relatives and riches remain together for some time and thereafter get separated. Their separation is certain.

shloka_text: यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे। समेत्य च व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कञ्चन।।2.105.26।। एवं भार्याश्चपुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च धनानि च। समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः।।2.105.27।।
transliteration: yathā kāṣṭhaṃ ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca sameyātāṃ mahārṇave| sametya ca vyapeyātāṃ kālamāsādya kañcana evaṃ bhāryāścaputrāśca jñātayaśca dhanāni ca| sametya vyavadhāvanti dhruvo hyeṣāṃ vinābhavaḥ
translation: यथा as, महार्णवे in a mighty ocean, काष्ठं च a piece of wood, काष्ठं च another piece of wood, समेयाताम् might meet, समेत्य having met, कञ्चन कालम् for a short span, आसाद्य remaining together, व्यपेयातां च get separated, एवम् in the same way, भार्याश्च wives, पुत्राश्च sons, ज्ञातयश्च relatives, धनानि च riches, समेत्य after coming together, व्यवधावन्ति get separated, एषाम् their, विनाभवः separation, ध्रुवो हि is certain.
explanation: In a mighty ocean, two pieces of logs meet one another, float together and in due course get separated. In the same way wives, sons, relatives and riches remain together for some time and thereafter get separated. Their separation is certain.

shloka_text: नात्र कश्चिद्यथाभावं प्राणी समभिवर्तते। तेन तस्मिन्न सामर्थ्यं प्रेतस्या स्त्यनुशोचतः।।2.105.28।।
transliteration: nātra kaścidyathābhāvaṃ prāṇī samabhivartate| tena tasminna sāmarthyaṃ pretasyā styanuśocataḥ
translation: अत्र then in this world, कश्चित् प्राणी any living being, यथाभावम् as one likes, न समभिवर्तते does not go, तेन therefore, प्रेतस्य for the dead, अनुशोचतः for one who grieves, तस्मिन् in the matter of death, सामर्थ्यम् capability, नास्ति not there.
explanation: No living being in this world can act as he likes. Therefore, no one should grieve for the dead.

shloka_text: यथा हि सार्थं गच्छन्तं ब्रूयात्कश्चित्पथि स्थितः। अहमप्यागमिष्यामि पृष्ठतो भवता मिति।।2.105.29।। एवं पूर्वैर्गतो मार्गः पितृपैतामहो ध्रुवः। तमापन्नः कथं शोचेद्यस्य नास्ति व्यतिक्रमः।।2.105.30।।
transliteration: yathā hi sārthaṃ gacchantaṃ brūyātkaścitpathi sthitaḥ| ahamapyāgamiṣyāmi pṛṣṭhato bhavatā miti evaṃ pūrvairgato mārgaḥ pitṛpaitāmaho dhruvaḥ| tamāpannaḥ kathaṃ śocedyasya nāsti vyatikramaḥ
translation: गच्छन्तम् while passing, सार्थम् caravan, (कच्चित्) पथि on the wayside, स्थितः standing, अहमपि I also, भवताम् your, पृष्ठतः behind, आगमिष्यामि I am coming, इति thus, यथा as, ब्रूयात् one may say, एवम् in this way, पूर्वैः by ancestors, गतः taken, पितृपैतामहः folowed by fathers and forefathers, मार्गः the path, ध्रुवः is certain, यस्य whosoever, व्यतिक्रमः violation, नास्ति not possible, तम् that very road, आपन्नः following, कथम् why, शोचेत् should one grieve?
explanation: Like a man standing on the wayside says to a passing caravan, 'I am following you', and follows them, the road taken by our fathers and forefathers is certain for every one and cannot be violated by a person treading that path. (So) why should a man grieve?

shloka_text: यथा हि सार्थं गच्छन्तं ब्रूयात्कश्चित्पथि स्थितः। अहमप्यागमिष्यामि पृष्ठतो भवता मिति।।2.105.29।। एवं पूर्वैर्गतो मार्गः पितृपैतामहो ध्रुवः। तमापन्नः कथं शोचेद्यस्य नास्ति व्यतिक्रमः।।2.105.30।।
transliteration: yathā hi sārthaṃ gacchantaṃ brūyātkaścitpathi sthitaḥ| ahamapyāgamiṣyāmi pṛṣṭhato bhavatā miti evaṃ pūrvairgato mārgaḥ pitṛpaitāmaho dhruvaḥ| tamāpannaḥ kathaṃ śocedyasya nāsti vyatikramaḥ
translation: गच्छन्तम् while passing, सार्थम् caravan, (कच्चित्) पथि on the wayside, स्थितः standing, अहमपि I also, भवताम् your, पृष्ठतः behind, आगमिष्यामि I am coming, इति thus, यथा as, ब्रूयात् one may say, एवम् in this way, पूर्वैः by ancestors, गतः taken, पितृपैतामहः folowed by fathers and forefathers, मार्गः the path, ध्रुवः is certain, यस्य whosoever, व्यतिक्रमः violation, नास्ति not possible, तम् that very road, आपन्नः following, कथम् why, शोचेत् should one grieve?
explanation: Like a man standing on the wayside says to a passing caravan, 'I am following you', and follows them, the road taken by our fathers and forefathers is certain for every one and cannot be violated by a person treading that path. (So) why should a man grieve?

shloka_text: वयसः पतमानस्य स्रोतसो वाऽनिवर्तिनः। आत्मा सुखे नियोक्तव्यस्सुखभाजः प्रजाः स्मृताः।।2.105.31।।
transliteration: vayasaḥ patamānasya srotaso vā'nivartinaḥ| ātmā sukhe niyoktavyassukhabhājaḥ prajāḥ smṛtāḥ
translation: स्रोतसो वा like the flow, अनिवर्तिनः never returns, वयसः of age, पतमानस्य while declining, आत्मा mind, सुखे in happiness (in the righteous act as source of hapiness),  नियोक्तव्यः is to be established, प्रजाः people, सुखभाजः tend to be happy, स्मृताः it is said.
explanation: Like the flow of water which never reverts to its source, age passes. Therefore, a man must employ his self in righteous acts that bring him happiness. By doing so, it is said, people will always be happy.

shloka_text: धर्मात्मा स शुभैः कृत्स्नैः क्रतुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः। स्वर्गं दशरथः प्राप्तः पिता नः पृथिवीपतिः।।2.105.32।।
transliteration: dharmātmā sa śubhaiḥ kṛtsnaiḥ kratubhiścāptadakṣiṇaiḥ| svargaṃ daśarathaḥ prāptaḥ pitā naḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
translation: न: our, पिता father, धर्मात्मा righteous one, स: पृथिवीपतिः that lord of the earth, दशरथ: Dasratha, शुभैः by auspicious, कृत्स्नैः wholly, आप्तदक्षिणैः by offering charities, क्रतुभिः by performing sacrifices, स्वर्गं to heaven, गतः went.
explanation: Our righteous father and lord of the earth, Dasaratha, attained heaven by giving abundant charities and performing several sacrifices in accordance with tradition.

shloka_text: भृत्यानां भरणात्सम्यक्प्रजानां परिपालनात्। अर्थादानाच्च धर्मेण पिता न स्त्रिदिवंगतः।।2.105.33।।
transliteration: bhṛtyānāṃ bharaṇātsamyakprajānāṃ paripālanāt| arthādānācca dharmeṇa pitā na stridivaṃgataḥ
translation: नः our, पिता father, भृत्यानाम् of dependents, भरणात् by nourishing, सम्यक् splendidly, प्रजानाम् subjects, परिपालनात् by governing, धर्मेण in righteous ways, अर्थानाम् of the wealth, आदानात् accepting, त्रिदिवम् heaven, गतः went.
explanation: Our father nourished his dependents, splendidly governed his subjects and accepted  wealth through righteous ways. Because of these pious acts, he could go to heaven.

shloka_text: कर्मभि स्तु शुभैरिष्टैः क्रतुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः। स्वर्गं दशरथः प्राप्तः पिता नः पृथिवीपतिः।।2.105.34।।
transliteration: karmabhi stu śubhairiṣṭaiḥ kratubhiścāptadakṣiṇaiḥ| svargaṃ daśarathaḥ prāptaḥ pitā naḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
translation: नः our, पिता father, पृथिवीपतिः lord of the earth, दशरथः Dasaratha, शुभैः auspicious, कर्मभिः  with acts, आप्तदक्षिणैः with abundant charities, इष्टैः offerings of, क्रतुभिश्च with sacrifices, स्वर्गम् heaven, प्राप्तः reached.
explanation: Dasaratha, our father and lord of the earth, reached heaven by performing auspicious acts and offering abundant charities in sacrifices.

shloka_text: इष्ट्वा बहुविधैर्यज्ञैर्भोगां श्चावाप्य पुष्कलान्। उत्तमं चायुरासाद्य स्वर्गतः पृथिवीपतिः।।2.105.35।।
transliteration: iṣṭvā bahuvidhairyajñairbhogāṃ ścāvāpya puṣkalān| uttamaṃ cāyurāsādya svargataḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
translation: पृथिवीपतिः lord of the earth, बहुविधैः by several kinds of, यज्ञैः with sacrifices, इष्ट्वा having performed, पुष्कलान् abundance of, भोगान् pleasures, अवाप्य च having enjoyed, उत्तमम् excellent, आयुश्च life also, आसाद्य having obtained , स्वर्गतः went to heaven.
explanation: King Dasaratha, lord of the earth, having performed various kinds of sacrifices and securing a long life, enjoyed abundance of pleasures and attained heaven.

shloka_text: आयुरुत्तममासाद्य भोगानपि च राघवः। स न शोच्यः पिता तात स्वर्गत स्सत्कृत स्सताम्।।2.105.36।।
transliteration: āyuruttamamāsādya bhogānapi ca rāghavaḥ| sa na śocyaḥ pitā tāta svargata ssatkṛta ssatām
translation: तात O dear, सताम् for the virtuous, सत्कृतः honoured, उत्तमम् best of, आयुः life, भोगानपि pleasures, आसाद्य having enjoyed, स्वर्गतः attained the heaven, पिता father, स राघवः that Dasaratha, न शोच्यः is not to be grieved.
explanation: O dear our father, king Dasaratha, who was honoured by the virtuous and enjoyed the best of pleasures attained heaven after a long life. Therefore, he is not to be grieved over.

shloka_text: स जीर्णं मानुषं देहं परित्यज्य पिता हि नः। दैवीमृद्धिमनुप्राप्तो ब्रह्मलोकविहारिणीम्।।2.105.37।।
transliteration: sa jīrṇaṃ mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ parityajya pitā hi naḥ| daivīmṛddhimanuprāpto brahmalokavihāriṇīm
translation: नः our, पिता father, सः king Dasaratha, जीर्णम् wornout, मानुषं देहम् mortal body, परित्यज्य  having abandoned, ब्रह्मलोकविहारिणीम् wandering in the world of Brahma, दैवीम् divine,  ऋद्धिम् treasure, अनुप्राप्तः हि obtained.
explanation: Our father, king Dasaratha, abandoned the wornout mortal body, and obtained divine prosperity of wandering in the world of Brahma.

shloka_text: तं तु नैवंविधः कश्चित्प्राज्ञ श्शोचितुमर्हति। तत्विधो मद्विधश्चापि श्रुतवान्बुद्धिमत्तरः।।2.105.38।।
transliteration: taṃ tu naivaṃvidhaḥ kaścitprājña śśocitumarhati| tatvidho madvidhaścāpi śrutavānbuddhimattaraḥ
translation: श्रुतवान् proficient in scriptural knowledge, बुद्धिमत्तरः highly sagacious, एवंविधः like this, प्राज्ञः learned man, कश्चित् none, तत्विध: like you, मद्विधश्चापि like me, तम् about him, शोचितुम् to mourn, नार्हति not proper.
explanation: No one like you or me should ever mourn about this highly sagacious and learned king who was proficient in scriptural knowledge.

shloka_text: एते बहुविधा शोका विलापरुदिते तथा। वर्जनीया हि धीरेण सर्वावस्थासु धीमता।।2.105.39।।
transliteration: ete bahuvidhā śokā vilāparudite tathā| varjanīyā hi dhīreṇa sarvāvasthāsu dhīmatā
translation: धीरेण courageously, धीमता by a wise man, बहुविधाः different, एते these, शोकाः griefs, तथा also, विलापरुदिते words of lamentation and this crying, सर्वावस्थासु in all circumstances, वर्जनीयाः हि should be avoided.
explanation: A wise man, holding on to his fortitude in all circumstances, should avoid such occasions of grief, these words of lamentation and this crying.

shloka_text: स स्वस्थो भव मा शोचेर्यात्वा चावसतां पुरीम्। तथा पित्रा नियुक्तोऽसि वशिना वदतां वर।।2.105.40।।
transliteration: sa svastho bhava mā śoceryātvā cāvasatāṃ purīm| tathā pitrā niyukto'si vaśinā vadatāṃ vara
translation: वदताम् वर the foremost of the eloquent, सः that you, स्वस्थः भव compose yourself, शोचेः  in grief, मा not, यात्वा having returned, तां पुरीम् to that city (Ayodhya), आवस reside, वशिना  by a man of selfcontrol, पित्रा by father, तथा like that, नियुक्तः असि you have been commanded.
explanation: O foremost of the eloquent, compose yourself. Do not grieve. Return to the city (Ayodhya) and reside there. You have been commanded so by our father who was a man of selfcontrol.

shloka_text: यत्राहमपि तेनैव नियुक्तः पुण्यकर्मणा। तत्रैवाहं करिष्यामि पितुरार्यस्य शासनम्।।2.105.41।।
transliteration: yatrāhamapi tenaiva niyuktaḥ puṇyakarmaṇā| tatraivāhaṃ kariṣyāmi piturāryasya śāsanam
translation: अहमपि I also, पुण्यकर्मणा by a man of sacred deeds, तेनैव by him (king Dasaratha), यत्र  wherever one, नियुक्तः have been commanded, तत्रैव that one only, आर्यस्य noble, पितुः father's, शासनम् order, करिष्यामि shall do.
explanation: I shall also stick to the command of our noble father who was a man of sacred deeds.

shloka_text: न मया शासनं तस्य त्यक्तुं न्याय्य मरिन्दम। स त्वयापि सदा मान्यं स वै बन्धु स नः पिता।।2.105.42।।
transliteration: na mayā śāsanaṃ tasya tyaktuṃ nyāyya marindama| sa tvayāpi sadā mānyaṃ sa vai bandhu sa naḥ pitā
translation: अरिन्दम O subduer of enemies, मया by me, तस्य his, शासनम् order, त्यक्तुम् to discard, न न्याय्यम् is not proper, त्वयापि by you also, तत् that one, सदा always, मान्यम् to be respected, सः he, नः for us, बन्धुः वै relation indeed, सः he, पिता father.
explanation: O subduer of enemies, I cannot violate the order of the king. You also must respect it for he is our father and friend indeed.

shloka_text: तद्वचः पितुरेवाहं सम्मतं धर्मचारिणः। कर्मणा पालयिष्यामि वनवासेन राघव।।2.105.43।।
transliteration: tadvacaḥ piturevāhaṃ sammataṃ dharmacāriṇaḥ| karmaṇā pālayiṣyāmi vanavāsena rāghava
translation: राघव O Bharata, तत् therefore, अहम् I, धर्मचारिणः of the champion of righteousness, पितुः father's, सम्मतम् acceptable, वचः एव word only, वनवासेन by dwelling in the forest, कर्मणा by that act, पालयिष्यामि I will obey.
explanation: O Bharata, I will, therefore, obey the command of our venerable father, the champion of righteousness, by living in the forest.

shloka_text: धार्मिकेणानृशंसेन नरेण गुरुवर्तिना। भवितव्यं नरव्याघ्र परलोकं जिगीषता।।2.105.44।।
transliteration: dhārmikeṇānṛśaṃsena nareṇa guruvartinā| bhavitavyaṃ naravyāghra paralokaṃ jigīṣatā
translation: नरव्याघ्र O best of men, परलोकम् the next world, जिगीषता by one who aspires to conquer, नरेण by a man, धार्मिकेण by being virtuous, नृशंसेन compassionate, गुरुवर्तिना obedient to preceptors, भवितव्यम् shall happen.
explanation: O best of men, if a man aspires to conquer the higher world, he should remain  virtuous, compassionate and obedient to his preceptors.

shloka_text: आत्मानमनुतिष्ठत्वं स्वभावेन नरर्षभ। निशाम्यतु शुभं वृत्तं पितुर्दशरथस्य नः।।2.105.45।।
transliteration: ātmānamanutiṣṭhatvaṃ svabhāvena nararṣabha| niśāmyatu śubhaṃ vṛttaṃ piturdaśarathasya naḥ
translation: नरर्षभ O best of men, नः our, पितुः father, दशरथस्य Dasaratha's, शुभम् auspicious, वृत्तम्  conduct, निशाम्य having seen, त्वम् you, आत्मानम् yourself, स्वभावेन with your duty, अनुतिष्ठ stick to.
explanation: O best of men, having seen the auspicious life of our father Dasaratha and his conduct, you also stick to your own duty.

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महात्मा पितुर्निदेश प्रतिपालनार्थम्। यवीयसं भ्रातरमर्थवच्च प्रभुर्मुहूर्ताद्विरराम रामः।।2.105.46।।
transliteration: ityevamuktvā vacanaṃ mahātmā piturnideśa pratipālanārtham| yavīyasaṃ bhrātaramarthavacca prabhurmuhūrtādvirarāma rāmaḥ
translation: महात्मा magnanimous, प्रभुः competent, रामः Rama, यवीयसम् younger, भ्रातरम् brother, इत्येवम् in this way, पितुः father's, निदेशप्रतिपालनार्थम् to obey the command of his father, अर्थवत् significant, वचनम् words, उक्त्वा having said, मुहूर्तात् in a moment, विरराम became silent.
explanation: Rama, the magnanimous lord, addressed his younger brother Bharata with words full of significance, saying, Obey father's command and remained silent in a moment. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredfifth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु विरते रामे वचनमर्थवत्। ततो मन्दाकिनीतीरे रामं प्रकृतिवत्सलम्।।2.106.1।। उवाच भरत श्चित्रं धार्मिको धार्मिकं वचः।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu virate rāme vacanamarthavat| tato mandākinītīre rāmaṃ prakṛtivatsalam uvāca bharata ścitraṃ dhārmiko dhārmikaṃ vacaḥ|
translation: रामे when Rama, एवम् in this way, अर्थवत् meaningful, वचनम् words, उक्त्वा having uttered, विरते had rested, ततः then, धार्मिकः righteous one, भरतः Bharata, मन्दाकिनी river Mandakini, तीरे on the bank, प्रकृतिवत्सलम् affectionate by nature, धार्मिकम् virtuous, रामम् Rama, धार्मिकम् conforming to righteouness, चित्रम् clear, वचः words, उवाच said.
explanation: Rama remained silent after saying these meaningful words on the bank of river Mandakini. Then the Bharata, conforming to righteousness, replied in clear words to the virtuous Rama who was affectionate by nature.
comments: Bharata pleads with Rama in several ways -- all priests, mothers etc. extol Bharata -- Rama determines to respect his father's word.

shloka_text: को हि स्यादीदृशो लोके यादृश स्त्वमरिन्दमः।।2.106.2।। न त्वां प्रव्यथयेद्दुःखं प्रीतिर्वा नप्रहर्षयेत्। सम्मतश्चासि वृद्धानां तांश्च पृच्छसि संशयान्।।2.106.3।।
transliteration: ko hi syādīdṛśo loke yādṛśa stvamarindamaḥ na tvāṃ pravyathayedduḥkhaṃ prītirvā napraharṣayet| sammataścāsi vṛddhānāṃ tāṃśca pṛcchasi saṃśayān
translation: अरिन्दम O subduer of enemies (Rama), त्वम् you, यादृशः of such nature, ईदृशः of such person, लोके in the world, कोहि स्यात् who he may be, त्वाम् you, दुःखम् sarrow, न प्रव्यथयेत् does not pain, प्रीतिः pleasure, न वा प्रहर्षयेत् does not delight, वृद्धानाम् for the elders, सम्मतः असि beloved,  तांश्च them, संशयान् doubts, पृच्छसि ask them.
explanation: O subduer of enemies, you are of such nature that neither sorrow pains you nor pleasure delights you. There are none in this world like you. You are loved by the elders, for you seek their counsel whenever you have doubts.

shloka_text: को हि स्यादीदृशो लोके यादृश स्त्वमरिन्दम।।2.106.2।। न त्वां प्रव्यथयेद्दुःखं प्रीतिर्वा नप्रहर्षयेत्। सम्मतश्चासि वृद्धानां तांश्च पृच्छसि संशयान्।।2.106.3।।
transliteration: ko hi syādīdṛśo loke yādṛśa stvamarindama na tvāṃ pravyathayedduḥkhaṃ prītirvā napraharṣayet| sammataścāsi vṛddhānāṃ tāṃśca pṛcchasi saṃśayān
translation: अरिन्दम O subduer of enemies (Rama), त्वम् you, यादृशः of such nature, ईदृशः of such person, लोके in the world, कोहि स्यात् who he may be, त्वाम् you, दुःखम् sarrow, न प्रव्यथयेत् does not pain, प्रीतिः pleasure, न वा प्रहर्षयेत् does not delight, वृद्धानाम् for the elders, सम्मतः असि beloved,  तांश्च them, संशयान् doubts, पृच्छसि ask them.
explanation: O subduer of enemies, you are of such nature that neither sorrow pains you nor pleasure delights you. There are none in this world like you. You are loved by the elders, for you seek their counsel whenever you have doubts.

shloka_text: यथा मृत स्तथा जीवन्यथाऽसति तथा सति। यस्यैष बुद्धिलाभ स्स्यात्परितप्येत केन सः।।2.106.4।।
transliteration: yathā mṛta stathā jīvanyathā'sati tathā sati| yasyaiṣa buddhilābha ssyātparitapyeta kena saḥ
translation: मृतः the dead, यथा as, जीवन् while living, तथा in the same way, असति about evil man, यथा same way सति about virtuous man, तथा like that, यस्य to whom, एषः this, बुद्धिलाभः gains of intellect, स्यात् becomes, सः he, केन by what, परितप्येत is distressed.
explanation: One should accept life and death, vice and virtue equally. How can one be afflicted when he has gained such an intellect?

shloka_text: परावरज्ञो यश्च स्याद् यथा त्वं मनुजाधिप। स एव व्यसनं प्राप्य न विषीदितुमर्हति।।2.106.5।।
transliteration: parāvarajño yaśca syād yathā tvaṃ manujādhipa| sa eva vyasanaṃ prāpya na viṣīditumarhati
translation: मनुजाधिप O lord of men, यः who  त्वं यथा like you, परावरज्ञः knower of past and future, सः that person, एव this, व्यसनम् distress, प्राप्य having obtained, विषीदितुं to lament, न अर्हति is not proper.
explanation: O lord of men, it is not proper for a person like you who knows the past and the future of human beings to feel distressed and lament over it.

shloka_text: अमरोपमसत्त्व स्त्वं महात्मा सत्यसङ्गरः। सर्वज्ञ स्सर्वदर्शी च बुद्धिमांश्चासि राघव।।2.106.6।।
transliteration: amaropamasattva stvaṃ mahātmā satyasaṅgaraḥ| sarvajña ssarvadarśī ca buddhimāṃścāsi rāghava
translation: राघव Rama, महात्मा the magnanimous one, त्वम् you, अमरोपमसत्त्वः resemble gods in nature, सत्यसङ्गरः true to your promis, सर्वज्ञः allknowing, सर्वदर्शी च allseeing, बुद्धिमांश्च असि you are a man of wisdom.
explanation: O magnanimous Rama, your nature is divine and you are true to your promises. You are omniscient, allseeing and wise.

shloka_text: न त्वामेवं गुणैर्युक्तं प्रभवाभवकोविदम्। अविषह्यतमं दुःखमासादयितुमर्हति।।2.106.7।।
transliteration: na tvāmevaṃ guṇairyuktaṃ prabhavābhavakovidam| aviṣahyatamaṃ duḥkhamāsādayitumarhati
translation: एवं गुणैः by such virtues, युक्तम् endowed with, प्रभवाभवकोविदम् cognizant of life and death, त्वाम् you, अविषह्यतमम् insufferable, दुःखम् grief, आसादयितुम् to reach, नार्हति not proper.
explanation: It is not proper for a virtuous man like you, who is cognizant in matters of life and death, to be overwhelmed by such insufferable grief.

shloka_text: प्रोषिते मयि यत्पापं मात्रा मत्कारणात्कृतम्। क्षुद्रया तदनिष्टं मे प्रसीदतु भवान्मम।।2.106.8।।
transliteration: proṣite mayi yatpāpaṃ mātrā matkāraṇātkṛtam| kṣudrayā tadaniṣṭaṃ me prasīdatu bhavānmama
translation: मयि me, प्रोषिते when I was away from home, क्षुद्रया by the meanminded, मात्रा by mother, मत्कारणात् for my sake, यत् पापम् which sin, कृतम् has been committed, तत् that one, मे to me, अनिष्टम् that disagreeable act, भवान् you, मम me, प्रसीदतु graciously pardon.
explanation: When I was away from home, my meanminded mother committed a sin for my sake which I never wished. You may pardon me graciously.

shloka_text: धर्मबन्धेन बद्धोऽस्मि तेनेमां नेह मातरम्। हन्मितीव्रेण दण्डेन दण्डार्हां पापकारिणीम्।।2.106.9।।
transliteration: dharmabandhena baddho'smi tenemāṃ neha mātaram| hanmitīvreṇa daṇḍena daṇḍārhāṃ pāpakāriṇīm
translation: धर्मबन्धेन by a bond of righteousness, बद्धः अस्मि I am bound, तेन for that reason, इह now, दण्डार्हाम् deserving punishment, पापकारिणीम् doing sinful acts, इमां मातरम् this mother, तीव्रेण severe, दण्डेन punishment, न हन्मि do not slay.
explanation: I am bound by a bond of righteousness for which I am unble to slay my mother who deserves severe punishment for her sinful acts.

shloka_text: कथं दशरथा ज्जात श्शुद्धाभिजनकर्मणः। जानन् धर्ममधर्मिष्ठं कुर्यां कर्म जुगुप्सितम्।।2.106.10।।
transliteration: kathaṃ daśarathā jjāta śśuddhābhijanakarmaṇaḥ| jānan dharmamadharmiṣṭhaṃ kuryāṃ karma jugupsitam
translation: शुद्धाभिजनकर्मणः of noble race and righteous deeds, दशरथात् from Dasaratha, जातः born of, धर्मम् righteousness, जानन् knowing, अधर्मिष्ठम् unrighteous, जुगुप्सितम् reprehensible, कर्म deed, कथम् how, कुर्याम् shall I do?.
explanation: How shall I, born to Dasaratha of noble race and righteous deeds, with the knowledge of dharma, do such a reprehensible and unrighteous deed?

shloka_text: गुरुः क्रियावान्वृद्धश्च राजा प्रेतः पितेतिच। तातं न परिगर्हेयं दैवतं चेति संसदि।।2.106.11।।
transliteration: guruḥ kriyāvānvṛddhaśca rājā pretaḥ pitetica| tātaṃ na parigarheyaṃ daivataṃ ceti saṃsadi
translation: गुरुः preceptor, क्रियावान् one who is devoted to meritorious acts, वृद्धश्च old, राजा king, प्रेतः departed soul, पिता father, इति च for this, दैवतं चेति as a god, संसदि in the assembly, तातम् father, न परिगर्हेयम् I cannot reproach.
explanation: King Dasaratha, my father and preceptor, is godlike to me. Devoted to meritorious acts, he departed from this world in his old age. For this reason, I cannot reproach him (publicly) in this assembly (of men).

shloka_text: को हि धर्मार्थयोर्हीनमीदृशं कर्म किल्बिषम्। स्त्रियाः प्रियं चिकीर्षु स्सन्कुर्याद्धर्मज्ञ धर्मवित्।।2.106.12।।
transliteration: ko hi dharmārthayorhīnamīdṛśaṃ karma kilbiṣam| striyāḥ priyaṃ cikīrṣu ssankuryāddharmajña dharmavit
translation: धर्मज्ञ O knower of ways of righteousness, धर्मवित् knower of righeousness, को हि who indeed, स्त्रियाः for the sake of a women, प्रियम् pleasure, चिकीर्षुः सन् desirous of doing, धर्मार्थयोः for dharma and artha, हीनम् bereft of, किल्बिषम् sinful, ईदृशम् this kind of, कर्म act, कुर्यात् will do?
explanation: O Rama, conversant with righteousness, will any one who knows the meaning of righteousness, do such a sinful act contrary to dharma and artha to please a woman?

shloka_text: अन्तकाले हि भूतानि मुह्यन्तीति पुरा श्रुतिः। राज्ञैवं कुर्वता लोके प्रत्यक्षं सा श्रुतिः कृता।।2.106.13।।
transliteration: antakāle hi bhūtāni muhyantīti purā śrutiḥ| rājñaivaṃ kurvatā loke pratyakṣaṃ sā śrutiḥ kṛtā
translation: भूतानि living beings, अन्तकाले at the time of death, मुह्यन्ति are deluded, इति thus, पुराश्रुतिः ancient saying, एवम् in this way, कुर्वता by doing, राज्ञा by the king, सा श्रुतिः that adage, लोके in this world, प्रत्यक्षं explicitly, कृता has been made.
explanation: There is an ancient saying that at the time of death, the intellect of people is deluded. By conducting himself in this way, king Dasaratha has proved it.

shloka_text: साध्वर्थमभिसन्धाय क्रोधान्मोहाच्च साहसात्। तातस्य यदतिक्रान्तं प्रत्याहरतु तद्भवान्।।2.106.14।।
transliteration: sādhvarthamabhisandhāya krodhānmohācca sāhasāt| tātasya yadatikrāntaṃ pratyāharatu tadbhavān
translation: क्रोधात् due to anger, मोहात् due to delusion, साहसात् due to a spirit of adventure, तातस्य father's, यत् अतिक्रान्तम् whichever trangression, तत् that, भवान् you, साधु prudently, अर्थम् meaning, अभिसन्धाय having thought over, प्रत्याहरतु will set it right.
explanation: Our father has trangressed righteousness due to anger or delusion or recklessness. Therefore, you may think over the matter prudently and set it right.

shloka_text: पितुर्हि समतिक्रान्तं पुत्रो यस्साधु मन्यते। तदपत्यं मतं लोके विपरीतमतोऽन्यथा।।2.106.15।।
transliteration: piturhi samatikrāntaṃ putro yassādhu manyate| tadapatyaṃ mataṃ loke viparītamato'nyathā
translation: यः पुत्रः that son, पितुः father's, समतिक्रान्तम् transgressions, साधु as right, मन्यते sets, तत् that son, लोके in the world, अपत्यम् as son, मतम् is considered, अतः for this, अन्यथा contrary happens, विपरीतम् reverse is so.
explanation: One who sets right the wrongs done by his father is a true son. Otherwise the son becomes just the opposite. (He is not  a son to the father).

shloka_text: तदपत्यं भवानस्तु मा भवान् दुष्कृतं पितुः। अभिपत्ता कृतं कर्म लोके धीरविगर्हितम्।।2.106.16।।
transliteration: tadapatyaṃ bhavānastu mā bhavān duṣkṛtaṃ pituḥ| abhipattā kṛtaṃ karma loke dhīravigarhitam
translation: भवान् you, तत् अपत्यम् अस्तु be such a son, लोके in this world, धीरविगर्हितम् condemned by men of wisdom, दुष्कृतम् sinful, पितुः father's, कृतम् committed, कर्म act, भवान् you, अभिपत्ता an approver, मास्तु let not become.
explanation: So be a worthy son and let not the sinful act committed by our father and condemned by men of wisdom be approved by you.

shloka_text: कैकेयीं मां च तातं च सुहृदो बान्धवांश्च नः। पौरजानपदान्सर्वांस्त्रातु सर्वमिदं भवान्।।2.106.17।।
transliteration: kaikeyīṃ māṃ ca tātaṃ ca suhṛdo bāndhavāṃśca naḥ| paurajānapadānsarvāṃstrātu sarvamidaṃ bhavān
translation: भवान् you, कैकेयीम् Kaikeyi, मां च me, तातं च father also, नः our, सुहृदः friends, बान्धवांश्च relations, सर्वान् all, पौरजानपदान् inhabitants of the city and countryside, सर्वम् entire, इदम् this kingodm, त्रातु protect.
explanation: Protect this entire kingdom, Kaikeyi, me and father, our friends and relations, citizens of the city and inhabitants of the countryside.

shloka_text: क्व चारण्यं क्वच क्षात्रं क्व जटाः क्व च पालनम्। ईदृशं व्याहतं कर्म न भवान्कर्तुमर्हति।।2.106.18।।
transliteration: kva cāraṇyaṃ kvaca kṣātraṃ kva jaṭāḥ kva ca pālanam| īdṛśaṃ vyāhataṃ karma na bhavānkartumarhati
translation: अरण्यं च the forest, क्व where, क्षात्रं च kshatriya'a duty, क्व where, जटाः matted locks, क्व where, पालनं च governance of the kingdom, क्व where, भवान् you, ईदृशम् such, व्याहतम् repulsive, कर्म act, कर्तुम् to do, न अर्हति not proper.
explanation: Where is the forest and where is kshatriya's duty? Where are matted locks and where is governance of the kingdom? It does not behave you to do such acts antithetical to each other.

shloka_text: एष हि प्रथमो धर्मः क्षत्रियस्याभिषेचनम्। येन शक्यं महाप्राज्ञ प्रजानां परिपालनम्।।2.106.19।।
transliteration: eṣa hi prathamo dharmaḥ kṣatriyasyābhiṣecanam| yena śakyaṃ mahāprājña prajānāṃ paripālanam
translation: महाप्राज्ञ O sagacious one, येन by whom, प्रजानाम् of the subjects', परिपालनम् governance, शक्यम् is possible, एषः this one, क्षत्रियस्य kshatriya's, अभिषेचनम् to be crowned, प्रथमः primary, धर्मः हि duty indeed.
explanation: O sagacious one, the primary duty of a kshatriya is to be crowned. This enables him to rule his subjects.

shloka_text: कश्च प्रत्यक्षमुत्सृज्य संशयस्थ मलक्षणम्। आयतिस्थं चरे द्धर्मं क्षत्रबन्दुरनिश्चितम्।।2.106.20।।
transliteration: kaśca pratyakṣamutsṛjya saṃśayastha malakṣaṇam| āyatisthaṃ care ddharmaṃ kṣatrabanduraniścitam
translation: कः who, क्षत्रबन्धुः a kshatriya, प्रत्यक्षम् first duty, उत्सृज्य abandoning संशयस्थम् doubtful, अलक्षणम् inauspcious, आयतिस्थम् standing at a remote future, अनिश्चितम् uncertain, धर्मम् righteousness, चरेत् will follow?
explanation: Will any kshatriya, setting aside his first duty, follow an uncertain course of piety which is contrary to his dharma and whose impact may be felt in a remote future.

shloka_text: अथ क्लेशज मेव त्वं धर्मं चरितु मिच्छसि। धर्मेण चतुरो वर्णान्पालयन् क्लेश माप्नुहि।।2.106.21।।
transliteration: atha kleśaja meva tvaṃ dharmaṃ caritu micchasi| dharmeṇa caturo varṇānpālayan kleśa māpnuhi
translation: अथ or, त्वम् you, क्लेशजम् born of physical exertion, धर्ममेव righteousness, चरितुम् to follow, इच्छसि यदि if you desire, चतुरः four, वर्णान् castes of social order, धर्मेण righteously, पालयन् governing, क्लेशम् exhaustion, आप्नुहि obtain.
explanation: If you so desire to follow the path of dharma acquired out of physical exertion, then bear the trouble of governing the four castes of the social order righteously.

shloka_text: चतुर्णामाश्रमाणां हि गार्हस्थ्यं श्रेष्ठमुत्तमम्। आहुर्धर्मज्ञ धर्मज्ञास्तं कथं त्यक्तु मर्हसि।।2.106.22।।
transliteration: caturṇāmāśramāṇāṃ hi gārhasthyaṃ śreṣṭhamuttamam| āhurdharmajña dharmajñāstaṃ kathaṃ tyaktu marhasi
translation: धर्मज्ञ one who is cognizant of duty, गार्हस्थ्यम् life a of householder, चतुर्णाम् the four, आश्रमाणाम् among modes of life, श्रेष्ठम् foremost, आश्रमम् mode of life, धर्मज्ञाः knowers of dharma, प्राहुः हि say, तम्  that one, त्यक्तुम् to renounce, कथम् how, अर्हसि are entitled?
explanation: O Rama, you are the one who knows his duty. The knowers of dharma maintain that the life of a householder is the foremost among the four modes of life. How can you renounce it?

shloka_text: श्रुतेन बालः स्थानेन जन्मना भवतो ह्यहम्। स कथं पालयिष्यामि भूमिं भवति तिष्ठति।।2.106.23।।
transliteration: śrutena bālaḥ sthānena janmanā bhavato hyaham| sa kathaṃ pālayiṣyāmi bhūmiṃ bhavati tiṣṭhati
translation: अहम् I, श्रुतेन in knowledge, स्थानेन in position, जन्मना in birth, भवतः compared to you, बालः हि am younger, सः such me, भवति when you, तिष्ठति while living, भूमिम् the earth, कथम् how, पालयिष्यामि can I rule?
explanation: Being younger to you in knowledge, position and birth, how can I rule the earth when you are present?

shloka_text: हीनबुद्धिगुणो बालो हीनः स्थानेन चाप्यहम्। भवता च विनाभूतो न वर्तयितुमुत्सुहे।।2.106.24।।
transliteration: hīnabuddhiguṇo bālo hīnaḥ sthānena cāpyaham| bhavatā ca vinābhūto na vartayitumutsuhe
translation: हीनबुद्धिगुणः deficient in intelligence and virtue, स्थानेन चापि even in position, हीनः low, बालः child, अहम् I, भवता by you, विनाभूतः deserted, वर्तयितुम् to live, न उत्सहे I  do not desire.
explanation: I am a child, deficient in intelligence and virtue and even inferior in position. Deserted by  you, I do not wish to live.

shloka_text: इदं निखिल मव्यग्रं राज्यं पित्र्यमकण्टकम्। अनुशाधि स्वधर्मेण धर्मज्ञ सहबान्धवैः।।2.106.25।।
transliteration: idaṃ nikhila mavyagraṃ rājyaṃ pitryamakaṇṭakam| anuśādhi svadharmeṇa dharmajña sahabāndhavaiḥ
translation: धर्मज्ञ O one, conversant with righteousness, पित्य्रम् relating to our father, निखिलम् entire, इदं राज्यम् this kingdom, अव्यग्रम् quietly, अकण्टकम् without hindrance बान्धवैस्सह with the relations, स्वधर्मेण in accordance with your duty, अनुशाधि rule .
explanation: O one, conversant with righteousness rule unhindered this entire kingdom along with our relations inherited from our father.

shloka_text: इहैव त्वाऽभिषिञ्चन्तु सर्वाः प्रकृतय स्सह। ऋत्विज स्सवसिष्ठाश्च मन्त्रविन्मन्त्रकोविदाः।।2.106.26।।
transliteration: ihaiva tvā'bhiṣiñcantu sarvāḥ prakṛtaya ssaha| ṛtvija ssavasiṣṭhāśca mantravinmantrakovidāḥ
translation: सर्वाः all, प्रकृतयः the subjects, सवसिष्ठाः including Vasistha, मन्त्रकोविदाः wellversed in the Vedic hymns, ऋत्विजश्च priests also, सह along with, त्वा you, इहैव here itself, मन्त्रवत् with sacred texts अभिषिञ्चन्तु may consecrate.
explanation: Let all ministers, subjects, and priests including Vasistha who are wellversed in Vedic hymns consecrate you here itself.

shloka_text: अभिषिक्तस्त्वमस्माभिरयोध्यां पालने व्रज। विजित्य तरसा लोकान्मरुद्भिरिव वासवः।।2.106.27।।
transliteration: abhiṣiktastvamasmābhirayodhyāṃ pālane vraja| vijitya tarasā lokānmarudbhiriva vāsavaḥ
translation: त्वम् you, अभिषिक्तः being consecrated, अस्माभिः along with us, पालने to govern, तरसा with vigour, लोकान् all the worlds, विजित्य having conquered, वासवः Indra, मरुद्भिरिव like Indra with Maruts, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, व्रज return.
explanation: After consecration, you too return to rule Ayodhya along with all of us like Indra who went back (to heaven), accompanied by Maruts after conquering all the worlds with his prowess.

shloka_text: ऋणानि त्रीण्यपाकुर्वन्दुर्हृदस्साधु निर्दहन्। सुहृदस्तर्पयन्कामैस्त्वमेवात्रानुशाधि माम्।।2.106.28।।
transliteration: ṛṇāni trīṇyapākurvandurhṛdassādhu nirdahan| suhṛdastarpayankāmaistvamevātrānuśādhi mām
translation: त्रीणि three, ऋणानि debts, अपाकुर्वन् discharging, दुर्हृदः enemies, साधु completely, निर्धहन्  subduing, सुहृदः friends, कामैः with desires, तर्पयन् gratifying, अत्र in Ayodhya, त्वमेव you alone, माम् me, अनुशाधि rule.
explanation: Discharging completely the three debts, to gods, to ancestors and to sages, subduing your enemies and gratifying your friends, you alone (have the right) to dictate me.

shloka_text: अद्याऽर्य मुदिता स्सन्तु सुहृदस्तेऽभिषेचने। अद्य भीताः पलायन्तां दुर्हृदस्ते दिशो दश।।2.106.29।।
transliteration: adyā'rya muditā ssantu suhṛdaste'bhiṣecane| adya bhītāḥ palāyantāṃ durhṛdaste diśo daśa
translation: आर्य O esteemed one, अद्य now, अभिषेचने at enthronement, ते your, सुहृदः friends, मुदिताः सन्तु let them be delighted, अद्य today, ते दुर्हृदः your enemies, भीताः frightened, दश दिशः in ten different directions, पलायन्ताम् will run away.
explanation: O my esteemed brother let all your friends be delighted today at your enthronement and your enemies flee in terror in ten different directions.

shloka_text: आक्रोशं मम मातुश्च प्रमृज्य पुरुषर्षभ। अद्य तत्र भवन्तं च पितरं रक्ष किल्बिषात्।।2.106.30।।
transliteration: ākrośaṃ mama mātuśca pramṛjya puruṣarṣabha| adya tatra bhavantaṃ ca pitaraṃ rakṣa kilbiṣāt
translation: पुरुषर्षभ O best of men, अद्य now, मम my, मातुः mother's, आक्रोशम् censure, प्रमृज्य wiping away, तत्र भवन्तम् revered one, पितरं च father also, किल्बिषात् from sin, रक्ष protect.
explanation: O best of men, wiping out all the censure on my mother, redeem our revered father from sin.

shloka_text: शिरसा त्वाऽभियाचेऽहं कुरुष्व करुणां मयि। बान्धवेषु च सर्वेषु भूतेष्विव महेश्वरः।।2.106.31।।
transliteration: śirasā tvā'bhiyāce'haṃ kuruṣva karuṇāṃ mayi| bāndhaveṣu ca sarveṣu bhūteṣviva maheśvaraḥ
translation: अहम् I, शिरसा with my head bowed low, त्वा you, अभियाचे beseech, मयि in me, सर्वेषु every one of, बान्धवेषु relations, भूतेषु in all living beings, महेश्वरः इव like Maheswara, करुणाम् compassion, कुरुष्व do.
explanation: I beseech you with my head bowed low, show mercy on me and every one of our relations, like Maheswara showing compassion on all living beings.

shloka_text: अथैतत्पृष्ठतः कृत्वा वनमेव भवानितः। गमिष्यति गमिष्यामि भवता सार्धमप्यहम्।।2.106.32।।
transliteration: athaitatpṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā vanameva bhavānitaḥ| gamiṣyati gamiṣyāmi bhavatā sārdhamapyaham
translation: अथ or, भवान् you, एतत् all these solicitations, पृष्ठतः कृत्वा keeping back, इतः from here, वनमेव to the forest itself, गमिष्यति if you set out, अहमपि I also, भवता सार्धम् along with you, गमिष्यामि I shall go.
explanation: If you turn your back on my solicitations and set out for the forest I shall also go along with you from here itself.

shloka_text: तथाहि रामो भरतेन ताम्यता प्रसाद्यमानश्शिरसा महीपतिः। नचैव चक्रे गमनाय सत्त्ववान्मतिं पितुस्तद्वचने प्रतिष्ठितः।।2.106.33।।
transliteration: tathāhi rāmo bharatena tāmyatā prasādyamānaśśirasā mahīpatiḥ| nacaiva cakre gamanāya sattvavānmatiṃ pitustadvacane pratiṣṭhitaḥ
translation: ताम्यता by the distressed, भरतेन by Bharata, तथा in that way, शिरसा with head bowed low, प्रसाद्यमानः propitiated, महीपतिः lord of the earth, सत्त्ववान् virtuous, रामः Rama, पितुः father's, तद्वचने in the words (of his father), प्रतिष्ठितः established, गमनाय to go back, मतिम् resolve, न चक्रे did not make.
explanation: Thus besought and propitiated by Bharata with his head bowed low and distressed, the virtuous lord of the world, Rama, firmly established in the words of his father, resolved not to go back to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: तदद्भुतं स्थैर्यमवेक्ष्य राघवे समं जनो हर्षमवाप दुःखितः। न यात्ययोध्यामिति दुःखितोऽभवत् स्थिरप्रतिज्ञत्वमवेक्ष्य हर्षितः।।2.106.34।।
transliteration: tadadbhutaṃ sthairyamavekṣya rāghave samaṃ jano harṣamavāpa duḥkhitaḥ| na yātyayodhyāmiti duḥkhito'bhavat sthirapratijñatvamavekṣya harṣitaḥ
translation: राघवे in Rama, अद्भुतम् that wonderful, तत् स्थैर्यम् that determination, अवेक्ष्य having seen, जनः all men, दुःखितः anguished, समम् simultaneously, हर्षम् delight, अवाप obtained, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, न याति will not go, इति thus, दुःखितः अभवत् were grieved, स्थिरप्रतिज्ञत्वम् firmness of resolve, अवेक्ष्य having seen, हर्षितः were delighted.
explanation: Having seen the wonderful deternmination of Rama, people were, at once, anguished and delighted, anguished because he would not return to Ayodhya, and delighted because he was firm in his resolve.

shloka_text: तमृत्विजो नैगमयूथवल्लभास्तदा विसंज्ञाश्रुकलाश्च मातरः। तथा ब्रुवाणं भरतं प्रतुष्टुवुः प्रणम्य रामं च ययाचिरे सह।।2.106.35।।
transliteration: tamṛtvijo naigamayūthavallabhāstadā visaṃjñāśrukalāśca mātaraḥ| tathā bruvāṇaṃ bharataṃ pratuṣṭuvuḥ praṇamya rāmaṃ ca yayācire saha
translation: ऋत्विजः the priests, नैगमयूथवल्लभाः the chiefs of merchant organizations, विसंज्ञाश्रुकलाः    with senses switched off and tears drained dry, मातरः mothers, तदा then, तथा in that way, ब्रुवाणम् speaking, तं भरतम् that Bharata, प्रतुष्टुवुः extolled, रामम् to Rama, प्रणम्य   reverentially saluting, सह together, ययाचिरे च implored.
explanation: All the priests, the chiefs of merchant organizations and mothers who had their senses switched off and theif tears drained dry extolled Bharata for his words. All of them, reverentially saluting Rama, implored him. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षडुत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredsixth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: पुनरेवं ब्रुवाणं तं भरतं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। प्रत्युवाच तत श्श्रीमान् ज्ञातिमध्येऽभिसत्कृतः।।2.107.1।।
transliteration: punarevaṃ bruvāṇaṃ taṃ bharataṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ| pratyuvāca tata śśrīmān jñātimadhye'bhisatkṛtaḥ
translation: ततः then, श्रीमान् prosperous, अभिसत्कृतः wellhonoured, लक्ष्मणाग्रजः Lakshmana's elder brother, ज्ञातिमध्ये amidst his relatives, पुनः again, एवम् thus, ब्रुवाणम् speaking, भरतम् to Bharata, प्रत्युवाच replied.
explanation: Wellhonoured in the midst of relatives, the celebrated Rama, elder brother of Lakshmana, then said to Bharata who was going to speak again.
comments: Rama advises Bharata to return back and rule the kingdom.

shloka_text: उपपन्नमिदं वाक्यं यत्त्वमेवमभाषथाः। जातः पुत्रो दशरथात्कैकेय्यां राजसत्तमात्।।2.107.2।।
transliteration: upapannamidaṃ vākyaṃ yattvamevamabhāṣathāḥ| jātaḥ putro daśarathātkaikeyyāṃ rājasattamāt
translation: राजसत्तमात् from the celebrated king, दशरथात् from Dasaratha, कैकेय्याम् to Kaikeyi, जातः born, पुत्रः son, त्वम् you, एवम् in this way, यत् which, अभ्यभाषथाः has spoken, इदम् this, वाक्यम् words, उपपन्नम् is appropriate.
explanation: Appropriate are the words spoken by you born to the celebrated king Dasaratha through Kaikeyi.

shloka_text: पुरा भ्रातः पिता न स्स मातरं ते समुद्वहन्। मातामहे समाश्रौषीद्राज्यशुल्कमनुत्तमम्।।2.107.3।।
transliteration: purā bhrātaḥ pitā na ssa mātaraṃ te samudvahan| mātāmahe samāśrauṣīdrājyaśulkamanuttamam
translation: भ्रातः my dear brother, पुरा earlier, सः that, नः पिता our father, ते मातरम् to your mother, समुद्वहन् at the time of wedding, मातामहे to (your) maternal grandfather, अनुत्तमम्  the best, राज्यशुल्कम् kingdom with good revenue, समाश्रौषीत् had promised.
explanation: Earlier when our father was to wed your mother, O dear brother, he had promised to your maternal grandfather that he would confer (on her) a kingdom with good revenue.

shloka_text: दैवासुरे च सङ्ग्रामे जनन्यै तव पार्थिवः। सम्प्रहृष्टो ददौ राजा वरमाराधितः प्रभुः।।2.107.4।।
transliteration: daivāsure ca saṅgrāme jananyai tava pārthivaḥ| samprahṛṣṭo dadau rājā varamārādhitaḥ prabhuḥ
translation: पार्थिवः king, प्रभुः lord, राजा king (Dasaratha), दैवासुरे between gods and demons, सङ्ग्रामे in the battle, आराधितः being propitialed, सम्प्रहृष्टः exceedingly pleased, तव जनन्यै to your mother, वरं च boon, ददौ granted.
explanation: Thereafter in the battle between gods and demons, the able king (Dasaratha) pleased  (with your mother) granted her a boon (as a token of gratitude).

shloka_text: ततस्सा सम्प्रतिश्राव्य तव माता यशस्विनी। अयाचत नरश्रेष्ठं द्वौ वरौ वरवर्णिनी।।2.107.5।। तव राज्यं नरव्याघ्र मम प्रव्राजनं तथा। तौ च राजा तदा तस्यै नियुक्तः प्रददौ वरौ।।2.107.6।।
transliteration: tatassā sampratiśrāvya tava mātā yaśasvinī| ayācata naraśreṣṭhaṃ dvau varau varavarṇinī tava rājyaṃ naravyāghra mama pravrājanaṃ tathā| tau ca rājā tadā tasyai niyuktaḥ pradadau varau
translation: नरव्याघ्र O tiger among men, ततः thereafter, यशस्विनी illustrious, वरवर्णिनी of best (fair) complexion, तव माता your mother, सम्प्रतिश्राव्य making him promise, नरश्रेष्ठम् to best of men, तव for you, राज्यम् kingdom, तथा likewise, मम to me, प्रव्राजनम् banishment, द्वौ two, वरौ boons, अयाचत demanded, तदा then, राजा च king also, नियुक्तः bound by agreement, तौ वरौ those two boons, तस्यै for her, प्रददौ granted.
explanation: Thereafter, O tiger among men, your illustrious mother of fair complexion, under oath demanded of that best of men, king Dasaratha, the two boons, namely kingdom for you and banishment for me. Bound by such agreement (oath), the king granted her the boons.

shloka_text: ततः सा सम्प्रतिश्राव्य तव माता यशस्विनी। अयाचत नरश्रेष्ठं द्वौ वरौ वरवर्णिनी।।2.107.5।। तव राज्यं नरव्याघ्र मम प्रव्राजनं तथा। तच्च राजा तदा तस्यै नियुक्तः प्रददौ वरौ।।2.107.6।।
transliteration: tataḥ sā sampratiśrāvya tava mātā yaśasvinī| ayācata naraśreṣṭhaṃ dvau varau varavarṇinī tava rājyaṃ naravyāghra mama pravrājanaṃ tathā| tacca rājā tadā tasyai niyuktaḥ pradadau varau
translation: नरव्याघ्र O tiger among men, ततः thereafter, यशस्विनी illustrious, वरवर्णिनी of best (fair) complexion, तव माता your mother, सम्प्रतिश्राव्य making him promise, नरश्रेष्ठम् to best of men, तव for you, राज्यम् kingdom, तथा likewise, मम to me, प्रव्राजनम् banishment, द्वौ two, वरौ boons, अयाचत demanded, तदा then, राजा च king also, नियुक्तः bound by agreement, तौ वरौ those two boons, तस्यै for her, प्रददौ granted.
explanation: Thereafter, O tiger among men, your illustrious mother of fair complexion, under oath demanded of that best of men, king Dasaratha, the two boons, namely kingdom for you and banishment for me. Bound by such agreement (oath), the king granted her the boons.

shloka_text: तेन पित्राऽहमप्यत्र नियुक्तः पुरुषर्षभ। चतुर्दश वने वासं वर्षाणि वरदानिकम्।।2.107.7।।
transliteration: tena pitrā'hamapyatra niyuktaḥ puruṣarṣabha| caturdaśa vane vāsaṃ varṣāṇi varadānikam
translation: पुरुषर्षभ O best of men, तेन that is why, पित्रा by father, अहमपि even I also, वरदानिकम् as per the boon, चतुर्दश वर्षाणि fourteen years, अत्र here, वने in the forest, वासम् to dwell, नियुक्तः have been ordered.
explanation: O best of men, that is why I have been ordered by father to live in the forest for fourteen years as per the (condition of the) boon.

shloka_text: सोऽहं वनमिदं प्राप्तो निर्जनं लक्ष्मणान्वितः। सीतया चाप्रतिद्वन्द्व स्सत्यवादे स्थितः पितुः।।2.107.8।।
transliteration: so'haṃ vanamidaṃ prāpto nirjanaṃ lakṣmaṇānvitaḥ| sītayā cāpratidvandva ssatyavāde sthitaḥ pituḥ
translation: अहम् I, लक्ष्मणान्वितः accompanied by Lakshmana, अप्रतिद्वन्द्वः unrivalled, पितुः father's, सत्यवादे truthfulness of words, स्थितः bent upon, सीतया च with Sita, निर्जनम् lonely, इदं वनम् this forest, प्राप्तः I have come.
explanation: I have come to this lonely forest accompanied by Lakshmana and Sita, bent upon upholding the truth of our unrivalled father's words.

shloka_text: भवानपि तथेत्येव पितरं सत्यवादिनम्। कर्तुमर्हति राजेन्द्र क्षिप्रमेवाभिषेचनात्।।2.107.9।।
transliteration: bhavānapi tathetyeva pitaraṃ satyavādinam| kartumarhati rājendra kṣipramevābhiṣecanāt
translation: राजेन्द्र O Indra among kings, भवानपि you also, तथेत्येव likewise, क्षिप्रमेव quickly, अभिषेचनात् by coronation, पितरम् father, सत्यवादिनम् true to his word, कर्तुम् to do, अर्हति should.
explanation: O Indra among kings, let your coronation be performed without delay since you are worthy and at the same time the truthfulness of our father's words be honoured.

shloka_text: ऋणान्मोचय राजानं मत्कृते भरत प्रभुम्। पितरं चापि धर्मज्ञं मातरं चाभिनन्दय।।2.107.10।।
transliteration: ṛṇānmocaya rājānaṃ matkṛte bharata prabhum| pitaraṃ cāpi dharmajñaṃ mātaraṃ cābhinandaya
translation: भरत O Bharata, मत्कृते for my sake, प्रभुम् competent, राजानम् king, ऋणात् from his debt (vow), मोचय redeem, धर्मज्ञम् one who knows righteousness, पितरम् चापि father also, मातरं च and mother, अभिनन्दय honour.
explanation: O Bharata, release for my sake the competent king from his debt (of vow) and honour the righteous father and the mother as well.

shloka_text: श्रूयते धीमता तात श्रुतिर्गीता यशस्विना। गयेन यजमानेन गयेष्वेव पितॄन् प्रति।।2.107.11।।
transliteration: śrūyate dhīmatā tāta śrutirgītā yaśasvinā| gayena yajamānena gayeṣveva pitṝn prati
translation: तात dear (brother), पुरा formerly, गयेष्वेव at a place known as Gaya, पितॄन् प्रति intended for ancestors, यजमानेन performing sacrifice, यशस्विना by an illustrious one, गयेन by Gaya, गीता chanted, श्रुतिः Vedic hymn, श्रूयते हि is heard.
explanation: Dear (brother), it is heard that long ago an illustrious king while performing a sacrifice intended for ancestors at a sacred place known as Gaya, the sacrificer Gaya chanted a Vedic hymn as follows:

shloka_text: पुन्नाम्नो नरकाद् यस्मात् पितरं त्रायते सुतः। तस्मात् पुत्र इति प्रोक्तः पितॄन् यः पाति सर्वतः।।2.107.12।।
transliteration: punnāmno narakād yasmāt pitaraṃ trāyate sutaḥ| tasmāt putra iti proktaḥ pitṝn yaḥ pāti sarvataḥ
translation: यस्मात् since, सुतः son, पितरम् father, पुन्नाम्नः by name 'Put', नरकात् from hell, त्रायते delivers, तस्मात् for that reason, यः who, सर्वतः in everyway, पितॄन् ancestors, पाति protects, he, पुत्र: इति as putra, प्रोक्तः has been told.
explanation: Putra is so called as he delivers his father from a hell known as Put and protects the ancestors in all possible ways.

shloka_text: एष्टव्या बहवः पुत्रा गुणवन्तो बहुश्रुताः। तेषां वै समवेतानामपि कश्चिद्गयां व्रजेत्।।2.107.13।।
transliteration: eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā guṇavanto bahuśrutāḥ| teṣāṃ vai samavetānāmapi kaścidgayāṃ vrajet
translation: गुणवन्तः virtuous, बहुश्रुताः learned, बहवः many, पुत्राः sons, एष्टव्याः are to be desired, समवेतानाम् together with, तेषाम् from among them, कश्चिदपि any one of them atleast, गयाम् to Gaya, व्रजेत् might go.
explanation: One should desire many virtuous and learned sons so that at least one of them may go to Gaya (to perform the father's obsequies).

shloka_text: एवं राजर्षय स्सर्वे प्रतीता राजनन्दन। तस्मात्राहि नरश्रेष्ठ पितरं नरकात्प्रभो।।2.107.14।।
transliteration: evaṃ rājarṣaya ssarve pratītā rājanandana| tasmātrāhi naraśreṣṭha pitaraṃ narakātprabho
translation: राजनन्दन भो O enhancer of the king's delight, सर्वे all, राजर्षयः rajarsis, एवम् this way, प्रतीताः have decided, प्रभो O lord, नरश्रेष्ठ O best of men, तस्मात् therefore, पितरम् father, नरकात् against hell, त्राहि protect.
explanation: O enhancer of the king's delight, O best of men rajarsis have decided this way. You may, therefore, O lord, protect your father against hell.

shloka_text: अयोध्यां गच्छ भरत प्रकृतीरनुरञ्जय। शत्रुघ्नसहितो वीर सह सर्वैर्द्विजातिभिः।।2.107.15।।
transliteration: ayodhyāṃ gaccha bharata prakṛtīranurañjaya| śatrughnasahito vīra saha sarvairdvijātibhiḥ
translation: वीर O valiant one, भरत Bharata, शत्रुघ्नसहितः with Satrughna, सर्वैः all, द्विजातिभिः सह with the twiceborn (brahmins), अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, गच्छ go, प्रकृतीः the subjects, अनुरञ्जय keep them delighted.
explanation: O valiant Bharata, go to Ayodhya accompanied by Satrughna and the twiceborn (brahmins) and keep the subjects delighted like pleased (with your rule).

shloka_text: प्रवेक्ष्ये दण्डकारण्यमहमप्यविलम्बयन्। आभ्यान्तु सहितो राजन् वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च।।2.107.16।।
transliteration: pravekṣye daṇḍakāraṇyamahamapyavilambayan| ābhyāntu sahito rājan vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca
translation: राजन् O king Bharata, अहमपि I also, अविलम्बयन् without delay, आभ्याम् of these two, वैदेह्या  with the princess from Videha (Sita), लक्ष्मणेन च and Lakshmana, सहितः in the company of, दण्डकारण्यम् Dandaka forest, प्रवेक्ष्ये shall enter.
explanation: O king (Bharata) I shall also enter the Dandaka forest without delay in the company of only these two -- the princess from Videha (Sita) and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: त्वं राजा भरत भव स्वयं नराणां वन्यानामहमपि राजराण्मृगाणाम्। गच्छ त्वं पुरवरमद्य सम्प्रहृष्टस्संहृष्टस्त्वहमपि दण्डकान्प्रवेक्ष्ये।।2.107.17।।
transliteration: tvaṃ rājā bharata bhava svayaṃ narāṇāṃ vanyānāmahamapi rājarāṇmṛgāṇām| gaccha tvaṃ puravaramadya samprahṛṣṭassaṃhṛṣṭastvahamapi daṇḍakānpravekṣye
translation: भरत O Bharata, त्वम् you, स्वयम् yourself, नराणाम् for men, राजा भव be king, अहमपि I also, वन्यानाम् of the wild  forest, मृगाणाम् of the beasts, राजराट् shall become supreme king, त्वम् you, सम्प्रम्हृष्टः in delight, अद्य now, पुरवरम् to the best of cities, गच्छ go, अहमपि and I also, संहृष्टः wellpleased, दण्डकान् in Dandaka forest, प्रवेक्ष्ये shall enter.
explanation: O Bharata, be the king of men. I shall also become the supreme king of the wild beasts in the forest. Go now happily to Ayodhya, the best of cities, and I shall enter Dandaka forest with delight.

shloka_text: छायां ते दिनकरभाः प्रबाधमानां वर्षत्रं भरत करोतु मूर्ध्नि शीताम्। एतेषामहमपि काननद्रुमाणां छायां तामतिशयिनीं सुखी श्रयिष्ये।।2.107.18।।
transliteration: chāyāṃ te dinakarabhāḥ prabādhamānāṃ varṣatraṃ bharata karotu mūrdhni śītām| eteṣāmahamapi kānanadrumāṇāṃ chāyāṃ tāmatiśayinīṃ sukhī śrayiṣye
translation: भरत O Bharata, वर्षत्रम् an umbrella, दिनकरभाः the sunshine, प्रबाधमानाम् repelling, ते मूर्ध्नि  over your head, शीताम् cool, छायाम् shade, करोतु let it provide, अहमपि I also, सुखी one with happiness, एतेषाम् these, काननद्रुमाणाम् woodland trees, अतिशयिनीम् dense, ताम् in that, छायाम् shade, श्रयिष्ये shall take refuge.
explanation: Let an umbrella protect you against (scorching) sunshine and provide its cool shade over your head, O Bharata As for me, I shall happily seek the shade of these dense woodland trees.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नः कुशलमतिस्तु ते सहायस्सौमित्रिर्मम विदितः प्रधानमित्रम्। चत्वारस्तनयवरा वयं नरेन्द्रं सत्यस्थं भरत चराम मा विषीद।।2.107.19।।
transliteration: śatrughnaḥ kuśalamatistu te sahāyassaumitrirmama viditaḥ pradhānamitram| catvārastanayavarā vayaṃ narendraṃ satyasthaṃ bharata carāma mā viṣīda
translation: भरत Bharata, कुशलमतिः intelligent, शत्रुघ्नः Satrughna, ते to you, सहायः assistance, सौमित्रिः son of Sumitra (Lakshmana), मम for me, प्रधानमित्रम् as my chief friend, विदितः is wellknown, तनयवराः worthy sons, वयम् all of us, चत्वारः four, नरेन्द्रम् to Indra among men (king Dasaratha), सत्यस्थम् as one, established in truth, चराम we shall move, मा विषीद do not grieve.
explanation: O Bharata, intelligent Satrughna will be your support and son of Sumitra (Lakshmana) as is wellknown will remain my best friend. All four of us, worthy sons of Dasaratha, shall follow the path of truth of our father. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredseventh sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: आश्वासयन्तं भरतं जाबालिर्ब्राह्मणोत्तमः। उवाच रामं धर्मज्ञं धर्मापेतमिदं वचः।।2.108.1।।
transliteration: āśvāsayantaṃ bharataṃ jābālirbrāhmaṇottamaḥ| uvāca rāmaṃ dharmajñaṃ dharmāpetamidaṃ vacaḥ
translation: ब्राह्मणोत्तमः the most virtuous brahmin, जाबालिः Jabali, भरतम् to Bharata, आश्वासयन्तम् consoling (convincing), धर्मज्ञम् cognizant of duty, रामम् to Rama, धर्मापेतम् deviating from  righteousness, इदम् this, वचः words, उवाच said.
explanation: While Rama, conversant with dharma, was consoling Bharata, Jabali an eminent brahmin addressed him in words contrary to righteousness.
comments: Jabali's efforts to convince Rama to accept Bharata's offer and rule the kingdom -- advocates the theory of nonbelievers of Vedic practices.

shloka_text: साधु राघव माऽभूत्ते बुध्दिरेवं निरर्थिका। प्राकृतस्य नरस्येव ह्यार्यबुद्धेर्मनस्विनः।।2.108.2।।
transliteration: sādhu rāghava mā'bhūtte budhdirevaṃ nirarthikā| prākṛtasya narasyeva hyāryabuddhermanasvinaḥ
translation: राघव O scion of the Raghu race (Rama), साधु very well, आर्यबुद्धेः of a nobleminded one, मनस्विनः highminded one, ते you, प्राकृतस्य नरस्येव like a common man, एवम् in that way, निरर्थिका nonsensical, बुद्धि: thought, माऽभूत् let there not be.
explanation: Very well, O scion of the Raghu race, you are nobleminded and highsouled. You, like a common man, must not entertain such nonsensical thought.

shloka_text: कः कस्य पुरुषो बन्धुः किमाप्यं कस्य केनचित्। यदेको जायते जन्तुरेक एव विनश्यति।।2.108.3।।
transliteration: kaḥ kasya puruṣo bandhuḥ kimāpyaṃ kasya kenacit| yadeko jāyate jantureka eva vinaśyati
translation: कः पुरषः which man, कस्य to whom, बन्धु: relation, कस्य to whom, केनचित् from any one, किम् what, आप्यम् is to be obtained, यत् for the reason, जन्तुः a creature, एकः alone, जायते is born, एक एव alone, विनश्यति dies.
explanation: Who is whose friend? who is to get what and from whom? Man is born alone and will die alone.

shloka_text: तस्मान्माता पिता चेति राम सज्जेत यो नरः। उन्मत्त इव स ज्ञेयो नास्ति कश्चिद्धि कस्यचित्।।2.108.4।।
transliteration: tasmānmātā pitā ceti rāma sajjeta yo naraḥ| unmatta iva sa jñeyo nāsti kaściddhi kasyacit
translation: राम O Rama, तस्मात् therefore, यः नरः a man, माता as mother, पिता चेति as father, सज्जेत is attached, सः he, उन्मत्त इव like a madman, सः ज्ञेयः is to be regarded, कश्चित् any one,  कस्य चित् to any one, नास्ति हि is nonexistent.
explanation: O Rama one who establishes relationship by saying, 'She is my mother he is my father' is to be regarded as a lunatic. In fact, no one belongs to any one.

shloka_text: यथा ग्रामान्तरं गच्छन्नरः कश्चित्क्वचिद्वसेत्। उत्सृज्य च तमावासं प्रतिष्ठेतापरेऽहनि।।2.108.5।। एवमेव मनुष्याणां पिता माता गृहं वसु। अवासमात्रं काकुत्स्थ सज्जन्ते नात्र सज्जनाः।।2.108.6।।
transliteration: yathā grāmāntaraṃ gacchannaraḥ kaścitkvacidvaset| utsṛjya ca tamāvāsaṃ pratiṣṭhetāpare'hani evameva manuṣyāṇāṃ pitā mātā gṛhaṃ vasu| avāsamātraṃ kākutstha sajjante nātra sajjanāḥ
translation: काकुत्स्थ O Rama, ग्रामान्तरम् from one village to another, गच्छन् while going, कश्चित् नरः a certain man, यथा as, क्वचित् somewhere, वसेत् may rest, तम् आवासम् that place of rest, उत्सृज्य leaving, अपरे on the next, अहनि day, प्रतिष्ठेत may proceed, एवमेव in the same way, मनुष्याणाम् to men, पिता father, माता mother, गृहम् home, वसु wealth, अवासमात्रम् resting places only, अत्र in this matter, सज्जनाः wise people, न सज्जन्ते are not attached to them.
explanation: A man who goes from one village to another takes rest somewhere on the way and the next day leaves the place and proceeds on his journey. Similarly, father, mother, home and wealth are restingplaces to a man. The wise do not get attached to them, O descendant the Kakutsthas

shloka_text: यथा ग्रामान्तरं गच्छन्नरः कश्चित्क्वचिद्वसेत्। उत्सृज्य च तमावासं प्रतिष्ठेतापरेऽहनि।।2.108.5।। एवमेव मनुष्याणां पिता माता गृहं वसु। अवासमात्रं काकुत्स्थ सज्जन्ते नात्र सज्जनाः।।2.108.6।।
transliteration: yathā grāmāntaraṃ gacchannaraḥ kaścitkvacidvaset| utsṛjya ca tamāvāsaṃ pratiṣṭhetāpare'hani evameva manuṣyāṇāṃ pitā mātā gṛhaṃ vasu| avāsamātraṃ kākutstha sajjante nātra sajjanāḥ
translation: काकुत्स्थ O Rama, ग्रामान्तरम् from one village to another, गच्छन् while going, कश्चित् नरः a certain man, यथा as, क्वचित् somewhere, वसेत् may rest, तम् आवासम् that place of rest, उत्सृज्य leaving, अपरे on the next, अहनि day, प्रतिष्ठेत may proceed, एवमेव in the same way, मनुष्याणाम् to men, पिता father, माता mother, गृहम् home, वसु wealth, अवासमात्रम् resting places only, अत्र in this matter, सज्जनाः wise people, न सज्जन्ते are not attached to them.
explanation: A man who goes from one village to another takes rest somewhere on the way and the next day leaves the place and proceeds on his journey. Similarly, father, mother, home and wealth are restingplaces to a man. The wise do not get attached to them, O descendant the Kakutsthas

shloka_text: पित्र्यं राज्यं परित्यज्य स नार्हसि नरोत्तम। आस्थातुं कापथं दुःखं विषमं बहुकण्टकम्।।2.108.7।।
transliteration: pitryaṃ rājyaṃ parityajya sa nārhasi narottama| āsthātuṃ kāpathaṃ duḥkhaṃ viṣamaṃ bahukaṇṭakam
translation: नरोत्तम O best of men, स: such as you, पित्य्रम् father's, राज्यम् kingdom, परित्यज्य abandoning, दुःखम् painful, विषमम् difficult, बहुकण्टकम् full of thorns, कापथम् unwise course, आस्थातुम् to adopt, नार्हसि should not.
explanation: O most virtuous of men, you ought not to abandon this patrimonial kingdom, adopt a course, which is painful, difficult and full of thorns (dangers). This (course) is unwise and unworthy of you.

shloka_text: समृद्धायामयोध्यायामात्मानमभिषेचय। एकवेणीधरा हि त्वां नगरी सम्प्रतीक्षते।।2.108.8।।
transliteration: samṛddhāyāmayodhyāyāmātmānamabhiṣecaya| ekaveṇīdharā hi tvāṃ nagarī sampratīkṣate
translation: समृद्धायाम् in a prosperous, अयोध्यायाम् in the city of Ayodhya, आत्मानम् yourself, अभिषेचय get coronated, नगरी that city, एकवेणीधरा wearing a single braid of hair, त्वाम् you, सम्प्रतीक्षते is awaiting.
explanation: Go back to that prosperous city of Ayodhya and get yourself coronated. That city is a chaste woman wearing a single braid of hair awaiting you, her lord.

shloka_text: राजभोगाननुभवन्महार्हान्पार्थिवात्मज। विहर त्वमयोध्यायां यथा शक्रस्त्रिविष्टपे।।2.108.9।।
transliteration: rājabhogānanubhavanmahārhānpārthivātmaja| vihara tvamayodhyāyāṃ yathā śakrastriviṣṭape
translation: पार्थिवात्मज O king's son, महार्हान् inestimable, राजभोगान् royal plesures, अनुभवन् enjoying, त्वम् you, शक्रः Indra, त्रिविष्ठपे यथा like in heaven, अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, विहर enjoy.
explanation: O king's son, enjoy inestimable royal pleasures in the city of Ayodhya like Indra in heaven.

shloka_text: न ते कश्चिद्धशरथ स्त्वं च तस्य न कश्चन। अन्यो राजा त्वमन्य स्तस्मात्कुरु यदुच्यते।।2.108.10।।
transliteration: na te kaściddhaśaratha stvaṃ ca tasya na kaścana| anyo rājā tvamanya stasmātkuru yaducyate
translation: ते to you, दशरथः Dasaratha, कश्चित् न is nobody, त्वं च you also, तस्य to him, कश्चन  न nobody, सः राजा that king, अन्यः another person, त्वम् you, अन्यः another person, तस्मात् therefore, यत् what, उच्यते is being told, कुरु do.
explanation: Dasaratha was nobody to you and you are nobody to him. That king is one person and you are another. Therefore, do what I tell you. (It does not matter what you are to him and what he means to you).

shloka_text: बीजमात्रं पिता जन्तो श्शुक्लं रुधिरमेव च। संयुक्तमृतुमन्मात्रा पुरुषस्येह जन्म तत्।।2.108.11।।
transliteration: bījamātraṃ pitā janto śśuklaṃ rudhirameva ca| saṃyuktamṛtumanmātrā puruṣasyeha janma tat
translation: पिता the father, जन्तोः for a being, बीजमात्रम् is a seed only, शुक्लम् white, रुधिरमेव blood, ऋतुमन्मात्रा in the mother's womb during her menstrual period (favourable time for conception), संयुक्तम् is blended, तत् due to that, इह in this world, पुरुषस्य man's, जन्म birth takes place.
explanation: For a living being, the father is only a drop of white blood (semen). During her menstrual period this is blended in the mother's womb due to which a man is born in this world.

shloka_text: गत स्स नृपतिस्तत्र गन्तव्यं यत्र तेन वै। प्रवृततिरेषा मर्त्यानां त्वं तु मिथ्या विहन्यसे।।2.108.12।।
transliteration: gata ssa nṛpatistatra gantavyaṃ yatra tena vai| pravṛtatireṣā martyānāṃ tvaṃ tu mithyā vihanyase
translation: सः that, नृपतिः king, तेन by him, यत्र wherever, गन्तव्यम् ought to go, तत्र there, गतः had gone, मर्त्यानाम् mortals', प्रवृत्ति: (destiny) nature, एषा such is, त्वं तु as for you, मिथ्या fruitlessly, विहन्यसे (undergoing difficulties).
explanation: That king (Dasaratha) has gone to the place where he ought to go. Such is the nature of mortals. You are fruitlessly undergoing difficulties.

shloka_text: अर्थधर्मपरा ये ये तांस्तांछोचामि नेतरान्। ते हि दुःखमिह प्राप्य विनाशं प्रेत्य भेजिरे।।2.108.13।।
transliteration: arthadharmaparā ye ye tāṃstāṃchocāmi netarān| te hi duḥkhamiha prāpya vināśaṃ pretya bhejire
translation: ये ये all those, अर्थधर्मपराः yearning for dharma and artha, तांस्तान् for all of them, शोचामि  feel sad, इतरान् for others, न not, ते they, इह in this world, दुःखम् sorrow, प्राप्य experiencing, प्रेत्य after death, विनाशम् destruction, भेजिरे had obtained (doubt).
explanation: I prity those who yearn for dharma and artha and not for other things since those who have experienced adversities in this world (disregarding their own interest), will be ultimately destroyed any way by death.

shloka_text: अष्टका पितृदैवत्यमित्ययं प्रसृतो जनः। अन्नस्योपद्रवं पश्य मृतो हि किमशिष्यति।।2.108.14।।
transliteration: aṣṭakā pitṛdaivatyamityayaṃ prasṛto janaḥ| annasyopadravaṃ paśya mṛto hi kimaśiṣyati
translation: अष्टका ashtaka ceremony, पितृदैवत्यम् इति the receivers are the spirits of ancestors, अयम्   जनः these people, प्रसृतः are engaged, अन्नस्य offering of food, उपद्रवम् wastage, पश्य look, मृतः the dead, किम् what, अशिष्यति will it eat?
explanation: People perform ashtaka ceremony for the spirits of ancestors and offer them food. Look at the amount of food being wasted. Will the dead (ever) eat food?

shloka_text: यदि भुक्तमिहान्येन देहमन्यस्य गच्छति। दद्यात्प्रवसत श्श्राद्धं न तत्पथ्यशनं भवेत्।।2.108.15।।
transliteration: yadi bhuktamihānyena dehamanyasya gacchati| dadyātpravasata śśrāddhaṃ na tatpathyaśanaṃ bhavet
translation: इह in this world, अन्येन by one person, भुक्तम् something eaten, अन्यस्य to other man's, देहम् body, गच्छति यदि if it reaches, प्रवसतः living in a distant place,  श्राद्धम् shraddha, दद्यात् may offer, तत् that one, पथि on the way, अशनम् न भवेत् will it not  be food?
explanation: If something eaten by one in this world can enter the body of another, then a shraddha can be performed for a person who has set out on a distant journey. Will that offering turn into food for him on his way?

shloka_text: दानसंवनना ह्येते ग्रन्था मेधाविभिः कृताः। यजस्व देहि दीक्षस्व तपस्तप्यस्व सन्त्यज।।2.108.16।।
transliteration: dānasaṃvananā hyete granthā medhāvibhiḥ kṛtāḥ| yajasva dehi dīkṣasva tapastapyasva santyaja
translation: यजस्व perform sacrifices, देहि give away, दीक्षस्व be initiated, तपः religious austerities, तप्यस्व practice, सन्त्यज renounce, एते these, ग्रन्थाः texts mannuals, मेधाविभिः by intelligent men, कृताः have been composed, दानसंवननाः हि to induce people to give charity.
explanation: It was to induce people to give charity that treatises are composed by intelligent men exhorting, 'perform sacrifices', 'give charity', 'be initiated', 'practise religious austerities', 'renounce', etc.

shloka_text: स नास्ति परमित्येव कुरु बुद्धिं महामते। प्रत्यक्षं यत्तदातिष्ठ परोक्षं पृष्ठतः कुरु।।2.108.17।।
transliteration: sa nāsti paramityeva kuru buddhiṃ mahāmate| pratyakṣaṃ yattadātiṣṭha parokṣaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kuru
translation: महामते O highminded one, सः such as you, परम् the next world, नास्ति does not exist, इत्येव like that, बुद्धिम् thinking, कुरु do, यत् whatever, प्रत्यक्षम् is evident, तत् that one, आतिष्ठ you practise, परोक्षम् what is beyond perception, पृष्ठतः कुरु turn your back on.
explanation: O highminded one thinking that the next world does not exist, practise whichever is evident and perceivable. And turn your back on what is beyond perception.

shloka_text: सतां बुद्धिं पुरस्कृत्य सर्वलोकनिदर्शिनीम्। राज्यं त्वं प्रतिगृह्णीष्व भरतेन प्रसादितः।।2.108.18।।
transliteration: satāṃ buddhiṃ puraskṛtya sarvalokanidarśinīm| rājyaṃ tvaṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva bharatena prasāditaḥ
translation: सः त्वम् such as you, सर्वलोकनिदर्शिनीम् that serves as an instance to all, सतां बुद्धिम्   judgement of the wise, पुरस्कृत्य treating with honour, भरतेन by Bharata, प्रसादितः pleased by, राज्यम् kingdom, प्रतिगृह्णीष्व accept.
explanation: Honour the decision of the wise that serves as an instance to all and accept the kingdom offered by Bharata with pleasure इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredeighth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: जाबालेस्तु वचश्श्रुत्वा राम स्सत्यात्मनां वरः। उवाच परया भक्त्या स्वबुद्ध्या चाविपन्नया।।2.109.1।।
transliteration: jābālestu vacaśśrutvā rāma ssatyātmanāṃ varaḥ| uvāca parayā bhaktyā svabuddhyā cāvipannayā
translation: सत्यात्मनाम् among truthful men, वरः best, रामः Rama, जाबालेः Jabali's, वचः words, श्रुत्वा hearing, परया supreme, भक्त्या with devotion, अविपन्नया unshaken, स्वबुद्ध्या च by his own judgment, उवाच said.
explanation: Hearing Jabali's words, Rama, the foremost among the truthful, gave a rejoinder, exercising his own judgment and firm conviction with due respect (to Jabali).
comments: Rama's justification for adhering to the supreme values of dharma and truth.

shloka_text: भवान्मे प्रियकामार्थं वचनं यदिहोक्तवान्। अकार्यं कार्यसङ्काशमपथ्यं पथ्यसम्मतम्।।2.109.2।।
transliteration: bhavānme priyakāmārthaṃ vacanaṃ yadihoktavān| akāryaṃ kāryasaṅkāśamapathyaṃ pathyasammatam
translation: भवान् you, मे to me, प्रियकामार्थम् with a desire to please, यत् what, वचनम् words, इह now, उक्तवान् has spoken, कार्यसङ्काशम् in the guise of an action fit to be done, अकार्यम् is unfit to be done, पथ्यसम्मतम् appears to be beneficial, अपथ्यम् is detrimental.
explanation: Althoug what you have said appears to be salutary, it is actually unwholesome. It appears to be beneficial but is really detrimental.

shloka_text: निर्मर्यादस्तु पुरुषः पापाचारसमन्वितः। मानं न लभते सत्सु भिन्नचारित्रदर्शनः।।2.109.3।।
transliteration: nirmaryādastu puruṣaḥ pāpācārasamanvitaḥ| mānaṃ na labhate satsu bhinnacāritradarśanaḥ
translation: निर्मर्यादः one who transgresses all bounds of morality, पापाचारसमन्वितः one who is engaged in evil deeds, भिन्नचारित्रदर्शनः opposed to good character, पुरुषः a man, सत्सु amongst the virtuous, मानम् respect, न लभते does not obtain.
explanation: A man not bound by morality, engaged in evil deeds and conducts himself contrary to good character is not respected by the virtuous.

shloka_text: कुलीनमकुलीनं वा वीरं पुरुषमानिनम्। चारित्रमेव व्याख्याति शुचिं वा यदि वाऽशुचिम्।।2.109.4।।
transliteration: kulīnamakulīnaṃ vā vīraṃ puruṣamāninam| cāritrameva vyākhyāti śuciṃ vā yadi vā'śucim
translation: कुलीनम् highborn, अकुलीनं वा or base, वीरम् brave, पुरुषमानिनम् proud of his manliness, शुचिं वा pure or honest, यदि वा or if, अशुचिं impure or dishonest, चारित्रमेव character alone, व्याख्याति tells.
explanation: It is only the character that tells whether a man is highborn or not, brave or only proud of his manliness, honest or dishonest.

shloka_text: अनार्यस्त्वार्यसङ्काश श्शौचाद्दीनस्ताथाऽशुचिः। लक्षण्यवदलक्षण्यो दुश्शीलश्शीलवानिव।।2.109.5।। अधर्मं धर्मवेशेण यदीमं लोकसङ्कुरम्। अभिपत्स्ये शुभं हित्वा क्रियाविधिविवर्जितम्।।2.109.6।। कश्चेतयानः पुरुषः कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः। बहुमंस्यति मां लोके दुर्वृत्तं लोकदूषणम्।।2.109.7।।
transliteration: anāryastvāryasaṅkāśa śśaucāddīnastāthā'śuciḥ| lakṣaṇyavadalakṣaṇyo duśśīlaśśīlavāniva adharmaṃ dharmaveśeṇa yadīmaṃ lokasaṅkuram| abhipatsye śubhaṃ hitvā kriyāvidhivivarjitam kaścetayānaḥ puruṣaḥ kāryākāryavicakṣaṇaḥ| bahumaṃsyati māṃ loke durvṛttaṃ lokadūṣaṇam
translation: आर्यसङ्काशः who appears as noble, अनार्यः ignoble, शौचात् clean, हीनः devoid of, तथा and, अशुचिः impure, लक्षण्यवत् appears virtuous, अलक्षण्यः bereft of virtues, शीलवानिव like a man of character, दुश्शीलः depraved, शुभम् auspiciousness, हित्वा abandoning, धर्मवेशेण under the guise of righteousness, लोकसङ्कुरम् confusion in the world, क्रियाविधिविवर्जितम् devoid of pious acts and scriptural practices, इमम् this, अधर्मम् unrighteousness, अभिपत्स्ये यदि if I were to acquire, दुर्वृत्तम् engaged in wicked acts, लोकदूषणम् harmful to the world, माम् me, लोके in the world, कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः discriminating between should and should not, चेतयानः sensible, कः पुरुषः what man, बहुमंस्यति would be held in high esteem?
explanation: If like a man who appears noble, though ignoble, clean, though unclean or dishonest, auspicious, though inauspicious, a man of character, though depraved, I forsake auspicious ways for unrighteousness, abandon pious acts and scriptural practices and indulge, under the cloak of dharma, in acts of wickedness by causing harm and confusion to the world, will any sensible man with a sense of discrimination between should and should not hold me in high esteem?

shloka_text: अनार्यस्त्वार्यसङ्काश श्शौचाद्दीनस्ताथाऽशुचिः। लक्षण्यवदलक्षण्यो दुश्शीलश्शीलवानिव।।2.109.5।। अधर्मं धर्मवेशेण यदीमं लोकसङ्कुरम्। अभिपत्स्ये शुभं हित्वा क्रियाविधिविवर्जितम्।।2.109.6।। कश्चेतयानः पुरुषः कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः। बहुमंस्यति मां लोके दुर्वृत्तं लोकदूषणम्।।2.109.7।।
transliteration: anāryastvāryasaṅkāśa śśaucāddīnastāthā'śuciḥ| lakṣaṇyavadalakṣaṇyo duśśīlaśśīlavāniva adharmaṃ dharmaveśeṇa yadīmaṃ lokasaṅkuram| abhipatsye śubhaṃ hitvā kriyāvidhivivarjitam kaścetayānaḥ puruṣaḥ kāryākāryavicakṣaṇaḥ| bahumaṃsyati māṃ loke durvṛttaṃ lokadūṣaṇam
translation: आर्यसङ्काशः who appears as noble, अनार्यः ignoble, शौचात् clean, हीनः devoid of, तथा and, अशुचिः impure, लक्षण्यवत् appears virtuous, अलक्षण्यः bereft of virtues, शीलवानिव like a man of character, दुश्शीलः depraved, शुभम् auspiciousness, हित्वा abandoning, धर्मवेशेण under the guise of righteousness, लोकसङ्कुरम् confusion in the world, क्रियाविधिविवर्जितम् devoid of pious acts and scriptural practices, इमम् this, अधर्मम् unrighteousness, अभिपत्स्ये यदि if I were to acquire, दुर्वृत्तम् engaged in wicked acts, लोकदूषणम् harmful to the world, माम् me, लोके in the world, कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः discriminating between should and should not, चेतयानः sensible, कः पुरुषः what man, बहुमंस्यति would be held in high esteem?
explanation: If like a man who appears noble, though ignoble, clean, though unclean or dishonest, auspicious, though inauspicious, a man of character, though depraved, I forsake auspicious ways for unrighteousness, abandon pious acts and scriptural practices and indulge, under the cloak of dharma, in acts of wickedness by causing harm and confusion to the world, will any sensible man with a sense of discrimination between should and should not hold me in high esteem?

shloka_text: अनार्यस्त्वार्यसङ्काश श्शौचाद्दीनस्ताथाऽशुचिः। लक्षण्यवदलक्षण्यो दुश्शीलश्शीलवानिव।।2.109.5।। अधर्मं धर्मवेशेण यदीमं लोकसङ्कुरम्। अभिपत्स्ये शुभं हित्वा क्रियाविधिविवर्जितम्।।2.109.6।। कश्चेतयानः पुरुषः कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः। बहुमंस्यति मां लोके दुर्वृत्तं लोकदूषणम्।।2.109.7।।
transliteration: anāryastvāryasaṅkāśa śśaucāddīnastāthā'śuciḥ| lakṣaṇyavadalakṣaṇyo duśśīlaśśīlavāniva adharmaṃ dharmaveśeṇa yadīmaṃ lokasaṅkuram| abhipatsye śubhaṃ hitvā kriyāvidhivivarjitam kaścetayānaḥ puruṣaḥ kāryākāryavicakṣaṇaḥ| bahumaṃsyati māṃ loke durvṛttaṃ lokadūṣaṇam
translation: आर्यसङ्काशः who appears as noble, अनार्यः ignoble, शौचात् clean, हीनः devoid of, तथा and, अशुचिः impure, लक्षण्यवत् appears virtuous, अलक्षण्यः bereft of virtues, शीलवानिव like a man of character, दुश्शीलः depraved, शुभम् auspiciousness, हित्वा abandoning, धर्मवेशेण under the guise of righteousness, लोकसङ्कुरम् confusion in the world, क्रियाविधिविवर्जितम् devoid of pious acts and scriptural practices, इमम् this, अधर्मम् unrighteousness, अभिपत्स्ये यदि if I were to acquire, दुर्वृत्तम् engaged in wicked acts, लोकदूषणम् harmful to the world, माम् me, लोके in the world, कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः discriminating between should and should not, चेतयानः sensible, कः पुरुषः what man, बहुमंस्यति would be held in high esteem?
