translation: ऋषिसत्तमः excellent among the sages (Atri), वैदेहीम् Sita, प्रतिगृह्णीष्व receive, महाभागाम्  highly virtuous, तापसीम् female ascetic, धर्मचारिणीम् who adheres to righteousness, अनसूयाम् to Anasuya, अब्रवीत् said, धर्मचारिणीम् who followed the ways of righteousness, तां  तापसीम् about his ascetic wife Anasuya, रामाय to Rama, आचचक्षे च related.
explanation: Atri, who was excellent among the sages said to his ascetic wife who was highly virtuous and an adherent of righteousness, Welcome Sita. Thereafter, he related to Rama a story about his asetic wife who follows the ways of righteousness.

shloka_text: दश वर्षाण्यनावृष्ट्या दग्धे लोके निरन्तरम्।।2.117.9।। यया मूलफले सृष्टे जाह्नवी च प्रवर्तिता। उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता नियमैश्चाप्यलङ्कृता।।2.117.10।। दश वर्ष सहास्राणि तया तप्तं महत्तपः। अनसूया व्रतै स्स्नाता प्रत्यूहाश्च निवर्तिताः।।2.117.11।। देवकार्यनिमित्तं च यया सन्त्वरमाणया। दशरात्रं कृता रात्रि स्सेयं मातेव तेऽनघ।।2.117.12।।
transliteration: daśa varṣāṇyanāvṛṣṭyā dagdhe loke nirantaram yayā mūlaphale sṛṣṭe jāhnavī ca pravartitā| ugreṇa tapasā yuktā niyamaiścāpyalaṅkṛtā daśa varṣa sahāsrāṇi tayā taptaṃ mahattapaḥ| anasūyā vratai ssnātā pratyūhāśca nivartitāḥ devakāryanimittaṃ ca yayā santvaramāṇayā| daśarātraṃ kṛtā rātri sseyaṃ māteva te'nagha
translation: अनघ O blameless one (Rama), लोके in this world, दशवर्षाणि ten years, अनावृष्ट्या by drought, निरन्तरम् constantly, दग्धे devastated, यया by whom, मूलफले roots and fruits, सृष्टे were created, जाह्नवी च Ganga, प्रवर्तिता caused to flow, उग्रेण rigid, तपसा with mortifications, युक्ता engaged, नियमैश्च अपि with selfimposed religious observances, अलङ्कृता decorated, यया by whom, दशवर्षसहस्राणि for ten thousand years,  महत् severe, तपः asceticism, तप्तम् was practised, देवकार्यनिमित्तम् for the sake of gods, सन्त्वरमाणया by her eagerly, यया by whom, प्रत्यूहां impediments, निवर्तिताः have been averted, दशरात्रं ten nights, रात्रिः as night, कृता was converted, सा such, व्रतैः स्नाता bathed in her vow, इयम् अनसूया this Anasuya, ते to you, मातेव like a mother.
explanation: O blameless one (Rama), once this world was consecutively ravaged by drought for ten years. It was the virtuous Anasuya who created roots and fruits and caused Ganga to flow. She was engaged in severe mortifications and selfimposed religious observances. She practised severe asceticism for ten thousand years bathed in her vows. Solicited on behalf of the gods, she removed all impediments and converted ten nights into one. She is like a your mother to you.

shloka_text: तामिमां सर्वभूतानां नमस्कार्यां यशस्विनीम् अभिगच्छतु वैदेही वृद्धामक्रोधनां सदा। अनसूयेति या लोके कर्मभिः ख्यातिमागता।।2.117.13।।
transliteration: tāmimāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ namaskāryāṃ yaśasvinīm abhigacchatu vaidehī vṛddhāmakrodhanāṃ sadā| anasūyeti yā loke karmabhiḥ khyātimāgatā
translation: सर्वभूतानाम् for all beings, नमस्कार्याम् worthy of adoration, यशस्विनीम् illustrious lady, वृद्धाम्  aged, सदा always, अक्रोधनाम् free from anger, ताम् to such a woman, इमाम् this Anasuya, वैदेही Sita, अभिगच्छतु let her approach, या who, कर्मभिः with deeds, आनसूयेति as Anasuya, ख्यातिम्  renown, आगता has acquired.
explanation: 'She is renowned throughout this world for her deeds as Anasuya, (one who is free from anger). Aged, illustrious she is free frm anger, worthy of adoration by all beings. Let Sita approach her'.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवाणं तमृषिं तथेत्युक्त्वा स राघवः। सीतामुवाच धर्मज्ञामिदं वचनमुत्तमम्।।2.117.14।।
transliteration: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tamṛṣiṃ tathetyuktvā sa rāghavaḥ| sītāmuvāca dharmajñāmidaṃ vacanamuttamam
translation: सः राघवः that Rama, एवम् in this way, ब्रुवाणम् speaking,  तम् ऋषिम् that sage, तथेति be it so, उक्त्वा having said, धर्मज्ञाम् wise in the ways of righteousness, सीताम् Sita, उत्तमम् excellent, इदं वचनम् these words, उवाच said.
explanation: Hearing those words of the sage, Rama said be it so and said to righteous Sita these choice words.

shloka_text: राजपुत्रि श्रुतमिदं मुनेरस्य समीरितम्। श्रेयोऽर्थमात्मनश्शीघ्रमभिगच्छ तपस्विनीम्।।2.117.15।।
transliteration: rājaputri śrutamidaṃ munerasya samīritam| śreyo'rthamātmanaśśīghramabhigaccha tapasvinīm
translation: राजपुत्रि O princess (Sita), अस्य मुनेः of this sage, इदं समीरितम् this saying, श्रुतम् has been heard, आत्मनः for your, श्रेयोऽर्थम् for your welfare, शीघ्रम् without delay, तपस्विनीम् ascetic, अभिगच्छ you may approach.
explanation: O princess, you have heard the message of the sage. Without delay approach the ascetic (Anasuya) for your welfare.

shloka_text: सीता त्वेतद वचः श्रुत्वा राघवस्य हितैषिणः। तामत्रिपन्तीं धर्मज्ञामभिचक्राम मैथिली।।2.117.16।।
transliteration: sītā tvetada vacaḥ śrutvā rāghavasya hitaiṣiṇaḥ| tāmatripantīṃ dharmajñāmabhicakrāma maithilī
translation: मैथिली daughter of the king of Mithila, सीता तु Sita, हितैषिणः  wishing her welfare, राघवस्य Rama's, एतद्वचः words, शृत्वा hearing, धर्मज्ञाम् knower of righteousness, ताम् to that,          अत्रिपत्नीम् wife of Atri (Devi Anasuya), अभिचक्राम circumamabulated in reverence.
explanation: Having heard the words of Rama, intended for her welfare, Sita, daughter of the king of Mithila, approached the consort of Atri (Devi Anasuya), knower of righteousness, and reverently circumambulated her.

shloka_text: शिथिलां वलितां वृद्धां जरापाण्डुरमूर्धजाम्। सततं वेपमानाङ्गीं प्रवाते कदलीं यथा।। 2.117.17।। तां तु सीता महाभागामनसूयां पतिव्रताम्। अभ्यवादयदव्यग्रा स्वं नाम समुदाहरत्।।2.117.18।।
transliteration: śithilāṃ valitāṃ vṛddhāṃ jarāpāṇḍuramūrdhajām| satataṃ vepamānāṅgīṃ pravāte kadalīṃ yathā tāṃ tu sītā mahābhāgāmanasūyāṃ pativratām| abhyavādayadavyagrā svaṃ nāma samudāharat
translation: सीता Sita, शिथिलाम् feeble, वलिताम् with wrinkles, वृद्धाम् old, जरापाण्डुरमूर्धजाम् hair turned  grey due to old age, प्रवाते in stormy wind, कदलीं यथा like a plantain tree, सततम्  constantly, वेपमानाङ्गीम् her body trembling, महाभागाम् highly fortunate, पतिव्रताम् chaste woman, ताम् अनसूयाम् that Anasuya, अव्यग्रा without haste, अभ्यवादयत् made obeisance, स्वनाम her name, समुदाहरत् pronounced.
explanation: Highly chaste and fortunate Anasuya was very old and feeble. Her skin was wrinkled and her hair turned grey due to old age. Her body was constantly trembling like a plantain tree in a stormy wind. Pronouncing her name to such Anasuya, Sita made obeisance to her with utmost concentration.

shloka_text: शिथिलां वलितां वृद्धां जरापाण्डुरमूर्धजाम्। सततं वेपमानाङ्गीं प्रवाते कदलीं यथा।। 2.117.17।। तां तु सीता महाभागामनसूयां पतिव्रताम्। अभ्यवादयदव्यग्रा स्वंनाम समुदाहरत्।।2.117.18।।

explanation: Highly chaste and fortunate Anasuya was very old and feeble. Her skin was wrinkled and her hair turned grey due to old age. Her body was constantly trembling like a plantain tree in a stormy wind. Pronouncing her name to such Anasuya, Sita made obeisance to her with utmost concentration.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्य च वैदेही तापसीं तामनिन्दिताम्। बद्धाञ्जलिपुटा हृष्टा पर्यपृच्छदनामयम्।।2.117.19।।
transliteration: abhivādya ca vaidehī tāpasīṃ tāmaninditām| baddhāñjalipuṭā hṛṣṭā paryapṛcchadanāmayam
translation: वैदेही Sita, अनिन्दिताम् blameless, तां तापसीम् to that asceetic (Anasuya), अभिवाद्य after paying her homage, बद्धाञ्जलिपुटा folding the palms, हृष्टा delighted lady, अनामयम् wellbeing, पर्यपृच्छत् enquired.
explanation: Sita offered her obeisance to the blameless ascetic, Anasuya, folding her palms and enquired of her wellbeing in delight.

shloka_text: ततस्सीतां महाभागां दृष्ट्वा तां धर्मचारिणीम्। सान्त्वयन्त्यब्रवीद्धृष्टा दिष्ट्या धर्ममवेक्षसे।।2.117.20।।
transliteration: tatassītāṃ mahābhāgāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ dharmacāriṇīm| sāntvayantyabravīddhṛṣṭā diṣṭyā dharmamavekṣase
translation: ततः then, महाभागाम् glorious lady, धर्मचारिणीम् engaged in righteous acts, तां सीताम् that Sita, सान्त्वयन्ती consoling, हृष्टा in delight, अब्रवीत् said, दिष्ट्या fortunately, धर्मम् rightful duty, अवेक्षसे you are observing.
explanation: Anasuya was delighted  to see the glorious Sita who was always engaged in righteous acts and  said in kind words, You are fortunate. You are observing your rightful duty.

shloka_text: त्यक्त्वा ज्ञातिजनं सीते मानमृद्धं च भामिनि। अवरुद्धं वने रामं दिष्ट्या त्वमनुगच्छसि।।2.117.21।।
transliteration: tyaktvā jñātijanaṃ sīte mānamṛddhaṃ ca bhāmini| avaruddhaṃ vane rāmaṃ diṣṭyā tvamanugacchasi
translation: भामिनः सीते O noble Sita, त्वम् you, दिष्ट्या by the grace of heaven, ज्ञातिजनम् your kins, मानम् pride, ऋद्धं च wealth, त्यक्त्वा after forsaking, वने in the forest, अवरुद्धम् confined, रामम् Rama, अनुगच्छसि you are following.
explanation: O noble Sita, by the grace of heaven you are following Rama, forsaking your kinsmen and wealth and confining yourself to the forest.

shloka_text: नगरस्थो वनस्थो वा पापो वा यदि वा शुभः। यासां स्त्रीणां प्रियो भर्ता तासां लोका महोदयाः।।2.117.22।।
transliteration: nagarastho vanastho vā pāpo vā yadi vā śubhaḥ| yāsāṃ strīṇāṃ priyo bhartā tāsāṃ lokā mahodayāḥ
translation: यासाम् those, स्त्रीणाम् women, नगरस्थः in the city, वनस्थो वा or in the forest, पापो वा or sinful, यदि वा or, शुभः virtuous, भर्ता husband, प्रियः dear, तासाम् for them, महोदयाः highly promising, लोकः worlds.
explanation: One who is devoted to her husband, whether he be in the city or in the forest, whether  he is sinful or virtuous, will attain the most prosperous worlds.

shloka_text: दुश्शीलः कामवृत्तो वा धनैर्वा परिवर्जितः। स्त्रीणामार्यस्वभावानां परमं दैवतं पतिः।।2.117.23।।
transliteration: duśśīlaḥ kāmavṛtto vā dhanairvā parivarjitaḥ| strīṇāmāryasvabhāvānāṃ paramaṃ daivataṃ patiḥ
translation: आर्यस्वभावानाम् of noble nature, स्त्रीणाम् for women, दुश्शीलः a man of bad character, कामवृत्तो वा or licentious, धनैः with riches, परिवर्जितो वा or devoid of, पतिः husband, परमम् is supreme, दैवतम् is deity.
explanation: For a woman of noble nature her husband, whether he be licentious or of bad character or devoid of riches, is her supreme lord.

shloka_text: नातो विशिष्टं पश्यामि बान्धवं विमृशन्त्यहम्। सर्वत्र योग्यं वैदेहि तपः कृतमिवाव्ययम्।।2.117.24।।
transliteration: nāto viśiṣṭaṃ paśyāmi bāndhavaṃ vimṛśantyaham| sarvatra yogyaṃ vaidehi tapaḥ kṛtamivāvyayam
translation: वैदेहि Sita, अहम् I, सर्वत्र all over, विमृशन्ती reflecting, कृतम् performed, अव्ययम् imperishable,  योग्यम् befitting, तपः इव like austerities, अतः more than husband, विशिष्टम् better, बान्धवम् relation, न पश्यामि I do not see.
explanation: O Sita, on reflection I know of none who is a better friend than the husband. He, like an imperishable penance, once acquired is never lost.

shloka_text: न त्वेवमवगच्छन्ति गुणदोषमसत्त्स्रियः। कामवक्तव्यहृदया भर्तृनाथाश्चरन्ति याः।।2.117.25।।
transliteration: na tvevamavagacchanti guṇadoṣamasattsriyaḥ| kāmavaktavyahṛdayā bhartṛnāthāścaranti yāḥ
translation: याः those women, कामवक्तव्यहृदयाः with minds overpowerd by carnal desires, भर्तृनाथाः as lords of their husbands, चरन्ति ranging at will, असत्त्स्रियः such wicked women, एवम् in this way, गुणदोषम् vice and virtue, न अवगच्छन्ति do not understand.
explanation: Those wicked women whose minds are overpowered by carnal desires, ranging at will as lords of their husbands, do not understand about vice and virtue.

shloka_text: प्राप्नुवन्त्य यशश्चैव धर्मभ्रंशं च मैथिलि। अकार्यवशमापन्नाः स्त्रियो याः खलु तद्विधाः।।2.117.26।।
transliteration: prāpnuvantya yaśaścaiva dharmabhraṃśaṃ ca maithili| akāryavaśamāpannāḥ striyo yāḥ khalu tadvidhāḥ
translation: मैथिलि O Sita, तद्विधाः such, स्त्रियः women, अकार्यवशम् the influence of unworthy acts, आपन्नः having obtained, अयशश्च infamy, पाप्नुवन्ति are obtaining, धर्मभ्रंशं च dislodged from the state of righteousness.
explanation: O Sita, those women  under the control of unworthy acts are dislodged from the path of righteousness and get infamy.

shloka_text: त्वद्विधास्तु गुणैर्युक्ता दृष्ट लोक परावराः। स्त्रिय स्स्वर्गे चरिष्यन्ति यथा धर्मकृतस्तथा।।2.117.27।।
transliteration: tvadvidhāstu guṇairyuktā dṛṣṭa loka parāvarāḥ| striya ssvarge cariṣyanti yathā dharmakṛtastathā
translation: गुणैः with virtues, युक्ताः endowed with, दृष्टलोकपरावरा who can distinguish between good and bad in the world, त्वद्विधाः like you, स्त्रियस्तु women, धर्मकृतः doing virtuous deeds, यथा as to how, तथा that way, स्वर्गे in heaven, चरिष्यन्ति will range about.
explanation: Women like you who are endowed with virtues and can distinguish between good and bad in this world, like those who  perform  virtuous deeds, will move about in heaven.

shloka_text: सात्वेवमुक्ता वैदेही अनसूयाऽनसूयया। प्रतिपूज्य वचो मन्दं प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे।।2.118.1।।
transliteration: sātvevamuktā vaidehī anasūyā'nasūyayā| pratipūjya vaco mandaṃ pravaktumupacakrame
translation: अनसूया one who is free from malice, सा वैदेही that Vaidehi, अनसूयया by Anasuya, एवम् in this way, उक्ता when  addressed, वचः those words, प्रतिपूज्य having worshipped, मन्दम् in a gentle tone, प्रवक्तुम् to tell, उपचक्रमे commenced.
explanation: When Anasuya thus addressed Vaidehi who is free from any malice, she worshipped  Anasuya  and started speaking in a gentle tone.
comments: Sita relates the story of her marriage to Anasuya -- Anasuya bestows Sita with divine gifts.

shloka_text: नैतदाश्चर्यमार्याया यन्मां त्वमभिभाषसे। विदितन्तु ममाप्येतद्यथा नार्याः पतिर्गुरुः।।2.118.2।।
transliteration: naitadāścaryamāryāyā yanmāṃ tvamabhibhāṣase| viditantu mamāpyetadyathā nāryāḥ patirguruḥ
translation: त्वम् you, माम् to me, यत् अभिभाषसे you are instructing, एतत् all this, आर्यायाः for a noble lady like you, आश्चर्यम् wonder, न not, नार्या for a woman, पतिः husband, गुरुः the revered one, यथा as, एतत् all this, ममापि to me, विदितं तु also known.
explanation: It is no wonder that a noble lady like you should  instruct me this way. It is known to me that a husband is a guru to his wife.

shloka_text: यद्यप्येष भवेद्भर्ता ममाऽर्ये वृत्तवर्जितः। अद्वैधमुपचर्तव्यस्तथाप्येष मया भवेत्।।2.118.3।।
transliteration: yadyapyeṣa bhavedbhartā mamā'rye vṛttavarjitaḥ| advaidhamupacartavyastathāpyeṣa mayā bhavet
translation: आर्ये O noble lady, एषः मम भर्ता my husband, वृत्तवर्जितः  devoid of good conduct, यद्यपि भवेत् even if it happens, तथापि even then, एषः he, मया by me, अद्वैधम् without hesitation, उपचर्तव्यः should be obeyed.
explanation: O noble lady, even if my husband is devoid of good conduct, he should be obeyed without showing any hesitation.

shloka_text: किं पुनर्यो गुणश्लाघ्य स्सानुक्रोशो जितेन्द्रियः। स्थिरानुरागो धर्मात्मा मातृवत्पितृवत्प्रियः।।2.118.4।।
transliteration: kiṃ punaryo guṇaślāghya ssānukrośo jitendriyaḥ| sthirānurāgo dharmātmā mātṛvatpitṛvatpriyaḥ
translation: यः such a man, गुणश्लाघ्यः is worthy of applause for his virtues, सानुक्रोश: compassionate, जितेन्द्रियः subdued his senses, स्थिरानुरागः ever affectionate, धर्मात्मा righteous man, मातृवत् like a mother, पितृवत् like a father, प्रियः is dear, किं पुनः where is the need to say.
explanation: What to speak of a husband if he is worthy of applause for his virtues, is compassionate, a subduer of the senses, righteous and ever affectionate like a mother and a father?

shloka_text: यां वृत्तिं वर्तते रामः कौसल्यायां महाबलः। तामेव नृपनारीणामन्यासामपि वर्तते।।2.118.5।।
transliteration: yāṃ vṛttiṃ vartate rāmaḥ kausalyāyāṃ mahābalaḥ| tāmeva nṛpanārīṇāmanyāsāmapi vartate
translation: महाबलः mighty, रामः Rama, कौसल्यायाम् in Kausalya, यां वृत्तिम् such treatment, वर्तते behaves, अन्यासाम् with others, नृपनारीणामपि consorts of  the king, तामेव the same way, वर्तते behaves.
explanation: Mighty Rama shows the same behaviour and treatment towards the other consorts of the king as he does towards his own mother Kausalya.

shloka_text: सकृद्दृष्टास्वपि स्त्रिषु नृपेण नृपवत्सलः। मातृवद्वर्तते वीरो मानमुत्सृज्य धर्मवित्।।2.118.6।।
transliteration: sakṛddṛṣṭāsvapi striṣu nṛpeṇa nṛpavatsalaḥ| mātṛvadvartate vīro mānamutsṛjya dharmavit
translation: नृपवत्सलः affectionate towards king Dasaratha, धर्मवित् one who is conversant with righteousness, वीरः heroic Rama, नृपेण by king, सकृत् only once, दृष्टासु seen, स्त्रिष्वपि in any woman, मानम् pride, उत्सृज्य setting aside, मातृवत् like a mother, वर्तते abides.
explanation: Heroic Rama is affectionate towards king Dasaratha and is conversant with righteousness. Renouncing the sense of selfrespect he honours all the women on whom his father had cast his glance even once just as his own mother.

shloka_text: आगच्छन्त्याश्च विजनं वनमेवं भयावहम्। समाहितं मे श्वश्र्वा च हृदये तद्धृतं महत्।।2.118.7।।
transliteration: āgacchantyāśca vijanaṃ vanamevaṃ bhayāvaham| samāhitaṃ me śvaśrvā ca hṛdaye taddhṛtaṃ mahat
translation: एवम् in this way, भयावहम् frightful, विजनम् desolate, वनम् forest, आगच्छन्त्याः when I was coming, मे to me, श्वश्वा by motherinlaw, समाहितम् imparted, तत् that, महत् wise instruction, हृदये in my heart, धृतम् is firmly grasped.
explanation: When departing for this frightful and desolate forest, the great (advice) imparted by my motherinlaw is firmly fixed in my mind.

shloka_text: पाणिप्रदानकाले च यत्पुरात्वग्नि सन्निधौ। अनुशिष्टा जनन्याऽस्मि वाक्यं तदपि मे धृतम्।।2.118.8।।
transliteration: pāṇipradānakāle ca yatpurātvagni sannidhau| anuśiṣṭā jananyā'smi vākyaṃ tadapi me dhṛtam
translation: पुरा formerly, पाणिप्रदानकाले च at the time of bestowal of my hand to Rama, अग्नि सन्निधौ in the presence of sacrificial marriage fire, जनन्या by my mother, यत् वाक्यम् that word,  अनुशिष्टा आस्मि I have been taught, तदपि that also, मे to me, धृतम् hold
explanation: When I have been taught by my mother earlier, at the time of bestowal of my hand to Rama in the presence of the sacrificial fire (as witness) is etched in my mind.

shloka_text: नवीकृतं तु तत्सर्वं वाक्यैस्ते धर्मचारिणि। पतिशुश्रूषणान्नार्यास्तपो नान्यद्विधीयते।।2.118.9।।
transliteration: navīkṛtaṃ tu tatsarvaṃ vākyaiste dharmacāriṇi| patiśuśrūṣaṇānnāryāstapo nānyadvidhīyate
translation: धर्मचारिणि O follower of righteous duty (Anasuya), ते वाक्यैः your words, तत् सर्वम् all that, नवीकृतम् renewed (reminded afresh), नार्याः for women, पतिशुश्रूषणात् more than obedience to her husband, अन्यत् other, तपः ascetic practice, न विधीयते is not laid down.
explanation: O righteous one (Anasuya), after listening to your words the instructions given by my motherinlaw and my mother are renewed (remembered again). For a woman, no other penance is laid down (in scriptures) except service to her husband.

shloka_text: सावित्री पतिशुश्रूषां कृत्वा स्वर्गे महीयते। तथावृत्तिश्च याता त्वं पतिशुश्रूषया दिवम्।।2.118.10।।
transliteration: sāvitrī patiśuśrūṣāṃ kṛtvā svarge mahīyate| tathāvṛttiśca yātā tvaṃ patiśuśrūṣayā divam
translation: पतिशुश्रूषाम् service to her husband, कृत्वा having rendered, सावित्री Savitri, स्वर्गे in heaven, महीयते is honoured, तथावृत्ति: having followed the same path, त्वं च you also, पतिशुश्रूषया through serving your husband, दिवम् to heaven, याता shall go.
explanation: Having served her husband (faithfully), Savitri is honoured in heaven. You also, by following the same path of serving your husband, shall reach the heaven.

shloka_text: वरिष्ठा सर्वनारीणामेषा च दिवि देवता। रोहिणी न विनाचन्द्रं मुहूर्तमपि दृश्यते।।2.118.11।।
transliteration: variṣṭhā sarvanārīṇāmeṣā ca divi devatā| rohiṇī na vinācandraṃ muhūrtamapi dṛśyate
translation: सर्वनारीणाम् among  all women, वरिष्ठा the very best, देवता goddess, एषा रोहिणी this Rohini, दिवि in the sky, चन्द्रं विना without the Moon, मुहूर्तमपि even for a moment, न दृश्यते is not seen.
explanation: Rohini, the very best among all women and the goddess of heaven, is never seen in the sky separated from the moon even for a moment.

shloka_text: एवंविधाश्च प्रवराः स्त्रियो भर्तृदृढव्रताः। देवलोके महीयन्ते पुण्येन स्वेन कर्मणा।।2.118.12।।
transliteration: evaṃvidhāśca pravarāḥ striyo bhartṛdṛḍhavratāḥ| devaloke mahīyante puṇyena svena karmaṇā
translation: एवंविधाः such women, प्रवराः excellent, भर्तृदृढव्रताः firm in their vows to their husbands, स्त्रियः women, पुण्येन by merit, स्वेन by their own, कर्मणा deeds, देवलोके in the world of the gods, महीयन्ते are highly revered.
explanation: Execellent women such as these, firm in their vows to their husband are highly revered in the world of gods through their own meritorious deeds.

shloka_text: ततोऽनसूया संहृष्टा श्रुत्वोक्तं सीतया वचः। शिरस्याघ्राय चोवाच मैथिलीं हर्षयन्त्युत।।2.118.13।।
transliteration: tato'nasūyā saṃhṛṣṭā śrutvoktaṃ sītayā vacaḥ| śirasyāghrāya covāca maithilīṃ harṣayantyuta
translation: ततः thereafter, सीतया by Sita, उक्तम् spoken, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, अनसूया Anasuya, संहृष्टा highly rejoiced, मैथिलीम् to Sita, शिरसि on her forehead, अघ्राय having kissed, हर्षयन्ती in order to make her happy, उवाच said.
explanation: Thereafter hearing Sita's words, Anasuya affectionately kissed her forehead and said this in order to make her happy:

shloka_text: नियमैर्विविधैराप्तं तपो हि महदस्ति मे। तत्संश्रित्य बलं सीते छन्दये त्वां शुचिव्रते।।2.118.14।।
transliteration: niyamairvividhairāptaṃ tapo hi mahadasti me| tatsaṃśritya balaṃ sīte chandaye tvāṃ śucivrate
translation: शुचिव्रते O woman of pure conduct, सीते O Sita, विविधैः by various, नियमैः by austerities, आप्तम् obtained, महत् great, तपः ascetic power, मे to me, अस्ति हि is there to my credit, तत् बलम् that ascetic power, संश्रित्य having resorted to, त्वाम् you, छन्दये I shall cause your enjoyment.
explanation: O Sita of pure conduct, I have great ascetic power obtained through practising various austerities. With its strength I shall give what you want for your enjoyment.

shloka_text: उपपन्नं मनोज्ञं च वचनं तव मैथिलि। प्रीता चास्म्युचितं किं ते करवाणि ब्रवीहि मे।।2.118.15।।
transliteration: upapannaṃ manojñaṃ ca vacanaṃ tava maithili| prītā cāsmyucitaṃ kiṃ te karavāṇi bravīhi me
translation: मैथिलि O Sita, तव वचनम् your words, उपपन्नम् are befitting, मनोज्ञं च also pleasing, प्रीता आस्मि I am pleased, उचितम् appropriate thing, किं what, ते to you, करवाणि shall I do, मे to me, ब्रवीहि  tell.
explanation: O Sita, I am glad to hear your befitting and pleasing words. Tell me what appropriate  thing you desire and I shall give you.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तद्  वचनं श्रूत्वा विस्मिता मन्दविस्मया। कृतमित्यब्रवीत् सीता तपोबलसमन्विताम्।।2.118.16।।
transliteration: tasyāstad  vacanaṃ śrūtvā vismitā mandavismayā| kṛtamityabravīt sītā tapobalasamanvitām
translation: सीता Sita, तस्याः her, तद्वचनम् those words, शुत्वा having heard, विस्मिता was surprised, मन्दविस्मया with a gentle smile, तपोबलसमन्विताम् endowed with ascetic power, कृतमिति has been done, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: On hearing her words Sita was surprised. With a gentle smile she said, to Anasuya who was endowed with ascetic power, 'I think you have already granted me the boons'.

shloka_text: सा त्वेवमुक्ता धर्मज्ञा तया प्रीततराऽभवत्। सफलं च प्रहर्षं ते हन्त सीते करोम्यहम्।।2.118.17।।
transliteration: sā tvevamuktā dharmajñā tayā prītatarā'bhavat| saphalaṃ ca praharṣaṃ te hanta sīte karomyaham
translation: धर्मज्ञा knower of righteous ways, सा she (Anasuya), तया by Sita, एवम् in this way, उक्ता having been addressed, प्रीततरा अभवत् she was immensely pleased, सीते O Sita, हन्त what a joy, प्रहर्षम् my delight, ते to you, सफलम् fruitful, अहम् I, करोमि shall do.
explanation: When Sita said so, Anasuya who knew her righteous duty was immensely pleased. and replied, 'What a joy I shall make the words you have spoken come true'.

shloka_text: इदं दिव्यं वरं माल्यं वस्त्रमाभरणानि च। अङ्गरागं च वैदेहि महार्हं चानुलेपनम्।।2.118.18।। मया दत्तमिदं सीते तव गात्राणि शोभयेत्। अनुरूपमसंक्लिष्टं नित्यमेव भविष्यति।।2.118.19।।
transliteration: idaṃ divyaṃ varaṃ mālyaṃ vastramābharaṇāni ca| aṅgarāgaṃ ca vaidehi mahārhaṃ cānulepanam mayā dattamidaṃ sīte tava gātrāṇi śobhayet| anurūpamasaṃkliṣṭaṃ nityameva bhaviṣyati
translation: वैदेहि O princess of Videha, सीते Sita, दिव्यम् divine, वरम् best, इदं माल्यम् this garland,  वस्त्रम् raiment, आभरणानि च jewellery, अङ्गरागं च fragrant unguents, महार्हम् precious, अनुलेपनं च ointment for anointing the body, मया by me, दत्तम् is bestowed, इदम् all this, तव to your, गात्राणि limbs, शोभयेत् will beautify, नित्यम् always, अनुरूपम् convenient, असंक्लिष्टम् भविष्यति will never impair.
explanation: O princess of Videha, O  Sita, I bestow on you this best garland of the gods, raiment, jewellery, fragrant unguents, and precious ointment for anointing your body with. All this will beautify your limbs. It is convenient (to use) and will never fade.

shloka_text: इदं दिव्यं वरं माल्यं वस्त्रमाभरणानि च। अङ्गरागं च वैदेहि महार्हं चानुलेपनम्।।2.118.18।। मया दत्तमिदं सीते तव गात्राणि शोभयेत्। अनुरूपमसंक्लिष्टं नित्यमेव भविष्यति।।2.118.19।।
transliteration: idaṃ divyaṃ varaṃ mālyaṃ vastramābharaṇāni ca| aṅgarāgaṃ ca vaidehi mahārhaṃ cānulepanam mayā dattamidaṃ sīte tava gātrāṇi śobhayet| anurūpamasaṃkliṣṭaṃ nityameva bhaviṣyati
translation: वैदेहि O princess of Videha, सीते Sita, दिव्यम् divine, वरम् best, इदं माल्यम् this garland,  वस्त्रम् raiment, आभरणानि च jewellery, अङ्गरागं च fragrant unguents, महार्हम् precious, अनुलेपनं च ointment for anointing the body, मया by me, दत्तम् is bestowed, इदम् all this, तव to your, गात्राणि limbs, शोभयेत् will beautify, नित्यम् always, अनुरूपम् convenient, असंक्लिष्टम् भविष्यति will never impair.
explanation: O princess of Videha, O  Sita, I bestow on you this best garland of the gods, raiment, jewellery, fragrant unguents, and precious ointment for anointing your body with. All this will beautify your limbs. It is convenient (to use) and will never fade.

shloka_text: अङ्गरागेण दिव्येन लिप्ताङ्गी जनकात्मजे। शोभयिष्यसि भर्तारं यथा श्रीर्विष्णुमव्ययम्।।2.118.20।।
transliteration: aṅgarāgeṇa divyena liptāṅgī janakātmaje| śobhayiṣyasi bhartāraṃ yathā śrīrviṣṇumavyayam
translation: जनकात्मजे O daughter of Janaka, दिव्ये O divine lady, अङ्गरागेण with fragrant unguent, लिप्ताङ्गी anointing to your body, श्रीः Lakshmi, अव्ययम् imperishable, विष्णुम् Vishnu, यथा how, भर्तारम् your husband, शोभयिष्यसि you will enhance the glory.
explanation: O daughter of Janaka, you will enhance the glory of your husband by anointing your body with this divine, fragrant unguent to your body like Lakshmi enhancing the glory of eternal Visnu.

shloka_text: सा वस्त्रमङ्गरागं च भूषणानि स्रजस्तथा। मैथिली प्रतिजग्राह प्रीतिदानमनुत्तमम्।।2.118.21।।
transliteration: sā vastramaṅgarāgaṃ ca bhūṣaṇāni srajastathā| maithilī pratijagrāha prītidānamanuttamam
translation: सा मैथिली that princess from Mithila, वस्त्रम् raiment, अङ्गरागं च fragrant unguent, भूषणानि jewellery, तथा and, स्रजः garlands, अनुत्तमम् incomparable, प्रीतिदानम् gifts of love, प्रतिजग्राह accepted.
explanation: That princess from Mithila accepted the incomparable gifts of love, the raiment, fragrant unguents, jewellery and also the garland.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य च तत्सीता प्रीतिदानं यशस्विनी। श्लिष्टाञ्जलिपुटा तत्र समुपास्त तपोधनाम्।।2.118.22।।
transliteration: pratigṛhya ca tatsītā prītidānaṃ yaśasvinī| śliṣṭāñjalipuṭā tatra samupāsta tapodhanām
translation: यशस्विनी illustrious lady, सीता Sita, तत् that, प्रीतिदानम् gifts of love, प्रतिगृह्य having accepted, श्लिष्टाञ्जलिपुटा with hands folded like a dish in reverence, तत्र there, तपोधनाम् ascetic, समुपास्त sat beside her.
explanation: Illustrious Sita accepted the gifts of love and with palms folded in reverence sat beside her, an ascetic.

shloka_text: तथा सीतामुपासीनामनसूया दृढव्रता। वचनं प्रष्टुमारेभे काञ्चित्प्रियकथामनु।।2.118.23।।
transliteration: tathā sītāmupāsīnāmanasūyā dṛḍhavratā| vacanaṃ praṣṭumārebhe kāñcitpriyakathāmanu
translation: दृढव्रता firm in her vows, अनसूया Anasuya, तथा in that way, उपासीनाम् sitting, सीताम् Sita, कांचित् certain, प्रियकथामनु relating to a dear tale (that was close to her heart), प्रष्टुम् to ask, वचनम् these words, आरेभे commenced.
explanation: Anasuya who was firm in her vows commenced to ask Sita this way about a certain tale (that was close to her heart).

shloka_text: स्वयं वरे किल प्राप्ता त्वमनेन यशस्विना। राघवेणेति मे सिते कथा श्रुतिमुपागता।।2.118.24।।
transliteration: svayaṃ vare kila prāptā tvamanena yaśasvinā| rāghaveṇeti me site kathā śrutimupāgatā
translation: सीते O Sita, त्वम् you, यशस्विना by the illustrious one, राघवेण by Rama, स्वयंवरे in the swayamvara (the choice of the husband by a princess in the public), प्राप्ता किल are obtained, इति कथा so runs the story, मे my, श्रुतिम् my ear, उपागता reached.
explanation: O Sita, I have heard that you have been won by the illustrious Rama in the swayamvara. At least that is the story which reached my ears.

shloka_text: तां कथां श्रोतुमिच्छामि विस्तरेण च मैथिलि। यथाऽनुभूतं कार्त्स्न्येन तन्मे त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि।।2.118.25।।
transliteration: tāṃ kathāṃ śrotumicchāmi vistareṇa ca maithili| yathā'nubhūtaṃ kārtsnyena tanme tvaṃ vaktumarhasi
translation: मैथिलि O daughter of the king of Mithila,  ताम् that story,  विस्तरेण in detail, श्रोतुम् to hear, इच्छामि I wish, तत् that one, त्वम् you, यथाऽनुभूतम् as you experienced, कात्स्न्येन entirely, वक्तुम् अर्हसि  you should tell me.
explanation: O daughter of Mithila, I would like to hear the story in detail. You should tell me the whole story as you experienced it.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु सा सीता तां ततो धर्मचारिणीम्। श्रूयतामिति चोक्त्वा वै कथयामास तां कथाम्।।2.118.26।।
transliteration: evamuktā tu sā sītā tāṃ tato dharmacāriṇīm| śrūyatāmiti coktvā vai kathayāmāsa tāṃ kathām
translation: एवम् thus, उक्ता  addressed, सा सीता that Sita, ततः then, श्रूयताम् इति  listen, उक्त्वा having said, ताम् that, धर्मचारिणीम् to one who practiced righteousness, तां कथाम् that story, कथयामास related.
explanation: 'Listen' said Sita, thus addressed, and began relating the story to Anasuya, a performer of austerities.

shloka_text: मिथिलाधिपतिर्वीरो जनको नाम धर्मवित्। क्षत्रधर्मे ह्यभिरतो न्यायतश्शास्ति मेदिनीम्।।2.118.27।।
transliteration: mithilādhipatirvīro janako nāma dharmavit| kṣatradharme hyabhirato nyāyataśśāsti medinīm
translation: मिथिलाधिपतिः king of Mithila, वीरः a warrior, धर्मवित् one conversant wtih righteousness, जनको नाम by name Janaka, क्षत्रधर्मे in the duties of kshatriya, अभिरतः engaged, न्यायतः  rightly, मेदिनीम् this earth, शास्ति was ruling.
explanation: There is a king in Mithila, Janaka by name. He is heroic and is conversant with  righteousness. Engaged in the duties of a kshatriya, he is rules the earth with justice.

shloka_text: तस्य लाङ्गलहस्तन्य कर्षतः क्षेत्रमण्डलम्। अहं किलोत्थिता भित्वा जगतीं नृपतेस्सुता।।2.118.28।।
transliteration: tasya lāṅgalahastanya karṣataḥ kṣetramaṇḍalam| ahaṃ kilotthitā bhitvā jagatīṃ nṛpatessutā
translation: तस्य his, लाङ्गलहस्तस्य of a man holding a plough in hand, क्षेत्रमण्डलम् the circular plot of land for performing sacrifice, कर्षतः while ploughing, अहम् I, नृपतेः king's, सुता as daughter, जगतीम् the earth, भित्वा breaking, उत्थिता किल arose, as they say.
explanation: When he was ploughing the circular plot of land for performing a sacrifice, it is said I emerged from the earth by breaking it and therefore I became his dauhghter.

shloka_text: स मां दृष्ट्वा नरपतिर्मुष्टिविक्षेपतत्परः। पांसुकुण्ठितसर्वाङ्गीं जनको विस्मितोऽभवत्।।2.118.29।।
transliteration: sa māṃ dṛṣṭvā narapatirmuṣṭivikṣepatatparaḥ| pāṃsukuṇṭhitasarvāṅgīṃ janako vismito'bhavat
translation: मुष्टिविक्षेपतत्परः eager to sow fistfuls of seeds, नरपतिः king, सः जनकः that Janaka, पांसुकुण्ठितसर्वाङ्गीं with my body covered with dust, माम् me, दृष्ट्वा having seen, विस्मितः अभवत् was astonished.
explanation: Engaged in sowing fistfuls of seeds, king Janaka found me covered with dust and was astonished.

shloka_text: अनपत्येन च स्नेहादङ्कमारोप्य च स्वयम्। ममेयं तनयेत्युक्त्वा स्नेहो मयि निपातितः।।2.118.30।।
transliteration: anapatyena ca snehādaṅkamāropya ca svayam| mameyaṃ tanayetyuktvā sneho mayi nipātitaḥ
translation: अनपत्येन being childless, स्वयम् himself, स्नेहात् out of affection, अङ्कम् in his lap, आरोप्य placing, इयम् this one, मम तनया is my daughter, इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, मयि in me,  स्नेहः affection, निपातितः showered
explanation: As he had no children, he, on his own accord, lifted me up and placing me on his lap, saying, This is my daughter, he began showering (lots of) love on me.

shloka_text: अन्तरिक्षे च वागुक्ताऽप्रतिमाऽमानुषी किल। एवमेतन्नरपते धर्मेण तनया तव।।2.118.31।।
transliteration: antarikṣe ca vāguktā'pratimā'mānuṣī kila| evametannarapate dharmeṇa tanayā tava
translation: नरपते O king, एतत् this, एवम् in this way, अप्रतिमा incomparable, अमानुषी not a human being, तव to you, धर्मेण by right, तनया daughter, अन्तरिक्षे from out of the sky, वाक् word, उक्ता  was uttered.
explanation: 'O king, she is an incomparable divine being. By right she is your daughter'. These were the words (Janaka) heard from out of the sky.

shloka_text: ततः प्रहृष्टो धर्मात्मा पिता मे मिथिलाधिपः। अवाप्तो विपुलां बुद्धिं मामवाप्य नराधिपः।।2.118.32।।
transliteration: tataḥ prahṛṣṭo dharmātmā pitā me mithilādhipaḥ| avāpto vipulāṃ buddhiṃ māmavāpya narādhipaḥ
translation: ततः thereafter, धर्मात्मा righteous, नराधिप: the king, मिथिलाधिपः the lord of Mithila, मे पिता my father, प्रहृष्टः was delighted, माम् me, अवाप्य having got, विपुलाम् noble, बुद्धिम् thought, अवाप्तः obtained.
explanation: Thereafter, my father and the righteous lord of Mithila was delighted in possessing  me when a noble thought struck his mind.

shloka_text: दत्ता चास्मीष्टवद्देव्यै ज्येष्ठायै पुण्यकर्मणा। तया सम्भाविता चास्मि स्निग्धया मातृसौहृदात्।।2.118.33।।
transliteration: dattā cāsmīṣṭavaddevyai jyeṣṭhāyai puṇyakarmaṇā| tayā sambhāvitā cāsmi snigdhayā mātṛsauhṛdāt
translation: पुण्यकर्मणा by a man of meritorious acts, ज्येष्ठायै to the chief, देव्यैः queen, इष्टवत् as the choicest one, दत्ता अस्मि I was given, स्निग्धया by a lady endowed with affection, तया by her, मातृसौहृदात् with the love of a mother, सम्भाविता अस्मि I was nourished.
explanation: Bestowed as the choicest one of meritorious acts on the chief queen, I was brought up by her, by nature affectionate, with the love of a mother.

shloka_text: पतिसंयोगसुलभं वयो दृष्ट्वा तु मे पिता। चिन्तामभ्यगमद्धीनो वित्तनाशादिवाधनः।।2.118.34।।
transliteration: patisaṃyogasulabhaṃ vayo dṛṣṭvā tu me pitā| cintāmabhyagamaddhīno vittanāśādivādhanaḥ
translation: मे पिता my father, पतिसंयोगसुलभम् a proper time for uniting with a husband, वयः age,         दृष्ट्वा having observed, दीनः desolate, वित्तनाशात् due to loss of wealth, अधनः इव like an poor man, चिन्ताम् sorrow, अभ्यगमत् obtained.
explanation: When my father saw I had attained  the marriageable age, he was immersed in sorrow like an indigent man who had lost all his wealth.

shloka_text: सदृशाच्चापकृष्टाच्च लोके कन्यापिता जनात्। प्रधर्षणामवाप्नोति शक्रेणापि समो भुवि।।2.118.35।।
transliteration: sadṛśāccāpakṛṣṭācca loke kanyāpitā janāt| pradharṣaṇāmavāpnoti śakreṇāpi samo bhuvi
translation: भुवि on earth, शक्रेण with Indra, समोऽपि though equal, कन्यापिता the father of an unmarried girl, सदृशाः equal, अपकृष्टात् by an inferior, जनात् from men, लोके in this world, प्रधर्षणाम् humiliation, अवाप्नोति will receive.
explanation: Even though he was an Indra on earth, as a father of  an unmarried girl he would be humiliated by men who are his equal or inferior in this world.

shloka_text: तां धर्षणामदूरस्थां दृष्ट्वा चात्मनि पार्थिवः। चिन्तार्णवगतः पारं नाससादाप्लवो यथा।।2.118.36।।
transliteration: tāṃ dharṣaṇāmadūrasthāṃ dṛṣṭvā cātmani pārthivaḥ| cintārṇavagataḥ pāraṃ nāsasādāplavo yathā
translation: पार्थिवः the king, तां धर्षणाम् that humiliation, आत्मनि in him, अदूरस्थाम् not very far, दृष्ट्वा having observed, चिन्तार्णवगतः submerged in a sea of sorrow, अप्लवो यथा like one without a float, पारम् the shore, नाससाद did not reach.
explanation: Having perceived that the humiliation is not very far, king Janaka was plunged in a sea of sorrow like one who cannot reach the shore without a float.

shloka_text: अयोनिजां हि मां ज्ञात्वा नाध्यगच्छद्विचिन्तयन्। सदृशं चानुरूपं च महीपालः पतिं मम।।2.118.37।।
transliteration: ayonijāṃ hi māṃ jñātvā nādhyagacchadvicintayan| sadṛśaṃ cānurūpaṃ ca mahīpālaḥ patiṃ mama
translation: महीपालः the ruler of earth, माम् me, अयोनिजाम् not born from the womb, ज्ञात्वा having known, मम for me, सदृशम् equal, अनुरूपं च suitable, पतिम् husband, विचिन्तयन् thinking over, नाध्यगच्छत् did not find.
explanation: The ruler of the earth knew that I was not born from a woman's womb, and could not find a suitable husband for me after deep reflection.

shloka_text: तस्य बुद्धिरियं जाता चिन्तयानस्य सन्ततम्। स्वयंवरं तनूजायाः करिष्यामीति धीमतः।।2.118.38।।
transliteration: tasya buddhiriyaṃ jātā cintayānasya santatam| svayaṃvaraṃ tanūjāyāḥ kariṣyāmīti dhīmataḥ
translation: सन्ततम् constantly, चिन्तयानस्य pondering deeply, धीमतः wise, तस्य his, तनूजायाः for the daughter, स्वयंवरम् swayamvara, करिष्यामि I shall perform, इति thus, इयं बुद्धि: this thought, जाता was born.
explanation: After constantly pondering over the matter, the wise king arrived at the decision to perform a swayamvara for his daughter.

shloka_text: महायज्ञे तदा तस्य वरुणेन महात्मना। दत्तं धनुर्वरं प्रीत्या तूणी चाक्षयसायकौ।।2.118.39।।
transliteration: mahāyajñe tadā tasya varuṇena mahātmanā| dattaṃ dhanurvaraṃ prītyā tūṇī cākṣayasāyakau
translation: तदा then, महायज्ञे at a great sacrifice, तस्य to him, महात्मना by the magnanimous, वरुणेन by Varuna, प्रीत्या with affection, धनुर्वरम् an excellent bow, दत्तम् was given, अक्षयसायकौ with two inexhaustible arrows, तूणी च and two quivers.
explanation: Magnanimous Varuna out of his affection had given him, on the occasion of a great sacrifice, an excellent bow with inexhaustible arrows and a pair of quivers.

shloka_text: असञ्चाल्यं मनुष्यैश्च यत्नेनापि च गौरवात्। तन्न शक्ता नमयितुं स्वप्नेष्वपि नराधिपाः।।2.118.40।।
transliteration: asañcālyaṃ manuṣyaiśca yatnenāpi ca gauravāt| tanna śaktā namayituṃ svapneṣvapi narādhipāḥ
translation: गौरवात् because of weight, मनुष्यैः by a human, यत्नेनापि even with great effort,  असञ्चाल्यम् cannot be moved, तत् that bow, नराधिपाः lords of men, स्वप्नेष्वपि even in their dreams, नमयितुम् to bend, न शक्ताः were not capable.
explanation: Because of its weight, no human could move that bow despite great effort nor were the kings capable of bending it even in their dreams.

shloka_text: तद्धनुः प्राप्य मे पित्रा व्याहृतं सत्यवादिना। समवाये नरेन्द्राणां पूर्वमामन्त्र्य पार्थिवान्।।2.118.41।।
transliteration: taddhanuḥ prāpya me pitrā vyāhṛtaṃ satyavādinā| samavāye narendrāṇāṃ pūrvamāmantrya pārthivān
translation: सत्यवादिना by a truthful man, मे पित्रा by my father, पूर्वम् previously, पार्थिवान् kings, आमन्त्र्य having invited, नरेन्द्राणाम् of kings, समवाये in the assembly, तत् धनुः that bow, प्राप्य having acquired, व्याहृतम् addressed them.
explanation: My truthful father, after having acquired the bow, invited all the princes and placed the great bow before them in the assembly where he declared:

shloka_text: इदं च धनुरुद्यम्य सज्यं यः कुरुते नरः। तस्य मे दुहिता भार्या भविष्यति न संशयः।।2.118.42।।
transliteration: idaṃ ca dhanurudyamya sajyaṃ yaḥ kurute naraḥ| tasya me duhitā bhāryā bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
translation: यः नर: any man, इदं धनुः this bow, उद्यम्य having lifted, सज्यं च string the bow, कुरुते who could do, तस्य to him, मे दुहिता my daughter, भार्या wife, भविष्यति shall become, संशयः न no doubt about it.
explanation: Whatever man lifts this bow and strings it, to him my daughter shall become his wife—of this there is no doubt.

shloka_text: तच्च दृष्ट्वा धनुश्श्रेष्ठं गौरवाद्गिरिसन्निभम्। अभिवाद्य नृपा जग्मुरशक्तास्तस्य तोलने।।2.118.43।।
transliteration: tacca dṛṣṭvā dhanuśśreṣṭhaṃ gauravādgirisannibham| abhivādya nṛpā jagmuraśaktāstasya tolane
translation: नृपाः the kings, गौरवात् due to heavy weight, गिरिसन्निभम् resembling a mountain, तत् धनुः श्रेष्ठम् that mighty bow, दृष्ट्वा beholding, तस्य its, तोलने in lifting, अशक्ताः were unable, अभिवाद्य paying obeisance, जग्मुः went away.
explanation: Beholding the mighty bow resembling a mountain in weight, the kings, unable to lift it, paid their homage and left.

shloka_text: सुदीर्घस्य तु कालस्य राघवोऽयं महाद्युतिः। विश्वामित्रेण सहितो यज्ञं द्रष्टुं समागतः।।2.118.44।। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा राम स्सत्यपराक्रमः।
transliteration: sudīrghasya tu kālasya rāghavo'yaṃ mahādyutiḥ| viśvāmitreṇa sahito yajñaṃ draṣṭuṃ samāgataḥ lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā rāma ssatyaparākramaḥ|
translation: सुदीर्घस्य कालस्य after a long time, राघवः Rama, महाद्युतिः resplendent, सत्यपराक्रमः whose prowess was truth, अयं रामः this Rama, भ्रात्रा with his brother, लक्ष्मणेन सह along with Lakshmana, विश्वामित्रेण सहितः together with Viswamitra, यज्ञम् the sacrifice, द्रष्टुम् to observe, समागतः arrived.
explanation: After a long time, resplendent Rama whose prowess was truth, arrived along with  his brother Lakshman and sage Viswamitra in order to witness the sacrifice.

shloka_text: विश्वामित्रस्तु धर्मात्मा मम पित्रा सुपूजितः।।2.118.45।। प्रोवाच पितरं तत्र भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
transliteration: viśvāmitrastu dharmātmā mama pitrā supūjitaḥ provāca pitaraṃ tatra bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau|
translation: धर्मात्मा the righteous man, विश्वामित्रस्तु as for Viswamitra, मम पित्रा by my father, सुपूजितः wellhonoured, तत्र there, भ्रातरौ brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ to Rama and Lakshmana, पितरम् to my father, प्रोवाच uttered.
explanation: Having accepted the honour extended by my father, righteous Viswamitra spoke to him about those two brothers, Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: सुतौ दशरथस्येमौ धनुर्दर्शकाङ्क्षिणौ। धनुर्दर्शय रामाय राजपुत्राय दैविकम्।।2.118.46।।
transliteration: sutau daśarathasyemau dhanurdarśakāṅkṣiṇau| dhanurdarśaya rāmāya rājaputrāya daivikam
translation: दशरथस्य king Dasaratha's, सुतौ sons, इमौ both these, धनुर्दर्शकाङ्क्षिणौ are desirous of seeing the bow, राजपुत्राय to this king's son, रामाय to Rama, दैविकम् divine, धनुः bow, दर्शय show.
explanation: 'Both these sons of king Dasaratha wish to see the bow. Show the divine bow to prince  Rama'.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तस्तेन विप्रेण तद्धनुस्समुपानयत्।।2.118.47।। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण तदाऽनम्य महाबलः। ज्यां समारोप्य झडिति पूरयामास वीर्यवान्।।2.118.48।।
transliteration: ityuktastena vipreṇa taddhanussamupānayat nimeṣāntaramātreṇa tadā'namya mahābalaḥ| jyāṃ samāropya jhaḍiti pūrayāmāsa vīryavān
translation: तेन विप्रेण by that ascetic, इति thus, उक्तः uttered, ततो then, धनुः bow, उपानयत् brought, महाबलः mighty one, वीर्यवान् valiant man, निमेषान्तरमात्रेण in the twinkling of an eye, तत् that one, आनम्य having bent, झडिति instantly, ज्याम् the string, समारोप्य pulling it, पूरयामास drew it.
explanation: At the words of that ascetic, my father brought out the bow. Mighty and valiant Rama bent it and strung it and drew it in the twinkling of an eye.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तस्तेन विप्रेण तद्धनुस्समुपानयत्।।2.118.47।। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण तदाऽनम्य महाबलः। ज्यां समारोप्य झडिति पूरयामास वीर्यवान्।।2.118.48।।
transliteration: ityuktastena vipreṇa taddhanussamupānayat nimeṣāntaramātreṇa tadā'namya mahābalaḥ| jyāṃ samāropya jhaḍiti pūrayāmāsa vīryavān
translation: तेन विप्रेण by that ascetic, इति thus, उक्तः uttered, ततो then, धनुः bow, उपानयत् brought, महाबलः mighty one, वीर्यवान् valiant man, निमेषान्तरमात्रेण in the twinkling of an eye, तत् that one, आनम्य having bent, झडिति instantly, ज्याम् the string, समारोप्य pulling it, पूरयामास drew it.
explanation: At the words of that ascetic, my father brought out the bow. Mighty and valiant Rama bent it and strung it and drew it in the twinkling of an eye.

shloka_text: तेन पूरयता वेगान्मध्ये भग्नं द्विधा धनुः। तस्य शब्दो भवद्भीमः पतितस्याशनेरिव।।2.118.49।।
transliteration: tena pūrayatā vegānmadhye bhagnaṃ dvidhā dhanuḥ| tasya śabdo bhavadbhīmaḥ patitasyāśaneriva
translation: पूरयता while stringing, तेन by Rama, वेगात् with force, धनुः bow, मध्ये in the middle, द्विधा into two, भग्नम् was broken, तस्य its, भीमः dreadful, शब्दः sound, पतितस्य fallen, अशनेरिव like that of a thunder, अभवत् arose.
explanation: When Rama was stringing the bow with force, it was broken into two in the middle and fell down with a dreadful sound like that of thunder.

shloka_text: ततोऽहं तत्र रामाय पित्रा सत्याभिसन्धिना। निश्चिता दातुमुद्यम्य जलभाजनमुत्तमम्।।2.118.50।।
transliteration: tato'haṃ tatra rāmāya pitrā satyābhisandhinā| niścitā dātumudyamya jalabhājanamuttamam
translation: ततः then, तत्र there, सत्याभिसन्धिना by one steadfast in truth, पित्रा by my father, उत्तमम् pure, जलभाजनम् watervessel, उद्यम्य having raised, अहम् I, रामाय to Rama , दातुम् to give, निश्चिता decided.
explanation: Then, my father steadfast in truth, held a vessel of pure water and declared his decision to offer me to Rama.

shloka_text: दीयमानां न तु तदा प्रतिजग्राह राघवः। अविज्ञाय पितुश्छन्दमयोध्याऽधिपतेः प्रभोः।।2.118.51।।
transliteration: dīyamānāṃ na tu tadā pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ| avijñāya pituśchandamayodhyā'dhipateḥ prabhoḥ
translation: तदा then, राघवः Rama, अयोध्याऽधिपतेः of the king of Ayodhya, प्रभोः lord, पितुः his father's, छन्दम् opinion, अविज्ञाय without knowing, दीयमानाम् being offered by father, न तु प्रतिजग्राह did not accept.
explanation: Then Rama did not accept the offer of my father straightaway before he knew the opinion of his father Dasaratha,  king of Ayodhya.

shloka_text: तत श्श्वशुरमामन्त्र्य वृद्धं दशरथं नृपम्। मम पित्रा त्वहं दत्ता रामाय विदितात्मने।।2.118.52।।
transliteration: tata śśvaśuramāmantrya vṛddhaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam| mama pitrā tvahaṃ dattā rāmāya viditātmane
translation: ततः then, मम पित्रा by my father, श्वशुरम् fatherinlaw, वृद्धम् aged, दशरथं नृपम् king Dasaratha, आमन्त्र्य having invited, अहम् I, विदितात्मन: of a man who is known for his sagacity, रामाय to Rama, दत्ता I was given.
explanation: Thereafter, my fatherinlaw, the aged king Dasaratha was invited and my father  offered me to Rama  known for his sagacity.

shloka_text: मम चैवानुजा साध्वी ऊर्मिला प्रियदर्शना। भार्यार्थे लक्ष्मणस्यापि दत्ता पित्रा मम स्वयम्।।2.118.53।।
transliteration: mama caivānujā sādhvī ūrmilā priyadarśanā| bhāryārthe lakṣmaṇasyāpi dattā pitrā mama svayam
translation: मम my, अनुजा younger sister, साध्वी chaste, प्रियदर्शना pleasing appearance, ऊर्मिला Urmila, भार्यार्थे as wife, मम पित्रा by my father, स्वयम् of his own accord, लक्ष्मणस्यापि for Lakshman, दत्ता was given.
explanation: My father, on his own accord, bestowed Urmila, my younger sister of chaste and of  pleasing appearance as wife to Lakshmana.

shloka_text: एवं दत्ताऽस्मि रामाय तदा तस्मिन्स्वयंवरे। अनुरक्ताऽस्मि धर्मेण पतिं वीर्यवतां वरम्।।2.118.54।।
transliteration: evaṃ dattā'smi rāmāya tadā tasminsvayaṃvare| anuraktā'smi dharmeṇa patiṃ vīryavatāṃ varam
translation: तदा then, तस्मिन् स्वयंवरे in that swayamvara, रामाय for Rama, एवम् in this way, दत्ता अस्मि was bestowed, वीर्यवताम् among valiant, वरम् foremost, पतिम् husband, धर्मेण in accordance with righteousness, अनुरक्ता अस्मि I remain devoted.
explanation: In this way my father bestowed me on Rama in that swayamvara and I remain devoted to my husband who is the foremost among the valiant in treading the path of  righteousness. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टादशोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः। Thus ends the one hundredeighteenth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अनसूया तु धर्मज्ञा श्रुत्वा तां महतीं कथाम्। पर्यष्वजत बाहुभ्यां शिरस्याघ्राय मैथिलीम्।।2.119.1।।
transliteration: anasūyā tu dharmajñā śrutvā tāṃ mahatīṃ kathām| paryaṣvajata bāhubhyāṃ śirasyāghrāya maithilīm
translation: धर्मज्ञा knower of righteousness, अनसूया तु Anasuya on her part, ताम् all that, महतीं कथाम्  great narrative, श्रुत्वा having heard, मैथिलीम् Sita, शिरसि on head, आघ्राय having smelt, बाहुभ्याम् with arms, पर्यष्वजत embraced.
explanation: Then righteous Anasuya, having heard the great story of Sita, kissed her on the forehead and embraced her with both the arms.
comments: Rama, Lakshmana and Sita take leave of Atri and Anasuya -- enter the Dandaka forest.

shloka_text: व्यक्ताक्षरपदं चित्रं भाषितं मधुरं त्वया। यथा स्वयंवरं वृत्तं तत्सर्वं हि श्रुतं मया।।2.119.2।। रमेऽहं कथया ते तु दृढं मधुरभाषिणि।
transliteration: vyaktākṣarapadaṃ citraṃ bhāṣitaṃ madhuraṃ tvayā| yathā svayaṃvaraṃ vṛttaṃ tatsarvaṃ hi śrutaṃ mayā rame'haṃ kathayā te tu dṛḍhaṃ madhurabhāṣiṇi|
translation: त्वया by you, व्यक्ताक्षरपदम् with each word and each syllable uttered clearly, चित्रम्   wonderful, मधुरम् sweet, भाषितम् spoken, स्वयंवरम् the ceremony in which the bride chooses the groom of her own accord, यथा as, वृत्तम् it happened, तत्सर्वं all that, मया by me, श्रुतं हि has been heard, मधुरभाषिणि O sweetspeaking, Sita, ते your, कथया in the story, अहम् I, दृढम् रमे I enjoy  greatly.
explanation: You have related wonderfully and sweetly your Swayamvara with each word and each syllable uttered clearly. I have heard everything as it happened. O sweetspeaking Sita, I have greatly enjoyed your story.

shloka_text: रविरस्तङ्गतश्श्रीमानुपोह्य रजनीं शिवाम्।।2.119.3।। दिवसं प्रतिकीर्णानामाहारार्थं पतत्रिणाम्। सन्ध्याकाले निलीनानां निद्रार्थं श्रूयते ध्वनिः।।2.119.4।।
transliteration: ravirastaṅgataśśrīmānupohya rajanīṃ śivām divasaṃ pratikīrṇānāmāhārārthaṃ patatriṇām| sandhyākāle nilīnānāṃ nidrārthaṃ śrūyate dhvaniḥ
translation: श्रीमान् resplendent, रविः Sun, शिवाम् auspicious, रजनीम् night, उपोह्य after drawing near, अस्तगतः has set, दिवसम् during day, आहारार्थम् for the sake of food, प्रतिकीर्णानाम् forage far and wide, सन्ध्याकाले in the twilight, निद्रार्थम् for the sake of sleep, निलीनानाम् resting, पतत्रिणाम् of birds, ध्वनिः sound, श्रूयते is heard.
explanation: The resplendent Sun has set. The auspcious night is drawing near. The birds who forage far and wide for food during the day return to their nests to rest for the night. You can hear them twittering.

shloka_text: रविरस्तङ्गतश्श्रीमानुपोह्य रजनीं शिवाम्।।2.119.3।। दिवसं प्रतिकीर्णानामाहारार्थं पतत्रिणाम्। सन्ध्याकाले निलीनानां निद्रार्थं श्रूयते ध्वनिः।।2.119.4।।
transliteration: ravirastaṅgataśśrīmānupohya rajanīṃ śivām divasaṃ pratikīrṇānāmāhārārthaṃ patatriṇām| sandhyākāle nilīnānāṃ nidrārthaṃ śrūyate dhvaniḥ
translation: श्रीमान् resplendent, रविः Sun, शिवाम् auspicious, रजनीम् night, उपोह्य after drawing near, अस्तगतः has set, दिवसम् during day, आहारार्थम् for the sake of food, प्रतिकीर्णानाम् forage far and wide, सन्ध्याकाले in the twilight, निद्रार्थम् for the sake of sleep, निलीनानाम् resting, पतत्रिणाम् of birds, ध्वनिः sound, श्रूयते is heard.
explanation: The resplendent Sun has set. The auspcious night is drawing near. The birds who forage far and wide for food during the day return to their nests to rest for the night. You can hear them twittering.

shloka_text: एते चाप्यभिषेकार्द्रा मुनयः कलशोद्यताः। सहिता उपवर्तन्ते सलिलाप्लुतवल्कलाः।।2.119.5।।
transliteration: ete cāpyabhiṣekārdrā munayaḥ kalaśodyatāḥ| sahitā upavartante salilāplutavalkalāḥ
translation: एते मुनयः च these sages, अभिषेकार्द्राः wet through ablution, कलशोद्यताः carrying waterpitchers, सलिलाप्लुतवल्कलाः their bark robes soaked with water, सहिता: in groups, उपवर्तन्ते are returning.
explanation: The sages also  are returning in groups with waterpitchers filled with water and their bark robes soaked with water after their ceremonial bath.

shloka_text: ऋषीणामग्निहोत्रेषु हुतेषु विधिपूर्वकम्। कपोताङ्गारुणो धूमो दृश्यते पवनोद्धतः।।2.119.6।।
transliteration: ṛṣīṇāmagnihotreṣu huteṣu vidhipūrvakam| kapotāṅgāruṇo dhūmo dṛśyate pavanoddhataḥ
translation: ऋषीणाम् of the ascetics, अग्निहोत्रेषु  in Agnihotra sacrifices, विधिपूर्वकम् duly, हुतेषु oblations offered, कपोताङ्गारुणः tawny like the pigeon's body, धूमः smoke, पवनोद्धतः raised by the wind, दृश्यते is seen.
explanation: The ascetics have duly offered oblations to the fire in Agnihotra sacrifices and the smoke, tawny like the pigeon's body, emanates wafted by the wind.

shloka_text: अल्पपर्णा हि तरवो घनीभूतास्समन्ततः। विप्रकृष्टेन्द्रिये देशेऽस्मिन्न प्रकाशन्ति वै दिशः।।2.119.7।।
transliteration: alpaparṇā hi taravo ghanībhūtāssamantataḥ| viprakṛṣṭendriye deśe'sminna prakāśanti vai diśaḥ
translation: समन्ततः on all sides, अल्पपर्णाः with sparse leaves, तरवः trees, घनीभूताः have grown dense, विप्रकृष्टेन्द्रिये with disturbed senses, अस्मिन् देशे in this region, दिशः the four quarters, न प्रकाशन्ति वै no longer look bright.
explanation: The trees with sparse leaves all over have grown dense, the quarters in the distant region are no longer discernible by the senses.

shloka_text: रजनीचरसत्त्वानि प्रचरन्ति समन्ततः। तपोवनमृगा ह्येते वेदितीर्थेषु शेरते।।2.119.8।।
transliteration: rajanīcarasattvāni pracaranti samantataḥ| tapovanamṛgā hyete veditīrtheṣu śerate
translation: रजनीचरसत्वानि the beings that range by night, समन्ततः everywhere, प्रचरन्ति are wandering, एते तपोवनमृगाः these deer of the penance grove, वेदितीर्थेषु around sacred altars, शेरते are sleeping.
explanation: The night rangers have started moving everywhere and the deer in the penance  grove are beginning to sleep around the sacred altars.

shloka_text: सम्प्रवृत्तानिशा सीते नक्षत्रसमलङ्कृता। ज्योत्स्नाप्रावरणश्चन्द्रो दृश्यतेऽभ्युदितोऽम्बरे।।2.119.9।।
transliteration: sampravṛttāniśā sīte nakṣatrasamalaṅkṛtā| jyotsnāprāvaraṇaścandro dṛśyate'bhyudito'mbare
translation: सीते O Sita, नक्षत्रसमलङ्कृता adorned with stars, निशा night, सम्प्रवृत्ता has commenced, ज्योत्स्नाप्रावरणः spread with the mantle of moonlight, चन्द्रः moon, अम्बरे in the sky, अभ्युदितः is rising, दृश्यते is appearing.
explanation: O Sita, adorned with stars, the night has commenced. You can see the moon rising in the sky spreading his mantle of light.

shloka_text: गम्यतामनुजानामि रामस्यानुचरी भव। कथायन्त्या हि मधुरं त्वयाऽहं परितोषिता।।2.119.10।।
transliteration: gamyatāmanujānāmi rāmasyānucarī bhava| kathāyantyā hi madhuraṃ tvayā'haṃ paritoṣitā
translation: गम्यताम् you may go now, अनुजानामि I give you my consent, रामस्य to Rama, अनुचरी भव be his companion, मधुरम् sweetly, कथयन्त्या storytelling, त्वया by you, अहम् I, परितोषिता  thoroughly contented.
explanation: With my permission you may go now and be a companion of Rama. I am thoroughly contented  with your story told so sweetly.

shloka_text: अलङ्कुरु च तावत्त्वं प्रत्यक्षं मम मैथिलि। प्रीतिं जनय मे वत्से दिव्यालङ्कारशोभिता।।2.119.11।।
transliteration: alaṅkuru ca tāvattvaṃ pratyakṣaṃ mama maithili| prītiṃ janaya me vatse divyālaṅkāraśobhitā
translation: मैथिलि O Sita, त्वम् you, मम my, प्रत्यक्षं तावत् in my presence, अलङ्कुरु adorn yourself, वत्से dear child, दिव्यालङ्कारशोभिता adorned with divine ornaments, मे to me, प्रीतिम् delight, जनय cause me.
explanation: O Sita, adorn yourself in my presence. Dear child, permit me the pleasure of  adorning  you with these divine ornaments.

shloka_text: सा तथा समलङ्कृत्य सीता सुरसुतोपमा। प्रणम्य शिरसा तस्यै रामं त्वभिमुखी ययौ।।2.119.12।।
transliteration: sā tathā samalaṅkṛtya sītā surasutopamā| praṇamya śirasā tasyai rāmaṃ tvabhimukhī yayau
translation: सुरसुतोपमा resembling the daughter of a god, सा सीता that Sita, तथा in that way, समलङ्कुत्य having adorned, तस्यै to her, शिरसा with her head, प्रणम्य saluting with reverence, रामम् to Rama, अभिमुखी towards, ययौ went.
explanation: Sita, adorned, looked like the daughter of a god. She bowed at the feet of Anasuya in reverence and set out to meet Rama.

shloka_text: तथा तु भूषितां सीतां ददर्श वदतां वरः। राघवः प्रीतिदानेन तपस्विन्या जहर्ष च।।2.119.13।।
transliteration: tathā tu bhūṣitāṃ sītāṃ dadarśa vadatāṃ varaḥ| rāghavaḥ prītidānena tapasvinyā jaharṣa ca
translation: वदताम् among those eloquent one, वरः excellent, राघवः Rama, तथा in that way, भूषिताम्  adorned, सीताम् Sita, ददर्श beheld, तपस्विन्याः of the female ascetic, प्रीतिदानेन with gifts of love, जहर्ष च rejoiced.
explanation: Rama, the most eloquent among men, saw Sita adorned, and rejoiced at the gifts of love given by the ascetic Anasuya.

shloka_text: न्यवेदयत्ततस्सर्वं सीता रामाय मैथिली। प्रीतिदानं तपस्विन्या वसनाभरणस्रजम्।।2.119.14।।
transliteration: nyavedayattatassarvaṃ sītā rāmāya maithilī| prītidānaṃ tapasvinyā vasanābharaṇasrajam
translation: मैथिली the princess of Mithila, सीता Sita, ततः there after, तपस्विन्याः of ascetic Anasuya, प्रीतिदानम् gifts of love, वसनाभरणस्रजम् raiment, jewellery and garlands, सर्वम् everything, रामाय to Rama, न्यवेदयत् related.
explanation: Sita the princess of Mithila related everything to Rama and showed him the gifts of love given by ascetic Anasuya -- raiment, jewellery and garlands.

shloka_text: प्रहृष्टस्त्वभवद्रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महारथः। मैथिल्यास्सत्क्रियां दृष्ट्वा मानुषेषु सुदुर्लभाम्।।2.119.15।।
transliteration: prahṛṣṭastvabhavadrāmo lakṣmaṇaśca mahārathaḥ| maithilyāssatkriyāṃ dṛṣṭvā mānuṣeṣu sudurlabhām
translation: रामः Rama, महारथः great charioteer, लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana also, मानुषेषु among mortals, सुदुर्लभाम् very difficult to obtain, मैथिल्याः to Sita, सत्क्रियाम् the honour, दृष्ट्वा having seen, प्रहृष्टः अभवत् was gratified.
explanation: Rama the great charioteer and Lakshmana were exceedingly gratified to see the honour conferred on Sita, rare among mortals.

shloka_text: ततस्तां शर्वरीं प्रीतः पुण्यां शशिनिभाननः। अर्चितस्तापसै स्सिद्धैरुवास रघुनन्दनः।।2.119.16।।
transliteration: tatastāṃ śarvarīṃ prītaḥ puṇyāṃ śaśinibhānanaḥ| arcitastāpasai ssiddhairuvāsa raghunandanaḥ
translation: ततः thereafter, शशिनिभाननः face like the Moon, रघुनन्दनः the descendant of Raghu, सिद्धैः by the acomplished, तापसैः by ascetics, अर्चितः hospitality having been extended, प्रीतः in delight, पुण्याम् holy, तां शर्वरीम् that night, उवास passed.
explanation: Thereafter, the descendant of Raghu, whose countenance resembled the Moon, having received the hospitality of the accomplished ascetics, passed that holy night in delight.

shloka_text: तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामभिषिच्य हुताग्निकान्। आपृच्छेतां नरव्याघ्रौ तापसान्वनगोचरान्।।2.119.17।।
transliteration: tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyāmabhiṣicya hutāgnikān| āpṛcchetāṃ naravyāghrau tāpasānvanagocarān
translation: तस्याम् that, रात्र्याम् night, व्यतीतायाम् had passed away, नरव्याघ्रौ the two great men, अभिषिच्य having bathed, हुताग्निकान् who performed their fireofferings, वनगोचरान् inhabiting the  forest, तापसान् ascetics, अपृच्छेताम् took leave of.
explanation: Night over, the two best men, Rama and Lakshmana, after their ablution took leave of the ascetics inhabiting the forest who offered morning oblations to the fire .

shloka_text: तावूचुस्ते वनचरास्तापसा धर्मचारिणः। वनस्य तस्य सञ्चारं राक्षसैस्समभिप्लुतम्।।2.119.18।।
transliteration: tāvūcuste vanacarāstāpasā dharmacāriṇaḥ| vanasya tasya sañcāraṃ rākṣasaissamabhiplutam
translation: वनचराः dwellers in the forest, धर्मचारिणः following the righteousness, ते तापसाः those ascetics, तस्य वनस्य of that forest, सञ्चारम् movement, राक्षसैः with demons, समभिप्लुतम्   inundated, तौ addressing both of them, ऊचुः said.
explanation: The righteous ascetics dwelling in the forest informed both Rama and Lakshmana  that  part of the forest infested by demons.

shloka_text: रक्षांसि पुरुषादानि नानारूपाणि राघव। वसन्त्यस्मिन्महारण्ये व्यालाश्च रुधिराशनाः।।2.119.19।।
transliteration: rakṣāṃsi puruṣādāni nānārūpāṇi rāghava| vasantyasminmahāraṇye vyālāśca rudhirāśanāḥ
translation: राघव O Rama, अस्मिन् महारण्ये in this great forest, पुरुषादानि maneaters, नानारूपाणि in various forms, रक्षांसि demons, रुधिराशनाः blooddrinking, व्यालाश्च wild animals, वसन्ति are living.
explanation: O Rama, this great forest is haunted by carnivorous demons who can assume any form and by blooddrinking wild animals.

shloka_text: उच्छिष्टं वा प्रमत्तं वा तापसं धर्मचारिणम्। अदन्त्यस्मिन्महारण्ये तान्निवारय राघव।।2.119.20।।
transliteration: ucchiṣṭaṃ vā pramattaṃ vā tāpasaṃ dharmacāriṇam| adantyasminmahāraṇye tānnivāraya rāghava
translation: राघव Rama, अस्मिन् महारण्ये in this great forest, उच्छिष्टं वा or impure, प्रमत्तं वा or not alert, तापसम् an ascetic, अदन्ति they (eat) devour, तान् them, निवारय prevent them.
explanation: O Rama, in this great forest demons will devour the  ascetics if they find them impure or intoxicated or indolent. Prevent them.

shloka_text: एष पन्था महर्षीणां फलान्याहरतां वने। अनेन तु वनं दुर्गं गन्तुं राघव ते क्षमम्।।2.119.21।।
transliteration: eṣa panthā maharṣīṇāṃ phalānyāharatāṃ vane| anena tu vanaṃ durgaṃ gantuṃ rāghava te kṣamam
translation: राघव Rama, एषः वने in the forest, फलानि fruits, आहरताम् of those gathering, महर्षीणाम् ascetics, एष पन्थाः this path, अनेन through this path, दुर्गम् impassable, वनम् the forest, गन्तुम् to go, ते to you, क्षमम् is safe.
explanation: O Rama, this is the one path in the forest used by the ascetics to gather fruits. You can safely cross the otherwise impassable forest through this path.

shloka_text: इतीव तैः प्राञ्जलिभिस्तपस्विभिर्द्विजैः कृतस्वस्त्ययनः परन्तपः। वनं सभार्यः प्रविवेश राघवस्सलक्ष्मणस्सूर्य इवाभ्रमण्डलम्।।2.119.22।।
transliteration: itīva taiḥ prāñjalibhistapasvibhirdvijaiḥ kṛtasvastyayanaḥ parantapaḥ| vanaṃ sabhāryaḥ praviveśa rāghavassalakṣmaṇassūrya ivābhramaṇḍalam
translation: प्राञ्जलिभिः (paying obeisance) with folded hands, तपस्विभिः by ascetics, तैः द्विजैः by those brahmins, इतीव thus, कृतस्वस्त्ययनः obtaining their blessings, परन्तपः tormentor of enemies, राघवः Rama, सभार्यः with his wife, सलक्ष्मणः with Lakshmana, सूर्यः Sun, अभ्रमण्डलम् इव like entering the mass of clouds, वनम् forest, प्रविवेश entered.
explanation: The ascetics offered their blessings to Rama the tormentor of enemies. Thereafter, accompanied by his wife and Lakshmana, he entered the great forest like the Sun entering the mass of clouds. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे श्रीमद्वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये चतुर्विंशत्सहस्रिकायां संहितयां श्रीमदयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनविंशत्युत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundrednineteenth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: प्रविश्य तु महारण्यं दण्डकारण्यमात्मवान्। ददर्श रामो दुर्धर्षस्तापसाश्रममण्डलम्।।3.1.1।।
transliteration: praviśya tu mahāraṇyaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyamātmavān| dadarśa rāmo durdharṣastāpasāśramamaṇḍalam
translation: आत्मवान् selfpossessed, दुर्धर्षः invincible रामः Rama, महारण्यम् great forest, दण्डकारण्यम् Dandaka forest, प्रविश्य having entered, तापसाश्रममण्डलम् multitude of hermitages of the ascetics, ददर्श saw.
explanation: The invincible and selfpossessed Rama entered the great forest of Dandaka and saw there a multitude of hermitages of the ascetics.
comments: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana enter the Dandaka forest -- Sages at Dandaka offer prayers and welcome Sri Rama.

shloka_text: कुशचीरपरिक्षिप्तं ब्राह्म्या लक्ष्म्या समावृतम्। यथा प्रदीप्तं दुर्दर्शं गगने सूर्यमण्डलम्।।3.1.2।।
transliteration: kuśacīraparikṣiptaṃ brāhmyā lakṣmyā samāvṛtam| yathā pradīptaṃ durdarśaṃ gagane sūryamaṇḍalam
translation: कुशचीरपरिक्षिप्तम्  ceremonial robes(made) of kusa grass spread all over ब्राह्म्या of the brahmanas, लक्ष्म्या of auspicious appearance, समावृतम् surrounded, गगने in the sky, प्रदीप्तम् glowing, सूर्यमण्डलं यथा like the orb of the Sun, दुर्दर्शम् difficult to gaze.
explanation: They (the hermitages) were strewn all over with kusa grass and robes by bark with auspicious sacrificial materials around and hence dazzling like the orb of the sun in the sky difficult to gaze.

shloka_text: शरण्यं सर्वभूतानां सुसम्मृष्टाजिरं सदा। मृगैर्बहुभिराकीर्णं पक्षिसङ्घैस्समावृतम्।।3.1.3।।
transliteration: śaraṇyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ susammṛṣṭājiraṃ sadā| mṛgairbahubhirākīrṇaṃ pakṣisaṅghaissamāvṛtam
translation: सर्वभूतानाम् for all beings, शरण्यम्  shelter, सदा always, सुसम्मृष्टाजिरं the courtyard being wellcleaned, wetted and decorated, बहुभिः by many, मृगैः by antelopes, आकीर्णम् filled all over, पक्षिसङ्घै by flocks of birds, समावृतम् filled with.
explanation: The courtyards (of the hermitages) were cleanswept, sprinkled with water and decorated. They provided shelter to all kinds of creatures and were filled all over with  flocks of birds and antelopes.

shloka_text: पूजितं च प्रनृत्तं च नित्यमप्सरसां गणैः। विशालैरग्निशरणैः स्रुग्भाण्डैरजिनैः कुशैः।।3.1.4।। समिद्भिस्तोयकलशैः फलमूलैश्च शोभितम्। आरण्यैश्च महावृक्षैः पुण्यैस्स्वादुफलैर्वृतम्।।3.1.5।।
transliteration: pūjitaṃ ca pranṛttaṃ ca nityamapsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ| viśālairagniśaraṇaiḥ srugbhāṇḍairajinaiḥ kuśaiḥ samidbhistoyakalaśaiḥ phalamūlaiśca śobhitam| āraṇyaiśca mahāvṛkṣaiḥ puṇyaissvāduphalairvṛtam
translation: अप्सरसाम्  by celestial damsels, गणैः by groups, पूजितं च glorified, प्रनृत्तं च and offered dances as service, विशालैः with vast, अग्निशरणैः with fire sanctuaries स्रुग्भाण्डैः with wooden ladles for offering ghee अजिनैः with deerskins, कुशैः with kusa grass, समिद्भि: with faggots (specially offered to fire in sacrificial ceremonies), तोयकलशैः pots filled with water, फलमूलैश्च with fruits and roots, शोभितम् adorned, आरण्यैः produced in forests, पुण्यैः sacred ones, स्वादुफलैः by sweet fruits, महावृक्षैः with huge trees, उपशोभितम् looking delightful all over.
explanation: The hermitages looked glorified with dances by celestial damsels. They were  adorned with vast fire sanctuaries, ladles for sacrificial ceremonies, deerskins and kusa grass faggots for pots of water, roots and fruits. They looked delightful with huge sacred trees of the forest laden with sweet fruits.

shloka_text: पूजितं च प्रनृत्तं च नित्यमप्सरसां गणैः। विशालैरग्निशरणैः स्रुग्भाण्डैरजिनैः कुशैः।।3.1.4।। समिद्भिस्तोयकलशैः फलमूलैश्च शोभितम्। आरण्यैश्च महावृक्षैः पुण्यैस्स्वादुफलैर्वृतम्।।3.1.5।।
transliteration: pūjitaṃ ca pranṛttaṃ ca nityamapsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ| viśālairagniśaraṇaiḥ srugbhāṇḍairajinaiḥ kuśaiḥ samidbhistoyakalaśaiḥ phalamūlaiśca śobhitam| āraṇyaiśca mahāvṛkṣaiḥ puṇyaissvāduphalairvṛtam
translation: अप्सरसाम्  by celestial damsels, गणैः by groups, पूजितं च glorified, प्रनृत्तं च and offered dances as service, विशालैः with vast, अग्निशरणैः with fire sanctuaries स्रुग्भाण्डैः with wooden ladles for offering ghee अजिनैः with deerskins, कुशैः with kusa grass, समिद्भि: with faggots (specially offered to fire in sacrificial ceremonies), तोयकलशैः pots filled with water, फलमूलैश्च with fruits and roots, शोभितम् adorned, आरण्यैः produced in forests, पुण्यैः sacred ones, स्वादुफलैः by sweet fruits, महावृक्षैः with huge trees, उपशोभितम् looking delightful all over.
explanation: The hermitages looked glorified with dances by celestial damsels. They were  adorned with vast fire sanctuaries, ladles for sacrificial ceremonies, deerskins and kusa grass faggots for pots of water, roots and fruits. They looked delightful with huge sacred trees of the forest laden with sweet fruits.

shloka_text: बलिहोमार्चितं पुण्यं ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम्। पुष्पैश्चान्यैः परिक्षिप्तं पद्मिन्या च सपद्मया।।3.1.6।। फलमूलाशनैर्दान्तैश्चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरैः। सूर्यवैश्वानराभैश्च पुराणैर्मुनिभिर्वुतम्।।3.1.7।।
transliteration: balihomārcitaṃ puṇyaṃ brahmaghoṣanināditam| puṣpaiścānyaiḥ parikṣiptaṃ padminyā ca sapadmayā phalamūlāśanairdāntaiścīrakṛṣṇājināmbaraiḥ| sūryavaiśvānarābhaiśca purāṇairmunibhirvutam
translation: बलिहोमार्चितम् worshipped with various offerings and sacrifices, पुण्यम् sacred, ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम् reverberating with chanting of the Vedas,अन्यैः पुष्पैः by other flowers, परिक्षिप्तम् scattered here and there, पद्मिन्या by a lotuspond, सपद्मया filled with lotuses, फलमूलाशनैः by those living on fruits and roots, दान्तै: selfrestrained ones, चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरैः wearing bark garments and skins of black antelopes, सूर्यवैश्वानराभैश्च glowing like the Sun or the fire, पुराणैः by the aged, मुनिभिः by the sages, वृतम् surrounded by.
explanation: The hermitages where various sacrificial offerings were made reverberated with Vedic chantings. Flowers were scattered all over. There was a lotuspond with lotuses. There were aged, selfrestrained sages glowing like the Sun or the fire, living on fruits and roots, clothed in bark and dark  deerskin.

shloka_text: बलिहोमार्चितं पुण्यं ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम्। पुष्पैश्चान्यैः परिक्षिप्तं पद्मिन्या च सपद्मया।।3.1.6।। फलमूलाशनैर्दान्तैश्चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरैः। सूर्यवैश्वानराभैश्च पुराणैर्मुनिभिर्वुतम्।।3.1.7।।
transliteration: balihomārcitaṃ puṇyaṃ brahmaghoṣanināditam| puṣpaiścānyaiḥ parikṣiptaṃ padminyā ca sapadmayā phalamūlāśanairdāntaiścīrakṛṣṇājināmbaraiḥ| sūryavaiśvānarābhaiśca purāṇairmunibhirvutam
translation: बलिहोमार्चितम् worshipped with various offerings and sacrifices, पुण्यम् sacred, ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम् reverberating with chanting of the Vedas,अन्यैः पुष्पैः by other flowers, परिक्षिप्तम् scattered here and there, पद्मिन्या by a lotuspond, सपद्मया filled with lotuses, फलमूलाशनैः by those living on fruits and roots, दान्तै: selfrestrained ones, चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरैः wearing bark garments and skins of black antelopes, सूर्यवैश्वानराभैश्च glowing like the Sun or the fire, पुराणैः by the aged, मुनिभिः by the sages, वृतम् surrounded by.
explanation: The hermitages where various sacrificial offerings were made reverberated with Vedic chantings. Flowers were scattered all over. There was a lotuspond with lotuses. There were aged, selfrestrained sages glowing like the Sun or the fire, living on fruits and roots, clothed in bark and dark  deerskin.

shloka_text: पुण्यैश्च नियताहारैः शोभितं परमर्षिभिः। तद्ब्रह्मभवनप्रख्यं ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम्।।3.1.8।।
transliteration: puṇyaiśca niyatāhāraiḥ śobhitaṃ paramarṣibhiḥ| tadbrahmabhavanaprakhyaṃ brahmaghoṣanināditam
translation: पुण्यैः by holy people, नियताहारैः  with regulated diet, परमर्षिभिः by great sages, शोभितम् shining, ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम् echoing with the chanting of the Vedas, ब्रह्मभवनप्रख्यम्  resembling the abode of Brahma, तत् that (hermitage).
explanation: The hermitages echoing with  the sounds of Vedic recitations and resembling the very abode of Brahma were adorned with great, holy sages living on regulated diet.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मविद्भिर्महाभागैर्ब्राह्मणैरुपशोभितम्। तद्दृष्ट्वा राघवः श्रीमांस्तापसाश्रममण्डलम्।।3.1.9।। अभ्यगच्छन्महातेजा विज्यं कृत्वा महद्धनुः।
transliteration: brahmavidbhirmahābhāgairbrāhmaṇairupaśobhitam| taddṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ śrīmāṃstāpasāśramamaṇḍalam abhyagacchanmahātejā vijyaṃ kṛtvā mahaddhanuḥ|
translation: ब्रह्मविद्भि: by those knowing the Supreme Spirit, महाभागैः by the venerable ones, बाह्मणैः by brahmins, उपशोभितम् was adorned, तत् that, तापसाश्रममण्डलम् groups of hermitages of the sages, दृष्ट्वा after seeing, श्रीमान्  illustrious, महातेजाः a man of great lustre, राघवः Rama, महत् great, धनुः bow, विज्यम् with loosened string, कृत्वा doing, अभ्यगच्छत् went forward.
explanation: The illustrious, effulgent Rama saw groups of hermitages adorned with venerable brahmins, with knowledge of the Supreme Spirit. On seeing them he loosened the string of his great bow and went forward.

shloka_text: दिव्यज्ञानोपपन्नास्ते रामं दृष्ट्वा महर्षयः।।3.1.10।। अभ्यगच्छन्स्तदा प्रीता वैदेहीं च यशस्विनीम्।
transliteration: divyajñānopapannāste rāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā maharṣayaḥ abhyagacchanstadā prītā vaidehīṃ ca yaśasvinīm|
translation: दिव्यज्ञानोपपन्नाः richly endowed with divine knowledge, ते महर्षयः those great sages, रामं Rama, यशस्विनीम् highly reputed, वैदेहीं च Sita too, दृष्ट्वा on seeing, प्रीताः pleased, तदा then, अभ्यगच्छन् went towards.
explanation: On seeing Rama with illustrious Sita, the great sages, richly endowed with divine knowledge, went forward to greet him.

shloka_text: ते तं सोममिवोद्यन्तं दृष्ट्वा वै धर्मचारिणम्।।3.1.11।। लक्ष्मणं चैव दृष्ट्वा तु वैदेहीं च यशस्विनीम्। मङ्गलानि प्रयुञ्जानाः प्रत्यगृह्णन्दृढव्रताः।।3.1.12।।
transliteration: te taṃ somamivodyantaṃ dṛṣṭvā vai dharmacāriṇam lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva dṛṣṭvā tu vaidehīṃ ca yaśasvinīm| maṅgalāni prayuñjānāḥ pratyagṛhṇandṛḍhavratāḥ
translation: दृढव्रताः steadfast in vows, ते they, उद्यन्तम् rising, सोममिव like the Moon, धर्मचारिणम् follower of  righteous path, दृष्ट्वा तु on seeing, लक्ष्मणं चैव Lakshmana too, यशस्विनीम् famed, वैदेहीं च Sita also, दृष्ट्वा तु seeing, मङ्गलानि words of benediction, प्रयुञ्जानाः uttering, प्रत्यगृह्णन् went towards and received them.
explanation: The sages, steadfast in their vows, saw Rama who was shining like the rising Moon, Lakshmana and the famed Sita went forward and received them with words of benediction.

shloka_text: ते तं सोममिवोद्यन्तं दृष्ट्वा वै धर्मचारिणम्।।3.1.11।। लक्ष्मणं चैव दृष्ट्वा तु वैदेहीं च यशस्विनीम्। मङ्गलानि प्रयुञ्जानाः प्रत्यगृह्णन्दृढव्रताः।।3.1.12।।
transliteration: te taṃ somamivodyantaṃ dṛṣṭvā vai dharmacāriṇam lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva dṛṣṭvā tu vaidehīṃ ca yaśasvinīm| maṅgalāni prayuñjānāḥ pratyagṛhṇandṛḍhavratāḥ
translation: दृढव्रताः steadfast in vows, ते they, उद्यन्तम् rising, सोममिव like the Moon, धर्मचारिणम् follower of  righteous path, दृष्ट्वा तु on seeing, लक्ष्मणं चैव Lakshmana too, यशस्विनीम् famed, वैदेहीं च Sita also, दृष्ट्वा तु seeing, मङ्गलानि words of benediction, प्रयुञ्जानाः uttering, प्रत्यगृह्णन् went towards and received them.
explanation: The sages, steadfast in their vows, saw Rama who was shining like the rising Moon, Lakshmana and the famed Sita went forward and received them with words of benediction.

shloka_text: रूपसंहननं लक्ष्मीं सौकुमार्यं सुवेषताम्। ददृशुर्विस्मिताकारा रामस्य वनवासिनः।।3.1.13।।
transliteration: rūpasaṃhananaṃ lakṣmīṃ saukumāryaṃ suveṣatām| dadṛśurvismitākārā rāmasya vanavāsinaḥ
translation: वनवासिनः (sages) living in the woods, रामस्य Rama's, रूपसंहननम् beauty of the body, लक्ष्मीम् splendour, सौकुमार्यम् tenderness, सुवेषताम् will attired, विस्मिताकाराः wonderstruck sages, ददृशुः saw.
explanation: Those sages living  in the forest were wonderstruck to see the handsome, graceful, delicate and welldressed Rama.

shloka_text: वैदेहीं लक्ष्मणं रामं नेत्रैरनिमिषैरिव। आश्चर्यभूतान्ददृशुः सर्वे ते वनचारिणः।।3.1.14।।
transliteration: vaidehīṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmaṃ netrairanimiṣairiva| āścaryabhūtāndadṛśuḥ sarve te vanacāriṇaḥ
translation: सर्वे all, ते वनचारिण: those forestrangers, आश्चर्यभूतान् creating wonder, वैदेहीम् Sita, लक्ष्मणं Lakshmana, चैव too, रामं Rama, अनिमिषैरिव unblinking, नेत्रै: with eyes, ददृशुः saw.
explanation: All the foresters looked at the wonderful figures of Rama, Sita and Lakshmana with unblinking eyes.

shloka_text: अत्रैनं हि महाभागा स्सर्वभूतहिते रताः। अतिथिं पर्णशालायां राघवं संन्यवेशयन्।।3.1.15।।
transliteration: atrainaṃ hi mahābhāgā ssarvabhūtahite ratāḥ| atithiṃ parṇaśālāyāṃ rāghavaṃ saṃnyaveśayan
translation: सर्वभूतहिते in the welfare of all beings, रताः engaged, महाभागाः glorious, अत्र here, पर्णशालायाम् in a leafy hut, अतिथिम् guest, एनम् राघवम् this Rama, संन्यवेशयन् made him sit and rest.
explanation: Ever engaged in the welfare of all beings, the sages made Rama, their guest, sit in their leafy hut.

shloka_text: ततो रामस्य सत्कृत्य विधिना पावकोपमाः। आजह्रुस्ते महाभागाः सलिलं धर्मचारिणः।।3.1.16।।
transliteration: tato rāmasya satkṛtya vidhinā pāvakopamāḥ| ājahruste mahābhāgāḥ salilaṃ dharmacāriṇaḥ
translation: ततः thereafter, पावकोपमाः comparable to fire, महाभागाः great ones, ते they, धर्मचारिणः followers of righteousness, विधिना as per tradition, सत्कृत्य after rendering due hospitality, रामस्य to Rama, सलिलम् water, आजह्रुः offered.
explanation: The great sages comparable to the firegod and followers of righteousness honoured Rama  according to tradition by offering water.

shloka_text: पुष्पं मूलं फलं सर्वमाश्रमं च महात्मनः। निवेदयित्वा धर्मज्ञास्ते ततः प्राञ्जलयोऽब्रुवन्।।3.1.17।।
transliteration: puṣpaṃ mūlaṃ phalaṃ sarvamāśramaṃ ca mahātmanaḥ| nivedayitvā dharmajñāste tataḥ prāñjalayo'bruvan
translation: धर्मज्ञाः knowers of dharma, ते they, तत: then, पुष्पम् flower, फलम् fruit, मूलं root, सर्वम् all, आश्रमं च and the hermitage, महात्मनः to the great self, निवेदयित्वा having offered, प्राञ्जलयः with folded palms, अब्रुवन् said.
explanation: The sages who were knowers of dharma saluted the noble Rama, offered fruits, roots and flowers available  at the hermitage and with folded palms said thus:

shloka_text: धर्मपालो जनस्यास्य शरण्यस्त्वं महायशाः। पूजनीयश्च मान्यश्च राजा दण्डधरो गुरुः।।3.1.18।।
transliteration: dharmapālo janasyāsya śaraṇyastvaṃ mahāyaśāḥ| pūjanīyaśca mānyaśca rājā daṇḍadharo guruḥ
translation: राजा king, महायशा: of great fame, जनस्यास्य of the people, धर्मपालः protector of dharma, शरण्यश्च  refuge, पूजनीयश्च worthy of worship, मान्यश्च respectable, दण्डधरः chastiser of evildoers, गुरुः a respectable one.
explanation: O king of great reputation, you are the refuge of the people, a protector of dharma, a chastiser of wrongdoers, a worshipful and respectable preceptor.

shloka_text: इन्द्रस्येह चतुर्भागः प्रजा रक्षति राघव। राजा तस्माद्वरान्भोगान्रम्यान् भुङक्तेलोकनमस्कृतः।।3.1.19।।
transliteration: indrasyeha caturbhāgaḥ prajā rakṣati rāghava| rājā tasmādvarānbhogānramyān bhuṅaktelokanamaskṛtaḥ
translation: राघव O Rama, इन्द्रस्य Indra's, इह here, चतुर्भागः fourth part, प्रजाः people, रक्षति protects, तस्मात् therefore, राजा king, नमस्कृतः obeyed, वरान् best, भोगान् pleasures, भुङक्ते enjoys.
explanation: O Rama, in this world a king is considered the fourth part of Indra as he protects the people. Therefore, he is respected and he enjoys the choicest pleasures of life.

shloka_text: ते वयं भवता रक्ष्या भवद्विषयवासिनः। नगरस्थो वनस्थो वा त्वं नो राजा जनेश्वरः।।3.1.20।।
transliteration: te vayaṃ bhavatā rakṣyā bhavadviṣayavāsinaḥ| nagarastho vanastho vā tvaṃ no rājā janeśvaraḥ
translation: भवद्विषयवासि residents of your domain, ते to you, वयम् we, भवता by you, रक्ष्याः deserve to be protected, नगरस्थः residing in a city, वनस्थः वा or staying in the forest, जनेश्वर: Lord of the people, त्वम् you, राजा king.
explanation: Since we are the residents of your territory we deserve to be protected by you. Whether you live in the city or in the forest, you are the lord of the people and our king.

shloka_text: न्यस्तदण्डा वयं राजञ्जितक्रोधा जितेन्द्रियाः। रक्षणीयास्त्वया शश्वदगर्भभूतास्तपोधनाः।।3.1.21।।
transliteration: nyastadaṇḍā vayaṃ rājañjitakrodhā jitendriyāḥ| rakṣaṇīyāstvayā śaśvadagarbhabhūtāstapodhanāḥ
translation: राजन् O king, जितक्रोधाः men who have conquered anger, जितेन्द्रियाः selfcontrolled, तपोधनाः  asceties, वयम् we, न्यस्तदण्डाः cast aside the symbol of authority, गर्भभूताः like your children, त्वया by you, शश्वत् forever, रक्षणीयाः to be protected.
explanation: O king, we have conquered our anger and have controlled our senses. We ascetics have cast aside all our authority. We are like your children and need to be protected by you forever

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा फलैर्मूलैः पुष्पैर्वन्यैश्च राघवम्। अन्यैश्च विविधाहारैः सलक्ष्मणमपूजयन्।।3.1.22।।
transliteration: evamuktvā phalairmūlaiḥ puṣpairvanyaiśca rāghavam| anyaiśca vividhāhāraiḥ salakṣmaṇamapūjayan
translation: एवम् in that manner, उक्त्वा having said, सलक्ष्मणम् along with Lakshmana, राघवम् Rama, फलैः with fruits, मूलैः with roots, पुष्पैः with flowers, अन्यैश्च and by other, वन्यैः by forest produce, विविधाहारैः different kinds of food, अपूजयन् offered with reverence.
explanation: Having said so, the ascetics offered with reverence fruits, roots, flowers and other forest  products to Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: कृतातिथ्योऽथ रामस्तु सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति। आम्नत्ऱ्य स मुनीन्सर्वान्वनमेवान्वगाहत।।3.2.1।।
transliteration: kṛtātithyo'tha rāmastu sūryasyodayanaṃ prati| āmnatṟya sa munīnsarvānvanamevānvagāhata
translation: अथ then, कृतातिथ्यः on receiving hospitality, सः रामस्तु that Rama also, सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति at the time of sunrise, सर्वान् all, मुनीन् sages, आम्नत्ऱ्य  took leave, वनमेव into the forest, अन्वगाहत entered deep.
explanation: After receiving hospitality from the sages, Rama took of all of them at sunrise and entered deep into the forest.
comments: Viradha attacks Rama and Lakshmana -- carries away Sita.

shloka_text: नानामृगगणाकीर्णमृक्षशार्दूल सेवितम्। ध्वस्तवृक्षलतागुल्मं दुर्दर्शसलिलाशयम्।।3.2.2।। निष्कूजनानाशकुनिझिल्लिकागणनादितम्। लक्ष्मणानुगतो रामो वनमध्यं ददर्श ह।।3.2.3।।
transliteration: nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇamṛkṣaśārdūla sevitam| dhvastavṛkṣalatāgulmaṃ durdarśasalilāśayam niṣkūjanānāśakunijhillikāgaṇanāditam| lakṣmaṇānugato rāmo vanamadhyaṃ dadarśa ha
translation: लक्ष्मणानुगतः followed by Lakshmana, रामः Rama, नानामृगगणाकीर्णम् filled with different kinds of animals, ऋक्षशार्दूलसेवितम् inhabited by bears and tigers, ध्वस्तवृक्षलतागुल्मम् a place where trees, creepers and bushes were crushed (due to frequent visit by demons), दुर्दश difficult to see, सलिलाशयम् waterreservoirs like wells, निष्कूजनानाशकुनि with the twitter of various birds, झिल्लिकागणनादितम् resounding with the chirping of crickets. वनमध्यम् midst of the forest, ददर्श ह witnessed.
explanation: With Lakshmana following, Rama went through the forest, filled with herds of animals and inhabited by bears and tigers.
