Lakshmana who had never seen Rama in such anger before said to him with folded hands and parched throat.
comments: Lakshmana pacifies Rama -- explains that destruction of the world is not proper -- initiates the search.

shloka_text: पुरा भूत्वा मृदुर्दान्तस्सर्वभूतहिते रतः। न क्रोधवशमापन्नः प्रकृतिं हातुमर्हसि।।3.65.4।।
transliteration: purā bhūtvā mṛdurdāntassarvabhūtahite rataḥ| na krodhavaśamāpannaḥ prakṛtiṃ hātumarhasi
translation: पुरा in the past, मृदुः gentle, दान्तः selfrestrained, सर्वभूतहिते in the welfare of all beings, रतः as engaged, भूत्वा after being, क्रोधवशम् under the spell of anger, आपन्नः attaining, प्रकृतिम् natural form, हातुम् to give up, नार्हसि do not behove.
explanation: Earlier you were gentle, self restrained and engaged in the welfare of all beings. (Now) it is not proper for you to give up your natural composure in anger.

shloka_text: चन्द्रे लक्ष्मीः प्रभा सूर्ये गतिर्वायौ भुवि क्षमा। एतत्तु नियतं सर्वं त्वयि चानुत्तमं यशः।।3.65.5।।
transliteration: candre lakṣmīḥ prabhā sūrye gatirvāyau bhuvi kṣamā| etattu niyataṃ sarvaṃ tvayi cānuttamaṃ yaśaḥ
translation: चन्द्रे of the Moon, लक्ष्मीः grace, सूर्ये of the Sun, प्रभा radiance, वायौ of the wind, गतिः motion, भुवि on earth, क्षमा forbearance, एतत् सर्वम् all this, नियतम् always, त्वयि in you, अनुत्तमम् the best, यशः च and fame.
explanation: In you are always present the grace of the Moon, the radiance of the Sun, the motion of the wind, the forbearance of the earth and reputation.

shloka_text: एकस्य नापराधेन लोकान् हन्तुं त्वमर्हसि। न तु जानामि कस्यायं भग्नस्साङ्ग्रामिको रथः।।3.65.6।। केन वा कस्य वा हेतोस्सायुधस्सपरिच्छदः।
transliteration: ekasya nāparādhena lokān hantuṃ tvamarhasi| na tu jānāmi kasyāyaṃ bhagnassāṅgrāmiko rathaḥ kena vā kasya vā hetossāyudhassaparicchadaḥ|
translation: एकस्य one's, अपराधेन by mistake, इह here, लोकान् worlds, हन्तुम् to destroy, नार्हसि it is not proper, सायुधः with weapons, सपरिच्छदः with all accesories, अयम् this, साङ्ग्रामिकः used in war, रथः chariot, कस्य whose, केन by whom, कस्य वा हेतोः for what reason, भग्नः broken, न जानामि I do not know.
explanation: To destroy the world for the mistake of a single person is not proper. Why and by whom is this warchariot broken with weapons and all its accesories I do not know.

shloka_text: खुरनेमिक्षतश्चायं सिक्तो रुधिरबिन्धुभिः।।3.65.7।। देशो निर्वृत्तसङ्ग्रामस्सुघोरः पार्थिवात्मज।
transliteration: khuranemikṣataścāyaṃ sikto rudhirabindhubhiḥ deśo nirvṛttasaṅgrāmassughoraḥ pārthivātmaja|
translation: पार्थिवात्मज O prince , खुरनेमिक्षतः damaged by hooves of horses and the rims of the chariot', रुधिरबिन्दुभिः by drops of blood, सिक्तः drenched, सुघोरः very dreadful, अयं देशः this place, निर्वृत्तसंग्रामः a great combat was fought here.
explanation: O prince, this place is damaged by the hooves of the horses and the rims of the chariot. It is soaked with drops of blood.Very dreadful must have been the fight here.

shloka_text: एकस्य तु विमर्धोऽयं न द्वयोर्वदतांवर।।3.65.8।। न हि वृत्तं हि पश्यामि बलस्य महतः पदम्।
transliteration: ekasya tu vimardho'yaṃ na dvayorvadatāṃvara na hi vṛttaṃ hi paśyāmi balasya mahataḥ padam|
translation: वदताम् of those intelligent in speech, वर the best one, अयम् this, एकस्य by one person, विमर्धः combat, द्वयोः of two people, न not, महतः great, बलस्य army, वृत्तम् this fight, पदम् footprints, न हि पश्यामि I do not see.
explanation: O, best of the eloquent  this fight involves only one and not two. I do not see the footprints of a big army.

shloka_text: नैकस्य तु कृते लोकान्विनाशयितुमर्हसि।।3.65.9।। युक्तदण्डा हि मृदवः प्रशान्ता वसुधाधिपाः।
transliteration: naikasya tu kṛte lokānvināśayitumarhasi yuktadaṇḍā hi mṛdavaḥ praśāntā vasudhādhipāḥ|
translation: एकस्य कृते for one's sake, लोकान् the worlds, विनाशयितुम् to destroy, नार्हसि not right, हि indeed, वसुधाधिपाः lords of the earth, युक्तदण्डाः punish the deserving, मृदवः gentle, प्रशान्ताः peaceful.
explanation: To destroy the entire world for one individual is not right. The lords of the earth should remain gentle, peaceful and punish only the deserving.

shloka_text: सदा त्वं सर्वभूतानां शरण्यः परमा गतिः।।3.65.10।। को नु दारप्रणाशं ते साधु मन्येत राघव।
transliteration: sadā tvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ śaraṇyaḥ paramā gatiḥ ko nu dārapraṇāśaṃ te sādhu manyeta rāghava|
translation: त्वम् you, सर्वभूतानाम् of all beings, सदा always, शरण्यः a refuge, परमा गतिः ultimate resort, राघव Raghava, ते to you, दारप्रणाशम् lost track of her whereabouts, को नु who will, साधु proper, मन्येत think.
explanation: You are the ultimate resort and refuge of all beings. Who would like that your wife should be abducted ?

shloka_text: सरितस्सागराश्शैला देवगन्धर्वदानवाः।।3.65.11।। नालं ते विप्रियं कर्तुं दीक्षितस्येव साधवः।
transliteration: saritassāgarāśśailā devagandharvadānavāḥ nālaṃ te vipriyaṃ kartuṃ dīkṣitasyeva sādhavaḥ|
translation: सरितः rivers, सागराः seas, शैलाः mountains, देवगन्धर्वदानवाः gods, gandharvas and demons, ते to you, साधवः pious people, दीक्षितस्येव those who observe religious vows, विप्रियम् disagreeable, कर्तुम् to do, नालम् they are not.
explanation: Just as pious men do not do anything disagreeable towards persons who observe religious vows, so also rivers, seas and mountains, gods, gandharvas and demons are not capable of causing unhappiness to you.

shloka_text: येन राजन्हृता सीता तमन्वेषितुमर्हसि।।3.65.12।। मद्वितीयो धनुष्पाणिस्सहायैः परमर्षिभिः।
transliteration: yena rājanhṛtā sītā tamanveṣitumarhasi madvitīyo dhanuṣpāṇissahāyaiḥ paramarṣibhiḥ|
translation: राजन् king, धनुष्पाणिः wielding a bow, मद्वितीयः followed by one, सहायैः with the help of, परमर्षिभिः by great sages, सीता Sita, येन whomsoever, हृता carried off, तम् him, अन्वेषितुम् to search, अर्हसि is proper for you.
explanation: O king bow in hands, followed by me and with the help of great sages you should search for the one who has abducted Sita.

shloka_text: समुद्रं च विचेष्यामः पर्वतांश्च वनानि च।।3.65.13।। गुहाश्च विविधा घोरा नदी पद्मवनानि च।
transliteration: samudraṃ ca viceṣyāmaḥ parvatāṃśca vanāni ca guhāśca vividhā ghorā nadī padmavanāni ca|
translation: समुद्रं च in the oceans, पर्वतांश्च in the mountains, वनानि च and the forests, विविधाः several, घोराः dreadful, गुहाश्च caves, नदीः rivers, पद्मवनानि lotus ponds, विचेष्यामः we will search.
explanation: We will search oceans, mountains, forests and several dreadful caves, rivers and lotusponds.

shloka_text: देवगन्धर्वलोकांश्च विचेष्यामस्समाहिताः।।3.65.14।। यावन्नाधिगमिष्यामस्तव भार्यापहारिणम्।
transliteration: devagandharvalokāṃśca viceṣyāmassamāhitāḥ yāvannādhigamiṣyāmastava bhāryāpahāriṇam|
translation: समाहिताः relentlessly, तव your, भार्यापहारिणम् the abductor of your wife, यावत् so long as, नाधिगमिष्यामःwe will not find, देवगन्धर्वलोकांश्च the world of the gods and gandharvas, विचेष्यामः we will search.
explanation: We will search relentlessly for the abductor of your wife everywhere including the world of gods and gandharvas till we find her.

shloka_text: न चेत्साम्ना प्रदास्यन्ति पत्नीं ते त्रिदशेश्वराः।।3.65.15।। कोसलेन्द्र ततः पश्चात्प्राप्तकालं करिष्यसि।
transliteration: na cetsāmnā pradāsyanti patnīṃ te tridaśeśvarāḥ kosalendra tataḥ paścātprāptakālaṃ kariṣyasi|
translation: कोसलेन्द्र lord of Kosala, Rama, त्रिदशेश्वराः gods, ते to you, पत्नीम् your wife, साम्ना with gentle request, न प्रदास्यन्ति not restore her, चेत् if so, ततः then, पश्चात् later, प्राप्तकालम् at the right time, करिष्यसि will take action.
explanation: O lord of Kosala when gods do not restore Sita on request, then you can think of taking action at the appropriate time.

shloka_text: शीलेन साम्ना विनयेन सीतां नयेन न प्राप्स्यसि चेन्नरेन्द्र। ततस्समुत्सादय हेमपुङ्खै र्महेन्द्रवज्रप्रतिमैश्शरौघैः।।3.65.16।।
transliteration: śīlena sāmnā vinayena sītāṃ nayena na prāpsyasi cennarendra| tatassamutsādaya hemapuṅkhai rmahendravajrapratimaiśśaraughaiḥ
translation: नरेन्द्र O king, शीलेन with right conduct, साम्ना by appeasing, विनयेन through humility, नयेन by diplomacy, सीताम् Sita, न प्राप्स्यसि यदि if you do not get her, ततः then, हेमपुङ्खैः with gold feathered, महेन्द्रवज्रप्रतिमैः equalling Indra's thunderbolt, शरौघैः by stream of arrows, समुत्सादय destroy.
explanation: O king if you fail to get Sita through appeasement, through humility or diplomacy then you destroy (the three worlds) by your goldtipped stream of arrows comparable to Indra's thunderbolt. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyfifth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तं तथा शोकसन्तप्तं विलपन्तमनाथवत्। मोहेन महताविष्टं परिद्यूनमचेतनम्।।3.66.1।। ततस्सौमित्रिराश्वास्य मुहूर्तादिव लक्ष्मणः। रामं सम्बोधयामास चरणौ चाभिपीडयन्।।3.66.2।।
transliteration: taṃ tathā śokasantaptaṃ vilapantamanāthavat| mohena mahatāviṣṭaṃ paridyūnamacetanam tatassaumitrirāśvāsya muhūrtādiva lakṣmaṇaḥ| rāmaṃ sambodhayāmāsa caraṇau cābhipīḍayan
translation: ततः then, सौमित्रिः son of Sumitra, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, तथा like that, शोकसन्तप्तम् afflicted with sorrow, अनाथवत् like an orphan, विलपन्तम् while weeping, महता mighty, मोहेन by delusion, आविष्टम् engrossed, परिद्यूनम् miserable, अचेतनम् devoid of consciousness, तं रामम् Rama, मुहूर्तादिव in a moment, आश्वास्य  consoled, चरणौ च his feet, अभिपीडयन् pressing, सम्बोधयामास addressed.
explanation: Lakshmana, son of Sumitra, consoling the mighty miserable Rama, who was afflicted with sorrow, and was weeping helplessly like an orphan, drowned in great delusion, devoid of consciousness, pressed his feet and addressed him:
comments: Lakshmana asks Rama to bear sorrow -- pleads with Rama to think rightly-- arouses Rama's wisdom.

shloka_text: तं तथा शोकसन्तप्तं विलपन्तमनाथवत्। मोहेन महताविष्टं परिद्यूनमचेतनम्।।3.66.1।। ततस्सौमित्रिराश्वास्य मुहूर्तादिव लक्ष्मणः। रामं सम्बोधयामास चरणौ चाभिपीडयन्।।3.66.2।।
transliteration: taṃ tathā śokasantaptaṃ vilapantamanāthavat| mohena mahatāviṣṭaṃ paridyūnamacetanam tatassaumitrirāśvāsya muhūrtādiva lakṣmaṇaḥ| rāmaṃ sambodhayāmāsa caraṇau cābhipīḍayan
translation: ततः then, सौमित्रिः son of Sumitra, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, तथा like that, शोकसन्तप्तम् afflicted with sorrow, अनाथवत् like an orphan, विलपन्तम् while weeping, महता mighty, मोहेन by delusion, आविष्टम् engrossed, परिद्यूनम् miserable, अचेतनम् devoid of consciousness, तं रामम् Rama, मुहूर्तादिव in a moment, आश्वास्य  consoled, चरणौ च his feet, अभिपीडयन् pressing, सम्बोधयामास addressed.
explanation: Lakshmana, son of Sumitra, consoling the mighty miserable Rama, who was afflicted with sorrow, and was weeping helplessly like an orphan, drowned in great delusion, devoid of consciousness, pressed his feet and addressed him:
comments: Lakshmana asks Rama to bear sorrow -- pleads with Rama to think rightly-- arouses Rama's wisdom.

shloka_text: महता तपसा राम महता चापि कर्मणा। राज्ञा दशरथेनासि लब्धोऽमृतमिवामरैः।।3.66.3।।
transliteration: mahatā tapasā rāma mahatā cāpi karmaṇā| rājñā daśarathenāsi labdho'mṛtamivāmaraiḥ
translation: राम Rama, राज्ञा by the king, दशरथेन by Dasaratha, महता great, तपसा penance, महता great, कर्मणाचापि the action, अमरैः by the gods, अमृतमिव like nectar, लब्धः असि obtained.
explanation: O Rama king Dasaratha begot you by doing a great penance and performing great deeds, just as gods begot the nectar.

shloka_text: तव चैव गुणैर्बद्धस्त्वद्वियोगान्महीपतिः। राजा देवत्वमापन्नो भरतस्य यथाश्रुतम्।।3.66.4।।
transliteration: tava caiva guṇairbaddhastvadviyogānmahīpatiḥ| rājā devatvamāpanno bharatasya yathāśrutam
translation: भरतस्य Bharata's, यथा as, श्रुतम् heard, महीपतिः lord of the earth, राजा king, तव your, गुणैः          virtues, बद्धः bound, त्वद्वियोगात् by your separation, देवत्वम् godhood, आपन्नः attained.
explanation: King Dasaratha, impelled by your virtues, and separation from you attained godhood as heard from Bharata.

shloka_text: दुःखितो हि भवान्लोकांस्तेजसा यदि धक्ष्यते। आर्ताः प्रजा नरव्याघ्र क्व नु यास्यन्ति निर्वृतिम्।।3.66.6।।
transliteration: duḥkhito hi bhavānlokāṃstejasā yadi dhakṣyate| ārtāḥ prajā naravyāghra kva nu yāsyanti nirvṛtim
translation: नरव्याघ्र O best among men, दुःखितः in grief, भवान् you, तेजसा by your brilliance, लोकान् worlds, धक्ष्यते burn, यदि if, आर्ताः afflicted, प्रजाः people, क्व where, निर्वृतिम् relief,  यास्यन्ति will get?
explanation: O best of men  if you grieve and burn the world with your brilliance, wherefrom will the (ordinary) afflicted people get relief?

shloka_text: लोकस्वभाव एवैष ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः। गतश्शक्रेण सालोक्यमनयस्तं समस्पृशत्।।3.66.7।।
transliteration: lokasvabhāva evaiṣa yayātirnahuṣātmajaḥ| gataśśakreṇa sālokyamanayastaṃ samaspṛśat
translation: एषः so, लोकस्वभावः एव it is natural order in the world, नहुषात्मजः Nahusha's son, ययातिः Yayati, शक्रेण to Indra, सालोक्यम् sharing his stay in the same world, गतः attached, अनयः curse, तम् him, समस्पृशत् touched .
explanation: It is the go of the world. Yayati, son of Nahusa, shared heaven with Indra but because of his curse (for his bad conduct) suffered misfortune.

shloka_text: महर्षिर्यो वसिष्ठस्तु यः पितुर्नः पुरोहितः। अह्ना पुत्रशतं जज्ञे तथैवास्य पुनर्हतम्।।3.66.8।।
transliteration: maharṣiryo vasiṣṭhastu yaḥ piturnaḥ purohitaḥ| ahnā putraśataṃ jajñe tathaivāsya punarhatam
translation: महर्षिः sage, यः who, वसिष्ठः Vasistha, यः that, नः पितुः our father's, पुरोहितः priest, अस्य his, अह्ना one day, पुत्रशतम् one hundred sons, जज्ञे gave birth to, पुनः again, तथैव in the same way, हतम् killed.
explanation: To sage Vasistha, our father's priest, were born a hundred sons in a day.But all of them were killed in one day the same way.

shloka_text: या चेयं जगतां माता देवी लोकनमस्कृता। अस्याश्च चलनं भूमेर्दृश्यते सत्यसंश्रव।।3.66.9।।
transliteration: yā ceyaṃ jagatāṃ mātā devī lokanamaskṛtā| asyāśca calanaṃ bhūmerdṛśyate satyasaṃśrava
translation: सत्यसंश्रव who adheres to truth, जगताम् for the worlds, माता mother, लोकनमस्कृता is adored by the whole world, या चेयम् she being so, देवी mother, अस्याः her, भूमेः earth, चलनम् movement, दृश्यते is seen.
explanation: You (rigidly) adhere to truth.(Like you) the mother earth who is adored by all the worlds, is unshakeable. Yet she is seen to be shaking at times.

shloka_text: यौ धर्मौ जगतां नेत्रौ यत्र सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। आदित्यचन्द्रौ ग्रहणमभ्युपेतौ महाबलौ।।3.66.10।।
transliteration: yau dharmau jagatāṃ netrau yatra sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam| ādityacandrau grahaṇamabhyupetau mahābalau
translation: यौ whoever, धर्मौ two righteous entities, जगताम् of  the worlds, नेत्रौ two eyes, यत्र where, सर्वम् all, प्रतिष्ठितम् is resting, महाबलौ two very powerful, आदित्यचन्द्रौ Sun and Moon, ग्रहणम् eclipse, अभ्युपेतौ endures.
explanation: The powerful Sun and Moon, righteous entities, who are the two eyes of these worlds and on whom everything rests firmly, also suffer eclipses sometimes.

shloka_text: सुमहान्त्यपि भूतानि देवाश्च पुरुषर्षभ। न दैवस्य प्रमुञ्चन्ति सर्वभूतानि देहिनः।।3.66.11।।
transliteration: sumahāntyapi bhūtāni devāśca puruṣarṣabha| na daivasya pramuñcanti sarvabhūtāni dehinaḥ
translation: पुरुषर्षभ O bull among men, सुमहन्ति भूतानि great beings, देवाश्च gods, सर्वभूतानि all creatures, देहिनः mortals, दैवस्य fate, न प्रमुञ्चन्ति cannot be released.
explanation: O best among men  Fate spares none. Great beings, every creature, even the gods cannot escape fate.

shloka_text: शक्रादिष्वपि देवेषु वर्तमानौ नयानयौ। श्रूयेते नरशार्दूल न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि।।3.66.12।।
transliteration: śakrādiṣvapi deveṣu vartamānau nayānayau| śrūyete naraśārdūla na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
translation: नरशार्दूल O tiger among men, शक्रादिषु among beings such as Indra and others, देवेषु deities, नयानयौ justice or otherwise, वर्तमानौ are present, श्रूयेते heard, त्वम् you, शोचितुम् to worry, नार्हसि not right for you.
explanation: It is I heard that Indra and other deities are also governed by the principle of justice. Therefore, you should not bewail, O tiger among men.

shloka_text: नष्टायामपि वैदेह्यां हृतायामपि चानघ शोचितुं नार्हसे वीर यथान्यः प्राकृतस्तथा।।3.66.13।।
transliteration: naṣṭāyāmapi vaidehyāṃ hṛtāyāmapi cānagha śocituṃ nārhase vīra yathānyaḥ prākṛtastathā
translation: अनघ O sinless soul, वीर hero, वैदेह्याम् when Vaidehi, नष्टायामपि killed, हृतायामपि when  carried off too, प्राकृतः an ordinary person, अन्यः यथा other man, शोचितुम् to worry, नार्हसि not right for you.
explanation: Even if Vaidehi is killed or abducted, you should not grieve like ordinary men, O sinless hero

shloka_text: त्वव्दिधा न हि शोचन्ति सततं सत्यदर्शिनः। सुमहत्स्वपि कृच्छ्रेषु रामानिर्विण्णदर्शनाः।।3.66.14।।
transliteration: tvavdidhā na hi śocanti satataṃ satyadarśinaḥ| sumahatsvapi kṛcchreṣu rāmānirviṇṇadarśanāḥ
translation: राम Rama, सततम् always, सत्यदर्शिनः those who see the truth, अनिर्विण्णदर्शनाः men whose vision is free from depression, त्वव्दिधाः men like you, सुमहत्सु in very great, क्रुच्छ्रेष्वपि even in great calamities, न शोचन्ति हि will not lose heart.
explanation: O Rama, you always see the truth. So  in the face of great difficulties men like you, whose vision is not blurred, should not lose heart.

shloka_text: तत्त्वतो हि नरश्रेष्ठ बुद्ध्या समनुचिन्तय। बुध्द्या युक्ता महाप्राज्ञा विजानन्ति शुभाशुभे।।3.66.15।।
transliteration: tattvato hi naraśreṣṭha buddhyā samanucintaya| budhdyā yuktā mahāprājñā vijānanti śubhāśubhe
translation: नरश्रेष्ठ O best among men, तत्त्वतः the facts, बुद्ध्या applying your intellect, समनुचिन्तय think rightly, महाप्राज्ञाः very wise, बुध्द्या with their intellect, युक्ताः endowed, शुभाशुभे right and wrong, विजानन्ति people know.
explanation: O best among men  judge the facts rightly with your intellect. The wise apply their minds and know what is right and what is wrong.

shloka_text: अदृष्टगुणदोषाणामध्रुवाणां तु कर्मणाम्। नान्तरेण क्रियां तेषां फलमिष्टं प्रवर्तते।।3.66.16।।
transliteration: adṛṣṭaguṇadoṣāṇāmadhruvāṇāṃ tu karmaṇām| nāntareṇa kriyāṃ teṣāṃ phalamiṣṭaṃ pravartate
translation: अदृष्टगुणदोषाणाम् of those who do not know their merits and demerits, अध्रुवाणाम् unstable, तेषाम् in this, कर्मणाम् deeds, इष्टम् good, फलम् results, क्रियाम् अन्तरेण from actions, न प्रवर्तते will not be obtained.
explanation: Good results are not expected from the actions of persons who cannot distinguish between their virtues and vices, from those who are unstable in their deeds.

shloka_text: त्वमेव हि पुरा राम मामेवं बहुशोऽन्वशाः। अनुशिष्याद्धि को नु त्वामपि साक्षाद्बृहस्पतिः।।3.66.17।।
transliteration: tvameva hi purā rāma māmevaṃ bahuśo'nvaśāḥ| anuśiṣyāddhi ko nu tvāmapi sākṣādbṛhaspatiḥ
translation: राम Rama, पुरा in the past, त्वमेव you yourself, माम् to me, एवम् that way, बहुशः many times, अन्वशाः you instructed, हि indeed, साक्षात् personally, बृहस्पतिरपि even Brihaspati, को नु who indeed, त्वाम् to you, अनुशिष्यात् हि can teach you.
explanation: O Rama you yourself in the past have instructed me many times that way. Who can be your adviser in this matter ? You are indeed like Brihaspati.

shloka_text: बुद्धिश्च ते महाप्राज्ञ देवैरपि दुरन्वया। शोकेनाभिप्रसुप्तं ते ज्ञानं सम्बोधयाम्यहम्।।3.66.18।।
transliteration: buddhiśca te mahāprājña devairapi duranvayā| śokenābhiprasuptaṃ te jñānaṃ sambodhayāmyaham
translation: महाप्राज्ञ very wise, ते बुद्धि: your intellect, देवैरपि gods too, दुरन्वया difficult to fathom, शोकेन by sorrow, अभिप्रसुप्तम् put to sleep, ते ज्ञानम् your wisdom, अहम् I am, सम्बोधयामि arousing you.
explanation: Even gods cannot fathom your intellect. I am only trying to rouse your wisdom your sorrow has sent to sleep.

shloka_text: दिव्यं च मानुषं च त्वमात्मनश्च पराक्रमम्। इक्ष्वाकुवृषभावेक्ष्य यतस्व द्विषतां वधे।।3.66.19।।
transliteration: divyaṃ ca mānuṣaṃ ca tvamātmanaśca parākramam| ikṣvākuvṛṣabhāvekṣya yatasva dviṣatāṃ vadhe
translation: इक्ष्वाकुवृषभ among the Ikshvakus, त्वम् you, दिव्यम् divine, मानुषं च mortal, आत्मनः yourself, पराक्रमम् powers, अवेक्ष्य after knowing, द्विषताम् of the enemies, वधे in killing, यतस्व make efforts.
explanation: O bull among the Ikshvakus, weigh your divine and human prowess before you try to kill your enemies.

shloka_text: किं तेन सर्वनाशेन कृतेन पुरुषर्षभ। तमेव त्वं रिपुं पापं विज्ञायोद्धर्तुमर्हसि।।3.66.20।।
transliteration: kiṃ tena sarvanāśena kṛtena puruṣarṣabha| tameva tvaṃ ripuṃ pāpaṃ vijñāyoddhartumarhasi
translation: पुरुषर्षभ best among men, कृतेन by the act of, तेन by that, सर्वनाशेन destruction of all, किम् what for, त्वम् you, पापम् sinful, तं रिपुम् एव your enemy, विज्ञाय after knowing, उद्धर्तुम् to uproot, अर्हसि ought to.
explanation: O best among men  where is the good in the destruction of all? Know your sinful enemy before you uproot him. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकेय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtysixth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: पूर्वजोऽप्युक्तमात्रस्तु लक्ष्मणेन सुभाषितम्। सारग्राही महासारं प्रतिजग्राह राघवः।।3.67.1।।
transliteration: pūrvajo'pyuktamātrastu lakṣmaṇena subhāṣitam| sāragrāhī mahāsāraṃ pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ
translation: सारग्राही who can grasp the essence, राघवः Rama, पूर्वज अपि being elder, लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, उक्तमात्रः तु only when told by, महासारम् the great essence, सुभाषितम् wise counsel, प्रतिजग्राह accepted.
explanation: Even though Rama was elder, he could grasp the quintessence of the wise counsel only after Lakshmana had said it.
comments: Rama and Lakshmana see the wounded Jatayu with wings clipped.

shloka_text: सन्निगृह्य महाबाहुः प्रवृत्तं कोपमात्मनः। अवष्टभ्य धनुश्चित्रं रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।।3.67.2।।
transliteration: sannigṛhya mahābāhuḥ pravṛttaṃ kopamātmanaḥ| avaṣṭabhya dhanuścitraṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt
translation: महाबाहुः longarmed, रामः Rama, प्रवृत्तम् risen, आत्मनः his own, कोपम् anger, सन्निगृह्य after restraining, चित्रम् wonderful, धनुः bow, अवष्टभ्य leaning over, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Restraining his anger, the longarmed Rama leaned over  his wonderful bow and spoke to Lakshmana:

shloka_text: किं करिष्यावहे वत्स क्व वा गच्छाव लक्ष्मण। केनोपायेन गच्छेयं सीतामिति विचिन्तय।।3.67.3।।
transliteration: kiṃ kariṣyāvahe vatsa kva vā gacchāva lakṣmaṇa| kenopāyena gaccheyaṃ sītāmiti vicintaya
translation: वत्स O child, लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, किम् what, करिष्यावहे shall we do, क्व वा where do we, गच्छाव will go, सीताम् Sita, केन उपायेन by what means, गच्छेयम् may I reach, इति this, विचिन्तय think.
explanation: O dear Lakshmana, what shall we do? Where do we go ? Think of some means by which we can reach Sita.

shloka_text: तं तथा परितापार्तं लक्ष्मणो राममब्रवीत्। इदमेव जनस्थानं त्वमन्वेषितुमर्हसि।।3.67.4।। राक्षसैर्बहुभिः कीर्णं नानाद्रुमलतायुतम्।
transliteration: taṃ tathā paritāpārtaṃ lakṣmaṇo rāmamabravīt| idameva janasthānaṃ tvamanveṣitumarhasi rākṣasairbahubhiḥ kīrṇaṃ nānādrumalatāyutam|
translation: तथा so, परितापार्तम् afflicted with grief, तं रामम् that Rama, लक्ष्मणः Lakshman, अब्रवीत् said, त्वम् you, बहुभिः many, राक्षसैः by demons, कीर्णम् full of, नानाद्रुमलतायुतम् covered with different trees and creepers, इमम् this, जनस्थानमेव Janasthna alone, अन्वेषितुम् to search, अर्हसि you should.
explanation: Lakshmana said to Rama, afflicted with grief, It is proper for you to (first) search in this Janasthana, covered with different kinds of trees and creepers, and teeming with demons.

shloka_text: सन्तीह गिरिदुर्गाणि निर्दराः कन्दराणि च।।3.67.5।। गुहाश्च विविधा घोरा नानामृगगणाकुलाः। आवासाः किन्नराणां च गन्धर्वभवनानि च।।3.67.6।।
transliteration: santīha giridurgāṇi nirdarāḥ kandarāṇi ca guhāśca vividhā ghorā nānāmṛgagaṇākulāḥ| āvāsāḥ kinnarāṇāṃ ca gandharvabhavanāni ca
translation: इह here, गिरिदुर्गाणि difficult mountains, निर्दराः valleys, कन्दराणि च and caves, विविधाः many, घोराः terrific, नानामृगगणाकुलाः inhabited by different animals, गुहाश्च caverns, किन्नराणाम् of kinneras, आवासाः dwellingplaces, गन्धर्वभवनानि च mansions of gandharvas, सन्ति are.
explanation: Here are difficult mountains, caves, valleys, dreadful caves full of different animals, dwellingplaces of kinneras and mansions of gandharvas.

shloka_text: सन्तीह गिरिदुर्गाणि निर्दराः कन्दराणि च।।3.67.5।। गुहाश्च विविधा घोरा नानामृगगणाकुलाः। आवासाः किन्नराणां च गन्धर्वभवनानि च।।3.67.6।।
transliteration: santīha giridurgāṇi nirdarāḥ kandarāṇi ca guhāśca vividhā ghorā nānāmṛgagaṇākulāḥ| āvāsāḥ kinnarāṇāṃ ca gandharvabhavanāni ca
translation: इह here, गिरिदुर्गाणि difficult mountains, निर्दराः valleys, कन्दराणि च and caves, विविधाः many, घोराः terrific, नानामृगगणाकुलाः inhabited by different animals, गुहाश्च caverns, किन्नराणाम् of kinneras, आवासाः dwellingplaces, गन्धर्वभवनानि च mansions of gandharvas, सन्ति are.
explanation: Here are difficult mountains, caves, valleys, dreadful caves full of different animals, dwellingplaces of kinneras and mansions of gandharvas.

shloka_text: तानि युक्तो मया सार्धं त्वमन्वेषितुमर्हसि। त्वद्विधा बुद्धिसम्पन्ना महात्मानो नरर्षभ।।3.67.7।। आपत्सु न प्रकम्पन्ते वायुवेगैरिवाचलाः।
transliteration: tāni yukto mayā sārdhaṃ tvamanveṣitumarhasi| tvadvidhā buddhisampannā mahātmāno nararṣabha āpatsu na prakampante vāyuvegairivācalāḥ|
translation: त्वम् you, युक्तः accompanied, मया सार्धम् along with me, तानि those, अन्वेषितुम् to search, अर्हसि it is proper for you, नरर्षभ: great men, बुद्धिसम्पन्नाः endowed with wisdom, त्वद्धिधाः of your type, महात्मानः great people, वायुवेगैः speed of wind, अचलाः इव like mountains, न प्रकम्पन्ते are not shaken.
explanation: Accompanied by me you should search for her in those spots. Great people endowed with wisdom do not destabilise in difficulties just as mountains are not shaken by the speed of the wind.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तस्तद्वनं सर्वं विचचार सलक्ष्मणः।।3.67.8।। क्रुद्धो रामश्शरं घोरं सन्धाय धनुषि क्षुरम्।
transliteration: ityuktastadvanaṃ sarvaṃ vicacāra salakṣmaṇaḥ kruddho rāmaśśaraṃ ghoraṃ sandhāya dhanuṣi kṣuram|
translation: क्रुद्धः becoming angry, रामः Rama, इति thus, उक्तः having been told, सलक्ष्मणः along with Lakskhmana , धनुषि in bow, घोरम् terrific, क्षुरं शरम् sharp arrows, सन्धाय fixing, सर्वम् all, तत् वनम् that forest, विचचार roamed.
explanation: Thus advised, the angry Rama fixed a sharp arrow to his bow and roamed in the forest accompanied by Lakshmana.

shloka_text: ततः पर्वतकूटाभं महाभागं द्विजोत्तमम्।।3.67.9।। ददर्श पतितं भूमौ क्षतजार्द्रं जटायुषम्।
transliteration: tataḥ parvatakūṭābhaṃ mahābhāgaṃ dvijottamam dadarśa patitaṃ bhūmau kṣatajārdraṃ jaṭāyuṣam|
translation: ततः then, पर्वतकूटाभम् like a mountain top, महाभागम् great, द्विजोत्तमम् a wonderful bird, भूमौ on the ground, पतितम् fallen down, क्षतजार्द्रम् drenched with blood, जटायुषम्  Jatayu, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Then he saw the great Jatayu, a wonderful bird, looking like a mountain top, drenched in blood and fallen on the ground.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा गिरिशृङ्गाभं रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।।3.67.10।। अनेन सीता वैदेही भक्षिता नात्र संशयः।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā giriśṛṅgābhaṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt anena sītā vaidehī bhakṣitā nātra saṃśayaḥ|
translation: गिरिशृङ्गाभम् like a peak of the mountain, तम् him, दृष्ट्वा after seeing, रामः Rama, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, अब्रवीत् said, अनेन by him, वैदेही Vaidehi, सीता Sita, भक्षिता is eaten, अत्र in this case, संशयः doubt, न no.
explanation: On seeing Jatayu looking like the peak of a mountain, Rama said to Lakshmana, There is no doubt that this bird has devoured Vaidehi.

shloka_text: गृध्ररूपमिदं रक्षो व्यक्तं भवति कानने।।3.67.11।। भक्षयित्वा विशालाक्षीमास्ते सीतां यथासुखम्। एनं वधिष्ये दीप्तास्यैर्घोरैर्बाणैरजिह्मगैः।।3.67.12।।
transliteration: gṛdhrarūpamidaṃ rakṣo vyaktaṃ bhavati kānane bhakṣayitvā viśālākṣīmāste sītāṃ yathāsukham| enaṃ vadhiṣye dīptāsyairghorairbāṇairajihmagaiḥ
translation: इदम् this, रक्षः demon, गृध्ररूपम् in the guise of a vulture, कानने in the forest, भवति is, व्यक्तम् it is clear, विशालाक्षीम् largeeyed lady, सीताम् Sita, भक्षयित्वा after eating away, यथासुखम् happily, आस्ते relaxing, दीप्तास्यैः glowing tipped, घोरैः terrific, अजिह्मगैः by those which can go straight, बाणैः by darts, एनम् him, वधिष्ये l will kill.
explanation: This demon in the guise of a vulture has evidently eaten away the largeeyed Sita and is happily relaxing in the forest. With my terrific arrows with burning tips that can go straight I will kill him.

shloka_text: गृध्ररूपमिदं रक्षो व्यक्तं भवति कानने।।3.67.11।। भक्षयित्वा विशालाक्षीमास्ते सीतां यथासुखम्। एनं वधिष्ये दीप्तास्यैर्घोरैर्बाणैरजिह्मगैः।।3.67.12।।
transliteration: gṛdhrarūpamidaṃ rakṣo vyaktaṃ bhavati kānane bhakṣayitvā viśālākṣīmāste sītāṃ yathāsukham| enaṃ vadhiṣye dīptāsyairghorairbāṇairajihmagaiḥ
translation: इदम् this, रक्षः demon, गृध्ररूपम् in the guise of a vulture, कानने in the forest, भवति is, व्यक्तम् it is clear, विशालाक्षीम् largeeyed lady, सीताम् Sita, भक्षयित्वा after eating away, यथासुखम् happily, आस्ते relaxing, दीप्तास्यैः glowing tipped, घोरैः terrific, अजिह्मगैः by those which can go straight, बाणैः by darts, एनम् him, वधिष्ये l will kill.
explanation: This demon in the guise of a vulture has evidently eaten away the largeeyed Sita and is happily relaxing in the forest. With my terrific arrows with burning tips that can go straight I will kill him.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वाभ्यपतद्गृध्रं सन्धाय धनुषि क्षुरम्। क्रुद्धो रामस्समुद्रान्तां कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्।।3.67.13।।
transliteration: ityuktvābhyapatadgṛdhraṃ sandhāya dhanuṣi kṣuram| kruddho rāmassamudrāntāṃ kampayanniva medinīm
translation: रामः Rama, इति thus, उक्त्वा saying so, क्रुद्धः in anger, धनुषि on the bow, क्षुरम् sharp  arrow, सन्धाय after fixing, समुद्रान्ताम् extending up to the sea, मेदिनीम् the earth, कम्पयन्निव as though shaking, गृध्रम् vulture, अभ्यपतत् fell upon.
explanation: Having siad so, Rama took his bow, fixed the sharp arrow, and aimed at the vulture. The seabound earth trembled.

shloka_text: तं दीनं दीनया वाचा सफेनं रुधिरं वमन्। अभ्यभाषत पक्षी तु रामं दशरथात्मजम्।।3.67.14।।
transliteration: taṃ dīnaṃ dīnayā vācā saphenaṃ rudhiraṃ vaman| abhyabhāṣata pakṣī tu rāmaṃ daśarathātmajam
translation: पक्षी तु but the bird, सफेनम् foamy, रुधिरम् blood, वमन् vomitting, दीनम् in a piteous way, तं him, दशरथात्मजम् Dasaratha's son, रामम् Rama, दीनया pathetic, वाचा with word, अभ्यभाषत spoke these words.
explanation: But the vulture who was in a piteous state, vomitting foamy blood, spoke these words pathetically to Rama, son of Dasaratha:

shloka_text: यामोषधिमिवायुष्मन्नन्वेषसि महावने। सा देवी मम च प्राणा रावणेनोभयं हृतम्।।3.67.15।।
transliteration: yāmoṣadhimivāyuṣmannanveṣasi mahāvane| sā devī mama ca prāṇā rāvaṇenobhayaṃ hṛtam
translation: आयुष्मन् longlived one, याम् whom, महावने in this great forest, ओषधिमिव like herbal medicine, अन्वेषसि you are searching , सा देवी that queen, मम my, प्राणाः च life also, उभयम् both, रावणेन by Ravana, हृतम् is taken away.
explanation: O Longlived one  she who you are searching in the forest like herbal medicine has been carried away by Ravana along with my life.

shloka_text: त्वया विरहिता देवी लक्ष्मणेन च राघव। ह्रियमाणा मया दृष्टा रावणेन बलीयसा।।3.67.16।।
transliteration: tvayā virahitā devī lakṣmaṇena ca rāghava| hriyamāṇā mayā dṛṣṭā rāvaṇena balīyasā
translation: राघव Rama, त्वया by you, लक्ष्मणेन च and by Lakshmana, विरहिता separated, देवी qeeen, बलीयसा by the powerful, रावणेन by Ravana, ह्रियमाणा taken away, मया I have, दृष्टा seen.
explanation: I have seen her snatched from you and from Lakshmana and carried off by powerful Ravana.

shloka_text: सीतामभ्यवपन्नोऽहं रावणश्च रणे मया। विध्वंसितरथश्चात्र पातितो धरणीतले।।3.67.17।।
transliteration: sītāmabhyavapanno'haṃ rāvaṇaśca raṇe mayā| vidhvaṃsitarathaścātra pātito dharaṇītale
translation: अहम् I, सीताम् Sita, अभ्यवपन्नः descended down, मया by me, रावणश्च Ravana, विध्वंसितरथः with his chariot destroyed, अत्र in this place, धरणीतले on this ground, पातितः I fell down.
explanation: I descended down to protect Sita, and in the battle with Ravana his chariot destroyed fell down here on the ground.

shloka_text: एतदस्य धनुर्भग्नमेतदस्य शरावरम्। अयमस्य रथो राम भग्नसाङ्ग्रामिको मया।।3.67.18।।
transliteration: etadasya dhanurbhagnametadasya śarāvaram| ayamasya ratho rāma bhagnasāṅgrāmiko mayā
translation: राम Rama, एतत् this, अस्य his, भग्नम् broken, धनुः bow, एतत् this, अस्य his, शरावरम् quiver, अयम् this, मया by me, भग्नः shattered, अस्य his, साङ्ग्रामिकः battle, रथः chariot.
explanation: O Rama this is his broken bow, this is his quiver and this is his warchariot all devastated by me.

shloka_text: अयं तु सारथिस्तस्य मत्पक्षनिहतो युधि। परिश्रान्तस्य मे पक्षौ छित्त्वा खड्गेन रावणः।।3.67.19।। सीतामादाय वैदेहीमुत्पपात विहायसम्। रक्षसा निहतं पूर्वं न मां हन्तुं त्वमर्हसि।।3.67.20।।
transliteration: ayaṃ tu sārathistasya matpakṣanihato yudhi| pariśrāntasya me pakṣau chittvā khaḍgena rāvaṇaḥ sītāmādāya vaidehīmutpapāta vihāyasam| rakṣasā nihataṃ pūrvaṃ na māṃ hantuṃ tvamarhasi
translation: अयं तु he is, युधि in the battle, मत्पक्षनिहतः killed by my wings, तस्य सारथिः his charioteer, रावणः Ravana, परिश्रान्तस्य an exhausted one, मे my, पक्षौ both wings, खड्गेन with a sword, छित्त्वा having cut, वैदेहीम् Vaidehi, सीताम् Sita, आदाय after taking, विहायसम् into the sky, उत्पपात flew up, रक्षसा by Ravana, पूर्वम् earlier, निहतम् slain, माम् me, त्वम् you, हन्तुम् to kill, नार्हसि not proper.
explanation: He is Ravana's charioteer slain by my wings in the battle.  As I was exhausted in the encounter Ravana clipped my wings,  took Sita, and flew into the sky. You need not kill me. I am already slain by the demon.

shloka_text: अयं तु सारथिस्तस्य मत्पक्षनिहतो युधि। परिश्रान्तस्य मे पक्षौ छित्त्वा खड्गेन रावणः।।3.67.19।। सीतामादाय वैदेहीमुत्पपात विहायसम्। रक्षसा निहतं पूर्वं न मां हन्तुं त्वमर्हसि।।3.67.20।।
transliteration: ayaṃ tu sārathistasya matpakṣanihato yudhi| pariśrāntasya me pakṣau chittvā khaḍgena rāvaṇaḥ sītāmādāya vaidehīmutpapāta vihāyasam| rakṣasā nihataṃ pūrvaṃ na māṃ hantuṃ tvamarhasi
translation: अयं तु he is, युधि in the battle, मत्पक्षनिहतः killed by my wings, तस्य सारथिः his charioteer, रावणः Ravana, परिश्रान्तस्य an exhausted one, मे my, पक्षौ both wings, खड्गेन with a sword, छित्त्वा having cut, वैदेहीम् Vaidehi, सीताम् Sita, आदाय after taking, विहायसम् into the sky, उत्पपात flew up, रक्षसा by Ravana, पूर्वम् earlier, निहतम् slain, माम् me, त्वम् you, हन्तुम् to kill, नार्हसि not proper.
explanation: He is Ravana's charioteer slain by my wings in the battle.  As I was exhausted in the encounter Ravana clipped my wings,  took Sita, and flew into the sky. You need not kill me. I am already slain by the demon.

shloka_text: रामस्तस्य तु विज्ञाय बाष्पपूर्णमुखस्तदा। द्विगुणीकृततापार्तस्सीतासक्तां प्रियां कथाम्।।3.67.21।।
transliteration: rāmastasya tu vijñāya bāṣpapūrṇamukhastadā| dviguṇīkṛtatāpārtassītāsaktāṃ priyāṃ kathām
translation: तदा then, रामः Rama, तस्य his, सीतासक्ताम् about Sita, प्रियाम् dear, कथाम् facts, विज्ञाय having, बाष्पपूर्णमुखः face full of tears, द्विगुणीकृततापार्तः  helpless and pitiable due to redoubled sorrow.
explanation: Having known from Jatayu the story of his beloved Sita, Rama was full of tears, his grief redoubled.

shloka_text: गृध्रराजं परिष्वज्य परित्यज्य महद्धनुः। निपपातावशो भूमौ रुरोद सहलक्ष्मणः।।3.67.22।।
transliteration: gṛdhrarājaṃ pariṣvajya parityajya mahaddhanuḥ| nipapātāvaśo bhūmau ruroda sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
translation: महत् great, धनुः bow, परित्यज्य giving up, गृध्रराजम् king of birds, परिष्वज्य embracing, अवशः despondent, भूमौ on the ground, निपपात fell down, सहलक्ष्मणः along with Lakshmana, रुरोद cried.
explanation: Rama dropped the bow and embraced the king of birds. He fell down despondent on the ground and began crying along with Lakshmana.

shloka_text: एकमेकायने दुर्गे निश्श्वसन्तं कथञ्चन। समीक्ष्य दुःखिततरो रामस्सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्।।3.67.23।।
transliteration: ekamekāyane durge niśśvasantaṃ kathañcana| samīkṣya duḥkhitataro rāmassaumitrimabravīt
translation: दुर्गे in a place difficult to reach, एकायने in a solitary place, एकम् lonely, कथञ्चन with great difficulty, निश्श्वसन्तम् sighing, समीक्ष्य on observing, रामः Rama, दुःखिततरः overcome by greater grief, सौमित्रिम् Saumitri, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Rama saw Jatayu breathing with difficulty in that solitary, inaccessible place.Overcome by greater grief  he said to Lakshmana:

shloka_text: राज्यं भ्रष्टं वने वासस्सीता नष्टा हतो द्विजः। ईदृशीयं ममालक्ष्मीर्निर्दहेदपि पावकम्।।3.67.24।।
transliteration: rājyaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ vane vāsassītā naṣṭā hato dvijaḥ| īdṛśīyaṃ mamālakṣmīrnirdahedapi pāvakam
translation: राज्यम् kingdom, भ्रष्टम् expelled, वने forest, वासः dwelling, सीता Sita, नष्टा lost, द्विजः Jatayu, हतः is slain, मम me, ईदृशी this kind of, अलक्ष्मीः bad luck, पावकमपि even fire, निर्दहेत्  it will burn.
explanation: I have been expelled from the kingdom. I am made to stay in the forest. I have lost Sita (my beloved wife). This bird (who was my wellwisher) has been slain. Such misfortune will burn even fire.

shloka_text: सम्पूर्णमपि चेदद्य प्रविशेयं महोदधिम्। सोऽपि नूनं ममालक्ष्म्या विशुष्येत्सरितांपतिः।।3.67.25।।
transliteration: sampūrṇamapi cedadya praviśeyaṃ mahodadhim| so'pi nūnaṃ mamālakṣmyā viśuṣyetsaritāṃpatiḥ
translation: अद्य now, सम्पूर्णम् full, महोदधिम् अपि even the great sea also, प्रविशेयं चेत् if I enter, सः that, सरितां पतिः अपि even the lord of rivers, sea, मम me, अलक्ष्मा misfortune, विशुष्येत् will dry up.
explanation: Now if I enter even the great sea, the lord of the rivers filled with water, it will also dry up due to my misfortune.

shloka_text: नास्त्यभाग्यतरो लोके मत्तोऽस्मिन्सचराचरे। येनेयं महती प्राप्ता मया व्यसनवागुरा।।3.67.26।।
transliteration: nāstyabhāgyataro loke matto'sminsacarācare| yeneyaṃ mahatī prāptā mayā vyasanavāgurā
translation: येन मया by me this way, इयम् this kind, महती great, व्यसनवागुरा snare of misfortunes, प्राप्ता attained, मत्तः more than me, अभाग्यतरः more unlucky, सचराचरे among animate and inanimate, अस्मिन् in this, लोके world, नास्ति not there.
explanation: In this world of the animate and the inanimate there is no one more unfortunate than me fallen into the trap of adversities.

shloka_text: अयं पितृवयस्यो मे गृध्रराजो जरान्वितः। शेते विनिहतो भूमौ मम भाग्यविपर्ययात्।।3.67.27।।
transliteration: ayaṃ pitṛvayasyo me gṛdhrarājo jarānvitaḥ| śete vinihato bhūmau mama bhāgyaviparyayāt
translation: मे my, पितृवयस्यः father's friend, जरान्वितः in old age, अयम् he is, गृध्रराजः king of birds, मम of me, भाग्यविपर्ययात् by my misfortune, विनिहतः was slain, भूमौ ground, शेते lying.
explanation: This aged king of birds is my father's friend. To my illluck, he is struck down and is lying on the ground.

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्त्वा बहुशो राघवस्सहलक्ष्मणः। जटायुषं च पस्पर्श पितृस्नेहं विदर्शयन्।।3.67.28।।
transliteration: ityevamuktvā bahuśo rāghavassahalakṣmaṇaḥ| jaṭāyuṣaṃ ca pasparśa pitṛsnehaṃ vidarśayan
translation: राघवः Rama, इत्येवम् in this manner, बहुशः many times, उक्त्वा after telling, सहलक्ष्मणः along with Lakshmana, पितृस्नेहम् filiat affection, विदर्शयन् showing, जटायुषम् Jatayu, पस्पर्श caressed.
explanation: Saying such words and showing filial affection, he caressed Jatayu repeatedly with Lakshmana.

shloka_text: निकृत्तपक्षं रुधिरावसिक्तं स गृध्रराजं परिरभ्य रामः। क्व मैथिली प्राणसमा ममेति विमुच्य वाचं निपपात भूमौ।।3.67.29।।
transliteration: nikṛttapakṣaṃ rudhirāvasiktaṃ sa gṛdhrarājaṃ parirabhya rāmaḥ| kva maithilī prāṇasamā mameti vimucya vācaṃ nipapāta bhūmau
translation: सः रामः that Rama, निकृत्तपक्षम् severed wings, रुधिरावसिक्तम् drenched in blood, गृध्रराजम् king of vultures, परिरभ्य hugging, मम my, प्राणसमा equal to my life, मैथिली Maithili, क्व where, इति this, वाचम् speaking, विमुच्य भूमौ leaving the ground, निपपात fell down.
explanation: Rama hugged the king of vultures with servered wings, drenched in blood and asking him where Sita who was as dear to him as his life was, he dropped him and fell down on the ground. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyseventh sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: रामस्सम्प्रेक्ष्य तं गृध्रं भुवि रौद्रेण पातितम्। सौमित्रिं मित्रसम्पन्नमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।3.68.1।।
transliteration: rāmassamprekṣya taṃ gṛdhraṃ bhuvi raudreṇa pātitam| saumitriṃ mitrasampannamidaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: रौद्रेण by fierce, भुवि ground, पातितम्  thrown down, तं गृध्रम् that vulture, प्रेक्ष्य seeing, रामः Rama, मित्रसम्पन्नम् friendly, सौमित्रिम् Lakshmana, इदं वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Seeing the vulture lying on the ground thrown down by the fierce demon, Rama said to friendly Lakshmana:
comments: Jatayu informs Rama about his combat with Ravana and Sita's abduction-- Jatayu's death-- cremation

shloka_text: ममायं नूनमर्थेषु यतमानो विहङ्गमः। राक्षसेन हतस्संख्ये प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यति दुस्त्यजान्।।3.68.2।।
transliteration: mamāyaṃ nūnamartheṣu yatamāno vihaṅgamaḥ| rākṣasena hatassaṃkhye prāṇāṃstyakṣyati dustyajān
translation: मम my, अर्थेषु in my objective, यतमानः while he is making efforts, अयं विहङ्गमः this bird, सङ्ख्ये in battle, राक्षसेन by demon, हतः struck, दुस्त्यजान्  hard to leave, प्राणान् life, त्यक्ष्यति going to give up, नूनम् surely.
explanation: Struck down by the demon in the combat on my account this bird is going to give up his life which is indeed difficult.

shloka_text: अयमस्य शरीरेऽस्मिन्प्राणो लक्ष्मण विद्यते। तथा हि स्वरहीनोऽयं विक्लबस्समुदीक्ष्यते।।3.68.3।।
transliteration: ayamasya śarīre'sminprāṇo lakṣmaṇa vidyate| tathā hi svarahīno'yaṃ viklabassamudīkṣyate
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, अस्य his, अस्मिन् शरीरे in this body, प्राणः life, (अतिखिन्नः suffering from intense pain), विद्यते appears, तथा हि like that, अयम् he, स्वरहीनः faint voice, विक्लबः frightened, समुदीक्ष्यते feeling excruciating pain.
explanation: O Lakshmana, it appears he is frightened and is experiencing excruciating pain in the body. His voice sounds faint, too.

shloka_text: जटायो यदि शक्नोषि वाक्यं व्याहरितुं पुनः। सीतामाख्याहि भद्रं ते वधमाख्याहि चात्मनः।।3.68.4।।
transliteration: jaṭāyo yadi śaknoṣi vākyaṃ vyāharituṃ punaḥ| sītāmākhyāhi bhadraṃ te vadhamākhyāhi cātmanaḥ
translation: जटायो Jatayu, पुनः again, व्याहरितुम् to speak, शक्नोषि यदि if you are able, ते भद्रम् be blessed, सीताम् about Sita, अख्याहि tell, आत्मनः yourself, वधम् striking, आख्याहि tell.
explanation: O Jatayu If you are still able to speak, tell me about Sita and about how you have been struck down.

shloka_text: किं निमित्तोऽहरत्सीतां रावणस्तस्य किं मया। अपराद्धं तु यं दृष्ट्वा रावणेन हृता प्रिया।।3.68.5।।
transliteration: kiṃ nimitto'haratsītāṃ rāvaṇastasya kiṃ mayā| aparāddhaṃ tu yaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇena hṛtā priyā
translation: रावणः Ravana, किं निमित्तः for what reason, सीताम् Sita, अहरत् abducted, मया by me, तस्य his, किम् what, अपराद्धम्  crime, यम् which, दृष्ट्वा seeing, प्रिया beloved, हृता taken?
explanation: Why did Ravana abduct Sita? What fault did he find with me so that he kidnapped my beloved ?

shloka_text: कथं तच्चन्द्रसङ्काशं मुखमासीन्मनोहरम्। सीतया कानि चोक्तानि तस्मिन्काले द्विजोत्तम।।3.68.6।।
transliteration: kathaṃ taccandrasaṅkāśaṃ mukhamāsīnmanoharam| sītayā kāni coktāni tasminkāle dvijottama
translation: द्विजोत्तम best of birds, चन्द्रसङ्काशम् Moon like, मनोहरम् delightful, तत् मुखम् her face, कथम् how, आसीत् it was, तस्मिन् काले at the time of abduction, सीतया by Sita,  कानि what, उक्तानि did she say?
explanation: O best of birds how did her delightful, Moonlike face look when she was hijacked. What did she say at that time?

shloka_text: कथं वीर्यः कथं रूपः किं कर्मा स च राक्षसः। क्व चास्य भवनं तात ब्रूहि मे परिपृच्छतः।।3.68.7।।
transliteration: kathaṃ vīryaḥ kathaṃ rūpaḥ kiṃ karmā sa ca rākṣasaḥ| kva cāsya bhavanaṃ tāta brūhi me paripṛcchataḥ
translation: सः राक्षसः the demon, कथं वीर्यः how powerful, कथं रूपः how did he look, किं कर्मा what he does, अस्य his, भवनं च mansion also, क्व च where, तात dear, परिपृच्छतः I am asking you, मे to me, ब्रूहि please tell.
explanation: O father  how powerful is that demon ? How does he look?What work does he do? Where does he dwell? Do answer my questions?

shloka_text: तमुद्वीक्ष्याथ दीनात्मा विलपन्तमनन्तरम्। वाचातिसन्नया रामं जटायुरिदमब्रवीत्।।3.68.8।।
transliteration: tamudvīkṣyātha dīnātmā vilapantamanantaram| vācātisannayā rāmaṃ jaṭāyuridamabravīt
translation: अनन्तरम् incessantly, दीनात्मा a piteous soul, जटायुः Jatayu, विलपन्तम् wailing, रामम् to Rama, उद्वीक्ष्य seeing, अथ this, अतिसन्नया in a faint voice, वाचा spoke, इदम् these, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Thereafter Jatayu, a piteous soul, looked up at Rama who was  crying incessantly and said this in a feeble voice:

shloka_text: हृता सा राक्षसेन्द्रेण रावणेन विहायसा। मायामास्थाय विपुलां वातदुर्दिनसङ्कुलाम्।।3.68.9।।
transliteration: hṛtā sā rākṣasendreṇa rāvaṇena vihāyasā| māyāmāsthāya vipulāṃ vātadurdinasaṅkulām
translation: सा she, राक्षसेन्द्रेण by the lord of demons, रावणेन by Ravana, वातदुर्दिनसङ्कुलाम् violent wind, विपुलाम् huge, मायाम् magic, आस्थाय creating, विहायसा in the sky, हृता taken away.
explanation: Ravana, the lord of the demons created violent winds through terrific magic and whisked her away in the sky.

shloka_text: परिश्रान्तस्य मे तात पक्षौ छित्वा स राक्षसः। सीतामादाय वैदेहीं प्रयातो दक्षिणां दिशम्।।3.68.10।।
transliteration: pariśrāntasya me tāta pakṣau chitvā sa rākṣasaḥ| sītāmādāya vaidehīṃ prayāto dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
translation: तात O my child, सः राक्षसः that demon, परिश्रान्तस्य when I was exhausted, मे myself, पक्षौ wings, छित्त्वा after cutting, वैदेहीम् princess of Videha, सीताम् Sita, आदाय taking,दक्षिणां दिशम् southern, प्रयातः went.
explanation: O my child  when I was exhausted, that demon cut off my wings and carried Sita off in the southern direction.

shloka_text: उपरुध्यन्ति मे प्राणा दृष्टिर्भ्रमति राघव। पश्यामि वृक्षान्सौवर्णानुशीरकृतमूर्धजान्।।3.68.11।।
transliteration: uparudhyanti me prāṇā dṛṣṭirbhramati rāghava| paśyāmi vṛkṣānsauvarṇānuśīrakṛtamūrdhajān
translation: राघव Rama, मे my, प्राणाः life, उपरुध्यन्ति obstructing, दृष्टिः sight, भ्रमति is reeling, अनुशीरकृतमूर्धजान् root hair grown on tops, सौवर्णान् golden , वृक्षान् trees, पश्यामि I see.
explanation: O scion of the Raghu race, I am gasping for breath. My eyes are reeling. I see root hair growing on the tops of golden trees.

shloka_text: येन याति मुहूर्तेन सीतामादाय रावणः। विप्रणष्टं धनं क्षिप्रं तत्स्वामी प्रतिपद्यते।।3.68.12।। विन्दो नाम मुहूर्तोऽयं स च काकुत्स्थ नाबुधत्।
transliteration: yena yāti muhūrtena sītāmādāya rāvaṇaḥ| vipraṇaṣṭaṃ dhanaṃ kṣipraṃ tatsvāmī pratipadyate vindo nāma muhūrto'yaṃ sa ca kākutstha nābudhat|
translation: काकुत्स्थ O Rama, रावणः Ravana, येन मुहूर्तेन by such moment, सीताम् Sita, आदाय taking, याति he, अयम् this, विन्द: Vinda, नाम by name, मुहूर्तः time, विनष्टम् lost, धनम् wealth, तत्स्वामी that person, क्षिप्रम् quickly, प्रतिपद्यते will obtain, सः च and he, नाबुधत् did not know.
explanation: The time Ravana kidnapped Sita is known as 'Vinda'. The effect (of that time), is that her husband will regain his lost wealth. O scion of the Kakutstha race  he (Ravana )did not know it.

shloka_text: त्वत्प्रियां जानकीं हृत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।।3.68.13।। झषवद्बडिशं गृह्य क्षिप्रमेव विनश्यति।
transliteration: tvatpriyāṃ jānakīṃ hṛtvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ jhaṣavadbaḍiśaṃ gṛhya kṣiprameva vinaśyati|
translation: राक्षसेश्वरः lord of the demons, रावणः Ravana, त्वत्प्रियाम् your beloved, जानकीम् Janaki, हृत्वा after carrying away, बडिशम् fish hook, गृह्य having picked up, झषवत् like the fish, क्षिप्रमेव quickly, विनश्यति will be destroyed.
explanation: Ravana, king of the demons, will perish soon for running away with your beloved Janaki just like a fish carrying away a fishhook (which causes its destruction).

shloka_text: न च त्वया व्यथा कार्या जनकस्य सुतां प्रति।।3.68.14।। वैदेह्या रंस्यसे क्षिप्रं हत्वा तं राक्षसं रणे।
transliteration: na ca tvayā vyathā kāryā janakasya sutāṃ prati vaidehyā raṃsyase kṣipraṃ hatvā taṃ rākṣasaṃ raṇe|
translation: त्वया by you, जनकस्य सुतां Janaka's daughter, प्रति with regard to, व्यथा worry, न कार्या need not be, रणे in battle, तं राक्षसम् that demon, क्षिप्रम् soon, हत्वा having slain, वैदेह्या with Vaidehi, रंस्यसे will sport.
explanation: You need not worry about Janaka's daughter. You will soon enjoy the company of your beloved, Vaidehi after killing that demon.

shloka_text: असम्मूढस्य गृध्रस्य रामं प्रत्यनुभाषतः।।3.68.15।। आस्यात्सुस्राव रुधिरं म्रियमाणस्य सामिषम्।
transliteration: asammūḍhasya gṛdhrasya rāmaṃ pratyanubhāṣataḥ āsyātsusrāva rudhiraṃ mriyamāṇasya sāmiṣam|
translation: रामं प्रति with Rama, अनुभाषतः conversing, असम्मूढस्य of the bird that was not deluded, म्रियमाणस्य while dying, गृध्रस्य vulture's, आस्यात् from his mouth, सामिषम् mixed with flesh, रुधिरम् blood, सुस्राव dripped.
explanation: As he(Jatayu) was speaking to Rama with an alert mind even while dying, blood mixed with flesh started oozing from Jatayu's mouth.

shloka_text: पुत्रो विश्रवसस्साक्षाद्भ्राता वैश्रवणस्य च।।3.68.16।। इत्युक्त्वा दुर्लभान्प्राणान्मुमोच पतगेश्वरः।
transliteration: putro viśravasassākṣādbhrātā vaiśravaṇasya ca ityuktvā durlabhānprāṇānmumoca patageśvaraḥ|
translation: विश्रवसः Visrava's, पुत्रः son, वैश्रवणस्य साक्षात् Vaisravana's lawful, भ्राता brother, इति thus, उक्त्वा said, पतगेश्वरः Jatayu, the king of birds, दुर्लभान्  rare, प्राणान् life, मुमोच gave up.
explanation: Ravana was Visrava's son and Vaisravana's (Kubera's) brother, said Jatayu and gave up his rare life.

shloka_text: ब्रूहि ब्रूहीति रामस्य ब्रुवाणस्य कृताञ्जलेः।।3.68.17।। त्वक्त्वा शरीरं गृध्रस्य जग्मुः प्राणा विहायसम्।
transliteration: brūhi brūhīti rāmasya bruvāṇasya kṛtāñjaleḥ tvaktvā śarīraṃ gṛdhrasya jagmuḥ prāṇā vihāyasam|
translation: कृताञ्जलेः waiting with folded palms, रामस्य Rama's, ब्रुहि ब्रुहि इति saying 'tell me, tell me', ब्रुवाणस्य as he spoke so, गृध्रस्य of the vulture, प्राणाः life, शरीरम् body, त्वक्त्वा after leaving, विहायसम् to the sky, जग्मुः went.
explanation: As Rama was saying to the vulture with folded palms 'Tell me, tell me'( about Ravana) the life breath of the vulture soared into the sky leaving the body.

shloka_text: स निक्षिप्य शिरो भूमौ प्रसार्य चरणौ तदा।।3.68.18।। विक्षिप्य च शरीरं स्वं पपात धरणीतले।
transliteration: sa nikṣipya śiro bhūmau prasārya caraṇau tadā vikṣipya ca śarīraṃ svaṃ papāta dharaṇītale|
translation: सः Jatayu, तदा then, शिरः head, भूमौ on the ground, निक्षिप्य after throwing, चरणौ feet, प्रसार्य stretching, स्वम् his, शरीरम् body, धरणीतले on the ground, विक्षिप्य scattering, पपात fallen down.
explanation: Then Jatayu dropped his head down, his feet thrown about, his body outstretched on earth.

shloka_text: तं गृध्रं प्रेक्ष्य ताम्राक्षं गतासुमचलोपमम्।।3.68.19।। रामस्सुबहुभिर्दुःखैर्दीनस्सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्।
transliteration: taṃ gṛdhraṃ prekṣya tāmrākṣaṃ gatāsumacalopamam rāmassubahubhirduḥkhairdīnassaumitrimabravīt|
translation: सुबहुभिः with much, दुःखै: with sorrow, दीनः dejected, रामः Rama, ताम्राक्षम् eyes red (with tears), गतासुम् with his life gone, अचलोपमम् looking like a mountain, तं गृध्रम् to that vulture, प्रेक्ष्य  seeing, सौमित्रिम् to Lakshmana, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Stricken with deep grief, his eyes red (with tears) Rama saw the vulture looking like a mountain. Seeing him dead, he said to Lakshmana:

shloka_text: बहूनि रक्षसां वासे वर्षाणि वसता सुखम्।।3.68.20।। अनेन दण्डकारण्ये विशीर्णमिह पक्षिणा।
transliteration: bahūni rakṣasāṃ vāse varṣāṇi vasatā sukham anena daṇḍakāraṇye viśīrṇamiha pakṣiṇā|
translation: रक्षसाम् the demon's, वासे dwellingplace, इह here, दण्डकारण्ये Dandaka forest, सुखम् happily, बहूनि many, वर्षाणि years, वसता living, अनेन by this, पक्षिणा by the bird, विशीर्णम् lost life.
explanation: Dwelling for many years happily in Dandaka forest, the abode of demons, the bird lost his life (on our account).

shloka_text: अनेकवार्षिको यस्तु चिरकालसमुत्थितः।।3.68.21।। सोऽयमद्य हतश्शेते कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः।
transliteration: anekavārṣiko yastu cirakālasamutthitaḥ so'yamadya hataśśete kālo hi duratikramaḥ|
translation: अनेकवार्षिकः many years old, यः he, चिरकालसमुत्थितः lived for a long time, सः अयम् this Jatayu, अद्य now, हतः dead, शेते lying down, कालः time (fate), दुरतिक्रमः हि not possible to escape.
explanation: This Jatayu, who lived for long years, is lying dead now. (The dictate of) destiny is inescapable.

shloka_text: पश्य लक्ष्मण गृध्रोऽयमुपकारी हतश्च मे।।3.68.22।। सीतामभ्यवपन्नो वै रावणेन बलीयसा।
transliteration: paśya lakṣmaṇa gṛdhro'yamupakārī hataśca me sītāmabhyavapanno vai rāvaṇena balīyasā|
translation: लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, सीताम् Sita, अभ्यवपन्नः he reached out for help, मे उपकारी my wellwisher, अयं गृध्रः this vulture, बलीयसा by the powerful, रावणेन by Ravana, हतः is killed, पश्य see.
explanation: O Lakshmana, see this Jatayu, my benefactor, killed by the powerful Ravana while he was reaching out to help Sita.

shloka_text: गृध्रराज्यं परित्यज्य पितृपैतामहं महत्।।3.68.23।। मम हेतोरयं प्राणान्मुमोच पतगेश्वरः।
transliteration: gṛdhrarājyaṃ parityajya pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat mama hetorayaṃ prāṇānmumoca patageśvaraḥ|
translation: अयं पतगेश्वरः this lord of the birds, पितृपैतामहम् ancestral, महत् great, गृध्रराज्यम् kingdom of vultures, परित्यज्य  left, मम हेतोः for my sake, प्राणान् life, मुमोच gave up.
explanation: This lord of the birds left his ancestral kingdom of viltures and gave up life for my sake.

shloka_text: सर्वत्र खलु दृश्यन्ते साधवो धर्मचारिणः।।3.68.24।। शूराश्शरण्यास्सौमित्रे तिर्यग्योनिगतेष्वपि।
transliteration: sarvatra khalu dṛśyante sādhavo dharmacāriṇaḥ śūrāśśaraṇyāssaumitre tiryagyonigateṣvapi|
translation: सौमित्रे Lakshmana, शूराः heroes, शरण्याः protectors, धर्मचारिणः rigteous people, साधवः good people, सर्वत्र all over, तिर्यग्योनिगतेष्वपि even among animals and birds, दृश्यन्ते खलु are seen.
explanation: O Lakshmana valiant souls and protectors, being righteous and honest are found even among animals and birds.

shloka_text: सीताहरणजं दुःखं न मे सौम्य तथाविधम्।।3.68.25।। यथा विनाशे गृध्रस्य मत्कृते च परन्तप।
transliteration: sītāharaṇajaṃ duḥkhaṃ na me saumya tathāvidham yathā vināśe gṛdhrasya matkṛte ca parantapa|
translation: परन्तप O scorcher of enemies, सौम्य handsome one, गृध्रस्य bird's, विनाशे at his death, मत्कृते च for my sake, यथा as, सीताहरणजम् caused by the abduction of Sita, दुःखम् grief, तथाविधम् in that way, न not experienced.
explanation: O scorcher of enemies, O handsome Lakshmana the grief I experience due to Jatayu's death on my account is more intense than Sita's abduction.

shloka_text: राजा दशरथश्श्रीमान्यथा मम महायशाः।।3.68.26।। पूजनीयश्च मान्यश्च तथाऽयं पतगेश्वरः।
transliteration: rājā daśarathaśśrīmānyathā mama mahāyaśāḥ pūjanīyaśca mānyaśca tathā'yaṃ patageśvaraḥ|
translation: महायशाः illustrious, श्रीमान् prosperous, राजा king, दशरथः Dasaratha, मम for me, यथा as, पूजनीयश्च worthy of reverence, मान्यश्च worthy of honour, अयम् this, पतगेश्वरः lord of the birds, तथा in the same way.
explanation: This lord of the birds for me is as worthy of reverence and honour as the famous and prosperous king Dasaratha.

shloka_text: सौमित्रे हर काष्ठानि निर्मथिष्यामि पावकम्।।3.68.27।। गृध्रराजं दिधक्षामि मत्कृते निधनं गतम्।
transliteration: saumitre hara kāṣṭhāni nirmathiṣyāmi pāvakam gṛdhrarājaṃ didhakṣāmi matkṛte nidhanaṃ gatam|
translation: सौमित्रे Saumitri, काष्ठानि firewood, हर fetch, पावकम् fire, निर्मथिष्यामि I will rub, मत्कृते for my sake, निधनम् गतम् died, गृध्रराजम् king of the birds, दिधक्षामि I wish to burn.
explanation: O Saumitri  fetch firewood. I shall generate fire by rubbing them and cremate the king of the birds who has laid down his life for my sake.

shloka_text: नाथं पतगलोकस्य चितामारोप्य राघव।।3.68.28।। इमं धक्ष्यामि सौमित्रे हतं रौद्रेण रक्षसा।
transliteration: nāthaṃ patagalokasya citāmāropya rāghava imaṃ dhakṣyāmi saumitre hataṃ raudreṇa rakṣasā|
translation: राघव O scion of the Raghu race, सौमित्रे Saumitri, रौद्रेण by the fierce, रक्षसा demon, हतम् killed, इमम् this, पतगलोकस्य नाथम् lord of the world of birds, चिताम् funeral pyre, आरोप्य placing, धक्ष्यामि I will cremate with honour.
explanation: O scion of the Raghus  I will place the body of the lord of the world of birds, killed by the fierce demon, on the funeral pyre and crimate him with honour.

shloka_text: या गतिर्यज्ञशीलानामाहिताग्नेश्च या गतिः।।3.68.29।। अपरावर्तिनां या च या च भूमिप्रदायिनाम्। मया त्वं समनुज्ञातो गच्छ लोकाननुत्तमान्।।3.68.30।। गृध्रराज महासत्त्व संस्कृतश्च मया व्रज।
transliteration: yā gatiryajñaśīlānāmāhitāgneśca yā gatiḥ aparāvartināṃ yā ca yā ca bhūmipradāyinām| mayā tvaṃ samanujñāto gaccha lokānanuttamān gṛdhrarāja mahāsattva saṃskṛtaśca mayā vraja|
translation: महासत्त्व very strong, गृध्रराज king of the birds, मया by me, समनुज्ञातः permitted, त्वम् you, यज्ञशीलानाम of those who perform sacrifices, या such, गतिः resort, आहिताग्नेश्च for him who kindles sacrificial fires, या गतिः attainment, अपरावर्तिनाम् of those who beat no retreat (from battle), या च and such state, भूमिप्रदायिनाम् for those who offer land in charity, या च that state, गच्छ go, मया by me, संस्कृतः च purified, अनुत्तमान् best of, लोकान् worlds, व्रज depart.
explanation: O mighty lord of the birds  by my grace attain the state of those who perform sacrifices, who kindle and maintain sacrificial fires, who beat no retreat from the battlefield and who offer land in charity. Purified by my offering of fire, you may depart for the best of the worlds.

shloka_text: या गतिर्यज्ञशीलानामाहिताग्नेश्च या गतिः।।3.68.29।। अपरावर्तिनां या च या च भूमिप्रदायिनाम्। मया त्वं समनुज्ञातो गच्छ लोकाननुत्तमान्।।3.68.30।। गृध्रराज महासत्त्व संस्कृतश्च मया व्रज।
transliteration: yā gatiryajñaśīlānāmāhitāgneśca yā gatiḥ aparāvartināṃ yā ca yā ca bhūmipradāyinām| mayā tvaṃ samanujñāto gaccha lokānanuttamān gṛdhrarāja mahāsattva saṃskṛtaśca mayā vraja|
translation: महासत्त्व very strong, गृध्रराज king of the birds, मया by me, समनुज्ञातः permitted, त्वम् you, यज्ञशीलानाम of those who perform sacrifices, या such, गतिः resort, आहिताग्नेश्च for him who kindles sacrificial fires, या गतिः attainment, अपरावर्तिनाम् of those who beat no retreat (from battle), या च and such state, भूमिप्रदायिनाम् for those who offer land in charity, या च that state, गच्छ go, मया by me, संस्कृतः च purified, अनुत्तमान् best of, लोकान् worlds, व्रज depart.
explanation: O mighty lord of the birds  by my grace attain the state of those who perform sacrifices, who kindle and maintain sacrificial fires, who beat no retreat from the battlefield and who offer land in charity. Purified by my offering of fire, you may depart for the best of the worlds.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा चितां दीप्तामारोप्य पतगेश्वरम्।।3.68.31।। ददाह रामो धर्मात्मा स्वबन्धुमिव दुःखितः।
transliteration: evamuktvā citāṃ dīptāmāropya patageśvaram dadāha rāmo dharmātmā svabandhumiva duḥkhitaḥ|
translation: धर्मात्मा righteous, रामः Rama, एवम् in that way, उक्त्वा having said, पतगेश्वरम् lord of birds, चिताम् on the pyre, आरोप्य having laid, दुःखितः sorrowful, स्वबन्धुमिव like his own relation, ददाह cremated.
explanation: Thus said, righteous Rama laid him on the pyre and sadly cremated the lord of the birds as one would do to his own relative.

shloka_text: रामोऽथ सहसौमित्रिर्वनं गत्वा स वीर्यवान्।।3.68.32।। स्थूलान्हत्वा महारोहीननुतस्तार तं द्विजम्।
transliteration: rāmo'tha sahasaumitrirvanaṃ gatvā sa vīryavān sthūlānhatvā mahārohīnanutastāra taṃ dvijam|
translation: अथ then, वीर्यवान् mighty, रामः Rama, सहसौमित्रिः with Saumitri, वनम् forest, गत्वा after going, स्थूलान् large, महारोहीन् stately deer, हत्वा killed, तं द्विजम् to that bird (Jatayu), अनुतस्तार spread it as offering.
explanation: Then the mighty Rama, accompanied by Saumitri, got into the forest and killed a huge deer, brought it and spread it as an offering (to the dead Jatayu).

shloka_text: रोहिमांसानि चोत्कृत्य पेशीकृत्य महायशाः।।3.68.33।। शकुनाय ददौ रामो रम्ये हरितशाद्वले।
transliteration: rohimāṃsāni cotkṛtya peśīkṛtya mahāyaśāḥ śakunāya dadau rāmo ramye haritaśādvale|
translation: महायशाः famed, रामः Rama, रोहिमांसानि flesh of the deer, उत्कृत्य cutting to pieces, पेशीकृत्य making into balls, रम्ये in a lovely, हरितशाद्वले green, grassy land, शकुनाय the bird Jatayu, ददौ offered.
explanation: Tearing the flesh of the deer to pieces and making them  into balls, the celebrated Rama laid it on a lovely, green grassy land as offering to the bird.

shloka_text: यत्तत्प्रेतस्य मर्त्यस्य कथयन्ति द्विजातयः।।3.68.34।। तत्स्वर्गगमनं तस्य पित्र्यं रामो जजाप ह।
transliteration: yattatpretasya martyasya kathayanti dvijātayaḥ tatsvargagamanaṃ tasya pitryaṃ rāmo jajāpa ha|
translation: तत् that, यत् whatever, द्विजातयः brahmins, प्रेतस्य for the dead, मर्त्यस्य for a mortal, स्वर्गगमनम् for ascending to heaven, कथयन्ति they utter, तत् all that, पित्र्यम् pertaining to father, तस्य that, जजाप muttered.
explanation: Rama muttered the mantras recommended by brahmins for dead mortals as one would do for his father, to help him ascend to heaven.

shloka_text: ततो गोदावरीं गत्वा नदीं नरवरात्मजौ।।3.68.35।। उदकं चक्रतुस्तस्मै गृध्रराजाय तावुभौ।
transliteration: tato godāvarīṃ gatvā nadīṃ naravarātmajau udakaṃ cakratustasmai gṛdhrarājāya tāvubhau|
translation: ततः then, उभौ तौ they both, नरवरात्मजौ two princes, गोदावरीं नदीम् to river Godavari, गत्वा after reaching, तस्मै for him, गृद्रराजाय for the vultureking, उदकम् libations, चक्रतुः offered.
explanation: Then both the princes went down to river Godavari and offered libations for the king of vultures.

shloka_text: शास्त्रदृष्टेन विधिना जले गृध्राय राघवौ।।3.68.36।। स्नात्वा तौ गृध्रराजाय उदकं चक्रतुस्तदा।
transliteration: śāstradṛṣṭena vidhinā jale gṛdhrāya rāghavau snātvā tau gṛdhrarājāya udakaṃ cakratustadā|
translation: तदा thereafter, (तौ) राघवौ both scions of the Raghu dynasty, शास्त्रदृष्टेन as ordained in scriptures, विधिना duly, गृध्राय for the vulture, जले in water, स्नात्वा bathing, गृध्रराजाय to the king of vultures, उदकम् water, चक्रतुः offered.
explanation: Thereafter both the scions of the Raghu dynasty bathed in water, offered libations for the king of vultures as ordained in the scriptures.

shloka_text: स गृध्रराजः कृतवान्यशस्करं सुदुष्करं कर्म रणे निपातितः। महर्षिकल्पेन च संस्कृतस्तदा जगाम पुण्यां गतिमात्मनश्शुभाम्।।3.68.37।।
transliteration: sa gṛdhrarājaḥ kṛtavānyaśaskaraṃ suduṣkaraṃ karma raṇe nipātitaḥ| maharṣikalpena ca saṃskṛtastadā jagāma puṇyāṃ gatimātmanaśśubhām
translation: रणे in battle, सुदुष्करम् very difficult feat, यशस्करम् glorious, कर्म deed, कृतवान् done, निपातितः was made to fall, सः गृध्रराजः that lord of the vultures, तदा then, महर्षिकल्पेन following the prescription of sages, संस्कृतः sanctified, पुण्याम् holy, शुभाम् auspicious, आत्मनः his, गतिम् state, जगाम reached.
explanation: The king of vultures had performed a very difficult and glorious feat by laying down his life fighting. Sanctified by Rama's offering as laid down in scriptures by the seers, he attained a holy, auspicious and divine state of the self.

shloka_text: कृतोदकौ तावपि पक्षिसत्तमे स्थिरां च बुद्धिं प्रणिधाय जग्मतुः। प्रवेश्य सीताधिगमे ततो मनो वनं सुरेन्द्रविव विष्णुवासवौ।।3.68.38।।
transliteration: kṛtodakau tāvapi pakṣisattame sthirāṃ ca buddhiṃ praṇidhāya jagmatuḥ| praveśya sītādhigame tato mano vanaṃ surendraviva viṣṇuvāsavau
translation: तौ अपि they both, कृतोदकौ  offering libation, पक्षिसत्तमे to the great bird, स्थिराम् settled, बुद्धिम् mind, प्रणिधाय employing their attention, ततः then, सीताधिगमे to search Sita, मनः mind, प्रवेश्य  entered , सुरेन्द्रौ like two lords of gods, विष्णुवासवाविव like Visnu and Indra, वनम् forest, जग्मतुः went.
explanation: Rama and Lakshmana, like two lords of gods, Indra and Visnu, offered libations for the great bird with their settled minds and concentrated and then entered deeper into the forest turning their attention to the search for Sita. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे अष्टषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyeighth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: कृत्वैवमुदकं तस्मै प्रस्थितौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। अवेक्षन्तौ वने सीतां पश्चिमां जग्मतुर्दिशम्।।3.69.1।।
transliteration: kṛtvaivamudakaṃ tasmai prasthitau rāmalakṣmaṇau| avekṣantau vane sītāṃ paścimāṃ jagmaturdiśam
translation: एवम् thus, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, तस्मै for him, उदकं कृत्वा after offering libation, प्रस्थितौ both started, पश्चिमाम् westward, दिशम् direction, वने in the forest, सीताम् Sita, अवेक्षन्तौ while both searching and looking, जग्मतुः went .
explanation: Rama and Lakshmana offered libations (for Jatayu) and went westward, looking for Sita in the forest.
comments: Rama and Lakshmana proceed to search Sita -- Lakshmana punishes Ayomukhi -- Kabandha seizes Rama and Lakshmana -- Rama's lamentations at the calamity -- Lakshmana gets unnerved

shloka_text: तौ दिशं दक्षिणां गत्वा शरचापासिधारिणौ। अविप्रहतमैक्ष्वाकौ पन्थानं प्रतिपेदतुः।।3.69.2।।
transliteration: tau diśaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ gatvā śaracāpāsidhāriṇau| aviprahatamaikṣvākau panthānaṃ pratipedatuḥ
translation: शरचापासिधारिणौ wielding bows, arrows and swords, तौ both, ऐक्ष्वाकौ two princes of the Ikshvaku race, (ताम् that), दक्षिणाम् southward, दिशम् direction, गत्वा went, अविप्रहतम् untrodden, पन्थानम् path, प्रतिपेदतुः reached.
explanation: Wielding bow, arrows and sword, both the princes of the Ikshvaku race went southward and entered an untrodden (densely wooded) tract.

shloka_text: गुल्मैर्वृक्षैश्च बहुभिर्लताभिश्च प्रवेष्टितम्। आवृतं सर्वतो दुर्गं गहनं घोरदर्शनम्।।3.69.3।।
transliteration: gulmairvṛkṣaiśca bahubhirlatābhiśca praveṣṭitam| āvṛtaṃ sarvato durgaṃ gahanaṃ ghoradarśanam
translation: बहुभिः by many, गुल्मैः by shrubs, वृक्षैश्च and  by trees, लताभिश्च and by creepers, प्रवेष्टितम् overgrown, सर्वतः all over, आवृतम् covered, दुर्गम् difficult to reach, गहनम् impenetrable, घोरदर्शनम् appearing ferocious
explanation: It was a dense, impenetrable and dreadful forest covered with shrubs, trees and creepers spread all over.

shloka_text: व्यतिक्रम्य तु वेगेन व्यालसिंहनिषेवितम्। सुभीमं तन्महारण्यं व्यतियातौ महाबलौ।।3.69.4।।
transliteration: vyatikramya tu vegena vyālasiṃhaniṣevitam| subhīmaṃ tanmahāraṇyaṃ vyatiyātau mahābalau
translation: महाबलौ two mighty princes, व्यालसिंहनिषेवितम् where serperts and lions dwell, सुभीमम् very fierceful, तत् that, महारण्यम् great forest, वेगेन swiftly, व्यतिक्रम्य after forging through, व्यतियातौ  both crossed over.
explanation: The two mighty heroes swiftly forged through the great forest, which was an abode of serpents and lions.

shloka_text: ततः परं जनस्थानातत्रिक्रोशं गम्य राघवौ। क्रौञ्चारण्यं विविशतुर्गहनं तौ महौजसौ।।3.69.5।।
transliteration: tataḥ paraṃ janasthānātatrikrośaṃ gamya rāghavau| krauñcāraṇyaṃ viviśaturgahanaṃ tau mahaujasau
translation: ततः then, परम् later, महौजसौ mighty, तौ they both, राघवौ two scions of the Raghus, जनस्थानात् from Janasthana, त्रिक्रोशम् three krosas distance (one krosa  2 miles), गम्य after going, गहनम् impassable, क्रौञ्चारण्यम् kraunchaforest, विविशतुः entered.
explanation: Both the mighty princes of the Raghu dynasty covered a distance of three krosas from Janasthana and entered the impassable kraunchaforest.

shloka_text: नानामेघघनप्रख्यं प्रहृष्टमिव सर्वतः। नानापक्षिगणैर्युक्तं नानाव्यालमृगैर्युतम्।।3.69.6।। दिदृक्षमाणौ वैदेहीं तद्वनं तौ विचिक्यतुः। तत्र तत्रावतिष्ठन्तौ सीताहरणकर्शितौ।।3.69.7।।
transliteration: nānāmeghaghanaprakhyaṃ prahṛṣṭamiva sarvataḥ| nānāpakṣigaṇairyuktaṃ nānāvyālamṛgairyutam didṛkṣamāṇau vaidehīṃ tadvanaṃ tau vicikyatuḥ| tatra tatrāvatiṣṭhantau sītāharaṇakarśitau
translation: सीताहरणकर्शितौ both tormented  by the abduction of Sita, तौ they two, वैदेहीम् Vaidehi, दिदृक्षमाणौ eager to see, तत्र there, अवतिष्ठन्तौ both stopping a while, नानामेघघनप्रख्यम्  looking like dense clouds, सर्वतः all over, प्रहृष्टमिव as if it was over joyed, नानापक्षिगणैः with different birds, युक्तम्  filled, नानाव्यालमृगैः by various snakes and animals, युतम् filled with, तत् that, वनम् forest, विचिक्यतुः they both searched.
explanation: Tormented due to abduction of Sita, the two princes anxious to see her searched all over the dense forest stopping here and there on the way. The thick forest looked like a conglomeration of big clouds. It was filled with different kinds of birds, snakes and animals.

shloka_text: नानामेघघनप्रख्यं प्रहृष्टमिव सर्वतः। नानापक्षिगणैर्युक्तं नानाव्यालमृगैर्युतम्।।3.69.6।। दिदृक्षमाणौ वैदेहीं तद्वनं तौ विचिक्यतुः। तत्र तत्रावतिष्ठन्तौ सीताहरणकर्शितौ।।3.69.7।।
transliteration: nānāmeghaghanaprakhyaṃ prahṛṣṭamiva sarvataḥ| nānāpakṣigaṇairyuktaṃ nānāvyālamṛgairyutam didṛkṣamāṇau vaidehīṃ tadvanaṃ tau vicikyatuḥ| tatra tatrāvatiṣṭhantau sītāharaṇakarśitau
translation: सीताहरणकर्शितौ both tormented  by the abduction of Sita, तौ they two, वैदेहीम् Vaidehi, दिदृक्षमाणौ eager to see, तत्र there, अवतिष्ठन्तौ both stopping a while, नानामेघघनप्रख्यम्  looking like dense clouds, सर्वतः all over, प्रहृष्टमिव as if it was over joyed, नानापक्षिगणैः with different birds, युक्तम्  filled, नानाव्यालमृगैः by various snakes and animals, युतम् filled with, तत् that, वनम् forest, विचिक्यतुः they both searched.
explanation: Tormented due to abduction of Sita, the two princes anxious to see her searched all over the dense forest stopping here and there on the way. The thick forest looked like a conglomeration of big clouds. It was filled with different kinds of birds, snakes and animals.

shloka_text: ततः पूर्वेण तौ गत्वा त्रिक्रोशं भ्रातरौ तदा। क्रौञ्चारण्यमतिक्रम्य मतङ्गाश्रममन्तरा।।3.69.8।। दृष्ट्वा तु तद्वनं घोरं बहुभीममृगद्विजम्। ननासत्त्वसमाकीर्णं सर्वं गहनपादपम्।।3.69.9।। ददृशाते तु तौ तत्र दरीं दशरथात्मजौ। पातालसमगम्भीरां तमसा नित्यसंवृताम्।।3.69.10।।
transliteration: tataḥ pūrveṇa tau gatvā trikrośaṃ bhrātarau tadā| krauñcāraṇyamatikramya mataṅgāśramamantarā dṛṣṭvā tu tadvanaṃ ghoraṃ bahubhīmamṛgadvijam| nanāsattvasamākīrṇaṃ sarvaṃ gahanapādapam dadṛśāte tu tau tatra darīṃ daśarathātmajau| pātālasamagambhīrāṃ tamasā nityasaṃvṛtām
translation: तदा then, भ्रातरौ the two brothers, तौ दशरथात्मजौ the two sons of Dasaratha, ततः then, पूर्वेण by eastern direction, त्रिक्रोशम् three krosas distance, गत्वा went, क्रौञ्चारण्यम्  kraunchaforest, अतिक्रम्य  crossed, मतङ्गाश्रमम् अन्तरा near the hermitage of sage Matanga, घोरम् terrific, बहुभीममृगद्विजम् filled with fearful beasts and birds, नानासत्त्वसमाकीर्णम् teeming with different kinds of creatures, गहनपादपम् dense trees, सर्वम् all, तत् that, वनम् forest, दृष्ट्वा seeing, तत्र there, (गिरौ  on the hill), पातालसमगम्भीराम् deep like the nether world, तमसा darkness, नित्यसंवृताम् always filled with, दरीम् cave, ददृशाते both saw.
explanation: Then both the sons of Dasaratha, went further east, crossed the kraunchaforest after three krosas. They saw a dreadful forest which was full of fierce animals and birds near the hermitage of sage Matanga. It was densely covered with trees. They saw there a cave perpetually enveloped in darkness which was as deep as the netherworld.

translation: तदा then, भ्रातरौ the two brothers, तौ दशरथात्मजौ the two sons of Dasaratha, ततः then, पूर्वेण by eastern direction, त्रिक्रोशम् three krosas distance, गत्वा went, क्रौञ्चारण्यम्  kraunchaforest, अतिक्रम्य  crossed, मतङ्गाश्रमम् अन्तरा near the hermitage of sage Matanga, घोरम् terrific, बहुभीममृगद्विजम् filled with fearful beasts and birds, नानासत्त्वसमाकीर्णम् teeming with different kinds of creatures, गहनपादपम् dense trees, सर्वम् all, तत् that, वनम् forest, दृष्ट्वा seeing, तत्र there, (गिरौ  on the hill), पातालसमगम्भीराम् deep like the nether world, तमसा darkness, नित्यसंवृताम् always filled with, दरीम् cave, ददृशाते both saw.
explanation: Then both the sons of Dasaratha, went further east, crossed the kraunchaforest after three krosas. They saw a dreadful forest which was full of fierce animals and birds near the hermitage of sage Matanga. It was densely covered with trees. They saw there a cave perpetually enveloped in darkness which was as deep as the netherworld.

translation: तदा then, भ्रातरौ the two brothers, तौ दशरथात्मजौ the two sons of Dasaratha, ततः then, पूर्वेण by eastern direction, त्रिक्रोशम् three krosas distance, गत्वा went, क्रौञ्चारण्यम्  kraunchaforest, अतिक्रम्य  crossed, मतङ्गाश्रमम् अन्तरा near the hermitage of sage Matanga, घोरम् terrific, बहुभीममृगद्विजम् filled with fearful beasts and birds, नानासत्त्वसमाकीर्णम् teeming with different kinds of creatures, गहनपादपम् dense trees, सर्वम् all, तत् that, वनम् forest, दृष्ट्वा seeing, तत्र there, (गिरौ  on the hill), पातालसमगम्भीराम् deep like the nether world, तमसा darkness, नित्यसंवृताम् always filled with, दरीम् cave, ददृशाते both saw.
explanation: Then both the sons of Dasaratha, went further east, crossed the kraunchaforest after three krosas. They saw a dreadful forest which was full of fierce animals and birds near the hermitage of sage Matanga. It was densely covered with trees. They saw there a cave perpetually enveloped in darkness which was as deep as the netherworld.

shloka_text: आसाद्य तौ नरव्याघ्रौ दर्यास्तस्याविदूरतः। ददृशाते महारूपां राक्षसीं विकृताननाम्।।3.69.11।।
transliteration: āsādya tau naravyāghrau daryāstasyāvidūrataḥ| dadṛśāte mahārūpāṃ rākṣasīṃ vikṛtānanām
translation: तौ  both of them, नरव्याघ्रौ best among men, आसाद्य  reached, तस्याः from that, दर्याः from the cave, विदूरतः not very far from that place, महारूपाम् a woman of huge size, विकृताननाम् a woman of disfigured face, राक्षसीम् demoness, ददृशाते both saw.
explanation: Both the princes,the best among men, reached the cave and saw a huge demoness with a disfigured face not far from the cave.

shloka_text: भयदामल्पसत्त्वानां बीभत्सां रौद्रदर्शनाम्। लम्बोदरीं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रां करालीं परुषत्वचम्।।3.69.12।। भक्षयन्तीं मृगान्भीमान्विकटां मुक्तमूर्धजाम्। प्रैक्षेतां तौ ततस्तत्र भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।।3.69.13।।
transliteration: bhayadāmalpasattvānāṃ bībhatsāṃ raudradarśanām| lambodarīṃ tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāṃ karālīṃ paruṣatvacam bhakṣayantīṃ mṛgānbhīmānvikaṭāṃ muktamūrdhajām| praikṣetāṃ tau tatastatra bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
translation: ततः then, भ्रातरौ both brothers, तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ both Rama and Lakshmana, अल्पसत्त्वानाम् for the timid, भयदाम् one creating fear, बीभत्साम् a woman of uncouth appearance, रौद्रदर्शनाम्    a woman of terrific appearance, लम्बोदरीम् a woman of big stomach, तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्राम् a woman with sharp teeth, करालीम् terrific woman, भीमान् fearful, मृगान् animals, भक्षयन्तीम् was eating, विकटाम् who had huge curved skins, मुक्तमूर्धजाम् a woman with hair spread out, तत्र there, प्रैक्षेताम् saw.
explanation: Then the two brothers saw a fearful demoness who could strike terror in the mind of the timid, an uncouth figure with huge curved skins, with a big stomach, dishevelled hair, sharp and long teeth, devouring wild animals.

shloka_text: भयदामल्पसत्त्वानां बीभत्सां रौद्रदर्शनाम्। लम्बोदरीं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रां करालीं परुषत्वचम्।।3.69.12।। भक्षयन्तीं मृगान्भीमान्विकटां मुक्तमूर्धजाम्। प्रैक्षेतां तौ ततस्तत्र भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।।3.69.13।।
transliteration: bhayadāmalpasattvānāṃ bībhatsāṃ raudradarśanām| lambodarīṃ tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāṃ karālīṃ paruṣatvacam bhakṣayantīṃ mṛgānbhīmānvikaṭāṃ muktamūrdhajām| praikṣetāṃ tau tatastatra bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
translation: ततः then, भ्रातरौ both brothers, तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ both Rama and Lakshmana, अल्पसत्त्वानाम् for the timid, भयदाम् one creating fear, बीभत्साम् a woman of uncouth appearance, रौद्रदर्शनाम्    a woman of terrific appearance, लम्बोदरीम् a woman of big stomach, तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्राम् a woman with sharp teeth, करालीम् terrific woman, भीमान् fearful, मृगान् animals, भक्षयन्तीम् was eating, विकटाम् who had huge curved skins, मुक्तमूर्धजाम् a woman with hair spread out, तत्र there, प्रैक्षेताम् saw.
explanation: Then the two brothers saw a fearful demoness who could strike terror in the mind of the timid, an uncouth figure with huge curved skins, with a big stomach, dishevelled hair, sharp and long teeth, devouring wild animals.

shloka_text: सा समासाद्य तौ वीरौ व्रजन्तं भ्रातुरग्रतः। एहि रंस्यावहेत्युक्त्वा समालम्बत लक्ष्मणम्।।3.69.14।।
transliteration: sā samāsādya tau vīrau vrajantaṃ bhrāturagrataḥ| ehi raṃsyāvahetyuktvā samālambata lakṣmaṇam
translation: सा she, वीरौ both heroes, तौ both, समासाद्य  coming close, एहि come on, रंस्यावहे we will both sport and enjoy sex, इति thus, उक्त्वा said, भ्रातुः brother's, अग्रतः in front of, व्रजन्तम् moving, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, समालम्बत held.
explanation: She came close to them, held Lakshmana who was walking ahead of his brother and said Come, let us enjoy.

shloka_text: उवाच चैनं वचनं सौमित्रिमुपगूह्य सा। अहं त्वयोमुखी नाम लब्धा ते त्वमसि प्रियः।।3.69.15।। नाथ पर्वतकूटेषु नदीनां पुलिनेषु च। आयुश्शेषमिमं वीर त्वं मया सह रंस्यसे।।3.69.16।।
transliteration: uvāca cainaṃ vacanaṃ saumitrimupagūhya sā| ahaṃ tvayomukhī nāma labdhā te tvamasi priyaḥ nātha parvatakūṭeṣu nadīnāṃ pulineṣu ca| āyuśśeṣamimaṃ vīra tvaṃ mayā saha raṃsyase
translation: सा she, सौमित्रिम् to Saumitri, उपगुह्य took hold of, एनम् him, वचनम् words, उवाच च spoke, अहं तु I am, अयोमुखी नाम Ayomukhi by name, ते to you, लब्धा obtained by you, त्वम् him, प्रियः dear, वीर hero, नाथ lord, इमम् this, आयुःशेषम् rest of your  life, त्वम् you, मया सह with me, पर्वतकूटेषु on the lofty hills, नदीनाम् पुलिनेषु  च on the river banks, रंस्यसे you will enjoy.
explanation: Taking hold of Saumitri the demoness said 'I am Ayomukhi and I have been obtained by you. You got me, O hero, O lord  For the rest of your life you will sport with me on the lofty hills and river banks.'

shloka_text: उवाच चैनं वचनं सौमित्रिमुपगूह्य सा। अहं त्वयोमुखी नाम लब्धा ते त्वमसि प्रियः।।3.69.15।। नाथ पर्वतकूटेषु नदीनां पुलिनेषु च। आयुश्शेषमिमं वीर त्वं मया सह रंस्यसे।।3.69.16।।
transliteration: uvāca cainaṃ vacanaṃ saumitrimupagūhya sā| ahaṃ tvayomukhī nāma labdhā te tvamasi priyaḥ nātha parvatakūṭeṣu nadīnāṃ pulineṣu ca| āyuśśeṣamimaṃ vīra tvaṃ mayā saha raṃsyase
translation: सा she, सौमित्रिम् to Saumitri, उपगुह्य took hold of, एनम् him, वचनम् words, उवाच च spoke, अहं तु I am, अयोमुखी नाम Ayomukhi by name, ते to you, लब्धा obtained by you, त्वम् him, प्रियः dear, वीर hero, नाथ lord, इमम् this, आयुःशेषम् rest of your  life, त्वम् you, मया सह with me, पर्वतकूटेषु on the lofty hills, नदीनाम् पुलिनेषु  च on the river banks, रंस्यसे you will enjoy.
explanation: Taking hold of Saumitri the demoness said 'I am Ayomukhi and I have been obtained by you. You got me, O hero, O lord  For the rest of your life you will sport with me on the lofty hills and river banks.'

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु कुपितः खड्गमुद्धृत्य लक्ष्मणः। कर्णनासास्तनं तस्या निचकर्तारिसूदनः।।3.69.17।।
transliteration: evamuktastu kupitaḥ khaḍgamuddhṛtya lakṣmaṇaḥ| karṇanāsāstanaṃ tasyā nicakartārisūdanaḥ
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः having been told, अरिसूदनः subduer of enemies, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, कुपितः became angry, खड्गम् sword, उद्धृत्य after lifting, तस्याः her, कर्णनासास्तनम् ears, nose and breasts, चकर्त cut off.
explanation: Thus addressed, Lakshmana, subduer of enemies, became angry, took out the sword and cut off her ears, nose and breasts.

shloka_text: कर्णनासे निकृत्ते तु विस्वरं सा विनद्य च। यथागतं प्रदुद्राव राक्षसी भीमदर्शना।।3.69.18।।
transliteration: karṇanāse nikṛtte tu visvaraṃ sā vinadya ca| yathāgataṃ pradudrāva rākṣasī bhīmadarśanā
translation: भीमदर्शना a woman of frightening appearance, सा राक्षसी that demoness, कर्णनासे ears and nose, निकृत्ते when they were cut, विस्वरम् with cracked voice, विनद्य after shouting, यथागतम् in the same way as she came, प्रदुद्राव ran away.
explanation: When the ears and nose of the frightening demoness were cut off she shouted in a fierce tone and ran away in the direction she had come from.

shloka_text: तस्यां गतायां गहनं व्रजन्तौ वनमोजसा। आसेदतुरमित्रघ्नौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।।3.69.19।।
transliteration: tasyāṃ gatāyāṃ gahanaṃ vrajantau vanamojasā| āsedaturamitraghnau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
translation: तस्याम् when she, गतायाम् went away, व्रजन्तौ as both were advancing, भ्रातरौ two brothers, अमित्रघ्नौ both being destroyers of enemies, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, ओजसा with their might, गहनम् dense, वनम् woods, आसेदतुः reached.
explanation: The destroyers of enemies, Rama and Lakshmana of great valour went through the dense forest after she ran away.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्तु महातेजास्सत्त्ववान् शीलवान् शुचिः। अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं भ्रातरं दीप्ततेजसम्।।3.69.20।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇastu mahātejāssattvavān śīlavān śuciḥ| abravītprāñjalirvākyaṃ bhrātaraṃ dīptatejasam
