shloka_text: कोटीसहस्रैर्दशभिः श्रीमान्परिवृतस्तदा। वीरश्शतवलिर्नाम वानरः प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.14।।
transliteration: koṭīsahasrairdaśabhiḥ śrīmānparivṛtastadā| vīraśśatavalirnāma vānaraḥ pratyadṛśyata
translation: तदा then, दशभिः by ten, कोटीसहस्रैः thousand crores, परिवृतः accompanied by, श्रीमान् glorious, वीरः warrior, शतवलिर्नाम named Satavali, वानरः monkey, प्रत्यदृश्यत appeared on the site.
explanation: Then appeared the glorious warrior named Satavali, followed by ten thousand crore of monkeys.

shloka_text: ततः काञ्चनशैलाभस्ताराया वीर्यवान्पिता। अनेकैर्दशसाहस्रैः कोटिभिः प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.15।।
transliteration: tataḥ kāñcanaśailābhastārāyā vīryavānpitā| anekairdaśasāhasraiḥ koṭibhiḥ pratyadṛśyata
translation: ततः then, काञ्चनशैलाभः appearing like the golden mountain (Meru), वीर्यवान् valiant, पिता father, दशसाहस्रैः by ten thousand, कोटिभिः by crores, अनेकैः and many, प्रत्यदृश्यत appeared with, ताराया Tara's.
explanation: (Next came) the valiant father of Tara of golden complexion like mount Meru followed by ten thousand crore of vanaras.

shloka_text: तथाऽपरेण कोटीनां सहस्रेण समन्वितः। पिता रुमाया सम्प्राप्तस्सुग्रीवश्वशुरो विभुः।।4.39.16।।
transliteration: tathā'pareṇa koṭīnāṃ sahasreṇa samanvitaḥ| pitā rumāyā samprāptassugrīvaśvaśuro vibhuḥ
translation: तथा likewise, विभुः mighty one, रुमायाः पिता father of Ruma, सुग्रीवश्वशुरः king Sugriva's fatherinlaw, अपरेण by another, कोटीनाम् by a crore, सहस्रेण thousand, समन्वितः accompanied with, सम्प्राप्तः reached.
explanation: Likewise mighty father of Ruma, fatherinlaw of Sugriva, reached there accompanied by a thousand crore monkeys.

shloka_text: पद्मकेसरसङ्काशस्तरुणार्कनिभाननः। बुद्धिमान्वानरश्रेष्ठस्सर्ववानरसत्तमः।।4.39.17।। अनेकैर्बहुसाहस्रैर्वानराणां समन्वितः। पिता हनुमतश्रशीमान्केसरी प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.18।।
transliteration: padmakesarasaṅkāśastaruṇārkanibhānanaḥ| buddhimānvānaraśreṣṭhassarvavānarasattamaḥ anekairbahusāhasrairvānarāṇāṃ samanvitaḥ| pitā hanumataśraśīmānkesarī pratyadṛśyata
translation: पद्मकेसरसङ्काशः like lotus filaments in colour, तरुणार्कनिभाननः with the countenance red like the early morning Sun, बुद्धिमान् wise, वानरश्रेष्ठः foremost of vanaras, सर्ववानरसत्तमः the best among vanaras, हनुमतः Hanuman's, पिता father, श्रीमान् prosperous, केसरी Kesari, वानराणाम् of vanaras, अनेकैः many, बहुसाहस्रैः by many thousands, समन्वितः accompanied by, प्रत्यदृश्यत appeared.
explanation: Then arrived Kesari, the wise and illustrious monkey, foremost and the best among vanaras, father of Hanuman. He was of the colour of lotus filaments and his countenance was red like the early morning Sun. He was accompanied by many thousands of monkeys.

shloka_text: पद्मकेसरसङ्काशस्तरुणार्कनिभाननः। बुद्धिमान्वानरश्रेष्ठस्सर्ववानरसत्तमः।।4.39.17।। अनेकैर्बहुसाहस्रैर्वानराणां समन्वितः। पिता हनुमतश्रशीमान्केसरी प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.18।।
transliteration: padmakesarasaṅkāśastaruṇārkanibhānanaḥ| buddhimānvānaraśreṣṭhassarvavānarasattamaḥ anekairbahusāhasrairvānarāṇāṃ samanvitaḥ| pitā hanumataśraśīmānkesarī pratyadṛśyata
translation: पद्मकेसरसङ्काशः like lotus filaments in colour, तरुणार्कनिभाननः with the countenance red like the early morning Sun, बुद्धिमान् wise, वानरश्रेष्ठः foremost of vanaras, सर्ववानरसत्तमः the best among vanaras, हनुमतः Hanuman's, पिता father, श्रीमान् prosperous, केसरी Kesari, वानराणाम् of vanaras, अनेकैः many, बहुसाहस्रैः by many thousands, समन्वितः accompanied by, प्रत्यदृश्यत appeared.
explanation: Then arrived Kesari, the wise and illustrious monkey, foremost and the best among vanaras, father of Hanuman. He was of the colour of lotus filaments and his countenance was red like the early morning Sun. He was accompanied by many thousands of monkeys.

shloka_text: गोलाङ्गूलमहाराजो गवाक्षो भीमविक्रमः। वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण वानराणामदृश्यत।।4.39.19।।
transliteration: golāṅgūlamahārājo gavākṣo bhīmavikramaḥ| vṛtaḥ koṭisahasreṇa vānarāṇāmadṛśyata
translation: वानराणाम् of vanaras, कोटिसहस्रेण by a thousand crores, वृतः surrounded, गोलाङ्गूलमहाराजः king of Langur, भीमविक्रमः a warrior of fierce valour, गवाक्षः Gavaksha, अदृश्यत was seen
explanation: Next arrived Gavaksha, king of Langurs (whose tail resembled the cow's), of fierceful courage surrounded by a thousand crore of vanaras.

shloka_text: ऋक्षाणां भीमवेगानां धूम्रश्शत्रुनिबर्हणः। वृतः कोटिसहस्राभ्यां द्वाभ्यां समभिवर्तत।।4.39.20।।
transliteration: ṛkṣāṇāṃ bhīmavegānāṃ dhūmraśśatrunibarhaṇaḥ| vṛtaḥ koṭisahasrābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ samabhivartata
translation: शत्रुनिबर्हणः destroyer of enemies, धूम्रः Dhumra, भीमवेगानाम् of those of frightening speed, ऋक्षाणाम् of bears, द्वाभ्याम् with two, कोटिसहस्राभ्याम् thousand crores, समभिवर्तत arrived there.
explanation: Dhumra, destroyer of enemies, came next followed by two thousand crore of bears of terrible speed.

shloka_text: महाचलनिभैर्घोरै: पनसो नाम यूथपः। आजगाम महावीर्यस्तिसृभिः कोटिभिर्वृतः।।4.39.21।।
transliteration: mahācalanibhairghorai: panaso nāma yūthapaḥ| ājagāma mahāvīryastisṛbhiḥ koṭibhirvṛtaḥ
translation: पनसो नाम Panasa by name, महावीर्यः a great warrior, यूथपः troop leader, तिसृभिः कोटिभिः by three crores, महाचलनिभैः by those resembling huge mountains, घोरैः by a dreadful one, वृतः surrounded by, आजगाम came.
explanation: Similarly, the great warrior named Panasa, leader of the troop, reported with three crore dreadful vanaras of the size of huge mountains.

shloka_text: नीलाञ्जनचयाकारो नीलो नामाऽथ यूथपः। अदृश्यत महाकायः कोटिभिर्दशभिर्वृतः।।4.39.22।।
transliteration: nīlāñjanacayākāro nīlo nāmā'tha yūthapaḥ| adṛśyata mahākāyaḥ koṭibhirdaśabhirvṛtaḥ
translation: अथ then, दशभिः कोटिभिः by ten crore, वृतः surrounded, नीलाञ्जनचयाकारः dark like a mountain of collyrium, महाकायः of huge body, नीलो नाम by name Nila, यूथपः leader, अदृश्यत appeared.
explanation: Then appeared Nila of huge body, dark like a mountain of collyrium accompanied by ten crore vanaras.

shloka_text: ततः काञ्चनशैलाभो गवयो नाम यूथपः। आजगाम महावीर्यः पञ्चभि: कोटिभिर्वृतः।।4.39.23।।
transliteration: tataḥ kāñcanaśailābho gavayo nāma yūthapaḥ| ājagāma mahāvīryaḥ pañcabhi: koṭibhirvṛtaḥ
translation: ततः then, काञ्चनशैलाभः appearing like golden mountain, महावीर्यः a great warrior, गवयो नाम Gavaya by name, यूथपः leader of a group, पञ्चभिः कोटिभिः by five crores, वृतः surrounded, आजगाम arrived.
explanation: Then arrived the leader of five crore vanaras, the great warrior Gavaya who resembled a golden mountain.

shloka_text: दरीमुखश्च बलवान्यूथपोऽभ्याययौ तदा। वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण सुग्रीवं समुपस्थितः।।4.39.24।।
transliteration: darīmukhaśca balavānyūthapo'bhyāyayau tadā| vṛtaḥ koṭisahasreṇa sugrīvaṃ samupasthitaḥ
translation: तदा then, बलवान् strong, दरीमुखः Darimukha, यूथपः leader, कोटिसहस्रेण with one thousand crores, वृतः surrounded, अभ्याययौ came near, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, समुपस्थितः approached.
explanation: Then the strong Darimukha, leader of a thousand crore monkeys approached Sugriva.

shloka_text: मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभावश्विपुत्रौ महाबलौ। कोटिकोटिसहस्रेण वानराणामदृश्यताम्।।4.39.25।।
transliteration: maindaśca dvividaścobhāvaśviputrau mahābalau| koṭikoṭisahasreṇa vānarāṇāmadṛśyatām
translation: महाबलौ two very powerful, अश्विपुत्रौ two sons of Asvi, मैन्दश्च Mainda, द्विविदश्च Dvivida, उभौ both, वानराणाम् vanaras, कोटिकोटिसहस्रेण by a thousand crores, अदृश्यताम् appeared.
explanation: Two very powerful sons of Asvini, Mainda and Dvivida, appeared with a thousand crore vanaras.

shloka_text: गजश्च बलवान् वीर: कोटिभिस्तिसृभिर्वृतः। आजगाम महातेजा सुग्रीवस्य समीपतः।।4.39.26।।
transliteration: gajaśca balavān vīra: koṭibhistisṛbhirvṛtaḥ| ājagāma mahātejā sugrīvasya samīpataḥ
translation: बलवान् stout, वीरः hero, महातेजाः mighty, गजश्च Gaja also, तिसृभिः कोटिभिः with three crores of vanaras, वृतः surrounded by, सुग्रीवस्य of Sugriva, समीपतः presence, आजगाम reached.
explanation: Strong and powerful Gaja also reached Sugriva with three crore vanaras.

shloka_text: ऋक्षराजो महातेजा जाम्बवान्नाम नामतः। कोटिभिर्दशभिः प्राप्तः सुग्रीवस्य वशे स्थितः।।4.39.27।।
transliteration: ṛkṣarājo mahātejā jāmbavānnāma nāmataḥ| koṭibhirdaśabhiḥ prāptaḥ sugrīvasya vaśe sthitaḥ
translation: महातेजाः glorious, नामतः by name, जाम्बवान् नाम called Jambavan, ऋक्षराजः king of bears, दशभिः ten, कोटिभि with crores, प्राप्तः got, सुग्रीवस्य to Sugriva, वशे under control, स्थितः stood.
explanation: Glorious Jambavan, king of bears, stood before Sugriva with ten thousand crore vanaras.

shloka_text: रुमण्वान्नाम विक्रान्तो वानरो वानरेश्वरम्। आययौ बलवांस्तूर्णं कोटीशतसमावृतः।।4.39.28।।
transliteration: rumaṇvānnāma vikrānto vānaro vānareśvaram| āyayau balavāṃstūrṇaṃ koṭīśatasamāvṛtaḥ
translation: विक्रान्तः victorious, वानरैः with vanaras, वृतः surrounded by, बलवान् sturdy, रुमण्वन्नाम  called Rumanvan, कोटीशतसमावृतः surrounded by hundred crores of vanaras, तूर्णम् swiftly, समावृतः came and assembled.
explanation: Sturdy and victorious vanara called Rumanvan came swiftly followed by a hundred crore vanaras.

shloka_text: ततः कोटिसहस्राणां सहस्रेण शतेन च। पृष्ठतोऽनुगतः प्राप्तो हरिभिर्गन्धमादनः।।4.39.29।।
transliteration: tataḥ koṭisahasrāṇāṃ sahasreṇa śatena ca| pṛṣṭhato'nugataḥ prāpto haribhirgandhamādanaḥ
translation: ततः then, कोटिसहस्राणाम् of a thousand crore, सहस्रेण by a thousand, शतेन च by a hundred also, वानरैः with vanara, पृष्ठतः behind him, अनुगतः followed, गन्धमादन: Gandhamadana, प्राप्तः came.
explanation: Then came Gandhamadana with a hundred thousand crore of vanaras following him.

shloka_text: ततः पद्मसहस्रेण वृतश्शङ्कुशतेन च। युवराजोऽङ्गदः प्राप्तः पितृतुल्यपराक्रमः।।4.39.30।।
transliteration: tataḥ padmasahasreṇa vṛtaśśaṅkuśatena ca| yuvarājo'ṅgadaḥ prāptaḥ pitṛtulyaparākramaḥ
translation: ततः then, पितुः तुल्यपराक्रमः comparable in prowess to his father, युवराजः heir apparent, अङ्गदः Angada, पद्मसहस्रेण with a thousand Padmas (trillion), शङ्कुशतेन च one hundred times Sanku (ten trillion), वृतः surrounded, प्राप्तः arrived.
explanation: Then arrived the heir apparent, Angada, whose prowess is comparable to that of his father with him came a thousand padmas and a hundred sankus of followers.

shloka_text: ततस्ताराद्युतिस्तारो हरिर्भीमपराक्रमः। पञ्चभिर्हरिकोटीभिर्दूरतः प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.31।।
transliteration: tatastārādyutistāro harirbhīmaparākramaḥ| pañcabhirharikoṭībhirdūrataḥ pratyadṛśyata
translation: ततः then, ताराद्युतिः shining like a star, भीमपराक्रमः a warrior of terrific valour, तारः Tara, हरिः vanara, पञ्चभिः with five, हरिकोटीभिः with crores of vanaras, दूरतः at a distance, प्रत्यदृश्यत was seen.
explanation: And Tara (brother of Ruma's father) of terrific valour shining like a star showed up at a distance with five crore vanaras.

shloka_text: इन्द्रजानुः कपिर्वीरो यूथपः प्रत्यदृश्यत। एकादशानां कोटीनामीश्वरस्तैस्समावृतः।।4.39.32।।
transliteration: indrajānuḥ kapirvīro yūthapaḥ pratyadṛśyata| ekādaśānāṃ koṭīnāmīśvarastaissamāvṛtaḥ
translation: एकादशानां कोटीनाम् of eleven crores of vanaras, ईश्वरः chief, वीरःhero, यूथपः leader of troop, इन्द्रजानुः Indrajanu, कपिः vanara, तैः with them, समावृतः surrounded, प्रत्यदृश्यत appeared.
explanation: Then Indrajanu the troop leader and chief of vanaras appeared along with eleven crore monkeys.

shloka_text: ततो रम्भस्त्वनुप्राप्तस्तरुणादित्यसन्निभः। अयुतेनावृतश्चैव सहस्रेण शतेन च।।4.39.33।।
transliteration: tato rambhastvanuprāptastaruṇādityasannibhaḥ| ayutenāvṛtaścaiva sahasreṇa śatena ca
translation: ततः thereafter, तरुणादित्यसन्निभः of the colour of the rising Sun, रम्भः Rambha, अयुतेना by one ayuta (10,000), सहस्रेण by a thousand, शतेन च by a hundred, वृतः surrounded, अनुप्राप्तः arrived
explanation: Thereafter Rambha of the colour of the rising Sun brought together an army of one thousand and one hundred ayuta troops.

shloka_text: ततो यूथपतिर्वीरो दुर्मुखो नाम वानरः। प्रत्यदृश्यत कोटीभ्यां द्वाभ्यां परिवृतो बली।।4.39.34।।
transliteration: tato yūthapatirvīro durmukho nāma vānaraḥ| pratyadṛśyata koṭībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ parivṛto balī
translation: ततः thereafter, यूथपतिः leader of the troop, वीरः hero, बली strong one, दुर्मुखो नाम Durmukha by name, वानरः vanara, द्वाभ्याम् with two, कोटीभ्याम् with crores, परिवृतः surrounded, प्रत्यदृश्यत appeared.
explanation: Thereafter the mighty hero, leader of the troop, by name Durmukha appeared with  two crore vanaras.

shloka_text: कैलासशिखराकारैर्वानरैर्भीमविक्रमैः। वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण हनुमान्प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.35।।
transliteration: kailāsaśikharākārairvānarairbhīmavikramaiḥ| vṛtaḥ koṭisahasreṇa hanumānpratyadṛśyata
translation: हनुमान् Hanuman, कैलासशिखराकारैः with those like the peaks of Kailasa mountain, भीमविक्रमैः with warriors of frightful valour, कोटिसहस्रेण by one thousand crores, वानरैः with vanaras, वृतः surrounded by, प्रत्यदृश्यत showed up.
explanation: And Hanuman showed up surrounded by a thousand crore vanaras of frightful valour. They looked like the peaks of Kailasa mountain.

shloka_text: नलश्चापि महावीर्यस्संवृतो द्रुमवासिभिः। कोटीशतेन सम्प्राप्तस्सहस्रेण शतेन च।।4.39.36।।
transliteration: nalaścāpi mahāvīryassaṃvṛto drumavāsibhiḥ| koṭīśatena samprāptassahasreṇa śatena ca
translation: महावीर्यः valiant, नलश्चापि Nala also, कोटीशतेन by a hundred crores, सहस्रेण by a thousand, शतेन च and by hundreds, द्रुमवासिभिः by the tree dwellers(monkeys), संवृतः surrounded by, सम्प्राप्तः arrived.
explanation: Valiant Nala also arrived surrounded by a hundred crore and a hundred thousand treedwellers (monkeys).

shloka_text: ततो दधिमुखश्रीमान्कोटिभिर्दशभिर्वृतः। सम्प्राप्तोऽभिमतस्तस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः।।4.39.37।।
transliteration: tato dadhimukhaśrīmānkoṭibhirdaśabhirvṛtaḥ| samprāpto'bhimatastasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
translation: ततः then, श्रीमान् prosperous, दधिमुखः Dadhimukha, दशभिः with ten, कोटिभिः with crore, वृतः surrounded with, अभिमतः a favourite one, तस्य his, महात्मनः सुग्रीस्य of great Sugriva, सम्प्राप्तः reached.
explanation: Then the illustrious Dadhimukha, great Sugriva's favourite leader reached with ten crore vanaras.

shloka_text: शरभः कुमुदो वह्निर्वानरो रंह एव च। एते चान्ये च बहवो वानराः कामरूपिणः।।4.39.38।। आवृत्य पृथिवीं सर्वां पर्वतांश्च वनानि च। यूथपा स्समनुप्राप्ता स्तेषां संख्या न विद्यते।।4.39.39।। आगताश्च विशिष्टाश्च पृथिव्यां सर्ववानराः।
transliteration: śarabhaḥ kumudo vahnirvānaro raṃha eva ca| ete cānye ca bahavo vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ āvṛtya pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ parvatāṃśca vanāni ca| yūthapā ssamanuprāptā steṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate āgatāśca viśiṣṭāśca pṛthivyāṃ sarvavānarāḥ|
translation: शरभः Sarabha, कुमुदः Kumuda, वानरः vanara, वह्निः Vahni, रंहः एव च and so also Ramha, एते all of them, कामरूपिणः who can assume any form at will, अन्ये च and others, बहवः many, तेषाम् of them, संख्या number, वानराः vanaras, यूथपाः troops, सर्वाम् entire, पृथिवीम् land, पर्वतांश्च and mountains, वनानि च and forests also, आवृत्य having occupied, समनुप्राप्ताः advancing towards, आगताः came, सर्ववानराः all the vanaras, पृथिव्याम् of the earth, विशिष्टाश्च outstanding.
explanation: Sarabha, Kumuda, Vahni and Ramhi and many other vanara troops who can assume any form at their will and others from all over the land, mountains and forest advanced towards Sugriva. All the outstanding vanaras of the earth came and covered the land.

shloka_text: शरभः कुमुदो वह्निर्वानरो रंह एव च। एते चान्ये च बहवो वानराः कामरूपिणः।।4.39.38।। आवृत्य पृथिवीं सर्वां पर्वतांश्च वनानि च। यूथपा स्समनुप्राप्ता स्तेषां संख्या न विद्यते।।4.39.39।। आगताश्च विशिष्टाश्च पृथिव्यां सर्ववानराः।
transliteration: śarabhaḥ kumudo vahnirvānaro raṃha eva ca| ete cānye ca bahavo vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ āvṛtya pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ parvatāṃśca vanāni ca| yūthapā ssamanuprāptā steṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate āgatāśca viśiṣṭāśca pṛthivyāṃ sarvavānarāḥ|
translation: शरभः Sarabha, कुमुदः Kumuda, वानरः vanara, वह्निः Vahni, रंहः एव च and so also Ramha, एते all of them, कामरूपिणः who can assume any form at will, अन्ये च and others, बहवः many, तेषाम् of them, संख्या number, वानराः vanaras, यूथपाः troops, सर्वाम् entire, पृथिवीम् land, पर्वतांश्च and mountains, वनानि च and forests also, आवृत्य having occupied, समनुप्राप्ताः advancing towards, आगताः came, सर्ववानराः all the vanaras, पृथिव्याम् of the earth, विशिष्टाश्च outstanding.
explanation: Sarabha, Kumuda, Vahni and Ramhi and many other vanara troops who can assume any form at their will and others from all over the land, mountains and forest advanced towards Sugriva. All the outstanding vanaras of the earth came and covered the land.

shloka_text: आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवङ्गमाः। अभ्यवर्तन्त सुग्रीवं सूर्यमभ्रगणा इव।।4.39.40।।
transliteration: āplavantaḥ plavantaśca garjantaśca plavaṅgamāḥ| abhyavartanta sugrīvaṃ sūryamabhragaṇā iva
translation: प्लवङ्गमाः monkeys, आप्लवन्तः leaping in enthusiasm, प्लवन्तश्च and jumping, गर्जन्तश्च and roaring, सूर्यम् Sun, अभ्रगणा इव like the clouds, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, अभ्यवर्तन्त approached.
explanation: The monkeys came leaping, jumping and roaring in enthusiasm and surrounded Sugriva just as clouds surround the Sun.

shloka_text: कुर्वाणा बहुशब्दांश्च प्रहृष्टा बाहुशालिनः। शिरोभिर्वानरेन्द्राय सुग्रीवाय न्यवेदयन्।।4.39.41।।
transliteration: kurvāṇā bahuśabdāṃśca prahṛṣṭā bāhuśālinaḥ| śirobhirvānarendrāya sugrīvāya nyavedayan
translation: प्रहृष्टाः happy ones, बाहुशालिनः of sturdy shoulders, बहुशब्दान् many kinds of noises, कुर्वाणाः while they made, शिरोभिः with their heads, वानरेन्द्राय to the lord of monkeys, सुग्रीवाय to Sugriva, न्यवेदयन् reported.
explanation: The leaders of monkeys possesing sturdy shoulders made many kinds of noises and reported to Sugriva, bending their heads in reverence.

shloka_text: अपरे वानरश्रेष्ठास्सङ्गम्य च यथोचितम्। सुग्रीवेण समागम्य स्थिताः प्राञ्जलय स्तदा।।4.39.42।।
transliteration: apare vānaraśreṣṭhāssaṅgamya ca yathocitam| sugrīveṇa samāgamya sthitāḥ prāñjalaya stadā
translation: अपरे others, वानरश्रेष्ठाः foremost of vanaras, यथोचितम् in a suitable manner, सङ्गम्य after coming together, सुग्रीवेण with Sugriva, समागम्य after reaching, तदा then, प्राञ्जलयः with folded hands in salutation, स्थिताः stood.
explanation: Thereafter the vanaras came close to Sugriva freely and on reaching him stood, offering salutations with folded hands.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्त्वरितो रामे सर्वांस्तां वानररर्षभान्। निवेदयित्वा धर्मज्ञः स्थितः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्।।4.39.43।।
transliteration: sugrīvastvarito rāme sarvāṃstāṃ vānarararṣabhān| nivedayitvā dharmajñaḥ sthitaḥ prāñjalirabravīt
translation: धर्मज्ञः knower of dharma, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, त्वरितः at once, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, स्थितः stood, वानरर्षभान् prominent vanaras, तान् them, सर्वान् all, रामे to Rama, निवेदयित्वा having presented, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Sugriva, knower of dharma, at once presented all the prominent vanaras to Rama, and standing with folded hands said.

shloka_text: यथासुखं पर्वतनिझरेषु वनेषु सर्वेषु च वानरेन्द्राः। निवेशयित्वा विधिवद्बलानि बलं बलज्ञः प्रतिपत्तुमीष्टे।।4.39.44।।
transliteration: yathāsukhaṃ parvatanijhareṣu vaneṣu sarveṣu ca vānarendrāḥ| niveśayitvā vidhivadbalāni balaṃ balajñaḥ pratipattumīṣṭe
translation: वानरेन्द्राः best of vanaras, पर्वतनिझरेषु by the side of swift mountain streams, सर्वेषु in all, वनेषु च in forests, यथासुखम् comfortably settled, विधिवत् as per tradition, बलानि army, निवेशयित्वा after lodging, बलज्ञः know the strength, बलम् of army, प्रतिपत्तुम् to know, ईष्टे decided.
explanation: Sugriva told the chiefs to station the forces by the side  of swift mountain streams, in forests, and hills and ascertain their exact number. इत्यार्ष श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyninth sarga of Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ राजा समृद्धार्थस्सुग्रीवः प्लवगेश्वरः। उवाच नरशार्दूलं रामं परबलार्दनम्।।4.40.1।।
transliteration: atha rājā samṛddhārthassugrīvaḥ plavageśvaraḥ| uvāca naraśārdūlaṃ rāmaṃ parabalārdanam
translation: प्लवगेश्वरः lord of monkeys, राजा king, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, समृद्धार्थः supported by massive army, अथ then, नरशार्दूलम्  tiger among men, परबलार्दनम् who could crush enemy army, रामम् to Rama, उवाच said.
explanation: Sugriva, lord of monkeys, who was supported by a massive army informed Rama, the tiger among men and a crusher of the enemy army
comments: Sugriva asks the army to move eastward -- description of eastern direction.

shloka_text: आगता विनिविष्टाश्च बलिनः कामरूपिणः। वानरा वारणेन्द्रभा: ये मद्विषयवासिनः।।4.40.2।।
transliteration: āgatā viniviṣṭāśca balinaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ| vānarā vāraṇendrabhā: ye madviṣayavāsinaḥ
translation: ये those, मद्विषयवासिनः residing in my kingdom, बलिनः strong, कामरूपिण: who can assume any form at will, वारणेन्द्रभा: huge like elephants, वानरेन्द्राः vanara heroes, आगताः have come, विनिविष्टाश्च have settled down here.
explanation: 'The vanaras living in my kingdom have come and have settled down. They are strong and huge like elephants and they can assume any form at will.

shloka_text: त इमे बहुविक्रान्तैर्हरिभिर्भीमविक्रमैः। आगता वानरा घोरा दैत्यदानवसन्निभाः।।4.40.3।।
transliteration: ta ime bahuvikrāntairharibhirbhīmavikramaiḥ| āgatā vānarā ghorā daityadānavasannibhāḥ
translation: घोराः dreadful, दैत्यदानवसन्निभाः resemble daityas and demons in form, ते those, इमे वानराः vanaras,  बहुविक्रान्तैः very powerful, हरिभिः monkeys, भीमविक्रमैः of frightening valour, आगताः have arrived.
explanation: 'Dreadful monkeys, powerful monkeys of fierce valour who resemble demons in form, have arrived.

shloka_text: ख्यातकर्मापदानाश्च बलवन्तो जितक्लमाः। पराक्रमेषु विख्याता व्यवसायेषु चोत्तमाः।।4.40.4।। पृथिव्यम्बुचरा राम नानानगनिवासिनः। कोट्यग्रश इमे प्राप्ता वानरास्तव किङ्कराः।।4.40.5।।
transliteration: khyātakarmāpadānāśca balavanto jitaklamāḥ| parākrameṣu vikhyātā vyavasāyeṣu cottamāḥ pṛthivyambucarā rāma nānānaganivāsinaḥ| koṭyagraśa ime prāptā vānarāstava kiṅkarāḥ
translation: राम O Rama, ख्यातकर्मापदानाश्च earned fame for their valiant deeds in the past, बलवन्तः powerful ones, जितक्लमाः indefatigable, पराक्रमेषु in might, विख्याताः famous, व्यवसायेषु in making efforts, उत्तमाः best, पृथिव्यम्बुचराः who can move on earth as well as water, नानानगनिवासिनः living on several mountains, इमे they, वानराः vanaras, कोट्यग्रश: crores of them, तव your, किङ्कराः vanaras, प्राप्ताः have come.
explanation: Powerful vanaras who have earned fame for their valiant deeds in the past, those who are indefatigable and wellknown for their valour having gained preeminence through their efforts and living on several mountains, those who can move on the earth as well as water, crores of them have arrived.

shloka_text: ख्यातकर्मापदानाश्च बलवन्तो जितक्लमाः। पराक्रमेषु विख्याता व्यवसायेषु चोत्तमाः।।4.40.4।। पृथिव्यम्बुचरा राम नानानगनिवासिनः। कोट्यग्रश इमे प्राप्ता वानरास्तव किङ्कराः।।4.40.5।।
transliteration: khyātakarmāpadānāśca balavanto jitaklamāḥ| parākrameṣu vikhyātā vyavasāyeṣu cottamāḥ pṛthivyambucarā rāma nānānaganivāsinaḥ| koṭyagraśa ime prāptā vānarāstava kiṅkarāḥ
translation: राम O Rama, ख्यातकर्मापदानाश्च earned fame for their valiant deeds in the past, बलवन्तः powerful ones, जितक्लमाः indefatigable, पराक्रमेषु in might, विख्याताः famous, व्यवसायेषु in making efforts, उत्तमाः best, पृथिव्यम्बुचराः who can move on earth as well as water, नानानगनिवासिनः living on several mountains, इमे they, वानराः vanaras, कोट्यग्रश: crores of them, तव your, किङ्कराः vanaras, प्राप्ताः have come.
explanation: Powerful vanaras who have earned fame for their valiant deeds in the past, those who are indefatigable and wellknown for their valour having gained preeminence through their efforts and living on several mountains, those who can move on the earth as well as water, crores of them have arrived.

shloka_text: निदेशवर्तिनस्सर्वे सर्वे गुरुहिते रताः। अभिप्रेतमनुष्ठातुं तव शक्ष्यन्त्यरिन्दम।।4.40.6।।
transliteration: nideśavartinassarve sarve guruhite ratāḥ| abhipretamanuṣṭhātuṃ tava śakṣyantyarindama
translation: अरिन्दम O subduer of foes, सर्वे all, निदेशवर्तिनः follow your orders, सर्वे all, गुरुहिते in the wellbeing of the elders, रताः engaged, तव your, अभिप्रेतम् your wish, अनुष्ठातुम् to fulfil, शक्ष्यन्ति are capable.
explanation: 'O Rama,the subduer of foes all of them will follow your command.They are engaged in seeking the wellbeing of elders and can fulfil your wish.

shloka_text: त इमे बहुसाहस्रैरनीकै भीमविक्रमैः। आगता वानरा घोरा दैत्यदानवसन्निभा:।।4.40.7।।
transliteration: ta ime bahusāhasrairanīkai bhīmavikramaiḥ| āgatā vānarā ghorā daityadānavasannibhā:
translation: त इमे these, घोरा dreadful, दैत्यदानवसन्निभा: resembling daityas and danavas, बहुसाहस्रै in many thousands, अनीकैः with forces, भीमविक्रमैः with fierce fighters, आगताः have arrived.
explanation: 'Dreadful monkeys who resemble demons have arrived along with thousands of fierce fighters.

shloka_text: यन्मन्यसे नरव्याघ्र प्राप्तकालं तदुच्यताम्। तत्सैन्यं त्वद्वशे युक्तमाज्ञापयितुमर्हसि।।4.40.8।।
transliteration: yanmanyase naravyāghra prāptakālaṃ taducyatām| tatsainyaṃ tvadvaśe yuktamājñāpayitumarhasi
translation: नरव्याघ्र O tiger among men, यत् such that, प्राप्तकालम् proper time, मन्यसे if you think, तत् that, उच्यताम् may be made known, त्वद्वशे at your command, युक्तम् proper, तत्सैन्यम् this army, आज्ञापयितुम्  you may order, अर्हसि you may.
explanation: 'O tiger among men announce the proper time for action. This army is at your command. Command them.

shloka_text: काममेषामिदं कार्यं विदितं मम तत्त्वतः। तथापि तु यथातत्त्वमाज्ञापयितुमर्हसि।।4.40.9।।
transliteration: kāmameṣāmidaṃ kāryaṃ viditaṃ mama tattvataḥ| tathāpi tu yathātattvamājñāpayitumarhasi
translation: इदम् this, कार्यम् task, मम to me, तत्त्वतः  in principle, एवम् that way, विदितं कामम् is known to me, तथापि even then, यथातत्त्वम् properly, आज्ञापयितुम् to order, अर्हसि you may.
explanation: This task is truly known to me in principle; even so, you may duly give the command as is proper.

shloka_text: इति ब्रुवाणं सुग्रीवं रामो दशरथात्मजः। बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य इदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।4.40.10।।
transliteration: iti bruvāṇaṃ sugrīvaṃ rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ| bāhubhyāṃ sampariṣvajya idaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: दशरथात्मजः Dasaratha's son, रामः Rama, इति thus, ब्रुवाणम् while he spoke, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, बाहुभ्याम् both shoulders, सम्परिष्वज्य hugged, इदं वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: On hearing him, Rama, Dasaratha's son, hugged Sugriva with his arms and said:

shloka_text: ज्ञायतां मम वैदेही यदि जीवति वा न वा। स च देशो महाप्राज्ञ यस्मिन्वसति रावणः।।4.40.11।।
transliteration: jñāyatāṃ mama vaidehī yadi jīvati vā na vā| sa ca deśo mahāprājña yasminvasati rāvaṇaḥ
translation: महाप्राज्ञ O very wise one, मम my, वैदेही Vaidehi, जीवति वा alive or, न वा not or, रावणः Ravana, यस्मिन् in whichever, वसति resides, सः he, देशः in a place, च and, ज्ञायताम् it may be found out.
explanation: 'O wise warrior I wish to know whether Vaidehi is alive or not. Let the kingdom of Ravana be found out.

shloka_text: अधिगम्य तु वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च। प्राप्तकालं विधास्यामि तस्मिन्काले सह त्वया।।4.40.12।।
transliteration: adhigamya tu vaidehīṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca| prāptakālaṃ vidhāsyāmi tasminkāle saha tvayā
translation: वैदेहीम् Vaidehi,रावणस्य Ravana's, निलयं home, च and, अधिगम्य going there, तस्मिन्काले at that time, त्वयासह in conjunction with you, प्राप्तकालम् at the right time, विधास्यामि I will take action.
explanation: 'On locating Vaidehi in the kingdom of Ravana I shall take up proper course of action  in conjunction with you.

shloka_text: नाहमस्मिन् प्रभुः कार्ये वानरेश न लक्ष्मणः। त्वमस्य हेतुः कार्यस्य प्रभुश्च प्लवगेश्वर।।4.40.13।।
transliteration: nāhamasmin prabhuḥ kārye vānareśa na lakṣmaṇaḥ| tvamasya hetuḥ kāryasya prabhuśca plavageśvara
translation: प्लवगेश्वर O lord of monkeys, वानरेश king of vanaras, अहम् I, अस्मिन् in this, कार्ये in the task, प्रभुः  commanders, न not, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, न  not, त्वम् you, अस्य of this, कार्यस्य of the task, हेतुः means, प्रभुश्च lord.
explanation: 'O lord of monkeys neither I nor my brother Lakshmana should command the monkeys. You are the right person to do it.

shloka_text: त्वमेवाऽज्ञापय विभो मम कार्यविनिश्चयम्। त्वं हि जानासि यत्कार्यं मम वीर न संशयः।।4.40.14।।
transliteration: tvamevā'jñāpaya vibho mama kāryaviniścayam| tvaṃ hi jānāsi yatkāryaṃ mama vīra na saṃśayaḥ
translation: विभो O king, मम to me, कार्यविनिश्चयम् understood the task to be performed, त्वमेव you only, आज्ञापय you order, वीर hero, मम my, यत् कार्यम् that task, त्वम् you, जानासि हि you are aware, संशयः  doubt न no.
explanation: 'O king you have understood the task to be performed and, therefore, issue orders without the least hesitation.

shloka_text: सुहृद्वितीयो विक्रान्तः प्राज्ञः कालविशेषवित्। भवानस्मध्दिते युक्त स्सुकृतार्थोऽर्थवित्तमः।।4.40.15।।
transliteration: suhṛdvitīyo vikrāntaḥ prājñaḥ kālaviśeṣavit| bhavānasmadhdite yukta ssukṛtārtho'rthavittamaḥ
translation: भवान् yourself, सुहृत् friend, द्वितीयो second friend, विक्रान्तः valiant, प्राज्ञः wise, कालविशेषवित् knower of timely action, अस्मध्दिते in our wellbeing, युक्तः capable, सुकृतार्थः strategic planner,  अर्थवित्तमः  knower of present purpose.
explanation: 'You are my second friend (Lakshmana being the first). You are valiant as well as wise. You are aware of timely action. You are interested in my wellbeing. You are capable. You know my purpose. You are a startegic planner'. (The present purpose is to plan the course of action. That is artha. Sugriva knows this artha very well).

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो विनतं नाम यूथपम्। अब्रवीद्रामसान्निध्ये लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः।।4.40.16।। शैलाभं मेघनिर्घोषमूर्जितं प्लवगेश्वरः।
transliteration: evamuktastu sugrīvo vinataṃ nāma yūthapam| abravīdrāmasānnidhye lakṣmaṇasya ca dhīmataḥ śailābhaṃ meghanirghoṣamūrjitaṃ plavageśvaraḥ|
translation: एवम् in that way, उक्तः having been asked, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, रामसान्निध्ये in the presence of Rama, धीमतः  learned, लक्ष्मणस्य च Lakshmana's, यूथपम् a troop leader, शैलाभम् lofty like a mountain, मेघनिर्घोषम्  who roared like a thunderous cloud, ऊर्जितम् wellbuilt body, विनतं नाम called Vinata, प्लवगेश्वरम् lord of monkeys, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: 'In response to Rama's desire, Sugriva beckoned a troopleader called Vinata who was wellbuilt and lofty like a mountain. And thundering like a cloud, said to him in the presence of Rama and wise Lakshmana:

shloka_text: सोमसूर्यात्मजै स्सार्धं वानरैर्वानरोत्तम।।4.40.17।। देशकालनयैर्युक्तः कार्या कार्यविनिश्चये। वृतश्शतसहश्रेण वानराणां तरस्विनाम्।।4.40.18।। अधिगच्छ दिशं पूर्वां सशैलवनकाननाम्।
transliteration: somasūryātmajai ssārdhaṃ vānarairvānarottama deśakālanayairyuktaḥ kāryā kāryaviniścaye| vṛtaśśatasahaśreṇa vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām adhigaccha diśaṃ pūrvāṃ saśailavanakānanām|
translation: वानरोत्तम O foremost of vanaras, देशकालनयैः with political wisdom in accordance with time and place, युक्तः endowed with, कार्यविनिश्चये in taking right decision, सोमसूर्यात्मजै along with sons of Sun and Moon, वानरैः सार्धम् followed by the vanaras, तरस्विनाम् of swift ones, वानराणाम् of vanaras, शतसहस्रेण with one hundred thousand, वृतः surrounded, सशैलवनकाननाम्  with mountains, gardens and forests, अधिगच्छ march forward, पूर्वाम्  to the eastern, दिशं direction.
explanation: 'O foremost of the vanaras march forward with the sons of Moon and Sun, followed by one lakh swift monkeys towards the eastern direction full of mountains, gardens, and forests. Endowed with political wisdom, you are capable of taking right decision in accordance with time and place.

shloka_text: सोमसूर्यात्मजै स्सार्धं वानरैर्वानरोत्तम।।4.40.17।। देशकालनयैर्युक्तः कार्या कार्यविनिश्चये। वृतश्शतसहश्रेण वानराणां तरस्विनाम्।।4.40.18।। अधिगच्छ दिशं पूर्वां सशैलवनकाननाम्।
transliteration: somasūryātmajai ssārdhaṃ vānarairvānarottama deśakālanayairyuktaḥ kāryā kāryaviniścaye| vṛtaśśatasahaśreṇa vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām adhigaccha diśaṃ pūrvāṃ saśailavanakānanām|
translation: वानरोत्तम O foremost of vanaras, देशकालनयैः with political wisdom in accordance with time and place, युक्तः endowed with, कार्यविनिश्चये in taking right decision, सोमसूर्यात्मजै along with sons of Sun and Moon, वानरैः सार्धम् followed by the vanaras, तरस्विनाम् of swift ones, वानराणाम् of vanaras, शतसहस्रेण with one hundred thousand, वृतः surrounded, सशैलवनकाननाम्  with mountains, gardens and forests, अधिगच्छ march forward, पूर्वाम्  to the eastern, दिशं direction.
explanation: 'O foremost of the vanaras march forward with the sons of Moon and Sun, followed by one lakh swift monkeys towards the eastern direction full of mountains, gardens, and forests. Endowed with political wisdom, you are capable of taking right decision in accordance with time and place.

shloka_text: तत्र सीतां च वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च।।4.40.19।। मार्गध्वं गिरिशृङ्गेषु वनेषु च नदीषु च।
transliteration: tatra sītāṃ ca vaidehīṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca mārgadhvaṃ giriśṛṅgeṣu vaneṣu ca nadīṣu ca|
translation: तत्र there, वैदेहीम् Vaidehi, सीतां च Sita also, रावणस्य Ravana's, निलयं च in the abode, गिरिशृङ्गेषु on the mountain peaks, वनेषु च and in the forests, नदीषु च and river banks, मार्गध्वम् you may search for.
explanation: 'Search for Sita in the abode of Ravana, on mountain peaks and river banks and in forests.

shloka_text: नदीं भागीरथीं रम्यां सरयूं कौशिकीं तथा।।4.40.20।। कालिन्दीं यमुनां रम्यां यामुनं च महागिरिम्। सरस्वतीं च सिन्धुं च शोणं मणिनिभोदकम्।।4.40.21।। महीं कालमहीं चैव शैलकाननशोभिताम्। ब्रह्ममालान्विदेहांश्च मालवान्कालिकोसलान्।।4.40.22।। मागधांश्च महाग्रामान्पुण्ड्रांन्वङ्गां स्तथैव च। पत्तनं कोशकाराणां भूमिं च रजताकराम्।।4.40.23।।
transliteration: nadīṃ bhāgīrathīṃ ramyāṃ sarayūṃ kauśikīṃ tathā kālindīṃ yamunāṃ ramyāṃ yāmunaṃ ca mahāgirim| sarasvatīṃ ca sindhuṃ ca śoṇaṃ maṇinibhodakam mahīṃ kālamahīṃ caiva śailakānanaśobhitām| brahmamālānvidehāṃśca mālavānkālikosalān māgadhāṃśca mahāgrāmānpuṇḍrāṃnvaṅgāṃ stathaiva ca| pattanaṃ kośakārāṇāṃ bhūmiṃ ca rajatākarām
translation: भागीरथीं नदीम् river Bhagirathi, रम्याम् beautiful, सरयूम् Sarayu, तथा so also, कौशिकीम् Kausiki, कालिन्दी Kalindi, रम्याम् picturesque, यमुनाम् Yamuna, यामुनम् found near  Yamuna, महागिरिं च great mountain, सरस्वतीं च and Saraswati, सिन्धुं च and Sindhu, मणिनिभोदकम् with crystalclear water, शोणम् Sona, महीम् Mahim, शैलकाननशोभिताम् picturesque with mountains and forests, कालमहीं चैव and at Kalamahi, ब्रह्ममालान् Brahmamala, विदेहांश्च and Videha, मालवान् Malava, काशिकोसलान् Kasi and Kosala, मागधान् belonging to Maghada, महाग्रामान् च and great villages, पुण्ड्रान् and Pundra, तथैव च in the same order, आङ्गान् Anga, कोशकाराणाम् country of silkworms, भूमिम् kingdom, रजताकराम् silver caves, भूमिं च and the land, मार्गध्वम् you may search for.
explanation: 'Look for Sita in the beautiful places on rivers Bhagirathi, Sarayu, Kausiki and Kalindi, on the great mountains adjacent to river Yamuna, banks of rivers Saraswati, Sindhu, Sona with crystalclear waters, the country of Mahim and Kalamahi adorned with mountains and forests. Proceed to Brahmamala, Videha, Malava, Kasi, Kosala and Maghada with great villages, the country of Pundram, Vanga, the country famous for silk worms and the land with silver caves. (It is the eastern direction of river Saravati between Himavat and Vindhya and not east of Kiskinda)

shloka_text: सर्वमेतद्विचेतव्यं मृगयद्भिस्ततस्ततः। रामस्य दयितां भार्यां सीतां दशरथस्नुषाम्।।4.40.24।।
transliteration: sarvametadvicetavyaṃ mṛgayadbhistatastataḥ| rāmasya dayitāṃ bhāryāṃ sītāṃ daśarathasnuṣām
translation: रामस्य Rama's, दयिताम् dear, भार्याम् wife, दशरथस्नुषाम् daughterinlaw of Dasaratha, सीताम् Sita, ततस्ततः in all places, मृगयद्भि: by searching, तत् सर्वम् all over, विचेतव्यम् search should be made.
explanation: 'Search all over the place looking carefully here and there for Sita the beloved consort of Rama, daughterinlaw of Dasaratha.

shloka_text: समुद्रमवगाढांश्च पर्वतान्पत्तनानि च। मन्दरस्य च ये कोटिं संश्रिताः केचिदायताम्।।4.40.25।। कर्णप्रावरणाश्चैव तथा चाप्योष्ठकर्णकाः। घोरलोहमुखाश्चैव जवनाश्चैकपादकाः।।4.40.26।। अक्षया बलवन्तश्च पुरुषाः पुरुषादकाः। किराताः कर्ण चूडाश्च हेमाङ्गा: प्रियदर्शनाः।।4.40.27।। आममीनाशनास्तत्र किराता द्वीपवासिनः। अन्तर्जलचरा घोरा नरव्याघ्रा इति शृताः।।4.40.28।। एतेषामाश्रयास्सर्वे विचेयाः कावनौकसः। गिरिभिर्ये च गम्यन्ते प्लवनेन प्लवेन च।।4.40.29।।
transliteration: samudramavagāḍhāṃśca parvatānpattanāni ca| mandarasya ca ye koṭiṃ saṃśritāḥ kecidāyatām karṇaprāvaraṇāścaiva tathā cāpyoṣṭhakarṇakāḥ| ghoralohamukhāścaiva javanāścaikapādakāḥ akṣayā balavantaśca puruṣāḥ puruṣādakāḥ| kirātāḥ karṇa cūḍāśca hemāṅgā: priyadarśanāḥ āmamīnāśanāstatra kirātā dvīpavāsinaḥ| antarjalacarā ghorā naravyāghrā iti śṛtāḥ eteṣāmāśrayāssarve viceyāḥ kāvanaukasaḥ| giribhirye ca gamyante plavanena plavena ca
translation: काननौकसः inhabitants of the forests, समुद्रम् the oceans, अवगाढान् deep pits, पर्वतानि on the mountains,पत्तनानि च and towns, मन्दरस्य on Mandara mountain, आयताम् living, कोटिम्  broad peaks, संश्रिताः taken shelter, केचित् some, कर्णप्रावरणाश्चैव who cover their ears,  ओष्ठकर्णकाः who have ears on lips, घोरलोहमुखाश्चैव who have iron faces, जवनाः of great speed, एकपादकाः with one foot, अक्षयाः  who cannot be destroyed, बलवन्तश्च powerful people, पुरुषाः men, पुरुषादकाः cannibals, किराताः Kiratas, आकर्ण चूडाः with hair reaching their ears, प्रियदर्शनाः of pleasing appearance, हेमाङ्गाः of goldencolour limbs, आममीनाशनाः eating uncooked fish, द्वीपवासिनः residents of island, किराताः Kiratas, इति thus, शृताः it is heard, अन्तर्जलचराः moving under water, घोराः fierce ones, नरव्याघ्राः tiger among men, एतेषाम् of them, सर्वे all, आश्रयाः shelters, विचेयाः should be searched, ये those, गिरिभिः by moutains, प्लवनेन  leaping animals, प्लवनेन च and jumping, गम्यन्ते should go and search.
explanation: 'There are people who have taken shelter in the deep pits in the midst of the sea, in deep valleys, mountains, cities and broad peaks of Mandara mountain and forests.All those regions should be thoroughly searched. There are innumerable inhabitants,such as strong cannibals, some who cover their ears, some who have ears extended up to the lips, some with dreadful metallic faces, some swiftmoving, onefooted indestructible beings. There are Kirata tribes of golden complexion and handsome looks whose tuft of hair is set to the sides so that it touches their ears. These Kiratas are Islanddwellers and they eat uncooked fish.They move in waters and are fierce, known as tigerlike men (Naravyagras because half of their body is human and other half is tiger in form). All the shelters of these forestdwellers should be searched well.Those who can be sent by crossing mountains, those who can leap (in air) and those who can swim through waters may be also dispatched.

There are innumerable inhabitants,such as strong cannibals, some who cover their ears, some who have ears extended up to the lips, some with dreadful metallic faces, some swiftmoving, onefooted indestructible beings. There are Kirata tribes of golden complexion and handsome looks whose tuft of hair is set to the sides so that it touches their ears. These Kiratas are Islanddwellers and they eat uncooked fish.They move in waters and are fierce, known as tigerlike men (Naravyagras because half of their body is human and other half is tiger in form). All the shelters of these forestdwellers should be searched well.Those who can be sent by crossing mountains, those who can leap (in air) and those who can swim through waters may be also dispatched.

shloka_text: रत्नवन्तं यवद्वीपं सप्तराज्योपशोभितम्। सुवर्णरूप्यकं चैव सुवर्णाकरमण्डितम्।।4.40.30।। यवद्वीपमतिक्रम्य शिशिरो नाम पर्वतः। दिवं स्पृशति शृङ्गेण देवदानवसेवितः।।4.40.31।। एतेषां गिरिदुर्गेषु प्रपातेषु वनेषु च। मार्गध्वं सहितास्सर्वे रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम्।।4.40.32।।
transliteration: ratnavantaṃ yavadvīpaṃ saptarājyopaśobhitam| suvarṇarūpyakaṃ caiva suvarṇākaramaṇḍitam yavadvīpamatikramya śiśiro nāma parvataḥ| divaṃ spṛśati śṛṅgeṇa devadānavasevitaḥ eteṣāṃ giridurgeṣu prapāteṣu vaneṣu ca| mārgadhvaṃ sahitāssarve rāmapatnīṃ yaśasvinīm
translation: सप्तराज्योपशोभितम् prosperous and divided into seven kingdoms, यवद्वीपम् island of Java, सुवर्णाकरमण्डितम् glittering with gold mines, सुवर्णरूप्यकं चैव island of gold and silver, रत्नवन्तम् rich in gems, यवद्वीपम् island of Java, अतिक्रम्य going beyond, शिशिरोनाम Sisira by name, देवदानवसेवितः frequented by gods and demons, पर्वतः mountains, शृङ्गेण with a peak, दिवम् sky, स्पृशति touching, सर्वे all, सहिताः together, एतेषाम् of those, गिरिदुर्गेषु inaccesible mountains, प्रपातेषु at water falls, वनेषु च and in forests, यशस्विनीम् famed, रामपन्तीम् Rama's wife, मार्गध्वम् search for.
explanation: 'Go beyond Java island filled with precious gems. It has seven kingdoms. It is adorned with gold and silver mines in abundance. There is a mountain Sisira (abode of Garuda) beyond Java Island. It touches the sky with its lofty cliffs. Gods and demons visit this mountain. You may look for illustrious Rama's consort in these inaccessible mountains, waterfalls and forests.

There is a mountain Sisira (abode of Garuda) beyond Java Island. It touches the sky with its lofty cliffs. Gods and demons visit this mountain. You may look for illustrious Rama's consort in these inaccessible mountains, waterfalls and forests.

shloka_text: ततो रक्तजलं शोणमगाधं शीघ्रगामिनम्। गत्वा पारं समुद्रस्य सिद्धचारणसेवितम्।।4.40.33।। तस्य तीर्थेषु रम्येषु विचित्रेषु वनेषु च। रावण स्सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः।।4.40.34।।
transliteration: tato raktajalaṃ śoṇamagādhaṃ śīghragāminam| gatvā pāraṃ samudrasya siddhacāraṇasevitam tasya tīrtheṣu ramyeṣu vicitreṣu vaneṣu ca| rāvaṇa ssaha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ
translation: ततः then, रक्तजलम् having red coloured water, शीघ्रगामिनम् fastflowing, शोणमगाधम् deep river Sona, (प्राप्य after reaching there), समुद्रस्य ocean's, सिद्धचारणसेवितम् inhabited by Siddhas and Charanas, पारम् to the opposite side, गत्वा on going, तस्य its, रम्येषु in delightful, तीर्थेषु in rivers, वचित्रेषु wonderful, वनेषु च and forests, ततस्ततः here and there, वैदेह्या along with Vaidehi, रावणः Ravana, मार्गितव्यः should be sought for.
explanation: 'Therefrom reach out to the swiftflowing river Sona which has redcoloured waters. Then crossing the sea which is the abode of Siddhas and Charanas search the different rivers reaching the sea, and the picturesque and wonderful forests to trace the abode of Ravana who has stolen Sita.

shloka_text: ततो रक्तजलं शोणमगाधं शीघ्रगामिनम्। गत्वा पारं समुद्रस्य सिद्धचारणसेवितम्।।4.40.33।। तस्य तीर्थेषु रम्येषु विचित्रेषु वनेषु च। रावण स्सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः।।4.40.34।।
transliteration: tato raktajalaṃ śoṇamagādhaṃ śīghragāminam| gatvā pāraṃ samudrasya siddhacāraṇasevitam tasya tīrtheṣu ramyeṣu vicitreṣu vaneṣu ca| rāvaṇa ssaha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ
translation: ततः then, रक्तजलम् having red coloured water, शीघ्रगामिनम् fastflowing, शोणमगाधम् deep river Sona, (प्राप्य after reaching there), समुद्रस्य ocean's, सिद्धचारणसेवितम् inhabited by Siddhas and Charanas, पारम् to the opposite side, गत्वा on going, तस्य its, रम्येषु in delightful, तीर्थेषु in rivers, वचित्रेषु wonderful, वनेषु च and forests, ततस्ततः here and there, वैदेह्या along with Vaidehi, रावणः Ravana, मार्गितव्यः should be sought for.
explanation: 'Therefrom reach out to the swiftflowing river Sona which has redcoloured waters. Then crossing the sea which is the abode of Siddhas and Charanas search the different rivers reaching the sea, and the picturesque and wonderful forests to trace the abode of Ravana who has stolen Sita.

shloka_text: तत स्समुद्रद्वीपांश्च सुभीमान्द्रष्टुमर्हथ। ऊर्मिमन्तं समुद्रं च क्रोशन्तमनिलोद्धतम्।।4.40.35।।
transliteration: tata ssamudradvīpāṃśca subhīmāndraṣṭumarhatha| ūrmimantaṃ samudraṃ ca krośantamaniloddhatam
translation: ततः then, सुभीमान् fierce, समुद्रद्वीपांश्च islands of the ocean, समुद्रं च and the ocean, अनिलोद्धतम् swept by wind, क्रोशन्तम् roaring, ऊर्मिमन्तम् stirred up by waves, द्रष्टुम् to see, अर्हथ it is proper for you.
explanation: 'Then you may continue your search in the frightening islands of the sea as well as the sea which roars when stirred up by the wind.

shloka_text: तत्रासुरा महाकायाश्छायां गृह्णन्ति नित्यशः। ब्रह्मणा समनुज्ञाता दीर्घकालं बुभुक्षिताः।।4.40.36।।
transliteration: tatrāsurā mahākāyāśchāyāṃ gṛhṇanti nityaśaḥ| brahmaṇā samanujñātā dīrghakālaṃ bubhukṣitāḥ
translation: तत्र there, दीर्घकालम् for a long time, बुभुक्षिताः very hungry people, महाकायाः those of huge body, असुराः demons, ब्रह्मणा by Brahma, समनुज्ञाताः have been permitted, नित्यम् ever, छायाम् shadow, गृह्णन्ति will be catching.
explanation: 'Demons of huge bodies catch the shadows of passersby in that place as they have been hungry for long and have the permission of Brahma to do so.

shloka_text: तं कालमेघप्रतिमं महोरगनिषेवितम्। अभिगम्य महानादं तीर्थेनैव महोदधिम्।।4.40.37।। ततो रक्तजलं भीमं लोहितं नाम सागरम्। गत्वा प्रेक्ष्यथ तां चैव बृहतीं कूटशाल्मलीम्।।4.40.38।।
transliteration: taṃ kālameghapratimaṃ mahoraganiṣevitam| abhigamya mahānādaṃ tīrthenaiva mahodadhim tato raktajalaṃ bhīmaṃ lohitaṃ nāma sāgaram| gatvā prekṣyatha tāṃ caiva bṛhatīṃ kūṭaśālmalīm
translation: कालमेघप्रतिमम् looking like black clouds at the time of dissolution, महोरगनिषेवितम् inhabited by great serpents, महानादम् roaring, महोदधिम् great ocean, रक्तजलं with red colured water, तीर्थेनैव through the river bank, अभिगम्य after reaching there, लोहितं नाम called Lohita, सागरम् sea, गत्वा going there, बृहतीम् a huge one, ताम् that one, कूटशाल्मलीम् Salmali tree (silkcotton tree), प्रेक्ष्यथ seeing, चैव also.
explanation: 'Reach out to the great roaring ocean which looks like a black cloud at the time of dissolution, inhabited by great serpents.Go through the bank of the river, and touch the frightening sea named Lohita of red coloured water.You will see a huge silkcotton tree in that place.

shloka_text: तं कालमेघप्रतिमं महोरगनिषेवितम्। अभिगम्य महानादं तीर्थेनैव महोदधिम्।।4.40.37।। ततो रक्तजलं भीमं लोहितं नाम सागरम्। गत्वा प्रेक्ष्यथ तां चैव बृहतीं कूटशाल्मलीम्।।4.40.38।।
transliteration: taṃ kālameghapratimaṃ mahoraganiṣevitam| abhigamya mahānādaṃ tīrthenaiva mahodadhim tato raktajalaṃ bhīmaṃ lohitaṃ nāma sāgaram| gatvā prekṣyatha tāṃ caiva bṛhatīṃ kūṭaśālmalīm
translation: कालमेघप्रतिमम् looking like black clouds at the time of dissolution, महोरगनिषेवितम् inhabited by great serpents, महानादम् roaring, महोदधिम् great ocean, रक्तजलं with red colured water, तीर्थेनैव through the river bank, अभिगम्य after reaching there, लोहितं नाम called Lohita, सागरम् sea, गत्वा going there, बृहतीम् a huge one, ताम् that one, कूटशाल्मलीम् Salmali tree (silkcotton tree), प्रेक्ष्यथ seeing, चैव also.
explanation: 'Reach out to the great roaring ocean which looks like a black cloud at the time of dissolution, inhabited by great serpents.Go through the bank of the river, and touch the frightening sea named Lohita of red coloured water.You will see a huge silkcotton tree in that place.

shloka_text: गृहं च वैनतेयस्य नानारत्नविभूषितम्। तत्र कैलाससङ्काशं विहितं विश्वकर्मणा।।4.40.39।।
transliteration: gṛhaṃ ca vainateyasya nānāratnavibhūṣitam| tatra kailāsasaṅkāśaṃ vihitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā
translation: तत्र there, नानारत्नविभूषितम् adorned with diffrent kinds of gems, कैलाससङ्काशम् looking like the Kailasa mountain, विश्वकर्मणा by Visvakarma, विहितम् constructed, वैनतेयस्य Garuda's, गृहम् house, च also.
explanation: 'You would see there a house of Garuda constructed by Visvakarma. It looks like the Kailasa mountain and is adorned with different kinds of gems.

shloka_text: तत्र शैलनिभा भीमा मन्देहा नाम राक्षसाः। शैलशृङ्गेषु लम्बन्ते नानारूपा भयावहाः।।4.40.40।।
transliteration: tatra śailanibhā bhīmā mandehā nāma rākṣasāḥ| śailaśṛṅgeṣu lambante nānārūpā bhayāvahāḥ
translation: तत्र there, शैलशृङ्गेषु on the mountain cliffs, शैलनिभा: huge as mountain, भीमाः frightening, नानारूपाः of different forms, भयावहाः fearsome, मन्देहाः नाम called Mandehas, राक्षसाः demons, लम्बन्ते will be hanging down.
explanation: 'There are frightening demons called Mandehas of different forms, fearsome as huge mountains hanging down the mountain peaks.

shloka_text: ते पतन्ति जले नित्यं सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति। निहता ब्रह्मतेजोभिरहन्यहनि राक्षसाः।।4.40.41।। अभितप्ताश्च सूर्येण लम्बन्ते स्म पुनः पुनः।
transliteration: te patanti jale nityaṃ sūryasyodayanaṃ prati| nihatā brahmatejobhirahanyahani rākṣasāḥ abhitaptāśca sūryeṇa lambante sma punaḥ punaḥ|
translation: ते those, राक्षसाः demons, अहन्यहनि every day, सूर्योदयनं प्रति at the time of Sunrise, नित्यम् always, सूर्येण by the Sun's heat, अभितप्ताः scorched, ब्रह्मतेजोभिः by the power of mantras recited by brahmins, निहताः dead, जले in water, पतन्ति drop down, पुनः पुनः again and again, लम्बन्ते स्म keep hanging on.
explanation: 'Those demons  keep dropping down in water at the time of Sunrise every day, by the power of Gayatri mantras recited by brahmins scorched by the heat of the Sun. Again and again they keep hanging  on to the cliffs.

shloka_text: ततः पाण्डुरमेघाभं क्षीरोदं नाम सागरम्।।4.40.42।। गत्वा द्रक्ष्यथ दुर्धर्षा मुक्ताहारमिवोर्मिभिः।
transliteration: tataḥ pāṇḍurameghābhaṃ kṣīrodaṃ nāma sāgaram gatvā drakṣyatha durdharṣā muktāhāramivormibhiḥ|
translation: दुर्धर्षाः one who is unassailable by the enemies, ततः then, गत्वा after going, पाण्डुरमेघाभम् appearing like white clouds, ऊर्मिभिः white waves, मुक्ताहारमिव like pearl chain, क्षीरोदं नाम  milky ocean by name, सागरम् ocean, द्रक्ष्यथ you will see.
explanation: 'You who are unassailable by the enemies, will see the milky ocean appearing like clouds, resembling a pearl necklace with its rows of waves.

shloka_text: तस्य मध्ये महान् श्वेतो ऋषभो नाम पर्वतः।।4.40.43।। दिव्यगन्धैः कुसुमितै राजितैश्च नगैर्वृतः। सरश्च राजतैः पद्मैर्ज्वलितैर्हेमकेसरैः।।4.40.44।। नाम्ना सुदर्शनं नाम राजहंसैस्समाकुलम्।
transliteration: tasya madhye mahān śveto ṛṣabho nāma parvataḥ divyagandhaiḥ kusumitai rājitaiśca nagairvṛtaḥ| saraśca rājataiḥ padmairjvalitairhemakesaraiḥ nāmnā sudarśanaṃ nāma rājahaṃsaissamākulam|
translation: तस्य मध्ये in the middle, दिव्यगन्धैः with wonderful fragrances, कुसुमितैः flowering, राजितैः  glowing, नगैः with mountains, वृतः surrounded, ऋषभो नाम called Rishaba, श्वेतः white, पर्वतः mountain, ज्वलितैः with glittering, हेमकेसरैः with golden filaments, राजतैः with silver, पद्मैः with lotuses, राजहंसैः with royal swans, समाकुलम् surrounded, नाम्ना known as, सुदर्शनं नाम called Sudarsana, सरश्च lake.
explanation: 'In the midst of that ocean stands a majestic white mountain named Rishaba surrounded by trees filled with silver flowers emitting wonderful fragrance.There is also a lake named Sudarsana with glittering silver lotuses having gleaming golden filaments. Royal swans inhabit these surroundings.

shloka_text: तस्य मध्ये महान् श्वेतो ऋषभो नाम पर्वतः।।4.40.43।। दिव्यगन्धैः कुसुमितै राजितैश्च नगैर्वृतः। सरश्च राजतैः पद्मैर्ज्वलितैर्हेमकेसरैः।।4.40.44।। नाम्ना सुदर्शनं नाम राजहंसैस्समाकुलम्।
transliteration: tasya madhye mahān śveto ṛṣabho nāma parvataḥ divyagandhaiḥ kusumitai rājitaiśca nagairvṛtaḥ| saraśca rājataiḥ padmairjvalitairhemakesaraiḥ nāmnā sudarśanaṃ nāma rājahaṃsaissamākulam|
translation: तस्य मध्ये in the middle, दिव्यगन्धैः with wonderful fragrances, कुसुमितैः flowering, राजितैः  glowing, नगैः with mountains, वृतः surrounded, ऋषभो नाम called Rishaba, श्वेतः white, पर्वतः mountain, ज्वलितैः with glittering, हेमकेसरैः with golden filaments, राजतैः with silver, पद्मैः with lotuses, राजहंसैः with royal swans, समाकुलम् surrounded, नाम्ना known as, सुदर्शनं नाम called Sudarsana, सरश्च lake.
explanation: 'In the midst of that ocean stands a majestic white mountain named Rishaba surrounded by trees filled with silver flowers emitting wonderful fragrance.There is also a lake named Sudarsana with glittering silver lotuses having gleaming golden filaments. Royal swans inhabit these surroundings.

shloka_text: विबुधाश्चारणा यक्षाः किन्नराश्चाप्सरोगणाः।।4.40.45।। हृष्टास्समभिगच्छन्ति नलिनीं तां रिरंसवः।
transliteration: vibudhāścāraṇā yakṣāḥ kinnarāścāpsarogaṇāḥ hṛṣṭāssamabhigacchanti nalinīṃ tāṃ riraṃsavaḥ|
translation: विबुधाः deities, चारणाः charanas, यक्षाः yakshas, किन्नराश्च even kinneras, अप्सरोगणाः groups of apasaras, हृष्टाः joyfully, रिरंसवः those desirous of strolling, तां that, नलिनीम् lotus pond, समभिगच्छन्ति keep coming.
explanation: 'The deities, called charanas, yakshas and kinneras, also apsarasas keep coming there to stoll by that lotus pond.

shloka_text: क्षीरोदं समतिक्रम्य तदा द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः।।4.40.46।। जलोदं सागरं शीघ्रं सर्वभूतभयावहम्।
transliteration: kṣīrodaṃ samatikramya tadā drakṣyatha vānarāḥ jalodaṃ sāgaraṃ śīghraṃ sarvabhūtabhayāvaham|
translation: वानराः O monkeys, क्षीरोदम् milky ocean, समतिक्रम्य going beyond, सर्वभूतभयावहम् most dreadful to all creatures, जलोदम् ocean, सागरम् sea, शीघ्रं swiftly, तदा then, द्रक्ष्यथ you will see.
explanation: 'O monkeys going beyond the milky ocean you will see the seas most dreadful to all creatures.

shloka_text: तत्र तत्कोपजं तेजः कृतं हयमुखं महत्।।4.40.47।। अस्याहुस्तन्महावेगमोदनं सचराचरम्।
transliteration: tatra tatkopajaṃ tejaḥ kṛtaṃ hayamukhaṃ mahat asyāhustanmahāvegamodanaṃ sacarācaram|
translation: तत्र there, तत्कोपजम् born out of his anger, महत् great, हयमुखम् face of horse, तेजः bright, कृतम् is created, सचराचरम् both movable and immovable creatures, महावेगम् very fast, तत् that, अस्य its, ओदनम् food, आहुः they said.
explanation: 'Here is born Hayamukha, out of the fastspreading fire of anger of the ocean. Its movable and  immovable creatures constitute his food.

shloka_text: तत्र विक्रोशतां नादो भूतानां सागरौकसाम्।।4.40.48।। श्रूयते च समर्थानां दृष्ट्वा तद्बडबामुखम्।
transliteration: tatra vikrośatāṃ nādo bhūtānāṃ sāgaraukasām śrūyate ca samarthānāṃ dṛṣṭvā tadbaḍabāmukham|
translation: तत्र there, तत् that, बडबामुखम् burning face of Vadava, दृष्ट्वा seeing, असमर्थानाम् of the weak, विक्रोशताम् crying loudly, सागरौकसाम् dwelling in the sea, भूतानाम् of creatures, नादः sound, श्रूयते is heard.
explanation: 'You can hear the sounds of helpless oceanic creatures crying loudly on seeing the burning face of Vadava.

shloka_text: स्वादूदस्योत्तरे देशे योजनानि त्रयोदश।।4.40.49।। जातरूपशिलो नाम महान्कनकपर्वतः।
transliteration: svādūdasyottare deśe yojanāni trayodaśa jātarūpaśilo nāma mahānkanakaparvataḥ|
translation: स्वादूदस्य of the ocean of tasty water, उत्तरे देशे  the north direction, त्रयोदश thirteen, योजनानि yojanas, महान् huge, कनकपर्वतः golden mountain, जातरूपशिलो नाम called Jatarupasila.
explanation: 'Thirteen yojanas to the north of this ocean of pure waters is a huge golden mountain called Jatarupasila.

shloka_text: तत्र चन्द्रप्रतीकाशं पन्नगं धरणीधरम्।।4.40.50।। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षं ततो द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः। आसीनं पर्वतस्याग्रे सर्वभूतनमस्कृतम्।।4.40.51।। सहस्रशिरसं देवमनन्तं नीलवाससम्।
transliteration: tatra candrapratīkāśaṃ pannagaṃ dharaṇīdharam padmapatraviśālākṣaṃ tato drakṣyatha vānarāḥ| āsīnaṃ parvatasyāgre sarvabhūtanamaskṛtam sahasraśirasaṃ devamanantaṃ nīlavāsasam|
translation: वानराः O monkeys, ततः then, तत्र there, पर्वतस्य mountain's, अग्रे on the top, आसीनम् seated, चन्द्रप्रतीकाशम् resembling the Moon in brightness, पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षम् of large eyes like lotus petals, सर्वभूतनमस्कृतम् revered by all beings, सहस्रशिरसम् thousandheaded, नीलवाससम् robed in blue cloth, देवम् worshipped, धरणीधरम् bearing the load of the earth, अनन्तम् Ananta, पन्नगम् serpent, द्रक्ष्यथ you will see.
explanation: 'O monkeys on top of the mountain you will see Ananta, a thousandhooded serpent seated, as bright as the Moon, robed in blue, with large eyes like lotus petals bearing the load of the earth, and revered by all beings.

shloka_text: तत्र चन्द्रप्रतीकाशं पन्नगं धरणीधरम्।।4.40.50।। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षं ततो द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः। आसीनं पर्वतस्याग्रे सर्वभूतनमस्कृतम्।।4.40.51।। सहस्रशिरसं देवमनन्तं नीलवाससम्।
transliteration: tatra candrapratīkāśaṃ pannagaṃ dharaṇīdharam padmapatraviśālākṣaṃ tato drakṣyatha vānarāḥ| āsīnaṃ parvatasyāgre sarvabhūtanamaskṛtam sahasraśirasaṃ devamanantaṃ nīlavāsasam|
translation: वानराः O monkeys, ततः then, तत्र there, पर्वतस्य mountain's, अग्रे on the top, आसीनम् seated, चन्द्रप्रतीकाशम् resembling the Moon in brightness, पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षम् of large eyes like lotus petals, सर्वभूतनमस्कृतम् revered by all beings, सहस्रशिरसम् thousandheaded, नीलवाससम् robed in blue cloth, देवम् worshipped, धरणीधरम् bearing the load of the earth, अनन्तम् Ananta, पन्नगम् serpent, द्रक्ष्यथ you will see.
explanation: 'O monkeys on top of the mountain you will see Ananta, a thousandhooded serpent seated, as bright as the Moon, robed in blue, with large eyes like lotus petals bearing the load of the earth, and revered by all beings.

shloka_text: त्रिशिराः काञ्चनः केतुस्तालस्तस्य महात्मनः।।4.40.52।। स्थापितः पर्वतस्याग्रे विराजति सवेदिकः।
transliteration: triśirāḥ kāñcanaḥ ketustālastasya mahātmanaḥ sthāpitaḥ parvatasyāgre virājati savedikaḥ|
translation: महात्मनः  highsouled, तस्य पर्वतस्य of that mountain, अग्रे on top, स्थापितः is fixed, केतुः flag of Ananta, त्रिशिराः triplecrowned, काञ्चनः golden, सवेदिकः with an altar, तालः Tala, विराजति shining.
explanation: 'Highsouled Ananta's flag is a threeheaded golden palm tree shining on an altar on top of the mountain.

shloka_text: पूर्वस्यां दिशि निर्माणं कृतं तत् त्रिदशेश्वरैः।।4.40.53।। ततः परं हेममय श्श्रीमानुदयपर्वतः। तस्य कोटिर्दिवं स्पृष्ट्वा शतयोजनमायता।।4.40.54।। जातरूपमयी दिव्या विराजति सवेदिका।
transliteration: pūrvasyāṃ diśi nirmāṇaṃ kṛtaṃ tat tridaśeśvaraiḥ tataḥ paraṃ hemamaya śśrīmānudayaparvataḥ| tasya koṭirdivaṃ spṛṣṭvā śatayojanamāyatā jātarūpamayī divyā virājati savedikā|
translation: तत् that, निर्माणम् arrangement , पूर्वस्यां दिशि in the eastern quarter, त्रिदशेश्वरैः by the gods, कृतम् done, ततः परम् beyond that, हेममयः full of gold, श्रीमान् famous, उदयपर्वतः mountain behind which the sun rises, तस्य its, जातरूपमयी golden, दिव्या divine, सवेदिका that altar, शतयोजनम् a hundred yojanas, आयता long, कोटिः the edge, दिवम् sky, स्पृष्ट्वा touching, विराजति shining.
explanation: 'The flag of Ananta is fixed by the gods in the eastern direction. Beyond that stands the famous golden mountain behind which the sun rises. Its golden peak with a divine altar spread over a hundred yojanas touches heaven.

shloka_text: पूर्वस्यां दिशि निर्माणं कृतं तत् त्रिदशेश्वरैः।।4.40.53।। ततः परं हेममय श्श्रीमानुदयपर्वतः। तस्य कोटिर्दिवं स्पृष्ट्वा शतयोजनमायता।।4.40.54।। जातरूपमयी दिव्या विराजति सवेदिका।
transliteration: pūrvasyāṃ diśi nirmāṇaṃ kṛtaṃ tat tridaśeśvaraiḥ tataḥ paraṃ hemamaya śśrīmānudayaparvataḥ| tasya koṭirdivaṃ spṛṣṭvā śatayojanamāyatā jātarūpamayī divyā virājati savedikā|
translation: तत् that, निर्माणम् arrangement , पूर्वस्यां दिशि in the eastern quarter, त्रिदशेश्वरैः by the gods, कृतम् done, ततः परम् beyond that, हेममयः full of gold, श्रीमान् famous, उदयपर्वतः mountain behind which the sun rises, तस्य its, जातरूपमयी golden, दिव्या divine, सवेदिका that altar, शतयोजनम् a hundred yojanas, आयता long, कोटिः the edge, दिवम् sky, स्पृष्ट्वा touching, विराजति shining.
explanation: 'The flag of Ananta is fixed by the gods in the eastern direction. Beyond that stands the famous golden mountain behind which the sun rises. Its golden peak with a divine altar spread over a hundred yojanas touches heaven.

shloka_text: सालैस्तालैस्तमालैश्च कर्णिकारैश्च पुष्पितैः।।4.40.55।। जातरूपमयैर्दिव्यै श्शोभते सूर्यसन्निभैः।
transliteration: sālaistālaistamālaiśca karṇikāraiśca puṣpitaiḥ jātarūpamayairdivyai śśobhate sūryasannibhaiḥ|
translation: जातरूपमयैः golden form, दिव्यैः divine, सूर्यसन्निभैः resembling the Sun, पुष्पितैः flowering, सालैः with  salas, तालैः with palmyras, तमालैश्च with tamalas, कर्णिकारैश्च with karnikaras also, शोभते enchanting.
explanation: 'The place looks beautiful with salas, palmyras, tamalas and karnikara trees in full bloom. These golden, divine flowers shine like the Sungod.

shloka_text: तत्र योजनविस्तारमुच्छ्रितं दशयोजनम्।।4.40.56।। शृङ्गं सौमनसं नाम जातरूपमयं ध्रुवम्।
transliteration: tatra yojanavistāramucchritaṃ daśayojanam śṛṅgaṃ saumanasaṃ nāma jātarūpamayaṃ dhruvam|
translation: तत्र there, योजनविस्तारम् spread over a yojana, दशयोजनम् ten yojanas, उच्छ्रितम् tall, जातरूपमयम् golden, ध्रुवम् certainly, सौमनसं नाम called Saumanasa, शृङ्गम् peak.
explanation: 'There is a huge golden peak called Saumanas of ten yojanas in height spread over a breadth of one yojana.

shloka_text: तत्रपूर्वं पदं कृत्वा पुरा विष्णुस्त्रिविक्रमे।।4.40.57।। द्वितीयं शिखरे मेरोश्चकार पुरुषोत्तमः।
transliteration: tatrapūrvaṃ padaṃ kṛtvā purā viṣṇustrivikrame dvitīyaṃ śikhare meroścakāra puruṣottamaḥ|
translation: पुरुषोत्तमः supreme being, विष्णुः Visnu, पुरा formerly, त्रिविक्रमे taking three strides, पूर्वम् first, तत्र there, पदम् foot, कृत्वा after that, द्वितीयम् second, मेरोः Meru's, शिखरे on the peak, चकार placed.
explanation: 'When the supreme being, Visnu took his three strides as Lord Vamana, he placed his first foot on this peak and the second on the peak of mount Meru.

shloka_text: त्तरेण परिक्रम्य जम्बूद्वीपं दिवाकरः।।4.40.58।। दृश्यो भवति भूयिष्ठं शिखरं तन्महोच्छ्रयम्।
transliteration: ttareṇa parikramya jambūdvīpaṃ divākaraḥ dṛśyo bhavati bhūyiṣṭhaṃ śikharaṃ tanmahocchrayam|
translation: दिवाकरः Sun, जम्बूद्वीपं उत्तरेण north of Jambu island, परिक्रम्य circumambulating, महोच्छ्रयम् very tall, तत् that, शिखरम् peak, भूयिष्ठम् greatly, दृश्यः is seen, भवति will be.
explanation: 'The Sun circumabulates Jambu island  and when he arrives at this lofty cliff of the mountain, it takes the northern direction and becomes visible to the world.

shloka_text: तत्र वैखानसा नाम वालखिल्या महर्षयः।।4.40.59।। प्रकाशमाना दृश्यन्ते सूर्यवर्णास्तपस्विनः।
transliteration: tatra vaikhānasā nāma vālakhilyā maharṣayaḥ prakāśamānā dṛśyante sūryavarṇāstapasvinaḥ|
translation: तत्र there, सूर्यवर्णाः those with the lustre of the Sungod, तपस्वीनः great ascetics, वैखानसा नाम named Vaikhanasas, वालखिल्याः महर्षयः Valakhilya sages, प्रकाशमानाः radiating, दृश्यन्ते appear.
explanation: 'Over there the great ascetics Vaikhanasas and Valakhilyas appear  like the radiating Sun.

shloka_text: अयं सुदर्शनो द्वीपः पुरो यस्य प्रकाशते।।4.40.60।। यस्मिं स्तेजश्च चक्षुश्च सर्वप्राणभृतामपि।
transliteration: ayaṃ sudarśano dvīpaḥ puro yasya prakāśate yasmiṃ stejaśca cakṣuśca sarvaprāṇabhṛtāmapi|
translation: यस्य its, पुरः in front of, सर्वप्राणभृतामपि  for all beings, चक्षुश्च the (ability to see with) eye, प्रकाशते shines, तत् that, तेजः glow, यस्मिन् therefore, अयम् this, सुदर्शनः द्वीपः island of Sudarsana.
explanation: 'The region in front of this mountain is called Sudarsana Island. This island is where the Sun who gives all beings the ability to see rises.

shloka_text: शैलस्य तस्य शृङ्गेषु कन्दरेषु वनेषु च।।4.40.61।। रावणस्सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः।
transliteration: śailasya tasya śṛṅgeṣu kandareṣu vaneṣu ca rāvaṇassaha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ|
translation: तस्य शैलस्य of that mountain, शृङ्गेषु on the peak, कन्दरेषु in the caves, वनेषु च in the forests, ततस्ततः here and there, रावणः Ravana, वैदेह्यासह with Vaidehi, मार्गितव्यः may be looked for.
explanation: You should search for Ravana and Vaidehi on the peak of that mountain, in the caves, in the forests here and there.

shloka_text: काञ्चनस्य च शैलस्य सूर्यस्य च महात्मनः।।4.40.62।। आविष्टा तेजसा सन्ध्या पूर्वा रक्ता प्रकाशते।
transliteration: kāñcanasya ca śailasya sūryasya ca mahātmanaḥ āviṣṭā tejasā sandhyā pūrvā raktā prakāśate|
translation: काञ्चनस्य of the golden, शैलस्य mountain's, महात्मनः of the great, सूर्यस्य च and Sun's, तेजसा with brightness, आविष्टा filled, पूर्वा सन्ध्या early morning twilight, रक्ता red in colour, प्रकाशते will be glowing.
explanation: 'The early morning twilight appears bright red because of the glow of the golden mountain as well as of the great Sungod.

shloka_text: पूर्वमेतत्कृतं द्वारं पृथिव्या भुवनस्य च।।4.40.63।। सूर्यस्योदयनं चैव पर्वा ह्येषा दिगुच्यते।
transliteration: pūrvametatkṛtaṃ dvāraṃ pṛthivyā bhuvanasya ca sūryasyodayanaṃ caiva parvā hyeṣā digucyate|
translation: पूर्वम् east, एतत् this, पृथिव्याः earth's, भुवनस्य for the world, द्वारम् entrance, सूर्यस्य Sun's, उदयनं च rise also, कृतम् was made, एषा this, पूर्वा दिक् eastern direction, उच्यते is being called.
explanation: 'Here is the entrance for the earth as well as for all the worlds and since the Sun also rises from this place it is called the eastern direction.

shloka_text: तस्य शैलस्य पृष्ठेषु निर्झरेषु गुहासु च।।4.40.64।। रावण स्सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः।
transliteration: tasya śailasya pṛṣṭheṣu nirjhareṣu guhāsu ca rāvaṇa ssaha vaidehyā mārgitavyastatastataḥ|
translation: तस्य शैलस्य this mountain's, पृष्ठेषु on the plain land, निर्झरेषु by the mountain streams, गुहासु च and in caves, वैदेह्या सह along with Vaidehi, रावणः Ravana, ततस्ततः all over, मार्गितव्यः should be searched.
explanation: 'You may look for Ravana and also for Vaidehi even behind the mountain on the plains and also near the mountain streams and caves all over.

shloka_text: ततः परमगम्या स्याद्दिक्पूर्वा त्रिदशावृता।।4.40.65।। रहिता चन्द्रसूर्याभ्यामदृश्या तिमिरावृता।
transliteration: tataḥ paramagamyā syāddikpūrvā tridaśāvṛtā rahitā candrasūryābhyāmadṛśyā timirāvṛtā|
translation: ततः परम् beyond that, त्रिदशावृता guarded by gods, चन्द्रसूर्याभ्याम् by Moon and Sun, रहिता not present, तिमिर darkness, आवृता pervaded by, पूर्वादिक् eastern direction, अगम्या स्यात् not possible to reach, अदृश्या invisible.
explanation: 'Beyond, there is no Sun or Moon. Darkness pervades. It is neither accessible nor visible. It is guarded by the gods.

shloka_text: शैलेषु तेषु सर्वेषु कन्दरेषु वनेषु च।।4.40.66।। ये च नोक्ता मया देशा विचेया तेषु जानकी।
transliteration: śaileṣu teṣu sarveṣu kandareṣu vaneṣu ca ye ca noktā mayā deśā viceyā teṣu jānakī|
translation: तेषु among those, शैलेषु on the mountains, सर्वेषु everywhere, कन्दरेषु in the caves, वनेषु च in the forests, मया my, ये those, देशाः spots, नोक्ताः not mentioned, तेषु in those places, जानकी Janaki, विचेया should be searched.
explanation: 'You should look for Janaki everywhere -- on the mountains, in the lakes and  in the places not indicated by me.

shloka_text: एतावद्वानरैश्शक्यं गन्तुं वानरपुङ्गवाः।।4.40.67।। अभास्करममर्यादं न जानीमस्ततः परम्।
transliteration: etāvadvānaraiśśakyaṃ gantuṃ vānarapuṅgavāḥ abhāskaramamaryādaṃ na jānīmastataḥ param|
translation: वानरपुङ्गवाः O chieftains of monkeys, एतावत् till there, वानरैः by monkeys, गन्तुम् to go, शक्यम् is possible, अभास्करम् where there is no Sunlight, अमर्यादं च devoid of boundaries, ततः परम् beyond that, न जानीमः is not known to us.
explanation: 'O chieftains monkeys can go that far. We know not what lies beyond those boundaries where no Sun shines.

shloka_text: अधिगम्य तु वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च।।4.40.68।। मासे पूर्णे निवर्तध्वमुदयं प्राप्य पर्वतम्।
transliteration: adhigamya tu vaidehīṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca māse pūrṇe nivartadhvamudayaṃ prāpya parvatam|
translation: उदयं पर्वतम् the mountain behind which the sun rises, प्राप्य after reaching, वैदेहीम् for Vaidehi, रावणस्य Ravana's, निलयं च home, अधिगम्य after reaching, मासे in one month, पूर्णे before completion, निवर्तध्वम् you may return.
explanation: 'Reaching the mountain behind which the sun rises, look for Vaidehi and the home of Ravana and return by the month's end.

shloka_text: ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न वस्तव्यं वसन्वध्यो भवेन्मम।।4.40.69।। सिद्धार्थास्सन्निवर्तध्वमधिगम्य तु मैथिलीम्।
transliteration: ūrdhvaṃ māsānna vastavyaṃ vasanvadhyo bhavenmama siddhārthāssannivartadhvamadhigamya tu maithilīm|
translation: मासात् ऊर्ध्वम् beyond one month, न वस्तव्यम् you should not stay away, वसन् while one stays, मम to me, वध्यः will be killed, सिद्धार्थाः accomplishing the goal, मैथिलीम् Maithili, अधिगम्य reaching, सन्निवर्तध्वम् return.
explanation: 'If you do not report within one month, you will be killed. May you see Maithili and come back after reaching the goal.

shloka_text: महेन्द्रकान्तां वनषण्डमण्डितां दिशं चरित्वा निपुणेन वानराः। अवाप्य सीतां रघुवंशजप्रियां ततो निवृत्तास्सुखिनो भविष्यथ।।4.40.70।।
transliteration: mahendrakāntāṃ vanaṣaṇḍamaṇḍitāṃ diśaṃ caritvā nipuṇena vānarāḥ| avāpya sītāṃ raghuvaṃśajapriyāṃ tato nivṛttāssukhino bhaviṣyatha
translation: वानराः O monkeys, महेन्द्रकान्ताम् Indra's beloved, वनषण्डमण्डिताम् bestowed with different kinds of forests and groves, दिशम् quarter, निपुणेन carefully, चरित्वा after going about, रघुवंशजप्रियाम् Rama's beloved, सीताम् Sita, अवाप्य after finding, ततः then, निवृत्ताः returning, सुखिनः happy ones, भविष्यथ you will be.
explanation: 'O monkeys go about the beloved quarter (east) of Indra bestowed with differnt kinds of forests and groves. Look out carefully for Rama's beloved Sita, spot her and return, you will live happily. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकांडे चत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortieth sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततः प्रस्थाप्य सुग्रीवस्तन्महद्वानरं बलम्। दक्षिणां प्रेषयामास वानरानभिलक्षितान्।।4.41.1।।
transliteration: tataḥ prasthāpya sugrīvastanmahadvānaraṃ balam| dakṣiṇāṃ preṣayāmāsa vānarānabhilakṣitān
translation: सुग्रीवः Sugriva, महत् great, तत् that, वानरं बलम् monkey army, प्रस्थाप्य after despatching, ततः then, अभिलक्षितान् those recognised for excellence, वानरान् monkeys, दक्षिणाम् southern direction, प्रेषयामास sent forth.
explanation: Sugriva then sends in the southern direction another vanara army known for their excellence.
comments: Sugriva sends another troop including Hanuaman, Nila, Angada and Jambavan in the southern direction

shloka_text: नील मग्निसुतं चैव हनुमन्तं च वानरम्। पितामहसुतं चैव जाम्बवन्तं महाबलम्।।4.41.2।। सुहोत्रं च शरारिं च शरगुल्मं तथैव च। गजं गवाक्षं गवयं सुषेणमृषभं तथा।।4.41.3।। मैन्दं च द्विविदं चैव विजयं गन्धमादनम्। उल्कामुखमसङ्गं च हुताशनसुतावुभौ।।4.41.4।। अङ्गदप्रमुखान्वीरान्वीर: कपिगणेश्वरः। वेगविक्रमसम्पन्नान्सन्दिदेश विशेषवित्।।4.41.5।।
transliteration: nīla magnisutaṃ caiva hanumantaṃ ca vānaram| pitāmahasutaṃ caiva jāmbavantaṃ mahābalam suhotraṃ ca śarāriṃ ca śaragulmaṃ tathaiva ca| gajaṃ gavākṣaṃ gavayaṃ suṣeṇamṛṣabhaṃ tathā maindaṃ ca dvividaṃ caiva vijayaṃ gandhamādanam| ulkāmukhamasaṅgaṃ ca hutāśanasutāvubhau aṅgadapramukhānvīrānvīra: kapigaṇeśvaraḥ| vegavikramasampannānsandideśa viśeṣavit
translation: वीरः hero, विशेषवित् extraordinary, कपिगणेश्वरः leader of the monkey army, अग्निसुतम् son of the firegod, नीलम् Nila, वानरम् monkey, हनुमन्तं च  and Hanumantha, पितामहसुतम् son of Brahma, महाबलम् of formidable strength, जाम्बवन्तं Jambavanta चैव also, सुहोत्रं च Suhotra and also, शरारिं च Sarari and, तथैव च so also, शरगुल्मम् Saragulma, गजम् Gaja, गवाक्षम् Gavaksha, गवयम् Gavaya, सुषेणम् Sushena, तथा so also, वृषभम् Vrisabha, मैन्दं च Mainda and, द्विविदं चैव Dvivida also, विजयम् Vijaya, गन्धमादनम् Gandhamadana, उल्कामुखम् Ulkamukha, असङ्गं च Asanga, हुताशनसुत son of firegod, उभौ both, अङ्गदप्रमुखान् Angada, वेगविक्रमसम्पन्नान् those endowed with speed and valour, वीरान् heroes, सन्दिदेश delivered the message.
explanation: The extraordinary Sugriva commanded Nila, son of the firegod, Hanuman, the formidable, Jambavan, son of Brahma, Suhotra, Sarari, Saragulma, Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Sushena, Vrishabam, Mainda, Dvivida, Vijaya, Gandhamadana, the two sons of Firegod, Ulkamuka and Asanga including Angada, leader of the group, to proceed. All of them were endowed with speed and valour.

shloka_text: तेषामग्रेसरं चैव महाबलमथाङ्गदम्। विधाय हरिवीराणामादिशद्दक्षिणां दिशम्।।4.41.6।।
transliteration: teṣāmagresaraṃ caiva mahābalamathāṅgadam| vidhāya harivīrāṇāmādiśaddakṣiṇāṃ diśam
translation: अथ then, तेषाम् of them, हरिवीराणाम् of those monkeys, महाबलम् one of formidable strength, अङ्गदम् Angada, अग्रेसरम् leader, दक्षिणां दिशम् southern direction, आदिशत् ordered.
explanation: Then Sugriva ordered mighty Angada to lead the group of the heroic monkeys in the southern direction.

shloka_text: ये केचन समुद्देशास्तस्यां दिशि सुदुर्गमाः। कपीशः कपिमुख्यानां स तेषां तानुदाहरत्।।4.41.7।।
transliteration: ye kecana samuddeśāstasyāṃ diśi sudurgamāḥ| kapīśaḥ kapimukhyānāṃ sa teṣāṃ tānudāharat
translation: तस्यां दिशि in that quarter, दुर्गमाः inaccessible, ये केचन those, समुद्देशाः spots, सः कपीशः the monkey king, कपिमुख्यानाम् to the chieftains of monkeys, तानुदाहरत् he gave an account.
explanation: Sugriva, the monkey king, explained to the monkey chiefs about the inaccessible places in the southern direction.

shloka_text: सहस्रशिरसं विन्ध्यं नानाद्रुमलतायुतम्। नर्मदां च नदीं रम्यां महोरगनिषेविताम्।।4.41.8।। ततो गोदावरीं रम्यां कृष्णवेणीं महानदीम्। वरदां च महाभागां महोरगनिषेविताम्।।4.41.9।। मेखलामुत्कलां चैव दशार्णनगराण्यपि। आश्ववन्तीमवन्तीं च सर्वामेवानुपश्यत।।4.41.10।।
transliteration: sahasraśirasaṃ vindhyaṃ nānādrumalatāyutam| narmadāṃ ca nadīṃ ramyāṃ mahoraganiṣevitām tato godāvarīṃ ramyāṃ kṛṣṇaveṇīṃ mahānadīm| varadāṃ ca mahābhāgāṃ mahoraganiṣevitām mekhalāmutkalāṃ caiva daśārṇanagarāṇyapi| āśvavantīmavantīṃ ca sarvāmevānupaśyata
translation: सहस्रशिरसम् of thousand peaks, नानाद्रुमलतायुतम् filled with several trees and creepers, विन्ध्यम् Vindhya, नर्मदां नदीं च and river Narmada, ततः then, रम्याम् delightful, गोदावरीम् Godavari, महानदीम् Mahanadi, कृष्णवेणीम् Krishnaveni, महाभागाम् Mahabhaga, महोरगनिषेविताम् inhabited by terrific serpents, वरदां च and Varada river, मेखलाम् river Mekhala, उत्कलां च एव Utkala also, दशार्णनगराण्यपि towns of Dasarna, आश्ववन्तीम् Asvavanti, अवन्तीम् Avanti, सर्वमेव all over, अनुपश्यत you may survey.
explanation: 'Search for Sita all over Vindhya of a thousand peaks filled with several trees and creepers, and along the river Narmada. Then proceed to Godavari, lovely Krishnaveni, Mahanadi, Varada and Mahabhaga inhabited by terrific serpents.You may search Mekhala, Utkala and Dasarna cities, Asvavanti and Avanti countries also.
