shloka_text: स तां भुजाभ्यां दीर्घाभ्यां पर्यष्वजत मारुतः। मन्मथाविष्टसर्वाङ्गो गतात्मा तामनिन्दिताम्।।4.66.15।।
transliteration: sa tāṃ bhujābhyāṃ dīrghābhyāṃ paryaṣvajata mārutaḥ| manmathāviṣṭasarvāṅgo gatātmā tāmaninditām
translation: अनिन्दिताम् blameless lady, ताम् her, गतात्मा lost his self, सः मारुतः that wind god, मन्मथाविष्टसर्वाङ्गः his whole body overpowered by love, दीर्घाभ्याम् with long ones, भुजाभ्याम् with shoulders, ताम् her, पर्यष्वजत embraced her.
explanation: 'The Windgod lost his control over himself. His whole being was overpowered by love for her beautiful, flawless body. He embraced her with his long arms.

shloka_text: सा तु तत्रैव सम्भ्रान्ता सुव्रता वाक्यमब्रवीत्। एकपत्नीव्रतमिदं को नाशयितुमिच्छति।।4.66.16।।
transliteration: sā tu tatraiva sambhrāntā suvratā vākyamabravīt| ekapatnīvratamidaṃ ko nāśayitumicchati
translation: तत्रैव on that spot itself, सम्भ्रान्ता bewildered lady, सुव्रता a chaste woman, सा तु she was, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said, इदम् this, एकपत्नीव्रतम् observing strict monoandry, कः who, नाशयितुम् to destroy, इच्छति is wishing?
explanation: 'She was bewildered by this and being chaste and strict observer of chastiny she said, 'Who is it that has destroyed my monoandry?

shloka_text: अञ्जनाया वच्शुत्वा मारुतः प्रत्यभाषत। न त्वां हिंसामि सुश्रोणि मा भूत्ते सुभगे भयम्।।4.66.17।।
transliteration: añjanāyā vacśutvā mārutaḥ pratyabhāṣata| na tvāṃ hiṃsāmi suśroṇi mā bhūtte subhage bhayam
translation: अञ्जनायाः Anjana's, वचः words, श्रुत्वा after hearing, मारुतः Windgod, प्रत्यभाषत replied, सुश्रोणि O woman of beautiful hips, त्वाम् you, न हिंसामि I do no harm, ते your, मनसः mind's, भयम् fear, मा भूत् do not entertain, सुभगे O auspicious lady
explanation: 'On hearing Anjana's words, the Windgod replied, ' O auspicious lady, I do you no harm, O lady of beautiful hips. I reached (enjoyed) you in mind, not body. You need not fear.'

shloka_text: मनसाऽस्मि गतो यत्त्वां परिष्वज्य यशस्विनीम्। वीर्यवान्बुद्धिसम्पन्न: पुत्रस्तव भविष्यति।।4.66.18।।
transliteration: manasā'smi gato yattvāṃ pariṣvajya yaśasvinīm| vīryavānbuddhisampanna: putrastava bhaviṣyati
translation: यशस्विनि O renowned woman, यत् such as, त्वाम् you, परिष्वज्य after embracing, मनसा mentally, गतः अस्मि I united with you, तव your, वीर्यवान् courageous, बुद्धिसम्पन्नः endowed with wisdom, पुत्रः son, भविष्यति will be born.
explanation: 'O renowned lady I have embraced you and united with you mentally (enjoyed you without physical contact).You will bring forth a son endowed with great wisdom and courage.

shloka_text: महासत्त्वो महातेजा महाबलपराक्रमः। लङ्घने प्लवने चैव भविष्यति हि मत्समः।।4.66.19।।
transliteration: mahāsattvo mahātejā mahābalaparākramaḥ| laṅghane plavane caiva bhaviṣyati hi matsamaḥ
translation: महासत्त्वः very powerful, महातेजाः highly lustrous one, महाबलपराक्रमः of great valour and strength, लङ्घने in jumping, प्लवने चैव even in leaping, हि मत्समः similar to me, भविष्यति he will be.
explanation: 'He will be very powerful, illustrious and will be of great valour and strength. He will be my equal in leaping and flying'.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता ततस्तुष्टा जननी ते महाकपे। गुहायां त्वां महाबाहो प्रजज्ञे प्लवगर्षभम्।।4.66.20।।
transliteration: evamuktā tatastuṣṭā jananī te mahākape| guhāyāṃ tvāṃ mahābāho prajajñe plavagarṣabham
translation: महाबाहो one of strong shoulders, महाकपे O great monkey, एवम् that way, उक्ता having been told, ते जननी your mother, तुष्टा pleased, ततः then, प्लवगर्षभम् bull among monkeys, त्वाम् you, गुहायाम् in the cave, प्रजज्ञे delivered you.
explanation: 'O great monkey O strongshouldered one having been assured that way, your mother was pleased and delivered you, a bull among monkeys, in a cave.

shloka_text: अभ्युत्थितं ततस्सूर्यं बालो दृष्ट्वा महावने। फलं चेति जिघृक्षुस्त्वमुत्प्लुत्याभ्युद्गतो दिवम्।।4.66.21।।
transliteration: abhyutthitaṃ tatassūryaṃ bālo dṛṣṭvā mahāvane| phalaṃ ceti jighṛkṣustvamutplutyābhyudgato divam
translation: ततः then, बालः a boy, त्वम् you, महावने in the deep forest, अभ्युत्थितम् rising, सूर्यम् Sun, दृष्ट्वा after seeing, फलं चेति treating it to be, जिघृक्षुः wished to seize, उत्प्लुत्य having jumped, दिवम् to sky, अभ्युद्गतः went flying.
explanation: 'On seeing the rising Sun in the deep forest, mistaking him to be a fruit, you wanted to seize it, when you were young.You suddenly flew into the sky and went flying towards the Sun.

shloka_text: शतानि त्रीणि गत्वाऽथ योजनानां महाकपे। तेजसा तस्य निर्धूतो न विषादं ततोगतः।।4.66.22।।
transliteration: śatāni trīṇi gatvā'tha yojanānāṃ mahākape| tejasā tasya nirdhūto na viṣādaṃ tatogataḥ
translation: महाकपे O great monkey, अथ then, योजनानाम् of yojanas, त्रीणि three, शतानि गत्वा after covering a distance of three hundred, तस्य his, तेजसा in brilliance, निर्धूतः you were pushed back, ततः then, विषादम् dull, न not, गतः attained.
explanation: 'O great monkey you went three hundred yojanas and were pushed back by the  Sun's radiance. Yet it did not leave you depressed.

shloka_text: तावदापपत स्तूर्णमन्तरिक्षं महाकपे। क्षिप्तमिन्द्रेण ते वज्रं कोपाविष्टेन धीमता।।4.66.23।।
transliteration: tāvadāpapata stūrṇamantarikṣaṃ mahākape| kṣiptamindreṇa te vajraṃ kopāviṣṭena dhīmatā
translation: महाकपे great monkey, तूर्णम् swiftly, अन्तरिक्षम् into space, कोपाविष्टेन in anger, धीमता by the wise, इन्द्रेण by Indra's, वज्रम् thunderbolt, ते at you, क्षिप्तम् hurled, तावत् so much, आपतत: while falling.
explanation: 'O great monkey while falling fast in space, wise Indra hurled his thunderbolt quickly at you, in anger.

shloka_text: तदा शैलाग्रशिखरे वामो हनुरभज्यत। ततो हि नामधेयं ते हनुमानिति कीर्त्यते।।4.66.24।।
transliteration: tadā śailāgraśikhare vāmo hanurabhajyata| tato hi nāmadheyaṃ te hanumāniti kīrtyate
translation: तदा then, शैलाग्रशिखरे on the edge of the mountain peak, वामः left, हनुः chin, अभज्यत was broken, ततः then, ते your, नामधेयम् named, हनुमानिति Hanuman, कीर्त्यते wellknown.
explanation: 'You fell on the edge of the mountain peak and your left chin  got broken. Since then you are widely known as Hanuman (one who has a wounded chin).

shloka_text: तस्त्वावि निहतं दृष्ट्वा वायुर्गन्धवहस्स्वयम्। त्रैलोक्ये भृशसङ्कृद्धो न ववौ वै प्रभञ्जनः।।4.66.25।।
transliteration: tastvāvi nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā vāyurgandhavahassvayam| trailokye bhṛśasaṅkṛddho na vavau vai prabhañjanaḥ
translation: ततः then, गन्धवहः carrier of fragrance (Windgod), प्रभञ्जनः one who breaks (trees), वायुः wind, त्वाम् you, निहतम् hit दृष्ट्वा seeing, स्वयम् himself, भृशसङ्कृद्धुः became very angry, त्रैलोक्यम् in the three worlds, न ववौवै (windgod) did not blow wind.
explanation: The Windgod who is a carrier of fragrance and breaker of trees became very angry on seeing (the injury on) you and stopped blowing in the three worlds.

shloka_text: सम्भ्रान्ताश्च सूरास्सर्वे त्रैलोक्ये क्षुभिते सति। प्रसादयन्ति संक्रुद्धं मारुतं भुवनेश्वराः।।4.66.26।।
transliteration: sambhrāntāśca sūrāssarve trailokye kṣubhite sati| prasādayanti saṃkruddhaṃ mārutaṃ bhuvaneśvarāḥ
translation: त्रैलोक्ये in all the three worlds, क्षुभिते सति  disturbed, भुवनेश्वराः all lords of the world, सर्वे all, सुराः Gods, संभ्रान्ताः became uneasy, संक्रुद्धम् angry, मारुतम् Maruta, प्रसादयन्ति propitiated.
explanation: When the three worlds were thrown into turmoil, all the gods and lords of the world, alarmed, propitiated the angered Wind-god.

shloka_text: प्रसादिते च पवने ब्रह्मा तुभ्यं वरं ददौ। अशस्त्रवध्यतां तात समरे सत्यविक्रम।।4.66.27।।
transliteration: prasādite ca pavane brahmā tubhyaṃ varaṃ dadau| aśastravadhyatāṃ tāta samare satyavikrama
translation: समरे in war, सत्यविक्रम O truly valiant, तात o dear, पवने when the Windgod, प्रसादिते propitiated, ब्रह्मा Brahma, तुभ्यम् to you, अशस्त्रवध्यताम् cannot be killed by a weapon, वरम् boon, ददौ he gave.
explanation: 'O dear when the Windgod was pleased, Brahma gave a boon to you, to appease his anger. The boon made you truly valiant so that you cannot be struck by any weapon and killed.

shloka_text: वज्रस्य च निपातेन विरुजं त्वां समीक्ष्य च। सहस्रनेत्रः प्रीतात्मा ददौ ते वरमुत्तमम्।।4.66.28।। स्वच्छन्दतश्च मरणं तेभूयादिति वै प्रभो।
transliteration: vajrasya ca nipātena virujaṃ tvāṃ samīkṣya ca| sahasranetraḥ prītātmā dadau te varamuttamam svacchandataśca maraṇaṃ tebhūyāditi vai prabho|
translation: प्रभो O lord, सहस्रनेत्रः the thousandeyed, वज्रस्य thunderbolt's, निपातेन by striking, त्वाम् you, विरुजम् not hurt, समीक्ष्य च on observing that, प्रीतात्मा a pleased self, तव your, स्वच्छन्दतः at your wish, मरणम् death, ते you, भूयात् will be, इति thus, उत्तमम् best, वरम् boon, ददौ gave.
explanation: 'O lord observing that you are not hurt even when struck by the thunderbolt, Indra offered, one of the best boons to you, to choose to die only when you wish.

shloka_text: स त्वं केसरिणः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजो भीमविक्रमः।।4.66.29।। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तेजसा चापि तत्समः। त्वं हि वायुसुतो वत्स प्लवने चापि तत्समः।।4.66.30।।
transliteration: sa tvaṃ kesariṇaḥ putraḥ kṣetrajo bhīmavikramaḥ mārutasyaurasaḥ putrastejasā cāpi tatsamaḥ| tvaṃ hi vāyusuto vatsa plavane cāpi tatsamaḥ
translation: भीमविक्रमः of terrific strength, सः त्वम् that you are, केसरिणः Kesari's, क्षेत्रजः the offspring (one of twelve sons according to Hindu scriptures), पुत्रः son, मारुतस्य Marutha's, औरसः पुत्रः lawful son, तेजसा with brilliance, तत्समश्च also equal to him, वत्स dear, वायुसुतः son of the Windgod, त्वम् you, प्लवने in flying, च अपि also, तत्समः हि equal to.
explanation: 'You are a son of Kesari endowed with terrific strength and a lawful son of Maruta also. You are, therefore, equal to the very Windgod in flying and in brilliance.

shloka_text: स त्वं केसरिणः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजो भीमविक्रमः।।4.66.29।। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तेजसा चापि तत्समः। त्वं हि वायुसुतो वत्स प्लवने चापि तत्समः।।4.66.30।।
transliteration: sa tvaṃ kesariṇaḥ putraḥ kṣetrajo bhīmavikramaḥ mārutasyaurasaḥ putrastejasā cāpi tatsamaḥ| tvaṃ hi vāyusuto vatsa plavane cāpi tatsamaḥ
translation: भीमविक्रमः of terrific strength, सः त्वम् that you are, केसरिणः Kesari's, क्षेत्रजः the offspring (one of twelve sons according to Hindu scriptures), पुत्रः son, मारुतस्य Marutha's, औरसः पुत्रः lawful son, तेजसा with brilliance, तत्समश्च also equal to him, वत्स dear, वायुसुतः son of the Windgod, त्वम् you, प्लवने in flying, च अपि also, तत्समः हि equal to.
explanation: 'You are a son of Kesari endowed with terrific strength and a lawful son of Maruta also. You are, therefore, equal to the very Windgod in flying and in brilliance.

shloka_text: वयमद्य गतप्राणा भवान्नस्त्रातु साम्प्रतम्। दाक्ष्यविक्रमसम्पन्नः कपिराज इवापरः।।4.66.31।।
transliteration: vayamadya gataprāṇā bhavānnastrātu sāmpratam| dākṣyavikramasampannaḥ kapirāja ivāparaḥ
translation: अद्य now, वयम् we, गतप्राणाः almost lost our life, भवान् you, साम्प्रतम् at present, त्रातु you may save us, दाक्ष्यविक्रमसम्पन्नः fully endowed with valour and courage, अपरः another, कपिराजः monkey king, इव like.
explanation: 'Now we have almost lost our life.You are our saviour like another monkeyking (like Garuda, king of birds).You are fully endowed with valour and courage.

shloka_text: त्रिविक्रमे मया तात सशैलवनकानना। त्रिस्सप्तकृत्वः पृथिवी परिक्रान्ता प्रदक्षिणम्।।4.66.32।।
transliteration: trivikrame mayā tāta saśailavanakānanā| trissaptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivī parikrāntā pradakṣiṇam
translation: तात dear, त्रिविक्रमे when Visnu took three strides, सशैलवनकानना with its mountains, trees and forests, पृथिवी the whole earth, मया by me, त्रिस्सप्तकृत्वः twenty one times, प्रदक्षिणम् परिक्रान्ता circumambulated.
explanation: 'O dear when Visnu (Vamana incarnate) took three strides I circumambulated the whole earth including its mountains and trees twentyone times.

shloka_text: तथा चौषधयोऽस्माभिस्सञ्चिता देवशासनात्। निष्पन्नममृतं याभिस्तदासीन्नो महद्बलम्।।4.66.33।।
transliteration: tathā cauṣadhayo'smābhissañcitā devaśāsanāt| niṣpannamamṛtaṃ yābhistadāsīnno mahadbalam
translation: तदा then, देवशासनात् by the command of the gods, याभिः by those, अमृतम् nectar, निष्पन्नम् produced, ओषधयः herbs, अस्माभिः by us, सञ्चिताः are collected, तदानीम्  then, नः for us, बलम् strength, महत् great.
explanation: 'Then on receiving orders from the gods, we collected medicinal herbs and nectar which gave us great strength.

shloka_text: स इदानीमहं वृद्धः परिहीनपराक्रमः। साम्प्रतं कालमस्माकं भवान्सर्वगुणान्वितः।।4.66.34।।
transliteration: sa idānīmahaṃ vṛddhaḥ parihīnaparākramaḥ| sāmprataṃ kālamasmākaṃ bhavānsarvaguṇānvitaḥ
translation: इदानीम् as such, वृद्धः old, सः अहम् I being, परिहीनपराक्रमः my valour is depleted, साम्प्रतं कालम् at this time, भवान् you have, अस्माकम् for us, सर्वगुणान्वितः endowed with all qualities.
explanation: 'I have become old and my valour is depleted. At this time you are the sole resort for us. You have all the necessary qualities.

shloka_text: तद्विजृम्भस्व विक्रान्त: प्लवतामुत्तमो ह्यसि। त्वद्वीर्यं द्रष्टुकामा हि सर्वा वानरवाहिनी।।4.66.35।।
transliteration: tadvijṛmbhasva vikrānta: plavatāmuttamo hyasi| tvadvīryaṃ draṣṭukāmā hi sarvā vānaravāhinī
translation: विक्रान्तः cheer up, तत् that, विजृम्भस्व expand yourself, प्लवताम् among the leaping ones, उत्तमः the best, असि हि you are, सर्वा entire, वानरवाहिनी monkey army, त्वद्वीर्यम् your valour, द्रष्टुकामा हि desiring to see.
explanation: 'Cheer up and advance.You are the best among the creatures that can leap.The entire army of monkeys want to see your valour.

shloka_text: उत्तिष्ठ हरिशार्दूल लङ्घयस्व महार्णवम्। परा हि सर्वभूतानां हनुमन्या गतिस्तव।।4.66.36।।
transliteration: uttiṣṭha hariśārdūla laṅghayasva mahārṇavam| parā hi sarvabhūtānāṃ hanumanyā gatistava
translation: हरिशार्दूल O tiger among monkeys, हनुमन् O Hanuman, उत्तिष्ठ rise up, महार्णवम् great ocean, लङ्घयस्व cross, तव your, या such, गतिः capacity, सर्वभूतानाम् among all beings, परा हि indeed supreme.
explanation: 'O Hanuman, tiger among monkeys, rise up and cross this great ocean.You have that supreme capacity among all beings.

shloka_text: विषण्णा हरयस्सर्वे हनुमन्किमुपेक्षसे। विक्रमस्व महावेगो विष्णुस्त्रीन्विक्रमानिव।।4.66.37।।
transliteration: viṣaṇṇā harayassarve hanumankimupekṣase| vikramasva mahāvego viṣṇustrīnvikramāniva
translation: हनुमन् O Hanuman, सर्वे all, हरयः monkeys, विषण्णाः are dejected, किम् why, उपेक्षसे do you delay, महावेग O warrior of great speed, विष्णुः Visnu, त्रीन् three, विक्रमानिव like Trivikrama, विक्रमस्व you move fast.
explanation: 'O Hanuman All the monkeys look dejected. Why do you delay? O warrior, act quick with your rapid speed like Trivikrama who took three strides that covered the entire universe'.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा जृम्भमाणं ते क्रमितुं शतयोजनम्। वीर्येणापूर्यमाणं च सहसा वानरोत्तमम्।।4.67.1।। सहसा शोकमुत्सृज्य प्रहर्षेण समन्विताः। विनेदुस्तुष्टुवुश्चापि हनूमन्तं महाबलम्।।4.67.2।।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā jṛmbhamāṇaṃ te kramituṃ śatayojanam| vīryeṇāpūryamāṇaṃ ca sahasā vānarottamam sahasā śokamutsṛjya praharṣeṇa samanvitāḥ| vinedustuṣṭuvuścāpi hanūmantaṃ mahābalam
translation: शतयोजनम् hundred yojanas, क्रमितुम् to cross, जृम्भमाणम् enlarging, सहसा at once, वीर्येण in strength, आपूर्यमाणं च and being filled, वानरोत्तमम् best of monkeys, महाबलम् a warrior of great strength, तं हनूमन्तम् he, Hanuman, दृष्ट्वा seeing, ते those monkeys, सहसा all at once, शोकम् grief, उत्सृज्य gave up, प्रहर्षेण with joy, समन्विताः endowed, विनेदुः screamed aloud, तुष्टुवुश्चापि also propitiated him.
explanation: 'In order to cross a hundred yojanas, Hanuman, the best of monkeys expanded his  might and strength. Seeing him, a warrior of great strength, all the monkeys, filled with enthusiasm at once gave up grief and collected together.They rejoiced and propitiated him screaming aloud.
comments: Hanuman displays his immeasurable might and proceeds to mount Mahendra

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा जृम्भमाणं ते क्रमितुं शतयोजनम्। वीर्येणापूर्यमाणं च सहसा वानरोत्तमम्।।4.67.1।। सहसा शोकमुत्सृज्य प्रहर्षेण समन्विताः। विनेदुस्तुष्टुवुश्चापि हनूमन्तं महाबलम्।।4.67.2।।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā jṛmbhamāṇaṃ te kramituṃ śatayojanam| vīryeṇāpūryamāṇaṃ ca sahasā vānarottamam sahasā śokamutsṛjya praharṣeṇa samanvitāḥ| vinedustuṣṭuvuścāpi hanūmantaṃ mahābalam
translation: शतयोजनम् hundred yojanas, क्रमितुम् to cross, जृम्भमाणम् enlarging, सहसा at once, वीर्येण in strength, आपूर्यमाणं च and being filled, वानरोत्तमम् best of monkeys, महाबलम् a warrior of great strength, तं हनूमन्तम् he, Hanuman, दृष्ट्वा seeing, ते those monkeys, सहसा all at once, शोकम् grief, उत्सृज्य gave up, प्रहर्षेण with joy, समन्विताः endowed, विनेदुः screamed aloud, तुष्टुवुश्चापि also propitiated him.
explanation: 'In order to cross a hundred yojanas, Hanuman, the best of monkeys expanded his  might and strength. Seeing him, a warrior of great strength, all the monkeys, filled with enthusiasm at once gave up grief and collected together.They rejoiced and propitiated him screaming aloud.
comments: Hanuman displays his immeasurable might and proceeds to mount Mahendra

shloka_text: प्रहृष्टा विस्मिताश्चैव वीक्षन्ते स्म समन्ततः। त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहं नारायणमिव प्रजाः।।4.67.3।।
transliteration: prahṛṣṭā vismitāścaiva vīkṣante sma samantataḥ| trivikramakṛtotsāhaṃ nārāyaṇamiva prajāḥ
translation: समन्ततः collected together, प्रहृष्टाः happily, विस्मिताश्चैव wonderstruck, प्रजाः people,  त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहम् Lord Visnu's enthusiasm in taking three strides, नारायणमिव like Lord Narayana, वीक्षन्ते स्म they observed.
explanation: The monkeys collected together happily, gazing at Hanuman.They were wonderstruck to see Hanuman in that huge form, just as all beings were when they saw Lord Narayana in his incarnation of Vamana.

shloka_text: संस्तूयमानो हनुमान्व्यवर्धत महाबलः। समाविध्य च लाङ्गूलं हर्षाद्बलमुपेयिवान्।।4.67.4।।
transliteration: saṃstūyamāno hanumānvyavardhata mahābalaḥ| samāvidhya ca lāṅgūlaṃ harṣādbalamupeyivān
translation: महाबलः mighty, हनुमान् Hanuman, संस्तूयमानः being praised, हर्षात् joyfully, बलम् strength, उपेयिवान् assumed, लाङ्गूलम् tail, समाविध्य whirling, व्यवर्धत grew.
explanation: The monkeys praised the mighty Hanuman as he grew in size whirling his tail around joyfully.

shloka_text: तस्य संस्तूयमानस्य सर्वैर्वानरपुङ्गवैः। तेजसापूर्यमाणस्य रूपमासीदनुत्तमम्।।4.67.5।।
transliteration: tasya saṃstūyamānasya sarvairvānarapuṅgavaiḥ| tejasāpūryamāṇasya rūpamāsīdanuttamam
translation: सर्वैः by all, वानरपुङ्गवैः by monkey leaders, संस्तूयमानस्य of him being praised, तेजसा with lustre, पूर्यमाणस्य who was filled, तस्य his, रूपम् body, अनुत्तमम् excellent, आसीत् became.
explanation: As Hanuman was being praised by the monkey leaders, his body filled with lustre. It looked excellent.

shloka_text: यथा विजृम्भते सिंहो विवृद्धो गिरिगह्वरे। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तथा सम्प्रति जृम्भते।।4.67.6।।
transliteration: yathā vijṛmbhate siṃho vivṛddho girigahvare| mārutasyaurasaḥ putrastathā samprati jṛmbhate
translation: विवृद्धः grown, गिरिगह्वरे in a mountain cave, सिंहः lion, यथा as, विजृम्भते he stretches himself, मारुतस्य Windgod's, औरसः पुत्रः lawful son, सम्प्रति at that time, तथा like that, जृम्भते grew.
explanation: Just as a lion grown in a mountain cave stretches its body, the Windgod's son stretched  (his limbs) at that time.

shloka_text: अशोभत मुखं तस्य जृम्भमाणस्य धीमतः। अम्बरीषमिवाऽदीप्तं विधूम इव पावकः।।4.67.7।।
transliteration: aśobhata mukhaṃ tasya jṛmbhamāṇasya dhīmataḥ| ambarīṣamivā'dīptaṃ vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ
translation: जृम्भमाणस्य on expansion, धीमतः of the wise person, तस्य his, मुखम् face, आदीप्तम्  glowing, अम्बरीषमिव like a burning oven, विधूमः smokeless, पावकः इव firelike, अशोभत was shining.
explanation: On expansion, wise Hanuman's face was bright, glowing like a burning oven and  shining like smokeless fire.

shloka_text: हरीणामुत्थितो मध्यात्सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः। अभिवाद्य हरीन्वृद्धान्हनुमानिदमब्रवीत्।।4.67.8।।
transliteration: harīṇāmutthito madhyātsamprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ| abhivādya harīnvṛddhānhanumānidamabravīt
translation: हरीणाम् from the monkeys, मध्यात् from the midst, उत्थितः he rose, सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः with the hair bristling on the body, हनुमान् Hanuman, वृद्धान् elderly, हरीन् monkeys (Jambavan), अभिवाद्य saluted reverentially, इदम् this word, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Hanuman risen from the midst of the monkeys with his hair bristling on the body (due to expansion of body), saluted reverentially to the elderly monkey Jambavan and said :

shloka_text: अरुजत्सर्वताग्राणि हुताशनसखोऽनिलः। बलवानप्रमेयश्च वायुराकाशगोचरः।।4.67.9।।
transliteration: arujatsarvatāgrāṇi hutāśanasakho'nilaḥ| balavānaprameyaśca vāyurākāśagocaraḥ
translation: हुताशनसखः friend of fire, हुताशन the consumer of oblations, बलवान् powerful one, अप्रमेयः च and immesurable, आकाशगोचरः one who wanders in the sky, अनिलः fire, वायुः wind, सर्वताग्राणि mountain tops, अरुजत् shattered.
explanation: 'The Windgod is a friend of fire who is a powerful consumer of oblations. His strength is immeasurable. He wanders in the sky and shatters the mountain tops.

shloka_text: तस्याहं शीघ्रवेगस्य शीघ्रगस्य महात्मनः। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रः प्लवनेनास्मि तत्समः।।4.67.10।।
transliteration: tasyāhaṃ śīghravegasya śīghragasya mahātmanaḥ| mārutasyaurasaḥ putraḥ plavanenāsmi tatsamaḥ
translation: शीघ्रवेगस्य swiftmoving god's, शीघ्रगस्य of a swift one, महात्मनः of a great one, तस्य his, मारुतस्य Windgod's, औरसः पुत्रः lawfulson, अहम् I am, प्लवनेन in leaping, तत्समः equal to him, अस्मि I am.
explanation: 'I am the lawfulson of the swiftmoving Windgod, Maruta, comparable to him in leaping.

shloka_text: उत्सहेयं हि विस्तीर्णमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम्। मेरुं गिरिमसङ्गेन परिगन्तुं सहस्रशः।।4.67.11।।
transliteration: utsaheyaṃ hi vistīrṇamālikhantamivāmbaram| meruṃ girimasaṅgena parigantuṃ sahasraśaḥ
translation: विस्तीर्णम् vast, expansive, अम्बरम् sky, अलिखन्तमिव as if rubbing , मेरुं गिरिम् Meru mount, असंगेन without touching, सहस्रशः thousand times, परिगन्तुम् can go round, उत्सहेयं हि I wish with all enthusiasm.
explanation: 'I can with all enthusiasm go round the vast mount Meru a thousand times without resting on it which is as though scratching the sky.

shloka_text: बाहुवेगप्रणुन्नेन सागरेणाहमुत्सहे। समाप्लावयितुं लोकं सपर्वतनदीह्रदम्।।4.67.12।।
transliteration: bāhuvegapraṇunnena sāgareṇāhamutsahe| samāplāvayituṃ lokaṃ saparvatanadīhradam
translation: अहम् I, बाहुवेगप्रणुन्नेन can drive away with my arms with high speed, सागरेण the ocean, सपर्वतनदीह्रदम् with mountains, rivers and lakes, लोकम् world, प्लावयितुम् to submerge, उत्सहे eager.
explanation: 'I can submerge this world including its mountains rivers and lakes. I can push back the sea waters quickly with my arms.

shloka_text: ममोरुजङ्घावेगेन भविष्यति समुत्थितः। सम्मूर्च्छितमहाग्राहस्समुद्रो वरुणालयः।।4.67.13।।
transliteration: mamorujaṅghāvegena bhaviṣyati samutthitaḥ| sammūrcchitamahāgrāhassamudro varuṇālayaḥ
translation: वरुणालयः  abode of Varuna,ocean समुद्रः ocean, मम my, ऊरुजङ्घावेगेन with the thrust of my thighs and calf muscles, समुत्थितः will rise up, सम्मूर्च्छितमहाग्राहः the mighty sea crocodiles stunned by the force, भविष्यति it will be.
explanation: 'Thrust by my thighs,the ocean will rise up, carrying with it the shanks and  mighty crocodiles stunned by the force.

shloka_text: पन्नगाशनमाकाशे पतन्तं पक्षिसेविते। वैनतेयमहं शक्तः परिगन्तुं सहस्रशः।।4.67.14।।
transliteration: pannagāśanamākāśe patantaṃ pakṣisevite| vainateyamahaṃ śaktaḥ parigantuṃ sahasraśaḥ
translation: पन्नगाशनम् a consumer of snakes, the Garuda, पक्षिसेविते occupied by birds, आकाशे in the sky, पतन्तम् flying, वैनतेयम् to son of Vinata (Garuda), सहस्रशः a thousand times, परिगन्तुम् to go round, अहम् I, शक्तः able.
explanation: 'I am capable of circumambulating a thousand times the great Garuda who consumes snakes and flies in the sky, the abode of birds.

shloka_text: उदयात्प्रस्थितं वापि ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्। अनस्तमितमादित्यमभिगन्तुं समुत्सहे।।4.67.15।। ततो भूमिमसंस्पृश्य पुनरागन्तुमुत्सहे। प्रवेगेनैव महता भीमेन प्लवगर्षभाः।।4.67.16।।
transliteration: udayātprasthitaṃ vāpi jvalantaṃ raśmimālinam| anastamitamādityamabhigantuṃ samutsahe tato bhūmimasaṃspṛśya punarāgantumutsahe| pravegenaiva mahatā bhīmena plavagarṣabhāḥ
translation: प्लवगर्षभाः O bull among monkeys, उदयात् from the mountain behind which the sun rises, प्रस्थितम् starts, ज्वलन्तम् blazing, रश्मिमालिनम् with rays, आदित्यम् the Sun, अनस्तमितम् before he sets, अभिगन्तुम् to approach, अहम् I, उत्सहे rise, ततः then, भूमिम् earth, अस्पृष्ट्वा without touching, भीमेन with a terrific, महता with great, प्रवेगेनैव with the same high speed, पुनः again, आगन्तुम् to return, उत्सहे I desire.
explanation: 'O bull among monkeys when the Sun rises from behind the eastern mountain it is possible for me to start with him and go to the western horizon and return before the blazing Sun with its beams of light sets. It is also possible for me to descend to  the earth with the same speed and return to the Sun without touching the earth.

shloka_text: उदयात्प्रस्थितं वापि ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्। अनस्तमितमादित्यमभिगन्तुं समुत्सहे।।4.67.15।। ततो भूमिमसंस्पृश्य पुनरागन्तुमुत्सहे। प्रवेगेनैव महता भीमेन प्लवगर्षभाः।।4.67.16।।
transliteration: udayātprasthitaṃ vāpi jvalantaṃ raśmimālinam| anastamitamādityamabhigantuṃ samutsahe tato bhūmimasaṃspṛśya punarāgantumutsahe| pravegenaiva mahatā bhīmena plavagarṣabhāḥ
translation: प्लवगर्षभाः O bull among monkeys, उदयात् from the mountain behind which the sun rises, प्रस्थितम् starts, ज्वलन्तम् blazing, रश्मिमालिनम् with rays, आदित्यम् the Sun, अनस्तमितम् before he sets, अभिगन्तुम् to approach, अहम् I, उत्सहे rise, ततः then, भूमिम् earth, अस्पृष्ट्वा without touching, भीमेन with a terrific, महता with great, प्रवेगेनैव with the same high speed, पुनः again, आगन्तुम् to return, उत्सहे I desire.
explanation: 'O bull among monkeys when the Sun rises from behind the eastern mountain it is possible for me to start with him and go to the western horizon and return before the blazing Sun with its beams of light sets. It is also possible for me to descend to  the earth with the same speed and return to the Sun without touching the earth.

shloka_text: उत्सहेयमतिक्रान्तुं सर्वानाकाशगोचरान्। सागरं क्षोभयिष्यामि दारयिष्यामि मेदिनीम्।।4.67.17।।
transliteration: utsaheyamatikrāntuṃ sarvānākāśagocarān| sāgaraṃ kṣobhayiṣyāmi dārayiṣyāmi medinīm
translation: आकाशगोचरान् those that fly in the sky, सर्वान् all, अतिक्रान्तुम् to overtake, उत्सहेयम् easily, सागरं ocean, क्षोभयिष्यामि I will stir up, मेदिनीम् earth, दारयिष्यामि I will tear up.
explanation: 'If I rise up, I can overtake all those creatures flying in the sky and from there I can stir up the ocean and tear up the earth easily.

shloka_text: पर्वतांश्चूर्णयिष्यामि प्लवमानः प्लवङ्गमाः। हरिष्याम्यूरुवेगेन प्लवमानो महार्णवम्।।4.67.18।।
transliteration: parvatāṃścūrṇayiṣyāmi plavamānaḥ plavaṅgamāḥ| hariṣyāmyūruvegena plavamāno mahārṇavam
translation: प्लवङ्गमाः O monkeys, प्लवमानः while I leap, पर्वतान् mountains, चूर्णयिष्यामि can crush them to powder, प्लवमानः when I leap, ऊरुवेगेन with the force of my thighs, महार्णवम् vast ocean, हरिष्यामि can pull with me.
explanation: 'O monkeys when I leap, I can crush the mountains into powder and pull the vast ocean with me with the force of my thighs.

shloka_text: लतानां विविधं पुष्पं पादपानां च सर्वशः। अनुयास्यन्ति मामद्य प्लवमानं विहायसा।।4.67.19।।
transliteration: latānāṃ vividhaṃ puṣpaṃ pādapānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ| anuyāsyanti māmadya plavamānaṃ vihāyasā
translation: अद्य now, विहायसा through the sky, प्लवमानम् as I leap, माम् me, लतानाम् of creepers, पादपानां च and of trees, विविधम् many, पुष्पम् flower, सर्वशः all over, अनुयास्यन्ति will follow me.
explanation: And then as I leap through the sky flowers of many kinds of creepers and trees will follow me.

shloka_text: भविष्यति हि मे पन्थास्स्वातेः पन्था इवाम्बरे। चरन्तं घोरमाकाशमुत्पतिष्यन्तमेव वा।।4.67.20।। द्रक्ष्यन्ति निपतिष्यन्तं च सर्वभूतानि वानराः।
transliteration: bhaviṣyati hi me panthāssvāteḥ panthā ivāmbare| carantaṃ ghoramākāśamutpatiṣyantameva vā drakṣyanti nipatiṣyantaṃ ca sarvabhūtāni vānarāḥ|
translation: वानराः monkeys अम्बरे in the sky, मे I, पन्थाः path, स्वातेः of the constellation of Swati, पन्थाः इव like the path, भविष्यति will be, घोरम् terrific, आकाशम् sky, उत्पतिष्यन्तमेव च as I am flying upward, चरन्तम् while I am moving, निपतिष्यन्तम् while I am descending, सर्वभूतानि all creatures, द्रक्ष्यन्ति will see me.
explanation: 'O monkey when I fly upward in the dreadful sky or descend down, all creatures will see me, for my path will be the path of the constellation of Swati (a group of stars).

shloka_text: महामेरुप्रतीकाशं मां द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः।।4.67.21।। दिवमावृत्य गच्छन्तं ग्रसमानमिवाम्बरम्।
transliteration: mahāmerupratīkāśaṃ māṃ drakṣyatha vānarāḥ divamāvṛtya gacchantaṃ grasamānamivāmbaram|
translation: वानरा: O monkeys, महामेरुप्रतीकाशम् like the great mount Meru, दिवम् sky, आवृत्य after enveloping, गच्छन्तम् while I go, अम्बरम् the sky, ग्रसमानम् इव like the one swallowing the sky, माम् me, द्रक्ष्यथ you will see.
explanation: 'O monkeys when I fly in the sky like the great mount Meru, you will see me as if I am swallowing the sky because I will be enveloping it with my strides.

shloka_text: विधमिष्यामि जीमूतान्कम्पयिष्यामि पर्वतान्।।4.67.22।। सागरं शोषयिष्यामि प्लवमानस्समाहितः।
transliteration: vidhamiṣyāmi jīmūtānkampayiṣyāmi parvatān sāgaraṃ śoṣayiṣyāmi plavamānassamāhitaḥ|
translation: समाहितः a composed self, प्लवमानः while I am leaping, जीमतान् clouds, विधमिष्यामि I scatter them up,पर्वतान् all mountains, कम्पयिष्यामि I will shake up, सागरम् ocean, शोषयिष्यामि I will agitate
explanation: Leaping in concentration, I shall scatter the clouds, shake the mountains, and dry up the ocean.

shloka_text: वैनतेयस्य या शक्तिर्मम सा मारुतस्य वा।।4.67.23।। ऋते सुपर्णराजानं मारुतं वा महाजवम्। न तद्भूतं प्रपश्यामि यन्मां प्लुतमनुव्रजेत्।।4.67.24।।
transliteration: vainateyasya yā śaktirmama sā mārutasya vā ṛte suparṇarājānaṃ mārutaṃ vā mahājavam| na tadbhūtaṃ prapaśyāmi yanmāṃ plutamanuvrajet
translation: वैनतेयस्य Garuda's, मारुतस्य वा Maruta's, या such, शक्तिः capacity, सा that, मम my, प्लुतम् flying, माम् me, यत् such, भूतम् a creature, अनुव्रजेत् that can follow, तत् that, सुपर्णराजानम् king of vultures, महाजवम् speedy, मारुतं वा ऋते or excepting the wind, न प्रपश्यामि I do not see.
explanation: 'Only Garuda and Maruta have the capacity to fly like me. No one other than the king of vultures and the Windgod have the speed to fly like me.

shloka_text: वैनतेयस्य या शक्तिर्मम सा मारुतस्य वा।।4.67.23।। ऋते सुपर्णराजानं मारुतं वा महाजवम्। न तद्भूतं प्रपश्यामि यन्मां प्लुतमनुव्रजेत्।।4.67.24।।
transliteration: vainateyasya yā śaktirmama sā mārutasya vā ṛte suparṇarājānaṃ mārutaṃ vā mahājavam| na tadbhūtaṃ prapaśyāmi yanmāṃ plutamanuvrajet
translation: वैनतेयस्य Garuda's, मारुतस्य वा Maruta's, या such, शक्तिः capacity, सा that, मम my, प्लुतम् flying, माम् me, यत् such, भूतम् a creature, अनुव्रजेत् that can follow, तत् that, सुपर्णराजानम् king of vultures, महाजवम् speedy, मारुतं वा ऋते or excepting the wind, न प्रपश्यामि I do not see.
explanation: 'Only Garuda and Maruta have the capacity to fly like me. No one other than the king of vultures and the Windgod have the speed to fly like me.

shloka_text: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण निरालम्बनमम्बरम्। सहसा निपतिष्यामि घनाद्विद्युदिवोत्थिता।।4.67.25।।
transliteration: nimeṣāntaramātreṇa nirālambanamambaram| sahasā nipatiṣyāmi ghanādvidyudivotthitā
translation: घनात् from the, उत्थिता generated, विद्युदिव like the lightning, निमेषान्तरमात्रेण in less than a  moment, सहसा at once, निरालम्बनम् that which has no support, अम्बरम् sky, निपतिष्यामि I will land.
explanation: 'Just as the lightning generated by the clouds lands at once flying in the sky without any support I can also land in less than a moment.

shloka_text: भविष्यति हि मे रूपं प्लवमानस्य सागरे। विष्णोर्विक्रममाणस्य पुरा त्रीन्विक्रमानिव।।4.67.26।।
transliteration: bhaviṣyati hi me rūpaṃ plavamānasya sāgare| viṣṇorvikramamāṇasya purā trīnvikramāniva
translation: सागरे in the ocean, प्लवमानस्य while I am leaping over, मे my, रूपम् form, पुरा earlier, त्रीन् three, विक्रमान् strides, प्रक्रममाणस्य who advanced, विष्णोः इव like Visnu, भविष्यति will be
explanation: As I leap over the ocean, my form will be like that of Vishnu of old measuring out his three strides.

shloka_text: बुद्ध्या चाहं प्रपश्यामि मनश्चेष्टा च मे तथा। अहं द्रक्ष्यामि वैदेहीं प्रमोदध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः।।4.67.27।।
transliteration: buddhyā cāhaṃ prapaśyāmi manaśceṣṭā ca me tathā| ahaṃ drakṣyāmi vaidehīṃ pramodadhvaṃ plavaṅgamāḥ
translation: प्लवङ्गमाः O monkeys, अहम् I, बुद्ध्या with my intellect, प्रपश्यामि I can visualise, मे my, मनश्चेष्टा च my feeling in mind, तथा so also, अहम् I am, वैदेहीम् Vaidehi, द्रक्ष्यामि I will see, प्रमोदध्वम् be happy.
explanation: 'O monkeys I have a feeling in my mind that I will see Vaidehi. Be happy.

shloka_text: मारुतस्य समो वेगे गरुडस्य समो जवे। अयुतं योजनानां तु गमिष्यामीति मे मतिः।।4.67.28।।
transliteration: mārutasya samo vege garuḍasya samo jave| ayutaṃ yojanānāṃ tu gamiṣyāmīti me matiḥ
translation: वेगे in speed, मारुतस्य Maruta's, समः equal, जवे in rapidity, गरुडस्य Garuda's, समः equal, योजनानाम् of yojanas, अयुतम् ten thousand, गमिष्यामीति I will go, मे my, मतिः feeling.
explanation: 'I am equal to Maruta and Garuda in speed. I feel I can cover ten thousand yojanas (at a stretch).

shloka_text: वासवस्य सवज्रस्य ब्रह्मणो वा स्वयम्भुवः। विक्रम्य सहसा हस्तादमृतं तदिहानये।।4.67.29।। लङ्कां वापि समुत्क्षिप्य गच्छेयमिति मे मतिः।
transliteration: vāsavasya savajrasya brahmaṇo vā svayambhuvaḥ| vikramya sahasā hastādamṛtaṃ tadihānaye laṅkāṃ vāpi samutkṣipya gaccheyamiti me matiḥ|
translation: विक्रम्य after advancing, सवज्रस्य of that Indra the wielder of thunderbolt, वासवस्य Vasava's, स्वयम्भुवः of the self born, ब्रह्मणो वा of the ceator Brahma even, हस्तात् from his hand, सहसा at once, अमृतम् nectar, इह here, आनये I will get, लङ्काम् Lanka, समुत्क्षिप्य वापि uprooting, गच्छेयम् I can go, इति this way, मे my, मतिः feel in mind.
explanation: 'I think I can encounter Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt and obtain nectar from his hands. I can even confront Brahma, the selfborn creator courageously. I can even uproot Lanka and carry it.'

shloka_text: तमेवं वानरश्रेष्ठं गर्जन्तममितौजसम्।।4.67.30।। प्रहृष्टा हरयस्तत्र समुदैक्षन्त विस्मिताः।
transliteration: tamevaṃ vānaraśreṣṭhaṃ garjantamamitaujasam prahṛṣṭā harayastatra samudaikṣanta vismitāḥ|
translation: तत्र there, एवम् in that way, गर्जन्तम् roaring aloud, अमितौजसम् shining brilliantly, तम् him, वानरश्रेष्ठम् best of monkeys, हरयः monkeys, प्रहृष्टाः joyful, विस्मिताः amazed, समुदैक्षन्त all looked at him.
explanation: The monkeys looked at him and were amazed, happy to see him roaring and shining in brilliance.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ज्ञातीनां शोकनाशनम्।।4.67.31।। उवाच परिसंहृष्टो जाम्बवान्हरिसत्तमः।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā jñātīnāṃ śokanāśanam uvāca parisaṃhṛṣṭo jāmbavānharisattamaḥ|
translation: तस्य his, तत् that, ज्ञातीनाम् of the kith and kin, शोकनाशनम् remover of  grief, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा on hearing, हरिसत्तम: finest of monkeys, जाम्बवान् Jambavan, परिसम्हृष्टः very glad, उवाच said.
explanation: Jambavan, the finest of the monkeys, felt very glad on hearing his words which put an end to the sorrow of the kith and kin and said:

shloka_text: वीर केसरिणः पुत्र हनुमान्मारुतात्मज।।4.67.32।। ज्ञातीनां विपुलश्शोकस्त्वया तात प्रणाशितः।
transliteration: vīra kesariṇaḥ putra hanumānmārutātmaja jñātīnāṃ vipulaśśokastvayā tāta praṇāśitaḥ|
translation: वीर O hero, केसरिणः Kesari's, पुत्र son, मारुतात्मज O son of Marutha, तात O dear, त्वया by you, ज्ञातीनाम् of the kith and kin, विपुलः profound, शोकः grief, प्रणाशितः has been removed.
explanation: 'O son of Kesari O son of Maruta O hero you have removed the great grief of your race, dear

shloka_text: तव कल्याणरुचयः कपिमुख्यास्समागताः।।4.67.33।। मङ्गलं कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं करिष्यन्ति समाहिताः।
transliteration: tava kalyāṇarucayaḥ kapimukhyāssamāgatāḥ maṅgalaṃ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ kariṣyanti samāhitāḥ|
translation: तव your, कल्याणरुचयः well wishers, समागताः collected, कपिमुख्याः chiefs of monkeys, समाहिताः collected together, कार्य(अर्थ)सिद्ध्यर्थम् to achieve your objective, मङ्गलां auspicious prayers, करिष्यन्ति they will offer.
explanation: Your well-wishers, the monkey chiefs, have gathered and will with one mind offer auspicious prayers for the success of your mission.

shloka_text: ऋषीणां च प्रसादेन कपिवृद्धमतेन च।।4.67.34।। गुरूणां च प्रसादेन प्लवस्व त्वं महार्णवम्।
transliteration: ṛṣīṇāṃ ca prasādena kapivṛddhamatena ca gurūṇāṃ ca prasādena plavasva tvaṃ mahārṇavam|
translation: ऋषीणाम् of sages, प्रसादेन by the grace, कपिवृद्धमतेन च elderly monkeys', गुरूणाम् of elderlies, प्रसादेन by grace, च and, त्वम् you, महार्णवम् vast ocean, प्लवस्य cross.
explanation: 'By the blessings of the sages and by the grace of the elderly monkeys may you cross over the vast ocean.

shloka_text: स्थास्यामश्चैकपादेन यावदागमनं तव।।4.67.35।। त्वद्गतानि च सर्वेषां जीवनानि वनौकसाम्।
transliteration: sthāsyāmaścaikapādena yāvadāgamanaṃ tava tvadgatāni ca sarveṣāṃ jīvanāni vanaukasām|
translation: तव your, आगमनं यावत् awaiting your arrival, एकपादेन on one foot, स्थास्यामः we will stand, सर्वेषाम् of all of us, वनौकसाम् of forestdwellers, जीवनानि lives, त्वद्गतानि will depend upon you.
explanation: We will stand poised on one foot awaiting your return, for the lives of all us forest-dwellers depend upon you.

shloka_text: ततस्तु हरिशार्दूलस्तानुवाच वनौकसः।।4.67.36।। नेयं मम मही वेगं लङ्घने धारयिष्यति।
transliteration: tatastu hariśārdūlastānuvāca vanaukasaḥ neyaṃ mama mahī vegaṃ laṅghane dhārayiṣyati|
translation: ततः then, हरिशार्दूलः tiger among monkeys, तान् to those, वनौकसः monkeys, उवाच said, इयं this, मही earth, मम my, वेगम् speed, लङ्घने while crossing, न धारयिष्यति it cannot sustain.
explanation: Then the tiger among monkeys, Hanuman said to those forestdwellers (monkeys), 'The earth cannot bear the thrust of my leaping.

shloka_text: एतानीह नगस्यास्य शिलासङ्कटशालिनः।।4.67.37।। शिखराणि महेन्द्रस्य स्थिराणि सुमहान्ति च।
transliteration: etānīha nagasyāsya śilāsaṅkaṭaśālinaḥ śikharāṇi mahendrasya sthirāṇi sumahānti ca|
translation: शिलासङ्कटशालिनः the rocks of the mountain ranges, अस्य of this, महेन्द्रस्य नगरस्य Mahendra mountain's, एतानि these, शिखराणि peaks, स्थिराणि stable, सुमहान्ति च are very  huge.
explanation: 'The rocks on the peaks of the ranges of mount Mahendra cannot with stand it, although they are huge and firm.

shloka_text: एषु वेगं करिष्यामि महेन्द्रशिखरेष्वहम्।।4.67.38।। नानाद्रुमविकीर्णेषु धातुनिष्यन्दशोभिषु।
transliteration: eṣu vegaṃ kariṣyāmi mahendraśikhareṣvaham nānādrumavikīrṇeṣu dhātuniṣyandaśobhiṣu|
translation: नानाद्रुमविकीर्णेषु  scattered with different kinds of trees, धातुनिष्यन्दशोभिषु shining with different kinds of minerals, एष: here I am, महेन्द्रशिखरेषु peaks of mountain Mahendra, अहम् I, वेगम् speed, करिष्यामि I will do.
explanation: 'I will pick up speed on the peaks of mount Mahendra filled with different kinds of trees and minerals.

shloka_text: एतानि मम निष्पेषं पादयोः प्लवतां वराः।।4.67.39।। प्लवतो धारयिष्यन्ति योजनानामितश्शतम्।
transliteration: etāni mama niṣpeṣaṃ pādayoḥ plavatāṃ varāḥ plavato dhārayiṣyanti yojanānāmitaśśatam|
translation: इतः from here, योजनानाम् of yojanas, शतम् one hundred, प्लवतः for me as I leap, मम to me, निष्पेषं crushing force of, पादयोः of both feet, प्लवतां वरा: best among those who leap, धारयिष्यन्ति will withstand.
explanation: 'O great monkeys these mountain peaks can withstand the crushing force of my feet as I leap over a hundred yojanas.

shloka_text: ततस्तं मारुतप्रख्यस्सहरिर्मारुतात्मजः।।4.67.40।। आरुरोह नगश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रमरिमर्दनः। वृतं नानाविधैः वृक्षैर्मृगसेवितशाद्वलम्।।4.67.41।। लताकुसुमसम्बाधं नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम्। सिंहशार्दूलचरितं मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम्।।4.67.42।। मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टं सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम्।
transliteration: tatastaṃ mārutaprakhyassaharirmārutātmajaḥ āruroha nagaśreṣṭhaṃ mahendramarimardanaḥ| vṛtaṃ nānāvidhaiḥ vṛkṣairmṛgasevitaśādvalam latākusumasambādhaṃ nityapuṣpaphaladrumam| siṃhaśārdūlacaritaṃ mattamātaṅgasevitam mattadvijagaṇodghuṣṭaṃ salilotpīḍasaṅkulam|
translation: ततः then, मारुतप्रख्यः as eminent as the Windgod, मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, अरिमर्दनः crusher of enemies, सः हरिः that monkey, नानाविधैः with several, वृक्षैः  trees, वृतम् covered, मृगसेवितशाद्वलम् grassy land inhabited by deer, लताकुसुमसम्बाधम् filled with creepers and fragrant flowers, नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम् ever with trees full of flowers and fruits, सिंहशार्दूलचरितं where lions and tigers move, मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम् inhabited by proud elephants, मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टम् filled with flocks of intoxicated birds, सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम् full of water falls, नगश्रेष्ठम् great mountain, महेन्द्रम् Mahendra, आरुरोह ascended.
explanation: The son of Maruta, who was as eminent as the Windgod, the crusher of enemies ascended the great mountain Mahendra, full of grassland inhabited by deer, thickly grown with various trees and creepers full of fragrant flowers and fruits, where roam lions and tigers and proud elephants, a place that echoes with sounds of intoxicated birds and waterfalls.

shloka_text: ततस्तं मारुतप्रख्यस्सहरिर्मारुतात्मजः।।4.67.40।। आरुरोह नगश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रमरिमर्दनः। वृतं नानाविधैः वृक्षैर्मृगसेवितशाद्वलम्।।4.67.41।। लताकुसुमसम्बाधं नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम्। सिंहशार्दूलचरितं मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम्।।4.67.42।। मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टं सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम्।
transliteration: tatastaṃ mārutaprakhyassaharirmārutātmajaḥ āruroha nagaśreṣṭhaṃ mahendramarimardanaḥ| vṛtaṃ nānāvidhaiḥ vṛkṣairmṛgasevitaśādvalam latākusumasambādhaṃ nityapuṣpaphaladrumam| siṃhaśārdūlacaritaṃ mattamātaṅgasevitam mattadvijagaṇodghuṣṭaṃ salilotpīḍasaṅkulam|
translation: ततः then, मारुतप्रख्यः as eminent as the Windgod, मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, अरिमर्दनः crusher of enemies, सः हरिः that monkey, नानाविधैः with several, वृक्षैः  trees, वृतम् covered, मृगसेवितशाद्वलम् grassy land inhabited by deer, लताकुसुमसम्बाधम् filled with creepers and fragrant flowers, नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम् ever with trees full of flowers and fruits, सिंहशार्दूलचरितं where lions and tigers move, मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम् inhabited by proud elephants, मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टम् filled with flocks of intoxicated birds, सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम् full of water falls, नगश्रेष्ठम् great mountain, महेन्द्रम् Mahendra, आरुरोह ascended.
explanation: The son of Maruta, who was as eminent as the Windgod, the crusher of enemies ascended the great mountain Mahendra, full of grassland inhabited by deer, thickly grown with various trees and creepers full of fragrant flowers and fruits, where roam lions and tigers and proud elephants, a place that echoes with sounds of intoxicated birds and waterfalls.

shloka_text: ततस्तं मारुतप्रख्यस्सहरिर्मारुतात्मजः।।4.67.40।। आरुरोह नगश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रमरिमर्दनः। वृतं नानाविधैः वृक्षैर्मृगसेवितशाद्वलम्।।4.67.41।। लताकुसुमसम्बाधं नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम्। सिंहशार्दूलचरितं मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम्।।4.67.42।। मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टं सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम्।
transliteration: tatastaṃ mārutaprakhyassaharirmārutātmajaḥ āruroha nagaśreṣṭhaṃ mahendramarimardanaḥ| vṛtaṃ nānāvidhaiḥ vṛkṣairmṛgasevitaśādvalam latākusumasambādhaṃ nityapuṣpaphaladrumam| siṃhaśārdūlacaritaṃ mattamātaṅgasevitam mattadvijagaṇodghuṣṭaṃ salilotpīḍasaṅkulam|
translation: ततः then, मारुतप्रख्यः as eminent as the Windgod, मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, अरिमर्दनः crusher of enemies, सः हरिः that monkey, नानाविधैः with several, वृक्षैः  trees, वृतम् covered, मृगसेवितशाद्वलम् grassy land inhabited by deer, लताकुसुमसम्बाधम् filled with creepers and fragrant flowers, नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम् ever with trees full of flowers and fruits, सिंहशार्दूलचरितं where lions and tigers move, मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम् inhabited by proud elephants, मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टम् filled with flocks of intoxicated birds, सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम् full of water falls, नगश्रेष्ठम् great mountain, महेन्द्रम् Mahendra, आरुरोह ascended.
explanation: The son of Maruta, who was as eminent as the Windgod, the crusher of enemies ascended the great mountain Mahendra, full of grassland inhabited by deer, thickly grown with various trees and creepers full of fragrant flowers and fruits, where roam lions and tigers and proud elephants, a place that echoes with sounds of intoxicated birds and waterfalls.

shloka_text: महद्भिरुच्छ्रितं शृङ्गैर्महेन्द्रं स महाबलः।।4.67.43।। विचचार हरिश्रेष्ठो महेन्द्रसमविक्रमः।
transliteration: mahadbhirucchritaṃ śṛṅgairmahendraṃ sa mahābalaḥ vicacāra hariśreṣṭho mahendrasamavikramaḥ|
translation: महेन्द्रसमविक्रमः equal to Indra in valour, महाबलः mighty, हरिश्रेष्ठः best of the monkeys, महद्भि: great, शृङ्गैः with peaks, उच्छ्रितम् high, तम् him, महेन्द्रम् Mahendra, विचचार strode.
explanation: The mighty, preeminent monkey who was equal to Indra in valour took a leap from the high peaks of the tall mountain, Mahendra৷৷

shloka_text: पादाभ्यां पीडितस्तेन महाशैलो महात्मना।।4.67.44।। रराज सिंहाभिहतो महान्मत्त इव द्विपः।
transliteration: pādābhyāṃ pīḍitastena mahāśailo mahātmanā rarāja siṃhābhihato mahānmatta iva dvipaḥ|
translation: महात्मना by great self, तेन by him, बाहुभ्याम् with both his shoulders, पीडितः crushed, महाशैलः mighty mountain, सिंहाभिहतः struck by a lion, मत्तः proud, महान् great, द्विपः इव like an elephant, रराज looked.
explanation: Crushed by the feet of the great self, Hanuman, the huge mountain looked like a proud elephant struck by a lion.

shloka_text: मुमोच सलिलोत्पीडान्विप्रकीर्णशिलोच्चयः।।4.67.45।। वित्रस्तमृगमातङ्गः प्रकम्पितमहाद्रुमः।
transliteration: mumoca salilotpīḍānviprakīrṇaśiloccayaḥ vitrastamṛgamātaṅgaḥ prakampitamahādrumaḥ|
translation: विप्रकीर्णशिलोच्चयः scattered rocks, वित्रस्तमृगमातङ्गः terrified deer and elephants, प्रकम्पितमहाद्रुमः violently shaken up trees, सलिलोत्पीडान् poured out gushing streams of water, मुमोच released.
explanation: The rocks of the mountain got scattered by the force. The deer and elephants were terrified. The trees were shaken up violently and streams of water gushed forth.

shloka_text: नानागन्धर्वमिथुनैः पानसंसर्गकर्कशैः।।4.67.46।। उत्पतद्भिश्च विहगैर्विद्याधरगणैरपि। त्यज्यमानमहासानुस्सन्निलीनमहोरगः।।4.67.47।। चलशृङ्गशिलोद्घातस्तदाऽभूत्स महागिरिः।
transliteration: nānāgandharvamithunaiḥ pānasaṃsargakarkaśaiḥ utpatadbhiśca vihagairvidyādharagaṇairapi| tyajyamānamahāsānussannilīnamahoragaḥ calaśṛṅgaśilodghātastadā'bhūtsa mahāgiriḥ|
translation: तदा then, सः महागिरिः that great mountain, पानसंसर्गकर्कशैः by those whose behaviour was rough in a drunken state, नानागन्धर्वमिथुनैः by different groups of copulating gandharvas, उत्पतद्भि: by those flying, विहगैश्च by birds in the sky, विद्याधरगणैरपि hosts of vidyadharas, त्यज्यमानमहासानुः abandoned by the vast mountain slopes, सन्निलीनमहोरगः with serpents resting, चलशृङ्गशिलोद्घातः the rocks shaken up on mountain tops, अभूत् appeared.
explanation: Shaken by the rude shock, couples of intoxicated gandharvas left in a huff the vast slopes of the great mountain. Flocks of birds and groups of vidyadharas flew away. The serpents went into hiding. Rocks fell off the shaken mountain.

shloka_text: नानागन्धर्वमिथुनैः पानसंसर्गकर्कशैः।।4.67.46।। उत्पतद्भिश्च विहगैर्विद्याधरगणैरपि। त्यज्यमानमहासानुस्सन्निलीनमहोरगः।।4.67.47।। चलशृङ्गशिलोद्घातस्तदाऽभूत्स महागिरिः।
transliteration: nānāgandharvamithunaiḥ pānasaṃsargakarkaśaiḥ utpatadbhiśca vihagairvidyādharagaṇairapi| tyajyamānamahāsānussannilīnamahoragaḥ calaśṛṅgaśilodghātastadā'bhūtsa mahāgiriḥ|
translation: तदा then, सः महागिरिः that great mountain, पानसंसर्गकर्कशैः by those whose behaviour was rough in a drunken state, नानागन्धर्वमिथुनैः by different groups of copulating gandharvas, उत्पतद्भि: by those flying, विहगैश्च by birds in the sky, विद्याधरगणैरपि hosts of vidyadharas, त्यज्यमानमहासानुः abandoned by the vast mountain slopes, सन्निलीनमहोरगः with serpents resting, चलशृङ्गशिलोद्घातः the rocks shaken up on mountain tops, अभूत् appeared.
explanation: Shaken by the rude shock, couples of intoxicated gandharvas left in a huff the vast slopes of the great mountain. Flocks of birds and groups of vidyadharas flew away. The serpents went into hiding. Rocks fell off the shaken mountain.

shloka_text: निश्श्वसद्भिस्तदाऽर्तैस्तु भुजङ्गैरर्धनि:सृतैः।।4.67.48।। सपताक इवाभाति स तदा धरणीधरः।
transliteration: niśśvasadbhistadā'rtaistu bhujaṅgairardhani:sṛtaiḥ sapatāka ivābhāti sa tadā dharaṇīdharaḥ|
translation: तदा then, सः that, धरणीधरः holder of the earth, mountain, निश्वसद्भि: hissing out of the rocks, अर्धनि:सृतैः protruding half of their body, भुजगैः serpents, सपताकः इव like the flags, आभाति appeared.
explanation: The serpents with their bodies half protruded out of the rocks and hissing looked like flags planted on the mountain.

shloka_text: ऋषिभिस्त्राससम्भ्रान्तैस्त्यज्यमानः शिलोच्चयः।।4.67.49।। सीदन्महति कान्तारे सार्थहीन इवाध्वगः।
transliteration: ṛṣibhistrāsasambhrāntaistyajyamānaḥ śiloccayaḥ sīdanmahati kāntāre sārthahīna ivādhvagaḥ|
translation: त्राससम्भ्रान्तै: by those alarmed and agitated, ऋषिभिः by sages, त्यज्यमानः being abandoned, शिलोच्चयः the mountain, सार्थहीनः berefit of a caravan, महति in a great, कान्तारे in the forest, सीदन् while worrying, अध्वगः इव like the traveller.
explanation: The alarmed and agitated sages abandonned the mountain peaks.The mountain appeared like a lone traveller separated from the caravan in the great forest.

shloka_text: सवेगवान् वेगसमाहितात्मा हरिप्रवीरः परवीरहन्ता। मनस्समाधाय महानुभावो जगाम लङ्कां मनसा मनस्वी।।4.67.50।।
transliteration: savegavān vegasamāhitātmā haripravīraḥ paravīrahantā| manassamādhāya mahānubhāvo jagāma laṅkāṃ manasā manasvī
translation: वेगवान् speeds, वेगसमाहितात्मा fixing his attention on speed, परवीरहन्ता destroyer of enemy warriors, मनस्वी sensitive , महानुभावः noble, सः that, हरिप्रवीरः heroic monkey मनः in mind, समाधाय composed, मनसा mentally, लङ्काम् Lanka, जगाम reached.
explanation: Magnanimous, wise and heroic Hanuman, destroyer of enemy warriors, fixed his attention on speed, betook himself mentally to Lanka (ere he reached it physically). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामाणये वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyseventh sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततो रावणनीतायाः सीतायाः शत्रुकर्शनः। इयेष पदमन्वेष्टुं चारणाचरिते पथि।।5.1.1।।
transliteration: tato rāvaṇanītāyāḥ sītāyāḥ śatrukarśanaḥ| iyeṣa padamanveṣṭuṃ cāraṇācarite pathi
translation: ततः then, शत्रुकर्शनः crusher off enemies, रावणनीतायाः carried by Ravana, सीतायाः Sita's, पदम् whereabouts, अन्वेष्टुम् to search, चारणाचरिते where charanas the celestial bards move, पथि way, इयेष resolved .
explanation: Hanuman, crusher of enemies resolved to find the whereabouts of Sita, carried away by Ravana. He followed the path of the Charanas, celestial bards.
comments: Hanuman courses through the path of the Charanas -- crosses the ocean --  reaches Lanka

shloka_text: दुष्करं निष्प्रतिद्वन्द्वं चिकीर्षन् कर्म वानरः। समुदग्रशिरोग्रीवो गवांपतिरिवाबभौ।।5.1.2।।
transliteration: duṣkaraṃ niṣpratidvandvaṃ cikīrṣan karma vānaraḥ| samudagraśirogrīvo gavāṃpatirivābabhau
translation: वानरः vanara, दुष्करम् formidable, निष्प्रतिद्वन्द्वम् which could not be challenged, चिकीर्षन् intending to (cross), समुदग्रशिरोग्रीवः raised his head and neck, गवां पतिः इव like the best of bulls, बभौ appeared.
explanation: Hanuman who raised his head and neck, intending to cross the formidable ocean which none else could accomplish, looked like a leading bull.

shloka_text: अथ वैडूर्यवर्णेषु शाद्वलेषु महाबलः। धीरः सलिलकल्पेषु विचचार यथासुखम्।।5.1.3।।
transliteration: atha vaiḍūryavarṇeṣu śādvaleṣu mahābalaḥ| dhīraḥ salilakalpeṣu vicacāra yathāsukham
translation: अथ then, महाबलः mighty, धीरः calm, वैडूर्यवर्णेषु of the colour of vaidurya (tawny), सलिलकल्पेषु on the sheet of water (marshy land with green grass that looked like sheet of water), शाद्वलेषु on green grassy lands, यथासुखम् very easily, विचचार strdled.
explanation: Tawnyhued Hanuman, gifted with extraordinary strength and patience happily strolled on the marshy tracts of grassy land which had the colour of vaidurya.

shloka_text: द्विजान् वित्रासयन् धीमानुरसा पादपान् हरन्। मृगांश्च सुबहून्निघ्नन् प्रवृद्ध इव केसरी।।5.1.4।।
transliteration: dvijān vitrāsayan dhīmānurasā pādapān haran| mṛgāṃśca subahūnnighnan pravṛddha iva kesarī
translation: धीमान् wise, द्विजान् birds, वित्रासयन् scaring, उरसा with his chest, पादपान् trees, हरन् uprooting, प्रवृद्धः grown, केसरी इव like a lion, सुबहून् groups, मृगांश्च animals also, निघ्नन् trampling.
explanation: Wise Hanuman went about like a lion scaring away birds, uprooting trees with his chest, and trampling many animals.

shloka_text: नीललोहितमांजिष्ठपत्रवर्णैः सितासितैः। स्वभावविहितैश्चित्रैर्धातुभिः समलङ्कृतम्।।5.1.5।। कामरूपिभिराविष्टमभीक्ष्णं सपरिच्छदैः। यक्षकिन्नरगन्धर्वैर्देवकल्पैश्च पन्नगैः।।5.1.6।।
transliteration: nīlalohitamāṃjiṣṭhapatravarṇaiḥ sitāsitaiḥ| svabhāvavihitaiścitrairdhātubhiḥ samalaṅkṛtam kāmarūpibhirāviṣṭamabhīkṣṇaṃ saparicchadaiḥ| yakṣakinnaragandharvairdevakalpaiśca pannagaiḥ
translation: नीललोहितमांजिष्ठपत्रवर्णैः blue, red, yellow and green coloured, सितासितैः as well as with white and black colours, स्वभावविहितैः in their natural state, चित्रैः by wonderful ones, धातुभिः with minerals, समलङ्कृतम् decorated all over, कामरूपिभिः by those who take any form at free will, सपरिच्छदैः  all surrounded by their retinue, यक्षकिन्नरगन्धर्वैः by yakshas, kinneras and gandharvas,अभीक्ष्णम् very much, आविष्टम् occupied, र्देवकल्पैश्च resembling gods, पन्नगैः by nagas.
explanation: The mountain was as though decorated with mineral rocks of varied colours like blue, red, yellow and green as well as black and white৷৷It was frequently visited  by yakshas, kinneras, gandharvas and nagas surrounded by their retinue, capable of assuming any form at their free will rivalling gods and nagas in splendour.

shloka_text: नीललोहितमांजिष्ठपत्रवर्णैः सितासितैः। स्वभावविहितैश्चित्रैर्धातुभिः समलङ्कृतम्।।5.1.5।। कामरूपिभिराविष्टमभीक्ष्णं सपरिच्छदैः। यक्षकिन्नरगन्धर्वैर्देवकल्पैश्च पन्नगैः।।5.1.6।।
transliteration: nīlalohitamāṃjiṣṭhapatravarṇaiḥ sitāsitaiḥ| svabhāvavihitaiścitrairdhātubhiḥ samalaṅkṛtam kāmarūpibhirāviṣṭamabhīkṣṇaṃ saparicchadaiḥ| yakṣakinnaragandharvairdevakalpaiśca pannagaiḥ
translation: नीललोहितमांजिष्ठपत्रवर्णैः blue, red, yellow and green coloured, सितासितैः as well as with white and black colours, स्वभावविहितैः in their natural state, चित्रैः by wonderful ones, धातुभिः with minerals, समलङ्कृतम् decorated all over, कामरूपिभिः by those who take any form at free will, सपरिच्छदैः  all surrounded by their retinue, यक्षकिन्नरगन्धर्वैः by yakshas, kinneras and gandharvas,अभीक्ष्णम् very much, आविष्टम् occupied, र्देवकल्पैश्च resembling gods, पन्नगैः by nagas.
explanation: The mountain was as though decorated with mineral rocks of varied colours like blue, red, yellow and green as well as black and white৷৷It was frequently visited  by yakshas, kinneras, gandharvas and nagas surrounded by their retinue, capable of assuming any form at their free will rivalling gods and nagas in splendour.

shloka_text: स तस्य गिरिवर्यस्य तले नागवरायुते। तिष्ठन् कपिवरस्तत्र ह्रदे नाग इवाबभौ।।5.1.7।।
transliteration: sa tasya girivaryasya tale nāgavarāyute| tiṣṭhan kapivarastatra hrade nāga ivābabhau
translation: सः that, कपिवरः leader of monkeys, तत्र there, नागवरायुते with lordly elephants, तस्य गिरिवर्यस्य at the great mountain, तले foot, तिष्ठन् stood, ह्रदे centre, नागः इव like elephant, अबभौ looked.
explanation: As the monkey leader stood at the foot of the great mountain filled with lordly elephants he looked like an elephant standing at the centre of a pond.

shloka_text: स सूर्याय महेन्द्राय पवनाय स्वयंभुवे। भूतेभ्यश्चाञ्जलिं कृत्वा चकार गमने मतिम्।।5.1.8।।
transliteration: sa sūryāya mahendrāya pavanāya svayaṃbhuve| bhūtebhyaścāñjaliṃ kṛtvā cakāra gamane matim
translation: सः that, सूर्याय to the Sun, महेन्द्राय to Mahendra, lord of the gods, पवनाय to the wind god, स्वयंभुवे to the creator, Brahma, भूतेभ्यः the attendants of lord Siva अञ्जलिम् salutations with folded palms, कृत्वा offered, गमने to go, मतिम् resolution, चकार he made.
explanation: Offering salutations with folded palms to the Sungod, to Mahendra, lord of the gods, to the windgod, to the Creator Brahma and to all the attendants of lord Siva, made up his mind to proceed (to Lanka).

shloka_text: अञ्जलिं प्राङ्मुखः कुर्वन् पवनायात्मयोनये। ततो हि ववृधे गन्तुं दक्षिणो दक्षिणां दिशम्।।5.1.9।।
transliteration: añjaliṃ prāṅmukhaḥ kurvan pavanāyātmayonaye| tato hi vavṛdhe gantuṃ dakṣiṇo dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
translation: प्राङ्मुखः facing the east, आत्मयोनये his father, पवनाय windgod, अञ्जलिम् salutations with folded palms, कृत्वा having offered, ततः then, दक्षिण with equanimity, दक्षिणां दिशम् southern direction, गन्तुम् to depart, ववृधे हि grew in size.
explanation: Hanuman, endowed with great equanimity, facing the east and joining his palms by way of salutaion to the Windgod, his father, he enlarged his size and turned south in order to depart.

shloka_text: प्लवङ्गप्रवरैर्दृष्टः प्लवने कृतनिश्चयः। ववृधे रामवृद्ध्यर्थं समुद्र इव पर्वसु।।5.1.10।।
transliteration: plavaṅgapravarairdṛṣṭaḥ plavane kṛtaniścayaḥ| vavṛdhe rāmavṛddhyarthaṃ samudra iva parvasu
translation: प्लवङ्गप्रवरैः the monkey troops, दृष्टः were gazing, प्लवने  taking leap, कृतनिश्चयः  resolved, पर्वसु during the fullmoon days, समुद्रः इव like the sea, रामवृद्ध्यर्थम् for the welfare of Rama, ववृधे began to grow in size.
explanation: Having made up his mind to leap for the cause of Rama, Hanuman began to grow in size just as the sea grows during the fullmoon and newmoon days, while the monkey troops were watching.

shloka_text: निष्प्रमाणशरीरः सन् लिलङ्घयिषुरर्णवम्। बाहुभ्यां पीडयामास चरणाभ्यां च पर्वतम्।।5.1.11।।
transliteration: niṣpramāṇaśarīraḥ san lilaṅghayiṣurarṇavam| bāhubhyāṃ pīḍayāmāsa caraṇābhyāṃ ca parvatam
translation: अर्णवम् ocean, लिलङ्घयिषुः one wishing to cross over, निष्प्रमाणशरीरः having an immeasurable figure, सन् while being, बाहुभ्याम् with both his arms, चरणाभ्यां च and with feet, पर्वतम् mountain, पीडयामास pressed.
explanation: Having swollen to an immeasurable figure, he pressed on the mountain with his feet and hands in an attempt to cross the ocean.

shloka_text: स चचालाचलश्चापि मुहूर्तं कपिपीडितः। तरूणां पुष्पिताग्राणां सर्वं पुष्पमशातयत्।।5.1.12।।
transliteration: sa cacālācalaścāpi muhūrtaṃ kapipīḍitaḥ| tarūṇāṃ puṣpitāgrāṇāṃ sarvaṃ puṣpamaśātayat
translation: कपिपीडितः pressed firmly by Hanuman, सः अचलश्चापि that mountain also, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, चचाल was shaken, पुष्पिताग्राणाम् flowers on the top, तरूणाम् of trees, सर्वम् all, पुष्पम् flowers, अशातयत् dropped down.
explanation: Pressed firmly by Hanuman, the mountain was shaken for a moment which caused the flowers to drop down from the tree tops.

shloka_text: तेन पादपमुक्तेन पुष्पौघेण सुगन्धिना। सर्वतः संवृतः शैलो बभौ पुष्पमयो यथा।।5.1.13।।
transliteration: tena pādapamuktena puṣpaugheṇa sugandhinā| sarvataḥ saṃvṛtaḥ śailo babhau puṣpamayo yathā
translation: शैलः the mountain, पादपमुक्तेन by those dropped down from the trees, सुगन्धिना full of fragrance, पुष्पौघेण heap of flowers, सर्वतः all over, संवृतः covered, यथा like, बभौ appeared, पुष्पमय: made of flowers.
explanation: With heaps of flowers full of fragrance fallen down from the trees all over the mountain, it looked as though it was a mountain of flowers.

shloka_text: तेन चोत्तमवीर्येण पीड्यमानः स पर्वतः। सलिलं सम्प्रसुस्राव मदं मत्त इव द्विपः।।5.1.14।।
transliteration: tena cottamavīryeṇa pīḍyamānaḥ sa parvataḥ| salilaṃ samprasusrāva madaṃ matta iva dvipaḥ
translation: उत्तमवीर्येण by the highly valiant self, तेन by him, पीड्यमानः  pressed very hard, सः पर्वतः that mountain, मत्तः intoxicated, द्विपः elephant, मदम् इव like the rut, सलिलम् the water, सम्प्रसुस्राव exuded profusely.
explanation: The mountain pressed hard under the feet of the valiant (Hanuman), discharged streams of water just as an elephant in rut would exude water of intoxication.

shloka_text: पीड्यमानस्तु बलिना महेन्द्रस्तेन पर्वतः। रीतीर्निर्वर्तयामास काञ्चनाञ्जनराजतीः।।5.1.15।।
transliteration: pīḍyamānastu balinā mahendrastena parvataḥ| rītīrnirvartayāmāsa kāñcanāñjanarājatīḥ
translation: बलिना by the powerful, तेन by him, पीड्यमानः having pressed, महेन्द्रः पर्वतः mount Mahendra, काञ्चनाञ्चनराजतीः of gold and silver, रीतीः streams, निर्वर्तयामास started forming.
explanation: Pressed by the powerful Hanuman, mount Mahendra let out streams of the hue of gold and silver (containing the ores of these minerals)৷৷

shloka_text: मुमोच च शिलाः शैलो विशालाः समनःशिलाः। मध्यमेनार्चिषा जुष्टा धूमराजीरिवानलः।।5.1.16।।
transliteration: mumoca ca śilāḥ śailo viśālāḥ samanaḥśilāḥ| madhyamenārciṣā juṣṭā dhūmarājīrivānalaḥ
translation: शैलः mountain, मध्यमेन in the midst, अर्चिषा by the flame, जुष्टा:possed with, अनलः fire, धूमराजीरिव like the columns of smoke, समनः शिलाः along with sulphur pigments, विशालाः big one, शिलाः boulders, मुमोच threw out, च even.
explanation: The mountain threw down big boulders along with sulphur just like fire emits columns of smoke, surrounded by flames.

shloka_text: गिरिणा पीड्यमानेन पीड्यमानानि सर्वतः। गुहाविष्टानि भूतानि विनेदुर्विकृतैः स्वरैः।।5.1.17।।
transliteration: giriṇā pīḍyamānena pīḍyamānāni sarvataḥ| guhāviṣṭāni bhūtāni vinedurvikṛtaiḥ svaraiḥ
translation: गुहाविष्टानि of the caves, भूतानि creatures, पीड्यमानेन being pressed, गिरिणा by the mountain, सर्वतः all over, पीड्यमानानि on account of pressing, विकृतैः with horrible, स्वरैः voices, विनेदुः shrieked.
explanation: Squeezed on all sides of the mountain by Hanuman, all creatures living in the caves shrieked making horrible sounds .

shloka_text: स महासत्त्वसन्नादः शैलपीडानिमित्तजः। पृथिवीं पूरयामास दिशश्चोपवनानि च।।5.1.18।।
transliteration: sa mahāsattvasannādaḥ śailapīḍānimittajaḥ| pṛthivīṃ pūrayāmāsa diśaścopavanāni ca
translation: शैलपीडानिमित्तजः caused by the crushing of the mountain, सः that, महासत्त्वसन्नादः loud noise of various creatures, पृथिवीम् the earth, दिशश्च all directions, उपवनानि च and the surrounding groves, पूरयामास filled.
explanation: Due to the crushing of the mountain, a loud noise of the various creatures shot up filling the earth in all directions and groves around.

shloka_text: शिरोभिः पृथुभिः सर्पा व्यक्तस्वस्तिकलक्षणैः। वमन्तः पावकं घोरं ददंशुर्दशनैः शिलाः।।5.1.19।।
transliteration: śirobhiḥ pṛthubhiḥ sarpā vyaktasvastikalakṣaṇaiḥ| vamantaḥ pāvakaṃ ghoraṃ dadaṃśurdaśanaiḥ śilāḥ
translation: सर्पाः snakes, व्यक्तस्वस्तिकलक्षणैः with signs of swastika marks, पृथुभिः by wide ones, शिरोभिः with hoods, घोरम् terrible, पावकम् fire, वमन्तः poured out, दशनैः with fangs, शिलाः ददंशुः bit the rocks.
explanation: The snakes spread out their broad hoods manifesting swastika marks on them and bit the rocks with their fangs pouring out terrible fire.

shloka_text: तास्तदा सविषैर्दष्टाः कुपितैस्तैर्महाशिलाः। जज्ज्वलुः पावकोद्दीप्ता बिभिदुश्च सहस्रधा।।5.1.20।।
transliteration: tāstadā saviṣairdaṣṭāḥ kupitaistairmahāśilāḥ| jajjvaluḥ pāvakoddīptā bibhiduśca sahasradhā
translation: तदा then, सविषैः by the venomous, कुपितैः by the angry, तैः by them, दष्टाः bitten, ताः महाशिलाः the huge rocks, पावकोददीप्ताः burnt by the flame, जज्वलुः burnt, सहस्रधा in a thousand pieces, बिभिदुश्च and broke.
explanation: Bitten by the venomous and angry snakes, the mountain was broken into a thousand pieces by the blazing flames.

shloka_text: यानि चौषधजालानि तस्मिन् जातानि पर्वते। विषघ्नान्यपि नागानां न शेकुः शमितुं विषम्।।5.1.21।।
transliteration: yāni cauṣadhajālāni tasmin jātāni parvate| viṣaghnānyapi nāgānāṃ na śekuḥ śamituṃ viṣam
translation: तस्मिन् पर्वते on that mountain, जातानि grown, यानि those, औषथजालानि medicinal herbs, विषघ्नान्यपि even those which can counteract poison, नागानाम् of the snakes, विषम् poison, शमितुम् to neutralize, न शेकुः were not able to.
explanation: Even the medicinal herbs grown on the mountain could not neutralize the effect of the poison of snakes.

shloka_text: भिद्यतेऽयं गिरिर्भूतैरिति मत्त्वा तपस्विनः। त्रस्ता विद्याधरास्तस्मादुत्पेतुः स्त्री गणैः सह।।5.1.22।। पानभूमिगतं हित्वा हैममासवभाजनम्। पात्राणि च महार्हाणि करकांश्च हिरण्मयान्।।5.1.23। लेह्यानुच्चावचान् भक्ष्यान् मांसानि विविधानि च। आर्षभाणि च चर्माणि खडगांश्च कनकत्सरून्।।5.1.24।।
transliteration: bhidyate'yaṃ girirbhūtairiti mattvā tapasvinaḥ| trastā vidyādharāstasmādutpetuḥ strī gaṇaiḥ saha pānabhūmigataṃ hitvā haimamāsavabhājanam| pātrāṇi ca mahārhāṇi karakāṃśca hiraṇmayān||5.1.23| lehyānuccāvacān bhakṣyān māṃsāni vividhāni ca| ārṣabhāṇi ca carmāṇi khaḍagāṃśca kanakatsarūn
translation: अयम् this, गिरिः mountain, भूतैः by creatures, भिद्यते broken, इति thus, मत्त्वा after, तपस्विनः ascetics, उत्पेतुः jumped up, विद्याधराः Vidyadharas, त्रस्ताः terrified, पानभूमिगतम् from the drinking places, हैमम् golden, आसवभाजनम् drinking cups, महार्हाणि valuable ones, करकांश्च goblets, उच्चावचान् various big and small ones, लेह्यान् food that is licked, भक्ष्यान् eatables, विविधानि of many kinds, मांसानि meat, आर्षभाणि of oxen, चर्माणि animal hides, कनकत्सरून् covered with golden sheaths, खडगांश्च swords, हित्वा after, स्त्रीगणैः सह along with groups of women, तस्मात् from that place, उत्पेतुः flew away.
explanation: Even the ascetics left the place approaching that the mountain would be broken into pieces by creatures. The alarmed vidyadharas leaped into the sky along with groups of their women, leaving behind golden jugs of wine as well as precious utensils, big and small sizes, and golden goblets, cups in the drinking place, as well as many tasty eatables like licking food, chewing food and many types of meat. They also left bullhides and swords with golden sheaths.

explanation: Even the ascetics left the place approaching that the mountain would be broken into pieces by creatures. The alarmed vidyadharas leaped into the sky along with groups of their women, leaving behind golden jugs of wine as well as precious utensils, big and small sizes, and golden goblets, cups in the drinking place, as well as many tasty eatables like licking food, chewing food and many types of meat. They also left bullhides and swords with golden sheaths.

explanation: Even the ascetics left the place approaching that the mountain would be broken into pieces by creatures. The alarmed vidyadharas leaped into the sky along with groups of their women, leaving behind golden jugs of wine as well as precious utensils, big and small sizes, and golden goblets, cups in the drinking place, as well as many tasty eatables like licking food, chewing food and many types of meat. They also left bullhides and swords with golden sheaths.

shloka_text: कृतकण्ठगुणाः क्षीबा रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनाः। रक्ताक्षाः पुष्कराक्षाश्च गगनं प्रतिपेदिरे।।5.1.25।।
transliteration: kṛtakaṇṭhaguṇāḥ kṣībā raktamālyānulepanāḥ| raktākṣāḥ puṣkarākṣāśca gaganaṃ pratipedire
translation: कृतकण्ठगुणाः wearing chains, क्षीबाः intoxicated ones, रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनाः wearing garlands and smearing with red unguents (sandalpaste), रक्ताक्षाः with red eyes, पुष्कराक्षाश्च with lotus like eyes, गगनम् to the sky, प्रतिपेदिरे flew into the sky.
explanation: The intoxicated vidyadharas with eyes red like lotuses, wearing garlands around the neck and smeared with red sandalpaste flew into the sky.

shloka_text: हारनूपुरकेयूरपारिहार्यधराः स्त्रियः। विस्मिताः सस्मितास्तस्थुराकाशे रमणैः सह।।5.1.26।।
transliteration: hāranūpurakeyūrapārihāryadharāḥ striyaḥ| vismitāḥ sasmitāstasthurākāśe ramaṇaiḥ saha
translation: हारनूपुरकेयूरपारिहार्यधराः wearing necklaces, anklets and armlets, स्त्रियः women, विस्मिताः wonderstruck, सस्मिताः gently  smiling, रमणैः सह with their lovers, आकाशे in the sky, तस्थुः stayed.
explanation: Adorned with necklaces, anklets and armlets, the vidyadharis stayed wonderstruck in the sky, smiling gently in the company of their lovers.

shloka_text: दर्शयन्तो महाविद्यां विद्याधरमहर्षयः। सहितास्तस्थुराकाशे वीक्षाञ्चक्रुश्च पर्वतम्।।5.1.27।।
transliteration: darśayanto mahāvidyāṃ vidyādharamaharṣayaḥ| sahitāstasthurākāśe vīkṣāñcakruśca parvatam
translation: विद्याधरमहर्षयः the seers among vidyadharas, महाविद्याम् proficient in different fields of knowledge, दर्शयन्तः watching, सहिताः collectively, आकाशे in the sky, तस्थुः stayed, पर्वतम् mountain, वीक्षांचक्रुश्च were also watching.
explanation: The seers among the Vidyadharas, proficient in different fields of knowledge were also watching the mountain from the sky along with others.

shloka_text: शुश्रुवुश्च तदा शब्दमृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्। चारणानां च सिद्धानां स्थितानां विमलेऽम्बरे।।5.1.28।।
transliteration: śuśruvuśca tadā śabdamṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām| cāraṇānāṃ ca siddhānāṃ sthitānāṃ vimale'mbare
translation: तदा then, विमले in a pure, अम्बरे in the sky, स्थितानाम् of those stationed, चारणानाम् of charanas, सिद्धानाम् of siddhas, भावितात्मनाम् of highly, ऋषीणां च and of seers, शब्दम् sound, शुश्रुवुः heard.
explanation: Then the vidyadharas heard the words of praise(of Hanuman) by the sages, seekers of the ultimate truth, the charanas and the siddhas who stood and watched in the clear sky:

shloka_text: एष पर्वतसङ्काशो हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः। तितीर्षति महावेगस्समुद्रं मकरालयम्।।5.1.29।।
transliteration: eṣa parvatasaṅkāśo hanumān mārutātmajaḥ| titīrṣati mahāvegassamudraṃ makarālayam
translation: पर्वतसङ्काशः resembling a mountain, मारुतात्मजः son of the windgod (Hanuman), महावेगः swift, एषः him, हनुमान् Hanuman, मकरालयम् abode of crocodiles, समुद्रम् ocean, तितीर्षति desiring to cross.
explanation: "Hanuman the son of the Windgod, who is like a mountain, with extraordinary might  intends to cross the ocean, the abode of crocodiles".

shloka_text: रामार्थं वानरार्थं च चिकीर्षन् कर्म दुष्करम्। समुद्रस्य परं पारं दुष्प्रापं प्राप्तुमिच्छति।।5.1.30।।
transliteration: rāmārthaṃ vānarārthaṃ ca cikīrṣan karma duṣkaram| samudrasya paraṃ pāraṃ duṣprāpaṃ prāptumicchati
translation: रामार्थम् for the purpose of Rama, वानरार्थं च for the sake of vanaras also, दुष्करम् impossible, कर्म task, चिकीर्षन् desirous of achieving, समुद्रस्य of the ocean, दुष्प्रापम् difficult to reach, परं पारम् the other side, प्राप्तुम् to reach, इच्छति he wishes.
explanation: "For the sake of Rama and the vanaras he wants to reach the other shore of the ocean, which is difficult, and indeed impossible".

shloka_text: इति विद्याधराः श्रुत्वा वचस्तेषां महात्मनाम्। तमप्रमेयं ददृशुः पर्वते वानरर्षभम्।।5.1.31।।
transliteration: iti vidyādharāḥ śrutvā vacasteṣāṃ mahātmanām| tamaprameyaṃ dadṛśuḥ parvate vānararṣabham
translation: विद्याधराः vidyadharas, इति thus, महात्मनाम् of great sages, तेषाम् of them, वचः word, श्रुत्वा having heard, पर्वते on the mountain, अप्रमेयम् beyond measure, वानरर्षभम् bull among the vanaras, Hanuman, तम् him, ददृशुः saw.
explanation: The vidyadharas heard the sages speaking in that manner on the mountain. They beheld Hanuman, the bull among vanaras, whose strength  was beyond measure.

shloka_text: दुधुवे च स रोमाणि चकम्पे चाचलोपमः। ननाद सुमहानादं सुमहानिव तोयदः।।5.1.32।।
transliteration: dudhuve ca sa romāṇi cakampe cācalopamaḥ| nanāda sumahānādaṃ sumahāniva toyadaḥ
translation: अचलोपमः huge as  mountain, सः he, रोमाणि hair, दुधुवे shook, चकम्पे च and moved, सुमहान् great, तोयदः इव like a cloud, सुमहानादम् huge sound, ननाद produced.
explanation: Hanuman, huge as a mountain moved his body and shook the hair on his body, thundering like a cloud.

shloka_text: आनुपूर्व्येण वृत्तं च लाङ्गूलं लोमभिश्चितम्। उत्पतिष्यन् विचिक्षेप पक्षिराज इवोरगम्।।5.1.33।।
transliteration: ānupūrvyeṇa vṛttaṃ ca lāṅgūlaṃ lomabhiścitam| utpatiṣyan vicikṣepa pakṣirāja ivoragam
translation: उत्पतिष्यन् ready to take off, आनुपूर्व्येण in an order, वृत्तम् covered, लोमभिः with hair, चितम् full of, लाङ्गूलम् tail, पक्षिराजः king of birds, उरगं इव like a serpent, विचिक्षेप shook, cast down.
explanation: Like the king of birds Garuda would shake a serpent, he shook his tail covered with hair in order to take off.

shloka_text: तस्य लाङ्गूलमाविद्धमात्तवेगस्य पृष्ठतः। ददृशे गरुडेनेव ह्रियमाणो महोरगः।।5.1.34।।
transliteration: tasya lāṅgūlamāviddhamāttavegasya pṛṣṭhataḥ| dadṛśe garuḍeneva hriyamāṇo mahoragaḥ
translation: आत्तवेगस्य of great, तस्य his, पृष्ठतः at the back, अविद्धम् curled, लाङ्गूलम् tail, गरुडेन by Garuda, ह्रियमाणः carried off, महोरगः इव like a big serpent, ददृशे appeared.
explanation: Hanuman had the tail curled at his back which appeared like a big serpent being carried off by Garuda.

shloka_text: बाहू संस्तम्भयामास महापरिघसन्निभौ। ससाद च कपिः कट्यां चरणौ सञ्चुकोच च।।5.1.35।।
transliteration: bāhū saṃstambhayāmāsa mahāparighasannibhau| sasāda ca kapiḥ kaṭyāṃ caraṇau sañcukoca ca
translation: कपिः monkey, महापरिघसन्निभौ like huge iron clubs, बाहू arms, संस्तम्भयामास pressing down firmly , कट्याम् in the waist, ससाद crouched in, चरणौ his feet, सञ्चुकोच च contracted.
explanation: The monkey fixed his arms, looking like iron clubs, firmly on the mountain and crouched his waist and contracted his feet.

shloka_text: संहृत्य च भुजौ श्रीमांस्तथैव च शिरोधराम्। तेजः सत्त्वं तथा वीर्यमाविवेश स वीर्यवान्।।5.1.36।।
transliteration: saṃhṛtya ca bhujau śrīmāṃstathaiva ca śirodharām| tejaḥ sattvaṃ tathā vīryamāviveśa sa vīryavān
translation: श्रीमान् glorious, वीर्यवान् courageous, सः Hanuman, भुजौ च even shoulders, तथैव च in the same way, शिरोधराम् his head, संहृत्य after contracting, तेजः glow, सत्त्वम् energy, तथा so also, वीर्यम् vigour, आविवेश summoned up.
explanation: The glorious and courageous Hanuman his head and shoulders contracted, summoned up all his energy and vigour.

shloka_text: मार्गमालोकयन्दूरादूर्ध्वं प्रणिहितेक्षणः। रुरोध हृदये प्राणानाकाशमवलोकयन्।।5.1.37।।
transliteration: mārgamālokayandūrādūrdhvaṃ praṇihitekṣaṇaḥ| rurodha hṛdaye prāṇānākāśamavalokayan
translation: ऊर्ध्वम् upward, प्रणिहितेक्षणः setting his eyes up, दूरात् from a distance, मार्गम् direction, आलोकयन् while looking at, आकाशम् sky, अवलोकयन् looking at, प्राणान् breath, हृदये in the chest,रुरोध restrained.
explanation: Having cast his eyes upward in order to view the distance and direction in which he had to leap, he restrained his breath in the chest while looking at the sky.

shloka_text: पद्भ्यां दृढमवस्थानं कृत्वा स कपिकुञ्जरः। निकुञ्च्य कर्णौ हनुमानुत्पतिष्यन् महाबलः।। वानरान् वानरश्रेष्ठ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।5.1.38।।
transliteration: padbhyāṃ dṛḍhamavasthānaṃ kṛtvā sa kapikuñjaraḥ| nikuñcya karṇau hanumānutpatiṣyan mahābalaḥ|| vānarān vānaraśreṣṭha idaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: कपिकुञ्जरः an elephant among monkeys, महाबलः very strong one, वानरश्रेष्ठः best of vanaras, सः हनुमान् that Hanuman, पद्भ्याम् feet, दृढम् firmly, अवस्थानम् standing in that position, कृत्वा did, कर्णौ ears, निकुञ्च्य contracted, उत्पतिष्यन् while preparing to leap, वानरान् vanaras, इदम् this, वचनम् word, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: A mighty elephant among vanaras, Hanuman holding his feet firmly and standing in that position, contracted his ears and addressed the monkeys, when he was about to leap:

shloka_text: यथा राघवनिर्मुक्तः शरः श्वसनविक्रमः। गच्छेत्तद्वद्गमिष्यामि लङ्कां रावणपालिताम्।।5.1.39।।
transliteration: yathā rāghavanirmuktaḥ śaraḥ śvasanavikramaḥ| gacchettadvadgamiṣyāmi laṅkāṃ rāvaṇapālitām
translation: राघवनिर्मुक्तः released by Raghava, शरः arrow, यथा similar manner, गच्छेत् goes, तद्वत् like that, श्वसनविक्रमः with the speed of wind, रावणपालिताम् governed by Ravana, लङ्काम् Lanka, गमिष्यामि I will reach.
explanation: "Just like an arrow released by Raghava would fly, I too will proceed with the speed of the wind to reach Lanka ruled by Ravana.

shloka_text: न हि द्रक्ष्यामि यदि तां लङ्कायां जनकात्मजाम्। अनेनैव हि वेगेन गमिष्यामि सुरालयम्।।5.1.40।।
transliteration: na hi drakṣyāmi yadi tāṃ laṅkāyāṃ janakātmajām| anenaiva hi vegena gamiṣyāmi surālayam
translation: लङ्कायाम् in Lanka, तां जनकात्मजाम् that daughter of Janaka, न हि द्रक्ष्यामि यदि If I am not able to find, अनेन with this, वेगेनैव हि with speed indeed, सुरालयम् abode of gods, गमिष्यामि I will go.
explanation: "If I am not able to find the  daughter of Janaka at Lanka I will go to heaven, abode of the gods, with the same speed.

shloka_text: यदि वा त्रिदिवे सीतां न द्रक्ष्याम्यकृतश्रमः। बद्ध्वा राक्षसराजानमानयिष्यामि रावणम्।।5.1.41।।
transliteration: yadi vā tridive sītāṃ na drakṣyāmyakṛtaśramaḥ| baddhvā rākṣasarājānamānayiṣyāmi rāvaṇam
translation: त्रिदिवे in heaven, सीताम् Sita, न द्रक्ष्यामि यदि वा If I do not find, अकृतश्रमः in spite of all my efforts, राक्षसराजानम् king of rakshasas, रावणम् Ravana, बद्ध्वा  bind, आनयिष्यामि will bring.
explanation: "If I do not find Sita in heaven in spite of my efforts, I will bind that king of demons, Ravana and bring him here.

shloka_text: सर्वथा कृतकार्योऽहमेष्यामि सह सीतया। आनयिष्यामि वा लङ्कां समुत्पाट्य सरावणाम्।।5.1.42।।
transliteration: sarvathā kṛtakāryo'hameṣyāmi saha sītayā| ānayiṣyāmi vā laṅkāṃ samutpāṭya sarāvaṇām
translation: अहम् I, सर्वथा by all means, कृतकार्यः doing my duty successfully, सह सीतया along with Sita, एष्यामि I will come, वा or, सरावणाम् along with Ravana, लङ्काम् Lanka, समुत्पाट्य  after uprooting, आनयिष्यामि will bring.
explanation: "I will, by all means return successful with Sita or else I will uproot Lanka along with Ravana and bring him here".

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु हनुमान्वानरान्वानरोत्तमः।।5.1.43।। उत्पपाताथ वेगेन वेगवानविचारयन्। सुपर्णमिव चात्मानं मेने स कपिकुञ्जरः।।5.1.44।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu hanumānvānarānvānarottamaḥ utpapātātha vegena vegavānavicārayan| suparṇamiva cātmānaṃ mene sa kapikuñjaraḥ
translation: वानरोत्तमः foremost vanara, हनुमान् Hanuman, वानरान् to vanaras, एवम् that way, उक्त्वा having said, अथ then, अविचारयन् without any exertion, वेगवान् swift, वेगेन speedily, उत्पपात leaped, सः he, कपिकुञ्जरः best of vanaras, elephantlike, आत्मानम् himself, सुपर्णमिव like bird Suparna (Garuda), मेने he felt.
explanation: Having thus addressed the monkeys the foremost of vanaras,Hanuman endowed with great speed leaped without any exertion. The elephant among monkeys felt like Garuda.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु हनुमान्वानरान्वानरोत्तमः।।5.1.43।। उत्पपाताथ वेगेन वेगवानविचारयन्। सुपर्णमिव चात्मानं मेने स कपिकुञ्जरः।।5.1.44।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu hanumānvānarānvānarottamaḥ utpapātātha vegena vegavānavicārayan| suparṇamiva cātmānaṃ mene sa kapikuñjaraḥ
translation: वानरोत्तमः foremost vanara, हनुमान् Hanuman, वानरान् to vanaras, एवम् that way, उक्त्वा having said, अथ then, अविचारयन् without any exertion, वेगवान् swift, वेगेन speedily, उत्पपात leaped, सः he, कपिकुञ्जरः best of vanaras, elephantlike, आत्मानम् himself, सुपर्णमिव like bird Suparna (Garuda), मेने he felt.
explanation: Having thus addressed the monkeys the foremost of vanaras,Hanuman endowed with great speed leaped without any exertion. The elephant among monkeys felt like Garuda.

shloka_text: समुत्पतति तस्मिंस्तु वेगात्ते नगरोहिणः। संहृत्य विटपान् सर्वान् समुत्पेतुः समन्ततः।।5.1.45।।
transliteration: samutpatati tasmiṃstu vegātte nagarohiṇaḥ| saṃhṛtya viṭapān sarvān samutpetuḥ samantataḥ
translation: तस्मिन् when he, समुत्पतति was leaping, वेगात् swiftly, ते they, नगरोहिणः numerous trees, सर्वान् all the, विटपान् branches, संहृत्य drawing together, समन्ततः from all over, समुत्पेतुः flew.
explanation: When he took off, numerous trees on the mountain drawing together the branches all over flew along with him.

shloka_text: स मत्तकोयष्टिमकान् पादपान् पुष्पशालिनः। उद्वहन्नूरुवेगेन जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे।।5.1.46।।
transliteration: sa mattakoyaṣṭimakān pādapān puṣpaśālinaḥ| udvahannūruvegena jagāma vimale'mbare
translation: सः he, मत्तकोयष्टिमकान् lapwings in heat, पुष्पशालिनः full of flowers, पादपान् trees, ऊरुवेगेन by the speed of his thighs, उद्वहन् while coursing, विमले  pristine (cloudless), अम्बरे in the sky, जगाम went.
explanation: He swept away the lapwings in heat on the blossoms of the trees by the speed of his thighs while he coursed through the cloudless sky.

shloka_text: ऊरुवेगोद्धता वृक्षा मुहूर्तं कपिमन्वयुः। प्रस्थितं दीर्घमध्वानं स्वबन्धुमिव बान्धवाः।।5.1.47।।
transliteration: ūruvegoddhatā vṛkṣā muhūrtaṃ kapimanvayuḥ| prasthitaṃ dīrghamadhvānaṃ svabandhumiva bāndhavāḥ
translation: ऊरुवेगोद्धताः bent forward by the force of his thighs, वृक्षाः trees, दीर्घम् long, अध्वानम् path, प्रस्थितम् starting, स्वबन्धुम् one's kith and kin, बान्धवाः इव like the relatives, कपिम् Hanuman, मुहूर्तम् for a while, अन्वयुः followed.
