explanation: Swept away by the force of his thighs, the trees bent forward following him for a while just as relatives accompany their kith and kin on long travel.

shloka_text: तमूरुवेगोन्मथिताः सालाश्चान्ये नगोत्तमाः। अनुजग्मुर्हनूमन्तं सैन्या इव महीपतिम्।।5.1.48।।
transliteration: tamūruvegonmathitāḥ sālāścānye nagottamāḥ| anujagmurhanūmantaṃ sainyā iva mahīpatim
translation: ऊरुवेगोन्मथिताः uprooted by the speed of thighs, सालाश्च sala trees also, अन्ये other, नगोत्तमाः great trees, सैन्याः troops, महीपतिम् इव like the king, हनूमन्तम् Hanuman, अनुजग्मुः follow.
explanation: Uprooted by the force of Hanuman's thighs,great trees like  sala followed him just like the troops follow the king.

shloka_text: सुपुष्पिताग्रैर्बहुभिः पादपैरन्वितः कपिः। हनुमान् पर्वताकारो बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनः।।5.1.49।।
transliteration: supuṣpitāgrairbahubhiḥ pādapairanvitaḥ kapiḥ| hanumān parvatākāro babhūvādbhutadarśanaḥ
translation: बहुभिः by many, सुपुष्पिताग्रैः with blossomed tops, पादपैः with trees, अन्वित: endowed with, कपिः vanaras, पर्वताकारः mountain like, हनुमान् Hanuman, अद्भुतदर्शनः queer appearance, बभूव became.
explanation: With numerous trees laden with flowers following him, Hanuman who looked like a mountain, presented a queer spectable.

shloka_text: सारवन्तोऽथ ये वृक्षा न्यमज्जन् लवणाम्भसि। भयादिव महेन्द्रस्य पर्वता वरुणालये।।5.1.50।।
transliteration: sāravanto'tha ye vṛkṣā nyamajjan lavaṇāmbhasi| bhayādiva mahendrasya parvatā varuṇālaye
translation: अथ and then, सारवन्तः huge, ये those, वृक्षाः trees, महेन्द्रस्य Indra's, भयात् out of fear, पर्वताः mountains, वरुणालये इव like the abode of Varuna, ocean, लवणाम्भसि in the salt sea, न्यमज्जन् sank.
explanation: Then the huge trees sank into the ocean of salt water even as mountains did, afraid of Indra's (thunderbolt).

shloka_text: स नानाकुसुमैः कीर्णः कपिः साङ्कुरकोरकैः। शुशुभे मेघसङ्काशः खद्योतैरिव पर्वतः।।5.1.51।।
transliteration: sa nānākusumaiḥ kīrṇaḥ kapiḥ sāṅkurakorakaiḥ| śuśubhe meghasaṅkāśaḥ khadyotairiva parvataḥ
translation: साङ्कुरकोरकैः with sprouts and buds, नानाकुसुमैः with different kinds of flowers, कीर्णः spread over, मेघसङ्काशः resembling a cloud, सः कपिः that Hanuman, खद्योतैः covered with fireflies, पर्वतः इव like a mountain, शुशुभे was shining brightly.
explanation: Covered with tender sprouts and buds of different kinds of flowers Hanuman shone brightly like a flying mountain with fireflies.

shloka_text: विमुक्तास्तस्य वेगेन मुक्त्वा पुष्पाणि ते द्रुमाः। अवशीर्यन्त सलिले निवृत्ताः सुहृदो यथा।।5.1.52।।
transliteration: vimuktāstasya vegena muktvā puṣpāṇi te drumāḥ| avaśīryanta salile nivṛttāḥ suhṛdo yathā
translation: तस्य his, वेगेन speed, विमुक्ताः released, ते द्रुमाः those trees, पुष्पाणि flowers, मुक्त्वा  having dropped, निवृत्ताः returning, सुहृदो यथा like friends, सलिले water, अवशीर्यन्त fallen into water.
explanation: Shedding their blossoms (under his thrust) the trees dropped into the waters of the sea just like close relatives follow at the time of farewell.

shloka_text: लघुत्वेनोपपन्नं तद्विचित्रं सागरेऽपतत्। द्रुमाणां विविधं पुष्पं कपिवायुसमीरितम्।।5.1.53।। ताराचितमिवाकाशं प्रबभौ स महार्णवः।
transliteration: laghutvenopapannaṃ tadvicitraṃ sāgare'patat| drumāṇāṃ vividhaṃ puṣpaṃ kapivāyusamīritam tārācitamivākāśaṃ prababhau sa mahārṇavaḥ|
translation: लघुत्वेन being light, उपपन्नम् risen up, विचित्रम् colourful, कपिवायुसमीरितम् driven by the wind caused by the speed of Hanuman, द्रुमाणाम् of the trees, तत् there, विविधम् various, पुष्पम् flowers, सागरे in the ocean, अपतत् fell, महार्णवः ocean, ताराचितम् filled with stars, आकाशमिव like the sky, प्रबभौ सः glowing.
explanation: Driven by the wind caused by Hanuman's speed a variety of flowers fell into the ocean because of their light weight and the ocean looked colourful and bright like the starspangled sky.

shloka_text: पुष्पौघेणानुबद्धेन नानावर्णेन वानरः। बभौ मेघ इवाकाशे विद्युद्गण विभूषितः।।5.1.54।।
transliteration: puṣpaugheṇānubaddhena nānāvarṇena vānaraḥ| babhau megha ivākāśe vidyudgaṇa vibhūṣitaḥ
translation: नानावर्णेन of different colours, अनुबद्धेन stuck, पुष्पौघेण by the blossoms, वानरः monkey (Hanuman), आकाशे in the sky, विद्युद्गणविभूषितः glowing like lightning, मेघः इव like the cloud, बभौ looked.
explanation: Covered with blossoms of different kinds and colours, Hanuman looked like a cloud brightened by lightnings in the sky.

shloka_text: तस्य वेगसमाधूतैः पुष्पैस्तोयमदृश्यत।।5.1.55।। ताराभिरभिरामाभिरुदिताभिरिवाम्बरम्।
transliteration: tasya vegasamādhūtaiḥ puṣpaistoyamadṛśyata tārābhirabhirāmābhiruditābhirivāmbaram|
translation: तस्य his, वेगसमाधूतैः dropped by the speed, पुष्पैः with flowers, तोयम् water, उदिताभिः rising ones, अभिरामाभिः by the very enchanting, ताराभिः by stars, अम्बरमिव like the sky, अदृश्यत appeared.
explanation: The seawater looked splendid with flowers dropped by dint of his speed. It  resembled the firmament spangled with enchanting stars just risen in the sky.

shloka_text: तस्याम्बरगतौ बाहू ददृशाते प्रसारितौ।।5.1.56।। पर्वताग्राद्विनिष्क्रान्तौ पञ्चास्याविव पन्नगौ।
transliteration: tasyāmbaragatau bāhū dadṛśāte prasāritau parvatāgrādviniṣkrāntau pañcāsyāviva pannagau|
translation: प्रसारितौ stretched out, अम्बरगतौ spread in the sky, तस्य his, बाहू two arms, पर्वताग्रात् from the top of the mountain, विनिष्क्रान्तौ emerging, पञ्चास्यौ fivehooded, पन्नगौ इव like snakes, ददृशाते looked.
explanation: That great Vanara appeared as if he was gulping the entire ocean with its rising waves. While he was looking upward it appeared as though he was keen to drink in the sea as well.

shloka_text: पिबन्निव बभौ चापि सोर्मिमालं महार्णवम्।।5.1.57।। पिपासुरिव चाकाशं ददृशे स महाकपिः।
transliteration: pibanniva babhau cāpi sormimālaṃ mahārṇavam pipāsuriva cākāśaṃ dadṛśe sa mahākapiḥ|
translation: सः that, महाकपिः great vanara, सोर्मिमालम् with its rising waves, महार्णवम् ocean, पिबन्निव as if gulping, बभौ looked, आकाशम् sky, च and , अपि also, पिपासुरिव as if thirsty, ददृशे looked.
explanation: While he was looking upward, that great vanara appeared as if, parched with thirst, he was gulping the entire ocean with its rising waves.

shloka_text: तस्य विद्युत्प्रभाकारे वायुमार्गानुसारिणः।।5.1.58।। नयने विप्रकाशेते पर्वतस्थाविवानलौ।
transliteration: tasya vidyutprabhākāre vāyumārgānusāriṇaḥ nayane viprakāśete parvatasthāvivānalau|
translation: वायुमार्गानुसारिणः of him following the direction of the wind, तस्य his, विद्युत्प्रभाकारे both appearing like the glow of lightning, नयने  eyes, पर्वतस्थौ on the mountain, अनलौ इव like two fires, विप्रकाशेते very glittering.
explanation: As he was moving in the sky following the direction of the wind, his eyes blazed like two fires burning on the mountain, flashing like lightning.

shloka_text: पिङ्गे पिङ्गाक्षमुख्यस्य बृहती परिमण्डले।।5.1.59।। चक्षुषी सम्प्राकाशेते चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ।
transliteration: piṅge piṅgākṣamukhyasya bṛhatī parimaṇḍale cakṣuṣī samprākāśete candrasūryāvivoditau|
translation: पिङ्गाक्षमुख्यस्य of the leader of monkeys, पिङ्गे reddishbrown, बृहती large, परिमण्डले round in shape, चक्षुषी eyes, उदितौ risen, चन्द्रसूर्याविव like Moon and Sun, सम्प्रकाशेते were shining.
explanation: The large, round, reddishbrown eyes of Hanuman shed their bright light like the rising Moon and Sun.

shloka_text: मुखं नासिकया तस्य ताम्रया ताम्रमाबभौ।।5.1.60।। सन्ध्यया समभिस्पृष्टं यथा तत्सूर्यमण्डलम्।
transliteration: mukhaṃ nāsikayā tasya tāmrayā tāmramābabhau sandhyayā samabhispṛṣṭaṃ yathā tatsūryamaṇḍalam|
translation: तस्य his, ताम्रम् copperred, मुखम् face, ताम्रया by the red colour, नासिकया of the nose, सन्ध्यया by twilight, समभिस्पृष्टम् coming close, तत् that, सूर्यमण्डलं यथा like the Sun's orb, आबभौ appeared.
explanation: By the reflection of his copperyred nose, his face looked red like the Sun's orb coming close at twilight.

shloka_text: लाङ्गूलं च समाविद्धं प्लवमानस्य शोभते।।5.1.61।। अम्बरे वायुपुत्रस्य शक्रध्वज इवोच्छ्रितम्।
transliteration: lāṅgūlaṃ ca samāviddhaṃ plavamānasya śobhate ambare vāyuputrasya śakradhvaja ivocchritam|
translation: अम्बरे in the sky, प्लवमानस्य when he was flying, वायुपुत्रस्य of the son of the Windgod, समाविद्धम् installed, लाङ्गूलम् tail, उच्छ्रितं lifted up (in the air), शक्रध्वजः इव like the flag staff of Indra, शोभते looks splendid.
explanation: As the son of the Windgod was flying through the sky, his coiled up tail looked splendid like the banner installed at the festival in honour of Indra (on the fifteenth day of the month of Bhadrapada).

shloka_text: लाङ्गूलचक्रेण महान् शुक्लदंष्ट्रोऽनिलात्मजः।।5.1.62।। व्यरोचत महाप्राज्ञः परिवेषीव भास्करः।
transliteration: lāṅgūlacakreṇa mahān śukladaṃṣṭro'nilātmajaḥ vyarocata mahāprājñaḥ pariveṣīva bhāskaraḥ|
translation: शुक्लदंष्ट्रः whiteteethed, महाप्राज्ञः very wise, महान् great, अनिलात्मजः son of the Windgod, लाङ्गूलचक्रेण  curled up tail, परिवेषी surrounded, भास्करः इव like the Sun, व्यरोचत halo
explanation: With his white teeth and curled up tail, the wise son of the Windgod looked splendid like the halo of the Sungod.

shloka_text: स्फिग्देशेनाभिताम्रेण रराज स महाकपिः।।5.1.63।। महता दारितेनेव गिरिर्गैरिकधातुना।
transliteration: sphigdeśenābhitāmreṇa rarāja sa mahākapiḥ mahatā dāriteneva girirgairikadhātunā|
translation: सः महाकपिः that great vanara, अभिताम्रेण with red one, स्फिग्देशेन with his buttocks, दारितेन इव as if split, महता by huge, गैरिकधातुना deposit of minerals, गिरिः इव like mountain, रराज shone.
explanation: The great monkey with copperred buttocks (other parts being dark) looked splendid like a cleft mountain with a huge deposit of minerals shining red.

shloka_text: तस्य वानरसिंहस्य प्लवमानस्य सागरम्।।5.1.64।। कक्षान्तरगतो वायुर्जीमूत इव गर्जति।
transliteration: tasya vānarasiṃhasya plavamānasya sāgaram kakṣāntaragato vāyurjīmūta iva garjati|
translation: सागरम् ocean, प्लवमानस्य while he was crossing, तस्य his, वानरसिंहस्य lion like vanara, कक्षान्तरगतः through the armpits, वायुः wind, जीमूतः इव like thundering cloud, गर्जति roared.
explanation: The wind passing through the arm pits of the lionlike vanara crossing the ocean sounded like a thundering cloud.

shloka_text: खे यथा निपतत्युल्का ह्युत्तरान्ताद्विनिःसृता।।5.1.65।। दृश्यते सानुबन्धा च तथा स कपिकुञ्जरः।
transliteration: khe yathā nipatatyulkā hyuttarāntādviniḥsṛtā dṛśyate sānubandhā ca tathā sa kapikuñjaraḥ|
translation: उत्तरान्तात् from the northern part, विनिःसृता released, सानुबन्धा च follows, उल्का a meteor, खे in the sky, यथा like, दृश्यते was seen, सः that, कपिकुञ्जरः elephant like vanara, तथा so, निपतति falling. .
explanation: The elephantlike monkey was seen darting across the ocean(going from north to south) like a meteor risen in the north  along with its tailend falling down the sky.

shloka_text: पतत्पतङ्गसङ्काशो व्यायतः शुशुभे कपिः।।5.1.66।। प्रवृद्ध इव मातङ्गः कक्ष्यया बध्यमानया।
transliteration: patatpataṅgasaṅkāśo vyāyataḥ śuśubhe kapiḥ pravṛddha iva mātaṅgaḥ kakṣyayā badhyamānayā|
translation: पतत्पतङ्गसङ्काशः resembled the setting Sun, व्यायतः broad, कपिः monkey (Hanuman), बध्यमानया bound with, कक्ष्यया with the girth, प्रवृद्धः expanded to an enormous size, मातङ्गः इव elephant like, शुशुभे appeared.
explanation: The vanara expanded into an enormous size form appeared as though moving like the setting Sun. He looked like a huge elephant bound round the waist.

shloka_text: उपरिष्टाच्छरीरेण छायया चावगाढया।।5.1.67।। सागरे मारुताविष्टा नौरिवासीत्तदा कपिः।
transliteration: upariṣṭāccharīreṇa chāyayā cāvagāḍhayā sāgare mārutāviṣṭā naurivāsīttadā kapiḥ|
translation: तदा then, कपि: vanara, उपरिष्टात् the top, शरीरेण with his body, सागरे in the ocean, अवगाढया reflected, छायया च  shadow also, मारुताविष्टा swept by the wind, नौरिव like the ship, आसीत् appeared.
explanation: When the vanara was flying in the sky, his shadow reflected in the ocean looked like a ship driven by the wind and sailing on the sea below (as if the lower part of his body was under water and upper part occupied the sky)

shloka_text: यं यं देशं समुद्रस्य जगाम स महाकपिः। स स तस्योरुवेगेन सोन्माद इव लक्ष्यते।।5.1.68।।
transliteration: yaṃ yaṃ deśaṃ samudrasya jagāma sa mahākapiḥ| sa sa tasyoruvegena sonmāda iva lakṣyate
translation: सः that, महाकपिः great vanara, समुद्रस्य of the ocean, यं यं देशं to whichever place, जगाम went, सः सः those, तस्य his, ऊरुवेगेन by the speed of his thighs, सोन्मादः इव riotous with eddies, whirlpools and revolving foam etc.like, लक्ष्यते was seen.
explanation: Whichever part of the sea over which that monkey flew, it appeared as though it was riotous with eddies, whirlpools and revolving foam etc., stirred up by the speed of his thighs.

shloka_text: सागरस्योर्मिजालानामुरसा शैलवर्ष्मणाम्। अभिघ्नंस्तु महावेगः पुप्लुवे स महाकपिः।।5.1.69।।
transliteration: sāgarasyormijālānāmurasā śailavarṣmaṇām| abhighnaṃstu mahāvegaḥ pupluve sa mahākapiḥ
translation: महावेगः very swift, सः that, महाकपिः great vanara, शैलवर्ष्मणाम् as mountains, सागरस्य of the ocean, ऊर्मिजालानाम् the rows of waves, उरसा by his chest, अभिघ्नन् while dashing against, पुप्लुवे flew.
explanation: As the great vanara was flying swiftly, the oceanic waves in rows dashing against his chest rose as high as the  mountain.

shloka_text: कपिवातश्च बलवान् मेघवातश्च निःसृतः। सागरं भीमनिर्घोषं कम्पयामासतुर्भृशम्।।5.1.70।।
transliteration: kapivātaśca balavān meghavātaśca niḥsṛtaḥ| sāgaraṃ bhīmanirghoṣaṃ kampayāmāsaturbhṛśam
translation: बलवान् forceful, कपिवातश्च wind generated by the swift movement of the monkey, निःसृतः rushing towards, मेघवातश्च and the wind of the clouds, भीम निर्घोषम् creating dreadful sounds, सागरम् ocean, भृशम् violently, कम्पयामासतुः both started agitating.
explanation: The forceful wind generated by the monkey moving swiftly, and by the clouds agitated the ocean violently, creating dreadful sounds.

shloka_text: विकर्षन्नूर्मिजालानि बृहन्ति लवणाम्भसि। पुप्लुवे कपिशार्दूलो विकिरन्निव रोदसी।।5.1.71।।
transliteration: vikarṣannūrmijālāni bṛhanti lavaṇāmbhasi| pupluve kapiśārdūlo vikiranniva rodasī
translation: कपिशार्दूलः a tiger among vanaras, लवणाम्भसि the saltwater ocean, बृहन्ति many, ऊर्मिजालानि mighty waves of the ocean, विकर्षन् pulling across, रोदसी the intermediary space (अन्तरिक्ष), विकिरन्निव drawing and dividing the earth and sky like, पुप्लुवे leaped forward.
explanation: As the tiger among the monkeys pushed the big network of waves of the saltwater ocean and leaped forward, it appeared as if  he was drawing the intermediary space dividing the earth and the sky.

shloka_text: मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशानुद्धतान् स महार्णवे। अत्यक्रामन्महावेगस्तरङ्गान् गणयन्निव।।5.1.72।।
transliteration: merumandarasaṅkāśānuddhatān sa mahārṇave| atyakrāmanmahāvegastaraṅgān gaṇayanniva
translation: महावेगः one who is of high speed, महार्णवे in the ocean, उद्धतान् risen, मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशान् resembling mountain Meru and Mandara, तरङ्गान् waves, गणयन्निव as if counting, सः that, अत्यक्रामत् crossed.
explanation: Hanuman moving along in high speed looked as if he was counting the mighty waves risen ike Meru and Mandara mountains.

shloka_text: तस्य वेगसमुद्धूतं जलं सजलदं तदा। अम्बरस्थं विबभ्राज शारदाभ्रमिवाततम्।।5.1.73।।
transliteration: tasya vegasamuddhūtaṃ jalaṃ sajaladaṃ tadā| ambarasthaṃ vibabhrāja śāradābhramivātatam
translation: तदा then, तस्य his, वेगसमुद्धूतम् raised by his onrush, सजलदम् along with the cloud, जलम् water, अम्बरस्थम् found in the sky, आततम् stretched, शारदाभ्रमिव like the autumnal clouds, विबभ्राज shone.
explanation: Then the water raised by his onrush along with the cloud widely spread in the sky shone like an outstreched autumnal cloud.

shloka_text: तिमिनक्रझषाः कूर्मा दृश्यन्ते विवृतास्तदा। वस्त्रापकर्षणेनेव शरीराणि शरीरिणाम्।।5.1.74।।
transliteration: timinakrajhaṣāḥ kūrmā dṛśyante vivṛtāstadā| vastrāpakarṣaṇeneva śarīrāṇi śarīriṇām
translation: तदा then, तिमिनक्रझषाः whales, crocodiles and fish, कूर्माः tortoises, वस्त्रापकर्षणेन clothes put off, शरीरिणाम् of the bodies, शरीराणीव limbs of the body, विवृताः exposed, दृश्यन्ते appeared.
explanation: On account of the seawater rising up,  the whales, crocodiles, fish and tortoises laid bare like the limbs of the body disrobed.

shloka_text: प्लवमानं समीक्ष्याथ भुजङ्गाः सागरालयाः। व्योम्नि तं कपिशार्दूलं सुपर्ण इति मेनिरे।।5.1.75।।
transliteration: plavamānaṃ samīkṣyātha bhujaṅgāḥ sāgarālayāḥ| vyomni taṃ kapiśārdūlaṃ suparṇa iti menire
translation: अथ and then, व्योम्नि in the sky, प्लवमानम् coursing through, तं कपिशार्दूलम् that tiger among vanaras, समीक्ष्य seeing, सागरालयाः those in the abode of the sea, भुजङ्गाः serpents, सुपर्णः इति to be Garuda, मेनिरे thought.
explanation: Seeing Hanuman, the tiger among vanaras, coursing through the sky the serpents in their seaabode mistook him for Garuda.

shloka_text: दशयोजनविस्तीर्णा त्रिंशद्योजनमायता। छाया वानरसिंहस्य जले चारुतराभवत्।।5.1.76।।
transliteration: daśayojanavistīrṇā triṃśadyojanamāyatā| chāyā vānarasiṃhasya jale cārutarābhavat
translation: दशयोजनविस्तीर्णा spread over ten yojanas in breadth, त्रिंशद्योजनम् thirty yojanas, आयता long, वानरसिंहस्य of the lion among monkeys, छाया shadow, जले in water, चारुतरा more pleasing, अभवत् looked.
explanation: The shadow of Hanuman, the lion among monkeys, thirty yojanas long and ten yojanas in breadth appeared more pleasing৷৷

shloka_text: श्वेताभ्रघनराजीव वायुपुत्रानुगामिनी। तस्य सा शुशुभे छाया वितता लवणाम्भसि।।5.1.77।।
transliteration: śvetābhraghanarājīva vāyuputrānugāminī| tasya sā śuśubhe chāyā vitatā lavaṇāmbhasi
translation: वायुपुत्रानुगामिनी following the Windgod's son, लवणाम्भसि in the salty sea, वितता spread out, तस्य his, सा that, छाया shadow, श्वेताभ्रघनराजीव like dark row of clouds sailing in the pristine sky, शुशुभे shone.
explanation: The broad shadow of the son of the Windgod in the sea following him shone like a dark row of clouds sailing in the pristine sky.

shloka_text: शुशुभे स महातेजा महाकायो महाकपिः। वायुमार्गे निरालम्बे पक्षवानिव पर्वतः।।5.1.78।।
transliteration: śuśubhe sa mahātejā mahākāyo mahākapiḥ| vāyumārge nirālambe pakṣavāniva parvataḥ
translation: महातेजाः splendid, महाकायः one with a huge body, सः he, महाकपिः great vanara, निरालम्बे without any support, वायुमार्गे in the direction of the wind, पक्षवान् having wings, पर्वतः इव like a mountain, शुशुभे seemed.
explanation: Hanuman the great vanara, splendid with a huge body coursing through the air seemed like a winged mountain flying the sky without any support.

shloka_text: येनासौ याति बलवान् वेगेन कपिकुञ्जरः। तेन मार्गेण सहसा द्रोणीकृत इवार्णवः।।5.1.79।।
transliteration: yenāsau yāti balavān vegena kapikuñjaraḥ| tena mārgeṇa sahasā droṇīkṛta ivārṇavaḥ
translation: बलवान् powerful, असौ he, कपिकुञ्जरः an elephant among monkeys, वेगेन swiftly, येन मार्गेण the path, याति proceeding, तेन by that, सहसा instantly, अर्णवः the sea, द्रोणीकृतः इव like a valley betwen two mountains.
explanation: As the powerful monkey, an elephant among vanaras, was proceeding swiftly along, the ocean got instantly transformed into a trough on account of water swelling by the force of his flight.

shloka_text: आपाते पक्षिसङ्घानां पक्षिराज इव व्रजन्। हनुमान् मेघजालानि प्रकर्षन् मारुतो यथा।।5.1.80।।
transliteration: āpāte pakṣisaṅghānāṃ pakṣirāja iva vrajan| hanumān meghajālāni prakarṣan māruto yathā
translation: हनुमान् Hanuman, मारुतो यथा like the wind, मेघजालानि strings of clouds, प्रकर्षन् while attracting, पक्षिसङ्घानाम् of the group of birds, आपाते when landed, व्रजन् while moving, पक्षिराजः इव like the king of birds.
explanation: Hanuman was found pulling clusters of big clouds along with him like the Windgod and appeared like Garuda,the king of birds, drawing flocks of birds along with him at the time of landing.

shloka_text: पाण्डुरारुणवर्णानि नीलमाञ्जिष्ठकानि च। कपिनाकृष्यमाणानि महाभ्राणि चकाशिरे।।5.1.81।।
transliteration: pāṇḍurāruṇavarṇāni nīlamāñjiṣṭhakāni ca| kapinākṛṣyamāṇāni mahābhrāṇi cakāśire
translation: कपिना by the vanara, आकृष्यमाणानि drawing, पाण्डुरारुणवर्णानि white and red colour, नीलमाञ्जिष्ठकानि च blue and yellow clouds, महाभ्राणि big clouds, चकाशिरे shining.
explanation: While Hanuman was drawing big clouds which were either white or red or blue or yellow, he looked charming.

shloka_text: प्रविशन्नभ्रजालानि निष्पतंश्च पुनः पुनः। प्रच्छन्नश्च प्रकाशश्च चन्द्रमा इव लक्ष्यते।।5.1.82।।
transliteration: praviśannabhrajālāni niṣpataṃśca punaḥ punaḥ| pracchannaśca prakāśaśca candramā iva lakṣyate
translation: अभ्रजालानि strings of clouds, पुनः पुनः again and again, प्रविशन् while entering, निष्पतंश्च and while coming out, प्रच्छन्नश्च hiding, प्रकाशश्च and shining, चन्द्रमाः इव like the Moon, लक्ष्यते was seen.
explanation: Entering into and emerging from the clouds, he looked like the Moon that appears and disappears (behind a bank of clouds).

shloka_text: प्लवमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा प्लवङ्गं त्वरितं तदा। ववर्षुः पुष्पवर्षाणि देवगन्धर्वदानवाः।।5.1.83।।
transliteration: plavamānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā plavaṅgaṃ tvaritaṃ tadā| vavarṣuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi devagandharvadānavāḥ
translation: तदा then, त्वरितम् quickly, प्लवमानम् crossing, तं प्लवङ्गम् that monkey, दृष्ट्वा after seeing, देवगन्धर्वदानवाः deva, gandharvas and danavas, पुष्पवर्षाणि rain of flowers, ववर्षुः rained.
explanation: Then seeing Hanuman crossing quickly, the gods, gandharvas and demons rained flowers on him.

shloka_text: तताप न हि तं सूर्यः प्लवन्तं वानरोत्तमम्। सिषेवे च तदा वायू रामकार्यार्थसिद्धये।।5.1.84।।
transliteration: tatāpa na hi taṃ sūryaḥ plavantaṃ vānarottamam| siṣeve ca tadā vāyū rāmakāryārthasiddhaye
translation: तदा then, प्लवन्तम् while he was leaping, तं वानरोत्तमम् that best of vanaras, सूर्यः Sun, रामकार्यार्थसिद्धये for accomplishing Rama's task, न हि तताप  did not discharge heat, वायुः च and even wind, सिषेवे served cool.
explanation: The Sun spared Hanuman from the heat and even the Windgod served him, blowing cool while he was taking leaps in order to fulfil Rama's mission.

shloka_text: ऋषयस्तुष्टुवुश्चैनं प्लवमानं विहायसा। जगुश्च देवगन्धर्वाः प्रशंसन्तो महौजसम्।।5.1.85।।
transliteration: ṛṣayastuṣṭuvuścainaṃ plavamānaṃ vihāyasā| jaguśca devagandharvāḥ praśaṃsanto mahaujasam
translation: विहायसा in the sky, प्लवमानम् while he leaped, महौजसम् a highly vigourous one, ऋषयः ascetics, तुष्टुवुश्चैनं extolled him, देवगन्धर्वाः gods and gandharvas, प्रशंसन्तः while prasing him, जगुश्च also sang.
explanation: The sages praised him while he was coursing through the sky, the gods and gandharvas sang in praise of him extolling his majesty and vigour.

shloka_text: नागाश्च तुष्टुवुर्यक्षा रक्षांसि विबुधाः खगाः। प्रेक्ष्य सर्वे कपिवरं सहसा विगतक्लमम्।।5.1.86।।
transliteration: nāgāśca tuṣṭuvuryakṣā rakṣāṃsi vibudhāḥ khagāḥ| prekṣya sarve kapivaraṃ sahasā vigataklamam
translation: विगतक्लमम् unwearied, कपिवरम् the great monkey, प्रेक्ष्य observing, सहसा at once, नागाश्च nagas, यक्षाः yakshas, रक्षांसि rakshasas (who were protecting the southwest), विबुधाः learned sages, खगाः birds, सर्वे all, तुष्टुवुः praised .
explanation: Observing the unwearied monkey the nagas, yakshas, the demons (protecting the southwest), the learned sages and birds praised him.

shloka_text: तस्मिन् प्लवगशार्दूले प्लवमाने हनूमति। इक्ष्वाकुकुलमानार्थी चिन्तयामास सागरः।।5.1.87।।
transliteration: tasmin plavagaśārdūle plavamāne hanūmati| ikṣvākukulamānārthī cintayāmāsa sāgaraḥ
translation: प्लवगशार्दूले when the tiger among vanaras, तस्मिन् हनूमति when that monkeychief, प्लवमाने while leaping, सागरः the Seagod, इक्ष्वाकुकुलमानार्थी wishing the wellbeing and honour of the Ikshvaku family, चिन्तयामास started thinking.
explanation: While the monkeychief was leaping (across the sea) the Seagod wished the wellbeing of the Ikshvaku family and honoured him. (The Seagod belonged to the same race) :

shloka_text: साहाय्यं वानरेन्द्रस्य यदि नाहं हनूमत:। करिष्यामि भविष्यामि सर्ववाच्यो विवक्षताम्।।5.1.88।।
transliteration: sāhāyyaṃ vānarendrasya yadi nāhaṃ hanūmata:| kariṣyāmi bhaviṣyāmi sarvavācyo vivakṣatām
translation: अहम् I, वानरेन्द्रस्य of the chief of monkeys, हनूमतः Hanuman's, साहाय्यम् help, न करिष्यामि यदि if I do not render, विवक्षताम् by all the wise speakers, सर्ववाच्यः will be  blamed, भविष्यामि I will be.
explanation: 'If I fail to help the monkeychief, the wise will blame me'.

shloka_text: अहमिक्ष्वाकुनाथेन सगरेण विवर्धितः। इक्ष्वाकुसचिवश्चायं नावसीदितुमर्हति।।5.1.89।।
transliteration: ahamikṣvākunāthena sagareṇa vivardhitaḥ| ikṣvākusacivaścāyaṃ nāvasīditumarhati
translation: अहम् I, इक्ष्वाकुनाथेन by the scion of the Ikshvakus, सगरेण by Sagara, विवर्धितः made to extend , इक्ष्वाकुसचिवः च and the minister of Ikshvaku race, अयम् this person, अवसीदितुम् to perish, नार्हति he shouldl not.
explanation: 'I expanded on account of a scion of the Ikshvaku race (Sagara) and I should not do anything to make him (Hanuman) suffer since he is the minister helping the Ikshvaku race'.

shloka_text: तथा मया विधातव्यं विश्रमेत यथा कपिः।।5.1.90।। शेषं च मयि विश्रान्तः सुखेनातिपतिष्यति।
transliteration: tathā mayā vidhātavyaṃ viśrameta yathā kapiḥ śeṣaṃ ca mayi viśrāntaḥ sukhenātipatiṣyati|
translation: कपिः monkey, यथा likewise, विश्रमेत he may take rest, तथा in that way, मया by myself, विधातव्यम् arrangement has to be made, मयि on me, विश्रान्तः the rest, शेषम् remaining, सुखेन comfortably, अतिपतिष्यति will leap over.
explanation: 'I will have to make arrangements for his rest. Later he can resume his journey comfortably'.

shloka_text: इति कृत्वा मतिं साध्वींसमुद्र श्छन्नमम्भसि।।5.1.91।। हिरण्यनाभं मैनाकमुवाच गिरिसत्तमम्।
transliteration: iti kṛtvā matiṃ sādhvīṃsamudra śchannamambhasi hiraṇyanābhaṃ mainākamuvāca girisattamam|
translation: समुद्रः the Seagod, इति thus, साध्वीं well, मतिम् in his mind, कृत्वा after resolving, अम्भसि in waters, छन्नम् hidden, हिरण्यनाभम् golden, गिरिसत्तमम् noble mountain, मैनाकम् to Mainaka, उवाच said.
explanation: Having resolved in his mind, the Seagod addressed the noble, golden mount Mainaka, hidden in the sea:

shloka_text: त्वमिहासुरसंघानां पातालतलवासिनाम्।।5.1.92।। देवराज्ञा गिरिश्रेष्ठ परिघः सन्निवेशितः।
transliteration: tvamihāsurasaṃghānāṃ pātālatalavāsinām devarājñā giriśreṣṭha parighaḥ sanniveśitaḥ|
translation: गिरिश्रेष्ठ O foremost mountain, त्वम् you, इह here, पातालतलवासिनाम् for those residing in the nether world, असुरसङ्घानाम् of hordes of demons, परिघः beam used as a barrier against the gateway, देवराज्ञा by the lord of the gods, सन्निवेशितः arranged.
explanation: 'O foremost mountain you are kept here by Indra, lord of the gods as a barrier against the intrusion of demons residing in the netherworld.

shloka_text: त्वमेषां जातवीर्याणां पुनरेवोत्पतिष्यताम्।।5.1.93।। पातालस्याप्रमेयस्य द्वारमावृत्य तिष्ठसि।
transliteration: tvameṣāṃ jātavīryāṇāṃ punarevotpatiṣyatām pātālasyāprameyasya dvāramāvṛtya tiṣṭhasi|
translation: जातवीर्याणाम् of the violent, एषाम् for these, पुनरेव again, उत्पतिष्यताम् prone to come up, त्वम् you, अप्रमेयस्य of the immeasurable, पातालस्य nether world's, द्वारम् entrance, आवृत्य  blocking, तिष्ठसि are staying.
explanation: "You are staying at the entrance preventing the violent demons of the immeasurable nether world from jumping onto the surface.

shloka_text: तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्चैव शक्तिस्ते शैल वर्धितुम्।।5.1.94।। तस्मात्संचोदयामि त्वामुत्तिष्ठ गिरिसत्तम।
transliteration: tiryagūrdhvamadhaścaiva śaktiste śaila vardhitum tasmātsaṃcodayāmi tvāmuttiṣṭha girisattama|
translation: शैल O mountain, तिर्यक् across, ऊर्ध्वम् upward, अधश्चैव and at the bottom, वर्धितुम् to grow, ते to you, शक्तिः energy, गिरिसत्तम O noble mountain, तस्मात् therefore, त्वाम् you, सञ्चोदयामि I am prompting, उत्तिष्ठ you mary rise.
explanation: "O noble mountain you have the capacity to grow across, upward and downward by your free will. I therefore prompt you to grow.

shloka_text: स एष कपिशार्दूलस्त्वामुपर्येति वीर्यवान्।।5.1.95।। हनूमान्रामकार्यार्थं भीमकर्मा खमाप्लुतः।
transliteration: sa eṣa kapiśārdūlastvāmuparyeti vīryavān hanūmānrāmakāryārthaṃ bhīmakarmā khamāplutaḥ|
translation: कपिशार्दूलः a tiger among monkeys, वीर्यवान् valiant one, भीमकर्मा a performer of dreadful deeds, सः एषः that great personality, हनूमान् Hanuman, रामकार्यार्थम् on account of Rama's work, खम् in the sky, आप्लुतः flew, त्वाम् you उपरि over, एति you
explanation: "Valiant Hanuman, a tiger among monkeys and a performer of dreadful deeds, is  flying over you to fulfil Rama's mission

shloka_text: अस्य साह्यं मया कार्यमिक्ष्वाकुकुलवर्तिनः।।5.1.96।। मम हीक्ष्वाकवः पूज्याः परं पूज्यतमास्तव।
transliteration: asya sāhyaṃ mayā kāryamikṣvākukulavartinaḥ mama hīkṣvākavaḥ pūjyāḥ paraṃ pūjyatamāstava|
translation: अस्य to him, इक्ष्वाकुकुलवर्तिनः for him who serves the Ikshvaku race, मया by me, साह्यम् help, कार्यम् should be given, मम to myself, इक्ष्वाकवः the kings of the Ikshvaku race, पूज्याः worthy of adoration, तव  to you, पूज्यतमाः most adorable .
explanation: "I should help him for he is working for the welfare of the Ikshavaku family. The Ikshvaku kings are worthy of adoration to me and for you as well.

shloka_text: कुरु साचिव्यमस्माकं न नः कार्यमतिक्रमेत्।।5.1.97।। कर्तव्यमकृतं कार्यं सतां मन्युमुदीरयेत्।
transliteration: kuru sācivyamasmākaṃ na naḥ kāryamatikramet kartavyamakṛtaṃ kāryaṃ satāṃ manyumudīrayet|
translation: अस्माकम् for us, साचिव्यम् counselling (the duty of a minister), कुरु you may do, नः for us, कार्यम् task, न अतिक्रमेत् may not be lost, कर्तव्यम् our duty, कार्यम्  task, अकृतम् not carried out, सताम् for pious men, मन्युम् anger, उदीरयेत् will cause.
explanation: "You may act as our minister and let us not miss this chance. Pious men lose their cool if a worthy act is left unfulfilled.

shloka_text: सलिलादूर्ध्वमुत्तिष्ठ तिष्ठत्वेष कपिस्त्वयि।।5.1.98।। अस्माकमतिथिश्चैव पूज्यश्च प्लवतां वरः।
transliteration: salilādūrdhvamuttiṣṭha tiṣṭhatveṣa kapistvayi asmākamatithiścaiva pūjyaśca plavatāṃ varaḥ|
translation: सलिलात् from the waters, ऊर्ध्वम् above, उत्तिष्ठ rise, अस्माकम् for us, अतिथिश्चैव guest also, पूज्यश्च worthy of worship also, प्लवताम् among the jumping ones, वरः noble, एषः कपिः this monkey, त्वयि on you, तिष्ठतु let him rest.
explanation: "Rise up from the waters. Let him rest on you since this noble monkey is our guest and worthy of worship.

shloka_text: चामीकरमहानाभ देवगन्धर्वसेवित।।5.1.99।। हनुमांस्त्वयि विश्रान्तस्ततः शेषं गमिष्यति।
transliteration: cāmīkaramahānābha devagandharvasevita hanumāṃstvayi viśrāntastataḥ śeṣaṃ gamiṣyati|
translation: चामीकरमहानाभ O goldenpeaked one, देवगन्धर्व सेवित resorted to by gods,  gandharvas, हनुमान् Hanuman, त्वयि by you, विश्रान्तः resting, ततः then, शेषम् remaing part, गमिष्यति will cover.
explanation: "O goldenpeaked mountainyou are the refuge of the gods and gandharvas. Let him also rest on you for a while before he negotiates the remaining part of the journey.

shloka_text: काकुत्स्थस्यानृशंस्यं च मैथिल्याश्च विवासनम्।।5.1.100।। श्रमं च प्लवगेन्द्रस्य समीक्ष्योत्थातुमर्हसि।
transliteration: kākutsthasyānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca maithilyāśca vivāsanam śramaṃ ca plavagendrasya samīkṣyotthātumarhasi|
translation: काकुत्स्थस्य Rama's, अनृशंस्यं च good nature, मैथिल्याः Sita's, विवासनं च deportation, प्लवगेन्द्रस्य Hanuman's, श्रमं च strain also, समीक्ष्य considering, उत्थातुम् to rise up, अर्हसि you ought to.
explanation: "You ought to rise up if you consider the nobility of the scion of the Kakusthas, the deportation of Mythili, and the exertion put forth by Hanuman, the lord of monkeys".

shloka_text: हिरण्यनाभो मैनाको निशम्य लवणाम्भसः।।5.1.101।। उत्पपात जलात्तूर्णं महाद्रुमलतायुतः।
transliteration: hiraṇyanābho maināko niśamya lavaṇāmbhasaḥ utpapāta jalāttūrṇaṃ mahādrumalatāyutaḥ|
translation: हिरण्यनाभः mountain with gold at its bosom, मैनाकः Mainaka, लवणाम्भसः of the salty ocean, निशम्य after listening, महाद्रुमलतायुतः with great trees and creepers, तूर्णम् at once, जलात् from the water, उत्पपात  rose up.
explanation: Hearing the command of the god of the ocean, mount Mainaka, rich in gold and covered with trees and creepers rose up at once from the water.

shloka_text: स सागरजलं भित्त्वा बभूवाभ्युत्थितस्तदा।।5.1.102।। यथा जलधरं भित्त्वा दीप्तरश्मिर्दिवाकरः।
transliteration: sa sāgarajalaṃ bhittvā babhūvābhyutthitastadā yathā jaladharaṃ bhittvā dīptaraśmirdivākaraḥ|
translation: तदा then, सः that mountain, सागरजलम् waters of the ocean, भित्त्वा projecting, दीप्तरमशिः the lord of glowing rays, दिवाकरः Sun, जलधरम् a cloud, भित्त्वा breaking, यथा as, अभ्युत्थितः rose up, बभूव appeared.
explanation: Just as the rising Sun comes out with glowing rays tearing the veil of dark clouds, the mountain rose up from the water of the ocean.

shloka_text: स महात्मा मुहूर्तेन सर्वतः सलिलावृतः।।5.1.103।। दर्शयामास शृङ्गाणि सागरेण नियोजितः। आदित्योदयसङ्काशैरालिखद्भिरिवाम्बरम्। शातकुम्भमयैः शृङ्गैः सकिन्नरमहोरगैः।।5.1.104।।
transliteration: sa mahātmā muhūrtena sarvataḥ salilāvṛtaḥ darśayāmāsa śṛṅgāṇi sāgareṇa niyojitaḥ| ādityodayasaṅkāśairālikhadbhirivāmbaram| śātakumbhamayaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ sakinnaramahoragaiḥ
translation: सकिन्नरमहोरगैः with nagas and kinnaras, आदित्योदयसङ्काशैः resembling the rising Sun, सर्वतः all over, सलिलावृत: submerged by water, अम्बरम् sky, आलिखद्भि: as if scraping the sky, इव like that, शातकुम्भमयैः golden, शृङ्गैः with peak, सर्वतः all over, सलिलावृतः covered with water, सः महात्मा the great mountain, सागरेण the ocean's, नियोजितः ordered, मुहूर्तेन in a moment, शृङ्गाणि mountain peak, दर्शयामास was seen.
explanation: At the instance of Varuna, (the presiding deity of the ocean) the lofty mountain appeared, projecting its peaks, hitherto submerged in the water. The golden peaks inhabited by nagas and kinnaras resemmbled the rising Sun as though scraping the sky in a moment.

shloka_text: स महात्मा मुहूर्तेन सर्वतः सलिलावृतः।।5.1.103।। दर्शयामास शृङ्गाणि सागरेण नियोजितः। आदित्योदयसङ्काशैरालिखद्भिरिवाम्बरम्। शातकुम्भमयैः शृङ्गैः सकिन्नरमहोरगैः।।5.1.104।।
transliteration: sa mahātmā muhūrtena sarvataḥ salilāvṛtaḥ darśayāmāsa śṛṅgāṇi sāgareṇa niyojitaḥ| ādityodayasaṅkāśairālikhadbhirivāmbaram| śātakumbhamayaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ sakinnaramahoragaiḥ
translation: सकिन्नरमहोरगैः with nagas and kinnaras, आदित्योदयसङ्काशैः resembling the rising Sun, सर्वतः all over, सलिलावृत: submerged by water, अम्बरम् sky, आलिखद्भि: as if scraping the sky, इव like that, शातकुम्भमयैः golden, शृङ्गैः with peak, सर्वतः all over, सलिलावृतः covered with water, सः महात्मा the great mountain, सागरेण the ocean's, नियोजितः ordered, मुहूर्तेन in a moment, शृङ्गाणि mountain peak, दर्शयामास was seen.
explanation: At the instance of Varuna, (the presiding deity of the ocean) the lofty mountain appeared, projecting its peaks, hitherto submerged in the water. The golden peaks inhabited by nagas and kinnaras resemmbled the rising Sun as though scraping the sky in a moment.

shloka_text: तप्तजाम्बूनदैः शृङ्गैः पर्वतस्य समुत्थितैः।।5.1.105।। आकाशं शस्त्रसङ्काशमभवत्काञ्चनप्रभम्।
transliteration: taptajāmbūnadaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ parvatasya samutthitaiḥ ākāśaṃ śastrasaṅkāśamabhavatkāñcanaprabham|
translation: समुत्थितैः by those risen ones, तप्तजाम्बूनदैः by barnished gold, पर्वतस्य mountain's, शृङ्गैः with peaks, शस्त्रसंकाशम् the colour of weapons, आकाशम् sky, काञ्चनप्रभम्, golden, अभवत् appeared.
explanation: The sky shone like barnished weapons smeared with the golden colour of the mountain peaks that rose up above the water.

shloka_text: जातरूपमयैः शृङ्गैर्भ्राजमानैः स्वयंप्रभैः।।5.1.106।। आदित्यशतसङ्काशः सोऽभवद्गिरिसत्तमः।
transliteration: jātarūpamayaiḥ śṛṅgairbhrājamānaiḥ svayaṃprabhaiḥ ādityaśatasaṅkāśaḥ so'bhavadgirisattamaḥ|
translation: स्वयंप्रभैः the selfeffulgent ones, भ्राजमानैः glittering , जातरूपमयैः  golden, शृङ्गैः by the peak, सः that, गिरिसत्तमः noble mountain, आदित्यशतसङ्काशः like a thousand Suns, अभवत् appeared.
explanation: The noble mountain, Mainaka was glittering  like a thousand Suns with selfeffulgent golden peaks shining.

shloka_text: तमुत्थितमसङ्गेन हनुमानग्रतः स्थितम्।।5.1.107।। मध्ये लवणतोयस्य विघ्नोऽयमिति निश्चितः।
transliteration: tamutthitamasaṅgena hanumānagrataḥ sthitam madhye lavaṇatoyasya vighno'yamiti niścitaḥ|
translation: लवणतोयस्य of the seawater, मध्ये in the midst, असङ्गेन impediment across, उत्थितम् rising up, अग्रतः in front, स्थितम् stood, तम् him, हनुमान् Hanuman, अयम् this, विघ्नः obstruction, इति thus, निश्चितः surely.
explanation: Hanuman considered the mountain rising up in the midst of the ocean and standing in front an impediment.

shloka_text: स तमुच्छ्र्रतमत्यर्थं महावेगो महाकपिः।।5.1.108।। उरसा पातयामास जीमूतमिव मारुतः।
transliteration: sa tamucchrratamatyarthaṃ mahāvego mahākapiḥ urasā pātayāmāsa jīmūtamiva mārutaḥ|
translation: महावेगः swift in action, सः महाकपिः that great vanara, अत्यर्थम् instantly, उच्छ्रितम् risen, तम् him, मारुतः the wind, जीमूतमिव like a cloud, उरसा with the chest, पातयामास pushed it down.
explanation: The great vanara,who was swift in action felled down the mountain that had risen high instantly with his chest just as the wind would strike a cloud.

shloka_text: स तथा पातितस्तेन कपिना पर्वतोत्तमः।।5.1.109।। बुद्ध्वा तस्य कपेर्वेगं जहर्ष च ननन्द च।
transliteration: sa tathā pātitastena kapinā parvatottamaḥ buddhvā tasya kapervegaṃ jaharṣa ca nananda ca|
translation: तेन कपिना by that vanara, तथा in that way, पातितः felled down, स पर्वतोत्तमः that high mountain, तस्य कपेः by the vanara's, वेगम् speed, बुद्ध्वा after realising, जहर्ष च felt happy, ननन्द च and roared in high pitch.
explanation: Felled by the vanara's speed, the tall mountain overwhelmed with joy roared in high pitch.

shloka_text: तमाकाशगतं वीरमाकाशे समुपस्थितः।।5.1.110।। प्रीतो हृष्टमाना वाक्यमब्रवीत्पर्वतः कपिम्। मानुषं धारयन् रूपमात्मनः शिखरे स्थितः।।5.1.111।।
transliteration: tamākāśagataṃ vīramākāśe samupasthitaḥ prīto hṛṣṭamānā vākyamabravītparvataḥ kapim| mānuṣaṃ dhārayan rūpamātmanaḥ śikhare sthitaḥ
translation: पर्वतः mountain, प्रीतः feeling happy, हृष्टमानाः gladly, मानुषम् human, रूपम् form, धारयन् assuming, आत्मनः his, शिखरे on the summit, स्थितः standing, आकाशगतम् gone to the aerial region, तं वीरं कपिम् that heroic vanara, आकाशे in the sky, समुपस्थितः  stood, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Now the mountain assumed a human form  and standing on its own summit, which stood very high, and glad at heart, addressed the heroic vanara gone to the aerial region.

shloka_text: तमाकाशगतं वीरमाकाशे समुपस्थितः।।5.1.110।। प्रीतो हृष्टमाना वाक्यमब्रवीत्पर्वतः कपिम्। मानुषं धारयन् रूपमात्मनः शिखरे स्थितः।।5.1.111।।
transliteration: tamākāśagataṃ vīramākāśe samupasthitaḥ prīto hṛṣṭamānā vākyamabravītparvataḥ kapim| mānuṣaṃ dhārayan rūpamātmanaḥ śikhare sthitaḥ
translation: पर्वतः mountain, प्रीतः feeling happy, हृष्टमानाः gladly, मानुषम् human, रूपम् form, धारयन् assuming, आत्मनः his, शिखरे on the summit, स्थितः standing, आकाशगतम् gone to the aerial region, तं वीरं कपिम् that heroic vanara, आकाशे in the sky, समुपस्थितः  stood, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Now the mountain assumed a human form  and standing on its own summit, which stood very high, and glad at heart, addressed the heroic vanara gone to the aerial region.

shloka_text: दुष्करं कृतवान्कर्म त्वमिदं वानरोत्तम। निपत्य मम शृङ्गेषु विश्रमस्व यथासुखम्।।5.1.112।।
transliteration: duṣkaraṃ kṛtavānkarma tvamidaṃ vānarottama| nipatya mama śṛṅgeṣu viśramasva yathāsukham
translation: वानरोत्तम O best of the vanaras, त्वम् you, दुष्करम् formidable, इदम् this, कर्म deed, कृतवान्  accomplished, मम my, शृङ्गेषु on this peak, निपत्य alighting, यथासुखम् comfortably, विश्रमस्व you may rest.
explanation: "O best of vanaras you have achieved a formidable deed. Alighting on my peak and comfortably resting awhile, you may resume your journey.

shloka_text: राघवस्य कुले जातैरुदधिः परिवर्धितः। स त्वां रामहिते युक्तं प्रत्यर्चयति सागरः।।5.1.113।।
transliteration: rāghavasya kule jātairudadhiḥ parivardhitaḥ| sa tvāṃ rāmahite yuktaṃ pratyarcayati sāgaraḥ
translation: उदधिः the ocean, राघवस्य of Raghava's, कुले in the family, जातैः by those born, परिवर्धितः is extended, सः सागरः that Sagara, रामहिते for the service of Rama, युक्तम् endowed with, त्वाम् you, प्रत्यर्चयति honour in return.
explanation: "The son of Rama's family, Sagara, has extended the ocean in the past.It is most appropriate that he (the god of the sea) honours you in return as you have set out in the service of Rama.

shloka_text: कृते च प्रतिकर्तव्यमेष धर्मः सनातनः। सोऽयं त्वत्प्रतिकारार्थी त्वत्तः सम्मानमर्हति।।5.1.114।।
transliteration: kṛte ca pratikartavyameṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ| so'yaṃ tvatpratikārārthī tvattaḥ sammānamarhati
translation: कृते when help is rendered, प्रतिकर्तव्यम्  it should be repaid, एषः this, सनातनः eternal, धर्मः dharma, तत्प्रतिकारार्थी for doing service in return, सः अयम् this, त्वत्तः from you, सम्मानम् honour, अर्हति he deserves.
explanation: When help is rendered it ought to be repaid—this is the eternal law; and he who seeks to do service in return deserves honour from you.

shloka_text: त्वन्निमित्तमनेनाहं बहुमानात्प्रचोदितः। तिष्ठ त्वं कपिशार्दूल मयि विश्रम्य गम्यताम्।।5.1.115।। तव सानुषु विश्रान्तः शेषं प्रक्रमतामिति। योजनानां शतं चापि कपिरेष समाप्लुतः।।5.1.116।।
transliteration: tvannimittamanenāhaṃ bahumānātpracoditaḥ| tiṣṭha tvaṃ kapiśārdūla mayi viśramya gamyatām tava sānuṣu viśrāntaḥ śeṣaṃ prakramatāmiti| yojanānāṃ śataṃ cāpi kapireṣa samāplutaḥ
translation: योजनानां शतम् a hundred yojanas, समाप्लुतः is leaping, एषः this, कपिः vanara, तव your, सानुषु on the peaks, विश्रान्तः resting, शेषम् remaining, प्रक्रमताम proceed thereafter, इति thus, अनेन by this ocean, त्वन्निमित्तम for your sake, अहम् I, बहुमानात् with honour, प्रचोदितः prompted, कपिशार्दूल: a tiger among monkeys, त्वम् you, तिष्ठ stay, मयि at my, विश्रम्य after resting, गम्यताम् you can go.
explanation: "I was prompted by the ocean for your sake since he has great regard for you. O great monkey you may rest here for a while and continue your journey. The lord of the ocean feels that this tiger among monkeys can cover the distance of a hundred yojanas. He tells me, 'let him rest on your peak and then cover the rest of the distance'.

shloka_text: त्वन्निमित्तमनेनाहं बहुमानात्प्रचोदितः। तिष्ठ त्वं कपिशार्दूल मयि विश्रम्य गम्यताम्।।5.1.115।। तव सानुषु विश्रान्तः शेषं प्रक्रमतामिति। योजनानां शतं चापि कपिरेष समाप्लुतः।।5.1.116।।
transliteration: tvannimittamanenāhaṃ bahumānātpracoditaḥ| tiṣṭha tvaṃ kapiśārdūla mayi viśramya gamyatām tava sānuṣu viśrāntaḥ śeṣaṃ prakramatāmiti| yojanānāṃ śataṃ cāpi kapireṣa samāplutaḥ
translation: योजनानां शतम् a hundred yojanas, समाप्लुतः is leaping, एषः this, कपिः vanara, तव your, सानुषु on the peaks, विश्रान्तः resting, शेषम् remaining, प्रक्रमताम proceed thereafter, इति thus, अनेन by this ocean, त्वन्निमित्तम for your sake, अहम् I, बहुमानात् with honour, प्रचोदितः prompted, कपिशार्दूल: a tiger among monkeys, त्वम् you, तिष्ठ stay, मयि at my, विश्रम्य after resting, गम्यताम् you can go.
explanation: "I was prompted by the ocean for your sake since he has great regard for you. O great monkey you may rest here for a while and continue your journey. The lord of the ocean feels that this tiger among monkeys can cover the distance of a hundred yojanas. He tells me, 'let him rest on your peak and then cover the rest of the distance'.

shloka_text: तदिदं गन्धवत्स्वादु कन्दमूलफलं बहु। तदास्वाद्य हरिश्रेष्ठ विश्रान्तोऽनु गमिष्यसि।।5.1.117।।
transliteration: tadidaṃ gandhavatsvādu kandamūlaphalaṃ bahu| tadāsvādya hariśreṣṭha viśrānto'nu gamiṣyasi
translation: हरिश्रेष्ठ O foremost of the monkeys, तत् इदम् such as this, गन्धवत् sweet smelling, स्वादु tasty, बहु plenty, कन्दमूलफलम् roots and fruits, इदम् this, तत् that, आस्वद्य after tasting, विश्रान्तः taking rest, अनु later, गमिष्यसि you may go.
explanation: "O foremost of the monkeys after eating plenty of sweet and tasty roots and fruits and resting a while you may go.

shloka_text: अस्माकमपि सम्बन्ध: कपिमुख्य त्वयास्ति वै। प्रख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु महागुणपरिग्रहः।।5.1.118।।
transliteration: asmākamapi sambandha: kapimukhya tvayāsti vai| prakhyātastriṣu lokeṣu mahāguṇaparigrahaḥ
translation: कपिमुख्य O chief of monkeys, त्रिषु in the three, लोकेषु in the worlds, प्रख्यातः wellknown, महागुणपरिग्रहः possesing great merits, सम्बन्धः kinship, त्वया with you, अस्माकमपि for us also, अस्ति वै  is there.
explanation: "O chief of monkeys, indeed we too have a relationship with you based on merit  which is wellknown to all the three worlds.

shloka_text: वेगवन्तः प्लवन्तो ये प्लवगा मारुतात्मज। तेषां मुख्यतमं मन्ये त्वामहं कपिकुञ्जर।।5.1.119।।
transliteration: vegavantaḥ plavanto ye plavagā mārutātmaja| teṣāṃ mukhyatamaṃ manye tvāmahaṃ kapikuñjara
translation: मारुतात्मज O son of the Windgod, कपिकुञ्जर O elephant among monkeys, वेगवन्तः  swift, प्लवन्तः jumping, ये those, प्लवगाः vanaras, तेषाम् of them, मुख्यतमम् the foremost, त्वाम् you, अहम् I, मन्ये believe.
explanation: "O son of the Windgod you are an elephant among monkeys, the foremost among them who move at a high speed.

shloka_text: अतिथिः किल पूजार्हः प्राकृतोऽपि विजानता। धर्मं जिज्ञासमानेन किं पुनस्त्वादृशो महान्।।5.1.120।।
transliteration: atithiḥ kila pūjārhaḥ prākṛto'pi vijānatā| dharmaṃ jijñāsamānena kiṃ punastvādṛśo mahān
translation: धर्मम् righteousness, जिज्ञासमानेन  who desires to know, विजानता by a wise man, प्राकृतोऽपि even an ordinary person, अतिथिः a guest, पूजार्हः worthy of worship, त्वादृशः a person like you, महान् great, किं पुनः what again, किल it is  said.
explanation: "Even a newcomer, however ordinary, deserves worship by a wise man who wishes to educate himself in the path of righteousness. Needless to say that distinguished guest like you deserves all reverence.

shloka_text: त्वं हि देववरिष्ठस्य मारुतस्य महात्मनः। पुत्रस्तस्यैव वेगेन सदृशः कपिकुञ्जर।।5.1.121।।
transliteration: tvaṃ hi devavariṣṭhasya mārutasya mahātmanaḥ| putrastasyaiva vegena sadṛśaḥ kapikuñjara
translation: कपिकुञ्जर foremost among vanaras, त्वम् you, देववरिष्ठस्य of the pre eminent one among the divine beings, महात्मनः of the highsouled, मारुतस्य wind god's, पुत्रः हि son indeed, वेगेन in speed, तस्यैव with his own self, सदृशः comparable.
explanation: "O foremost among the vanaras you are the son of the highsouled Windgod's, preeminent among the gods, you are also equal to him in speed.

shloka_text: पूजिते त्वयि धर्मज्ञ पूजां प्राप्नोति मारुतः। तस्मात्त्वं पूजनीयो मे शृणु चाप्यत्र कारणम्।।5.1.122।।
transliteration: pūjite tvayi dharmajña pūjāṃ prāpnoti mārutaḥ| tasmāttvaṃ pūjanīyo me śṛṇu cāpyatra kāraṇam
translation: धर्मज्ञ O knower of righteousness, त्वयि when you, पूजिते if you are worshipped, मारुतः Windgod, पूजाम् veneration, प्राप्नोति will recieve, तस्मात् therefore, त्वम् you, अपि also, मे to me, पूजनीयः worshipworthy, अत्र here, कारणं च also the cause, शृणु listen.
explanation: "O knower of righteousness to worship you is to honour the Windgod. Therefore you are worthy of worship for me. I will tell you the reason. Listen.

shloka_text: पूर्वं कृतयुगे तात पर्वताः पक्षिणोऽभवन्। ते हि जग्मुर्दिशः सर्वा गरुडानिलवेगिनः।।5.1.123।।
transliteration: pūrvaṃ kṛtayuge tāta parvatāḥ pakṣiṇo'bhavan| te hi jagmurdiśaḥ sarvā garuḍānilaveginaḥ
translation: तात O dear son, पूर्वम् formerly, कृतयुगे in Krita yuga, पर्वताः mountains,पक्षिणः had wings, अभवन् endowed, ते  they, गरुडानिलवेगिनः swift like Garuda and wind, सर्वाः all, दिशः directions, जग्मुः went about.
explanation: "Formerly in Kritayuga, O dear, mountains were endowed with wings. They used to move speedily in all directions like Garuda and the Windgod.

shloka_text: ततस्तेषु प्रयातेषु देवसङ्घा: महर्षिभिः। भूतानि च भयं जग्मुस्तेषां पतनशङ्कया।5.1.124।।
transliteration: tatasteṣu prayāteṣu devasaṅghā: maharṣibhiḥ| bhūtāni ca bhayaṃ jagmusteṣāṃ patanaśaṅkayā|5.1.124||
translation: ततः then, तेषु when they, प्रयातेषु went about, सहर्षिभिः and sages, देवसङ्घा: hosts of gods, भूतानि च and all creatures, तेषाम् their, पतनशङ्कया out of fear of their falling down, भयम् fear, जग्मुः felt.
explanation: "When they moved about, even hosts of sages, gods and creatures panicked for fear of falling down (and destroying all worlds).

shloka_text: ततः क्रुद्धः सहस्राक्षः पर्वतानां शतक्रतुः। पक्षान् चिच्छेद वज्रेण तत्र तत्र सहस्रशः।।5.1.125।।
transliteration: tataḥ kruddhaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ parvatānāṃ śatakratuḥ| pakṣān ciccheda vajreṇa tatra tatra sahasraśaḥ
translation: ततः then, शतक्रतुः one who has performed a hundred yajnas, सहस्राक्षः Indra, क्रुद्धः in anger, तत्र तत्र here and there, सहस्रशः in thousand, पर्वतानाम् of the mountains, पक्षान् wings, वज्रेण with the thunderbolt, चिच्छेद cut into pieces.
explanation: "Provoked at this, the thousandeyed Indra who had performed a hundred sacrifices cut off the wings of mountains into a thousands pieces with his thunderbolt.

shloka_text: स मामुपागतः क्रुद्धो वज्रमुद्यम्य देवराट्। ततोऽहं सहसा क्षिप्तः श्वसनेन महात्मना।।5.1.126।।
transliteration: sa māmupāgataḥ kruddho vajramudyamya devarāṭ| tato'haṃ sahasā kṣiptaḥ śvasanena mahātmanā
translation: सः he, देवराट् Indra, क्रुद्धः in wrath, वज्रम् thunderbolt, उद्यम्य held, माम् to me, उपागतः came, ततः then, अहम् I, महात्मना by the great self, श्वसनेन by the Windgod, सहसा at once, क्षिप्तः dropped down.
explanation: "Angry Indra held the thunderbolt and came towards me chasing. At that time the great Wind-god tossed me into the air and dropped me down at once.

shloka_text: अस्मिन्लवणतोये च प्रक्षिप्तः प्लवगोत्तम। गुप्तपक्षसमग्रश्च तव पित्राभिरक्षितः।।5.1.127।।
transliteration: asminlavaṇatoye ca prakṣiptaḥ plavagottama| guptapakṣasamagraśca tava pitrābhirakṣitaḥ
translation: प्लवगोत्तम O distinguished among the vanaras, गुप्तपक्षसमग्रश्च kept my wings intact, अस्मिन् in this, लवणतोये in the salt waters of the sea, प्रक्षिप्तः thrown down, तव पित्रा by your father, अभिरक्षितः protected.
explanation: "O distinguished vanara your father, the Windgod threw me down into this saltwater sea. Thus my wings were protected.

shloka_text: ततोऽहं मानयामि त्वां मान्यो हि मम मारुतः। त्वया मे ह्येष सम्बन्धः कपिमुख्य महागुणः।।5.1.128।।
transliteration: tato'haṃ mānayāmi tvāṃ mānyo hi mama mārutaḥ| tvayā me hyeṣa sambandhaḥ kapimukhya mahāguṇaḥ
translation: कपिमुख्य O esteemed vanara, मारुतः Windgod, मम my, मान्यः हि revered one, ततः therefore, अहम् I, त्वाम् you, मानयामि I will honour you, त्वया by you, मे to me, एषः this, सम्बन्धः relationship, महागुणः is great.
explanation: "O esteemed vanara the Windgod is revered by me and so I honour you. O chief of monkeys, my bondage with you is therefore of high value to me, indeed.

shloka_text: अस्मिन्नेवंगते कार्ये सागरस्य ममैव च। प्रीतिं प्रीतमनाः कर्तुं त्वमर्हसि महाकपे।।5.1.129।।
transliteration: asminnevaṃgate kārye sāgarasya mamaiva ca| prītiṃ prītamanāḥ kartuṃ tvamarhasi mahākape
translation: महाकपे O great monkey, अस्मिन् in this, कार्ये  work, एवंगते reached such a position, त्वम् you, प्रीतमनाः wholeheartedly, सागरस्य च and the ocean's, ममैव च and mine also, प्रीतिम् pleasure, कर्तुम् to do, अर्हसि you ought to.
explanation: "O great monkey when I hold you so high, you ought to oblige me and the (god of the) ocean wholeheartedly (and accept our hospitalty).

shloka_text: श्रमं मोक्षय पूजां च गृहाण कपिसत्तम। प्रीतिं च बहुमन्यस्व प्रीतोऽस्मि तव दर्शनात्।।5.1.130।।
transliteration: śramaṃ mokṣaya pūjāṃ ca gṛhāṇa kapisattama| prītiṃ ca bahumanyasva prīto'smi tava darśanāt
translation: कपिसत्तम O noble monkey, श्रमम् fatigue, मोक्ष्य after being relieved, पूजां  च and offerings, गृहाण accept, प्रीतिम् love, बहुमन्यस्व oblige us, तव your, दर्शनात् by your presence, प्रीतः अस्मि I am pleased.
explanation: "O noble monkey oblige us by accepting our offering given with love and be relieved of your fatigue. Your presence itself is welcome to me".

shloka_text: एवमुक्तः कपिश्रेष्ठस्तं नगोत्तममब्रवीत्। प्रीतोऽस्मि कृतमातिथ्यं मन्युरेषोऽपनीयताम्।।5.1.131।।
transliteration: evamuktaḥ kapiśreṣṭhastaṃ nagottamamabravīt| prīto'smi kṛtamātithyaṃ manyureṣo'panīyatām
translation: एवम् in that way, उक्तः having addressed, कपिश्रेष्ठः the great monkey, तं नगोत्तमम् to the lord of mountains, अब्रवीत् said, प्रीतः pleased, अस्मि I am, आतिथ्यम् hospitality, कृतम् is offered, एषः this, मन्युः unhappiness, अपनीयताम् remove.
explanation: The great Hanuman, pleased with the words of Mainaka, said "I am pleased at your hospitality. Remove your unhappiness.

shloka_text: त्वरते कार्यकालो मे अहश्चाप्यतिवर्तते। प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता न स्थातव्यमिहान्तरे।।5.1.132।।
transliteration: tvarate kāryakālo me ahaścāpyativartate| pratijñā ca mayā dattā na sthātavyamihāntare
translation: मे to me, कार्यकालः schedule, त्वरते hastens, अहः च the day also, अतिवर्तते exceeds, मया by me, प्रतिज्ञा vow, दत्ता च is made, अन्तरे in between, इह here, न स्थातव्यम् I will not halt.
explanation: "My commitment is hastening me. The day set (for the accomplishment of the task) is also drawing to a close. A vow is made and I will not halt in the middle of my work."

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा पाणिना शैलमालभ्य हरिपुङ्गवः। जगामाकाशमाविश्य वीर्यवान् प्रहसन्निव।।5.1.133।।
transliteration: ityuktvā pāṇinā śailamālabhya haripuṅgavaḥ| jagāmākāśamāviśya vīryavān prahasanniva
translation: वीर्यवान् heroic, हरिपुङ्गवः chief of monkeys, इति thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, शैलम् the mountain, पाणिना with his hand, आलभ्य gently touching, आकाशम् to the sky, आविश्य ascended, प्रहसन्निव with a smile on his face, जगाम departed.
explanation: Having said this, the mighty monkey gently touched the mountain with his hands before ascending to the sky with a smile on his face.

shloka_text: स पर्वतसमुद्राभ्यां बहुमानादवेक्षितः। पूजितश्चोपपन्नाभिराशीर्भिरनिलात्मजः।।5.1.134।।
transliteration: sa parvatasamudrābhyāṃ bahumānādavekṣitaḥ| pūjitaścopapannābhirāśīrbhiranilātmajaḥ
translation: सः he, अनिलात्मजः son of the Windgod, पर्वतसमुद्राभ्याम् by both the mountain and ocean, बहुमानात् with great respect, आवेक्षितः was adored, उपपन्नाभिः with proper ones, आशीर्भिः with blessings, पूजितः च also honoured.
explanation: The mountain and the sea honoured and adored the son of the Windgod and gave him appropriate  blessings.

shloka_text: अथोर्ध्वं दूरमुत्प्लुत्य हित्वा शैलमहार्णवौ। पितुः पन्थानमास्थाय जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे।।5.1.135।।
transliteration: athordhvaṃ dūramutplutya hitvā śailamahārṇavau| pituḥ panthānamāsthāya jagāma vimale'mbare
translation: अथ then, शैलमहार्णवौ the mountain and the ocean, हित्वा after leaving, ऊर्ध्वम् high, दूरम् long distance, उत्प्लुत्य leaping into, विमले in the clear, अम्बरे in sky, पितुः father's, पन्थानम् the path, आस्थाय after taking, जगाम went.
explanation: And thereafter leaping a long distance into the clear sky, he (Hanuman) took the path of the Windgod, his father, leaving behind the mountain and the sea.

shloka_text: भूयश्चोर्ध्वं गतिं प्राप्य गिरिं तमवलोकयन्। वायुसूनुर्निरालम्बे जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे।।5.1.136।।
transliteration: bhūyaścordhvaṃ gatiṃ prāpya giriṃ tamavalokayan| vāyusūnurnirālambe jagāma vimale'mbare
translation: वायुसूनुः son of the Windgod, भूयः च further, ऊर्ध्वम् high up, गतिम् path, प्राप्य taking, तं गिरिम् the mountain, अवलोकयन् while looking at, निरालम्बे in a place without any support, विमले pure, cloudless, अम्बरे in the sky, जगाम went.
explanation: Rising higher and further up and looking at the mountain (which was going down into the ocean), the son of the Windgod coursed through the cloudless sky unsupported.

shloka_text: तद् द्वितीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। प्रशशंसुः सुराः सर्वे सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः।।5.1.137।।
transliteration: tad dvitīyaṃ hanumato dṛṣṭvā karma suduṣkaram| praśaśaṃsuḥ surāḥ sarve siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ
translation: हनुमतः of Hanuman, तत् that, सुदुष्करम् most difficult, द्वितीयम् a second, कर्म task, दृष्ट्वा on seeing, सर्वे all, सुराः gods, सिद्धाश्च siddhas, परमर्षयः great sages, प्रशंशसुः praised him.
explanation: Gods, siddhas as well as the great sages praised him for the second great achievment of Hanuman, which is impossible for others to accomplish.

shloka_text: देवताश्चाभवन् हृष्टास्तत्रस्थास्तस्य कर्मणा। काञ्चनस्य सुनाभस्य सहस्राक्षश्च वासवः।।5.1.138।।
transliteration: devatāścābhavan hṛṣṭāstatrasthāstasya karmaṇā| kāñcanasya sunābhasya sahasrākṣaśca vāsavaḥ
translation: तत्रस्थाः those who were there, देवताश्च gods, सहस्राक्षः the thousandeyed, वासवश्च Indra, काञ्चनस्य of the golden Mainaka, तस्य his, सुनाभस्य of Sunabha, कर्मणा by the task, हृष्टाः delighted, अभवन् became.
explanation: The gods who happened to be present at that time (on the mountain) and the thousandeyed Indra were delighted by the gesture of golden Sunabha (Mainaka) mountain.

shloka_text: उवाच वचनं धीमान् परितोषात्सगद्गदम्। सुनाभं पर्वतश्रेष्ठं स्वयमेव शचीपतिः।।5.1.139।।
transliteration: uvāca vacanaṃ dhīmān paritoṣātsagadgadam| sunābhaṃ parvataśreṣṭhaṃ svayameva śacīpatiḥ
translation: धीमान् wise, शचीपतिः husband of Sachi, Indra, पर्वतश्रेष्ठम् best mountain, सुनाभम् Sunabha, परितोषात् satisfied, सगद्गदम् with throat choked, स्वयमेव himself, वचनम् these words, उवाच spoke.
explanation: Indra, the lord of Sachi, was personally satisfied and spoke to Mainaka, the best of mountains, in faltering tone, his throat choked out of joy.

shloka_text: हिरण्यनाभ शैलेन्द्र परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते भृशम्। अभयं ते प्रयच्छामि तिष्ठ सौम्य यथासुखम्।।5.1.140।।
transliteration: hiraṇyanābha śailendra parituṣṭo'smi te bhṛśam| abhayaṃ te prayacchāmi tiṣṭha saumya yathāsukham
translation: हिरण्यनाभ O Hiranyanabha, शैलेन्द्र O lord of mountains, ते with you, भृशम् a lot, परितुष्टः अस्मि I am pleased, सौम्य O pious one, ते to you, अभयम् security, प्रयच्छामि I give, यथासुखम् happily as you please, तिष्ठ you may stay on.
explanation: "O Hiranyanabha, the foremost among the mountains I am highly pleased with you. I give you security (free from fear of losing wings). O pious one you may stay on happily as you please.

shloka_text: साह्यं कृतं ते सुमहद्विक्रान्तस्य हनूमतः। क्रमतो योजनशतं निर्भयस्य भये सति।।5.1.141।।
transliteration: sāhyaṃ kṛtaṃ te sumahadvikrāntasya hanūmataḥ| kramato yojanaśataṃ nirbhayasya bhaye sati
translation: विक्रान्तस्य of one attempting to leap, योजनशतम् a hundred yojanas, क्रमतः while  leaping, भये सति when there is reason to fear, निर्भयस्य of a fearless one, हनूमतः Hanuman, ते by you, सुमहत् very valuable, साह्यम् help, कृतम् rendered.
explanation: "You have rendered very valuable help to Hanuman who was attempting to leap  a distance of a hundred yojanas. He is fearless even when there is reason to fear (of falling down).

shloka_text: रामस्यैष हितायैव याति दाशरथेर्हरिः। सत्क्रियां कुर्वता तस्य तोषितोऽस्मि दृढं त्वया।।5.1.142।।
transliteration: rāmasyaiṣa hitāyaiva yāti dāśaratherhariḥ| satkriyāṃ kurvatā tasya toṣito'smi dṛḍhaṃ tvayā
translation: एषः हरिः this vanara, दाशरथेः of the son of Dasaratha, रामस्य Rama's, पितायैव for his wellbeing only, याति  going, तस्य his, सत्क्रियाम् honour, कुर्वता for doing, त्वया by you, दृढम् surely, तोषितः अस्मि I am pleased.
explanation: "The vanara has gone on a mission to help the son of Dasaratha. I am highly pleased with the service rendered to him.

shloka_text: ततः प्रहर्षमगमद्विपुलं पर्वतोत्तमः। देवतानां पतिं दृष्ट्वा परितुष्टं शतक्रतुम्।।5.1.143।।
transliteration: tataḥ praharṣamagamadvipulaṃ parvatottamaḥ| devatānāṃ patiṃ dṛṣṭvā parituṣṭaṃ śatakratum
translation: तत: thereafter, पर्वतोत्तमः the best of mountains, देवतानाम् of gods,पतिम् lord, शतक्रतुम् who had performed a hundred yajnas, Indra, परितुष्टम् extremely happy,दृष्ट्वा after seeing, विपुलम् very much, प्रहर्षम् delight, आगमत् experienced.
explanation: Thereafter Mainaka, the great mountain was delighted to see Indra,  lord of the gods, performer of a hundred yajnas satisfied.

shloka_text: स वै दत्तवरः शैलो बभूवावस्थितस्तदा। हनुमांश्च मुहूर्तेन व्यतिचक्राम सागरम्।।5.1.144।।
transliteration: sa vai dattavaraḥ śailo babhūvāvasthitastadā| hanumāṃśca muhūrtena vyaticakrāma sāgaram
translation: तदा then, दत्तवरः who received a boon, सः he, शैलः Mainaka, अवस्थितः he became stable, बभूव became, हनुमांश्च Hanuma also, मुहूर्तेन in a short while, सागरम् ocean, व्यतिचक्राम crossed over.
explanation: Then mount Mainaka, assured by Indra became secure. And Hanuman also crossed over the ocean in a short while.

shloka_text: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। अब्रुवन् सूर्यसङ्काशां सुरसां नागमातरम्।।5.1.145।।
transliteration: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ| abruvan sūryasaṅkāśāṃ surasāṃ nāgamātaram
translation: ततः then, सगन्धर्वाः including gandharvas, देवाः gods, सिद्धाश्च and siddhas, परमर्षयः great sages, सूर्यसङ्काशाम् shining like the Sun, नागमातरम् mother of nagas, सुरसाम् Surasa, अब्रुवन् said.
explanation: Then the gods, gandharvas, siddhas and great sages approached Surasa, the mother of nagas, who was glowing like the Sungod and said:.

shloka_text: अयं वातात्मजः श्रीमान्प्लवते सागरोपरि। हनुमान्नाम तस्य त्वं मुहूर्तं विघ्नमाचर।।5.1.146।। राक्षसं रूपमास्थाय सुघोरं पर्वतोपमम्। दंष्ट्राकरालं पिङ्गाक्षं वक्त्रं कृत्वा नभः समम्।।5.1.147।।
transliteration: ayaṃ vātātmajaḥ śrīmānplavate sāgaropari| hanumānnāma tasya tvaṃ muhūrtaṃ vighnamācara rākṣasaṃ rūpamāsthāya sughoraṃ parvatopamam| daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ piṅgākṣaṃ vaktraṃ kṛtvā nabhaḥ samam
translation: हनुमन्नाम named Hanuman, श्रीमान् glorious, अयं this person, वातात्मजः son of the Windgod, सागरोपरि over the sea, प्लवते is flying, त्वम् you, सुघोरम् hideous, पर्वतोपमम् gigantic like a mountain, राक्षसम् demoniac, रूपम् form, आस्थाय assuming, दंष्ट्राकरालम् with big teeth, पिङ्गाक्षम्  yellowbrown eyes, नभः समम् like the sky, वक्त्रम् mouth, कृत्वा doing, मुहूर्तम् for a short while, तस्य him, विघ्नम् obstruction, आचर make.
explanation: "The glorious son of the Windgod, called Hanuman, is crossing the ocean. Obstruct him for sometime by assuming the hideous form of a demon, gigantic as a mountain, fearful with yellowishbrown eyes, with big teeth and a wide mouth like the sky.

shloka_text: अयं वातात्मजः श्रीमान्प्लवते सागरोपरि। हनुमान्नाम तस्य त्वं मुहूर्तं विघ्नमाचर।।5.1.146।। राक्षसं रूपमास्थाय सुघोरं पर्वतोपमम्। दंष्ट्राकरालं पिङ्गाक्षं वक्त्रं कृत्वा नभः समम्।।5.1.147।।
transliteration: ayaṃ vātātmajaḥ śrīmānplavate sāgaropari| hanumānnāma tasya tvaṃ muhūrtaṃ vighnamācara rākṣasaṃ rūpamāsthāya sughoraṃ parvatopamam| daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ piṅgākṣaṃ vaktraṃ kṛtvā nabhaḥ samam
translation: हनुमन्नाम named Hanuman, श्रीमान् glorious, अयं this person, वातात्मजः son of the Windgod, सागरोपरि over the sea, प्लवते is flying, त्वम् you, सुघोरम् hideous, पर्वतोपमम् gigantic like a mountain, राक्षसम् demoniac, रूपम् form, आस्थाय assuming, दंष्ट्राकरालम् with big teeth, पिङ्गाक्षम्  yellowbrown eyes, नभः समम् like the sky, वक्त्रम् mouth, कृत्वा doing, मुहूर्तम् for a short while, तस्य him, विघ्नम् obstruction, आचर make.
explanation: "The glorious son of the Windgod, called Hanuman, is crossing the ocean. Obstruct him for sometime by assuming the hideous form of a demon, gigantic as a mountain, fearful with yellowishbrown eyes, with big teeth and a wide mouth like the sky.

shloka_text: बलमिच्छामहे ज्ञातुं भूयश्चास्य पराक्रमम्। त्वां विजेष्यत्युपायेन विषादं वा गमिष्यति।।5.1.148।।
transliteration: balamicchāmahe jñātuṃ bhūyaścāsya parākramam| tvāṃ vijeṣyatyupāyena viṣādaṃ vā gamiṣyati
translation: अस्य his, बलम् strength, भूयः once again, पराक्रमं च and valour, उपायेन intelligence त्वाम्  you, विजेष्यति he will win, वा or else, विषादम् dejected, गमिष्यति will give way, ज्ञातुम् to know, इच्छामहे we wish.
explanation: "We want to assess his strength, valour and intelligence once again. We wish to know whether he will win or give way to despondency".

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी दैवतैरभिसत्कृता। समुद्रमध्ये सुरसा बिभ्रती राक्षसं वपुः।।5.1.149।। विकृतं च विरूपं च सर्वस्य च भयावहम्। प्लवमानं हनूमन्तमावृत्येदमुवाच ह।।5.1.150।।
transliteration: evamuktā tu sā devī daivatairabhisatkṛtā| samudramadhye surasā bibhratī rākṣasaṃ vapuḥ vikṛtaṃ ca virūpaṃ ca sarvasya ca bhayāvaham| plavamānaṃ hanūmantamāvṛtyedamuvāca ha
translation: देवी the divine being, सा सुरसा Surasa, दैवतैः by gods, एवम् that way, उक्ता having been addressed, अभिसत्कृता received their honour, समुद्र मध्ये in the midst of the ocean, विकृतम् terrific, विरूपं च ugly form, सर्वस्य for all, भयावहम् frightening, राक्षसं वपुः demoniac form, बिभ्रती  put up, प्लवमानम् leaping, हनूमन्तम् Hanuman, आवृत्य after encirding him, इदम् these words, उवाच ह said.
explanation: Thus honoured by the gods, Surasa assumed a terrific ugly form frightening to all and stood in the midst of the ocean. Putting up a distorted appearance and encompassing Hanuman who was crossing the ocean, she spoke to him:

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी दैवतैरभिसत्कृता। समुद्रमध्ये सुरसा बिभ्रती राक्षसं वपुः।।5.1.149।। विकृतं च विरूपं च सर्वस्य च भयावहम्। प्लवमानं हनूमन्तमावृत्येदमुवाच ह।।5.1.150।।
transliteration: evamuktā tu sā devī daivatairabhisatkṛtā| samudramadhye surasā bibhratī rākṣasaṃ vapuḥ vikṛtaṃ ca virūpaṃ ca sarvasya ca bhayāvaham| plavamānaṃ hanūmantamāvṛtyedamuvāca ha
translation: देवी the divine being, सा सुरसा Surasa, दैवतैः by gods, एवम् that way, उक्ता having been addressed, अभिसत्कृता received their honour, समुद्र मध्ये in the midst of the ocean, विकृतम् terrific, विरूपं च ugly form, सर्वस्य for all, भयावहम् frightening, राक्षसं वपुः demoniac form, बिभ्रती  put up, प्लवमानम् leaping, हनूमन्तम् Hanuman, आवृत्य after encirding him, इदम् these words, उवाच ह said.
explanation: Thus honoured by the gods, Surasa assumed a terrific ugly form frightening to all and stood in the midst of the ocean. Putting up a distorted appearance and encompassing Hanuman who was crossing the ocean, she spoke to him:

shloka_text: मम भक्षः प्रदिष्टस्त्वमीश्वरैर्वानरर्षभ। अहं त्वां भक्षयिष्यामि प्रविशेदं ममाननम्।।5.1.151।।
transliteration: mama bhakṣaḥ pradiṣṭastvamīśvarairvānararṣabha| ahaṃ tvāṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmi praviśedaṃ mamānanam
translation: वानरर्षभ O bull among, त्वम् you, ईश्वरैः by lords of the universe, मम to me, भक्षः food, प्रदिष्टः are provided, अहम् I, त्वाम् you, भक्षयिष्यामि I will eat you, इदम् this, मम my, आननम् mouth, प्रविश enter.
explanation: "O bull among vanaras the lords of the universe have provided you as food for me. I will eat you. Enter my mouth".

shloka_text: एवमुक्तः सुरसया प्राञ्जलिर्वानरर्षभः। प्रहृष्टवदनः श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।5.1.152।।
transliteration: evamuktaḥ surasayā prāñjalirvānararṣabhaḥ| prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ śrīmānidaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: सुरसया by Surasa,एवम् In that way, उक्तः spoken, श्रीमान् glorious, वानरर्षभः वहतत bull among vanaras, प्रहृष्टवदनः with a blooming face, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, इदं वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Thus addressed by Surasa,  the glorious Hanuman said this with a blooming face and folded hands:

shloka_text: रामो दाशरथिर्नाम प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या चापि भार्यया।।5.1.153।।
transliteration: rāmo dāśarathirnāma praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam| lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā
translation: दाशरथिः Dasaratha's son, रामो नाम called Rama, भ्रात्रा with his brother, लक्ष्मणेन सह accompanied by Lakshmana, भार्यया with his wife, वैदेह्या चापि with Vaidehi also, दण्डकावनम् Dandaka forest, प्रविष्टः entered.
explanation: "Dasaratha's son called Rama accompanied by his brother Lakshmana and his wife Vaidehi entered Dandaka forest.

shloka_text: अन्यकार्यविषक्तस्य बद्धवैरस्य राक्षसैः। तस्य सीता हृता भार्या रावणेन यशस्विनी।।5.1.154।।
transliteration: anyakāryaviṣaktasya baddhavairasya rākṣasaiḥ| tasya sītā hṛtā bhāryā rāvaṇena yaśasvinī
translation: राक्षसैः with rakshasas, बद्धवैरस्य  deeprooted enmity, तस्य his, अन्यकार्यविषक्तस्य while he was engaged in some other work, यशस्विनी a glorious lady, भार्या wife, सीता Sita, रावणेन by Ravana, हृता was abducted.
explanation: "While Rama was engaged otherwise, his glorious wife Sita was abducted by Ravana actuated by deeprooted enmity of demons with him.

shloka_text: तस्याः सकाशं दूतोऽहं गमिष्ये रामशासनात्। कर्तुमर्हसि रामस्य साह्यं विषयवासिनि।।5.1.155।।
transliteration: tasyāḥ sakāśaṃ dūto'haṃ gamiṣye rāmaśāsanāt| kartumarhasi rāmasya sāhyaṃ viṣayavāsini
translation: अहम् I, रामशासनात् by Rama's command, दूतः emissary, तस्याः her, सकाशम् for, गमिष्ये I shall go, विषयवासिनि O resident of his kingdom, रामस्य of Rama, साह्यम् help, कर्तुम् to render, अर्हसि it proper for you.
explanation: "I am going as Rama's emissary to search for his wife. It is proper for you to render help since you are a resident of his kingdom.

shloka_text: अथवा मैथिलीं दृष्ट्वा रामं चाक्लिष्टकारिणम्। आगमिष्यामि ते वक्त्रं सत्यं प्रतिशृणोमि ते।।5.1.156।।
transliteration: athavā maithilīṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ cākliṣṭakāriṇam| āgamiṣyāmi te vaktraṃ satyaṃ pratiśṛṇomi te
translation: अथवा alternatively, मैथिलीम् Mythili, अक्लिष्टकारिणम् one who may makes work easy (without any trouble), रामं च and Rama, दृष्ट्वा after seeing, ते to your, वक्त्रम् mouth, आगमिष्यामि I will reach, सत्यम् truly, ते you, प्रतिशृणोमि I promise.
explanation: Or else, after seeing Maithili and the ever-untroubled Rama, I shall return into your mouth—this I truly promise you.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता हनुमता सुरसा कामरूपिणी। अब्रवीन्नातिवर्तेन्मां कश्चिदेष वरो मम।।5.1.157।।
transliteration: evamuktā hanumatā surasā kāmarūpiṇī| abravīnnātivartenmāṃ kaścideṣa varo mama
translation: हनुमता by Hanuman, एवम् in that way, उक्ता having been spoken, कामरूपिणी one who can assume any form at free will, सुरसा Surasa, अब्रवीत् said, कश्चित् no one, नातिवर्तेत cannot cross, एषः such, मम to me, वरः boon.
explanation: Having heard Hanuman, Surasa capable of taking any form at her free will told him that no one can cross (her region) as she had been given such a boon(by the Creator)৷৷

shloka_text: तं प्रयान्तं समुद्वीक्ष्य सुरसा वाक्यमब्रवीत्। बलं जिज्ञासमाना वै नागमाता हनूमतः।।5.1.158।।
transliteration: taṃ prayāntaṃ samudvīkṣya surasā vākyamabravīt| balaṃ jijñāsamānā vai nāgamātā hanūmataḥ
translation: नागमाता mother of serpents, सुरसा Surasa, हनूमतः of Hanuman, बलम् strength, जिज्ञासमाना वै desirous of knowing, प्रयान्तम् who was attempting to go away, तम् her, समुद्वीक्ष्य observing, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Surasa, mother of serpents, observing that Hanuman was attempting to escape, said this in order to gauge his strength:

shloka_text: प्रविश्य वदनं मेऽद्य गन्तव्यं वानरोत्तम। वर एष पुरा दत्तो मम धात्रेति सत्वरा।।5.1.159।। व्यादाय विपुलं वक्त्रं स्थिता सा मारुतेः पुरः।
transliteration: praviśya vadanaṃ me'dya gantavyaṃ vānarottama| vara eṣa purā datto mama dhātreti satvarā vyādāya vipulaṃ vaktraṃ sthitā sā māruteḥ puraḥ|
translation: वानरोत्तम O best of the vanaras, अद्य today, मे my, वदनम् face (mouth), प्रविश्य after entering, गन्तव्यम् you may go, एषः वरः such a boon, पुरा past, मम to me, धात्रा by Brahma, दत्तः is given, इति thus, सत्वरा quickly, विपुलम् wide, वक्त्रम् mouth, व्यादाय opened, सा she, मारुतेः vanara's, पुरः front, स्थिता stood.
explanation: "O best vanara you must pass through my mouth today. Such is the boon granted to me by Brahma in the past". Then she quickly opened her big mouth and stood.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तः सुरसया क्रुद्धो वानरपुङ्गवः।।5.1.160।। अब्रवीत्कुरु वै वक्त्रं येन मां विषहिष्यसे।
transliteration: evamuktaḥ surasayā kruddho vānarapuṅgavaḥ abravītkuru vai vaktraṃ yena māṃ viṣahiṣyase|
translation: सुरसया by Surasa, एवम् in that way, उक्तः having been spoken to, वानरपुङ्गवः supreme vanara, क्रुद्धः got angry, अब्रवीत् he said, वक्त्रम् mouth, कुरु वै open, येन in such a way, माम् me, विषहिष्यसे you can bear me.
explanation: Thus addressed by Surasa, Hanuman the supreme vanara said, "Open your mouth wide enough to hold me."

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा सुरसां क्रुद्धो धशयोजनमायता।।5.1.161।। दशयोजनविस्तारो बभूव हनुमांस्तदा।
transliteration: ityuktvā surasāṃ kruddho dhaśayojanamāyatā daśayojanavistāro babhūva hanumāṃstadā|
translation: तदा then, हनुमान् Hanuman, सुरसां Surasa, इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, क्रुद्धः angry, दशयोजनम् ten yojanas, आयतां wide, दशयोजनविस्तारः ten yojanas in breadth, बभूव became.
explanation: Provoked by the words of Surasa, Hanuman stretched himself to ten yojanas.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा मेघसङ्काशं दशयोजनमायतम्।।5.1.162।। चकार सुरसा चास्यं विंशद्योजनमायतम्।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā meghasaṅkāśaṃ daśayojanamāyatam cakāra surasā cāsyaṃ viṃśadyojanamāyatam|
translation: दशयोजनम् ten yojanas, आयतम् wide, मेघसङ्काशम् like a cloud, तम् him, दृष्ट्वा after seeing, सुरसा च Surasa too, आस्यम् her mouth, विंशद्योजनम् twenty yojanas, आयतम् wide, चकार stretched.
explanation: Seeing his body stretched to ten yojanas like a cloud, Surasa also widened her mouth to twenty yojanas.

shloka_text: हनुमांस्तु ततः क्रुद्धस्त्रिंशद्योजनमायतः।।5.1.163।। चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं चत्वारिंशत्तथोच्छ्रितम्। बभूव हनुमावनीरः पञ्चाशद्योजनोच्छ्रितः।।5.1.164।।
transliteration: hanumāṃstu tataḥ kruddhastriṃśadyojanamāyataḥ cakāra surasā vaktraṃ catvāriṃśattathocchritam| babhūva hanumāvanīraḥ pañcāśadyojanocchritaḥ
translation: ततः then, हनुमांस्तु Hanuman also, क्रुद्धः in anger, त्रिंशद्योजनम् thirty yojanas, आयतः wide, सुरसा Surasa, तथा like that, वक्त्रम् mouth, चत्वारिंशम् forty yojanas, उच्छ्रितम् high, चकार did, वीरः hero, हनुमान् Hanuman, पञ्चाशद्योजनोच्छ्रितः fifty yojanas high, बभूव became.
explanation: Provoked, Hanuman further stretched his body to thirty yojanas and Surasa on her own enlarged her mouth to forty yojanas. Then the great hero Hanuman stretched his body to fifty yojanas.

shloka_text: हनुमांस्तु ततः क्रुद्धस्त्रिंशद्योजनमायतः।।5.1.163।। चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं चत्वारिंशत्तथोच्छ्रितम्। बभूव हनुमावनीरः पञ्चाशद्योजनोच्छ्रितः।।5.1.164।।
transliteration: hanumāṃstu tataḥ kruddhastriṃśadyojanamāyataḥ cakāra surasā vaktraṃ catvāriṃśattathocchritam| babhūva hanumāvanīraḥ pañcāśadyojanocchritaḥ
translation: ततः then, हनुमांस्तु Hanuman also, क्रुद्धः in anger, त्रिंशद्योजनम् thirty yojanas, आयतः wide, सुरसा Surasa, तथा like that, वक्त्रम् mouth, चत्वारिंशम् forty yojanas, उच्छ्रितम् high, चकार did, वीरः hero, हनुमान् Hanuman, पञ्चाशद्योजनोच्छ्रितः fifty yojanas high, बभूव became.
explanation: Provoked, Hanuman further stretched his body to thirty yojanas and Surasa on her own enlarged her mouth to forty yojanas. Then the great hero Hanuman stretched his body to fifty yojanas.

shloka_text: चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं षष्टियोजनमायतम्। तथैव हनुमावनीरः सप्ततीयोजनोच्छ्रितः।।5.1.165।।
transliteration: cakāra surasā vaktraṃ ṣaṣṭiyojanamāyatam| tathaiva hanumāvanīraḥ saptatīyojanocchritaḥ
translation: सुरसा Surasa, वक्त्रम् mouth, षष्टियोजनम् sixty yojanas, आयतम् wide, चकार did, वीरः heroic, हनुमान् Hanuman, तथैव in the same way, सप्ततीयोजनोच्छ्रितः increased to seventy yojanas.
explanation: Surasa widened her mouth sixty yojanas and then the heroic Hanuman enlarged himself to seventy yojanas.

shloka_text: चकार सुरसा वक्त्रमशीतीयोजनायतम्। हनुमानचलप्रख्यो नवतीयोजनोच्छ्रितः।।5.1.166।।
transliteration: cakāra surasā vaktramaśītīyojanāyatam| hanumānacalaprakhyo navatīyojanocchritaḥ
translation: सुरसा Surasa, वक्त्रम् mouth, अशीतीयोजनायतम् eighty yojanas wide, चकार  made, अचलप्रख्यः like a mountain, हनुमान् Hanuman, नवतीयोजनोच्छ्रितः ninety yojanas.
explanation: Surasa widened her mouth to eighy yojanas and the heroic Hanuman grew up to ninety yojanas, looking like a mountain.

shloka_text: चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं शतयोजनमायतम् तव सानुषु विश्रान्तः शेषं प्रक्रमतामिति। तद्दृष्ट्वा व्यादितं त्वास्यं वायुपुत्रः सुबुद्धिमान्। दीर्घजिह्वं सुरसया सुघोरं नरकोपमम्।।5.1.167।। सुसंक्षिप्यात्मनः कायं बभूवाङ्गुष्ठमात्रकः।
transliteration: cakāra surasā vaktraṃ śatayojanamāyatam tava sānuṣu viśrāntaḥ śeṣaṃ prakramatāmiti| taddṛṣṭvā vyāditaṃ tvāsyaṃ vāyuputraḥ subuddhimān| dīrghajihvaṃ surasayā sughoraṃ narakopamam susaṃkṣipyātmanaḥ kāyaṃ babhūvāṅguṣṭhamātrakaḥ|
translation: सुबुद्धिमान् very intelligent, वायुपुत्रः Hanuman, सुरसया by Surasa, व्यादितम् opened, दीर्घजिह्वम् long tongued, सुघोरम् dreadful, नरकोपमम् like hell, तत् आस्यम् that mouth, दृष्ट्वा on seeing, आत्मनः his, कायम् body, सुसंक्षिप्य shrunk, अङ्गुष्ठमात्रकः of the size of a thumb, बभूव became.
explanation: Intelligent Hanuman observing Surasa's enlarged mouth open and dreadful like hell with a long tongue, suddenly shrunk his body to the size of a thumb.

shloka_text: सोऽभिपत्याशु तद्वक्त्रं निष्पत्य च महाबलः। अन्तरिक्षे स्थितः श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।5.1.168।।
transliteration: so'bhipatyāśu tadvaktraṃ niṣpatya ca mahābalaḥ| antarikṣe sthitaḥ śrīmānidaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: श्रीमान् glorious one, महाबलः mighty, सः he, आशु immediatly, तद्वक्त्रम् her mouth, अभिपत्य got in, निष्पत्य च and got out, अन्तरिक्षे in the sky, स्थितः stood, इदम् this, वचनम् word, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Glorious and mighty  Hanuman quickly went into her mouth and got out and stood in the sky and said:.

shloka_text: प्रविष्टोऽस्मि हि ते वक्त्रं दाक्षायणि नमोऽस्तु ते। गमिष्ये यत्र वैदेही सत्यं चासीद्वरस्तव।।5.1.169।।
transliteration: praviṣṭo'smi hi te vaktraṃ dākṣāyaṇi namo'stu te| gamiṣye yatra vaidehī satyaṃ cāsīdvarastava
translation: दाक्षायणि O dughter of Daksha, ते your, वक्त्रम् mouth, प्रविष्टः I have entered, अस्मि हि I am indeed, ते to you, नमः salutations, अस्तु may be, वैदेही Vaidhehi, यत्र wherever, गमिष्ये I will go, तव your, वरः च boon also, सत्यम् true, आसीत् was.
explanation: "O Dakshayani I have indeed entered your mouth and your boon has come true (as nobody can go against the boon of the Creator). Allow me to proceed in quest of Vaidhehi. My salutations to you."

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा वदनान्मुक्तं चन्द्रं राहुमुखादिव। अब्रवीत्सुरसा देवी स्वेन रूपेण वानरम्।।5.1.170।।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vadanānmuktaṃ candraṃ rāhumukhādiva| abravītsurasā devī svena rūpeṇa vānaram
translation: राहुमुखात् from the mouth of Rahu, चन्द्रमिव like the Moon, वदनात् from the mouth, मुक्तम् released, तं him, वानरम् that vanara, दृष्ट्वा seeing, सुरसा देवी the divine Surasa, स्वेन in her true, रूपेण form, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Seeing Hanuman released out of her mouth like the Moon released from the mouth of Rahu, Surasa assumed her true form and said:

shloka_text: अर्थसिद्ध्यै हरिश्रेष्ठ गच्छ सौम्य यथासुखम्। समानयस्व वैदेहीं राघवेण महात्मना।।5.1.171।।
transliteration: arthasiddhyai hariśreṣṭha gaccha saumya yathāsukham| samānayasva vaidehīṃ rāghaveṇa mahātmanā
translation: सौम्य O noble one, हरिश्रेष्ठ O best of vanaras, अर्थसिद्ध्यै for achieving your purpose, यथासुखम् with pleasure, गच्छ proceed, वैदेहीम् Vaidehi, महात्मना with the great self, राघवेण with Raghava, समानयस्व unite.
explanation: "O noble vanara proceed happily to achieve your purpose. Go and unite Vaidehi with the noble self, Raghava.

shloka_text: तत्तृतीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। साधु साध्विति भूतानि प्रशशंसुस्तदा हरिम्।।5.1.172।।
transliteration: tattṛtīyaṃ hanumato dṛṣṭvā karma suduṣkaram| sādhu sādhviti bhūtāni praśaśaṃsustadā harim
translation: सुदुष्करम् very difficult, हनुमतः of Hanuman, तत् that, तृतीयं कर्म a third feat, दृष्ट्वा after witnessing, तदा then, भूतानि  living beings, साधु साधु इति welldone, welldone this, हरिम् vanara, प्रशशंसुः applauded.
explanation: Witnessing Hanuman achieving a very difficult feat for the third time, all the living beings applauded him saying "Well done, welldone".

shloka_text: स सागरमनाधृष्यमभ्येत्य वरुणालयम्। जगामाकाशमाविश्य वेगेन गरुडोपमः।।5.1.173।।
transliteration: sa sāgaramanādhṛṣyamabhyetya varuṇālayam| jagāmākāśamāviśya vegena garuḍopamaḥ
translation: वेगेन speedily, गरुडोपमः like Garuda, सः he, अनाधृष्यम् invincible, वरुणालयम् abode of varuna, सागरम् ocean, अभ्येत्य piercing through, आकाशम् sky, आविश्य coursing, जगाम went.
explanation: Rising above the invincible ocean, the abode of lord Varuna, Hanuman coursed through the sky speedily like Garuda.

shloka_text: सेविते वारिधाराभिः पतगैश्च निषेविते। चरिते कैशिकाचार्यैरैरावतनिषेविते।।5.1.174।। सिंहकुञ्जरशार्दूलपतगोरगवाहनैः। विमानैः सम्पतद्भिश्च विमलैः समलङ्कृते।।5.1.175।। वज्राशनिसमाघातैः पावकैरुपशोभिते। कृतपुण्यैर्महाभागैः स्वर्गजिद्भिरलङ्कृते।।5.1.176।। वहता हव्यमत्यर्धं सेविते चित्रभानुना। ग्रहनक्षत्रचन्द्रार्कतारागण विभूषिते।।5.1.177।। महर्षिगणगन्धर्वनागयक्षसमाकुले। विविक्ते विमले विश्वे विश्वावसुनिषेविते।।5.1.178।। देवराजगजाक्रान्ते चन्द्रसूर्यपथे शिवे। विताने जीवलोकस्य वितते ब्रह्मनिर्मिते।।5.1.179।। बहुशः सेविते वीरैर्विद्याधरगणैर्वरैः। जगाम वायुमार्गे तु गरुत्मानिव मारुतिः।।5.1.180।।
