shloka_text: सहस्रं वाहिनीस्तत्र जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृताः।।5.6.34।। हेमजालपरिच्छन्नास्तरुणादित्यसन्निभाः। ददर्श राक्षसेन्द्रस्य रावणस्य निवेशने।।5.6.35।।
transliteration: sahasraṃ vāhinīstatra jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtāḥ hemajālaparicchannāstaruṇādityasannibhāḥ| dadarśa rākṣasendrasya rāvaṇasya niveśane
translation: तत्र there, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य demon king's, रावणस्य Ravana's, निवेशने in the residence, जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृताः bedecked with the gold, हेमजालपरिच्छन्नाः  protected by the rays emerging from, तरुणादित्यसन्निभाः like the rising Sun, सहस्रम् thousands, वाहिनीः troops, ददर्श saw
explanation: He saw in the palace of Ravana, the demon king, thousands of troops adorned with gold, fully protected with armour of gold shining like the morning Sun.

shloka_text: सहस्रं वाहिनीस्तत्र जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृताः।।5.6.34।। हेमजालपरिच्छन्नास्तरुणादित्यसन्निभाः। ददर्श राक्षसेन्द्रस्य रावणस्य निवेशने।।5.6.35।।
transliteration: sahasraṃ vāhinīstatra jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtāḥ hemajālaparicchannāstaruṇādityasannibhāḥ| dadarśa rākṣasendrasya rāvaṇasya niveśane
translation: तत्र there, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य demon king's, रावणस्य Ravana's, निवेशने in the residence, जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृताः bedecked with the gold, हेमजालपरिच्छन्नाः  protected by the rays emerging from, तरुणादित्यसन्निभाः like the rising Sun, सहस्रम् thousands, वाहिनीः troops, ददर्श saw
explanation: He saw in the palace of Ravana, the demon king, thousands of troops adorned with gold, fully protected with armour of gold shining like the morning Sun.

shloka_text: शिबिका विविधाकाराः स कपिर्मारुतात्मजः। लतागृहाणि चित्राणि चित्रशालागृहाणि च।।5.6.36।। क्रीडागृहाणि चान्यानि दारुपर्वतकानपि। कामस्य गृहकं रम्यं दिवागृहकमेव च।।5.6.37।। ददर्श राक्षसेन्द्रस्य रावणस्य निवेशने।
transliteration: śibikā vividhākārāḥ sa kapirmārutātmajaḥ| latāgṛhāṇi citrāṇi citraśālāgṛhāṇi ca krīḍāgṛhāṇi cānyāni dāruparvatakānapi| kāmasya gṛhakaṃ ramyaṃ divāgṛhakameva ca dadarśa rākṣasendrasya rāvaṇasya niveśane|
translation: मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, सः कपिः that monkey (Hanuman), राक्षसेन्द्रस्य of the lord of demons, रावणस्य Ravana's, निवेशने in the dwelling, विविधाकाराः of several foms, शिबिकाः palanquins, चित्राणि colourful, लतागृहाणि bowers, चित्रशालागृहाणि homes with picture galleries, अन्यानि and other, क्रीडागृहाणि sporting homes, दारुपर्वतकानपि hillocks made of wood, कामस्य for lovemaking (romance), गृहकम् home, रम्यम् delighting, दिवागृहकमेव च for daytime activities, ददर्श saw
explanation: The son of the Windgod saw at the palace of Ravana, the lord of demons, colourful palanquins of several kinds, bowers, picture galleries, spots for sporting, hillocks (artificial) made of wood, apartments for romance, for pleasures and day time activities.

shloka_text: शिबिका विविधाकाराः स कपिर्मारुतात्मजः। लतागृहाणि चित्राणि चित्रशालागृहाणि च।।5.6.36।। क्रीडागृहाणि चान्यानि दारुपर्वतकानपि। कामस्य गृहकं रम्यं दिवागृहकमेव च।।5.6.37।। ददर्श राक्षसेन्द्रस्य रावणस्य निवेशने।
transliteration: śibikā vividhākārāḥ sa kapirmārutātmajaḥ| latāgṛhāṇi citrāṇi citraśālāgṛhāṇi ca krīḍāgṛhāṇi cānyāni dāruparvatakānapi| kāmasya gṛhakaṃ ramyaṃ divāgṛhakameva ca dadarśa rākṣasendrasya rāvaṇasya niveśane|
translation: मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, सः कपिः that monkey (Hanuman), राक्षसेन्द्रस्य of the lord of demons, रावणस्य Ravana's, निवेशने in the dwelling, विविधाकाराः of several foms, शिबिकाः palanquins, चित्राणि colourful, लतागृहाणि bowers, चित्रशालागृहाणि homes with picture galleries, अन्यानि and other, क्रीडागृहाणि sporting homes, दारुपर्वतकानपि hillocks made of wood, कामस्य for lovemaking (romance), गृहकम् home, रम्यम् delighting, दिवागृहकमेव च for daytime activities, ददर्श saw
explanation: The son of the Windgod saw at the palace of Ravana, the lord of demons, colourful palanquins of several kinds, bowers, picture galleries, spots for sporting, hillocks (artificial) made of wood, apartments for romance, for pleasures and day time activities.

shloka_text: स मन्दरगिरिप्रख्यं मयूरस्थानसङ्कुलम्।।5.6.38।। ध्वजयष्टिभिराकीर्णं ददर्श भवनोत्तमम्। अनेकरत्नसङ्कीर्णं निधिजालं समन्ततः।।5.6.39।। धीरनिष्ठितकर्मान्तं गृहं भूतपतेरिव।
transliteration: sa mandaragiriprakhyaṃ mayūrasthānasaṅkulam dhvajayaṣṭibhirākīrṇaṃ dadarśa bhavanottamam| anekaratnasaṅkīrṇaṃ nidhijālaṃ samantataḥ dhīraniṣṭhitakarmāntaṃ gṛhaṃ bhūtapateriva|
translation: सः he, मन्दरगिरिप्रख्यम् comaparable to mount Mandara, मयूरस्थानसङ्कुलम् places crowded with peacocks, ध्वजयष्टिभिः with flag staffs fixed, आकीर्णम् filled with, धीरनिष्ठितकर्मान्तम् built by skilled craftsmen with great care, भूतपतेः of Siva, the lord of all creatures, गृहमिव like home, भवनोत्तमम् magnificent mansion, समन्ततः every where, अनेकरत्नसङ्कीर्णम् full of gems, निधिजालम् treasure troves, ददर्श saw
explanation: Comparable to mount Mandara, it was crowded with peacocks, set with flag staffs fixed all over, magnificent mansions built by skilled craftsmen with great efforts, decked with gems of several kinds, rich with treasures comparable to Kailasa, the home of Siva, the Lord of all beings.

shloka_text: स मन्दरगिरिप्रख्यं मयूरस्थानसङ्कुलम्।।5.6.38।। ध्वजयष्टिभिराकीर्णं ददर्श भवनोत्तमम्। अनेकरत्नसङ्कीर्णं निधिजालं समन्ततः।।5.6.39।। धीरनिष्ठितकर्मान्तं गृहं भूतपतेरिव।
transliteration: sa mandaragiriprakhyaṃ mayūrasthānasaṅkulam dhvajayaṣṭibhirākīrṇaṃ dadarśa bhavanottamam| anekaratnasaṅkīrṇaṃ nidhijālaṃ samantataḥ dhīraniṣṭhitakarmāntaṃ gṛhaṃ bhūtapateriva|
translation: सः he, मन्दरगिरिप्रख्यम् comaparable to mount Mandara, मयूरस्थानसङ्कुलम् places crowded with peacocks, ध्वजयष्टिभिः with flag staffs fixed, आकीर्णम् filled with, धीरनिष्ठितकर्मान्तम् built by skilled craftsmen with great care, भूतपतेः of Siva, the lord of all creatures, गृहमिव like home, भवनोत्तमम् magnificent mansion, समन्ततः every where, अनेकरत्नसङ्कीर्णम् full of gems, निधिजालम् treasure troves, ददर्श saw
explanation: Comparable to mount Mandara, it was crowded with peacocks, set with flag staffs fixed all over, magnificent mansions built by skilled craftsmen with great efforts, decked with gems of several kinds, rich with treasures comparable to Kailasa, the home of Siva, the Lord of all beings.

shloka_text: अर्चिर्भिश्चापि रत्नानां तेजसा रावणस्य च।।5.6.40।। विरराजाथ तद्वेश्म रश्मिमानिव रश्मिभिः।
transliteration: arcirbhiścāpi ratnānāṃ tejasā rāvaṇasya ca virarājātha tadveśma raśmimāniva raśmibhiḥ|
translation: तत् that, वेश्म place, रत्नानाम् of the gems, अर्चिर्भिश्चापि by the wonderful hues of gems, रावणस्य Ravana's, तेजसा च and with brightness, अथ there, रश्मिभिः with rays, रश्मिमानिव like the brightness of Sunrays, विरराज shone
explanation: The palace of Ravana looked splendid with gems of different hues and with Ravana's presence, it was shining like the radiant Sungod.

shloka_text: जाम्बूनदमयान्येन शयनान्यासनानि च।।5.6.41।। भाजनानि च मुख्यानि ददर्श हरियूथपः।
transliteration: jāmbūnadamayānyena śayanānyāsanāni ca bhājanāni ca mukhyāni dadarśa hariyūthapaḥ|
translation: हरियूथपः vanara leader, जाम्बूनदमयान्येव made of Jambunada gold, शयनानि beds, आसनानि च seats, मुख्यानि chief, भाजनानि vessels, ददर्श saw
explanation: The leader of the vanaras saw there beds, seats and main vessels made of gold.

shloka_text: मध्वासवकृतक्लेदं मणिभाजनसङ्कुलम्।।5.6.42।। मनोरममसंबाधं कुबेरभवनं यथा। नूपुराणां च घोषेण काञ्चीनां निनदेन च।।5.6.43।। मृदङ्तलघोषैश्च घोषवद्भिर्विनादितम्। प्रासादसङ्घातयुतं स्त्रीरत्नशतसङ्कुलम्।।5.6.44। सुव्यूढकक्ष्यं हनुमान् प्रविवेश महागृहाम्।
transliteration: madhvāsavakṛtakledaṃ maṇibhājanasaṅkulam manoramamasaṃbādhaṃ kuberabhavanaṃ yathā| nūpurāṇāṃ ca ghoṣeṇa kāñcīnāṃ ninadena ca mṛdaṅtalaghoṣaiśca ghoṣavadbhirvināditam| prāsādasaṅghātayutaṃ strīratnaśatasaṅkulam||5.6.44| suvyūḍhakakṣyaṃ hanumān praviveśa mahāgṛhām|
translation: ध्वासवकृतक्लेदम् drenched with liqour and other drinks, मणिभाजनसङ्कुलम् with gemencrusted vessels scattered all over, मनोरमम् very delightful, असम्बाधम् spacious, कुबेरभवनं यथा like the mansion of Kubera, नूपुराणाम् of anklets, घोषेण by the sound, काञ्चीनाम् of girdles, निनदेन with the sounds, घोषवद्भि:  filled with sounds of, मृदङ्गतल घोषैश्च with the sounds of drums, विनादितम् resonating, प्रासादसङ्घातयुतम् with rows of mansions, स्त्रीरत्नशतसङ्कुलम् filled with hundreds of exquisite women, सुव्यूढकक्ष्यम् with welllaid apartments, महागृहम् lofty palace, हनुमान् Hanuman, प्रविवेश entered
explanation: Hanuman entered the delightful, lofty palace comparable to Kubera's mansion. It was filled with vessels encrusted with gems scattered all over. The floor was drenched with liquor. It was resonating with sounds of golden anklets of women and of drums. The rows of mansions, lofty palaces with welllaid apartments were full of hundreds of exquisite women. इत्यार्षे वाल्मीकीये श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे षष्ठस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: स वेश्मजालं बलवान् ददर्श व्यासक्तवैडूर्यसुवर्णजालम्। यथा महत् प्रावृषि मेघजालं विद्युत्पिनद्धं सविहङ्गजालम्।।5.7.1।।
transliteration: sa veśmajālaṃ balavān dadarśa vyāsaktavaiḍūryasuvarṇajālam| yathā mahat prāvṛṣi meghajālaṃ vidyutpinaddhaṃ savihaṅgajālam
translation: बलवान् powerful, सः he, व्यासक्तवैडूर्यसुवर्णजालम् fitted with golden lattices encrusted with vaidurya, प्रावृषि in the rainy season, विद्युत्पिनद्धम् with streaks of lightning, सविहङ्गजालम् with flocks of birds, महत् great, मेघजालं यथा like the abode of clouds, वेश्मजालम्  conglomeration of houses, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Powerful Hanuman beheld the conglomeration of buildings with golden lattices encrusted with vaidurya, with flocks of birds comparable to a complex of clouds pierced by lightning during rainy season.
comments: Description of the aerial car -- Pushpaka.

shloka_text: निवेशनानां विविधाश्च शालाः प्रधानशङ्खायुधचापशालाः। मनोहराश्चापि पुनर्विशालाः ददर्श वेश्माद्रिषु चन्द्रशालाः।।5.7.2।।
transliteration: niveśanānāṃ vividhāśca śālāḥ pradhānaśaṅkhāyudhacāpaśālāḥ| manoharāścāpi punarviśālāḥ dadarśa veśmādriṣu candraśālāḥ
translation: निवेशनानाम् of the houses, विविधाः several, शालाः halls, प्रधानशङ्खायुधचापशालाः for storing valuable conches, weapons and bows, पुनः again, वेश्माद्रिषु on top of attics on the houses, मनोहराः delightful, विशालाः spacious, चन्द्रशालाः terraces, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Attached to the spacious halls of the houses, were storehouses for valuable  conches, weapons, bows and arrows. On the top of the attics on these mansions, were large and delightful terraces open to the Moon.

shloka_text: गृहाणि नानावसुराजितानि देवासुरैश्चापि सुपूजितानि। सर्वैश्च दोषैः परिवर्जितानि कपिर्ददर्श स्वबलार्जितानि।।5.7.3।।
transliteration: gṛhāṇi nānāvasurājitāni devāsuraiścāpi supūjitāni| sarvaiśca doṣaiḥ parivarjitāni kapirdadarśa svabalārjitāni
translation: कपिः monkey, नानावसुराजितानि various kinds treasures, देवासुरैश्चापि even by gods and demons, सुपूजितानि worshipped by, सर्वैः by all, दोषैः defects, परिवर्जितानि devoid, स्वबलार्जितानि earned by his might, गृहाणि houses, ददर्श saw.
explanation: The monkey saw numerous kinds of treasures, cherished by gods and demons, which were won by Ravana's might.

shloka_text: तानि प्रयत्नाभिसमाहितानि मयेन साक्षादिव निर्मितानि। महीतले सर्वगुणोत्तराणि ददर्श लङ्काधिपतेर्गृहाणि।।5.7.4।।
transliteration: tāni prayatnābhisamāhitāni mayena sākṣādiva nirmitāni| mahītale sarvaguṇottarāṇi dadarśa laṅkādhipatergṛhāṇi
translation: तानि those, प्रयत्नाभिसमाहितानि collected with great care and effort, साक्षात् directly, मयेन by Maya, निर्मितानीव as though built, महीतले on earth, सर्वगुणोत्तराणि of excellent quality, लङ्काधिपतेः of the lord of Lanka, गृहाणि mansions, ददर्श saw.
explanation: The mansions of the lord of Lanka built with great care and  effort on earth were  by all means excellent  and appeared as though built personally by Maya (the divine architect wellknown for magical skills).

shloka_text: ततो ददर्शोछ्रचितमेघरूपं मनोहरं काञ्चनचारुरूपम्। रक्षोऽधिपस्यात्मबलानुरूपं गृहोत्तमं ह्यप्रतिरूपरूपम्।।5.7.5।।
transliteration: tato dadarśochracitamegharūpaṃ manoharaṃ kāñcanacārurūpam| rakṣo'dhipasyātmabalānurūpaṃ gṛhottamaṃ hyapratirūparūpam
translation: ततः then, उछ्रचितमेघरूपम् appearing like a towering cloud, मनोहरम् soulcaptivating, काञ्चनचारुरूपम् golden palace possessing splendour of molten gold, अप्रतिरूपरूपम् matchless, आत्मबलानुरूपम् worthy of the might of Ravana, रक्षोधिपस्य of the lord of demons, गृहोत्तमम् magnificent palace, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Hanuman beheld the magnificent and soulcaptivating palace possessing the splendour of molten gold. Of matchless beauty, it looked like a towering cloud worthy of the might of Ravana, the lord of ogresses.

shloka_text: महीतले स्वर्गमिव प्रकीर्णं श्रिया ज्वलन्तं बहुरत्नकीर्णम्। नानातरूणां कुसुमावकीर्णं गिरेरिवाग्रं रजसावकीर्णम्।।5.7.6।।
transliteration: mahītale svargamiva prakīrṇaṃ śriyā jvalantaṃ bahuratnakīrṇam| nānātarūṇāṃ kusumāvakīrṇaṃ girerivāgraṃ rajasāvakīrṇam
translation: महीतले on earth, प्रकीर्णम् scattered, स्वर्गमिव like heaven, श्रिया with splendour, ज्वलन्तम् while glittering, बहुरत्नकीर्णम् with many gems, नानातरूणाम् of all kinds of trees, कुसुमावकीर्णम् scattered with flowers, रजसा with dust, अवकीर्णम् covered, गिरेः mountain, अग्रमिव like the peak.
explanation: It appeared splendid like a scattered piece of heaven on earth, glittering with countless gems. It looked like a mountain peak covered with pollen of flowers dropped from all kinds of trees.

shloka_text: नारीप्रवेकैरिव दीप्यमानं तटिद्भिरम्भोदवदर्च्यमानम्। हंसप्रवेकैरिव वाह्यमानं श्रिया युतं खे सुकृतां विमानम्।।5.7.7।।
transliteration: nārīpravekairiva dīpyamānaṃ taṭidbhirambhodavadarcyamānam| haṃsapravekairiva vāhyamānaṃ śriyā yutaṃ khe sukṛtāṃ vimānam
translation: नारीप्रवेकैः by resplendent women,दीप्यमानमिव as if lit up,तटिद्भिः with lightning, अम्भोदवत् like a raincloud, अर्च्यमानम् worshipped, हंसप्रवेकैः borne by swans, वाह्यमानम् इव as if being drawn by, श्रिया auspicious, युतम् endowed, खे in the sky, सुकृताम् royal, विमानम् aerial chariot.
explanation: The aerial chariot was lit up by resplendent women just as a raincloud dazzles with flashes of lightning. It was auspicious, worthy of worship. It looked as if it was drawn by royal swans in the sky.

shloka_text: यथा नगाग्रं बहुधातुचित्रं यथा नभश्च ग्रहचन्द्रचित्रम्। ददर्शयुक्तीकृतमेघचित्रं विमानरत्नं बहुरत्नचित्रम्।।5.7.8।।
transliteration: yathā nagāgraṃ bahudhātucitraṃ yathā nabhaśca grahacandracitram| dadarśayuktīkṛtameghacitraṃ vimānaratnaṃ bahuratnacitram
translation: युक्तीकृतमेघचित्रम् mass of colourful clouds, ग्रहचन्द्रचित्रम् looking colourful with planets and Moon, नभः यथा like the sky, बहुरत्नचित्रम् colourful on account of gems encrusted, बहुधातुचित्रम् colourful on account of many minerals, नगाग्रं यथा like the peak of a mountain, विमानरत्नम् jewel of a chariot, ददर्श saw.
explanation: A jewel among aerial chariots, it looked colourful with many gems beset. It appeared like the summit of a mountain decorated with the colours of minerals, like the sky bespangled with planets and the Moon and like a mass of multicoloured clouds adorned by a rainbow.

shloka_text: मही कृता पर्वतराजिपूर्णा शैलाः कृता वृक्षवितानपूर्णाः। वृक्षाः कृताः पुष्पवितानपूर्णाः पुष्पं कृतं केसरपत्रपूर्णम्।।5.7.9।।
transliteration: mahī kṛtā parvatarājipūrṇā śailāḥ kṛtā vṛkṣavitānapūrṇāḥ| vṛkṣāḥ kṛtāḥ puṣpavitānapūrṇāḥ puṣpaṃ kṛtaṃ kesarapatrapūrṇam
translation: मही earth, पर्वतराजिपूर्णा filled with mountain ranges, कृता drawn, शैलाः mountains, वृक्षवितानपूर्णाः filled with a canopy of trees, कृताः drawn, वृक्षाः trees, पुष्पवितानपूर्णाः filled with a canopy of flowers, कृताः drawn on it, पुष्पम् flowers, केसरपत्रपूर्णम् filled with petals and filaments, कृतम् drawn.
explanation: The whole  earth had been picturised on it. It was filled with rows of mountains  and a canopy of trees all over. The trees were filled with lovely flowers with petals and filaments drawn on them.

shloka_text: कृतानि वेश्मानि च पाण्डुराणि तथा सुपुष्पाण्यपि पुष्कराणि। पुनश्च पद्मानि सकेसराणि धन्यानि चित्राणि तथा वनानि।।5.7.10।।
transliteration: kṛtāni veśmāni ca pāṇḍurāṇi tathā supuṣpāṇyapi puṣkarāṇi| punaśca padmāni sakesarāṇi dhanyāni citrāṇi tathā vanāni
translation: पाण्डुराणि white in colour, वेश्मानि च houses, कृतानि drawn, तथा so also, सुपुष्पाणि with beautiful flowers, पुष्कराणि च ponds also, पुनश्च again, स केसराणि having filaments, पद्मानि lotuses, तथा so also, धन्यानि complete, चित्राणि paintings, वनानि gardens.
explanation: There were pictures of mansions white in colour and pools of crystalclear water filled with lovely flowers. There were pictures of beautiful lotuses drawn on it.

shloka_text: पुष्पाह्वयं नामविराजमानं रत्नप्रभाभिश्च विवर्धमानम्। वेश्मोत्तमानामपि चोच्यमानं महाकपिस्तत्र महाविमानम्।।5.7.11।।
transliteration: puṣpāhvayaṃ nāmavirājamānaṃ ratnaprabhābhiśca vivardhamānam| veśmottamānāmapi cocyamānaṃ mahākapistatra mahāvimānam
translation: तत्र there, महाकपिः great vanara, पुष्पाह्वयम् Pushpaka chariot by name, नामविराजमानम् splendid indeed, रत्नप्रभाभिः glitter of gems, विवर्धमानम् glowing, वेश्मोत्तमानामपि of magnificent mansions, उच्यमानम् tall, महाविमानम् great chariot.
explanation: There, the great Hanuman indeed saw a splendid chariot called Pushpaka. It was glowing with glittering gems. Taller than the biggest mansion, it was a great chariot.

shloka_text: कृताश्च वैडूर्यमया विहङ्गाः रूप्यप्रवालैश्च तथा विहङ्गाः। चित्राश्च नानावसुभिर्भुजङ्गाः जात्यानुरूपास्तुरगाः शुभाङ्गाः।।5.7.12।।
transliteration: kṛtāśca vaiḍūryamayā vihaṅgāḥ rūpyapravālaiśca tathā vihaṅgāḥ| citrāśca nānāvasubhirbhujaṅgāḥ jātyānurūpāsturagāḥ śubhāṅgāḥ
translation: वैडूर्यमयाः made of vaidurya, विहङ्गाः birds, तथा similarly, रूप्यप्रवालैश्च made of silver and corals, विहङ्गाः birds, नानावसुभिः with various gems, चित्राः colourful, भुजङ्गाः serpents, जात्याः due to there good breeding, अनुरूपाः similar, शुभाङ्गाः with auspicious limbs, तुरगाः horses, कृताः drawn.
explanation: Inside were birds made of vaidurya, silver and corals. There were colourful serpents made of various gems, and highclass horses of exquisite limbs drawn.

shloka_text: प्रवालजाम्बूनदपुष्पपक्षाः सलीलमावर्जितजिह्मपक्षाः। कामस्य साक्षादिव भान्ति पक्षाः कृता विहङ्गाः सुमुखाः सुपक्षाः।।5.7.13।।
transliteration: pravālajāmbūnadapuṣpapakṣāḥ salīlamāvarjitajihmapakṣāḥ| kāmasya sākṣādiva bhānti pakṣāḥ kṛtā vihaṅgāḥ sumukhāḥ supakṣāḥ
translation: प्रवालजाम्बूनदपुष्पपक्षाः wings engraved with corals and gold, सुपक्षाः having beautiful wings, सलीलम् in a sportive way, आवर्जितजिह्मपक्षाः with their artificial wings bent down (tossed), विहङ्गाः birds, कृताः were drawn, साक्षात् truly, कामस्य cupid's, पक्षाः इव like wings, भान्ति seemed.
explanation: It had curved figures of birds with beautiful wings carved out of corals and gold The wings were shining as if they were really the wings of allies of Cupid, the god of love.

shloka_text: नियुज्यमानास्तु गजाः सुहस्ताः सकेसराश्चोत्पलपत्रहस्ताः। बभूवदेवी च कृता सुहस्ता लक्ष्मी स्तथा पद्मिनि पद्महस्ता।।5.7.14।।
transliteration: niyujyamānāstu gajāḥ suhastāḥ sakesarāścotpalapatrahastāḥ| babhūvadevī ca kṛtā suhastā lakṣmī stathā padmini padmahastā
translation: पद्मिनि in a lotuspond, सुहस्ता having beautiful hands, सकेसराश्च with filaments, उत्पलपत्रहस्ताः blue lotuses by their trunk carried, लक्ष्मीः goddess of wealth, नियुज्यमानास्तु stationed in place, गजाः elephants, तथा similarly, पद्महस्ता holding a lotus in hand, सुहस्ता of beautiful hand, देवी च goddess, कृता drawn, बभूव appeared.
explanation: He saw on it lotus ponds, artificial elephants with shapely trunks, offering to Laxmi who herself was a lotus, holding in her beautiful hands blue lotuses shining with filaments.

shloka_text: इतीव तद्गृहमभिगम्य शोभनम् सविस्मयो नगमिव चारुशोभनम्। पुनश्च तत्परमसुगन्धि सुन्दरम् हिमात्यये नगमिव चारुकन्दरम्।।5.7.15।।
transliteration: itīva tadgṛhamabhigamya śobhanam savismayo nagamiva cāruśobhanam| punaśca tatparamasugandhi sundaram himātyaye nagamiva cārukandaram
translation: इतीव in that way, शोभनम् auspicious, चारुशोभनम् beautifully fashioned, नगमिव like a mountain, तद्गृहम् that palace, अभिगम्य having reached, सविस्मयः wonderstruck, परमसुगन्धि highly fragrant, सुन्दरम् beautiful, हिमात्यये at the end of winter, चारुकन्दरम् having beautiful caves, नगमिव like mountain, तत् that, पुनश्च once again.
explanation: Thus he reached the auspicious palace appearing like a beautiful mountain and stood wonderstruck. Once again he looked at that beautiful palace which appeared like a mountain with lovely caverns in spring time filled with wonderful fragrance

shloka_text: ततः स तां कपिरभिपत्य पूजितां चरन् पुरीं दशमुखबाहुपालिताम्। अदृश्य तां जनकसुतां सुपूजितां सुदुःखितः पतिगुणवेगवर्जिताम्।।5.7.16।।
transliteration: tataḥ sa tāṃ kapirabhipatya pūjitāṃ caran purīṃ daśamukhabāhupālitām| adṛśya tāṃ janakasutāṃ supūjitāṃ suduḥkhitaḥ patiguṇavegavarjitām
translation: ततः then, सः कपिः monkey, पूजिताम् worshipped, दशमुखबाहुपालिताम् ruled by the arms of the tenheaded king, तां पुरीम् that city, अभिपत्य having reached, चरन् while moving about, सुपूजिताम् venerable, पतिगुणवेगवर्जिताम् who was deprived of the benefit of her husband's virtuous conduct, तां जनकसुताम् that Janaka's daughter Sita, अदृश्य unable to find, सुदुःखितः was deeply sorrowful.
explanation: Then Hanuman moved about that cherished city ruled by the strength of arms of the tenheaded king. Unable to find venerable Sita, who was deprived of the benefit of her husband's virtuous proximity, he became deeply sad.

shloka_text: ततस्तदा बहुविधभावितात्मनः कृतात्मनो जनकसुतां सुवर्त्मनः। अपश्यतोऽभवदतिदुःखितं मनः सुचक्षुषः प्रविचरतो महात्मनः।।5.7.17।।
transliteration: tatastadā bahuvidhabhāvitātmanaḥ kṛtātmano janakasutāṃ suvartmanaḥ| apaśyato'bhavadatiduḥkhitaṃ manaḥ sucakṣuṣaḥ pravicarato mahātmanaḥ
translation: ततः from there, तदा then, बहुविधभावितात्मनः thinking of many things in his mind, कृतात्मनः of a great soul, सुवर्त्मनः of the followers of righteous path, सुचक्षुषः foresighted, प्रविचरतः while he moved, जनकसुताम् daughter of Janaka, अपश्यत: unable to find, महात्मनः of the great self, मनः mind, अतिदुःखितम् very distressed, अभवत् became.
explanation: Unable to find Sita, the disciplined and foresighted Hanuman, who always kept the righteous path, felt distressed while moving about, his mind oppressed by all kinds of thought. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventh sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: स तस्य मध्ये भवनस्य संस्थितं महद्विमानं मणिवज्रचित्रितम्। प्रतप्तजाम्बूनदजालकृत्रिमं ददर्श वीरः पवनात्मजः कपिः।।5.8.1।।
transliteration: sa tasya madhye bhavanasya saṃsthitaṃ mahadvimānaṃ maṇivajracitritam| prataptajāmbūnadajālakṛtrimaṃ dadarśa vīraḥ pavanātmajaḥ kapiḥ
translation: वीरः courageous, पवनात्मजः son of the Windgod, सः कपिः that vanara, तस्य भवनस्य of that mansion, मध्ये in the middle, संस्थितम् standing, मणिवज्रचित्रितम् rendered beautiful with gems and diamonds, प्रतप्तजाम्बूनदजालकृत्रिमम् adorned with latticed windows of barnished gold, महत् great, विमानम् aerial chariot, ददर्श saw.
explanation: The courageous son of the Windgod, Hanuman, the vanara saw the aerial chariot kept in the middle of the mansion inlaid with gems and diamonds latticed with artificial windows of barnished gold.
comments: Further description of  the aerial car, Pushpaka

shloka_text: तदप्रमेयाप्रतिकारकृत्रिमं कृतं स्वयं साध्विति विश्वकर्मणा। दिवं गतं वायुपथप्रतिष्ठितं व्यराजतादित्यपथस्य लक्ष्मवत्।।5.8.2।।
transliteration: tadaprameyāpratikārakṛtrimaṃ kṛtaṃ svayaṃ sādhviti viśvakarmaṇā| divaṃ gataṃ vāyupathapratiṣṭhitaṃ vyarājatādityapathasya lakṣmavat
translation: अप्रमेयाप्रतिकारकृत्रिमम् with images of incomparable beauty and immeasureable skill, विश्वकर्मणा by Visvakarma, स्वयम् himself, साध्विति product of excellent achievement, कृतम् fashioned, दिवम् sky, गतम् going, वायुपथप्रतिष्ठितम् which was placed in the aerial path, तत् that, आदित्यपथस्य in the orbit of the Sun, लक्ष्मवत् like a beaconlight, व्यराजत shone.
explanation: The immeasurable Pushpaka fashioned by Visvakarma with images of incomparable beauty was not possible to describe. An excellent  product of his achievement, it was placed in the aerial path appearing as a beaconlight (signpost) in the orbit of the Sun.

shloka_text: न तत्र किञ्चिन्न कृतं प्रयत्नतो न तत्र किञ्चिन्न महार्हरत्नवत्। न ते विशेषा नियताः सुरेष्वपि न तत्र किञ्चिन्न महाविशेषवत्।।5.8.3।।
transliteration: na tatra kiñcinna kṛtaṃ prayatnato na tatra kiñcinna mahārharatnavat| na te viśeṣā niyatāḥ sureṣvapi na tatra kiñcinna mahāviśeṣavat
translation: तत्र there, प्रयत्नतः by special effort, न कृतम् not only done, किञ्चित् anything, न not, तत्र there, न महार्हरत्नवत् with costly gems, किञ्चित् a litttle, न not, ते those, विशेषाः unique, सुरेष्वपि even to deities, न नियताः not present, तत्र there, न महाविशेषवत् very special, किञ्चित् न indeed it was.
explanation: There was nothing in Pushpaka which was not executed carefully with special effort, nothing which was not made of precious stones. Such privileges were not available to even gods. Indeed there was nothing which was not unique.

shloka_text: तपः समाधानपराक्रमार्जितं मनः समाधानविचारचारिणम्। अनेकसंस्थानविशेषनिर्मितं ततस्ततस्तुल्यविशेषदर्शनम्।।5.8.4।।
transliteration: tapaḥ samādhānaparākramārjitaṃ manaḥ samādhānavicāracāriṇam| anekasaṃsthānaviśeṣanirmitaṃ tatastatastulyaviśeṣadarśanam
translation: तपः spiritual efforts, समाधानपराक्रमार्जितम् designed through concentration and prowess, मनः समाधानविचारचारिणम् which can reach the places desired by the thought of its master, अनेकसंस्थानविशेषनिर्मितम् built with many special seats, ततस्ततः at all places, तुल्यविशेषदर्शनम्  of equally good appearance
explanation: (The Pushpaka) was designed by dint of divine efforts and prowess (of Kubera). It could touch any place its master commanded with a cool mind. It had many beautiful places of rest.

shloka_text: विशेषमालम्ब्य विशेषसंस्थितं विचित्रकूटं बहुकूटमण्डितम्। मनोऽभिरामं शरदिन्दुनिर्मलं विचित्रकूटं शिखरं गिरेर्यथा।।5.8.5।।
transliteration: viśeṣamālambya viśeṣasaṃsthitaṃ vicitrakūṭaṃ bahukūṭamaṇḍitam| mano'bhirāmaṃ śaradindunirmalaṃ vicitrakūṭaṃ śikharaṃ gireryathā
translation: विशेषम् special, आलम्ब्य resorting to, विशेषसंस्थितम् designed in a unique manner, विचित्रकूटम् with wonderful peaks, बहुकूटमण्डितम् decorated with many peaks, मनोऽभिरामम् delightful to the mind, शरदिन्दुनिर्मलम् pleasing as autumnal fullmoon, गिरेः mountain's, विचित्रकूटम् wonderful towers, शिखरं यथा like the peak.
explanation: The Pushpaka was specially designed in a unique manner. It was decorated with many colourful peaks. It was delghtful and pleasing to the mind and bright like the autumnal fullmoon. It looked like a mountain with many wonderful towers around.

shloka_text: वहन्ति यं कुण्डलशोभिताननाः महाशना व्योमचरा निशाचराः। विवृत्तविध्वस्तविशाललोचनाः महाजवा भूतगणाः सहस्रशः।।5.8.6।।
transliteration: vahanti yaṃ kuṇḍalaśobhitānanāḥ mahāśanā vyomacarā niśācarāḥ| vivṛttavidhvastaviśālalocanāḥ mahājavā bhūtagaṇāḥ sahasraśaḥ
translation: यम् such (a chariot), कुण्डलशोभिताननाः faces brightened by the earrings, महाशनाः  gluttons, व्योमचराः ranging in the sky, निशाचराः nightrangers, विवृत्तविध्वस्त विशाललोचनाः with big rolling and frightening eyes, महाजवाः of tremendous speed, भूतगणाः groups of Bhutas, सहस्रशः in thousands, वहन्ति  drawing.
explanation: The Pushpaka was borne by multitudes of Bhutas whose faces were shining with earrings, who were demons ranging in the night sky. They were gluttons endowed with great speed, and they had big, rolling and frightening eyes.

shloka_text: वसन्तपुष्पोत्करचारुदर्शनं वसन्तमासादपि कान्तदर्शनम्। स पुष्पकं तत्र विमानमुत्तमं ददर्श तद्वानरवीरसत्तमः।।5.8.7।।
transliteration: vasantapuṣpotkaracārudarśanaṃ vasantamāsādapi kāntadarśanam| sa puṣpakaṃ tatra vimānamuttamaṃ dadarśa tadvānaravīrasattamaḥ
translation: तत् that, वानरवीरसत्तमः hero among monkeys, सः he, वसन्तपुष्पोत्करचारुदर्शनम् looking beautiful like a collection of blossoms of spring, वसन्तमासादपि more delightful than spring, कान्तदर्शनम् appearing beautiful, पुष्पकम् Pushpaka, उत्तमम् excellent, विमानम् aerial chariot, तत्र there, ददर्श saw.
explanation: That hero among monkeys, beheld the aerial chariot looking beautiful like a colourful collection of spring blossoms. Its appearance was more pleasant than spring itself. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eighth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तस्यालयवरिष्ठस्य मध्ये विपुलमायतं। ददर्श भवनश्रेष्ठं हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः।।5.9.1।।
transliteration: tasyālayavariṣṭhasya madhye vipulamāyataṃ| dadarśa bhavanaśreṣṭhaṃ hanumānmārutātmajaḥ
translation: मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, हनुमान् Hanuman, तस्य his, आलयवरिष्ठस्य of the main building, मध्ये in the centre, विपुलम् spacious, आयतम् huge, भवनश्रेष्ठम् excellent among mansions, ददर्श saw.
explanation: The son of the Windgod, Hanuman, saw a huge, spacious and excellent of all mansions in the centre of the palace.
comments: Description of the harem of Ravana.

shloka_text: अर्धयोजनविस्तीर्णमायतं योजनं हि तत्। भवनं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य बहुप्रासादसङ्कुलम्।।5.9.2।।
transliteration: ardhayojanavistīrṇamāyataṃ yojanaṃ hi tat| bhavanaṃ rākṣasendrasya bahuprāsādasaṅkulam
translation: राक्षसेन्द्रस्य of Indra among demons, तत् that, बहुप्रासादसङ्कुलम् of multitude of palaces, भवनम् mansion, अर्धयोजनविस्तीर्णम्  width of half yojana, योजनम् yojana, आयतम् long.
explanation: The mansion of the lord of demons was a conglomeration of palaces half a yojana long and half a yojana wide.

shloka_text: मार्गमाणस्तु वैदेहीं सीतामायतलोचनाम्। सर्वतः परिचक्राम हनूमानरिसूदनः।।5.9.3।।
transliteration: mārgamāṇastu vaidehīṃ sītāmāyatalocanām| sarvataḥ paricakrāma hanūmānarisūdanaḥ
translation: अरिसूदनः subduer of enemies, हनुमान् Hanuman, वैदेहीम् Vaidehi, आयतलोचनाम् broadeyed, सीताम् for Sita, मार्गमाणः तु  in search, सर्वतः all over, परिचक्राम went allround .
explanation: Hanuman, the subduer of enemies, went  around in search of  the largeeyed Vaidehi.

shloka_text: उत्तमं राक्षसावासं हनुमानवलोकयन्। आससादाथ लक्ष्मीवान् राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्।।5.9.4।। चतुर्विषाणैर्द्विरदैस्त्रिविषाणैस्तथैव च। परिक्षिप्तमसम्बाधं रक्ष्यमाणमुदायुधैः।।5.9.5।।
transliteration: uttamaṃ rākṣasāvāsaṃ hanumānavalokayan| āsasādātha lakṣmīvān rākṣasendraniveśanam caturviṣāṇairdviradaistriviṣāṇaistathaiva ca| parikṣiptamasambādhaṃ rakṣyamāṇamudāyudhaiḥ
translation: अथ now, लक्ष्मीवान् endowed with brightness, हनुमान् Hanuman, उत्तमम् best, राक्षसावासम् residence of demons, चतुर्विषाणैः fourtusked, तथैव च and similarly, त्रिविषाणैः threetusked, द्विरदैः twotusked, परिक्षिप्तम् surrounded by, असम्बाधम् spacious, उदायुधैः holding weapons, रक्ष्यमाणम् guarded by, राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम् home of the lord of the ogres, अवलोकयन् seeing, आससाद reached.
explanation: Searching the excellent residences of important demons, Hanuman finally reached  the palace of the lord of ogres guarded by armed demons with elephants with two or three or four tusks.

shloka_text: उत्तमं राक्षसावासं हनुमानवलोकयन्। आससादाथ लक्ष्मीवान् राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्।।5.9.4।। चतुर्विषाणैर्द्विरदैस्त्रिविषाणैस्तथैव च। परिक्षिप्तमसम्बाधं रक्ष्यमाणमुदायुधैः।।5.9.5।।
transliteration: uttamaṃ rākṣasāvāsaṃ hanumānavalokayan| āsasādātha lakṣmīvān rākṣasendraniveśanam caturviṣāṇairdviradaistriviṣāṇaistathaiva ca| parikṣiptamasambādhaṃ rakṣyamāṇamudāyudhaiḥ
translation: अथ now, लक्ष्मीवान् endowed with brightness, हनुमान् Hanuman, उत्तमम् best, राक्षसावासम् residence of demons, चतुर्विषाणैः fourtusked, तथैव च and similarly, त्रिविषाणैः threetusked, द्विरदैः twotusked, परिक्षिप्तम् surrounded by, असम्बाधम् spacious, उदायुधैः holding weapons, रक्ष्यमाणम् guarded by, राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम् home of the lord of the ogres, अवलोकयन् seeing, आससाद reached.
explanation: Searching the excellent residences of important demons, Hanuman finally reached  the palace of the lord of ogres guarded by armed demons with elephants with two or three or four tusks.

shloka_text: राक्षसीभिश्च पत्नीभी रावणस्य निवेशनम्। आहृताभिश्च विक्रम्य राजकन्याभिरावृतम्।।5.9.6।। तन्नक्रमकराकीर्णं तिमिङ्गिलझषाकुलम्। वायुवेगसमाधूतं पन्नगैरिव सागरम्।।5.9.7।।
transliteration: rākṣasībhiśca patnībhī rāvaṇasya niveśanam| āhṛtābhiśca vikramya rājakanyābhirāvṛtam tannakramakarākīrṇaṃ timiṅgilajhaṣākulam| vāyuvegasamādhūtaṃ pannagairiva sāgaram
translation: रावणस्य Ravana's, पत्नीभिः with wives, राक्षसीभिः च by demonesses also, विक्रम्य by winning, आहृताभिः brought, राजकन्याभिः by princesses, आवृतम् surrounded, निवेशनम् palace, तत् नक्रमकराकीर्णम् filled with crocodiles and sharks, तिमिङ्गिलझषाकुलम् with whales and fish, वायुवेगसमाधूतम् shaken by the force of the wind, पन्नगैः with serpents, सागरम् इव like an ocean, तत् he saw.
explanation: Hanuman entered the palace of Ravana crowded with shedemons who were the wives of Ravana and the princesses brought by him after winning them in wars. To Hanuman, it looked like an ocean filled with crocodiles, sharks, whales, and a variety of fishes and snakes tossed by the force of the wind.

shloka_text: राक्षसीभिश्च पत्नीभी रावणस्य निवेशनम्। आहृताभिश्च विक्रम्य राजकन्याभिरावृतम्।।5.9.6।। तन्नक्रमकराकीर्णं तिमिङ्गिलझषाकुलम्। वायुवेगसमाधूतं पन्नगैरिव सागरम्।।5.9.7।।
transliteration: rākṣasībhiśca patnībhī rāvaṇasya niveśanam| āhṛtābhiśca vikramya rājakanyābhirāvṛtam tannakramakarākīrṇaṃ timiṅgilajhaṣākulam| vāyuvegasamādhūtaṃ pannagairiva sāgaram
translation: रावणस्य Ravana's, पत्नीभिः with wives, राक्षसीभिः च by demonesses also, विक्रम्य by winning, आहृताभिः brought, राजकन्याभिः by princesses, आवृतम् surrounded, निवेशनम् palace, तत् नक्रमकराकीर्णम् filled with crocodiles and sharks, तिमिङ्गिलझषाकुलम् with whales and fish, वायुवेगसमाधूतम् shaken by the force of the wind, पन्नगैः with serpents, सागरम् इव like an ocean, तत् he saw.
explanation: Hanuman entered the palace of Ravana crowded with shedemons who were the wives of Ravana and the princesses brought by him after winning them in wars. To Hanuman, it looked like an ocean filled with crocodiles, sharks, whales, and a variety of fishes and snakes tossed by the force of the wind.

shloka_text: या हि वैश्रवणे लक्ष्मीर्या चेन्द्रे हरिवाहने। सा रावणगृहे सर्वा नित्यमेवानपायिनी।।5.9.8।।
transliteration: yā hi vaiśravaṇe lakṣmīryā cendre harivāhane| sā rāvaṇagṛhe sarvā nityamevānapāyinī
translation: वैश्रवणे by Vaisravana, या whatever, लक्ष्मीः wealth हरिवाहने on greenish horse, the mount, इन्द्रे च of Indra, या as much, सा that, सर्वा everything, रावणगृहे in the residence of Ravana, नित्यमेव always, अनपायिनी present.
explanation: Whatever wealth was possessed by Vaisravana (Kubera, the son of sage Vishrava) and also Indra who rides the Ucchaisrava green horse, was there in the palace of Ravana.

shloka_text: या च राज्ञः कुबेरस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च। तादृशी तद्विशिष्टा वा ऋद्धी रक्षोगृहेष्विह।।5.9.9।।
transliteration: yā ca rājñaḥ kuberasya yamasya varuṇasya ca| tādṛśī tadviśiṣṭā vā ṛddhī rakṣogṛheṣviha
translation: राज्ञः of  the king, कुबेरस्य Kubera's, या whatever, यमस्य Yama's, वरुणस्य Varuna's, च and, या whatever, तादृशी such, तद्विशिष्टा वा or more exquisite than, ऋद्धि: wealth इह here, रक्षोगृहेषु in the houses of demons.
explanation: The wealth stored in Ravana's palace was akin to what lay in the palaces of Kubera, Yama or Varuna, and ever more exquisite.

shloka_text: तस्य हर्म्यस्य मध्यस्थं वेश्म चान्यत्सुनिर्मितं। बहुनिर्यूहसङ्कीर्णं ददर्श पवनात्मजः।।5.9.10।।
transliteration: tasya harmyasya madhyasthaṃ veśma cānyatsunirmitaṃ| bahuniryūhasaṅkīrṇaṃ dadarśa pavanātmajaḥ
translation: पवनात्मजः son of the Windgod, तस्य of that, हर्म्यस्य of the palace, मध्यस्थम् in the centre, सुनिर्मितम् well built, बहुनिर्यूहसङ्कीर्णम् a complex many houses, अन्यत् another, वेश्म home, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Hanuman saw in the centre of that palace a complex of many wellbuilt houses.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मणोऽर्थे कृतं दिव्यं दिवि यद्विश्वकर्मणा। विमानं पुष्पकं नाम सर्वरत्नविभूषितम्।।5.9.11।। परेण तपसा लेभे यत्कुबेरः पितामहात्। कुबेरमोजसा जित्वा लेभे तद्राक्षसेश्वरः।।5.9.12।।
transliteration: brahmaṇo'rthe kṛtaṃ divyaṃ divi yadviśvakarmaṇā| vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ nāma sarvaratnavibhūṣitam pareṇa tapasā lebhe yatkuberaḥ pitāmahāt| kuberamojasā jitvā lebhe tadrākṣaseśvaraḥ
translation: सर्वरत्नविभूषितम् decorated with all kinds of gems, पुष्पकं नाम called Pushpaka, यत् that, दिव्यम् wonderful, विमानम् aerial chariot, विश्वकर्मणा by Visvakarma, दिवि in the sky, ब्रह्मणः अर्थे for Brahma, कृतम् built, यत् the same one, कुबेरः Kubera, पितामहात् from grandfather the creator, परेण with supreme, तपसा by penance, लेभे got, तत् that, राक्षसेश्वरः lord of demons, ओजसा by his might, कुबेरम् Kubera, जित्वा after defeating, लेभे acquired.
explanation: There was a wonderful aerial chariot called Pushpaka embellished with all kinds of gems built by Visvakarma for Brahma. It was the same one that Kubera had won from his grandfather, the creator Brahma, through his supreme penance. The lord of ogres acquired it (as a memento for his victory) by defeating Kubera with his might.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मणोऽर्थे कृतं दिव्यं दिवि यद्विश्वकर्मणा। विमानं पुष्पकं नाम सर्वरत्नविभूषितम्।।5.9.11।। परेण तपसा लेभे यत्कुबेरः पितामहात्। कुबेरमोजसा जित्वा लेभे तद्राक्षसेश्वरः।।5.9.12।।

explanation: There was a wonderful aerial chariot called Pushpaka embellished with all kinds of gems built by Visvakarma for Brahma. It was the same one that Kubera had won from his grandfather, the creator Brahma, through his supreme penance. The lord of ogres acquired it (as a memento for his victory) by defeating Kubera with his might.

shloka_text: ईहामृगसमायुक्त्तै: कार्तस्वरहिरमण्मयैः। सुकृतैराचितं स्तम्भैः प्रदीप्तमिव च श्रिया।।5.9.13।। मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशैरुल्लिखद्भिरिवाम्बरं। कूटागारैश्शुभाकारैस्सर्वतस्समलङ्कृतम्।।5.9.14।।
transliteration: īhāmṛgasamāyukttai: kārtasvarahiramaṇmayaiḥ| sukṛtairācitaṃ stambhaiḥ pradīptamiva ca śriyā merumandarasaṅkāśairullikhadbhirivāmbaraṃ| kūṭāgāraiśśubhākāraissarvatassamalaṅkṛtam
translation: ईहामृगसमायुक्तै: with images of wolves carved, कार्तस्वरहिरण्मयैः made of Kartaswara and Hiranmaya, two types of gold, सुकृतैः finely built, स्तम्भैः with pillars, आचितम् supported, श्रिया lustrous, प्रदीप्तमिव as though blazing, मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशैः resembling mountain Meru and Mandara, अम्बरम् sky, उल्लिखद्भिरिव as though scraping, शुभाकारैः by auspicious, कूटागारैः with multitude of pleasurehouses, सर्वतः everywhere, समलङ्कृतम् decorated.
explanation: It was supported by finely built pillars of two types of gold (Kartaswara and Hiranmaya) with images of wolves carved on them and blazing. It was tall as if scraping the sky and resembled mountains like Meru and Mandara. It was graced with multitudes of  auspicious and decorated pleasurehouses everywhere.

shloka_text: ईहामृगसमायुक्त्तै: कार्तस्वरहिरमण्मयैः। सुकृतैराचितं स्तम्भैः प्रदीप्तमिव च श्रिया।।5.9.13।। मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशैरुल्लिखद्भिरिवाम्बरं। कूटागारैश्शुभाकारैस्सर्वतस्समलङ्कृतम्।।5.9.14।।
transliteration: īhāmṛgasamāyukttai: kārtasvarahiramaṇmayaiḥ| sukṛtairācitaṃ stambhaiḥ pradīptamiva ca śriyā merumandarasaṅkāśairullikhadbhirivāmbaraṃ| kūṭāgāraiśśubhākāraissarvatassamalaṅkṛtam
translation: ईहामृगसमायुक्तै: with images of wolves carved, कार्तस्वरहिरण्मयैः made of Kartaswara and Hiranmaya, two types of gold, सुकृतैः finely built, स्तम्भैः with pillars, आचितम् supported, श्रिया lustrous, प्रदीप्तमिव as though blazing, मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशैः resembling mountain Meru and Mandara, अम्बरम् sky, उल्लिखद्भिरिव as though scraping, शुभाकारैः by auspicious, कूटागारैः with multitude of pleasurehouses, सर्वतः everywhere, समलङ्कृतम् decorated.
explanation: It was supported by finely built pillars of two types of gold (Kartaswara and Hiranmaya) with images of wolves carved on them and blazing. It was tall as if scraping the sky and resembled mountains like Meru and Mandara. It was graced with multitudes of  auspicious and decorated pleasurehouses everywhere.

shloka_text: ज्वलनार्कप्रतीकाशं सुकृतं विश्वकर्मणा। हेमसोपानसंयुक्तं चारुप्रवरवेदिकम्।।5.9.15।।
transliteration: jvalanārkapratīkāśaṃ sukṛtaṃ viśvakarmaṇā| hemasopānasaṃyuktaṃ cārupravaravedikam
translation: विश्वकर्मणा by Visvakarma, सुकृतम् well built, ज्वलनार्कप्रतीकाशम् glowing like fire and the Sun, हेमसोपानसंयुक्तम् had stairways of gold, चारुप्रवरवेदिकम् had beautiful paltforms.
explanation: It was well built by Visvakarma and and had golden stairways, with radiant platforms glowing like fire and Sun.

shloka_text: जालवातायनैर्युक्तं काञ्चनैः स्स्फाटिकैरपि। इन्द्रनीलमहानीलमणिप्रवरवेदिकम्।।5.9.16।।
transliteration: jālavātāyanairyuktaṃ kāñcanaiḥ ssphāṭikairapi| indranīlamahānīlamaṇipravaravedikam
translation: काञ्चनैः with gold, स्फाटिकैरपि with crystal also, जालवातायनैः by latticed windows, युक्तम् endowed, इन्द्रनीलमहानीलमणिप्रवरवेदिकम् platforms encrusted with saphires called Indraneela and Mahaneela.
explanation: It had latticed windows made of gold inlaid with crystals. The platforms were encrusted with saphires called Indraneela and Mahaneela appropriately.

shloka_text: विद्रुमेण विचित्रेण मणिभिश्च महाघनैः। निस्तुलाभिश्च मुक्ताभिस्तलेनाभिविराजितम्।।5.9.17।।
transliteration: vidrumeṇa vicitreṇa maṇibhiśca mahāghanaiḥ| nistulābhiśca muktābhistalenābhivirājitam
translation: विचित्रेण with colourful, विद्रुमेण with corals, महाघनैः by very precious, मणिभिश्च by gems even, निस्तुलाभिः with peerless (invaluable), मुक्ताभिः with pearls, तलेन on the surface, अभिविराजितम् shining very brightly.
explanation: It was shining bright with colourful corals, precious gems and peerless pearls fixed on its floor.

shloka_text: चन्दनेन च रक्तेन तपनीयनिभेन च। सुपुण्यगन्धिना युक्तमादित्यतरुणोपमम्।।5.9.18।।
transliteration: candanena ca raktena tapanīyanibhena ca| supuṇyagandhinā yuktamādityataruṇopamam
translation: रक्तेन in red, तपनीयनिभेन च comparable to pure and polished gold, सुपुण्यगन्धिना with sweet fragrance, चन्दनेन with sandal, युक्तम् endowed, आदित्यतरुणोपमम् like the rising Sun.
explanation: It was bright like molten gold, fragrant with red sandal comparable to the rising Sun.

shloka_text: कूटागारैर्वराकारैर्विविधैस्समलङ्कृतम्। विमानं पुष्पकं दिव्यमारुरोह महाकपिः।।5.9.19।।
transliteration: kūṭāgārairvarākārairvividhaissamalaṅkṛtam| vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ divyamāruroha mahākapiḥ
translation: महाकपिः Hanuman, वराकारैः of excellent appearance, कूटागारैः with many corridors, समलङ्कृतम् decorated, दिव्यम् wonderful, पुष्पकं विमानम् Pushpaka chariot, आरुरोह ascended.
explanation: Hanuman ascended the wonderful Pushpaka, welldecked with many corridors.

shloka_text: तत्रस्थस्स तदा गन्धं पानभक्ष्यान्नसम्भवम्। दिव्यं सम्मूर्छितं जिघ्रद्रूपवन्तमिवानिलम्।।5.9.20।।
transliteration: tatrasthassa tadā gandhaṃ pānabhakṣyānnasambhavam| divyaṃ sammūrchitaṃ jighradrūpavantamivānilam
translation: स: he, तदा then, तत्रस्थः present there, पानभक्ष्यान्नसम्भवम् rising from drinks and food, दिव्यम् divine, सम्मूर्छितम् stupefying, रूपवन्तम् having a solid form, आनिलमिव like wind, गन्धम् fragrance, जिघ्रत् smelt.
explanation: There he smelt the stupefying, unearthly odour of food and drink. He felt as though the fragrance had taken a potentially solid form. (Note: The wind has no form. But when he carried the aroma of food and drink it appeared like the personification of wind which could be smelt. गन्धवती पृथवी fragrance comes from earth पृथवीतत्त्व the poet transmits the same to the wind who has got only स्पर्श sense of touch).

shloka_text: स गन्धस्तं महासत्त्वं बन्धुर्बन्धुमिवोत्तमम्। इत एहीत्युवाचेन तत्र यत्र स रावणः।।5.9.21।।
transliteration: sa gandhastaṃ mahāsattvaṃ bandhurbandhumivottamam| ita ehītyuvācena tatra yatra sa rāvaṇaḥ
translation: स: गन्धः that fragrance, महासत्त्वम् mighty, तम् him (Hanuman), उत्तमम् great, बन्धुम् relative, बन्धुरिव like a relative, सः रावणः that Ravana, यत्र wherever, तत्र there, इतः एहि come here, इति thus, उवाच इव as if told.
explanation: The fragrance was as if inviting the mighty hero like a relative inviting his kith and kin, saying 'come here' and leading him to a place where Ravana rested.

shloka_text: ततस्तां प्रस्थितश्शालां ददर्श महतीं शुभाम्। रावणस्य मनः कान्तां कान्तामिव वरस्त्रियम्।।5.9.22।।
transliteration: tatastāṃ prasthitaśśālāṃ dadarśa mahatīṃ śubhām| rāvaṇasya manaḥ kāntāṃ kāntāmiva varastriyam
translation: ततः then, प्रस्थितः he started, कान्ताम् beloved, वरस्त्रियमिव like his chief queen, रावणस्य Ravana's, मनः कान्ताम् dear his to heart, शुभाम् auspicious, महतीम् great, शालाम् hall, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Then he proceeded to an auspicious hall, which was Ravana's favourite like his chief queen dear to his heart.

shloka_text: मणिसोपानविकृतां हेमजालविभूषिताम्। स्फाटिकैरावृततलां दन्तान्तरितरूपिकाम्।।5.9.23।।
transliteration: maṇisopānavikṛtāṃ hemajālavibhūṣitām| sphāṭikairāvṛtatalāṃ dantāntaritarūpikām
translation: मणिसोपानाविकृताम् staircase inlaid with special gems, हेमजालविभूषिताम् latticed with gold, स्फाटिकैः with crystals, आवृततलाम् floors covered with, दन्तान्तरितरूपिकाम् inlaid with silver set in ivory frame.
explanation: The stairways of the mansion were inlaid with special gems, windows were latticed with gold, floors were covered with crystals, figures of ivory with silver.

shloka_text: मुक्ताभिश्च प्रवालैश्च रूप्यचामीकरैरपि। विभूषितां मणिस्तम्भैस्सुबहुस्तम्भभूषिताम्।।5.9.24।।
transliteration: muktābhiśca pravālaiśca rūpyacāmīkarairapi| vibhūṣitāṃ maṇistambhaissubahustambhabhūṣitām
translation: मुक्ताभिश्च with pearls, प्रवालैश्च with corals also, रूप्यचामीकरैरपि with silver and gold, मणिस्तम्भैः with pillars inlaid with gems, विभूषिताम् ornamented, सुबहुस्तम्भभूषिताम् with pillars.
explanation: It was decorated with pillars of silver and gold inlaid with pearls and corals and gems.

shloka_text: नम्रैरृजुभिरत्युच्चैस्समन्तात्सुविभूषितैः। स्तम्भै: पक्षैरिवात्युच्चैर्दिवं संप्रस्थितामिव।।5.9.25।।
transliteration: namrairṛjubhiratyuccaissamantātsuvibhūṣitaiḥ| stambhai: pakṣairivātyuccairdivaṃ saṃprasthitāmiva
translation: नम्रैः bent, ऋजुभिः straight ones, अत्युच्चै: with very lofty, समन्तात् all over, सुविभूषितैः well decorated, स्तम्भैः with columns, अत्युच्छैः long, पक्षैः with wings, दिवम् heaven, सम्प्रस्थितामिव as if started to reach
explanation: It had highly ornamented pillars all over, some slightly bent and others straight. With lofty columns looking like wings it appeared as if the mansion had started on its journey to heaven.

shloka_text: महत्या कुथयास्तीर्णां पृथिवीलक्षणाङ्कया। पृथिवीमिव विस्तीर्णां सराष्ट्रगृहमालिनीम्।।5.9.26।।
transliteration: mahatyā kuthayāstīrṇāṃ pṛthivīlakṣaṇāṅkayā| pṛthivīmiva vistīrṇāṃ sarāṣṭragṛhamālinīm
translation: पृथिवीलक्षणाङ्कया with several murals of earth, महत्या with expansive, कुथया with a carpet, आस्तीर्णाम् covered, सराष्ट्रगृहमालिनीम् having the garland of places and houses drawn on it, विस्तीर्णाम् expansive, पृथिवीमिव like the earth itself.
explanation: The floor was covered with a wide carpet spread from wall to wall with designs of different murals of many places and houses drawn in a row (garland like). The big carpet appeared like the expanse of earth itself.

shloka_text: नादितां मत्तविहगैर्दिव्यगन्धाधिवासिताम्। परार्ध्यास्तरणोपेतां रक्षोधिपनिषेविताम्।।5.9.27।।
transliteration: nāditāṃ mattavihagairdivyagandhādhivāsitām| parārdhyāstaraṇopetāṃ rakṣodhipaniṣevitām
translation: मत्तविहगैः with birds in heat, नादिताम् resounding, दिव्यगन्धाधिवासिताम् scented with divine fragrance, परार्ध्यास्तरणोपेताम् laid with valuable tapestries, रक्षोधिपनिषेविताम् inhabitted by the king of demons.
explanation: The mansion was resounding with the noise of birds singing in heat. It had wonderful fragrance. It was laid with exquisite tapestries and served as a dwelling place for the king of demons.

shloka_text: धूम्रामगरुधूपेन विमलां हंसपाण्डुराम्। चित्रां पुष्पोपहारेण कल्माषीमिव सुप्रभाम्।।5.9.28।।
transliteration: dhūmrāmagarudhūpena vimalāṃ haṃsapāṇḍurām| citrāṃ puṣpopahāreṇa kalmāṣīmiva suprabhām
translation: अगरुधूपेन with smoke of agaru, धूम्राम् smoky, विमलाम् pure white, हंसपाण्डुराम् white like swan, पुष्पोपहारेण due to offering of flowers, चित्राम् colourful, सुप्रभाम् shining, कल्माषीमिव like the wishfulfilling cow.
explanation: It was smoky with fumes of agaru incence though spotless like a swan. It was colourful and radiant like Kamadhenu, the wishfulfilling cow, because of the offering of flowers.

shloka_text: मनस्संह्लादजननीं वर्णस्यापि प्रसादिनीम्। तां शोकनाशिनीं दिव्यां श्रियः सञ्जननीमिव।।5.9.29।।
transliteration: manassaṃhlādajananīṃ varṇasyāpi prasādinīm| tāṃ śokanāśinīṃ divyāṃ śriyaḥ sañjananīmiva
translation: मनः संह्लादजननीम् one which was soul ravishing, वर्णस्यापि with colour and complexion, प्रसादिनीम् pleasing, शोकनाशिनीम् banished sorrow, श्रियः of prosperity, सञ्जननीमिव like the source, दिव्याम् wonderful, ताम् it was.
explanation: (The mansion) was so full of effulgence and soul ravishing that it served as an adornment even to splendour. It looked as though it banished all sorrow and was a source of prosperity.

shloka_text: इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थैस्तु पञ्च पञ्चभिरुत्तमैः। तर्पयामास मातेव तदा रावणपालिता।।5.9.30।।
transliteration: indriyāṇīndriyārthaistu pañca pañcabhiruttamaiḥ| tarpayāmāsa māteva tadā rāvaṇapālitā
translation: रावणपालिता chamber of Ravana, तदा then, माता इव like a mother, उत्तमैः with excellent, पञ्चभिः with the five, इन्द्रियार्थैः with objects of the senses, पञ्च five, इन्द्रियाणि sense organs, तर्पयामास satisfied.
explanation: The chamber of Ravana, like a mother, gratified all the five senses of Hanuman with proper objects of the senses.

shloka_text: स्वर्गोऽयं देवलोकोऽयमिन्द्रस्येयं पुरी भवेत्। सिद्धिर्वेयं परा हि स्यादित्यमन्यत मारुतिः।।5.9.31।।
transliteration: svargo'yaṃ devaloko'yamindrasyeyaṃ purī bhavet| siddhirveyaṃ parā hi syādityamanyata mārutiḥ
translation: अयम् this, स्वर्गः heaven, अयम् this, देवलोकः world of gods, इयम् thus, इन्द्रस्य Indra's, पुरी city (of Amaravati), भवेत् may be, इयम् this one, परा supreme, सिद्धि: achievement, स्यात् may be, इति thus, मारुतिः Maruti, अमन्यत thought.
explanation: 'This may be heaven or world of gods. It may be Amaravati, the abode of Indra or else it may be the supreme achievment (of the Creator), thought Maruti৷৷

shloka_text: प्रध्यायत इवापश्यत्प्रदीपांस्तत्र काञ्चनान्। धूर्तानिव महाधूतैर्देवनेन पराजितान्।।5.9.32।।
transliteration: pradhyāyata ivāpaśyatpradīpāṃstatra kāñcanān| dhūrtāniva mahādhūtairdevanena parājitān
translation: महाधूर्तै: with expert gamblers, देवनेन by a game of dice, पराजिताम् defeated, धूर्तानिव like the gamblers, प्रध्यायत इव like one who is deep in thought, काञ्चनान् golden, प्रदीपान् lamps, आपश्यत् he saw.
explanation: Seeing the golden lamps that stood burning steadily, Hanuman thought they looked like  gamblers in deep thought defeated by expert  gamblers in a game of dice.

shloka_text: दीपानां च प्रकाशेन तेजसा रावणस्य च। अर्चिर्भिर्भूषणानां च प्रदीप्तेत्यभ्यमन्यत।।5.9.33।।
transliteration: dīpānāṃ ca prakāśena tejasā rāvaṇasya ca| arcirbhirbhūṣaṇānāṃ ca pradīptetyabhyamanyata
translation: दीपानाम् of the lamps, प्रकाशेन by the glow, रावणस्य Ravana's, तेजसा च and by his brightness, भूषणानाम् of ornaments, अर्चिर्भिः च by the glow spread there, प्रदीप्ता इति as if glowing like fire, अमन्यत he thought in his mind.
explanation: Hanuman fancied that the entire place was set ablaze with the glow of lamps, the lustre of Ravana and the brilliant glow of Ravana's ornaments (everything was shining).

shloka_text: ततोऽपश्यत्कुथाऽऽसीनं नानावरायम्बरस्रजम्। सहस्रं वरनारीणां नानावेषविभूषितम्।।5.9.34।।
transliteration: tato'paśyatkuthā''sīnaṃ nānāvarāyambarasrajam| sahasraṃ varanārīṇāṃ nānāveṣavibhūṣitam
translation: ततः then, कुथासीनम् seated on carpets, नानावर्णाम्बरस्रजम् wearing clothes and garlands of different colours, नानावेषविभूषितम् dressed various clothes, वरनारीणाम् of beautiful women, सहस्रम् thousand, अपश्यत् he saw.
explanation: He found thousands of beautiful women seated on carpets wearing different clothes and garlands and dressed in various attires.

shloka_text: परिवृत्तेऽर्धरात्रे तु पाननिद्रावशं गतम्। क्रीडित्वोपरतं रात्रौ सुष्वाप बलवत्तदा।।5.9.35।।
transliteration: parivṛtte'rdharātre tu pānanidrāvaśaṃ gatam| krīḍitvoparataṃ rātrau suṣvāpa balavattadā
translation: रात्रौ at night, क्रीडित्वा having sported, उपरतम् wearied, पाननिद्रावशं गतम् succumbed to drinks and sleep, तदा then, अर्धरात्रे when midnight, परिवृत्ते rolled away, बलवत् compelled, सुष्वाप to sleep.
explanation: Drinking and sporting until midnight, they had dropped off to sleeptired.

shloka_text: तत्प्रसुप्तं विरुरुचे निश्शब्दान्तरभूषणम्। निःशब्दहंसभ्रमरं यथा पद्मवनं महत्।।5.9.36।।
transliteration: tatprasuptaṃ viruruce niśśabdāntarabhūṣaṇam| niḥśabdahaṃsabhramaraṃ yathā padmavanaṃ mahat
translation: नि:शब्दान्तरभूषणम् the sounds of ornaments stilled, प्रसुप्तम् slept, तत् that, निःशब्दहंसभ्रमरम् like silent swans and bees, महत् great, पद्मवनं यथा resembling a forest of lotuses, विरुरुचे looked beautiful.
explanation: Fast asleep, sounds of their ornaments silenced, the young women looked like a large bed of lotuses with swans and bees sitting calm without their usual noise.

shloka_text: तासां संवृतदन्तानि मीलिताक्षीणि मारुतिः। अपश्यत्पद्मगन्धीनि वदनानि सुयोषिताम्।।5.9.37।।
transliteration: tāsāṃ saṃvṛtadantāni mīlitākṣīṇi mārutiḥ| apaśyatpadmagandhīni vadanāni suyoṣitām
translation: मारुतिः son of the Windgod, तासां सुयोषिताम् of those wellbred young women, संवृतदन्तानि with teeth concealed, मीलिताक्षीणि closed eyes, पद्मगन्धीनि giving out smell of lotuses, वदनानि faces, अपश्यत् looked.
explanation: Hanuman looked at the faces of the wellbred young women with closed eyes and concealed teeth, fragrant like lotuses.

shloka_text: प्रबुद्धानीव पद्मानि तासां भूत्वा क्षपाक्षये। पुनस्संवृतपत्राणि रात्राविव बभुस्तदा।।5.9.38।।
transliteration: prabuddhānīva padmāni tāsāṃ bhūtvā kṣapākṣaye| punassaṃvṛtapatrāṇi rātrāviva babhustadā
translation: तासाम् of those women, क्षपाक्षये at the end of night, प्रबुद्धानि from early morning, पद्मानीव like lotuses, भूत्वा having been, पुनः again, रात्रौ at night, संवृतपत्राणिव closing up their petals, तदा then, बभुः looked.
explanation: The faces of the women looked like blooming lotuses at daybreak, their petals closed up again at night.

shloka_text: इमानि मुखपद्मानि नियतं मत्तषट्पदाः। अम्बुजानीव फुल्लानि प्रार्थयन्ति पुनः पुनः।।5.9.39।।
transliteration: imāni mukhapadmāni niyataṃ mattaṣaṭpadāḥ| ambujānīva phullāni prārthayanti punaḥ punaḥ
translation: मत्तषट्पदाः intoxicated bees, इमानि these, मुखपद्मानि lotuslike faces, फुल्लानि bloomed, अम्बुजानीव like lotuses, पुनः पुनः again and again, नियतम् always, प्रार्थयन्ति desire.
explanation: The intoxicated bees would again and again long to enjoy these beautiful faces which were like blooming lotuses.

shloka_text: इति चामन्यत श्रीमानुपपत्त्या महाकपिः। मेने हि गुणतस्तानि समानि सलिलोद्भवैः।।5.9.40।।
transliteration: iti cāmanyata śrīmānupapattyā mahākapiḥ| mene hi guṇatastāni samāni salilodbhavaiḥ
translation: श्रीमान् the illustrious, महाकपिः great monkey, उपपत्त्या ascertained to be true, इति thus, अमन्यत felt, तानि those, गुणतः by their qualities, सलिलोद्भवैः with waterborn lotuses, समानि  similar मेने हि he thought.
explanation: The illustrious Hanuman felt it to be correct to compare those faces with lotuses for their fragrance.

shloka_text: सा तस्य शुशुभे शाला ताभिस्त्रीभिर्विराजिता। शारदीव प्रसन्ना द्यौस्ताराभिरभिशोभिता।।5.9.41।।
transliteration: sā tasya śuśubhe śālā tābhistrībhirvirājitā| śāradīva prasannā dyaustārābhirabhiśobhitā
translation: तस्य his (Ravana's), सा शाला that mansion, ताभिः स्त्रीभिः by the women, विराजिता shone, ताराभिः with stars, अभिशोभिता very endearing, प्रसन्ना pleasant, शारदी autumnal, द्यौः इव sky like, शुशुभे seemed.
explanation: Brightened by (the beauty of) the maidens, the mansion shone like the autumnal sky endearing  and pleasing with stars.

shloka_text: स च ताभिः परिवृतश्शुशुभे राक्षसाधिपः। यथा ह्युडुपतिश्शीमांस्ताराभिरभिसंवृतः।।5.9.42।।
transliteration: sa ca tābhiḥ parivṛtaśśuśubhe rākṣasādhipaḥ| yathā hyuḍupatiśśīmāṃstārābhirabhisaṃvṛtaḥ
translation: ताभिः with them, परिवृतः surrounded, सः राक्षसाधिपः the lord of demons, ताराभिः with stars, अभिसंवृतः encircled, श्रीमान् beautiful, उडुपतिः यथा like the Moon, शुशुभे shone.
explanation: The lord of demons surrounded by women shone like the beautiful Moon encircled by stars.

shloka_text: याश्च्यवन्तेऽम्बरात्ताराः पुण्यशेषसमावृताः। इमास्तास्सङ्गताः कृत्स्ना इति मेने हरिस्तदा।।5.9.43।।
transliteration: yāścyavante'mbarāttārāḥ puṇyaśeṣasamāvṛtāḥ| imāstāssaṅgatāḥ kṛtsnā iti mene haristadā
translation: याः those, ताराः stars, पुण्यशेषसमावृताः with left over merits, अम्बरात् from the sky, च्यवन्ते fallen, ताः those, कृत्स्नाः entirely, इमाः these women, सङ्गताः collected together, इति thus, तदा then, हरिः the monkey, मेने thought.
explanation: Seeing those women lying together Hanuman imagined them to be numerous meteors dropped from heaven after enjoying their merits, enjoyed and exhausted.

shloka_text: ताराणामिव सुव्यक्तं महतीनां शुभार्चिषाम्। प्रभावर्णप्रसादाश्च विरेजुस्तत्र योषिताम्।।5.9.44।।
transliteration: tārāṇāmiva suvyaktaṃ mahatīnāṃ śubhārciṣām| prabhāvarṇaprasādāśca virejustatra yoṣitām
translation: तत्र there, योषिताम् of the young women, प्रभावर्णप्रसादाश्च lustre and grace, शुभार्चिषाम् releasing auspicious glow, महतीनाम् of the great, ताराणामिव like the stars, सुव्यक्तम् clearly, विरेजुः looked brilliant.
explanation: It was clear that the grace and lustre of those women looked brilliant like the lustre and grace of brilliant stars releasing an auspicious glow.

shloka_text: व्यावृत्तगुरुपीनस्रक्प्रकीर्णवरभूषणाः। पानव्यायामकालेषु निद्रापहृतचेतसः।।5.9.45।।
transliteration: vyāvṛttagurupīnasrakprakīrṇavarabhūṣaṇāḥ| pānavyāyāmakāleṣu nidrāpahṛtacetasaḥ
translation: पानव्यायामकालेषु drinking and sexual exercise, व्यावृत्तगुरुपीनस्रक्प्रकीर्णवरभूषणाः jewels scattered and garlands displaced, निद्रापहृतचेतसः minds dazed in slumber.
explanation: Garlands displaced and jewels scattered, they were drowsy due to drink and sexual exercise.

shloka_text: व्यावृत्ततिलकाः काश्चित्काश्चिदुद्भ्रन्तनूपुराः। पार्श्वे गलितहाराश्च काश्चित्परमयोषितः।।5.9.46।।
transliteration: vyāvṛttatilakāḥ kāścitkāścidudbhrantanūpurāḥ| pārśve galitahārāśca kāścitparamayoṣitaḥ
translation: कश्चित् a few, परमयोषितः other women, व्यावृत्ततिलकाः had vermilion mark (on the forehead) smudged, काश्चित् and a few, उद्भ्रान्तनूपुराः anklets let loose, काश्चित् a few, पार्श्वे on one side, गलितहाराश्च neckalces dislodged.
explanation: A few young women had their circular vermilion mark (on the forehead) smudged, some had their anklets loosened and a few had their necklaces.

shloka_text: मुक्ताहाराऽवृताश्चान्याः काश्चिद्विस्रस्तवाससः। व्याविद्धरशनादामाः किशोर्य इव वाहिताः।।5.9.47।।
transliteration: muktāhārā'vṛtāścānyāḥ kāścidvisrastavāsasaḥ| vyāviddharaśanādāmāḥ kiśorya iva vāhitāḥ
translation: अन्याः others, मुक्ताहारावृताः had broken pearl strings on girdle, काश्चित् some, विस्रस्तवाससः had their clothes slipped off, व्यावद्धिरशनादामाः waist belts snapped, वाहिताः fallen to rest, किशोर्यः इव like young mares.
explanation: Some had their strings of pearl broken, others had their clothes slipped off, and some had their waist belts snapped. They were like young mares fallen to rest after carrying heavy loads.

shloka_text: सुकुण्डलधराश्चान्या विच्छिन्नमृदितस्रजः। गजेन्द्रमृदिताः फुल्ला लता इव महावने।।5.9.48।।
transliteration: sukuṇḍaladharāścānyā vicchinnamṛditasrajaḥ| gajendramṛditāḥ phullā latā iva mahāvane
translation: सुकुण्डलधराः good eartops, अन्याः others, विच्छिन्नमृदितस्रजः with broken and crushed flower garlands, महावने in the dense forest, गजेन्द्रमृदिताः crushed by mighty elephants, फुल्लाः blooming, लताः इव like creepers.
explanation: With their good eartops broken and flower garlands crushed some looked like blooming creepers in a dense forest crushed by mighty elephants.

shloka_text: चन्द्रांशुकिरणाभाश्च हाराः कासांचिदुत्कटाः। हंसा इव बभुस्सुप्ताः स्तनमध्येषु योषिताम्।।5.9.49।।
transliteration: candrāṃśukiraṇābhāśca hārāḥ kāsāṃcidutkaṭāḥ| haṃsā iva babhussuptāḥ stanamadhyeṣu yoṣitām
translation: कासांचित् some, योषिताम् of young women, स्तनमध्येषु between their breasts, उत्कटाः large, चन्द्रांशुकिरणाभाश्च resembling the rays of the Moon, हाराः chains, सुप्ताः sleeping, हंसाः इव like the swans, बभुः appeared.
explanation: The pearl chains, large and shining like rays of the Moon in the space between the breasts looked like sleeping swans.

shloka_text: अपरासां च वैडूर्याः कादम्बा इव पक्षिणः। हेमसूत्राणि चान्यासां चक्रवाका इवाभवन्।।5.9.50।।
transliteration: aparāsāṃ ca vaiḍūryāḥ kādambā iva pakṣiṇaḥ| hemasūtrāṇi cānyāsāṃ cakravākā ivābhavan
translation: परासां च and for some, वैडूर्याः vaidurya, कादम्बाः kadamba, पक्षिणः इव like birds, अन्यासाम् of others, हेमसूत्राणि golden chains ,चक्रवाकाः इव like ruddy geese, अभवन् seemed.
explanation: The vaidurya worn by women (on the breasts) looked like Kadamba birds while the golden chains put on by some others appeared like ruddy geese.

shloka_text: हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णाश्चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः। आपगा इव ता रेजुर्जघनैः पुलिनैरिव।।5.9.51।।
transliteration: haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇāścakravākopaśobhitāḥ| āpagā iva tā rejurjaghanaiḥ pulinairiva
translation: पुलिनैरिव like river banks, जघनैः with hips, ताः those women, हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णाः crowded with swans and Karandava birds, चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः abounded with ruddy geese, आपगा इव like rivers, रेजुः were shining.
explanation: Their hips were like river banks crowded with swans, karandava and Chakravaka birds shining like rivers.

shloka_text: किङ्किणीजालसङ्कोशास्ता हैमविपुलाम्बुजाः। भावग्राहा यशस्तीराः सुप्ता नद्य इवाऽऽबभुः।।5.9.52।।
transliteration: kiṅkiṇījālasaṅkośāstā haimavipulāmbujāḥ| bhāvagrāhā yaśastīrāḥ suptā nadya ivā''babhuḥ
translation: किङ्किणीजालसङ्कोशाः tiny bells tied round the waist looking like buds, हैमविपुलाम्बुजाः bold golden ornaments looking like lotuses, भावग्राहाः their amorous gestures of love play like crocodiles, यशस्तीराः radiant beauty of silver banks, सुप्ताः sleeping, नद्यः इव resembled rivers, आबभुः appeared.
explanation: With their tiny bells round their girdle looking like buds, the bold golden ornaments like lotuses, their gestures of love like crocodiles and their radiant beauty like silver banks, the women looked like smoky rivers.

shloka_text: मृदुष्वङ्गेषु कासाञ्चित्कुचाग्रेषु च संस्थिताः। बभुर्वर्भूषणानीव शुभा भूषणराजयः।।5.9.53।।
transliteration: mṛduṣvaṅgeṣu kāsāñcitkucāgreṣu ca saṃsthitāḥ| babhurvarbhūṣaṇānīva śubhā bhūṣaṇarājayaḥ
translation: कासांचित् for some women, मृदुषु on their tender, अङ्गेषु limbs, कुचाग्रेषु च and on the nipples of breasts, संस्थिताः set, शुभाः beautiful, भूषणराजयः collections of ornaments, भूषणानीव like ornaments, बभूवुः appeared.
explanation: The beautiful imprints made by the (heavy) ornaments on the tender limbs, breasts and nipples of some women appeared like many ornaments.

shloka_text: अंशुकान्ताश्च कासाञ्चिन्मुखमारुतकम्पिताः। उपर्युपरि वक्त्राणां व्याधूयन्ते पुनः पुनः।।5.9.54।।
transliteration: aṃśukāntāśca kāsāñcinmukhamārutakampitāḥ| uparyupari vaktrāṇāṃ vyādhūyante punaḥ punaḥ
translation: कासाञ्चित् for some, मुखमारुतकम्पिताः shaken by the breath released by their mouth, अंशुकान्ताश्च the fringes of garments, वक्त्राणाम् on their faces, उपर्युपरि drawn, पुनः पुनः again and again, व्याधूयन्ते fluttered.
explanation: Shaken by the breath released from their mouths the fringes of the garments of some women were drawn towards their faces again and againfluttering.

shloka_text: ताः पताका इवोद्धूताः पत्नीनां रुचिरप्रभाः। नानावर्णसुवर्णानां वक्त्रमूलेषु रेजिरे।।5.9.55।।
transliteration: tāḥ patākā ivoddhūtāḥ patnīnāṃ ruciraprabhāḥ| nānāvarṇasuvarṇānāṃ vaktramūleṣu rejire
translation: नानावर्णसुवर्णानाम् of the women of different beautiful hues, पत्नीनाम् of the wives, वक्त्रमूलेषु on the edges of their faces, ताः those, रुचिरप्रभाः with beautiful glow, उध्दूताः raised, पताकाः इव like flags, रेजिरे shone.
explanation: The fringes of their garments glowing beautifully close to the faces of the wives (of Ravana) with different beautiful hues, shone splendid like flags.

shloka_text: ववल्गुश्चात्र कासांचित्कुण्डलानि शुभार्चिषाम्। मुखमारुतसंसर्गान्मन्दं मन्दं सुयोषिताम्।।5.9.56।।
transliteration: vavalguścātra kāsāṃcitkuṇḍalāni śubhārciṣām| mukhamārutasaṃsargānmandaṃ mandaṃ suyoṣitām
translation: शुभार्चिषाम् with auspicious radiance, कासाञ्चित् for some, योषिताम् women, कुण्डलानि eartops, अत्र here,मुखमारुतसंसर्गात् by the touch of their breath, मन्दं मन्दम् softly and gently, ववल्गुश्च mild sound of vibration.
explanation: The eartops of some women endowed with auspicious charm were swinging softly generating a gentle sound by the touch of their breath.

shloka_text: शर्कराऽसवगन्धैश्च प्रकृत्या सुरभिः सुखः। तासां वदननिश्वासस्सिषेवे रावणं तदा।।5.9.57।।
transliteration: śarkarā'savagandhaiśca prakṛtyā surabhiḥ sukhaḥ| tāsāṃ vadananiśvāsassiṣeve rāvaṇaṃ tadā
translation: तदा then, प्रकृत्या natural, शर्करासवगन्धैश्च the sweet smell of wine (made from sugarcane juice), सुरभिः fragrant, सुखः happy, तासाम् their, वदननिश्वासः breath from their mouth, रावणम् Ravana, सिषेवे served.
explanation: The sweet smell of wine emitted from their mouth and the natural fragrance of their breath was refreshing to Ravana  as if it was serving him at that time.

shloka_text: रावणाननशङ्काश्च काश्चिद्रावणयोषितः। मुखानि स्म सपत्नीनामुपाजिघ्रन्पुनः पुनः।।5.9.58।।
transliteration: rāvaṇānanaśaṅkāśca kāścidrāvaṇayoṣitaḥ| mukhāni sma sapatnīnāmupājighranpunaḥ punaḥ
translation: काश्चित् some, रावणयोषितः Ravana's wives, रावणाननशङ्काश्च assuming it to be Ravana's face, पुनः पुनः again and again, सपत्नीनाम् of their cowives, मुखानि mouths, उपाजिघ्रन् smelt.
explanation: Some women of Ravana (overcome by blind passion) smelt again and again the mouths of their cowives next to them  assuming it to be Ravana's.

shloka_text: अत्यर्थं सक्तमनसो रावणे ता वरस्त्रियः। अस्वतन्त्राः सपत्नीनां प्रियमेवाऽचरंस्तदा।।5.9.59।।
transliteration: atyarthaṃ saktamanaso rāvaṇe tā varastriyaḥ| asvatantrāḥ sapatnīnāṃ priyamevā'caraṃstadā
translation: रावणे at Ravana, अत्यर्थम् therefore, सक्तमनसः devoted to (Ravana), वरस्त्रियः beautiful women, अस्वतन्त्राः having no freedom, तदा then, सपत्नीनाम् of their cowives, प्रियमेव pleasing , आचरन् did.
explanation: Even though the beautiful wives (should have been angry with their cowives for smelling their mouths) they behaved pleasingly, having no freedom to act with Ravana

shloka_text: बाहूनुपनिधायान्याः पारिहार्यविभूषितान्। अंशुकानि च रम्याणि प्रमदास्तत्र शिश्यिरे।।5.9.60।।
transliteration: bāhūnupanidhāyānyāḥ pārihāryavibhūṣitān| aṃśukāni ca ramyāṇi pramadāstatra śiśyire
translation: अन्याः others, प्रमदाः women, पारिहार्यविभूषितान् laying aside their adornments, बाहून् arms, रम्याणि beautiful, अंशुकानि garment, उपनिधाय placing, तत्र there, शिश्यिरे slept.
explanation: Some women slept pillowed on their arms, laying aside their adornments and others had their garment under the head as pillows and lay in sleep.

shloka_text: अन्या वक्षसि चान्यस्यास्तस्याः काचित्पुनर्भुजम्। अपरा त्वङ्कमन्यस्यास्तस्याश्चाप्यपरा भुजौ।।5.9.61।।
transliteration: anyā vakṣasi cānyasyāstasyāḥ kācitpunarbhujam| aparā tvaṅkamanyasyāstasyāścāpyaparā bhujau
translation: अन्याः some women, अन्यस्याः on the other women's, वक्षसि on the chest, काचित् पुनः another again, तस्याः her, भुजम् arms अपरा तु another, अन्यस्याः on the others, अङ्कम् lap, अपरा another, तस्याः her, भुजौ on the arms.
explanation: Some women lay placing their arms on the breasts of the other while their own arms were used as pillow by another. One woman placed her head  on the lap of the other and slept.

shloka_text: ऊरुपार्श्वकटीपृष्ठमन्योन्यस्य समाश्रिताः। परस्परनिविष्टाङ्ग्यो मदस्नेहवशानुगाः।।5.9.62।।
transliteration: ūrupārśvakaṭīpṛṣṭhamanyonyasya samāśritāḥ| parasparaniviṣṭāṅgyo madasnehavaśānugāḥ
translation: मदस्नेहवशानुगाः given to intoxication and love, अन्योन्यस्य with one another, ऊरुपार्श्वकटीपृष्ठम् on thighs, side, hips and back on the lap of the other, समाश्रिताः had slept, परस्परनिविष्टाङ्ग्यः lay intertwined, one on the other.
explanation: Given to intoxication and sex, the women slept touching one another's thighs, sides, hips, back and lap of the other, with their limbs intertwined.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यभुजसूत्रेण स्त्रीमाला ग्रथिता हि सा। मालेव ग्रथिता सूत्रे शुशुभे मत्तषट्पदा।।5.9.63।।
transliteration: anyonyabhujasūtreṇa strīmālā grathitā hi sā| māleva grathitā sūtre śuśubhe mattaṣaṭpadā
translation: अन्योन्यभुजसूत्रेण shoulders of one another, ग्रथिता knit, सा that, स्त्रीमाला chain of women, सूत्रे in a thread, ग्रथिता intertwined, मत्तषट्पदा with drunken bees resting on it, मालेव like garland of flowers, शुशुभे shone.
explanation: Knit with the shoulders of one another like a garland of flowers intertwined with the tipsy bees resting the women shone.

shloka_text: लतानां माधवे मासि फुल्लानां वायुसेवनात्। अन्योन्य मालाग्रथितं संसक्तकुसुमोच्चयम्।।5.9.64।। व्यतिवेष्टितसुस्कन्धमन्योन्यभ्रमराकुलम्। आसीद्वनमिवोद्धूतं स्त्रीवनं रावणस्य तत्।।5.9.65।।
transliteration: latānāṃ mādhave māsi phullānāṃ vāyusevanāt| anyonya mālāgrathitaṃ saṃsaktakusumoccayam vyativeṣṭitasuskandhamanyonyabhramarākulam| āsīdvanamivoddhūtaṃ strīvanaṃ rāvaṇasya tat
translation: अन्योन्यमालाग्रथितम् linked to each other like a chain, संसक्तकुसुमोच्छयम् flowers in a string, व्यतिवेष्टितसुस्कन्धम् tangled together with strong joints, अन्योन्यभ्रमराकुलम् with bees swarming, रावणस्य Ravana's, तत् that, स्त्रीवनम् a garden of women, माधवे मासि in the month of spring, वायुसंसेवनात् by the blowing of the wind, फुल्लानाम् of the blooms, लतानाम् of the creepers, अन्योन्यमालाग्रथितम् one to one linked like a garland, अन्योन्यभ्रमराकुलम् like the swarm of bees, उद्धूतम् shaken, वनमिव like thickets, आसीत् appeared.
explanation: The women of Ravana appeared like a garden in spring. They were as if a cluster of creepers blossomed in spring due to the caresses of the breeze. They were knit together as one string forming a garland, flowers of one creeper striking the other. The joints of these creepers had grown strong when tangled together. Shaken by the breeze, the bees resting on one creeper would go to the other.

shloka_text: लतानां माधवे मासि फुल्लानां वायुसेवनात्। अन्योन्य मालाग्रथितं संसक्तकुसुमोच्चयम्।।5.9.64।। व्यतिवेष्टितसुस्कन्धमन्योन्यभ्रमराकुलम्। आसीद्वनमिवोद्धूतं स्त्रीवनं रावणस्य तत्।।5.9.65।।
transliteration: latānāṃ mādhave māsi phullānāṃ vāyusevanāt| anyonya mālāgrathitaṃ saṃsaktakusumoccayam vyativeṣṭitasuskandhamanyonyabhramarākulam| āsīdvanamivoddhūtaṃ strīvanaṃ rāvaṇasya tat
translation: अन्योन्यमालाग्रथितम् linked to each other like a chain, संसक्तकुसुमोच्छयम् flowers in a string, व्यतिवेष्टितसुस्कन्धम् tangled together with strong joints, अन्योन्यभ्रमराकुलम् with bees swarming, रावणस्य Ravana's, तत् that, स्त्रीवनम् a garden of women, माधवे मासि in the month of spring, वायुसंसेवनात् by the blowing of the wind, फुल्लानाम् of the blooms, लतानाम् of the creepers, अन्योन्यमालाग्रथितम् one to one linked like a garland, अन्योन्यभ्रमराकुलम् like the swarm of bees, उद्धूतम् shaken, वनमिव like thickets, आसीत् appeared.
explanation: The women of Ravana appeared like a garden in spring. They were as if a cluster of creepers blossomed in spring due to the caresses of the breeze. They were knit together as one string forming a garland, flowers of one creeper striking the other. The joints of these creepers had grown strong when tangled together. Shaken by the breeze, the bees resting on one creeper would go to the other.

shloka_text: उचितेष्वपि सुव्यक्तं न तासां योषितां तदा। विवेकः शक्य आधातुं भूषणाङ्गाम्बरस्रजाम्।।5.9.66।।
transliteration: uciteṣvapi suvyaktaṃ na tāsāṃ yoṣitāṃ tadā| vivekaḥ śakya ādhātuṃ bhūṣaṇāṅgāmbarasrajām
translation: तदा then, तासां योषिताम् of those women, भूषणाङ्गाम्बरस्रजाम् of ornaments, garments, limbs and garlands, विवेकः to distinguish, सुव्यक्तम् clearly, आधातुम् to place, उचितेष्वपि in right spots, न शक्यः not possible.
explanation: It was not possible to distinguish clearly between their jewels, limbs, garments and garlands and to place them in the right spots.

shloka_text: रावणे सुखसंविष्टे तास्त्रियो विविधप्रभाः। ज्वलन्तः काञ्चना दीपाः प्रैक्षन्तानिमिषा इव।।5.9.67।।
transliteration: rāvaṇe sukhasaṃviṣṭe tāstriyo vividhaprabhāḥ| jvalantaḥ kāñcanā dīpāḥ praikṣantānimiṣā iva
translation: रावणे when Ravana, सुखसंविष्टे was sleeping happily, विधप्रभाः gods of lights, ताः स्त्रियः those women, ज्वलन्तः glowing, काञ्चनाः दीपाः इव golden lampposts, अनिमिषाः without winking, प्रैक्षन्त इव gazed at him.
explanation: When Ravana was happily asleep, the gods of light burning on the gold lampposts gazed without winking as it were, at the women, whom they dare  not gaze for fear of waking Ravana.

shloka_text: राजर्षिपितृदैत्यानां गन्धर्वाणां च योषितः। राक्षसानां च याः कन्यास्तस्य कामवशं गताः।।5.9.68।।
transliteration: rājarṣipitṛdaityānāṃ gandharvāṇāṃ ca yoṣitaḥ| rākṣasānāṃ ca yāḥ kanyāstasya kāmavaśaṃ gatāḥ
translation: राजर्षिपितृदैत्यानाम् of royal sages, ancestral gods and demons, गन्धर्वाणाम् of gandharvas, योषितः women, राक्षसानाम् of ogres, याः कन्याः those girls, तस्य his, कामवशम्गताः they were infatuated with him.
explanation: The women halled from the families of royal sages, ancestral deities, daityas and demons who were infatuated with him.

shloka_text: युद्धकामेन ताः सर्वा रावणेन हृताः स्त्रियः। समदा मदनेनैव मोहिताः काश्चिदागताः।।5.9.69।।
transliteration: yuddhakāmena tāḥ sarvā rāvaṇena hṛtāḥ striyaḥ| samadā madanenaiva mohitāḥ kāścidāgatāḥ
translation: सर्वाः all, ताः स्त्रियः those women, युद्धकामेन on account of his love for war, रावणेन by Ravana, हृताः kidnapped, समदाः passionate ones, काश्चित् a few, मदनेन by lust, मोहिताः एव deluded, आगताः came.
explanation: Many were brought by Ravana as captives of war and some came on their own deluded by lust.

shloka_text: न तत्र काचित्प्रमदा प्रसह्य वीर्योपपन्नेन गुणेन लब्धा। न चान्यकामापि न चान्यपूर्वा विना वरार्हां जनकात्मजां ताम्।।5.9.70।।
transliteration: na tatra kācitpramadā prasahya vīryopapannena guṇena labdhā| na cānyakāmāpi na cānyapūrvā vinā varārhāṃ janakātmajāṃ tām
translation: वरार्हाम् revered, ताम् her, जनकात्मजां विना except Sita, तत्र there, काचित् प्रमदा any women, वीर्योपपन्नेन on account of his valour, प्रसह्य लब्धा obtained forcibly, न not, गुणेन by virtues, अन्यकामापि not in love with others, न च and not, अन्यपूर्वा च married by others earlier, न not.
explanation: Except Sita no other woman among them had been taken there by force. They were won only on account of his valour and virtues. None loved any one earlier and none was married to others.

shloka_text: न चाकुलीना न च हीनरूपा नादक्षिणा नानुपचारयुक्ता। भार्याभवत्तस्य न हीनसत्त्वा न चापि कान्तस्य न कामनीया।।5.9.71।।
transliteration: na cākulīnā na ca hīnarūpā nādakṣiṇā nānupacārayuktā| bhāryābhavattasya na hīnasattvā na cāpi kāntasya na kāmanīyā
translation: तस्य his, भार्या wife, अकुलीना lowbred, न च अभवत् did not become, हीनरूपा च without beauty, न not, अदक्षिणा unkind, न not, अनुपचारयुक्ता discourteous, न not, हीनसत्त्वा without strength, न not, कान्तस्य for the lover, न कामनीया च not loveable, न none.
explanation: None among them was born of a lowly family, nor lacked beauty, kindness, skill, strength or brightness. No one was not lovable to Ravana.

shloka_text: बभूव बुद्धिस्तु हरीश्वरस्य यदीदृशी राघवधर्मपत्नी। इमा यथा राक्षसराजभार्याः सुजातमस्येति हि साधुबुद्धेः।।5.9.72।।
transliteration: babhūva buddhistu harīśvarasya yadīdṛśī rāghavadharmapatnī| imā yathā rākṣasarājabhāryāḥ sujātamasyeti hi sādhubuddheḥ
translation: इमाः these, राक्षसराजभार्याः wives of the demon lord, यथा as, राघवधर्मपत्नी Rama's lawful wife, ईदृशी such a lady, अस्य his, सुजातम् born of good family, इति thus, साधुबुद्धेः of the wise, हरीश्वरस्य Hanuman's, बुद्धिस्तु thought also, बभूव was.
explanation: 'If the lawful wife of Rama born of a good family can be allowed to remain with Rama in the same way as the consorts of the lord of demons, how fortunate it would be, thought the wise lord of monkeys'.

shloka_text: पुनश्च सोऽचिन्तयादात्तरूपो ध्रुवं विशिष्टा गुणतो हि सीता। अथायमस्यां कृतवान्महात्मा लङ्केश्वरः कष्टमनार्यकर्म।।5.9.73।।
transliteration: punaśca so'cintayādāttarūpo dhruvaṃ viśiṣṭā guṇato hi sītā| athāyamasyāṃ kṛtavānmahātmā laṅkeśvaraḥ kaṣṭamanāryakarma
translation: सः he, आत्तरूपः assuming his true form, पुनश्च once again, अचिन्तयत् he thought, सीता Sita, ध्रुवम् surely, गुणतः by her virtues, विशिष्टा distinguished one, अथ now, महात्मा great, अयं लङ्केश्वरः that lord of Lanka, अस्याम् in her case, अनार्यम् an unfit act not befitting a noble one, कृतवान् did, कष्टम् alas.
explanation: Hanuman once again assuming his true form said to himself, 'Sita is surely a virtuous lady superior to and more distinguished than them all. Alas, this lord of Lanka committed an ignoble, act (by abducting her). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे नवमस्सर्गः। Thus ends the ninth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तत्र दिव्योपमं मुख्यं स्फाटिकं रत्नभूषितम्। अवेक्षमाणो हनुमान् ददर्श शयनासनम्।।5.10.1।। दान्तकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गैर्वैडूर्यैश्च वरासनैः। महार्हास्तरणोपेतैरुपपन्नं महाधनैः।।5.10.2।।
transliteration: tatra divyopamaṃ mukhyaṃ sphāṭikaṃ ratnabhūṣitam| avekṣamāṇo hanumān dadarśa śayanāsanam dāntakāñcanacitrāṅgairvaiḍūryaiśca varāsanaiḥ| mahārhāstaraṇopetairupapannaṃ mahādhanaiḥ
translation: तत्र there, आवेक्षमाणः while looking around, हनुमान् Hanuman, दिव्योपमम् fine, heavenly मुख्यम् foremost, स्फाटिकम् made with crystals, रत्नभूषितम् encrusted with gems, दान्तकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गैः inlaid with colourful ivory and gold, वैडूर्यैः with Vaidurya, महार्हास्तरणोपेतैः with exquisite coverings, महाधनैः rich, वरासनैः fine dais, उपेतम् endowed with, शयनासनम् couch, ददर्श observed.
explanation: Looking around, Hanuman noticed a bed chamber, with a heavenly dais on which he saw a couch encrusted with crystals, vaidurya, and inlaid with colourful ivory and gold. It had an exquisite rich covering.
comments: Hanuman chances upon Mandodari, wife of Ravana -- mistakes her for Sita on account of her beauty and charm.

shloka_text: तत्र दिव्योपमं मुख्यं स्फाटिकं रत्नभूषितम्। अवेक्षमाणो हनुमान् ददर्श शयनासनम्।।5.10.1।। दान्तकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गैर्वैडूर्यैश्च वरासनैः। महार्हास्तरणोपेतैरुपपन्नं महाधनैः।।5.10.2।।

translation: तत्र there, आवेक्षमाणः while looking around, हनुमान् Hanuman, दिव्योपमम् fine, heavenly मुख्यम् foremost, स्फाटिकम् made with crystals, रत्नभूषितम् encrusted with gems, दान्तकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गैः inlaid with colourful ivory and gold, वैडूर्यैः with Vaidurya, महार्हास्तरणोपेतैः with exquisite coverings, महाधनैः rich, वरासनैः fine dais, उपेतम् endowed with, शयनासनम् couch, ददर्श observed.
explanation: Looking around, Hanuman noticed a bed chamber, with a heavenly dais on which he saw a couch encrusted with crystals, vaidurya, and inlaid with colourful ivory and gold. It had an exquisite rich covering.
