translation: मयि me, संयुगे in a battle, रक्षोभिः by ogres, विशस्ते वा if I am killed, गृहीते वा or captured, रामस्य of Rama, कार्यसाधने to accomplish the task, अन्यम् another, सहायम् help, न पश्यामि I do not see.
explanation: "If I am killed in the combat or captured by the demons, I do not see another person who can help in accomplishing this task.

shloka_text: विमृशंश्च न पश्यामि यो हते मयि वानरः।।5.30.33।। शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं लङ्घयेत महोदधिम्।
transliteration: vimṛśaṃśca na paśyāmi yo hate mayi vānaraḥ śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ laṅghayeta mahodadhim|
translation: मयि when I am, हते killed, यः whosoever, वानरः vanara, शतयोजनविस्तीर्णम् extended over a distance of hundred yojanas, महोदधिम् the ocean, लङ्घयेत् can leap over, विमृशन् च even while reflecting carefully, न पश्यामि I cannot see.
explanation: "When I am killed here, I cannot see any other vanara who can leap over a hundred yojanas of the ocean (to reach this place).

shloka_text: कामं हन्तुं समर्थोऽस्मि सहस्राण्यपि रक्षसाम्।।5.30.34।। न तु शक्ष्यामि सम्प्राप्तुं परं पारं महोदधेः।
transliteration: kāmaṃ hantuṃ samartho'smi sahasrāṇyapi rakṣasām na tu śakṣyāmi samprāptuṃ paraṃ pāraṃ mahodadheḥ|
translation: रक्षसाम् of demons, सहस्राण्यपि even thousands of them, हन्तुम् to kill, समर्थः capable, अस्मि कामम् I am surely, तु also, महोदधेः of the ocean, परं पारम् to cross over, सम्प्राप्तुम् to reach, न शक्ष्यामि it may not be possible.
explanation: "I may be capable of killing even thousands of demons but thereafter (thoroughly exhausted) reach the other side of the ocean.

shloka_text: असत्यानि च युद्धानि संशयो मे न रोचते।।5.30.35।। कश्च निस्संशयं कार्यं कुर्यात्प्राज्ञः ससंशयम्।
transliteration: asatyāni ca yuddhāni saṃśayo me na rocate kaśca nissaṃśayaṃ kāryaṃ kuryātprājñaḥ sasaṃśayam|
translation: युद्धानि battles, असत्यानि च not true, संशयः doubtful, मे I, न रोचते it does not please me, कः who, प्राज्ञः wise man, निःसंशयम् without any doubt, कार्यम् task, ससंशयम् without any doubt, कुर्यात् will take up.
explanation: "Battles, no doubt, are unpredictable. Which wise man with a sound intellect will take up a doubtful work unhesitatingly?

shloka_text: प्राणत्यागश्च वैदेह्या भवेदनभिभाषणे।।5.30.36।। एष दोषो महान्हि स्यान्मम सीताभिभाषणे।
transliteration: prāṇatyāgaśca vaidehyā bhavedanabhibhāṣaṇe eṣa doṣo mahānhi syānmama sītābhibhāṣaṇe|
translation: अनभिभाषणे if I do not speak, वैदेह्याः of Vaidehi, प्राणत्यागश्च abandonement of life, भवेत् may be, सीताभिभाषणे on talking to Sita, मम to me, एषः such, महान् great, दोषः drawback, स्यात् will be.
explanation: "If I talk to Vaidehi it will be a great mistake on my part.If I do not speak to Vaidehi she may give up her life.

shloka_text: भूताश्चार्था विनश्यन्ति देशकालविरोधिताः।।5.30.37।। विक्लबं दूतमासाद्य तमः सूर्योदये यथा।
transliteration: bhūtāścārthā vinaśyanti deśakālavirodhitāḥ viklabaṃ dūtamāsādya tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā|
translation: विक्लबम् a confused person, दूतम् messenger, आसाद्य by appointing, भूताः even sure ones, अर्थाः missions, देशकालविरोधिताः if place and time are not propitious, सूर्योदये at Sunrise, तमः यथा like the darkness, विनश्यन्ति will be destroyed.
explanation: "Even well planned diplomatic missions fail like darkness dispelled at Sunrise if the messenger is confused and if the place and time are not propitious for them.

shloka_text: अर्थानर्थान्तरे बुद्धिनिश्चितापि न शोभते।।5.30.38।। घातयन्ति हि कार्याणि दूताः पण्डितमानिनः।
transliteration: arthānarthāntare buddhiniścitāpi na śobhate ghātayanti hi kāryāṇi dūtāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ|
translation: अर्थानर्थान्तरे swinging from a course of action or an action leading to calamity, बुद्धि intelligence, निश्चितापि though decided, न शोभते not proper, पण्डितमानिनः selfstyled scholars, दूताः messengers, कार्याणि their missions, घातयन्ति हि will be destroyed.
explanation: "Swinging from a course of action or an action leading to calamity is not proper. Messengers who assume that they are scholars (blinded by ego) destroy their mission.

shloka_text: न विनश्येत्कथं कार्यं वैक्लब्यं न कथं भवेत्।।5.30.39।। लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य कथं नु न वृथा भवेत्।
transliteration: na vinaśyetkathaṃ kāryaṃ vaiklabyaṃ na kathaṃ bhavet laṅghanaṃ ca samudrasya kathaṃ nu na vṛthā bhavet|
translation: कार्यम् task, कथम् how, न विनश्येत् may not be spoilt, वैक्लब्यम् failure, कथम् how, न भवेत् not be allowed to take place, समुद्रस्य ocean's, लङ्घनं च crossing, कथं नु how indeed, वृथा wasteful, न भवेत् not to be.
explanation: "How can the mission succeed? How can failure of mission be avoided? How can the crossing of the great ocean be not wasted?"

shloka_text: कथं नु खलु वाक्यं मे शृणुयान्नोद्विजेत वा। इति सञ्चिन्त्य हनुमांश्चकार मतिमान्मतिम्।।5.30.40।।
transliteration: kathaṃ nu khalu vākyaṃ me śṛṇuyānnodvijeta vā| iti sañcintya hanumāṃścakāra matimānmatim
translation: मे वाक्यम् my words, कथं नु how to, शृणुयायात् she may listen, न उद्विजेत वा and not get agitated, इति thus, सञ्चिन्त्य reflecting, मतिमान् wise, हनुमान् Hanuman, मतिम् in his mind, चकार exercised.
explanation: Wise Hanuman came to a decision after reflecting in his mind about how not to create fear in Sita (while communicating with her.)

shloka_text: राममक्लिष्टकर्माणं सुबन्धुमनुकीर्तयन्।।5.30.41।। नैनामुद्वेजयिष्यामि तद्बन्धुगतमानसाम्।
transliteration: rāmamakliṣṭakarmāṇaṃ subandhumanukīrtayan naināmudvejayiṣyāmi tadbandhugatamānasām|
translation: अक्लिष्टकर्माणम् one who is judicious in action, सुबन्धुम् very dear to her, रामम् Rama, अनुकीर्तयन् by praising him, तद्बन्धुगतमानसाम् since her mind is absorbed in him, एनाम् her, नोद्वेजयिष्यामि I will not create fear.
explanation: "By praising Rama who is very dear, who is judicious in action and in whom her mind is absorbed, I will not create fear.

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकूणां वरिष्ठस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः।।5.30.42।। शुभानि धर्मयुक्तानि वचनानि समर्पयन्। श्रावयिष्यामि सर्वाणि मधुरां प्रब्रुवन् गिरम्।।5.30.43।। श्रद्धास्यति यथाहीयं तथा सर्वं समादधे।
transliteration: ikṣvākūṇāṃ variṣṭhasya rāmasya viditātmanaḥ śubhāni dharmayuktāni vacanāni samarpayan| śrāvayiṣyāmi sarvāṇi madhurāṃ prabruvan giram śraddhāsyati yathāhīyaṃ tathā sarvaṃ samādadhe|
translation: इक्ष्वाकूणाम् in Ikshvaku race, वरिष्ठस्य of the esteemed person, विदितात्मनः of the knower of the self, रामस्य Rama's, शुभानि auspicious, वचनानि words, समर्पयन् by offering, मधुराम् sweet, गिरम् word, प्रब्रुवन् while uttering, सर्वाणि everything, श्रावयिष्यामि will make her listen, इयम् this, यथा as, श्रद्धास्यति will trust me, सर्वम् everything, समाददे I will present.
explanation: "I shall present in auspicious words the esteemed Rama of Ikshvaku family who is a knower of self and make her listen to everything in such a sweet manner that she will trust me.

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकूणां वरिष्ठस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः।।5.30.42।। शुभानि धर्मयुक्तानि वचनानि समर्पयन्। श्रावयिष्यामि सर्वाणि मधुरां प्रब्रुवन् गिरम्।।5.30.43।। श्रद्धास्यति यथाहीयं तथा सर्वं समादधे।
transliteration: ikṣvākūṇāṃ variṣṭhasya rāmasya viditātmanaḥ śubhāni dharmayuktāni vacanāni samarpayan| śrāvayiṣyāmi sarvāṇi madhurāṃ prabruvan giram śraddhāsyati yathāhīyaṃ tathā sarvaṃ samādadhe|
translation: इक्ष्वाकूणाम् in Ikshvaku race, वरिष्ठस्य of the esteemed person, विदितात्मनः of the knower of the self, रामस्य Rama's, शुभानि auspicious, वचनानि words, समर्पयन् by offering, मधुराम् sweet, गिरम् word, प्रब्रुवन् while uttering, सर्वाणि everything, श्रावयिष्यामि will make her listen, इयम् this, यथा as, श्रद्धास्यति will trust me, सर्वम् everything, समाददे I will present.
explanation: "I shall present in auspicious words the esteemed Rama of Ikshvaku family who is a knower of self and make her listen to everything in such a sweet manner that she will trust me.

shloka_text: इति स बहुविधं महानुभावो जगतिपतेः प्रमदामवेक्षमाणः। मधुरमवितथं जगाद वाक्यं द्रुमविटपान्तरमास्थितो हनूमान्।।5.30.44।।
transliteration: iti sa bahuvidhaṃ mahānubhāvo jagatipateḥ pramadāmavekṣamāṇaḥ| madhuramavitathaṃ jagāda vākyaṃ drumaviṭapāntaramāsthito hanūmān
translation: महानुभावः magnanimous, सः हनूमान् that Hanuman, द्रुमविटपान्तरम् behind the branch of the tree, आस्थितः seated, जगतिपतेः of the lord of the universe, प्रमदाम् wife, अवेक्षमाणः seeing, बहुविधम् in many ways, अवितथम् faithful, वाक्यम् words, इति thus, जगाद spoke
explanation: Highsouled Hanuman seated on the branch of the tree without being seen began to speak faithfully in praise of the lord of the universe in many ways while looking at her. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtieth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवं बहुविधां चिन्तां चिन्तयित्वा महाकपिः। संश्रवे मधुरं वाक्यं वैदेह्या व्याजहार ह।।5.31.1।।
transliteration: evaṃ bahuvidhāṃ cintāṃ cintayitvā mahākapiḥ| saṃśrave madhuraṃ vākyaṃ vaidehyā vyājahāra ha
translation: महाकपिः great vanara, एवम् thus, बहुविधाम् in several ways, चिन्ताम् thought, चिन्तयित्वा deliberating in his mind, वैदेह्याः Vaidehi's, संश्रवे hearing, मधुरम् sweet, वाक्यम् words, व्याजहार ह  spoke.
explanation: After deliberating in several ways the great Hanuman spoke these sweet words to Vaidehi:
comments: Hanuman sings the story of glory of Rama within Sita's hearing.

shloka_text: राजा दशरथो नाम रथकुञ्जरवाजिमान्। पुण्यशीलो महाकीर्तिरिक्ष्वाकूणां महायशाः।।5.31.2।।
transliteration: rājā daśaratho nāma rathakuñjaravājimān| puṇyaśīlo mahākīrtirikṣvākūṇāṃ mahāyaśāḥ
translation: रथकुञ्जरवाजिमान् with chariots, elephants and horses, पुण्यशीलः foremost in merits, महाकीर्तिः renowned, इक्ष्वाकूणाम् in Ikshvaku race, महायशाः illustrious, दशरथो नाम called Dasaratha, राजा king.
explanation: "There was an illustrious king called Dasaratha in Ikshvaku race, a master of chariots, elephants and horses. He was highly meritorious and renowned.

shloka_text: राजर्षीणां गुणश्रेष्ठस्तपसा चर्षिभि स्समः। चक्रवर्तिकुले जातः पुरन्दरसमो बले।।5.31.3।।
transliteration: rājarṣīṇāṃ guṇaśreṣṭhastapasā carṣibhi ssamaḥ| cakravartikule jātaḥ purandarasamo bale
translation: राजर्षीणाम् among sagelike kings, गुणश्रेष्ठः most virtuous one, तपसा in austerity, ऋषिभिः with sages, समः equal, चक्रवर्तिकुले in a dynasty of emperors, जातः born, बले in might, पुरन्दरसमः crusher of citadels like Indra.
explanation: "He was the most virtuous among royal sages, equal to sages in austerity, born in the race of emperors and equal to Indra in might.

shloka_text: अहिंसारतिरक्षुद्रो घृणी सत्यपराक्रमः। मुख्यश्चेक्ष्वाकुवंशस्य लक्ष्मीवान् लक्ष्मिवर्धनः।।5.31.4।।
transliteration: ahiṃsāratirakṣudro ghṛṇī satyaparākramaḥ| mukhyaścekṣvākuvaṃśasya lakṣmīvān lakṣmivardhanaḥ
translation: अहिंसारतिः committed to nonviolence, अक्षुद्रः magnanimous, घृणी compassionate, सत्यपराक्रमः one whose strength truth, इक्ष्वाकुवंशस्य of Ikshvaku family, मुख्यश्च chief, लक्ष्मीवान् prosperous, लक्ष्मिवर्धनः increaser of riches.
explanation: "He was committed to nonviolence, magnanimous, compassionate and one whose strength was truth. He was not only a prosperous king of Ikshvaku family but also a promoter of prosperity of others too.

shloka_text: पार्थिवव्यञ्जनैर्युक्तः पृथुश्रीः पार्थिवर्षभः। पृथिव्यां चतुरन्तायां विश्रुतस्सुखदस्सुखी।।5.31.5।।
transliteration: pārthivavyañjanairyuktaḥ pṛthuśrīḥ pārthivarṣabhaḥ| pṛthivyāṃ caturantāyāṃ viśrutassukhadassukhī
translation: पार्थिवव्यञ्जनैः with signs of kingship, युक्तः endowed, पृथुश्रीः with vast wealth, पार्थिवर्षभः a bull among rulers, चतुरन्तायाम् surrounded by the sea, पृथिव्याम् on the earth, विश्रुतः well known, सुखदः provider of happiness (to people), सुखी happy man.
explanation: "Endowed with signs of kingship and vast wealth, he was a bull among rulers of the vast earth, surrounded by the sea. A happy king himself, he was wellknown as a provider of happiness.

shloka_text: तस्य पुत्रः प्रियो ज्येष्ठस्ताराधिपनिभाननः। रामो नाम विशेषज्ञः श्रेष्ठ स्सर्वधनुष्मताम्।।5.31.6।।
transliteration: tasya putraḥ priyo jyeṣṭhastārādhipanibhānanaḥ| rāmo nāma viśeṣajñaḥ śreṣṭha ssarvadhanuṣmatām
translation: तस्य his, प्रियः beloved, ताराधिपनिभाननः of Moon like face, विशेषज्ञः scholar of all knowledge, सर्वधनुष्मताम् among all those wielders of bow, श्रेष्ठः foremost, रामो नाम called Rama, ज्येष्ठः पुत्रः eldest son.
explanation: "His beloved eldest son Rama, whose countenance is like the full moon, is a scholar of all branches of knowledge and is foremost among the bowmen on earth.

shloka_text: रक्षिता स्वस्य धर्मस्य स्वजनस्य च रक्षिता। रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य धर्मस्य च परन्तपः।।5.31.7।।
transliteration: rakṣitā svasya dharmasya svajanasya ca rakṣitā| rakṣitā jīvalokasya dharmasya ca parantapaḥ
translation: परन्तपः scourage of foes, स्वस्य his, धर्मस्य of righteousness, रक्षिता a  protector, स्वजनस्य of his kins, रक्षिता a protector, जीवलोकस्य of all living creatures, धर्मस्य च and of righteousness, रक्षिता protector.
explanation: "The scourage of enemies, he is a protector of righteousness and of his kins and all living creatures. He is an embodiment of righteousness.

shloka_text: तस्य सत्याभिसन्धस्य वृद्धस्य वचनात्पितुः। सभार्यस्सह च भ्रात्रा वीरः प्रव्राजितो वनम्।।5.31.8।।
transliteration: tasya satyābhisandhasya vṛddhasya vacanātpituḥ| sabhāryassaha ca bhrātrā vīraḥ pravrājito vanam
translation: सत्याभिसन्धस्य ever steadfast in truth, वृद्धस्य of the aged, पितुः father, तस्य his, वचनात्  honouring the word, वीरः hero, सभार्यः along with wife, सह च भ्रात्रा and accompanied by his brother, वनम् forest, प्रव्राजितः went as a wanderer.
explanation: "Honouring the word of his aged father who was ever steadfast in truth, Rama left for the forest along with his wife and brother.

shloka_text: तेन तत्र महारण्ये मृगयां परिधावता। राक्षसा निहताश्शूरा बहवः कामरूपिणः।।5.31.9।।
transliteration: tena tatra mahāraṇye mṛgayāṃ paridhāvatā| rākṣasā nihatāśśūrā bahavaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
translation: तत्र there, महारण्ये in the thick forest, मृगयाम् hunting, परिधावता while chasing, तेन by him, शूराः warriors, कामरूपिणः those who can assume any form at their will, बहवः many, राक्षसाः demons, निहताः killed.
explanation: "In the deep forest he went round hunting animals and killing the demon warriors who assumed any form at their free will.

shloka_text: जनस्थानवधं श्रुत्वा हतौ च खरदूषणौ। ततस्त्वमर्षापहृता जानकी रावणेन तु।।5.31.10।। वञ्चयित्वा वने रामं मृगरूपेण मायया।
transliteration: janasthānavadhaṃ śrutvā hatau ca kharadūṣaṇau| tatastvamarṣāpahṛtā jānakī rāvaṇena tu vañcayitvā vane rāmaṃ mṛgarūpeṇa māyayā|
translation: ततः then, जनस्थानवधम् killing at Janasthana, हतौ killed, खरदूषणौ च Khara and Dooshana, श्रुत्वा having heard, वने in the forest, रामम्  Rama, मृगरूपेण in the form of a deer, मायया by creating illusion, वञ्चयित्वा having deceived, रावणेन by Ravana, जानकी Janaki, अमर्षापहृता abducted out of anger.
explanation: "Ravana having heard about the killing of all demons at Janasthana including Khara and Dooshana in the forest, deceived Rama in the guise of a deer and abducted Janaki in anger.

shloka_text: स मार्गमाणस्तां देवीं रामस्सीतामनिन्दिताम्।।5.31.11।। आससाद वने मित्रं सुग्रीवं नाम वानरम्।
transliteration: sa mārgamāṇastāṃ devīṃ rāmassītāmaninditām āsasāda vane mitraṃ sugrīvaṃ nāma vānaram|
translation: सः रामः that Rama, अनिन्दिताम् sinless, देवीम् goddesslike lady, तां सीताम् that Sita, मार्गमाणः looking for, वने in the forest, सुग्रीवं नाम called Sugriva, वानरम् monkey, मित्रम् friendship, आससाद met.
explanation: "While looking for the goddesslike lady, the sinless Sita in the forest, Rama met a monkey called Sugriva and made friendship with him

shloka_text: तत स्स वालिनं हत्वा रामः परपुरञ्जयः।।5.31.12।। प्रायच्छत्कपिराज्यं तत्सुग्रीवाय महाबलः।
transliteration: tata ssa vālinaṃ hatvā rāmaḥ parapurañjayaḥ prāyacchatkapirājyaṃ tatsugrīvāya mahābalaḥ|
translation: ततः then, परपुरञ्जयः one who can win over enemy forts, महाबलः powerful, सः रामः that Rama, वालिनम् that Vali, हत्वा having killed, तत् that, कपिराज्यम् kingdom of the monkeys, सुग्रीवाय to Sugriva, प्रायच्छत् offered.
explanation: "Rama, a powerful king, who can win enemy forts killed Vali and offered the monkey kingdom to Sugriva.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवेणापि सन्दिष्टा हरयः कामरूपिणः।।5.31.13।। दिक्षु सर्वासु तां देवीं विचिन्वन्ति सहस्रशः।
transliteration: sugrīveṇāpi sandiṣṭā harayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ dikṣu sarvāsu tāṃ devīṃ vicinvanti sahasraśaḥ|
translation: सुग्रीवेण by Sugriva, सन्दिष्टाः received orders, कामरूपिणः those who can assume any form, कपयः monkeys, सहस्रशः in thousands, सर्वासु all over, दिक्षु in directions, तां देवीम् that divine queen, विचिन्वन्ति are searching.
explanation: "Having received Sugriva's orders thousands of monkeys who can assume any form went searching for that divine queen in all directions.

shloka_text: अहं सम्पातिवचनाच्छतयोजनमायतम्।।5.31.14।। अस्या हेतोर्विशालाक्ष्याः सागरं वेगवान्प्लुतः।
transliteration: ahaṃ sampātivacanācchatayojanamāyatam asyā hetorviśālākṣyāḥ sāgaraṃ vegavānplutaḥ|
translation: अहम् I am, सम्पातिवचनात् by the words of Sampati, वेगवान् swiftly, अस्याः for her, विशालाक्ष्याः largeeyed, हेतोः for the cause, शतयोजनम् a hundred yojanas, आयतम् wide, सागरम् ocean, प्लुतः leaped.
explanation: "On hearing the words of Sampati I leaped the wide ocean swiftly crossing a hundred yojanas in quest of the largeeyed Sita.

shloka_text: यथारूपां यथावर्णां यथालक्ष्मीवतीं च निश्चिताम्।।5.31.15।। अश्रौषं राघवस्याहं सेयमासादिता मया।
transliteration: yathārūpāṃ yathāvarṇāṃ yathālakṣmīvatīṃ ca niścitām aśrauṣaṃ rāghavasyāhaṃ seyamāsāditā mayā|
translation: अहम् I, राघवस्य Raghava's, ताम् her, यथारूपाम् of a similar form, यथावर्णाम् of the same complexion, यथालक्ष्मी of similar glow, अश्रौषम् I heard, सा she, इयम् the same one, मया by me, आसादिता has been found.
explanation: "Surely I have seen here a lady of similar body, of similar complexion, of similar glow and beauty as described by Rama".

shloka_text: विररामैवमुक्त्वासौ वाचं वानरपुङ्गवः।।5.31.16।। जानकी चापि तच्छ्रुत्वा परं विस्मयमागता।
transliteration: virarāmaivamuktvāsau vācaṃ vānarapuṅgavaḥ jānakī cāpi tacchrutvā paraṃ vismayamāgatā|
translation: असौ he, वानरपुङ्गवः chief of the vanaras, एवम् in that way, वाचम् word, उक्त्वा having spoken, विरराम stopped, जानकी चापि even Janaki, तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, परम् great, विस्मयम् wonder, आगता felt.
explanation: Having spoken thus, the great vanara stopped speaking after that. Janaki was wonderstruck by the words of the vanara.

shloka_text: ततस्सा वक्रकेशान्ता सुकेशी केशसंवृतम्।।5.31.17।। उन्नम्य वदनं भीरुश्शिंशुपावृक्षमैक्षत।
transliteration: tatassā vakrakeśāntā sukeśī keśasaṃvṛtam unnamya vadanaṃ bhīruśśiṃśupāvṛkṣamaikṣata|
translation: ततः then, वक्रकेशान्ता one who had hair curled up at the ends, भीरुः (timid) lady, क्लेशसंवृतम् covered with hanging hair, सा she, वदनम् face, उन्नम्य by raising, शिंशुपावृक्षम् Simsupa tree, ऐक्षत looked up.
explanation: Then Sita looked up at the Simsupa tree timidly, her face covered with beautiful curly hair.

shloka_text: निशम्य सीता वचनं कपेश्च दिशश्च सर्वाः प्रदिशश्च वीक्ष्य। स्वयं प्रहर्षं परमं जगाम सर्वात्मना राममनुस्मरन्ती ।।5.31.18।।
transliteration: niśamya sītā vacanaṃ kapeśca diśaśca sarvāḥ pradiśaśca vīkṣya| svayaṃ praharṣaṃ paramaṃ jagāma sarvātmanā rāmamanusmarantī
translation: सीता Sita, कपेः Hanuman's, वचनम् word, निशम्य after hearing, सर्वाः all, दिशश्च directions, प्रदिशश्च and quarters, वीक्ष्य after observing, स्वयम् herself, सर्वात्मना self of all, रामम् Rama, अनुस्मरन्ती contemplating on, परमम् supreme, प्रहर्षम् joy, जगाम experienced.
explanation: On hearing Hanuman's words Sita looked at all directions and quarters while quietly contemplating on Rama, the self of all and experienced supreme joy.

shloka_text: सा तिर्यगूर्ध्वं च तथाप्यधस्तान्निरीक्षमाणा तमचिन्त्यबुद्धिम्। ददर्श पिङ्गाधिपतेरमात्यं वातात्मजं सूर्यमिवोदयस्थम्।।5.31.19।।
transliteration: sā tiryagūrdhvaṃ ca tathāpyadhastānnirīkṣamāṇā tamacintyabuddhim| dadarśa piṅgādhipateramātyaṃ vātātmajaṃ sūryamivodayastham
translation: सा she, तिर्यक् obliquely, ऊर्ध्वं च vertically, तथापि so also, अथस्तात् downward, निरीक्षमाणा observing, अचिन्त्यबुद्धिम् of unimaginable intelligence, पिङ्गाधिपतेः of king of monkeys, अमात्यम् minister, उदयस्थम् rising, सूर्यमिव like Sun, तं वातात्मजम् that son of the Windgod, ददर्श saw.
explanation: She looked obliquely, up, and down and saw Hanuman of unimaginable intelligence, the minister of the monkey lord, son of the Windgod, who looked like the rising Sun. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकत्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyfirst sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततश्शाखान्तरे लीनं दृष्ट्वा चलितमानसा। वेष्टितार्जुनवस्त्रं तं विद्युत्सङ्घातपिङ्गलम्।।5.32.1।।
transliteration: tataśśākhāntare līnaṃ dṛṣṭvā calitamānasā| veṣṭitārjunavastraṃ taṃ vidyutsaṅghātapiṅgalam
translation: ततः then, शाखान्तरे in between the branches, लीनम् hidden, वेष्टितार्जुनवस्त्रम्  clad in white, विद्युत्सङ्घातपिङ्गलम् of tawny complexion like a cluster of lightnings, तम् him, दृष्ट्वा  seeing, चलितमानसा got perplexed.
explanation: Sita got perplexed on seeing him (Hanuman), who was tawny in complexion and looked like a cluster of lightnings, clad in white  and hidden in between the branches.
comments: Sita's conjucture

shloka_text: सा ददर्श कपिं तत्र प्रश्रितं प्रियवादिनम्। फुल्लाशोकोत्कराभासं तप्तचामीकरेक्षणम्।।5.32.2।।
transliteration: sā dadarśa kapiṃ tatra praśritaṃ priyavādinam| phullāśokotkarābhāsaṃ taptacāmīkarekṣaṇam
translation: सा she, तत्र there, फुल्लाशोकोत्कराभासम् bright like fullyblossomed Ashoka flower, तप्तचामीकरेक्षणम् whose eyes are bright like molten gold, प्रश्रितम् was readily approaching, प्रियवादिनम् one who spoke softly and pleasingly, कपिम् monkey, ददर्श saw.
explanation: There (on the tree) she noticed a monkey like a cluster of fully blossomed Ashoka flower, shining bright, whose eyes were glowing like pure molten gold, speaking softly and pleasingly.

shloka_text: मैथिली चिन्तयामास विस्मयं परमं गता। अहो भीममिदं रूपं वानरस्य दुरासदम्।।5.32.3।। दुर्निरीक्षमिति ज्ञात्वा पुनरेव मुमोह सा।
transliteration: maithilī cintayāmāsa vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatā| aho bhīmamidaṃ rūpaṃ vānarasya durāsadam durnirīkṣamiti jñātvā punareva mumoha sā|
translation: मैथिली Mythili, परमम् supreme, विस्मयम् astonishment, गता felt, चिन्तयामास began thinking, अहो Oh, वानरस्य vanara's, दुरासदम् inaccessible, इदम् this, रूपम् appearance, भीमम् frightening, दुर्निरीक्षम् impossible to look at, इति thus, ज्ञात्वा thinking, सा she, पुनरेव once again, मुमोह fainted.
explanation: Astonisted Mythili began thinking. 'Oh this vanara's appearance is frightening. He is terrible to look at. He is inaccessible'. Thinking over this again and again, she fainted.

shloka_text: विललाप भृशं सीता करुणं भयमोहिता।।5.32.4।। रामरामेति दुःखार्ता लक्ष्मणेति च भामिनी। रुरोद बहुधा सीता मन्दं मन्दस्वरा सती।।5.32.5।।
transliteration: vilalāpa bhṛśaṃ sītā karuṇaṃ bhayamohitā rāmarāmeti duḥkhārtā lakṣmaṇeti ca bhāminī| ruroda bahudhā sītā mandaṃ mandasvarā satī
translation: भामिनी a noble lady, सीता Sita, भयमोहिता overcome with fear, दुःखार्ता sorrowful, रामरामेति saying Rama, Rama, लक्ष्मणेति च and Lakshmana also, भृशम् repeatedly, करुणम् pitiably, विललाप cried, सीता Sita, मन्दस्वरा सती in low voice, बहुधा many ways, रुरोद cried.
explanation: Overcome with sorrow and fear, noble Sita sobbed pitiably muttering repeatedly. 'O Rama, O Rama, O Lakshmana'.

shloka_text: विललाप भृशं सीता करुणं भयमोहिता।।5.32.4।। रामरामेति दुःखार्ता लक्ष्मणेति च भामिनी। रुरोद बहुधा सीता मन्दं मन्दस्वरा सती।।5.32.5।।
transliteration: vilalāpa bhṛśaṃ sītā karuṇaṃ bhayamohitā rāmarāmeti duḥkhārtā lakṣmaṇeti ca bhāminī| ruroda bahudhā sītā mandaṃ mandasvarā satī
translation: भामिनी a noble lady, सीता Sita, भयमोहिता overcome with fear, दुःखार्ता sorrowful, रामरामेति saying Rama, Rama, लक्ष्मणेति च and Lakshmana also, भृशम् repeatedly, करुणम् pitiably, विललाप cried, सीता Sita, मन्दस्वरा सती in low voice, बहुधा many ways, रुरोद cried.
explanation: Overcome with sorrow and fear, noble Sita sobbed pitiably muttering repeatedly. 'O Rama, O Rama, O Lakshmana'.

shloka_text: सा तं दृष्ट्वा हरिश्रेष्ठं विनीतवदुपस्थितम्। मैथिली चिन्तयामास स्वप्नोऽयमिति भामिनी।।5.32.6।।
transliteration: sā taṃ dṛṣṭvā hariśreṣṭhaṃ vinītavadupasthitam| maithilī cintayāmāsa svapno'yamiti bhāminī
translation: भामिनी noble lady, सा मैथिली that Maithili, विनीतवत् humbly, उपस्थितम् stood near, तम् him, हरिश्रेष्ठम् best of vanaras, दृष्ट्वा after seeing, अयम् this, स्वप्नः dream, इति thus, चिन्तयामास began thinking.
explanation: Noble Sita, seeing the best of vanaras who stood near humbly, began reflecting 'Is this a dream'?

shloka_text: सा वीक्षमाणा पृथुभुग्नवक्त्रं शाखामृगेन्द्रस्य यथोक्तकारम्। ददर्श पिङ्गाधिपते रमात्यं वातात्मजं बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठम्।।5.32.7।।
transliteration: sā vīkṣamāṇā pṛthubhugnavaktraṃ śākhāmṛgendrasya yathoktakāram| dadarśa piṅgādhipate ramātyaṃ vātātmajaṃ buddhimatāṃ variṣṭham
translation: सा she, वीक्षमाणा was looking here and there, पृथुभुग्नवक्त्रम् with a large curved face, शाखामृगेन्द्रस्य of the lord of monkeys, यथोक्तकारम् obedient servant, पिङ्गाधिपते of the king of monkeys, अमात्यम् minister, बुद्धिमताम् among the intelligent, वरिष्ठम् foremost, वातात्मजम् son of the windgod, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Looking here and there, she saw a monkey with a large, curved face, an obedient servant and a minister of the monkeylord, the foremost among the intelligentia and the son of the Windgod.

shloka_text: सा तं समीक्ष्यैव भृशं विसंज्ञा गतासुकल्पेन बभूव सीता। चिरेण संज्ञां प्रतिलभ्य भूयो विचिन्तयामास विशालनेत्रा।।5.32.8।।
transliteration: sā taṃ samīkṣyaiva bhṛśaṃ visaṃjñā gatāsukalpena babhūva sītā| cireṇa saṃjñāṃ pratilabhya bhūyo vicintayāmāsa viśālanetrā
translation: सा सीता that Sita, तम् him, समीक्ष्यैव after looking at, भृशम् greatly, विसंज्ञा lost senses, गतासुकल्पेव as if she was almost dead, बभूव remained, विशालनेत्रा largeeyed, चिरेण after a long time, संज्ञाम् senses, प्रतिलभ्य after getting back, भूयः again, विचिन्तयामास started thinking
explanation: The largeeyed Sita lost her senses looking at him. She got back her senses after a long time and started thinking again:

shloka_text: स्वप्ने मयाऽयं विकृतोऽद्य दृष्टश्शाखामृगश्शास्त्रगणैर्निषिद्धः। स्वस्त्यस्तु रामाय स लक्ष्मणाय तथा पितुर्मे जनकस्य राज्ञः।।5.32.9।।
transliteration: svapne mayā'yaṃ vikṛto'dya dṛṣṭaśśākhāmṛgaśśāstragaṇairniṣiddhaḥ| svastyastu rāmāya sa lakṣmaṇāya tathā piturme janakasya rājñaḥ
translation: अद्य today, मया by me, विकृतः an ugly form, शास्त्रगणैः by sastras, निषिद्धः prohibited, शाखामृगः monkey, स्वप्ने in a dream, दृष्टः is seen, सलक्ष्मणाय for Lakshmana, रामाय for Rama, तथा so also, मे पितुः my father, जनकस्य राज्ञः of the king Janaka, स्वस्ति auspicious, अस्तु be
explanation: 'Today I saw an ugly monkey in my dream. Its sight in a dream is inauspicious according to sastras. Let it be auspicious for Lakshmana and Rama for the sake of my father Janaka.

shloka_text: स्वप्नोऽपि नायं नहि मेऽस्ति निद्रा शोकेन दुःखेन च पीडितायाः। सुखं हि मे नास्ति यतोऽस्मि हीना तेनेन्दुपूर्णप्रतिमाननेन।।5.32.10।।
transliteration: svapno'pi nāyaṃ nahi me'sti nidrā śokena duḥkhena ca pīḍitāyāḥ| sukhaṃ hi me nāsti yato'smi hīnā tenendupūrṇapratimānanena
translation: अयम् this, स्वप्नोऽपि even in a dream, न not, शोकेन with grief, दुःखेन च and with sorrow, पीडितायाः  a tormented woman, मे  to me, निद्रा sleep, नास्ति हि not there, मे to me, सुखम् pleasure, नास्ति हि not there, यतः therefore, इन्दुपूर्णप्रतिमाननेन whose face is like a fullmoon, तेन with him, हीना devoid, अस्मि I am
explanation: "But no, it was not a dream for tormented by grief and sorrow I cannot have a dream. When separated from the moonfaced Rama I have no sleep or pleasure, how can I have dream?

shloka_text: रामेति रामेति सदैव बुद्ध्या विचिन्त्य वाचा ब्रुवती तमेव। तस्यानुरूपां च कथां तदर्थमेवं प्रपश्यामि तथा शृणोमि।।5.32.11।।
transliteration: rāmeti rāmeti sadaiva buddhyā vicintya vācā bruvatī tameva| tasyānurūpāṃ ca kathāṃ tadarthamevaṃ prapaśyāmi tathā śṛṇomi
translation: रामेति रामेति only Rama Rama, सदा ऐव always, बुद्ध्या with my brain, विचिन्त्य after thinking, तमेव him alone, ब्रुवती thinking of, तस्य his, अनुरूपाम् favourable, तदर्थम् for his sake, कथाम् talk, एवम् in this way, प्रपश्यामि I am seeing, तथा so  also, शृणोमि I am hearing.
explanation: "I am always meditating upon Rama and thinking of him alone. I am talking about things related to him. Because of that I see him and hear him.

shloka_text: अहं हि तस्याद्य मनोभवेन सम्पीडिता तद्गतसर्वभावा। विचिन्तयन्ती सततं तमेव तथैव पश्यामि तथा शृणोमि।।5.32.12।।
transliteration: ahaṃ hi tasyādya manobhavena sampīḍitā tadgatasarvabhāvā| vicintayantī satataṃ tameva tathaiva paśyāmi tathā śṛṇomi
translation: अद्य now, अहम् I, तस्य his, मनोभवेन by love for him, सम्पीडिता tormented, तद्गतसर्वभावा all my thoughts immersed in him, सततम् always, तमेव about him only, विचिन्तयन्ती while I am thinking of, तथैव in a similar manner, पश्यामि I am seeing, तथैव only in such a way, शृणोमि I am listening.
explanation: "I am tormented by intense love for Rama, with all my thoughts immersed in him. Since I am constantly thinking of him I see him and hear words about him. (She thinks it is all hallucination.)

shloka_text: मनोरथस्स्यादिति चिन्तयामि तथापि बुद्ध्या च वितर्कयामि। किं कारणं तस्य हि नास्ति रूपं सुव्यक्तरूपश्च वदत्ययं माम्।।5.32.13।।
transliteration: manorathassyāditi cintayāmi tathāpi buddhyā ca vitarkayāmi| kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tasya hi nāsti rūpaṃ suvyaktarūpaśca vadatyayaṃ mām
translation: मनोरथः desire, स्यात् may be, इति thus, चिन्तयामि I think, बुद्ध्या च thinking, तथा like that, वितर्कयामि I am deliberating, तस्य its, रूपम् form, नास्ति हि is not seen, अयम् this, सुव्यक्तरूपः seen in a manifested form, माम् by me, वदति speaks, कारणम् cause, किम् what?
explanation: "I feel it is only the desire in my mind. Desire has no form. But the one who is addressing me has a form. I cannot understand this.

shloka_text: नमोऽस्तु वाचस्पतये सवज्रिणे स्वयंभुवे चैव हुताशनाय च। अनेन चोक्तं यदिदं ममाग्रतो वनौकसा तच्छ तथास्तु नान्यथा।।5.32.14।।
transliteration: namo'stu vācaspataye savajriṇe svayaṃbhuve caiva hutāśanāya ca| anena coktaṃ yadidaṃ mamāgrato vanaukasā taccha tathāstu nānyathā
translation: सवज्रिणे along with Indra, वाचस्पतये for Brihaspati, स्वयंभुवे चैव even for the creator Brahma, हुताशनाय for god of fire, च also, नमः salutations, अस्तु may be, अनेन by him, वनौकसा by the resident of the forest, मम अग्रतः in front of me, यत् whatever, इदम् this, उक्तम् spoken, तत् that, तथा true, अस्तु may be, अन्यथा other than that, न not be.
explanation: "My salutations to Indra, Brihaspati, Brahma the creator and also to the firegod. Let all those words spoken by the vanara here in front of me be true and not other than that." इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे द्वात्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtysecond sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सोऽवतीर्य द्रुमात्तस्माद्विद्रुमप्रतिमाननः। विनीतवेषः कृपणः प्रणिपत्योपसृत्य च।।5.33.1।। तामब्रवीन्महातेजा हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय सीतां मधुरया गिरा।।5.33.2।।
transliteration: so'vatīrya drumāttasmādvidrumapratimānanaḥ| vinītaveṣaḥ kṛpaṇaḥ praṇipatyopasṛtya ca tāmabravīnmahātejā hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ| śirasyañjalimādhāya sītāṃ madhurayā girā
translation: विद्रुमप्रतिमानन: whose face was like the colour of a coral, महातेजाः shining, मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, सः हनुमान् Hanuman, तस्मात् from that, द्रुमात् from the tree, अवतीर्य having climbed down, विनीतवेषः dressed in a sober manner, कृपणः piteous, प्रणिपत्य having offered salutations, उपसृत्य went near her, शिरसि on his head, अञ्चलिम् having folded palms, आधाय placed, तां सीताम् her, Sita, मधुरया in sweet, गिरा words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Hanuman, son of the Windgod whose face shone like coral, dressed in a sober manner climbed down the tree, went close to Sita, offered salutations with his palms on his head and spoke in sweet words:
comments: Sita reveals her story to Hanuman.

shloka_text: सोऽवतीर्य द्रुमात्तस्माद्विद्रुमप्रतिमाननः। विनीतवेषः कृपणः प्रणिपत्योपसृत्य च।।5.33.1।। तामब्रवीन्महातेजा हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय सीतां मधुरया गिरा।।5.33.2।।
transliteration: so'vatīrya drumāttasmādvidrumapratimānanaḥ| vinītaveṣaḥ kṛpaṇaḥ praṇipatyopasṛtya ca tāmabravīnmahātejā hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ| śirasyañjalimādhāya sītāṃ madhurayā girā
translation: विद्रुमप्रतिमानन: whose face was like the colour of a coral, महातेजाः shining, मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, सः हनुमान् Hanuman, तस्मात् from that, द्रुमात् from the tree, अवतीर्य having climbed down, विनीतवेषः dressed in a sober manner, कृपणः piteous, प्रणिपत्य having offered salutations, उपसृत्य went near her, शिरसि on his head, अञ्चलिम् having folded palms, आधाय placed, तां सीताम् her, Sita, मधुरया in sweet, गिरा words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Hanuman, son of the Windgod whose face shone like coral, dressed in a sober manner climbed down the tree, went close to Sita, offered salutations with his palms on his head and spoke in sweet words:
comments: Sita reveals her story to Hanuman.

shloka_text: का नु पद्मपलाशाक्षि क्लिष्टकौशेयवासिनि। द्रुमस्य शाखामालम्ब्य तिष्ठसि त्वमनिन्दिते।।5.33.3।।
transliteration: kā nu padmapalāśākṣi kliṣṭakauśeyavāsini| drumasya śākhāmālambya tiṣṭhasi tvamanindite
translation: पद्मपलाशाक्षि O one with eyes like lotus petals, क्लिष्टकौशेयवासिनि robed in crumpled silk, अनिन्दिते blameless lady, द्रुमस्य of the tree, शाखाम् branch, आलम्ब्य by holding, तिष्ठसि you are standing, का नु who are you?
explanation: "O blameless lady with eyes like lotus petals, in crumpled silk, holding a branch, and standing, who are you?

shloka_text: किमर्थम् तव नेत्राभ्यां वारि स्रवति शोकजम्। पुण्डरीकपलाशाभ्यां विप्रकीर्णमिवोदकम्।।5.33.4।।
transliteration: kimartham tava netrābhyāṃ vāri sravati śokajam| puṇḍarīkapalāśābhyāṃ viprakīrṇamivodakam
translation: पुण्डरीकपलाशाभ्याम् from two petals of white lotus, विप्रकीर्णम् trickled, उदकम् इव like water, तव your, नेत्राभ्याम् from your eyes, शोकजम् tears of grief, वारि water, किमर्थम् for what reason, स्रवति is flowing.
explanation: "Why are tears of grief flowing from your eyes like water trickling down a pair of petals of white lotuses?

shloka_text: सुराणामसुराणां वा नागगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्। यक्षाणां किन्नराणां वा का त्वं भवसि शोभने।।5.33.5।।
transliteration: surāṇāmasurāṇāṃ vā nāgagandharvarakṣasām| yakṣāṇāṃ kinnarāṇāṃ vā kā tvaṃ bhavasi śobhane
translation: शोभने O auspicious one, त्वम् you, सुराणाम् among gods, असुराणां वा or demons, नागगन्धर्वरक्षसाम् of nagas, gandharvas, rakshasas, यक्षाणाम् of yakshas, किन्नराणां वा or kinneras, का who, भवसि you are.
explanation: "O noble lady, are you a goddess or a demoness, a naga, a gandharva, a rakshasa, a yaksha or a kinnera?

shloka_text: का त्वं भवसि रुद्राणां मरुतां वा वरानने। वसूनां हि वरारोहे देवता प्रतिभासि मे।।5.33.6।।
transliteration: kā tvaṃ bhavasi rudrāṇāṃ marutāṃ vā varānane| vasūnāṃ hi varārohe devatā pratibhāsi me
translation: वरानने O beautiful lady, त्वम् you, रुद्राणाम् of the Rudras, मरुतां वा or even Marutas, वसूनाम् of Vasus, का who, भवसि you are, वरारोहे O fine woman, देवता goddess, मे to me, प्रतिभासि  you appear
explanation: "O beautiful lady Do you belong to the race of Rudras, or Marutas, or Vasus?. O noble lady, you appear a goddess to me.

shloka_text: कि नु चन्द्रमसा हीना पतिता विबुधालयात्। रोहिणी ज्योतिषां श्रेष्ठा श्रेष्ठसर्वगुणान्विता।।5.33.7।।
transliteration: ki nu candramasā hīnā patitā vibudhālayāt| rohiṇī jyotiṣāṃ śreṣṭhā śreṣṭhasarvaguṇānvitā
translation: चन्द्रमसा from the Moon, हीना separated, विबुधालयात् from the abode of the gods, पतिता fallen down, ज्योतिषाम् among the luminaries, श्रेष्ठा best one, श्रेष्ठसर्वगुणान्विता who has all best qualities, रोहिणी Rohini किं नु you may be
explanation: "are you Rohini, embellished with best virtues among the constellations? Have you come down from the abode of the luminaries separated from the Moon, her lord?

shloka_text: का त्वं भवसि कल्याणि त्वमनिन्दितलोचने। कोपाद्वा यदि वा मोहाद्भर्तारमसितेक्षणे।।5.33.8।। वसिष्ठं कोपयित्वा त्वं नासि कल्याण्यरुन्धती।
transliteration: kā tvaṃ bhavasi kalyāṇi tvamaninditalocane| kopādvā yadi vā mohādbhartāramasitekṣaṇe vasiṣṭhaṃ kopayitvā tvaṃ nāsi kalyāṇyarundhatī|
translation: असितेक्षणे O lady of lovely black eyes, त्वम् you, कोपाद्वा or out of anger, यदि वा or else, मोहात् out of delusion, भर्तारम् husband, वसिष्ठम् Vasistha, कोपयित्वा making him angry, कल्याणि O auspicious lady, अरुन्धती Arundhati, नासि are you not
explanation: "O lady of lovely black eyes who are you? Have you by any chance offended your husband out of anger or out of delusion? Are you the auspicious Arundhati dislodged for making your lord Vasistha angry?

shloka_text: को नु पुत्रः पिता भ्राता भर्ता वा ते सुमध्यमे।।5.33.9।। अस्माल्लोकादमुं लोकं गतं त्वमनुशोचसि।
transliteration: ko nu putraḥ pitā bhrātā bhartā vā te sumadhyame asmāllokādamuṃ lokaṃ gataṃ tvamanuśocasi|
translation: सुमध्यमे O woman of beautiful waist, अस्मात् from this, लोकात् from the world, अमुं लोकम् to this world, गतम् dead, त्वम् your, अनुशोचसि worrying about, ते your, पुत्रः son, पिता father, भ्राता brother, भर्ता वा or is it husband, को नु is he?
explanation: "O woman of beautiful waist from which world have you come here? For whom are you worrying? Who is your son, father, brother or husband? Are you worrying about some one dead?.

shloka_text: रोदनादतिनिश्श्वासाद्भूमिसंस्पर्शनादपि।।5.33.10।। न त्वां देवीमहं मन्ये राज्ञ स्सर्वज्ञावधारणात्।
transliteration: rodanādatiniśśvāsādbhūmisaṃsparśanādapi na tvāṃ devīmahaṃ manye rājña ssarvajñāvadhāraṇāt|
translation: रोदनात् from your weeping, अतिनिश्श्वासात् breathing heavily, भूमिसंस्पर्शनादपि your touching the ground, राज्ञः royal, संज्ञावधारणात् having signs of sovereignty, त्वाम् you, देवीम् O goddess, अहम् I, न मन्ये I do not think.
explanation: "From your weeping, your sighing and your touching the earth (gods do not touch the earth) and your signs of sovereignty, I do not think you are a goddess (meaning otherwise she posessed divine grace).

shloka_text: व्यञ्जनानि च ते यानि लक्षणानि च लक्षये।।5.33.11।। महिषी भूमिपालस्य राजकन्या च मे मता।
transliteration: vyañjanāni ca te yāni lakṣaṇāni ca lakṣaye mahiṣī bhūmipālasya rājakanyā ca me matā|
translation: ते your, यानि those, व्यञ्जनानि signs, लक्षणानि च also qualities, लक्षये I see, भूमिपालस्य king's, महिषी consort, राजकन्या च and a princess, मे to me, मता it is felt.
explanation: "On the basis of your royal signs and other qualities I infer that you are the daughter of a king or his consort.

shloka_text: रावणेन जनस्थानाद्बलादपदहृता यदि।।5.33.12।। सीता त्वमसि भद्रं ते तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः।
transliteration: rāvaṇena janasthānādbalādapadahṛtā yadi sītā tvamasi bhadraṃ te tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ|
translation: त्वम् you, जनस्थानात् from Janasthana, रावणेन by Ravana, बलात् forcibly, अपहृता borne away, सीता Sita, असि यदि if you are, तत् that, पृच्छतः  enquiring, मम to me, आचक्ष्व you tell, ते भद्रम् wish you well.
explanation: "If you are Sita, who was forcefully borne away by Ravana from Janasthana you may kindly reveal to me freely. May god bless you.

shloka_text: यथा हि तव वै दैन्यं रूपं चाप्यतिमानुषम्।।5.33.13।। तपसा चान्वितो वेषस्त्वं राममहिषी ध्रुवम्।
transliteration: yathā hi tava vai dainyaṃ rūpaṃ cāpyatimānuṣam tapasā cānvito veṣastvaṃ rāmamahiṣī dhruvam|
translation: तव your, दैन्यम् plight, अतिमानुषम् superhuman, रूपं च and your form, तपसा with austerity, अन्वितः endowed, वेषः your dress, यथा as much, त्वम् you are, ध्रुवम् surely, राममहिषी Rama's queen.
explanation: "Indeed your plight, the superhuman beauty and your robes marked with asceticism, surely tell me that you are Rama's queen."

shloka_text: सा तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा रामकीर्तनहर्षिता।।5.33.14।। उवाच वाक्यं वैदेही हनुमन्तं द्रुमाश्रितम्।
transliteration: sā tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā rāmakīrtanaharṣitā uvāca vākyaṃ vaidehī hanumantaṃ drumāśritam|
translation: सा वैदेही that Vaidehi, तस्य his, वचनम् word, श्रुत्वा having heard, रामकीर्तनहर्षिता happy to hear words of praise of Rama, द्रुमाश्रितम् on the tree, हनुमन्तम् Hanuman, वाक्यम् these words, उवाच spoke.
explanation: Happy to have heard words of praise of Rama, Vaidehi spoke this to Hanuman, who got up the tree:

shloka_text: पृथिव्यां राजसिंहानां मुख्यस्य विदितात्मनः।।5.33.15।। स्नुषा दशरथस्याहं शत्रुसैन्यप्रतापिनः।
transliteration: pṛthivyāṃ rājasiṃhānāṃ mukhyasya viditātmanaḥ snuṣā daśarathasyāhaṃ śatrusainyapratāpinaḥ|
translation: अहम् I am, पृथिव्याम् on earth, राजसिंहानाम् among great kings, मुख्यस्य foremost, विदितात्मनः of the knower of self, शत्रुसैन्यप्रतापिनः of the slayer of enemy army, दशरथस्य Dasaratha's, स्नुषा daughterinlaw.
explanation: "I am daughterinlaw of king Dasaratha, knower of the self, the foremost among kings on earth and a slayer of enemy army.

shloka_text: दुहिता जनकस्याहं वैदेहस्य महात्मनः।।5.33.16।। सीतेति नाम नाम्नाऽहं भार्या रामस्य धीमतः।
transliteration: duhitā janakasyāhaṃ vaidehasya mahātmanaḥ sīteti nāma nāmnā'haṃ bhāryā rāmasya dhīmataḥ|
translation: अहम् I am, वैदेहस्य Videha's, महात्मनः great soul, जनकस्य Janaka's, दुहिता daughter, नाम्ना सीतेति नाम Sita by name, अहम् I am, धीमतः of the sagacious, रामस्य Rama's, भार्या wife.
explanation: "I am daughter of the great soul, Janaka, king of Videha, known as Sita. I am the wife of that sagacious Rama.

shloka_text: समा द्वादश तत्राहं राघवस्य निवेशने।।5.33.17।। भुञ्जाना मानुषान्भोगान्सर्वकामसमृद्धिनी।
transliteration: samā dvādaśa tatrāhaṃ rāghavasya niveśane bhuñjānā mānuṣānbhogānsarvakāmasamṛddhinī|
translation: अहम् I am, तत्र there, राघवस्य Rama's, निवेशने the abode, मानुषान् mortal, भोगान् pleasures, भुञ्जाना experiencing, सर्वकामसमृद्धिनी all kinds of pleasures provided, द्वादश twelve, समाः years.
explanation: "I enjoyed worldly pleasures in abundance for twelve years at Rama's abode.

shloka_text: तत्र त्रयोदशे वर्षे राज्येनेक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम्।।5.33.18।। अभिषेचयितुं राजा सोपाध्यायः प्रचक्रमे।
transliteration: tatra trayodaśe varṣe rājyenekṣvākunandanam abhiṣecayituṃ rājā sopādhyāyaḥ pracakrame|
translation: ततः then, त्रयोदशे in the thirteenth, वर्षे in the year, सोपाध्यायः with his preceptor, राजा the king, इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम् delight of the Ikshvakus, राज्येन in the kingdom, अभिषेचयितुम् to coronate, प्रचक्रमे arranged.
explanation: "Then in the thirteenth year king Dasaratha along with the royal preceptor arranged to  coronate Rama, delight of the Ikshvaku family, in the kingdom.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्सम्भ्रियमाणे तु राघवस्याभिषेचने।।5.33.19।। कैकयी नाम भर्तारं देवी वचनमब्रवीत्।
transliteration: tasminsambhriyamāṇe tu rāghavasyābhiṣecane kaikayī nāma bhartāraṃ devī vacanamabravīt|
translation: तस्मिन् in that, राघवस्य Rama's, अभिषेचने in the coronation, सम्भ्रियमाणे while preparations were being made, कैकेयी नाम called Kaikeyi, देवी queen, भर्तारम् to her husband, वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: "While preparations for the coronation were on, queen Kaikeyi said to her husband:

shloka_text: न पिबेयं न खादेयं प्रत्यहं मम भोजनम्।।5.33.20।। एष मे जीवितस्यान्तो रामो यद्यभिषिच्यते।
transliteration: na pibeyaṃ na khādeyaṃ pratyahaṃ mama bhojanam eṣa me jīvitasyānto rāmo yadyabhiṣicyate|
translation: न पिबेयम् I shall not drink, प्रत्यहम् daily, भोजनम् food, न खादेयम् I will not eat, रामः Rama, यदि if, अभिषिच्यते is coronated, एषः this is, मे my, जीवितस्य life's, अन्तः end.
explanation: 'I shall not drink or eat food, if Rama is coronated. I shall end my life this moment.

shloka_text: यत्तदुक्तं त्वया वाक्यं प्रीत्या नृपतिसत्तम।।5.33.21।। तच्छेन्न वितथं कार्यं वनं गच्छतु राघवः।
transliteration: yattaduktaṃ tvayā vākyaṃ prītyā nṛpatisattama tacchenna vitathaṃ kāryaṃ vanaṃ gacchatu rāghavaḥ|
translation: नृपतिसत्तम the foremost among kings, त्वया by you, प्रीत्या lovingly, यत् such, तत् वाक्यम् words, उक्तम् spoken, तत् the same, वितथम् false, न कार्यं that promise, यदि if you please, राघवः Rama, वनम् to the forest, गच्छतु  go.
explanation: 'O Dasaratha, the foremost among kings if the promise lovingly made by you earlier is not going to be false, Rama should go to the forest'.

shloka_text: स राजा सत्यवाग्देव्या वरदानमनुस्मरन्।।5.33.22।। मुमोह वचनं श्रुत्वा कैकेय्याः क्रूरमप्रियम्।
transliteration: sa rājā satyavāgdevyā varadānamanusmaran mumoha vacanaṃ śrutvā kaikeyyāḥ krūramapriyam|
translation: सत्यवाक् ever truthful, सः राजा that king, देव्याः to the queen, वरदानम् boons, अनुस्मरन् remembering, कैकेय्याः of Kaikeyi, क्रूरम् cruel, अप्रियम् unpleasant, वचनम् word, श्रुत्वा having heard, मुमोह fainted.
explanation: "Remembering the boons the ever truthful king had granted to Kaikeyi, he fainted after hearing her cruel and harsh words.

shloka_text: ततस्तु स्थविरो राजा सत्ये धर्मे व्यवस्थितः।।5.33.23।। ज्येष्ठं यशस्विनं पुत्रं रुदन्राज्यमयाचत।
transliteration: tatastu sthaviro rājā satye dharme vyavasthitaḥ jyeṣṭhaṃ yaśasvinaṃ putraṃ rudanrājyamayācata|
translation: ततः then, सत्ये by truth, धर्मे by rigteousness, व्यवस्थितः one who held, स्थविरः aged, राजा king, रुदन् while crying, यशस्विनम् glorious one, ज्येष्ठम् eldest, पुत्रम् son, राज्यम् kingdom, अयाचत begged.
explanation: "The aged king who held on to truthfulness and righteousness begged his famed eldest son Rama to return the kingdom.

shloka_text: स पितुर्वचनं श्रीमानभिषेकात्परं प्रियम्।।5.33.24।। मनसा पूर्वमासाद्य वाचा प्रतिगृहीतवान्।
transliteration: sa piturvacanaṃ śrīmānabhiṣekātparaṃ priyam manasā pūrvamāsādya vācā pratigṛhītavān|
translation: श्रीमान् illustrious one, सः he, पितुः father's, वचनम् word, अभिषेकात् more than coronation, परम् supreme, प्रियम् dear, मनसा by his mind, पूर्वम् first, आसाद्य having accepted, वाचा by word, प्रतिगृहीतवान् accepted
explanation: "The illustrious Rama who valued his father's word more than sovereignty, bowed to the command of the father.

shloka_text: दद्यान्न प्रतिगृह्णीयान्न ब्रूयात्किञ्चिदप्रियम्।।5.33.25।। अपि जीवितहेतोर्वा रामस्सत्यपराक्रमः।
transliteration: dadyānna pratigṛhṇīyānna brūyātkiñcidapriyam api jīvitahetorvā rāmassatyaparākramaḥ|
translation: सत्यपराक्रमः one whose truthfulness was his strength, रामः Rama, दद्यात् he give,न प्रतिगृह्णीयात् he will not take, जीवितहेतोर्वा even for his life, किञ्चित् even a little, अप्रियम् harsh, न ब्रूयात् he will not speak .
explanation: "Rama, whose strength was his truthfulness, gave whatever others sought but would not accept anything in return. He would not speak a harsh word.

shloka_text: स विहायोत्तरीयाणि महार्हाणि महायशाः।।5.33.26।। विसृज्य मनसा राज्यं जनन्यै मां समादिशत्।
transliteration: sa vihāyottarīyāṇi mahārhāṇi mahāyaśāḥ visṛjya manasā rājyaṃ jananyai māṃ samādiśat|
translation: महायशाः a highly renowned, सः he, महार्हाणि luxurious, उत्तरीयाणि upper garments, विहाय cast off, मनसा whole heartedly, राज्यम् kingdom, विसृज्य having given up, माम् me, जनन्यै to his mother, समादिशत् entrusted.
explanation: "Having given up the kingdom  voluntarily, Rama, a highly renowned king cast off his luxurious upper garments and asked me to take care of his mother.

shloka_text: साहं तस्याग्रतस्तूर्णं प्रस्थिता वनचारिणी।।5.33.27।। न हि मे तेन हीनाया वासस्स्वर्गेऽपि रोचते।
transliteration: sāhaṃ tasyāgratastūrṇaṃ prasthitā vanacāriṇī na hi me tena hīnāyā vāsassvarge'pi rocate|
translation: सा अहम् I myself, वनचारिणी a forestdweller, तूर्णम् quickly, तस्य his, अग्रतः ahead of him, प्रस्थिता started, तेन by him, हीनायाः separated, मे  me, स्वर्गेऽपि न रोचते did not prefer even heaven.
explanation: "I, however resolved to live in the forest, marched ahead of him quickly as I did not prefer even heaven without him.

shloka_text: प्रागेव तु महाभागस्सौमित्रिर्मित्रनन्दनः।।5.33.28।। पूर्वजस्यानुयात्रार्थे द्रुमचीरैरलङ्कृतः।
transliteration: prāgeva tu mahābhāgassaumitrirmitranandanaḥ pūrvajasyānuyātrārthe drumacīrairalaṅkṛtaḥ|
translation: महाभागः a noble one, मित्रनन्दनः a delight to friends, सौमित्रिः Saumitri, प्रागेव already, पूर्वजस्य eldest brother's, अनुयात्रार्थे to follow him, द्रुमचीरैः an bark, अलङ्कृतः dressed.
explanation: Already the noble Saumitri, delight of his friends, clad in bark garments, had set out to follow his elder brother.

shloka_text: ते वयं भर्तुरादेशं बहुमान्य दृढव्रताः।।5.33.29।। प्रविष्टास्स्म पुरादृष्टं वनं गम्भीरदर्शनम्।
transliteration: te vayaṃ bharturādeśaṃ bahumānya dṛḍhavratāḥ praviṣṭāssma purādṛṣṭaṃ vanaṃ gambhīradarśanam|
translation: ते then वयम् we, भर्तुः king's, आदेशम् order, बहुमान्य respecting, दृढव्रताः resolved firmly, पुरा in the past, अदृष्टम् not seen, गम्भीरदर्शनम् impenetrable, वनम् forest, प्रविष्टाः स्मः we entered.
explanation: "Respecting the king's order and determined firmly, we entered the impenetrable forest.

shloka_text: वसतो दण्डकारण्ये तस्याहममितौजसः।।5.33.30।। रक्षसाऽपहृता भार्या रावणेन दुरात्मना।
transliteration: vasato daṇḍakāraṇye tasyāhamamitaujasaḥ rakṣasā'pahṛtā bhāryā rāvaṇena durātmanā|
translation: दण्डकारण्ये in the Dandaka forest, वसतः while living, अमितौजसः the most valiant, तस्य his, भार्या wife, अहम् am, दुरात्मना by evilminded, रावणेन by Ravana, अपहृता was abducted.
explanation: "While the most valiant Rama was living in the Dandaka forest, I, his wife was borne away by the evilminded Ravana.

shloka_text: द्वौ मासौ तेन मे कालो जीवितानुग्रहः कृतः।।5.33.31।। ऊर्ध्वं द्वाभ्यां तु मासाभ्यां ततस्तक्ष्यामि जीवितम्।
transliteration: dvau māsau tena me kālo jīvitānugrahaḥ kṛtaḥ ūrdhvaṃ dvābhyāṃ tu māsābhyāṃ tatastakṣyāmi jīvitam|
translation: तेन by him, द्वौ two, मासौ months, मे to me, जीवितानुग्रहः grant of time to live, कृतः given, ततः then, द्वाभ्याम् after the two, मासाभ्याम् months, ऊर्ध्वम् after that, जीवितम् life, त्यक्ष्यामि I will give up.
explanation: "He has allowed me two months time to live. After two months I will have to give up my life." इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रयस्त्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtythird sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा हनुमान्हरिपुङ्गवः। दुःखाद्दुःखाभिभूताया स्सान्त्वमुत्तरमब्रवीत्।।5.34.1।।
transliteration: tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā hanumānharipuṅgavaḥ| duḥkhādduḥkhābhibhūtāyā ssāntvamuttaramabravīt
translation: हरिपुङ्गवः monkey leader, हनुमान् Hanuman, दुःखात् with sadness, दुःखाभिभूतायाः overwhelmed with grief, तस्याः to her, तत् those, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा after hearing, सान्त्वम् comforting, उत्तरम् reply, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Hearing the words of Sita who was overwhelmed with grief, the monkey leader Hanuman felt sad and thus spoke comforting her:
comments: Hanuman tells the story of Rama to Sita.

shloka_text: अहं रामस्य सन्देशाद्देवि दूतस्तवागतः। वैदेहि कुशली रामस्त्वां च कौशलमब्रवीत्।।5.34.2।।
transliteration: ahaṃ rāmasya sandeśāddevi dūtastavāgataḥ| vaidehi kuśalī rāmastvāṃ ca kauśalamabravīt
translation: देवि O queen, वैदेहि Vaidehi, अहम् I am, रामस्य Rama's, सन्देशात् by order, तव your, दूतः messenger, आगतः reached, कुशली is well, रामः Rama, त्वां च and you, कुशलम् welfare, अब्रवीत् wished you.
explanation: "By the command of Rama I am here as a messenger. He is keeping well. He is well and wishes you well.

shloka_text: यो ब्रह्ममस्त्रं वेदांश्च वेद वेदविदांवरः। स त्वां दाशरथी रामो देवि कौशलमब्रवीत्।।5.34.3।।
transliteration: yo brahmamastraṃ vedāṃśca veda vedavidāṃvaraḥ| sa tvāṃ dāśarathī rāmo devi kauśalamabravīt
translation: देवि O godlike lady, वेदविदाम् mastered the Vedas, वरः choicest, यः he is, ब्रह्मम् अस्त्रम् weapon of Brahma (Brahmastra), वेदांश्च and Vedas, वेद knows, सः he, दाशरथिः son of Dasaratha, रामः Rama, त्वाम् you, कौशलम् welfare, अब्रवीत् conveyed.
explanation: "O godlike lady Rama, son of Dasaratha, master of the Vedas, wielder of Brahmastra wishes you well.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणश्च महातेजा भर्तुस्तेऽनुचरः प्रियः। कृतवान्शोकसन्तप्तश्शिरसा तेऽभिवादनम्।।5.34.4।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaśca mahātejā bhartuste'nucaraḥ priyaḥ| kṛtavānśokasantaptaśśirasā te'bhivādanam
translation: महातेजाः very mighty, ते भर्तुः your husband, प्रियः dear, अनुचरः follower, लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana also, शोकसन्तप्तः immersed in grief, शिरसा with his head in obeisance, ते to you, अभिवादनम् offers salutations, कृतवान् has done.
explanation: "The mighty Lakshmana too, a dear brother and follower of your husband is immersed in grief, and sends salutations to you."

shloka_text: सा तयोः कुशलं देवी निशम्य नरसिंहयोः। प्रीतिसंहृष्टसर्वाङ्गी हनुमन्तमथाब्रवीत्।।5.34.5।।
transliteration: sā tayoḥ kuśalaṃ devī niśamya narasiṃhayoḥ| prītisaṃhṛṣṭasarvāṅgī hanumantamathābravīt
translation: सा देवी that queen, तयोः of both of them, नरसिंहयोः of lions among men, कुशलम् wellbeing, निशम्य on hearing, प्रीतिसंहृष्टसर्वाङ्गी overtaken by joy experienced in all her limbs, अथ then, हनुमन्तम् Hanuman, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: On hearing the wellbeing of Rama and Lakshman, lions among men, Sita experienced thrill all over her body. She then  spoke to Hanuman:

shloka_text: कल्याणी बत गाथेयं लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मा। एति जीवन्तमानन्दो नरं वर्षशतादपि।।5.34.6।।
transliteration: kalyāṇī bata gātheyaṃ laukikī pratibhāti mā| eti jīvantamānando naraṃ varṣaśatādapi
translation: जीवन्तम् who lives, नरम् human being, वर्षशतादपि a hundred years, आनन्दः happiness, एति comes, इयम् this, लौकिकी popular, गाथा adage, कल्याणी is auspicious, मा to me, प्रतिभाति appears.
explanation: "The adage that 'joy comes to a living being even though it be at the end of  a hundred years' is popular. It appears true in my case".

shloka_text: तया समागते तस्मिन्प्रीतिरुत्पादिताऽद्भुता। परस्परेण चालापं विश्वस्तौ तौ प्रचक्रतुः।।5.34.7।।
transliteration: tayā samāgate tasminprītirutpāditā'dbhutā| paraspareṇa cālāpaṃ viśvastau tau pracakratuḥ
translation: समागते when the meeting took place, तस्मिन् in him, तथा like that, अद्भुता wonderful, प्रीतिः pleasure, उत्पादिता was created, तौ in both, विश्वस्तौ confiding in the other, परस्परेण each to the other, आलापं च converse, चक्रतुः started.
explanation: Hanuman thus created a sense of wonderful joy in her as they came together. Both of them started to converse restoring confidence in each other.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा हनुमान्हरियूथपः। सीतायाश्शोकदीनायास्समीपमुपचक्रमे।।5.34.8।।
transliteration: tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā hanumānhariyūthapaḥ| sītāyāśśokadīnāyāssamīpamupacakrame
translation: हरियूथपः leader of the monkey troops, हनुमान् Hanuman, शोकदीनायाः of the piteous lady stricken with grief, तस्याः her, सीतायाः Sita's, तत् that, वचनम् word, श्रुत्वा after hearing, समीपम् close by, उपचक्रमे moved.
explanation: Hearing the reply of Sita, who was crying piteously, stricken with grief, the monkey leader, Hanuman moved close to her.

shloka_text: यथा यथा समीपं स हनुमानुपसर्पति। तथा तथा रावणं सा तं सीता परिशङ्कते।।5.34.9।।
transliteration: yathā yathā samīpaṃ sa hanumānupasarpati| tathā tathā rāvaṇaṃ sā taṃ sītā pariśaṅkate
translation: सः हनुमान् Hanuman, यथा यथा slowly that way, समीपम् near, उपसर्पति started moving, तथा तथा in the same way, सा सीता that Sita, तम् him, रावणम् Ravana, परिशङ्कते suspected.
explanation: As Hanuman started slowly drawing close, Sita suspected he might be Ravana.

shloka_text: अहो धिग्दुष्कृतमिदं कथितं हि यदस्य मे। रूपान्तरमुपागम्य स एवायं हि रावणः।।5.34.10।।
transliteration: aho dhigduṣkṛtamidaṃ kathitaṃ hi yadasya me| rūpāntaramupāgamya sa evāyaṃ hi rāvaṇaḥ
translation: अहो Oh, धिक् fie upon, मे to myself, इदम् this, अस्य to him, कथितम् story, दुष्कृतम् that which should not have been said, अयम् he, रूपान्तरम् in cognito, उपागम्य has come, सः रावणः हि verily he is Ravana.
explanation: "Ohshame on me. I have told him my story which should not have been said. This is verily Ravana come in a disguise".

shloka_text: तामशोकस्य शाखां सा विमुक्त्वा शोककर्शिता। तस्यामेवानवद्याङ्गी धरण्यां समुपाविशत्।।5.34.11।।
transliteration: tāmaśokasya śākhāṃ sā vimuktvā śokakarśitā| tasyāmevānavadyāṅgī dharaṇyāṃ samupāviśat
translation: अनवद्याङ्गी who has flawless limbs, सा she, अशोकस्य Ashoka tree's, ताम् that, शाखाम् branch, विमुक्त्वा later leaving, शोककर्शिता emaciated out of sorrow, तस्याम् on that, धरण्यामेव on the ground, समुपाविशत् sat near.
explanation: So saying Sita of flawless limbs, emaciated with grief, left the branch of Ashoka tree held by her and squatted on the ground.

shloka_text: हनुमानपि दुःखार्तां तां दृष्ट्वा भयमोहिताम्। अवन्दत महाबाहुस्ततस्तां जनकात्मजाम्।।5.34.12।। सा चैनं भयवित्रस्ता भूयो नैवाभ्युदैक्षत।
transliteration: hanumānapi duḥkhārtāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhayamohitām| avandata mahābāhustatastāṃ janakātmajām sā cainaṃ bhayavitrastā bhūyo naivābhyudaikṣata|
translation: महाबाहुः longarmed one, हनुमानपि Hanuman too, दुःखार्ताम् sorrowful lady, भयमोहिताम् deluded with fear, ताम् her, दृष्ट्वा on seeing, ततः then, तां जनकात्मजाम् the daughter of Janaka, अवन्दत prostrated, सा च and she, भयवित्रस्ता trembling with fear, एनम् him, भूयः again, नाभ्युदैक्षत did not look at him.
explanation: The longarmed Hanuman saw Sita, who was stricken with grief and deluded with fear. He prostrated to her. But out of fear she did not look at him.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा वन्दमानं तु सीता शशिनिभानना।।5.34.13।। अब्रवीद्धीर्घमुच्छवस्य वानरं मधुरस्वरा।
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vandamānaṃ tu sītā śaśinibhānanā abravīddhīrghamucchavasya vānaraṃ madhurasvarā|
translation: शशिनिभानना moonfaced lady, सीता Sita, तम् him, वन्दमानम् prostrating, दृष्ट्वा on seeing, दीर्घम् deep, उच्छवस्य after breathing out, मधुरस्वरा in a sweet voice, वानरम् to vanara, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: On seeing the vanara prostrated, the moonfaced lady, sighed deeply and spoke to him in a sweet voice:

shloka_text: मायां प्रविष्टो मायावी यदि त्वं रावणस्स्वयम्।।5.34.14।। उत्पादयसि मे भूयस्सन्तापं तन्न शोभनम्।
transliteration: māyāṃ praviṣṭo māyāvī yadi tvaṃ rāvaṇassvayam utpādayasi me bhūyassantāpaṃ tanna śobhanam|
translation: त्वम् you, मायाम् disguised, प्रविष्टः entered, मायावी trickster, स्वयम् yourself, रावणः यदि if you are Ravana, मे to me, भूयः again, सन्तापम् grief, उत्पादयसि you have created, तत् that, शोभनम् न not good.
explanation: "If you are that trickster Ravana who appears incognito before me, it is not good for you. You are causing grief again.

shloka_text: स्वं परित्यज्य रूपं यः परिव्राजकरूपध्रुत्। जनस्थाने मया दृष्टस्त्वं स एवासि रावणः।।5.34.15।।
transliteration: svaṃ parityajya rūpaṃ yaḥ parivrājakarūpadhrut| janasthāne mayā dṛṣṭastvaṃ sa evāsi rāvaṇaḥ
translation: यः रावणः that Ravana, स्वं रूपम् his own form, परित्यज्य after giving up, परिव्राजकरूपवान् taking the form of a mendicant, जनस्थाने in Janasthana, मया by me, दृष्टः seen, त्वं you, स एव असि you are the same one.
explanation: "You are the same Ravana who took the guise of a mendicant, giving up your real form and came to Janasthana.

shloka_text: उपवासकृशां दीनां कामरूप निशाचर। सन्तापयसि मां भूयस्सन्तप्तां तन्न शोभनम्।।5.34.16।।
transliteration: upavāsakṛśāṃ dīnāṃ kāmarūpa niśācara| santāpayasi māṃ bhūyassantaptāṃ tanna śobhanam
translation: कामरूप one who can assume any form, निशाचर nightstalker, उपवासकृशां an emaciated lady, सन्तप्तां a lady stricken with grief, दीनां pitiable, माम् me, भूयः again, सन्तापं grief, सन्तापयसि you are making me sorrowful, तत् that, शोभनं न not good for you.
explanation: "Oh you are one who can assume any form at will. You are a nightstalker. It is not good for you to cause pain to me who is already emaciated through fasting, who is pitiable and who is already afflicted.

shloka_text: अथवा नैतदेवं हि यन्मया परिशङ्कितम्।।5.34.17।। मनसो हि मम प्रीतिरुत्पन्ना तव दर्शनात्।
transliteration: athavā naitadevaṃ hi yanmayā pariśaṅkitam manaso hi mama prītirutpannā tava darśanāt|
translation: अथवा or may be, मया by me, यत् that which, परिशङ्कितम् that I am suspecting, एतत् because, एवम् all this, न हि not true, तव your, दर्शनात् by your presence, मम my, मनसः mind, प्रीतिः pleased, उत्पन्ना हि is generated.
explanation: "May be my suspicion is not correct Because I am experiencing pleasure in my mind in your presence.

shloka_text: यदि रामस्य दूतस्त्वमागतो भद्रमस्तु ते।।5.34.18।। पृच्छामि त्वां हरिश्रेष्ठ प्रिया रामकथा हि मे।
transliteration: yadi rāmasya dūtastvamāgato bhadramastu te pṛcchāmi tvāṃ hariśreṣṭha priyā rāmakathā hi me|
translation: त्वम् you, रामस्य Rama's, दूतः messenger, आगतः यदि if you have come here, ते to you, भद्रम् be auspicious, अस्तु be, हरिश्रेष्ठ O great vanara, मे to me, रामकथा Rama'story, प्रिया हि dear, त्वाम् you, पृच्छामि I ask you.
explanation: "O great vanara, If on the other hand you have come here as Rama's messenger I wish you well. I love Rama's story. Tell me.

shloka_text: गुणान्रामस्य कथय प्रियस्य मम वानर।।5.34.19।। चित्तं हरसि मे सौम्य नदीकूलं यथा रयः।
transliteration: guṇānrāmasya kathaya priyasya mama vānara cittaṃ harasi me saumya nadīkūlaṃ yathā rayaḥ|
translation: वानर vanara, मम my, प्रियस्य dear lord's, रामस्य Rama's, गुणान् virtues, कथय you may tell me, सौम्य O gentle one, नदीकूलम् river bank, रयः यथा like the current of water, मे my, चित्तम् mind, हरसि you are luring.
explanation: "O vanara Rama's virtues are dear to me to hear. O gentle one just as the current of the river wears away its banks, my mind is lured by your presence.

shloka_text: अहो स्वप्नस्य सुखता याहमेवं चिराहृता।।5.34.20।। प्रेषितं नाम पश्यामि राघवेण वनौकसम्।
transliteration: aho svapnasya sukhatā yāhamevaṃ cirāhṛtā preṣitaṃ nāma paśyāmi rāghaveṇa vanaukasam|
translation: स्वप्नस्य of a dream, सुखता pleasure, अहो Oh, चिराहृता kept dreaming for a long time, या that, राघवेण by Rama, प्रेषितं नाम  person sent, वनौकसम् vanara, एवम् that way, पश्यामि I am seeing.
explanation: "Oh I have been seeing the person sent by Rama in my dream for a long time. This is a pleasant dream to me.

shloka_text: स्वप्नेऽपि यद्यहं वीरं राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्।।5.34.21।। पश्येयं नावसीदेयं स्वप्नोऽपि मम मत्सरी।
transliteration: svapne'pi yadyahaṃ vīraṃ rāghavaṃ sahalakṣmaṇam paśyeyaṃ nāvasīdeyaṃ svapno'pi mama matsarī|
translation: अहम् I, स्वप्नेऽपि even in a dream, सहलक्ष्मणम् along with Lakshmana, वीरम् heroic, राघवम् Rama, पश्येयं यदि if I can see, नावसीदेयम् I will not be despondent, मम my, स्वप्नोऽपि even the dream, मत्सरी inimical to me.
explanation: "Even if I can see the heroic Rama together with Lakshmana in my dream my pain will be gone. Even the dream is inimical to me (I cannot sleep and thus cannot dream.)

shloka_text: नाहं स्वप्नमिमं मन्ये स्वप्ने दृष्ट्वा हि वानरम्।।5.34.22।। न शक्योऽभ्युदयः प्राप्तुं प्राप्तश्चाभ्युदयो मम।
transliteration: nāhaṃ svapnamimaṃ manye svapne dṛṣṭvā hi vānaram na śakyo'bhyudayaḥ prāptuṃ prāptaścābhyudayo mama|
translation: अहम् I am, इमम् this, स्वप्नम् dream, न मन्ये I do not think so, स्वप्ने in a dream, वानरम् vanara, दृष्ट्वा having seen, अभ्युदयः welfare, प्राप्तुम् to attain, न शक्यः not possible, मम to me, अभ्युदयः pleasure, प्राप्तश्च is experienced.
explanation: "I do not think it is a dream. Pleasure cannot be experienced by seeing a vanara in a dream. I experience pleasure now (seeing a monkey in a dream is a bad omen).

shloka_text: किन्नु स्याचित्तमोहोऽयं भवेद्वातगतिस्त्वियम्।।5.34.23।। उन्मादजो विकारो वा स्यादियं मृगतृष्णिका।
transliteration: kinnu syācittamoho'yaṃ bhavedvātagatistviyam unmādajo vikāro vā syādiyaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇikā|
translation: अयम् this, चित्तमोहः delusion in the mind, स्यात् किं नु why do I feel like this? इयम् this kind of, वातगतिः mental inbalance, भवेत् may be, उन्मादजः developed due to madness, विकारो वा or else is it a change?, इयम् this, मृगतृष्णिका a mirage, स्यात् may be.
explanation: "Can this be a delusion of my mind or a mental imbalance (resulting in movement of the mind in the body). Is it a malady born of  my madness? Or is it a mirage?

shloka_text: अथवा नायमुन्मादो मोहोऽप्युन्मादलक्षणः।।5.34.24।। सम्बुध्ये चाहमात्मानमियं चापि वनौकसम्।
transliteration: athavā nāyamunmādo moho'pyunmādalakṣaṇaḥ sambudhye cāhamātmānamiyaṃ cāpi vanaukasam|
translation: अथवा if not, अयम् this, उन्मादः insanity, उन्मादलक्षणः sign of insanity, मोहोऽपि delusion also, न not, अहम् I, आत्मानम् myself, इमम् this, वनौकसम् vanara, सम्बुध्ये recognise.
explanation: "No, this cannot be insanity. nor even delusion. But I recognise this vanara well"

shloka_text: इत्येवं बहुधा सीता सम्प्रधार्य बलाबलम्।।5.34.25।। रक्षसां कामरूपत्वान्मेने तं राक्षसाधिपम्।
transliteration: ityevaṃ bahudhā sītā sampradhārya balābalam rakṣasāṃ kāmarūpatvānmene taṃ rākṣasādhipam|
translation: सीता Sita, इत्येवम् in this manner, बलाबलम् strength and weakness, बहुधा in many ways, सम्प्रधार्य after considering, रक्षसाम् of demons, कामरूपत्वात्  taking any form at will, तम् him, राक्षसाधिपम् king of demons, मेने he thought.
explanation: Considering the strength and weakness of demons in that manner Sita thought that Hanuman was none other than the king of demons who can asume any form at will.

shloka_text: एतां बुद्धिं तदा कृत्वा सीता सा तनुमध्यमा।।5.34.26।। न प्रतिव्याजहाराथ वानरं जनकात्मजा।
transliteration: etāṃ buddhiṃ tadā kṛtvā sītā sā tanumadhyamā na prativyājahārātha vānaraṃ janakātmajā|
translation: तदा then, तनुमध्यमा lady with a fair waist, जनकात्मजा Janaka's daughter, सा सीता that Sita, एताम् in this way, बुद्धिम् thought, कृत्वा having entertained, अथ then, वानरम् to vanara, न प्रतिव्याजहार did not respond.
explanation: Having entertained such thoughts, Sita, the lady with a fairwaist, daughter of Janaka,  did not respond to the vanara.

shloka_text: सीतायाश्चिन्तितं बुद्ध्वा हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः।।5.34.27।। श्रोत्रानुकूलैर्वचनैस्तदा तां संप्रहर्षयत्।
transliteration: sītāyāścintitaṃ buddhvā hanumānmārutātmajaḥ śrotrānukūlairvacanaistadā tāṃ saṃpraharṣayat|
translation: मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, हनुमान् Hanuman, सीतायाः Sita's, चिन्तितम् thought, बुद्ध्वा understood, तदा then, ताम् her, श्रोत्रानुकूलैः pleasing to hear, वचनैः by the words, सम्प्रहर्षयत् pleased.
explanation: Hanuman, son of the Windgod understood what was going on in Sita's mind and spoke pleasing words that brought joy in her.

shloka_text: आदित्य इव तेजस्वी लोककान्तश्शशी यथा।।5.34.28।। राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवो वैश्रवणो यथा। विक्रमेणोपपन्नश्च यथा विष्णुर्महायशाः।।5.34.29।।
transliteration: āditya iva tejasvī lokakāntaśśaśī yathā rājā sarvasya lokasya devo vaiśravaṇo yathā| vikrameṇopapannaśca yathā viṣṇurmahāyaśāḥ
translation: आदित्य इव like the Sun, तेजस्वी glorious, शशी यथा like the Moon, लोककान्तः brings delight to the whole world, देवः god, वैश्रवणो यथा like Vaisravana, सर्वस्य of all, लोकस्य of the worlds, राजा king, महायशाः is renowned, विष्णुः यथा like Visnu, विक्रमेण in valour, उपपन्नश्च endowed .
explanation: "Rama is glorious as the Sun, brings delight to the whole world like the Moon, is the king of kings like Vaisravana,  and renowned like Visnu endowed with valour.

shloka_text: आदित्य इव तेजस्वी लोककान्तश्शशी यथा।।5.34.28।। राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवो वैश्रवणो यथा। विक्रमेणोपपन्नश्च यथा विष्णुर्महायशाः।।5.34.29।।
transliteration: āditya iva tejasvī lokakāntaśśaśī yathā rājā sarvasya lokasya devo vaiśravaṇo yathā| vikrameṇopapannaśca yathā viṣṇurmahāyaśāḥ
translation: आदित्य इव like the Sun, तेजस्वी glorious, शशी यथा like the Moon, लोककान्तः brings delight to the whole world, देवः god, वैश्रवणो यथा like Vaisravana, सर्वस्य of all, लोकस्य of the worlds, राजा king, महायशाः is renowned, विष्णुः यथा like Visnu, विक्रमेण in valour, उपपन्नश्च endowed .
explanation: "Rama is glorious as the Sun, brings delight to the whole world like the Moon, is the king of kings like Vaisravana,  and renowned like Visnu endowed with valour.

shloka_text: सत्यवादी मधुरवाग्देवो वाचस्पतिर्यथा। रूपवान्सुभग श्रीमान् कन्दर्प इव मूर्तिमान्।।5.34.30।।
transliteration: satyavādī madhuravāgdevo vācaspatiryathā| rūpavānsubhaga śrīmān kandarpa iva mūrtimān
translation: सत्यवादी truthful in speech, देवः god, वाचस्पतिर्यथा like Brihaspati, मधुरवाक् sweet tongued, रूपवान् handsome, सुभगः graceful, श्रीमान् prosperous, मूर्तिमान् a personification, कन्दर्पः इव like Kamadeva.
explanation: "He is truthful in speech like Brihaspati, prosperous (like Kubera), sweettongued, handsome, graceful like Kamadeva.

shloka_text: स्थानक्रोधः प्रहर्ता च श्रेष्ठो लोके महारथः। बाहुच्छायामवष्टब्धो यस्य लोको महात्मनः।।5.34.31।।
transliteration: sthānakrodhaḥ prahartā ca śreṣṭho loke mahārathaḥ| bāhucchāyāmavaṣṭabdho yasya loko mahātmanaḥ
translation: स्थानक्रोधः who shows anger to the proper person, प्रहर्ता च who punishes, लोके the world, श्रेष्ठः supreme, महारथः great charioteer, लोकः in the world, यस्य whose, महात्मनः of the great self, बाहुच्छायामवष्टब्धो under the shadow of whose shoulders refuge is taken.
explanation: "He shows anger to one who deserves it, he is the foremost charioteer of the world and he is a great self under the shadow of whose shoulders the whole world takes refuge.

shloka_text: अपकृष्याश्रमपदान्मृगरूपेण राघवम्। शून्ये येनापनीतासि तस्य द्रक्ष्यसि यत्फलम्।।5.34.32।।
transliteration: apakṛṣyāśramapadānmṛgarūpeṇa rāghavam| śūnye yenāpanītāsi tasya drakṣyasi yatphalam
translation: येन since, राघवम् Rama, मृगरूपेण in the form of a deer, आश्रमपदात् from the hermitage, अपकृष्य were abducted, शून्ये isolated place, अपनीता you are borne away, असि you, तस्य its, यत्फलम् result, द्रक्ष्यसि you will see.
explanation: "You will see the consequences of the action of Ravana who abducted you deceitfully in the form of deer when Rama was away from the hermitage.

shloka_text: न चिराद्रावणं संख्ये यो वधिष्यति वीर्यवान्। रोषप्रमुक्तैरिषुभिर्ज्वलद्भिरिव पावकैः।।5.34.33।। तेनाहं प्रेषितो दूत स्त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः। त्वद्वियोगेन दुःखार्त स्स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्।।5.34.34।।
transliteration: na cirādrāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye yo vadhiṣyati vīryavān| roṣapramuktairiṣubhirjvaladbhiriva pāvakaiḥ tenāhaṃ preṣito dūta stvatsakāśamihāgataḥ| tvadviyogena duḥkhārta ssa tvāṃ kauśalamabravīt
translation: वीर्यवान् heroic, यः who, नचिरात् soon, रोषप्रमुक्तै: released in great anger, ज्वलद्भिः by burning, पावकैः इव like fire, इषुभि with arrows, संख्ये in war, रावणम् Ravana, वधिष्यति would slay, तेन therefore, दूतः envoy, प्रेषितः sent, इह here, त्वत्सकाशम् your presence, आगतः I have come, त्वद्वियोगेन due to separation from you, दुःखार्तः filled with sorrow, सः he, त्वाम् to you, कौशलम् welfare, अब्रवीत् asking.
explanation: "Heroic Rama will soon release many scorching, fiery arrows in anger and kill Ravana. I seek your permission as an envoy of Rama. Filled with grief by your separation, he has made inquiries about your welfare.

shloka_text: न चिराद्रावणं संख्ये यो वधिष्यति वीर्यवान्। रोषप्रमुक्तैरिषुभिर्ज्वलद्भिरिव पावकैः।।5.34.33।। तेनाहं प्रेषितो दूत स्त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः। त्वद्वियोगेन दुःखार्त स्स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्।।5.34.34।।
transliteration: na cirādrāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye yo vadhiṣyati vīryavān| roṣapramuktairiṣubhirjvaladbhiriva pāvakaiḥ tenāhaṃ preṣito dūta stvatsakāśamihāgataḥ| tvadviyogena duḥkhārta ssa tvāṃ kauśalamabravīt
translation: वीर्यवान् heroic, यः who, नचिरात् soon, रोषप्रमुक्तै: released in great anger, ज्वलद्भिः by burning, पावकैः इव like fire, इषुभि with arrows, संख्ये in war, रावणम् Ravana, वधिष्यति would slay, तेन therefore, दूतः envoy, प्रेषितः sent, इह here, त्वत्सकाशम् your presence, आगतः I have come, त्वद्वियोगेन due to separation from you, दुःखार्तः filled with sorrow, सः he, त्वाम् to you, कौशलम् welfare, अब्रवीत् asking.
explanation: "Heroic Rama will soon release many scorching, fiery arrows in anger and kill Ravana. I seek your permission as an envoy of Rama. Filled with grief by your separation, he has made inquiries about your welfare.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणश्च महातेजास्सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः। अभिवाद्य महाबाहुस्स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्।।5.34.35।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaśca mahātejāssumitrānandavardhanaḥ| abhivādya mahābāhussa tvāṃ kauśalamabravīt
translation: महातेजाः brilliant, सुमित्रानन्दस्सवर्धनः delight of Sumitra, महाबाहुः longarmed one, सः लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmna, त्वाम् to you, अभिवाद्य offering salutations, कौशलम् welfare, अब्रवीत् enquired.
explanation: "The brilliant, longarmed Lakshmana, delight of Sumitra enquires about your welfare and offers salutations to you.

shloka_text: रामस्य च सखा देवि सुग्रीवो नाम वानरः। राजा वानरमुख्यानां स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्।।5.34.36।।
transliteration: rāmasya ca sakhā devi sugrīvo nāma vānaraḥ| rājā vānaramukhyānāṃ sa tvāṃ kauśalamabravīt
translation: देवि O goddesslike lady, रामस्य Rama's, सखा friend, वानरमुख्यानाम् of vanara chiefs, राजा king, सुग्रीवो नाम called Sugriva, सः वानरः  that vanara, त्वाम् you, कौशलम् wellbeing, अब्रवीत् asked.
explanation: "O goddess like lady Rama's friend Sugriva, king of vanara chieftans inquires about your wellbeing.

shloka_text: नित्यं स्मरति रामस्त्वां ससुग्रीव स्सलक्ष्मणः। दिष्ट्या जीवसि वैदेहि राक्षसीवशमागता।।5.34.37।।
transliteration: nityaṃ smarati rāmastvāṃ sasugrīva ssalakṣmaṇaḥ| diṣṭyā jīvasi vaidehi rākṣasīvaśamāgatā
translation: ससुग्रीवः together with Sugriva, सलक्ष्मणः and Lakshmna, रामः Rama, त्वाम् you, नित्यम् always, स्मरति remembers, वैदेहि Vaidehi, राक्षसीवशम् under the clutches of shedemons, आगता come, दिष्ट्या luckily, जीवसि you are alive.
explanation: "O Vaidehi Rama, Lakshmana and Sugriva always remember you. Luckily you are alive even though you are under the clutches of shedemons.

shloka_text: नचिराद्द्रक्ष्यसे रामं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्। मध्ये वानरकोटीनां सुग्रीवं चामितौजसम्।।5.34.38।।
transliteration: nacirāddrakṣyase rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam| madhye vānarakoṭīnāṃ sugrīvaṃ cāmitaujasam
translation: रामम् Rama, महाबलम् mighty, लक्ष्मणं Lakshmana, वानरकोटीनाम् among crores of vanaras, मध्ये in the midst, अमितौजसम् of a hero of unlimited prowess, सुग्रीवं च also Sugriva, नचिरात् very soon, द्रक्ष्यसे you will see.
explanation: "Very soon you will see mighty Rama, Lakshmana and Sugriva of unlimited prowess surrounded by crores of vanaras.

shloka_text: अहं सुग्रीवसचिवो हनुमान्नाम वानरः। प्रविष्टो नगरीं लङ्कां लङ्घयित्वा महोदधिम्।।5.34.39।।
transliteration: ahaṃ sugrīvasacivo hanumānnāma vānaraḥ| praviṣṭo nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ laṅghayitvā mahodadhim
translation: अहम् I am, सुग्रीवसचिवः minister of Sugriva, हनुमान्नाम called Hanuman, वानरः a vanara, महोदधिम् great ocean, लङ्घयित्वा having leaped, लङ्कां नगरीम् city of Lanka, प्रविष्टः I have entered.
explanation: "I am Sugriva's minister known as Hanuman, a vanara who entered the city of Lanka after leaping over the great ocean.

shloka_text: कृत्वा मूर्ध्नि पदन्यासं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः। त्वां द्रष्टुमुपयातोऽहं समाश्रित्य पराक्रमम्।।5.34.40।।
transliteration: kṛtvā mūrdhni padanyāsaṃ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ| tvāṃ draṣṭumupayāto'haṃ samāśritya parākramam
translation: दुरात्मनः cruelminded, रावणस्य Ravana's, मूर्ध्नि: on the head, पदन्यासम् placing my foot, कृत्वा of having done, पराक्रमम् valour, समाश्रित्य using, अहम् I, त्वाम् you, द्रष्टुम् to see, उपयातः came here.
explanation: "Setting my foot with my valour on the head of the cruelminded Ravana, using my valour,  I came here to see you.

shloka_text: नाहमस्मि तथा देवि यथा मामवगच्छसि। विशङ्का त्यज्यतामेषा श्रद्धत्स्व वदतो मम।।5.34.41।।
transliteration: nāhamasmi tathā devi yathā māmavagacchasi| viśaṅkā tyajyatāmeṣā śraddhatsva vadato mama
translation: देवि O goddesslike lady, माम् me, यथा as, अवगच्छसि you suppose, अहम् I, तथा like that, नास्मि I am not, एषा such, विशङ्का suspicion, त्यज्यताम् shake off, वदतः as I speak, मम my, श्रद्धत्स्व you may trust.
explanation: "O goddesslike lady I am not  a deceitful person as you suppose me to be. Shake off your suspicion as I speak to you and trust me." इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुस्त्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyfourth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तां तु रामकथां श्रुत्वा वैदेही वानरर्षभात्। उवाच वचनं सान्त्वमिदं मधुरया गिरा।।5.35.1।।
transliteration: tāṃ tu rāmakathāṃ śrutvā vaidehī vānararṣabhāt| uvāca vacanaṃ sāntvamidaṃ madhurayā girā
translation: वैदेही Vaidehi, वानरर्षभात् from the bull among vanaras, ताम् that, रामकथाम् Rama's story, श्रुत्वा heard, मधुरया in sweet, गिरा word, सान्त्वम् polite, इदम् these, वचनम् words, उवाच spoke.
explanation: On hearing about Rama from the bull among vanaras, thus spoke Vaidehi politely in a sweet voice:
comments: Hanuman further narrates his story to Sita -- Gives description of Rama and Lakshmana

shloka_text: क्व ते रामेण संसर्गः कथं जानासि लक्ष्मणम्। वानराणां नराणां च कथमासीत्समागमः।।5.35.2।।
transliteration: kva te rāmeṇa saṃsargaḥ kathaṃ jānāsi lakṣmaṇam| vānarāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca kathamāsītsamāgamaḥ
translation: ते to you, रामेण with Rama, संसर्गः contact, क्व where, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, कथम् how, जानासि do you assess, वानराणाम् of vanaras, नराणां च a human, समागमः union, कथम् how, आसीत् took place.
explanation: "Where did you come in contact with Rama? How did you assess Lakshmana? How did an alliance of vanaras and humans take place?

shloka_text: यानि रामस्य लिङ्गानि लक्ष्मणस्य च वानर। तानि भूयस्समाचक्ष्व न मां शोकस्समाविशेत्।।5.35.3।।
transliteration: yāni rāmasya liṅgāni lakṣmaṇasya ca vānara| tāni bhūyassamācakṣva na māṃ śokassamāviśet
translation: वानर O vanara, रामस्य Rama's, लक्ष्मणस्य च and Lakshmana's, यानि those, लिङ्गानि identification marks, तानि those, समाचक्ष्व you may tell, माम् to me, भूयः again, शोकः sorrow, न not, समाविशेत् entire account.
explanation: "O vanara tell me all about the identification marks of Rama and Lakshmana again so that grief does not enter my mind.

shloka_text: कीदृशं तस्य संस्थानं रूपं रामस्य कीदृशम्। कथमूरू कथं बाहू लक्ष्मणस्य च शंस मे।।5.35.4।।
transliteration: kīdṛśaṃ tasya saṃsthānaṃ rūpaṃ rāmasya kīdṛśam| kathamūrū kathaṃ bāhū lakṣmaṇasya ca śaṃsa me
translation: तस्य his, रामस्य Rama's, लक्ष्मणस्य Lakshmana's, संस्थानम् form, कीदृशम् how, रूपम् form, कीदृशम् how does his look, ऊरू thighs, कथम् how, बाहू arms, कथम् how, मे to me, शंस tell.
explanation: "What does Rama look like? And Laksmana? How are his thighs, arms? Tell me".

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु वैदेह्या हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः। ततो रामं यथातत्त्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे।।5.35.5।।
transliteration: evamuktastu vaidehyā hanumānmārutātmajaḥ| tato rāmaṃ yathātattvamākhyātumupacakrame
translation: वैदेह्या by Vaidehi, एवम् in that manner, उक्तः spoken, मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, हनुमान् Hanuman, ततः thereafter, रामम् Rama, यथातत्त्वम् as it is, आख्यातुम् to describe, उपचक्रमे he started telling.
explanation: Questioned thus by Vaidehi, Hanuman, son of the Windgod started describing Rama's physique as it is.

shloka_text: जानन्ती बत दिष्ट्या मां वैदेहि परिपृच्छसि। भर्तुः कमलपत्त्राक्षि संस्थानं लक्ष्मणस्य च।।5.35.6।।
transliteration: jānantī bata diṣṭyā māṃ vaidehi paripṛcchasi| bhartuḥ kamalapattrākṣi saṃsthānaṃ lakṣmaṇasya ca
translation: कमलपत्त्राक्षि eyes like lotus petals, वैदेहि Vaidehi, जानन्ती even though you know, दिष्ट्या by good fortune, भर्तुः husband's, लक्ष्मणस्य च and Lakshmana's, संस्थानम् form and distinguishing marks, परिपृच्छसि have asked, बत indeed.
explanation: "O Vaidehi with eyes like lotus petals although you know your husband's and Lakshmana's form and distinguishing marks, it is my good fortune that you asked me (to describe them).

shloka_text: यानि रामस्य चिह्नानि लक्ष्मणस्य च यानि वै। लक्षितानि विशालाक्षि वदतश्शृणु तानि मे।।5.35.7।।
transliteration: yāni rāmasya cihnāni lakṣmaṇasya ca yāni vai| lakṣitāni viśālākṣi vadataśśṛṇu tāni me
translation: विशालाक्षि O largeeyed lady, रामस्य Rama's, यानि लक्षणानि those distinguishing marks, लक्ष्मणस्य च and Lakshmana's, यानि those, लक्षितानि signs, तानि them, वदतः as I describe, मे myself, शृणु listen.
explanation: "O largeeyed lady I will describe those distinguishing marks of Rama and Lakshmana Listen.

shloka_text: रामः कमलपत्त्राक्ष स्सर्वसत्त्वमनोहरः। रूपदाक्षिण्यसम्पन्नः प्रसूतो जनकात्मजे।।5.35.8।।
transliteration: rāmaḥ kamalapattrākṣa ssarvasattvamanoharaḥ| rūpadākṣiṇyasampannaḥ prasūto janakātmaje
translation: जनकात्मजे O Janaka's daughter, रामः Rama, कमलपत्त्राक्षः one who has eyes like lotus petals, सर्वसत्त्वमनोहरः one who delights all beings, रूपदाक्षिण्यसम्पन्नः endowed richly with charm and politeness, प्रसूतः born with.
explanation: "O daughter of Janaka Rama with eyes like lotus petals is a person born with a delightful form, richly endowed with indescribable charm and politeness.

shloka_text: तेजसाऽदित्य सङ्काशः क्षमया पृथिवीसमः। बृहस्पतिसमो बुद्ध्या यशसा वासवोपमः।।5.35.9।।
transliteration: tejasā'ditya saṅkāśaḥ kṣamayā pṛthivīsamaḥ| bṛhaspatisamo buddhyā yaśasā vāsavopamaḥ
