translation: तेजसा in effulgence, आदित्यसङ्काशः vies with the Sun, क्षमया in tolerance, पृथिवीसमः equals the earth, बुद्ध्या in intelligence, बृहस्पतिसमः equal to Brihaspathi, यशसा in fame, वासवोपमः equals Indra.
explanation: "He vies with the Sun in effulgence, with earth in forbearance, with Brihaspati in intelligence, and in fame with Indra.

shloka_text: रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य स्वजनस्याभिरक्षिता। रक्षिता स्वस्य वृत्तस्य धर्मस्य च परन्तपः।।5.35.10।।
transliteration: rakṣitā jīvalokasya svajanasyābhirakṣitā| rakṣitā svasya vṛttasya dharmasya ca parantapaḥ
translation: परन्तपः scorcher of enemies, जीवलोकस्य of the world of living beings, रक्षिता protector, स्वजनस्य of his own people, अभिरक्षिता protector, स्वस्य of his own, वृत्तस्य of the race, धर्मस्य च and guards righteousness
explanation: "Rama is a protector of the entire world of living beings not to speak of his own people. He is a protector of his own race. He guards righteousness. He is a scorcher of enemies.

shloka_text: रामो भामिनि लोकस्य चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य रक्षिता। मर्यादानां च लोकस्य कर्ता कारयिता च सः।।5.35.11।।
transliteration: rāmo bhāmini lokasya cāturvarṇyasya rakṣitā| maryādānāṃ ca lokasya kartā kārayitā ca saḥ
translation: भामिनि O beautiful lady, रामः Rama, लोकस्य world's, चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य of the four classes of society, रक्षिता protector, सः he, लोकानाम् of all the worlds, मर्यादानाम् code and conduct, कर्ता maker, कारयिताचैव will make others follow.
explanation: "O beautiful lady Rama is a protector of the four classes of society (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaisya and Sudra) in the world. He follows codes of conduct and makes others follow them.

shloka_text: अर्चिष्मानर्चितोऽत्यर्थं ब्रह्मचर्यव्रते स्थितः। साधूनामुपकारज्ञः प्रचारज्ञश्च कर्मणाम्।।5.35.12।।
transliteration: arciṣmānarcito'tyarthaṃ brahmacaryavrate sthitaḥ| sādhūnāmupakārajñaḥ pracārajñaśca karmaṇām
translation: अर्चिष्मान् luminous, अत्यर्थम् intensely, अर्चितः worshipped, ब्रह्मचर्यव्रते observing the vow of selfcontrol, स्थितः one who is steadfast, साधूनाम् for the holy men, उपकारज्ञः recognises right action, कर्मणाम् rites, प्रचारज्ञश्च  of the ways of  administration.
explanation: "He is luminous and highly revered. He observes vow of selfcontrol. He is steadfast and recognises services rendered by sages. He is aware of the rites and the ways of administration.

shloka_text: राजविद्याविनीतश्च ब्राह्मणानामुपासिता। श्रुतवान्शीलसम्पन्नो विनीतश्च परन्तपः।।5.35.13।।
transliteration: rājavidyāvinītaśca brāhmaṇānāmupāsitā| śrutavānśīlasampanno vinītaśca parantapaḥ
translation: राजविद्याविनीतश्च welltrained in statecraft, ब्राह्मणानाम् of the brahmins, उपासिता a devotee, श्रुतवान् learned in scriptures, शीलसम्पन्नः endowed with excellent conduct, विनीतः is disciplined, परन्तपः  is a scorcher of enemies.
explanation: "He is welltrained in statecraft. He is devoted to brahmins. Endowed with an excellent conduct, he is learned in scriptures and a scorcher of enemies.

shloka_text: यजुर्वेदविनीतश्च वेदविद्भिस्सुपूजितः। धनुर्वेदे च वेदेषु वेदाङ्गेषु च निष्ठितः।।5.35.14।।
transliteration: yajurvedavinītaśca vedavidbhissupūjitaḥ| dhanurvede ca vedeṣu vedāṅgeṣu ca niṣṭhitaḥ
translation: यजुर्वेदविनीतश्च versed in Yajurveda, वेदविद्भिः by the knowers of the Vedas, सुपूजितः respected, धनुर्वेदे च and in Dhanurveda also, वेदेषु in other Vedas also, वेदाङ्गेषु च Vedangas (auxillary Vedas) also, निष्ठितः is an expert.
explanation: "He is versed in Yajurveda and is respected by Vedic scholars. He has mastered Dhanurveda and other Vedas and auxillary Vedas as well.

shloka_text: विपुलांसो महाबाहुः कम्बुग्रीवश्शुभाननः। गूढजत्रुस्सुताम्राक्षो रामो देवि जनै श्श्रुतः।।5.35.15।।
transliteration: vipulāṃso mahābāhuḥ kambugrīvaśśubhānanaḥ| gūḍhajatrussutāmrākṣo rāmo devi janai śśrutaḥ
translation: देवि goddess like lady, रामः Rama, विपुलां सः broadshouldered, महाबाहुः strongarmed, कम्बुग्रीवः with conchshaped neck, शुभाननः with an auspicious countenance, गूढजत्रुः has round shoulders, सुताम्राक्षः copperyred eyes  जनैः in all worlds, श्रुतः renowned.
explanation: "O godlike lady Rama has broad shoulders, strong arms, conchshaped neck and an auspicious countenance. With his fleshy round arms and copperyred eyes, he is renowned in all the worlds.

shloka_text: दुन्दुभिस्वननिर्घोष स्स्निग्धवर्णः प्रतापवान्। सम स्समविभक्ताङ्गो वर्णं श्यामं समाश्रितः।।5.35.16।।
transliteration: dundubhisvananirghoṣa ssnigdhavarṇaḥ pratāpavān| sama ssamavibhaktāṅgo varṇaṃ śyāmaṃ samāśritaḥ
translation: दुन्दुभिस्वननिर्घोषः his tone is resonant like the drums, स्निग्धवर्णः has beautiful shining complexion, प्रतापवान् full of valour, समः not too tall or short, समविभक्ताङ्गः his limbs are symmetrical, श्यामम् dark, वर्णम् colour, समाश्रितः has proportionate limbs.
explanation: "His tone is resonant like drums, he has a beautiful, dark, shining complexion. He has symmetrical, well proportioned limbs. He is neither too tall nor too short.

shloka_text: त्रिस्थिरस्त्रिप्रलम्बश्च त्रिसमस्त्रिषु चोन्नतः। त्रिताम्रस्त्रिषु च स्निग्धो गम्भीरस्त्रिषु नित्यशः।।5.35.17।।
transliteration: tristhirastripralambaśca trisamastriṣu connataḥ| tritāmrastriṣu ca snigdho gambhīrastriṣu nityaśaḥ
translation: त्रिस्थिरः has the three stiff limbs (chest, fist and wrists), त्रिप्रलम्बश्च long in three (arms, eyebrows and scrotum), त्रिसमः has three even parts (locks of hair, knees and testicles), त्रिषु elevated in three parts (abdomen, navel and chest), उन्नतः raised, त्रिषु च all the three parts (soles, nails and eyes), स्निग्धः has coppery reddish colour, नित्यशः all over, त्रिषु in the three parts (the underlines of feet, the hair and the reproductive  organs), गम्भीरः is majestic.
explanation: "He has three stiff parts, three long parts, three even parts, three shining parts, elevated in three parts, has three raised parts, his body has lines in three parts and is  of coppery reddish colour in three parts. He has a majestic look.

shloka_text: त्रिवलीवांस्त्र्यवनतश्चतुर्व्यङ्गस्त्रिशीर्षवान्। चतुष्कलश्चतुर्लेखश्चतुष्किष्कुश्चतु स्समः।।5.35.18।।
transliteration: trivalīvāṃstryavanataścaturvyaṅgastriśīrṣavān| catuṣkalaścaturlekhaścatuṣkiṣkuścatu ssamaḥ
translation: त्रिवलीवान् has three folds on his neck, स्त्र्यवनतः his nipples and middle of his soles are depressed, चतुर्व्यङ्गः four parts of his body are depressedneck, penis, shanks and back, त्रिशीर्षवान् has three spirals in the head, चतुष्कलः has four lines under his thumb, चतुर्लेखः has four lines on the forehead, चतुष्किष्कुः he is four cubits in height, चतुस्समः he has arms, knees, cheeks and thighs well proportioned
explanation: "He has three folds in the skin of his neck and belly, is depressed in the middle of his soles and the nipples, undersized at four placesthe neck, penis, shanks and back, has three spirals on his head, has four lines under his thumb, has four lines on his forehead, he is a person with four cubits in height and symmetrical arms, cheeks and thighs.

shloka_text: चतुर्दशसमद्वन्द्वश्चतुर्दंष्ट्रश्चतुर्गतिः। महोष्ठहनुनासश्च पञ्चस्निग्धोऽष्टवंशवान्।।5.35.19।।
transliteration: caturdaśasamadvandvaścaturdaṃṣṭraścaturgatiḥ| mahoṣṭhahanunāsaśca pañcasnigdho'ṣṭavaṃśavān
translation: चतुर्दशसमद्वन्द्वः he is person with the fourteen parts of his body (eyebrows, nostrils, eyes, ears, lips, nipples, elbows, wrists, knees, testicles, loins, arms, legs and buttocks) in good proportion, चतुर्दंष्ट्रः he is one with four sharp teeth, चतुर्गतिः he moves like a lion, leopard, elephant and bull as occasion demands, महोष्ठहनुनासश्च he has sharp nose, charming lips and jaws, पञ्चस्निग्ध: he is one with five smooth parts (hair, eyes, skin, teeth and feet), अष्टवंशवान् his eight parts of the body (backbone, trunk, limbs, fingers, toes, nose, eyes and testicles) are long.
explanation: "He is a person with his pairs of eyebrows, nostrils, eyes, ears, lips, nipples, elbows, wrists, knees, testicles, loins, arms, legs and buttocks in good symmetry he has four sharp teeth. He walks in different gaits like a lion, leopard, elephant and bull as occasion demands he has sharp nose, charming lips and jaws. He has smooth hair, eyes, skin, teeth and feet and his eight parts of his body namely back, trunk, limbs, fingers, toes, eyes and testicles are long.

shloka_text: दशपद्मो दशबृहत्त्रिभिर्व्याप्तो द्विशुक्लवान्। षडुन्नतो नवतनुस्त्रिभिर्व्याप्नोति राघवः।।5.35.20।।
transliteration: daśapadmo daśabṛhattribhirvyāpto dviśuklavān| ṣaḍunnato navatanustribhirvyāpnoti rāghavaḥ
translation: राघवः Rama, दशपद्मः ten lotuslike limbs (eyes, face, mouth, tongue, lips, cheeks, nipples, nails, feet and hands), दशबृहत् he is one with ten wellproportioned limbs (head, forehead, ears, neck, chest, heart, belly, hands, legs, buttocks), त्रिभिः covered with three aspects (splendour, fame and glory), व्याप्तः well known, द्विशुक्लवान् two white limbs teeth and eyes, षडुन्नतः he has six elevated  limbs (nose, shoulders, forehead, chest and arm pits), नवतनुः has nine fine features (moustache, nails, knuckles, beard, skin, hair, penis, acumen, perception), त्रिभिः he pursues spiritual merit, worldly comforts and sensual delight in three periodsforenoon, middday and evening of the day, व्याप्नोति follows righteous principles.
explanation: "Ten limbs of the body resemble lotuses. He has proportionate limbs. He is known by the virtue of his spledour, fame and glory. Both his teeth and eyes are fair. Six parts of his body are elevated, nine parts of his body are fine and sharp. He pursues spiritual merit, worldly comfort and sensual delight in three periods of the dayforenoon, midday and evening. He always adopts the righteous way of life.

shloka_text: सत्यधर्मपरश्श्रीमान् सङ्ग्रहानुग्रहे रतः। देशकालविभागज्ञस्सर्वलोकप्रियंवदः।।5.35.21।।
transliteration: satyadharmaparaśśrīmān saṅgrahānugrahe rataḥ| deśakālavibhāgajñassarvalokapriyaṃvadaḥ
translation: सत्यधर्मपरः established in truth and righteousness, श्रीमान् prosperous, सङ्ग्रहानुग्रहे रतः he is involved in both accumulation and favourable disposition towards others, देशकालविभागज्ञः who discharges his duties at proper time and place, सर्वलोकप्रियंवदः who is loved by all for his endearing words.
explanation: "He is ever established in truth and righteousness. He is prosperous and desires to accumulate wealth in order to shower favour on others. He knows the right use of time and place in discharging his duties. He has endeared himself to all by his words.

shloka_text: भ्राता तस्य च द्वैमात्रस्सौमित्रिरपराजितः। अनुरागेण रूपेण गुणैश्चैव तथाविधः।।5.35.22।।
transliteration: bhrātā tasya ca dvaimātrassaumitriraparājitaḥ| anurāgeṇa rūpeṇa guṇaiścaiva tathāvidhaḥ
translation: तस्य his, द्वैमात्रः born of a different mother, भ्राता brother, अपराजितः one who has never been defeated, सौमित्रिः Saumitri, अनुरागेण in affection, रूपेण in charm, गुणैश्चैव in virtues, तथाविधः similar to him.
explanation: "His invincible brother Saumitri born of a different mother is a replica of Rama in affection, charm and virtues.

shloka_text: तावुभौ नरशार्दूलौ त्वद्दर्शनसमुत्सुकौ। विचिन्वन्तौ महीं कृत्स्नामस्माभिरभिसङ्गतौ।।5.35.23।।
transliteration: tāvubhau naraśārdūlau tvaddarśanasamutsukau| vicinvantau mahīṃ kṛtsnāmasmābhirabhisaṅgatau
translation: नरशार्दूलौ tiger among men, तौ they, उभौ both, त्वद्दर्शनसमुत्सुकौ eager to see you, कृत्स्नाम् entire, महीम् earth, विचिन्वन्तौ both searching for, अस्माभिः by us, अभिसङ्गतौ they met us.
explanation: "While earnestly searching for you all over the earth both tigers among men came in contact with us.

shloka_text: त्वामेव मार्गमाणौ तौ विचरन्तौ वसुन्धराम्। ददर्शतुर्मृगपतिं पूर्वजेनावरोपितम्।।5.35.24।। ऋश्यमूकस्य पृष्ठे तु बहुपादपसङ्कुले। भ्रातुर्भयार्तमासीनं सुग्रीवं प्रियदर्शनम्।।5.35.25।।
transliteration: tvāmeva mārgamāṇau tau vicarantau vasundharām| dadarśaturmṛgapatiṃ pūrvajenāvaropitam ṛśyamūkasya pṛṣṭhe tu bahupādapasaṅkule| bhrāturbhayārtamāsīnaṃ sugrīvaṃ priyadarśanam
translation: त्वामेव for you, मार्गमाणौ while searching, वसुन्धराम् all over the earth, विचरन्तौ while both were wandering, तौ they both, बहुपादपसङ्कुले filled with many trees, ऋश्यमूकस्य पृष्ठे on the mountain Rshyamuka, आसीनम् seated, पूर्वजेन by the elder brother, अवरोपितम् one who has been thrown out, भ्रातुः brother's, भयार्तम् frightened, प्रियदर्शनम् one who is pleasing to see, मृगपतिम् lord of animals, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, ददर्शतुः both of them saw.
explanation: "While both of them were wandering, searching for you all over the earth they saw Sugriva, the lord of animals who had been thrown out of kingship by his elder brother and was living on the mountain Rshyamuka frightened of him.

shloka_text: त्वामेव मार्गमाणौ तौ विचरन्तौ वसुन्धराम्। ददर्शतुर्मृगपतिं पूर्वजेनावरोपितम्।।5.35.24।। ऋश्यमूकस्य पृष्ठे तु बहुपादपसङ्कुले। भ्रातुर्भयार्तमासीनं सुग्रीवं प्रियदर्शनम्।।5.35.25।।
transliteration: tvāmeva mārgamāṇau tau vicarantau vasundharām| dadarśaturmṛgapatiṃ pūrvajenāvaropitam ṛśyamūkasya pṛṣṭhe tu bahupādapasaṅkule| bhrāturbhayārtamāsīnaṃ sugrīvaṃ priyadarśanam
translation: त्वामेव for you, मार्गमाणौ while searching, वसुन्धराम् all over the earth, विचरन्तौ while both were wandering, तौ they both, बहुपादपसङ्कुले filled with many trees, ऋश्यमूकस्य पृष्ठे on the mountain Rshyamuka, आसीनम् seated, पूर्वजेन by the elder brother, अवरोपितम् one who has been thrown out, भ्रातुः brother's, भयार्तम् frightened, प्रियदर्शनम् one who is pleasing to see, मृगपतिम् lord of animals, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, ददर्शतुः both of them saw.
explanation: "While both of them were wandering, searching for you all over the earth they saw Sugriva, the lord of animals who had been thrown out of kingship by his elder brother and was living on the mountain Rshyamuka frightened of him.

shloka_text: वयं तु हरिराजं तं सुग्रीवं सत्यसङ्गरम्। परिचर्यामहे राज्यात्पूर्वजेनावरोपितम्।।5.35.26।।
transliteration: vayaṃ tu harirājaṃ taṃ sugrīvaṃ satyasaṅgaram| paricaryāmahe rājyātpūrvajenāvaropitam
translation: वयं तु we too, पूर्वजेन by his elder brother, राज्यात् from the kingdom, अवरोपितम् deposed, सत्यसङ्गरम् one who is committed to truth, हरिराजम् king of vanaras, तम् him, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, परिचर्यामहे we serve him.
explanation: "Sugriva, king of vanaras who is committed to defend truth has been deposed from the kingdom by his elder brother. We keep attending on him.

shloka_text: ततस्तौ चीरवसनौ धनुः प्रवरपाणिनौ। ऋश्यमूकस्य शैलस्य रम्यं देशमुपागतौ।।5.35.27।।
transliteration: tatastau cīravasanau dhanuḥ pravarapāṇinau| ṛśyamūkasya śailasya ramyaṃ deśamupāgatau
translation: ततः then, चीरवसनौ clad in bark robes, धनुःप्रवरपाणिनौ armed with powerful bows, तौ both, ऋश्यमूकस्य शैलस्य on the Rshyamukha mountain, रम्यम् beautiful, देशम् location, उपागतौ both reached.
explanation: "Both the princes clad in bark robes and armed with powerful bows reached the beautiful location of Rshyamukha mountain.

shloka_text: स तौ दृष्ट्वा नरव्याघ्रौ धन्विनौ वानरर्षभः। अवप्लुतो गिरेस्तस्य शिखरं भयमोहितः।।5.35.28।।
transliteration: sa tau dṛṣṭvā naravyāghrau dhanvinau vānararṣabhaḥ| avapluto girestasya śikharaṃ bhayamohitaḥ
translation: सः he, वानरर्षभः bull among vanaras, धन्विनौ armed with bows, तौ both of them, नरव्याघ्रौ tigers among men, दृष्ट्वा on seeing, भयमोहितः deluded with fear, तस्य from that, गिरेः mountain, शिखरम् top, अभिप्लुतः jumped.
explanation: "On seeing the tigers among men armed with bows, Sugriva, the bull among vanaras jumped from the mountain deluded with fear and reached the peak.

shloka_text: ततस्स शिखरे तस्मिन्वानरेन्द्रो व्यवस्थितः। तयोस्समीपं मामेव प्रेषयामास सत्वरम्।।5.35.29।।
transliteration: tatassa śikhare tasminvānarendro vyavasthitaḥ| tayossamīpaṃ māmeva preṣayāmāsa satvaram
translation: ततः thereafter, सः he, वानरेन्द्रः lord of vanaras, तस्मिन् on that, शिखरे mountain top, व्यवस्थितः staying there, मामेव me only, तयोः of both of them, समीपम् towads, सत्वरम् quickly, प्रेषयामास sent.
explanation: "Thereafter the lord of vanaras staying on the mountain top quickly sent me to meet both of them.

shloka_text: तावहं पुरुषव्याघ्रौ सुग्रीववचनात्प्रभू। रूपलक्षणसम्पन्नौ कृताञ्जलिरुपस्थितः।।5.35.30।।
transliteration: tāvahaṃ puruṣavyāghrau sugrīvavacanātprabhū| rūpalakṣaṇasampannau kṛtāñjalirupasthitaḥ
translation: अहम् I, सुग्रीववचनात् according to the instruction of Sugriva, पुरुषव्याघ्रौ two tigers among men, प्रभू two lords, रूपलक्षणसम्पन्नौ both endowed with charming appearance and auspicious marks, तौ both, कृताञ्जलिः joined palms in salutation, उपस्थितः approached.
explanation: At Sugriva's bidding I approached with joined palms those two tigers among men, two lords endowed with charming form and auspicious marks.

shloka_text: तौ परिज्ञाततत्त्वार्थौ मया प्रीतिसमन्वितौ। पृष्ठमारोप्य तं देशं प्रापितौ पुरुषर्षभौ।।5.35.31।।
transliteration: tau parijñātatattvārthau mayā prītisamanvitau| pṛṣṭhamāropya taṃ deśaṃ prāpitau puruṣarṣabhau
translation: परिज्ञाततत्त्वर्थौ realised the true position, प्रीतिसमन्वितौ filled with pleasure, पुरुषर्षभौ two bulls among men, तौ both, मया by me, पृष्ठम् back, आरोप्य placing, तं देशम् to that place, प्रापितौ carried.
explanation: "I recognised the true status of  both the mighty men who were filled with joy, placed them on my back, and reached the mountaintop.

shloka_text: निवेदितौ च तत्त्वेन सुग्रीवाय महात्मने। तयोरन्योन्यसल्लापाद्भृशं प्रीतिरजायत।।5.35.32।।
transliteration: niveditau ca tattvena sugrīvāya mahātmane| tayoranyonyasallāpādbhṛśaṃ prītirajāyata
translation: महात्मने to the great self, सुग्रीवाय to Sugriva, तत्त्वेन faithfully, निवेदितौ reported by me, तयोः of both of them, अन्योन्यसल्लापात् got to know each other through conversation, भृशम् fond, प्रीतिः friendship, अजायत developed.
explanation: "I reported faithfully about both the highsouled men to Sugriva. As they got to know each other through conversation a fast friendship developed between them.

shloka_text: ततस्तौ प्रीतिसम्पन्नौ हरीश्वरनरेश्वरौ। परस्परकृताश्वासौ कथया पूर्ववृत्तया।।5.35.33।।
transliteration: tatastau prītisampannau harīśvaranareśvarau| parasparakṛtāśvāsau kathayā pūrvavṛttayā
translation: ततः then, प्रीतिसम्पन्नौ full of joy, तौ both, हरीश्वरनरेश्वरौ king of monkeys and the king of people, पूर्ववृत्तया with their past, कथया with account, परस्परकृताश्वासौ they consoled each other.
explanation: Then the king of the monkeys and the king of men, full of joy, consoled each other with the account of their past.

shloka_text: ततस्स सान्त्वयामास सुग्रीवं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। स्त्रीहेतोर्वालिना भ्रात्रा निरस्तमुरुतेजसा।।5.35.34।।
transliteration: tatassa sāntvayāmāsa sugrīvaṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ| strīhetorvālinā bhrātrā nirastamurutejasā
translation: ततः thereafter, सः he, लक्ष्मणाग्रजः the elder brother of Lakshmana, उरुतेजसा with great prowess, भ्रात्रा by the brother, वालिना by Vali, स्त्रीहेतो on account of a woman, निरस्तम्  deposed, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, सान्त्वयामास consoled.
explanation: "Then Rama, consoled Sugriva who was dethroned and abandoned on acount of a woman by his brother Vali, endowed with great prowess.

shloka_text: ततस्त्वन्नाशजं शोकं रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। लक्ष्मणो वानरेन्द्राय सुग्रीवाय न्यवेदयत्।।5.35.35।।
transliteration: tatastvannāśajaṃ śokaṃ rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ| lakṣmaṇo vānarendrāya sugrīvāya nyavedayat
translation: ततः then, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, अक्लिष्टकर्मणः one who is adept in accomplishing tasks with ease, रामस्य Rama's, त्वन्नाशजम् on account of your loss, शोकम् grief, वानरेन्द्राय to the lord of vanaras, सुग्रीवाय to Sugriva, न्यवेदयत् revealed.
explanation: "Then Lakshmana spoke to the lord of vanaras, Sugriva about your loss and the grief caused to Rama, who is adept in accomplishing difficult deeds with ease.

shloka_text: स श्रुत्वा वानरेन्द्रस्तु लक्ष्मणेनेरितं वचः। तदासीन्निष्प्रभोऽत्यर्थं ग्रहग्रस्त इवांशुमान्।।5.35.36।।
transliteration: sa śrutvā vānarendrastu lakṣmaṇeneritaṃ vacaḥ| tadāsīnniṣprabho'tyarthaṃ grahagrasta ivāṃśumān
translation: सः he, वानरेन्द्रस्तु to the king of vanaras, लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, ईरितम् spoken वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, तदा then, ग्रहग्रस्तः overshadowed by the planet, अंशुमानिव like the Sun, अत्यर्थम् extremely, निष्प्रभः lustreless, आसीत् became.
explanation: "Having heard the words of Lakshmana, the king of vanaras became extremely lustreless like the Sun overshadowed by the planet Rahu.

shloka_text: ततस्त्वद्गात्रशोभीनि रक्षसा ह्रियमाणया। यान्याभरणजालानि पातितानि महीतले।।5.35.37।। तानि सर्वाणि रामाय आनीय हरियूथपाः। संहृष्टा दर्शयामासुर्गतिं तु न विदुस्तव।।5.35.38।।
transliteration: tatastvadgātraśobhīni rakṣasā hriyamāṇayā| yānyābharaṇajālāni pātitāni mahītale tāni sarvāṇi rāmāya ānīya hariyūthapāḥ| saṃhṛṣṭā darśayāmāsurgatiṃ tu na vidustava
translation: ततः at that time, रक्षसा by the demon, ह्रियमाणया when you were borne away, त्वद्गात्रशोभिनी adorned your limbs, यानि those, आभरणजालानि bundle of ornaments, पातितानि dropped down, तानि सर्वाणि all of them, आनीय brought, हरियूथपाः vanara leaders, संहृष्टाः with great joy, रामाय to Rama, दर्शयामासुः showed, तव your, गतिं तु whereabouts, न विदुः did not know.
explanation: The vanara leaders joyfully brought to Rama all the bundles of ornaments that had dropped to the ground from your limbs as the demon bore you away, and showed them, though they did not know your whereabouts.

shloka_text: ततस्त्वद्गात्रशोभीनि रक्षसा ह्रियमाणया। यान्याभरणजालानि पातितानि महीतले।।5.35.37।। तानि सर्वाणि रामाय आनीय हरियूथपाः। संहृष्टा दर्शयामासुर्गतिं तु न विदुस्तव।।5.35.38।।
transliteration: tatastvadgātraśobhīni rakṣasā hriyamāṇayā| yānyābharaṇajālāni pātitāni mahītale tāni sarvāṇi rāmāya ānīya hariyūthapāḥ| saṃhṛṣṭā darśayāmāsurgatiṃ tu na vidustava
translation: ततः at that time, रक्षसा by the demon, ह्रियमाणया when you were borne away, त्वद्गात्रशोभिनी adorned your limbs, यानि those, आभरणजालानि bundle of ornaments, पातितानि dropped down, तानि सर्वाणि all of them, आनीय brought, हरियूथपाः vanara leaders, संहृष्टाः with great joy, रामाय to Rama, दर्शयामासुः showed, तव your, गतिं तु whereabouts, न विदुः did not know.
explanation: The vanara leaders joyfully brought to Rama all the bundles of ornaments that had dropped to the ground from your limbs as the demon bore you away, and showed them, though they did not know your whereabouts.

shloka_text: तानि रामाय दत्तानि मयैवोपहृतानि च। स्वनवन्त्यवकीर्णानि तस्मिन्विगतचेतसि।।5.35.39।।
transliteration: tāni rāmāya dattāni mayaivopahṛtāni ca| svanavantyavakīrṇāni tasminvigatacetasi
translation: मयैव by me, उपहृतानि collected, तानि those ornaments, रामाय to Rama, दत्तानि gave, तस्मिन् them, विगतचेतसि lost senses, स्वनवन्ति making jingling sound, अवकीर्णानि having scattered.
explanation: "I collected the ornaments and gave them to Rama. He lost his senses on seeing the jingling ornaments scattered.

shloka_text: तान्यङ्के दर्शनीयानि कृत्वा बहुविधं तव। तेन देवप्रकाशेन देवेन परिदेवितम्।।5.35.40।।
transliteration: tānyaṅke darśanīyāni kṛtvā bahuvidhaṃ tava| tena devaprakāśena devena paridevitam
translation: दर्शनीयानि beautiful ones, तव your, तानि those, अङ्के on his lap, कृत्वा having placed, देवप्रकाशेन by an effulgent one looking like the divine, तेन by him, देवेन divine self, बहुविधम् in many ways, परिदेवितम् wailed.
explanation: "The divine self who is effulgent like god wailed in many ways placing the beautiful ornaments on his lap.

shloka_text: पश्यतस्तानि रुदतस्ताम्यतश्च पुनः पुनः। प्रादीपयन्दाशरथेस्तानि शोकहुताशनम्।।5.35.41।।
transliteration: paśyatastāni rudatastāmyataśca punaḥ punaḥ| prādīpayandāśarathestāni śokahutāśanam
translation: तानि them, पश्यतः as looked at, रुदतः while he wept, पुनः पुनः again and again, ताम्यतश्च  regretting, दाशरथेः Dasaratha's son Rama's, शोकहुताशनम् fire in the form of grief, तानि them, प्रादीपयन् inflamed.
explanation: "Rama looked at them and wept clasping them again and again in grief which inflamed like fire.

shloka_text: शयितं च चिरं तेन दुःखार्तेन महात्मना। मयापि विविधैर्वाक्यैः कृच्छ्रादुत्थापितः पुनः।।5.35.42।।
transliteration: śayitaṃ ca ciraṃ tena duḥkhārtena mahātmanā| mayāpi vividhairvākyaiḥ kṛcchrādutthāpitaḥ punaḥ
translation: दुःखार्तेन immersed in sorrow, तेन by him, महात्मना by the great self, शयितं च lay down, मयापि by me also, विविधैः by many, वाक्यैः by words, कृच्छ्रात् with great difficulty, पुनः again, उत्थापितः helped to get up.
explanation: "Rama, the great self, immersed in sorrow lay down on the ground. I also consoled him with great difficulty and helped him to get up.

shloka_text: तानि दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुर्दर्शयित्वा मुहुर्मुहुः। राघवस्सह सौमित्रिस्सुग्रीवे स न्यवेदयत्।।5.35.43।।
transliteration: tāni dṛṣṭvā mahābāhurdarśayitvā muhurmuhuḥ| rāghavassaha saumitrissugrīve sa nyavedayat
translation: महाबाहुः longarmed one, सः राघवः that Rama, सहसौमित्रिः along with Lakshmana, तानि those, मुहुः मुहुः again and again, दर्शयित्वा after showing, सुग्रीवे to Sugriva, न्यवेदयत् presented.
explanation: "Longarmed Rama along with Lakshmana looked at them again and again and gave them to the care of Sugriva.

shloka_text: स तवादर्शनादार्ये राघवः परितप्यते। महता ज्वलता नित्यमग्निनेवाग्निपर्वतः।।5.35.44।।
transliteration: sa tavādarśanādārye rāghavaḥ paritapyate| mahatā jvalatā nityamagninevāgniparvataḥ
translation: आर्ये O divine lady, सः राघवः that Rama, तव your, अदर्शनात् separation from you, नित्यम् always, ज्वलता burning, महता great, अग्निना in fire, अग्निपर्वतः इव like a mountain of fire, परितप्यते  ever blazing.
explanation: "O divine lady on account of your separation he is ever blazing like a mountain of fire (Samvartaka).

shloka_text: त्वत्कृते तमनिद्रा च शोकश्चिन्ता च राघवम्। तापयन्ति महात्मानमग्न्यगारमिवाग्नयः।।5.35.45।।
transliteration: tvatkṛte tamanidrā ca śokaścintā ca rāghavam| tāpayanti mahātmānamagnyagāramivāgnayaḥ
translation: त्वत्कृते on account of, महात्मानम् the great one, तं राघवम् that Rama, अनिद्रा च not sleeping, शोकः grief, चिन्ता च intense anxiety, अग्न्यगारम् like a furnace, अग्नयः इव like the three fires, तापयन्ति keep intensely heated.
explanation: "Rama is burning like a furnace by (three fires) sleeplessness, grief and intense anxiety just as the three sacred fires keep a firesanctuary intensely heated.

shloka_text: तवादर्शनशोकेन राघवः प्रविचाल्यते। महता भूमिकम्पेन महानिव शिलोच्चयः।।5.35.46।।
transliteration: tavādarśanaśokena rāghavaḥ pravicālyate| mahatā bhūmikampena mahāniva śiloccayaḥ
translation: तव your, अदर्शनशोकेन by the sorrow of not being able to see you, राघवः Rama of Raghu dynasty, महता with great, भूमिकम्पेन by earthquake, महान् great, शिलोच्छयः lofty mountain, प्रविचाल्यते is shaken.
explanation: "On account of sorrow caused by not being able to see you, Rama of Raghu dynasty is shaken up like a lofty mountain is shaken by earthquake.

shloka_text: काननानि सुरम्याणि नदीः प्रस्रवणानि च। चरन्न रतिमाप्नोति त्वामपश्यन्नृपात्मजे।।5.35.47।।
transliteration: kānanāni suramyāṇi nadīḥ prasravaṇāni ca| caranna ratimāpnoti tvāmapaśyannṛpātmaje
translation: नृपात्मजे daughter of a king, त्वाम् you, अपश्यन् unable to see, सुरम्याणि very delightful, काननानि forests, नदीः rivers, प्रस्रवणानि च and streams, चरन् while moving, रतिम् happiness, न आप्नोति not finding.
explanation: "Oh princess unable to see you, Rama has found no joy in roaming delightful forests, rivers and streams.

shloka_text: स त्वां मनुजशार्दूलः क्षिप्रं प्राप्स्यति राघवः। समित्रबान्धवं हत्वा रावणं जनकात्मजे।।5.35.48।।
transliteration: sa tvāṃ manujaśārdūlaḥ kṣipraṃ prāpsyati rāghavaḥ| samitrabāndhavaṃ hatvā rāvaṇaṃ janakātmaje
translation: जनकात्मजे Oh daughter of Janaka, मनुजशार्दूलः a tiger among men, सः राघवः that Rama, समित्रबान्धवम् along with his friends and relatives, रावणम् Ravana, हत्वा after killing, त्वाम् you, क्षिप्रम् soon, प्राप्स्यति will attain.
explanation: "Oh daughter of Janaka after killing Ravana, along with his friends and relatives Rama, the tiger among men, will meet you.

shloka_text: सहितौ रामसुग्रीवावुभावकुरुतां तदा। समयं वालिनं हन्तुं तव चान्वेषणं तथा।।5.35.49।।
transliteration: sahitau rāmasugrīvāvubhāvakurutāṃ tadā| samayaṃ vālinaṃ hantuṃ tava cānveṣaṇaṃ tathā
translation: तदा then, रामसुग्रीवौ Rama and Sugriva, उभौ both, सहितौ together with, वालिनम् Vali, हन्तुम् to kill, तथा likewise, तव your, अन्वेषणम् search, समयम् agreement, अकुरुताम् reached.
explanation: "(Having become friends) Rama and Sugriva together reached an agreement to kill Vali and search for you.

shloka_text: ततस्ताभ्यां कुमाराभ्यां वीराभ्यां स हरीश्वरः। किष्किन्धां समुपागम्य वाली युद्धे निपातितः।।5.35.50।।
transliteration: tatastābhyāṃ kumārābhyāṃ vīrābhyāṃ sa harīśvaraḥ| kiṣkindhāṃ samupāgamya vālī yuddhe nipātitaḥ
translation: ततः thereafter, वीराभ्याम् by both the heroes, ताभ्याम् by both of them, कुमाराभ्याम् by both princes, किष्किन्धाम् to Kishkinda, समुपागम्य after reaching, हरीश्वरः king of vanaras, सः that, वाली Vali, युद्धे in war, निपातितः killed.
explanation: "Thereafter both the princes together arrived at Kishkinda and killed Vali, king of vanaras in a combat.

shloka_text: ततो निहत्य तरसा रामो वालिनमाहवे। सर्वर्क्षहरिसङ्घानां सुग्रीवमकरोत्पतिम्।।5.35.51।।
transliteration: tato nihatya tarasā rāmo vālinamāhave| sarvarkṣaharisaṅghānāṃ sugrīvamakarotpatim
translation: ततः then, रामः Rama, आहवे in a combat, तरसा quickly, वालिनम् Vali, निहत्य killed, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, सर्वर्क्षहरिसङ्घानाम् for all troops of vanaras, पतिम् king, अकरोत् made.
explanation: "Then Rama quickly killed Vali in a combat and made Sugriva the lord of all troops of vanaras and bears.

shloka_text: रामसुग्रीवयोरैक्यं देव्येवं समजायत। हनुमन्तं च मां विद्धि तयोर्दूतमिहागतम्।।5.35.52।।
transliteration: rāmasugrīvayoraikyaṃ devyevaṃ samajāyata| hanumantaṃ ca māṃ viddhi tayordūtamihāgatam
translation: देवि Oh Illustrious lady, रामसुग्रीवयोः of both Rama and Sugriva, ऐक्यम् alliance, एवम् in that way, समजायत established, माम् me, तयोः their, दूतम् messenger, आगतम् came here, हनुमन्तम् Hanuman, विद्धि you may know.
explanation: "Oh Illustrious lady In that manner alliance was established between Rama and Sugriva. Know me to be Hanuman, arrived here as their messenger.

shloka_text: स्वराज्यं प्राप्य सुग्रीवस्समानीय हरीश्वरान्। त्वदर्थं प्रेषयामास दिशो दश महाबलान्।।5.35.53।।
transliteration: svarājyaṃ prāpya sugrīvassamānīya harīśvarān| tvadarthaṃ preṣayāmāsa diśo daśa mahābalān
translation: सुग्रीवः Sugriva, स्वराज्यम् his kingdom, प्राप्य having obtained, महाबलान् great army, हरीश्वरान् monkey leaders, समानीय after collecting, त्वदर्थम् for your sake, दश ten, दिशः directions, प्रेषयामास sent.
explanation: "Having obtained his kingdom Sugriva despatched the vanara leaders to all ten directions (to search for you).

shloka_text: आदिष्टा वानरेन्द्रेण सुग्रीवेण महौजसा। अद्रिराजप्रतीकाशास्सर्वतः प्रस्थितौ महीम्।।5.35.54।।
transliteration: ādiṣṭā vānarendreṇa sugrīveṇa mahaujasā| adrirājapratīkāśāssarvataḥ prasthitau mahīm
translation: वानरेन्द्रेण by the monkey leaders, महौजसा very powerful one, सुग्रीवेण by Sugriva, आदिष्टाः ordered, अद्रिराजप्रतीकाशाः huge as the Himalayas, king of mountains, सर्वतः all over, महीम् the earth, प्रस्थिता started moving.
explanation: "Following Sugriva's orders, the powerful monkey leaders huge as the Himalayas, king of mountains went all over the earth (searching).

shloka_text: ततस्ते मार्गमाणा वै सुग्रीववचनातुराः। चरन्ति वसुधां कृत्स्नां वयमन्ये च वानराः।।5.35.55।।
transliteration: tataste mārgamāṇā vai sugrīvavacanāturāḥ| caranti vasudhāṃ kṛtsnāṃ vayamanye ca vānarāḥ
translation: ततः then, ते they, वयम् we, अन्ये others, वानराः च and the vanaras, सुग्रीववचनातुराः eager to carry out Sugriva's order, मार्गमाणाः while searching, कृत्स्नाम् entire, वसुधाम् the earth, चरन्ति we are moving about.
explanation: "Following Sugriva's orders, we, the monkeys, since then are moving about searching the entire earth eager to find you or to carry out Sugriva's orders.

shloka_text: अङ्गदो नाम लक्ष्मीवान्वालिसूनुर्महाबलः। प्रस्थितः कपिशार्दूलस्त्रिभागबलसंवृतः।।5.35.56।।
transliteration: aṅgado nāma lakṣmīvānvālisūnurmahābalaḥ| prasthitaḥ kapiśārdūlastribhāgabalasaṃvṛtaḥ
translation: लक्ष्मीवान् prosperous, वालिसूनुः Vali's son, महाबलः mighty, अङ्गदो नाम called Angada, हरिशार्दूलः a tiger among vanaras, त्रिभागबलसंवृतः together with one third of the army, प्रस्थितः departed.
explanation: The prosperous and mighty son of Vali, a tiger among monkeys named Angada, set out together with a third of the army.

shloka_text: तेषां नो विप्रणष्टानां विन्ध्ये पर्वतसत्तमे। भृशं शोकपरीतानामहोरात्रगणा गताः।।5.35.57।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ no vipraṇaṣṭānāṃ vindhye parvatasattame| bhṛśaṃ śokaparītānāmahorātragaṇā gatāḥ
translation: विन्ध्ये in Vindhya, पर्वतसत्तमे in the great mountain, विप्रणष्टानाम् of those who were lost, भृशम् greatly, शोकपरीतानाम् of those immersed in sorrow, तेषाम् of all of them, नः of us, अहोरात्रगणाः many nights and days, गताःpassed
explanation: "We wasted many nights and days immersed in disappointment (for not being able to find you) and we missed our path in the great Vindhya mountain.

shloka_text: ते वयं कार्यनैराश्यात्कालस्यातिक्रमेण च। भयाच्च कपिराजस्य प्राणांस्त्यक्तुं व्यवस्थिताः।।5.35.58।।
transliteration: te vayaṃ kāryanairāśyātkālasyātikrameṇa ca| bhayācca kapirājasya prāṇāṃstyaktuṃ vyavasthitāḥ
translation: ते वयम् we were, कार्यनैराश्यात् disappointed, कालस्य of the time limit, अतिक्रमेण च exceeding, कपिराजस्य of monkey king's, भयाच्च out of fear also, प्राणान् life also, त्यक्तुम् to give up, व्यवस्थिताः decided.
explanation: "We decided to give up our lives due to disappointment, transgression of the time limit  fixed for us and fear of the monkey lord (fear of facing the king without finding you).

shloka_text: विचित्य वनदुर्गाणि गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च। अनासाद्य पदं देव्याः प्राणांस्त्यक्तुं समुद्यताः।।5.35.59।।
transliteration: vicitya vanadurgāṇi giriprasravaṇāni ca| anāsādya padaṃ devyāḥ prāṇāṃstyaktuṃ samudyatāḥ
translation: वनदुर्गाणि impenetrable forest forts, गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च mountain streams, विचित्य having searched, देव्याः the queen's, पदम् feet, अनासाद्य by not getting, प्राणान् life, त्यक्तुम् to give up, समुद्यताः we decided.
explanation: "We decided to give up our lives since we were unable to see the feet of the queen (Sita) even after searching the forest fortresses and the (banks of) mountain streams.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा प्रायोपविष्टांश्च सर्वान्वानरपुङ्गवान्। भृशं शोकार्णवे मग्नः पर्यदेवयदङ्गदः।।5.35.60।। तव नाशं च वैदेहि वालिनश्च वधं तथा। प्रायोपवेशमस्माकं मरणं च जटायुषः।।5.35.61।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā prāyopaviṣṭāṃśca sarvānvānarapuṅgavān| bhṛśaṃ śokārṇave magnaḥ paryadevayadaṅgadaḥ tava nāśaṃ ca vaidehi vālinaśca vadhaṃ tathā| prāyopaveśamasmākaṃ maraṇaṃ ca jaṭāyuṣaḥ
translation: वैदेहि oh Vaidehi, प्रायोपविष्टान् when we decided to die, सर्वान् all, वानरपुङ्गवान् vanara leaders, दृष्ट्वा on seeing, अङ्गदः Angada, भृशम् intensely, शोकार्णवे in the sea of sorrow, मग्नः plunged, तव yourself, नाशं च not found, तथा वालिनः similarly Vali's, वधं च and his killing, जटायुषः Jatayu's, मरणं च death also, अस्माकम् all of us, प्रायोपवेशम् decision to die, पर्यदेवयत् he was grieved.
explanation: Seeing all the vanara leaders resolved to die, Angada, plunged in a sea of sorrow, grieved aloud over your disappearance, the slaying of Vali, the death of Jatayu, and our own resolve to fast unto death.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा प्रायोपविष्टांश्च सर्वान्वानरपुङ्गवान्। भृशं शोकार्णवे मग्नः पर्यदेवयदङ्गदः।।5.35.60।। तव नाशं च वैदेहि वालिनश्च वधं तथा। प्रायोपवेशमस्माकं मरणं च जटायुषः।।5.35.61।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā prāyopaviṣṭāṃśca sarvānvānarapuṅgavān| bhṛśaṃ śokārṇave magnaḥ paryadevayadaṅgadaḥ tava nāśaṃ ca vaidehi vālinaśca vadhaṃ tathā| prāyopaveśamasmākaṃ maraṇaṃ ca jaṭāyuṣaḥ
translation: वैदेहि oh Vaidehi, प्रायोपविष्टान् when we decided to die, सर्वान् all, वानरपुङ्गवान् vanara leaders, दृष्ट्वा on seeing, अङ्गदः Angada, भृशम् intensely, शोकार्णवे in the sea of sorrow, मग्नः plunged, तव yourself, नाशं च not found, तथा वालिनः similarly Vali's, वधं च and his killing, जटायुषः Jatayu's, मरणं च death also, अस्माकम् all of us, प्रायोपवेशम् decision to die, पर्यदेवयत् he was grieved.
explanation: Seeing all the vanara leaders resolved to die, Angada, plunged in a sea of sorrow, grieved aloud over your disappearance, the slaying of Vali, the death of Jatayu, and our own resolve to fast unto death.

shloka_text: तेषां नस्वामिसन्देशान्निराशानां मुमूर्षताम्। कार्यहेतोरिवायातश्शकुनिर्वीर्यवान्महान्।।5.35.62।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ nasvāmisandeśānnirāśānāṃ mumūrṣatām| kāryahetorivāyātaśśakunirvīryavānmahān
translation: स्वामिसन्देशात् according to the king's cmmand (that who ever overstays would be killed), निराशानाम् disappointed, मुमूर्षताम् when we were desiring to die, तेषाम् for such of us, नः to us, कार्यहेतोरिव as if to fulfil the task, वीर्यवान् powerful, महान् gigantic, शकुनिः bird, आयातः came.
explanation: "When we were disappointed (in tracing you) and were at the point of death having been commanded by the king (that whosoever overstays would be killed) a gigantic powerful bird appeared to fulfil our task.

shloka_text: गृध्रराजस्य सोदर्यः सम्पातिर्नाम गृध्रराट्। श्रुत्वा भ्रातृवधं कोपादिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।5.35.63।।
transliteration: gṛdhrarājasya sodaryaḥ sampātirnāma gṛdhrarāṭ| śrutvā bhrātṛvadhaṃ kopādidaṃ vacanamabravīt
translation: गृध्रराजस्य of the king of vultures, सोदर्यः brother, सम्पातिर्नाम called Sampati, गृध्रराट् king of birds, भ्रातृवधम् death of Jatayu, श्रुत्वा on hearing, कोपात् with anger, इदम् this, वचनम् word, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: "That king of vultures, Sampati was the brother of king of birds Jatayu. Hearing about the death of his younger brother Sampati felt distresed and spoke in anger:

shloka_text: यवीयान्केन मे भ्राता हतः क्व च निपातितः। एतदाख्यातुमिच्छामि भवद्भिर्वानरोत्तमाः।।5.35.64।।
transliteration: yavīyānkena me bhrātā hataḥ kva ca nipātitaḥ| etadākhyātumicchāmi bhavadbhirvānarottamāḥ
translation: मे my, यवीयान् younger, भ्राता brother, केन by whom, हतः was killed, क्व where, निपातितः was he dropped, वानरोत्तमाः of best of vanaras, भवद्भिः by you, एतत् this, आख्यातुम् to tell, इच्छामि I desire.
explanation: 'O best of vanaras by whom was my younger brother killed? Where was he dropped down? I wish you to tell me all about that.

shloka_text: अङ्गदोऽकथयत्तस्य जनस्थाने महद्वधम्। रक्षसा भीमरूपेण त्वामुद्दिश्य यथातथम्।।5.35.65।।
transliteration: aṅgado'kathayattasya janasthāne mahadvadham| rakṣasā bhīmarūpeṇa tvāmuddiśya yathātatham
translation: त्वाम् you, उद्दिश्य aiming at, भीमरूपेण by a dreadful person, रक्षसा by the demon, जनस्थाने in Janasthana, महद्वधम् great killing, यथातथम् as it happened faithfully, अङ्गदः Angada, तस्य to him, अकथयत् told.
explanation: Angada faithfully told him of the great slaughter wrought in Janasthana on your account by the demon of dreadful form.

shloka_text: जटायुषो वधं श्रुत्वा दुःखितस्सोऽरुणात्मजः। त्वां शशंस वरारोहे वसन्तीं रावणालये।।5.35.66।।
transliteration: jaṭāyuṣo vadhaṃ śrutvā duḥkhitasso'ruṇātmajaḥ| tvāṃ śaśaṃsa varārohe vasantīṃ rāvaṇālaye
translation: वरारोहे oh charming lady, सः he, अरुणात्मजः Aruna's son, जटायुषः Jatayu's, वधं death, श्रुत्वा having heard, दुःखितः became sad, त्वाम् yourself, रावणालये in Ravana's palace, वसन्तीम् living, शशंस narrated to us.
explanation: "Having heard about the death of Jatayu, O charming lady that Sampati Aruna's son felt sad and told us that you are at Ravana's palace.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सम्पातेः प्रीतिवर्धनम्। अङ्गदप्रमुखास्तूर्णं ततस्सम्प्रस्थिता वयम्।।5.35.67।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sampāteḥ prītivardhanam| aṅgadapramukhāstūrṇaṃ tatassamprasthitā vayam
translation: तस्य his, सम्पातेः Samapati's, प्रीतिवर्धनम् that which was pleasing, तत् that, वचनम् word, श्रुत्वा having heard, अङ्गदप्रमुखाः Angada and others, वयम् all of us, तूर्णम् quickly, ततः from there, प्रस्थिताः departed.
explanation: "Having heard Sampati's encouraging words all of us led by Angada departed immediately.

shloka_text: विन्ध्यादुत्थाय सम्प्राप्ता स्सागरस्यान्तमुत्तरम्। त्वद्धर्शनकृतोत्साहा हृष्टास्तुष्टाः प्लवङ्गमाः।।5.35.68।।
transliteration: vindhyādutthāya samprāptā ssāgarasyāntamuttaram| tvaddharśanakṛtotsāhā hṛṣṭāstuṣṭāḥ plavaṅgamāḥ
translation: प्लवङ्गमाः vanaras, त्वद्दर्शनकृतोत्साहा enthused to see you, हृष्टाः joyfully, तुष्टाः satisfied, विन्ध्यात् from Vindhya, उत्थाय having got up, सागरस्य towards the sea, उत्तरम् अन्तम् the limit of the northern direction, सम्प्राप्ताः reached.
explanation: "The happy monkeys were satisfied. Enthusiastic about seeing you, they rose from the Vindhya mountain and reached the limit of the sea  shore in the north.

shloka_text: अङ्गदप्रमुखास्सर्वे वेलोपान्तमुपस्थिताः। चिन्तां जग्मुः पुनर्भीतास्त्वद्दर्शनसमुत्सुकाः।।5.35.69।।
transliteration: aṅgadapramukhāssarve velopāntamupasthitāḥ| cintāṃ jagmuḥ punarbhītāstvaddarśanasamutsukāḥ
translation: अङ्गदप्रमुखाः Angada and other leaders, सर्वे all, त्वद्दर्शनमुत्सुकाः enthusiastic to see you, वेलोपान्तम् sea shore, उपस्थिताः reached, भीताः they were frightened, पुनः again, चिन्ताम् worry, जग्मुः felt.
explanation: Angada and all the other leaders, eager to see you, reached the seashore but, frightened, again sank into worry.

shloka_text: अथाहं हरिसैन्यस्य सागरं प्रेक्ष्य सीदतः। व्यवधूय भयं तीव्रं योजनानां शतं प्लुतः।।5.35.70।।
transliteration: athāhaṃ harisainyasya sāgaraṃ prekṣya sīdataḥ| vyavadhūya bhayaṃ tīvraṃ yojanānāṃ śataṃ plutaḥ
translation: अथ then, अहम् I, सागरम् ocean, प्रेक्ष्य after looking at, सीदतः in desperate mood, हरिसैन्यस्य Vanara army's, तीव्रम् intense, भयम् fear, व्यवधूय after pushing aside, योजनानाम् of yojanas, शतम् one hundred, प्लुतः leaped.
explanation: "When the vanara army was feeling despondent at the sight of the ocean, I leaped across the sea, a hundred yojanas, pushing aside  all my fear.

shloka_text: लङ्का चापि मया रात्रौ प्रविष्टा राक्षसाकुला। रावणश्च मया दृष्टस्त्वं च शोकपरिप्लुता।।5.35.71।।
transliteration: laṅkā cāpi mayā rātrau praviṣṭā rākṣasākulā| rāvaṇaśca mayā dṛṣṭastvaṃ ca śokapariplutā
translation: राक्षसाकुला filled with demons, लङ्का चापि Lanka also, मया by me, रात्रौ at night, प्रविष्टा entered, मया by me, रावणश्च Ravana also, दृष्टः is seen, शोकपरिप्लुता immersed in sorrow, त्वं च you also.
explanation: "I entered at night the city of Lanka teeming with demons and saw Ravana and saw you immersed in sorrow.

shloka_text: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथावृत्तमनन्दिते। अभिभाषस्व मां देवि दूतो दाशरथेरहम्।।5.35.72।।
transliteration: etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yathāvṛttamanandite| abhibhāṣasva māṃ devi dūto dāśaratheraham
translation: अनिन्दिते O sinless lady, देवि O divine lady, एतत् this, सर्वम् everything, यथावृत्तम् as it happened, ते to you, आख्यातम् narrated, माम् me, अभिभाषस्व you may speak, अहम् I, दाशरथेः Dasaratha's son, दूतः messenger.
explanation: "O sinless lady I have given you a faithful account. I am a messenger of Dasaratha's son. And you may speak now, O divine lady

shloka_text: तं मां रामकृतोद्योगं त्वन्निमित्तमिहागतम्। सुग्रीवसचिवं देवि बुद्ध्यस्व पवनात्मजम्।।5.35.73।।
transliteration: taṃ māṃ rāmakṛtodyogaṃ tvannimittamihāgatam| sugrīvasacivaṃ devi buddhyasva pavanātmajam
translation: देवि O divine lady, तं माम् such me, रामकृतोद्योगम् have taken up Rama's mission, त्वन्निमित्तम् on your account, इह here, आगतम् came, सुग्रीवसचिवम् minister of Sugriva, पवनात्मजम् son of Vayu, बुद्ध्यस्व you may know.
explanation: "O divine lady Know that I have come here for your cause carrying out the mission of Rama. I am Sugriva'a minister and son of the Windgod.

shloka_text: कुशली तव काकुत्स्थस्सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। गुरोराराधने युक्तो लक्ष्मणश्च सुलक्षणः।।5.35.74।।
transliteration: kuśalī tava kākutsthassarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ| gurorārādhane yukto lakṣmaṇaśca sulakṣaṇaḥ
translation: सर्वशस्त्रभृताम् among all wielders of weapons, वरः supreme, तव your, काकुत्स्थ Rama of the Kakutstha race, कुशली he is keeping well, गुरोः of his venerable teacher, आराधने in service, युक्तः engaged, सुलक्षणः a man of auspicious signs, लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana also.
explanation: "Your lord Rama of Kakutstha race, supreme among wielders of weapons is doing well. So is venerable Lakshmana endowed with auspicious signs engaged in serving him.

shloka_text: तस्य वीर्यवतो देवि भर्तुस्तव हिते रतः। अहमेकस्तु सम्प्राप्त स्सुग्रीववचनादिह।।5.35.75।।
transliteration: tasya vīryavato devi bhartustava hite rataḥ| ahamekastu samprāpta ssugrīvavacanādiha
translation: देवि O queen, वीर्यवतः of valourous, तव your, भर्तुः husband's, तस्य his, हिते seeking welfare, रतः engaged, अहम् I, सुग्रीववचनात् at the behest of Sugriva, इह here, एकः alone, प्राप्तः reached.
explanation: "O queen seeking the welfare of your Valiant husband I came here at the behest of Sugriva all alone.

shloka_text: मयेयमसहायेन चरता कामरूपिणा। दक्षिणा दिगनुक्रान्ता त्वन्मार्गविचयैषिणा।।5.35.76।।
transliteration: mayeyamasahāyena caratā kāmarūpiṇā| dakṣiṇā diganukrāntā tvanmārgavicayaiṣiṇā
translation: त्वन्मार्गविचयैषिणा while searching for your location, कामरूपिणा by a person who can take any form at will, असहायेन without any help, चरता while moving, मया by myself, इयम् this, दक्षिणा दिक् southern direction, अनुक्रान्ता reached.
explanation: "I can assume any form at my will. I searched for you without any help moving in the southern direction and reached this place .

shloka_text: दिष्ट्याहं हरिसैन्यानां त्वन्नाशमनुशोचताम्। अपनेष्यामि सन्तापं तवाभिगमशंसनात्।।5.35.77।।
transliteration: diṣṭyāhaṃ harisainyānāṃ tvannāśamanuśocatām| apaneṣyāmi santāpaṃ tavābhigamaśaṃsanāt
translation: दिष्ट्या fortunately for me, अहम् I, त्वन्नाशम् your loss, अनुशोचताम् regretting, हरिसैन्यानाम् of the vanara army, सन्तापम् grief, तव your, अभिगमशंसनात् by letting them know, अपनेष्यामि I will dispel their sorrow.
explanation: "Fortunately for me I can finally dispel the fear of the vanara chiefs who are regretting your loss, by letting them know that you have been found.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या हि मम न व्यर्थं देवि सागरलङ्घनम्। प्राप्स्याम्यहमिदं दिष्ट्या त्वद्दर्शनकृतं यशः।।5.35.78।।
transliteration: diṣṭyā hi mama na vyarthaṃ devi sāgaralaṅghanam| prāpsyāmyahamidaṃ diṣṭyā tvaddarśanakṛtaṃ yaśaḥ
translation: देवि oh queen, दिष्ट्या luckily, मम my, सागरलङ्घनम् crossing the ocean, न व्यर्थम् is not wasted, दिष्ट्या fortunately, अहम् I, त्वद्दर्शनकृतम् by the act of seeing you, इदम् thus, यशः fame, प्राप्स्यामि I will attain.
explanation: "Oh queen luckily for me, crossing the ocean has not gone in vain. I am fortunate because I will attain fame of finding you.

shloka_text: राघवश्च महावीर्यः क्षिप्रं त्वामभिपत्स्यते। समित्रबान्धवं हत्वा रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्।।5.35.79।।
transliteration: rāghavaśca mahāvīryaḥ kṣipraṃ tvāmabhipatsyate| samitrabāndhavaṃ hatvā rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam
translation: महावीर्यः mighty hero, राघवश्च Raghava, समित्रबान्धवम् accompanied by friends and relatives, राक्षसाधिपम् king of demons, रावणम् Ravana, हत्वा after killing, क्षिप्रम् very soon, त्वाम् yourself, अभिपत्स्यते will reach you.
explanation: "Mighty Raghava will take you after killing Ravana, the king of demons along with his kith and kin.

shloka_text: माल्यवान्नाम वैदेहि गिरीणामुत्तमो गिरिः। ततो गच्छति गोकर्णं पर्वतं केसरी हरिः।।5.35.80।।
transliteration: mālyavānnāma vaidehi girīṇāmuttamo giriḥ| tato gacchati gokarṇaṃ parvataṃ kesarī hariḥ
translation: वैदेहि Vaidehi, गिरीणाम् among the mountains, उत्तमः the best one, माल्यवान्नाम Malyavan, गिरिः mountain, ततः from there, केसरी Kesari, हरिः monkey, गोकर्णम् Gokarna, पर्वतम् mountain, गच्छति went.
explanation: "Oh Vaidehi there is a famous mountain called Malyavan. From there a monkey called Kesari went to mount Gokarna.

shloka_text: स च देवर्षिभिर्दिष्टः पिता मम महाकपिः। तीर्थे नदीपतेः पुण्ये शम्बसादनमुद्धरत्।।5.35.81।।
transliteration: sa ca devarṣibhirdiṣṭaḥ pitā mama mahākapiḥ| tīrthe nadīpateḥ puṇye śambasādanamuddharat
translation: देवर्षिभिः by the divine sages, दिष्टः predicted, मम my, पिता father, सः महाकपिः that great monkey, नदीपतेः of lord of rivers, ocean, पुण्ये holy, तीर्थे in a place, शम्बसादनम् Sambasadanam, उद्धरत् raised.
explanation: "He (Kesari) is said to be my father by the divine sages. He retrieved a piece of land in a holy spot of that sea shore and killed Sambasadana, a demon who was oppressing righteous people.

shloka_text: तस्याहं हरिणः क्षेत्रे जातो वातेन मैथिलि। हनुमानिति विख्यातो लोके स्वेनैव कर्मणा।।5.35.82।।
transliteration: tasyāhaṃ hariṇaḥ kṣetre jāto vātena maithili| hanumāniti vikhyāto loke svenaiva karmaṇā
translation: मैथिलि Mythili, अहम् I, तस्य his, हरिणः monkey's, क्षेत्रे in the land, वातेन by the Windgod, जातः born, स्वेन कर्मणा एव by my own act, लोके by people, हनुमानिति Hanuman, विख्यातः came to be known.
explanation: "O Mythili I was born in that land retrieved by the Windgod. I am known as Hanuman by virtue of my own action.

shloka_text: विश्वासार्थं तु वैदेहि भर्तुरुक्ता मया गुणाः। अचिराद्राघवो देवि त्वामितो नयिताऽनघे।।5.35.83।।
transliteration: viśvāsārthaṃ tu vaidehi bharturuktā mayā guṇāḥ| acirādrāghavo devi tvāmito nayitā'naghe
translation: वैदेहि Vaidehi, विश्वासार्थम् for inspiring confidence, मया by me, भर्तुः  your husband's, गुणाः qualities, उक्ताः are described, देवि O queen, राघवः Raghava, अचिरात् very soon, त्वाम् you, इतः from here, नयिता he will take you away, अनघे lady free from sins.
explanation: "In order to inspire confidence in you about me I have narrated the virtues of your husband. O sinless queen Rama will take you from here very soon".

shloka_text: एवं विश्वासिता सीता हेतुभिश्शोककर्शिता। उपपन्नैरभिज्ञानैर्दूतं तमवगच्छति।।5.35.84।।
transliteration: evaṃ viśvāsitā sītā hetubhiśśokakarśitā| upapannairabhijñānairdūtaṃ tamavagacchati
translation: शोककर्शिता tormented by grief, सीता Sita, एवम् in that way, हेतुभिः with possible reasons, विश्वासिता having trusted, उपपन्नैः by the evidences, अभिज्ञानैः with identification, तम् him, दूतम् as a messenger, अवगच्छति she understood.
explanation: The griefstricken Sita trusted him by his logical presentation of reasons as well as identifications. She believed that he was a messenger (of Rama).

shloka_text: अतुलं च गता हर्षं प्रहर्षेण च जानकी। नेत्राभ्यां वक्रपक्ष्माभ्यां मुमोचानन्दजं जलम्।।5.35.85।।
transliteration: atulaṃ ca gatā harṣaṃ praharṣeṇa ca jānakī| netrābhyāṃ vakrapakṣmābhyāṃ mumocānandajaṃ jalam
translation: जानकी Janaki, अतुलम् immeasurable, हर्षम् happiness, गता च experienced, प्रहर्षेण in her joy, वक्रपक्ष्माभ्याम् through her curved eyelashes, नेत्राभ्याम् from both eyes, आनन्दजम् arising out of joy, जलम् tears, मुमोच shed.
explanation: Janaki experienced immeasurable happiness and shed tears of joy through her curved eyes.

shloka_text: चारु तद्वदनं तस्यास्ताम्रशुक्लायतेक्षणम्। अशोभत विशालाक्ष्या राहुमुक्त इवोडुराट्।।5.35.86।।
transliteration: cāru tadvadanaṃ tasyāstāmraśuklāyatekṣaṇam| aśobhata viśālākṣyā rāhumukta ivoḍurāṭ
translation: विशालाक्ष्याः of largeeyed lady, तस्याः her, चारु lovely, ताम्रशुक्लायतेक्षणम् having wide white eyes with tinge of red corners, तत् that, वदनम् face, राहुमुक्तः released from Rahu, उडुराडिव like the Moon, अशोभत shone.
explanation: Her face with large eyes with a tinge of red corners shone like the Moon released from Rahu.

shloka_text: हनुमन्तं कपिं व्यक्तं मन्यते नान्यथेति सा। अथोवाच हनूमांस्तामुत्तरं प्रियदर्शनाम्।।5.35.87।।
transliteration: hanumantaṃ kapiṃ vyaktaṃ manyate nānyatheti sā| athovāca hanūmāṃstāmuttaraṃ priyadarśanām
translation: सा she, हनुमन्तम् Hanuman, व्यक्तम् clearly, कपिम् the monkey, मन्यते realised, अन्यथा इति none other than, अथ then, हनूमान् Hanuman, प्रियदर्शनाम् a lady pleasing to see, ताम् her, उत्तराम् later, उवाच spoke.
explanation: She realised that the monkey was none other than Hanuman. Then he looked at her who was pleasing to see and spoke again:

shloka_text: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं समाश्वसिहि मैथिलि। किं करोमि कथं वा ते रोचते प्रतियाम्यहम्।।5.35.88।।
transliteration: etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ samāśvasihi maithili| kiṃ karomi kathaṃ vā te rocate pratiyāmyaham
translation: मैथिलि Mythili, ते to you, एतत् सर्वम् everything, आख्यातम् is narrated, समाश्वसिहि calm down, किम् what, करोमि shall I do, ते to you, कथं वा or how, रोचते it pleases, अहम् I, प्रतियामि I will go back.
explanation: "Mythili, everything I intended to say has been narrated to you. Calm yourself down. What shall I do? Or else, tell me what pleases you. I shall go back.

shloka_text: हतेऽसुरे संयति शम्बसादने कपिप्रवीरेण महर्षिचोदनात्। ततोऽस्मि वायुप्रभवो हि मैथिलि प्रभावतस्तत्प्रतिमश्च वानरः।।5.35.89।।
transliteration: hate'sure saṃyati śambasādane kapipravīreṇa maharṣicodanāt| tato'smi vāyuprabhavo hi maithili prabhāvatastatpratimaśca vānaraḥ
translation: मैथिलि Maithili, संयति in a fight, शम्बसादने Sambasadana, असुरे when the demon, कपिप्रवरेण mighty monkey, महर्षिचोदनात् by the command of great sage, हते सति where he was slain, अथ then, वायुप्रभवः by the spread of wind, प्रभावतः by his prowess, तत्प्रतिमः equal to him, वानरः vanara, अस्मि I am.
explanation: "(My father) a mighty monkey killed Sambasadana in a battle on the command of a great seer. I am a vanara (born to a monkey) by the impact of the Windgod. I am equal to the Windgod in power." इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चत्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyfifth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: भूय एव महातेजा हनूमान्पवनात्मजः। अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं सीताप्रत्ययकारणात्।।5.36.1।।
transliteration: bhūya eva mahātejā hanūmānpavanātmajaḥ| abravītpraśritaṃ vākyaṃ sītāpratyayakāraṇāt
translation: महातेजाः mighty, पवनात्मजः son of the Windgod, हनुमान् Hanuman, सीताप्रत्ययकारणात् in order to inspire trust in Sita, भूय एव again this way, प्रश्रितम् humbly, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Mighty Hanuman, the son of the Windgod again spoke to Sita humbly to inspire confidence in her.
comments: Hanuman hands over the signet ring to Sita

shloka_text: वानरोऽहं महाभागे दूतो रामस्य धीमतः। रामनामाङ्कितं चेदं पश्य देव्यङ्गुलीयकम्।।5.36.2।।
transliteration: vānaro'haṃ mahābhāge dūto rāmasya dhīmataḥ| rāmanāmāṅkitaṃ cedaṃ paśya devyaṅgulīyakam
translation: महाभागे O noble lady, अहम् I am, धीमतः learned, रामस्य Rama's, दूतः envoy, वानरः vanara, देवि O godlike lady, रामनामाङ्कितम् which has the name of Rama inscribed, इदम् this, अङ्गुलीयकं च ring also, पश्य you see.
explanation: "O noble lady I am a vanara, an envoy of learned Rama. You see this ring with Rama's name inscribed on it, O godlike lady

shloka_text: प्रत्ययार्थं तवाऽनीतं तेन दत्तं महात्मना। समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते क्षीणदुःखफला ह्यसि।।5.36.3।।
transliteration: pratyayārthaṃ tavā'nītaṃ tena dattaṃ mahātmanā| samāśvasihi bhadraṃ te kṣīṇaduḥkhaphalā hyasi
translation: महात्मना greatself, तेन by him, दत्तम् given, तव your, प्रत्ययार्थम् to make you trust, अनीतम् is brought, समाश्वसिहि be calm, ते to you, भद्रम् let you be auspicious, क्षीणदुःखफला your sorows ended, असि हि indeed.
explanation: "Be calm. Be blessed. Your sorrows have come to an end. This (the ring) is given by the great self, Rama, to make you trust me.

shloka_text: गृहीत्वा प्रेक्षमाणा सा भर्तुः करविभूषणम्। भर्तारमिव सम्प्राप्ता जानकी मुदिताऽभवत्।।5.36.4।।
transliteration: gṛhītvā prekṣamāṇā sā bhartuḥ karavibhūṣaṇam| bhartāramiva samprāptā jānakī muditā'bhavat
translation: भर्तुः husband, करविभूषणम् ornament that adorned his hand, गृहीत्वा having received, प्रेक्षमाणा gazing, सा जानकी Janaki, भर्तारम् husband, सम्प्राप्ता इव as if reached, मुदिता delighted, अभवत् became.
explanation: She received the ornament that adorned her husband's hand and gazed at it and felt delighted as though her husband had arrived.

shloka_text: चारु तद्वदनं तस्यास्ताम्रशुक्लायतेक्षणम्। अशोभत विशालाक्ष्या राहुमुक्त इवोडुराट्।।5.36.5।।
transliteration: cāru tadvadanaṃ tasyāstāmraśuklāyatekṣaṇam| aśobhata viśālākṣyā rāhumukta ivoḍurāṭ
translation: तस्यास्ताम्रशुक्लायतेक्षणम् her white eyes with reddish tinge at the corners of the eyes, चारु beautiful, तद्वदनं her countenance, विशालाक्ष्या largeeyed, राहुमुक्त released by Rahu, इवोडुराट् like the Moon अशोभत shone
explanation: Her beautiful countenance with large white eyes with a reddish tinge in the corners shone like the Moon released from Rahu.

shloka_text: ततस्सा ह्रीमती बाला भर्तृसन्देशहर्षिता। परितुष्टा प्रियं कृत्वा प्रशशंस महाकपिम्।।5.36.6।।
transliteration: tatassā hrīmatī bālā bhartṛsandeśaharṣitā| parituṣṭā priyaṃ kṛtvā praśaśaṃsa mahākapim
translation: ततः then, बाला young lady, सा that Sita, भर्तृसन्देशहर्षिता delighted at the news of her husband, ह्रीमती blushing lady, परितुष्टा felt happy, प्रियम् pleasing, कृत्वा action, महाकपिम् by the great monkey, प्रशशंस praised.
explanation: Young Sita felt delighted about her husband's news and blushed. By praising him for his action, she pleased the great monkey.

shloka_text: विक्रान्तस्त्वं समर्थस्त्वं प्राज्ञस्त्वं वानरोत्तम। येनेदं राक्षसपदं त्वयैकेन प्रधर्षितम्।।5.36.7।।
transliteration: vikrāntastvaṃ samarthastvaṃ prājñastvaṃ vānarottama| yenedaṃ rākṣasapadaṃ tvayaikena pradharṣitam
translation: वानरोत्तम O foremost among the vanaras, एकेन single handed, येन by which, त्वया by you, इदम् this, राक्षसपदम् demon's abode, प्रधर्षितम् assailed, त्वम् you, विक्रान्तः you are very brave, त्वम् you, समर्थः are able, त्वम् you, प्राज्ञः are wise.
explanation: "O foremost among the vanaras you have trespassed the abodes of demons all alone. You are mighty and capable and wise.

shloka_text: शतयोजनविस्तीर्ण स्सागरो मकरालयः। विक्रमश्लाघनीयेन क्रमता गोष्पदीकृतः।।5.36.8।।
transliteration: śatayojanavistīrṇa ssāgaro makarālayaḥ| vikramaślāghanīyena kramatā goṣpadīkṛtaḥ
translation: विक्रमश्लाघनीयेन by your admirable prowess, क्रमता advancing, शतयोजनविस्तीर्णः extended over a hundred yojanas, मकरालयः abode of crocodiles, सागरः ocean, गोष्पदीकृतः is reduced to calf's hoof mark.
explanation: "You with your admirable prowess have reduced this ocean which is an abode of crocodiles stretching over a hundred yojanas to a cow's hoof mark.

shloka_text: न हि त्वां प्राकृतं मन्ये वानरं वानरर्षभ। यस्य ते नास्ति सन्त्रासो रावणान्नापि सम्भ्रमः।।5.36.9।।
transliteration: na hi tvāṃ prākṛtaṃ manye vānaraṃ vānararṣabha| yasya te nāsti santrāso rāvaṇānnāpi sambhramaḥ
translation: वानरर्षभ O bull among vanaras, यस्य of whom, ते to you, रावणात् from Ravana, सन्त्रासः fear, नास्ति not there, सम्भ्रमः अपि even excitement, न not, त्वाम् for you, प्राकृतम् ordinary, वानरम् monkey, न मन्ये I do not think.
explanation: "I do not think you are an ordinary monkey. You have no fear or excitement about Ravana. You are a bull among vanaras.

shloka_text: अर्हसे च कपिश्रेष्ठ मया समभिभाषितुम्। यद्यसि प्रेषितस्तेन रामेण विदितात्मना।।5.36.10।।
transliteration: arhase ca kapiśreṣṭha mayā samabhibhāṣitum| yadyasi preṣitastena rāmeṇa viditātmanā
translation: कपिश्रेष्ठ O best among monkeys, विदितात्मना by a knower of self, तेन by him, रामेण by Rama, प्रेषितः sent, असि यदि you are, मया by me, समभिभाषितुम् to converse, अर्हसे you deserve.
explanation: "O best of monkeys As you have been sent by Rama, the knower of the self, it is proper for me to converse with you.

shloka_text: प्रेषयिष्यति दुर्धर्षो रामो न ह्यपरीक्षितम्। पराक्रममविज्ञाय मत्सकाशं विशेषतः।।5.36.11।।
transliteration: preṣayiṣyati durdharṣo rāmo na hyaparīkṣitam| parākramamavijñāya matsakāśaṃ viśeṣataḥ
translation: दुर्धर्षः formidable, रामः Rama, पराक्रमम् valour, अविज्ञाय without knowing, अपरीक्षितम् without testing, न प्रेषयिष्यति हि would not send any body, विशेषतः specially, मत्सकाशम् to me.
explanation: "The formidable Rama will not send any one specially to me without testing him or knowing his valour.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या च कुशली रामो धर्मात्मा सत्यसङ्गरः। लक्ष्मणश्च महातेजास्सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः।।5.36.12।।
transliteration: diṣṭyā ca kuśalī rāmo dharmātmā satyasaṅgaraḥ| lakṣmaṇaśca mahātejāssumitrānandavardhanaḥ
translation: दिष्ट्या luckily, धर्मात्मा righteous, सत्यसङ्गरः one who follows truth, रामः Rama, महातेजाः glorious, सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः enhancer of Sumitra's joy, लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana also, कुशली well.
explanation: "To my luck, righteous Rama who abides in truth and glorious Lakshmana who enhances the joy of Sumitra are keeping well.

shloka_text: कुशली यदि काकुत्स्थः किं नु सागरमेखलाम्। महीं दहति कोपेन युगान्ताग्निरिवोत्थितः।।5.36.13।।
transliteration: kuśalī yadi kākutsthaḥ kiṃ nu sāgaramekhalām| mahīṃ dahati kopena yugāntāgnirivotthitaḥ
translation: काकुत्स्थः Kakutsthas, कुशली यदि if he is keeping well, उत्थितः generated, युगान्ताग्निरिव at the time of dissolution of the era, सागरमेखलाम् oceangirdled, महीम् earth, कोपेन with his rage, किम् why, न दहति not burning?
explanation: "Indeed if Kakutstha is well wherefore does he not burn the oceangirdled earth in his rage as (the earth is burnt) at the time of dissolution of the era?

shloka_text: अथवा शक्तिमन्तौ तौ सुराणामपि निग्रहे। ममैव तु न दुःखानामस्ति मन्ये विपर्ययः।।5.36.14।।
transliteration: athavā śaktimantau tau surāṇāmapi nigrahe| mamaiva tu na duḥkhānāmasti manye viparyayaḥ
translation: अथवा or else, तौ both, सुराणामपि even gods, निग्रहे in subduing, शक्तिमन्तौ both are capable, तु but, मम my, दुःखानामेव for my sorrow, विपर्ययः disaster, नास्ति not there, मन्ये I think.
explanation: "Both of them are capable of subduing even the gods. I think the reversal of  my fate is reason for their inaction.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्न व्यथितो रामः कच्चिन्न परितप्यते। उत्तराणि च कार्याणि कुरुते पुरुषोत्तमः।।5.36.15।।
transliteration: kaccinna vyathito rāmaḥ kaccinna paritapyate| uttarāṇi ca kāryāṇi kurute puruṣottamaḥ
translation: रामः Rama, न व्यथितः कच्चित् whether not depressed, न परितप्यते कच्चित् indeed not suffering, पुरुषोत्तमः great among men, उत्तराणि necessary steps, कार्याणि action, कुरुते will be carrying out perhaps?
explanation: "Is Rama the greatest among men not depressed? Does he not feel helpless? He is (perhaps) taking necessary steps (for my recovery).

shloka_text: कच्चिन्न दीन स्सम्भ्रान्तः कार्येषु न च मुह्यति। कच्चित्पुरुषकार्याणि कुरुते नृपतेस्सुतः।।5.36.16।।
transliteration: kaccinna dīna ssambhrāntaḥ kāryeṣu na ca muhyati| kaccitpuruṣakāryāṇi kurute nṛpatessutaḥ
translation: नृपतेः सुतः king's son, दीनः depressed, सम्भ्रान्तः perplexed, न कच्चित् not indeed, कार्येषु at work, न च मुह्यति is not spoiling, पुरुषकार्याणि the actions of men of achievement, कच्चित् कुरुते surely he is doing I trust
explanation: "I suppose prince Rama is not too depressed or perplexed to attend to his work. He will (perhaps) be doing the duties expected of a manly person.

shloka_text: द्विविधं त्रिविधोपायमुपायमपि सेवते। विजिगीषुस्सुहृत्कच्चिन्मित्रेषु च परन्तपः।।5.36.17।।
transliteration: dvividhaṃ trividhopāyamupāyamapi sevate| vijigīṣussuhṛtkaccinmitreṣu ca parantapaḥ
translation: परन्तपः scorcher of enemies, द्विविधम् two kinds, उपायम् strategies, त्रिविधोपायमपि even three kinds of trategies, सेवते following, विजगीषुः he who desires to be victorious, मित्रेषु with friends, सुहृत् कच्चित् has a good team indeed
explanation: "Tell me if Rama, scorcher of enemies, desirous of victory is following a two-fold policy (confrontation and conciliation) A tough enemy cannot be defeated by following this method. A three-fold strategy has to be adopted in this case (confrontation, conciliation and creation of dissension among his foes) to be victorious. I hope he is well-disposed to his friends and has a good team!

shloka_text: कच्चिन्मित्राणि लभते मित्रैश्चाप्यभिगम्यते। कच्चित्कल्याणमित्त्रश्च मित्रत्त्रैश्चापि पुरस्कृतः।।5.36.18।।
transliteration: kaccinmitrāṇi labhate mitraiścāpyabhigamyate| kaccitkalyāṇamittraśca mitrattraiścāpi puraskṛtaḥ
translation: मित्राणि allies, कच्चित् लभते hope he will be making, मित्रैः with allies, अपि अभिगम्यते will want his friendship, कल्याणमित्रश्च कच्चित् hope he has good allies, मित्रैश्च by his allies, अपि पुरस्कृतः honoured
explanation: "I hope he is making new friends, who desire his friendship. Hopefully, Rama is well honoured  by his allies.

shloka_text: कच्चिदाशास्ति देवानां प्रसादं पार्थिवात्मजः। कच्चित्पुरुषकारं च दैवं च प्रतिपद्यते।।5.36.19।।
transliteration: kaccidāśāsti devānāṃ prasādaṃ pārthivātmajaḥ| kaccitpuruṣakāraṃ ca daivaṃ ca pratipadyate
translation: पार्थिवात्मजः prince, देवानाम् of gods, प्रसादम् blessings, आशास्ति कच्चित् is there any hope, पुरुषकारं च his personal efforts, दैवं च providence, प्रतिपद्यते he obeys
explanation: "Does the prince ever seek the blessings of gods or fall back upon personal effort as well as providence?

shloka_text: कच्चिन्न विगतस्नेहः प्रवासान्मयि राघवः। कच्चिन्मां व्यसनादस्मान्मोक्षयिष्यति वानर।।5.36.20।।
transliteration: kaccinna vigatasnehaḥ pravāsānmayi rāghavaḥ| kaccinmāṃ vyasanādasmānmokṣayiṣyati vānara
translation: राघवः Rama, प्रवासात् due to separation, मयि in me विगतस्नेहः devoid of love, न कच्चित् suppose not, वानर vanara, माम् me, अस्मात् from this, व्यसनात् worry, मोक्षयिष्यति कच्चित् will liberate me from this
explanation: "I hope Rama is not devoid of love towards me by  my separation. O Vanara, hope he will liberate me from this misery.

shloka_text: सुखानामुचितो नित्यमसुखानामनौचितः। दुःखमुत्तरमासाद्य कच्चिद्रामो न सीदति।।5.36.21।।
transliteration: sukhānāmucito nityamasukhānāmanaucitaḥ| duḥkhamuttaramāsādya kaccidrāmo na sīdati
translation: नित्यम् always, सुखानाम् delight, उचितः one who deserves, असुखानाम् of difficulties, अनौचितः he does not deserve, राघवः Rama, उत्तरम् later, दुःखम् sorrow, आसाद्य having experienced, न सीदति कच्चित्  hope he is not depressed
explanation: "I hope Rama who deserves happiness and not suffering has not become depressed now , having experienced a spate of sorrows.

shloka_text: कौसल्यायास्तथा कच्चित्सुमित्रायास्तथैव च। अभीक्ष्णं श्रूयते कच्चित्कुशलं भरतस्य च।।5.36.22।।
transliteration: kausalyāyāstathā kaccitsumitrāyāstathaiva ca| abhīkṣṇaṃ śrūyate kaccitkuśalaṃ bharatasya ca
translation: कौसल्यायाः Kausalya's, तथा in the same manner, सुमित्रायाः Sumitra's, तथैव च in the same way, भरतस्य Bharata's, कुशलम् welfare, अभीक्ष्णम् constantly, श्रूयते कच्चित् hope he is hearing
explanation: "I hope he regularly receives news about the welfare of Kausalya, Sumitra and Bharata.

shloka_text: मन्निमित्तेन मानार्हः कच्चिच्छोकेन राघवः। कच्चिन्नान्यमना रामः कच्चिन्मां तारयिष्यति।।5.36.23।।
transliteration: mannimittena mānārhaḥ kaccicchokena rāghavaḥ| kaccinnānyamanā rāmaḥ kaccinmāṃ tārayiṣyati
translation: मानार्हः respectable, राघवः Rama, मन्निमित्तेन on my account, शोकेन because of sorrow, कच्चित् I hope, रामः Rama, नअन्यमनाः he is not absent minded, न कच्चित् may be, माम् me, कच्चित् तारयिष्यति will he save me?
explanation: "I hope respectable Rama is not too absentminded for being immersed in sorrow on my account. Hope he will save me.

shloka_text: कच्चिदक्षौहिणीं भीमां भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। ध्वजिनीं मन्त्रिभिर्गुप्तां प्रेषयिष्यति मत्कृते।।5.36.24।।
transliteration: kaccidakṣauhiṇīṃ bhīmāṃ bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ| dhvajinīṃ mantribhirguptāṃ preṣayiṣyati matkṛte
translation: भ्रातृवत्सलः devoted to brother, भरतः Bharata, मत्कृते for my sake, मन्त्रिभिः with his ministers, गुप्ताम् protected, भीमाम् formidable, अक्षौहिणीम् ध्वजिनीम् akshauhini army, कच्चित् प्रेषयिष्यति  I trust he will send
explanation: "Will Bharata, the devoted brother, send his formidable army of one akshavhini protected by ministers for my cause? I trust he will. (Akshauhini  109350 foot soldiers  65610 horse soldiers  21860 elephants soldiers on chariot)

shloka_text: वानराधिपतिश्शीमान्सुग्रीवः कच्चिदेष्यति। मत्कृते हरिभिर्वीरैर्वृतो दन्तनखायुधैः।।5.36.25।।
transliteration: vānarādhipatiśśīmānsugrīvaḥ kaccideṣyati| matkṛte haribhirvīrairvṛto dantanakhāyudhaiḥ
translation: मत्कृते for my sake, श्रीमान् illustrious, वानराधिपतिः king of vanaras, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, दन्तनखायुधै: those who use their teeth and nails as weapons, वीरैः with valiant ones, हरिभिः with vanaras, वृतः surrounded, एष्वति कच्चित् trust he will reach.
explanation: "I trust that the illustrious Sugriva surrounded  by valiant vanaras who use their teeth and nails as weapons will reach this place.

shloka_text: कच्चिच्छ लक्ष्मणश्शूरस्सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः। अस्त्रविच्छरजालेन राक्षसान्विधमिष्यति।।5.36.26।।
transliteration: kacciccha lakṣmaṇaśśūrassumitrānandavardhanaḥ| astraviccharajālena rākṣasānvidhamiṣyati
translation: शूरः hero, सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः who enhances Sumitra's delight, अस्त्रवित् a master of weapons, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, शरजालेन by network of arrows, राक्षसान् demons, कच्चित् विधमिष्यति trust he will blow away.
explanation: "Hope heroic Lakshmana, enhancer of the joy of Sumitra, who has mastered the use of weapons will blow away the demons through a network of arrows.

shloka_text: रौद्रेण कच्चिदस्त्रेण ज्वलता निहतं रणे। द्रक्ष्याम्यल्पेन कालेन रावणं ससुहृज्जनम्।।5.36.27।।
transliteration: raudreṇa kaccidastreṇa jvalatā nihataṃ raṇe| drakṣyāmyalpena kālena rāvaṇaṃ sasuhṛjjanam
translation: ज्वलता burning, रौद्रेण with anger, अस्त्रेण by weapon, रणे in the battle, ससुहृज्जनम् along with his relatives, निहतम् slain, रावणम् Ravana, अल्पेन कालेन  in a short time, द्रक्ष्यामि कच्चित् hope to see.
explanation: "Can I hope to see Ravana and his relatives slain in the battle by fiery weapons in a short time?

shloka_text: कच्चिन्न तद्धेमसमानवर्णं तस्याननं पद्मसमानगन्धि। मया विना शुष्यति शोकदीनं जलक्षये पद्ममिवातपेन।।5.36.28।।
transliteration: kaccinna taddhemasamānavarṇaṃ tasyānanaṃ padmasamānagandhi| mayā vinā śuṣyati śokadīnaṃ jalakṣaye padmamivātapena
translation: तस्य his, हेमसमानवर्णम् complexion like gold, पद्मसमानगन्धि fragrance  like  lotus, तत् that, आननम् face, मया विना without me, शोकदीनम् pale with grief, जलक्षये when water dries up, आतपेन due to heat, पद्ममिव like a lotus, न शुष्यति कच्चित् not scorched
explanation: "Hope, Rama's moonlike face without me with its golden complexion and lotus fragrance must not have been pale and withered with tears like the lotus in a pond scorched by the heat.

shloka_text: धर्मापदेशात्त्यजतश्च राज्यं मां चाप्यरण्यं नयतः पदातिम्। नासीद्व्यथा यस्य न भीर्न शोकः कच्चित्स धैर्यं हृदये करोति।।5.36.29।।
transliteration: dharmāpadeśāttyajataśca rājyaṃ māṃ cāpyaraṇyaṃ nayataḥ padātim| nāsīdvyathā yasya na bhīrna śokaḥ kaccitsa dhairyaṃ hṛdaye karoti
translation: धर्मापदेशात् for the cause of establishing righteousness, राज्यम् sovereignty, त्यजतः given up, मां चापि including me, पदातिम् on foot, अरण्यम् to the forest, नयतः conducted, यस्य whose, व्यथा agony, नासीत् not shown, भीः fear, न not, शोकः grief, न not, सः he, हृदये at heart, धैर्यम् courage, करोति कच्चित् will sustain I hope.
explanation: "Rama has given up sovereignty for the sake of establishing righteousness and led me into the forest on foot.He had not then felt any fear, anxiety or grief at heart.Rama showed patience, instead. Hope he retains them.

shloka_text: न चास्य माता न पिता च नान्यः स्नेहाद्विशिष्टोऽस्ति मया समो वा। तावत्त्वहं दूत जिजीविषेयं यावत्प्रवृत्तिं शृणुयां प्रियस्य।।5.36.30।।
transliteration: na cāsya mātā na pitā ca nānyaḥ snehādviśiṣṭo'sti mayā samo vā| tāvattvahaṃ dūta jijīviṣeyaṃ yāvatpravṛttiṃ śṛṇuyāṃ priyasya
translation: अस्य his, स्नेहात् due to love, मया with me, समो वा equal or, विशिष्टः superior, माता mother, न not, पिता father, न not, अन्यः any one else, नास्ति not  there, दूत messenger, प्रियस्य beloved's, प्रवृत्तिम् news, यावत् until, शृणुयाम् I may hear, तावत्तु so long, अहम् I, जिजीविषेयम् I wish to survive.
explanation: "His love for me is superior to his love for his father, mother or any one else. O messenger, I wish to survive till I hear any  news from my dear lord."

shloka_text: इतीव देवी वचनं महार्थं तं वानरेन्द्रं मधुरार्थमुक्त्वा। श्रोतुं पुनस्तस्य वचोऽभिरामं रामार्थयुक्तं विरराम रामा।।5.36.31।।
transliteration: itīva devī vacanaṃ mahārthaṃ taṃ vānarendraṃ madhurārthamuktvā| śrotuṃ punastasya vaco'bhirāmaṃ rāmārthayuktaṃ virarāma rāmā
translation: देवी queen, तं वानरेन्द्रम् that vanara leader, महार्थम् very meaningful, मधुरार्थम् sweet, वचनम् word, उक्त्वा having spoken, तस्य his, अभिरामम्  loving Rama, रामार्थयुक्तम् said for Rama's cause, वचः word, पुनः again, श्रोतुम् to hear, विरराम stopped.
explanation: The godlike lady, having spoken to the vanara leader in a very meaningful and sweet manner about her beloved Rama, she remained silent, waiting to hear Hanuman's attractive words of description of Rama once again.

shloka_text: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः। शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत्।।5.36.32।।
transliteration: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā mārutirbhīmavikramaḥ| śirasyañjalimādhāya vākyamuttaramabravīt
translation: भीमविक्रमः fearsome power, मारुतिः Maruti, सीतायाः Sita's, वचनम् word, श्रुत्वा on hearing, शिरसि on his head, अञ्जलिम् both his hands, आधाय placing, उत्तरम् reply, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Having heard Sita, Hanuman endowed with fearsome power placed his folded hands on his head and said this:

shloka_text: न त्वामिहस्थां जानीते रामः कमललोचने। तेन त्वां नानयत्याशु शचीमिव पुरन्दरः।।5.36.33।।
transliteration: na tvāmihasthāṃ jānīte rāmaḥ kamalalocane| tena tvāṃ nānayatyāśu śacīmiva purandaraḥ
translation: कमललोचने lotuseyed, त्वाम् you, इहस्थाम् being here, रामः Rama, न जानीते he does not know, तेन therefore, पुरन्दरः Indra, शचीमिव like Sachi, त्वाम् you, आशु immediately, नानयति he is not taking away.
explanation: "O lotuseyed one Rama knows not that you are here. Therefore he has not taken you away immediately as did Indra to rescue his wife Sachi.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वैव तु वचो मह्यं क्षिप्रमेष्यति राघवः। चमूं प्रकर्षन्महतीं हर्यृक्षगणसङ्कुलाम्।।5.36.34।।
transliteration: śrutvaiva tu vaco mahyaṃ kṣiprameṣyati rāghavaḥ| camūṃ prakarṣanmahatīṃ haryṛkṣagaṇasaṅkulām
translation: मह्यं my, वचः word, श्रुत्वैव तु after hearing, राघवः Rama, हर्यृक्षगणसङ्कुलाम् troops of vanaras and bears, महतीम् huge, चमूम् army, प्रकर्षन् leading, क्षिप्रम् at once, एष्यति will approach.
explanation: "As soon as he hears your words from me, Rama will reach (here), leading a huge army of powerful troops of vanaras and bears.

shloka_text: विष्टम्भयित्वा बाणौघैरक्षोभ्यं वरुणालयम्। करिष्यति पुरीं लङ्कां काकुत्स्थः शान्तराक्षसाम्।।5.36.35।।
transliteration: viṣṭambhayitvā bāṇaughairakṣobhyaṃ varuṇālayam| kariṣyati purīṃ laṅkāṃ kākutsthaḥ śāntarākṣasām
translation: काकुत्स्थः Kakutstha, अक्षोभ्यम् imperturbable, वरुणालयम् abode of Varuna, बाणौघैः by torrent of arrows, विष्टम्भयित्वा make still, लङ्कां पुरीम् city of Lanka, शान्तराक्षसाम् all the demons, करिष्यति will make.
explanation: "Kakutstha Rama will still the imperturbable abode of Varuna (ocean) by the torrent of his arrows and rid the city of Lanka of all the demons.

shloka_text: तत्र यद्यन्तरा मृत्युर्यदि देवास्सहासुराः। स्थास्यन्ति पथि रामस्य स तानपि वधिष्यति।।5.36.36।।
transliteration: tatra yadyantarā mṛtyuryadi devāssahāsurāḥ| sthāsyanti pathi rāmasya sa tānapi vadhiṣyati
translation: तत्र there, रामस्य Rama's, पथि on his way, अन्तरा in between, मृत्युः death, सहासुराः including all demons, देवाः gods, स्थास्यन्ति यदि if they obstruct, सः he, तानपि even them, वधिष्यति will slay.
explanation: "Thereafter, whoever comes Rama's way,  be it  gods or demons or even death or any one else he will destroy them.

shloka_text: तवादर्शनजेनार्ये शोकेन स परिप्लुतः। न शर्म लभते रामस्सिंहार्दित इव द्विपः।।5.36.37।।
transliteration: tavādarśanajenārye śokena sa pariplutaḥ| na śarma labhate rāmassiṃhārdita iva dvipaḥ
translation: आर्ये O noble lady, सः रामः that Rama, तव your, अदर्शनजेन on account of not seeing you, शोकेन in sorrow, परिप्लुतः immersed, सिंहार्दितः tormented by a lion, द्विपः इव like an elephant, शर्म न लभते is not happy.
explanation: "O noble lady not being able to see you, Rama is immersed in an ocean of sorrow, he has no solace like an elephant tormented by a lion.

shloka_text: मलयेन च विन्ध्येन मेरुणा मन्दरेण च। दर्दुरेण च ते देवि शपे मूलफलेन च।।5.36.38।। यथा सुनयनं वल्गु बिम्बोष्ठं चारु कुण्डलम् । मुखं द्रक्ष्यसि रामस्य पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्।।5.36.39।।
transliteration: malayena ca vindhyena meruṇā mandareṇa ca| dardureṇa ca te devi śape mūlaphalena ca yathā sunayanaṃ valgu bimboṣṭhaṃ cāru kuṇḍalam | mukhaṃ drakṣyasi rāmasya pūrṇacandramivoditam
translation: देवि O Sita, मलयेन च by Malaya mountain, विन्ध्येन by Vindhya, मेरुणा by Meru, दर्दुरेण by Dardura, मूलफलेन by roots and fruits, ते to you, शपे I swear, यथा as, सुनयनम्  with beautiful eyes, वल्गु बिम्बोष्ठम् lips like bimba fruit, चारु कुण्डलम् with lovely earrings, उदितम् risen, पूर्णचन्द्रमिव like the fullmoon, रामस्य Rama's, मुखम् face, द्रक्ष्यसि you will see.
explanation: "O Sita I swear in the name of mountains like Malaya, Vindhya, Meru, and Dardura (the abodes of monkeys and bears) and  by the roots and fruits as well (which are the food of vanaras). you will soon behold Rama with beautiful eyes, red lips like bimba fruit, lovely earrings and a countenance resembling the full moon.

shloka_text: मलयेन च विन्ध्येन मेरुणा मन्दरेण च। दर्दुरेण च ते देवि शपे मूलफलेन च।।5.36.38।। यथा सुनयनं वल्गु बिम्बोष्ठं चारु कुण्डलम् । मुखं द्रक्ष्यसि रामस्य पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्।।5.36.39।।
transliteration: malayena ca vindhyena meruṇā mandareṇa ca| dardureṇa ca te devi śape mūlaphalena ca yathā sunayanaṃ valgu bimboṣṭhaṃ cāru kuṇḍalam | mukhaṃ drakṣyasi rāmasya pūrṇacandramivoditam
translation: देवि O Sita, मलयेन च by Malaya mountain, विन्ध्येन by Vindhya, मेरुणा by Meru, दर्दुरेण by Dardura, मूलफलेन by roots and fruits, ते to you, शपे I swear, यथा as, सुनयनम्  with beautiful eyes, वल्गु बिम्बोष्ठम् lips like bimba fruit, चारु कुण्डलम् with lovely earrings, उदितम् risen, पूर्णचन्द्रमिव like the fullmoon, रामस्य Rama's, मुखम् face, द्रक्ष्यसि you will see.
explanation: "O Sita I swear in the name of mountains like Malaya, Vindhya, Meru, and Dardura (the abodes of monkeys and bears) and  by the roots and fruits as well (which are the food of vanaras). you will soon behold Rama with beautiful eyes, red lips like bimba fruit, lovely earrings and a countenance resembling the full moon.

shloka_text: क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि वैदेहि रामं प्रस्रवणे गिरौ। शतक्रतुमिवासीनं नागराजस्य मूर्धनि।।5.36.40।।
transliteration: kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi vaidehi rāmaṃ prasravaṇe girau| śatakratumivāsīnaṃ nāgarājasya mūrdhani
translation: वैदेहि Vaidehi, प्रस्रवणे गिरौ on mount Prasravana, रामम् Rama, नागराजस्य elephant's, मूर्धनि on the back, आसीनम् seated, शतक्रतुम् इव like Indra who has performed a hundred sacrifices, क्षिप्रम् soon, द्रक्ष्यसि you will see.
explanation: "O Vaidehi, you will soon see Rama seated on the Prasravana mountain just as Indra (who performed a hundred sacrifices) seated on the back of the king of elephants.

shloka_text: न मांसं राघवो भुङक्ते न चाऽपि मधु सेवते। वन्यं सुविहितं नित्यं भक्तमश्नाति पञ्चमम्।।5.36.41।।
transliteration: na māṃsaṃ rāghavo bhuṅakte na cā'pi madhu sevate| vanyaṃ suvihitaṃ nityaṃ bhaktamaśnāti pañcamam
translation: राघवः Rama, मांसम् meat, न भुङक्ते not eating, मधुचापि even wine, न सेवते he is not taking, नित्यम् always, पञ्चमम् fifth meal, सुविहितम् prescribed for, वन्यम् available in the forest, भुक्तम् food, अश्नाति eats.
explanation: "Rama is not eating meat, nor drinking wine. He takes only the one fifth of a meal (sanctioned for an ascetic) available in the forest.

shloka_text: नैव दंशान्न मशकान्न कीटान्न सरीसृपान्। राघवोऽपनयेद्गात्रात्त्वद्गतेनान्तरात्मना।।5.36.42।।
transliteration: naiva daṃśānna maśakānna kīṭānna sarīsṛpān| rāghavo'panayedgātrāttvadgatenāntarātmanā
translation: राघवः Rama, त्वद्गतेन thinking of you, अन्तरात्मना with heart, गात्रात् from his limbs, दंशान् flies, नैव अपनयेत् will not drive away, मशकान् mosquitoes, न not, कीटान् insects, न not, सरीसृपान् serpents, न not.
explanation: "Since you left, Rama has been always thinking sincerely of you, no longer drives away flies or mosquitoes nor insects or serpents from his body (his mind entirely fixed on you).

shloka_text: नित्यं ध्यानपरो रामो नित्यं शोकपरायणः। नान्यच्चिन्तयते किञ्चित्स तु कामवशं गतः।।5.36.43।।
transliteration: nityaṃ dhyānaparo rāmo nityaṃ śokaparāyaṇaḥ| nānyaccintayate kiñcitsa tu kāmavaśaṃ gataḥ
translation: रामः Rama, नित्यम् ever, ध्यानपरः reflecting on you, नित्यम् ever, शोकपरायणः totally given to grief, सः he, कामवशं गतः absorbed in love for you, अन्यत् no other thoughts, न चिन्तयते he is not thinking.
explanation: "Rama is always lost in thought. He is totally given to grief. Absorbed in love for you, he thinks of none else৷৷

shloka_text: अनिद्रस्सततं रामस्सुप्तोऽपि च नरोत्तमः। सीतेति मधुरां वाणीं व्याहरन्प्रतिबुध्यते।।5.36.44।।
