explanation: "You alone can know about who he is and what he is about. A serpent alone knows the movement (footprints) of another serpent. There is no doubt about it.

shloka_text: अहमप्यस्य भीतास्मि नैनं जानामि को न्वयं। वेद्मि राक्षसमेवैनं कामरूपिणमागतम्।।5.42.10।।
transliteration: ahamapyasya bhītāsmi nainaṃ jānāmi ko nvayaṃ| vedmi rākṣasamevainaṃ kāmarūpiṇamāgatam
translation: अहमपि I am also, अस्य at him, भीता अस्मि I am scared of,  एनम् him, को नु who he is, अयम् this person, न जानामि I do not know, एनम् him, आगतम् came, कामरूपिणम् who has assumed his desired form in various ways, राक्षसमेव demon only, वेद्मि I think.
explanation: "I am also scared of him. I do not know who he is. I think he is a demon, who came here assuming a form of his choice.

shloka_text: वैदेह्या वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षस्यो विद्रुता दिशः। स्थिताः काश्चिद्गताः काश्चिद्रावणाय निवेदितुम्।।5.42.11।।
transliteration: vaidehyā vacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasyo vidrutā diśaḥ| sthitāḥ kāścidgatāḥ kāścidrāvaṇāya niveditum
translation: वैदेह्याः Vaidehi's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा after listening to, राक्षस्यः ogresses, दिशः in all directions, विद्रुताः ran, काश्चित् some, स्थिताः stood there, काश्चित् some, रावणाय to Ravana, निवेदितुम् to report, गताः fled.
explanation: LIstening to Vaidehi's words the ogresses divided themselves and fled in all directions. While some stood there, others went to report to Ravana.

shloka_text: रावणस्य समीपे तु राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः। विरूपं वानरं भीममाख्यातुमुपचक्रमुः।।5.42.12।।
transliteration: rāvaṇasya samīpe tu rākṣasyo vikṛtānanāḥ| virūpaṃ vānaraṃ bhīmamākhyātumupacakramuḥ
translation: विकृताननाः uglyfaced, राक्षस्यः shedemons, रावणस्य to Ravana, समीपे presence, विरूपम्  disfigured, भीमम् frightening, वानरम् vanara, आख्यातुम् to report, उपचक्रमुः started.
explanation: The uglyfaced ogresses went to the presence of Ravana and reported about the frightening form of the vanara.

shloka_text: अशोकवनिकामध्ये राजन्भीमवपुः कपिः। सीतया कृतसंवादस्तिष्ठत्यमितविक्रमः।।5.42.13।।
transliteration: aśokavanikāmadhye rājanbhīmavapuḥ kapiḥ| sītayā kṛtasaṃvādastiṣṭhatyamitavikramaḥ
translation: राजन् O king, सीतया with Sita, कृतसंवादः had a dialogue, भीमवपुः fearsome figure, अमितविक्रमः very powerful, कपिः vanara, अशोकवनिकामध्ये in the midst of Ashoka garden, तिष्ठति is stationed.
explanation: "Your majesty an extremely powerful and frightening Vanara had a dialogue with Sita. He is stationed in the midst of Ashoka garden.

shloka_text: न च तं जानकी सीता हरिं हरिणलोचना। अस्माभिर्बहुधा पृष्टा निवेदयितुमिच्छति।।5.42.14।।
transliteration: na ca taṃ jānakī sītā hariṃ hariṇalocanā| asmābhirbahudhā pṛṣṭā nivedayitumicchati
translation: हरिणलोचना deereyed, जानकी Janaki, सीता Sita, अस्माभिः by us, पृष्टा questioned, तम् about him, निवेदयितुम् to disclose, न इच्छति not willing.
explanation: "The deereyed Sita is not willing to disclose to us his identity even when we questioned her.

shloka_text: वासवस्य भवेद्दूतो दूतो वैश्रवणस्य वा। प्रेषितो वापि रामेण सीतान्वेषणकाङ्क्षया।।5.42.15।।
transliteration: vāsavasya bhaveddūto dūto vaiśravaṇasya vā| preṣito vāpi rāmeṇa sītānveṣaṇakāṅkṣayā
translation: वासवस्य Vasava's, दूतः envoy, वैश्रवणस्य Vaisravana's, दूतो वा is he an envoy, सीतान्वेषणकाङ्क्षया or one who has come to trace Sita, रामेण by Rama, प्रेषितो वापि or sent, भवेत् may be.
explanation: "He may be an envoy of Indra or Kubera or of Rama sent with an intent to trace Sita.

shloka_text: तेन त्वद्भुतरूपेण यत्तत्तव मनोहरम्। नानामृगगणाकीर्णं प्रमृष्टं प्रमदावनम्।।5.42.16।।
transliteration: tena tvadbhutarūpeṇa yattattava manoharam| nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇaṃ pramṛṣṭaṃ pramadāvanam
translation: अद्भुतरूपेण by a person of wonderful form, तेन  by him, मनोहरम् delightful, नानामृगगणाकीर्णम् filled with various kinds of animals, यत् such, तव your, प्रमदावनम् beautiful pleasure garden, प्रमृष्टम् ruined.
explanation: "Your beautiful pleasure garden filled with a variety of beasts has been ruined by this wonderful figure.

shloka_text: न तत्र कश्चिदुद्देशो यस्तेन न विनाशितः। यत्र सा जानकी सीता स तेन न विनाशितः।।5.42.17।।
transliteration: na tatra kaściduddeśo yastena na vināśitaḥ| yatra sā jānakī sītā sa tena na vināśitaḥ
translation: तेन by him, यः whichever, न विनाशितः not ruined, उद्देशः place, तत्र there, कश्चित् even one, न not, सा that, जानकी Janaki, सीता Sita, यत्र wherever, सः that place, तेन by him, न विनाशितः not ruined.
explanation: There is not a single place that has not been ruined by him there. Only the place where Janaka's daughter, Sita is resting has not been touched.

shloka_text: जानकीरक्षणार्थं वा श्रमाद्वा नोपलभ्यते। अथवा कश्श्रमस्तस्य सैव तेनाभिरक्षिता।।5.42.18।।
transliteration: jānakīrakṣaṇārthaṃ vā śramādvā nopalabhyate| athavā kaśśramastasya saiva tenābhirakṣitā
translation: जानकीरक्षणार्थं वा is it to protect Janaki, श्रमाद्वा or is it because he was tired, नोपलभ्यते we are not able to understand, अथवा or else, तस्य his, श्रमः tiresomeness, कः what, तेन by him, सैव she alone, अभिरक्षिता is spared.
explanation: "It is not clear whether he spared that place for protecting Janakai or he stopped due to exhaustion. What is fatigue for him? It must be to save her that she is spared by him.

shloka_text: चारुपल्लवपुष्पाढ्यं यं सीता स्वयमास्थिता। प्रवृद्धश्शिंशुपावृक्ष स्स च तेनाभिरक्षितः।।5.42.19।।
transliteration: cārupallavapuṣpāḍhyaṃ yaṃ sītā svayamāsthitā| pravṛddhaśśiṃśupāvṛkṣa ssa ca tenābhirakṣitaḥ
translation: सीता Sita, चारुपल्लवपुष्पाढ्यम् a tree with lovely tender leaves and flowers, यम् whom, स्वयम् personally, आस्थिता she resorted, सः that, प्रवृद्धः large, शिंशुपावृक्षः simsupa tree, तेन by him, अभिरक्षितः is saved from destruction.
explanation: "He has spared the simsupa tree with lovely, tender leaves and flowers which is a chosen  resort by Sita.

shloka_text: तस्योग्ररूपस्योग्र त्वं दण्डमाज्ञातुमर्हसि। सीता सम्भाषिता येन तद्वनं च विनाशितम्।।5.42.20।।
transliteration: tasyograrūpasyogra tvaṃ daṇḍamājñātumarhasi| sītā sambhāṣitā yena tadvanaṃ ca vināśitam
translation: येन whomsoever, सीता Sita, सम्भाषिता had dialogue, तत् वनं च that garden also, विनाशितम् has been ruined, तस्य his, उग्ररूपस्य of a fierce form, त्वम् you, उग्रम् severe, दण्डम् punishment, आज्ञातुम् to order, अर्हसि is proper
explanation: "Your highness should take severe action on that person of fierce appearance with whom Sita dared to speak, and by whom the garden is ruined.

shloka_text: मनः परिगृहीतां तां तव रक्षोगणेश्वर। कस्सीतामभिभाषेत यो न स्यात्त्यक्तजीवितः।।5.42.21।।
transliteration: manaḥ parigṛhītāṃ tāṃ tava rakṣogaṇeśvara| kassītāmabhibhāṣeta yo na syāttyaktajīvitaḥ
translation: रक्षोगणेश्वर O lord of the demon clan, मनः परिगृहीताम् one who is desired by you, तां सीताम् that Sita, यः whoever, त्यक्तजीवितः given up hope of life, न स्यात् if not, कः who, अभिभाषेत he will dare to talk.
explanation: "O lord of the demon clan Who dares to talk to Sita if he has not given up all hope of life, since she is desired by you".

shloka_text: राक्षसीनां वचश्त्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। हुताग्निरिव जज्वाल कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः।।5.42.22।।
transliteration: rākṣasīnāṃ vacaśtrutvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ| hutāgniriva jajvāla kopasaṃvartitekṣaṇaḥ
translation: राक्षसेश्वरः lord of ogres, रावणः Ravana, राक्षसीनाम् shedemons, वचः words, श्रुत्वा after hearing, कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः his eyeballs rolling in anger, हुताग्निरिव like sacrificial fire into which offering is made,जज्वाल flared.
explanation: On listening to the report of the ogresses, Ravana, the lord of demons flared up like blazing flame of a sacrificial fire, his eyeballs rolling in rage.

shloka_text: तस्य क्रुद्धस्य नेत्राभ्यां प्रापतन्नास्रबिन्दवः। दीप्ताभ्यामिव दीपाभ्यां सार्चिष स्स्नेहबिन्दवः।।5.42.23।।
transliteration: tasya kruddhasya netrābhyāṃ prāpatannāsrabindavaḥ| dīptābhyāmiva dīpābhyāṃ sārciṣa ssnehabindavaḥ
translation: क्रुद्धस्य of the angry, तस्य his, नेत्राभ्याम् from both the eyes, दीप्ताभ्याम् burning ones, दीपाभ्याम् from two lamps, सार्चिषः with flames, स्नेहबिन्दवः इव like drops of oil, अस्रबिन्दवः drops of tears, प्रापतन् fell down.
explanation: From his angry eyes fell down drops of tears just as burning drops of oil drip from two burning lamps.

shloka_text: आत्मनस्सदृशान्शूरान्किङ्करान्नाम राक्षसान्। व्यादिदेश महातेजा निग्रहार्थं हनूमतः।।5.42.24।।
transliteration: ātmanassadṛśānśūrānkiṅkarānnāma rākṣasān| vyādideśa mahātejā nigrahārthaṃ hanūmataḥ
translation: महातेजाः powerful, हनूमतः Hanuman's, निग्रहार्थम् to catch, आत्मनः his, सदृशान् equals, शूरान् heroes, किङ्करान्नाम called kinkaras, राक्षसान् demons, व्यादिदेश commanded.
explanation: Then powerful Ravana commanded heroic demons called kinkaras who vied in strength to catch Hanuman.

shloka_text: तेषामशीतिसाहस्रं किङ्कराणां तरस्विनाम्। निर्ययुर्भवनात्तस्मात्कूटमुद्गरपाणयः।।5.42.25।। महोदरा महादंष्ट्रा घोररूपा महाबलाः। युद्धाभिमनसस्सर्वे हनुमद्ग्रहणोद्यताः।।5.42.26।।
transliteration: teṣāmaśītisāhasraṃ kiṅkarāṇāṃ tarasvinām| niryayurbhavanāttasmātkūṭamudgarapāṇayaḥ mahodarā mahādaṃṣṭrā ghorarūpā mahābalāḥ| yuddhābhimanasassarve hanumadgrahaṇodyatāḥ
translation: तरस्विनाम् of swiftmoving ones, तेषां किङ्कराणाम् of the kinkaras, अशीतिसाहस्रम् eighty thousand, महोदराः largebellied, महादंष्ट्राः largetoothed, घोररूपाः dreadfullooking, महाबलाः powerful, युद्धाभिमनसः ready to fight in war, सर्वे all, कूटमुद्गरपाणयः hammers and clubs, हनुमद्ग्रहणोद्यताः resolved to capture Hanuman, तस्मात् from that, भवनात् building, निर्ययुः came out.
explanation: Eighty thousand powerful  kinkaras (a clan of demons), largebellied, with large teeth and of dreadful appearance, swift in action, armed with hammers and clubs marched from there, resolved to capture Hanuman.

shloka_text: तेषामशीतिसाहस्रं किङ्कराणां तरस्विनाम्। निर्ययुर्भवनात्तस्मात्कूटमुद्गरपाणयः।।5.42.25।। महोदरा महादंष्ट्रा घोररूपा महाबलाः। युद्धाभिमनसस्सर्वे हनुमद्ग्रहणोद्यताः।।5.42.26।।
transliteration: teṣāmaśītisāhasraṃ kiṅkarāṇāṃ tarasvinām| niryayurbhavanāttasmātkūṭamudgarapāṇayaḥ mahodarā mahādaṃṣṭrā ghorarūpā mahābalāḥ| yuddhābhimanasassarve hanumadgrahaṇodyatāḥ
translation: तरस्विनाम् of swiftmoving ones, तेषां किङ्कराणाम् of the kinkaras, अशीतिसाहस्रम् eighty thousand, महोदराः largebellied, महादंष्ट्राः largetoothed, घोररूपाः dreadfullooking, महाबलाः powerful, युद्धाभिमनसः ready to fight in war, सर्वे all, कूटमुद्गरपाणयः hammers and clubs, हनुमद्ग्रहणोद्यताः resolved to capture Hanuman, तस्मात् from that, भवनात् building, निर्ययुः came out.
explanation: Eighty thousand powerful  kinkaras (a clan of demons), largebellied, with large teeth and of dreadful appearance, swift in action, armed with hammers and clubs marched from there, resolved to capture Hanuman.

shloka_text: ते कपीन्द्रं समासाद्य तोरणस्थमवस्थितम्। अभिपेतुर्महावेगाः पतङ्गा इव पावकम्।।5.42.27।।
transliteration: te kapīndraṃ samāsādya toraṇasthamavasthitam| abhipeturmahāvegāḥ pataṅgā iva pāvakam
translation: ते they, तोरणस्थम् near the archway, अवस्थितम् stood ready, कपीन्द्रम् leader of vanaras, समासाद्य having approached, महावेगाः swift ones, पतङ्गाः moths, पावकम् इव like rushing into the flame, अभिपेतुः rushed.
explanation: The kinkaras rushed towards the leader of vanaras who stood near the archway like the moths rushing towards the flame.

shloka_text: ते गदाभिर्विचित्राभिः परिघैः काञ्चनाङ्गदैः। आजघ्नुर्वानरश्रेष्ठं शरैश्चादित्यसन्निभैः।।5.42.28।।
transliteration: te gadābhirvicitrābhiḥ parighaiḥ kāñcanāṅgadaiḥ| ājaghnurvānaraśreṣṭhaṃ śaraiścādityasannibhaiḥ
translation: ते they, विचित्राभिः with wonderful ones, गदाभिः with iron maces, काञ्चनाङ्गदैः edged with gold, परिघैः with crowbars, आदित्यसन्निभैः resembling the Sun, शरैश्च with arrows, वानरश्रेष्ठम् best of vanaras, आजघ्नुः assailed.
explanation: They assailed Hanuman with iron maces, crowbars edged with gold and shining arrows resembling the Sun.

shloka_text: मुद्गरैः पट्टिशैश्शूलैः प्रासतोमरशक्तिभिः। परिवार्य हनूमन्तं सहसा तस्थुरग्रतः।।5.42.29।।
transliteration: mudgaraiḥ paṭṭiśaiśśūlaiḥ prāsatomaraśaktibhiḥ| parivārya hanūmantaṃ sahasā tasthuragrataḥ
translation: मुद्गरैः with hammers, पट्टि with sharpedged spears, शूलैः with tridents, प्रासतोमरशक्तिभिः with barbed missiles and powerful javelins, सहसा at once, हनूमन्तम् Hanuman, परिवार्य surrounded, अग्रतः in front of him, तस्थुः stood.
explanation: They quickly surrounded Hanuman and stood with hammers, sharpedged spears, tridents, barbed missiles and powerful javelins.

shloka_text: हनुमानपि तेजस्वी श्रीमान्पर्वतसन्निभः। क्षितावाविध्य लाङ्गूलं ननाद च महास्वनम्।।5.42.30।।
transliteration: hanumānapi tejasvī śrīmānparvatasannibhaḥ| kṣitāvāvidhya lāṅgūlaṃ nanāda ca mahāsvanam
translation: तेजस्वी brilliant, श्रीमान् illustrious one, पर्वतसन्निभः resembling a mountain, हनुमानपि Hanuman also, लाङ्गूलम् tail, क्षितौ on the ground, आविध्य waved, महास्वनम् causing loud sound, ननाद च roared.
explanation: Gigantic Hanuman, illustrious and brilliant, roared and waved his tail striking it with force on the ground causing loud sound.

shloka_text: स भूत्वा सुमहाकायो हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः। धृष्टमास्फोटयामास लङ्कां शब्देन पूरयन्।।5.42.31।।
transliteration: sa bhūtvā sumahākāyo hanumānmārutātmajaḥ| dhṛṣṭamāsphoṭayāmāsa laṅkāṃ śabdena pūrayan
translation: मारुतात्मजः Maruti's son, सः हनुमान् that Hanuman, सुमहाकायः with a huge body, भूत्वा assuming, शब्देन by the sound, लङ्काम् entire Lanka, पूरयन् echoed, धृष्टम् wildly, अस्फोटयामास patted.
explanation: Hanuman, son of Maruti, enlarged his body to a huge size and patted himself wildly  making loud noise that echoed the entire Lanka.

shloka_text: तस्यास्फोटितशब्देन महता सानुनादिना। पेतुर्विहङ्गा गगनादुच्चैश्चेदमघोषयत्।।5.42.32।।
transliteration: tasyāsphoṭitaśabdena mahatā sānunādinā| peturvihaṅgā gaganāduccaiścedamaghoṣayat
translation: सानुनादिना by the frightening echoing sound, महता with great, तस्य his, अस्फोटितशब्देन by the sound of the patting, विहङ्गाः birds, गगनात् from the sky, पेतुः fell down, उच्चैः with a loud noise, इदम् thus, अघोषयत् च proclaimed.
explanation: By the highly frightening sound caused by Hanuman patting, the birds from the sky fell down making a loud noise and Hanuman proclaimed in a loud voice as follows:

shloka_text: जयत्यतिबलो रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः। राजा जयति सुग्रीवो राघवेणाभिपालितः।।5.42.33।।
transliteration: jayatyatibalo rāmo lakṣmaṇaśca mahābalaḥ| rājā jayati sugrīvo rāghaveṇābhipālitaḥ
translation: अतिबलः mighty, रामः Rama, जयति is victorious, महाबलः powerful, लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana also, राघवेण by Rama, अभिपालितः ruled, राजा king, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, जयति is victorious.
explanation: "Victory to Rama, the mighty and powerful, Victory to Lakshmana. Victory to king Sugriva who is ruled by Rama."

shloka_text: दासोऽहं कोसलेन्द्रस्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। हनुमान्शत्रुसैन्यानां निहन्ता मारुतात्मजः।।5.42.34।।
transliteration: dāso'haṃ kosalendrasya rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ| hanumānśatrusainyānāṃ nihantā mārutātmajaḥ
translation: शत्रुसैन्यानाम् of the enemy army, निहन्ता killer, मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, हनुमान् Hanuman, अहम् I am, कोसलेन्द्रस्य of the lord of Kosala kingdom, अक्लिष्टकर्मणः a man of unwearied action, रामस्य Rama's, दासः servant.
explanation: "I, son of the Windgod, destroyer of hostile armies, am a servant of Rama, the lord of Kosala kingdom, a man of unwearied action.

shloka_text: न रावणसहस्रं मे युद्धे प्रतिबलं भवेत्। शिलाभिस्तु प्रहरतः पादपैश्च सहस्रशः।।5.42.35।।
transliteration: na rāvaṇasahasraṃ me yuddhe pratibalaṃ bhavet| śilābhistu praharataḥ pādapaiśca sahasraśaḥ
translation: सहस्रशः a thousand ways, शिलाभिः with stones, पादपैश्च with even trees, प्रहरतः while I pound, मे to me, युद्धे in war, रावणसहस्रम् a thousand Ravanas, प्रतिबलम् match in strength, न भवेत् will not.
explanation: Even a thousand Ravanas will not match me in strength when I pound stones and trees in a thousand ways.

shloka_text: अर्दयित्वा पुरीं लङ्कामभिवाद्य च मैथिलीम्। समृद्धार्थो गमिष्यामि मिषतां सर्वरक्षसाम्।।5.42.36।।
transliteration: ardayitvā purīṃ laṅkāmabhivādya ca maithilīm| samṛddhārtho gamiṣyāmi miṣatāṃ sarvarakṣasām
translation: सर्वरक्षसाम् all ogres, मिषताम् as they gaze, लङ्कां पुरीम् city of Lanka, अर्दयित्वा shall destroy, मैथिलीम् to Mythili, अभिवाद्य च and pay respects, समृद्धार्थः having accomplished my purpose, गमिष्यामि I will return.
explanation: "I shall destroy the city of Lanka and pay my respects to Mythili right under the nose of all demons. I will return with my purpose accomplished.

shloka_text: तस्य सन्नादशब्देन तेऽभवन्भयशङ्किताः। ददृशुश्च हनूमन्तं सन्ध्यामेघमिवोन्नतम्।।5.42.37।।
transliteration: tasya sannādaśabdena te'bhavanbhayaśaṅkitāḥ| dadṛśuśca hanūmantaṃ sandhyāmeghamivonnatam
translation: ते they, तस्य his, सन्नादशब्देन with the sound of hearing, भयशङ्किता: errified, अभवन् seemed, सन्ध्यामेघमिव like a cloud in twilight, उन्नतम् towering, हनूमन्तम् Hanuman, ददृशुश्च saw.
explanation: Terrified on hearing the roar, the kinkaras looked at the towering Hanuman who seemed like a cloud in twilight (red in colour).

shloka_text: स्वामिसन्देशनिश्शङ्कास्ततस्ते राक्षसाः कपिम्। चित्रैः प्रहरणैर्भीमैरभिपेतुस्ततस्ततः।।5.42.38।।
transliteration: svāmisandeśaniśśaṅkāstataste rākṣasāḥ kapim| citraiḥ praharaṇairbhīmairabhipetustatastataḥ
translation: ततः then, ते they, राक्षसाः demons, स्वामिसन्देशनिःशङ्का: on account the king's command putting aside their fear, चित्रैः with dreadful, प्रहरणैः with weapons, कपिम् the vanara, अभिपेतुः attacked him.
explanation: Obeying their king's commnad, putting aside their fear, the kinkaras freely attacked the vanara  from all directions with dreadful weapons.

shloka_text: स तैः परिवृतश्शूरैस्सर्वतस्सुमहाबलः। आससादाऽयसं भीमं परिघं तोरणाश्रितम्।।5.42.39।।
transliteration: sa taiḥ parivṛtaśśūraissarvatassumahābalaḥ| āsasādā'yasaṃ bhīmaṃ parighaṃ toraṇāśritam
translation: सुमहाबलः exceesively powerful one, सः he, Hanuman, शूरैः with heroes, तैः with those, सर्वतः all over, परिवृतः surrounded, तोरणाश्रितम् near the  archway, भीमम् terrific, आयसम् a weapon made of iron, परिघम् iron beam, आससाद picked up.
explanation: Extremely powerful Hanuman surrounded by heroes all over, on his part went to the archway and picked up a terrific iron beam.

shloka_text: स तं परिघमादाय जघान रजनीचरान्। स पन्नगमिवादाय स्फुरन्तं विनतासुतः।।5.42.40।। विचचाराम्बरे वीरः परिगृह्य च मारुतिः।
transliteration: sa taṃ parighamādāya jaghāna rajanīcarān| sa pannagamivādāya sphurantaṃ vinatāsutaḥ vicacārāmbare vīraḥ parigṛhya ca mārutiḥ|
translation: सः he, तं परिघम् that iron beam, आदाय took hold, रजनीचरान् nightrangers, जघान struck them, वीरः hero, सः मारुतिः that Maruti, विनतासुतः just as Vinatha's son, स्फुरन्तम् shoots, पन्नगम् serpent, आदाय seized, परिगृह्य took hold, अम्बरे in the sky, विचचार started moving.
explanation: Hanuman, the mighty hero, seized the iron beam and struck the kinkaras, just as Garuda, the son of Vinata shoots up a struggling serpent and starts taking strides in the sky with the weapon in his hand (like Indra with his thunderbolt did with demons).

shloka_text: स हत्वा राक्षसान्वीरान्किङ्करान्मारुतात्मजः।।5.42.41।। युद्धाकाङ्क्षी पुनर्वीरस्तोरणं समुपाश्रितः।
transliteration: sa hatvā rākṣasānvīrānkiṅkarānmārutātmajaḥ yuddhākāṅkṣī punarvīrastoraṇaṃ samupāśritaḥ|
translation: वीरः hero, सः मारुतात्मजः that Windgod's son, वीरान् heroes, किङ्करान् kinkaras, राक्षसान् ogres, हत्वा having killed, पुनः again, युद्धाकाङ्क्षी desiring further combat, तोरणम् archway, समुपाश्रितः reached.
explanation: The great Windgod's son killed the kinkaras, and returned to the archway desiring further combat.

shloka_text: ततस्तस्माद्भयान्मुक्ताः कतिचित्तत्र राक्षसाः।।5.42.42।। निहतान्किङ्करान्सर्वान्रावणायन्यवेदयन्।
transliteration: tatastasmādbhayānmuktāḥ katicittatra rākṣasāḥ nihatānkiṅkarānsarvānrāvaṇāyanyavedayan|
translation: ततः then, तत्र that, तस्मात् from fear, भयात् out of fear, मुक्ताः relieved, कतिचित् some, राक्षसाः ogres, सर्वान् all, किङ्करान् kinkaras, निहतान् killed, रावणाय to Ravana, न्यवेदयन् reported.
explanation: Then a few surviving ogres took to their heels after getting over that shock and reported to Ravana of the destruction of the kinkaras in the combat

shloka_text: स राक्षसानां निहतं महद्बलं निशम्य राजा परिवृत्तलोचनः। समादिदेशाप्रतिमं पराक्रमे प्रहस्तपुत्रं समरे सुदुर्जयम्।।5.42.43।।
transliteration: sa rākṣasānāṃ nihataṃ mahadbalaṃ niśamya rājā parivṛttalocanaḥ| samādideśāpratimaṃ parākrame prahastaputraṃ samare sudurjayam
translation: स he, राजा king, राक्षसानाम् of ogres, महत् mighty, बलम् army, निहतम् killed, निशम्य after hearing, परिवृत्तलोचनः with his eyes rolling, पराक्रमे in valour, अप्रतिमम् matchless, समरे in war, सुदुर्जयम् difficult to conquer, प्रहस्तपुत्रम् son of Prahasta, समादिदेश commanded.
explanation: The mighty demon king having heard about the killing of the formidable army of ogres, his eyes rolling in rage, commanded the son of Prahasta, who is difficult to conquer and matchless in war. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortysecond sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततस्स किङ्करान्हत्वा हनुमान्ध्यानमास्थितः। वनं भग्नं मया चैत्यप्रासादो न विनाशितः।।5.43.1।। तस्मात्प्रासादमप्येवं भीमं विध्वंसयाम्यहं। इति सञ्चिन्त्य मनसा हनुमान्दर्शयन्बलम्।।5.43.2।। चैत्यप्रासादमाप्लुत्य मेरुशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्। आरुरोह कपिश्रेष्ठो हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः।।5.43.3।।
transliteration: tatassa kiṅkarānhatvā hanumāndhyānamāsthitaḥ| vanaṃ bhagnaṃ mayā caityaprāsādo na vināśitaḥ tasmātprāsādamapyevaṃ bhīmaṃ vidhvaṃsayāmyahaṃ| iti sañcintya manasā hanumāndarśayanbalam caityaprāsādamāplutya meruśṛṅgamivonnatam| āruroha kapiśreṣṭho hanumānmārutātmajaḥ
translation: ततः then, सः हनुमान् that Hanuman, किङ्करान् kinkaras, हत्त्वा having slain, ध्यानम् reflected, आस्थितः resumed, मया by me, वनम् garden, भग्नम् destroyed, चैत्यप्रासादः the Chaitya palace, न विनाशितः not ruined, तस्मात् therefore, अद्य now, अहम् I, भीमम् fearsome, प्रासादम् building, एवम् in this way, विध्वंसयामि I will destroy, कपिश्रेष्ठः foremost of vanaras, मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, हनुमान् Hanuman, मनसा in his mind, इति thus, सञ्चिन्त्य thinking, बलम् strength, दर्शयन्  showed, मेरुशृङ्गमिव like the peak of mount Meru, उन्नतम् tall, चैत्यप्रासादम् Chaitya palace, उत्ल्पुत्य jumped, आरुरोह climbed
explanation: Having slain the kinkaras, Hanuman stood and reflected, ' I have ruined the garden and not the palatial buildings that are like temples (Chaityas)'. Then Hanuman, son of the Windgod, decided in his mind to show his strength and jumped on to the top of the palatial building that appeared like the peak of mount Meru.
comments: Hanuman destroys the demons in the palace

shloka_text: ततस्स किङ्करान्हत्वा हनुमान्ध्यानमास्थितः। वनं भग्नं मया चैत्यप्रासादो न विनाशितः।।5.43.1।। तस्मात्प्रासादमप्येवं भीमं विध्वंसयाम्यहं। इति सञ्चिन्त्य मनसा हनुमान्दर्शयन्बलम्।।5.43.2।। चैत्यप्रासादमाप्लुत्य मेरुशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्। आरुरोह कपिश्रेष्ठो हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः।।5.43.3।।
transliteration: tatassa kiṅkarānhatvā hanumāndhyānamāsthitaḥ| vanaṃ bhagnaṃ mayā caityaprāsādo na vināśitaḥ tasmātprāsādamapyevaṃ bhīmaṃ vidhvaṃsayāmyahaṃ| iti sañcintya manasā hanumāndarśayanbalam caityaprāsādamāplutya meruśṛṅgamivonnatam| āruroha kapiśreṣṭho hanumānmārutātmajaḥ
translation: ततः then, सः हनुमान् that Hanuman, किङ्करान् kinkaras, हत्त्वा having slain, ध्यानम् reflected, आस्थितः resumed, मया by me, वनम् garden, भग्नम् destroyed, चैत्यप्रासादः the Chaitya palace, न विनाशितः not ruined, तस्मात् therefore, अद्य now, अहम् I, भीमम् fearsome, प्रासादम् building, एवम् in this way, विध्वंसयामि I will destroy, कपिश्रेष्ठः foremost of vanaras, मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, हनुमान् Hanuman, मनसा in his mind, इति thus, सञ्चिन्त्य thinking, बलम् strength, दर्शयन्  showed, मेरुशृङ्गमिव like the peak of mount Meru, उन्नतम् tall, चैत्यप्रासादम् Chaitya palace, उत्ल्पुत्य jumped, आरुरोह climbed
explanation: Having slain the kinkaras, Hanuman stood and reflected, ' I have ruined the garden and not the palatial buildings that are like temples (Chaityas)'. Then Hanuman, son of the Windgod, decided in his mind to show his strength and jumped on to the top of the palatial building that appeared like the peak of mount Meru.
comments: Hanuman destroys the demons in the palace

shloka_text: ततस्स किङ्करान्हत्वा हनुमान्ध्यानमास्थितः। वनं भग्नं मया चैत्यप्रासादो न विनाशितः।।5.43.1।। तस्मात्प्रासादमप्येवं भीमं विध्वंसयाम्यहं। इति सञ्चिन्त्य मनसा हनुमान्दर्शयन्बलम्।।5.43.2।। चैत्यप्रासादमाप्लुत्य मेरुशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्। आरुरोह कपिश्रेष्ठो हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः।।5.43.3।।
transliteration: tatassa kiṅkarānhatvā hanumāndhyānamāsthitaḥ| vanaṃ bhagnaṃ mayā caityaprāsādo na vināśitaḥ tasmātprāsādamapyevaṃ bhīmaṃ vidhvaṃsayāmyahaṃ| iti sañcintya manasā hanumāndarśayanbalam caityaprāsādamāplutya meruśṛṅgamivonnatam| āruroha kapiśreṣṭho hanumānmārutātmajaḥ
translation: ततः then, सः हनुमान् that Hanuman, किङ्करान् kinkaras, हत्त्वा having slain, ध्यानम् reflected, आस्थितः resumed, मया by me, वनम् garden, भग्नम् destroyed, चैत्यप्रासादः the Chaitya palace, न विनाशितः not ruined, तस्मात् therefore, अद्य now, अहम् I, भीमम् fearsome, प्रासादम् building, एवम् in this way, विध्वंसयामि I will destroy, कपिश्रेष्ठः foremost of vanaras, मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, हनुमान् Hanuman, मनसा in his mind, इति thus, सञ्चिन्त्य thinking, बलम् strength, दर्शयन्  showed, मेरुशृङ्गमिव like the peak of mount Meru, उन्नतम् tall, चैत्यप्रासादम् Chaitya palace, उत्ल्पुत्य jumped, आरुरोह climbed
explanation: Having slain the kinkaras, Hanuman stood and reflected, ' I have ruined the garden and not the palatial buildings that are like temples (Chaityas)'. Then Hanuman, son of the Windgod, decided in his mind to show his strength and jumped on to the top of the palatial building that appeared like the peak of mount Meru.
comments: Hanuman destroys the demons in the palace

shloka_text: आरुह्य गिरिसङ्काशं प्रासादं हरियूथपः। बभौ स सुमहातेजाः प्रतिसूर्य इवोदितः।।5.43.4।।
transliteration: āruhya girisaṅkāśaṃ prāsādaṃ hariyūthapaḥ| babhau sa sumahātejāḥ pratisūrya ivoditaḥ
translation: हरियूथपः vanara leader, सुमहातेजाः brilliant, सः he, गिरिसङ्काशम् resembling a mountain, प्रासादम् palace, आरुह्य after climbing, उदितः rising, प्रतिसूर्यः इव like another Sun, बभौ looked
explanation: The powerful vanara leader climbed the tall, palatial building which resembled a mountain. He looked like another Sun, just risen.

shloka_text: संप्रधृष्य च दुर्धर्षं चैत्यप्रासादमुत्तमम्। हनुमान्प्रज्वलन्लक्ष्म्या पारियात्रोपमोऽभवत्।।5.43.5।।
transliteration: saṃpradhṛṣya ca durdharṣaṃ caityaprāsādamuttamam| hanumānprajvalanlakṣmyā pāriyātropamo'bhavat
translation: हनुमान् Hanuman, दुर्धर्षम् indomitable, उत्तमम् fine, चैत्यप्रासादम् palace building, सम्प्रधृष्य च  having surrounded लक्ष्म्या with glory, प्रज्वलन् blazing, पारियात्रोपमः like mountain Pariyatra, अभवत् appeared
explanation: Having destroyed the fine palace building, the indomitable Hanuman was blazing with glory like the mountain Pariyatra. (one of the seven Kula mountains viz., Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Shuktiman, Riksha, Vindhya and Pariyatra)

shloka_text: स भूत्वा सुमहाकायः प्रभावान्मारुतात्मजः। धृष्टमास्फोटयामास लङ्कां शब्देन पूरयन्।।5.43.6।।
transliteration: sa bhūtvā sumahākāyaḥ prabhāvānmārutātmajaḥ| dhṛṣṭamāsphoṭayāmāsa laṅkāṃ śabdena pūrayan
translation: सः मारुतात्मजः that son of the Wind god, प्रभावात् by his prowess, सुमहाकायः of a huge body, भूत्वा being, शब्देन by the sound, लङ्काम् Lanka, पूरयन् while filling, धृष्टम् roughly, अस्फोटयामास started patting (his arms)
explanation: Hanuman heaved his body  huge  with his prowess and patted his arms loudly filling the city of Lanka with that terrible sound.

shloka_text: तस्यास्फोटितशब्देन महता श्रोत्रघातिना। पेतुर्विहङ्गमास्तत्र चैत्यपालाश्च मोहिताः।।5.43.7।।
transliteration: tasyāsphoṭitaśabdena mahatā śrotraghātinā| peturvihaṅgamāstatra caityapālāśca mohitāḥ
translation: तस्य by the, श्रोत्रघातिना by the deafening sound, महता with a loud, अस्फोटितशब्देन with the sound of patting, तत्र there, विहङ्गमाः birds, पेतुः fell down, चैत्यपालाश्च guards of the palace, मोहिताः lost consciousness.
explanation: By the deafening sound caused by the patting, the birds fell down and the guards of the palace lost consciousness.

shloka_text: अस्त्रविज्जयतां रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः। राजा जयति सुग्रीवो राघवेणाभिपालितः।।5.43.8।।
transliteration: astravijjayatāṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇaśca mahābalaḥ| rājā jayati sugrīvo rāghaveṇābhipālitaḥ
translation: अस्त्रवित् knowledgeable about all missiles, रामः Rama, जयताम् be victorious, महाबलः matchless warrior, लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana also, राघवेण by Rama, अभिपालितः ruled, राजा king, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, जयति be victorious.
explanation: 'May Sri Rama, unsurpassed in the use of missiles be victorious May his brother, mighty Lakshmana, a matchless warrior be victorious. May King Sugriva ruled by Rama be victorious.'

shloka_text: दासोऽहं कोसलेन्द्रस्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। हनुमान्शत्रुसैन्यानां निहन्ता मारुतात्मजः।।5.43.9।।
transliteration: dāso'haṃ kosalendrasya rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ| hanumānśatrusainyānāṃ nihantā mārutātmajaḥ
translation: शत्रुसैन्यानाम् of enemy army, निहन्ता killer, मारुतात्मजः son of the Windgod, हनुमान् Hanuman, अहम् I, कोसलेन्द्रस्य king of Kosala's, अक्लिष्टकर्मणः one who can  acomplish any task with ease, रामस्य Rama's, दासः servant.
explanation: 'I am the son of the Windgod, destroyer of enemy army. I am a servant of Rama, the king of Kosala who can accomplish any task with ease.

shloka_text: न रावणसहस्रं मे युद्धे प्रतिबलं भवेत्। शिलाभिस्तु प्रहरतः पादपैश्च सहस्रशः।।5.43.10।।
transliteration: na rāvaṇasahasraṃ me yuddhe pratibalaṃ bhavet| śilābhistu praharataḥ pādapaiśca sahasraśaḥ
translation: सहस्रशः in a thousand ways, शिलाभिः with rocks, पादपैश्च or even with trees, प्रहरतः hurling, मे to me, युद्धे in war, रावणसहस्रम् a thousand Ravanas, प्रतिबलम् match in might, तु also, न भवेत् not be.
explanation: 'Not even a thousand Ravanas can stand my might  in combat as I start assailing them with thousands of  rocks or even trees.

shloka_text: अर्दयित्वा पुरीं लङ्कामभिवाद्य च मैथिलीम्। समृद्धार्थो गमिष्यामि मिषतां सर्वरक्षसाम्।।5.43.11।।
transliteration: ardayitvā purīṃ laṅkāmabhivādya ca maithilīm| samṛddhārtho gamiṣyāmi miṣatāṃ sarvarakṣasām
translation: सर्वरक्षसाम् of all ogres, मिषताम् they keep looking, लङ्कां पुरीम् city of Lanka, अर्थयित्वा destroying, मैथिलीम् Mythili, अभिवाद्य च offering obeisance, समृद्धार्थः having accomplished the task, गमिष्यामि return to.
explanation: 'I shall return only after accomplishing the destruction of the city of Lanka and offering obeisance to Sita, while all demons keep looking at me'.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा विमानस्थश्चैत्यस्थान्हरियूथपः। ननाद भीमनिर्ह्रादो रक्षसां जनयन्भयम्।।5.43.12।।
transliteration: evamuktvā vimānasthaścaityasthānhariyūthapaḥ| nanāda bhīmanirhrādo rakṣasāṃ janayanbhayam
translation: हरियूथपः monkey leader, विमानस्थः standing on the vimana, चैत्यस्थान् of the palace, एवम् that way, उक्त्वा having said, भीमनिर्ह्रादः making terrific sound, रक्षसाम् to the ogres, भयम् fear, जनयन् while creating, ननाद roared.
explanation: Having made proclamations that way from the top of the Vimana (palace) the monkey leader roared making terrific sound frightening the ogres.

shloka_text: तेन शब्देन महता चैत्यपालाश्शतं ययुः। गृहीत्वा विविधानस्त्रान्प्रासान्खङ्गान्परश्वथान्।।5.43.13।। विसृजन्तो महाकाया मारुतिं पर्यवारयन्।
transliteration: tena śabdena mahatā caityapālāśśataṃ yayuḥ| gṛhītvā vividhānastrānprāsānkhaṅgānparaśvathān visṛjanto mahākāyā mārutiṃ paryavārayan|
translation: महता with terrific, तेन शब्देन by that sound, शतम् hundred, चैत्यपालाः guards of the palace, विविधान् many, अस्त्रान् weapons, प्रासान् darts, खङ्गान् swords, परश्वथान् axes, गृहीत्वा after picking, ययुः marked, महाकायाः those of huge bodies, विसृजन्तः hurling, मारुतिम् Maruti, पर्यवारयन् surrounded.
explanation: Hearing the terrific sound, a hundred gigantic guards of the palace set forth, holding different kinds of weapons like darts, swords and axes and hurled at Maruti surrounding him.

shloka_text: ते गदाभिर्विचित्राभिः परिघैः काञ्चनाङ्गदैः। आजघ्नुर्वानरश्रेष्ठं बाणैश्चादित्यसन्निभैः।।5.43.14।।
transliteration: te gadābhirvicitrābhiḥ parighaiḥ kāñcanāṅgadaiḥ| ājaghnurvānaraśreṣṭhaṃ bāṇaiścādityasannibhaiḥ
translation: ते they, विचित्राभिः with astonishing, गदाभिः with maces, काञ्चनाङ्गदैः maces decorated with gold, परिघैः with crowbars, आदित्यसन्निभैः sharp like the Sun's rays, बाणैश्च with arrows, वानरश्रेष्ठम् foremost of vanaras, अजघ्नुः hit.
explanation: Holding astonishing maces decorated with gold, iron crowbars and sharp arrows resembling the rays of the Sun the ogres hit Hanuman, the foremost of vanaras.

shloka_text: आवर्त इव गङ्गायास्तोयस्य विपुलो महान्। परिक्षिप्य हरिश्रेष्ठं स बभौ रक्षसां गणः।।5.43.15।।
transliteration: āvarta iva gaṅgāyāstoyasya vipulo mahān| parikṣipya hariśreṣṭhaṃ sa babhau rakṣasāṃ gaṇaḥ
translation: सः that, रक्षसां गणः horde of ogres, हरिश्रेष्ठम् best of vanaras, परिक्षिप्य having surrounded, गङ्गायाः of the river Ganga, तोयस्य of the water, महान् huge, विपुलः big, आवर्त इव like a whirlpool, बभौ looked.
explanation: The demons surrounding the great monkey looked like a big whirlpool of the water of the river Ganga.

shloka_text: ततो वातात्मजः क्रुद्धो भीम रूपं समास्थितः।।5.43.16।। प्रासादस्य महन्तस्य स्तम्बं हेमपरिष्कृतम्। उत्पाटयित्वा वेगेन हनुमान्पवनात्मजः।।5.43.17।। ततस्तं भ्रामयामास शतधारं महाबलः।
transliteration: tato vātātmajaḥ kruddho bhīma rūpaṃ samāsthitaḥ prāsādasya mahantasya stambaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam| utpāṭayitvā vegena hanumānpavanātmajaḥ tatastaṃ bhrāmayāmāsa śatadhāraṃ mahābalaḥ|
translation: ततः then, वातात्मज son of the Windgod, क्रुद्धः infuriated, भीमम् fearsome, रूपम् form, समास्थितः assumed, महान् great, पवनात्मजः son of the Windgod, महाबलः mighty, हनुमान् Hanuman, तस्य प्रासादस्य of that palace, हेमपरिष्कृतम् decked with gold, स्तम्भं pillar, उत्पाटयित्वा uprooted, ततः then, शतधारम् holding a hundred edged, तम् that, वेगेन swiftly, भ्रामयामास whirled round.
explanation: Thereupon the infuriated son of the Windgod, assumed a fearsome form, uprooted a pillar of the palace decked with gold and holding that hundred edged pillar whirled it round swiftly.

shloka_text: ततो वातात्मजः क्रुद्धो भीम रूपं समास्थितः।।5.43.16।। प्रासादस्य महन्तस्य स्तम्बं हेमपरिष्कृतम्। उत्पाटयित्वा वेगेन हनुमान्पवनात्मजः।।5.43.17।। ततस्तं भ्रामयामास शतधारं महाबलः।
transliteration: tato vātātmajaḥ kruddho bhīma rūpaṃ samāsthitaḥ prāsādasya mahantasya stambaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam| utpāṭayitvā vegena hanumānpavanātmajaḥ tatastaṃ bhrāmayāmāsa śatadhāraṃ mahābalaḥ|
translation: ततः then, वातात्मज son of the Windgod, क्रुद्धः infuriated, भीमम् fearsome, रूपम् form, समास्थितः assumed, महान् great, पवनात्मजः son of the Windgod, महाबलः mighty, हनुमान् Hanuman, तस्य प्रासादस्य of that palace, हेमपरिष्कृतम् decked with gold, स्तम्भं pillar, उत्पाटयित्वा uprooted, ततः then, शतधारम् holding a hundred edged, तम् that, वेगेन swiftly, भ्रामयामास whirled round.
explanation: Thereupon the infuriated son of the Windgod, assumed a fearsome form, uprooted a pillar of the palace decked with gold and holding that hundred edged pillar whirled it round swiftly.

shloka_text: तत्र चाग्निस्समभवत्प्रासादश्चाप्यदह्यत।।5.43.18।। दह्यमानं ततो दृष्ट्वा प्रासादं हरियूथपः। स राक्षसशतं हत्त्वा वज्रेणेन्द्र इवासुरान्।।5.43.19।। अन्तरिक्षे स्थितश्श्तीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
transliteration: tatra cāgnissamabhavatprāsādaścāpyadahyata dahyamānaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā prāsādaṃ hariyūthapaḥ| sa rākṣasaśataṃ hattvā vajreṇendra ivāsurān antarikṣe sthitaśśtīmānidaṃ vacanamabravīt|
translation: तत्र thereafter, अग्नि: च and fire, समभवत् was created, प्रासादश्च the palace, अपि also, अदह्यत was burnt, ततः then, सः हरियूथपः Hanuman, दृष्ट्वा after seeing, इन्द्रः Indra, वज्रेण with a thunderbolt, असुरानिव like the ogres, राक्षसशतम् a hundred ogres, हत्त्वा having killed, श्रीमान् illustrous, अन्तरिक्षे in the aerial region, स्थितः stood, इदम् this, वचनम् word, अब्रवीत् proclaimed.
explanation: Thereafter fire was generated (through friction) and with if the palace blazed. Hanuman saw the palace burning. He killed a hundred demons there as Indra killed demons with his thunderbolt. (The whirling pillar that generated fire apeared like a thunderbolt) Later he stood in the air and proclaimed this:

shloka_text: तत्र चाग्निस्समभवत्प्रासादश्चाप्यदह्यत।।5.43.18।। दह्यमानं ततो दृष्ट्वा प्रासादं हरियूथपः। स राक्षसशतं हत्त्वा वज्रेणेन्द्र इवासुरान्।।5.43.19।। अन्तरिक्षे स्थितश्श्तीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।

explanation: Thereafter fire was generated (through friction) and with if the palace blazed. Hanuman saw the palace burning. He killed a hundred demons there as Indra killed demons with his thunderbolt. (The whirling pillar that generated fire apeared like a thunderbolt) Later he stood in the air and proclaimed this:

shloka_text: मादृशानां सहस्राणि विसृष्टानि महात्मनाम्।।5.43.20।। बलिनां वानरेन्द्राणां सुग्रीववशवर्तिनाम्। अटन्ति वसुधां कृत्स्नां वयमन्ये च वानराः।।5.43.21।।
transliteration: mādṛśānāṃ sahasrāṇi visṛṣṭāni mahātmanām balināṃ vānarendrāṇāṃ sugrīvavaśavartinām| aṭanti vasudhāṃ kṛtsnāṃ vayamanye ca vānarāḥ
translation: महात्मनाम् huge, बलिनाम् of mighty, सुग्रीववशवर्तिनाम् of those loyal to Sugriva, मादृशानाम् of people like me, वानरेन्द्राणाम् of the best of  vanara leaders, सहस्राणि in thousands, विसृष्टानि are despatched, वयम् we, अन्ये others, वानराश्च and vanaras, कृत्स्नाम् entire, वसुधाम् the earth, अटन्ति we are wandering.
explanation: "Thousands of huge and mighty monkeys, equal to me, loyal to king Sugriva, are coming under the orders and have been recruited from the entire earth. They  are the best among monkeys.

shloka_text: मादृशानां सहस्राणि विसृष्टानि महात्मनाम्।।5.43.20।। बलिनां वानरेन्द्राणां सुग्रीववशवर्तिनाम्। अटन्ति वसुधां कृत्स्नां वयमन्ये च वानराः।।5.43.21।।
transliteration: mādṛśānāṃ sahasrāṇi visṛṣṭāni mahātmanām balināṃ vānarendrāṇāṃ sugrīvavaśavartinām| aṭanti vasudhāṃ kṛtsnāṃ vayamanye ca vānarāḥ
translation: महात्मनाम् huge, बलिनाम् of mighty, सुग्रीववशवर्तिनाम् of those loyal to Sugriva, मादृशानाम् of people like me, वानरेन्द्राणाम् of the best of  vanara leaders, सहस्राणि in thousands, विसृष्टानि are despatched, वयम् we, अन्ये others, वानराश्च and vanaras, कृत्स्नाम् entire, वसुधाम् the earth, अटन्ति we are wandering.
explanation: "Thousands of huge and mighty monkeys, equal to me, loyal to king Sugriva, are coming under the orders and have been recruited from the entire earth. They  are the best among monkeys.

shloka_text: दशनागबलाः केचित्केचिद्दशगुणोत्तराः। केचिन्नागसहस्रस्य बभूवुस्तुल्यविक्रमाः।।5.43.22।।
transliteration: daśanāgabalāḥ kecitkeciddaśaguṇottarāḥ| kecinnāgasahasrasya babhūvustulyavikramāḥ
translation: केचित् some, दशनागबलाः have ten elephants strength, केचित् some, दशगुणोत्तराः ten hundred elephants strength, केचित् some, नागसहस्रस्य thousand elephants strength, तुल्यविक्रमाः equal in power, बभूवुः will be.
explanation: "Of them some have the strength equal to ten elephants, others are ten times stronger, and still others have a thousand elephants' strength.

shloka_text: सन्ति चौघबलाः केचित्केचिद्वायुबलोपमाः। अप्रमेयबलाश्चान्ये तत्रासन्हरियूथपाः।।5.43.23।।
transliteration: santi caughabalāḥ kecitkecidvāyubalopamāḥ| aprameyabalāścānye tatrāsanhariyūthapāḥ
translation: केचित् some, ओघबलाः strong as flood, सन्ति there are, केचित् some, वायुबलोपमाः have the power of wind, तत्र there, अन्ये others, हरियूथपाः leaders of monkeys, अप्रमेयबलाश्च of immeasureable strength, आसन् there are.
explanation: "Some have the strength of flood waters, some are powerful as wind and yet others have strength beyond measure.

shloka_text: ईदृग्विधैस्तु हरिभिर्वृतो दन्तनखायुधैः। शतैश्शतसहस्रैश्च कोटीभिरयुतैरपि।।5.43.24।। आगमिष्यति सुग्रीवः सर्वेषां वो निषूदनः।
transliteration: īdṛgvidhaistu haribhirvṛto dantanakhāyudhaiḥ| śataiśśatasahasraiśca koṭībhirayutairapi āgamiṣyati sugrīvaḥ sarveṣāṃ vo niṣūdanaḥ|
translation: ईद्दृग्विधैः endowed with such warriors, दन्त अपितु नखायुधै: by those using teeth and nails as weapons, शतैः in hundreds, अयुतैः in ayuta (ten thousand), शतसहस्रैः a hundred thousand, कोटीभिः in crores, हरिभिः with vanaras also, वृतः surrounded, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, सर्वेषाम् of all of them, वः you, निषूदनः killer, आगमिष्यति would come here.
explanation: "Sugriva will come here with hundreds of thousands of crores of vanaras who would be fighting with their teeth and nails as weapons.

shloka_text: नेयमस्ति पुरी लङ्का न यूयं न च रावणः।5.43.25।। यस्मादिक्ष्वाकुनाथेन बद्धं वैरं महात्मना।
transliteration: neyamasti purī laṅkā na yūyaṃ na ca rāvaṇaḥ|5.43.25|| yasmādikṣvākunāthena baddhaṃ vairaṃ mahātmanā|
translation: यस्मात् since, महात्मना with great self, इक्ष्वाकुनाथेन with the lord of Ikshvaku dynasty, वैरम् enmity, बद्धम् is bound, इयम् this, लङ्कापुरी city of Lanka, नास्ति will not be found, यूयम् even you, न not, रावणः च and Ravana, न also.
explanation: "You have established great enmity with the noble lord of Ikshvaku dynasty. Neither this Lanka will endure nor you, nor even Ravana will be traced. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortythird sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सन्दिष्टो राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रहस्तस्य सुतो बली। जम्बुमाली महादंष्ट्रो निर्जगाम धनुर्धरः।।5.44.1।। रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरस्स्रग्वी रुचिरकुण्डलः। महान्विवृत्तनयनश्चण्डस्समरदुर्जयः।।5.44.2।। धनुश्शक्रधनुः प्रख्यं महद्रुचिरसायकम्। विष्फारयाणो वेगेन वज्राशनिसमस्वनम्।।5.44.3।।
transliteration: sandiṣṭo rākṣasendreṇa prahastasya suto balī| jambumālī mahādaṃṣṭro nirjagāma dhanurdharaḥ raktamālyāmbaradharassragvī rucirakuṇḍalaḥ| mahānvivṛttanayanaścaṇḍassamaradurjayaḥ dhanuśśakradhanuḥ prakhyaṃ mahadrucirasāyakam| viṣphārayāṇo vegena vajrāśanisamasvanam
translation: महादंष्ट्रः one with big front teeth, धनुर्धरः bow in hand, रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरः adorned with a garland of red flowers and red clothes, स्रग्वी wearing a chaplet, रुचिरकुण्डलः with beautiful earrings, महान् great, विवृत्तनयनः who had big round eyes, चण्डः fierce, समरदुर्जयः  invincible in war, बली mighty, प्रहस्तस्य सुतः son of Prahasta,जम्बुमाली Jambumali,राक्षसेन्द्रेण by the demon king, सन्दिष्टः commanded, महत् huge, रुचिरसायकम् who had radiant arrows, वज्राशनिसमस्वनम् making sounds like thunderbolt, शक्रधनुःप्रख्यम् like Indra's splendid bow (a rainbow), धनुः bow, वेगेन very swiftly, विष्फारयाणः as if thundering, निर्जगाम went out.
explanation: Commanded  by the demon king, Jambumali the invincible son of Prahasta, who had large teeth in front, big rolling eyes, red flower garland, red robes and a chaplet with beautiful earrings. He went round twanging his producing thunderous sound. His arrows were huge, shining and beautiful.
comments: Killing of Jambumali by Hanuman

shloka_text: तस्य विष्फारघोषेण धनुषो महता दिशः। प्रदिशश्च नभश्चैव सहसा समपूर्यत।।5.44.4।।
transliteration: tasya viṣphāraghoṣeṇa dhanuṣo mahatā diśaḥ| pradiśaśca nabhaścaiva sahasā samapūryata
translation: तस्य his, धनुषः bow's, महता by the huge, विष्फारघोषेण by the twang, दिशः all directions, प्रदिशश्चैव and intermediate directions, नभश्चैव heavens also, सहसा at once, समपूर्यत were filled.
explanation: All directions including the intermediate directions and the sky were filled with that loud sound produced by his twang.

shloka_text: रथेन खरयुक्तेन तमागतमुदीक्ष्य सः। हनुमान्वेगसम्पन्नो जहर्ष च ननाद च।।5.44.5।।
transliteration: rathena kharayuktena tamāgatamudīkṣya saḥ| hanumānvegasampanno jaharṣa ca nanāda ca
translation: खरयुक्तेन drawn by donkeys, रथेन by the chariot, आगतम् reached, तम् him, उदीक्षय after seeing, सः हनुमान् that Hanuman, वेगसम्पन्नः who was endowed with speed, जहर्ष च felt glad, ननाद च and made a loud noise.
explanation: Seeing him coming in a chariot drawn by donkeys, Hanuman who was swift to act was glad (to have an opportunity to fight) and made a loud noise.

shloka_text: तं तोरणविटङ्कस्थं हनुमन्तं महाकपिम्। जम्बुमाली महाबाहुर्विव्याध निशितैश्शरैः।।5.44.6।।
transliteration: taṃ toraṇaviṭaṅkasthaṃ hanumantaṃ mahākapim| jambumālī mahābāhurvivyādha niśitaiśśaraiḥ
translation: महाबाहुः strongarmed one, जम्बुमाली Jambumali, तोरणविटङ्कस्थम् who stood on top of the exit archway, महाकपिम् great monkey, तं हनुमन्तम् that Hanuman, निशितैः with sharp, शरैः with arrows, विव्याध hit hard.
explanation: Strongarmed Jambumali with his sharp arrows hit great Hanuman who stood on top of the exit archway.

shloka_text: अर्धचन्द्रेण वदने शिरस्येकेन कर्णिना। बाह्वोर्विव्याध नाराचैर्दशभिस्तं कपीश्वरम्।।5.44.7।।
transliteration: ardhacandreṇa vadane śirasyekena karṇinā| bāhvorvivyādha nārācairdaśabhistaṃ kapīśvaram
translation: अर्धचन्द्रेण with a crescentshaped arrow, वदने on the face, एकेन with one, कर्णिना ear shaped arrow, शिरसि on the head, दशभिः ten, नाराचैः iron arrows, बाह्वोः into the arms, तं कपीश्वरम् that lord of monkeys, विव्याध hit.
explanation: Jambumali released a crescentshaped arrow on the face, one earshaped (barbed) arrow on the head and ten iron arrows into the arms of the lord of monkeys.

shloka_text: तस्य तच्छुशुभे ताम्रं शरेणाभिहतं मुखम्। शरदीवाम्बुजं फुल्लं विद्धं भास्कररश्मिना।।5.44.8।।
transliteration: tasya tacchuśubhe tāmraṃ śareṇābhihataṃ mukham| śaradīvāmbujaṃ phullaṃ viddhaṃ bhāskararaśminā
translation: शरेण by an arrow, अभिहतम् struck, ताम्रम् reddish, तत् his, मुखम् face, शरदि in autumn, भास्करश्मिना with Sun's radiance, विद्धम् hit, फुल्लम् blown, अम्बुजमिव like a lotus, शुशुभे appeared.
explanation: His red face struck by an arrow appeared like a fullblown lotus in autumn season hit  by  the rays of the Sun.

shloka_text: तत्तस्य रक्तं रक्तेन रञ्जितं शुशुभे मुखम्। यथाकाशे महापद्मं सिक्तं चन्दनबिन्दुभिः।।5.44.9।।
transliteration: tattasya raktaṃ raktena rañjitaṃ śuśubhe mukham| yathākāśe mahāpadmaṃ siktaṃ candanabindubhiḥ
translation: रक्तेन by blood, रञ्जितम् glowing, रक्तम् red, तस्य his, तत् that, मुखम् face, चन्दनबिन्दुभिः with sandal drops, सिक्तम् sprinkled, आकाशे in the sky, महापद्मं यथा like a great lotus, शुशुभे looked bright.
explanation: His red face  stained with blood was glowing bright like red lotus in the sky sprinkled with drops of red sandal.

shloka_text: चुकोप बाणाभिहतो राक्षसस्य महाकपिः। ततः पार्श्वेऽतिविपुलां ददर्श महतीं शिलाम्।।5.44.10।।
transliteration: cukopa bāṇābhihato rākṣasasya mahākapiḥ| tataḥ pārśve'tivipulāṃ dadarśa mahatīṃ śilām
translation: बाणाभिहतः struck by the shafts, महाकपिः great monkey, राक्षसस्य of the demon, चुकोप enraged, ततः then, पार्श्वे lying beside, अतिविपुलाम् huge, महतीम् on the ground, शिलाम् rock, ददर्श he saw.
explanation: Struck by the shafts of the ogre, the great monkey was enraged and happened to see a huge,  heavy rock lying beside him on the ground.

shloka_text: तरसा तां समुत्पाट्य चिक्षेप बलवद्भली। तां शरैर्दशभिः क्रुद्धस्ताडयामास राक्षसः।।5.44.11।।
transliteration: tarasā tāṃ samutpāṭya cikṣepa balavadbhalī| tāṃ śarairdaśabhiḥ kruddhastāḍayāmāsa rākṣasaḥ
translation: बली a powerful one, ताम् that boulder, तरसा with vehemence, समुत्पाट्य having lifted, बलवत् with his strength, चिक्षेप hurled, राक्षसः giant, क्रुद्धः angrily, ताम् that rock, दशभिः with ten, शरैः with arrows, ताडयामास smashed.
explanation: Powerful Hanuman with all vehemence lifted the rock and hurled it at the giant which he angrily smashed with ten arrows.

shloka_text: विपन्नं कर्म तद्दृष्ट्वा हनुमांश्चण्डविक्रमः। सालं विपुलमुत्पाट्य भ्रामयामास वीर्यवान्।।5.44.12।।
transliteration: vipannaṃ karma taddṛṣṭvā hanumāṃścaṇḍavikramaḥ| sālaṃ vipulamutpāṭya bhrāmayāmāsa vīryavān
translation: चण्डविक्रमः who had fierce power, वीर्यवान् a warrior, हनुमान् Hanuman, तत् that कर्म action, विपन्नम् failed, दृष्ट्वा seeing, विपुलम् huge, सालम् sala tree, उत्पाट्य pulled out, भ्रामयामास whirled.
explanation: Hanuman, a strong, powerful and fierce warrior pulled out a sala tree and whirled it. Seeing that his attempt has failed.

shloka_text: भ्रामयन्तं कपिं दृष्ट्वा सालवृक्षं महाबलम्। चिक्षेप सुबहून्बाणान्जम्बुमाली महाबलः।।5.44.13।।
transliteration: bhrāmayantaṃ kapiṃ dṛṣṭvā sālavṛkṣaṃ mahābalam| cikṣepa subahūnbāṇānjambumālī mahābalaḥ
translation: महाबलः mighty, जम्बुमाली Jambumali, सालवृक्षम् sala tree, भ्रामयन्तम् after whirling, महाबलम् mighty, कपिम् monkey, दृष्ट्वा after seeing, सुबहून् many, बाणान् arrows, चिक्षेप fired.
explanation: Gigantic Jambumali seeing the mighty Hanuman whirling the sala tree fired many arrows at him.

shloka_text: सालं चतुर्भिश्चिच्छेद वानरं पञ्चभिर्भुजे। उरस्येकेन बाणेन दशभिस्तु स्तनान्तरे।।5.44.14।।
transliteration: sālaṃ caturbhiściccheda vānaraṃ pañcabhirbhuje| urasyekena bāṇena daśabhistu stanāntare
translation: सालम् sala tree, चतुर्भिः with four, चिच्छेद cut off, वानरम् vanara, पञ्चभिः with five, भुजे on his arm, उरसि on his chest, एकेन बाणेन with one arrow, स्तनान्तरे in the hollow of the chest, दशभिः with ten.
explanation: He struck the sala tree with four arows, the arm of Hanuman with five arrows, chest with one, the hollow of the chest with ten more arrows.

shloka_text: स शरैः पूरिततनु: क्रोधेन महता वृतः। तमेव परिघं गृह्य भ्रामयामास वेगितः।।5.44.15।।
transliteration: sa śaraiḥ pūritatanu: krodhena mahatā vṛtaḥ| tameva parighaṃ gṛhya bhrāmayāmāsa vegitaḥ
translation: शरैः arrows, पूरिततनु: the body was filled, सः that, महता intense, क्रोधेन with anger, वृतः endowed, वेगितः speedily, तं परिघमेव the same iron spear, गृह्य seized, भ्रामयामास started whirling.
explanation: Hanuman filled with arrows all over his body, seized an iron spear (which he made use of in the initial battle) and impetuously spun it in  intense anger.

shloka_text: अतिवेगोऽतिवेगेन भ्रामयित्वा बलोत्कटः। परिघं पातयामास जम्बुमालेर्महोरसि।।5.44.16।।
transliteration: ativego'tivegena bhrāmayitvā balotkaṭaḥ| parighaṃ pātayāmāsa jambumālermahorasi
translation: बलोत्कटः of immeasurable strength, अतिवेगः a hero of great speed, परिघम् iron spear, अतिवेगेन with great speed, भ्रामयित्वा after turning round and round, जम्बुमालेः on Jambumali, महोरसि on the broad chest, पातयामास hurled.
explanation: Hanuman of immeasurable strength hurled the iron spear after turning it round and round at high speed on the broad chest of Jambumali.

shloka_text: तस्य चैव शिरो नास्ति न बाहू न च जानुनी। न धनुर्न रथो नाश्वास्तत्रादृश्यन्त नेषवः।।5.44.17।।
transliteration: tasya caiva śiro nāsti na bāhū na ca jānunī| na dhanurna ratho nāśvāstatrādṛśyanta neṣavaḥ
translation: तत्र there, तस्य his, शिरः चैव even head, नास्ति not there, बाहू shoulders, न not, जानुनी knees, न not, धनुः bow, न not, रथः chariot, न not, अश्वाः donkeys, horses, नादृश्यन्तः not there to discern, इषवः न nothing was seen.
explanation: Neither his head could be discerned nor his arms, knees, nor bow, chariot nor donkeys. Nothing was seen.

shloka_text: स हतस्सहसा तेन जम्बुमाली महाबलः। पपात निहतो भूमौ चूर्णिताङ्गविभूषणः।।5.44.18।।
transliteration: sa hatassahasā tena jambumālī mahābalaḥ| papāta nihato bhūmau cūrṇitāṅgavibhūṣaṇaḥ
translation: तेन by that blow, हतः killed, महाबलः mighty, जम्बुमाली Jambumali, सहसा inconsiderately, निहतः having been killed, चूर्णिताङ्गविभूषणः with his ornaments reduced to powder, भूमौ on the floor, पपात fell down.
explanation: Mighty Jambumali killed  by that blow dropped down dead at once with his ornaments reduced to powder.

shloka_text: जम्बुमालिं च निहतं किङ्करांश्च महाबलान्। चुक्रोध रावणश्शुत्वा कोपसंरक्तलोचनः।।5.44.19।।
transliteration: jambumāliṃ ca nihataṃ kiṅkarāṃśca mahābalān| cukrodha rāvaṇaśśutvā kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ
translation: रावणः Ravana, जम्बुमालिं च even Jambumali, निहतम् being klled, महाबलान् of great strength, किंकरांश्च and kinkaras also, श्रुत्वा hearing, कोपसंरक्तलोचनः bloodshot eyes, चुक्रोध got enraged.
explanation: Ravana's eyes became bloodshot in anger when he heard about the death of Jambumali and of the strong army of kinkaras.

shloka_text: स रोषसंवर्तितताम्रलोचनः प्रहस्तपुत्त्रे निहते महाबले। अमात्यपुत्त्रानतिवीर्यविक्रमान् समादिदेशाशु निशाचरेश्वरः।।5.44.20।।
transliteration: sa roṣasaṃvartitatāmralocanaḥ prahastaputtre nihate mahābale| amātyaputtrānativīryavikramān samādideśāśu niśācareśvaraḥ
translation: महाबले who had great strength, प्रहस्तपुत्त्रे Prahasta's son, निहते killed, सः निशाचरेश्वरः demon king, रोषसंवर्तितताम्रलोचनः his eyes red and rolling in anger, आशु quickly, अतिवीर्यविक्रमान् highly valiant wariors, अमात्यपुत्रान् sons of ministers, समादिदेश commanded.
explanation: When the mighty son of Prahasta was killed, infuriated Ravana, his eyes red and rolling, commanded the highly valiant sons of ministers. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyfourth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततस्ते राक्षसेन्द्रेण चोदिता मन्त्रिणस्सुताः। निर्ययुर्भवनात्तस्मात्सप्तसप्तार्चिवर्चसः।।5.45.1।। महाबलपरीवारा धनुष्मन्तो महाबलाः। कृतास्त्रास्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठाः परस्परजयैषिणः।।5.45.2।। हेमजालपरिक्षिप्तैर्ध्वजवद्भिः पताकिभिः। तोयदस्वननिर्घोषैर्वाजियुक्तैर्महारथैः।।5.45.3।। तप्तकाञ्चनचित्राणि चापान्यमितविक्रमाः। विस्फारयन्तस्संहृष्टास्तटित्वन्त इवाम्बुदाः।।5.45.4।।
transliteration: tataste rākṣasendreṇa coditā mantriṇassutāḥ| niryayurbhavanāttasmātsaptasaptārcivarcasaḥ mahābalaparīvārā dhanuṣmanto mahābalāḥ| kṛtāstrāstravidāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ parasparajayaiṣiṇaḥ hemajālaparikṣiptairdhvajavadbhiḥ patākibhiḥ| toyadasvananirghoṣairvājiyuktairmahārathaiḥ taptakāñcanacitrāṇi cāpānyamitavikramāḥ| visphārayantassaṃhṛṣṭāstaṭitvanta ivāmbudāḥ
translation: ततः then, सप्तार्चिवर्चसः energetic like fire, महाबलपरीवाराः endowed with great army, धनुष्मन्तः experts in archery, महाबलाः mighty, कृतास्त्राः अस्त्रविदाम् distinguished wielders of weapons, श्रेष्ठाः foremost, परस्परजयैषिणः wished to conquer each other, अमितविक्रमाः very valiant, सप्त seven, ते they, मन्त्रिणः ministers, सुताः sons, राक्षसेन्द्रेण by the lord of ogres, चोदिताः directed, संहृष्टाः gladly, तप्तकाञ्चनचित्राणि decked with shining gold, चापानि bows, विष्फारयन्तः by sporting, तटित्वन्तः shining with lightning, अम्बुदाः इव like storm clouds, हेमजलपरिक्षिप्तैः decked with golden mesh, ध्वजवद्भिः bearing staffs, पताकिभिः with flags,तोयदस्वननिर्घोषैः making sounds like stormy clouds, वाजियुक्तै: yoked to horses,महारथैः with great chariots, तस्मात् from that, भवनात् from the palace, निर्ययुः departed.
explanation: Commanded by Ravana, the seven sons of minister blazing like fire followed by large army of experts in archery, possessing great valour, armed with weapons, being distinguished wielders of weapons, skilled in the use of weapons, who were equally capable of conquering each other sallied forth gladly to fight with Hanuman. They drove chariots yoked with horses which were decked with golden mesh, holding totem staffs (a figure engraved to identify a hero) and flags, neighing like clouds. The valiant heroes were sporting and making sounds like stormy  clouds wielding wonderful bows glittering like molten gold, shining like lightning. As they marched from the palace they looked like  stormy clouds accompanied by lightning.
comments: Hanuman kills the seven sons of Ravana's chief minister

shloka_text: ततस्ते राक्षसेन्द्रेण चोदिता मन्त्रिणस्सुताः। निर्ययुर्भवनात्तस्मात्सप्तसप्तार्चिवर्चसः।।5.45.1।। महाबलपरीवारा धनुष्मन्तो महाबलाः। कृतास्त्रास्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठाः परस्परजयैषिणः।।5.45.2।। हेमजालपरिक्षिप्तैर्ध्वजवद्भिः पताकिभिः। तोयदस्वननिर्घोषैर्वाजियुक्तैर्महारथैः।।5.45.3।। तप्तकाञ्चनचित्राणि चापान्यमितविक्रमाः। विस्फारयन्तस्संहृष्टास्तटित्वन्त इवाम्बुदाः।।5.45.4।।

translation: ततः then, सप्तार्चिवर्चसः energetic like fire, महाबलपरीवाराः endowed with great army, धनुष्मन्तः experts in archery, महाबलाः mighty, कृतास्त्राः अस्त्रविदाम् distinguished wielders of weapons, श्रेष्ठाः foremost, परस्परजयैषिणः wished to conquer each other, अमितविक्रमाः very valiant, सप्त seven, ते they, मन्त्रिणः ministers, सुताः sons, राक्षसेन्द्रेण by the lord of ogres, चोदिताः directed, संहृष्टाः gladly, तप्तकाञ्चनचित्राणि decked with shining gold, चापानि bows, विष्फारयन्तः by sporting, तटित्वन्तः shining with lightning, अम्बुदाः इव like storm clouds, हेमजलपरिक्षिप्तैः decked with golden mesh, ध्वजवद्भिः bearing staffs, पताकिभिः with flags,तोयदस्वननिर्घोषैः making sounds like stormy clouds, वाजियुक्तै: yoked to horses,महारथैः with great chariots, तस्मात् from that, भवनात् from the palace, निर्ययुः departed.

They drove chariots yoked with horses which were decked with golden mesh, holding totem staffs (a figure engraved to identify a hero) and flags, neighing like clouds. The valiant heroes were sporting and making sounds like stormy  clouds wielding wonderful bows glittering like molten gold, shining like lightning. As they marched from the palace they looked like  stormy clouds accompanied by lightning.
comments: Hanuman kills the seven sons of Ravana's chief minister

shloka_text: ततस्ते राक्षसेन्द्रेण चोदिता मन्त्रिणस्सुताः। निर्ययुर्भवनात्तस्मात्सप्तसप्तार्चिवर्चसः।।5.45.1।। महाबलपरीवारा धनुष्मन्तो महाबलाः। कृतास्त्रास्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठाः परस्परजयैषिणः।।5.45.2।। हेमजालपरिक्षिप्तैर्ध्वजवद्भिः पताकिभिः। तोयदस्वननिर्घोषैर्वाजियुक्तैर्महारथैः।।5.45.3।। तप्तकाञ्चनचित्राणि चापान्यमितविक्रमाः। विस्फारयन्तस्संहृष्टास्तटित्वन्त इवाम्बुदाः।।5.45.4।।
transliteration: tataste rākṣasendreṇa coditā mantriṇassutāḥ| niryayurbhavanāttasmātsaptasaptārcivarcasaḥ mahābalaparīvārā dhanuṣmanto mahābalāḥ| kṛtāstrāstravidāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ parasparajayaiṣiṇaḥ hemajālaparikṣiptairdhvajavadbhiḥ patākibhiḥ| toyadasvananirghoṣairvājiyuktairmahārathaiḥ taptakāñcanacitrāṇi cāpānyamitavikramāḥ| visphārayantassaṃhṛṣṭāstaṭitvanta ivāmbudāḥ
translation: ततः then, सप्तार्चिवर्चसः energetic like fire, महाबलपरीवाराः endowed with great army, धनुष्मन्तः experts in archery, महाबलाः mighty, कृतास्त्राः अस्त्रविदाम् distinguished wielders of weapons, श्रेष्ठाः foremost, परस्परजयैषिणः wished to conquer each other, अमितविक्रमाः very valiant, सप्त seven, ते they, मन्त्रिणः ministers, सुताः sons, राक्षसेन्द्रेण by the lord of ogres, चोदिताः directed, संहृष्टाः gladly, तप्तकाञ्चनचित्राणि decked with shining gold, चापानि bows, विष्फारयन्तः by sporting, तटित्वन्तः shining with lightning, अम्बुदाः इव like storm clouds, हेमजलपरिक्षिप्तैः decked with golden mesh, ध्वजवद्भिः bearing staffs, पताकिभिः with flags,तोयदस्वननिर्घोषैः making sounds like stormy clouds, वाजियुक्तै: yoked to horses,महारथैः with great chariots, तस्मात् from that, भवनात् from the palace, निर्ययुः departed.
explanation: Commanded by Ravana, the seven sons of minister blazing like fire followed by large army of experts in archery, possessing great valour, armed with weapons, being distinguished wielders of weapons, skilled in the use of weapons, who were equally capable of conquering each other sallied forth gladly to fight with Hanuman. They drove chariots yoked with horses which were decked with golden mesh, holding totem staffs (a figure engraved to identify a hero) and flags, neighing like clouds. The valiant heroes were sporting and making sounds like stormy  clouds wielding wonderful bows glittering like molten gold, shining like lightning. As they marched from the palace they looked like  stormy clouds accompanied by lightning.
comments: Hanuman kills the seven sons of Ravana's chief minister

shloka_text: ततस्ते राक्षसेन्द्रेण चोदिता मन्त्रिणस्सुताः। निर्ययुर्भवनात्तस्मात्सप्तसप्तार्चिवर्चसः।।5.45.1।। महाबलपरीवारा धनुष्मन्तो महाबलाः। कृतास्त्रास्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठाः परस्परजयैषिणः।।5.45.2।। हेमजालपरिक्षिप्तैर्ध्वजवद्भिः पताकिभिः। तोयदस्वननिर्घोषैर्वाजियुक्तैर्महारथैः।।5.45.3।। तप्तकाञ्चनचित्राणि चापान्यमितविक्रमाः। विस्फारयन्तस्संहृष्टास्तटित्वन्त इवाम्बुदाः।।5.45.4।।
transliteration: tataste rākṣasendreṇa coditā mantriṇassutāḥ| niryayurbhavanāttasmātsaptasaptārcivarcasaḥ mahābalaparīvārā dhanuṣmanto mahābalāḥ| kṛtāstrāstravidāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ parasparajayaiṣiṇaḥ hemajālaparikṣiptairdhvajavadbhiḥ patākibhiḥ| toyadasvananirghoṣairvājiyuktairmahārathaiḥ taptakāñcanacitrāṇi cāpānyamitavikramāḥ| visphārayantassaṃhṛṣṭāstaṭitvanta ivāmbudāḥ
translation: ततः then, सप्तार्चिवर्चसः energetic like fire, महाबलपरीवाराः endowed with great army, धनुष्मन्तः experts in archery, महाबलाः mighty, कृतास्त्राः अस्त्रविदाम् distinguished wielders of weapons, श्रेष्ठाः foremost, परस्परजयैषिणः wished to conquer each other, अमितविक्रमाः very valiant, सप्त seven, ते they, मन्त्रिणः ministers, सुताः sons, राक्षसेन्द्रेण by the lord of ogres, चोदिताः directed, संहृष्टाः gladly, तप्तकाञ्चनचित्राणि decked with shining gold, चापानि bows, विष्फारयन्तः by sporting, तटित्वन्तः shining with lightning, अम्बुदाः इव like storm clouds, हेमजलपरिक्षिप्तैः decked with golden mesh, ध्वजवद्भिः bearing staffs, पताकिभिः with flags,तोयदस्वननिर्घोषैः making sounds like stormy clouds, वाजियुक्तै: yoked to horses,महारथैः with great chariots, तस्मात् from that, भवनात् from the palace, निर्ययुः departed.
explanation: Commanded by Ravana, the seven sons of minister blazing like fire followed by large army of experts in archery, possessing great valour, armed with weapons, being distinguished wielders of weapons, skilled in the use of weapons, who were equally capable of conquering each other sallied forth gladly to fight with Hanuman. They drove chariots yoked with horses which were decked with golden mesh, holding totem staffs (a figure engraved to identify a hero) and flags, neighing like clouds. The valiant heroes were sporting and making sounds like stormy  clouds wielding wonderful bows glittering like molten gold, shining like lightning. As they marched from the palace they looked like  stormy clouds accompanied by lightning.
comments: Hanuman kills the seven sons of Ravana's chief minister

shloka_text: जनन्यस्तु ततस्तेषां विदित्वा किङ्करान्हतान्। बभूवुश्शोकसम्भ्रान्तास्सबान्धवसुहृज्जनाः।।5.45.5।।
transliteration: jananyastu tatasteṣāṃ viditvā kiṅkarānhatān| babhūvuśśokasambhrāntāssabāndhavasuhṛjjanāḥ
translation: ततः then, तेषाम् their, सबान्धवसुहृज्जनाः with friends and relatives, जनन्यस्तु mothers, किंकरान् kinkaras, हतान् killed, विदित्वा having known, कसम्भ्रान्ताः were agitated with grief, बभूवुः became.
explanation: Their mothers and relatives and their friends were struck with grief when they learnt about the kinkaras killed.

shloka_text: ते परस्परसङ्घर्षात्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाः। अभिपेतुर्हनूमन्तं तोरणस्थमवस्थितम्।।5.45.6।।
transliteration: te parasparasaṅgharṣāttaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ| abhipeturhanūmantaṃ toraṇasthamavasthitam
translation: तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाः barnished ornaments of gold, ते they, परस्परसङ्घर्षात् by dashing against each other, तोरणस्थम् at the main archway, अवस्थितम् stood, हनूमन्तम् Hanuman, अभिपेतुः attacked.
explanation: The barnished golden ornaments worn by them were shining as they brushed shoulders with one another (eager to fight first) to attack Hanuman who stood waiting at the main archway.

shloka_text: सृजन्तो बाणवृष्टिं ते रथगर्जितनिस्स्वनाः। वृष्टिमन्त इवांभोदा विचेरुर्नैऋताम्बुदाः।।5.45.7।।
transliteration: sṛjanto bāṇavṛṣṭiṃ te rathagarjitanissvanāḥ| vṛṣṭimanta ivāṃbhodā vicerurnaiṛtāmbudāḥ
translation: रथगर्जितनिस्वनाः the rattling of the chariots mixed with the roaring of the warriors, ते they, नैऋताम्बुदाः the clouds of demons, बाणवृष्टिम् torrent of arrows, सृजन्तः sent forth, वृष्टिमन्तः thundering, अम्भोदाः इव like the storm clouds, विचेरुः went about.
explanation: They went roaring with their chariots rattling, sending forth torrents of arrows like the stormy clouds thundering.

shloka_text: अवकीर्णस्ततस्ताभिर्हनुमान्शरवृष्टिभिः। अभवत्संवृताकारश्शैलराडिव वृष्टिभिः।।5.45.8।।
transliteration: avakīrṇastatastābhirhanumānśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ| abhavatsaṃvṛtākāraśśailarāḍiva vṛṣṭibhiḥ
translation: ततः then, ताभिः by them, शरवृष्टिभिः by the shower of arrows, अवकीर्णः scattered all over, हनुमान् Hanuman, वृष्टिभिः with shower of rain, संवृताकारः covered, शैलराडिव like the king of mountains, अभवत् appeared.
explanation: Later, Hanuman covered with showers of arrows scattered all over appeared like the king of mountains shot with showers of rain.

shloka_text: स शरान्मोघयामास तेषामाशुचरः कपिः। रथवेगं च वीराणां विचरन्विमलेऽम्बरे।।5.45.9।।
transliteration: sa śarānmoghayāmāsa teṣāmāśucaraḥ kapiḥ| rathavegaṃ ca vīrāṇāṃ vicaranvimale'mbare
translation: आशुचरः moving fast, सः कपिः that monkey, विमले in the clear, अम्बरे  sky, विचरन् moving, तेषां वीराणाम् of the heroes, शरान् by the arrows, रथवेगं च and the speed of their chariot, मोघयामास rendered futile.
explanation: Then the monkey moving fast in the clear sky rendered the arrows of the giant heroes and speeding chariots futile.

shloka_text: स तैः क्रीडन्धनुष्मद्भिर्व्योम्नि वीरः प्रकाशते। धनुष्मद्भिर्यथा मेघैर्मारुतः प्रभुरम्बरे।।5.45.10।।
transliteration: sa taiḥ krīḍandhanuṣmadbhirvyomni vīraḥ prakāśate| dhanuṣmadbhiryathā meghairmārutaḥ prabhurambare
translation: व्योम्नि in the sky, धनुष्मद्भिः with those bows in their hands, तैः by them, क्रीडन् while sporting, सः वीरः that hero, अम्बरे in the sky, धनुष्मद्भिः armed with rainbow, मेघैः by the clouds, प्रभुः god, मारुतः यथा like the wind, प्रकाशते shining.
explanation: Sporting in the sky with the giants who held bows in their hands, Hanuman shone like the powerful Windgod sporting in the sky surrrounded by rambling dark clouds.

shloka_text: स कृत्वा निनदं घोरं त्रासयंस्तां महाचमूम्। चकार हनुमान्वेगं तेषु रक्षस्सु वीर्यवान्।।5.45.11।।
transliteration: sa kṛtvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ trāsayaṃstāṃ mahācamūm| cakāra hanumānvegaṃ teṣu rakṣassu vīryavān
translation: वीर्यवान् valiant one, सः he, घोरम् terrific, निनदम् sound, कृत्वा making, ताम् that, महाचमूम् great army, त्रासयन् frightening, तेषु रक्षस्सु those ogres, वेगम् speed, चकार created.
explanation: Valiant Hanuman making terrific sound and frightening the army of ogres marched swiftly.

shloka_text: तलेनाभ्यहनत्कांश्चित्पादैः कांश्चित्परन्तपः। मुष्टिनाभ्यहनत्कांश्चिन्नखैः कांश्चिद्व्यदारयत्।।5.45.12।।
transliteration: talenābhyahanatkāṃścitpādaiḥ kāṃścitparantapaḥ| muṣṭinābhyahanatkāṃścinnakhaiḥ kāṃścidvyadārayat
translation: परन्तपः scorcher of enemies, कांश्चित् some, तलेन with palm, अभ्यहनत् hit, कांश्चित् some, पादैः with feet, कांश्चित् some, मुष्टिना with fist, अभ्यहनत् struck, कांश्चित् some, नखैः with nails, व्यदारयत् pierced .
explanation: The scorcher of enemies, Hanuman hit some ogres with his palm, some with his feet and some with his fist and pierced some with his nails.

shloka_text: प्रममाथोरसा कांश्चिदूरुभ्यामपरान्कपिः। केचित्तस्य निनादेन तत्रैव पतिता भुवि।।5.45.13।।
transliteration: pramamāthorasā kāṃścidūrubhyāmaparānkapiḥ| kecittasya ninādena tatraiva patitā bhuvi
translation: कपिः monkey, कांश्चित् some, उरसा with his chest, अपरान् and others, ऊरुभ्याम् with his thighs, प्रममाथ strangled, केचित् a few, तस्य his, निनादेन by the roar, तत्रैव there itself, भुवि on the ground, पतिताः fell down.
explanation: The monkey strangled some with his chest and some between his thighs. A few fell down dead on the ground hearing his roaring noise.

shloka_text: ततस्तेष्ववसन्नेषु भूमौ निपतितेषु च। तत्सैन्यमगमत्सर्वं दिशोदश भयार्दितम्।।5.45.14।।
transliteration: tatasteṣvavasanneṣu bhūmau nipatiteṣu ca| tatsainyamagamatsarvaṃ diśodaśa bhayārditam
translation: तेषु when they (sons of minister), अवसन्नेषु were annexed, भूमौ on the ground, निपतितेषु च when fallen dead on the ground, ततः then, सर्वम् all, तत् that, सैन्यम् army, भयार्दितम् struck with fear, दश दिशः in all ten directions, अगमत् fled.
explanation: Struck by fear on seeing Hanuman, the seven sons of ministers dropped down dead on the ground, and their army fled in all the ten directions.

shloka_text: विनेदुर्विस्वरं नागा निपेतुर्भुवि वाजिनः। भग्ननीडध्वजच्छत्रैर्भूश्च कीर्णाऽभवद्रथैः।।5.45.15।।
transliteration: vinedurvisvaraṃ nāgā nipeturbhuvi vājinaḥ| bhagnanīḍadhvajacchatrairbhūśca kīrṇā'bhavadrathaiḥ
translation: नागाः elephants, विस्वरम् discordantly, विनेदुः trumpeted in fear, वाजिनः horses, भुवि on ground, निपेतुः fell down, भूश्च the earth also, भग्ननीडध्वजच्छत्रैः with broken seats, parasols, flag staffs, रथैः by chariots, कीर्णा अभवत् strewn all over.
explanation: The elephants trumpeted discordantly out of fear, the horses fell down on the ground and even the chariots with seats, parasols and flag staffs broken were strewn all over the ground.

shloka_text: स्रवता रुधिरेणाथ स्रवन्त्यो दर्शिताः पथि। विविधैश्च स्वरैर्लङ्का ननाद विकृतं तदा।।5.45.16।।
transliteration: sravatā rudhireṇātha sravantyo darśitāḥ pathi| vividhaiśca svarairlaṅkā nanāda vikṛtaṃ tadā
translation: अथ then, स्रवता flowing, रुधिरेण by blood, पथि way, स्रवन्त्यः flowed, दर्शिताः seen, तदा then, लङ्का Lanka, विविधैः with many, स्वरैः with sounds, विकृतम् horrifying cries, ननाद roared.
explanation: Streams of blood flowed and Lanka was filled with many kinds of horrifying sounds of cries.

shloka_text: स तान्प्रवृद्धान्विनिहत्य राक्षसान् महाबलश्चण्डपराक्रमः कपिः। युयुत्सुरन्यैः पुनरेव राक्षसै स्तमेव वीरोऽभिजगाम तोरणम्।।5.45.17।।
transliteration: sa tānpravṛddhānvinihatya rākṣasān mahābalaścaṇḍaparākramaḥ kapiḥ| yuyutsuranyaiḥ punareva rākṣasai stameva vīro'bhijagāma toraṇam
translation: वीरः hero, महाबलः mighty one, चण्डपराक्रमः whose valiance was fierce, सः कपिः that Hanuman, प्रवृद्धान् the ogres who were old and grew stronger, तान् राक्षसान् those gaints, विनिहृत्य slayed, अन्यैः others, राक्षसैः by ogres, युयुत्सुः desiring to wage war, पुनरेव once again, तम् that, तोरणमेव archway, अभिजगाम went forth.
explanation: Having killed the ogres who were old and strong, the valiant and mighty Hanuman, wishing to slay the other ogres advanced towards the archway. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyfifth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: हतान्मन्त्रिसुतान् बुद्ध्वा वानरेण महात्मना। रावणस्संवृताकारश्चकार मतिमुत्तमाम्।।5.46.1।।
transliteration: hatānmantrisutān buddhvā vānareṇa mahātmanā| rāvaṇassaṃvṛtākāraścakāra matimuttamām
translation: रावणः Ravana, महात्मना the great, वानरेण by the vanara, मन्त्रिसुतान् sons of the ministers, हतान् killed, बुद्द्वा knowing, संवृताकारः who had concealed his agony, उत्तमाम् good, मतिम् thought, चकार formulated.
explanation: Coming to know that the seven sons of the ministers were slain by the great vanara,  Ravana, who had concealed his feelings of agony thought of a good plan.
comments: Five Generals of Ravana done to death by Hanuman in war

shloka_text: स विरूपाक्षयूपाक्षौ दुर्धरं चैव राक्षसम्। प्रघसं भासकर्णं च पञ्चसेनाग्रनायकान्।।5.46.2।। सन्दिदेश दशग्रीवो वीरान्नयविशारदान्। हनुमद्ग्रहणव्यग्रान्वायुवेगसमान्युधि।।5.46.3।।
transliteration: sa virūpākṣayūpākṣau durdharaṃ caiva rākṣasam| praghasaṃ bhāsakarṇaṃ ca pañcasenāgranāyakān sandideśa daśagrīvo vīrānnayaviśāradān| hanumadgrahaṇavyagrānvāyuvegasamānyudhi
translation: सः दशग्रीवः the tenheaded Ravana, वीरान् warriors, नयविशारदान् skilled in statecraft, हनुमद्ग्रहणव्यग्रान् eager to capture Hanuman, युथि in battle, वायुवेगसमान् equal to wind in speed, विरूपाक्षयूपाक्षौ Virupaksha and Yupaksha, दुर्धरम् Durdhara, राक्षसं चैव also a giant, प्रघसम् Praghasa, भासकर्णं च Bhaskarna and, सेनाग्रनायकान् army Generals पञ्च five,सन्दिदेश commanded.
explanation: The tenheaded Ravana, eager to capture Hanuman, commanded his five army Generals called Virupaksha, Yupaksha, Durdhara, Praghasa and Bhaskarna, who were great warriorstatesmen valiant and, equal to wind in speed.

shloka_text: स विरूपाक्षयूपाक्षौ दुर्धरं चैव राक्षसम्। प्रघसं भासकर्णं च पञ्चसेनाग्रनायकान्।।5.46.2।। सन्दिदेश दशग्रीवो वीरान्नयविशारदान्। हनुमद्ग्रहणव्यग्रान्वायुवेगसमान्युधि।।5.46.3।।

explanation: The tenheaded Ravana, eager to capture Hanuman, commanded his five army Generals called Virupaksha, Yupaksha, Durdhara, Praghasa and Bhaskarna, who were great warriorstatesmen valiant and, equal to wind in speed.

shloka_text: यात सेनाग्रगास्सर्वे महाबलपरिग्रहाः। सवाजिरथमातङ्गास्स कपिश्शास्यतामिति।।5.46.4।।
transliteration: yāta senāgragāssarve mahābalaparigrahāḥ| savājirathamātaṅgāssa kapiśśāsyatāmiti
translation: सेनाग्रगाः O Army generals, सर्वे all, महाबलपरिग्रहाः accompanied by large, strong army, सवाजिरथमातङ्गाः along with horses, chariots and elphants, यात march, सः कपिः that vanara, शास्यताम्  punish, इति thus.
explanation: "O Army generals march with a large, strong army with horses, chariots and elephants and punish the vanara.

shloka_text: यत्नैश्च खलु भाव्यं स्यात्तमासाद्य वनालयम्। कर्म चापि समाधेयं देशकालाविरोधिनम्।।5.46.5।।
transliteration: yatnaiśca khalu bhāvyaṃ syāttamāsādya vanālayam| karma cāpi samādheyaṃ deśakālāvirodhinam
translation: तम् him, वनालयम् a forestdweller, आसाद्य after reaching, यत्नैः च with all efforts, भाव्यम् should be engaged, देशकालाविरोधिनम् that which is not against time and space, कर्म चापि even action, समाधेयम् should be done.
explanation: "Go to that forestdweller and make all efforts to impose on him punishment appropriate to time and place (keeping in view the harm he has done).

shloka_text: न ह्यहं तं कपिं मन्ये कर्मणा प्रतितर्कयन्। सर्वथा तन्महद्भूतं महाबलपरिग्रहम्।।5.46.6।।
transliteration: na hyahaṃ taṃ kapiṃ manye karmaṇā pratitarkayan| sarvathā tanmahadbhūtaṃ mahābalaparigraham
translation: अहम् I, कर्मणा by his actions, प्रतितर्कयन् judging again and again,तम् him, कपिम् monkey, न मन्ये I do not think, सर्वथा by all its actions, तत् that, महाबलपरिग्रहम् endowed with great strength, महत् great, भूतम् a being.
explanation: "Judging again and again from all actions, I do not think he is an ordinary monkey. He is a being endowed with great strength.

shloka_text: भवेदिन्द्रेण वा सृष्टमस्मदर्थं तपोबलात्। सनागयक्षगन्धर्वा देवासुरमहर्षयः।।5.46.7।। युष्माभिस्सहितैस्सर्वैर्मया सह विनिर्जिताः। तैरवश्यं विधातव्यं व्यलीकं किञ्चिदेव नः।।5.46.8।। तदेव नात्र सन्देहः प्रसह्य परिगृह्यताम्। नावमान्यो भवद्भिश्च हरिर्धीरपराक्रमः।।5.46.9।।
transliteration: bhavedindreṇa vā sṛṣṭamasmadarthaṃ tapobalāt| sanāgayakṣagandharvā devāsuramaharṣayaḥ yuṣmābhissahitaissarvairmayā saha vinirjitāḥ| tairavaśyaṃ vidhātavyaṃ vyalīkaṃ kiñcideva naḥ tadeva nātra sandehaḥ prasahya parigṛhyatām| nāvamānyo bhavadbhiśca harirdhīraparākramaḥ
translation: अस्मदर्धम् it seems to me, तपोबलात् by ascetic power, इन्द्रेण by Indra, सृष्टं वा may be created, भवेत् may be, सहितैः along with, सर्वैः by all, युष्माभिः of you, मया by me, सनागयक्षगन्धर्वाः nagas, yakshas, gandharvas,देवासुरमहर्षयः gods, demons and ascetics, विनिर्जिताः subdued, तैः by them, नः us, किञ्चिदेव even a little, व्यलीकम् harm, अवश्यम् certainly, विधातव्यम् should be done, तदेव this is same reaction, अत्र in this case, सन्देहः doubt, न no, प्रसह्य with force, परिगृह्यताम् he may be captured, धीरपराक्रमः a warrior of heroic strength, हरिः monkey, भवद्भि by you also, नावमान्यः should not be insulted.
explanation: "To me it appears he is created by Indra with his ascetic power (for punishing us). I have subdued nagas, yakshas, gandharvas and even gods, asuras and ascetics with your help. So you should certainly bring him here without doing any harm. Capture the monkey forcibly. Do not insult that mighty monkey.

So you should certainly bring him here without doing any harm. Capture the monkey forcibly. Do not insult that mighty monkey.

So you should certainly bring him here without doing any harm. Capture the monkey forcibly. Do not insult that mighty monkey.

shloka_text: दृष्टा हि हरयः पूर्वं मया विपुलविक्रमाः। वाली च सहसुग्रीवो जाम्बवांश्च महाबलः।।5.46.10।। नीलस्सेनापतिश्चैव ये चान्ये द्विविदादयः। नैवं तेषां गतिर्भीमा न तेजो न पराक्रमः।।5.46.11।। न मतिर्न बलोत्साहौ न रूपपरिकल्पनम्।
transliteration: dṛṣṭā hi harayaḥ pūrvaṃ mayā vipulavikramāḥ| vālī ca sahasugrīvo jāmbavāṃśca mahābalaḥ nīlassenāpatiścaiva ye cānye dvividādayaḥ| naivaṃ teṣāṃ gatirbhīmā na tejo na parākramaḥ na matirna balotsāhau na rūpaparikalpanam|
translation: पूर्वम् earlier, मया by me, विपुलविक्रमाः of immense prowess, हरयः monkeys, सहसुग्रीवः with Sugriva, वाली च and Vali, महाबलः mighty, जाम्बवांश्च and Jambavan, सेनापतिः army chief, नीलः Nila, द्विविदादयः Dvivida and others, अन्ये च and others, ये those, दृष्टाः हि have seen, तेषाम् for them, गतिः movement, एवम् that way, भीमा tremendous, न not, तेजः splendour, पराक्रमः valour, न not, मतिः intellect, न not, बलोत्साहौ strength and energy, रूपपरिकल्पनम् ability to change form at will.
explanation: "Earlier I have seen monkeys of immense prowess, like Vali and Sugriva as well as Jambavan, the bear. Also I have seen the army general, Nila, Dvivida and others. They do not have such tremendous splendour or movement valour, intellect and strength and energy. They did not have such ability to change form at their will.

shloka_text: दृष्टा हि हरयः पूर्वं मया विपुलविक्रमाः। वाली च सहसुग्रीवो जाम्बवांश्च महाबलः।।5.46.10।। नीलस्सेनापतिश्चैव ये चान्ये द्विविदादयः। नैवं तेषां गतिर्भीमा न तेजो न पराक्रमः।।5.46.11।। न मतिर्न बलोत्साहौ न रूपपरिकल्पनम्।

translation: पूर्वम् earlier, मया by me, विपुलविक्रमाः of immense prowess, हरयः monkeys, सहसुग्रीवः with Sugriva, वाली च and Vali, महाबलः mighty, जाम्बवांश्च and Jambavan, सेनापतिः army chief, नीलः Nila, द्विविदादयः Dvivida and others, अन्ये च and others, ये those, दृष्टाः हि have seen, तेषाम् for them, गतिः movement, एवम् that way, भीमा tremendous, न not, तेजः splendour, पराक्रमः valour, न not, मतिः intellect, न not, बलोत्साहौ strength and energy, रूपपरिकल्पनम् ability to change form at will.
explanation: "Earlier I have seen monkeys of immense prowess, like Vali and Sugriva as well as Jambavan, the bear. Also I have seen the army general, Nila, Dvivida and others. They do not have such tremendous splendour or movement valour, intellect and strength and energy. They did not have such ability to change form at their will.

shloka_text: महत्सत्त्वमिदं ज्ञेयं कपिरूपं व्यवस्थितम्।।5.46.12।। प्रयत्नं महदास्थाय क्रियतामस्य निग्रहः।
transliteration: mahatsattvamidaṃ jñeyaṃ kapirūpaṃ vyavasthitam prayatnaṃ mahadāsthāya kriyatāmasya nigrahaḥ|
translation: इदम् this, कपिरूपम् a monkey form, व्यवस्थितम् concluded, महत् great, सत्त्वम्  being, ज्ञेयम् It should be understood, महत् extraordinary, प्रयत्नम् effort, आस्थाय by putting up, अस्य his, निग्रहः capture, क्रियताम् do.
explanation: "It should be understood that he has taken the form of a monkey. You have to put in extraordinary effort to capture him by acting in a suitable manner.

shloka_text: कामं लोकास्त्रयस्सेन्द्रास्ससुरासुरमानवाः।।5.46.13।। भवतामग्रतः स्थातुं न पर्याप्ता रणाजिरे।
transliteration: kāmaṃ lokāstrayassendrāssasurāsuramānavāḥ bhavatāmagrataḥ sthātuṃ na paryāptā raṇājire|
translation: सेन्द्राः including Indra, ससुरासुरमानवाः suras, asuras and humans together, त्रयः all the three, लोकाः worlds, रणाजिरे in the battlefield, भवताम् your, अग्रतः in front, स्थातुम् to stand, न पर्याप्ताः not competent, कामम् indeed.
explanation: "Even Indra, suras, asuras and humans and the three worlds together are incompetent to stand before you in a battlefield.

shloka_text: तथापि तु नयज्ञेन जयमाकाङ्क्षता रणे।।5.46.14।। आत्मा रक्ष्यः प्रयत्नेन युद्धसिद्धिर्हि चञ्चला।
transliteration: tathāpi tu nayajñena jayamākāṅkṣatā raṇe ātmā rakṣyaḥ prayatnena yuddhasiddhirhi cañcalā|
translation: तथापि तु even then, रणे in a war, जयम् victory, आकाङ्क्षता while desiring, नयज्ञेन by carefully adopting war strategies in an intelligent manner, प्रयत्नेन making effort, आत्मा your own self, रक्ष्यः should be protected, युद्धसिद्धिः victory in war, चञ्चला हि is uncertain.
explanation: "Even then, you should safeguard yourself with great effort adopting warstrategies in an intelligent  manner to be victorious, for success in war is uncertain.

shloka_text: ते स्वामिवचनं सर्वे प्रतिगृह्य महौजसः।।5.46.15।। समुत्पेतुर्महावेगा हुताशसमतेजसः। रथैर्मत्तैश्च मातङ्गैर्वाजिभिश्च महाजवैः।।5.46.16।। शस्त्रैश्च विविधैस्तीक्ष्णैस्सर्वैश्चोपचिता बलैः।
transliteration: te svāmivacanaṃ sarve pratigṛhya mahaujasaḥ samutpeturmahāvegā hutāśasamatejasaḥ| rathairmattaiśca mātaṅgairvājibhiśca mahājavaiḥ śastraiśca vividhaistīkṣṇaissarvaiścopacitā balaiḥ|
translation: महौजसः very strong, हुताशसमतेजसः resplendant as sacrificial fire, ते सर्वे all of them, स्वामिवचनम् king's words, प्रतिगृह्य accepting, महावेगाः who were swift, रथैः with chariots, मत्तै intoxicated, मातङ्गै: with elephants, महाजवैः of great speed, वाजिभिश्च with horses, तीक्ष्णैः sharp, विविधैः many kinds, शस्त्रै: with weapons, सर्वे all, बलैः strong army, उपचिताः collecting,समुत्पेतुः sallied forth together
