translation: विमलाम्बांसि pellucid water, सरांसि of the lakes, द्रुमाकीर्णान् of many trees, पर्वताम् mountains, समान् plain, भूमि land, प्रदेशांश्च and in locations, फलवन्ति filled with fruits, वनानि च and forests, सा that, मध्येन in the centre, समान्ता त् plain land, तिर्यक् obliquely, अथश्च underneath, स अविशत्  plucking and eating
explanation: The vanaras went through the pellucid waters of the centre of the lakes. They went obliquely at the mountains, walked on plain lands and underneath trees filled with fruits, plucking them and eating.

shloka_text: समावृत्य महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम महती चमूः । तेहृष्टवदना स्सर्वे जग्मुर्मारुतरंहसः ।।6.4.62।।
transliteration: samāvṛtya mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ jagāma mahatī camūḥ | tehṛṣṭavadanā ssarve jagmurmārutaraṃhasaḥ
translation: महती great, चमूः army, कृत्स्नाम् all over the land, महीम् land, समावृत्य spreading, जगाम went, मारुतरंहसः with the swiftness of wind, ते सर्वे all of them, हृष्टवदनाः with cheerful face, जग्मु went
explanation: The great vanara army spread all over the land went with the swiftness of wind with cheerful faces.

shloka_text: हरयो राघवस्यार्थे समारोपितविक्रमाः ।।6.4.63।। हर्षंवीर्य बलोद्रेकान्दर्शयन्तः परस्परम् । यौवनोत्सेकजान्दर्पाद्विविधांश्चक्रुरध्वनि ।।6.4.64।।
transliteration: harayo rāghavasyārthe samāropitavikramāḥ  harṣaṃvīrya balodrekāndarśayantaḥ parasparam | yauvanotsekajāndarpādvividhāṃścakruradhvani
translation: राघवस्वार्थे for the purpose of Rama,समारोपितविक्रमाः showing their valour to each other, हरयः happiness,बलोद्रेकात्  their prowess charged with emotion, हर्षम् joy, वीर्यम् spirit, परस्परम् one to the other, दर्शयन्तः exhibiting, अध्वनि on the way, यौवनोत्सेकजावत् natural youthful enthusiasm, दर्पात् arrogance, विविधान् several( gestures), चक्रुः went
explanation: For the purpose of Rama, the vanaras went showing their valour, happiness and prowess charged with emotion towards one another on the way. They showed their joy and spirit to one another exhibiting their natural youthful enthusiasm, arrogance and several other gestures.

shloka_text: हरयो राघवस्यार्थे समारोपितविक्रमाः ।।6.4.63।। हर्षंवीर्य बलोद्रेकान्दर्शयन्तः परस्परम् । यौवनोत्सेकजान्दर्पाद्विविधांश्चक्रुरध्वनि ।।6.4.64।।
transliteration: harayo rāghavasyārthe samāropitavikramāḥ  harṣaṃvīrya balodrekāndarśayantaḥ parasparam | yauvanotsekajāndarpādvividhāṃścakruradhvani
translation: राघवस्वार्थे for the purpose of Rama,समारोपितविक्रमाः showing their valour to each other, हरयः happiness,बलोद्रेकात्  their prowess charged with emotion, हर्षम् joy, वीर्यम् spirit, परस्परम् one to the other, दर्शयन्तः exhibiting, अध्वनि on the way, यौवनोत्सेकजावत् natural youthful enthusiasm, दर्पात् arrogance, विविधान् several( gestures), चक्रुः went
explanation: For the purpose of Rama, the vanaras went showing their valour, happiness and prowess charged with emotion towards one another on the way. They showed their joy and spirit to one another exhibiting their natural youthful enthusiasm, arrogance and several other gestures.

shloka_text: तत्र केचिद्द्रुतं जग्मुरुत्पेतुश्च तथापरे । केचित्किलकिलां चक्रुर्वानरा वनगोचराः ।।6.4.65।।
transliteration: tatra keciddrutaṃ jagmurutpetuśca tathāpare | kecitkilakilāṃ cakrurvānarā vanagocarāḥ
translation: तत्र being so, वनगोचराः inhabitants of forests, vanaras, केचित् some, वानराः vanaras, द्रुतम् swiftly , जग्मु went, तथा so also, अपरे others, उत्पेतुश्च jumped, केचित् some, किलकिलाम् made sounds like 'kila kila', चक्रुः went
explanation: Being vanaras some went swiftly, some jumped, and some others made sound 'kila kila'(the usual sounds of monkeys) while they went.

shloka_text: प्रास्पोटयंश्च पुच्छानि सन्निजग्मु: पदान्यपि । भुजावनिक्षिप्य शैलांश्च द्रुमानन्ये बभञ्जिरे ।।6.4.66।।
transliteration: prāspoṭayaṃśca pucchāni sannijagmu: padānyapi | bhujāvanikṣipya śailāṃśca drumānanye babhañjire
translation: पुच्छानि tails, प्रास्पोटयन् hit the ground, पदानि  feet, सन्निजग्मु: stamped on the ground, अपि and, अन्ये others, भुजान् arms, विक्षिप्य crushed, शैलांश्च mountains, द्रुमान् trees, बभञ्जिरे broken
explanation: Some hit their tails on the ground, some stamped their feet on the ground, some crushed the mountains with their arms and some broke the trees.

shloka_text: आरोहन्तश्च शृङ्गाणि गिरीणां गिरिगोचराः । महानादान्प्रमुञ्चन्ति क्ष्वेळ्वामन्ये प्रचक्रिरे ।।6.4.67।।
transliteration: ārohantaśca śṛṅgāṇi girīṇāṃ girigocarāḥ | mahānādānpramuñcanti kṣveḻvāmanye pracakrire
translation: गिरिगोचराः inhabitants of mountains, गिरीणाम् of the mountains, शृङ्गाणि on the peaks, आरोहन्तश्च climbing on top, महा नादान् loud noise, प्रमुञ्चन्ति snapping ,अन्ये others, क्ष्वेळ्वाम् roared like lion, प्रचक्रिरे went round and round
explanation: Vanaras, being the inhabitants of mountains, climbed on peaks of mountains and made loud noises like snapping and roaring like lions. Some went round and round.

shloka_text: ऊरुवेगैश्च ममृदुर्लताजालान्यनेकशः । जृम्भमाणाश्च विक्रान्ता विचिक्रीडुश्शिलाद्रुमै ः ।।6.4.68।।
transliteration: ūruvegaiśca mamṛdurlatājālānyanekaśaḥ | jṛmbhamāṇāśca vikrāntā vicikrīḍuśśilādrumai ḥ
translation: ऊरुवेगैः with the speed of their thighs,अनेकशः several, लताजालानि meshes of creepers, ममृदुः broken, जृम्बमाणा while yawning , विक्रान्ता courageous, शिलाद्रुमैः stones and trees, विचिक्रीडुः whirled round and played
explanation: With the speed of their shaking thighs, the vanaras broke several meshes of creepers. While yawning also some showed their courage by whirling round and throwing stones and trees.

shloka_text: शतश्शतसहस्रैश्च कोटिभिश्च सहस्रशः । वानराणां सुघोराणां श्रीमत्परिवृता मही ।।6.4.69।।
transliteration: śataśśatasahasraiśca koṭibhiśca sahasraśaḥ | vānarāṇāṃ sughorāṇāṃ śrīmatparivṛtā mahī
translation: शतः one hundred, मही land, सुघोराणाम् formidable, वानराणाम् vanaras, शतसहस्रैश्च hundred thousands, सहास्रशः lakhs, कोटिभिः and crores, श्रीमत् splendid, परिवृता spread around
explanation: Formidable vanaras in hundreds, thousands, lakhs and crores spread in a splendid manner around the land.

shloka_text: सा स्म याति दिवारात्रं महती हरिवाहिनी । प्रहृष्टमुदितास्सेना सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिताः ।।6.4.70।। वानरास्त्वरितं यान्ति सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः । प्रमोक्षयिषव स्सीतां मुहूर्तं क्वापि नावसन् ।।6.4.71।।
transliteration: sā sma yāti divārātraṃ mahatī harivāhinī | prahṛṣṭamuditāssenā sugrīveṇābhipālitāḥ  vānarāstvaritaṃ yānti sarve yuddhābhinandinaḥ | pramokṣayiṣava ssītāṃ muhūrtaṃ kvāpi nāvasan
translation: महती mighty, सा हरिवाहिनी that vanara force, दिवारात्रम् day and night, यती  स्म somehow we, सुग्रीवेण by Sugriva, अभिपालिताः protected by, सर्वे all sides, वानराः vanaras, प्रहृष्टमुदिताः delighted at heart, सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः  happy about war , त्वरिताः speedily, यान्ति सीताम् somehow that Sita, प्रमोक्षयिष्वः to liberate, क्वापि  nowhere, मुहूर्तम्  a short while, वासन् not stood
explanation: The mighty vanara force protected by Sugriva from all sides cheerful at heart, walked day and night speedily. Being eager to somehow liberate Sita they were happy about war and stood nowhere for a while.

shloka_text: सा स्म याति दिवारात्रं महती हरिवाहिनी । प्रहृष्टमुदितास्सेना सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिताः ।।6.4.70।। वानरास्त्वरितं यान्ति सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः । प्रमोक्षयिषव स्सीतां मुहूर्तं क्वापि नावसन् ।।6.4.71।।
transliteration: sā sma yāti divārātraṃ mahatī harivāhinī | prahṛṣṭamuditāssenā sugrīveṇābhipālitāḥ  vānarāstvaritaṃ yānti sarve yuddhābhinandinaḥ | pramokṣayiṣava ssītāṃ muhūrtaṃ kvāpi nāvasan
translation: महती mighty, सा हरिवाहिनी that vanara force, दिवारात्रम् day and night, यती  स्म somehow we, सुग्रीवेण by Sugriva, अभिपालिताः protected by, सर्वे all sides, वानराः vanaras, प्रहृष्टमुदिताः delighted at heart, सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः  happy about war , त्वरिताः speedily, यान्ति सीताम् somehow that Sita, प्रमोक्षयिष्वः to liberate, क्वापि  nowhere, मुहूर्तम्  a short while, वासन् not stood
explanation: The mighty vanara force protected by Sugriva from all sides cheerful at heart, walked day and night speedily. Being eager to somehow liberate Sita they were happy about war and stood nowhere for a while.

shloka_text: ततः पादपसम्भाधं नानामृगसमायुताम । सह्यपर्वतमासेदुर्मलयञ्च महीधरम् ।।6.4.72।।
transliteration: tataḥ pādapasambhādhaṃ nānāmṛgasamāyutāma | sahyaparvatamāsedurmalayañca mahīdharam
translation: ततः thereafter, ते महीधरम् that land, पादपसम्बाधम् dense with trees, नानामृगसमावृतम् inhabited by different kinds of animals, मलयञ्च Malaya and, सह्यपर्वतम् Sahaya mountain, सेदु:boundary , आसाद्य having reached, समायुताम् assembled
explanation: Thereafter having reached the dense forest filled with trees surrounded by the Malaya and Sahaya Mountain inhabited by different kinds of animals, the vanaras assembled.

shloka_text: काननानि विचित्राणि नदी: प्रस्रवणानि च । पश्यन्ननि ययौ रामस्सह्यस्य मलयस्य च ।।6.4.73।।
transliteration: kānanāni vicitrāṇi nadī: prasravaṇāni ca | paśyannani yayau rāmassahyasya malayasya ca
translation: रामः नि Rama also,सह्यस्य Sahaya's,च and, विचित्राणि wonderful, काननानि woods, नदीप्रस्रवणानि च streams of rivers, पश्यन् to see, ययौ went
explanation: Rama too went to see the wonderful woods and streams of rivers of Sahaya mountain.

shloka_text: वकुळान्स्तिलकांश्चूतानसोकान् सिन्धुवारकान् । करवीरांश्च तिनिशान् भजन्ति स्म प्लवङ्गगमाः ।।6.4.74।।
transliteration: vakuḻānstilakāṃścūtānasokān sindhuvārakān | karavīrāṃśca tiniśān bhajanti sma plavaṅgagamāḥ
translation: प्लवङ्गमाः leaping animals(vanaras), वकुळान् Vakula trees, तिलकान् Tilaka , चूतान् असोकान् Mango and Asoka, सिन्धुवारकान् Sinduvara , तिनिशान् Tinisa, करवीरांश्च Karaveera and, भजन्ति स्म adoring them
explanation: The vanaras went adoring the Vakula, Tilaka, Mango, Asoka, Tinisa, Sinduvara and Karaveera trees.

shloka_text: अङ्कोलांश्च करञ्चांश्च प्लक्षन्यग्रोधतिन्दुकान् । जम्बुकामलकान्नापान्भजन्ति स्म प्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.4.75।।
transliteration: aṅkolāṃśca karañcāṃśca plakṣanyagrodhatindukān | jambukāmalakānnāpānbhajanti sma plavaṅgamāḥ
translation: प्लवङ्गमाः vanaras, अङ्कोलान् Ankola, करञ्चांश्च Karanja and , प्लक्षन्यग्रोधपादपान् Plaksa and Nyagrodha, जम्बुकामलकान् Jambu and Amla, नीपान् Neepa, भजन्ति स्म adoring them
explanation: Vanaras went adoring the Ankola, Karanja, Plaksa, Nyagrodha, Jambu,Amla and neepa trees.

shloka_text: प्रस्तरेषु च रम्येषु विविधाः काननद्रुमाः । वायुवेगप्रचलिताः पुष्पैरवकिरन्ति तान् ।।6.4.76।।
transliteration: prastareṣu ca ramyeṣu vividhāḥ kānanadrumāḥ | vāyuvegapracalitāḥ puṣpairavakiranti tān
translation: रम्येषु beautiful, प्रस्तरेषु on rocks, विविधाः many kinds, काननद्रुमाः forest trees, वायुवेगप्रचलिताः shaken by the fury of winds, तान् their, पुष्पैः flowers, अवकिरन्ति showered
explanation: Many kinds of trees standing on beautiful rocks and of the forest shaken by the fury of the wind showered their flowers on the vanaras.

shloka_text: मारुतस्सुखसंस्पर्शो वाति चन्दनशीतलः । षटपदैरनुकूजद्भिर्वनेषु मधुगन्धिषु ।।6.4.77।।
transliteration: mārutassukhasaṃsparśo vāti candanaśītalaḥ | ṣaṭapadairanukūjadbhirvaneṣu madhugandhiṣu
translation: मधुगन्धिषु spreading sweet fragrance of honey,वनेषु  of the forest, अनुकूजद्भि: humming in delight,षटपदैः bees, सुख संस्पर्शः by their cool touch,चन्दनशीतलः like the coolness of sandal, मारुतः breeze, वाति blowed
explanation: As the bees humming in delight were spreading the sweet fragrance of honey accompanied the breeze that blew, it was cool like the cool touch of sandal (to the vanaras).

shloka_text: अधिकं शैलराजस्तु धातुभिस्सुविभूषितः । धातुभ्यःप्रसृतो रेणुर्वायुवेग विघट्टितः । सुमहद्वानरानीकं छादयामास सर्वतः ।।6.4.78।।
transliteration: adhikaṃ śailarājastu dhātubhissuvibhūṣitaḥ | dhātubhyaḥprasṛto reṇurvāyuvega vighaṭṭitaḥ | sumahadvānarānīkaṃ chādayāmāsa sarvataḥ
translation: शैलराजस्तु lord of mountains, धातु: minerals, अधिकम् richly, सुविभूषितः shone brightly, वायुवेग speed of the wind, विघट्टितः by the stamping(crushing), रेणुः particles, धातुभ्य: of minerals, प्रसृतः raised, सुमहत् huge, वानरानीकम् vanara troops, सर्वतः all over, छादयामास covered
explanation: That lord of mountains richly adorned with minerals shone very brightly. The mineral particles raised by the stamping of the vanara troops covered the huge vanaras all over.

shloka_text: गिरिप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु सर्वत सम्प्र पुष्पिताः । केतकस्सिन्दुवाराश्च वासन्त्यश्च मनोरमाः ।।6.4.79।। माधव्यो गन्धपूर्णाश्च कुन्दगुल्माश्च पुष्पिताः । चिरिबिल्वा मधूकाश्च वञ्जुला प्रियकास्तथा ।।6.4.80।। सुफूर्जकास्तिलकाश्चैव नागवृक्षाश्च पुष्पिताः । चूताः पाटलयकाश्चैव कोविदाराश्च पुष्पिताः ।।6.4.81।। मुचुलिन्दार्जुनाश्चैव शिंशुपाः कुटजास्तथा । धवा श्शाल्मलयश्चैव रक्ता: कुरवकास्तथा ।।6.4.82।। हिन्तालास्तिनिशाश्चैव चूर्णका नीपकास्तथा । नीलाशोकाश्च वरणा अङ्कोलाः पद्मकास्तथा ।।6.4.83।। प्लवमानै: प्लवंगैस्तु सर्वे पर्याकुलीकृतां ।।6.4.84।।
transliteration: giriprastheṣu ramyeṣu sarvata sampra puṣpitāḥ | ketakassinduvārāśca vāsantyaśca manoramāḥ  mādhavyo gandhapūrṇāśca kundagulmāśca puṣpitāḥ | ciribilvā madhūkāśca vañjulā priyakāstathā  suphūrjakāstilakāścaiva nāgavṛkṣāśca puṣpitāḥ | cūtāḥ pāṭalayakāścaiva kovidārāśca puṣpitāḥ  muculindārjunāścaiva śiṃśupāḥ kuṭajāstathā | dhavā śśālmalayaścaiva raktā: kuravakāstathā  hintālāstiniśāścaiva cūrṇakā nīpakāstathā | nīlāśokāśca varaṇā aṅkolāḥ padmakāstathā  plavamānai: plavaṃgaistu sarve paryākulīkṛtāṃ
translation: रम्येषु beautiful, गिरिप्रस्तेषु  in the mountain ranges, सर्वतः all over, सम्प्रपुष्पिताः well blossomed, केतन्यः Kethaka, सिन्धुवाराश्च Sinduvaara,मनोरमाः Manorama, वासन्त्यः Vaasantha(mango),माधव्य: Madhavi( a kind of jasmine),पुष्पिताः blossoms,गन्धपूर्णाः filled with fragrance,कुन्दगुल्माश्च Kunda and Gulma( fragrant creepers),चिरिबिल्वाः Chiribilva( a kind of wild tree), मधुकाश्च Madhuka( a kind of tree whose flowers are used for making liquor) also, वञ्जुलाः Vajula(cane), तथा so also, वकुलाः Vakula, रञ्जकाः Ranjaka( red sandal ), तिलकाश्चैव and Tilaka( a kind of tree with beautiful flowers), कुरवका: Kuruvaka, नागवृक्षाश्च Naga trees, चूताः Chuta, पाटलिकाश्चैव Patalaya, रक्ता: of red flowers, मुचुलिन्दार्जुनाश्चैव Muchulinda and Arjuna( a tree with white flowers), शिंशुपाः Simsupa, तथा in the same way, कुटजाः Kutaja?B, धवाः Dhava, शाल्मलश्चैव Salmala, तथा so also, रक्त कुरनाः red Kurana, हिंतालाः Hinthala, तिनिशाश्चैव Tinisa, चूर्णकाः Churnaka, तथा similarly, नीपकाः Neepa, नीलाशोकाः dark flowered Asoka,सरलाः Sarala( a kind of pine), आङ्कोलाः Ankola, पद्मकाः Padamaka, सर्वे all, प्लवमानै: vanaras, प्लवङ्गैः for shaking and jumping about, पर्याकुलीकृताः were convenient
explanation: In the mountain ranges were well blossomed trees  such as Kethaka, Sinduvaara and Mango trees Manorama, Madhavi, Kunda, Gulma creepers filled with blossoms of fragrance Chiribilva, Madhuka like wild trees,Vajula,Vakula ,Ranjaka, Tilaka,Kuruvaka, Naga trees Patalaya trees trees with red flowers Arjuna, Simsupa trees with white flowers Kutaja, Dhava and Salmala, Red Kurana, Hinthala,Tinisa,and Churanaka trees, so also dark flowered Asoka trees, Pine trees, Ankola and Padmaka trees were convenient for the monkeys to shake and jump.

explanation: In the mountain ranges were well blossomed trees  such as Kethaka, Sinduvaara and Mango trees Manorama, Madhavi, Kunda, Gulma creepers filled with blossoms of fragrance Chiribilva, Madhuka like wild trees,Vajula,Vakula ,Ranjaka, Tilaka,Kuruvaka, Naga trees Patalaya trees trees with red flowers Arjuna, Simsupa trees with white flowers Kutaja, Dhava and Salmala, Red Kurana, Hinthala,Tinisa,and Churanaka trees, so also dark flowered Asoka trees, Pine trees, Ankola and Padmaka trees were convenient for the monkeys to shake and jump.

shloka_text: गिरिप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु सर्वत सम्प्र पुष्पिताः । केतकस्सिन्दुवाराश्च वासन्त्यश्च मनोरमाः ।।6.4.79।। माधव्यो गन्धपूर्णाश्च कुन्दगुल्माश्च पुष्पिताः । चिरिबिल्वा मधूकाश्च वञ्जुला प्रियकास्तथा ।।6.4.80।। सुफूर्जकास्तिलकाश्चैव नागवृक्षाश्च पुष्पिताः । चूताः पाटलयकाश्चैव कोविदाराश्च पुष्पिताः ।।6.4.81।। मुचुलिन्दार्जुनाश्चैव शिंशुपाः कुटजास्तथा । धवा श्शाल्मलयश्चैव रक्ता: कुरवकास्तथा ।।6.4.82।। हिन्तालास्तिनिशाश्चैव चूर्णका नीपकास्तथा । नीलाशोकाश्च वरणा अङ्कोलाः पद्मकास्तथा ।।6.4.83।। प्लवमानै: प्लवंगैस्तु सर्वे पर्याकुलीकृतां ।।6.4.84।।

shloka_text: वाप्यस्तस्मिन् गिरौ शिता: पल्वलानि तथैव च । चक्रवाकानुचरिताः कारण्डवनिषेविताः ।।6.4.85।। प्लवैः क्रौञ्चेश्च सङ्कीर्णा वराहमृग सेविताः । ऋक्षैस्तरक्षुभिस्सिम्हैश्शार्दूलैश्च भयावहैः ।।6.4.86।। व्यालैश्च बहुभिर्भीमै स्सेव्यमाना स्समन्ततः । पद्मैस्सौगन्दिकैः पुल्लैः कुमुदैश्चोत्पलैस्तथा ।।6.4.87।। वारिजैर्विविधैः पुष्पै रम्यास्तत्र जलाशयाः ।
transliteration: vāpyastasmin girau śitā: palvalāni tathaiva ca | cakravākānucaritāḥ kāraṇḍavaniṣevitāḥ  plavaiḥ krauñceśca saṅkīrṇā varāhamṛga sevitāḥ | ṛkṣaistarakṣubhissimhaiśśārdūlaiśca bhayāvahaiḥ  vyālaiśca bahubhirbhīmai ssevyamānā ssamantataḥ | padmaissaugandikaiḥ pullaiḥ kumudaiścotpalaistathā  vārijairvividhaiḥ puṣpai ramyāstatra jalāśayāḥ |
translation: तस्मिन् in those, गिरौ mountains, शीता: cool, वाप्यः reservoirs, तथैव च  in the same way, पल्वलानि च and ponds, तत्र there, चक्रवाकानुचरिताः inhabited by  Chakravaka birds, कारण्डवनिषेविताः frequented by ravens, प्लवैः birds, क्रौञ्चेश्च and Krauncha birds, सङ्कीर्णाः flocks of birds dwelling, वराहमृगसेविताः occupied by boars etc, ऋक्षैः bears, तरक्षुभिः hyenas, सिंहैः lions, भयावहैः frightening, शार्दूलैश्च tigers too, भीमैः terrific, बहुभिः of many kinds, व्यालैः wild elephants, समन्ततः all over, सेव्यमानाः frequented, पद्मैः woodlands, पुल्लैः flowers  in full bloom, सौगन्दिकैः fragrant ones, कुमुदैः lotuses, तथा like that, उत्पलैः blue lotus, वारिजैः red lotus, विविधैः many kinds, पुष्पैः blossoms, रम्या  delightful, जलाशयाः lakes
explanation: In the mountains were reservoirs of water and ponds with cool water inhabited by flocks of Chakravaka birds, water birds like ravens and Krauncha birds. The woodlands were terrific, frequented by boars, bears, hyenas, lions and frightening tigers and many kinds of wild elephants. With flowers in full bloom, the white, blue and red lotuses in the lakes were delightful.

shloka_text: वाप्यस्तस्मिन् गिरौ शिता: पल्वलानि तथैव च । चक्रवाकानुचरिताः कारण्डवनिषेविताः ।।6.4.85।। प्लवैः क्रौञ्चेश्च सङ्कीर्णा वराहमृग सेविताः । ऋक्षैस्तरक्षुभिस्सिम्हैश्शार्दूलैश्च भयावहैः ।।6.4.86।। व्यालैश्च बहुभिर्भीमै स्सेव्यमाना स्समन्ततः । पद्मैस्सौगन्दिकैः पुल्लैः कुमुदैश्चोत्पलैस्तथा ।।6.4.87।। वारिजैर्विविधैः पुष्पै रम्यास्तत्र जलाशयाः ।

translation: तस्मिन् in those, गिरौ mountains, शीता: cool, वाप्यः reservoirs, तथैव च  in the same way, पल्वलानि च and ponds, तत्र there, चक्रवाकानुचरिताः inhabited by  Chakravaka birds, कारण्डवनिषेविताः frequented by ravens, प्लवैः birds, क्रौञ्चेश्च and Krauncha birds, सङ्कीर्णाः flocks of birds dwelling, वराहमृगसेविताः occupied by boars etc, ऋक्षैः bears, तरक्षुभिः hyenas, सिंहैः lions, भयावहैः frightening, शार्दूलैश्च tigers too, भीमैः terrific, बहुभिः of many kinds, व्यालैः wild elephants, समन्ततः all over, सेव्यमानाः frequented, पद्मैः woodlands, पुल्लैः flowers  in full bloom, सौगन्दिकैः fragrant ones, कुमुदैः lotuses, तथा like that, उत्पलैः blue lotus, वारिजैः red lotus, विविधैः many kinds, पुष्पैः blossoms, रम्या  delightful, जलाशयाः lakes
explanation: In the mountains were reservoirs of water and ponds with cool water inhabited by flocks of Chakravaka birds, water birds like ravens and Krauncha birds. The woodlands were terrific, frequented by boars, bears, hyenas, lions and frightening tigers and many kinds of wild elephants. With flowers in full bloom, the white, blue and red lotuses in the lakes were delightful.

shloka_text: तस्य सानुषु कूजन्ति नानाद्विजगणास्तथा ।।6.4.88।। स्नात्वा पीत्वोदकान्यत्र जले क्रीडन्ति वानराः । अन्योन्यं प्लावयन्ति स्म शैलमारुह्य वानराः ।।6.4.89।।
transliteration: tasya sānuṣu kūjanti nānādvijagaṇāstathā  snātvā pītvodakānyatra jale krīḍanti vānarāḥ | anyonyaṃ plāvayanti sma śailamāruhya vānarāḥ
translation: तथा that way, तस्य its, सानुषु in the mountain ranges, नानाद्विजगणाः different kinds of flocks of birds, कूजन्ति singing , वानराः vanaras, जले in water, स्नात्वा after taking a bath, उदकानि the water, पीत्वा drinking, क्रीडन्ति sporting, शैलम् mountain, अरुह्य climbing up, अन्योन्यम् one over the other, प्लावयन्ति स्म jumping
explanation: At that time different kinds of flocks of birds were singing in the mountain ranges. The vanaras after having taken their bath were drinking and sporting with water with each other (pouring water over another) climbing up the mountain.

shloka_text: तस्य सानुषु कूजन्ति नानाद्विजगणास्तथा ।।6.4.88।। स्नात्वा पीत्वोदकान्यत्र जले क्रीडन्ति वानराः । अन्योन्यं प्लावयन्ति स्म शैलमारुह्य वानराः ।।6.4.89।।
transliteration: tasya sānuṣu kūjanti nānādvijagaṇāstathā  snātvā pītvodakānyatra jale krīḍanti vānarāḥ | anyonyaṃ plāvayanti sma śailamāruhya vānarāḥ
translation: तथा that way, तस्य its, सानुषु in the mountain ranges, नानाद्विजगणाः different kinds of flocks of birds, कूजन्ति singing , वानराः vanaras, जले in water, स्नात्वा after taking a bath, उदकानि the water, पीत्वा drinking, क्रीडन्ति sporting, शैलम् mountain, अरुह्य climbing up, अन्योन्यम् one over the other, प्लावयन्ति स्म jumping
explanation: At that time different kinds of flocks of birds were singing in the mountain ranges. The vanaras after having taken their bath were drinking and sporting with water with each other (pouring water over another) climbing up the mountain.

shloka_text: फलान्य मृतगन्धीनि मूलानि कुसुमानि च । बभञ्जुर्वास्तत्र पादपानं मदोत्कटाः ।।6.4.90।।
transliteration: phalānya mṛtagandhīni mūlāni kusumāni ca | babhañjurvāstatra pādapānaṃ madotkaṭāḥ
translation: तत्र then, मदोत्कटाः one deluded with pride, वानराः vanaras, पादपानाम्  climbing trees, अमृतगन्धीनि of nectar like aroma, फलानि fruits, मूलानि roots, कुसुमानि च and flowers, बभञ्जुः ate
explanation: Then the vanaras who were deluded with pride climbed the trees and ate the fruits with nectar like aroma, roots and flowers.

shloka_text: द्रोणमात्रप्रमाणानि लम्बमानानि वानराः । ययुः पिबन्त हृष्टास्ते मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः ।।6.4.91।।
transliteration: droṇamātrapramāṇāni lambamānāni vānarāḥ | yayuḥ pibanta hṛṣṭāste madhūni madhupiṅgalāḥ
translation: मधुपिङ्गलाः tawnyeyed, ते वानराः those vanras, लम्बमानानि hanging, द्रोणमात्रप्रमाणानि honey coombs of ten litres size, मधूनि the honey of, पिबन्तः drinking, हृष्टा: joyfully, ययुः went
explanation: The tawnyeyed monkeys went joyfully drinking the honey from the large honeycombs hanging there.

shloka_text: पादपानवभञ्जन्तो विकर्षन्त स्तथा लताः । विधमन्तो गिरिवरान्प्रययुः प्लवगर्षभाः ।।6.4.92।।
transliteration: pādapānavabhañjanto vikarṣanta stathā latāḥ | vidhamanto girivarānprayayuḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ
translation: प्ल वगर्षभाः the best among the leaping ones, पादपान् trees, अवभञ्जन्तः smashing, तथा that way, लताः creepers, विकर्षन्तः pulling out, गिरिवरान् best of mountains, विधिमन्तः purposefully destroying, प्रययुः went
explanation: The vanaras (who are best among leaping animals) went smashing the trees, pulling out the creepers and purposefully destroying the mountains (on their way).

shloka_text: वृक्षेभ्योऽन्ये तु कपयो नदन्तो मधुदर्पिताः । अन्ये वृक्षान्प्रपद्यन्ते प्रपिबन्त्यपि चापरे ।।6.4.93।।
transliteration: vṛkṣebhyo'nye tu kapayo nadanto madhudarpitāḥ | anye vṛkṣānprapadyante prapibantyapi cāpare
translation: अन्ये others, कपयः monkeys, मधुदर्पिताः intoxicated by drinking excessive honey, वृक्षेभ्यः where the trees, नदन्तः walking, अन्ये others, वृक्षान् the trees, प्रपद्यन्ते climbed, अपरे top, प्रपिबन्ति jumped
explanation: While some monkeys that were intoxicated by drinking excessive honey walked where there were no trees, others climbed the tree tops and jumped.

shloka_text: बभूव वसुधा तैस्तु सम्पूर्णा हरियूथपै: । यथा कलमकेदारैः पक्वैरिव वसुन्दरा ।।6.4.94।।
transliteration: babhūva vasudhā taistu sampūrṇā hariyūthapai: | yathā kalamakedāraiḥ pakvairiva vasundarā
translation: तैः those, हरियूथपै: vanara heroes, सम्पूर्ण filled completely, वसुन्धरा the land, पक्वैः fully ripe, कलमकेदारै like paddy field, वसुन्धरा यथेव the land seemed, बभूव was seen
explanation: That land filled completely with the vanara heroes seemed like a fully ripe paddy field.

shloka_text: महेन्द्रमथ सम्प्राप्य रामो राजीवलोचनः । अध्यारोहन्महाबाहुश्शिखरं द्रुमभूषितम् ।।6.4.95।।
transliteration: mahendramatha samprāpya rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ | adhyārohanmahābāhuśśikharaṃ drumabhūṣitam
translation: अथ and then, राजीवलोचनः lotuseyed , महाबाहुः of mighty shoulders, रामः Rama, महेन्द्रम् Mahendra mountain, सम्प्राप्य arriving at, द्रुमभूषितम् adorned with beautiful trees, शिखरम् top, अध्यारोह  climbed up
explanation: At that time Lotuseyed Rama of mighty shoulders climbed up the the top of mountain Mahendra adorned with beautiful trees.

shloka_text: ततश्शिखरमारुह्य रामो दशरथात्मजः । कूर्ममीनसमाकीर्णमपश्यत्सलिलाकुलम् ।।6.4.96।।
transliteration: tataśśikharamāruhya rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ | kūrmamīnasamākīrṇamapaśyatsalilākulam
translation: ततः then, दशरथात्मजः Dasaratha's son, रामः Rama, शिखरम् top , आरुह्या on climbing, कूर्मामीनसमाकीर्णम् inhabited by tortoises and fish, सलिलाकुलम् ocean, अपश्यत् observed
explanation: Then Rama the son of Dasaratha on climbing to the top (of Mahendra mountain) observed the ocean inhabited by tortoises and fish.

shloka_text: ते सह्यं समतिक्रम्य मलयं च महागिरिम् । आसेदुरानुपूर्व्येण समुद्रं भमनिस्स्वनम् ।।6.4.97।।
transliteration: te sahyaṃ samatikramya malayaṃ ca mahāgirim | āsedurānupūrvyeṇa samudraṃ bhamanissvanam
translation: ते they, सह्याम् Sahya mountain, महागिरिम् great mountain, मलयं च and Malaya mountain, समतिक्रम्य likewise, आनुपूर्व्येण crossing one after the other, भीमनिस्वनम् of frightening size, समुद्रम् ocean, आसेदुः reached
explanation: The vanaras crossing over the great Sahya and Malaya mountains one after another reached near the frightening ocean.

shloka_text: अवरुह्य जगामाशु वेलावनमनुत्तमम् । रामो रमयतां श्रेष्ट स्ससुग्रीव स्सलक्ष्मणः ।।6.4.98।।
transliteration: avaruhya jagāmāśu velāvanamanuttamam | rāmo ramayatāṃ śreṣṭa ssasugrīva ssalakṣmaṇaḥ
translation: ससुग्रीव along with Sugriva, सलक्ष्मणः with Lakshmana, रमयताम् among those who cause delight, श्रेष्टः best, रामः Rama, अवरुह्य got down, आशु soon, अनुत्तमम् best, वेलावनम् wood on the sea coast, जगाम went
explanation: Rama, who causes delight to others, got down (the mountain) along with Lakshmana and Sugriva and soon reached the wood on the sea coast.

shloka_text: अथ धौतोपलतलां तोयौघै स्सहसोत्थितैः । वेलामासाद्य विपुलान्रामो वचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.4.99।।
transliteration: atha dhautopalatalāṃ toyaughai ssahasotthitaiḥ | velāmāsādya vipulānrāmo vacanamabravīt
translation: अथ and from there, रामः Rama, सहसा atonce, उत्थितैः sprung up, तोयौघैः by waves, धौतो पलतलाम् polished surface of the earth, विपुलाम् extensive, वेलाम् soon, आसाद्य reaching, वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke
explanation: Atonce Rama sprung from there (top of mountain) on to an extensive surface of the earth polished by the waves of the ocean spoke these words on reaching there.

shloka_text: एते वयमनुप्राप्ता स्सुग्रीव वरुणालयम् । इहेदानीं विचिन्ता साया नः पूर्वसमुत्थिता ।।6.4.100।।
transliteration: ete vayamanuprāptā ssugrīva varuṇālayam | ihedānīṃ vicintā sāyā naḥ pūrvasamutthitā
translation: सुग्रीव Sugriva, एते वयम् that which we, वरुणालयम् abode of Varuna, sea, समनुप्राप्ताः have reached, या that which, पूर्वम् earlier, सा that, विचिन्ता idea, इह here, इदानीम् now, नः we, समुत्थिता have to think of
explanation: Sugriva We have reached the ocean and now we have to think of that idea now, which we thought of earlier.

shloka_text: अतः परमतीरोऽयं सागर स्सरितां पतिः । न चायमनुपायेन शक्यस्तरितुमर्णवः ।।6.4.101।।
transliteration: ataḥ paramatīro'yaṃ sāgara ssaritāṃ patiḥ | na cāyamanupāyena śakyastaritumarṇavaḥ
translation: सरितां पतिः lord of the rivers,ocean, आयुं सागरः all ocean , अतः परम् and the shore, अतीरः beyond this, आयम् we, अर्णवः ocean, अनुपायेन without any mode, तरितुम् to cross, न शक्यः not possible.
explanation: There is only the ocean, the lord of rivers, and the shore is beyond this. We cannot cross the ocean without any mode.

shloka_text: तदिहैव निवेशोऽस्तु मन्त्रः प्रस्तूयतामिह । यथेदं वानरबलं परं पारमवाप्नुयात् ।।6.4.102।।
transliteration: tadihaiva niveśo'stu mantraḥ prastūyatāmiha | yathedaṃ vānarabalaṃ paraṃ pāramavāpnuyāt
translation: तत् there, इहैव here itself,निवेशः land, अस्तु will have to, इदम् this, वानरबलम् army of vanaras, यथा that way, पारम् other shore, अवाप्नुयात्  getting there, मन्त्रः deliberation, इह प्रस्तूयताम् camp here
explanation: We will have to leave the army of vanaras here itself. We have to deliberate how to get the vanaras to the other shore.

shloka_text: इतीव स महाबाहुस्सीताहरणकर्शितः । रामस्सागरमासाद्य वासमाज्ञापयत्तदा ।।6.4.103।।
transliteration: itīva sa mahābāhussītāharaṇakarśitaḥ | rāmassāgaramāsādya vāsamājñāpayattadā
translation: महाबाहुः mightyarmed, सीताहरणकर्शितः tormented by abduction of Sita, सः रामः that Rama, तदा this way, सागरम् at ocean, आसाद्य seeing, इतीव in this way, वासम् quartering of, आज्ञापयत् ordered
explanation: On seeing the ocean, the mightyarmed Rama, tormented by the abduction of Sita in that way, ordered about the quartering of the vanaras.

shloka_text: सर्वा स्सेना निवेश्यन्तां वेलायां हरिपुङ्गव । सम्प्राप्तो मन्त्रकालो नस्सागरस्येह लङ्घने ।।6.4.104।।
transliteration: sarvā ssenā niveśyantāṃ velāyāṃ haripuṅgava | samprāpto mantrakālo nassāgarasyeha laṅghane
translation: हरिपुङ्गवः O Best among monkeys, सर्वाः  for all, सेनाः the army, वेलायाम् at the sea coast, निवेश्यन्ताम् for arranging to reside, इह now, सागरस्य ocean's, लङ्घने to cross, नः for us, मन्त्रकालः time for deliberation, सम्प्राप्तः has set in
explanation: "O Best of monkeys Now make preparation for all the army to reside at the sea coast. The time to deliberate about crossing the ocean has set in."

shloka_text: स्वां स्वां सेनां समुत्सृज्य मा च कश्चित्कुतो व्रजेत् । गच्छन्तु वानराश्शूराज्ञेयं छन्नं भयं च नः ।।6.4.105।।
transliteration: svāṃ svāṃ senāṃ samutsṛjya mā ca kaścitkuto vrajet | gacchantu vānarāśśūrājñeyaṃ channaṃ bhayaṃ ca naḥ
translation: कश्चित् none, स्वां स्वाम् their respective, सेनाम् army, समुत्सृज्य leaving, कुतः  what so ever, मा व्रजेत्  not to go, नः us, छन्नम् a parasol,भयम् dangerous, ज्ञेयं च should be known, शूराः warriors, वानराः vanaras, गच्छन्तु should keep guarding
explanation: "None of the army should go wherever leaving the parasol. The vanara warriors should keep guarding and you may know that it is dangerous".

shloka_text: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीव स्सहलक्ष्मणः । सेनां निवेशयततीरे सागरस्य द्रुमायुते ।।6.4.106।।
transliteration: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīva ssahalakṣmaṇaḥ | senāṃ niveśayatatīre sāgarasya drumāyute
translation: सहलक्ष्मणः with Lakshmana, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, रामस्य Rama's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard,सागरस्य of the ocean, द्रुमायुते filled with trees, तीरे shore, सेनाम् the army, निवेशयत् to reside
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, Sugriva and Lakshmana made the army to reside on the sea shore filled with trees.

shloka_text: विरराज समीपस्थं सागरस्य तु तद्बलम् । मधुपाण्डुजल श्रशीमान् द्वितीय इव सागरः ।।6.4.107।।
transliteration: virarāja samīpasthaṃ sāgarasya tu tadbalam | madhupāṇḍujala śraśīmān dvitīya iva sāgaraḥ
translation: सागरस्य of the sea, समीपस्थम् proximity, तत् that, बलम् vast army, मधुपाण्डुजलः like tawny coloured water, श्रीमान् prosperous, द्वितीयः second, सागरः इव like sea, विरराज shone
explanation: That vast (sea of) army of monkeys in tawny colour (settled) at the proximity of the sea (that was white) seemed like a prosperous second sea in bright colour.

shloka_text: वेलावनमुपागम्य ततस्ते हरिपुङ्गवाः । निविष्टाश्च परं पारं काङ्क्षमाणा महोदधेः ।।6.4.108।।
transliteration: velāvanamupāgamya tataste haripuṅgavāḥ | niviṣṭāśca paraṃ pāraṃ kāṅkṣamāṇā mahodadheḥ
translation: ततः then, ते they, हरिपुङ्गवाः best of monkeys, वेलावनम्forest close to the sea , उपागम्य having arrived, महोदधेः mighty ocean , परं पारम् the other side , काङ्क्षमाणाः desiring to reach, निविष्टाश्च stood here and there
explanation: Then the heroic monkeys having arrived at the forest close to the ocean stood there desiring to reach the other shore.

shloka_text: तेषां निविशमानानां सैन्यसन्नाहनिस्स्वनः । अन्तर्धाय महानादमर्णवस्य प्रशुश्रुवे ।।6.4.109।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ niviśamānānāṃ sainyasannāhanissvanaḥ | antardhāya mahānādamarṇavasya praśuśruve
translation: तेषाम् by their, निविशमानानाम्  quartering there, सैन्यसन्नाहनिस्स्वनः by the assembly of the army, अर्णवस्य of the ocean, महानादम् great noise, अन्तर्धाय drowning, प्रशुश्रुवे that which was produced
explanation: The noise of the ocean was drowned by the great sound produced by the assembly of the army quartered there.

shloka_text: सा वानराणां ध्वजिनी सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिता । त्रिधा निविष्टा महती रामस्यार्थपराऽभवत् ।।6.4.110।।
transliteration: sā vānarāṇāṃ dhvajinī sugrīveṇābhipālitā | tridhā niviṣṭā mahatī rāmasyārthaparā'bhavat
translation: त्रिथा the three( army groups), निविष्टा encamped, सुग्रीवेण by Sugriva, अभिपालिता  protected by, सा that, वानराणाम् army of vanaras, ध्वजिनी enthusiastic, रामस्य of Rama, अर्थपरा purpose, अभवत् appeared
explanation: The three army groups of vanaras protected by Sugriva encamped for the purpose of Rama appeared enthusiastic.

shloka_text: सा महार्णवमासाद्य हृष्टा वानरवाहिनी । वायुवेगसमाधूतं पश्यमाना महार्णवम् ।।6.4.111।।
transliteration: sā mahārṇavamāsādya hṛṣṭā vānaravāhinī | vāyuvegasamādhūtaṃ paśyamānā mahārṇavam
translation: सा those, हरिवाहिनी mass of vanaras, महार्णवम् great ocean, आसाद्य having arrived at, वायवेगसमाधूतम्  the ocean lashed by the fury of the wind, महार्णवम् great ocean, पश्यमाना seeing, हृष्टा felt rejoiced.
explanation: Having arrived at the great ocean and seeing the ocean lashed by the fury of the wind the vanaras felt rejoiced.

shloka_text: दूरपारमसम्बाधं रक्षोगणनिषेवितम् । पश्यन्तो वरुणावासं निषेदुर्हरियूथपाः ।।6.4.112।।
transliteration: dūrapāramasambādhaṃ rakṣogaṇaniṣevitam | paśyanto varuṇāvāsaṃ niṣedurhariyūthapāḥ
translation: दूरपारम् shores far away, असम्बाधम् not connected, रक्षोगणनिषेवितम् protected by rakshasa army, वरुणावासम् abode of rain god, पश्यन्तः on seeing,हरियूथपाः vanara army, निषेदुः not obstructed (expansive)
explanation: On seeing the expansive ocean, the vanara army thought 'how to cross the abode of rain god whose shores are far away and not connected and is protected by rakshasas'?

shloka_text: चण्डनक्रग्राहं घोरं क्षपादौ दिवसक्ष्ये । हसन्तमिव फेनौघैर्नृत्यन्तमिव चोर्मिभिः ।।6.4.113।।
transliteration: caṇḍanakragrāhaṃ ghoraṃ kṣapādau divasakṣye | hasantamiva phenaughairnṛtyantamiva cormibhiḥ
translation: चण्डनक्रग्रहम्  crocodiles which can catch any animal, घोरम् terrific, दिवसक्ष्ये during  at the end of the day, क्षपादौ when night sets in , फेनौघैः foamy waters, हसन्तमिव as if laughing, ऊर्मिभिः waves, नृत्यन्तमिव as if dancing
explanation: As the day was ending and night was setting in, the ocean filled with crocodiles which could catch any animal looked terrific and its waves seemed as if it were laughing and dancing.

shloka_text: चन्द्रोदये समुद्भूतं प्रतिचन्द्रसमाकुलम् । चण्डानिलमहाग्राहैः कीर्णं तिमितिमिङ्गिलैः ।।6.4.114।।
transliteration: candrodaye samudbhūtaṃ praticandrasamākulam | caṇḍānilamahāgrāhaiḥ kīrṇaṃ timitimiṅgilaiḥ
translation: चन्द्रोदये at the time of moon rise, समुद्भूतम् lofty rising, प्रति चन्द्रसमाकुलम् with reflections of several images of moon, चण्डानिलमहाग्राहैः  huge  dark swift crocodiles, तिमितिमिङ्गिलैः huge fish called Timingalam which swallows small fish(Timi), कीर्णम् scattering
explanation: At the time of the moon rise, the lofty ocean inhabited by dark swift crocodiles, huge Timingala fish scattered in it was rising up with several images of moon reflected in its water.

shloka_text: दीप्तभोगैरिवाकीर्णं भुजङ्गैर्वरुणालयम् । अवगाढं महासत्त्वैर्नानाशैलसमाकुलम् । सुदुर्गं दुर्गमार्गं तमगाध मसुरालयम् ।।6.4.115।।
transliteration: dīptabhogairivākīrṇaṃ bhujaṅgairvaruṇālayam | avagāḍhaṃ mahāsattvairnānāśailasamākulam | sudurgaṃ durgamārgaṃ tamagādha masurālayam
translation: दीप्तभोगैरिव adored with the glowing hoods,भुजङ्गेः serpents, आकीर्णम्  filled with hordes, वरुणालयम् abode of Varuna, महासत्त्वै: huge  snakes, अवगाढम् under water, नानाशैलसमाकुलम् different kinds mountains, सुदुर्गम् very difficult, दुर्गमार्गम् difficult path, अगाधम् deep, मसुरालयम् fathomless abode of rakshasas
explanation: Filled with serpents glowing with flaming gems on hoods, the abode of Varuna (was like underworld) with huge snakes and different mountains under water is a difficult path inaccessible and a fathomless abode of rakshasas (vanaras thought).

shloka_text: मकरैर्नागभोगैश्च विगाढा वातलोलिताः । उत्पेतुश्च निपेतुश्च प्रवृद्धा जलराशयः ।।6.4.116।।
transliteration: makarairnāgabhogaiśca vigāḍhā vātalolitāḥ | utpetuśca nipetuśca pravṛddhā jalarāśayaḥ
translation: मकरैः sea animals (like sharks and crocodiles), नागभोगैश्च swarmed with serpents, विगाढाः with force, वातलोलिताः  stormy,प्रवृद्धाः rising, जलराशयः huge volumes of water, उत्पेतुश्च jumping, निपेतुश्च throwing up and down
explanation: Swarmed with sea animals like sharks and crocodiles and serpents were jumping with huge volumes of water rising and down with force by the stormy wind.

shloka_text: अग्निचूर्णमिवाविद्धं भास्वराम्बुमहोरगम् । सुरारिविषयं घोरं पाताळविषमं सदा ।।6.4.117।।
transliteration: agnicūrṇamivāviddhaṃ bhāsvarāmbumahoragam | surāriviṣayaṃ ghoraṃ pātāḻaviṣamaṃ sadā
translation: अविद्धम् penetrated, अग्निचूर्णमिव like sparks of fire, भास्वराम्बुमहोरगम्the drops of water in the sea, सदा  as though, सुरारिविषयं the domain of snakes, घोरम् terrific, पाताळविषमं like the pataala (underworld)
explanation: The sea that was the domain of snakes was shining as though sparks of fire from the sky penetrated the drops of sea water.

shloka_text: सागरं चाम्बरप्रख्यमम्बरं सागरोपमम् । सागरं चाम्बरं चेति निर्विशेष मदृश्यत ।।6.4.118।।
transliteration: sāgaraṃ cāmbaraprakhyamambaraṃ sāgaropamam | sāgaraṃ cāmbaraṃ ceti nirviśeṣa madṛśyata
translation: सागरम् the ocean, अम्बरप्रख्यम्  resembling the sky, अम्बरम् sky, सागरोपमम् like the ocean, सागरं च and the ocean, अम्बरं चेति like the sky identical, निर्विशेषम् not at all, अदृश्यत not appeared
explanation: The ocean resembled the sky and the sky like the ocean were identical as no difference appeared.

shloka_text: सम्पृक्तं नभसाप्यम्भस्सम्पृक्तं च नभोऽम्भसा । तादृग्रूपेच दृश्यते तारारत्नसमाकुले ।।6.4.119।।
transliteration: sampṛktaṃ nabhasāpyambhassampṛktaṃ ca nabho'mbhasā | tādṛgrūpeca dṛśyate tārāratnasamākule
translation: अम्भः water, नभसा of the sky, सम्पृक्तम् close to each other, तारारत्नसमाकुले covered with stars and gems, तादृग्रूपे those two, दृश्येते appeared
explanation: The ocean and the sky filled with gems and stars respectively appeared alike.

shloka_text: समुत्पतितमेघस्य वीचिमालाकुलस्य च । विशेषो न द्वयोरासीत्सागरस्याम्बरस्य च ।।6.4.120।।
transliteration: samutpatitameghasya vīcimālākulasya ca | viśeṣo na dvayorāsītsāgarasyāmbarasya ca
translation: समुत्पतितमेघस्य the rising clouds, सागरस्य of the ocean, वीचिमालाकुलस्य the moving waves, अम्बरस्य and that of sky, द्वयोः both, विशेषः distinguishing between,नासीत् was not there
explanation: There was no distinction between the sky with rising clouds and the ocean with moving waves.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यैराहता स्सक्ता स्सस्वनुर्भीमनिस्स्वनाः । ऊर्मयस्सिन्धुराजस्य महाभेर्य इवाहवे ।।6.4.121।।
transliteration: anyonyairāhatā ssaktā ssasvanurbhīmanissvanāḥ | ūrmayassindhurājasya mahābherya ivāhave
translation: अन्योन्यैः one to the other, सक्ताः striking each other, आहताः beaten, भीमनिस्सनाः  frightening sound, सिन्धुराजस्य the ocean's, ऊर्मयः waves, हवे challenging each other , महाभेर्य इव like the blowing of horns of war, सस्वनुः made noise
explanation: The waves of the ocean striking each other making frightening sounds like the blowing of war horns seemed as if challenging each other.

shloka_text: रत्नौघ जलसन्नादं विषक्तमिव वायुना । उत्पतन्तमिव क्रुद्धं यादोगणसमाकुलम् ।।6.4.122।। ददृशुस्ते महोत्साह वाताहतजलाशयम् । अनिलोद्धूतमाकाशे प्रवल्गन्त ममिवोर्मिभिः ।।6.4.123।।
transliteration: ratnaugha jalasannādaṃ viṣaktamiva vāyunā | utpatantamiva kruddhaṃ yādogaṇasamākulam  dadṛśuste mahotsāha vātāhatajalāśayam | aniloddhūtamākāśe pravalganta mamivormibhiḥ
translation: महोत्साह with great enthusiasm, ते they, रत्नौघजलसन्नादम् the sound of gems and water, वायुना  by the cause of the wind , विषक्तमिव  concentrated, क्रुद्धमिव   as if infuriated , उत्पतन्तम् rising up, यादोगणसमाकुलम् the abode of animals filled with water, वाताहतजलाशयम्  the ocean, आकाशे of the sky, अनिलोद्धूतम् the vanaras, ऊर्मिभिः even the waves, प्रवल्गन्तम् talking, इव like, ददृशुः appeared
explanation: The enthusiastic vanaras saw the sea inhabited by animals filled with gems and water concentrated in one place rising to the sky, as though infuriated. The rising of the waves (the noise) of the ocean by the cause of wind seemed as if they were talking about.

shloka_text: रत्नौघ जलसन्नादं विषक्तमिव वायुना । उत्पतन्तमिव क्रुद्धं यादोगणसमाकुलम् ।।6.4.122।। ददृशुस्ते महोत्साह वाताहतजलाशयम् । अनिलोद्धूतमाकाशे प्रवल्गन्त ममिवोर्मिभिः ।।6.4.123।।
transliteration: ratnaugha jalasannādaṃ viṣaktamiva vāyunā | utpatantamiva kruddhaṃ yādogaṇasamākulam  dadṛśuste mahotsāha vātāhatajalāśayam | aniloddhūtamākāśe pravalganta mamivormibhiḥ
translation: महोत्साह with great enthusiasm, ते they, रत्नौघजलसन्नादम् the sound of gems and water, वायुना  by the cause of the wind , विषक्तमिव  concentrated, क्रुद्धमिव   as if infuriated , उत्पतन्तम् rising up, यादोगणसमाकुलम् the abode of animals filled with water, वाताहतजलाशयम्  the ocean, आकाशे of the sky, अनिलोद्धूतम् the vanaras, ऊर्मिभिः even the waves, प्रवल्गन्तम् talking, इव like, ददृशुः appeared
explanation: The enthusiastic vanaras saw the sea inhabited by animals filled with gems and water concentrated in one place rising to the sky, as though infuriated. The rising of the waves (the noise) of the ocean by the cause of wind seemed as if they were talking about.

shloka_text: ततो विस्मयमापन्ना हरयो ददृशुर्हरयस्तदा । भ्रान्तोर्मिजालसन्नादं प्रलोलमिव सागरम् ।।6.4.124।।
transliteration: tato vismayamāpannā harayo dadṛśurharayastadā | bhrāntormijālasannādaṃ pralolamiva sāgaram
translation: तदा then, तत्र there, हरयः vanaras, भ्रान्तोर्मिजालसन्नादम् the noise of the  rolling waves, प्रलोलमिव as if highly agitated, सागरम् ocean, विस्मयम् wonderstruck, आपन्नाः distressed, ददृशुः saw
explanation: The vanaras were wonder struck when they saw the ocean that was noisy with rolling waves as if it was highly agitated and distressed. ।।इत्यार्षे वाल्मीकीये श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये युद्धकाण्डे चतुर्थस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the fourth Sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सातुनीलेनविधिवत्स्वारक्षासुसमाहिता । सागरस्योत्तरेतीरेसाधुसेनानिवेशिता ।।6.5.1।।
transliteration: sātunīlenavidhivatsvārakṣāsusamāhitā | sāgarasyottaretīresādhusenāniveśitā
translation: नीलेन: by Nila, विधिवत्:  as per tradition, स्वारक्षा: their guard, सुसमाहिता: collected there, सा: that, सेना: army, सागरस्य: at the sea, उत्तरेतीरे: northern shore, साधु: successfully, निवेशिता: made to reside
explanation: Nila settled the army successfully by making them reside on the northern shore of the sea, as per tradition.
comments: Rama is reminded of Sita while talking to Lakshmana and gets immersed in grief.

shloka_text: मैन्दश्चद्विविदश्चोभौतत्रवानरपुङ्गवौ । विचेरतुश्चतांसेनांरक्षार्थंसर्वतोदिशम् ।।6.5.2।।
transliteration: maindaścadvividaścobhautatravānarapuṅgavau | viceratuścatāṃsenāṃrakṣārthaṃsarvatodiśam
translation: तत्र: then, वानरपुङ्गवौ: the best of the vanaras, मैन्दश्च: Mainda and, द्विविदश्चैव: with Dwivida, उभौ: both, रक्षार्थम्: for safeguarding, सर्वतोदिशम्: in all directions, तांसेनाम्: that army, विचेरतुः moving about
explanation: Dwivida and Mainda, the best of the vanaras, went about in all directions for safeguarding the army.

shloka_text: निविष्टायांतुसेनायांतीरेनदनदीपतेः । पार्श्वस्थंलक्ष्मणंदृष्टवारामोवचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.5.3।।
transliteration: niviṣṭāyāṃtusenāyāṃtīrenadanadīpateḥ | pārśvasthaṃlakṣmaṇaṃdṛṣṭavārāmovacanamabravīt
translation: नदनदीपतेः lord of rivers and streams (the ocean), तीरे: shore, सेनायाम्: when the army, निविष्टायाम्: after having settled down, रामः Rama, पार्श्वस्थम्: beside, लक्ष्मणम्: at Lakshmana, दृष्टवा: seeing, वचनम्: these words, अब्रवीत्: spoke
explanation: After the army had settled down on the shores of the lord of rivers (sea), Rama spoke to Lakshmana who stood beside him.

shloka_text: शोकश्चकिलकालेनगच्छताह्यपगच्छति । ममचापश्यतःकान्तामहन्यहनिवर्धते ।।6.5.4।।
transliteration: śokaścakilakālenagacchatāhyapagacchati | mamacāpaśyataḥkāntāmahanyahanivardhate
translation: शोकः grief, गच्छता: goes, कालेन: as time passes, अपगच्छतिकिल: indeed progressing, कान्ताम्: beloved, अपश्यतः unable to see, ममच: for me, अहन्यहनि: day by day, वर्धते: increases
explanation: As time passes, grief passes away. However my sorrow is progressing day by day being unable to see my beloved.

shloka_text: ﻿नमेदुःखंप्रियादूरेनमेदुःखंहृतेतिवा । एतदेवानुशोचामिवयोस्याह्यतिवर्तते ।।6.5.5।।
transliteration: ﻿nameduḥkhaṃpriyādūrenameduḥkhaṃhṛtetivā | etadevānuśocāmivayosyāhyativartate
translation: ﻿ प्रिया: beloved, दूरे: at distance, मे: my, दुःखम्: grief, न: not, हृतेतिग: is abducted, वामे: or my, दुःखम्: sorrow, न: not, अस्याः her, वयः age, अतिवर्ततेहि: advancing, एतदेव: on this account, अनुशोचामि: I am feeling
explanation: ﻿ There is no grief in me that my beloved is at a distance, nor that she is taken away. Indeed her age is advancing. On this account I am feeling for her.

shloka_text: वाहिवातयतःकान्तातांस्पृष्टवामामपिस्पृश । त्वयिमेगात्रसंस्पर्शश्चन्द्रेदृष्टिसमागमः ।।6.5.6।।
transliteration: vāhivātayataḥkāntātāṃspṛṣṭavāmāmapispṛśa | tvayimegātrasaṃsparśaścandredṛṣṭisamāgamaḥ
translation: वात: oh Wind, कान्ता: beloved, यतः that place, वाहि: carry, ताम्: her, स्पृष्टवा: touched, मामपि: me too, स्पृश: touch, मे: my, गात्रसंस्पर्शः beloved's touch of my body like, त्वयि: by you, दृष्टिसमागमः contact with eyes, चन्द्रे: through moon
explanation: O Wind Touch that place where my beloved is and touch me as it will give me the same feeling as my beloved's touch. Through the moon I will get her eye contact too.

shloka_text: तन्मेदहतिगात्राणिविषंपीतमिवाशये । हानाथेतिप्रियासामांह्रियमाणायदब्रवीत् ।।6.5.7।।
transliteration: tanmedahatigātrāṇiviṣaṃpītamivāśaye | hānāthetipriyāsāmāṃhriyamāṇāyadabravīt
translation: ह्रियमाणा: being carried away, साप्रिया: she my beloved, हा नाथ इति: saying 'Ha beloved', अब्रवीत्: uttered इतियत्: this at that time, तत्: then, पीतम्: drunk, विषम् इव: like poison, आशये: my stomach, मे: me, गात्राणि: my body, दहति: is burning
explanation: While being carried away that beloved of mine would have cried aloud saying 'oh my lord'. This thought is burning my body as though I have consumed poison in my stomach.

shloka_text: तद्वियोगेन्धनवतातच्चिन्ताविपुलार्चिषा । रात्रिंदिवंशरीरंमेदह्यतेमदनाग्निना ।।6.5.8।।
transliteration: tadviyogendhanavatātaccintāvipulārciṣā | rātriṃdivaṃśarīraṃmedahyatemadanāgninā
translation: तद्वियोगेन्धनवता: the separation from her as fuel, तच्चिन्ता: the thought about her, विपुलार्चिषा: extensive flames, मदनाग्निना: by the fire of  love, मे: my, शरीरम्: body, रात्रिंदिवम्: day and night, दह्यते: is burning
explanation: The pain of separation from her is working as fuel and the thought about hers is engulfing me as extensive flame and burning my body day and night.

shloka_text: अवगाह्यर्णवंस्वप्स्येसौमित्रेभवताविना । कथञ्चित्प्रज्वलन्कामस्समांसुप्तंजलेदहेत् ।।6.5.9।।
transliteration: avagāhyarṇavaṃsvapsyesaumitrebhavatāvinā | kathañcitprajvalankāmassamāṃsuptaṃjaledahet
translation: सौमित्रे: O Saumitri, सभवताविना: without you, अर्णवम्: into the ocean, अवगाह्य: plunging, स्वप्स्ये: will lie down, कथञ्चित्: probably, जले: in water, सुप्तम्: be sleeping, माम् प्रज्वलन्: to burn me, कामः god of love, नदहेत्: will not be able to consume me
explanation: O Saumitri Plunging into water alone I will lie down. Probably then the god of love will not be able to consume me while sleeping.

shloka_text: बह्वेतत्कामयानस्यशक्यमेतेनजीवितुम् । यदहंसाचवामोरूरेकांधरणिमाश्रितौ ।।6.5.10।।
transliteration: bahvetatkāmayānasyaśakyametenajīvitum | yadahaṃsācavāmorūrekāṃdharaṇimāśritau
translation: अहम्: I, सा: her, वामोरूःच: of charming thighs, एकाम्: one, धरणिम्: land, आश्रितौइतियत्: this way seeking refuge, कामयानस्य: desiring, बहु: very much, एतेन: because of that, जीवितुम्: survival, शक्यम्: will be possible
explanation: Me and Sita are seeking refuge on the same land indeed. Because of that only survival is possible for me, who is desiring for her very much.

shloka_text: केदारस्येवकेदारस्सोदकस्यनिरूदकः । उपस्नेहेनजीवामिजीवन्तींयच्छृणोमिताम् ।।6.5.11।।
transliteration: kedārasyevakedārassodakasyanirūdakaḥ | upasnehenajīvāmijīvantīṃyacchṛṇomitām
translation: ताम्: she, जीवन्तीम्: is living यत्: that, शृणोमि: I hearing, सोदकस्य: with water, केदारस्य: like a paddy field, उपस्नेहेन: getting wet, निरूदकः without water, केदारःइवजीवामि: am living like crop with water
explanation: I am living only because of hearing about her survival, just as a paddy field without water gets wet by the proximity of a neighboring paddy field with water.

shloka_text: कदानुखलुसुश्रोणींशतपत्त्रायतेक्षणाम् । विजित्यशत्रून्द्रक्ष्यामिसीतास्फीतामिवश्रियम् ।।6.5.12।।
transliteration: kadānukhalusuśroṇīṃśatapattrāyatekṣaṇām | vijityaśatrūndrakṣyāmisītāsphītāmivaśriyam
translation: शत्रून्: enemies, विजित्य: winning, सुश्रोणीम्: lady with charming limbs, शतपत्रायतेक्षणाम्: of large beautiful eyes like lotus petals, स्फीताम्: abundance of, श्रियमिव: like fortune, सीताम्: Sita, कदानुखलु: when indeed, द्रक्ष्यामि: will be able to see
explanation: When will I be able to win the enemies and see that Sita of charming limbs, with large and beautiful eyes like lotus petals, who is like an abundance of fortune?

shloka_text: कदानुचारुबिम्बोष्ठंतस्याःपद्ममिवाननम् । ईषदुन्नम्यपास्यामिरसायनमिवातुरः ।।6.5.13।।
transliteration: kadānucārubimboṣṭhaṃtasyāḥpadmamivānanam | īṣadunnamyapāsyāmirasāyanamivāturaḥ
translation: चारुबिम्बोष्ठम्: beautiful lips like Bimba fruit, पद्ममिव: lotus like, तस्याः her, आननम्: face, ईषत्: slightly, उन्नाम्य: lifting, आतुरः one who is afflicted, रसायनमिव: like a sweet drink, कदा: when, पास्यामि: shall I drink?
explanation: I do not know when I will lift her lotuslike face slightly and drink her beautiful lips like an afflicted man drinks sweet juice.

shloka_text: ﻿तस्यात्तुसंहितौपीनौस्तनौतालफलोपमौ । कदानुखलुसोत्कम्पौश्लिष्यन्त्यामांभजिष्यत: ।।6.5.14।।
transliteration: ﻿tasyāttusaṃhitaupīnaustanautālaphalopamau | kadānukhalusotkampauśliṣyantyāmāṃbhajiṣyata:
translation: ﻿ शिलष्ययन्त्या: desire to cling to, तस्याः her, सहितौ: along with, तुपीनौ: that plump, तालफलोपमौ: like the Palmyra fruit, सोत्कम्पौ: eagerly, तौ: those, स्तनौ: breasts, माम्: me, कदाखलु: when indeed, भजिष्यथ: will I enjoy
explanation: ﻿ Indeed I am eager to embrace my chest with hers like the palmyra -fruit trees hold the fruits.When will it happen?

shloka_text: सानूनमसितापाङ्गीरक्षोमध्यगतासती । मन्नाथानाथहीनेवत्रातारंनाधिगच्छति ।।6.5.15।।
transliteration: sānūnamasitāpāṅgīrakṣomadhyagatāsatī | mannāthānāthahīnevatrātāraṃnādhigacchati
translation: असितापाङ्गी: lady of dark eyes, मन्नाधा: has me as her lord, सा: she, रक्षोमध्यगता: in the midst of Rakshasas, सती: wife, नूनम्: surely, नाथहीनेव: emaciated being away from husband, त्रातारम्: protector, नाधिगच्छति: not getting
explanation: That darkeyed lady (Sita), even though she has me (husband), is in the midst of rakshasas. Surely she is sad and emaciated being away from her husband, without a protector.

shloka_text: कथंजनकरजस्यदुहिताममचप्रिया । राक्षसीमध्यगाशेतेस्नुषादशरथस्यच ।।6.5.16।।
transliteration: kathaṃjanakarajasyaduhitāmamacapriyā | rākṣasīmadhyagāśetesnuṣādaśarathasyaca
translation: जनकराजस्य: king Janaka's, दुहिता: daughter, ममप्रिया: my beloved wife, दशरथस्य: Dasaratha's, स्नुषा: daughterinlaw, राक्षसीमध्यगा: in the midst of rakshasas, कथम्: how, शेते: sleeping
explanation: My beloved is king Janaka's daughter and daughterinlaw of Dasaratha. Yet she is sleeping amid Rakshasas. How is it?

shloka_text: कदाऽविक्षोभ्यरक्षांसिसाविधूयोत्पतिष्यति । विधूयजलदान्नीलान् शशिरेखाशरत्स्विव ।।6.5.17।।
transliteration: kadā'vikṣobhyarakṣāṃsisāvidhūyotpatiṣyati | vidhūyajaladānnīlān śaśirekhāśaratsviva
translation: कदा: when will, शरत्स्तुइव: like in autumn season, शशिरेखा: crescent moon, नीलान्: dark, जलदान्: clouds, विधूयइव: like pushing, सा: she, अविक्षोभ्य: unshakeable, रक्षांसि: Rakshasas, विधूय: pushing, उत्पतिष्यति: will come out
explanation: When will she come out pushing the Rakshasas like the crescent moon comes out pushing the dark clouds in autumn?

shloka_text: स्वभावतनुकानूनंशोकेनानशनेनच । भूयस्तनुतरासीतादेशकालविपर्ययात् ।।6.5.18।।
transliteration: svabhāvatanukānūnaṃśokenānaśanenaca | bhūyastanutarāsītādeśakālaviparyayāt
translation: स्वभावतनुका: by nature slim, सीता: Sita, देशकालविपर्ययात्: due to unfavorable time and space, शोकेन: in grief, अनशनेन: due to abstaining from eating, नूनम्: surely, भूयः would be, तनुतरा: slender
explanation: Sita who is by nature slim would surely be slender due to abstaining from eating, unfavorable time and location.

shloka_text: कदानुराक्षसेन्द्रस्यनिधायोरसिसायकान् । सीतांप्रत्याहरिष्यामिशोकमुत्सृज्यमानसम् ।।6.5.19।।
transliteration: kadānurākṣasendrasyanidhāyorasisāyakān | sītāṃpratyāhariṣyāmiśokamutsṛjyamānasam
translation: राक्षसेन्द्रस्य: rakshasa king's, निधायोरसि: into the chest, सायकान्: arrows, सीतां: Sita, प्रत्याहरिष्यामि: will get back, शोकमुत्सृज्य: casting off grief, मानसम्: from my mind, कदानु: indeed
explanation: Indeed by shooting arrows into the chest of rakshasa king, when will I get back Sita and cast off grief from my mind.

shloka_text: कदानुखलुमांसाध्वीसीतासुरसुतोपमा । सोत्कण्ठाकण्ठमालम्ब्यमोक्ष्यत्यानन्दजंजलम् ।।6.5.20।।
transliteration: kadānukhalumāṃsādhvīsītāsurasutopamā | sotkaṇṭhākaṇṭhamālambyamokṣyatyānandajaṃjalam
translation: साध्वी: chaste woman, सुरसुतोपमा: like the daughter of the gods, सीता: Sita, सोत्कण्ठा: with an excited longing, माम्: me, कण्ठम्: neck, आलम्ब्य clinging, कदाखलु: indeed, आनन्दजम्: of joy, जलम्: water(here tears), मोक्ष्यति: will shed
explanation: When will Sita, the chaste woman, who is like the daughter of Gods, cling to my neck, and indeed shed tears of joy?

shloka_text: कदाशोकमिमंघोरंमैथिलीविप्रयोगजम् । सहसाविप्रमोक्ष्यामिवासश्शुक्लेतरंयथा ।।6.5.21।।
transliteration: kadāśokamimaṃghoraṃmaithilīviprayogajam | sahasāvipramokṣyāmivāsaśśukletaraṃyathā
translation: मैथिली: Mythili, विप्रयोगजम्: born out of separation, घोरम्: terrible, इमम्: this, शोकम्: grief, शुक्लेतरम्: soiled, वासःयथा: like a garment, कदा: when, सहसा: suddenly, विप्रमोक्ष्यामि: shall I abandon
explanation: When will I get rid of this terrible grief of separation from Mythili for good, just like discarding a soiled garment?

shloka_text: एवंविलपतस्तस्यतत्ररामस्यधीमतः । दिनक्षयान्मन्दवपुर्भास्करोऽस्तमुपागतः ।।6.5.22।।
transliteration: evaṃvilapatastasyatatrarāmasyadhīmataḥ | dinakṣayānmandavapurbhāskaro'stamupāgataḥ
translation: धीमतः sagacious, तस्य: his, रामस्य: Rama's, तत्र: there, एवम्: in that way, विलपतः wailing, दिनक्षयात्: due to the ending of the day, मन्दवपुः dim, भास्करः sun's light, अस्तम्: west, उपागतः descended
explanation: While sagacious Rama was wailing in that way the day came to an end with the sun descending to the west.

shloka_text: आश्वासितोलक्ष्मणेनरामस्सन्ध्यामुपासत । स्मरन्कमलपत्राक्षींसीतांशोकाकुलीकृतः ।।6.5.23।।
transliteration: āśvāsitolakṣmaṇenarāmassandhyāmupāsata | smarankamalapatrākṣīṃsītāṃśokākulīkṛtaḥ
translation: कमलपत्राक्षीम्: lotus petal eyed, सीताम्: Sita, स्मरन्: remembering, शोकाकुलीकृतः distracted with grief, रामः Rama, लक्ष्मणेन: by Lakshmana, आश्वासितः comforted, सन्ध्याम्: evening prayers, उपासत: set in
explanation: Remembering the lotus petal eyed Sita, Rama who was distracted with grief, comforted by Lakshmana offered evening prayers. ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्दकाण्डेपञ्चमस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the fifth Sarga of Yuddhakanda of the first epic, the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: लङ्कायांतुकृतंकर्मघोरंदृष्टवाभयावहम् । राक्षसेन्द्रोहनुमताशक्रेणेवमहात्मना ।।6.6.1।। अब्रवीद्राक्षसान्  सर्वान्ह्रियाकिञ्चिदवाङ्मुखः ।
transliteration: laṅkāyāṃtukṛtaṃkarmaghoraṃdṛṣṭavābhayāvaham | rākṣasendrohanumatāśakreṇevamahātmanā  abravīdrākṣasān  sarvānhriyākiñcidavāṅmukhaḥ |
translation: महात्मना: great soul, शक्रेणेव: like Indra in might, हनुमता: Hanuman, लङ्कयाम् at Lanka, कृतम् carried out, भयावहम् terrifying, घोरम् dreadful, कर्म: action, दृष्टवा: considering, राक्षसेन्द्रः Lord of Rakshasas, ह्रियाकिञ्चित् a bit shy आवाङ्मुखः bending the head down, सर्वान् all, राक्षसान् Rakshasas, अब्रवीत् addressed.
explanation: Considering the terrifying, dreadful action that was carried by the great soul Hanuman who was like Indra in might, the Lord of Rakshasas felt a bit shy and bending down his head addressed all Rakshasas.
comments: At Lanka,Ravana holds consultations with the rakshasas about winning over Rama.

shloka_text: धर्षिताचप्रविष्टाचलङ्कादुष्प्रसहापुरी ।।6.6.2।। तेनवानरमात्रेणदृष्टासीताचजानकी ।
transliteration: dharṣitācapraviṣṭācalaṅkāduṣprasahāpurī  tenavānaramātreṇadṛṣṭāsītācajānakī |
translation: तेन that, वानरमात्रेणतेन: after all a monkey in size, दुष्प्रसहा: difficult to enter, लङ्कापुरी: city of Lanka, धर्षिताच: destroyed, प्रविष्टाच: and entered जानकी: Janaka's daughter, Janaki, सीताच: and Sita दृष्टा: saw.
explanation: "(Hanuman) After all a monkey in size, entered the inaccessible city of Lanka, destroyed it and saw Sita, daughter of king of Janaka."

shloka_text: प्रासादोधर्षितश्चैत्यःप्रवराराक्षसाहताः ।।6.6.3।। आविलाचपुरीलङ्कासर्वाहनुमताकृता ।
transliteration: prāsādodharṣitaścaityaḥpravarārākṣasāhatāḥ  āvilācapurīlaṅkāsarvāhanumatākṛtā |
translation: हनुमता: Hanuman, चैत्यप्रासादः huge mansions, धर्षितः destroyed, प्रवराः topmost, राक्षसृः Rakshasas, हताः killed, सर्वा: all, लङ्कापुरी: the city of Lanka, अविला: shattered, कृता: did.
explanation: "Hanuman destroyed huge mansions, killed topmost Rakshasas and shattered all the city of Lanka."

shloka_text: किंकरिष्यामिभद्रंवोकिंवायुक्तमनन्तरम् ।।6.6.4।। उच्यतांनस्समर्थंयत्कृतंचसुकृतंभवेत् ।
transliteration: kiṃkariṣyāmibhadraṃvokiṃvāyuktamanantaram  ucyatāṃnassamarthaṃyatkṛtaṃcasukṛtaṃbhavet |
translation: वः and now, भद्रम् best, किम्  What is, करिष्यामि: should we do, अनन्तरम् ultimately, किं: what, वा: to you, युक्तम् advisable, नः for us, यत् that which, समर्थम् effective, कृतम् strategy, सुकृतम् that which is good, भवेत् for us, उच्यताम् you may suggest.
explanation: "What is the best thing to do now? What should we do ultimately? What is advisable to do? What strategy is effective? You may suggest that which is good for us."

shloka_text: मन्त्रमूलंचविजयंप्रवदन्तिमनस्विनः ।।6.6.5।। तस्मद्वैरोचयेमन्त्रंरामंप्रतिमहाबलाः ।
transliteration: mantramūlaṃcavijayaṃpravadantimanasvinaḥ  tasmadvairocayemantraṃrāmaṃpratimahābalāḥ |
translation: महाबलाः of great strength, विजयम् victory, मन्त्रमूलम् through wise counsel, मनस्विनः wise elders, प्रवदन्ति: say, तस्मात् therefore, रामंप्रति: in case of Rama, मन्त्रम् advice, रोचम् thinking of seeking.
explanation: "O mighty Rakshasas Wise elders say that through wise counsel victory is possible. Therefore, in the case of Rama I am thinking of seeking your advice."

shloka_text: त्रिविधाःपुरुषालोकेउत्तमाधममध्यमाः ।।6.6.6।। तेषांतुसमवेतानांगुणदोषौवदाम्यहम् ।
transliteration: trividhāḥpuruṣālokeuttamādhamamadhyamāḥ  teṣāṃtusamavetānāṃguṇadoṣauvadāmyaham |
translation: लोके: in the world, उत्तमाधममध्यमाः good, bad and mediocre, त्रिविधाः three kinds, पुरुषाः men, समवेतानाम् their differences, तेषाम् there, गुणदोषौ: flaws in characteristics, अहम् I, वदामि: will tell.
explanation: "In the world, men are of three kinds  good, mediocre and lowly. It is difficult to know their differences. I will tell you about the flaws in their characteristics."

shloka_text: मन्त्रिभिर्हितसंयुक्तैस्समर्थैर्मन्त्रनिर्णये ।।6.6.7।। मित्रैर्वापिसमानार्थैर्बान्धवैरपिवाधिकैः । सहितोमन्त्रियित्वायःकर्मारम्भान्प्रवर्तयेत् ।।6.6.8।। दैवेचकुरुतेयत्नंतमाहुःपुरुषोत्तमम् ।
transliteration: mantribhirhitasaṃyuktaissamarthairmantranirṇaye  mitrairvāpisamānārthairbāndhavairapivādhikaiḥ | sahitomantriyitvāyaḥkarmārambhānpravartayet  daivecakuruteyatnaṃtamāhuḥpuruṣottamam |
translation: यः he who, हितसंयुक्तेः with wellwishers, मन्न्त्रनिर्णये: who decides with counsel, समर्थैः capable ones, मन्त्रिभिः ministers, समानार्थैः relatives with common interests, मित्रैर्वापि: or friends, अधिकैः very well, बान्धवैर्यापि: or with relatives, सहितः friends, मन्त्रयित्वा: deliberating with, कर्मारम्भान् to begin his work प्रवर्तयेत् before undertaking, दैवेच: with faith in god, यत्नम् makes his attempt, कुरुते: does, तम् him, पुरुषोत्तमम् best among men, आहु: said to be.
explanation: "He who decides, after deliberating with his wellwishers, with capable ministers of good counsel, relatives of common interest or friends before undertaking his task and tries with faith in god is said to be best among men."

shloka_text: मन्त्रिभिर्हितसंयुक्तैस्समर्थैर्मन्त्रनिर्णये ।।6.6.7।। मित्रैर्वापिसमानार्थैर्बान्धवैरपिवाधिकैः । सहितोमन्त्रियित्वायःकर्मारम्भान्प्रवर्तयेत् ।।6.6.8।। दैवेचकुरुतेयत्नंतमाहुःपुरुषोत्तमम् ।
transliteration: mantribhirhitasaṃyuktaissamarthairmantranirṇaye  mitrairvāpisamānārthairbāndhavairapivādhikaiḥ | sahitomantriyitvāyaḥkarmārambhānpravartayet  daivecakuruteyatnaṃtamāhuḥpuruṣottamam |
translation: यः he who, हितसंयुक्तेः with wellwishers, मन्न्त्रनिर्णये: who decides with counsel, समर्थैः capable ones, मन्त्रिभिः ministers, समानार्थैः relatives with common interests, मित्रैर्वापि: or friends, अधिकैः very well, बान्धवैर्यापि: or with relatives, सहितः friends, मन्त्रयित्वा: deliberating with, कर्मारम्भान् to begin his work प्रवर्तयेत् before undertaking, दैवेच: with faith in god, यत्नम् makes his attempt, कुरुते: does, तम् him, पुरुषोत्तमम् best among men, आहु: said to be.
explanation: "He who decides, after deliberating with his wellwishers, with capable ministers of good counsel, relatives of common interest or friends before undertaking his task and tries with faith in god is said to be best among men."

shloka_text: कोऽर्थंविमृशेदेकोधर्मेप्रकुरुतेमनः ।।6.6.9।। कःकार्याणिकुरुतेतमाहुर्मध्यमंनरम् ।
transliteration: ko'rthaṃvimṛśedekodharmeprakurutemanaḥ  kaḥkāryāṇikurutetamāhurmadhyamaṃnaram |
translation: कः alone, अर्थम् thinks, विमृशेत् deliberates with in, एकः alone, धर्मे: duty, मनः in his mind, प्रकुरुते: executes, एकः alone, कार्याणि: tasks, कुरुते: does, तंनरम् that person, मध्यमम् mediocre intermediate one, आहुः is said to be.
explanation: "He who thinks solitarily (not with others), deliberates with in his mind on his duty and executes his tasks, is said to be a (mediocre) a mediocre one."

shloka_text: गुणदोषौवनिशिचत्य त्यक्त्यादैवव्यपाश्रयम् ।।6.6.10।। करिष्यामीतियःकार्यमुपेक्षेत्सनराधमः ।
transliteration: guṇadoṣauvaniśicatya tyaktyādaivavyapāśrayam  kariṣyāmītiyaḥkāryamupekṣetsanarādhamaḥ |
translation: यः he who, गुणदोषौ: merits and de merits, न: not, निश्चित्य: deciding, व्यक्तम् failing to consider, दैवव्यपाश्रयः giving up faith in God, करिष्यामिइति: I will do it, कार्यम् task, उपेक्षेत् begins to do, सः he, नराधमः lowly one among men.
explanation: "He who fails to consider the merits and de merits, decides to do on his own and begins without faith in god saying, 'I' will do it, is a lowly one among men."

shloka_text: यथेमेपुरुषानित्यमुत्तमाधममध्यमाः ।।6.6.11।। वंमन्त्राऽहिविज्ञेयाउत्तमाधममध्यमः ।
transliteration: yathemepuruṣānityamuttamādhamamadhyamāḥ  vaṃmantrā'hivijñeyāuttamādhamamadhyamaḥ |
translation: नित्यम् invariably, इमे: thus, पुरुषाः men, यथा: similarly, उत्तमाधममध्यमाः good, intermediate and lowly people, एवम् in the same way, मन्त्राऽहि: even their counsel, उत्तमाधममध्यमः good, mediocre and lowly kinds, विज्ञेयः you know.
explanation: "Just as among men there are good, intermediate and lowly people invariably their counsel is also of three kinds  good, mediocre and lowly."

shloka_text: ऐकमत्यमुपागम्यशास्त्रदृष्टेनचक्षुषा ।।6.6.12।। मन्त्रिणोयत्रनिरतास्तमाहुर्मन्त्रमुत्तमम् ।
transliteration: aikamatyamupāgamyaśāstradṛṣṭenacakṣuṣā  mantriṇoyatraniratāstamāhurmantramuttamam |
translation: मन्त्रिणः ministers, शास्त्रदृष्टेन: based on Sastras, चक्षुषा: in view, ऐकमत्यम् all of them come to one conclusion, उपागम्य: having come together, यत्र: then निरताः remain attached, तम् such, मन्त्रम् counsel, उत्तमम् best, आहु: said to be.
explanation: "When all ministers are unanimous and come to one conclusion based on sastras, and having come together remain firm, such counsel is said to be the best."

shloka_text: बह्व्योऽपिमतीर्गत्वामन्त्रिणामर्थनिर्णये ।।6.6.13।। पुनर्यत्रैकतांप्राप्तस्समन्त्रोमध्यमस्स्मृतः ।
transliteration: bahvyo'pimatīrgatvāmantriṇāmarthanirṇaye  punaryatraikatāṃprāptassamantromadhyamassmṛtaḥ |
translation: बह्व्य: many, मतीर्गत्वा: due to different points of view, मन्त्रिणाम् ministers, अर्थनिर्णयः in decision, पुनः again, यत्र: that, एकताम् altogether, प्राप्तः attained unanimity, सः that, मन्त्रः adviser, मध्यमः mediocre, स्मृतः vision.
explanation: "The conclusion in which many ministers have different points of view and attain unanimity in decision after meeting different points of view is a mediocre vision."

shloka_text: अन्योन्यमतिमास्थाययत्रसम्प्रतिभाष्यते ।।6.6.14।। नचैकमत्येश्रेयोऽस्तिमन्त्रस्सोऽधमउच्यत ।
transliteration: anyonyamatimāsthāyayatrasampratibhāṣyate  nacaikamatyeśreyo'stimantrasso'dhamaucyata |
translation: यत्रअन्योन्यमतिम् where counsellors with different opinions, आस्थाय: holding on to their individual opinions, सम्प्रतिभाष्यते: speak What pleases them, ऐकमत्ये: unanimous opinion, श्रेयः good outcome, नास्ति: not, सःमन्त्रः such counsel, अधमः a bad one, उच्यते: is said.
explanation: "Where counsellors with different opinions hold on to their individual opinions that pleases them and are not for the outcome of a unanimous decision, such a counsel is said to be bad."

shloka_text: तस्मात्सुमन्त्रितंसाधुभवन्तोमतिसत्तमा: ।।6.6.15।। कार्यंसम्प्रतिपद्यन्तामेतत्कृत्यंमतंमम ।
transliteration: tasmātsumantritaṃsādhubhavantomatisattamā:  kāryaṃsampratipadyantāmetatkṛtyaṃmataṃmama |
translation: तस्मात् on account of that, मतिसत्तामाः wise ones, भवन्तः your, सुमन्त्रितम् thinking over well, साधु: rightly, कार्यम् task, सम्प्रतिपद्यन्ताम् that which has to be done, एतत् all that, मम: to me, कृत्यम् required action, मतम् I need.
explanation: "On account of that, O wise ones Think over very well, rightly of the task to be done and determine the action required by me now."

shloka_text: वानराणांहिधीराणांसहस्रैःपरिवारितः ।।6.6.16।। रामोऽभ्येतिपुरीलङ्कामस्माकमुपरोधकः ।
transliteration: vānarāṇāṃhidhīrāṇāṃsahasraiḥparivāritaḥ  rāmo'bhyetipurīlaṅkāmasmākamuparodhakaḥ |
translation: रामः Rama, धीराणाम् valorous, वानराणाम् Vanaras, सहस्रैः thousands, परिवारितः to besiege, अस्माकम् us, उपरोधकः is approaching, लङ्कांपुरीम् city of Lanka, अभ्येति: reaching.
explanation: Accompanied by thousands of Vanaras, Rama is approaching to besiege us and reaching the city of Lanka.

shloka_text: तरिष्यतिचसुव्यक्तंराघवस्सागरंसुखम् ।।6.6.17।। तरसायुक्तरूपेणसानुजस्सबलानुगः ।
transliteration: tariṣyaticasuvyaktaṃrāghavassāgaraṃsukham  tarasāyuktarūpeṇasānujassabalānugaḥ |
translation: राघवः Rama, युक्तरूपेण: worthy of his might, तरसा: speedily, सानुजः his brother, सबलानुगः and his army, सागरम् ocean, सुव्यक्तम् it is clear, सुखम् easily, तरिष्यतिच: will be able to cross.
explanation: "Rama who is worthy of his might, accompanied by his brother and army will be able to cross the ocean speedily and easily."

shloka_text: समुद्रमुच्छोषयतिवीर्येणान्यत्करोतिवा ।।6.6.18।। अस्मिन्नेवंगतेकार्येविरुद्धेवानरैस्सह । हितंपुरेचसैन्येचसर्वसम्मन्त्रयतांमम ।।6.6.19।।
transliteration: samudramucchoṣayativīryeṇānyatkarotivā  asminnevaṃgatekāryeviruddhevānaraissaha | hitaṃpurecasainyecasarvasammantrayatāṃmama
translation: समुद्रम् ocean, उच्चोषयति: dry up, वीर्येण: out of his power, अन्यद्वा: or something else, करोति: will do, वानरैः Vanara, सह: with, विरुद्धे: encounters, अस्मिन् when his army, एवंगते: has set out that way, कार्ये: task, मम: me, पुरे: for the city, सैन्ये: army, हितम् benefiting, सर्वम् for all, सम्मन्त्रयताम् advise me a plan
explanation: Rama may dry up the ocean or do something else out of his power. If Vanaras come and encounter us, we will clash with him. When his army has set out that way, you may advise me of a plan that benefits the army and city of Lanka." ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेषष्ठमस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the sixth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: इत्युक्ताराक्षसेन्द्रेणराक्षसास्तेमहाबलाः । ऊचुःप्रान्जलयःसर्वेरावणंराक्षसेश्वरम् ।।6.7.1।।
transliteration: ityuktārākṣasendreṇarākṣasāstemahābalāḥ | ūcuḥprānjalayaḥsarverāvaṇaṃrākṣaseśvaram
translation: राक्षसेन्द्रेण: to the leader of Rakshasas, सर्वे: all Rakshasas, महाबलाः of mighty strength प्रान्जलयः greeting with folded hand s, राक्षसास्ते: the Rakshasas, राक्षसेश्वरम्: Lord of Rakshasas, रावणं: to Ravana ऊचुः having heard, इत्युक्ता: thus spoke.
explanation: All the Rakshasas of mighty strength, having heard the Lord of Rakshasas, thus spoke to their leader, greeting with folded hands.
comments: All the Rakshasas praise their might and inspire confidence in Ravana.

shloka_text: द्विषत्पक्षमविज्ञायनीतिबाह्यास्त्वबुद्धयः । राजन्परिघशक्त्यृष्टिशूलपट्टिशकुन्तलम् ।।6.7.2।।
transliteration: dviṣatpakṣamavijñāyanītibāhyāstvabuddhayaḥ | rājanparighaśaktyṛṣṭiśūlapaṭṭiśakuntalam
translation: राजन्: o king परिघ: iron bars, शक्त्यृष्टि: javelins, शूलपट्टि: arrows, and swords, शकुन्तलम्: sharp edged spears, द्विषत्पक्षम: double edged swords, अविज्ञाय: not  knowing, नीतिबाह्या: political intelligence, स्त्वबुद्धयः submitted by themselves.
explanation: "O King The ogres are not having political intelligence. They have submitted themselves, even though they are mighty and are having iron bars, javelins, sharp edged spears, and doubleedged swords."

shloka_text: इत्युक्ताराक्षसेन्द्रेणराक्षसास्तेमहाबलाः । ऊचुःप्रान्जलयःसर्वेरावणंराक्षसेश्वरम् ।।6.7.3।। द्विषत्पक्षमविज्ञायनीतिबाह्यास्त्वबुद्धयः ।
transliteration: ityuktārākṣasendreṇarākṣasāstemahābalāḥ | ūcuḥprānjalayaḥsarverāvaṇaṃrākṣaseśvaram  dviṣatpakṣamavijñāyanītibāhyāstvabuddhayaḥ |
translation: इत्युक्ता: having spoken thus, राक्षसेन्द्रेण: by the Lord of Rakshasas, राक्षसास्ते    (तेराक्षसा ): those Rakshasa, महाबलाः who were very strong, द्विषत्पक्षं: the enemy's side अविज्ञाय: ignorant about, नीतिबाह्या: without having political wisdom,  (नीतिबाह्यास्त्वबुद्धयःनीतिबाह्या:  तु  अबुद्धय:) अबुद्धय: not intelligent, ऊचुः told, प्रान्जलयः with folded hands, रावणं: to Ravana, राक्षसेश्वरम्: the king of Rakshasas.
explanation: The Lord of Rakshasas having spoken like that, to the Rakshasas, who were very strong, but ignorant about the enemy's strength and who were not endowed with political wisdom, spoke to Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, the following words with folded hands.

shloka_text: राजन्परिघशक्त्यृष्टिशूलपट्टिशकुन्तलम् ।।6.7.4।।
transliteration: rājanparighaśaktyṛṣṭiśūlapaṭṭiśakuntalam
translation: राजन्: Oh king, परिघ: iron bars, शक्ति: javelins, ऋष्टि: double edged swords, शूल: spear, पट्टिश: spear with a sharp edge or some other weapon with three points, कुन्तलम्: ploughs.
explanation: "Oh king, (our army is equipped with) iron bars, javelins, double edged swords, spears, three pointed weapons, ploughs etc."

shloka_text: सुमहन्नोबलंकस्माद्विषादंभजतेभवान् । त्वयाभोगवतींगत्वानिर्जिताःपन्नगायुधि ।।6.7.5।।
transliteration: sumahannobalaṃkasmādviṣādaṃbhajatebhavān | tvayābhogavatīṃgatvānirjitāḥpannagāyudhi
translation: सुमहन्नोबलं: mighty army strength, कस्माद्: why, विषादं: despondent भजते: give way भवान्: you, त्वया: by you पन्नगा: Nagas, युधि: in war, भोगवतीं: Bhogavathi, गत्वा: going, निर्जिताः subdued
explanation: "Why are you despondent? You have huge and mighty army strength. When you went to Bhogavathi, the Nagas were subdued in war by your mighty army."

shloka_text: कैलासशिखरावासीयक्षैर्बहुभिरावृतः । सुमहत्कदनंकृत्वावश्यस्तेधनदःकृतः ।।6.7.6।।
transliteration: kailāsaśikharāvāsīyakṣairbahubhirāvṛtaḥ | sumahatkadanaṃkṛtvāvaśyastedhanadaḥkṛtaḥ
translation: कैलासशिखरावासी: he who lives on the peak of mount Kailas: बहुभि: numerous, यक्षै: Yakshas, (बहुभि:  आवृत:  बाहुभिरावृत:) आवृतः surrounded by, सुमहत: great, कदनं: sorrow कृत्वा: being caused, वश्यस्ते: surrendered to you, धनदः bestow er of wealth (Kubera) कृतः remained.
explanation: He who dwells on the peak of Mount Kailasa, surrounded by numerous yakshas, was, after great affliction was visited upon him, made to submit to you.

shloka_text: समहेश्वरसख्येनश्लाघमानस्त्वयाविभो । निर्जितःसमरेरोषाल्लोकपालोमहाबलः ।।6.7.7।।
transliteration: samaheśvarasakhyenaślāghamānastvayāvibho | nirjitaḥsamareroṣāllokapālomahābalaḥ
translation: स: that, महेश्वरसख्येन: by the friendship of Maheswara (Siva), श्लाघमान: priding महाबलः strong, ल्लोकपालो: ruler of the world, स्त्वया: by you might, विभो: O king, निर्जितः subdued, समरे: in conflict.
explanation: "O King Proud of his friendship with Lord Maheshwara (Siva), that mighty ruler of the world Kubera was subdued by you in the conflict."

shloka_text: विनिहत्यचयक्षौघान्विक्षोभ्यचविनिगृह्यच । त्वयाकैलासशिखराद्विमानमिदमाहृतम् ।।6.7.8।।
transliteration: vinihatyacayakṣaughānvikṣobhyacavinigṛhyaca | tvayākailāsaśikharādvimānamidamāhṛtam
translation: त्वया: by you, यक्षौघान्: hordes of yaksha, विनिहत्य: taking as prisoners, विक्षोभ्यच: causing disturbance by stirring and, विनिगृह्यच: and taking away, कैलासशिखराद्: from mount Kailas, विमानमिदमाहृतम्: brought this great aerial chariot.
explanation: "Causing terrific disturbance to the hordes of Yakshas and taking them as prisoners, you have brought the great aerial chariot from mount Kailas."

shloka_text: मयेनदानवेन्द्रेणत्वद्भयात्सख्यमिच्छता । दुहितातवभार्यार्थेदत्ताराक्षसपुङ्गव ।।6.7.9।।
transliteration: mayenadānavendreṇatvadbhayātsakhyamicchatā | duhitātavabhāryārthedattārākṣasapuṅgava
translation: राक्षसपुङ्गव: leader of Rakshasas, दानवेन्द्रेण: ruler of Danavas, मयेन: by Maya, त्वद्भयात्: out of fear of you, मिच्छता: sought, सख्य: alliance, दत्ता: given तव: to you, भार्यार्थे: wife, दुहिता: daughter.
explanation: "Maya, the ruler of Danavas has given his daughter (Mandodari) to you as a wife out of fear of you, O leader of Rakshasas"

shloka_text: दानवेन्द्रोमधुर्नामवीर्योत्सिक्तोदुरासदः । विगृह्यवशमानीतःकुम्भीनस्याःसुखावहः ।।6.7.10।।
transliteration: dānavendromadhurnāmavīryotsiktodurāsadaḥ | vigṛhyavaśamānītaḥkumbhīnasyāḥsukhāvahaḥ
translation: दुरासदः difficult to approach, वीर्योत्सिक्तो: proud of his valour, कुम्भीनस्याः Kumbhinasi (your sister), सुखावहः who brings joy to her (who is husband of), दानवेन्द्रो: ruler of Danavas, मधुर्नाम: called as Madhu, विगृह्य: offering to fight and win, वशमानीतः subjugated to you.
explanation: "Madhu, another ruler of Danavas who was proud of his valour and difficult to approach, the husband of Kumbhinasi was subjugated by you by your offering to fight with him."

shloka_text: निर्जितास्तेमहाबाहोनागागत्वारसातलम् । वासुकिस्तक्षकःशङखोजटीचवशमाहृताः ।।6.7.11।।
transliteration: nirjitāstemahābāhonāgāgatvārasātalam | vāsukistakṣakaḥśaṅakhojaṭīcavaśamāhṛtāḥ
translation: महाबाहो: mighty armed, स्ते: you गत्वा: going to, रसातलम्: subterranean region वासुकि:: Vasuki, तक्षकः Takshaka, शङखो: Shanka, जटीच: and Jati, नागा: serpent demons, र्जिता: winning over, वशमाहृताः made them submit to you.
explanation: "O mighty armed king Going to the subterranean world, you won over the serpent demons Vasuki, Takshaka, Shanka and Jati and made them submit to you."

shloka_text: अक्षयाबलवन्तश्चशूरालब्धवराःपुनः । त्वयासंवत्सरंयुद्ध्वासमरेदानवाविभो ।।6.7.12।।
transliteration: akṣayābalavantaścaśūrālabdhavarāḥpunaḥ | tvayāsaṃvatsaraṃyuddhvāsamaredānavāvibho
translation: अक्षया: imperishable, बलवन्तश्च: strong and mighty, शूरा: warriors, लब्धवराः who had obtained boon, त्वया: by you, संवत्सरं: one year, युद्ध्वा: fighting, पुनः again, समरे: in war, दानवा: Danavas, विभो: Oh Lord.
explanation: "The mighty and strong Danava warriors who had obtained boon were made to fight a war by you for one year."

shloka_text: स्वबलंसमुपाश्रित्यनीतावशमरिन्दम । मायाश्चाधिगतास्तत्रबह्व्योवैराक्षसाधिप ।।6.7.13।।
transliteration: svabalaṃsamupāśrityanītāvaśamarindama | māyāścādhigatāstatrabahvyovairākṣasādhipa
translation: राक्षसाधिप: king of Rakshasas, स्वबलं: your own strength, समुपाश्रित्य: resorting to, मायाश्च: deceitful tricks, अधिगता: learned, तत्र: there, बह्वो: many, नीता: reduced to, वशम: sub mission, अरिन्दम: subduer of enemies.
explanation: "O king of Rakshasas (Those Danavas) were reduced to sub mission by resorting to your own strength. Oh subduer of enemies, many deceitful tricks were learned from them."

shloka_text: शूराश्चबलवन्तश्चवरुणस्यसुतारणे । निर्जितास्तेमहाभागचतुर्विधबलानुगाः ।।6.7.14।।
transliteration: śūrāścabalavantaścavaruṇasyasutāraṇe | nirjitāstemahābhāgacaturvidhabalānugāḥ
translation: महाभाग: blessed one, चतुर्विधबलानुगाः four kinds of army, शूराश्च: capable heroes, बलवन्तश्च: mighty strong, वरुणस्य: Varuna's, सुता: sons, रणे: in war, निर्जिता: have won, ते: by you.
explanation: "O blessed king Mighty strong sons of Varuna, heroes capable of war and of all the four kinds of army have been won by you."

shloka_text: मृत्युदण्डमहाग्राहंशाल्मलिद्रुममण्डितम् । कालपाशमहावीचिंयमकिंकरपन्नगम् ।।6.7.15।। महाज्वरेणदुर्धर्षंयमलोकमहार्णवम् । अवगाह्यत्वयाराजन्यमस्यबलसागरम् ।।6.7.16।। जयश्चविपुलःप्राप्तोमृत्युश्चप्रतिषेधितः । सुयुद्धेनचतेसर्वेलोकास्तत्रसुतोषिताः ।।6.7.17।।
transliteration: mṛtyudaṇḍamahāgrāhaṃśālmalidrumamaṇḍitam | kālapāśamahāvīciṃyamakiṃkarapannagam  mahājvareṇadurdharṣaṃyamalokamahārṇavam | avagāhyatvayārājanyamasyabalasāgaram  jayaścavipulaḥprāptomṛtyuścapratiṣedhitaḥ | suyuddhenacatesarvelokāstatrasutoṣitāḥ
translation: मृत्युदण्ड: Yama's rod of death, महाग्राहं: huge alligator, शाल्मलिद्रुममण्डितम्: adorned with Salmali trees (bristling with thorns to be used as weapons), कालपाश: noose of time (Kala), महावीचिं: hugely turbulent wave, यमकिंकरपन्नगम्: Lord of death 's attendants as serpents, महाज्वरेण: on account of mighty Jwara (spirit of fever), दुर्धर्षं: unassailable, यमलोकमहार्णवम्: ocean in the shape of Yama's realm, अवगाह्य: plunging into. त्वया: by you, राजन्: Oh King, यमस्य: realm of death, बलसागरम्: ocean of army, जयश्च: victory, विपुल: great, प्राप्तो: obtained, मृत्युश्च: and death, प्रतिषेधितः warded off, सुयुद्धेनच: and by good battle, ते: your, सर्वे: all, लोका: people (of that world), तत्र: there, सुतोषिताः were delighted.
explanation: "Oh King Plunging into the ocean, which was in the shape of Yama's realm, with an enormous alligator in the form of rod of death, adorned with Salmali trees, turbulent with a huge wave in the form of Death 's noose, infested with Lord of  Death's attendants as serpents, unassailable on account of the mighty Jwara (spirit of fever), you have obtained a great victory over the Lord of Death 's great army and the army was warded off. By your good battle all the people (of the world) were delighted.
