translation: अहम् I, सप्रहस्तम् with Prahastha, सबान्धवः with relatives, दशग्रीवम् tenheaded Ravana, हत्वा: killing, त्वाम् you, राजानम् crown as the king, करिष्यामि: will make you, मे: my, एतत् this, सत्यम् true, ब्रवीमि: telling.
explanation: "By Killing the tenheaded Ravana along with Prahastha and relatives I will make you the king. I am telling you, this is true."

shloka_text: रसातलंवाप्रविशेत्पाताळंवापिरावणः । पितामहासकाशंवानमेजीवन्विमोक्ष्यते ।।6.19.20।।
transliteration: rasātalaṃvāpraviśetpātāḻaṃvāpirāvaṇaḥ | pitāmahāsakāśaṃvānamejīvanvimokṣyate
translation: रावणः Ravana, रसातलम् hell, पातालंवापि: even under the ground, प्रविशेत् if enters, पितामहासकाशंवा: or the abode of Brahma, जीवन् with life, मे: I, नविमोक्ष्यते: will not let.
explanation: "Even if Ravana enters the hell or underground or the abode of Brahma the creator, I will not let him be alive."

shloka_text: अहत्वारावणंसङ् ख्येसपुत्रजनबान्धवम् । अयोध्यांनप्रवेक्ष्यामित्रिभिस्तैर्भ्रातृभिश्शपे ।।6.19.21।।
transliteration: ahatvārāvaṇaṃsaṅ khyesaputrajanabāndhavam | ayodhyāṃnapravekṣyāmitribhistairbhrātṛbhiśśape
translation: सपुत्रजनबान्दवम् accompanied with sons and relatives and people, रावणम् Ravana, सङ् ख्ये: in war, अहत्वा: without putting an end to, अयोध्याम् into Ayodhya, नप्रवेक्ष्यामि: will not enter, तै: those, त्रिभिः three, भ्रातृभिः brothers, शपे vow.
explanation: "I vow upon my three brothers that I will not enter Ayodhya without putting an end to Ravana along with his people, sons and relatives."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वातुवचनंतस्यरामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः । शिरसावन्द्यधर्मात्मावक्तुमेवोपचक्रमे ।।6.19.22।।
transliteration: śrutvātuvacanaṃtasyarāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ | śirasāvandyadharmātmāvaktumevopacakrame
translation: धर्मात्मा: righteous man, अक्लिष्टकर्मणः untiring in action, तस्यरामस्य: at Rama's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा: after having heard, शिरसा: with head, अवन्द्य: bent down, वक्तुमेव: to speak, उपचक्रमे: started.
explanation: After having heard the words of Rama of untiring in action, Vibheeshana of righteous nature, started to speak with his head bent down (in reverence).

shloka_text: राक्षसानांवधेसाह्यंलङ्कायाश्चप्रधर्षणे । करिष्यामियथाप्राणंप्रवेक्ष्यामिचवाहिनीम् ।।6.19.23।।
transliteration: rākṣasānāṃvadhesāhyaṃlaṅkāyāścapradharṣaṇe | kariṣyāmiyathāprāṇaṃpravekṣyāmicavāhinīm
translation: लङ्कायाः Lanka's, प्रधर्षणे: for storming, राक्षसानाम् for Rakshasas, वथे: for killing, साह्यम् help, करिष्यामि: will render, यथाप्राणम् with all my strength, वाहिनीम् army, प्रवेक्ष्यामिच: to enter.
explanation: "I will render assistance with all my strength for storming Lanka, for killing the Rakshasas and for the army to enter."

shloka_text: इतिब्रुवाणांरामस्तुपरिष्वज्यविभीषणम् । अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणंप्रीतस्समुद्राज्जलमानय ।।6.19.24।।
transliteration: itibruvāṇāṃrāmastupariṣvajyavibhīṣaṇam | abravīllakṣmaṇaṃprītassamudrājjalamānaya
translation: रामस्तु: even Rama also, प्रीत: pleased, इति: thus, ब्रुवाणम् spoken, विभीषणम् by Vibheeshana, परिष्वज्य: embracing, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, अब्रवीत् said, समुद्रात् from the ocean, जलम् water, आनय: get water.
explanation: When Vibheeshana had spoken in that manner, Rama was pleased and embraced him. He called for Lakshmana to get water from the ocean (for consecration).

shloka_text: तेनचेमंमहाप्राज्ञमभिषिञ्चविभीषणम् । राजानंरक्षसांक्षिप्रंप्रसन्नेमयिमानद ।।6.19.25।।
transliteration: tenacemaṃmahāprājñamabhiṣiñcavibhīṣaṇam | rājānaṃrakṣasāṃkṣipraṃprasannemayimānada
translation: मानद: respectable one, मयि: I am, प्रसन्ने: pleased with, महाप्राज्ञम् highly intelligent, इमम् this, विभीषणम् Vibheeshana, रक्षसाम् Rakshasa, राजानम् crowned king, क्षीप्रम् at once, तेन: so, अभिषिञ्च: will coronate.
explanation: "I am pleased with this highly intelligent Vibheeshana, a respectable one. I will coronate him at once as king of Rakshasas."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुसौमित्रिरभ्यषिञ्चद्विभीषणम् । मध्येवानरमुख्यानांराजानंरामशासनात् ।।6.19.26।।
transliteration: evamuktastusaumitrirabhyaṣiñcadvibhīṣaṇam | madhyevānaramukhyānāṃrājānaṃrāmaśāsanāt
translation: एवम् in that way, उक्ताः having spoken, सौमित्रि: Saumithri, वानमुख्यानाम् chiefs of army of Vanaras, मध्ये: midst, रामशासनात् by the command of Rama, विभीषणम् Vibheeshana, राजानम् as king, अभ्यषिञ्चत् coronated.
explanation: (Rama) having spoken that way, Saumithri crowned Vibheeshana as crowned king on the command of Rama amid Vanara army chiefs.

shloka_text: तंप्रसादंतुरामस्यदृष्टवासद्यःप्लवङ्गमाः । प्रचुक्रुशुर्महात्मानंसाधुसाध्वितिचाब्रुवन् ।।6.19.27।।
transliteration: taṃprasādaṃturāmasyadṛṣṭavāsadyaḥplavaṅgamāḥ | pracukruśurmahātmānaṃsādhusādhviticābruvan
translation: प्लवङ्गमाः the leaping animals (Vanaras), रामस्य: Rama's, तम्: that, सद्यः that, प्रसादम् grace, दृष्टवा: seeing, प्रचुक्रुशुः moving about in joy, महात्मानम् great self, साधुसाधुइति: good, अब्रुवन् च: hailed saying.
explanation: At that instant the Vanaras jumped, moving about exhibiting their joy on witnessing great Rama's grace saying "Good, good."

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद् हनूमांश्चसुग्रीवश्चविभीषणम् । कथंसागरमक्षोभ्यंतरामवरुणालयम् ।।6.19.28।। सैन्यैःपरिवृतास्सर्वेवानराणांमहौजसाम् ।
transliteration: athābravīd hanūmāṃścasugrīvaścavibhīṣaṇam | kathaṃsāgaramakṣobhyaṃtarāmavaruṇālayam  sainyaiḥparivṛtāssarvevānarāṇāṃmahaujasām |
translation: हनूमांश्च: Hanuman also, विभीषणम् to Vibheeshana, अब्रवीत् said, सुग्रीवश्च: to Sugriva, सर्वे: entire lot of, महौजसाम् highly energetic, वानराणाम् with Vanaras, सैन्यैः army, परिवृताः surrounded, अक्षोभ्यम् imperturbable, वरुणालयम् abode of Varuna (ocean), सागरम् ocean, कथम् how, तराम: to cross.
explanation: Hanuman and Sugriva enquired of Vibheeshana as to how to cross this ocean that is imperturbable along with the entire lot of energetic Vanara army.

shloka_text: उपायंनाधिगच्छामोयथानदनदीपतिम् । तरामतरसासर्वेससैन्यावरुणालयम् ।।6.19.29।।
transliteration: upāyaṃnādhigacchāmoyathānadanadīpatim | tarāmatarasāsarvesasainyāvaruṇālayam
translation: नदनदीपतिम् Lord of rivers and streams, god of water, वरुणालयम् abode of Varuna, ससैन्याः with the army, सर्वे: entire, तरसा: to cross, यथा: this way, तराम: to cross, उपायैः strategy, अभिगच्चाम: shall we approach.
explanation: "What strategy should we adopt to cross this abode of Varuna, the Lord of rivers and streams with the entire army of Vanaras?" (Hanuman and Sugriva asked Vibheeshana).

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुधर्मज्ञःप्रत्युवाचविभीषणः । समुद्रंराघवोराजाशरणंगन्तुमर्हति ।।6.19.30।।
transliteration: evamuktastudharmajñaḥpratyuvācavibhīṣaṇaḥ | samudraṃrāghavorājāśaraṇaṃgantumarhati
translation: एवम् in that way, उक्तः having said, धर्मात्मा: righteous self, विभीषणः Vibheeshana, प्रत्युवाच: replied, राजा: O King, राघवः Raghava, समुद्रम् ocean, शरणम् refuge, गन्तुम् will go, अर्हति: we ought to.
explanation: (Hanuman) having asked so, righteous Vibheeshana said, "O king Raghava We ought to go and seek refuge from the god of the ocean."

shloka_text: खानितस्सगरेणायमप्रमेयोमहोदधिः । कर्तुमर्हतिरामस्यज्ञाते: कार्यंमहामतिः ।।6.19.31।।
transliteration: khānitassagareṇāyamaprameyomahodadhiḥ | kartumarhatirāmasyajñāte: kāryaṃmahāmatiḥ
translation: आप्रमेयः unbounded, अयम: this, महोदधिः great ocean, सगरेण: by Sagara, खनितः excavated, महामतिः king of the great ocean, ज्ञात: race, रामस्य: Rama's, कार्यम् task, कर्तुम् to do, अर्हति: ought to.
explanation: "This immeasurable great ocean was excavated by Sagara (A King of the Ikshvaku dynasty). The great ocean needs to do the task of Rama who is of the same race."

shloka_text: एवंविभीषणेनोक्तोराक्षसेनविपश्चिता । अजगामाथसुग्रीवोयत्ररामस्सलक्ष्मणः ।।6.19.32।।
transliteration: evaṃvibhīṣaṇenoktorākṣasenavipaścitā | ajagāmāthasugrīvoyatrarāmassalakṣmaṇaḥ
translation: अथ: and then, विपश्चिता: learned, राक्षसेना: by rakshasa, विभीषणेन: by Vibheeshana, एवम् in that manner, उक्तः having spoken, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, सलक्ष्मणेन: accompanied by Lakshmana, रामः Rama, यत्र: where, आजगाम: reached.
explanation: Vibheeshana having spoken in that manner, Sugriva accompanied by Lakshmana reached near Rama.

shloka_text: ततश्चाख्यातुमारेभेविभीषणवचश्शुभम् । सुग्रीवोविपुलग्रीवोस्सागरस्योपवेशनम् ।।6.19.33।।
transliteration: tataścākhyātumārebhevibhīṣaṇavacaśśubham | sugrīvovipulagrīvossāgarasyopaveśanam
translation: ततः thereafter, विपुलग्रीवः broadnecked, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, विभीषणवचः Vibheeshana's words of advice, सागरस्य: about Sagara, उपवेशनम् sitting down, आख्यातुम् to make him know आरेभे: started.
explanation: Thereafter broadnecked Sugriva started to communicate to Rama the advice of Vibheeshana about Sagara.

shloka_text: प्रकृत्याधर्मशीलस्यराघवस्याप्यरोचत ।।6.19.34।। सलक्ष्मणंमहातेजास्सुग्रीवंचहरीश्वरम् । सत्क्रियार्थंक्रियादक्षंस्मितपूर्वमुवाचह ।।6.29.35।।
transliteration: prakṛtyādharmaśīlasyarāghavasyāpyarocata  salakṣmaṇaṃmahātejāssugrīvaṃcaharīśvaram | satkriyārthaṃkriyādakṣaṃsmitapūrvamuvācaha
translation: प्रकृत्या: by nature, धर्मशीलस्य: one who is of righteous character, अस्यरामस्यापि: to Rama also, रोचित: pleasing, महातेजाः brilliant, सः he, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, क्रियादक्षम् skilful at action, हरीश्वरम् king of Vanaras, सुग्रीवंच: and Sugriva also, सत्क्रियार्थम् about the task to be undertaken, स्मितपूर्वम् smilingly, उवाच: said.
explanation: To Rama who was by nature righteous the advice (of Vibheeshana) was pleasing. To the brilliant Lakshmana of skilful action, to Sugriva the king of monkeys, Rama said smilingly.

shloka_text: प्रकृत्याधर्मशीलस्यराघवस्याप्यरोचत ।।6.19.34।। सलक्ष्मणंमहातेजास्सुग्रीवंचहरीश्वरम् । सत्क्रियार्थंक्रियादक्षंस्मितपूर्वमुवाचह ।।6.29.35।।
transliteration: prakṛtyādharmaśīlasyarāghavasyāpyarocata  salakṣmaṇaṃmahātejāssugrīvaṃcaharīśvaram | satkriyārthaṃkriyādakṣaṃsmitapūrvamuvācaha
translation: प्रकृत्या: by nature, धर्मशीलस्य: one who is of righteous character, अस्यरामस्यापि: to Rama also, रोचित: pleasing, महातेजाः brilliant, सः he, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, क्रियादक्षम् skilful at action, हरीश्वरम् king of Vanaras, सुग्रीवंच: and Sugriva also, सत्क्रियार्थम् about the task to be undertaken, स्मितपूर्वम् smilingly, उवाच: said.
explanation: To Rama who was by nature righteous the advice (of Vibheeshana) was pleasing. To the brilliant Lakshmana of skilful action, to Sugriva the king of monkeys, Rama said smilingly.

shloka_text: विभीषणस्यमन्त्रोऽयंममलक्ष्मण रोचते । सुग्रीवःपण्डितोनित्यंभवान्मन्त्रविचक्षणः ।।6.19.36।। उभाभ्यांसम्प्रधार्यार्थंरोचतेयत्तदुच्यताम् ।
transliteration: vibhīṣaṇasyamantro'yaṃmamalakṣmaṇa rocate | sugrīvaḥpaṇḍitonityaṃbhavānmantravicakṣaṇaḥ  ubhābhyāṃsampradhāryārthaṃrocateyattaducyatām |
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, विभीषणस्य: Vibheeshana's, आयंमन्त्रः this advice, मम: to me,रोचते: pleasing, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, पण्डितः learned, भवान् me, नित्यम् ever, मन्त्रविशारद: capable of good advice, उभाभ्याम् for both, अर्थम् meaningful, सम्प्रधार्य: tradition, यत् that which, रोचते: appeals, तत् that, उच्यताम् may be told to me.
explanation: "Lakshmana This advice of Vibheeshana is pleasing to me. Sugriva is learned, and you are always capable of good advice. That which appeals to both of you, and which is meaningful may be informed to me."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तौततोवीरावुभौसुग्रीवलक्ष्मणौ । समुदाचारसंयुक्तमिदंवचनमूचतुः ।।6.19.37।।
transliteration: evamuktautatovīrāvubhausugrīvalakṣmaṇau | samudācārasaṃyuktamidaṃvacanamūcatuḥ
translation: ततः then, एवम् that way, उक्तौ: having been said, वीरौ: heroic, सुग्रीवलक्ष्मणौ: to Sugriva and Lakshmana, उभौ: both, समुदाचारसंयुक्तम् mixed with respectful tradition, इदम् these, वचनम् words, ऊचतुः gave reply.
explanation: Heroic Rama having said that way to both, Lakshmana and Sugriva replied thus respectfully following tradition (with folded hands).

shloka_text: किमर्थनौनरव्याघ्र: नरोचिष्यतिराघव: । विभीषणेनयच्चोक्तमस्मिन् कालेसुखावहम् ।।6.19.38।।
transliteration: kimarthanaunaravyāghra: narociṣyatirāghava: | vibhīṣaṇenayaccoktamasmin kālesukhāvaham
translation: नरव्याघ्र: tiger among kings, राघव: Raghava, अस्मिन् this, काले: time, सुखावहम् good, यत् that which, विभीषणेन: by Vibheeshana, उक्तम् has been spoken, नौ: us, किमर्थम् why will, नरोचिष्यति: it not be pleasing.
explanation: "O Raghava, the tiger among kings Why will this good advice given to us at this time by Vibheeshana be not pleasing?" Sugriva and Lakshmana said to Rama."

shloka_text: अबध्वासागरेसेतुंघोरेऽस्मिन्वरुणालये । लङ्कानासादितुंशक्यासेन्द्रैरपिसुरासुरैः ।।6.19.39।।
transliteration: abadhvāsāgaresetuṃghore'sminvaruṇālaye | laṅkānāsādituṃśakyāsendrairapisurāsuraiḥ
translation: घोरे: terrific, वरुणालये: ocean, अस्मिन् सागरे: over this ocean, सेतुम् bridge, अबध्वा: building, लङ्का: Lanka city, सेन्द्रैरपि: even for Indra, सुरासुरैरपि: for Suras and Asuras also, आसादितुम् to cross over, नशक्या: not possible.
explanation: Without building a bridge over this terrific ocean, the abode of Varuna, it is not possible to cross over to Lanka even for Indra, suras or Asuras.

shloka_text: विभीषणस्यशूरस्ययथार्थंक्रियतांवचः ।।6.19.40।। अलंकालात्ययंकृत्वासागरोऽयंनियुज्यताम् । यथासैन्येनगच्छामपुरींरावणपालिताम् ।।6.19.41।।
transliteration: vibhīṣaṇasyaśūrasyayathārthaṃkriyatāṃvacaḥ  alaṃkālātyayaṃkṛtvāsāgaro'yaṃniyujyatām | yathāsainyenagacchāmapurīṃrāvaṇapālitām
translation: शूरस्य: valiant, विभीषणस्य: Vibheeshana's, वचः words of advice, यथार्थम् are true, क्रियताम् to execute, कालात्ययम् no use was ting time, कृत्वा: to do, अलम् it is enough, रावणपालिताम् ruled by Ravana, पुरीम् city, यथा: like that, सैन्येन: army, गच्छाम: to proceed, सागर: अयं: over th is ocean, नियुज्यताम् let us request.
explanation: "Valiant Vibheeshana's words are true. Let us proceed and let us not waste time. Let us request Sagara to help the army to be able to proceed to Lanka ruled by Ravana (Sugriva and Lakshmana said to Rama)."

shloka_text: विभीषणस्यशूरस्ययथार्थंक्रियतांवचः ।।6.19.40।। अलंकालात्ययंकृत्वासागरोऽयंनियुज्यताम् । यथासैन्येनगच्छामपुरींरावणपालिताम् ।।6.19.41।।
transliteration: vibhīṣaṇasyaśūrasyayathārthaṃkriyatāṃvacaḥ  alaṃkālātyayaṃkṛtvāsāgaro'yaṃniyujyatām | yathāsainyenagacchāmapurīṃrāvaṇapālitām
translation: शूरस्य: valiant, विभीषणस्य: Vibheeshana's, वचः words of advice, यथार्थम् are true, क्रियताम् to execute, कालात्ययम् no use was ting time, कृत्वा: to do, अलम् it is enough, रावणपालिताम् ruled by Ravana, पुरीम् city, यथा: like that, सैन्येन: army, गच्छाम: to proceed, सागर: अयं: over th is ocean, नियुज्यताम् let us request.
explanation: "Valiant Vibheeshana's words are true. Let us proceed and let us not waste time. Let us request Sagara to help the army to be able to proceed to Lanka ruled by Ravana (Sugriva and Lakshmana said to Rama)."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तःकुशास्तीर्नोतीरेनदनदीपतेः । संविवेशतदारामोवेद्यामिवहुताशनः ।।6.19.42।।
transliteration: evamuktaḥkuśāstīrnotīrenadanadīpateḥ | saṃviveśatadārāmovedyāmivahutāśanaḥ
translation: एवम् in that way, उक्तः having said, रामः Rama, तदा: then, नदनदीपतेः ocean, कुशास्तीर्णे: on the Kusa grass mat, तीरे: shore, हुताशन: fire God, वेद्यामिव: like in the sacrificial altar, संविवेश: sat.
explanation: Then when they (Sugriva and Lakshmana) said so to Rama, he sat on Kusa grass mat on the shore of the ocean just as fire stayed in the sacrificial altar. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेएकोनविंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the nineteenth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततोनिविष्टांध्वजिनींसुग्रीवेणाभिपालिताम् । ददर्शराक्षसोऽभ्येत्यशार्दूलोनामवीर्यवान् ।।6.20.1।।
transliteration: tatoniviṣṭāṃdhvajinīṃsugrīveṇābhipālitām | dadarśarākṣaso'bhyetyaśārdūlonāmavīryavān
translation: ततः then, वीर्यवान् heroic one, शार्दूलोनाम: by name Shardula, राक्षसः Rakshasa, आभ्येत्य: entering into, निविष्टाम् encamped, सुग्रीवेण: by Sugriva, अभिपालिताम् under the command of, ध्वजिनीम् bearing a flag as a mark, ददर्श: saw.
explanation: Then the heroic Rakshasa called Shardula entered into the area encamped by the army under Sugriva's command and saw the sign flag of the army.
comments: Ravana sends Suka as an envoy to Sugriva knowing that the Vanara army is advancing to Lanka. Vanaras capture Suka and Rama prevents the Vanaras from killing him and sets him free.

shloka_text: चारोराक्षसराजस्यरावणस्यदुरात्मनः । तांदृष्ट्वासर्वतोव्यग्रंप्रतिगम्यसराक्षसः ।।6.20.2।। प्रविश्यलङ्कांवेगेनरावणंवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
transliteration: cārorākṣasarājasyarāvaṇasyadurātmanaḥ | tāṃdṛṣṭvāsarvatovyagraṃpratigamyasarākṣasaḥ  praviśyalaṅkāṃvegenarāvaṇaṃvākyamabravīt |
translation: दुरात्मनः evil minded one, राक्षसराजस्य: Rakshasa kin g's, रावणस्य: Ravana's, चारः spy, सःराक्षसः that Rakshasa, अव्यग्रः not ruffled, ताम् that, सर्वतः all over, दृष्टवा: seeing, प्रतिगम्य: went back, वेगेन: speedily, लङ्काम् to Lanka, प्रविश्य: entered, रावणम् to Ravana, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: The evil minded raskshasa who was a spy of Ravana went back to Lanka speedily unruffled after having observed all over the camp and spoke these words to Ravana.

shloka_text: एषवानरऋक्षौघोलङ्कांसमभिवर्तते । अगाधश्चाप्रमेयश्चद्वितीयइवसागरः ।।6.20.3।।
transliteration: eṣavānaraṛkṣaugholaṅkāṃsamabhivartate | agādhaścāprameyaścadvitīyaivasāgaraḥ
translation: द्वितीयः second, सागरःइव: like the ocean, अगाधश्च: deep, आप्रमेयश्च: and immeasurable, एषः that way, वानरऋक्षौघः Vanaras and Bears, लङ्काम् into Lanka, समभिवर्तते: are heading towards.
explanation: As if it is a second ocean deep and immeasurable, the ocean of Vanaras and Bears are heading towards Lanka (reported the spy).

shloka_text: पुत्रौदशरथस्येमौभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.20.4।। उत्तमौरूपसम्पन्नौसीतायाःपदमागतौ । एतौसागरमासाद्यसन्निविष्टौमहाद्युती ।।6.20.5।।
transliteration: putraudaśarathasyemaubhrātaraurāmalakṣmaṇau  uttamaurūpasampannausītāyāḥpadamāgatau | etausāgaramāsādyasanniviṣṭaumahādyutī
translation: दशरथस्य: Dasaratha's, पुत्रौ: sons, उत्तमौ: great, रूपसम्पन्नौ: endowed with beautiful form, महाद्युती: exceptional fortitude, भ्रातरौ: brothers, इमौ: these, रामलक्ष्मणौ: Rama and Lakshmana, सीतायाः Sita's, पदम् to set foot, आगतौ: have come, सागरम् sea, आसाद्य: reached, सन्निविष्टौ: settled.
explanation: "Great sons of Dasaratha, Rama and Lakshmana, endowed with beautiful form and exceptional fortitude have come and set their foot on the seashore and settled to come to Sita."

shloka_text: पुत्रौदशरथस्येमौभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.20.4।। उत्तमौरूपसम्पन्नौसीतायाःपदमागतौ । एतौसागरमासाद्यसन्निविष्टौमहाद्युती ।।6.20.5।।
transliteration: putraudaśarathasyemaubhrātaraurāmalakṣmaṇau  uttamaurūpasampannausītāyāḥpadamāgatau | etausāgaramāsādyasanniviṣṭaumahādyutī
translation: दशरथस्य: Dasaratha's, पुत्रौ: sons, उत्तमौ: great, रूपसम्पन्नौ: endowed with beautiful form, महाद्युती: exceptional fortitude, भ्रातरौ: brothers, इमौ: these, रामलक्ष्मणौ: Rama and Lakshmana, सीतायाः Sita's, पदम् to set foot, आगतौ: have come, सागरम् sea, आसाद्य: reached, सन्निविष्टौ: settled.
explanation: "Great sons of Dasaratha, Rama and Lakshmana, endowed with beautiful form and exceptional fortitude have come and set their foot on the seashore and settled to come to Sita."

shloka_text: बलंचामाकाशमावृत्यसर्वतोदशयोजनम् । तत्त्वभूतंमहाराज क्षिप्रंवेदितुमर्हसि ।।6.20.6।।
transliteration: balaṃcāmākāśamāvṛtyasarvatodaśayojanam | tattvabhūtaṃmahārāja kṣipraṃveditumarhasi
translation: महाराज: O king, बलंच: army also, सर्वतः all over, दशयोजनम् ten yojanas, आयतम् spread, आकाशम् sky, आवृत्य: going round, तत्त्वभूतम् real situation, क्षिप्रम् at once, वेदितुम् should know, अर्हसि: you ought to.
explanation: "Mighty king Ravana the army also is spread all over ten yojanas. I have seen going round the sky. You ought to know the real situation at once."

shloka_text: तवदूतामहाराजक्षिप्रमर्हन्त्यवेक्षितुम् । उपप्रदानंसान्त्वंवाभेदोवात्रप्रयुज्यताम् ।।6.20.7।।
transliteration: tavadūtāmahārājakṣipramarhantyavekṣitum | upapradānaṃsāntvaṃvābhedovātraprayujyatām
translation: महाराज: O king, तव: your, दूताः spies, क्षिप्रम् at once, अवेक्षितुम् seeing, अर्हन्ति: having a claim, उपप्रदानम् entrusting, सान्त्वंवा: by conciliation, भेदोवा: by creating difference, अत्रप्रयुज्यताम् to be deployed there.
explanation: "O king at once your spies should be deployed there and entrusted to have claims either by conciliation or creating differences."

shloka_text: शार्दूलस्यवचश्श्रुत्वारावणोराक्षसेश्वरः । उवाचसहसाव्यग्रस्सम्प्रधार्यार्थमात्मनः ।।6.20.8।। शुकंनामतदारक्षोवाक्यमर्थविदांवरम् ।
transliteration: śārdūlasyavacaśśrutvārāvaṇorākṣaseśvaraḥ | uvācasahasāvyagrassampradhāryārthamātmanaḥ  śukaṃnāmatadārakṣovākyamarthavidāṃvaram |
translation: राक्षसेश्वरः Lord of Rakshasas, रावणः Ravana, शार्दूलस्य: Shardula's, वचः words, श्रुत्वा: on hearing, सहसा: rashly, व्यग्रः disturbed, आत्मनः own self, अर्थम् What to do, सम्प्रधार्य: as usual, तदा: then, अर्थविदाम् praising, वरम् supreme, शुकंनाम: called Suka, रक्षः to protect, वाक्यम् these words, उवाच: spoke.
explanation: Ravana the tiger among Rakshasas, after having heard Shardula's words decided within himself and said to Suka who is good at work praising him very much as usual.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवंब्रूहिगत्वाशुराजानंवचनान्मम । यथासन्देशमक्लीबंश्लक्ष्णयापरयागिरा ।।6.20.9।।
transliteration: sugrīvaṃbrūhigatvāśurājānaṃvacanānmama | yathāsandeśamaklībaṃślakṣṇayāparayāgirā
translation: राजानम् to the king, सुग्रीवम् to Sugriva, आशु: fast, गत्वा: approaching, मम: my, वचनात् words, यथासन्देशम् this message, परया: stranger, श्लक्ष्णया: gently, गिरा speaking, अक्लीबम् without getting disturbed, ब्रूहि: to speak.
explanation: "Departing quickly, speak to the king Sugriva boldly without getting disturbed but in a gentle way and communicate this message."

shloka_text: त्वंवैमहाराजकुलप्रसूतोमहाबलश्चर् क्षरजस्सुतश्च । नकश्चिदार्थस्तवनास्त्यनर्थस्तथाहिमेभ्रातृसमोहरीश ।।6.20.10।।
transliteration: tvaṃvaimahārājakulaprasūtomahābalaścar kṣarajassutaśca | nakaścidārthastavanāstyanarthastathāhimebhrātṛsamoharīśa
translation: महाराज: O king, हरीश: Vanara, त्वम् your, कुलप्रसूतःवै: eminent kings, महाबलश्च: mighty strong, ऋक्षरजस्सुतश्च: and Rksharaja's son, तव: your, अर्थः meaning, कश्चन: a little, नास्ति: not, अनर्थः harm, न: not, तथापि: so also, मे: I am, भ्रातृसमः like your brother.
explanation: "O Sugriva, king of Vanaras You are born in a race of eminent kings, a mighty son of Rksharaja. Even a little harm has not been done to you by me. I am like your brother (Ravana's words to Sugriva to be communicated by Suka)."

shloka_text: अहंयद्यहरंभार्यांराजपुत्रस्यधीमतः । किंतत्रतवसुग्रीव: किष्किन्धांप्रतिगम्यताम् ।।6.20.11।।
transliteration: ahaṃyadyaharaṃbhāryāṃrājaputrasyadhīmataḥ | kiṃtatratavasugrīva: kiṣkindhāṃpratigamyatām
translation: सुग्रीव: Sugriva, धीमतः wise one, राजपुत्रस्य: prince's, भार्याम् consort, अहम् I, अहरंयदि: even if I have brought away also, तत्र: there, तव: your, किम् what, किष्किन्धांप्रति: return to Kishkinda, गम्यताम् to reach.
explanation: "Sugriva What harm is done to you if I have brought the consort of prince? You are a wise one, go back to Kishkinda."

shloka_text: नहीयंहरिभिर्लङ्काशक्याप्राप्तुंकथञ्चन । देवैरपिसगन्धर्वैःकिंपुनर्नरवानरैः ।।6.20.12।।
transliteration: nahīyaṃharibhirlaṅkāśakyāprāptuṃkathañcana | devairapisagandharvaiḥkiṃpunarnaravānaraiḥ
translation: इयंलङ्का: in this Lanka, हरिभिः even Vanaras, प्राप्तुम् to get here, नशक्याहि: is not possible, सगन्धर्वैः even Gandharvas, देवैरपि: even Devas also, नरवानरैः of humans and Vanaras, किंपुनः what to say.
explanation: "It is not possible for Vanaras to get here even for Gandharvas or Devas also. What to say of humans and Vanaras? (You may tell this to Sugriva)."

shloka_text: सतथाराक्षसेन्द्रेणसन्दिष्टोरजनीचरः । शुकोविहङ्गमोभूत्वातूर्णमाप्लुत्यचाम्बरम् ।।6.20.13।।
transliteration: satathārākṣasendreṇasandiṣṭorajanīcaraḥ | śukovihaṅgamobhūtvātūrṇamāplutyacāmbaram
translation: तथा: so, राक्षसेन्द्रे: ruler of Rakshasas, सन्दिष्टः commanded thus, सः that, शुकः Suka, विहङ्गमः bird, भूत्वा: transforming, अम्बरम् sky, तूर्णम् immediately, आप्लुत्यच: rose apace into.
explanation: Thus, commanded by the ruler of Rakshasas, Suka immediately transformed into a bird form and rose apace into the sky.

shloka_text: सगत्वादूरमध्वानमुपर्युपरिसागरम् । संस्थितोह्यम्बरेवाक्यंसुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.20.14।।
transliteration: sagatvādūramadhvānamuparyuparisāgaram | saṃsthitohyambarevākyaṃsugrīvamidamabravīt
translation: सः he (Suka), सागरम् ocean, दूरम् long way, अध्वानम् having distant space, गत्वा: gone, अम्बरे: in the sky, संस्थितः stationed, सुग्रीवम् to Sugriva, इदम् these, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Suka having gone a long way in the sky to a distant place, stationed there spoke these words to Sugriva.

shloka_text: सर्वमुक्तंयथादिष्टंरावणेनदुरात्मना । तंप्रापयन्तंवचनंतूर्णमाप्लुत्यवानराः ।।6.20.15।। प्रापद्यन्तदिवंक्षिप्रंलोप्तुंहन्तुंचमुष्टिभि: ।
transliteration: sarvamuktaṃyathādiṣṭaṃrāvaṇenadurātmanā | taṃprāpayantaṃvacanaṃtūrṇamāplutyavānarāḥ  prāpadyantadivaṃkṣipraṃloptuṃhantuṃcamuṣṭibhi: |
translation: दुरात्मना: evil minded one, रावणेन: by Ravana, यथा: thus, आदिष्टम् commanded, सर्वम् everything, उक्तम् spoke, तम् his, वचनम् words, प्रापयन्तम् while communicating, वानराः Vanara, अप्लुत्य: rose up तदा:: then, क्षिप्रम् at once, लोप्तुम् injuring, मुष्टिभिः with fists, हन्तुंच: to kill, प्रापद्यन्त: started.
explanation: Thus, commanded by evil minded Ravana, Suka communicated everything as spoken by Ravana. At once the Vanaras rose and started to injure Suka with their fists.

shloka_text: सतैःप्लवङ्गैःप्रसभंनिगृहीतोनिशाचरः । गगनाद्भूतलेचाशुपरिगृह्यनिपातितः ।।6.20.16।।
transliteration: sataiḥplavaṅgaiḥprasabhaṃnigṛhītoniśācaraḥ | gaganādbhūtalecāśuparigṛhyanipātitaḥ
translation: सतैः the bird Suka, प्लवङ्गैः leaping animals, प्रसभम् violently, निगृहीतः seizing, निशाचरः night ranger, आशु: at once, परिगृह्य: held, गगनात् from the sky, भूतले: to the ground, निपातितः thrown down.
explanation: At once the Vanaras violently seized the night ranger Suka and held him and threw him down to the ground from the sky.

shloka_text: वानरैःपीड्यमानस्तुशुकोवचनमब्रवीत् । नदूतान्घ्नन्तिकाकुत्स्थ वार्यन्तांसाधुवानराः ।।6.20.17।।
transliteration: vānaraiḥpīḍyamānastuśukovacanamabravīt | nadūtānghnantikākutstha vāryantāṃsādhuvānarāḥ
translation: वानरैः: by Vanaras, पीड्यमानस्तु: being attacked, शुकोवचनमब्रवीत् Suka told these words, न: not, दूतान्: messenger, घ्नन्ति: to be killed. काकुत्स्थ: Rama of Kakuthsa race, वानराः Vanaras, साधु: good, वार्यन्ताम् prevented.
explanation: Being attacked by Vanaras, Suka told these words. "Oh Kakuthsa Rama messengers should not be killed. It will be good to prevent the Vanaras."

shloka_text: यस्तुहित्वामतंभर्तुस्स्वमतंसम्प्रभाषते । अनुक्तवादीदूतस्सन् सदूतोवधमर्हति ।।6.20.18।।
transliteration: yastuhitvāmataṃbhartussvamataṃsamprabhāṣate | anuktavādīdūtassan sadūtovadhamarhati
translation: यः he who, भर्तुः king's, मतम् opinion, हित्वा: putting aside, स्वमतम् his own opinion, सम्प्रभाषते: expresses, धूतस्सन् envoy's, अनुक्तवादी: speaks that which has not been said by the king, सः such he, दूतः messenger, वधम् killing, अर्हति: ought to.
explanation: "The envoy who puts aside the king's opinion and expresses his own opinion, which has not been said by the king ought to be killed."

shloka_text: शुकस्यवचनंश्रुत्वारामस्तुपरिदेवितम् । उवाचमावधिष्टेतिघ्नतश्शाखामृगर्षभान् ।।6.20.19।।
transliteration: śukasyavacanaṃśrutvārāmastuparidevitam | uvācamāvadhiṣṭetighnataśśākhāmṛgarṣabhān
translation: रामः Rama, शुकस्य Suka's, वचनम् words, परिदेवितम् appeal, श्रुत्वा after hearing, घ्नतः shouting, शाखमृगर्षभान् animals that jump about branches of trees, (Vanaras), मावधिष्टेति: indicated not to kill, इति: thus, उवाच: said.
explanation: After hearing the appeal of Suka and seeing the monkeys shouting, Rama spoke indicating not to kill him.

shloka_text: सचपत्रलघुर्भूत्वाहरिभिर्दर्शितेभये । अन्तरिक्षेस्थितोभूत्वापुनर्वचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.20.20।।
transliteration: sacapatralaghurbhūtvāharibhirdarśitebhaye | antarikṣesthitobhūtvāpunarvacanamabravīt
translation: सः he, च and, हरिभिः monkeys also, अभये feeling secure, दर्शिते exhibited, पत्रलघुः light winged Suka, भूत्वा existing, अन्तरिक्षे in the sky, स्थितः settled, भूत्वा being, पुनः again, वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Suka, felt secure in the air and finding monkeys also settled, once again spoke these words.

shloka_text: सुग्रीव:स त्त्वसम्पन्न: महाबलपराक्रम: । किंमयाखलुवक्तव्योरावणोलोकरावणः ।।6.20.21।।
transliteration: sugrīva:sa ttvasampanna: mahābalaparākrama: | kiṃmayākhaluvaktavyorāvaṇolokarāvaṇaḥ
translation: सत्त्वसम्पन्न rich in spirit, महाबलपराक्रम mighty prowess and strength, सुग्रीव Sugriva, लोकरावणः one who makes the world cry, रावणः Ravana, मया by me, किम् what, वक्तव्य should I convey.
explanation: "Oh Sugriva Who is rich in spirit and endowed with mighty prowess What should I convey to Ravana who makes the world cry?"

shloka_text: सएवमुक्तःप्लवगाधिपस्तदाप्लवङ्गमानामृषभोमहाबलः । उवाचवाक्यंरजनीचरस्यचारंशुकंतूर्णमदीनसत्त्वः ।।6.20.22।।
transliteration: saevamuktaḥplavagādhipastadāplavaṅgamānāmṛṣabhomahābalaḥ | uvācavākyaṃrajanīcarasyacāraṃśukaṃtūrṇamadīnasattvaḥ
translation: तदा: then, एवम् in that way, उक्तः having spoken, महाबलः strong, प्लवगाधिपः leader of monkeys, सः he, अदीनसत्त्वः one who is not depressed in spirit, रजनीचरस्य: to the Rakshasa's, चारम् spy, तूर्णम् quickly, शुकम् to Suka, वाक्यम् words, उवाच: spoke.
explanation: Suka having spoken in that way, Sugriva the leader of the monkeys who was not depressed in his spirit spoke these pleasant words to the Rakshasa spy.

shloka_text: नमेऽसिमित्रंनतथानुकम्प्योनचोपकर्तापिनमेप्रियोऽसि । अरिश्चरामस्यसहानुबन्धस्ततोऽसिवालीववधार्हवध्यः ।।6.20.23।।
transliteration: name'simitraṃnatathānukampyonacopakartāpinamepriyo'si | ariścarāmasyasahānubandhastato'sivālīvavadhārhavadhyaḥ
translation: वधार्ह: one who deserves death, मे: my, मित्रम् friend, नअसि: is not, तथा: likewise, अनुकम्प्यः worthy of sympathy, न: not, उपकर्ताच: well wisher, नअसि: are not, मे: my, प्रियः beloved, नअपि: also not, रामस्य: Rama's, अरिः enemy, ततः that, वालीव: Vali's, सहानुबन्धः like relative, वध्यः killed, असि: to be.
explanation: "O Rakshasa, you are the one who deserves death (Convey to Ravana this as my word). You are an enemy to my friend, like wise you are not worthy of sympathy, not my well wisher and also not dear to me. You are Rama's enemy, so like your relative Vali you are to be killed."

shloka_text: निह्नन्म्यहंत्वांससुतंसबन्धुंसज्ञातिवर्गरजनीचरेश । लङ्काञ्चसर्वांमहताबलेनक्षिप्रंकरिष्यामिसमेत्यभस्म ।।6.20.24।।
transliteration: nihnanmyahaṃtvāṃsasutaṃsabandhuṃsajñātivargarajanīcareśa | laṅkāñcasarvāṃmahatābalenakṣipraṃkariṣyāmisametyabhasma
translation: रजनीचरेश: one who wanders at night (Rakshasa), ससुतम् your sons, सबन्धुं: your relatives, सज्ञातिवर्गम् your kinsfolk, त्वाम् you, अहम् I, निहम्नि: will kill, महता: mighty, बलेन: prowess, समेत्यसर्वाम् altogether, लङ्काम् even Lanka, क्षिप्रम् at once, भस्म: burn to ashes, करिष्यामि: I will turn into.
explanation: "O Night ranger Ravana I shall kill all your sons, relatives, your kinsfolk. I shall come at once and even burn Lanka into ashes with my mighty prowess."

shloka_text: नमोक्षयसेरावण: राघवस्यसुरैस्सहेन्द्रैदपिमूढगुप्तः । अन्तर्हितस्सूर्यपथंगतोऽवा ।तथैवपातालमनुप्रविष्टः ।।6.20.25।। गिरीशपादम्बुजसङ्गतोवाहतोऽसिरामेणसहानुजस्त्वम् ।।6.20.26।।
transliteration: namokṣayaserāvaṇa: rāghavasyasuraissahendraidapimūḍhaguptaḥ | antarhitassūryapathaṃgato'vā |tathaivapātālamanupraviṣṭaḥ  girīśapādambujasaṅgatovāhato'sirāmeṇasahānujastvam
translation: रावण: Ravana, मूढ: foolish, सहेन्द्रैः including Indra, सर्वै: all, गुप्तःअपि: even to a secret place, अन्तर्हितः are rendered invisible by your interposition, सूर्यपथम् into the orbit of Sun, गतोवा: even if you go, तथैव: so also, पातालम् to underground, अनुप्रविष्टः even if you enter, गिरीशपादाम्बुजसङ्गतोवा: or even if you seek the lotus feet of Lord Siva, राघवस्य: from Rama, नमोक्षयसे: cannot escape, सहानुजः along with your brother, त्वम् you, रामेण: by Rama, हतः slain, असि: will be.
explanation: "O Foolish Ravana Even if you go to a secret place, or rendered invisible by your interposition, or go into the orbit of the Sun, or go underground to Patala or go to the feet of Lord Siva for protection, you cannot escape from Rama. You along with your brother will be slain."

shloka_text: नमोक्षयसेरावण: राघवस्यसुरैस्सहेन्द्रैदपिमूढगुप्तः । अन्तर्हितस्सूर्यपथंगतोऽवा ।तथैवपातालमनुप्रविष्टः ।।6.20.25।। गिरीशपादम्बुजसङ्गतोवाहतोऽसिरामेणसहानुजस्त्वम् ।।6.20.26।।
transliteration: namokṣayaserāvaṇa: rāghavasyasuraissahendraidapimūḍhaguptaḥ | antarhitassūryapathaṃgato'vā |tathaivapātālamanupraviṣṭaḥ  girīśapādambujasaṅgatovāhato'sirāmeṇasahānujastvam
translation: रावण: Ravana, मूढ: foolish, सहेन्द्रैः including Indra, सर्वै: all, गुप्तःअपि: even to a secret place, अन्तर्हितः are rendered invisible by your interposition, सूर्यपथम् into the orbit of Sun, गतोवा: even if you go, तथैव: so also, पातालम् to underground, अनुप्रविष्टः even if you enter, गिरीशपादाम्बुजसङ्गतोवा: or even if you seek the lotus feet of Lord Siva, राघवस्य: from Rama, नमोक्षयसे: cannot escape, सहानुजः along with your brother, त्वम् you, रामेण: by Rama, हतः slain, असि: will be.
explanation: "O Foolish Ravana Even if you go to a secret place, or rendered invisible by your interposition, or go into the orbit of the Sun, or go underground to Patala or go to the feet of Lord Siva for protection, you cannot escape from Rama. You along with your brother will be slain."

shloka_text: तस्यतेत्रिषुलोकेषुनपिशाचंनराक्षसम् । त्रातारमनुपश्यामिनगन्धर्वंनचासुरम् ।।6.20.27।।
transliteration: tasyatetriṣulokeṣunapiśācaṃnarākṣasam | trātāramanupaśyāminagandharvaṃnacāsuram
translation: तस्य: your, ते: to you, त्रातारम् saved, त्रिषुलोकेषु: in the three world, नअनुपश्यामि: I do not see, पिशाचम् devils, न: not, राक्षसम् Rakshasas, न: not, गन्दर्वम् Gandharvas, न: not, च: also, न: not.
explanation: "I do not see anyone who can save you in these three worlds, not Rakshasas, not devils or even Gandharvas."

shloka_text: अवधीर्यजरावृद्दंगृध्रराजंजटायुषम् । किंनुतेरामसान्निध्येसकाशेलक्ष्मणस्यवा ।।6.20.28।। हृतासीताविशालाक्षीयांत्वंगृह्यनबुध्यसे ।
transliteration: avadhīryajarāvṛddaṃgṛdhrarājaṃjaṭāyuṣam | kiṃnuterāmasānnidhyesakāśelakṣmaṇasyavā  hṛtāsītāviśālākṣīyāṃtvaṃgṛhyanabudhyase |
translation: जरावृद्धम् aged and old, गृध्रराजम् vulture, जटायुषम् that Jatayu, अवधीर्य: killed disregard, त्वम् you, याम् restrained, गृह्य: seize, नबुधघ्यसे: not heed to, विशालाक्षीं: broadeyed, सीता: Sita, रामसान्निध्ये: in the presence of Rama, लक्ष्मणस्यच: and Lakshmana, सकाशे: in the presence of, किंनु: why did you, नहृता: not take away.
explanation: "When the aged and old vulture Jatayu restrained you, why did you disregard and seize broadeyed Sita? Why did you not take her away in the presence of Rama or even Lakshmana?"

shloka_text: महाबलंमहात्मानंदुर्धर्षममरैरपि । नबुध्यसेरघुश्रेष्ठंयस्तेप्राणान्हरिष्यति ।।6.20.29।।
transliteration: mahābalaṃmahātmānaṃdurdharṣamamarairapi | nabudhyaseraghuśreṣṭhaṃyasteprāṇānhariṣyati
translation: यः he who, ते: your, प्राणान् life, हरिष्यति: will take away, महाबलम् extraordinary might, महात्मानम् a benevolent one, अमरैरपि: like Indra, दुर्धर्षम् difficult to overcome, रघुश्रेष्ठम् foremost of Raghus, नबुध्यसे: you do not understand.
explanation: "You do not understand that the foremost of Raghu's, a benevolent one, is difficult to overcome even for Indra. He will take away your life with his extraordinary might."

shloka_text: ततोऽब्रवीद्वालिसुतस्त्वङ्गदोहरिसत्तमः । नायंदूतोमहाराजचारिकःप्रतिभातिमे ।।6.20.30।।
transliteration: tato'bravīdvālisutastvaṅgadoharisattamaḥ | nāyaṃdūtomahārājacārikaḥpratibhātime
translation: ततः that, वालिसुतः Vali's son, हरिसत्तमः noble one of the Vanaras, अङ्गदः Angada, अब्रवीत् said, महाराज: king, अयम् this, दूतः messenger, न: not, चारिकः spy, मे: to me, प्रतिभाति: it appears.
explanation: "Then Angada, the noble one among Vanaras, the son of Vali, said," O King, to me it appears that he is not a messenger but a spy."

shloka_text: तुलितंहिबलंसर्वमनेनात्रैवतिष्ठता । गृह्यतांमागमल्लङ्कामेतद्दिममरोचते ।।6.20.31।।
transliteration: tulitaṃhibalaṃsarvamanenātraivatiṣṭhatā | gṛhyatāṃmāgamallaṅkāmetaddimamarocate
translation: तिष्ठता: standing, अनेन: surely, सर्वम् entire, बलम् strength of the army, तुलितम् हि: has been assessed, गृह्यताम् take him captive, लङ्काम् to Lanka, मागमत् not return, एतत् thus, मम: I, रोचते: wish.
explanation: "While standing here surely he has assessed the entire strength of the army. I hope he is taken as a captive and not returned to Lanka."

shloka_text: ततोराज्ञासमादिष्टास्समुत्पत्यवलीमुखाः । जगृहुश्चबबन्धुश्चविलपन्तमनाथवत् ।।6.20.32।।
transliteration: tatorājñāsamādiṣṭāssamutpatyavalīmukhāḥ | jagṛhuścababandhuścavilapantamanāthavat
translation: तः then, राज्ञा: by the king, समादिष्टाः having been commanded, वलीमुखाः the bird Suka, समुत्पत्य: getting up, अनाथवत् like a forlorn one, विलपन्तम् wailing, जगृहुश्च: caught him, बबन्धुश्च: and bound.
explanation: Then having been commanded by the king he caught the forlorn wailing Rakshasa Suka and bound him.

shloka_text: शुकस्तुवानरैश्चण्डैस्तत्रतैस्सम्प्रपीडितः । व्याचुक्रोशमहात्मानंरामंदशरथात्मजम् ।।6.20.33।।
transliteration: śukastuvānaraiścaṇḍaistatrataissamprapīḍitaḥ | vyācukrośamahātmānaṃrāmaṃdaśarathātmajam
translation: तत्र: thereafter, चण्डैः severely, तैःवानरैः by the Vanaras, सम्प्रपीडितः tormented, शुकस्तु: at Suka, महात्मानम् benevolent, दशरथात्मजम् Dasaratha's son, रामम् Rama, व्याचुक्रोश: went towards.
explanation: "Thereafter Suka who was severely tormented by the Vanaras went towards benevolent Rama and wailed."

shloka_text: लुप्येतेमेबलात्पक्षौभिद्येतेमेतथाऽक्षिणी ।।6.20.34।। यांचरात्रिंमरिष्यामिजायेरात्रिंचयामहम् । एतस्मिन्नन्तरेकालेयन्मयाह्यशुभंकृतम् ।।6.20.35।। सर्वंत्वमुपपद्येधाजह्यांचेद्यदिजीवितम् ।
transliteration: lupyetemebalātpakṣaubhidyetemetathā'kṣiṇī  yāṃcarātriṃmariṣyāmijāyerātriṃcayāmaham | etasminnantarekāleyanmayāhyaśubhaṃkṛtam  sarvaṃtvamupapadyedhājahyāṃcedyadijīvitam |
translation: मे: my पक्षौ: wings, बलात् forcibly, लुप्येते: are cut off, तथा: likewise, मे: my अक्षिणी: eyes, भिद्येते: are injured, अहम् I, यांच: from that, रात्रिम् night, जाये: I was born, यंचरात्रिम् till the night, मरिष्यामि: I am dead, एतस्मिन् on account of this, अन्तरेकाले: in the intervening time, मया: by me, यत् that which, अशुभम् inauspicious, कृतम् action, तत् that, सर्वम् all sins, जीवितम् life, जह्यां: leaving my original form, चेद्यदि: even, उपपद्येथाः will happen.
explanation: "If my wings are cut off and my eyes are injured, on account of that inauspicious act you will take on all sins of my life from the night I was born till the night I am dead leaving my original form, even will happen (Suka tells Rama)."

shloka_text: लुप्येतेमेबलात्पक्षौभिद्येतेमेतथाऽक्षिणी ।।6.20.34।। यांचरात्रिंमरिष्यामिजायेरात्रिंचयामहम् । एतस्मिन्नन्तरेकालेयन्मयाह्यशुभंकृतम् ।।6.20.35।। सर्वंत्वमुपपद्येधाजह्यांचेद्यदिजीवितम् ।
transliteration: lupyetemebalātpakṣaubhidyetemetathā'kṣiṇī  yāṃcarātriṃmariṣyāmijāyerātriṃcayāmaham | etasminnantarekāleyanmayāhyaśubhaṃkṛtam  sarvaṃtvamupapadyedhājahyāṃcedyadijīvitam |
translation: मे: my पक्षौ: wings, बलात् forcibly, लुप्येते: are cut off, तथा: likewise, मे: my अक्षिणी: eyes, भिद्येते: are injured, अहम् I, यांच: from that, रात्रिम् night, जाये: I was born, यंचरात्रिम् till the night, मरिष्यामि: I am dead, एतस्मिन् on account of this, अन्तरेकाले: in the intervening time, मया: by me, यत् that which, अशुभम् inauspicious, कृतम् action, तत् that, सर्वम् all sins, जीवितम् life, जह्यां: leaving my original form, चेद्यदि: even, उपपद्येथाः will happen.
explanation: "If my wings are cut off and my eyes are injured, on account of that inauspicious act you will take on all sins of my life from the night I was born till the night I am dead leaving my original form, even will happen (Suka tells Rama)."

shloka_text: नाघातयत्तदारामश्श्रुत्वातत्परिदेवनम् । वानरानब्रवीद्रामोमुच्यतांदूतआगतः ।।6.20.36।।
transliteration: nāghātayattadārāmaśśrutvātatparidevanam | vānarānabravīdrāmomucyatāṃdūtaāgataḥ
translation: तदा: then, रामः Rama, तत् that, परिदेवनम् lamentation, श्रुत्वा: having heard, नाघातयत् do not kill, दूतः envoy, आगतः come, मुच्यताम् set free, वानरान् to Vanaras, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: "Having heard the lamentation, Rama said to the Vanaras" Do not kill him. Set him free as he had come as an envoy." ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेविंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the twentieth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततस्सागरवेलायांदर्भानास्तीर्यराघवः । अञ्जलिंप्राङ्मुखःकृत्वाप्रतिशिश्येमहोदधेः ।।6.21.1।। बाहुंभुजगभोगाभमुपधायारिसूदनः ।
transliteration: tatassāgaravelāyāṃdarbhānāstīryarāghavaḥ | añjaliṃprāṅmukhaḥkṛtvāpratiśiśyemahodadheḥ  bāhuṃbhujagabhogābhamupadhāyārisūdanaḥ |
translation: ततः then, अरिसूदनः one who is a destroyer of his foes, राघवः Raghava, सागरवेलायाम् on the sea shore, दर्भान् on kusa grass, आस्तीर्य spread, महोदधेः great ocean, अञ्जलिम् obeisance, कृत्वा offering, प्राङ्मुखः face turned towards east, भुजगभोगाम् like serpent coiled and resting, बाहुम् shoulders, उपधाय resting upon, प्रतिशिश्ये lay down.
explanation: Then Raghava the destroyer of foes, offered his obeisance turning his face towards east, spread the kusa grass mat on the seashore and lay down resting his head upon his shoulders like a coiled serpent.
comments: When the ocean did not give way, Rama gets angry and resorts to stirring up the ocean with his arrows.

shloka_text: वरकाञ्चनकेयूरमुक्ताप्रवरभूषणैः ।।6.21.2।। भुजैःपरमनारीणामभिमृष्टमनेकदा ।।6.21.3।।
transliteration: varakāñcanakeyūramuktāpravarabhūṣaṇaiḥ  bhujaiḥparamanārīṇāmabhimṛṣṭamanekadā
translation: वरकाञ्चनकेयूरमुक्ताप्रवरभूषणैः armlet adorned with best of gold, pearls and coral ornaments, परमनारीणाम् by supreme women, भुजैः shoulders, अनेकाथा many times, अभिमृष्टम् besmeared.
explanation: The shoulders that have been adorned with the best of gold, pearl and coral ornaments, were besmeared many times by supreme women.

shloka_text: वरकाञ्चनकेयूरमुक्ताप्रवरभूषणैः ।।6.21.2।। भुजैःपरमनारीणामभिमृष्टमनेकदा ।।6.21.3।।
transliteration: varakāñcanakeyūramuktāpravarabhūṣaṇaiḥ  bhujaiḥparamanārīṇāmabhimṛṣṭamanekadā
translation: वरकाञ्चनकेयूरमुक्ताप्रवरभूषणैः armlet adorned with best of gold, pearls and coral ornaments, परमनारीणाम् by supreme women, भुजैः shoulders, अनेकाथा many times, अभिमृष्टम् besmeared.
explanation: The shoulders that have been adorned with the best of gold, pearl and coral ornaments, were besmeared many times by supreme women.

shloka_text: चन्दनागुरुभिश्चैवपुरस्तादधिवासितम् । बालसूर्यप्रकाशैश्चन्दनैरुपशोभितम् ।।6.21.4।।
transliteration: candanāgurubhiścaivapurastādadhivāsitam | bālasūryaprakāśaiścandanairupaśobhitam
translation: पुरस्तात् earlier, चन्दनागुरुभिश्चैव with sandal paste and Agaru, अधिवासितम् emitting, बालसूर्यप्रकाशैः the brilliance of rising Sun, चन्धनैः sandal, उपशोभितम् very charming.
explanation: The very charming shoulders, smeared with sandal paste and Agaru fragrance emitting the brilliance of the rising Sun.

shloka_text: शयनेचोत्तमाङ्गेनसीतायाश्शोभितंपुरा । तक्षकस्येवसम्भोगगङ्गाजलनिषेचितम् ।।6.21.5।।
transliteration: śayanecottamāṅgenasītāyāśśobhitaṃpurā | takṣakasyevasambhogagaṅgājalaniṣecitam
translation: पुरा earlier, शयने while he slept, सीतायाः Sita's, उत्तमाङ्गेन the best of women, शोभितम् graced, गङ्गाजलनिषेवितम् given bath with waters of Ganga, तक्षकस्य Takshaka's, सम्भोगमिव as if united in delight.
explanation: (The shoulders) which resembled the coils of Takshaka (in chubbiness) a principal serpent, was graced by Sita while in bed, was bathed by the best of women with waters of Ganga.

shloka_text: संयुगेयुगसङ्काशंशत्रूणांशोकवर्धनम् । सुहृदानन्दनंदीर्घंसागरान्तव्यपाश्रयम् ।।6.21.6।।
transliteration: saṃyugeyugasaṅkāśaṃśatrūṇāṃśokavardhanam | suhṛdānandanaṃdīrghaṃsāgarāntavyapāśrayam
translation: दीर्घम् long, युगसङ्काशम् like the union of Yuga, संयुगे in war, शत्रूणाम् to the enemies, शोकवर्थनम् that which brings grief, सुहृदाम् to friends, नन्दनम् delightful, सागरान्तव्यपाश्रयम् like the earth bound by the ocean on all sides.
explanation: The shoulders were long like the union of Yugas, which brought grief to the enemies in war and delight to the friends, and like the earth bound by the ocean on all sides.

shloka_text: असत्याचपुनस्सव्यंज्याघातविगतत्वचम् । दक्षिणोदक्षिणंबाहुंमहापरिघसन्निभम् ।।6.21.7।। गोसहस्रप्रदारंमुपधायमहत्भुजम् । अद्यमेमरणंवादतरणंसागरस्यवा ।।6.21.8।। तिरामोमतिंकृत्वामहाबाहुर्महोदधिम् । अधिशिश्येचविधिवत्प्रयतोनियतोमुनिः ।।6.21.9।।
transliteration: asatyācapunassavyaṃjyāghātavigatatvacam | dakṣiṇodakṣiṇaṃbāhuṃmahāparighasannibham  gosahasrapradāraṃmupadhāyamahatbhujam | adyamemaraṇaṃvādataraṇaṃsāgarasyavā  tirāmomatiṃkṛtvāmahābāhurmahodadhim | adhiśiśyecavidhivatprayatoniyatomuniḥ
translation: महाबाहुः mighty armed, दक्षिणः to left, रामः Rama, अस्यता released, ज्याघातविगतत्वचम् hardened by the large number of arrows released, सव्यम् by it, बाहुम् by the arm, महापरिघसन्निभम् like the iron bar, गोसहस्रप्रदातारम् thousands of cows given as gift, महत् large, दक्षिणम् to the left, भुजम् arm, उपधाय by strokes, अद्य now, मे my, सागरस्य of the ocean तरणंवा or the crossing over, मरणंवा or death, इति thus, धृतिम् determined, कृत्वा having resolved, अत्र and then, विधिवत् accordingly, प्रयतो self restrained, मुनिः sage, नियतः one who is subdued, महादधिम् great ocean, अधिशिश्ये lay down.
explanation: The mighty armed Rama's arms were hardened like that of iron bars by the large number of arrows received by the left arm and strained by giving thousands of cows as gifts by the right arm. Rama was determined now to cross over the great ocean or meet the sea with death and lay down subdued and restrained like a sage.

shloka_text: असत्याचपुनस्सव्यंज्याघातविगतत्वचम् । दक्षिणोदक्षिणंबाहुंमहापरिघसन्निभम् ।।6.21.7।। गोसहस्रप्रदारंमुपधायमहत्भुजम् । अद्यमेमरणंवादतरणंसागरस्यवा ।।6.21.8।। तिरामोमतिंकृत्वामहाबाहुर्महोदधिम् । अधिशिश्येचविधिवत्प्रयतोनियतोमुनिः ।।6.21.9।।
transliteration: asatyācapunassavyaṃjyāghātavigatatvacam | dakṣiṇodakṣiṇaṃbāhuṃmahāparighasannibham  gosahasrapradāraṃmupadhāyamahatbhujam | adyamemaraṇaṃvādataraṇaṃsāgarasyavā  tirāmomatiṃkṛtvāmahābāhurmahodadhim | adhiśiśyecavidhivatprayatoniyatomuniḥ
translation: महाबाहुः mighty armed, दक्षिणः to left, रामः Rama, अस्यता released, ज्याघातविगतत्वचम् hardened by the large number of arrows released, सव्यम् by it, बाहुम् by the arm, महापरिघसन्निभम् like the iron bar, गोसहस्रप्रदातारम् thousands of cows given as gift, महत् large, दक्षिणम् to the left, भुजम् arm, उपधाय by strokes, अद्य now, मे my, सागरस्य of the ocean तरणंवा or the crossing over, मरणंवा or death, इति thus, धृतिम् determined, कृत्वा having resolved, अत्र and then, विधिवत् accordingly, प्रयतो self restrained, मुनिः sage, नियतः one who is subdued, महादधिम् great ocean, अधिशिश्ये lay down.
explanation: The mighty armed Rama's arms were hardened like that of iron bars by the large number of arrows received by the left arm and strained by giving thousands of cows as gifts by the right arm. Rama was determined now to cross over the great ocean or meet the sea with death and lay down subdued and restrained like a sage.

shloka_text: असत्याचपुनस्सव्यंज्याघातविगतत्वचम् । दक्षिणोदक्षिणंबाहुंमहापरिघसन्निभम् ।।6.21.7।। गोसहस्रप्रदारंमुपधायमहत्भुजम् । अद्यमेमरणंवादतरणंसागरस्यवा ।।6.21.8।। तिरामोमतिंकृत्वामहाबाहुर्महोदधिम् । अधिशिश्येचविधिवत्प्रयतोनियतोमुनिः ।।6.21.9।।
transliteration: asatyācapunassavyaṃjyāghātavigatatvacam | dakṣiṇodakṣiṇaṃbāhuṃmahāparighasannibham  gosahasrapradāraṃmupadhāyamahatbhujam | adyamemaraṇaṃvādataraṇaṃsāgarasyavā  tirāmomatiṃkṛtvāmahābāhurmahodadhim | adhiśiśyecavidhivatprayatoniyatomuniḥ
translation: महाबाहुः mighty armed, दक्षिणः to left, रामः Rama, अस्यता released, ज्याघातविगतत्वचम् hardened by the large number of arrows released, सव्यम् by it, बाहुम् by the arm, महापरिघसन्निभम् like the iron bar, गोसहस्रप्रदातारम् thousands of cows given as gift, महत् large, दक्षिणम् to the left, भुजम् arm, उपधाय by strokes, अद्य now, मे my, सागरस्य of the ocean तरणंवा or the crossing over, मरणंवा or death, इति thus, धृतिम् determined, कृत्वा having resolved, अत्र and then, विधिवत् accordingly, प्रयतो self restrained, मुनिः sage, नियतः one who is subdued, महादधिम् great ocean, अधिशिश्ये lay down.
explanation: The mighty armed Rama's arms were hardened like that of iron bars by the large number of arrows received by the left arm and strained by giving thousands of cows as gifts by the right arm. Rama was determined now to cross over the great ocean or meet the sea with death and lay down subdued and restrained like a sage.

shloka_text: तस्यरामस्यसुप्तस्यकुशास्तीर्णेमहीतले । नियमादप्रमत्तस्यनिशास्तिस्रोऽतिचक्रमुः ।।6.21.10।।
transliteration: tasyarāmasyasuptasyakuśāstīrṇemahītale | niyamādapramattasyaniśāstisro'ticakramuḥ
translation: नियमात् with vow, अप्रमत्तस्य kept himself alert, तस्य his, रामस्य Rama's, कुशास्तीर्णे on the kusa grass mat, महीतले on the ground, सुप्तस्य lying down, तिस्रः three, निशाः nights, अतिचक्रमुः rolled fast.
explanation: As Rama kept himself alert with a vow and lay on the kusa grass m at spread on the ground, three nights rolled fast.

shloka_text: सत्रिरात्रोषितस्तत्रनयज्ञोधर्मवत्सलः । उपासततदारामस्सागरंसरितांपतिम् ।।6.21.11।।
transliteration: satrirātroṣitastatranayajñodharmavatsalaḥ | upāsatatadārāmassāgaraṃsaritāṃpatim
translation: तदा then, तत्र there, नयज्ञः one having political foresight, धर्मवत्सलः lover of dharma, रामः Rama, त्रीरात्रोषितः spent three nights, सरितांपतिम् Lord of rivers, सागरम् the ocean, उपासत waiting upon.
explanation: Rama, a lover of dharma, who had political foresight, spent three nights waiting upon the ocean, the Lord of rivers.

shloka_text: नचदर्शयतेरूपंमन्दोरामस्यसागरः । प्रयतेनापिरामेणयथार्हमभिपूजितः ।।6.21.12।।
transliteration: nacadarśayaterūpaṃmandorāmasyasāgaraḥ | prayatenāpirāmeṇayathārhamabhipūjitaḥ
translation: प्रयतेन though selfrestrained, रामेण by Rama, यथार्हम् according to propriety, अभिपूजितः well respected, अपि also, मन्दः dull, सागरः the ocean, रामस्य to Rama, रूपम् real form, नचदर्शयते did not show.
explanation: Though Rama remained selfrestrained and respected the ocean well according to propriety, the ocean was dull and did not show its real form.

shloka_text: समुद्रस्यततःक्रुद्धोरामोरक्तान्तलोचनः । समीपस्थमुवाचेदंलक्ष्मणंशुभलक्ष्मणम् ।।6.21.13।।
transliteration: samudrasyatataḥkruddhorāmoraktāntalocanaḥ | samīpasthamuvācedaṃlakṣmaṇaṃśubhalakṣmaṇam
translation: ततः then, समुद्रस्य at the ocean, क्रुद्ध: enraged, रक्तान्तलोचनः eyes turned red, रामः Rama, समीपस्थम् went near, शुभलक्षणम् possessed of auspicious marks, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, इदम् thus, उवाच addressed.
explanation: Enraged at the ocean, Rama's eyes turned red. He went near Lakshmana who was endowed with auspicious marks and thus addressed.

shloka_text: अवलेपस्समुद्रस्यनदर्शयतियत्स्वयम् । प्रशमश्चक्षमाचैवआर्जवंप्रियवादिता ।।6.21.14।। असामर्थ्यंफल्नात्येतेनिर्गुणेषुसतांगुणाः ।
transliteration: avalepassamudrasyanadarśayatiyatsvayam | praśamaścakṣamācaivaārjavaṃpriyavāditā  asāmarthyaṃphalnātyetenirguṇeṣusatāṃguṇāḥ |
translation: यः who is it, स्वयम् by himself, नदर्शयति does not show up, समुद्रस्य ocean's, अवलेपः pride, प्रशमश्चैव calmness also, क्षमाचैव with forbearance, आर्जवम् straight forwardness, प्रियवादिता politeness of speech, एते all these, सताम् virtues, गुणाः qualities, निर्गुणेषु without attributes, असामर्थ्यफलाःहि construed indeed as incapability.
explanation: "Why is it that the ocean does not show up to me? Indeed, calmness, forbearance, straightforwardness, politeness of speech are all attributes of virtuous qualities and one without these attributes are considered incapable."

shloka_text: आत्मप्रशंसिनंदृष्टंधृष्टंविपरिथावकम् । सर्वत्रोत्सृष्टदण्डंचलोकस्सत्कुरुतेनरम् ।।6.21.15।।
transliteration: ātmapraśaṃsinaṃdṛṣṭaṃdhṛṣṭaṃviparithāvakam | sarvatrotsṛṣṭadaṇḍaṃcalokassatkurutenaram
translation: लोकः the world, आत्मप्रशंसिनम् praising one's own self, दुष्टम् wicked ones, धृष्टम् impudent, विपरिथावकम् an unchaste one, सर्वत्र all over उत्सृष्टदण्डंचनरम् one who goes about with a rod of punishment, सत्कुरुते treat with respect.
explanation: "Indeed, the world treats one with respect, who praises himself, as an impudent one, an unchaste one and one who goes about with a rod of punishment (not the one who is virtuous)."

shloka_text: नसाम्नाशक्यतेकीर्तिर्नसाम्नाशक्यतेयशः । प्राप्तुंलक्ष्मण लोकेऽस्मिन् ञ्जयोवारणमूर्धनि ।।6.21.16।।
transliteration: nasāmnāśakyatekīrtirnasāmnāśakyateyaśaḥ | prāptuṃlakṣmaṇa loke'smin ñjayovāraṇamūrdhani
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, अस्मिन् in this, लोके world, साम्ना in front, कीर्तिः popularity, प्राप्तुम् is attained, नशक्यते not possible, यशः fame, न not, रणमूर्धनि in battlefront, जयोवा victorious, न not.
explanation: "O Lakshmana Neither fame nor popularity can win a battle front in this world."

shloka_text: अद्यमद्बाणनिर्भग्नैर्मकरैर्मकरानिलयम् । निरुद्धतोयंसौमित्रेप्लवभदिःपश्यसर्वतः ।।6.21.17।।
transliteration: adyamadbāṇanirbhagnairmakarairmakarānilayam | niruddhatoyaṃsaumitreplavabhadiḥpaśyasarvataḥ
translation: सौमित्रे Saumithri, अद्य now, महद्बाणनिर्भग्नैः shattered by my ruthless arrows, प्लवबदिः jumping and floating, मकरैः crocodiles, सर्वतः all over, निरुद्दतोयम् water splashed all sides, मकरालयम् abode of crocodiles, पश्य witness.
explanation: "Saumithri Witness the crocodiles shattered by my ruthless arrows jumping and floating in the ocean with water splashed on all sides."

shloka_text: महाभोगानिमत्स्यानांकरिणांचकराह । भोगिनांपश्यनागानांमयाछिन्नानिलक्ष्मण ।।6.21.18।।
transliteration: mahābhogānimatsyānāṃkariṇāṃcakarāha | bhogināṃpaśyanāgānāṃmayāchinnānilakṣmaṇa
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, मया by me, छिन्नानि cut into pieces, भोगिनाम् serpents, नागानां serpents coiled, मत्स्यानाम् fishes, महाभोगानि huge snakes, करिणाम् sea elephants, काराह large, इह now here, पश्य see.
explanation: "Lakshmana See here the coils of serpents, huge snakes, fish and large sea elephants cut into pieces by me."

shloka_text: सशङ्खशुक्तिजालंसमीनमकरंतथा । अद्ययुद्धेनमहतासमुद्रंपरिशोषये ।।6.21.19।।
transliteration: saśaṅkhaśuktijālaṃsamīnamakaraṃtathā | adyayuddhenamahatāsamudraṃpariśoṣaye
translation: सशङ्खशुक्तिकाजालम् water with its shells, conchs, तथा so also, समीनमकरम् with fishes and crocodiles, समुद्रम् ocean, अद्य now, महता, great युद्धेन combat, परिशोषये will make it dry.
explanation: "I shall make the ocean dry up with its shells and conchs, fishes and crocodiles in this great combat."

shloka_text: क्षमयाहिसमायुक्तंमामयंमकरालयः । असमर्थंविजानातिधिक् क्षमामीदृशेजने ।।6.21.20।।
transliteration: kṣamayāhisamāyuktaṃmāmayaṃmakarālayaḥ | asamarthaṃvijānātidhik kṣamāmīdṛśejane
translation: क्षमया tolerance, समायुक्तम् remaining, माम् me, आयम् this, मकरालयः abode of fish, असमर्थम् incapable, विजानाति do not know, ईदृशे endowed with such qualities, जने people, क्षमाम् forbearance, धिक् show.
explanation: "By my being tolerant, this ocean treats me to be incapable. Endowed with such qualities of forbearance, I will show the people (ocean)."

shloka_text: नदर्शयतिसाम्नामेसागरोरूपमात्मनः ।।6.21.21।। चापमानयसौमित्रेशरांश्चाशीविषोपमान् । सागरंशोषयिष्यामिपद् भ्यांयान्तुप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.21.22।।
transliteration: nadarśayatisāmnāmesāgarorūpamātmanaḥ  cāpamānayasaumitreśarāṃścāśīviṣopamān | sāgaraṃśoṣayiṣyāmipad bhyāṃyāntuplavaṅgamāḥ
translation: सागरः ocean's, साम्ना to me, मे I, आत्मानम् its own form, नदर्शयिती not shown, सौमित्रे O Saumithri, चापम् bow, आशीविषोषमान् resembling venomous snake, शरांश्च arrows, आनय get, समुद्रम् ocean, शोषयिष्यामि will make it dry, प्लवङ्गमाः all the Vanaras, पद् ब्याम् by foot, यान्तु go.
explanation: "The ocean has not shown his own form to me. O Lakshmana Get the bow and venomous snake like arrows, I will dry up the ocean and the Vanaras can walk by foot and go."

shloka_text: नदर्शयतिसाम्नामेसागरोरूपमात्मनः ।।6.21.21।। चापमानयसौमित्रेशरांश्चाशीविषोपमान् । सागरंशोषयिष्यामिपद् भ्यांयान्तुप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.21.22।।
transliteration: nadarśayatisāmnāmesāgarorūpamātmanaḥ  cāpamānayasaumitreśarāṃścāśīviṣopamān | sāgaraṃśoṣayiṣyāmipad bhyāṃyāntuplavaṅgamāḥ
translation: सागरः ocean's, साम्ना to me, मे I, आत्मानम् its own form, नदर्शयिती not shown, सौमित्रे O Saumithri, चापम् bow, आशीविषोषमान् resembling venomous snake, शरांश्च arrows, आनय get, समुद्रम् ocean, शोषयिष्यामि will make it dry, प्लवङ्गमाः all the Vanaras, पद् ब्याम् by foot, यान्तु go.
explanation: "The ocean has not shown his own form to me. O Lakshmana Get the bow and venomous snake like arrows, I will dry up the ocean and the Vanaras can walk by foot and go."

shloka_text: अद्याक्षोभ्यमपिक्रुद्धःक्षोभयिष्यामिसागरम् । वेलासुकृतमर्यादंसहस्रोर्मिसमाकुलम् ।।6.21.23।। निर्मर्यादंकरिष्यामिसायायिकैर्वरुणालयम् । महार्णवंक्षोभयिष्येमहादानवसङ्कुलम् ।।6.21.24।।
transliteration: adyākṣobhyamapikruddhaḥkṣobhayiṣyāmisāgaram | velāsukṛtamaryādaṃsahasrormisamākulam  nirmaryādaṃkariṣyāmisāyāyikairvaruṇālayam | mahārṇavaṃkṣobhayiṣyemahādānavasaṅkulam
translation: क्रुद्ध: made to be angry, अद्य now, अक्षोभ्यमपि even though imperturbable, सागरम् ocean, क्षोभयिष्यामि will torment, वेलासु thousands, कृतमर्यादम् one who has limits, सहस्रोर्मिसमाकुलम् with thousands of waves, वरुणालयम् the ocean, an abode of Lord Varuna, निर्मर्यादम् cross its boundary, सायकैः with arrows, करिष्यामि will make it, महादानवसङ्कुलम् mighty demons, महार्णवम् great ocean, क्षोभयिष्ये will torment.
explanation: "(The ocean) Having made me angry, now I will torment the ocean even though it is imperturbable and has its limits. I will torment the ocean with its thousands of waves and mighty demons by my arrows and make the ocean cross its boundary."

shloka_text: अद्याक्षोभ्यमपिक्रुद्धःक्षोभयिष्यामिसागरम् । वेलासुकृतमर्यादंसहस्रोर्मिसमाकुलम् ।।6.21.23।। निर्मर्यादंकरिष्यामिसायायिकैर्वरुणालयम् । महार्णवंक्षोभयिष्येमहादानवसङ्कुलम् ।।6.21.24।।
transliteration: adyākṣobhyamapikruddhaḥkṣobhayiṣyāmisāgaram | velāsukṛtamaryādaṃsahasrormisamākulam  nirmaryādaṃkariṣyāmisāyāyikairvaruṇālayam | mahārṇavaṃkṣobhayiṣyemahādānavasaṅkulam
translation: क्रुद्ध: made to be angry, अद्य now, अक्षोभ्यमपि even though imperturbable, सागरम् ocean, क्षोभयिष्यामि will torment, वेलासु thousands, कृतमर्यादम् one who has limits, सहस्रोर्मिसमाकुलम् with thousands of waves, वरुणालयम् the ocean, an abode of Lord Varuna, निर्मर्यादम् cross its boundary, सायकैः with arrows, करिष्यामि will make it, महादानवसङ्कुलम् mighty demons, महार्णवम् great ocean, क्षोभयिष्ये will torment.
explanation: "(The ocean) Having made me angry, now I will torment the ocean even though it is imperturbable and has its limits. I will torment the ocean with its thousands of waves and mighty demons by my arrows and make the ocean cross its boundary."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वाधनुष्पाणिःक्रोधविस्फारितेक्षणः । बभूवरामोदुर्धर्षोयुगान्तानगिरिवज्वलन् ।।6.21.25।।
transliteration: evamuktvādhanuṣpāṇiḥkrodhavisphāritekṣaṇaḥ | babhūvarāmodurdharṣoyugāntānagirivajvalan
translation: एवम् in that manner, उक्त्वा having spoken, धनुष्पाणिः bows etc. क्रोधविस्फारितेक्षणः with flaming red eyes, रामः Rama, ज्वलन् burning, युगान्तानगिरिव like the flame at the end of the universe, दुर्धर्षः unassailable, बभूव seemed.
explanation: Having spoken like that, Rama with his flaming red eyes seemed like the flame at the end of the universe and unassailable.

shloka_text: सम्पीड्यचधनुर्घोरंकम्पयित्वाशरैर्जगत् । मुमोचविशिखानुग्रान्वज्रानिवशतक्रतुः ।।6.21.26।।
transliteration: sampīḍyacadhanurghoraṃkampayitvāśarairjagat | mumocaviśikhānugrānvajrānivaśatakratuḥ
translation: घोरम् terrific, धनुः bow, सम्पीड्यच bending, शरैः arrow, जगत् universe, कम्पयित्वा making to tremble, शतक्रतुः one who has performed a hundred sacrifices, वज्रानिव like Indra, उग्रान् frightful, विशिखान् arrows, मुमोच released.
explanation: Bending the terrific bow, he released frightful arrows like Indra (who released thunderbolts) who performed a hundred sacrifices.

shloka_text: तेज्वलन्तोमहावेगास्तेजसासायकोत्तमाः । प्रविशन्तिसमुद्रस्यसलिलंत्रस्तपन्नगम् ।।6.21.27।।
transliteration: tejvalantomahāvegāstejasāsāyakottamāḥ | praviśantisamudrasyasalilaṃtrastapannagam
translation: तेजसा glowing in brilliance, ज्वलन्तः flaming, वेगाः speedily, ते that, सायकोत्तमाः best among the arrows, त्रस्तपन्नगम् like the snakes, समुद्रस्य into the ocean, सलिलम् waters, प्रविशन्ति pierced.
explanation: Glowing in brilliance like flame, the arrows of the best among the arrows pierced like snakes into the water of the ocean.

shloka_text: तोयवेगस्समुद्रस्यसनक्रमकरोमहान् । सम्बभूवमहाघोरस्समारुतरवस्तदा ।।6.21.28।।
transliteration: toyavegassamudrasyasanakramakaromahān | sambabhūvamahāghorassamārutaravastadā
translation: समुद्रस्य ocean's, समीनमकरः with fishes and crocodiles, तदा similarly, समारुतरवः with wind, महान् powerful, सः that, तोयवेगः rush of water, महाघोरः terrible, बभूव seemed.
explanation: Then the ocean seemed terrible with the fish and crocodiles rushing out with the speed of water and powerful wind.

shloka_text: महोर्मिकुलाविततश्शङ्खजालसमावृतः । सधूमःपरिवृत्तोर्मिस्सहसासीन्महोदधिः ।।6.21.29।।
transliteration: mahormikulāvitataśśaṅkhajālasamāvṛtaḥ | sadhūmaḥparivṛttormissahasāsīnmahodadhiḥ
translation: सहसा all of a sudden, महोदधिः great ocean, महोर्मिजालचलितः with the movement of the water, शङ्खजालसमावृतः filled with conchs and shells, सधूमः terrific smoke, परिवृत्तोर्मिः whirling round and rising up, आसीत् played around.
explanation: With the movement of the sea water filled with the conchs and shells suddenly terrific smoke whirling round and rising played around.

shloka_text: व्यथिताःपन्नगाश्चासदनीप्तास्यादीप्तलोचनाः । दानवाश्चमहावीर्याःपाताळतलवासिनः ।।6.21.30।।
transliteration: vyathitāḥpannagāścāsadanīptāsyādīptalocanāḥ | dānavāścamahāvīryāḥpātāḻatalavāsinaḥ
translation: दीप्तास्याः those blazing, दीप्तलोचनाः ones with glowing eyes, पन्नगाः snakes, पाताळतलवासिनः those who reside in underworld, महावीर्याः highly valiant ones, दानवाश्च and the demons, व्यथित्याः oppressed आसन् became.
explanation: Those snakes with blazing hoods and glowing eyes residing in the underworld and the demons became oppressed.

shloka_text: ऊर्मयस्सिन्धुराजस्यसनक्रमकरास्तथा । विन्द्यमन्दरसङ्काशास्समुत्पेतुस्सहस्रशः ।।6.21.31।।
transliteration: ūrmayassindhurājasyasanakramakarāstathā | vindyamandarasaṅkāśāssamutpetussahasraśaḥ
translation: तथा so also, सिन्दुराजस्य king of rivers, सनक्रमकराः which were like, विन्द्यमन्दरसङ्काशाः Vindhya and Mandara mountain peaks, ऊर्मयः waves, सहस्रशः in thousands, समुत्पेतुः rose up.
explanation: Thousands of waves of the ocean rose like the peaks of Vindhya and Mandara mountains.

shloka_text: आघूर्णिततरङ्गौघस्सम्भ्रान्तोरगराक्षसः । उद्वर्तितमहाग्राहस्संवृत्तस्सलिलाशयः ।।6.21.32।।
transliteration: āghūrṇitataraṅgaughassambhrāntoragarākṣasaḥ | udvartitamahāgrāhassaṃvṛttassalilāśayaḥ
translation: आघूर्णिततरङ्गौघः the waves tossing and whirling about, सम्भ्रान्तोरगराक्षसः the agitated Nagas and Rakshasas, उद्वर्तितमहाग्राहः thrown up highly disturbed, सलिलाशयः from the waters, सघोषः made great sound.
explanation: The waves rose up tossing and whirling about. The agitated Nagas and Rakshasas were thrown up by a highly disturbed ocean that produced a great sound.

shloka_text: ततस्तुतंराघवमुग्रवेगंप्रकर्षमाणंधनुरप्रमेयम् । सौमित्रिरुत्पत्यसमुच्छवसन्तंमामेतिचोक्त्वादनुराललम्बे ।।6.21.33।।
transliteration: tatastutaṃrāghavamugravegaṃprakarṣamāṇaṃdhanuraprameyam | saumitrirutpatyasamucchavasantaṃmāmeticoktvādanurālalambe
translation: ततः then, सौमित्रिः Saumithri, उत्पत्य got up, उग्रवेगम् at high speed, अप्रमेयम् immeasurably great, धनुः bow, प्रकर्षमाणम् was stretching exceedingly, विनिश्श्वनन्तम् breathing hard in anger, राघवम् at Rama, मामाइति that is enough that is enough, उक्त्वा saying, धनुः bow, आललम्बे seized.
explanation: Then Saumithri got up and rushed very fast to Rama who was stretching his bow exceedingly and breathing hard in anger and said, 'no more, no more' and seized the bow. ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेएकविंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the twenty first sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथोवाचरघुश्रेष्टस्सागरंदारुणंवचः । अद्यत्वांशोषयिष्यामिसपाताळंमहार्णव: ।।6.22.1।।
transliteration: athovācaraghuśreṣṭassāgaraṃdāruṇaṃvacaḥ | adyatvāṃśoṣayiṣyāmisapātāḻaṃmahārṇava:
translation: अथ and thereafter, रघुश्रेष्ट the best one among Raghu's, सागरम् to ocean, दारुणम् terrific, वचः words, उवाच uttered, महार्णव ocean, अद्य now, सपाताळम् that under world, त्वाम् you, शोषयिष्यामि will make it dry.
explanation: Thereafter, Rama uttered, "I shall make you dry up to the underworld", to the ocean that made his terrific presence.
comments: The Sun god appears before Rama and sustains the construction of the bridge by Nila. Rama crosses the ocean accompanied by Lakshmana and the army.

shloka_text: शरनिर्दग्धतोयस्यपरिशुष्कस्यसागर: । मयाशोषितसत्त्वस्यपांसुरुत्पद्यतेमहान् ।।6.22.2।।
transliteration: śaranirdagdhatoyasyapariśuṣkasyasāgara: | mayāśoṣitasattvasyapāṃsurutpadyatemahān
translation: सागर O ocean, मया by me, शरनिर्दग्दतोयस्य water dried up by the arrows, परिशुष्कस्य when it is dried up, शोषितसत्त्वस्य dried up to the core, महान् huge, सांसुः sand, उत्पद्यते will appear.
explanation: "O Ocean When your water is dried up to the core by my arrows, huge sand will appear."

shloka_text: मत्कार्मुकविसृष्टेवशरवर्षेणसागर । पारंतेऽद्यगमिष्यन्तिपदभिरेवप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.22.3।।
transliteration: matkārmukavisṛṣṭevaśaravarṣeṇasāgara | pāraṃte'dyagamiṣyantipadabhirevaplavaṅgamāḥ
translation: सागर O Ocean, मत्कार्मुकविसृष्टेन all the creatures inhabiting you, शरवर्षेण by the rain of arrows, प्लवङ्गमाः monkeys, पदभिरेव to the other side of the shore, परंअद्य now to the other, गमिष्यन्ति will go.
explanation: "O Ocean, now the monkeys will go to the other side of the shore on your drying up with all the creatures inhabiting you by the rain of arrows showered by me."

shloka_text: विचिन्वन्नाभिजानासिपौरुषंनापिविक्रमम् । दानवालयसन्तापंमत्तोनाधिगमिष्यसि ।।6.22.4।।
transliteration: vicinvannābhijānāsipauruṣaṃnāpivikramam | dānavālayasantāpaṃmattonādhigamiṣyasi
translation: दानवालय abode of demons, विचिन्वन् abode, पौरुषम् valour, नाभिजानासि, not known, विक्रममपि even prowess, न not, मत्तः mine, सन्तापम् sorrow, गमिष्यसिनाम will face from me.
explanation: "You, who are the abode of demons are not aware of my valour and prowess. You are not aware of the sorrow that you will face from me."

shloka_text: ब्राह्मेणास्त्रेणसंयोज्यब्रह्मदण्डनिभम् शरम् । संयोज्यधनुषिश्रेष्ठविचकर्षमहाबलः ।।6.22.5।।
transliteration: brāhmeṇāstreṇasaṃyojyabrahmadaṇḍanibham śaram | saṃyojyadhanuṣiśreṣṭhavicakarṣamahābalaḥ
translation: महाबलः strong, ब्रह्मदण्डनिभम् resembling the rod of punishment of the creator, Brahma, शरम् arrow, ब्राह्मेणअस्त्रेण energized by Brahma, संयोज्य stretched, श्रेष्ठे best one, धनुषि by the bow, संयोज्य stretched, विचकर्ष released.
explanation: Rama proceeded to stretch the mighty bow that resembled the rod of punishment of Brahma energized by Brahma and released that best of bows.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्विविकृष्टेसहसाराघवेणशरासने । रोदसीसम्पफालेवपर्वताश्चचकम्पिरे ।।6.22.6।।
transliteration: tasminvivikṛṣṭesahasārāghaveṇaśarāsane | rodasīsampaphālevaparvatāścacakampire
translation: तस्मिन् by that, शरासने arrows from the bow, राघवेण by Rama, विकृष्टे pulled out, सहसा at once, रोदसी from the sky, सम्पफालेन to the earth, पर्वताश्च even mountains, चकम्पिरे trembled.
explanation: When Rama released the arrows from the bow, at once the sky to the earth including mountains trembled.

shloka_text: तमश्चलोकमाव्रतेदिशश्चवचकाशिरे । प्रतिचुक्षुभिरेचाशुसरांसिसरितस्तथा ।।6.22.7।।
transliteration: tamaścalokamāvratediśaścavacakāśire | praticukṣubhirecāśusarāṃsisaritastathā
translation: तदा then, तमश्च by darkness, लोकम् world, अव्रते engulfed, दिशश्च even the directions, नचकाशिरे not noticeable, चाशसरांसिसरितः Furthermore rivers, प्रतिचुक्षुभिरे got agitated.
explanation: Then darkness engulfed the world, the directions were not noticeable and further the rivers were agitated.

shloka_text: तिर्यक्चसहानेक्षत्रैस्सङ्गतौचन्द्रभास्करौ । भास्करांशुभिरादीप्तंतमसाचसमावृतम् ।।6.22.8।। चकाशेतदाकाशमुल्काशतविदीपितम् । अन्तरिक्षाच्चनिर्घातानिर्जग्मुरतुलस्वनाः ।।6.22.9।।
transliteration: tiryakcasahānekṣatraissaṅgataucandrabhāskarau | bhāskarāṃśubhirādīptaṃtamasācasamāvṛtam  cakāśetadākāśamulkāśatavidīpitam | antarikṣāccanirghātānirjagmuratulasvanāḥ
translation: चन्द्रभास्करौ the Sun and moon, नक्षत्रेःसह with stars, तिर्यक् obliquely, सङ्गतौ moved, भास्करांशुभिः even the Sun light, आदीप्तम् not shining, तमसाच on account of darkness, समावृतम् engulfed all over, तत् then, आकाशम् sky, उल्काशत by the meteors, विदीपितम् again lighted, प्रचकाशे shone, अन्तरिक्षात् from the sky, अतुलस्वनाः unparalleled, निर्घाताः thunder, निर्जग्मुः shot forth.
explanation: The Sun and moon moved obliquely (from south to North) along with the stars. On account of the darkness that covered even the sun was not shining. The sky lighted by the meteors shone and unparalleled thunder shot forth.

shloka_text: तिर्यक्चसहानेक्षत्रैस्सङ्गतौचन्द्रभास्करौ । भास्करांशुभिरादीप्तंतमसाचसमावृतम् ।।6.22.8।। चकाशेतदाकाशमुल्काशतविदीपितम् । अन्तरिक्षाच्चनिर्घातानिर्जग्मुरतुलस्वनाः ।।6.22.9।।
transliteration: tiryakcasahānekṣatraissaṅgataucandrabhāskarau | bhāskarāṃśubhirādīptaṃtamasācasamāvṛtam  cakāśetadākāśamulkāśatavidīpitam | antarikṣāccanirghātānirjagmuratulasvanāḥ
translation: चन्द्रभास्करौ the Sun and moon, नक्षत्रेःसह with stars, तिर्यक् obliquely, सङ्गतौ moved, भास्करांशुभिः even the Sun light, आदीप्तम् not shining, तमसाच on account of darkness, समावृतम् engulfed all over, तत् then, आकाशम् sky, उल्काशत by the meteors, विदीपितम् again lighted, प्रचकाशे shone, अन्तरिक्षात् from the sky, अतुलस्वनाः unparalleled, निर्घाताः thunder, निर्जग्मुः shot forth.
explanation: The Sun and moon moved obliquely (from south to North) along with the stars. On account of the darkness that covered even the sun was not shining. The sky lighted by the meteors shone and unparalleled thunder shot forth.

shloka_text: वपुस्फुरुश्चघनादिव्यादिविमारुतपङ् ख्कयः । बभञ्जचतदावृक्षान्जलदानुद्वहन्नपिः ।।6.22.10।।
transliteration: vapusphuruścaghanādivyādivimārutapaṅ khkayaḥ | babhañjacatadāvṛkṣānjaladānudvahannapiḥ
translation: दिव्यमारुतपङ् ख्कयः terrific wind blew, वपुस्फुरुश्चघनादिव्यादि breaking forth the clouds, तदा then, जलदान् abode of cold water, उद्वहन् taking away in upward direction, अपिः even, वृक्षान् trees, बभञ्जच broke into.
explanation: Then terrific wind blew breaking forth the clouds, which is an abode of cold water, taking them away in upward direction breaking trees.

shloka_text: अरुजंश्चैनशैलाग्राशनिखराणिबभञ्जनः । दिविस्पृशोमहमेघास्सङ्गतास्समहास्वनाः ।।6.22.11।। मुमुचुर्वैद्युताननगींस्तेमहाशनयस्तदा ।
transliteration: arujaṃścainaśailāgrāśanikharāṇibabhañjanaḥ | divispṛśomahameghāssaṅgatāssamahāsvanāḥ  mumucurvaidyutānanagīṃstemahāśanayastadā |
translation: शैलाग्रान् mountain peaks, अरुजन् च sounding, शिखराणि tops, बभञ्जच breaking, महामेधा huge cloud, दिवि sky, संगताः collecting together, महास्वनाः having extraordinary speed, वैद्युतान् fire of lightning, अनगीन् from the sky, मुमुचुः clouds, तदा then, ते those, महाशनयः loud sound.
explanation: Huge clouds collected were moving at extraordinary speed in the sky breaking mountain peaks. Those clouds in the sky sent forth fire of lightning making a loud sound.

shloka_text: यानिभूतानिदृश्यानिचुक्रुशुश्चाशनेसमम् ।।6.22.12।। अदृश्यानिचभूतानिमुमुचुर्भैरवस्वनम् । शिशियरेचाभिभूतानिसन्त्रस्ताम्यद्विजन्तिच ।।6.22.13।। सम्प्रविव्यथिरेचापिवचपस्पन्दिरेभयात् ।
transliteration: yānibhūtānidṛśyānicukruśuścāśanesamam  adṛśyānicabhūtānimumucurbhairavasvanam | śiśiyarecābhibhūtānisantrastāmyadvijantica  sampravivyathirecāpivacapaspandirebhayāt |
translation: दृश्यानि that which could be seen, यानि those, भूतानि creatures, आशनेसमम् remained still, चुकुश्रुः suffering pain, अदृश्यानि that which are seen, भूतानिच beings also, भैरवस्वन् like the devils and ghosts, मुमुचुः clouds, अभिभूतानि few other creatures, सन्त्रस्तानि from their place, उद्विजन्तिच came to appear, शिशियरेच even though cold, सम्प्रविव्यथिरेचापि although were together, भयात् in fear, नचपस्पन्दिरे were even thrown off.
explanation: The creatures like humans etc. That could be seen and those that could not be seen like devils and ghosts remained still out of fear. Few other creatures came out of their place even though it was cold. Some were thrown off from their habitation in fear although they were together.

shloka_text: यानिभूतानिदृश्यानिचुक्रुशुश्चाशनेसमम् ।।6.22.12।। अदृश्यानिचभूतानिमुमुचुर्भैरवस्वनम् । शिशियरेचाभिभूतानिसन्त्रस्ताम्यद्विजन्तिच ।।6.22.13।। सम्प्रविव्यथिरेचापिवचपस्पन्दिरेभयात् ।

shloka_text: सहाभूतैस्सतोयोर्मिस्सनागस्सहराक्षसः ।।6.22.14।। सहसाऽभूत्ततोवेगाबदीमवेगोमहोदधिः । योजनंव्यतिचक्रामवेलामन्यत्रसम्ल्पवात् ।।6.22.15।।
transliteration: sahābhūtaissatoyormissanāgassaharākṣasaḥ  sahasā'bhūttatovegābadīmavegomahodadhiḥ | yojanaṃvyaticakrāmavelāmanyatrasamlpavāt
translation: ततः thereafter, सतोयोर्मिः those waves of water, सहाभूतै with its creatures, सनागः with serpents, सहराक्षसः with the demons, महोदधि great ocean, सहसा at once, भीमवेगः at terrific speed, अभूत् unprecedented, वेगात् speed, सम्ल्पवात् thrown out, अन्यत्रवेलाम् by the other tides, योजनम् one yojana, व्यतिचक्राम was thrown.
explanation: There after those waves of water with its creatures, serpents and demons were at once thrown off at terrific speed that was unprecedented. They were thrown beyond a yojana by the high tides.

shloka_text: सहाभूतैस्सतोयोर्मिस्सनागस्सहराक्षसः ।।6.22.14।। सहसाऽभूत्ततोवेगाबदीमवेगोमहोदधिः । योजनंव्यतिचक्रामवेलामन्यत्रसम्ल्पवात् ।।6.22.15।।

translation: ततः thereafter, सतोयोर्मिः those waves of water, सहाभूतै with its creatures, सनागः with serpents, सहराक्षसः with the demons, महोदधि great ocean, सहसा at once, भीमवेगः at terrific speed, अभूत् unprecedented, वेगात् speed, सम्ल्पवात् thrown out, अन्यत्रवेलाम् by the other tides, योजनम् one yojana, व्यतिचक्राम was thrown.

shloka_text: तंतदासमतिक्रान्तंनातिचक्रामराघवः । समुद्धतममित्रघ्नोरामोनदनदीपतिम् ।।6.22.16।।
transliteration: taṃtadāsamatikrāntaṃnāticakrāmarāghavaḥ | samuddhatamamitraghnorāmonadanadīpatim
translation: राघवः Rama, अमित्रघ्नः destroyer of foes, रामः Rama, तदा then, समतिक्रान्तम् transgressing, समुद्धतम् overweening, तम् them, नदनदीपतिम् Lord of rivers, नातिचक्राम not go far.
explanation: Rama the destroyer of foes did not attempt at the ocean that went far from the boundary, which was transgressing and overweening.

shloka_text: ततोमथ्यात्समुद्रस्यसागरस्स्वयमुत्थितः । उदयन् हिमहाशैलान्मेरोरिवदिवाकरः ।।6.22.17।।
transliteration: tatomathyātsamudrasyasāgarassvayamutthitaḥ | udayan himahāśailānmerorivadivākaraḥ
translation: ततः then, महामेरोः over the mighty Meru, उदयं rising, दिवाकरःइव like the Sun, सागरः Lord of ocean, समुद्रस्य ocean's, मध्यात् middle, स्वयम् himself, उत्थितः risen.
explanation: Then Sagara, the Lord of the ocean himself rising like the Sun over the mighty Meru Mountain rose from the middle of the ocean.

shloka_text: पन्नगैस्सहदीप्तास्यैस्समुद्रःप्रत्यदृश्यत । स्निग्धवैढूर्यसङ्काशोजाम्बूनदविभूषणः ।।6.22.18।।
transliteration: pannagaissahadīptāsyaissamudraḥpratyadṛśyata | snigdhavaiḍhūryasaṅkāśojāmbūnadavibhūṣaṇaḥ
translation: स्निग्धवैदूर्यसङ्काशः bright like Vaidurya stone, जम्बूनदविभूषणः decked in pure gold, समुद्रः Lord of the ocean, दीप्तास्यैः as though blazing, पन्नगैरक्तमाल्यास्सह with serpents, प्रदृश्यत appeared.
explanation: Then the Lord of the Ocean shining like the Vaidurya stone decked in pure gold as if blazing appeared along with serpents.

shloka_text: रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरःपद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणः । सर्वपुष्पमयींदिव्यांशिरसाधारयन् स्रजम् ।।6.22.19।। जातरूपमयैश्चैवतपनीयविभूषितैः । आत्मजानांचरत्नानांभूषितोभूषणोत्तमैः ।।6.22.20।। धातुभिर्मण्डितश्शैलोविविधैर्हिमवानिव । एकावलीमध्यगतंतरलंपाटलप्रभम् ।।6.22.21।। विपुलेनोरसा बिभ्रत्कौस्तुभस्य सहोदरम् । अघूर्णिततरङ्गौघःकालिकानिलसङ्गुलः ।।6.22.22।। गङ्गासिन्दुप्रधाननाभिरापगाभिस्समावृतः । देवतानांसरूपाभिर्नानारूपाभिरीश्वरः ।।6.22.23।। सागरस्समुपक्रम्यपूर्वमाम्नत्यरवीर्यवान् । अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यंराघवंशरपाणिनम् ।।6.22.24।।
transliteration: raktamālyāmbaradharaḥpadmapatranibhekṣaṇaḥ | sarvapuṣpamayīṃdivyāṃśirasādhārayan srajam  jātarūpamayaiścaivatapanīyavibhūṣitaiḥ | ātmajānāṃcaratnānāṃbhūṣitobhūṣaṇottamaiḥ  dhātubhirmaṇḍitaśśailovividhairhimavāniva | ekāvalīmadhyagataṃtaralaṃpāṭalaprabham  vipulenorasā bibhratkaustubhasya sahodaram | aghūrṇitataraṅgaughaḥkālikānilasaṅgulaḥ  gaṅgāsindupradhānanābhirāpagābhissamāvṛtaḥ | devatānāṃsarūpābhirnānārūpābhirīśvaraḥ  sāgarassamupakramyapūrvamāmnatyaravīryavān | abravītprāñjalirvākyaṃrāghavaṃśarapāṇinam
translation: रत्क्तमाल्याम्बरधरः clad in red coloured robes, पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणः whose eyes were like lotus petals, शिरसा on the head, सर्वपुष्पमयीम् wearing different kinds of flowers, दिव्याम् wonderful, प्रजम् wreath, धारयन् wearing, जातरूपमयैश्चैव of polished gold, तपनीयविभूषणैः decked in shining ornaments, आत्मजानाम् from his own territory, रत्नानाम् precious gems, भूषणोत्तमैः best of ornaments, भूषितः decked, मण्डितः with different kinds of minerals, हिमनान् शैलःइव resembled the Himalaya mountain, एकावलीमध्यगतम् in the midst of pearl necklace on his bosom, पाण्डरप्रभम् shedding white lustre, कौस्तुभस्यसहोदरम् resembling Kausthuba (a precious jewel with emerald gem worn by Lord Vishnu), तरलम् hanging necklace, विपुलेन broad, उपसा near, बिभ्रत् moving, अघूर्णिततरङ्गौघः with several tides rising up, कालिकानिलसङ्कुलः with multitude of tides touching the of clouds, देवतानाम् goddesses, सरूपाभि forms also, नानारूपाभिः of diverse forms, गङ्गासिन्दुप्रधानाभिः Ganga and Sindhu, such important rivers, आपगाभिः coming near, समावृतः surrounded by, ईश्वरः Lord, वीर्यवान् valiant one, सागरः Sagara, समुपक्रम्य all coming near, पूर्वम् first, आम्नत्यर greeting, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hand s, शरपाणिनम् one who held the arrow, राघवम् to Rama, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Clad in red coloured robes, endowed with lotus petal like eyes having a wonderful wreath of diverse flowers on head, decked in shining ornaments of polished gold encrusted with precious gems from his own territory, he resembled the Himalayan Mountain with minerals. He had a hanging pearl necklace in the centre of his bosom shedding white lustre that resembled the Kausthuba of Lord Vishnu. With several tides moving near, and multitude of tides reaching the clouds threatening, surrounded by Goddesses of several forms and deities of important rivers like Ganga and Sindhu, the valiant Lord of the ocean greeted with folded palms and spoke these words to Rama who was wielding an arrow in his hand.
