explanation: "On the Mandara mountain Vishwakarma gave a boon to my mother. I am that Vishwakarma's own son, and I am like him at work by that cause. I have put in my memory all about the ocean. I am aware of the truth of the ocean. I could not speak of my qualities unless questioned. I can build a bridge over the abode of Varuna.Right away let the Vanara leaders get the material required for building the bridge (said Nala)."

shloka_text: ततोविसृष्टारामेणसर्वतोहरियूथपाः । अभिपेतुर्महारण्यंहृष्टाश्शतसहस्रशः ।।6.22.52।।
transliteration: tatovisṛṣṭārāmeṇasarvatohariyūthapāḥ | abhipeturmahāraṇyaṃhṛṣṭāśśatasahasraśaḥ
translation: ततः then, रामेण by Rama, विसृष्टाः directed, रियूथपाः Vanara troop leaders, हृष्टाः gladly, शतसहस्रशः hundred thousand, महारण्यम् huge forest, सर्वतः all over, अभ्युत्पेतुः sprang up.
explanation: Then directed by Rama the Vanara troop leaders in hundreds and thousands sprang up gladly all over the huge forest.

shloka_text: तेनगान्नगसङ्काशाश्शाखामृगगणर्षभाः । बभञ्जुःवानरास्तत्रप्रचकर्षुश्चसागरम् ।।6.22.53।।
transliteration: tenagānnagasaṅkāśāśśākhāmṛgagaṇarṣabhāḥ | babhañjuḥvānarāstatrapracakarṣuścasāgaram
translation: नगसङ्काशाः mountain like, ते those, शाखामृगगणर्षभाः bulls among Vanaras, तत there upon, नगान् from the mountain, पादपान् roots of trees, बभञ्जुः collected, सागरम् into the sea, प्रचकर्षुश्च started moving.
explanation: Mountain like bodied Vanara bulls there upon started collecting roots of trees from the foot of mountain and moved them into the sea.

shloka_text: तेसालैश्चाश्वकर्णैश्चधवैशैश्चवानराः । कुटजैरर्जुनैस्तालैस्तिलकैस्न्तिशैरपि ।।6.22.54।। बिल्वकैस्सप्तपर्णैश्चकर्णिकारैश्चसुपुष्पितैः । चूतैश्चाशोकवृक्षैश्चसागरंसमपूरयन् ।।6.22.55।।
transliteration: tesālaiścāśvakarṇaiścadhavaiśaiścavānarāḥ | kuṭajairarjunaistālaistilakaisntiśairapi  bilvakaissaptaparṇaiścakarṇikāraiścasupuṣpitaiḥ | cūtaiścāśokavṛkṣaiścasāgaraṃsamapūrayan
translation: वानराः Vanaras, सालैश्च sala trees, अश्वकर्णैश्च as vakarna trees, धवैः dhava trees, वंशैश्च bamboo, कुटजैः kutaja, अर्जुनैः arjuna, तालैः palmira, तिलकैः tilaka, न्तिशैरपि trisaira, बिल्वकैः bilva, सप्तपर्णैश्च and saptaparni, पुष्पितैःकर्णिकारैः karnikara blossoms, चूतैश्च mango, अशोकवृक्षैश्च and ashoka trees, सागरम् into ocean, पर्यपूरयन् brought and dumped.
explanation: The Vanaras brought sala, asvakarna, dhava, bamboo, kutaja arjuna, palmira, tilaka, trisaira, bilva, saptaparni trees karnikara plants with blossoms, mango trees and ashoka trees and dumped into the ocean.

shloka_text: तेसालैश्चाश्वकर्णैश्चधवैशैश्चवानराः । कुटजैरर्जुनैस्तालैस्तिलकैस्न्तिशैरपि ।।6.22.54।। बिल्वकैस्सप्तपर्णैश्चकर्णिकारैश्चसुपुष्पितैः । चूतैश्चाशोकवृक्षैश्चसागरंसमपूरयन् ।।6.22.55।।
transliteration: tesālaiścāśvakarṇaiścadhavaiśaiścavānarāḥ | kuṭajairarjunaistālaistilakaisntiśairapi  bilvakaissaptaparṇaiścakarṇikāraiścasupuṣpitaiḥ | cūtaiścāśokavṛkṣaiścasāgaraṃsamapūrayan
translation: वानराः Vanaras, सालैश्च sala trees, अश्वकर्णैश्च as vakarna trees, धवैः dhava trees, वंशैश्च bamboo, कुटजैः kutaja, अर्जुनैः arjuna, तालैः palmira, तिलकैः tilaka, न्तिशैरपि trisaira, बिल्वकैः bilva, सप्तपर्णैश्च and saptaparni, पुष्पितैःकर्णिकारैः karnikara blossoms, चूतैश्च mango, अशोकवृक्षैश्च and ashoka trees, सागरम् into ocean, पर्यपूरयन् brought and dumped.
explanation: The Vanaras brought sala, asvakarna, dhava, bamboo, kutaja arjuna, palmira, tilaka, trisaira, bilva, saptaparni trees karnikara plants with blossoms, mango trees and ashoka trees and dumped into the ocean.

shloka_text: समूलांश्चविमूलांश्चपादपान् हरिसत्तमाः । इन्द्रकेतूनिवोद्यम्यप्रजह्रूर्वानरास्तरून् ।।6.22.56।।
transliteration: samūlāṃścavimūlāṃścapādapān harisattamāḥ | indraketūnivodyamyaprajahrūrvānarāstarūn
translation: हरिसत्तमाः foremost of the Vanaras, समूलान् च along with the roots, विमूलान् च some without roots, पादपान् trees, इन्द्रकेतूनिव like Indra's flagstaff, उद्यम्य lifting up, प्रजह्रुः hurled वानरास्तरून् Vanaras thrown down (into the sea)
explanation: Lifting some trees with roots and some without roots like the staff of Indra's flag, Vanaras hurled down the trees into the sea.

shloka_text: ताळानदाडिमगुल्मांश्चनारिकेळन्विभीतकान् । वकुलान्कदिरान्निम्बान्समाजह्रुस्समन्ततः ।।6.22.57।।
transliteration: tāḻānadāḍimagulmāṃścanārikeḻanvibhītakān | vakulānkadirānnimbānsamājahrussamantataḥ
translation: ताळान् palmira, दाडिमगुल्मांश्च dadima trees, नारिकेळविभीतकान् coconut trees, करीरान् karira, बकुलान् bakula, निम्बान् nimba, समन्ततः brought all of them, समाजह्रुः and dropped into the ocean.
explanation: They brought palmira, dadima, coconut, karira, bakula and nimba trees and dropped all of them into the ocean.

shloka_text: हस्तिमतान्महाकायाःपाषाणांश्चमहाबलाः । पर्वतांश्चसमुत्पाट्ययन्स्सरैःपरिवहन्तिच ।।6.22.58।।
transliteration: hastimatānmahākāyāḥpāṣāṇāṃścamahābalāḥ | parvatāṃścasamutpāṭyayanssaraiḥparivahantica
translation: महाकायाः of huge body, महाबालाः strong, हस्तिमात्रान् like elephants, पाषाणान् stones, पर्वतांश्च mountains, समुत्पाट्य collecting and lifting up, यन्स्रैः by machines, परिवहन्तिच transported.
explanation: The Vanaras of huge body size and strong like elephants collected stones and mountains, lifted them, and transported into the sea.

shloka_text: प्रक्षिप्यमाणैरचलैस्सहसाजलमुद्दृतम् । समुत्ससर्पआकाशमवासर्पत्ततस्ततः ।।6.22.59।।
transliteration: prakṣipyamāṇairacalaissahasājalamuddṛtam | samutsasarpaākāśamavāsarpattatastataḥ
translation: सहसा at once, प्रक्षिप्यमाणैः thrown up, अचलैः mountains, उद्दृतम् rose up, जलम् water, आकाशम् sky, समुत्ससर्प touched, ततः then, पुनः again, अवासर्पत् spread
explanation: At once the water threw up (by dropping the mountains) rose, touching the sky and spreading.

shloka_text: समुद्रंक्षोभयामासुर्वानराश्चस्समन्ततः । सूत्राण्यन्येप्रगृह्णान्तिव्यायतंशतयोजनम् ।।6.22.60।।
transliteration: samudraṃkṣobhayāmāsurvānarāścassamantataḥ | sūtrāṇyanyepragṛhṇāntivyāyataṃśatayojanam
translation: समन्ततः all over, निपतन्तः on account of throwing, समुद्रम् into the sea, क्षोभयामासुः stirred up, अन्ये others, शतयोजनम् a hundred yojanas, आयतम् breadth, सूत्राणि by rope, प्रगृह्णन्ति held.
explanation: On account of throwing into the sea it got stirred up Others held the rope over a hundred yojanas in breadth (to make it even).

shloka_text: नलश्चक्रेमहासेतुंमध्येनदनदीपतेः । सतदाक्रियतेसेतुर्वानरैर्घोरकर्मभिः ।।6.22.61।।
transliteration: nalaścakremahāsetuṃmadhyenadanadīpateḥ | satadākriyateseturvānarairghorakarmabhiḥ
translation: नलः Nala, नदनदीपतेः Lord of rivers, मध्ये centre, महासेतुम् huge bridge, चक्रे started, तदा then, घोरकर्मभिः terrific task, वानरैः with Vanaras, सेतुः bridge, क्रियते built.
explanation: Nala started the task of building the huge bridge in the centre of the ocean with Vanaras.

shloka_text: दण्डानन्येप्रगृह्णन्तिविचिन्वन्तितथापरे ।।6.22.62।। वानरैश्शतशस्तत्ररामस्याज्ञापुरस्सराः । मेघाभैःपर्वताग्रैश्चतृणैःकाष्ठैर्बबन्धिरे ।।6.22.63।।
transliteration: daṇḍānanyepragṛhṇantivicinvantitathāpare  vānaraiśśataśastatrarāmasyājñāpurassarāḥ | meghābhaiḥparvatāgraiścatṛṇaiḥkāṣṭhairbabandhire
translation: अन्ये others, दण्डान् sticks, प्रगृह्णन्ति holding, तथा in the same way, अपरे some others, विचिन्वन्ति following, रामस्य of Rama, आज्ञापुरस्सरैः the command in front, शतशः in hundreds, मेघाभिः like clouds, पर्वताग्रैश्च like top of mountains, वानरैः with Vanaras, तृणैः reeds, काष्ठैश्च logs of wood, बबन्धिरे built.
explanation: Others held sticks and some held logs of wood and reeds following the command of Rama, hundreds of Vanaras who looked like clouds and mountain tops built the bridge.

shloka_text: दण्डानन्येप्रगृह्णन्तिविचिन्वन्तितथापरे ।।6.22.62।। वानरैश्शतशस्तत्ररामस्याज्ञापुरस्सराः । मेघाभैःपर्वताग्रैश्चतृणैःकाष्ठैर्बबन्धिरे ।।6.22.63।।
transliteration: daṇḍānanyepragṛhṇantivicinvantitathāpare  vānaraiśśataśastatrarāmasyājñāpurassarāḥ | meghābhaiḥparvatāgraiścatṛṇaiḥkāṣṭhairbabandhire
translation: अन्ये others, दण्डान् sticks, प्रगृह्णन्ति holding, तथा in the same way, अपरे some others, विचिन्वन्ति following, रामस्य of Rama, आज्ञापुरस्सरैः the command in front, शतशः in hundreds, मेघाभिः like clouds, पर्वताग्रैश्च like top of mountains, वानरैः with Vanaras, तृणैः reeds, काष्ठैश्च logs of wood, बबन्धिरे built.
explanation: Others held sticks and some held logs of wood and reeds following the command of Rama, hundreds of Vanaras who looked like clouds and mountain tops built the bridge.

shloka_text: पुष्पिताग्रैश्चतरुभिस्सेतुंबध्नन्तिवानराः । पाषाणांश्चगिरिप्रख्यागनिरीणांशिखराणिच ।।6.22.64।। दृश्यन्तेपरिधावन्तोगृह्यदानवसन्निभाः ।
transliteration: puṣpitāgraiścatarubhissetuṃbadhnantivānarāḥ | pāṣāṇāṃścagiriprakhyāganirīṇāṃśikharāṇica  dṛśyanteparidhāvantogṛhyadānavasannibhāḥ |
translation: वानराः Vanaras, पुष्पिताग्रैः trees with blossoms on top, तरुभिः creepers, सेतुम् for the bridge, बध्नन्ति binding दानवसन्निभा like the Danavas, गिरिप्रख्यान् like the huge mountains, पाषाणांश्च boulders also, गिरीणाम् mountains, शिखराणिच tops, गृह्य seizing, परिधावन्त running, दृश्यन्ते were found.
explanation: The Vanaras who were like Danavas, huge mountains in size were seen seizing boulders from the mountain, the trees with blossoms, and creepers for binding the bridge and running.

shloka_text: शिलानांक्षिप्यमाणानांशैलानांनिपात्यताम् । बभूवतुमुलश्शब्दस्तदातस्मिन्महोदधौ ।।6.22.65।।
transliteration: śilānāṃkṣipyamāṇānāṃśailānāṃnipātyatām | babhūvatumulaśśabdastadātasminmahodadhau
translation: तस्मिन् in that, महोदधौ lofty ocean, क्षिप्यमाणानां hurling, शिलानाम् mountains, तत्र so also, निपात्यताम् by throwing, शैलानाम् mountains, तुमुलः tumultuous, शब्दः sound, तदा then, बभूव arose.
explanation: By hurling off the mountains in that lofty ocean and throwing stones, a tumultuous sound arose.

shloka_text: कृतानिप्रथमेनाह्नायोजनानिचतुर्दश । प्रहृष्टैर्गजसङ्काश्चैस्त्वरमाणैःप्लवङ्गमैः ।।6.22.66।।
transliteration: kṛtāniprathamenāhnāyojanānicaturdaśa | prahṛṣṭairgajasaṅkāścaistvaramāṇaiḥplavaṅgamaiḥ
translation: प्रहृष्टैः rejoicing, गजसङ्काशैः elephant like, त्वरमाणैः speedily, प्लवङ्गमैः the monkeys, प्रथमेन first, अह्ना one day, चतुर्धश fourteen, योजनानि yojana distance, कृतानि was built.
explanation: Elephants like monkeys rejoiced over building speedily fourteen yojanas the distance of the bridge on the first day.

shloka_text: द्वितीयेनतथैचाह्नायोजनानितुविंशतिः । कृतानिप्लवगैस्तूर्णंभीमकायैर्महाबलैः ।।6.22.67।।
transliteration: dvitīyenatathaicāhnāyojanānituviṃśatiḥ | kṛtāniplavagaistūrṇaṃbhīmakāyairmahābalaiḥ
translation: तथैन in the same order, भीमकायैः of fierce body, महाबलैः extremely strong, प्लवगैः Vanaras, तूर्णम् soon, द्वितीयेन on the second, अह्ना one day, विंशतिः twenty, योजनानि yojanas, कृतानि built.
explanation: In the same order the Vanaras of fierce bodies and extremely strong ones soon built twenty yojanas on the second day.

shloka_text: अह्नातृतयेनतथायोजनानिकृतानिच । त्वरमाणैर्महाकायैरेकविंशतिरेवच ।।6.22.68।।
transliteration: ahnātṛtayenatathāyojanānikṛtānica | tvaramāṇairmahākāyairekaviṃśatirevaca
translation: तथा that way, त्वरमाणैः very fast, महकायैः of huge body, तृतीयेन on the third, अह्ना one day, एकविंशतिरेवच twenty one, योजनानि yojanas, कृतानिच constructed.
explanation: Endowed with huge body that way the Vanaras built extremely fast, twenty one yojanas on the third day.

shloka_text: चतुर्थेनतथाचाह्नाद्वाविंशतिरथासिवा । योजनानिमहावेगैःकृतानित्वरितस्तुतैः ।।6.22.69।।
transliteration: caturthenatathācāhnādvāviṃśatirathāsivā | yojanānimahāvegaiḥkṛtānitvaritastutaiḥ
translation: ततः there upon, महावेगैः of great speed, त्वरितैः at once, अथापि so also, वा and, चतुर्धेन on the fourth, अह्ना a day, द्वाविंशतिः twenty two, योजनानि yojanas, कृतानि did.
explanation: There upon at once Vanaras of great speed built twenty two yojanas on the fourth day.

shloka_text: पञ्चमेनतथाचाह्नाप्लवगैःक्षिप्रकारिभिः । योजनानित्रयोविंशत्सुवेलमधिकृत्यवै ।।6.22.70।।
transliteration: pañcamenatathācāhnāplavagaiḥkṣiprakāribhiḥ | yojanānitrayoviṃśatsuvelamadhikṛtyavai
translation: तथा similarly, पञ्चमेन fifth day, अह्ना a day, क्षिप्रकारिभिः those who were endowed with great impetus, प्लवगैः Vanaras, सुवेलम् अधिकृत्य crossing mount Suvela, त्रयोविंशत् twentythree, योजनानि yojanas.
explanation: Similarly, on the fifth day the Vanaras endowed with great impetus built twenty three yojanas and crossed Mount Suvela.

shloka_text: सवानरवरश्रशीमान्विश्वकर्मात्माजोबली । बबन्धसागरेसेतुंयथाचाप्यतथापिता ।।6.22.71।।
transliteration: savānaravaraśraśīmānviśvakarmātmājobalī | babandhasāgaresetuṃyathācāpyatathāpitā
translation: वानरवरः foremost of the Vanaras, श्रीमान् glorious, विश्वकर्मात्मजः son of Vishwakarma, बलि strong one, सः he, अस्य his, पिता father, यथा like, तथा so also, सागरे in the sea, सेतुम् bridge, बबन्ध built.
explanation: Nala the son of Vishwakarma, the foremost of the Vanaras and strong like his father built the bridge in the sea.

shloka_text: सनलेनकृतस्सेतुस्सागरेमकरालये । शुशुभेसुभगश्रशीमान् स्वातीपथइवाम्बरे ।।6.22.72।।
transliteration: sanalenakṛtassetussāgaremakarālaye | śuśubhesubhagaśraśīmān svātīpathaivāmbare
translation: मकरालये abode crocodiles, सागरे in the sea, नलेन by Nala, कृतः built, सुभगः auspicious, श्रीमान् glorious, सः that, सेतुः bridge, अम्बरे sky, स्वातीपथइव like the street of stars, शुशुभे looked.
explanation: The bridge was built on the sea, an abode of crocodiles, was auspicious, glorious, and looked like the street in space (milky path).

shloka_text: ततोदेवस्सगन्धर्वास्सिद्दाश्चपरमर्षयः । आगम्यगगनेतस्थुर्द्रष्टुकामास्तदद्बुतम् ।।6.22.73।।
transliteration: tatodevassagandharvāssiddāścaparamarṣayaḥ | āgamyagaganetasthurdraṣṭukāmāstadadbutam
translation: ततः then, सगन्धर्वा the Gandharvas, देवाः gods, सिद्दाश्च even siddhas, परमर्षयः very happy, तत् then, अद्भुतम् it is wonderful, द्रष्टुकामाः desiring to see that, आगम्यगगने reached the sky, तस्थुः stationed.
explanation: The Gandharvas, gods and even siddhas felt happy and reached their stationed in the sky to see the wonderful bridge.

shloka_text: दशयोजनविस्तीर्णंशतयोजनमायतम् । ददृशुर्देवगन्धर्वानलसेतुंसुदुष्करम् ।।6.22.74।।
transliteration: daśayojanavistīrṇaṃśatayojanamāyatam | dadṛśurdevagandharvānalasetuṃsuduṣkaram
translation: देवगन्धर्वाः gods and Gandharvas, दशयोजनविस्तीर्णम् ten yojanas in width, शतयोजनम् hundred yojanas, आयतम् in length, सुदुष्करम् exceedingly difficult to build, नलसेतुम् bridge built by Nala, ददृशुः witnessed.
explanation: Gods and Gandharvas witnessed the bridge built by Nala that was ten yojanas in width and hundred yojanas in length.

shloka_text: आप्लवन्तःप्लवन्तश्चगर्जन्तश्चप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.22.75।। तदच्नित्यमसह्यंचह्यद्भुतंरोमहर्षणम् । ददृशुस्सर्वभूतानिसागरेसेतुबन्धनम् ।।622.76।।
transliteration: āplavantaḥplavantaścagarjantaścaplavaṅgamāḥ  tadacnityamasahyaṃcahyadbhutaṃromaharṣaṇam | dadṛśussarvabhūtānisāgaresetubandhanam ||622.76||
translation: प्लवङ्गमाः monkeys, आप्लवन्तः here and there jumping, प्लवन्तश्च jumping about, गर्जन्तश्च roaring, सर्वभूतानि all creatures, आच्नित्यम् that which cannot be conceived in mind, असह्यंच impossible, अद्भुतम् marvellous, रोमहर्षणम् which is thrilling, सागरे in the sea, तत् that, सेतुबन्दनम् bridge constructed, ददृशुः witnessed.
explanation: The monkeys were jumping about here and there roaring (in joy). All creatures witnessed the bridge that was inconceivable, marvellous, thrilling, and impossible to build constructed in the sea.

shloka_text: आप्लवन्तःप्लवन्तश्चगर्जन्तश्चप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.22.75।। तदच्नित्यमसह्यंचह्यद्भुतंरोमहर्षणम् । ददृशुस्सर्वभूतानिसागरेसेतुबन्धनम् ।।622.76।।
transliteration: āplavantaḥplavantaścagarjantaścaplavaṅgamāḥ  tadacnityamasahyaṃcahyadbhutaṃromaharṣaṇam | dadṛśussarvabhūtānisāgaresetubandhanam ||622.76||
translation: प्लवङ्गमाः monkeys, आप्लवन्तः here and there jumping, प्लवन्तश्च jumping about, गर्जन्तश्च roaring, सर्वभूतानि all creatures, आच्नित्यम् that which cannot be conceived in mind, असह्यंच impossible, अद्भुतम् marvellous, रोमहर्षणम् which is thrilling, सागरे in the sea, तत् that, सेतुबन्दनम् bridge constructed, ददृशुः witnessed.
explanation: The monkeys were jumping about here and there roaring (in joy). All creatures witnessed the bridge that was inconceivable, marvellous, thrilling, and impossible to build constructed in the sea.

shloka_text: तानिकोटिसहस्राणिवानराणांमहौजसाम् । बध्नन्तस्सागरेसेतुंजुग्मुःपारंमहोदधेः ।।6.22.77।।
transliteration: tānikoṭisahasrāṇivānarāṇāṃmahaujasām | badhnantassāgaresetuṃjugmuḥpāraṃmahodadheḥ
translation: महौजसाम् the glorious, वानराणाम् Vanaras, तानि those, कोटिसहस्राणि thousands of crores, सागरे sea, सेतुम् bridge, बध्नन्तः constructed, महोदधेः from the great ocean, पारम् other side, जग्मुः reached.
explanation: The glorious Vanaras in thousands of crores reached the other side of the sea from the bridge constructed in the great sea.

shloka_text: विशालस्सुकृतश्रशीमान् सुभूमिस्सुसमाहितः । अशोभतमहान् सेतुस्सीमन्तइवसागरे ।।6.22.78।।
transliteration: viśālassukṛtaśraśīmān subhūmissusamāhitaḥ | aśobhatamahān setussīmantaivasāgare
translation: विशालः broad, सुकृतः well built, श्रीमान् magnificent, सुभूमिः extensive, सुसमाहितः smootheven without ups and downs, महान् huge, सेतुः bridge, सागरे in the sea, सीमन्तइवअशोभत was charming like the partition in the woman's hair.
explanation: That huge bridge was well built, magnificent, evenly built, and extensive and looked charming like the partition in a woman's hair.

shloka_text: ततःपारेसमुद्रस्यगदापाणिर्विभीषणः । परेषामभिघातार्थमतिष्ठत्सचिवैस्सहा ।।6.22.79।।
transliteration: tataḥpāresamudrasyagadāpāṇirvibhīṣaṇaḥ | pareṣāmabhighātārthamatiṣṭhatsacivaissahā
translation: ततः there upon, विभीषणः Vibheeshana, गदापाणिः holder of mace, परेषाम् enemies, अभिघातार्थम् to slay the aforesaid, सचिवैःसहा along with friends, समुद्रस्य from the ocean, पारे other side, अतिष्ठत् stayed.
explanation: There upon Vibheeshana holding the mace stood on the other side of the ocean along with his friends to slay the enemies.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्तुततःप्राहरामंसत्यपराक्रमम् । हनूमन्तंत्वमारोहअङ्गदंचापिलक्ष्मणः ।।6.22.80।। अयंहिविपुलोवीरसागरोमकरालयः । वैहायपौयुवामेतौवानरौतारयिष्यतः ।।6.22.81।।
transliteration: sugrīvastutataḥprāharāmaṃsatyaparākramam | hanūmantaṃtvamārohaaṅgadaṃcāpilakṣmaṇaḥ  ayaṃhivipulovīrasāgaromakarālayaḥ | vaihāyapauyuvāmetauvānarautārayiṣyataḥ
translation: ततः then, सुग्रीवस्तु Sugriva also, सत्यपराक्रमम् one of truthful valour, रामम् Rama, प्राह mount, वीर heroic, मकरालयः home of crocodiles, अयम् this, आरोह climbing, अथ and so, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, त्वम् you, हनूमन्तम् Hanuman's, हि will do, अङ्गदम् Angada, एतौ like that, वानरौ Vanaras, वैहायसौ to the sky, युवाम् hold up both, तारयिष्यतः will assist to cross.
explanation: Sugriva addressed Rama of truthful valour and said, "You mount on heroic Hanuman, let Lakshmana climb on Angada. These Vanaras will hold you up in the sky and assist you to cross the ocean."

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्तुततःप्राहरामंसत्यपराक्रमम् । हनूमन्तंत्वमारोहअङ्गदंचापिलक्ष्मणः ।।6.22.80।। अयंहिविपुलोवीरसागरोमकरालयः । वैहायपौयुवामेतौवानरौतारयिष्यतः ।।6.22.81।।
transliteration: sugrīvastutataḥprāharāmaṃsatyaparākramam | hanūmantaṃtvamārohaaṅgadaṃcāpilakṣmaṇaḥ  ayaṃhivipulovīrasāgaromakarālayaḥ | vaihāyapauyuvāmetauvānarautārayiṣyataḥ
translation: ततः then, सुग्रीवस्तु Sugriva also, सत्यपराक्रमम् one of truthful valour, रामम् Rama, प्राह mount, वीर heroic, मकरालयः home of crocodiles, अयम् this, आरोह climbing, अथ and so, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, त्वम् you, हनूमन्तम् Hanuman's, हि will do, अङ्गदम् Angada, एतौ like that, वानरौ Vanaras, वैहायसौ to the sky, युवाम् hold up both, तारयिष्यतः will assist to cross.
explanation: Sugriva addressed Rama of truthful valour and said, "You mount on heroic Hanuman, let Lakshmana climb on Angada. These Vanaras will hold you up in the sky and assist you to cross the ocean."

shloka_text: अग्रतस्तस्यसैन्यस्यश्रीमान्रामस्सलक्ष्मणः । जगामधन्वीधर्मात्मासुग्रीवेणसमन्वितः ।।6.22.82।।
transliteration: agratastasyasainyasyaśrīmānrāmassalakṣmaṇaḥ | jagāmadhanvīdharmātmāsugrīveṇasamanvitaḥ
translation: सलक्ष्मणः accompanied by Lakshmana, श्रीमान् glorious, धर्मात्मा righteous, रामः Rama, सुग्रीवेण with Sugriva, समन्वितः joining together, धन्वी wielder of bow, तस्यसैन्यस्य his army, अग्रतः in front, जगाम proceeded.
explanation: Accompanied by Lakshmana and joined together with Sugriva, glorious and righteous Rama walked in front of the army.

shloka_text: न्येमध्येनगच्छन्तिपार्श्वतोऽन्येप्लवङ्गमाः । सलिलंप्रपतन्तन्येमार्गमन्येनलेभिरे ।।6.22.83।। केचिद्वैहायसगतास्सुपर्णाइवपुप्लुवुः ।
transliteration: nyemadhyenagacchantipārśvato'nyeplavaṅgamāḥ | salilaṃprapatantanyemārgamanyenalebhire  kecidvaihāyasagatāssuparṇāivapupluvuḥ |
translation: अन्ये others, प्लवङ्गमाः monkeys, मध्येनगच्छन्ति going in the middle, अन्ये some others, पार्श्वतः in the side, अन्ये some others, सलिलम् water, प्रपतन्ति falling down (having no space to walk), अन्ये some others, मार्गम् path, नलेभिरे on the shore, केचित् a few, वैहायसगताः through the path of sky, सुपर्णाःइव like birds, पुप्लुवुः went.
explanation: While some monkeys walked in the middle some went in the side, some others were falling down in water (for the want of space to walk) some others went like birds in the path of the sky.

shloka_text: घोषेणमहतातस्यसिन्धोर्घोषंसमुच्छ्रितम् । भीमन्तर्दधेभीमातरन्तीहरिवाहिनी ।।6.22.84।।
transliteration: ghoṣeṇamahatātasyasindhorghoṣaṃsamucchritam | bhīmantardadhebhīmātarantīharivāhinī
translation: तरन्ती by the advancement, भीमा frightening, हरिवाहिनी army troops of monkeys, महता massive, घोषेण by the loud noise, समुच्छ्रितम् risen, भीमम् terrific, तस्य its सिन्धोः of the ocean, घोषम् sound, अन्तर्धधे drowned.
explanation: The terrific sound caused by the frightening advancement of massive monkey troops the sound of the ocean got drowned.

shloka_text: वानराणांहिसातीर्णावाहिनीनलसेतुना । तीरेनिविविशेराज्ञाबहुमूलफलोदके ।।6.22.85।।
transliteration: vānarāṇāṃhisātīrṇāvāhinīnalasetunā | tīreniviviśerājñābahumūlaphalodake
translation: नलसेतुना the bridge of Nala, तीर्णा having reached, वानराणाम् Vanaras, सा that, वाहिनी, army राज्ञा by the king, बहुमूलफलोदके filled with several roots and fruits, तीरे shore, निविविशे settled.
explanation: The Vanara army having crossed the bridge of Nala by the king's order settled on the other shore that was filled with several roots and fruits.

shloka_text: तदद्बुतंराघवकर्मदुष्करंसमीक्ष्यदेवास्सहसिद्धचारणैः । उपेत्यरामसहसामहार्षिभिस्समभ्यषिञ्चन् सुशुभैर्जलैःपृथक् ।।6.2 2.86।।
transliteration: tadadbutaṃrāghavakarmaduṣkaraṃsamīkṣyadevāssahasiddhacāraṇaiḥ | upetyarāmasahasāmahārṣibhissamabhyaṣiñcan suśubhairjalaiḥpṛthak ||6.2 2.86||
translation: देवाः gods, सिद्धचारणैः siddhas and charanas, महर्षिभिःसह including sages, अद्भुतम् wonderful, दुष्करम् most difficult, तत् that is, राघवकर्म Rama's action, समीक्ष्य seeing, सहसा at once, रामम् to Rama, उपेत्य, reached towards, सुशुभैः auspicious, जलैः water, पृथक् each one separately, तम् him, अभ्यषिञ्चन् sprinkled
explanation: At once the gods, siddhas, charanas and sages came towards Rama looking at his wonderful and most difficult action and sprinkled auspicious water on him individually. (As a mark of worship and blessing).

shloka_text: जयस्वशत्रून्नरदे व:मेदिनींससागरांपालयशाश्वतीस्समाः । इतीवरामंनरदेवसत्कृ तंशुभैर्वचोभिर्विविधैरपूजयन् ।।6.22.87।।
transliteration: jayasvaśatrūnnarade va:medinīṃsasāgarāṃpālayaśāśvatīssamāḥ | itīvarāmaṃnaradevasatkṛ taṃśubhairvacobhirvividhairapūjayan
translation: नरदेव god of human beings, शत्रून् enemies, जयस्व win, ससागरम् ocean, मेदिनीम् the whole land, शाश्वतीः ever, स्समाः, पालय you rule, इतीव thus, नरदेवसत्कृतम् one who is respected by human as well as gods, रामम् Rama, शुभैः be auspicious, विविधैः several, वचोभिः words, अपूजयन् worshipped.
explanation: "O Rama the Lord of human beings Let you win over enemies and rule the land for ever." Thus, hailing Rama who is worshipped by humans as well as gods, was worshipped with auspicious words (by the aforesaid gods, siddhas and charanas). ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेद्वाविंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the twenty second sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: निमित्तानिनिमित्ताज्ञोदृष्टवालक्ष्मणपूर्वजः । सौमित्रिंसम्परिष्वज्यइदंवचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.23.1।।
transliteration: nimittāninimittājñodṛṣṭavālakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ | saumitriṃsampariṣvajyaidaṃvacanamabravīt
translation: निमित्तज्ञः one who is aware of portents, लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः Lakshmana's elder brother, दृष्टवा perceiving, निमित्तानि portents, सौमित्रिम् to Saumithri, इदम् these, सम्परिष्वज्य embracing, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Perceiving the portents, Rama spoke these words embracing Saumithri who was aware of the portents.
comments: Rama points out to Lakshmana the evil portents indicating destruction of Rakshasas, monkeys, and people.

shloka_text: निमित्तानिपरिगृह्योदकंशीतंवनानिफलवन्तिच । बलौघंसंविभज्येमंव्यूह्यतिष्ठेमलक्ष्मण ।।6.23.2।।
transliteration: nimittāniparigṛhyodakaṃśītaṃvanāniphalavantica | balaughaṃsaṃvibhajyemaṃvyūhyatiṣṭhemalakṣmaṇa
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, शीतम् cool, उदकम् water, फलवन्ति fruit, वनानिच forests, परिगृह्य arranging, इदम् this, बलौघम् battalions of army, संविभज्य dividing, व्यूह्य the group, तिष्ठेम will remain.
explanation: "Lakshmana Arrange a place in this forest where there is cool water and fruits for the battalions of the army, we shall remain (alert)."

shloka_text: लोकक्षयकरंभीमंभयंपश्याम्युपस्थितम् । निबर्हणंप्रवीराणामृक्षवानररक्षसाम् ।।6.23.3।।
transliteration: lokakṣayakaraṃbhīmaṃbhayaṃpaśyāmyupasthitam | nibarhaṇaṃpravīrāṇāmṛkṣavānararakṣasām
translation: लोकक्षयकरम् that which bodes destruction to the people, भीमम् dreadful, प्रवीराणाम् for the warriors, ऋक्षवानररक्षसाम् Bears, monkeys and Rakshasas, निबर्हणम् will be slain, भयम् fear, उपस्थितम् will happen, पश्यामि I foresee.
explanation: "Dreadful warriors, Bears, monkeys, and Rakshasas will be slain, and I foresee that which bodes destruction of people."

shloka_text: वाताश्चकलुषावान्तिकम्पतेचवसुन्धराः । पर्वताग्राणिवेपन्तेपतन्तिचमहीरुहाः ।।6.23.4।।
transliteration: vātāścakaluṣāvāntikampatecavasundharāḥ | parvatāgrāṇivepantepatanticamahīruhāḥ
translation: वाताः wind, कलुषाः mixed with dust is blowing, वान्ति cracking, वसुन्धराच even the earth, कम्पते shaking, पर्वताग्राणि mountain tops, वेपन्ते breaking, महीरुहाः huge trees, पतन्तिच and falling down.
explanation: "The wind is blowing mixed with dust, even the earth is cracking, mountain tops are shaking, and huge trees are breaking and falling down."

shloka_text: मेघाःक्रव्यादसङ्काशाःपरुषाःपरुषस्वनाः । क्रूराःक्रूरंप्रवर्षन्तिमिश्रंशोणितबिन्दुभिः ।।6.23.5।।
transliteration: meghāḥkravyādasaṅkāśāḥparuṣāḥparuṣasvanāḥ | krūrāḥkrūraṃpravarṣantimiśraṃśoṇitabindubhiḥ
translation: क्रव्यादसङ्काशाः clouds resembling raw flesh in colour, परुषाः harsh, परुषस्वनाः in harsh tone, क्रूराः cruel, मेघाः clouds, क्रूरम् frightening, शोणितबिन्दुभिः even drops of blood, मिश्रम् mixed, प्रवर्षन्ति raining.
explanation: "Clouds resembling raw flesh in colour, are making harsh frightening sounds, and rain mixed with drops of blood."

shloka_text: रक्तचन्दनसङ्काशासन्ध्यापरमदारुणा । ज्वलतःप्रपतत्येतदादित्यादग्निमण्डलम् ।।6.23.6।।
transliteration: raktacandanasaṅkāśāsandhyāparamadāruṇā | jvalataḥprapatatyetadādityādagnimaṇḍalam
translation: रक्तचन्दनसङ्काशा like red sandal, सन्ध्या twilight, परमदारुणा very frightening, ज्वलतः blazing, आदित्यात् from the Sun, एतत of variegated colours, अग्निमण्डलम् , masses of fire प्रपतति raining.
explanation: "The twilight in red sandal colour is very frightening. The Sun is blazing, raining masses of fire in variegated colours."

shloka_text: दीनादीनस्वराःक्रूरास्सर्वतोमृगपक्षिणः । प्रत्यादित्यंविनर्धन्तिजनयन्तोमहाद्भयम् ।।6.23.7।।
transliteration: dīnādīnasvarāḥkrūrāssarvatomṛgapakṣiṇaḥ | pratyādityaṃvinardhantijanayantomahādbhayam
translation: सर्वतः all over, क्रूराःमृगाः wild animals, दीनाः pathetic, दीनस्वराः wailing in low tone, महात् great, भयम् fear, जनयन्तः producing, प्रत्यादित्य opposite the Sun, विनर्धन्ति indicating.
explanation: "The wild animals all over have a piteous look and wailing in low tone standing opposite the Sun is indicating fear."

shloka_text: रजन्यामप्रकाशस्तुसन्तापयतिचन्द्रमाः । कृष्णरक्तांशुपर्यन्तोलोकक्षयइवोदितः ।।6.23.8।।
transliteration: rajanyāmaprakāśastusantāpayaticandramāḥ | kṛṣṇaraktāṃśuparyantolokakṣayaivoditaḥ
translation: लोकक्षये at the time of dissolution of the universe, उदितइव like the Sun, कृष्णरक्तांशपर्यन्तः with black rays around and red rays behind, चन्द्रमाः moon, रजन्याम् in the night, अप्रकाशः devoid of glow, सन्तापयति causing sorrow.
explanation: "The moon devoid of glow even in the night is like the Sun with black rays around and red aura behind (the black)."

shloka_text: ह्रस्वोरूक्षोऽप्रशस्तश्चपरिवेषस्सुलोहितः । आदित्येविमलेनीलंलक्ष्मलक्ष्मणदृश्यते ।।6.23.9।।
transliteration: hrasvorūkṣo'praśastaścapariveṣassulohitaḥ | ādityevimalenīlaṃlakṣmalakṣmaṇadṛśyate
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, विमले white, आदित्ये Sun, ह्रस्वः becoming small, रूक्षः dreary, अप्रशस्तः that which had not been seen before, लोहितः copper coloured, परिवेषः around, नीलम् black, लक्ष्म in the centre, दृश्यते appears.
explanation: "Lakshmana the white Sun is appearing in copper colour around with black colour in the centre which had not been seen before. It is small and dreary."

shloka_text: रजसामहताचापिनक्षत्राणिहतानिच । युगान्तमिवलोकानांपश्यशंसन्तीवलक्ष्मण ।।6.23.10।।
transliteration: rajasāmahatācāpinakṣatrāṇihatānica | yugāntamivalokānāṃpaśyaśaṃsantīvalakṣmaṇa
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, महता great, रजसा brightness, हतानि devoid, नक्षत्राणि the stars, लोकानाम् in the worlds, युगान्तम् end of universe at the time of dissolution, शंसन्तीव as if indicating, पश्य appears.
explanation: "Lakshmana the stars devoid of brightness are indicating as though it is the time of dissolution of the universe?"

shloka_text: काकाश्श्येनास्तथानीचागृध्राःपरिपतन्तिच । शिवाश्चाप्यशिवान्नादान्नदन्तिसुमहाभयान् ।।6.23.11।।
transliteration: kākāśśyenāstathānīcāgṛdhrāḥparipatantica | śivāścāpyaśivānnādānnadantisumahābhayān
translation: काकाः crows, श्येनाः hawks, ततागृध्राः likewise eagles, नीचाः small, परिपतन्ति falling down, शिवाश्चापि also jackals, महाभयान् great fear, अशिवान् creating, नादान् howls, नदन्ति making.
explanation: "The crows, hawks and eagles are falling down like small animals. Also, the jackals are creating fear by making howls."

shloka_text: शैलैश्शूलैश्चखढगैश्चविसृष्टैःकपिराक्षसैः । भविष्यत्यावृताभूमिर्मांसशोणितकर्दमा ।।6.23.12।।
transliteration: śailaiśśūlaiścakhaḍhagaiścavisṛṣṭaiḥkapirākṣasaiḥ | bhaviṣyatyāvṛtābhūmirmāṃsaśoṇitakardamā
translation: कपिराक्षसैः Vanaras and Rakshasas, विसृष्टैः hurled, शैलैः mountains, शूलैश्च tridents, खढगैश्च with swords, मांसशोणितकर्दमा covered with flesh and blood, भूमिः earth, आवृता turning to, भविष्यति will become.
explanation: "The earth will turn into a mass of flesh and blood and will be covered by the mountains and tridents hurled by Vanaras and Rakshasas."

shloka_text: क्षिप्रमद्यैवदुर्दर्षांपुरींरावणपालिताम् । अभियामजनेनैवसर्वतोहरिभिर्ववृताः ।।6.23.13।।
transliteration: kṣipramadyaivadurdarṣāṃpurīṃrāvaṇapālitām | abhiyāmajanenaivasarvatoharibhirvavṛtāḥ
translation: सर्वैः all, हरिभिः Vanaras, आवृताः turning direction, अद्यैव now itself, क्षिप्रम् immediately, जवेनैव swiftly, रावणपालिताम् ruled by Ravana, पुरीम् city, अभियाम will go.
explanation: All the Vanaras turning their direction will go immediately and now itself, swiftly to the city ruled by Ravana (said Rama to Lakshmana).

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्त्वाधर्मात्माधनवीसङ्ग्रामहर्षणः । प्रतस्थेपुरतोरामोलङ्कामभिमुखोविभुः ।।6.23.14।।
transliteration: ityevamuktvādharmātmādhanavīsaṅgrāmaharṣaṇaḥ | pratasthepuratorāmolaṅkāmabhimukhovibhuḥ
translation: रामः Rama, सङ्ग्रामधर्षणः one who subdues his enemies in war, विभुः a celebrated one, रामः Rama, इत्येवम् in this way, उक्त्वा having spoken, धनवी wielding a bow, पुरतः in front, लङ्काम् to Lanka, अभिमुखः towards, प्रतस्थे proceeded.
explanation: Rama, the subduer of enemies in war, a celebrated one having spoken this way proceeded towards Lanka going in front wielding a bow.

shloka_text: सविभीषणसुग्रीवास्ततस्तेवानरर्षभाः । प्रतस्थिरेविनर्दन्तोनिश्चिताद्विषतांवधे ।।6.23.15।।
transliteration: savibhīṣaṇasugrīvāstatastevānararṣabhāḥ | pratasthirevinardantoniścitādviṣatāṃvadhe
translation: सविभीषण then Vibheeshana, सुग्रीवाः Sugriva, सर्वे all, ते of them, वानरर्षभाः bulls among Vanaras, विनर्दन्तः roaring, निश्चितानाम् determined, द्विषताम् in the matter of, वधे slaying, प्रतस्थिरे went
explanation: Then Vibheeshana, Sugriva and all bulls among Vanaras determined in the matter of slaying (the enemies) went roaring.

shloka_text: राघवस्यप्रियार्थंतुसुतरांवीर्यशालिनाम् । हरीणांकर्मचेष्टाभिस्तुतोषरघुपुङ्गवः ।।6.23.16।।
transliteration: rāghavasyapriyārthaṃtusutarāṃvīryaśālinām | harīṇāṃkarmaceṣṭābhistutoṣaraghupuṅgavaḥ
translation: सुतरां excessively, वीर्यशालिनाम् heroes, हरीणाम् Vanaras, राघवस्य to Rama, प्रियार्थम् to make him happy, कर्मचेष्टाभिः actions, रघुपुङ्गवः the delight of Raghus, तुतोष saw and felt happy
explanation: To make Rama happy, the excessively heroic Vanaras made monkey actions. Seeing that Rama felt happy. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेत्रयोविंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the twenty third sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सावीरसमितीराज्ञाविरराजव्यवस्थिता । शशिनाशुभनक्षत्रापौर्णमासीवशारदी ।।6.24.1।।
transliteration: sāvīrasamitīrājñāvirarājavyavasthitā | śaśināśubhanakṣatrāpaurṇamāsīvaśāradī
translation: व्यवस्थिता settled, सा that, वीरसमितिः army of Vanaras, राज्ञा by the king (Rama), शुभनक्षत्रा with auspicious stars, शारदी autumn, पौर्णमासी full moon, शशिनाइव like the moon, विरराज shone.
explanation: The army of Vanaras settled that way by Rama's command shone like the autumnal full moon with auspicious stars.
comments: Applauding the splendour of Lanka, Rama asks Lakshmana to see the beauty of the gardens and palaces. Rama asks Suka to be released. Suka returns to Ravana and describes Ramas army.

shloka_text: प्रचचालचवेगेनत्रस्ताचैववसुन्धरा । पीड्यमानाबलौघेनतेनसागरवर्चसा ।।6.24.2।।
transliteration: pracacālacavegenatrastācaivavasundharā | pīḍyamānābalaughenatenasāgaravarcasā
translation: सागरवर्चसा like the ocean, तेन by that, बलौघेन the army, पीड्यमाना tormented by, वसुन्धरा the earth, वेगेन swift movement, त्रस्ता frightened, प्रचचाल started shaking.
explanation: The frightened army (of Vanaras) that was like a tormented ocean started moving swiftly, shaking like the earth.

shloka_text: ततश्शुश्रुवुराक्रुष्टंलङ्कायांकाननौकसः । भेरीमृदङ्गसङ्घुष्टंतुमुलंरोमहर्षणम् ।।6.24.3।।
transliteration: tataśśuśruvurākruṣṭaṃlaṅkāyāṃkānanaukasaḥ | bherīmṛdaṅgasaṅghuṣṭaṃtumulaṃromaharṣaṇam
translation: ततः there upon, काननौकसः army having settled, लङ्कायां from Lanka, आक्रुष्टम् terrific, तुमुलम् tumultuous, रेमहर्षणम् that which causes horripilation, भेरीमृदङ्गसङ्घुष्टम् drums and percussion instruments, शुश्रुवुः came to hear.
explanation: There upon having settled down, the army hordes heard from Lanka terrific and tumultuous noise of drums and percussion instruments that caused horripilation.

shloka_text: बभूवुस्तेनघोषेणसंहृष्टाहरियूथपाः । अमृष्यमाणास्तंघोषंविनेदुर्घोषवत्तरम् ।।6.24.4।।
transliteration: babhūvustenaghoṣeṇasaṃhṛṣṭāhariyūthapāḥ | amṛṣyamāṇāstaṃghoṣaṃvinedurghoṣavattaram
translation: हरियूथपाः leaders of Vanara troops, तेन of that (Lanka), घोषेण by the loud noises, संहृष्टाः felt very happy, बभूवुः became, तम् that which, घोषम् noise, अमृष्यमाणाः unable to tolerate, घोषवत्तरम् louder than the noise, विनेदुः roared in joy.
explanation: The leaders of Vanara troops felt very happy at the noise from (Lanka) which they were unable to tolerate and roared louder (than that in joy).

shloka_text: राक्षसास्तुप्लवङ्गानांशुश्रुवुश्चाऽपिगर्जितम् । नर्दतामिवदृप्तानांमेघानामम्बरेस्वनम् ।।6.24.5।।
transliteration: rākṣasāstuplavaṅgānāṃśuśruvuścā'pigarjitam | nardatāmivadṛptānāṃmeghānāmambaresvanam
translation: राक्षसाःअपि even the Rakshasas, दृप्तानाम् in their pride, प्लवङ्गनाम् the Vanaras, अम्बरे in the sky, नर्दताम् bellowing, मेघानाम् clouds, स्वनम् इव like the sound, गर्जितम् roared, शुश्रुवुःच heard.
explanation: Even the Rakshasas heard the roaring of Vanaras in their pride that was bellowing like that of clouds in the sky.

shloka_text: दृष्टवादाशरथिर्लङ्कांचित्रध्वजपताकिनीम् । जगाममनसासीतंदूयमानेनचेतसा ।।6.24.6।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭavādāśarathirlaṅkāṃcitradhvajapatākinīm | jagāmamanasāsītaṃdūyamānenacetasā
translation: दाशरधिः Rama the son of Dasaratha, चित्रध्वजपताकिनीम् adored with colourful flags and posts, लङ्काम् of Lanka, दृष्टवा seeing, दूयमानेन afflicted by sorrow, चेतसा thinking, सीताम् of Sita, मनसा in his mind, जगाम went about.
explanation: Afflicted by sorrow upon seeing the colourful flags and posts of Lanka even Rama's thoughts went about thinking of Sita.

shloka_text: अत्रसामृगशाबाक्षीरावणेनोपरुध्यते । अभिभूताग्रहेणेवलोहिताङ्गेनरोहिणी ।।6.24.7।।
transliteration: atrasāmṛgaśābākṣīrāvaṇenoparudhyate | abhibhūtāgraheṇevalohitāṅgenarohiṇī
translation: मृगशाबाक्षी doveeyed, सा she, लोहिताङ्गेन red colour bodied planet (Mars), ग्रहेणव caught by, अभिभूता conquered, रोहिणीव like Rohini, रावणेन by Ravana, अत्र there, उपरुध्यते obstructed.
explanation: The doveeyed Sita is obstructed by Ravana there (at Lanka) like the planet Rohini is caught by the red coloured planet (Mars).

shloka_text: दीर्घमुष्णंचनिश्वस्यसमुद्वीक्ष्यचलक्ष्मणम् । उवाचवचनंवीरस्तत्कालहितमात्मनः ।।6.24.8।।
transliteration: dīrghamuṣṇaṃcaniśvasyasamudvīkṣyacalakṣmaṇam | uvācavacanaṃvīrastatkālahitamātmanaḥ
translation: वीरः heroic one, दीर्घम् long, उष्णंच hot, निश्वस्य heaving, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, समुद्वीक्ष्यच and looking at, आत्मनः himself, तात्कालहितम् that which is good at that time, वचनम् words, उवाच spoke.
explanation: Heroic Rama heaving hot and long breath looking at Lakshmana spoke these words that were good for him at that time.

shloka_text: आलिखन्तीमिवाकाशमुत्थितांपश्यलक्ष्मण । मनसेवकृतांलङ्कांनगाग्रेविश्वकर्मणा ।।6.24.9।।
transliteration: ālikhantīmivākāśamutthitāṃpaśyalakṣmaṇa | manasevakṛtāṃlaṅkāṃnagāgreviśvakarmaṇā
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, विश्वकर्मणा by Vishwakarma, नगाग्रे on top of the mountain, मनसा with mind, कृताम् इव like the one created, उत्थिताम् elevated, आकाशम् sky, आलिखन्तीम् as if clasping, लङ्काम् Lanka, पश्य you may see.
explanation: "Lakshmana, you may see the city of Lanka elevated on top of the mountain as though clasping the sky, like the one created in the mind of Vishwakarma."

shloka_text: विमानैर्बहुभिर्लङ्कासङ्कीर्णाभुविराजते । विष्णोःपदमिवाकाशंछादितंपाण्डुभिर्घनैः ।।6.24.10।।
transliteration: vimānairbahubhirlaṅkāsaṅkīrṇābhuvirājate | viṣṇoḥpadamivākāśaṃchāditaṃpāṇḍubhirghanaiḥ
translation: भुवि existing, राजते appears splendid, लङ्का Lanka, बहुभि with many, विमानैः tall skyscrapers, सङ्कीर्णा mass of, विष्णोः of Vishnu's, पदम् path, आकाशम् the sky, पाण्डुभिः with white, घनैः clouds, छादितम् इव as if covered.
explanation: "This Lanka appears splendid with a mass of skyscrapers like white clouds covering the path of Vishnu in the sky."

shloka_text: पुष्पितैश्शोभितालङ्कावनैश्चत्ररथोपमैः । नानापतगसङ्घुष्टै: फलपुष्पोपगैश्शुभैः ।।6.24.11।।
transliteration: puṣpitaiśśobhitālaṅkāvanaiścatrarathopamaiḥ | nānāpatagasaṅghuṣṭai: phalapuṣpopagaiśśubhaiḥ
translation: लङ्का Lanka, नानापतगसङ्घुष्टै: with flocks of bird of several kinds singing sweetly फलपुष्पोपगैः with charming flowers and fruits, शुभैः auspicious (gardens), पुष्पितैः decorated with flowers, चित्ररथोपमैः like the Chaitraratha, वनैः gardens, शोभिता delighting.
explanation: "Lanka is filled with flocks of birds of several kinds singing sweetly, the gardens with charming flowers and fruits are delighting like auspicious gardens of Chaitrara, the garden of Kubera, the god of wealth."

shloka_text: पश्यमत्तविहाङ्गानिप्रलीनभ्रमराणिच । कोकिलाकुलषण्डानिदोधवीतिशिवोऽनिलः ।।6.24.12।।
transliteration: paśyamattavihāṅgānipralīnabhramarāṇica | kokilākulaṣaṇḍānidodhavītiśivo'nilaḥ
translation: शिवः pleasant, अनिलः breeze, मत्तविहङ्गानि inhabited by proud birds प्रलीनभ्रमराणीच drunken honeybees, कोकिलाकुलषण्डानि crowded with cuckoos and other birds, दोधवीति shaking violently, पश्य you may see (said Rama to Lakshmana).
explanation: "You may see the trees shaking violently by the pleasant breeze, inhabited by proud birds, drunken honeybees and crowded with cuckoos and other birds (Rama said to Lakshmana)."

shloka_text: इतिदाशरथीरामोलक्ष्मणंसमभाषत । बलंचतद्वैविभजन् शास्त्रदृष्टेनकर्मणा ।।6.24.13।।
transliteration: itidāśarathīrāmolakṣmaṇaṃsamabhāṣata | balaṃcatadvaivibhajan śāstradṛṣṭenakarmaṇā
translation: दाशरथिः Dasaratha's, रामः Rama, इतिलक्ष्मणम् thus to Lakshmana, समभाषत talked, तद्वै in that manner, शास्त्रदृष्टेन in accordance with what is said in sastras, कर्मणा the task, बलं army, विभजच्छ and divide.
explanation: Dasaratha's son Rama thus talked to Lakshmana in that manner and asked to divide the task of the army in accordance with what is said in sastras.

shloka_text: शशासकपिसेनायांबलमादायवीर्यवान् । अङ्गदस्सहनीलेनतिष्ठेदुरसिदुर्जयः ।।6.24.14।।
transliteration: śaśāsakapisenāyāṃbalamādāyavīryavān | aṅgadassahanīlenatiṣṭhedurasidurjayaḥ
translation: शशास terror for the enemies, वीर्यवान् valiant one, दुर्जयः one who is difficult to win over, अङ्गदः Angada, बलात् with his army, ताम् those, कपिसेनायाम् army of Vanaras, आदाय taking, नीलेनसह along with Nila, उरसि heart (central place), तिष्ठेत् remain.
explanation: Let the valiant Angada who is difficult to win over, who is a terror to the enemies, take the army along with Nila and remain at the centre (of the army structure).

shloka_text: तिष्ठेद्वानरवाहिन्यावानरौघसमावृतः । आश्रित्यदक्षिणंपार्श्वमृषभोवानरर्षभ:।। 6.24.15।।
transliteration: tiṣṭhedvānaravāhinyāvānaraughasamāvṛtaḥ | āśrityadakṣiṇaṃpārśvamṛṣabhovānararṣabha:
translation: ऋषभोवानरर्षभ: Rshaba a bull among Vanaras, वानरौघसमावृतः accompanied by his troop of Vanaras, वानरवाहिन्याः Vanara contingent, दक्षिणम् south, पार्श्वम् side, आश्रितः approaching, तिष्ठेत् remain.
explanation: Let Rshaba the bull among Vanaras approach the south side of the army accompanied by his troop of Vanara contingent and remain there.

shloka_text: गन्धहस्तीवदुर्धर्षस्तरस्वीगन्धमादनः । तिष्ठेद्वानरवाहिन्यास्सव्यंपार्श्वंसमाश्रित:।। 6.24.16।।
transliteration: gandhahastīvadurdharṣastarasvīgandhamādanaḥ | tiṣṭhedvānaravāhinyāssavyaṃpārśvaṃsamāśrita:
translation: गन्धहस्तीव like a proud elephant, दुर्धर्षः difficult to conquer, तरस्वी strong one, गन्धमादनः Gandhamadana, वानरवाहिन्याः Vanara battalion, सव्यंपार्श्वम् right side, समाश्रितः assemble, तिष्ठेत् remain.
explanation: "Let the mighty Gandhamadana, a difficult one to conquer like a proud elephant, take the battalion of army and stay on the right side"

shloka_text: मूर्ध्निस्थास्याम्यहंयुक्तोलक्ष्मणेनसमन्वितः । जाम्बवांश्चसुषेणश्चवेगदर्शीचवानरः ।।6.24.17।। ऋक्षमुख्यामहात्मानःकुक्षिंरक्षन्तुतेत्रयः ।
transliteration: mūrdhnisthāsyāmyahaṃyuktolakṣmaṇenasamanvitaḥ | jāmbavāṃścasuṣeṇaścavegadarśīcavānaraḥ  ṛkṣamukhyāmahātmānaḥkukṣiṃrakṣantutetrayaḥ |
translation: अहम् myself, लक्ष्मणेन along with Lakshmana, समन्वितः alert, युक्त: appropriate, मूर्ध्नि at the head, स्थास्यामि will remain, जाम्बवांश्च Jambavan and also, सुषेणश्च Sushena, वानरः Vanaras, वेगदर्शीच quick at sighting, महात्मानः great ones, ते those, त्रयः three, ऋक्षमुख्याः chiefs of Bears, कुक्षिम् the belly part, रक्षन्तु remain protecting.
explanation: "I and Lakshmana will be alert at the head side. Let Jambavan Sushena and the three chiefs of Bears who are strong and quick at sighting remain protecting the belly of the army."

shloka_text: जघनंकपिसेनायाःकपिराजोऽभिरक्षतु । पश्चार्धमिवलोकस्यप्रचेतास्तेजसावृतः ।।6.24.18।।
transliteration: jaghanaṃkapisenāyāḥkapirājo'bhirakṣatu | paścārdhamivalokasyapracetāstejasāvṛtaḥ
translation: तेजसा brilliant, आवृतः covered, प्रचेताः Pracheta, लोकस्य world's, पश्चार्धमिव as if ruling the west, कपिराजः king of Vanaras, कपिसेनायाः Vanara army's, जघम् hips and loins, अभिरक्षु let him protect.
explanation: "Just as Pracheta who is covered by brilliance, rules the western side of the world, let the king of Vanaras protect the hips and loin portion of the Vanara army."

shloka_text: सुविभक्तमहाव्यूहामहावानररक्षिता । अनीकिनीसाविबभौयथाद्यौस्साभ्रसम्प्लवा ।।6.24.19।।
transliteration: suvibhaktamahāvyūhāmahāvānararakṣitā | anīkinīsāvibabhauyathādyaussābhrasamplavā
translation: सुविभक्तमहाव्यूहा organized that way in the protection of Vanaras, महावानररक्षिता protected the army of Vanaras, साअनीकिनी that army force, साभ्रसम्प्लवा mass of clouds, द्यौःइव like the heavens विबभौ shone.
explanation: The Vanara army force organized that way to protect the Vanaras, shone like the mass of clouds in heaven.

shloka_text: प्रगृह्यगिरिशृङ्गाणिमहातश्चमहीरुहन् । लङ्कांविमर्दयिषवोरणे ।।6.24.20।।
transliteration: pragṛhyagiriśṛṅgāṇimahātaścamahīruhan | laṅkāṃvimardayiṣavoraṇe
translation: वानराः Vanaras, गिरशृङ्काणि with peaks of mountains, महतः great, महीरुहान् huge trees, प्रगृह्य seizing, रणे in war, विमर्धयिषवः smash, लङ्काम् to Lanka, आशेदुः resolved.
explanation: Vanaras resolved to go taking peaks of mountains and huge trees to smash Lanka in war.

shloka_text: शिखरैर्विकिरामैनांलङ्कांमुष्टभिरेववा । इतिस्मदधिरेसर्वेमनांसिहरिपुङ्गवाः ।।6.24.21।।
transliteration: śikharairvikirāmaināṃlaṅkāṃmuṣṭabhirevavā | itismadadhiresarvemanāṃsiharipuṅgavāḥ
translation: एनाम् thus, लङ्काम् that Lanka, शिखरैः with peaks, मुष्टिभिरेववा or with bare fists, विकिराम crush it to powder, इतिसर्वे thus all, हरिपुङ्गवाः Vanara leaders, मनांसि determined in their mind, दधिरे hold, स्म indeed.
explanation: Thus resolved the Vanara leaders in their mind to crush Lanka with its mountain peaks into powder with their bare fists, indeed.

shloka_text: ततोरामोमहातेजास्सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत् । सुविभक्तानिसैन्यानिशुकएषविमुच्यताम् ।।6.24.22।।
transliteration: tatorāmomahātejāssugrīvamidamabravīt | suvibhaktānisainyāniśukaeṣavimucyatām
translation: ततः there upon, महातेज splendid, रामः Rama, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva's, इदम् , thus, अब्रवीत् spoke, सैन्यानि the army, सुविभक्तानि the divided, एषः thus, शुकः Suka, विमुच्यताम् relieved.
explanation: Having heard Sugriva, there after splendid Rama spoke thus. "The army is divided (placed in position). Suka may be relieved."

shloka_text: रामस्यतुवचश्श्रुत्वावानरेन्द्रोमहाबलः । मोचयामासतंदूतंशुकंरामस्यशासनात् ।।6.24.23।।
transliteration: rāmasyatuvacaśśrutvāvānarendromahābalaḥ | mocayāmāsataṃdūtaṃśukaṃrāmasyaśāsanāt
translation: महाबल mighty, वानरेन्द्रः king of Vanaras, रामस्य Rama's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, रामस्य Rama's, शासनात् by the instruction, तंदूतम् that envoy, शुकम् happy, मोचयामास was relieved.
explanation: Having heard Rama's words Sugriva, the mighty king of Vanaras was happy and relieved the envoy on the instruction of Rama.

shloka_text: मोचितोरामवाक्येनवानरैश्चनिपीडितः । शुकःपरमसन्त्रस्तोरक्षोधिपमुपागमत् ।।6.24.24।।
transliteration: mocitorāmavākyenavānaraiścanipīḍitaḥ | śukaḥparamasantrastorakṣodhipamupāgamat
translation: वानरैः by Vanaras, निपीडितः tormented, रामवाक्येन by Rama's word, मोचितः relieved, शुकः Suka, परमसन्त्रप्त highly terrified, रक्षोधिपम् to the king of Rakshasas, उपागमत् returned.
explanation: Relieved by the word of Rama, tormented Suka who was highly terrified returned to the king of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: रावणःप्रहसन्नेवशुकंवाक्यमुवाचह ।।6.24.25।। किमिमौतेसितौपक्षौलूनपक्षश्चदृश्यसे । कच्चिन्नानेकचित्तानांतेषांत्वंवशमागतः ।।6.24.26।।
transliteration: rāvaṇaḥprahasannevaśukaṃvākyamuvācaha  kimimautesitaupakṣaulūnapakṣaścadṛśyase | kaccinnānekacittānāṃteṣāṃtvaṃvaśamāgataḥ
translation: रावणः Ravana, प्रहसन्नेव laughing, शुकम् at Suka, वाक्यम् these words, उवाचह spoken, ते to you, इमौ these, पक्षौसीतौकिम् why are your wings fastened? , लूनपक्षश्चकूड even your wings have been clipped, दृश्यसे it appears, त्वम् you, अनेकचित्तानाम् fickle minded, तेषाम् their, वशम् clutches, नआगतः not fallen under कच्चित् I suppose.
explanation: Laughing at Suka, Ravana spoke these words. "Why are your wings fastened? Your wings have been clipped, it appears!. I suppose you have not fallen under the clutches of the fickle minded Vanaras!"

shloka_text: रावणःप्रहसन्नेवशुकंवाक्यमुवाचह ।।6.24.25।। किमिमौतेसितौपक्षौलूनपक्षश्चदृश्यसे । कच्चिन्नानेकचित्तानांतेषांत्वंवशमागतः ।।6.24.26।।
transliteration: rāvaṇaḥprahasannevaśukaṃvākyamuvācaha  kimimautesitaupakṣaulūnapakṣaścadṛśyase | kaccinnānekacittānāṃteṣāṃtvaṃvaśamāgataḥ
translation: रावणः Ravana, प्रहसन्नेव laughing, शुकम् at Suka, वाक्यम् these words, उवाचह spoken, ते to you, इमौ these, पक्षौसीतौकिम् why are your wings fastened? , लूनपक्षश्चकूड even your wings have been clipped, दृश्यसे it appears, त्वम् you, अनेकचित्तानाम् fickle minded, तेषाम् their, वशम् clutches, नआगतः not fallen under कच्चित् I suppose.
explanation: Laughing at Suka, Ravana spoke these words. "Why are your wings fastened? Your wings have been clipped, it appears!. I suppose you have not fallen under the clutches of the fickle minded Vanaras!"

shloka_text: ततस्सभयसंविग्नस्तदाराज्ञाभिचोदितः । वचनंप्रत्युवाचेदंराक्षसाधिपमुत्तमम् ।।6.24.27।। सागरस्योत्तरेतीरेऽब्रवंतेवचनंतथा । यथासन्धेशमक्लिष्टंसान्त्वयन् श्लक्ष्णयागिरा ।।6.24.28।।
transliteration: tatassabhayasaṃvignastadārājñābhicoditaḥ | vacanaṃpratyuvācedaṃrākṣasādhipamuttamam  sāgarasyottaretīre'bravaṃtevacanaṃtathā | yathāsandheśamakliṣṭaṃsāntvayan ślakṣṇayāgirā
translation: ततः then, भयसंविग्नः caught by fear, सः he, तदा then, राज्ञा by king, चोदितः directed, राक्षसाधिपम् Ravana, उत्तमम् excellent, इदम these, वचनम् words, प्रत्युवाच replied, सागरस्य ocean's, उत्तरेतीरे northern bank श्लक्ष्णया gently, गिरा speech, सान्त्वयन् trembling, यथासन्देशम् as conveyed by you, अक्लिष्टम् , ते you, वचनम् words, तथा like that, अब्रवम् told.
explanation: Then Suka who was caught by fear, having been asked by the king, trembling away thus replied to the Rakshasa king. "I went to the northern shore of the ocean and delivered gently the speech just as it was conveyed by you."

shloka_text: ततस्सभयसंविग्नस्तदाराज्ञाभिचोदितः । वचनंप्रत्युवाचेदंराक्षसाधिपमुत्तमम् ।।6.24.27।। सागरस्योत्तरेतीरेऽब्रवंतेवचनंतथा । यथासन्धेशमक्लिष्टंसान्त्वयन् श्लक्ष्णयागिरा ।।6.24.28।।
transliteration: tatassabhayasaṃvignastadārājñābhicoditaḥ | vacanaṃpratyuvācedaṃrākṣasādhipamuttamam  sāgarasyottaretīre'bravaṃtevacanaṃtathā | yathāsandheśamakliṣṭaṃsāntvayan ślakṣṇayāgirā
translation: ततः then, भयसंविग्नः caught by fear, सः he, तदा then, राज्ञा by king, चोदितः directed, राक्षसाधिपम् Ravana, उत्तमम् excellent, इदम these, वचनम् words, प्रत्युवाच replied, सागरस्य ocean's, उत्तरेतीरे northern bank श्लक्ष्णया gently, गिरा speech, सान्त्वयन् trembling, यथासन्देशम् as conveyed by you, अक्लिष्टम् , ते you, वचनम् words, तथा like that, अब्रवम् told.
explanation: Then Suka who was caught by fear, having been asked by the king, trembling away thus replied to the Rakshasa king. "I went to the northern shore of the ocean and delivered gently the speech just as it was conveyed by you."

shloka_text: क्रुद्धैस्सैरहमुत्प्लुतदृष्टमात्रःप्लवङ्गमैः । गृहीतोऽस्म्यपिचारब्दोहन्तुंलोप्तुंचमुष्टिभि ।।6.24.29।।
transliteration: kruddhaissairahamutplutadṛṣṭamātraḥplavaṅgamaiḥ | gṛhīto'smyapicārabdohantuṃloptuṃcamuṣṭibhi
translation: दृष्टमात्रः as soon as they saw, अहम् me, क्रुद्धै enraged, तैःप्लवङ्गमैः those monkeys, उत्प्लुत्य rising up, गृहीतःअस्मि taking hold of me, अपिच and also, मुष्टिभिः with fists, हन्तुम् to slay, लोप्तुंच and injuring, आरब्दः started.
explanation: As soon as they saw me, the enraged Vanaras rising up (into the sky) took hold of me and started injuring me and slaying me.

shloka_text: नैवसम्भाषितुंशक्यास्सम्प्रश्नोऽत्रनलभ्यते । प्रकृत्याकोपनास्तीक्ष्णानानराराक्षसाधिप ।।6.24.30।।
transliteration: naivasambhāṣituṃśakyāssampraśno'tranalabhyate | prakṛtyākopanāstīkṣṇānānarārākṣasādhipa
translation: राक्षसाधिप king of Rakshasas, ते to you, सम्भाषितुम् to negotiate, नशक्याः was not possible, अत्र there, सम्प्रश्नः to question, नलम्यते had no opportunity, वानराः Vanaras, प्रकृत्या by nature, कोपनाः are violent, तीक्ष्णाः highly furious.
explanation: "O king of Rakshasas! It was not possible to negotiate there with the Vanaras). I had no opportunity to interrogate with them. By nature, Vanaras are violent and are highly furious."

shloka_text: सचहन्ताविराधस्यकबन्धस्यखरस्यच । सुग्रीवसहितोरामस्सीताया: पदमागतः ।।6.24.31।।
transliteration: sacahantāvirādhasyakabandhasyakharasyaca | sugrīvasahitorāmassītāyā: padamāgataḥ
translation: विराधस्य Viradha's, कबन्धस्य Kabhanda's, खरस्य Khara's, हन्ता life was taken, सःरामः by that Rama, सुग्रीवसहितः accompanied by Sugriva, सीताया: Sita's, पदम् set foot into, आगतः arrived.
explanation: "The life of Viradha, Kabhanda and Khara has been taken away by Rama. Accompanied by Sugriva they have set their foot into Lanka for Sita's sake."

shloka_text: सकृत्वासागरेसेतुंतीर्त्वाचलवणोदधिम् । एषरक्षांसिनिर्दूयधन्वीतिष्ठतिराघवः ।।6.24.32।।
transliteration: sakṛtvāsāgaresetuṃtīrtvācalavaṇodadhim | eṣarakṣāṃsinirdūyadhanvītiṣṭhatirāghavaḥ
translation: एषः such, राघवः Raghava, सागरे on the ocean, सेतुम् bridge, कृत्वा having crossed, लवणोदधिम् salt sea, तीर्त्वाच shore of, रक्षां Rakshasas, विर्दूय distancing, धन्वी wielding a bow, तिष्ठति stands.
explanation: "Mighty Raghava having crossed the salt sea and reached the shore of Rakshasas, organized them (Vanaras) and stood wielding a bow."

shloka_text: ऋक्षवानरसङ्घानामनीकानिसहस्रशः । गिरिमेघनिकाशानांछादयन्तिवसुन्धराम् ।।6.24.33।।
transliteration: ṛkṣavānarasaṅghānāmanīkānisahasraśaḥ | girimeghanikāśānāṃchādayantivasundharām
translation: गिरिमेघनिकाशानाम् resembling mountains and clouds, ऋक्षवानरसङ्घानाम् army of Bears and Vanaras, सहस्रशः in thousands, अनीकानि an army force, वसुन्धराम् on the land, छादयन्ति settled.
explanation: "Thousands of army forces of monkeys and Bears resembling mountains and clouds have settled on the ground."

shloka_text: राक्षसानांबलौघस्यवानरेन्द्रबलस्यच । नैतयोर्विद्यतेसन्धिर्देवदानवयोरिव ।।6.24.34।।
transliteration: rākṣasānāṃbalaughasyavānarendrabalasyaca | naitayorvidyatesandhirdevadānavayoriva
translation: राक्षसां Rakshasas, बलौघस्य for Bears, वानरेन्द्रबलस्यच for army of Vanara king's, एतयोः for both of them, देवदानवयोरिव like for gods and demons, सन्धि: alliance, नविद्यते not possible.
explanation: Alliance is not possible between Rakshasas and army of Bears and Vanaras, just as alliance is not possible between gods and demons.

shloka_text: पुराप्राकारमायान्तिक्षिप्रमेकतरंकुरु । सीतांवास्मैप्रयच्छाशुसुयुद्धंवापिप्रदीयताम् ।।6.24.35।।
transliteration: purāprākāramāyāntikṣipramekataraṃkuru | sītāṃvāsmaiprayacchāśusuyuddhaṃvāpipradīyatām
translation: प्राकारम् boundary, पुरा of the city, आयान्ति will reach, क्षिप्रम् at once, एकतरम् one of the two, कुरु do, अस्मै you may, आसु give back, सीताम् Sita, प्रयच्छवा or implore you, सुयुद्धम् वापि or give good battle, प्रदीयताम् I suggest you
explanation: "They will reach the boundary wall. At once you may do one of the two that I suggest you do. I implore you either to give away Sita or give good battle."

shloka_text: शुकस्यवचनंश्रुत्वारावणोवाक्यमब्रवीत् । रोषसंरक्तनयनोनिर्दहन्निनचक्षुषा ।।6.24.36।।
transliteration: śukasyavacanaṃśrutvārāvaṇovākyamabravīt | roṣasaṃraktanayanonirdahanninacakṣuṣā
translation: रावणः Ravana, शुकस्य Suka's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, रोषसंरक्तनयनः with angry red eyes, चक्षुषा from his eyes, निर्दहन्निव as if he would burn with his glance, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवित् spoke.
explanation: Angry, redeyed Ravana, having heard Suka's words spoke as though he would burn him with his glance.

shloka_text: यदिमांप्रतियुध्येरन् देवगन्धर्वदानवाः । नैवसीतांप्रदास्यामिसर्वलोकभयादपि ।।6.24.37।।
transliteration: yadimāṃpratiyudhyeran devagandharvadānavāḥ | naivasītāṃpradāsyāmisarvalokabhayādapi
translation: देवगन्धर्वदानवाः gods, Gandharvas and demons, माम् with me, प्रतियुध्येरन्नपि even if come to wage war, सर्वलोकभयादपि even if all worlds threaten me, सीताम् Sita, नावप्रदास्यामि I shall not give away.
explanation: "Even if gods, Gandharvas and demons come to wage war with me, even if all the worlds threaten me, I shall not give away Sita."

shloka_text: कदासमभिधावन्तिराघवंमामकाश्शराः । वसन्तेपुष्पितंमत्ताभ्रमराइवपादपम् ।।6.24.38।।
transliteration: kadāsamabhidhāvantirāghavaṃmāmakāśśarāḥ | vasantepuṣpitaṃmattābhramarāivapādapam
translation: मामकाः my, शराः arrows, राघवम् to Raghava वसन्ते spring season, पुष्पितम् blossoms, पादपम् trees, मत्ताः drunken, ब्रमराःइव like the bees, कदा when, समभिधावन्ति would attack.
explanation: "Just as drunken bees reach the trees with blossoms in spring when will my arrows attack Rama?"

shloka_text: कदातूणीयशैर्दीप्तैर्गणश: कार्मुकच्युतैः । शरैरादीपयाम्येनमुल्काभिरिवकुञ्जरम् ।।6.24.39।।
transliteration: kadātūṇīyaśairdīptairgaṇaśa: kārmukacyutaiḥ | śarairādīpayāmyenamulkābhirivakuñjaram
translation: दीप्तै: glowing, तूणीयशै: from the famed quiver, कार्मुकच्युतैः fit to pierce, गणश: thousands of, शरैः darts, येन by which, कुञ्जरम् elephant, उल्काभिरिव like the burning sticks, कदाआदीपयामि when will I able to goad.
explanation: "When will the glowing arrows from my quiver, that are fit to pierce in thousands, be able to goad Rama like the burning fire sticks goad the elephants?"

shloka_text: तच्चास्यबलमादास्येबलेनमहतावृतः । ज्योतिषामिवसर्वेषांप्रभामुद्यन्दिवाकरः ।।6.24.40।।
transliteration: taccāsyabalamādāsyebalenamahatāvṛtaḥ | jyotiṣāmivasarveṣāṃprabhāmudyandivākaraḥ
translation: उद्यन् rising, दिवाकरः Sun, सर्वेषाम् of all, ज्योतिषाम् light, प्रभामिव like the radiance, महता great, बलेन army, वृतः surrounded by, अस्य his, तत् that, बलम् strength, आदास्ये obscure.
explanation: "Just as the rising Sun light obscures the radiance of all (other stars) when will I obscure him surrounded by his army?"

shloka_text: सागरस्येवमेवेगोमारुतस्येवमेगति: । नहिदाशरथिर्वेदतेनमांयोद्धुमिच्छति ।।6.24.41।।
transliteration: sāgarasyevamevegomārutasyevamegati: | nahidāśarathirvedatenamāṃyoddhumicchati
translation: मे I, वेगः speed, सागरस्येव like the ocean, मे I, गति: swiftness, मारुतस्येव like the WindGod, दाशरथिः Dasaratha's son, नहिवेद not know, तेव that is why, माम् with me, योध्दुम् to wage war, इच्छति desiring.
explanation: "I have the speed of the ocean and swiftness like the WindGod. Rama does not know this and desires to wage war with me."

shloka_text: नमेतूणीशयान्बाणान् सविषानिवपन्नगान् । रामःपश्यतिसङ्ग्रामेतेनमांयोध्दुमिच्छति ।।6.24.42।।
transliteration: nametūṇīśayānbāṇān saviṣānivapannagān | rāmaḥpaśyatisaṅgrāmetenamāṃyodhdumicchati
translation: सविषान् the poisonous, पन्नगानिव serpents like, तूणीशयान् in my quiver, मेबाणान् my arrows, रामः Rama, सङ्ग्रामे in battle, नपश्यति has not seen, तेन therefore, माम् with me, योध्दुम् combat, इच्छति desiring.
explanation: "Rama has not seen the poisonous arrows in my quiver in battle. Therefore, he is desiring comb at with me."

shloka_text: नजानातिपुरावीर्यममयुद्धेसराघवः । ममचापमयींवीणांशरकोणैःप्रवादिताम् ।।6.24.43।। ज्याशब्दतुमुलांघोरामार्तभीतमहास्वनाम् । नाराचतलसन्नादांतांममाहितवाहिनीम् ।।6.24.44।। अवगाह्यमहारङ्गंवादयिष्याम्यहंरणे ।
transliteration: najānātipurāvīryamamayuddhesarāghavaḥ | mamacāpamayīṃvīṇāṃśarakoṇaiḥpravāditām  jyāśabdatumulāṃghorāmārtabhītamahāsvanām | nārācatalasannādāṃtāṃmamāhitavāhinīm  avagāhyamahāraṅgaṃvādayiṣyāmyahaṃraṇe |
translation: सःराघवः that Rama, पुरा in the past, युद्धे in war, मम my, वीर्यम् valour, नजानाति not known, अहम् I, रणे in war, ताम् them, मम my, आहितवाहिनीम् entering the enemy's army, महारङ्गम् formidable Veena, अवगाह्य holding, शरकोणैः by the sharp heads of arrows, प्रवादिताम् makes sounds of challenge, ज्याशब्दतुमुलाम् that tumultuous noise, घोराम् terrific, आर्तभीतमहास्वनाम् high sound caused by the destitute and frightened ones, नाराचतलंसन्नादाम् its sound like that of iron arrows, चापमयीम् with that bow in hand, मम of mine, वीणाम् Veena, वादयिष्यामि will play.
explanation: "He has not known my valour in war. Entering the enemy's army holding my formidable Veena, making challenging sounds with the sharp heads of arrows, causing tumultuous noise like the sound of cry of destitute and frightened ones with iron arrows, I will play the Veena of my bow in hand."

shloka_text: नजानातिपुरावीर्यममयुद्धेसराघवः । ममचापमयींवीणांशरकोणैःप्रवादिताम् ।।6.24.43।। ज्याशब्दतुमुलांघोरामार्तभीतमहास्वनाम् । नाराचतलसन्नादांतांममाहितवाहिनीम् ।।6.24.44।। अवगाह्यमहारङ्गंवादयिष्याम्यहंरणे ।
transliteration: najānātipurāvīryamamayuddhesarāghavaḥ | mamacāpamayīṃvīṇāṃśarakoṇaiḥpravāditām  jyāśabdatumulāṃghorāmārtabhītamahāsvanām | nārācatalasannādāṃtāṃmamāhitavāhinīm  avagāhyamahāraṅgaṃvādayiṣyāmyahaṃraṇe |
translation: सःराघवः that Rama, पुरा in the past, युद्धे in war, मम my, वीर्यम् valour, नजानाति not known, अहम् I, रणे in war, ताम् them, मम my, आहितवाहिनीम् entering the enemy's army, महारङ्गम् formidable Veena, अवगाह्य holding, शरकोणैः by the sharp heads of arrows, प्रवादिताम् makes sounds of challenge, ज्याशब्दतुमुलाम् that tumultuous noise, घोराम् terrific, आर्तभीतमहास्वनाम् high sound caused by the destitute and frightened ones, नाराचतलंसन्नादाम् its sound like that of iron arrows, चापमयीम् with that bow in hand, मम of mine, वीणाम् Veena, वादयिष्यामि will play.
explanation: "He has not known my valour in war. Entering the enemy's army holding my formidable Veena, making challenging sounds with the sharp heads of arrows, causing tumultuous noise like the sound of cry of destitute and frightened ones with iron arrows, I will play the Veena of my bow in hand."

shloka_text: नवासवेनापिसहस्रचक्षुषायथास्मिशक्योवरुणेनवास्वयम् । यमेनवाधर्षयितुंशराग्निनामहाहवेवैश्रवणेनवापुन: ।। 6.24.45।।
transliteration: navāsavenāpisahasracakṣuṣāyathāsmiśakyovaruṇenavāsvayam | yamenavādharṣayituṃśarāgnināmahāhavevaiśravaṇenavāpuna:
translation: सहस्रचक्षुषा thousand eyed one, Indra, वासवेनानिपि even god of water, पुन: again, वरुणेनापि for Varuna also, युध्दे in war, यमेनवा if he is god of death, Yama also, महाहवे great fire, स्वयम् himself, वैश्रवणेनवा even if he be Lord of wealth Kubera, शराग्निना by my arrows, शक्यः possible, न not.
explanation: "It is not possible (to win over) for the thousand eyed Indra, or even Varuna, the god presiding over water, or even for Yama, the god of death and again even for Kubera the god of wealth to face the fire of my arrows (said Ravana to Suka)." ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकावेयुध्दकाण्डेचतुर्विंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the twenty fourth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic, the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सबलेसागरंतीर्णेरामेदशरथात्मजे । अमात्यौरावणश्रीमानब्रवीच्छुकसारणौ ।।6.25.1।।
transliteration: sabalesāgaraṃtīrṇerāmedaśarathātmaje | amātyaurāvaṇaśrīmānabravīcchukasāraṇau
translation: सबले along with army, दशरथात्मजे Dasaratha's son, रामे Rama, सागरम् ocean, तीर्णे crossing the shore, श्रीमान् exuberant, रावणः Ravana, अमात्यौ with ministers, शुकसारणौ to Suka and Saarana, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: On hearing about Rama, the son of Dasaratha crossing the shore of the ocean along with the army, exuberant Ravana spoke to his ministers Suka and Saarana.
comments: Ravana sends Suka and Saarana as spies to the Vanara army. They assume the form of Vanaras and enter the Vanara army. Vibheeshana recognizes them but Rama lets them go.

shloka_text: समग्रंसागरंतीर्णंदुस्तरंवानरंबलम् । अभूतपूर्वंरामेणसागरेसेतुबन्धनम् ।।6.25.2।।
transliteration: samagraṃsāgaraṃtīrṇaṃdustaraṃvānaraṃbalam | abhūtapūrvaṃrāmeṇasāgaresetubandhanam
translation: समग्रं all of them together, वानरम् Vanaras, बलम् army, दुस्तरम् arduous, सागरम् ocean, तीर्णम् crossed, रामेण by Rama, सागरे in the ocean अभूतपूर्वम् that which is not known before, सेतुबन्धनम् construction.
explanation: "That all the Vanara army together with Rama have crossed the arduous ocean and that the construction of a bridge (is possible) in the sea is not known before."

shloka_text: सागरेसेतुबन्दंतुनश्रद्दध्यांकथञ्चन । अवश्यंचापिसङ् ख्येयंतन्मयावानरंबलम् ।।6.25.3।।
transliteration: sāgaresetubandaṃtunaśraddadhyāṃkathañcana | avaśyaṃcāpisaṅ khyeyaṃtanmayāvānaraṃbalam
translation: सागरे in the sea, तम् they, सेतुबन्धम् constructed bridge, कथञ्चन even, नश्रद्दधाम् not believable, तत् those, वानरंबलम् Vanara force, मया to me, अवश्यम् surely, सङ् ख्येयंच the size of their army.
explanation: "It is not believable even to me that they constructed a bridge in the sea. Surely I wish to know the size of their army."

shloka_text: भवन्तौवानरंसैन्यंप्रविश्यानुपलक्षितौ । परिमाणंचवीर्यंचयेचमुख्याःप्लवङ्घमाः ।।6.25.4।। मन्त्रिणोयेचरामस्यसुग्रीवस्यचसम्मता: । येपूर्वमभिवर्तन्तेयेचशूराःप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.25.5।। सचसेतुर्यथाबद्धस्सागरेसलिलार्णवे । निवेशंचयधातेषांवानराणांमहात्मनाम् ।।6.25.6।। रामस्यव्यवसायंचवीर्यंप्रहरणानिच । लक्ष्मणस्यचवीर्यंतत्त्वतोज्ञातुमर्हथः ।।6.25.7।।
transliteration: bhavantauvānaraṃsainyaṃpraviśyānupalakṣitau | parimāṇaṃcavīryaṃcayecamukhyāḥplavaṅghamāḥ  mantriṇoyecarāmasyasugrīvasyacasammatā: | yepūrvamabhivartanteyecaśūrāḥplavaṅgamāḥ  sacaseturyathābaddhassāgaresalilārṇave | niveśaṃcayadhāteṣāṃvānarāṇāṃmahātmanām  rāmasyavyavasāyaṃcavīryaṃpraharaṇānica | lakṣmaṇasyacavīryaṃtattvatojñātumarhathaḥ
translation: भवन्तौ you both, अनुपलक्षितौ without their notice, वानरम् Vanara's, सैन्यम् army, प्रविश्य entering, परिमाणंच size of it, वीर्यंच heroes, ये of those, प्लवङ्गमाः of the monkeys, मुख्याः chief, रामस्य Rama's, सुग्रीवस्यच and Sugriva's, ये of those, मन्त्रिणः ministers, सङ्गताः groups, ये of those, पूर्वम् earlier, अभिवर्तन्ते those who are in forefront, ये of those, प्लवङ्गमाः monkeys, शूराः warriors, सलिलार्णने in the abode of waters, सागरे in the sea, सः that, सेतुः bridge, यधा centre, बद्धः built, महात्मनाम् great, तेषां of those वानराणाम् of the Vanaras, निवेशम् location, यथा in the same way, रामस्यव्यवसायंच Rama's efforts, वीर्यम् valour, प्रहरणानिच weapons also, वीरस्य of the heroes, लक्षयणस्यच and of Lakshmana's, तत्त्वतः truly, ज्ञातुम् wish to know, अर्हथः I ought.
explanation: "Both of you enter Vanara's army without their knowledge and know about the size of the army, of Rama and Sugriva's ministers, of army chiefs who are in the forefront, of the warriors, how they have built bridge in the middle of the sea, about the location of Vanaras and in the same way the efforts and valour of heroes Rama and Lakshmana, I ought to know truly."

shloka_text: कश्चसेनापतिस्तेषांवानराणांमहौजसाम् । तच्चज्ञात्वायथातत्त्वंशीघ्रमगन्तुमर्हथः ।।6.25.8।।
transliteration: kaścasenāpatisteṣāṃvānarāṇāṃmahaujasām | taccajñātvāyathātattvaṃśīghramagantumarhathaḥ
translation: महौजसाम् highly energetic ones, तेषाम् those, वानराणाम् among the Vanaras, सेनापतिः army chief, कः who, तच्च all these, यथातत्त्वम् their matters, ज्ञात्वाशीघ्रम् knowing quickly, अगन्तुम् you return, अर्हथः fit.
explanation: Among those energetic Vanaras, who is the chief of the army? Knowing all these matters, it is fit for you to return quickly.

shloka_text: इतिप्रतिसमादिष्टौराक्षसौशुकसारणौ । हरिरूपधरौवीरौप्रविष्टौवानरंबलम् ।।6.25.9।।
transliteration: itipratisamādiṣṭaurākṣasauśukasāraṇau | harirūpadharauvīraupraviṣṭauvānaraṃbalam
translation: इति thus, प्रतिसमाधिष्टौ having accepted the order, वीरौ heroes, शुकसारणौ S uka and Saarana, राक्षसौ both Rakshasas, हरिरूपधरौ taking the form of Vanaras, वानरम् in to Vanaras, बलम् army, प्रविष्टौ entered.
explanation: Having accepted the order, both the Rakshasa heroes, Suka and Saarana took the form of Vanaras and entered the Vanara army.

shloka_text: ततस्तद्वानरंसैन्यमचिन्त्यंरोमहर्षणम् । सङ् ख्यातुंनाध्यगच्छेतांतदातौशुकसारणौ ।।6.25.10।।
transliteration: tatastadvānaraṃsainyamacintyaṃromaharṣaṇam | saṅ khyātuṃnādhyagacchetāṃtadātauśukasāraṇau
translation: ततः there upon, तौ both of them, शुकसारणौ Suka and Saarana, आचिन्त्यम् that which cannot be conceived, रोमहर्षणम् that which caused raising of hair (stunned), तत् that, वानरम् Vanara's, सैन्यम् army, सङ् ख्यातुम् to count the numbers, तदा that time, नाध्यगच्छेताम् whose number could not be known (not conceived).
explanation: There upon both Suka and Saarana did not know the numbers (of the army) at that time as they could not count the numbers from there as it could not be conceived. It caused the raising of their hair.

shloka_text: संस्थितंपर्वताग्रेषुनिर्दरेषुगुहासुच । समुद्रस्यचतीरेषुवनेषूपवनेषुच ।।6.25.11।। तरमाणंचतीर्णंचतर्तुकामंचसर्वशः । निविष्टंनिविश्चैवभीमनादंमहाबलम् ।।6.25.12।। तद्बलार्णवमक्षोभ्यंददृशातेनिशाचरौ ।
transliteration: saṃsthitaṃparvatāgreṣunirdareṣuguhāsuca | samudrasyacatīreṣuvaneṣūpavaneṣuca  taramāṇaṃcatīrṇaṃcatartukāmaṃcasarvaśaḥ | niviṣṭaṃniviścaivabhīmanādaṃmahābalam  tadbalārṇavamakṣobhyaṃdadṛśāteniśācarau |
translation: पर्वताग्रेषु on mountain summits, निर्दरेषु in caverns, गुहासुच in caves, समुद्रस्य ocean's, तीरेषु shores, वनेषु in forests, उपवनेषुच and adjoining gardens, स्थितम् settled, तरमाणम् crossing, तीर्णंच shores, तर्तुकामंच some in the process of crossing, सर्वशः all over, निविष्टम् settled, निविश्चे staying, भीमनादम् terrific noise, महाबलम् great force, अक्षोभ्यम् that which is never ending, तद्बलार्णवम् that ocean of army, निशाचरौ the Rakshasas, ददृशाते witnessed.
explanation: The ocean of army settled on the mountain summits, in caverns and caves, on the shores of the ocean, in the forests and adjoining gardens some who crossed the sea some in the process of crossing settled all over was witnessed by the Rakshasas. It was never ending and making terrific noise.
