shloka_text: तेषांप्रविशतांतत्रवानराणांमहौजसाम् । पुष्पसंसर्गसुरभिर्ववौघ्राणसुखोऽनिलः ।।6.39.13।।
transliteration: teṣāṃpraviśatāṃtatravānarāṇāṃmahaujasām | puṣpasaṃsargasurabhirvavaughrāṇasukho'nilaḥ
translation: महौजसाम् of extraordinary energy, तेषाम् all of them, वानराणाम् the Vanaras, तत्र then, प्रविशताम् as they were entering, पुष्पसंसर्गसुरभिः breeze redolent with the fragrance of flowers, घ्राणसुखः enjoying the fragrance, अनिलः wind, ववौ blew
explanation: Then the Vanaras of extraordinary energy, were enjoying the breeze redolent with the fragrance of flowers as they were entering, and the wind blew.

shloka_text: अन्येतुहरिवीराणांयूथान्निष्क्रम्ययूथपाः । सुग्रीवेणाभ्यनुज्ञातालङ्कांजग्मुःपताकिनीम् ।।6.39.14।।
transliteration: anyetuharivīrāṇāṃyūthānniṣkramyayūthapāḥ | sugrīveṇābhyanujñātālaṅkāṃjagmuḥpatākinīm
translation: अन्ये others, यूथपाःतु heroes too, हरिवीराणाम् monkey heroes, यूथात् troops, निष्क्रम्य left, सुग्रीवेण to Sugriva, अभ्यनुज्ञाताः permitted by, पताकिनीम् decorated with flags, लङ्काम् Lanka, जग्मुः went.
explanation: Some other monkey heroes permitted by Sugriva went to Lanka decorated with flags.

shloka_text: वित्रासयन्तोविहगांस्त्रासयन्तोमृगद्विपान् । कम्पयन्तश्चतांलङ्कांनादैस्तेनदतांवराः ।।6.39.15।।
transliteration: vitrāsayantovihagāṃstrāsayantomṛgadvipān | kampayantaścatāṃlaṅkāṃnādaistenadatāṃvarāḥ
translation: नदताम् capable of roaring, वराः best, विहगां birds, वित्रासयन्तः spreading, मृगद्विपान् dispiriting the deer and elephants, नादैः by the sound, ते they, लङ्काम् into Lanka, कम्पयन्तश्च terrifying.
explanation: Other monkeys capable of roaring went into Lanka, spreading out terrifying the birds, dispiriting the deer and elephants by noise.

shloka_text: कुर्वन्तस्तेमहावेगामहींचरणपीडिताम् । रजश्चसहसैवोर्थ्वंजगामचरणोत्थितम् ।।6.39.16।।
transliteration: kurvantastemahāvegāmahīṃcaraṇapīḍitām | rajaścasahasaivorthvaṃjagāmacaraṇotthitam
translation: महावेगाः capable of speed, ते they, महीम् great force, चरणपीडिताम् trampling down with feet, कुर्वन्तः doing, चरणोत्थितम् under feet, रजश्च dust, सहसैव in a second, ऊर्थ्वम् up to the sky, जगाम wentrose.
explanation: Those Vanaras endowed with speed went trampling down on the ground with force, the dust under their feet rose to the sky in a fraction of a second.

shloka_text: ऋक्षास्सिंहावराहाश्चमहिषावारणामृगाः । तेनशब्देनवित्रस्ताजग्मुर्भीतादिशोदश ।।6.39.17।।
transliteration: ṛkṣāssiṃhāvarāhāścamahiṣāvāraṇāmṛgāḥ | tenaśabdenavitrastājagmurbhītādiśodaśa
translation: तेन by that, शब्देन sound, ऋक्षाः Bears, सिंहावराहश्च lions and pigs, महिषाः buffaloes, वारणामृगाः elephants, वित्रस्ताः alarmed, भीताः frightened, दश ten, दिशः directions, जग्मुः went.
explanation: Alarmed by that sound the Bears, lions, pigs, elephants, buffaloes were frightened and went in all the ten directions.

shloka_text: शिखरंतत्त्रिकूटस्यप्रांशुचैकंदिविस्पृशम् । समन्तात्पुष्पसंञ्छन्नंमहारजतसन्निभम् ।।6.39.18।। शतयोजनविस्तीर्णंविमलंचारुदर्शनम् । श्लक्ष्णंश्रीमन्महच्छैवदुष्प्रापंशकुनैरपि ।।6.39.19।। मनसाऽपिदुरारोहंकिंपुनःकर्मणाजनैः ।
transliteration: śikharaṃtattrikūṭasyaprāṃśucaikaṃdivispṛśam | samantātpuṣpasaṃñchannaṃmahārajatasannibham  śatayojanavistīrṇaṃvimalaṃcārudarśanam | ślakṣṇaṃśrīmanmahacchaivaduṣprāpaṃśakunairapi  manasā'pidurārohaṃkiṃpunaḥkarmaṇājanaiḥ |
translation: समन्तात् all over, पुष्पसञ्छन्नम् covered with flowers, महारजतसन्निभम् sparkled with gold, शतयोजनविस्तीर्णम् spread over a hundred yojanas, विमलम् whitepure, चारुदर्शनम् beautiful to look, श्लक्ष्णम् smooth, श्रीमत् splendid, महच्छैव sages, शकुनैरपि even for birds, दुष्प्रापम् not possible to reach, जनैः people, मनसापि in thought, दुरारोहम् difficult to access, कर्मणा by physical action, किंपुनः why again, प्रांशु praise worthy, दिविस्पृशम् touching the sky, एकम् alone, त्रिकूटस्यशिखरम् peak of Trikuta.
explanation: Trikuta peak was fully covered with flowers, sparkled with gold, spread over a hundred yojanas, beautiful to look at, splendid and smooth. It is difficult even for birds to reach, for sages even in thought and difficult to access by any physical action. It is praiseworthy as if touching the sky alone.

shloka_text: शिखरंतत्त्रिकूटस्यप्रांशुचैकंदिविस्पृशम् । समन्तात्पुष्पसंञ्छन्नंमहारजतसन्निभम् ।।6.39.18।। शतयोजनविस्तीर्णंविमलंचारुदर्शनम् । श्लक्ष्णंश्रीमन्महच्छैवदुष्प्रापंशकुनैरपि ।।6.39.19।। मनसाऽपिदुरारोहंकिंपुनःकर्मणाजनैः ।

shloka_text: निविष्टातत्रशिखरेलङ्कारावणपालिता ।।6.39.20।। शतयोजनविस्तीर्णात्रिंशद्योजनमायता ।
transliteration: niviṣṭātatraśikharelaṅkārāvaṇapālitā  śatayojanavistīrṇātriṃśadyojanamāyatā |
translation: तत्र there, शिखरे on top of the peak, रावणपालिता ruled by Ravana, शतयोजनविस्तीर्णा a hundred yojanas in breadth, त्रिंशद्योजनम् thirty yojanas, आयता long, लङ्का Lanka, निविष्टा experienced.
explanation: Lanka ruled by Ravana was a hundred yojanas in breadth and thirty yojanas in length was seen.

shloka_text: सापुरीगोपुरैरुच्चैःपाण्डुराम्बुदसन्निभैः । काञ्चनेनचशालेनराजतेनचशोभते ।।6.39.21।।
transliteration: sāpurīgopurairuccaiḥpāṇḍurāmbudasannibhaiḥ | kāñcanenacaśālenarājatenacaśobhate
translation: सा that, पुरी city, उच्चैः tall, पाण्डुराम्बुदसन्निभैः like white cluster of clouds, गोपुरैः towers, काञ्चनेन with gold, राजतेनच and silver, शालेन fortified, शोभते charming.
explanation: The city of Lanka looked charming with tall towers resembling white cluster of clouds fortified with gold and silver.

shloka_text: प्रासादैश्चविमानैश्चलङ्कापरमभूषिता । घनैरिवाऽतपापायेमध्यमंवैष्णवंपदम् ।।6.39.22।।
transliteration: prāsādaiścavimānaiścalaṅkāparamabhūṣitā | ghanairivā'tapāpāyemadhyamaṃvaiṣṇavaṃpadam
translation: प्रासादैश्च even the buildings, विमानैश्च resembled air planes, परमभूषिता decorated beautifully, लङ्का Lanka, आतपापापये exposed to the sun, घनैः rainy clouds, मध्यमम् in the centre, वैष्णवंपदम् इव resembling the abode of Vishnu.
explanation: The tall buildings decorated beautifully resembled air planes and were shining like heavy rainy clouds exposed to the sun. The building in the centre resembled the abode of Vishnu.

shloka_text: यस्यांस्तम्भसहस्रेणप्रासादस्समलङ्कृतः । कैलासशिखराकारोदृश्यतेखमिवोललिखन् ।।6.39.23।। चैत्यस्सराक्षसेन्द्रस्यबभूवपुरभूषणम् । शतेनरक्षसांनित्यंयस्समग्रेणरक्ष्यते ।।6.39.24।।
transliteration: yasyāṃstambhasahasreṇaprāsādassamalaṅkṛtaḥ | kailāsaśikharākārodṛśyatekhamivolalikhan  caityassarākṣasendrasyababhūvapurabhūṣaṇam | śatenarakṣasāṃnityaṃyassamagreṇarakṣyate
translation: यस्याम् in that city, यः that which is, नित्यम् always, रक्षसाम् protected, समग्रेण fully, शतेन hundred, रक्ष्यते graced, स्तम्बसहस्रेण thousand pillars, समलङ्कङ्कृतः ornament, कैलासशिखराकारः peak of mount Kailasa, प्रासादः palace, खम् sky, उललिखन्निव as if scraping, दृश्यते appeared, सः that, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य Rakshasa Lord's, पुरभूषणम् ornament of city, बभूव looked.
explanation: In that city, which was always protected fully by a hundred Rakshasas, there was a palace with thousand pillars, which looked like peak of mount Kailas, and was as though it was scraping the sky and it as like an ornament of Lanka, the city of Rakshasa's Lord.

shloka_text: यस्यांस्तम्भसहस्रेणप्रासादस्समलङ्कृतः । कैलासशिखराकारोदृश्यतेखमिवोललिखन् ।।6.39.23।। चैत्यस्सराक्षसेन्द्रस्यबभूवपुरभूषणम् । शतेनरक्षसांनित्यंयस्समग्रेणरक्ष्यते ।।6.39.24।।
transliteration: yasyāṃstambhasahasreṇaprāsādassamalaṅkṛtaḥ | kailāsaśikharākārodṛśyatekhamivolalikhan  caityassarākṣasendrasyababhūvapurabhūṣaṇam | śatenarakṣasāṃnityaṃyassamagreṇarakṣyate
translation: यस्याम् in that city, यः that which is, नित्यम् always, रक्षसाम् protected, समग्रेण fully, शतेन hundred, रक्ष्यते graced, स्तम्बसहस्रेण thousand pillars, समलङ्कङ्कृतः ornament, कैलासशिखराकारः peak of mount Kailasa, प्रासादः palace, खम् sky, उललिखन्निव as if scraping, दृश्यते appeared, सः that, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य Rakshasa Lord's, पुरभूषणम् ornament of city, बभूव looked.
explanation: In that city, which was always protected fully by a hundred Rakshasas, there was a palace with thousand pillars, which looked like peak of mount Kailas, and was as though it was scraping the sky and it as like an ornament of Lanka, the city of Rakshasa's Lord.

shloka_text: मनोज्ञांकाननवतींपर्वतैरुपशोभिताम् । नानाधातुविचित्रैश्चउद्यानैरुपशोभिताम् ।।6.39.25।। नानाविहङ्गासङ्घुष्टांनानामृगनिषेविताम् । नानाकुसुमसञ्छन्नांनानाराक्षससेविताम् ।।6.39.26।। तांसमृद्धांसमृद्धार्धांलक्ष्मीनान्लक्ष्मणाग्रजः । रावणस्यपुरींरामोददर्शसहवानरैः ।।6.39.27।।
transliteration: manojñāṃkānanavatīṃparvatairupaśobhitām | nānādhātuvicitraiścaudyānairupaśobhitām  nānāvihaṅgāsaṅghuṣṭāṃnānāmṛganiṣevitām | nānākusumasañchannāṃnānārākṣasasevitām  tāṃsamṛddhāṃsamṛddhārdhāṃlakṣmīnānlakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ | rāvaṇasyapurīṃrāmodadarśasahavānaraiḥ
translation: लक्ष्मीवान् prosperous, लक्ष्मणाग्रजः Lakshmana's brother, रामः Rama, मनोज्ञाम् delightfully, काननवतीम् different kinds of forests, नानाधातुविचित्रैः different kinds of minerals, पर्वतैः mountains, उपशोभिताम् very charming, उद्यानैः gardens, उपशोभिताम् very delightful, नानाविहङ्गसङ्घुष्टाम् variety of birds singing happily, नानामृगनिषेविताम् frequented by different kinds of deer, नानाकुसुमसञ्छन्नाम् endowed with different varieties of flowers, नानाराक्षससेविताम् attended by many Rakshasas, समृद्धाम् blooming, समृद्धार्थाम् prosperous, ताम् that city, पुरीम् city, वानरैःसह along with Vanaras, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Prosperous Rama, brother of Lakshmana along with Vanaras saw different kinds of forests, mountains filled with different kinds of minerals, delightful gardens endowed with different varieties of flowers, charming birds singing happily, frequented by a variety of deer, attended by Rakshasas. The city was blooming with prosperity.

shloka_text: तांमहागृहसम्बाधांदृष्टवालक्ष्मणपूर्वजः । नगरीममरप्रख्योविस्मयंप्राप्यवीर्यवान् ।।6.39.28।।
transliteration: tāṃmahāgṛhasambādhāṃdṛṣṭavālakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ | nagarīmamaraprakhyovismayaṃprāpyavīryavān
translation: वीर्यवान् valiant, लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः brother of Lakshmana, महागृहसम्बाधाम् filled with great palaces, अमरप्रख्यः distinct like Lord do Devatas, ताम् that, नगरीम् city, दृष्टवा on seeing, विस्मयम् wondered, प्राप्य became
explanation: Valiant brother of Lakshmana wondered seeing the city filled with great palaces, distinct like Lord Indra's city.

shloka_text: तांरत्नपूर्णांबहुसंविधानांप्रासादमालाभिरलङ्कृतांच । पुरींमहायन्त्रकवाटमुख्यांददर्शरामोमहताबलेन ।।6.39.29।।
transliteration: tāṃratnapūrṇāṃbahusaṃvidhānāṃprāsādamālābhiralaṅkṛtāṃca | purīṃmahāyantrakavāṭamukhyāṃdadarśarāmomahatābalena
translation: महता huge, बलेन army, रामः Rama, रत्नपूर्णम् jewelsgems, बहुसंविधानाम् accompanied by Vanaras, प्रासादमालाभिः garland s of buildings, अलङ्कृतांच adorned with, महायन्त्रकवाटमुख्याम् gates fitted with huge machines for war, महता large, बलेन by army, ताम् that, पुरीम् city, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Accompanied by huge Vanara army, Rama saw in the city of Lanka rows of buildingspalaces, adorned with gems, gates fitted with huge machines for war and large army of Ravana. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेएकोनचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the thirty ninth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततोरामस्सुवेलाग्रंयोजनद्वयमण्डलम् । अरुरोहससुग्रीवोहरियूधपसम्वृतः ।।6.40.1।।
transliteration: tatorāmassuvelāgraṃyojanadvayamaṇḍalam | arurohasasugrīvohariyūdhapasamvṛtaḥ
translation: ततः there upon, ससुग्रीवः Sugriva, हरियूथपः Vanara troop, सम्वृतः surrounded by, रामः Rama, योजनद्वयमण्डलम् spread over yojanas, सुवेलाग्रम् Suvela peak, उपारोहत् ascended.
explanation: Rama accompanied by Vanara troop and Sugriva, ascended the peak of Suvela mountain spread over yojanas.
comments: Rama catches the sight of Ravana standing on top of the palace. Provoked by anger Sugriva springs from the top of the mountain to Ravana, fights with him and returns back successfully.

shloka_text: स्थित्वामुहूर्तंतत्रैवदिशोदशविलोकयन् । त्रिकूटशिखरेरम्येनिर्मितांविश्वकर्मणा ।।6.40.2।। ददर्शलङ्कांसुन्यस्तांरम्यकाननशोभिताम् ।
transliteration: sthitvāmuhūrtaṃtatraivadiśodaśavilokayan | trikūṭaśikhareramyenirmitāṃviśvakarmaṇā  dadarśalaṅkāṃsunyastāṃramyakānanaśobhitām |
translation: मुहूर्तम् for a short while, तत्रैव there itself, स्थित्वा remaining, दश ten, दिशः directions, विलोयन् observing, रम्ये charming, त्रिकूटशिखरे peak of Trikuta, विश्वकर्मणा by Vishwakarma, निर्मिताम् constructed, सुन्यस्ताम् strongly, रम्यकाननशोभिताम् with delightful groves, लङ्काम् Lanka, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Remaining there for a short while, Rama observed the view of Lanka in all directions. He saw Lanka built on the charming peak of Trikuta strongly by Vishwakarma, endowed with delightful groves.

shloka_text: तस्यांगोपुरशृङ्गस्थंराक्षसेन्द्रंदुरासदम् ।।6.40.3।। श्वेतचामरपर्यन्तंविजयच्छत्रशोभितम् । रक्तचन्दनसंलिप्तंरत्नाभरणभूषितम् ।।6.40.4।। नीलजीमूतसङ्काशंहेमसञ्छादिताम्बरम् । ऐरावतविषाणाग्रैरुत्कृष्टकिणवक्षसम् ।।6.40.5।। शशलोहितरागेणसंवीतंरक्तवाससा । सन्ध्यातपेनसंवीतंमेघराशिमिवाम्बरे ।।6.40.6।।
transliteration: tasyāṃgopuraśṛṅgasthaṃrākṣasendraṃdurāsadam  śvetacāmaraparyantaṃvijayacchatraśobhitam | raktacandanasaṃliptaṃratnābharaṇabhūṣitam  nīlajīmūtasaṅkāśaṃhemasañchāditāmbaram | airāvataviṣāṇāgrairutkṛṣṭakiṇavakṣasam  śaśalohitarāgeṇasaṃvītaṃraktavāsasā | sandhyātapenasaṃvītaṃmegharāśimivāmbare
translation: तस्याम् from that, गोपुरशृङ्गस्थम् peak of the tower, दुरासदम् difficult to approach, श्वेतचामरपर्यन्तम् fanned by white whisks on both sides, विजयच्छत्रशोभितम् graced with triumphal parasol, रत्नचन्दनसंलिप्तम् decorated with red sandal paste, रक्ताभरणभूषितम् adorned in red coloured ornaments, नीलजीमूतसङ्काशम् resembling dark clouds, हेमसञ्छादिताम्बरम् attired in red embroidered with golden colour thread, विषाणाग्रैः by the indentations made by the tusks of Airavata elephant of Indra earlier, उत्कृष्टकिणवक्षसम् with scars on chest, शशलोहितरागेण colour of hare's blood, रक्तवाससा by the red coloured attire, संवीतम् सन्ध्यातपेन covered like sun shine at sun set, सञ्छन्नम् , अम्बरे sky, मेघराशिम् इव mass of clouds, राक्षसेन्द्रम् rakshasa king.
explanation: From there Rama saw on the peak of the tower the Rakshasa king, who is difficult to approach. He was fanned by white whisks on both sides, graced with triumphal parasol, decorated his body with red sandal paste, adorned in redcoloured ornaments, resembling dark clouds, attired in red like the hare's blood, embroidered with golden thread, with scars on his chest caused by indentations made by the tusks of Airavata the elephant of Indra, looked like a mass of cloud covered by sunshine at dusk.

shloka_text: तस्यांगोपुरशृङ्गस्थंराक्षसेन्द्रंदुरासदम् ।।6.40.3।। श्वेतचामरपर्यन्तंविजयच्छत्रशोभितम् । रक्तचन्दनसंलिप्तंरत्नाभरणभूषितम् ।।6.40.4।। नीलजीमूतसङ्काशंहेमसञ्छादिताम्बरम् । ऐरावतविषाणाग्रैरुत्कृष्टकिणवक्षसम् ।।6.40.5।। शशलोहितरागेणसंवीतंरक्तवाससा । सन्ध्यातपेनसंवीतंमेघराशिमिवाम्बरे ।।6.40.6।।
transliteration: tasyāṃgopuraśṛṅgasthaṃrākṣasendraṃdurāsadam  śvetacāmaraparyantaṃvijayacchatraśobhitam | raktacandanasaṃliptaṃratnābharaṇabhūṣitam  nīlajīmūtasaṅkāśaṃhemasañchāditāmbaram | airāvataviṣāṇāgrairutkṛṣṭakiṇavakṣasam  śaśalohitarāgeṇasaṃvītaṃraktavāsasā | sandhyātapenasaṃvītaṃmegharāśimivāmbare
translation: तस्याम् from that, गोपुरशृङ्गस्थम् peak of the tower, दुरासदम् difficult to approach, श्वेतचामरपर्यन्तम् fanned by white whisks on both sides, विजयच्छत्रशोभितम् graced with triumphal parasol, रत्नचन्दनसंलिप्तम् decorated with red sandal paste, रक्ताभरणभूषितम् adorned in red coloured ornaments, नीलजीमूतसङ्काशम् resembling dark clouds, हेमसञ्छादिताम्बरम् attired in red embroidered with golden colour thread, विषाणाग्रैः by the indentations made by the tusks of Airavata elephant of Indra earlier, उत्कृष्टकिणवक्षसम् with scars on chest, शशलोहितरागेण colour of hare's blood, रक्तवाससा by the red coloured attire, संवीतम् सन्ध्यातपेन covered like sun shine at sun set, सञ्छन्नम् , अम्बरे sky, मेघराशिम् इव mass of clouds, राक्षसेन्द्रम् rakshasa king.
explanation: From there Rama saw on the peak of the tower the Rakshasa king, who is difficult to approach. He was fanned by white whisks on both sides, graced with triumphal parasol, decorated his body with red sandal paste, adorned in redcoloured ornaments, resembling dark clouds, attired in red like the hare's blood, embroidered with golden thread, with scars on his chest caused by indentations made by the tusks of Airavata the elephant of Indra, looked like a mass of cloud covered by sunshine at dusk.

shloka_text: तस्यांगोपुरशृङ्गस्थंराक्षसेन्द्रंदुरासदम् ।।6.40.3।। श्वेतचामरपर्यन्तंविजयच्छत्रशोभितम् । रक्तचन्दनसंलिप्तंरत्नाभरणभूषितम् ।।6.40.4।। नीलजीमूतसङ्काशंहेमसञ्छादिताम्बरम् । ऐरावतविषाणाग्रैरुत्कृष्टकिणवक्षसम् ।।6.40.5।। शशलोहितरागेणसंवीतंरक्तवाससा । सन्ध्यातपेनसंवीतंमेघराशिमिवाम्बरे ।।6.40.6।।
transliteration: tasyāṃgopuraśṛṅgasthaṃrākṣasendraṃdurāsadam  śvetacāmaraparyantaṃvijayacchatraśobhitam | raktacandanasaṃliptaṃratnābharaṇabhūṣitam  nīlajīmūtasaṅkāśaṃhemasañchāditāmbaram | airāvataviṣāṇāgrairutkṛṣṭakiṇavakṣasam  śaśalohitarāgeṇasaṃvītaṃraktavāsasā | sandhyātapenasaṃvītaṃmegharāśimivāmbare
translation: तस्याम् from that, गोपुरशृङ्गस्थम् peak of the tower, दुरासदम् difficult to approach, श्वेतचामरपर्यन्तम् fanned by white whisks on both sides, विजयच्छत्रशोभितम् graced with triumphal parasol, रत्नचन्दनसंलिप्तम् decorated with red sandal paste, रक्ताभरणभूषितम् adorned in red coloured ornaments, नीलजीमूतसङ्काशम् resembling dark clouds, हेमसञ्छादिताम्बरम् attired in red embroidered with golden colour thread, विषाणाग्रैः by the indentations made by the tusks of Airavata elephant of Indra earlier, उत्कृष्टकिणवक्षसम् with scars on chest, शशलोहितरागेण colour of hare's blood, रक्तवाससा by the red coloured attire, संवीतम् सन्ध्यातपेन covered like sun shine at sun set, सञ्छन्नम् , अम्बरे sky, मेघराशिम् इव mass of clouds, राक्षसेन्द्रम् rakshasa king.
explanation: From there Rama saw on the peak of the tower the Rakshasa king, who is difficult to approach. He was fanned by white whisks on both sides, graced with triumphal parasol, decorated his body with red sandal paste, adorned in redcoloured ornaments, resembling dark clouds, attired in red like the hare's blood, embroidered with golden thread, with scars on his chest caused by indentations made by the tusks of Airavata the elephant of Indra, looked like a mass of cloud covered by sunshine at dusk.

shloka_text: तस्यांगोपुरशृङ्गस्थंराक्षसेन्द्रंदुरासदम् ।।6.40.3।। श्वेतचामरपर्यन्तंविजयच्छत्रशोभितम् । रक्तचन्दनसंलिप्तंरत्नाभरणभूषितम् ।।6.40.4।। नीलजीमूतसङ्काशंहेमसञ्छादिताम्बरम् । ऐरावतविषाणाग्रैरुत्कृष्टकिणवक्षसम् ।।6.40.5।। शशलोहितरागेणसंवीतंरक्तवाससा । सन्ध्यातपेनसंवीतंमेघराशिमिवाम्बरे ।।6.40.6।।
transliteration: tasyāṃgopuraśṛṅgasthaṃrākṣasendraṃdurāsadam  śvetacāmaraparyantaṃvijayacchatraśobhitam | raktacandanasaṃliptaṃratnābharaṇabhūṣitam  nīlajīmūtasaṅkāśaṃhemasañchāditāmbaram | airāvataviṣāṇāgrairutkṛṣṭakiṇavakṣasam  śaśalohitarāgeṇasaṃvītaṃraktavāsasā | sandhyātapenasaṃvītaṃmegharāśimivāmbare

explanation: From there Rama saw on the peak of the tower the Rakshasa king, who is difficult to approach. He was fanned by white whisks on both sides, graced with triumphal parasol, decorated his body with red sandal paste, adorned in redcoloured ornaments, resembling dark clouds, attired in red like the hare's blood, embroidered with golden thread, with scars on his chest caused by indentations made by the tusks of Airavata the elephant of Indra, looked like a mass of cloud covered by sunshine at dusk.

shloka_text: पश्यतांवानरेन्द्राणांराघवस्यापिपश्यतः । दर्शनाद्राक्षसेन्द्रस्यसुग्रीवस्सहसोत्थितः ।।6.40.7।।
transliteration: paśyatāṃvānarendrāṇāṃrāghavasyāpipaśyataḥ | darśanādrākṣasendrasyasugrīvassahasotthitaḥ
translation: सुग्रीवः Sugriva, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य Rakshasa king, दर्शनात् sight of looking, वानरेन्द्राणाम् by the king of Vanaras, पश्यताम् seeing, राघवस्यापि at Raghava, पश्यतः seeing, सहसा rashly, उत्थितः got up.
explanation: Looking at the sight of Raghava seeing Rakshasa king, Sugriva the king of Vanaras got up instantly rashly.

shloka_text: क्रोधवेगेनसंयुक्तस्सत्त्वेनचबलेनच । अचलाग्रादथोत्थायपुप्लुवेगोपुरस्थले ।।6.40.8।।
transliteration: krodhavegenasaṃyuktassattvenacabalenaca | acalāgrādathotthāyapupluvegopurasthale
translation: क्रोथवेगेन provoked by anger, सत्त्वेनच courageous, बलेनच and strong, संयुक्तः impetuous, अथ then, अचलाग्रात् the top of the peak, उत्थाय rose up, गोपुरस्थले peak of the tower, पुप्लुवे flew.
explanation: Provoked by anger, courageous and strong Sugriva rose up impelled by impetuosity and flew to the peak of the tower.

shloka_text: स्थित्वामुहूर्तंसम्प्रेक्ष्यनिर्भयेनान्तरात्मना । तृणीकृत्यचतद्रक्षस्सोऽब्रवीत्परुषंवचः ।।6.40.9।।
transliteration: sthitvāmuhūrtaṃsamprekṣyanirbhayenāntarātmanā | tṛṇīkṛtyacatadrakṣasso'bravītparuṣaṃvacaḥ
translation: सः he, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, स्थित्वा stood, सम्प्रेक्ष्य looking at, निर्भयेन fearlessly, अन्तरात्मना internally, तत् that, रक्षः ogre, तृणीकृत्यः treating like a straw, परुषम् harsh, वचः words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: For a moment he stood looking at the ogre fearlessly in his mind and treating him like straw spoke harsh words.

shloka_text: लोकनाथस्यरामस्यसखादासोऽस्मिराक्षस । नमयामोक्ष्यसेऽद्यत्वंपार्थिवेन्द्रस्यतेजसा ।।6.40.10।।
transliteration: lokanāthasyarāmasyasakhādāso'smirākṣasa | namayāmokṣyase'dyatvaṃpārthivendrasyatejasā
translation: राक्षस Rakshasa, लोकनाथस्य ruler of the world, रामस्य at Rama, सखा friend, दासः servant, अस्मि I am, त्वम् your, अद्य his, पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य best of kings, तेजसा power, मया by me, नमोक्ष्यसे will not leave you.
explanation: "O Rakshasa! I am a friend and servant of the king of kings, ruler of the world. By his power I will not leave you!", Sugriva said.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वासहसोत्पत्यपुप्लुवेतस्यचोपरि । आकृष्यमुकुटंचित्रंपातयित्वाऽपतद्भुवि ।।6.40.11।।
transliteration: ityuktvāsahasotpatyapupluvetasyacopari | ākṛṣyamukuṭaṃcitraṃpātayitvā'patadbhuvi
translation: इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, सहसा speedily, उत्पत्य got up, तस्य his, उपरि top, पुप्लुवे flying, चित्रम् wonderful, मुकुटम् diadem, आकृष्य held, तत् then, भुवि on the ground, पातयित्वा fell.
explanation: Having spoken thus, Sugriva got up speedily and flew to the top of the tower (here Ravana was located) held the diadem and pushed it on the ground.

shloka_text: समीक्ष्यतूर्णमायान्तमबभाषेनिशाचरः । सुग्रीवस्त्वपरोक्षम् मेहीनग्रीवोभविष्यसि ।।6.40.12।।
transliteration: samīkṣyatūrṇamāyāntamababhāṣeniśācaraḥ | sugrīvastvaparokṣam mehīnagrīvobhaviṣyasi
translation: निशाचरः night ranger, तूर्णम् quickly, आयान्तम् coming towards, तम् him, समीक्ष्य observing, बभाषे announced, त्वम् you, मे my, परोक्षम् without being seen by me, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, हीनग्रीवः without neck, भविष्यसि will make.
explanation: Observing Sugriva coming towards him, Ravana said, "When you were not seen by me you had a neck. I will make you neckless."

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वोत्थायतंक्षिप्रंबाहुभ्यामाक्षिपत्तले । कन्तुवत्तंसमुत्थायबाहुभ्यामाक्षिपद्धरि ।।6.40.13।।
transliteration: ityuktvotthāyataṃkṣipraṃbāhubhyāmākṣipattale | kantuvattaṃsamutthāyabāhubhyāmākṣipaddhari
translation: इति like that, उक्त्वा said, उत्थाय getting up, बाहुभ्याम् hand s, तम् his, क्षिप्रम् instantly, तले head, आक्षिपत् dashed, सः he, हरिः Vanara, कन्तुवत् like a ball, समुत्थाय getting up, बाहुभ्याम् with both hand s, आक्षिपत् pushed down
explanation: Telling like that that Ravana got up and threw Sugriva by his hand s to the ground. Then Sugriva getting up like a ball fallen pushed Ravana down.

shloka_text: परस्परंस्वेदविदग्धगात्रौपरस्परंशोणितदिग्धदेहौ । परस्परंलशिष्टनिरुद्धचेष्टौपरस्परंशाल्मलिकिंशुकौयधा ।।6.40.14।। मुष्टिप्रहारैश्चतलप्रहारैररत्निघातैश्चकराग्रघातैः । तौचक्रतुर्युद्धमसह्यरूपंमहाबलौराक्षसवानरेन्द्रौ ।।6.40.15।।
transliteration: parasparaṃsvedavidagdhagātrauparasparaṃśoṇitadigdhadehau | parasparaṃlaśiṣṭaniruddhaceṣṭauparasparaṃśālmalikiṃśukauyadhā  muṣṭiprahāraiścatalaprahārairaratnighātaiścakarāgraghātaiḥ | taucakraturyuddhamasahyarūpaṃmahābalaurākṣasavānarendrau
translation: परस्परम् one against the other, स्वेदद्विग्धगात्रौ sweating all over the body, परस्परम् one against the other, शोणितरक्तदेहौ bodies coloured red with blood, परस्परम् each one the other, लशिष्टनिरुद्धचेष्टौ clinging to each other bodies interlocked stood motionless, परस्परम् one another, शाल्मलिकिंशुकानिव like the red silkcotton trees, महाबलौ strong, तौ both, राक्षसवानरेन्द्रौ Rakshasa and Vanara kings, मुष्टिप्रहारैश्च fighting with their fists, तलप्रहारैः slaps with palms, अरत्निघातैःच and blows of forearms, कराग्रघातैः hurting with nails, असह्यरूपम् युद्धम् unbearable forms of war, चक्रतुः carried out.
explanation: Sugriva and Ravana, their bodies sweating all over, bodies coloured red with blood looking like red silk cotton trees, their bodies clinging together interlocked with each other stood motionless. They were fighting with their fists, palms and blows of forearms, hurting each other with nails and carrying out unbearable forms of war.

shloka_text: परस्परंस्वेदविदग्धगात्रौपरस्परंशोणितदिग्धदेहौ । परस्परंलशिष्टनिरुद्धचेष्टौपरस्परंशाल्मलिकिंशुकौयधा ।।6.40.14।। मुष्टिप्रहारैश्चतलप्रहारैररत्निघातैश्चकराग्रघातैः । तौचक्रतुर्युद्धमसह्यरूपंमहाबलौराक्षसवानरेन्द्रौ ।।6.40.15।।
transliteration: parasparaṃsvedavidagdhagātrauparasparaṃśoṇitadigdhadehau | parasparaṃlaśiṣṭaniruddhaceṣṭauparasparaṃśālmalikiṃśukauyadhā  muṣṭiprahāraiścatalaprahārairaratnighātaiścakarāgraghātaiḥ | taucakraturyuddhamasahyarūpaṃmahābalaurākṣasavānarendrau
translation: परस्परम् one against the other, स्वेदद्विग्धगात्रौ sweating all over the body, परस्परम् one against the other, शोणितरक्तदेहौ bodies coloured red with blood, परस्परम् each one the other, लशिष्टनिरुद्धचेष्टौ clinging to each other bodies interlocked stood motionless, परस्परम् one another, शाल्मलिकिंशुकानिव like the red silkcotton trees, महाबलौ strong, तौ both, राक्षसवानरेन्द्रौ Rakshasa and Vanara kings, मुष्टिप्रहारैश्च fighting with their fists, तलप्रहारैः slaps with palms, अरत्निघातैःच and blows of forearms, कराग्रघातैः hurting with nails, असह्यरूपम् युद्धम् unbearable forms of war, चक्रतुः carried out.
explanation: Sugriva and Ravana, their bodies sweating all over, bodies coloured red with blood looking like red silk cotton trees, their bodies clinging together interlocked with each other stood motionless. They were fighting with their fists, palms and blows of forearms, hurting each other with nails and carrying out unbearable forms of war.

shloka_text: कृत्वानियुद्धंभृशमुग्रवेगौकालंचिर, गोपुरवेदिमध्ये । उत्क्षिप्यचोत्क्षिप्यविनम्यदेहौपादक्रमाद्गोपुरवेदिलग्नौ ।।6.40.16।।
transliteration: kṛtvāniyuddhaṃbhṛśamugravegaukālaṃcira, gopuravedimadhye | utkṣipyacotkṣipyavinamyadehaupādakramādgopuravedilagnau
translation: भृशम् violently, उग्रवेग्रौ with aggressive terrible combat, चिरंकालम् for long, गोपुरवेदिमध्ये in the middle of the flat portion of the tower, नियुद्धम् , कृत्वा having done, देहौ body, उत्क्षिप्यउत्क्षिप्य throwing each other repeatedly, विनम्य bending, पादक्रमात् by moving their feet in a direction, गोपुरवेदिलग्नौ stood on the tower.
explanation: Violently fighting like that aggressively for long, throwing each other down repeatedly, bending and moving their feet in a direction, stood on the fl at area of the peak in the middle portion.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यमाविध्यवेदिलग्नौतौपेततुस्सालनिखातमध्ये । उत्पेततुर्भूतलमस्पृशन्तौस्थित्वामुहूर्तंत्वभिनिश्श्वसन्तौ ।।6.40.17।।
transliteration: anyonyamāvidhyavedilagnautaupetatussālanikhātamadhye | utpetaturbhūtalamaspṛśantausthitvāmuhūrtaṃtvabhiniśśvasantau
translation: तौ both, अन्योन्यम् one another, विध्य squeezed, वेदिलग्नौ defensive walls, सालनिखातमध्ये between the boundary and the moat, निपेततुः dropped down, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, अभिनिःश्वसन्तौ gasping heavily, स्थित्वा remaining, स्पृशन्तौ clinging their bodies, भूमितलम् on the ground, उत्पेततुः jumping.
explanation: Squeezing their bodies of each other they dropped down between the boundary of the peak and the moat. They were gasping heavily for a moment and clung their body to each other jumping.

shloka_text: आलिङ् ग्यचालिङ् ग्यचबाहुयोक्स्रैस्संयोजयामासतुराहवेतौ । सम्रम्भशिक्षाबलसम्प्रयुक्तौसंचेरतुस्सम्प्रतियुद्धमार्गैः ।।6.40.18।।
transliteration: āliṅ gyacāliṅ gyacabāhuyoksraissaṃyojayāmāsaturāhavetau | samrambhaśikṣābalasamprayuktausaṃceratussampratiyuddhamārgaiḥ
translation: तौ they, बाहुयोक्स्रै pressing their bosoms, आलिङ् ग्यच clung to each other, आलिङ् ग्यच and fastened to each other in embrace, आहवे in combat, संयोजयामासतुः having received similar training, सम्रम्भशिक्षाबलसम्प्रयुक्तौ endowed with might, सम्प्रति at this time, युद्धमार्गैः war methods, सुचेरतुः went on.
explanation: Both pressing their bosom to each other, clung to each other, and fastened themselves in embrace in the comb at having received similar training in war and both endowed with might. At this time, they went on in comb at using several war methods.

shloka_text: शार्दूरसिंहाविवजातदर्पौगजेन्द्रपोताविवसम्प्रयुक्तौ । संहत्यचापीड्यचतावुरोभ्यांनिपेततुर्वैयुगपद्धरण्याम् ।।6.40.19।।
transliteration: śārdūrasiṃhāvivajātadarpaugajendrapotāvivasamprayuktau | saṃhatyacāpīḍyacatāvurobhyāṃnipetaturvaiyugapaddharaṇyām
translation: तौ both, जातदर्पौ affected by pride, शार्दूलसिंहानिव l who resembled tiger and lion, सम्प्रयुक्तौ connecting to each other, गजेन्द्रपोताविव like Lordly elephants, तावुरोभ्याम् through their shoulders, चापीड्य hitting, संवेद्यच and hurting each other, युगपत् simultaneously at once, धरायाम् holding one another, पेततुःवै fell on the ground.
explanation: Both of them resembled a tiger and lion affected by pride, connecting to each other through their shoulders like Lordly elephants, hitting and hurting one another holding one another fell down at once simultaneously.

shloka_text: उद्यम्यचान्योन्यमधिक्षिपन्तौसञ्चक्रमातेबहुयुद्धमार्गे: । व्यायामशिक्षाबलसम्प्रयुक्तौक्लमंनतौजग्मतुराशुवीरौ ।।6.40.20।।
transliteration: udyamyacānyonyamadhikṣipantausañcakramātebahuyuddhamārge: | vyāyāmaśikṣābalasamprayuktauklamaṃnataujagmaturāśuvīrau
translation: अन्योन्यम् one another, उद्यम्य holding, अधिक्षिपन्तौ snubbing each other, युद्धमार्गै: kinds of war, बहु many, सञ्चक्रमाते gradually, व्यायामशिक्षाबलसम्प्रयुक्तौ well trained in wrestling and fighting, तौ both of them, वीरौ heroes, क्लमम् tiresomeness, नजग्मतुः not felt.
explanation: Both of them were holding one another, snubbing each other gradually following many kinds of combat. As both the heroes were well trained in wrestling and fighting, they did not feel tiresome.

shloka_text: बाहूत्तमैर्वारणवारणाभैर्निवारयन्तौवरवारणाभौ । चिरेणकालेनतुसम्प्रयुक्तौसञ्चेरतुर्मण्डलमार्गमाशु ।।6.40.21।।
transliteration: bāhūttamairvāraṇavāraṇābhairnivārayantauvaravāraṇābhau | cireṇakālenatusamprayuktausañceraturmaṇḍalamārgamāśu
translation: र्वारणवारणाभै Sugriva and Ravana both, वारणवारणाभैः resisting each other, बाहूत्तमैः endowed with mighty arms, निवारयन्तौ keeping away each other, चिरेणकालेन for long time, तु, सम्प्रयुक्तौ engaged in combat, आशु swiftly, मण्डलमार्गम् going round and round, संचेरतुः remained moving.
explanation: Both Ravana and Sugriva endowed with mighty arms, were resisting each other, and keeping away one another engaging in comb at for a long time. They kept on moving, going around each other swiftly.

shloka_text: तौपरस्परमासाद्ययत्तावन्योन्यसूदने । मार्जाराविवभक्ष्यार्थेऽवितस्थातेमुहुर्मुहुः ।।6.40.22।।
transliteration: tauparasparamāsādyayattāvanyonyasūdane | mārjārāvivabhakṣyārthe'vitasthātemuhurmuhuḥ
translation: अन्योन्यसूदने intending to destroy each other, यत्तौ approaching each other, तौ both, परस्परम् one another, आसाद्य to kill, भक्ष्यार्थे for the sake of food, मार्जाराविव like cats, मुहुर्मुहुः again and again, अवितस्थाते falsely.
explanation: Both of them intent on destroying each other were approaching one another and now and then growling like cats for the sake of food.

shloka_text: मण्डलानिविचित्राणिस्थानानिविविधानिच । मूत्रकाणिचित्राणिगतप्रत्यागतानिच ।।6.40.23।। तिरच्शीनगतान्येवतथावक्रगतानिच । परिमोक्षंप्रहाराणांवर्जनंपरिधावनम् ।।6.40.24।। अभिद्रवणमाप्लावमावस्थानंसविग्रहम् । परावृत्तमपावृत्तमपद्रुतमवप्लुतम् ।।6.40.25।। उपन्यस्तपमन्यस्तंयुद्धमार्गविशारदौ । तौसञ्चेचेरतुरन्योन्यंवानरेन्द्रश्चरावणः ।।6.40.26।।
transliteration: maṇḍalānivicitrāṇisthānānivividhānica | mūtrakāṇicitrāṇigatapratyāgatānica  tiracśīnagatānyevatathāvakragatānica | parimokṣaṃprahārāṇāṃvarjanaṃparidhāvanam  abhidravaṇamāplāvamāvasthānaṃsavigraham | parāvṛttamapāvṛttamapadrutamavaplutam  upanyastapamanyastaṃyuddhamārgaviśāradau | tausañceceraturanyonyaṃvānarendraścarāvaṇaḥ
translation: युद्धमार्गविशारदौ learned in war craft, तौ both, वानरेन्द्रश्च Vanara king's, रावणः Ravana, विचित्राणि wonderful, मण्डलानि circles, विविधानि many, स्थानानि postures, चित्राणि wonderful, गोमूत्रकाणि ox's urine, गतप्रत्यागतानिच forward and backward movements, तिरच्शीनगतान्येव horizontal and oblique movement, तथा similarly, वक्रगतानिच roundabout and evasive movements, प्रहाराणाम् hitting, परिमोक्षम् delivering, वर्जनम् abandoning, परिधावनम् striking, अभिद्रवणम् assaulting, आप्लावम् jumping, सविग्रहम् motionless, अवस्थानम् standing steadily, परावृत्तम् , अपावृत्तम् going away circling round, अपद्रुतम् going backwards, अवप्लुतम् jumping behind, उपन्यस्तम् holding the hand, अपन्यस्तम् folding the hand, सञ्चेरतुः exhibiting.
explanation: Both Vanara king and Ravana being learned in war craft, went around in circles like ox's urine, stood in different wonderful postures, moved forward and backward horizontally and obliquely to evade movements, hitting, and delivering each other, standing steadily motionless, striking, jumping, assaulting each other coming forward and going away, going backwards jumping from behind, holding hands and folding to resist exhibiting their skill in combat.

translation: युद्धमार्गविशारदौ learned in war craft, तौ both, वानरेन्द्रश्च Vanara king's, रावणः Ravana, विचित्राणि wonderful, मण्डलानि circles, विविधानि many, स्थानानि postures, चित्राणि wonderful, गोमूत्रकाणि ox's urine, गतप्रत्यागतानिच forward and backward movements, तिरच्शीनगतान्येव horizontal and oblique movement, तथा similarly, वक्रगतानिच roundabout and evasive movements, प्रहाराणाम् hitting, परिमोक्षम् delivering, वर्जनम् abandoning, परिधावनम् striking, अभिद्रवणम् assaulting, आप्लावम् jumping, सविग्रहम् motionless, अवस्थानम् standing steadily, परावृत्तम् , अपावृत्तम् going away circling round, अपद्रुतम् going backwards, अवप्लुतम् jumping behind, उपन्यस्तम् holding the hand, अपन्यस्तम् folding the hand, सञ्चेरतुः exhibiting.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेरक्षोमायाबलमथात्मनः । आरब्धुमुपसंपेदेज्ञात्वातंवानराधिपः ।।6.40.27।। उत्पपाततदाकाशंजितकाशीजितक्लमः । रावणःस्थितएवात्रहरिराजेववञ्चितः ।।6.40.28।।
transliteration: etasminnantarerakṣomāyābalamathātmanaḥ | ārabdhumupasaṃpedejñātvātaṃvānarādhipaḥ  utpapātatadākāśaṃjitakāśījitaklamaḥ | rāvaṇaḥsthitaevātraharirājevavañcitaḥ
translation: अथ then, एतस्मिन् in the, अन्तरे meantime, रक्षः Rakshasa, आत्मनः in himself, मायाबलम् jugglery, आरब्दुम् exhibit, उपसंपेदे superior, वानराधिपः Vanara leader, तम् , ज्ञात्वा knowing, जितकाशी assuming the air of victor, जितक्लमः one who is untiring, तदा then, आकाशम् sky, उत्पपात rose up, हरिराजेन Vanara king's, वञ्चितः baffled, रावणः Ravana, अत्रैव there, स्थितः stood
explanation: In the meantime, Ravana thought of exhibiting his superiority by jugglery and jumped to the sky. Knowing that Sugriva, the untiring Vanara king assumed the air of victor and rose up to the sky. Baffled Ravana stood thinking Sugriva would come there.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेरक्षोमायाबलमथात्मनः । आरब्धुमुपसंपेदेज्ञात्वातंवानराधिपः ।।6.40.27।। उत्पपाततदाकाशंजितकाशीजितक्लमः । रावणःस्थितएवात्रहरिराजेववञ्चितः ।।6.40.28।।
transliteration: etasminnantarerakṣomāyābalamathātmanaḥ | ārabdhumupasaṃpedejñātvātaṃvānarādhipaḥ  utpapātatadākāśaṃjitakāśījitaklamaḥ | rāvaṇaḥsthitaevātraharirājevavañcitaḥ
translation: अथ then, एतस्मिन् in the, अन्तरे meantime, रक्षः Rakshasa, आत्मनः in himself, मायाबलम् jugglery, आरब्दुम् exhibit, उपसंपेदे superior, वानराधिपः Vanara leader, तम् , ज्ञात्वा knowing, जितकाशी assuming the air of victor, जितक्लमः one who is untiring, तदा then, आकाशम् sky, उत्पपात rose up, हरिराजेन Vanara king's, वञ्चितः baffled, रावणः Ravana, अत्रैव there, स्थितः stood
explanation: In the meantime, Ravana thought of exhibiting his superiority by jugglery and jumped to the sky. Knowing that Sugriva, the untiring Vanara king assumed the air of victor and rose up to the sky. Baffled Ravana stood thinking Sugriva would come there.

shloka_text: अथहरिवरनाथःप्राप्यसङ्ग्रामकीर्तिंनिशिचरपतिमाजौयोजयित्वाश्रमेण । गगनमतिविशालंलङ्घयित्वार्कसूनुर्हरिगणमध्येरामपार्श्वंजगाम ।।6.40.29।।
transliteration: athaharivaranāthaḥprāpyasaṅgrāmakīrtiṃniśicarapatimājauyojayitvāśrameṇa | gaganamativiśālaṃlaṅghayitvārkasūnurharigaṇamadhyerāmapārśvaṃjagāma
translation: अथ and then, हरिनरनाथः Lord of Vanara chiefs, अर्कसूनुः son of Sun god, प्राप्यसङ्ग्रामकीर्तिः who had won fame in winning battles, आजौ victorious, निशिचरपतिम् Lord of night rangers, श्रमेण exhausting, योजयित्वा travelling, अतिविशालम् extensive, गगनम् sky, लङ्घयित्वा flying, हरिगणबलमध्ये in the midst of Vanara army, रामपार्श्वम् side of Rama, जगाम reached.
explanation: Then Sugriva, the Sun god's son, the Lord of Vanara chiefs, who had won fame of winning in battles, victorious exhausting Ravana in comb at flying the extensive sky reached Rama who was amid Vanara army.

shloka_text: इतिससवितृसूनुस्तत्रतत्कर्मकृत्वापवनगतिरनीकंप्राविशत्ससम्प्रहृष्टः । रघुवरनृपसूनोद्वर्धयन्युद्धहर्षंतरुमृगगणमुख्यैःपूज्यमानोहरीन्द्रः ।।6.40.30।।
transliteration: itisasavitṛsūnustatratatkarmakṛtvāpavanagatiranīkaṃprāviśatsasamprahṛṣṭaḥ | raghuvaranṛpasūnodvardhayanyuddhaharṣaṃtarumṛgagaṇamukhyaiḥpūjyamānoharīndraḥ
translation: सवितृसूनुः son of Sun god, सः that Sugriva, तत्र there, तत् कर्म that feat, कृत्वा having done, रघुवरनृपसूनोः foremost of the Raghu's, युद्धहर्षम् the joy of combat, वर्धयन् increasing, तरुमृगगणमुख्यैः adored by the foremost monkey chiefs, पूज्यमानः adored, सम्प्रहृष्टः rejoiced, पवनगतिः wind speed, अनीकम् now, प्राविशत् entered.
explanation: Sugriva the son of the Sun god, having completed the feat, rejoiced by increasing the joy of foremost of Raghus. Then he who is adored by the monkey chiefs entered the army of Vanaras. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the fortieth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथतस्मिन्निमित्तानिदृष्टवालक्ष्मणपूर्वजः । सुग्रीवंसम्परिष्वज्यतथावचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.41.1।।
transliteration: athatasminnimittānidṛṣṭavālakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ | sugrīvaṃsampariṣvajyatathāvacanamabravīt
translation: अथ and then, लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः Lakshmana's brother, तथा likewise, तस्मिन् for his, निमित्तानि signs, दृष्टवा seeing, सुग्रीवम् in Sugriva, संपरिष्वज्य embraced, वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Rama, brother of Lakshmana, seeing the signs of war, embraced Sugriva and spoke these words.
comments: Sri Rama warns Sugriva against such action being a king and commands Vanara army generals to besiege all the four gates of Lanka. Angada is sent to Ravana to communicate Rama's message that unless Ravana returns Sita back to Rama, he will be killed and Vibheeshana will be made the king of Lanka.

shloka_text: असन्त्ऱ्यमयासार्थंतदिदंसाहसंकृतम् । एवंसाहसुक्तानिनकुर्वन्तिजनेश्वराः ।।6.41.2।।
transliteration: asantṟyamayāsārthaṃtadidaṃsāhasaṃkṛtam | evaṃsāhasuktāninakurvantijaneśvarāḥ
translation: मयासार्थम् with me, असन्त्ऱ्य consulting, तत् that, इदम् thus, साहसम् boldly, कृतम् done, जनेश्वराः rulers, एवम् in this way, साहसयुक्तानि courageous actions, नकुर्वन्ति do not do.
explanation: "You have done this courageous feat without consulting me. Rulers do not do such actions."

shloka_text: संशयेस्थाप्यमांचेदंबलंचसविभीषणम् । कष्टंकृतमिदंवीर साहसंसाहसप्रिय ।।6.41.3।।
transliteration: saṃśayesthāpyamāṃcedaṃbalaṃcasavibhīṣaṇam | kaṣṭaṃkṛtamidaṃvīra sāhasaṃsāhasapriya
translation: साहसप्रिय one who is fond of daring action, वीर hero, मांच for me, इदम् this, बलंच army also, सविभीषणंच and also Vibheeshana, संशये doubt, स्थाप्य created, कष्टम् difficult, इदम् this, साहसम् bold action, कृतम् performed by you.
explanation: "O hero, who is fond of daring actions! To me, to the army and Vibheeshana you created a great doubt by this bold action of yours."

shloka_text: इदानींमाकृथावीर एवंविधमचिन्तितम् । त्वयिकिञ्चित्समापन्नेकिंकार्यंसीतयामम ।।6.41.4।। भरतेनमहाबाहो लक्ष्मणेनयवीयसा । शत्रुघ्नेनचशत्रुघ्नस्वशरीरेणवापुन:।। 6.41.5।।
transliteration: idānīṃmākṛthāvīra evaṃvidhamacintitam | tvayikiñcitsamāpannekiṃkāryaṃsītayāmama  bharatenamahābāho lakṣmaṇenayavīyasā | śatrughnenacaśatrughnasvaśarīreṇavāpuna:
translation: अरिन्दम tamer of foes, वीर hero, इदानीम् here after, एवंविधम् this kind of, माकृथाः not do, महाबाहो broad shouldered, शत्रुघ्न destroyer of foes, त्वयि your, किञ्चित् even a little, समापन्ने harm, मम my, सीतया Sita, भरतेन also Bharata, यवीयसा, लक्ष्मणेन even Lakshmana, शत्रुघ्नेन and Satrughna also, स्वशरीरेणवा my own body पुनः again, किंकार्यम् What is the use?
explanation: "O broad shouldered hero, tamer of foes! Do not do this kind of action. Even if you were harmed a bit, O destroyer of foes, of what use is it to me or even to Sita, Bharata, Satrughna or to Lakshmana or even to my body?"

shloka_text: इदानींमाकृथावीर एवंविधमचिन्तितम् । त्वयिकिञ्चित्समापन्नेकिंकार्यंसीतयामम ।।6.41.4।। भरतेनमहाबाहो लक्ष्मणेनयवीयसा । शत्रुघ्नेनचशत्रुघ्नस्वशरीरेणवापुन:।। 6.41.5।।
transliteration: idānīṃmākṛthāvīra evaṃvidhamacintitam | tvayikiñcitsamāpannekiṃkāryaṃsītayāmama  bharatenamahābāho lakṣmaṇenayavīyasā | śatrughnenacaśatrughnasvaśarīreṇavāpuna:
translation: अरिन्दम tamer of foes, वीर hero, इदानीम् here after, एवंविधम् this kind of, माकृथाः not do, महाबाहो broad shouldered, शत्रुघ्न destroyer of foes, त्वयि your, किञ्चित् even a little, समापन्ने harm, मम my, सीतया Sita, भरतेन also Bharata, यवीयसा, लक्ष्मणेन even Lakshmana, शत्रुघ्नेन and Satrughna also, स्वशरीरेणवा my own body पुनः again, किंकार्यम् What is the use?
explanation: "O broad shouldered hero, tamer of foes! Do not do this kind of action. Even if you were harmed a bit, O destroyer of foes, of what use is it to me or even to Sita, Bharata, Satrughna or to Lakshmana or even to my body?"

shloka_text: त्वयिचानागतेपूर्वमितिमेनिश्चितामतिः । जानतश्चापितेवीर्यंमहेन्द्रवरुणोसम ।।6.41.6।। हत्वाऽहंरावणंयुद्धेसपुत्रबलवाहनम् । अभिषिच्यचलङ्कायांविभीषणमथापिच ।।6.41.7।। भरतेराज्यमावेश्यत्यक्ष्येदेहंमहाबल ।
transliteration: tvayicānāgatepūrvamitimeniścitāmatiḥ | jānataścāpitevīryaṃmahendravaruṇosama  hatvā'haṃrāvaṇaṃyuddhesaputrabalavāhanam | abhiṣicyacalaṅkāyāṃvibhīṣaṇamathāpica  bharaterājyamāveśyatyakṣyedehaṃmahābala |
translation: महेन्द्रवरुणोसम resembling Indra and Varuna, महाबल mighty, त्वयि your, अनागते before arrival, ते your, वीर्यम् valour, जानतश्चापि even though known, मे to me, मतिः mind, पूर्वम् earlier, निश्चिता decided, अहम् I, युद्धे in battle, सपुत्रबलवाहनम् sons and relatives, रावणम् of Ravana, हत्वा killing, विभीषणम् to Vibheeshana, लङ्कायाम् Lanka, अभिषिच्य coronate, अथापिच myself, भरते to Bharata, राज्यम् kingdom, आरोप्य handing over, देहम् body, त्यक्ष्ये give up.
explanation: "Mighty Sugriva! You resemble Indra and Varuna in might. Your valour is known to me. I have decided in my mind to kill the sons of Ravana and his relatives in battle, coronate Vibheeshana in Lanka, and hand over the kingdom to Bharata and give up my body."

shloka_text: त्वयिचानागतेपूर्वमितिमेनिश्चितामतिः । जानतश्चापितेवीर्यंमहेन्द्रवरुणोसम ।।6.41.6।। हत्वाऽहंरावणंयुद्धेसपुत्रबलवाहनम् । अभिषिच्यचलङ्कायांविभीषणमथापिच ।।6.41.7।। भरतेराज्यमावेश्यत्यक्ष्येदेहंमहाबल ।
transliteration: tvayicānāgatepūrvamitimeniścitāmatiḥ | jānataścāpitevīryaṃmahendravaruṇosama  hatvā'haṃrāvaṇaṃyuddhesaputrabalavāhanam | abhiṣicyacalaṅkāyāṃvibhīṣaṇamathāpica  bharaterājyamāveśyatyakṣyedehaṃmahābala |
translation: महेन्द्रवरुणोसम resembling Indra and Varuna, महाबल mighty, त्वयि your, अनागते before arrival, ते your, वीर्यम् valour, जानतश्चापि even though known, मे to me, मतिः mind, पूर्वम् earlier, निश्चिता decided, अहम् I, युद्धे in battle, सपुत्रबलवाहनम् sons and relatives, रावणम् of Ravana, हत्वा killing, विभीषणम् to Vibheeshana, लङ्कायाम् Lanka, अभिषिच्य coronate, अथापिच myself, भरते to Bharata, राज्यम् kingdom, आरोप्य handing over, देहम् body, त्यक्ष्ये give up.
explanation: "Mighty Sugriva! You resemble Indra and Varuna in might. Your valour is known to me. I have decided in my mind to kill the sons of Ravana and his relatives in battle, coronate Vibheeshana in Lanka, and hand over the kingdom to Bharata and give up my body."

shloka_text: तमेवंवादिनंरामंसुग्रीवःप्रत्यभाषत ।।6.41.8।। तवभार्यापहर्तारंदृष्टवाराघव रावणम् । मर्षयामिकथंवीरजानपौरुषमात्मनः ।।6.41.9।।
transliteration: tamevaṃvādinaṃrāmaṃsugrīvaḥpratyabhāṣata  tavabhāryāpahartāraṃdṛṣṭavārāghava rāvaṇam | marṣayāmikathaṃvīrajānapauruṣamātmanaḥ
translation: एवंवादिनम् told in that manner, तम् by, रामम् Rama, सुग्रीवः to Sugriva, प्रत्यभाषत replied, वीर hero, राघव Raghava, तव your, भार्यापहर्तारम् borne away your consort, रावणम् Ravana, दृष्टवा seeing, आत्मनः I myself, बलम् strength, जानन् knowing, कथम् how can, मर्षयामि tolerate.
explanation: To Rama who was speaking in that manner, Sugriva replied, "Heroic Rama! Seeing that Ravana, who has borne away your consort, and knowing my own strength, how can I tolerate?"

shloka_text: तमेवंवादिनंरामंसुग्रीवःप्रत्यभाषत ।।6.41.8।। तवभार्यापहर्तारंदृष्टवाराघव रावणम् । मर्षयामिकथंवीरजानपौरुषमात्मनः ।।6.41.9।।
transliteration: tamevaṃvādinaṃrāmaṃsugrīvaḥpratyabhāṣata  tavabhāryāpahartāraṃdṛṣṭavārāghava rāvaṇam | marṣayāmikathaṃvīrajānapauruṣamātmanaḥ
translation: एवंवादिनम् told in that manner, तम् by, रामम् Rama, सुग्रीवः to Sugriva, प्रत्यभाषत replied, वीर hero, राघव Raghava, तव your, भार्यापहर्तारम् borne away your consort, रावणम् Ravana, दृष्टवा seeing, आत्मनः I myself, बलम् strength, जानन् knowing, कथम् how can, मर्षयामि tolerate.
explanation: To Rama who was speaking in that manner, Sugriva replied, "Heroic Rama! Seeing that Ravana, who has borne away your consort, and knowing my own strength, how can I tolerate?"

shloka_text: इत्येवंवादिनंवीरमभिनन्द्यचराघवः । लक्ष्मणंलक्षीसम्पन्नमिदंवचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.41.10।।
transliteration: ityevaṃvādinaṃvīramabhinandyacarāghavaḥ | lakṣmaṇaṃlakṣīsampannamidaṃvacanamabravīt
translation: राघवः Raghava, इत्येवंवादिनम् thus spoken, वीरम् hero, अभिनन्द्य applauding, लक्ष्मिसम्पन्नम् endowed with prosperity, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, इदम् these, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Raghava heard the hero Sugriva, applauding him and spoke these words to Lakshmana, who was endowed with prosperity.

shloka_text: परिगृह्योदकंशीतंवनानिफलवन्तिच । बलौघंसंविभज्येमंव्यूह्यतिष्ठेमलक्ष्मण ।।6.41.11।।
transliteration: parigṛhyodakaṃśītaṃvanāniphalavantica | balaughaṃsaṃvibhajyemaṃvyūhyatiṣṭhemalakṣmaṇa
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, शीतम् cool, उदकम् water, फलवन्ति good fruits, वनानिच woods, परिगृह्य occupying, इमम् this, बलौघम् army, संविभज्य divide, व्यूह्य plan, तिष्ठाम be ready.
explanation: "Lakshmana! We should occupy a region with cool water and good fruits and plan to divide the army and be ready."

shloka_text: लोकक्षयकरंभीमंभयंपश्याम्युपस्थितम् । निबर्हणंप्रवीराणामृक्षवानररक्षसाम् ।।6.41.12।।
transliteration: lokakṣayakaraṃbhīmaṃbhayaṃpaśyāmyupasthitam | nibarhaṇaṃpravīrāṇāmṛkṣavānararakṣasām
translation: लोकक्षयकरम् that which bodes destruction of the world, भीमम् terrific, प्रवीराणाम् eminent heroes, ऋक्षवानररक्षसाम् to Bears, monkeys and Rakshasas, निबर्हणम् danger, भयम् fear, उपस्थितम् approaching, पश्यामि see.
explanation: "I foresee the terrific destruction of eminent heroes among Bears, monkeys and Rakshasas. I see the danger approaching."

shloka_text: वाताश्चहिपरुषांवान्तिकम्पतेचवसुन्धरा । पर्वताग्राणिवेपन्तेपतन्तिधरणीधराः ।।6.41.13।।
transliteration: vātāścahiparuṣāṃvāntikampatecavasundharā | parvatāgrāṇivepantepatantidharaṇīdharāḥ
translation: वाताः winds, परुषम् severely, वान्ति blowing, वसुन्धराच in the earth, कम्पते quacking, पर्वताग्राणि mountain peaks, वेपन्ते shaking, धरणीधराः those elephants bearing the earth, पतन्ति falling.
explanation: "The winds are blowing severely, the earth is quaking in, the mountain peaks are shaking, and the elephants bearing the earth (in the four corners) are falling."

shloka_text: मेघाःक्रवादसङ्काशाःपरुषाःपरुषस्वनाः । क्रूराःक्रूरंप्रवर्षन्तिमिश्रंशोणितबिन्दुभिः ।।6.41.14।।
transliteration: meghāḥkravādasaṅkāśāḥparuṣāḥparuṣasvanāḥ | krūrāḥkrūraṃpravarṣantimiśraṃśoṇitabindubhiḥ
translation: क्रनादसङ्काशाः like wild birds, परुषाः harsh, परुषस्वनाः producing harsh sounds, क्रूराः fierce, मेघाः clouds, क्रूरम् terrific, शोणितबिन्धुभिः blood drops, मिश्रम् mixed with, प्रवर्षन्ति raining
explanation: "The fierce clouds resembling wild birds are making terrible harsh sounds and rain mixed with drops of blood is showering."

shloka_text: रक्तचन्दनसङ्काशासन्ध्यापरमदारुणा । ज्वलच्चनिपतत्येतदादित्यादग्निमण्डलम् ।।6.41.15।।
transliteration: raktacandanasaṅkāśāsandhyāparamadāruṇā | jvalaccanipatatyetadādityādagnimaṇḍalam
translation: रक्तचन्दनसङ्काशा resembling red sanders, सन्ध्या twilight, परमदारुणा very frightening, आदित्यात् from Sun, ज्वलत् fire, एतत् all this, अग्निमण्डलम् like mass of fire, विपतति falling down.
explanation: "The twilight appears like red sander trees, the burning fire falling from the sun is like a mass of fire and frightening."

shloka_text: आदित्यमभिवाश्यन्तिजनयन्तोमहद्भयम् । दीनादीनस्वराःघोरानप्रशस्तामृगद्विजाः ।।6.41.16।।
transliteration: ādityamabhivāśyantijanayantomahadbhayam | dīnādīnasvarāḥghorānapraśastāmṛgadvijāḥ
translation: दीनाः desperate, दीनस्वराः crying pitifully, घोराः dreadful, नप्रशस्ताः inauspicious, मृगद्विजाः ominous beasts, महत् great, भयम् fear, जनयन्तः creating, आदित्यम् from Sun, अभिवाश्यन्ति facing the Sun.
explanation: "The desperate inauspicious sounds of ominous beasts crying pitifully facing the sun are causing great fear."

shloka_text: रजन्यामप्रकाशश्चसन्तापयतिचन्द्रमाः । कृष्णरक्तांशुपर्यन्तोयथालोकस्यसंक्ष्ये ।।6.41.17।।
transliteration: rajanyāmaprakāśaścasantāpayaticandramāḥ | kṛṣṇaraktāṃśuparyantoyathālokasyasaṃkṣye
translation: लोकस्य of the universe, संक्ष्येयथा like the dissolution, कृष्णरक्तांशुपर्यन्तः surrounded with black and red halo, अप्रकाशः not radiant, चन्द्रमाः the moon, रजन्याम् in the night, सन्तापयति tormented.
explanation: "Like at the time of universal dissolution, the moon is not radiant, being surrounded by black and red halo at night and is tormenting."

shloka_text: ह्रस्वोरूक्षोऽप्रशस्तश्चपरिवेषस्सुलोहितः । आदित्यमण्डलेनीलंलक्ष्मलक्ष्मण दृश्यते ।।6.41.18।।
transliteration: hrasvorūkṣo'praśastaścapariveṣassulohitaḥ | ādityamaṇḍalenīlaṃlakṣmalakṣmaṇa dṛśyate
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, आदित्यमण्डले Sun 's orbit, ह्रस्वः shortened, रूक्षः dreary, अप्रशस्तः inauspicious, सुलोहितः copper coloured, परिवेषः surrounding, नीलम् dark, लक्ष्म seen, लक्षयते observable.
explanation: "Lakshmana! Short dark spot observed in the Sun 's orbit is inauspicious. moon is surrounded by copper colour and dreary."

shloka_text: दृश्यन्तेनयथावच्छनक्षत्राण्यभिवर्तते । युगान्तमिवलोकस्यपश्यलक्ष्मण शंसति ।।6.41.19।।
transliteration: dṛśyantenayathāvacchanakṣatrāṇyabhivartate | yugāntamivalokasyapaśyalakṣmaṇa śaṃsati
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, नक्षत्राणि even stars, यथावत् so also, नदृश्यन्ते not visible, लोकस्य in the universe, युगान्तम् end of the universe, शंसतीव spots on the moon, अभिवर्तते dirty, पश्य seen.
explanation: "Just as the spots on the moon, the stars are also dirty and not visible. It forebodes the end of the universe Lakshmana!"

shloka_text: काकाश्येनास्तथागृध्रानीचैःपरिपतन्तिच । शिवाश्चाप्यशिवावाचःप्रवदन्तिमहास्वनाः ।।6.41.20।।
transliteration: kākāśyenāstathāgṛdhrānīcaiḥparipatantica | śivāścāpyaśivāvācaḥpravadantimahāsvanāḥ
translation: काकाः crows, श्येनाः hawks, तथा so also, गृध्राः vultures, नीचैः lowly, परिपतन्तिच joining, महास्वनाः in loud tone, शिवाश्च jackals, अशिवाश्च inauspicious, अशुभाः not good, वाचः sounds, प्रवदन्ति making.
explanation: "The crows, hawks and also vultures are joining lowly animals like jackals and making loud noises which is inauspicious and not good."

shloka_text: क्षिप्रमद्यदुराधर्षांलङ्कांरावणपालिताम् । अभियामजवेनैवसर्वतोहरिभिर्वृताः ।।6.41.21।।
transliteration: kṣipramadyadurādharṣāṃlaṅkāṃrāvaṇapālitām | abhiyāmajavenaivasarvatoharibhirvṛtāḥ
translation: हरिभिः Vanaras, वृताः accompanied by, अद्य now, क्षिप्रम् immediately, दुराधर्षम् difficult to attack, रावणपालिताम् ruled by Ravana, लङ्काम् Lanka, सर्वतः all, जवेनैव with good speed, अभियाम march forward.
explanation: Surrounded on all sides by the vanaras, let us now march swiftly upon the impregnable Lanka ruled by Ravana.

shloka_text: शैलैःशूलैश्चखडगैश्चविमुक्स्सैःकपिराक्षसैः । भविष्यत्यावृताभूमिर्मांसशोणितकर्दमा ।।6.41.22।।
transliteration: śailaiḥśūlaiścakhaḍagaiścavimukssaiḥkapirākṣasaiḥ | bhaviṣyatyāvṛtābhūmirmāṃsaśoṇitakardamā
translation: कपिराक्षसैः by Vanaras and Rakshasas, विमुक्स्सैः hurled, शैलैः rocks, शूलैश्च tridents, खडगैश्च swords, भूमिः the earth, आवृता covered, मांसशोणितकर्दमा with flesh and blood, भविष्यति will remain.
explanation: "The land will remain covered by rocks, tridents, swords hurled by the Vanaras and Rakshasas and with flesh and blood."

shloka_text: इत्येवंतुवदवनीर्वोलक्ष्मणंलक्ष्मणाग्रजः । तस्मादवातरच्छीघ्रंपर्वताग्रान्महाबलः ।।6.41.23।।
transliteration: ityevaṃtuvadavanīrvolakṣmaṇaṃlakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ | tasmādavātaracchīghraṃparvatāgrānmahābalaḥ
translation: वीरः hero, महाबलः mighty, लक्ष्मणाग्रजः Lakshmana's elder brother, इत्येवम् in this manner, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, वदन् said, तस्मात् from there, पर्वताग्रात् peak of the mountain, शीघ्रम् without delay, अवातरत् descended.
explanation: Mighty hero Rama, (the elder brother of Lakshmana) said to Lakshmana in this manner (as described earlier) and descended from the peak of the mountain without delay.

shloka_text: अवतीर्यचधर्मात्मातस्माच्छैलात्सराघवः । परैःपरमदुर्धर्षंददर्शबलमात्मनः ।।6.41.24।।
transliteration: avatīryacadharmātmātasmācchailātsarāghavaḥ | paraiḥparamadurdharṣaṃdadarśabalamātmanaḥ
translation: धर्मात्माच righteous, सःराघवः that Raghava, तस्मात् शैलात् from the mountain, अवतीर्य climbing down, परैः foes, परमदुर्धर्षम् very difficult to assail, आत्मनः in the mind, बलम् army strength, ददर्श reviewed.
explanation: Climbing down the mountain, the righteous Rama reviewed in his mind the strength of his army and the enemy which is difficult to assail.

shloka_text: सन्नह्यतुससुग्रीवःकपिराजबलंमहत् । कालज्ञोराघवःकालेसंयुगायाभ्यचोदयत् ।।6.41.25।।
transliteration: sannahyatusasugrīvaḥkapirājabalaṃmahat | kālajñorāghavaḥkālesaṃyugāyābhyacodayat
translation: ससुग्रीवः Sugriva, कालज्ञः knower of when to do, राघवः Raghava, महत् great, कपिराजबलम् army of Vanaras, सन्नह्य ready, काले time, संयुगाय motivated, अभ्यचोदयत् ordered.
explanation: Raghava, who is knowledgeable of when to do what, motivated the army of Vanaras and Sugriva and ordered.

shloka_text: ततःकालेमहाबाहुर्बलेनमहतावृतः । प्रस्थितःपुरतोधवनीलङ्कामभिमुखःपुरीम् ।।6.41.26।।
transliteration: tataḥkālemahābāhurbalenamahatāvṛtaḥ | prasthitaḥpuratodhavanīlaṅkāmabhimukhaḥpurīm
translation: ततः then, महाबाहुः broad shouldered, महता great, बलेन army, वृतः surrounded by, पुरतः in front, धवनी early morning, काले time, लङ्कांपुरीं Lanka, अभिमुखः towards, प्रस्थितः proceeded.
explanation: Surrounded by a large army in front, the broad shouldered Rama proceeded towards Lanka.

shloka_text: तंविभीषणसुग्रीवौहनूमाञ्जाम्बवान्नळ । ऋक्षराजस्तथानीलोलक्ष्मणश्चान्वयुस्तदा ।।6.41.27।।
transliteration: taṃvibhīṣaṇasugrīvauhanūmāñjāmbavānnaḻa | ṛkṣarājastathānīlolakṣmaṇaścānvayustadā
translation: तदा then, विभीषणसुग्रीवौ Vibheeshana and Sugriva, हनुमान् Hanuman, ऋक्षराजः king of Bears, जाम्बवान् Jambavan, नलः Nala, तथा in the same way, नीलः Neela, लक्ष्मणश्च and Lakshmana, तम् them, अन्वयुः followed.
explanation: Then Vibheeshana, Sugriva, Hanuman, Jambavan, Nala, Neela in the same way Lakshmana followed.

shloka_text: ततःपशचात्सुमहतीपृतनर् क्षवनौकसाम् । प्रच्छाद्यमहतींभूमिमनुयातिस्मराघवम् ।।6.41.28।।
transliteration: tataḥpaśacātsumahatīpṛtanar kṣavanaukasām | pracchādyamahatīṃbhūmimanuyātismarāghavam
translation: ततः then, ऋक्षवनौकसाम् bears and monkeys, महती great, पृतना land महतीम् all over, भूमिम् land, प्रच्छाद्य covering, राघवम् Rama, अनुयातिस्म followed पशचात्सु behind.
explanation: Then the bears, monkeys, covering all over the land went behind Rama.

shloka_text: शैलशृङ्गाणिशतशःप्रवृद्धांश्चमहीरुहान् । जगृहुःकुञ्जरप्रख्यावानराःपरवारणाः ।।6.41.29।।
transliteration: śailaśṛṅgāṇiśataśaḥpravṛddhāṃścamahīruhān | jagṛhuḥkuñjaraprakhyāvānarāḥparavāraṇāḥ
translation: परवारणाः capable of warding off the enemy, कुञ्जरप्रख्याः whose body were the size of elephants, वानराः monkeys, शैलशृङ्गाणि mountain peaks, प्रवृद्धान् fully grown, शतशः in hundreds, महीरुहान् huge trees, जगृहुः bore in their hands.
explanation: The monkeys who were of the size of elephants capable of warding off the enemy, bore huge grown up trees in their hands and went.

shloka_text: तौत्वदीर्घेणकालेनभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ । रावणस्यपुरींलङ्कामसेदतुररिन्दमौ ।।6.41.30।।
transliteration: tautvadīrgheṇakālenabhrātaraurāmalakṣmaṇau | rāvaṇasyapurīṃlaṅkāmasedaturarindamau
translation: अरिन्दमौ tamers of foes, भ्रातरौ the two brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, अदीर्घेण in a short, कालेन time, रावणस्य Ravana's, पुरीम् city, लङ्काम् of Lanka, आसेदतुः reached.
explanation: In a short while the two brothers Rama and Lakshmana, tamers of foes reached the city of Lanka.

shloka_text: पताकामालिनींरम्यामुद्यानवनशोभिताम् । चित्रवप्रासुदुष्प्रापमुच्चैःप्राकारतोरणाम् ।।6.41.31।। तांसुरैरपिदुर्धर्षांरामवाक्यप्रचोदिताः । यथानिदेशंसम्पीड्यन्यविशन्तवनौकसः ।।6.41.32।।
transliteration: patākāmālinīṃramyāmudyānavanaśobhitām | citravaprāsuduṣprāpamuccaiḥprākāratoraṇām  tāṃsurairapidurdharṣāṃrāmavākyapracoditāḥ | yathānideśaṃsampīḍyanyaviśantavanaukasaḥ
translation: रामवाक्यप्रचोदिताः commanded by Rama's words, वनौकसः gardens, पताकामालिनीम् decorated with flags, रम्याम् beautiful to look at, उद्यानवनशोभिताम् embellished with gardens, चित्रवस्राम् wonderful, सुदुष्प्रापाम् defensive walls, उच्चैः tall प्राकारतोरणाम् archways of boundary, सुरैरपि even for Devatas, दुर्धर्षाम् difficult to access, ताम् they, यथानिदेशम् as ordained, सम्पीड्य remaining, न्यविशन्त entered.
explanation: Commanded by Rama's words the Vanaras remaining in their positions as ordained, entered the wonderful Lanka, which was decorated with flags, embellished with gardens. The defensive walls and arches of the boundary of Lanka were difficult to access even for Devatas.

shloka_text: पताकामालिनींरम्यामुद्यानवनशोभिताम् । चित्रवप्रासुदुष्प्रापमुच्चैःप्राकारतोरणाम् ।।6.41.31।। तांसुरैरपिदुर्धर्षांरामवाक्यप्रचोदिताः । यथानिदेशंसम्पीड्यन्यविशन्तवनौकसः ।।6.41.32।।
transliteration: patākāmālinīṃramyāmudyānavanaśobhitām | citravaprāsuduṣprāpamuccaiḥprākāratoraṇām  tāṃsurairapidurdharṣāṃrāmavākyapracoditāḥ | yathānideśaṃsampīḍyanyaviśantavanaukasaḥ
translation: रामवाक्यप्रचोदिताः commanded by Rama's words, वनौकसः gardens, पताकामालिनीम् decorated with flags, रम्याम् beautiful to look at, उद्यानवनशोभिताम् embellished with gardens, चित्रवस्राम् wonderful, सुदुष्प्रापाम् defensive walls, उच्चैः tall प्राकारतोरणाम् archways of boundary, सुरैरपि even for Devatas, दुर्धर्षाम् difficult to access, ताम् they, यथानिदेशम् as ordained, सम्पीड्य remaining, न्यविशन्त entered.
explanation: Commanded by Rama's words the Vanaras remaining in their positions as ordained, entered the wonderful Lanka, which was decorated with flags, embellished with gardens. The defensive walls and arches of the boundary of Lanka were difficult to access even for Devatas.

shloka_text: लङ्कायास्तूत्तरंद्वारंशैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम् । रामःसहानुजोधन्वीजुगोपचरुरोधच ।।6.41.33।।
transliteration: laṅkāyāstūttaraṃdvāraṃśailaśṛṅgamivonnatam | rāmaḥsahānujodhanvījugopacarurodhaca
translation: सहानुजः accompanied by his brother, रामः Rama, धन्वी armed with bow, लङ्कायाः into Lanka, शैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम् like a lofty mountain peak, तम् that, उत्तरद्वारम् northern gate, जुगोप blocked, रुरोधच protected.
explanation: Accompanied by his brother Lakshmana, Rama, armed with bow, blocked the northern gate of Lanka which was like a lofty mountain peak and protected.

shloka_text: लङ्कामुपनिविष्टस्तुरामोदशरथात्मजः । लक्ष्मणानुचरोवीरःपुरींरावणपालिताम् ।।6.41.34।। उत्तरद्वारमासाद्ययत्रतिष्ठतिरावणः । नान्योरामाद्धितद् द्वारंसमर्थःपरिरक्षितुम् ।।6.41.35।। सायुथैराक्षसैर्भीमैरभिगुप्तंसमन्ततः । लघूनांत्रासजननंपाताळमिवदानवैः ।।6.41.36।।
transliteration: laṅkāmupaniviṣṭasturāmodaśarathātmajaḥ | lakṣmaṇānucarovīraḥpurīṃrāvaṇapālitām  uttaradvāramāsādyayatratiṣṭhatirāvaṇaḥ | nānyorāmāddhitad dvāraṃsamarthaḥparirakṣitum  sāyuthairākṣasairbhīmairabhiguptaṃsamantataḥ | laghūnāṃtrāsajananaṃpātāḻamivadānavaiḥ
translation: दशरथात्मजः Dasaratha's son, लक्ष्मणानुचरः follower Lakshmana, वीरः heroic, रामः Rama, रावणः Ravana, यत्र there, तिष्ठति settled, उत्तरद्वारम् at northern gate, आसाद्य having reached, रावणपालिताम् ruled by Ravana, तम् that, वरुणेन by Varuna, सागरम् इव like an ocean, भीमम् frightening, सायुधैः guarded by,भीमैः terrific, राक्षसैः Rakshasa, समन्ततः all over, अभिगुप्तम् secretly hidden, दानवैः Rakshasas, पाताळमिव like subterranean, लघूनाम् small pieces, त्रासजननम् numerous, तत् द्वारम् that gateway, परिरक्षितुम् highly protected, रामात् by Rama, अन्यः other than, नसमर्थःहि not possible.
explanation: (Dasaratha's son) Rama who had Lakshmana as follower reached the northern gate protected by Ravana. Just as the ocean is guarded by Varuna, it was guarded by terrific Rakshasas, who were secretly hiding all over like the Rakshasas in the subterranean region with small amounts of numerous armours for protection. It was not possible for anyone other than Rama to enter.

shloka_text: लङ्कामुपनिविष्टस्तुरामोदशरथात्मजः । लक्ष्मणानुचरोवीरःपुरींरावणपालिताम् ।।6.41.34।। उत्तरद्वारमासाद्ययत्रतिष्ठतिरावणः । नान्योरामाद्धितद् द्वारंसमर्थःपरिरक्षितुम् ।।6.41.35।। सायुथैराक्षसैर्भीमैरभिगुप्तंसमन्ततः । लघूनांत्रासजननंपाताळमिवदानवैः ।।6.41.36।।
transliteration: laṅkāmupaniviṣṭasturāmodaśarathātmajaḥ | lakṣmaṇānucarovīraḥpurīṃrāvaṇapālitām  uttaradvāramāsādyayatratiṣṭhatirāvaṇaḥ | nānyorāmāddhitad dvāraṃsamarthaḥparirakṣitum  sāyuthairākṣasairbhīmairabhiguptaṃsamantataḥ | laghūnāṃtrāsajananaṃpātāḻamivadānavaiḥ
translation: दशरथात्मजः Dasaratha's son, लक्ष्मणानुचरः follower Lakshmana, वीरः heroic, रामः Rama, रावणः Ravana, यत्र there, तिष्ठति settled, उत्तरद्वारम् at northern gate, आसाद्य having reached, रावणपालिताम् ruled by Ravana, तम् that, वरुणेन by Varuna, सागरम् इव like an ocean, भीमम् frightening, सायुधैः guarded by,भीमैः terrific, राक्षसैः Rakshasa, समन्ततः all over, अभिगुप्तम् secretly hidden, दानवैः Rakshasas, पाताळमिव like subterranean, लघूनाम् small pieces, त्रासजननम् numerous, तत् द्वारम् that gateway, परिरक्षितुम् highly protected, रामात् by Rama, अन्यः other than, नसमर्थःहि not possible.
explanation: (Dasaratha's son) Rama who had Lakshmana as follower reached the northern gate protected by Ravana. Just as the ocean is guarded by Varuna, it was guarded by terrific Rakshasas, who were secretly hiding all over like the Rakshasas in the subterranean region with small amounts of numerous armours for protection. It was not possible for anyone other than Rama to enter.

shloka_text: लङ्कामुपनिविष्टस्तुरामोदशरथात्मजः । लक्ष्मणानुचरोवीरःपुरींरावणपालिताम् ।।6.41.34।। उत्तरद्वारमासाद्ययत्रतिष्ठतिरावणः । नान्योरामाद्धितद् द्वारंसमर्थःपरिरक्षितुम् ।।6.41.35।। सायुथैराक्षसैर्भीमैरभिगुप्तंसमन्ततः । लघूनांत्रासजननंपाताळमिवदानवैः ।।6.41.36।।
transliteration: laṅkāmupaniviṣṭasturāmodaśarathātmajaḥ | lakṣmaṇānucarovīraḥpurīṃrāvaṇapālitām  uttaradvāramāsādyayatratiṣṭhatirāvaṇaḥ | nānyorāmāddhitad dvāraṃsamarthaḥparirakṣitum  sāyuthairākṣasairbhīmairabhiguptaṃsamantataḥ | laghūnāṃtrāsajananaṃpātāḻamivadānavaiḥ
translation: दशरथात्मजः Dasaratha's son, लक्ष्मणानुचरः follower Lakshmana, वीरः heroic, रामः Rama, रावणः Ravana, यत्र there, तिष्ठति settled, उत्तरद्वारम् at northern gate, आसाद्य having reached, रावणपालिताम् ruled by Ravana, तम् that, वरुणेन by Varuna, सागरम् इव like an ocean, भीमम् frightening, सायुधैः guarded by,भीमैः terrific, राक्षसैः Rakshasa, समन्ततः all over, अभिगुप्तम् secretly hidden, दानवैः Rakshasas, पाताळमिव like subterranean, लघूनाम् small pieces, त्रासजननम् numerous, तत् द्वारम् that gateway, परिरक्षितुम् highly protected, रामात् by Rama, अन्यः other than, नसमर्थःहि not possible.
explanation: (Dasaratha's son) Rama who had Lakshmana as follower reached the northern gate protected by Ravana. Just as the ocean is guarded by Varuna, it was guarded by terrific Rakshasas, who were secretly hiding all over like the Rakshasas in the subterranean region with small amounts of numerous armours for protection. It was not possible for anyone other than Rama to enter.

shloka_text: विन्यस्तानिचयोधानांबहूनिविविधानिच । ददर्शाऽयुधजालानितत्रैवकवचानिच ।।6.41.37।।
transliteration: vinyastānicayodhānāṃbahūnivividhānica | dadarśā'yudhajālānitatraivakavacānica
translation: योधानाम् for the combatants of war, विन्यस्तानि of every kind, बहूनि numerous, विविधानिच and different kind, आयुधजालानि weapons, तथैव so also, कवचानिच and shields, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Rama Saw there, numerous weapons of every kind so also shields for the combatants of war.

shloka_text: पूर्वंतुद्वारमासाद्यनीलोहरिचमूपतिः । अतिष्ठत्सहमैन्देनद्विविदेनचवीर्यवान् ।।6.41.38।।
transliteration: pūrvaṃtudvāramāsādyanīloharicamūpatiḥ | atiṣṭhatsahamaindenadvividenacavīryavān
translation: हरिचमूपतिः commander of the army of monkeys, वीर्यवान् valiant one, नीलः Neela, मैन्देन Mainda सह and also, द्विविदेनचसह Dwivida also, पूर्वंद्वारम् east gate, आसाद्य reached, अतिष्ठत् remained there.
explanation: Neela the commanderinchief of the army of monkeys, a valiant one, also Dwivida, and Mainda reached the east gate and remained there.

shloka_text: अङ्गदोदक्षिणद्वारंजग्राहसुमहाबलः । ऋषभेणगवाक्षेणगजेनगवयेनच ।।6.41.39।।
transliteration: aṅgadodakṣiṇadvāraṃjagrāhasumahābalaḥ | ṛṣabheṇagavākṣeṇagajenagavayenaca
translation: सुमहाबलः of great prowess, अङ्गदः Angada, ऋषभेण with Rshaba, गवाक्षेण and Gavaksha, गजेन Gaja, गवयेनच and Gavaya, दक्षिणद्वारम् south gate, जग्राह reached.
explanation: Angada endowed with great prowess along with Rshaba, Gavaksha, Gaja, and Gavaya reached the south gate.

shloka_text: हनुमान् पश्चिमद्वारंररक्षबलवान्कपिः । प्रमाथिप्रषुभ्यांचवीरैरन्यैश्चसङ्गतः ।।6.41.40।।
transliteration: hanumān paścimadvāraṃrarakṣabalavānkapiḥ | pramāthipraṣubhyāṃcavīrairanyaiścasaṅgataḥ
translation: बलवान् mighty, कपिः monkey, हनुमान् Hanuman, प्रमाथिप्रषुभ्यांच Pramati and Praghasa, अन्यैः and others, वीरैश्च heroes, सङ्गतः united with, पश्चिमद्वारम् west gate, ररक्ष protected.
explanation: Mighty monkey Hanuman united with heroes Pramati and Praghasa and others protected the west gate.

shloka_text: मध्यमेचस्वयंगुल्मेसुग्रीवस्समतिष्ठत । सहसर्वैर्हरिश्रेष्ठैस्सुपर्णश्वसनोपमैः ।।6.41.41।।
transliteration: madhyamecasvayaṃgulmesugrīvassamatiṣṭhata | sahasarvairhariśreṣṭhaissuparṇaśvasanopamaiḥ
translation: सुग्रीवः Sugriva, सर्वैः all, सुपर्णश्वसनोपमैः equal to Garuda of beautiful wings endowed with wind speed, हरिश्रेष्ठैः chief and best of monkey army, स्वयम् himself, मध्यमे middle, गुल्मे post, समतिष्ठत remained.
explanation: Sugriva chief of all army and best of the monkey army who was equal to Garuda of beautiful wings, endowed with wind speed remained in the middle (of north and west) post.

shloka_text: वानराणांतुषटित्रंशत्कोट्यःप्रख्यातयूथपाः । निपीड्योपनिविष्टाश्चसुग्रीवोयत्रवानरः ।।6.41.42।।
transliteration: vānarāṇāṃtuṣaṭitraṃśatkoṭyaḥprakhyātayūthapāḥ | nipīḍyopaniviṣṭāścasugrīvoyatravānaraḥ
translation: प्रख्यातयूथपाः renowned generals, वानराणाम् of the Vanaras, षटित्रंशत्कोट्यः thirty six crores, वानरः Vanara, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, यत्र there, निपीड्य stood, उपनिविष्टाः camped.
explanation: Renowned generals of the Vanara army and thirtysix crores of Vanaras stood there camping.

shloka_text: शासनेनतुरामस्यलक्ष्मणस्सविभीषणः । द्वारेद्वारेहरीणांतुकोटिंकोटिंन्यवेशयेत् ।।6.41.43।।
transliteration: śāsanenaturāmasyalakṣmaṇassavibhīṣaṇaḥ | dvāredvāreharīṇāṃtukoṭiṃkoṭiṃnyaveśayet
translation: सविभीषणः Vibheeshana, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, रामस्य by Rama's, शासनेन command, द्वारेद्वारे crores and crores, हरीणाम् Vanaras, कोटिंकोटिम् crores and crores, न्यवेशयत् posted as per need.
explanation: By the command of Rama, Vibheeshana accompanied by Lakshmana posted crores and crores of Vanaras there.

shloka_text: पश्चिमेनतुरामस्यसुषेणःसहजाम्बवान् ।।6.41.44।। आदूरान्मध्यमेगुल्मेतस्थौबहुबलानुगः ।
transliteration: paścimenaturāmasyasuṣeṇaḥsahajāmbavān  ādūrānmadhyamegulmetasthaubahubalānugaḥ |
translation: सुषेणः Sushena, सहजाम्बवान् along with Jambavan, बहुबलानुगः with large army, रामस्य by Rama, पश्चिमेन at the west, अदूरात् not far from, मध्यमेगुल्मे in the centre, तस्थौ at the back.
explanation: Sushena along with Jambavan and a large army of Vanaras were posted in the centre not far from Rama at the west by Rama's order.

shloka_text: तेतुवानरशार्धूलाःशार्दूलाइवदंष्ट्रिणः ।।6.41.45।। गृहीत्वाद्रुमशैलाग्रान्हृष्टायुद्धायतस्थिरे ।
transliteration: tetuvānaraśārdhūlāḥśārdūlāivadaṃṣṭriṇaḥ  gṛhītvādrumaśailāgrānhṛṣṭāyuddhāyatasthire |
translation: शार्दूलाःइव resembling tiger, दंष्ट्रिणः endowed with sharp teeth, ते they, वानरशार्दूलाः tigers among Vanaras, हृष्टाः joyfully, द्रुमशैलाग्रान् trees and peaks of mountains, गृहीत्वा holding, युद्धाय to combat, तस्थिरे waited.
explanation: Vanaras who resembled tigers, endowed with sharp teeth joyfully stood there holding trees and peaks of mountain waiting to combat.

shloka_text: सर्वेविकृतलाङ्गूलास्सर्वेदंष्ट्रानखायुधा:।। 6.41.46।। सर्वेविकृतचित्राङ्गास्सर्वेचविकृताननाः ।
transliteration: sarvevikṛtalāṅgūlāssarvedaṃṣṭrānakhāyudhā: sarvevikṛtacitrāṅgāssarvecavikṛtānanāḥ |
translation: सर्वे all, विकृतालाङ्गूलाः unusually lifted up, सर्वे all, दंष्ट्रानखायुधा: had their teeth and nails as weapons, सर्वे all, विकृतचित्राङ्गाः unnatural faces, सर्वेच and all, विकृताननाः distorted eyes.
explanation: All had their tails lifted unusually, had their nails and teeth sharp as weapons, some had unnatural face, and all of them had distorted eyes (as in fury).

shloka_text: दशनागबलाःकेचित्केचिद्धशगुणोत्तराः ।।6.41.47।। केचिन्नागसहस्रस्यबभूवुस्तुल्यविक्रमाः ।
transliteration: daśanāgabalāḥkecitkeciddhaśaguṇottarāḥ  kecinnāgasahasrasyababhūvustulyavikramāḥ |
translation: केचित् a few, दशनागबलाः strength of ten elephants, केचित् some, दशगुणोत्तराः ten times more strong than others, केचित् a few, नागसहस्रस्य equal to thousand elephants in strength, तुल्यविक्रमाः endowed with great strength, बभूवुः were.
explanation: A few of them were having the strength of ten elephants, some had ten times more than others, and a few were endowed with great strength equal to thousand elephants.

shloka_text: सन्तिचौघबलाःकेचित्केचिच्छतगुणोत्तराः ।।6.41.48।। अप्रमेयबलाश्चान्येतत्रासन्हरियूथपाः
transliteration: santicaughabalāḥkecitkecicchataguṇottarāḥ  aprameyabalāścānyetatrāsanhariyūthapāḥ
translation: केचित् few, ओघबलाः strength of an ogha, केचित् some, शतगुणोत्तराः hundred times more, सन्ति still, तत्र there, अन्ये others, हरियूथपाः monkey commanders, अप्रमेयाबलाश्च immeasurable strength, आसन् possessed.
explanation: Few monkeys had strength of an ogha, some had a hundred times more, and the monkey commanders possessed immeasurable strength.

shloka_text: अद्भुतश्चविचित्रश्चतेषामासीत्समागमः ।।6.41.49।। तत्रवानरसैन्यानांशलभानामिवोद्यमः ।
transliteration: adbhutaścavicitraścateṣāmāsītsamāgamaḥ  tatravānarasainyānāṃśalabhānāmivodyamaḥ |
translation: तत्र there, शलभानाम् in that place, उद्यमःइव like locusts, तेषाम् they, वानरसैन्यानाम् Vanara army, समागमः gathered, अद्भुतश्च amazing, विचित्रश्च astonishing, आसीत् seemed.
explanation: There it seemed as if a flight of locusts had gathered, with monkey army gathered there. It was amazing and astonishing.

shloka_text: प्रतिपूर्णमिवाकाशंसञ्छन्नेवचमेदिनी ।।6.41.50।। लङ्कापुमनिविष्टैश्चसम्पतद्भिश्चवानरैः ।
transliteration: pratipūrṇamivākāśaṃsañchannevacamedinī  laṅkāpumaniviṣṭaiścasampatadbhiścavānaraiḥ |
translation: लङ्काम् in Lanka, उपनिविष्टैः settled, वानरैः with Vanara, सम्पतद्भिश्च already staying, आकाशम् the sky, प्रतिपूर्णमिव fully around like, मेदिनीच on the land, सञ्छन्ने covering.
explanation: Vanaras settled in such a way all around Lanka completely covering the land with those already at Lanka.

shloka_text: शतंशतसहस्राणांपृथगृक्षवनौकसाम् ।।6.41.51।। लङ्काद्वाराङयुपाजग्मुरन्येयोद्धुंसमन्ततः ।
transliteration: śataṃśatasahasrāṇāṃpṛthagṛkṣavanaukasām  laṅkādvārāṅayupājagmuranyeyoddhuṃsamantataḥ |
translation: ऋक्षवनौकसाम् bears and monkeys, शतसहस्राणाम् a hundred thousand, शतम् a hundred, पृथक् several, अन्ये others, समन्ततः gathered, लङ्काद्वाराणि at the gates of Lanka, योद्धुम् to fight, उपाजग्मुः proceeded.
explanation: A hundred thousand bars and monkeys and several others already gathered at the gates of Lanka to fight proceeded.

shloka_text: आवृतस्सगिरिस्सर्वैस्सैस्समन्तात् प्लवङ्गमैः ।।6.41.52।। अयुतानांसहस्रंचपुरींतामभ्यवर्तत ।
transliteration: āvṛtassagirissarvaissaissamantāt plavaṅgamaiḥ  ayutānāṃsahasraṃcapurīṃtāmabhyavartata |
translation: सःगिरिः that mountain, समन्तात् all over, तैः those, प्लवङ्गमैः monkeys, आवृतः surrounded, अयुतानाम् boundary, सहस्रम् all over, ताम् them, पुरीम् city, अभ्यवर्तत to collect information.
explanation: All over the mountain the monkeys surrounded the boundary wall of Lanka city to collect information.

shloka_text: वानरैर्बलवद्भिश्चबभूवद्रुमपाणिभिः ।।6.41.53।। सम्वृतासर्वतोलङ्कादुष्प्रवेशाऽपिवायुना ।
transliteration: vānarairbalavadbhiścababhūvadrumapāṇibhiḥ  samvṛtāsarvatolaṅkāduṣpraveśā'pivāyunā |
translation: द्रुमपाणिभिः with uprooted trees, बलवद्भिः might, वानरैः Vanaras, सर्वतः everywhere, सम्वृता occupied, लङ्का Lanka, वायुनापि even for wind, दुष्प्रवेशा difficult to enter, बभूव appeared.
explanation: Mighty Vanaras holding uprooted trees occupied everywhere and it seemed difficult for even wind to enter Lanka.

shloka_text: राक्षसाविस्मयंजग्मुःसहसाऽभिनिपीडिताः ।।6.41.54।। वानरैर्मेघसङ्काशैश्शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमैः ।
transliteration: rākṣasāvismayaṃjagmuḥsahasā'bhinipīḍitāḥ  vānarairmeghasaṅkāśaiśśakratulyaparākramaiḥ |
translation: मेघसङ्काशैः clouds, शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमैः Indra of great valour, वानरैः Vanaras, सहसा equalled, अभिनिपीडिताः caught, राक्षसाः Rakshasa, विस्मयम् wondered, जग्मुः gave way.
explanation: Caught by Vanaras like clouds and equalled Indra in valour gave way to wonder for the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: महान् शब्दोऽभवत्तत्रबलौघस्याभिवर्ततः ।।6.41.55।। सागरस्येवभिन्नस्ययथास्यात्सलिलस्वनः ।
transliteration: mahān śabdo'bhavattatrabalaughasyābhivartataḥ  sāgarasyevabhinnasyayathāsyātsalilasvanaḥ |
translation: तत्र thereafter, भिन्नस्य divisions, सागरस्येव like the ocean, बलौघस्य on the mountain peak, अभिवर्ततः appeared, सलिलस्वनः roaring sound of water, यथा like that, स्यात् , महान् great, शब्दः sound, अभवत् appeared.
explanation: Thereafter with the divisions of the Vanara army moving like the ocean on the mountain peak, appeared like the roaring sound of water in the ocean moving out of boundary.

shloka_text: तेनशब्देनमहतासप्राकारासतोरणा ।।6.41.56।। लङ्काप्रचलितासर्वासशैलवनकानना ।
transliteration: tenaśabdenamahatāsaprākārāsatoraṇā  laṅkāpracalitāsarvāsaśailavanakānanā |
translation: महता great, तेनशब्देन by that sound, सप्राकारा that boundary, सतोरणा the archways, सशैलवनकानना mountains forests, सर्वा all, लङ्का Lanka, प्रचलिता shook violently.
explanation: By the great sound the boundary, the archways and the mountains and forests shook violently.

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणगुप्तासासुग्रीवेणचवाहिनी ।।6.41.57।। बभूवदुर्धर्षतरासर्वैरपिसुरासुरैः ।
transliteration: rāmalakṣmaṇaguptāsāsugrīveṇacavāhinī  babhūvadurdharṣatarāsarvairapisurāsuraiḥ |
translation: रामलक्ष्मणगुप्ता protected by Rama and Lakshmana, सुग्रीवेणच and Sugriva, सा that, हरिवाहिनी monkey army, सर्वैः all, सुरासुरैरपि Rakshasas and Devatas, दुर्धर्षतरा highly difficult, बभूव became.
explanation: Protected by Rama and Lakshmana and Sugriva that an army of monkeys became difficult to assail even for Rakshasas and Devatas.

shloka_text: राघवःसन्निवेश्यैवंस्वसैन्यंरक्षसांवधे ।।6.41.58।। सम्मन्त्ऱ्यमन्त्रिभिस्सार्थंनिश्चित्यचपुनःपुनः । आनन्तर्यमभिप्रेप्सुःक्रमयोगार्थतत्त्ववित् ।।6.41.59।। विभीषणस्यानुमतेराजधर्ममनुस्मरन् । अङ्गदंवालितनयंसमाहूयेदमब्रवीत् ।।6.41.60।।
transliteration: rāghavaḥsanniveśyaivaṃsvasainyaṃrakṣasāṃvadhe  sammantṟyamantribhissārthaṃniścityacapunaḥpunaḥ | ānantaryamabhiprepsuḥkramayogārthatattvavit  vibhīṣaṇasyānumaterājadharmamanusmaran | aṅgadaṃvālitanayaṃsamāhūyedamabravīt
translation: क्रमयोगार्थतत्त्ववित् deliberating the action repeatedly, राघवः Raghava, स्वम् himself, सैन्यम् army, रक्षसाम् Rakshasas, वधे to kill, एवम् in the same way, संनिवेश्य gathering together, मन्त्रिभिः even ministers सार्थम् all of them, पुनःपुनः again and again, सम्मन्त्ऱ्य discussing, निश्चित्य decision taken, अनन्तर्यम् later, अभिप्रेप्सुः recalling राजधर्मम् king's duty, अनुस्मरन् calling, विभीषणस्य with Vibhishana, अनुमते per mission, वालितनयम् Vali's son, अङ्गदम् Angada, समाहूय summoning, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Deliberating on the action to be taken to kill the Rakshasas, Raghava himself called the army and gathered them and the ministers all of them again and again discussed and took the decision. Later recalling the king's duty with Vibheeshana, summoned Vali's son Angada and spoke these words.

shloka_text: राघवःसन्निवेश्यैवंस्वसैन्यंरक्षसांवधे ।।6.41.58।। सम्मन्त्ऱ्यमन्त्रिभिस्सार्थंनिश्चित्यचपुनःपुनः । आनन्तर्यमभिप्रेप्सुःक्रमयोगार्थतत्त्ववित् ।।6.41.59।। विभीषणस्यानुमतेराजधर्ममनुस्मरन् । अङ्गदंवालितनयंसमाहूयेदमब्रवीत् ।।6.41.60।।

explanation: Deliberating on the action to be taken to kill the Rakshasas, Raghava himself called the army and gathered them and the ministers all of them again and again discussed and took the decision. Later recalling the king's duty with Vibheeshana, summoned Vali's son Angada and spoke these words.

shloka_text: राघवःसन्निवेश्यैवंस्वसैन्यंरक्षसांवधे ।।6.41.58।। सम्मन्त्ऱ्यमन्त्रिभिस्सार्थंनिश्चित्यचपुनःपुनः । आनन्तर्यमभिप्रेप्सुःक्रमयोगार्थतत्त्ववित् ।।6.41.59।। विभीषणस्यानुमतेराजधर्ममनुस्मरन् । अङ्गदंवालितनयंसमाहूयेदमब्रवीत् ।।6.41.60।।
