Later recalling the king's duty with Vibheeshana, summoned Vali's son Angada and spoke these words.

shloka_text: गत्वासौम्य दशग्रीवंब्रूहिमद्वचनात्कपे । लङ्घयित्वापुरींलङ्कांभयंत्यक्त्वागतव्यधः ।।6.41.61।। भ्रष्टश्रीक गतैश्वर्य मुमूर्षो नष्टचेतनः ।
transliteration: gatvāsaumya daśagrīvaṃbrūhimadvacanātkape | laṅghayitvāpurīṃlaṅkāṃbhayaṃtyaktvāgatavyadhaḥ  bhraṣṭaśrīka gataiśvarya mumūrṣo naṣṭacetanaḥ |
translation: सौम्य noble, कपे monkey, लङ्कांपुरीम् Lanka's, लङ्घयित्वा crossing over, भयम् fear, त्यक्त्वा giving up, गतव्यधः past difficulty, भ्रष्टश्रीक lost sovereignty, गतैश्वर्य fallen out of past fortune, मुमूर्षोनष्टचेतनः lost his sense, दशग्रीवम् tenheaded king, गत्वा gone, मद्वचनात् proudly, ब्रूहि said.
explanation: "O noble Hanuman crossing over Lanka without fear, giving up the difficulties experienced earlier we reached. Admonish the tenheaded king who has lost senses, his past fortune and sovereignty."

shloka_text: ऋषीणांदेवतानांचगन्धर्वाप्सरसांतथा ।।6.41.62।। नागानामथयक्षाणांराज्ञांचरजनीचर । यच्चपापंकृतंमोहादवलिप्तेनराक्षस ।।6.41.63।। नूनंतेविगतोदर्पःस्वयम्भुवरदानजः । तस्यपापस्यसम्प्राप्ताव्युष्टिरद्यदुरसदा ।।6.41.64।।
transliteration: ṛṣīṇāṃdevatānāṃcagandharvāpsarasāṃtathā  nāgānāmathayakṣāṇāṃrājñāṃcarajanīcara | yaccapāpaṃkṛtaṃmohādavaliptenarākṣasa  nūnaṃtevigatodarpaḥsvayambhuvaradānajaḥ | tasyapāpasyasamprāptāvyuṣṭiradyadurasadā
translation: रजनीचर night ranger, ऋषीणाम् for the sages, देवतानाम् Devatas, तथा so also, गन्धर्वाप्सरसाम् Gandharvas and celestial beauties, नागानाम् Nagas, अथ and, यक्षाणाम् Yakshas, राज्ञांच and kings, मोहात् because of delusion, अवलिप्तेन conceited, यत् that, पापम् sin, कृतम् done, तस्य by him, पापस्य sin's, दुरासदा dangerous to approach, व्युष्टिः boon, अद्य obtained, सम्प्राप्ता begotten, नूनम् surely, ते those, स्वयम्भुवरदानजः granted by self born creator, दर्पः pride, विगतः has gone.
explanation: "O night ranger! the time has come for punishment for the sins committed by you to the sages, Devatas, so also to Gandharvas, celestial beauties, Nagas, Yakshas and the kings because of your delusion in conceit. Surely your pride about the boons begotten from the selfborn creator will be gone, said Rama.

Surely your pride about the boons begotten from the selfborn creator will be gone, said Rama.

shloka_text: तस्यदण्डधरस्तेऽहंदाराहरकर्शितः । दण्डंधारयमाणस्तुलङ्काद्वारेव्यवस्थितः ।।6.41.65।।
transliteration: tasyadaṇḍadharaste'haṃdārāharakarśitaḥ | daṇḍaṃdhārayamāṇastulaṅkādvārevyavasthitaḥ
translation: दाराहरणकर्शितः one who has abducted my wife, अहम् I am, तस्य your, ते to you, दण्डधरः holding rod दण्डम् punish, धारयामाणः chastiser, लङ्काद्वारे o king of Lanka, व्यवस्थितः taken position.
explanation: "You, who have abducted my wife, I will punish you with a rod of punishment. I am your chastiser, O king of Lanka I have taken position."

shloka_text: पदवींदेवतानांचमहर्षीणांचराक्षस । राजर्षीणांचसर्वेषांगमिष्यसिमयाहतः ।।6.41.66।।
transliteration: padavīṃdevatānāṃcamaharṣīṇāṃcarākṣasa | rājarṣīṇāṃcasarveṣāṃgamiṣyasimayāhataḥ
translation: राक्षस Rakshasa, मया by me, हतः killed, देवतानांच even Devatas, महर्षीणांच even sages, सर्वेषाम् all of them, राजर्षीणांच royal sages, पदवीम् position, गमिष्यसि lost.
explanation: "O Rakshasa! Even Devatas, sages and even royal sages have also lost their lives, killed by me."

shloka_text: बलेनयेनवैसीतांमाययाराक्षसाधम । यामतिक्रामयित्वात्वंहृतवांस्तद्विदर्शय ।।6.41.67।।
transliteration: balenayenavaisītāṃmāyayārākṣasādhama | yāmatikrāmayitvātvaṃhṛtavāṃstadvidarśaya
translation: राक्षसाधम lowly Rakshasa, त्वम् your, येन that, बलेन power, मायया to me, माम् me, अतिक्रामयित्वा by deceiving me, सीताम् Sita, हृतवान् took away, तत् that, द्विदर्शय display it now.
explanation: "O lowly Rakshasa! By deceiving me you took away Sita. Display that strength now."

shloka_text: अराक्षसमिमंलोकंकर्तास्मिनिशितैःशरैः । नचेच्छरणमभ्येषितामादायतुमैथिलीम् ।।6.41.68।।
transliteration: arākṣasamimaṃlokaṃkartāsminiśitaiḥśaraiḥ | naceccharaṇamabhyeṣitāmādāyatumaithilīm
translation: ताम् her, मैथिलीम् Mythili, आदाय seek, शरणम् my protection, नअभ्येषियदि if not take, निशितैः sharp, शरैः arrows, इमम् this, लोकम् world, अराक्षसम् devoid of Rakshasas, कर्तास्मि will make.
explanation: "If you do not seek my protection I will devoid this world of Rakshasas with my sharp arrows."

shloka_text: धर्मात्माराक्षसश्रेष्ठःसम्प्राप्तोऽयंविभीषणः । लङ्कैश्वर्यंधृवंश्रीमानयंप्राप्नोत्यकण्डकम् ।।6.41.69।।
transliteration: dharmātmārākṣasaśreṣṭhaḥsamprāpto'yaṃvibhīṣaṇaḥ | laṅkaiśvaryaṃdhṛvaṃśrīmānayaṃprāpnotyakaṇḍakam
translation: धर्मात्मा righteous, राक्षसश्रेष्ठः best of Rakshasas, अयंविभीषणः this Vibhishana, सम्प्राप्तः having got, श्रीमान् fortunate, अकण्डकम् glorious, धृवम् undoubtedly, लङ्कैश्वर्यम् kingdom of Lanka, प्राप्नोति will get.
explanation: "This Vibheeshana, the best of Rakshasas will be glorious and fortunate undoubtedly having got the kingdom of Lanka."

shloka_text: नहिराज्यमधर्मेणभोक्तुंक्षणमपित्वया । शक्यंमूर्खसहायेनपापेनाविदितात्मना ।।6.41.70।।
transliteration: nahirājyamadharmeṇabhoktuṃkṣaṇamapitvayā | śakyaṃmūrkhasahāyenapāpenāviditātmanā
translation: मूर्खसहायेन with the help of foolish mates, पापेन a sinner, अविदितात्मना not aware of himself, त्वया by you, क्षणमपि even a moment, राज्यम् kingdom, अथर्मेण unrighteousness, भोक्तुम् to enjoy, नशक्यंहि not possible.
explanation: "One who is not aware of himself, an unrighteous sinner ruling with foolish mates cannot enjoy the kingdom even for a moment."

shloka_text: युध्यस्ववाधृतिंकृत्वाशौर्यमालम्ब्यराक्षस । मच्छरैस्त्वंरणेशान्तस्ततःशान्तोभविष्यसि ।।6.41.71।।
transliteration: yudhyasvavādhṛtiṃkṛtvāśauryamālambyarākṣasa | maccharaistvaṃraṇeśāntastataḥśāntobhaviṣyasi
translation: राक्षस Rakshasa, वा or, धृतिम् fortitude, कृत्वा resorting to, शौर्यम् valour, आलम्ब्य embracing, युध्यस्व gallantry, त्वम् you, रणे in war, मच्छरैः my arrows, शान्तः peace, ततः then, भविष्यसि will obtain.
explanation: "O Rakshasa! You are resorting to fortitude and valour and embracing gallantry in war. By my arrows you will obtain peace (in death)."

shloka_text: यद्वाविशसिलोकांस्त्रीन्पक्षीभूतोमनोजवः । ममचक्षुष्पथंप्राप्यनजीवन्प्रतियास्यसि ।।6.41.72।।
transliteration: yadvāviśasilokāṃstrīnpakṣībhūtomanojavaḥ | mamacakṣuṣpathaṃprāpyanajīvanpratiyāsyasi
translation: मनोजवः one who has no control over mind, मम my, चक्षुःपथम् range of my eyesight, प्राप्य having come in, पक्षी bird, भूत्वा range, त्रीन् three, लोकान् worlds, अविशसि entering, जीवन् with life, नप्रतियास्यसि not go alive again.
explanation: "O Ravana! You have no control over your mind, and if you come in the range of my eyesight and enter the three worlds also you will not go alive again."

shloka_text: ब्रवीमित्वांहितंवाक्यंक्रियतामौर्ध्वदैहिकम् । सुदृष्टाक्रियतांलङ्काजीवितंतेमयिस्थितम् ।।6.41.73।।
transliteration: bravīmitvāṃhitaṃvākyaṃkriyatāmaurdhvadaihikam | sudṛṣṭākriyatāṃlaṅkājīvitaṃtemayisthitam
translation: त्वाम् these, हितम् well meaning, वाक्यम् words, ब्रवीमि having spoken, और्ध्वहिकम् obsequies, क्रियताम् to do, लङ्का in Lanka, सुदृष्टा to do the last rites, क्रियताम् do तेजीवितम् for your life, मयि I, स्थितम् will do.
explanation: Having addressed it in well meaning words, Rama said 'I will do you obsequies as no one will be left in Lanka to do your last rites'.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तःसतुतारेयोरामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । जगामाकाशामाविश्यमूर्तिमानिवहव्यवाट् ।।6.41.74।।
transliteration: ityuktaḥsatutāreyorāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā | jagāmākāśāmāviśyamūrtimānivahavyavāṭ
translation: अक्लिष्टकर्मणा unwearied in action, रामेण by Rama, इति this way, उक्तः spoken, तारेयः Tara's son, मूर्तिमान् resembled, हव्यवाट् इव like fire, आकाशम् sky, आविश्य flew, जगाम went.
explanation: Rama having spoken that way, Tara's son, Angada, who was like fire god, who was unwearied in action flew to the sky.

shloka_text: सोऽतिपत्यमुहूर्तेनश्रीमान्रावणमन्दिरम् । ददर्शासीनमव्यग्रंरावणंसचिवैःसह ।।6.41.75।।
transliteration: so'tipatyamuhūrtenaśrīmānrāvaṇamandiram | dadarśāsīnamavyagraṃrāvaṇaṃsacivaiḥsaha
translation: श्रीमान् prosperous, सः that he, मुहूर्तेन in a moment, रावणमन्दिरम् Ravana's palace, अतिपत्य having landed, सचिवैःसह with his ministers, आसीनम् seated, रावणम् Ravana, अव्यग्रम् tiger, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Angada landed on Ravana's palace in a moment and saw the tiger like prosperous Ravana seated with his ministers.

shloka_text: ततस्तस्य I विदूरेणनिपत्यसहरिपुङ्गवः । दीप्ताग्निसदृशस्तस्थावङ्गदःकनकाङ्गदः ।।6.41.76।।
transliteration: tatastasya I vidūreṇanipatyasaharipuṅgavaḥ | dīptāgnisadṛśastasthāvaṅgadaḥkanakāṅgadaḥ
translation: ततः thereafter, सहरिपुङ्गवः that leader of monkeys, दीप्ताग्निसदृशः blazing like fire, कनकाङ्गदः adorned with golden armlets, अङ्गदः Angada, तस्य his, अविदूरेण at a short distance, निपत्य landed, तस्थौ stood.
explanation: Thereafter, the leader of the monkeys, Angada adorned with golden armlets stood like a blazing fire at a distance.

shloka_text: तद्रामवचनंसर्वमन्यूनाधिकमुत्तमम् । सामात्यंश्रावयामासनिवेद्यात्मानमात्मना ।।6.41.77।।
transliteration: tadrāmavacanaṃsarvamanyūnādhikamuttamam | sāmātyaṃśrāvayāmāsanivedyātmānamātmanā
translation: आत्मानम् I am, आत्मना myself, निवेद्य known, तत् that, उत्तमम् best, सर्वम् all, रामवचनम् Rama's words, अन्यूनाधिकम् without adding or deleting, सामात्यम् completely, श्रावयामास you may listen.
explanation: "I made known the words of Rama completely without adding or deleting. You may listen."

shloka_text: दूतोऽहंकोशलेन्द्रस्यरामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः । वालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदोनामयदितेश्रोत्रमागतः ।।6.41.78।।
transliteration: dūto'haṃkośalendrasyarāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ | vāliputro'ṅgadonāmayaditeśrotramāgataḥ
translation: वालिपुत्रः Vali's son, अङ्गदोनाम by name Angada, अहम् I am, कोशलेन्द्रस्य Kosala King's, अक्लिष्टकर्मणः unwearied in action, रामस्य Rama's, दूतः envoy, ते to you, श्रोत्रम् land, आगतःयदि have landed.
explanation: "I am the son of Vali,by name Angada,an envoy of Rama ,the king of Kosala of unwearied action. You may know that I have landed"

shloka_text: अहत्वांराघवोरामःकौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः । निष्पत्यप्रतियुध्यस्वनृशंस पुरुषोभव ।।6.41.79।।
transliteration: ahatvāṃrāghavorāmaḥkausalyānandavardhanaḥ | niṣpatyapratiyudhyasvanṛśaṃsa puruṣobhava
translation: राघवः Raghava, कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः enhancer of happiness of Kausalya (Rama), रामः Rama, त्वाम् to you, आह you, नृशंस ruthless, निष्पत्य sallying forth, युध्यस्व in combat, पुरुषः man, भव to me.
explanation: "Raghava, the enhancer of the happiness of Kausalya speaks to you. Ruthless Rakshasa! Sallying forth, get ready for combat."

shloka_text: हन्तास्मित्वांसहामात्यंसपुत्रज्ञातिबान्धवम् । निरुद्विग्नास्त्रयोलोकाभविष्यन्तिहतेत्वयि ।।6.41.80।।
transliteration: hantāsmitvāṃsahāmātyaṃsaputrajñātibāndhavam | nirudvignāstrayolokābhaviṣyantihatetvayi
translation: सहामात्यम् along with ministers, सपुत्रज्ञातिबान्धवम् sons, relatives and followers, त्वाम् you, हन्तास्मि been killed, त्वयि of you, हते killed, त्रयः three, लोकाः worlds, निरुद्विग्नाः rid of fear, भविष्यन्ति will become.
explanation: "You and your son's relatives and followers being killed (by me) the three worlds will be rid of fear of you."

shloka_text: देवदानवयक्षाणांगन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम् । शत्रुमद्योद्धरिष्यामित्वामृषीणांचकण्टकम् ।।6.41.81।।
transliteration: devadānavayakṣāṇāṃgandharvoragarakṣasām | śatrumadyoddhariṣyāmitvāmṛṣīṇāṃcakaṇṭakam
translation: देवदानवयक्षाणाम् gods, Danavas and Yakshas, गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम् Gandharvas, Nagas, शत्रुम् enemy, ऋषीणाम् for the sages, कण्टकंच thorn in the neck, त्वाम् you, अद्य being, उद्धरिष्यामि uproot you.
explanation: "You are an enemy of the gods, Danavas and Yakshas, Gandharvas and Nagas and being a thorn in the neck of sages, I will uproot you from here."

shloka_text: विभीषणस्यचैश्वर्यंभविष्यतिहतेत्वयि । नचेत्सत्कृत्यवैदेहींप्रणिपत्यप्रदास्यसि ।।6.41.82।।
transliteration: vibhīṣaṇasyacaiśvaryaṃbhaviṣyatihatetvayi | nacetsatkṛtyavaidehīṃpraṇipatyapradāsyasi
translation: प्रणिपत्य bowing down, वैदेहीम् Vaidehi, सत्कृत्य respectfully, नप्रदास्यसिचेत् not return back, त्वयि by you, हते being killed, ऐश्वर्यम् fortune, विभीषणस्य to Vibhishana, भविष्यति will be getting.
explanation: "Unless you return back Vaidehi respectfully, bowing down to me you will be killed and Vibheeshana will get the fortune."

shloka_text: इत्येवंपरुषंवाक्यंब्रुवाणेहरिपुङ्गवे । अमर्षवशमापन्नोनिशाचरगणेश्वरः ।।6.41.83।।
transliteration: ityevaṃparuṣaṃvākyaṃbruvāṇeharipuṅgave | amarṣavaśamāpannoniśācaragaṇeśvaraḥ
translation: हरिपुङ्गवे leader of monkey army, इत्येवम् in this way, परुषम् harsh, वाक्यम् words, ब्रुवाणे having spoken, निशाचरगणेश्वरः ruler of night rangers, अमर्षवशम् by fury, आपन्नः overtaken.
explanation: The leader of the monkeys having spoken in that manner, Ravana the ruler of night rangers was overtaken by fury.

shloka_text: ततस्सरोषताम्राक्षश्शशापसचिवांन्नोस्तदा । गृह्यतामेषदुर्मेधावध्यतामितिचासकृत् ।।6.41.84।।
transliteration: tatassaroṣatāmrākṣaśśaśāpasacivāṃnnostadā | gṛhyatāmeṣadurmedhāvadhyatāmiticāsakṛt
translation: ततः thereafter, रोषम् shaken by fury, आपन्नः overtaken, सः he, तदा then, एष in this way, सचिवान् ministers, असकृत् repeatedly, शशास commanded, दुर्मेधाः evil minded, गृह्यताम् seize him, वध्यताम् kill him.
explanation: Thereafter, Ravana who was shaken by fury repeatedly commanded his ministers and said 'Let this evil minded monkey be seized and killed'.

shloka_text: रावणस्यवच्शुत्वादीप्ताग्निसमतेजसा । जगृहुस्तंततोघोराश्चत्वारोरजनीचराः ।।6.41.85।।
transliteration: rāvaṇasyavacśutvādīptāgnisamatejasā | jagṛhustaṃtatoghorāścatvārorajanīcarāḥ
translation: ततः thereafter, घोराः terrific, चत्वारः four, रजनीचराः night rangers, रावणस्य of Ravana, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, समतेजसा of equal brilliance, दीप्ताग्नि blazing like fire, तम् him, Angada, जगृहुः seized.
explanation: Thereafter, having heard the words of Ravana, the four Rakshasas seized Angada blazing in brilliance like fire.

shloka_text: ग्राहयामासतारेयस्स्वयमात्मनमात्मवान् । बलंदर्शयितुंवीरोयातुधानगणेतदा ।।6.41.86।।
transliteration: grāhayāmāsatāreyassvayamātmanamātmavān | balaṃdarśayituṃvīroyātudhānagaṇetadā
translation: तदा then, आत्मवान् himself, वीरः heroic, तारेयः son of Tara, यातुधानगणे in the presence of Rakshasa army, बलम् strength, दर्शयितुम् to exhibit, स्वयम् on his own, आत्मानम् by his, ग्राहयामास allowed to be caught.
explanation: Then Angada, the son of Tara, on his own wanting to exhibit his strength in the presence of the Rakshasa army allowed himself to be caught.

shloka_text: सतान्बाहुद्वयासक्तानादायपतगानिव । प्रासादंशैलसङ्कामुत्पपाताङ्गदस्तदा ।।6.41.87।।
transliteration: satānbāhudvayāsaktānādāyapatagāniva | prāsādaṃśailasaṅkāmutpapātāṅgadastadā
translation: तदा then, सःअङ्गदः that Angada, बाहुद्वयसक्तान् holding the arms, तान् from that, पतगानिव like birds, आदाय came, शैलसङ्काशम् which stood like a mountain peak, प्रासादम् palace, उत्पपात came down.
explanation: Then Angada holding the Rakshasas by his arms came down like birds on the roof of the palace which stood like a mountain.

shloka_text: तेन्तरिक्षाद्विनिर्धूतास्तस्यवेगेनराक्षसाः । भूमौनिपतिताःसर्वेराक्षसेन्द्रस्यपश्यतः ।।6.41.88।।
transliteration: tentarikṣādvinirdhūtāstasyavegenarākṣasāḥ | bhūmaunipatitāḥsarverākṣasendrasyapaśyataḥ
translation: तेन by that, अन्तरिक्षात् from the sky, तस्य its, निर्धूता crushed, वेगेन speed, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य Rakshasa king's, तस्य from (the mountain), तत्र there, सर्वे all, भूमौ on the ground, निपतिताः fell.
explanation: Crushed by that speed of Angada coming down as if from the sky all the Rakshasas fell down on the ground while the Rakshasa king looked on.

shloka_text: ततःप्रासादशिखरंशैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम् । ददर्शराक्षसेन्द्रस्यवालिपुत्रःप्रतापवान् ।।6.41.89।।
transliteration: tataḥprāsādaśikharaṃśailaśṛṅgamivonnatam | dadarśarākṣasendrasyavāliputraḥpratāpavān
translation: ततः then, प्रतापवान् courageous, वालिपुत्रः Vali's son, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य at Ravana, शैलशृङ्गमिव like the peak of mountain, उन्नतम् high, प्रासादशिखरम् peak of the palace, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Then as the courageous Vali's son landed on the high peak of the palace which resembled a mountain peak, Ravana stood looking.

shloka_text: तत्पफालपदाक्रान्तंदशग्रीवस्यपश्यतः । पुराहिमवतश्शृङ्गंवज्रिणेवविदारितम् ।।6.41.90।।
transliteration: tatpaphālapadākrāntaṃdaśagrīvasyapaśyataḥ | purāhimavataśśṛṅgaṃvajriṇevavidāritam
translation: पदाक्रान्तम् trampled by, पुरा earlier, वज्रिण Indra, विदारितम् broken, हिमवतःशृङ्गमिव Himalayan peak, दशग्रीवस्य Ravana's, पश्यतः as he was looking, तत्पफाल cleft
explanation: As Ravana was looking, Angada trampling his feet gave way to the palace just as Himalayan peak broke to hit Indra.

shloka_text: भङ् क्त्वाप्रासादशिखरंनामविश्राव्यचात्मनः । विनद्यसुमहानादमुत्पपातविहायसम् ।।6.41.91।।
transliteration: bhaṅ ktvāprāsādaśikharaṃnāmaviśrāvyacātmanaḥ | vinadyasumahānādamutpapātavihāyasam
translation: प्रासादशिखरम् peak of the palace, भङ् क्त्वा hitting, आत्मनः his own, नाम name, विश्रान्य declaring, सुमहानादम् loud sound, विनद्य emitting, विहायसा into the sky, उत्पपात rose.
explanation: Hitting on the peak of the palace, Angada declaring his own name emitting loud sound rose up to the sky.

shloka_text: व्यथयन्राक्षसान्सर्वान्हर्षयंश्चापिवानरान् । सवानराणांमध्येतुरामपार्श्वमुपागतः ।।6.41.92।।
transliteration: vyathayanrākṣasānsarvānharṣayaṃścāpivānarān | savānarāṇāṃmadhyeturāmapārśvamupāgataḥ
translation: सः he, सर्वान् all, राक्षसान् Rakshasas, व्यथयन् causing pain, वानरान् Vanaras, हर्षयंश्चापि delighting, वानराणाम् to Vanaras, मध्ये midst, रामपार्श्वम् near Rama, उपागतः returned back.
explanation: Angada caused pain to the Rakshasas and delighted the monkeys and returned to the midst of Vanaras near Rama.

shloka_text: रावणस्तुपरंचक्रेक्रोधंप्रासादधर्षणात् । विनाशंचात्मनःपश्यन्निश्श्वासपरमोऽभवत् ।।6.41.93।।
transliteration: rāvaṇastuparaṃcakrekrodhaṃprāsādadharṣaṇāt | vināśaṃcātmanaḥpaśyanniśśvāsaparamo'bhavat
translation: रावणस्तु even Ravana, प्रासादधर्षणात् for shattering the palace, परम् very, क्रोधम् angry, चक्रे exhibiting, आत्मनः for him, विनाशम् destruction, पश्यन् seeing, निःश्वासपरमः sighing, अभवत् exhibited.
explanation: Ravana exhibiting extreme anger at the shattering of his palace and seeing his destruction started sighing heavily.

shloka_text: रामस्तुबहुभिर्हृष्टर्निनदद्भिःप्लवङ्गमैः । वृतोरिपुवधाकाङ्क्षीयुद्धायैवाभ्यवर्तत ।।6.41.94।।
transliteration: rāmastubahubhirhṛṣṭarninadadbhiḥplavaṅgamaiḥ | vṛtoripuvadhākāṅkṣīyuddhāyaivābhyavartata
translation: रामस्तु On Rama's part, हृष्टैः delighted, विनदद्भिः roaring like a lion, बहुभिः many, प्लवङ्गमैः monkey groups, वृतः surrounded, रिपुवधाकाङ्क्षी desirous of destruction of enemy, युद्धायैव for war, अभ्यवर्तत waiting.
explanation: Delighted by the roaring sound of many monkeys Rama awaited surrounded by groups of monkeys desirous of starting war.

shloka_text: सुषेणस्तुमहावीर्योगिरिकूटोपमोहरिः । बहुभिःसम्वृतस्तत्रवानरैःकामरूपिभिः ।।6.41.95।।
transliteration: suṣeṇastumahāvīryogirikūṭopamohariḥ | bahubhiḥsamvṛtastatravānaraiḥkāmarūpibhiḥ
translation: महावीर्यः of great prowess, गिरिकूटोपमः resembling mountain, हरिः Monkey, सुषेणस्तु Sushena also, तत्र there, कामरूपिभिः who change their form according to their will, बहुभिः many, वानरैः Vanaras, सम्वृतः surrounded.
explanation: Sushena of great prowess, who resembled a mountain in form stood there surrounded by many Vanaras who could change their form at their will.

shloka_text: सचतुर्द्वाराणिसर्वाणिसुग्रीववचनात्कपिः । पर्यक्रामतदुर्धर्षोनक्षत्राणीवचन्द्रमाः ।।6.41.96।।
transliteration: sacaturdvārāṇisarvāṇisugrīvavacanātkapiḥ | paryakrāmatadurdharṣonakṣatrāṇīvacandramāḥ
translation: दुर्धर्षः one who is difficult to encounter, कपिः monkey, सुग्रीववचनात् by the command of Sugriva, चतुर्द्वाराणि the four gates, सर्वाणि all, चन्द्रमाः moon, नक्षत्राणीव stars, पर्यक्रामत moves around.
explanation: Sushena, a monkey who is difficult to encounter, went around all the four gates just like the moon goes around stars by the order of Sugriva.

shloka_text: तेषामक्षौहिणिशतंसमवेक्ष्यवनौकसाम् । लङ्कामुपनिविष्टानांसागरंचानिवर्तताम् ।।6.41.97।। राक्षसाविस्मयंजग्मुस्त्रासंजग्मुस्तथापरे । अपरेसमरोध्धर्षाद्धर्षमेवप्रपेदिरे ।।6.41.98।।
transliteration: teṣāmakṣauhiṇiśataṃsamavekṣyavanaukasām | laṅkāmupaniviṣṭānāṃsāgaraṃcānivartatām  rākṣasāvismayaṃjagmustrāsaṃjagmustathāpare | aparesamarodhdharṣāddharṣamevaprapedire
translation: लङ्काम् उपनिविष्टानाम् staying near Lanka, सागरंच extending beyond the ocean, अनिवर्तताम् spreading beyond, तेषाम् them, वनौकसाम् Vanara army, अक्षौहिणिशतम् a hundred Akshauhinis, समवेक्ष्य collected together, राक्षसाः Rakshasas, विस्मयम् wonder struck, जग्मुः feared, अपरे alarmed, समरे war, हर्षात् joyful, हर्षमेव joy alone, प्रपेदिरे exhibited.
explanation: Seeing the large army of a hundred Akshauhinis of monkeys staying near Lanka spreading beyond the sea waiting for war the Rakshasas were wonder struck, some feared, some were alarmed to witness the jubilant Vanaras who exhibited joy alone.

shloka_text: तेषामक्षौहिणिशतंसमवेक्ष्यवनौकसाम् । लङ्कामुपनिविष्टानांसागरंचानिवर्तताम् ।।6.41.97।। राक्षसाविस्मयंजग्मुस्त्रासंजग्मुस्तथापरे । अपरेसमरोध्धर्षाद्धर्षमेवप्रपेदिरे ।।6.41.98।।
transliteration: teṣāmakṣauhiṇiśataṃsamavekṣyavanaukasām | laṅkāmupaniviṣṭānāṃsāgaraṃcānivartatām  rākṣasāvismayaṃjagmustrāsaṃjagmustathāpare | aparesamarodhdharṣāddharṣamevaprapedire
translation: लङ्काम् उपनिविष्टानाम् staying near Lanka, सागरंच extending beyond the ocean, अनिवर्तताम् spreading beyond, तेषाम् them, वनौकसाम् Vanara army, अक्षौहिणिशतम् a hundred Akshauhinis, समवेक्ष्य collected together, राक्षसाः Rakshasas, विस्मयम् wonder struck, जग्मुः feared, अपरे alarmed, समरे war, हर्षात् joyful, हर्षमेव joy alone, प्रपेदिरे exhibited.
explanation: Seeing the large army of a hundred Akshauhinis of monkeys staying near Lanka spreading beyond the sea waiting for war the Rakshasas were wonder struck, some feared, some were alarmed to witness the jubilant Vanaras who exhibited joy alone.

shloka_text: कृत्स्नंहिकपिभिर्व्याप्तंप्राकारपरिखान्तरम् । ददृशूराक्षसादीनाःप्राकारंनानरीकृतम् ।।6.41.99।। हाहाकारंप्रकुर्वन्तिराक्षसाभयमोहिताः ।
transliteration: kṛtsnaṃhikapibhirvyāptaṃprākāraparikhāntaram | dadṛśūrākṣasādīnāḥprākāraṃnānarīkṛtam  hāhākāraṃprakurvantirākṣasābhayamohitāḥ |
translation: राक्षसाः Rakshasa, दीनाः desperate, कपिभिः even monkeys, व्याप्तम् spread over, कृत्स्नम् dark, प्राकारपरिखान्तरम् entire area from the boundary and moat, नानरीकृतम् filled with monkeys, प्राकारम् boundary, ददृशुः saw, राक्षसाः Rakshasas, भयम् fear, आगताः reached, हाहाकारम् making noise, प्रकुर्वन्ति converted to defensive walls.
explanation: The Rakshasas were desperate to see the spread of monkeys over the entire area from the boundary to moat of Lanka. The way the space between was filled with Vanaras seemed as though the Vanaras converted into boundaries. Rakshasas were seen making a loud noise.

shloka_text: ततस्तेराक्षसास्तत्रगत्वारावणमन्दिरम् । न्यवेदयन्पुरींरुद्धांरामेणसहवानरैः ।।6.42.1।।
transliteration: tatasterākṣasāstatragatvārāvaṇamandiram | nyavedayanpurīṃruddhāṃrāmeṇasahavānaraiḥ
translation: तत then, राक्षसा Rakshasas, स्तत्र there, रावणमन्दिरम् Ravana's abode, गत्वा proceeding to, रामेण Rama's, वानरैः Vanaras, सह along with, रुद्धां occupied, न्यवेदय informed, न्पुरीं total city.
explanation: Then the Rakshasas proceeding to Ravana's abode informed that Rama along with the vanaras have occupied the whole of Lanka.
comments: Lanka is laid siege by the Vanara army. Ravana beholds the army of vanaras from the top of his palace. Rama and Lakshman take position of the Northern gate of Lanka. Ravana mobilizes his army and severe conflict takes place between Rakshasas and Vanara army.

shloka_text: रुद्धांतुनगरींश्रुत्वाजातक्रोधोनिशाचरः । विधानंद्विगुणंश्रुत्वाप्रासादंसोऽध्यरोहत ।।6.42.2।।
transliteration: ruddhāṃtunagarīṃśrutvājātakrodhoniśācaraḥ | vidhānaṃdviguṇaṃśrutvāprāsādaṃso'dhyarohata
translation: रुद्धां occupied, तु also, नगरीं city, श्रुत्वा hearing, जातक्रोधो very furious, निशाचरः night ranger, विधानं knowing, द्विगुणं twice, श्रुत्वा hearing, प्रासादं top of the mansion, अध्यरोहत planning for the protection of Lanka.
explanation: On knowing that Lanka is occupied, the night ranger Ravana, became very furious and doubled the forces of Lanka for the protection and went to the top of Lanka palace.

shloka_text: सददर्शावृतांलङ्कांसशैलवनकाननाम् । असङ्ख्येयैर्हरिगणैःसर्वतोयुद्धकाङ्क्षिभिः ।।6.42.3।।
transliteration: sadadarśāvṛtāṃlaṅkāṃsaśailavanakānanām | asaṅkhyeyairharigaṇaiḥsarvatoyuddhakāṅkṣibhiḥ
translation: स: he, युद्धकाङ्क्षिभिः desirous of combat, असङ्ख्येयै countless numbers, हर्रिगणैः troops of Vanaras, सशैलवनकाननाम् mountains and forests, सर्वतो all over, अवृतां occupied, लङ्कां Lanka, ददर्शा observed.
explanation: He observed a countless number of Vanara troops spread all over Lanka, mountains, and forests.

shloka_text: सदृष्ट्वावानरैःसर्वांवसुधांकवलीकृताम् । कथंक्षपयितव्याःस्युरितिचिन्तापरोऽभवत् ।।6.42.4।।
transliteration: sadṛṣṭvāvānaraiḥsarvāṃvasudhāṃkavalīkṛtām | kathaṃkṣapayitavyāḥsyuriticintāparo'bhavat
translation: स: he, वानरैः Vanaras, सर्वां all, वसुधां earth, कवलीकृताम् occupied, दृष्ट्वा seeing, कथं how, स्युरिति thought, क्षपयितव्याः to destroy, चिन्तापरो thinking, अभवत् started.
explanation: Seeing the Vanaras occupying the entire earth, Ravana thought of destroying and started thinking.

shloka_text: सचिन्तयित्वासुचिरंधैर्यमालम्ब्यरावणः । राघवंहरियूथांश्चददर्शायतलोचनः ।।6.42.5।।
transliteration: sacintayitvāsuciraṃdhairyamālambyarāvaṇaḥ | rāghavaṃhariyūthāṃścadadarśāyatalocanaḥ
translation: स: he, रावणः Ravana, सुचिरं for long, चिन्तयित्वा thinking over, धैर्यमालम्ब्य picking up courage, अयतलोचनः with thoughtful eyes, राघवं Raghava, हरियूथांश्च at the Vanaras, ददर्शा saw.
explanation: Ravana, thinking over for long, picking up courage, saw Rama's Vanaras with thoughtful eyes.

shloka_text: राघवःसहसैन्येनमुदितोनामपुप्लुवे । लङ्कांददर्शगुप्तांवैसर्वतोराक्षसैर्वृताम् ।।6.42.6।।
transliteration: rāghavaḥsahasainyenamuditonāmapupluve | laṅkāṃdadarśaguptāṃvaisarvatorākṣasairvṛtām
translation: राघवः Raghava, मुदितो happily, सहसैन्येन with army, पुप्लुवे near, लङ्कां Lanka, सर्वतो all over, राक्षसैर्वृताम् fully filled with Rakshasas, गुप्तांवै protected, लङ्कां Lanka, ददर्श witnessed.
explanation: Raghava accompanied by the army happily went near and witnessed Lanka filled with Rakshasas all over.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वादाशरथिर्लङ्कांचित्रध्वजपताकिनीम् । जगामसहसासीतांदूयमानेनचेतसा ।।6.42.7।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvādāśarathirlaṅkāṃcitradhvajapatākinīm | jagāmasahasāsītāṃdūyamānenacetasā
translation: दाशरथि son of Dasaratha, चित्रध्वजपताकिनीम् decorated with flags and posts, लङ्कां Lanka, चेतसा thinking, सीतां of Sita, दूयमानेन worried, सहसा very much, जगाम remained.
explanation: The son of Dasaratha saw Lanka decorated with flags and posts and thinking of Sita he became very worried.

shloka_text: अत्रसामृगशावाक्षीमत्कृतेजनकात्मजा । पीड्यतेशोकसन्तप्ताकृशास्थण्डिलशायिनी ।।6.42.8।।
transliteration: atrasāmṛgaśāvākṣīmatkṛtejanakātmajā | pīḍyateśokasantaptākṛśāsthaṇḍilaśāyinī
translation: अत्र here, सा she, मृगशावाक्षी dove eyed, जनकात्मजा Janaka's daughter, पीड्यते tormented, मत्कृते because of me, शोकसन्तप्ता immersed in sorrow, कृशा emaciated, स्थण्डिलशायिनी without food struggling.
explanation: "Here (Lanka) is the daughter of Janaka, immersed in sorrow because of me, tormented and emaciated without food and struggling."

shloka_text: पीड्यमानांसधर्मात्मावैदेहीमनुचिन्तयन् । क्षिप्रमाज्ञापयामासवानरान्द्विषतांवधे ।।6.42.9।।
transliteration: pīḍyamānāṃsadharmātmāvaidehīmanucintayan | kṣipramājñāpayāmāsavānarāndviṣatāṃvadhe
translation: धर्मात्मा righteous, स: he (Rama), पीड्यमानां pained, वैदेहीम Vaidehi, अचिन्तयन् thinking of very much, क्षिप्रमाज्ञापयामास immediately ordered, वानरान् Vanaras, द्विषतां enemies, वधे to kill.
explanation: Thinking of Vaidehi again and again, who is pained, Rama ordered the Vanaras to kill the enemies immediately.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तेतुवचनेरामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । संघर्षमाणाःप्लवगाःसिम्हनादैरनादयन् ।।6.42.10।।
transliteration: evamuktetuvacanerāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā | saṃgharṣamāṇāḥplavagāḥsimhanādairanādayan
translation: क्लिष्टकर्मणा one who does not cause sorrow, एवमुक्ते having ordered that way तु, वचने his words, प्लवगाः monkeys, संघर्षमाणाः getting ready for war, सिम्हनादैरनादयन् roared like a lion
explanation: Ordered in that way by Rama, who does not cause sorrow, the monkeys roared like lions getting ready for war on hearing Rama's words.

shloka_text: शिखरैर्विकिरामैनांलङ्कांमुष्टिभिरेववा । इतिस्मदधिरेसर्वेमनांसिहरियूथपाः ।।6.42.11।।
transliteration: śikharairvikirāmaināṃlaṅkāṃmuṣṭibhirevavā | itismadadhiresarvemanāṃsihariyūthapāḥ
translation: हरियूथपाः Vanara troops, लङ्कां Lanka, शिखरैर्विकिरामैनां with mountain peaks, मुष्टिभिरेववा or with fists, इति this, स्मदधिरे will crush, सर्वे all, मनांसि thought.
explanation: The monkey troops thought of crushing Lanka with their fists and mountain peaks.

shloka_text: उद्यम्यगिरिशृङ्गाणिशिखराणिमहान्तिच । तरूंश्चोत्पाट्यविविधांस्तिष्ठन्तिहरियूथपाः ।।6.42.12।।
transliteration: udyamyagiriśṛṅgāṇiśikharāṇimahāntica | tarūṃścotpāṭyavividhāṃstiṣṭhantihariyūthapāḥ
translation: हरियूथपाः Vanara leaders, गिरिशृङ्गाणि mountains, शिखराणि peaks, तरूंश्चोत्पाट्य holding trees, महान्तिच huge, विविधां many kinds, स्तिष्ठन्ति ready to fight.
explanation: Holding the mountain peaks, huge trees of many kinds, the Vanara leaders stood ready to fight.

shloka_text: प्रेक्षतोराक्षसेन्द्रस्यतान्यनीकानिभागशः । राघवप्रियकामार्थंलङ्कामारुरुहुस्तदा ।।6.42.13।।
transliteration: prekṣatorākṣasendrasyatānyanīkānibhāgaśaḥ | rāghavapriyakāmārthaṃlaṅkāmāruruhustadā
translation: राक्षसेन्द्रस्य king of Rakshasas, प्रेक्षतो as he was looking, तान्यनीकानि all the Vanara army, राघवप्रियकामार्थं to make Rama happy, भागशः in divisions, लङ्काम Lanka, आरुरुहुस्तदा ascended the boundary.
explanation: To make Rama happy, all the Vanara army divided into groups and started ascending the boundary (of Lanka) walls the king of Rakshasas was witnessing.

shloka_text: तेताम्रवक्त्राहेमाभारामार्थेत्यक्तजीविताः । लङ्कामेवाभ्यवर्तन्तसालतालशिलायुधाः ।।6.42.14।।
transliteration: tetāmravaktrāhemābhārāmārthetyaktajīvitāḥ | laṅkāmevābhyavartantasālatālaśilāyudhāḥ
translation: ताम्रवक्त्रा having copper colour faces, हेमाभा golden coloured, रामार्थे for the sake of Rama, त्यक्तजीविताः giving up life, सालतालशिलायुधाः Sala, Tala trees and rocks as weapons, लङ्कामेवाभ्यवर्तन्त went to Lanka.
explanation: Vanaras of copper colour faces and golden coloured ones, dedicating their lives for the sake of Rama holding Sala trees and rocks went towards Lanka.

shloka_text: तेद्रुमैःपर्वताग्रैश्चमुष्टिभिश्चप्लवङ्गमाः । प्राकाराग्राण्यरण्यानिममन्थुस्तोरणानिच ।।6.42.15।।
transliteration: tedrumaiḥparvatāgraiścamuṣṭibhiścaplavaṅgamāḥ | prākārāgrāṇyaraṇyānimamanthustoraṇānica
translation: ते they (Vanaras ), द्रुमैः trees, पर्वताग्रैश्च peaks of mountains, मुष्टिभिश्च even with fists, प्लवङ्गमाः monkeys, प्राकाराग्रा top of boundary, अरण्यानि forests, ममन्थुस्तोरणानिच gateways of the city
explanation: With the means of mountain peaks, as well as their fists, the Vanaras scaled the boundary walls and gateways of the city.

shloka_text: पारिखाःपूरयन्तिस्मप्रसन्नसलिलायुताः । पांसुभिःपर्वताग्रैश्चतृणैःकाष्ठैश्चवानराः ।।6.42.16 ।।
transliteration: pārikhāḥpūrayantismaprasannasalilāyutāḥ | pāṃsubhiḥparvatāgraiścatṛṇaiḥkāṣṭhaiścavānarāḥ
translation: वानराः Vanaras, पारिखाः with soil, पर्वताग्रैश्च with mountain peaks, तृणैः with grass, काष्ठैश्च wooden pieces, पांसुभिः moats also, प्रसन्नसलिलायुताः with pure water, पूरयन्ति filled.
explanation: The Vanaras started filling the moats with soil, pure water, logs of wood, grass, and mountain peaks.

shloka_text: ततःसहस्रयूथाश्चकोटीयूथाश्चवानराः । कोटीशतयुताश्चान्येलङ्कामारुरुहुस्तदा ।।6.42.17।।
transliteration: tataḥsahasrayūthāścakoṭīyūthāścavānarāḥ | koṭīśatayutāścānyelaṅkāmāruruhustadā
translation: ततः then, वानराः Vanaras, सहस्रयूथाश्च thousand, कोटीयूथाश्च one crore, कोटीशतयुताश्चान्ये hundred crores, लङ्काम into Lanka, आरुरुहुस्तदा ascended then.
explanation: Then the Vanaras in thousands and crores ascended Lanka.

shloka_text: काञ्चनानिप्रमृद्नन्तस्तोरणानिप्लवङ्गमाः । कैलासशिखराभानिगोपुराणिप्रमथ्यच ।।6.42.18।।
transliteration: kāñcanānipramṛdnantastoraṇāniplavaṅgamāḥ | kailāsaśikharābhānigopurāṇipramathyaca
translation: काञ्चनानि golden, प्रमृद्नन्तस्तोरणानि breaking the gateways, कैलासशिखराभानि like the peaks of Kailasa mountain, गोपुराणि towers, प्रमथ्यच crushing, प्लवङ्गमाः monkeys went.
explanation: The Vanaras started breaking the golden gateways and crushing them which were like peaks of Kailasa mountain.

shloka_text: आप्लवन्तःप्लवन्तश्चगर्जन्तश्चप्लवङ्गमाः । लङ्कांतामभिधावन्तिमहावारणसंनिभाः ।।6.42.19।।
transliteration: āplavantaḥplavantaścagarjantaścaplavaṅgamāḥ | laṅkāṃtāmabhidhāvantimahāvāraṇasaṃnibhāḥ
translation: आप्लवन्तः jumping here and there, महावारणसंनिभाः like huge elephants, प्लवन्तश्च Vanaras, गर्जन्तश्च roaring like lion, लङ्कांतामभिधावन्ति went up to Lanka.
explanation: Jumping here and there like huge elephants, the Vanaras roaring like lions went into Lanka.

shloka_text: जयत्यतिबलोरामोलक्ष्मणश्चमहाबलः । राजाजयतिसुग्रीवोराघवेणाभिपालितः ।।6.42.20।।
transliteration: jayatyatibalorāmolakṣmaṇaścamahābalaḥ | rājājayatisugrīvorāghaveṇābhipālitaḥ
translation: जयत्य victorious, अतिबलो exceedingly strong, रामो Rama, महाबलः endowed with supreme, strength, लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana also, राजा king, जयति victorious, सुग्रीवो Sugriva, राघवेण by Raghava, अभिपालितः protected by on all sides.
explanation: "Victorious is Sri Rama, who is exceedingly strong and Lakshmana who is endowed with supreme strength. Victorious is Sugriva the king of Vanaras who is protected by Raghava on all sides."

shloka_text: इत्येवंघोषयन्तश्चगर्जन्तश्चप्लवङ्गमाः । अभ्यधावन्तलङ्कायाःप्राकारंकामरूपिणः ।।6.42.21।।
transliteration: ityevaṃghoṣayantaścagarjantaścaplavaṅgamāḥ | abhyadhāvantalaṅkāyāḥprākāraṃkāmarūpiṇaḥ
translation: कामरूपिणः who could change their form at will, इत्येवं in this manner, घोषयन्तश्च shouting, गर्जन्तश्च roaring, लङ्कायाः into Lanka, प्राकारं defensive walls, अभ्यधावन्त rushed over.
explanation: Shouting in that manner, the monkeys who could change their form at their will started roaring and rushed towards the defensive walls.

shloka_text: वीरबाहुःसुबाहुश्चनलश्चवनगोचरः । निपीड्योपनिविष्टास्तेप्राकारंहरियूथपाः । एतस्मिन्नन्तरेचक्रुःस्कन्धावारनिवेशनम् ।।6.42.22 ।।
transliteration: vīrabāhuḥsubāhuścanalaścavanagocaraḥ | nipīḍyopaniviṣṭāsteprākāraṃhariyūthapāḥ | etasminnantarecakruḥskandhāvāraniveśanam
translation: वीरबाहुः Veerabahu, सुबाहुश्च and Subahu, नल Nala, वनगोचरः foremost of monkeys, निपीड्योप storming, निविष्टास्ते defensive, प्राकारं boundary walls, हरियूथपाः Vanara leaders, एतस्मिन्नन्तरे in the meantime inside, चक्रुः went, स्कन्धावारनिवेशनम् remained stationed at northeast.
explanation: Veerabahu, Subahu, Nala and the foremost of the Vanara leaders storming the boundary walls in the meantime went inside and stationed at the northeast gate.

shloka_text: पूर्वद्वारंतुकुमुदःकोटीभिर्दशभिर्वृतः । आवृत्यबलवांस्तस्थौहरिभिर्जितकाशिभिः ।।6.42.23।।
transliteration: pūrvadvāraṃtukumudaḥkoṭībhirdaśabhirvṛtaḥ | āvṛtyabalavāṃstasthauharibhirjitakāśibhiḥ
translation: कुमुदः Kumuda, तु also, कोटीभि one crore, र्दशभि ten, आर्वृतः surrounded by, पूर्वद्वारं east gate, आवृत्य surrounded, बलवां mighty, स्तस्थौ remained, हरिभि monkeys also, र्जितकाशिभिः appearing victorious.
explanation: Kumuda, surrounded by ten crores of mighty monkeys, who appeared like conquerors, stationed at the east gate.

shloka_text: साहाय्यार्थंतुतस्यैवनिविष्टःप्रघसोहरिः । पनसश्चमहाबाहुर्वानरैर्बहुभिर्वृतः ।।6.42.24।।
transliteration: sāhāyyārthaṃtutasyaivaniviṣṭaḥpraghasohariḥ | panasaścamahābāhurvānarairbahubhirvṛtaḥ
translation: प्रघसो Praghasa, हरिः monkey, महाबाहु broad shouldered, पनसश्च Panasa also, वानर Vanaras, साहाय्यार्थं for assisting, तस्यैव himself, निविष्टः encamped, बहुभि many, आर्वृतः surrounded.
explanation: Praghasa the broad shouldered Vanara, was surrounded by Panasa for assisting him who encamped surrounded by many.

shloka_text: दक्षिणंद्वारमागम्यवीरःशतबलिःकपिः । आवृत्यबलवांस्तस्थौविंशत्याकोटिभिर्वृतः ।।6.42.25।।
transliteration: dakṣiṇaṃdvāramāgamyavīraḥśatabaliḥkapiḥ | āvṛtyabalavāṃstasthauviṃśatyākoṭibhirvṛtaḥ
translation: वीरः valiant, शतबलिः Satabali, कपिः monkey, विंशत्या twenty, कोटिभि crores, आवृत्य surrounded by, बलवांस्तस्थौ stood besieging, दक्षिणं south, द्वारमागम्य reached the gate.
explanation: Valiant Satabali with twenty crores of monkeys stood besieging the south gate.

shloka_text: सुषेणःपश्चिमद्वारंगतस्तारापिताहरिः । आवृत्यबलवांस्तस्थौषष्टिकोटिभिरावृतः ।।6.42.26।।
transliteration: suṣeṇaḥpaścimadvāraṃgatastārāpitāhariḥ | āvṛtyabalavāṃstasthauṣaṣṭikoṭibhirāvṛtaḥ
translation: गतस्तारापिता father of Tara (wife of Vali), बलवांस्तस्थौ the mighty, सुषेणः Sushena, आवृत्य along with, षष्टिकोटिभिरावृतः sixty crores of monkeys surrounding, पश्चिमद्वारं at the western gate.
explanation: Sushena, father of Tara, (Vali's wife) the mighty, stood with sixty crores of monkeys at the western gate.

shloka_text: उत्तरंद्वारमासाद्यरामःसौमित्रिणासह । आवृत्यबलवांस्तस्थौसुग्रीवश्चहरीश्वरः ।।6.42.27।।
transliteration: uttaraṃdvāramāsādyarāmaḥsaumitriṇāsaha | āvṛtyabalavāṃstasthausugrīvaścaharīśvaraḥ
translation: उत्तरंद्वारमासाद्य reaching north gate, रामः Rama, सौमित्रिणा Saumithri, सह along with, आवृत्य accompanied by, बलवांस्तस्थौ blockading the gate, हरीश्वरः Lord of monkeys, सुग्रीवश्च Sugriva.
explanation: Reaching the north gate, Sri Rama along with Saumithri, blockading the gate stood Sugriva the Lord of monkeys.

shloka_text: गोलाङ्गूलोमहाकायोगवाक्षोभीमदर्शनः । वृतःकोट्यामहावीर्यस्तस्थौरामस्यपार्श्वतः ।।6.42.28।।
transliteration: golāṅgūlomahākāyogavākṣobhīmadarśanaḥ | vṛtaḥkoṭyāmahāvīryastasthaurāmasyapārśvataḥ
translation: महाकायो of gigantic body, गवाक्षो Gavaksha, भीमदर्शनः of fierce appearance, गोलाङ्गूलो Golangula species of monkeys, कोट्या crore, वृतः surrounded by, महावीर्यस्तस्थौ of extraordinary virility, रामस्य Rama's, पार्श्वतः by the side of.
explanation: Gavaksha of gigantic body and fierce appearance, along with one crore of Golangula species of monkeys endowed with extraordinary virility stood by the side of Sri Rama.

shloka_text: ऋक्षाणांभीमवेगानांधूम्रःशत्रुनिबर्हणः । वृतःकोट्यामहावीर्यस्तस्थौरामस्यपार्श्वतः ।।6.42.29।।
transliteration: ṛkṣāṇāṃbhīmavegānāṃdhūmraḥśatrunibarhaṇaḥ | vṛtaḥkoṭyāmahāvīryastasthaurāmasyapārśvataḥ
translation: वृतः accompanied by, कोट्या one crore, ऋक्षाणां bears, भीमवेगानां of redoubtable fury, धूम्रः Dhumra (brother of Jambavan), शत्रुनिबर्हणः exterminator of his foes, महावीर्यस्तस्थौ endowed with extraordinary valour, रामस्य Rama's, पार्श्वतः by the side of.
explanation: Accompanied by a crore of Bears of redoubtable fury, Dhumra (brother of Jambavan), an exterminator of foes endowed with extraordinary valour stood by Rama's side.

shloka_text: सन्नद्धस्तुमहावीर्योगदापाणिर्विभीषणः । वृतोयस्तैस्तुसचिवैस्तस्थौतत्रमहाबलः ।।6.42.30।।
transliteration: sannaddhastumahāvīryogadāpāṇirvibhīṣaṇaḥ | vṛtoyastaistusacivaistasthautatramahābalaḥ
translation: वृतो accompanied by, सन्नद्धस्तु defensive clamour, महावीर्यो of extraordinary virility, गदापाणि wielding mace, विर्भीषणः Vibheeshana, यस्तैस्तु stood, सचिवैस्तस्थौ with ministers stood, तत्र there, महाबलः mighty.
explanation: Vibheeshana with defensive clamour, of extraordinary virility accompanied by his mighty ministers, stood there with his mace in hand.

shloka_text: गजोगवाक्षोगवयःशरभोगन्धमादनः । समन्तात्परिधावन्तोररक्षुर्हरिवाहिनीम् ।।6.42.31।।
transliteration: gajogavākṣogavayaḥśarabhogandhamādanaḥ | samantātparidhāvantorarakṣurharivāhinīm
translation: गजो Gaja, गवाक्षो Gavaksha, गवयः Gava, शरभ Sarabha, गन्धमादनः Gandamadhana, मन्तात्परिधावन्तो all over wandering, ररक्षु protecting, हर्रिवाहिनीम् monkey troops.
explanation: Gaja, Gavaksha, Gava, Sarabha, Gandhamadana stood protecting the monkey troops wandering all over.

shloka_text: ततःकोपपरीतात्मारावणोराक्षसेश्वरः । निर्याणंसर्वसैन्यानांद्रुतमाज्ञापयत्तदा ।।6.42.32।।
transliteration: tataḥkopaparītātmārāvaṇorākṣaseśvaraḥ | niryāṇaṃsarvasainyānāṃdrutamājñāpayattadā
translation: ततः thereafter, राक्षसेश्वरः Lord of Rakshasas, रावण Ravana, सर्वसैन्यानां all his forces, निर्याणं to depart, कोपपरीतात्मा overcome by fury, द्रुत to advance, आज्ञापयत्तदा ordered.
explanation: Thereafter Ravana, the Lord of Rakshasas overcome by fury ordered all his forces to advance.

shloka_text: एतच्छ्रुत्वाततोवाक्यंरावणस्यमुखोद्गतम् । सहसाभीमनिर्घोषमुद्घुष्टंरजनीचरैः ।।6.42.33।।
transliteration: etacchrutvātatovākyaṃrāvaṇasyamukhodgatam | sahasābhīmanirghoṣamudghuṣṭaṃrajanīcaraiḥ
translation: रावणस्य from Ravana's, मुखोद्गतम् command issued from his mouth, एतच्छ्रुत्वा as soon as it was heard, ततो that, वाक्यं words. सहसा instantly, भीमनिर्घोषमुद्घुष्टं terrific roar, रजनीचरैः night rangers.
explanation: Hearing the command issued from Ravana's mouth, immediately a terrific roar was raised by the night rangers.

shloka_text: ततःप्रचोदिताभेर्यश्चन्द्रपाण्डरपुष्कराः । हेमकोणाहताभीमाराक्षसानांसमन्ततः ।।6.42.34।।
transliteration: tataḥpracoditābheryaścandrapāṇḍarapuṣkarāḥ | hemakoṇāhatābhīmārākṣasānāṃsamantataḥ
translation: ततः then, प्रचोदिता shone, भेर्यश्चन्द्र like the moon, पाण्डरपुष्कराः white discs, भीमा terrific, राक्षसानां Rakshasas, हेमकोणाहता gold sticks.
explanation: Then shone the white discs like the moon beaten by the Rakshasas with gold sticks making terrific sound.

shloka_text: विनेदुश्चमहाघोषाःशङ्खाःशतसहस्रशः । राक्षसानांसुघोराणांमुखमारुतपूरिताः ।।6.42.35।।
transliteration: vineduścamahāghoṣāḥśaṅkhāḥśatasahasraśaḥ | rākṣasānāṃsughorāṇāṃmukhamārutapūritāḥ
translation: राक्षसानां Rakshasas, सुघोराणां terrific sounds, शतसहस्रशः hundred thousand, महाघोषाः loud noise, शङ्खाः with conchs, विनेदुश्च sonorous, मुखमारुत with wind from their mouth, पूरिताः blown.
explanation: With hundred thousand Rakshasas blowing sonorous conchs, with the wind from their mouths, terrific noise arose.

shloka_text: तेबभुःशुभनीलाङ्गाःसशङ्खारजनीचराः । विद्युन्मण्डलसन्नद्धाःसबलाकाइवाम्बुदाः ।।6.42.36।।
transliteration: tebabhuḥśubhanīlāṅgāḥsaśaṅkhārajanīcarāḥ | vidyunmaṇḍalasannaddhāḥsabalākāivāmbudāḥ
translation: ते they, बभुः brilliant, शुभनीलाङ्गाः dark limbs, रजनीचराः night rangers, सशङ्खा with conches, इवाम्बुदाः like clouds, विद्युन्मण्डलसन्नद्धाः provided with armour with flashes of lightning, सबलाका accompanied by herons.
explanation: The night rangers with their brilliant dark limbs, with conchs, were like dark clouds provided with armour with flashes of lightning and accompanied by herons.

shloka_text: निष्पतन्तिततःसैन्याहृष्टारावणचोदिताः । समयेपूर्यमाणस्यवेगाइवमहोदधेः ।।6.42.37।।
transliteration: niṣpatantitataḥsainyāhṛṣṭārāvaṇacoditāḥ | samayepūryamāṇasyavegāivamahodadheḥ
translation: रावणचोदिताः urged by Ravana, सैन्या army, ततः then, हृष्टा joyfully, निष्पतन्ति rushed forth, वेगा swiftly, महोदधेः great ocean, इव like, समये at the time of, पूर्यमाणस्य universal destruction.
explanation: Urged by Ravana, the army then joyfully rushed forth swiftly like a great ocean at the time of universal destruction.

shloka_text: ततोवानरसैन्येनमुक्तोनादःसमन्ततः । मलयःपूरितोयेनससानुप्रस्थकन्दरः ।।6.42.38।।
transliteration: tatovānarasainyenamuktonādaḥsamantataḥ | malayaḥpūritoyenasasānuprasthakandaraḥ
translation: ततो thereafter, वानरसैन्येन by the Vanara army, मुक्तो emitted, नादः sound, समन्ततः on all sides, पूरितो filled, मलयः Malaya mountain, येन by that, स that, सानुप्रस्थकन्दरः major and minor peaks and caves.
explanation: Thereafter the Vanara army emitted a sound that filled all sides of Malaya Mountain, its major and minor caves.

shloka_text: शङ्खदुन्दुभिसंघुष्टःसिम्हनादस्तरस्विनाम् । पृथिवींचान्तरिक्षंचसागरंचैवनादयन् ।।6.42.39।।
transliteration: śaṅkhadundubhisaṃghuṣṭaḥsimhanādastarasvinām | pṛthivīṃcāntarikṣaṃcasāgaraṃcaivanādayan
translation: शङ्खदुन्दुभिसंघुष्टः blast of conchs and roll of drums, सिम्हनाद roar of lions, स्तरस्विनाम् and of Vanara and Rakshasa heroes, पृथिवीं earth, चान्तरिक्षंच to sky, सागरंचैव up to ocean, नादयन् resounded.
explanation: By the blast of conchs and roll of drums, and roar of lions of Vanara and Rakshasa forces it resounded all over the earth, sky and up to the ocean.

shloka_text: गजानांबृंहितैःसार्धंहयानांहेषितैरपि । रथानांनेमिघोषैश्चरक्षसाम्वदनस्वनः ।।6.42.40 ।।
transliteration: gajānāṃbṛṃhitaiḥsārdhaṃhayānāṃheṣitairapi | rathānāṃnemighoṣaiścarakṣasāmvadanasvanaḥ
translation: गजानां of elephants, बृंहितैः trumpeting, सार्धंहयानां neighing of horses, हेषितैरपि clatter of wheels, रथानां of chariots, नेमिघोषैश्च shout of, रक्षसाम्, Rakshasas, वदनस्वनः resounded in the air.
explanation: The trumpeting of the elephants, the neighing of horses, the clatter of the wheels of the chariots and the shout of Rakshasas resounded in the air.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेघोरःसङ्ग्रामःसमवर्तत । रक्षसांवानराणांचयथादेवासुरेपुरा ।।6.42.41।।
transliteration: etasminnantareghoraḥsaṅgrāmaḥsamavartata | rakṣasāṃvānarāṇāṃcayathādevāsurepurā
translation: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे in the meantime, घोरः dreadful, सङ्ग्रामः conflict, समवर्तत all over, रक्षसां Rakshasas, वानराणांच between Vanaras, यथादेवासुरे like the conflict between Devas and asuras, पुरा earlier.
explanation: In the meantime, dreadful conflict arose all over between Rakshasas and Vanaras, which was like the conflict between Devas and asuras earlier.

shloka_text: तेगदाभिःप्रदीप्ताभिःशक्तिशूलपरश्वधैः । निजघ्नुर्वानरान्घोराःकथयन्तःस्वविक्रमान् ।।6.42.42।।
transliteration: tegadābhiḥpradīptābhiḥśaktiśūlaparaśvadhaiḥ | nijaghnurvānarānghorāḥkathayantaḥsvavikramān
translation: ते the Rakshasas, स्वविक्रमान् vaunting their own prowess, गदाभिः with maces, प्रदीप्ताभिः flaming शक्तिशूलपरश्वधैः with javelins, tridents and pikes, निजघ्नु fiercely struck, नरान्घोराः at Vanaras, कथयन्तः attacked.
explanation: Vowing their own prowess, the Rakshasas began to strike the Vanaras with maces, flaming javelins, tridents, and pikes fiercely.

shloka_text: राजाजयतिसुग्रीवइतिशब्दोमहानभूत् । राजन्जयजयेत्युक्त्वास्वस्वनामकथान्ततः ।।6.42.43।।
transliteration: rājājayatisugrīvaitiśabdomahānabhūt | rājanjayajayetyuktvāsvasvanāmakathāntataḥ
translation: राजा king, जयति victory, सुग्रीव Sugriva, इति thus, शब्दो sound, महानभूत् be triumphant, राजन् king, जय victorious, जयेत्युक्त्वा saying victory to you, स्वस्वनामकथान्ततः arose war cry from the Vanaras.
explanation: "May the vanara king,triumphant Sugriva be victorious", thus sounded the cry of vanaras in the battlefield.

shloka_text: तथावृक्षैर्महाकायाःपर्वताग्रैश्चवानराः । निजघ्नुस्तानिरक्षांसिनखैर्दन्तैश्चवेगिताः ।।6.42.44।।
transliteration: tathāvṛkṣairmahākāyāḥparvatāgraiścavānarāḥ | nijaghnustānirakṣāṃsinakhairdantaiścavegitāḥ
translation: तथा in the same manner, वृक्षैर्महाकायाः with trees, पर्वताग्रैश्च with mountain peaks, वानराः Vanaras, रक्षांसि at Rakshasas, नखैर्दन्तैश्च with nails and teeth, निजघ्नुस्तानि attacked, वेगिताः swiftly.
explanation: Vanaras in the same manner attacked the Rakshasas, with trees and mountains, swiftly and with their nails and teeth.

shloka_text: राक्षसास्त्वपरेभीमाःप्राकारस्थामहीगतान् । भिन्दिपालैश्चखड्गैश्चशूलैश्चैवव्यदारयन् ।।6.42.45।।
transliteration: rākṣasāstvaparebhīmāḥprākārasthāmahīgatān | bhindipālaiścakhaḍgaiścaśūlaiścaivavyadārayan
translation: राक्षसास्त्वपरे redoubtable Rakshasas, प्राकारस्था standing on the walls, भीमाः dreadful, भिन्दिपालैश्च Bhindipalas (javelin like weapons), खड्गैश्च and swords, शूलैश्चैव with tridents, व्यदारयन् pierced.
explanation: Standing on the walls, the redoubtable Rakshasas, pierced the Vanaras with swords, dreadful Bhindipalas.

shloka_text: वानराश्चापिसङ्क्रुद्धाःप्राकारस्थान्महीगताः । राक्षसान्पातयामासुःसमाप्लुत्यप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.42.46।।
transliteration: vānarāścāpisaṅkruddhāḥprākārasthānmahīgatāḥ | rākṣasānpātayāmāsuḥsamāplutyaplavaṅgamāḥ
translation: प्राकारस्थान्महीगताः stationed on the boundary walls, वानराश्चापि Vanaras also, राक्षसान्पातयामासुः dragged down the Rakshasas, प्लवङ्गमाः monkeys, समाप्लुत्य jumping up.
explanation: The vanaras jumping up dragged the Rakshasas stationed on the boundary wall down to the ground.

shloka_text: ससम्प्रहारस्तुमुलोमांसशोणितकर्दमः । रक्षसांवानराणांचसम्बभूवाद्भुतोपमाः।।6.42.47।।
transliteration: sasamprahārastumulomāṃsaśoṇitakardamaḥ | rakṣasāṃvānarāṇāṃcasambabhūvādbhutopamāḥ
translation: स that, सम्प्रहार conflict, रक्षसां of Rakshasas, वानराणांच and Vanaras, तमुलो intense, मांस flesh, शोणित blood, कर्दमः like mire, सम्बभूवा that happened, अद्भुतोपमाः was amazing.
explanation: The conflict that happened between the Rakshasas and Vanaras was amazing and intense and left a mire of flesh and blood. ।। इत्यार्षेश्रीमद्वाल्मीकिरामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेद्विचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty second sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: युध्यतांतुततस्तेषांवानराणांमहात्मनाम् । रक्षसांसम्बभूवाथबलकोपस्सुदारुणः ।।6.43.1।।
transliteration: yudhyatāṃtutatasteṣāṃvānarāṇāṃmahātmanām | rakṣasāṃsambabhūvāthabalakopassudāruṇaḥ
translation: ततः thereafter, महात्मानाम् gigantic, तेषांवानराणाम् those Vanaras, रक्षसांच and Rakshasas, युध्यताम् waging war, अथ while, सुदारुणः exceedingly terrific, बलरोषः anguished, सम्बभूव could not tolerate the sight.
explanation: Thereafter the gigantic army of Vanaras were fighting with exceedingly terrific Rakshasas and the anguished Rakshasas could not tolerate the sight.
comments: In the course of conflict between Rakshasas and Vanaras Angada fights with Indrajith. Other Rakshasas are lopped off by Rama and Nikumbha by Neela. Sushena kills Vidyunmali.

shloka_text: तेहयैःकाञ्चनापीडैर्ध्वश्चाग्निशिखोपमैः । रथैश्चादित्यसङ्काशैःकवचैश्चमनोरमैः ।।6.43.2।। निर्ययूराक्षसव्याघ्रानादयन्तोदिशोदश । राक्षसाभीमकर्माणोरावणस्यजयैषिणः ।।6.43.3।।
transliteration: tehayaiḥkāñcanāpīḍairdhvaścāgniśikhopamaiḥ | rathaiścādityasaṅkāśaiḥkavacaiścamanoramaiḥ  niryayūrākṣasavyāghrānādayantodiśodaśa | rākṣasābhīmakarmāṇorāvaṇasyajayaiṣiṇaḥ
translation: रावणस्य for Ravana, जयैषिणः desiring victory, राक्षसव्याघ्राः tiger among Rakshasas, भीमकर्माणः of terrible deeds, तेराक्षसाः those Rakshasas, काञ्चनापीडैः provided with golden trappings, हयैः horses, अग्निशिखोपमैः like flames of fire, ऊर्ध्वैः posts, आदित्यसङ्काशैः shining like sun's rays, रथैः chariots, मनोरमैः delightful, कवचैश्च shields, दश ten, दिशः directions, नादयन्तः resounding, निर्ययुः sallied forth.
explanation: Wishing victory for Ravana, the tiger among ogres, the Rakshasas of terrific deeds sallied forth accompanied by horses with golden trappings and seizing posts, which were like flames of fire shining like the sun's rays on the chariots and delightful shields, roaring resounding in all the ten directions.

shloka_text: तेहयैःकाञ्चनापीडैर्ध्वश्चाग्निशिखोपमैः । रथैश्चादित्यसङ्काशैःकवचैश्चमनोरमैः ।।6.43.2।। निर्ययूराक्षसव्याघ्रानादयन्तोदिशोदश । राक्षसाभीमकर्माणोरावणस्यजयैषिणः ।।6.43.3।।
transliteration: tehayaiḥkāñcanāpīḍairdhvaścāgniśikhopamaiḥ | rathaiścādityasaṅkāśaiḥkavacaiścamanoramaiḥ  niryayūrākṣasavyāghrānādayantodiśodaśa | rākṣasābhīmakarmāṇorāvaṇasyajayaiṣiṇaḥ
translation: रावणस्य for Ravana, जयैषिणः desiring victory, राक्षसव्याघ्राः tiger among Rakshasas, भीमकर्माणः of terrible deeds, तेराक्षसाः those Rakshasas, काञ्चनापीडैः provided with golden trappings, हयैः horses, अग्निशिखोपमैः like flames of fire, ऊर्ध्वैः posts, आदित्यसङ्काशैः shining like sun's rays, रथैः chariots, मनोरमैः delightful, कवचैश्च shields, दश ten, दिशः directions, नादयन्तः resounding, निर्ययुः sallied forth.
explanation: Wishing victory for Ravana, the tiger among ogres, the Rakshasas of terrific deeds sallied forth accompanied by horses with golden trappings and seizing posts, which were like flames of fire shining like the sun's rays on the chariots and delightful shields, roaring resounding in all the ten directions.

shloka_text: वानराणामपिचमूर्बृहतीजयमिच्छताम् । अभ्यधावततांसेनांरक्षसांकामरूपिणम् ।।6.43.4।।
transliteration: vānarāṇāmapicamūrbṛhatījayamicchatām | abhyadhāvatatāṃsenāṃrakṣasāṃkāmarūpiṇam
translation: जयम् triumph, इच्छताम् wishing, वानराणाम् Vanaras, बृहती powerful, चमूःअपि army too, घोरकर्मणाम् of terrible deeds, रक्षसाम् Rakshasas, तांसेनाम् those army, अभ्यधावत went ahead.
explanation: Wishing triumph even the powerful army of powerful Vanaras of terrific deeds went ahead to fight with Rakshasas.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेतेषामन्योन्यमभिधावताम् । रक्षसांवानराणांचद्वन्द्वयुद्धमवर्तत ।।6.43.5।।
transliteration: etasminnantareteṣāmanyonyamabhidhāvatām | rakṣasāṃvānarāṇāṃcadvandvayuddhamavartata
translation: एतस्मिन् अन्तरे at that time, अन्योन्यम् one another, अभिधावताम् facing one over the other, तेषाम् those, रक्षसाम् Rakshasas, वानराणांच and Vanaras, द्वन्द्वयुद्धम् duel fight, आवर्तत began.
explanation: At that time the Vanaras and Rakshasas facing each other started a dual fight.

shloka_text: अङ्गदेन्द्रजित्सार्धंवालिपुत्रेणराक्षसः । आयुध्यतमहातेजास्त्ऱ्यम्बकेणयथाऽन्तकः ।।6.43.6।।
transliteration: aṅgadendrajitsārdhaṃvāliputreṇarākṣasaḥ | āyudhyatamahātejāstṟyambakeṇayathā'ntakaḥ
translation: महातेजाः exceedingly brilliant, राक्षसः Rakshasa, इन्द्रजित् Indrajith, वालिपुत्रेण with Vali's son, अङ्गदेव Angada, सार्धम् contended with, अन्तकः and haka, स्त्ऱ्यम्बकेणयथा like Lord Siva with Lord of death, अयुध्यत fought
explanation: Indrajith, an exceedingly brilliant Rakshasa, contended with Angada, son of Vali just like Lord Siva with and haka, the Lord of death.

shloka_text: प्रजङ्घेनचसम्पातिर्नित्यंदुर्मर्षणोरणे । जम्बुमालिनमारब्धोहनुमानपिवानरः ।।6.43.7।।
transliteration: prajaṅghenacasampātirnityaṃdurmarṣaṇoraṇe | jambumālinamārabdhohanumānapivānaraḥ
translation: रणे in war, नित्यम् invariably, दुर्मर्षणः difficult to encounter, सम्पातिः Sampathi, प्रजङ्घेन Prajangha, वानरः Vanara, हनुमानपि Hanuman, जम्बुमालिनम् with Jambumali, आरब्दः started.
explanation: Sampathi , who is invariably difficult to encounter in war fought with Prajangha, and Hanuman started with Jambumali.

shloka_text: संगतस्तुमहाक्रोधोराक्षसोरावणानुजः । समरेतीक्ष्णवेगेनमित्रघ्नेनविभीषणः ।।6.43.8।।
transliteration: saṃgatastumahākrodhorākṣasorāvaṇānujaḥ | samaretīkṣṇavegenamitraghnenavibhīṣaṇaḥ
translation: महाक्रोधः highly furious, रावणानुजः Ravana's brother, राक्षसः Rakshasa, विभीषणः Vibheeshana, समरे in war, तीक्ष्णवेगेन endowed with high speed, मित्रघ्नेन Mitraghna, सङ्गतः contended.
explanation: Highly furious Rakshasa, Vibheeshana, brother of Ravana fought with Rakshasa, Mitraghna.

shloka_text: तपनेनगजस्सार्धंराक्षसेनमहाबलः । निकुम्भेनमहातेजानीलोऽपिसमयुध्यत ।।6.43.9।।
transliteration: tapanenagajassārdhaṃrākṣasenamahābalaḥ | nikumbhenamahātejānīlo'pisamayudhyata
translation: महाबलः of great strength, गजः Gaja, तपनेन with Tapa, राक्षसेनसार्धम् with Rakshasa, महातेजाः highly energetic, नीलोऽपि Neela too, निकुम्बेन with Nikumbha, समयुध्यत fought with each other.
explanation: Gaja of great strength fought with Rakshasa Tapa, and highly energetic Neela fought with Nikumbha.

shloka_text: वानरेन्द्रस्तुसुग्रीवःप्रघसेनसमागतः । सङ्गतःसमरेश्रीमान्विरूपाक्षेणलक्ष्मणः ।।6.43.10।।
transliteration: vānarendrastusugrīvaḥpraghasenasamāgataḥ | saṅgataḥsamareśrīmānvirūpākṣeṇalakṣmaṇaḥ
translation: वानरेन्द्र Lord of Vanaras, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, प्रघनेन with Praghana, समागतः encountered, श्रीमान् prosperous, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, विरूपाक्षेण Virupaksha, समरे in war, सङ्गतः encountered.
explanation: Sugriva the Lord of Vanaras fought with Praghana and prosperous Lakshmana fought with Virupaksha.

shloka_text: अग्निकेतुश्चसुदुर्धर्षोरश्मिकेतुश्चराक्षसः । सुप्तघ्नोयज्ञकोपश्चरामेणसहसङ्गताः ।।6.43.11।।
transliteration: agniketuścasudurdharṣoraśmiketuścarākṣasaḥ | suptaghnoyajñakopaścarāmeṇasahasaṅgatāḥ
translation: सुदुर्धर्षः difficult to win over, अग्निकेतुः Agnikethu, राक्षसः Rakshasa, रश्मिकेतुश्च and Rasmikethu, सुप्तघ्नुः Suptaghna, यज्ञकेपश्च Yajnakepu, रामेणसह along with Rama, सङ्गताः waged.
explanation: Agnikethu, a Rakshasa who is difficult to win over, Rasmikethu, Suptaghna and Yajnakepu waged war with Rama.

shloka_text: वज्रमुष्टिस्तुमैन्देनद्विविदेनाशनिप्रभः । राक्षसाभ्यांसुघोराभ्यांकपिमुख्यौसमागतौ ।।6.43.12।।
transliteration: vajramuṣṭistumaindenadvividenāśaniprabhaḥ | rākṣasābhyāṃsughorābhyāṃkapimukhyausamāgatau
translation: वज्रमुष्टिः Vajramushti, तु also, मैन्देन with Mainda, अशनिप्रभः Asaniprabhu, द्विविदेन with Dwivida कपिमुख्यौ chief of monkeys, सुघोराभ्याम् fearful, राक्षसाभ्याम् with the two Rakshasas, समागतौ fought.
explanation: Vajramushti with Mainda and Asaniprabhu with Dwivida, the chief of monkeys, fought with the two Rakshasas.

shloka_text: वीरःप्रतपनोघोरोराक्षसोरणदुर्धरः । समरेतीक्ष्णवेगेननळेनसमयुध्यत ।।6.43.13।।
transliteration: vīraḥpratapanoghororākṣasoraṇadurdharaḥ | samaretīkṣṇavegenanaḻenasamayudhyata
translation: वीरः heroic, घोरः dreadful, रणदुर्धरः indomitable in war, प्रतपनः Pratapana, समरे in battle, तीक्ष्णवेगेन with high speed, नळेन Nala, समयुध्यत fought with.
explanation: Heroic and dreadful Pratapana, who is indomitable in the battle, fought with Nala endowed with high speed.

shloka_text: धर्मस्यपुत्रोबलवान्सुषेणइतिविश्रुतः । सविद्युन्मालिनासार्धमयुध्यतमहाकपिः ।।6.43.14।। वानराश्चापरेभीमाराक्षसैरपरैस्सह । द्वन्द्वंसमीयुस्सहसायुद्धायबहुभिस्सह ।।6.43.15।।
transliteration: dharmasyaputrobalavānsuṣeṇaitiviśrutaḥ | savidyunmālināsārdhamayudhyatamahākapiḥ  vānarāścāparebhīmārākṣasairaparaissaha | dvandvaṃsamīyussahasāyuddhāyabahubhissaha
translation: धर्मस्यपुत्रो righteous son, बलवान्सुषेण of mighty Sushena, इति so also, विश्रुतः well known, सविद्युन्मालिना with Vidyunmali, सार्धमयुध्यत fought with, महाकपिः great monkey, घोराः fierce, अपरे other, वानराश्च Vanaras also, बहुभिःसह along with many, युद्धायच fought in war, अपरैः, राक्षसैःसह Rakshasas also, द्वन्द्वंसमीयुः duel fight.
explanation: Mighty Sushena, the righteous son fought with well known Vidyunmali. And fierce monkeys and Rakshasas fought in dual war with each other.

shloka_text: धर्मस्यपुत्रोबलवान्सुषेणइतिविश्रुतः । सविद्युन्मालिनासार्धमयुध्यतमहाकपिः ।।6.43.14।। वानराश्चापरेभीमाराक्षसैरपरैस्सह । द्वन्द्वंसमीयुस्सहसायुद्धायबहुभिस्सह ।।6.43.15।।
transliteration: dharmasyaputrobalavānsuṣeṇaitiviśrutaḥ | savidyunmālināsārdhamayudhyatamahākapiḥ  vānarāścāparebhīmārākṣasairaparaissaha | dvandvaṃsamīyussahasāyuddhāyabahubhissaha
translation: धर्मस्यपुत्रो righteous son, बलवान्सुषेण of mighty Sushena, इति so also, विश्रुतः well known, सविद्युन्मालिना with Vidyunmali, सार्धमयुध्यत fought with, महाकपिः great monkey, घोराः fierce, अपरे other, वानराश्च Vanaras also, बहुभिःसह along with many, युद्धायच fought in war, अपरैः, राक्षसैःसह Rakshasas also, द्वन्द्वंसमीयुः duel fight.
explanation: Mighty Sushena, the righteous son fought with well known Vidyunmali. And fierce monkeys and Rakshasas fought in dual war with each other.

shloka_text: तत्रासीत्सुमहद्युद्धंतुमुलंरोमहर्षणम् । रक्षसांवानराणांचवीराणांजयमिच्छताम् ।।6.43.16।।
transliteration: tatrāsītsumahadyuddhaṃtumulaṃromaharṣaṇam | rakṣasāṃvānarāṇāṃcavīrāṇāṃjayamicchatām
translation: तत्र there, जयम् victory, इच्छताम् longing, वीराणाम् heroes, रक्षसाम् Rakshasas, वानराणांच and Vanaras, रोमहर्षणम् fierce which made hair stand on end, तुमुलम् confused, सुमहत् great, युद्धम् war, आसीत् happened.
explanation: Fierce war which made hair stand on end happened there, with the heroic Rakshasas and Vanaras longing for victory.

shloka_text: हरिराक्षसदेहेभ्यःप्रभूताःकेशशाद्वलाः । शरीरसङ्घाटावहाःप्रसुस्रुश्शोणितापगाः ।।6.43.17।।
transliteration: harirākṣasadehebhyaḥprabhūtāḥkeśaśādvalāḥ | śarīrasaṅghāṭāvahāḥprasusruśśoṇitāpagāḥ
translation: हरिराक्षसदेहेभ्यः from the body of Rakshasas and Vanaras, प्रभूताः come out, केशशाद्वलाः in the form of hair, शरीरसङ्घाटवहाः the dead bodies like logs of wood, शोणितापगाः streams of blood, प्रसुस्रुः flown.
explanation: In that war, the streams of blood that flowed from the bodies of Vanaras and Rakshasas were strewn like weeds in the form of hair, bearing logs of wood in the form of dead bodies.

shloka_text: अजघानेन्द्रजित्क्रुद्धोवज्रेणेवशतक्रतुः । अङ्गदंगदयावीरंशत्रुसैन्यविदारणम् ।।6.43.18।।
transliteration: ajaghānendrajitkruddhovajreṇevaśatakratuḥ | aṅgadaṃgadayāvīraṃśatrusainyavidāraṇam
translation: क्रुद्धः enraged, इन्द्रजित् Indrajith, शतक्रतुः who has done a hundred sacrifices, वज्रेणेव Indra thunderbolt, गदया mace, शत्रुसैन्यविदारणम् destroyer of hostile forces, वीरम् heroic, अङ्गदम् Angada, आजघान struck.
explanation: Enraged, Indrajith struck Angada with his mace, the destroyer of hostile forces which was like Indra who had done a hundred sacrifices, would strike with his thunderbolt.

shloka_text: तस्यकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गंरथंसाश्वंससारथिम् । जघानसमरेश्रीमानङ्गदोवेगवान्कपिः ।।6.43.19।।
transliteration: tasyakāñcanacitrāṅgaṃrathaṃsāśvaṃsasārathim | jaghānasamareśrīmānaṅgadovegavānkapiḥ
translation: कपिः monkey, अङ्गदः Angada, वेगवान् swiftly, समरे in fight, तस्य his, काञ्चनचित्राङ्गम् bright with gold, साश्वम् horses, ससारथिम् with charioteer, रथम् chariot, जघान destroyed.
explanation: With the same mace (snatched from the Rakshasa) Angada swiftly struck Indrajit hand destroyed the horse, chariot, and charioteer.

shloka_text: सम्पातिस्तुत्रिभिर्भाणैःप्रजङ्घेनसमाहतः । निजघानश्वकर्णेनप्रजङ्घंरणमूर्धनि ।।6.43.20।।
transliteration: sampātistutribhirbhāṇaiḥprajaṅghenasamāhataḥ | nijaghānaśvakarṇenaprajaṅghaṃraṇamūrdhani
translation: प्रजङ्घेन Prajangha, त्रिभिः three, बाणैः arrows, समाहतः injured, सम्पातिस्तु and Sampathi also, रणमूर्धनि in the midst of war, अश्वकर्णेन A swakarna, प्रजङ्घम् Prajangham, निजघान killed.
explanation: While Prajangha injured Sampathi with three arrows, in turn Sampathi killed him with Aswakarna tree in the midst of war.

shloka_text: जम्बुमालीरथस्थस्तुरथशक्त्यामहाबलः । बिबेदसमरेक्रुद्धोहनूमन्तंस्तनान्तरे ।।6.43.21।।
transliteration: jambumālīrathasthasturathaśaktyāmahābalaḥ | bibedasamarekruddhohanūmantaṃstanāntare
translation: महाबलः of extraordinary mighty, रथस्थः chariot's, जम्बुमाली Jambumali, क्रुद्धः angry, समरे in the battle, हनूमन्तम् Hanuman, रथशक्त्या mounting on the chariot, स्तनान्तरे in the chest, बिभेद pierced
explanation: Jambumali of extraordinary might mounting on the chariot in the battle pierced Hanuman in his chest.

shloka_text: तस्यतंरथमास्थायहनूमान् मारुतात्मजः । प्रममाथतलेनाशुसहतेनैवरक्षसा ।।6.43.22।।
transliteration: tasyataṃrathamāsthāyahanūmān mārutātmajaḥ | pramamāthatalenāśusahatenaivarakṣasā
translation: मारुतात्मजः son of wind god, हनुमान् Hanuman, तस्य his, तंरथम् that chariot, आस्थाय taking position, आशु quickly, तेनरक्षसा that Rakshasa, तलेन with the palm, प्रमामथ destroyed.
explanation: Hanuman the son of wind god, getting on to the chariot quickly destroyed that Rakshasa Jambumali with his palm.

shloka_text: नदन् प्रतपनोघोरोनलंसोप्यन्वधावत । नलःप्रतपनस्याशुपातयामासचक्षुषी ।।6.43.23।।
transliteration: nadan pratapanoghoronalaṃsopyanvadhāvata | nalaḥpratapanasyāśupātayāmāsacakṣuṣī
translation: घोरः dreadful, सःप्रतपनः that Pratapan, नदन् roaring, नलम् on Nala, अन्वधावत jumping, नलः Nala, आशु that, प्रतपनस्य Pratapan's, चक्षुषी eyes, पातयामास gouged out.
explanation: Dreadful Pratapan roared and jumped over Nala. Nala in turn gouged out the eyes of Pratapan.

shloka_text: भिन्नगात्रश्शरैस्तीक्ष्णैःक्षिप्रहस्तेनरक्षसा । ग्रसन्तमिवसैन्यानिप्रघसंवानराधिपः ।।6.43.24।। सुग्रीवस्सप्तपर्णेननिर्भिभेदजघानच ।
transliteration: bhinnagātraśśaraistīkṣṇaiḥkṣiprahastenarakṣasā | grasantamivasainyānipraghasaṃvānarādhipaḥ  sugrīvassaptaparṇenanirbhibhedajaghānaca |
translation: क्षिप्रहस्तेन as if consuming monkey troops, रक्षसा Rakshasa, तीक्ष्णैः sharp, शरैः arrows, भिन्नगात्रः opening his throat, वानराधिपः Vanara leader, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, सैन्यानि army, ग्रसन्तमिव as if swallowing, प्रघसम् Praghasan, सप्तपर्णेन Sapataparni, जघानच hit speedily, निर्भिभेद and killed.
explanation: Sugriva, the Vanara leader, taking hold of Sapataparni tree hit Pratapan who had his mouth open as if to swallow the army and killed him.

shloka_text: अग्निकेतुश्चदुर्धर्षोरश्मिकेतुश्चराक्षसः ।।6.43.25।। सुप्तघ्नोयज्ञकोपश्चरामंनिर्भिभिदुश्शरैः ।
transliteration: agniketuścadurdharṣoraśmiketuścarākṣasaḥ  suptaghnoyajñakopaścarāmaṃnirbhibhiduśśaraiḥ |
translation: दुर्धर्षः difficult to attack, अग्निकेतुश्च even Agnikethu, राक्षसः Rakshasa, रश्मिकेतुश्च and Rasmi kethu, मित्रघ्नः Mitraghna, यज्ञकोपश्च Yajakopa, रामम् Rama, शरैः with arrows, निर्भिभिदुः mangled.
explanation: Even Agnikethu who is difficult to attack, Rakshasas Rasmikethu, also Mitarghna and Yajakopa mangled Sri Rama with arrows.

shloka_text: तेषांचतुर्णांरामस्तुशिरांसिनिशितैश्शरैः । क्रुद्धश्चतुर्भिश्चिच्छेदघोरैरग्निशिखोपमैः ।।6.43.26।।
transliteration: teṣāṃcaturṇāṃrāmastuśirāṃsiniśitaiśśaraiḥ | kruddhaścaturbhiścicchedaghorairagniśikhopamaiḥ
translation: निशितैः sharp, रामस्तु even Rama, क्रुद्धः anguished, घोरैः fierce, अग्निशिखोपमैः like flames of fire, चतुर्भिः all the four, शरैः by arrows, तेषाम् them, चतुर्णाम् four, शिरांसि heads, चिच्छेद shattered.
explanation: Raged Rama with his sharp arrows which were like flames of fire destroyed all the four Rakshasas by cutting their heads.

shloka_text: वज्रमुष्टिस्तुमैन्देनमुष्टिनानिहतोरणे । पपातसरथस्साश्वःपुराट्टइवभूतले ।।6.43.27।।
transliteration: vajramuṣṭistumaindenamuṣṭinānihatoraṇe | papātasarathassāśvaḥpurāṭṭaivabhūtale
translation: वज्रमुष्टिस्तु Vajramushti also, रणे in the battle, मैन्देन Mainda, मुष्टिना with fist, निहतः killed, सरथः charioteer, साश्वः horses, पुराट्टःइव like the fort, भूतले on the ground, पपात fell.
explanation: Even Vajramushti fell on the ground struck with the fist by Mainda and the chariot and charioteer fell like the fort.

shloka_text: निकुम्बस्तुरणेनीलंनीलाञ्जनचयप्रभम् । निर्बिभेदशरैस्तीक्ष्णैःकरैर्मेघमिवांशुमान् ।।6.43.28।।
transliteration: nikumbasturaṇenīlaṃnīlāñjanacayaprabham | nirbibhedaśaraistīkṣṇaiḥkarairmeghamivāṃśumān
translation: निकुम्भस्तु Nikumbha also, रणे in battlefield, नीलाञ्जनचयप्रभम् like a mass of dark collyrium, नीलम् Nila, अंशुमान् Sun, करैः dark, मेघमिव cloud like, तीक्ष्णैः sharp, शरैः arrows, निर्भिभेद shattered.
explanation: Just as the Sun 's rays pierced through clouds Nikumbha was shattered and fell like a mass of collyrium in the battlefield.

shloka_text: पुनश्शरशतेनाथक्षिप्रहस्तोनिशाचरः । बिभेदसमरेनीलंनिकुम्भःप्रजहासच ।।6.43.29।।
transliteration: punaśśaraśatenāthakṣiprahastoniśācaraḥ | bibhedasamarenīlaṃnikumbhaḥprajahāsaca
translation: क्षिप्रहस्तः endowed with speed in shooting arrows, निशाचरः night ranger, निकुम्भः Nikumbha, अथ there, शरशतेन a thousand arrows, समरे in the battle, नीलम् Nila, पुनः again, बिभेद shattered, प्रजहासच and laughed heartily.
explanation: Nikumbha, the night ranger who was endowed with speed in shooting arrows again shot with a thousand arrows and laughed heartily.

shloka_text: तस्यैवरथचक्रेणनीलोविष्णुरिवाहवे । शिरश्चिच्छेदसमरेनिकुम्भस्यचसारथेः ।।6.43.30।।
transliteration: tasyaivarathacakreṇanīloviṣṇurivāhave | śiraścicchedasamarenikumbhasyacasāratheḥ
translation: नीलः Nila, आहवे, विष्णुरिव like Vishnu, तस्यैव his own, रथचक्रेण chariot wheels, समरे in battle, निकुम्भस्य at Nikumbha, सारथेः charioteer, शिरः head, चिच्छेदः broken to pieces.
explanation: Like Lord Vishnu, Nila took the wheels of the chariot of Nikumbha and shattered the charioteer into pieces.

shloka_text: वज्राशनिसमस्पर्शोद्विविदोऽप्यशनिप्रभम् । जघानगिरिशृङ्गेणमिषतांसर्वरक्षसाम् ।।6.43.31।।
transliteration: vajrāśanisamasparśodvivido'pyaśaniprabham | jaghānagiriśṛṅgeṇamiṣatāṃsarvarakṣasām
translation: वज्राशनिसमस्पर्शः like thunderbolt to touch, द्विविदोपि Dwivida's body, सर्वरक्षसाम् all Rakshasas, मिषताम् watching, गिरिशृङ्गेण mountain peak, अशनिप्रभम् Asaniprabhu, जघान moved about.
explanation: Dwivida whose body was like a thunderbolt to feel, moved about on the mountain peak as Rakshasas were watching.

shloka_text: द्विदिधंवानरेन्द्रंतुनगयोधिनमाहवे । शरैरशनिसङ्काशैस्सविव्याधाशनिप्रभः ।।6.43.32।।
transliteration: dvididhaṃvānarendraṃtunagayodhinamāhave | śarairaśanisaṅkāśaissavivyādhāśaniprabhaḥ
translation: सःअशनिप्रभः that Asaniprabha, आहवे fighting with, नगयोधिनम् with trees, वानरेन्द्रम् Vanara Lord, तु you, द्विविधम् Dwivida, आशनिसङ्काशैः resembling lightening, शरैः arrows, विव्याध wounded
explanation: Asaniprabha shot arrows resembling lightning at Dwivida the Vanara Lord who was fighting with trees.

shloka_text: सशरैरभिविद्धाङ्गोद्विविदःक्रोधमूर्छितः । सालेनसरथंसाश्वंनिजघानाशनिप्रभम् ।।6.43.33।।
transliteration: saśarairabhividdhāṅgodvividaḥkrodhamūrchitaḥ | sālenasarathaṃsāśvaṃnijaghānāśaniprabham
translation: शरैः arrows, अभिविद्धाङ्गः whose limbs have been injured, सःद्विविदः that Dwivida, क्रोधमूर्छितः enraged, सालेन Sala tree, सरथम् charioteer, साश्वम् horses, अशनिप्रभम् Asaniprabha, निजघान killed.
explanation: Dwivida whose limbs have been injured being enraged took Sala tree and killed Asaniprabha and the charioteer as well as the horses.

shloka_text: विद्युन्मालीरथस्थस्तुशरैःकाञ्चनभूषणैः । सुषेणंताडयामासननादचमुहुर्मुहुः ।।6.43.34।।
transliteration: vidyunmālīrathasthastuśaraiḥkāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ | suṣeṇaṃtāḍayāmāsananādacamuhurmuhuḥ
translation: रथस्थः in the chariot, विद्युन्माली Vidyunmali, काञ्चनभूषणैः decorated with gold, शरैः arrows, मुहुर्मुहुः again and again, सुषेणम् at Sushena, ताडयामास beating, ननादच roared.
explanation: Vidyunmali mounting the chariot started releasing arrows covered with gold at Sushena and roared.

shloka_text: तंरथस्थमथोदृष्टवासुषेणोवानरोत्तमः । गिरिशृङ्गेणमहतारथमाशुन्यपातयत् ।।6.43.35।।
transliteration: taṃrathasthamathodṛṣṭavāsuṣeṇovānarottamaḥ | giriśṛṅgeṇamahatārathamāśunyapātayat
translation: अथो Nay!, वानरोत्तमः leader of Vanaras, सुषेणः Sushena, रथस्थम् chariot, तम् him, दृष्टवा top, महता great, गिरिशृङ्गेण peak of the mountain, आशु there, रथम् chariot, न्यपातयत् crushed.
explanation: Nay, Sushena, the leader of Vanaras, saw himself down and Jambumali on top in the chariot. He crushed him with a big mountain peak.

shloka_text: लाघवेनतुसंयुक्तोविद्युन्मालीनिशाचरः । अपक्रम्यरथात्तूर्णंगदापाणिःक्षितौस्थितः ।।6.43.36।।
transliteration: lāghavenatusaṃyuktovidyunmālīniśācaraḥ | apakramyarathāttūrṇaṃgadāpāṇiḥkṣitausthitaḥ
translation: लाघवेन huge, संयुक्तः, निशाचरः night ranger, विद्युन्माली Vidyunmali, रथात् from the chariot, तूर्णम् quickly, अपक्रम्य got down, गदापाणिः mace, क्षितौ placed on the chest, स्थितः remained.
explanation: Vidyunmali seeing Sushena, the monkey leader got a huge rock, and hit him on his chest with the mace.

shloka_text: ततःक्रोधसमाविष्टःसुषेणोहरिपुङ्गवः । शिलांसुमहतींगृह्यनिशाचरमभिद्रवत् ।।6.43.37।।
transliteration: tataḥkrodhasamāviṣṭaḥsuṣeṇoharipuṅgavaḥ | śilāṃsumahatīṃgṛhyaniśācaramabhidravat
translation: ततः thereafter, क्रोधसमाविष्टः overtaken by anger, हरिपुङ्गवः monkey leader, सुषेणः Sushena, महतीम् huge, शिलाम् rock, गृह्य seizing, निशाचरम् Rakshasa, अभिद्रवत् dropped.
explanation: Thereafter overtaken by anger, the monkey leader Sushena seized the huge rock from the Rakshasa and dropped it.

shloka_text: तमापतन्तंगदयाविद्युन्मालीनिशाचरः । वक्षस्यभिजघानाशुसुषेणंहरिपुङ्गवः ।।6.43.38।।
transliteration: tamāpatantaṃgadayāvidyunmālīniśācaraḥ | vakṣasyabhijaghānāśusuṣeṇaṃharipuṅgavaḥ
translation: निशाचरः night ranger, विद्युन्माली Vidyunmali, आपतन्तम् , तम् him, हरिपुङ्गवः leader of monkeys, सुषेणम् Sushena, आशु with, गदया the mace, वक्षसि on the chest, अभिजघानह hit him.
explanation: Then Vidyunmali, seeing the leader of monkeys getting the huge rock, hit him on the chest with the mace.

shloka_text: गदाप्रहारंतंघोरमच्नित्यप्लवगोत्तमः । तांशिलांपातयामासतस्योरसिमहामृधे ।।6.43.39।।
transliteration: gadāprahāraṃtaṃghoramacnityaplavagottamaḥ | tāṃśilāṃpātayāmāsatasyorasimahāmṛdhe
translation: महामृधे great monkey, प्लवगोत्तमः leader of monkeys, घोरम् dreadful, तंगदाप्रहारम् that mace, अच्नित्य not caring, शिलाम् rock, ताम् him, तस्य his, उरसि chest, पातयामास dropped.
explanation: The great monkey leader Sushena, not caring for the mace, dropped the rock on Vidyunmali's chest.

shloka_text: शिलाप्रहारभिहतोविद्युन्मालीनिशाचरः । निष्पिष्टहृदयोभूमौगतासुर्निपपातह ।।6.43.40।।
transliteration: śilāprahārabhihatovidyunmālīniśācaraḥ | niṣpiṣṭahṛdayobhūmaugatāsurnipapātaha
translation: शिलाप्रहाराभिहतः hit by the huge rock, निशाचरः night ranger, विद्युन्माली Vidyunmali, निप्पिष्टहृदयः ceased of life, गतासुः gone, भूमौ on the ground, निपपातह dropped.
explanation: Vidyunmali, the Rakshasa hit by the huge rock, was ceased of life.

shloka_text: एवंतैर्वानरैश्शूरैश्शूरास्तेरजनीचराः । द्वन्द्वेविमृदितास्तत्रदैत्याइवदिवौकसैः ।।6.43.41।।
transliteration: evaṃtairvānaraiśśūraiśśūrāsterajanīcarāḥ | dvandvevimṛditāstatradaityāivadivaukasaiḥ
translation: शूराः warriors, तेरजनीचराः those Rakshasas, शूरैः with warriors, तैःवानरैः those Vanaras, एवम् in that manner, तत्र there, द्वन्द्वे duel fight, दिवौकसैः wonderful, दैत्याइव like Devatas, विमृदिताः delighted.
explanation: In that manner the Rakshasa warriors and the Vanara warriors fought the duel wonderfully and like the way Devatas killed the Demons, the Rakshasas were killed.

shloka_text: भग्नैखडगैर्गदाभिश्चशक्तितोमरपट्टसै: । अपविद्धैश्चाभिन्नैश्चरथैस्साङ्ग्रामिकैर्हयैः ।।6.43.42।। निहतैःकुञ्जरैर्मत्स्सैस्तथावानरराक्षसैः । चक्राक्षयुगदण्डैश्चभग्नैर्धरणिसंश्रितैः ।।6.43.43।। बभूवायोधनंघोरंगोमायुगणसेवितम् ।
transliteration: bhagnaikhaḍagairgadābhiścaśaktitomarapaṭṭasai: | apaviddhaiścābhinnaiścarathaissāṅgrāmikairhayaiḥ  nihataiḥkuñjarairmatssaistathāvānararākṣasaiḥ | cakrākṣayugadaṇḍaiścabhagnairdharaṇisaṃśritaiḥ  babhūvāyodhanaṃghoraṃgomāyugaṇasevitam |
translation: गोमायुगणसेवितम् frequented by groups of jackals, अयोधनम् battlefield, भग्नैः broken, खडगैः swords, गदाभिश्च and maces, शक्तितोमरपट्टिशै: spears javelins maces. अपविद्धैः broken, रथैश्चापि chariots also, तथा similarly, साङ्ग्रामिकैः fit for war, हयैः horses, निहतैः dead, मत्स्सैः by elephants, कुञ्जरैः horses, तथा similarly, वानरराक्षसैः Vanaras and Rakshasas, भग्नैः broken, धरणिसंश्रितैः on the ground, चक्राक्षयुगदण्डैश्च wheels and axles of chariots, घोरम् dreadful, बभूव seemed.
explanation: The battlefield was dreadful and, frequented by jackals with spears, javelins, maces, and swords, strewn all over, similarly with broken chariots, horses, elephants, and monkeys fit for war. Broken wheels and axles of chariots were found all over.

shloka_text: भग्नैखडगैर्गदाभिश्चशक्तितोमरपट्टसै: । अपविद्धैश्चाभिन्नैश्चरथैस्साङ्ग्रामिकैर्हयैः ।।6.43.42।। निहतैःकुञ्जरैर्मत्स्सैस्तथावानरराक्षसैः । चक्राक्षयुगदण्डैश्चभग्नैर्धरणिसंश्रितैः ।।6.43.43।। बभूवायोधनंघोरंगोमायुगणसेवितम् ।
transliteration: bhagnaikhaḍagairgadābhiścaśaktitomarapaṭṭasai: | apaviddhaiścābhinnaiścarathaissāṅgrāmikairhayaiḥ  nihataiḥkuñjarairmatssaistathāvānararākṣasaiḥ | cakrākṣayugadaṇḍaiścabhagnairdharaṇisaṃśritaiḥ  babhūvāyodhanaṃghoraṃgomāyugaṇasevitam |
translation: गोमायुगणसेवितम् frequented by groups of jackals, अयोधनम् battlefield, भग्नैः broken, खडगैः swords, गदाभिश्च and maces, शक्तितोमरपट्टिशै: spears javelins maces. अपविद्धैः broken, रथैश्चापि chariots also, तथा similarly, साङ्ग्रामिकैः fit for war, हयैः horses, निहतैः dead, मत्स्सैः by elephants, कुञ्जरैः horses, तथा similarly, वानरराक्षसैः Vanaras and Rakshasas, भग्नैः broken, धरणिसंश्रितैः on the ground, चक्राक्षयुगदण्डैश्च wheels and axles of chariots, घोरम् dreadful, बभूव seemed.
explanation: The battlefield was dreadful and, frequented by jackals with spears, javelins, maces, and swords, strewn all over, similarly with broken chariots, horses, elephants, and monkeys fit for war. Broken wheels and axles of chariots were found all over.

shloka_text: कबन्धानिसमुत्पेतुर्दिक्षुवानररक्षसाम् ।।6.43.44।। विमर्देतुमुलेतस्मिन्देवासुररणोपमे ।
transliteration: kabandhānisamutpeturdikṣuvānararakṣasām  vimardetumuletasmindevāsuraraṇopame |
translation: देवासुररणोपमे like the war between Devatas and demons, तस्मिन् their, तुमुले confused, विमर्दे rubbing together, वानररक्षसाम् Vanaras and Rakshasas, कबन्धानि trunks of body, दिक्षु directions, समुत्पेतुः scattered.
explanation: It was like the war between Devatas and demons, with the trunks of the bodies of Vanaras and Rakshasas rubbing together lying scattered in all directions.

shloka_text: विदार्यमाणाहरिपुङ्गवैस्तदानिशाचराश्शोणितदिग्धगात्राः । पुनःसुयुद्धंतरसासमास्थितादिवाकरस्यास्तमयाभिकाङ्क्षिणः ।।6.43.45।।
transliteration: vidāryamāṇāharipuṅgavaistadāniśācarāśśoṇitadigdhagātrāḥ | punaḥsuyuddhaṃtarasāsamāsthitādivākarasyāstamayābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ
translation: तदा then, हरिपुङ्गवैः monkey leader, विदार्यमाणाः killed by, शोणितदिग्धगात्राः full of blood, निशाचराः Rakshasas, दिवाकरस्य sun's, अस्तमयाभिकाङ्क्षिणः looking for Sun set, तरसा, पुनः again, सुयुद्धम् that war, समास्थिता adhering together.
explanation: Then the Rakshasas killed by Vanara leaders, their bodies full of blood were looking for sunset and again picking up strength began to battle. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेत्रिचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty third sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: युध्यतामेनतेषांतुतदावानरराक्षसाम् । रविरस्तंगतोरात्रिःप्रवृत्ताप्राणहारिणी ।।6.44.1।।
transliteration: yudhyatāmenateṣāṃtutadāvānararākṣasām | ravirastaṃgatorātriḥpravṛttāprāṇahāriṇī
translation: तेषाम् their, वानररक्षसाम् Vanara and Rakshasa, युध्यतामेव battling, तदा then, रविः sun, अस्तम् set, गतः went, प्राणहारिणी harmful to the life, रात्रिः night, प्रवृत्ता began.
explanation: Thus, as the Vanaras and Rakshasas were battling, the Sun began to set, which is not favourable to the life of Vanaras.
comments: In the fierce fight that took place in the night Indrajith gets vanquished by Angada. Sri Rama and Lakshmana also put up a great fight and eventually get bound by a noose of serpents.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यंबद्धवैराणांघोराणांजयमिच्छताम् । सम्प्रवृत्तंनिशायुद्धंतदावानररक्षसाम् ।।6.44.2।।
transliteration: anyonyaṃbaddhavairāṇāṃghorāṇāṃjayamicchatām | sampravṛttaṃniśāyuddhaṃtadāvānararakṣasām
translation: तदा then, अन्योन्यम् to one another, बद्धवैराणाम् strong enmity, घोराणाम् dreadful, जयम् victory, इच्छताम् wishing, वानररक्षसाम् Vanara and Rakshasas, निशायुद्धम् night battle, सम्प्रवृत्तम् started.
explanation: Then Vanaras and dreadful Rakshasas being strongly inimical to each other started the night battle wishing victory.

shloka_text: राक्षसोऽसीतिहरयोहरिश्चाऽसीतिराक्षसाः । अन्योन्यंसमरेजघ्नुस्तस्मिंस्तमसिदारुणे ।।6.44.3।।
transliteration: rākṣaso'sītiharayohariścā'sītirākṣasāḥ | anyonyaṃsamarejaghnustasmiṃstamasidāruṇe
translation: दारुणे fierce, तस्मिन् them, तमसि darkness, राक्षसःअसि thinking to be Rakshasa, इति thus, हरयः monkeys, हरिश्च and monkeys, असि thinking to be, इति thus, राक्षसाः Rakshasa, समरे fought, अन्योन्यम् one another, जघ्नुः hit .
explanation: In the fierce darkness that prevailed, monkeys hit monkeys thinking to be Rakshasas and Rakshasas hit Rakshasas thinking to be Vanaras (not knowing in darkness) hit each other.

shloka_text: जहिदारयचैहीतिकथंविद्रवसीतिच । एवंसुतुमुलश्शब्दस्तस्मिंस्तमसिशुश्रुवे ।।6.44.4।। कालाःकाञ्चनसन्नाहास्तस्मिंस्तमसिराक्षसाः । सम्प्रदृश्यन्तशैलेन्द्रादीप्तौषधिवनाइव ।।6.44.5।।
transliteration: jahidārayacaihītikathaṃvidravasītica | evaṃsutumulaśśabdastasmiṃstamasiśuśruve  kālāḥkāñcanasannāhāstasmiṃstamasirākṣasāḥ | sampradṛśyantaśailendrādīptauṣadhivanāiva
translation: जहिदारय strike, चैहीति tear, कथं how, विद्रवसीतिच why do you run away, एवं in this manner, सुतुमुलश्शब्द loud echo, स्तस्मिं such was, स्तमसि darkness, शुश्रुवे heard, तस्मिन् such was, तमसि dark complexioned, कालाः night, काञ्चनसन्नाहाः covered with golden armour, राक्षसाः Rakshasa, दीप्तौषधिवनाः shining like the herbs in the forests, शैलेन्द्राः mountain, सम्प्रदृश्यन्त appeared.
explanation: "Strike", "Tear", "Why are you running away?" were the kind of tumultuous echo heard in the darkness of the night. In that darkness the dark complexioned Vanaras and Rakshasas covered with golden armour in the night seemed like shining herbs of the forest in the mountain.

shloka_text: जहिदारयचैहीतिकथंविद्रवसीतिच । एवंसुतुमुलश्शब्दस्तस्मिंस्तमसिशुश्रुवे ।।6.44.4।। कालाःकाञ्चनसन्नाहास्तस्मिंस्तमसिराक्षसाः । सम्प्रदृश्यन्तशैलेन्द्रादीप्तौषधिवनाइव ।।6.44.5।।
