transliteration: jahidārayacaihītikathaṃvidravasītica | evaṃsutumulaśśabdastasmiṃstamasiśuśruve  kālāḥkāñcanasannāhāstasmiṃstamasirākṣasāḥ | sampradṛśyantaśailendrādīptauṣadhivanāiva
translation: जहिदारय strike, चैहीति tear, कथं how, विद्रवसीतिच why do you run away, एवं in this manner, सुतुमुलश्शब्द loud echo, स्तस्मिं such was, स्तमसि darkness, शुश्रुवे heard, तस्मिन् such was, तमसि dark complexioned, कालाः night, काञ्चनसन्नाहाः covered with golden armour, राक्षसाः Rakshasa, दीप्तौषधिवनाः shining like the herbs in the forests, शैलेन्द्राः mountain, सम्प्रदृश्यन्त appeared.
explanation: "Strike", "Tear", "Why are you running away?" were the kind of tumultuous echo heard in the darkness of the night. In that darkness the dark complexioned Vanaras and Rakshasas covered with golden armour in the night seemed like shining herbs of the forest in the mountain.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तमसिदुष्पारेराक्षसाःक्रोधमूर्छिताः । परिपेतुर्महावेगाभक्षयन्तःप्लवङ्गमान् ।।6.44.6।।
transliteration: tasmiṃstamasiduṣpārerākṣasāḥkrodhamūrchitāḥ | paripeturmahāvegābhakṣayantaḥplavaṅgamān
translation: दुष्पारे difficult to penetrate, तस्मिन् in that, तमसि darkness, क्रोधमूर्छिता lost senses overcome by anger, राक्षसाः Rakshasas, प्लवङ्गमान् monkeys, भक्षयन्तः devouring, महावेगाः swiftly, परिपेतुः wandered.
explanation: In that pitch darkness, which was difficult even to move, the Rakshasas overcome by anger and lost senses were wandering devouring the monkeys.

shloka_text: तेहयान् काञ्चनापीडान् ध्वजांश्चाशीविषोपमान् । आप्लुत्यदशनैस्तीक्ष्णैर्भीमकोपाव्यदारयन् ।।6.44.7।। वानराबलिनोयुद्धेऽक्षोभयन् राक्षसींचमूम् ।
transliteration: tehayān kāñcanāpīḍān dhvajāṃścāśīviṣopamān | āplutyadaśanaistīkṣṇairbhīmakopāvyadārayan  vānarābalinoyuddhe'kṣobhayan rākṣasīṃcamūm |
translation: भीमकोपाः terribly angry, बलिनः mighty strong, तेवानराः those Vanaras, आप्लुत्य springing up, तीक्ष्णैः their sharp, धवनैः teeth, काञ्चनापीडान् golden ornaments, हयान् horses, आशीविषोपमान् pervading like fire, ध्वजांश्च of the horses, व्यदारयन् splitting, युद्धे in battle, राक्षसीम् Rakshasa's, चमूम् , अक्षोभयन् tore to pieces.
explanation: The mighty strong Vanaras, terribly angry at the Rakshasas sprang up to the sky, and tore with their sharp teeth, the horses of Rakshasas decked with golden ornaments pervading like fire in the battle.

shloka_text: कुञ्जरान् कुञ्जरारोहान् पताकाध्वजिनोरथान् ।।6.44.8।। कर्षुश्चददंशुश्चदशनैःक्रोधमूर्छिताः ।
transliteration: kuñjarān kuñjarārohān patākādhvajinorathān  karṣuścadadaṃśuścadaśanaiḥkrodhamūrchitāḥ |
translation: व्यदारयन् lost sense with anger, कुञ्जरान् elephants, कुञ्जरारोहान् mounted on elephants, पताकाध्वजिनः posts tied with flags, रथान् chariots, चकर्षुः dragged them, दशनैः with teeth, ददंशुश्च destroyed.
explanation: Having lost senses in fury they dragged the elephants, those mounted upon them, and the chariots decorated with posts and flags and tore them with their teeth.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणश्चापिरामश्चशरैराशीविषोपमैः ।।6.44.9।। दृश्यादृश्यानिरक्षांसिप्रवराणिनिजघ्नतुः ।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaścāpirāmaścaśarairāśīviṣopamaiḥ  dṛśyādṛśyānirakṣāṃsipravarāṇinijaghnatuḥ |
translation: रामश्च Rama as well, लक्ष्मणश्चापि as Lakshmana also, आशीविषोपमैः shining like venomous snakes, शरैः arrows, दृश्यादृश्यानि visible and invisible, प्रवराणि principal, रक्षांसि Rakshasas, निजघ्नतुः killed
explanation: Then Rama as well as Lakshmana with their venomous snakelike arrows killed both visible and invisible principal Rakshasas.

shloka_text: तुरङ्गखुरविध्वस्तंरथनेमिसमुत्थितम् ।।6.44.10।। रुरोधकर्णनेत्राणियुध्यतांधरणीरजः ।
transliteration: turaṅgakhuravidhvastaṃrathanemisamutthitam  rurodhakarṇanetrāṇiyudhyatāṃdharaṇīrajaḥ |
translation: तुरङ्गखुरविध्वस्तम् pulverised by the horses hooves, रथनेमिसमुत्थितम् crushed by the wheels of chariots, धरणीरजः dust from the ground, युध्यताम् risen, कर्णनेत्राणि ears and eyes, रुरोध filled.
explanation: Then the dust rose from the ground pulverised the horses' hooves and crushed by the chariot wheels, filling the ears and eyes of those in war.

shloka_text: वर्तमानेतथाघोरेसङ्ग्रामेरोमहर्षणे ।।6.44.11।। रुधिरोधामहाघोरानद्यस्तत्रप्रसुस्रुवुः ।
transliteration: vartamānetathāghoresaṅgrāmeromaharṣaṇe  rudhirodhāmahāghorānadyastatraprasusruvuḥ |
translation: तथा like that, घोरे terrible, रोमहर्षणे horripilation, सङ्ग्रामे war, वर्तमाने moving, रुधिरोधा river of blood, महाघोराः terrific, नद्यः noise, तत्र there, प्रसुस्रुवुः flowed.
explanation: In that way as the war was going on, and rivers of blood flowing with the terrific noise it made hair stand on end.

shloka_text: ततोभेरीमृदङ्गानांपणवानांचनिस्स्वनः ।।6.44.12।। शङ्खवेणुस्वनोन्मिश्रस्सम्भूवाद्भुतोपमः ।
transliteration: tatobherīmṛdaṅgānāṃpaṇavānāṃcanissvanaḥ  śaṅkhaveṇusvanonmiśrassambhūvādbhutopamaḥ |
translation: ततः there, भेरीमृदङ्गानाम् kettle drums and wooden drums, पणवानांच musical instrument panava, शङ्खवेणुस्वनोमनिश्रः sounds of conchs, flutes mixed, अद्भुतोपमः wonderful, निस्स्वनः rattling sounds, सम्बभूव arose.
explanation: There arose wonderful sounds of musical instruments, the sounds of kettle drums, wooden drums, mixed with conchs and flutes.

shloka_text: हतानांस्तनमानानांराक्षसानांचनिःस्वनः ।।6.44.13।। शस्तानांवानराणांचसम्बभूवातिदारुणः ।
transliteration: hatānāṃstanamānānāṃrākṣasānāṃcaniḥsvanaḥ  śastānāṃvānarāṇāṃcasambabhūvātidāruṇaḥ |
translation: अत्र there, स्तनमानानाम् in the battlefield, हतानाम् wounded, राक्षसानांच Rakshasas, शस्तानाम् appeased, वानराणांच and Vanaras, दारुणः dreadful, निःस्वनः roaring sounds, सम्बभूव arose.
explanation: There from the battlefield arose the roaring sounds of wounded and appeased Rakshasas and Vanaras.

shloka_text: हतैर्वानरवीरैश्चशक्तिशूलपरश्वधैः ।।6.44.14।। निहतैःपर्वताकारैराक्षसैःकामरूपिभिः । शस्त्रपुष्पोपहाराचतत्रासीद्युद्धमेदिनी ।।6.44.15।। दुर् ज्ञेयादुर्निवेशाचशोणितास्रावकर्दमा ।
transliteration: hatairvānaravīraiścaśaktiśūlaparaśvadhaiḥ  nihataiḥparvatākārairākṣasaiḥkāmarūpibhiḥ | śastrapuṣpopahārācatatrāsīdyuddhamedinī  dur jñeyādurniveśācaśoṇitāsrāvakardamā |
translation: तत्र there, शस्त्रपुष्पोपहारा offering of flowers dropped from enemies (from the mountain), युद्धमेदिनी on the battlefield, हतैः killed, वानरवीरैश्च Vanara warriors also, शक्तिशूलपरश्वधैः by javelins, tridents and axes, निहतैः wounded, कामरूपिभिः who can change their form at will, पर्वताकारैः of mountain size, राक्षसैः Rakshasa, शोणितास्रावकर्दमा wetted by the flow of blood, दुर् ज्ञेया muddy, दुर्निवेशाच difficult to reach, आसीत् remained.
explanation: There with warriors of Vanaras wounded by javelins, tridents and axes, and the Rakshasas of mountain size who could change their form at will, the battlefield was muddy, and wet with blood flowing and difficult to reach.

shloka_text: हतैर्वानरवीरैश्चशक्तिशूलपरश्वधैः ।।6.44.14।। निहतैःपर्वताकारैराक्षसैःकामरूपिभिः । शस्त्रपुष्पोपहाराचतत्रासीद्युद्धमेदिनी ।।6.44.15।। दुर् ज्ञेयादुर्निवेशाचशोणितास्रावकर्दमा ।
transliteration: hatairvānaravīraiścaśaktiśūlaparaśvadhaiḥ  nihataiḥparvatākārairākṣasaiḥkāmarūpibhiḥ | śastrapuṣpopahārācatatrāsīdyuddhamedinī  dur jñeyādurniveśācaśoṇitāsrāvakardamā |
translation: तत्र there, शस्त्रपुष्पोपहारा offering of flowers dropped from enemies (from the mountain), युद्धमेदिनी on the battlefield, हतैः killed, वानरवीरैश्च Vanara warriors also, शक्तिशूलपरश्वधैः by javelins, tridents and axes, निहतैः wounded, कामरूपिभिः who can change their form at will, पर्वताकारैः of mountain size, राक्षसैः Rakshasa, शोणितास्रावकर्दमा wetted by the flow of blood, दुर् ज्ञेया muddy, दुर्निवेशाच difficult to reach, आसीत् remained.
explanation: There with warriors of Vanaras wounded by javelins, tridents and axes, and the Rakshasas of mountain size who could change their form at will, the battlefield was muddy, and wet with blood flowing and difficult to reach.

shloka_text: साबभूवनिशाघोराहरिराक्षसहारिणी ।।6.44.16।। कालरात्रीवभूतानांसर्वेषांदुरतिक्रमा ।
transliteration: sābabhūvaniśāghorāharirākṣasahāriṇī  kālarātrīvabhūtānāṃsarveṣāṃduratikramā |
translation: सर्वेषाम् for all beings, भूतानाम् beings, दुरतिक्रमा difficult to pass, कालरात्रीव like the night of dissolution, सानिशा that night, घोरा fierce, हरिराक्षसनाशिनी destructive to Vanaras and Rakshasas, बभूव remained.
explanation: Like the dreadful night for all beings, difficult to spend, as if it were a dissolution, destructive to Vanaras and Rakshasas.

shloka_text: ततस्तेराक्षसास्तत्रतस्मिंस्तमसिदारुणे ।।6.44.17।। राममेवाभ्यवर्तन्तसम्हृष्टाश्शरवृष्टिभिः ।
transliteration: tatasterākṣasāstatratasmiṃstamasidāruṇe  rāmamevābhyavartantasamhṛṣṭāśśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ |
translation: ततः thereafter, तत्र there, परमदारुणे exceedingly fearsome, तस्मिन् तमसि in that dark night, तेराक्षसाः those Rakshasas, सम्हृष्टाः highly delighted, शरवृष्टिभिः rain of arrows, राममेव Rama himself, अभ्यवर्तन्त assailed.
explanation: Thereafter in that exceedingly fearsome dark night in the battlefield highly delighted Rakshasas assailed Rama with a rain of arrows.

shloka_text: तेषामापततांशब्दःक्रुद्धानामपिगर्जताम् ।।6.44.18।। उद्वर्तइवसत्त्व, नांसमुद्राणांप्रशुश्रुवे ।
transliteration: teṣāmāpatatāṃśabdaḥkruddhānāmapigarjatām  udvartaivasattva, nāṃsamudrāṇāṃpraśuśruve |
translation: क्रुद्धानाम् angry Rakshasas, गर्जताम् thundering, आपतताम् rushing towards, तेषाम् them, शब्दः noise, सत्त्वानाम् seven seas, उद्वर्ते risen to flow, समुद्राणाम् into ocean, प्रशुश्रुवे heard.
explanation: The thundering noise of the angry Rakshasas rushing towards Rama was like the seven seas rising to flow into the ocean.

shloka_text: तेषांरामश्शरैःषडिभःषडजघाननिशाचरान् ।।6.44.19।। निमेषान्तरमात्रेणशितैरग्निशिखोपमैः । यमशत्रुश्चदुर्धर्षोमहापार्श्वमहोदरौ ।।6.44.20।। वज्रदंष्ट्रोमहाकायस्तौचोभौशुकसारणौ । तेतुरामेणबाणौघैस्सर्वेमर्मसुताडिताः ।।6.44.21।। युद्धादपसृतास्तत्रसावशेषायुषोऽभवन् ।
transliteration: teṣāṃrāmaśśaraiḥṣaḍibhaḥṣaḍajaghānaniśācarān  nimeṣāntaramātreṇaśitairagniśikhopamaiḥ | yamaśatruścadurdharṣomahāpārśvamahodarau  vajradaṃṣṭromahākāyastaucobhauśukasāraṇau | teturāmeṇabāṇaughaissarvemarmasutāḍitāḥ  yuddhādapasṛtāstatrasāvaśeṣāyuṣo'bhavan |
translation: तेषां their, रामश्शरैः Rama's shafts, षडिभः six, षडजघान striking the six best, निशाचरान् Rakshasas, निमेषान्तरमात्रेण in the time of twinkling of eyelid, शितैरग्निशिखोपमै like flames, दुर्धर्षः difficult to overcome, यमशत्रुश्च Yamastru, महापार्श्वमहोदरौ Mahaparva, Mahodara, महाकायः Mahakaya, वज्रदंष्ट्रः Vajradamshtra, तौ them, उभौ both, शुकसारणौ Suka, Sarana, ते they, रामेण by Rama, बाणौघैः fire of arrows, सर्वमर्मसु vital parts, ताडिताः pierced by, तत्र there, युद्धात् from tha battle, अपसृताः escaped, सावशेषायुषः with left over life, अभवन् remained.
explanation: On Rama striking with the six best of shafts like flames in a time of twinkling of eyelids, the six Rakshasas, Yamasatru, Mahaparva, Mahodara, Mahakaya, and Vajradamshtra found it difficult to overcome. Along with the two Suka, Saranas all of them were struck by Rama's fire like arrows in their vital parts and escaped with leftover life.

shloka_text: तेषांरामश्शरैःषडिभःषडजघाननिशाचरान् ।।6.44.19।। निमेषान्तरमात्रेणशितैरग्निशिखोपमैः । यमशत्रुश्चदुर्धर्षोमहापार्श्वमहोदरौ ।।6.44.20।। वज्रदंष्ट्रोमहाकायस्तौचोभौशुकसारणौ । तेतुरामेणबाणौघैस्सर्वेमर्मसुताडिताः ।।6.44.21।। युद्धादपसृतास्तत्रसावशेषायुषोऽभवन् ।
transliteration: teṣāṃrāmaśśaraiḥṣaḍibhaḥṣaḍajaghānaniśācarān  nimeṣāntaramātreṇaśitairagniśikhopamaiḥ | yamaśatruścadurdharṣomahāpārśvamahodarau  vajradaṃṣṭromahākāyastaucobhauśukasāraṇau | teturāmeṇabāṇaughaissarvemarmasutāḍitāḥ  yuddhādapasṛtāstatrasāvaśeṣāyuṣo'bhavan |
translation: तेषां their, रामश्शरैः Rama's shafts, षडिभः six, षडजघान striking the six best, निशाचरान् Rakshasas, निमेषान्तरमात्रेण in the time of twinkling of eyelid, शितैरग्निशिखोपमै like flames, दुर्धर्षः difficult to overcome, यमशत्रुश्च Yamastru, महापार्श्वमहोदरौ Mahaparva, Mahodara, महाकायः Mahakaya, वज्रदंष्ट्रः Vajradamshtra, तौ them, उभौ both, शुकसारणौ Suka, Sarana, ते they, रामेण by Rama, बाणौघैः fire of arrows, सर्वमर्मसु vital parts, ताडिताः pierced by, तत्र there, युद्धात् from tha battle, अपसृताः escaped, सावशेषायुषः with left over life, अभवन् remained.
explanation: On Rama striking with the six best of shafts like flames in a time of twinkling of eyelids, the six Rakshasas, Yamasatru, Mahaparva, Mahodara, Mahakaya, and Vajradamshtra found it difficult to overcome. Along with the two Suka, Saranas all of them were struck by Rama's fire like arrows in their vital parts and escaped with leftover life.

transliteration: teṣāṃrāmaśśaraiḥṣaḍibhaḥṣaḍajaghānaniśācarān  nimeṣāntaramātreṇaśitairagniśikhopamaiḥ | yamaśatruścadurdharṣomahāpārśvamahodarau  vajradaṃṣṭromahākāyastaucobhauśukasāraṇau | teturāmeṇabāṇaughaissarvemarmasutāḍitāḥ  yuddhādapasṛtāstatrasāvaśeṣāyuṣo'bhavan |
translation: तेषां their, रामश्शरैः Rama's shafts, षडिभः six, षडजघान striking the six best, निशाचरान् Rakshasas, निमेषान्तरमात्रेण in the time of twinkling of eyelid, शितैरग्निशिखोपमै like flames, दुर्धर्षः difficult to overcome, यमशत्रुश्च Yamastru, महापार्श्वमहोदरौ Mahaparva, Mahodara, महाकायः Mahakaya, वज्रदंष्ट्रः Vajradamshtra, तौ them, उभौ both, शुकसारणौ Suka, Sarana, ते they, रामेण by Rama, बाणौघैः fire of arrows, सर्वमर्मसु vital parts, ताडिताः pierced by, तत्र there, युद्धात् from tha battle, अपसृताः escaped, सावशेषायुषः with left over life, अभवन् remained.
explanation: On Rama striking with the six best of shafts like flames in a time of twinkling of eyelids, the six Rakshasas, Yamasatru, Mahaparva, Mahodara, Mahakaya, and Vajradamshtra found it difficult to overcome. Along with the two Suka, Saranas all of them were struck by Rama's fire like arrows in their vital parts and escaped with leftover life.

shloka_text: तत्रकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गैश्शरैरग्निशिखोपमैः ।।6.44.22।। दिशश्चकारविमलाःप्रदिशश्चमहारथः ।
transliteration: tatrakāñcanacitrāṅgaiśśarairagniśikhopamaiḥ  diśaścakāravimalāḥpradiśaścamahārathaḥ |
translation: महारथः mighty, तत्रकाञ्चनचित्रङ्गैः decorated with gold, शरैः shafts, अग्निशिखोपमैः like the flames of fire, दिशश्च in all the directions, प्रदिशश्च brightened, विमलाः bright, चकार created.
explanation: Mighty Rama with his shafts that were like flames of fire, decorated with gold, brightened in all directions.

shloka_text: येत्वन्येराक्षसाभीमारामस्याभिमुखेस्थिताः ।।6.44.23।। तेऽपिनष्टाःसमासाद्यपतङ्गाइवपावकम् ।
transliteration: yetvanyerākṣasābhīmārāmasyābhimukhesthitāḥ  te'pinaṣṭāḥsamāsādyapataṅgāivapāvakam |
translation: रामस्य Rama's, अभिमुखे in front, स्थिताः stood, अन्ये other, ये who so ever, भीमा fierce, राक्षसाः Rakshasa, तेऽपि be it, पावकम् fire, आसाद्य fallen, पतङ्गाःइव like fireflies, नष्टाः destroyed.
explanation: Those fierce Rakshasas who stood in front of Rama were destroyed like fireflies fallen in fire.

shloka_text: सुवर्णपुङ्खैर्विशिखैस्सपतद्भिस्सहस्रशः ।।6.44.24।। बभूवरजनीचित्राखद्योतैरिवशारदी ।
transliteration: suvarṇapuṅkhairviśikhaissapatadbhissahasraśaḥ  babhūvarajanīcitrākhadyotairivaśāradī |
translation: सहस्रशः thousands, सम्पतद्भिः raining, सुवर्णपुङ्खैः golden feathered, विशिखैः arrows, रजनी night, खद्योतैः illumined by fireflies, शारदीव in autumnal, चित्रा wonderful, बभूव appeared.
explanation: By the rain of thousands of golden feathered arrows, the night appeared as if illumined by fireflies and like a wonderful autumnal night.

shloka_text: राक्षसानांचनिनदैर्हरीणांचापिनिस्स्वनैः ।।6.44.25।। साबभूवनिशाघोराभूयोघोरतरातदा ।
transliteration: rākṣasānāṃcaninadairharīṇāṃcāpinissvanaiḥ  sābabhūvaniśāghorābhūyoghoratarātadā |
translation: घोरा fierce, सानिशा that night, तदा then, राक्षसानाम् Rakshasas, हरीणाम् Vanaras, निस्स्वनैःच making noise, भूयः appeared, घोरतरा more dreadful, बभूव was.
explanation: The night which was fierce appeared more dreadful with the loud noise of Rakshasas and Vanaras.

shloka_text: तेनशब्देनमहताप्रवृद्धेनसमन्ततः ।।6.44.26।। त्रिकूटःकन्दराकीर्णःप्रव्याहरदिवाचलः ।
transliteration: tenaśabdenamahatāpravṛddhenasamantataḥ  trikūṭaḥkandarākīrṇaḥpravyāharadivācalaḥ |
translation: समन्ततः all over, प्रवृद्धेन risen, महता huge, तेन by that, शब्देन sound, कन्धराकीर्णः groups of caves, त्रिकूटःअचलः Trikuta mountain, प्रव्याहरदिव responded as if it was someone's call.
explanation: Resounding with the sound rising all over the caves of Trikuta mountain echoed and it looked as if the mountain was responding to someone's call.

shloka_text: गोलाङ्गूलामहाकायास्तमसातुल्यवर्चसः ।।6.44.27।। सम्परिष्वज्यबाहुभ्यांभक्षयन्रजनीचरान् ।
transliteration: golāṅgūlāmahākāyāstamasātulyavarcasaḥ  sampariṣvajyabāhubhyāṃbhakṣayanrajanīcarān |
translation: महाकायाः of gigantic body, तमसा dark complexioned, तुल्यवर्चसः highly energetic, गोलाङ्गूलाः endowed with long tails and black face, बाहुभ्याम् with their shoulders, सम्परिष्वज्य holding, रजनीचरान् Rakshasas, भक्षयन् allowed to be devoured.
explanation: The dark complexioned Rakshasas of gigantic body, who were highly energetic were held tightly by the monkeys with black faces and long tails and allowed them to be devoured.

shloka_text: अङ्गदस्तुरणेशत्रूननिहन्तुंसमुपस्थितः ।।6.44.28।। रावणिंनिजघानाशुसारथिंचहयानपि ।
transliteration: aṅgadasturaṇeśatrūnanihantuṃsamupasthitaḥ  rāvaṇiṃnijaghānāśusārathiṃcahayānapi |
translation: रणे in war, शत्रून् enemies, निहन्तुम् killing, समुपस्थितः who stood determined, अङ्गदस्तु Angada's, आशु in no time, रावणिम् Ravana's, सारथिंच charioteer, हयानपि horses also, निजघान wounded.
explanation: Angada who was determined to kill the enemies, in no time wounded Ravana's charioteer and also the horses.

shloka_text: वर्तमानेतदाघोरेसङ्ग्रामेभृशदारुणे ।।6.44.29।। इन्द्रजित्तुरथंत्यक्त्वाहताश्वोहतसारथिः । अङ्गदेनमहामायस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ।।6.44.30।।
transliteration: vartamānetadāghoresaṅgrāmebhṛśadāruṇe  indrajitturathaṃtyaktvāhatāśvohatasārathiḥ | aṅgadenamahāmāyastatraivāntaradhīyata
translation: तदा then, घोरे terrific, भृशदारुणे violent, सङ्ग्रामे from the battlefield, अङ्गदेन by Angada, हताश्वः horses being killed, हतसारथिः charioteer killed, महामायः great cheater, इन्द्रजित्तु Indrajith, तत्स्रैव himself, अन्तरधीयत disappeared.
explanation: As the violent war was going on, the great cheat, Indrajith disappeared from there as Angada had already killed his horses and charioteer.

shloka_text: वर्तमानेतदाघोरेसङ्ग्रामेभृशदारुणे ।।6.44.29।। इन्द्रजित्तुरथंत्यक्त्वाहताश्वोहतसारथिः । अङ्गदेनमहामायस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ।।6.44.30।।
transliteration: vartamānetadāghoresaṅgrāmebhṛśadāruṇe  indrajitturathaṃtyaktvāhatāśvohatasārathiḥ | aṅgadenamahāmāyastatraivāntaradhīyata
translation: तदा then, घोरे terrific, भृशदारुणे violent, सङ्ग्रामे from the battlefield, अङ्गदेन by Angada, हताश्वः horses being killed, हतसारथिः charioteer killed, महामायः great cheater, इन्द्रजित्तु Indrajith, तत्स्रैव himself, अन्तरधीयत disappeared.
explanation: As the violent war was going on, the great cheat, Indrajith disappeared from there as Angada had already killed his horses and charioteer.

shloka_text: तत्कर्मवालिपुत्रस्यसर्वेदेवास्सहर्षिभिः । तुष्टुवुःपूजनार्हस्यतौचोभौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.44.31।।
transliteration: tatkarmavāliputrasyasarvedevāssaharṣibhiḥ | tuṣṭuvuḥpūjanārhasyataucobhaurāmalakṣmaṇau
translation: पूजनार्हस्य one who deserves to be worshipped, वालिपुत्रस्य Vali's son's, तत् कर्म that deed, सहर्षिभिः even sages, सर्वे all, देवाः deities, उभौ both, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshman, तुष्टुवुः praised.
explanation: Angada who was worthy of worship, was praised by even the sages, all deities and both Rama and Lakshmana for his action.

shloka_text: प्रभावंसर्वभूतानिविदुरिन्द्रजितोयुधि । तेनतेतंमहात्मानंतुष्टाःदृष्टवाप्रधर्षितम् ।।6.44.32।।
transliteration: prabhāvaṃsarvabhūtānividurindrajitoyudhi | tenatetaṃmahātmānaṃtuṣṭāḥdṛṣṭavāpradharṣitam
translation: युधि in war, इन्द्रजितः Indrajith, प्रभावम् deeds, सर्वभूतानि all beings, विदुः knew, तेन therefore, महात्मानम् great, ते his, प्रधर्षितम् gratified, तं him, दृष्टवा seeing, तुष्टाः rejoiced.
explanation: All beings present in war were aware of Indrajith's deeds. Therefore, they were gratified to see him defeated.

shloka_text: ततःप्रहृष्टाःकपयस्ससुग्रीवविभीषणाः । साधुसाध्वितिनेदुश्चदृष्टवाशत्रुंप्रधर्षितम् ।।6.44.33।।
transliteration: tataḥprahṛṣṭāḥkapayassasugrīvavibhīṣaṇāḥ | sādhusādhvitineduścadṛṣṭavāśatruṃpradharṣitam
translation: ततः thereafter, ससुग्रीवविभीषणाः Sugriva and Vibheeshana, कपयः all monkeys, शत्रुम् enemy, प्रधर्षितम् gratification, दृष्टवा seeing, प्रहृष्टाः rejoiced, साधुसाध्विति excellent well done, नेदुश्च cried out.
explanation: Thereafter, Sugriva, Vibheeshana and all monkeys gratified with Angada's deed cried out saying "Excellent, Well done".

shloka_text: इन्द्रजित्तुतदातेननिर्जितोभीमकर्मणा । संयुगेवालिपुत्रेणक्रोधंचक्रेसुदारुणम् ।।6.44.34।।
transliteration: indrajittutadātenanirjitobhīmakarmaṇā | saṃyugevāliputreṇakrodhaṃcakresudāruṇam
translation: तदा then, भीमकर्मणा of terrible deeds, तेनवालिपुत्रेण by Vali's son Angada, सम्युगे in the combat, निर्जितः defeated, इन्द्रजित्तु Indrajith, सुदारुणम् terrible, क्रोधम् anger, चक्रे turned.
explanation: Then Indrajith of terrible deeds defeated by Angada in the comb at became terribly angry.

shloka_text: सोऽन्तर्धानगतःपापोरावणीरणकर्कशः । अदृश्योनिशितान्बाणान्मुमोचाशनिवर्चसः ।।6.44.35।।
transliteration: so'ntardhānagataḥpāporāvaṇīraṇakarkaśaḥ | adṛśyoniśitānbāṇānmumocāśanivarcasaḥ
translation: पापः sinful, रणकर्कशः capable of encounter, सःरावणि that Ravana, अदृश्यः rising up, अशनिवर्चसः remaining invisible, निशितान् sharp arrows, बाणान् by arrows, मुमोच remained.
explanation: That sinful son of Ravana, who is capable of encountering rising up remained invisible and shot sharp arrows.

shloka_text: सरामंलक्ष्मणंचैवघोरैर्नागमयैश्शरैः । बिभेदसमरेक्रुद्धःसर्वगात्रेषुराक्षसः ।।6.44.36।।
transliteration: sarāmaṃlakṣmaṇaṃcaivaghorairnāgamayaiśśaraiḥ | bibhedasamarekruddhaḥsarvagātreṣurākṣasaḥ
translation: क्रुद्धः angry, समरे in war, घोरैः terrific, नागमयैः full of serpents, शरैः arrows, राक्षसः Rakshasa, रामंच at Rama, लक्ष्मणंचैव and Lakshmana, सर्वगात्रेषु all over the body, बिभेद pierced.
explanation: The angry Rakshasa (remaining invisible) pierced arrows full of serpents all over the body of Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: माययासम्वृतस्तत्रमोहयन्राघवौयुधि । अदृश्यस्सर्वभूतानांकूटयोधीनिशाचरः ।।6.44.37।। बबन्धशरबन्धेनभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।
transliteration: māyayāsamvṛtastatramohayanrāghavauyudhi | adṛśyassarvabhūtānāṃkūṭayodhīniśācaraḥ  babandhaśarabandhenabhrātaraurāmalakṣmaṇau |
translation: कूटयोधी waging war incognito, निशाचरः Rakshasa, तत्र there, युधि in war, मयया by supernatural power, सम्वृतः surrounded, राघवौ Raghava, मोहयन् in delusion, सर्वभूतानाम् all beings, अदृश्यः, भ्रातरौ brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshman, शरबन्धेन network of arrows, बबन्ध bound.
explanation: The Rakshasa waging war in invisible form with all beings by his supernatural powers fought with both the brothers, Rama and Lakshmana and bound them in a network of arrows.

shloka_text: तेनतौपुरुषव्याघ्रौक्रुद्धेनाशीविषैश्शरैः ।।6.44.38।। सहसानिहतौवीरौतदाप्रैक्षन्तवानराः ।
transliteration: tenataupuruṣavyāghraukruddhenāśīviṣaiśśaraiḥ  sahasānihatauvīrautadāpraikṣantavānarāḥ |
translation: तदा then, वानराः Vanara, क्रुद्धेन by angry, तेन their, आशीविषैः like venomous monkeys, शरैः arrows, सहसा forcibly, अनिहतौ bound, वीरौ warriors, पुरुषव्याघ्रौ tigers among men, तौ they both, प्रैक्षन्त beheld.
explanation: Then the Vanaras beheld the two brothers, tigers among men bound forcibly by the angry Rakshasas like venomous monkeys.

shloka_text: प्रकाशरूपस्तुतदानशक्तस्तौबाधितुंराक्षसराजपुत्रः । मायांप्रयोक्तुंसमुपाजगामबबन्धतौराजसुतौदुरात्मा ।।6.44.39।।
transliteration: prakāśarūpastutadānaśaktastaubādhituṃrākṣasarājaputraḥ | māyāṃprayoktuṃsamupājagāmababandhataurājasutaudurātmā
translation: तदा then, राक्षसराजपुत्रः Rakshasa king's son, प्रकाशरूपः bright form, तौ both, बाधितुम् to bind, नशक्तः incapable, मायाम् deceitfully, प्रयोक्तुम् using, समुपाजगाम remaining invisible, दुरात्मा evil minded, तौ both, राजसुतौ king's sons, बबन्ध bound.
explanation: Then the evil minded Rakshasa king's son, being incapable of getting bound in visible form, by remaining invisible, bound them deceitfully. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेचतुश्चत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty fourth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सतस्यगतिमन्विच्छन्राजपुत्रःप्रतापवान् । दिदेशातिबलोरामोदशवानरयूथपान् ।।6.45.1।।
transliteration: satasyagatimanvicchanrājaputraḥpratāpavān | dideśātibalorāmodaśavānarayūthapān
translation: राजपुत्रः king's son, प्रतापवान् powerful, अतिबलः very strong, सःरामः Rama, तस्य his, गतिम् where about, अन्विच्छन् to know, दश ten, वानरयूथपान् Vanara troops, दिदेश assigned.
explanation: Rama, the son of the king, a powerful and strong warrior, ordered ten Vanaras to know the whereabouts (of Indrajith).
comments: Sri Rama and Lakshmana get distressed by the arrows pierced and the Vanaras become despondent.

shloka_text: द्वौसुषेणस्यदायादौनीलंचप्लवगर्षपम् । अङ्गदंवालिपुत्रंचशरभंचतरस्विनम् ।।6.45.2।। विनतंजाम्बवन्तंचसानुप्रस्थंमहाबलम् । ऋषभंचर्षभस्कन्थमादिदेशपरन्तपः ।।6.45.3।।
transliteration: dvausuṣeṇasyadāyādaunīlaṃcaplavagarṣapam | aṅgadaṃvāliputraṃcaśarabhaṃcatarasvinam  vinataṃjāmbavantaṃcasānuprasthaṃmahābalam | ṛṣabhaṃcarṣabhaskanthamādideśaparantapaḥ
translation: परन्तप scorcher of enemies, सुषेणस्य to Sushena, द्वौ both, दायादौ Dwivida, प्लवगर्षपम् best of Vanaras, नीलंच and Neela, जाम्बवन्तंच and Jambavantha, अङ्गदम् Angada, तरस्विनम् courageous, शरभंच Sarabha, विनतंच Vinatha, हनूमन्तम् Hanumantha, महाबलम् mighty strong, सानुप्रस्थम् Sanuprastha, ऋषभंच and Rshabam, ऋषभस्कन्धम् Rshaba Skanda, आदिदेश ordered.
explanation: Rama, the scorcher of enemies, ordered the two sons of Sushena, the best of Vanaras Neela, Jambavantha, Angada, as well as courageous Sarabha, Vinatha, and Hanumantha and Sanuprastha endowed with extraordinary might, also Rshaba and Rshaba Skanda.

shloka_text: द्वौसुषेणस्यदायादौनीलंचप्लवगर्षपम् । अङ्गदंवालिपुत्रंचशरभंचतरस्विनम् ।।6.45.2।। विनतंजाम्बवन्तंचसानुप्रस्थंमहाबलम् । ऋषभंचर्षभस्कन्थमादिदेशपरन्तपः ।।6.45.3।।
transliteration: dvausuṣeṇasyadāyādaunīlaṃcaplavagarṣapam | aṅgadaṃvāliputraṃcaśarabhaṃcatarasvinam  vinataṃjāmbavantaṃcasānuprasthaṃmahābalam | ṛṣabhaṃcarṣabhaskanthamādideśaparantapaḥ
translation: परन्तप scorcher of enemies, सुषेणस्य to Sushena, द्वौ both, दायादौ Dwivida, प्लवगर्षपम् best of Vanaras, नीलंच and Neela, जाम्बवन्तंच and Jambavantha, अङ्गदम् Angada, तरस्विनम् courageous, शरभंच Sarabha, विनतंच Vinatha, हनूमन्तम् Hanumantha, महाबलम् mighty strong, सानुप्रस्थम् Sanuprastha, ऋषभंच and Rshabam, ऋषभस्कन्धम् Rshaba Skanda, आदिदेश ordered.
explanation: Rama, the scorcher of enemies, ordered the two sons of Sushena, the best of Vanaras Neela, Jambavantha, Angada, as well as courageous Sarabha, Vinatha, and Hanumantha and Sanuprastha endowed with extraordinary might, also Rshaba and Rshaba Skanda.

shloka_text: तेसम्प्रहृष्टाहरयोभीमानुद्यम्यपादपान् । आकाशंविविशुस्सर्वेमार्गमाणादिशोदशः ।।6.45.4।।
transliteration: tesamprahṛṣṭāharayobhīmānudyamyapādapān | ākāśaṃviviśussarvemārgamāṇādiśodaśaḥ
translation: सर्वे all, तेहरयः those monkeys, सम्प्रहृष्टाः exceedingly delighted, भीमान् huge, मार्गमाणा searching, दिशोदशः ten directions, पादपान् held huge trees, आकाशं sky, विविशुस्सर्वे sprang.
explanation: All those monkeys, exceedingly rejoiced, held huge trees, and went in ten directions searching and sprang to the sky.

shloka_text: तेषांवेगवतांवेगमिषुभिर्वेगवत्तरैः । अस्त्रवित्परमास्तैरैस्तुवारयामासरावणिः ।।6.45.5।।
transliteration: teṣāṃvegavatāṃvegamiṣubhirvegavattaraiḥ | astravitparamāstairaistuvārayāmāsarāvaṇiḥ
translation: अस्त्रवित् skilled in the use of weapons, रावणिः Ravana's son, परमास्तै: expert in mystic weapons, वेगवत्तरैः endowed with speed, इषुभिः arrows, वेगवताम् charged with energy, तेषाम् them, वेगम् swiftly, वारयामास prohibited
explanation: Ravana's son being skilled in the use of weapons and an expert in mystic powers, he prohibited the speed of the Vanaras with his swift arrows.

shloka_text: तंभीममार्गमाणादिशोदशःवेगाहरयोनाराचैःक्षतविग्रहाः । अन्धकारेनददृशुर्मेघैस्सूर्यमिवावृतम् ।।6.45.6।।
transliteration: taṃbhīmamārgamāṇādiśodaśaḥvegāharayonārācaiḥkṣatavigrahāḥ | andhakārenadadṛśurmeghaissūryamivāvṛtam
translation: नाराचैः iron arrows, क्षतविग्रहाः mangled, भीमवेगाः endowed with high speed, हरयः Vanaras, अन्धकारे in utter darkness, तम् him, Indrajith मेघैः cloud, आवृतम् covered, सूर्यमिव like Sun, नददृशुः not seen.
explanation: The Vanaras were mangled with iron arrows, however endowed with high speed they could not make out Indrajith in utter darkness just as the sun covered by clouds.

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणयोरेवसर्वदेहभिदश्शरान् । भृशमावेशयामासरावणिस्समितिञ्जयः ।।6.45.7।।
transliteration: rāmalakṣmaṇayorevasarvadehabhidaśśarān | bhṛśamāveśayāmāsarāvaṇissamitiñjayaḥ
translation: समितिञ्जयः ever victorious, रावणिः Indrajith, सर्वदेहभिदः all over the body, शरान् arrows, भृशम् repeatedly, रामलक्ष्मणयोरेव on Rama and Lakshmana, आवेशयामास pierced.
explanation: Indrajith who is ever victorious, pierced repeatedly arrows all over the body of Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: निरन्तरशीरीरौतुतावुभौरामलक्ष्मणौ । क्रुद्धेनेन्द्रजितावीरौपन्नगैश्शरतांगतैः ।।6.45.8।।
transliteration: nirantaraśīrīraututāvubhaurāmalakṣmaṇau | kruddhenendrajitāvīraupannagaiśśaratāṃgataiḥ
translation: वीरौ heroic, तौ they, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, उभौ both, क्रुद्धेन furious, इन्द्रजिता Indrajith, शरताम् with arrows, गतैः pierced, पन्नगैः serpents, निरन्तरशरीरौ all over the body
explanation: Both Rama and Lakshmana were pierced by furious Indrajith with serpents like arrows furious.

shloka_text: तयोःक्षतजमार्गेणसुस्रावरुधिरंबहु । तावुभौचप्रकाशेतेपुष्पिताविवकिंशुकौ ।।6.45.9।।
transliteration: tayoḥkṣatajamārgeṇasusrāvarudhiraṃbahu | tāvubhaucaprakāśetepuṣpitāvivakiṃśukau
translation: तयोः both of them, क्षतजमार्गेण wounded profusely, बहु excessively, रुधिरम् red with blood, सुस्राव flowing, तौ they, उभौ both, पुष्पितौ flowery, किंशुकौइव like Kimsuka trees, प्रकाशितौ looked bright.
explanation: Both Rama and Lakshmana bleeding excessively, wounded profusely, looked bright and red like Kimsuka trees with flowers.

shloka_text: ततःपर्यन्तरक्ताक्षोभिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमः । रावणिर्भ्रातरौवाक्यमन्तर्धानगतोऽब्रवीत् ।।6.45.10।।
transliteration: tataḥparyantaraktākṣobhinnāñjanacayopamaḥ | rāvaṇirbhrātarauvākyamantardhānagato'bravīt
translation: ततः then, पर्यन्तरक्ताक्षः corners of eyes turned red, भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमः like a huge collyrium, रावणिः Ravana's son, अन्तर्धानगतः vanished, भ्रातरौ brothers, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Then Ravana's son with the corner of his eyes turned red in anger looking like a huge collyrium, vanished from there and spoke these words to the two brothers, Rama, and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: युध्यमानमनालक्षयंशक्रोऽपित्रिदशेश्वरः । द्रष्टुमासादितुंवापिनशक्तःकिंपुनर्युवाम् ।।6.45.11।।
transliteration: yudhyamānamanālakṣayaṃśakro'pitridaśeśvaraḥ | draṣṭumāsādituṃvāpinaśaktaḥkiṃpunaryuvām
translation: अनालक्षयम् who has fire like eyes, युध्यमानम् while fighting war, त्रिदशेश्वरः Lord of gods, शक्रोऽपि Indra also, द्रष्टुम् to see, आसादितुंनापि cannot discern, नशक्तः not possible, युवाम् for you, किंपुनः why again
explanation: Indrajith who had fire like eyes, said," even the ruler of gods cannot discern while I am fighting war, why speak about you? It is not possible."

shloka_text: प्रावृताविषुजालेनराघवौकङ्कपत्रिणा । एषरोषपरीतात्मानयामियमसादनम् ।।6.45.12।।
transliteration: prāvṛtāviṣujālenarāghavaukaṅkapatriṇā | eṣaroṣaparītātmānayāmiyamasādanam
translation: राघवौ Raghava brothers, कङ्कपत्रिणा plumes of arrows, शरजालेन by the fire of arrows, प्रावृतौ enmeshed, रोषपरीतात्मा my anger, एषः in that way, यमसादनम् to the abode of Lord of death, नयामि am about to senddispatch you.
explanation: "Raghava brothers! You are enmeshed with plumes of arrows all over the body. My anger will not go waste. I will send you to the abode of Yama, the Lord of death."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वातुधर्मज्ञौभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ । निर्बिभेदशितैर्बाणैःप्रजहर्षननादच ।।6.45.13।।
transliteration: evamuktvātudharmajñaubhrātaraurāmalakṣmaṇau | nirbibhedaśitairbāṇaiḥprajaharṣananādaca
translation: धर्मज्ञौ righteous, भ्रातरौ brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, एवम् in that way, उक्त्वा having been told, शितैः stood, बाणैः arrows, निर्बिभेद paining, प्रजहर्ष rejoiced, ननादच roaring aloud.
explanation: Indrajith having spoken to the righteous brothers Rama and Lakshmana in that way, began to pain them with arrows and stood rejoiced roaring aloud.

shloka_text: भिन्नाञ्जनचयश्यामोविष्फार्यविपुलंधनुः । भूयोभूयश्शरान्घोरान् विससर्जमहामृथे ।।6.45.14।।
transliteration: bhinnāñjanacayaśyāmoviṣphāryavipulaṃdhanuḥ | bhūyobhūyaśśarānghorān visasarjamahāmṛthe
translation: भिन्नाञ्जनचयश्यामः like a crushed black hill, विपुलम् huge, धनुः bow, विस्फार्यः mounting, महामृथे great conflict, भूयोभूय again and again, घोरान् terrific, शरान् arrows, विससर्ज released.
explanation: Indrajith who was like a mass of crushed black hill, mounting the huge bow released terrific arrows again and again in that great conflict.

shloka_text: ततोमर्मसुमर्मज्ञोमज्जयननिशितान् शरान् । रामलक्ष्मणयोर्वीरोननदाचमुहुर्मुहुः ।।6.45.15।।
transliteration: tatomarmasumarmajñomajjayananiśitān śarān | rāmalakṣmaṇayorvīronanadācamuhurmuhuḥ
translation: मर्मज्ञः vital, वीरः warrior, ततः thereafter, रामलक्ष्मणयोः Rama and Lakshmana, मर्मसु vital parts, निशितान् sharp, शरान् arrows, मज्जयन् digging, मुहुर्मुहुः again and again, ननादच kept roaring.
explanation: There after that warrior went on digging sharp arrows into the vital parts of Rama and Lakshmana again and again and kept roaring.

shloka_text: बद्धौतुशरशब्देनतावुभौरणमूर्धनि । निमेषान्तरमात्रेणनशेकतुदीक्षितुम् ।।6.45.16।।
transliteration: baddhautuśaraśabdenatāvubhauraṇamūrdhani | nimeṣāntaramātreṇanaśekatudīkṣitum
translation: रणमूर्धनि facing the battle, निमेषान्तरमात्रेण in a fraction of twinkling of an eye, बद्धौ bound, तौउभौ both of them, उदीक्षितुम् to retaliate, नशेकतुः not have energy.
explanation: In a fraction of a second, both Rama and Lakshmana facing the battle were bound by arrows and did not have energy to retaliate.

shloka_text: ततोविभिन्नसर्वाङ्गौशरशल्याचितावुभौ । ध्वजाविवमहेन्द्रस्यरज्जुमुक्तौप्रकम्पितौ ।।6.45.17।। तौसम्प्रचलितौवीरौमर्मभेदेनकर्शितौ । निपेततुर्महेष्वासौजगत्यांजगतीपती ।।6.45.18।।
transliteration: tatovibhinnasarvāṅgauśaraśalyācitāvubhau | dhvajāvivamahendrasyarajjumuktauprakampitau  tausampracalitauvīraumarmabhedenakarśitau | nipetaturmaheṣvāsaujagatyāṃjagatīpatī
translation: ततः and then, विभिन्नसर्वाङ्गौ pierced all over the body, शरशल्याचितौ with heads of arrows, कृतौ staggered, रज्जुमुक्तौ freed from their cords, प्रकम्पितौ violently, महेन्द्रस्य Indra's ध्वजाविव like banners, सम्प्रचलितौ shaking, वीरौ heroes, मर्मभेदेन in vital parts, कर्शितौ pained, महेष्वासौ gallant princes, जगतीपती Lords of the world, तौ both, जगत्याम् world, निपेततुः fell.
explanation: Pierced all over their bodies with the heads of arrows, the gallant princes freed themselves from the cords by shaking violently like the banners of Indra. Pained by the hurting of the vital parts of both the princes, the Lords of the world fell.

shloka_text: ततोविभिन्नसर्वाङ्गौशरशल्याचितावुभौ । ध्वजाविवमहेन्द्रस्यरज्जुमुक्तौप्रकम्पितौ ।।6.45.17।। तौसम्प्रचलितौवीरौमर्मभेदेनकर्शितौ । निपेततुर्महेष्वासौजगत्यांजगतीपती ।।6.45.18।।
transliteration: tatovibhinnasarvāṅgauśaraśalyācitāvubhau | dhvajāvivamahendrasyarajjumuktauprakampitau  tausampracalitauvīraumarmabhedenakarśitau | nipetaturmaheṣvāsaujagatyāṃjagatīpatī
translation: ततः and then, विभिन्नसर्वाङ्गौ pierced all over the body, शरशल्याचितौ with heads of arrows, कृतौ staggered, रज्जुमुक्तौ freed from their cords, प्रकम्पितौ violently, महेन्द्रस्य Indra's ध्वजाविव like banners, सम्प्रचलितौ shaking, वीरौ heroes, मर्मभेदेन in vital parts, कर्शितौ pained, महेष्वासौ gallant princes, जगतीपती Lords of the world, तौ both, जगत्याम् world, निपेततुः fell.
explanation: Pierced all over their bodies with the heads of arrows, the gallant princes freed themselves from the cords by shaking violently like the banners of Indra. Pained by the hurting of the vital parts of both the princes, the Lords of the world fell.

shloka_text: तौवीरशयनेवीरौशयानौरुधिरोक्षितौ । शरवेष्टितसर्वाङ्गैवार्तौपरमपीडितौ ।।6.45.19।।
transliteration: tauvīraśayanevīrauśayānaurudhirokṣitau | śaraveṣṭitasarvāṅgaivārtauparamapīḍitau
translation: वीरशयने warrior's bed, शयानौ bed, रुधिरोक्षितौ drenched in blood, शरवेष्टितसर्वाङ्गै all their limbs covered with arrows, परमपीडितौ highly distressed, तौवीरौ those warriors, आर्तौ lying.
explanation: The princes were lying on the warrior's bed in the battlefield, their limbs fully covered with arrows, in a highly distressed state.

shloka_text: नह्यविद्धंतयोर्गात्रेबभूवाङ्गुळमन्तरम् । नानिर्भिन्नंनचास्तब्दमाकराग्रादजिह्मगैः ।।6.45.20।।
transliteration: nahyaviddhaṃtayorgātrebabhūvāṅguḻamantaram | nānirbhinnaṃnacāstabdamākarāgrādajihmagaiḥ
translation: योः their, गात्रे in the body, अविद्धम् not wounded, अङ्गुळमात्रम् not even finger breadth space (an inch of space), अन्तरम् all over, नबभूव remained without being pierced, अजिह्मगैः unhurt, आकराग्रात् not even a part of the body was left, अनिर्भिन्नम् not wounded, अस्तब्दम् unshaken, न not.
explanation: Not an inch of space on their bodies remained without being pierced. Not even a part of the body was left unshaken, unhurt, or wounded.

shloka_text: तौतुक्रूरेणनिहतौरक्षसाकामरूपिणा । असृक्सुस्रुवतुस्तीव्रंजलंप्रस्रवणाविव ।।6.45.21।।
transliteration: tautukrūreṇanihataurakṣasākāmarūpiṇā | asṛksusruvatustīvraṃjalaṃprasravaṇāviva
translation: क्रूरेण by the cruel, कामरूपिणा capable of acquiring desired form, रक्षसा Rakshasa, निहतौ wounded, तौ both, प्रस्रवणौ flowed, जलम् इव like water, तीव्रम् copiously, असृक् vital breaths, सुस्रुवतुः brought forth.
explanation: Wounded by the cruel Rakshasas capable of changing form at their will, blood flowed from their body copiously like water from spring bringing out their vital life breaths.

shloka_text: पपातप्रथमंरामोविद्धोमर्मसुमार्गणैः । क्रोधादिन्द्रजितायेनपुराशक्रोविनिर्जितः ।।6.45.22।।
transliteration: papātaprathamaṃrāmoviddhomarmasumārgaṇaiḥ | krodhādindrajitāyenapurāśakrovinirjitaḥ
translation: येन by whom, पुरा earlier, शक्रः Indra, विनिर्जितः utterly defeated, इन्द्रजिता Indrajith, क्रोधात् in anger, मार्गणैः arrows, मर्मसु vital parts, विद्धः, रामः Rama, प्रधमम् first, पपात fell.
explanation: Rama fell first pierced by arrows in his vital parts released in anger by Indrajith, by whom Indra was utterly defeated.

shloka_text: रुक्मपुङ्खैःप्रसन्नाग्रैरधोगतिभिराशुगैः । नाराचैरर्धनाराचैर्भल्लैरञ्जलिकैरपि ।।6.45.23।। विव्याधवत्सदन्तैश्चसिंहदंष्ट्रैःक्षुरैस्तथा ।
transliteration: rukmapuṅkhaiḥprasannāgrairadhogatibhirāśugaiḥ | nārācairardhanārācairbhallairañjalikairapi  vivyādhavatsadantaiścasiṃhadaṃṣṭraiḥkṣuraistathā |
translation: रुक्मपुङ्खैः coated with gold, प्रसन्नाग्रैः pure bright tips, अधोगतिभिः descending unobstructed like dust, आशुगैः quickly, नाराचैः with even and circular heads, अर्थनाराचैः halfmoon shaped heads, भल्लैः axe like heads, अञ्जलिकैरपि heads like joined palms, वत्सदन्तैश्च heads resembling teeth of calf, सिंहदंष्ट्रैः like lion's teeth, तथा in the same way, क्षुरैः heads as sharp as a razor, विव्याध hurt.
explanation: Indrajith pierced Rama with arrows coated with gold and gold tipped arrows, which had even and circular heads, with halfmoon arrows, with axe like heads, heads like joined palms, heads resembling teeth of calf and lion teeth arrows as well as razor sharp arrows which descended quickly unobstructed like dust.

shloka_text: सवीरशयनेशिश्येविज्यमादायकार्मुकम् ।।6.45.24।। भिन्नमुष्टिपरीणाहंत्रिणतंरुक्मभूषितम् ।
transliteration: savīraśayaneśiśyevijyamādāyakārmukam  bhinnamuṣṭiparīṇāhaṃtriṇataṃrukmabhūṣitam |
translation: सः he, Rama, विज्यम् quitting, भिन्नमुष्टिपरीणाहम् strung and bent at both ends, three places, रुक्मभूषितम् gold plated, कार्मुकम् bow, आदाय holding, वीरशयने hero's bed, शिश्ये relaxed.
explanation: Rama lay relaxed on the hero's bed quitting his goldplated bow strung and bent at both ends, and the middle.

shloka_text: बाणपातान्तरेरामंपतितंपुरुषर्षभम् ।।6.45.25।। सतत्रलक्ष्मणोदृष्टवानिराशोजीवितेऽभवत् ।
transliteration: bāṇapātāntarerāmaṃpatitaṃpuruṣarṣabham  satatralakṣmaṇodṛṣṭavānirāśojīvite'bhavat |
translation: लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, तत्र there, बाणपातान्तरे at an arrow's throw, पतितम् fallen, पुरुषर्षभम् best of men, दृष्टवा beholding, जीविते life, निराशः disappointed, अभवत् remained.
explanation: Lakshmana remained beholding the best of men fallen at an arrow's throw disappointed at his life.

shloka_text: रामंकमलपत्राक्षंशरबन्धपरिक्षतम् ।।6.45.26।। शुशोचभ्रातरंदृष्टवापतितंधरणीतले ।
transliteration: rāmaṃkamalapatrākṣaṃśarabandhaparikṣatam  śuśocabhrātaraṃdṛṣṭavāpatitaṃdharaṇītale |
translation: कमलपत्राक्षम् lotus petal eyed, भ्रातरम् brother, रामम् at Rama, शरबन्धपरिक्षतम् pained by pierced arrows, धरणीतले on the ground, पतितम् fallen, दृष्टवा seeing, शुशोच grieved.
explanation: Lakshmana grieved seeing his elder brother Rama pierced by arrows, pained, and fallen on the ground.

shloka_text: हरयश्चापितंदृष्टवासन्तापंपरमंगताः ।।6.45.27।। शोकार्ताश्चुक्रशुर्घोरमश्रुपूरितलोचनाः ।
transliteration: harayaścāpitaṃdṛṣṭavāsantāpaṃparamaṃgatāḥ  śokārtāścukraśurghoramaśrupūritalocanāḥ |
translation: हरयश्चापि even the monkeys, तम् him, दृष्टवा beholding, परमम् very, सन्तापम् much stricken, गताः fallen, शोकार्ताः in agony, अश्रुपूरियलोचनाः their eyes filled with tears, घोरम् terrible, चुक्रुशुः shrieked.
explanation: Even the monkeys' eyes were filled with tears, very much stricken with grief seeing Rama fallen and shrieked.

shloka_text: बद्धौतुवीरौपतितौशयानौतेवानरास्सम्परिवार्यतस्थुः । समागतावायुसुतप्रमुख्याविषादमार्ताःपरमंचजग्मुः ।।6.45.28।।
transliteration: baddhautuvīraupatitauśayānautevānarāssamparivāryatasthuḥ | samāgatāvāyusutapramukhyāviṣādamārtāḥparamaṃcajagmuḥ
translation: वायुसुतप्रमुख्याः wind god's son's army, तेवानराः the Vanaras, समागताः collected together, बद्धौ bound, वीरौपतितौ fallen heroes, शयानौ lying, तौ both, सम्परिवार्य surrounding, तस्थुः stood, आर्ताः despondent, परमम् extremely, विषादम् sorrow, जग्मुःच remained.
explanation: Hanuman's army of Vanaras collected together stood surrounding fallen princes lying on the ground, despondent and extremely sorrowful. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेपञ्चचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty fifth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततोद्यांपृथिवींचैववीक्षमाणावनौकसः । ददृशुःसन्ततौबाणैर्भ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.46.1।।
transliteration: tatodyāṃpṛthivīṃcaivavīkṣamāṇāvanaukasaḥ | dadṛśuḥsantataubāṇairbhrātaraurāmalakṣmaṇau
translation: ततः thereafter, द्याम् at the sky, पृथिवींचैव on the ground, वीक्षमाणा seeing, वनौकसः Vanara leaders, बाणैः arrows, सन्ततौ, भ्रातरौ brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, ददृशुः saw.
explanation: Thereafter looking at the sky and the ground for Rama and Lakshmana, the Vanara leaders saw the two brothers, lying on the ground hurt by arrows.
comments: The vanaras feel frustrated seeing Rama and Lakshmana enmeshed and lying on the ground. Vibheeshana exhorts Sugriva and sees Indrajith hiding. Indrajith reports to Ravana that Rama and Lakshman are killed by him.

shloka_text: वृष्टवेवोपरतेदेवेकृतकर्मणिराक्षसे । आजगामाथतंदेशंससुग्रीवोविभीषणः ।।6.46.2।।
transliteration: vṛṣṭavevoparatedevekṛtakarmaṇirākṣase | ājagāmāthataṃdeśaṃsasugrīvovibhīṣaṇaḥ
translation: देवे cloud, वृष्टवेव after raining, राक्षसे Rakshasa, कृतकर्मणि having completed the task, उपरते retired, अथ and then, विभीषणः Vibheeshana, ससुग्रीवः Sugriva, तंदेशम् that location, आजगाम reached.
explanation: Indrajith retired after completing the task, like a cloud that retires after raining. Then came Vibheeshana and Sugriva to that location.

shloka_text: नीलद्विविदमैन्दाश्चसुषेणःकुमुदाङ्गदा: । तूर्णंहनुमतासार्धमन्वशोचन्तराघवौ ।।6.46.3।।
transliteration: nīladvividamaindāścasuṣeṇaḥkumudāṅgadā: | tūrṇaṃhanumatāsārdhamanvaśocantarāghavau
translation: नीलश्च Neela and, द्विविदः Dwivida, मैन्दः Mainda, सुषेणः Sushena, कुमुदः Kumuda, अङ्गदा: Angada, हनुमतासार्धम् accompanied by Hanuman, तूर्णम् intensely, राघवौ Ragahavas, अन्वशोचन्त grieved looking at.
explanation: Neela, Dwivida, Mainda, Sushena, Kumuda, Angada accompanied by Hanuman grieved intensely on looking at the Raghavas.

shloka_text: अचेष्टौमन्दनिश्श्वासौशोणितौघपरिप्लुतौ । शरजालाचितौस्तब्दौशयानौशरतल्पयोः ।।6.46.4।। निःश्वसन्तौयथासर्पौनिश्चेष्टौमन्दविक्रमौ । रुधिरस्राद्विग्धाङ्गौतापनीयाविवध्वजौ ।।6.46.5।। तौवीरशयनेवीरौशयानौमन्दचेष्टितौ । यूथपैस्तै: परिवृतौबाष्पव्याकुललोचनैः ।।6.46.6।। राघवौपतितौदृष्टवाशरजालसमावृतौ । बभूवुर्वेर्व्यथितास्सर्वेवानरास्सविभीषणाः ।।6.46.7।।
transliteration: aceṣṭaumandaniśśvāsauśoṇitaughapariplutau | śarajālācitaustabdauśayānauśaratalpayoḥ  niḥśvasantauyathāsarpauniśceṣṭaumandavikramau | rudhirasrādvigdhāṅgautāpanīyāvivadhvajau  tauvīraśayanevīrauśayānaumandaceṣṭitau | yūthapaistai: parivṛtaubāṣpavyākulalocanaiḥ  rāghavaupatitaudṛṣṭavāśarajālasamāvṛtau | babhūvurvervyathitāssarvevānarāssavibhīṣaṇāḥ
translation: अचेष्टौ unable to move, मन्दनिश्श्वासौ with feeble breath, शोणितौघ drenched in blood, परिप्लुतौ covered all over, शरजालाचितौ with arrows, स्तब्दौ motionless, शयानौ on bed, शरतल्पयोः of arrows, सर्पौयथा like serpents, निश्श्वसन्तौ feeble breath, निश्चेष्टौ stunned, मन्दचेष्टितौ inactive, रुधिरस्राद्विग्धाङ्गौ drenched in blood, तापनीयौ distressed, ध्वजौइव like posts, वीरशयने heroic bed, शयानौ lying, वीरौ heroes, मन्दविक्रमौ prowess reduced, बाष्पव्याकुललोचनैः eyes filled with tears, स्सैः breath, यूथपैः army, परिवृतौ surrounded by, शरजालसमावृतौ network of arrows, तौराघवौ both the scions, दृष्टवा seeing, सविभीषणाः Vibheeshana, सर्वे all, वानराः Vanara, व्यथिताः worried, बभूवुः appeared.
explanation: Unable to move, with feeble breath, drenched in blood and the body covered all over with arrows, lying on a bed of arrows, stunned, with reduced prowess, sighing like serpents, the heroes, Rama, and Lakshmana, who were like golden posts became dull. Rama and Lakshmana were lying on a heroic bed, arrows stuck to the bodies. Vibheeshana and all the Vanaras kept seeing both the scions and wept surrounding them.

shloka_text: अचेष्टौमन्दनिश्श्वासौशोणितौघपरिप्लुतौ । शरजालाचितौस्तब्दौशयानौशरतल्पयोः ।।6.46.4।। निःश्वसन्तौयथासर्पौनिश्चेष्टौमन्दविक्रमौ । रुधिरस्राद्विग्धाङ्गौतापनीयाविवध्वजौ ।।6.46.5।। तौवीरशयनेवीरौशयानौमन्दचेष्टितौ । यूथपैस्तै: परिवृतौबाष्पव्याकुललोचनैः ।।6.46.6।। राघवौपतितौदृष्टवाशरजालसमावृतौ । बभूवुर्वेर्व्यथितास्सर्वेवानरास्सविभीषणाः ।।6.46.7।।

shloka_text: अन्तरिक्षंनिरीक्षन्तोदिशस्सर्वाश्चवानराः । नचैनंमाययाछन्नंददृशूरावणिःरणे ।।6.46.8।।
transliteration: antarikṣaṃnirīkṣantodiśassarvāścavānarāḥ | nacainaṃmāyayāchannaṃdadṛśūrāvaṇiḥraṇe
translation: अन्तरिक्षम् sky, सर्वाः all over, दिशश्च directions, निरीक्षन्तः looking, वानराः Vanaras, रणे battle, मायया mystical power, चैनं not find, छन्नम् searched, एनम् all over, रावणिम् Indrajith, ददृशुः could not see.
explanation: Though the Vanaras searched all over the battlefield and in all directions of the sky, they could not see Indrajith of mystical powers.

shloka_text: तंतुमायाप्रतिच्छन्नंमाययैवविभीषणः । वीक्षमाणोददर्शाथभ्रातुःपुत्रमवस्थितम् ।।6.46.9।।
transliteration: taṃtumāyāpraticchannaṃmāyayaivavibhīṣaṇaḥ | vīkṣamāṇodadarśāthabhrātuḥputramavasthitam
translation: विभीषणः Vibheeshana, माययैव occult, वीक्षमाणः started looking, मायाप्रतिच्छन्नम् searched with occult powers, अथ and then, अवस्थितम् stood, तम् his, भ्रातुःपुत्रम् brother's son, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Vibheeshana started looking with occult powers for his brother's son endowed with occult power following occult means and found Indrajith.

shloka_text: तमप्रतिकर्माणमप्रतिद्वन्द्वमाहवे । ददर्शान्तर्हितंवीरंवरदानाद्विभीषणः ।।6.46.10।। तेजसायशसाचैवविक्रमेणचसम्युतम् ।
transliteration: tamapratikarmāṇamapratidvandvamāhave | dadarśāntarhitaṃvīraṃvaradānādvibhīṣaṇaḥ  tejasāyaśasācaivavikrameṇacasamyutam |
translation: तेजसा brilliant, यशसाचैव glory, विक्रमेणच capable of difficult deeds, सम्युतम् endowed with, विभीषणः Vibheeshana, अप्रतिमकर्माणम् incomparable in his task, आहवे in fight, अप्रतिद्वन्दम् unrivalled in battle, वरदानात् by virtue of a boon, अन्तर्हितम् hidden, तम् him, वीरम् hero, ददर्श seen.
explanation: Brilliant and glorious Vibheeshana, capable of difficult deeds, incomparable at work, and in fight, unrivalled in battle, saw the hidden hero Indrajith by virtue of a boon (from Brahma).

shloka_text: इन्द्रजित्त्वात्मनःकर्मतौशयानौसमीक्ष्यच ।।6.46.11।। उवाचपरमप्रीतोहर्षयन् सर्वनैरृतान् ।
transliteration: indrajittvātmanaḥkarmatauśayānausamīkṣyaca  uvācaparamaprītoharṣayan sarvanairṛtān |
translation: इन्द्रजित्तु Indrajith, आत्मनः himself, कर्म action, शयानौ on the bed, तौच both, समीक्ष्य reviewing, परमप्रीतः very happily, सर्वनैरृतान् to all Rakshasas, हर्षयन् making to rejoice, उवाच spoke.
explanation: Reviewing the scions lying on bed by his action, Indrajith caused extreme joy to all Rakshasas and spoke.

shloka_text: दूषणस्यचहन्तारौखरस्यचमहाबलौ ।।6.46.12।। सादितौमामकैर्बाणैर्भ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।
transliteration: dūṣaṇasyacahantāraukharasyacamahābalau  sāditaumāmakairbāṇairbhrātaraurāmalakṣmaṇau |
translation: दूषणस्यच Dushana, खरस्यच and Khara, हन्तारौ slayer, महाबलौ very strong, भ्रातरौ brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, मामकैः by my, बाणैः arrows, सादितौ struck.
explanation: "The two brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, who slayed Dushana and Khara have been struck."

shloka_text: नेमौमोक्षयितुंशक्यावेतस्मादिषुबन्धनात् ।।6.46.13।। सर्वैरपिसमागम्यसर्षिसङ्घैस्सुरासुरैः ।
transliteration: nemaumokṣayituṃśakyāvetasmādiṣubandhanāt  sarvairapisamāgamyasarṣisaṅghaissurāsuraiḥ |
translation: सर्वैः all, सर्षिसङ्घैः sages, सुरासुरैः Devatas and Rakshasas, समागम्य collected together, इमौ this, एतस्मात् by them, इषुबन्धनात् to rid of this network, मोक्षयितुम् liberate, नशक्यौ not possible.
explanation: "Even if all the sages, Devatas and Rakshasas collected together come, they cannot get liberated from this bondage of arrows."

shloka_text: यत्कृतेचिन्तयानस्यशोकार्तस्यपितुर्मम ।।6.46.14।। अस्पृष्टवाशयनंगात्रैस्त्रियामायातिशर्वरी । त्स्नेयंयत्कृतेलङ्कानदीवर्षास्विवाकुला ।।6.46.15।। सोऽयंमूलहरोऽनर्थःसर्वेषांनिहतोमया ।
transliteration: yatkṛtecintayānasyaśokārtasyapiturmama  aspṛṣṭavāśayanaṃgātraistriyāmāyātiśarvarī | tsneyaṃyatkṛtelaṅkānadīvarṣāsvivākulā  so'yaṃmūlaharo'narthaḥsarveṣāṃnihatomayā |
translation: यत्कृकते on whose account, चिन्तयानस्य with this thought, शोकार्तस्य is in grief, ममपितुः my father, गात्रैः body, शयनम् bed, अस्पृष्टवा not understood clearly, त्रियामा three periods, शर्वरी night, याति passed away, यत्कृते by what action, कृत्स्ना dark, इयंलङ्का this Lanka, वर्षासु raining, नदीइव like river, आकुला agitated, सः he, अयम् all, सर्वेषाम् all of us, मूलहरः root cause, अनर्थः got rid of, मया by me, निहतः killed.
explanation: "On whose account my father was in grief and spent all night and passed the three parts of the night (without sleep) and why he was unable to sleep was not understood clearly. By his (Rama's) action this Lanka is agitated like a river during the rainy season. He, who is the root cause of this calamity, has been got rid of by me," thought Indrajith.

shloka_text: यत्कृतेचिन्तयानस्यशोकार्तस्यपितुर्मम ।।6.46.14।। अस्पृष्टवाशयनंगात्रैस्त्रियामायातिशर्वरी । त्स्नेयंयत्कृतेलङ्कानदीवर्षास्विवाकुला ।।6.46.15।। सोऽयंमूलहरोऽनर्थःसर्वेषांनिहतोमया ।
transliteration: yatkṛtecintayānasyaśokārtasyapiturmama  aspṛṣṭavāśayanaṃgātraistriyāmāyātiśarvarī | tsneyaṃyatkṛtelaṅkānadīvarṣāsvivākulā  so'yaṃmūlaharo'narthaḥsarveṣāṃnihatomayā |
translation: यत्कृकते on whose account, चिन्तयानस्य with this thought, शोकार्तस्य is in grief, ममपितुः my father, गात्रैः body, शयनम् bed, अस्पृष्टवा not understood clearly, त्रियामा three periods, शर्वरी night, याति passed away, यत्कृते by what action, कृत्स्ना dark, इयंलङ्का this Lanka, वर्षासु raining, नदीइव like river, आकुला agitated, सः he, अयम् all, सर्वेषाम् all of us, मूलहरः root cause, अनर्थः got rid of, मया by me, निहतः killed.
explanation: "On whose account my father was in grief and spent all night and passed the three parts of the night (without sleep) and why he was unable to sleep was not understood clearly. By his (Rama's) action this Lanka is agitated like a river during the rainy season. He, who is the root cause of this calamity, has been got rid of by me," thought Indrajith.

shloka_text: रामस्यलक्ष्मणस्यैवसर्वेषांचवनौकसाम् । विक्रमानिष्फलाःसर्वेयथाशरदितोयदाः ।।6.46.16।।
transliteration: rāmasyalakṣmaṇasyaivasarveṣāṃcavanaukasām | vikramāniṣphalāḥsarveyathāśaraditoyadāḥ
translation: रामस्य Rama's, लक्ष्मणस्यैव and even Lakshmana's, सर्वेषाम् everything, वनौकसाम् Vanaras, सर्वे all, विक्रमाः valiant, शरदि autumn, तोयदाःइव like clouds, निष्फलाः wasted.
explanation: "Rama, and Lakshmana and even all valiant Vanaras have been got rid of just like clouds of autumn are wasted."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वातुतान् सर्वान्राक्षसान्परिपार्श्वतः ।।6.46.17।। यूथपानपितान्सर्वांस्ताडयामासरावणिः ।
transliteration: evamuktvātutān sarvānrākṣasānparipārśvataḥ  yūthapānapitānsarvāṃstāḍayāmāsarāvaṇiḥ |
translation: सःरावणिः that Indrajith, तान् his, सर्वान् all, राक्षसान् Rakshasas, एवम् in that way, उक्त्वा having spoken, परिपार्श्वतः those looking at him, सर्वान् all, यूथपानपि army generals, ताडयामास began to strike.
explanation: Indrajith, having spoken in that way to all Rakshasas, began to strike all the Vanara leaders looking at him.

shloka_text: नीलंनवभिराहत्यमैन्दंचद्विविदंतथा ।।6.46.18।। त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरमित्रघ्नस्ततापप्रवरेषुभिः ।
transliteration: nīlaṃnavabhirāhatyamaindaṃcadvividaṃtathā  tribhistribhiramitraghnastatāpapravareṣubhiḥ |
translation: अमित्रघ्नः slayer of enemies, च and, नीलम् Neela, नवभिः nine shafts, आहत्य attacking, मैन्दम् Mainda, तथा so also, द्विविदम् Dwivida, त्रिभिःत्रिभिः three and three, प्रवरेषुभिः sharp edged shafts, तताप attacked.
explanation: The slayer of enemies, Indrajith attacked Neela with nine shafts, so also Mainda and Dwivida with three separate sharpedged shafts.

shloka_text: जाम्बवन्तंमहेष्वासोविद् ध्वाबाणेनवक्षसि ।।6.46.19।। हनूमतोवेगवतोविससर्जशरान्दश ।
transliteration: jāmbavantaṃmaheṣvāsovid dhvābāṇenavakṣasi  hanūmatovegavatovisasarjaśarāndaśa |
translation: महेष्वासः endowed with great bow, जाम्बवन्तम् Jambavantha, वक्षसि in the chest, बाणेन with shafts, विद् ध्वा pierced, वेगवतः endowed with speed in war, हनूमतः Hanuman, दश ten, शरान् arrows, विससर्ज released.
explanation: Indrajith endowed with great bow pierced Jambavan in his chest, and released ten arrows at Hanuman, endowed with speed in war.

shloka_text: गवाक्षंशरभंचैवद्वावप्यमिततेजसौ ।।6.46.20।। द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्यांमहावेगोविव्याधयुधिरावणिः ।
transliteration: gavākṣaṃśarabhaṃcaivadvāvapyamitatejasau  dvābhyāṃdvābhyāṃmahāvegovivyādhayudhirāvaṇiḥ |
translation: महावेगः endowed with speed, रावणिः Indrajith, युधि in war, अमिततेजसौ highly energetic, तौ both, गवाक्षम् Gavaksha, शरभंचैव Sarabha, द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्याम् two and two, विव्याध attacked.
explanation: Indrajith endowed with speed in war, attacked highly energetic Gavaksha and Sarabha with two arrows each.

shloka_text: गोलाङ्गूलेश्वरंचैववालिपुत्रमथाङ्गदम् ।।6.46.21।। विव्याधबहुभिर्बाणैस्त्वरमाणोऽथरावणिः ।
transliteration: golāṅgūleśvaraṃcaivavāliputramathāṅgadam  vivyādhabahubhirbāṇaistvaramāṇo'tharāvaṇiḥ |
translation: अथ and then, रावणिः Ravana's son, त्वरमाणः swiftly, गोलाङ्गूलेश्वरम् ruler of Golangulas, अथ and then, वालिपुत्रम् Vali's son, अङ्गदम् Angada, बहुभिः many, बाणैः arrows, विव्याद pierced.
explanation: Thereafter Indrajith attacked the ruler of Golangulas, and Vali's son Angada with many arrows.

shloka_text: तान्वानरवरान्भित्त्वाशरैरग्निशिखोपमैः ।।6.46.22।। ननादबलवांस्तत्रमहासत्त्वस्सरावणिः ।
transliteration: tānvānaravarānbhittvāśarairagniśikhopamaiḥ  nanādabalavāṃstatramahāsattvassarāvaṇiḥ |
translation: बलवान् mighty, महासत्त्व: strong, सःरावणिः that son of Ravana, तत्र there, अग्निशिखोपमैः like flames of fire, शरैः shafts, तान् himself, वानरवरान् best of monkeys, भित्त्वा attacked, ननाद and roared.
explanation: Mighty son of Ravana, then attacked the best of monkeys with arrows which were like flames of fire.

shloka_text: तानर्धयित्वाबाणौघैस्त्रासयित्वाचवानरान् ।।6.46.23।। प्रजहासमहाबाहुर्वचनंचेदमब्रवीत् ।
transliteration: tānardhayitvābāṇaughaistrāsayitvācavānarān  prajahāsamahābāhurvacanaṃcedamabravīt |
translation: तान् Indrajith, बाणौघैः hails of arrows, अर्धयित्वा struck, वानरान् Vanaras, त्रासयित्वाच terrifying, महाबाहुः of strong arms, प्रजहास laughing, इदम् these, वचनंच words, अब्रवीत् spoken.
explanation: Indrajith hurt the Vanaras with hails of arrows terrifying them. Then the mighty armed son of Ravana laughed and spoke these words.

shloka_text: शरशब्देनघोरेणमयाबद्धौचमूमुखे ।।6.46.24।। सहितौभ्रातरवेतौनिशामयतराक्षसाः ।
transliteration: śaraśabdenaghoreṇamayābaddhaucamūmukhe  sahitaubhrātaravetauniśāmayatarākṣasāḥ |
translation: राक्षसाः Rakshasas, घोरेण terrible, शरबन्धेन bound by arrows, चमूमुखे in the forefront, मया by me, बद्धौ bound, सहितौ together, एतौभ्रातरौ these two brothers, निशामयत fallen.
explanation: "O Rakshasas! Look at these two brothers together bound by my fierce arrows in front of you."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तास्तुतेसर्वेराक्षसाःकूटयोधिनः ।।6.46.25।। परंविस्मयामाजग्मुःकर्मणातेनहर्षिताः ।
transliteration: evamuktāstutesarverākṣasāḥkūṭayodhinaḥ  paraṃvismayāmājagmuḥkarmaṇātenaharṣitāḥ |
translation: एवम् in that way, उक्ताः having said, कूटयोधिनः cheerful, ते they, सर्वेराक्षसाः all Rakshasas, तेनकर्मणा by that action, परम् extremely, विस्मयम् amazed, आजग्मुः went, हर्षिताः laughing.
explanation: Indrajith having spoken in that way to the Rakshasas, all of them were highly amazed by the action of Indrajith and went laughing.

shloka_text: विनेदुश्चमहानादान् सर्वेतेजलदोपमाः ।।6.46.26।। हतोरामइतिज्ञात्वारावणिंसमपूजयन् ।
transliteration: vineduścamahānādān sarvetejaladopamāḥ  hatorāmaitijñātvārāvaṇiṃsamapūjayan |
translation: जलदोपमाः like clouds, तेसर्वे all of them, महानादान् roaring aloud, विनेदुः joyfully, रामः Rama, हतःइति is killed, ज्ञात्वा thinking, रावणिम् Son of Ravana, समपूजयन् offered prayers.
explanation: The Rakshasas thundering like rain clouds, roaring aloud thinking 'Rama is killed' by Ravana's son offered prayers.

shloka_text: निष्पन्दौतुतदादृष्टवाभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.46.27।। वसुधायांनिरुच्छवासौहतावित्यन्वमन्यत ।
transliteration: niṣpandaututadādṛṣṭavābhrātaraurāmalakṣmaṇau  vasudhāyāṃnirucchavāsauhatāvityanvamanyata |
translation: तदा thereafter, निष्पन्दौ not responding, निरुच्छवासौ without breathing, भ्रातरौ brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, वसुधायाम् on the ground, दृष्टवा having seen, हताविति dead, अन्वमन्यत thought.
explanation: Thereafter having seen the two brothers Rama and Lakshmana not responding or breathing, lying on the ground, he thought they were dead.

shloka_text: हर्षेणतुसमाविष्टइन्द्रजित्समितिञ्जयः ।।6.46.28।। प्रविवेशपुरींलङ्कांहर्षयन् सर्वनैर्वृतान् ।
transliteration: harṣeṇatusamāviṣṭaindrajitsamitiñjayaḥ  praviveśapurīṃlaṅkāṃharṣayan sarvanairvṛtān |
translation: समितिञ्जयः one who is victorious in battles, इन्द्रजित् Indrajith, हर्षेण felt happy, समाविष्टः collected there, सर्वनैर्वतान् for all Rakshasas, हर्षयन् creating happiness, लङ्कांपुरीम् Lanka city, प्रविवेश entered
explanation: Indrajith, who is victorious in battles, feeling happy and creating happiness to all Rakshasas collected there entered the city of Lanka.

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणयोर्दृष्टवाशरीरेसायकैश्चिते ।।6.46.29।। सर्वाणिचाङ्गोपाङ्गानिसुग्रीवंभयमाविशत् ।
transliteration: rāmalakṣmaṇayordṛṣṭavāśarīresāyakaiścite  sarvāṇicāṅgopāṅgānisugrīvaṃbhayamāviśat |
translation: रामलक्ष्मणयोः Rama and Lakshmana, सायकैः by arrows, चिते riddled with, शरीरे body, सर्वाणि all over, अङ्गोपाङ्गानि from head to foot, दृष्टवा seeing, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, भयम् feared, आविशत् possessed.
explanation: Sugriva was overtaken by fear on seeing Rama and Lakshmana riddled with arrows from head to foot all over the body

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणयोर्दृष्टवाशरीरेसायकैश्चिते ।।6.46.29।। सर्वाणिचाङ्गोपाङ्गानिसुग्रीवंभयमाविशत् ।
transliteration: rāmalakṣmaṇayordṛṣṭavāśarīresāyakaiścite  sarvāṇicāṅgopāṅgānisugrīvaṃbhayamāviśat |
translation: रामलक्ष्मणयोः Rama and Lakshmana, सायकैः by arrows, चिते riddled with, शरीरे body, सर्वाणि all over, अङ्गोपाङ्गानि from head to foot, दृष्टवा seeing, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, भयम् feared, आविशत् possessed.
explanation: Sugriva was overtaken by fear on seeing Rama and Lakshmana riddled with arrows from head to foot all over the body

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणयोर्दृष्टवाशरीरेसायकैश्चिते ।।6.46.29।। सर्वाणिचाङ्गोपाङ्गानिसुग्रीवंभयमाविशत् ।
transliteration: rāmalakṣmaṇayordṛṣṭavāśarīresāyakaiścite  sarvāṇicāṅgopāṅgānisugrīvaṃbhayamāviśat |
translation: रामलक्ष्मणयोः Rama and Lakshmana, सायकैः by arrows, चिते riddled with, शरीरे body, सर्वाणि all over, अङ्गोपाङ्गानि from head to foot, दृष्टवा seeing, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, भयम् feared, आविशत् possessed.
explanation: Sugriva was overtaken by fear on seeing Rama and Lakshmana riddled with arrows from head to foot all over the body

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणयोर्दृष्टवाशरीरेसायकैश्चिते ।।6.46.29।। सर्वाणिचाङ्गोपाङ्गानिसुग्रीवंभयमाविशत् ।
transliteration: rāmalakṣmaṇayordṛṣṭavāśarīresāyakaiścite  sarvāṇicāṅgopāṅgānisugrīvaṃbhayamāviśat |
translation: रामलक्ष्मणयोः Rama and Lakshmana, सायकैः by arrows, चिते riddled with, शरीरे body, सर्वाणि all over, अङ्गोपाङ्गानि from head to foot, दृष्टवा seeing, सुग्रीवम् Sugriva, भयम् feared, आविशत् possessed.
explanation: Sugriva was overtaken by fear on seeing Rama and Lakshmana riddled with arrows from head to foot all over the body

shloka_text: पर्यवस्थापयात्मानमनाथंमांचवानर ।।6.46.33।। सत्यधर्माभिरक्तानांनास्तिमृत्युकृतंभयम् ।
transliteration: paryavasthāpayātmānamanāthaṃmāṃcavānara  satyadharmābhiraktānāṃnāstimṛtyukṛtaṃbhayam |
translation: वानर Vanara, आत्मानम् our self, अनाथम् helpless, मांच and mine, पर्यमास्थापय restoring, सत्यधर्मानिरक्तानाम् for those following righteousness and truthfulness, मृत्युकृतम् from death, भयम् fear, नास्ति not.
explanation: "O Vanara! We are helpless, be confident, for those following righteousness and truthfulness there is no fear of death."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वाततस्तस्यजलक्लन्नेनपाणिना ।।6.46.34।। सुग्रीवस्यशुभेनेत्रेप्रममार्जविभीषणः ।
transliteration: evamuktvātatastasyajalaklannenapāṇinā  sugrīvasyaśubhenetrepramamārjavibhīṣaṇaḥ |
translation: विभीषणः Vibheeshana, एवम् in that manner, उक्त्वा spoken, ततः then, जलक्लिन्नेन dipping in water, पाणिना hand, तस्यसुग्रीवस्य Sugriva's, शुभे beautiful, नेत्रे eyes, प्रममार्ज brightened.
explanation: Vibheeshana, having spoken in that manner, there after dipped his hand in water and wiped the beautiful eyes of Sugriva to brighten.

shloka_text: ततस्सलिलमादायविद्ययापरिजप्यच ।।6.46.35।। सुग्रीवनेत्रेधर्मात्मासममार्जविभीषणः ।
transliteration: tatassalilamādāyavidyayāparijapyaca  sugrīvanetredharmātmāsamamārjavibhīṣaṇaḥ |
translation: ततः thereafter, धर्मात्मा dutiful, विभीषणः Vibheeshana, सलिलम् water, आदाय taking, विद्यया as per tradition, परिजस्यच chanting sacred text to consecrate, सुग्रीवनेत्रे Sugriva's eyes, सममार्ज wiped.
explanation: Thereafter the dutiful Vibheeshana taking water as per tradition consecrated chanting sacred text and wiped Sugriva's eyes.

shloka_text: विमृज्यवदनंतस्यकपिराजस्यधीमतः ।।6.46.36।। अब्रवीत्कालसम्प्राप्तसम्भ्रान्तमिदंवचः ।
transliteration: vimṛjyavadanaṃtasyakapirājasyadhīmataḥ  abravītkālasamprāptasambhrāntamidaṃvacaḥ |
translation: धीमतः wise, तस्यकपिराजस्य that monkey king, वदनम् countenance, विमृज्य wiped clean, कालसम्प्राप्तम् as per that time, असम्भ्रान्तम् opportune, इदंवचः these words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Wise Vibheeshana having wiped Sugriva's face clean in accordance with time addressed with opportune words.

shloka_text: नकालःकपिराजेन्द्रवैक्लब्यमवलम्बितुम् ।।6.46.37।। अतिस्नेहोऽप्यकालेऽस्मिन्मरणायोपकल्पते ।
transliteration: nakālaḥkapirājendravaiklabyamavalambitum  atisneho'pyakāle'sminmaraṇāyopakalpate |
translation: कपिराजेन्द्र monkey king, वैक्लब्यम् faint heartedness, अवलम्बितुम् to follow, कालः time, न not this, अस्मिन् our, काले time, अतिस्नेहोऽप्य with extreme attachment, मरणाय death, उपकल्पते lead.
explanation: "O king of monkeys! This is not the time for faint heartedness. Extreme attachment at this time will lead us to death."

shloka_text: तस्मादुत्सृज्यवैक्लब्यंसर्वकार्यविनाशनम् ।।6.46.38।। हितंरामपुरोगणांसैन्यानानुचिन्त्यताम् ।
transliteration: tasmādutsṛjyavaiklabyaṃsarvakāryavināśanam  hitaṃrāmapurogaṇāṃsainyānānucintyatām |
translation: तस्मात् therefore, सर्वकार्यविनाशनम् all actions will be destroyed, वैक्लब्यम् faintheartedness, उत्सृज्य give up, रामपुरोगणाम् following Rama, सैन्यानाम् army, हितम् welfare, अनुचिन्त्यताम् think of.
explanation: "Therefore, give up faintheartedness as all actions will be destroyed by that. Following Rama's leadership, think of the army's welfare."

shloka_text: अथवारक्ष्यतांरामोयावत्संज्ञाविपर्ययः ।।6.46.39।। लब्धसंज्ञौहिकाकुत्स्थौभयंनौव्यपनेष्यतः ।
transliteration: athavārakṣyatāṃrāmoyāvatsaṃjñāviparyayaḥ  labdhasaṃjñauhikākutsthaubhayaṃnauvyapaneṣyataḥ |
translation: अथवा or else, यावत्संज्ञाविपर्ययः till they become conscious, रामः Rama, रक्ष्यताम् protect, लब्धसंज्ञौ when they get back consciousness, काकुत्स्थौ both Kakuthsa princes, नौ, भयम् fear, व्यपनेष्यतःहि will be able to get rid off.
explanation: "Or else till they become conscious, protect the Kakuthsa princes. When they become conscious, they can get rid of our fear."

shloka_text: नैतत्किञ्चनरामस्यनचरामोमुमूर्षति ।।6.46.40।। नह्येनंहास्यतेलक्ष्मीद्दुर्लभायागतायुषाम् ।
transliteration: naitatkiñcanarāmasyanacarāmomumūrṣati  nahyenaṃhāsyatelakṣmīddurlabhāyāgatāyuṣām |
translation: एतत् therefore, रामस्य Rama's, किञ्चन even a little, न not, रामः Rama, नमुमूर्षति not going to die, या whatever, गतायुषाम् life is lost, दुर्लभा difficult, लक्ष्मीः prosperous, एनम् , नहास्यतेहि not leave him.
explanation: "Therefore, Rama has no fear of death, even a little. Whatever splendour is lost, prosperity will not leave him."

shloka_text: तस्मादाश्वासयात्मानंबलंचाश्वासयस्वकम् ।।6.46.41।। यावत्कार्याणिसर्वाणिपुनःसंस्थापयाम्यहम् ।
transliteration: tasmādāśvāsayātmānaṃbalaṃcāśvāsayasvakam  yāvatkāryāṇisarvāṇipunaḥsaṃsthāpayāmyaham |
translation: तस्मात् therefore, आत्मानम् ourselves, आश्वासय restoring breath, स्वकम् myself, बलम् army, आश्वासय reassure, अहम् I, सर्वाणि all, कार्यानि actions, पुनः again, यावत् संस्थापयामि all the army restore confidence.
explanation: "Therefore, restoring breath let us reassure the army again till all actions are carried out by restoring their confidence."

shloka_text: एतेहिफुल्लनयनास्त्रासादागतसाध्वसाः ।।6.46.42।। कर्णेकर्णेप्रकथिताहरयोहरिसत्तम ।
transliteration: etehiphullanayanāstrāsādāgatasādhvasāḥ  karṇekarṇeprakathitāharayoharisattama |
translation: हरिसत्तम monkey leader, एते these, हरयः monkeys, फुल्लनयनाः dilated eyes, त्रासात् by fear, आगतसाध्वसाः seized with fear, कर्णेकर्णे ear to ear, प्रकथिताः talking to each other.
explanation: "O Monkey leader! these monkeys whose eyes have become big (are dilated) with fear are talking ear to ear (about Rama)."

shloka_text: मांतुदृष्टवाप्रधावन्तमनीकंसम्प्रहर्षितुम् ।।6.46.43।। त्यजस्तुहरयस्त्रासंभुक्तपूर्वामिवस्रजम् ।
transliteration: māṃtudṛṣṭavāpradhāvantamanīkaṃsampraharṣitum  tyajastuharayastrāsaṃbhuktapūrvāmivasrajam |
translation: अनीकम् army forces, सम्प्रहर्षितुम् made them happy, प्रधावन्तम् inherent, माम् me, दृष्टवा seeing, हरयः monkeys, त्रासम् moving in fear, भुक्तपूर्वम् enjoyed earlier, स्रजम् garland of flowers, इव like that, त्यजन्तु discard.
explanation: "Let the army forces of monkeys be happy seeing me moving, getting rid of the inherent fear in them just as they discard a garland of flowers enjoyed by them earlier."

shloka_text: समाश्वास्यतुसुग्रीवंराक्षसेन्द्रोविभीषणः ।।6.46.44।। विद्रुतंवानरानीकंतत्समाश्वासयत्पुनः ।
transliteration: samāśvāsyatusugrīvaṃrākṣasendrovibhīṣaṇaḥ  vidrutaṃvānarānīkaṃtatsamāśvāsayatpunaḥ |
translation: राक्षसेन्द्रः king of Rakshasas, विभीषणः Vibheeshana, सुग्रीवम् to Sugriva, समाश्वास्य assured, विद्रुतम् knowing, तत् वानरानीकम् that Vanara army, पुनः again, समाश्वासयत् reassured.
explanation: The king of Rakshasas, Vibheeshana having assured Sugriva, knowing the Vanara army he reassured them.

shloka_text: इन्द्रजित्तुमहामायःसर्वसैन्यसमावृतः ।।6.46.45।। विवेशनगरींलङ्कांपितरंचाभ्युपागमत् ।
transliteration: indrajittumahāmāyaḥsarvasainyasamāvṛtaḥ  viveśanagarīṃlaṅkāṃpitaraṃcābhyupāgamat |
translation: महामायः great, इन्द्रजित्तुः Indrajith, सर्वसैन्यसमावृतः all the army surrounding him, लङ्कां Lanka नगरीम् City, विवेश entered, पितरम् father, अभ्युपागमत् च approached.
explanation: Great Indrajith surrounded by all army entered the city of Lanka and approached his father.

shloka_text: तत्ररावणमासाद्यअभिवाद्यकृताञ्जलिः ।।6.46.46।। आचचक्षेप्रियंपित्रेनिहतौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।
transliteration: tatrarāvaṇamāsādyaabhivādyakṛtāñjaliḥ  ācacakṣepriyaṃpitrenihataurāmalakṣmaṇau |
translation: तत्र there, रावणम् Ravana, आसाद्य having reached, अभिवाद्य greeted, कृताञ्जलिः with folded palms, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, निहतौ are killed, पित्रे O father, प्रियम् dear, आचचक्षे broke the news.
explanation: Having reached Ravana, Indrajith greeted him with folded palms and broke the pleasant news, "Rama and Lakshmana are killed."

shloka_text: उत्पपातततोहृष्टःपुत्रंचपरिषस्वजे ।।6.46.47।। रावणोरक्षसांमध्येश्रुत्वाशत्रूनिपातितौ ।
transliteration: utpapātatatohṛṣṭaḥputraṃcapariṣasvaje  rāvaṇorakṣasāṃmadhyeśrutvāśatrūnipātitau |
translation: रक्षसाम् Rakshasas, मध्ये midst, रावणः Ravana, शत्रू enemy, निपातितौ killed, श्रुत्वा hearing, ततः then, हृष्टः rejoiced, उत्पपात got up, पुत्रम् son, पर्षिस्वजेच embraced
explanation: In the midst of Rakshasas, Ravana hearing the news of his enemies being killed, rejoiced, and got up from his couch and embraced his son.

shloka_text: उपाघ्रायचतंमूद् र्नेनंपप्रच्छप्रीतमानसः ।।6.46.48।। पृच्छतेचयथावृत्तंपित्रेतस्मैसर्वंन्यवेदयत् । यथातौशरबन्धेननिश्चेष्टौनिष्प्रभौकृतौ ।।6.46.49।।
transliteration: upāghrāyacataṃmūd rnenaṃpapracchaprītamānasaḥ  pṛcchatecayathāvṛttaṃpitretasmaisarvaṃnyavedayat | yathātauśarabandhenaniśceṣṭauniṣprabhaukṛtau
translation: पृच्छते enquired, पित्रे father, तौ both of them, शरबन्धेन from the network of arrows, निश्चेष्टौ stunned, निष्प्रभौ splendour gone, यथा like that, कृतौ did, तस्मै their, यथावृत्तम् all in detail, न्यवेदयत् presented.
explanation: Delighted Ravana kissed his son on the forehead and enquired of him of the details. Indrajith presented details saying that both Rama and Lakshmana were stunned in the network of arrows, and lost splendour.

shloka_text: उपाघ्रायचतंमूद् र्नेनंपप्रच्छप्रीतमानसः ।।6.46.48।। पृच्छतेचयथावृत्तंपित्रेतस्मैसर्वंन्यवेदयत् । यथातौशरबन्धेननिश्चेष्टौनिष्प्रभौकृतौ ।।6.46.49।।
transliteration: upāghrāyacataṃmūd rnenaṃpapracchaprītamānasaḥ  pṛcchatecayathāvṛttaṃpitretasmaisarvaṃnyavedayat | yathātauśarabandhenaniśceṣṭauniṣprabhaukṛtau
translation: पृच्छते enquired, पित्रे father, तौ both of them, शरबन्धेन from the network of arrows, निश्चेष्टौ stunned, निष्प्रभौ splendour gone, यथा like that, कृतौ did, तस्मै their, यथावृत्तम् all in detail, न्यवेदयत् presented.
explanation: Delighted Ravana kissed his son on the forehead and enquired of him of the details. Indrajith presented details saying that both Rama and Lakshmana were stunned in the network of arrows, and lost splendour.

shloka_text: सहर्षवेगानुगतान्तरात्माश्रुत्वावचस्तस्यमहारथस्य । जहौज्वरंदाशरथेःसमुत्थितंप्रहृष्यवाचाऽभिननन्दपुत्रम् ।।6.46.50।।
transliteration: saharṣavegānugatāntarātmāśrutvāvacastasyamahārathasya | jahaujvaraṃdāśaratheḥsamutthitaṃprahṛṣyavācā'bhinanandaputram
translation: महारथस्य of the great chariot warrior, तस्य his, वचः words, श्रुत्वा on hearing, हर्षवेगानुगतान्तरात्मा filled with joy at heart, सः he, दाशरथेः Dasaratha's son, समुत्थितम् fear, ज्वरम् agony, जहौ gone, प्रहृष्यवाचा joyful words, पुत्रम् son, अभिननन्द greeted.
explanation: Hearing the words of the great chariot warrior, Ravana was filled with excessive joy at heart. His fear and agony of Dasaratha's son having gone on hearing the words of his son, Ravana greeted him. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेषटचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty sixth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: प्रतिप्रविष्टेलङ्कायांकृतार्थेरावणात्मजे । राघवंपरिवार्यार्तुरक्षुर्वानरर्षभाः ।।6.47.1।।
transliteration: pratipraviṣṭelaṅkāyāṃkṛtārtherāvaṇātmaje | rāghavaṃparivāryārturakṣurvānararṣabhāḥ
translation: पति king, रावणात्मजे Ravana's son, कृतार्थे accomplished the task, लङ्कायाम् into Lanka, प्रविष्टे entered, अथ and then, वानरर्षभाः bull among monkeys, राघवम् at Raghava, परिवार्यार्तुः around, ररक्षुः guarded.
explanation: After accomplishing the task Ravana's son entered Lanka while the bull among monkeys guarded Raghava staying around.
comments: Hanuman and others guard Rama and Lakshmana. Ravana commands Rakshasa woman to take Sita in the Pushpaka and show her the state of Rama and Lakshmana. Sita bursts on seeing the fate of Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: हनुमानङ्गदोनीलःसुषेणःकुमुदोनलः । गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः ।।6.47.2।। जाम्बवानृषभःसुन्दोरम्भःशतवलिःपृथुः । व्यूढानीकाश्चयत्ताश्चद्रुमानादायसर्वतः ।।6.47.3।। वीक्षमाणादिशस्सर्वास्तिर्यगूर्ध्वंचवानराः । तृणेष्वपिचचेष्टत्सुराक्षसाइतिमेनिरे ।।6.47.4।।
transliteration: hanumānaṅgadonīlaḥsuṣeṇaḥkumudonalaḥ | gajogavākṣogavayaśśarabhogandhamādanaḥ  jāmbavānṛṣabhaḥsundorambhaḥśatavaliḥpṛthuḥ | vyūḍhānīkāścayattāścadrumānādāyasarvataḥ  vīkṣamāṇādiśassarvāstiryagūrdhvaṃcavānarāḥ | tṛṇeṣvapicaceṣṭatsurākṣasāitimenire
translation: हनुमान् Hanuman, अङ्गदः Angada, नीलः Nila, सुषेणः Sushena, कुमुदः Kumuda, नलः Nala, गवयः Gava, शरभः Sarabha, गन्धमादनः Gandhamadana, सानुप्रस्थः Sanuprastha, जाम्बवान् Jambavan, ऋषभः Rshaba, सुन्दः Sandhu, रम्भः Rambha, शतवलिः Satavali, पृथुः Pruthu, वानराः Vanara, सर्वतः always, व्यूढानीका having arranged, यत्ताश्च in place, द्रुमान् trees, आदाय getting, सर्वाः all, दिशः directions, तिर्यक् above, ऊर्ध्वंच either side, वीक्षमाणाः looking, तृणेष्वपि even a blade of grass, चेष्टत्सु moved, राक्षसाःइति thinking to be Rakshasas, मेनिरे watched.
explanation: Having arranged the army in place, Hanuman, Angada, Nila, Kumuda, Nala, Gava, Sarabha, Gandhamadana, Sanuprastha, Jambavan, Rshaba, Rambha, Satavali, Pruthu, who are always alert were holding trees and looking above, on either side and in all directions and guarded Rama. Whenever there was movement of even a blade of grass, they thought that it might be Rakshasa.

shloka_text: हनुमानङ्गदोनीलःसुषेणःकुमुदोनलः । गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः ।।6.47.2।। जाम्बवानृषभःसुन्दोरम्भःशतवलिःपृथुः । व्यूढानीकाश्चयत्ताश्चद्रुमानादायसर्वतः ।।6.47.3।। वीक्षमाणादिशस्सर्वास्तिर्यगूर्ध्वंचवानराः । तृणेष्वपिचचेष्टत्सुराक्षसाइतिमेनिरे ।।6.47.4।।
transliteration: hanumānaṅgadonīlaḥsuṣeṇaḥkumudonalaḥ | gajogavākṣogavayaśśarabhogandhamādanaḥ  jāmbavānṛṣabhaḥsundorambhaḥśatavaliḥpṛthuḥ | vyūḍhānīkāścayattāścadrumānādāyasarvataḥ  vīkṣamāṇādiśassarvāstiryagūrdhvaṃcavānarāḥ | tṛṇeṣvapicaceṣṭatsurākṣasāitimenire
translation: हनुमान् Hanuman, अङ्गदः Angada, नीलः Nila, सुषेणः Sushena, कुमुदः Kumuda, नलः Nala, गवयः Gava, शरभः Sarabha, गन्धमादनः Gandhamadana, सानुप्रस्थः Sanuprastha, जाम्बवान् Jambavan, ऋषभः Rshaba, सुन्दः Sandhu, रम्भः Rambha, शतवलिः Satavali, पृथुः Pruthu, वानराः Vanara, सर्वतः always, व्यूढानीका having arranged, यत्ताश्च in place, द्रुमान् trees, आदाय getting, सर्वाः all, दिशः directions, तिर्यक् above, ऊर्ध्वंच either side, वीक्षमाणाः looking, तृणेष्वपि even a blade of grass, चेष्टत्सु moved, राक्षसाःइति thinking to be Rakshasas, मेनिरे watched.
explanation: Having arranged the army in place, Hanuman, Angada, Nila, Kumuda, Nala, Gava, Sarabha, Gandhamadana, Sanuprastha, Jambavan, Rshaba, Rambha, Satavali, Pruthu, who are always alert were holding trees and looking above, on either side and in all directions and guarded Rama. Whenever there was movement of even a blade of grass, they thought that it might be Rakshasa.

shloka_text: हनुमानङ्गदोनीलःसुषेणःकुमुदोनलः । गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः ।।6.47.2।। जाम्बवानृषभःसुन्दोरम्भःशतवलिःपृथुः । व्यूढानीकाश्चयत्ताश्चद्रुमानादायसर्वतः ।।6.47.3।। वीक्षमाणादिशस्सर्वास्तिर्यगूर्ध्वंचवानराः । तृणेष्वपिचचेष्टत्सुराक्षसाइतिमेनिरे ।।6.47.4।।
transliteration: hanumānaṅgadonīlaḥsuṣeṇaḥkumudonalaḥ | gajogavākṣogavayaśśarabhogandhamādanaḥ  jāmbavānṛṣabhaḥsundorambhaḥśatavaliḥpṛthuḥ | vyūḍhānīkāścayattāścadrumānādāyasarvataḥ  vīkṣamāṇādiśassarvāstiryagūrdhvaṃcavānarāḥ | tṛṇeṣvapicaceṣṭatsurākṣasāitimenire
translation: हनुमान् Hanuman, अङ्गदः Angada, नीलः Nila, सुषेणः Sushena, कुमुदः Kumuda, नलः Nala, गवयः Gava, शरभः Sarabha, गन्धमादनः Gandhamadana, सानुप्रस्थः Sanuprastha, जाम्बवान् Jambavan, ऋषभः Rshaba, सुन्दः Sandhu, रम्भः Rambha, शतवलिः Satavali, पृथुः Pruthu, वानराः Vanara, सर्वतः always, व्यूढानीका having arranged, यत्ताश्च in place, द्रुमान् trees, आदाय getting, सर्वाः all, दिशः directions, तिर्यक् above, ऊर्ध्वंच either side, वीक्षमाणाः looking, तृणेष्वपि even a blade of grass, चेष्टत्सु moved, राक्षसाःइति thinking to be Rakshasas, मेनिरे watched.
explanation: Having arranged the army in place, Hanuman, Angada, Nila, Kumuda, Nala, Gava, Sarabha, Gandhamadana, Sanuprastha, Jambavan, Rshaba, Rambha, Satavali, Pruthu, who are always alert were holding trees and looking above, on either side and in all directions and guarded Rama. Whenever there was movement of even a blade of grass, they thought that it might be Rakshasa.

shloka_text: रावणश्चापिसम्हृष्टोविसृज्येन्द्रजितंसुतम् । अजुहावततस्सीताक्षिणीराक्षसीस्तदा ।।6.47.5।।
transliteration: rāvaṇaścāpisamhṛṣṭovisṛjyendrajitaṃsutam | ajuhāvatatassītākṣiṇīrākṣasīstadā
translation: रावणश्चापि Ravana also, सम्हृष्टः contended, सुतम् son, इन्द्रजितम् Indrajith, विसृज्य sending away, ततः then, सीताक्षिणीः caretaker of Sita, राक्षसीः rakshasi, तदा then, आजुहाव called for.
explanation: Ravana was also content to send away his son Indrajith and calls for the Rakshasa woman, caretaker of Sita.

shloka_text: राक्षस्यस्त्रिजटाचैवशासनात्समुपस्थिताः । ताउवाचततोहृष्टोराक्षसीराक्षसाधमः ।।6.47.6।।
transliteration: rākṣasyastrijaṭācaivaśāsanātsamupasthitāḥ | tāuvācatatohṛṣṭorākṣasīrākṣasādhamaḥ
translation: राक्षस्यः rakshasi, त्रिजटाचैव Trijata also, शासनात् by the order, तम् his, उपस्थिताः waited, ततः there, हृष्टः joyful, राक्षसाधमः lowly Rakshasa, ताःराक्षसीः that rakshasi, उवाच addressed.
explanation: The rakshasi and also Trijata came and waited there by the order. Lowly Rakshasa, Ravana, full of joy addressed rakshasi.

shloka_text: हताविन्द्रजिताख्यातवैदेह्यारामलक्ष्मणौ । पुष्पकंतत्समारोप्यदर्शयध्वंहतौरणे ।।6.47.7।।
transliteration: hatāvindrajitākhyātavaidehyārāmalakṣmaṇau | puṣpakaṃtatsamāropyadarśayadhvaṃhatauraṇe
translation: रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, इन्द्रता by Indrajith, हतौ killed, वैदेह्याः to Vaidehi, तत् that, पुष्पकम् aerial car, समारोप्य ascended, रणे war, हतौ killed, दर्शयध्वम् you may show.
explanation: "Rama and Lakshmana are killed by Indrajith in war. Take Vaidehi in the aerial car and show her."

shloka_text: यदाश्रयादवष्टब्धामामुपतिष्ठति । सोऽस्याभर्तासहभ्रात्रानिहतोरणमूर्धनि ।।6.47.8।।
transliteration: yadāśrayādavaṣṭabdhāmāmupatiṣṭhati | so'syābhartāsahabhrātrānihatoraṇamūrdhani
translation: इयम् that husband, यताश्रयात् with whose support, अवष्टब्धा being proud, माम् to me, नउपतिष्ठते not yielding, सः he, अस्याः, भर्ता husband, रणमूर्धनि unconscious in the war, भ्रात्रासह along with brother, निहतः has been killed.
explanation: "That husband with whose support she was proud and not yielding to me is unconscious along with his brother who have been killed," said Ravana.

shloka_text: निर्विशङ्कानिरुद्विग्नानिरपेक्षाचमैथिली । मामुपस्थास्यतेसीतासर्वाभरणभूषिता ।।6.47.9।।
transliteration: nirviśaṅkānirudvignānirapekṣācamaithilī | māmupasthāsyatesītāsarvābharaṇabhūṣitā
translation: मैथिली Mythili, सीता Sita, निर्विशङ्का rid of sorrow, निरुद्विग्ना free from perturbation, निरपेक्षा giving up hope, सर्वाभरणभूषिता adorned with all kinds of jewels, माम् me, उपस्थास्यते wait on me.
